summary: This non-peer-reviewed technical report examines bioimpedance phase angle clusters as an alternative to body mass index.

The Weather Channel’s Android app uses IBM mesh-networking technology to relay emergency information directly between phones when centralized mobile networks fail. Designed for developing countries, it transmits data 200–500 feet via Bluetooth and Wi-Fi without extra battery burden or network reconfiguration. Its effectiveness depends on enough users running the app, while digital signatures protect message authenticity. Launching in Asia, Latin America and Africa, the 3.2MB app also supports older 2G networks.

Sensient Technologies reported quarterly EPS of $0.80, exceeding the $0.78 consensus estimate. The company had a 9.13% net margin and 16.73% return on equity. Shares opened at $78.53. Sensient announced a $0.30 quarterly dividend. KeyCorp raised its price target to $84 with an “overweight” rating, while Zacks upgraded the stock from “sell” to “hold.”

XYZprinting showcased the $19,950 MfgPro220 xPF industrial stereolithography printer at Rapid + TCT 2018. Powered by Nexa3D’s LSPc technology, it offers a 16-liter build volume, high-speed, high-resolution production, machine-learning optimization, integrated monitoring, and local or cloud operation. It targets functional prototypes, tooling, end-use parts, and customized mass production. XYZprinting also partnered with BEGO and Nexa3D to develop, manufacture, and market a specialized high-speed dental printer, following an earlier investment and manufacturing agreement with Nexa3D.

A November 2016 Blue Cross Blue Shield of Mississippi grant funded Bell Academy’s new physical education building. Parent and community volunteers constructed and equipped the gym, giving students a safer, quieter indoor space for expanded physical activities. A horizontal rock-climbing wall is planned before the building’s Friday ribbon cutting. Teacher Joyce Aycock thanked parents and the community for their support.

Collagen provides structural support, strength and elasticity to skin, tendons, bones and other tissues, but natural production declines with age. Of roughly 28 collagen types, types I–V are most common; oral supplements mainly contain types I, II and III.

Supplements include hydrolysed collagen, unprocessed chicken cartilage and gelatin. Most are animal-derived, commonly from marine, bovine, porcine or chicken sources. Hydrolysed collagen may be most effective because it is easily digested and absorbed.

Studies suggest collagen supplements may support skin firmness and hydration, nail growth, bones, joints and connective tissues, while evidence for thicker hair is limited to mice. Potentially effective doses vary by goal, from 2.5 grams daily for skin and joint benefits to 15 grams for muscle mass alongside resistance training. Research remains ongoing, and manufacturers often recommend at least 12 weeks of use. Third-party-tested products are advised.

A balanced diet can support natural collagen production through protein-rich foods, vitamin C sources and foods such as bone broth.

Bethesda will release Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus for Nintendo Switch on June 29 digitally and physically, though the cartridge requires a download and likely microSD storage. The port follows Bethesda’s Switch releases of Doom and Skyrim.

The council says it is coordinating roadworks and utility maintenance to reduce congestion around Southway, Tamerton Foliot and the Derriford Transport Scheme. Measures include restricting temporary signals to off-peak hours, requesting night or weekend work, suspending Tavistock Road bus-lane restrictions, maintaining two general traffic lanes and adjusting traffic-light timings at George Junction. It is reviewing lane markings and traffic arrangements at Budshead Roundabout, subject to a safety audit, and considering additional signs to help side-road traffic merge. Traffic flow is continually monitored, while planned works and likely disruptions are publicised online, through alerts, media, social channels and roadside signs.

ADT is presented as undervalued relative to newly listed Verisure, supported by revenue growth, improving profitability, recurring revenue, Google and State Farm partnerships, debt reduction, and share buybacks producing an 11% shareholder yield. Customer churn and stagnant subscriber numbers remain concerns, while AI, remote assistance, and smart-home investments target retention. A 12–14x P/E valuation suggests more than 33% upside. The author holds ADT shares or derivatives and states the article reflects personal opinions, not investment advice.

The lecture introduces discrete stochastic processes, emphasizing that probability’s central challenge is constructing appropriate real-world models rather than solving well-posed mathematical problems. Models simplify uncertain phenomena but may fail despite correct mathematics, so their assumptions must be critically examined.

The course originated from communication networks and queueing applications and covers counting and Poisson processes, Markov chains, renewal processes, random walks, and martingales. Stochastic processes model sequences of random variables over time; discrete processes use discrete time or sample values. Applications include communications, computer systems, queueing, risk and catastrophe management, system failures, biology, medicine, optics, and control.

Kolmogorov’s framework consists of a sample space, events, and a probability measure. Events are suitably restricted subsets closed under complements and countable unions. Probabilities are nonnegative, the sample space has probability one, and probabilities add over disjoint countable events. Consequences include complement rules, monotonicity, and the union bound.

Independent events have joint probability equal to the product of their probabilities. Independent experiments can be combined through Cartesian-product sample spaces, supporting models of repeated trials and infinite sequences.

A random variable is a function from sample points to finite real values, subject to measurability conditions ensuring relevant sets are events. Distribution functions exist for every random variable and accommodate discrete, continuous, mixed, and other distributions; probability mass functions and densities apply only in particular cases.

The lecture also stresses learning proofs alongside intuition because complicated systems cannot always be analyzed intuitively.

The football Drive concept pairs a 10–12-yard basic route with a trailing 3–4-yard shallow cross from the same side, creating a triangle read that stresses linebackers. It is effective against man coverage, where receivers remain moving, and Cover 4, where the post and basic routes can pressure the safety. It is less effective against Cover 2 and Cover 3 because additional underneath defenders limit space and big-play opportunities.

Against zone, the tight end and slot receiver settle into open areas; against man, they continue across the field. The quarterback first checks the post pre-snap, particularly against Cover 4 or a favorable matchup. The post-snap progression is the X receiver’s go route, slot receiver’s shallow cross, tight end’s basic route, and running back’s flare check-down. The quarterback must quickly identify man or zone coverage and adjust accordingly.

The concept can be paired with bunch formations to create natural picks and rubs against man coverage. It can also serve as a backside option in other passing schemes, providing a quick answer against blitzes or an outlet when downfield combinations are unavailable.

The Department of Higher Education and Training is working to integrate NSFAS systems with universities and colleges after payment delays triggered student protests. Minister Naledi Pandor called unresolved funding for continuing students unacceptable and said registration-data problems were delaying bursary agreements and allocations. The department will assess NSFAS processes, strengthen cooperation with institutional financial aid offices, and provide R105m to improve administrative capacity. Government allocated nearly R7.2bn in 2018 for new bursaries, including R4.6bn for university students and R2.6bn for TVET students. NSFAS funding is set to rise from about R9.9bn in 2017-18 to over R35.3bn in 2020-21. The DA’s Belinda Bozzoli requested an urgent parliamentary meeting, criticizing officials for not stating how many students remain unpaid, why, or when they will receive funding.

The bill would grant states public land or scrip totaling about 6.06 million acres to establish colleges teaching agriculture, mechanic arts, and other studies. The objections characterize the measure as inexpedient and unconstitutional. They argue it would reduce federal land-sale revenue during fiscal difficulty, blur federal and state responsibilities, encourage state dependence and extravagance, promote land speculation harmful to settlers and new states, provide no enforceable federal control over the funds, and disadvantage existing colleges. The constitutional argument holds that Congress may dispose of public lands only for authorized federal purposes, not give them away for state education. Earlier educational land grants to new states are distinguished as measures that encouraged settlement and increased the value and sale of remaining federal lands.

Tesla Motors’ unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2016 reported revenue of $1.15 billion, up from $939.9 million a year earlier, while gross margin declined to 22.0% from 27.7%. Net loss widened to $282.3 million, or $2.13 per share, from $154.2 million, or $1.22 per share. Operating expenses rose to $500.7 million, driven by research, development, sales, service, and administrative expansion.

Tesla ended the quarter with $9.19 billion in assets, $8.18 billion in liabilities, and $1.44 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Operating activities used $249.6 million, investing activities used $233.8 million, and financing activities provided $715.4 million. Customer deposits increased to $391.4 million. Inventory was $1.30 billion, and property, plant and equipment totaled $3.59 billion.

Tesla produced 15,510 vehicles during the quarter, including about 2,650 Model X vehicles, and had delivered more than 122,000 vehicles cumulatively. Model X production faced supplier shortages. The company targeted 80,000–90,000 Model S and Model X deliveries in 2016 and planned to support more than 50,000 deliveries in the second half. Model 3 received over 325,000 reservations within one week of unveiling, with volume production and deliveries expected in late 2017. Tesla advanced its target of producing 500,000 vehicles annually to 2018, noting this would be challenging and likely require additional capital.

Tesla expected 2016 capital expenditures to be approximately 50% above its previous $1.5 billion estimate and operating expenses to grow 20%–25%. Planned investments included Model 3 production, Gigafactory equipment, more than 70 retail and service locations, and about 250 Supercharger locations. The Gigafactory began assembling Tesla Energy products in late 2015, with battery cell production expected in the fourth quarter of 2016.

The company identified risks involving production ramps, supplier concentration, international expansion, vehicle resale guarantees, leasing residual values, financing availability, construction costs, and liquidity. As of March 31, Tesla had $565 million outstanding under its asset-based credit facility, of which $350 million was repaid in April. Tesla stated existing liquidity and projected operating cash flows were expected to support its plans through at least the end of 2016.

Allen reported that Kim Ok-kiun, leader of the 1884 revolution and a refugee in Japan, was assassinated in Shanghai by Hong Chong-oo. China transferred Hong and Kim’s body to Korea, where the body was mutilated and distributed around the country. Foreign representatives declined to join Japan in formally opposing the mutilation, limiting themselves to unofficial explanations. Separately, Japanese police forcibly entered the Korean legation in Tokyo to arrest a conspirator after Korean officials refused to surrender him without judicial participation.

Sill reported uprisings in Cholla, Chung-ch’ong, and Kiong-sang provinces against oppressive officials. Some officials and their families were killed, while others were beaten, expelled, or had property destroyed. Korean troops appeared ineffective. At the Government’s request, American missionaries were recalled from the interior, and the King sought an American naval visit to Chemulpo. Sill supported more frequent American ship visits for their perceived moral effect.

UPMSP will announce the 2018 Class 10 and 12 results on April 29 at 12:30 pm through upresults.nic.in and upmspresults.up.nic.in. Students can check using their roll numbers or by SMS to 56263. Class 10 exams ran February 6–22, while Class 12 exams ran February 6–March 12.

Joe Bryant’s Week 10 fantasy football analysis ranks passing and rushing matchups from offense-favoring “Locks” to defense-favoring “Slam Dunks.” Favorable passing situations include New Orleans, San Diego, Oakland, Green Bay, Indianapolis, and Kansas City. Strong rushing matchups include Stephen Davis, the Giants’ backs, Curtis Martin, Edgerrin James, Ricky Williams, and Tampa Bay’s backs. Difficult matchups include Tennessee’s passing game against Pittsburgh, Cincinnati against Baltimore, Eddie George against Pittsburgh, and Charlie Garner against New Orleans. The report also discusses injuries, lineup changes—including Jeff George starting for Washington—and player usage trends, emphasizing that matchups should supplement overall player rankings rather than determine starts alone.

The series has featured tight checking, difficult forechecking, and strong puck handling by Hasek. Frustration over scoring and Detroit’s adjustments contributed to defensive lapses, despite close games and a strong performance by Arturs. The team plans to refocus on tighter defensive-zone play, review mistakes on video, and trust the coaching staff’s lineup changes.

The document defines AMD Versioned Chip Endorsement Key (VCEK) certificates and the Key Distribution System (KDS) interface for SEV-SNP environments. A VCEK is a chip- and TCB-version-specific ECDSA key. Its certificate chain uses a product-specific AMD Root Key (ARK) and an AMD SEV Key (ASK) intermediate authority.

VCEK certificates are generated on request rather than stored in KDS. They are X.509v3 certificates valid from one day before issuance until seven years afterward. Custom extensions identify the product, hardware ID, and TCB security patch levels. Family 19h hardware IDs are 64 bytes, while Family 1Ah Turin and later use 8-byte IDs.

KDS provides a TLS 1.2 HTTP interface at `https://kdsintf.amd.com` for retrieving VCEK certificates, PEM-formatted ARK/ASK chains, and DER-formatted revocation lists. Product names are derived from processor CPUID information and are case-sensitive in URL paths. Requests may receive errors for malformed parameters, unsupported devices, excessive SPL values, or rate limits; clients should honor `Retry-After`.

The service accepts legal future SPL values, allowing customers to pre-fetch and cache certificates for smoother firmware and microcode upgrades.

Russia’s central bank cut its key rate from 9.75 to 9.25 percent, exceeding forecasts, as inflation fell to 4.2–4.3 percent. It signaled gradual further cuts while monitoring inflation, global volatility and a projected oil-price decline.

The invention describes a vehicle sensing and driver-assistance system using a two-dimensional array of radar transmitting and receiving antennas. A controller applies two-dimensional multiple input multiple output (MIMO) processing to create an enhanced virtual antenna aperture, improving simultaneous horizontal and vertical object-detection accuracy and resolution without time-multiplexed scans. An illustrated configuration uses 12 transmitting antennas in three rows and 16 receiving antennas in four columns, functioning as 192 virtual receivers, though other two-dimensional arrangements may be used.

The system processes radar data to detect objects around a vehicle and may support autonomous or semi-autonomous driving, parking assistance, blind-spot detection, cross-traffic alerts, lane-change assistance, emergency braking, pedestrian detection, turn assistance, and intersection collision mitigation. Radar data may be combined with camera images. Upon detecting an object, the system may alert occupants, control vehicle steering or braking, or highlight the object on a display showing rearward, forward, side, or surround-view images.

At 22, Jennifer Thompson was raped and mistakenly identified Ronald Cotton, who was convicted. Eleven years later, DNA testing identified Bobby Poole, who had raped six more women while Cotton was imprisoned. Thompson attributes her error to the fallibility of memory, particularly after trauma and questioning. After Cotton’s exoneration, he forgave her, and they became close friends. Thompson founded Healing Justice, where harmed parties share their experiences, and Cotton regularly attends its retreats.

The Oct. 15 paycheck for 1.3 million active-duty military members could pressure Congress and the White House to end the government shutdown or pass a temporary continuing resolution, Goldman Sachs economists said. Prediction markets indicate a 71% chance the shutdown lasts beyond Oct. 14. If troops are paid through alternative funding or targeted legislation, few other clear deadlines may force a broader agreement. Potential catalysts include TSA disruptions, delayed mortgage payments for service members, expiring Women, Infants and Children benefits, Obamacare enrollment and Thanksgiving travel. Analysts still warn the shutdown could continue into November, while President Trump has threatened to make some temporary layoffs permanent.

On Day 1 of the 2025 World Grand Prix, Rob Cross won a deciding leg, Ratajski defeated the top seed 2-0 with a 95.94 average, Menzies eliminated the eighth seed, and Cullen beat James Wade 2-0 after overturning a 2-0 deficit in the second set.

A report says Minnesota’s Edina School District introduces “white privilege” concepts in kindergarten, including a K-2 Melanin Project focused on skin tone and equality. Separately, Michigan State professor Shreena Gandhi and co-author Lillie Wolff argue that U.S. yoga is linked to white supremacy, colonialism, capitalism, labor exploitation, and cultural appropriation.

Ghana’s major gold miners support new government export certification tests aimed at improving oversight and taxation. The Precious Minerals Marketing Company now observes gold pours, collects assay samples and participates in pre-shipment procedures. Ghana earned $5.78 billion from gold exports last year, while the government says about $5 billion in export revenues to the UAE remain unaccounted for. A ban on small-scale mining remains in place amid efforts to curb illegal mining.

A diverse workforce helps businesses understand global markets, but subconscious biases involving gender, race, and ethnicity can exclude qualified candidates. Studies found hiring and callback disparities affecting women, African Americans, and applicants with non-English surnames. Employers can reduce bias by using behavior-focused language in job postings, removing names from resumes, reassessing rejected applications, and evaluating skills through tests before collecting personal information. Hiring decisions should rigorously compare relevant qualifications while excluding factors such as race and gender. Employers should also examine negative interview impressions to ensure they arise from experience rather than prejudice.

China’s foreign exchange regulator said capital outflow pressure eased somewhat in 2016 and yuan exchange-rate flexibility would increase in 2017. Authorities planned to attract more foreign investment while curbing capital flight. The yuan fell 6.5% against the dollar in 2016. China recorded a $196.4 billion current account surplus, equal to 1.8% of GDP, and a $26.3 billion capital and financial account surplus.

Teach For America argues that high-dosage tutoring can improve student achievement, support teachers and create a pipeline into teaching. Its Ignite Fellowship has trained over 5,500 virtual tutors across more than 40 communities. Reported results include accelerated growth in middle school math and elementary reading.

The program emphasizes structured training, curriculum-aligned coaching and technology that expands rather than replaces relationships. Research cited in the passage found that Ignite tutors were nearly three times as likely to apply to Teach For America’s teacher program, particularly men, people of color and non-education majors. Since Ignite launched, 550 fellows have joined Teach For America’s teaching corps, including 280 new teachers this year. The author concludes that tutoring should be treated as a long-term academic and teacher-recruitment strategy rather than only a response to pandemic learning loss.

The outgoing President thanks his administration and the American people, expresses confidence in the nation, and pledges support for the President-elect and an orderly transition. He describes the Presidency as powerful but constrained by law, public consent, congressional authority, and democratic scrutiny. He warns that special interests can undermine the common good while emphasizing the President’s responsibility to represent the entire nation.

He identifies three global challenges: nuclear destruction, environmental stewardship, and human rights. The United States must remain militarily strong while working with other nations to control and reduce nuclear arsenals. Humanity must also confront pollution, resource depletion, soil erosion, overpopulation, and other threats to the planet through courage and foresight.

He argues that America must defend human rights at home and abroad by opposing deprivation, torture, terrorism, persecution, discrimination, and intolerance, while improving education, medical care, justice, and employment. During an era of tension and scarce resources, the nation must preserve its principles of equality, liberty, and individual dignity. Democracy remains unfinished and must be renewed by every generation.

He closes by reaffirming efforts to secure the freedom of American hostages in Iran and promising to continue working as a citizen for the nation’s founding values.

The 2025 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine was awarded to Shimon Sakaguchi, Mary Brunkow and Fred Ramsdell for discoveries involving regulatory T cells. Sakaguchi identified these cells, which prevent immune attacks on the body, limit inflammation and help prevent fetal rejection. Brunkow and Ramsdell linked a mutation to fatal autoimmune disease in mice and related mutations in humans. Researchers are exploring T-regs as treatments for immune disorders, cancer and other conditions.

A CMOS-compatible hybrid microwave platform was fabricated using 100 nm NbN coplanar-waveguide resonators on n-doped Si/Si₀.₇Ge₀.₃ quantum-well wafers. The chip contained two studied quarter-wave resonators capacitively coupled to a common feedline. Fabrication combined reactive NbN sputtering, electron-beam lithography, dry etching, and a 1 μm deep substrate etch in the CPW gaps. This additional etch relocates substrate–vacuum interfaces and quantum-well charge-noise sources away from high-electric-field regions.

Microscopy showed epitaxial SiGe–Si–SiGe quantum-well layers and oxygenation with reduced crystallinity in the Si cap. Two nominally identical samples had resonances near 5.04–5.60 GHz at 50 mK. Internal quality factors increased with power: sample S1 rose from about 860 in the single-photon regime to 1064, while S2 ranged from approximately 500 to 600. Coupling quality factors remained largely power-independent. Measurements over four cooldowns spanning two years showed no measurable degradation.

Increasing input power produced an upward resonance shift of up to 700 kHz, attributed to saturation of two-level-system defects. Loss modelling indicated that TLS defects contribute to dissipation, but power-independent scattering from structural imperfections, interfaces, and the conductive wafer dominates. Temperature measurements from 150 mK to 1.7 K showed TLS-related behavior at lower temperatures and increasing quasiparticle losses at higher temperatures.

The calculated effective permittivity was 6.35, and an RLC model included geometric and kinetic inductance. The estimated maximum gatemon relaxation time for the present wafer and design was about 14 ns, indicating that improved coupling design, wafer growth, interfaces, doping, roughness, and buffer thickness are needed. The platform’s NbN resonators demonstrated long-term stability, magnetic-field tolerance, and compatibility with Si/SiGe semiconductor processing.

Geary County deputies arrested Fort Riley resident Isaac Torgerson on suspicion of aggravated assault after witnesses reported a pickup passenger waved a gun at another vehicle near US 77. Authorities initially could not locate the truck, but Fort Riley later stopped it at Estes Gate.

Enron replaced CFO Andrew Fastow with former treasurer Jeff McMahon to restore investor confidence amid an SEC inquiry into partnerships Fastow managed. Questions over conflicts of interest, off-balance-sheet financing, a $1.2 billion shareholder-equity reduction, and inadequate disclosure drove analyst downgrades, lawsuits, and steep stock losses. Enron shares closed at $16.41, down 17% that day and roughly half since October 16, while concerns spread to other energy-trading companies. Enron denied wrongdoing and maintained that its operations, liquidity, and financial position remained sound.

Mauricio Pochettino named a largely first-choice 26-player USMNT roster for October friendlies in Austin and Commerce City. Christian Pulisic, who has six goals and two assists for AC Milan this season, headlines the squad. Antonee Robinson returns after knee surgery, while Weston McKennie rejoins for the first time since March. Aidan Morris and Tanner Tessmann earned selection following strong club performances. Several players were omitted because of injuries or selection decisions. All three countries involved have qualified for the 2026 World Cup.

Founded by Jeff Bezos, Amazon launched in 1995 as an online bookstore focused on customer service, discounts, reviews, and convenient ordering. Its 1997 IPO raised $54 million. Over the next 20 years, Amazon expanded into numerous product categories through internal development and acquisitions, including Audible, Zappos, and Quidsi.

Amazon introduced Prime in 2005, Kindle in 2007, and later developed Fire tablets, Fire TV, and Echo devices. Prime evolved from discounted shipping into a broader membership program offering digital content, storage, rentals, and shopping benefits. By 2017, Prime membership approached half of U.S. households. Amazon Web Services began in 2006 by renting excess computing capacity and grew into a major cloud infrastructure business. Some initiatives, including the Fire Phone, Amazon Destinations, WebPay, Amazon Auctions, and premium diapers, failed, reflecting the company’s stated tolerance for experimentation.

Amazon prioritized long-term market leadership and sustainable free cash flow over short-term accounting profits. By its IPO’s 20th anniversary, it was the fourth-largest U.S. public company, with a $458 billion market capitalization and a shareholder return of nearly 64,000%. However, cumulative net income from 1997 through 2016 was only $4.9 billion, with 60% earned in 2015–16.

From 2014 to 2016, net sales rose from $89.0 billion to $136.0 billion, operating income increased from $178 million to $4.2 billion, and net income improved from a $241 million loss to $2.4 billion. Operating cash flow increased from $6.8 billion to $16.4 billion, while free cash flow rose from $1.9 billion to $9.7 billion. In 2016, AWS generated $12.2 billion in sales and $3.1 billion in operating income, compared with retail’s $123.8 billion in sales and $1.1 billion in operating income. Some observers expected Amazon’s GAAP earnings to grow substantially despite its continuing emphasis on long-term investment.

Microsoft’s fiscal 2020 Form 10-K describes its mission to empower people and organizations through software, cloud services, devices, advertising, and gaming. Its strategy centers on productivity and business processes, intelligent cloud and edge platforms, and personal computing. Operations are reported through three segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing.

Microsoft highlights Microsoft 365, Teams, Dynamics, LinkedIn, Azure, Windows, Surface, Xbox, and cloud gaming as major offerings and growth areas. It invests substantially in cloud infrastructure, artificial intelligence, mixed reality, research and development, digital skills, sustainability, and racial equity. The company pledged to become carbon negative by 2030 and remove its historical direct and electricity-related carbon emissions by 2050.

COVID-19 accelerated remote work and digital transformation but created significant operational and economic uncertainty. Microsoft closed offices, restricted travel, and shifted events online.

As of June 30, 2020, Microsoft employed approximately 163,000 people. It held more than 63,000 issued patents and 24,500 pending patent applications worldwide. Its products are distributed through direct sales, original equipment manufacturers, resellers, distributors, and digital marketplaces.

Key risks include intense competition, changing technology and business models, cloud execution, unsuccessful investments or acquisitions, cybersecurity threats, data privacy failures, supply-chain disruptions, and lower margins. As of December 31, 2019, non-affiliate-held common stock had an aggregate market value of $1.2 trillion; 7.57 billion shares were outstanding on July 27, 2020.

The Yankees will start Paul Goldschmidt at first base and bat him sixth in ALDS Game 4 against Toronto, benching Ben Rice. Toronto plans a bullpen game led by opener Louis Varland. Rice could later replace Austin Wells at catcher or pinch-hit against a right-handed reliever.

EIP-7732’s enshrined Proposer–Builder Separation removes trusted MEV-Boost relays and improves scalability through separate payload and blob deadlines. However, it gives builders an approximately eight-second “free option” to withhold data after observing external information, making unfavorable blocks non-canonical without additional protocol penalties. This can produce empty slots, harm network liveness, distort on-chain prices, and impose losses on liquidity providers.

The paper models and empirically studies this risk using Ethereum blocks containing relevant DEX trades from January 2024 to March 2025. Option value and exercise probability rise with volatility, liquidity, option-window length, and reliance on CEX–DEX MEV. With an eight-second window, the estimated average exercise rate is 0.82%, representing 34.6% of missed blocks, but daily missed-block rates can reach 5.5% during volatile periods. Smaller builders heavily dependent on CEX–DEX flow show higher exercise rates, while trailing MEV reduces incentives for consecutive exercises.

Shortening the option window and penalizing builders both reduce exercise probability. Reducing the window from eight to six seconds lowers it by over 33%, while a 0.075 ETH penalty lowers it by roughly 75%. A dynamic penalty mechanism targeting a 0.1% exercise rate achieves 0.096% with an average penalty of 0.104 ETH. These mitigations involve trade-offs: shorter windows reduce scalability, while penalties increase builder capital requirements, entry barriers, and potential blob costs.

After Temu resumed direct shipping from China following a pause and a US-China trade truce, the author placed an order despite concerns about tariffs and duty fees. The package arrived without extra charges, though product quality was mixed. Earlier tariff changes ended the de minimis exemption that supported Temu and Shein’s low prices, prompting both companies to emphasize US-warehouse products. Prices nevertheless increased, with Shein prices reportedly rising about 30% on average.

Donnell Gibson, a behavior intervention specialist and junior varsity basketball coach at Como Park Senior High in St. Paul, helps students address life challenges and uses basketball to teach broader lessons. After surviving childhood homelessness and rescuing a family of 10 from a burning house in 2015, Gibson broadened his goals beyond sports. He founded the Gibson Foundation to mentor young African-American inner-city men through speakers, college tours and basketball, inspired by a high school principal who helped him recognize his potential.

The team held a positive meeting about game-plan adjustments. While physical play remains important, it needs to improve its speed and skating. Strong goaltending kept the last two games close despite subpar performances. Players must prepare mentally, focus on individual roles, and use the home crowd’s energy to deliver their best game.

The passage cautions that market rallies can reverse quickly. Nvidia’s strong earnings were already priced in, prompting a “sell the news” reaction, but its bounce from a rising 50-day trendline signals technical support and potential new highs. Micron’s rally may be brief: shares remain below a bearish 50-day moving average, and the rebound stems from oversold conditions. Resistance near $84 could trigger another reversal. Western Digital is mentioned but not analyzed.

A collection of October 23, 2001 reports describes mounting pressure on Enron. A securities class action alleged Enron and its leaders misrepresented financial results, delayed asset write-downs, and concealed problems in broadband and partnerships managed by CFO Andrew Fastow. The SEC sought information about related-party transactions, while Enron disclosed third-quarter charges of $1.01 billion and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. Its shares fell sharply, investors questioned management credibility and opaque off-balance-sheet financing, and Moody’s considered downgrading its debt. Enron sought a $750 million Citigroup loan and cited available credit lines, but executives provided limited clarification during an investor call. Although most Wall Street analysts retained positive ratings, some downgraded the stock.

A Texas Monthly article traces Enron’s transformation from a pipeline company into a dominant energy trader under Kenneth Lay and Jeffrey Skilling. It credits innovative trading and aggressive recruitment for rapid growth but describes a harsh, short-term culture, subjective accounting, troubled international and broadband investments, California-related criticism, and Skilling’s abrupt resignation.

Separate reports say AES accused the Orissa state government of contract violations, intimidation, interference, and unpaid bills, warning India’s treatment of foreign power investors could undermine confidence.

A February 2001 press roundup covers California’s electricity crisis. Gov. Gray Davis announced a tentative $2.7 billion agreement to buy Southern California Edison’s transmission lines while pursuing broader deals with PG&E and Sempra. Proposed arrangements aimed to stabilize near-bankrupt utilities, repay debts, secure lower-cost long-term power, and avoid consumer rate increases, though negotiations, funding responsibilities, and legislative details remained disputed.

California’s power alerts ended for the first time since January 13 as weather improved, plants returned from maintenance, imports increased, and more electricity was purchased in advance. Officials warned that supplies remained tight and conservation was still necessary. State electricity purchases were projected to exceed $3 billion by mid-March.

Other developments included proposed price cuts from small and renewable generators, potentially saving billions; legislation offering discounts and blackout exemptions near power plants; opposition to an Enron hydroelectric project’s transmission lines; and criticism of expanding political control over the power system. Republicans sought to use the crisis against Davis but lacked a unified alternative, while polling showed continued public support for the governor.

President Trump said back pay for furloughed federal workers during the seven-day shutdown “depends” on the employee. A draft White House memo argued retroactive pay is not guaranteed without specific congressional funding, despite recent administration guidance and a 2019 law stating furloughed employees shall be paid after a funding lapse. The administration’s position is viewed as pressure on Senate Democrats to support a Republican stopgap funding bill. Trump also warned that substantial permanent layoffs could begin if the shutdown continues. Democrats seek an extension of enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits in any short-term resolution. The American Federation of Government Employees called the back-pay argument a misinterpretation of law and urged Congress to end the shutdown.

Donchian Channels, developed by Richard Donchian, use upper and lower bands based on the highest high and lowest low over the previous N bars. Traditionally, traders buy upside breakouts and sell downside breakouts to follow trends.

The passage reports that trend-following applications work better for commodities, currencies, and Treasuries than for stocks, partly because modern stock markets trend less. Curtis Faith’s 1996–2007 tests on non-stock assets produced annual returns of 29.4% and 57.2% for two variations. A long-only S&P 500 test from 1960 to October 2021 returned a 4.57% CAGR, below buy-and-hold’s 7.15%, but with lower drawdowns.

Reversing the indicator into a mean-reversion strategy produced favorable results on SPY from 1993 to October 2021. Several lookback periods performed well, with a 5-day period generating a 9.16% CAGR, small drawdowns, and a high win rate. Donchian Channels resemble Bollinger Bands visually but can produce different backtest results.

Canadian lumber shares fell after BMO downgraded West Fraser, Interfor and Canfor, citing U.S. duties, a stronger Canadian dollar, litigation and little progress in resolving the lumber dispute. BMO expects near-term earnings pressure but sees more positive prospects over three to five years.

Japan’s economy grew an annualised 4% in the second quarter, exceeding expectations, as consumer spending and capital expenditure increased. Strong domestic demand offset lower exports, while Olympic investment also supported growth. The figures may bolster Prime Minister Shinzo Abe’s efforts to combat deflation and slow growth.

Select Security acquired Charlotte-based Intelligent Technology Inc. and Carolina Security Group, adding nearly 1,000 customers, personnel and a downtown branch that will consolidate western North Carolina operations. Founded in 2003, Select Security serves nearly 30,000 customers across nine states.

Hungary’s education system is shaped by its demographic decline, parliamentary government, economy, and longstanding educational traditions. Compulsory schooling currently covers ages six to sixteen, and students progress through primary, secondary, vocational, and higher education. School admissions, examinations, and school-leaving requirements are often rigorous, while families may choose among public and private institutions.

General teacher preparation varies by educational level and specialization. Primary and secondary teachers complete multi-year programs combining disciplinary, pedagogical, psychological, and practical training. Special education teachers complete a four-year university program and specialize in areas such as autism, intellectual disabilities, physical disabilities, sensory impairments, learning disabilities, behavioral disorders, or speech therapy. New teachers undergo a two-year traineeship, and continuing training may affect salary progression.

Hungary established special education institutions beginning in the nineteenth century and has enacted laws guaranteeing educational rights and support for students with disabilities. Placement recommendations are made by professional committees, but parents make the final decision. Available services include early intervention, counseling, therapy, specialized care, and inclusive instruction. In 2019, Hungary had more than 88,000 students with special educational needs, 60% of whom were educated inclusively.

Current challenges include difficult diagnostic procedures, inaccessible school buildings, incomplete inclusion, limited disability-related preparation for general teachers, lecture-focused teaching, low teacher pay, and attrition. The article recommends stronger referral and diagnostic systems, improved accessibility, broader inclusion, expanded teacher training, higher wages and incentives, and adoption of supportive practices associated with higher-retention institutions.

Newcastle University scientists produced the first 3D-printed human corneas using donor corneal stem cells mixed with alginate and collagen. A low-cost bio-printer formed a cornea in under 10 minutes, and the cells subsequently grew. Researchers also printed corneas matching patient-specific eye scans. The proof-of-concept could eventually help address the global shortage of transplant corneas, but further testing is required and clinical use remains several years away.

Texas Gulf beaches are regularly tested for bacteria associated with feces from humans and animals, often carried into ocean water by storm runoff. A Galveston Beach advisory near 57th Street was lifted Friday after samples cleared. Officials advise avoiding water under advisory because ingestion may cause illness. Conditions usually improve within 48 hours. Beach status is available at TexasBeachWatch.com, GCHD.org and posted seawall signs.

The passage identifies archival and published sources on Reagan administration foreign policy, including the papers of Alexander Haig and Donald Regan, State Department files, the Reagan Library, Library of Congress, National Security Council, and major newspapers and journals. It also documents 1980 campaign speeches and statements by Ronald Reagan and George Bush on defense, peace, China and Taiwan, arms control, and foreign policy, with archival citations and related press coverage.

A 70-mile-wide radar mass over Colorado, initially thought to be migrating birds, was identified as swarms of Painted Lady butterflies. The butterflies have recently appeared around Denver and migrate toward northern Mexico and the southwestern US during colder months, following winds and gliding hundreds of miles daily.

VentureWire’s May 16, 2001 edition reports continued venture financing, acquisitions, launches, layoffs and closures. Buzzsaw.com cut 30% of staff while preparing a $20 million round; UGO acquired Bla-Bla.com; EYP Mission raised $57.5 million to separate from its parent; and Flatiron Partners moved into J.P. Morgan Chase offices to reduce costs. Significant financings included STSN’s $66.5 million round, DigiPlex’s $48 million equity and $35 million debt, and Creditek’s $30 million investment. Market difficulties prompted layoffs or shutdowns at WorkingWoman.com, Metiom, Mybiz.com, OnSite Access, Eyecast and eLedger. The issue also covers multiple technology launches, acquisitions, executive appointments and new venture funds, including Invesco’s $150 million EuroMedia fund and Schneider Electric’s $44 million corporate venture arm.

At the University of Virginia, President Reagan praised Thomas Jefferson’s influence on higher education, self-government, religious freedom, and the balance between governmental duties and individual rights. Drawing parallels between Jefferson’s era and the 1980s, Reagan described a global expansion of democracy and free-market economics, along with progress in arms reduction, regional conflicts, human rights, and U.S.-Soviet relations.

Reagan cautioned that fundamental differences with the Soviet Union remained and advocated military strength, candid diplomacy, treaty verification, and sustained Western resolve. He argued that Soviet reforms were not inevitable and credited both Mikhail Gorbachev’s actions and democratic nations’ firmness. He also urged cooperation between Congress and the President while defending distinct executive authority in foreign affairs.

Reagan concluded by invoking Jefferson and John Adams as examples of tolerance, reconciliation, and commitment to self-government. In questions, he advocated judging Soviet reforms by actions, described PLO concessions as a step toward Middle East negotiations, defended resistance to terrorism, encouraged young people to vote, and cited military rebuilding, tax reductions, deregulation, job creation, and renewed national pride as administration achievements. He said he planned to remain politically active after leaving office, while Nancy Reagan would continue her antidrug work.

Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) frequently develops resistance to androgen signaling inhibitors and taxanes, leaving limited treatment options. The passage examines microtubule (MT) dynamics as a functional marker of prostate cancer progression and drug susceptibility. Androgen receptor (AR) variants interact differently with MTs: ARv567 remains taxane-sensitive, whereas AR-V7 shows reduced MT association, persistent nuclear accumulation, and clinical taxane resistance. In isogenic prostate cancer cells, AR-V7 expression increased average MT growth speed from approximately 16–17 to 24.6 μm/min and eliminated the slowdown normally observed near cell edges.

The described computational system tracks fluorescent EB1 or EB3 proteins at growing MT tips in live-cell microscopy. It detects and links comet-shaped signals using image filtering, Kalman tracking, statistical distance measures, and global spatiotemporal clustering, enabling measurement of MT growth, shortening, pausing, catastrophe, and rescue behavior.

The authors propose using MT-dynamics signatures in patient-derived organoids to match individual prostate tumors with effective tubulin inhibitors. Primary prostate organoid culture is complicated by mixed benign and tumor tissue and the tendency of normal epithelial cells to overgrow high-grade tumor cells. Reducing the ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 helped temporarily select resilient high-grade tumor cells because benign cells were more dependent on the inhibitor.

Androgen-independent mCRPC circulating tumor cells may be only slightly larger than leukocytes and therefore missed by size-based detection methods. PSMA labeling and quantitative microscopy can identify these small cells. The passage also discusses AR-independent signaling through FGF, MAPK, GSK3, pVHL, and cytoskeletal regulators. Upregulation of the MT inhibitor Op18/STMN1 was associated with reduced MT polymerization, smaller cellular structures, and possible treatment resistance.

Both abnormally high and abnormally low MT turnover are presented as hallmarks of resistance. ERG expression inhibited taxane engagement with tubulin, while paclitaxel suppressed rapidly growing MTs and reduced overall polymerization rates. In A549 cells, paclitaxel induced circular MT bundles in 83% of parental cells but only 27% of BRCA1-knockdown cells; bundle intensity was also lower after BRCA1 knockdown. Circular Hough transform was used to quantify these responses.

pVHL and GSK3β jointly regulate MT homeostasis. Functional pVHL reduced MT turnover and catastrophe events, while pVHL loss or GSK3β-mediated phosphorylation increased MT dynamics. Serum-starved quiescent cells showed increased MT turnover, which was attenuated by GSK3 inhibition. Different VHL mutations and pVHL isoforms produced distinct MT signatures that could potentially guide selection between MT-stabilizing and MT-destabilizing drugs.

The proposed framework combines live-cell MT measurements, gene-expression signatures, organoid drug testing, xenografts, tissue cultures, and image-based morphology to anticipate and overcome resistance. Potential sensitizing strategies include targeting MT-regulating genes, GSK3 isoforms, pVHL-related pathways, GPX4-dependent persister cells, and AR domains, as well as using NAD+ or other endogenous compounds. The passage emphasizes that tubulin inhibitors have nonlinear, dose-dependent effects, making patient-specific drug and dose selection important. It also proposes organoid–immune-cell co-cultures to screen compounds that enhance tumor-specific T-cell and natural killer-cell activity.

The ICRC launched the nationwide “Pehlay Zindagi: Give Way to Ambulances—Give Way to Life” campaign to encourage motorists to prioritize ambulances and raise awareness of challenges facing ambulance staff. Supported by over 30 organizations, the campaign will use television, radio, social media, a website and public pledges through December 2017. Part of the global Health Care in Danger project, it follows the 2016 “Rasta Dein” campaign, which recorded a 16% impact. Observational studies will assess changes in motorists’ behaviour before and after the campaign.

Mariners-Tigers ALDS Game 3 in Detroit was delayed by rain with the series tied 1-1. Originally scheduled for 4:08 p.m. ET, the Tigers later expected a 7 p.m. start, while the broadcast reported MLB was targeting 7:30 p.m. The game was moved from FS1 to FS2 due to overlap with Blue Jays-Yankees and would also air on MLB Network and the Fox One App.

The Non-Farm Payrolls report, released by the US Department of Labor’s Bureau of Labor Statistics, measures monthly changes in US non-agricultural employment. It is typically published on the first Friday of each month at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time and excludes farm workers, federal employees, private household employees, and nonprofit workers.

NFP is a major indicator of US economic health and can influence Federal Reserve interest-rate decisions. Markets compare reported employment with prior figures and consensus expectations. Stronger-than-expected data is generally positive for the US dollar and stocks but negative for bonds because it may increase expectations of inflation and higher interest rates. Weaker data generally produces the opposite response. The report also affects commodities, including gold and energy.

Backtests found that SPY gained an average of 0.09% from open to close on NFP release days, while TLT averaged a 0.02% loss. SPY’s average return five days after release was negative 0.04%, and bonds also performed poorly afterward. The article concludes that NFP figures are difficult to predict and that its backtests found no reliable trading edge in macroeconomic releases.

Bridgeton National Bank sued Hepner on a $1,400 renewal promissory note originally issued to Kil-Tone Company and endorsed to the bank. Hepner alleged that Kil-Tone obtained the note through fraudulent stock representations and promised not to negotiate or enforce it unless the stock was resold profitably. He sought to attribute knowledge of the fraud to the bank because its cashier, Hitchner, was also Kil-Tone’s treasurer and allegedly participated in the fraud. The trial court excluded this evidence and directed a verdict for the bank. Applying New Jersey precedent that an agent’s knowledge binds the principal only when the principal acting independently would have received notice, the court upheld the exclusion and discharged the rule for a new trial.

This Greater Manchester study developed a reproducible, data-driven method for prioritising AI-detected chest X-ray abnormalities for suspected lung cancer. It compared 1,282 retrospective chest X-rays from patients with confirmed, radiographically visible lung cancer against 13,802 prospectively collected primary-care X-rays analysed in shadow mode. The AI system assessed 124 possible findings, whose prevalence ratios across cohorts informed three prioritisation strategies.

Strategy 1 selected 19 high-risk findings with prevalence ratios above five, achieving 92.82% sensitivity and 87.21% specificity. Strategy 2 included 41 high-risk findings, increasing sensitivity to 97.27% but reducing specificity to 62.68%. Strategy 3 combined prevalence data with clinical judgement and selected 32 findings, achieving 95.87% sensitivity, 79.11% specificity, 4.43% positive predictive value, and 99.95% negative predictive value. The authors considered Strategy 3 the best balance between detecting cancers and limiting unnecessary prioritisation.

The approach enables rapid evaluation before clinical deployment and reduces reliance on expert opinion alone. However, both cohorts came from one region, and performance calculations for the referral cohort assumed a 1% detectable cancer prevalence rather than using individual reference standards. External validation and prospective implementation studies are needed to assess generalisability, workflow effects, reporting delays for non-prioritised conditions, and patient perspectives.

Lower global and U.S. interest rates may support a housing-sector rebound over the next one to four years. Homebuilders and home-improvement stocks have historically outperformed during falling-rate periods, except during the subprime crisis. Lumber tariffs currently favor domestic manufacturers, though trade deals could alter this. Despite loose-lending risks, leverage appears lower than in 2007, supporting a diversified housing-stock approach. The author holds no mentioned securities and provides opinions, not investment advice.

The Appellate Division reversed Solomon Montlake’s first-degree grand larceny conviction and ordered a new trial. The prior jury’s discharge, prompted by the prosecutor’s repeated accusations against defense counsel, was within the trial judge’s discretion and did not establish former jeopardy. Cross-examining an alibi witness about unpaid rent was improper because it did not indicate moral turpitude. More importantly, the trial court wrongly instructed jurors that the alibi had to prove the defendants could not have been at the crime scene. Alibi evidence need only create, with all other evidence, a reasonable doubt about the defendant’s presence; the prosecution retains the burden of proving guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.

The lecture examines pseudorandomness through the eigenvalues of \(n,d,\lambda\) graphs: \(d\)-regular graphs whose nonprincipal adjacency eigenvalues have absolute value at most \(\lambda\). The expander mixing lemma shows that smaller \(\lambda\) yields smaller discrepancies between actual and expected edge counts.

Cayley graphs provide deterministic pseudorandom examples. For the Paley graph on \(\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z\), with \(p\equiv1\pmod4\) and edges defined by nonzero quadratic residues, Fourier-type eigenvectors explicitly diagonalize the adjacency matrix. Gauss-sum calculations show that all nonprincipal eigenvalues are small relative to the degree, establishing the graph’s pseudorandomness. More generally, spectral information for Abelian Cayley graphs corresponds to Fourier coefficients, while representation theory plays an analogous role for non-Abelian groups.

For Cayley graphs, discrepancy and eigenvalue conditions are equivalent up to a constant factor. Specifically, the eigenvalue condition with parameter \(\epsilon\) implies discrepancy with parameter \(\epsilon\), while discrepancy with parameter \(\epsilon\) implies the eigenvalue condition with parameter \(8\epsilon\). This reverse implication fails for general graphs, as illustrated by adjoining a small disconnected clique to a large random regular graph. The proof for Cayley graphs uses group symmetries and Grothendieck’s inequality, which compares a difficult sign-valued bilinear optimization problem with its efficiently computable semidefinite relaxation within a constant factor.

The lecture then addresses how small \(\lambda\) can be when \(d\) is fixed and \(n\) grows. The Alon–Boppana bound states that the second-largest eigenvalue is at least \(2\sqrt{d-1}-o(1)\). One proof uses the Courant–Fischer characterization and carefully weighted vectors supported on distant neighborhoods. A second, slightly weaker proof uses the trace method: even spectral moments count closed walks, whose number is bounded below using walks on the infinite \(d\)-regular tree and Catalan numbers. The quantity \(2\sqrt{d-1}\) is the spectral radius of that infinite tree.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2022 reported net sales of $117.2 billion, down 5% year over year, and net income of $30.0 billion, down from $34.6 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.88 versus $2.10. Foreign-currency weakness contributed to lower iPhone and Mac sales, while iPad and Services sales increased. Sales declined across all geographic segments.

Gross margin was $50.3 billion, or 43.0% of sales, compared with 43.8% a year earlier. Operating expenses rose to $14.3 billion, primarily from higher headcount-related research, development, and administrative expenses. Operating income decreased to $36.0 billion.

At quarter-end, Apple had $346.7 billion in assets, $290.0 billion in liabilities, and $56.7 billion in shareholders’ equity. Cash generated by operations was $34.0 billion. The company repurchased 133 million shares for $19.0 billion and paid $3.8 billion in dividends and equivalents. Commercial paper declined to $1.7 billion, while term debt totaled $109.4 billion.

COVID-related disruption temporarily reduced capacity at Apple’s primary iPhone 14 Pro assembly facility in Zhengzhou, China. Apple also cited inflation, rising interest rates, and currency fluctuations as business risks. The company reported effective disclosure controls, no material changes in internal controls, market risks, critical accounting estimates, or risk factors, and no material impact from settled legal matters.

The October 12, 2000 Haas alumni jobs bulletin lists 20 opportunities in technology, retail, finance, consulting, healthcare, media, education, supply chain, and business development. Positions range from analysts and financial consultants to directors, vice presidents, and startup executives, primarily in California and New York, with additional openings in Colorado, Florida, Nevada, and New Jersey. Many roles prefer or require an MBA and relevant professional experience. The bulletin provides detailed responsibilities, qualifications, and application contacts, promotes Haas career-advisory services, and notes that listed employers and search firms have not been researched by the school.

Rite-Hite’s Uni-Dox Inflatable Shelter accommodates varied trailer configurations by inflating around secured trailers and retracting behind protection before departure. Draft pads, counterweight retraction, controls, and the PitMaster seal help prevent damage, leaks, debris, and pests while preserving full trailer access.

The speaker names the Bird Celtics and Magic Lakers as basketball’s greatest teams, followed by Michael Jordan’s Bulls. He recalls discovering hockey through Birmingham’s Bulls, supporting Ron Hextall and the Flyers, and later attending Blackhawks games. He praises the intensity of Stanley Cup playoff overtime while criticizing the largely uncompetitive NBA playoffs. He identifies Hextall as his favorite hockey player and mentions supporting Seth Jones. Discussing Kevin Durant, he argues that great teammates reduce individual burdens and make the game easier, drawing on his own experience playing with Dan Majerle and Kevin Johnson in Phoenix. He concludes that sustained winning is difficult and ranks teams with multiple championships above one-time winners.

Japan upgraded its business sentiment assessment in April after improved corporate confidence, exports and factory output. Its overall view remained that the economy is recovering gradually despite weaknesses. Consumer spending, capital expenditure and exports showed recovery, while overseas economic uncertainty and financial market fluctuations remained risks.

A Barrio 18 attack on police searching for illegal weapons in San Salvador killed one officer and two gunmen and wounded eight officers. One slain gunman was a gang leader suspected in more than a dozen murders. The wounded officers had superficial injuries; four were released and four were expected to leave within a week.
A 26-year-old Aroland man was charged with assault with a weapon after a 30-year-old injured man died in hospital. Police continue investigating the death, with a postmortem planned.

NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 28, 2018 reported third-quarter revenue of $3.18 billion, up 21% year over year, and net income of $1.23 billion, up 47%. Diluted earnings per share rose 48% to $1.97. Gross margin was 60.4%, while operating income increased 18% to $1.06 billion. Operating expenses grew 28% to $863 million.

GPU revenue increased 25% to $2.77 billion, supported by professional visualization, datacenter and gaming. Tegra Processor revenue declined 3% to $407 million. By market, gaming revenue was $1.76 billion, datacenter $792 million, professional visualization $305 million, automotive $172 million, and OEM and IP $148 million. Cryptocurrency mining demand declined sharply, contributing to a $57 million charge related to prior-generation components and chips.

For the first nine months, revenue rose 40% to $9.51 billion and net income increased to $3.58 billion from $1.93 billion. Operating cash flow was $2.85 billion. At quarter-end, NVIDIA held $7.59 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, with total assets of $13.66 billion and liabilities of $4.18 billion.

NVIDIA returned $1.13 billion to shareholders during the first nine months through $855 million in share repurchases and $273 million in dividends. The board authorized an additional $7.00 billion for repurchases and increased the quarterly dividend to $0.16 per share.

The company reported ongoing patent litigation but recorded no related accrual because liabilities were considered possible rather than probable. Management concluded that disclosure controls were effective, and no material changes occurred in internal controls or previously disclosed risk factors.

Comcast abandoned its pursuit of most Twenty-First Century Fox assets, citing insufficient engagement to make a definitive offer. Disney remains the sole suitor for the $40 billion-plus deal, which sources said could be reached this month. The assets include Sky and India’s Star network.

Using U.S. death certificate data for non-Hispanic Black and White people under age 85 from 1999–2020, researchers assessed racial differences in excess mortality and years of potential life lost (YPLL), stratified by sex, age, and cause of death.

Compared with White people, Black females experienced an estimated 658,356 excess deaths and 34.9 million excess YPLL, while Black males experienced 1.15 million excess deaths and 47.0 million excess YPLL. Disparities declined through the early 2010s but then plateaued. In 2020, coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic, excess mortality and YPLL rose sharply, largely eliminating prior gains.

Heart disease produced the highest excess mortality, while perinatal deaths produced the highest excess YPLL. Disparities were especially pronounced among infants: Black-White mortality and YPLL rate ratios exceeded 2.3 for children younger than one year. Excess mortality generally increased through adulthood, while YPLL disparities peaked earlier.

The study proposes excess deaths and YPLL as publicly reported measures for tracking health equity. It concludes that persistent racial mortality disparities warrant national attention and new strategies, while noting possible inaccuracies in death-certificate race and cause-of-death data.

Thirty-seven Cadwalader lawyers, including 10 incoming partners, are joining Orrick offices in Charlotte, London, Washington, D.C., and New York. Cadwalader has experienced significant partner departures amid lagging revenue growth and market-sensitive finance practices, though it retains strong profitability, brand recognition, and desirable talent. The firm is responding by adding a second managing partner and hiring lawyers to strengthen core practices.

APP_CMD (CMD55) marks the immediately following command as application-specific; defined, undefined, and illegal ACMDs are distinguished through response handling and APP_CMD status, with special rules for ACMD41. CMD56 is unspecified in the simplified specification.

CMD6 checks or switches card functions across six groups, including access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. Mode 0 reports support, readiness, and maximum current or power; Mode 1 changes selected functions. CMD6 returns a 512-bit status block containing supported functions, selections, busy states, and power consumption. Version 1.10 or later cards must support CMD6. Power Limit defaults to 0.72 W and may be raised according to host supply, thermal, connector, and card requirements.

High-Speed mode provides a 25 MB/s interface at 50 MHz and is optionally selected with CMD6. Reserved command-system commands can acquire standard, vendor-specific, or extension-defined behavior. CMD8, issued in Idle state before ACMD41, verifies host voltage and returns an R7 response echoing the accepted voltage and check pattern.

ACMD41’s CCS bit identifies SDSC versus SDHC/SDXC. SDSC uses byte addressing and CMD16-selected block lengths; SDHC and SDXC use fixed 512-byte blocks and block addressing, without partial or misaligned access.

Hosts may alter or stop the clock subject to transaction-completion and ACMD41 restrictions. CRC7 protects commands and most responses; CRC16 protects data blocks. CRC or illegal-command errors prevent execution and set status bits.

Read, write, and erase operations have defined timeout rules. High-capacity reads use at least 100 ms; writes generally use 250 ms, with some SDXC cases allowing 500 ms and UHS-II data bursts allowing one second.

Commands are fixed 48-bit words and belong to capability classes. Responses include R1/R1b, R2, R3, R6, and R7. Cards expose Card Status, 512-bit SD Status, and queued Task Status. SD Status reports features including protected area, speed classes, allocation-unit sizes, erase timing, performance enhancements, and command queue support.

Speed Class, UHS Speed Grade, and Video Speed Class methods characterize recording performance. Allocation Units contain Recording Units, and performance depends on sequential writing, fragmentation, file-system updates, and interface conditions. SDXC requires entirely free AUs for Speed Class performance and does not support move performance. CMD20, mandatory for SDXC and optional for SDHC, identifies recording start, directory updates, and continuous-information updates so cards can maintain Speed Class behavior.

U.S. colleges are increasing security and restricting campus access ahead of demonstrations marking the second anniversary of Hamas’s Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israeli civilians. Columbia requires advance protest plans and suspended some guest passes, while the University of Maryland limited access to campus ID holders. Pro-Palestinian events and other demonstrations are planned nationwide.

The passage documents AMD AGESA software interfaces for processor and platform initialization, event logging, memory management, suspend/resume, host call-outs, and build customization.

- Event-log routines return the oldest circular-buffer entry, including status, application-specific event information, and four data parameters. Multiple entries may relate to one error; zero EventInfo indicates an empty log.
- Structure-management routines allocate and release parameter-block storage. Published entry functions are the only interfaces assured to remain available.
- Boot initialization proceeds through ordered stages. Reset performs minimal per-core initialization, configures FCH options and up to three aligned execution-cache regions, and distinguishes BSP and AP tasks. Early initialization configures links, PCIe, graphics, processor power management, platform settings, and may request a warm reset. Post initialization discovers and configures memory, transfers pre-memory artifacts, and prepares processors and memory for host control. Environment initialization moves HOB/artifact data into host-managed permanent memory. Later stages configure graphics and generate ACPI, DMI, P-State, WHEA, IVRS, CRAT, and CDIT data before OS boot.
- Cache-region requests must obey address, alignment, size, boundary, and processor-resource limits. Violations may be adjusted, rejected, and logged. The host must not alter cache controls during Cache-As-RAM operation.
- Platform parameters cover core leveling, C-states, boost, power and frequency limits, connected standby, IO APICs, VRMs, PCIe topology, graphics, display, FCH, SATA, IDE, USB, audio, IOMMU, and power-failure behavior.
- Memory controls include interleaving, ECC, timing, frequency, refresh, power-down, UMA, memory context restoration, capsule preservation, DIMM technology, AMP overclocking, training modes, voltage controls, and memory limits. Initialization reports memory boundaries, holes, cacheable ranges, system limit, DDR voltage, and status conditions.
- Ready-to-Boot routines save critical and volatile silicon context for suspend. Resume routines restore memory from self-refresh, processor registers, and silicon state in stages before OS re-entry.
- Required host functions allocate, locate, and free buffers; initiate warm or cold resets; read DIMM SPD data where applicable; and dispatch tasks to APs. Optional hooks support IDS data, heap relocation, memory timing and voltage changes, PCIe resets, video reposting, FCH customization, and platform-specific controls.
- Most procedures require a previously established stack, and multicore phases require the host to avoid interfering with core communication.
- Customization is provided through platform build settings, modification of initialized structures, IDS controls, and timed call-outs. Build options remove unneeded code for memory types, ECC, training, power features, tables, processor families, sockets, S3, and related functions. Build configuration elements define motherboard limits and defaults without changing code size, including VRM capabilities, CPU frequency, PCI MMIO, IO APIC count, and ACPI table content.

A simple moving average (SMA) continuously averages an asset’s closing prices over a specified period. It indicates trend direction, smooths volatility, and may identify support and resistance. Short-period SMAs respond quickly and generate more signals but can create whipsaws; long-period SMAs are smoother, lag more, and produce fewer signals. A rising SMA suggests an uptrend, a falling SMA a downtrend, and a flat SMA a sideways market.

Backtests indicate short-term stock movements tend toward mean reversion: buying when price crosses below a short SMA and selling after it crosses above can be profitable. Longer-term results favor trend following by buying above a long SMA and selling below it. The best reported result came from buying above the 200-day SMA and holding for 200 days, averaging 10.93% per trade without reinvested dividends. A 200-day strategy returned 7.89% with a 28% maximum drawdown.

Unlike the equally weighted SMA, the exponential moving average gives greater weight to recent prices and reacts faster. SMAs can lag, produce false signals in volatile or range-bound markets, and misrepresent seasonal or cyclical patterns. Traders can adjust periods, combine multiple SMAs, or use other indicators. No SMA period is universally best; settings should be backtested for each asset.

Tesla Motors filed a Form 8-K reporting that it issued a press release on April 3, 2015, furnished under Items 2.02 and 7.01. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. Chief Financial Officer Deepak Ahuja signed the filing.

Yahoo is in advanced talks to sell AOL to Milan-based Bending Spoons for about $1.4 billion, though no deal is final. Bending Spoons, which recently agreed to acquire Vimeo, could gain AOL’s growing younger audience and advertising reach.

Tesla delivered a record 497,100 vehicles in the third quarter, exceeding estimates as buyers sought the expiring $7,500 EV tax credit. Berkshire Hathaway agreed to buy Occidental Petroleum’s chemical business for $9.7 billion in cash, while Occidental plans to use most proceeds to reduce debt.

September job-cut announcements fell 37% from August, but year-to-date cuts were the highest since 2020. Planned hiring was down 58% year over year and at its lowest year-to-date level since 2009.

Caterpillar shares rose 32% year to date as investors anticipated AI-related demand for its turbines, mining equipment and construction machinery. Wedbush expects AI spending pressures to accelerate acquisitions of smaller technology firms, identifying Tenable, Qualys, SentinelOne, Elastic and C3.ai among potential targets. Music labels are also negotiating licensing arrangements for AI-generated music and model training.

The President thanks his predecessor and presents the inauguration as a new beginning rooted in enduring principles, spirituality, liberty, justice, mercy, and humility. He calls for renewed unity, trust, faith in the American dream, and cooperation between citizens and government. Domestically, he urges competent and compassionate government, equality of opportunity, human rights, fair laws, environmental preservation, dignity, and resistance to poverty, ignorance, and injustice. Acknowledging national limits, he advocates sacrifice for the common good and strength at home as the basis for influence abroad. In foreign policy, he pledges adherence to American moral standards, support for freedom and human rights, sufficient strength without needless combat, and efforts to build a just and peaceful world. He also commits to limiting armaments and moving toward eliminating nuclear weapons. He hopes his presidency will help restore confidence and foster lasting peace based on shared values rather than warfare.

The disclosure describes multicarrier wireless communication and scheduling for LTE and 5G systems. It covers OFDM resources, carrier aggregation, dual and multi-connectivity, timing advance groups, random access, PUCCH groups, LTE/5G interworking, centralized and distributed gNB architectures, network slicing, and licensed-assisted access with listen-before-talk.

Base stations and wireless devices may communicate over multiple carriers using configurable protocol layers, serving cells, master and secondary cell groups, and timing-aligned carrier groups. Logical channels may be mapped to selected cells, transmission-time intervals, numerologies, and priorities according to bearer and quality-of-service requirements. A MAC logical-channel-prioritization procedure may allocate grants and multiplex channel data into MAC protocol data units.

A UE may be configured with multiple downlink and uplink bandwidth parts, each defining parameters such as subcarrier spacing, cyclic prefix, resource blocks, and control-resource sets. DCI or higher-layer signaling may select active bandwidth parts. Timers may return a UE to a default bandwidth part after inactivity, while common control-resource sets can reduce switching and synchronization problems. Bandwidth-part configuration may support bandwidth adaptation, load balancing, paired or unpaired spectrum, control-channel monitoring, random access, paging, and pre-emption indications.

The DAWn-Plasma study was a multicenter, randomized, open-label phase 2 trial comparing standard care plus convalescent plasma with standard care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Participants were allocated 2:1; 489 were randomized and 483 formed the full analysis set, with 320 in the plasma group and 163 controls. Plasma recipients were assigned four units totaling 800–1000 mL, administered in two sessions within 48 hours. The median administered volume was 884 mL, and 80.7% of units had neutralizing-antibody titers of at least 1/320.

At Day 15, the proportion alive and free of mechanical ventilation did not differ between groups: 83.7% with plasma versus 84.1% with control (odds ratio 0.99; p=0.976). No statistically significant differences occurred in mortality or other secondary endpoints. Adverse events, fatal events, and serious adverse events were similar between groups. Transfusion-related effects occurred in 19 of 320 plasma recipients, with no reported TRALI cases.

Neutralizing-antibody titers increased by Day 6, but the intervention did not influence this increase. Higher baseline and Day 6 titers correlated with better outcomes. The trial concluded that early administration of four high-titer plasma units did not significantly improve clinical status or alter the natural course of hospitalized COVID-19. The study followed ethical approval, informed-consent, Good Clinical Practice, and Declaration of Helsinki requirements.

San Francisco State University’s Department of Biology will host Personalized Medicine 10.0 on June 2, 2017, in partnership with SF State Alumni and the City of South San Francisco. Titled “Has It Changed Your Life?”, the conference will review a decade of developments and predictions in personalized, genomic and precision medicine while considering future scientific and business directions. Topics include bioinformatics, oncology, epigenetics, rare diseases, sequencing, the microbiome, gene therapy, genome editing, regulation and ethics. Keynote speaker Amylynne Santiago Volker will discuss genetic sequencing’s life-saving potential and barriers to routine clinical use, including provider training, interpretation and insurance coverage. Founded by Michael A. Goldman and SF State alumni Dan Maher, Ken Hitchner and John Wulf, the annual conference brings together scientists, professionals and students. Registration is open to researchers, executives, health professionals, students and the public.

Averaging down means buying additional shares after a price decline, reducing the average purchase price and the subsequent rise needed to break even. The breakeven price equals total purchase cost divided by total shares, excluding trading fees. It does not erase losses; the price must still recover to the new average cost.

The strategy can support a planned scale-in approach, particularly for long-term investors who understand the company or traders using a backtested system. However, buying solely because a price has fallen can increase exposure and losses if the decline continues. Short-term traders may struggle to distinguish temporary declines from major downturns and often favor strict loss limits. Averaging up instead adds to positions as prices rise, though reversals can still cause losses.

A backtest on SPY used RSI signals, divided capital into two equal purchases, and sold the entire position upon a sell signal.
