Averaging down produced nearly the same ending capital as the non-averaging strategy but delivered smoother performance, improved trading metrics, reduced drawdowns, and more efficient capital use.

The passage considers stocks the most suitable market for averaging down because they tend toward mean reversion. Other markets may be less mean-reverting, making backtesting and a margin of safety important.

Therapeutic antibodies require effective binding and developability properties such as thermostability, low hydrophobicity, and strong expression. Because wet-lab optimization is costly and datasets are small, Bayesian optimization can guide iterative refinement, though its success depends on surrogate models and acquisition functions. Prior work has not adequately examined structural information, particularly when antibody-antigen binding poses are unknown. This work investigates how structural information can be incorporated into Bayesian optimization, which tasks benefit, whether antibody-specific structural models outperform general protein models, and whether structure is necessary. It also proposes a protein language model “soft constraint” for sequence-only prior information. Bayesian optimization iteratively uses an uncertainty-aware surrogate model and acquisition function to balance exploration and exploitation when optimizing expensive black-box functions.

Cleveland police sought Steve Stephens, 37, suspected of fatally shooting Robert Godwin Sr., 74, and posting the incident online. Stephens cited ex-girlfriend Joy Lane, who expressed condolences and described him as kind and generous. Officials were investigating his unverified claim of killing more than a dozen people.

Aberdeen Emerging Markets Equity Income Fund, Inc. resulted from consolidating seven funds into the Aberdeen Chile Fund and was renamed effective April 30, 2018, trading on NYSE American as AEF. It follows a multi-cap emerging-markets equity-income strategy, seeking current income and long-term capital appreciation by investing at least 80% of assets and investment borrowings in emerging-market equities. Leverage was permitted but not then used. As of May 25, 2018, its largest holdings included Tencent Holdings at 6.45%, China Mobile at 2.96%, SAIC Motor at 2.59%, and two Samsung Electronics preferred positions totaling 5.07%. Cash and equivalents represented 5.81%. A tender offer and special capital-gains distribution totaling approximately 41% of April 27 assets could alter the portfolio. Figures were unaudited, holdings subject to change, and investment value and market price may fluctuate.

Valeant Pharmaceuticals shares fell 0.3%, closing at $16.73. Eighteen analysts set an average 12-month price target of $16.75, ranging from $8 to $35. Its average brokerage recommendation is 2.83, with 3 Buy, 2 Outperform, 7 Hold, 6 Underperform and no Sell ratings. The stock’s 14-period Average True Range is 0.7, weekly volatility is 3.31%, monthly volatility is 3.81%, and RSI is 43.3. Valeant has a $5.85 billion market capitalization and 349.76 million outstanding shares. Previous trading volume was 7.02 million shares, below the 13.9 million average.

SpaceX will deliver Hewlett Packard Enterprise’s “Spaceborne Computer” to the International Space Station. Capable of one trillion calculations per second, it could process high-resolution satellite data aboard the station, reducing the amount transmitted to Earth. Unlike traditionally hardened space computers, it uses commercial hardware and specialized software designed to respond to hazards such as radiation. After startup and initial testing, scientists will evaluate it for a year. Continued operation could support deploying more powerful computers and eventually aid Mars missions, where communication delays or outages would require astronauts to process data and solve problems independently.

London-St. Thomas unemployment rose slightly to 5.5% in September, while the labour force shrank by 3,000 and was down 9,300 year over year. Only 75% of residents aged 25-54 were working, the lowest among 15 major Ontario cities. A King’s University College study found only half of working adults had permanent full-time jobs with benefits; others held precarious positions. Such work was linked to stress, depression, anger, poor health and diminished family life, with young people and minorities particularly affected. National unemployment remained at 6.2%, while Ontario employment increased by 35,000 and unemployment fell to 5.6%.

A study of 2,097 Project Baseline Health Study participants compared chest radiograph-based biological age (CXR-Age) with Horvath Age and DNAm PhenoAge epigenetic clocks. Epigenetic clocks correlated more strongly with chronological age than CXR-Age, while CXR-Age acceleration was not significantly associated with either epigenetic age acceleration.

Higher CXR-Age and DNAm PhenoAge acceleration were associated with greater coronary artery calcium, poorer pulmonary function, frailty, and disability. CXR-Age showed broader associations across cardiopulmonary and physical-function measures and remained informative in adults as young as 45. Horvath Age was not significantly associated with these outcomes. Proteomic analysis identified significant associations between CXR-Age acceleration and CDH13 and ApoD; DNAm PhenoAge was associated with 13 proteins, including CDH13. Radiographs with high CXR-Age acceleration often showed lung abnormalities, prior thoracic surgery, or pacemakers, although some had no clear explanatory findings.

The findings suggest CXR-Age and DNAm PhenoAge capture different aspects of biological aging. CXR-Age could potentially support opportunistic screening and age-based medical decisions using routinely acquired chest radiographs. Limitations include the retrospective observational design, absence of longitudinal outcomes, possible residual confounding, uncertain generalizability, limited comparison with newer aging clocks, and poor interpretability of the deep-learning model. The study was funded by Verily Life Sciences, and all authors reported institutional research grants from Verily.

Researchers demonstrated that limiting a nutrient needed by malaria parasites can harness competition between drug-sensitive and drug-resistant strains. In mice receiving traditional drugs, providing the nutrient caused treatment failure in 40 percent of cases due to emerging resistance, while limiting it prevented infections from rebounding. Resistant parasites survived nutrient restriction when alone but failed to grow when competing with sensitive parasites, even when initially numerous. The proof-of-principle suggests resource-limiting interventions could extend existing drugs’ usefulness and prevent resistance to new drugs. Further research must identify resources disproportionately needed by resistant strains and determine effective intervention methods and timing.

This preprint describes PhenoID, a transformer-based pipeline that extracts abnormal dysmorphology findings from electronic health record text and maps them to Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms. Researchers created a manually annotated corpus of 3,826 observations from 1,655 individuals, containing 935 HPO terms. Four clinical genetics physicians annotated findings, achieving an average inter-annotator F1 score of 0.844.

PhenoID uses a Bio-ClinicalBERT sequence labeler to identify finding spans and a separate transformer classifier to normalize them to HPO identifiers. The pipeline addresses overlapping, disjoint, and negated mentions using two BIO-labeling heuristics. Its training data included annotated observations and generated examples based on HPO preferred terms and synonyms.

PhenoID achieved an F1 score of 0.717 for normalization, outperforming six comparison systems; with gold-standard spans, performance increased to 0.820. The Noisy-BIO approach performed better overall than Recast-BIO. The system correctly normalized 45.9% of disjoint terms, 44.5% of overlapping terms, and 30% of terms that were both. It incorrectly treated only 1.6% of negated findings as abnormal.

Major normalization errors involved ontology imperfections, descriptive wording, misplaced model attention, and prediction of broader HPO terms. Span extraction reduced overall performance, while the model also showed limited semantic understanding. The authors note limited author diversity as a dataset limitation and suggest improving extraction and normalization with future NLP advances. Data and source code are publicly available.

A prospective hospital-based study assessed surgical diagnoses and postoperative outcomes among adults undergoing laparotomy for suspected acute intestinal obstruction at three Dar es Salaam regional referral hospitals from December 2021 to July 2022. Participants were followed from surgery to discharge. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and multivariable logistic regression.

The study included 228 patients, 75.4% male, with a median age of 34 years and median hospital stay of four days. Adhesions were the most frequent diagnosis (98 cases), followed by hernia (48), volvulus (37), and abdominal tumors (20); some patients had multiple diagnoses. Of the participants, 173 (76%) were discharged home, 20 (9%) developed superficial surgical-site infections, two had wound dehiscence, one had an anastomotic leak, eight were referred elsewhere, and 12 (5.3%) died. Outcomes were unknown for 12 patients. No significant hospital-level differences, confounding, or interactions were identified.

The authors concluded that adhesions were the leading diagnosis, contrasting with reports that hernias predominate in developing countries, though referral bias may have influenced this finding. They highlighted the male predominance, mortality rate, and unknown outcomes as areas requiring further study, including assessment of socioeconomic factors and risks among older adults. The authors reported no conflicts of interest.

The royal commission exposed widespread misconduct by bank and AMP financial advisers, including false witnessing, conflicted advice, insurance rorts and fees for no service, despite years of whistleblower testimony, scandals and parliamentary inquiries.

Children’s cell phone ownership varies widely by country and age. In Germany, 51% of children ages 6 to 13 have a mobile phone, often not a smartphone. Across seven European countries, 46% of children ages 9 to 16 owned smartphones, with differences in school restrictions and internet affordability. In the United States, 45% of children ages 10 to 12 had smartphones with service plans, while 42% of children 8 and younger owned tablets.

In South Korea, 72% owned smartphones by ages 11 to 12. Taiwanese cell phone use rose from 45% among 11-year-olds to 71% among 15-year-olds. Turkish parents most commonly identified ages 12 to 17 as the appropriate period for getting a phone. Ownership or access also varied substantially across South Africa, Ghana, Malawi and Australia.

The American Academy of Pediatrics says there is no single correct age for a child’s first phone. It recommends limited media use for young children, monitoring content and apps, avoiding screens before bedtime and during meals, and not relying solely on media to calm children.

The Renewable Energy Alaska Project and Southeast tribes are training residents of Kake, Angoon, Hoonah, Yakutat and Metlakatla to conduct affordable household energy assessments. The $25 assessments identify low-cost efficiency improvements, such as replacing bulbs with LEDs and reducing appliance electricity use, offering an alternative to private audits costing thousands of dollars. Though these changes do not address communities’ reliance on diesel, they may reduce household electric bills by nearly 10 percent and ease financial burdens. The Home Energy Leader Program runs through July 31.

The passage describes methods, apparatuses, systems, and computer-readable media for near-real-time classification of objects represented by 3D point clouds, including those generated by chirped or phase-coded LIDAR. LIDAR determines range from optical signals and can generate point clouds representing object surfaces.

The classification method extracts surface normals to establish translation- and rotation-invariant coordinate systems, then derives feature variables. Two classifiers independently estimate an object class: one may use spin-image statistics with dimensionality reduction and nearest-neighbor searching, while another may use covariance matrices clustered by class. If their classifications disagree, an iterative closest point classifier compares the input point cloud only with model point clouds for the proposed classes. The selected class can guide a device, such as a display, vehicle, or projectile system. Objects may also be labeled outside all predefined classes.

The disclosed LIDAR apparatus includes a laser source, modulator, splitter, optical couplers, detector, and processor. Both heterodyne and homodyne chirped configurations are described, along with beat-frequency range calculation, point-cloud generation, k-d tree searches, occluded models, and general computing hardware.

Experiments classified cones, boxes, pipes, cubes, pistols, and similar toy guns. Reported results showed high classification rates, including 100% for several classes and lower rates of 87% to 97% for more similar objects.

Commercial property owners in Southern Nevada have been charged trash fees that municipal ordinances appear to require local lawmakers to approve. Las Vegas plans to introduce an ordinance codifying several fees already charged by Republic Services, the region’s exclusive trash collector. Fees include commercial container delivery, removal and exchange charges and an industrial dry-run fee. Officials generally could not recall approving them, while a waste-services manager said the unapproved charges could total thousands of dollars per client. Republic says it annually reports supplemental service fees to municipalities and considers that process approval. Las Vegas and North Las Vegas officials cited their ordinances without further comment; Henderson said the charges may violate its ordinance and will investigate, while Clark County said commissioner approval is unnecessary.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended April 1, 2017 reported quarterly net sales of $52.9 billion, up 5% year over year, and net income of $11.0 billion, up from $10.5 billion. Diluted earnings per share rose to $2.10 from $1.90. Gross margin was $20.6 billion, or 38.9% of sales, while operating income was $14.1 billion. For the first six months, net sales were $131.2 billion and net income was $28.9 billion.

Quarterly iPhone revenue increased 1% to $33.2 billion despite a 1% decline in units. Mac revenue rose 14%, Services rose 18%, and Other Products rose 31%, while iPad revenue fell 12%. Sales increased in the Americas, Europe, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific, but declined 14% in Greater China. Currency weakness reduced results in several markets.

At April 1, 2017, Apple had total assets of $334.5 billion, including $256.8 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. Total liabilities were $200.5 billion, including $88.5 billion of term debt and $10.0 billion of commercial paper. Six-month operating cash flow was $39.6 billion. Apple spent $18.0 billion on share repurchases and $6.1 billion on dividends and dividend equivalents during the period, while issuing $11.0 billion of long-term debt in the second quarter.

Research and development expense increased to $2.8 billion for the quarter, and selling, general and administrative expense rose to $3.7 billion. Apple forecast third-quarter gross margin of 37.5% to 38.5%.

Apple had $8.8 billion of gross unrecognized tax benefits. It appealed the European Commission’s decision requiring Ireland to recover up to €13 billion plus interest. The company also disclosed supply-chain concentration, foreign exchange, legal, tax, competitive, and component-availability risks.
TCI Fund Management valued Zodiac Aerospace shares at 7–10 euros after its first-half loss and urged Safran to abandon its bid, arguing any offer above 10 euros would destroy value.

Guinness will partner with former Arsenal footballer Thierry Henry for its Made of Black campaign in Nigeria and across Africa. Henry, an acclaimed player with multiple league, FA Cup and individual awards, will highlight people who embody the campaign’s spirit. Launched in 2014, Made of Black celebrates African attitudes and achievements. Guinness will also engage football fans through Fanzone events, live football and music experiences, rewards, and continued sponsorship of EPL broadcasts on DStv.

The work develops a computationally efficient embedded atom method potential for ternary tungsten–hydrogen–helium systems to simulate radiation damage in fusion reactor plasma-facing components. It targets light-gas binding to vacancies and voids, defect relaxation volumes, tungsten surfaces, and gaseous interactions. Existing potentials can inaccurately represent bubbles, voids, surface energies, or relaxation volumes.

The new potential extends Mason’s W–H model with helium interactions using a generalized Finnis–Sinclair formulation that permits negative electron-density contributions. Its loss function compares predicted and DFT-derived defect formation energies, relaxation volumes, binding energies, and gaseous configuration energies, emphasizing physically important defect properties. Optimization combines parallel parameter-space sampling through Gaussian mixture models with local Simplex minimization.

Training data primarily come from published DFT studies, supplemented by new VASP calculations for hydrogen–helium defect clusters. Physics-informed priors and spline functions enforce stable short- and long-range behavior, including agreement with the Ziegler–Biersack–Littmark model during close atomic collisions.

The tungsten–helium interaction is constrained to reflect weak helium adsorption on metals. Helium’s embedding function models repulsion from both positive and negative electron densities. The helium–helium potential balances experimental low-pressure virial coefficients with DFT energy and stress data for high-pressure hexagonal close-packed helium, improving descriptions of small helium clusters. Hydrogen–helium interactions are fitted to DFT dimer data and defect properties while preserving vacuum behavior. Charge-density analysis is used to assess whether the selected functional forms qualitatively represent electronic interactions involving helium in tungsten.

Dell CEO Michael Dell said AI computing demand remains “tremendous,” with no current signs of excess data-center construction. Dell’s server networking business grew 58% last year and 69% last quarter. The company expects to ship $20 billion in AI servers in fiscal 2026, double last year’s sales. Dell raised its annual revenue growth target to 7%–9% and earnings-per-share growth target to 15%, sending shares up more than 3% Tuesday.

This preprint used bidirectional and multivariable Mendelian randomization with European GWAS data to assess causal relationships among 211 gut microbial taxa, 1,400 plasma metabolites, and fibromyalgia. Four taxa—Enterobacteriaceae, Butyricicoccus, Coprococcus1, and Enterobacteriales—were associated with reduced fibromyalgia risk, while Eggerthella and Ruminococcaceae UCG005 were associated with increased susceptibility; no reverse causality was detected.

The analysis identified 82 fibromyalgia-associated plasma metabolites. Enriched pathways included caffeine and α-linolenic acid metabolism and GLP-1/incretin synthesis, secretion, and inactivation. Protective metabolites included AFMU, eicosapentaenoic acid, and stearidonic acid, while 7-methylxanthine, 1-methylxanthine, and Oleoyl-EA were described as risk-associated. Mediation analysis indicated that 2,3-dihydroxypyridine and palmitoylcholine potentially mediated associations of Enterobacteriaceae and Enterobacteriales with fibromyalgia, accounting for 14.91% and 12.34% of effects, respectively.

The authors propose dietary strategies involving reduced caffeine and oxalate intake, increased omega-3 consumption, and a low-glycemic-index diet. Limitations include unavailable demographic data, predominantly European ancestry, and the need for experimental and clinical validation.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell-based GeForce RTX 50 Series introduces FP4 support in fifth-generation Tensor Cores, reducing generative AI model memory requirements and improving performance. FP4 cuts FLUX.dev’s VRAM use from over 23GB to under 10GB with virtually no quality loss using advanced quantization.

Fourth-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and add hardware support for Mega Geometry and Linear Swept Spheres. Mega Geometry enables full-fidelity ray tracing of detailed, dynamically changing geometry through cluster-level acceleration structures, batched GPU-driven BVH management, and partitioned top-level acceleration structures. It supports DirectX 12, Vulkan, OptiX 9.0, and all RTX GPUs, with Blackwell-specific acceleration. Linear Swept Spheres render strand-like geometry such as hair about twice as fast as triangle-strip methods while using about five times less VRAM.

Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 improves thread coherence and neural-shading performance with twice as efficient reorder logic. The RISC-V-based AI Management Processor moves GPU-context scheduling from the CPU to the GPU, reducing latency and coordinating concurrent AI and graphics workloads.

Blackwell adds hardware encoding and decoding for 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC video. Ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality, adds AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, and supports multiple encoders; the RTX 5090 offers over 50% faster exports than the previous generation. Sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed. DisplayPort 2.1b provides up to 80Gbps and supports 8K at 165Hz or 4K at 480Hz with compression.

Max-Q improvements include finer power, clock, and voltage-rail gating, memory power management, clocks that adapt 1,000 times faster, and deep-sleep entry ten times faster than Ada. These changes can reduce power consumption by up to 50% in small-language-model inference examples.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame. Its model is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and employs GPU-based Flip Metering for smoother pacing. New transformer models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA use twice as many parameters as prior CNN models and improve temporal stability, motion detail, lighting, anti-aliasing, and ghosting.

Blackwell expands neural shading through Cooperative Vectors APIs for DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Applications include neural materials, texture compression, radiance caching, subsurface scattering with RTX Skin, and generative face rendering with RTX Neural Faces. Neural Texture Compression reduces material memory use, while Neural Radiance Cache approximates multi-bounce indirect lighting from limited path-traced rays.

The flagship GB202 GPU contains 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, and 768 Tensor cores, and powers the RTX 5090. GB203 contains 45.6 billion transistors and 10,752 CUDA cores for the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 contains 31 billion transistors and 6,400 CUDA cores for the RTX 5070.

The patent describes implantable medical devices, particularly cochlear implants, designed to manage torque on implanted magnets during exposure to external magnetic fields such as MRI fields. A magnet is enclosed within a body and positioned between structural components, such as plates. Initial magnet rotation pushes the components apart, tensioning elastomeric material or resilient elements that resist further separation and limit rotation. Alternative configurations use springs, rails, rigid housings, shaped plates, tracks, bumpers, and low-friction surfaces. The magnet may revolve within a sealed container while remaining constrained against excessive rotation. An elastomeric housing may also include a slit permitting magnet insertion or removal. The teachings may apply to other hearing prostheses, pacemakers, stimulators, and implantable devices containing magnets.
The appellants’ appeal from two 2008 Supreme Court orders was unanimously withdrawn pursuant to the parties’ January 11, 2010 stipulation.

The passage lists QuantifiedStrategies.com articles on market timing, including regime indicators, SuperTrend, PENTAD, Fabian, Coppock Curve, Yale Hirsch’s Best 6 Months, Sy Harding’s seasonal strategy, and Bitcoin timing. The strategies range from simple seasonal or trend-following models to complex systems using multiple indices, with articles covering rules, backtests, performance, and risk. The site is managed by experienced independent traders Hakan Samuelsson and Oddmund Groette.

The agreement sets minimum quantities for Congo products while allowing further purchases based on requirements and stocks. Prices are to be agreed between Belgium and the purchasing British or U.S. government, with payments made through customary methods. Britain may protect purchased goods from customs treatment less favorable than British colonial products. Britain and the United States will seek to supply the Congo within wartime limits, while Belgium will prohibit transactions aiding enemy powers and coordinate Congo export licensing with British-administered African territories. The agreement takes effect upon signature.

The U.S. State Department accepted possible revision following Belgian territorial liberation, requested agreed Belgian-British prices and transaction details, and emphasized incentives for maximum production. It questioned paying for unshipped commodities still in the Congo, preferred transfer against warehouse receipts at export points, rejected guaranteed shipping, and supported moving unfinished transactions into the new agreement. It also proposed giving Britain and the United States options on the entire output of listed products and adding provisions for Congo production development.

The article backtests three candlestick patterns—Bearish Engulfing, Three Outside Down, and Bullish Harami—on the SPY ETF from its 1993 inception to October 2021. Trades invest 100% of equity and exit when the daily close exceeds the previous day’s high.

Despite its traditional bearish label, Bearish Engulfing produced the strongest bullish results: 296 trades, a 0.53% average gain, 5% CAGR, 71% win rate, 16% maximum drawdown, and 2.5 profit factor. Three Outside Down generated 112 trades, a 0.7% average gain, 2.3% CAGR, 78% win rate, 14% maximum drawdown, and 2.6 profit factor. Bullish Harami produced 306 trades, a 0.33% average gain, 3.1 CAGR, 76% win rate, 25% maximum drawdown, and 1.65 profit factor.

The authors conclude that these patterns performed reasonably well, although most candlestick patterns lack predictive value in their tests and may benefit from additional variables.

David Moyes urged relegation-threatened Sunderland to create more chances for Jermain Defoe and improve collectively. Bottom of the league and seven points from safety, Sunderland face Watford, Leicester City and Manchester United in eight days.

Turkish prosecutors issued detention warrants for 133 current and former Finance and Labor Ministry personnel over alleged Gülen movement links and use of ByLock; four were active employees. Separate operations detained 14 women, at least 18 dismissed teachers, 19 military personnel, nine people in Adana and seven in a Bitlis-based investigation. Turkish authorities consider ByLock a communication tool used by Gülen followers. The government blamed the movement for the July 15, 2016 coup attempt, which killed 249 people; Fethullah Gülen denied involvement and requested an international investigation. Since the attempt, the Justice Ministry reported 50,510 arrests and legal proceedings involving 169,013 people, while more than 150,000 public employees have been suspended or dismissed.

Leaked benchmarks show Nvidia’s $3,000 Titan V outperforming the Titan Xp and GTX 1080 Ti despite lower boosted clock speeds. Its Volta architecture, HBM2, and 652.8 GB/s memory bandwidth deliver strong synthetic and 1440p gaming performance. Designed mainly for AI, prosumers, and developers, it signals potentially more affordable Volta cards ahead.

Microsoft’s Board amended its proxy access bylaw on September 20, 2016. Changes clarified when fund groups count as one shareholder, extended the recall period for loaned shares from three to five business days, removed a recall requirement at nomination notice, clarified indemnification provisions, and reduced the voting support required for candidate re-nomination from 25% to 15%. Microsoft also scheduled its 2016 Annual Shareholders Meeting for November 30, with September 30 as the record date. The amended bylaws were filed as Exhibit 3.2.

DNA from Vancouver Aquarium belugas Qila and Aurora, which died from an unidentified toxin in 2016, enabled researchers to sequence a highly complete beluga genome. The genome will support research and conservation by providing insights into traits, evolution and environmental adaptation.

Erie Federal Credit Union reopened the former Glenwood School as its corporate headquarters and ninth branch after an 18-month renovation. The 42,000-square-foot facility offers full banking services, a drive-through, community room and space for future growth. The locally completed project preserved school and community history, returned the property to tax rolls and revitalized a previously unused structure.

Citadel Securities hired Societe Generale’s Anthony Cronin to lead European Treasuries trading, expanding coverage across Europe, parts of Asia and the Middle East. It also hired Michele How for fixed-income sales and is targeting clients in Hong Kong, mainland China and Japan. Since launching direct investor market-making in 2016, Citadel has grown to more than 450 counterparties and nearly quadrupled average daily volume. Treasury trading reached $6 trillion in 2017, driven largely by off-the-run securities. The firm plans to add inflation-protected securities and strips, potentially enabling it to seek Federal Reserve primary-dealer status.
Dwyane Wade, Gabrielle Union and Zion Wade visited Miami’s Frost Museum of Science, enjoying a planetarium show, marine exhibits and food. Wade also rebuked a Twitter critic.

RSI, ADX, and IBS are technical indicators used for short-term mean-reversion and trend-following strategies. RSI measures price momentum on a 0–100 scale, with values above 70 generally indicating overbought conditions and below 30 indicating oversold conditions. Stock backtests favored short RSI periods of two or three days.

ADX measures trend strength but not direction. Backtests suggested periods of 5–10 days and strong-trend thresholds around 30–40. IBS measures the close relative to the price bar’s high and low, ranging from 0 to 1; low values are bullish and high values bearish.

Individual backtests produced positive results, but ADX added greater value when combined with other indicators. A combined strategy on SPY averaged 0.86% per trade while invested 14% of the time, and its only losing year was 2018. On QQQ, it averaged 1.3% per trade with no losing years since 2000. The passage emphasizes backtesting, simplicity, and that no trading strategy guarantees profits.

Developed by Marc Chaikin in the 1980s, the Chaikin Oscillator measures market momentum and accumulation or distribution. It is calculated by deriving money flow volume and the Accumulation/Distribution Line, then subtracting a longer exponential moving average from a shorter one. Positive values indicate buying pressure or accumulation, while negative values suggest selling pressure or distribution. Bullish and bearish divergences and zero-line crossings may signal potential reversals but require confirmation.

Quantified S&P 500 tests found limited predictive value. A strategy buying above zero and selling below produced a 2.4% CAGR over 20 years. Reversing those rules yielded 287 trades, a 0.54 average per trade, a 1.76 profit factor, and a 37% maximum drawdown. Two RSI-based strategies each generated 216 trades averaging 0.3%, with a 1.6 profit factor and maximum drawdowns of 18% and 17%. Overall, none of the ten tested strategies showed significant profitability, though other criteria might produce different results.

Marine Le Pen’s prospects in France’s presidential election may benefit from François Fillon’s payroll scandal and unrest following a young black man’s alleged rape by police. Riots involving many immigrants and minorities have led to burned cars, attacks on authorities, and nearly 250 arrests. Reports suggest disturbances across towns near Paris may be broader than officially disclosed, though no firearms have been reported. With immigration tensions already high, Le Pen’s anti-immigrant, tough-on-crime platform and support for police could attract wary voters if violence escalates. While her victory remains considered unlikely, the unexpected outcomes of Brexit and Donald Trump’s election counsel against ruling it out.

Leon Cooperman believes the bull market is in a late, riskier stage marked by stretched valuations, momentum-driven investing, and “ridiculously high” AI company valuations. The S&P 500 has risen nearly 40% since April lows, while the Buffett Indicator reached 217%, signaling market exuberance. Despite stock risks, Cooperman considers government bonds riskier because inflation erodes their fixed returns.

University of Kansas researcher Brock Ternes surveyed 864 Kansans and found that well ownership was significantly associated with increased watering during droughts, with conservation practices varying by well type. Although well owners tend to be more aware of water supplies, many use groundwater during droughts to sustain crops when precipitation is inadequate. Ternes argues that resource use during scarcity does not necessarily contradict environmentalism, but groundwater stewardship requires selective timing of extraction. His research treats well owners as a distinct social group whose drought responses matter, particularly as over-pumping threatens the High Plains Aquifer’s ability to support irrigation wells in parts of southwestern Kansas within 25 years.

Zach Parise and Andy Greene said the team remained confident despite frustration over home losses and missed scoring chances. They emphasized converting opportunities, reducing turnovers, improving power-play entries, passing and shooting, and maintaining strong execution against an opponent that forechecks hard and has an effective penalty kill. Road travel could help by limiting distractions and restoring routine, while shorter travel and extra rest may benefit the team as the series continues. Video review reinforced that the team had controlled play and generated offensive-zone time, even when goals were not coming. Both expected the team to refocus and produce a stronger effort.

Big Brothers Big Sisters of Mercer County paired seven children awaiting mentors with Trenton police officers, FBI agents and community members to assemble and test new bicycles. Each team also built a bicycle for donation through Capital K-9. The grant-funded event promoted teamwork, mentoring and stronger ties between children and law enforcement.

Major school districts have approved union contracts with teacher raises despite lacking sufficient funding. Philadelphia agreed to 3% annual raises but sought authorization to borrow up to $1.5 billion amid delayed state funding, with the impasse adding about $15 million in interest costs. Chicago approved a $1.5 billion union contract while facing a $734 million deficit, later balancing its budget through refinancing and other measures.

Baltimore County rescinded a scheduled 5% raise after reduced federal relief and insufficient local funding, then renegotiated a 3.05% increase. Fairfax County received less than half the requested funding for promised raises and revised its first collective bargaining agreement in nearly 50 years.

Nationwide public-school debt increased from $415 billion in 2013 to more than $586 billion in 2023. Expiring pandemic aid and funding shortfalls have strained district budgets and forced borrowing or contract renegotiations.
Tippecanoe Middle School released its principal’s list and honor roll for sixth-, seventh-, and eighth-grade students for the second grading period of the 2017–18 school year.
SEC establishes 32-bit C execution and a stack via AMD_ENABLE_UEFI_STACK. Two PEIMs control AMD initialization; one initializes processors and publishes AmdCpuEarlyInit PPI.

The disclosure describes methods and apparatus for HARQ ACK/NACK feedback in wireless networks where a user equipment communicates with multiple transmission reception points (TRPs). A base station may configure per-TRP PDCCH monitoring occasions, indicate whether feedback bundling across TRPs is permitted, provide bundling rules, and specify whether downlink assignment indices are joint across TRPs or independently maintained by each TRP. The UE uses these configurations, received DCIs, monitoring occasions, timing, and DAIs to determine the ACK/NACK codebook size and feedback content. It may transmit joint bundled feedback over PUCCH/PUSCH or separate PUCCH feedback to individual TRPs. Bundling rules can account for whether TRPs transmit the same payload for diversity or different payloads. Joint DAIs count grants across TRPs and carriers, while independent DAIs count grants separately for each TRP and may require the UE to combine counts. The disclosure also outlines implementations in hardware, software, computer-readable media, base stations, and UEs within LTE or 5G NR communication systems.

The disclosure describes an autonomous vehicle management system designed to improve the safety of autonomous vehicles and machines. Using data from onboard or remote sensors, the system maintains a three-dimensional internal map representing the vehicle, surrounding objects, and environmental conditions. It combines this map with goals, localization information, safety constraints, route information, and operational history to generate and execute plans through steering, braking, propulsion, auxiliary, or specialized equipment systems.

The system uses artificial intelligence techniques, including convolutional neural networks for object detection and reinforcement learning for action selection. It simulates multiple “what-if” scenarios by modifying internal-map parameters, such as object speed, direction, or distance, to evaluate possible future conditions and eliminate unsafe actions. Decision trees may be pruned according to the goal, and map regions relevant to a maneuver may be represented in greater detail.

The system can dynamically control sensors by changing their field of view, resolution, collection rate, communication rate, data volume, or operating state. This allows it to request detailed information when needed while reducing unnecessary data and resource use.

Additional safety mechanisms include confidence scores measuring how closely inference data resembles AI training data, enabling unreliable predictions to be rejected or overridden. Reinforcement-learning actions may be evaluated with a safety indicator and interrupted when unsafe. The system can also present planned actions and their reasons to passengers, remote users, or nearby entities, supporting awareness and manual intervention.

The architecture includes sensor-interface, localization, perception, planning, control, and information subsystems, implemented locally or remotely in software, hardware, or both.

CompareCards presents partner credit cards featuring introductory 0% APR periods of 6–21 months, cash back or travel rewards, sign-up bonuses, and often no annual fee. Offers from Discover, Bank of America, Citi, Capital One, and others carry varying post-intro APRs, transfer fees, spending requirements, and reward limits. The site explains fixed versus variable rates, advises reviewing application terms, and states issuer compensation does not influence its data-driven ratings.

Swiss Economic Affairs Minister Johann Schneider-Ammann said ministries would consider arms industry requests to extend export licences and permit sales to countries in internal conflicts. Industry cites declining exports, competitive disadvantages and threatened jobs. Critics argue easing rules would violate Swiss neutrality. The government may propose amending the War Material Ordinance.

VentureWire’s November 17, 2000 issue reports extensive venture financing, acquisitions, executive appointments and fund activity. GovWorks cut staff amid restructuring and a possible sale, while Whitney & Co. planned a $2.5 billion global fund. eHitex appointed Robert Lewis CEO, and PlanetOut agreed to merge with Gay.com parent Online Partners.

Major funding rounds included Workscape’s $45 million, Brodia Group’s $30 million, CriticalArc Technologies’ $29 million, RAW Communications’ $27 million, Symmorphix’s $25 million and Tridium’s $20 million from Enron and kRoad Ventures. BeautyJungle closed, TheStreet.com planned to shut its U.K. venture, and GiftCertificates.com withdrew its IPO while raising $13 million in debt.

Acquisitions included Intuit’s $39 million purchase of EmployeeMatters and TeleCommunication Systems’ planned $65.2 million stock acquisition of Xypoint. Dresdner Kleinwort Benson launched a $125 million Japan technology fund, while Netyear Group planned a venture arm focused on wireless business-to-business companies.

C-BerryTrans is a GNU GPL 3.0 C++ program for ab initio calculation of Berry curvature, anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC), and anomalous Nernst conductivity (ANC) from WIEN2k outputs. It directly uses DFT eigenvalues and momentum-matrix elements in the Kubo formula, avoiding Wannier interpolation and its dependence on high-quality Wannier functions. AHC is obtained by Brillouin-zone integration weighted by the Fermi–Dirac distribution, while ANC uses entropy-based weighting.

The program requires spin–orbit-coupled WIEN2k calculations because the transverse responses vanish without spin–orbit coupling. It generates dense full-Brillouin-zone k-meshes, calculates band-resolved Berry curvature, and stores results in compact binary files. OpenMP parallelization distributes Berry-curvature and transport calculations over k-points, while batch processing limits RAM usage. Stored curvature data enables rapid post-processing over user-defined temperature and chemical-potential ranges without repeating the main calculation.

Users configure crystal structure, spin polarization, k-mesh, thread count, energy windows, temperatures, chemical potentials, and target property through an input file. The workflow modifies WIEN2k inputs, generates and divides k-point lists, extracts eigenvalues and momentum matrices, computes curvature, and produces AHC or ANC results. A Python visualization module plots Fermi- or entropy-weighted Berry curvature.

The intrinsic formalism is most appropriate for clean to moderately dirty systems and lower temperatures; it excludes extrinsic scattering mechanisms that may affect dirty systems or room-temperature measurements. The code was tested on Fe, Pd, Fe₃Al, and Co₂FeAl and is designed for scalable, interpolation-free materials studies.

Markets shifted decisively risk-off after a week of earnings, economic data, tariff developments and political uncertainty. Major indexes fell 2.2%–4.2%, forming bearish engulfing patterns as volume, market internals and most sectors weakened.

Second-quarter earnings generally exceeded expectations, with 82% of reporting S&P 500 companies beating EPS estimates and 79% surpassing revenue estimates. Earnings revisions also rose. However, investors sold into strong results amid doubts about continued growth and limited new buying.

GDP grew 3%, above the 2.5% expectation, but tariff-related import volatility distorted the data, while weak personal spending indicated softer demand. Payrolls increased by 73,000 versus 100,000 expected, with substantial downward revisions to prior months. The unemployment rate edged up to 4.2%.

The FOMC had two dissenting votes, while Chair Powell emphasized patience amid inflation, tariff and labor-force uncertainty. Markets assigned over 75% odds to a September rate cut and expected three cuts by January. Bond prices strengthened as economic slowdown concerns increased.

Utilities were the only sector to rise, while transports, retail and regional banks weakened. Short- and intermediate-term indicators remained risk-off, though some measures approached moderately oversold levels. Longer-term earnings expectations continued to suggest improving growth into 2026.

World stocks rebounded as fears of a U.S.-North Korea nuclear confrontation eased, following their largest weekly losses of 2017. European and Asia-Pacific shares rose, U.S. futures indicated a higher opening, and market volatility declined. Investors returned focus to solid corporate earnings and global growth.

The dollar strengthened against the yen and Swiss franc as demand for safe-haven currencies weakened. Japanese stocks nonetheless fell 1 percent despite 1 percent second-quarter economic growth, amid concerns over the yen’s recent appreciation.

Signs of global recovery raised questions about whether U.S. and euro zone central banks could reduce stimulus. U.S. and German bond yields rose from recent lows, while investors awaited Federal Reserve and European Central Bank meeting minutes. Chinese markets were largely unaffected by weaker-than-forecast but still solid economic data, though the figures weighed on oil prices.

UBS will continue increasing dividends and execute a USD 2 billion share buyback through 2027 despite regulatory pressure for higher capital buffers. CEO Sergio Ermotti said Credit Suisse integration is progressing, with Swiss systems consolidation expected by early 2026, and that capital requirements can be met without restricting shareholder returns. Analysts view the strategy as demonstrating financial strength but warn worsening markets could complicate the balance between regulatory compliance and investor expectations.

The Single/Double Offense uses double and down screens to free shooters, requiring defenders to disrupt screens, deny passes, and protect against post mismatches. NBA teams generally prefer “show and recover” rather than switching: defenders influence shooters away from preferred areas, show hard on screens, chase shooters, recover to screeners, deny passes, pressure the ball, and pack the weak side. Post mismatches may be trapped.

An aggressive SOS alternative uses sequential contact switches and wing traps to disrupt planned routes. The on-ball defender pushes the point guard toward the sideline, while other defenders deny shooters and screeners. When the ball reaches a wing, defenders double-team the receiver, front the post, block reversal passes, and rotate into help positions. Rotations must occur as the pass leaves the passer’s hands, with additional traps used on post entries or baseline drives.

The passage proposes a hybrid method for multiscale electromagnetic problems involving detailed antennas and electrically large environments such as radomes, reflectors, or biological tissue. Unlike earlier MoM–T-matrix approaches, the environment is discretized using the method of moments (MoM), while the antenna is represented by a compact generalized scattering matrix (GSM). This reduces unknowns, supports reuse of antenna data, and enables translation, rotation, and array synthesis operations.

The framework can also produce fully coupled GSM–physical optics variants for large reflectors and GSM–T-matrix variants for structures suited to spherical-wave expansions. It is intended to combine full-wave accuracy, computational efficiency, and modular modeling.

For a penetrable structure containing an antenna, the total field is decomposed into incident, structure-scattered, and antenna-generated fields. Equivalent electric and magnetic surface currents on the structure are determined through PMCHWT integral equations, RWG basis functions, and Galerkin-tested MoM. Antenna fields are expanded in outgoing spherical vector waves, while fields incident on the antenna from external currents use regular spherical waves. Coupling matrices connect the MoM currents and spherical-wave coefficients. The antenna GSM then maps free-space and guided-mode excitations to radiated and waveguide responses through port, receiving, transmitting, and scattering matrices.

Reykjavik experienced its grayest, wettest May and June since 1914, while high pressure brought heat to Britain and Scandinavia and redirected clouds and rain toward Iceland. Reykjavik received only 70 hours of June sunshine, with temperatures peaking below the monthly average, after rain fell every day in May. Repeatedly worsening forecasts fueled disappointment and increased demand for beach holidays and tanning salons, while outdoor businesses struggled. Tourism was only slightly affected, as campers generally adapted; some visitors preferred Iceland’s cool weather. Conditions recalled June 1914, when heavy rain compounded Reykjavik’s poor roads and sewage system. Residents nevertheless expressed hope that the weather would improve.

Apple’s 2019 Form 10-K reports fiscal-year net sales of $260.2 billion, down 2%, and net income of $55.3 billion. Lower iPhone sales were partly offset by growth in Services, iPad, and Wearables, Home and Accessories. Services sales rose 16% to $46.3 billion, while iPhone sales fell 14% to $142.4 billion. Apple repurchased $67.1 billion of stock and paid $14.1 billion in dividends and equivalents.

Apple designs and sells smartphones, computers, tablets, wearables, accessories and related services. It had approximately 137,000 employees and generated 69% of sales through indirect distribution channels. Its principal risks include intense competition, supply-chain concentration, economic and currency fluctuations, product defects, cybersecurity and privacy incidents, legal and regulatory matters, dependence on third parties, and rapid technological change.

Russian authorities rejected Captain Scullun’s claimed $45,000 in lost whaling profits as exaggerated and requested vouchers for other claims, proposing $2,500 as sufficient compensation for losses caused by the Cape Horn Pigeon’s temporary detention. Scullun reported that a Russian naval officer seized the American vessel near Sakhalin while it was cruising for whales, alleging illegal whaling in the closed Sea of Okhotsk, and that the crew was taken to Vladivostok and left without food or shelter. U.S. chargé d’affaires George W. Wurts requested an investigation and assistance for the crew while expressing doubt about the deprivation claim. Russian officials stated that Scullun had declined offered lodging and food, announced the vessel’s release, and said the inquiry into the crew’s treatment would continue.

Louisville officials warn that neighborhood fireworks create particle pollution, worsening air quality and respiratory conditions. Airborne and exploding fireworks are illegal within city limits. Citywide use of smaller fireworks can pollute more than the official display; smoke last exceeded federal limits in 2015.

The court held claims 1–3 of Curtis and Cook’s portable elevated railroad patent invalid because uncontradicted testimony established prior use of a substantially similar railway in 1866. Claim 4, covering an overhead main track combined with branch tracks, a switch, and a traveler, remained presumptively patentable and was infringed by the defendant’s structure. The court authorized a decree for the plaintiff concerning claim 4.
Justice Wolfe filed the court’s opinion on April 7, 1932.

Kenyon College’s student-led Whiteness Group aims to educate students about white privilege, allyship, and anti-racist action. Founder Juniper Cruz said the group seeks sustainable activism beyond social media. Its rules encourage unpopular opinions but prohibit white participants from directing questions to people of color, requiring them to seek answers themselves, and discourage sharing meeting comments. About 50 students attended the first meeting, and college chaplain Rachel Kessler said shame and fear are unproductive in combating racism.

DDR memory controller terminals use per-byte data strobes to synchronize 32-bit bus transfers, acting as outputs during writes and inputs during reads. DQS[3] serves bits [31:24], while DQS[0] serves bits [7:0]. Pins operate from DVDD_DDR[0] or DVDD_DDR[1]. Internal pullups or pulldowns are enabled during reset and generally disabled or switched after reset. DDR[1] DQM signals correspond to specific byte lanes.

The Supreme Court appeared sympathetic to counselor Kaley Chiles’s challenge to Colorado’s ban on conversion therapy for minors. Chiles argues that the law discriminates against her viewpoint by preventing her from helping clients pursue certain goals involving sexuality or gender identity. Lower courts upheld the ban as regulation of professional conduct subject to rational-basis review.

Colorado defended the bipartisan law as regulation of a narrow medical treatment associated with serious harm, while Chiles and the Trump administration argued that speech-based therapy deserves stronger constitutional protection. Justices debated Chiles’s standing because Colorado has not enforced the law against her, whether the measure regulates treatment or speech, and whether it constitutes viewpoint discrimination. Several suggested that, if strict scrutiny applies, lower courts should evaluate the law under that standard rather than the Supreme Court striking it down immediately.

He recalls disappointment after falling short in the finals but happiness for his brother. Playing together strengthened their bond on and off the ice. His line’s success comes from continuity and trust, while strong goaltending has been crucial for both teams.

The lecture reviews the Weierstrass M-test: a series of functions converges uniformly when each term is bounded by a corresponding term of a convergent numerical series. This establishes uniform convergence and continuity for an example involving cosine functions.

Applying the M-test to power series shows that a power series converges uniformly on every closed interval strictly inside its radius of convergence. Consequently, it may be integrated term by term there. Its formally differentiated series has the same radius of convergence, allowing term-by-term differentiation. Repeated differentiation is also valid, and evaluating derivatives at the center gives \(f^{(k)}(x_0)=k!a_k\).

The lecture then proves the Weierstrass approximation theorem: every continuous function on \([0,1]\) is the uniform limit of polynomials. It first reduces the argument to functions vanishing at both endpoints, which can be continuously extended by zero outside the interval.

Normalized polynomials
\[
q_n(x)=c_n(1-x^2)^n
\]
are introduced on \([-1,1]\). They are nonnegative, integrate to one, and converge uniformly to zero away from the origin. A bound \(c_n\leq\sqrt n\) helps establish this concentration property.

For a continuous function \(f\), the approximating polynomials are defined by
\[
p_n(x)=\int_0^1 f(t)q_n(t-x)\,dt.
\]
After a change of variables, these act as approximations to the identity, concentrating the integral near \(t=0\) and thus near \(f(x)\). Uniform continuity and boundedness of \(f\), together with the concentration estimates for \(q_n\), show that \(p_n\) converges uniformly to \(f\).

A citizen-science study collected 50 household tap-water samples from 32 administrative regions across 19 Chinese provinces/regions between December 2020 and August 2021, including samples following the 2021 Henan floods and Typhoon In-Fa. Student volunteers used standardized low-cost kits to filter, freeze, and transport samples. Researchers extracted DNA and conducted 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding.

Microbial DNA was detected in 22 samples, yielding 7,635 amplicon sequence variants and revealing diverse tap-water microbiomes. Mycobacterium, Acinetobacter, and Legionella were found in all PCR-positive samples. Samples collected after extreme weather contained pathogenic species, including Salmonella enterica, and toxin-producing cyanobacteria such as Microcystis. The study presents citizen science as a cost-effective supplement to professional drinking-water monitoring in China, while noting limited sampling. The preprint has not been peer reviewed.

President Trump’s address emphasized nationalism, sovereignty, self-government, and patriotism over globalism. He argued that strong, independent nations should prioritize their citizens, preserve their cultures, protect their borders, and cooperate through mutual respect.

Trump highlighted U.S. economic growth, employment gains, energy production, military investment, and efforts to make allies share defense costs. He defended trade reforms, including agreements with Canada, Mexico, Japan, and the United Kingdom, while accusing China of unfair trade practices and supporting major changes to the World Trade Organization. He expressed hope for a fair agreement with China and urged it to protect Hong Kong’s freedoms.

On security, Trump defended sanctions against Iran, called for its denuclearization and an end to its regional aggression, and promoted normalized relations between Israel and its neighbors. He also urged North Korea to denuclearize, pledged continued counterterrorism and peace efforts in Afghanistan, and stated that the United States seeks cooperation rather than permanent enemies or endless wars.

Trump described illegal migration as harmful to migrants and nations, condemned human smuggling, defended border enforcement, and praised regional cooperation. He supported democratic change in Venezuela, Cuba, and Nicaragua and denounced socialism and communism as systems serving ruling elites.

He also addressed threats from foreign technology, social media censorship, bureaucratic power, and attacks on national traditions. He affirmed support for free speech, LGBTQ people facing criminal punishment, women’s economic empowerment, religious liberty, opposition to taxpayer-funded abortion, and Americans’ right to bear arms.

Trump concluded that liberty, democracy, peace, and progress depend on citizens devoted to their nations, urging leaders to honor their histories, cultures, and people while building stronger and more prosperous countries.
Sixteen years after a border-area crash left an unidentified Mexican youth in a vegetative state, a Facebook photo led relatives to wonder whether “Pancho” was Gilberto.

Dr. Pasvolsky said respect for international obligations was inherent in the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals but could be explicitly included. Honduras supported a treaty-respect provision, while Chile disputed that the principle was clearly established in international law. After correcting a statement misattributed to Venezuela, the previous meeting’s minutes were approved.

Discussion then addressed Security Council composition. Pasvolsky said the Council must be both effective and representative. Permanent membership for five countries reflected their military and industrial power and willingness to bear major responsibilities. Nonpermanent members should outnumber permanent members so the latter could not decide matters alone. Although League of Nations Council membership had reflected geographic representation, Pasvolsky advised against prescribing selection rules because other criteria had been proposed. He expected the American republics to remain represented.

Chile opposed repeating positions already summarized because the meetings would not make decisions. Brazil argued that Latin America should have permanent Council representation and emphasized the organization’s preventive purpose; participants requested that these remarks be recorded.

Quarters coverage uses four deep and three underneath defenders, with cornerbacks covering No. 1 receivers, safeties reading No. 2 receivers and supporting the run, outside linebackers defending the flats, and the middle linebacker covering the hook area. Its blend of zone and man-style responsibilities allows defenses to respond quickly.

Offenses commonly attack quarters coverage through the flats and open deep middle. Hitch routes can stress flat defenders, while play-action and three-level concepts exploit aggressive safeties and create downfield one-on-one matchups. Routes that draw safeties away from the middle allow receivers and tight ends to fill the vacated space. Overload concepts, such as double posts combined with a wheel route, also strain coverage assignments.

Five examples include BYU’s play-action double verticals with an X sluggo, Kansas State’s stick concept with a backside option route, Ohio State’s shallow sting, Georgia’s double-post Y leak, and Wake Forest’s play-action slot cross. These plays use safety manipulation, linebacker conflicts, crossing routes, checkdowns, and coverage rotations to create opportunities.
Caffeine content varies by coffee chain. Reported amounts per ounce are 9 mg at McDonald’s, 12.7 mg at Dunkin’ Donuts, 16.7 mg at Peet’s, 20.6 mg at Starbucks, and 54.2 mg in Deathwish coffee.

In Morris v. Scott, Morris sued for malicious prosecution after Scott allegedly caused his arrest and trial without probable cause; Morris was acquitted. The lower court nonsuited Morris because his declaration did not allege jurisdiction in the magistrate or special sessions court. On appeal, the court held that malicious prosecution may be maintained despite a lack of jurisdiction when malice and falsehood form the gravamen and arrest or imprisonment is alleged as a consequence. The offered evidence should therefore have been admitted. The judgment was reversed and a new trial ordered, with costs to abide the outcome.

The post-election stock rally faces risks from historically high valuations and uncertainty over the Trump administration’s ability to deliver tax cuts, infrastructure spending and deregulation. Failed healthcare legislation raises doubts about implementing policies expected to boost corporate earnings. Meanwhile, confidence indicators have surged, but actual economic data remain weaker, with first-quarter growth forecast at 1.2 percent and earnings estimates rising more slowly than before the election.

Federal Reserve officials have described asset prices as rich or frothy, raising the possibility of faster interest-rate increases. Historically, current valuation levels have predicted poor equity returns, only marginally above bonds. The rally therefore depends heavily on substantial policy implementation, but comprehensive tax reform appears unlikely. Piecemeal measures, such as foreign cash repatriation that may fund share buybacks, are more probable than a broad return to stronger growth and inflation.

Child care academies in at least 11 North Carolina counties provide accelerated, low- or no-cost training to address early childhood educator shortages. Programs last two to six weeks and involve 20 to 64 instructional hours, often through partnerships among community colleges, Smart Start organizations, and Child Care Resource and Referral agencies.

The classroom-ready model provides required health, safety, registration, and background-check preparation, qualifying graduates to work in licensed facilities but not as lead teachers. The teaching credential model adds early childhood development coursework and awards EDU 3119 credit, which substitutes for EDU 119 at all 58 state community colleges. Graduates can become lead teachers, work as elementary teaching assistants, and apply the credit toward further education.

North Carolina’s House budget included a $1.476 million expansion pilot, but it was excluded from legislation signed in August. Separately, the state Division of Child Development and Early Education is offering grants of up to $50,000 to as many as 10 eligible institutions operating academies from October 2025 through July 2026.

Programs report graduates entering child care jobs or higher education. Wayne County has graduated 63 students, Johnston County 26, Stanly County 13, and McDowell County six. Durham’s bilingual, six-week credential academy received 140 applications for 20 places. Funding sources include foundations, community grants, and local organizations, with reported costs ranging from about $430 to $1,264 per student. Leaders say the academies reduce entry barriers, connect participants with local employers and resources, and support continued education, though child care wages remain low.

The patent describes automated object-sortation systems using robotic manipulators, perception devices, conveyors, carriages, and dynamically assigned intermediate containers. Unlike conventional systems with fixed destination-bin mappings, the system identifies an object, assigns an available intermediate location based on its destination and operational heuristics, and retains that assignment until the container is emptied. Containers can then be reassigned to new destinations.

Objects may arrive through single, circulating, or multiple conveyors, hoppers, or designated input areas. Robots select, identify, and place objects into assigned bins; unidentified or temporarily unassignable objects may be returned to the input stream or sent for manual handling. A central controller tracks objects and bin contents, determines when bins are complete, and coordinates their transfer for downstream processing.

Assignments may consider historical trends, incoming shipments, current system contents, sorting times, object dimensions, destination demand, facility layout, and downstream costs. This flexibility can reduce unused outputs, space, labor, and capital and operating costs while improving scalability and resilience.

Some embodiments use drop-camera units to capture multiple views of falling objects, followed by shuttle carriages that move objects to rows of collection bins. Multiple shuttle wings and robotic arms may operate in parallel. Frequently used destinations can be assigned nearer carriage home positions to reduce cycle time. Completed bins may be removed, bagged, labeled, or transported by conveyors or tracks. The architecture can be expanded by adding sorters, wings, robots, or parallel cells.

The team hopes to rebound after losing the first game by creating traffic in front of goaltender Roberto, obstructing his view and pursuing rebounds. They aim to improve after learning their opponent’s tendencies and return home with a series split.

The lower highs and lower lows pattern consists of consecutive bars whose highs and lows are below those of previous bars. Backtests on the S&P 500, gold, and long-term Treasuries entered long after one or more such daily bars and exited after 1–10 bars. Results generally improved with longer holding periods, partly reflecting each asset’s upward drift during the test periods. A two-day pattern slightly improved average gains in the S&P 500 but offered little benefit in gold or Treasuries. In stocks, entering after three consecutive lower highs and lower lows increased average gain and profit factor, with a 9.9% maximum drawdown for a one-day holding period. Overall, the tests characterize the pattern as a short-term reversal setup that works best in stocks, although other strategies may offer better returns for short holding periods.

Three former D.C. Department of Corrections employees alleged they were terminated in retaliation for speaking publicly about halfway-house conditions. Before trial, the parties tentatively agreed to a $625,000 payment for dismissal of the claims but disputed whether the settlement also required retirement-system re-enrollment. Applying D.C. contract law, the court found no meeting of the minds on retirement benefits and declined to enforce the settlement, including separately as to one plaintiff. The plaintiffs were given until September 9, 2002, to accept $625,000 without retirement benefits or reject the offer and proceed toward trial.

Niantic will add 80 second-generation Pokémon to Pokémon Go later this week, bringing the generation’s in-game total to 88. The update also introduces Nanab and Pinap Berries, new avatar customization options, purchasable items, and new battle reactions. Twelve second-generation Pokémon remain absent, including six legendaries, while first-generation legendaries also remain unavailable.

The passage defines GHCB communication requirements for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors. It covers AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration and unregistration, feature discovery, termination requests, protocol negotiation, VMGEXIT handling, secrets-page data, EFI communication, and non-automatic exit processing.

SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB GPA before first use. Guests may request a hypervisor-preferred GPA, register another shared page, or unregister the current GPA. Registration replaces any prior registration, and mismatched GPAs require guest termination. Multi-VMPL support permits separate registrations by VMPL level.

During negotiation, guests determine supported GHCB versions and the memory-encryption bit, configure page tables, allocate and share a GHCB page, and write its GPA to the GHCB MSR. SEV-SNP guests additionally use the registration protocol. VMGEXIT processing requires protected access to the GHCB, generally by disabling interrupts and preemption.

For non-automatic exits, a #VC identifies the exit reason. The guest supplies required state and validity bits in the GHCB, invokes VMGEXIT, processes the hypervisor’s response, advances RIP, and returns through IRET. Both parties reset the validity bitmap before each exchange. Nonzero SW_EXITINFO1 values report errors or request exception injection.

Special handling is described for I/O, MSR accesses, hypercalls, MMIO, page-state changes, and SNP guest requests. I/O and MMIO operations may use decrypted shared buffers and multiple VMGEXIT calls. Page-state changes support private/shared transitions and optional PSMASH or UNSMASH hints, with progress recorded to permit interrupted operations to resume.

SNP guest requests use separate shared request and response pages. The hypervisor translates their addresses, manages response-page ownership, invokes firmware, returns the firmware status, and may rate-limit excessive requests. Guests must retry rate-limited requests before issuing another request to prevent message-sequence and AES-GCM IV reuse problems.

The SNP secrets page includes reserved fields for 64-bit per-VMPL request sequence numbers, an AP jump-table address, and guest-defined data. EFI firmware can communicate SNP secrets and CPUID pages through a specified configuration table.

At IHRMP’s ninth graduation ceremony in Accra, President Dr. Edward Kwapong urged HR practitioners to prioritize professional certification over academic qualifications. The institute graduated 136 associates and nine certified members, a 32% increase. Graduates were encouraged to uphold professional standards. Guest speaker Irene Asare said artificial intelligence, robotics and humans must combine to improve workplace productivity.

Tesla delivered its first 30 Model 3 cars to employee buyers, with advance reservations exceeding 500,000. The base model costs $35,000 and has a 220-mile range, while a $44,000 version offers 310 miles. Musk warned of at least six months of difficult production as Tesla seeks to produce 500,000 vehicles next year, nearly six times its 2016 output. The launch is central to Tesla’s shift from luxury electric vehicles to the mass market. Production delays, quality concerns and more than $2 billion in cash spending pose risks, while steady deliveries could provide funding for Tesla’s broader clean energy and transportation plans.

The lecture examines smart contracts, decentralized applications, token sales, blockchain platforms, and related legal issues. Smart contracts are defined, following Nick Szabo, as digitally specified promises incorporating protocols that parties perform against. They are typically automated algorithms rather than artificial intelligence and may not qualify as legal contracts.

Ethereum shares Bitcoin’s cryptographic and decentralized consensus features but differs in transaction design. It is account-based, uses state transitions, supports Turing-complete programming, and stores multiple forms of data in Merkle trees. Ethereum currently uses proof of work, has shorter block times, and began through a presale. Its monetary policy has been altered by community-approved software changes, indicating greater flexibility and more centralized leadership than Bitcoin. Other smart-contract platforms include EOS, NEO, and Ethereum Classic, with EOS and NEO using delegated Byzantine fault tolerance. Existing decentralized applications remain limited in adoption and are concentrated in gaming, gambling, exchanges, and finance.

Initial coin offerings raise funds to develop networks, usually issuing transferable native tokens before those networks are functional. Token values depend largely on expectations of future use and appreciation. Billions of dollars have been raised through thousands of offerings, but many projects have failed or have been identified as possible scams or frauds.

Larry Lessig explains that contracts exchange promises or performances and always operate within a legal framework. Even automated performance-for-performance arrangements, such as vending machines, include legally implied terms. Governments may refuse to enforce contracts, prohibit them, regulate their terms, or tax their transactions. Code can supplement or conflict with law, as illustrated by digital rights management restricting uses that copyright law may permit.

Contract law primarily allocates risk and depends on enforcement systems. Blockchain technology may substitute for weak legal infrastructure, lower transaction costs, verify external facts, and enable products such as automatically paid flight-delay insurance. However, real-world information still requires credible inputs, and governments remain relevant. Smart contracts may also increase costs when complex agreements require deliberate ambiguity for unlikely contingencies that courts would ordinarily resolve afterward. Hybrid agreements could automate clear cases while referring uncertain ones to courts.

Existing electronic-signature law likely addresses most questions of recognizing coded agreements, but courts still face difficulties interpreting software and opaque automated systems. Lessig argues that lawyers need sufficient technical knowledge to understand code as a form of regulation and to assess coded contractual terms.

Backtests indicate a Santa Claus rally in European markets, with Christmas-period returns significantly exceeding random weekly gains. Using the EWG ETF for German stocks, the average gain per trade was 2.1%, with an 81% win rate and profit factor of 13. The FEZ ETF for the Euro Stoxx 50 averaged 1.5%, also with an 81% win rate and a profit factor of 9. Recent returns were below earlier averages. Positions were generally held for several days, with entry timing affecting returns, volatility, and holding periods. The backtest began in 2001, used no leverage, and compounded equity. Historical results do not guarantee future performance.

Collagen provides structural support, strength and elasticity to skin, tendons, bones and other tissues, but natural production declines with age. Of roughly 28 collagen types, I, II and III are most common in oral supplements. Supplements include hydrolysed collagen, unprocessed chicken-cartilage collagen and gelatin, usually sourced from fish, cows, pigs or chickens. Hydrolysed collagen may be most effective because it is easily digested and absorbed.

Studies suggest collagen supplements may support skin growth and firmness, reduce wrinkles and brittle nails, strengthen bones, alleviate joint pain, support connective tissues and help repair muscle damage. Evidence for thicker hair is limited to mouse studies, and research overall remains ongoing.

Studied daily doses include 2.5 grams for joint pain, skin health and hydration; 5 grams for bone density in postmenopausal people with osteopenia; 15 grams with resistance training for muscle mass; and up to 40 milligrams for joint health. Manufacturers often recommend at least 12 weeks, and third-party-tested products are advised.

A balanced diet can support collagen production through protein-rich foods, vitamin C sources and foods such as bone broth.

Midline Option is a downhill option play in which the quarterback reads an interior defensive lineman and either hands to a fullback attacking the A-gap or keeps through the B-gap. Used in modernized forms by programs such as Oregon and Coastal Carolina, it remains a complement to inside and outside veer offenses. Its main advantage is leaving a defender unblocked and using veer-like wingback motion to misdirect the defense. Its primary weakness is exposing the quarterback to frequent hits, favoring durable runners.

Against 3-4 and 4-3 fronts, linemen block or bypass assigned defenders to reach linebackers, while the fullback runs the midline, one wingback simulates veer motion, and the other leads through the B-gap. The quarterback keeps if the dive key crashes toward the fullback and hands off if the defender expands or moves upfield.

Common variations include Flexbone Midline, which replaces the playside tight end with a receiver to spread the defense, and Midline “Follow,” which adds a wingback as a lead blocker for short-yardage quarterback keeps.

Twelve-year-old Billy Caldwell, who has epilepsy, received a short-term licence for medicinal cannabis oil while undergoing treatment in London. His return to Northern Ireland awaits Department of Health ratification. His mother says officials have been unresponsive and suitable London accommodation is unavailable, while the department says it is actively coordinating with the Home Office and Belfast Trust.

Soccer formations strategically arrange players for defense and attack. Selection depends mainly on team size, player skills, and the coach’s tactical comfort. Formation labels list defenders, midfielders, and forwards, excluding the assumed goalkeeper; examples include 4-3-3 and 4-4-2. U.S. Soccer recommends age-based formations, including 4-3-3 or 4-4-2 for U15–U19, 4-3-3 for U13–U14, and 3-2-3 for U9–U12. Coaches use discretion for smaller-sided youth games. Introducing formations can help young players progress toward team-oriented play. Successful implementation requires understanding positions, player placement, tactics, teamwork, and clearly diagramming and explaining the formation.

Hubble imaged NGC 6000, a spiral galaxy 102 million light-years away in Scorpius. Its yellow center contains older, cooler stars, while its blue spiral arms host young, massive stars. Observations detected faint remnants of supernovae SN 2007ch and SN 2010as, helping researchers study their progenitors and possible companions.
