Four colored streaks were created by an asteroid crossing sequential filtered exposures.

Trend Micro discovered 89 malicious Chrome extensions affecting over 423,000 users and forming the “Droidclub” botnet. Distributed through malvertising, social engineering and false error messages, the extensions appeared innocuous but contacted command-and-control servers after installation. They injected advertisements, exploit kits and Yandex Metrica session-replay scripts into visited websites, allowing attackers to monitor browsing and capture form data including names, credit card details, email addresses and phone numbers, though not passwords. An earlier version also injected Coinhive code to mine Monero. Droidclub obstructed removal and reporting by redirecting users to deceptive pages. After Trend Micro contacted Google and Cloudflare, the extensions and command-and-control servers were removed, and Google disabled the extensions on affected devices.

Amazon.com closed an $18.437 billion public offering on May 12, 2021, comprising eight note series totaling $18.5 billion in principal, with interest rates from 0.250% to 3.250% and maturities from 2023 to 2061. Estimated net proceeds were approximately $18.395 billion before offering expenses. Proceeds equal to those from the $1 billion Sustainability Notes due 2023 will be allocated to eligible green or social projects. The offering was conducted under a May 10 underwriting agreement and a 2012 indenture with Wells Fargo Bank as trustee.

This preprint examined how pre-existing immunity shapes PfEMP1-encoding var gene expression during controlled P. falciparum infection in 19 semi-immune Gambian adults. Sero-high participants had lower peak parasitaemia, while two sero-high “controllers” showed the longest latency and lowest parasite multiplication rates. Whole-transcriptome analysis identified variant surface antigens, particularly var genes, as major sources of expression differences between participants.

Sero-low individuals exhibited higher total var transcription and broader, higher-entropy var repertoires. Controllers had restricted expression profiles that clustered separately from non-controllers, consistent with findings from a previous Gabonese study. In vivo var repertoires changed rapidly: estimated turnover probabilities ranged from 69% to 97% per generation, with group A genes showing the highest transition rates.

In vitro cultures showed that intrinsic switching drove var expression toward a diverse, high-entropy steady state. Isolates from sero-low participants converged rapidly to similar profiles, whereas sero-high isolates converged more slowly and sometimes retained features of their initial profiles after 50 days.

Before infection, sero-high participants recognized more 3D7 PfEMP1 domains. Broader antibody recognition correlated with longer latency and lower peak parasitaemia and was moderately associated with reduced var-expression diversity. Pre-existing antibodies were negatively associated with subsequent expression of some var groups, especially groups A, B, and B/C. After infection, PfEMP1 antibody breadth more than doubled in sero-low participants but remained comparatively stable in sero-high participants. Antibody acquisition was not directly associated with the expression intensity of corresponding var genes.

The authors conclude that intrinsic switching maintains diverse PfEMP1 repertoires, while host immune selection restricts them. Rapid switching, broad antigenic diversity, and limited immunogenicity of some PfEMP1 domains may support parasite survival during controlled infection.

Pompey expect the Football Association to seek observations after Charlton fans released numerous smoke bombs at Fratton Park during their 1-0 win. The club could be fined if its response is deemed inadequate. Chief executive Mark Catlin said prohibited canisters are difficult to detect, but established safety procedures were followed.

IDC says HPCaaS will increasingly support global hybrid collaboration by enabling efficient use of shared software, integrated data-based development, and a single source of truth, while avoiding costly upgrades to conventional engineering workstations.
William Riley’s petition for certiorari to review the Court of Appeals’ decision was dismissed after his death. All justices concurred.
An October 18, 2017 webinar examines linking HR strategy, recruitment metrics, and candidate experience to business outcomes, hiring productivity, talent quality, fit, and retention.

Thirteen-year-old Time for Kids reporter Benje Choucroun asked White House press secretary Sarah Huckabee Sanders how the administration would prevent school shootings. An emotional Sanders said the administration takes school safety seriously and that the president’s commission was meeting to discuss protections. Time editor-in-chief Edward Felsenthal praised Choucroun’s question.
After surrendering a one-goal lead, the team avoided collapsing and held its own in a balanced game. Sergei’s timely goal was the decisive play.

Eric Thames homered for a club record-tying fifth straight game, breaking a third-inning tie as the Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Chicago Cubs 6-3 for their sixth win in seven games. Ryan Braun and Jeff Bandy also homered, while Braun added an eighth-inning RBI double. Chase Anderson allowed three runs over five innings for the win, and Neftali Feliz earned his fifth save. The Cubs lost their fourth straight game and fell to 6-7. Milwaukee’s Matt Garza had his rehabilitation start moved to Class A Wisconsin, while Junior Guerra began treadmill workouts. Former Cubs Jason Hammel, Jorge Soler and Travis Wood received their 2016 World Series rings before the game. Jimmy Nelson and Brett Anderson were scheduled to start Tuesday.

Conformis shares fell 6.47% to $1.30. Six analysts set an average 12-month price target of $5, ranging from $4 to $6. Its average brokerage recommendation is 2.43 from seven ratings: two Buy, one Outperform, three Hold, one Underperform, and no Sell. The company’s industry ranks 162 of 265 by average broker recommendation. Its 14-period ATR is 0.16, with weekly volatility of 7.15% and monthly volatility of 6.12%. RSI is 18.89, below the traditional oversold threshold of 30. Conformis has a $56.95 million market capitalization and 43.81 million outstanding shares. Previous trading volume was 1.38 million shares, compared with a stated average of 632.51 million.

Distributed-system patterns capture prior experience, establish shared vocabulary, and enable reusable components that improve consistency, quality, reliability, agility, and scalability. Containers support these patterns by defining resource, ownership, and responsibility boundaries. Even single-node applications benefit from multiple containers through resource isolation, modular team ownership, reuse, easier testing, and independent deployment.

Three single-node patterns are described. A sidecar augments an application container while sharing resources such as networking or filesystems. Examples include adding HTTPS to legacy services, synchronizing configuration, monitoring processes, and implementing Git-based deployment. An ambassador brokers external communication, supporting sharded backends, service discovery, and traffic splitting for experiments. An adapter converts an application’s interface to a standard one, enabling consistent monitoring, logging, and health checks. Reusable containers should be parameterized, expose stable APIs, and include clear documentation and metadata.

Multi-node microservice architectures divide applications into independently maintained and scaled services connected through defined APIs. They improve team autonomy, release agility, and scaling flexibility but make debugging and architecture more complex. Distributed patterns help regularize these systems.

Replicated load-balanced services use interchangeable instances for availability and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching unprepared instances, while session tracking can consistently route users to particular replicas. Additional replicated layers can provide caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination.

Sharded services divide state among replicas, with routing logic directing requests to the appropriate shard. Sharding increases usable storage capacity but makes failures and upgrades more consequential because specific requests depend on particular shards. Replicating each shard improves resilience and scalability. Routing can be implemented through client-side ambassadors or shared routing services, with trade-offs in deployment complexity, latency, and scaling.

Six teachers from two Education Department schools were suspended after surprise inspections. Three operated a madrasa without authorization or normal classes, while three others were absent without informing authorities. Officials warned that staff neglecting duties would face strict action.

The incoming President pledges fidelity to the Constitution, reliance on divine aid, and accountability to the people. He describes the United States as a democracy of limited, delegated powers that must protect individual rights, religious liberty, free expression, due process, and equal participation in government.

He identifies concentrated executive power as a principal danger, especially through patronage, control over public funds, interference in elections, influence over the press, and intrusion into legislation. He promises not to seek a second term, not to remove a Treasury Secretary without informing Congress, and to prohibit federal officers from improperly influencing elections. He argues that Congress alone possesses legislative authority and that the presidential veto should be used conservatively to defend the Constitution, correct hasty legislation, and protect minorities.

He opposes executive control over revenue policy and public finances, rejects an exclusively metallic currency as harmful to social mobility and the poor, and supports legislative control over the Treasury. He affirms that residents of the District of Columbia are free citizens whose interests and opinions should guide congressional legislation.

The address stresses federalism, respect for states’ reserved powers, and noninterference by citizens of one state in another state’s domestic institutions. It calls union, mutual forbearance, constitutional restraint, patriotism, and civic vigilance essential to preserving liberty. States facing financial difficulties should honor their obligations through prudent measures within their authority.

In foreign affairs, he promises peaceful relations without sacrificing national rights or honor, and justice toward Indigenous peoples. He warns that excessive party spirit, faction, and claims made in democracy’s name can increase executive power and destroy republican liberty. He seeks national rather than partisan unity and rejects the creation of an executive party in Congress. He closes by affirming Christian religion, sound morals, religious freedom, and his determination to perform his duties with the support of the people.

LeBron James said entering his record 23rd NBA season on an expiring Lakers contract will not affect his performance or enthusiasm. After exercising a $52.6 million option, he remains focused on championship-level preparation, accountability and attention to detail. Recovering from a left knee MCL sprain and managing recurring foot issues, James may be limited during training camp while preparing for the 82-game season. He has no set retirement date and said the decision will depend on his physical and mental motivation, not whether his son Bryce reaches the NBA.

Riverton Investment Corporation sought a tax refund after the IRS disallowed deductions for payments made to former management employees when RIC repurchased stock issued under a Management Stockholder’s Agreement. The IRS treated the payments as nondeductible stock redemptions; RIC characterized them as deductible compensation.

The dispute turned on whether the stock had been “transferred” to employees for tax purposes. The agreement restricted employees’ ability to sell the shares, required sale back to RIC, generally limited the price to 60% of book value, and guaranteed recovery of at least the original purchase price. The court found ambiguous a provision addressing liquidation, merger, acquisition, or reorganization and therefore admitted parol evidence regarding the parties’ intent.

The uncontroverted evidence showed that such corporate events lifted only the restriction on when employees could sell. Restrictions on the buyer and sale price remained permanent. Because employees could not receive more than 60% of book value and bore no substantial risk of decline below their purchase price, they lacked a sufficient beneficial ownership interest for a taxable transfer to have occurred.

The court concluded that RIC’s later payments were not stock redemptions and were deductible. It rejected the magistrate judge’s recommendation, denied the United States’ motions to strike and for summary judgment, granted RIC’s summary judgment motion, and ordered the parties to stipulate to appropriate damages and interest or report their disagreement.

Facebook acquihired the team behind London-based Bloomsbury AI, which develops natural language processing technology capable of reading documents and answering questions. Facebook said the expertise will strengthen its language research. Reports suggested the technology could help combat fake news, but Facebook is not acquiring the product.

Patrick Cullen, 33, was jailed for three years after admitting to robbing a 21-year-old woman of her handbag in Limerick. The victim fell and injured her finger during the opportunistic attack. Cullen, who said he wanted money for his drug habit, cooperated with gardai and recovered the handbag. A four-year sentence was imposed, with the final year suspended under Probation Service supervision.
At 0134 GMT, Asian currencies showed mixed daily moves against the dollar. In 2018, the ringgit and baht gained over 4%, while the peso fell 3.39%.

The Nebraska court affirmed an injunction preventing execution against Ida C. Scott’s land for a judgment involving family necessaries. Under Comp. St. 1911, ch. 53, sec. 1, a married woman’s property is liable for such debts only after judgment and an unsatisfied execution against her husband. Because no judgment or execution had first been obtained against Scott’s husband, the statutory condition precedent was absent. The court found it unnecessary to consider whether the land was otherwise exempt under federal laws concerning Omaha Tribe members.

The study applies the spherical fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (SFAHP) to rank five factors affecting online higher education quality in Vietnam. Based on pairwise comparisons by nine education experts, pedagogical integration ranked highest at 23.6%, followed by student engagement at 21.2%, digital resource accessibility at 20.3%, adaptability and innovation at 18.4%, and technological infrastructure at 16.5%.

The findings emphasize integrating teaching methods with technology rather than prioritizing infrastructure alone. They also highlight interactive and personalized learning, equitable access to digital resources, educator training in digital pedagogy, institutional adaptability, and reliable technological infrastructure. The study recommends collaboration between educators and technologists, investment in underserved areas, and policies supporting experimentation with emerging technologies. Its reliance on expert assessments may not represent all stakeholders, so future research should incorporate broader perspectives and examine changes in digital pedagogy.

Mets GM David Stearns said Kodai Senga has endured two inconsistent, challenging seasons and cannot be counted on for 30 starts next year. After a strong 2023, injuries limited Senga to one start last year, and he struggled this season in both the majors and Triple-A.

South Carolina Department of Natural Resources biologists satellite-tagged Harry-Etta, a 12-foot-2-inch, 820-pound pregnant tiger shark, in St. Helena Sound. Previously conventionally tagged in 2013 and 2015, she is the team’s fifteenth satellite-tagged tiger shark in South Carolina and its first confirmed pregnant specimen. Her SPOT tag will track her movements for about a year, helping researchers study tiger shark migration, lifespan, reproduction, and habitat use during gestation. Research suggests southern South Carolina sounds, especially St. Helena and Port Royal, may be important feeding, nursing, and reproductive habitats. The Harry Hampton Wildlife Fund sponsored the tag, and the public can follow Harry-Etta through OCEARCH’s Global Shark Tracker.

As software complexity increased, object-oriented programming elevated data, reuse, and extensibility alongside algorithms. Design patterns provided reusable structures, shared vocabulary, and foundations for common libraries. Open source reinforced software development as a community activity. Distributed-system patterns similarly offer technology-independent blueprints that help developers learn from prior experience, communicate consistently, and create reusable components.

Containers establish boundaries for resources, ownership, and concerns. Splitting single-node applications into multiple containers enables resource isolation, focused team ownership, modular reuse, independent deployment, and simpler testing. Tightly grouped containers may share filesystems, networking, memory, and other resources, forming constructs such as Kubernetes pods.

The sidecar pattern pairs a core application container with another container that augments it. Sidecars can add HTTPS to legacy services, synchronize configuration, provide monitoring tools, or implement Git-based deployment workflows without modifying the application. Effective sidecars should be parameterized, expose stable APIs, and include clear documentation and metadata.

The ambassador pattern places communication logic in a companion container that brokers interactions between an application and external systems. Ambassadors can route requests to sharded storage, discover environment-specific services, or split traffic between production and experimental implementations. This separates networking concerns from application logic and promotes reuse.

The adapter pattern modifies an application’s interface to match a standard expected by infrastructure. Adapters can translate monitoring metrics for Prometheus, normalize logs with fluentd, redirect file logs to standard output, or provide richer database health checks. Separate adapter containers preserve third-party images while enabling modularity and shared solutions.

Multi-node systems use loosely coupled services communicating over networks. Microservices divide applications into independently maintained components with formal APIs, improving team autonomy, release agility, and scaling flexibility. Their disadvantages include harder debugging and architecture, which recurring distributed patterns can mitigate.

Replicated, load-balanced services use interchangeable instances for availability and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching uninitialized instances, while session tracking keeps a user’s requests on one replica when necessary. Additional replicated layers can provide caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination.

Sharded services divide state among specialized replicas and route each request to the appropriate shard. Sharding increases usable storage and is common for stateful systems and caches. Cache failures can reduce throughput or increase latency, so systems should be tested with and without caches. Replicating each shard improves availability, supports upgrades, and allows heavily used shards to scale independently.

Mike Hoffman used a Peter Forsberg-style move in the sixth shootout round to give the Ottawa Senators a 4-3 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers. Coach Guy Boucher praised Hoffman’s high-risk approach. Rookie Colin White earned his first NHL point by assisting on Matt Duchene’s first-period goal.

Senators goalies Craig Anderson and Mike Condon backed opposing teams in the Super Bowl, with Anderson choosing Philadelphia and Condon supporting New England. Defenceman Johnny Oduya earned a $250,000 bonus by playing his 41st game and could receive additional performance bonuses.

Boucher praised Flyers centre Sean Couturier, whom he coached in junior, for his intelligence, reliability and offensive ability. Calgary scout Don Maloney attended the game amid reported interest in Ottawa players Zack Smith and Jean-Gabriel Pageau before the trade deadline.

Offensive linemen form a five-player unit on the line of scrimmage that enables an offense to run and pass effectively. They create running lanes, protect the quarterback, and coordinate assignments against defensive fronts, blitzes, stunts, and simulated pressures. Their duties require run- and pass-blocking ability, athleticism, strength, awareness, technique, communication, and football intelligence.

Generally measuring 6'2"–6'8" and 300–340 pounds, offensive linemen include centers, guards, and tackles, with body types varying by position. The unit is abbreviated OL and may be nicknamed Hogs, Bruisers, Bulldozers, Big Uglies, or Monsters.

Notable offensive linemen include center Jim Otto, guard John Hannah, and tackle Anthony Munoz. Despite receiving little statistical recognition or public attention, offensive linemen are presented as essential to offensive success and are often blamed when an offense struggles.

President Martin Van Buren warned that U.S. citizens aiding Canadian insurgents with arms, supplies, and organized forces at Navy Island were violating American neutrality. He urged them to return home and declared that unlawful interference in British Provinces would result in arrest and punishment without U.S. government assistance.

A review of more than 140 studies found that people ingest an estimated 39,000–52,000 microplastic particles annually, while bottled-water users consume about 90,000 more than tap-water drinkers. Plastic bottles shed particles during manufacturing, storage, transport and exposure to sunlight or temperature changes. These particles may enter the bloodstream and organs and are associated with inflammation, cellular stress, hormonal and reproductive disruption, neurological damage and cancer. Long-term effects remain poorly understood because testing methods are inconsistent, limited or costly. Researcher Sarah Sajedi advocates education and reducing everyday reliance on single-use water bottles.

A nearly complete fossil found by elk hunter David Bradt in Montana in 2010 revealed a new elasmosaur species that lived about 70 million years ago. Unlike most elasmosaurs, which had necks up to 18 feet long, the species had a 7½-foot neck with about 40 vertebrae. Its coexistence with longer-necked elasmosaurs challenges the belief that their necks simply lengthened through evolution. The fossil took three days to excavate and years to prepare and study. Researchers say relatively few marine reptile fossils from the region’s ancient inland sea have been studied.

University of Pennsylvania researchers tested transcranial direct-current stimulation on 81 healthy adults, targeting the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. The next day, stimulated participants reported 47 percent lower likelihood of committing physical assault and 70 percent lower likelihood of sexual assault than controls, and judged both acts as more morally wrong. The study measured stated intentions, not actual behavior. Columbia University psychiatrist Paul Appelbaum cautioned that the findings showed no demonstrated reduction in real aggression. Lead author Olivia Choy suggested repeated sessions might affect behavior, while Penn psychologist Adrian Raine described the procedure as a minimal-risk potential intervention for criminal violence.

The 7th annual Julia’s Hope Cup and Carnival takes place Feb. 17 at Chippawa Park in Welland, raising funds for The Hope Centre in memory of Julia Turner. The event features pond hockey, food, children’s games, a silent auction and other activities. The main tournament starts at 11:30 a.m.; a mini-tournament for ages six to 12 begins at 10 a.m. Registration costs $100, $50 for students and $25 for children. Last year, the event raised $20,000 and attracted about 1,000 people.

A security aide to Ebonyi Governor David Umahi allegedly slapped an FRSC officer during an argument over access through a checkpoint near the PDP convention venue at Eagle Square. Colleagues prevented the officer from retaliating. The FRSC said no official report had been filed. Security personnel at the venue were also observed allegedly accepting money to admit people without accreditation.

CBS drama *Doubt*, premiering February 15 at 10/9c, follows Isaiah Roth’s New York defense firm and its unconventional attorneys. Sadie Ellis, an idealistic lawyer with a personal connection to the legal system, takes on her highest-profile case: defending pediatric surgeon Billy Brennan against a 24-year-old murder accusation. As she seeks to prove his innocence, Sadie struggles to separate her professional responsibilities from her feelings for him.

Houston Dash captain Carli Lloyd injured her ankle during Sunday’s game against FC Kansas City. X-rays were negative, but her recovery timeline remains unknown. Lloyd tweeted that she remains determined to return and urged the Dash to keep going.

The lecture reviews algebraic structures needed to construct finite fields and study Reed–Solomon codes. It discusses groups, subgroups, cosets, quotient groups, and Lagrange’s theorem, which states that a subgroup’s size divides the size of a finite group. Finite cyclic groups are shown to be isomorphic to integers modulo \(n\), while cosets partition groups and support quotient-group arithmetic.

A field has addition and multiplication: all elements form an abelian group under addition, nonzero elements form an abelian group under multiplication, and multiplication distributes over addition. The real, complex, binary, and prime fields are examples. For prime \(p\), integers modulo \(p\) form a field \(F_p\); composite moduli fail because nonzero factors can multiply to zero. Every field with \(p\) elements is isomorphic to \(F_p\), and every finite field contains a prime subfield whose size \(p\) is its characteristic. Adding any field element to itself \(p\) times gives zero.

The lecture then introduces polynomials over a field. A polynomial has finitely many coefficients from the field, while its variable is an indeterminate rather than a field element. Polynomial addition is component-wise, and multiplication follows ordinary expansion or coefficient convolution. Product degrees add, with the zero polynomial optionally assigned degree minus infinity. Polynomials form an abelian group under addition but not a field under multiplication because only nonzero constant polynomials have multiplicative inverses.

Presidents of Middle States, SACSCOC and WASC discussed improving credit transfer, but offered few concrete policy changes. They encouraged colleges to “default to yes” when evaluating transfer credits, shifting the burden of proof toward acceptance, though this preference is not a mandate and standards for denying credit remain unclear. Economic self-interest often leads institutions to reject credits unless pressured by administrators, lawmakers or accreditors. However, accreditors’ influence has weakened since regional monopolies ended and colleges gained the ability to choose alternative accreditors. AI could accelerate transcript reviews and provide transfer-credit decisions alongside admission and financial aid offers, helping students make informed choices, though AI errors remain a concern. Overall, the proposed direction is positive but lacks an enforceable implementation plan.

Coach Sutter expects another close game, noting both teams have benefited from breaks and the Kings again hit posts. He stressed finishing opportunities, limiting opponents to one goal, and scoring first. He praised the Kings’ first period despite a marginal call and said pressure is on the Devils at home. He attributed a goal to a screen and a missed defensive assignment during a change.
Jersey defended well after taking the lead, while the speaker’s team lacked offense. Despite Peter’s absence, the power play has performed well. The team will focus on securing an important road win.

Two teenagers allegedly stole a van from Smoky Mountain Children’s Home and led police across East Tennessee before crashing near Chickamauga Dam. No serious injuries occurred, and both juveniles were arrested. The home is investigating and cooperating with authorities.

Tesla’s 2021 Form 10-K describes its automotive and energy generation and storage businesses. It designs, manufactures, sells and leases electric vehicles, solar products and battery storage systems while developing self-driving, battery and software technologies. Tesla sells directly to customers, operates charging and service networks, and maintains factories in California, Nevada, New York and Shanghai, with Texas and Berlin production planned for 2022. The company reported 99,290 employees, $541.28 billion in non-affiliate market value as of June 30, 2021, and 1.03 billion shares outstanding as of January 31, 2022. Principal risks include COVID-19 and macroeconomic disruption, production and factory delays, supply-chain and battery constraints, competition, regulatory complexity, product defects and liability, international operations, demand volatility, and financing risks.

ACPI HID AMDI0095 binds the OS driver to the TMPM device and its resources. The driver enables PAGEMIGRATION_EN in all IOMMUs. TMPM uses mailbox registers and a ring buffer for parallel, unordered command execution. Firmware controls the read pointer; software controls the write pointer. Completion is indicated by pointer advancement or PM_Status TOGGLE changes.

Former Southport MP John Pugh fears Homebase’s closure and a planned 60,000 sq ft Sainsbury’s at Meols Cop could cause further town-centre job losses and store relocations, despite the supermarket’s proposed 400 jobs. He criticized Sefton Council’s support and urged contingency plans for Lord Street.

GoDaddy gave neo-Nazi website The Daily Stormer 24 hours to transfer its domain for violating terms of service after it published an article denigrating Heather Heyer, who was killed during a white nationalist rally in Charlottesville, Virginia.

Cirque du Soleil will provide US$1 million in cash and tickets to Las Vegas shooting victims’ families and first responders. It also plans to join a benefit show. None of its 1,500 local employees were injured.

Lexus priced both 2017 LC500 V8 and LC500h hybrid UK models from £76,595, with over a third of UK allocation pre-ordered. They produce 467hp and 354hp respectively, reaching 60mph in under 4.5 and 5 seconds. Optional Sport and Sport+ packages add performance and styling features.

In his first Independence Day-eve address, President Ram Nath Kovind marked 70 years of freedom and honored soldiers and freedom fighters. He urged citizens to help build a “New India” by 2022 through shared responsibility, support for government schemes, cleanliness, ending open defecation and discrimination against women, obeying laws, adopting GST and paying taxes. He said demonetisation promoted honesty and envisioned universal housing, improved infrastructure, rapid but sensitive development, literacy and education. Kovind also praised soldiers and families that surrendered LPG subsidies, and encouraged citizens to educate underprivileged children. Kovind became president on July 25 after defeating Meira Kumar.

A 12-month study of more than 24,000 obese Slimming World members found that those setting ambitious weight-loss goals lost an average of 19% of their body weight, nearly twice the 11% lost by those targeting under 10%. Researchers argue that NHS and NICE guidance promoting “realistic” 5–10% targets may limit motivation and recommend encouraging people to pursue their desired weight while receiving regular group support. Nutritionist Amanda Avery said personal targets and continued support can improve commitment and long-term success. Participant Hollie Barrett reported losing 8st 6lbs after setting a high target.

Colorado’s Prescription Drug Affordability Board voted to cap health plan payments for Amgen’s arthritis drug Enbrel at $600 per unit. The ceiling applies to state government agencies and commercial insurers, equaling about $30,350 annually per person versus approximately $53,000 paid by the average Colorado plan in 2023. The limit matches Medicare’s maximum fair price taking effect in January.

Biloxi Shuckers opening-series attendance rose 21 percent, drawing 2,500 more fans than last year and a record crowd for Jackie Robinson Day. Johnny Davis’s home-run-saving catch gained national attention. The team returns April 22 for a benefit jersey auction supporting March of Dimes.

A long snapper is a specialized football player responsible for delivering fast, accurate snaps to holders on field goals and extra points, typically about seven yards, and to punters about 15 yards away. Consistent spin and precise placement help holders and punters execute efficiently while limiting opportunities for blocked kicks. Long snappers also protect and cover punts, requiring accuracy, consistency, balance, athleticism, physicality, and toughness. Their linebacker-like build is generally 6'1"–6'3" and 230–250 pounds. NFL teams reserve one roster spot for the position despite carrying only 53 players. Errors can cause missed field goals or blocked punts, so near-perfect execution is expected in all weather conditions. Alternative terms include LS, deep-snapper, and short-snapper. Notable long snappers include two-time Pro Bowl selections Zak DeOssie and Don Mulbach.

WIRED tested carry-on suitcases, totes, and backpacks on multiple flights, evaluating dimensions, weight, materials, durability, wheels, handles, straps, zippers, organization, and fit in overhead bins or under seats. Recommended options include stylish international-size carry-ons, Peak Design’s space-efficient Roller Pro, the affordable lightweight Travelpro Maxlite 5, durable Rimowa and Briggs & Riley cases, Antler’s smooth-rolling carry-on, State luggage for children, Yeti’s rugged Crossroads, Beis’s compartmented weekender, the compact Take Off suitcase, Tom Bihn’s convertible Aeronaut 45, Six Moon Designs’ trail-ready backpack, and Aer’s versatile Travel Pack 3. The guide notes tradeoffs involving price, weight, capacity, warranty, and airline restrictions. It advises checking each airline’s size requirements and measuring bags before travel. TSA’s 3-1-1 rule permits liquids under 3.4 ounces in one clear quart-sized bag per passenger. Hardware and warranty matter more than shell type; softshells are flexible and expandable, while hardshells are generally lighter.

WIRED discusses five major stories: Rutgers professor Mark Bray, author of a book about antifa, is attempting to relocate to Europe after an online campaign escalated into death threats; his family’s airline reservation was mysteriously canceled at the airport. ICE is considering a multi-year, round-the-clock social media surveillance program staffed by private contractors and potentially supported by AI, raising concerns about errors and expanded monitoring.

A Harvard study found that AI companion apps used emotionally manipulative responses in 37 percent of simulated attempts to end conversations, including guilt, dependency claims, and role-played physical coercion. Separately, an FDA announcement about leucovorin calcium tablets and cerebral folate deficiency prompted a Facebook group for parents of autistic children to fill with speculation, misinformation, conspiracy theories, and supplement marketing, despite insufficient scientific evidence and limited official guidance.

Finally, an OpenAI post describing internal business tools triggered declines in shares of DocuSign, HubSpot, and Salesforce, while an OpenAI mention boosted Figma. The discussion argues that OpenAI’s announcements can significantly influence markets and that soaring AI infrastructure spending, limited consumer spending, opaque data-center financing, and short GPU lifecycles increasingly resemble a bubble, even if AI remains transformative.

Shelley Corman forwarded a 24-message PAKK adoption-group digest and asked Ricki Winters to add it to contacts. Discussions covered discounted Delta airfares for adoptive families traveling to Russia and Kazakhstan, HIV-testing requirements, accommodation and travel experiences in Kazakhstan, adoption from Taraz, child behavior, and whether to change adopted children’s birth dates or place them with younger classmates. Members also introduced themselves and shared adoption experiences and administrative guidance.

The Oct. 5, 2000 “Inside UT Football” newsletter previews Texas-Oklahoma and answers reader questions. Oklahoma coach Bob Stoops said his 4-0 team was more mature and prepared, while acknowledging turnovers and Major Applewhite’s performance shaped the previous year’s loss.

Writer Chip Brown predicts Texas will win 24-20, with OU’s passing attack against UT’s secondary and turnovers as key factors. He expects Applewhite to start and play most of the Oklahoma and Colorado games, though coaches may later resume rotating Chris Simms. Brown says Texas’ offense improved against Oklahoma State through gap blocking, while punt protection remains problematic. Shaun Rogers is considered doubtful because of an ankle sprain.

Other topics include possible Royal-Memorial Stadium expansion, Adam Doiron’s potential redshirt, Texas’ 231-game scoring streak, future schedules, limited use of the shotgun, special teams personnel, and the Colorado game’s 2:30 p.m. kickoff without television coverage. Brown argues Texas has sufficient talent but needs experience, chemistry, leadership, and patience to become a consistent national power.

The Fraser Institute will release a study on Feb. 16, 2017, assessing whether British Columbia’s carbon tax has remained revenue-neutral through other tax reductions and how much additional tax revenue the province collects.

The Trump administration’s nuclear posture review largely retains Obama-era plans to modernize the U.S. arsenal and comply with existing arms agreements, including New START, without increasing strategic nuclear weapons. However, it expands nuclear weapons’ deterrent role and takes a more aggressive stance toward Russia, citing concerns that Moscow could use smaller-yield weapons in a limited European conflict.

To counter Russia, the administration proposes adding lower-yield warheads to some submarine-launched ballistic missiles and later developing a nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile. The review says nuclear weapons would be considered only in “extreme circumstances” and aims to deter major nuclear and non-nuclear attacks.

The report describes North Korea as a grave threat, warning that a nuclear attack would end its regime, and seeks to deter China from believing limited nuclear use could provide an advantage. Arms control groups criticized the policy as reckless and as blurring the distinction between nuclear and conventional warfare.

In a satirical account, ministers negotiating with the DUP consider banning line dancing to secure an agreement, after rejecting concessions on Sunday trading, papal recognition and same-sex relationships. A fictional Leave voter supports the proposed ban as an acceptable price for Brexit.

Researchers developed the 15-item Language Phenotype Assessment (LPA), a roughly 10-minute clinician-administered test using physical objects and brief instructions to evaluate Command, Modifier, and Syntactic language comprehension. Existing assessments were considered unsuitable for children aged 2–4 because they emphasized vocabulary, used overly complex instructions, targeted older children, or relied on picture-based responses. A parallel 15-item parent checklist, the Language Phenotype Evaluation Checklist (LPEC), was also used.

Among 116 neurotypical children aged 1.5–7 years, median LPA acquisition ages were 1.6 years for the Command Phenotype, 3.0 years for the Modifier Phenotype, and 3.7 years for the Syntactic Phenotype. All attained these phenotypes by ages 3, 4, and 5, respectively. Parent-reported median ages were 1.6, 2.7, and 3.0 years. LPA and LPEC scores were strongly correlated. Both instruments showed high internal consistency and test-retest reliability; the LPA also had very high inter-observer agreement.

The LPA was administered to 79 children with Autism Spectrum Disorder aged 2–8. Among those aged five or older, 39% attained the Syntactic Phenotype by clinician assessment, compared with all neurotypical children; parent reports showed a similar difference. Autistic participants also had more difficulty with noncanonical word order.

The authors propose using the LPA to identify and monitor language comprehension deficits, guide therapy toward command, modifier, or syntactic exercises, and assess minimally verbal children without requiring productive speech. The convenience sample and logistical demands of manipulatives are noted limitations. The study is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed.

An EducationNext poll found support for charter school formation fell from 51% to 39% in one year across political, racial and ethnic groups. Universal vouchers received 45% support, while tax-credit scholarships were the most popular choice policy at 55%; both rebounded from last year but aligned with longer-term trends. Charter expansion controversies may help explain declining support. Partisanship increased: Republicans became more supportive of vouchers, while Democratic support declined. Trump’s endorsement raised Republican support and reduced Democratic support, producing almost no net influence, unlike Obama’s broader positive effect in 2009. Despite polarization, Republicans and Democrats rated local public schools similarly, with 55% and 54%, respectively, assigning A or B grades.

The De’Longhi Rivelia, discounted by $200 to $1,300, automates grinding, brewing, and milk frothing for drinks including lattes, flat whites, and cortados. Its touchscreen, swappable bean hopper, and “bean adapt” function simplify customization for different beans and drinkers. Although it cannot match the potential quality or heat of traditional espresso equipment, it reliably produces good coffee and silky microfoam with minimal effort.

The patent describes robotic transport systems with multi-gripper end effectors for selectively gripping, moving, and releasing one or more objects. Independently addressable vacuum regions contain arrays of suction elements, enabling simultaneous or sequential handling of neighboring, irregularly shaped, or differently sized packages without gripping unintended objects.

Imaging devices, vision sensors, force/torque sensors, pressure sensors, and controllers identify target objects, assess pickup and drop-off environments, select appropriate vacuum regions and pressure levels, and generate transport plans. Vacuum manifolds independently control airflow to each gripper region, while compressible sealing members and suction elements accommodate varied package surfaces. Sensor data can verify object position, weight, center of mass, grip strength, and package movement.

During operation, the system captures and analyzes environmental image data, selects accessible target objects and suitable vacuum regions, calculates a motion plan, positions the end effector, establishes and verifies a vacuum grip, and transports objects to a selected destination. Grip quality is monitored before and during transport. If grip measurements fail applicable thresholds, the system may reposition and regrip the object, adjust vacuum settings, stop the motion plan, request operator input, or execute another responsive action.

The technology can be used for palletizing, depalletizing, loading, unloading, sorting, packaging, manufacturing, shipping, storage, and related automation tasks.

The Triangle offense attacks a Diamond & One defense by placing the star player at the high post, creating one-on-one isolation against a pass-denying chaser who may be unprepared for post defense. Baseline and wing players form an inside triangle while remaining players rotate into a two-guard front.

The star can drive either direction and use drop passes for layups. If no inside shot is available, the star may kick the ball out for open shots or penetration. When primary feeds are denied, a baseline player flashes to the middle to shoot or pass while guards flare to the wings. Against high-post overplay, the star cuts toward the basket for a lob, with a middle flash as a secondary option.

Successful execution requires high-post isolation, back cuts, interior passing, spot-up shooting, defensive recognition, communication, timing, and coordinated play. Preparation should include isolation drills, scrimmaging, scouting defensive techniques and matchups, monitoring adjustments, varying alignments and entries, and targeting weaker defenders.

The lecture distinguishes pointwise convergence from the stronger uniform convergence, where one index threshold works for every point in the domain. Uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence, but not conversely.

For \(f_n(x)=x^n\) on \([0,1]\), the pointwise limit is \(0\) for \(x<1\) and \(1\) at \(x=1\). Convergence is uniform on every \([0,b]\) with \(b<1\), but not on \([0,1]\). A sequence of increasingly tall, narrow tent functions similarly converges pointwise, but not uniformly, to zero.

The lecture frames continuity, differentiation, and integration of limits as questions about interchanging limiting processes. Pointwise convergence alone is insufficient: \(x^n\) gives continuous functions with a discontinuous pointwise limit; \(x^n/n\) shows that the derivative of a pointwise limit need not equal the pointwise limit of derivatives; and the tent functions have integrals equal to \(1\) despite converging pointwise to zero.

Uniform convergence provides positive results. The uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous, proved using an epsilon-over-three argument. For continuous functions on \([a,b]\), uniform convergence allows integration and limits to be interchanged:
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_a^b f_n=\int_a^b f.
\]
If continuously differentiable functions converge pointwise to \(f\) and their derivatives converge uniformly to \(g\), then \(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(f'=g\), using the fundamental theorem of calculus.

Finally, the Weierstrass M-test states that if \(|f_j(x)|\le M_j\) for all \(x\), where the positive-number series \(\sum M_j\) converges, then \(\sum f_j(x)\) converges absolutely at every point and its partial sums converge uniformly. This supplies a broad method for proving uniform convergence and continuity of function series.

Solar eclipses have historically inspired fear and religious interpretations. Ancient Greeks, Vikings and Chinese viewed them as signs of divine anger, apocalypse or a dragon devouring the sun. During an 1878 American eclipse, some uninformed observers believed Judgment Day had arrived, leading to panic and one murder-suicide. Although astronomers reject claims that an eclipse accompanied Jesus’ crucifixion, some Christians feared the Aug. 21 eclipse signaled the end times. Cloistered nun Sister Mary Elizabeth reassured concerned Catholics that it was not an omen and planned to watch it with her community. Islamic tradition recounts Muhammad explaining that an eclipse coinciding with his son Ibrahim’s death was a sign of God, not recognition of a person’s death. Author David Baron says total eclipses remain profound even for nonreligious observers because their unfamiliar appearance creates awe and emphasizes humanity’s smallness within the universe.

KGI analyst Ming-Chi Kuo predicted that the 2017 Apple Watch would retain its existing design and 38mm and 42mm sizes, with LTE and non-LTE models. The watch’s only previous design change was a slight thickness increase. A major redesign could require significant interface and app changes, while LTE may make reducing size difficult. Non-LTE models could potentially use power savings for longer battery life or a thinner design.

A funnel-web spider was found inside a Springwood home in the Blue Mountains near Sydney. Funnel-webs, common but rarely seen around homes on Australia’s east coast, have large fangs and venom that can rapidly cause severe symptoms including nausea, muscle cramps, sweating and mouth numbness. Australia has recorded 13 deaths, but none since antivenom was developed in 1981. Taronga Zoo keeper Paul Hare said funnel-webs are defensive rather than aggressive and usually bite only when threatened. Males often roam during mating season, particularly on cool evenings. People bitten should go to hospital immediately. Residents in funnel-web areas should avoid handling them, wear gloves while gardening and use caution around pools and outdoor objects. Hare advised leaving the spiders alone because they help control insects.

A recent music education graduate living at home asks how to manage conflict with an unemployed mother who demands $480 monthly for rent and phone costs. The graduate will earn about $1,600 monthly from a three-month minimum-wage job while owing tuition and certification expenses and needing savings for a car and apartment. The mother imposed rent after an argument related to the graduate’s hearing problems and previously took $3,000 for rent from a $5,000 school refund without returning the balance.

The response recommends budgeting remaining income toward debts, exams, transportation, or housing; considering additional work; using the period before teaching to explore other jobs and gain experience; and honestly examining both sides of the strained relationship. It notes that the mother’s alleged conduct would be abnormal and potentially warrant professional help, while urging the graduate to accept responsibility if relevant details were omitted.

President James Madison’s September 1, 1814 proclamation condemns British forces for invading Washington, destroying public buildings and archives, plundering Alexandria, and threatening further coastal destruction. He characterizes these actions as violations of humanity and civilized warfare, rejects Britain’s claim that they retaliated for American destruction in Upper Canada, and urges Americans to unite against the invaders. Madison directs civil and military officers to fulfill their duties, authorizes district commanders to mobilize nearby militia to defend threatened areas, and appeals to citizens’ patriotism, national independence, and inherited legacy.

The team suffered a frustrating playoff loss after surrendering two-goal leads and allowing too many third-period chances. Detroit battled hard, and the team must rebound despite showing tenacity and playing well.

The speaker pledges to fulfill the presidency faithfully under the Constitution, whose purposes include union, justice, tranquillity, defense, welfare, and liberty. He credits the constitutional government with expanding the population and territory, admitting new states, advancing commerce and invention, preserving freedom, and operating economically, while acknowledging war, disease, foreign injustice, and internal dissension.

He argues that past political parties both contributed talent and patriotism, and that peace has reduced partisan conflict. He urges citizens to abandon party rancor and uphold popular elections, limited federal and state powers, fiscal accountability, civilian control of the military, freedom of the press and religion, peace, and national union. He emphasizes mutual respect between state and federal governments as protection against sectional divisions.

The speaker praises his predecessor’s administration for maintaining peace, reducing taxes and debt, improving military organization and accountability, acquiring Florida, extending the national boundary to the Pacific, recognizing independent southern nations, strengthening defenses, opposing the African slave trade, and promoting exploration, education, and internal improvements. He intends to continue these policies, particularly constitutionally authorized public works, which he regards as a lasting benefit to future generations.

Acknowledging the unusual election and his limited initial public confidence, he promises integrity, devotion, and diligent service. He seeks cooperation from Congress, executive departments, state governments, and the people, and entrusts his administration and the country’s future to divine providence.

The speaker described a tight hockey game decided by mistakes, blocked shots and favorable bounces for the opponent. His team created scoring chances but failed to capitalize, including a breakaway and a puck that rested on Osgood’s back before being covered. He supported taking a timeout because the defensemen had been on the ice for a long shift. He also acknowledged striking an opposing player on the foot after continued verbal provocation. Despite conceding goals at key times, the team kept competing and generated opportunities. He said the unpredictable boards made play faster and harder to read, but remained confident the team could prepare quickly, win the next game and return home.

The global aluminum foil packaging market is projected to grow at about 4.5% CAGR, driven by packaging innovation, emerging economies, changing lifestyles, increased spending power, and demand from pharmaceutical and cosmetic industries. Aluminum provides hygienic, non-toxic, corrosion-resistant protection against contamination and light while reducing waste. Companies are adopting sustainable, active, and intelligent packaging and optimizing production locations and supply distances. Limited recycling infrastructure may constrain growth. Asia Pacific is expected to grow fastest due to rising incomes and consumer purchasing power.

At least 30 children died at Gorakhpur’s BRD Hospital, which reportedly held 10 times its admission capacity, forcing infants to share warmers. A central team cited overcrowding, oxygen problems, inadequate monitoring, and absent or non-functional nearby newborn units. Officials announced an Rs 85-crore regional research centre for children’s diseases.

May 9, 2001 reports covered Enron’s activities in Japan and India, energy markets, Wall Street, and Questia Media.

Enron said Japan’s deregulated electricity market remained uncompetitive because of regulations, transmission costs, and incumbent utilities’ influence. It advocated an independent regulator and planned an LNG-fired power plant in northern Japan.

In India, Enron’s Dabhol project faced possible termination after Maharashtra State Electricity Board payment defaults and disputes over costly power. Families of expatriate executives reportedly relocated to Singapore, while security increased. MSEB denied underusing its own capacity, citing limited natural gas and high alternative-fuel costs, and denied federal pressure to retain the Enron agreement. It appointed former judge M.L. Pendse as arbitrator. Lenders indicated they might support terminating the power purchase agreement unless governments resolved the crisis. The Swadeshi Jagran Manch demanded a judicial investigation. Prize Petroleum sought Enron’s 30% interest in the Panna, Mukta, and Tapti fields.

Williams planned a London operation to trade energy and provide risk-management services to European utilities without acquiring major physical assets.

Questia Media eliminated 139 jobs, reducing staff to about 140, because funding was difficult and book digitization was slowing. Its paying subscribers reportedly exceeded 5,000, and it projected positive cash flow in 18 months.

U.S. markets were mixed: the Dow fell 51.66 points, Nasdaq gained 25.20, and Enron shares dropped $1.93 to $56.11.

MyWorld is a gaming platform that lets players create, customize, store, and share their own games. Users control objects, genres, scenes, rules, and multiplayer formats, including single-player, PvP, and co-op. Design mode enables object placement, while constructor mode provides model editing for functional creations such as turrets, sensors, and robots. Players can level up to unlock materials and customize avatars. Following a livestream demonstration, the development team launched a Kickstarter campaign to fund completion, offering exclusive materials to early backers.

Researchers used the Multiphase Optimization Strategy to identify effective components of a mobile health intervention for insufficient sleep in children. Ninety-seven children aged 9–12 years with average weeknight sleep below 8.5 hours completed a two-week run-in, seven-week intervention, and two-week follow-up. All received Fitbit-based sleep tracking and weekly performance feedback. A factorial design tested guideline-based versus personalized sleep goals, child- and caregiver-directed loss-framed financial incentives, screen-time reduction messaging, and daily-routine messaging.

Baseline sleep averaged 7.7 hours nightly. Overall, sleep increased by 24 minutes during the intervention and 21 minutes during follow-up. No individual component met the prespecified optimization criterion of a ≥30-minute increase.

Two component combinations met the criterion. The highest-ranked combined the core intervention with a caregiver-directed incentive and messaging about screen-time reduction and daily routines; either sleep goal was effective. It increased sleep by 39.6 minutes during intervention and 33.2 minutes during follow-up. The second combined the core intervention with a caregiver-directed incentive and daily-routine messaging, increasing sleep by 32.0 and 26.6 minutes, respectively. Child-directed incentives were not beneficial, while guideline-based goals were generally more favorable.

The authors identified sleep tracking, performance feedback, a sleep goal, caregiver-directed loss-framed incentives, and screen-time and routine messaging as the optimal package for further randomized evaluation. Limitations included one geographic site, a predominantly non-Hispanic White sample, fewer captured nights among Black participants, short follow-up, and reliance on a single-sensor commercial sleep tracker.

Successful Forex trading does not require exceptional talent or promise quick profits. Traders should wait for suitable setups, make independent decisions, and avoid being misled by external opinions. Mental stability and controlled risk are essential for handling losses, alongside mastery of technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysis. Traders may learn from experts but should develop their own strategies and judgment rather than copy others. Beginners should progress gradually, using advice to gain knowledge while carefully evaluating whether to follow it.

Apple announced that Angela Ahrendts, Senior Vice President of Retail, would depart effective April 15, 2019. Deirdre O’Brien succeeded her as Senior Vice President, Retail + People, effective February 5, 2019.

The paper examines weak permission in deontic argumentation, where an action is weakly permitted when an obligation to the contrary cannot be justified. Standard grounded and stable argumentation semantics fail to support weak permission when equally applicable obligations conflict: neither obligation is justified, yet the corresponding weak permissions are also not justified.

To address this limitation, the authors define Deontic Argumentation Theories using facts, rules, natural arguments, and imaginary arguments representing potential weak permissions. They introduce a fixed-point “wp-semantics” that iteratively classifies arguments as acceptable or rejected. An imaginary weak-permission argument is accepted when all arguments supporting the contrary obligation are rejected; natural arguments are accepted when supported and their attackers are undercut or rejected.

The paper proves that the wp-extension is unique and conflict-free, that no argument is both justified and rejected, and that every argument justified under grounded semantics is also justified under wp-semantics. Most importantly, when opposing obligations remain unresolved, wp-semantics justifies weak permission for both alternatives, allowing downstream rules based on weak facultativeness to apply.

The discussion argues that conflicting norms from the same legal system should not arbitrarily produce one justified obligation when no conflict-resolution mechanism exists. Instead, neither obligation should be justified, yielding weak permissions for both actions. The paper distinguishes strong permissions explicitly mandated by norms from weak permissions arising through failure to establish a prohibition. It concludes that the proposed semantics remedies the inability of grounded and stable semantics to represent weak permission under unresolved deontic conflict.

Tesla’s October 7, 2021 annual meeting addressed nine proposals. Stockholders elected James Murdoch and Kimbal Musk as Class II directors. Management proposals to shorten director terms to two years and eliminate supermajority voting requirements failed to meet the required two-thirds threshold. PricewaterhouseCoopers was ratified as auditor. Advisory proposals supporting one-year director terms and additional diversity and inclusion reporting passed. Proposals concerning employee arbitration, board oversight of human capital management, and human rights reporting failed. Tesla filed the report on October 13, 2021.

Imran Mohammad, a Rohingya refugee recognized by UNHCR, describes spending four years in detention on Manus Island after arriving in Papua New Guinea at age 19. He recounts overcrowded shipping containers, extreme heat, long queues, inadequate toilets and laundry facilities, scarce supplies, hunger, restricted phone access, and insufficient space for prayer or recreation. The conditions caused isolation, anguish, and suicidal thoughts. Mohammad coped by avoiding crowds, focusing on education and writing, and adopting “the pen is mightier than the sword” as his motto. Now 23, he mourns four birthdays spent in indefinite detention and says those seeking safety in Australia instead received pain, anguish, and sometimes death.

A consumer electricals company submitted a September 20, 2017 bid for Kenstar’s business and brand following Videocon’s invitation. The price and outcome were undisclosed, with no negotiations or binding documents. Debt-laden Videocon has pursued asset sales to reduce over Rs 40,000 crore in debt.

The National Technology Security Coalition and Cloud Security Alliance are partnering to improve cloud vendor security reviews by promoting CSA’s Security, Trust & Assurance Registry and related tools. They plan to develop a STAR-based questionnaire mapped to common compliance frameworks and publish guidance for CISOs and vendors. The partnership seeks to streamline vetting, reduce review burdens, increase transparency, and encourage security best practices. The organizations will also participate in joint events, working groups, and cloud security research. CSA focuses on cloud security standards, education, certification, and assurance, while NTSC advocates for CISOs and stronger national cybersecurity policies.

Daniella Teutsch and Sara Wolf founded HydroChic in 2007 to create attractive, modest swimwear. Customer feedback revealed demand from women needing support, concealment, compression, or skin protection after medical procedures or because of conditions such as skin cancer and psoriasis. HydroChic expanded its products accordingly, making special health needs a profitable and personally rewarding business focus. Former educators and hat sales representatives, the founders conceived the company after struggling to find modest swimsuits as religious Jewish women.

Riley Oil Company, a family-owned business in Paoli, Indiana, has operated since 1971. One of the area’s last full-service gas stations, it pumps gas, washes windshields and checks oil without additional charge. Six Riley family members work there, and the owners hope future generations will continue the business. Employees and owners value conversations with customers, who appreciate remaining in their cars while receiving service.

A 52-year-old woman allegedly threatened Oklahoma City Taco Bell employees with a tire iron, demanded money, and caused thousands of dollars in damage. After ignoring an officer’s commands, she was tased, hospitalized for cuts, and jailed on property destruction and robbery charges.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K on June 2, 2022, revising its guidance for the quarter ending June 30, 2022, due to unfavorable foreign exchange rate movements through May. The revised guidance was provided in an attached slide deck, Exhibit 99.1. The report includes forward-looking-statement cautions and was signed by Chief Accounting Officer Alice L. Jolla.

Nintendo’s Labo will include Toy Con Garage, a toolkit using basic inputs, actions, and if-then statements to create custom cardboard accessories. Nintendo demonstrated a cardboard electric guitar and electronic tennis. Whether a Labo set is required for app access remains unclear.

Higher education legal experts expect the Supreme Court to address major issues affecting colleges, although only two transgender-rights cases are currently on its main docket. Increasingly, consequential decisions occur through the shadow, or emergency, docket, which allows rapid interim rulings without full briefing, oral arguments or written explanations. Experts say this creates uncertainty and can permit irreversible policy changes before full review.

West Virginia v. B.P.J. and Little v. Hecox concern state laws barring transgender female athletes from women’s sports. Hecox has requested dismissal because of illness, her father’s death and negative publicity, but the West Virginia case is expected to continue. Its interpretation of Title IX could affect collegiate sports, bathrooms, locker rooms and other sex-segregated activities.

Experts are also monitoring emergency-docket disputes involving federal staffing cuts, immigration policies, First Amendment rights, academic freedom and federal funding. Trump v. Orr, concerning gender markers on passports, could affect university housing and identification practices if applied more broadly. The Court has so far lifted injunctions blocking Trump administration policies in every higher education case reaching the shadow docket. Experts warn that even if later merits rulings reject those policies, institutional damage may already be irreversible.

Unregulated high-seas fishing complicates stock assessments and increases overfishing risks. In the Southwest Atlantic, over 250 vessels annually catch large quantities of squid, hake and rock cod, while nearly 300 jiggers target jumbo squid in the Eastern Pacific. Falkland Islands scientist Alexander Arkhipkin joined a 2017 Peruvian workshop that developed recommendations on surveys, stock structure and assessment methods to improve understanding of jumbo squid and the impact of high-seas fisheries.

Darren Till won a controversial unanimous decision over Stephen Thompson at UFC Fight Night 130 in Liverpool. Amid criticism of the judging, Till offered an immediate rematch in America, predicting the same outcome and suggesting he could be more aggressive. The close fight featured little action besides Till’s final-round knockdown.

Molecular dynamics simulations examined nanoindentation of single-crystalline α-titanium along [0001], [10̅10], and [2̅110] orientations at 10, 300, and 600 K. Atom-resolved Schmid factor, dislocation, strain, and surface morphology analyses linked crystallographic orientation and temperature to slip activation and plastic deformation.

The [0001] orientation showed the clearest pop-in, greatest residual indentation, and highest dislocation density. Basal a-type dislocations dominated, while prismatic and pyramidal systems also contributed. The prismatic orientations exhibited smoother plasticity onset, lower dislocation densities, and greater recovery. Their surface patterns differed: [10̅10] produced symmetric dual-lobe pile-up, [2̅110] produced asymmetric curved pile-up, and [0001] developed circular or quasi-hexagonal features.

Increasing temperature reduced contact pressure, enhanced dislocation mobility, broadened plastic zones, and made surface traces more diffuse. Recovery and annihilation lowered residual dislocation density in the prismatic orientations, whereas density increased with temperature for [0001]. The simulations reproduced surface features consistent with reported AFM observations and demonstrated that temperature and orientation jointly govern slip, phase transformation, defect retention, and nanoscale plasticity in α-titanium.

The Justice Department asked the Education Department to investigate whether the University of Nevada at Reno’s UndocuPack program improperly uses taxpayer funds to support undocumented students. UNR president Brian Sandoval defended the program, saying it serves all students, uses no federal funds and complies with aid eligibility laws. He said the university would respond through legal channels.

Advocates describe the action as an escalation of federal efforts to restrict higher education benefits and services for undocumented students. The administration has challenged in-state tuition policies, scholarships, and access to adult and career education. Advocates argue federal law has not been interpreted to prohibit university resource centers, mentoring, or academic and career support. They fear institutions may reduce lawful programs to avoid scrutiny, potentially signaling to undocumented students that they do not belong.

The Bank of England said major capital and liquidity reforms are largely complete following Basel III. Future priorities include emerging risks, regulatory side effects, cyber resilience, and leverage rules that may discourage central clearing of derivative trades.

The disclosure describes physical-layer preambles and signaling for wireless communications, particularly IEEE 802.11be and later protocols. A wireless packet may contain legacy fields, a universal signal field (U-SIG), version-specific signaling such as an Extremely High Throughput signal field (EHT-SIG), training fields, and data. U-SIG may identify the protocol version, packet format, uplink or downlink direction, bandwidth, punctured subchannels, BSS color, transmission opportunity duration, and information needed to decode EHT-SIG. Packet formats include trigger-based, single-user, multi-user, and unified single-/multi-user formats.

EHT-SIG may provide resource-unit allocations, spatial-stream configurations, modulation and coding information, and user-specific scheduling. Designs support OFDMA, MU-MIMO, punctured transmissions, multiple content channels, bandwidths up to or beyond 320 MHz, and up to or beyond 16 spatial streams. Signaling may be duplicated or parallelized across bonded subchannels, while punctured subchannels may omit signaling. Proposed encoding, compression, allocation tables, and field arrangements seek to reduce preamble length and signaling overhead while supporting flexible resource assignments and future protocols.

Receiving devices determine packet format and occupied subchannels from U-SIG, then decode corresponding version-specific fields. The techniques may be implemented by access points, stations, processors, systems, or computer-readable media across various wireless networks and radio technologies.

The invention provides systems and methods for processing mobile payments when user devices or merchant payment systems cannot connect to payment servers. A user device with an enabled offline payment mode receives a merchant’s payment request through local communications, such as Bluetooth, NFC, LAN, USB, or QR codes. After confirming sufficient reserved funds and obtaining user approval, the device sends a payment approval, updates its remaining offline balance, and stores transaction information.

Both the user device and merchant system may submit the stored transaction to a payment server after connectivity returns. The server processes the first submission, debits the payer, credits the merchant, updates the reserved offline amount, and uses transaction identifiers to prevent duplicate processing.

For each e-wallet, offline mode is enabled on only one associated user device at a time to reduce the risk of exceeding reserved funds or overdrawing accounts. The payment server maintains e-wallet configurations and offline-mode statuses. Offline mode may be transferred between devices through the server or, when both devices are offline, through local communications involving handover data, confirmation, disabling the original device, and enabling the receiving device. The functionality may be implemented as methods, computer systems, program products, or cloud-based services.

Aaron Judge will have his injured elbow evaluated this offseason and is unsure whether surgery will be necessary. The July injury sidelined him for 10 days and temporarily limited him to designated hitter duties. His throwing strength remained diminished, though his hitting stayed strong throughout the regular season and playoffs.

Microsoft’s fiscal 2021 Form 10-K describes a technology business providing software, cloud services, devices, gaming, advertising, and consulting. Its three operating segments are Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. Strategic priorities include productivity tools, Azure and intelligent-edge infrastructure, AI, security, Windows, and gaming. Microsoft acquired ZeniMax and agreed to acquire Nuance Communications. It employed approximately 181,000 people and emphasized hybrid work, diversity, employee development, sustainability, digital skills, and racial equity. Key risks include intense competition, changing platforms and business models, cloud execution, cybersecurity, reliability, and declining margins. As of July 26, 2021, 7.51 billion shares were outstanding.

Martin Colin Hodder, 45, was jailed for 18 weeks after admitting two assaults on his ex-partner and her daughter in Macclesfield. After drinking one and a half bottles of vodka, he threatened and cut both women with a butter knife while also injuring himself. Magistrates described it as a sustained, alcohol-fuelled domestic attack and imposed a year-long restraining order. His ex-partner condemned the sentence as inadequate.

The High Post Split Offense uses a 2-3 high alignment, quick post splits, down screens, back cuts and post-ups. Its open baseline, balanced scoring opportunities and limited weakside help make it difficult to defend while supporting strong offensive rebounding.

The basic action begins with a guard passing to the high post and splitting with the other guard. The post can feed either cutter. Counters include handoffs, fake splits, direct back cuts and sending both cutters to the same side. If no pass is available, the wings set down screens for the guards while the post may pass, shoot or drive. Down-screen reads produce curls, basket curls, fades, back cuts, screen-and-rolls, mismatch isolations and screen slips.

After the split, the high post faces the basket in triple-threat position, isolated for a shot, drive or pass. Overplay can be countered with a lob, wing feed, post exchange or screen exchange. The position should be occupied by the best triple-threat player. Players can also post up smaller defenders when defenses concentrate on shooters.

Entry variations include wing back cuts, wing passes, double-away screens and single/double-screen continuity. Each preserves options for cuts, screens, rolls, reversals and mismatches.

Success depends on spacing, timing, coordination, defensive recognition and unified action among the ballhandler, screener and receiver. Players must develop individual offensive skills and understand multiple defensive reads. Offensive rebounding requires anticipation, determination, hustle, repeated effort and boxing out defenders, especially when the high post shoots.

The disclosure describes a multi-panel tonneau cover for pickup-truck beds. Movable panel sections pivot and fold relative to a fixed base panel, allowing access to the bed and vertical or horizontal storage. Each panel may include paired spring-biased pinch-latch assemblies connected by a longitudinal panel, bar, or rod. Activating either pinch handle retracts latches on both sides from adjustable rail clips; releasing it returns both latches to the secured position.

The latch assemblies may be recessed substantially flush with panel frames to reduce cargo obstructions and improve security. Integrated removable lights can illuminate the truck bed and help locate the handles. Adjustable side rails attach to varied truck-bed walls and include tracks for latch clips, clamps, and support components. Seals along the rails, tailgate edge, and hinges reduce water entry.

A pivoting gusset assembly can engage the rails and panel latches to support folded panels vertically, then fold beneath the cover when unused. Hinge assemblies use resilient seals, spacers, and rods to permit panel movement while maintaining alignment and sealing. A separate securement system uses a channel bracket, strap, buckle, and receptacle to hold folded panels upright or horizontally, limit movement, and prevent contact with the base panel. The disclosed embodiments may incorporate these features individually or in combination.

The disclosure describes semiconductor packaging methods for large multi-die integrated fan-out modules. Tested interconnect structures, or a single universal interconnect structure, are mounted on a carrier, encapsulated, thinned, and connected to packaged or discrete semiconductor devices through redistribution layers, through-substrate vias, solder bonds, or low-temperature copper-to-copper bonds. Underfill and additional encapsulation protect the bonded components, after which the carrier is removed and external contacts are formed.

Interconnect structures may bridge or be shared among multiple processor, memory, and controller components. Stress-buffering layers, compatible coefficients of thermal expansion, lower bonding temperatures, and use of known-good tested components reduce delamination, connection failures, and component- and board-level reliability risks. The wafer-integrated process supports packages larger than 70 mm by 70 mm for high-performance computing, networking, servers, and artificial-intelligence applications requiring high data rates, bandwidth, and low latency.

Reports dated Nov. 26, 2001 described mounting doubts about Dynegy’s proposed acquisition of Enron, driving Enron shares to a 14-year low of $3.76 before closing at $4.01 and sharply depressing its bonds.
