Edinburgh University was criticised for asking law lecturers to provide past lecture recordings to replace classes missed during industrial action.

A National Academies report supports allowing heritable human DNA editing only to prevent serious, strongly inherited diseases when no reasonable alternatives exist, while opposing genetic enhancement for traits such as intelligence, strength or beauty. Germline editing remains illegal in the United States, but CRISPR-Cas9 has made precise gene editing increasingly feasible. The panel recommended rigorous risk-benefit assessment, public oversight addressing fairness and dignity, appropriate regulation, and long-term monitoring of effects on future generations. It also urged continued international public debate as scientific advances accelerate.

Aiden Markram said he was honoured to captain South Africa after Faf du Plessis withdrew with a finger injury. Despite added pressure and responsibility, Markram expects support from senior players and advice from Du Plessis. With the Proteas trailing India 1-0 in the six-match series, he called for an improved all-round performance in the second ODI.

Chronic hepatitis C can progress to cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, serious complications, and extrahepatic disorders including type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). HCV infection increases T2DM risk, while viral clearance may reduce it. Although the prognostic nutritional index (PNI), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR) reflect nutritional or inflammatory status and predict outcomes in cancers, their prognostic value in HCV-associated cirrhosis with T2DM remains unclear.

This study evaluated these markers in patients treated at Fu yang Second People’s Hospital from January 2018 to December 2021. Participants included 56 patients with HCV-associated cirrhosis and T2DM, 85 with HCV-associated cirrhosis, and 85 with T2DM. After six months of treatment, the combined-disease group was classified into poor-prognosis (23) and good-prognosis (33) groups. Admission laboratory measurements included albumin, AST, ALT, and blood-cell counts. NLR was calculated as neutrophils divided by lymphocytes, PNI as albumin plus five times the lymphocyte count, and PLR as platelets divided by lymphocytes. Ethical approval and written informed consent were obtained.

The Rubber Band trading strategy is a contrarian, mean-reversion approach primarily used for stocks. It identifies overbought or oversold prices expected to return toward their mean, using tools such as Keltner Channels, Bollinger Bands, or momentum oscillators. With Keltner Channels, prices above the upper band suggest a possible downward reversal, while prices below the lower band suggest a possible upward reversal. Reversal candlestick patterns may provide confirmation, though they require backtesting. Profit targets are typically near the middle band or the opposite band.

The strategy relies on buying amid excessive negative sentiment and selling during market euphoria. An XLP backtest produced 328 trades, a 0.45% average gain per trade, 6.1% CAGR, a profit factor of 2, 16% maximum drawdown, and 20% market exposure. The approach reportedly works mainly on stocks and is more difficult to apply to assets such as gold and commodities.

Singapore police arrested eight women for allegedly advertising sexual services, 14 men over illegal gambling, and one man for drink-driving during a May 21–27 operation. About 700 people across more than 70 units in Yishun, Ang Mo Kio and Sengkang were checked. Cash and 10 phones were seized; investigations continue.

Google added speech recognition for 30 languages and locales, bringing its total to 119. The expansion includes eight Indian languages, Swahili and Amharic, initially available in Gboard for Android, Voice Search and the Cloud Speech API, with future support planned for products such as Google Translate. U.S. English users can also dictate emojis. Aimed particularly at growing mobile internet markets in India and Africa, the technology was developed by combining native-speaker speech samples with machine learning to improve recognition accuracy.

Saints begin their Anglo-Welsh Cup campaign at Exeter Chiefs on November 4, before hosting Dragons, visiting Sale Sharks and hosting Harlequins. Grouped with Saracens, Scarlets and Worcester Warriors, they must top their pool to reach the semi-finals.

Shonda Rhimes’ Shondaland signed a deal to create new series for Netflix, though financial terms and duration were undisclosed. Existing shows including “Grey’s Anatomy,” “Scandal” and “How to Get Away With Murder” will remain on ABC. Rhimes said Netflix offered opportunities to expand her audience and creative identity.

Alere said financial statements for 2013-2015 should not be relied upon due to misstatements, primarily involving South Korean revenue recognition. A Japanese transaction shifted about $1 million from 2012 to 2013. Material control weaknesses remain, and its first-quarter filing may be delayed.

CoreLogic reported U.S. home prices rose 7.1% annually and 1.1% monthly in May 2018, driven by limited supply and strong demand. Of the 100 largest metropolitan markets, 40% were overvalued, 26% undervalued and 34% fairly valued. Utah, Washington, Nevada and Idaho posted double-digit annual gains. CoreLogic forecast 5.1% national growth through May 2019, while noting renters’ strong interest in buying despite high prices and mortgage rates.

The American Academy of Pediatrics advises that five commonly ordered tests may be unnecessary for otherwise healthy children who are short, overweight or show limited signs of early puberty. These include certain hormone, endocrine, vitamin D, thyroid and insulin tests, and thyroid ultrasounds. Testing should be guided by specific concerns, such as abnormal growth rates, significant short stature relative to parental height, bone disorders, thyroid symptoms or marked thyroid enlargement. The AAP urges doctors and families to weigh risks, benefits, costs and potential anxiety.

TeraAgent is a distributed extension of BioDynaMo designed to overcome single-server limits in agent-based simulations. It partitions simulation space across MPI ranks and supports aura exchanges, agent migration, and load balancing while largely hiding distributed execution from users.

To reduce communication overhead, TeraAgent introduces a serialization mechanism that directly uses mutable objects from received buffers, avoiding unnecessary pointer deduplication, endian conversion, schema evolution, and most deserialization work. It also applies delta encoding and compression to exploit gradual changes between simulation iterations. Communication uses non-blocking MPI, while global and diffusive methods balance workloads.

Evaluations show that TeraAgent reproduces BioDynaMo results and can run largely unchanged models across laptops, servers, clouds, and supercomputers. It simulated 501.51 billion agents on 84,096 CPU cores, compared with BioDynaMo’s reported 1.7-billion-agent limit. It achieved eight times Biocellion’s agent-update efficiency per CPU core and improved ParaView in-situ visualization performance by 39 times. Its serialization reached median speedups of 110 times and deserialization 37 times, while delta encoding reduced transferred data by up to 3.5 times. Compression improved runtime in most tested simulations, although delta-encoding overhead prevented further runtime gains on a high-bandwidth, low-latency interconnect.

This ADNI study evaluated whether plasma biomarkers combined with MRI, demographics, APOE4, and baseline cognitive scores could predict cognitive decline and progression to mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or dementia in non-demented individuals. Two cohorts were analyzed: one with plasma NfL and p-tau181, and a subset also containing Aβ42/40. Participants had at least two years of follow-up.

A two-stage machine-learning framework used ridge linear regression to derive MRI scores and random forest regression to predict annual changes in composite measures of memory, executive function, language, and visuospatial ability. Models included basic clinical variables alone or added plasma biomarkers, MRI, or both. Performance was assessed through repeated nested 10-fold cross-validation.

For memory decline, adding plasma biomarkers improved correlation from 0.38 to 0.45, while the combined plasma-MRI model achieved 0.50. Biomarkers offered limited improvement in other domains, except language. MRI and baseline cognitive scores were generally the strongest predictors; NfL and p-tau181 contributed more than Aβ42/40. Biomarkers and MRI had little importance for visuospatial decline.

Prediction was substantially more accurate in MCI than cognitively unimpaired participants, particularly for memory, executive function, and language. Predicted memory decline best forecast progression: the combined model achieved C-indices of 0.76 for progression from cognitively unimpaired status to MCI or dementia and 0.79 for progression from MCI to dementia. Individuals in the highest predicted-decline tertile had over 33 times the progression risk among cognitively unimpaired participants and over 29 times the risk among those with MCI compared with the lowest tertile.

The findings support combining plasma biomarkers with MRI and cognitive assessments, especially for predicting memory decline and dementia progression. Limitations include reliance on AD-specific biomarkers and the ADNI cohort, which may reduce generalizability to non-memory domains and other dementias.

A vehicle driver-monitoring and vision system uses interior and exterior cameras, vehicle sensors, and an electronic control unit to estimate driver attention from driving workload and distraction workload, optionally relative to a maximum workload. Inputs may include driver identity, behavior, posture, emotion, health, gaze, drowsiness, vehicle control, media use, passengers, traffic, road, weather, visibility, and driving duration.

Driving and distraction workloads may receive dynamically adjusted weights based on conditions, testing, operation, or prior behavior of a specific driver. Driver attention may be calculated by subtracting weighted workloads from the maximum workload and expressed as a percentage. System modules assign states, confidence levels, availability values, and calibration weights or functions to inputs and outputs. Machine learning may adjust calibration elements and predict future outputs.

The system can identify attentive, distracted, drowsy, or overloaded drivers, reflecting the premise that attention is finite and increased task difficulty can reduce performance elsewhere. Passenger monitoring may refine distraction estimates, such as when a passenger operates the radio.

Image processing may detect vehicles, pedestrians, hazards, or other objects, display images or alerts, and highlight detected objects. If the driver is not attending to a hazard, the system may autonomously brake or steer when risk exceeds a threshold. The system may use cameras, radar, lidar, ultrasonic sensors, vehicle networks, and vehicle-to-vehicle or vehicle-to-infrastructure communications.

In autonomous vehicles, “driver” includes an occupant positioned to assume control when required. The system may monitor that occupant’s readiness and attention during autonomous or semi-autonomous operation.

A district judge ordered Texas State University to reinstate history professor Thomas Alter without pay or teaching duties after his termination over a socialism conference speech. Alter alleges free speech, due process and contract violations. The university will review his case while litigation continues.

Letters published by Grassroots Leadership describe women’s experiences in immigration detention and the anguish of separation from their children. One anonymous Guatemalan woman said she spent eight days in a chain-link holding facility near Hidalgo, Texas, called “la perrera,” without bathing or brushing her teeth, sleeping on the floor under aluminum blankets. She was separated from her 17-year-old son upon arrival and her 9-year-old daughter the next day, then waited 21 days before speaking with them. Her children were eventually released to their father, and she was released June 26 after transfers to Laredo and the T. Don Hutto Residential Center.

Other women wrote emotional messages to their children or appealed publicly for reunification, describing limited contact, uncertainty, and severe distress. Grassroots Leadership volunteers helped women at Hutto share the letters to seek release and reunification. ICE said it could not address specific mistreatment allegations because names and facility details were unclear or redacted.

The application describes displaying marker elements for user- or teammate-marked items directly within a virtual scene. A terminal receives marker indication information, obtains and renders marker graphics, and displays them near the target item. A server may synchronize markers among team members based on each controlled object’s visible distance. Markers can identify selected types or marking users, show straight-line, horizontal, or height-distance information, and appear on thumbnail maps. Users may select targets with a crosshair and choose marker types. Markers can be hidden when targets are outside visibility conditions or removed after preset durations. The disclosure also covers corresponding terminal apparatuses, computer devices, modules, and non-transitory computer-readable storage media.

Pairs trading is a statistical-arbitrage strategy that simultaneously buys one asset and shorts another historically related asset, seeking profit when their price spread converges after diverging. It is intended to be market-neutral, although differences in beta, volatility, leverage, fundamentals, and company performance mean positions may remain exposed to market risk.

Pairs may include stocks, ETFs, futures, currencies, or options. Selection commonly considers historical correlation, cointegration, technical indicators, and shared fundamental or industry factors. Cointegration may be more useful than correlation because it measures the stability of the difference between two assets over time.

Advantages include potential returns in rising, falling, or sideways markets and returns that may be uncorrelated with the broader market. Risks and disadvantages include leverage, short-borrowing costs, commissions, slippage, four transactions per trade, hard-to-borrow stocks, unstable relationships, sudden spread shifts, and rare large losses that can erase many small gains.

Research cited reports average annualized excess returns of roughly 11% to 15.92%, though transaction costs and methodology affect results. Backtests of KO/PEP and GS/MS produced returns below buying and holding the S&P 500, while a modified GS/MS exit rule improved results. The passage concludes that pairs trading can remain profitable, but opportunities have diminished, diversification and fundamental understanding are important, and the strategy offers no easy profits.

Soil-transmitted helminths infect more than one billion people, mainly in marginalized populations. WHO recommends sanitation, hygiene education and preventive chemotherapy (PC), with impact assessment surveys (IAS) typically conducted after five years to determine whether treatment should continue. Conventional surveys are costly and often disregard baseline and implementation data.

The paper proposes a model-based geostatistical (MBG) approach that combines baseline prevalence, environmental risk factors, PC coverage history and candidate sampling locations. It models species-specific baseline prevalence surfaces, uses a multi-state Markov model to project changes among five endemicity classes based on effective PC rounds, and applies local thinning to estimate prevalence at impact. Candidate survey designs vary the number of schools, children per school, inclusion probabilities and minimum distances between sampled locations. Their performance is evaluated through simulations and treatment-classification accuracy.

The method was applied to Kenya, Sierra Leone and Zimbabwe. Kenya’s longitudinal data were used to estimate transition probabilities, while actual impact surveys served as reference standards. Projected and actual prevalence surfaces were similar in Kenya but differed more in Sierra Leone and Zimbabwe, whose endemicity levels differed from Kenya’s.

At equivalent accuracy, MBG designs substantially reduced sample sizes and estimated survey costs. Average cost reduction was 80%, including 91% in Zimbabwe, 86% in Kenya and 62% in Sierra Leone. The approach also produces detailed prevalence maps that may identify residual hotspots. The authors are developing guidance and a web application, and state that the framework could be adapted to other neglected tropical diseases.

Researchers studying blood samples from 40 ALS patients and 28 controls found that ALS patients had stronger T cell responses to C9orf72, a neuron-associated protein, while responses to TDP-43 and SOD1 were similar between groups. Patients with C9orf72 mutations showed stronger responses, and those whose T cells produced more anti-inflammatory IL-10 were predicted to survive longer than patients with more inflammatory responses.

The findings suggest autoimmunity may contribute to ALS and could potentially provide targets for treatment or disease monitoring. However, researchers cautioned that the study does not establish ALS as an autoimmune disease because self-reactive T cells may result from neuronal damage rather than cause disease progression. Larger studies and animal models are planned to test whether these immune cells drive ALS.

Henrik Lundqvist said the team was disappointed by a late first-period goal and its current situation but still believes it can turn the series around. He felt the games have been close, with a few plays, deflections and some luck making the difference. Lundqvist said he has tracked the puck well but must raise his level, focus on each shot and help secure the team’s first win. He emphasized starting strongly, working hard, limiting mistakes, creating traffic at the net and earning opportunities against a skilled, defensively strong opponent and goaltender.

The S&P 500 gained 2.2% in July, reaching 7.8% year to date, and remained above its 10-month moving average for a third month. Frontier markets led monthly returns, while global stocks outperformed U.S. large caps year to date. Stocks rose and bonds fell during July. However, the index dropped 1.6% on August’s first day, volatility and credit spreads showed seasonal increases, and short-term technical indicators weakened. Portfolios are increasingly concentrated in technology stocks, while U.S. electricity demand reached a record high. Despite near-term risks and seasonal headwinds, medium- and long-term trend indicators remained healthy.

Tesla Motors’ unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2016 reported third-quarter revenue of $2.30 billion, up from $936.8 million a year earlier, gross profit of $636.7 million, operating income of $85.6 million, and net income of $21.9 million, or $0.15 per basic share. For the first nine months, revenue was $4.72 billion and net loss was $553.6 million. Operating activities generated $324.4 million in cash, investing used $821.7 million, and financing provided $2.37 billion.

At September 30, Tesla had $3.08 billion in cash and equivalents, $12.59 billion in total assets, $9.90 billion in liabilities, and $2.68 billion in stockholders’ equity. Inventory totaled $1.60 billion, property and equipment totaled $4.31 billion, customer deposits were $690.4 million, and accrued warranty reserves were $226.8 million. Tesla raised approximately $1.7 billion through a May 2016 common-stock offering.

Tesla produced approximately 25,180 vehicles in the third quarter, including about 10,450 Model X vehicles, a 37% production increase from the prior quarter. It planned approximately 50,000 deliveries in the second half of 2016, targeted Model 3 volume production and deliveries in the second half of 2017, and aimed for annual production of 500,000 vehicles in 2018. The company expected substantial capital requirements and described this production increase as challenging.

Tesla continued expanding vehicle, energy-product, sales, service, charging, Gigafactory, and Fremont manufacturing operations. It expected 2016 operating expenses to rise approximately 30% from 2015, excluding the proposed SolarCity acquisition. Gigafactory costs incurred totaled $608.4 million, and cell production was expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2016.

Tesla agreed to acquire SolarCity in an all-stock transaction using an exchange ratio of 0.110 Tesla shares per SolarCity share, subject to closing conditions and shareholder votes scheduled for November 17, 2016. In October, Tesla purchased 24.5 acres adjacent to its Fremont factory for $30.8 million.

Risks cited included production ramp difficulties, supplier concentration and shortages, manufacturing inefficiencies, international expansion, substantial capital needs, vehicle residual values, financing availability, Gigafactory costs and timing, legal proceedings, and differences between forward-looking expectations and actual results.

Cryptocurrency-related crime is rising in Japan despite an overall decline in reported crime. Coincheck’s January theft of 523 million NEM coins, valued at ¥58 billion, highlighted security concerns previously raised by the Financial Services Agency. Japan plays a major role in cryptocurrency trading, recognizing bitcoin as legal tender and registering 16 exchanges, though Coincheck was not among them. Earlier incidents include Mt. Gox’s 2014 collapse, alleged Ripple-related fraud, and ransomware attacks. Authorities are also concerned about initial coin offerings, which can fund startups through digital tokens but carry risks of fraud, volatility, and total loss. The FSA has warned investors but ICO regulation remains uncertain. Facebook banned ICO advertising, while the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission halted an allegedly fraudulent $600 million ICO. Japan may pursue similar enforcement, but consumers currently invest at their own risk.

The priority is preventing scoring, avoiding turnovers, and winning two more games rather than personal records. Previous experience helps manage media attention, which is enjoyable but sometimes excessive.

An Ontario government-commissioned report recommends eliminating provincewide EQAO tests in Grades 3 and 9, removing the mandatory high school literacy graduation requirement, and reducing other standardized assessments while giving teachers more responsibility. Education Minister Indira Naidoo-Harris supported broader changes but deferred action pending consultation after the June 7 election. The passage argues that scaling back testing would weaken independent accountability and make systemic problems in literacy and mathematics harder to detect. Teachers’ organizations have long opposed standardized testing, while EQAO expressed concern that ending primary-division assessments would remove substantial independent data. The report supports reviewing testing, improving accessibility for First Nations students, and preventing school rankings. It was criticized for not consulting EQAO, despite the agency’s two decades of assessment work.

Motivate introduced 250 electric pedal-assist Ford GoBike Plus bicycles at stations across western San Francisco. Officials and cyclists demonstrated the bikes on steep Page Street, where electric assistance made climbing easier. The e-bikes aim to attract more users, accommodate the city’s hills, lengthen average trips, reduce reliance on cars and ride-hailing services, and improve connections to transit. San Francisco is the only city in the regional Ford GoBike program currently receiving e-bikes. Motivate emphasized that it coordinated with city agencies on station locations and fleet size, contrasting its approach with the sudden arrival of electric scooters.

Auswide Bank originated from mergers of building societies in Queensland’s Wide Bay Burnett region, later expanding to Sydney and Melbourne. It listed on the Australian Stock Exchange in 1994 and became a bank in 2015. Its mission emphasizes customer focus and competing with Australia’s four largest banks.

At June 30, 2020, Auswide reported AUD3.789 billion in assets, AUD3.206 billion in net loans, AUD3.019 billion in deposits and short-term borrowings, and AUD242.0 million in equity. Fiscal 2020 net interest revenue was AUD70.5 million, net profit after tax was AUD18.5 million, and dividends paid were AUD13.6 million.

The case presents representative fiscal 2021 transactions, including a AUD4.9 million share issue, AUD40 million term-facility borrowing, purchases of supplies and furniture, net customer deposits of AUD200 million, and net loan originations of AUD230 million. The bank received AUD120 million of loan interest, incurred AUD37 million of deposit interest, paid AUD24 million in employee benefits and AUD8 million in mortgage broker commissions, and sold a loan for a AUD50,000 gain. It also paid a AUD12 million dividend and recorded AUD3 million of depreciation and AUD8 million of loan impairment expense, with no goodwill impairment.

The assignment asks students to record these transactions using the balance-sheet equation, prepare a June 30, 2021 balance sheet, and calculate fiscal 2021 net income and cash flow, ignoring taxes and assuming no other transactions occurred.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa will form paediatrician-led committees to oversee an October measles vaccination campaign targeting 4.3 million children aged nine to 59 months. Officials emphasized staff training, quality vaccines, logistics, referral systems, communication and parental awareness. The campaign follows rising measles cases across nearly all provincial districts.
The speaker cherished joining Detroit, winning the Stanley Cup, and hopes to repeat. He respects the retiring coach and enjoyed this victory more because it lacked controversy and felt more familiar.

The Los Angeles Angels will not exercise manager Ron Washington’s 2026 option after two losing seasons, and interim manager Ray Montgomery also will not receive the full-time role. Washington, who missed much of 2025 after quadruple-bypass surgery, said general manager Perry Minasian attributed the decision to team performance rather than his health. The Angels finished 72-90, their 10th consecutive losing season, while Washington compiled a 99-137 record over two years. He said he remains healthy and wants to continue managing or coaching. The Angels will seek their sixth manager in nine years, with former players Albert Pujols and Torii Hunter considered candidates.

IDC identifies IT-based simulation, modeling, data analytics, and high-performance computing (HPC) as key enablers of manufacturing agility, innovation, productivity, and competitiveness. Virtual processes can accelerate product development and manufacturing, optimize materials, supply chains, energy use, and sustainability, and support digital products, services, and business models.

HPC is increasingly necessary to meet growing simulation complexity and performance needs. Enterprises can use custom or standard on-premises systems, public cloud services, HPC-as-a-Service, or hybrid models to improve scalability and agility. Effective digital transformation also requires a holistic data strategy and a consistent, accessible single source of truth across the entire product lifecycle and value chain.

IDC recommends establishing virtual development processes, assessing HPC operating models according to utilization, budget, performance, flexibility, security, and skills, and prioritizing scalability, security, and energy efficiency. Enterprises lacking specialized expertise should engage service providers or ecosystem partners.

The findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 technology decision-makers at industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

A Gallup-Walton Family Foundation survey found that more than one-quarter of U.S. public school teachers lack basic materials or staffing needed to work effectively, reducing job satisfaction. Nearly two-thirds reported shortages of teaching assistants, aides, paraprofessionals or behavior specialists, while 62% lacked sufficient mental health resources or special educators.

Although 72% said they had necessary teaching equipment, 24% lacked adequate furniture, 25% lacked laptops or computers, and 35% lacked printing supplies. One-third described ordering materials as difficult. Technology shortages were more common in low-income schools, while staffing and furniture shortages occurred at similar or higher rates in wealthier schools.

Adequate resources strongly correlated with satisfaction: 77% of sufficiently resourced teachers were satisfied at work, compared with 44% of those without adequate resources. About half said professional development was not based on student needs. Teachers valued collaborative planning and classroom observation, but only one-third had opportunities to observe colleagues.

Gallup surveyed roughly 2,000 teachers during each of three periods between October 2024 and May 2025.

The lecture introduces digital network implementations of causal linear shift-invariant systems described by linear constant-coefficient difference equations. Such implementations require three basic operations: delay, scalar multiplication, and addition. Block diagrams represent delays by \(z^{-1}\), multiplication by weighted branches, and addition by summers.

Signal flow graphs provide an alternative representation using directed branches and nodes. Source nodes supply inputs, sink nodes represent outputs, and internal node values equal the sums of incoming branch outputs. For linear flow graphs, each branch output is its input multiplied by a scalar or function of \(z\). A first-order equation such as \(y(n)=a y(n-1)+x(n)\) can therefore be represented using a feedback branch with gain \(a\) and a delay branch with transmittance \(z^{-1}\).

Flow graphs correspond to systems of linear equations and can be expressed in matrix form. When branches are restricted to scalar gains or single-sample delays, the network matrix can be separated into a coefficient matrix and a delay matrix. In the time domain, this yields coupled first-order difference equations, effectively decomposing an \(n\)-th order difference equation into first-order equations.

The ordering of network nodes determines whether their values can be computed sequentially. A numbering is computable exactly when the coefficient matrix has no nonzero entries on or above its main diagonal. Delay-free loops produce non-computable networks, although their equations may still be solved or rearranged. Subsequent lectures will examine common structures for recursive infinite impulse response and non-recursive finite impulse response digital filters.

Special education teacher shortages are concentrated in high-poverty urban and rural districts, while teacher demographics often differ substantially from student populations. Alternative certification programs can expand and diversify the workforce, but quality varies, particularly among programs unaffiliated with higher education institutions. Effective preparation generally combines rigorous coursework, supervised clinical experience, mentoring, culturally responsive practices, community partnerships, and technology integration.

An exploratory case study examined the Washington Education Association Teacher Residency Program, the first union-led U.S. teacher preparation program. Piloted in 2023–24 without direct affiliation to an in-state higher education institution, it prepares special education teachers through collaboration among the teachers’ union, school districts, and the Center for Innovation, Design, and Digital Learning’s Tech Alliance. The study assessed its training components, use of emerging technologies, and resident incentives through needs assessments, interviews, observations, document analysis, and coursework and field-experience reviews.

Sixteen bachelor’s-degree holders entered the 18-month program across Federal Way, Mukilteo, and Walla Walla districts. Of those admitted, 38% were from non-White racial or ethnic backgrounds, 31% primarily spoke a language other than English, 63% held emergency substitute status, 56% had paraprofessional experience, and 14% reported a disability.

The program emphasized cultural competency, equity, inclusion, family engagement, Universal Design for Learning, and alignment with Washington teaching standards. Its hybrid-flexible curriculum combined synchronous and asynchronous coursework with four nine-week special education placements. Paid, trained mentors, district coaches, and field supervisors supported and assessed residents through competency-based measures.

Technology was incorporated through AI-supported Mursion teaching simulations, instructional and assistive technologies, digital tools, and professional development. Residents evaluated technologies for individual students during placements, with guidance from mentors, coaches, supervisors, and CIDDL faculty.

Residents received salaries of at least $40,000, health benefits, funded coursework, mentoring, coaching, and multiple placements. In exchange, they committed to working three years in their residency district after licensure. Initial certified-teacher pay was approximately $72,000 annually. Grants supporting the program exceeded $10.5 million.

The study concludes that the program offers an evidence-based, technology-integrated model for addressing shortages and workforce diversity. However, its small sample, short study period, and unresolved scalability and sustainability limit generalizability; certification, persistence, and retention outcomes were not yet available.

Musicians Sarah and Laura Ayoub credit Scotland’s funded music education, including individual lessons and ensemble experience, as crucial to their successful classical careers. They argue that all interested children should receive similar opportunities regardless of income.

Music tuition policies vary across Scotland. Highland Council is among 22 authorities charging for lessons, while Clackmannanshire has doubled annual fees to £524 for most families. West Lothian is consulting on cuts. By contrast, Renfrewshire, one of ten councils offering free tuition, has increased spending by £200,000 to widen access and participation.

Musicians and campaigners, including Duncan Chisholm, Dame Evelyn Glennie, Nicola Benedetti and Paolo Nutini, warn that costs create barriers. Former Royal Conservatoire head John Wallace said council music services could disappear if cuts continue, while the EIS teaching union reported music teacher numbers falling from 1,100 to 640 over a decade.

The Scottish government points to its Youth Music Initiative, including a £1.6m launch intended to ensure children experience tuition by Primary 6. Culture Secretary Fiona Hyslop opposes charging for additional tuition but says local councils control their budgets. Campaigners consider this insufficient, while Sarah Ayoub argues music education benefits students even when they pursue non-musical careers.

After losing 2-0 to Tottenham, Manchester United seek to strengthen their top-four position against Huddersfield in Alexis Sanchez’s home debut. Jose Mourinho is expected to discuss Marouane Fellaini’s fitness and his reported touchline issues with Paul Pogba.

Toy Lykins sued the Aluminum Workers International Union and Local 480, alleging that compulsory union dues were being spent on political or ideological purposes unrelated to collective bargaining, contract administration, or grievance adjustment, contrary to his wishes. The unions sought summary judgment, arguing there was no justiciable controversy, Lykins had failed to exhaust available remedies, and no First Amendment violation existed.

The court denied summary judgment. Because the unions possessed and allegedly misused Lykins’s compulsory payments, his inability to identify specific expenditures without an accounting did not defeat a justiciable controversy. Section 201(c) of the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act provided access to financial information, not a remedy for improper expenditures; Lykins had requested an accounting and had no obligation to attend union meetings.

The court found sufficient governmental action because the union-security agreement operated under federal authorization in the National Labor Relations Act. To avoid constitutional concerns, it interpreted the NLRA as not authorizing unions to use dissenters’ compulsory dues for political or ideological purposes. The precise categories of refundable expenditures required further factual development.

The court initially directed Lykins to amend his jurisdictional allegations, but a January 1981 order withdrew that requirement after noting the elimination of the amount-in-controversy requirement under 28 U.S.C. § 1331 and the availability of jurisdiction under § 1337(a). Discovery and pretrial proceedings were scheduled.

Elliott Management, which owns about 6 percent of NXP, valued the chipmaker at US$135 per share, above Qualcomm’s US$110 offer, arguing the bid suppresses NXP’s valuation and exploits a depressed share price. Elliott cited growth prospects in automotive and industrial semiconductors and commissioned UBS to analyze NXP. Meanwhile, Qualcomm rejected Broadcom’s US$103 billion takeover approach.

In June 1843, British minister Henry Fox stated that Britain had not authorized the occupation of the Sandwich Islands and would investigate it, though Lord Aberdeen later rejected Hawaiian compensation claims. Amid British and French rivalry and predominant American influence, Hawaiians favored the United States, which had shown goodwill and informally recognized Hawaiian autonomy. Hawaiian ambassadors William Richards and Timoteo Haalilio sought formal recognition abroad. In December 1842, Secretary of State Daniel Webster recognized Hawaiian independence, opposed foreign interference, and deemed a formal treaty unnecessary; President Tyler then submitted the correspondence and his policy to Congress. The ambassadors later secured a November 1843 convention in which Britain and France agreed to regard the islands as independent and never occupy any portion of them. The convention bound only those two powers and did not guarantee Hawaii against intervention by others.

NVIDIA reported that its Compensation Committee approved a new global performance-based restricted stock unit notice and agreement under its 2007 Equity Incentive Plan on March 6, 2019. On March 8, 2019, the committee adopted its fiscal 2020 Variable Compensation Plan, providing eligible executives cash awards based on achievement of specified revenue goals at threshold, base, and stretch levels. Participants generally must remain employed through the payment date. Base-plan target awards were $1.1 million for CEO Jen-Hsun Huang, $300,000 for CFO Colette Kress, $650,000 for Ajay Puri, and $250,000 each for Debora Shoquist and Timothy Teter.

Robert Cyrus Garrison was convicted of first-degree rape and sentenced to thirty years after a prior trial ended with a hung jury. He challenged only the punishment-stage instruction concerning good-time credits under 57 O.S.Supp.1969, § 138. Citing Williams v. State, the court held the mandated instruction unconstitutional and prejudicial because jurors could wrongly assume Garrison would serve approximately half his sentence. Although the error did not warrant reversal, the court reduced the sentence from thirty to fifteen years and otherwise affirmed the judgment.

A state audit found former Duquesne superintendent Barbara McDonnell authorized $41,000 in unapproved, no-interest personal loans to herself and three employees, including $22,000 for herself. Though repaid through payroll deductions, the matter was referred to the State Ethics Commission. The audit also identified undocumented transportation reimbursements and at least $180,000 in state overpayments.

NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the 7nm Ampere GA100 architecture, targets AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. It contains 108 streaming multiprocessors, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, and a 40 MB L2 cache.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. Compared with V100, A100 provides higher mixed-precision, FP64, and inference performance. TF32 accelerates FP32-based workloads with minimal software changes, while FP16 and BF16 provide greater training throughput. Fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity can double Tensor Core throughput, particularly for inference.

A100 introduces Multi-Instance GPU technology, allowing one GPU to be securely divided into as many as seven isolated instances with dedicated memory-system resources and predictable performance. Third-generation NVLink supplies 600 GB/s aggregate bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4, Magnum IO, InfiniBand, Ethernet, and NVSwitch support scalable multi-GPU and multi-node systems.

Additional features include larger L1/shared memory, L2 residency controls, compute data compression, asynchronous memory copies and barriers, task-graph acceleration, improved error isolation, and CUDA 11 programmability enhancements. These capabilities support both large clustered workloads and multiple smaller, independent workloads while improving utilization, scalability, and performance per watt.

Tesla appointed Zachary Kirkhorn, 34, as Chief Financial Officer effective March 13, 2019, succeeding Deepak Ahuja. Kirkhorn previously served as Vice President of Finance, Financial Planning and Business Operations. He will receive $12 million in stock options and $4 million in restricted stock units vesting over four years.

Tesla also appointed Vaibhav Taneja, 41, as Chief Accounting Officer. Taneja had served as Corporate Controller and previously held accounting roles at Tesla, SolarCity and PricewaterhouseCoopers. He will receive $6 million in stock options and $2 million in restricted stock units vesting over four years.

Port Hardy Secondary School’s senior girls soccer team placed second at the Island Championships in Duncan, qualifying for its first BC Single A High School Provincials. PHSS defeated Duncan Christian 6-1, lost 5-4 to top-ranked Glenlyon Norfolk, and beat St. Andrews 3-1 in overtime after a 1-1 regulation tie. The team then lost the final 4-3 to Glenlyon Norfolk but was the only team to score against them during the tournament. Provincials will take place in Penticton from May 31 to June 3. Coaches praised the team’s effort and emphasized representing the school well.

The Japan Society of Technology Education (JSTE) developed the New Framework for Technology and Engineering Education (NGTE) to clarify the field’s role in Japanese STEAM education and respond to technological and social changes associated with Society 5.0.

A survey of 1,656 junior high school students in Hyogo Prefecture found generally positive perceptions of Technology classes and active, collaborative learning. However, students had limited opportunities to explore technology through inquiry, experimentation, and observation. Design problem-solving activities were also weakly linked to abilities for technological innovation and governance.

NGTE focuses on technology and engineering literacy for all citizens, aiming to develop innovation, governance, and broader competencies. Its scope connects materials, energy conversion, biological cultivation, and information technologies with engineering sciences and technological systems such as AI, IoT, robotics, and Big Data. It also introduces a Triple-Loop Engineering Design Process comprising needs exploration, technological “seeds” exploration, and creation. A STEAM learning model places engineering design at the center of transdisciplinary projects that create technological products or systems addressing authentic social problems.

JSTE developed the framework through annual ideathons, symposiums, surveys, and consultation with members and curriculum specialists. Evaluation by 90 JSTE members showed general agreement with its proposals, although the definition of engineering required revision. The resulting process illustrates how academic societies can assess learners, interpret social and curricular needs, propose standards, and contribute to national curriculum reform. Future work will test NGTE through classroom practice and address teacher education and training.

The passage argues that Trumpism conflicts with Founders’ concerns about civilian control of the military, immigration, rule of law, checks and balances, and judicial independence. It cites the Declaration’s grievances against military supremacy, restrictions on immigration, and interference with courts. Warren Buffett is reportedly considering a roughly $10 billion deal for petrochemical unit OxyChem, potentially Berkshire Hathaway’s largest acquisition since buying Alleghany for $11.6 billion in 2022. Berkshire holds $344 billion in cash and a 28.2% Occidental stake. Buffett will step down as CEO at the end of 2025, with energy expert Greg Abel succeeding him.

Christian Pulisic scored and assisted Jozy Altidore as the United States defeated Panama 4-0 in World Cup qualifying. Altidore scored twice, including a penalty, and Bobby Wood added the final goal. The victory ended a three-match qualifying winless streak and moved the U.S. into third place, the region’s final automatic berth, with 12 points. A win Tuesday at Trinidad and Tobago would almost certainly secure an eighth straight World Cup appearance. Pulisic, playing centrally, contributed to 11 of the Americans’ 14 goals in the qualifying hexagonal.

Joel Greenblatt’s Magic Formula ranks stocks by earnings yield and return on invested capital to identify undervalued, financially strong companies. Investors combine both rankings, select the best stocks, diversify, rebalance, and monitor performance. Historical tests reported substantial long-term outperformance in US and Nordic markets, though results weakened after 2014. Criticisms include small-cap bias, omitted transaction costs, sector concentration, reliance on historical data, and disregard for qualitative company factors. The strategy is simple to implement but does not guarantee future returns and requires due diligence.

Accepting the Republican presidential nomination, the speaker advocates constitutional, party-based representative government over personal or executive rule. He calls for restoring congressional authority, administrative competence, lawful government, and cooperation among the executive, Cabinet, House, and Senate.

He rejects American participation in a world super-government or military alliance while supporting friendship, international justice, disarmament, and an association of nations that preserves American independence. He promises formal peace and opposes delegating decisions to send Americans to war.

Domestically, he urges greater production, efficiency, thrift, economic stabilization, reduced government spending, currency deflation, and action against profiteering. He supports fair competition, high wages matched by productivity, collective bargaining that preserves individual rights, and cooperation among labor, management, and capital. He opposes government ownership of railroads, favors transportation rehabilitation and infrastructure development, and supports agriculture through cooperative associations, reclamation, and federal assistance.

His program also includes protective tariffs, a merchant marine, adequate defense, regulated immigration and Americanization, improved labor conditions, anti-lynching action, housing aid, equitable taxation, Black citizens’ rights, veterans’ support, women’s suffrage, and stable relations with Mexico. He emphasizes civil liberties but supports suppressing violent sedition and insists on honest enforcement of all constitutional laws. He concludes by affirming American unity, liberty, patriotism, faith, and his commitment to serve faithfully.

Lobster 207, formally the Maine Lobstering Union, was established in 2013 as both an International Association of Machinists local and a statewide marketing cooperative. It emerged after Maine lobstermen faced record-low prices, regulatory pressures, limited political influence, industry consolidation, and antitrust restrictions preventing coordinated price demands.

IAM organizers helped lobstermen build membership, leadership, and political influence while leaving control with elected lobstermen. The organization contributed to legislative victories, opposed regulations viewed as harmful, supported members seeking public office, and partnered with other groups on environmental and labor issues. By November 2017, it represented about 550 lobstermen, with 250 current on dues.

Cooperative status exempted members from certain antitrust restrictions and allowed them to market catches collectively, negotiate wholesale prices, share profits, and potentially reduce operating costs through group purchasing. In 2017, Lobster 207 financed a $4 million acquisition of the wholesale operations of Trenton Bridge Lobster Pound using Bank of Labor financing, loans from IAM locals, seller financing, and IAM credit support. The acquisition expanded purchases from 30 to 130 member boats and enabled marketing as “union lobster.”

Lobster 207 planned to expand statewide, attract more members, and eventually distribute profits based on members’ contributed catch. However, its board faced debt, operating costs, investment decisions, and tensions as self-employed lobstermen became business owners and overseers. Its long-term economic success remained uncertain, though the wholesale business was reportedly profitable and statewide lobster prices had risen by 2016. The experience raised questions about IAM’s capabilities, lessons for organized labor, and whether the model could be replicated elsewhere.

Alpha-N Performance modified a BMW M4 Coupe to produce 560 horsepower, adding GTS-derived transmission software, differential and stability settings, Öhlins suspension, lightweight wheels, carbon-fiber aerodynamic parts and Recaro seats. The car completed the Nürburgring bridge-to-gantry course in 7:20, compared with BMW’s reported 7:28 for the M4 GTS.

Secretary of State John Hay certified on September 1, 1900, that attached documents were true copies from State Department files. Captain George O. Baker, a 58-year-old master mariner with six years’ experience in the Okhotsk and Japan seas, testified that the Okhotsk whaling season generally lasted from mid-August to mid-October, with September being most productive. Continuous northerly and easterly gales typically made later whaling impractical. He considered six to ten right whales a fair seasonal catch. From Vladivostok on October 1, after rough weather began, he would sail directly to San Francisco rather than spend eight to ten days returning to nearly finished whaling grounds. Nine whales would yield approximately 10,000 pounds of bone and 900 barrels of oil.

Roundhill Investments relaunched its actively managed meme-stock ETF under the MEME ticker, offering investors exposure to volatile, heavily discussed stocks. Its previous launch in December 2021 coincided with a Nasdaq peak; by its 2023 closure, the Nasdaq had fallen nearly 10% and the fund more than 96%. MDC faction leader Thokozani Khupe accused male rivals of cowardice and defended Linda Masarira’s election as spokesperson, saying she met party requirements and strengthened its 50-50 gender representation. Khupe, who split from Nelson Chamisa after accusing him of seizing control following Morgan Tsvangirai’s death, was elected leader at an extraordinary congress alongside a new executive.
