Mega Geometry’s GPU-driven cluster generation and fast BVH construction support subdivision surfaces. By mapping per-frame tessellation into triangle clusters and rapidly building BVHs from CLASes, it improves real-time ray-tracing performance for animated or viewpoint-dependent, smooth quad-based meshes.

The passage argues that Exxon Mobil is attractively valued near its 2015 lows, citing a 4.1% dividend yield, 20% year-over-year cash flow growth, potential buybacks, a price-to-cash-flow discount, and a forward earnings multiple below 16. Stabilizing crude oil and natural gas prices could improve the energy sector’s outlook, with Exxon positioned to benefit after outperforming during the recent oil and gas bear market. The company expects to double earnings by 2025, requiring roughly 10% annual profit growth, while further dividend increases may be announced in April. Technically, the stock is near important support around $71.60; a break below would be concerning, but the author expects buying interest near that level. Based on valuation, income potential, and the energy outlook, the author considers Exxon a strong buying opportunity and discloses a long position.

The lecture explains the theorem of irrelevance: for signals confined to a finite-dimensional space with independent noise outside it, detection need consider only the received components within that space. In white Gaussian noise, modulation waveforms are therefore equivalent for basic noise analysis, reducing the problem to finite-dimensional vectors; practical differences arise from synchronization, filtering, and implementation.

For independent transmitted symbols and independent noise, joint maximum-likelihood sequence detection gives the same decisions as detecting each symbol separately. If inputs are dependent, as with error-correcting codes, using the full observation can lower error probability. This motivates probabilistic decoding methods that exploit all received information.

The lecture compares orthogonal, simplex, and biorthogonal signal sets. Removing an orthogonal code’s mean produces a simplex code with the same error probability but lower energy. Orthogonal codes may still aid phase and frequency recovery. Biorthogonal codes retain the same energy while approximately doubling the likely error events. For large orthogonal signal sets, conditioning on the received component in the transmitted direction improves upon a simple union bound. The resulting error probability decreases exponentially with the number of transmitted bits when \(E_b/N_0>\ln 2\), identifying the unlimited-bandwidth Gaussian channel capacity threshold.

The course then shifts to wireless communication, where channels vary with time and frequency, experience fading and interference, and involve multiple transmitters and receivers. Cellular networks connect mobiles through base stations and switching offices to wired networks. Their reverse links are multiple-access channels, while forward links are broadcast channels carrying separate messages. Network procedures include selecting base stations, locating mobiles, and routing calls, though the course focuses on physical channel modeling. Wireless design must account for propagation, carrier frequency, Doppler shift, coherence across time and frequency, narrowband versus wideband operation, and idealized radiation and reflection models.

Kalidou Koulibaly’s stoppage-time header gave Napoli a dramatic away win over Juventus, reducing the Serie A leaders’ advantage to one point with four games remaining. Juventus lost Giorgio Chiellini to injury and hit the post through Miralem Pjanic, while Napoli created several chances before Koulibaly scored from Jose Callejon’s corner. The result revived Napoli’s hopes of a first Scudetto since 1989-90.

The disclosure describes display apparatuses using thin, flexible vibration modules mounted behind a display panel to vibrate the panel and produce sound or haptic feedback. Each module combines piezoelectric inorganic portions, which provide vibration, with flexible organic portions that absorb impacts, improve durability, and permit bending. This structure is intended to provide strong sound pressure, sound localization, flexibility, and resistance to damage while supporting curved, rollable, bendable, wearable, and other flexible displays.

The piezoelectric and organic portions may have line, circular, triangular, polygonal, or other patterns, with their sizes and arrangements adjusted to control flexibility and low-, middle-, or high-frequency sound characteristics. Electrode layers apply electrical signals to polarize and actuate the piezoelectric composite, while protection films cover the module. Stacked piezoelectric composite layers may form a bimorph structure that increases vertical vibration and sound pressure.

A manufacturing method forms a composite from piezoelectric inorganic material and flexible organic material, deposits electrodes on opposing surfaces, polarizes the inorganic portions by applying voltage under a temperature atmosphere, and adds protective films.

The vibration module may cover most or all of the display area, increasing the vibrating region and improving sound pressure and localization. Adhesive attachment may include an air gap to reduce vibration loss. Multiple modules may separately vibrate left and right display regions to produce stereo sound. Partition members and enclosed air gaps can isolate channels, limit vibration regions, reduce sound interference and leakage, and tune frequency characteristics. The display panel may be supported by a rear structure, while omission of a front frame can reduce bezel width.

Tesla reported that stockholders approved CEO Elon Musk’s performance-based stock option award at a March 21, 2018 special meeting. The proposal received approximately 81% approval under NASDAQ rules, 80% under Tesla’s bylaws, and 73% excluding shares owned directly or indirectly by Elon and Kimbal Musk. The award’s material terms were previously summarized in Tesla’s February 8, 2018 proxy statement, incorporated as Exhibit 99.1.

Cornwall parent Jerica Devos has spent about $70 on required supplies for her son’s Grade 1 class and argues costs and purchasing options should be consistent across P.E.I. schools. Westwood Primary School’s list includes specific brands and colours, which Devos believes parents should not have to follow when buying supplies themselves.

The Public Schools Branch provides a master list that schools may modify by removing items or specifying quantities, colours and brands, but they cannot add items. Some schools purchase supplies and charge parents a flat fee capped at $40, with an option to buy supplies independently. Parents at schools without this system cannot choose to pay a fee instead. Branch director Parker Grimmer encouraged concerned parents to contact principals or the branch, saying feedback could prompt a review. Devos plans to raise her concerns with both.

A bullish engulfing pattern is a two-candlestick bullish reversal pattern appearing after a downward price swing. It consists of a small bearish candle followed by a larger bullish candle that completely engulfs it, signaling a possible shift from bearish to bullish momentum. The signal often occurs near support levels and may be more reliable after a significant pullback in an uptrend.

Traders should seek confirmation through follow-through price action or another bullish pattern and consider market conditions, support and resistance, volume, entry and exit criteria, profit targets, stop losses, and opposite signals. Effective trading requires a defined plan for profitable and losing trades, appropriate risk management, and avoidance of common mistakes. Backtesting uses historical data to identify patterns, apply specific entry and exit rules, simulate trades, and evaluate performance.

Disability activist Doug Paulley found that only eight of Scotland’s 32 councils expect to meet the recommended October deadline for Section 167 lists of wheelchair-accessible taxis. Perth and Kinross is the only council to have completed one; seven plan to do so by October, six have no deadline, ten are undecided and eight have no plans. Without these lists, new Equality Act provisions fining drivers up to £1,000 for refusing wheelchair users or charging extra cannot be enforced. Across England, Scotland and Wales, 11% of councils have lists and 59% lack firm plans to meet the deadline. Research also found limited wheelchair-accessible vehicles and disability training. Paulley and Muscular Dystrophy UK urged councils and government to act.

VentureWire’s December 7, 2000 edition reports that Providence Equity Partners closed a $2.8 billion fund, Insight Capital Partners was raising $750 million, and optical networking firm Caspian Networks raised $85 million. Numerous technology companies announced financing, including GiantBear, Advent Networks, Mediatrix, Quidnunc, In-Fusio, InfoMedics, Xpert, and Simulant, while PacketVideo and United Devices sought additional funding.

Market difficulties prompted HarvardNet to eliminate 280 jobs and end DSL services, Exp.com to cut 15% of staff, @Viso to stop funding Diamond.com, divine interVentures to withdraw a $10 million commitment, and CarsDirect.com to cancel its IPO. Other developments included product launches, a Brightstar–IncuVest alliance, acquisitions involving Beliefnet, FilmTrust, Dairy.com, and BuyMedia, and multiple board and executive appointments. Corrections clarified InPhonic’s total funding as $21 million, Nisus’s website address, and Salesnet’s new name.

Todd Kimberlain forwarded a National Hurricane Center file, constructed by Mark Demaria and assumed complete for the continental United States, listing storm watch and warning areas from 1963–1998. Records include date, hour, storm name, warning count, storm ID, alert type, and coastal endpoints. Codes identify hurricane warnings and watches, storm and gale warnings, and tropical storm warnings and watches; endpoint order is arbitrary.
Research suggests losing 5% of body weight requires 10% fewer calories to maintain it. The issue also highlights weight maintenance and dMeetings diabetes education.

This prospective cohort study evaluated whether baseline point-of-care lung ultrasound findings predicted oxygen-support requirements or death among 264 adults hospitalized with COVID-19 at Johns Hopkins Hospital from April 2020 to September 2021. Researchers used a mean lung ultrasound score (mLUSS), calculated across available lung zones, allowing inclusion of patients without scans of all 12 zones.

Higher mLUSS values were associated with progression to ICU-level care and 28-day mortality, but not significantly with the composite outcome of mechanical ventilation or death. A lines were associated with lower risks of ICU-level care and mortality, while pleural abnormalities were associated with mechanical ventilation or death. Results remained similar after accounting for available lung zones, symptom duration, and asymptomatic infections. Reader agreement for mLUSS was high.

The findings support using mLUSS and individual ultrasound abnormalities to help triage hospitalized COVID-19 patients, even when all lung zones cannot be scanned. Limitations included hospital-based convenience sampling, variable enrollment timing, small samples for some analyses, and wide confidence intervals. Further validation in additional and non-hospitalized populations was recommended.

An international study found that established alien species have increased continuously worldwide over the past 200 years, with no general sign of saturation. Researchers analyzed over 45,000 first records covering more than 16,000 species; 37% were introduced between 1970 and 2014. Introductions peaked in 1996 at 585 recorded species. Trends vary by taxonomic group and reflect activities such as horticulture, colonial introductions, and globalized trade. Except for mammals and fishes, recent introduction rates show no slowdown. Alien species can increase regional richness but also homogenize ecosystems and contribute to native extinctions. Researchers concluded that existing measures are insufficient and called for stronger prevention policies.

Mercedes is introducing a Grand Edition package for non-AMG GLS-Class SUVs to strengthen its flagship model against growing competition. It adds exclusive 20-inch wheels, badges, full nappa leather dashboard, unique wood trim, special leather combinations, quilted seats and velour mats. The €8,250 upgrade is available across the GLS range. Orders opened October 6, with deliveries beginning in March 2018.

Lenovo’s Legion Go S with SteamOS is $120 off and offers a streamlined alternative to Windows handhelds. It features comfortable grips, well-placed controls, a bright 120-Hz IPS display, 1 TB of storage, 32 GB of memory, and MicroSD expansion. Though newer games may require settings adjustments, it outperforms an aging Steam Deck and handles many portable games with minimal tweaking. Its compact size and SteamOS support make it a capable option for travelers and couch gaming.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that it issued an April 26, 2022 press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2022. The release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under the Exchange Act. The report was signed by Chief Accounting Officer Alice L. Jolla.

Russian journalist Arkady Babchenko appeared alive in Kiev after Ukrainian authorities staged his reported killing to thwart an assassination plot. Security officials said a Ukrainian recruited for $40,000 by Russian security services hired a suspected gunman. Babchenko, a Kremlin critic who fled Russia after threats, apologized to family and friends unaware of the operation.

The Czech central bank will likely raise interest rates once more near year-end, board member Toms Nidetzky said. Despite weaker-than-expected crown appreciation, slowing inflation and slightly anti-inflationary risks mean no short-term hike is needed. The repo rate is currently 0.75 percent.

President George Washington declares that conciliation and offers of forgiveness have failed to end armed resistance to federal law in western Pennsylvania. Invoking his constitutional duty to ensure faithful execution of the laws, he announces that militia from New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Maryland, and Virginia are moving toward the affected region. He promises protection to lawful citizens and good-faith treatment for offenders who qualify for indemnity. Washington urges citizens and officials to oppose efforts promoting insurrection and misinformation, uphold the Constitution and laws, refrain from assisting insurgents, and bring offenders before the law.

A Providence community health system study evaluated no-cost, pathologist-directed comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) using a 523-gene DNA/RNA assay for 3,216 patients with advanced solid tumors tested between September 2019 and November 2021. Testing at diagnosis made results available earlier for clinical decisions, with a median turnaround of 14 days.

At least one guideline-based actionable biomarker was found in 49% of cases; TMB-high was most common. CGP matched 53% of patients to at least one arm in three assessed basket trials, versus 26% using an in silico legacy 50-gene panel. Combining guideline and trial matching, actionable alterations were identified in 67% of CGP cases versus 33% with the smaller panel.

Among 1,482 patients with documented treatment and follow-up, precision therapies and immunotherapies were used more often than chemotherapy alone. Targeted therapy was administered to 59% of patients with an actionable targeted-therapy biomarker, while 63% with immunotherapy-positive biomarkers received immunotherapy with or without chemotherapy. Across tumor types, median overall survival was 25 months with targeted therapy versus 17 months with chemotherapy alone; adjusted hazard ratio was 0.66. For non-small cell lung cancer, median survival was 26 versus 16 months, with an adjusted hazard ratio of 0.55.

The study concludes that community-based CGP can expand actionable findings, support greater use of precision treatments, and improve survival. Remaining barriers include cost, insurer coverage, physician adoption, treatment access, non-actionable findings, and resistance to targeted therapies.

An infant sustained Erb’s palsy during delivery involving shoulder dystocia. A jury found the municipal hospital and staff negligent. The appellate court upheld reduced damages, finding them reasonable and declining to reinstate the original future pain-and-suffering award.

Protesters across several U.S. cities rallied against hatred, racism and white supremacy following deadly violence at a Charlottesville demonstration. Events included marches and vigils in San Francisco, Seattle, Denver, New York and Charlottesville. Seattle police arrested three men, while New York demonstrators urged President Trump to denounce white nationalist groups.

FoLix is an FDA-cleared, noninvasive fractional laser treatment for early to moderate hair loss in men and women. It creates microscopic scalp channels to stimulate healing, circulation, and growth signals in existing follicles, so it is unsuitable for complete baldness or extensive scarring.

Sessions take 20 to 30 minutes without anesthesia or significant downtime. Patients typically need three to six treatments during the first year and up to twice-yearly maintenance. Each session costs about $750 to $1,250. Possible temporary effects include redness, tightness, scalp sensitivity, and shedding.

FoLix may appeal to patients seeking an alternative to surgery, daily medication, or PRP procedures involving blood draws. Doctors recommend medical consultation because hair loss can have causes other than genetics, and earlier treatment may improve the chance of success.

The team is confident playing in front of either goaltender and believes it can compete with the favored opponent but must execute better. Despite creating chances, the players need persistence after bad bounces. The pulled goaltender had battled hard but was left unsupported, signaling teammates to improve. The team was tentative rather than unphysical and sought to avoid penalties or losing position against a strong puck-moving opponent.

Birel ART-supported teams competed among 191 drivers in Round 2 of the Florida Winter Tour ROK Edition at Palm Beach. Ryan Norberg won the ROK Senior final, recorded the fastest lap and regained the championship lead. Scott Davidson earned his first ROK Shifter Master win of the season. Igor Pushkin placed fifth, Ryan MacDermid tenth and Justin Aresneu twelfth.

The team missed scoring chances but intends to remain positive and focus on the crucial third game. They must avoid lapses and turnovers against an opponent that capitalizes on mistakes, while maintaining confidence and giving their full effort at home.

Anna Gasser won the Olympic debut of women’s Big Air snowboarding in Pyeongchang, scoring 96 on her final double cork 1080 for a 185.00 total. Jamie Anderson, who led before the final round, fell on her last landing and took silver. Zoi Sadowski Synnott earned bronze with 157.50, giving New Zealand its first Winter Olympic medal in 26 years. Officials had moved the final forward because of wind concerns, and the event was held in mostly calm conditions.

A Teagasc survey of 314 male farmers in south-east Ireland found higher mortality from cardiovascular disease and cancer than in other occupations. Although 39% reported recent ill health, 20% had never consulted a doctor. Common issues included back pain, arthritis and anxiety. Farmers reported lower weekly alcohol use and smoking than national male averages, but similar binge drinking; rheumatoid arthritis was three times more prevalent.

The passage is a polemic accusing Hillary Clinton of dishonesty, arrogance, security failures, and responsibility for Libya’s destabilization following U.S.-backed regime change. It cites WikiLeaks, her private email server, Bill Clinton’s meeting with Attorney General Loretta Lynch, and alleged FBI and media favoritism. The author lists numerous Clinton-related controversies, invokes Christopher Hitchens’s criticism of her truthfulness, condemns her supporters, and concludes that Donald Trump would have to be exceptionally evil to be worse than Clinton.

This qualitative case study examined the distance education experiences of seven visually impaired undergraduate and graduate music students in Turkey during COVID-19. Data were collected through semi-structured telephone and online interviews and analyzed using content analysis.

Most courses were conducted synchronously, though some students relied on recorded lessons because of health issues or ineffective live-learning systems. Students used computers, phones, and tablets independently, but course materials were often inaccessible. Some required parental or peer assistance, while students able to read large print reported fewer difficulties. Participants stated that their special needs were generally not considered when materials were prepared.

Assessment practices varied. Some instructors provided individual arrangements, such as video examinations, homework, or separate applied-course assessments, while others used standard written examinations that created difficulties. Reported strengths of distance education included flexibility in time and place and, for one student, greater social acceptance. Two participants identified no strengths.

Major weaknesses included inaccessible screen-dependent systems, unsuitable documents, poor sound quality and synchronization, inability to perform music simultaneously online, inadequate technical infrastructure, and instructors’ limited technological competence. Participants recommended accessible interfaces, screen customization, screen readers, speech-to-text tools, audio documents, notation-reading software, Braille music archives, faster technical support, alternative platforms, and more supportive instructors.

The study concludes that visually impaired music students were largely overlooked in distance education planning, which was designed around students without disabilities. Their reliance on parents, friends, or enlarged text reduced educational independence. Accessible technologies, customized materials, disability-sensitive programs, and cooperation among students, families, educators, and specialists are needed to make distance music education equitable and effective.

The United States sued Hale County, Alabama, under the Voting Rights Act of 1965, challenging post-1964 laws that changed County Commission elections from district-based to at-large voting. Alabama was designated for Voting Rights Act coverage in 1965, and the court held that this designation automatically included all political subdivisions, including Hale County.

Hale County adopted at-large elections through enactments in 1965, 1971, and 1973 but never obtained the preclearance required by Section 5. The court therefore declared those enactments legally unenforceable and elections conducted under them unlawful. Actions taken by officials previously elected at large remained valid until lawful successors could be elected. Unless federal preclearance was later obtained, the county was required to return to district elections under its 1959 law.

The court allowed the November 2, 1976 election to proceed, with commissioners serving provisionally. Defendants were ordered to submit the three enactments and requested information to the Attorney General within fifteen days. If the Attorney General objected, defendants could seek a declaratory judgment from the District Court for the District of Columbia within thirty days. Absent a successful challenge or approval of the 1973 law, the county was required to hold prompt district-based elections.

In its supplemental opinion, the court relied on the Voting Rights Act’s legislative history and federal cases indicating that designation of an entire state subjects every political subdivision within it to the Act’s preclearance requirements. The court retained jurisdiction for further relief.

The patent describes flexible, electromagnetically shielded cables for routing DC and radio-frequency signals through cryogenic quantum computing systems. The cables may contain parallel single- or multilayer striplines between grounded planes, conductive shielding vias, fanout regions, stiffeners, and rigid circuit boards at one or both ends. Boards can host connectors, filters, attenuators, amplifiers, and other components and can be mechanically and thermally anchored to isothermal plates.

Cable and board assemblies may use solder bumps, indium sheets, push-on connectors, wire bonds, flip-chip connections, or compliant spring joints. Integrated absorptive materials and ground-plane windows can provide high-frequency filtering near a quantum processing unit. Conductors may be superconducting or non-superconducting, allowing different cable sections to balance thermal conduction and electrical loss across cryostat temperature stages.

The designs aim to increase signal density, reduce thermal load and space requirements, improve mechanical integrity and impedance matching, and simplify assembly, disassembly, and component replacement. They may connect quantum processors containing superconducting circuits and can also serve other high-frequency interconnect applications.

Former New York Judge Louis L. Nock joined Anderson Kill the same day judicial ethics regulators dropped misconduct charges in exchange for his resignation and agreement never to hold judicial office again. Complaints alleged that Nock behaved rudely toward court staff and threatened grievances or criminal complaints against commission staff and witnesses unless charges were dismissed. Nock denied the allegations and resigned after motions to dismiss them failed. Anderson Kill said he disclosed the case before being hired and emphasized that no wrongdoing was found. Nock’s lawyer said he denied the demeanor allegations, respected commission staff and chose not to continue fighting because he already planned to leave the bench due to family considerations and approaching mandatory retirement.

The speaker calls the finals the biggest game, expects nerves but says the team is calm and excited. An injured teammate’s presence would mean a lot, while enthusiastic fans and citywide support have made the playoffs memorable.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture improves graphics, ray tracing, AI, memory, and I/O performance over Turing. Its Streaming Multiprocessors support FP32 operations on both datapaths, doubling peak FP32 throughput while retaining concurrent FP32 and INT32 execution. Second-generation RT Cores provide up to twice the ray-tracing performance, concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute, and hardware-accelerated motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32, BF16, and structured sparsity, which can double throughput for supported neural-network operations and accelerate DLSS, AI denoising, training, and inference.

The full GA102 GPU contains seven GPCs, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA cores, 112 ROPs, 6 MB of L2 cache, and a 384-bit memory interface. Each SM includes 128 CUDA cores, four Tensor Cores, one RT Core, and 128 KB of configurable L1/shared memory. Ampere increases cache capacity and shared-memory bandwidth, while delivering up to 1.9 times Turing’s power efficiency at equivalent performance.

GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling to reach 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/s, while professional RTX A6000 and A40 GPUs use 48 GB of GDDR6, expandable to 96 GB through third-generation NVLink. PCIe 4.0 doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth. RTX IO, working with Microsoft DirectStorage, enables GPU-based asset decompression and direct SSD-to-GPU transfers to reduce CPU use and loading times.

Ampere supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 4K at 120 Hz, and 8K at 60 Hz. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware AV1 decoding up to 8K60 HDR, while seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

Products include the gaming-focused RTX 3090, 3080, and 3070; the RTX A6000 desktop workstation GPU; and the A40 data-center GPU. The A6000 and A40 target professional visualization, simulation, AI, virtual workstations, and large datasets.

The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 LIVE-AIR trial evaluated lenzilumab, a GM-CSF-neutralizing antibody, in hospitalized adults with COVID-19 pneumonia who had not received invasive mechanical ventilation. Among 520 randomized participants, lenzilumab improved survival without ventilation through day 28 compared with placebo (HR 1.54; 95% CI 1.02–2.32; p=0.0403).

Baseline C-reactive protein (CRP) was the strongest predictor of progression to invasive mechanical ventilation or death. Participants with baseline CRP below 150 mg/L, representing 78% of those with evaluable CRP, experienced the greatest benefit from lenzilumab, including improved survival without ventilation (HR 2.54; 95% CI 1.46–4.41; nominal p=0.0009), fewer incidents of invasive ventilation, ECMO, or death, more ventilator-free days, fewer ICU days, and faster recovery. Comparable benefits were not observed among participants with CRP at or above 150 mg/L.

Patients progressing to ventilation or death had persistently elevated CRP, while CRP declined rapidly among those surviving without ventilation. Lenzilumab reduced CRP more quickly than placebo. No serious adverse events attributable to lenzilumab were reported.

Most CRP analyses were post hoc and not prospectively powered. The findings suggest baseline CRP may help identify hospitalized COVID-19 patients most likely to benefit from lenzilumab, particularly before CRP exceeds 150 mg/L.

The White House confirmed plans to withdraw Kathleen Hartnett White’s nomination to lead the Council on Environmental Quality after it stalled in the Senate. White, a climate change skeptic and former Texas environmental official, criticized mainstream climate science, opposed stricter pollution limits and praised fossil fuels. She was affiliated with a think tank funded by fossil-fuel companies. Senator Tom Carper welcomed the withdrawal and urged the administration to nominate an environmental and public health advocate.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years for the 2014 murder-for-hire of her former son-in-law, Florida State University law professor Dan Markel. Adelson maintained her innocence and denied prior knowledge of the plot, prompting Judge Stephen Everett to cite her “utter lack of remorse.” Prosecutors alleged the killing was motivated by the family’s desire for Markel’s ex-wife, Wendi Adelson, to relocate with their children. Adelson’s husband also insisted she was innocent.

Ray tracing realistically simulates lighting but historically was too computationally intensive for real-time single-GPU use. After nearly 10 years of collaboration, NVIDIA enabled real-time ray tracing through Turing GPUs and hardware acceleration engines called RT Cores.

Christopher K. Merker studied whether governance affects public pension fund performance, developing a research protocol with Marquette University colleagues because reliable governance data was scarce. Among 35 public pension plans representing about 14.5% of industry assets, five-year annualized returns from 2008 to 2012 ranged from 15% to -4.2%, revealing substantial differences in investment approaches and outcomes.

The research defined asset owner governance as structured group investor behavior and found that behavioral biases affecting individuals also influence pension trustees. Performance was linked to institutional knowledge, organizational stability, professionalism, board composition, engagement, staffing, and diligence. Monthly board meetings performed better than quarterly meetings, retired board members were statistically more effective, and delegation to reliable staff and consultants improved results. Investment expenses and required contribution rates were not statistically significant.

Plans in the highest 20% of Fiduciary Effectiveness Quotient scores outperformed the lowest 20% by nearly two to one. Each unit of FEQ improvement corresponded to a 0.36% increase in five-year investment performance, with the relationship persisting under a one-year lag. The study concludes that governance influences investment performance and can be measured.

Pregnant with her second child, Chrissy Teigen said she has long had stretch marks due to family predisposition but none on her belly. She spends 10–15 minutes nightly applying Aquaphor, coconut oil and Lumière de Vie concentrate to moisturize and help prevent pregnancy stretch marks, with assistance from husband John Legend and daughter Luna. Teigen has publicly shared photos of her thigh marks and said stretch marks and dimples are common among women, including supermodels.

Hui Ying Financial Holdings reported 2017 revenue of $46.50 million, up 88.4% from restated 2016 results, while net income rose 343.9% to $15.27 million. Diluted EPS increased to $0.21 from $0.05. Operating income reached $17.95 million, with operating margin improving to 38.6%.

Loans facilitated increased 59.9% to $1.31 billion across 23,263 loans. The platform served 8,047 borrowers and 69,232 investors, while year-end outstanding loans totaled $436.3 million. Revenue comprised $26.70 million in origination fees, $18.21 million in repayment management fees, and $1.58 million from the newly launched entrusted-loan business.

Operating expenses rose 41.2% to $28.55 million, mainly from sales, marketing, and Nasdaq uplisting-related costs. At year-end, cash and equivalents were $12.68 million, current assets were $55.27 million, current liabilities were $17.47 million, and total assets were $59.06 million. Operating activities generated $24.07 million in cash.

A cross-sectional study assessed contraceptive knowledge, attitudes, and practices among 217 female students at NTA TV College, Nigeria, using questionnaires and logistic regression. Participants averaged 22 years old; 73.7% had experienced sexual intercourse. Good knowledge, attitude, and practice were reported by 55.3%, 47.5%, and 50.7%, respectively. Friends and the internet were the main information sources, while condoms and oral contraceptive pills were most commonly used. Fear of side effects or health risks was the leading reason for non-use.

Being older than 19 predicted good knowledge. Diploma enrollment, off-campus residence, and good knowledge predicted positive attitudes. Plateau indigenous status and previous sexual activity predicted good contraceptive practice. The authors recommend targeted advocacy, improved policies, comprehensive sexuality education, and youth-friendly sexual and reproductive health services. Limitations included restricted generalizability and possible under-reporting of sexual behavior and contraceptive use.

A survey of 9,859 UK adolescents aged 10–15 found girls used social media more than boys and experienced a larger decline in well-being. Girls using social media for at least an hour daily by age 10 had lower well-being at 15. No association between social media use and boys’ well-being was observed. Researchers recommended monitoring girls’ early social media use but noted the link may be underestimated because data were self-reported and covered only school days.

A free domestic violence support group for women meets Tuesdays at noon; call 541-400-0186 for details. AARP offers free walk-in federal and Oregon tax assistance in Hood River and The Dalles. Registration is open for the Feb. 24 Chess for Success tournament for K-12 students. Hood River Valley High School Girl Up is collecting cleaned bras during February for women in need and homeless shelters.

Chicago granted landmark status to the former Johnson Publishing Company headquarters, longtime home of Ebony and Jet. 3L Real Estate bought the building for $10 million and plans a $20 million conversion into 150 luxury apartments while preserving features including the publications’ façade signs. Completion was expected in 2019.

A January 26, 2001 media roundup covers Enron-related energy, financial and workplace issues. California’s power crisis is attributed to flawed deregulation, retail price caps, restricted long-term contracts, declining generation and rising demand. Wind power is gaining renewed investment as a cheaper, cleaner but intermittent supplement, with Enron expanding wind farms in several states.

Enron shares rose after forecasting 2001 profits above analysts’ expectations. Commentary also highlights Enron’s profits from California’s shortage, executives’ political contributions to President Bush, and controversy surrounding its dealings abroad.

In India, Maharashtra faced pressure to honor its Enron contract despite high electricity costs and political resistance to tariff increases. The Maharashtra State Electricity Board was expected to miss a $34.3 million payment to Enron’s Dabhol Power, potentially triggering government-backed guarantees.

Enron employees criticized a comparative performance-ranking system that assigns workers to fixed categories and may place low-ranked staff at risk. Management denied alleged bargaining over rankings and defended the system as appropriate for Enron’s entrepreneurial culture.

The President returns the river and harbor appropriations bill unsigned despite supporting several nationally important projects, including Potomac marsh reclamation, harbor lines, and Mississippi River improvements. He objects that many appropriations benefit only particular localities, exceed Congress’s constitutional powers, and encourage escalating demands for similar local spending. River and harbor appropriations rose from about $4 million in 1870 to nearly $18.7 million in the current bill. He also argues that the total exceeds present needs and cannot be spent economically within one fiscal year, while extravagant spending harms government administration. He suggests appropriating only half the bill’s total, with expenditures limited to projects selected by the Secretary of War under presidential direction and capped at the amounts designated in the bill. Congress can reconsider the subject when it reconvenes in four months.

The Federal Government announced development projects for the South-East, beginning with the Assumpta Science Centre in Owerri, established through an agreement with the Vatican’s Pontifical Council for Culture. Science and Technology Minister Ogbonnaya Onu said the centre supports economic diversification, sustainable development and self-sufficiency through science, technology and innovation. He urged governments and stakeholders to sustain the project. Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha pledged support for its speedy completion.

Pakistan Volleyball Federation Chairman Chaudhry Mohammad Yaqoob urged the federal government to build a well-equipped sports complex in Abbottabad, citing its moderate summer climate as suitable for national camps and international events. He criticized the Rs1.2 billion Narowal Sports Complex as inaccessible and noted that Islamabad’s Liaquat Gymnasium lacks air conditioning. Yaqoob also proposed expanding accommodation at Pakistan Sports Complex. He requested an early, four-month volleyball camp for the August 18–September 2 Asian Games, while camps faced delays and financial issues. Youth and junior camps were moved to Peshawar, where Iranian coach Hamid Movahedi was expected to oversee junior, youth and senior training.

The coach said Chris Pronger’s absence required the entire defense to assume more minutes and responsibilities, with Joe DiPenta entering the lineup and Jackman receiving additional power-play and offensive opportunities. The team had handled similar adversity before and relied heavily on special teams, discipline, and collective effort.

He emphasized reducing avoidable penalties while accepting those taken to prevent scoring chances. Chris Kunitz remained a game-time decision, with his health evaluated after warmup. Players would be used extensively to maximize the chance of winning, but medical staff would not risk anyone’s well-being.

The team began the game overly emotional, took penalties, and struggled on special teams, but strong goaltending and penalty killing kept it competitive. After regrouping, it established its forecheck and played a more cohesive, desperate team game. Huskins contributed effectively by retrieving pucks and making sound decisions, while the defense performed well overall.

Teemu Selanne and Dustin Penner made high-skill plays that helped secure the win. Selanne’s leadership, passion, and revitalized career were praised, though the coach stressed that the organization had not yet achieved its ultimate goal.

The team maintained pressure and a cycle game after gaining the lead rather than sitting back. Matchups were largely deemphasized except for using Pahlsson against the Spezza line. Despite holding a series lead, the coach said the next game would be the hardest to win and preparation had to begin immediately.

The Eagles practiced Monday ahead of Thursday’s preseason game against Buffalo. Newly acquired cornerback Ronald Darby joined the first-team defense Sunday despite limited knowledge of the calls. Questions remain about Alshon Jeffery’s preseason debut and playing time for Carson Wentz and other starters.

CoreWeave shares rose as much as 8% after the cloud provider introduced serverless tools for developing AI agents. The reinforcement learning service automatically adjusts computing power and, according to tests, trains models at 40% lower cost than locally operated Nvidia H100 GPUs without affecting quality. The launch follows CoreWeave’s $1 billion acquisition of AI developer software startup Weights and Biases and complements its GPU rental business. CoreWeave also plans to acquire data center infrastructure provider Core Scientific for $9 billion, despite shareholder opposition.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies up to 2 MHz and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full bridge.

Duty cycles above 50% can cause subharmonic oscillation. Programmable slope compensation mitigates this instability; the minimum is half the inductor’s falling-current slope, while the recommended value equals the full falling slope. A resistor from RSC to AVSS sets compensation. The transconductance error amplifier supports Type 2A or Type 2B compensation, with Type 2A adding a high-frequency noise-attenuation capacitor. Compensation design involves selecting crossover frequency, calculating power-stage transconductance, and choosing RCOMP, CCOMP, and optional CHF.

Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical 175°C junction temperature and restarts power-up below 160°C. During operation, the oscillator turns on the external power switch, and sensed current turns it off when it reaches the internally divided COMP voltage.

A synchronous push-pull GaN design example uses a 500-kHz switching frequency, 5-V output, approximately 25-ns dead time, 50-ns leading-edge blanking, and 7.5-ms soft start. Selected values include a 205-kΩ timing resistor, 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback divider, 20.5-kΩ dead-time resistors, 49.9-kΩ blanking resistor, and 33-nF soft-start capacitor. The transformer uses a 2.5 turns ratio and 40-µH primary inductance. Primary and synchronous-rectifier GaN FET ratings are 170 V and 80 V, respectively. An RCD clamp limits switch-node overshoot.

The example uses a 0.47-µH output inductor and approximately 2.3 mF output capacitance, exceeding the calculated 1.3-mF minimum to improve single-event-transient mitigation. Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins near 35 A using a 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω sense resistor. Other selections include a 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation with 40.2-kΩ RCOMP, 15-nF CCOMP, and 47-pF CHF, plus a 102-kΩ slope-compensation resistor.

The controllers require a regulated 4-V to 14-V supply and at least 0.1 µF of close ceramic input bypassing. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds with a single connection, minimizing switch-node area and high-current loops, routing sensitive feedback and current-sense traces away from switching signals, placing bypass and compensation components near the controller, and using short, wide high-current traces. CFP backside metallization should connect to AVSS through multiple vias.

MIT’s manufacturing process control course emphasizes understanding, modeling, and reducing variation to improve product quality and conformance to specifications. It covers statistical process control, physical and empirical process models, design of experiments, process optimization and robustness, and feedback control. Examples span semiconductor fabrication, microfluidics, assembly, connectors, airframes, and injection molding.

Students should have experience with manufacturing processes and basic probability and statistics. Course materials are distributed through the Stellar website, and lectures are video-linked between Cambridge and Singapore. Two textbooks are required: Gary May and Costas Spanos’s semiconductor process control book and Montgomery’s *Introduction to Statistical Quality Control*.

Assessment consists of about eight individual problem sets worth 40%, two quizzes worth 40%, and a three-person team project; there is no final exam. Problem-set collaboration is permitted, but each student must independently explain and justify their work. Team projects may address process diagnosis, improvement, optimization, robustness, yield, or defect modeling, preferably using substantial existing or newly generated data. Each team delivers a presentation and joint report.

The course frames manufacturing as transforming a workpiece’s geometry or material properties through equipment, tooling, process environments, and controllable settings. Its progression begins with detecting process disturbances through statistical process control, continues with modeling and optimizing processes to reduce sensitivity to variation, and concludes with feedback strategies that adjust controls to counter disturbances.

CJ Affiliate, formerly Commission Junction, is a long-established affiliate network connecting advertisers with publishers. It provides centralized program management, sales and lead tracking, payments, reporting, and promotional tools such as links, banners, coupons, widgets, and product feeds.

Joining is free. Applicants need a website or social media profile with relevant content and an audience, particularly from the US or Canada. After creating an account, publishers complete their network profile, website description, payment details, and tax information. They can then search and filter programs by niche, commission type, category, or country, apply to advertisers, obtain affiliate links, and track clicks, sales, and commissions through the dashboard.

CJ offers thousands of programs across many niches and supports direct deposit, checks, and Payoneer. Payments are issued within 20 days after month-end when minimum balances are met. Earnings depend on the publisher’s effort and may range from a few dollars to thousands.

The platform is described as user-friendly and suitable for beginners and advanced affiliates, though it has a learning curve and advertiser approval may be strict. Its broad advertiser network, detailed reporting, and tracking and payment options make it useful for both advertisers and publishers.

This longitudinal study translated and culturally adapted the Waterloo Footedness Questionnaire-Revised into modern standard Arabic (WFQ-Ar) and evaluated its measurement properties. Following established translation guidelines, two forward translations, synthesis, two back translations, expert review, and pilot testing with 30 Arabic-speaking adults were completed. Minor changes clarified one item and replaced response abbreviations with full words.

The finalized questionnaire was tested twice, one week apart, by 290 adults recruited across Saudi Arabia. Participants had a mean age of 29.9 years; 90.3% identified the right foot as dominant using a ball-kicking question. Participants and experts considered the questionnaire clear, relevant, and appropriate, with no floor or ceiling effects.

Factor analysis supported a single footedness dimension, explaining 55.79% of variance, with all 10 items loading above 0.5. Internal consistency was excellent (Cronbach’s α=0.93), as was test-retest reliability (ICC=0.94; 95% CI 0.93–0.95). The standard error of measurement was 4.5 points. WFQ-Ar scores correlated significantly with the foot-dominance question (r=0.48, p<0.001).

The study concluded that the WFQ-Ar is a valid, reliable, and clinically useful measure of footedness for Arabic-speaking adults. Because participants were Saudi Arabian and non-disabled, testing in other Arabic-speaking countries and populations is recommended.

Lasting peace requires equal rights for all nations, grounded in their collective strength rather than differences in power or resources. Governments must derive authority from the consent of the governed, peoples must not be transferred between sovereigns as property, and vulnerable populations must receive security and freedom. An independent, autonomous Poland is offered as an example. Stability depends on justice, liberty, and popular acceptance. Nations should have access to global commerce through territorial outlets or neutralized rights of way, while the seas must remain free and safe. Achieving this may require revising international rules, limiting naval and land armaments, and encouraging cooperation among governments and navies. Peace demands candour, accommodation, concession, sacrifice, and deliberate planning by states. The speaker presents these principles as reflecting both the views of the United States and the unspoken hopes of people worldwide suffering from war.

President Nana Akufo-Addo will deliver the State of the Nation Address in Parliament on February 8, 2018. Members must arrive by 9:15 a.m. and avoid bringing guests. Parliament will adjourn early the previous day to prepare the chamber.

Seasonal trading uses recurring price patterns linked to times of the year. Silver historically performs best from December to February and July to August, possibly because industrial users place orders early in the financial year. January and July are positive 69.5% and 63.6% of the time, while June and September are weaker.

A strategy backtested since 2001 holds silver from early December through February and again from July through August. Despite holding silver only five months annually, it outperformed buy and hold by about 4% per year, achieved a 26.93% risk-adjusted return versus 7.33%, and reduced maximum drawdown from 71.65% to 23.34%.

The passage specifies TMS320DM8127/DM814x device configuration, electrical, power, reset, clocking, interconnect, and peripheral requirements. Analog TV outputs drive 75-Ω loads in normal mode using nearby feedback resistors; bypass mode exposes video DAC outputs requiring nominal 1500-Ω loads and external amplifiers. Unused outputs and reserved pins generally remain unconnected. Required supply and ground pins must remain connected even when associated peripherals are unused.

Boot configuration is sampled from BTMODE[15:0] when POR or RESET is de-asserted. BTMODE fields select boot order, GPMC configuration, Ethernet PHY mode, XIP multiplexing, and PCIe addressing. Supported boot interfaces include XIP/NOR, NAND, I2C EEPROM, MMC/SD, SPI, EMAC, PCIe, and UART.

PINCNTL1–PINCNTL270 registers control pin multiplexing; zero normally tri-states the output. Multimuxed functions may have pin-dependent timing. Unused inputs require enabled internal pulls or external resistors to prevent floating. External pulls are strongly recommended for undriven boot pins.

The device uses L3/L4 interconnects, multiple voltage and power domains, internal SRAM LDOs, and SmartReflex-related DVFS. Power domains can be switched off, losing associated SRAM contents. I/O groups independently support 1.8 V or 3.3 V, while DDR interfaces support 1.5 V or 1.8 V. Supply sequencing, filtering, decoupling, and reset timing requirements must be followed.

The PRCM manages power, reset, wake-up, and clocks. Reset types include power-on, external or emulation warm, watchdog, software cold or warm, test, and local resets. Most I/O pins enter Hi-Z during reset; boot pins are latched at reset release, after which the ARM Cortex-A8 executes Boot ROM. PCIe and EMAC support reset isolation.

DEV and optional AUX clocks may use crystals or 1.8-V LVCMOS sources. PCIe requires a low-jitter, AC-coupled differential SERDES clock. PLLs start in bypass mode and must remain within specified frequency limits.

The device provides programmable ARM and DSP interrupt controllers, EDMA channels, advanced event triggering, trace, JTAG, two DCAN interfaces, and a three-port Ethernet switch supporting MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII. Ethernet external I/O requires 3.3-V-compatible PHYs.

The city’s $75,000 contract with LIHI covered four months of operating and providing case management at Camp Second Chance through 2017. The self-managed camp requires resident security, prohibits minors, and gives campers no veto over LIHI decisions. A 2018 contract and possible second-year site renewal remained pending.

A March 2001 news digest describes California’s escalating energy crisis. Gov. Gray Davis requested another $500 million for state power purchases, while Edison and PG&E began repaying more than $100 million. Regulators approved rate increases of up to 46%, affecting more customers than initially estimated, as officials warned of summer shortages and possible blackouts.

California accelerated power-plant approvals, relaxed some environmental requirements, and considered about $1 billion in conservation programs. Proposals included appliance rebates, efficiency upgrades, aid for low-income households, and incentives to reduce consumption. Regulators also considered restoring penalties for businesses that failed to interrupt power use during emergencies.

Republican lawmakers sued Davis for details of state power contracts, while criticism of his crisis management grew ahead of the Democratic convention. Utilities were ordered to provide San Francisco and Huntington Beach with detailed blackout information for emergency planning.

President Bush called energy a paramount concern, rejected mandatory Kyoto emissions reductions, and supported expanded domestic or Canadian energy supplies. Canada offered increased oil and natural gas exports. State Controller Kathleen Connell projected a potential $7.4 billion shortfall if California continued buying electricity, though the Department of Finance disputed her estimate.

Judge Susan Illston temporarily halted Trump administration layoffs of federal workers during the government shutdown. Unions alleged the administration unlawfully used the shutdown to cut staff. An Office of Management and Budget filing identified 4,132 to 4,232 planned layoffs across several departments, while OMB head Russell Vought projected about 10,000. Hundreds of thousands of workers remain furloughed or unpaid, prompting financial hardship and increased demand for bridge loans. The administration may appeal the ruling.

The disclosure describes video encoding and decoding methods that allow one bitstream derived from an HDR master to support both HDR and SDR systems. An encoder uses an HDR master, a reference SDR master, and optionally target SDR display properties to determine a color-volume transform that produces SDR output substantially matching the reference SDR presentation.

In one embodiment, transformed SDR values are encoded. SDR systems display the decoded values directly, while HDR systems use metadata identifying an inverse transform to reconstruct HDR values. In another embodiment, HDR values are encoded; HDR systems display them directly, while SDR systems use metadata to transform them into SDR values. Metadata may specify tone-mapping parameters, scaling factors, three-dimensional lookup tables, or sets of one-dimensional lookup tables.

The encoder may optimize the transform by evaluating candidates, emulating target display operations, and selecting the transform that minimizes differences from reference SDR values. Encoding and decoding may also include color-space and color-primary conversion, transfer functions, quantization, chroma subsampling, and corresponding inverse operations. The approach reduces the storage, processing, and bandwidth requirements associated with maintaining separate HDR and SDR bitstreams.

India’s selectors faced a difficult task choosing squads for three ODIs and three T20Is against England in January 2017 because of injuries and plans to rest players before upcoming Tests. The series was India’s final limited-overs tour before the June Champions Trophy.

With Rohit Sharma unavailable, KL Rahul and Shikhar Dhawan were expected to open, with Rishabh Pant potentially selected ahead of Mandeep Singh. Virat Kohli and MS Dhoni were certainties in the middle order, while Manish Pandey, Karun Nair, Suresh Raina and Deepak Hooda were also likely choices. Injuries and expected rest for established bowlers could create opportunities for Amit Mishra, Kuldeep Yadav and Shahbaz Nadeem. Jasprit Bumrah, Ashish Nehra and Bhuvneshwar Kumar were projected as the main seamers. The squad was expected to balance winning the England series with preparations for the Champions Trophy.

Model Ella Ravenscroft, 20, had four changing moles removed after using sunbeds once or twice weekly for two years. The resulting scars prompted her to warn others about skin cancer risks and switch to fake tan. Sunbed use can increase melanoma risk by 16–20%. Nearly 500 people are diagnosed with melanoma annually in Greater Manchester, and about one-fifth die.

Most moles are harmless, but changes in size, shape, colour, texture, edges, or symptoms such as itching, bleeding, inflammation, oozing, crusting or scabbing should be checked by a doctor. People should know their normal skin appearance and seek medical advice about unusual moles, new growths or sores that do not heal, because early treatment can prevent cancer from spreading.

Sprint and The Sprint Foundation will provide free devices and wireless service to 180,000 low-income high school students in over 1,300 schools across 32 states during the coming school year. The five-year 1Million Project aims to connect one million students lacking home internet. Participants receive a smartphone, tablet, or hotspot and 3GB of monthly high-speed LTE data for up to four years. Sprint plans to donate about $2.16 billion in service, support, and staffing. A pilot involving 3,750 students reported improved attitudes toward learning and homework among 86% of participants.

Josie Goodenow will present “All About Bees” at the Laguna Beach Garden Club on Oct. 13, comparing native Blue Orchard Mason Bees with European honeybees and discussing ways to support bee populations and yard health. The free first-visit program begins at 9:30 a.m. at Laguna Presbyterian Church.

Gulf stock markets mostly declined on Wednesday. Qatar’s index fell 2.3% as major banks and blue chips retreated on profit-taking after gains linked to MSCI weighting increases. Dubai dropped 0.5% amid uncertainty over the economic impact of proposed visa and foreign-ownership reforms, though DXB Entertainments gained 4.1%. Abu Dhabi fell 0.4%, while Saudi Arabia edged up 0.1% as Al Tayyar rose after early loan repayment. Egypt’s benchmark lost 1.4%, led lower by property and investment shares.

Pennsylvania parents Nicole Sciortino and Vincent Licciardello, both 30, were charged with endangering their two children after allegedly leaving them unsupervised for three days while Sciortino was in Florida. Police found the children, ages 10 and 11, alone in a trash-strewn home at 58 degrees. Licciardello had occasionally delivered food. Both received $10,000 unsecured bail and were released. The children are staying with family friends.

Hexane is a crude-oil-derived hydrocarbon solvent found in some plants and gasoline. Pure hexane is mainly used in laboratories, while solvent-based hexane is used to extract vegetable oils and manufacture or clean products in the textile, printing, furniture, leather, rubber, glue, gasoline, and cement industries. A sodium hydroxide and methanol alternative has successfully extracted soybean oil, though high moisture increases methanol use. Excess hexane inhalation can cause weakness, numbness, blurred vision, headache, and fatigue; OSHA sets a 500 ppm exposure limit. Demand is expected to rise with refined cooking-oil consumption and hexane’s ability to remove unwanted tastes and odors. China leads global production and consumption, while affordable skilled labor attracts manufacturers to Asia Pacific. North American and European markets are expected to grow due to automotive-industry demand for rubber products.

Jon Klemm is underrated; Greg de Vries had a strong year and became a solid NHL defenseman. Skoula is a promising, well-rounded defenseman, while another talented player ranks highly in goals, assists, and points.

This study evaluated cerebrospinal fluid tumor-derived DNA (CSF-tDNA) for diagnosing and monitoring leptomeningeal disease (LMD) in advanced lung cancer. Using CAPP-Seq, researchers analyzed 81 CSF, blood, and tissue samples from 24 patients, including 12 prospectively treated with osimertinib.

CSF-tDNA variant allele fractions were substantially higher than plasma circulating tumor DNA levels and positively correlated with them. For definitive LMD, CSF-tDNA sensitivity was 91.7%, compared with 81.8% for cytology and 80.0% for MRI. Detectable CSF-tDNA was associated with poorer overall survival. Resistance mutations commonly found in plasma, including EGFR T790M and MET amplification, were often absent from matched CSF, indicating compartment-specific resistance mechanisms.

In the osimertinib cohort, increased CSF-tDNA after three weeks was observed in patients with CNS progression. On-treatment CSF-tDNA was strongly associated with subsequent CNS progression, whereas pretreatment levels were not. Osimertinib CSF penetration did not significantly correlate with CSF-tDNA levels.

The findings suggest CSF-tDNA may improve LMD diagnosis, prognostication, early treatment-response assessment, and identification of spatially distinct resistance. Limitations included small numbers of CSF samples at resistance and limited collection volumes. Further prospective trials and functional studies are needed.

In 2016-17, 719 people were hospitalized with eating disorders in Devon, Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly, including two children under 10. Women and girls accounted for 94% of admissions; anorexia represented 45% and bulimia 24%. Admissions reached a record high, more than doubling from 298 in 2010-11. Charities called for early intervention and timely community care, while cautioning that hospital data reflects only severe cases and does not prove eating disorders have become more prevalent.

NVIDIA entered an underwriting agreement on June 14, 2021, to issue $5.0 billion of unsecured senior notes in four $1.25 billion tranches: 0.309% notes due 2023, 0.584% due 2024, 1.550% due 2028, and 2.000% due 2031. Net proceeds were approximately $4.98 billion and are intended for general corporate purposes, potentially including debt repayment.

The notes are governed by NVIDIA’s 2016 indenture with Wells Fargo Bank as trustee. They may be redeemed before maturity under specified terms and require a 101% repurchase offer following both a change of control and qualifying credit-rating downgrades. The indenture also imposes certain restrictions on liens, sale-leaseback transactions, mergers, and asset sales. The notes rank equally with NVIDIA’s other unsecured, unsubordinated debt but are subordinate to secured debt and subsidiary liabilities.

Medication non-adherence is common among hemodialysis patients, who often take 10–20 tablets daily, and is associated with inadequate complication management and increased mortality. Person-centered care (PCC), including continuity, needs-driven practice, coordination, shared decision-making, and attention to patient preferences, may improve adherence, but empirical evidence is limited. Trust in physicians may mediate the relationship between PCC and adherence.

This study examined relationships among PCC, physician trust, and medication adherence in Japanese hemodialysis patients, including whether trust mediates PCC’s effect on adherence. The multicenter cross-sectional study recruited eligible adult patients from six outpatient hemodialysis facilities between April 2022 and February 2023. Participants provided written consent and completed paper questionnaires. Those without regular prescriptions or with severe dementia or complete blindness were excluded. Medication adherence was assessed using the Japanese 12-item Adherence Starts with Knowledge scale, covering inconvenience or forgetfulness, treatment beliefs, and behavior; higher scores indicate greater adherence difficulties.

- The ADS868xW uses either its factory-trimmed 4.096 V internal reference or an external 4.096 V reference, selected by `INTREF_DIS` in `RANGE_SEL_REG`. The internal reference is enabled by default and requires at least 4.7 µF between REFIO and REFGND. REFIO must not directly drive external loads. Solder reflow and mechanical or thermal stress can shift reference accuracy; placing the device in the second reflow pass minimizes repeated exposure.  
- In external-reference mode, REFIO is an input and the internal buffer drives REFCAP. REFCAP requires at least 10 µF plus a nearby 1 µF capacitor. The buffer must not drive external loads. Its typical temperature drift is 0.5 ppm/°C and maximum drift is 2 ppm/°C over –40°C to +125°C.
- The 16-bit ADC supports single-ended and differential, bipolar and unipolar ranges, with straight-binary output. LSB size equals the full-scale range divided by \(2^{16}\).
- Alarm functions monitor the analog input and AVDD. Input high and low thresholds and common hysteresis are programmable; AVDD thresholds are fixed at typically 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Active flags update each conversion and clear after the current conversion, while tripped flags remain until `ALARM_REG` is read. Alarm status can be provided through the multifunction pin, registers, or appended output flags.
- The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI and source-synchronous transfers, using single or dual SDO outputs. The host sees a 32-bit input/output shift register. Multiple devices can be daisy-chained with common CONVST/CS and SCLK; an optimal frame contains \(32 \times N\) clock edges, and throughput decreases as device count increases.
- The device has RESET, acquisition, and conversion states. The active-low RST pin can perform an application reset or power-on reset. Acquisition begins after power-up, reset, or conversion completion. A CONVST/CS rising edge starts conversion; further transitions are ignored until conversion finishes.
- Data frames begin when CONVST/CS falls and end when it rises. A 32-clock frame accepts a valid command, a shorter frame performs no write but can return selected output MSBs, and a longer frame uses the final 32 input bits as the command. Register reads return data in the next frame; otherwise output normally contains the latest 16-bit conversion result. Device address, range, alarm, and parity information can be appended.
- Nine configuration registers control identification, reset and power, input and output protocols, output content, reference and range selection, and alarm status and thresholds. Standard SPI modes 00, 01, 10, and 11 are supported; SPI-00 is the reset default. Source-synchronous mode outputs a data-aligned clock on RVS and supports internal or external clock sources.
- The ADS868xW integrates a programmable-gain analog front end, ADC driver, reference, and buffer. An example industrial design combines an ADS8681W with an eight-channel differential multiplexer for configurable voltage, current, or temperature inputs, settling to 1% in under 5 µs.
- AVDD and DVDD are independent supplies. Recommended decoupling includes at least 10 µF and 1 µF on AVDD, and close DVDD decoupling. NAP mode reduces acquisition-state power and wakes on a CONVST/CS falling edge; deep power-down disables analog blocks while retaining registers and the active interface.
- PCB guidance includes separating analog and digital routing, using short low-impedance ground paths, placing supply and reference capacitors close to pins without intervening vias, and protecting the device from electrostatic discharge.

Archive360 was named a finalist in two 2017 DBTA Readers’ Choice Awards categories: Archive2Azure for Best Cloud Storage Solution and FastCollect for PSTs for Best Data Storage Solution. Archive2Azure provides Microsoft Azure-based compliant storage and management for legacy email archives and other unstructured data. FastCollect automates PST discovery, rehydration, migration, deletion, storage and auditing while preserving metadata and content for legal and regulatory compliance. Winners were to be featured on DBTA’s website and in its August 2017 magazine.
The 2018 Jaguar F-Pace SVR was filmed testing at the Nürburgring. It may use a 5.0-liter supercharged V8 from the F-Type R or SVR, producing 500 or 575 horsepower.

The Supreme Court is considering Victor Tony Jones’s request to block his scheduled Florida execution. The court has denied more than 30 execution-stay applications this year, contributing to a decade-high 33 executions as of Tuesday morning. Jones would be Florida’s 13th execution of 2025 and the nation’s 34th.

Executions had declined for years, reaching 11 in 2021, amid lethal-injection concerns and a federal moratorium imposed by the Biden administration. President Donald Trump ended that moratorium after returning to office, calling capital punishment essential for deterrence and punishment.

Although the court rarely explains emergency stay denials, it sometimes delays executions to consider underlying cases. It also ruled favorably for death-row inmates in three cases during the 2024-25 term. In the coming term, the justices will consider how courts should evaluate multiple IQ scores when determining whether a capital defendant is intellectually disabled. Up to 43 executions may occur in 2025, the most since 2012.
Figures 1–7 show perspective, front, rear, side, top, and bottom views of an electric fat tire bike. Broken lines depict unclaimed portions.

Coach Sutter praised a veteran’s winning background, professionalism and playoff performance, while describing the opposing team as skilled, hardworking, fast and strong. He said the teams are closely matched and should focus on the next game without making major strategic changes. Sutter emphasized disciplined physical play, drawing penalties, effective forechecking, puck positioning and maintaining a five-player structure. Poor ice, heat, shift length, faceoffs and icings can affect line combinations and puck movement. He dismissed chasing individual matchups, particularly because the home team has the last change, arguing that several defensemen can handle difficult assignments. He noted that players are not machines and that close games can turn on a bounce, call, change or single opportunity, but expected both teams to play hard.
Sid Sivakumar edited the puzzle. August Miller is a farmer and crossword constructor; Rapp is a research administrator, former biologist and published puzzle creator.

Enron ranked 16th on Fortune’s Global 500 amid weakening U.S. corporate profits. Western electricity price declines and federal price caps prompted cancellation of some generating projects, including a Portland General turbine, raising concerns about winter reliability, though others cited conservation and new capacity.

Internationally, climate agreements encouraged emissions trading and greener investments, while Kobe Steel secured financing for two coal-fired generators as Japan deregulated electricity markets. Enron abandoned a Miami-Dade power plant proposal to focus on a stalled Deerfield Beach project.

White House adviser Karl Rove faced scrutiny for meeting with companies, including Enron, while owning their stock before divesting in June. Separately, Enron executives Kenneth Lay and Jeffrey Skilling sold substantial shareholdings while publicly describing the stock as undervalued. Enron’s broadband business recorded a $109 million loss, prompting cutbacks and analysts to remove broadband value from company estimates.

MKM Partners raised Tutor Perini’s price target from $31 to $34 and maintained a buy rating. Eight analysts are evenly split between hold and buy ratings, with a reported consensus target of $27.29. Shares opened at $28, with a $1.38 billion market capitalization. Quarterly earnings of $0.57 per share missed estimates by $0.05, while revenue declined 0.6% year over year. Analysts forecast annual earnings of $1.92 per share. COO James A. Frost sold 7,500 shares for $215,925. Insiders own 23.40% of shares, while hedge funds and institutional investors own 82.52%.

Markets face seasonal weakness, thin liquidity, tax-loss selling and institutional rebalancing. Technical analysis suggests yields may fall further and bond fund TLT could break resistance, potentially supporting SPY, while signaling a possible performance shift. A weaker dollar may benefit commodities, energy and raw materials, while rising gold and lower yields generally indicate risk-off conditions. Growth continues to outperform value. The passage emphasizes monitoring key technical ranges and states the analysis is educational, not trading advice. It also warns that financial and cryptocurrency trading carries substantial risk and website data may be delayed or inaccurate.

The North Carolina Court of Appeals affirmed dismissal of Lewis Williamson’s challenge to Surf City’s closure of a 20-foot portion of North Shore Drive. The town sought the closure to construct public beach-access facilities partly within the former right-of-way. It adopted and published a resolution, notified adjoining owners, posted notices, held a public hearing, and approved the closure under N.C.G.S. § 160A-299.

Williamson conceded compliance with the statute’s procedural requirements and did not dispute that title vested in the adjoining owners to the street’s centerline. He argued that the town’s intended construction made the closure improper. The court held that the statute does not restrict a town’s authority based on its intended use after closure when statutory procedures are followed. Unlike the town in Wooten v. Town of Topsail Beach, Surf City owned adjoining property and therefore acquired a vested interest in part of the closed street. The court also rejected Williamson’s argument that the statute permits only closure of an entire street, concluding that a town may close all or part of a street upon compliance with statutory procedures.

DLSS 4 replaces CNN-based models with transformer architectures for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA. Self-attention enables analysis across larger pixel windows, twice as many parameters, improved frame-to-frame stability, reduced ghosting and denoising artifacts, enhanced lighting, and greater detail in motion.

Blackwell introduces developer-created neural shaders, combining traditional graphics processing with AI through enhanced Tensor Cores, Shader Execution Reordering 2.0, and the Cooperative Vectors API for DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Applications include neural material approximation, texture compression, radiance caching, subsurface scattering through RTX Skin, and generative facial rendering through RTX Neural Faces. Neural Texture Compression reduces memory use, while Neural Radiance Cache estimates multi-bounce indirect illumination from partially traced rays.

The Blackwell GPU family targets multiple market segments. The flagship GB202 contains 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, and 768 Tensor cores, and powers the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, and 336 Tensor cores, supporting the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 has 31 billion transistors, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, and 200 Tensor cores, and powers the RTX 5070.

NVIDIA states that specifications may change, provides the materials without warranties, limits liability, and places responsibility on customers to verify suitability and conduct necessary testing.

The study develops hybrid time-series models to forecast short-term and long-term daily COVID-19 confirmed cases and deaths in the USA, India, Brazil, Russia, and the UK. COVID-19 data are described as dynamic, robust, and containing both linear and nonlinear patterns, making individual ARIMA, SVM, or autoregressive neural network models potentially inadequate.

The proposed hybrid approaches combine linear and nonlinear methods to reduce prediction bias and variance. Experimental evaluation identifies the ARNN-SVM model as effective for confirmed cases and the SVM-ARNN model as effective for deaths. The models are presented as interpretable, adaptable to seasonality, and capable of robust prediction.

Daily country-level data, each containing more than 300 observations and ending January 15, 2021, were obtained from the Global Change Data Lab. Preliminary analysis found that the datasets were not normally distributed and that epidemic curves had not yet shown a sharp decline. The study aims to provide forecasts useful to healthcare workers, policymakers, economists, corporate leaders, and researchers. The preprint had not been peer reviewed and was not intended to guide clinical practice.

Royalty North Partners granted 35,000 five-year stock options exercisable at C$1.47 per share and awarded 37,500 Restricted Share Rights vesting over two years. The Vancouver-based TSXV company finances private mid-market businesses to build a diversified portfolio of cash-flowing royalties.

Tesla entered the U.S. auto industry with a strategy of selling premium electric vehicles before moving into the mass market. Its Roadster, Model S, and Model X established the brand, while the $35,000 Model 3 attracted hundreds of thousands of reservations. However, Model 3 production suffered delays, bottlenecks, quality issues, and excessive automation. Tesla eventually approached 5,000 Model 3s per week in 2018, but continued reporting substantial losses and faced concerns about cash, profitability, and long-term viability.

The established auto industry featured high entry and exit barriers, large capital and research requirements, low automaker margins, extensive supplier networks, and limited customer brand loyalty. Traditional manufacturers increasingly faced competition from startups and technology companies investing in electric vehicles, autonomous driving, connectivity, and mobility services.
