Suppliers were generally more profitable than automakers and were investing in new technologies as electric vehicles required fewer components.

Consumer preferences and transportation patterns were also changing. Millennials researched vehicles extensively online, showed lower car ownership and licensing rates than earlier generations, and prioritized technology features. Buyers increasingly disliked dealerships and expressed interest in purchasing cars online. Urbanization, ride-hailing, car-sharing, bicycles, and electric scooters contributed to declining reliance on private vehicles in some cities.

Electric-vehicle adoption was supported by government incentives and falling lithium-ion battery costs, though limited charging infrastructure remained a constraint. Major automakers, including GM, Ford, Toyota, and BMW, planned substantial electric-vehicle investments. Autonomous driving and connected-car services promised new revenue sources but involved technical, regulatory, safety, and consumer-acceptance challenges. Some forecasts anticipated a shift from vehicle ownership toward mobility purchased as a service.

Tesla differentiated itself through extensive vertical integration, direct sales, proprietary charging infrastructure, software updates, and plans for autonomous ride-sharing. It produced many Model 3 components internally and built batteries and motors at its Nevada Gigafactory. Its highly automated Fremont factory departed from conventional production practices, contributing to manufacturing difficulties. Tesla also faced state restrictions on direct sales and maintained a relatively limited service network.

By 2018, Tesla had achieved a market capitalization exceeding GM’s despite recording profits in only two quarters. Supporters credited Elon Musk and Tesla with accelerating automotive innovation and the transition toward sustainable energy, while skeptics questioned whether the company could survive and prosper amid operational, financial, and competitive pressures.

The application describes a rotating shaft mechanism for foldable mobile terminals intended to reduce folded thickness while protecting and supporting a flexible display. The mechanism includes a main shaft assembly, paired swing arms connected to the terminal housings, connecting rods, and support plates. Swing arms and connecting rods rotate around different parallel axes and slide relative to each other, causing the support plates to move between a flat unfolded position and a folded position that encloses space for the bent display. In the folded state, mechanism thickness is approximately equal to that of the two stacked housings.

Engaging gears synchronize movement of opposing connecting rods and housings. Cam-based limiting mechanisms with elastic parts can maintain folded or unfolded positions and provide folding resistance. Arc-shaped sliding slots and arms guide rotation, while staggered components can improve connection stability. The support plates may connect rotatably to the swing arms or main shaft and slidably to connecting rods or swing arms.

An optional flexible blocking layer, made from elastic steel, plastic, or combined flexible and rigid pieces, covers openings in the main shaft assembly and moves with the folding mechanism. The flexible display may be adhesively attached to the housings and optionally to the support plates, leaving a non-adhesive region that bends into droplet-shaped or semi-arc-shaped accommodation space. The design seeks even display support when unfolded, sufficient bending space when folded, synchronized housing movement, minimal gaps, and an equal-thickness folded structure.

A Kuwaiti court sentenced parents Salem Buhan and Amira Hussein to death for torturing and killing their three-year-old daughter, then freezing her body. The hanging verdict remains subject to appeals and supreme court review.

Dr. Ian K. Smith’s *The Clean 20* promotes clean eating by reducing processed foods and choosing nutritious options across all food groups. It features 20 accessible foods, daily meal plans, 60 recipes and substitutions, and 20-minute workouts to support weight loss, disease prevention, and overall health.

The United States opposed using armed force to collect ordinary contractual debts owed by foreign governments, viewing it as contrary to sovereignty, harmful to weaker states, and conducive to oppression and war. While force might be justified in cases involving fraud, wrongdoing, or treaty violations, the Rio Conference recommended that the Second Hague Conference, representing both creditor and debtor nations, consider peaceful methods for resolving pecuniary disputes.

The passage also describes successful joint mediation by the United States and Mexico in ending a war among Guatemala, Honduras, and Salvador. Peace negotiations aboard a United States warship saved lives and prevented extensive suffering and property loss. The Rio Conference praised this mediation as an example of how coordinated action among American republics could reduce suspicion, encourage peaceful treatment of disputes, strengthen international responsibility, and promote broader peace.
The Ohio Supreme Court reversed the court of appeals’ judgment based on State v. Szefcyk. Six justices concurred; Justice Cook did not participate.

Netflix fell 0.68% in premarket trading despite signing Shonda Rhimes to create future shows, while her existing series remain on ABC. The deal follows Disney’s decision to withdraw movies for its own service and Netflix’s Millarworld acquisition. Barron’s predicted a 50% share decline, citing content losses and rising debt. Netflix remained up 32.95% for the year.

Scientists created kirigami-inspired Mylar parachutes with concentric slits that automatically unfurl into lattice structures, generating drag and falling straight down regardless of their initial orientation. Tests showed they landed closer to targets than traditional parachutes or uncut disks and are simpler to construct and deploy, though their holes reduce drag. A 0.5-meter parachute slowed a dropped 1-kilogram bottle to about 14 meters per second. Potential applications include humanitarian aid, package delivery and space missions, with biodegradable materials and alternative descent patterns under consideration.

The North Carolina Court of Appeals reversed the dismissal of controlled-substance charges against Ryan Jeffery Adams. After cocaine and marijuana were seized, the Department of Revenue assessed a $456,574.26 drug-tax liability, part of which Adams paid. The trial court dismissed the criminal charges on double-jeopardy grounds. The Court of Appeals held that prior North Carolina decisions had rejected the same constitutional challenge and were binding. Although Adams relied on the Fourth Circuit’s contrary decision in Lynn v. West, lower federal appellate decisions are not binding on North Carolina courts. Any reconsideration of state precedent or modification of the drug-tax statute must come from the North Carolina Supreme Court or General Assembly.

The Manchester, Sheffield and Lincolnshire Railway opened the Lincoln–Barnetby–Grimsby line in 1848, primarily to serve Grimsby’s port and transport goods and fish. At Stamp End, chief engineer John Fowler designed a bridge carrying the double-track railway over roads and the River Witham. He adopted William Fairbairn’s then relatively untested wrought-iron tubular box-girder technology following the fatal 1847 Dee Bridge collapse.

The bridge originally comprised a 74-foot central iron span and two likely timber side spans. Its box-girder design predated notable bridges using similar technology, including Robert Stephenson’s Menai bridge and Brunel’s Royal Albert Bridge. An engineering report described it as possibly Britain’s, or even the world’s, oldest surviving wrought-iron box-girder railway bridge and Britain’s oldest still carrying trains.

Increasing train size and weight prompted major alterations. Around 1901–03, the timber side spans were replaced with steel structures, while the central span gained additional support. Cross-girders were reinforced in 1948, and a steel deck was installed in 1968. Network Rail has now replaced the bridge in a £7 million project using one of the world’s largest cranes.

The shiitake mushroom market is projected to grow at a 15.31% CAGR, reaching USD 35.4 billion by 2023. Asia Pacific held 82.54% of the market in 2017, with China accounting for 97% regionally. Growth is driven by nutritional, medicinal, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic applications. Major players include Bonduelle, Mitoku, Agro Dutch Industries, The Mushroom Company, and Modern Mushroom Farms.

Intraday trading involves buying and selling stocks, futures, or forex within the same trading day. It includes scalping small price movements and day trading larger moves while closing positions before the market closes. Its goal is to exploit daily fluctuations while avoiding overnight gaps, but it is difficult and risky, and most traders lose money.

In the US stock market, FINRA classifies certain active traders as pattern day traders. They must maintain at least $25,000 in margin-account equity and generally cannot exceed four times their maintenance-margin excess in buying power. Stock CFDs can offer higher leverage outside the US but are prohibited within the US.

Successful intraday trading requires market education, realistic goals, independent decision-making, a reputable low-fee broker, liquid securities, awareness of company fundamentals, and a quantified, backtested trading plan. Automated systems may reduce emotional interference, while results should be reviewed over meaningful samples of trades.

Common approaches include scalping, momentum, news-based trading, and trend following. Popular indicators include moving averages, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and RSI, though the passage questions their usefulness for intraday strategies. Liquid and volatile markets are preferred, with stocks described as offering better opportunities than forex. The first two hours after opening are presented as a favorable period because liquidity and volatility are high.

A WTI crude-oil futures strategy based on successive lower lows and lower highs performed poorly from 2000 to 2021, averaging a 0.11% loss per trade with a 47% win rate. Its later out-of-sample test recorded 21 trades averaging 0.57%. Intraday strategies are described as harder to backtest and less likely than daily-data strategies to succeed out of sample because of market noise.

Concerns that Google might discontinue Inbox stem from its history of ending services, Gmail’s adoption of Inbox features, and fewer prominent Inbox updates. However, Google says the upcoming Gmail changes will not affect Inbox, which remains a product for specific workflows and a testing ground for email innovations.

Inbox has continued receiving features, including AI-powered Highlights, unsubscribe suggestions, and follow-up reminders. It also remains distinct from Gmail through automatic message bundles, travel information, integrated cross-service reminders, and email-specific reminders. Although Google once hoped Inbox might eventually replace Gmail, its current usage and long-term strategy are unclear. Available signs—including continued development, 10 million Android installs, and a recent update—suggest Inbox was not abandoned or facing imminent closure.

Freelance writer Oobah Butler created a fake TripAdvisor listing for “The Shed at Dulwich,” supposedly an appointment-only London restaurant located in his garden shed. Using a burner phone, a website featuring emotion-themed menus, misleading food photographs and fake reviews from friends and family, he raised the nonexistent restaurant from last place to TripAdvisor’s No. 1 London ranking in November 2017.

As its ranking rose, the Shed received reservation requests, business offers, free samples and international attention. Butler rejected all bookings while emphasizing its exclusivity. TripAdvisor later said it had already removed reviews and penalized the listing before Butler publicized the hoax, adding that its fraud controls primarily target manipulation involving real businesses rather than invented restaurants.

The experiment drew attention to vulnerabilities in online review platforms and wider concerns about algorithmically amplified misinformation. Butler eventually opened the Shed for one night, serving inexpensive instant food to actors and genuine diners; at least one real customer reportedly asked to return.

The Buck Sweep, associated with Tubby Raymond and the University of Delaware, is a signature Wing-T play adaptable to other offenses. It is a misdirection off-tackle run using two pulling lead blockers to exploit defensive indecision and create a vertical running crease, though it can also reach the perimeter.

Within the traditional Buck Series, layered handoffs, a weak-side fullback Trap fake, strong-side tailback movement, and a quarterback bootleg stress multiple defensive gaps and obscure who carries the ball. Its angled blocking allows smaller offensive linemen to displace defenders horizontally. However, the play requires precise timing, spacing, footwork, backfield exchanges, and guards or tackles capable of pulling and blocking in space.

Against both 3-4 and 4-3 fronts, the right guard generally pulls to kick out the cornerback, while the left guard leads through the resulting alley. Other linemen and tight ends use reach, down, back, or combination blocks to form the alley. The tailback follows the guards’ blocks, the fullback fakes Trap, and the quarterback completes the exchange before booting weak-side.

Variations include a shotgun version featuring a simpler mesh and possible quarterback keeper, and an I-Wing version in which the tailback takes a counter step while the core blocking remains unchanged.

This preprint investigates motor coordination after chronic stroke using an easy-to-use high-density electromyography (HD-EMG) forearm sleeve. Seven participants with stroke and seven able-bodied participants attempted functional hand, wrist, and forearm movements while EMG was recorded. Stroke participants completed clinical assessments of motor function, dexterity, and spasticity.

Signals were filtered, corrected for artifacts, converted to root-mean-square features, and standardized across sleeve sizes and arms. Electrode activity was mapped to six forearm muscle groups using able-bodied data. Analyses assessed co-contraction, muscle coupling, and muscle synergies to compare coordination between stroke-affected and able-bodied arms and explore HD-EMG features associated with functional movement ability. The study aims to identify potential motor biomarkers for stroke rehabilitation, movement-disorder research, and clinical care.

A multicenter cross-sectional study assessed SARS-CoV-2 humoral immunity among 1,411 adult emergency-department patients at five university hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, during August–September 2022. Participants provided serum samples and information on vaccination, prior infection, medical conditions, and immunosuppression. Researchers measured Spike (S)-IgG, Nucleocapsid (NC)-IgG, and neutralization against Wu01, BA.4/5, and BQ.1.1.

S-IgG was detected in 95.6% of participants, while 94.4% had received at least one vaccination, 45.7% reported prior infection, and 67.7% met age-based German vaccination recommendations. S-IgG levels increased with vaccination and infection exposures but were lower among immunosuppressed participants. NC-IgG was detected in 24.0% and was the strongest predictor of S-IgG levels.

Neutralizing activity was detected in 94.4% against Wu01 and 84.9% against BA.4/5. BA.4/5 neutralization was 5.92-fold lower than Wu01 neutralization. In a representative 423-person subsample, 73.8% showed neutralization against BQ.1.1. Neutralizing activity against BQ.1.1 was 23.6-fold lower than against Wu01 and 4.2-fold lower than against BA.4/5. Among individuals with detectable S-IgG below 1,000 BAU/ml, 59.6% lacked detectable BQ.1.1 neutralization.

S-IgG levels were the strongest predictor of neutralization across variants, while prior infections, vaccinations, NC-IgG status, age, timing of infection or vaccination, and some clinical factors also contributed. The authors concluded that BQ.1.1 substantially impaired serum neutralization and that S-IgG alone had reduced accuracy for assessing protection against immune-evasive variants, particularly at low levels. They recommended improving vaccine uptake among eligible individuals. The emergency-department population was not representative of the general population, limiting the external validity of seroprevalence estimates.

Reusable container images should document ports, environment parameters, defaults, and metadata through Dockerfile directives such as EXPOSE, ENV, and LABEL, preferably using shared label schemas.

Single-node container patterns separate concerns through modular containers. Sidecars augment applications, ambassadors broker external communication, and adapters standardize application interfaces. Ambassadors can route requests to sharded storage, discover environment-specific services, or split traffic between production and experimental systems. Adapters can normalize monitoring metrics, logging formats, and health checks without modifying third-party application images. Kubernetes examples use Redis, twemproxy, nginx, Prometheus exporters, Fluentd, and MySQL health-check adapters.

Multi-node microservice architectures divide applications into independently maintained services connected by defined APIs. They support team autonomy, independent releases, reliability, and service-specific scaling, but make debugging and system design more difficult.

Replicated load-balanced services improve availability and horizontal scalability. Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching uninitialized instances, while session tracking can consistently route users to particular replicas. Additional replicated layers can provide caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination.

Sharded services partition state when it exceeds one machine’s capacity. Sharded caches use memory more efficiently than replicated caches but can suffer degraded performance when a shard fails or changes. Replicating each shard improves resilience and permits independent scaling of hot shards. Sharding functions should be deterministic, uniform, and based on keys that group equivalent requests. Consistent hashing limits remapping when shard counts change.

The scatter/gather pattern distributes parts of a request across multiple workers and combines their results, reducing computation time or searching data spread across shards. Excessive parallelism introduces overhead, straggler latency, and availability risks; replicating each shard improves reliability and upgradeability.

Function-as-a-service supports event-driven applications by deploying source code directly, automatically scaling and restarting functions, and encouraging modular stateless designs. Its strict decoupling also requires network communication and external state storage, which can complicate operations.

Actress Sonali Bendre Behl announced she has metastatic high-grade cancer and is undergoing treatment in New York. She expressed optimism and gratitude for the support of family, friends, and well-wishers.

Port Gregory suffered repeated power outages over four days, disrupting medical equipment and spoiling frozen food. Resident Betty Sawers reported losing about $500 in food, while a neighbour could not use his CPAP machine. Western Power blamed storm-related resource constraints and said the area’s spur-line location and salt and dust buildup increased vulnerability. Customers without power for 12 consecutive hours could claim up to $80.

The dollar hit multiweek highs against the yen and euro after September U.S. wages rose 0.5%, despite hurricane-driven job losses. Stronger data, possible tax cuts and expectations of a December Federal Reserve rate increase supported the currency, with markets pricing a 93% hike probability.

The coalition’s divergent nationalist aims have produced uncoordinated strategy, conflict among Allies, and misunderstandings with Russia, while contributing to Italian and Romanian military disasters. Sustained unity requires pooling political purposes, broadening popular consent, and shifting power toward moderate-left parties, despite resistance from nationalist governments. Allied success depends on exhausting German reserves on the Western Front while maintaining morale, resources, administrative efficiency, and an effective diplomatic response to German liberal appeals. Germany is expected to pursue winter peace discussions to weaken Allied unity, while the Allies would resist until securing German withdrawal behind the Meuse and Scheldt and beginning an invasion through Lorraine. Such gains—destroying submarine bases, recovering northern France, and threatening German territory—would permit negotiations, while growing American reserves would strengthen the Allies as Germany faced the possible reconquest of Lorraine.

Following U.S. tax reform, Apple gained greater access to foreign cash reserves previously held abroad to avoid repatriation taxes. With a net cash position of $163 billion, Apple plans to become approximately net cash neutral over time, meaning cash and debt would be equal. Achieving this could involve reducing cash through special dividends, larger share repurchases, or increased annual dividends, while managing existing debt through early repayment, refinancing, or scheduled maturities. Apple said it would provide more specific capital-allocation plans with its second-quarter results.

Using cryogenic 4D-STEM and Kikuchi-band asymmetry, researchers mapped local polarization in SrTiO3 down to about 20 K. No polarization appeared in the room-temperature cubic phase, but nanoscale polar domains emerged below the antiferrodistortive transition near 105 K despite the average structure remaining non-polar. At 69 K, domains had a correlation length of about 20 nm and displayed periodic spatial correlations with a roughly 25 nm length scale. Below the quantum paraelectric crossover near 40 K, domains became smaller, fragmented, randomly oriented, and less periodically ordered, reaching a correlation length near 14 nm at 35 K. Thus, quantum paraelectricity in SrTiO3 involves re-entrant disordering of pre-existing polar nanodomains rather than a complete absence of local polarization. Multislice simulations confirmed that polarization direction determines the asymmetry of inversion-related Kikuchi bands.

Fior Markets’ report analyzes the global cooking oil market from 2017 to 2022, covering trends, forecasts, market size, segmentation, competitors, technologies, regulations, trade, and growth factors. It examines product, application, and regional segments, including the USA, Europe, Japan, China, India, and Southeast Asia, using primary and secondary research.

The S&P 500 slipped 0.11% Friday, ending a six-day streak of record closes, while the Dow fell 0.01%. The Nasdaq gained 0.07%, extending its record-closing streak to six sessions. Sentiment weakened after U.S. nonfarm payrolls declined by 33,000 in September amid hurricane disruptions, though wages rose more than expected. Walgreens and CVS each dropped 4.9% on reports Amazon may sell prescription drugs, while Costco fell 6% after reporting lower gross margins. Energy shares declined with oil prices, and concerns included a possible North Korean missile test. Despite Friday’s weakness, all three major indexes gained for the week.

PIMS employees continued their fifth day of protests demanding separation from Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Medical University, forcing Vice Chancellor Prof. Javed Akram from his office and sealing it. Akram offered to resign but opposed suspending medical services, citing up to 20,000 daily patients. Government officials said legal formalities and objections concerning the amendment bill had been resolved and its summary would be sent to the Prime Minister, who had agreed in principle to the separation. Despite appeals to end the strike for patient care, protesters vowed to continue until the bill passes, citing previous unfulfilled promises. Political and civic representatives also joined the protest in solidarity.

Peruvian police are considering expelling U.S. citizen John Dougherty and Canadian Jennifer Moore for allegedly violating tourist status by inciting rural protests against Hudbay Minerals’ Constancia copper mine. The mine temporarily halted operations in November amid demonstrations demanding promised development projects.

Singapore Airlines will restart nonstop Singapore–Newark flights on Oct. 12, creating the world’s longest route by distance at approximately 9,537 miles. Flights will take about 18.5 hours and cut at least four hours from connecting options. The route, discontinued in 2013 because Airbus A340 operations were unprofitable, will use new Airbus A350-900ULR aircraft configured with 67 business-class and 94 premium-economy seats. Service will begin three times weekly before becoming daily after an additional aircraft enters service. Singapore Airlines has ordered seven ULR aircraft and also plans nonstop Singapore flights from Los Angeles.

The team is accustomed to starting series on the road and playing in loud arenas, though the increased media attention is unfamiliar. After persevering through many close playoff games, it delivered a passive, hesitant effort against New Jersey and failed to pressure its defense or Brodeur. The players recognize the Devils’ strong system but plan to remain patient, stick to their established approach, skate harder, create more shots, and improve their work rate in the next game.

Dinbych overcame a 12-10 half-time deficit to defeat Wrexham in a competitive Division Two (North) encounter. Wrexham matched the hosts try-for-try and defended strongly, but second-half tries from Aidyn Jones and Owain Davies put Dinbych ahead. Jack Ratcliff’s late converted try earned Wrexham a losing bonus point. In Division Three (North), Dinbych 2nds also secured a losing bonus point in a 16-10 defeat at Flint.

Egyptian archaeologists discovered a 4,400-year-old tomb near Cairo’s pyramids, likely belonging to Hetpet, a high-ranking 5th Dynasty woman close to royalty. Wall paintings show hunting, fishing and monkeys gathering fruit and dancing. Excavations are underway for another tomb believed to belong to Hetpet in Giza’s western necropolis.

A federal judge rejected the government’s request to delay transgender military enlistment, allowing it from January 1, 2018. The Pentagon is preparing to comply, while the Justice Department reviews legal options.

This mapping review examined U.S. occupational therapy fieldwork research published from 1989 through October 2020. Using the AOTA Occupational Therapy Education Research Agenda–Revised (2018), reviewers categorized studies by research priority, occupational therapy or occupational therapy assistant (OTA) education, and Level I or Level II fieldwork. Four databases and the Journal of Occupational Therapy Education were searched, with independent abstract and full-text screening.

Of 1,619 screened records, 67 articles met inclusion criteria. Fifty-five focused exclusively on occupational therapy, five included both occupational therapy and OTA students, one focused exclusively on OTA students, and six did not specify. Forty-six addressed Level II fieldwork, 16 addressed Level I, and five included both. Most articles concerned learner characteristics and competencies (31) or instructional methods (23). Six addressed professional socialization, three addressed faculty development and resources, and four did not map to the agenda. None addressed theory building, signature pedagogies, or diversity, inclusion, and equity. More than half focused on Level II occupational therapy fieldwork, while Level I OTA fieldwork was nearly absent.

The findings indicate that trends identified in a previous international review persist, with substantial gaps involving OTA and Level I fieldwork. Limitations included the absence of quality assessment, inconsistent descriptions of fieldwork levels, exclusion of gray and non-U.S. literature, difficulty applying the research agenda categories, and publication delays. The authors recommend collaborative research involving academic coordinators, faculty, educators, practitioners, students, and consumers, along with explicit inclusion of fieldwork in future AOTA education research agendas.

A vulnerability in Atlassian Jira and Confluence can enable XSS and SSRF attacks, exposing AWS access keys and potentially allowing server takeover, data theft, or destruction. Although Atlassian fixed the moderately rated flaw and most deployments were updated, researcher Robert Wiggins found numerous major companies and government agencies using exposed legacy versions. Several organizations secured, removed, or migrated vulnerable servers after notification, while at least three unnamed organizations remained vulnerable. Many other deployments may still be affected, making software updates the recommended solution.

England qualified for the 2018 World Cup after an unconvincing 1-0 win over Slovenia, prompting concerns about Gareth Southgate’s cautious 4-2-3-1 system. The passage argues that England should adopt a more adventurous formation using three centre backs and attacking wing-backs. Dele Alli is identified as England’s best No. 10, while Raheem Sterling should remain on the wing. Friendlies against Brazil and Germany are presented as opportunities to test a bolder approach built around Alli’s creativity, Marcus Rashford’s speed and Harry Kane’s finishing.

Texas will replace STAAR in 2027-28 with three shorter tests administered at the beginning, middle and end of the school year. Districts may select approved national assessments for the first two, while the Texas Education Agency will develop the final exam. Results must be released within about two days, and practice tests for grades 3-8 will be banned.

Supporters say the system will monitor academic growth, reduce testing time and ease pressure. Critics fear three exams could increase stress, particularly if all use STAAR-style restrictions, and note that the end-of-year test will continue to heavily influence school accountability ratings. A new progress metric will not be ready at launch, while a TEA report on reducing testing’s weight is not due until 2029-30 and need not be implemented.

Educators and parents want teacher input, relaxed testing conditions and access to assessments such as MAP, which many districts already use to measure growth. They argue that meaningful stress reduction depends on avoiding lockdown-style protocols and reducing the high stakes attached to test results.

This 1902 Foreign Relations volume presents U.S. claims against Russia for the arrest and seizure of the American vessels “Cape Horn Pigeon,” “James Hamilton Lewis,” “C. H. White,” and “Kate and Anna.” It includes correspondence transmitting an English translation of Herbert H. D. Peirce’s memorandum to arbitrator T. M. C. Asser at The Hague, supporting indemnity claims by the vessels’ owners, officers, and crews. The 2018 ebook edition preserves the printed volume’s content and recommends citing persistent document numbers rather than page numbers.

Turkey’s education administration is described as highly centralized, hierarchical, and directorate-based, with limited local participation and top-down appointments. The study argues that principles such as accountability, transparency, democracy, participation, sustainability, efficiency, and flexibility are insufficiently reflected in this system. Turkey’s 2018 PISA scores and GDP per capita were below OECD averages, while the examined OECD countries commonly used educational boards or commissions.

The research aimed to develop a local education management board model for Turkey based on OECD practices and stakeholder views. It used an exploratory sequential mixed-method design. Qualitative analysis examined educational administration in 15 OECD countries whose PISA results and GDP exceeded OECD averages, alongside Turkey. Quantitative data came from an electronic questionnaire administered to teachers and administrators in Seyhan, Adana. Of 421 participants, 61.5% preferred local administration, 61% favored elected boards or commissions, and 41% wanted independent provincial education boards to lead localization. Participants generally supported broad stakeholder representation and transferring most operational responsibilities from the Ministry to local units while retaining central policy, regulation, monitoring, and auditing functions.

The study proposes a Local Education Boards model. Centrally, a National Education Supreme Council would set policies and plans, the Ministry would oversee implementation and evaluation, and a Higher Education Council would coordinate autonomous universities. Locally, provincial and district boards would establish education policies, oversee implementation, select administrators, manage budgets and personnel, determine curricula-related matters, and conduct evaluation through independent supervisory bodies. Vocational education and school boards would include relevant educators, students, parents, unions, universities, local authorities, civil society, and economic organizations.

The study concludes that board-based administration could distribute authority, increase participation, and support accountability, transparency, democratic governance, sustainability, and educational quality. It recommends piloting and evaluating the model before wider implementation and conducting further research on board composition and operation. Limitations include the selected OECD countries, the Seyhan-based sample, the study period, and the model’s focus on general organizational structure.

Spotify, Comcast, and Oracle recently adopted co-CEO structures, though only about 1.2% of Russell 3000 companies have used the model over the past five years. Interest may grow as rapid changes such as AI prompt companies to rethink leadership.

A Harvard Business Review study found companies with co-CEOs averaged 9.5% annual shareholder returns from 1996 to 2020, compared with 6.9% for single-leader companies. Experts said dual leadership can divide responsibilities, support succession, and increase productivity, but unclear authority can create power struggles, employee confusion, added compensation costs, and strategic conflict.

Spotify joins companies including Netflix, Salesforce, Sony Interactive Entertainment, Chipotle, Lennar, Warby Parker, and Revolve in trying the model, either temporarily or long term. Comcast appointed President Mike Cavanagh alongside longtime CEO Brian Roberts, with both expected to work jointly rather than divide duties. Some experts warned this could leave Cavanagh subordinate and recommended clearly assigning operations, strategy, and final decision-making authority.

Oracle appointed two CEOs while former CEO Safra Catz became executive chair and founder Larry Ellison remained chairman, raising questions about where strategic power resides. Experts emphasized that success depends on complementary leaders, clear governance, aligned objectives, shared accountability, and a strong ability to collaborate.

The lecture examines collective Thomson scattering spectra using the spectral density function, which describes electron-density fluctuations and contains electron and ion components. Although scattering occurs only from electrons, some electrons reveal electron behavior while others follow ions and therefore provide ion information. For Maxwellian distributions, plasma susceptibilities depend on the collective parameter \(\alpha=1/(k\lambda_{De})\), species temperatures, and the ratio of wave phase velocity to thermal velocity.

When \(\alpha\to0\), fluctuation wavelengths are shorter than the electron Debye length. Plasma susceptibilities vanish, the permittivity approaches one, collective modes disappear, and the spectrum reduces to the electron velocity distribution. Experimentalists can alter \(\alpha\) through probe wavelength and scattering angle.

For arbitrary \(\alpha\), high-frequency resonances correspond to electron plasma or Langmuir waves. Their dispersion relation depends on electron density and temperature, while Landau damping determines peak width. At very large \(\alpha\), peak position mainly indicates density and width indicates temperature; otherwise both affect peak position.

Low-frequency resonances correspond to ion-acoustic waves. Their existence and damping depend strongly on \(Z T_e/T_i\). They are strongly damped when this ratio is below roughly three and become pronounced when it is much greater than one. Their frequency depends on ion charge, electron temperature, ion temperature, ion mass, and \(\alpha\). The ion-acoustic spectrum ranges from an ion-distribution-like shape to strong paired resonances as damping decreases.

The Saltpeter approximation gives the frequency-integrated electron and ion contributions for approximately equal electron and ion temperatures. Small \(\alpha\) favors the electron feature, while large \(\alpha\) favors the ion feature. Because electron-plasma and ion-acoustic frequencies differ greatly, separate spectrometers are generally needed to resolve both.

Relative electron-ion drift breaks the symmetry of the two ion-acoustic peaks by changing electron Landau damping in opposite directions. Fitting the full spectrum can determine the drift component along the scattering wave vector. Combined with density, this yields the corresponding local current component. With additional symmetry assumptions and spatial measurements, the current may be used to infer magnetic fields. Ion-acoustic spectra can also provide electron temperature, ion temperature, bulk ion velocity, and electron-ion drift, while electron density generally requires the electron-plasma feature.

Magnetic fields can modulate spectral features at ion or electron cyclotron frequencies, but measurement requires nearly perpendicular observation and is difficult. Collisions damp collective features and modify even incoherent spectra, so neglecting them can cause incorrect interpretation.

Finite sampling volumes, measurement times, and collection angles mix spectra from regions or directions with different temperatures, velocities, and wave vectors. Velocity gradients or turbulence can broaden features and mimic higher temperatures. Smaller collection volumes and angles reduce these effects but also reduce signal, requiring more laser power; excessive power can heat the plasma or trigger laser-plasma instabilities.

Current research includes efficient treatment of non-Maxwellian distributions, including machine-learning methods, and multi-angle optical systems that recover two- or three-dimensional velocity-distribution information.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture improves programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI performance by up to 2× through enhanced FP32 processing, second-generation RT Cores, and third-generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity. It also introduces GDDR6X memory, reaching 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/s on the GeForce RTX 3090.

RTX IO works with Microsoft DirectStorage to transfer compressed game assets from NVMe SSDs to GPUs for asynchronous, lossless GPU decompression. This reduces CPU workload, improves I/O performance, and supports faster loading and streaming.

Ampere GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 4K at 120 Hz, and 8K at 60 Hz. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for codecs including H.264, HEVC, VP9, and AV1. GA10x can decode up to 8K60 HDR AV1 content with low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC offloads video encoding and supports up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC encoding.

The data-center NVIDIA A40 combines Ampere graphics, compute, and AI capabilities with 48 GB of memory, expandable to 96 GB through NVLink. It supports virtualization, Quadro Sync, three DisplayPort outputs, and the NVIDIA EGX platform. Compared with Quadro RTX 6000, it provides up to 2× FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to 5× AI throughput, or 10× with sparsity.

The RTX A6000 provides 10,752 CUDA cores and 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, expandable to 96 GB using two cards and NVLink. It targets professional rendering, simulation, AI, and large datasets. The RTX 3090 includes 24 GB of GDDR6X and is described as 1.5× faster than TITAN RTX, while the RTX 3070 exceeds RTX 2080 Ti performance.

Error Detection and Replay technology detects GDDR6X transmission errors and retries transactions, causing performance to plateau as overclocking errors increase and helping users identify memory limits before crashes. NVIDIA states that specifications may change, products require suitability testing, and the materials are provided without warranties.

NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 25, 2015 reported quarterly revenue of $1.305 billion, up 7% year over year, and net income of $246 million, up from $173 million. Diluted earnings per share rose to $0.44 from $0.31. Nine-month revenue increased 5% to $3.609 billion, while net income declined to $406 million from $437 million, partly reflecting $97 million in restructuring and other charges.

Quarterly GPU revenue increased 12% to $1.110 billion, driven primarily by high-end GeForce gaming products. Tegra Processor revenue declined 23% to $129 million as lower smartphone and tablet sales were partly offset by automotive, SHIELD, and development-service growth. Quarterly gross margin was 56.2%, compared with 55.2% a year earlier.

At October 25, 2015, NVIDIA had $471 million in cash and cash equivalents, $4.257 billion in marketable securities, $7.174 billion in total assets, and $1.406 billion in long-term debt. Operating activities generated $664 million during the first nine months, while investing and financing activities used $187 million and $503 million, respectively.

NVIDIA began winding down Icera modem operations after failing to identify a viable buyer. The restructuring affected approximately 5% of its global workforce, with an additional $25 million to $35 million in charges expected in the fourth quarter. The company also recorded a $21 million charge related to the recall of certain SHIELD tablets whose batteries could overheat.

During the first nine months, NVIDIA returned $604 million to shareholders through repurchases and dividends. It completed a $400 million accelerated share repurchase covering 18 million shares and subsequently entered another $135 million accelerated repurchase. NVIDIA increased its quarterly dividend by 18% to $0.115 per share and announced plans to return approximately $1 billion in fiscal 2017.

The company continued patent litigation with Samsung and Qualcomm before federal courts, the International Trade Commission, and the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office. No contingent liability was recorded because losses were considered possible but not probable and could not be reasonably estimated.

NVIDIA also began construction of a new Santa Clara headquarters under an off-balance-sheet operating lease arrangement with bank funding commitments of up to $380 million. Product developments included GRID 2.0, new GeForce GPUs, GameWorks VR, GeForce NOW, SHIELD expansion, and automotive computing partnerships.

The New York Court of Claims awarded compensation for several State appropriations from claimant’s approximately 365-acre property near Massena for the St. Lawrence River project. The property was divided by Middle Road, with land north zoned agricultural and land south zoned industrial.

Applying United States v. Miller, the court held that project-related enhancement could not be included in valuing the 183 acres north of Middle Road taken in 1955 because the record did not establish whether the land was probably within the project’s scope. Despite agricultural zoning, its highest and best use was industrial. The court awarded $32,000, finding no consequential damage to the remainder.

The court found that the southern land was adjacent property not originally expected to be taken, so its value could include enhancement from proximity to the project. It awarded $100 for a 0.15-acre permanent flooding easement. For the 25.34-acre fee taking that separated about 57 acres from the remaining property, it awarded $39,750: $12,675 in direct damages and $27,075 in consequential damages. For a permanent electrical-transmission easement over 55.38 acres, which destroyed the market value of claimant’s remaining interest in that parcel, it awarded $27,700. No additional consequential damages were found.

The total principal award was $99,550, with interest for the periods specified for each appropriation.

Bitcoin reached a six-week high, rising 4.4% to $9,340.88 amid reports of growing institutional interest in cryptocurrencies. Gains boosted other digital currencies, lifting total market capitalization to $427 billion and 24-hour trading volume to $28 billion. Reports cited Goldman Sachs hiring a digital-assets executive, Barclays considering a trading desk, and a survey showing one in five financial institutions may trade cryptocurrencies within a year. Market participants cautioned that regulatory challenges remain unresolved.

A display device includes a substrate, pixel and opposing electrodes, and an encapsulation portion of alternately deposited organic and inorganic layers. A planarization layer covers at least the encapsulation edge, with a steeper side angle than the encapsulation edge, potentially at least about 70 degrees. The planarization layer may cover all or part of the encapsulation, expose a portion of it, and have a flat upper surface.

Patterns such as touch electrodes and wiring may be formed on the planarization layer. Flattening the gradually thinning encapsulation edge expands the area available for these patterns, reduces touch-insensitive dead space and bezel size, and decreases parasitic capacitance between the touch sensor and opposing electrode. The underlying encapsulation limits moisture penetration through the organic planarization layer.

The device may use a top-emission OLED structure with thin-film transistors controlling pixel electrodes. The touch sensor may be an on-cell capacitive sensor using mutual- or self-sensing electrodes arranged in a touch-sensitive area, with associated wiring primarily in the peripheral area.

A substantial Supreme Court majority appeared inclined to allow Rep. Michael Bost to challenge an Illinois law counting mail-in ballots received up to 14 days after Election Day, despite lower courts finding he lacked standing. The justices debated the appropriate standing test. Bost’s attorney proposed allowing candidates to challenge any material election-rule change, while Justice Elena Kagan suggested requiring a likely electoral disadvantage without proof that the rule could change the outcome. Justices Sonia Sotomayor and Ketanji Brown Jackson questioned Bost’s standing because the rule was unlikely to cost him his safely Republican seat. Bost argued the law threatened his victory margin and increased monitoring expenses. Illinois maintained that neither a reduced margin alone nor Bost’s allegations established standing, though outcome-changing or severe reputational harm could. Justice Brett Kavanaugh also warned that denying pre-election standing could force disputes into difficult post-election litigation with uncertain remedies.

DWI arrests in Wichita Falls declined from 39 between January 1 and March 19, 2016, to 25 this year, with five arrests over St. Patrick’s Day weekend. Sgt. Harold McClure attributed the decrease to greater public awareness, sober-driver options including Uber and Lyft, and police presence at celebrations. Uber surveys indicate riders believe ridesharing reduces drunk driving.

Defending the UCLA offense requires disrupting high-post rub cuts, attacking down screens, and protecting the low post. In the NBA “show and recover” approach, defenders avoid switching a big onto a small. The cutter is forced behind the high-post screen, the screener’s defender shows to widen the cut, and the original defender recovers while weakside defenders congest the basket. Defenders then show and recover on weakside down screens, pressure the ball, deny passes, and push post players off the block.

The “SOS” strategy disrupts the offense by trapping the wing after the first pass, exploiting the point guard’s low-post cut and limiting ball reversal. Defenders deny the high post, rotate into helpside and denial positions, and anticipate passes from the trap. On a cross-court pass, rotations follow the near-player concept and occur as the ball leaves the passer’s hands. Once matched up, defenders apply standard SOS pressure, helpside positioning, denial, and post-fronting principles.

Y-Cross is a versatile Air Raid drop-back concept adaptable to multiple formations, personnel groups, play action and coverages. Its core routes are a post, deep crosser and running back flat/check-down, with optional backside combinations. The tight end or a speedy slot receiver can run the crosser.

The concept creates opportunities for deep shots and intermediate completions, particularly against man coverage and Cover 4. It is less favorable against Cover 3 because a post safety occupies the middle, though it can still be used against any defense.

The quarterback’s base progression is post, deep crosser, then running back check-down or dig. Against two-high coverage, the quarterback reads the free safety before creating a high-low read on the Will linebacker. Route adjustments include running check-downs through man coverage, settling against zone and controlling tempo in open voids. Variations include a post-wheel combination and a curl-flat tag, with personnel, quarterback vision and arm strength influencing their use.

The study uses in-situ microscale four-point probe measurements within an SEM, alongside XRD, EDS, EBSD, and bulk resistivity measurements, to relate microstructure to electrical resistivity in heat-treated Al-Mg-Si alloys. Three principal alloy compositions and annealing conditions of 300°C for 24 h, 350°C for 72 h, and 350°C for 120 h were examined.

The alloys contain Al solid-solution grains and Si and Mg₂Si precipitates. Increasing Mg and Si content increases the volume fraction of secondary phases and generally raises bulk resistivity. Grain boundaries, vacancies, and dislocations were considered negligible because of the large grains, absence of mechanical deformation, and limited treatment-temperature range.

For alloys treated at 350°C for 72 h, grain-interior resistivity was similar across compositions, at approximately 2.81–2.88 μΩ cm. For a fixed composition, however, it varied with heat treatment, reflecting changes in solid solution and nanoscale precipitates. No clear relationship was found between lattice parameter and grain-interior resistivity.

Regions containing Si or Mg₂Si precipitates of comparable dimensions showed equivalent resistivity within experimental uncertainty, regardless of precipitate identity or morphology. Thus, precipitate volume fraction, rather than phase type, primarily determines their contribution. Bulk resistivity increased linearly with total Mg and Si concentration for each annealing condition, with heat-treatment-dependent coefficients. The work demonstrates direct microscale separation of matrix and precipitate contributions to alloy resistivity.

Markets face seasonal weakness, thin liquidity, tax-loss selling, institutional rebalancing, and fading earnings optimism. Technical analysis suggests lower yields and a weakening dollar could support bonds, equities, commodities, energy, and gold, though shifts in relative performance and key resistance levels should be monitored. The passage also promotes AI-selected portfolios and warns that financial and cryptocurrency trading carries substantial risk, website data may be inaccurate or delayed, and content is educational rather than official trading advice.

Recent hurricanes exposed lasting health hazards, including power and resource shortages, contaminated floodwaters, toxic chemical releases, mold, mosquito-borne disease risks, unstable infrastructure, heat exposure, mental stress, economic damage and impaired health systems. The author argues that stronger prevention and planning could substantially reduce these impacts before, during and after natural disasters. Recommended measures include improved public education, hardened infrastructure, secured industrial and hazardous sites, stronger seawalls, regular tree trimming and more storm-resistant electrical grids. Despite Florida utilities upgrading poles and flood monitoring, Hurricane Irma cut power to half the state’s customers, and full restoration to habitable structures took ten days.

A Tennessee mother’s video of her son Keaton describing bullying at school received over 18 million views and widespread support. Athletes and entertainers offered friendship, visits and invitations, while a fundraiser for his education collected more than $29,000. Keaton urged others not to criticize people for being different.

The study presents a bibliometric citation analysis of artificial intelligence in STEM education from 2020 to 2024. Using the Dimensions database, researchers identified 101 documents with relevant title or abstract keywords and analyzed a final dataset of 35 journal articles using Microsoft Excel and VOSviewer.

AI applications in STEM education include personalized and adaptive learning, intelligent tutoring, advanced analytics, automated assessment, administrative support, and virtual experimentation. These applications may improve learning outcomes, engagement, creativity, problem-solving, AI literacy, and instructional efficiency. STEM education itself supports critical thinking, collaboration, practical skills, creativity, workforce preparation, and social inclusion. Challenges include ethical concerns, data privacy, learner autonomy, unequal adoption, limited AI literacy, teacher-training needs, curricular alignment, and reduced engagement when AI dominates learning oversight.

Publication and citation activity increased markedly in 2024, when 15 publications received 234 citations, averaging 15.62 citations each. The United States led with nine documents and 103 citations, while China produced five documents with no citations. Nesra Yannier, Kenneth R. Koedinger, and Scott E. Hudson were the most cited authors, each associated with one document receiving 55 citations. The most cited article was “Active Learning is About More Than Hands-On: A Mixed-Reality AI System to Support STEM Education,” with 55 citations, followed by “Smiley Cluster,” with 43. The International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education was the most cited source, and Carnegie Mellon University was the most cited institution.

The study concludes that AI has growing transformative potential in STEM education but requires balanced, ethical implementation and ongoing evaluation. Suggested research areas include long-term impacts, cross-cultural comparisons, ethical frameworks, AI literacy, and integration with technologies such as virtual and augmented reality. Limitations include the restricted timeframe, reliance on one database, and the inability of citation counts alone to indicate research quality.

Coccolithophores are microscopic, chlorophyll-containing ocean algae whose calcium carbonate plates help regulate climate. They remove carbon from seawater, produce oxygen, support marine food webs, and transport carbon into deep-sea sediments, while their fossilized plates form geological records of past climates. Annually, they generate more than 1.5 billion tonnes of calcium carbonate.

Climate-driven changes in ocean temperature, acidity, chemistry, and nutrients threaten coccolithophores and dependent ecosystems. European research teams are studying their carbon storage, species differences, interactions with bacteria, viruses and grazers, responses to environmental change, geographic distribution, and fossil record. Five institutions are campaigning to designate October 10 as International Coccolithophore Day to increase public awareness, ocean literacy, policy attention, and engagement with these organisms’ planetary importance.

On June 28, 2021, NVIDIA completed a corporate restructuring that repatriated economic rights to certain non-U.S. intellectual property through domestication of a foreign subsidiary. NVIDIA raised its expected second-quarter fiscal 2022 GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates from 10% to 13%, plus or minus 1%, excluding discrete items. The domestication is expected to provide a one-time tax benefit of approximately $250 million to $300 million and better align NVIDIA’s corporate and operating structures with relevant international conclusions and U.S. and European tax laws.

At the California Democratic Party convention, Dave Min and Hans Keirstead secured endorsements in Orange County congressional races against Republican Reps. Mimi Walters and Dana Rohrabacher, respectively. Min survived a floor challenge after opponents gathered enough signatures, while Keirstead’s opponents said security delays prevented their challenge from being submitted before the deadline. Endorsed candidates will be identified on sample ballots and can use the designation in fundraising and campaigning.

No candidates in three other targeted Southern California Republican districts reached the required 60 percent threshold. Mike Levin and Bryan Caforio each received 53 percent, while Jay Chen received 47 percent.

No gubernatorial or U.S. Senate candidate earned an endorsement. Kevin de León led Sen. Dianne Feinstein among delegates, 54 percent to 37 percent. Gavin Newsom led the gubernatorial vote with 37 percent, while Antonio Villaraigosa finished fourth with 9 percent.

The Trump administration proposed requiring employers to pay $100,000 for new H-1B visas, citing alleged program abuse. As of June 30, more than 16,000 H-1B workers were employed by at least 930 U.S. colleges and universities, often as researchers, academic staff, physicians and medical-center employees. Nearly half of 16,797 approved visas were concentrated at 50 institutions, and the top 100 institutions held about 70 percent.

The fee would not affect current visa holders, but it remains unclear whether universities will pay it for new applications. Universities, nonprofit research institutions and national laboratories are currently exempt from the annual 85,000-visa cap. The directive permits national-interest exemptions, which higher education advocates argue should cover research and medical hires. Experts and the National Postdoc Association warned that the fee could prevent colleges from filling essential roles and attracting international talent.

Gunmen kidnapped 52 farmers, mostly ethnic Uzbeks, from three villages in Jowzjan province’s Darz Ab district. Police blamed Taliban fighters controlling the area and said elders were negotiating for their release, with a rescue operation possible. The Taliban said it was investigating. The motive remained unclear.

EUR/USD is the world’s most traded and liquid currency pair, reflecting economic conditions in the eurozone and United States. Its exchange rate is influenced by interest-rate differentials, inflation, employment, GDP, central-bank policies, geopolitical events, news releases, and market sentiment. Higher relative U.S. interest rates generally strengthen the dollar against the euro.

Trading approaches include fundamental, technical, and sentiment analysis, using tools such as moving averages, support and resistance, Fibonacci retracements, candlestick patterns, and trend indicators. The passage emphasizes creating strict, quantifiable rules and backtesting them, while noting that results from spot, futures, and other instruments may differ.

Common styles include position trading, swing trading, day trading, scalping, breakouts, carry trades, and correlation-based strategies. Day trading and scalping are described as especially difficult, with most participants losing money. CFDs and leverage can amplify both gains and losses.

Risk management should include appropriate position sizing, limited leverage, diversification across uncorrelated strategies or pairs, and carefully tested stop-loss rules. Traders should adapt exposure during volatile conditions and avoid risking excessive account capital on one trade.

EUR/USD activity is generally highest when European and U.S. sessions overlap, particularly around 12:00–16:00 GMT in summer and 13:00–17:00 GMT in winter, though the best time depends on the strategy. Traders should choose regulated, secure brokers with suitable platforms, fees, tools, and support. Demo accounts can help test strategies and platforms before live trading, although they do not reproduce the psychology of risking real money.

Common mistakes include excessive leverage, poor discipline, inadequate risk management, insufficient diversification, impulsive trading, failing to monitor performance, and trading without a clear, backtested plan. Despite its liquidity, tight spreads, extensive information, and accessibility, EUR/USD is not presented as easy to trade, and backtested profitability does not guarantee future success.

The team is regrouping for tomorrow’s important game. Despite controlling the first two periods, weak power-play scoring and a third-period letup allowed the opponent to rally, emphasizing the need for sustained effort.

The article argues that gold’s rally, miners’ weak response, a bullish inverse head-and-shoulders pattern in the USD Index, and bearish stock signals resemble conditions in 2008. It interprets GDXJ’s limited rebound and underperformance relative to gold as signs of an early, larger precious-metals decline, while expecting the dollar to rise and stocks to fall. The passage also includes investment promotions, reader criticism, related headlines, and disclosures warning that financial trading carries substantial risk and website data may be inaccurate or delayed.

A rare white moose filmed in Sweden captivated viewers worldwide. About 100 live in the country, with their white fur caused by a genetic mutation rather than albinism. Online commenters compared it to creatures from fantasy stories.

Dallas Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones was fined $250,000 by the NFL after video showed him briefly making an obscene gesture toward fans during Sunday’s 37-22 victory at MetLife Stadium. Jones called the gesture accidental, saying he intended to give Cowboys fans a thumbs-up while celebrating the team’s final touchdown. The Cowboys are likely to appeal and have until Friday to decide. The NFL has previously fined other owners for inappropriate interactions with fans.

This study compared prodromal health conditions and medication use before Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), using UK primary-care records from THIN and selected replication in the UK Biobank. THIN included 20,214 AD, 28,222 PD, 4,682 DLB, and 20,214 control patients. Associations were assessed across periods up to 15 years before diagnosis.

All 12 examined health conditions were more frequent in affected patients than controls during the five years before diagnosis. Memory problems were more common before AD, tremor before PD, and confusion, hallucinations, falls, depression, and several autonomic symptoms before DLB. Constipation, urinary dysfunction, and hypotension preceded all three disorders, with generally stronger associations for PD and DLB. Treatments for depression, anxiety, and constipation, including serotonin reuptake inhibitors and benzodiazepines, were more frequently prescribed before diagnosis.

Antidiabetic drugs and several antihypertensive classes were prescribed less often before the disorders than among controls. Beta-blockers were more frequently prescribed before PD and DLB than before AD. Statin use was lower before PD than before AD or DLB; this difference was replicated in the UK Biobank, although cholesterol measurements did not differ between PD and AD in the small available sample.

Among PD patients, prescriptions for hypercholesterolemia, constipation, depression, and psychosis before PD diagnosis were associated with dementia developing within five years. The authors conclude that neurodegenerative diseases have long, partly distinct prodromal profiles observable in primary care. Limitations include potentially delayed or imprecise diagnoses, disease heterogeneity, control matching, and the inability to determine whether medication associations were causal or reflected underlying symptoms or comorbidities. Further research was recommended on lipid-lowering therapies, cholesterol, neurodegenerative disease risk, and dementia after PD diagnosis.

Gold is a precious metal used for jewelry, exchange, status, and storing value. Gold trading seeks to profit from price movements through futures, options, spot markets, stocks, CFDs, and ETFs, with most transactions cash settled. Traders may also use gold as a hedge or safe-haven asset.

Gold has historically served as currency and backed fiat money, including under the Bretton Woods system. After the gold standard ended, gold futures began trading on COMEX in 1974, followed by growth in over-the-counter and online trading.

Gold strategies are difficult because prices depend heavily on unpredictable macroeconomic news. A backtest using the GLD ETF from late 2004 to September 2021 found that most gains occurred overnight. Holding GLD from Thursday’s close to Friday’s close averaged 0.14% per trade with a 1.4 profit factor. Holding from Thursday’s close to Monday’s open averaged 0.19%, with a 1.3 profit factor. The passage states that adding one simple, unspecified parameter improved the weekend strategy enough to justify a small position.

The study reviewed the latest Voluntary National Reviews submitted between 2016 and 2021 by 18 Eastern Mediterranean Region countries, assessing reporting on health-related Sustainable Development Goal targets and indicators and comparing data availability with WHO records.

All countries had mechanisms for monitoring SDG progress, and 11 reported on all 17 goals. Higher-income countries generally reported more comprehensively. Although 17 countries prioritized targets and indicators, only eight specified national 2030 targets. Fourteen reviews identified limited data availability as a challenge, alongside insufficient analytical capacity, poor data quality, limited disaggregation, inadequate statistical tools and restricted transparency.

Reporting varied by indicator type and income level. Maternal mortality was reported by all countries, while neonatal and under-five mortality were also commonly included. Trend reporting was limited: Qatar alone reported trends across all SDG3 indicators. Reviews averaged data for about 11 SDG3 indicators, and data reported to WHO were often omitted. Indicators derived from disease surveillance and civil registration systems were reported more often than those based on routine information systems or national surveys.

Because VNR reporting is voluntary, omitted indicators do not necessarily indicate unavailable data. Nevertheless, the findings highlight weaknesses in health information systems. Strengthening regulatory frameworks, analytical and data-collection capacity, civil registration and vital statistics systems, population surveys, investment and data access could improve monitoring and support achievement of health-related SDGs.

Tesla Motors’ unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2015 reported quarterly revenue of $955.0 million, up from $769.3 million a year earlier, primarily due to increased Model S deliveries. Quarterly gross margin declined from 27.7% to 22.3%, while net loss widened to $184.2 million from $61.9 million. For the first six months, revenue was $1.89 billion and net loss was $338.4 million.

At June 30, Tesla had $6.47 billion in assets, $5.70 billion in liabilities, $715.9 million in stockholders’ equity, and $1.15 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Six-month operating cash outflow was $291.3 million, investing outflow was $855.2 million, largely reflecting $831.2 million in property and equipment purchases, and financing inflow was $404.5 million.

Tesla had delivered more than 78,000 Model S vehicles through June 2015. It planned to begin Model X deliveries late in the third quarter, target Model 3 deliveries in late 2017, and deliver 50,000–55,000 Model S and Model X vehicles during 2015. Tesla expected approximately $1.5 billion in 2015 capital expenditures and 45%–50% growth in operating expenses.

The company continued expanding production capacity, stores, service centers and its 480-location Supercharger network. Gigafactory construction near Reno continued, with initial production planned for the first quarter of 2016. Tesla had incurred $206.6 million in Gigafactory construction costs.

Tesla borrowed $114.3 million under a warehouse credit facility and $50.0 million under a revolving credit facility. Its 2018 convertible notes became convertible during the third quarter of 2015, while its 2019 and 2021 notes remained classified as long-term debt. Management stated that existing liquidity and projected operating cash flow were expected to fund operations for the following 12 months, while identifying production ramps, supplier performance, foreign expansion, resale guarantees, leasing, and Gigafactory execution as risks.

Origin PC’s customizable Eon15-S gaming laptop starts at $999, featuring Nvidia GeForce 1050Ti graphics, a Core i3 processor and 120GB SSD. An additional $100 upgrades it to Core i5 and double the storage. It costs more than competing Dell and Acer models but offers an IPS display and 24/7 US-based lifetime support, with a one-year warranty.

The Supreme Court declined to hear Ghislaine Maxwell’s appeal of a ruling concerning Jeffrey Epstein’s 2007 non-prosecution agreement. Maxwell argued that its protection of potential co-conspirators bound all U.S. attorney’s offices and barred some charges against her. The 2nd Circuit held that such agreements bind only the region making them unless they explicitly cover multiple districts. Solicitor General D. John Sauer said the agreement’s unusual, case-specific interpretation did not warrant Supreme Court review. Maxwell is serving a 20-year sentence for sex trafficking of a minor and other charges.

Princeton researchers and international collaborators developed Diag2Diag, an AI tool that uses data from existing fusion sensors to generate detailed synthetic readings for other diagnostics, including missing or degraded sensors. Trained on data from the DIII-D National Fusion Facility, it can provide information about rapidly changing plasma conditions, especially at the difficult-to-measure pedestal edge.

The tool could improve plasma monitoring and control while reducing the number of diagnostics needed in commercial reactors, making them more compact, reliable, and economical. Diag2Diag also produced evidence supporting the theory that resonant magnetic perturbations suppress damaging edge-localized modes by creating magnetic islands that flatten plasma temperature and density at the edge. Researchers plan to apply the system to additional fusion diagnostics and potentially to fields such as spacecraft and robotic surgery.

The strategy goes long when IBS is below 0.25 and the close is below the previous five days’ lowest low, then exits after five days. Since January 1993, it produced 517 trades, including 309 winners, averaging 0.46% per trade with a 60% win rate. Profitability peaks after 3–7 days; five-day exits yielded a 10.76% annualized return with less market exposure than buy and hold. Recent performance has weakened. A short-selling variation uses higher range criteria, around 0.75–0.9, and returned nearly 10%, though short strategies were less profitable and harder to identify.

Neural Radiance Cache uses real-time-trained neural shaders to infer multi-bounce indirect lighting from path-traced rays after one bounce. This reduces GPU ray-tracing workload while improving global illumination quality, scalability, adaptability, and image quality across varied game scenarios.
The Washington Court of Appeals reversed and remanded the Spokane County Superior Court’s judgment in State v. Douglas John Nelson in an unpublished opinion filed July 3, 2014.

The passage compares 10 AI writing tools for creating marketing copy, blog posts, articles, product descriptions, social media content and other materials. Jasper emphasizes original, SEO-optimized long-form content. Copy.ai provides templates, multilingual generation and short-form copy. Frase focuses on research, competitor analysis and SEO optimization. Article Forge generates articles from keywords and supports bulk automation. Rytr offers multilingual writing, varied tones and plagiarism checking. CopySmith targets e-commerce content and Shopify product descriptions. Hypotenuse creates audience-specific copy and automated product descriptions. Kafkai specializes in niche, SEO-ready articles, while Peppertype provides templates, copywriting frameworks, autocorrection and engagement tracking. The tools vary in quality, word or credit limits, free trials, subscription prices and enterprise options. The passage recommends choosing according to requirements and budget, identifies Jasper as the author’s preferred option, and discloses affiliate links.

The study evaluated the MicroGEM Sal6830 SARS-CoV-2 Saliva Test as a point-of-care RT-PCR system operated by healthcare workers without laboratory training. Unlike nasopharyngeal-swab tests requiring additional sample handling, patients self-deposit saliva into a sealed cartridge, reducing discomfort, operator exposure, contamination, and sample mix-ups. Results are displayed in approximately 30 minutes.

At two U.S. clinics, six healthcare workers tested 48 blinded samples. All valid results matched expectations; one positive sample produced an invalid result. A prospective comparison involving 119 patients assessed Sal6830 against the Cepheid Xpert Xpress CoV-2/Flu/RSV test. Positive, negative, and overall agreement were 87.2%, 97.2%, and 93.3%, respectively.

Nine non-laboratory healthcare workers completed a usability questionnaire. They reported that Sal6830 was easy to operate, required no technical support, produced readily interpretable results, and was suitable for point-of-care use. The study concluded that non-laboratory-trained healthcare workers could use Sal6830 confidently and accurately with self-collected saliva samples.

The speaker is thrilled to win the Stanley Cup, praises Buffalo’s young team, and dismisses controversy over an unseen goal. After missing the previous playoffs, he appreciated the grueling journey, adversity, and injuries involved. He credits experienced teammates, including Hull and Mike, for playing hurt and battling hard throughout the series.

Ovarian cancer is often diagnosed late in the UK, partly because symptoms are mistaken for common conditions, appointments are delayed, or concerns are dismissed. The four main symptoms are persistent bloating, difficulty eating or feeling full quickly, needing to urinate more frequently or urgently, and persistent abdominal or pelvic pain. Other possible signs include lower-back pain, digestive discomfort, nausea, unexplained fatigue, and postmenopausal bleeding.

There is no routine screening test for ovarian cancer, and cervical screening does not detect it. A CA-125 blood test may support assessment but cannot diagnose ovarian cancer alone because other conditions can raise the protein level.

Anyone experiencing persistent or unusual symptoms should consult a doctor, even without all four main symptoms. A symptom diary or Ovarian Cancer Action’s online checker may help identify patterns and support medical discussions. Early detection is critical: the passage reports a 95% survival chance when caught early, compared with 16% at stage four. Awareness among patients, families, and friends can encourage earlier medical attention.

In *New York State Rifle & Pistol Ass’n v. Bruen*, the Supreme Court established a two-step Second Amendment test: challengers must show that the amendment’s plain text covers their conduct, after which the government must demonstrate that its regulation accords with the nation’s historical firearm-regulation tradition.

Critics argue that this test demands historical expertise judges lack. The author responds that judges are lawyers, not historians, and use history differently because they must resolve legal disputes despite uncertainty. Historical inquiry is already inherent in adjudication, while legal tools such as burdens of persuasion help courts reach decisions when evidence is unclear.

The author argues that *Bruen*’s historical demands are manageable. Precedent clarifies much of the Second Amendment’s text, and genuine regulatory traditions should appear across durable legal sources such as statutes, judicial decisions, legislative records, treatises, and administrative materials. Historical work will be greatest when governments seek recognition of new regulatory traditions, though early American firearm regulation was limited.

Justice Breyer favored supplementing history with means-ends scrutiny. The author contends that this could place judges in a legislative role and maintains that understanding law requires confronting its historical foundations.

Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico on September 20, 2017, causing severe flooding, widespread infrastructure and electricity failures, over $82 billion in damages, and major agricultural losses. Indirect deaths can result from disrupted transportation, medicine, and health services, but inconsistent death-classification practices complicate mortality estimates. Earlier studies of excess mortality had limited timeframes, causes, or treatment of population displacement.

The research proposes a semiparametric Poisson regression model to estimate cause-specific excess deaths after Maria and determine how long mortality effects persisted. The model incorporates population size and displacement, pre- and post-emergency periods, causes of death, interactions between period and cause, annual mortality trends, and smooth within-year variation. Parameters are estimated through penalized likelihood, with smoothing penalties selected using restricted maximum likelihood. Excess deaths are calculated by comparing predicted mortality under post-emergency and baseline conditions using a population size unaltered by post-emergency displacement to avoid double-counting its effect.

The passage describes a voice-directed inspection system that enables multiple inspectors to inspect the same business asset concurrently. A host computer supplies an inspection plan to a site computer, which divides unfinished work into sections and assigns noninterfering sections to inspectors’ portable devices and headsets.
