The devices provide audible instructions, recognize spoken updates, and return results to the site computer, which consolidates and sends them to the host.

Assignments may request specific or any unfinished section. Sections can correspond to distinct physical parts or systems and may be allocated by priority, request order, inspector qualifications, or prior work. If only one unfinished section remains, it is assigned to one inspector; if none remain, the system reports no available work.

The system includes speech recognition, text-to-speech conversion, inspection-plan editing, result review, authorization, mandatory-step enforcement, barcode scanning, free-form transcription, and network communication. Inspection plans may be created or modified centrally or at an inspection site. The disclosed subject matter may be implemented as hardware, software, methods, systems, or computer-readable program instructions.

Dylan Drysdale, Tim Loughran and Garry Cullum won their respective class titles at the final round of the 2017 Molecule ProKart Series at Agrisea Raceway. Drysdale secured the Wifiplus KZ2 title by four points over final and round winner Aaron Wilson, after Mat Kinsman crashed early in the Final. Loughran won the Aarque Group KZ2 Masters title and round, while Brett Hollander finished second overall and Enrico van der Griend retained third despite crashing. Cullum dominated KZ2 Restricted, winning every race to claim a record fourth title, 20 points ahead of Regan Hall. Aaron Wooley placed third overall.

DryShips raised $14.5 million by issuing 7.9 million shares at an average $1.79 under its continuous offering, despite requesting $30 million from Kalani Investors. The issuance increased outstanding shares to 54.92 million and caused 16.8% dilution. Weak trading demand limited issuance to 8.86% of volume.

At the April 17 close, $173.4 million remained under the offering, compared with DryShips’ $106 million market capitalization. At the recent pace, completion would take about 54 trading days and require approximately 105.7 million additional shares, producing substantial dilution.

The author argues that continued equity issuance and price declines could stall the offering, prompting DryShips to obtain debt financing. The author also expects the company could resume equity issuance following any debt-related stock-price increase. DryShips remained roughly 30% above the $75 million market-value threshold associated with F-3 issuance rules. The author disclosed no current position but anticipated potentially trading the highly volatile stock.

The ADS868xW family integrates a high-bandwidth ADC input driver, programmable gain amplifier, precision reference and buffer around a 16-bit SAR ADC. It supports single-ended or differential bipolar and unipolar inputs, producing straight-binary output with an LSB size of full-scale range divided by 2¹⁶.

The device defaults to an internal 4.096-V reference, selected through INTREF_DIS. Internal-reference operation requires at least 4.7 µF between REFIO and REFGND; REFIO must not directly drive external loads. Soldering and repeated reflow can shift reference accuracy, so minimizing thermal exposure is recommended. External-reference mode accepts 4.096 V at REFIO and uses the internal buffer; REFCAP requires at least 10 µF plus a nearby 1-µF capacitor. The buffer operates from –40°C to 125°C with typical drift of 0.5 ppm/°C and maximum drift of 2 ppm/°C.

Programmable input alarms compare conversion results against independent high and low thresholds with shared hysteresis. Fixed AVDD alarms trigger below 4.7 V or above 5.3 V. Active flags update each conversion and clear afterward unless the condition persists; tripped flags remain until ALARM_REG is read. Alarm information is available through the multifunction output pin, registers or appended output flags.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI, dual-SDO and source-synchronous protocols using internal or external clocks. Devices can be connected individually or in a daisy chain. Daisy-chained devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, require identical configuration, and optimally use 32 × N clocks per frame; throughput decreases as device count increases.

The device has RESET, acquisition and conversion states. RESET can perform an application reset or full power-on reset. Acquisition begins after power-up, reset or conversion completion. A CONVST/CS rising edge starts conversion, during which further transitions are ignored. Nine configuration registers control reset, power, SPI input and output protocols, output formatting, input range, reference selection and alarms.

Data-transfer frames begin when CONVST/CS falls and end when it rises. A 32-clock frame accepts a valid command; shorter frames permit partial output reads but treat writes as NOP, while longer frames use the final 32 input bits. Commands support byte and half-word reads, writes, bit setting and bit clearing. Output can contain conversion data, register data or fixed patterns, with optional device address, range, alarm and parity fields.

The device supports NAP and deep power-down modes. NAP is entered after conversion while CONVST/CS remains high and exits on its falling edge. Power-down disables analog blocks while retaining registers and keeping the interface active.

An example industrial design combines the ADS8681W with an eight-channel differential multiplexer for software-configurable voltage or current inputs. Supported industrial ranges include ±2.5 V, ±5 V, ±10 V, 0–5 V, 0–10 V, 4–20 mA and 0–20 mA. The device settles to 1% within 5 µs and supports inputs up to ±12.288 V.

AVDD and DVDD are independent supplies. Recommended decoupling includes 10 µF and 1 µF on AVDD and at least 10 µF near DVDD. PCB layout should separate analog and digital sections, use short low-impedance grounding, keep bypass capacitors close to pins and avoid vias between reference or supply pins and their capacitors.
NASA’s proposed HAMMER spacecraft could deflect small asteroids or deploy a nuclear device against Bennu, a potentially hazardous asteroid with a 1-in-2,700 Earth-impact chance in 2135.

The authors reconsider their premature bearish stance on U.S. equities, arguing that 21 charts and improving market breadth indicate underlying strength despite low VIX concerns. They disclose long positions in U.S. equities and VIX and state the analysis is opinion, not investment solicitation.

When an injury is not immediately addressed by the referee and no attack is underway, players may kick the ball out as an act of sportsmanship. After treatment, the opposing team takes the throw-in but should return possession, usually backward to a defender. Neither team should exploit this courtesy, and play should resume only after the receiver controls the ball and the thrower is positioned. Similar etiquette applies to dropped-ball restarts when the injured player’s team had possession.

Teachers’ Union of Ireland general secretary John MacGabhann warned teachers that Facebook friendships with students can undermine professional boundaries and that careless social media posts may threaten employment or create legal problems. He urged teachers to pause before posting, avoid online feuds, and settle disputes offline. He also criticised employers who expect constant electronic availability, advising teachers not to respond to unreasonable out-of-hours messages and to switch off their devices.

The lecture emphasizes evaluating poker decisions by expected value rather than actual outcomes, since luck can reward poor decisions or punish good ones in the short term. The law of large numbers causes repeated random outcomes to approach their expected values.

Three reasoning levels are presented. Level one compares a specific hand against an assumed specific opposing hand and is generally unfounded. Level two, exploitative play, compares one’s hand with an opponent’s probability distribution of hands, using prior actions and tendencies to maximize expected value. Its weakness is that opponents can adapt. Level three, optimal play, compares both players’ ranges and selects frequencies that prevent exploitation. This resembles a Nash equilibrium, unlike exploitative strategies that can be counter-exploited.

Blinds create incentives to play; without forced money in the pot, rational players would generally fold. Stack sizes should therefore be measured in big blinds. Effective stack size reflects how much can actually be won or lost against remaining opponents.

Position determines how many players remain between a player and the blinds. Later positions permit weaker opening hands because fewer opponents must be overcome. Equity is the probability of winning, or the expected fraction of the pot, based on unknown future cards or opponents’ possible hands. It can be calculated by counting outs and hand combinations or using tools such as PokerStove.

When no one has entered a pot, beginners should generally raise rather than call, giving themselves a chance to win the blinds immediately. A suggested tournament opening size is about 2.25 big blinds. With antes and an effective stack of roughly 12 big blinds or less, going all-in is recommended; without antes, the threshold is about 10 big blinds. Antes encourage wider and more aggressive play.

Opening ranges should be tight in early position and expand substantially near the button. Beginners are advised to favor conservative ranges because premium hands are easier to play. Decisions should increasingly depend on position, effective stack size, ranges, and equity rather than cards alone. Very short stacks do not automatically justify playing any hand because opponents receive favorable calling odds.

Bluffing means betting a weak hand to induce folds. Value betting means betting strong hands to obtain calls, while medium-strength hands are often checked toward showdown. Final examples apply pot odds, equity, and Nash ranges to preflop all-in decisions, showing that a hand such as suited king-queen can have sufficient equity against multiple opponents.

Hendrik Bessembinder’s 2017 study examined 26,000 U.S. stocks from 1926 to 2015 and found that only 43% outperformed one-month Treasury Bills during their public lifetimes. Just 86 stocks generated half of total market returns, while 30 companies produced 30% of returns. Thus, strong historical market averages of about 10% annually were driven by relatively few exceptional stocks, while the median stock performed poorly.

A similar study of the Oslo Stock Exchange from 1985 to 2017 found that only 18 large companies, representing 2.7% of IPOs, accounted for all 2,000 billion NOK in added value. Most shares underperformed risk-free interest rates.

These findings show that randomly selecting individual stocks has a high probability of producing poor returns. The passage recommends passive funds as the easiest solution and emphasizes diversification for investors choosing individual stocks.

VentureWire’s May 17, 2001 edition reports venture financings, restructurings, acquisitions, product launches, and personnel changes. Tahoe Networks launched with $38 million, Hermes allocated $965 million to private investments, Startups.com shifted to market intelligence and cut 30% of staff, and OffRoad Capital reorganized while halving its workforce. Other funding recipients included Alphamosaic, Xora, Foundstone, Beyond Genomics, Comlase, and e.Intelligence. Eazel ceased operations after failing to secure financing, while RoundArch cut 12% of its North American staff. Several technology and printing-related acquisitions were announced. Bezeq and Discount Capital Markets established a $50 million communications venture fund, and multiple companies and venture firms announced executive or personnel appointments.

E-Maintenance integrates real-time monitoring, predictive intelligence, communications, and web-enabled tools to reduce downtime, assess equipment degradation, and connect manufacturing systems with e-business platforms such as ERP, customer relationship management, and supply chain management. Proper implementation can improve equipment reliability, asset performance, and coordination with suppliers and customers.

Further development requires degradation-prediction methods, links between machine degradation and product quality, data-mining tools, scalable communications platforms, stronger security, distributed decision-making systems, workforce training, and an enterprise culture supportive of e-manufacturing.

Reconfigurable maintenance aligns production systems with changing customer requirements and demand. Shared diagnostic knowledge, service activities, and production data can improve reconfiguration efficiency and support system reliability, sustainability, and serviceability. Modular systems use distributed communication, sensors, remote monitoring, and control centers to schedule and optimize maintenance while reducing costs. Historical data, expert systems, and knowledge bases help detect abnormalities, identify degradation trends and causes, select corrective measures, and adapt maintenance policies when system configurations change.

Because mass customization, competition, and market fluctuations require rapid, low-cost responses, enterprises need integrated reconfigurable maintenance systems to address adverse production conditions, maintain quality, and ensure the reliability of changing production configurations.

The focus is on starting strong against a team fighting to extend the series and return to the speaker’s building. Given the opponent’s home playoff success, the team must expect a difficult game and be prepared to compete.

The speaker accepts executive office with gratitude and accountability, pledging to dedicate his abilities to public service. He promises to execute federal duties within constitutional limits, preserve peace and honorable foreign relations, respect state sovereignty, practice strict fiscal economy, reduce national debt, and ensure accountable use of public funds. Agriculture, commerce, and manufacturing should receive equitable treatment, while internal improvements and knowledge should be constitutionally promoted. He opposes expanding standing armies, supports civilian control of the military, naval improvement, maintained defenses, and a strong national militia. He advocates just treatment of Indian tribes and reform of federal patronage and appointments to protect elections and remove unfaithful or incompetent officials. He intends to appoint diligent, talented, and honest public servants, seek guidance from predecessors and other government branches, rely on public support, and pray for continued divine protection of the country.

Fired federal prosecutor Michael Ben’Ary said a false social media post apparently prompted his dismissal while he was prosecuting an Afghanistan airport bombing case. His letter accused Justice Department leaders of prioritizing punishment of President Trump’s perceived enemies over national security. Ben’Ary was targeted online as a Biden administration ally amid the indictment of former FBI Director James Comey.

Yandex will report second-quarter 2018 financial results on July 26, 2018. Management will hold a conference call and webcast at 8:00 a.m. U.S. Eastern Time, with a replay available until August 2. Yandex develops machine-learning-powered technology products and services.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said India’s SCO membership strengthens the group’s political profile and ability to stabilize Central and South Asia, including Afghanistan. He praised India’s independent foreign policy but called bilateral trade unsatisfactory, citing a $30 billion target by 2025 and increased Russian defence technology transfers. Lavrov argued that the US force-based Afghanistan strategy had failed to curb terrorism and drug production. He denied Russia supported the Taliban, saying contacts sought to protect citizens and encourage UN-compliant negotiations. He criticized US rejection of the Moscow Process and said an Afghan settlement requires the government, Taliban, neighbours and influential regional countries, preferably through a smaller forum including Central Asian states.

TRNC education policies have evolved through historical and political developments, particularly after 1974 and the republic’s declaration in 1983. Education has served both academic purposes and the construction of Turkish Cypriot identity, with close cooperation with Turkey influencing curricula, teacher training, infrastructure, exchanges, and higher education.

Education Council decisions and presidential discourse have jointly shaped reforms. Priorities have included teacher training, textbook revision, curriculum development, school infrastructure, education quality, Turkish-medium instruction, internationalization, and balancing secular and religious education. Presidential priorities varied: Rauf Denktaş emphasized national identity and integration with Turkey; Mehmet Ali Talat focused on European harmonization and modernization; Derviş Eroğlu promoted cooperation with Turkey and technical education; Mustafa Akıncı highlighted multiculturalism, peace, and intercommunal dialogue; and Ersin Tatar stressed national identity and integration with Turkey.

History textbooks traditionally presented a Turkish-centered account of Cyprus, emphasizing Turkish Cypriot victimization and conflict with Greek Cypriots. Since the early 2000s, EU harmonization, bicommunal projects, and post-2004 reforms encouraged more pluralistic and reconciliatory narratives, though political changes and concerns about identity erosion impeded implementation.

The study concludes that education remains central to identity formation and is strongly affected by political leadership. It recommends politically independent, scientifically neutral, multi-perspective curricula; long-term education planning; teacher training and public-awareness initiatives supporting reconciliation; and cooperation with Turkey that also respects local needs and TRNC educational autonomy.

Alexa can simplify household cleaning by scheduling tasks through the Cleaning Buddy skill, ordering supplies from Amazon using voice purchasing and a confirmation code, and controlling compatible Neato or Roomba robot vacuums with voice commands. It can also book laundry pickup and delivery through Laundrapp, available in about 100 US cities, or provide stain-removal advice through the Good Housekeeping and Stains Be Gone skills.

New England Patriots receiver Malcolm Mitchell will receive America’s Promise Alliance’s Promise Hero Award for overcoming literacy struggles and promoting youth reading. At the University of Georgia, Mitchell recognized that he read poorly and began rebuilding his skills with children’s books, treating reading practice like football training. His improvement developed into a passion for literacy.

Mitchell founded Read with Malcolm to provide books and promote grade-level reading skills among children in underserved communities. He began by reading at elementary schools and sharing his message that reading can change lives. The initiative addresses limited access to age-appropriate books, particularly in low-income households.

A communications graduate and author of *The Magician’s Hat*, Mitchell hopes to continue playing football, writing inspirational books, visiting schools, and encouraging children to overcome adversity. He credits his mother, Pratina Woods, with teaching him to lead and pursue what is best despite social expectations. His advice to children facing similar struggles is to never give up, improve each day, and approach adversity as an opportunity.

The Supreme Court appears likely to uphold President Donald Trump’s removal of FTC Commissioner Rebecca Kelly Slaughter without fully overturning *Humphrey’s Executor*, the 1936 precedent permitting Congress to protect certain agency leaders from presidential removal.

*Humphrey’s Executor* characterized the 1935 FTC as a bipartisan body of experts performing primarily legislative and judicial, rather than executive, functions. Recent Supreme Court decisions, however, have emphasized examining an agency’s actual structure and powers. The court rejected similar protections for the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau because its single director exercised substantial regulatory, adjudicative, and enforcement authority.

The modern FTC retains a bipartisan, multi-member structure, but its rulemaking and law-enforcement powers have expanded, its adjudicative role has diminished, and its activity has become increasingly political. These changes may lead the court to conclude that the FTC now exercises considerable executive power, making its commissioners subject to presidential removal.

Rather than categorically repudiating *Humphrey’s Executor*, the court could revise its framework to distinguish agencies exercising primarily executive powers from institutions such as the Federal Reserve, whose structure, history, and functions differ. The wording of the question accepted for review also separates the legality of Slaughter’s removal from whether *Humphrey’s Executor* should be overruled.

MIT researchers engineered a more accurate prime-editing system by modifying Cas9 proteins and improving RNA-template stability. Prime editing corrects mutations using a single-strand DNA cut, but incorrect incorporation can cause potentially harmful errors. Cas9 mutations that shifted the cutting location destabilized old DNA strands, helping corrected strands integrate properly. Combining these mutations with an RNA-binding protein produced an editor called vPE, which reduced errors to one-sixtieth of the original rate. Depending on the editing mode, error rates improved from about one in seven to one in 101 edits, and from one in 122 to one in 543. Tests were conducted in mouse and human cells. Researchers are working to further improve editing efficiency and delivery to specific tissues and hope the system will support both gene therapies and laboratory research.

British police declared a major incident after a man and woman in their 40s were found unconscious in Amesbury and hospitalized in critical condition following exposure to an unknown substance. Counterterrorism officers joined local police investigating the case near Salisbury, where Sergei and Yulia Skripal were poisoned. Authorities said the substance and circumstances remain unknown, and no wider public risk is believed to exist.

Digital accessibility remains poorly integrated into computer science education and professional training, particularly in India, despite legal requirements, economic consequences, and widespread skills shortages. To address this gap, researchers conducted a one-day, beginner-friendly workshop for 73 Indian software engineers, educators, and UX designers.

The workshop covered accessibility fundamentals, inclusive design, accessible software development, testing and reporting, and accessibility education. It used active and experiential learning through assistive technologies, testing tools, case studies, disability simulations, thematic booths, and lightning talks. Pre- and post-workshop surveys assessed participants’ knowledge, confidence, attitudes, and perceptions.

Participants rated the workshop highly for engagement, effectiveness, and practical relevance. Accessibility tool demonstrations received the strongest activity ratings. All participants said they would recommend the workshop, and 52% reported a significant shift in their perception of accessibility and personal responsibility. Participants requested further learning on advanced inclusive design, AI applications, diverse user needs, organizational policy, and real-world practice.

Challenges included technical content that was difficult for some educators and designers, reliance on disability simulations, insufficient domain-specific examples, and limited support for continued learning. The authors recommend pre-workshop materials, role-specific content, practical case studies, peer learning, follow-up resources, and sustained engagement. They conclude that experiential accessibility training can build skills and inclusive mindsets across academia and industry, but continued interventions and evaluation of workplace application are needed.

In a parliamentary response to the 2017 State of the Nation Address, DA leader Mmusi Maimane accused President Jacob Zuma and the ANC of abandoning ordinary South Africans, citing the Esidimeni deaths, Marikana, alleged corruption, parliamentary violence and policies he said benefited connected elites. He argued that Zuma’s “radical socio-economic transformation” agenda, including land reform, black economic empowerment, nuclear procurement and mining proposals, concealed personal enrichment and threatened investment and jobs.

Maimane highlighted youth unemployment, educational exclusion and the millions of young people outside education, employment or training. He presented the DA’s proposed “Rescue Plan” for this “Lost Generation,” centred on educational reform, teacher development, expanded student funding, vocational training, apprenticeships and government internships.

The plan also proposed private-sector-led job creation, support for small businesses and entrepreneurs, labour reform, infrastructure investment, independent power production, partial privatisation of state-owned enterprises and broader-based economic empowerment. Additional proposals included transferring land ownership, redistributing government land, increasing and specialising police personnel, improving basic healthcare, reducing ministries and government privileges, and making procurement transparent. Maimane concluded that the DA would pursue inclusive growth, honest government and cooperation across racial groups.

The study investigates surface defects introduced by electropolishing highly polished bulk niobium used in superconducting radio-frequency cavities. White-light interferometry and atomic-force microscopy showed that electropolishing creates intergranular sloped steps up to about 70 nm high with local slope angles approaching 50°. Roughness generally increased with material removal, but step geometry depended more strongly on relative grain orientation and local microstructure than on electropolishing depth. Sequential measurements showed that earlier steps were smoothed while new steps formed at shifted grain-boundary locations. Electrolyte exposure without applied voltage caused only minor additional etching, indicating that electropolishing itself primarily creates the defects.

London-theory calculations found that these steps can enhance local magnetic fields, suppress the superheating field, promote vortex penetration, and thereby limit the peak fields achievable in niobium cavities. Magnetic-field enhancement becomes less severe as penetration depth increases through impurity alloying, whereas superheating-field suppression becomes more severe as coherence length decreases. Diffusion modeling also showed that sloped steps can reduce impurity concentration near the preferred vortex-entry location while increasing it near the step top, compromising the uniformity and effectiveness of shallow impurity treatments such as low-temperature baking and nitrogen infusion.

The results indicate that electropolished grain-boundary topography can degrade high-field Meissner-state stability more than previously expected. Achieving fields near or beyond niobium’s superheating field therefore requires minimizing both intergranular step height and slope angle. The authors also caution that power spectral density analysis can obscure performance-relevant defect geometry because it discards phase information and is relatively insensitive to slope angle. Future polishing methods and next-generation superconducting coatings should be evaluated using microscopic surface characterization rather than visual descriptions such as “mirror-smooth.”

A 13-year-old girl was hospitalized in serious but stable condition after being shot in the thigh while sitting in an open garage in Guildford. Police believe the Tuesday night shooting was not random and are waiting to interview her.

Following ICE arrests in the Austin-San Antonio area, Austin ISD instructed employees not to distribute unvetted resources or discuss political or controversial issues, citing heightened scrutiny from state lawmakers. The arrests increased anxiety among students concerned about their families. Board Vice President Paul Saldana criticized the memo, saying it contradicted district commitments and was issued without briefing the board. Superintendent Paul Cruz posted general resources, while Education Austin distributed detailed immigration guidance, lawyer contacts and hosted rights seminars. The union urged clearer district communication and planned a news conference, while board members were scheduled to discuss the memo.

Sen. Mark Warner accused Republicans of trying to discredit Robert Mueller’s investigation, the FBI and Justice Department through the partisan Nunes memo. He said Senate intelligence leaders were denied access before its release and questioned its methodology and handling of classified information. Warner also warned that President Trump’s failure to acknowledge election interference as a national threat leaves the country without a coordinated defense against future cyberwarfare.

Horse polo originated in Persia more than 20 centuries ago, spread across Asia, and developed into its modern form in India. British travelers brought it to England and later the United States, which now has about 250 clubs in 43 states.

The Milwaukee Polo Club, founded in the Milwaukee area in 1923, has operated at its Hartland location for more than 20 years. It promotes polo as an accessible, “blue collar” sport involving members of varied ages and occupations. Matches cost $5 for adults, with children admitted free, and spectators can meet players and horses.

Games typically consist of six seven-minute chukkers, include a halftime divot stomp, and last about two hours. Weather and field conditions determine whether matches proceed because horse and rider safety is central. On unsuitable days, members may offer demonstrations and answer visitors’ questions.

The club emphasizes that horses are teammates requiring careful feeding, grooming, limited workloads, rest, and balanced physical and mental activity.

Penny stocks, generally shares below $5, mostly trade over the counter because companies cannot or choose not to meet formal exchange requirements. They are highly speculative due to unproven or failing businesses, limited financial disclosure, low liquidity, wide bid-ask spreads, volatility, and trading costs. Thin, less-regulated markets also enable scams, including pump-and-dump promotions, fraudulent “guru” claims, and misuse of share issuance or reverse splits. Although rare successes attract investors seeking rapid wealth, most penny stocks ultimately fail or become worthless. The passage recommends avoiding them or investing only after understanding the possibility of losing the entire investment and conducting extensive due diligence.

D.A.N. Joint Venture III sought to deny Chapter 7 debtor Ambrozy Jerry Fasolak’s discharge under Bankruptcy Code §§ 727(a)(2)–(5), alleging fraudulent transfers or concealment, inadequate financial records, false oaths, and unexplained loss of assets.

Fasolak had owned A & F Corporation, a formerly successful Pennsylvania manufacturing business, for over 30 years. He retired in 2002, and the corporation later entered bankruptcy and liquidation. His 2002 financial statement reported a net worth of $2.742 million, but his 2004 Chapter 7 schedules disclosed limited assets. Before filing, funds and a vehicle were transferred to or held by his wife, and her accounts contained substantial proceeds associated partly with the sale of her Pennsylvania home. Fasolak’s bankruptcy filings also contained omissions and inaccuracies that were later amended.

The court found insufficient evidence that Fasolak transferred or concealed assets with actual intent to hinder, delay, or defraud creditors. The transfers could reasonably be associated with his retirement, withdrawal from financial affairs, and household finances. The plaintiff also failed to identify specific missing records or show that Fasolak’s financial condition could not be determined.

Although Fasolak made inaccurate statements and omitted prior bankruptcies, corporate stock, income, and certain transactions, the court found these errors resulted from mistake, misunderstanding, or forgetfulness rather than fraudulent intent. Finally, the 2002 financial statement did not establish an unexplained loss of identifiable assets: A & F Corporation had been liquidated, and the listed personal effects were not itemized.

The court entered judgment for Fasolak on all counts and ordered that he receive a Chapter 7 discharge.

The speaker emphasizes preparation, focus, execution, and living in the present rather than relying on momentum. Losing would be devastating because salary-cap constraints, injuries, and competitive parity make championship opportunities rare. Players should avoid distractions, enjoy the experience, and prepare individually and collectively.

He supports a player’s prior decision, saying it was carefully made and should be embraced, and praises his performance. Both finalists owe their success to depth, drafting, and player development; relying on only a few players leaves teams vulnerable to fatigue, injury, and defensive pressure. Effective matchups also depend on depth, starting on time, and playing with the lead.

Reviewing the previous game, he says poor puck handling and turnovers made the opposing forecheck appear stronger, while better positioning and execution resolved the problem. Goaltenders and teams have generally performed better at home, and both the goalie and team must contribute on the road.

The organization expects to win annually, but success requires players to compete and sacrifice for one another. He defines team building as winning together, blocking shots, enduring physical play, and paying the price rather than merely socializing. He praises the goalie for responding professionally to adversity and helping the team, while stressing that the series remains unfinished.

He says both teams have experienced uneven games, with outcomes driven more by team play than individuals. He encourages players and family to appreciate the opportunity because future chances are uncertain, the teams are closely matched, and winning is extremely difficult.

Harvard President Drew Faust announced she will step down June 30, 2018, after 11 years, coinciding with the end of the university’s fundraising campaign, which has raised $8 billion. Harvard’s first female president, Faust is credited with restoring campus trust, encouraging academic collaboration and expanding financial aid. Her tenure also faced controversies involving social clubs, diversity, the men’s soccer team and endowment losses. She plans a sabbatical before returning to scholarship, while Harvard will form a committee to choose her successor.

The ATR trailing stop is a technical indicator introduced by J. Welles Wilder that uses average true range to set dynamic stop-loss levels based on current market volatility. Stop values are commonly calculated by multiplying ATR by 3.5, then subtracting the result from the previous close for long positions or adding it for short positions. The indicator can help determine entries and exits, protect profits, limit losses, identify potential breakouts or reversals, and manage positions in instruments such as stocks and futures. ATR bands gauge volatility and support risk management and position sizing. A price crossing or repeatedly breaching trailing stop levels may signal changing market dynamics or a trend reversal. However, the indicator focuses primarily on current volatility and may not adequately account for past price performance. Traders should consider trading uncertainty and supplement it with other technical and fundamental analyses.

The passage studies fairness in many-to-one two-sided matching between participants and teams when both sides have ordinal preferences, possibly with ties. Participant-justified envy-freeness alone may treat teams unfairly, while team-EF1 can conflict with participant fairness. To address this, the authors introduce team-justified SD-EF1, which disregards participants who strictly prefer the team receiving them before evaluating whether remaining team envy can be eliminated by removing one participant.

Two preliminary approaches provide only subsets of the desired properties. A restricted round-robin method achieves team-justified SD-EF1 and participant envy-freeness but may be highly unbalanced. An auxiliary one-to-one matching method achieves team-justified SD-EF1, participant-justified envy-freeness, and balancedness but may fail swap stability.

The main polynomial-time algorithm creates balanced team slots and gradually expands each participant’s eligible teams. In every iteration, it computes an eligible matching that lexicographically maximizes team-slot values in round-robin order and then participants’ preferences. The resulting allocation simultaneously satisfies team-justified SD-EF1, participant-justified envy-freeness, balancedness, and Pareto optimality, which implies swap stability. When participants are indifferent among teams, the algorithm reduces to round-robin; with strict preferences on both sides, it reduces to participant-proposing Gale–Shapley.

With augmented tie-breaking, the algorithm is group-strategyproof for participants: no coalition can misreport preferences so that every member strictly benefits. It is not strategyproof for teams. The framework extends to team quotas and preferences for remaining unassigned by adding dummy participants and a dummy team. The extended polynomial-time algorithm satisfies stability, Pareto optimality, extended team-justified SD-EF1, and participant group-strategyproofness.

Texas A&M receiver Christian Kirk is the school’s best chance to extend its streak of having a first-round NFL draft pick every year since 2011. Kirk, who skipped his senior season, is considered a fringe first-round prospect and plans to watch the draft from home in Arizona.

Safety Armani Watts is projected as a mid-round pick, while receiver Damion Ratley could be selected late. Defensive tackle Zaycoven Henderson’s pending criminal case has hurt his draft prospects after he was arrested in December.

A&M’s limited pool of likely selections follows disappointing 2013 and 2014 recruiting classes and an especially young 2017 roster. The Aggies’ first-round streak began with Von Miller in 2011 and includes Ryan Tannehill, Luke Joeckel, Jake Matthews, Mike Evans, Johnny Manziel, Cedric Ogbuehi, Germain Ifedi and 2017 No. 1 overall pick Myles Garrett.

The address reviews a century of American self-government, praising the Constitution for strengthening the Union, expanding freedom, surviving civil war, and establishing national supremacy while preserving local self-government. It identifies emancipation and equal citizenship as transformative achievements and pledges constitutional protection for Black citizens. It condemns suppression of voting rights, warns that ignorance, corruption, and illiteracy threaten republican government, and urges universal education through national, state, and voluntary efforts.

The speaker calls for reconciliation between sections and races, abandonment of settled controversies, and pursuit of peaceful national development. He attributes current prosperity partly to sound public credit and resumed specie payments, supports gold and silver as the monetary foundation, favors redeemable paper notes, and advocates refinancing the national debt without disrupting commerce.

The address urges greater governmental support for agriculture, manufacturing, transportation, waterways, and American commercial interests in any interoceanic canal. It defends religious liberty but calls for congressional action against polygamy and ecclesiastical interference with government. It also proposes legal regulation of civil-service tenure and removals.

The administration pledges to act within constitutional limits, uphold national authority, enforce federal law, practice fiscal economy, and require honest public service. The speaker asks for popular and congressional support and invokes divine blessing.

Digital leaders cultivate learning, responsible risk-taking, transparent data access, measurable goals, and alignment between strategy and employees’ objectives. They combine broad data availability with governance controls, use metrics and reviews to support adaptation, and give teams flexibility in how they achieve clearly defined outcomes. Standardized APIs are reported at 88% of digital leaders versus 27% of laggards.

Digital laggards prioritize short-term needs, narrow training, process adherence, and tightly controlled data. Risk aversion, distrust, departmental silos, burdensome access procedures, and reliance on senior individuals’ judgment can inhibit experimentation and collaboration. Their goals are often aspirational but poorly grounded in data or connected to strategy, leading employees to emphasize effort and qualitative processes rather than measurable results.

Cultural change remains difficult even for digital leaders. Regulatory requirements, deadlines, excessive analysis, and inconsistent data literacy can constrain experimentation and decision-making. A pharmaceutical company addressed such constraints through controlled experimentation, producing an automated compliance tool that reduced processing time and spread to other groups. A retailer’s upgraded systems enabled sales data to be reported three times daily, supporting faster decisions across business units.

A strong data culture aligns organizations vertically through shared objectives and horizontally through common data models and transparent access. Successful transformation requires leadership support, consistent values and behavior, and sustained changes in beliefs about employee capabilities. Organizations commonly fit four patterns: data novices lack enabling culture and systems; insight-ready firms support experimentation but lack analytical capabilities; tech-enabled firms have technology but discourage innovation; and data-reliant firms overuse data at the expense of critical thinking.

Michigan State Superintendent Michael Rice is retiring after serving since 2019. Reflecting on his tenure, he urged lawmakers to ensure students receive 180 instructional days by ending policies that count up to seven teacher professional development days as instructional time. Schools may also use up to 15 virtual-learning days, while emergencies can further reduce in-person instruction.

Rice led through the pandemic, which brought lower test performance, increased absenteeism and mental health concerns, and slow academic recovery. He cited progress in equitable funding, preschool enrollment, a record 82% graduation rate, and efforts to address teacher shortages, though Michigan has not fully achieved any goals in its strategic education plan.

Rice said Michigan should follow Mississippi’s focused literacy policies, including research-based materials, teacher training, literacy coaches and smaller early-grade classes in high-poverty schools. He supports mandatory science-of-reading training for Michigan K-5 teachers.

State investments in scholarships, student-teacher stipends and “grow your own” programs have helped increase the number preparing to teach from 9,500 in 2017 to 18,000 annually, but Rice said shortages will not be over until challenged communities have fully credentialed teachers in every classroom.

Alphabet will pay $24.5 million to settle Donald Trump’s lawsuit over YouTube’s suspension of his account after the January 6, 2021, Capitol riot. Trump will receive $22 million, directed to the Trust for the National Mall and construction of a White House ballroom, while co-plaintiffs receive $2.5 million. YouTube reinstated Trump in March 2023. Alphabet admitted no liability. Trump previously settled similar cases with Meta for $25 million and X for $10 million, bringing total settlements related to his social media bans above $57 million.
Scientists report cheetahs have vanished from 91% of their historic range and urge an IUCN “Endangered” listing based on low southern African populations.

The Ghana Football Association’s Executive Committee removed Vice President George Afriyie after months of reported conflict with president Kwesi Nyantakyi over financial matters and Afriyie’s declared intention to contest the 2019 GFA election. Afriyie had already been replaced as head of the Black Stars Management Committee, while divisions within the Executive Committee became public.

Afriyie says his experience over three Executive Committee terms qualifies him to succeed Nyantakyi and build on the administration’s achievements. However, previous sidelined vice presidents lost influence under Nyantakyi.

Although Nyantakyi has repeatedly said he will not seek re-election, Afriyie’s dismissal has increased speculation that he may pursue a fourth term. Nyantakyi has led the GFA since 2005, overseeing three consecutive World Cup qualifications but also facing public criticism over the decline of the Ghana Premier League and the earlier dormancy of the FA Cup.

HPBOSE announced the Class 12 Result 2018 on April 24 at hpbose.org. Students can check results online using their roll number or via SMS by sending HP12ROLLNUMBER to 56263. Class 12 examinations were held from March 6 to 29.
Seven candidates joined the 6th Congressional District race, bringing the field to 15. The April 18 special election will replace Tom Price, with a possible runoff June 20.

Eight years after graduating, the author reflects fondly on college but regrets missing opportunities and not realizing how much time was available for adventure. While acknowledging that college experiences vary, the author recalls exceptional people, fascinating classes, and enjoying campus, then introduces the things they would do differently.

Peter Lynch managed Fidelity’s Magellan Fund from 1977 to 1990, earning about 29% annually and growing its assets from $20 million to $14 billion. His approach emphasized “invest in what you understand,” identifying undervalued companies with clear business models, strong products, sound finances, and long-term growth potential rather than predicting markets or reacting to short-term price changes.

Lynch categorized companies as slow-growing, moderately growing, fast-growing, cyclical, crisis-recovery, or possessing undervalued assets. He particularly sought small, fast-growing companies overlooked by major investors, while maintaining diversified exposure to other categories. He regularly reviewed holdings, stayed fully invested, and adjusted allocations according to earnings, prospects, valuation, and other fundamentals. He sold when prices rose without corresponding fundamental improvement or when business prospects weakened, while buying more when strong companies declined despite stable or improving fundamentals.

Lynch’s early work as a golf caddy introduced him to corporate leaders and investing. He later attended Wharton, interned at Fidelity, and joined the firm as an analyst before leading Magellan. His investment philosophy and slogans, including “ten baggers,” were presented in his 1989 book, *One Up On Wall Street*.

June 8 reports focused on the dispute between Enron-promoted Dabhol Power Company and Maharashtra State Electricity Board. Indian and foreign lenders appointed Stone & Webster to assess the costs of suspending or mothballing the largely completed 1,444-MW second phase, potentially for one year, while seeking resolution of the power purchase agreement and resumption of phase-I purchases. Lenders also formed a committee to negotiate with MSEB.

Enron reportedly offered to reduce its projected rate of return from 16% to 11%, while the Godbole panel said return on equity should not exceed 16%. Reports questioned whether other states could afford Dabhol power even after tariff reductions.

DPC petitioned the Bombay High Court to overturn a Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission order barring arbitration and reactivation of its escrow account, arguing that disputes under the power purchase agreement belonged in international arbitration. DPC also objected to public regulatory hearings. The Godbole panel accused DPC of taking inconsistent negotiating positions, while activist Medha Patkar demanded a judicial inquiry and Enron’s removal from India.
Liverpool open the 2017/18 Premier League season at Watford on August 12 and finish at home to Brighton on May 13. All dates may change.

The Geminid meteor shower peaks Wednesday night, with optimal viewing from midnight to 4 a.m. Thursday. Up to 50 bright, long-lasting meteors may be visible, especially in rural areas, as Earth passes through debris from asteroid Phaethon.

A British study found that CT lung cancer screening may encourage high-risk smokers who are receptive to quitting. Among eligible participants, 10 percent of those screened had quit after two weeks and 15 percent after two years, compared with 5 percent of those not invited for screening. A negative screening result did not reduce motivation to quit. Researchers noted that participants were self-selected and may already have considered quitting, while concern about lung cancer may have supported cessation. They concluded that CT screening provides a “teachable moment” and could strengthen smoking-cessation initiatives when combined with other interventions.

The USGS awarded Caltech and six partners $4.9 million and purchased $1 million in sensors for ShakeAlert, a West Coast earthquake-warning system. Completing it requires an estimated $38.3 million, plus $16.1 million annually.

The speaker says the series has featured momentum swings, hard play and strong performances by both teams, but the deciding game is now an exciting opportunity. He praises his team’s resilience through injuries, emphasizes staying poised and focused on execution, and says prior championships provide confidence. Detroit has played more comfortably and assertively at home, supported by passionate Michigan fans facing difficult economic conditions. He values the Red Wings’ history and continued involvement of former players, whose techniques influence current coaching. He calls the Stanley Cup hockey’s greatest prize, urges everyone to enjoy the moment, and highlights individual battles and strong goaltending as good for the sport. Players such as Hossa are told simply to fulfill their roles because winning matters more than who scores.

Northwestern’s NCAA tournament hopes rose after a 66-59 upset of Wisconsin, but coaches and players emphasized staying focused amid growing attention. The Wildcats next host Maryland without Scottie Lindsey, who will miss his fourth straight game with mono.

Valmet’s Board approved a long-term share-based incentive plan for approximately 120 key employees covering 2018–2020. Annual performance criteria will be set by the Board; 2018 rewards depend on Comparable EBITA margin and stable-business orders growth. Rewards will be paid in shares and cash, with transfer restrictions and employment conditions. Executive Team members are recommended to hold shares equal to their annual base salary. Total rewards are capped at approximately 586,000 shares. Valmet reported 2016 net sales of approximately EUR 2.9 billion and employs 12,000 people globally.

The Basque Country has recorded rising imported dengue, chikungunya, and Zika cases alongside expanding Aedes albopictus and established Aedes japonicus populations, although no local Aedes-borne disease transmission has occurred. This study modeled invasive Aedes abundance using ovitrap egg counts and temperature, humidity, and precipitation data.

Egg-count data from 2013–2023 covered 63 municipalities, while meteorological data from 2016–2023 were aggregated into biweekly intervals. Provincial analyses used the 20 highest egg counts to reduce inconsistencies in ovitrap coverage and prevalent zeros. Araba was excluded from modeling because its sparse positive counts were insufficient for reliable training, leaving Gipuzkoa and Bizkaia.

Egg counts were strongly associated with temperature, particularly temperatures recorded two weeks earlier. Humidity showed weaker positive relationships, while precipitation approximately ten weeks earlier showed weak negative relationships. Incorporating lagged environmental variables and egg counts generally improved model performance.

Generalized linear, SARIMAX, Random Forest, and Conditional Inference Tree models were compared. Random Forest fit training data best, explaining 98% of variance in both provinces, but showed weaker test performance and possible overfitting. The Gaussian generalized linear model performed best on 2023 test data, explaining 85% of variance in Gipuzkoa and 81% in Bizkaia, followed closely by SARIMAX. Conditional Inference Trees performed worst. Bizkaia’s unusually high 2023 egg counts reduced test accuracy.

Models trained through 2023 forecast lower mosquito abundance in 2024 than in 2023. The study concludes that continuous, localized egg surveillance, environmental monitoring, and temporal predictors are important for forecasting mosquito abundance and informing vector-control strategies. Limitations include provincial climatic variability, biweekly sampling, sparse data in some areas, and sensitivity to training-test partitioning.

American Airlines offers roundtrip domestic and international Net SAAver weekend fares for travel November 29–December 4, 2001, with purchase required by November 23. The email lists routes and prices, AAdvantage mileage awards, vacation, hotel and car-rental promotions, booking instructions, and fare restrictions. Tickets are nonrefundable, availability is limited, and taxes, fees, and change charges may apply.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth summoned hundreds of senior military leaders worldwide to advocate reshaping a force he described as soft and “woke.” New York Times Pentagon reporter Greg Jaffe discusses the speech.
A100 increases per-SM L1/shared memory capacity, offers 40 GB HBM2 at 1555 GB/s, expands L2 cache to 40 MB, and adds cache controls and Compute Data Compression.

A survey of 202 Illinois daycare staff found sun safety ranked below nutrition, exercise and dental hygiene as a health-teaching priority. About half of programs provided sunscreen, but 77 percent did not let children apply it themselves, possibly reflecting confusion over school medication rules or restrictions on touching children. Many used spray sunscreen, though some applied it incorrectly by spraying children’s faces. Most programs reported no sunburns and limited outdoor exposure during excessive heat. Researchers noted the study was limited to Illinois but said early-childhood programs need greater awareness of long-term sun risks. Experts recommended staff education and parental support through applying or supplying sunscreen, protective clothing and modeling sun-safe behavior.

Lawyer Angela B. Ryan describes how pregnancy changed her understanding of pregnant colleagues and made her body a subject of courtroom commentary and unwanted touching. She argues that stroking a pregnant person’s belly without consent is assault and workplace harassment, despite being socially minimized as harmless affection. Citing legal protections against pregnancy-based harassment, she urges the legal profession to prohibit such contact explicitly through policies, training and workplace culture: consent does not end with conception.

A Denver federal jury found former radio host David Mueller liable for assault and battery for groping Taylor Swift during a 2013 preconcert photo session. Swift, who countersued after Mueller claimed her accusation caused his firing from KYGO, received the symbolic $1 she requested. The jury also determined that Swift’s mother and manager had not improperly interfered with Mueller’s employment. A judge had previously dismissed Swift from Mueller’s suit for insufficient evidence that she fabricated the encounter. Mueller denied inappropriate contact and sought about $260,000 in lost wages, while Swift testified she was stunned and avoided creating a scene. After the verdict, Swift said she would donate to organizations helping sexual assault victims defend themselves.

The team has improved its puck management and offensive-zone play despite limited scoring. After two straight wins, players are confident but focused solely on Thursday’s road game. They expect a strong home performance from their opponent but believe travel and venue will not be decisive, though home teams gain matchup and faceoff advantages. The team feels its play and timing have improved after a ten-day layoff. Its goaltender has provided a major lift and strengthened team confidence. Both teams are comfortable with their defensive matchups and have demonstrated an ability to come back after conceding first. The speaker also expressed confidence in overtime while acknowledging the team has been fortunate.

On Christmas Eve 2012, Commander Chris Hadfield celebrated aboard the International Space Station by hiding family cards for five crewmates. Orbiting Earth every 92 minutes complicated traditional timing, while microgravity required adaptations such as non-crumbly fruitcake, packaged turkey and potatoes, a Velcro-mounted artificial tree, and stockings filled with chocolate and nuts. Hadfield’s American and Russian crew selected holidays from their cultures and planned familiar celebrations. He considered recognizing holidays, birthdays and family deaths essential to psychological health and mission success, emphasizing that traditions support reflection, relationships and well-being even in space.
Polling began for 69 Uttarakhand assembly seats, with 74 lakh voters, 628 candidates, 10,685 booths, 30,000 security personnel and 60,000 officials. Karnaprayag votes March 9.

Samsung announced three cheaper, water- and dust-resistant Galaxy A smartphones: the 4.7-inch A3, 5.2-inch A5 and 5.7-inch A7. Launching first in Russia, they feature 16-megapixel cameras, fingerprint sensors and up to 32GB storage. Pricing remains unannounced. The release follows the costly Galaxy Note 7 recall.
China launched a visa program attracting young science and technology professionals as the US imposed a $100,000 H-1B fee, prompting xenophobic backlash.

The passage references memory maps, interconnect details, package pin assignments, and terminal functions for the TMS320DM814x. The TILER provides an additional 4-GB address range using a 33rd address bit for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views; the full range is accessible only to HDVPSS and ISS, while other masters can access one view through the base-map 512-MB region. Terminal tables document signal names, ball numbers, pin types, pulls, supply sources, multiplexing, control registers, and deselected input states. Boot configuration pins are sampled at reset for GPMC settings and watchdog reset-output behavior, then operate as GPMC multiplexed address/data pins.

The plaintiff was injured while bowling when a splinter projecting from the defendant’s worn, warped floor entered his finger as he delivered a ball with his hand near, but not touching, the floor. The reused flooring was old, dirty, uneven, and visibly splintered; worn bowling approaches customarily required planing. The injury required three operations to remove splinter fragments.

A jury awarded the plaintiff $750. The court held that the evidence permitted findings that the unsafe condition was longstanding and that the defendant failed to exercise reasonable care in maintaining the premises. Because delivering the ball close to the floor was not shown to be improper and the plaintiff had not noticed the splinter beforehand, contributory negligence was a factual question for the jury. The trial judge properly denied a directed verdict and refused instructions based on unsupported assumptions that the plaintiff struck the floor or used the approach improperly. Judgment was ordered for the plaintiff.

After the July 4 Kerr County floods killed 25 Camp Mystic campers, two counselors and the camp director, bereaved parents organized with lobbyists to press Texas lawmakers for stronger camp protections. Gov. Greg Abbott signed bills requiring overnight cabins outside floodplains, weather radios and alert systems, emergency plans, evacuation training and routes to higher ground. Parents including Matthew and Wendie Childress, whose 18-year-old daughter Chloe died while serving as a counselor, and Blake Bonner, whose 9-year-old daughter Lila died, viewed the reforms as a way to honor their children and prevent future deaths, while acknowledging that legislative success could not ease their profound grief.

The 1902 rules state that only the Secretary of State may issue U.S. passports. Eligible applicants abroad should apply through U.S. diplomatic or consular officials, while residents of insular possessions should apply to their chief executive. Passports may be granted only to persons owing allegiance to the United States; a declaration of intent to become a citizen is insufficient.

Domestic applicants must submit a sworn written application stating birth, occupation, residence, intended temporary travel and return, take an oath of allegiance, provide a physical description, and obtain certification from a credible witness. Native citizens generally need only these requirements. Persons born abroad to native-citizen fathers must establish the father’s U.S. birth, residence, and citizenship. Naturalized citizens must provide naturalization records and details of emigration, residence, and naturalization. Additional documentation applies to women claiming citizenship through marriage, children through a naturalized parent, and insular residents, who must deny allegiance to other governments and provide two supporting witnesses.

An international cross-sectional analysis of 747 participants with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) from 49 countries examined self-reported diagnostic testing in the COVID-PCD cohort. Overall, 92% reported diagnostic testing; 75% reported biopsy, 58% genetic testing, and 49% of participants older than five reported nasal nitric oxide measurement. Only 36% of tested participants older than five reported receiving all three tests, with substantial variation between countries. Recall was poorest for nasal nitric oxide testing and for how biopsy samples were analysed.

Participants diagnosed after 2010 reported more testing than those diagnosed before 2000, while those with situs abnormalities reported fewer tests. Age at diagnosis was not associated with test use. The findings suggest that many people with PCD have incomplete diagnostic characterization, particularly those diagnosed longer ago or with situs abnormalities. The authors recommend reviewing prior results and considering supplementary testing to support accurate characterization, personalized treatment, and eligibility for clinical trials.

The passage describes SD Memory Card Physical Layer Specification 6.00 operations and commands. ACMD23 pre-erases a specified number of blocks before CMD25 to accelerate multiple-block writes; ACMD22 reports successfully written blocks after an error. Erase, DISCARD, and Full User Area Logical Erase use CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38 in sequence. DISCARD marks data as “don’t care,” while FULE logically erases the entire user area. Both are limited to SDHC/SDXC cards, unavailable through SPI, require support checks, and signal activity by holding DAT0 low.

Write protection includes a host-managed mechanical switch, optional internal protection, and password locking. CMD42 manages passwords, locking, unlocking, clearing passwords, and force erase. Passwords persist across power cycles, and cards with passwords set automatically lock after power-up. Card Ownership Protection adds a Force Erase Password, COP Unlock, protected force erase, and restrictions on clearing passwords or performing ordinary force erase. Incorrect commands or passwords set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED. Force erase removes user data and the card password but not the secure area; FEP-protected erase requires the correct FEP and leaves FEP stored.

CMD55 identifies the next command as application-specific. CMD6 queries or changes functions in six groups, including access speed, command system, driver strength, and power limit. Mode 0 checks support, readiness, and power consumption; Mode 1 switches functions. Function 0 is the default, and 0xF preserves the current selection. High-Speed mode raises interface speed to 25 MB/s using a 50 MHz clock and is optional.

CMD8 checks host voltage compatibility during initialization. SDSC cards use byte addressing and CMD16-defined block lengths, whereas SDHC/SDXC cards use 512-byte block addressing and fixed 512-byte memory-access blocks.

Hosts may vary or stop the clock subject to transaction-completion requirements. Commands and most responses use CRC7; data uses CRC16. CRC failures and illegal commands set status errors without executing the command. Recommended minimum read timeout is 100 ms for SDHC/SDXC; write busy periods are generally 250 ms, with specified SDXC cases allowing 500 ms. DISCARD has a 250 ms timeout and FULE a one-second timeout.

SD commands use fixed 48-bit formats and are organized into command classes. Responses vary by type, with R1 carrying card status and R1b optionally adding a busy signal. UHS-II modifies or replaces some command behavior and uses packet data length for normal transfer termination.

AI and large language models could expand computational social science by providing scalable synthetic data, automating tasks such as sentiment analysis and response coding, and supporting hypothesis and theory development. Key limitations include dataset and computing costs, biased or stereotyped simulations, uncertain validity, misinformation risks, and the need for human interpretation, multidisciplinary expertise, and oversight.

Generative AI also creates regulatory challenges involving misinformation, deepfakes, discrimination, rapid technological change, jailbreaks, and differing national rules. The passage advocates forward-looking, human-centered governance that balances innovation with safety and fundamental rights. It calls for cooperation among industry, academia, policymakers, developers, and users; combined top-down and bottom-up regulation; transparent reporting and investigation of emerging risks; timely updates to rules; and monitoring of community-specific concerns.

A federal judge rejected a challenge to the Biden administration’s gainful-employment rule and sided with the Education Department. The rule requires for-profit and nondegree programs to show graduates can afford loan payments and earn more than high school graduates; programs failing for two consecutive years could lose federal aid. Trump officials defended the regulations in court. Representatives of for-profit colleges anticipate revisions during upcoming rule-making, while Student Defense praised the ruling as protecting students from low-value career programs.
Halliburton reported first-quarter net income of $46 million, or 5 cents per share. Adjusted earnings met expectations at 41 cents per share, while $5.74 billion in revenue missed forecasts.

A New Delhi court deferred until July 6 consideration of the Enforcement Directorate’s money-laundering chargesheet against Karti Chidambaram and two companies in the Aircel-Maxis deal. The ED alleges Maxis’s actual Rs 3,565.91 crore investment was presented as Rs 180 crore to obtain Finance Ministry approval, bypassing the Cabinet committee. It also alleges payments to companies linked to Karti. He has interim protection from arrest until July 10.

Prava Chatterjee sought to invalidate an $87,000 settlement and release concerning her son’s death in the 1975 CORINTHOS-QUEENY maritime disaster. She alleged that her son-in-law lacked authority to represent her, forged her signature on a power of attorney, and withheld the proceeds. The Third Circuit held that Indian law governs the power of attorney, while federal maritime law governs the release. Under maritime law, shipowners bear the burden of proving that a seaman’s survivor freely and knowingly executed a release without deception or coercion. Although the district court properly excluded prior deposition testimony because the shipowners lacked an adequate opportunity for cross-examination, its refusal to authorize a new commission in India prevented Chatterjee from presenting evidence of fraud and forgery and denied her a fair trial. The court vacated the order upholding the settlement and remanded with instructions to commission testimony in India.

NAFTA strengthened Canadian growth and manufacturing, making its modernization a federal priority. However, Canada remains overly dependent on North American trade, while exports to most other free-trade partners have not increased. New agreements alone will not ensure prosperity.

Canada needs a five-part trade strategy: improve domestic competitiveness through tax and regulatory reform; address non-tariff barriers such as subsidies, procurement exemptions and currency manipulation; prioritize partners with natural business, legal and historical ties; build on existing integrated supply chains and proven industrial strengths; and help small and medium-sized firms expand globally by consolidating export-support programs. Government and industry should begin structural reforms immediately to reduce Canada’s vulnerability and enable exporters to compete beyond North America.

Pokémon GO’s fire-and-ice Solstice Event increases relevant spawns and offers triple XP for catches, accurate throws, curveballs, and first throws. Discounted Lucky Eggs can raise catch-related rewards to six times normal XP, encouraging active, skillful play rather than evolution-based leveling, which receives no bonus. The event may help casual and midcore players prepare for upcoming gym changes, though high-level players benefit less. Its seasonal theme also reflects the game’s worldwide reach.

Theresa May faced warnings from Conservative Brexiteers ahead of a cabinet meeting at Chequers that compromising on Brexit could damage the party and provoke rebellion. Andrea Jenkyns said remaining “half in and half out” of the EU would be catastrophic, while Jacob Rees-Mogg urged May to uphold promises to leave the single market and customs union. Brexiteers fear a “soft Brexit” would restrict trade policy and retain EU alignment, while Remain supporters argue compromise is needed to prevent disruption. Michael Gove expressed confidence that May would maintain her red lines, secure cabinet unity and avoid ministerial resignations.

The speaker says a player probably will not play but declines to confirm his status for tomorrow. Fatigue is not considered a factor. The team accepts an inconclusive replay decision, believes venue has had little impact, and remains confident despite possible home distractions affecting top players in the previous game.

U.S. international student arrivals in August were 19 percent lower than in August 2024, broadly matching predictions that visa interview delays and new screening policies would reduce enrollment. Arrival figures exclude students who stayed in the country over summer or entered later, while separate SEVIS data showing a 0.8 percent enrollment increase was criticized as incomplete and inconsistent with institutional reports.

Declines were greatest among students from Africa, Asia and the Middle East. Arrivals from India, the leading source country, fell 44.5 percent, representing over 33,000 fewer students. Experts warned the eventual enrollment decline could exceed 20 percent, harming universities and local economies and potentially worsening in 2026. More reliable institution-reported figures are expected in November.

Guyana will host the Caribbean Water and Wastewater Association’s annual conference from October 16–20, 2017. Over 250 delegates and 40 exhibitors will address water, wastewater and waste management, review a regional action plan, and develop the Caribbean’s position for the 2018 World Water Forum.

Bogleheads portfolios follow Jack Bogle’s low-cost, passive approach using broad index funds. The 3 Fund Portfolio includes U.S. stocks, international stocks, and U.S. bonds; the 4 Fund Portfolio adds international bonds for greater global diversification. Suggested allocations are 50% U.S. stocks, 30% international stocks, and either 20% U.S. bonds or 10% each in U.S. and international bonds. Fund selection should consider goals, risk tolerance, expenses, and performance, with periodic rebalancing and a long-term perspective. Market volatility affects stocks, while interest-rate changes affect bonds. Backtests reported annual returns of 7.6% with a 28% maximum drawdown for the 3 Fund Portfolio and 7.8% with a 31% maximum drawdown for the 4 Fund Portfolio.

LG introduced the V35 ThinQ, featuring a Snapdragon 845 processor, 6GB RAM, a 6-inch OLED display without a notch, dual 16MP rear cameras, and AI-assisted photography. It includes IP68 resistance, MIL-STD 810G testing, a headphone jack, 3,300 mAh battery, biometric security, and 64GB or 128GB storage expandable by microSD. Pricing and availability remain unannounced.

Reporting to Congress after the Yalta Conference, Roosevelt urged American support for agreements intended to accelerate Germany’s defeat and establish lasting international peace. Allied leaders coordinated military operations, arranged direct daily communication among western, eastern, and Italian fronts, and reaffirmed the demand for Germany’s unconditional surrender.

Germany would be temporarily occupied in four zones by the United States, Britain, the Soviet Union, and France. Allied policy called for eliminating Nazism and militarism, disarming Germany, punishing war criminals, and requiring reparations in kind, while avoiding the starvation or enslavement of the German people.

The conference resolved remaining differences over the proposed international security organization, including Security Council voting procedures. A United Nations conference was scheduled for April 25, 1945, in San Francisco to draft a charter requiring Senate approval. Roosevelt emphasized bipartisan participation and argued that peace depended on continuing international cooperation and shared responsibility.

The three major powers agreed jointly to assist liberated European countries and former Axis satellites in establishing representative interim governments, democratic processes, and free elections. They also recognized the need for economic reconstruction. On Poland, they agreed to broaden the provisional government, hold elections by universal suffrage and secret ballot, and establish boundaries through compromise, including territorial gains in the north and west to compensate for losses east of the Curzon Line. France was invited to participate in Germany’s occupation, the San Francisco conference, the Security Council, and responsibilities for liberated Europe.

Roosevelt warned that victory remained distant, particularly against Japan, whose unconditional surrender and demilitarization were also essential. He described Yalta as a turning point requiring the United States to choose between sustained world collaboration and the risk of another global conflict.

The broadcast launches a nationwide mobilization to protect unemployed Americans and their families from hunger, cold, and deprivation during the coming winter. A national organization led by Walter Gifford will coordinate governments, businesses, labor groups, charities, churches, and local relief agencies in raising and administering funds. Assistance will include employment, direct family relief, health services, and character-building programs.

Federal, state, and local governments are expanding public works and relief activities, while industry is spreading available work among employees. Despite these measures, voluntary community support remains necessary. Drawing on successful efforts from the previous winter, the speaker argues that local responsibility, mutual aid, and individual generosity are essential to democracy and national unity. He calls on Americans to ensure that no deserving person suffers and to make November 26 an exceptional Thanksgiving by removing fear of winter from distressed families. The address closes by invoking Yorktown as a symbol of national perseverance through sacrifice and hardship.

The S&P 500 nearly quadrupled from post-crisis lows, but recent conditions may signal a more difficult market environment. By early 2018, the index had gone over 60 trading days without a new high, while the Federal Reserve continued raising rates and shrinking its balance sheet rather than reassuring investors with stimulus. Other central banks remained less committed to tightening, creating potential policy-related turbulence despite strong projected corporate earnings.

Volatility rose sharply after historically low levels in 2017. The VIX remained above 15 following its February spike and repeatedly approached the high 20s. The S&P 500 moved more than 1% on 31 of the first 79 trading days of 2018, compared with eight days during all of 2017, placing 2018 among the most volatile postwar years by this measure.

The author argues that sustained volatility could foreshadow a bull-market peak, even if stocks reach new highs, and expects a future bear market to be slow and prolonged because policymakers may lack sufficient tools to counter it. The passage concludes that policy-supported markets impede price discovery and advises investors to examine overlooked risks rather than rely on optimistic earnings and growth forecasts.

The study compares open-access (OA) and controlled-access (CA) contributions to the Elsevier Biology Knowledge Graph, focusing on rare-disease and drug-target relations relevant to drug repurposing. Using Elsevier’s NLP-extracted relations, it found that OA and CA contribute roughly equally at the relation level, although more statements and articles came from CA sources. OA contributions have grown substantially since 2006, and more than half of relations needed for rare-disease drug repurposing are now available in OA. Citation rates and time to first citation were essentially identical for OA and CA facts.

More than half of knowledge-graph relations are supported by only one reference, with such relations accumulating rapidly in both OA and CA literature. About 85% of uncited relations were extracted from peer-reviewed publications, and most appeared to originate from original research that received no subsequent follow-up. CA-only knowledge continues to grow, but more slowly than OA knowledge.
