The study concludes that accessibility does not significantly affect citation patterns and recommends additional confidence measures for knowledge-graph relations beyond reference counts, including epistemic analysis, citation metrics, alignment with existing graph knowledge, and distinction between self-citation and independent confirmation.
Iraq began bombing Islamic State-held Tal Afar, with a ground assault planned afterward. The town became the next target following Iraqi forces’ recapture of Mosul.

A chronological index of diplomatic records and telegrams dated January 8–September 3, 1942, primarily exchanged between Washington and Helsinki, with additional communications from Kuibyshev, Stockholm, London, and Ankara. Entries list archival reference numbers, dispatch locations and times, and receipt times, many filed under “European War 1939.”

Lawmakers are using President Trump’s first State of the Union address to highlight political and social issues. Many Democratic women will wear black in solidarity with the #MeToo movement, while some invited sexual assault survivors. Democrats also invited young immigrants protected under DACA, while Republican Kevin Cramer invited an executive whose company developed a prototype border wall. At least eight Democratic representatives plan to boycott the speech, calling Trump divisive. Bill Nye will attend as the guest of Republican Rep. Jim Bridenstine, Trump’s NASA administrator nominee, despite Nye’s criticism of Trump’s environmental policies. Massachusetts Rep. Joe Kennedy, grandson of Robert F. Kennedy, will deliver the Democratic response and promote the party’s policies to the middle class.

The lecture reviews control charts as repeated hypothesis tests. Control limits are set from the false-alarm probability, alpha, while beta represents missed alarms after a process shift. Average run length is \(1/\alpha\) for false alarms and \(1/(1-\beta)\) for detecting a true shift. Increasing sample size narrows sampling distributions and reduces beta while control limits adjust to preserve alpha.

Control limits must not be confused with specification limits: control limits identify statistically unusual behavior, whereas specifications define acceptable product performance. Any control-chart alarm requires investigation because the chart alone cannot distinguish false from true alarms. Recommended steps include verifying measurement equipment, reviewing historical trends, and examining operators, equipment, feedstock, and other process changes.

Process capability compares an in-control process with design requirements. \(C_P\) measures specification width relative to six process standard deviations and does not account for centering. \(C_{PK}\) uses the shortest distance from the process mean to a specification limit and therefore penalizes mistargeting. Higher values imply fewer nonconforming parts and greater robustness to mean shifts. A quadratic quality-loss function similarly penalizes both variance and deviation from target.

The lecture also discusses complications from multiple process steps, correlated variables, and many simultaneous control charts, which require aggregate false-alarm considerations. Standard x-bar charts filter short-term variation but depend on sample size and independence assumptions. Future material will cover moving-average, exponentially weighted moving-average, and cumulative-sum charts for detecting small shifts or trends more quickly.

The first quiz will cover statistical basics through control charting, be closed-book, permit one page of notes and a calculator, and provide needed statistical tables. Yield modeling will not be included.

Sarahah is a free Android and iOS app for sending anonymous messages to user profiles. Already popular in Egypt and Saudi Arabia, it recently spread widely through social media. The app presents anonymous feedback as a tool for self-development, but reviews are sharply divided, with users reporting hateful comments and warning that it can enable bullying. Privacy controls let users hide profiles from search, restrict comments to logged-in users, block senders, flag or delete messages, and save favourites. Its simple design focuses on private messaging rather than the more public interactions of earlier anonymous apps such as Yik Yak, Secret, and Whisper. Despite its current popularity, it remains uncertain whether Sarahah will endure or fade like similar platforms.

Managed by Q launched in New York in April 2014 as a technology-enabled office cleaning, maintenance, and supplies provider. Its founders, Dan Teran and Saman Rahmanian, sought to make facility management transparent through customer iPads and operator apps that displayed tasks, schedules, service status, messages, and feedback.

Q initially subcontracted cleaners but switched to employing them directly after finding inconsistent quality and limited control. All employees were called operators. Field operators received above-industry pay, training, stable schedules, travel pay, advancement opportunities, and benefits when eligible. Q standardized work through detailed procedures, mentoring, assessments, and its centralized Q Knowledge repository while allowing city teams operational autonomy.

The company emphasized service quality, transparency, employee inclusion, communication, and community. Operators could report problems, recommend services, and communicate with customers. Customers could adjust tasks and rate service. By June 2015, customer retention exceeded 90%, with positive reviews across New York, Chicago, and San Francisco.

By July 2015, Q employed 247 field operators and served 281 accounts across the three cities. Cleaning generated about 70% of typical customer spending, while maintenance had the highest gross margin. Q had raised $17.4 million and was growing approximately 33% monthly.

Teran faced two growth options: expand into additional cities, including Boston, Atlanta, and Washington, DC, or deepen existing markets by acquiring customers and adding services, including vetted third-party vendors. Geographic expansion offered speed against competitors but involved differing real estate and labor markets and the complexity of training a workforce. Platform services appeared more scalable and higher-margin. Teran aimed to pursue growth without undermining Q’s employment model, service quality, or culture.

Detective Mike Wissbaum inhaled heroin mixed with fentanyl while administering Narcan and rescue breaths to an overdose victim in Washington, Missouri. Both experienced medical emergencies, were hospitalized, and recovered. Police warned that fentanyl-laced heroin increasingly threatens first responders.

The PGA848 is a monolithic, high-voltage, high-bandwidth precision programmable-gain instrumentation amplifier with a single-ended output. It provides eight binary gain settings from 0.5V/V to 100V/V, selected through three digital pins, and targets automation, data acquisition, measurement, and semiconductor-test applications. Its linear input range extends to within 3V maximum of either supply while maintaining high common-mode rejection.

A typical application drives an ADS8860 16-bit, 1MSPS SAR ADC using ±15V input-stage supplies and a 5.3V output-stage supply shared with the ADC. A REF6250 supplies the 5V ADC reference, while a precision divider and OPA192 buffer establish the PGA848 REF voltage at 2.5V. Three filters address EMI/RFI, amplifier bandwidth, and ADC charge kickback. The nominal –3dB bandwidth is 318kHz, potentially decreasing to 277kHz with feedback-resistor tolerance, while maintaining –0.1dB flatness to 41kHz. C0G capacitors are recommended in the signal path.

The OPA192 REF buffer uses dual feedback and a 20Ω isolation resistor, providing an 86° phase margin. Changes to REF bypass capacitance require recalculation and simulation, with more than 60° phase margin recommended.

Nominal performance uses ±15V input- and output-stage supplies. Output supplies must remain within input-stage supply levels, and supplies above 40V total permanently damage the device.

Recommended PCB practices include symmetrical input paths, local 0.1µF low-ESR bypass capacitors, separation of inputs from supply and output traces, minimizing leakage, parasitic capacitance, vias, thermal junctions, and exposure to heat sources. Appropriate ESD precautions are required.

TI provides PSpice for TI and free TINA-TI simulation tools, related technical documentation, update notifications, and TI E2E support. Design resources are supplied “as is,” may change without notice, and remain subject to TI terms, limitations, and disclaimers.

The study examined tungsten oxidation in dry air from 400–1050°C, WO₃ sublimation, and oxide-scale microstructure using thermal analysis, microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and Raman spectroscopy. Oxidation transitioned from diffusion-controlled parabolic kinetics to non-protective linear growth, with activation energies of 180.4 ± 3.8 and 117.5 ± 3.3 kJ/mol, respectively. Preferential edge oxidation increased with perimeter-to-area ratio and promoted brittle spalling. Above 600°C, voids and cracks contributed to dust and oxide-scale detachment. WO₃ sublimation increased with temperature and had an activation energy of 335.8 ± 17 kJ/mol. The oxide scale comprised an inner 30–50 nm WO₂ layer, a 10–20 µm WO₂.72 layer, and an outer WO₂.9/WO₃ layer. The WO₂ layer may help explain low detritiation efficiency in JET tungsten tiles.

Katie Albert, a psychology student studying abroad in Florence, describes her increasingly advanced Italian classes, outdoor painting and drawing projects, university cooking classes, and school trips to Siena, Pisa and Lucca. During spring break, she visited seven countries in 10 days, touring museums and cities in Denmark, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, France, Germany and Switzerland. A particularly emotional experience was visiting Becherbach, Germany, where her fourth-great-grandfather was born. She ended the trip by tandem paragliding near the French-Swiss border. After returning to increasingly crowded Florence, she traveled to Croatia for rafting, cliff diving, beach time and Krka National Park, reaching her milestone of visiting 20 countries by age 20. With three weeks remaining, she feels conflicted about leaving Florence and her friends while looking forward to returning home.

The Ontario Court of Appeal overturned Joseph Nicholson’s first-degree murder verdict, ruling the jury was inadequately instructed, and ordered sentencing for second-degree murder. Nicholson received life imprisonment for fatally stabbing 16-year-old Joey Tanner and attempting to murder Jeremy Rodgers in Barrie in 2007. His parole ineligibility may now fall between 10 and 25 years instead of the mandatory 25; the Crown seeks 16 years. Prosecutors cited the violent attack, Nicholson’s criminal record and prison misconduct. Nicholson apologized and said he wanted rehabilitation. Tanner’s parents described their continuing grief and distress over the appeal. Justice Guy Di Tomaso will impose the sentence Aug. 11.

Jeffing, created by Olympian Jeff Galloway in the 1970s, alternates running with planned walking breaks. The method can improve aerobic endurance, reduce fatigue, provide muscle recovery, support consistent training, and lower overuse stress and injury risk. Beginners can alternate 1–2 minutes of running and walking, gradually extending running intervals as fitness improves. Experienced runners may use Jeffing for long runs or recovery weeks to maintain mileage with less stress. It may particularly benefit long-distance runners but is less suitable for sports requiring sustained high-intensity effort. Poor mechanics or progressing too quickly can still cause injuries such as knee pain, shin splints, or plantar fasciitis. Gallucci recommends comfortable, sustainable intervals, good form, gradual adjustment, and consistency.

The survey studies combinatorial, algebraic, geometric, and topological invariants of matroids and complex hyperplane arrangements. It introduces matroids, lattices of flats, realizability, multinets, nets, and their connections to Latin squares and finite groups. It then develops the Orlik–Solomon algebra, holonomy and Chen Lie algebras, resonance varieties, and Koszul modules, explaining their relationships to arrangement complements, cohomology, fundamental groups, and Chen ranks. Open questions concern higher-degree resonance, torsion, realizability, multinet inequalities, and whether all projective 3-nets are algebraic.

The last trading day of the month has historically been weak for the S&P 500. From 1993, holding SPY from the second-last close to the final close produced an average loss of 0.06% per trade and a negative 0.8% annual CAGR, compared with a 0.04% average daily gain. Overnight performance averaged a 0.04% gain, while holding from the final day’s open to close averaged a 0.11% loss with a 42% win rate. The poor results therefore stem mainly from intraday performance. Profit-taking is suggested as a possible explanation, though the cause remains uncertain.

The suicide of Sharon Haliwell, 48, prompted North West Boroughs NHS Foundation Trust to improve communication between mental health teams. Assessments following a suicide attempt found she remained at risk, but an error prevented her counselling referral. The coroner issued a prevention of death notice, citing continuing communication concerns. The trust introduced staff training, patient-record alerts and procedures requiring clinicians to share risk and treatment information.

Australia will replace the Child Care Rebate and Child Care Benefit with a single means- and activity-tested subsidy on July 2. Of 1.2 million eligible families, 489,000 risk delayed payments unless they update Centrelink details through myGov, including estimated 2018/19 income, parents’ activity hours and childcare type.

Subsidies range from 85 per cent of fees for families earning up to $66,958, tapering across income bands to 20 per cent for those earning $341,248–$351,248. Families earning more receive nothing. Annual rebate caps will be removed below $186,958 and raised to just over $10,000 per child above that income.

Generally, both parents must work, study, volunteer or seek work for at least eight hours per fortnight. Depending on activity levels, families can receive 36, 72 or 100 subsidised care hours per fortnight, determined by the parent with fewer activity hours. Exemptions and additional assistance apply in some circumstances.

Payments are subject to hourly rate caps based on care type. Children must meet immunisation requirements or have a valid exemption. The reforms include a $1.2 billion safety net for vulnerable, disadvantaged, regional and remote children.

The Stanley Cup Final is described as a race to four wins in which adrenaline overrides fatigue. The team relies on its experience and ability to rebound after losses. New Jersey’s Sykora-Elias-Arnott line is effective because of its familiarity, but physical defense could contain it. Joe Nieuwendyk is also defended as playing well despite limited scoring, particularly through offensive-zone pressure and creating chances with his linemates.

Hackers released unaired episodes of HBO’s “Curb Your Enthusiasm,” “Insecure,” “Ballers” and “The Deuce,” but no “Game of Thrones” content. HBO declined communication with the hackers, who sought a multimillion-dollar ransom. The breach occurred as Time Warner awaits approval for its AT&T sale.

The Texas Supreme Court denied Anna Black’s application for writ of error in an enforcement action under the Health Spa Act. It declined to approve the appellate court’s distinction between untimely identification of witnesses and documents and emphasized that good cause for admitting unidentified evidence must be shown in the record under Rule 215.5.

Tiffany Gholston, born with a heart murmur, received a pacemaker at 20. Now 41, she supports her health through activity, nutrition and meditation. As a Circle of Red member, she promotes heart health and raises research funds for the American Heart Association.

The passage lists The 74’s education news, commentary, documentaries and donation appeals. Topics include a Texas camp reopening after deadly floods, school integration, academic recovery, student achievements, education policy, STEM, college access, youth culture and historical civil rights cases.

Presenter and interior designer Anna Ryder Richardson, 53, is leaving Manor House Wildlife Park in Pembrokeshire and divorcing Colin MacDougall after 16 years, saying the financial pressures, workload and loss of privacy involved in running the zoo destroyed their marriage.

The couple bought the rundown park for £1 million in 2008 and spent another £1 million renovating it. Their family life and work were featured in Channel 4’s *Chaos At The Zoo* and ITV’s *Anna’s Welsh Zoo*. They endured difficult living conditions, constant work and arguments while trying to generate the £600,000 annually needed to operate the attraction.

A 2010 accident in which a falling tree seriously injured a child and his mother led to more than £100,000 in fines and costs. Anna believes the incident may have marked the beginning of the end of the marriage.

Although the couple remain friends, Anna says they are no longer in love. Colin will continue managing the zoo, while Anna plans to move with daughters Bibi and Dixie to a ruined farmhouse near Bordeaux. She is also rebuilding her television career by co-presenting *60 Minute Makeover* with Peter Andre.

Albert Einstein College of Medicine researchers found that exercise-induced body warming may temporarily suppress appetite through temperature-sensitive TRPV1-like receptors in hypothalamic arcuate nucleus POMC neurons. In mouse tissue, heat and capsaicin activated these neurons, about two-thirds of which carried the receptors. Capsaicin infusion into the arcuate nucleus reduced food intake for 12 hours, an effect prevented by blocking the receptors or silencing their gene. After 40 minutes of treadmill exercise, mice showed increased body and brain temperatures and ate about 50 percent less than inactive mice. Exercise did not reduce food intake in mice whose POMC neurons lacked the receptors. The findings suggest body temperature can regulate feeding behavior and may inform approaches to appetite suppression or weight loss.

Motley Fool Money highlights the no-annual-fee Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card, which offers unlimited 2% cash rewards, a $200 bonus after $500 in purchases within three months, and 0% introductory APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers. Afterward, a variable APR of 18.99%, 23.99%, or 28.99% applies. Additional benefits include Visa Signature concierge service and up to $600 in cell phone protection with a $25 deductible. Approval is most likely for applicants with good or excellent credit, generally scores of 670–850.

Alternatives include the Capital One Quicksilver Cash Rewards Credit Card, offering unlimited 1.5% cash back, 5% on certain Capital One Travel bookings, limited-time welcome bonuses totaling $300, and 0% introductory APR for 15 months; and a Citi card offering up to 2% cash back on purchases, 5% through Citi Travel, a $200 bonus after spending $1,500 in six months, and an 18-month introductory balance-transfer APR.

Motley Fool Money receives partner commissions that may affect offer placement and coverage but says compensation does not influence product ratings. Approval is not guaranteed, and applicants should choose cards suited to their needs.

McLaren says it has resolved the reliability problems that disrupted pre-season testing, including wheel nut, battery, exhaust and overheating issues. Racing director Eric Boullier expects progress at the Australian opener but says McLaren’s position in a tight midfield remains uncertain. Fernando Alonso believes the Renault-powered MCL33 has significant potential, while acknowledging further development is needed.

Researchers propose using a global network of mobile phones and low-cost radio receivers to detect fast radio bursts (FRBs) originating within the Milky Way. Participating devices would monitor relevant frequencies and upload candidate signals to a central system, which would correlate simultaneous detections. GPS timing could locate a burst, while frequency data could help estimate its Galactic distance. FRBs are brief signals of unknown origin; most have been identified only after occurring, though repeating FRB 121102 was traced to a galaxy three billion light-years away. Researchers estimate a Milky Way FRB may occur every 30 to 1,500 years, while a repeating source could produce weekly bursts.

Early forecasts make viewing Philadelphia’s partial solar eclipse uncertain because a southern weather system may bring clouds north. More reliable forecasts are expected Friday. Philadelphia is outside the path of totality, which crosses South Carolina; the last U.S.-visible total eclipse occurred in 1979.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that it issued an October 26, 2017 press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2017. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under the Exchange Act. Chief Accounting Officer Frank H. Brod signed the report.
Huddersfield Giants followed a pre-season win over Warrington with a 28-16 victory at Widnes. Coach Rick Stone urged continued improvement ahead of Salford.

After eight difficult years in the league, the speaker celebrates winning his first Stanley Cup and fulfilling a long-held dream. He praises Larry Murphy, teammates, dressing-room leaders, coach Scotty, and his supportive family, especially his six-year-old daughter. He describes adapting to international hockey, overcoming doubts and maintaining motivation and fitness despite age. Feeling healthy, he considers continuing to play. He also hopes to bring the Cup to Moscow to generate interest and investment in Russian hockey.

On March 22, 2016, NVIDIA entered an accelerated share repurchase agreement with Barclays Bank. NVIDIA will pay $500 million and initially receive 12,108,715 common shares as part of its plan to return $1 billion to shareholders through dividends and repurchases during the fiscal year. Final settlement may involve additional shares, NVIDIA-delivered shares, or cash, based on the stock’s average daily volume-weighted price during the agreement.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that on July 18, 2019, it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2019. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Exchange Act. The report was signed by Chief Accounting Officer Frank H. Brod.

The passage lists English-language governmental reports on the 1945 San Francisco Conference. The compilation links the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals to the United Nations Charter, emphasizing the United States’ role, policy development, informal negotiations, debates, and drafting. It traces U.S. recommendations through May 1945 and Conference work from May 7 to the Charter’s signing on June 26. Documentation includes minutes from U.S., “Big Four,” “Big Five,” and inter-American meetings; records from Secretary of State Stettinius; diplomatic correspondence; policy statements; and presidential papers. Many meeting records were informal notes rather than approved verbatim minutes. Materials came from U.S. government files, libraries, archives, the U.S. Mission to the United Nations, and State Department publications.

Systems and methods adapt, update, or evaluate radiotherapy plans using real-time functional and anatomical imaging data, including PET, MRI, SPECT, CT, ultrasound, and magnetic particle imaging. Biological and physiological measures may include tracer uptake and kinetics, metabolism, hypoxia, gene expression, blood flow, vascularity, tumor morphology, and lymphatic activity.

Measured data are compared with approved ranges, plan quality indices, dose thresholds, or bounded dose-volume histograms. Plans may then proceed, trigger notifications or clinician review, be suspended, or be modified by changing target geometry, dose distribution, treatment duration, session count, fractionation, beam delivery, or organ-at-risk sparing. Specific tracer measurements can guide dose increases or decreases in biologically distinct regions.

The system may combine imaging equipment, a radiation treatment system, a controller, and a clinician interface. The controller processes current imaging data, predicts plan quality, generates delivery commands, and displays metrics and tiered statuses such as pass, pass within tolerance, pass with exceptions, or fail. Rapid gantry movement and dynamic multi-leaf collimation can reduce latency between imaging and radiation delivery.

Bounded dose-volume histograms may be generated by simulating changes in target position or image intensity, calculating dose distributions, and deriving minimum and maximum DVH curves. Current DVHs outside these bounds can generate visual or audible notifications.

Adaptation may occur online before radiation delivery, repeatedly in real time during treatment, or offline for later sessions. Updated plans may account for changes in metabolism, hypoxia, DNA or protein synthesis, receptor expression, immune activity, pulmonary function, tumor volume, and tracer uptake while maintaining clinical dose objectives.

Intel is reportedly in early talks to manufacture AMD chips through its foundry business. A deal would provide Intel Foundry with a major customer and signal AMD’s willingness to use its largest x86 chip competitor for production, though the potential manufacturing volume is unclear. Intel shares rose 7% Wednesday and are up nearly 77% in 2025; AMD gained more than 1%. Intel declined comment, while AMD called the report rumor or speculation.

The Stack Offense compacts players into two stacks outside the free-throw line, limiting ballhandling to three players while two posts screen. Ballhandlers penetrate toward a wing as a teammate pops off a post screen, then rotate into the stack. Overplayed players back cut or roll to the basket; posts may roll when defenders help or step out as pressure releases. Ballhandlers may drive when the basket is unprotected, use drop passes if post defenders help, and should avoid offensive fouls. Players then reset the stack alignment.

Reports highlight California’s declining forward power prices, which reduced the value of $43 billion in long-term contracts by an estimated 15%. Enron had sold aggressively into the market, while California secured some June–September power at lower prices. Separately, investors sold options amid expectations of range-bound stock markets; a large bullish Enron options spread accompanied a rise in its shares.

Saudi Arabia selected international companies for three natural-gas projects requiring about $25 billion, reopening its energy sector to substantial foreign investment. Exxon Mobil, Shell, BP and Phillips were chosen for South Ghawar; Exxon would lead the Red Sea project with Enron and Occidental; and Shell, TotalFinaElf and Conoco received the Shaybah project. Leaders for South Ghawar and Shaybah were expected by June 5, alongside preliminary agreements. The projects encompass gas development, power generation, desalination and chemicals, supporting Saudi economic growth, employment and domestic energy demand.

Steven Kean said Enron’s role in defending Export-Import Bank funding was smaller than reported and aligned with its reduced interest. Enron had cut related staffing and spending, but Kean believed project-finance work remained important for existing projects, ongoing pursuits and asset-sale transfers. John Hardy said Enron would support Ex-Im and OPIC programs without leading lobbying efforts, noting active Electrobolt negotiations and troubled projects requiring agency support.

News reports described major exporters lobbying against a proposed 25% Ex-Im budget cut. Other coverage addressed Enron’s Houston office tower, Dutch gas-market competition, California utility insolvency and unfinished power contracts, doubts about Sierra Pacific’s proposed Portland General Electric acquisition, and falling U.S. natural-gas prices.

The coach said the team shortens third-period shifts so players retain energy. Line combinations remain unsettled, with Hrkac, Plante, Hogue, Sydor and Keane among the options; Sydor offers greater size and physical impact. Hull is considered doubtful for the next game because returning too soon could worsen his injury, while Hogue may join the pregame warmup and could return if his progress continues.

The team’s shutdown pair is assigned to whichever opposing line poses the greatest offensive threat, with attention shifting among players such as Brown, Peca, Sanderson and others. Injury locations are withheld to protect players, but the coach aims to be clear about whether injured players will play. Keane and Carbonneau were offered rest after heavy workloads.

The coach described learning to manage Hull’s personality and creativity through compromise: Hull has freedom with the puck but must follow the team’s physical and aggressive system without it. The team practices exploiting goaltender weaknesses, though only composed players such as Nieuwendyk can consistently execute delicate plays under pressure.

Players believe they lacked sufficient physical and mental sacrifice in a previous overtime loss to Colorado and want a stronger performance. The team aims to prevent dangerous leaders such as Peca from controlling the game’s offensive, physical or emotional tempo and to keep him away from the net.

A video posted by Kimberly Jones showing her sixth-grade son, Keaton Jones, describing bullying at Horace Maynard Middle School went viral and drew support from celebrities, athletes and the public. Principal Greg Clay said he was unaware of repeated bullying, the reported lunchroom incident had been resolved, and action was taken involving other students. The school planned an assembly and a January anti-bullying talk. Parents said bullying occurs occasionally but did not consider it more prevalent in Union County than elsewhere.

A cross-sectional secret-shopper study assessed whether 335 New York City pharmacies would hypothetically fill electronically prescribed, nameless expedited partner therapy (EPT) for chlamydia and whether access varied by neighborhood socioeconomic vulnerability. Only 40% of pharmacists knew about EPT, and 30% were willing to dispense nameless prescriptions. Awareness strongly increased willingness to dispense, but only 46% of potentially fillable prescriptions followed New York State guidelines. Common refusal reasons were unfamiliarity with EPT and the belief that a patient name was legally required. Insurance could be used for 86% of potentially fillable prescriptions.

National chain pharmacists were more likely than non-chain pharmacists to report EPT awareness. Contrary to the study hypothesis, awareness was higher in more socioeconomically vulnerable neighborhoods, while vulnerability was not associated with willingness to dispense. Neighborhood chlamydia rates, borough, pharmacy type, and vulnerability were not significantly associated with willingness.

The study identifies limited awareness, low willingness to dispense nameless prescriptions, and poor guideline adherence as barriers to EPT implementation. It recommends pharmacist education, policy and workflow improvements, and streamlined electronic prescribing. Limitations include hypothetical telephone interactions, possible variation among secret shoppers, focus on one metropolitan area, and no direct examination of pharmacist decision-making.

Skinimalism simplifies skincare by using a few high-quality, targeted, multitasking products rather than layering many potentially conflicting ingredients. According to Dr Hazel Parkinson, this approach supports the skin barrier, reduces irritation and sensitivity, and may lower costs, waste, packaging, and anxiety about achieving a “perfect” routine.

Most people can benefit from a balanced, barrier-friendly routine, though acne, pigmentation, rosacea, and other concerns may still require specific actives such as azelaic acid, salicylic acid, retinoids, or niacinamide. These should be used selectively, with professional guidance when appropriate. Consistent use of a suitable active and daily SPF may be more effective and tolerable than a complex regimen.

Routines should reflect individual skin needs, age, lifestyle, and tolerance. Dry or reactive skin may need hydration and barrier repair, while oily or congested skin may benefit from salicylic acid. Menopausal skin may require richer moisturisers and targeted ingredients. Those reducing a multi-step routine should remove products gradually, allowing two to four weeks for their skin to adapt, and consult a professional if unsure.

A case study examined whether smartphone touchscreen interactions reflect medication- and seizure-related behavioural changes in a man with refractory temporal lobe epilepsy. Over 185 days, an app recorded 718,357 interactions alongside seizure reports and video-EEG monitoring during anti-seizure medication withdrawal. Daily inter-touch interval distributions were compared before, during and after tapering, and around a focal to bilateral tonic-clonic convulsion. Medication tapering significantly increased fast next-interval dynamics, an effect reversed after medication restart. The convulsion day, consisting mostly of post-ictal data, showed slower dynamics than the preceding three days. These findings suggest smartphone interactions may unobtrusively track fluctuating behavioural effects of anti-seizure medications and convulsions that cross-sectional assessments may miss. The study evaluated only one patient and did not assess focal seizure effects; cohort studies are needed to determine generalisability and clinical utility.

The passage argues that globalization increasingly shapes societies, education policies, communication, and English curricula. English functions as an international communication tool, while global education can prepare university students to understand cultural diversity, cooperate across borders, and address shared problems. Suggested curriculum topics include global warming, energy, environmental protection, health, war, economics, human rights, cultures, technology, and international institutions. Teaching methods include discussions, role-play, multimedia, online resources, news analysis, presentations, and cross-cultural interaction.

Researchers implemented an 18-week globalization-focused English program with 372 non-English-major students at three Taiwanese universities. Students studied topics such as climate change, tourism, festivals, food, technology, sports, endangered animals, conflict, energy, medicine, architecture, and environmental protection. Data were collected through surveys, online reflections, classroom discussions, and social media activities.

Most participants considered globalization education important, interesting, and suitable for formal curricula. They identified global warming, energy, and environmental protection as leading concerns. Large majorities reported that online materials supported learning and that global topics increased English-learning motivation, while 57% said the program increased confidence in international interaction. Students recommended travel, films, historical and current events, international music, guest speakers, English-language news, exchanges, games, and debates as teaching approaches.

The passage concludes that English curricula should integrate current global issues according to students’ majors and interests. Such instruction may strengthen English proficiency, intercultural understanding, global awareness, and students’ capacity to participate in international cooperation.

The passage describes a hardware-aware machine learning model scaling and swapping system designed to reduce resource consumption while maintaining model performance under changing hardware and environmental conditions. Conventional manual model design and neural architecture search are computationally intensive and often optimize models only for specific platforms or metrics.

The system uses a trained, overparameterized “supernet” containing multiple smaller “subnets” optimized for different constraints. A performance auditor monitors inference quality and context information, including power modes, processor and memory utilization, available cores, battery state, temperature, physical environment, and network conditions. When configured thresholds indicate a status change, a subnet selector searches for replacement models that satisfy performance and hardware constraints.

Replacement selection emphasizes similarity to the currently deployed subnet. Model parameters can be vectorized, allowing the system to identify shared parameters and transfer only differing values. A two-stage algorithm first builds a candidate set of subnets meeting performance and operational constraints, then selects the candidate with the lowest data-transfer cost. This approach seeks to minimize memory writes, loading time, communication overhead, and dynamic power during model replacement. The search mechanism is modular and may use various neural architecture search or multi-objective evolutionary algorithms.

Users configure the system through an interface that can specify a supernet, datasets, tasks, domains, target hardware, quality metrics, constraints, search settings, and supported libraries. Monitored metrics may include accuracy, error, latency, throughput, power consumption, memory use, processor utilization, and computational operations.

Potential applications include autonomous vehicles, remote sensor arrays, drones, IoT image-recognition devices, edge systems, and federated learning. The described implementation can run across client, edge, cloud, or embedded computing platforms and may use CPUs, GPUs, neural accelerators, programmable hardware, memory, and storage components.

Microsoft’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2018 reported revenue of $29.1 billion, up 19% year over year; operating income of $10.0 billion, up 29%; net income of $8.8 billion, up 34%; and diluted earnings per share of $1.14, up from $0.84. Commercial cloud revenue rose 47% to $8.5 billion.

Revenue increased across all segments. Productivity and Business Processes revenue grew 19% to $9.8 billion, Intelligent Cloud grew 24% to $8.6 billion, and More Personal Computing grew 15% to $10.7 billion. Growth included Azure revenue rising 76%, Gaming 44%, LinkedIn 33%, and Office Commercial 17%.

Microsoft generated $13.7 billion in operating cash flow and used $3.0 billion for investing and $7.4 billion for financing. It repurchased $3.7 billion of stock and paid $3.2 billion in dividends. At quarter-end, assets totaled $257.6 billion, including $135.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments; liabilities were $171.7 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $86.0 billion.

The effective tax rate declined to 14% from 18%, primarily because of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. Microsoft’s planned $7.5 billion stock acquisition of GitHub was expected to close by the end of October 2018. Deloitte’s review found no material modifications necessary for the interim financial information to conform with U.S. GAAP.

A University of Connecticut study found that nicotine-based e-cigarette vapor caused DNA damage comparable to unfiltered cigarette smoke. Researchers used a low-cost, 3D-printed device containing human metabolic enzymes and DNA to simulate lung exposure. Potential damage increased with the number of puffs and depended on vapor intake and additives. Because DNA mutations can lead to cancer, the findings challenge claims that vaping is considerably safer than tobacco smoking. The research was published in ACS Sensors.

The passage explains how to backtest a momentum strategy in Python using yfinance, pandas, NumPy, and matplotlib. Adjusted closing prices for selected sector SPDR ETFs are resampled monthly, with momentum defined as rolling nine-month performance. Each month, the strategy selects the three best-performing ETFs, holds them in an equally weighted portfolio, and calculates returns. Performance is then plotted and compared with SPY. Since 2005, the strategy achieved a 9.89% compound annual growth rate versus SPY’s 9.46%, producing little additional return. The approach can be customized with different assets or momentum periods.

Anna Mae Blessing, 92, was charged with first-degree murder, aggravated assault and kidnapping after allegedly fatally shooting her 72-year-old son in their Arizona home during a dispute over assisted living. Authorities said she also pointed two pistols at his girlfriend, who disarmed her before deputies arrived.

The Evening Star is a three-candle bearish reversal pattern: a tall bullish candle, a small candle gapping above it, and a bearish candle closing below the first candle’s midpoint. Reliability increases with a significant gap, a long third candle, and confirmation from resistance levels, trendlines, momentum oscillators, RSI, stochastic oscillator, or Bollinger Bands. Traders may enter short positions after confirmation, using profit targets and stop-loss orders. The pattern can be backtested with defined rules and adapted across timeframes and market conditions. Risks include false signals, volatility, over-reliance on technical analysis, insufficient diversification, and losses from poor risk management.

Market Basket, a New England supermarket chain, combined low prices, high sales volume, debt-free growth, strong customer service, experienced employees, internal promotion, profit sharing, bonuses, flexible scheduling, and close supplier relationships. By 2014, it employed 25,000 people at 71 stores and generated $4.6 billion in revenue. Its operating margin exceeded several competitors despite relatively high labor costs.

The company was divided by a longstanding ownership dispute between cousins Arthur T. and Arthur S. Demoulas. After Arthur S.’s faction gained board control, it restricted Arthur T.’s authority, approved a $300 million shareholder distribution, and fired him and other senior executives in June 2014. Employees feared that new leadership would undermine the company’s business model, wages, benefits, prices, and culture.

In July, most headquarters employees, warehouse workers, and drivers walked out, demanding Arthur T.’s reinstatement. Store employees, customers, vendors, politicians, unions, and local businesses supported the protest and boycott. Deliveries largely stopped, sales fell more than 90%, part-time employees were dismissed, and suppliers and neighboring businesses suffered losses. Replacement efforts and return-to-work ultimatums were largely unsuccessful.

On August 27, Arthur T. and his family agreed to purchase the opposing family’s 50.5% stake for $1.6 billion. Arthur T. and his management team regained operational authority, employees returned, and customers and vendors quickly resumed business. The purchase required $1.6 billion in financing secured partly by company real estate. Although employees remained confident and committed to reducing costs, observers questioned whether Market Basket could maintain low prices, generous compensation and benefits, and continued growth while carrying the new debt.

Wide receivers are increasingly valuable as football offenses become more pass-oriented, reflected by six being selected in the first 20 picks of the 2022 NFL draft. Their primary responsibilities are running precise routes, getting open, catching passes, winning one-on-one matchups, understanding coverages, and maintaining coordination with the quarterback. They also contribute through perimeter run blocking, where effort can help turn short gains into touchdowns.

The position’s name comes from receivers typically lining up wide, near the sideline, to receive quarterback passes. Other names include WR, wideout, split-end, and flanker. Key skills include route-running, blocking, body control, speed, strong hands, coordination, and agility. Receivers generally have lean builds, though sizes and playing styles vary.

Notable historical receivers include Jerry Rice, Randy Moss, and Steve Largent. Elite receivers can disrupt defenses, command extra attention, affect safety alignment, and create strategic opportunities for offensive coordinators.

PerovSegNet is a lightweight SEM-image segmentation framework for identifying perovskite, lead iodide, and defects in perovskite solar-cell films. Built on YOLOv8x-seg, it introduces an Adaptive Shuffle Dilated Convolution Block for multi-scale feature extraction and boundary localization, plus a Separable Adaptive Downsampling module that preserves fine textures and large-scale morphology.

The PerovData dataset contains 10,994 augmented images derived from 40 manually annotated SEM images, divided into training, validation, and test sets before augmentation. UMAP analysis indicated clear separation among the three material classes. PerovSegNet was trained for 300 epochs using AdamW and evaluated through precision, recall, mAP, parameter count, and GFLOPs.

Reported comparisons show PerovSegNet outperforming Mask R-CNN, Cascade Mask R-CNN, and Cascade InternImage-XL while requiring fewer computational resources than several baselines. Ablation experiments found that combining both proposed modules produced an mAP@0.5 of 87.25% and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 79.96%, while reducing parameters and GFLOPs by approximately 24% and 25% relative to YOLOv8x-seg. Defect segmentation accuracy increased from 33% to 64%. Qualitative results showed sharper boundaries and fewer missed lead iodide clusters and defects.

The framework also quantifies material area, count, grain-size distribution, and shape complexity. Analysis of approximately 25 published studies found positive correlations between PCE and perovskite area, lead iodide area, and perovskite count, while defect area and count correlated negatively with PCE. These correlations are observational and do not establish causality.

Limitations include dataset size and diversity, class imbalance, segmentation errors, varying imaging conditions, and insufficient speed for in situ workflows. The dataset and source code are publicly available on GitHub.

Twelve autism units—five primary and seven post-primary—were planned for Sligo/Leitrim and Donegal during 2018/19. Leitrim’s ASD classes had increased from two to five since 2011. Minister Richard Bruton also reported substantial national increases in SNA support, resource teachers and special classes. Placement requires a professional report, and oversubscribed schools must use fair, non-discriminatory selection processes. The NCSE advises parents to apply early.

Vanuatu’s Reserve Bank may investigate AFIC, a savings and loan scheme promising 50% interest despite having no commercial bank deposits. Ambae volcano activity was downgraded to level 3, while aid was collected for displaced communities. New teacher salaries begin in 2018, and 21 retired teachers received service medals.

The author rejects Ambassador Hartman’s proposal to trade uncertain INF deployment for an arms-control agreement. Although INF originally aimed to reassure Europe, deployment has become a test of NATO’s viability. The author argues European support remains sufficient, recommends maintaining the zero-zero option, and urges scheduled deployment unless the Soviets adopt a balanced position. Only after deployment and meaningful Soviet concessions should asymmetrical reductions be considered; prematurely abandoning zero-zero would strengthen European anti-deployment forces and weaken incentives for Soviet compromise.

Separately, Secretary Shultz and Ambassador Dobrynin agreed to hold regular discussions on arms control, regional, and bilateral issues. They favored a Foreign Ministers’ meeting before the next UN General Assembly and considered a U.S.-Soviet summit desirable if it produced concrete results. Dobrynin argued that major arms-control disputes required resolution through the Shultz-Gromyko channel because Geneva negotiators lacked sufficient flexibility.

Crystal Palace host Newcastle at Selhurst Park on Sunday. Both managers had unsatisfactory transfer windows. Palace have six long-term absentees, including Bakary Sako, while Newcastle’s Islam Slimani is doubtful. Palace’s form is LDWWLD; Newcastle’s is LDWDLD.

The second edition of *The New Zealand Land and Food Annual*, edited by Professor Claire Massey, was launched at National Field Days. Featuring 31 experts, it examines how New Zealand’s $33 billion land and food sector can grow sustainably through nutrition-driven agriculture operating within planetary boundaries. Contributors emphasize that current practices are unsustainable but New Zealand could adopt smarter agri-food systems.

International and U.S. legal authorities recognize compensation for loss of a vessel’s use during unjustified detention or necessary collision repairs. Where a market rate for vessel use exists, it determines damages; otherwise, expected profits may be considered. Compensation may include lost catch for whaling vessels or anticipated hire and freight, less ordinary operating expenses. The objective is full indemnity for actual loss, including repair costs and earnings lost during the reasonable repair period. This principle was applied to whaling ships forced by the Confederate cruiser Shenandoah to abandon their voyages, though owners and officers were also expected to take precautions, such as having the mate replace an unavailable captain.

The study examined chemical polishing of Cd₁₋ₓZnₓTe₁₋ᵧSeᵧ (CZTS) detector crystals with selenium contents of y = 0, 0.02, 0.06, and 0.1 using fresh 5% bromine–methanol solution. Mechanical processing creates damaged surface layers that impede charge collection and increase leakage currents, making their removal essential for detector fabrication.

Samples with similar zinc content were etched at approximately 19°C for up to eight minutes. Etching depth, surface morphology, trajectories, and average rates were measured. Average rates decreased from 24 μm/min for selenium-free CZT to 18, 15, and 13 μm/min for increasing selenium concentrations. Even about 2% selenium reduced the rate by roughly 20–24%. Rates also declined as the damaged surface layer was removed and the stronger bulk crystal became exposed. Stirring could increase rates by 1.5–2 times, while prolonged etching beyond 3–5 minutes could increase roughness and intensify etching near defects.

A thermodynamic model related the lower CZTS etching rate to its negative excess Gibbs energy relative to CZT. For y = 0.02, the model predicted a 22% reduction, close to the experimental 24%. The results indicate that selenium hardens the CZTS crystal structure, with the strongest relative change occurring at low selenium concentrations and rate differences leveling off at higher concentrations. These findings can guide chemical-polishing conditions for CZTS radiation-detector elements.

Sixteen Miami Valley seniors graduated May 20 from a Latter-day Saints seminary program in Huber Heights after studying the Book of Mormon. More than 100 students attended. Graduates spoke about spiritual growth and applying scripture. Eleven volunteers taught this year’s classes, which are open to all high school students.

U.S. public education has long adopted business practices, including bureaucratic organization, professional standards, competition, testing, accountability, and charter schools. Efforts to professionalize teaching improved training and certification but did not substantially improve teacher financial security or student test scores. No Child Left Behind imposed standardized testing and escalating consequences for schools failing to demonstrate annual progress. Charter schools produced mixed results: some achieved academic success, while others increased segregation, disparities, financial inefficiencies, and disruptions without broad gains in test scores.

The passage critiques the medical model of education, which attributes learning outcomes to inherent biological traits and uses diagnosis to categorize disabilities. Although diagnosis can support effective treatment, it may also encourage fixed mindsets, stigma, stereotype threat, disengagement, and feelings of inferiority. In contrast, framing disabilities as problems that can be understood and addressed may foster growth, self-knowledge, and productive solutions.

Problem-solving is presented as the foundation of learning across biological, cognitive, and educational systems. It involves interaction with the environment, prediction, explanation, testing, error correction, and theory revision. Research on children suggests they naturally behave like scientists by forming theories, exploring them, and revising explanations. Perception itself similarly relies on experience-based heuristics and predictions that develop through environmental interaction.

The passage argues that education should be reorganized around this universal problem-solving process. Metacognition, teacher feedback, mentoring, collaboration, and project-based learning can help students reflect on and regulate their learning. Rather than categorizing students against standardized norms, schools should assess individual progress toward goals and provide each student with trained personal support.

A problem-solving structure could operate recursively across classrooms, administration, and institutions. Students would work toward self-directed learning, teachers would model hypothesis formation and testing, and administrators would address problems beyond classroom capacity using the same process. The proposed restructuring would replace business-oriented bureaucracy with collaborative support designed to help all students understand their abilities, solve educational problems, and manage lifelong learning.

The State Department clarified that passport applicants need not promise to return within two years, though passports should not be issued to citizens who do not intend to return. Passports remain valid for two years and may be renewed upon satisfactory application. During a mission head’s absence, the first secretary ordinarily serves as chargé d’affaires ad interim; assigning a second or third secretary requires prior Department consultation. Leave should be coordinated to maintain appropriate staffing. An April 1902 executive order prohibited diplomatic and consular officers from publicly attacking, criticizing, or filing charges against colleagues; such concerns must be communicated confidentially to the Department of State.

The statistical analysis plan describes pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, efficacy, and safety analyses by treatment group. Plasma drug and glucose concentrations, changes from baseline, PK/PD metrics, and glucose recovery will be summarized and displayed through tables, concentration-time plots, Kaplan–Meier curves, histograms, and sensitivity analyses. The primary PD endpoint is plasma glucose area under the effect curve above baseline from 0 to 30 minutes.

Safety analyses use the safety set and cover insulin use, hypoglycemia induction, trial medication, rescue glucose, local tolerability, adverse events, laboratory tests, vital signs, ECGs, and immunogenicity. Treatment-emergent adverse events are coded using MedDRA and summarized by type, relationship, severity, system organ class, and preferred term. ADA incidence includes treatment-induced and treatment-boosted cases among evaluable patients.

The plan specifies data presentation, rounding, missing-date handling, unit conversions, baseline-change calculations, listings, and programming conventions. SAS quality control includes program and log review, output verification, dataset validation, source-data checks, figure comparisons, and retained documentation. Protocol changes include revised primary efficacy analysis wording, added sensitivity and supportive analyses, and modified terminology for secondary efficacy time points.

DAWN-PLASMA is a randomized, open-label, phase 2 multicenter trial comparing supportive standard care with standard care plus convalescent plasma in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Outcomes align with WHO protocols to facilitate data pooling.

Amazon.com’s 2019 Form 10-K describes operations across North America, International, and AWS, serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators. Amazon emphasizes customer focus, invention, operational excellence, and long-term thinking. It employed approximately 798,000 people at year-end.

2019 net sales were $280.5 billion, operating income $14.5 billion, net income $11.6 billion, and diluted earnings per share $23.01. Operating cash flow reached $38.5 billion; year-end assets totaled $225.2 billion. Cash, equivalents, and marketable securities were $55.0 billion.

Amazon identifies risks involving intense competition, expansion, fluctuating results, international operations, fulfillment capacity, seasonality, acquisitions, foreign exchange, personnel, cybersecurity, system interruptions, inventory, intellectual property, regulation, taxation, suppliers, payments, litigation, and seller misconduct.

Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen challenged Trump administration claims that Dodd-Frank restricts lending and weakens US banks, citing healthy credit growth, strong profitability, resilience and increased capital. She acknowledged burdens on community banks and supported exempting them from the Volcker Rule rather than dismantling Dodd-Frank. Yellen urged productivity-focused fiscal policies that maintain sustainable federal accounts, warning some proposals could increase deficits. She also said interest rates should rise sooner to avoid rapid increases later.

Anthology is restructuring after accumulating more than $1 billion in debt, losing nearly $80 million and seeing revenue fall by $80 million over two years. Oaktree Capital Management and Nexus Capital Management will provide $50 million as Anthology focuses on Blackboard and sells its enterprise, life-cycle engagement and student success businesses to bidders including Ellucian and Encoura. Analysts attribute its decline to acquisition-driven expansion, difficulties integrating a sprawling product portfolio, rising costs and interest rates, increased competition, and an unsuccessful assumption that institutions would buy combined learning management, student information and customer relationship management systems. Institutions are not expected to be disrupted because Anthology’s products will continue under other buyers. Analysts describe the restructuring as part of a broader shift in education technology from rapid growth toward sustainable, modular and interoperable platforms.

The TPS7H500x-SP push-pull converter example uses a 49.9-kΩ leading-edge blanking resistor for about 50 ns, subject to optimization for PCB parasitics and gate-driver delay. A 33-nF soft-start capacitor provides approximately 7.5 ms. The transformer design targets a 35% maximum duty cycle, a 2.5 turns ratio, and 6% magnetizing current; 40 µH primary inductance was used instead of the calculated 33 µH.

Primary-side GaN FETs were conservatively rated at 170 V for a 36-V maximum input, while 80-V GaN FETs were selected for synchronous rectification. Parallel Schottky diodes can reduce soft-start current and dead-time reverse-conduction losses. An RCD clamp may limit switch-node overshoot, with component values requiring test optimization.

The output stage uses a 0.47-µH inductor targeting 40% ripple. Calculations require at least 1.3 mF output capacitance, but approximately 2.3 mF was used for radiation-induced single-event transient mitigation. An optional secondary LC filter can reduce ripple, with damping added if high-frequency peaking occurs.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins near 35 A. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω sense resistor are used. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover using 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF components. A 102-kΩ slope-compensation resistor connects RSC to AVSS.

The controllers require a regulated 4-V to 14-V supply and at least 0.1 µF VIN bypassing. Layout guidance emphasizes short, wide high-current paths; minimized switching loops and switch-node copper; separation of analog and power grounds with a single connection point; close placement of bypass, filtering, sensing, and compensation components; and isolation of sensitive traces from high-dv/dt signals and magnetics. CFP backside metallization should connect to AVSS through multiple vias.

German Chancellor Angela Merkel and Polish Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki discussed Poland’s rule-of-law dispute with the EU, European unity, migration support, economic cooperation and security in Warsaw. Merkel welcomed prospects for resolving the judicial standoff, while Morawiecki said agreement required mutual understanding. Both called for a firm EU response to the poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal, citing indications of Russian responsibility. Russia denied involvement.

Education Department employees will be affected by federal mass layoffs initiated by Office of Management and Budget director Russell Vought during the government shutdown, though the number and offices involved remained unclear. Sources said the Office of Federal Student Aid would be spared, while elementary and secondary education and communications staff could be affected. A senior department leader said OMB directed the unexpected cuts. The employees’ union pledged legal opposition, calling the layoffs an illegal effort to dismantle the department. Earlier Education Department layoffs were initially blocked by lower courts but allowed by the Supreme Court. Layoff notices also reached Health and Human Services employees. Democrats argued that firing workers during a shutdown is unconstitutional and accused the administration of using layoffs to pressure the Senate over a budget stopgap bill.

Germany’s education system developed from compulsory Prussian schooling into a state-administered, stratified system. Modern secondary education generally includes Hauptschule for vocational preparation, Realschule for intermediate education, Gymnasium for university preparation, and integrated Gesamtschule. Public education has been free since reunification, while structures and school-placement policies vary by federal state.

Special schools emerged in the 1920s to educate students with disabilities, often for low-wage vocational roles. Germany continues to operate specialized schools for different disability categories alongside inclusive programs. Around 577,000 students attend special schools, while inclusion rates remain comparatively moderate. Students with disabilities are more frequently included in elementary than secondary education and often attend Hauptschule rather than academically advanced Gymnasium. Eligibility for services involves assessment and collaboration among educators, specialists, parents, and sometimes students to develop individualized support.

Teachers complete university study followed by a structured, paid, two-year school induction and state examination. Special education teachers receive additional training in pedagogy, behavior management, disability-related needs, and multiple academic subjects. They commonly work in elementary, vocational, or specialized schools.

National and state policies, including equal-treatment legislation, the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, and state inclusion reforms, have expanded educational and employment protections. However, implementation differs among states.

Current challenges include unstable funding, inaccessible buildings, teacher concerns and limited training, inconsistent inclusion practices, social isolation, and restricted academic and employment opportunities. Teacher attitudes strongly affect students’ social integration. Germany is moving toward greater inclusion, potentially shifting special educators from primary instructors in specialized schools to support roles in general schools, while recognizing that placement should reflect individual needs and preferences.

The disclosure describes FinFET and planar transistor structures using cobalt and/or metal silicide in replacement gate electrodes, source/drain contacts, and gate contacts. A metal nitride barrier, such as titanium nitride or tantalum nitride, underlies the metal-containing layer. The fabrication process includes forming fins, isolation regions, dummy gates, epitaxial source/drain regions, interlayer dielectrics, replacement gate dielectrics, work-function layers, contacts, and vias. Cobalt-containing layers may include cobalt silicide and substantially silicon-free cobalt, with composition controlled by deposition temperature. Compared with tungsten nucleation layers, cobalt and metal silicides provide better adhesion to TiN, lower resistivity at small dimensions, greater acid-corrosion resistance, and smoother films, reducing metal loss and improving transistor performance.

A Journal of Consumer Psychology study using four experiments in the US and India found that mothers tended to favor daughters financially, while fathers favored sons. Researchers attributed this to stronger identification with same-sex children. In one raffle experiment, 75 percent of mothers chose girls’ backpacks and 87 percent of fathers chose boys’ backpacks, though over 90 percent denied having a favorite child.

OpenAI’s invite-only iOS app Sora uses Sora 2 to create a TikTok-like feed of nine-second AI videos with generated visuals, scripts, and sound. Users can make digital avatars by recording their face and voice, control who may use their likeness in “cameos,” and view any resulting videos, including drafts.

WIRED found that personalized deepfakes could appear convincingly real despite frequent errors. OpenAI acknowledges risks of addiction, bullying, and likeness misuse, and restricts sexual material, graphic violence involving real people, extremist propaganda, hate, self-harm, and some third-party characters. Testing showed inconsistent enforcement: prompts involving bikinis, crack, self-harm, Darth Vader, and a Taylor Swift impersonator were blocked, while marijuana use and some Pokémon characters were allowed.

The app follows Meta’s similar AI-video feed. WIRED described Sora’s dynamic, personalized deepfakes as entertaining but concerning, noting that one synthetic video was realistic enough that the author’s partner initially mistook it for a filter.

Small-body reservoirs are remnants of planetesimal discs and potential sources of exocomets. The Solar System contains diverse reservoirs, including near-Earth asteroids, the main asteroid belt, co-orbital and resonant populations, Trojans, trans-Neptunian objects, Centaurs, comets, and the Oort cloud. Outer reservoirs are especially numerous and predominantly icy, while inner populations show compositional gradients from volatile-poor to more water-rich bodies.

Stars form through the collapse of rotating dense molecular cores, producing protostars and surrounding discs. Young stars evolve through Classes 0–III as envelopes and discs dissipate. Class 0/I discs are generally massive and thick, while Class II discs commonly contain rings and gaps associated with planet formation. Stellar clusters can alter discs through radiation and close flybys, causing truncation, destruction, material transport, and chemical changes.

Planetesimal composition depends strongly on disc temperature, stellar luminosity, location, dust properties, and evolutionary timing. Snowlines separate regions where molecules remain gaseous or solid; around solar-mass stars, water and CO snowlines lie near 1–2 au and 20–30 au, respectively. Chemical processing, freeze-out, turbulence, and radial drift complicate simple snowline-based compositions. More luminous stars have more distant snowlines.

Dust grows through collisions, sedimentation, and trapping, but bouncing, fragmentation, and rapid inward drift inhibit direct growth to planetesimal sizes. The favored pathway involves local pebble concentration followed by gravitational collapse. Pressure bumps, vortices, vertical settling, and streaming instability can raise pebble densities, although the streaming instability’s precise role remains uncertain. Simulations and Solar System observations support initial planetesimal diameters near 100 km, with formation size potentially increasing with distance from the star.

Host-star mass affects multiplicity, disc lifetimes, snowline locations, and planetary populations. Wide-orbit giant planets appear more common with increasing stellar mass up to about two solar masses, while lower-mass wide-orbit planets remain difficult to detect. Exocomets are preferentially observed around A stars because of observational sensitivity, not because planetesimals form only there.

After gas dispersal, remnant solids form debris discs. These likely exocomet reservoirs are detected around about 20% of nearby AFGK stars and vary widely in width, radius, mass, and morphology. Warps, gaps, clumps, eccentric structures, and sharp edges may indicate planetary interactions. Collisions progressively grind bodies into dust, reducing disc mass with age and making exocomets more likely to be detected in younger systems.

Solar System orbital distributions, surface colors, spectra, cometary gases, returned samples, and spacecraft measurements constrain formation and evolution. However, later dynamical, physical, and chemical processing complicates reconstruction of primordial conditions. Trans-Neptunian populations, Trojans, irregular satellites, and comets appear linked to a primordial distant disc, while compositional groups may reflect different formation locations relative to volatile sublimation boundaries.

The Oort cloud, source of long-period comets, may contain roughly 10¹¹ objects larger than 0.3 km in radius, though estimates are uncertain. It likely formed from scattered planetesimals whose orbits were altered by Galactic tides and the Sun’s birth environment. It may include objects captured from other stars. Stellar encounters can deplete and reshape Oort clouds while temporarily increasing inward comet flux. Exo-Oort clouds are theoretically possible but remain unobserved.

Small-body reservoirs should occur around most main-sequence stars, but their architecture, composition, and exocomet production depend on stellar environment, disc chemistry, planets, collisions, migration, and encounters. Major unresolved questions concern planetesimal formation, debris-disc masses and origins, planetary requirements for comet delivery, captured objects, Oort-cloud formation, and identifying which reservoirs dominate exocomet production. Future observations with JWST, ALMA, Rubin Observatory, SPHEREx, Roman, and large ground-based telescopes are expected to improve understanding.

The TMS320DM814x includes 128 hardware-assisted spinlocks for single-read resource locking and a mailbox module for communication among the ARM Cortex-A8, C674x DSP, and Media Controller. The mailbox provides processor assignment, four-message FIFO queues, interrupt notifications, and four processor-directed interrupts.

The device uses unified L3/L4 memory maps where possible, with limited DSP peripheral access. The TILER adds a 4-GB extended address range for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views; the full range is accessible only to HDVPSS and ISS, while other masters can access one view through the base 512-MB TILER region.

Terminal-function tables describe package pins, multiplexing, electrical types, pull resistors, supply voltages, and de-selected input states. Covered interfaces include boot configuration, DDR2/DDR3, EMAC, GPIO, GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, SD, SPI, clocks, timers, UART, USB, video, reset, interrupts, and JTAG. Required power, grounding, resistor, and unused-pin connections are also specified.

Boot configuration is sampled from BTMODE[15:0] when reset is de-asserted. These bits determine boot order, GPMC settings, Ethernet PHY mode, XIP multiplexing, and PCIe addressing. Supported boot-related configurations include XIP, NAND, I2C, MMC/SD, SPI, EMAC, PCIe, and UART.

Pin multiplexing is controlled individually through PINCNTL1–PINCNTL270 MUXMODE fields. Most pins default to tri-state mode. Unused inputs should use internal or external pulls to prevent floating, and supply pins generally remain connected even when associated interfaces are unused.

Universities including MIT, Columbia, Michigan and Rochester Institute of Technology are testing MicroMasters programs that offer rigorous, low-cost online coursework in specialized fields. MIT’s supply chain MicroMasters costs $1,350, compared with $67,938 for its yearlong master’s program. The certification can help working students gain skills and employer recognition without completing a full degree. Those seeking MIT’s graduate degree must gain admission and complete a semester on campus at full cost. MIT expects to admit 40 students annually to this blended program, using online course performance to evaluate applicants more reliably. Employers including GE, Walmart, IBM and Volvo recognize MicroMasters and encourage employees and applicants to enroll.

NVIDIA RTX Blackwell advances AI-powered gaming and professional applications through neural rendering, shading, DLSS, ray reconstruction, and generative AI. These technologies improve realism, performance, simulations, character creation, and design workflows while reducing computational and memory costs. The architecture honors mathematician and statistician David H. Blackwell.

The speaker emphasizes the urgency of winning tomorrow and expects an exciting game. He praises Colorado fans’ strong support and hopes to play before them again. He recalls wishing during the Olympics to someday play alongside Ray, whose later trade strengthened the struggling Avalanche through leadership, hard work, teamwork, and unselfishness.
STAT’s personnel feature reports that enGene hired Hussein Sweiti as chief medical officer. He previously led oncology clinical development globally at Johnson & Johnson.

The coach said goaltending was not responsible for recent losses and expressed confidence in the team’s goalies and ability to respond. Kris Letang will not return during the series. Archie entered the lineup to add enthusiasm, energy and speed, while Carter Rowney has provided strong minutes, faceoffs, penalty killing, size and physical play. The staff separates certain players to improve lineup balance, though Phil has shown chemistry with Geno. Despite losing, the team considered the previous game its strongest of the series, generating quality chances but failing to convert. Coaches will continue adjusting lines to seek balanced and secondary scoring, correct preventable defensive mistakes, and focus on controllable factors.

The application describes embodiments of a side-by-side off-road utility vehicle with a frame, cargo box, seating area, ground-engaging members, drivetrain, steering, braking, suspension, roll-over protection structure, body panels, doors, lighting, fuel system, and accessories. A disclosed rear suspension positions the left lower A-arm pivot axis on the right side of the vehicle centerline and the right pivot axis on the left side.

Vehicle configurations may include two- or four-wheel drive, selectable differentials, adjustable side-by-side seating, removable and stowable passenger seat bases, adjustable steering, and front and rear anti-roll bars. The frame supports the seats, suspension, fuel tank, cargo box, drivetrain, and body components. The roll-over protection structure uses interconnected members, mating channels, and accessory attachment portions.

The brake system may include a pivoting pedal assembly, master cylinder, pressure switch, remote fluid reservoir, adjustable brake balance, and power assistance. Front and rear suspensions may use upper and lower A-arms, knuckles, coil-over damping members, bearings, and adjustable shocks. The drivetrain may include an engine or motor, transmission, differentials, drive shafts, half-shafts, vibration isolators, and a continuously variable transmission with sealed, removable covers and cooling airflow.

Additional features include a steering rack and column-mounted gear selector, floorboard drainage gutters and access covers, protected fuel filling components, a receiver hitch, cab doors, handholds, bumpers, cooling and exhaust systems, and a tilting cargo box.

PIM Capital, named PAN Finance’s Fund Structuring Partner of the Year for Mauritius and South Africa, provides tailored fund structuring and administration for alternative investments and cross-border opportunities. Operating across Sub-Saharan Africa, Mauritius and Guernsey, it addresses emerging-market challenges such as grey-listing, regulatory complexity and currency volatility. The firm emphasizes upfront planning, flexible structures, local professional networks and long-term client partnerships. Its clientele has expanded from emerging firms to global asset managers managing billions of dollars. Christopher Erasmus leads its Mauritius team.

The Tom Davis-developed “Boston” zone offense assigns each player one fixed role while allowing side changes. It emphasizes low-post play, dribble-entry initiation, up-tempo offense, ball reversal, overloads, and floor spacing. The alignment includes a ballhandling point guard, baseline runner, low-post scorer, outside shooting guard, and weakside rebounder.

Effective execution requires accurate passing, sideline-to-sideline ball movement, skip passes, post feeds, and avoiding forced passes or unnecessary dribbling. Ball reversals trigger wing movement, baseline runs, basket cuts, post flashes, and renewed overloads.

The post establishes inside position based on the defender’s location, while perimeter players spot up when defenders collapse. The baseline runner creates matchup, vision, and communication problems by moving behind the zone. Against overplay, players use skip passes, cross-court passes, back cuts, post isolation, and dribble penetration. Defensive help against penetration creates opportunities for kick-out shots or drop passes. The offense includes specific reads, counters, and special actions against 2-3, 1-2-2, 3-2, and 1-3-1 zones.
FPIs showed strong interest in corporate bond limits, bidding Rs 5,898 crore against Rs 3,360 crore offered, with a 15.25-basis-point cut-off, compared with 1.20 basis points for G-secs.

At Amazon.com, Inc.’s May 30, 2018 Annual Meeting, shareholders elected Jeffrey P. Bezos, Tom A. Alberg, Jamie S. Gorelick, Daniel P. Huttenlocher, Judith A. McGrath, Jonathan J. Rubinstein, Thomas O. Ryder, Patricia Q. Stonesifer, and Wendell P. Weeks as directors. Shareholders ratified Ernst & Young LLP as independent auditor for fiscal 2018 and approved executive compensation in an advisory vote.
