Simple Syllabus says institutions and faculty can restrict visibility, but Texas disclosure requirements complicate privacy. Faculty face conflicting pressures to minimize public syllabus details for safety while documenting course content thoroughly to avoid complaints or disciplinary action.

Diabetes increases the risk of severe COVID-19, while vaccination reduces symptomatic infection, hospitalization, and mortality. This preprint examined glucose control after a BNT162b2 mRNA booster in healthy, pre-diabetic, and diabetic adults and after repeated vaccination in mice. Two weeks after boosting, all human groups showed similar increases in immune-response measures. However, pre-diabetic and diabetic participants had increased HbA1c, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, and triglyceride-glucose index, while fasting glucose and insulin did not significantly change. HOMA-IR correlated positively with vaccine-related immune measures.

Mice receiving weekly vaccination developed impaired glucose tolerance after the fourth dose, elevated triglycerides, reduced insulin responsiveness, and weaker insulin-induced Akt phosphorylation, without significant changes in fasting glucose, insulin, or body weight. Metformin improved glucose tolerance, insulin sensitivity, and insulin signaling in vaccinated mice without significantly altering measured vaccine immune responses.

The authors conclude that repeated COVID-19 vaccination may impair insulin sensitivity, particularly in people with pre-diabetes or type 2 diabetes, and recommend monitoring glucose control. They propose spike protein and immune responses as possible mechanisms and call for long-term studies. The experiments were not randomized, and investigators were not blinded.

Hugh Jackman is again being treated for basal cell carcinoma, his fifth reported treatment since 2013. He credited regular checks and doctors, urged fans to wear sunscreen, and continues promoting upcoming films Logan and The Greatest Showman on Earth.

Valeant, Pearson, Pershing Square and Ackman agreed to jointly manage Allergan-related litigation, split the first $10 million in post-agreement legal costs, mutually release claims and restrict related actions. The agreement may terminate Nov. 1, 2017.

Stan Lee, 95, was hospitalized after experiencing shortness of breath and an irregular heartbeat. His condition remained stable, and he was discharged feeling well, though he requires monitoring. He had recently attended the Hollywood premiere of “Black Panther,” which he co-created with Jack Kirby in 1966.

New Ontario Progressive Conservative leader Doug Ford launched his election campaign at a packed, enthusiastic Toronto Congress Centre rally. Former leadership rivals Christine Elliott, Caroline Mulroney and Tanya Granic Allen attended, signaling party unity. Ford identified Premier Kathleen Wynne and the Liberals as his opponents, criticized government spending and debt, and promised broader prosperity and responsible use of taxpayers’ money. Kory Teneycke is expected to manage the campaign, with Jeff Silverstein handling communications. Candidates, volunteers and Ford allies expressed optimism while acknowledging the election would be difficult. The event drew strong support from “Ford Nation” and included tributes to Ford’s late brother, former Toronto mayor Rob Ford.

Despite clear mammograms, an ultrasound, negative genetic testing, and no symptoms, Olivia Munn took a two-minute breast cancer risk assessment that estimated her lifetime risk at 37%. An MRI subsequently detected stage 1 breast cancer when she was 43. The assessment also led to her mother’s stage 1 diagnosis. Munn advocates making such assessments standard care; people scoring at least 20% are encouraged to discuss earlier screening with doctors.

Severe storms and at least three confirmed tornadoes damaged homes, trees, roads and Jacksonville State University in northern Alabama on Monday night, causing power outages but no reported injuries in Limestone County. More than 29 million people across the Southeast faced threats of intense, long-track tornadoes, winds up to 70 mph and hail up to 3 inches wide. Tornado warnings remained in northern Alabama and southern Tennessee, while northern Georgia was under a tornado watch. Alabama increased emergency staffing, schools dismissed early, the University of Alabama suspended operations and opened shelters, and Gov. Kay Ivey urged residents to follow safety plans.

This prospective study compared 101 cardiomyopathy patients, including 43 with dilated cardiomyopathy, with 101 healthy controls. Blood inflammatory, oxidative stress, and disease-severity markers were measured using ELISA and biochemical assays. Cardiomyopathy patients had significantly higher CRP, TNF-α, MDA, GPX activity, and NT-proBNP levels than controls. TNF-α correlated positively with GPX and MDA, while NT-proBNP correlated positively with MDA and GPX. The findings indicate associations among inflammation, oxidative stress, and disease severity in cardiomyopathy, suggesting interaction between inflammatory and oxidative processes in late-stage disease.

Chinese Premier Li Keqiang pledged to further open China’s economy, expand foreign access to services and manufacturing, lower import tariffs, ensure fair competition, prevent forced technology transfers and strengthen intellectual property protection. The commitments come amid trade-war concerns following US steel and aluminium tariffs and expected tariffs on up to US$60 billion of Chinese goods.

Amadeus FiRe AG corrected its 10 February 2017 voting-rights announcement. BNP Paribas Investment Partners S.A.’s holding fell from 5.003% to 4.99%, or 259,295 voting rights, on 9 February 2017. No voting rights were held through instruments.

The speaker emphasizes relying on preparation, habits, routine, and teamwork despite the higher stakes of the final. Meb Faber’s Three-Way Momentum/Trend-Following Model invests in stocks, bonds, and gold when each asset’s monthly 3-period moving average exceeds its 10-period moving average. Capital is divided equally among qualifying assets and adjusted as signals change.

The strategy reflects momentum investing, which assumes assets with strong 3–12-month historical returns may continue performing well over the following 3–12 months. Momentum results require adjustment for survivorship bias.

Faber’s original 1971–2015 test returned about 13% annually. A later backtest using SPY, TLT, and GLD from 2006 grew $100,000 to $422,000, producing an 8.9% annual return, 57% win rate, 1.6 profit factor, and 18% maximum drawdown. Since 2015, returns declined to 5.3% annually, though drawdowns remained relatively low. Applying 1.5 leverage produced 13.1% annual returns and a 26% maximum drawdown. Similar results across nearby moving-average settings suggest the model was not curve-fitted.

The update adds usability, security, battery, stability and speed improvements. Launched in India at Rs 14,900, the dual-SIM phone has a 5-inch HD display, 13MP rear camera, 3GB RAM, 32GB storage and 2400mAh battery.

Huntington University Hospital’s cardiac surgery transfusion rate averaged 71% from 2011–2013, well above the national average of 48.9%. Transfusions were associated with lower long-term survival, while bleeding-related complications cost HUH nearly $8 million in 2013. Dr. Frank Young was appointed to lead a project aiming to reduce blood-product use by two-thirds by the end of 2014, save $2.5 million annually, and improve patient survival.

Young proposed techniques including careful bleeding control, autologous blood harvest, and retrograde autologous priming. However, HUH’s fragmented structure complicated implementation: surgical team members reported through separate hierarchies, surgeons lacked formal authority over staff, and transfusions could occur without surgeon notification. Compensation arrangements also encouraged competition and surgical volume rather than teamwork or cost awareness.

Young received support from administrators, nurses, perfusionists, cardiologists, some surgeons, and ICU director Anil Gupta, who had long questioned blood-product use. Several veteran surgeons resisted changing established routines. Young therefore needed to determine how to engage colleagues, persuade skeptics, coordinate multidisciplinary teams, and sustain new practices.

Mark Haedicke asks to be removed from the State Bar of Michigan e-Journal mailing list. The forwarded October 25, 2000 edition contains Michigan and Sixth Circuit case summaries, legal service listings, classified advertisements, professional announcements, and upcoming bar events.

Soccer passing-direction terminology describes the ball’s expected path from passer to receiver, generally from the perspective of a player facing the attacking goal. Passes may travel on the ground or through the air. The principal clockwise directions are forward, angled right, right, back-right, back, back-left, left, and angled left.

Forward passes move toward the attacking goal; back passes toward the defended goal. Right and left passes are lateral or square when parallel to the halfway line, while angled passes occupy the spaces between forward, sideways, and backward directions. Diagonal passes are neither parallel nor perpendicular to the sideline. “Wide” targets a sideline or wing, “centering” moves the ball from a sideline toward midfield, and “reverse” describes a pass of more than 90 degrees to a trailing teammate.

Additional terms distinguish distance and field geometry. Short passes generally travel 15 yards or less; long passes exceed approximately 30 yards. “Down the line” follows a touchline upfield, while “switch fields” transfers the ball across the field. Near-post and far-post passes target the closest or farthest goal upright. Possession passes retain control, outlets initiate quick attacks from near the defensive goal, and interface passes travel between defenders to an attacker near goal.

RaySearch and Eckert & Ziegler BEBIG will integrate RayStation and RayCare with BEBIG brachytherapy systems, creating a complete solution spanning treatment devices, planning and oncology information management. Experts attributed the decline to economic fundamentals, particularly interest rates, earnings, liquidity and value, rather than political developments.

The statistical analysis plan compares dasiglucagon 0.6 mg primarily with placebo, with GlucaGen as a marketed reference. Based on assumed median recovery times of 10 versus 50 minutes, 20 dasiglucagon and 10 placebo patients provide 90% power at a two-sided 5% significance level over 45 minutes; 10 GlucaGen patients are expected to suffice.

The safety set includes randomized patients receiving trial product, classified by actual treatment. The full analysis set (FAS) uses randomized treatment, and the per-protocol set excludes relevant protocol deviations. Primary efficacy analyses use the FAS, supportive analyses use the per-protocol set, and safety analyses use the safety set.

The primary endpoint is time within 45 minutes to the first plasma-glucose increase of at least 20 mg/dL from baseline without rescue intravenous glucose. It will be analyzed using Kaplan–Meier methods and a log-rank test stratified by age group and injection site. Patients receiving rescue glucose or not recovering within 45 minutes are classified as not recovered and censored at 45 minutes in the primary analysis. Sensitivity analyses alter rescue-glucose censoring, while supportive analyses include a stratified Wilcoxon test, proportional-hazards models when assumptions permit, and linearly interpolated recovery times.

Secondary endpoints are recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes and glucose changes from baseline at those times. Recovery rates will be compared using Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel tests stratified by age and injection site, with Fisher’s exact test if needed. Glucose changes will use analysis of variance adjusted for treatment, age group, and injection site. A hierarchical two-sided 0.05 testing sequence controls multiplicity for dasiglucagon versus placebo, beginning with the primary endpoint and proceeding through recovery rates and glucose changes. GlucaGen comparisons are outside this hierarchy. No interim analysis is planned, and missing data will not be imputed.

Pharmacokinetic analyses describe dasiglucagon and glucagon concentrations and noncompartmental metrics. Pharmacodynamic analyses include plasma-glucose concentrations, changes from baseline, and area under the effect curve from 0 to 30 minutes. Prespecified rules address sampling times, values below quantification limits, and missing measurements.

Safety assessments include treatment exposure, rescue glucose, local tolerability, treatment-emergent adverse events, laboratory tests, vital signs, electrocardiograms, and antidrug antibodies. Adverse events are summarized by treatment, system organ class, preferred term, relationship, severity, seriousness, and selected categories. Missing causality is treated as related when clarification is unavailable. Immunogenicity incidence includes treatment-induced and treatment-boosted antibodies.

Analyses will use SAS 9.4 or higher and Phoenix WinNonlin 6.4 or higher. Results will be presented through treatment-group tables, listings, and figures under ICH conventions. Continuous variables use descriptive statistics; categorical variables use counts and percentages. Appendices specify formatting, derivations, quality-control procedures, validation requirements, and planned outputs.

Peloton launched five AI-enabled fitness products as part of a post-pandemic turnaround effort. Its premium Bike+, Tread+, and Row+ include Peloton IQ, which offers real-time form feedback, rep counting, weight suggestions, and training plans. Equipment prices rose, with the Tread+ reaching $6,695, while monthly membership fees increased by $5 to $49.99. The launch follows declining shares, leadership turnover, layoffs, and a treadmill recall fine. Peloton shares ended Wednesday down 3.67%.

Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days discounts the 48-inch LG C4 OLED to a record-low $800, while the 65-inch model costs $1,300. The C4 offers strong HDR brightness, natural colors, deep blacks, solid reflection handling, and wide viewing quality. Features include VRR up to 144 Hz on four HDMI inputs, LG’s webOS platform, a versatile Magic Remote, and a slim design with a center-mounted stand. The 48-inch model suits bedrooms or gaming setups, while the 65-inch is recommended for living rooms.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture reorganizes ROPs within graphics processing clusters, increases raster capacity, doubles peak FP32 processing per streaming multiprocessor, expands L1 cache and shared-memory bandwidth, and provides up to 1.9 times Turing’s power efficiency at equal performance.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput, support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute, and add hardware acceleration for motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores support additional data types and structured sparsity, which can double matrix throughput by skipping zero values. These capabilities improve ray tracing, AI inference, denoising, and DLSS; the RTX 3080 rendered the cited Wolfenstein frame in 6.7 ms, while DLSS enables higher-resolution gaming, including 8K applications.

GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, reaching 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/s bandwidth. RTX IO, used with Microsoft DirectStorage, moves lossless decompression from CPUs to GPUs, potentially improving I/O performance, loading, asset streaming, and CPU utilization. Error Detection and Replay detects and retries GDDR6X transmission errors during memory overclocking.

Ampere supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 4K at 120 Hz, and 8K at 60 Hz. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware AV1 decoding up to 8K60 HDR with low CPU usage, while seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

Products based on GA10x include GeForce RTX 30-series cards and professional GPUs. The RTX 3090 has 24 GB of GDDR6X memory; the RTX 3070 uses GDDR6 and omits NVLink. The A40 targets data centers with 48 GB memory, virtualization, PCIe Gen4, and optional 96 GB capacity through NVLink. The RTX A6000 provides 10,752 CUDA cores and 48 GB of GDDR6, expandable to 96 GB with two boards, for rendering, simulation, AI, and scientific workloads.

The study uses the XTANT-3 hybrid code, combining transport Monte Carlo, Boltzmann collision integrals, and tight-binding molecular dynamics, to model nonequilibrium, nonthermal, and nonadiabatic radiation effects in phlogopite. Simulations employed 92 eV, 10 fs laser pulses and varied absorbed doses.

The calculated electronic structure agrees qualitatively with previous studies, with a room-temperature band gap of about 6.5 eV. At approximately 0.17 eV/atom, hydrogen detaches and migrates while the remaining lattice stays stable. This threshold agrees with experimental β- and γ-irradiation damage near 0.2 eV/atom. Electron-phonon coupling cools the electronic system and suppresses nonthermal Mg and Si damage, raising the threshold relative to Born-Oppenheimer simulations.

At about 0.4 eV/atom, magnesium becomes liquid-like alongside hydrogen while the other sublattices remain solid, producing a two-subsystem superionic state. Near 0.5 eV/atom, the entire lattice disorders at differing rates and defect levels appear within the band gap. Around 0.9 eV/atom, the band gap collapses and phlogopite becomes metallic. At 2 eV/atom, nonthermal acceleration—especially of oxygen and potassium—strengthens electron-phonon coupling and causes complete disorder within hundreds of femtoseconds.

The results indicate dose-dependent superionic, semi-metallic, metallic, and disordered transient states. Estimated photon-fluence thresholds may guide future X-ray irradiation experiments.

Oskar and Barbie are praised for intelligence, timing, effort, chemistry, and communication. The team believes it has improved throughout each series and must stay aggressive in the best-of-three. Better structure, composure, and key saves from Binner helped in the last game, but continued improvement remains necessary.

The coach said the team’s previous performance was deficient offensively, physically, defensively and on special teams, but expressed confidence it would respond with its best effort. He declined to discuss lineup or goaltending decisions while praising Michael’s playoff performance and home record. He said the team has generally supported its goaltenders better at home and cannot control Chicago’s choices. The coach highlighted the team’s resilience in difficult situations, praised a player’s professionalism, expected strong games from Mike Richards and Jeff, and said he uses past experiences and the team’s challenging path as motivation in pursuing a championship.

Topological insulator lasers aim to overcome conventional lasers’ sensitivity to defects and their tendency at high power to emit unwanted colors and unstable beam profiles. In topological insulators, conducting surface states resist scattering because reversing an electron’s direction also requires a difficult spin flip.

Researchers recreated this protection for photons using a two-dimensional lattice of coupled optical waveguide rings. Exciting only the outer rings confines light to the edge, while intermediary rings shift its phase as it moves between rings. Light outside the protected state is scattered out, leaving protected light to be amplified by the gain material.

Experiments compared lattices with protected and unprotected edge states. Protected-state lasers continued operating even when rings were removed, were more efficient, and maintained a single color as power increased, unlike unprotected lasers. Accurate modeling and precise fabrication were essential. Such stable, sharply defined lasers could be useful for applications including 5G networks and space-based interferometers.

Law enforcement planned security for Super Bowl LII in Minneapolis for two years, with the city’s police department coordinating federal, state and local agencies. Measures include tactical officers, bomb-sniffing dogs, helicopters, fencing, early stadium screening and first-time indoor prescreening at remote locations because of severe cold. The FBI leads counterterrorism efforts, assesses threats based on past mass attacks and conducts background checks for more than 30,000 credentialed workers. Homeland Security Investigations will monitor counterfeit goods, while more than 400 Minnesota National Guard members will help fill security gaps. Officials aim to keep the event both safe and enjoyable.

Waterstone Financial received a positive Accern media sentiment score of 0.26 and an impact score suggesting limited near-term share-price effects. BidaskClub downgraded the stock to “hold,” while Sandler O’Neill upgraded it to “buy” with a $20 target. Shares traded at $19.45 Friday, down 0.26%. The lecture examines how utility from beliefs shapes information seeking, self-deception, and decision-making. Anticipatory and ego utility can motivate people to hold optimistic beliefs because these beliefs improve present well-being or expectations about the future. However, optimism may distort choices involving treatment, finances, relationships, and other actions, while also creating future disappointment. Optimal expectations therefore balance present happiness against decision errors and disappointment.

Evidence suggests people are often optimistic about positive life events, underestimate personal risks, and overrate their abilities. MIT students are an exception regarding academic confidence, particularly female students, possibly because frequent feedback limits overconfidence. Positive illusions may support motivation and mental health, though underconfidence can either encourage effort or cause discouragement. Positive biases tend to be stronger for personally important or ambiguous outcomes and weaker when people receive clear, repeated feedback.

Experiments show asymmetric processing of self-relevant information. People incorporate favorable feedback about intelligence or attractiveness more readily than unfavorable feedback, pay more for information expected to be positive, and later remember positive signals better than negative ones. Real-world studies associate overconfidence with excessive trading and value-destroying corporate mergers.

The lecture then addresses failures of Bayesian learning. People generally update beliefs in the correct direction but struggle to determine the appropriate magnitude because Bayes’ rule is cognitively demanding. They therefore use heuristics that enable quick judgments but create systematic errors.

Three major deviations are discussed. The gambler’s fallacy is the belief that an outcome is “due” after a streak of another outcome, despite independent draws. The hot-hand fallacy is excessive belief that recent success predicts continued success. Both can arise from belief in a “law of small numbers,” under which small samples are expected to represent underlying probabilities too closely. Base-rate neglect occurs when people focus on new evidence, such as a test’s accuracy, while overlooking the prior prevalence of an outcome. These biases can affect consequential decisions by judges, loan officers, and users of medical tests.

Additional heuristics include representativeness, where similarity substitutes for probability and can produce conjunction errors, and availability, where easily recalled events are judged more frequent. For example, salient homicides may be perceived as more common than suicides.

The policy response depends on why beliefs are inaccurate. Making information salient may help when attention is limited or people misunderstand causal relationships. It may be ineffective when people deliberately avoid threatening information. Correcting motivated beliefs can even reduce welfare when optimism provides utility and cannot improve future action. By contrast, identifying systematic learning biases can help design interventions that improve decisions.

McGill University researchers developed DOLPHIN, an AI tool that analyzes how exons are spliced within genes to reveal disease markers hidden by conventional gene-level analysis. Researchers say DOLPHIN could support earlier disease detection, help match patients to treatments, and reduce trial and error. Its detailed single-cell profiles may also enable virtual cell models that simulate disease behavior and drug responses before laboratory or clinical trials. The team plans to expand the tool from a few datasets to millions of cells.

The study recorded medical problems after BNT162b1, BNT162b2, BNT162b2SA, placebo, and booster doses. Serious medical problems were uncommon, and no single serious problem occurred in at least 1% of any group. Researchers considered most serious problems unrelated to study vaccines, though some temporary serious problems in participants aged 16 or older may have been vaccine-related. Booster groups showed similarly low rates.

No one died in Phase 1. In Phase 2/3, 85 participants initially receiving BNT162b2, 62 initially receiving placebo and later BNT162b2, and 23 receiving placebo before any BNT162b2 died from varied causes. Researchers did not consider the deaths caused by BNT162b2. No BNT162b2SA recipient described in Phase 3 died.

Neutral particle diagnostics indirectly measure core ion distributions in magnetically confined plasmas. Core ions can become neutrals through charge exchange with edge neutrals or injected neutral beams, allowing them to escape magnetic confinement. Their survival depends on attenuation from electron-impact ionization, ion-impact ionization, and especially resonant charge exchange. For 10 keV neutrals at an ion density of \(10^{20}\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}\), the estimated mean free path is about 10 cm; useful measurements therefore require relatively low line-integrated densities, around \(10^{19}\,\mathrm{m^{-2}}\) or less.

Edge fueling can produce detectable core neutrals, while radiative recombination is negligible at typical core conditions because neutrals are rapidly re-ionized. In passive charge-exchange analysis, escaping neutrals pass through a stripping cell, become ions without substantially changing velocity, and are magnetically separated by energy. The resulting spectrum can provide ion temperature and reveal non-Maxwellian fast-ion tails, but the measurement is line-integrated and difficult to localize.

Active diagnostics use a neutral beam to localize charge exchange to the intersection of the beam and detector view. Charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy transfers electrons to fully stripped impurity ions, causing characteristic emission that can determine impurity density, temperature from Doppler broadening, and flow velocity from Doppler shift. Beam modulation helps separate this weak emission from background radiation.

Beam-emission spectroscopy detects light from beam neutrals excited by plasma collisions. Its intensity reflects electron density and can measure localized density fluctuations associated with turbulent transport, though accurate analysis must include multiple atomic processes and beam attenuation.

The motional Stark effect arises because beam neutrals moving through a magnetic field experience an electric field proportional to \(-\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{B}\). This splits hydrogen energy levels and produces polarized spectral components. Measuring their separation and polarization provides magnetic-field direction, the poloidal magnetic-field component, current-profile information, and magnetic reconstruction.

Radiotheranostics combines targeted molecular imaging and therapy, but radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) commonly uses standardized activities and schedules despite patient variability. Computational nuclear oncology and theranostic digital twins (TDTs) aim to enable personalized, dosimetry-driven treatment. Physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models support this goal by integrating patient physiology, radiopharmaceutical properties, imaging, and biofluid data to predict biodistribution, absorbed doses, treatment response, and toxicity.

PBPK models comprise computational, anatomical-physiological, radiopharmaceutical, and treatment-protocol frameworks. They may be developed through bottom-up approaches using preclinical data, top-down approaches fitted to patient data, or middle-out approaches combining mechanistic knowledge with patient-specific calibration. The middle-out approach is particularly suitable for data-limited RPT applications.

Reliable clinical use requires verification, validation, and uncertainty quantification (VVUQ). Verification confirms appropriate model structure, equations, parameters, units, mass balance, and physiological behavior. Internal validation assesses agreement with training data through graphical diagnostics, residual analysis, goodness-of-fit metrics, predictive checks, and parameter precision. Model selection methods such as AIC, AICc, BIC, and F-tests balance fit against complexity. Sensitivity analysis identifies influential parameters, while external validation uses independent data, data splitting, or resampling to evaluate generalizability.

Uncertainty quantification assigns statistical distributions to parameters, propagates uncertainty through sampling methods, and characterizes prediction precision and accuracy using confidence intervals and metrics such as relative deviation, RMSE, and MAPE. These results help assess predictions against clinical efficacy and toxicity thresholds.

Dynamic TDTs extend PBPK modeling through repeated imaging, laboratory measurements, biomarkers, radiobiological models, and bidirectional feedback between patients and simulations. Their continual updating creates additional VVUQ challenges involving sparse or noisy data, scanner and protocol differences, changing pharmacokinetics, and treatment response. Iterative verification and validation across treatment cycles are therefore essential.

Although PBPK modeling is supported in conventional pharmaceutical regulation, comparable radiopharmaceutical standards remain undefined. Fit-for-purpose VVUQ frameworks and collaboration with professional and regulatory organizations are needed to support clinical and regulatory adoption.

Toyota’s Macon, Georgia plant faced serious quality and delivery risks from ChassisCo’s Athens facility, which supplied rear suspension cradles for the 2003 Suprima. Fourteen months after launch, Athens operated at roughly 60% of its target rate, received nonconforming parts, lacked effective defect tracking, and continued to produce problematic welds despite extensive Toyota support.

Toyota’s production system emphasized jidoka, just-in-time production, continuous improvement, respect for people, problem solving, and close, long-term supplier collaboration. ChassisCo had successfully produced cradles for the 1997 Suprima and 1999 Responsa, leading Toyota to give it broader responsibility for sourcing, logistics, inventory, and project management for the more complex 2003 model.

The expanded assignment exceeded ChassisCo’s capabilities. The new cradle had 85 parts, substantially more welding, increased automation, and unfamiliar riveting processes. ChassisCo lacked integrated project management, parts tracking, supplier management, tuning expertise, standardized work, inspection systems, and sufficient engineering resources. Corporate decentralization had dispersed experienced personnel, while numerous simultaneous launches stretched resources. Aggressive pricing encouraged inadequate plant space, low-cost suppliers, and underestimated logistics costs. ChassisCo also failed to communicate that Toyota’s target price was unrealistic or to expose supplier problems early.

Toyota underestimated the capability gap, transferred responsibility too quickly, rotated experienced engineers, provided limited knowledge about tuning and technical requirements, and discovered second-tier supplier problems late. The launch proceeded in September 2003 despite Athens failing Toyota’s high-volume production trial three times.

During 2004, high scrap, downtime, poor parts quality, overtime, and extensive inspection persisted. Toyota audits found critical weld defects, and Athens scored 13% on an arc-welding process audit. External defects rose sharply compared with the previous model. Toyota devoted substantial personnel and expertise, but progress remained slow. By late 2004, ChassisCo sought a price increase to cover mounting costs, while Toyota emphasized correcting underlying quality and process problems and considered what further intervention was necessary.

The paper proposes a scalable framework for evaluating and improving LLM persuasion based on Bayesian persuasion, which models an informed Sender strategically revealing information to influence a rational Receiver’s beliefs and actions. This approach addresses limitations of existing evaluations, including inconsistent metrics, heterogeneous contexts, subjective human judgments, and high resource costs.

The authors repurpose human-persuasion datasets to create environments in which both Sender and Receiver are LLMs, and conduct a 45-participant study supporting the plausibility of the design. Experiments show that stronger frontier models, including DeepSeek-R1, achieve greater persuasion gains and display theoretically aligned strategies such as adaptive information disclosure. Reinforcement learning substantially improves strategic persuasion, enabling a small Llama3.2-3B-Instruct model to perform comparably to larger models. These improvements also transfer across Receiver architectures.

The framework measures persuasiveness through gains in Sender utility relative to prior beliefs and through conditional mutual information, which captures how much state-relevant information an LLM reveals during dynamic interactions. High information values indicate adaptive signaling, while low values may reflect deliberate withholding. The benchmark applies these measures to opinion-change tasks, where a Sender attempts to move a Receiver toward target stances. Bayesian persuasion theory explains why controlled partial disclosure can outperform either full transparency or complete opacity.

The Clock is a simple, versatile zone offense using a 1-3-1 freelance passing attack, crisp ball movement, and clockwise or counterclockwise rotations. It works against person-to-person, 1-3-1, 1-2-2, and trapping defenses, creating outside shots, basket cuts, post rolls, and weak-side opportunities.

When a wing passes to a corner, the wing cuts to the basket while other outside players rotate. The corner may return the pass, feed the post, or initiate ball reversal. A wing may instead dribble-clear the corner, causing the corner player to back cut and exchange roles. Quick reversals attack the weak side when defenses stop an overload.

Against a 1-3-1, the offense targets baseline vulnerabilities; against a 1-2-2, it attacks the middle and corners. If the corner is double-teamed, the offense shifts to a “Cat” 2-1-2 alignment, avoids dribbling, and passes to a middle flash or open perimeter player. The post rolls whenever the ball reaches a baseline corner, and baseline players back cut on middle entries.

Late-clock specials include “Vegas,” featuring a double screen away for a skip-pass shot and post-roll options, and “Back,” which uses weak-side screens, reversals, and lob opportunities before returning to normal Clock action if unavailable.

The passage describes systems, methods, and computer-readable media for a variable multiplexer that enables an external device to communicate with vehicle buses, such as CAN, despite manufacturer-specific data-link connector pinouts. After detecting a connection, the device determines the vehicle’s pinout either by sending an identifier, such as a VIN, to a remote vehicle-data index or by monitoring bus traffic and comparing active pins, received data, and checksums against known configurations. It then commands the multiplexer to adopt the identified mapping. The system may include connection detection, pinout determination and modification components, data storage, a network gateway, and conventional processor, memory, software, and communication hardware.

Equality is presented as a moral and social ideal opposing discrimination and encompassing political, racial, social, economic, gender, and educational dimensions. Education is described as a continuous process shaped by social, moral, economic, and political structures that develops individuals’ skills, attitudes, culture, and behavior. Equality of opportunity in education means enabling everyone to develop their abilities and access suitable educational conditions without discrimination or unfair advantage. It does not necessarily require identical services, but services adapted to individual characteristics and needs.

Educational equality is affected by economic, geographical, political, individual, and social factors. In Turkey, the Ministry of National Education shapes policy, while National Education Councils support discussion and reform. Patterns enable reusable components, improving software quality through broad use and shared maintenance. Containers establish boundaries for resources, ownership, and concerns, allowing single-node applications to be divided into modular components that can be independently tested, deployed, prioritized, and reused.

Single-node container patterns use tightly coupled, coscheduled containers that may share filesystems, networks, process namespaces, and memory. The sidecar pattern augments an application with functionality such as HTTPS proxying, configuration synchronization, monitoring, or Git-based deployment. The ambassador pattern brokers external communication, including shard routing, service discovery, and experimental traffic splitting. The adapter pattern converts heterogeneous application interfaces into standardized forms for monitoring, logging, and health checks. Reusable containers should be parameterized, expose stable APIs, and include clear documentation and metadata.

Multi-node microservice architectures divide applications into independently maintained and scaled services communicating through defined APIs. They improve team autonomy, reliability, agility, and scaling flexibility, but make design and debugging more difficult. Distributed patterns help regularize these architectures.

Replicated load-balanced services use interchangeable instances for availability and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching unprepared instances, while session tracking can consistently route users to particular replicas. Additional replicated layers can provide caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service defense, and SSL termination.

Sharded services divide state among servers and route each request to the appropriate shard. Sharded caches use memory more efficiently than fully replicated caches but can lose capacity or performance when a shard fails. Replicating each shard improves resilience and permits independent scaling. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, and their keys must group requests that produce identical results without combining requests whose responses differ.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture introduces a hybrid rendering model combining rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation. The flagship TU102 GPU contains six Graphics Processing Clusters, 72 Streaming Multiprocessors, 4,608 CUDA cores, 576 Tensor Cores, 72 RT Cores, 96 ROPs, 6 MB of L2 cache, and a 384-bit GDDR6 interface. Each SM includes 64 FP32 cores, 64 INT32 cores, eight Tensor Cores, one RT Core, four texture units, and configurable 96 KB L1/shared memory. Parallel FP32 and INT32 execution, unified cache architecture, and other SM changes provide up to 50% higher delivered performance per CUDA core than Pascal.

Second-generation NVLink enables direct GPU memory access and faster multi-GPU communication. TU102 provides two x8 links with 100 GB/s aggregate bidirectional bandwidth, while TU104 provides one. Turing supports two-way SLI through NVLink, but not three- or four-way SLI.

RT Cores accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, offloading thousands of software instructions from SMs. Combined with hybrid rendering and denoising, they enable real-time ray-traced reflections, shadows, refractions, ambient occlusion, and indirect lighting. Turing can deliver over 10 Giga Rays per second and approximately ten times Pascal’s software ray-tracing performance.

Turing Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, and INT4 operations for deep-learning training, inference, and neural graphics. NVIDIA NGX uses these cores for features including Deep Learning Super Sampling, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Resolution. DLSS is trained from 64-times supersampled reference images and can provide image quality similar to temporal anti-aliasing with less shading work. The passage reports that an RTX 2080 Ti using 4K DLSS reaches twice the performance of a GTX 1080 Ti in the cited workload.

The Tesla T4, based on TU104, targets data-center, enterprise, and edge inference. It includes 2,560 CUDA cores, 320 Tensor Cores, 16 GB of memory, and 320 GB/s bandwidth, delivering up to 130 INT8 TOPS and 260 INT4 TOPS. The passage reports up to 40-times higher inference performance and over 50-times higher energy efficiency than specified CPU-based systems. Turing also adds enhanced video decoding, Multi-Process Service improvements, and greater memory capacity and bandwidth.

Turing is the first NVIDIA architecture to use GDDR6, operating at 14 Gbps with a stated 20% power-efficiency improvement over GDDR5X. Larger L2 caches, higher cache bandwidth, and improved lossless compression give TU102-based RTX 2080 Ti approximately 50% greater effective memory bandwidth than GTX 1080 Ti.

Display and media features include DisplayPort 1.4a, Display Stream Compression 1.2, HDR processing, support for two 8K 60 Hz displays, HEVC 8K encoding at 30 fps, expanded HEVC and VP9 decoding, and improved encoding quality. USB-C and VirtualLink combine display, data, and power for VR headsets through one connector.

New graphics capabilities include Mesh Shading to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks; Variable Rate Shading for content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering; Texture Space Shading for decoupled and reusable shading; and Multi-View Rendering for up to four hardware views per pass. These features target complex scenes, VR, improved image stability, and more efficient rendering.

TU104 retains Turing’s RT, Tensor, and SM features and is used in products including GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. TU106 contains three GPCs, 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores; it powers GeForce RTX 2070 but lacks NVLink and SLI support.

NVIDIA defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based hybrid-rendering metric that weights Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations according to assumed utilization. The passage calculates 78 RTX-OPS for RTX 2080 Ti.

Pete Newell introduced the Reverse Action Offense in the late 1950s. Its guard-around continuity combines precise footwork, timing, spacing, post screens, weakside rub cuts, post-ups, two-player isolation, and counters to defensive overplay.

The basic sequence begins with a guard passing to a wing and cutting to the corner. The opposite wing cuts off a post screen toward the basket; if unavailable, the ball reverses and the pattern repeats on the other side. Any pass or dribble can initiate the offense through weakside, strongside, dribble-clear, or backdoor entries.

Players read defenders and counter with over-the-top or baseline cuts, screener pops or dives, back cuts, lobs, and skip passes. Guard-around and screen-and-roll actions counter defensive coverage with drives, kick-outs, pull-up jumpers, opposite drives, rolls, and slips.

Sideline triangle options include lob and high-post feeds, post splits, screens, isolation, and responses to sagging or double-teaming defenses. Post players adjust according to whether defenders play high side, baseline side, behind, in front, or double-team, using power layups, baby hooks, triple-threat moves, lobs, ball reversals, or pressure releases.

The alignment also supports quick-hitting late-game plays such as weakside screen-and-rolls, double screens, and back-screen lobs.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell RTX architecture is optimized for neural shaders and introduces unified FP32/INT32 cores, higher integer and texture throughput, fifth-generation Tensor Cores supporting FP4 and FP6, and fourth-generation RT Cores with doubled ray-triangle intersection throughput. FP4 reduces AI model memory requirements and improves performance while advanced quantization preserves quality.

RTX 50-Series GPUs use GDDR7 with PAM3 signaling, higher bandwidth, energy-efficiency improvements, built-in single-bit error correction, Enhanced CRC, and Error Detection and Replay. The RTX 5090 provides 1.792 TB/s peak memory bandwidth, while the RTX 5080 provides 960 GB/s.

Mega Geometry accelerates ray tracing of detailed, dynamically changing geometry through cluster-level acceleration structures, GPU-driven BVH management, and partitioned top-level acceleration structures. Blackwell also adds hardware support for Linear Swept Spheres, improving hair and strand rendering speed and memory use. SER 2.0 makes thread reordering more efficient, while the RISC-V-based AI Management Processor offloads GPU-context scheduling from the CPU.

Blackwell expands video capabilities with hardware 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC encoding and decoding. Ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality, while sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed. The RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders. DisplayPort 2.1b supports up to 80 Gbps, including 8K at 165 Hz and 4K at 480 Hz with compression.

Power-efficiency features include finer clock, power, and rail gating; independent core and memory voltage control; clocks that adapt 1,000 times faster; and sleep entry up to ten times faster than Ada. These features can reduce power use by up to 50% in the cited small-language-model inference example.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three generated frames per rendered frame. Its model is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than the prior method. Transformer models replace CNNs for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability, motion detail, lighting, anti-aliasing, and ghosting.

New neural-shader capabilities include Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. Cooperative Vectors APIs expose Tensor Cores to graphics shaders in DirectX 12 and Vulkan.

The flagship GB202 contains 92.2 billion transistors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT Cores, and 768 Tensor Cores. GB203 contains 45.6 billion transistors and 10,752 CUDA cores, while GB205 contains 31 billion transistors and 6,400 CUDA cores. These chips support the RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070 product tiers.

News reports focused on Enron’s financial condition, opaque financing arrangements and declining share price. Enron said it expected asset sales, including $1.55 billion from Portland General Electric, to help repay about $3.3 billion in notes issued by investment vehicles and due within 20 months. Treasurer Ben Glisan said Enron might issue up to $1 billion in stock if sales proved insufficient, potentially diluting shareholders.

Chairman Kenneth Lay and other executives sought to reassure investors that Enron had adequate liquidity and that its businesses were performing well. They defended Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow but declined to discuss partnerships he formerly managed, citing an SEC inquiry and shareholder lawsuits. Analysts criticized Enron’s limited disclosure and questioned potential conflicts of interest, off-balance-sheet financing and a recent $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. Enron shares closed at $19.79 after falling more than 40% in a week.

Enron reported $1.85 billion in commercial paper backed by $3.35 billion in bank credit lines and separately sought a $750 million loan from Citigroup. High volatility in Enron options prompted discussion of straddle strategies, while commentators warned investors that the company remained under a cloud.

Other reports mentioned Enron-related energy projects in India, an LNG vessel contracted to Enron, a proposed $254 million tax refund for Enron under a House stimulus bill, and a securities class-action investigation covering Enron investors.

News reports from November 14–18, 2001 focus on efforts to resolve the Dabhol Power Company crisis. Indian financial institutions, exposed to more than Rs 6,000 crore in project debt, sought at least $700 million for the 85 percent stake held by Enron, Bechtel and General Electric. Tata Power and BSES began due diligence but reportedly valued the stake nearer $400 million and sought concessions, including lower tariffs and interest rates, tax and customs relief, rupee-denominated debt, distribution rights, payment security, and separation of the LNG facilities from power generation.

MSEB opposed surrendering profitable distribution zones, requested postponement of DPC’s November 19 Houston board meeting, and decided not to attend. Courts temporarily restrained DPC from issuing a final termination notice and prevented authorities from encashing customs-related bank guarantees. A London arbitration tribunal was scheduled to meet November 24 regarding MSEB’s unpaid December 2000 bill.

Reports said Enron’s acquisition by Dynegy would not immediately affect Dabhol negotiations. Commentary highlighted Enron’s financial disclosures and questioned auditor Arthur Andersen’s oversight.

Separately, Shipping Corporation of India joined the LNG tanker venture LNG Laxmi. Oman rescued the project after lenders withheld financing, acquiring 50 percent of the owning company and agreeing to charter the vessel for 20 years.

Packers coach Mike McCarthy praised cornerback Damarious Randall’s offseason performance, particularly at the nickel “star” position. Randall is seeking to rebound from an injury-plagued, inconsistent second season complicated by Sam Shields’ absence. Despite Green Bay adding Davon House and Kevin King, Randall remains important to rebuilding the secondary. A soccer defensive wall places defenders shoulder-to-shoulder, normally 10 yards from a nearby free kick, to block the near side of the goal while the goalkeeper protects the far side. Walls become important when players can shoot accurately and powerfully, typically around age 12 on full-sized fields. The goalkeeper decides whether to form a wall and how many players it needs based on the ball’s distance and angle from goal. Generally, closer and more central kicks require more defenders.

Under Law 13, defenders must retreat 10 yards unless positioned on their goal line between the posts. Attackers may take a quick free kick before a wall is ready, and referees need not allow time to build one. Deliberately blocking a restart can result in a yellow card. For ceremonial free kicks, attackers may request enforcement of the 10-yard distance and must then wait for the referee’s whistle. When at least three defenders form a wall, attackers must remain one yard away until the ball is in play.

Wall construction requires urgency and coordinated responsibilities: designated players form the wall, others mark attackers and prepare a counterattack. Traditionally, an “Anchor” aligns 10 yards from the ball on an imaginary line between the ball and near post. The goalkeeper directs the Anchor’s final position, and other wall players assemble tightly beside them without gaps. An alternative uses an upfield “Wall Setter,” allowing the goalkeeper to watch the ball and prepare for a quick kick.

Wall players should face the ball, remain compact and avoid turning, rushing forward, or creating openings. They may protect specified body areas with arms held tightly against the body and may jump, provided the ball cannot pass underneath. After the kick, they must react immediately. A defender may also lie behind the wall to block low shots.

For rare indirect free kicks less than 10 yards from goal, defenders form rapidly on the goal line between the posts. Coaching should emphasize positioning, legal conduct, resistance to deceptive set plays, balanced goalkeeper movement, and using only enough wall players to block the goal without leaving attackers unmarked.

The Kansas court affirmed summary judgment for Farmway Credit Union. Before Melvin Douglas’s death, he was in default on secured debts totaling $111,290.17 and had agreed with Farmway that collateral, including farm equipment, crops, and livestock, could be sold. After his death, his heirs cooperated with the sales, and the estate administrator did not seek to halt them.

The court held that although an administrator generally has the right and duty to possess and marshal estate property under K.S.A. 59-1401, that right is limited by contractual arrangements made by the decedent. Farmway was entitled under its security agreement and K.S.A. 59-1303 to take possession of and sell the collateral without filing an estate claim or commencing a foreclosure action. The court did not decide whether self-help repossession would be permissible without a specific agreement granting possession upon default.

Summary judgment was not premature because the relevant facts—the security agreement and the pre-death agreement authorizing disposition of the collateral—were uncontroverted. No additional material facts remained to be discovered, leaving only a question of law.

The reverse is a high-risk football trick play that deceives defenses by moving the ball in one direction before transferring it to a player running the opposite way. Its success depends on timing, disguise, player momentum, and blockers forming seals or screens to prevent defenders from recovering.

A 2018 Carolina Panthers example used DJ Moore to draw the defense right before Curtis Samuel reversed left. Effective blocking helped Samuel gain yardage and ultimately score. The play exploited man coverage and created traffic that disrupted defenders.

Variations include a fake reverse, in which Arizona quarterback Kyler Murray used multiple fake handoffs and receiver motion to draw away safeties before running behind blockers; a reverse screen, where Purdue moved the ball through several players before throwing a prepared screen behind six blockers; and a reverse pass, where the quarterback handed off, slipped toward the sideline, and received a pass from the reversing receiver for a touchdown.

China criticized a U.S. nuclear strategy report portraying Beijing as a potential adversary, urging Washington to reduce its larger arsenal and promote stability. China said its 300-warhead arsenal is the minimum needed for security and pledged never to use nuclear weapons first. The United States and Russia each possess about 7,000 warheads. Trump’s doctrine ends the Obama administration’s effort to reduce nuclear weapons’ military role while retaining arms-control commitments, including New START limits. Two years after Alaska Airlines acquired Virgin America for $2.6 billion, the airline’s final branded revenue flights will depart San Francisco Tuesday night for Newark and Los Angeles. Fans and frequent fliers planned commemorative events, while Alaska promised surprises for passengers. Virgin America was noted for innovations including mood lighting, spending-based loyalty rewards, fleet-wide Wi-Fi, in-seat power, seat-based ordering, and fresher food.

Overnight, Alaska will remove Virgin America branding at 29 U.S. and Mexican airports and consolidate operations under Alaska’s flight network, website, app, kiosks, computer systems, and call center. Alaska expects a smooth transition after extensive preparation. Some Virgin America aircraft liveries and interiors will remain temporarily, with updates and cabin retrofits expected to be completed by the end of 2019.

IDC identifies visualization, cloud engineering workstations, AR/VR, digital twins, simulations, modeling, and data analytics as important technologies for manufacturing development and new digital business models. Digital twins can monitor products and processes, test scenarios, support quality management, and enable services such as product-as-a-service and outcome-based offerings.

High-performance computing (HPC) addresses increasing calculation complexity, outdated simulations, limited computing capacity, and lengthy iterations. Four out of five surveyed decision makers view HPC as a game changer because it enables complex calculations, faster and more numerous iterations, new applications, and greater innovation and agility. More than a quarter of surveyed enterprises already use professional HPC infrastructure, while 39% are planning or piloting deployment.

Most HPC users favor external infrastructure: 87% use or plan cloud-based external HPC, while 74% operate or plan infrastructure in colocation datacenters. Key challenges include security, investment and licensing costs, energy consumption, sustainability, insufficient computing power, availability, complexity, and limited expertise.

Public and hybrid cloud architectures are expected to become prominent because they offer scalability, flexibility, resilience, and access to modern hardware and methods. HPC as a Service can reduce upfront investment, support pay-as-you-go usage, facilitate global collaboration, and enable HPC-based business models, though skilled personnel remain necessary.

IDC recommends establishing virtual product and manufacturing development, creating a holistic data strategy and single source of truth, selecting HPC operating models according to utilization, budget, performance, flexibility, security, and skills, prioritizing scalability and energy efficiency, and using external expertise where needed. Findings are based on a December 2021 survey of 200 decision makers at industrial enterprises with over 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Texas quarterback Arch Manning has delivered two strong and two poor performances in his first four games as the full-time starter. He completed 61.3% of his passes for 888 yards, nine touchdowns and three interceptions. Counter is a gap run that initially resembles Power in one direction before sending the runner opposite. Typically, the backside guard pulls to kick out the edge defender, while a fullback follows through the created lane to block a linebacker. The scheme exploits aggressive defenses that over-pursue Power action, creates favorable blocking angles, and brings extra blockers to the point of attack.

Its slower development makes it vulnerable to penetration, particularly through the vacated backside B gap. Defenses may also “spill” the play by wrong-arming the pulling guard, forcing the runner outside toward pursuing linebackers and safeties.

Against 3-4 and 4-3 fronts, linemen use back blocks, down blocks, hinges, combinations, and climbs to form the running lane. The fullback counters before following the guard, while the tailback reads the guard’s kick-out or log block. The quarterback fakes Power, hands off in the opposite direction, and boots away; receivers target nearby safeties.

In Singleback GT Counter, the backside tackle replaces the fullback as the linebacker insert blocker, while the fullback secures the backside edge. Gun Split GT Counter adds triple-option reads of the backside edge and alley defenders.

The paper develops a mathematical framework for studying cubic–tetragonal phase coexistence in ferroelectrics using high-resolution single-crystal X-ray diffraction and three-dimensional reciprocal-space mapping. Because pure cubic and tetragonal lattices generally cannot form a mismatch-free interface, the model uses an adaptive state: periodic pairs of tetragonal ferroelastic domains whose averaged lattice can connect coherently to the cubic phase along a habit plane. Unlike conventional adaptive-state models, it does not require domain miniaturization.

The framework derives domain-volume ratios, habit-plane orientations, direct- and reciprocal-lattice orientation relationships, and predicted Bragg-peak separations. Six permissible tetragonal-domain pairings produce 24 possible mismatch-free cubic–adaptive–tetragonal variants. When tetragonal domains diffract independently, each variant produces a three-component split Bragg peak representing the cubic phase and two tetragonal domains.

The model was tested on PMN-35PT near its cubic-to-tetragonal transition at approximately 435 K. The material exhibited phase coexistence over about 4 K, with lattice parameters satisfying a condition that places habit planes along {110} planes and permits domain ratios of 2/3 and 1/3. Reciprocal-space maps measured at 437 K showed strong agreement between predicted and observed peak separations. Peak widths suggested tetragonal domains several hundred nanometers in size, supporting an adaptive-state-like orientation relationship without requiring miniaturized domains.

BA.2.86 carries 33 spike mutations relative to BA.2, distributed across the N-terminal, receptor-binding, and S1/S2–S2 domains. Researchers used pseudovirus neutralization assays and a reverse mutational scanning library of 33 single BA.2.86-to-BA.2 reversions to identify mutations contributing to antibody escape. Plasma came from 30 healthcare workers before and after receiving the BNT162b2 XBB.1.5-adapted booster.

Before the adapted booster, neutralization was reduced approximately 40-fold for BA.2.86 and 80-fold for JN.1 relative to Wuhan-Hu-1. Mutations ins16MPLF, K356T, N460K, V483Δ, A484K, F486P, and P621S contributed to BA.2.86 immune escape. After XBB.1.5-adapted vaccination, neutralization of BA.2.86 and JN.1 increased substantially and reached comparable levels. Removing the MPLF insertion, restoring Y144, and reverting K554E or K484A restored neutralization toward BA.2 levels after boosting.

The authors propose reverse mutational scanning as a method for identifying escape epitopes in highly mutated lineages and polyclonal serum responses. Limitations include reliance on pseudoviruses, uncertain prior infections among participants, cohort immune heterogeneity, and analysis of only single mutations rather than combinations.

The Washington Supreme Court affirmed confirmation of South Bend’s local improvement assessment roll. The city initially estimated $9,500 to fill low and tide lands, anticipating inexpensive material from federal dredging. Changed federal plans required private contractors to complete the fill, increasing the actual cost assessed against benefited property to $89,199.92.

Under the governing statutes, the preliminary estimate served to guide the city council in deciding whether to initiate the improvement. When actual bona fide costs exceeded the estimate, the city could add the difference to the assessment roll after notice and hearing. Because the assessment did not exceed the actual bona fide cost and the increase was explained by changed conditions, it was valid.

The court also held that the ordinance was not indefinite because it contained all material statutory provisions. Evidence supported the assessed benefits, and the proceedings were regular.

Reagan began a two-day campaign tour after announcing his candidacy and competed against President Ford in the 1976 Republican primaries. Ford defeated Reagan on the first convention ballot. Reagan congratulated Ford, pledged party unity, and later urged delegates to promote a platform defending economic and individual freedom while confronting nuclear danger. He argued that future generations’ freedom and survival depended on meeting these challenges and called for unity and victory. In 1979, Georgetown professor Jeane Kirkpatrick’s “Dictatorships & Double Standards” criticized the Carter administration’s foreign policy, citing the planned Panama Canal transfer, Soviet military expansion, stagnant U.S. forces, growing Soviet influence, and declining American standing in the Third World.

A quantitative study examined 90 grade 1–5 mathematics teachers’ perceptions of distance education in UAE schools during 2020–2021. Participants completed a validated 37-item online questionnaire addressing perceptions, obstacles, and future preferences.

Teachers generally reported confidence in using digital technologies, adapting lessons, and presenting mathematical concepts online. However, they considered online teaching more time-consuming, stressful, and workload-intensive, and questioned its suitability and effectiveness for elementary students. Reported challenges included maintaining student communication, motivation, participation, and learning outcomes. Most teachers received adequate school resources, training, and administrative support.

Although 64.4% enjoyed teaching mathematics online, 76.7% preferred face-to-face instruction. Perceptions and obstacles did not differ significantly by gender or experience. Educational level did not affect perceptions, but graduate-qualified teachers reported significantly greater obstacles.

The study recommends expanded professional development, technical and institutional support, strategies for student engagement, improved online assessment and feedback, and exploration of hybrid teaching models. Limitations include the 90-person convenience sample, participants’ relatively strong access to support and resources, and data collection during compulsory pandemic-related online teaching.

The document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for interoperability between guest operating systems and hypervisors supporting SEV-ES or SEV-SNP. These technologies encrypt guest register state during world switches. Automatic Exits require no exposed register state, while Non-Automatic Exits allow guests to selectively share required state through the GHCB.

The GHCB is a 4 KB decrypted page modeled partly on the SEV-ES VMCB save-state area. It limits exposure by providing only information needed to process VMGEXIT operations. The specification covers GHCB establishment, negotiation, layout, protocols, guest exits, SMP booting, interrupts, nested virtualization, restricted injection, and SNP-specific functions.

Version 2 adds initial SEV-SNP support, SEV-ES enhancements, and hypervisor feature advertisement. Later revisions add 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, expanded error reporting, a VLEK certificate GUID, APIC ID retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, SEV-ES page-state changes, restricted-injection IPI and timer requests, and the SEV-SNP Confidential Computing Blob EFI protocol.

The team has created chances but needs stronger net-front presence, quicker reactions to rebounds, and better execution. The opponent is skilled, physical, strong in puck battles and faceoffs, and well-rounded. Improved quality chances and converting opportunities are essential to winning.

Diluted earnings per share rose to $1.52 from $1.40. Growth was led by Services, iPhone and Mac, while iPad sales declined. Gross margin increased to 43.7%.

For the first six months, net sales were $221.2 billion, net income was $59.6 billion and operating cash flow was $75.1 billion. At quarter-end, Apple had $350.7 billion in assets, $283.3 billion in liabilities and $67.4 billion in shareholders’ equity.

Quarterly regional sales increased 19% in the Americas, 5% in Europe and 3% in Greater China; Japan was flat and Rest of Asia Pacific declined 7%. Apple repurchased $22.9 billion of stock and paid $3.6 billion in dividends during the quarter. Apple cited continuing COVID-19-related operational and supply disruptions. Disclosure controls were deemed effective, with no material changes to internal controls, market risks or previously reported risk factors.

The Broncos snapped a league-long 37-game streak without a 100-yard rusher when a player gained 101 yards in a 28-3 win over Cincinnati. Denver outgained the Bengals by 353 yards and improved to 2-2. Their previous 100-yard performance came from Latavius Murray in the 2022 season finale.
