Langmuir probes are conducting tips inserted into plasma to measure current as a function of probe voltage. Because electrons move faster than ions, an unbiased probe initially collects electrons and charges negatively until electron and ion currents balance at the floating potential, which differs from the plasma potential. A sheath forms around a sufficiently negative probe, shielding its perturbation within several Debye lengths.

Using quasi-planar, collisionless sheath theory with cold ions and Maxwellian electrons, probe-surface fluxes can be related to bulk plasma density and electron temperature. The current–voltage characteristic includes electron saturation, a transition region near the floating potential, and ion saturation. Sweeping voltage near the floating potential allows electron temperature to be inferred from the slope of the electron-current characteristic; the ion saturation current can then provide density. Operating near the floating potential limits heating and avoids regimes where the theory is less reliable, though uncertainty in ion saturation and finite sweep time restrict accuracy and temporal resolution.

A double probe uses two mutually biased tips, forcing current entering one to leave through the other. Its current follows a hyperbolic-tangent dependence on bias voltage and cannot exceed the ion saturation current, reducing the risk of melting, but it still requires voltage sweeping. A triple probe adds a floating tip, providing three simultaneous points on the current–voltage curve. This enables density and temperature measurements without sweeping and improves time resolution, but assumes the chosen curve model is accurate.

Practical complications include sheath-area changes, probe heating, probe interference, collisions, and magnetic fields. Magnetic fields alter particle orbits and presheath geometry, while collisions modify particle flux through diffusion; both require more advanced sheath models.
The player credited a fortunate goal to shooting through traffic, emphasized staying positive and confident during struggles, and acknowledged his father’s essential support.

The turn-of-the-month strategy buys at the close of the fifth-last trading day and sells at the close of the third trading day of the next month, producing roughly 33% market exposure. In S&P 500 backtests since 1960, it achieved a 7.1% compounded annual growth rate, outperformed buy-and-hold without dividend adjustments, and had smaller, shorter drawdowns. Returns outside this period were poor.

The effect also appeared across several international markets, sectors, Bitcoin, commodities, real estate, high-yield funds, and gold miners, though it was weak or nonexistent in gold and more erratic in technology stocks and commodities. Possible causes include saver capital inflows and fund rebalancing, but the reason is uncertain.

Tests indicate that the final trading day is the weakest of the last seven trading days, while calendar day 31 averaged a 0.1% gain versus 0.04% for a random day. Calendar dates and trading days differ, requiring appropriate coding. Some tests used Fidelity funds as long-history proxies rather than recommended trading instruments. The article provides backtesting resources and related Python code, while warning that the code was originally written for another strategy.

CompareCards highlights credit cards offering introductory 0% APR periods of 12–21 months for purchases or balance transfers, along with cash-back, travel-reward, and sign-up offers. Featured cards from Discover, Bank of America, Citi, Capital One, and others provide varying rewards, including up to 6% cash back in selected categories, unlimited flat-rate rewards, travel points, and bonuses worth roughly $200–$300. Many have no annual fee, while standard variable APRs and balance-transfer fees apply after promotional periods.

The site notes that low-interest cards can reduce borrowing costs, but promotional rates eventually revert to regular APRs. Fixed APRs remain relatively stable, while variable APRs generally track benchmark rates. Cardholders who pay balances fully and on time usually benefit most. CompareCards says its rankings use a data-driven review of more than 100 cards from over 50 issuers, and that issuer compensation does not affect ratings. Applicants should verify current terms through the card issuer.

The study developed a structured Patient Report Template (PRT) to streamline electronic health record use and improve nursing handoffs. Based on SBAR and I PASS the BATON, the PRT organizes patient profile, review of systems, situation, safety, background, actions, timing, ownership, and next steps. Large language models are proposed as a potential means of summarizing clinical notes into this format.

A survey distributed to University of Iowa Health Care nurses assessed the template’s perceived usefulness and attitudes toward AI. Feedback from 106 nurses generally rated PRT components as useful. Patient identification, code status, chief complaint, medications, allergies, safety alerts, care responsibility, required actions, and escalation signs received particularly strong ratings. Level of uncertainty, family history, rationale for actions, coordination, and some review-of-systems categories received lower but generally positive ratings.

Nurses reported low comfort with and trust in AI-generated reports, averaging 2.38 and 2.5 on five-point scales, while expected utility averaged 3. Respondents represented varied departments, ages, and experience levels, though over half had ten or fewer years of nursing experience.

The findings suggest the PRT could support clearer information transfer, reduce charting burden, and improve patient safety. However, the study measured anticipated usefulness rather than actual clinical use and was limited to one health system. Future research should test usability, accuracy, adaptability, and AI-generated reports in clinical settings. The research is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed.

A Gallup-Walton Family Foundation survey found that more than one-quarter of U.S. public school teachers lack essential materials or staffing support, reducing job satisfaction. Nearly two-thirds reported shortages of teaching assistants, aides, paraprofessionals or behavior specialists, while 62% lacked sufficient mental health resources or special educators.

Although 72% said they had necessary teaching equipment, 24% lacked adequate furniture, 25% lacked computers and 35% lacked printing supplies. One-third described ordering materials as difficult. Technology shortages were more prevalent in low-income schools, while staffing and furniture shortages affected schools across income levels.

Among teachers with adequate resources, 77% were satisfied at work, compared with 44% of those without them. About half said professional development was not based on student needs. Teachers valued collaborative planning and classroom observation, but only one-third had opportunities to observe colleagues. Gallup surveyed roughly 2,000 teachers during each of three periods in the 2024-25 school year.

A physically strong, smart hockey player delivered another solid game. The team played better in the first and third periods but needed more aggression and chance creation. Physical confrontations are part of the game; players should avoid retaliation, distractions, and complaints about officiating.

Logging varies across systems in levels, destinations, and structured formats, creating problems for containerized applications and log aggregation. Adapter containers can redirect file-based logs to stdout and transform diverse formats into a consistent representation with appropriate timestamps. While developers may modify their own applications, adapters are often cheaper and easier to maintain, share, and reuse when working with third-party container images.

High-performance computing (HPC), cloud technologies, visualization, AR/VR, and digital twins can accelerate industrial development, improve collaboration, reduce material use and emissions, and enable new products, services, and business models. Digital twins allow detailed monitoring, analysis, and simulation of products and processes; Bridgestone reports virtual tire development can reduce development time by up to 50%.

Manufacturers face growing computational demands as simulations become more complex. Forty-two percent use outdated or inaccurate simulations, while half report that calculations take too long. Demand for high-performance calculations is expected to rise sharply. HPC addresses these issues through parallel processing, specialized architectures, faster memory, and improved connectivity, enabling more complex, frequent, and accurate analyses. Eighty-one percent of surveyed decision makers consider HPC a game changer, rising to 96% among enterprises already using it. More than a quarter already use professional HPC infrastructure, while 39% are planning or piloting deployment.

Most users prefer external infrastructure: 87% use or plan cloud-based HPC, 74% use or plan colocation facilities, and 43% engage or plan to engage research institutions. Only 6% currently operate on-premises HPC, though 28% plan to within two years.

Key challenges include security concerns, cited by 72%; high energy consumption and sustainability, cited by 58%; costs, performance limitations, availability, scalability, infrastructure complexity, and skills shortages. Forty-two percent report insufficient expertise, and 39% expect eventually to need external support.

Public cloud is expected to become the leading HPC architecture, followed by hybrid cloud models. Cloud-based HPC offers scalable peak performance, flexibility, access to current technologies, and potential cost advantages through operating-expense or usage-based billing. Hybrid architectures can retain sensitive workloads on premises while shifting peaks or noncritical tasks to public cloud resources.

HPC as a Service can support global collaboration, shared data environments, scalable engineering workstations, and HPC-based commercial services. Among existing HPC users, 81% intend to develop HPC-based business models. However, cloud HPC still requires skilled personnel to configure systems, program calculations, and interpret results.
The patent depicts a color animated graphical interface with three sequential images; broken-line screen elements and transition timing are unclaimed.

Eight major oil companies showed improving financial and operating trends through the second quarter of 2017, suggesting they can sustain profitability near $50 per barrel. Aggregate revenues, oil prices, cash flows, margins, and production rose from 2016 lows, though revenues remained below 2015 levels. From 2Q15 to 2Q17, aggregate oil production increased 5.3%, natural gas production 9.7%, and combined production 7.2%.

Operating cash flow improved while upstream capital spending declined, raising net operating cash flow; all eight companies reported positive NOCF in 2Q17. Chevron and Statoil recorded particularly strong improvements in return on sales. Declining inventories and a narrowing gap between global supply and demand also indicated gradual market rebalancing. The author expects these positive trends to strengthen in late 2017 and continue into 2018, provided companies maintain disciplined spending and project selection.

Fifteen Sacred Heart Academy students and five chaperones spent spring break in Alajuelita, a poor neighborhood of San Jose, Costa Rica. The mission trip combined Spanish practice with community service and relationship-building. Students played games, sang songs, and shared meals with local children, visited a senior center, and worked alongside experienced American missionaries. They also hiked La Cruz de Alajuelita. Participants said their Spanish improved and that they gained appreciation for the language, local residents, and the value of caring for others. Spanish teacher April Dice described watching the students grow and help others as rewarding and expressed interest in future trips.

The Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly passed the Rs 95,666.97 crore budget for 2018-19, a 20 per cent increase, through a voice vote. The budget includes Rs 51,244.72 crore in revenue expenditure and Rs 44,422.24 crore in capital expenditure. The appropriation bill introduces reforms requiring timely fund releases, detailed classification of plan allocations, mandatory use of BEAMS for payments, and procurement planning within 60 days. It prioritizes state shares of centrally sponsored schemes, utility shifting and land compensation under PMDP projects. It also prohibits departments from hiring new casual or need-based workers.

The speaker expects a close, physical series between disciplined, similarly constructed teams with strong goaltending, solid lines and comparable styles. The opening game may be a feeling-out period, while special teams could decide the series. He argues that disciplined, positional hockey remains exciting and attributes lower scoring to excellent goaltending rather than limited chances.

Success requires avoiding penalties against Dallas’s strong power play, effective penalty killing and contributions from the entire team. Veteran experience and leadership are advantages, but games must still be won on the ice. The team intends to maintain its own physical style rather than adjust to its opponent.

The speaker views coaching as a continual learning process and says self-questioning supports improvement without indicating doubt in his abilities. Following a prolonged slump and coaching change, greater discipline helped the team grow stronger and closer throughout the playoffs. A forceful team address was delivered because players were underperforming and immediate action was needed. He also emphasizes the difficulty of winning repeatedly, the value of the Stanley Cup, and the important contributions made by rookies and other players throughout the roster.

The Imperial German Government asks neutral governments to convey its response to the rejection of the Central Powers’ December 12 peace proposal. It denies that the offer was insincere, asserting that immediate negotiations could achieve a just peace and prevent further bloodshed. Germany attributes the war to British, French, Russian, and Serbian policies and actions, while claiming the Central Powers fought defensively. It accuses the adversaries of pursuing territorial conquest, refusing to examine the peace offer or make counterproposals, applying principles of nationality and freedom inconsistently, and violating international law through maritime restrictions, pressure on neutrals, starvation tactics, colonial troops, prisoner mistreatment, and civilian deportations.

SD card reads use clock-synchronous, CRC-protected block transfers up to 512 bytes. CMD17 reads one block; CMD18 continuously reads consecutive blocks until CMD12 stops transmission. Read commands are rejected for block-length or address errors. Power loss during reads does not destroy data, except during host-issued write or erase operations. Partial blocks must remain within 512-byte boundaries.

PATCH combines preferential attachment, triadic closure, and homophily to study segregation, degree inequality, and group inequity in growing networks. Simulations show homophily primarily drives segregation and inequity, while preferential attachment drives degree inequality. Unbiased triadic closure generally moderates segregation and inequity, whereas biased triadic closure has context-dependent effects and often increases degree inequality. The group with greater visibility also tends to have greater internal inequality, meaning its advantage benefits relatively few nodes.

Applied to five decades of physics and computer-science collaboration and citation networks, likelihood-free inference finds that observed gender inequalities are best reproduced when both global and friends-of-friends links are biased by popularity and moderate gender homophily. Women remain underrepresented and generally disadvantaged in visibility. The findings suggest that reducing multiple network inequalities requires addressing homophily, preferential attachment, and triadic closure together, because changing one mechanism alone may create trade-offs or unintended consequences.

Researchers found that dandelion seeds detach far more easily when pulled upward at an angle than downward or straight out, helping them favor upward gusts and avoid downward flights. Imaging revealed an off-center tether surrounded by horseshoe-shaped shielding at each seed’s attachment point. The structure supports the seed unless force tilts it toward the horseshoe’s open side, where the tether is overwhelmed and the seed lifts off. Tests showed downward removal required about ten times more force than upward-slanting release.

The Rotary Club of Greenwich awarded Greenwich United Way a $5,000 grant for its Reading Champions program. The funding will support tutor supplies, books, and year-end awards for participating children.

The Supreme Court announced that Collegium recommendations on judicial appointments, transfers and elevations, along with reasons for selections and rejections, will be published online when sent to the government. The move follows criticism from lawyers, judicial bodies and Justice Chelameswar over the Collegium’s lack of transparency. Reasons for October 2017 recommendations to the Madras and Kerala High Courts have already been posted under “Collegium Resolutions,” though Chief Justice Dipak Misra’s decision has also drawn criticism from parts of the judicial community.

MAFLD affects 32.4% of the global population and is more prevalent among people with type 2 diabetes (T2D), who face increased risks of advanced liver disease, cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and liver-related mortality. African evidence remains limited despite rising diabetes and metabolic disease burdens.

This systematic review assessed MAFLD prevalence and its association with HbA1c among African adults with T2D. Registered with PROSPERO and conducted under PRISMA guidelines, it searched major and African-specific databases through December 6, 2023. Eligible observational studies involved adults with T2D in African countries and reported diagnosable MAFLD prevalence. Two reviewers independently selected studies and extracted data, while quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Random-effects meta-analysis was planned for prevalence and pooled correlations with HbA1c.

Of 659 references identified, 10 studies involving 1,667 participants were included. Nine were cross-sectional and one was case-control, spanning Nigeria, Ethiopia, Morocco, Egypt, Ghana, and Sudan. Participants were predominantly female, generally older than 50, and commonly overweight or obese with poor glycemic control. MAFLD was diagnosed mainly by ultrasonography, with some studies using the Fatty Liver Index or Hepatic Steatosis Index.

Drug addiction has high overdose mortality and treatment dropout, especially in opioid addiction. Traditional measures such as self-reports and urine toxicology have limitations, including reporting bias, reduced insight, social desirability, treatment-stage sensitivity, and inability to capture dynamic use patterns. Prior research suggests objective cognitive-behavioral measures—particularly tasks assessing drug-biased attention, choice, language, and executive functioning—may better predict drug use, relapse, abstinence, and treatment retention.

This study tested whether picture-choice and verbal-fluency measures of drug bias predicted four-month treatment adherence among inpatients with opioid use disorder (iOUD) better than demographics, self-reported drug use, and craving. Follow-up attendance after a randomized treatment component served as the clinical endpoint. Researchers hypothesized that iOUD participants would show greater drug-biased choice and fluency than healthy controls, that these measures would better inform treatment completion, and, exploratorily, that drug-biased behavior would decline at follow-up.

Participants were 59 residential-treatment inpatients with iOUD and 29 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. All provided informed consent, and the inpatients received relapse prevention, anger management, Seeking Safety therapy, and other counseling services.

Hurricane Irma threatened five major U.S. Atlantic agricultural ports after devastating the eastern Caribbean. Nearly half of U.S. poultry exports transit these ports, led by Savannah at 32% and Jacksonville at 9%. Other notable shares include Jacksonville beer at 25%, Miami grapefruit at 31%, and Norfolk soybean oil at 18%.

The TLV321x and TLV322x are single-, dual-, and quad-channel high-speed comparators operating from 1.8V to 5V over –40°C to 125°C. They provide 40ns propagation delay, 40µA quiescent current per channel, rail-to-rail inputs extending 200mV beyond each supply rail, low offset, and 1.8mV internal hysteresis.

TLV321x devices use push-pull outputs capable of sourcing and sinking current to drive capacitive loads such as MOSFET gates. TLV322x devices use open-drain outputs that support pullups from 0V to 5.5V, logic-level translation, and wired-OR connections. A power-on-reset circuit holds outputs low until the supply crosses 1.65V and a delay of up to 32µs expires.

Input clamp current must be limited to 10mA, with series resistance recommended for transients or faults. Unused input pairs require at least 50mV differential voltage and must not be tied together. Proper high-speed PCB layout, close 0.1µF supply bypassing, and minimized input-output coupling are recommended. Applications include current sensing, zero-cross detection, and other speed-critical circuits; external hysteresis can reduce noise-induced output chatter.

Source Energy Services seeks about C$250 million in an IPO valuing it near C$1 billion as oil drilling revives. Proceeds would fund a Wisconsin facility acquisition, debt reduction and capital spending. The TriWest-backed fracking sand distributor operates in Western Canada, North Dakota and Texas.

Numerous professional boxers entered mixed martial arts with mixed results. Holly Holm was the clearest success, becoming UFC bantamweight champion by knocking out Ronda Rousey. James Toney lost his sole MMA fight to Randy Couture, while Art Jimmerson was submitted by Royce Gracie at UFC 1. Ray Mercer, Heather Hardy and Mia St. John each won their only MMA appearance, with Mercer knocking out Tim Sylvia. Eric “Butterbean” Esch compiled a 15-10 MMA record after a lengthy boxing career. Ricardo Mayorga went winless, recording one no decision and three losses. Ana Julaton finished 2-2 after twice winning a boxing title. Marcus Davis and Chris Lytle built substantial MMA careers but never challenged for major titles. Most other crossover fighters achieved limited or sporadic success.

This preprint used ultra-short-echo 7-tesla magnetic resonance spectroscopy to compare 16 metabolites in the occipital and dorsomedial prefrontal cortices of 43 healthy controls, 42 first-degree biological relatives of people with psychosis, and 64 people with psychotic psychopathology. Methods incorporated macromolecule signals, tissue composition corrections, and modeling intended to reduce quantification errors. Six metabolites—GABA, glutamate, glutamine, glutathione, N-acetyl-aspartate (NAA), and N-acetyl-aspartylglutamate (NAAG)—were selected for primary analyses.

Occipital NAA was significantly lower in people with psychosis and relatives than in controls. After adjustment for age, sex, and body mass index, the difference remained significant for people with psychosis but not relatives. Prefrontal NAAG was lower in people with psychosis, although this difference was not significant after demographic adjustment. No significant primary group differences were found for GABA, glutamate, glutamine, or glutathione.

Post hoc analyses found significantly higher prefrontal glucose in people with psychosis than controls, with relatives showing intermediate values; a similar occipital pattern did not remain significant after multiple-comparison correction. Age, sex, body mass index, tissue composition, and antipsychotic medication levels did not appear sufficient to explain the glucose differences. Hierarchical clustering associated higher glucose in both regions with greater psychiatric symptoms and abnormalities in visual-task performance. No examined metabolite differed significantly between participants with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.

Repeat scans in subsets of controls and people with psychosis showed fair-to-excellent longitudinal reliability across metabolites. The authors concluded that the findings indicate metabolic dysfunction across brain regions in people with psychosis and, to a lesser extent, their relatives. Limitations included demographic differences, transdiagnostic sampling, limited repeat-scan data, and participant selection requirements. The research has not been peer reviewed and should not guide clinical practice.

CMD6, mandatory for SD cards Version 1.10 and later, checks or switches functions while the card is in Transfer State. Hosts should verify support through SCR or CSD. CMD6 supports six function groups with sixteen functions each; Function 0 is default and 0xF preserves the current selection. Mode 0 reports supported functions, readiness, and maximum current or power, while Mode 1 performs switching. Invalid selections cancel switching, and busy functions cannot be changed. CMD6 returns R1 plus a 512-bit status block and has a 100 ms timeout. Function changes take effect within eight clocks. Power cycling, CMD0, or selecting defaults restores default functions.

Function groups control access mode, command-system extensions, UHS-I driver strength, and power limits. The default power limit is 0.72 W; hosts may increase it according to supply, thermal, and connector capabilities to enable higher performance. Hosts should query power requirements with CMD6 Mode 0 before switching. UHS-II requires Function Group 4, does not use Groups 1 and 3, and optionally supports Group 2.

High-Speed mode, optionally supported by Version 1.10 and later cards, provides a 25 MB/s interface using a 50 MHz clock and requires a one-to-one host-card connection. Command-system switching changes how reserved commands CMD34–37, CMD50, and CMD57 are interpreted.

CMD8 initializes Version 2.00 or later cards by checking host voltage and echoing a check pattern in R7. SDSC uses byte addressing and configurable block lengths; SDHC and SDXC use 512-byte block addressing and fixed 512-byte memory-access blocks.

Hosts may vary or stop the bus clock, but must supply eight clocks after transactions. CRC7 protects commands and most responses; CRC16 protects data blocks, separately on each data line in wide-bus mode. Invalid or CRC-failed commands do not execute and set status errors.

Read timeout guidance is generally 100 ms. Write busy is normally limited to 250 ms, though specified SDXC cases may reach 500 ms; implementations are strongly encouraged to allow more than 500 ms. UHS-II data bursts may remain busy for up to one second. Erase timeout should use SD Status parameters when available.

Commands are fixed 48-bit codewords and are organized into command classes. Classes 0, 2, 4, 5, and 8 are mandatory; additional requirements depend on card type and features. Responses include R1/R1b, R2, R3, R6, and R7. Cards provide Card Status, 512-bit SD Status, and, in command-queue mode, Task Status.

Performance classifications include Speed Classes 2, 4, 6, and 10; UHS Speed Grades 1 and 3; and Video Speed Classes 6, 10, 30, 60, and 90. These methods are optional in Version 6.00. Performance is organized around Allocation Units and Recording Units. SDSC/SDHC fragmented-write performance considers write and move performance, while SDXC and UHS grades require sequential writing to entirely free allocation units and treat move performance as zero. CMD20 supports optimized Speed Class recording, directory updates, and Continuous Information updates; it is mandatory for SDXC and optional for SDHC. UHS Speed Grade 1 requires at least 10 MB/s, and Grade 3 requires at least 30 MB/s.

The device uses Microsoft WM-DRM to protect licensed content. If its security is compromised, Microsoft may revoke its ability to obtain new licenses, though unprotected content remains playable.
