Users may not modify, reverse engineer, decompile, rent, separate, embed, or disclose the software or its proprietary information. Permitted copies must remain unmodified and include all notices and the agreement.

The software is provided “as is” without warranties. SanDisk and its licensors disclaim liability for indirect or consequential damages, and total liability cannot exceed the amount paid for the software. The license may be terminated for violations, requiring destruction of all copies. The software is unsuitable for hazardous, fail-safe applications.

The agreement is governed by California and U.S. federal law, with disputes heard in Santa Clara County. Export controls apply. The device must not be discarded with unsorted household waste; users should consult local collection authorities.

The discrete-time Fourier transform converges when a sequence is absolutely summable. The Z-transform generalizes it by exponentially weighting the sequence:
\[
X(z)=\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}x[n]z^{-n},\quad z=re^{j\omega}.
\]
On the unit circle, \(z=e^{j\omega}\), it equals the Fourier transform. Its region of convergence (ROC) contains values of \(z\) for which \(x[n]r^{-n}\) is absolutely summable.

For \(x[n]=(1/2)^n u[n]\), \(X(z)=z/(z-1/2)\) with ROC \(|z|>1/2\), so the Fourier transform exists. The left-sided sequence \(-(1/2)^n u[-n-1]\) has the same algebraic expression but ROC \(|z|<1/2\), so its Fourier transform does not exist. Thus, a Z-transform requires both its formula and ROC.

For rational Z-transforms, numerator roots are zeros and denominator roots are poles; the ROC contains no poles and is bounded by poles, zero, or infinity. Right-sided sequences have an ROC outside the outermost pole, left-sided sequences inside the innermost relevant pole, and two-sided sequences between poles. A Fourier transform exists when the ROC includes the unit circle.

The Z-transform converts convolution into multiplication. For systems, the transform of the unit-sample response is the system function. Stability requires its ROC to include the unit circle, while causality requires a right-sided impulse response and an ROC outside the outermost pole. Difference equations may therefore represent different systems depending on the specified ROC, stability, or causality.

House appropriators proposed $661.3 billion in FY02 discretionary spending, largely following President Bush’s priorities but increasing Labor-HHS, VA-HUD, and Energy and Water funding. Appropriations leaders also planned to keep the FY01 supplemental near Bush’s requested level despite calls for more military spending.

House Republican leaders said Democratic control of the Senate was unlikely to improve House bipartisanship and could free Republicans to advance energy, prescription drug, campaign finance, tax, patients’ rights, and trade legislation. Democrats maintained that Republicans had not meaningfully consulted them.

Rep. Steve Largent announced he would resign Nov. 29 to focus on running for Oklahoma governor and requested an early special election. Rep. Asa Hutchinson’s expected confirmation as Drug Enforcement Administration chief could leave business-backed liability legislation without its principal House sponsor.

Labor Secretary Elaine Chao scheduled public ergonomics forums for July and planned a policy direction by September. Republicans welcomed the review, while Democrats urged adoption of a new workplace rule.

FDA officials warned that roughly two million mailed parcels containing regulated products enter the United States annually, overwhelming inspection capacity and exposing consumers to potentially unsafe or counterfeit drugs. Separately, the House Energy and Commerce Committee considered adding generic-drug patent reforms to Medicare prescription drug legislation.

European officials said Bush’s steel-import investigation and rejection of the Kyoto Protocol would complicate the upcoming EU-U.S. summit, while expressing concern about U.S. unilateralism.

Senate Republicans developed proposed assurances for prompt consideration of Bush nominees as negotiations continued over a new organizing resolution. Bush planned to nominate Jo Anne Barnhart to a six-year term as Social Security commissioner.

Republican Census Monitoring Board members defended the accuracy of the 2000 census and questioned statistical sampling. House lawmakers introduced legislation requiring public consultation and congressional approval for presidential monuments exceeding 50,000 acres. An aviation hearing was scheduled to review airline customer-service improvements.

Ashby Fields Primary School in Daventry is consulting parents on closing at 1.15pm on Fridays, reducing its weekly timetable by two hours, to give teachers development time and improve work-life balance, recruitment and retention. Parent Kelly Holmes objected, citing limited, paid on-site childcare, disruption for working parents and concerns about lost teaching time. The school said governors will review feedback before deciding whether to develop a formal proposal for consideration by the InMat Trust Board. Results are expected in May.

CompareCards lists partner credit cards offering introductory 0% APR periods, typically 12–21 months, for purchases or balance transfers. Featured cards provide cash back, travel points or miles, welcome bonuses, and benefits such as no annual or foreign transaction fees. Offers include Discover cashback matching, Bank of America customizable rewards and travel points, Citi cash back and balance-transfer promotions, Capital One travel and cash rewards, and cards earning bonus points in selected spending categories. Eligibility, transfer fees, spending caps and post-promotional variable APRs vary. Introductory rates eventually revert to standard rates, while variable APRs may change with prevailing interest rates. CompareCards says its editors use a data-driven system to evaluate more than 100 cards from over 50 issuers. The site receives compensation from listed companies but states this does not affect ratings or reviews; applicants should verify current terms before applying.

Michael Coren argues that opposition to sex education, often organized by conservative religious groups, stems from misunderstanding, fear and cultural taboos. He says modern curricula reduce shame about sexuality, including same-sex attraction, teach bodily autonomy, and help children recognize and report abuse. While acknowledging parents’ role, Coren maintains that schools support families by providing education parents may not adequately offer. He urges Christians to view social change with greater trust and openness.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 include zero-wait-state SRAM retained in RUN, SLEEP, STOP, and STANDBY modes, with 1KB write-protection resolution. They support up to 45 GPIO pins, configurable IOMUX routing, wake-up functions, and input filtering.

Analog features include a 12-bit ADC operating up to 1.6 Msps with external reference, internal temperature and supply-monitoring channels, selectable 1.4V or 2.5V references, an internally connected calibrated temperature sensor, and a comparator with wake-up, timer fault handling, and an 8-bit reference DAC.

The low-frequency subsystem contains an RTC and independent watchdog. Communications include three UARTs with LIN support, I2C up to 1 Mbps with SMBus 3.0 support, and SPI up to 16 Mbit/s. UART, I2C, and SPI provide separate transmit and receive FIFOs supporting DMA transfers.

Supervision and timing functions include an independent watchdog that generates a power-on reset, a windowed watchdog supporting reset, interrupt, and interval modes, and a 32kHz RTC with calendar, alarms, periodic interrupts, calibration, and temperature-drift compensation. General-purpose and advanced 16-bit timers support prescaling, synchronization, peripheral triggering, PWM, capture/compare, and fault handling.

Security and debug capabilities include configurable code and data firewalls, CRC-16, Arm-compatible two-wire SWD, configurable peripheral behavior during debug, a debug mailbox, SWD lockout, and password-authenticated debugging. Read-only factory memory stores device capabilities, identifiers, and calibration data.

TI recommends 10µF and 0.1µF low-ESR ceramic decoupling capacitors near VDD/VSS, a 47kΩ pullup and 1000pF pulldown capacitor on NRST, required crystal capacitors where applicable, and pullups for 5V-tolerant open-drain outputs. Experimental “X” devices are intended only for internal evaluation, while “MSP” devices are fully qualified for production. The September 2025 revision updated specifications and identification tables, removed DGS32 package information, revised ADC ENOB information, and added the debug subsystem section.

The Tenth Circuit affirmed the INS’s reinstatement of Alejandro Mendez Suarez’s 1996 exclusion and deportation order. Suarez, a Mexican citizen, had attempted entry with counterfeit documents, was deported, and unlawfully reentered in 1999. After his 2002 arrest in Colorado, the INS reinstated the prior order.

The court held that the district court properly transferred Suarez’s habeas petition because it was effectively a request for appellate review of the reinstatement order. His pending state criminal charges and bond conditions did not prevent reinstatement, which required only a prior removal order, previous removal, and unlawful reentry.

Applying the reinstatement statute was not impermissibly retroactive because Suarez unlawfully reentered after the statute became effective. The record also contradicted his assertion that he had voluntarily departed, though such a departure under an exclusion order would still constitute removal.

Suarez was ineligible for adjustment of status because his prior attempt to gain admission through misrepresentation made him inadmissible. The court lacked jurisdiction to review the original deportation proceeding. It declined to decide his constitutional challenge to the reinstatement procedure because he could not show prejudice: he did not dispute the prior exclusion order or his unlawful reentry, so additional process would not have changed the outcome.

Chinese 11-year-olds were asked to determine a ship captain’s age from the presence of 26 sheep and 10 goats onboard. Pupils and adults offered varied answers, but the Shunqing Education Department confirmed the problem had no correct solution. It was intended to encourage individual thinking, with different responses reflecting different personalities.

Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) affects an estimated 5–15% of reproductive-aged women and is associated with metabolic, reproductive, cardiovascular, and mental health disorders. This study systematically reviewed controlled observational research through July 2021 and conducted random-effects meta-analyses to estimate PCOS-associated anxiety, depression, eating disorders, postpartum depression, and related U.S. healthcare costs.

Among 25 included studies, women with PCOS had higher prevalences of anxiety (prevalence ratio [PR] 1.42), depression (PR 1.65), and eating disorders (PR 1.48) than age-matched controls. Postpartum depression was not significantly associated with PCOS (PR 1.20) and was excluded from economic calculations. Estimated excess cases attributable to PCOS were 216,248 for anxiety, 262,176 for depression, and 48,764 for eating disorders.

In 2021 U.S. dollars, annual excess direct healthcare costs were estimated at $1.939 billion for anxiety, $1.678 billion for depression, and $644 million for eating disorders, totaling approximately $4.261 billion. Mental health disorders represented about 28% of the estimated annual direct PCOS burden, which exceeded $15 billion. Publication-bias adjustment preserved significant associations for anxiety and depression but not eating disorders, indicating less robust evidence for the latter.

Limitations included few eligible studies, inclusion of non-U.S. studies in the meta-analysis despite U.S.-based cost estimates, and exclusion of some PCOS-associated mental disorders. The estimates also omitted indirect productivity losses and intangible quality-of-life costs. The findings support improved PCOS detection, clinical attention to associated mental health conditions, and increased research investment.

Apple reported fiscal Q1 2024 net sales of $119.6 billion, up 2% year over year, and net income of $33.9 billion, up from $30.0 billion. Diluted earnings per share rose to $2.18 from $1.88, while gross margin increased to 45.9% from 43.0%. iPhone sales grew 6% to $69.7 billion and Services rose 11% to $23.1 billion; iPad and Wearables, Home and Accessories declined 25% and 11%, respectively. Regional sales increased in the Americas, Europe, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific, but fell 13% in Greater China.

Operating cash flow was $39.9 billion. Apple repurchased $20.5 billion of stock and paid $3.8 billion in dividends and equivalents. At December 30, 2023, it held $40.8 billion in cash and equivalents, $131.8 billion in marketable securities, and $106.0 billion in term debt. Total assets were $353.5 billion and shareholders’ equity was $74.1 billion.

Apple disclosed App Store litigation with Epic Games, an import dispute involving certain Apple Watch models, regulatory risks related to App Store changes and the EU Digital Markets Act, and ongoing antitrust investigations. Management concluded disclosure controls were effective, with no material changes to internal controls or market risk.

President Theodore Roosevelt proclaimed September 19, 1901, the day of President McKinley’s burial, a national day of mourning and prayer. He urged Americans to gather in places of worship to honor McKinley’s life, courage, and service and to grieve his assassination.

On March 7, 2018, NVIDIA’s Compensation Committee adopted its fiscal 2019 Variable Compensation Plan. Eligible executive officers may receive cash awards based on achievement of specified fiscal 2019 revenue goals at threshold, base, and stretch levels. Participants generally must remain employed through the payment date. Base-plan target awards are: CEO Jen-Hsun Huang, $1.1 million (110% of salary); CFO Colette Kress, $300,000 (33%); Ajay Puri, $650,000 (68%); Debora Shoquist, $250,000 (29%); and Timothy Teter, $250,000 (29%). NVIDIA’s fiscal 2019 ends January 27, 2019.

A collection of October 23, 2001 reports describes intensifying pressure on Enron. A securities class action alleged Enron and its executives misrepresented operations and overstated results between January 2000 and October 2001. The SEC sought information about transactions with partnerships managed by CFO Andrew Fastow after Enron announced $1.01 billion in third-quarter charges and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. Enron shares fell sharply, while insiders reportedly sold more than $73 million in stock during the class period.

Enron sought a $750 million Citigroup loan amid possible debt downgrades and concerns about its reliance on commercial paper, complex off-balance-sheet financing, asset sales and partnership obligations. Executives said the company had sufficient credit, but provided limited additional detail during an investor call. Many analysts retained positive ratings, citing Enron’s core trading business, while investors questioned management credibility, disclosure practices and potential investment-banking conflicts.

A Texas Monthly article traces Enron’s transformation from a pipeline company into a dominant energy trader under Kenneth Lay and Jeffrey Skilling. It credits innovation, deregulation and aggressive recruiting while describing subjective accounting, intense internal competition, rapid employee turnover and emphasis on short-term profits. Enron later faced problems involving California electricity, overseas projects, broadband investments, accounting scrutiny and Skilling’s resignation.

Separate reports say AES asked India’s prime minister to address alleged interference, contract violations, intimidation and unpaid bills involving its operations in Orissa. AES warned that unresolved disputes could weaken foreign-investor confidence and said its commitment to remaining in India was being tested.

Resource Generation (RG) is a 20-year-old nonprofit helping about 500 wealthy Americans ages 18 to 35 examine the origins and advantages of their wealth and direct it toward grassroots movements addressing social, economic and racial injustice. Through 17 chapters, RG encourages members to share their “money stories,” learn budgeting and accountable giving, evaluate organizations, and campaign for structural changes involving taxes, health care and workers’ rights.

RG does not pool or distribute members’ money. Instead, it promotes principles that give communities affected by injustice greater control over spending decisions. Executive director Iimay Ho argues that voluntary philanthropy cannot replace economic restructuring and may preserve wealthy donors’ power.

Members including Emily Bookstein, Adam Roberts, Elizabeth Baldwin and Hanna Mahon significantly increased their giving after joining RG. Mahon’s family foundation now supports organizations led by people of color, while Baldwin has worked to strengthen RG’s inclusion and support for anti-racist groups.

RG’s work responds to widening U.S. wealth inequality, inherited wealth and racial disparities. Supporters acknowledge contradictions in wealthy people fighting inequality but argue that openly recognizing structural advantages can motivate them to use their money and influence for change.

Williams Jones & Associates reduced its Star Bulk Carriers stake by 52.6% in the second quarter, retaining 31,600 shares worth $311,000. Other investors, including Goldman Sachs, Citadel and Impala Asset Management, increased holdings, while GLG Partners and Capital Fund Management bought new stakes. Institutional investors owned 75.03% of the stock. Star Bulk shares opened at $10.28, with a $651.91 million market capitalization and a 52-week range of $4.04 to $13.40. Analysts’ consensus rating was “Buy,” with a $12.80 average target. Star Bulk operates an international fleet of dry bulk carriers, comprising 73 vessels as of December 31, 2016.

The government imposed quarantine and poultry-movement restrictions within a 7-kilometer radius of San Luis, Pampanga, after a bird flu outbreak. Workers were scheduled to cull infected chickens, while a temporary ban on fowl shipments from Luzon and local quarantine measures aimed to prevent further spread. Agriculture Secretary Manny Piñol said the detected H5 strain was not transmissible to humans, though samples were sent to Australia to test for H5N6. Health officials described human infection as remote, advised proper precautions and said properly cooked chicken is safe. Epidemiologists were deployed to monitor farm workers and test those showing symptoms.

A May 16, 2001 media roundup highlights Enron-related energy developments. Reports scrutinized the Bush energy task force’s private consultations, including meetings between Vice President Cheney and Enron chairman Kenneth Lay, while environmental and consumer groups criticized limited access. Texaco considered an offshore Louisiana LNG terminal amid rising U.S. gas demand. Enron settled its lawsuit against NGX, which agreed to include EnronOnline trades in Alberta gas-price indexes. Enron advocated further Japanese electricity-market deregulation and participated in bidding for Saudi gas projects. In India, lenders considered terminating the Dabhol power contract amid payment disputes, while officials pursued renegotiation and debated the project’s costs. Karnataka commissioned two Sharavathi hydroelectric units and outlined additional power projects. Reports also examined electricity shortages and investment policies in Chile and Brazil.

Alex Caruso, the Lakers’ inaugural two-way player, had spent 42 of his allowed 45 days with the NBA team and appeared in 25 games. Coach Luke Walton said the system improves familiarity, chemistry and continuity while developing players within the organization. Caruso’s contract extends through next season, and the Lakers believe he could eventually join the regular rotation. The 24-year-old averaged 2.6 points and 1.9 assists for the Lakers, compared with 19 points and 7.4 assists for South Bay. He will earn nearly $300,000, far above the G-League maximum of $26,000, and said his progress offers hope to other G-League players.

The Olympics’ elimination format differs from playoffs, which allow teams to recover from losses. Both tournaments are draining and demand sustained unity and focus. The coach remains relaxed when players perform but uses mental tactics to restore their edge, fostering mutual understanding with few words.

Mercer’s 231-city quality-of-life survey ranked Vienna first for the ninth consecutive year, citing its culture, healthcare and moderate housing costs, while Baghdad remained last. Zurich ranked second, with Auckland and Munich joint third. Europe held eight top-10 positions. Regional leaders included Vancouver, Singapore, Montevideo and Durban. London fell to 41st. Sarajevo and Bratislava recorded major long-term improvements, while conflict-affected Sanaa and Damascus ranked near the bottom.

Israel separated Druze education from the Arab school system in the 1970s, establishing a dedicated unit, curricula, textbooks, teacher training, facilities, and Druze heritage studies. The system aimed to preserve Druze identity while strengthening identification with and loyalty to Israel. Since the separation, Druze matriculation eligibility has risen substantially, reaching about 89% in 2022, alongside increased participation in higher education.

The study examined whether separation contributed to these achievements. It used documents and semi-structured interviews with nine Druze principals, supervisors, and trainee principals, supplemented by questions concerning students’ academic readiness. Interview transcripts underwent thematic analysis.

Interviewees expressed broad satisfaction with Druze students’ matriculation achievements but emphasized the need to improve certificate quality, excellence rates, Hebrew proficiency, psychometric performance, and preparation for competitive academic fields. They attributed success chiefly to strong school leadership, qualified teaching staff, targeted programs, resource use, rising educational awareness, sociocultural modernization, and increased participation by Druze women.

Druze curricula largely resemble those of other sectors in mathematics, English, and science, while differing in heritage, history, and language content intended to reinforce Druze identity. Views on separation were divided. Some participants believed autonomy enabled focused supervision, resources, curricula, and planning. Others argued that sociocultural and economic changes, rather than separation, drove achievement, and viewed separation partly as a state effort to distance Druze students from Arab identity.

Participants agreed that schools should prepare students for higher education, but reported inadequate guidance, follow-up, resources, and programs. The study identifies a gap between strong high-school performance and students’ preparedness and achievements in academia. It recommends culturally responsive academic-preparation programs, stronger alignment between matriculation requirements and university demands, continued investment in educators and leadership, and consideration of successful Druze practices in other school systems.

The findings are limited by a small convenience sample, subjective interview accounts, possible interpretive bias, and unavailable separate data for Christian students. The study therefore does not establish conclusively that separation itself caused improved Druze educational outcomes.

Alcoa shares rose 68% after the Arconic spinoff, supported by expectations for higher bauxite production and third-party sales. The company expects to ship 47.5 million to 48.5 million metric tons of bauxite in 2017 and has secured supply contracts worth nearly $600 million in 2016 and 2017. One contributor argues these developments and potential earnings growth make Alcoa attractive.

Another contributor remains cautious. Although shares trade below reported book value, asset closures and impairments have reduced that value and could continue. Alcoa also faces risks from commodity prices, possible U.S. trade policies, reliance on foreign raw materials, and uncertain profitability as a recently independent company.

The study assessed COVID-19 booster uptake and compliance with testing and isolation protocols in France, Belgium, and Italy for winter 2022/2023. A survey of 4,594 Influenzanet participants informed a branching-process model parameterized for Omicron. Respondents reported high willingness to test when symptomatic and comply with isolation, although testing declined substantially when tests cost up to €20. Booster willingness among older respondents was lowest in France and highest in Belgium.

Assuming an effective reproductive number of 1.6 and isolation reducing transmissibility by 75%, testing and isolation were predicted to reduce transmission by 18.4% under the French protocol, 17.2% under the Belgian protocol, and 24.4% under the Italian protocol. None would reduce the reproductive number below 1 alone. Charging for tests reduced predicted effectiveness by about 60%. French and Belgian protocols produced average isolation periods of about six days and released approximately 60% of people while still infectious. The Italian protocol reduced this proportion to 8% but required about 11 isolation days.

Simpler Belgian-style rules achieved performance similar to French rules while requiring about 30% fewer tests. Italian rules were more effective but imposed greater social costs through longer isolation. Expected booster uptake would substantially raise vaccine-conferred protection, but reported fall 2022 coverage was much lower than survey intentions, particularly in France and Italy. The study concluded that free testing, support for isolation, simpler guidance, high booster coverage, and additional measures such as masking remained important.

Limitations included a non-age-stratified model, no direct assessment of hospital impacts, possible participant self-selection toward health-conscious behavior, and an assumed isolation effectiveness of 75%.

A collection of March 17–19, 2001 articles examines California’s energy crisis. San Diego regulators allowed the Cabrillo power plant to emit more nitrogen oxides to increase electricity production, with potentially significant ozone increases if it burns fuel oil.

Federal regulators identified $55 million in possible February power overcharges and ordered six suppliers to justify prices above $430 per megawatt-hour during Stage 3 alerts or issue refunds. California officials and consumer advocates argued the action was inadequate compared with the state’s multibillion-dollar electricity costs. Suppliers denied gouging.

California’s Department of Water Resources was spending about $350 million weekly buying electricity for financially troubled utilities. Officials acknowledged limited trading experience and weak bargaining leverage, while withholding details of long-term contracts involving about $40 billion.

Unpaid suppliers threatened involuntary bankruptcy proceedings against Southern California Edison, while PG&E also faced financial pressure. The utilities had accumulated more than $13 billion in debt, and bankruptcy concerns complicated negotiations over state purchases of transmission systems.

OPEC’s planned 4% production cut prompted calls for increased U.S. energy production and concern about higher gasoline prices. Other groups invoked the crisis to challenge electric-car, overtime, and water-flow policies.

PG&E revised blackout exemptions, removing about 810,000 customers and adding 690,000. A commentary described erroneous PG&E billing and service termination at a restaurant. An editorial warned that political hostility toward out-of-state generators could produce inefficient energy policies.

Tamil Nadu’s sugar output is expected to fall from about 1 million tonnes in 2016/17 to 600,000 tonnes in 2017/18 because of its worst drought in over a century. Drought, crop losses and debt prompted farmers to protest in New Delhi. India’s 2016/17 sugar production forecast was cut to 20.3 million tonnes. Uneven monsoon rainfall left southern areas parched, while Tamil Nadu’s cotton output is projected to decline 21 percent.

Tesla’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2017 reported revenue of $2.70 billion, up from $1.15 billion a year earlier, and gross profit of $667.9 million. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $330.3 million, or $2.04 per share, compared with $282.3 million, or $2.13 per share, in 2016.

At March 31, Tesla had $25.05 billion in assets, $18.89 billion in liabilities, $4.01 billion in cash and equivalents, and $8.52 billion in total debt. Operating activities used $69.8 million, investing activities used $926.9 million, and financing activities provided $1.60 billion. Tesla raised net proceeds through common stock and convertible-note offerings.

Tesla operates automotive and energy generation and storage segments. Quarterly automotive revenue was $2.48 billion, while energy generation and storage revenue was $213.9 million. U.S. revenue totaled $1.28 billion, China revenue $503.9 million, and other geographic markets accounted for the remainder.

Tesla acquired Grohmann Engineering for $109.5 million in cash to improve manufacturing speed and efficiency. It continued integrating SolarCity, acquired in November 2016 for $2.1 billion in stock. Solar energy systems leased or intended for lease totaled $6.09 billion.

The company disclosed supplier concentration risks, warranty obligations, resale-value guarantees, legal proceedings, and commitments related to Gigafactory 2 in Buffalo. It reported compliance with all financial debt covenants as of March 31, 2017.

Metrocosm’s animation maps recorded city populations from ancient Eridu onward. A Yale-led team created the underlying dataset by standardizing historical research, extending urban population records to 3700 B.C. Though incomplete and uneven geographically, it enables long-term analysis of accelerating global urbanization.

Enron agreed to be acquired by smaller Houston rival Dynegy for about $7.7–$9 billion, with Dynegy also assuming roughly $13 billion in debt. Enron’s collapse followed disclosures of complex off-balance-sheet partnerships, overstated profits, understated debt, a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity and an SEC investigation. The company restated results since 1997, reducing net income by nearly $600 million and increasing debt by $2.5 billion. Former CFO Andrew Fastow and other employees were linked to the partnerships, prompting dismissals, internal investigations and shareholder lawsuits.

Commentators attributed Enron’s crisis to opaque finances, declining investor confidence, failed investments and restricted access to capital. Although its disappearance was viewed as a blow to Houston’s business image, Dynegy’s local ownership was expected to preserve operations and reinforce the city’s energy-trading role.

California’s energy crisis, falling power prices and the economic slowdown hurt energy companies and delayed deregulation in several states. Analysts nevertheless said competitive power generation and trading continued to expand and could recover with the economy.

Wall Street, investors and accounting organizations increased scrutiny of pro forma earnings and excluded charges, with Enron cited as a prominent example of misleading financial complexity. Standard & Poor’s planned broader inclusion of restructuring costs, stock-option expenses and operating write-downs in earnings measures.

Separately, stocks rose above pre-September 11 levels after a Federal Reserve rate cut and improved consumer sentiment. A Senate economic stimulus bill drew criticism for combining unemployment and tax measures with subsidies and provisions benefiting specific industries and regions.

The work introduces a bound-preserving coupling of cell-centered finite volume (CCFV) and discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods for steady convection-diffusion problems. CCFV is inexpensive, locally conservative, and monotone under standard two-point flux approximations but generally low-order and prone to layer smearing. DG offers high-order accuracy, adaptivity, and sharp layer resolution but is costlier and may produce overshoots and undershoots.

The proposed adaptive procedure detects DG cells whose averages violate prescribed bounds and reverts a small surrounding region to CCFV. Once bound-preserving cell averages are obtained, standard conservative slope limiters can enforce bounds throughout the solution. The approach leaves cell averages unchanged, does not modify either underlying discretization, and can be incorporated into hp-adaptivity routines. Related alternatives include postprocessing, modified FV-DG convective forms, artificial viscosity, flux-corrected transport, and nonlinear bound-preserving formulations, each with trade-offs involving cost, conservation, accuracy, or formal analysis.

The model is a steady convection-diffusion-reaction equation on a bounded polygonal or polyhedral domain with Dirichlet and homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. The domain is divided into matching FV and DG regions. FV cells use two-point flux admissible meshes requiring orthogonality between cell-center connections and shared facets, together with shape regularity. Harmonic normal diffusion averages define face transmissibilities. The coupled approximation space uses piecewise constants in the FV region and degree-\(k\) polynomials in the DG region, with facet jumps and averages defined for DG, FV, boundary, and FV-DG interfaces.

The author disputes Keith E. Whittington’s argument that professors should exercise discretion after Kirk’s assassination to preserve academic freedom. While faculty should generally teach competently and remain relevant to their subjects, the author argues that fleeting off-topic or controversial remarks should not invite discipline, especially when enforcement reflects viewpoint discrimination. Academic freedom should rest on intellectual honesty, truth, free expression, and its value to society—not on professors avoiding offensive or polarizing speech. The author also notes that the AAUP’s 1940 principles treated caution in public speech as moral guidance rather than a punishable rule, while 1970 comments affirmed controversy as central to academic inquiry. The passage concludes that fear-driven demands for discretion undermine rather than protect academic freedom, which should apply even to unpopular or objectionable views.

Wyong Race Club and owner Gary Leafe are disputing compensation after dogs attacked and seriously injured filly Eyes To Heaven following trackwork. The horse is expected to recover, while Leafe seeks $8,300 in training and feed costs. The club wants a settlement but has requested a breakdown of the claim.

Hugh Bowman requires reductions in two careless-riding suspensions to ride Winx in the Apollo Stakes. Trainer Michael Tubman celebrated an early 70th birthday present when Bye See won at Rosehill, her third victory in eight starts.

Trainer Brad Widdup, who has 35 horses in work, hopes to expand to about 60 and secure more metropolitan-class runners. Stewards questioned Corey Brown over his Canonbury Stakes ride on Exceltic; Brown said he followed instructions to find clear running outside.

Menari is set to begin his autumn campaign in The Galaxy, while Terravista will have a limited campaign featuring the Lightning Stakes and TJ Smith Stakes. Caulfield winner Kinky Boom shortened from $101 to $35 for the Golden Slipper.

Erik Demaine introduces a course on the mathematics and algorithms of geometric folding and unfolding. Applications include robotics, computer graphics, mechanical linkages, manufacturing, optics, medicine, aerospace, biology, origami sculpture, and reconfigurable architecture. The course examines three main structures: linkages made of rigid bars and hinges, non-stretching and uncut paper, and polyhedral surfaces.

Problems are classified as foldability questions, which ask how a given structure can fold, and design questions, which seek structures that achieve specified goals. Results generally establish universality, efficient decision algorithms, or computational intractability.

For linkages, mechanisms can trace polynomial curves and even signatures when crossings are allowed, but comparable results without crossings remain open. Two-dimensional rigidity can be tested efficiently, while three-dimensional rigidity is unresolved. Nonintersecting chains can always be reconfigured in two dimensions but may lock in three dimensions; trees may lock even in two dimensions. Higher-dimensional chains and trees are easier. These questions relate to robotic arms and protein folding.

For paper, determining whether a general crease pattern folds flat is NP-hard, though the single-vertex case is understood. Even deciding flat foldability for certain two-by-\(n\) map patterns remains open. Origami design has universality results: paper can form arbitrary polygons, polyhedra, and two-color patterns. Origamizer produces crease patterns for arbitrary polyhedra and works efficiently in practice, while TreeMaker designs limb-like origami bases, although optimal paper usage is NP-complete. Other topics include one-cut constructions for arbitrary polygon collections, curved-crease sculpture, self-folding sheets, universal hinge patterns, and the largely open challenge of modeling material thickness.

For polyhedra, whether every convex polyhedron has a nonoverlapping edge unfolding remains unknown; some nonconvex polyhedra do not. General cuts always work for convex polyhedra and for orthogonal polyhedra, though current methods may require exponentially many cuts. Vertex unfoldings are possible for triangulated surfaces. Algorithms can also enumerate polyhedra obtainable by folding certain polygons.

Hinged dissections allow one connected chain of pieces to fold without collision into any finite collection of equal-area polygons. Related three-dimensional constructions require an additional condition and can support transforming sculptures or robots.

The class consists mainly of mandatory lectures, several problem sets, and a project with a final presentation. Projects may involve sculpture, software, algorithms, open problems, applications, or surveys, and collaboration is encouraged. Optional weekly sessions focus on solving open research problems.

The course examines how to build secure systems through research-paper discussions and practical labs using multiple programming languages. Students must read assigned papers, submit responses before lectures, and follow MIT’s legal and network-use rules. Labs cover exploiting and defending web servers, finding bugs, browser worms, and languages including C, Assembly, Python, and JavaScript.

Security is defined as achieving a goal despite an adversary. Secure-system design comprises three elements: a policy specifying goals such as confidentiality, integrity, and availability; a threat model describing assumptions about attackers; and mechanisms implementing the policy under those assumptions. Security is difficult because it requires preventing all unauthorized behavior, not merely demonstrating expected behavior. Designs therefore require iterative identification and correction of weak links.

Policies can fail through weak account-recovery procedures or interactions among services, as illustrated by attacks on Yahoo and linked Gmail, Apple, and Amazon accounts. Threat models fail when they rely on unrealistic human behavior, outdated cryptographic assumptions, trusted hardware, universally reliable certificate authorities, or unsecured development infrastructure. Mechanisms fail through implementation errors, including unlimited password attempts in an iCloud interface, missing access checks at Citibank, predictable random values affecting Bitcoin software, and inconsistent string encodings in SSL certificates.

Buffer overflows demonstrate how unsafe C functions can overwrite stack data and return addresses, allowing attackers to redirect execution, inject code, or reuse existing code. Defenses such as non-executable stacks make exploitation harder but are incomplete. Stronger designs minimize the trusted computing base by concentrating policy enforcement in a small number of components.

Microsoft reported results from its November 28, 2018 annual shareholders meeting. Of 7.68 billion eligible shares, 6.72 billion were voted. Shareholders re-elected all 14 director nominees, approved executive compensation with 96.0% support, and ratified Deloitte & Touche LLP as independent auditor for fiscal 2019 with 97.6% support. The filing was signed November 29, 2018 by Corporate Secretary Carolyn Frantz.

The lecture examines how companies can build effective sustainability strategies using Porter’s corporate social responsibility framework. Moral obligation, license to operate, reputation, and broad sustainability claims are insufficient primary drivers because they are difficult to measure, may not align with company capabilities, lack demonstrated business value, or are too vague for short-term decisions.

Companies should instead distinguish generic social issues from impacts tied to their value chains and competitive context. They should consciously decline or minimally address lower-priority issues, mitigate relevant risks, and concentrate resources on sustainability initiatives that strengthen competitive positioning or improve core operations. Examples include Whole Foods integrating sustainability into its retail model, Siemens and GE aligning internal energy efficiency with energy-product markets, UPS reducing fuel use, and Nestlé supporting farmers within its supply chain.

A life-cycle perspective helps identify where impacts occur, including among suppliers and customers. Companies should determine supply-chain involvement according to material impacts, strategic importance, and risk. Automotive firms should prioritize vehicle-use emissions because most life-cycle emissions occur during use, while food companies such as Starbucks, Unilever, and Nestlé may need deep supplier engagement because agricultural sourcing is central to product quality and continuity. Starbucks’ CAFE Practices illustrate supplier certification, auditing, training, and environmental and labor standards.

Waste, packaging, transportation, and energy commonly attract action because reductions can produce measurable cost savings. However, feasible initiatives are not automatically strategic priorities. Life-cycle assessment and reliable measurement are necessary for evaluating trade-offs and connecting environmental objectives to product design and operations.

Implementation requires selecting priorities, establishing ambitious but credible goals, linking them to operational measures and incentives, and incorporating sustainability into routine decisions. Metrics should rely on data such as energy use, mileage, waste, or fuel consumption rather than retrospective estimates. Third-party verification can improve credibility. Supplier sustainability requirements often begin with voluntary information requests and training, then progress to procurement scorecards, mandatory reporting, reduction targets, and possible loss of supplier status.

Stakeholders, NGOs, policy, and reporting systems can inform strategy, but companies should not simply pursue rankings or external demands. Effective sustainability becomes part of a company’s capabilities and decision-making systems while remaining aligned with its business strategy. The final team project should compare companies, assess their sustainability performance, and determine whether external rankings are justified.

Tesla’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2018 reported quarterly revenue of $4.00 billion, operating loss of $621.4 million, and net loss attributable to common stockholders of $717.5 million, or $4.22 per share. For the first six months, revenue was $7.41 billion and common-stockholder net loss was $1.43 billion. Operating and investing activities used $528.0 million and $1.41 billion in cash, respectively, while financing provided $770.3 million.

At June 30, Tesla had $27.91 billion in assets, including $2.24 billion in cash, $3.32 billion in inventory, and $10.97 billion in property and equipment. Liabilities totaled $22.64 billion, including $9.14 billion current liabilities. Total debt principal was $10.91 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash declined to $2.78 billion from $3.96 billion at year-end 2017. Customer deposits were $942.1 million.

Tesla adopted ASC 606 on January 1, 2018, changing revenue recognition for certain vehicle sales with resale guarantees from lease accounting to sales with rights of return. Adoption reduced opening accumulated deficit by $623.2 million and increased six-month automotive sales revenue by $664.7 million while reducing automotive leasing revenue by $354.2 million. It lowered the reported six-month net loss by $90.3 million.

The company operates automotive and energy generation and storage segments. Quarterly automotive revenue was $3.36 billion, energy generation and storage revenue was $374.4 million, and services and other revenue was $270.1 million. Tesla identified dependence on predominantly single-source suppliers as a material risk.

Inventory increased from $2.26 billion at year-end to $3.32 billion. Property and equipment increased to $10.97 billion, with cumulative Gigafactory 1 costs of $4.14 billion. Tesla was compliant with all financial debt covenants.

Stockholders approved a 20.3 million-option CEO performance award in March 2018. Its 12 tranches require both market-capitalization milestones, beginning at $100 billion and increasing in $50 billion increments, and specified revenue or adjusted EBITDA milestones. As of June 30, three operational milestones were considered probable of achievement.

British consumer credit complaints rose to 7,281 in the second quarter from 5,846 a year earlier, with payday loans accounting for nearly half. The Financial Ombudsman Service criticised lenders’ repayment checks. Annual complaints increased 89 percent. PPI remained the most complained-about product, with 42,401 new cases, mostly submitted through claims-management companies despite free direct complaints.

Asia-Pacific markets rose as U.S. officials downplayed conflict risks with North Korea, while U.S. stocks recorded their largest weekly loss in months. Japan’s economy grew 4.0% annualized, driven by household spending. U.S. inflation remained subdued, the weaker dollar could support growth, and Fed official Robert Kaplan favored awaiting higher inflation before further rate increases.

JPMorgan’s Michael Liersch says investors can succeed by planning, maintaining perspective, and remaining patient. He recommends creating a budget to understand spending and determine how much to save and invest. Reframing sacrifices as progress toward future goals—and market declines as buying opportunities—can reduce anxiety. Investors should match investments to their timelines and avoid reacting emotionally or trying to time the market. A trusted partner can challenge assumptions and provide balance. Finally, taking small steps, such as paying down debt, contributing to an IRA, or automating retirement and savings transfers, can build momentum.

Microsoft’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2016 reported quarterly revenue of $20.5 billion, operating income of $5.3 billion, and net income of $3.8 billion, compared with $21.7 billion, $6.6 billion, and $5.0 billion, respectively, a year earlier. Diluted earnings per share declined to $0.47 from $0.61. For the nine-month period, revenue was $64.7 billion, operating income $17.1 billion, net income $13.7 billion, and diluted earnings per share $1.70.

At March 31, 2016, Microsoft had $181.9 billion in assets, including $105.6 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments. Total liabilities were $107.1 billion, including $40.9 billion in long-term debt, while stockholders’ equity was $74.8 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow totaled $24.9 billion. Microsoft used $9.4 billion for financing and $13.9 billion for investing activities.

Quarterly segment revenue was $6.5 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $6.1 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $9.5 billion for More Personal Computing. Segment operating income was $3.0 billion, $2.2 billion, and $1.6 billion, respectively. Corporate and Other included $1.6 billion of Windows 10 revenue deferrals; deferred Windows 10 revenue totaled $4.6 billion for the nine months.

Commercial cloud annualized revenue exceeded $10 billion. Office 365 Consumer subscribers reached 22.2 million, Azure revenue grew 110%, Windows 10 was active on more than 270 million devices, and Xbox Live monthly active users rose 26% to 46 million.

Microsoft completed 14 acquisitions for $1.3 billion during the nine months. It issued $13.0 billion of debt in November 2015 and repurchased $11.2 billion of common stock during the period. The company had $10.7 billion remaining under its share-repurchase authorization.

Microsoft continued its phone hardware restructuring plan, targeting elimination of up to 7,800 positions by June 30, 2016; cumulative related charges were $780 million. Aggregate accrued legal liabilities were $530 million, with approximately $1.6 billion of additional adverse outcomes considered reasonably possible.

Microsoft early adopted new share-based payment accounting guidance and expects forthcoming revenue-recognition and lease standards to materially affect its consolidated financial statements or balance sheets. Deloitte reported no material modifications were needed for the interim statements to conform with U.S. GAAP.

The study uses parameter-free quasiparticle self-consistent GW with excitonic ladder diagrams (QSGŴ) to investigate electronic and excitonic proximity effects in WSe₂/CrI₃ bilayers and ferromagnetic or antiferromagnetic CrI₃/WSe₂/CrI₃ trilayers. Unlike LDA, QSGW and QSGŴ predict type-I band alignment, with both band edges primarily located in WSe₂ and gaps near 2.2 eV. The heterostructures preserve WSe₂ A and B Wannier–Mott excitons and localized CrI₃ Frenkel excitons while generating new interlayer excitons between the A and B energies.

These interlayer excitons combine dipolar WSe₂ character with magnetic CrI₃ character, have binding energies around 400 meV, and are approximately twenty times brighter than intralayer CrI₃ Frenkel excitons, though substantially darker than the WSe₂ A exciton. Their energy ordering and presence are robust across the studied layer and magnetic configurations. Proximity-induced splitting of A and B excitons ranges from tens to hundreds of GHz in the bilayer and antiferromagnetic trilayer and reaches about 1000 GHz in the ferromagnetic trilayer. The splitting is highly sensitive to alignment between Cr-d and W-d states and may vary with structure, strain, interlayer spacing, and phonon coupling. The authors identify the robust, bright, magnetic interlayer excitons as promising for photonic and spintronic applications, while noting that exciton lifetimes cannot be calculated within the present static treatment.

The Poland school board dissolved teacher Cassandra Kibler’s contract after her state teaching license was revoked following allegations of an inappropriate relationship with a student. Architects also presented two plans to reduce district operating costs through school closures, consolidation and new construction. Both would repurpose Dobbins Elementary for athletics, while either maintaining two campuses or placing most grades on the high-school campus. The board took no action and will review the proposals.

Molecular-dynamics simulations based on a first-principles-parameterized effective Hamiltonian were used to study polar topological textures in Ba(ZrₓTi₁₋ₓ)O₃. In an ordered 12.5% Zr superlattice, chemical unit-cell doubling along [111] produces alternating topological sectors: a charge −2 antiskyrmion composed of six −1/3 quarks and a charge +4 skyrmion composed of six +2/3 quarks. Both share nearly identical six-vortex geometries, with an effective charge shift of +1 at each vortex. A complementary field-theoretic description attributes this alternation to the binary chemical background, although the microscopic charge-transfer mechanism remains unresolved.

Random Zr substitution from 0% to 12.5% preserves stable, nontrivial nanodomains at 1 K but increasingly pins, distorts, and fragments their vortex structures. The resulting textures exhibit spatially varying topological charge and resemble a disorder-pinned skyrmion glass rather than a single well-defined texture.

Thermal simulations show that pure BaTiO₃ has the greatest intrinsic stability, with critical temperatures ranging from about 65 K for 3.5 nm domains to about 110 K for 6.5 nm domains. Zr initially lowers stability, with a minimum near 6–8% substitution, followed by partial recovery toward 12.5% due to disorder-assisted pinning and self-averaging. Larger domains are generally more stable.

The ordered 12.5% superlattice remains rhombohedral above room temperature, with rhombohedral–orthorhombic transitions near 320 K on cooling and 345 K on heating. At 293 K, nanodomains are not retained without bias, but a local [111] electric field of about 350 kV/cm writes and maintains volatile charge +4 textures. Under similar conditions, random 12.5% BZT instead forms multidomain states. Strain, electrostatic screening, and compositional patterning are proposed as possible routes toward room-temperature nonvolatile stabilization.

The paper argues that the reproduction number \(R\) inadequately measures viral spread when testing varies over time because it tracks cases without controlling for diagnostic effort. It proposes the acceleration index \(\varepsilon\), an elasticity measuring the proportional change in cases relative to the proportional change in tests. The index also represents current positivity relative to historical average positivity and distinguishes acceleration (\(\varepsilon>1\)) from deceleration (\(\varepsilon<1\)).

The authors derive the relationship \(\varepsilon=R(A/B)\), where \(A\) is infectivity intensity and \(B\) is test intensity. Thus, \(R\) and \(\varepsilon\) coincide only when infectivity and testing intensities match. When test intensity exceeds infectivity intensity, \(R\) tends to overestimate acceleration; when infectivity intensity exceeds test intensity, it tends to underestimate it. The acceleration index therefore nests a testing-adjusted reproduction number.

Using French data from May 2020 to October 2022, the authors find sizeable differences between the indicators. The reproduction number often underestimated spread, particularly during the Omicron period, and sometimes suggested improvement while the acceleration index indicated continuing acceleration. During France’s second lockdown, \(R\) indicated deceleration earlier than the acceleration index because testing also declined. Analyses of five other countries show that the direction and magnitude of the discrepancy vary by country and period.

The paper recommends that public health authorities track either the acceleration index alone or the reproduction number together with test and infectivity intensities. It favors the acceleration index as the more parsimonious approach. Its limitations include uncounted infections, asymptomatic cases, dependence on sufficient testing, and the resource costs of active testing policies.

May 24, 2001 news reports focused on the Dabhol power dispute. Renegotiation committee chairman Madhav Godbole resigned after Sharad Pawar criticized the panel’s approach, prompting cancellation of a meeting with Dabhol Power Company. Godbole withdrew his resignation after Maharashtra’s Cabinet unanimously affirmed confidence in him and clarified that Pawar’s comments were personal. The next renegotiation meeting was scheduled for May 29.

The Centre said it would facilitate negotiations, consider recommendations acceptable to DPC and the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, and reassure lenders, but would avoid direct intervention until Maharashtra decided whether to retain or scrap the project. Officials were considering using Power Trading Corporation to sell Dabhol electricity to power-deficit states. Maharashtra also referred disputes involving termination notices, arbitration, rebates and payments to the state electricity regulator.

Domestic lenders, which had suspended further Phase II disbursements, hoped a Friday meeting would resolve the crisis. Separately, MSEB faced a contempt petition for failing to provide all documents requested by Prayas concerning three private power projects.

Extracts from the Godbole Committee report argued that Dabhol’s design as a base-load project was seriously flawed. They said Maharashtra lacked demand to absorb its output, lower-cost alternatives existed, negotiations increased projected costs, and purchasing Phase II power would require unrealistic demand growth, reduced losses and substantial tariff increases. An editorial said the Dabhol controversy had prompted scrutiny of private power agreements elsewhere and called for reforms to electricity distribution, tariffs and government negotiation practices.

The study examined Ethiopian education policy intentions and secondary school principals’ and teachers’ understandings of curriculum differentiation. It analyzed three national policy documents and interviewed two principals and 17 teachers from one regular and one special day secondary school in Addis Ababa.

The Education and Training Policy and General Education Curriculum Framework conceptualize differentiation through school types, study fields, streams, subjects, and ability groupings. In contrast, the national guideline on curriculum differentiation emphasizes adapting content, instruction, assessment, and learning environments within inclusive classrooms. This lack of policy coherence may create confusion in implementation.

Principals’ and teachers’ understandings varied. They described curriculum differentiation as gifted education, placement into subjects, streams or schools, special curricula for student groups, identification and accommodation of talents, or general curriculum planning and teaching strategies. Some views aligned with policy intentions, while others reflected limited awareness. Participants often focused on gifted and high-achieving students, with less attention to other students with special educational needs.

The study concludes that Ethiopia needs clearer, aligned policies defining curriculum differentiation, giftedness, student selection, school administration, and links to further education and careers. It also recommends more flexible secondary curricula, offering varied subjects and difficulty levels based on students’ interests, abilities, and career goals rather than relying mainly on uniform natural and social science streams or separate school types.

The American whaling bark Cape Horn Pigeon sailed on December 7, 1891, and entered the Okhotsk Sea in 1892. Its captain had previously visited Vladivostok and sought Russian permission to whale in certain coastal bays, consistent with a Russian notice prohibiting whaling within 3 miles of the coast. Although permission was denied, Russia gave no indication that it claimed jurisdiction over the entire sea. On September 10, 1892, a Russian naval officer forcibly seized the bark on the open sea, claiming the Okhotsk Sea was closed, and compelled its crew to navigate the Russian vessel to Vladivostok. Despite the captain’s protest, the bark was detained until October 1. The captain notified the United States legation, whose chargé d’affaires contacted the Russian foreign ministry and was subsequently informed that the vessel had been released.

Using China Education Panel Survey data from 13,981 seventh- and ninth-grade students, the study applies multiple linear regression to examine links between parental education and children’s cognitive ability, including gender, urban-rural, and mediating differences. Parental education is significantly positively associated with cognitive ability: each additional year in the higher-educated parent’s schooling corresponds to a 0.019-point increase. Educational expectations, educational investment, children’s expectations, and parent-child companionship partially mediate this relationship. The association is stronger for girls than boys, for urban than rural children, and among children with lower cognitive ability.

The stackless assembler initialization procedure uses register passing to configure processors and cache, allocate per-core pre-memory stack regions, map them globally, set x86-64 MTRRs, and create a UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF instance. It must run on every processor core. Protected-mode hosts must provide an SS descriptor with base zero; real mode uses a 16-bit-compatible SS:ESP. The host must rely exclusively on this procedure for stack creation. It may return success, a warning for stack reentry, or a fatal error for an unknown processor family.

A corresponding stack-removal procedure disables Cache-as-RAM after the PEI core relocates the stack and synchronizes MTRRs. It runs on all cores, flushes cache lines, preserves EBX, and leaves BSP cache enabled but invalidated without write-back. It should be invoked only by the BSP, and 16-bit hosts must establish Big Real mode. AARCH64 APUs with a Platform Security Processor do not use these early stack macros because the PSP initializes DRAM.

AmdCreateStruct allocates and initializes parameter structures with defaults. Allocation methods include an internal pre-memory Cache-as-RAM heap, post-memory DRAM allocation, or host-provided storage. With host allocation, the caller must ensure sufficient space; successful initialization overlays the parameter structure, while insufficient space returns an error and retains its contents.

The course primarily uses Sean Carroll’s general relativity textbook, with supplementary references including Bernard Schutz, Misner, Thorne and Wheeler, and Wald. Grades are based entirely on 11 problem sets, with no final exam.

The first half develops the mathematical foundations needed to derive the Einstein field equations; the second applies them to Newtonian gravity, cosmology, black holes, gravitational waves, and neutron stars. Special relativity is initially presented geometrically to establish tools for later analysis.

Spacetime is defined as a manifold of events endowed with a metric. A manifold specifies connectedness, an event is where and when something happens, and coordinates are adjustable labels for events. The metric provides distances between events and ultimately encodes gravity.

An inertial reference frame is described as a freely moving, nonrotating lattice of orthogonal, uniformly marked measuring rods and uniformly ticking clocks. Its clocks are synchronized using light: the reflection time at a second clock equals the average of the emission and reception times at the first. This relies on light having the same speed for every inertial observer. Units are chosen so the speed of light equals one.

Spacetime displacement vectors exist independently of coordinate representations, though different inertial observers assign different components related by Lorentz transformations. Greek indices generally denote spacetime components, repeated upper and lower indices are summed under Einstein’s convention, summed indices are dummy indices, and unsummed indices are free indices. A spacetime vector is a quartet of components that transforms like displacement under Lorentz transformations and obeys vector-space linearity laws.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture, including GA102 and GA104 GPUs, improves traditional graphics performance by up to 1.7x and ray tracing by up to 2x over Turing. GA102 combines up to 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second-generation RT Cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor Cores. Its redesigned streaming multiprocessor doubles peak FP32 processing, expands L1 cache and shared-memory bandwidth, and supports concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute workloads.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and add hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur, which can render up to eight times faster than on Turing. Third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32, BF16, and structured sparsity, enabling up to twice the matrix throughput and accelerating AI applications such as DLSS, denoising, broadcasting, and 8K super-resolution.

GA10x products include the GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3080, RTX 3070, RTX A6000, and data-center-focused A40. The RTX 3090 supports many games at 8K and 60 fps using DLSS, while the RTX 3080 offers up to twice the RTX 2080’s performance. The RTX A6000 and A40 provide 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, expandable to 96 GB through third-generation NVLink.

Additional features include GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, reaching 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/s bandwidth; PCIe 4.0; HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a for 8K displays; RTX IO for GPU-based asset decompression and faster storage access; fifth-generation NVDEC with AV1 decoding up to 8K60 HDR; and seventh-generation NVENC encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC. Error Detection and Replay technology detects and retries GDDR6X transmission errors during memory overclocking. Ampere GPUs are also described as up to 1.9 times more power-efficient than Turing at equal performance.

The lecture examines portfolio-level financing for sustainable real estate through public markets, focusing on real estate investment trusts (REITs), green bonds, and sustainability benchmarking.

REITs are publicly traded companies that primarily invest in income-producing real estate. In the United States, they receive corporate tax benefits if at least 75% of their assets and income relate to real estate and they distribute 90% of annual income. Compared with direct property ownership, REITs offer greater liquidity, geographic diversification, transparency, shared risk, and lower capital requirements, but investors have less control. REIT structures vary internationally. China recently introduced infrastructure-focused REITs to help governments raise capital after declining land-sale revenues, with possible expansion into commercial real estate.

Many large REITs have adopted net-zero and ESG targets. Interviews suggest institutional investors, especially European, Canadian, and Australian organizations, often drive these commitments by directing capital toward sustainable portfolios. Research cited in the lecture associates greener REIT portfolios with higher returns on assets and equity, lower risk, and greater resilience, though reverse causality remains a concern. Current MIT research is developing separate “green talking” and “green doing” measures to evaluate whether sustainability pledges and actual investments affect REIT performance.

Green bonds are fixed-income instruments issued by governments or companies to finance projects such as renewable energy, resilient infrastructure, and green buildings. Their appeal to issuers is potentially lower capital costs, as investor demand can increase bond prices and reduce yields. REITs and government-sponsored enterprises such as Fannie Mae may issue green bonds backed by sustainable properties or mortgages. Green-bond principles and external validation are intended to ensure proceeds support stated environmental purposes and limit greenwashing.

Reliable data, measurement, disclosure, and benchmarking are necessary to establish credibility. Tools include the EPA’s Portfolio Manager for utility data, Measurabl for ESG and carbon accounting, third-party assurance, carbon-risk models, and GRESB. GRESB functions as a portfolio-level sustainability rating system, assessing management, stakeholder engagement, energy, materials, water, waste, and other ESG factors. Studies cited associate higher GRESB scores with stronger fund or REIT performance and lower borrowing costs. However, ESG rating systems often produce inconsistent results, prompting MIT’s ESG Confusion project to develop more reliable measures from conflicting ratings.

The study evaluated deep-learning mammographic density predictions from low-dose images acquired at about 10% of standard radiation. ResNet-18 models were trained separately on 15,290 standard and simulated low-dose PROCAS mammograms, then tested on paired standard and low-dose images from 147 women aged 31–45 in the ALDRAM dataset.

Standard- and low-dose predictions were highly similar. Averaging predictions across cranial-caudal and mediolateral oblique views improved agreement, while averaging two independently trained models improved it further, reaching a Spearman correlation of 0.990 and RMSE of 1.92. Prediction differences were not associated with age or dose ratio. Performance was poorer for higher-density breasts and smaller breast areas; image-size effects were likely related to differences in breast area. Large differences between views or between models indicated greater variation between standard- and low-dose predictions. Few prediction differences exceeded 10 percentage points, with no notable outliers.

The findings support low-dose mammography for automated density estimation, particularly when combining views and models, but systematic underprediction and reduced agreement for smaller or denser breasts require further investigation and possible correction.

Tecomaria capensis, or Cape honeysuckle, is a popular garden and hedging plant in the Bignoniaceae family. It is a scrambling shrub or small tree reaching 6 m, with compound toothed leaves, trumpet-shaped orange-red to pale-yellow flowers, and slender flattened fruit. Native to thickets and forest margins across southern, eastern and tropical Africa, it is classified as Least Concern. Game and livestock browse it, while sunbirds, butterflies, bees and hawkmoth larvae visit or feed on it. Traditional medicinal uses include treating fever, pain, sleeplessness, chest ailments and dysentery, and supporting lactation. Its wood is also used for symbolic Xhosa nursing-mother necklets. It grows best in well-drained, composted soil, requires regular watering until established, and benefits from late-winter pruning.
