GroceryDB is an open-source database of over 50,000 food and beverage products collected in May 2021 from Walmart, Target, and Whole Foods websites. It uses FoodProX, a machine-learning classifier trained on NOVA labels, to convert nutrition facts into a continuous Food Processing Score (FPro) from 0 for unprocessed foods to 1 for ultra-processed foods. The database also organizes ingredient lists as trees and introduces an Ingredient Processing Score (IgFPro) to estimate individual ingredients’ contributions to processing.

Most grocery-store offerings had high FPro scores, though Whole Foods offered more minimally processed products and Target had a particularly high proportion of ultra-processed items. Processing choices varied by category: cereals, milk and milk substitutes, pasta-noodles, and snack bars covered broad ranges, while jerky, popcorn, chips, bread, biscuits, and macaroni and cheese offered narrower ranges. GroceryDB’s FPro distribution resembled USDA food databases, but many products were absent from those and from Open Food Facts.

Across categories, a 10% increase in FPro corresponded to an 8.7% decrease in price per calorie, although relationships differed substantially by category. Soups and stews showed a 24.3% decline, cereals a 1.2% decline, and milk and milk substitutes showed increasing prices with processing. Whole Foods generally provided broader processing choices and different suppliers than Walmart and Target, while pizza, macaroni and cheese, and popcorn were highly processed across stores.

Products with more complex ingredient trees generally had higher processing scores. IgFPro identified sodium tripolyphosphate, polysorbate 60, corn syrup, palm oil, vegetable oil, and soybean oil as strong signals of ultra-processing, while brain octane, flaxseed, and olive oils contributed less. Not all additives contributed equally.

The authors propose GroceryDB and TrueFood.Tech as tools for consumer substitutions, food-environment interventions, ingredient prioritization, and product reformulation. Key limitations include incomplete and inconsistent ingredient data, reliance on a small set of nutrients and manually assigned processing labels, and limited ability to detect processing methods or food-matrix changes not represented in nutrition facts.

From 1961 to 1962, the Special Group (Augmented) oversaw Operation Mongoose, a covert program coordinated by Edward Lansdale to overthrow Cuba’s Castro regime. Kennedy also created the Special Group (Counter-Insurgency), while Johnson later assigned overseas counterinsurgency coordination to the Secretary of State. In 1964, Special Group 5412 became the 303 Committee without changing its duties. It reviewed major covert actions, though most CIA projects were low-risk operations handled without committee review. Nixon required annual reviews and, in 1970, replaced the 303 Committee with the 40 Committee, reaffirming the DCI’s operational responsibilities and requiring approval for major or politically sensitive actions. Formal meetings later declined, and some major operations bypassed the committee, including Nixon’s directive to promote a coup against Chilean President Salvador Allende. The 1974 Hughes-Ryan amendment required a presidential finding for each covert action and notification to Congress that it served national security.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces technologies for hybrid rendering, virtual reality, AI-enhanced graphics, and more efficient geometry and shading. VirtualLink combines power, display, and data for VR headsets through one USB-C connector. NVLink replaces earlier SLI interfaces on supported TU102 and TU104 GPUs, providing higher bandwidth for two-way SLI and advanced display configurations; three- and four-way SLI are unsupported.

Turing’s RT Cores accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray tracing on a single GPU. NVIDIA advocates hybrid rendering, using rasterization for primary visibility and ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, and other effects. Denoising reduces the rays required per pixel. Turing delivers over 10 Giga Rays per second in described workloads, approximately ten times Pascal’s software-based ray-tracing performance. Ray tracing can also support physics, collision detection, audio simulation, AI visibility queries, and path tracing.

NVIDIA NGX uses Turing Tensor Cores and pretrained deep neural networks for graphics functions. Deep Learning Super-Sampling renders with fewer input samples and infers target-resolution images, providing image quality similar to temporal anti-aliasing with less shading work. DLSS 2X aims to approach 64-times supersampled quality. Other NGX features include content-aware inpainting, interpolated slow-motion video, and AI-based image or video enlargement.

Mesh Shading introduces cooperative Task and Mesh Shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks, process many objects in parallel, select levels of detail, and manipulate geometry. Variable Rate Shading independently adjusts shading rates across 16-by-16-pixel regions. Its applications include content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility from appearance sampling, stores shading results in texture space, and reuses them across pixels, views, or frames. Multi-View Rendering processes up to four hardware views per pass, improving stereo VR, wide-field headsets, shadows, and repeated geometry.

Turing also expands DirectX 12 resource binding and heap support. Its VR features include VirtualLink, Multi-View Rendering, foveated rendering, and RT Core acceleration for VRWorks Audio.

The full TU104 contains 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and one x8 NVLink connection; it is used in products including GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. Tesla T4 uses 2,560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, contains 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores but lacks NVLink and SLI.

NVIDIA defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based hybrid-rendering metric combining weighted Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations. The passage also explains ray casting, BVH construction and refitting, denoising, and ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections. It concludes that hybrid rendering, denoising, BVHs, and RT Cores collectively make real-time ray tracing practical.

The lecture examines economically motivated cybercrime, focusing on spam. Because spam is cheap and requires few successful purchases, attackers remain profitable despite extremely low conversion rates. Markets supply botnets, compromised accounts, exploits, hosting, stolen data, and CAPTCHA-solving labor.

The spam ecosystem comprises advertising, click support, and realization. Attackers use botnets, compromised webmail, IP hijacking, fast-flux DNS, redirects, distributed infrastructure, and affiliate programs to evade filtering and takedowns. Defenses such as blacklists, CAPTCHAs, micropayments, and computational puzzles raise costs but face practical limitations, circumvention, and user inconvenience.

Payment processing may offer a stronger choke point because relatively few acquiring banks serve spammers. Credit-card rules, transaction classification, chargeback penalties, and limited banking relationships encourage sellers to deliver products and avoid overt fraud. Visa subsequently classified pharmaceutical sales as high-risk and strengthened prohibitions against illegal drugs and trademark-infringing goods.

The lecture also discusses cyber-arms markets, legal ambiguity, research ethics, and private-sector “hackbacks,” in which companies attack botnets or recover assets using arguments such as trademark infringement.

The June 4, 2001 ISDA press report covers Basel II, credit derivatives, Argentina’s debt swap, California’s power-grid governance, and structured options.

Basel II, scheduled for completion by year-end and implementation in 2004, would align bank capital requirements more closely with loan risk but faces criticism over complexity, operational-risk measurement, implementation costs, and timing. Australia’s regulator warned that mortgage rules could favor large banks using internal ratings and proposed lower standardized risk weights. Asian central bankers said limited infrastructure and expertise could prevent implementation by 2004. Banks also argued that the accord could raise capital costs, disadvantage developing countries and smaller institutions, and rely excessively on external ratings. ISDA criticized rigid capital floors, operational-risk charges, the 15% “W” charge on credit derivatives, and calibration of internal ratings.

ISDA working groups were developing standardized documentation for swaps involving convertible bonds and addressing how credit-default swaps should be treated when companies split or restructure. California’s grid operator faced a potential conflict with federal regulators over whether state influence had compromised its independence. The state had become a major electricity buyer, replaced the operator’s board, and sought access to sensitive information. Critics argued that the operator had become a state advocate, while California officials defended greater control during the energy emergency.

Structured options products, including capital-protected notes and index-linked investments, were described as tools combining limited capital risk with market-linked returns. Such products were presented as potentially attractive in India amid falling interest rates and demand for alternatives to equities and fixed deposits.

A self-driving Uber SUV struck and killed 49-year-old pedestrian Elaine Herzberg in Tempe, Arizona, marking the first death involving a fully autonomous test vehicle. The vehicle was traveling about 40 mph in autonomous mode with a human backup driver when Herzberg, walking a bicycle outside a crosswalk, entered the street. Authorities had not determined fault, and federal agencies sent investigators.

Uber suspended autonomous-vehicle testing in Phoenix, Pittsburgh, San Francisco and Toronto. Experts said the crash could damage public confidence and prompt stronger state and federal regulation. Autonomous vehicles are promoted as a way to reduce traffic deaths caused by human error, but oversight varies by state; Arizona has light regulations and no incident-reporting requirements.

The death followed earlier crashes involving automated technology, including a fatal 2016 Tesla Autopilot accident. Safety advocates urged federal officials and Congress to strengthen oversight while considering autonomous-vehicle legislation.

Taxpayers can also use an app and QR codes, with over 1.2 million mobile users this year. The company reported weaker Gaming demand, macroeconomic pressures, China lockdown effects, supply-chain constraints and demand-forecasting challenges. New U.S. export-license requirements covering certain advanced products sold to China could affect sales, product development and customer support. Children’s mobile phone ownership varies widely across countries and cultures. Sara Zaske observed that few third-graders in Berlin owned phones, while her daughter was the only fourth-grader in her California class without a smartphone. Zaske plans to provide a flip phone before allowing a smartphone in high school.

A 2015 European study found that 46% of children ages 9 to 16 owned smartphones, with differing school restrictions and sensitivity to data costs. In the United States, 45% of children ages 10 to 12 had smartphones with service plans, while 42% of children 8 and younger owned tablets. In South Korea, 72% owned smartphones by ages 11 to 12 and used them up to 5.4 hours daily. Ownership also increased with age in Taiwan.

Studies reported varying access elsewhere: 81% of South African secondary students owned or could access a phone, while ownership was lower among children in Ghana and Malawi. In an Australian study, the median age for first owning or using a mobile phone was 8.

The American Academy of Pediatrics says there is no single right age for a child’s first phone. It recommends limited media use for young children, monitoring content and apps, avoiding screens before bedtime, and keeping meals screen-free.

One year after Hurricane Helene severely flooded four western North Carolina school buildings, districts continue repairs, relocations, and flood-mitigation work.

Atkinson Elementary in Henderson County reopened before Christmas 2024 after replacing flooded floors. Students temporarily attended the local Boys & Girls Club, which continues supporting the district through mentoring, transportation, and after-school programming. The school is improving drainage, vegetation, and flooring resilience.

Old Fort Elementary in McDowell County remained closed through 2024-25 while students joined Pleasant Gardens Elementary. It reopened Aug. 25, 2025, with new flooring, doors, HVAC systems, paint, and flood protections, including elevated HVAC units and creek reinforcement.

Valle Crucis School in Watauga County flooded across about 70% of its building. Students remain distributed among community institutions because Helene and regional workforce shortages delayed completion of a replacement school already under construction. The district is seeking FEMA and insurance funding to preserve the historic building’s dry rock section.

Micaville Elementary in Yancey County closed permanently after flooding. Its students transferred elsewhere while classrooms were added at Burnsville and Blue Ridge elementary schools. The district also adopted Starlink and radio-based emergency communications. Yancey County continues addressing drainage, mold, damaged infrastructure, and facility needs while navigating FEMA processes.

Superintendents emphasized community partnerships, reliable emergency communications, staff resilience, and long-term planning to prepare for future disasters.

The speaker said the team lost the first two games despite seeking favorable matchups and had not played near its best. A leading player challenged the entire team to respond, while the coaching staff acknowledged it also needed to improve. Returning home after New Jersey won its home games, the team focused on playing confidently, skating, managing the puck, controlling emotions, winning faceoffs, and directing shots toward the net. The speaker emphasized that possession and sound decisions are essential against an opponent that allows few opportunities. Although encouraged by the improved play and defensive performance, he stressed that it was only one game, but one that gave the series a chance to become competitive.

After the Third Circuit remanded Willie Tyler’s case, the district court scheduled a retrial on two obstruction-of-justice counts arising from Doreen Proctor’s 1992 murder. Tyler had been convicted in 2000 of witness tampering by murder and by intimidation or threats and sentenced to life imprisonment. Subsequent legal developments required the government to prove either that Tyler contemplated a particular federal proceeding or that there was a reasonable likelihood Proctor would have communicated with a federal law-enforcement officer. The government conceded it could not prove the former theory, but the court found Tyler had not established actual innocence under the latter and vacated his convictions for legal error while ordering a new trial.

Tyler moved to dismiss the indictment under the Confrontation, Double Jeopardy, and Due Process Clauses. The court rejected his Confrontation Clause claim, holding that a detective’s testimony about Proctor’s statements would be offered to show that she made a communication likely to reach federal authorities, not to establish the statements’ truth. It therefore would not violate Crawford, though Tyler could object at trial to improper use.

The court also rejected Tyler’s double-jeopardy arguments. His prior Pennsylvania prosecution did not bar federal prosecution under the dual-sovereignty principle. Retrial was also permissible because his federal convictions were vacated for errors of law, not insufficient evidence. The jury instructions had failed to incorporate standards later established by Arthur Andersen and Fowler, and retrial following reversal for legal error is generally allowed.

Finally, the court rejected Tyler’s claim of outrageous government conduct. Evidence did not support his allegation that prosecutors fabricated investigator Ronald Diller’s status as a DEA adviser or consultant. Tyler also failed to establish that the government’s delayed disclosure of Mark Spotz’s statement concerning shotgun shells constituted a prejudicial or willful Brady violation. Because Tyler did not show a reasonable probability of a different result or misconduct warranting dismissal, the court denied all motions to dismiss.

President Trump said the U.S. will impose an additional 100% tariff on Chinese goods and export controls on critical software starting Nov. 1, 2025, potentially raising total tariffs to 130%. The move follows China’s new restrictions on rare-earth exports, including licensing requirements beginning Dec. 1. Kinder Morgan operates extensive North American midstream assets, including 70,000 miles of natural gas pipelines, oil transportation capacity of 2.1 million barrels per day, and 152 million barrels of terminal capacity. Its largely fee-based infrastructure provides relatively stable cash flow and potential expansion opportunities.

After acquisitions, falling oil prices, and financing pressures contributed to a 75% dividend cut and sharp share-price decline, the company shifted toward higher-return expansion projects funded internally. Its 2017 budget projected $4.46 billion in distributable cash flow, a $1.1 billion dividend cost, and approximately $3.2 billion in growth investment. Kinder Morgan also reduced net debt by $5.8 billion, saving roughly $500 million annually in interest.

The company planned a 60% dividend increase in 2018 and 25% increases in both 2019 and 2020, reaching $1.25 per share. Hong introduces quantum field theory (QFT) as the framework for quantum dynamics of fields. Quantizing electromagnetic fields yields photons and quantum electrodynamics. QFT describes three fundamental interactions completely, offers partial tools for quantum gravity, and is widely used across theoretical physics. This course is the first of a three-semester sequence, emphasizing foundational concepts and intuition; problem sets are essential for developing understanding.

QFT can be viewed as quantum mechanics with infinitely many degrees of freedom. Conceptual difficulties may reflect gaps in quantum mechanics, while formalism becomes clearer when connected to the physical problems it addresses. Intuition develops through examples and reflection on solved problems.

The lecture introduces locality: interactions propagate between neighboring points rather than acting instantaneously at a distance. Fields assign dynamical variables to every spatial point, and local equations involve fields, sources, and finitely many derivatives at the same point. Maxwell’s equations and Einstein’s gravity exemplify locality. Fields may be scalar, vector, tensor, or spinor.

Classical field theory generalizes classical mechanics. Its action is the spacetime integral of a local Lagrangian density depending on fields and their derivatives. Locality excludes terms directly coupling fields at separated points. Actions generally contain only first time derivatives so equations of motion require only positions and velocities as initial data. Lorentz invariance places space and time derivatives on equal footing.

Canonical momentum and Hamiltonian densities are defined analogously to classical mechanics. Varying the action and discarding boundary terms produces the Euler–Lagrange field equations. The course primarily considers translationally and Lorentz-invariant theories.

Examples include Maxwell theory, Einstein gravity, and real scalar fields. A general local, translationally and Lorentz-invariant scalar action contains a derivative term and a potential \(V(\phi)\) with constant parameters. A linear potential acts as an external force. A quadratic potential yields the linear Klein–Gordon equation, while higher-order potentials produce nonlinear equations.

Snowy plover nests were found at Clatsop Spit for the first time in decades, three years after Fort Stevens State Park created a half-mile special management area. Biologists say the nests connect western Washington and northern Oregon populations of the threatened species. Recent successful hatchings also occurred at Nehalem Bay State Park and Sitka Sedge Natural Area.

The Flex offense uses continuous baseline and down screens in a “Pick the Picker” action, forcing defenses to handle multiple screens while creating open shots and weakside rebounding opportunities. Players reverse the ball, screen for cutters, and exploit options including shots, baseline feeds, corner passes, post isolations, and pop-outs.

Against defensive overplay, the offense employs bump-backs, back cuts, lob passes, and replacement rotations to maintain continuity. It supports several entries, including high-post rubs, weakside shuffle cuts, and dribble-clear action. A “Pop” variation adds a weakside double screen, allowing cutters to go high, low, or pop out for a shot.

Because shooters often move away from the basket, offensive rebounding requires assigned responsibilities, anticipation, aggression, hustle, inside position, and repeated efforts.

Digital Foundry found Monster Hunter World enjoyable but technically disappointing across Xbox One and PS4 consoles. Strong monster and character models, detailed textures, shadows, and environments are undermined by weak contrast, minimal HDR impact, clipping, collision issues, motion blur, uneven frame rates, and inconsistent controller response.

The base PS4 runs at 1080p and generally around or below 30 fps, while the Xbox One runs at 864p with lower performance. On PS4 Pro and Xbox One X, players can prioritize resolution, frame rate, or graphics. Resolution mode reaches 1800p via checkerboarding on Pro and 1728p natively on One X; the Pro is often slightly faster, while some distant assets are missing on One X. Frame-rate mode uses 1080p on both, with the One X generally performing better. Graphics mode also uses 1080p but increases detail distances, with markedly better performance on One X.

Overall, the enhanced consoles deliver adequate but disappointing results, suggesting limited optimization, particularly for Xbox One X.

Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday’s game against the Texans with a hamstring injury suffered in a 37-20 loss. Backup Cooper Rush will start for injury-plagued Baltimore, which is 1-3 and has ruled out several Pro Bowlers. The Ravens are 4-10 without Jackson since 2018. Early benchmarks of Qualcomm’s top-tier Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme reference laptop show strong gains. Its 18-core CPU scored 1,974 in Cinebench 2024 multi-core, 62% above Apple’s base M4 and 15% above the M4 Pro, though its 161 single-core score remained behind the M4.

Graphics improved substantially over the original Snapdragon X chips. The X2 Elite Extreme scored 5,628 in 3DMark Steel Nomad Light, 53% above Intel Lunar Lake, and was 30% faster than Apple’s M4 in Solar Bay. However, performance was roughly half that of an Nvidia RTX 5050, and game compatibility on ARM Windows remains a concern. Qualcomm also claims significant improvements in Adobe applications, but these were not independently tested.

The results came from a relatively large 16-inch reference system, so retail laptops, especially smaller models, may perform differently. Standard X2 Elite systems were unavailable for testing.

The lineup includes two 18-core chips and one 12-core chip. All feature an 80-TOPS neural processor, but the Extreme model offers higher memory bandwidth intended to accelerate AI workloads. Real-world performance and comparisons await shipping devices.

President Donald Trump told young TikTok users they “owe” him for preserving the platform in the U.S. Trump, who sought to ban TikTok in 2020, recently approved a pending deal allowing a consortium including Larry Ellison, Rupert Murdoch, and Michael Dell to control and restructure its American operations. The passage presents a quantum framework for generalized linear model (GLM) sparsification, which replaces a large dataset with a smaller weighted subset preserving the loss within a multiplicative \(1\pm\varepsilon\) factor. It applies to proper loss functions satisfying auto-Lipschitz and lower-homogeneity conditions, covering linear, multiple, ridge, Lasso, Huber, \(\ell_p\), and \(\gamma_p\) regression.

The main algorithm constructs, with high probability, an \(\widetilde O(n\log(s_{\max}/s_{\min})/\varepsilon^2)\)-sparse approximation in time
\[
\widetilde O\!\left((n^\omega+nr^2+r\sqrt{mn}/\varepsilon)\log(s_{\max}/s_{\min})\right),
\]
where \(m\) is the sample count, \(n\) the dimension, and \(r\) the row sparsity. For homogeneous losses such as \(\ell_p\), dependence on the scale ratio can be removed. When \(\varepsilon\) is constant and \(m\gg n\), the framework provides a quadratic speedup in \(m\) over cited classical methods.

The approach introduces multiscale leverage score overestimates as importance scores across different residual scales. A quantum algorithm computes these scores using recursive weight refinement and quantum leverage-score approximation. Quantum state preparation then samples rows according to unnormalized importance scores, while quantum sum estimation determines the normalization needed for reweighting. A separate initialization procedure constructs suitable starting weights by modifying the loss functions and applying quantum leverage-score approximation with binary search.

For \(p\in(0,2]\), both \(\ell_p(x)=|x|^p\) and the defined \(\gamma_p\) loss satisfy the required properness conditions. Their sparsifiers can be constructed in \(\widetilde O(r\sqrt{mn}/\varepsilon+n^\omega+nr^2)\) time, after which a classical solver operates on the reduced problem. The resulting algorithms approximately solve \(\ell_p\) and \(\gamma_p\) regression in \(\widetilde O(r\sqrt{mn}/\varepsilon)+\operatorname{poly}(n,1/\varepsilon)\) time. Linear regression is recovered at \(p=2\), Huber regression from \(\gamma_1\), while multiple, ridge, and Lasso regression are embedded into the GLM formulation through expanded matrices and appropriate losses.

DSS Consulting, founded in 1997 to support small school districts, faced stagnant growth as its founders reduced their involvement, client needs became more complex, and regional standards diverged. Under COO Meg Cooke, DSS reorganized from functional practice groups into regional cross-functional teams responsible for client relationships, service delivery, and product development, while smaller practice groups provided specialist support. The strategy aimed to reach larger districts and eliminate functional silos.

Chris Peterson, an experienced IT project manager, was chosen to lead the Southwest Region team. She selected skilled consultants who already knew and liked one another, co-located them early, and emphasized cohesion and focus. Drawing on shared client experiences, the team identified small districts’ need for an affordable integrated budgeting and planning system. Initial feedback from districts was generally positive, though questions about customization, price, and competing products complicated the design process. A team retreat helped restore focus and finalize specifications.

Development required support from DSS functional specialists, but the team often received limited assistance, particularly on complex issues. Meg expressed sympathy but did not intervene directly. Despite frustration and concerns about organizational politics, the team conducted independent research and completed a product ready for beta testing.

During an update meeting, Chris emphasized the product’s progress and her team’s effectiveness. However, she lacked detailed information about broader regional client needs and other teams’ services. She also acknowledged that the system, designed mainly for small districts, might not initially appeal to the larger districts central to DSS’s strategy.

The following Monday, Meg canceled the project, citing limited capacity to support new products, lack of interest reported by other regional teams, and doubts about demand from large districts. She also decided that the Southwest team would focus exclusively on marketing, undergo membership changes, and cease product development. Meg asked Chris whether she could lead the redirected team or preferred returning to the IT practice group.

Using SEER data from 2000–2018, this study analyzed overall survival and mortality among 24,849 U.S. patients with six soft-tissue sarcoma types, including heart cancer. Kaplan-Meier analysis, multivariable Cox models, and nomograms assessed demographic, tumor, stage, and treatment factors.

Median diagnosis age was 59; 56% were male and 82% white. Myxofibrosarcoma had the highest overall survival rate at 75%, while spindle cell sarcoma had the lowest at 37%. Increasing age, male sex, non-white race, higher tumor grade, and advanced stage negatively affected survival. Metastatic disease carried a 3.66-fold higher death hazard than localized disease.

Surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy were generally associated with lower mortality, with surgery showing the largest reduction. Primary systemic therapy produced conflicting results. Nomograms predicted five- and ten-year survival using patient characteristics, tumor factors, and treatment; predicted and observed outcomes were closely calibrated.

Limitations included unavailable clinicopathological and recurrence data, incomplete treatment details, missing confounders, short follow-up, and the need for external validation. The report is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed.

A December 2000 McKinsey memorandum provides a country-by-country update on global electric-power privatization and restructuring from June through November 2000.

Governments facing rising demand and limited public funds were increasingly opening generation to foreign investment, unbundling state utilities, and introducing wholesale and retail competition. Some international investors shifted toward lower-risk U.S. and European markets.

European liberalization was driven by the EU Directive, though implementation varied. Nordic markets were largely open and integrated through NordPool, while France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and others pursued phased access, asset sales, regulatory reform, and consolidation. Central and Eastern European countries were restructuring and privatizing utilities, often under IMF or EU-related pressure, but faced political, regulatory, and financial obstacles.

Asian economies were resuming reforms after the financial crisis. Australia, Japan, South Korea, New Zealand, Singapore, and others expanded competition or restructured state utilities. China, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, and the Philippines faced problems including weak guarantees, insolvent utilities, disputed power-purchase agreements, regulatory uncertainty, and investor withdrawals.

Latin American privatization had slowed because of inflation, currency instability, drought, ownership limits, labor conflict, and political uncertainty. Most major economies except Venezuela and Mexico had privatized generation and distribution to some extent. Several countries were offering transmission projects or assets, while approximately 75 million rural residents remained without grid access.

African and Middle Eastern governments increasingly permitted independent power producers, though few had advanced to broad privatization. Drought and dependence on hydropower created supply and pricing pressures. Regional transmission initiatives included networks linking countries in southern and western Africa, the eastern Mediterranean, and the Gulf. Several governments were considering utility unbundling, partial privatization, or increased private generation investment.

The address portrays the United States as recovering from the Great War, with renewed confidence, business activity, and prosperity. It credits national progress to sustained effort and argues that future success depends on learning from history, preserving American independence, and applying enduring principles of government and human relations.

In foreign affairs, the nation should remain politically independent while assisting humanity through relief, diplomacy, arbitration, international conferences, and adherence to the Permanent Court of International Justice. It should support international law, arms limitation, economic rehabilitation, and peaceful settlement of disputes while maintaining a modern, balanced defensive force. Permanent peace ultimately requires righteousness, religious conviction, brotherhood, and a genuine desire for peace.

At home, responsible political parties should faithfully implement the mandates received from voters. The address interprets the election as affirming constitutional guarantees, judicial determination of rights, private ownership, economy in government, tax reduction, and tax reform. Public waste burdens workers, while excessive tax rates discourage business and harm prosperity. Property rights carry duties of responsible production and conservation.

The nation is described as enjoying strong employment, high wages, improving transportation, and a recovering agricultural sector, aided by restrictive immigration and protective tariffs. Its central task is to preserve constitutional government, divided sovereignty, and independent branches. Citizens must obey laws they help create, while Congress and the President should cooperate in legislation.

The address also advocates national unity, racial tolerance, religious freedom, education, enterprise, resource development, justice, and peaceful relations. America is presented as seeking neither empire nor foreign dominion, but peace, prosperity, humanitarian service, and divine favor.

BART will expand its 14-member rapid response cleaning team by five and add a mobile biohazard reporting option after increasing complaints about discarded needles, including a report of a rider being pricked by a syringe. The lecture examines efficient natural structures, especially sandwich constructions and radial density gradients. Monocot leaves such as iris, cattail, and grasses use dense outer fibers separated by low-density cores or webs, providing stiffness at low weight. Tests on iris leaves produced stiffness predictions in the same order of magnitude as measurements, supporting their treatment as sandwich beams.

Other natural sandwich structures include sea kelp with buoyant honeycomb-like cores, lightweight bird skulls with trabecular bone between outer plates, cuttlefish shells with gas-filled compartments for buoyancy, and horseshoe crab and tortoise shells. These structures often serve multiple functions while minimizing material and weight.

Palm stems achieve mechanical efficiency differently. As palms grow taller without substantially increasing diameter, they add cell-wall layers, increasing tissue density. The densest material occurs near the outer surface, where bending stresses are greatest. Measurements showed that palm stiffness and strength increase strongly with density. Analysis indicated that this radial density gradient makes a stem about 2.5 times stiffer than uniformly distributing the same mass. Its strength distribution also closely matches its bending-stress distribution, avoiding excess material near the center. Bamboo similarly places denser material outside and less-dense material inside.

The study evaluates Temperature Scaling (TS) for calibrating CNN confidence in binary brain-tumor classification from T1-weighted MRI images under Gaussian, Poisson, Salt-and-Pepper, Speckle, and Uniform synthetic noise. A lightweight CNN was trained on a composite dataset from Figshare, SARTAJ, and Br35H, using normalized 256×256×3 images, augmentation, dropout, and stratified data splits. TS optimized a scalar temperature by minimizing Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL) on validation data.

Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, NLL, and Expected Calibration Error (ECE). Under most noisy conditions, TS reduced NLL and ECE while maintaining or slightly improving classification performance. On clean data, accuracy remained 0.98, while calibration produced only minor metric changes and slightly increased false negatives. Experiments with ResNet50 showed that TS also reduced calibration errors and generally improved false-positive and false-negative rates without reducing overall accuracy.

The study concludes that TS is a computationally efficient method for improving confidence reliability under varied noise conditions. Future work will test larger datasets and contemporary architectures, examine false-positive and false-negative reductions, and compare TS with adaptive, entropy-based, and sample-dependent calibration methods under changing noise and distribution shifts.

Cantor’s theorem states that every set \(A\) has strictly smaller cardinality than its power set \(\mathcal P(A)\). An injection sends each \(x\in A\) to \(\{x\}\). Assuming a surjection \(g:A\to\mathcal P(A)\), define \(B=\{x\in A:x\notin g(x)\}\). Surjectivity gives \(g(b)=B\) for some \(b\), producing the contradiction \(b\in g(b)\) if and only if \(b\notin g(b)\). Thus infinitely many distinct infinite cardinalities exist.

The lecture then begins characterizing \(\mathbb R\) as the unique ordered field containing \(\mathbb Q\) with the least upper bound property. An ordered set permits comparison of any two elements and has a transitive order. Upper and lower bounds, suprema, and infima are defined, with examples showing that suprema and infima need not belong to the subsets they bound.

An ordered set has the least upper bound property when every nonempty subset bounded above has a supremum. Finite ordered sets, the negative integers, and the integers have this property, but \(\mathbb Q\) does not. For \(E=\{q\in\mathbb Q:q>0,\ q^2<2\}\), any rational supremum \(x\) would need to satisfy \(x\ge1\) and \(x^2=2\). The lecture proves \(x^2\) cannot be less than \(2\) by constructing \(x+h\in E\), contradicting that \(x\) is an upper bound. The remaining case \(x^2>2\) is deferred.

RDRAND and RDSEED MMIO access is relatively slow, so latency-sensitive applications can seed software PRNGs with hardware-generated values. AMD’s Secure RNG library abstracts low-level Zen processor instructions, providing an API for applications such as cryptographic key generation.

Ford began exploring electric vehicles shortly after its 1903 founding but repeatedly abandoned EV projects over the following century. After discontinuing the Focus Electric in 2018, Ford sharply expanded planned EV investment, reaching $50 billion through 2026 and targeting EVs as 50% of global production by 2030. Its Mustang Mach-E, F-150 Lightning, and E-Transit initially generated strong demand and made Ford the second-largest U.S. EV seller by the end of 2021.

Momentum later weakened amid declining consumer enthusiasm and competitive pricing pressure. In October 2023, Ford delayed $12 billion of planned EV investment. Ford Model e, reported separately from conventional vehicle operations, recorded losses before interest and taxes of $0.9 billion in 2021, $2.1 billion in 2022, and $4.7 billion in 2023.

Ford’s 2023 R&D expense was $8.2 billion, compared with consolidated profit before interest and taxes of $5.5 billion. Under U.S. GAAP, Ford expenses R&D costs as incurred. Under IFRS, research costs are expensed, but qualifying development costs may be capitalized after technical and commercial feasibility is established, then amortized later. CFO John Lawler recognized that foreign competitors benefited from capitalizing portions of development spending.

This case study examined how two middle grades teacher candidates with ESL endorsements understood and used translanguaging during year-long Professional Development School placements. Translanguaging draws on multilingual learners’ complete linguistic repertoires for communication and learning, challenges monolingual classroom norms, and can support academic development, identity, inclusion, and belonging.

The participants, Patricia and Ruby, completed relevant coursework and more than 100 clinical hours with multilingual learners in different middle schools. Data collected over two academic years included four interviews per participant, course and supervision field notes, and classroom observations. Researchers analyzed the data through open, axial, and contrastive coding.

Both candidates viewed translanguaging positively and believed their coursework had provided useful strategies. However, they struggled to apply those strategies consistently. Patricia used peer support, translation technology, translated materials, and independent research but lacked confidence in fully implementing translanguaging. Ruby primarily used greetings, felt constrained by not speaking Spanish, and remained uncertain about adapting instruction. Their cooperating teachers also expressed positive attitudes but rarely modeled translanguaging, generally relying on English-only or translation-based practices.

The findings identify a gap between theoretical preparation and classroom practice. Coursework, positive beliefs, ESL endorsements, and extensive clinical experience did not ensure effective implementation. The study concludes that teacher preparation programs should also train cooperating teachers to create linguistically inclusive classrooms and model translanguaging. It recommends professional development for middle grades educators, stronger collaboration and co-teaching structures, and further research focused specifically on translanguaging with multilingual young adolescents.

NVIDIA’s fiscal 2021 third-quarter revenue rose 57% year over year to $4.73 billion, while net income increased 49% to $1.34 billion and diluted earnings per share reached $2.12. Nine-month revenue was $11.67 billion and net income was $2.88 billion. Graphics quarterly revenue grew 25% to $2.79 billion, and Compute & Networking revenue rose 146% to $1.94 billion. Gaming and Data Center revenue reached $2.27 billion and $1.90 billion, respectively.

NVIDIA completed its $7.13 billion Mellanox acquisition in April 2020; Mellanox contributed 13% of quarterly revenue. It also agreed to acquire Arm for a transaction valued at $40 billion, with closing expected in early 2022 subject to approvals. At October 25, 2020, NVIDIA reported $26.88 billion in assets, $15.33 billion in shareholders’ equity, and $10.14 billion in cash, equivalents, and marketable securities. NVIDIA noted that COVID-19 strengthened Gaming and Data Center demand but created supply-chain uncertainty.

HCPEA named Dr. Terry Woodward its next president. A director since 2014, Woodward co-founded Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan’s healthcare private equity practice in 2009 and previously led venture capital, growth equity, R&D and corporate development initiatives. HCPEA’s members collectively manage over $1 trillion and have started more than 1,500 healthcare businesses.

Cboe Global Markets launched bitcoin futures trading, marking the first bitcoin-backed security offered on a government-regulated exchange. Heavy website traffic followed, though trading systems operated normally. Bitcoin rose about 8% shortly after trading began, surpassing $15,700 and later $16,000, while futures contracts expiring the next month traded above $18,000. Futures allow investors to speculate on bitcoin’s price without owning it and make betting against it easier. Bitcoin had risen roughly 1,500% that year but remained highly volatile, prompting warnings from economists and financiers that it was a bubble or fraud. Industry insiders expected broader acceptance, while one attorney suggested futures could help rationalize its price.

Billionaire investor Jeff Greene said low Federal Reserve interest rates and its $4.5 trillion balance sheet fueled the long-running stock rally. He warned that Republican fiscal policies, including tax cuts and infrastructure spending, could raise rates and slow the economy, potentially ending the bull market. Greene argued that cheap borrowing stimulates investors more than tax cuts. However, he described economic growth as weak and said interest rates would likely rise very slowly.

North American cannabis stocks fell sharply, with the North American Marijuana Index down 27.2%, driven largely by Canadian stocks. More than $1.2 billion in Canadian producer offerings and concerns over Aphria’s Nuuvera acquisition reportedly weakened investor confidence. The U.S. Marijuana Index declined 18.1%, while major cannabis ETFs lost 19.2% to 29.61%. Individual stocks including Aurora Cannabis, Cronos, Canopy Growth, Aphria and THC Biomed dropped more than 30%.

Industry developments included MassRoots raising $4.75 million, DOJA Cannabis and Tokyo Smoke merging into Hiku Brands, Jane West launching a crowdfunding campaign, and the creation of new cannabis stock indexes. Canopy launched a $50 million venture fund, iAnthus acquired Citiva for about $18 million, and ABCANN announced a $70 million bought deal.

The UAE delayed Barakah nuclear plant’s first reactor launch to late 2019 or early 2020. Once complete, four reactors will generate 5,600 megawatts, meeting about 25 percent of national electricity demand and supporting clean-energy targets.

MIT’s 14.271 introduces industrial organization theory and empirical methods, emphasizing their interaction. The course generally presents theory on Wednesdays and related empirical work on Mondays. Industrial organization is inherently theoretical because major policy questions, such as breaking up technology firms, cannot be tested through repeated natural experiments. Empirical analysis helps determine which theoretical assumptions and predicted effects fit observed behavior and how models should be refined.

A single-product monopolist maximizes revenue minus cost by setting marginal revenue equal to marginal cost. Its Lerner index—the markup as a share of price—equals the negative inverse of demand elasticity. Thus, firms with market power base pricing on demand elasticity rather than demand levels. Monopoly creates deadweight loss by preventing trades where willingness to pay exceeds production cost. Other possible concerns include productive inefficiency, quality distortions, rent-seeking, and transfers from consumers to firms. Standard IO models usually assume quasi-linear preferences and set aside income effects and equity concerns.

Multiproduct firms must price their goods as a system. A price change for one product can divert sales toward or away from another product, so markups depend on cross-product effects and profits from related goods. For substitutes, such as differently colored phones, diversion to another product owned by the same firm can justify higher markups. For complements, such as printers and ink or phones and accessories, firms may price one product below cost to increase sales of a highly profitable complementary product. Google’s search profits similarly help explain payments to become the default search engine.

For product quality, a monopolist chooses quality by equating its marginal cost with the marginal consumer’s willingness to pay for improvement. A social planner instead considers average benefits across consumers. Monopoly quality can therefore differ from socially optimal quality because the monopolist focuses on marginal buyers and serves fewer consumers. With identical consumers, however, the marginal and average consumer coincide, producing a strong optimal-quality result.

For durable goods, a monopolist with commitment power should set the monopoly price initially and commit not to make later sales rather than progressively lowering prices. Selling later at lower prices encourages forward-looking consumers to delay purchases. Real-world price declines may reflect preferences for early access or exclusivity, falling production costs, technological improvement, learning, capacity constraints, or inability to commit to future prices. Without commitment, firms lower prices over time and earn less profit.

The Coase conjecture states that, under certain conditions, a durable-goods monopolist’s profits approach zero as opportunities to revise prices become arbitrarily frequent. However, this outcome may be avoided because price changes and consumer purchases take time, firms develop reputations, new high-value consumers enter, consumers may not be fully forward-looking, and firms can use rentals, best-price guarantees, or capacity limits.

Information design examines how firms or intermediaries control product information. Some markets provide detailed attributes, while others, such as mattresses or wholesale used cars, provide little information. A monopolist may profit by withholding information because uncertainty makes consumers more homogeneous and allows greater surplus extraction, though this can reduce social surplus. Intermediaries such as Amazon or Yelp may instead design partial information to increase consumer surplus. In the sandwich example, categorizing consumers as having low, medium, or high values can induce a lower monopoly price and raise both consumer surplus and monopoly profit relative to full information.

The next lecture will complete information design, followed by empirical papers on monopoly pricing by Chevalier-Goolsbee and Gentzkow-Shapiro.

Britain’s FTSE 100 rose 0.6% to 7,353.89, recovering from a three-month low as banks and miners gained amid easing North Korea tensions. Mid caps climbed 0.8%. TUI reached a record high after a Credit Suisse upgrade, while Morgan Stanley downgrades pushed Experian and G4S lower. Weak energy shares limited gains as oil prices retreated.

On May 29, 1865, President Andrew Johnson appointed William W. Holden provisional governor of North Carolina to help loyal residents restore a republican state government and constitutional relations with the federal government. Holden was authorized to convene a convention of loyal delegates to amend the state constitution. Convention voters and delegates were required to take the presidential amnesty oath and meet North Carolina’s voting qualifications in effect before May 20, 1861. The convention or subsequent legislature would determine future qualifications for voting and holding office. Johnson directed military and naval personnel to assist without obstructing reorganization. He also ordered federal departments to restore state, revenue, postal, judicial, naval, and interior operations in North Carolina, generally preferring qualified loyal residents for appointments. Federal courts were to resume proceedings, enforce justice, and confiscate property subject to federal law.

Divergence trading compares price action with oscillators or other indicators to identify potential momentum shifts, reversals, or trend continuations. Classical divergence occurs when price makes a lower low while the indicator makes a higher low, or price makes a higher high while the indicator makes a lower high. Hidden divergence occurs when price makes a higher low while the indicator makes a lower low in an uptrend, or price makes a lower high while the indicator makes a higher high in a downtrend.

Common indicators include RSI, MACD, Stochastic Oscillator, and CCI, as well as price- and volume-based measures. No indicator is universally best; traders should backtest indicators for specific markets. Volume can strengthen or weaken divergence signals by showing the level of market participation.

The strategy may offer early indications of market changes, clear entry and exit signals, and applicability across instruments, time frames, and trading styles. Confirmation through candlestick patterns, trendline breaks, other indicators, market context, and volume can reduce false signals. Key risks include misunderstanding divergence, relying on it alone, overtrading, poor risk management, and emotional decisions.

Examples include bullish Nasdaq 100 and Tesla signals during the March 2020 crash, a bearish S&P 500 signal before the pandemic decline, and a hidden bearish Nasdaq 100 signal in December 2018. A simple S&P 500 ETF backtest produced favorable profit factors and Sharpe ratios across several settings, low drawdowns, and one losing year, but had relatively few trades and possible curve fitting.

Power traces should be short, direct, and thick, with closely placed power components and aligned switching-current loops to reduce inductance, losses, noise, ringing, and EMI. Ground planes are required; high-di/dt output currents should use a dedicated power-ground section, while analog circuitry and VREF connect to signal ground. VCC and VREF require high-frequency ceramic bypass capacitors, and vias should be sized for current.

TI provides documentation updates and support forums, warns that ESD can damage the device, and supplies mechanical, packaging, ordering, material, and part-marking information subject to change. Preproduction parts may be unqualified and sold without warranties. TI provides technical resources “as is”; developers are responsible for product selection, design validation, testing, and compliance.

The Tenth Circuit affirmed dismissal of Charles A. Meeker’s § 1983 claims arising from a New Mexico child abuse investigation that transferred custody of his four daughters to the Human Services Department. The court declined to consider the daughters’ purported appeal, holding that a nonattorney parent may not represent minor children under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 17(c) and 28 U.S.C. § 1654. It adopted the district court’s conclusions that claims against most defendants were barred by res judicata following unsuccessful prior actions and that service was invalid as to four defendants. The court also held that the daughters’ guardian ad litem was not acting under color of state law because her independent professional duty and undivided loyalty were owed to the minors rather than the state. All defendants’ motions to affirm were granted.

The Missouri Court of Appeals affirmed summary judgment for the Bank of St. Louis and its employees in Harvey F. Euge’s malicious prosecution action seeking actual and punitive damages. Euge had been convicted of obtaining money through a bogus check, but the Missouri Supreme Court later reversed the conviction because the check was drawn on an existing account containing funds and therefore was not “bogus” under the applicable statute.

Euge argued that the reversal established lack of probable cause, that the indictment was improperly procured using false information, and that probable cause was a jury question. The court held that a conviction creates a presumption of probable cause even when later reversed, unless obtained through false testimony, fraud, or other improper means. Euge did not dispute the underlying facts and challenged only their legal effect. Because undisputed facts made probable cause a legal question, the court determined probable cause existed as a matter of law. The unusual statutory interpretation leading to reversal could not reasonably have been anticipated by those reporting Euge’s conduct. Consequently, Euge could not establish the absence of probable cause required for malicious prosecution.

The paper introduces video object segmentation-aware audio generation, a Foley synthesis task that generates sound for a user-selected object rather than an entire scene. The proposed Segmentation-Aware Generative Audio Network (SAGANet) extends the pretrained MMAudio model with a lightweight control module conditioned on text, video, and object segmentation masks. It combines global video context with cropped, localized views through shared Synchformer features and gated cross-attention, while keeping most pretrained parameters frozen. Optional LoRA fine-tuning adapts relevant audio-generator attention layers.

The authors also present Segmented Music Solos, containing 5,395 training, 665 validation, and 745 test clips across more than 25 instruments. Its five-second clips include object labels and frame-level segmentation masks. Training data combines solo performances from MUSIC21, AVSBench, and Solos, while testing uses multi-instrument URMP recordings with separate ground-truth audio tracks. A pipeline verifies visual and auditory object presence and generates masks using Florence-2, GroundedSAM2, and SAM2.

Although trained only on single-source videos, SAGANet generalizes to multi-source test scenes and generates audio for the segmented instrument. Compared with MMAudio, it improves distribution matching, audio quality, semantic alignment, and especially temporal synchronization. LoRA fine-tuning provides further gains on most metrics. Ablations indicate that combining global context with localized visual information produces the strongest semantic and temporal performance.

Tom Petty’s cause of death was deferred pending further tests after his cardiac arrest and autopsy. The 66-year-old died after his family switched off life support upon learning he had no brain activity. Musicians and fans paid tribute to the Heartbreakers and Traveling Wilburys star.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they were ready to prevent regional oil exports if US measures halted Iranian oil sales, supporting President Hassan Rouhani’s threat to disrupt neighbouring countries’ shipments. Iranian officials have previously threatened to block the Strait of Hormuz. Washington withdrew from the 2015 nuclear deal and ordered countries to stop importing Iranian oil by November 4 or face financial measures. Iran’s Opec governor warned the policy would raise global oil prices and harm US consumers. The European Union hopes to preserve the nuclear accord despite sanctions, while Rouhani said Iran would remain if other signatories guaranteed its benefits. Their foreign ministers planned talks in Vienna.

The RSPCA investigated 2,902 animal cruelty complaints in Nottinghamshire in 2017, averaging eight daily and down about 8% from 2016. Cases included two kittens beaten to death, for which their owner was jailed for 20 weeks, and 40 animals found in stacked cages without food, water, bedding or toys. Five dogs were euthanized, while most surviving animals entered RSPCA care or were rehomed. Dogs accounted for most complaints, followed by cats and horses. Nationally, 141,760 animal welfare complaints were investigated.

The Gretna Trust & Savings Bank, executor of Priscilla Lewis’s succession, sought recovery of $505.58 withdrawn by her son David after her death, plus alleged rent. David claimed the funds repaid loans he had made to his mother. The court held that the money belonged to the succession and that David, as a creditor, could not satisfy his claim by taking estate assets but must present it through succession proceedings. The rent claim was not proven. The dismissal was reversed, and judgment was entered against David for $505.58, legal interest, and court costs.

GST authorities reportedly demanded over Rs 6,000 crore from banks for free or bundled services to customers maintaining minimum balances, valuing them using charges imposed on customers who fail to do so. Banks are expected to challenge the retrospective five-year demand, arguing such charges are deterrents rather than service costs. If upheld, banks may pass the costs to customers.

A Karolinska Institutet study of 27,500 middle-aged and older UK Biobank participants linked poorer self-reported sleep to older-looking brains on MRI scans analyzed with machine learning. Each one-point decline in a five-factor sleep score corresponded to a roughly six-month increase in the gap between biological and chronological brain age; poor sleepers’ brains appeared one year older on average. Low-grade inflammation explained just over 10% of the association. Researchers suggest healthier sleep might help prevent accelerated brain aging and cognitive decline, but noted limitations including self-reported sleep and the UK Biobank’s healthier-than-average population.

The report links the saying “Sell in May and come back in November” to recurring Treasury liquidity patterns rather than seasons, holidays, or horse races. Treasury cash-balance data from 2006–2017 show recurring peaks around January, May, and November. January activity involves Federal Reserve reverse repurchase operations. May’s more consistent liquidity increase is attributed to government tax refunds, which the author argues disproportionately reach wealthy recipients likely to invest in stocks, bonds, and real estate. This may produce a stock-market rise that investors can sell before relatively flat summer fiscal flows.

November liquidity is associated with Federal Reserve Treasury buybacks, potentially directing former bondholders’ funds into stocks and contributing to a Christmas rally. The strength of these effects depends on the size of fiscal flows and varies by year. The author suggests 2018 and 2019 could see particularly strong May effects because of tax-law changes, while February and November patterns may strengthen when the federal funds rate changes. Further research is proposed on those patterns. The author discloses no positions in the securities mentioned and no related business relationships.

A 14-year-old girl was charged with mischief after allegedly damaging her grandmother’s home during an outburst over a broken phone. Police apprehended her following a foot chase, and she was released to her mother pending a court date.

The work proposes an ontology-based method for robots to compare valid competing plans, infer which is preferable, and explain the differences to humans. It extends the OCRA ontology with plan qualities—cost, expected makespan, and number of tasks—and relations describing whether qualities and plans are better, worse, or equivalent. Logical rules compare quality values and infer plan-level relations, while a ROSPlan- and KnowRob-based framework instantiates plans and performs reasoning.

The proposed ACXON algorithm retrieves divergent knowledge about pairs of plans from a time-indexed knowledge graph and constructs textual contrastive narratives at three specificity levels. It removes repeated and non-divergent information, then applies casting, clustering, ordering, and grouping to generate explanations. Although developed for plans, the algorithm can compare other ontological entities.

ACXON was evaluated against the AXON baseline using 30 plan pairs from three temporal-planning domains. It produced statistically significant reductions in knowledge tuples and communication time, particularly at higher specificity levels, without major construction-time differences. However, detailed narratives remained lengthy, and readability generally required college-level comprehension. A proposed refinement restricts retrieval to selected ontological classes, enabling shorter and potentially personalized explanations. Future work includes improving linguistic accessibility, conducting user studies, learning user preferences, and investigating when robots should explain plans relative to physical execution.

The United States and Russia welcome the Israeli and Palestinian leaders’ declaration of principles on interim Palestinian self-government. The agreement builds on earlier peace efforts at Camp David and Madrid and seeks to reconcile Israeli security with Palestinian hopes. Praising the courage of Israeli, Palestinian, Norwegian, and past American leaders, the speaker pledges active U.S. support for implementation. Despite expected opposition and difficulties, the accord is presented as an opportunity for mutual recognition, regional cooperation, economic development, and a peaceful future for Israeli and Arab children.

Weak gravitational lensing provides percent-level constraints on the structure-growth parameter \(S_8\), but cosmological inference is limited by intrinsic galaxy alignments (IA), baryonic feedback, and the degeneracy between \(\Omega_m\) and \(\sigma_8\). Unmodelled or inaccurately modelled IA can substantially bias results. Existing IA descriptions include non-linear alignment, density-weighted alignment, tidal torque, combined TATT, halo, and effective-field-theory models. Observations suggest strong alignments for bright red galaxies and little alignment for blue galaxies, though survey selection complicates generalisation.

The paper introduces a pipeline that inserts NLA, extended-NLA, tidal-torque, and a new extended tidal-torque model into a common large N-body simulation. It also couples tidal fields to galaxies generated through halo occupation distributions to assess realistic non-linear galaxy bias. The resulting shear catalogues support validation of two-point predictions, investigation of IA effects on non-Gaussian lensing statistics, and study of source clustering with linear and non-linear biased tracers.

Two-point shear correlations are predicted from the matter power spectrum using the Limber approximation and measured from simulated galaxy ellipticities. The analysis adopts an LSST Year-1 redshift distribution divided into five tomographic bins, uses unit galaxy weights, and generally omits shape noise. Because two-point statistics do not fully describe non-linear matter structure, the work also generates convergence and aperture-mass maps to examine complementary non-Gaussian statistics, using Kaiser–Squires mass reconstruction on spherical Healpix maps.

Oil fell below US$56 after the API reported a larger-than-expected 9.9-million-barrel rise in U.S. crude inventories, raising doubts that production cuts have tightened supply. Brent declined to US$55.62 and U.S. crude to US$52.84. OPEC achieved over 90 per cent compliance with output curbs in January, but rising U.S. stocks, recovering U.S. production, uneven OPEC adherence and smaller non-OPEC cuts limited price gains. A stronger U.S. dollar also pressured oil prices.

Tesla’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2019 reported quarterly revenue of $6.30 billion, gross profit of $1.19 billion, operating income of $261 million and net income attributable to common stockholders of $143 million, or $0.78 per diluted share. For the first nine months, revenue was $17.19 billion and net loss attributable to common stockholders was $967 million.

At September 30, Tesla had $32.80 billion in assets, including $5.34 billion in cash and equivalents, and $25.31 billion in liabilities. Nine-month operating cash flow was $980 million, investing used $1.03 billion and financing provided $1.61 billion. Tesla designs and sells electric vehicles, solar generation and energy storage products through automotive and energy segments. It acquired Maxwell Technologies for $207 million and adopted new lease-accounting rules. As of October 21, 2019, 180,244,858 common shares were outstanding.
A collection of quotations criticizes taxation, debt-driven banking, corporate tax avoidance, patriotism, inequality, and educational control, while emphasizing learning from mistakes.

Harvard visiting law professor Carlos Portugal Gouvêa was arrested Oct. 1 after firing a pellet gun near a Jewish temple during Yom Kippur, prompting a lockdown. He said he was hunting rats. Charged with several offenses, including property damage, he was placed on administrative leave. Police and synagogue officials said antisemitism was not a factor.

The paper presents a general method for constructing codensity presentations of monads through the principle “Codensity Monads = Density + Duality.” A codensity setting factors a functor through a dual equivalence, the opposite of a dense functor, and a contravariant right adjoint. Its main theorem states that, in every such setting, the monad induced by the dual adjunction is isomorphic to the pointwise codensity monad of the original functor. This reduces difficult codensity proofs to typically better-understood density and duality results.

The framework gives shorter, uniform derivations of many known presentations and several new ones. Applications include ultrafilter and filter monads on sets and topological spaces; neighbourhood and double-dualization monads; Isbell duality; Vietoris, lower Vietoris, and sobrification monads; and probability-related monads such as the expectation, Giry, Radon, Kantorovich, and finite-semiring-valued measure monads. For probability monads, integral representation theorems identify the required dual adjunction and isolate where measure-theoretic arguments are needed.

The paper also reviews monads, algebraic categories, dual adjunctions, dense functors, Kan extensions, and codensity monads. It concludes by proposing extensions to monads in 2-categories, monad extensions, comparisons with earlier general ultrafilter results, and further applications to Vietoris variants and probabilistic powerdomains.

Jacob Hackin became the first person prosecuted in Cambridge for failing to clear up dog fouling after ignoring a fixed penalty notice issued at Midsummer Common. He pleaded guilty and was ordered to pay a £75 fine, £125 council costs and a £30 victim surcharge. The council said the prosecution should deter others.

Kelly Keefe will become the first woman to lead ERC in its 97-year history when she succeeds longtime president Pat Perry on Jan. 1. Keefe has worked at ERC for nearly 13 years and currently oversees training, consulting, and coaching services. Perry will remain chairman, assisting with the transition and several programs. Keefe previously spent eight years at Deloitte and plans to continue ERC’s regional and national impact.

The passage commemorates Henry Clay as a nationally influential statesman whose public career spanned nearly half a century. Born in Virginia in 1777 with limited formal education, Clay became a Kentucky lawyer, state legislator, U.S. representative and House speaker, senator, peace commissioner, and secretary of state. Although repeatedly defeated for the presidency, he retained widespread political support and influence.

Clay is praised for combining eloquence, judgment, determination, patriotism, and devotion to liberty. He promoted the War of 1812, helped secure Missouri’s admission to the Union, and devised compromises during the Nullification crisis and disputes over slavery in territories acquired from Mexico. The passage presents him as a leader especially trusted during national crises and committed to preserving the Union by balancing sectional interests.

Clay supported struggles for liberty in Greece and South America. Though a slaveholder, he opposed slavery in principle, advocated gradual emancipation in Kentucky, and rejected both immediate abolition that threatened the Union and arguments denying human equality. As an early member and longtime president of the American Colonization Society, he supported gradually ending slavery while relocating free Black Americans to Africa. The tribute concludes that Clay’s leadership substantially contributed to the country’s prosperity, power, and preservation.

Microsoft’s Form 8-K reports a January 30, 2017 underwriting agreement for a $17 billion public offering of senior unsecured notes. The offering comprises seven tranches: $1.5 billion at 1.850% due 2020; $1.75 billion at 2.400% due 2022; $2.25 billion at 2.875% due 2024; $4 billion at 3.300% due 2027; $2.5 billion at 4.100% due 2037; $3 billion at 4.250% due 2047; and $2 billion at 4.500% due 2057. Interest is payable semiannually on February 6 and August 6, beginning August 6, 2017. The notes will rank equally with Microsoft’s other unsecured, unsubordinated debt and may be redeemed under circumstances specified in the prospectus supplement. They will be issued under Microsoft’s 2009 base indenture, supplemented by a twelfth supplemental indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company as trustee.

Former CIA officer Kevin Mallory, 60, is accused of giving a Chinese agent classified information, including details about human assets, for $25,000. Prosecutors said undeclared cash found after a Shanghai trip and messages on a Chinese-provided phone revealed his espionage, while searches uncovered secret documents, some sent to the recruiter. The defense argued Mallory was trying to expose the Chinese operation by providing false documents and had alerted CIA contacts before the airport search prosecutors say prompted his cover story. CIA witnesses confirmed Mallory contacted them in February 2017, though testimony differed about his purpose. Mallory is on trial in Virginia under an espionage statute carrying a possible life sentence.

Restoration Affiliates (RA) was founded in 2011 by leaders of four independent restoration and reconstruction companies, including Rich Piltch of ARS. Guided by a “Go-Giver” philosophy, RA sought to help regional firms compete with national providers by jointly offering nationwide coverage, sharing resources during catastrophes, and maintaining local expertise. By fall 2013, it had 21 members with combined revenue of $300 million.

The restoration industry was fragmented but increasingly pressured by national companies, franchises, and third-party administrators. Large insurers and property managers preferred fewer providers capable of serving multiple locations. ARS had reduced its reliance on insurers by developing direct relationships with property managers, offering priority service agreements, training, disaster planning, continuous live telephone coverage, and detailed project updates.

RA operated as a limited liability corporation whose members were equal shareholders. A nine-person board governed the organization, supported by committees. Full members generally needed at least $5 million in annual revenue, commercial restoration capabilities, appropriate insurance, dedicated marketing personnel, and compliance with service and communication standards. Members paid annual and marketing dues plus referral fees; smaller firms could join as associates under different terms.

RA lacked an integrated system for assigning and tracking jobs, referrals, and communications. It also had to choose how to market competing disaster-planning software developed by two members. Interest in RA’s coverage and technology helped the group secure a three-year nationwide contract with Forest City Enterprises.

Despite this success, RA faced unresolved strategic issues: how much authority to give its administrator versus its board; how to ensure member accountability and information sharing; whether customers should contact RA centrally or established member relationships; how to standardize service, pricing, and technology across independent firms; whether referral fees supported or undermined cooperation; how to define customer ownership and manage overlapping territories; and how to market RA against national competitors. Piltch viewed RA as a low-risk growth strategy but wanted other members to assume greater leadership responsibility.

Sen. John McCain criticized President Trump’s approval of the GOP-Nunes memo’s release, calling it a partisan attack on the FBI and Justice Department that benefited Putin and undermined the rule of law. The memo alleges FBI surveillance abuses involving former Trump adviser Carter Page. Democrats and some Republicans condemned its release, while Democrats sought publication of their own memo.

Thabane Sigadla, 24, was sentenced to 38 years in prison after being convicted of two carjackings and possessing an unlicensed firearm and ammunition. Police arrested him in June 2017 after a New Germany hijacking and linked him to a 2016 KwaDabeka case.

A broker sued a purchaser for commission after unsuccessfully attempting to secure acceptable purchase terms. Another broker obtained an offer the purchaser accepted. Because no special contract required the purchaser to pay commission and the plaintiff did not procure the sale, the judgment for plaintiff was reversed and a new trial granted.

Azerbaijan’s Health Ministry rejected US warnings against surgery in Azerbaijan and concerns about tuberculosis. Spokesperson Safaya Ahmadova said foreigners receive high-quality treatment, tuberculosis rates are declining, and the Global Fund supports the statistics. The US also advised travelers to bring sufficient prescription medicine.

The President transmits correspondence concerning Hawaii and notes the islands’ growing civilization, developing government, strategic Pacific location, and importance to American shipping, especially whaling. Although the Hawaiian Government remains weak, it appears peaceful and committed to education, religion, morality, and other institutions. The United States seeks no exclusive control but supports Hawaiian independence, security, and prosperity and would oppose another power’s attempt to seize or colonize the islands. Congress is urged to fund the American consul sufficiently to protect citizens and address complaints involving them.

In China, Britain’s treaty has opened four additional ports to British commerce without determining access for other nations. Given substantial and growing American trade with China, the United States should seek its own arrangements. The opening of new ports may increase demand for American goods, despite China’s inexpensive labor and established habits. Because no American agent presently provides adequate oversight, Congress is asked to fund a commissioner in China to protect American persons, property, and commercial interests, communicate with local and imperial authorities when authorized, and receive compensation appropriate to the mission’s importance.

The disclosure describes a virtual object machine learning system that generates labeled synthetic training data from rigged 3D models to classify dynamic subjects, poses, and gestures. Models such as hands or dogs are programmatically varied by pose, texture, background, lighting, and camera position. Model markers and regions of interest provide metadata for key points, enabling supervised training without manually labeling large image sets. A rendering engine iterates through combinations of models, gestures, textures, and environmental variables, including spherical high-dynamic-range backgrounds, to produce diverse training images.

A machine learning engine trains classifiers using methods such as support vector machines, K-nearest neighbors, logistic regression, neural networks, or unsupervised schemes. Trained models receive images or video, detect key points, classify objects and poses, and may generate pixel masks or key-point data for other systems. Processing can be divided between servers and client devices.

The system may be integrated into a networked messaging platform containing client applications, server applications, image processing, social networking, annotations, content collections, and ephemeral timers. Detected gestures or poses can trigger media overlays; for example, recognizing a hand gesture or a playful dog pose may cause corresponding text to be added before publication.
