The disclosure also details message structures, database records, temporary access controls, software architecture, and computing hardware capable of implementing these functions.

*Upgrade* blends science fiction, horror, and action in a near-future story about Grey Trace, a technology-averse mechanic left paralyzed after a brutal attack. An experimental processor called STEM restores his movement with machine-like precision, enabling him to pursue revenge while raising questions about artificial intelligence, bodily control, and technological danger. The review praises the film’s believable futuristic world, philosophical themes, intense but purposeful violence, strong action scenes, and depiction of STEM controlling Grey’s body. However, its central mystery is predictable, and the ninety-five-minute runtime leaves insufficient room for exposition and dramatic development. Despite these drawbacks, the film is described as highly entertaining, successful across multiple genres, and Leigh Whannell’s best since *Saw*.

Nanyang Polytechnic scientists developed a method to convert coffee waste into biodegradable plastic. Water and Cupriavidus necator bacteria are added to locally roasted “Nanyang coffee” waste and left for seven to 10 days, producing the biopolymer PHA. The bacteria works at room temperature, reducing energy needs.

Researchers replaced conventional heavy extraction solvents with cheaper, environmentally friendly acetone and an alkaline solvent. After genetically modifying the bacteria to improve yields, they achieved more than 50 per cent purity, obtaining roughly 1g to 3g of pure PHA from 100g of coffee waste.

PHA decomposes faster and releases fewer toxic compounds than PVC. Having completed laboratory experiments begun in 2013, the team is seeking industrial partners and aims to commercialise the process within three to five years.

The Iowa Supreme Court held that Gary Kehde was not required to seek rehearing before obtaining judicial review of his unemployment-benefits denial. It further held that Dubuque Packing Company’s withdrawal of its protest did not affect eligibility, which depended on the underlying facts. Substantial evidence showed Kehde possessed a lit marijuana cigarette on company premises, deliberately violating lawful workplace expectations and creating safety risks. This constituted employment-related misconduct under Iowa law, regardless of whether he knew the specific company rule. The court reversed the district court’s award of benefits and remanded for an order disqualifying Kehde.

A regulation American football field measures 120 yards by 53.3 yards, including two 10-yard end zones, while the main playing area is 100 yards long. Goal lines define the end zones, and a ball must cross their plane for a touchdown. Yard lines mark field position, with full-width lines every five yards and numbers generally every ten yards. Hash marks determine ball placement and vary by level: 18 feet 6 inches apart in the NFL, 40 feet in college, and 53 feet 4 inches in high school. Sideline numbers also vary in distance from the boundary: 12 yards in the NFL, 9 yards in college, and usually 6 yards in high school. Six-foot-wide boundaries define the field and help protect participants, while coaching areas are commonly restricted between the 25-yard lines.

STAT’s biotech newsletter highlights a request by U.K. patient groups for an antitrust investigation into drugmakers’ investment halts, alongside news on the U.S. government shutdown, pharmaceutical tariffs and pricing, women’s health, autism treatment, drug trials, FDA regulation, and major biotech therapies and investments.

The IMF praised Ghana’s “Ghana beyond Aid” vision and economic performance as an inspiration to Africa. Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta said domestic revenue mobilisation and investment in job-creating sectors would support sustained growth and achieve the agenda within a generation.

AI-Noether is an abductive reasoning system designed to reconcile data-derived scientific formulae with incomplete or incorrect background theory. It assumes axioms and hypotheses are real polynomial equations and generates candidate axioms that augment or replace existing theory so a target hypothesis becomes derivable.

The method has three stages: encode known axioms and the hypothesis as an ideal and its solution variety; decompose the variety into irreducible components using primary decomposition; and reason over component generators using Gröbner bases and variable elimination to identify candidate missing axioms. It requires neither observations for missing axioms nor prior knowledge of their variables and can report when no single candidate suffices.

Tests on scientific systems including Kepler’s law, Compton scattering, Einstein relations, escape velocity, light damping, Hagen–Poiseuille flow, neutrino decay, Hall effects, and the carrier-resolved photo-Hall effect recovered nearly all individually removed axioms. Recovery of pairs and triples was less reliable, with success rates of 25–60%, particularly declining when three axioms were absent. A sufficient recoverability criterion is provided using ideals of equal height and common minimal associated primes. Future work includes extending the approach to non-polynomial laws such as ordinary and partial differential equations and applying it to new data-driven discoveries.

The court held that German Christmas tree ornaments exported after January 1, 1938, should be appraised at invoice unit prices plus 3% social assessments and, when excluded from invoice prices, packing, containers, coverings, and shipment-preparation expenses reported as dutiable. The parties stipulated that the merchandise and market conditions matched those in F. W. Woolworth Co. Other portions of the appeal were dismissed as abandoned.

MoviePass says its low-cost subscription is measurably affecting box office results. Its purchases represented 13.21% of the opening weekend domestic gross for *Roman J. Israel, Esq.* and 10% for *Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri*, while its share increased during the second weeks of several other films. The company also signed a performance-based marketing agreement with an unnamed independent distributor to promote a particular film and earn revenue from increased ticket sales. This advertising strategy aligns with MoviePass owner Helios and Matheson Analytics’ plan to collect viewing data and target subscribers with marketing. MoviePass declined to identify the distributor.

China’s stricter standards and reduced acceptance of contaminated recyclables have created challenges for Canadian municipalities. MRC Vaudreuil-Soulanges, which generates about 17,000 tonnes of recyclables annually, reassured residents that Tricentris continues to process materials successfully by investing in quality improvements and market diversification. Officials urged citizens to keep recycling while improving sorting quality, supported by the online tool tricycle-mrcvs.ca and the Tricentris Express newsletter.

Asteroid 2025 TF, measuring 1–3 meters, passed 428 ± 7 km above Antarctica on October 1 and was detected hours later by the Catalina Sky Survey. ESA astronomers used follow-up observations to precisely determine its trajectory. The asteroid posed no danger, as objects this small typically burn up as fireballs. The encounter demonstrated the value of coordinated surveys and follow-up telescopes in refining detection systems, prediction models, and planetary-defense capabilities.

Industry-sponsored clinical trials have become increasingly complex, lengthening trials and increasing burdens on participants, sites, and staff. Merck evaluated “Lean Design,” which rebuilds schedules of assessment (SoAs) from a minimal “Ground Zero” containing only essential elements. Proposed assessments are added only when supported by plausible biological effects, appropriate timing, sample-size rationale, or participant-safety needs. The Faro Smart Design Tool quantified participant and staff time, costs, blood volumes, resource needs, and operational complexity.

Six protocols across cardiovascular, medical, psychiatric, and oncology areas underwent workshops. Recommendations commonly included fewer laboratory tests and physical examinations, reduced assessment frequency, and use of participant subsets for selected measurements. Potential reductions ranged from 4 to 47 participant hours per trial. In a cardiovascular trial involving 12,600 participants, recommended reductions of $9,000 per participant could save nearly $120 million; adopted reductions of $4,000 per participant were estimated to save almost $58 million. Few changes were recommended for the oncology trial because cancer-progression assessments were highly standardized.

Teams adopted only some recommendations, partly because protocols were already in late development and changes were optional. Concerns about unexpected findings, regulatory expectations, and resistance from quality-of-life and pharmacology groups also limited adoption. Estimated savings covered only SoA activities and excluded downstream costs such as data monitoring, cleaning, analysis, and reporting.

The authors conclude that early use of Lean Design, supported by quantitative feedback and organizational leadership, may substantially reduce unnecessary assessments, trial burden, complexity, and costs. Merck subsequently launched company-wide implementation, though the approach requires evaluation in other companies. The project was funded by Merck, and the authors disclosed affiliations with Merck and Faro Health.

On March 27, 2018, Stagno tested 124 VPN and proxy providers for WebRTC IP leaks: 20 leaked users’ IP addresses, while 101 kept them hidden. The passage links to the complete results and several IP-leak testing sites. Users whose VPNs leak can manually disable WebRTC or install a browser add-on. It also lists non-leaking services, including ExpressVPN, NordVPN, StrongVPN, Private Internet Access, VyprVPN, CyberGhost, and others.
Live Nation offered over 1.5 million $20 all-in tickets to thousands of comedy and music events during National Concert Week, April 30 through May 8, via its website.

Winning the opening game builds confidence and forces the opponent to adjust. The extended break allowed the team to enjoy its San Jose win without creating a disadvantage. A key faceoff and penalty-kill player remains day to day. Despite a strong, skilled opponent, reaching team potential is the priority.

The disclosure describes a non-occluding intravascular axial blood pump designed to reduce hemolysis and clotting while allowing blood to flow around the device. The pump uses a cylindrical shroud, centrally aligned impeller and motor, and pillars connecting the motor to the shroud. Proposed design features include a trumpeted and elongated inlet, extended bare impeller hub, raked blade leading edges, optimized blade wrap and clearance, matched impeller–stator flare angles, and pillars aligned with outlet flow while mismatched in number or position relative to the blades.

Computational fluid dynamics, hotspot analysis, particle-based blood-damage estimates, and in vitro testing identified major shear-stress regions at the impeller, inlet shroud, and pillars. Iterative prototypes reduced turbulent flow and shear while maintaining or improving hydraulic output. The P_31 design combined an extended inlet shroud, refined hub and blade geometry, and pillars oriented at approximately 30 degrees. Compared with the initial design, maximum impeller shear was reduced by 150–200 Pa, average impeller shear remained below 400 Pa up to 30,000 rpm, and the normalized index of hemolysis improved by 78% at 20,000 rpm. The resulting approximately 6 mm pump is intended as a minimally invasive circulatory support device, particularly for NYHA Class III and early Class IV patients.

A Federal High Court in Katsina remanded former Governor Ibrahim Shema in EFCC custody until April 27 over alleged misappropriation of N5.7 billion in SURE-P funds. Shema pleaded not guilty to 26 fraud-related charges. The court will hear his written bail application on April 27.

The $399 Pixel Watch 4 offers several days of battery life, fast charging, offline Google Maps, dual-band GPS, satellite emergency calling, and strong Fitbit-based health and sleep tracking. Its slim design is comfortable, while 5ATM water resistance supports swimming and surfing.

The Apple Watch Ultra 3 is the stronger adventure watch, with greater durability, 10ATM water resistance, recreational diving support, broader international satellite coverage, and regular satellite texting. It also lasted a weekend during testing but costs about twice as much.

Both watches require active carrier plans for satellite access and include safety check-ins, fall detection, and crash detection, though the Pixel Watch failed to detect a hard fall during testing. Despite its limitations, the Pixel Watch 4 stands out as an attractive, practical outdoor smartwatch with satellite emergency service for under $500.

Molecular dynamics simulations examined primary radiation damage in pure niobium at 300 K for 1–75 keV primary knock-on atom energies using EAM, FS-1, FS-2, and SNAP interatomic potentials. All models showed rapid Frenkel-pair production, partial recombination, and stabilization, but predicted substantially different defect counts, clustering, and morphologies.

Cascades remained compact below roughly 20 keV and increasingly divided into subcascades at higher energies. Surviving Frenkel pairs followed two power-law regimes separated near this threshold. Vacancy clustering consistently exceeded interstitial clustering. EAM produced the highest vacancy clustering and largest vacancy clusters, exceeding 60 vacancies at 75 keV. SNAP generally showed the strongest interstitial clustering, while FS-2 produced the largest interstitial clusters.

Defect morphology depended strongly on potential choice. EAM generated a balanced mixture of C15-like rings and dislocation loops, with occasional ⟨100⟩ clusters. FS-1 favored ⟨110⟩ dumbbells, crowdions, small C15 rings, and hybrid or disordered structures. FS-2 predominantly produced extended 1/2⟨111⟩ dumbbells, crowdions, and large 1/2⟨111⟩ dislocation loops. SNAP formed compact cascades, disordered clusters, ⟨111⟩ dumbbells, and many C15-like rings containing up to nine atoms; these rings may develop into 1/2⟨111⟩ or ⟨100⟩ loops.

At low energies, cascade behavior reflected combined effects of short-range repulsive stiffness, threshold displacement energy, and defect formation energies, although FS-1 was an exception. Above the subcascade threshold, these properties alone could not explain cascade evolution. Older classical potentials produced more defects and predicted incorrect self-interstitial ground-state configurations compared with newer potentials.

Horsell Lodge near Woking offers personalised short-term respite, long-term residential and dementia care. Prospective residents should verify its suitability and report inaccurate or missing information by email.

Jason Day will face Louis Oosthuizen, Jason Dufner and James Hahn in the WGC-Match Play group stage. Marc Leishman drew Branden Grace, Bubba Watson and Julian Suri, while Cameron Smith faces Hideki Matsuyama, Patrick Cantlay and Yusaku Miyazato. Smith needs a strong result to secure a Masters invitation.

The passage develops logical and computational frameworks over commutative, positive, non-trivial semirings. It defines semiring semantics for propositional, first-order, and existential second-order logics, including formula comparisons, satisfiability, Boolean connectives, and quantified semiring-valued relations. It also introduces BSS machines over semirings, nondeterministic polynomial time \(NP_K\), reductions, and completeness. The main stated contribution is a semiring analogue of Fagin’s theorem, \(ESO^{=}_K = NP_K\), proved by polynomial-time formula evaluation and by encoding accepting BSS computations as existential second-order formulas. The article additionally announces analogues of Cook’s theorem and completeness of the true existential theory of \(K\) for the Boolean part of \(NP_K\).

Idaho’s Week 7 high school football rankings remained stable at the top, with Bishop Kelly retaining No. 1 after a 22-20 win over Columbia and No. 4 Eagle defeating Mountain View 21-14. Rocky Mountain, Timberline, Lakeland, Owyhee and several other teams remained undefeated, while four-time reigning 1A champion Kendrick won 90-0 and extended its winning streak to 10 games. Minico entered the rankings at 4-1, and Ririe debuted after improving to 6-0. Coeur d’Alene’s 50-9 victory dropped Sandpoint from No. 15, though the Bulldogs remained ranked. Middleton and Capital fell out following losses to Meridian and Timberline, respectively.

USA TODAY Sports lists the NBA’s complete 2017–18 national television schedule, covering games from Oct. 17 through April 11 on TNT, ESPN, ABC and NBA TV. The Christmas Day slate features Philadelphia–New York, Cleveland–Golden State, Washington–Boston, Houston–Oklahoma City and Minnesota–L.A. Lakers.

Euro zone stocks began 2017 at their highest in over a year after manufacturing activity grew at its fastest pace in more than five years. Italy’s FTSE MIB led gains, while German and French indexes also reached multi-month highs. Thin holiday trading contributed to volatility.

The euro fell below US$1.05 as the dollar resumed its rise, supported by expectations of U.S. rate increases and fiscal expansion under Donald Trump. Stronger risk appetite lowered Italian, Spanish and Portuguese bond yields.

Markets showed little reaction to Islamic State attacks in Istanbul and Baghdad, though the Turkish lira weakened near record lows amid concerns about security, tourism and the economy. Chinese manufacturing expanded for a fifth month but slowed slightly, while the yuan ended 2016 down almost 7 percent. Bitcoin rose above US$1,000 for the first time since late 2013.

Machine learning-assisted genome-wide association studies (GWAS) impute missing phenotypes to increase sample size and statistical power, but conventional methods treat imputed values as observed and can produce false-positive associations. In a UK Biobank type 2 diabetes analysis, GWAS of imputed phenotypes had an 81% replication failure rate despite reasonable imputation accuracy and near-perfect genetic correlation with the observed-phenotype GWAS. Many false associations arose because HbA1c, the strongest imputation predictor, is influenced by erythrocytic variants unrelated to diabetes risk. Thus, high imputation accuracy and genome-wide genetic correlation do not ensure SNP-level validity.

The authors introduce Post-prediction GWAS (POP-GWAS), which combines summary statistics from three analyses: GWAS of observed and imputed phenotypes in labeled samples and GWAS of imputed phenotypes in unlabeled samples. Differences between observed- and imputed-phenotype effects in labeled data are used to correct bias for each SNP. POP-GWAS is presented as unbiased, type-I-error controlled, computationally efficient, and more powerful than GWAS restricted to observed phenotypes, without assumptions about the imputation algorithm, predictors, imputation quality, or genetic architecture. It is also described as the best linear unbiased estimator, with power determined by imputation quality and labeled and unlabeled sample sizes.

Simulations showed that conventional imputed-phenotype GWAS produced biased estimates and inflated type-I error under heterogeneous genetic effects, whereas POP-GWAS remained calibrated and gained power as imputation quality or unlabeled sample size increased. In the type 2 diabetes benchmark, all POP-GWAS loci replicated, erythrocytic false positives disappeared, and POP-GWAS identified 13 loci versus six using labeled samples alone.

POP-GWAS was applied to dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-derived bone mineral density across 14 skeletal sites in UK Biobank. It increased effective sample size by 9.7%–50.7% and identified 188 independent loci, 39% more than conventional GWAS. Combined with independent studies, the analysis identified 303 genome-wide significant loci, including 89 novel loci. Results indicated site-specific genetic architecture, strong site-matched relationships between bone density and fracture risk, associations with osteoarthritis in weight-bearing joints, and candidate genes and pathways involved in bone biology. The analysis was mainly restricted to participants of European ancestry, requiring future evaluation in other populations.

The Supreme Court is returning from summer recess for its “long conference,” where justices will review accumulated petitions and likely accept five to 15 cases ahead of the 2025-26 term beginning Oct. 6. Justice Clarence Thomas questioned rigid adherence to precedent, while former Justice Anthony Kennedy urged the court to reduce antagonism and partisanship. Commentary also highlighted Justice Amy Coney Barrett’s restrained originalism and former Justice Lewis Powell’s openness to reconsidering difficult issues.

The upcoming term includes disputes over Federal Trade Commission removal protections, Louisiana’s majority-Black congressional districts, the Voting Rights Act, and Ten Commandments displays in public schools. The Trump administration has asked the court to review birthright citizenship and allow termination of protected status for Venezuelans. The court also permitted the administration to withhold nearly $4 billion in foreign aid. An analysis of 2024 emergency cases found conservative outcomes were decided faster on average than liberal outcomes.

The study develops a practical method for designing dilute polyisobutylene–polybutene Boger fluids with prescribed shear modulus \(G_0\), relaxation time \(\tau\), and first normal stress coefficient \(\psi_1\). The fluids use polyisobutylene polymer and a solvent mixture of polybutene and light mineral oil. Solvent viscosity varies exponentially with polybutene fraction, while sufficiently low polymer concentrations preserve dilute, nearly constant-viscosity behavior.

Small-amplitude oscillatory shear and rotational measurements were interpreted using a three-parameter Zimm model. Despite polymer polydispersity, the longest relaxation mode captured the dynamic moduli. The polymer–solvent interaction parameter remained near \(0.30\), indicating that the solvent mixture is poor for polyisobutylene but close to theta-solvent behavior. The standard Zimm estimate \(\psi_1=2\chi G_0\tau^2\) consistently overestimated measurements, requiring an empirical correction factor.

Experiments established power-law relationships between rheological properties and polymer concentration \(c\), molecular weight \(M\), and solvent viscosity \(\eta_s\). Measured dependencies were approximately:
- \(G_0\propto c^{1.00}M^{-0.93}\eta_s^{0.01}\)
- \(\tau\propto c^{0.10}M^{1.54}\eta_s^{0.84}\)
- \(\psi_1\propto c^{1.41}M^{1.86}\eta_s^{1.61}\)

These empirical relationships differ from ideal scaling predictions and form an invertible design matrix linking target rheological properties to fluid composition. Validation fluids successfully varied \(G_0\) while maintaining \(\tau\), varied \(\tau\) while maintaining \(G_0\), and maintained nearly constant \(\psi_1\) while viscosity varied substantially. The framework can help decouple viscous and elastic effects, estimate properties below rheometer resolution, assess polymer degradation, and test dilute viscoelastic-flow models.

Enron transformed from a debt-burdened pipeline company into a dominant energy trader under Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling. Skilling’s Gas Bank, trading model, aggressive recruitment, performance-based compensation, and expansion into electricity, commodities, broadband, and international projects drove rapid growth and Wall Street acclaim.

The company’s culture prized intelligence, risk-taking, speed, and immediate profits but became intensely competitive and unforgiving. Forced rankings, high turnover, weak loyalty, harsh customer dealings, and pressure for short-term results undermined morale and long-term planning. Enron also used mark-to-market accounting extensively, recording anticipated profits upfront.

By 2001, costly international projects, California energy-crisis criticism, the telecommunications collapse, failed ventures, accounting concerns, and questions about asset sales weakened investor confidence. Enron’s stock fell sharply, while Skilling’s confrontational responses further damaged trust. After six months as CEO, Skilling resigned, citing personal sacrifices and a desire to change his life. Lay returned as CEO and promised to focus innovation closer to Enron’s core business while reconsidering practices that had harmed morale.

The passage defines Bengali transliteration mappings for digits, currency and special signs. A following “~” replaces a typed Bengali character with a symbol. Standard English punctuation remains unchanged. Ligatures render automatically; ZWJ creates half-formed consonants or separates vowel pairs, while ZWNJ creates dead consonants.

Apple Inc.’s fiscal 2015 Form 10-K covers the year ended September 26, 2015. Apple, a California corporation founded in 1977, designs, manufactures and markets mobile devices, computers, media players, software, services and accessories. Its offerings include iPhone, iPad, Mac, iPod, Apple Watch, Apple TV, iOS, OS X, watchOS, iCloud, Apple Pay and Internet Services. New products announced in September 2015 included iPhone 6s and 6s Plus, iPad Pro, Apple TV and tvOS.

Apple manages operations geographically through the Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific. Products are sold to consumers, businesses, education, enterprise and government customers through Apple’s stores and sales force and through carriers, wholesalers, retailers and resellers. Direct and indirect channels represented 26% and 74% of 2015 net sales, respectively; international sales accounted for 65%. No customer represented more than 10% of net sales in 2013–2015.

Apple’s strategy emphasizes integrated hardware, software and services, product innovation, digital-content distribution, third-party development, retail expansion and customer support. Research and development spending rose from $4.5 billion in 2013 to $6.0 billion in 2014 and $8.1 billion in 2015.

Substantially all hardware is manufactured by a small number of outsourcing partners, primarily in Asia, while some Macs are manufactured in the U.S. and Ireland. Apple relies on single or limited sources for numerous components, creating supply, pricing and production risks. Purchase commitments generally cover up to 150 days.

Major identified risks include economic weakness, intense competition and price pressure, rapid technological change, unsuccessful product introductions, distributor dependence, inventory and supply constraints, manufacturing disruptions, product defects, loss of third-party content, software or intellectual-property access, litigation, regulatory and tax changes, international operations, cybersecurity and privacy breaches, key-personnel loss, disasters, currency fluctuations, credit exposure and stock-price volatility.

As of September 26, 2015, Apple employed approximately 110,000 full-time-equivalent employees and owned or leased 25.6 million square feet of building space. Non-affiliate-held stock had an aggregate market value of approximately $709.9 billion on March 27, 2015. Apple had 5.575 billion shares outstanding on October 9, 2015.

Apple paid dividends of $11.4 billion in 2015 and $11.0 billion in 2014 and expected quarterly dividends of $0.52 per share, subject to board approval. Its common stock trades on NASDAQ under AAPL. Apple reported no unresolved SEC staff comments and stated that pending legal claims were not considered reasonably likely to cause a material loss, though outcomes remained uncertain.

Private college presidents’ average compensation rose 9% to $570,000 in 2015, while 58 earned over $1 million, up from 39. Ohio’s Daniel Curran ranked eighth with more than $2.4 million. Barbara Snyder, Grant Cornwell and Marvin Krislov also ranked among the top 100.

Oil prices declined after Israel and Hamas agreed to pause fighting in Gaza, allowing hostages to be exchanged for Palestinian prisoners and easing regional risks. U.S. benchmark crude fell to $62.34 per barrel, while Brent slipped to $66.07.

U.S. stocks were little changed near record highs, with the S&P 500 up 0.1%. Gold remained near its record at $4,054.50 per ounce, and Treasury yields rose slightly. PepsiCo exceeded adjusted earnings expectations despite weaker North American demand, while Delta’s strong results and outlook lifted airline shares. Akero Therapeutics surged after the Wegovy maker announced a $4.7 billion acquisition.

European markets were mixed, while most Asian markets gained, led by Japan’s Nikkei 225, which rose 1.8%.

The African Union Commission’s First Start Up Fest brought together entrepreneurs, technology hubs, officials, businesses, development partners, academia, and civil society to discuss youth entrepreneurship and start-up development. Objectives included assessing start-up and tech-hub capacity needs, facilitating public-private policy dialogue, supporting African start-ups, and laying foundations for a continental association. Speakers emphasized SMEs’ role in competitiveness, production, and employment; the need for infrastructure, education, training, effective labor markets, and job-focused policies; and the importance of entrepreneurship, digital technology, inclusion, finance, and economic opportunities in addressing youth unemployment. Participants called for greater youth involvement in manufacturing, agro-processing, blue economies, and intra-African trade. A follow-up event was planned for the 2018 Transform Africa Summit in Kigali to discuss establishing an African Association of Community Innovation Hubs.

Callinex Mines filed an independent preliminary economic assessment for its wholly owned Nash Creek and Superjack projects in New Brunswick. The PEA outlines a 10-year, 3,900-tonne-per-day open-pit operation, with pre-tax IRR of 34.1%, post-tax IRR of 25.2%, pre-tax NPV of C$230 million and post-tax NPV of C$128 million, based on C$168 million in pre-production capital and zinc at US$1.25/lb. Nash Creek is near major highway, power, smelting, port and rail infrastructure. Callinex planned drilling to explore potential satellite deposits across its 150 km² land package. The assessment includes speculative Inferred Mineral Resources, and there is no certainty its projections will be realized.

The retail apparel sector has fallen about 20% amid e-commerce competition, excess stores and malls, and trade-policy uncertainty. The author argues Francesca’s Holdings could emerge stronger because of its profitability, cash generation, and debt-free balance sheet.

Francesca’s operates more than 670 stores targeting women aged 18–35 and plans to expand toward 900. It has $48 million in cash, no debt, and approximately $57.6 million in free cash flow. In the first quarter of 2017, sales rose 1% to $107.7 million due to new stores, while comparable sales fell 5%. Net income declined from $7.1 million to $4.3 million, and diluted EPS fell from $0.18 to $0.12.

Fiscal-year guidance projected sales of $518–537 million and EPS of $1.07–1.17, with 60–65 openings and 10–15 closures. Francesca’s price-to-earnings ratio of 8.4 was below profitable peers and the industry median, although its price-to-book valuation was higher. The author describes its valuation measures as mixed but considers its returns and cash-based profitability solid. Share repurchases may benefit investors at the prevailing price.

Despite fierce competition and industry uncertainty, the author projects a share price of $14.50–$17 within one to three years and $27–$29 within three to five years. The author disclosed no stock positions or related business relationships.

Offsites may focus on alignment, communication, coordination or celebration, but breakthroughs require a disruptive, connecting environment, shared purpose, purpose-aligned organization, deeper relationships and practical follow-through. HATCH applies BRAVE questions covering environment, values, attitudes, relationships and behaviors. Its experiences use unfamiliar communal settings with limited connectivity, an inclusive mission combining creativity, technology and design thinking, and carefully selected diverse participants. Programs balance preparation, talks, exercises, activities, prototyping, music, meals, socializing and free time to foster creativity, vulnerability, collaboration and measurable action.

DPI (UK), a Castle Donington manufacturer of aluminium frames and lightboxes, has received a £12,200 Collaborate grant toward an automated saw. The equipment will enable larger products to be made in-house, double output, reduce contract times and support future job creation. Launched three years ago, DPI grew 37% last year and has expanded its staff and premises. Collaborate, funded by the European Regional Development Fund and partners, offers eligible Leicester and Leicestershire businesses grants of £5,000 to £25,000 covering one-third of capital project costs, alongside workshops and business advice.

President Trump’s description of the House-passed health care bill as “mean” frustrated conservatives he had pressured to support it, especially after previously calling it “a great plan.” Trump urged the Senate to create a “more generous” version. Senate Republicans remained divided over Medicaid expansion, coverage requirements and subsidies, potentially delaying passage until late July.

Chiefs defensive lineman Chris Jones admitted he stopped pursuing Trevor Lawrence because he mistakenly thought the quarterback was down before Lawrence scored the Jaguars’ game-winning touchdown. Jones called it a learning experience and promised it would not happen again. He said his social media accounts had been deactivated before the game, not to avoid criticism, and that he is now focused on Kansas City’s upcoming prime-time matchup against the NFL’s top-scoring offense.

The study used Multi-ancEstry TRanscriptOme-wide analysis (METRO) and FOCUS fine-mapping to identify genes associated with general cognitive function, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Gene expression and genotype data came from 1,032 African ancestry and 801 European ancestry GENOA participants and were integrated with published GWAS summary statistics.

Before fine-mapping, METRO identified 602 genes associated with cognitive function, 45 with WMH, 231 with AD in a European ancestry GWAS, and 9 with AD in an African ancestry GWAS. Fine-mapping retained 266, 23, and 69 genes for cognitive function, WMH, and European ancestry AD, respectively; 82, 12, and 45 had not been identified in the corresponding original GWAS analyses. Two genes were retained for African ancestry AD. Identified pathways involved innate immunity, vascular dysfunction, neuroinflammation, protein regulation, neurodevelopment, and amyloid-related processes.

ICA1L was the only fine-mapped gene shared by WMH and AD and the only gene overlapping across all compared WMH and AD TWAS results. Decreased ICA1L expression was associated with greater AD and WMH risk, suggesting possible shared AD and vascular dementia neuropathology. European and African ancestry expression models contributed similarly for cognitive function and AD, while European ancestry weights contributed more strongly for most WMH genes.

Limitations included expression measurements from transformed blood B-lymphocytes rather than brain-related tissues, correlated genes within genomic regions, reliance primarily on European ancestry GWAS, and limited power in the African ancestry AD GWAS. The study demonstrates that integrating expression data across ancestries can identify shared and distinct transcriptomic mechanisms and potential targets for dementia prevention or treatment.

Enron agreed to supply 60% of 400 megawatts contracted annually by Chicago and 47 suburbs, with Commonwealth Edison supplying the remainder. Chicago separately proposed buying 60% of municipal electricity from Enron under an eight-year deal expected to save about $3 million annually.

Enron Broadband participated in a $30 million investment in software developer AP Engines. Enron Power Operations also leased additional London office space.

Lenders held three days of talks over Enron’s troubled $3 billion Dabhol power project in India, ending with unspecified “positive developments.” The dispute arose after the Maharashtra State Electricity Board failed to pay bills and stopped buying Dabhol’s costly power. Lenders considered whether to complete the more than 90%-finished second phase, while Indian Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee expressed confidence that the disagreement could be resolved. Dabhol maintained its power-purchase agreement remained valid and reportedly planned to challenge a regulatory restriction on seeking international arbitration.

Other reports examined India’s delayed privatizations and uneven foreign-investment reforms, opposition from U.S. steel consumers to possible import restrictions, Pacific Hydro’s renewable-energy expansion, and California regulators’ consideration of suspending direct electricity purchases from alternative suppliers. A Chicago City Council redistricting blueprint sought to preserve African-American representation while likely increasing Hispanic-majority wards. A commentary criticized California Attorney General Bill Lockyer’s remarks invoking prison rape as punishment for Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay.

Tesla’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2022 reported:

- Revenue of $18.76 billion, up from $10.39 billion a year earlier, including $16.86 billion in automotive revenue.
- Gross profit of $5.46 billion, operating income of $3.60 billion and net income attributable to common stockholders of $3.32 billion.
- Diluted earnings per share of $2.86, compared with $0.39 in the prior-year quarter.
- Operating cash flow of $4.00 billion, investing outflows of $2.17 billion and financing outflows of $1.91 billion.
- Total assets of $66.04 billion, liabilities of $30.63 billion and stockholders’ equity of $34.09 billion.
- Cash and cash equivalents of $17.51 billion, inventory of $6.69 billion and total debt carrying value of $3.42 billion, excluding finance leases.
- Property and equipment investment focused on Gigafactory Berlin, Gigafactory Texas, Gigafactory Shanghai expansion, and manufacturing equipment and tooling.
- Digital assets with a $1.26 billion carrying value and $1.96 billion fair value.
- Stock-based compensation expense of $418 million.

Tesla operates automotive and energy generation and storage segments. It cited continuing COVID-19 effects, supply-chain and semiconductor constraints, inflation, higher logistics, raw-material and labor costs, and related product-price adjustments. The filing also describes tax matters, debt repayments, executive compensation awards, factory commitments, supplier dependence, regulatory investigations and ongoing litigation involving the SolarCity acquisition, executive and director compensation, taking Tesla private statements, alleged race discrimination and a JPMorgan warrant dispute.

The study compared antibody responses from two-dose mRNA vaccination alone with hybrid immunity from vaccination plus SARS-CoV-2 infection. Using ELISA and live-virus neutralization assays, researchers analyzed responses against the ancestral WA1 strain and Alpha, Beta, Delta, Omicron BA.1, and BA.2 variants.

Hybrid immunity produced significantly higher antibody levels, neutralizing titers, neutralization efficiency, and cross-variant activity than vaccination alone. Among 46 hybrid-immune participants, intervals of 35–404 days between infection and vaccination were positively associated with antibody levels and neutralizing titers, regardless of whether infection occurred before or after vaccination. Longer intervals particularly improved neutralization and cross-reactivity against vaccine-resistant variants, including Beta and Omicron, with responses continuing to improve for at least 400 days.

The findings suggest that immune responses continue developing for more than a year after initial exposure and that delayed subsequent exposure can strengthen and broaden hybrid immunity. The authors state that intentional infection is not a reasonable public-health strategy because of the risks of severe illness, complications, and death; instead, the results support vaccine access, including for previously infected people whose vaccination has been delayed.
Sensors reveal greater noctule bats catching songbirds at night.

Moody’s said India may meet its 3.3% fiscal deficit target for 2018-19 by cutting capital spending, despite revenue and expenditure risks. Most poll respondents expected fiscal slippage and viewed rising oil prices as a major economic risk. Moody’s said subsidy reforms have reduced oil-related sovereign credit risks, though prolonged high prices remain a downside. Respondents also considered the public-sector bank recapitalisation package insufficient.

ARDD praised Jordanian agencies and UNHCR for rapidly establishing free, coordinated legal support for Syrian refugees, including camp-based courts, family protection, documentation assistance, awareness programmes and training for legal providers. The report said legal services protect refugees’ rights and enable access to education and health. Challenges include emerging needs, formal labour-market access, limited evaluation and funding, and pressure on Jordan’s resources. A recent registration campaign helped 25,000 refugees register with UNHCR and obtain documentation.

Texas Instruments warns that ESD can degrade or destroy MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 devices. The September 2025 revision removes DGS32 package information and updates power modes, specifications, CPU features, ADC ENOB, debug content, and identification tables. Mechanical and assembly guidance covers thermal-pad soldering, optional vias, stencil design, solder coverage, dimensions, and packaging. Information may change without notice. TI provides resources “as is,” limits liability, and assigns product selection, design, validation, testing, and regulatory compliance to developers.

TyreWatch, launched at Harwell Innovation and Science Campus, is a predictive tyre management system for commercial fleets. Wheel-rim sensors continuously monitor tyre pressure and temperature, transmitting real-time data via cellular and satellite networks to a central server. Artificial intelligence identifies concerning trends and issues maintenance or critical alerts, enabling preventive repairs and safer stops. The system works with existing multi-brand tyres, continues monitoring parked vehicles, and can integrate with manufacturer systems and third-party telematics. TyreWatch says testing prevented 95% of tyre-related breakdowns while reducing fuel use, tyre wear, downtime and safety risks. Developed by the Pathway to Autonomous Commercial Vehicles consortium, it received £1.2 million in government funding through Innovate UK.

Andrew Lo introduces MIT’s 15.401 Finance Theory, an introductory course for first-year MBA students. He presents finance as the disciplined study of monetary transactions and argues that it is central to business and management because it combines rigorous analysis with practical decision-making.

Examples of James Simons, Warren Buffett, and Jack Welch illustrate that successful finance can draw on advanced mathematics, basic arithmetic and accounting, or managerial judgment. Despite their different backgrounds, all three understand financial language and use it to make investment and management decisions.

The course examines four components of the financial system: households, financial intermediaries, non-financial corporations, and capital markets. Financial analysis has two fundamental tasks: valuing assets and managing them. Management involves selecting options based on their value and the decision-maker’s objectives. An auction of an unidentified package demonstrates how markets discover prices with limited information; the package sells for $45 and contains an iPod Nano valued at $149, showing how limited transparency can reduce price.

Accounting provides the framework for financial analysis. Balance sheets measure stocks of assets and liabilities, while income statements measure flows of income and expenses. Corporate finance follows cash raised, invested, generated, reinvested, and returned to investors, with the objective of maximizing shareholder wealth. The same framework applies to household decisions involving education, employment income, consumption, borrowing, savings, investments, and personal objectives.

Time and risk are presented as the defining challenges of finance. Early lectures focus on valuation over time, followed by risk and then their combination in modern finance. Lo introduces three of six fundamental principles: systematic free lunches are unlikely; people generally prefer more money, earlier payment, and less risk; and agents act to advance their own interests.

The course covers introductory material, valuation and discounting, pricing financial assets, risk, and corporate finance applications. Grades consist of participation and attendance, a case study, a midterm, and a cumulative final. Optional problem sets with solutions support practice, and most exam points come from those problems. Students are encouraged to preview notes, take detailed notes, review lectures, work both independently and in groups, ask questions, and apply the material personally and practically.

The “Horns” offense attacks a Box-and-One defense by using double mid screens to free the star ballhandler in either direction. The star can drive, pass to a rolling screener, kick out to corner shooters, or exploit post defenders who provide help. Screeners may also use opposite roll-and-pop actions. If no shot develops, a reversal pass initiates single/double screen continuity. Success requires coordinated screen execution, post play, defensive recognition, communication, timing, drills, and scrimmaging. Teams should scout defensive tendencies, monitor adjustments, vary alignments, and target weak defenders. In a Box-and-One, four defenders play a box zone while a chaser aggressively denies one opponent the ball and rebounds.

Jammu and Kashmir Deputy Chief Minister Nirmal Singh said the government is considering skill-development courses and an optional curriculum paper to strengthen students’ technical abilities and entrepreneurship.

Japanese government bonds firmed after strong demand at a two-year auction, with bids 5.51 times the amount offered. Most yields declined, while the benchmark 10-year yield held at 0.015 percent. Investors awaited details of the Bank of Japan’s May bond purchases. The BOJ has adjusted buying to reduce volatility and says it can meet interest-rate targets with fewer purchases. It kept monetary policy unchanged Thursday and issued its most optimistic economic assessment in nine years. March core consumer prices rose for a third month but more slowly than expected.

A fired Washington Walmart employee returned for a safe he had allegedly tried to steal. Employees found heroin and Xanax inside. He admitted owning the drugs and was jailed for unlawful possession of a controlled substance.

A database privacy system enables clients to analyze sensitive data without direct access to record-level information. It receives a query and client-specified differential privacy parameters, verifies authorization and privacy budget, accesses and integrates required data, modifies query operations to satisfy differential privacy, and returns a perturbed result. Database owners may impose limits on information release.

The system includes a user interface, software library, account management, query handling, data integration, and privacy modules. Supported queries include counts, medians, means, variances, interquartile ranges, histograms, regression and support-vector models trained through batch or stochastic gradient methods, random forests, model testing, and synthetic database generation. Differential privacy is defined for neighboring databases differing by at most one entry, using privacy parameters ε and δ and sensitivity measures.

Privacy mechanisms add Gaussian, Laplace, or Cauchy noise to query outputs or computation processes. Means and variances may be calculated from subsets and processed through a private median. Histograms perturb bin counts directly or through wavelet coefficients. Model-training engines perturb loss functions, gradient updates, or random-forest leaf proportions. Model testing privately generates thresholds and confusion matrices.

The synthetic database engine projects data into fewer dimensions while preserving approximate spatial relationships and providing differential privacy, allowing further analysis such as clustering. A validation engine tests queries on neighboring example databases and may certify, reject, or deny queries based on whether they satisfy specified privacy requirements. The disclosed methods may be implemented in hardware, software, firmware, or combinations thereof on standalone or networked computing systems.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K on October 26, 2021, announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2021. The related press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1, along with an interactive data file. The report was signed by Chief Accounting Officer Alice L. Jolla.

Two pieces of ammunition were found in a Litchfield High School bathroom Wednesday morning, prompting a soft lockdown of the high school and middle school. Police surrounded the campus, and students were dismissed to their parents around 10 a.m.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years for the 2014 murder of Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, her former son-in-law, and related conspiracy and solicitation charges. Adelson maintained her innocence and denied knowing about the murder-for-hire plot beforehand, prompting Judge Stephen Everett to cite her “utter lack of remorse.” Prosecutors alleged she plotted with her son, Charlie Adelson, to kill Markel so his ex-wife, Wendi Adelson, could move to South Florida with their children. Charlie Adelson, Katherine Magbanua and one hit man were convicted of murder; another pleaded guilty to second-degree murder. Adelson’s husband, Harvey, also insisted she was innocent.

The Yankees reflect baseball’s shift from starting pitching toward stronger reliance on relievers and closers, exemplified by Aroldis Chapman’s contract and a bullpen tradition dating to Joe Torre’s era. The passage questions whether highly paid starters justify their salaries when managers routinely remove them after about five innings; MLB starters averaged only 87 pitches per start in 2015. Hall of Famer John Smoltz advocates allowing pitchers to work more, arguing that greater use builds strength. Heavy bullpen use also lengthens games, prompting the commissioner to consider limits on relievers. The passage urges fans and MLB to question early removals of starters and address the trend before it becomes entrenched.

Cloud architecture has expanded HPC options beyond customized and prebuilt systems. IDC expects public-cloud and hybrid HPC to become increasingly important in manufacturing because they offer scalable performance, flexibility, and reduced reliance on costly in-house hardware. Hybrid models can retain sensitive workloads on-premises while using public clouds for demand peaks and non-critical tasks.

HPC as a Service (HPCaaS) can replace capital expenditure with operating or usage-based costs, provide access to current hardware and analysis methods, support occasional users, improve global collaboration, and enable HPC-based products and services. Among surveyed HPC users, 81% intend to implement HPC-based business models. However, cloud HPC still requires skilled personnel to configure clusters, program calculations, and interpret results.

IDC views HPC-enabled simulation, modeling, and analytics as important for faster development, optimized supply chains and energy use, sustainability, and new digital offerings. It recommends creating virtual development processes, establishing a holistic data strategy and single source of truth, selecting operating models according to utilization, budget, performance, flexibility, security, and available skills, and prioritizing scalability, security, and energy efficiency. Enterprises lacking specialist expertise should use external service providers or ecosystem partners.

The findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 technology decision makers at industrial enterprises with over 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

A retrospective review examined adrenal vessels in 30 adrenalectomy specimens from 2018 to September 2022 and fetal adrenal vessels from nine autopsies. Adult adrenal veins consistently showed age-associated asymmetrical longitudinal smooth muscle bundles, medial gaps, and disorganized or absent elastic tissue resembling fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD). These changes occurred within adrenal tissue but not surrounding arteries.

Adrenal cortical adenomas commonly contained hyalinized arterial walls, macrophages, intimal fibroplasia, and medial degeneration or necrosis consistent with segmental arterial mediolysis (SAM). Pheochromocytomas commonly showed thin-walled arteries, blood lakes, medial degeneration, and intimal fibroplasia. Hemorrhage and thrombosis were the most frequent complications. Fetal adrenal vessels lacked these abnormalities.

The authors propose that FMD, SAM, adrenal venous changes, placental acute atherosis, and Moyamoya disease or syndrome may share pathogenic mechanisms involving adrenal hormones, local tissue conditions, or hormone-receptor signaling. The findings support considering FMD and SAM as a spectrum and suggest further investigation of adrenal hormonal effects on vascular smooth muscle integrity. No funding or conflicts of interest were reported.

A Boeing-funded study suggests passengers seeking to avoid colds or flu should choose a window seat and remain seated, reducing contact with people moving through the cabin. Researchers observed 10 U.S. flights, tested surfaces and air, and modeled exposure to an infectious aisle-seat passenger. They estimated that, on average, one of about 150 passengers would become infected, with the 11 nearest passengers at highest risk. Aisle-seat passengers moved most frequently, while 38 percent of all passengers never left their seats. However, researchers observed only one coughing passenger and detected none of 18 tested viruses. Independent experts said the small study could not support broad conclusions but offered novel data on passenger movement and contact aboard airplanes.

The Supertrend Indicator, created by Oliver Seban, is a lagging, trend-following tool that uses price and Average True Range (ATR) to identify trend direction, reversals, and potential entry or exit points. It appears below price in green during uptrends and above price in red during downtrends, reversing when the closing price crosses its previous value. Its bands are calculated from the median price, ATR period, and multiplier; Seban’s default settings are a 10-period ATR and multiplier of 3.

A weekly, long-only S&P 500 backtest over 60 years produced 38 trades, a win rate of about 66–67%, and a maximum drawdown of 24.6%, compared with 56.24% for buy-and-hold. The test excluded commissions, slippage, and reinvested dividends. Results may vary with market conditions, assets, timeframes, and parameters, making further backtesting important.

Supertrend can be applied to intraday, daily, or weekly charts, though the article favors weekly use for stocks and instruments sustaining long trends. It dynamically widens or tightens with volatility and may also be adapted for ranging markets. Its benefits include clear trend signals, noise filtering, and risk-management support. Limitations include false signals and whipsaws in volatile or choppy markets. Moving averages, RSI, Bollinger Bands, oscillators, price analysis, and risk-management techniques may provide confirmation.

The address expresses gratitude for peace, liberty, healthful seasons, and abundant harvests. It reports generally peaceful foreign relations, while noting the Russo-Ottoman war and hope for aid to the Greeks. Commerce with France is growing, though American indemnity claims remain unresolved. The King of the Netherlands has been selected to arbitrate the northeastern boundary dispute with Great Britain. British restrictions on direct colonial trade and navigation require congressional attention, while a commercial treaty with Austria advances principles of reciprocity and freer trade.

Indemnity claims against Denmark are being settled. Relations with Latin American nations remain friendly despite internal conflicts; peace between Buenos Aires and Brazil is welcomed, and negotiations continue over American claims and commercial agreements.

Federal revenue exceeded expectations. About $12 million was applied to public debt principal and interest, leaving an estimated debt of $58.36 million at the start of 1829. European grain shortages have opened markets for American agricultural exports, supporting expectations that 1829 revenue will equal or exceed that of 1828 and permit another $10 million reduction in debt.

The address defends protection of domestic industry against discriminatory British trade policies while acknowledging that the tariff should be revised if it unfairly burdens any region or economic interest. It emphasizes balancing agricultural, commercial, and manufacturing interests and warns against state resistance to federal laws on claims of unconstitutionality.

Army discipline is described as generally good. Congress is asked to reconsider relations with Indigenous tribes, balancing justice toward them with state claims to sovereignty and land. Fortifications, naval improvements, roads, canals, river and harbor works, and the Military Academy at West Point are presented as important national undertakings.

The Navy has largely suppressed piracy, defended neutral commerce, prepared a Pacific and South Sea surveying expedition, acquired ship timber, advanced dry docks, and developed plans for navy-yard improvements. The postal system has expanded from fewer than 200 offices in 1792 to nearly 8,000, though annual expenditures exceeded receipts by about $25,000.

The District of Columbia penitentiary has been completed but requires legislation governing prisoners. British payments under the Treaty of Ghent have been distributed to claimants. Public-land revenues approached $2 million, and Congress is asked to consider extending purchasers’ repayment deadlines.

Finally, Congress is urged to prepare early for the fifth census, preferably beginning in spring, with improved manufacturing data, expanded age categories, sufficient time, and better compensation for census officials.

Case Western Reserve University researchers estimate that childhood exposure to domestic violence costs the U.S. economy more than $55 billion annually through increased health-care costs, violent crime and reduced productivity. About 15.5 million U.S. children are exposed to intimate partner violence each year, and more than 25 percent experience it during childhood. The estimated lifetime economic cost per exposed child is nearly $50,000 by age 64, including $11,042 in medical costs, $13,922 related to violent crime and $25,531 in productivity losses. Researchers said the study is the first to quantify this economic burden and could support preventive and therapeutic interventions.

Canadian Blood Services will open Canada’s largest donation clinic at Eau Claire Market on July 10, replacing Calgary’s current clinic. The 20-bed facility aims to boost donations amid a critical national shortage, particularly of O-negative blood. The organization needs 50,000 more donations by June’s end to reach its 150,000-donation goal. Calgary is also set to become a blood-services hub with a new operations facility planned for 2020.

The Shepherd Express criticizes We Energies, a regulated monopoly, for high rates, highly paid executives, overbuilding power plants, and prioritizing shareholder returns. It argues that utilities face little competition and contrasts investor-owned power companies with municipally owned utilities, which it says usually provide lower-cost, more accountable service.

Milwaukee-area electric rates were once among the nation’s lowest under former utility CEO Charlie McNeer. The passage attributes subsequent increases, culminating in the Midwest’s highest rates, to a compliant Public Service Commission that approved repeated utility requests. The Citizens Utility Board and large energy-consuming businesses have opposed these increases. A new business coalition, the Initiative for Competitive Energy, seeks lower prices to support economic growth. We Energies has proposed freezing rates through 2019, but critics, including ICE and CUB, argue that rates may need to be rolled back instead.

F2 Logistics seeks a fourth straight win and the No. 2 seed against Generika-Ayala in the PSL Grand Prix. Sta. Lucia faces winless Smart in the opener, while five teams continue battling for positions Nos. 3 to 7.

Encode general counsel Nathan Calvin accused OpenAI of using subpoenas and intimidation to undermine critics and weaken California’s SB 53 AI safety law. Calvin, who was personally subpoenaed alongside the three-person nonprofit, said OpenAI sought private communications about the legislation under the pretext of investigating possible ties to Elon Musk. Encode denies receiving Musk funding and refused to provide documents.

OpenAI strategy chief Jason Kwon said Encode’s support for Musk’s lawsuit and insufficiently disclosed funding justified questions about third-party collaboration, describing subpoenas as standard litigation practice. Another nonprofit founder reported receiving similarly broad demands.

Calvin alleged OpenAI sought provisions that could exempt companies participating in federal or international safety frameworks from state requirements. He spoke publicly after SB 53 was signed, disputing OpenAI’s claim that it worked to improve the legislation.

OpenAI employees, former staff and AI safety researchers expressed concern about the alleged tactics. Calvin acknowledged OpenAI’s valuable products and safety research but questioned whether its conduct aligned with its nonprofit mission.

Cromwell and four employees sought to enjoin NASD Regulation from compelling testimony in its investigation of Pallet trading, disciplining employees who invoked self-incrimination privileges, and using federal grand jury materials. They alleged Regulation acted as an agent of federal prosecutors.

Although NASD’s enforcement division and its Criminal Assistance Prosecution Unit shared facilities and administrative resources, the court credited testimony that their investigations were functionally separate. It found the Rule 8210 interview demands resulted from the enforcement division’s independent private investigation, not government coercion, encouragement, or suggestion. Because Regulation was not acting as a state actor, the demands did not implicate the Fifth Amendment.

The court also found no credible evidence that protected grand jury materials were disclosed to unauthorized Regulation personnel. Documents shown during NASD testimony may have been seized under a search warrant, but plaintiffs did not establish that they concerned matters occurring before a grand jury and were protected by Rule 6(e).

Accordingly, the court found no basis for an injunction. It nevertheless advised Regulation to reconsider the physical and administrative relationship between its criminal-assistance and enforcement units because the existing arrangements created sufficient doubt about their independence to require a trial.

Prince’s music became available on Spotify after his death despite his opposition to the platform, prompting both celebration and accusations of betrayal. Other artists resisting Spotify include Taylor Swift, who argues music should be properly valued; Garth Brooks, who avoids major digital platforms; Thom Yorke, a vocal critic despite Radiohead’s presence; Beyoncé, whose album *Lemonade* is exclusive to Tidal; and Joanna Newsom, who condemns Spotify’s major-label structure.

The message reports peace, effective defense, reduced industrial conflict, advances in education, science, and public health, and extensive private, state, local, and federal relief efforts during the worldwide depression. Emergency credit and financial measures, including the Reconstruction Finance Corporation and Federal Reserve actions, are credited with preventing economic disaster and supporting recovery, though emergency agencies should be dissolved once the depression ends.

The administration identifies three priorities for recovery: reducing government spending and balancing the federal budget, immediately reorganizing the banking system, and strengthening international economic cooperation. Proposed budget measures include major appropriation cuts, limits on federal public works, continued employee furloughs, temporary salary reductions, elimination of certain veterans’ payments while protecting service-related and unsupported disabled veterans, broader manufacturing taxes, and consolidation of federal agencies.

Banking reform is presented as essential because thousands of bank suspensions, lost deposits, currency hoarding, and restricted credit intensified economic hardship. The message calls for stronger organization, regulation, and safe practices without currency inflation or government-operated banking, alongside reforms to agricultural credit institutions.

Internationally, it advocates disarmament, economic and monetary cooperation, expanded trade, and adherence to agreements. It opposes suspending upcoming war-debt payments while offering ways to address exchange difficulties.

The message also renews earlier legislative proposals and argues that government should preserve individual liberty, equality of opportunity, local and personal responsibility, voluntary cooperation, and private initiative. Federal intervention should generally remain regulatory and be used directly only during emergencies, ending when the danger passes.

Market Research Future forecasts significant growth in the global blowout preventer market through 2021, driven by oil and gas demand, unconventional drilling, offshore exploration, and stricter safety standards. The report segments the market by type, well type, and region while assessing growth factors, revenues, competition, and industry developments. The Middle East is expected to dominate due to onshore drilling, while Asia-Pacific is projected to register strong growth because of hydrocarbon potential. Key companies include Aker Solutions, Weatherford, FMC Technologies, Cameron International, National Oil Well Verco, Proserve, and Uztel.

European stocks edged higher Tuesday as rising oil prices boosted energy shares after the leaking Forties pipeline was shut. Brent crude reached a 30-month high. Investors awaited interest-rate decisions from the US Federal Reserve, Bank of England and European Central Bank.

Outgoing Federal Reserve chair Janet Yellen said elevated Wall Street valuations did not constitute a bubble but urged investor caution and diversification. She described the US economy and labor market as strong. Yellen acknowledged disappointment at not receiving a second term. Jerome Powell was set to replace her after she became the first woman to lead the Fed.

Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and Public Safety Minister Ralph Goodale expressed condolences after a van struck pedestrians in Toronto, killing 10 and injuring 15. Both praised first responders and said the investigation had found no apparent terrorism or national security link. Goodale described the case as a major homicide investigation led by Toronto police with support from all levels of government. Police arrested 25-year-old Alek Minassian, who was scheduled to appear in court on April 24, 2018.

Lake Lugano, in Switzerland’s Italian-speaking canton of Ticino near Lake Como, offers a quieter destination with a mild climate, alpine scenery, palm-lined promenades, art, hiking, local cuisine, and historic lakeside villages. Ferries and funiculars connect visitors to Gandria, Morcote, Bré, Monte San Salvatore, and Monte Generoso. Attractions include scenic trails, parks, museums, gardens, wine tastings, grotto restaurants, and lakefront accommodations. Experts describe the region as blending Swiss and Italian culture and recommend enjoying its nature, villages, and relaxed pace.

The tax department may use the net asset value method to determine fair market value of unlisted shares for capital gains, targeting undervalued property sales through companies. Experts say this could avoid disputes associated with subjective discounted cash flow valuations. The budget proposal has concerned start-ups and investors involved in frequent stake sales.

Former Katsina Governor Ibrahim Shehu Shema was remanded in EFCC custody over alleged laundering of N5.7 billion in SURE-P funds. He pleaded not guilty to 26 charges. The Federal High Court scheduled his written bail application for April 27, 2018, after rejecting an oral application.

The SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 is a non-confidential subset provided “AS-IS,” without warranties or implied licenses. Implementations may require licenses from the SD Card Association or SD-3C, LLC, particularly when incorporating SD Specifications versions 1.0 or 1.01.

The specification defines SD Memory Card physical interfaces, command protocols, operating states, registers, electrical characteristics, performance classes, SPI mode, UHS interfaces, and related application guidance. SD cards support protected and user-accessible storage, optional security mechanisms, read/write or ROM operation, and standard, miniSD, and microSD form factors. Capacity categories are SDSC up to 2 GB, SDHC above 2 GB through 32 GB, and SDXC above 32 GB through 2 TB. Hosts supporting higher-capacity cards must also support lower-capacity cards.

The standard defines Default, High Speed, UHS-I, and UHS-II bus modes. UHS-I reaches 104 MB/s using 1.8 V signaling, while UHS-II modes reach up to 624 MB/s. Version 6.00 introduces FD624 and distinguishes UHS-II and UHS-III card capabilities. Additional features include Speed Class, Video Speed Class, Application Performance Class, cache, self-maintenance, command queuing, write protection, password locking, error correction, and content protection.

SD bus communication is host-controlled and uses command, response, and block-data tokens protected by CRC. Commands may be broadcast or card-addressed. Transfers can use one or four data lines, support single or multiple blocks, and use DAT0 for busy signaling. SPI protocol is separately defined, while UHS-II details appear in its addendum.

Cards operate in identification and data-transfer modes. Initialization uses CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3 to reset cards, validate voltage, establish capacity support, obtain identification, and assign a relative card address. UHS-I initialization additionally negotiates 1.8 V signaling through ACMD41 and CMD11, selects bus width and speed, and may use CMD19 for timing calibration. UHS-II initialization includes physical-layer initialization, device initialization, enumeration, configuration, and SD-TRAN initialization.

In data-transfer mode, CMD7 selects one card for point-to-point communication. Read and write operations may be stopped with CMD12; valid final write blocks may still be programmed. Cards may buffer block writes and indicate busy status on DAT0. ROM cards reject write and erase commands, may optionally support locking and security commands, and full-size ROM cards lack a write-protect switch.

The court dismissed exceptions and confirmed distribution of the estate to all grandchildren, including descendants of afterborn children. The majority held that the will’s unqualified term “grandchildren” was unambiguous and naturally included every grandchild. Neither the “per stirpes” provision nor the naming of four children limited the class. Because heirs cannot be disinherited without express language or necessary implication, speculation about the testator’s probable intent could not override the will’s clear wording.

Justice Stearne dissented, joined by Justice Sinkler. He argued that the will’s overall scheme showed an intent to benefit only the four named children and their issue. Three children born after execution of the will had already received intestate shares through partial statutory revocation. In his view, allowing descendants of an afterborn child also to share in the trust produced an unjust distribution inconsistent with the testator’s intent. He would have construed “grandchildren” as referring only to the issue of the four named children and sustained the exceptions.

Founded in 2016, Madrid-based Dunas Capital manages about €4.5 billion across financial and real-estate investments for local and international clients. Supervised by Spain’s CNMV and DGSFP, the independent group employs more than 80 professionals and operates according to principles including transparency, innovation and sustainability.

Its investment philosophy prioritizes capital preservation through value investing, absolute returns, cross-asset analysis and strict volatility-based risk budgets. Portfolios may include equities, public and private debt, hybrids, convertibles and subordinated instruments, while options and futures may mitigate tail risk.

Dunas offers four jointly managed mutual funds with progressively higher return and volatility targets. Dunas Valor Prudente, its flagship with nearly €1.5 billion, targets 12-month Euribor plus 100 basis points with maximum 3% ex ante volatility. Equilibrado, Flexible and Audaz target Euribor plus 200, 400 and 600 basis points, with volatility limits of 6%, 10% and 15%, respectively. The firm also offers sustainable alternative investments in infrastructure, renewable energy, transportation and agriculture.

Dogs of the Dow is a stock-picking strategy that invests equal amounts in the 10 highest-dividend-yielding stocks among the 30 Dow Jones Industrial Average components. The portfolio is selected at year-end, held for a year, and rebalanced annually. Investors can implement it through individual stocks, ETFs, or mutual funds.

The strategy became popular after Michael B. O’Higgins published *Beating the Dow* in 1991, though related ideas date to 1951. It seeks to outperform the market through high-yield blue-chip stocks but offers limited diversification.

Backtests showed significant underperformance versus the S&P 500. Since August 1998, a $10,000 investment grew to $32,000 using the strategy, compared with $60,000 in the S&P 500, with respective compound annual growth rates of 5% and 7.7%. From April 2014, $10,000 grew to $19,000 in SDOG, $11,600 in IDOG, $11,200 in EDOG, and $23,300 in the S&P 500. The passage concludes that, despite its simplicity, the strategy should represent only a small portion of assets.

AMD’s specification standardizes the 4 KB Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) used by SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests to selectively share state with hypervisors while protecting encrypted guest registers. It defines protocol negotiation, feature advertisement, GHCB registration, automatic and non-automatic exits, VMGEXIT processing, error handling, page-state changes, guest requests, AP creation, restricted interrupt injection, trusted I/O, Secure AVIC, SMP booting, NMI handling, and termination requests.

Version 2 adds SEV-SNP support and optional feature discovery. Later revisions add 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, VLEK certificates, APIC ID retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, SEV-ES page-state changes, EFI confidential-computing data exchange, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, and GHCB unregistration. SEV-SNP guests must register their GHCB guest physical address before use; communication pages generally must be shared with the hypervisor.

The protocol specifies required guest and hypervisor state through GHCB fields and validity bits. Guests should disable interrupts and preemption during VMGEXIT operations and protect GHCB access in NMI contexts. It also defines support for MMIO, I/O, MSRs, hypercalls, timers, IPIs, firmware requests, certificates, device attestation, and AP boot management. System Management Mode and nested virtualization are unsupported.

The specification is provided “as is,” may change without notice, and carries no warranties or liability. Use is limited to designing interoperable products and providing feedback; AMD retains intellectual-property rights. Voluntary feedback may be used without restriction. Users must comply with export laws, and California law and Santa Clara County jurisdiction govern disputes.

FULE logically erases the entire user area using CMD32(start 0), CMD33(end), then CMD38(argument 00000002h). Hosts must verify FULE_SUPPORT. Unsupported cards or incomplete ranges use ERASE; sequencing errors reset the sequence. FULE supports only SDHC/SDXC outside SPI, with DAT0 low during operation.

U.S. home prices continued rising in February 2018. The S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller National Index increased 6.3% year over year, while the 10-City and 20-City Composites gained 6.5% and 6.8%, respectively. Seattle led the 20 cities with a 12.7% annual increase, followed by Las Vegas at 11.6% and San Francisco at 10.1%. Thirteen cities recorded faster annual growth than in January.

Month over month, the National Index rose 0.4% before seasonal adjustment and 0.5% after adjustment. Both city composites increased 0.7% unadjusted and 0.8% adjusted, with all 20 cities posting gains. National prices have risen annually for 70 consecutive months since May 2012, averaging 6% per year. Employment growth was cited as supporting prices, although gains in some cities, particularly San Francisco and Los Angeles, exceeded what employment increases would suggest.

California and power suppliers began federally ordered settlement talks over alleged electricity overcharges. The state sought about $8.9 billion in refunds, while generators disputed the claim and demanded payment of unpaid bills. Mediator Curtis Wagner urged compromise; related issues included long-term contracts, buyer creditworthiness, natural gas costs, PG&E’s bankruptcy and possible legal immunity. New FERC commissioners met Gov. Gray Davis and pledged cooperation, inspections and attention to natural gas competition.

Three former Duke Energy workers alleged that plant operations reduced output and discarded parts to influence prices; Duke denied wrongdoing and said it followed grid-manager instructions.
