State officials also considered suspending customer choice of alternative electricity providers to protect repayment of nearly $50 billion in state energy purchases.

Other reports described growing solar-home development, aided by lower equipment costs and subsidies but constrained by manufacturing capacity and builder concerns. Proposed power plants could expand supply, though uncertainty remained over construction, ownership concentration and future prices.

Austria’s Financial Market Authority raised its forecast for Heta Asset Resolution’s asset-sale proceeds from €6 billion to €8.6 billion, citing better-than-expected results. The increase benefits Austria and Carinthia, Heta’s largest creditor. Around €4 billion of Heta’s €8.1 billion cash reserves is expected to be distributed to creditors over the summer.

Dr. William Betteys held an accident policy covering accidental disability or death, with his wife as beneficiary. After his 1918 death, allegedly resulting from an infected hand injury, insurer Ætna recalled death-proof forms and denied death benefits on the ground that he died from disease, while offering to consider timely proof for weekly disability indemnity.

The court held that letters from Ætna and its agents were admissible on whether proof requirements had been waived. Ætna’s denial of liability excused the beneficiary from submitting proof of death and its cause within 60 days. However, waiver of proof requirements did not waive the policy’s separate deadline for filing suit. Efforts to persuade Ætna, even when encouraged by its agent, neither waived that limitation nor estopped Ætna from asserting it.

Because the beneficiary had nearly eight months after Ætna’s formal denial to sue but failed to do so within the contractual period, her death-benefit claim was barred. The judgment for the beneficiary was reversed. A new trial was granted solely on the claim for weekly disability indemnity, with costs awarded to Ætna.

Three police officers and former corporal Derwin Eastman testified in the preliminary inquiry into the robbery-related murders of pensioners Phyllis Caesar and Constance Fraser. Defendants Imran Khan and Steven Andrews questioned the witnesses, while attorney Saphier Hussein represented Phillip Suffrien. The inquiry continues Monday.

Coach Quenneville said the team’s experience in major games, resilient core, depth, preparation, and focus have helped it through a difficult playoff journey. He emphasized maintaining the same approach, concentrating on each shift and opponent, starting strongly, and improving each game without looking ahead. He praised Hossa as a consistent, complete player; Kimmo for reliability, experience, defense, and offensive support; and the team’s top players for rising to challenges and improving those around them. Deadline acquisitions and depth players have also contributed when others missed games. Quenneville said the opponent’s forecheck limits space and options, requiring greater quickness and puck movement. He described coaching as an evolving process centered on communication, accountability, maximizing players’ effectiveness, and putting the team first.

The IMF urged Saudi Arabia to implement economic reforms and price increases gradually to avoid harming growth. Following the oil-price decline, the kingdom recorded $200 billion in deficits over three years, with a $53-billion shortfall forecast this year. The IMF expects a deficit of 9 percent of GDP and growth of 0.1 percent. It recommended delaying a balanced budget target from 2019 to 2022. Vision 2030 measures include higher energy and water prices, excise taxes, expatriate labour fees and a planned five-percent VAT. Non-oil growth is expected to improve, while overall growth remains near zero due to reduced oil production.

The study proposes a hybrid DNN-Transformer-Autoencoder framework for corporate tax-risk supervision. The DNN models static enterprise attributes, the Transformer captures temporal dependencies in financial and taxation records, and the Autoencoder detects anomalous behavior through reconstruction error. Their outputs are fused to classify enterprises into low-, medium-, or high-risk categories.

The model was evaluated on records from approximately 12,000 enterprises across manufacturing, retail, internet services, and other industries. Data included static attributes, quarterly financial and tax indicators, and expert-assigned risk labels. The dataset was divided into 70% training, 15% validation, and 15% test sets.

The hybrid model achieved 0.91 accuracy, 0.86 recall, and 0.88 F1-score, outperforming logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and DNN-LSTM baselines. Training and validation losses converged near 0.05 after approximately 40 epochs, indicating stable convergence and generalization.

The framework may support risk grading, early warning, precision supervision, and regulatory resource allocation. Limitations include the exclusion of macroeconomic conditions and inter-firm relationships and potentially high computational requirements. Future work could incorporate macroeconomic and policy data and develop more interpretable, lightweight models.

COVIDFast is a laboratory-developed, extraction-free RT-qPCR assay for rapid, high-throughput SARS-CoV-2 detection using anterior nasal swabs (SwabFAST) or saliva (SalivaFAST). It combines specimen-specific buffers, proteinase K treatment, standardized bar-coded cryovials, and automation-compatible equipment to eliminate RNA extraction and streamline processing.

TBE-based viral transport buffer produced the strongest results for swabs, while TCEP improved proteinase K efficacy for saliva. The swab transport buffer remained effective across tested temperatures and durations. Extraction-free testing produced qualitative and similar quantitative results compared with methods using RNA extraction. Both specimen assays had a confirmed limit of detection of 4 viral copies/µL, with all 20 replicates testing positive.

Against extraction-based testing, SwabFAST achieved 100% positive and negative agreement, while SalivaFAST achieved 98.8% and 99.4%, respectively. Compared with SalivaDirect, SwabFAST showed 83.3% positive and 99.4% negative agreement; SalivaFAST showed 95% and 100%. By December 23, 2021, 409,883 COVIDFast tests had been performed, including 342,734 swab and 67,149 saliva tests, with an overall positivity rate of 8.10%. The system supported more than 5,000 tests daily with a 24-hour turnaround after laboratory receipt.

Value area trading uses volume profiles to identify the price range containing 70% of trading volume during a selected period. Traders treat this area as potential support and resistance and seek opportunities from breakouts, reversals, rejections, pullbacks, candlestick patterns, or momentum divergences. The method is used mainly on intraday and daily charts but can also apply to weekly or monthly timeframes and across futures, stocks, and forex.

Value areas may help set stop-losses, profit targets, and confirm other signals. Risks include false signals, changing or outdated value areas, and overreliance on past price action. Risk management includes stop-loss orders, position sizing, diversification, discipline, and considering other factors. Although the passage discusses backtesting, it states that clear trading rules and settings are required and does not provide a backtest.

Scientists and citizen volunteers will use telescopes, satellites, planes, balloons, apps, photos and video to study the upcoming U.S. solar eclipse from Oregon to South Carolina. Federally funded projects will examine the sun’s corona, Earth’s weather and space weather, and animal and plant behavior. The corona, normally obscured by the sun’s brightness, is central to research on magnetic activity, plasma and why the sun’s outer atmosphere is much hotter than its surface. More than 200 Citizen CATE volunteers will combine observations into a movie of the sun’s edge, while other public projects will document wildlife and create an eclipse megamovie. Past eclipses enabled the identification of helium’s spectrum and helped confirm Einstein’s general theory of relativity through observations of starlight bending.

The study develops a unified quantum-geometric description of orbital degrees of freedom in strongly coupled magnon–phonon systems. It identifies two origins of bosonic orbital angular momentum (OAM): global lattice rotation and self-rotation of quasiparticle wavepackets governed by the quantum geometry of Bloch wavefunctions. The latter is linked to a quasi–quantum geometric tensor and applies broadly to bosonic and fermionic periodic systems.

Using a two-dimensional honeycomb antiferromagnet with Néel order, parameterized for MnPS₃, the authors analyze magnon–phonon hybridization. Magnetoelastic coupling breaks relevant symmetries and enables transfer of both intra-band and inter-band OAM between magnon- and phonon-dominated portions of magnon-polarons. Consequently, linearly polarized out-of-plane phonon modes can acquire finite out-of-plane OAM and magnetic moment despite the absence of lattice rotation. Nonzero intra-band OAM requires broken combined inversion and time-reversal symmetry, while inter-band OAM arises from virtual transitions and becomes significant near narrow hybridization gaps.

The study proposes detecting this OAM through electric polarization and a transverse voltage generated when a temperature or strain gradient excites magnon-polarons. The voltage contains contributions from spin Berry curvature and orbital moment. In the modeled MnPS₃ system, magnetoelastic coupling makes the orbital contribution dominant, enhances total polarization by five to six orders of magnitude relative to a previously considered Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya-only case, and produces transverse voltages of several microvolts at low magnetic fields. The response increases with temperature and coupling strength, vanishes without magnon–phonon interaction, and remains finite at zero temperature. The framework establishes a basis for phonon orbitronics and links it conceptually with magnon orbitronics.

The passage lists The 74’s education news and commentary, led by the ICE arrest of Iowa’s largest school district superintendent. Other topics include school integration, education policy, student achievement, pandemic recovery, youth initiatives, STEM, college access, public funding, and notable teachers and students.

A Danish study found that children born to mothers with rheumatoid arthritis were nearly three times more likely to develop the disease, 2.2 times more likely to develop thyroid disease, and 1.6 times more likely to develop epilepsy. Researchers urged increased medical attention to these children.

In Waterhouse v. Gibson, the court held that an execution levy on land is construed like a deed and conveys all buildings belonging to the debtor and standing on the land, regardless of whether their foundations are sunk into the soil. The plaintiff purchased land previously levied upon under an execution against defendant Jack. Although the levy’s written returns contained no reservation, the defendants sought to prove orally that the creditor intended to exclude the barn and blacksmith’s shop, allowed Jack to remove them, and accidentally omitted the exception from the returns.

The court rejected this evidence. While certain trade fixtures erected by tenants may remain personal property, buildings owned by the landowner generally form part of the real estate and pass with a conveyance of the land. Because the levy included both the land and buildings, parol evidence could not alter its written legal effect. Judgment was entered for the plaintiff for the value of the removed buildings.

CMD19 tunes sampling timing for specific host/card combinations; it is mandatory for HOST-SDR-VD and optional for HOST-SDR-FD. It operates in transfer state under 1.8 V signaling on unlocked cards, uses a fixed tuning block, and permits up to 40 consecutive executions within 150 ms, excluding host processing time.

During identification, hosts remain at fOD; data transfer may use fPP. CMD9 reads CSD, CMD4 optionally configures drivers, and CMD7 selects or deselects cards. Only one card may occupy Transfer State. CMD12 can abort reads and writes, while programming and erase may continue after deselection. DAT0 indicates busy. Resetting with CMD0 or CMD15 terminates programming and may damage data.

The default bus width is one bit; ACMD6 selects four-bit operation but is rejected by locked cards. Reads and writes are block-oriented and CRC-protected. CMD17 reads one block, CMD18 reads multiple blocks, CMD24/CMD25 write blocks, and CMD16 sets applicable block length. SDHC and SDXC use fixed 512-byte blocks and block addressing; SDSC uses byte addressing and CMD16-defined lengths. Misalignment, invalid lengths, write protection, and CRC failures generate errors or discard data.

ACMD23 can pre-erase blocks before CMD25 to improve multiple-block writing, while ACMD22 reports successfully written blocks. Erase uses CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38. DISCARD and Full User Area Logical Erase also use CMD38 with distinct arguments, require support checks, apply only to SDHC/SDXC outside SPI, and signal busy on DAT0. DISCARD has a 250 ms timeout; FULE has a one-second timeout.

Write protection includes a host-managed mechanical switch, optional internal protection, and password locking. CMD42 manages passwords, locking, unlocking, clearing, and force erase. Card Ownership Protection adds a Force Erase Password, COP Unlock, protected force erase, and restrictions on clearing passwords. Incorrect parameters or passwords set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED. Force erase clears user data and the normal password but not the secure area; FEP Force Erase retains FEP.

CMD55 marks the next command as application-specific. CMD6 checks or switches function groups, including access mode, command systems, driver strength, and power limit. It returns 512 bits of status and supports check and set modes. High-Speed mode optionally raises interface speed to 25 MB/s at 50 MHz and requires a one-to-one host/card connection.

CMD8, issued in Idle state before ACMD41, checks host voltage compatibility and echoes the voltage and check pattern. Hosts may vary or stop the clock subject to transaction-completion and ACMD41 restrictions.

CRC7 protects commands and most responses; CRC16 protects data blocks, separately on each data line in wide-bus mode. CRC failures and illegal commands do not change card state and set status errors. Read timeout is generally at most 100 ms; write timeout is generally at most 250 ms, including SDHC operations.

The study develops a first-principles statistical-mechanics framework for calculating dilute equilibrium vacancy concentrations in multicomponent alloys at fixed composition. An embedded cluster expansion trained on density functional theory data models atomic and vacancy ordering on a body-centered cubic lattice, while canonical Monte Carlo simulations sample finite-temperature configurations. Chemical potentials are obtained through free-energy integration and Widom particle exchange.

Applied to a nine-component refractory alloy system containing group 4, 5, and 6 elements, the model reproduces formation energies with errors below about 8 meV per site. Alloys containing only group 5 and 6 elements exhibit very low vacancy concentrations, whereas adding Ti, Zr, or Hf increases concentrations by factors of 10–100 or more. Approximately 50–60% group 4 content is required in examined ternary and nonary systems to reach vacancy concentrations of about 10⁻⁵–10⁻⁴ at 1500°C.

Vacancy concentrations depend strongly on short-range order and chemical bonding. Favorable bonds suppress vacancy formation, while unfavorable bonds promote it. Vacancies preferentially associate with Zr and Hf in the first-neighbor shell and Mo in the second-neighbor shell in HfMoNbTiZr. Comparisons show that single special quasi-random structures can underestimate vacancy concentrations because they do not fully capture finite-temperature ordering and chemical potentials.

The framework agrees with grand-canonical simulations while requiring substantially fewer samples. Its main limitations are the dilute-vacancy approximation and omission of vibrational free-energy contributions, divacancies, and larger vacancy clusters.

A University of Maryland study of 1,099 college students found that persistent or occasional energy drink consumption between ages 21 and 24 was associated with increased risk of later cocaine or non-medical prescription stimulant use. Researchers said the link requires further investigation.

Azerbaijan plans to increase honey and beekeeping-product exports as global demand rises. Agriculture Minister Heydar Asadov said Azerbaijan’s organic honey has strong prospects in premium markets, particularly China and Japan. The ministry is developing programs and proposals to expand state support for beekeeping.

Microsoft’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2020 reported quarterly revenue of $35.0 billion, operating income of $13.0 billion, net income of $10.8 billion, and diluted earnings per share of $1.40, all higher than the prior-year quarter. Nine-month revenue was $105.0 billion and net income was $33.1 billion. Commercial cloud revenue rose 39% to $13.3 billion, supported by growth in Office 365, Azure, LinkedIn, and Dynamics 365. At March 31, Microsoft had $137.6 billion in cash, equivalents, and short-term investments, $285.4 billion in assets, and $114.5 billion in stockholders’ equity. COVID-19 had minimal net quarterly revenue impact: remote work and learning increased cloud, Windows, Surface, and gaming demand, while transactional licensing and advertising weakened. Microsoft repurchased $6.0 billion of shares during the quarter and declared a $0.51-per-share dividend.

The speaker fondly recalls Detroit as his first team, including two semifinal runs and strong ties to the city and teammates. His trade to Washington was initially difficult and unsuccessful, but he retained faith in its players and is excited by its improvement. Returning to Detroit will be special.

Marc Ó Sé believes an injury-free James O'Donoghue could significantly boost Kerry. The 2014 Footballer of the Year scored nine points against Clare, and Ó Sé expects regular games to build his confidence and form a formidable partnership with Paul Geaney.

The annual Scottish Accountancy & Finance Awards recognise accountants supporting private and public organisations. Hosted by Sarah Heaney, the event includes dinner, entertainment by DNA, and awards across seven categories. Tickets cost £132 plus VAT individually, with tables of 10 or 12 available.

The disclosure describes video encoding and decoding using intra prediction and non-separable transforms. For a block coded with a directional mode, coding information identifies a nominal mode and angular offset. The resulting prediction direction is derived from the nominal angle and offset, while a transform set is selected based on the nominal mode regardless of the offset. A signaled transform index may identify a non-separable transform within that set, and the block is reconstructed using the directional prediction and transform.

The non-separable transform may be primary or secondary, including a low-frequency non-separable transform. Reduced transforms map input coefficients to lower-dimensional vectors, decreasing computation and matrix-storage requirements. Secondary transforms may operate only on selected low-frequency coefficients or top-left coefficient regions, and may be restricted according to block size, significant-coefficient position, transform type, prediction mode, or transform-skip status. Certain implementations disable them for PAETH, recursive filtering, intra sub-partition, or matrix-based prediction modes.

The disclosure also covers transform-set mappings for non-directional modes, including DC, PAETH, SMOOTH, vertical and horizontal SMOOTH, recursive-filtering, and chroma-from-luma modes. Related techniques include multi-line prediction, line graph transforms, quantization, entropy coding, motion compensation, and block-based encoder and decoder architectures. The methods may be implemented by processing circuitry or instructions stored on a non-transitory computer-readable medium and applied in standards or formats including AV1, HEVC, and VVC.

The Texas Education Agency is investigating hundreds of teachers’ social media posts about Charlie Kirk’s killing, with Commissioner Mike Morath recommending possible license suspensions for remarks deemed inappropriate. Gov. Greg Abbott supported the inquiry, while districts have also disciplined employees under local conduct codes.

Legal experts and education advocates argue the investigations threaten teachers’ First Amendment rights when they speak personally on matters of public concern. They say disciplinary action generally requires evidence that comments significantly disrupted the workplace or impaired job performance, and public outrage alone may not meet that standard. Critics also warn that political pressure could deter educators from lawful speech.

The agency did not explain how it would account for free speech protections. Texas American Federation of Teachers President Zeph Capo described the response as a politically fueled “witch hunt” and argued that disagreement with educators’ personal views does not justify firing them.

Enron and Northwest Natural Gas confirmed talks over Portland General Electric. Reports valued the proposed transaction at about $1.8 billion in cash and stock plus assumed debt, potentially giving Enron a minority stake, though financing, terms, and board approval remained uncertain. Enron also planned to cut up to 500 European jobs. In India, BG’s $388 million purchase of Enron’s offshore assets faced an operatorship dispute, while Tata Power considered bidding for Enron’s Dabhol stake; BSES declined interest.

After ABC canceled the “Roseanne” reboot over Roseanne Barr’s racist tweet about former Obama adviser Valerie Jarrett, President Trump criticized the network and Disney CEO Bob Iger for not apologizing to him over negative statements aired on ABC. Democratic lawmakers condemned Trump’s response. Jarrett said Iger personally apologized and emphasized ABC’s zero tolerance for racist comments. She called the incident a teaching moment, saying national leadership shapes public tone while citizens also have a responsibility to oppose bigotry.

Bitcoin fell as much as 16% below US$8,000 before recovering to US$8,715, leaving it down 21% for the week and over half from its December peak. Regulatory threats, the US$500 million Coincheck theft, manipulation fears and Facebook’s cryptocurrency ad ban weighed on markets. Ripple, Ether and Litecoin also fell at least 18%.

Best Hope Services will launch Nigeria’s first online trade exhibition on May 1, enabling local inventors, researchers and entrepreneurs to showcase innovations globally without physical venues. The e-fair will cover expos, networking, trade and events across sectors including technology, automobiles and electronics. Nigerians are encouraged to register online before the event.

Microsoft announced that Chief Accounting Officer Frank H. Brod will step down July 31, 2020, and remain through September 30 to assist with the transition. Corporate Controller Alice L. Jolla will become Chief Accounting Officer effective July 31. She will receive a $1.5 million stock award vesting 6.25% quarterly, subject to continued employment.

Bond trading strategies systematically buy or sell bonds to pursue capital preservation, income, or appreciation. Approaches vary by time horizon, risk tolerance, market conditions, and objectives, including yield curve, duration, credit spread, tactical allocation, scalping, seasonal, intermarket, and price-action strategies.

Bond issuers borrow investor capital in exchange for scheduled interest and principal repayment at maturity. Bond prices generally fall when interest rates rise and increase when rates decline, creating interest-rate risk. Common trading mistakes include misunderstanding market dynamics, relying excessively on historical data, neglecting risk management, chasing yield, overlooking credit or liquidity risks, misjudging rates, inadequate diversification, inflexibility, and emotional bias.

The passage focuses on backtests using TLT, an ETF tracking 20-year Treasury bonds. Several seasonal, intermarket, and swing-trading strategies reportedly produced favorable historical results, though past patterns may not persist. Combining two bond strategies with an S&P 500 strategy bundle increased annual returns from 11.5% to 18.6% while reducing drawdowns, illustrating bonds’ potential diversification value and generally low correlation with stocks.

Day trading bonds seeks small intraday price movements but is challenging because bonds are often less volatile and sensitive to rates, economic data, and central-bank policies. Traders commonly focus on liquid government securities. Bond strategies can be automated using predefined algorithms, although human oversight remains important. Dollar-cost averaging is presented as a beginner strategy.

The study examines Hungarian higher education lecturers, using national and international statistics, legislation, and comparative analyses of staffing, qualifications, earnings, and doctoral education.

After 1990, Hungarian higher education expanded rapidly from a fragmented, low-capacity system toward mass education. Student numbers peaked in the mid-2000s before declining under demographic pressures and increasingly restrictive admissions and funding policies. Policies introduced after 2010 reduced access for some groups and contributed to Hungary’s low proportion of young graduates. Meanwhile, most state universities were transferred to public foundations in 2020, weakening institutional autonomy and replacing civil-service employment with labor-market contracts, though affected lecturers received substantial pay increases tied to performance evaluations.

Lecturer numbers initially followed student growth but diverged after 2005. The student-teacher ratio rose from 5.9 in 1990 to 17.9 in 2006, then fell to 10.4 by 2022. Hungarian lecturers are around the international middle range by age, while women represented 41.5% of lecturers in 2020. The number of university and college professors declined substantially after 2005, reflecting retirements, funding reductions, stricter appointment requirements, and low salaries.

Hungarian law specifies qualifications, appointment procedures, workloads, and research obligations for academic positions. Universities regained authority to award PhDs after 1993, although the Hungarian Academy of Sciences retained elements of the earlier centralized qualification system.

Academic careers offer weak financial returns. Doctorate holders working in academia earn less than graduates in the business sector for much of their careers, and their lifetime earnings are below the average for all university graduates. Hungary also ranks below 40th internationally in doctoral students per capita. Since doctoral student numbers correlate with scientific publication output, the limited doctoral population may threaten the future supply of educators and researchers. The study identifies low pay, emigration, career abandonment, institutional rigidity, limited transparency, unequal opportunities, and inadequate infrastructure as additional obstacles requiring policy attention.

China and the United States share interests in peace, trade, modernization, and concern over Soviet military expansion, but disagree on Taiwan. The speaker proposes strong, strategic U.S.-China relations, expanded trade and cultural ties, regional cooperation for growth and stability, and resistance to aggression or hegemony. He criticizes Carter’s normalization concessions and argues that U.S. commitments to Taiwan must follow the Taiwan Relations Act. The Act promotes peaceful, close relations with both Taiwan and mainland China, treats nonpeaceful efforts to determine Taiwan’s future as a grave concern, provides defensive weapons to Taiwan, and requires U.S. capacity to resist coercion threatening Taiwan. It also establishes procedures, funding, auditing, and congressional oversight for official relations conducted through the American Institute in Taiwan.

Microsoft is reportedly developing Polaris, a lightweight, modular Windows 10 version built on Windows Core OS for desktops, laptops and 2-in-1 devices. It would use Microsoft Store UWP apps instead of traditional desktop software and feature the scalable CShell interface. Removing legacy code could improve security, performance and battery life, but users could not upgrade Polaris to Windows 10 Pro. Microsoft is reportedly exploring remote virtualization to run legacy applications in containers. Windows Central suggested Polaris could appear in 2019.

The JACL Kakehashi Program will select up to 200 Japanese or Asian American students and young professionals ages 18–25 for nine-day Japan trips promoting U.S.-Japan relations through educational, cultural and homestay activities. Trips run Dec. 13–20 and March 12–20, with applications due Oct. 9 and Jan. 2.

Intel launched 14nm Coffee Lake desktop processors and Z370 chipsets, with motherboard vendors selling compatible boards worldwide. Additional desktop, enterprise and notebook Coffee Lake products are planned through mid-2018. Gemini Lake launches were scheduled for November 2017, followed by 10nm Cannon Lake and Ice Lake products.

Weekly making tips include adding rare-earth magnets to tester wires for difficult hookups, repurposing an old motor as a filming turntable, fitting a hobby knife into a compass for circular cuts, marking untrue material edges with squiggly lines, converting a drill press into a drum sander, and using an inexpensive flexi-neck LED lamp for directed workbench lighting.

Wal-Mart’s bid for online clothing retailer Bonobos is part of its strategy to challenge Amazon in online fashion and attract younger, affluent shoppers. If completed, it would be Wal-Mart’s fourth acquisition of a small online apparel brand in 2017, following ShoeBuy, Moosejaw and ModCloth. The effort is led by e-commerce chief Marc Lore, who joined after Wal-Mart’s $3.3 billion purchase of Jet.com. Although Wal-Mart is the largest brick-and-mortar clothing retailer, online sales represent about 3 percent of total sales, and it has struggled to attract customers and major apparel brands online. Analysts said the acquisitions remain too small for a material impact, while critics noted Wal-Mart’s previous acquisition-based efforts have performed poorly. Amazon led the U.S. online clothing and footwear market with $13 billion in 2016 sales.

Researchers from the Russian Academy of Sciences, MIPT and other institutions established how polypropylene’s molecular regularity and thermal treatment influence its mechanical properties. Polypropylene chains vary in isotacticity, determined by the orientation of attached methyl groups. More isotactic segments form more crystalline crosslinks, generally producing harder, stronger material.

The team tested polypropylene films with isotacticity ranging from 25% to over 95%. Films were either rapidly quenched in ice water or slowly cooled, then stretched mechanically. Stress-strain measurements showed that elasticity and toughness depend on isotacticity, crystallinity and cooling history. Rapidly and slowly cooled samples also formed differently shaped crystallites. The findings could enable manufacturers to adjust molecular structure and processing conditions to produce polypropylene with predetermined properties, ranging from elasticity to hardness.

The “Drive & Kick” offense uses a three-player weave from a 3-2 spread. Players attack the basket, avoiding charges, then pass outside and replace receivers when penetration is denied. The continuity can consume clock before a set play. Against baseline help, players may kick to the corner or pass to a back cutter.

On May 30, 1976, Kent Howerton won the AMA 500cc National opener, followed by Bob Hannah and Tony DiStefano, with six brands filling the top six. In 1982, Ricky Johnson won the High Point 250 National, while Darrell Shultz won the 500 class. Mark Barnett won the Toronto Supercross. Yamaha’s budget cuts affected bikes and coaching, while riders favored better-paying overseas events. Ross Pederson won the 1987 Montreal Supercross.

The Housing Authority of Santa Barbara received a Gold Nugget Award for Bradley Studios, a 54-unit affordable housing development completed in 2012. Replacing blighted buildings, the environmentally responsible Craftsman-style project houses low-income residents with special needs. Amenities include community spaces and offices offering mental health care, addiction counseling, job training and life-skills classes.

Materials modeling seeks atomistic structures representative of disordered materials, requiring accurate, scalable methods that reproduce experimental structural distributions. Conventional Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics do not guarantee experimental agreement. Reverse and hybrid reverse Monte Carlo improve agreement by optimizing against experimental observables, but simple potentials can produce artifacts and require material-specific constraints. Machine-learning potentials have enabled ab-initio-accurate hybrid methods and XPS matching without such constraints, though Monte Carlo remains computationally inefficient.

Previous molecular-dynamics approaches to experimental matching suffered from poor scaling, inaccurate finite-difference gradients, omitted thermal broadening, unstable structures, and bonding constraints. The article presents molecular augmented dynamics (MAD), an O(N) modified MD method for finding low-energy, ab-initio-accurate structures consistent with experimental data. It derives smooth, analytic, thermally broadened experimental forces for XRD, neutron diffraction, pair distribution functions, and XPS, including descriptor-based observables, and reports CPU and GPU implementations in TurboGAP.

MAD uses the Hamiltonian \(H=T+V+\tilde V\), combining kinetic energy, an interatomic potential, and an experimental potential measuring disagreement with data. Its dynamics jointly optimize physical energy and experimental agreement: \(V\) discourages unphysical configurations, \(\tilde V\) imposes experimental constraints, and \(T\) influences sampled entropy. Analytical negative gradients of both potentials provide interatomic and experimental forces for computational efficiency.

Acting CDC Director Jim O’Neill urged manufacturers to replace the combined measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine with three separate vaccines, echoing President Trump. The passage states there is no evidence separate shots are safer or more effective, and monovalent vaccines are unavailable in the U.S. Developing them would require years of trials, manufacturing changes, and FDA review. A 2017 study found higher completion rates for combination vaccines than single-antigen vaccines. The MMR vaccine has been administered for decades, is highly effective, and has minimal side-effect risks, though it carries a small increased risk of febrile seizures. Experts warned that calls to separate the vaccines could reduce vaccination rates and leave more children vulnerable to preventable diseases.

The study examined empathy among 206 education faculty teachers across three campuses of a Spanish university. Participants completed the Spanish Interpersonal Reactivity Index, measuring Perspective Taking, Fantasy, Empathic Concern and Personal Distress, alongside a demographic questionnaire.

Overall empathy was high, with above-theoretical-average scores for Perspective Taking, Fantasy and Empathic Concern, while Personal Distress was moderate. Female participants scored significantly higher than others in overall empathy and every dimension. Empathy did not differ significantly by degree taught, campus, contractual status or length of teaching experience. Prior non-university teaching experience was associated with higher Perspective Taking, Fantasy and Empathic Concern, whereas university-only experience was associated with higher Personal Distress, although total empathy did not significantly differ.

The findings suggest teachers display a potentially protective balance between empathy and emotional overinvolvement. They support equipping university teacher educators with skills for empathic interactions, enabling them to model empathy for students in line with sustainable education goals. Limitations include the small sample and possible social desirability bias, which restrict generalisation.

NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere GA100 architecture and TSMC’s 7nm process, targets AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. It contains 108 streaming multiprocessors, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1,555 GB/s, and a 40 MB L2 cache.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. Compared with V100, A100 delivers up to 2.5 times greater dense mixed-precision and FP64 performance. TF32 accelerates FP32-based workloads without requiring script changes, while 2:4 structured sparsity can double Tensor Core throughput by skipping zero values.

Memory and execution improvements include larger shared memory and L1 cache, higher L2 bandwidth, cache-residency controls, compute data compression, simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, asynchronous global-to-shared memory copies, asynchronous barriers, improved atomic operations, and hardware-accelerated JPEG, video, optical-flow, and stereo-disparity processing. CUDA 11 supports these capabilities along with task graphs, which reduce launch overhead and inter-kernel latency.

Multi-Instance GPU technology partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU instances with dedicated compute and memory-system resources. This provides predictable performance, quality of service, fault isolation, and improved utilization for virtual machines, containers, processes, and multi-tenant cloud environments. GPU instances can also be divided into compute instances for simultaneous context execution.

Third-generation NVLink doubles total GPU interconnect bandwidth over V100 to 600 GB/s. A100 also supports NVSwitch, PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, Magnum IO, InfiniBand, Ethernet, and enhanced error detection, containment, and recovery.

The DGX A100 system combines eight A100 GPUs, offering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and as many as 56 isolated GPU instances. Its NVLink, NVSwitch, InfiniBand, Magnum IO, NGC software, and support for Slurm and Kubernetes enable deployments ranging from individual workloads to large AI clusters.

Using spatial transcriptomics, single-cell imaging, and immunohistochemistry, the study characterized IDO1- and PD-L1-expressing immune niches in dermal leishmaniasis. In Sri Lankan cutaneous leishmaniasis lesions, these checkpoints were enriched in mature dendritic cells and CCL18+ macrophages within myeloid-rich regions. Their closest cellular neighbours commonly included CD8+ memory T cells, regulatory T cells, and other macrophages.

IL-32 was highly expressed by neighbouring CD8+ memory T cells and regulatory T cells, while associated myeloid cells expressed CXCL9, CCL18, IL-24, IFNGR2, and IL-1β. IL32β and IL32γ were elevated in lesions relative to healthy skin. Analyses of Brazilian cutaneous leishmaniasis and Indian post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis identified a shared IDO1/PD-L1-associated signature comprising IL32, LYZ, GBP1, IFI30, and FTH1.

Among 25 Sri Lankan patients treated with sodium stibogluconate, low lesion abundance of IL-32 and IL-32+CD8+ cells was associated with earlier cure. IL-32+FoxP3+ regulatory T-cell abundance was not significantly associated with cure rate. The authors propose that CCL18+ macrophages recruit IL-32-producing T cells, which promote checkpoint expression in dendritic cells and macrophages, thereby suppressing effector T-cell activity and potentially limiting immune-dependent chemotherapy. Limitations included restricted biopsy sampling, small cohorts, use of unmatched reference data for cell deconvolution, and inability to functionally characterize lesion-derived cells.

The Department opposed dividing the General Assembly into regional sections, fearing decentralization would complicate establishment and weaken the effectiveness of a strong international organization. Regional committees might later be useful, but discussion should await the Organization’s firm establishment.

The February 21 Mexico City Conference would allow American republics to discuss mutual concerns, potentially including Argentina and the Dumbarton Oaks proposals. The United States intended to seek support without accepting inconsistent commitments, continuing its policy in discussions with Latin American ambassadors.

The Dumbarton Oaks proposals called for an International Court of Justice as the Organization’s principal judicial organ, governed by an annexed statute binding on members and open conditionally to nonmembers. Its statute could revise or replace that of the Permanent Court. Because unresolved legal and practical issues affected enemy, armistice, and neutral states, the recommended procedure was to convene about fifteen technically qualified jurists selected by the United States, United Kingdom, Soviet Union, and China. They would draft a statute based on the existing one and propose alternative implementation procedures for consideration at the United Nations Conference.

Three Illinois gang members were fatally shot at point-blank range during Larry’s Fun Fest at Great Lakes Dragaway near Union Grove, Wisconsin, on Aug. 13, 2017. Authorities identified the victims as David L. Watson, Khalid R. Howard and Derek K. Edwards. Kenosha County Sheriff David Beth said the targeted killings appeared gang-related, but the motive remained unknown. The suspected shooter, described as a thin, athletic Black man in his 20s, fled in an unidentified vehicle and remained at large. A pistol was used but not recovered. The event drew about 15,000 people and had private security, though spectators were not screened for weapons. Investigators preserved evidence overnight and reported difficulty obtaining assistance from victims’ relatives.

UNC Chapel Hill placed associate professor Dwayne Dixon on leave while investigating alleged advocacy of politically motivated violence. Dixon formerly belonged to Silver Valley Redneck Revolt, an antifascist, antiracist and anticapitalist group that disbanded in 2019, and previously participated in armed protection of counterprotesters.

The investigation followed controversy over Georgetown University fliers promoting a potential chapter of the John Brown Gun Club, a Redneck Revolt affiliate. Turning Point USA spokesperson Andrew Kolvet subsequently highlighted Dixon’s former membership and called for his firing. UNC did not confirm whether Kolvet’s post or related media coverage prompted its action.

Dixon said he left Redneck Revolt in 2018. A petition seeking his reinstatement received more than 900 signatures, while North Carolina and UNC chapters of the American Association of University Professors accused administrators of responding to unsubstantiated right-wing claims. Dixon is among numerous faculty members recently disciplined or investigated after being identified on social media by right-wing figures.

The MSPM0C1105/6 are ultra-low-power 32-bit microcontrollers based on an Arm Cortex-M0+ CPU operating at up to 32MHz. They support 1.62V to 3.6V supplies and temperatures from –40°C to 125°C, with up to 64KB flash and 8KB SRAM. The CPU subsystem includes instruction prefetch, a two-line cache, SysTick, and an interrupt controller with four priority levels.

Five operating modes—RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN—provide configurable power and performance options across two power domains. Integrated clock sources include 32kHz and factory-trimmed 32MHz oscillators, with support for external low- and high-frequency clocks.

Peripherals include three-channel DMA, an event-routing system, CRC-16, up to 45 GPIOs, configurable IOMUX, a 12-bit ADC operating at up to 1.6Msps, temperature sensor, selectable 1.4V or 2.5V reference, comparator with 8-bit DAC, RTC, independent and windowed watchdogs, general-purpose and advanced 16-bit timers, three UARTs, two I2C interfaces, and one SPI interface. Supported communication features include LIN, IrDA, DALI, Manchester, smart card, SMBus, and PMBus.

Flash has 1KB sectors; selected sectors support up to 100,000 program/erase cycles. SRAM provides zero-wait-state access, configurable 1KB write protection, and retention through STANDBY but not SHUTDOWN. Security and debugging features include memory firewalls, SWD, debug lockout, password-authenticated debugging, and factory-programmed identification and trim data.

TI recommends 10µF and 0.1µF VDD decoupling capacitors, a 47kΩ NRST pullup with a 1000pF capacitor, and pullups for 5V-tolerant open-drain outputs. TI provides development boards, software, configuration tools, documentation, and support resources. Revision A removed DGS32 package information, updated specifications and CPU details, revised ADC ENOB information, added DEBUGSS content, and updated device-identification tables.

A federal appeals court allowed the Education Department to proceed with firing half of the Office for Civil Rights’ 550 employees, staying a lower-court injunction. The court said the case was not sufficiently different from a parallel case in which the Supreme Court permitted department-wide layoffs, while acknowledging concerns that the cuts could imperil OCR’s enforcement of federal civil rights laws.

The AMD Secure RNG library provides high-level APIs for accessing hardware-generated random values through the x86 RDRAND and RDSEED instructions. RDRAND returns 16-, 32-, or 64-bit random values, while RDSEED returns conditioned values in the same sizes. APIs support individual values, arrays of 32- or 64-bit values, and byte arrays, with status reporting and configurable retry attempts.

The library abstracts low-level instruction handling, detects hardware failures, and includes CPUID-based functions to verify RDRAND and RDSEED support before use. It is intended for applications requiring random numbers, including Monte Carlo simulations, communication protocols, gaming, cryptography, authentication, e-commerce, and PRNG seeding.

Each hardware request reads from the AMD Secure Processor’s cryptographic co-processor through memory-mapped I/O, making it slower than software PRNGs. For latency-sensitive applications, hardware-generated values can seed a software PRNG to combine improved performance with stronger security.

A bearish engulfing candlestick pattern typically appears during an uptrend and consists of a small bullish candle followed by a larger bearish candle whose body completely engulfs the first. It indicates a shift toward bearish sentiment and a potential reversal, but does not guarantee one.

Traders may close long positions, enter short positions, or adjust stop-loss orders. For short trades, a stop-loss can be placed above the first candle’s high, with profit targeted near support. Validity may be confirmed using other indicators, changes in momentum or price action, and the broader trend context.

Backtests on the S&P 500 report a 55–65% win rate and 311 occurrences since 1993. However, one test found that buying the pattern and selling eight days later produced an average 0.73% gain across 258 trades, suggesting it can behave bullishly or as a continuation pattern. Filtering for a five-day RSI above 60 raised the average gain to 0.88% across 58 trades.

Reliability depends on market conditions, volatility, timeframe, and trading rules. Risks include false signals, leverage, and unexpected price movements. Recommended risk controls include stop-losses, position sizing, diversification, hedging, risk/reward ratios, and a defined risk-management plan. Other bearish reversal patterns include dark cloud cover, evening star, and bearish harami.

Carolina Herrera appointed Lisa Arnold vice president of retail and Thea Terenik vice president of global merchandising, both reporting to president Emilie Rubinfeld in New York. Arnold will oversee global retail and client service, while Terenik will direct brand positioning, product strategy and distribution. The company also added Maria Borges to its fall campaign.

The 50 EMA strategy uses the 50-day exponential moving average to identify medium-term trends and generate trading signals. Traders commonly enter long positions when price is above an upward-sloping EMA and short positions when price is below a downward-sloping EMA, often confirming signals with RSI, MACD, or other indicators. Medium-term timeframes such as four-hour or daily charts are typical, though strategies should be backtested across timeframes and market conditions.

A basic moving-average crossover performed poorly across several assets. On the S&P 500 from 1960, it returned 6.8% annually versus 7.3% for buy-and-hold, but reduced maximum drawdown from 56% to 32%. Using the 50 EMA as a filter with a second indicator improved results. For QQQ, the strategy produced 477 trades, a 0.6% average gain, 73% win rate, 11.5% annual return, 27% market exposure, and 22% maximum drawdown. For SPY, it generated 614 trades, a 0.45% average gain, 8.9% annual return, 29% exposure, and 16% maximum drawdown. Results for TLT were decent, though its average gain per trade was only 0.18%.

Risk controls may include stop-loss and take-profit orders, suitable risk-reward ratios, and diversification, although the passage notes that stop-losses rarely improved the authors’ backtests. The strategy’s simplicity and clear signals are advantages, but effective use requires confirmation, testing, adaptation, patience, and discipline.

British shares fell after Federal Reserve minutes signaled balance-sheet reductions later in 2017, with the FTSE 100 down about 0.6 percent. Banks Lloyds and RBS declined amid a broader European banking sell-off. Pearson dropped 8.9 percent after an Exane downgrade and trading ex-dividend. Allied Minds hit a record low below its IPO price following funding cuts to seven portfolio companies. Real estate and mining stocks gained, while Tullow Oil rose 6 percent and BTG advanced 3.8 percent on a bullish forecast.

U.S. manufacturing has nearly 390,000 openings, but automation and advanced technology require skills many displaced workers lack. As workplaces transform through technology and global pressures, trained workers benefit while others struggle to adapt.

Coach Quenneville and Stan Bowman discussed Chicago’s preparation for the upcoming series, emphasizing the opponent’s strong positioning, checking, playmaking, shooting and goaltending. Chicago intends to play to its strengths, create traffic at the net and force the opponent to defend.

Bowman praised Corey’s consistent goaltending and gradual development into an established NHL starter. Quenneville highlighted the team’s maturity, playoff experience, enthusiasm and improvement through recent rounds. Both credited continuity, incremental roster improvements, player development, coaching and organizational teamwork for the season’s success.

Bowman also praised Bryan “Bicks” for developing into a consistent, important contributor, while noting the impact of younger players including Andrew Shaw, Brandon Saad and Nick Leddy. Quenneville identified Chara’s defensive presence and the opponent’s mobile defense and point shooting as major challenges. He also commended Sharpie’s productive, responsible playoff performance.

Liberal nonprofits are preparing for potential Trump administration investigations, legal challenges, funding restrictions, and loss of tax-exempt status. Proposed responses include creating emergency funds, merging or dissolving organizations, becoming businesses, relocating abroad, accelerating grants, and reviewing financial and legal compliance.

Following Charlie Kirk’s murder, Trump administration figures and allies blamed nonprofit networks for supporting radical-left activism and violence. Trump called for investigations into funding associated with “antifa,” while Justice Department officials reportedly drafted plans to investigate the Open Society Foundations. The foundation rejected the accusations as politically motivated, affirming that its work is peaceful and lawful.

Republican lawmakers have also proposed measures targeting organizations accused of supporting terrorism, demonstrations, or riots. Nonprofit leaders warn that even unsuccessful government actions could damage reputations, drain resources, reduce donations, and encourage self-censorship. Foundations are consequently distributing money more quickly to offset funding cuts and prepare organizations for a more difficult operating environment.

The 1-2-2 zone is effective against outside shooting teams, supports fast breaks, protects late leads, and can extend into half- or full-court pressure. The point starts atop the circle, wings at the elbows, and baseline defenders above the blocks. Defenders shift while passes are airborne, keeping arms extended.

The nearest defender covers the ball; teammates protect the high and low posts, basket, passing lanes, and weakside rebounding areas. Baseline players move together, while wings shift oppositely. The point guards the ball out front and protects the high post when the ball moves to a wing or corner. If the ball enters the middle, all defenders collapse.

On corner passes, coaches may have the wing deny the return pass or drop to assist against a strong post player. The defense can also trap the corner, with other defenders blocking return and high-post passes. Because offenses often use two guards, the 1-2-2 can switch to a 2-1-2 after the first pass, placing an active defender in the middle and maintaining weakside rebounding coverage.

Emory University researchers studied whether the probiotic Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) could protect the liver from acetaminophen-induced damage. Mice fed an LGG-rich diet for two weeks showed a stronger liver antioxidant response after receiving high doses of acetaminophen than mice on a normal diet. The study identified the protein Nrf2, which regulates genes involved in combating free radicals, as important in protecting against oxidative liver injury. Although the findings suggest probiotic effects may extend beyond the gastrointestinal tract, further studies are needed to determine whether they apply to humans. Probiotics are not a substitute for medical treatment, and people should consult a doctor before taking new supplements.

NVIDIA Turing introduces mesh shading for flexible, GPU-driven geometry processing, supporting more objects, geometric synthesis, and LOD management. Variable Rate Shading dynamically adjusts shading frequency to improve efficiency and frame rates. Texture-space shading caches and reuses results to reduce duplicate work or improve quality. Multi-View Rendering renders multiple views with different positions or directions in one pass.

Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) enforced Kenya’s 2014 national referral guidelines on July 1, 2021, requiring prior consultation and official referral letters to ensure that only patients needing specialized orthopaedic and trauma care were admitted. A pre-post study reviewed 468 referrals from five months before and after enforcement.

Most referrals originated in Nairobi and neighboring counties, and about three-fifths came from government facilities. Enforcement did not significantly change referrals by facility ownership, but referral patterns differed significantly by facility tier. Direct referrals from tiers II and III declined, while referrals from tiers IV–VI increased. Forty-three facilities stopped referring to KNH, including 29 private facilities; over four-fifths were tiers II–IV.

Major referral factors were inadequate human resources, infrastructure, equipment and implants, financial considerations, and patient preference. Patient preference was more prominent among private-facility referrals. The study concluded that referral guidelines can be successfully enforced and recommended continued sensitization, stronger health-facility capacity, standardized procedures, staff training, and adherence to referral requirements. Limitations included COVID-19 effects and the retrospective quasi-experimental design.

March 28, 2001 news reports covered Enron’s falling share price, executive bonuses, online energy trading, regulatory developments, and international power projects. CEO Jeffrey Skilling attributed Enron’s stock decline to reduced valuations for high-PE companies, while an analyst cited Enron-specific concerns involving broadband, India’s Dabhol plant, and the ended Blockbuster agreement. Chairman Kenneth Lay received a $7 million bonus and Skilling $5.6 million after Enron’s 2000 profit rose 32 percent to $1.3 billion.

Other reports said ICE planned Colonial Pipeline product trading; FERC sought input on coordinating regional transmission organizations; Nigeria planned to dismantle its state electricity monopoly; and an Enron unit proposed a two-million-kilowatt LNG power plant in Japan. Viacom abandoned plans to spin off its remaining Blockbuster stake. California regulators approved electricity rate increases approaching 50 percent to support utilities and power purchases, a move Skilling said could help balance supply and demand.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K on January 28, 2019, reporting updated guidance for the quarter ended January 27, 2019. The filing includes a press release and shareholder letter as exhibits, furnished but not deemed filed under applicable securities laws. CFO Colette M. Kress signed the report.

Texas Tech University posted, then removed after three days, an FAQ clarifying policies restricting faculty instruction and speech about transgender identity. The guidance said research was unaffected, discouraged LGBTQ allyship statements and pronoun language on syllabi, and allowed relevant classroom discussions provided instructors did not advocate a particular view. It acknowledged possible effects on faculty recruitment and retention but did not explicitly mention “transgender” in its answers.

The FAQ applied only to the flagship campus, leaving other system campuses without written guidance. A Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center faculty member said instructors were verbally told not to use terms including “transgender,” “gender-affirming care,” “diversity, equity and inclusion,” and “affirmative action.” Health-care faculty expressed concern because transgender patient care appears on licensing certification exams, while instructors remain uncertain how to respond when students raise the topic.

The Texas conference of the American Association of University Professors criticized the policies as threats to academic freedom and faculty rights.

Closson sought to foreclose a lien for lumber supplied to contractor Worley for Billman’s residence. Closson had also signed Worley’s $1,500 performance bond. Because the construction contract required Worley to furnish and pay for materials, the bond’s requirement to complete the residence “according to his contract” included delivering it free of material liens. Closson was therefore liable as a guarantor, not a surety, for Worley’s default. His resulting liability provided a defense to the lien action, avoiding circuity of action. Notice of acceptance was unnecessary because the guaranty was executed contemporaneously with the underlying transaction. Closson bore the burden of pleading and proving lack of notice of default and resulting damage. The judgment for defendants was affirmed.

Motley Fool Money highlights the no-annual-fee Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card for its unlimited 2% cash rewards, $200 bonus after $500 in purchases within three months, and 0% introductory APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers. Afterward, a variable APR of 18.99%, 23.99%, or 28.99% applies. Additional benefits include nonexpiring rewards, Visa Signature concierge service, and up to $600 in cell phone protection with a $25 deductible. Applicants generally need good or excellent credit, though approval is not guaranteed.

Alternatives include the Capital One Quicksilver card, offering 1.5% cash back, selected 5% travel rewards, up to $300 in welcome bonuses, and a 15-month introductory APR period; and a Citi card offering up to 2% cash back, selected 5% travel rewards, a $200 bonus, and an 18-month balance-transfer introductory APR.

Motley Fool Money receives partner commissions but states that compensation does not influence ratings and that not all market offers are included.

The paper examines how COVID-19 affected global education and how Comparative and International Education can support progress toward Sustainable Development Goal 4 and the Incheon Declaration’s 2030 vision of inclusive, equitable, quality education and lifelong learning. Education is also presented as a prerequisite for achieving the other Sustainable Development Goals.

Before the pandemic, global education already faced major deficiencies in participation, quality and equality. In 2020, 258 million school-age children were not attending school. Education systems showed weaknesses in resources, teaching and learning, student outcomes, and education’s effects on later life. Inequalities persisted across socioeconomic status, gender and race or ethnicity.

COVID-19 closures affected about 91% of the global student population and prompted a rapid transition to online and home-based learning. This reduced opportunities and quality for many learners while disproportionately harming disadvantaged students and worsening existing inequalities. In South Africa, substantial numbers of learners lost contact with teachers, received no homework, or attended schools unable to collect fees.

The pandemic also forced education systems to adopt technologies they had previously resisted. The paper argues that Comparative and International Education should study pandemic-related damage and evaluate technology-based responses across diverse educational and societal contexts. Such comparisons could inform effective use of technology in pursuing the 2030 goals.

Taking on this role could also address weaknesses within the field, including insufficient responsiveness to new developments, limited attention to classroom teaching and learning, reliance on theories from other disciplines, marginalization in universities, Northern dominance, and limited influence on scholarship, practice, system reform and policy. The paper concludes that the field can help education systems recover beyond pre-pandemic conditions and build improved systems aligned with the 2030 vision.

A traditional Bulgarian and Turkish method uses four live ants in warmed cow’s milk. The ants and their bacteria acidify and thicken the milk into yogurt, while frozen or dehydrated ants are less effective.

Delta Insurance aims to become a key partner for the South Island’s booming technology sector, offering technology, cyber, liability, drone, environmental and pollution risk insurance. It has joined Canterbury Tech and provides cyber risk assessments and expert support. South Island underwriter Karl Samson brings 12 years’ industry experience and local knowledge of brokers and businesses.

W. T. Hay, discharged in bankruptcy, sought to stay execution on a pre-bankruptcy judgment levied against real estate previously conveyed through his brother to his wife. Because Hay neither owned nor claimed the property and execution against him personally had been stayed, the court held that the sale could not affect his rights and dismissed his appeal. Questions concerning the creditor’s authority and title passing at sale could be raised by Hay’s wife, not Hay.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for planning vehicle, particularly AGV, routes using maps containing nodes and node information. A scheduling system modifies map data based on the locations and motion status of other vehicles, then determines start and destination nodes and calculates route costs. Static vehicles cause nearby nodes to receive high weights, turn restrictions, or impassable status; planned paths of moving vehicles may similarly affect node weights. This helps routes avoid collisions.

Route costs may combine node weight, accumulated parent-node cost, distance, turning cost, and estimated distance to the destination. An iterative search using open and closed node sets selects minimum-cost nodes until reaching the destination. If an initial route conflicts with moving vehicles, the system may further modify the map and perform a second route planning process.

The disclosed implementations include processor-based systems, devices, modules, methods, and computer-readable media. A route planning system may contain servers, networks, vehicles, terminals, and storage devices. It can support applications such as freight transport, sightseeing, and automated delivery. The system may also allocate tasks according to vehicle availability, assigning specified tasks to designated vehicles or unspecified tasks to the nearest idle vehicle. Maps and node information may be periodically updated to reflect changing conditions.

VentureWire’s June 7, 2001 edition reports that FreeMarkets and Adexa terminated their proposed $340 million acquisition, replacing it with a $6 million FreeMarkets investment and strategic relationship. inVentures and Redwood Partners merged to form Redwood Partners International, which is raising a $100 million fund. ChipData raised $23 million, and Matrix Partners appointed former Crosspoint partner Bob Lisbonne.

Funding announcements include $31 million for ThruPoint, $18.5 million for Corus Pharma, $14 million for Decision Management International, $12.6 million for Blackstone Technology, $11 million for DevelopOnline, and $8.5 million for Idesta. nCoTec completed a $38.2 million first closing for its first venture fund.

Business setbacks included Intransit Networks closing its Seattle office, Music.com shutting down, Notara cutting 9% of staff, and Wapit filing for bankruptcy. i-drive discontinued free consumer storage to focus on software.

Acquisition activity included Salu buying ScanRx technology assets, ClosingGuard acquiring MBH Settlement, Platinum Equity agreeing to buy McKessonHBOC product groups, and Manugistics planning to acquire selected SpaceWorks assets. Triton Systems spun off Elecon, Tribond, and Sensera with combined financing of $9.75 million.

Personnel changes included new leadership at Gemini Voice Solutions, Nationtax Online, and BlueKite.com. Whitney & Co. managing director Mark Murphy departed amid broader staffing reductions and office spin-offs.

The policy calls for firm, verifiable arms-control agreements based on real reductions, equality, stability, and warhead limits, while emphasizing Soviet responsibility for stalled progress. Regional diplomacy should test Soviet intentions on Afghanistan, address southern Africa, Kampuchea, China, and Nicaragua, and avoid restoring Moscow’s Middle East role. Human-rights efforts should prioritize private diplomacy on prisoners, divided families, Pentecostalists, Jewish emigration, Poland, and CSCE commitments. Economic measures must not strengthen or subsidize the USSR and should align trade with broader strategy. Reciprocal cultural and bilateral initiatives could broaden access to Soviet society. Dialogue should develop cautiously through potential summitry, ministerial meetings, ambassadors, and specialist contacts. The overall aim for 1983 is intensified engagement that protects U.S. security and encourages Soviet concessions without weakening established policy; if Moscow fails to meet U.S. criteria, responsibility for continued tensions would rest with the USSR.

MacKenzie Scott is reinforcing her commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion through large, unrestricted education grants. Recent gifts include $42 million to college-access nonprofit 10,000 Degrees, tens of millions to Native Forward, and $70 million to UNCF to strengthen endowments across 37 HBCUs. Her trust-based philanthropy prioritizes underrepresented, low-income, and first-generation students while giving recipients flexibility over spending. Scott has donated more than $19 billion to thousands of organizations over five years, including roughly $2 billion in 2024, and is expanding into mission-aligned investments focused on economic mobility, education, and health.

Apple Inc. reported completing a $7 billion senior unsecured note offering on November 13, 2017. The offering comprised six series: $1 billion of 1.800% notes due 2019, $1 billion of 2.000% notes due 2020, $750 million of 2.400% notes due 2023, $1.5 billion of 2.750% notes due 2025, $1.5 billion of 3.000% notes due 2027, and $1.25 billion of 3.750% notes due 2047. Interest is payable semiannually. The notes rank equally with Apple’s other unsecured, unsubordinated debt. Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, and Merrill Lynch represented the underwriters. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, note forms, legal opinion, and earnings-to-fixed-charges computation.

Amazon filed a Form 8-K on February 1, 2018, announcing fourth-quarter and full-year 2017 financial results. The filing incorporates a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. CFO Brian T. Olsavsky signed the report.
The Jerusalem Post seeks $5 monthly reader support to sustain open journalism, offering fewer ads, premium content, magazines, The Jerusalem Report and a daily ePaper.

Best Buy is discounting the Lenovo Legion 7i Gen 10 by $220 to $1,650. The gaming laptop features a color-accurate 2,560 x 1,600 OLED display with 1,000-nit peak brightness, a 165-Hz refresh rate, and a 115-watt RTX 5060 GPU. It also has a strong keyboard and trackpad, but battery life lasted under five hours in video playback testing. The discount helps offset its higher price compared with lower-wattage RTX 5060 laptops.

Cu-doped NiO thin films were fabricated on ITO-coated glass using spray pyrolysis at 450°C with a 1.5-minute deposition time and evaluated for LPG sensing. The doped precursor contained 7 wt% copper chloride dihydrate relative to nickel chloride hexahydrate. Structural, optical, electrical, and sensing properties were examined using XRD, FESEM, UV-Vis, Raman, photoluminescence, and current-voltage measurements.

XRD showed cubic NiO with a (111) peak and no separate Cu phase, indicating Cu²⁺ substitution for Ni²⁺. Cu doping expanded the lattice parameter from 4.18 to 4.20 Å and reduced crystallite size from 21 to 20 nm. Raman peak shifts and disappearance of the TO mode further indicated lattice distortion and successful Cu incorporation.

Cu-doped NiO exhibited greater visible-light absorption and a bandgap reduction from 3.70 to 3.65 eV. Photoluminescence intensity decreased, while peak broadening and red shifts indicated increased defect density and non-radiative recombination centers.

Under approximately 1 vol% LPG, both films showed increased current and reduced resistance. At 5 V, NiO current increased from 249 to 327 mA, while NiO:Cu increased from 265 to 480 mA. Sensitivity at 5 V was 1.3 for NiO and 1.8 for NiO:Cu. The improved response was attributed to enhanced charge transport, additional adsorption sites, defect states, and increased surface reactivity. The study identifies ultra-fast spray-deposited Cu-doped NiO as a cost-effective material for responsive LPG sensors.

U.S. airlines posted record-low domestic flight cancellations, mishandled baggage, and involuntary bumping rates in 2016. On-time arrivals improved to 81.4 percent, led by Hawaiian Airlines, while traveler complaints declined 11.3 percent to 17,904. Cancellation rates fell to 1.17 percent from 1.5 percent in 2015.

Alek Minassian, 25, was charged with 10 counts of first-degree murder after allegedly driving a rental van into Toronto pedestrians, killing 10 and injuring 15. Officials said the attack did not threaten national security, and the motive remained unknown. Prime Minister Justin Trudeau urged Canadians to remain united and not live in fear. Memorials appeared across Toronto, flags were lowered, and the CN Tower went dark. The officer who arrested Minassian peacefully was praised.

Oregon Health & Science University researchers report that a technique previously used to create healthy mouse pups from lab-made eggs has been mostly unsuccessful with human cells. They developed “mitomeiosis,” a process that reduces chromosome numbers to prevent embryos from having twice the normal amount. Significant obstacles remain before clinical testing, but the approach could eventually help treat infertility, prevent inherited diseases, and enable same-sex couples to have genetically related children.

The passage documents AMD AGESA firmware integration across UEFI PEI/DXE, boot, suspend, and resume phases. It describes:

- PPIs and HOBs signaling completion of early processor and memory initialization and reporting system memory ranges.
- PEIMs coordinating initialization and warm-reset requests, plus DXE drivers that perform late initialization, publish AGESA-generated tables, and control integrated-GPU VGA decoding.
- Reference files, UEFI build-control files, environment variables, platform option files, and binary-module or source-integration build methods.
- Cache-As-RAM stack macros and restrictions, including required stack setup, cache-control preservation, architecture-specific behavior, and stack removal after memory becomes available.
- Utility services for allocating structures, reading event logs, querying processors, memory, PCI/APIC addresses, execution-cache capacity, DIMM data-eye results, and updating MMIO mappings.
- The initialization sequence: minimal reset initialization, early processor and interconnect configuration, memory initialization, post-memory environment setup, graphics configuration, late ACPI/DMI table generation, Ready-to-Boot context saving, and S3 resume restoration.
- Extensive platform configuration options covering CPU power management, VRMs, PCIe, graphics, displays, chipset controllers, memory timing, interleaving, ECC, UMA, training, refresh, and overclocking.
- Required host call-outs for memory-buffer allocation, lookup and release, system resets, SPD reads, and executing tasks on application processors.
- Dependencies, architecture limitations, cache-allocation rules, required execution order, and AGESA status codes for success, warnings, errors, and fatal failures.

Lisa Baird became commissioner of the National Women’s Soccer League in March 2020, just as COVID-19 halted U.S. sports. Concerned that canceling the season could threaten the eight-year-old league, she coordinated medical, financial, competition, location, player, childcare, and social justice workstreams to develop a safe, affordable return-to-play plan.

The NWSL emerged after two previous U.S. women’s professional soccer leagues failed financially. Founded in 2013, it emphasized stability, cost controls, a single-entity structure, and support from U.S. Soccer, which funded national-team player salaries and league operations. Despite featuring leading players and benefiting from the successful U.S. Women’s National Team, the league faced low salaries, uneven attendance, limited media coverage, and difficulty converting casual viewers into committed fans. Its highly engaged supporters relied heavily on social media and niche publications.

Before the pandemic, the NWSL secured broadcasting agreements with CBS and Twitch and introduced higher salary limits, allocation money, longer contracts, and year-round housing. However, many non-national-team players still struggled financially, while prominent players could earn more overseas.

Using a Paycheck Protection Program loan, the league paid non-allocated players and maintained health insurance. From June 27 to July 26, 2020, it staged the Challenge Cup in Utah under strict testing and movement protocols. Eight teams participated, with players permitted to opt out. The league conducted more than 2,000 COVID-19 tests without a positive result and spent $1.8 million on the tournament. CBS audiences set successive league records, culminating in more than 650,000 viewers for Houston’s championship victory over Chicago. Players also used the tournament to protest racial injustice and support Black Lives Matter.

The NWSL followed with an 18-game regional Fall Series after Baird secured television slots left open by postponed college football. Teams partnered with local businesses competing for community grants, although many players opted out or moved temporarily to European clubs.

By 2021, the league had increased television viewership, sponsorship revenue, social and traditional media attention, and its number of teams and investors. It also formally separated from U.S. Soccer. Its remaining priorities included deepening fan engagement, expanding sustainably, strengthening media exposure, defining a new relationship with U.S. Soccer, balancing player investment with cost controls, developing a new brand, supporting social justice, competing globally for talent, and negotiating its first collective bargaining agreement with the players’ association.

Improving farmers’ conditions requires broad, practical education that develops individual ability, citizenship, respect for labor, cooperation, and public spirit. Farmers’ organizations can provide economic and social benefits, while government assistance is most effective through such associations. The Department of Agriculture is coordinating with state and educational authorities, supporting specialized agricultural education, and cooperating with farmers against threats such as the boll weevil and cattle fever tick. Federal irrigation and forest-preservation policies have benefited the Rocky Mountains and Great Plains, and similar action is urged for the White Mountains and Southern Appalachians. Congress is also asked to fund preliminary work for a memorial amphitheater at Arlington honoring military dead. Finally, national authority over marriage and divorce is advocated because differing state laws cause abuses, threaten home life, and prevent effective action against polygamy.

AMC proposes doubling authorized shares to 1.1 billion, raising dilution risk. Despite refinancing, net debt exceeds $3 billion amid weak Q3 box office revenue, ongoing losses, negative equity, and cash burn. These factors contribute to AMC’s valuation discount relative to CNK. The author holds no related positions and provides general information, not investment advice.

A study of 19 mothers and their babies found that mothers’ brains released more dopamine when they watched videos of their own infants. Higher dopamine release was associated with greater sensitivity to infants’ needs and more responsive caregiving, while less responsive mothers released less dopamine.
