Researchers suggest this mechanism may motivate maternal care and could continue as children grow or operate in other close relationships. Responsive caregiving may support infants’ brain development and later well-being. However, the study was small, cannot establish whether stronger bonding responses are innate or developed, and did not determine whether fathers or other caregivers experience similar dopamine effects.

Researchers used somatic cell nuclear transfer to place nuclei from human skin fibroblasts into emptied donor eggs. After fertilization failed to trigger chromosome reduction, the chemical roscovitine induced the cells to expel chromosomes and form early embryos.

However, chromosome separation was random and abnormal. None of the embryos had the correct 46 chromosomes or developed beyond about six days, making them nonviable. The researchers view the work as proof that halving the human genome is possible, but the method remains inefficient, risky and dependent on donor eggs. Clinical testing is estimated to be at least a decade away and may face U.S. restrictions on modifying human embryos. The technology could eventually help some infertile people and same-sex male couples have genetically related children.

The passage highlights Robert Stuart’s critique of the BBC Panorama documentary “Saving Syria’s Children,” which reported that an incendiary bomb struck a Syrian school in August 2013. It argues that inconsistencies in the footage and reporting raise doubts about the event’s portrayal. These include medical professionals questioning the visible injuries, conflicting estimates of 25 to 50 victims treated at Atareb hospital, and accounts placing the attack at times up to six hours apart. It also questions why BBC journalists present could not establish a precise timeline.

The passage further emphasizes the military, political, and humanitarian connections of doctors Saleyah Ahsan and Rola Hallam, suggesting possible links to Western-backed efforts against Syrian President Assad. It compares the reported injuries with simulated medical injuries and alleges that the BBC footage may have been staged. The author concludes that possible fabrication should prompt broader scrutiny of media narratives used to support Western military intervention, surveillance, and restrictions on freedom.

The July 31 IEP news digest covers California’s energy crisis. Reports criticize Gov. Gray Davis’ $43 billion in long-term power contracts, examine an SEC inquiry into possible insider trading by state energy advisers, and disclose spokesman Steve Maviglio’s Calpine stock purchase. Five consultants were fired over potential conflicts, while communications advisers Chris Lehane and Mark Fabiani agreed to forgo payment. Other articles address efforts to rescue Southern California Edison, proposals for public power in San Francisco, and federal limits reducing California’s potential electricity refunds to under $4 billion. Additional reports discuss Baltimore Gas and Electric’s proposed restructuring and the delayed launch of Texas’ electricity deregulation pilot program.

Trauma can impair postsecondary students’ attendance, academic performance, self-efficacy, cognition, relationships, and well-being. Healthcare and occupational therapy (OT) students may also encounter secondary traumatic stress and vicarious trauma through education and clinical activities. Studies indicate that trauma is common among OT students, affects daily routines and learning, and may go undisclosed because of stigma.

The paper reviewed peer-reviewed and foundational literature on trauma-informed care (TIC) in health professions education (HPE) and OT programs. SAMHSA’s TIC framework emphasizes safety; trust and transparency; peer support; collaboration; empowerment, voice, and choice; and respect for cultural, historical, and gender-related factors. Implementation requires institutional leadership, training, inclusive policies, safe environments, survivor and student involvement, appropriate referrals, and ongoing evaluation.

Recommended educational practices include faculty development, predictable and flexible instruction, clear communication, advance notice of potentially triggering content, student check-ins, equal participation opportunities, self-care instruction, peer support, culturally responsive curricula, universal design, simulation-based training, and reflective practice. TIC seeks to remove barriers to learning without eliminating challenging material.

Evidence from the simulation-based PATH model showed improved student knowledge, self-efficacy, and understanding of adverse childhood experiences and TIC. Health and wellness coaching may also support coping, resilience, and behavior change. However, TIC content remains limited in OT curricula despite its alignment with accreditation standards.

The paper concludes that integrating TIC throughout classroom, clinical, and continuing education may create safer and more supportive learning environments, improve student engagement and academic success, and potentially increase retention, graduation, and degree attainment.

Newark police sought public help locating nine suspects in seven unsolved shootings and robberies dating to June 2016. Cases include three armed men suspected of robbing La Mina De Oro Grocery and separate robberies and shootings. Officials released suspect photos and asked for confidential tips through phone lines, the department website or smartphone app, with possible rewards.

Asus launched the Zenfone 5Z in India, exclusively on Flipkart from July 15. Three variants cost Rs. 29,999 to Rs. 36,999. It features a 6.2-inch notched display, Snapdragon 845, up to 8GB RAM and 256GB storage, Android Oreo, dual rear cameras, and a 3300mAh battery. Launch offers include ICICI discounts, no-cost EMI, mobile protection, and Jio benefits.

House appropriators proposed dividing $661.3 billion in FY2002 discretionary spending largely in line with President Bush’s requests, while increasing Labor-HHS, VA-HUD, and Energy and Water funding. House and Senate appropriators indicated they would likely maintain Bush’s nearly $7 billion FY2001 supplemental request despite calls for more defense spending; administration allies warned a larger bill could face a veto.

House Republican leaders said the Democratic takeover of the Senate was unlikely to improve House bipartisanship and could free Republicans to advance their agenda. Priorities before the August recess include energy, prescription drugs, campaign finance, tax cuts, patients’ rights, and trade authority. Democrats continued to criticize Republicans for insufficient consultation.

Rep. Steve Largent announced he would resign November 29 to focus on running for Oklahoma governor and requested an early special election. Republicans described his district as strongly Republican, though Democrats said it could be competitive.

Rep. Asa Hutchinson’s expected departure to lead the Drug Enforcement Administration left business groups seeking a new House sponsor for legislation limiting punitive damages against small businesses and product sellers. Senate Democratic control was expected to make broader liability reforms more difficult.

Labor Secretary Elaine Chao scheduled three July forums on ergonomics and planned to develop a policy by September. Republicans praised the approach, while Democrats urged adoption of a new workplace rule.

FDA officials warned that roughly two million mailed parcels containing regulated products enter the United States annually, overwhelming inspection capacity. They said imported drugs may be counterfeit, improperly stored, unsafe, or unapproved. Lawmakers acknowledged both the safety risks and the high domestic prices prompting consumers to purchase foreign drugs.

The House Energy and Commerce Committee remained open to including generic-drug patent reforms in Medicare prescription-drug legislation. Potential changes concern patent-related 30-month delays and the first generic producer’s 180-day exclusivity period, though lawmakers and brand-name manufacturers expressed reservations.

European Union officials said Bush’s steel-import investigation and rejection of the Kyoto Protocol could complicate the upcoming EU-U.S. summit. They also voiced concern about U.S. unilateralism and said announcing a new trade round at the summit would be premature.

Senate Republicans drafted proposed assurances for prompt consideration of Bush nominees as part of negotiations with Democrats over a new organizing resolution. Both sides reported progress and hoped for Senate action Tuesday.

Bush planned to nominate Jo Anne Barnhart to a six-year term as Social Security commissioner. Republican members of the Census Monitoring Board defended the 2000 census and questioned statistical sampling. A House aviation hearing was scheduled to assess airline customer-service improvements. House Republicans also introduced legislation requiring public and congressional review of national monuments larger than 50,000 acres.

Gas colic occurs when normal gas from hindgut fermentation fails to pass through the large colon. Though considered the least serious colic form, it can cause intense pain and complications such as colon displacement or twisting. Contributing factors include insufficient forage, confinement, stress, ulcers, inflammation, inadequate exercise, dehydration, and abrupt feed or forage changes.

Continuous forage access supports digestion and natural grazing behavior. Restriction can cause stress, acid accumulation, rapid eating, poor chewing, ulcers, excessive fermentation, and reduced hindgut motility. Stall confinement similarly limits movement and circulation, preventing gas from being expelled. Pasture turnout or outdoor exercise with hay and water can improve motility and reduce stress.

New hay should be introduced gradually over about a week, while new fortified feeds may require two to three weeks. Concentrated meals should follow hay consumption. Unfamiliar weekly bran mashes may trigger colic; if used, they should be introduced gradually and fed consistently. Suggested supplements include B vitamins, yeast, and colostrum. The passage also recommends reducing inflammatory ingredients such as sugar and soy products.

Slow feeders kept continuously filled may simulate grazing and help horses regulate intake. The primary prevention strategy is maximizing outdoor movement and maintaining forage availability 24 hours a day.

Tesla reported that underwriters exercised their option to purchase an additional $127.5 million of 2.375% Convertible Senior Notes due March 15, 2022. Tesla issued the notes on March 30, 2017. Related hedge transactions cost approximately $26.6 million and were intended to reduce potential dilution or excess conversion payments. Tesla also issued warrants allowing counterparties to acquire up to approximately 0.8 million common shares at $655 per share, receiving approximately $6.9 million in proceeds. The warrants may be dilutive if Tesla’s share price exceeds the strike price unless cash-settled.

Malaria rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) commonly detect PfHRP2 and PfHRP3 proteins, but increasing pfhrp2/3 gene deletions can cause false-negative results and threaten malaria control. Deletions have been reported in 40 of 47 surveyed countries, with false-negative rates reaching 80% in some settings. Alternative pLDH-based tests have lower sensitivity or limited availability, particularly where tests must distinguish P. falciparum from P. vivax.

This study updated an individual-based malaria transmission model to assess global selection and spread of pfhrp2 deletions. It incorporated malaria prevalence, treatment-seeking, diagnostic practices, adherence to RDT results, RDT types, PfHRP3 cross-reactivity, parasite fitness costs, and the association between pfhrp2 and pfhrp3 deletions. Two measures were developed: the Innate Risk Score, estimating how quickly clinically relevant false-negative cases rise from 1% to the WHO threshold of 5% under HRP2-based testing, and the Prospective Risk Score, modelling future spread from current deletion estimates and between neighbouring regions.

Globally, an estimated 63.5% of pfhrp2-deleted samples also had pfhrp3 deletions; in Africa, the estimate was 61.2%, indicating strong positive linkage. Model fitting estimated pfhrp2-deleted parasites had 96.4% of wild-type fitness and that PfHRP3 cross-reactivity produced positive HRP2-based RDT results in 29.0% of infections containing only pfhrp2-deleted parasites.

Malaria prevalence was the strongest determinant of deletion selection. Lower-prevalence settings generally favoured faster selection, although very low transmission increased stochastic uncertainty and the possibility of deletion loss. Under the Innate Risk scenario, 73 of 106 modelled countries had at least one first-level administrative region predicted to exceed the 5% threshold within 20 years. High-prevalence regions in Central and West Africa generally had lower risk, often requiring more than 40 years.

Under prospective modelling based on current surveillance, 29 of 49 African countries had at least one region predicted to reach or already exceed 5% within 20 years. Deletions were projected to spread southward from the Horn of Africa through East Africa and increase in parts of West Africa, particularly Senegal and Mali. Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Senegal, Zambia, and Kenya were among countries consistently identified as high risk. Prospective estimates classified fewer regions as high risk because they accounted for non-HRP2 RDT use and current deletion prevalence.

Key limitations included sparse and inconsistent surveillance, uncertainty in malaria prevalence and fitness estimates, simplified modelling of geographic spread, assumptions of constant future transmission and treatment, and limited representation of non-RDT-driven deletion emergence. The resulting maps and interactive tool are intended to guide surveillance, decisions about alternative RDT deployment, and further research, particularly in high-risk regions such as Senegal, Zambia, and Kenya.

Higher wind supply, easing demand and improved French nuclear availability pushed European prompt power prices lower, while forwards followed declining coal. German and French Wednesday baseload prices fell 16% and 20%, respectively. Traders remained bearish as demand was expected to drop sharply next week.

The lecture models protein backbones as fixed-angle linkages: edge lengths and bond angles remain fixed, while subchains may rotate around edges. This abstraction ignores amino acids, energy, and biological actuators to study mechanically possible folding. Four problems are considered: span, flattening, flat-state connectivity, and locked chains.

Span is the distance between an open chain’s endpoints. Finding minimum or maximum span among flat configurations is NP-hard through reductions from partition. For unrestricted three-dimensional fixed-angle chains, both optimization problems remain open. Maximum span can be found in linear time for orthogonal chains, but the general case is unresolved.

Flattening asks whether a non-self-intersecting fixed-angle chain has any planar configuration. This is NP-hard, though the proof requires extreme edge-length ratios. Cases with equal or polynomially bounded edge lengths remain open.

Flat-state connectivity asks whether every pair of planar states can be joined by a collision-free three-dimensional motion. It is unknown whether all open fixed-angle chains or trees are flat-state connected. Positive results cover orthogonal and obtuse chains, equal acute angles, and certain other restricted cases. Orthogonal chains can be lifted edge by edge into a canonical staircase, allowing any two flat states to connect through that form. Partially rigid trees provide disconnected examples, with impossibility established through linked-loop topology.

Fixed-angle chains can also be locked. Equilateral or equiangular restrictions alone do not prevent locking, and examples satisfying both appear possible. The important unresolved case combines equal lengths, equal obtuse angles, and fixed angles, approximating protein backbones. More generally, narrow ranges of lengths and angles also remain open.

The lecture then incorporates protein production by a ribosome. A chain is modeled as emerging link by link from the apex of a cone and cannot re-enter the cone or self-intersect outside it. Such “producible” chains gain useful structure despite the added obstacle. For chains whose turn angles are bounded by an angle alpha, a canonical, helix-like configuration is constructed inside a cone of half-angle alpha/2.

By reversing the production motion and canonicalizing each edge as it returns into the cone, every producible configuration can reach this canonical state. Consequently, all producible configurations lie in one connected component. Flat states can also be produced, so producible chains are flat-state connected and can be transformed algorithmically between flat and canonical configurations without self-intersection. This provides a possible mechanical framework for understanding protein folding, though the physical forces implementing such folding remain unknown.

American Girl is releasing its first male doll, Logan Everett, a drummer in a new contemporary series, following longstanding customer requests for greater diversity. The company is also returning colonial-era Felicity Merriman and introducing filmmaker Z Yang and World War II-era Hawaiian character Nanea later in 2017.

At Manchester Students’ Union’s Earth Week panel, campaigners linked climate change, displacement, and migration justice. Asad Rehman said developing countries suffer disproportionately despite richer countries producing most emissions, arguing climate refugees deserve legal protection rather than vilification. Martin Empson urged participation through protests, petitions, contacting MPs, or donations, and called for environmental and migration movements to collaborate in creating a hopeful agenda.

The Michigan Supreme Court held that sexual delinquency is an alternate sentencing provision, not merely a penalty enhancement, and may be determined only after conviction of the principal offense. Because it permits a sentence of one day to life and requires broad, discretionary fact-finding, the delinquency charge must, unless waived, be heard by a separate jury empaneled immediately after conviction. The defendant receives 20 peremptory challenges for that jury, while challenges for the principal-offense jury depend only on that offense’s potential sentence.

A sexual-delinquency charge must be included in the original indictment or added before trial; filing it after trial begins is waived. The jury hearing the principal offense must not learn of the delinquency charge, or mistrial or reversal may result.

Helzer’s gross-indecency convictions were affirmed because that trial was proper. His sexual-delinquency determination was invalid because the same jury decided both matters and he was denied 20 challenges. The case was remanded for a new delinquency hearing before a separate jury if the prosecutor proceeds; otherwise, or upon acquittal, Helzer must be resentenced only for gross indecency. The Court deferred his constitutional claims. Chief Justice Kavanagh dissented, viewing the sexual-delinquency statute as unconstitutionally vague.

Canada’s Privacy Commissioner launched a formal investigation into Uber’s 2016 data breach affecting more than 57 million riders and drivers worldwide. Uber has not disclosed how many Canadians were affected and says there is no evidence of misuse. The breach was concealed for over a year after thieves received $100,000. Similar investigations and an Alberta class action are underway.

The American Cancer Society updated its guideline to recommend colorectal cancer screening for average-risk adults beginning at age 45, citing rising incidence among younger adults and modeling showing a favorable benefit-to-burden balance. The recommendation for ages 45–49 is qualified because direct evidence is limited, while screening from age 50 is strongly recommended.

Adults may choose stool-based tests or visual examinations based on preference and availability. Options include annual FIT or high-sensitivity guaiac testing, stool DNA testing every three years, colonoscopy every 10 years, and CT colonography or flexible sigmoidoscopy every five years. Positive non-colonoscopy results require timely colonoscopy. Screening should continue through age 75 for healthy adults with life expectancy over 10 years, be individualized for ages 76–85, and be discouraged after 85.

Colorectal cancer incidence among people under 50 has increased 51% since 1994, with recent increases in mortality. Updated modeling incorporating these trends found that several strategies beginning at 45 produced more life-years gained than starting at 50.

President-elect Donald Trump criticized CNN’s *Unprecedented: The Election That Changed Everything*, calling its cover image the worst photo of himself. His tweet prompted users to post awkward Trump photos and accuse him of vanity or misplaced priorities. Other recent Twitter activity attracting attention included his brief following of “Emergency Kittens,” comments about anticipating his electoral victory, and a retweeted Ivanka Trump photo montage celebrating 2016.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture introduces GDDR6 memory at 14 Gbps, larger and faster L2 caches, improved compression, and approximately 50% greater effective bandwidth than Pascal. Its display and video engines support DisplayPort 1.4a, dual 8K displays at 60 Hz, HDR tone mapping, HEVC 8K encoding, enhanced decoding, and higher-quality streaming. USB-C and VirtualLink consolidate VR display, data, and power into one connector, while second-generation NVLink increases two-GPU SLI bandwidth.

Turing enables hybrid rendering by combining rasterization with real-time ray tracing. Dedicated RT Cores accelerate bounding-volume-hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection tests, producing over 10 Giga Rays per second and roughly ten times Pascal’s software ray-tracing performance. Denoising and selective ray tracing reduce ray requirements while improving reflections, shadows, ambient occlusion, and other lighting effects.

The NGX software stack uses Turing Tensor Cores for AI-enhanced graphics. Its features include DLSS, which provides image quality similar to temporal anti-aliasing with less shading work; DLSS 2X for quality approaching 64-times supersampling; image inpainting; interpolated slow-motion video; and real-time AI super-resolution.

Additional graphics capabilities include Mesh Shading, which reduces CPU draw-call bottlenecks and supports dynamic level of detail; Variable Rate Shading, which adjusts shading rates by region or primitive for content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering; Texture Space Shading, which decouples visibility and appearance sampling and reuses shading results; and Multi-View Rendering, which renders up to four hardware-supported views per pass. Turing also expands DirectX 12 resource binding and heap support.

The TU104 GPU contains up to 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and one second-generation NVLink connection. Tesla T4 uses a TU104 configuration with 2,560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores. TU106, used in the GeForce RTX 2070, contains 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores but lacks NVLink and SLI.

NVIDIA defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based hybrid-rendering metric combining weighted Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 throughput. For the RTX 2080 Ti, the stated calculation yields 78 RTX-OPS. NVIDIA also states that product information may change, materials are provided “as is,” suitability testing is the customer’s responsibility, and liability is limited by its sales terms.

Terry Rozier scored a career-high 31 points with seven rebounds in his second NBA start, leading the injury-depleted Boston Celtics to a 119-110 win over the Atlanta Hawks. Jayson Tatum added a career-high 27 points, while Jaylen Brown scored 19 and Al Horford had 17. Boston, missing Kyrie Irving and three other players, overcame a two-point halftime deficit by outscoring Atlanta 41-20 in the third quarter. Taurean Prince led the Hawks with a career-high 31 points, and Dennis Schroder added 25. Boston earned its fourth win in five games, while Atlanta lost for the fifth time in six.

An international rescue team found 12 boys and their soccer coach alive after nine days trapped by floodwater 1.2 miles inside Thailand’s Tham Luang Nang Non cave. A cave rescue expert describes the operation as exceptionally difficult because monsoon rains may keep the cave flooded for months. Although the cave’s warm temperature reduced hypothermia risk, the group had gone nine days without food and needed gradual feeding and time to regain strength.

Flooded-cave rescues generally favor waiting for water to subside while monitoring conditions, pumping or diverting water, seeking other entrances, and using divers to deliver supplies. In Thailand, waiting may take weeks or months. The main alternatives are teaching the weakened group to dive through dark, narrow, flooded passages; drilling a new entrance; or finding another natural entrance. Diving is extremely strenuous and dangerous for novices, while drilling requires precise mapping and heavy equipment, and searches for another entrance had been unsuccessful. If the group’s location remains safe and supplies can reach them, they could stay until conditions improve; otherwise, diving them out may be the only option.

Quantum spin-relaxation simulations support applications in quantum computing, spintronics, spectroscopy, and quantum biophysics, including radical-pair mechanisms in organic semiconductors, molecular qubits, and avian magnetoreception. Radical-pair modelling is difficult because room-temperature nuclear spins require ensemble averaging, Hilbert and Liouville spaces grow exponentially with nuclear-spin number, and relaxation requires stable long-time propagation. Classical nuclear-spin approximations can work at high fields or with many nuclei, but full quantum treatments are needed for quantitative accuracy and non-Markovian hyperfine relaxation.

The work introduces tensor-network methods to spin chemistry, explains radical-pair challenges, and examines avian magnetoreception. Radical-pair Hamiltonians include Zeeman, hyperfine, exchange, dipolar, and Haberkorn relaxation terms. Electronic-state populations may be calculated through density-matrix traces or Monte Carlo sampling of initial spin configurations.

Three tensor-network approaches are introduced. Stochastic matrix product states represent wavefunctions compactly, reducing storage from exponential scaling to \(O(Ndm^2)\), and use spin-coherent-state sampling. Matrix product density operators provide deterministic mixed-state calculations without extensive stochastic sampling. Their vectorised form maps density operators into matrix-product-state-like structures, reducing storage from \(O(d^{2N})\) to \(O(Nd^2\chi^2)\). A locally purified matrix-product-state representation is also considered. Time-dependent variational-principle methods permit real-time evolution with long-range interactions, unlike time-evolving block decimation, which is largely limited to nearest-neighbour Hamiltonians.

The Bank of Japan is unlikely to quickly exit ultra-loose monetary policy despite strong growth, as low inflation and fears that normalization could trigger a sharp yen appreciation threaten the export-reliant recovery. Although consumption, employment and economic expansion have improved, policymakers reportedly want inflation to exceed 1 percent before considering a rate increase.

Any rise in yield targets next year would likely be modest and isolated rather than the start of sustained tightening. Political pressure to prevent yen gains, uncertainty over Governor Haruhiko Kuroda’s successor, and concerns about stock prices also constrain policy. However, continued easing leaves the BOJ with limited tools against a future recession and hurts financial institutions. The bank has slowed government bond purchases, while analysts suggest gradually raising yield targets and reducing asset purchases to rebuild policy capacity.

The study describes a minimally invasive blood test for detecting glial malignancies in patients with intracranial space-occupying lesions. Circulating glial cells were enriched from 5–7.5 mL blood samples and identified by GFAP and OLIG2 expression using multiplexed immunocytochemistry; PanCK helped distinguish epithelial cancers with brain metastases.

Analytical validation showed cell stability for up to 48 hours, a detection limit of 1 cell per 5 mL, and marker sensitivities of 92.5–95.0% with 100% specificity. Blinded case-control and prospective studies generally reported 100% sensitivity and specificity, although one prospective cohort yielded 92.9% sensitivity and 100% specificity. EGFR amplification in circulating cells showed complete concordance with matched tissue findings in 44 cases.

The test differentiated glial malignancies from benign brain tumors, non-glial CNS malignancies, healthy samples, and epithelial cancers with brain metastases. It does not identify tumor grade or subtype and does not detect some rare malignancies, including CNS lymphoma and gliosarcoma. The study was funded entirely by Datar Cancer Genetics Private Limited, whose founder and several employees were authors.

U.S. stock futures edged higher ahead of the Federal Reserve’s expected rate increase and Janet Yellen’s economic commentary. Tuesday’s options trading was average, with the CBOE equity put/call ratio falling to 0.64. Apple shares gained nearly 1% after CEO Tim Cook confirmed its focus on autonomous systems; more than 1.1 million options traded, 60% calls. Tesla options rose on favorable reports, while Micron rebounded following bullish Macquarie Research commentary.

Patrick Kane credits his father and several coaches for supporting his development. He enjoys both scoring and assisting, and will play wing or center as needed. He chose the OHL over college and hopes to help Buffalo win a Stanley Cup, though any team drafting him would be special.

The Arizona Supreme Court held that A.R.S. § 13-4033(B) prohibits a defendant from directly appealing a contested post-judgment restitution order entered under a plea agreement that requires restitution up to a capped amount. Frank Hoffman had agreed to pay up to $53,653.45 and was later ordered to pay $40,933.45. Because the order was a direct consequence of his plea agreement and part of his sentence, appellate review was available only through Rule 32 post-conviction relief proceedings. The Court affirmed dismissal of Hoffman’s direct appeal.

Carleton University is creating a five-year renewable chair in conjuring arts to research and teach the history of magic, perception, and deception. Supported by a $2 million Slaight Family Foundation grant matched by Carleton, the program will fund salary, graduate hiring, travel, and a global digital magic archive. About 80 people have applied. The research aims to explain why people deceive and are deceived, including through fake news and political persuasion. A University of London experiment found that misleading gestures made participants less likely to identify a magic trick’s simple solution, suggesting people can become attached to initial explanations and struggle to reconsider assumptions. Magician consultant Michael Close said people often invent or rationalize explanations when they lack knowledge, partly because of laziness.

Adam Henrique and Travis Zajac described the Kings as a big, fast, physical and deep team with puck-moving defensemen, strong goaltending and contributions from all four lines. They said their own team began nervously and tentatively, turning over pucks, failing to forecheck effectively and losing battles, but improved as the game progressed and remained competitive. They expect better execution next game, particularly by getting pucks behind the defense, sustaining cycles, creating traffic and taking more shots. They also noted that regaining a key leader increased their depth and ability to roll four lines.

Apple filed a Form 8-K reporting that it issued a July 31, 2018 press release and data sheet covering financial results for its third fiscal quarter ended June 30, 2018. The documents are attached as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. CFO Luca Maestri signed the report.

Apple reported fiscal first-quarter 2022 net sales of $123.9 billion, up 11% year over year, and net income of $34.6 billion, compared with $28.8 billion. Diluted earnings per share rose to $2.10 from $1.68. Gross margin increased to $54.2 billion, or 43.8% of sales, while operating income reached $41.5 billion.

iPhone sales increased 9% to $71.6 billion, Mac sales rose 25% to $10.9 billion, Services grew 24% to $19.5 billion, and Wearables, Home and Accessories increased 13% to $14.7 billion. iPad sales declined 14% to $7.2 billion. Sales grew in the Americas, Europe, Greater China and Rest of Asia Pacific, but declined 14% in Japan.

Apple generated $47.0 billion in operating cash flow. At December 25, 2021, it held $37.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $165.5 billion in marketable securities. Total assets were $381.2 billion, liabilities were $309.3 billion, and shareholders’ equity was $71.9 billion. Term debt totaled $117.8 billion.

During the quarter, Apple repurchased 124 million shares for $20.4 billion and paid $3.7 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents. It had $40.5 billion remaining under its share-repurchase authorization and manufacturing purchase obligations of $47.6 billion.

COVID-19 continued to affect staffing, retail operations, suppliers and logistics, causing supply shortages. Apple reported no material changes to market risk, internal controls, critical accounting estimates or risk factors. In the Epic Games case, Apple prevailed on nine of ten claims and its breach-of-contract claims; both parties appealed, and Apple received a stay pending appeal.

U.S. stocks rallied after Donald Trump’s election on expectations of tax cuts, infrastructure spending and deregulation, but gains slowed after his inauguration amid legislative difficulties.

- Hospital stocks fell 7.1% before inauguration, then gained 4.1%, as Republican efforts to repeal Obamacare stalled.
- Infrastructure stocks rose 13%, then 2.4%, as Trump’s proposed $1 trillion program had not materialized.
- Bank stocks gained 20.8%, then 3.1%, initially driven by deregulation and higher-rate expectations, before concerns emerged over loan growth and Trump’s ability to enact reforms.
- Small-cap stocks rose 12.6%, then 5.3%, supported by anticipated corporate tax cuts.

Investors increasingly questioned Trump’s ability to advance his domestic agenda after the failed initial healthcare bill and amid his involvement in international issues.

Major topics include Enron’s financial deterioration and proposed Dynegy acquisition, California electricity policy, new federal price controls, utility acquisitions, planned power plants, environmental and nuclear issues, and forecasts indicating adequate winter electricity supplies in the U.S. Midwest and Plains.

Former U.S. Sen. Mark Begich’s entry into Alaska’s gubernatorial race has raised concerns that he and independent Gov. Bill Walker could split Democratic and independent voters, benefiting the Republican nominee. Begich insists he can win, while Democratic leaders reject the spoiler argument. The Sixth Circuit affirmed Dr. Howard Ellzey’s convictions for conspiracy and eleven counts of illegally distributing controlled substances. Ellzey routinely issued amphetamine prescriptions to “diet patients” after minimal or no examination, operating two offices with separate records that allowed patients to obtain multiple prescriptions. A DEA survey found that he wrote 29,000 of 39,000 Schedule II prescriptions examined, nearly all for amphetamine-type drugs. The court found substantial evidence supporting the convictions and held that the prescriptions were relevant to intent and willfulness. It rejected arguments that the indictment improperly used “distributing” rather than “dispensing,” concluding that Ellzey acted outside accepted medical practice on a large scale. The court also found no error in evidentiary rulings, jury instructions, or voir dire.

Mulgrave beat Sherburn by 28 runs in Division One after scoring 165-5 and dismissing Sherburn for 137. The author describes living with panic disorder, which affects two to three percent of Americans, and managing it through professional guidance, therapy, and medication. Unlike persistent anxiety, a panic attack is a sudden burst of intense fear, usually lasting under 30 minutes; attacks associated with panic disorder may have no apparent trigger.

Symptoms can include a pounding heart, sweating, trembling, breathing difficulties, chest discomfort, nausea, dizziness, numbness, feelings of unreality, and fears of losing control or dying. A physical exam is important to rule out other conditions.

Experts recommend carrying written reminders that panic attacks are not life-threatening and have been survived before, along with realistic responses to catastrophic thoughts. Other strategies include visualizing panic as a wave that rises and passes, using smartphone games or relaxing audio as distractions, and practicing slow, deep breathing daily so it can be used effectively during an attack.

Eagles receiver A.J. Brown expressed frustration with limited targets and production, saying he wants the ball during offensive struggles and high-pressure moments. Brown has surpassed 30 receiving yards once, while DeVonta Smith has not exceeded 60 yards in a game. Despite Philadelphia’s 4-0 record, the passage argues offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo must involve both receivers more.

A UK laboratory study found that bumblebee queens exposed to field-realistic traces of the neonicotinoid thiamethoxam were 26 percent less likely to lay eggs, potentially threatening colony survival and wild populations. Researchers cautioned that the pesticide’s impact in nature remains uncertain relative to other threats, including poor nutrition and parasites. The findings may support tighter restrictions as the European Union considers making its temporary moratorium permanent. Pesticide companies and some farmers oppose restrictions, citing reduced canola yields and increased use of other insecticides.

Using the 2019 National Survey of Early Care and Education, researchers analyzed recent child care and early education searches by 1,190 households with a child under six, not yet in kindergarten, that considered multiple providers. Latent class analysis classified searches using up to two reported sources: friends and family, known providers, social media, internet tools, and Child Care Resource & Referral agencies or other local organizations.

Five search types emerged: CCR&R or friends/family; internet or social media; known providers or friends/family; social media or friends/family; and friends/family or internet. About half of families reported one source and half reported two. Friends and family were the most common source, followed by internet searches.

Search types differed significantly in whether families sought information about types of care, but not six other information categories. Searches involving CCR&Rs or known providers were more likely than other types to concern children with conditions affecting care provision. Search types also varied geographically: known-provider searches were more prevalent in the West, while friends/family-or-internet searches were more prevalent in the Northeast. No relationships were found with other examined family and child characteristics.

The findings are exploratory and correlational and cannot explain why differences occurred. Limitations include recording only the first two sources, excluding 79% of the broader household sample because they lacked a recent qualifying search, and an analytic sample that was higher-income, more often English-speaking, and more likely to include two working parents than the overall population.

The lecture surveys web security vulnerabilities and defenses. Shellshock exploited attacker-controlled HTTP headers converted into Bash environment variables, allowing commands to execute because of a parser flaw. Cross-site scripting similarly arises when applications embed untrusted input into HTML, enabling attacker-supplied code to run under a victim site’s authority.

XSS defenses include browser filters, HTTP-only cookies, separating untrusted content onto distinct domains, server-side sanitization, restricted markup languages, Content Security Policy, and disabling content-type sniffing. These measures are partial because HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and browser behavior are complex and inconsistently parsed. Rigorous encoding and framework-provided interfaces also help prevent SQL injection and malicious file-path traversal.

Cookies commonly store session identifiers and require careful domain isolation. Alternatives include authenticating each request with message authentication codes, storing authentication data in origin-restricted DOM storage, and using client certificates. These approaches introduce challenges involving key storage, replay attacks, revocation, implementation, and usability.

Other vulnerabilities result from inconsistent URL parsing and interactions among file formats. The GIFAR attack combined valid GIF and JAR data, allowing uploaded images to contain executable Java code that could run through an XSS vulnerability.

The lecture also describes covert-channel attacks that infer browsing history through visited-link colors, cache timing, DNS timing, or rendering behavior. Browser defenses can hide link state, but preventing all such timing and parsing attacks remains difficult.

A Spring Valley woman became San Diego County’s first confirmed West Nile virus case this year. California has reported 231 illnesses and 12 deaths. County officials advised residents to use repellent, wear protective clothing, and eliminate standing water. The mosquito-borne virus often causes no symptoms but can rarely be fatal.

Swarthmore students face intense pressure to excel academically and socially, but mistakes are a normal part of college and can provide valuable lessons. Students should laugh at minor failures, recognize that setbacks are rarely life-changing, and appreciate the campus’s unusual, intense environment. They should also forgive others, seek clarification when statements seem offensive, and assume good intent because people often misspeak. Laughter cannot solve most problems, but it can ease discomfort and help students cope.

NVIDIA’s A100 GPU uses 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1555 GB/s bandwidth, SECDED ECC protection, and a 40 MB L2 cache with 2.3 times V100’s L2 bandwidth. Cache residency controls and Compute Data Compression improve data reuse, effective bandwidth, and capacity.

A100 has 108 streaming multiprocessors and third-generation Tensor Cores supporting larger operations, mixed precision, and structured sparsity. Improvements include wider thread data sharing, fewer instructions and register accesses, asynchronous global-to-shared-memory copies, asynchronous barriers, and 164 KB shared memory per SM. CUDA 11 supports these features alongside accelerated task graphs, cooperative groups, and L2 persistence controls.

Multi-Instance GPU technology partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory resources, predictable performance, fault isolation, and quality of service. GPU Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances, support MPS, VMs, containers, and migration, and improve utilization for multi-user and multi-tenant workloads.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4 supplies 31.5 GB/s per direction over x16 and supports SR-IOV. Additional features include improved fault handling, five NVDEC units, a five-core NVJPG decoder, an optical-flow accelerator, and faster FP16 and FP32 atomic operations.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs through NVSwitch, delivers up to 5 PFLOPS, supports up to 56 isolated MIG accelerators, and scales through InfiniBand, Magnum IO, Slurm, and Kubernetes. Its software stack includes CUDA 11, the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC containers, frameworks, inference tools, analytics libraries, and HPC software.

A100’s fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity balances workloads while reducing computation and memory traffic, with evaluations reporting virtually no accuracy loss across various neural networks.

A multicentre study used structural brain MRI and deep learning to distinguish healthy ageing from multiple sclerosis-specific brain damage. Researchers analysed 4,392 patients from 15 European centres and validated models in a longitudinal cohort of 252 patients with early multiple sclerosis.

The established brain-age model showed that patients’ brains appeared, on average, 7.81 years older than their chronological age. A disease-duration model predicted duration with a mean absolute error of 5.63 years and explained more variance than lesion or thalamic volumes. Its prediction error, termed the disease-duration gap, was largely independent of the brain-age gap. Both measures were associated with physical disability, but the disease-duration gap provided additional explanatory value. Annual increases in both gaps correlated with disability worsening, and disease-duration gap changes added information beyond brain-age changes. A multiple sclerosis-specific age model was accurate but remained correlated with conventional brain age and did not significantly improve prediction of disability severity or progression.

The findings support the disease-duration gap as a complementary MRI biomarker of multiple sclerosis-specific damage, severity, and progression. Limitations include uncertainty in clinical disease-onset dates, possible treatment-related confounding, prediction bias related to disease duration, and the need for broader longitudinal validation.

The lecture completes Chapter 11 with Hadamard-transform realizations of Reed-Muller codes. The binary Hadamard transform uses recursively defined, lower-triangular matrices that are self-inverse. Reed-Muller codes can be generated by allowing selected transform inputs to vary while fixing others to zero. Recursive graphical realizations use only binary variables and simple equality and zero-sum constraints. A reduced realization of the \((8,4,4)\) code has 12 simple constraints but contains cycles.

Cycle-free realizations can be obtained by combining constraints. For the \((8,4,4)\) code, this produces a two-section trellis with larger state and branch complexity. Thus, representations with cycles are simpler but yield approximate decoding, while cycle-free graphs are more complex but support exact decoding. Agglomerated Hadamard-transform realizations also provide cycle-free representations of general Reed-Muller codes that meet the cut-set bound.

The lecture briefly compares normal graphs with factor graphs, Markov graphs, and directed Bayesian networks. Chapter 11 introduced codes on graphs; Chapter 12 begins decoding them using the sum-product algorithm, followed by capacity-approaching codes in Chapter 13.

The sum-product algorithm performs a posteriori probability decoding exactly on cycle-free graphs and becomes iterative and approximate on graphs with cycles. On trellises it is the BCJR algorithm. APP decoding computes probability vectors for external and internal variables, minimizing bit-error probability, though bitwise decisions may not form a codeword. These soft probabilities are useful when larger codes combine smaller component codes.

APP probabilities can be expressed as sums of products of channel likelihoods, separating intrinsic information from the directly observed symbol and extrinsic information from other observations. On a cycle-free graph, removing any internal edge separates the graph into past and future portions. Their independent contributions, conditioned on the edge variable, can be multiplied to obtain its posterior probability. This past-future decomposition is the basis for the sum-product update rule.

The passage presents the Situation Calculus as a logical framework for modeling dynamic systems through actions, situations, fluents, precondition axioms, and successor state axioms. Reiter’s successor state axioms address the frame problem under a Markov assumption, while non-Markovian extensions allow action prerequisites and effects to depend on past situations. Such extensions are useful for domains including database transactions, planning, and smart contracts.

The paper applies a prior Situation Calculus account of obligations to formalize a taxonomy of obligation types using non-Markovian theories. It introduces sequential and temporal Situation Calculus, where actions occur at specified times and situations represent finite action histories. Markovian basic action theories include action preconditions, successor state axioms, unique-name axioms, initial-state descriptions, and foundational axioms. Non-Markovian theories instead permit bounded formulas referring to preceding situations.

A running example models an agent opening and closing a door through actions such as moving, pressing a button, locking, unlocking, and notifying a manager. Preconditions specify when actions are possible, while successor state axioms describe changes to the door’s state, the agent’s location, and manager notification.

Obligations are represented through a deontic accessibility fluent, \(O(s',s)\), meaning that situation \(s'\) is deontically accessible from \(s\). An obligation \(Oblg(\phi,s)\) holds when \(\phi\) is true in every situation deontically accessible from \(s\). This approach combines deontic modalities with time and supports actions that change an agent’s obligations.

Researchers combined fossil evidence with 17 horizontal gene transfers to constrain fungi’s evolutionary timeline. Their analysis dates the common ancestor of living fungi to roughly 1.4–0.9 billion years ago, hundreds of millions of years before land plants. Early fungi likely interacted with algae, broke down rock, recycled nutrients, and formed primitive soils, potentially preparing terrestrial environments for plants. The gene transfers provided “older than/younger than” relationships that helped compensate for fungi’s sparse fossil record and calibrate molecular-clock estimates.

Beijing ordered 15 property websites to remove false advertising, misleading price claims, feng shui, financing advice, and offers involving residence permits or school enrolment. The move follows higher down-payment requirements, shorter mortgage terms and a ban on third-home purchases, amid concerns over rising prices, household debt and bank risks.

The passage argues that U.S. strategic superiority compelled the Soviet Union to retreat during the Cuban Missile Crisis, but subsequent American policymakers underestimated Soviet ambitions as Moscow expanded its military strength and influence. It criticizes the Carter administration’s responses to Soviet forces in Cuba and Afghanistan as weak, inconsistent, and damaging to U.S. credibility. Drawing lessons from World War II, it contends that weakness invites aggression, while firmness backed by strong defenses preserves peace. The proposed alternative is a prudent restoration of conventional and strategic military strength, firm opposition to terrorism, renewed leadership and consultation within U.S. alliances, and an unwavering commitment to American principles and freedom.

United Airlines promoted uncrowded airport lounges and seatback entertainment as part of its premium strategy, indirectly criticizing Delta’s crowded Sky Clubs and American’s limited domestic seatback screens. United said screens are installed on more than 146,000 seats across 765 aircraft, representing 64% of its fleet and a $1.6 billion investment.

Delta has raised lounge prices, tightened access and introduced higher-end lounges to address crowding. American favors tablet holders and passenger devices on most domestic aircraft, citing customer preferences and savings on weight and fuel.

United’s third-quarter premium cabin revenue rose 6% year over year, compared with Delta’s 9%. United shares fell more than 7% after revenue missed expectations, though they remained up over 34% for the year.

China warned against using Hong Kong to threaten national sovereignty, central government authority, or mainland stability amid concerns over a small independence movement. Leader Leung Chun-ying will not seek re-election, while hardliner Regina Ip’s candidacy has raised further concerns about tighter Chinese control.

The Competition and Markets Authority warned that some care homes may be breaking consumer law through unclear pricing, pre-entry charges, fees after residents’ deaths, eviction threats and inadequate complaint processes. Self-funding residents were particularly affected. The CMA is pursuing a test case and considering recommending tighter legislation, while maintaining that sector-wide returns cover current operating costs.

Caring Health Center in Springfield marked National Health Center Week with discussions, an Elected Officials Day event and healthcare honors. The center serves more than 20,000 people and seeks greater awareness of community health services.

He highlighted economic growth, job creation, fiscal surpluses, reduced poverty and crime, expanded education and health coverage, environmental protection, and America’s global leadership. He urged the nation to maintain fiscal responsibility, continue leading internationally against shared threats and poverty, and strengthen unity by treating all people fairly regardless of background or identity. The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting up to 2 MHz and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge.

Maximum duty cycle is configured through DCL: supported devices provide 100% with DCL tied to VLDO, 75% when floating, or 50% with DCL tied to AVSS. Only TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP support the 50% setting and active OUTB/SRB signals; TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50%. External synchronization is most precise with a 50% clock duty cycle.

CS_ILIM senses primary-side current for PWM control and overcurrent protection. Outputs turn off when sensed peak current reaches COMP/2, including a 150-mV offset. At the nominal 1.05-V current-limit threshold, cycle-by-cycle limiting begins and CHICC charges. When CHICC reaches 0.6 V, switching stops and soft-start discharges; restart occurs after CHICC rises to 1 V and then discharges to 0.3 V. A minimum 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor is recommended.

The FAULT pin enables external protections. A voltage above 0.6 V for the specified 0.4–1.4-µs minimum pulse width stops switching and discharges soft-start. After FAULT falls below 0.5 V, restart follows a delay of approximately 15 switching cycles plus internal delay.

Slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle. The minimum recommended for full-range stability is half the inductor falling-current slope, while matching that slope is recommended. An RSC-to-AVSS resistor programs compensation. Type 2A or Type 2B loop compensation may be used; Type 2A adds a high-frequency attenuation capacitor.

Thermal shutdown stops switching at a typical junction temperature of 175°C and restarts below 160°C. The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require at least 0.1 µF of VIN bypass capacitance.

A TPS7H5001-SP synchronous push-pull design example uses 500-kHz switching, 5-V output, approximately 25-ns dead time, 50-ns leading-edge blanking, 7.5-ms soft-start, a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 0.47-µH output inductance, and approximately 2.3 mF output capacitance. It uses 170-V primary and 80-V synchronous-rectifier GaN FETs, begins current limiting near 35 A, and applies Type 2A compensation with a 10-kHz target crossover.

Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds with a single connection, minimizing high-current and high-dv/dt loops, isolating feedback and other sensitive traces from switching signals, placing bypass, filtering, sensing, and compensation components near the controller, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS with multiple vias.

Seven-year-old Joseph Nyberg created “Heart Cents” after his grandfather died from heart disease. He collected pennies and dollars around Savannah and Richmond Hill to support St. Joseph’s heart patients. Matching and anonymous donations increased his total to $672.14, helping cover transportation and co-pays. Joseph plans to continue fundraising in his grandfather’s honor.

Ohio education regulators are reviewing a former Electronic Classroom of Tomorrow employee’s allegation that the now-closed online charter school intentionally manipulated student attendance data to increase state funding. The whistleblower said officials adjusted results from ActivTrak software after initial data showed students completed only slightly more than half the hours needed to justify full enrollment payments.

The Ohio Department of Education had previously determined ECOT over-reported full-time-equivalent students and ordered it to repay $60 million for 2015-2016, followed by a $19 million penalty for 2016-2017. Officials also found duplicated learning hours in ActivTrak data. The whistleblower alerted the department in August 2017, but officials did not interview him until December. His claims were also included in a pending state financial audit.

ECOT representatives disputed or said they were unaware of the allegations. Democratic state officials and an ECOT critic called for criminal investigation, while Franklin County Prosecutor Ron O’Brien said he had received no referral.

Blockchain integration requires cross-functional expertise spanning management, finance, supply chains, IT security, law, procurement, and sales, alongside technical, social, methodological, and personal competencies. To assess blockchain education, researchers examined 533 U.S. universities with AACSB-accredited business schools in March 2024, identifying and categorizing 361 blockchain courses across 151 institutions.

Computer Science and Information Systems departments offered the most courses, though offerings also appeared in fields such as finance, law, engineering, biology, literature, and political science. Business represented the largest academic area with 216 courses, followed by Computer Science with 85 and Law with 31. Most courses were undergraduate-level. Public universities offered more courses overall, but private universities had a higher participation rate. Larger universities were generally more likely to offer blockchain courses.

Course content primarily covered blockchain fundamentals, digital assets and cryptocurrencies, and technical development. Fewer courses addressed business implications, law and compliance, supply chains and governance, or blockchain’s interplay with other technologies. Artificial intelligence and machine learning were the most frequently mentioned related technologies, followed by the Internet of Things and non-fungible tokens.

The study concludes that blockchain education is interdisciplinary and increasingly connected with emerging technologies. It recommends further research comparing course competencies with industry and job-level needs and repeating the study in five years to track changes.

In the year ending in May, home prices rose 8.3% in Los Angeles County, 8.2% in Riverside and San Bernardino counties, and 6.2% in Orange County, despite slower sales. National prices increased 7.1%, while California prices gained 8.9%. CoreLogic attributed rising prices to limited inventory, particularly entry-level homes, as homeowners retain low-rate mortgages. Buyer interest also exceeds homeowners’ plans to sell.

Valid writes require at least 32 SCLK cycles per data-transfer frame. Read protocols include legacy SPI-compatible modes with single or dual SDO-x and source-synchronous protocols. After power-up or asynchronous reset, SPI-00-S is the default. Other SPI modes are selected through SDI_MODE[1:0], with SDO_MODE[1:0] set to 00b for SPI reads. RVS remains low during SPI-compatible transfers. Short frames can read selected MSBs; long frames with SDO_CNTL_REG = 00h enable daisy-chain operation. Dual SDO mode is enabled by setting SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] to 11b, making the ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin SDO-1 and launching two data bits per SCLK edge. Timing specifications are otherwise the same for single and dual SDO modes.
Nobel Prizes honor discoveries but leave much science unseen; Katalin Karikó won in 2023.

Kesha publicly supported Taylor Swift during her legal battle with former DJ David Mueller, praising her strength and commitment to truth. Mueller’s lawsuit against Swift was dismissed, while Swift’s $1 assault-and-battery countersuit remained. Swift previously donated $250,000 to Kesha during her dispute with producer Dr. Luke. Kesha recently released her chart-topping album “Rainbow” after years of legal conflict.

The book aims to establish reusable patterns for designing reliable, agile, and scalable distributed systems. Although distributed applications span multiple machines, their atomic elements are often groups of containers colocated on one node.

Dividing single-node applications into containers creates boundaries for resources, team ownership, and responsibilities. Resource isolation lets critical user-facing services receive priority over background tasks and protects them during resource contention. Modular containers also support small, focused teams and enable reusable components, such as a Git synchronization tool shared across multiple web environments.

Separating concerns makes applications easier to understand, test, update, and deploy. Independent deployments reduce dependencies and rollout scope, improving reliability, rollback capability, agility, and flexibility. The described single-node patterns assume tightly dependent containers that can be reliably scheduled together and may share filesystems, networks, memory, and other resources. Kubernetes calls this grouping a pod, though the concept is more broadly applicable.

The invention describes a surgical robotic wrist with distal, intermediate, and basal segments. Two transverse, preferably perpendicular, rotational axes are positioned between proximal and distal roll joints. Torque sensors associated with the transverse joints detect forces applied in multiple directions to a surgical instrument or end effector; optional sensors measure torque about the roll axes. A processor distinguishes externally applied torque from motor-driven torque and may provide haptic force feedback to the surgeon.

The wrist may use a universal, spherical, or paired-revolute joint and may be located at the end of either a robot arm or a surgical instrument. Its arrangement provides hemispherical movement, avoids kinematic singularities and high-speed joint requirements, and allows instrument rotation with limited disruption to patient tissue. The broader robot arm uses alternating roll and pitch joints to achieve mobility while remaining relatively slim and lightweight. Torque sensing may use resistance-based, piezoelectric, or magnetostrictive gauges, with wired or wireless signal transmission. The design supports accurate positioning, close operation of multiple arms, flexible base placement, and surgical motion resembling that of a human wrist.

The disclosure describes noninvasive physiological monitoring systems that combine raw or minimally processed optical sensor data from multiple patient measurement sites to generate a single measurement. Sensors may be placed at cephalic and peripheral sites, such as the nose and finger, and may use multiple light emitters and photodetectors. A signal processor combines features from the sensor streams, including amplitude, phase, wavelength ratios, measurement-site information, and tissue information, to estimate parameters such as oxygen saturation, pulse rate, plethysmograph waveform, perfusion index, pleth variability index, methemoglobin, carboxyhemoglobin, total hemoglobin, and glucose. It may also calculate site-specific measurements and compare or average them.

Individual sensors may distribute multiple photodetectors in three-dimensional configurations conforming to patient anatomy. This arrangement provides varied light paths, information about sensor placement, and measurements across the covered tissue area. Sensors may use clips, housings, or adhesive tape and can be attached to sites including the nose, ear, forehead, fingers, limbs, hands, feet, or face.

Combining data from multiple sites and detectors can improve measurement robustness, reduce site-specific noise or errors, enable cross-checking, and provide information unavailable from a single site. The described embodiments, configurations, processing methods, and component combinations are illustrative and may be modified, reordered, combined, or implemented separately.

Mikel Obi said Nigeria’s Super Eagles will give their best against England in a June 2, 2018 friendly at Wembley ahead of the World Cup. Nigeria will then face the Czech Republic before playing Croatia, Iceland and Argentina in Group D. England’s Group G opponents are Tunisia, Panama and Belgium.

The “Combo” defense counters spread offenses by using three aggressive perimeter pass denials and two baseline zone defenders. The on-ball defender prevents middle penetration and forces play toward sidelines. Inside defenders rotate to trap penetrations while maintaining backside support. When dribbles stop, defenders smother the ball and deny outlets. Use a quarter-court 1-3-1 trap if inside opponents handle and shoot well.

Figures 1–4 show four graphical user interface embodiments for a display screen. Figure 5 shows the first embodiment applied to an electronic device; the others may be similarly applied. Broken-line elements are not part of the claimed design.

United Distributors sued Airco Appliance & Hardware, Henry Burke, and Alfred Willis in solido for $3,107.82 owed on a corporate note, relying on a continuing personal guarantee signed by Willis. Willis had signed the guarantee while considering acquiring a 50% interest in Airco. Two days later, he abandoned that plan, and United Distributors was informed. Its salesman returned documents associated with Willis’s participation and represented that all papers were being returned, although the guarantee remained in the company’s files.

Airco, operated solely by Burke, incurred the disputed debt about a year later. The Louisiana Supreme Court found that Willis’s sole motive for signing the guarantee was his intended ownership and participation in Airco. Because that plan never materialized and the plaintiff knew Willis would not be associated with the corporation, the motive failed and the guarantee became ineffective. The judgment dismissing the suit against Willis was affirmed.

ConocoPhillips agreed to sell its San Juan Basin assets to a Hilcorp Energy affiliate for $2.7 billion, plus up to $300 million in payments tied to Henry Hub natural gas prices over six years. The assets contain 0.6 billion barrels of oil equivalent in proved reserves, primarily natural gas, and cover 1.3 million acres.

The sale, following a $13.3 billion Canadian asset divestiture, reduces ConocoPhillips’ exposure to North American natural gas. It is expected to cut production by about 115,000 barrels per day and reduce operating cash flow by $0.2 billion to $0.3 billion. The assets’ $5.9 billion book value will also result in a likely non-cash impairment, potentially providing future tax benefits.

Management said proceeds would support general corporate purposes without specifying an allocation. Possible uses include debt reduction, share repurchases, capital spending, or asset purchases. The author considers the sale reasonable but says its value depends on how management deploys the cash.

The Inquiry would assess unstable regions, develop possible economic arrangements, and safeguard minorities and weak peoples. It would support peace conference work on boundaries, government, economics, and protections by providing indexed data, maps, reports, analyses, and trained personnel. Matters outside its scope—including prisoners, devastated areas, armaments, aircraft law, reconstruction resources, commercial treaties, current commitments, and official records—were assigned to other government departments. S. E. Mezes requested a proposed inter-American agreement as a confidential model for studying international cooperation. Secretary of State Robert Lansing supplied the draft “Pan American Treaty,” restricting its circulation. The treaty sought mutual guarantees of territorial integrity, political independence, republican government, defined boundaries, peaceful dispute settlement, international justice, and domestic and regional peace.

Johnson & Johnson’s first-quarter update was mixed: sales slightly missed consensus while adjusted earnings per share met expectations. The company raised 2017 guidance, including the Actelion acquisition, to sales of $75.4–$76.1 billion and adjusted earnings of $7.00–$7.15 per share. Remicade sales fell 6% year over year, while baby care, oral care and wound care sales also declined. Group earnings per share increased, though excluding buybacks they would have been $1.57 rather than $1.61.

At about $125, JNJ traded at 19 times forward earnings and 11.9 times enterprise value to EBITDA, valuations described as neither prohibitive nor especially attractive. Falling interest rates supported its long-term debt, which recently outperformed its shares, although expected rate increases create fixed-income risk. Regulatory uncertainty, pharmaceutical pricing pressure and subdued growth remain concerns. The author views JNJ’s fundamentals as solid but believes market conditions and interest rates may matter more operationally, concluding that better value exists elsewhere.

The Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed the denial of Mumma Brothers Drilling Co.’s tax refund claim. Mumma, a contractor installing water wells, pumps, and plumbing, was subject to sales or use tax on equipment incorporated into real property unless the ultimate users qualified for an exemption. The court held that the exemption for machinery directly used to extract tangible personal property did not apply because customers generally extracted water for personal, farm, or business use rather than resale. Construing the exemption strictly, the court found insufficient evidence of eligibility and reaffirmed that part of the original claim was barred by the statute of limitations.

VIX futures, introduced in 2004, are Cboe Futures Exchange derivatives based on the VIX Index, which measures expected 30-day U.S. equity-market volatility. Traders use them to speculate on volatility, hedge equity risk, diversify portfolios, or pursue arbitrage. Strategies may combine technical or fundamental indicators with defined entry, exit, position-sizing, and risk-management rules.

VIX prices are primarily influenced by stock-market cycles and the futures curve. VIX generally falls during bullish markets and rises during bearish markets. Futures may trade at a premium to a low spot VIX during contango or at a discount to an extremely high spot VIX during backwardation. VIX futures do not precisely track spot VIX, and contract rolling can make long-term hedging costly.

Full and mini contracts have multipliers of $1,000 and $100 respectively. The full contract’s tick size is $50, representing a minimum fluctuation of 0.05 index points. Contracts expire monthly, are financially settled using a Special Opening Quotation, and have a 200-contract block minimum. The futures symbol is VX; the index symbol is VIX.

Trading requires a funded futures-broker account. Futures leverage can magnify losses substantially. CFDs differ because they are broker agreements without expiry dates, while futures trade on standardized exchanges. The VIX Index’s cited high was 89.53 in October 2008 and low was 8.56 in November 2017; VIX futures reached 80.850 in March 2020.

A simultaneous low-dose ADF-EDS-EELS tomography method was developed to map nanoscale 3D structure, chemical composition, and transition-metal valence states in NCM111 cathode particles without separate tilt series or complex registration. Applied to pristine and 50-, 100-, and 200-cycled particles, it revealed degradation pathways inaccessible to conventional 2D analysis.

Capacity declined by 34.3% after 50 cycles and 52.2% after 100 cycles, with complete loss by 200 cycles. The initial layered structure became spinel-like by 100 cycles and rock-salt by 200 cycles. Oxygen content remained near 66–67% through 100 cycles but fell to 61% at 200 cycles, corresponding to an estimated 33.7% rock-salt particle volume. Chemical composition changed largely uniformly with depth, while transition-metal segregation was approximately twice as pronounced near the surface.

Valence states showed strong depth dependence. Between 100 and 200 cycles, Mn4+ decreased from 80.7% to 53.4%, Co3+ from 77.5% to 11.0%, while Mn2+ rose from 12.1% to 42.0% and Co2+ from 22.5% to 89.0%. Surface-localized transition-metal inhomogeneity existed even in pristine particles and evolved non-monotonically during cycling.

The results identify three interacting degradation mechanisms: structural phase transitions, transition-metal migration that initially reduces inhomogeneity, and dissolution-driven segregation that subsequently increases it. Composition evolves throughout primary particles, whereas valence changes and segregation exhibit strong surface-to-core gradients. The tomography framework is presented as broadly applicable to correlated structural, chemical, and electronic analysis of complex materials.

Brayan Rocchio hit a go-ahead home run off a 99.9 mph fastball from Tigers reliever Troy Melton, igniting Cleveland’s five-run eighth inning and forcing a decisive Game 3 in the AL Wild Card Series. The homer overcame difficult shadows and strong winds and continued Rocchio’s turnaround after a six-week Triple-A stint. Detroit stranded a team postseason-record 15 runners, while Cleveland’s pitchers repeatedly escaped trouble. Both teams face elimination Thursday, with Guardians manager Stephen Vogt expecting another close contest.

The Supreme Court considered whether restitution under the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act is criminal punishment subject to the ex post facto clause. Because the law postdated Holsey Ellingburg’s offense, both Ellingburg and the government argued it could not increase his punishment, while court-appointed counsel defended the sentence. Justice Samuel Alito emphasized restitution’s victim-focused, civil features. Justices Elena Kagan and Ketanji Brown Jackson stressed its integration into criminal sentencing and penal character. The author predicts the court will reject applying the newer statute to Ellingburg.

The passage documents AGESA software interfaces for processor, cache, memory, graphics, PCIe, FCH, power-management, boot, suspend, and resume initialization.

Stackless assembler routines establish per-core pre-memory Cache-as-RAM stacks, configure address mappings and x86-64 MTRRs, and later disable the pre-memory stack when main memory becomes available. These routines run on all processor cores, preserve or destroy specified registers, and return success, warning, or fatal status codes. AArch64 APUs with a Platform Security Processor use PSP-initialized DRAM instead of these early stack mechanisms.

Utility procedures create and release initialized parameter structures using pre-memory heap, post-memory DRAM, or host-provided storage. Other services retrieve DIMM data-eye results, APIC and PCI addresses, current core identity, memory-address-to-DIMM location, available execution-cache size, event-log entries, and MMIO mappings. Most require an established stack and, where applicable, operational coherent HyperTransport links.

Boot entry procedures execute in time-point order. Reset initialization performs minimal processor and chipset setup and allocates up to three execution-cache regions under alignment, boundary, and capacity rules. Early initialization configures HyperTransport, processor power management, PCIe topology, platform characteristics, VRMs, C-states, performance limits, and related options. Post initialization discovers and initializes memory, performs training and interleaving configuration, establishes UMA and ECC options, moves pre-memory artifacts, and transitions to main-memory operation. Environment, graphics, late, and ready-to-boot stages preserve HOB data, configure display hardware, generate ACPI/DMI tables, finalize processor state, and save suspend context.

Suspend support saves critical context into nonvolatile and volatile storage. Resume procedures restore memory from self-refresh, processor and silicon registers, PCI-related state, and final OS-entry configuration.

The host environment must implement required call-outs for allocating, locating, and freeing buffers; issuing warm or cold resets; reading DIMM SPD data; and dispatching tasks to application processors. Optional or feature-dependent call-outs support IDS data, heap relocation, memory-timing hooks, external voltage and Vref control, PCIe resets and clock requests, video BIOS reposting, FCH customization, and memory testing. Platform customization is supplied through build settings, platform limits, configuration structures, and user-defined register tables.

Elliott Wave theory, developed by Ralph Nelson Elliott after studying 75 years of stock data, proposes that asset prices move in recognizable patterns. Impulse waves move with the trend and contain five sub-waves, while corrective waves move against it and contain three sub-waves labeled A, B, and C. Traders across stock, forex, and commodity markets use these patterns to identify potential buying and selling opportunities, often alongside moving averages, trend lines, RSI, or stochastic indicators.

The method provides probabilities rather than certainty and is highly subjective. Wave identification, nesting, entry points, and exits lack clear definitions, making the strategy difficult to test and vulnerable to curve fitting. Suitable timeframes depend on trading style: day traders use intraday charts, while swing traders may use daily charts. Key impulse-wave rules include that wave 2 cannot retrace more than 100% of wave 1 and wave 3 cannot be the shortest motive wave.

Verizon shares closed Friday down $0.37 at $48.81 despite a net inflow of $56.85 million, the day’s 11th highest among tracked companies. Analysts’ consensus rating was “Hold,” with an average price target of $52.86. Unusually high options activity included 87,567 call purchases, 524% above typical volume.
