Quarterly earnings matched estimates at $0.96 per share, while revenue of $30.55 billion exceeded expectations and rose 0.1% year over year. Analysts projected annual earnings of $3.76 per share. Verizon increased its quarterly dividend from $0.58 to $0.59, representing a 4.84% yield. Insiders sold 1,830 shares during the quarter, while hedge funds and institutional investors owned 62.24% of the company.

Paying off debt requires sustained discipline rather than brief deprivation. Reduce credit card use, create a spending plan and emergency fund, and apply extra income toward monthly payments. Cut nonessential expenses and prioritize debts with the highest interest rates. After paying off one balance, redirect those payments to the next. Make gradual lifestyle changes without eliminating the things you value most.

Price action trading is technical analysis based primarily on historical price movements rather than fundamentals or indicators. Day traders use intraday price swings, chart structures, candlestick patterns, trends, support, and resistance to identify entries and exits. Patterns may signal reversals or trend continuation, while common strategies include trend following, breakouts, reversals, and scalping.

Some traders use pure price action, while others add tools such as moving averages, VIX, or RSI. No strategy is universally best because results vary by strategy and market. Strategies should be translated into specific rules and backtested, though price action can be difficult to code and manual testing is vulnerable to cognitive biases.

An example using WTI crude oil futures performed poorly from 2000–2021 but produced a 0.57% average across 21 out-of-sample trades after July 2021. The passage emphasizes using performance metrics, out-of-sample testing, and incubation periods to distinguish durable strategies from random results. Diversifying across strategies and markets may also reduce risk under changing conditions.

Spanish police freed over 20 transsexual victims recruited through fake Venezuelan competitions and forced into prostitution and drug dealing in Barcelona and Palma de Mallorca. Fourteen suspects were arrested; the network allegedly earned up to €1 million over five years.

The bill allows districts and charter schools to propose innovative education plans and seek rule waivers. LEAs may use certain restricted funds and accept private support. Approved plans require charter agreement updates and reporting to the State Board, which may grant waivers or terminate plans. USBE must report annually to the Education Interim Committee. Because no applications or approved plans are known, recommendations include creating program webpages, developing optional application forms, and promoting the program through existing channels.

Alexis Perez appealed his 51-month sentence after pleading guilty to conspiracy to commit mail fraud. The Eleventh Circuit held that he was not entitled to a three-level reduction for an incomplete conspiracy because the conspirators had developed a detailed plan, possessed the means to execute it, and were on the verge of doing so when authorities intervened. The court also upheld the denial of a minor-role reduction because Perez was significantly involved in planning and preparation, understood the scheme’s implementation, received payment, and failed to show he was less culpable than most participants. Although the sentence-appeal waiver was unenforceable because the district court had not adequately questioned Perez about it, the court affirmed his sentence.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture addresses gaming, professional visualization, data-center computing, display, and video workloads. RTX IO works with Microsoft DirectStorage to transfer compressed data from NVMe SSDs to RTX GPUs for GPU-based decompression, reducing CPU demand, improving I/O performance, loading times, frame rates, asset streaming, and professional rendering workflows.

Ampere provides up to twice the programmable shading, ray-tracing, and AI performance of the prior generation. It includes second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores with structural sparsity, and GDDR6X memory support. Ampere GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, including 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz under specified compression or pixel-format requirements.

Fifth-generation NVDEC hardware decodes MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, HEVC, VP8, VP9, and AV1. GA10x GPUs can decode up to 8K60 HDR AV1 with low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding up to 4K in H.264 and 8K in HEVC while freeing CPU and graphics resources.

The A40 data-center GPU offers 48 GB of memory, expandable to 96 GB through NVLink, PCIe Gen4, virtualization support, and acceleration for visualization, AI, simulation, and rendering. The RTX A6000 provides 48 GB of GDDR6, expandable to 96 GB, for large professional workloads. The RTX 3090 includes 24 GB of GDDR6X, while the RTX 3070 uses GDDR6 and excludes NVLink.

Error Detection and Replay protects GA10x GDDR6X transfers by retrying failed transactions, helping overclockers identify memory limits through plateauing performance. NVIDIA states that specifications may change, products require suitability testing, and the materials are provided without warranties.

UK employment rose by 109,000 in the three months to April, lifting the employment rate to a joint-record 74.8%. However, annual regular earnings growth slowed to 1.7%, while inflation reached 2.9%, causing real pay to fall and pressuring consumer spending. Election-related uncertainty may also weaken business confidence and investment, leaving growth dependent on exports and corporate services. Moderating company input-cost growth suggests inflation may ease later in the year after potentially exceeding 3% in autumn. Wage growth is unlikely to improve soon, and the labour market may weaken. Given weak wages, Brexit uncertainty and temporarily higher inflation, Bank of England policymakers are increasingly likely to keep interest rates unchanged.

Google honored physicist Max Born’s 135th birthday with a Doodle celebrating his contributions to quantum mechanics. Born was born Dec. 11, 1882, in Breslau, Germany, and became a theoretical physics professor at the University of Göttingen, attracting prominent scientists. He maintained a 40-year friendship and correspondence with Albert Einstein despite differing views on quantum theory. After Hitler’s rise, Born and other Jewish academics were expelled, prompting his emigration to England. In 1954, he received the Nobel Prize for the Born Rule, which calculates the probability of a quantum measurement outcome as the square of its amplitude and underlies most quantum physics predictions. Born died Jan. 5, 1970, at age 87.

NEMA warned of impending floods and storms in parts of Enugu, Anambra and Ebonyi, based on NIHSA and NiMET forecasts. Coordinator Walson Ibarakumo attributed the risks to climate change and urged early preparation and changes in energy use. High-risk areas include Enugu South and East, Aguata, Idemili North and Ogbaru, with numerous other communities identified as flood-prone.

DBS expects Indian government bond yields to remain under upward pressure from increased issuance and rising developed-market yields, though future increases may be more modest after the recent sell-off. It favors shorter-term bonds and remains neutral-to-negative on longer maturities. The rupee and Sensex have weakened amid India’s widening current account deficit and need for capital inflows. DBS expects the savings-investment gap to reach 2–2.2% of GDP in FY19 and sees rising US rates and weaker global equities pushing the rupee toward 67 this year.

Minister Schoenfeld told Finnish Foreign Minister Witting that reports of favorable American opinion toward Finland were inaccurate and reaffirmed the existing U.S. position. Witting said Minister Procopé remained pessimistic about long-term prospects. Witting defended Finland’s strategic aims, including control of the Karelian and Onega Isthmuses, while Schoenfeld argued that security should rest on political foundations rather than territorial lines. Witting viewed British and German claims about small nations as substantially alike and attributed Finnish policy to historical experience with Russia. Schoenfeld concluded that Witting recognized Finland’s increasing subjection to forces beyond its control.

Separately, the Secretary of State informed Procopé that U.S.-citizen personnel of Finnish diplomatic and consular offices were subject to Finnish authority and could be required to comply with U.S. inquiry requirements or lose their official positions. Finnish consular personnel were required to make such inquiries before leaving their consular cities.

On December 21, 2015, Apple’s Board amended its bylaws to implement proxy access. Shareholders, or groups of up to 20 shareholders, owning at least 3% of Apple’s common stock continuously for three years may nominate directors representing up to 20% of the Board for inclusion in annual meeting proxy materials, subject to bylaw requirements. Related and conforming amendments were also adopted. The amended bylaws were filed as Exhibit 3.2.

Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) commonly develops resistance to androgen-signaling inhibitors and taxanes, leaving few treatment options. Androgen receptor (AR) variants interact differently with microtubules (MTs): ARv567 remains taxane-sensitive, whereas AR-V7 shows reduced MT association and correlates with docetaxel resistance. In isogenic prostate cancer cells, AR-V7 expression increased MT growth speed by over 40% and altered MT spatial organization relative to wild-type AR.

The study describes an automated microscopy method that tracks fluorescent EB1/EB3 markers at growing MT tips. Image filtering, Kalman tracking, and spatiotemporal clustering quantify MT growth, pausing, shortening, catastrophe, and rescue. The authors propose using these MT-dynamics signatures in patient-derived organoids to predict susceptibility to tubulin inhibitors.

Prostate organoid establishment is complicated by mixed normal and tumor tissue and the preferential growth of normal epithelial cells. Reducing the ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 temporarily selected resilient high-grade tumor cells, while benign cells were more dependent on the inhibitor. The passage also describes small, androgen-independent circulating tumor cells that may evade size-based detection but can be identified through prostate-specific membrane antigen.

Several mechanisms are linked to treatment resistance. Op18 upregulation may reduce MT polymerization and cell size in androgen-independent tumors. ERG expression can inhibit taxane–tubulin engagement. Both abnormally rapid and abnormally slow MT turnover, MT acetylation, altered cell size, and increased MT density are associated with resistance. Paclitaxel reduced MT growth rates and suppressed rapidly polymerizing MTs in breast cancer cells.

The pVHL tumor suppressor and GSK3β regulate MT homeostasis. Functional pVHL attenuates MT turnover and catastrophe, while loss of pVHL increases MT dynamics. During serum starvation, GSK3β phosphorylation of pVHL suppresses its MT-stabilizing function; GSK3 inhibition restores lower turnover. Different pVHL mutations and isoforms produce distinct MT signatures that may support selection of stabilizing or destabilizing tubulin drugs.

Paclitaxel-induced circular MT bundles were computationally detected using a circular Hough transform. Most parental A549 cells formed bundles after treatment, whereas BRCA1-knockdown cells showed substantially reduced responses, demonstrating resistance. The authors propose correlating live-cell MT dynamics, gene-expression profiles, organoid drug responses, xenografts, tissue cultures, and clinical outcomes to anticipate resistance and select therapies and doses.

Potential sensitization strategies discussed include targeting MT-regulating genes, GSK3 isoforms, pVHL pathways, GPX4-dependent persister cells, and AR domains, as well as using NAD+ or related molecules. The passage also proposes screening compounds that enhance patient-derived immune-cell responses against matched tumor organoids. Overall, quantitative imaging of cytoskeletal dynamics is presented as a possible functional assay for personalized treatment selection in localized and metastatic prostate cancer.

Al-Qaida-linked militants shot down a Russian Su-25 fighter jet near Saraqeb in Syria’s Idlib province and killed its pilot after he ejected and resisted capture. Russia said preliminary information indicated a portable ground-to-air missile was used. The incident occurred amid intense Russian and Syrian airstrikes supporting a government offensive in Idlib, where more than 270,000 people have been displaced since Dec. 15.

Separately, fighting continued around the Kurdish-held enclave of Afrin. Turkey said three soldiers were killed in attacks linked to its Operation Olive Branch, bringing Turkish military deaths to eight, alongside at least 24 allied Syrian opposition fighters. Turkey aims to remove the U.S.-backed YPG, which it considers a terrorist group, from its border. Ankara demanded that the YPG withdraw east of the Euphrates and leave Manbij, while urging the United States to end its support and maintain communication to avoid confrontation.

Xiaomi’s Redmi 5 goes on sale in India at 12 pm through Amazon India, Mi.com and Mi Home stores, with over four lakh units available. Prices are Rs 7,999 for 2GB/16GB, Rs 8,999 for 3GB/32GB and Rs 10,999 for 4GB/64GB. The phone features a 5.7-inch HD+ 18:9 display, Snapdragon 450 processor, 3300mAh battery, metal unibody, rear fingerprint scanner, 12MP rear and 5MP front cameras, and expandable storage up to 128GB. It runs Android 7.1.2 with MIUI 9 and comes in Black, Gold, Lake Blue and Rose Gold.

The President declines to submit the 1853 Tehuantepec transit convention with Mexico for Senate ratification. He objects that it would commit the United States for many years to guarantee a private company’s contract, personnel, property, and capital in a country vulnerable to civil unrest, while limiting withdrawal from those obligations. He also argues that the convention conflicts with the 1850 agreement with Great Britain covering interoceanic communication through Tehuantepec.

NVIDIA’s fiscal 2015 Form 10-K describes its visual computing business, organized into GPU and Tegra Processor segments serving Gaming, Enterprise, High Performance Computing & Cloud, and Automotive markets. Its brands include GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, GRID, Tegra, DRIVE and SHIELD. The company follows a fabless manufacturing model, relying on external foundries and subcontractors.

For the year ended January 25, 2015, NVIDIA reported revenue of $4.68 billion, operating income of $759.0 million and net income of $630.6 million, or $1.12 per diluted share. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $4.62 billion, while long-term debt was $1.38 billion. NVIDIA returned $1.00 billion to shareholders through $813.6 million in share repurchases and $186.5 million in dividends. It intended to return approximately $600 million in fiscal 2016.

NVIDIA invested $1.36 billion in research and development and employed 9,228 people, including 6,658 in R&D. Fiscal 2015 developments included Maxwell-based GeForce and Quadro GPUs, Tesla K80, GRID virtualization initiatives, SHIELD gaming devices, Tegra X1, and DRIVE automotive computers.

Primary risks include intense competition, failure to secure product design wins, defects, cybersecurity incidents, dependence on third-party manufacturers, low manufacturing yields, supply or operational disruptions, customer concentration, demand forecasting errors, international exposure, intellectual-property disputes, fluctuating operating results and substantial indebtedness. NVIDIA filed patent infringement actions against Qualcomm and Samsung in September 2014; Samsung subsequently filed a complaint against NVIDIA and Velocity Micro.

The passage describes integrating AGESA software with a host BIOS through a bridge, dispatcher, call-out port, and host-implemented call-out router. The host must locate the binary image, prepare standard configuration headers, establish a valid stack, route requested functions, allocate buffers, and preserve required data. Calls use a common dispatcher, while AGESA requests host services through the router in 32-bit protected flat mode.

UEFI integration spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases using separate libraries, drivers, PEIMs, PPIs, HOBs, and protocols. SEC establishes 32-bit execution and a Cache-As-RAM stack. PEI initializes processors and memory, coordinates resets, and publishes initialization events and memory information. DXE performs late initialization, creates system tables, and manages functions such as integrated-GPU VGA decoding.

AGESA supports binary-module and source-integration build methods. Platform options, control files, environment variables, and compiler or assembler tools configure builds. The host must avoid modifying stack registers or cache controls while Cache-As-RAM is active.

Provided stackless assembly macros establish and remove pre-memory stacks. PSP-enabled AArch64 APUs instead rely on the PSP to initialize DRAM. Service routines create and release parameter structures, query processor, cache, PCI, memory, and DIMM information, update MMIO mappings, and read event logs.

Initialization entry points proceed in boot order. They perform reset-time processor setup, early processor and interconnect configuration, memory initialization, transfer of temporary artifacts into host-controlled memory, graphics configuration, late generation of ACPI, DMI, P-state, WHEA, IVRS, CRAT, and CDIT tables, and final ready-to-boot processing. Suspend and resume routines save processor context, restore memory and silicon state, reload registers, and prepare for operating-system re-entry.

The host environment must implement required call-outs, including post-memory buffer allocation, and supply services needed for AGESA operation. Only published entry points are guaranteed to remain available.

The Colts lost 13-7 in overtime after a late penalty erased a go-ahead conversion, marking their sixth blown lead and fourth straight defeat. Blizzard conditions and a short turnaround before facing Denver raised recovery concerns. Indianapolis has been eliminated from playoff contention, extending its postseason drought to three years and renewing questions about coach Chuck Pagano’s future. Players nevertheless emphasized finishing the season strongly. Ryan Kelly and Rashaan Melvin practiced Monday, while Donte Moncrief remains week to week with an ankle injury.

Strong mentoring relationships with adults and peers—through schools, after-school programs, community organizations, or naturally occurring relationships—support students’ academic achievement, engagement, confidence, attendance, behavior, graduation, and educational attainment. Teachers and other school personnel are among the most common youth mentors.

Mentoring is especially important following COVID-19 disruptions, which produced substantial unfinished learning, weakened school connectedness, and increased depression and anxiety. These effects were greatest among low-income students, students of color, students with disabilities, and marginalized youth.

Meta-analyses and research syntheses consistently find positive educational effects from evidence-based mentoring. School- and community-based programs have improved grades, test scores, attendance, completed coursework, classroom behavior, graduation, and college enrollment. Cross-age peer mentoring can benefit both younger participants and older mentors. Natural mentoring relationships with teachers and other caring adults are associated with stronger school attachment, motivation, academic performance, and educational attainment. For students of color, mentors may also strengthen racial regard, reduce stereotype threat, and help address systemic oppression.

Access remains unequal: youth of color, low-income youth, and youth whose parents have limited education report fewer mentoring relationships, particularly with school personnel. Expanding high-quality mentoring requires private and public investment and supportive policies at local, state, and federal levels.

A longitudinal evaluation followed 11 SARS-CoV-2–positive residents of a Georgia nursing home from October 2020 through April 2021 to characterize antibody responses after infection and Pfizer-BioNTech vaccination. Participants had a median age of 74 years; 10 had at least three underlying conditions, four developed severe illness, and 10 received two vaccine doses.

Among 10 residents with post-infection serology, nine developed detectable Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA antibodies, and eight developed IgM. Median detection occurred within 13–16 days. Pan-Ig and IgG remained elevated, while IgM and IgA began declining 31–60 days after infection. Antibody detection coincided with or followed negative viral cultures but did not consistently correlate with negative RT-PCR or antigen results. One unvaccinated resident retained Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA for at least 150 days.

All vaccinated participants had detectable Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA after vaccination, while six had detectable IgM. Vaccination substantially increased Pan-Ig, IgG, and IgA titers; post-vaccination IgG geometric mean titers were 10–200 times higher than post-infection levels. Titers began decreasing 61–90 days after vaccination.

The findings indicate that these residents mounted durable, diverse antibody responses after infection that were augmented by vaccination. Limitations included the small sample, monthly sampling, short follow-up, use of one vaccine product, and evaluation before Delta and Omicron emerged.

The Court of Customs and Patent Appeals affirmed dismissal of Lever Brothers’ opposition to Thrift-D-Lux Cleaners’ registration of “Thrift-D-Lux” for dry-cleaning and pressing services. Lever Brothers relied on its longstanding, extensively advertised “Lux” trademarks for soaps and detergents and its affiliated “Lux Laundries.”

The court found that “Thrift-D-Lux” conveys economy combined with “de luxe” quality, not “Thrifty Lux.” Because “de luxe” is a common suggestive term in the public domain, Lever Brothers could not restrict its use. The court also distinguished earlier cases involving more similar marks or closely related goods. It deemed the relationship between Lever Brothers’ products and Thrift-D-Lux’s services tenuous and found no evidence of likely confusion with “Lux Laundries.” Lever Brothers therefore failed to show probable damage from registration.

An outside day, or outside bar, is a two-bar pattern in which the current bar has a higher high and lower low than the previous bar, consuming its full range. It indicates increased volatility and may signal continuation or reversal depending on the bars’ directions, the prevailing trend, and chart context. A bullish outside day has a bullish second bar, while a bearish outside day has a bearish second bar. An outside reversal occurs when the second bar moves opposite to the prior bar and price swing.

Because interpretation is subjective, outside-day patterns should be combined with technical analysis such as trend, support and resistance, pivot, and Fibonacci levels, and any strategy should be backtested.

Backtests on SPY found that returns after an outside day averaged zero from open to close. When the outside day closed higher than the preceding day, the next-day average return was negative 0.07%; when it closed lower, the average was positive 0.06%. The passage concludes that these results are not tradable and that outside days have shown little usefulness for day trading, though other opportunities may exist.

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court affirmed judgment for assignees of a Pennsylvania judgment. The bona fide assignment, made in Pennsylvania among Pennsylvania parties, was valid everywhere and left the assignor without an attachable interest. A later New York attachment served on the judgment debtors did not supersede the assignees’ rights, despite their lack of prior notice and the debtors’ payment under the New York judgment. The New York court lacked jurisdiction over the assigned property and the assignees, who were neither parties nor privies and were not required to contest proceedings after informal notice. Full faith and credit permits inquiry into another state court’s jurisdiction. Although oyer of a record was not demandable, any error was waived when the parties accepted and supplemented the filed record.

Oclaro’s fiscal 2017 revenue rose 47%, while expanded margins helped EPS increase 460% to $0.79. Despite trading below 11 times earnings, analysts expect limited EPS growth through 2019. Demand is shifting from declining legacy products and China toward high-speed optical networking. China revenue fell sequentially and is expected to decline further in the near term, although management anticipates future demand from 25G, 100G and 5G deployments.

Oclaro is strongly positioned in newer products: 100G represents 81% of revenue, QSFP28 sales doubled sequentially, and 400G products are beginning to generate revenue. Datacenters, cloud computing, streaming, IoT, AI, 4G and 5G are cited as longer-term capacity drivers. The company’s focus on high-speed products may reduce legacy-product losses while supporting growth and margins.

Revenue has doubled since mid-2015, margins have improved, and Oclaro has no debt, $258 million in cash and short-term investments, and positive operating and free cash flow. Management forecasts first-quarter 2018 revenue of $151 million to $159 million, gross margins of 38%–41%, and operating income of $30 million–$34 million. The article argues the shares are undervalued because Oclaro’s product mix may protect it from a severe cyclical downturn.

The court affirmed summary judgment dismissing plastic surgeon James Horne’s disability discrimination complaint against the New York State Department of Health. Horne alleged that his medical license was wrongfully revoked because of adult Attention Deficit Disorder and sought restoration of the license. The court held that the complaint’s essence was a challenge to the Administrative Review Board’s revocation decision, which had to be brought through a CPLR article 78 proceeding and was time-barred. It rejected Horne’s argument that article 78 review was optional because Public Health Law § 230-c (5) uses “may,” explaining that independent review would circumvent established administrative review law. The court did not address res judicata or collateral estoppel.

Northern Ireland’s health service lacks ministerial leadership and faces ageing-related demand, staffing shortages, rising drug costs and long hospital waits, despite £30m additional funding. Recent crises included recalling 3,200 neurology patients and findings of degrading treatment at Dunmurry Manor. Rafael Bengoa’s 2016 reform plan received cross-party support, but reforms have lacked leadership since Stormont collapsed in January 2017.

Nassau County jurors acquitted 18-year-old Jasmine Copeland of manslaughter, gang assault and other charges in the 2014 stabbing death of 17-year-old Abbigale Thomas during a Freeport brawl. Prosecutors alleged Copeland used a steak knife after social-media taunts escalated into a confrontation. Her attorney maintained Copeland carried but did not use a knife and said blood would otherwise have been on her clothes.

Comedian Aziz Ansari said he has used neither email nor a smartphone for about a decade, relying instead on an assistant, flip phone, taxis, and help from others. He believes reduced technology use gives him space to think and supports his writing, while acknowledging that living offline is not realistic for everyone. Ansari is skeptical of ChatGPT, arguing that it outsources critical thinking, homogenizes opinions, reinforces existing beliefs, makes mistakes, and diminishes human interaction. Other celebrities, including Christopher Nolan, Dolly Parton, and Christopher Walken, have also described limited technology use, while some members of the public are adopting basic phones or makeshift landlines to reduce screen and social-media time.

Zeta Global agreed to acquire Marigold’s enterprise software business for $325 million, its largest and 17th acquisition. The deal includes Marigold Loyalty, Cheetah Digital, Sailthru, and Selligent, while Marigold retains its small and midsize business products. Zeta expects the acquisition to expand its Fortune 500 customer base and presence in Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, while adding loyalty data to improve targeting and advertising algorithms. Zeta will pay $100 million in cash and $100 million in shares upfront, with the remaining $125 million in cash and stock paid through a seller note. Zeta expects the deal to bolster earnings in its first year.

Marian Gaborik and Dwight King said the team must avoid another two-goal deficit and improve its starts despite fatigue from three consecutive overtime games. They expect to recover, find energy and face a strong effort from the Rangers at home. Gaborik described returning to Madison Square Garden after his trade as special, citing its fans, history and energy. King emphasized rest, preparation, net-front traffic within the rules, and quickly shifting playoff momentum. Both expressed confidence in the team’s calm mindset, leadership and ability to respond under pressure.

In his bicentennial inaugural address, the President thanks Ronald Reagan, invokes George Washington, and emphasizes the continuity of American democracy. He presents freedom, democracy, free markets, free speech, and free elections as foundations for prosperity and justice. He argues that power must serve people and calls for unity, generosity, tolerance, duty, sacrifice, and civic participation.

The address urges Americans to value friendship, family, work, and service above material possessions. It identifies homelessness, neglected children, addiction, welfare dependency, crime, poverty, and unsupported young mothers as urgent problems. Because public funds are limited and the deficit must be reduced, the President advocates prudent spending and greater hands-on involvement by citizens, community organizations, young people, and the elderly through a “Thousand Points of Light.”

He calls for renewed cooperation between the executive branch and Congress, bipartisan action to balance the federal budget, and an end to divisions rooted in Vietnam. In foreign policy, he pledges strength to preserve peace, fidelity to treaties and alliances, efforts to help detained and missing Americans, and continued cautious engagement with the Soviet Union.

The President also calls for greater social tolerance while declaring drugs an intolerable national scourge. He closes with confidence that American courage, faith, and collective will can overcome the nation’s challenges and begin a new chapter defined by unity, diversity, and generosity.

East Dunbartonshire Council faces further industrial action affecting refuse services from July 12–15 by GMB, Unison and Unite members. Working to rule and overtime bans also continue. Council leaders expressed concern while impact assessments and union talks proceed. Previous action caused widespread disruption, with unions warning of further strikes over changes to employment terms and conditions.

Buchanan, convicted and sentenced to death for poisoning his wife, sought Supreme Court review, alleging denial of due process and an impartial jury because juror Paradise became physically and mentally incapacitated during deliberations and jurors temporarily separated. The New York Court of Appeals upheld the verdict, finding no prejudicial separation and insufficient evidence of Paradise’s incompetence amid conflicting medical affidavits and evidence that the jury had agreed before his illness. The Supreme Court held that a juror’s physical and mental condition and competency are factual questions not reviewable on writ of error to a state’s highest court. The application was denied.

AI chipmaker Cerebras withdrew its IPO plans more than a year after filing its prospectus, shortly after raising $1.1 billion at an $8.1 billion valuation. The company gave no formal reason but said it still hopes to go public. A spokesperson said the original prospectus was outdated and the government shutdown was not a factor. Cerebras has shifted from selling systems toward cloud services using its chips.

A study identified 50 objects most likely to generate additional debris through collisions in low-Earth orbit. Most are old rocket bodies: 76 percent were deposited before 2000, and 88 percent are rockets. Russia and the Soviet Union account for 34 objects, China 10, the United States three, Europe two, and Japan one.

Removing all 50 objects could halve debris-generation risk, while removing the top 10 could reduce it by 30 percent. However, 26 hazardous rocket bodies have been abandoned since January 2024, including 21 launched by China. Nine Chinese upper stages used for the Guowang and Thousand Sails satellite constellations are expected to remain in orbit beyond the internationally recommended 25-year limit. Continued deployments could leave more than 100 additional long-lived rocket bodies.

Although some Chinese rockets can deorbit their upper stages, others lack restartable engines or would sacrifice payload capacity by reserving fuel. China says it is researching debris removal. Such removal is technically feasible, but funding and a viable commercial market remain uncertain.

The lecture reviews stochastic methods for high-dimensional problems. Probability-weighted integrals arise in statistical mechanics and Bayesian analysis, where likelihoods and priors combine to describe parameter distributions and predictions.

Metropolis Monte Carlo requires careful step-size selection: overly large steps cause frequent rejection, while overly small steps explore space poorly. Adaptive adjustment, multiple initial states, physical reasonableness checks, and broad sampling help assess convergence. Monte Carlo errors decrease as \(1/\sqrt{n}\), so rough estimates are inexpensive but additional significant figures require substantially more samples. Reducing dimensions by removing irrelevant degrees of freedom can greatly improve efficiency.

Kinetic Monte Carlo addresses nonstationary probability distributions with enormous state spaces. The Gillespie algorithm uses random numbers to choose event times and event types. Simulations should sample initial conditions, often using Poisson distributions, and calculate desired averages during execution because storing all trajectories may be impractical. Fast, irrelevant processes can be approximated or slowed, while negligible low-probability processes may be omitted. Rare events have large statistical uncertainty.

Molecular dynamics integrates atomic motion, commonly with the velocity Verlet algorithm and thermostats. It is useful for time-dependent processes on picosecond-to-nanosecond scales but may be inefficient for equilibrium properties or processes occurring over much longer times. Initial conformations must also be sampled appropriately.

Metropolis Monte Carlo, kinetic Monte Carlo, and molecular dynamics suit different problems, so method selection should match the desired quantities and time scales. Efficient weighting functions favor concentrated probability distributions and nearly constant sampled functions. Marginal integration can remove parameters or degrees of freedom that are not of interest.

The passage describes patent technology for early detection of gastric neoplasia by measuring DNA methylation in differentially methylated regions (DMRs). Candidate markers were identified through case-control comparisons of gastric cancer samples with normal gastric, colon, plasma, and white blood cell DNA, using methods including Reduced Representation Bisulfite Sequencing. The technology covers 274 DMRs and marker panels selected for high discrimination, signal-to-noise ratio, and low background.

Highlighted markers include ARHGEF4, ELMO1, ABCB1, CLEC11A, ST8SIA1, SFMBT2, CD1D, CYP26C1, ZNF569, and C13ORF18. A plasma panel comprising ELMO1, ZNF569, and C13ORF18 detected gastric cancer with 86% sensitivity at 100% specificity. Samples may include gastric tissue, plasma, blood, stool, urine, or other biological materials.

Methylation may be assessed at one or multiple bases using bisulfite treatment, methylation-specific PCR, QuARTS, sequencing, restriction enzymes, mass spectrometry, target capture, or related techniques. Results are compared with normal reference methylation states to identify gastric neoplasia or calculate cancer risk. The technology also includes primers, probes, control nucleic acids, reaction mixtures, kits, sample collectors, software, databases, and computer systems for processing multiple-marker results and alerting users to cancer-associated methylation patterns.

The UN World Water Development Report 2018 urges nature-based solutions to rising water insecurity caused by population growth, development, consumption patterns and climate change. It warns that up to five billion people could face poor water access by 2050. Examples include China’s rainwater-recycling Sponge City, Ukraine’s artificial wetlands and community-led restoration in Rajasthan, India. There, Tarun Bharat Sangh helped communities build water-harvesting structures and regenerate soils and forests, raising groundwater, forest cover and farmland productivity. The report praised women’s leadership in securing freshwater and highlighted Sustainable Development Goal 6, which seeks universal access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene by 2030.

Michael Cohen removed “personal attorney to President Donald J. Trump” from his Twitter biography amid a federal criminal investigation, though LinkedIn retained the title. After years as Trump’s lawyer and “fixer,” Cohen told ABC News he prioritizes family and country over loyalty to Trump, praised FBI agents’ professionalism, and reportedly signaled willingness to provide prosecutors information about the President.

Peter’s aggressive, high-pressure system took up to two months to master but has improved the team’s conditioning and produced success. The opponent is described as highly competitive, tenacious, versatile and deserving close attention. Despite limited rest and travel, the team expects no letdown in the finals. Success will require consistent hockey, strong defense and avoiding a fast-paced track meet against an evenly matched opponent. Offensively, the plan is to shoot often, create traffic and score gritty goals. The speaker also praises an opposing leader as relentless, confident and among the world’s best players.

Six-year-old Ryan became a major YouTube star through “Ryan ToysReview,” where his parents film him opening, playing with and reviewing toys. Started in March 2015 after Ryan asked why he was not on YouTube, the channel surged following a viral video featuring more than 100 toys. It reached over 10 million subscribers, generated more than 8 billion views during one 12-month period, and earned $11 million in revenue between June 2016 and June 2017, ranking eighth on Forbes’ list of highest-paid YouTube entrepreneurs.

The channel combines toy “unboxing,” family activities and child-focused entertainment, emphasizing surprises and simple play rather than detailed analysis. Advertising and product links generate income, while Ryan’s enthusiasm can strongly influence toy sales. His parents said most videos were not branded and that most reviewed toys were donated to charity.

Ryan’s family posts daily while arranging filming around his school schedule and protecting his surname and residence. Young viewers often watch for hours, imitate him, request featured products and regard him as a friend. Parents report both commercial influence and perceived benefits, including helping some children develop speech, imagination and play skills.

The team remains confident despite a difficult series, citing improved play and scoring chances. Players trust Marc based on his season and playoff record. Although emotions may cause frustration, returning home with favorable matchups and lineup changes could help secure a first win and build momentum.

WIRED recommends the $499 Pixel 9a for most buyers because of its strong cameras, bright 6.3-inch OLED display, Tensor G4 performance, long battery life, and seven years of support. Its 8 GB of RAM excludes features such as Call Notes and Pixel Screenshots.

The Pixel 10 adds a faster Tensor G5 chip, brighter display, louder speakers, 5X optical zoom, sharper selfies, Pixelsnap Qi2 magnetic charging, and newer AI features. US models are eSIM-only. The Pixel 10 Pro and Pro XL offer larger camera sensors, 16 GB of RAM, vapor-chamber cooling, 1–120-Hz displays, Pro Res Zoom up to 100X, and cloud-processed 8K Video Boost. The XL adds faster wired and 25W wireless charging, stronger audio, and longer battery life.

The $1,799 Pixel 10 Pro Fold provides an 8-inch folding display, Qi2 support, and improved durability, but it is heavy and lacks several Pro camera and cooling features. Older Pixel 9 models remain worthwhile only at substantial discounts. Recent Pixel generations receive seven years of operating-system and security updates, while some older A-series phones have battery-related concerns.

Recommended accessories include Qi2-compatible cases from Google, Mous, Dbrand, Bellroy, and Peak Design, plus Google’s Ring Stand, Pixelsnap chargers, screen protectors, and a 65W USB-C adapter. The Pixel Buds Pro 2 and Pixel Watch 4 complement the phones.

Pixel software features include call screening, hold assistance, transcription, translation, Gemini tools, Recorder, Magic Cue, theft protection, satellite emergency messaging, photo and video editing, astrophotography, Add Me, Best Take, Audio Magic Eraser, and Now Playing. Many features depend on the Pixel model, Tensor generation, RAM, language, or region.

The disclosure describes methods, apparatuses, systems, and program products for improving wireless downlink reliability through coordinated downlink control and data assignments. A user equipment monitors control-channel candidates in multiple control resource sets, receives assignments, determines data-channel allocations and demodulation reference-signal locations using the assignments and OFDM-symbol sets, and decodes the corresponding data channels. When allocations collide with control resources, reference-signal placement may depend on the control resource set ending later.

Associated search spaces may correspond to different control resource sets and reference-signal quasi-colocation relationships. The equipment determines monitoring occasions for each search space and a shared subset, then monitors candidates assumed to carry identical downlink control information. Multiple PDCCHs carrying the same information or scheduling PDSCHs carrying the same transport block may be transmitted from multiple transmission points. Their likelihood information may be combined to improve decoding reliability.

The disclosure also addresses repeated PDSCH transmissions, shared HARQ process numbers, acknowledgment-resource selection, transmission configuration indicator states, beam switching, and timing of configuration updates. A successful decoding of one associated PDSCH may stop further decoding and produce one positive acknowledgment; negative acknowledgment occurs only if all associated transmissions fail. Configuration changes generally are not applied during a PDSCH reception window.

Additional embodiments specify consistent PUCCH-resource determination across multiple control resource sets, control-channel-element indexing constraints, monitoring periodicities and durations, and implementation through processors, receivers, transmitters, memory, hardware, software, or combinations thereof.

Apple reportedly planned to unveil a “Blush Gold” iPhone 8 at its September keynote. Leaker Benjamin Geskin claimed the color was an internal Foxconn name and would come in 64GB and 128GB versions. Other rumored features included an edge-to-edge screen, no home button, and wireless charging, though the final color name remained uncertain.

A defensive switch occurs when the first defender is beaten and the supporting second defender takes over the ball carrier. The first defender then covers the second defender’s original mark or assumes a supporting position. The second defender initiates the switch, usually creating a crossing movement between defenders.

The support defender should remain goalside, behind and inside the first defender, positioned to block the direct route to goal and encourage play toward the sideline. They must maintain suitable distance, avoid overrunning play, adopt a proper defensive stance, adjust with the attacker’s movement, and announce their arrival.

Communication includes “support” to confirm cover, “jockey” or “contain” to delay the attacker, “tackle” to authorize a challenge, and “switch” when the first defender is beaten. After danger passes, “switch back” or “return” signals resumption of normal assignments.

Training should progress from stationary positioning to relative movement, half-speed communication drills, and full-speed game conditions. Scenarios include switches when beaten down the sideline or toward the field’s interior, and midfield switches used to prevent open space or collisions. Switches may also occur when an opponent runs past a defender without dribbling. Recovering defenders should take the most direct route to their new position.

The report analyzes the global pyridine market from 2012 to 2022, including sales, revenue, pricing, market share, and growth across the United States, China, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia, and India. It covers chemical-synthesized and coal-tar-extracted pyridine for agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, and chemical synthesis. Major manufacturers include BASF, Bayer, Dow Chemical, DuPont, Mitsubishi Chemical, Lonza, Vertellus, Royal DSM, Sanonda, and others. Detailed regional data are provided for the United States, China, and Europe, while market valuation and CAGR figures remain unspecified.

In *Lewis v. Bayer AG*, plaintiffs sought certification of four classes arising from use of Baycol, a cholesterol-lowering drug withdrawn by Bayer in August 2001 after reports of severe rhabdomyolysis and deaths. Proposed classes included Pennsylvania and nationwide medical-monitoring classes for users without diagnosed injury, and Pennsylvania and nationwide personal-injury classes. Claims included medical monitoring, negligence, unjust enrichment, and violations of Pennsylvania’s Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law.

Applying Pennsylvania Rules of Civil Procedure 1702 and 1708, the court found numerosity satisfied because approximately 700,000 consumers had used Baycol. It concluded, however, that individual questions concerning medical history, dosage, treatment duration, other medications, warnings, causation, and injuries predominated in the personal-injury classes. Nationwide certification was also inappropriate because state laws governing medical monitoring, unjust enrichment, consumer protection, negligence, and product liability differed, and the law of each class member’s state would apply.

The court found common questions for a Pennsylvania medical-monitoring class. These included whether Baycol was hazardous, whether defendants inadequately disclosed its risks, whether users faced an increased risk of latent disease, and whether proposed testing for CoQ10 depletion, elevated CK levels, and heart conditions was reasonably necessary. The named Pennsylvania plaintiffs had ingested Baycol but had not been diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis or congestive heart failure, making their claims typical of asymptomatic users seeking monitoring.

The court rejected class certification for the consumer-protection claim because reliance and causation required individualized proof. General unjust-enrichment claims also required individual determinations. Although purchasers told to stop using Baycol after its withdrawal potentially shared common unjust-enrichment issues, plaintiffs presented insufficient evidence that the named representatives personally paid for unused medication or suffered monetary loss, so typicality was not established.

The court held that a class action was a fair and efficient method for resolving the Pennsylvania medical-monitoring claim. It certified a class of all Pennsylvania persons prescribed and ingesting Baycol who had not been diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis or congestive heart disease, seeking medical monitoring and related equitable relief. Arthur Conner, Milton Angert, and Lisa Frost were appointed class representatives, plaintiffs’ counsel was appointed class counsel, and certification was denied for all other classes. The parties were directed to submit proposed notice procedures and forms within 30 days.

The passage defines requirements for integrating AMD AGESA software with a host BIOS. Only published interface functions may be called, and execution caching must not be enabled before main-memory initialization except through AGESA functions. AGESA calls return status codes ranging from SUCCESS and UNSUPPORTED through WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL, and FATAL; the host environment must implement the appropriate response. Most errors create event-log entries, with the 16 latest retrievable through AmdReadEventLog.

Binary modules execute in 32-bit protected mode; 16-bit real-mode support is deprecated. A host bridge calls the AGESA dispatcher, while AGESA call-outs reach host services through a host-implemented router. The host must provide a valid stack, populate standard headers, implement required call-outs, and use published dispatcher identifiers. UEFI integration spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases, with PEIMs coordinating processor, memory, and reset initialization and publishing PPIs, HOBs, and protocols. The DXE driver performs late initialization and publishes generated system tables.

Build support includes binary-module and source-integration methods, platform option files, UEFI control files, environment variables, reference files, and platform-specific customization. Cache-as-RAM must be enabled using provided AGESA procedures before AmdInitReset. While CAR is active, the host must not modify SS, ESP, cache controls, or MTRRs. Provided stack macros establish and remove pre-memory stacks; relevant routines are stackless assembly and must run as specified across processor cores. AArch64 APUs with a Platform Security Processor instead rely on the PSP to initialize DRAM.

Utility interfaces create and release parameter structures, query DIMM data-eye results, APIC and PCI addresses, execution-cache size, current processor identity, memory-address location, MMIO mappings, and event logs. Structures must be released after creation, and most services require a stack.

Initialization proceeds through published entry points. AmdInitReset performs minimal processor initialization and allocates constrained execution-cache regions. AmdInitEarly performs full processor, HyperTransport, power-management, PCIe, graphics, and platform configuration before memory initialization. AmdInitPost initializes memory, handles training, interleaving, ECC, UMA, voltage, refresh, and related policies, transfers pre-memory data, and disables the pre-memory stack. Later environment and graphics calls preserve HOB data, configure FCH/GNB and display hardware, and must occur around memory allocation and PCI enumeration as specified. AmdInitLate generates operating-system information tables such as DMI, P-state, WHEA, IVRS, CRAT, CDIT, and ACPI data. Ready-to-boot routines save processor context for suspend, while resume routines restore silicon, memory, and saved registers. The host remains responsible for memory allocation, AP coordination, table registration, suspend initiation, context preservation, MTRR restoration, and handling all returned errors.

WHO urban data from 1,622 locations in 92 countries ranked population-weighted PM2.5 concentrations. Pakistan had the most polluted urban areas, followed by Qatar and Afghanistan; Australia had the least polluted, followed by Brunei and New Zealand. Turkey, Bulgaria and Serbia had Europe’s most polluted cities, while Estonia performed best in Europe. The UK ranked 21st. Rankings cover cities only and may not represent national air quality.

Air Force cyber leaders argue that rapid technological change requires flexible organization, continuous training, innovation and openness to unconventional ideas. The Maryland Air National Guard’s 175th Cyberspace Operations Group exemplifies this approach by combining military training with members’ diverse civilian expertise in cybersecurity, software development, system architecture and other fields.

Activated in 2016, the group grew from a 35-Airman detachment to more than 200 personnel across four squadrons conducting offensive, defensive and support operations. Its missions have included protecting government networks, supporting presidential inaugurations, collaborating with Estonia and assisting federal agencies and military cyber organizations.

Tech. Sgt. Kyle Hanslovan said civilian cybersecurity work improves Guard members’ offensive and defensive capabilities, while competitions and the National Guard’s Innovations Program provide opportunities to test and rapidly apply new techniques. Leaders also emphasized transparent operational environments where expertise can outweigh rank.

The Air National Guard’s personnel continuity and private-sector experience can support specialized, long-term capabilities such as cyber tool development, data analytics and artificial intelligence. However, leaders identified slow hiring, personnel turnover, promotion structures that move skilled operators away from technical work and difficulty retaining full-time cyber talent as major challenges. They advocated faster recruitment, career paths for hands-on specialists and broader outreach to sustain the cyber force.

The Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) guarantees students with disabilities a free appropriate public education (FAPE) and permits families to pursue due process hearings over alleged violations. Pennsylvania has historically had high IDEA dispute activity, including significant pandemic-era compliance problems in Philadelphia and Pittsburgh. Nationally, fewer due process complaints and decisions occurred early in the pandemic, while failure to provide FAPE became the most common post-pandemic hearing issue.

This study examines whether COVID-19 influenced due process hearings involving Pennsylvania city local education agencies (LEAs). It asks whether city LEAs appeared in more hearings after the pandemic, whether the pandemic was significantly related to hearing officer outcomes, and what remedies city LEAs were required to provide afterward.

Using an ex-post facto design, the study reviews publicly available Pennsylvania Office for Dispute Resolution decisions uploaded from March 16, 2018, through March 15, 2022. After removing 24 duplicates, 323 decisions remain for screening, with non-city LEA cases excluded. March 16, 2020, separates pre- and post-COVID-19 periods. Frequency distributions will compare hearing activity, and a chi-square test will assess the relationship between period and ruling outcomes. Outcomes are classified from fully favoring the student to fully favoring the LEA. Post-pandemic remedies are categorized as independent educational evaluations, compensatory education, or financial reimbursements.

The Georgia Court of Appeals affirmed an order granting Ricky Rau sole legal and physical custody of his three children and modifying child support. The majority held that appellant Kathrine Clark’s pro se brief failed to provide clear enumerations of error, supporting arguments, record citations, or authority, and that no transcript was supplied. Consequently, the court presumed the trial proceedings were regular and supported by sufficient evidence. It also concluded that the trial court’s finding of a substantial change in circumstances affecting the children’s welfare sufficiently reflected the applicable standard, despite not expressly stating that modification served their best interests.

The dissent argued that Clark’s filings sufficiently challenged the custody order and that appellate courts must liberally construe such filings to reach the merits. It maintained that the order was facially deficient because custody modification requires findings both of materially changed circumstances and that the change serves the children’s best interests. The dissent would have vacated the order and remanded for application of the complete legal standard.

A bilateral trade deal permits China to export cooked poultry to the United States in exchange for accepting U.S. beef and liquefied natural gas. Cooking requirements address concerns that raw poultry could transmit avian influenza. Properly cooked poultry poses no viral or bacterial risk, but inadequate cooking or cross-contamination could spread salmonella or campylobacter. Additional concerns include antibiotic residues and heavy metals, especially given weak enforcement and limited public food-safety data in China.

The USDA requires foreign poultry safeguards to be equivalent to U.S. standards. China certifies and inspects eligible plants, while U.S. officials conduct at least annual audits. Because cooked poultry is exempt from country-of-origin labeling, consumers may not know when products were grown and processed in China, including at restaurants. Chinese poultry could find a U.S. market if competitively priced, though its industry currently lacks the integration and technology of the U.S. industry.

The passage defines a bear market as the S&P 500 trading below its 200-day moving average. Since 1960, such periods have occurred about twice yearly, lasted an average of 25 trading days, and represented 30% of market time.

Its recommended approach is to follow a disciplined plan, backtest strategies across bull and bear cycles, and prepare to trade both long and short. Short strategies may improve in falling markets, while long strategies can benefit from sharp bear-market rallies. A cited long-only QQQ strategy reportedly performed especially well during bear markets, illustrating the importance of limiting losses, preserving capital, and compounding from a higher base.

Long-term investors are advised to continue investing and use lower prices as buying opportunities rather than attempting to identify the market bottom. The passage warns against cognitive biases such as buying after strong performance and selling after declines. Overall, traders should remain adaptable, ignore pessimistic news, avoid changing validated strategies out of fear, and continue executing backtested systems.

The lecture compares model-free policy-gradient and value-function methods. Policy gradients scale to high-dimensional systems, exploit smoothness, are simple, and offer strong convergence, but perform local searches with high-variance updates that may require many trials. Value methods can learn faster by reusing data and compactly estimating expected returns, but changing a value estimate can abruptly change the policy, causing instability, oscillation, or divergence.

Actor-critic methods combine both approaches by representing a policy, the “actor,” and a value estimate, the “critic.” The critic supplies an expected reward against which observed rewards are compared, reducing update variance while preserving policy-gradient convergence when its estimate is uncorrelated with exploration noise. Better value estimates accelerate convergence. Typically, the policy changes more slowly than the value estimate, creating a two-timescale algorithm. The policy-gradient theorem relates policy gradients to the stationary state-action distribution, the Q-function, and gradients of policy log probabilities.

Tedrake illustrates actor-critic learning through his Toddler walking robot. Toddler was based on a stable three-dimensional passive walker, with ankle actuators, sensors, onboard computation, nine degrees of freedom, and four motors. Its objective was to reproduce a downhill passive-walking limit cycle on arbitrary slopes by learning a policy that made its return map approach a deadbeat controller.

The robot updated its policy once per footstep using a linear, barycentric-grid function approximator and a very low-dimensional value estimate. Starting as a passive walker on flat ground, it learned to step in place in about one minute, walk under joystick guidance in about five minutes, and usually converge within 10–20 minutes. Retaining the learned value function while resetting the policy reduced relearning to roughly two minutes. The controller recovered from disturbances, adapted when moving between tile and carpet, and even learned to walk with a broken ankle.

Learning remained active continuously and required sufficiently small policy perturbations that exploration was not visually obvious. A heavily discounted reward with gamma 0.2 emphasized approximately one-step corrections, improving learning speed at the expense of aggressive multistep behavior. The work showed that simple actor-critic methods could rapidly learn robust control on a real underactuated robot without an accurate dynamics model.

Human Rights Watch said Turkish border guards shot, beat and turned back Syrians fleeing intensified fighting in north-west Syria, sometimes denying medical care. Escalating Syrian government attacks in Idlib, Hama and Aleppo reportedly killed dozens of civilians, including families fleeing by road. Shelling and air raids also killed civilians in Douma, while 400,000 people in besieged eastern Ghouta faced severe food and medicine shortages and widespread malnutrition.

The passage criticizes celebrities, including KISS, who declined to perform at Donald Trump’s inauguration, calling their decisions disrespectful and politically biased. It notes that Jackie Evancho, the Radio City Rockettes, Mormon Tabernacle Choir, military, police and first responders would participate. The author predicts public backlash against the celebrities and increased fame for Evancho.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K on May 13, 2019, announcing the final consideration for its offer to exchange all outstanding Maxwell Technologies common shares for Tesla common stock. The filing includes Tesla’s press release and legal opinions from Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati and DLA Piper regarding material U.S. federal income tax consequences of the offer and subsequent merger. CFO Zachary J. Kirkhorn signed the report.

Strength training builds muscle, strength and endurance, but poor technique, inadequate warm-ups, repetitive movements or lifting beyond your ability can cause injuries. Common problems include rotator cuff injuries, hamstring strains or tears, herniated discs, tendonitis, and tennis or golfer’s elbow.

Risk can be reduced by maintaining good form and posture, stretching regularly, warming up properly, limiting repetitive forceful movements, working within comfortable limits and increasing workout intensity gradually. Dynamic movements and jogging on the spot can prepare the body for exercise, while static stretches are more suitable after a workout. Cooling down helps blood flow and allows the cardiovascular system to transition gradually out of exercise.

Do not continue exercising through pain. Stop, rest and consult a doctor if discomfort persists. Treatment may include rest, painkillers, physiotherapy, injections or surgery, depending on the injury and its severity. Gentle exercise may aid recovery from a herniated disc after initial rest. Ice, compression, elevation, hydration and a good diet may also support recovery. A qualified fitness instructor or personal trainer can help create an achievable programme and ensure exercises are performed correctly.

A study in Value in Health found that testing seven cancer-associated genes—BRCA1, BRCA2, TP53, PTEN, CDH1, STK11, and PALB2—could cost-effectively improve life expectancy for women at risk of hereditary breast cancer compared with BRCA1/2-only testing. A decision-analytic model estimated costs of $69,920 and $48,328 per quality-adjusted life-year gained for women aged 50 and 40, respectively, levels considered cost effective under World Health Organization guidelines. The findings highlight the potential value of expanded genetic panels followed by appropriate risk-reduction treatment.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell RTX architecture improves AI, ray tracing, rendering, video, display, and power efficiency. FP4 reduces model memory requirements and accelerates workloads such as FLUX.dev, allowing them to run on more GeForce GPUs.

Fourth-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and add hardware for Mega Geometry and Linear Swept Spheres. Mega Geometry supports detailed, frequently changing geometry through cluster-level acceleration structures, batched GPU-driven BVH management, and partitioned top-level acceleration structures. It supports modern level-of-detail systems, high object counts, and real-time ray tracing of subdivision surfaces. Linear Swept Spheres render strand-like geometry such as hair about twice as fast as triangle strips while using roughly one-fifth the geometry memory. SER 2.0 improves thread reordering efficiency and neural-shading performance.

The AI Management Processor uses a dedicated RISC-V processor to schedule GPU contexts, reducing CPU involvement, latency, and potential game stuttering. Blackwell also adds hardware encoding and decoding for 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC video. Ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality, while sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed. RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders. DisplayPort 2.1b provides up to 80 Gbps and supports 8K at 165 Hz or 4K at 480 Hz with compression.

Max-Q improvements include finer power and clock gating, separate GPU-core and memory voltage rails, clocks that adapt 1,000 times faster, and sleep entry up to ten times faster than Ada. These changes can reduce power consumption substantially in intermittent workloads.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three generated frames per rendered frame. Its model is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and uses GPU-based Flip Metering for more precise pacing. Transformer models replace CNNs for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability, motion detail, lighting, anti-aliasing, and reducing ghosting.

Blackwell enables neural shaders through Cooperative Vectors APIs for DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Applications include neural materials, texture compression, radiance caching, subsurface scattering with RTX Skin, and generative facial rendering with RTX Neural Faces. Neural Texture Compression reduces material memory use, while Neural Radiance Cache estimates multi-bounce indirect lighting from limited path-traced rays.

The flagship GB202 contains 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, and 768 Tensor cores, and powers the RTX 5090. GB203 contains 45.6 billion transistors and 10,752 CUDA cores for the RTX 5080 and 5070 Ti. GB205 contains 31 billion transistors and 6,400 CUDA cores for the RTX 5070. NVIDIA states that specifications may change and disclaims warranties and liability beyond its sales terms.

Plantation police arrested Eric Robinson, 46, on a first-degree murder charge, alleging he killed his roommate and dumped the body behind a shopping center. Neighbors described the unidentified victim as kind and reported frequent domestic disturbances involving Robinson and a woman at their duplex. Robinson had recent arrests for domestic violence, strangulation and cocaine possession. The victim’s name is withheld pending family notification.

Shop & Save Market signed a letter of intent to open a grocery store in South Shore’s Jeffery Plaza, vacant since Dominick’s closed in 2014. Owner Cezary Jakubowski said the deal remains unfinished but the store could open within 18 to 24 months. More than $10 million in city tax increment financing may support the project. Shop & Save hopes to buy the entire plaza, retain existing tenants and renovate the deteriorated space. City Hall has classified South Shore as a food desert since the closure.

SOS Pressure Defense uses automatic contact switching to disrupt on- and off-ball screens, deny passing lanes and quick shots, reduce hesitation and fouls, force turnovers, and interrupt offensive flow. Defenders communicate “Screen-Over-Switch”: the screener’s defender alerts, hedges into the cutter’s path, and switches while the teammate covers the screener. Off-ball switches emphasize close-contact SNUGGLE pass denial. Baseline screens follow a “Hi-Lo” rule: switch when the cutter goes low along the baseline, but not when the cutter goes high. On-ball screens above the free-throw-line extended receive aggressive contact switches to prevent jump shots and middle penetration; screens below it trigger aggressive baseline or corner traps, Triangle I rotations, and nearest-player closeouts. Any resulting mismatches prompt immediate traps using Near Player rotations.

The patent continuation describes storage systems supporting artificial intelligence infrastructure and reproducibility. Architectures include storage arrays, direct-mapped flash devices, dual controllers, clustered storage nodes, compute resources, and cloud connectivity. Controllers directly manage flash allocation, wear leveling, garbage collection, redundancy, and metadata, while NVRAM provides fast writes and uses stored energy to preserve data during power loss. Distributed authorities assign ownership and locations for data and metadata, enabling erasure coding, mirroring, automatic failover, proactive rebuilding, load balancing, and non-disruptive hardware replacement. Scalable, hot-pluggable storage clusters distribute processing and storage across blades, migrate authorities when nodes change or fail, and support standard network and storage protocols. Cloud providers may supply infrastructure, platforms, software, authentication, or storage services through public or private deployments.

Mediclinic’s shares rose after improved Middle East prospects. Switzerland, southern Africa and Dubai met expectations, while Abu Dhabi faced regulatory challenges. Middle East revenue fell 8%, but Mediclinic expects regional performance to improve.

A study led by University of Guelph professor Nigel Raine found that bumblebee queens exposed to field-realistic levels of thiamethoxam, a widely used neonicotinoid pesticide, were 26 per cent less likely to lay eggs and start colonies. Mathematical modelling suggested this reduction could threaten long-term population survival and increase extinction risk. Researchers also tested a common parasite but observed little effect. Raine said the findings may be conservative because wild bumblebees face additional pesticides, diseases and habitat destruction. The study was published in Nature Ecology & Evolution.

For the UC1825B-SP push-pull converter, output-diode voltage stress equals maximum input voltage plus output voltage; the selected diode is rated at 60 V to allow for parasitic spikes. Primary MOSFETs experience approximately twice the input voltage plus ringing and should be rated at 2.5–3 times the input voltage.

Approximately 1145 µF of output capacitance was selected to limit ripple and withstand load steps. Six ceramic capacitors precede a 500-nH output-filter inductor, followed by bulk tantalum and ceramic capacitors. A 0.5-Ω resistor across the inductor damps high-frequency peaking. Type IIB compensation was designed around a 5-kHz crossover, with its zero below 500 Hz and its pole near the capacitors’ ESR zero. The current-sense resistor monitors transformer ripple current and terminates switching when the CS pin approaches its approximately 1-V threshold.

Tests used a 48-V input and 10-A load, including MOSFET stress, output ripple, and a 0-to-10-A transient. The controller supply range is 10–30 V and should be well regulated; remote supplies may require about 100 µF of additional bulk capacitance.

PCB guidance emphasizes closed-core, low-EMI inductors; short, thick power traces; closely grouped power components; separated signal and power areas; and ground planes. Feedback and compensation components should remain close to the IC and away from inductors and noisy traces. VCC must be bypassed to power ground, while VREF and analog circuitry are bypassed to signal ground. Proper ESD handling is required, and TI’s documentation, design resources, packaging data, and advice are subject to change and provided under stated limitations and disclaimers.

A jury at Mold Crown Court heard that Redvers Bickley attacked housemate Tyler Denton, her sisters Cody and Shannen, and their father Paul after a birthday gathering in Rhyl. Prosecutor John Philpotts said Bickley stabbed Tyler in the neck, causing fatal internal blood loss, and seriously wounded her relatives before Paul and Cody overpowered him. Shannen reportedly survived by pretending to be dead. Bickley, 21, admits killing 25-year-old Tyler on September 9 but denies murder and attempting to murder her father and sisters. The six-day trial continues.

Micro-business advocate Tony Robinson has become patron of the John Cracknell Youth Enterprise Bank, which offers grants up to £1,000 to young people across parts of Yorkshire. More than 400 recipients have received funding to develop their ideas.

Five English clubs—Manchester City, Manchester United, Liverpool, Tottenham and Chelsea—reached the Champions League last 16, a competition record for one country. Group runners-up Chelsea can draw only Paris St Germain, Barcelona or Besiktas, while Bayern Munich, Juventus and Real Madrid are major threats for the four English group winners. Tottenham cannot face Real after finishing above them. Basel, Sevilla, Shakhtar Donetsk and Porto are considered more favourable opponents. PSG are bookmakers’ favourites, ahead of Manchester City and Real Madrid. In the Europa League draw, seeded Arsenal could face Celtic but will avoid other group winners and the four best third-placed Champions League teams.

Whitworth University will cut annual tuition from $54,000 to $26,900 next fall and publish a transparent, GPA-based merit scholarship scale. Officials say the change responds to research showing that families want clearer cost information, not declining enrollment. The university calculated the price by considering current student payments, scholarships and need-based aid.

College sticker prices are often much higher than what students pay after grants and scholarships, but families may not understand these discounts. Whitworth leaders argue that the traditional model of high prices and opaque awards creates unnecessary confusion and may become less effective as students increasingly prioritize affordability and return on investment.

Research indicates tuition resets do not generally increase overall enrollment but may attract more Pell-eligible students by reducing sticker shock. However, colleges may resist lowering published prices because high tuition can signal quality, creating what one economist described as a prisoner’s dilemma. Whitworth leaders report overwhelmingly positive feedback from families about the new model’s simplicity and transparency.

The passage describes power, reset, clocking, interrupts, peripheral interfaces, and timing requirements for a TI DM8127/DM814x device. SmartReflex supports real-time Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling through selectable operating performance points; Adaptive Voltage Scaling is described but not supported. SRAM blocks can enter shutdown with data loss, while I/O and DDR interfaces support independently selectable supply voltages.

Low-power standby turns off switchable domains, minimizes ARM frequency, and gates unused clocks. Supplies must follow specified sequencing, voltage-difference, filtering, decoupling, and reset requirements. Multiple reset types are supported, including power-on, warm, watchdog, software, emulation, test, local, PCIe-isolated, and optionally EMAC-isolated resets. Reset behavior determines module state, pin impedance, boot-mode latching, and ARM execution from Boot ROM.

Device clocks derive from external crystals or 1.8-V LVCMOS inputs, PLLs, and dividers. DEV and optional AUX clocks generally operate from 20–30 MHz; PCIe requires a low-jitter differential SERDES clock. PLLs start in bypass mode and must remain within specified frequency and supply limits. The device provides configurable clock inputs and outputs, SYSCLKs, and module clocks.

The ARM interrupt controller handles up to 128 programmable requests, while the C674x DSP combines up to 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts. The passage also specifies AC timing, board-routing considerations, and monotonic signal transitions.

Peripheral coverage includes DCAN, EDMA, advanced debugging and trace, JTAG, Ethernet switching and MDIO, GPIO, GPMC/ELM memory interfaces, and HDMI. The Ethernet switch supports two external 10/100/1000-Mbps ports and MII, GMII, RMII, or RGMII modes using 3.3-V signaling. GPIO provides up to 128 configurable channels. GPMC interfaces with NOR, NAND, SRAM, pseudo-SRAM, and custom logic, while ELM locates BCH errors. HDMI supports HDMI 1.3a, DVI, multichannel audio, and resolutions up to 1080p, with controlled-impedance TMDS routing and ESD protection requirements.
