Ankit, an engineering graduate, admitted killing Sheelu and her cousin Shivani after Sheelu rejected his marriage proposal in Bulandshahr. He burned their bodies, and police solved the case within 24 hours using mobile surveillance.

Enron evolved from a debt-burdened pipeline company created through the 1985 merger of Houston Natural Gas and InterNorth into a dominant energy trader. Ken Lay backed Jeff Skilling’s Gas Bank concept, which guaranteed gas supply and pricing while Enron assumed trading risks. Its success led Enron into electricity, commodities, online trading, broadband, international power projects, and water privatization, driving rapid revenue and stock growth.

Skilling built an aggressive culture favoring elite recruits, rapid dealmaking, large performance bonuses, and forced employee rankings. Enron pursued immediate profits, frequently abandoned lower-margin projects, treated clients as “counterparties,” and used mark-to-market accounting extensively, often recording projected long-term profits upfront. Internal competition, work pressure, secrecy, and employee turnover intensified as the company expanded.

By 2001, Enron faced declining stock prices, criticism over California’s energy crisis, costly international projects, the collapse of telecommunications investments, failed ventures such as Azurix and the Blockbuster agreement, and growing scrutiny of its accounting. Skilling responded combatively to critics and resigned after six months as CEO, citing personal sacrifices and family priorities. Lay returned as CEO, acknowledged morale problems, and promised to refocus innovation closer to Enron’s core businesses.

A prospective single-center study assessed bioimpedance spectroscopy (BIS) in 157 patients hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure, including 72 with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and 111 with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Overhydration and the overhydration-to-extracellular-water ratio were measured at admission and discharge. During 10.7 ± 7.1 months of follow-up, 51 patients experienced major adverse cardiovascular events and 45 were rehospitalized for heart failure. BIS detected fluid-status changes, with significantly greater reductions in the overhydration ratio among HFrEF patients than non-HFrEF patients. However, BIS measurements and their changes did not significantly predict either outcome across CKD, non-CKD, HFrEF, or non-HFrEF groups. The study concludes that BIS can monitor fluid status, particularly in HFrEF, but its prognostic value remains limited. Limitations included the single-center design, small sample, absence of a non-BIS control group, and relatively short follow-up.

The David Swensen Portfolio, or Yale Model, was developed by Yale endowment chief David Swensen with Dean Takahashi. It diversifies across stocks, bonds, real estate, private equity, hedge funds, natural resources, and other alternatives, while emphasizing low-cost index funds, passive investing, undervalued assets, and risk management.

Swensen transformed Yale’s traditionally structured endowment into a highly successful fund. From 1985 to 2020, the Yale Model returned an annualized 12.5%, compared with 9.7% for the S&P 500. However, historical performance does not guarantee future results, and individual implementations may differ from Yale’s portfolio.

Investors can approximate the strategy using ETFs covering domestic and international stocks, emerging markets, real estate, Treasury bonds, and inflation-protected securities. Allocations may be adjusted according to goals and risk tolerance and regularly rebalanced.

A recent ETF-based backtest produced annual returns of 6.23% and underperformed the S&P 500, largely because of its bond allocation and weak emerging-market performance. Its drawdowns were lower than the S&P 500’s. The strategy may not suit every investor, so personal objectives and risk tolerance should be considered.

NVIDIA’s A100 GPU uses 108 SMs and 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, delivering up to 312 TFLOPS of dense mixed-precision FP16/FP32 performance and 19.5 TFLOPS of FP64 performance. It supports FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. TF32 enables Tensor Core acceleration for FP32-based AI training without script changes, while FP16 or BF16 mixed precision provides up to twice TF32 throughput.

A100 introduces 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity, which compresses weights and doubles Tensor Core throughput by skipping zero values. Its memory architecture includes 40 GB of HBM2 with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, and 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory per SM. Compute Data Compression can improve DRAM and L2 bandwidth by up to fourfold. Other improvements include asynchronous memory copies and barriers, L2 residency controls, simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, faster atomic operations, hardware JPEG decoding, five video decoders, and optical-flow acceleration.

For HPC, A100 accelerates IEEE-compliant FP64 calculations and mixed-precision iterative solvers. In tests of cuSOLVER’s TCAIRS solver, TF32 provided the strongest convergence and a geometric-mean 2.0× speedup over the FP64 solver, reaching up to 4× for some large complex matrices.

Multi-Instance GPU technology partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute, cache, memory bandwidth, and fault isolation. Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances and support MPS, virtual machines, containers, migration, and multi-tenant workloads.

Third-generation NVLink supplies twelve links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth, twice V100’s total, while PCIe Gen 4 provides 31.5 GB/s per direction for x16 connections and supports SR-IOV. CUDA 11 supports A100 features including Tensor Cores, sparsity, MIG, CUDA Graphs, asynchronous copies and barriers, cooperative groups, and cache controls.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs, six NVSwitches, and 4.8 TB/s aggregate bidirectional interconnect bandwidth. It delivers up to 5 PFLOPS, supports as many as 56 isolated GPU Instances, and is designed to scale from individual workloads to large AI and HPC clusters.

BrainWorking Recursive Therapy is now available in Dunstable for conditions including anxiety, depression, stress and irrational fears. Developed by Terence Watts in 2011, it aims to interrupt reactions before conscious awareness. Practitioner Keith Tunstall offers free consultations and confidential appointments, including via Skype or FaceTime.

TOPIC (Topology-constrained Prediction of Inorganic Crystals) is a crystal-structure prediction algorithm designed to discover oxide solid-state electrolytes with fully connected oxygen corner-sharing frameworks. It reduces the search space by imposing bond-topology and coordination constraints, uses machine-learning interatomic potentials for structural optimization, and applies density functional theory (DFT) for final energy and property evaluations.

TOPIC reproduced known oxide structures containing up to 192 atoms per unit cell, including LLZO after algorithmic modification, and identified previously unreported low-energy polymorphs. Screening representative quaternary oxide systems showed that low lithium ratios, defined as Li atoms divided by non-Li metal atoms, favor corner-sharing frameworks. Among examined structures, 39% of corner-sharing frameworks exceeded the selected high-conductivity threshold at 1000 K, compared with 3% of non-corner-sharing structures.

A broader screening considered 45 quaternary compositions with lithium ratios no greater than 1.0. After structure prediction, stability filtering, machine-learning molecular dynamics, and DFT validation, the study identified 92 candidates with extrapolated room-temperature ionic conductivities above 0.1 mS cm−1. Fifteen low-energy candidates retained conductivities above this threshold in DFT-based simulations. Thirteen contained silicon and five contained hafnium. NASICON-type Li4Hf2Si3O12 had the highest predicted conductivity, 14.09 mS cm−1, a 6.5 eV band gap, and the lowest predicted energy for its composition.

The identified materials include known framework types and novel prototypes with quasi-two-dimensional or three-dimensional lithium pathways. Increasing lithium content generally reduced migration barriers through site distortion and Li–Li interactions, although overcrowding could suppress transport in quasi-one-dimensional channels. Hafnium doping of Li2Ta2SiO8 changed its conduction network from quasi-one-dimensional to three-dimensional and increased predicted room-temperature conductivity from 0.0004 to 0.193 mS cm−1. The present search was limited mainly to quaternary frameworks composed of octahedral and tetrahedral polyhedra; other coordinations, garnet families, quinary systems, and doped materials remain for future study.

NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 30, 2017 reported second-quarter revenue of $2.23 billion, up 56% year over year, and net income of $583 million, up 123%. Diluted earnings per share rose to $0.92 from $0.41, while gross margin increased to 58.4%. Operating income was $688 million, and operating expenses rose 21% to $614 million.

GPU revenue increased 59% to $1.90 billion, supported by gaming, datacenter, professional visualization and cryptocurrency-mining demand. Tegra Processor revenue doubled to $333 million, driven by gaming platforms, services and automotive products. By market, gaming generated $1.19 billion, datacenter $416 million, professional visualization $235 million, automotive $142 million, and OEM and intellectual property $251 million. Intel patent-license revenue concluded in the first quarter.

For the first half of fiscal 2018, revenue was $4.17 billion and net income was $1.09 billion. Operating cash flow totaled $987 million. At July 30, 2017, NVIDIA held $5.88 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, with total assets of $9.40 billion and shareholders’ equity of $5.97 billion.

NVIDIA repurchased five million shares for $758 million and paid $166 million in dividends during the first half. It intended to return $1.25 billion to shareholders during fiscal 2018. Long-term debt was $1.98 billion, and $86 million of convertible notes remained outstanding.

The company continued constructing a new headquarters under an off-balance-sheet lease arrangement with up to $380 million of bank funding. It also continued defending patent litigation brought by Polaris Innovations and recorded no related contingent liability because a loss was not considered probable.

Wireless communication differs from wireline communication because propagation involves fading, motion, reflections, and multiple paths. In free space, electromagnetic field strength decreases as \(1/r\), includes antenna-pattern attenuation, and is delayed by distance divided by the speed of light. Fixed antennas therefore form a linear time-invariant channel similar to a wireline Gaussian-noise channel.

Receiver motion creates Doppler shift, making the channel linear but time varying. A single Doppler shift can be tracked by frequency recovery and is generally manageable. The main difficulty is multipath propagation: signals traveling along paths with different delays and Doppler shifts can reinforce or cancel, causing rapid or “fast” fading. Reflections may also alter distance-based attenuation; for example, a direct path combined with a ground-reflected path can make received power decrease as \(1/r^4\) rather than \(1/r^2\).

Because real environments contain many complex, changing paths and reflectors, directly solving and storing the electromagnetic field is impractical. Ray tracing instead models each path using a time-varying attenuation and propagation delay. The received signal is the sum of delayed, attenuated versions of the transmitted signal.

Such channels cannot be analyzed as ordinary linear time-invariant systems: a sinusoidal input may produce multiple shifted frequencies, so frequency-domain input-output multiplication does not apply. However, they can be represented through time-varying convolution, with an impulse response that changes slowly over time.

At baseband, Doppler shifts appear as time-varying phase terms. Frequency recovery removes an average Doppler shift, leaving differences among path shifts. The Doppler spread—the range between path Doppler shifts—determines how long the channel appears approximately time invariant and how frequently its characteristics must be measured.

Amazon.com closed an $8.25 billion aggregate principal amount debt offering on December 1, 2022, comprising notes due in 2024, 2025, 2027, 2029, and 2032 with interest rates ranging from 4.550% to 4.700%. The aggregate public offering price was $8.246 billion, with estimated net proceeds of approximately $8.235 billion after underwriting discounts and before offering expenses. J.P. Morgan Securities, Barclays Capital, BofA Securities, and SG Americas Securities managed the underwriting. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, officers’ certificate, note forms, and related legal opinion and consent.

After Ontario recognized an 18th-century treaty affirming Haudenosaunee hunting rights in 2013, Six Nations hunters gained regulated access to Short Hills Provincial Park for a six-day annual deer harvest using bows. Government officers and biologists now assist hunters and collect data, reversing earlier conditions in which hunters such as Chester Gibson risked prosecution outside the reserve.

The harvest supports cultural renewal, provides venison and hides, and distributes meat among longhouses, elders and hunters. Participants say it allows younger generations to learn ancestral skills and improves access to traditional food in a community facing high rates of obesity and diabetes. Research cited in the passage associates lean deer and moose meat with better health outcomes.

Protesters oppose hunting in the park, confronting hunters and recording vehicles. Some Indigenous participants and supporting organizations view the protests as attacks on Indigenous culture or racially discriminatory because other regional hunts are not similarly targeted. Protest organizer Liz White says her criticism is directed at the ministry, not the Haudenosaunee, and denies involvement in reported vandalism.

Supporters also argue the harvest benefits the ecosystem. The province estimated about 400 deer in Short Hills in 2016, far above its carrying capacity of 50, and a biologist said deer had damaged vegetation and endangered plant species. Protesters argue some Ontario lands should remain free from hunting so ecological processes can be observed.

Amazon’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2020 reported net sales of $75.45 billion, up 26% year over year, while operating income declined to $3.99 billion and net income fell to $2.54 billion, or $5.01 per diluted share. North America, International, and AWS sales were $46.13 billion, $19.11 billion, and $10.22 billion, respectively; AWS generated $3.08 billion in operating income.

Operating cash flow was $3.06 billion for the quarter and $39.73 billion for the trailing twelve months. Free cash flow for the trailing twelve months was $24.34 billion. At March 31, Amazon had $27.20 billion in cash and equivalents, $22.09 billion in marketable securities, $221.24 billion in assets, $23.44 billion in long-term debt, and $65.27 billion in stockholders’ equity.

COVID-19 increased demand for essential products but reduced discretionary demand, disrupted supply chains, and raised fulfillment, employee, workplace-safety, and shipping costs. Amazon expected these effects to continue through at least the second quarter. Extending server useful lives from three to four years reduced quarterly depreciation by $786 million and increased net income by $602 million.

Amazon disclosed $150.64 billion in contractual commitments and ongoing tax, sanctions, antitrust, and other legal proceedings. It stated that available liquidity and borrowing arrangements should meet anticipated operating needs for at least twelve months.

The speaker described a more defensive game, with two quick goals hurting the team despite a strong first period. The team dominated the third but could not score. Frustrated by the loss, he remained confident about returning home, where the team has played well, and briefly credited his first professional goalie coach.

European Monday spot electricity prices rose to 36 euros/MWh in France and Germany as lower wind output was forecast, while demand remained near 112.5 GW. French nuclear availability stayed at 76 percent. Forward prices were mixed: German 2018 baseload was flat, while French and Czech contracts gained. Coal prices rose, but oil, gas and carbon weakened. RWE shares increased following a buy recommendation.

Sterling Bank increased net loans and advances by 27 per cent to N598.1 billion in 2017 despite an industry trend toward reduced lending. Gross earnings reached N133.5 billion, while non-interest income rose 87.8 per cent to N23.2 billion. Profit before tax increased to N8.606 billion and profit after tax to N8.521 billion. Customer deposits grew 17.1 per cent to N684.8 billion, shareholders’ funds rose 20.2 per cent to N102.9 billion, and total assets reached N1.1 trillion.

Asset quality improved, with the non-performing loan ratio declining from 9.9 per cent to 6.2 per cent. Major lending allocations included N251.59 billion to oil and gas, N70.293 billion to real estate and N19.24 billion to agriculture.

Chief Executive Abubakar Suleiman attributed the performance to prudent loan growth, diversified funding, retail expansion and non-interest banking. The bank launched the Specta online lending platform and invested in process-management technology. Its strategy focuses on agility, digitisation and specialisation, particularly in health, education, agriculture, renewable energy and transportation.

NASA employees and contractors supporting Artemis missions with SpaceX and Blue Origin must continue working during the U.S. government shutdown. Employees will be unpaid during the funding lapse but should record their hours and are expected to receive back pay after reopening. NASA plans to furlough about 15,000 workers while retaining roughly 3,000 part- or full-time staff. It will also support International Space Station operations and satellites already in operation. Artemis II is scheduled to send four astronauts around the Moon in early 2026, Artemis III would use SpaceX to land astronauts near the lunar south pole in 2027, and Artemis V is expected to involve Blue Origin. Neither company has finalized its lunar lander design.

The speakers praise an opposing player’s skating, size, strength, skill, work ethic, leadership, and increased goal scoring. They stress staying alert, maintaining position, and playing physically against him.

Budgens owner Food Retail Operations Ltd entered administration, leaving 27 Prestwick supermarket staff and almost 900 nationwide facing uncertainty. Administrators will continue trading all 34 stores while seeking buyers. Former owner Co-Op may intervene if none is found. Booker declined to comment on whether Tesco’s proposed acquisition affected the store.

March gasoline demand reached a record 9.6 million barrels per day, while high exports and falling inventories pushed the national average price up two cents to $2.55. Prices were 26 cents higher than a year earlier. Hawaii and California remained the most expensive markets, while several Southern states had the cheapest gas. Inventories stayed above 85 million barrels and may rise as Motiva’s Texas refinery resumes processing.

Neo Performance Materials appeared attractive because of its low 6.1x EV/EBITDA valuation and expected growth in neodymium demand from permanent magnet motors used in electric and automated vehicles. Its Magnequench segment, a leader in rare earth magnetic powders, generated 46.7% of 2017 revenue and 72.8% of EBITDA.

However, two patents covering most Magnequench products expired in December 2017. Their expiration could allow competitors to produce similar products without compensation, potentially increasing lower-priced competition and reducing Neo’s revenue and earnings from 2018 onward. Although other patents or new products might limit the impact, the risk was considered too significant and uncertain to justify an investment position.

The team ran out of energy as injuries mounted, including Donovan’s sprained MCL and Robyn’s ankle injury. The speaker praised the officials, congratulated Tampa and Jay, called Tampa a great team, and expressed pride in the players despite the loss.

Kashmiri student Aftab said 15–20 people assaulted him and a friend after prayers in Mahenderhgarh. Police registered an FIR, while Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Mehbooba Mufti urged Haryana to investigate and take stringent action.

The team was outplayed defensively and allowed skilled opponents to capitalize on power plays. Despite several scoring chances, they lost control. The goalie performed sharply after months out, but received insufficient support.

The author contrasts Nicaraguan students demanding civil liberties with Canadian campus activists seeking protection from challenging views. Citing Lindsay Shepherd’s treatment at Wilfrid Laurier University after showing a Jordan Peterson debate, the author argues that identity politics and political correctness have undermined academic freedom. The passage says these attitudes have spread to workplaces and expanded harassment investigations beyond legal requirements. Not every complaint, unpleasant exchange, rude management style, performance critique, or disciplinary action constitutes harassment. Complaints must meet an objective materiality threshold, while stress requires a medically qualifying condition to constitute a disability. Employers may address poor performance and suspected abuse of leave, which otherwise may create resentment among other employees.

Microsoft’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2015 reported quarterly revenue of $23.8 billion, operating income of $6.0 billion, net income of $5.0 billion, and diluted earnings per share of $0.62. These declined from $26.5 billion, $7.8 billion, $5.9 billion, and $0.71, respectively, in the prior-year quarter. Revenue and operating income were affected by a $1.7 billion net Windows 10 revenue deferral and unfavorable foreign currency movements.

For the six-month period, revenue was $44.2 billion, operating income $11.8 billion, net income $9.6 billion, and diluted earnings per share $1.20. Operating cash flow totaled $14.2 billion. At December 31, 2015, Microsoft had $102.6 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments; $180.1 billion in total assets; $41.4 billion in long-term debt including the current portion; and $76.8 billion in stockholders’ equity.

Microsoft reported through three segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. Quarterly Intelligent Cloud revenue rose to $6.3 billion, while Productivity and Business Processes revenue declined to $6.7 billion and More Personal Computing revenue declined to $12.7 billion. Commercial cloud annualized revenue exceeded $9.4 billion, Office 365 Consumer subscribers reached 20.6 million, Windows 10 ran on more than 200 million devices, and Xbox Live monthly active users reached 48 million.

During the six months, Microsoft repurchased $7.6 billion of common stock and paid $5.3 billion in dividends. It issued $13.0 billion of debt securities in November 2015. The company completed 12 acquisitions for $782 million and continued a phone restructuring plan expected to eliminate up to 7,800 positions by June 30, 2016. Aggregate accrued legal liabilities were $560 million, with approximately $1.5 billion of additional adverse outcomes considered reasonably possible.

The Nigerian Immigration Service told an Abuja court that suspended Supreme Court Justice Sylvester Ngwuta illegally used two similar standard passports interchangeably. An official said a replacement was issued after Ngwuta declared the first missing, but he failed to return it after recovery. Six passports—four diplomatic and two standard—were found in his possession, though forensic analysis showed no forgery. Justice John Tsoho adjourned the trial until October 20.

The Tri State Psychology Conference will celebrate its 25th anniversary April 20 at West Liberty University. Founded at Marshall University in 1993, it gives psychology students professional conference experience. The free regional event has included up to 25 schools and is supported by Psi Chi grant funding.

NES Global Talent seeks an Aberdeen-based Performance Specialist for a six-month onshore contract with a global operator. Responsibilities include PSCM performance management, planning, reporting, compliance, risk and assurance. Candidates need finance, accounting and procurement knowledge, strong analytical and communication skills, and advanced Excel expertise.

Martin Braithwaite left Middlesbrough for Bordeaux in January to improve his chances of regular football and selection for Denmark’s 2018 World Cup squad, where Viktor Fischer was a key rival. The author considers the decision understandable but disappointing, suggesting Braithwaite could instead have fought to earn a place under Tony Pulis and potentially helped Boro gain promotion. His move will be vindicated if he succeeds at the World Cup, while Middlesbrough could show him what he missed by reaching the play-offs and returning to the Premier League.

Russia’s foreign ministry said U.S. missile defence systems in Romania and planned installations in Poland violate the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty. Washington says the sites protect against rogue states, while Moscow argues they target Russia’s nuclear arsenal.

The Texas Rangers are focusing their managerial search on internal candidate Skip Schumaker, their special adviser and the 2023 National League Manager of the Year. Chris Young said formal interviews have begun, with no external candidates yet considered. Schumaker joined Texas in November after managing Miami for two seasons. He would replace Bruce Bochy, who departed after his three-year contract ended following an 81-81 season. Bochy, a four-time World Series champion with 2,252 career wins, has been offered a Rangers advisory role.

Las Vegas Valley residents had until 10 p.m. April 18 to postmark 2016 tax returns. The Postal Service advised using sufficient postage, clear addresses, sealed envelopes and retaining mailing receipts.

Vernon defeated Wenatchee 3-1 to take a 2-0 series lead, with Ty Taylor improving his playoff numbers to a 1.65 goals-against average and .942 save percentage. Wenatchee, which led the league in regular-season scoring, has managed only two goals through two games.

Penticton beat Trail 7-2 for a 2-0 lead, scoring five times on seven power plays. Owen Sillinger recorded a hat trick, while Ethan Martini received a five-minute major for a blow to the head.

Powell River won 3-2 in Victoria to lead its series 2-0. Kings goaltender Matteo Paler-Chow stopped 40 of 41 shots, while Victoria’s Zachary Rose made 29 saves. The Grizzlies had only one power play despite outshooting Powell River 41-32.

Surrey rebounded from a 9-1 opening loss to defeat Prince George 3-2 and even the series. Mario Cavaliere made 46 saves as Surrey was outshot 48-19. Desi Burgart, Aaron White and John Wesley scored for the Eagles.

Surrey defenceman Jackson Ross committed to Colorado College for the fall. The Colorado native became the sixth Eagles player this season to earn a scholarship.

LLMs may help social scientists generate hypotheses and theories, but concerns about originality, validity, falsifiability, and oversimplified representations of human behavior require nuanced human oversight. Effective human-AI collaboration should combine automation with human intuition and use LLMs as complementary research tools.

Generative AI is transforming sectors including finance, healthcare, and education while creating risks such as misinformation, deepfakes, bias, discrimination, and malicious jailbreaks. Existing laws, corporate principles, and industry initiatives aim to protect rights, inclusiveness, safety, transparency, and accountability, but governance remains difficult because technology evolves rapidly, risks may emerge only through real-world use, and governments and industry lack shared understanding and international consensus.

The passage calls for forward-looking, human-centered governance that balances innovation with risk mitigation. It recommends partnerships among industry, academia, and policymakers; stronger communication and international cooperation; and frameworks combining top-down regulation with bottom-up reporting by developers, researchers, users, and communities. Governments and companies should create transparent channels to identify incidents, investigate risks, update regulations promptly, and monitor regulatory needs in specific communities.

Because #HV ignores interrupt shadows, guests should execute HLT with interrupts disabled without first examining pending interrupts. Hosts should immediately re-enter halted guests when interrupts or non-maskable events are pending, and resumed guests should examine interrupt state as after #HV.

The #HV doorbell page is configured through GHCB VMGEXIT code 0x8000_0014. Guests may request a preferred physical address, must set a page when Restricted Injection is enabled, and may query existing configuration. Guests should relinquish page access with PVALIDATE before host mapping, access mapped pages with C=0, and use the page assignment protocol before reusing an old location with C=1.

Hosts must emulate APIC interrupt presentation and lifecycle semantics. When an interrupt becomes ready, the host writes the highest-priority vector to PendingEvent while the vCPU is not running. It sends #HV only when no vector was already pending and NoFurtherSignal was zero, then sets NoFurtherSignal. Hosts track presented vectors, acknowledgements, in-service state, and whether explicit EOI is required. Non-maskable events are indicated through PendingEvent flags and trigger #HV only when NoFurtherSignal was previously clear.

Guests receiving #HV must be prepared for APIC interrupts. They must atomically exchange PendingEvent with zero before acting on a vector, may dispatch immediately or defer until permitted, and must validate vectors. For EOI, guests atomically clear NoEoiRequired; if it was already zero, they must perform an APIC register write through VMGEXIT. Non-maskable events must remain dispatchable when EFLAGS.IF=0, with atomic clearing of their flags and NoFurtherSignal. Non-cooperative behavior may cause lost notifications or denial of service, but does not compromise host integrity or corrupt guest state.

ASTROCO is a conformer-style encoder for self-supervised representation learning from irregular stellar light curves. It combines multi-head self-attention, depthwise convolutions with Gated Linear Units, and gated feed-forward networks to model long-range dependencies, local phenomena, and adaptive information flow. Magnitudes and uncertainties are concatenated with sinusoidal time embeddings, projected into a shared representation, and processed using residual connections and normalization. Trainable softmax weights mix hidden states from all layers before masked mean pooling.

Pretraining uses masked reconstruction on 50% of sequence positions, including masked, randomly replaced, and unchanged values. Zero placeholders prevent leakage from masked or padded inputs. On the MACHO R-band dataset, both ASTROCO-S and ASTROCO-L achieved lower reconstruction errors and higher macro-F1 classification scores than Astromer v1/v2. The smaller model outperformed prior work with less training time and hardware, while the larger model produced the strongest overall benchmark and transferred effectively to few-shot classification.

The lecture develops combinatorial bounds and algorithms for gluing polygon boundaries into convex polyhedra using gluing trees. A combinatorial gluing type records the abstract tree, its junctions, and which polygon vertices or edges meet there, while ignoring exact positions along edges. This removes infinities caused by rolling belts.

For a polygon with \(n\) vertices, a gluing tree has at most \(n+4\) leaves because edge fold points contribute \(180^\circ\) curvature and total curvature is \(720^\circ\). After controlling degree-two junctions, the tree has \(O(n)\) nodes. Counting tree structures, vertex-or-edge assignments, and labels gives an upper bound of \(2^{O(n)}\) combinatorial gluings. A highly spiked star polygon supplies \(2^{\Theta(n)}\) valid gluings, even when only whole edges are glued, establishing a matching exponential lower bound.

For bounded-sharpness polygons, every reflex angle is at most \(360^\circ-\gamma\) for a fixed positive constant \(\gamma\). Every gluing-tree leaf then contributes at least \(\gamma\) curvature, so there are at most \(720/\gamma\) leaves. Accounting for branching nodes, degree-two junctions, and rolling belts yields polynomially many combinatorial gluings; a stated bound is \(n^{2L-2}\) for \(L\) leaves.

An edge-to-edge dynamic-programming algorithm uses subproblems defined by polygon boundary chains from \(V_i\) to \(V_j\). Trying each possible edge paired with the first edge divides a subproblem into two smaller ones. Enumerating all solutions takes exponential time, matching the possible output size. For decision, retaining only the solution minimizing the angle glued at the endpoints gives an \(O(n^3)\) algorithm.

For arbitrary gluings, subproblems must also allow a vertex to meet an edge and represent intervals of possible positions along that edge. “Zip” and “tug” operations reduce these cases to smaller subproblems. This enumerates general gluings in exponential time and becomes polynomial for bounded-sharpness polygons. No polynomial decision algorithm is known for unrestricted polygons.

Examples include a cross with 85 gluings producing 23 distinct polyhedra, including the cube, and rolling-belt families for equilateral triangles and squares.

The team played solidly and created chances but brief defensive lapses led to quick goals they could not recover. They remain confident but must play consistently, as the opponent capitalizes on chances and defends well. Scoring will require sustained pressure, deep play, and getting pucks to the net.

The coach said his team played poorly against Anaheim, committing turnovers, mishandling the puck, losing defensive coverage and struggling against an aggressive, physical forecheck. Despite the late loss, he considered the game winnable and expected improved execution, support in the defensive zone and adherence to the game plan. He criticized the ineffective five-on-three power play and noted extra contact around goaltender Ray Emery, saying he would seek clarification from league officials about permitted play. He planned to give his established lines time to respond against Anaheim’s checking unit and strong defensemen. He also discussed drafting Getzlaf and Perry, praising their competitiveness and development, and said Jason’s performance must return to its earlier playoff level.

The ninth Carlsberg UK Northamptonshire Food and Drink Awards celebrated county producers, dining venues and culinary workers at Northampton’s Royal & Derngate on November 15. The event opened with William Sitwell leading a tribute to chef Antonio Carluccio OBE, who had died the previous week. Five venues were also recognised through the Eat Out Eat Well healthy-choice scheme.

Major winners included The Hopping Hare for Booker Food Pub of the Year, The Folly for Restaurant of the Year and Great Service, Workbridge Coffee Shop for Independent Café/Tea Room, The Exotic Dining for Spice Restaurant, and The Dukes Arms for Community Pub. Richard Walker of Fawsley Hall Hotel won Chef of the Year, while Victoria Austin of Highgate House won Young Chef of the Year. Other awards went to local producers, farms, workplaces and drinks businesses. Steve Reid of Friars Farm was named Local Food Hero, Tom Warner and Christina Warner-Keogh received the F&B Achiever award, and Alaric Neville of Phipps NBC received the Chairman’s Award.

Girlfriends is preparing corsages, tuxedos and other accessories for Liberal High School’s April 22 prom and several nearby schools. Staff help students select flowers, ribbons, stones and matching details. Work began around March 1 because flowers ordered from Arkansas take time to arrive. The shop has received nearly 100 orders, including 20 to 30 tuxedo and corsage orders in recent days. Kenna McNeil said demand is steady, with many students ordering two weeks before prom, and urged students to order soon.

Fishermen clashed with police in central Vietnam while attempting to sue Taiwanese firm Formosa for compensation over a 2016 toxic waste spill that devastated fish stocks and livelihoods. Activists reported beatings, hospitalizations and brief detentions. Formosa paid Vietnam’s government $500 million, but the fishermen said they had received nothing.

Digital leaders use relevant data and detailed metrics to set goals, track progress, and evaluate performance, supplemented by 360-degree reviews. Clear, measurable objectives promote adaptation, autonomy, experimentation, innovation, and creative risk-taking rather than rigidly constraining employees.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K dated July 19, 2016, announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2016. The related press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act. Chief Accounting Officer Frank H. Brod signed the report.

The Colchester-Milton Rotary Club joined Dealer.com, Vermont Gas, the Intervale Center and U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to plant saplings at Pine Island Farm along the Winooski River, supplementing a 2014 restoration project. The trees are intended to absorb greenhouse gases and reduce erosion. The effort fulfills Rotary International president Ian H.S. Riseley’s challenge to plant one tree per member during the Rotary year. The 45-member club had previously planted five larger trees at Porters Point School to provide shade and hopes to organize similar projects in Milton next year.

The paper reviews twelve shared tasks organised by NFDI4DS, a German consortium supporting FAIR, transparent, reproducible, sustainable, and interoperable research data infrastructure for data science and AI. Shared tasks promote community engagement, methodological comparison, standardisation, collaboration, and reusable datasets and tools, often through venues including SDP, NSLP, CLEF, SemEval, and ISWC.

Seven completed tasks address software mention extraction, scientific visual question answering, climate-claim verification against scholarly literature, research-field classification, multilingual subject tagging, ontology learning with large language models, and question answering over scholarly knowledge graphs. Reported competitions produced datasets and benchmarks, attracted participating teams, and explored methods including multimodal models, retrieval-generation pipelines, multilingual LLMs, hybrid machine-learning approaches, and multi-source question answering.

The ongoing CLEF 2025 CheckThat! task focuses on detecting science-related discourse in tweets and retrieving scientific papers implicitly referenced by online claims.

Four tasks are under development. One will detect dataset and machine-learning model mentions in scholarly articles using GSAP-NER corpora. ReadMe2KG will extract entities from GitHub README files and link them to the NFDI4DS knowledge graph. CURED, planned for 2026, will evaluate clinical prognosis models that provide predictions and calibrated uncertainty estimates. Algorithm2Domain is developing a community-based meta-benchmarking platform for algorithm generalisability, domain adaptation, FAIR benchmarking standards, and shared knowledge development.

Together, these tasks apply community-based evaluation to scholarly information processing and support the broader NFDI mission across disciplines.

The Triangle Offense creates distinctive defensive challenges because its options depend on defensive positioning. Traditional NBA defenses generally deny inside play, congest the three-second area, force perimeter shots, and use “show and recover,” physical cut denial, weakside help, trapping, and quick closeouts. Against post feeds, defenders pressure the post, defend baseline cuts, disrupt splits, and attack dribbles. On screens and rolls, defenders show, fight over screens, recover, and pack the weakside.

SOS disruption applies more aggressive pressure to interrupt the Triangle’s initial flow. It may extend three-quarter or full court to lengthen passing lanes and move the offense away from normal operating areas. Defenders pressure ballhandlers toward sideline or baseline checkpoints, deny return passes, front the post, occupy Helpside “I” positions, sag and switch on post splits, and use contact switches against screens.

All Out SOS Disruption traps the wing immediately after the first pass, forcing the offense into freelance play. Other defenders rotate into “Triangle I” help positions and cover likely outlets. On passes out of traps, the nearest defender closes out while teammates rotate to deny the post and protect help areas. Baseline drives, post feeds, and corner passes trigger specified traps and rotations, which must begin as the ball leaves the passer’s hands.

The Motley Fool Money highlights the no-annual-fee Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card for unlimited 2% cash rewards, a $200 bonus after spending $500 in three months, and 0% introductory APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers. It also offers up to $600 in cell phone protection and Visa Signature Concierge service. The recommended credit score is 670–850, though approval is not guaranteed.

Alternative offers include the Capital One Quicksilver card, with unlimited 1.5% cash back, select travel rewards, welcome bonuses, and a 15-month introductory APR; and a Citi card offering up to 2% cash back, a $200 bonus, and an 18-month balance-transfer introductory APR. Motley Fool receives advertiser compensation but states that compensation does not influence product ratings.

Hollywood hopes an early summer season led by “Avengers: Infinity War” and “Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom” will revive a box office down nearly 3 percent after 2017 ticket sales hit a 25-year low. Numerous sequels and established franchises are scheduled, but reporter Ben Fritz warns that oversaturation forces tent-poles to compete for the same audience and can produce more flops. Competition from Netflix and the concentration of revenue among a few films, including “Black Panther,” are also intensifying pressure.

Studios are emphasizing variety alongside blockbusters. Universal is offering action films, independent dramas and documentaries, while Warner Bros. has female-led movies, comedies and “Crazy Rich Asians” rather than a major live-action DC release. Other summer offerings include female-led remakes, action movies, unconventional comedies and horror, Sundance breakouts and original projects such as the dystopian thriller “Hotel Artemis.” Industry figures say theatrical business now spans the full year, discerning audiences require diverse choices, and distinctive films with strong personalities may provide an alternative to formulaic sequels and reboots.

Free-agent wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. accepted a six-game NFL suspension for violating the performance-enhancing drugs policy after failing a test last season. Beckham denied knowingly taking a banned substance and said the league cited elevated testosterone levels. He will be eligible to play in Week 12 and hopes to return this season. Beckham was released by Miami in December after recording nine catches for 55 yards in nine games.

Wall Street surrendered early gains as rising Treasury yields and declining technology shares outweighed strong corporate earnings. Inflation concerns increased after the Federal Reserve’s statement and economic data showing a tight labor market, higher factory prices and rising labor costs. The Dow gained 0.14%, while the S&P 500 fell 0.06% and Nasdaq dropped 0.35%. Financial stocks rose 1.0%, benefiting from higher rates. eBay surged 13.8% after earnings and plans to replace PayPal as its main payments partner, while PayPal fell 8.1% and UPS declined 6.1%. Analysts projected 14.9% fourth-quarter S&P 500 earnings growth, with 79.7% of reporting companies beating estimates. After hours, Amazon rose over 6%, Alphabet fell nearly 3% and Apple declined about 1% following results.

The UK Competition and Markets Authority designated Google Search with Strategic Market Status after a 10-month investigation, enabling targeted interventions under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act. Potential measures include offering rival search options, fair ranking principles, greater data portability, and requiring permission to use publishers’ content in AI Overviews without affecting search visibility. The designation covers Search features including News, Top Stories, and Discover, but excludes Google News and Gemini. The CMA says Google handles over 90 percent of UK general searches, while UK firms spent more than £10 billion on its search advertising in 2024. Google warned that proposed interventions could hinder innovation, delay products, and raise business costs. Implementation may take months, and the CMA could impose broader restrictions than the EU, particularly concerning AI integration.

This study examined whether increased, cognitively engaging physical education improves attention among 75 students in Classes 6 and 7. Participants were assigned by class to experimental or control conditions; Class 6 received four weekly PE hours, while Class 7 received two. Activities included agility drills, coordination circuits, volleyball, badminton, and strategic games. Attention was assessed in October and December using the Bells Test, measuring detection speed over 30 seconds and sustained attention over 120 seconds.

Experimental groups in both classes significantly improved 30-second attention speed, while control groups showed no significant changes. Sustained attention improved significantly only in the Class 6 experimental group. The findings suggest that increased PE hours may particularly benefit short-term attention, with four weekly hours producing stronger results than two. However, the study did not establish which specific activities caused the improvements. Limitations included possible effects from schedules, fatigue, and extracurricular activities, restricted applicability beyond the studied age group, and uncertainty regarding activity-specific effects. Further research is needed on long-term outcomes and particular PE content.

NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU targets HPC, AI, analytics, and data-center workloads with higher compute, memory, interconnect, and virtualization capabilities than Tesla V100. Its 108 streaming multiprocessors deliver peak FP64 throughput of 19.5 TFLOPS, 2.5 times V100, while third-generation Tensor Cores support FP64, TF32, BF16, FP16, and mixed-precision computation. In cuSOLVER iterative-refinement tests, TF32 provided the fastest and most robust mixed-precision results, averaging a 2.0× speedup over an FP64 solver and reaching up to 4× for large complex matrices.

A100 introduces 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity, retaining two nonzero values per four entries. Sparse matrix instructions skip zero values, doubling Tensor Core throughput while compressed weights halve data footprint and bandwidth. NVIDIA’s process of dense training, structured pruning, and fine-tuning produced virtually no inference-accuracy loss across evaluated networks.

The GPU includes 40 GB of HBM2 with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, and 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory per SM. L2 bandwidth is 2.3 times V100, while compute data compression can improve DRAM and L2 bandwidth by up to fourfold. SECDED ECC protects HBM2, caches, and register files. Separate FP32 and INT32 cores permit simultaneous execution, while asynchronous memory copies, barriers, larger shared memory, cache-residency controls, and fewer Tensor Core instructions improve efficiency and strong scaling.

Multi-Instance GPU technology partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory-system resources. It provides predictable quality of service, fault isolation, and support for virtual machines, containers, multiple users, and Compute Instances with MPS. Instances can be migrated between compatible GPU partitions to consolidate workloads or service hardware.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth, twice V100’s total. A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, enhanced fault handling, five NVDEC units, five-core hardware JPEG decoding, an optical-flow accelerator, and faster FP16 and FP32 atomic operations.

CUDA 11 supports A100 features including Tensor Cores, sparsity, MIG, task graphs, asynchronous copies and barriers, L2 residency controls, and Cooperative Groups. CUDA Graph optimizations reduce launch and execution latency, while persistent L2 caching can accelerate repeatedly accessed data.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs through six NVSwitches, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS and 4.8 TB/s total bidirectional interconnect bandwidth. MIG can expose up to 56 isolated accelerators in one system. The platform includes CUDA, container tooling, NGC software, deep-learning frameworks, inference, analytics, and HPC applications, and can scale from individual workloads to large clusters.

Rockwood School District in Missouri keeps students in grade-level classrooms for whole-class phonics and comprehension instruction, then uses flexible, needs-based groups for reteaching, enrichment, and targeted interventions. Lessons incorporate movement, multimodal teaching, scaffolded support, complex tasks for advanced readers, and daily independent or partner reading.

The district argues that fixed ability grouping can limit exposure to grade-level vocabulary and comprehension strategies, making it difficult for struggling students to catch up. In 2024–25, Rockwood kindergarteners exceeded national proficiency averages in every measured skill group, sometimes by more than 17 percentage points, while first and second graders surpassed national averages in nearly every domain. Rockwood attributes these outcomes to strong universal instruction combined with strategic support, while acknowledging the model may not suit every setting.

The study examines 2015–2025 Times Higher Education World University Rankings trends for the top five higher education institutions in ten populous Asian countries: Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Pakistan, the Philippines, Russia, Thailand, and Vietnam. Using a qualitative multiple-case design and document analysis, it evaluates whether institutions’ rankings rose, declined, or remained stable. Two external evaluators reviewed the analysis.

Chinese institutions showed the strongest and most consistently improving performance, with most selected universities reaching the global top 50 by 2025. Japanese institutions remained prominent, particularly the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, while several others recovered after fluctuations. Russian institutions generally maintained stable, comparatively strong rankings. Indian institutions mostly improved, although their positions remained below those of leading Chinese, Japanese, and Russian institutions.

Institutions in Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, and Vietnam generally experienced declining or weak ranking trends. Pakistani institutions showed inconsistent patterns without a clear overall direction. Bangladeshi institutions entered the rankings only recently and generally maintained neutral positions, limiting longitudinal analysis.

Overall, most selected Asian institutions lagged behind international competitors and lacked stable positive ranking patterns, except those in China, Japan, and Russia. The study recommends stronger international research, teaching, and exchange networks; improved global marketing and public relations; expanded government funding; and overseas offices supported by appropriate financial and legal policies.

The research is limited to five institutions in each selected country and uses only THE rankings. It recommends that future studies include more Asian countries and institutions and examine other recognized ranking systems.

A global study found neonicotinoids in 75% of 198 honey samples, with 45% containing multiple compounds. Exposure was highest in North America. These insecticides can impair bees’ brain function, colony growth, and pollinator health.

China announced it will close its domestic ivory market by the end of 2017. Elephant populations have fallen sharply as poachers exploit exceptions for ivory obtained before the 1989 international ban. Conservationists say reducing demand in China, the world’s largest ivory market, is essential to curbing poaching. China plans to redirect ivory carvers to museum pieces or other projects and educate the public about ivory trading’s effects. The decision may encourage other ivory-trading countries to adopt similar bans.

Open source communities demonstrated that software and distributed-systems development are collaborative endeavors. Distributed-system patterns provide technology-independent design blueprints, capture prior experience, establish shared terminology, and enable reusable components implemented across languages through containers and HTTP interfaces.

Containers create boundaries for resources, ownership, and concerns. Even applications on one machine benefit from multiple containers through resource isolation, modular team ownership, reuse, independent deployment, and easier testing. Three single-node patterns are described:
- **Sidecar:** augments an application container, such as by adding HTTPS, synchronizing configuration, monitoring processes, or updating code from Git.
- **Ambassador:** brokers external communication, including routing to database shards, discovering services across environments, and splitting traffic for experiments.
- **Adapter:** converts an application’s interface to a standard one for monitoring, logging, or health checks.

Reusable containers should be parameterized, expose stable APIs, and document ports, configuration, ownership, and versions. Environment variables, Dockerfile directives, and standardized labels support these goals.

Microservices divide applications into independently maintained services communicating through defined APIs. They improve team autonomy, release agility, and independent scaling, but make architecture and debugging more difficult. Distributed patterns help address these challenges.

Replicated load-balanced services provide availability and horizontal scaling, particularly for stateless workloads. Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching uninitialized instances, while session tracking can route a user consistently to one replica. Additional replicated layers can provide caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination.

Sharded services divide state among servers when one machine cannot hold or serve all data. Sharded caches improve memory utilization but can lose capacity or performance when a shard fails. Replicating each shard improves resilience and permits independent scaling. Applications can access shards through client-side ambassadors or shared routing services, with trade-offs in deployment complexity, scaling, latency, and network use.

The disclosure describes configurable hardware for implementing Deep Neural Network activation functions efficiently using programmable lookup tables. Calibration data is processed by a hardware representation, and inputs to each activation module are monitored to determine the expected input range. Lookup data approximating an activation function over that range is then generated and loaded into the hardware, improving table utilization and accuracy while reducing area and power demands.

Input ranges may be based on observed minima and maxima or probability distributions. Values outside the calibrated range may be clamped to boundary outputs or handled by extrapolation. A programmable offset may center inputs before lookup. Tables may store function samples or curve parameters and support linear or quadratic interpolation, using input most significant bits for addressing and remaining bits for interpolation. Separate stores can hold alternating entries for simultaneous retrieval, while dual datasets allow one activation function to be loaded during execution of another.

Calibration may be repeated for each activation function, processing stage, or activation module. A dedicated ReLU path may bypass and disable the lookup table to reduce power, or clamp inputs before table processing. The described CNN hardware also includes convolution engines, accumulators, normalization and pooling modules, buffers, and memory interfaces.

The methods and hardware may be implemented through software, firmware, programmable logic, integrated circuits, computer-readable instructions, or integrated-circuit definition datasets. Manufacturing systems may process hardware descriptions into circuit layouts and fabricate corresponding integrated circuits.

Teach For America argues that high-dosage tutoring can improve student achievement while developing future teachers. Its Ignite Fellowship has trained more than 5,500 virtual tutors across over 40 communities, producing accelerated growth in math and reading. The program emphasizes structured training, ongoing coaching, curriculum alignment and technology that expands rather than replaces relationships. Research found that Ignite tutoring nearly triples participants’ likelihood of applying to TFA’s teacher program, particularly among men, people of color and non-education majors. Since launch, 550 fellows have joined TFA’s teaching corps. The author urges policymakers and educators to treat well-supported tutoring as both an instructional strategy and a long-term teacher pipeline.

The lecture examines renormalization and Sudakov logarithms in soft-collinear effective theory (SCET), beginning with the heavy-to-light \(b\to s\gamma\) current. One-loop contributions separate into infrared terms matching QCD, ultraviolet divergences canceled by operator counterterms, and finite matching terms. The counterterm contains both \(1/\epsilon^2\) poles and logarithms. In this process, external kinematics fix the collinear momentum label \(\omega\) to \(m_b\), so the Wilson coefficient remains outside loop integrals.

Differentiating the renormalization factor yields a finite anomalous dimension containing a regular term and a logarithmic term governed by the cusp anomalous dimension. The cusp term produces the leading logarithms. With fixed coupling, solving the renormalization-group equation gives a Sudakov exponential that sums terms with one coupling per double logarithm. In QCD, running coupling modifies the exponent into a function of coupling ratios. Logarithmic accuracy is classified using \(\log C\): leading-log terms scale as \(\alpha_s^k L^{k+1}\), next-to-leading-log terms as \(\alpha_s^k L^k\), and subsequent orders contain progressively fewer logarithms. Leading-log accuracy requires tree-level matching and the one-loop cusp anomalous dimension; higher accuracy requires higher-loop cusp and regular anomalous dimensions and eventually loop-level matching. Varying the hard matching scale estimates truncation uncertainty.

The cusp originates from intersecting ultrasoft Wilson lines associated with the heavy-quark and lightlike collinear directions. A lightlike cusp produces a single logarithm in the anomalous dimension to all perturbative orders, while its coefficient receives loop corrections. Related double poles also arise when collinear Wilson lines terminate on quark fields.

Momentum labels are fixed by external kinematics when an operator contains only one building block for each collinear direction, producing multiplicative renormalization. When multiple fields share one collinear direction, some momentum combinations enter loop integrals, and renormalization becomes convolutional. Such operators generate evolution equations including DGLAP, Brodsky–Lepage, and equations relevant to deeply virtual Compton scattering.

The lecture then introduces inclusive deep-inelastic scattering in the Breit frame. For generic Bjorken \(x\), the incoming proton is collinear while the final state is hard, enabling hard-collinear factorization. Matching the forward electromagnetic-current product onto leading-power quark and gluon SCET operators produces structures associated with quark and gluon parton distribution functions. Forward matrix elements constrain one momentum-label combination, while the remaining combination describes the parton momentum fraction and includes quark and antiquark contributions. The next lecture will use these operators to derive the DIS factorization theorem and its renormalization-group evolution.

The review examines evolving models and quality issues in higher education. COVID-19 accelerated online learning, highlighting the importance of technological infrastructure, digital literacy, instructional design, instructor competence, student support, social interaction, institutional resources, and gender-sensitive approaches. Studies also emphasize leadership spirituality, proactive change management, stakeholder engagement, organizational resilience, and strategic planning as contributors to institutional quality.

Broader themes include quality assurance frameworks, accreditation, university rankings, internationalization, service quality, student and faculty expectations, equity and inclusion, academic freedom, faculty development, career preparation, entrepreneurship, and recognition of informal learning. Emerging technologies—including virtual platforms, artificial intelligence, big data, and Industry 4.0 curricula—offer opportunities for access, collaboration, innovation, and efficiency while presenting challenges involving privacy, inequality, reliability, and resistance to change.

The review concludes that higher education publications and scholarly communication are shifting toward open access, collaborative digital platforms, inclusivity, accessibility, and agility. It calls for critical engagement, strategic adaptation, and collaboration among scholars, institutions, publishers, administrators, faculty, students, and policymakers.

Platinum futures are standardized, leveraged contracts used for speculation, diversification, and hedging. CME contracts represent 50 troy ounces, trade under symbol PL, have a $0.10-per-ounce minimum fluctuation equaling $5 per contract, and settle through physical delivery. Platinum prices are volatile and influenced by supply and demand, industrial uses, production costs, economic and political events, and developments in major producers such as South Africa and Russia.

A platinum strategy should use defined entry, exit, position-sizing, and risk-management rules supported by backtesting, while considering profitability and portfolio correlation. One combined long-short backtest recorded 473 trades, a 64% win rate, 0.57% average gain, and 1.7 profit factor. A seasonal strategy recorded 60 trades, a 75% win rate, 0.66% average gain, and 2.3 profit factor. Platinum has historically performed better during winter and spring in the cited analysis.

Investors can access platinum through futures, CFDs, ETFs, stocks, options, or physical metal. Futures leverage can magnify gains and losses, while CFDs avoid delivery and contract-expiry concerns. The passage identifies platinum’s historical futures high as $2,308.80 in March 2008 and low as $267.10 in July 1985.

The President vetoes House bill No. 7864, which would exclude most immigrants over 16 unable to read and write, subject applicants to a literacy test, restrict certain cross-border foreign labor, and penalize employers. He argues that literacy does not reliably indicate desirable citizenship or protect against disorder, that family exceptions are incomplete and unclear, and that unemployment stems largely from economic depression. He also contends that labor restrictions would disrupt beneficial relations along the northern border, invite retaliation, and use language too indefinite for criminal law. He concludes that the bill is unnecessarily harsh, oppressive, poorly constructed, and harmful to citizens.

Kyle Busch earned his third consecutive 2018 NASCAR Cup victory at Richmond, matching Kevin Harvick’s streak and securing a likely playoff place. Despite his momentum, Busch worries about peaking too early. He credits his short-track experience with Kyle Busch Motorsports for an advantage. Busch expects extending the streak at Talladega to be difficult because restrictor-plate racing is unpredictable.

Biosecurity software screens DNA orders for hazardous proteins, but AI-modified toxins and viral proteins can evade existing filters. Researchers tested about 76,000 AI-generated variants of 72 harmful proteins and found that software patches substantially improved detection, including for fragmented genes, though about 3 percent remained unflagged. The study was entirely computational, so whether the variants remained functional is unknown. Experts said malicious protein orders are extremely rare but screening remains an important safeguard.

In October 1944, representatives of the United States, Great Britain, and China informally discussed dissolving the League of Nations and transferring its functions to the United Nations. The United States, not a League member, awaited initiatives from League members. The League’s Supervisory Committee later arranged for a Conciliation Committee to confer with a United Nations group. U.S. officials made no commitments, pending plans for a United Nations Conference. The recommended policy was for the United States to take no initiative unless Britain or China proposed another procedure.

At a January 31, 1945 meeting with representatives of certain American republics, Acting Secretary Grew emphasized progress on the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals before the Mexico City Conference and invited further discussion. The Chilean Ambassador requested clarification of earlier minutes, stating that respect for international treaties was considered essential, although its placement among the organization’s purposes and principles remained undecided.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K dated May 10, 2018, reporting the release of financial results for the quarter ended April 29, 2018. Exhibits include the first-quarter fiscal 2019 earnings press release and CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress. The materials are furnished rather than filed and are not incorporated into other SEC filings.
Roma are reportedly interested in signing Manchester United winger Adnan Januzaj as a potential replacement for Liverpool-bound Mohamed Salah after his disappointing Sunderland loan.

Boston leads the global life sciences industry through abundant lab space and billions in venture capital and federal research funding. However, federal funding cuts and threats to higher education are challenging the foundations of the region’s biotech-driven prosperity.

Hurricane Katrina devastated New Orleans’ Lower Ninth Ward in 2005, displacing residents and accelerating abandonment, development and gentrification. Since then, the city has adopted measures including evacuation centers, elevated homes, solar panels, rain gardens and safer methods for growing food in contaminated areas.

The Greater New Orleans Urban Water Plan seeks to address flooding and subsidence by replacing reliance on pumping with infrastructure that captures and gradually absorbs water, including parks, ponds, redesigned streets and the planned Mirabeau Water Garden.

Across Louisiana, wetlands are disappearing rapidly, increasing flood risks. The state’s 2017 Coastal Master Plan proposes $50 billion in projects to restore barrier islands, wetlands and marshes, build levees and flood gates, elevate homes and relocate some residents.

Oil and gas extraction contributes to coastal subsidence, while rising global sea levels are expected to become Louisiana’s greatest future threat. Researchers believe the state’s adaptation efforts could provide lessons elsewhere, though poorer communities may have fewer resources to become resilient.

The cup and handle is a bullish continuation chart pattern formed during an uptrend. It consists of a rounded U-shaped cup following a rally and a handle that typically drifts slightly downward. The pattern completes when price breaks above the handle’s resistance, preferably with increased volume. Typical criteria include a 30–50% cup retracement and a handle that remains above the cup’s halfway depth.

Volume generally declines during the cup and handle, then rises during recovery and breakout. Traders may confirm the pattern with moving averages, RSI, MACD, broader market conditions, and fundamental analysis. A projected target is calculated by adding the cup’s depth to the breakout level. Stop-loss orders may be placed below the handle’s low or the cup’s bottom.

The inverted version forms in a downtrend and signals bearish continuation. A double cup and handle contains two successive cups before the final breakout. Formation may take several months to more than a year, while the handle often lasts weeks or months. High volatility can distort the formation and produce false signals, whereas low-to-moderate volatility may make it clearer.

Common mistakes include trading before confirmation, ignoring volume and market context, setting unsuitable targets or stops, and relying solely on the pattern. Backtest evidence is inconclusive: one 2016–2018 S&P 500 test underperformed the index, while Thomas Bulkowski reported a 26% failure rate, falling to 10% after waiting for an upside breakout, and an average gain of 38%. The passage concludes that strict, fully quantified profitability has not been established.

O’Reilly Media published Brendan Burns’s 2018 copyrighted work, with print and online purchasing options. The publisher and author disclaim responsibility for errors, omissions, damages, and compliance with applicable software licenses or third-party intellectual property rights.

Higher-order self-energy corrections contain loop integrals that behave logarithmically and diverge at infinite momentum, producing unphysical infinite results. Introducing a cutoff preserves sensible calculations but leaves an infinite high-energy contribution. Renormalization absorbs corrections into bare masses and coupling constants, allowing predictions at the finite scales where experiments occur. Physical masses and electromagnetic, weak, and strong couplings depend on the energy scale and therefore “run.” These couplings do not appear to converge at very high scales, but new particles and interactions could alter their running and potentially unify them at a particular scale.

The study introduces NL2GeoSQL and presents GeoSQL-Eval, an end-to-end automated framework for evaluating large language models on PostGIS query generation. It addresses limitations of existing SQL and geospatial coding benchmarks, which do not comprehensively assess PostGIS-specific syntax, functions, spatial semantics, schema linking, execution, and robustness.

GeoSQL-Eval covers conceptual understanding, structured SQL generation, semantic alignment and function invocation, execution accuracy, and robust generalization. Its benchmark, GeoSQL-Bench, contains 14,178 tasks: 2,380 multiple-choice and true/false questions, 7,488 explicit and underspecified syntax-generation tasks, and 4,310 explicit and underspecified schema-retrieval tasks. Data were derived primarily from 340 functions and 756 examples in the PostGIS 3.5 manual. Schema-retrieval tasks span eight thematic categories and 82 databases based on UN-GGIM and ISO 19115 classifications. GPT-4o assisted with controlled task generation, followed by dual expert review and adjudication.

Generated queries are parsed, executed in PostGIS, and evaluated using metrics for syntax validity, execution success, table and field identification, function and argument matching, geometric and non-geometric result accuracy, repeated-generation success, stability, robustness, resource use, and error types. Entropy weighting produces overall rankings. Twenty-four models and strategies across six categories were tested, with each generation task repeated five times.

General non-reasoning and reasoning-enhanced models performed best overall. GPT-5, o4-mini, and DeepSeek-R1-0528 ranked highly across dimensions, while o4-mini achieved the strongest balance of accuracy, stability, and efficiency. SpatialSQL ranked second on schema-level evaluation and entered the overall top five. Larger SQL-specialized models, particularly XiYan-SQL-32B, substantially outperformed smaller models. Syntax accuracy was often high but did not ensure successful execution. Semantic function selection and parameter matching remained major weaknesses, and schema-retrieval tasks were substantially harder than syntax-level generation.

Repeated generation improved success rates, especially for reasoning-enhanced models; o4-mini approached 90% pass@5 on syntax-level tasks. However, underspecified prompts caused substantial accuracy declines, revealing weak handling of ambiguity. PostGIS function and SQL syntax errors dominated failures, while geometry parsing and SRID or dimensional mismatches occurred less frequently but increased in schema-based tasks.

The study publicly releases a GeoSQL-Eval leaderboard. Identified limitations include incomplete coverage of PostGIS functions, emphasis on vector processing, exclusion of many extensions and other spatial databases, and limited model coverage. Future work may expand functions, systems, models, modalities, and continuous evaluation infrastructure.

The lecture proves the induced graph removal lemma, which states that a graph with few induced copies of a fixed graph \(H\) can be made induced-\(H\)-free by adding or deleting few edges. The usual regularity-lemma proof fails because induced subgraphs involve both edges and non-edges, so irregular pairs cannot simply be deleted.

A strong regularity lemma resolves this obstacle. It produces nested partitions \(P\) and \(Q\), where \(P\) is regular, \(Q\) is an extremely regular refinement, and their energies are close. A corollary yields large subsets \(W_i\) inside partition classes \(V_i\) such that every pair \(W_i,W_j\), including self-pairs, is regular, while most corresponding densities in \(V_i,V_j\) and \(W_i,W_j\) are close.

For induced removal, low-density class pairs are emptied and high-density pairs are completed. This changes only a small number of edges. If an induced copy of \(H\) remained, the counting lemma applied to the regular \(W_i\) sets would produce many induced copies in the original graph, contradicting the hypothesis.

The same framework gives a colored removal lemma and an infinite removal lemma for possibly infinite families of forbidden induced subgraphs. In property testing, removal lemmas justify randomized testers that sample a constant number of vertices. The infinite removal lemma implies that every hereditary graph property is testable with one-sided error by an oblivious tester.

Senator Sherwin Gatchalian urged DepEd to streamline clearance processing and resolve longstanding delays in teachers’ performance-based bonuses. Teachers had not received 2016–2017 bonuses, with DepEd citing failed biddings and delayed clearances despite funding allocated in fiscal year 2016.

The passage compares dollar-cost averaging—investing fixed amounts regularly regardless of market conditions—with lump sum investing, which invests the full amount immediately. Dollar-cost averaging reduces concern about short-term volatility, while lump sum investing provides earlier market exposure and more time for growth. The article backtests a lump sum buy-and-hold approach using an equally weighted, diversified portfolio spanning U.S. and foreign stocks, U.S. bonds, U.S. REITs, and global commodities. It concludes that historically, remaining invested over long horizons, preferably at least ten years, offers a higher probability of success. Earlier investment produced greater total profit in the cited backtests, and financial crises became less significant over longer periods. The choice between approaches also depends on individual preferences and risk tolerance.

Apple entered an underwriting agreement on February 2, 2015, with Goldman Sachs and Deutsche Bank Securities for $6.5 billion of senior unsecured notes. The offering comprises $500 million of floating-rate notes due 2020 and fixed-rate notes totaling $6 billion, with interest rates from 1.55% to 3.45% and maturities from 2020 to 2045. Floating-rate interest is payable quarterly, while fixed-rate interest is payable semiannually. The notes rank equally with Apple’s other unsecured, unsubordinated debt. The Form 8-K, signed by CFO Luca Maestri on February 9, 2015, includes the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, note forms, legal opinion, and earnings-to-fixed-charges calculation.

NeoWorld is a framework for constructing infinitely expandable, interactive virtual worlds from a single image. It initially represents scenes with lightweight, object-centric 2.5D Gaussian layers, then progressively converts nearby or user-selected foreground objects into full 3D models. This hybrid approach aims to balance computational efficiency, visual immersion, viewpoint consistency, and object-level interaction.

The system uses panoptic segmentation and compact codebook embeddings to bind instance semantics to Gaussian primitives. New views are generated through iterative scene reconstruction, rendering, and inpainting, while cross-view matching maintains object identity. Reconstructed 3D objects undergo coarse and fine alignment for position, rotation, and scale. Unreliable reconstructions revert to 2.5D representations. A large language model interprets natural-language commands to select objects and specify translations, rotations, animations, or physical parameters.

Experiments compare NeoWorld with world-generation, video-diffusion, object-segmentation, and dynamics methods. NeoWorld achieved higher human-rated 3D consistency and scene quality than WonderJourney and WonderWorld, while maintaining an 18.14-second novel-view generation time. Its object-centric representation reached 70.53 IoU against manually annotated masks, outperforming OmniSeg3DGS and GaussianGrouping. For dynamic animation, it achieved a human PromptAlign score of 61.95 and a VideoCLIP score of 17.05, exceeding the compared video models. Ablations indicate that joint optimization, KNN smoothing, the compact codebook, and both alignment stages improve performance or efficiency.
