NeoWorld is a cascade of pretrained external modules rather than an end-to-end model. Its limitations include propagated upstream errors, alignment failures, language-model misinterpretation, image-to-3D errors under occlusion or complex textures, and segmentation errors affecting reconstruction.

Former president Robert Mugabe returned to Zimbabwe amid worsening tensions with President Emmerson Mnangagwa’s government following the June 24 Bulawayo bombing, which killed two and injured more than 40. Mnangagwa said he suspected Mugabe-aligned Generation 40 members were behind the alleged assassination attempt, though police were still investigating and he acknowledged having no evidence. Mugabe’s family reportedly dismissed the allegations.

Relations deteriorated after the military intervention that forced Mugabe to resign in November. Mugabe has called Mnangagwa’s administration illegitimate, demanded a return to constitutionalism, and has been linked to opposition groups ahead of the July 30 election. Mugabe’s nephew Patrick Zhuwao warned British Prime Minister Theresa May that Mnangagwa might use the bombing to justify a crackdown on opponents. Former minister Jonathan Moyo also accused the administration of growing paranoia.

News coverage on June 4–5, 2001, focused heavily on California’s energy crisis. Southern California natural-gas prices remained unusually high amid limited pipeline capacity, low storage, growing demand and allegations that companies manipulated gas and electricity markets. El Paso and Southern California Gas denied accusations of inflating prices. Federal regulators considered transaction disclosures, pipeline-capacity price caps and broader scrutiny of energy trading.

The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission introduced a price-mitigation plan based on generators’ production costs during tight supply periods. Critics, including Governor Gray Davis, argued it contained loopholes, excluded many out-of-state transactions and should apply throughout the Western United States. California’s Senate authorized subpoenas seeking pricing and bidding records from eight power companies, including Enron, while potentially seeking records from Los Angeles and state agencies.

PBS’s “Frontline” documentary “Blackout” examined deregulation, alleged market manipulation, corporate profits and Enron’s role as a major energy trader. Reviews praised its depth but differed over whether it unfairly emphasized Texas-based companies. Houston’s PBS station adjusted its pledge-drive schedule to air the documentary promptly.

Indian and international lenders met to preserve Enron’s $2.9 billion Dabhol power project amid unpaid bills, tariff disputes and termination threats. Indian lenders, with substantial exposure, sought continued support and government intervention. Separately, Marathon replaced Enron in a Saudi natural-gas venture after Enron withdrew, reflecting Enron’s increasing focus on commodity trading rather than infrastructure.

Other Enron mentions concerned a Connecticut fuel-cell funding dispute, a yen-denominated securities offering, possible involvement in Georgia-Pacific mill purchases, newsprint trading, retail-energy policy, and White House adviser Karl Rove’s Enron stock holdings.

Dr. Maria Pane is a GBMC neonatologist who cares for critically ill newborns and involves parents in treatment discussions. She values her collaborative team and supports the annual Father’s Day 5K fundraiser benefiting the neonatal intensive care unit.

The Federal Reserve raised its federal funds target range by 0.25 percentage points to 1–1.25 percent, its second increase in six months and third since rates remained near zero for seven years after the 2007 financial crisis.

Tuberculosis commonly affects the lungs but can also occur at extrapulmonary sites, particularly lymph nodes and pleura. Standard treatment uses rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol, although extrapulmonary TB treatment remains less studied and generally follows pulmonary TB regimens.

The study developed a whole-body physiologically based pharmacokinetic model to simulate time-dependent concentrations of all four first-line drugs, including distribution to pleural fluid and lymph nodes. The model comprised 17 tissue compartments governed by 18 ordinary differential equations and incorporated blood and lymph flow, tissue partitioning, absorption, clearance, and rifampicin reabsorption. Slow and fast isoniazid acetylators were modeled separately. Parameters were calibrated using plasma and lung concentration data and validated against independent data.

The model generally reproduced plasma, lung, and pleural concentrations, although it overpredicted rifampicin in pleural fluid. Rifampicin exceeded its critical concentration in all simulated sites, while isoniazid exceeded its threshold in all compartments but was eliminated faster in rapid acetylators. Ethambutol did not reach its critical concentration in the brain, kidney, bone, or skin. Pyrazinamide remained below its critical concentration or MIC in all simulated compartments. Limited cerebrospinal fluid penetration suggested possible overprediction of brain concentrations for rifampicin and ethambutol.

Limitations included the use of a single consolidated lymph-node compartment, scarce tissue data, omission of drug interactions, rifampicin autoinduction, age-dependent pharmacokinetics, disease-related pharmacokinetic differences, immune effects, and drug synergy. The model provides a starting point for evaluating and optimizing extrapulmonary TB treatment, but additional in vivo data are needed to validate predictions at extrapulmonary sites.

Microsoft’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2017 reported revenue of $24.5 billion, up from $21.9 billion a year earlier, operating income of $7.7 billion, and net income of $6.6 billion, or $0.84 diluted earnings per share. Service and other revenue rose to $10.2 billion, while product revenue declined to $14.3 billion. Commercial cloud revenue increased from $3.2 billion to $5.0 billion.

Operating cash flow was $12.4 billion. Microsoft ended the quarter with $138.5 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments; $249.1 billion in total assets; $159.5 billion in liabilities; and $89.6 billion in stockholders’ equity. The company repurchased $1.6 billion of shares and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.42 per share.

Segment revenue was $8.2 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $6.9 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $9.4 billion for More Personal Computing. Segment operating income was $3.0 billion, $2.1 billion, and $2.6 billion, respectively. LinkedIn contributed $1.1 billion in revenue.

Microsoft adopted new revenue-recognition and lease-accounting standards effective July 1, 2017, restating prior periods. The changes increased previously reported September 2016 quarterly revenue by $1.5 billion and net income by $977 million, while recognizing operating lease assets and liabilities on the balance sheet.

Unearned revenue totaled $24.9 billion, and contracted revenue not yet recognized was $59 billion. Long-term debt, including its current portion, had a carrying value of $77.3 billion. The effective tax rate was 18%. Microsoft reported $371 million in accrued legal liabilities and approximately $1.1 billion of additional reasonably possible exposure. Deloitte reported no material modifications were needed for the interim financial statements.

Researchers harmonized South Korea’s CRCS-K and Taiwan’s TREAT-AIS registries into the K-T collaborative EVT registry, comprising 9,941 patients treated with endovascular thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke. Taiwanese patients were older, had more vascular risk factors and severe strokes, experienced longer treatment timelines, and achieved less 90-day functional independence than Korean patients. Successful recanalization and symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage rates were broadly similar, while mortality was higher in the Korean cohort.

Age strongly influenced outcomes, particularly between 75 and 85 years. Patients aged 80 or older had lower functional recovery and recanalization rates and higher mortality than younger patients, but symptomatic hemorrhage did not significantly differ by age. Pre-stroke independence and baseline stroke severity consistently modified outcomes; bridging thrombolysis also predicted improved outcomes among elderly patients.

The findings do not support excluding patients from thrombectomy solely because of age, as some carefully selected elderly patients achieved favorable outcomes. The registry’s strengths include its large, multinational, prospectively collected dataset, while limitations include differing registry methods, enrollment periods, unavailable detailed imaging and post-discharge data, and retrospective analyses. Future work should refine thrombectomy strategies and incorporate imaging, longitudinal follow-up, and regional care differences.

Amazon’s unaudited Form 10-Q covers the quarter ended June 30, 2022. Q2 net sales rose 7% year over year to $121.2 billion, while operating income fell from $7.7 billion to $3.3 billion. Amazon reported a $2.0 billion net loss, or $0.20 per share, compared with $7.8 billion in net income in Q2 2021. The loss included a $3.9 billion valuation loss on its Rivian investment.

For the first six months, sales increased 7% to $237.7 billion, operating income declined to $7.0 billion, and net loss was $5.9 billion. AWS sales grew 33% in Q2 to $19.7 billion and generated $5.7 billion in operating income. North America recorded a $627 million operating loss, while International recorded a $1.8 billion loss.

Operating cash flow for the trailing twelve months declined to $35.6 billion. At June 30, Amazon had $37.5 billion in cash and equivalents, $23.2 billion in marketable securities, $419.7 billion in assets, $58.1 billion in long-term debt, and $131.4 billion in stockholders’ equity.

Amazon acquired MGM for approximately $6.1 billion in cash and assumed and repaid $2.5 billion of debt. It agreed to acquire One Medical for approximately $3.9 billion. The company repurchased $6.0 billion of stock and had $6.1 billion remaining under its authorization.

Amazon completed a 20-for-1 stock split on May 27, 2022. Extending server and networking equipment useful lives reduced first-half depreciation by $1.9 billion and benefited net loss by $1.5 billion. Increased fulfillment, transportation, wages, incentives, supply-chain constraints, inflation, foreign exchange movements, and normalization from pandemic demand affected results.

This study examined how pharmacological pupil dilation affects retinal image gradability and AI-based diabetic retinopathy (DR) detection using a portable Phelcom Eyer camera. Retinal images from 327 patients were captured before and after dilation with tropicamide. Certified ophthalmologists assessed image quality and DR, while a ResNet-200d model trained on the mydriatic mBRSET dataset classified images as normal or DR.

Mydriasis produced significantly more gradable images than non-mydriatic imaging: 1,056 images (82.1%) versus 699 (55.6%; P<0.001). In non-mydriatic imaging, systemic hypertension, older age, longer diabetes duration, male gender, and Indigenous race were associated with reduced gradability.

AI analysis included 597 paired images. The model achieved 82.91% accuracy, an F1 score of 0.83, and an AUC of 0.94 for mydriatic images, compared with 79.23%, 0.79, and 0.93 for non-mydriatic images. Mydriatic imaging produced fewer false positives but slightly more false negatives. Overall performance differences were not statistically significant (P=0.3279).

The findings indicate that mydriasis improves portable-camera image quality and may modestly improve AI screening performance, particularly by reducing false positives. However, dilation may be impractical in resource-limited settings. Limitations included operator learning effects, selection bias from paired-image analysis, reduced sample size, and use of one dataset and camera model.

The lecture introduces probabilistically checkable proofs (PCPs) and previews computationally sound arguments. A PCP transforms a witness into a polynomially sized oracle proof that a randomized polynomial-time verifier checks by querying only a few, typically nonadaptive, locations. Completeness requires valid instances to have an accepted proof, while soundness bounds acceptance of every proof for invalid instances. The verifier normally reads the full instance, though PCPs of proximity relax this.

The stated goal is a PCP for every NP language with completeness 1, soundness 1/2, and polylogarithmic randomness and query complexity; stronger known results require only three queries. For cryptographic applications, the proof must also be efficiently computable from the instance and witness.

The construction focuses on 3SAT and unfolds the GKR protocol. For each layer of a shallow, suitably uniform verification circuit, the prover records the low-degree extension of all gate values. It also records every possible transcript of each sumcheck protocol for each layer, evaluation point, and partial verifier-randomness sequence. The verifier uses this oracle as a fixed GKR prover, checking the output and following randomly selected sumcheck paths down to the input layer.

Parameters are chosen so the field size is polylogarithmic while the expanded transcript remains polynomial in the circuit size. Soundness follows from GKR and a union bound over the \(2d\) sumchecks: with individual error proportional to \(3m|H|/|F|\), choosing \(|F|>12dm|H|\) yields soundness below 1/2. Completeness is 1, and randomness and query complexity are polylogarithmic. A low-degree test is additionally required for the input witness extension because, unlike ordinary GKR, the verifier does not possess the witness.

The paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI), Big Data (BD), and advanced analytics (AA) interact within digital business platforms and enterprise transformation. It defines AI as a digital innovation powered by data and analytics to improve decision-making, products, services, business models, competitiveness, and operational performance.

Using literature from 2010–2019 and semi-structured interviews with Russian National Technology Initiative experts, the study develops a multidimensional taxonomy and maturity framework. Digital business platforms are organized into seven overlapping areas: information systems, customer experience, data and analytics, Internet of Things, ecosystems, trust, and integration platforms.

The proposed AI/BD/AA micro-level value chain covers data acquisition and preparation, data curation and quality management, storage and interpretation, and data-driven decision-making and usage. The enterprise maturity framework identifies five stages of human-machine interaction:

1. Human-led, initial analytics  
2. Human-led and machine-supported, Advanced Analytics I  
3. Machine-led and human-supported, Advanced Analytics II  
4. Machine-led and human-governed, Advanced Analytics III  
5. Machine-controlled, Advanced Analytics IV  

The framework is intended to help organizations assess AI readiness, automation opportunities, platform capabilities, and investment priorities across industries and functions. The paper emphasizes that successful AI transformation requires changes in people, processes, technology, data readiness, leadership, skills, ecosystems, and business models. It also stresses the need for broad participation in establishing ethical norms to reduce unintended commercial and societal consequences.

Image registration aligns moving and fixed images through affine and deformable coordinate transforms but becomes computationally and memory intensive at ultra-high resolutions. Existing approaches reliably handle roughly 50 million warp parameters, while high-resolution brain scans may require over 11 billion.

The paper introduces Flash Fused Distributed Primitives (FFDP), which applies IO-aware fused operations and distributed processing to large-scale registration. It identifies three major bottlenecks: deformable interpolation and warp composition, localized normalized cross-correlation (LNCC), and mutual information (MI). A composite implicit grid sampler avoids materializing coordinate grids, an implicit Parzen-windowing implementation computes MI histograms in shared memory, and a fused LNCC kernel reduces intermediate storage. These components support problems up to 64 times larger than existing algorithms on one GPU.

For multi-GPU registration, Grid Parallel shards images, deformation fields, and optimizer states while synchronizing boundaries for convolutional operations. A distributed ring sampler circulates image shards and accumulates interpolation results without gathering the full moving image on every GPU. Distributed MSE, LNCC, and MI losses aggregate local computations across hosts.

FFDP accelerated traditional registration pipelines by up to 7.48 times while reducing memory use by up to 59%, and deep-learning pipelines by up to 6.14 times with up to 24% less memory. It registered a 250 µm in-vivo MRI to a 100 µm ex-vivo FLASH brain volume in about one minute on eight NVIDIA A6000 GPUs, optimizing over 11 billion parameters. On the simulated 250 µm faux-OASIS dataset, it improved Dice and inverse-weighted Dice while reducing Hausdorff distance and requiring up to 500 times fewer GPU-hours than alternatives. Ablations showed that fused kernels substantially lowered memory and runtime, while boundary synchronization prevented artifacts.

The Georgia Court of Appeals affirmed Robert Pearl Bryson’s convictions for aggravated sodomy, aggravated child molestation, child molestation, and failure to register as a sex offender.

Testimony and recorded interviews described Bryson’s sexual contact with two boys, ages eight and ten. The court held this evidence sufficient to support the aggravated sodomy convictions, noting that sodomy requires contact, not penetration. Evidence that Bryson kissed the ten-year-old on the mouth, considered alongside other molestation evidence, supported the jury’s finding of sexual intent and the child molestation conviction.

Bryson had registered as a sex offender in Stephens County after a North Carolina conviction but left Georgia for more than a year without notifying local authorities. The court found this sufficient to support his failure-to-register conviction, rejecting his argument that the state had to prove a change of domicile or identify his precise new residence.

The court upheld denial of Bryson’s motions to quash the indictment. The sheriff’s wife’s service on the grand jury did not render it unlawfully constituted, and Bryson’s challenge to Count 8’s form was untimely. It also upheld denial of appointed counsel’s motion to withdraw four days before trial because counsel was prepared and substitution would have delayed proceedings.

Severance of the registration charges was unnecessary because Bryson’s flight connected those charges to the molestation offenses and provided circumstantial evidence of guilt. The case was not too complex for the jury to evaluate each count separately.

Bryson failed to preserve his objection to admission of his North Carolina no-contest plea. The plea was admissible to establish a conviction for registration purposes, and the jury was instructed not to treat it as an admission of guilt or similar-transaction evidence.

Finally, Bryson waived his ineffective-assistance claim by declining to pursue it in the trial court despite a warning and an opportunity to present evidence.
EUR/USD rose for a fourth session toward 1.1840 as the dollar weakened after US inflation data. Traders await ECB and FOMC minutes for guidance on QE tapering and balance-sheet reduction.

The Mississippi Supreme Court affirmed Ulysses S. Gandy’s second manslaughter conviction and ten-year sentence arising from a 1976 collision that killed three occupants of another car. Although testimony conflicted, sufficient evidence supported the jury’s findings that Gandy was intoxicated, drove into the wrong lane on a straight, unobstructed highway, and thereby acted with culpable negligence causally connected to the deaths.

The Court upheld refusal of Gandy’s proposed intoxication instruction because other instructions adequately presented the issue and the proposed factors required only ordinary judgment. It also upheld admission of three sketches showing the vehicles and debris as personally observed by witnesses shortly after the collision. Unlike sketches improperly admitted at Gandy’s first trial, these did not reconstruct the collision but illustrated witnesses’ observations. Finally, the Court rejected Gandy’s claim that jurors should have received a food or refreshment recess during their approximately two-hour-and-fifty-minute deliberations, noting they could have requested one and Gandy cited no supporting authority.

Texas Instruments warns that improper ESD handling can cause performance degradation or complete integrated-circuit failure. Revision A, dated May 2025, changes ADS8685W and ADS8689W from Advance Information to Production Data. Mechanical, packaging, ordering, material, RoHS, finish, moisture sensitivity, reflow, and marking information is current but subject to change. Preproduction parts may be incomplete, altered, discontinued, and sold without warranties. TI relies partly on third-party material information and limits related liability to the annual purchase price of affected parts. Technical resources are provided “as is” for skilled developers, who are responsible for product selection, application design, validation, testing, and compliance. Resource use is restricted to developing applications using the described TI products, and TI products remain subject to applicable terms of sale.

The CS5535 Revision A3 update documents multiple silicon issues and workarounds:

- Simultaneous IRQ and SSMI events may allow trapped I/O to complete before SSMI signaling; SSMIs are unreliable.
- UDMA fails if IDE bus mastering is enabled before sending the PIO command packet; send the packet first.
- GPIO[27:24] wake inputs do not work from ACPI S3; use PWRBTN# and, if needed, external OR circuitry.
- An extended CMOS RAM write followed immediately by a legacy RAM read can return incorrect data; no resolution is provided.
- Block and demand-mode legacy DMA can block LPC I/O; use single-transfer mode.
- USB controller register reads may fail while idle if clock gating is enabled; disable clock gating.
- Unexpected IDE interrupts can reset bus mastering during ATAPI transfers; revised drive firmware avoids the observed case.
- Reading Port 60h incorrectly clears AuxOutputFull; use interrupts for PS/2-emulated USB keyboard and mouse management.
- tACK settings do not affect IDE_DACK setup timing, which remains 30 ns and meets requirements.
- WORD-aligned PRDs may hang ATAC; require DWORD alignment.
- LPC transactions may abort after turnaround, discarding writes or returning all ones on reads; a PLD workaround is available.
- SMB NEGACK behavior is inconsistent; clear it with two specified writes to SMB_STS.
- GLPCI retry counting includes unrelated PCI retries; increase or disable the retry limit.
- After suspend, atomic writes to GPIO high-bank feature registers clear unselected bits; use read-modify-write.
- SMBus data hold timing is noted against the 300 ns SMB 2.0 requirement.
- LOWBAT_FLAG may not be set after an abnormal low-battery standby transition; no resolution is provided.
- Excessive sleep-control delays can prevent SLEEP_X, SLEEP_Y, PCI, and IDE signals from reactivating; program those delays below PM_SED.

The study developed an extended age-structured SIR model linking Google Community Mobility Reports (GCMRs) to SARS-CoV-2 transmission. It assumed activity changes were linearly related to transmission-relevant contacts in four settings—workplaces, transit stations, grocery and pharmacy, and retail and recreation—while temperature and Alpha and Delta variants multiplicatively affected infection risk. Region- and week-specific parameters represented transmission outside these settings. The model was fitted to weekly hospitalizations in 11 Norwegian and 21 Swedish regions from February 2020 to July 2021, accounting for vaccination and variants, and separately to Bavaria and Berlin through December 2020.

The model attributed 60.0% of infections in Sweden and 38.7% in Norway to the four GCMR settings, with substantial regional variation. Transit stations and workplaces had the largest estimated contributions at pre-pandemic activity levels, followed by retail and recreation and grocery and pharmacy. A 20°C temperature increase was associated with about a 40% reduction in transmissibility. Delta approximately doubled transmissibility relative to the wildtype, while Alpha showed a modest increase only in Norway.

In Berlin and Bavaria, GCMRs accounted for 65.2% of infections. Retail and recreation contributed most there, followed by transit and workplaces. A 20°C temperature increase reduced modeled transmission probability by about half.

The analysis found a clear association between GCMRs and infection dynamics, but interpretation was limited by assumptions of linear and time-constant activity-contact relationships, uniform seasonal and variant effects across settings, simplified vaccination immunity, fixed epidemiological parameters, and possible GCMR measurement error. The authors suggest direct, real-time measurements of contact frequencies could better explain transmission.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2-MSPS data-acquisition system with per-channel input clamps, programmable-gain amplifiers, selectable input ranges and low-pass filters. Inputs tolerate swings to ±18 V; clamp current must remain below ±10 mA. Its common-mode rejection circuitry supports up to ±12 V by default and can be configured by channel and input mode.

Conversion data is available in straight-binary or two’s-complement format. The device requires a continuous differential or lower-power single-ended sampling clock; stopped clocks invalidate output data and clocks. SMPL_SYNC synchronizes channel sampling and frame alignment across multiple devices. An internal low-drift reference can be bypassed with 10 µF and disabled when using an external reference.

The source-synchronous interface supports two or four lanes in SDR or DDR modes. Each 20-bit result is transmitted MSB-first in a 24-bit packet with six trailing zeroes. Optional output randomization reduces correlation between interface ground bounce and analog input signals. Simple averaging improves SNR while halving output rate; moving averaging preserves the output rate. Fixed, ramp, and alternating test patterns support interface debugging.

Reset and power-down are controlled through pins or registers. Initialization requires prescribed register writes with a free-running sampling clock. Speed-boost mode converts one selected channel pair at up to 8 MSPS while the other six channels remain idle.

Configuration uses 16-bit registers in three banks through 24-bit SPI frames. Register reads require enabling read mode, while multiple devices can be configured and read through an SPI daisy chain.

In an ATE example, post-calibration TUE is 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. Low-noise bandwidth reaches 22.7 kHz, while wide-bandwidth mode reaches 700 kHz and settles to 99.95% full scale in 7.5 µs. The device uses 5-V analog, 1.8-V core, and I/O supplies without a required power-up sequence. Recommended layout practices include close bypass and reference capacitors, short ground connections, and separation of analog paths from digital lines and noise sources.

Despite a historically poor offensive performance, the Patriots remained within seven points of Miami late. Stephen Gostkowski then attempted what Jon Gruden called “the most bizarre onside kick,” which the Dolphins recovered to secure the win.

Reports on Enron and the energy sector focused on California’s power crisis and India’s Dabhol project. California records showed that numerous public and private suppliers charged high electricity prices in early 2001; some criticized companies, including Enron, Dynegy, Duke and Mirant, charged below the state’s average. Failed refund negotiations led a federal judge to propose hundreds of millions to potentially $1 billion in refunds, far below California’s $8.9 billion demand. Investigators also sought generator pricing documents, with Duke disputing public release of confidential bidding data and California authorized to share documents from Reliant, Mirant and Dynegy with Oregon and Washington.

Dabhol Power CEO Neil McGregor resigned after his contract expired amid a prolonged payment dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board. Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay met Indian officials but reached no resolution. He said Enron remained committed to India and hoped for a quick settlement, while India rejected a proposed central-utility buyout. Construction on Dabhol’s second phase had stopped because of payment defaults and suspended financing. Enron also sought assistance from the Confederation of Indian Industry, while lenders considered appointing a new engineering consultant.

Separately, Enron Broadband Services participated in Tropic Networks’ $60 million financing. Despite Enron’s California exposure, stalled asset sale, broadband losses and Dabhol difficulties, analysts largely rated its stock a buy and expected it to meet second-quarter earnings targets.

Grief is a highly personal emotional response to losing someone or something important, including bereavement, declining health, retirement, caregiving responsibilities, or leaving a long-term home. Its effects, duration, and coping process vary according to factors such as personality, life experience, and the circumstances of the loss.

Grief may begin before an expected death, allowing time to prepare and say goodbye while creating pressure to remain strong. Moving home can also cause grief, particularly after a partner’s death or when separation from possessions and support networks increases loneliness. If possible, major decisions about moving should be delayed for several months after bereavement.

Grief does not follow fixed stages. People may move repeatedly between numbness, denial, relief, yearning, restlessness, sleep disturbance, loss of confidence, guilt, anger, sadness, and depression. Recounting what happened may help someone accept the death. Feelings such as sensing the deceased’s presence, regret, or relief after prolonged illness can be normal.

There is no set duration for grief, and time alone does not remove the loss. However, intense grief usually lessens, with good days eventually outnumbering bad ones. Support from friends and family can help; those experiencing depression or needing additional assistance should contact a GP, specialist, or bereavement-support organisation.

Accepting the presidential nomination, the speaker presents the election as a choice between Republican principles of limited government, individual freedom, economic growth, lower taxes, and military strength, and Democratic policies he characterizes as promoting taxation, spending, inflation, dependency, and weakness abroad.

He blames previous Democratic leadership for economic decline, high inflation, interest rates, taxes, poverty, and weakened defense. He credits his administration with reducing inflation and interest rates, cutting taxes and spending growth, creating jobs, encouraging investment, strengthening the military, restoring alliances, and renewing national confidence. He advocates a balanced-budget amendment, a line-item veto, tax simplification and reductions, tuition tax credits, enterprise zones, anticrime legislation, voluntary school prayer, and continued defense preparedness.

On foreign policy, he supports NATO, Israel, anti-Communist allies in Latin America, the Grenada intervention, and nuclear-arms reductions negotiated with the Soviet Union. He argues that military strength preserves peace.

The speaker rejects bigotry and antisemitism, emphasizes individual dignity, human life, independence, and restrained government, and welcomes disaffected Democrats. Concluding with stories of the Olympic torch and the Statue of Liberty, he celebrates America’s diversity, opportunity, freedom, and hopeful future.

Beating the offside trap requires attackers to recognize defenders moving forward, remain onside when passes are made, avoid interfering if caught offside, and exploit the space behind the defense. Effective tactics include dribbling instead of passing, properly timed through passes, horizontal, checking, deep-lying, bending, or delayed runs, short or back passes, possession play, and designated non-runners on free kicks. Timing and communication between the passer and receiver are critical. Attackers should also identify when a defender fails to move up, leaving players onside. Successfully defeating the trap can create a one-on-one opportunity with the goalkeeper and may discourage defenders from using it again.

Ocean acidification harms many shell-building organisms by reducing available carbonate ions. Researchers found that periwinkles exposed to predicted 2100 conditions lowered their metabolism but accelerated shell production, creating less-dense inner shells and less-soluble, more resistant shells. These changes suggest some calcifying organisms may adapt to increasingly acidic oceans.
The court reversed Roldán’s judgment and acquitted him, applying the reasoning from nearly identical case No. 2037. Justice Wolf did not participate.

China blacklisted Canadian research firm TechInsights and nine subsidiaries after its analysis of Huawei AI chips raised questions about Western export controls. The restrictions prohibit Chinese organisations from conducting business, collaborating, or sharing data with the firm. The move reflects tighter Chinese control over technology information and growing geopolitical barriers to independent semiconductor research and supply-chain transparency.

Researchers led by Vanderbilt University’s Joshua Caldwell improved the hyperlensing potential of hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) by producing crystals with 99 percent isotopically pure boron. Natural boron’s two isotopes degrade infrared optical properties. Purification reduced optical losses, tripled the lifetime and travel distance of surface phonon polaritons, and increased potential imaging resolution roughly tenfold. The researchers calculate that lenses made from the material could image objects as small as 30 nanometers, including some viruses, compared with an infrared diffraction limit of about 3,250 nanometers. Unlike electron-based and atomic-force microscopes, hyperlenses could potentially image living cells in their natural environments using non-damaging, low-energy infrared light while also providing spectroscopic information. The technology may benefit biological and medical research, communications, and nanoscale optical components. The team expects larger purified hBN crystals could yield further improvements.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data-acquisition system with a built-in analog front end. It supports simple averaging, which halves output data rate, and moving averaging, which preserves data rate. Debug test patterns can replace ADC results independently for channel groups CH[4:1] and CH[8:5], using fixed, digital-ramp, or alternating patterns configured through bank-1 registers 0x13–0x1B.

The device can be reset or powered down through pins or register fields. After power-up or reset, initialization requires a free-running sampling clock and a prescribed register-write sequence. User settings include analog-input range, bandwidth, common-mode range, data format, output-lane count, and internal-reference selection. Speed-boost mode converts one selected channel pair on every sampling clock at up to 8MSPS while leaving the other six channels idle.

Configuration registers are 16-bit values organized into three banks and addressed with 8-bit addresses. Bank 0 is always accessible; banks 1 and 2 are selected through register 0x03. SPI register reads and writes use 24-bit frames. Multiple devices can be configured in a daisy chain by sharing CS and SCLK and connecting each device’s SDO to the next device’s SDI. Daisy-chain transfers require N × 24 clock cycles, with chain length configured as the number of ADCs excluding the first.

For automated-test-equipment applications, calibration reduces total unadjusted error to 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. The device offers low-noise bandwidth up to 22.7kHz and wide bandwidth up to 700kHz; wide-bandwidth mode settles multiplexed signals to 99.95% full scale in 7.5µs. It uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies without a required power-up sequence. Layout guidance includes close 0.1µF bypass capacitors, short ground connections, and separation of analog and reference paths from digital noise.

Ryan Kerr, 26, admitted multiple assaults, including punching a woman and attacking two men, one of whom was left unconscious. The court heard he had prior assault convictions and showed no remorse. Judge David Ticehurst remanded him in custody while considering sentencing and a request for psychiatric reports.

Barron’s argues Netflix could lose more than half its value because of growing competition from Disney, Facebook, and Amazon, along with cash burn and accounting concerns. The passage counters that Netflix has continued growing despite established rivals, expanding from 23.6 million largely domestic subscribers to 104 million global streaming accounts. It also highlights Netflix’s ability to raise prices without slowing subscriber growth, diversify revenue, spread content costs across a large customer base, and attract creators through market dominance. While acknowledging the stock is expensive and may correct, the author concludes that Netflix’s scale and growth make betting against it risky.

Chef Shannon Bard and her husband, Tom, permanently closed Portland’s Zapoteca after six years to spend more time with their five children. They continue operating Toroso, Salud, a cooking school and catering company. Bard published “The Gourmet Mexican Kitchen,” appeared on Food Network programs and cooked at the James Beard House.

A Pediatrics study found nearly 17,000 US children under 6 were treated for window blind-related injuries from 1990 to 2015. Most injuries were minor, but cord entanglements accounted for nearly 80% of 726 hospitalizations and over 94% of 271 deaths. Incidents usually occurred at home, often within minutes while children were unwitnessed despite being under parental care. Researchers and safety advocates called for mandatory standards requiring cordless blinds or inaccessible cords, arguing that voluntary standards, recalls, supervision and safety kits are insufficient. A proposed revision would require most pre-made blinds to be cordless or have inaccessible cords, while custom corded products would remain available. The Consumer Product Safety Commission recommends cordless or inaccessible-cord coverings in homes children live in or visit.

Peterborough City Council brought 179 of 574 privately owned homes empty for over six months back into use last year. Over five years, it restored 663 homes and generated more than £3 million through the New Homes Bonus. The council also pledged £4 million for homes in Midland Road and Bretton Court. Its Phase Two budget proposals aim to protect vital services amid an 80% reduction in government grants, from £55 million to £10 million over eight years. The council argues outdated population figures disadvantage the rapidly growing city and is seeking support for its funding campaign. Six months after introducing Public Space Protection Orders, littering fines and unauthorised city-centre cycling have decreased. The new CHUMS service will support children and young people with mild-to-moderate mental health issues and provide preventative interventions for behaviours including self-harm.

Lubrizol announced an US$80 million expansion of its engineered polymers TPU business across North America, Europe, and Asia. Investments include added production, storage, logistics, compounding, extrusion, elastomer, aliphatic, and adhesive capabilities. New capacity was expected in 2018, with further Asian and European expansions planned for 2019.

The study evaluated the efficacy and safety of best supportive care plus high-volume, high-neutralizing-antibody convalescent plasma versus supportive care alone in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Investigators hypothesized that early administration would reduce mechanical ventilation. Secondary outcomes included clinical severity, oxygenation, ventilation, and hospitalization. The rationale cited limited antiviral options, mixed trial results, and possible effects of treatment timing, plasma volume, and antibody titers. Ethics committees approved the protocol, amendments, and consent documents; serious or unexpected adverse events required reporting. The study followed Declaration of Helsinki and ICH Good Clinical Practice guidelines, and participants or authorized representatives provided informed consent after receiving study information and an opportunity to ask questions.

The NAAIM Exposure Index, published weekly by the National Association of Active Investment Managers, measures members’ average exposure to U.S. equity markets based on surveys conducted each Wednesday. Its indicator line uses a two-week moving average. High readings reflect bullish positioning, while low readings indicate bearish positioning, so the index is often viewed as a contrarian sentiment indicator.

However, the index reflects active managers’ recent account adjustments rather than predicting future market performance. Backtests using data since July 2006 found limited value: investing when readings were below the 10-week moving average produced a 4.4% CAGR excluding dividends, compared with 2.5% when readings were above it. Other moving-average periods and extreme readings did not materially improve results, leading to the conclusion that other contrarian indicators, such as the VIX, may perform better.

Manchester City hosts Burnley at the Etihad Stadium on Jan. 2 at 10:00 AM ET. City must keep winning to challenge Chelsea, while Burnley seeks points to avoid relegation. Sergio Aguero returns for City, with Kevin de Bruyne and David Silva expected to help break down Burnley’s defense. Burnley, just above the relegation zone and struggling away, will rely on Andre Gray and Sam Vokes. City must control midfield and defend Burnley’s strong set pieces.

President Trump announced a deal under which Pfizer will lower prices for Medicaid and direct-pay patients, price new medicines comparably with other countries, and receive certain tariff exemptions while investing in U.S. manufacturing. Policy experts questioned its affordability impact because Medicaid patients already pay little and existing law requires substantial discounts. Key details remain undisclosed.

Jeff Horn will defend his WBO welterweight title against British underdog Gary Corcoran in Brisbane, aiming to validate his disputed victory over Manny Pacquiao and secure potential 2018 bouts with Terence Crawford or Pacquiao. Horn remains unbeaten in 18 fights, while Corcoran is 17-1 and contesting his first world title. The buildup featured accusations of head-butting against Horn and biting threats from Corcoran, prompting mockery from both camps. Both fighters expect an aggressive contest.

Apple reported completing the June 20, 2017 issuance and sale of $1 billion in 3.000% senior unsecured notes due June 20, 2027. Interest is payable semiannually beginning December 20, 2017. The offering was conducted under a June 13 underwriting agreement with representatives Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan Securities, and Merrill Lynch. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, note form, and Hogan Lovells legal opinion and consent.

This non-peer-reviewed study examined neural noise in adults with Tourette syndrome (TS) using EEG responses to median nerve electrical stimulation. Nineteen right-handed adults with TS who completed EEG testing were compared with 19 age- and sex-matched neurologically healthy controls. Neural noise was defined as trial-by-trial variability in the magnitude or timing of somatosensory evoked potentials (SEPs).

Early- and mid-latency SEP components generally showed similar timing, temporal variability, and spatial topography across groups. The TS group had a substantially larger P2/P100 response, whose magnitude was positively associated with tic-related impairment. Trial-by-trial SEP amplitude variability was higher in TS throughout the recording epoch, including before stimulation. However, stimulation produced comparable reductions in standardized variability and coefficient of variation in both groups. No increased variability in SEP timing was found in TS; N2 timing variability was instead lower.

Power spectral density was elevated in the TS group at high-beta and gamma frequencies, producing a flatter 1/f slope consistent with greater asynchronous neural activity. Somatosensory stimulation increased alpha-, beta-, and low-gamma-band inter-trial phase coherence in both groups. The early increase was generally shallower in TS, while beta coherence was elevated around the P100 period.

Clinical analyses linked larger P100 responses to greater tic impairment, alpha-coherence changes to motor tic severity, gamma-coherence and variability changes to premonitory urges, and SEP variability and high-frequency spectral power to IQ scores. The authors conclude that recruitment of sensorimotor neuronal populations may be less stable at rest in TS but may normalize following stimulation.

Facebook published its detailed, roughly 8,000-word internal community standards, explaining what content it permits on issues including drugs, sex work, bullying, hate speech and violence. The move aims to improve transparency amid criticism that Facebook both inadequately combats harmful content and removes posts at governments’ behest without sufficient explanation.

Users will now be able to appeal removals of individual content, not just accounts, Groups and Pages, and Facebook will provide specific removal reasons in more cases. Its 7,500 moderators and automated systems enforce rules that are reviewed every two weeks and shaped partly by feedback from over 100 external organizations and experts. Public forums are planned for May and June.

The standards include detailed restrictions on violent imagery, non-medical drug use, harassment, sales of regulated goods and hacked material. Separate procedures govern government requests involving local laws, with content blocked only in the relevant country when appropriate. The standards do not cover false information or personal-data issues; Facebook seeks to reduce misinformation’s distribution rather than prohibit it.

Finnish irritation with German troops was increasing, though Finland remained dependent on Germany for military supplies and food. German influence appeared in pressure on the Finnish press and censorship aligned with Nazi doctrine. War weariness and social tensions were growing, particularly among Social Democrats and trade unions, which warned that continued war would worsen conditions and food inequality. Popular resistance to holding Soviet Karelia also increased, suggesting Finland’s capacity to sustain the war could erode.

Soviet official Vyshinski denied knowledge of rumored Soviet-Finnish talks. In Washington, a U.S. official warned Finnish representative Toivola that censorship and Finnish press attacks on the United States could undermine Finland’s American and British support. Toivola acknowledged the danger and promised to urge Helsinki to exercise greater care, while explaining that dependence on German food prevented criticism of Germany. Both agreed German pressure likely influenced the anti-American coverage.

Amazon’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2018 reported net sales of $51.0 billion, up 43% year over year, operating income of $1.9 billion, and net income of $1.63 billion, or $3.27 per diluted share. North America, International, and AWS sales were $30.7 billion, $14.9 billion, and $5.4 billion; respective operating results were income of $1.15 billion, a $622 million loss, and income of $1.4 billion.

At March 31, Amazon had $126.4 billion in assets, $31.5 billion in stockholders’ equity, $16.7 billion in cash and cash equivalents, and $24.6 billion in long-term debt. Operating cash flow was negative $1.8 billion for the quarter but $18.2 billion for the trailing twelve months. Cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash declined to $17.6 billion.

Amazon adopted new revenue-recognition guidance, increasing retained earnings by approximately $650 million, and expects new lease-accounting rules adopted in 2019 to materially affect its balance sheet. The company reported contractual commitments of $119.2 billion and ongoing tax, regulatory, and patent contingencies. On April 12, 2018, Amazon acquired Ring for approximately $900 million in cash, net of acquired cash.

A federal jury unanimously cleared retired Little Rock police lieutenant David Hudson of using excessive force against Jon “Chris” Erwin outside a restaurant in October 2011. Video showed Hudson punching Erwin seven times and taking him to the ground, but jurors concluded after two days of testimony that the force was reasonable from Hudson’s perspective.

Hudson testified that Erwin became agitated, refused orders, put his hands on him and continued resisting arrest. He said he used punches and then took Erwin down in accordance with the police department’s escalating use-of-force policy. Witnesses offered differing views of the confrontation, with some fearing police brutality and others believing Hudson was under attack. Several testified that Erwin’s group appeared intoxicated and had behaved disruptively, though Erwin denied resisting arrest and maintained that he was a victim of excessive force.

Erwin suffered facial injuries requiring three stitches and later sought physical therapy for back pain. His misdemeanor charges were dismissed for procedural reasons, but the jury was not permitted to hear testimony about the charges. Hudson said the verdict vindicated his actions, while Erwin said his lawsuit sought accountability rather than money. Claims against Little Rock and the restaurant’s owner had been settled before trial, though details were unavailable.

Florida State linebacker Ethan Pritchard left the hospital nearly six weeks after being shot in the head in an apparent mistaken-identity incident. Alert and able to communicate, he was transferred to a Jacksonville rehabilitation facility. Four people have been arrested. His father thanked medical staff, law enforcement, coach Mike Norvell and supporters, while noting Pritchard faces a long recovery.

The paper investigates reusable ontology design patterns (ODPs) for modeling scientific workflows and material-processing transformations in Materials Science and Engineering (MSE). It defines three requirements: process structure and execution order; data, resources, and parameters; and project goals, participants, and roles.

The study analyzes PMDcore, the General Process Ontology (GPO), WILD, P-PLAN, Metadata4Ing (M4I), and OPMW. Manually extracted patterns were reviewed by nine domain experts from the NFDI-MatWerk Linked Open Data Working Group. P-PLAN, OPMW, and GPO support process and resource patterns; WILD supports process patterns; M4I supports resource and project patterns; and PMDcore supports all three categories.

A baseline automated method converts textual requirements and ontology annotations into vector embeddings, ranks concepts by cosine similarity, and evaluates retrieved classes and properties against curated ground truth using precision, recall, and F1-score. Selected concepts are converted into reusable modules through ROBOT extraction. After comparing extraction configurations, STAR with no intermediate classes was selected for producing compact, semantically coherent modules.

P-PLAN achieved the highest F1-scores for process and resource extraction, at 0.59 and 0.53. PMDcore covered all categories, with F1-scores of 0.36 for process, 0.21 for resources, and 0.25 for projects. The results indicate that semantic similarity can support ODP extraction, but performance is affected by annotation quality, requirement wording, fixed retrieval limits, and the independent processing of ontologies.

Future work will cover additional MSE modeling needs, incorporate ontology mappings and structural features, reduce annotation and wording biases, use multi-expert validation, and develop a platform for publishing patterns, usage scenarios, and community feedback.

Old Forge High School seniors Christian Killino, Iain Kerrigan and Kole Barbetti organized a Math-a-thon benefiting St. Jude’s Research Hospital, raising $3,864 through donations tied to completed math problems. Rosemarie Corigliano was installed as president of the Wayne Memorial Hospital Auxiliary, whose new officers will serve two-year terms. The nonprofit’s former leadership contributed more than $250,000 to the hospital, and upcoming fundraisers include Attic Treasures and a Best of the Eagles concert. Fifth-generation beekeeper Hannah Perry Burgess presented a conservation-focused program on honey bees to the Scranton City Chapter of the DAR.

GoDaddy gave neo-Nazi website The Daily Stormer 24 hours to move its domain after publisher Andrew Anglin posted an article insulting Heather Heyer, who was killed during the Charlottesville white nationalist rally. GoDaddy said the article could incite further violence and violated its terms, clarifying that it manages only the domain, not the site’s content. Contributor Andrew Auernheimer said a subsequent claim that the site had been hacked was a prank and that an alternate domain was available. The Daily Stormer, founded in 2013, is known for Nazi propaganda and coordinated harassment campaigns. Anglin has faced a lawsuit over one such campaign, while PayPal and an advertising company have also banned the site.

Enron transformed from a debt-burdened pipeline company formed through Houston Natural Gas’s 1985 merger with InterNorth into a dominant energy trader. Jeff Skilling’s Gas Bank model enabled Enron to buy, sell, and assume risks for natural gas, later extending its trading approach to electricity, commodities, broadband capacity, and other markets. By 2000, revenues had reached $100 billion, and the company was celebrated for innovation and rapid growth.

Skilling fostered an aggressive culture emphasizing intelligence, risk-taking, speed, and large performance-based rewards. Enron recruited heavily from elite schools, encouraged internal competition, and annually dismissed poorly ranked employees. Its pursuit of immediate profits weakened teamwork and loyalty, while widespread use of mark-to-market accounting allowed projected long-term profits to be recorded upfront.

Enron increasingly favored trading over asset-heavy businesses. Rebecca Mark’s international power and water ventures struggled, particularly the Dabhol plant in India and Azurix, which declined after its 1999 public offering. After Mark’s departure, Skilling became CEO in February 2001.

Enron then faced criticism over California’s energy crisis, costly international projects, the collapse of telecommunications markets, the failed Blockbuster agreement, and growing questions about its accounting. Its stock fell from $80 in January 2001 to below $40 by late August. Skilling resigned after six months as CEO, citing personal sacrifices and family priorities. Ken Lay returned, promised to focus innovation closer to Enron’s core businesses, and acknowledged that the performance-review system had harmed morale.

Fad diets may offer temporary weight loss but are not healthy or sustainable. Dietician Bonnie Taub-Dix recommends reconnecting with food, building a healthy relationship with the body, avoiding deprivation, and practicing moderation, including consuming dietary fat.

The coach said frequent, consistently applied penalties have prevented both teams from establishing rhythm or style, though the calls affect them equally. His team must move the puck and position itself more quickly, simplify its offense, and send more shots toward the net. In July 2021, Public Health Wales investigated a Salmonella Typhimurium outbreak linked to an Eid al-Adha barbecue and lunches in Cardiff’s North African community. Among a 43-person social network, 22 symptomatic cases were identified; most illnesses began the day after the barbecue, while later cases suggested person-to-person transmission. Twelve cases sought emergency care, six were admitted, and one required intensive care.

A cohort study and Firth logistic regression identified consumption of the traditional raw sheep-liver dish “marrara” as the most likely transmission vehicle. Raw-liver consumers were approximately 50 times more likely to be cases than non-consumers. Lamb and spicy sauce were not significant after adjustment. Investigators noted undercooked lamb, prolonged lack of refrigeration, reuse of raw-liver marinade, and other opportunities for cross-contamination.

Five cultured human samples were genetically indistinguishable Salmonella Typhimurium isolates. Eleven raw-lamb samples, along with samples from local butchers and the supplying abattoir, had identical sequences to the human isolates, indicating widespread contamination, although the point of contamination could not be established. Raw liver was unavailable for testing.

Public Health Wales worked with community representatives to provide culturally sensitive, multilingual food-safety information. The investigation concluded that routine outbreak questionnaires should include culturally relevant dishes and recommended proactive messaging about risks from raw or undercooked meat and offal, particularly around religious and cultural events.

The Coppock Curve, devised by economist E.S.C. Coppock in 1965 for identifying long-term investment opportunities, is a smoothed momentum indicator mainly used for major stock-market swings. It is calculated as a 10-month weighted moving average of the sum of 11-month and 14-month rates of change. These periods were inspired by Coppock’s research into mourning recovery times.

The strategy enters long positions when the curve crosses above zero and exits when it crosses below zero. Designed for monthly time frames, it produced only 12 trades from 1960 over 63 years. Two cited S&P 500 trades lasted about six years each, returning approximately 80% and 65%.

The backtest reported that all trades were profitable, though the small sample limits the significance of this result. Compared with buy-and-hold, the strategy reduced drawdowns, spent about one-quarter less time in the market, and achieved higher risk-adjusted returns. The article concludes that the strategy remains useful for exploiting markets’ bullish bias while filtering corrective phases.

The lecture examines financing sustainable real estate at the asset level, covering sustainable finance, mortgages, and private equity. Sustainable buildings can generate higher rents through lower operating costs, better indoor conditions, tenant preferences, and regulatory compliance, ultimately supporting higher property values and developer returns.

Sustainable finance treats climate risk as financial risk and incorporates environmental externalities into asset pricing. Investors allocate capital among bonds, stocks, and real estate according to risk and return. Green buildings may offer higher net operating income and lower perceived risk than conventional buildings, increasing asset values and shifting portfolio capital toward them. Early investors may earn higher returns, but increased demand can raise prices and reduce equilibrium returns. Brown buildings may face penalties, lost tenants, reduced revenue, higher risk premiums, and declining values. Limited green-building supply, information asymmetry, and market frictions can preserve investment in brown buildings.

Investment decisions compare an asset’s expected return with the weighted average cost of debt and equity capital. Projects proceed when expected returns exceed capital costs or when discounted cash flows produce a positive net present value.

Climate hazards such as floods, hurricanes, and wildfires can reduce property values and increase mortgage delinquency and default. When property values fall below loan balances, borrowers may rationally default, leaving lenders with losses. Research cited in the lecture found increased mortgage defaults in wildfire zones. Government-backed mortgages and flood insurance create additional challenges because lower-income households often occupy riskier locations and depend on subsidies. Accurately pricing climate risk could improve appraisal and lending but may impose higher borrowing costs on vulnerable households, creating social-justice and political concerns.

Green mortgages offer favorable terms for energy-efficient properties. Banks may lend more or charge lower interest rates because efficient buildings can have higher values, lower energy expenses, and reduced default risk. Studies cited found energy-efficient homes were substantially less likely to default, with stronger effects among low-income households; similar results were reported for commercial properties. Banks may also finance renovations upfront when expected efficiency improvements will raise property values and reduce loan-to-value ratios.

Private real estate equity commonly uses commingled funds in which general partners manage investments and contribute a minority stake while limited partners provide passive capital. A football blitz occurs when a defense sends five or more defenders—sometimes up to eight—into the offensive backfield to pressure the quarterback or stop a runner. Unlike a typical four-player rush, blitzing can create quicker pressure, poor throws, sacks, and disrupted runs, but it leaves fewer defenders available for pass coverage and can be vulnerable to mobile quarterbacks.

Defensive coordinators call blitzes to confuse blocking assignments and help the defense regain possession. Variations include zone blitzes, where a lineman drops into coverage as a linebacker rushes; safety and cornerback blitzes, which sacrifice defensive-back coverage for surprise pressure; zero blitzes, which leave no deep safety and are often used against expected runs; and run blitzes aimed at quickly reaching the point of attack.

Offenses can counter blitzes with quick passes to open receivers or running backs, quarterback mobility, and max-protection schemes that keep additional players back to block. Successfully beating a blitz depends on identifying the defense’s weakened area before or immediately after the snap.

The work integrates behavioral framing into Bayesian persuasion and studies how large language models can optimize persuasive communication. Its model includes a sender who observes the world state, a receiver who chooses an action based on beliefs, a signaling or recommendation scheme, and a framing space whose elements induce receiver beliefs through a potentially Bayesian or non-Bayesian belief oracle.

Three optimization variants are defined: recommendation-only with fixed framing, framing-only with a fixed recommendation scheme, and joint optimization of framing and recommendations. Assuming access to a noisy LLM-based framing-to-belief oracle, the authors show that framing-only optimization is NP-hard to approximate and that sender utility can be discontinuous in induced beliefs, making oracle errors consequential. Joint optimization is more tractable: optimized sender utility is continuous in induced beliefs, and the authors provide a quasi-polynomial-time approximation scheme.

A practical hill-climbing method combines LLMs for generating framings and estimating beliefs with analytical optimization of recommendation strategies. Case studies involving a realtor’s property recommendations and a clothing brand’s advertising and discount strategy show strong performance by LLM-based measures. Human evaluations produce less pronounced and more variable responses, but align directionally with predictions and approximately match effect magnitudes.

The framework treats framing as language or descriptions accompanying signals and models it as influencing beliefs rather than payoffs. Framing spaces may be discrete or continuously relaxed, with continuous inducible beliefs assumed convex. The work argues that LLMs enable scalable selection of textual framing alongside quantitative recommendations, while noting future potential for images and video.
