The adapter pattern uses a separate container to transform an application container’s interface into a standard interface expected by other systems. It is useful in heterogeneous environments where applications differ in logging, monitoring, and health-check conventions. Examples include adapting Redis metrics for Prometheus, using Fluentd to normalize Redis or Apache Storm logs, redirecting file logs to stdout, and adding rich database health checks without modifying the original container. Separate adapters improve reuse, maintenance, resource isolation, and sharing.

Multi-node distributed systems consist of loosely coupled components communicating through network APIs. Microservices divide applications into independently developed, released, and scaled services, improving agility, reliability, and separation of concerns. Their disadvantages include more difficult debugging, coordination, and architecture, which distributed design patterns can help address.

Replicated load-balanced services use interchangeable servers behind a load balancer. Stateless services are replicated for availability and horizontal scaling, while readiness probes ensure traffic reaches only initialized instances. Session-tracked services route a user consistently to one replica, preferably through application-level identifiers such as cookies when external IP addresses are unreliable. Application-layer proxies can add caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination. A layered Kubernetes deployment may use replicated application servers, Varnish caches, and nginx SSL terminators.

Sharded services divide requests or data among specialized replicas and are generally used when state exceeds one machine’s capacity. Sharded caches use memory more efficiently than replicated caches but may suffer performance degradation when a shard fails or changes. Replicating each shard improves resilience and permits independent scaling of hot shards. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, use keys that reflect response identity, and may employ consistent hashing to minimize remapping when shard counts change. Routing can be provided by per-pod ambassadors or shared routing services.

Scatter/gather distributes each request across multiple workers, then combines their partial results. It can reduce processing time and support datasets larger than one machine by sharding data across leaves. Document search illustrates combining intersections or unions of results. Excessive parallelism introduces request overhead, straggler latency, and greater failure probability. Replicating each leaf shard improves availability, scalability, and upgrade safety.

Function-as-a-service executes stateless functions in response to events and automatically manages scaling and failures. It simplifies deployment and encourages modularity, but complicates dependency visibility, debugging, monitoring, state management, long-running processing, and workloads requiring large in-memory datasets. Per-request pricing is attractive for intermittent traffic but may become expensive under sustained load. Suitable patterns include request or response decorators, such as adding API defaults, and asynchronous event handlers, such as sending two-factor authentication codes. Event-based pipelines can connect independent processing stages as a directed graph.

San Juan High School’s baseball program warned Citrus Heights businesses about an alleged fraudulent fundraising scheme. Someone posing as a team representative solicited sponsorships, leading an auto repair shop to pay about $1,400 for a message board sign that did not exist. The soliciting company, “Athletic Sports,” has no website, uses a UPS postal box and did not answer calls. The team filed a police report, shared the flyer on social media and urged businesses to verify fundraising requests directly with schools or programs before contributing.

The S&P/TSX Composite edged up 0.08% to 15,564.28, supported by gains in CN Rail, Restaurant Brands, and materials stocks as gold stabilized. Teck Resources, Barrick Gold and Centerra Gold each rose about 3% or more. Mitel Networks gained 10.1% on a $2 billion sale agreement, while Prairiesky Royal fell 6.5%.

The lecture develops numerical methods for the second-order wave equation. Rewriting it as a symmetric first-order system reveals waves traveling at speeds \(c\) and \(-c\). The continuous solution consists of two nondispersive components moving in opposite directions and is determined by initial displacement and velocity.

Spatial discretization by centered second differences produces a semidiscrete method of lines. Fourier analysis shows that its frequency factor approximates the continuous one with second-order accuracy but introduces dispersion, causing different frequencies to travel at different speeds. Fully discretizing time yields the multistep leapfrog method. Analysis of its amplification factors shows stability when the Courant number \(r=c\Delta t/\Delta x\) does not exceed one, corresponding to the Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy condition. The lecture also notes complications from variable coefficients, forcing, high frequencies, boundaries, and previews staggered-grid methods used in electromagnetism.

Gold prices are influenced by supply and demand, the US dollar, investor risk appetite, central bank reserves, jewelry demand, and inflation. A weaker dollar and rising inflation generally support higher gold prices. From 1955 to 2022, gold recorded 80 monthly all-time highs, about 10% of all months, though it experienced a 14-year period without a new high between 1981 and 2005. The article backtests a strategy using monthly World Bank gold prices to trade near all-time highs. The strategy’s specific rules are restricted to members. Its returns are lower, but it remains invested only about one-third of the time and reduces maximum drawdown by nearly half, potentially helping identify gold bull markets.

Tencent added Batman to Arena of Valor, joining other DC characters. The update introduces an eight-minute, five-team Death Match mode, Valor TV for viewing competitions, and improvements to lobby menus, friends lists and messaging.

Vegas officials discussed the team’s unexpected run to the Stanley Cup Final, emphasizing teamwork, competitiveness and steady improvement rather than numerical goals. A road trip featuring convincing wins in Dallas and Nashville strengthened players’ belief that they could beat anyone.

George McPhee described the expansion draft as uniquely favorable because salary-cap pressures allowed Vegas to acquire better players and draft picks. The organization prioritized young, developing talent, speed, competitiveness and good character while aiming to avoid becoming an embarrassment or “doormat.” Washington later tried unsuccessfully to reacquire Nate Schmidt after Vegas selected him.

The team chose not to appoint a captain, instead relying on a six-player leadership group. That approach proved successful, with Deryk Engelland selected by teammates to receive the trophy in Winnipeg. McPhee praised the coaching staff’s businesslike, game-by-game approach and said the coach provided patience, leadership, playing experience and an ability to command players’ respect.

The organization also reflected on the emotional aftermath of the Las Vegas tragedy. Players and staff focused on honoring victims, helping the community heal and continuing charitable support, often privately. Though rarely discussed openly, the event remained in players’ thoughts.

Looking ahead to Washington, Vegas recognized Nicklas Backstrom and the Capitals’ overall team strength. McPhee said Alex Ovechkin remained the same hardworking, physical scoring threat who absorbs intense pressure. Despite excitement about reaching the Final, the team remained focused on preparing for the next game.

Japan deployed over 4,000 troops to Korea, occupied Seoul and strategic routes, and continued sending reinforcements. China increased its forces, with 5,000 troops ordered to embark and additional forces being prepared. Japan refused to withdraw without guarantees against Chinese interference and later demanded Korean governmental and policy reforms made in consultation with Japanese authorities. Japan alleged China violated the 1885 Tientsin Convention by providing notice only after deploying troops.

Foreign representatives proposed simultaneous withdrawal. Both sides referred the proposal to their governments, but China stated its troops would remain because Japan refused to withdraw. Li Hung Chang reportedly received broad authority to determine peace or war, while China reportedly redirected funds from the Empress’s birthday celebration toward the crisis. With conflict considered imminent, the American representative agreed to provide asylum to Korea’s royal family and senior officials if necessary and secured an increase in the legation guard from 12 to 120 men.

Scale AI eliminated a Dallas-based contractor team of more than a dozen people handling generalist AI training tasks. The company cited growing demand for specialized, expert-level data work. Workers received four weeks’ severance, healthcare through October, and invitations to join Scale’s freelance platform, Outlier. Scale said other Dallas contractors and customer delivery were unaffected.

Vishay Intertechnology shares rose 2.08% to $19.65. Analysts’ 12-month average price target is $20, ranging from $18 to $22. The stock’s average brokerage recommendation is 3.75, while its industry ranks 138th of 265. Reported ratings include one Buy, three Holds, one Underperform, and one Sell. Its 14-period Average True Range is 0.55, with weekly volatility of 2.47% and monthly volatility of 2.50%. The Relative Strength Index is 53.51. Vishay has a $2.83 billion market capitalization and 144.15 million outstanding shares. Previous trading volume was 1.23 million shares, versus an average of about 1.5 million.

The study demonstrates controlled defect engineering in CVD-grown monolayer MoS₂ using 1 MeV electron-beam irradiation at fixed flux and exposure times of 30, 60, and 120 seconds. Raman spectroscopy indicated increasing sulfur-vacancy-related disorder, while photoluminescence showed exciton blueshifts, intensity quenching, and stronger defect-bound emission 200–300 meV below the neutral exciton as irradiation increased.

XPS revealed irradiation-induced Mo⁵⁺ and increasingly prominent Mo⁶⁺ states, alongside enhanced Mo–O bonding, attributed to oxygen interaction at sulfur vacancies. KPFM showed a work-function increase from 4.8 to 5.24 eV after 120 seconds, indicating p-type doping associated with oxygen incorporation and electron withdrawal. Temperature-dependent measurements identified deep and shallow defect states near 1.64 and 1.73 eV. Defect-bound excitons persisted to approximately 210–240 K and exhibited stronger exciton–phonon coupling than free excitons. Power-dependent measurements confirmed increased densities of optically active defect states and enhanced defect-mediated recombination after irradiation.

Circular polarization-resolved photoluminescence showed that the defect emission was unpolarized and that valley polarization decreased from 62% in the untreated sample to 38% after 120 seconds, consistent with defect-mediated intervalley scattering and carrier trapping. First-principles calculations found that sulfur vacancies produce donor states, whereas oxygen bonding or adsorption at vacancies creates acceptor states near the valence band, supporting the observed p-type behavior and defect emission. The calculations also indicated reduced energy separation between relevant valleys, supporting enhanced depolarization.

The results establish high-energy electron irradiation as a tunable method for introducing optically active defects in monolayer MoS₂, with potential extension to other transition-metal dichalcogenides after optimization.

The Wing-T offense, developed by Harold “Tubby” Raymond at the University of Delaware, uses misdirection, similar-looking plays, motion, unusual formations, and a diverse running game to slow aggressive defenses and conceal the ball’s destination.

Traditional personnel includes at least two capable running backs, particularly a fullback who can run inside and catch passes; an athletic quarterback with good footwork; and quick offensive linemen skilled at pulling and trapping. Its strengths include adaptability, deception, and unfamiliarity to modern defenses. Its primary weakness is the lack of a conventional dropback passing game, though teams can supplement it with shotgun spread formations.

Common formations include the Wing, Wing-Slot, and unbalanced sets. Major running plays are the Buck Sweep, featuring pulling guards and backfield fakes; the Down play, which creates blocking angles for the fullback; and the Trap, which attacks aggressive defensive linemen. Common passes include the Waggle, a play-action counterpart to the Buck Sweep; option routes for isolated receivers; and quick vertical play-action passes.

The traditional Wing-T is largely absent from major college football but remains common in high schools. Its principles also influence modern spread offenses, including those used by Gus Malzahn at Auburn and UCF.

ADA occurrence will be described by treatment group without statistical testing. Overall incidence includes treatment-induced cases and baseline-positive patients with ≥5-fold titer increases, divided by evaluable patients with reportable post-dose samples; unscheduled-visit results are included.

The speaker describes a tough loss, citing turnovers, poor puck decisions, and weak third-period execution. Despite a strong opening and chances to win, the team made things too easy for its opponent and must improve next game.

The ADS868xW enters acquisition state after power-up, reset, or conversion, and begins conversion on a CONVST/CS rising edge. During conversion, further CONVST/CS transitions are ignored. Completion is indicated by RVS or the maximum conversion-time interval.

Data-transfer frames begin when CONVST/CS falls and end when it rises. A 32-clock frame accepts a valid 32-bit command; shorter frames invalidate writes but can read selected output MSBs, while longer frames use the final 32 input bits. Register reads appear in the following frame; otherwise, output generally contains the latest 16-bit conversion result. Configurable flags include device address, input range, supply and input alarms, and parity.

The multiSPI interface supports four standard SPI modes, single- or dual-SDO output, and source-synchronous protocols using RVS as the output clock. SPI-00-S is the default after power-up or asynchronous reset. Nine configuration registers control identification, reset and power modes, input/output protocols, output formatting, input range, and alarm thresholds and status.

The ADS868xW integrates a 16-bit SAR ADC, analog front end, programmable gain amplifier, driver, and reference. An example eight-channel industrial input design combines the ADS8681W with a MUX36D08 multiplexer and supports voltage, current, and temperature sensing. Programmable input alarms provide thresholds and hysteresis to reduce false triggering.

Power-saving options include NAP mode and deep power-down, both enabled through the protected RST_PWRCTL_REG. Recommended implementation practices include separate AVDD and DVDD supplies, close decoupling capacitors, analog/digital PCB partitioning, short ground paths, and appropriate reference-pin capacitors.

Christopher Drone Bassett was sentenced to life plus 35 years for the 2015 murder of 15-year-old Zaevion Dobson, who shielded friends from gunfire. Richard Gregory Williams III received 143 years and Kipling Deshawn Colbert 109 years for facilitating the murder, with both totals including sentences for unrelated charges.

The S&P 500 Financial Services sector includes banks, investment firms, insurers, and fintech companies serving individuals and organizations. Its capitalization-weighted index is tracked by ETFs including VFH and XLF. As of July 2022, major stocks included Berkshire Hathaway, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup, and Goldman Sachs.

The sector fell 85% from its 2007 peak during the 2008–09 financial crisis, leading to failures, bailouts, consolidation, and significant industry changes. A backtested XLF strategy produced 198 trades, a 1.05% average gain, 73% win rate, 21% maximum drawdown, and 2.25 profit factor. The sector offers high volatility for trading but is strongly correlated with the broader market.

The article develops a long-only trading strategy for the Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF (BOTZ), using short-term Donchian Channels for signals and an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) to filter false signals. BOTZ, founded in 2016, offers broader industry exposure and more usable price history than individual robotics and AI startups.

Daily backtests from September 13, 2016 found most tested Donchian Channel settings profitable on paper. The strategy selected a three-period Donchian Channel and a 200-period EMA, favoring common, non-optimal settings to reduce curve-fitting risk. Adding an EMA generally improved results, while the resulting strategy reportedly outperformed buy-and-hold with lower volatility.

Only 87 trades were generated, limiting statistical reliability and increasing curve-fitting concerns. Two-hour testing also produced a smooth equity curve with results close to the daily timeframe, but the article cautions against early conclusions. It recommends out-of-sample testing and an incubation period before considering live or short-term trading use.

ADS9803 board-layout guidance recommends separating digital lines from analog and reference paths, using nearby 0.1-µF ceramic bypass capacitors without intervening vias, placing reference decoupling close to REFIO and REFM, and making short ground-plane connections. TI provides development tools, documentation-update notifications, and TI E2E support forums, with linked content supplied as-is. The device requires ESD precautions because damage can range from degraded performance to failure. Mechanical, packaging, ordering, lifecycle, material, RoHS, finish, moisture-sensitivity, reflow, and marking information may change and includes qualifications for preproduction parts. TI relies partly on third-party material information and limits related liability to the annual purchase price of affected parts. Technical resources are provided as-is for skilled developers, who remain responsible for product selection, application design, testing, validation, and compliance. Resource use is limited to developing applications using the described TI products and does not grant additional intellectual-property rights or warranties.

San Miguel Pure Foods postponed its planned P100–150-billion follow-on offering to the third or fourth quarter amid competing stock rights offerings and market volatility. The offering will raise public ownership in the consolidated San Miguel Food and Beverage to the required 15% from 4.3%. SMPFC reported 2017 net income of P6.9 billion on P117 billion in revenues.

At reset de-assertion, BTMODE pins are sampled into CONTROL_STATUS. BTMODE[15:11] configure GPMC, [4:0] set ordered boot modes, [7:5] are reserved, [9:8] select Ethernet PHY mode for EMAC boot, and [10] selects GPMC muxing for XIP boot.

Nigeria is experiencing rapid growth in shopping malls, particularly in Lagos, driven by demand for convenience, one-stop shopping, brand awareness and after-work access. Retailers such as Shoprite and Spar are expanding nationwide. Industry representatives say malls reflect investor confidence and changing lifestyles while creating jobs, increasing tax revenues and offering shopping and entertainment under one roof.

Amazon is reportedly developing a top-secret domestic robot codenamed “Vesta,” overseen by Gregg Zehr at its Lab126 hardware division. The company has increased robotics hiring and may test robots in employees’ homes by year-end, with a possible consumer launch in 2019, though plans could change. The robot’s purpose remains unclear, but it may function as a mobile Alexa. Prototypes use cameras and computer vision to navigate homes. The project is separate from Amazon’s warehouse robotics operations. Advances in artificial intelligence, vision, cameras and voice activation could make home robots more practical, while Amazon may subsidize devices for Prime users. The consumer robot market is projected to reach about $15 billion annually by 2023.

Corning, founded in 1851, built its identity around sustained materials innovation, creating products and businesses including Pyrex, television glass, optical fiber, ceramic emissions-control substrates, LCD glass, and life-sciences products. After concentrating heavily on telecommunications, the 2001–2002 market crash reduced revenue from $6.3 billion to $3.1 billion, caused a $5.4 billion loss and more than 12,000 layoffs, and drove its stock from $100 to $1.50. Corning nevertheless maintained research spending and reaffirmed innovation as its core strategy. By 2008, it had recovered, led by LCD glass, renewed telecommunications sales, and emerging markets.

Corning organized centralized long-term research alongside business units responsible for product development, manufacturing, sales, and marketing. Its innovation process moved projects through five stages, from knowledge gathering to lifecycle management. The Corning Technology Council evaluated early-stage opportunities, while the Growth and Strategy Council (GSC) managed high-potential and later-stage projects. A centralized new-business-development function explored opportunities outside existing businesses.

Led by the CEO, COO, and CTO, the GSC met several times monthly to advise innovation programs, allocate resources, pace investments, and balance existing and developing businesses. It used project-level zero-based budgeting and considered market potential, major trends, customer value, differentiation, fit with Corning’s capabilities, and available resources. The council supported long-term “patient money,” reflecting that businesses such as display glass and optical fiber took many years to become profitable.

Corning spent about 10% of revenue on research, development, and engineering. Of its approximately $600 million budget, 64% supported development and engineering in existing businesses, while 36% funded corporate research. Low employee turnover, centralized research, cross-business movement of technical talent, and shared expertise in glass and ceramics supported knowledge transfer.

The GSC helped accelerate investments in diesel filters and fiber-to-the-home products when customer demand emerged sooner than expected. However, managers cited large meetings, presentation pressures, and possible overload as concerns. As Corning sought to increase the rate of new-business creation, the council faced challenges in prioritizing opportunities, preserving candid dialogue, maintaining strategic focus, and evaluating unfamiliar businesses and business models.

The work presents a simple, scalable method for fabricating visible Fabry–Perot microcavities from buckled dielectric membrane mirrors. Silicon wafers are smoothed through repeated oxidation and HF removal, reducing measured surface roughness to 33–50 pm. A 21-pair SiO₂/Ta₂O₅ dielectric coating is deposited, patterned, and released by backside silicon etching. Built-in compressive strain buckles the suspended films into rotationally symmetric concave mirrors. Mirror diameters can be varied to produce radii of curvature from 0.9 to 21 mm.

Cavities formed from two micromirrors were characterized at 780.24 nm using swept ring-down measurements. The highest measured finesse was 0.89 × 10⁶ with a linewidth of (2π)233 ± 1 kHz, while the highest quality factor was 2.3 × 10⁹ with a linewidth of (2π)124 ± 0.5 kHz. Finesse decreased with cavity length because of diffraction and mirror-shape imperfections, while quality factor initially increased, plateaued, and then declined. The measured loss bounds absorption plus scattering at 2.20 ppm and implies surface roughness no greater than 90 pm.

The process also produced manually assembled cavities as small as 2 mm³. A 45 µm cavity had finesse 0.616 × 10⁶, quality factor 7.45 × 10⁷, and a 3.18 THz free spectral range; a 1 mm cavity achieved finesse 0.263 × 10⁶ and quality factor 6.74 × 10⁸. These compact cavities may support visible lasers, sensing, quantum networking, optical filtering, laser stabilization, and integration with neutral-atom, ion-trap, fiber, or photonic-chip systems.

The disclosure describes computer-implemented methods, systems, and program products for creating and simulating digital twins of physical assets. Real-time data from sensors, IoT devices, and recording systems represents asset components and performance. As an asset changes through maintenance, replacement, configuration, wear, damage, or other events, separate time-stamped digital twin versions may be created and stored.

Users can simulate a current or previous digital twin version, modify components, or construct a hybrid model from components of multiple versions. Simulations may selectively bypass components, substitute alternatives, or use overriding intermediate values for non-simulated portions. Intermediate results can feed downstream simulation stages and be verified before continuing. These options allow simulations to focus on selected components and compare how component or configuration changes affect performance.

A digital twin module may include creation, data collection, version management, simulation, and reporting engines. It can identify asset changes from user reports or collected performance data, manage version timelines and logs, execute configured simulations, and display or archive results. Augmented reality interfaces may support component selection and hybrid-model construction.

The system may operate on networked, cloud, virtualized, or containerized computing infrastructure. Its workflow covers creating or associating a digital twin, collecting and analyzing asset data, generating new versions when changes occur, configuring simulations, executing them, reporting results, and optionally revising parameters or rerunning simulations.

Exeter City manager Paul Tisdale praised his depleted side despite a 1-0 defeat at league leaders Luton Town, decided by Harry Cornick’s deflected strike. With six defenders missing, 20-year-old Jordan Storey made his first league start and impressed, supported by development work from Matt Taylor, Andy Tillson and the reserve team. Tisdale acknowledged Luton deserved victory but was proud of Exeter’s defensive effort. Liam McAlinden’s late equaliser was disallowed for Robbie Simpson’s foul on goalkeeper Marek Stech, though Tisdale believed the goal should have stood. Ahead of facing promotion rivals Wycombe Wanderers, he maintained Exeter’s performance levels and overall form remained strong.

Apple reported results from its March 10, 2015 annual shareholder meeting. Shareholders elected Tim Cook, Al Gore, Bob Iger, Andrea Jung, Art Levinson, Ron Sugar, and Sue Wagner as directors. They approved Ernst & Young LLP as independent auditor, executive compensation, and a 50 million-share increase under the Employee Stock Purchase Plan. Shareholder proposals concerning a risk report and proxy access were rejected. The amended purchase plan was filed as Exhibit 10.1.

Environment and Climate Change Canada found that more than a dozen studied phthalates posed no human-health risk, though one requires further environmental review. Environmental Defence criticized the decision, citing stricter European findings and urging Canada to modernize chemical laws. The government plans to address recommended reforms by June 2018.

Messaging apps are evolving into ecosystems of services while retaining chat as their core. WeChat already integrates commerce, games and dating, while WhatsApp, with 94% reach in India, is adding calls and payments and could expand into professional content and gaming. Hike could compete by combining payments with Airtel TV and Wynk, while Paytm’s Gamepind signals gaming’s engagement potential. Competition among globally backed internet giants could make leadership in chat decisive for the next decade.

The patent describes a network security appliance with an integrated touch-screen interface for local administration when attacks, such as denial-of-service events, prevent remote access. The appliance can prioritize local controls and reserve resources so administrators can block ports or sources, modify and reprioritize filters, and maintain local network operation. It may quarantine packets from unrecognized devices until physically authorized. Packet filtering can use multidimensional geoprocessing and R-tree indexes to accelerate rule matching. A management server distributes mandatory rules to all appliances and probabilistically assigns potential-threat rules based on likelihood, reducing memory, processing, and bandwidth use while enabling early attack detection and rule promotion. The system supports packet blocking, forwarding, modification, logging, notifications, periodic rule updates, and implementation across varied computing and network hardware.

AMP chairman David Murray blamed increasingly prescriptive ASX guidelines for worsening financial-sector governance and creating a trust deficit, urging institutions to redesign governance mechanisms rather than conform to one-size-fits-all rules.

Gardaí renewed appeals for information about 18-year-old Cameron Reilly’s murder in Dunleer, particularly seeking his distinctive iPhone and information from local young people. Separately, armed officers arrested two people during a suspected firearm handover in west Dublin and seized a semi-automatic shotgun, cash, 6kg of heroin and 2kg of cocaine.

Standardized testing influences curricula and teaching, often narrowing instruction and encouraging educators to teach to specific exams. Some states extend public-school testing requirements to private school choice programs, while others require the ACT or SAT for graduation, scholarships, or assessment. The passage argues that these mandates constrain educational diversity and promote declining or biased standards.

Rather than banning standardized tests, the author advocates assessment choice. Schools and students could select tests aligned with their educational approaches while retaining standardized measures useful for admissions. The Classic Learning Test is presented as an alternative emphasizing literature, philosophy, history, literacy, and numeracy. A cited study found a 0.89 correlation between CLT and SAT scores, suggesting different exams can be aligned for comparison.

The author recommends that states offer multiple assessments for school choice programs, graduation, public college admissions, and scholarships. Arkansas and Florida already permit several assessment options, and Florida requires public colleges and universities to accept the CLT alongside the ACT and SAT.

A Canadian Society of Palliative Care Physicians analysis concludes that expanding palliative and hospice care across Canada would improve patient care while reducing costs and hospital use. Studies cited indicate hospital-based palliative care saves about $7,000–$8,000 per patient, while outpatient services can reduce direct costs by approximately 30%. Home-based care may improve quality of life and reduce reliance on expensive services; expanding it in Ontario could avoid $191 million–$385 million in costs. Moving appropriate patients from acute care to residential hospices could save about $600 daily. Palliative care also improves satisfaction, symptom control and quality of life, and may extend survival. The society recommends a mix of hospital, outpatient, home and hospice programs, supported and evaluated by federal, provincial and territorial governments.

The Central Bank of Nigeria introduced FORM X to simplify foreign exchange applications for SMEs and retail businesses needing $10,000 or less. Applicants must provide the form, an application letter, beneficiary invoice, and bank wire transfer.

The seventh Johnston Press South Business Awards, held at Brighton’s Grand Hotel and hosted by Nick Wallis, celebrated businesses across the south coast. Chichester’s Guardian Angel Carers won Overall Business of the Year and Large Business of the Year. Other winners included Gardiner and Scardifield for customer service, Bespoke You Beauty Retreat and Spar for best startup, Ricardo Plc for innovation, Pearl Fit Out for small business, Nature Shop for green business, Transalis for medium-sized business, Talks at Six for community contribution, Digi Tool Box for employer, GTMS for best team, Olive and Vine for place to eat or drink, Brandon Relph for young achiever, Si Protech for manufacturing and construction, Southsea Bathing Hut for retailer, Dawn Lawrence for business personality, and Martin Putman for lifetime achievement.

The Supreme Court will consider whether Colorado’s 2019 law barring licensed mental health professionals from providing conversion therapy to minors violates free speech. Licensed counselor Kaley Chiles argues that because she uses only talk therapy, the law discriminates based on the content and viewpoint of her speech and should face strict scrutiny. She says Colorado lacks evidence that her counseling causes harm and that the law is both overinclusive and underinclusive.

A federal district court declined to block enforcement, and a divided 10th Circuit panel affirmed, holding that the law regulates professional conduct that only incidentally involves speech and therefore satisfies rational basis review. The federal government supports applying strict scrutiny, arguing that Colorado regulates Chiles’ messages because of their viewpoint and lacks persuasive evidence that the ban advances its stated interests.

Colorado contends the law narrowly prohibits an unsafe and ineffective treatment intended to change a minor’s sexual orientation or gender identity, while allowing other discussions and exempting religious ministry. It argues that states have traditionally regulated substandard health care, including care delivered through words, and warns that ruling for Chiles could destabilize health-care regulation. Colorado maintains that rational basis review applies but says the law could also survive strict scrutiny because protecting minors from harmful and ineffective treatment is a compelling interest.

The court affirmed a verdict for the defendants in an automobile-collision case. The jury instructions adequately presented the plaintiff’s allegations, including failure to sound a horn. The court was not required, absent specific requests or supporting pleadings, to instruct on intersection right-of-way or reduction of speed. Stating that both parties could lawfully use the highway was proper because the court also required each to exercise ordinary care. Instructions concerning statutory and ordinance violations did not exclude other negligence claims. Comparative-negligence instructions were authorized by evidence that both parties may have been negligent, despite the pleadings. Any error concerning damages was harmless because defendants prevailed. Conflicting evidence supported the verdict, and no legal error appeared.

NVIDIA appointed Donald F. Robertson Jr. Vice President, Chief Accounting Officer and Principal Accounting Officer effective June 17, 2019, reporting to CFO Colette Kress. Robertson previously held accounting leadership roles at Western Digital and SanDisk. He succeeds Michael Byron, who moved to a finance role focused on merger integration and financial systems. Robertson’s at-will employment includes a $650,000 annual salary, a repayable $600,000 signing bonus, 15,000 restricted stock units vesting over approximately four years, benefits, stock-purchase plan eligibility, and a standard indemnity agreement.

A100 includes 40 MB of shared, partitioned L2 cache, 6.7 times V100’s capacity, delivering 2.3 times higher bandwidth and 5,120 bytes/clock read bandwidth. It supports hardware coherence, MIG slice allocation, programmer-controlled cache residency, and compression providing up to fourfold DRAM and L2 read bandwidth improvements.

Travis Haydon, 20, was jailed for 18 months in a young offender institution after stabbing Liam Brown in the abdomen with a flick knife during an argument over a spilt drink at Plymouth’s Newmarket Tavern. Brown suffered a two-centimetre puncture wound, stayed overnight in hospital and was not thought to have lasting injuries. Haydon pleaded guilty to assault causing actual bodily harm, possessing an offensive weapon and cannabis, and breaching a suspended sentence for affray. The judge cited Haydon’s record of violence and weapons offences, alcohol and drug use, and said the case could have led to a more serious charge. His lawyer said Haydon feared being punched, had complied with his suspended sentence conditions and had a seriously ill father.

A 167-million-year-old fossil lizard discovered on Scotland’s Isle of Skye combined snake-like jaws and curved teeth with a short body and fully formed limbs. Named Breugnathair elgolensis, it was assigned to the newly defined predatory squamate group Parviraptoridae. Its mixture of snake- and gecko-like features shows they belonged to one animal, but researchers remain uncertain whether it was related to snake ancestors or independently evolved snake-like adaptations.

Breast cancer is the UK’s most common cancer, with around 56,000 new cases annually. Lumps vary: they may feel pea-sized, hard, irregular, or larger, and can occur anywhere in the breast or armpit. Other warning signs include swelling, changes in breast shape or size, skin dimpling, redness, rashes, unexplained pain, nipple inversion, discharge, or other nipple changes.

Regular self-examination every two weeks to monthly helps establish what is normal. Check breasts and armpits visually and by touch while standing, lying down, and sitting, noting any new or unfamiliar changes. Seek medical advice for concerning changes, even if they may be harmless. A doctor may review medical and family history, examine the breast, and arrange a referral.

Risk factors include BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations, early menstruation, later menopause, some reproductive factors, and prolonged combined hormone replacement therapy. An active lifestyle and breastfeeding may reduce risk. Men can also develop breast cancer, usually between ages 60 and 70, and should report lumps or nipple changes.

Early diagnosis improves the likelihood of effective treatment. Screening and treatment advances have almost doubled survival rates over 40 years, and more than three-quarters of diagnosed women remain alive after 10 years.

AI models Evo 1 and Evo 2 created bacteriophage genomes from scratch. Some resulting viruses outperformed a well-studied bacteria-killing strain in laboratory dishes, suggesting potential use in phage therapy.

SPYR announced that shareholders of record on May 19, 2017, would receive one share in a new spin-off company for each SPYR share owned. The spin-off will separate SPYR’s restaurant division and intends to register with the SEC as an independently traded company. It will focus on licensing or franchising the Eat at Joe’s name, manufacturing and distributing branded foods, and potentially acquiring food-concept companies.

Stock Market Media Group, SPYR’s exclusive publisher, stated that its content may include opinions and is not investment advice. It disclosed a one-year promotional services contract with SPYR beginning February 1, 2015, providing a $5,000 monthly fee and 250,000 restricted SPYR common shares, subject to securities laws and sales restrictions.

Saudi Aramco plans to change its Asian crude pricing formula from October, its first benchmark change since the mid-1980s. The formula will use a 50:50 average of DME Oman futures and Platts-assessed Dubai cash prices, replacing Platts assessments for both Oman and Dubai. The move is expected to increase DME Oman futures and derivatives liquidity. Aramco’s prices influence over 12 million barrels per day of Asia-bound crude. It remains unclear whether other Middle Eastern producers will follow.

The passage describes techniques for improving fast-forward, rewind, skipping, and other “trick-play” operations for streamed video. Instead of downloading complete video portions or relying on low-resolution thumbnails, a client buffers selected frames—often key frames—from areas outside the continuous normal-playback buffer. Metadata or indexes identify frame locations, enabling individual byte-range requests while omitting intervening frames. The selected frames provide frequently updated, faster-than-real-time playback with reduced latency and bandwidth use.

A streaming client maintains a normal buffer window containing continuous video and one or more trick-play windows containing subsets of frames. Frame selection, spacing, quality, bitrate, source stream, and buffer size may be adjusted according to playback rate, network performance, anticipated trick-play behavior, frame sizes, and jump points. Different trick-play windows may support different rates or resolutions. Missing intervening frames can later be downloaded and inserted without re-requesting cached frames, converting a trick-play region into continuous content for normal playback.

The system may use adaptive streaming across multiple representations of a video with different bitrates. A performance monitor measures factors such as latency, throughput, bandwidth, and jitter. A trick-play optimizer uses these metrics and content indexes to determine which frames to request and when. Multiple network channels may support overlapping downloads and abandonment of content that arrives too late to remain relevant.

Indexes may specify addresses, sizes, timestamps, and dependencies for key frames, delta frames, audio, trick-play sequences, or likely jump points. Jump points may be derived from metadata, content analysis, user activity, or logs. A proxy server can add indexing, metadata, alternate streams, or request translation when an origin server lacks required functionality. It may construct proxy streams containing only audio, video, key frames, or frames tailored to specific trick-play modes.

The architecture includes video repositories, streaming or proxy servers, clients, buffers, video players, performance monitors, and trick-play optimizers. It supports HTTP byte-range requests, HLS, and potentially other streaming protocols. Video players may dynamically adjust displayed frame timing, playback rates, scaling, and frame selection to approximate requested trick-play speeds despite sparse buffered frames or differing source qualities.

Chicago is preparing heightened security for three major sports events expected to draw enormous crowds: the Chicago Marathon, a Cubs playoff game and a Bears football game. Concerns intensified after the Las Vegas mass shooting and reports that the gunman had previously booked rooms overlooking Chicago’s Lollapalooza festival.

Security experts urged coordination with workers in nearby high-rises and public vigilance, while noting that copycat attacks are rare and layered defenses such as bag checks and metal detectors are effective. Measures introduced after the Boston Marathon bombing include random bag checks, restrictions on unattended belongings and limited access to marathon start and finish areas.

Mayor Rahm Emanuel said officials had reexamined plans and expressed full confidence in security. Chicago police will deploy 1,000 additional officers Sunday, including more undercover personnel among spectators, runners and near the finish line. Emergency officials are also coordinating with downtown buildings and considering threats from multiple locations, including high-rises.

Some runners said Las Vegas increased their concerns, particularly for their families, but did not deter them from participating.

Some parents are questioning Township High School District 113’s transparency in selecting Highland Park High School’s new principal, particularly why only two parents are on the 18-member stakeholder committee. The Florida appellate court reversed the denial of Genel Altimeaux’s unemployment benefits. The appeals referee had found that Altimeaux voluntarily quit Ocean Construction during a pay dispute involving Haitian workers. However, the finding relied solely on testimony from an initial hearing that Altimeaux did not attend and at which he could not cross-examine the supervisor who claimed he quit. At a second hearing, Altimeaux denied quitting, and another supervisor admitted he never personally heard Altimeaux say he would stop working. Because the initial testimony was incompetent and the remaining evidence did not establish that Altimeaux voluntarily quit, the court directed reinstatement of his unemployment award.

DoorDash unveiled Dot, a nearly five-foot-tall autonomous delivery robot designed to travel on sidewalks, roads, and bike lanes as part of a hybrid delivery system involving people, drones, and autonomous vehicles. Equipped with nine cameras and seven other sensors, Dot was developed by DoorDash Labs, while the company also partners with Coco Robotics.

Delivery robots have improved but often still rely on remote human intervention. Researchers equipped greater noctule bats with biologgers that recorded movement, altitude and sound to investigate how they hunt migrating songbirds at night. Among 611 hunting events, two involved bats climbing above 1,200 meters, approaching birds with high-frequency feeding buzzes and diving vertically. One bird escaped, while another was captured and consumed during a 23-minute flight, with distress calls, chewing and normal flight recorded. Additional evidence included severed bird wings bearing greater noctule bite DNA and captured bats with blood and feathers around their mouths. Although no video was recorded, the findings provide evidence that greater noctules capture, dismember and eat songbirds in flight.

Pin and Pull is a perimeter running play that uses down blocks to create favorable angles and pulling linemen as lead blockers in space. Its strengths are placing extra blockers at the point of attack, adapting blocking assignments to defensive fronts, and allowing the tailback to run from the C-gap to the sideline based on the guards’ blocks. It requires at least two guards capable of pulling effectively and works best with a fast tailback who can threaten horizontally and turn vertically with one cut.

Unlike the original Buck Sweep, which includes a simultaneous inside run threat such as a fullback dive, Pin and Pull is a true perimeter run. Against both 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, linemen use combinations of down, reach, back, and pull blocks. The right guard generally kicks out the edge defender, while the left guard reads that block and either inserts inside or wraps around. The tailback follows the left guard, and receivers block second-level defenders.

Variations include an under-center toss using receiver motion to draw in the cornerback and a tight end-wing toss formation that creates a four-man blocking surface and advantageous angles.

Brock University researchers found that rosemary extract inhibited the growth, survival and spread of aggressive human lung cancer cells in laboratory tests. The extract promoted programmed cell death, blocked the Akt signalling pathway and prevented activation of certain proteins involved in cancer cell multiplication. Researchers said the findings suggest potential anti-tumour and chemopreventive properties but cautioned against recommending increased rosemary consumption. Further studies will examine whether carnosic acid and rosmarinic acid are responsible for the effects.

The MSPM0G3519/G3518/G1519/G1518 devices include an RTC_B operating from a 32kHz source, with calendar counters, binary or BCD formats, leap-year correction, configurable calendar and periodic alarms, standby interrupt capability, ±240ppm calibration and temperature compensation, and a GPIO calibration output.

Jane Goodall, who died October 1 at 91, preserved skeletons of known chimpanzees from Tanzania’s Gombe National Park alongside studying their social lives. COTUTOR is an AI-assisted educational framework integrating generative AI, Bayesian Knowledge Tracing, signal processing, and convex optimization to provide personalized learning support. Unlike systems relying mainly on end-to-end generation or retrieval-augmented prompts, it maintains an explicit, interpretable model of each student’s evolving knowledge state. The framework aims to improve transparency, computational efficiency, pedagogical oversight, and real-time adaptation.

COTUTOR continuously collects time-series signals from submissions, grades, participation logs, resource access, chatbot queries, and feedback. It smooths, normalizes, aggregates, and embeds these signals before updating mastery probabilities through Bayesian Knowledge Tracing. An iterative algorithm then recommends resources, updates policy parameters through regularized optimization, and refines each student’s latent learning representation.

For programming education, COTUTOR uses Online Judge data such as submission verdicts, errors, execution efficiency, timestamps, attempts, and problem difficulty. Correct and incorrect submissions update estimated mastery using learning, slip, and guess rates. The system can recommend harder exercises, reviews, or targeted interventions based on these estimates.

Implemented through My Code Weapon and Nemobot, its chatbot provides reminders, answers questions, recommends linked resources, tracks learning trajectories, and adapts task difficulty. Reliability measures include standardized references, output logging, and instructor review.

A case study formulates educational resource allocation as a convex optimization problem across multiple sessions and resource types. It incorporates resource budgets, prerequisite relationships, student sentiment, emotional volatility, and alternative influence functions. COTUTOR optimizes allocations for individual students or collectively by maximizing minimum sentiment. Evaluation hypotheses compare its knowledge-state estimation and learning outcomes with traditional instruction, BKT, DKT, and code-DKT. The passage reports that benchmarking and a controlled classroom study indicated improved performance, engagement, retention, and learning effectiveness.

Researchers conducted the first large-scale trial using poplar trees fortified with probiotic bacteria to remove trichloroethylene (TCE) from contaminated groundwater at a California Superfund site. At the trial site, inoculated trees were larger, healthier and more resilient than untreated trees after one and three years, while containing greatly reduced TCE levels. Groundwater downstream also had lower TCE concentrations, and increased chloride near the roots provided evidence that bacteria inside the trees were degrading the pollutant.

The method enhances phytoremediation by protecting trees from TCE’s toxic effects while accelerating its breakdown. Researchers say it could offer a lower-cost, sustainable alternative to conventional cleanup methods such as excavation and groundwater pumping.

The passage describes multi-camera imaging systems that combine images from economical or low-performance cameras to detect faint or low-contrast objects. Co-registering and combining N images can improve signal-to-noise ratio by approximately √N, increase effective bit depth, support advanced deconvolution, and reduce cosmic-ray artifacts without altering individual camera optics.

Three configurations are presented. A common field array points multiple cameras at a shared region and combines their images. A hybrid field array combines images within overlapping camera sub-arrays and stitches the results into a wider composite view. An adaptive field array initially surveys a broad area, then automatically redirects cameras toward a detected target to create a shared field and higher-sensitivity image.

The scalable architecture may use co-located or geographically dispersed cameras, network switches, distributed computing, GPS, and raw, uncompressed image data. Cameras can be added, removed, partitioned into independently steerable sub-arrays, or organized hierarchically.

Calibration processes address dark frames, flat fields, sensor bias, lens distortion, and sky coordinates. Processing includes star matching, image registration, pixel summation, masking, streak detection, streak characterization, and initial orbit determination. Detected orbital parameters may be compared with a space-object catalog; unmatched objects are classified as uncorrelated targets for follow-up. Applications include astrophotography, space-object detection and tracking, tactical sensing, and night vision.

The patent describes scanning ladar transmitter designs intended to improve dwell time, coverage, and compactness. Optical field splitter/inverters rearrange resonant scan patterns so slower scan portions cover central or otherwise important regions, while faster portions move to field edges. Prism, W-shaped reflector, paired-mirror, and adjustable overlapping configurations are disclosed to increase centerline gaze and support dynamic field-of-view control.

For Lissajous scanning, periodic phase drift can be applied to one or both mirrors to reduce scan gaps and blind spots in selected regions without sacrificing pattern periodicity. A feedback process identifies excessive gaps, optimizes drift parameters using total least squares, and can update the pattern per frame.

The patent also discloses a compact beam scanner using an ellipsoidal conjugate reflector between two scanning mirrors. Placing the mirrors near the ellipsoid’s focal points reimages the beam onto the second mirror, permitting smaller, similarly sized mirrors and potentially increasing scan speed, tilt angle, and field of view. A focusing element and coplanar-angle design constraint maintain collimation and reduce scan-field distortion. Applications include vehicle autonomy, surveillance, mapping, remote sensing, biomedical imaging, and virtual or augmented reality.

Natural zircon single-crystal plates were shock-compressed to 13.6 and 51.3 GPa to examine phase transformation and trace-element behavior. X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy showed that zircon remained the dominant phase at 13.6 GPa, although it became strongly fractured and developed localized structural defects. At 51.3 GPa, it transformed predominantly into textured, mosaic reidite with minor residual stressed zircon, which was more abundant near fractures.

Cathodoluminescence intensity decreased and shifted toward shorter wavelengths with increasing pressure. Reidite contained numerous micrometer-scale, crystallographically organized regions with enhanced rare-earth-element luminescence, especially from Dy³⁺. These regions were interpreted as segregation of trace cations along planar defects generated during the zircon–reidite transition. Because segregation occurred within tens of seconds without prolonged annealing, rapid transport through vacancies, grain boundaries, dislocations, or interstitial configurations was proposed. The reconstructive transition may alter charge-compensating defects, expel some substituting trivalent ions from lattice sites, and promote their migration.

Shock loading caused extensive fracturing, with fracture patterns differing nonlinearly between pressures. The resulting increase in surface area and trace-element segregation may enable rapid element release during interaction with fluids or melts, while bulk isotopic characteristics and trace-element ratios in zircon and reidite may remain approximately those of the original zircon.

Asteroid Bennu has an estimated 1-in-2,700 chance of hitting Earth around September 21, 2135. Although Bennu is not considered an extinction-level threat, the study aims to prepare for future hazardous objects. NASA detects about 1,000 near-Earth objects annually, though roughly 10,000 may remain unidentified. Bennu’s well-studied shape and orbit make it useful for testing defense calculations. American Electric Power acquired Enron Wind’s 160-megawatt Indian Mesa project for $175 million, while Credit Suisse First Boston resigned from Enron’s creditors committee. The Consumer Mortgage Coalition urged the Treasury Department to let mortgage lenders use the National Directory of New Hires for rapid, consent-based income verification amid problems with the IRS’s IVES system. It said the alternative could prevent closing delays and expand credit access, while also requesting congressional funding to modernize IVES.

Eric Fung, 37, left California for Tokyo after becoming dissatisfied with Bay Area costs and culture. His career included advertising, startups, founding and exiting a company, and opening three restaurants. He now leads US-registered Colega AI with a largely Asia-based remote team, targeting Japan’s many small businesses. Fung faces language and cultural barriers while adapting to Japan’s hierarchical work culture. He and his wife appreciate Tokyo’s safety, convenience, dining, and lower housing and everyday costs, though forming friendships remains difficult.
ESPN highlights creative 2025 MLB ballpark foods, the Oct. 9 Savannah Bananas selection show, and Stephen A. Smith’s reaction to a Yankees comeback.

Sirius XM has fixed-rate debt near 4.3%, strong cash flow coverage, and 11–12% ROIC versus roughly 6% WACC. Satellite spending cuts could increase free cash flow about 20% by 2026, while share repurchases support per-share value. Trading at 7.6× EV/EBITDA versus a historical 15×, the author estimates 2–3× upside and discloses a long position.

CompareCards highlights credit cards offering introductory 0% APR periods of 6 to 18 months for purchases and up to 21 months generally, alongside cash-back, travel-reward, and sign-up bonuses. Featured issuers include Discover, Bank of America, Citi, Capital One, and Wells Fargo, with post-promotional variable APRs, balance-transfer fees, spending requirements, and reward structures varying by card. Some cards have no annual or foreign transaction fees.

Low-interest cards can reduce borrowing costs, but introductory rates eventually revert to standard APRs. Variable APRs may change with prevailing rates, while fixed APRs remain relatively stable. Consumers should review application terms for current details. CompareCards states that its editors use a data-driven system covering over 100 cards from more than 50 issuers and that compensation from listed companies does not influence ratings or reviews.

Bayhorse Silver increased its proposed private placement to 3 million units at C$0.10 each, targeting C$300,000, subject to TSX-V approval. Each unit includes one share and half a warrant exercisable at C$0.15 for 24 months. Proceeds will support Bayhorse Silver Mine equipment, working capital, and administrative costs.

The automated fare collection (AFC) system market was valued at $4.81 billion in 2016 and is projected to reach $12.81 billion by 2024, with a 13.3% CAGR. AFC automates public-transport ticketing through components such as gates, vending machines, and ticket checkers, improving efficiency, accuracy, security, and transaction speed. Growth is driven by technological adoption, new transportation systems, and government investment, while limited awareness and smart-card use are restraints. The market is segmented by component, application, technology platform, and geography. Major participants include Cubic Transportation Systems, NXP Semiconductors, Samsung SDS, Thales Group, Omron, and LG CNS.

Massachusetts lawmakers passed supplemental budget bills providing $15 million to districts educating more than 2,300 students who arrived from Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria. Funding would follow the existing education aid formula based on additional enrollment. Springfield accepted the most students. House and Senate differences must be resolved before the bill reaches Gov. Baker.

A study of the 2014–2016 West African Ebola epidemic found that 3 percent of patients caused about 61 percent of infections. Although each patient infected an average of 2.39 people, many infected no one, while a few “superspreaders” sustained transmission. Spread occurred mainly among people who remained at home, where caregivers and traditional funeral practices increased exposure to infectious bodily fluids; transmission declined after hospitalization. Age was identified as a predictor, as sick children and elderly people often attracted close contact from caregivers. The epidemic infected more than 28,000 people and killed at least 11,000 across Guinea, Sierra Leone and Liberia. It was ultimately controlled through safe burials, rapid hospitalization and other public health measures. Researchers said identifying high-risk behaviors and demographics could help contain future epidemics.

The passage describes methods for reducing signaling, latency, collisions, and power consumption when transmitting small uplink data in 5G NR. A network may broadcast contention-based configured-grant PUSCH resources and NOMA parameters, allowing UEs in RRC-IDLE or RRC-INACTIVE states to transmit without conventional connection establishment. Configurations may specify time-frequency resources, periodicity, DMRS ports, multiple-access signatures, interleavers, coding, guard bands, and extended cyclic prefixes.

To mitigate grant-free NOMA collisions, UE-specific reference bits derived from UE and multiple-access identities may be jointly encoded with information bits using systematic LDPC coding. The reference bits may form a preamble or DMRS for activity detection, channel estimation, signature identification, and improved decoding. Additional techniques include UE-specific interleaving, rate matching, symbol spreading, sparse subcarrier mapping, asynchronous-transmission protection, response monitoring, and retransmission procedures. NOMA may also reduce collisions during random access by distinguishing UEs that selected the same preamble.

After unexpectedly passing an online “Jeopardy!” test, John Kizer reflects on how the brain stores and recalls memories. Neuroscience still lacks consensus on the physiological, cellular or molecular basis of learning and memory, despite its importance for aging populations. Experiments have produced conflicting evidence: Karl Lashley’s work suggested memories are distributed throughout the brain, while Wilder Penfield elicited specific memories by stimulating localized areas. Recent UCLA research indicates RNA may transfer memory in snails, echoing James McConnell’s 1960s experiments in which trained flatworms were fed to others. Kizer unsuccessfully attempted to replicate McConnell’s findings in his youth, illustrating that scientific research is often uncertain and difficult to interpret.

Acting CDC Director Jim O’Neill approved recommendations allowing people over 6 months to receive updated Covid-19 vaccines after discussing risks and benefits with providers. The decision enables states to order shots for low-income children through the Vaccines for Children program, though prescription requirements remain unclear. O’Neill also endorsed separate MMR and chickenpox shots for children under 4.

Agents Mutual plans to float OnTheMarket.com on London’s Alternative Investment Market and raise £50 million to compete with market leaders Rightmove and Zoopla. The funds will support marketing, sales, customer relations and technology, including a national advertising campaign. OnTheMarket, launched in 2015 and currently Britain’s third-largest property portal, recently abandoned its mutual status and secured long-term listing agreements with several property firms. Analyst George Salmon said the strategy was sensible but warned that challenging Rightmove remained difficult. The company also won a case supporting its rule limiting agents to one additional rival portal.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture improves programmable shading, ray tracing, AI processing, memory, interconnects, I/O, and power efficiency over Turing. Second-generation RT Cores provide up to twice the ray-tracing performance, support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute, and accelerate motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32, BF16, and structured sparsity, enabling higher AI throughput, accelerated denoising, and DLSS at resolutions up to 8K. Redesigned SMs double peak FP32 processing, expand L1/shared memory, and increase shared-memory bandwidth.

GA102 includes up to seven GPCs, 84 SMs, 112 ROPs, a 384-bit memory interface, and 6 MB of L2 cache. Third-generation NVLink can combine two A40 or RTX A6000 GPUs for 96 GB of memory, while PCIe 4.0 doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth. GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling to reach 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/s bandwidth.

RTX IO works with Microsoft DirectStorage to move compressed data directly from storage to the GPU for decompression, reducing CPU use and accelerating loading. GA10x also supports HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K displays, hardware AV1 decoding, and hardware video encoding.

The A40 targets data-center visual computing, while the RTX A6000 targets professional workstations; both offer 48 GB of GDDR6 and NVLink scaling. GeForce RTX 30-series products apply these features to gaming and creation, with the RTX 3090 providing 24 GB of GDDR6X and the RTX 3070 using GDDR6. Ampere GPUs are stated to be up to 1.9 times as power efficient as Turing at equal performance.

Police are seeking witnesses after a father was allegedly spat at, punched and kicked in Coed Bach Park, Pontarddulais, on 29 June. The attack occurred after he asked a moped rider to take more care around children. His children witnessed the assault. Police issued descriptions of two male attackers and a woman accompanying them.

The Tax Court reviewed an IRS determination permitting levy collection of Robert Eugene Poindexter’s unpaid 1994 and 1996 income taxes, which he had reported on his own returns but not paid. Poindexter claimed the reported liabilities were inaccurate, principally because of a royalty dispute with record companies, and requested IRS assistance in obtaining information from them. He declined to specify whether his income was overstated or understated, file amended returns, propose collection alternatives, or identify incorrect income, deductions, credits, or computations.

The Court rejected the IRS’s argument that taxpayers cannot challenge self-reported liabilities in a collection due process hearing, citing Montgomery v. Commissioner. Nevertheless, it granted summary judgment for the IRS because Poindexter failed to allege specific facts showing that the assessments were erroneous or establishing any other procedural error. The Appeals officer had verified compliance with applicable requirements and determined that the levy appropriately balanced efficient collection against intrusiveness. The proposed levy was therefore sustained.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed income tax deficiencies assessed against Pacific Basin Manufacturing & Trade Company for 1975 and 1976. Although the American Samoa-based corporation qualified under 26 U.S.C. § 931(a) to exclude possession-sourced income, payments from its Hawaiian parent were deposited into its Honolulu bank account. Under § 931(b), otherwise excludable amounts are taxable when received within the United States. Applying the ordinary meaning of “received,” the court held that the taxpayer obtained custody and control of the funds in Honolulu. It rejected the argument that receipt should depend on the location of the corporation’s primary operations, reasoning that this interpretation would largely nullify § 931(b).

The burglary policies excluded coverage unless the insured kept records enabling the insurers to determine the loss accurately. Plaintiff kept a check-cashing fund of cash and payroll checks in a safe and recorded only its aggregate total, allegedly $2,922, on a scratch pad. After a burglary, he recovered $182 by recalling details of two stolen checks, and the jury awarded $2,740.

The court held that substantial compliance with the record-keeping clause required separate identification of each check, including information permitting claims against its drawer. Because adequate records could have reduced the loss further, the aggregate scratch-pad notation was insufficient. The judgment was reversed and the case remanded with directions to dismiss the complaint.

The National Endowment for the Humanities and First Nations Development Institute will each contribute about $2 million to support tribal Native language revitalization programs. Funding will prioritize effective immersion initiatives and established language retention or restoration efforts through a competitive nationwide proposal process. An advisory committee will evaluate submissions, with about 15 programs funded annually. Alaska languages such as Tlingit and Central Yup’ik may be strong candidates.

Louisiana Rep. Garret Graves said the shooting of Rep. Steve Scalise and three others reflected harmful political divisiveness, rhetoric and misinformation. Scalise remained in critical condition after being shot by James T. Hodgkinson, a former Bernie Sanders campaign volunteer with anti-Republican views, though police had not identified a motive. Sanders condemned the violence and advocated nonviolent action. Some Republicans said political hostility had increasingly promoted threats, while President Donald Trump called for national unity, safety and peace.

An Ilorin court remanded herdsmen Shehu Abubakar and Abdulkareem Maikudi for allegedly fatally beating colleague Musa Kareem with sticks after a cell phone dispute. Charged with criminal conspiracy and culpable homicide, they were denied bail and held at Okekura Prisons pending further investigation. The case was adjourned until July 12.

U.S. enrollment in language education is declining, threatening programs, particularly German and French. The article argues that language education should emphasize that “language connects” people, cultures, and communities.

An imagined-communities approach helps students envision themselves authentically using a target language and participating in its cultures. Implemented through task-based instruction, it uses plausible real-world scenarios, authentic materials, student autonomy, and just-in-time support. Activities may include selecting and furnishing an apartment abroad, navigating transportation, shopping, planning meals, exploring university courses, applying for jobs, or contacting landlords.

A yearlong study in two eighth-grade German classrooms found that students explored language and culture more deeply, viewed cultures in new ways, and felt greater connection to target-language speakers and communities. Many also continued studying the language beyond required years, though this was not formally measured.

Implementation requires instructors to design context-specific scenarios, activities, and authentic assessments aligned with curriculum and student interests. No additional funding is necessary, but substantial planning, collaboration, documentation, reflection, and revision may be needed. The approach can be adapted across K–16 education, proficiency levels, contexts, and languages to strengthen connection, engagement, retention, and language-program sustainability.

A May 3, 2001 news digest highlights Enron-related energy developments. Pompano Beach planned a public hearing on Enron’s proposed power plant. California officials debated refusing electricity purchases above set prices, weighing lower costs against increased blackouts and economic harm. Indian lenders sought government help resolving Dabhol Power’s dispute with Maharashtra over electricity pricing and $48 million in unpaid bills; Dabhol agreed to meet a renegotiation panel without committing to revise its contract.

The Democratic National Committee criticized energy-industry influence on the Bush administration’s policies. Innogy began European electricity trading, while European corporations increasingly used credit derivatives to manage payment risks. Allegheny Energy purchased three Enron plants totaling 1,710 MW. Enron also agreed to supply 200 MW of wind turbines for EnergieKontor projects in Germany and Spain.

Other reports covered Mosaic Group’s revenue growth and expanded New Power contract, improving European telecom bond prospects, reduced forecasts for U.S. power-generation profitability after 2001, Fitch’s stable outlook for Northern Border entities, and Scottish Power’s restructuring and possible asset sales.

Amazon.com’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2019 reported Q3 net sales of $70.0 billion, up 24% year over year, while operating income declined from $3.7 billion to $3.2 billion and net income fell from $2.9 billion to $2.1 billion. For the first nine months, net sales rose 20% to $193.1 billion, operating income increased to $10.7 billion, and net income reached $8.3 billion.

Q3 sales were $42.6 billion for North America, $18.3 billion for International, and $9.0 billion for AWS. Segment operating income was $1.3 billion, a $386 million loss, and $2.3 billion, respectively. At September 30, Amazon had $199.1 billion in assets, $56.5 billion in stockholders’ equity, and $43.4 billion in cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, and marketable securities. Operating cash flow for the trailing twelve months was $35.3 billion.

Amazon adopted new lease accounting guidance, recognizing approximately $21 billion in operating lease assets and liabilities. It had $24.3 billion of unsecured senior notes outstanding and total contractual commitments of $137.3 billion. The company also disclosed ongoing tax, regulatory, and legal contingencies.

The work evaluates steady-state variance reduction techniques (VRTs) in time-dependent Monte Carlo neutron transport and examines their interactions with population control techniques (PCTs). VRTs such as implicit capture, weight windows, CADIS, FW-CADIS, and Cooper-Larsen improve statistical efficiency by modifying particle weights and distributions. PCTs regulate particle populations between time steps; uniform combing preserves weight-distribution shape on average, while weight-based combing resets surviving particles to a uniform weight.

Tests used Shift, coupled with DENOVO for adjoint calculations, and the fully time-dependent MC/DC code. Performance was measured using a figure of merit based on runtime and variance, including auxiliary simulation costs.

In Shift’s pulsed-slab problem, FW-CADIS produced the highest average efficiency, though gains were modest because weight windows lacked time dependence, weight-based combing was mandatory, and the problem was relatively simple. Its benefits increased at later times as the flux became more spatially heterogeneous.

In MC/DC’s AZURV1 benchmark, Cooper-Larsen weight windows combined with uniform combing substantially improved statistics in low-flux regions. Time-dependent weight windows outperformed static windows. Combining weight windows with weight-based combing caused excessive splitting and memory exhaustion because combing reset particle weights out of alignment with the windows. Implicit capture also performed poorly with uniform combing.

The moving-surface SCRAM problem similarly showed that population control improved efficiency and manageability. Cooper-Larsen weight windows with uniform combing performed best, while weight windows with weight-based combing again failed because of excessive splitting.

The results show that method compatibility is critical. Cooper-Larsen weight windows and uniform combing can provide effective global variance reduction, whereas weight windows with weight-based combing and implicit capture with uniform combing can reduce efficiency. Time-dependent adaptations of steady-state VRTs offer further potential for efficient large-scale dynamic simulations.

The speaker felt energized despite extensive power-play and penalty-killing duties. He credited the team’s four scoring lines and strong penalty killing, while noting difficult ice and effective shot blocking. After maintaining composure, he found an open lane, shot high past Irbe, and capitalized on the opportunity.

Energy Central’s January 15, 2002 newsletter covers power-industry developments, led by Enron’s collapse, investigations into document destruction and accounting practices, political contributions, bankruptcy proceedings, and UBS’s acquisition of Enron’s trading business. Other reports address National Grid’s Niagara Mohawk takeover, California utility procurement and bankruptcy disputes, electricity deregulation, mergers, regulation, power pricing, outages, renewable and nuclear energy, environmental policy, international electricity markets, and utility stock performance.

A New York Times survey found widespread dissatisfaction among responding federal judges with the Supreme Court’s emergency docket decisions involving President Donald Trump’s second-term policies. Of 65 judges, 47 said the Court had not used the docket appropriately, while 48 said lower courts lacked sufficient guidance. Of 54 respondents, 42 said the orders harmed public perception of the judiciary.

At least seven of roughly 20 emergency orders lacked reasoning, and nearly all benefited Trump, enabling major policy actions. Respondents included 28 Republican and 37 Democratic presidential nominees. The Times acknowledged they may not represent the entire judiciary, while critics argued the survey may have disproportionately attracted dissatisfied judges and included districts sympathetic to challenges against Trump policies.

The court affirmed the denial of unemployment benefits, finding substantial evidence that Moss committed disqualifying misconduct by threatening his supervisor with a box cutter. His denial presented a credibility issue for the Appeal Board.

JPMorgan downgraded Valero Energy from Overweight to Neutral while raising its price target from $75 to $78. Analysts said improved capital discipline, stable returns and stronger free cash flow have already lifted its valuation, while further gains may take time due to industry cyclicality. JPMorgan expects cash flow to cover dividends but says buybacks could cease, estimating 6% total return potential versus 7% for the group.

Nigeria launched its National Cancer Control Plan 2018–2022 to improve equitable access to cost-effective cancer diagnosis, treatment, and medicines. BIO Ventures for Global Health presented the African Access Initiative (AAI), which supports Nigeria through delivery of medicines, technologies, training, infrastructure development, and clinical and research capacity building. AAI, developed with several international partners, initially operates in Nigeria, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, Kenya, and Rwanda. BVGH completed needs assessments at eight Nigerian hospitals, with eight more underway, to identify gaps and develop sustainable access to cancer treatment.
