The address recommends consolidating federal legal work under the Attorney General, modifying restrictions on special oil-case counsel, and continued federal and state enforcement of Prohibition. It concludes that prosperity and peace require sustained work, public confidence, international generosity, moderation, justice, and national intellectual, moral, and spiritual development.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 26, 2016 reported quarterly net sales of $50.6 billion, down 13% year over year, and net income of $10.5 billion, down from $13.6 billion. Diluted earnings per share declined to $1.90 from $2.33, while gross margin fell to 39.4% from 40.8%. Lower iPhone sales and weaker foreign currencies drove the decline, partly offset by growth in Services and Other Products.

Quarterly iPhone revenue fell 18% to $32.9 billion on 51.2 million units; iPad revenue declined 19% to $4.4 billion; and Mac revenue decreased 9% to $5.1 billion. Services revenue rose 20% to $6.0 billion, while Other Products increased 30% to $2.2 billion. Regional sales declined in the Americas, Europe, Greater China and Rest of Asia Pacific, while Japan increased 24%.

For the first six months, net sales were $126.4 billion and net income was $28.9 billion, compared with $132.6 billion and $31.6 billion a year earlier. Operating cash flow was $39.1 billion. Apple spent $13.5 billion on share repurchases and $5.9 billion on dividends and dividend equivalents, while issuing $15.5 billion of term debt.

At March 26, 2016, Apple had $232.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, total assets of $305.3 billion, liabilities of $174.8 billion and shareholders’ equity of $130.5 billion. Commercial paper totaled $8.0 billion, and total term debt was $71.9 billion. Apple expected third-quarter gross margin of 37.5%–38.0%.

The filing also discussed supply concentration, foreign exchange and interest-rate exposure, tax uncertainties, legal proceedings and product-related risks. The European Commission continued investigating alleged Irish state aid, with Apple unable to estimate the potential impact. Samsung paid Apple $548 million in December 2015 related to patent litigation, though further proceedings remained pending.

Pet owners spend nearly £3,500 in the first year on average, ranging from £769 for fish to £12,654 for horses. Insurance claims also highlight potential costs from veterinary care and pet-caused household damage. Nationwide advises prospective owners to budget carefully for lifelong expenses.

Dr Chukwuma Agubata of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, said Irvingia fat from ogbono nuts could improve the delivery and efficacy of the anti-malaria drug Artemether, which has low water solubility and limited absorption. Researchers formulated the fat as microparticles that carried the drug into the bloodstream. Agubata said taking ogbono soup with Artemether could aid its effectiveness and called for government and private support to expand production and research.

On 9 December, Palmerston North Rescue Helicopter transported three injured patients: a man with a suspected spinal injury, a motorcyclist with a fractured leg, and a boy with a back injury. The donation-supported PSRT operates rescue helicopters across the Central North Island.

Ariel Miranda pitched seven shutout innings, allowing four hits with five strikeouts and no walks, as Seattle beat Miami 6-1. He aggressively relied on his fastball, throwing it 63 times among 97 pitches. Robinson Cano broke a slump with a 441-foot homer, and Nelson Cruz followed with a 410-foot blast, providing key run support.

Oil prices fell as easing Middle East tensions and progress toward a Gaza ceasefire reduced supply concerns. Brent dropped 1.4% to $65.07 per barrel, while WTI declined to $61.55. Rising U.S. inventories, slowing transport and manufacturing demand, increased non-OPEC production, and subdued consumption in Europe and parts of Asia also pressured prices. Analysts expect supply-demand fundamentals and macroeconomic data to drive relatively stable short-term markets unless geopolitical tensions return.

The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau finalized rules requiring payday and auto title lenders to verify borrowers can repay loans within 30 days and limiting repeated account debits without authorization. The CFPB found that over 80 percent of payday loans are rolled over or followed by another loan within two weeks. Consumer advocates say the rules will prevent debt traps, while the industry warns they could eliminate regulated credit options for millions. The CFPB estimates loan volume could fall by half, forcing many stores to close. The rules, scheduled for 2019, face possible reversal by congressional Republicans seeking to weaken the CFPB and Dodd-Frank regulations. Separately, federal regulators lifted restrictions on banks making small-dollar loans. A Pew poll found 70 percent of surveyed adults favored greater payday-lender regulation.

The defendants sought dismissal because County Attorney Bill Vassar left office in January 1939 and his successor, Frank McVey, was not substituted within six months as required by Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 25(d). The court found the rule and corresponding federal statute mandatory and applicable despite the claim that Vassar was merely a nominal party acting for Oklahoma. It held that the actions had abated and dismissed all eight cases without prejudice, allowing the plaintiff exceptions.

The study examines how preservice language teachers reconstruct professional identities by negotiating personal beliefs, emotions, and priorities with institutional expectations and classroom realities. Drawing on borderland discourse, it treats identity as multiple, fluid, socially situated, and continuously negotiated through language, practice, and relationships.

Narratives from Laura and Richard/Ricardo’s internship reports and Moodle interactions from 2010–2011 reveal tensions between university theory and public-school practice. Laura initially identified gaps in her preparation but developed a flexible, critical teacher identity centered on adapting methods, responding to students, and maintaining professional autonomy. Richard criticized traditional, content-focused training and expressed anxiety about evaluation and authority. Although he significantly developed his professional identity, he ultimately rejected becoming a foreign-language teacher and identified as a mother-language teacher.

The study identifies shifting identities as student, intern, language teacher, and sociocultural actor, without a fixed developmental order. It emphasizes supervised internships, virtual and face-to-face communities, and personal narratives as important spaces for reflection, emotional support, and professional identity reconstruction.

Yen Bai plans to expand high-tech agro-forestry-fishery processing, branding and markets by leveraging major supplies of timber, tea, cinnamon and cassava. Existing processing facilities are numerous but often use low-tech equipment, limiting product quality. The province seeks investment in export furniture, tea, cassava, cinnamon oil, camellia fruit, bamboo shoots and cattle meat processing. Wood-processing revenue is targeted at 850 billion VND by 2020 and twice that by 2025, while camellia and bamboo-shoot value is targeted at 200 billion VND by 2025.

Researchers analyzing Gulf of Alaska data found that marine heatwaves altered plankton communities and disrupted the ocean’s biological carbon pump, slowing carbon transport from the surface to the deep sea. During the 2013–2015 heatwave, carbon particles accumulated around 200 meters deep; during the 2019–2020 event, recycled carbon and detritus built up near the surface before lingering at 200–400 meters. Shifts toward small grazers that produce less fast-sinking waste kept carbon circulating in upper waters, increasing its potential return to the atmosphere rather than long-term deep-ocean storage.

The study combined more than a decade of robotic-float measurements with ship-based plankton surveys, pigment chemistry, and environmental DNA sequencing. Because the two heatwaves affected food webs differently, researchers emphasized sustained, coordinated monitoring before, during, and after such events. Marine heatwaves have expanded and intensified in recent decades, potentially weakening ocean carbon storage and affecting ecosystems, fisheries, and climate.

Austria-Hungary informed neutral powers that the enemy governments had rejected the Central Powers’ proposal for peace negotiations without offering a counterproposal or learning their terms. It denied that the initiative was insincere, maintained that Austria-Hungary and its allies had acted defensively rather than seeking territorial conquest, and accused their adversaries of expansionist aims and inconsistent support for national rights and small states. The government declined to revisit responsibility for the war or debate the military situation, asserting that both were already clear. It placed responsibility for continued conflict on its opponents and declared that Austria-Hungary and its allies would continue fighting until obtaining a peace securing their peoples’ existence, honor, development, and equal cooperation among European states.

The lecture reviews coherent states as annihilation-operator eigenstates closely related to classical electromagnetic fields. Their phase-space distributions rotate at the field frequency, exhibit Poissonian photon statistics, and saturate the Heisenberg uncertainty limit. Three quasi-probability representations are discussed: the always-positive Q function, the Glauber-Sudarshan P representation, and the Wigner function, whose projections give position and momentum distributions but which may be negative.

Light fluctuations are characterized using the second-order coherence function \(g^{(2)}\) and the Fano factor. Coherent light is Poissonian with \(g^{(2)}=1\); thermal light is super-Poissonian with \(g^{(2)}=2\); and photon-number states are sub-Poissonian with \(g^{(2)}=(n-1)/n\), reaching zero for a single photon. Values below one indicate non-classical light.

Attenuating a coherent state does not create a single-photon Fock state because photon-number fluctuations remain. Single photons can instead be produced using single atoms in cavities or heralded Raman transitions in atomic ensembles. The Hanbury Brown–Twiss experiment measures photon correlations using a beam splitter and two detectors, distinguishing coherent, thermal, and single-photon light. Single-mode treatments lack nontrivial time dependence; temporal coherence behavior arises from multiple modes or repeatedly replenished sources.

Starbucks shares have been roughly flat since late 2015, largely amid weaker U.S. comparable-store sales. Mobile Order & Pay created congestion at some stores, though management reported improvements. Promotions such as the Unicorn drink and Frappuccino Happy Hour may support sales, while loyalty-program changes and revised traffic reporting had previously hurt results. Starbucks began paying quarterly dividends in 2010 and increased its payout from 20 to 25 cents per share in November 2016, with dividend growth exceeding a 26% compound annual rate. In China, the company is opening about 500 stores annually, recorded 7% comparable-store sales growth last quarter, and expects sustained expansion.

Celebrity chef Mario Batali stepped away from daily operations of his restaurant empire and took leave from ABC’s “The Chew” after Eater New York reported sexual misconduct allegations involving at least four women over 20 years. Batali acknowledged the complaints matched his past behavior, apologized and accepted responsibility. His company said an October employee report was its first formal complaint and resulted in reprimand and training. ABC announced a review, while Food Network suspended plans to revive “Molto Mario.” Batali rose to fame through that show and co-owns numerous restaurants through Batali & Bastianich Hospitality Group.

Carolina Panthers quarterback Cam Newton apologized for calling it “funny” that female reporter Jourdan Rodrigue asked about routes. After backlash and losing his Oikos sponsorship, Newton called his remarks degrading and unacceptable, accepted responsibility, and urged young people to learn from his mistake.

The Fifth Circuit held that above-median-income Chapter 7 debtors may claim the IRS Local Standards vehicle ownership deduction even when they have no loan or lease payments. The Tates owned two unencumbered vehicles and, with the deduction, fell below the statutory threshold for presumptive abuse. Adopting the Seventh Circuit’s plain-language approach, the court concluded that “applicable” refers to the debtor’s geographic region and number of vehicles, not actual expenses. The statute distinguishes standardized Local Standards deductions from actual “Other Necessary Expenses,” excludes debt payments from monthly expenses, and does not incorporate the Internal Revenue Manual’s methodology. The court therefore reversed the district court’s affirmance of dismissal and remanded for further proceedings.
Liberty Island was evacuated after a person climbed the Statue of Liberty’s base. Six others were arrested for displaying an “Abolish I.C.E.” banner; organizers denied connection to the climber.

The study developed the Grocery Basket Score (GBS), a model intended to complement product-level systems by automatically evaluating the health properties of entire shopping baskets based on their association with mortality. It used self-reported dietary recalls from 35,462 participants in the 2001–2018 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey linked to 2019 mortality data.

Dietary signals were expressed mainly as nutrient densities because basket duration and household size are generally unknown. Cox proportional hazard models, adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and poverty-income ratio, assessed mortality associations. The selected GBS combines separate food and beverage models using calorie-weighted averages. Its food model includes saturated fat, sugar, fiber, sodium, and deficiencies in protein, vitamin C, and iron. Fiber is associated with reduced risk, while the other signals are associated with increased risk. The beverage model penalizes calorie density.

Validation used 913,298 products from Open Food Facts and dietary recalls from 4,382 NHANES 2017–2018 participants. The GBS correlated 0.60 with Nutri-Score across individual products, with cluster-level correlations ranging from 0.25 to 0.75. Correlations with the Alternate Healthy Eating Index were −0.62 without and −0.60 with its assumed protective effect of moderate alcohol consumption, compared with −0.48 and −0.47 for calorie-weighted Nutri-Scores.

The GBS requires no manual food annotation and could operate through retailer loyalty or digital basket systems. Limitations include reliance on U.S. self-reported data, potentially proxy-based signals, omitted alcohol harms beyond calorie density, missing nutritional information during validation, and necessary judgment in signal selection. The authors conclude that GBS can assess basket-level dietary patterns and possible deficiencies while remaining compatible with Nutri-Score and nutritional guidelines.

The DAWn-plasma trial randomized 320 hospitalized COVID-19 patients to four units of high-titer convalescent plasma plus standard care and 163 to standard care alone. Convalescent plasma did not improve survival without mechanical ventilation at days 15 or 30, mortality, or any secondary endpoint. Laboratory markers, vital signs, and per-protocol results were also similar between groups.

Adverse-event rates were comparable: 28.13% with plasma plus standard care and 30.06% with standard care. Fatal adverse events occurred in 10.31% and 9.82%, respectively, while serious adverse events occurred in approximately 20.6% of each group. Five adverse events led to treatment discontinuation, all in the plasma group; 14 events and seven serious events were considered treatment-related. Transfusion-related effects occurred in 19 of 320 plasma recipients, with no reported TRALI cases.

Neutralizing-antibody titers increased by day 6, but the increase was not influenced by treatment. Higher titers at baseline and day 6 correlated with better outcomes, while the magnitude of titer increase did not. Overall, early administration of four high-titer plasma units did not change the clinical course of hospitalized COVID-19.

Southeast Asian stock markets recovered from early declines as investors sought bargains amid concerns over a Sino-U.S. trade war. Indonesia closed 1.8% higher after hitting a 15-month low, supported by financial and consumer stocks. Philippine shares gained 1.1% for a fourth consecutive rise, with foreign investors buying equities ahead of inflation data. Singapore advanced 0.3%, Vietnam rose 1%, Thailand reached a one-week high, and Malaysia gained 0.5%. Despite Wednesday’s gains, all six markets remained down for the year.

The guide describes AMD Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM), an optional extension to SEV and SNP that offloads copying pages and updating virtual-to-physical mappings. TMPM availability is indicated by the ENGINE_READY bit and requires IOMMU enablement. It can pause DMA during migration and move protected SNP guest pages inaccessible to the hypervisor or operating system.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates DMA-targeted pages while coordinating with IOMMUs and requires the relevant host page-table entry. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages from Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid states to destinations in the Pre-Migration state. Afterward, source pages enter Pre-Migration state and destinations inherit source states. The Pre-Migration state uses a platform-specific ASID and cannot be converted to Guest-Valid through PVALIDATE.

Commands can migrate up to 128 nonadjacent pages, including pages from multiple guests. PM_SUCCESS means all migrations succeeded, PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires checking per-page statuses, and other results mean no migrations occurred. PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE may be retried after resolving the conflict. Commands containing at least 16 pages provide higher bandwidth, with maximum performance at 128 pages. Keeping the ring buffer populated and limiting interrupts also improves performance.

Unsupported migration targets include IOMMU structures accessed through system physical addresses, private vIOMMU page tables, pinned vIOMMU backing buffers, the ring buffer, and argument pages. Host software must prevent concurrent changes to referenced IOMMU page-table entries.

Firmware reload requires paused operations, ring-buffer teardown, and preferably disabled PAGEMIGRATION_EN bits. Reload firmware must be the same or a later version, and software must verify ENGINE_READY afterward. Reload capability and the EPYC-specific procedure are determined with PM_GET_CAPABILITIES; EPYC Family 19h uses FW_VER_Major 71.

FoodSEM is an open-source, fine-tuned large language model for identifying food mentions and linking them to entities in FoodOn, SNOMED-CT, and the Hansard taxonomy. It addresses limited food-domain semantic resources and the difficulty non-specialists face when manually linking data to ontologies for FAIR data management.

The model uses Meta Llama 3 8B Instruct, loaded in 4-bit precision and fine-tuned with LoRA. Its instruction-response dataset derives from the CafeteriaFCD recipe corpus and CafeteriaSA scientific-abstract corpus, supplemented with artificial examples to improve coverage of underrepresented ontology entities. The final dataset contains 21,027 instances, including named-entity recognition and linking tasks.

Five-fold cross-validation showed macro-weighted F1 scores of 0.937–0.974 on artificial linking samples, 0.827–0.863 on CafeteriaFCD, and 0.654–0.730 on CafeteriaSA. Lower recall on scientific abstracts was attributed to recognition errors propagating into entity linking. FoodSEM substantially outperformed its non-fine-tuned version under zero-, one-, and five-shot prompting; zero-shot results were 0, while five-shot F1 reached at most 0.417. It also exceeded previously reported BERT and BioBERT results on the Cafeteria corpora. The code, datasets, and model are publicly available. Future work will add scientific datasets and investigate retrieval-augmented generation for entities unseen during training.

TLV321x comparators include ESD clamps to both supply rails; inputs should remain within 0.2 V beyond the rails, with clamp current limited to 10 mA using a series resistor when connected to low-impedance sources. An internal power-on reset holds open-drain and push-pull outputs low for up to 32 µs after the supply crosses 1.65 V.

The comparator output changes according to the differential input, with logic polarity reversible by swapping inputs. Propagation delay varies by transition direction and overdrive voltage; overdrive below 100 mV increases delay. Because internal hysteresis is only 1.8 mV, external positive-feedback hysteresis may be added to prevent output chatter near the switching threshold. Inverting configurations use a three-resistor network, while non-inverting configurations use two resistors and a reference voltage.

A low-side current-sensing application uses an amplifier to amplify shunt voltage and a comparator to signal when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1 V. Supply pins require a nearby low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic bypass capacitor and solid grounding to prevent ringing, false triggering, and oscillation. Inputs must remain within their recommended range for single or split supplies. PCB layouts should minimize input-output coupling, place input resistors near the device, and may use an output resistor below 100 Ω or controlled-impedance traces for long connections.

TI states that application guidance and linked resources are provided as-is, require customer validation, and may change without notice. Proper ESD handling is required because damage can range from performance degradation to complete failure.

Michael Daniels, 40, a former head salesman at BMW Berry in Chiswick, was jailed for five years and three months for conspiring to steal nine cars worth £210,000. Between December 2015 and February 2016, Daniels accessed customers’ addresses and supplied spare keys to Alex Tingle, who stole the vehicles with Vincent Murphy. The cars were given false number plates and delivered to an unidentified person known as “Ali.” Victims suffered significant personal consequences, including one missing his daughter’s birth. Tingle confessed after police linked him to CCTV footage and implicated Daniels. Tingle received a two-year sentence but was due for immediate release after 13 months in custody, while Murphy had previously been jailed for 16 months. The judge described Daniels’ actions as a “horrendous breach of trust.”

President Bush describes Iraq’s election, in which more than 10 million people voted, as a major step toward constitutional democracy and a stronger alliance against terrorism. He acknowledges that prewar intelligence about Iraqi weapons of mass destruction was largely wrong but maintains that removing Saddam Hussein was justified.

Bush says the conflict has been more difficult than expected, with slow reconstruction, delays in training Iraqi security forces, continued violence, and significant sacrifices. He argues that terrorists seek broader political goals and that withdrawing would embolden them, abandon Iraqi allies, undermine U.S. credibility, and dishonor military sacrifices.

He outlines a three-part strategy: continuing military operations while transferring security responsibilities to more than 125 Iraqi combat battalions; supporting inclusive democratic institutions; and rebuilding Iraq’s economy and infrastructure. He says progress in these areas will eventually allow fewer American troops, with troop levels determined by conditions and military advice rather than fixed timetables.

Bush asks Congress to fund the military and urges Americans, including opponents of the war, to remain patient and committed. He accepts responsibility for the decision to invade and its losses, while asserting that success in Iraq is essential to U.S. security and future peace.

Sony’s “Baby Driver” surpassed $100 million domestically after seven weeks and earned $67 million overseas, against a $34 million budget. Directed and written by Edgar Wright, the Atlanta-shot action film opened June 28, earned $39 million in its first week, received a 94% Rotten Tomatoes score, and still awaited release in several major markets.

Jury selection resumed in Isaiah Hagan’s retrial for Halee Rathgeber’s killing after an earlier mistrial. Ten of 14 jurors have been chosen; selection concludes Thursday, with opening statements Monday.

Founded in 2014 by Daniel Yanisse and Jonathan Perichon, Checkr uses AI and automation to provide fast, accurate background checks. After observing that candidates with conviction records—disproportionately Black and Hispanic—were frequently rejected, the company adopted a mission of advancing fair chance hiring while maintaining workplace safety. By 2024, Checkr had 1,200 employees, served more than 100,000 customers, completed 30 million annual checks, and was valued at $5 billion.

Fair chance hiring provides qualified people with records equitable access to employment without lowering hiring standards. Roughly 80 million Americans had arrest or conviction records in 2024, while formerly incarcerated people faced high unemployment, low wages, extensive legal restrictions, and high recidivism. At the same time, the United States had 9.5 million job openings and 6.5 million unemployed people. Advocates argued that hiring justice-impacted workers could expand talent pools, reduce turnover, improve diversity and performance, lower recidivism, and strengthen communities and the economy.

Checkr supports fair chance hiring through products such as Candidate Stories, which lets applicants explain their backgrounds; Assess, which filters convictions by relevance, age, or date; a dashboard measuring hiring practices against guidelines and peers; and an expungement tool. Since launch, Candidate Stories had helped nearly 45,000 applicants receive approval, while Assess had filtered records for more than 2 million people.

Checkr also practices fair chance hiring internally. About 4% of its workforce had records, and their attrition rate was 5%, compared with 22% for other employees. The company partners with nonprofits to recruit talent, provides employee education and volunteering opportunities, and launched a 12-month apprenticeship program in 2023. Its CSR division and Checkr.org support training, advocacy, fundraising, and grants. Through the Pledge 1%, Checkr committed portions of employee time, products, equity, and profits to its mission.

After noticing that some employees viewed mission activities as separate from their regular work, leadership clarified that mission impact depended on customer value, growth, and profitability. Checkr prioritized products benefiting both the mission and business, while directing less commercial projects through nonprofit partners. Approaching its tenth anniversary and amid speculation about an IPO, the company faced the challenge of demonstrating fair chance hiring’s strategic and financial value to potential stakeholders while preserving alignment between its social mission and business performance.

A Bihar girl diagnosed with tuberculosis in 2012 developed drug-resistant TB and deteriorated despite treatment. By October 2016, she weighed 25 kg and was taken to Mumbai specialist Dr Zarir Udvadia, who recommended Bedaquiline. Government restrictions limited the drug to selected cities and excluded her because she was not from Delhi. After other efforts failed, her father petitioned the Delhi High Court, which ordered that she receive the medicine. Udvadia said Bedaquiline has achieved a 70% success rate among 30 of his patients but remains difficult to access despite urgent need. The passage acknowledges potentially fatal side effects as grounds for restrictions but questions inflexible bureaucracy. It also warns that missed doses can cause resistance, treatment lasts 18 months, and drug-resistant TB has no preventive vaccine.

Count Tisza privately urged Ambassador Penfield to inform U.S. leaders and the public that Entente peace terms sought the destruction of Germany and the dismemberment of Austria-Hungary and Turkey, conflicting with President Wilson’s views. He also argued that national self-development was impractical in ethnically mixed southeastern Europe and that the Dual Monarchy best approximated this ideal.

German Ambassador Bernstorff informed Colonel House that Germany trusted Wilson and would accept his help in arranging a peace conference, though it would not publicly state peace terms while the Entente demanded Germany’s humiliation. Germany supported a postwar international conference but said preparations made postponing the submarine blockade impossible. It promised to protect American interests and end the blockade if Wilson’s efforts produced an acceptable peace. Germany justified unrestricted submarine warfare as a response to Entente war aims, trade restrictions, and rejection of negotiations based on equal rights.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 27, 2020 reported quarterly net sales of $59.7 billion, up 11% year over year, and net income of $11.3 billion, up from $10.0 billion. Diluted earnings per share rose to $2.58 from $2.18. Growth occurred across all geographic segments and product categories, led by iPad, Mac and Services. Quarterly sales were $26.4 billion for iPhone, $7.1 billion for Mac, $6.6 billion for iPad, $6.5 billion for Wearables, Home and Accessories, and $13.2 billion for Services.

For the first nine months of fiscal 2020, sales totaled $209.8 billion and net income was $44.7 billion. Operating activities generated $60.1 billion in cash. At quarter-end, Apple had $317.3 billion in assets, $245.1 billion in liabilities and $72.3 billion in shareholders’ equity. Cash and marketable securities totaled approximately $193.6 billion, while term debt totaled $100.1 billion.

Apple repurchased $54.5 billion of stock and paid $10.6 billion in dividends during the nine-month period. It announced a four-for-one stock split effective in August 2020.

COVID-19 caused store closures, remote work and reduced demand, particularly in April, followed by improvement in May and June. Apple stated that the pandemic’s future impact remained uncertain.

The company adopted new lease and hedging accounting standards. It also disclosed ongoing legal matters involving VirnetX, iPhone performance management claims and a €1.1 billion French competition fine. The European General Court annulled a European Commission state-aid tax decision, subject to appeal.

Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) are baskets of securities traded on stock exchanges like individual stocks. They offer intraday pricing, liquidity, diversification, relatively low costs, and exposure to assets including equities, bonds, commodities, and currencies. Unlike mutual funds, ETFs can be bought or sold throughout the trading day, sold short, or purchased on margin.

ETF strategies include trend following, mean reversion, momentum, sector rotation, arbitrage, quantitative trading, options, volatility trading, pair trading, market-neutral and global macro approaches, smart beta, currency hedging, fixed income, and commodities trading. Strategies should use predetermined, preferably backtested criteria. The passage recommends combining strategies across assets, time frames, and market directions rather than seeking one best strategy.

ETFs support long-term investing, swing trading, day trading, and scalping, although the passage considers swing trading more suitable than day trading for retail traders. Liquidity affects spreads and execution costs, while expense ratios reduce returns over time. Major risks include market losses, volatility, low liquidity, tracking errors, and the complexity of leveraged or inverse ETFs. Leveraged ETFs amplify daily outcomes and risk, while inverse ETFs seek gains from market declines.

ETF history includes early products in 1989 and 1990, followed by the recognized launch of SPY in 1993. The market grew substantially after the 2008–09 financial crisis. Prominent ETFs include SPY, which tracks the S&P 500; VTI, covering the U.S. stock market; and IEFA, holding developed-market stocks outside North America.

Investors are advised to evaluate liquidity, expense ratios, historical tracking error, volatility, taxation, and strategy fit. The passage recommends backtesting ideas and observing them for months before live trading.

Duncan Keith says his teammates work and compete hard, and have matured by learning to stay level-headed when things do not go their way. He acknowledges Rask’s strong play but notes the team has scored against good goalies before. Keith praises his coach for communicating selectively, being fair, demanding high standards, and maintaining an even keel. He describes a longtime friendship and effective on-ice partnership with a teammate, strengthened by living together early in their careers and remaining neighbors. Their conversations and lifestyles have changed as they have grown older and started families or relationships. Keith believes some teammates have been misunderstood because youthful incidents received attention. He says the largely unchanged team, including Toews and Kane, has matured collectively through three years of experience and consecutive first-round losses.

AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine extends SEV/SNP to offload migration between memory tiers while preserving guest physical addresses. It requires IOMMU enablement and supports DMA-active pages and SNP-protected guest pages otherwise inaccessible to the hypervisor.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates 4 KB hypervisor or default pages, coordinates with IOMMUs, pauses or flushes DMA, updates host page-table entries, and preserves encryption. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages from Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid states to destinations in the new Pre-Migration state; afterward, destinations inherit source states and sources become Pre-Migration. Guest migration does not support concurrent DMA. Commands can process up to 128 independent entries, with per-page status and partial-success reporting. Batches of at least 16 pages improve bandwidth, with 128-page commands providing maximum performance.

Commands use a dedicated ring buffer managed by an OS driver. Firmware controls the read pointer, software controls the write pointer, and commands may execute asynchronously and out of order across parallel units. The interface supports pausing, resuming, completion and error interrupts, queue-empty and low-water interrupts, and status reporting. Initialization requires checking ENGINE_READY, configuring a physically contiguous 1–255-page ring buffer, validating configuration fields, enabling PAGEMIGRATION_EN on all IOMMUs, and obtaining PS_ASID_VAL. Ring-buffer memory, argument pages, IOMMU structures, and pinned vIOMMU storage are non-migratable.

Most system physical addresses must be 4 KB aligned; host page-table entries require 8-byte alignment, and 2 MB addresses require 2 MB alignment. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO does not directly migrate 2 MB pages, while guest 2 MB migration requires physically contiguous 4 KB pages. Software must prevent CPU access during migration and avoid concurrent modification of relevant IOMMU entries.

TMPM firmware can be reloaded only after operations stop and the ring buffer is torn down. Reload firmware must be the same or a newer version, and software must recheck ENGINE_READY. EPYC Family 19h is identified by FW_VER_Major 71.

Command, entry, ring-buffer, and hardware errors are reported through command status, per-entry status, PM_STATUS, or Machine Check Architecture. Hardware failures during a batch may leave all affected pages unrecoverable, requiring software to preserve state, terminate virtual machines, stop issuing TMPM commands, or reboot.
GBP/USD traded narrowly after hawkish Yellen testimony strengthened the dollar. UK jobs data, US economic releases and Fed remarks may influence trading.

Following President William Henry Harrison’s death, the Vice President assumes the presidency under the Constitution, acknowledging the unprecedented transition and pledging reliance on the people, Providence, and constitutional principles.

His foreign policy will pursue peace and justice while resisting injustice, protecting national honor, and maintaining effective military defenses. Domestically, he warns against concentrating control of public funds and appointments in the presidency. He supports separating financial custody from executive power, limiting patronage, and preventing officeholders from using official influence in elections. Honest officials will generally remain, while partisan interference may justify removal.

He advocates strict economy, avoidance of peacetime debt, abolition of sinecures, explicit appropriations, official accountability, and strong punishment for financial misconduct. Though promising to enforce existing financial laws until Congress repeals them, he considers them oppressive and will support constitutional legislation restoring a sound circulating medium.

He pledges to resist unauthorized expansion of federal power, preserve the constitutional balance between the federal government and the states, prevent factional and sectional conflict, protect individual rights and free institutions, and preserve the Union for future generations.

The speaker says improved skating, aggression, urgency and physical play made the difference in Game 2 after a passive opener, allowing the team to tie the series. The intense, low-scoring game reflected playoff hockey and strong goaltending, though the team hopes to create more offensive chances at home. Game 3 is considered crucial, requiring the same pressure, emotion and willingness to fight for every inch without giving the opponent time and space. The team expects strong support from a loud home crowd and will draw confidence and lessons from recent home playoff games.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture improves graphics, ray tracing, AI, memory, connectivity, storage I/O, display, and video processing over Turing. GA102 contains up to seven GPCs, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA cores, 112 ROPs, a 384-bit memory interface, and 6 MB of L2 cache. Each SM provides 128 CUDA cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation RT Core, and 128 KB of configurable L1/shared memory. Dual FP32-capable datapaths double peak FP32 throughput, while expanded caches and shared-memory bandwidth further improve performance. Ampere GPUs are stated to be up to 1.9 times more power-efficient than Turing at equal performance.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput, support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute, and add hardware acceleration for moving and deforming geometry motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32, BF16, FP16, INT8, INT4, and structured sparsity, which can double effective matrix throughput by skipping zero values. These capabilities accelerate AI functions including DLSS, denoising, RTX Voice, and other neural services. DLSS uses neural networks to reconstruct higher-resolution images and enables supported RTX 3090 games to reach 8K at 60 fps.

GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling to transfer two bits per clock edge, reaching 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/s on GA10x products. The RTX 3080 provides 1.5 times the memory bandwidth of the RTX 2080 Super. Third-generation NVLink supplies 112.5 GB/s bidirectional aggregate bandwidth between two GPUs and allows paired A40 or RTX A6000 GPUs to combine 48 GB each into 96 GB. PCIe 4.0 doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth, providing up to 64 GB/s through a x16 slot.

RTX IO works with Microsoft DirectStorage to move compressed assets from NVMe storage to the GPU for asynchronous decompression, reducing CPU use and accelerating loading and streaming. Ampere also supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 4K at 120 Hz, and 8K at 60 Hz. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware AV1 decoding up to 8K60 HDR with low CPU use, while seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware H.264 encoding up to 4K and HEVC up to 8K.

The A40 and RTX A6000 target professional and data-center workloads with 48 GB of GDDR6, optional 96 GB through NVLink, virtualization support, and accelerated graphics, compute, AI, and rendering. The RTX 3090 includes 10,496 CUDA cores and 24 GB of GDDR6X, while the RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6 without NVLink. Error Detection and Replay protects GDDR6X transfers by detecting errors and retrying transactions, helping users identify unstable memory overclocks through performance plateaus.

Merck halted a late-stage trial of Alzheimer’s drug verubecestat after an independent study found virtually no chance of success in patients with mild-to-moderate disease. The decision follows Eli Lilly’s failed solanezumab trial and intensifies doubts about beta amyloid theory, which links brain plaques to Alzheimer’s. No treatment has been proven to slow the disease, despite successes in laboratory animals. About 47 million people worldwide have dementia, with Alzheimer’s accounting for an estimated 60–80% of cases; dementia cases are projected to reach 131 million by 2050. Merck continues studying verubecestat in earlier-stage patients, while several companies are testing similar BACE inhibitors and Biogen is trialling aducanumab. Experts described the failure as a major setback but said research should continue. Merck’s shares fell nearly 2% after the announcement.

The passage argues that détente and arms-control negotiations with the Soviet Union are necessary but meaningful only if both sides reduce tensions and weapons. It opposes agreements such as SALT II that allegedly legitimize a one-sided Soviet nuclear buildup and advocates restoring U.S. military strength while pursuing verifiable mutual reductions. Citing the Austrian State Treaty, it presents determined negotiation as effective. It warns that Soviet strategy seeks to divide NATO, expand influence in the Arabian Gulf, South Asia, the Caribbean, and Central America, isolate China, and gain military superiority that could force U.S. submission or conflict. The passage calls for public sacrifice to strengthen national defense, asserting that credible military power is the best means to deter war and encourage genuine arms limits. It portrays American strength as defensive and contrasts American ideals of freedom and self-determination with Soviet coercion, militarism, empire-building, and privilege.

DTE Maharashtra released the MHT CET 2018 syllabus and exam pattern for May admissions to engineering, technology, pharmacy and Pharma-D courses. Questions will have 20% Class XI and 80% Class XII weightage, no negative marking, and difficulty comparable to JEE.

The TMS320DM814x routes C674x MDMA accesses through a system MMU to protect Cortex-A8 memory and translate virtual addresses; EDMA channels 0 and 1 may also use the MMU. The Media Controller manages HDVPSS and ISS, while HDVICP2 accelerates major video encode, decode, and transcode standards. Other modules include face detection and tracking, 128 hardware spinlocks for multiprocessor synchronization, and interrupt-driven mailboxes connecting the Cortex-A8, C674x DSP, and Media Controller.

A unified memory map provides consistent resource access, with defined L3/L4 peripheral maps and limited DSP peripheral access. The TILER adds a 4-GB extended addressing range for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views, fully accessible only to HDVPSS and ISS; other masters can access one view through a 512-MB region.

The terminal-function tables document package pins, multiplexed functions, control registers, input states, pull resistors, and supply voltages. Interfaces include boot configuration, camera, DDR2/DDR3, EMAC, GPIO, GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, SD, SPI, clocks, timers, UART, USB, and digital and analog video. They also specify reset behavior, external resistor requirements, unused-pin handling, and mandatory power and ground connections.

Edward C. Turner’s driver’s license was revoked for six months after he refused a chemical alcohol test following arrest for driving under the influence. The revocation was upheld administratively, but the district court reduced it to three months after finding six months excessive in light of Turner’s driving record.

The Oklahoma Supreme Court affirmed the revocation but reversed the reduction. Relying on State ex rel. Department of Public Safety v. Kopczynski, the majority held that, before the 1975 amendment to 47 O.S. § 755, district courts lacked authority to shorten the mandatory six-month revocation. The amendment created only a prospective, limited exception for extreme and unusual hardship. Because the statutory issues—driving under the influence, arrest, and refusal to test—were resolved affirmatively, the six-month revocation was mandatory.

Justice Simms dissented, joined by Vice Chief Justice Hodges and Justice Doolin. The dissent argued that Kopczynski addressed modification based only on hardship and did not control a reduction based on an excessive period. It maintained that § 6-211(e), which governed implied-consent appeals, expressly authorized courts to consider a licensee’s driving record and reduce an excessive suspension. The dissent viewed the 1975 amendment as adding hardship-based limited driving privileges rather than eliminating existing modification authority, and therefore would have affirmed the district court.

Vermont City Electric (VCE), a municipal utility serving about 19,600 residential and commercial accounts, has used demand-side management (DSM) since 2000 to reduce electricity consumption and peak demand. Following the 2008 economic downturn, VCE limited 2009 DSM spending to $800,000 and must determine which of nine programs to retain.

Electricity demand is expected to grow with annual population growth of 0.52% and per-capita use growth of 0.22%. Annual demand is represented by five load blocks, ranging from an average 60.1 MW during 365 peak hours to 27.1 MW during 480 low-use hours.

VCE supplies electricity through its wood-powered McNeil plant, an oil-fired gas turbine, hydroelectric and wood-based contracts, and the ISO-New England wholesale market. Their costs, capacities, and carbon emissions vary by source and load block. A 5.2 MW wind facility is expected in 2012. McNeil costs are projected to rise 3% annually through 2014, other non-wind sources 4%, while wind costs remain flat. Future costs are discounted to 2009 values.

The nine DSM programs address commercial and residential construction, existing buildings, efficient retail products, lighting, heating and cooling, outdoor lighting, and LED streetlights. Together, they cost $1,035,027 in 2009, exceeding the budget, and provide different power savings across load blocks. Their savings are expected to persist from 2009 through 2014.

The assignment requires building a least-cost mixed-integer optimization model for 2009–2014. The model must select electricity sources by year and load block, account for capacity, demand growth, costs, discount factors, wind capacity, and carbon emissions, and compare outcomes without and with DSM. Binary variables represent DSM program selection under the $800,000 limit. The analysis must identify recommended programs, quantify costs and carbon impacts, assess whether the budget constraint affects the optimal choice, and evaluate whether increasing the budget is justified. An optional question considers how a 2014 carbon tax could affect supply choices and emissions.

The course requires prior quantum field theory knowledge and uses five problem sets plus a final presentation, with no exams. Its first half introduces general effective field theory principles; the second focuses on soft-collinear effective field theory and applications to LHC jet physics.

Effective field theory isolates physics at a chosen scale using the simplest framework that captures essential phenomena while retaining systematic higher-order corrections. Constructing one requires identifying relevant degrees of freedom, symmetries, expansion parameters, and a leading-order Lagrangian. Power counting determines the relative importance of terms and is as fundamental as symmetry. Effective theories rely on low-energy physics being insensitive to detailed higher-energy dynamics, though expansions may involve quantities such as velocity rather than only ratios of mass scales.

Hydrogen illustrates multiple effective expansions: heavy particles such as bottom quarks give suppressed corrections, quark structure is unresolved at atomic momentum transfers, the proton behaves approximately as a static charge, and electron dynamics are nonrelativistic. Integrating out heavy particles can also redefine low-energy couplings. These principles remain valid despite ultraviolet divergences.

Effective field theories can be developed top-down or bottom-up. In the top-down approach, a known high-energy theory is matched onto a lower-energy theory by integrating out degrees of freedom. The theories agree on shared infrared observables but may differ in ultraviolet behavior. Examples include heavy-quark effective theory, nonrelativistic QED and QCD, and soft-collinear effective theory. In the bottom-up approach, the high-energy theory is unknown or matching is impractical. The low-energy theory is built from all operators consistent with its degrees of freedom, symmetries, and power counting, while unknown coefficients are determined experimentally or numerically. Examples include chiral perturbation theory, the Standard Model viewed as an effective theory, and quantum gravity.

Effective theories organize both power corrections and logarithms. Renormalization of the low-energy theory can explain and resum logarithmic terms. Viewed bottom-up, the Standard Model is the leading Lagrangian in an expansion whose higher-dimensional operators encode physics above Standard Model scales.

Traditional renormalizability requires ultraviolet divergences to be absorbed into finitely many parameters. Effective field theory instead requires renormalizability order by order in the expansion, allowing infinitely many operators overall but only finitely many at any fixed order.

The patent describes wireless multi-user transmission methods intended to improve WLAN clustering, scheduling, and control efficiency beyond IEEE 802.11ac limitations. Access points may organize stations into flexible clusters supporting uplink and downlink OFDMA, OFDM MU-MIMO, or combinations thereof. Membership, user positions, transmission modes, cluster identifiers, and resource assignments may be signaled through management frames, physical-layer headers, control frames, beacon frames, or updated for each transmission opportunity.

To reduce MAC overhead, multi-user control information may be carried in null data packet (NDP) MAC PPDUs containing physical-layer headers without MAC bodies. Proposed formats use either one NDP signal field or separate common and user/resource-specific signal fields. These fields may identify the NDP frame type, transmission mode, access-point or station address, group or cluster, duration, bandwidth, synchronization data, response protocol, and resource allocation.

NDP-based control frames include MU request-to-send, clear-to-send, poll, response/request, schedule, and acknowledgment frames. A station may identify an NDP frame using transmission length or an NDP indicator, determine whether it is an intended recipient, process scheduling and synchronization information, set its network allocation vector if not selected, and generate an appropriate response. Responses may be transmitted through time-, frequency-, code-, or spatial-domain division. The disclosed designs support per-transmission scheduling, dynamic user and sub-channel assignments, synchronization, channel feedback, and reduced control-frame duration.

During a family road trip to several national parks, the author reflects on weather and climate communication. Old Faithful’s estimated eruption window prompts him to argue that weather forecasts should better convey uncertainty through probability ranges rather than absolute predictions. The Draw is a run play disguised briefly as a pass, intended to exploit defenses expecting a throw by spreading defenders before a delayed handoff up the middle. It works best in pass-heavy offenses and obvious passing situations but is vulnerable to unblocked interior blitzes, so offenses often attach an RPO.

Against 3-4 and 4-3 fronts, linemen initially use pass sets, invite defenders upfield, and create an interior lane through combination blocks or releases to linebackers. The quarterback sells the pass before handing off, while the tailback initially appears to scan for pass protection and then runs opposite the center’s block. Slots sell seam routes before blocking safeties, and outside receivers run vertical releases to remove cornerbacks.

Variations include the QB Draw, which preserves the blocking rules and may include a perimeter RPO, and the Lead Draw from 12-personnel Strong-I, where the tight end and fullback block linebackers. Lead Draw is effective only if the offense also regularly passes from that formation.

Quinton Tellis’ defense attorney, Darla Palmer, alleged that Panola County District Attorney John Champion tried to induce another defendant, Jalen Caudle, to falsely claim Tellis said Jessica Chambers called him “Eric.” Caudle stated Champion offered reduced charges, suggested replacing Palmer with a friendly public defender, and promised he would not receive a life sentence if he cooperated. Palmer asked that Champion be removed and punished, the September retrial delayed, and the Mississippi attorney general’s office take over prosecution. Champion declined to discuss the motion before a scheduled hearing.

Tellis is accused of fatally burning 19-year-old Chambers in 2014. His first trial ended with a hung jury. Witnesses testified Chambers named “Eric” or “Derek” as her attacker, though prosecutors also presented evidence that her burns may have prevented clear speech. Prosecutors say cellphone-location and other evidence implicated Tellis, who denies killing Chambers.

Westman reported renewed Finnish confidence in German success against Russia after Allied reverses, alongside concern that German exhaustion might later expose Finland to concentrated Soviet pressure. In Washington, the Finnish Minister acknowledged that Finland’s alignment with Germany made a separate Finnish-Soviet war untenable and could lead to a rupture with the United States. He saw no solution, noting Finland could not fight both Russia and German forces present in the country.

Finland’s increased bread ration was threatened when Baltic ice delayed German grain shipments. Authorities requisitioned seed and farmers’ grain reserves, underscoring Finland’s dependence on Germany for essential food supplies.

Strategies for containing a basketball superstar include full pass denial, defensive help, trapping mismatches, drawing charges, boxing out, directing play away, and forcing the player to expend energy through defense, transition, penetration, screens, and rebounding.

This study examines Moroccan teachers’ perspectives on educational leadership and sustained ICT use after COVID-19. Of 297 surveyed teachers, 130 had stopped using technology after face-to-face classes resumed. Most reported limited access to devices, reliable internet, digital resources, training, and institutional support. Only 22.3% had received ICT training, often brief or unstructured. Teachers also identified students’ need for devices, connectivity, user-friendly technologies, and self-learning skills.

The findings attribute barriers primarily to leadership and systemic factors rather than demographic variables. Moroccan education leaders have not fully met standards concerning digital equity, strategic planning, stakeholder empowerment, system design, and continuous professional learning. The study recommends unified learning platforms, stronger coordination among stakeholders, expanded teacher training, evaluation and sharing of digital content, improved access to devices and connectivity, and digital literacy instruction. It concludes that stronger educational leadership and sustained institutional investment are necessary to preserve and develop the technological gains made during the pandemic.

The passage explains how to backtest a Bollinger Band strategy in Python using pandas, NumPy, matplotlib, and yfinance. First-principles calculations were used to study how stacking controls structural, electronic, magnetic, and magnetoelectric properties in CrI₂ bilayers. Density functional theory with Hubbard corrections and dispersion interactions determined relaxed structures and energies, while OpenMX and TB2J provided isotropic exchange, symmetric anisotropy, and Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction parameters.

Monolayer CrI₂ has a stripe antiferromagnetic AFx ground state, approximately 4.2 μB per Cr, and a 1.12 eV band gap. Bilayer formation preserves stripe antiferromagnetism but strengthens the principal in-plane antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic exchange channels by about 6–10%. These intralayer interactions dominate the magnetic energy scale, whereas interlayer exchange is roughly an order of magnitude weaker and changes sign depending on stacking registry and interlayer spin alignment.

Among direct and indirect stackings, inversion-related BA′ with antiparallel AFx layers is the global ground state. Prime stackings such as BA′ and AB′ reduce iodine–iodine repulsion through inversion and lateral displacement. Bilayer gaps range from 0.99 to 1.07 eV and depend jointly on registry, orbital hybridization, and magnetic alignment rather than solely on interlayer distance. Broken inversion and time-reversal symmetries also produce momentum-dependent spin splitting without requiring spin–orbit coupling.

Controlled sliding reveals stable stacking minima separated by barriers of approximately 25–50 meV per formula unit. Stacking symmetry determines the anisotropic interactions: centrosymmetric structures forbid Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya coupling, while inversion-breaking bilayers exhibit finite DMI and registry-dependent symmetric anisotropy. Indirect stackings also support in-plane polarization linked to inequivalent iodine environments, with spin–orbit coupling generally modifying or reducing it.

Spin-resolved band centers indicate strongly spin-selective Cr-d/I-p hybridization underlying antiferromagnetic superexchange. Overall, CrI₂ bilayers exhibit a hierarchy in which intralayer exchange sets the primary magnetic scale, stacking symmetry selects anisotropic and magnetoelectric terms, and weak interlayer exchange provides secondary tuning. These properties support mechanically reconfigurable magnetic, ferroelectric, spintronic, and multiferroic device concepts.

Skoltech researchers developed a mathematical model in which memories, or engrams, represent concepts through sensory features and evolve toward a stable distribution. The model found that a seven-dimensional conceptual space maximizes the number of distinct concepts retained, suggesting seven senses may optimize memory capacity. Researchers describe applying this conclusion to humans as speculative but say it could inform robotics, artificial intelligence, and theories of memory. Soccer players specialize by position within a formation and system of play, but all players—especially young ones—should learn every skill and experience all positions. Coaches should select position names and use them consistently.

The four general position groups are goalkeeper, defenders, midfielders, and forwards. The goalkeeper is the only position named in the IFAB Laws, wears a contrasting jersey, and may handle the ball within the team’s penalty area. Defenders protect the goal, cover opponents, challenge for the ball, block shots, and can initiate counterattacks. Midfielders connect defense and attack, support possession, and require strong all-around skills and fitness. Forwards create scoring opportunities and need accurate passing, shooting, and ball control under pressure.

Specific names vary with formations and duties. Defenders include center backs, outside backs, stoppers, sweepers, and liberos. Midfield roles include central, attacking, holding, defensive, outside, wide, and wing midfielders or wing backs. Forward roles include center forwards, strikers, inside forwards, wings, withdrawn forwards, supporting strikers, and wide strikers. Coaches should choose formations suited to their players’ talents and consistently apply their chosen terminology.

RiseEngineer, a U.S. publicly traded green design and construction company, won a $1.2 billion government contract in corruption-prone Elysium. Newly promoted internal audit head Marsha Jackson investigates an anonymous allegation of misconduct.

Larry Williams created the Williams Vix Fix in 2007 as a synthetic VIX for securities lacking an official volatility index. It calculates the percentage difference between the current low and the highest close over 22 trading days, making it a lagging measure of recent price volatility.

Like the VIX, it tends to rise with market fear and fall during low-volatility conditions. Its movements resemble the VIX in levels, timing, and magnitude, supporting its use in other markets. Tests on stock indices produced positive results, including strategies using PercentRank. An improved QQQ strategy averaged nearly 1% per trade across 352 trades, had a 75% win rate and 20% maximum drawdown, and returned 12.7% versus 9.2% for buy-and-hold while invested only 20% of the time. The indicator appears mean-reverting and works reasonably well for both long and short stock-index strategies, though other asset classes were not tested.

Opera launched Neon, an AI-powered subscription browser that autonomously performs tasks such as completing forms, comparing websites and writing code. Operating locally for greater privacy, it offers AI-managed workspaces and reusable prompts. Opera aims to compete in agentic browsing, though reliability, safety, transparency and regulatory compliance remain challenges.

Melania Trump is hosting executives from Amazon, Snap, Facebook, Google, Twitter and other internet organizations to discuss cyberbullying and online safety, her first public event on the issue since naming it a priority as first lady. Her focus has drawn questions because President Trump frequently insults people on Twitter.

Technology companies prohibit harassment but largely rely on users to report abuse. Despite policies and educational resources, bullying remains widespread, including humiliating photos, cruel comments and shared private messages. A Pew poll found 41 percent of US adults believed they had experienced online harassment. Twitter has strengthened protections, while Yik Yak closed partly after bullying complaints led schools to ban it.

Enforcement is complicated by the enormous volume of online content and tensions between preventing abuse and protecting expression. Twitter, citing news value, has declined calls to ban President Trump over disparaging tweets. No federal anti-bullying law exists, and state laws vary. Cyberbullying expert Sameer Hinduja said federal authorities could support schools with funding and resources. Melania Trump has also promoted children’s well-being, kindness, reduced online time and awareness of internet content.

Warby Parker is presented as an attractive investment due to retail expansion, customer growth, rising average selling prices, new products, and high gross margins despite tariffs. The disclosure describes a footwear sole structure with an outsole containing traction elements arranged around a central axis. A medial forefoot annular cleat set includes concentric rings of larger major cleats and smaller minor cleats. Radial cleat sets extend from the central axis toward the lateral side and toe, with some incorporating angled peripheral cleats for traction under lateral or angular forces. A separate heel cleat set includes major and minor cleats.

The sole structure may use modular forefoot and heel plates composed of shells, internal skeletons, and cleat inserts. It may also include a composite midsole with an outer casing and cushioning core, plus a rigid shank and cradle between the plates. The arrangement is intended to provide longitudinal and lateral traction while permitting rotation about the annular set’s central axis, and the composite construction allows different materials to provide durability, flexibility, stiffness, and cushioning.

Tennessee middle school student Keaton Jones drew national attention after his mother posted a video of him tearfully describing school bullying, including insults and having milk poured on him. Keaton’s sister, Lakyn Jones, defended her family and said her brother was happy about the awareness and support the video generated.

Several research teams have produced high-energy muon beams using compact, laser-driven particle accelerators instead of kilometer-scale facilities. Lasers create plasma waves that accelerate electrons, which generate muons when they strike dense materials such as lead. Experiments at Berkeley Lab, Romania’s ELI-NP facility and Shanghai produced muons with energies of roughly one to several billion electron volts.

Muons can penetrate concrete, stone and metals with limited scattering, allowing imaging of concealed materials. Artificial beams could overcome the scarcity of naturally occurring muons and enable faster scanning of shipping containers for substances such as plutonium and uranium. Laser accelerators are not yet portable, but improving technology could make portable muon sources possible. A Colorado State University experiment demonstrated that a laser-produced muon beam could detect a lead object inside a truck, providing an early proof of principle.

This study examined whether vitamin B12 metabolism or genetically determined B12 levels influence Parkinson’s disease (PD) risk, age at onset, or progression. Researchers analyzed common variants, pathway-specific polygenic risk scores, rare variants from 4,929 cases and 68,029 controls, Mendelian randomization, and genetic correlations using European-ancestry datasets. No robust association was found between PD and common or rare B12-metabolism variants; nominal polygenic and cohort-specific rare-variant signals did not survive correction or replication. Mendelian randomization found no causal association between B12 levels and PD risk, onset, motor progression, or cognitive progression, and no genetic correlation was detected. Progression analyses had limited statistical power, and findings may not generalize beyond European ancestry. The authors conclude that B12 levels and metabolism likely have no prominent genetic role in PD, while non-genetic factors such as gastrointestinal dysfunction, reduced food intake, and altered gut microbiota may contribute to lower B12 levels observed in patients. Addressing B12 deficiency remains important for preventing deficiency-related symptoms.

The lecture explains energy-absorption diagrams for foams, derived from compressive stress-strain curves and normalized by solid modulus. The optimal “shoulder point” occurs near the end of the stress plateau, where maximum energy is absorbed before densification sharply increases peak stress. Families of curves can represent different foam densities, strain rates, and temperatures. Elastomeric foams can share a general normalized diagram, while yielding foams require curves specific to the ratio of solid yield strength to modulus.

Models for linear elasticity, plateau collapse, and densification reproduce experimental diagrams for open- and closed-cell foams. These models show that low-density foams can absorb a given energy at peak stresses orders of magnitude below those of dense solids. Energy-absorption diagrams can guide selection of foam material, density, and thickness for impact protection. Examples include packaging calculations using iterative thickness estimates and bicycle-helmet selection, for which 5%-dense expanded polystyrene is identified as suitable.

The lecture also examines why woodpeckers tolerate repeated decelerations up to about 1,500g without brain injury. No special cushioning material exists between their brains and skulls. Their tolerance is attributed to smaller brain size, brain orientation, and very short impact duration. Woodpeckers also have stiff tail feathers and two-forward, two-back toe arrangements that support pecking. The next topic will be engineered and natural sandwich panels.

The paper develops minimal mean-field Ising pseudospin models for proton-tautomeric phenyltetrazole crystals APHTZ and MPHTZ. Their switchable dipoles arise from proton relocation, associated π-bond switching, and ionic displacements.

APHTZ is modeled as a two-sublattice canted ferroelectric with ferroelectric order along the a axis and antiferroelectric order along b. The model predicts a second-order transition near 425 K, single ferroelectric hysteresis for an a-axis field, and field-induced 90° polarization rotation with double antiferroelectric hysteresis for a b-axis field. The transverse-field phase diagram contains first- and second-order switching regions separated by a tricritical point, calculated near 409 K.

MPHTZ is represented by a four-sublattice model reducible to a conventional two-sublattice uniaxial antiferroelectric model with checkerboard interchain ordering. Fitting available polarization data gives a predicted transition near 421 K and a tricritical point near 413 K. An a-axis field induces the standard antiferroelectric-to-ferroelectric transition and double hysteresis loops.

Both models yield mean-field Ising behavior, including square-root order-parameter scaling near the transition, low-temperature saturation, Curie-Weiss dielectric response, and switching fields proportional to spontaneous order and intersublattice coupling. Available experimental data agree with the models but are insufficient for firm validation, especially for APHTZ. Further measurements of polarization, permittivity, switching, and phase-transition properties are required to refine parameters and test the predictions.

OpenChart-SE is a citizen science project addressing limited access to Swedish electronic health record (EHR) text for clinical natural language processing research. Swedish physicians and medical students created artificial records for plausible emergency department patients using a Swedish mock EHR form. All submissions were reviewed for realistic language, structure, and medical content by an experienced emergency physician.

The pilot collected 50 quality-approved artificial EHRs, released openly as OpenChart-SE corpus version 1. Records ranged from 954 to 2,738 characters, covered patients aged 18–94, and included varied emergency scenarios and diagnoses. Six described priority-one patients, 29 female patients, and 21 male patients. Each record had at least one empty field, reflecting patterns in real EHRs.

Although the corpus cannot provide clinical insights because it contains no real patient data, it closely resembles Swedish emergency EHRs and is intended for training and validating clinical NLP tools. Additional quality-controlled submissions will be released periodically.

Andrew Lo uses Lehman Brothers’ 2007 finances and bankruptcy to explain leverage and financial instability. Despite $19 billion in revenue, $4 billion in net income, $145 billion in long-term capital, and $282 billion under management, Lehman disappeared within nine months. Its 16-to-1 leverage meant modest asset declines could rapidly exhaust capital, much as a small house down payment magnifies both gains and losses. Rising mortgage payments, falling home values, and non-recourse loans encouraged some homeowners to default. The Federal Reserve declined to back Lehman’s potential acquisition, leading it to file for Chapter 11. Uncertain asset values, lost confidence, and counterparties’ unwillingness to trade destroyed its business viability.

Lo predicts short-term disruption in financial hiring but identifies later opportunities, particularly in asset management and other organizations needing financial expertise.

He then distinguishes nominal returns from real returns. Inflation measures changes in purchasing power, so real wealth equals nominal wealth adjusted for price changes. The real return is approximately the nominal return minus inflation. Net present value calculations should consistently match nominal cash flows with nominal discount rates and real cash flows with real rates.

The ADS9803 requires a free-running sampling clock and a defined register-write initialization sequence after power-up or reset. Users can then configure analog input range, bandwidth, common-mode range, reference selection, and output-lane mode. Speed-boost mode converts one selected input-channel pair on every sampling clock at rates up to 8 MSPS while leaving the other six channels idle.

Its 16-bit configuration registers use three banks addressed through 8-bit addresses. Bank 0 is always accessible; banks 1 and 2 are selected through register 0x03. Register writes and reads use 24-bit SPI frames, with read access controlled by SPI_RD_EN and SPI_MODE. Multiple ADCs can be connected in a daisy chain with shared CS and SCLK signals. Daisy-chain length excludes the first ADC, and operations require N × 24 clock cycles for N devices.

Registers control initialization, data format and averaging, test patterns, XOR processing, speed boost, gain correction, analog bandwidth, channel power-down, reference selection, output lanes, common-mode range, and PGA operation. Reserved fields must remain at reset values.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2-MSPS data-acquisition system with an integrated analog front end. For an ATE example, post-calibration total unadjusted error is 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. It supports low-noise bandwidth up to 22.7 kHz and wide bandwidth up to 700 kHz, with multiplexed signals settling to 99.95% full scale in 7.5 µs.

The device uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies without a required power-up sequence. Layout guidance includes close 0.1-µF bypass capacitors, short ground connections, nearby reference decoupling, and separation of analog paths from digital lines and noise sources. TI states that application guidance and resources are provided as-is, and users are responsible for component selection, design validation, testing, and compliance.

Light-field imaging captures spatial and angular information from a 3D scene in a single exposure, avoiding sequential scanning used in conventional microscopy. This can improve volumetric imaging speed and reduce phototoxicity, although camera readout, sensor size, and signal quality remain limiting factors. The technique derives from integral photography and the plenoptic function, commonly reduced from seven dimensions to a four-dimensional representation describing ray position and direction.

Microlens, pinhole, Fourier, and related optical configurations encode directional information on a camera sensor. Computational processing then enables refocusing, synthetic-aperture imaging, multi-view visualization, and volumetric reconstruction. Geometric-optics models provide intuitive ray descriptions, while wave-optics models account for diffraction and interference and offer greater accuracy in high-numerical-aperture microscopy and complex or scattering samples at higher computational cost.

Biomedical implementations include light-field microscopy, mesoscopy, and endoscopy. Light-field microscopy supports rapid imaging of neural activity, intracellular dynamics, whole organisms, organoids, and tissues. Fourier light-field microscopy samples spatial frequencies to reduce artifacts and improve volumetric performance. Mesoscopic systems provide cellular-resolution imaging across millimeter-to-centimeter scales, including large cortical regions and freely moving animals, but face aberration, scattering, depth, and hardware constraints. Light-field endoscopy adds depth reconstruction and digital refocusing to rigid or flexible probes through microlens arrays, tunable lenses, GRIN lenses, camera arrays, or fiber bundles, though resolution, working distance, and transmission of angular information remain challenges.

Key trade-offs involve speed, spatial resolution, angular sampling, field of view, and depth of field. Compressive sensing, event cameras, and squeezed light-field microscopy can reduce data volume and enable kilohertz-scale imaging, but performance depends on sample sparsity and preservation of disparity information. Scanning and virtual-scanning methods can restore resolution, although physical scanning reduces speed and deep-learning approaches may lack generalizability.

Meta-optics may improve sampling, aperture use, depth of field, and device compactness by controlling phase, polarization, spectrum, and other light properties, but current metalenses face aberrations, crosstalk, and limited large-field performance. Artificial intelligence can accelerate reconstruction and reduce artifacts through fully learned or hybrid physics-based models. However, dependence on training data, overfitting, limited interpretability, and the risk of misleading reconstructions remain unresolved concerns.
