The City of Bisbee sought mandamus compelling Cochise County officials to remit penalties, fees, costs, and interest collected on delinquent city taxes. The trial court sustained demurrers and dismissed the action.

The Arizona Supreme Court held that mandamus could compel the county treasurer to pay city funds improperly diverted to county accounts. However, the county and board of supervisors were not proper defendants because the money was held in trust by the treasurer and never legally became county funds.

Under the statutes governing collections before June 13, 1931, additional sums collected on delinquent city taxes belonged to Bisbee and had to be remitted with the taxes and interest. The limitations period did not begin until the treasurer repudiated the trust by notifying Bisbee that payment would be refused; therefore, the action was timely. Bisbee was entitled to an accounting for qualifying collections through June 12, 1931.

A 1931 statute directed that interest, penalties, charges, and fees collected on delinquent taxes be credited to the county general fund. Bisbee therefore had no claim to amounts collected after June 12, 1931.

The judgment was reversed and remanded with instructions to overrule the demurrer as to Treasurer Kitchel and proceed consistently with the opinion.

The MSPM0G3519/G3518/G1519/G1518 devices provide secure storage for up to four 128- or 256-bit AES keys, 16- and 32-bit CRC, hardware-accelerated 32-bit mathematics, UART, I2C, SPI, CAN-FD, general-purpose and advanced timers, RTC, and watchdog timers. Communications features include UART LIN support, I2C rates up to 1 Mbit/s with SMBus 3.0, SPI rates up to 32 Mbit/s on supported pins, and CAN-FD rates up to 5 Mbit/s. Multiple peripherals support FIFOs and DMA.

The low-frequency subsystem uses a typical 32-kHz clock and contains RTC_B and an independent watchdog. RTC_B provides calendar, alarm, periodic interrupt, calibration, and temperature-drift compensation functions. The independent watchdog can generate a power-on reset after periods from 2 ms to 2 hours. The windowed watchdog supports reset, interrupt, sleep stopping, and interval-timer operation. TIMG and TIMA timers support configurable counting, prescaling, synchronization, triggers, DMA, and capture/compare; advanced timers additionally provide complementary PWM, dead-band insertion, and fault handling.

IOMUX selects peripheral pin functions and controls drivers, inputs, and shutdown wake-up. DAC_OUT uses PA15, so external signals on PA15 are discouraged while it is enabled. Debugging uses a two-wire Arm-compatible SWD interface. The boot strap loader supports UART or I2C programming, 256-bit password protection, optional disabling, hardware or software invocation, and automatic startup on blank devices. Device capabilities, identification, revisions, and trim data reside in a read-only, memory-mapped FACTORY region.

Recommended hardware includes 10-µF and 0.1-µF VDD decoupling capacitors, a 47-kΩ NRST pullup with a 10-nF capacitor, and a 0.47-µF VCORE capacitor. SYSOSC frequency correction requires an external precision 100-kΩ resistor. Five-volt-tolerant open-drain outputs require pullups.

Researchers say marine reptile fossils remain relatively understudied compared with land-dwelling dinosaurs.

Skinimalism simplifies skincare by using a few high-quality, targeted, multitasking products instead of layering many potentially conflicting ingredients. It aims to support the skin barrier, reduce irritation and sensitivity, embrace natural texture, and promote long-term skin health. It may also reduce stress, spending, packaging, and waste.

Most people may benefit from a balanced, barrier-friendly routine, although conditions such as acne, eczema, rosacea, hyperpigmentation, and menopausal skin can require specific treatments. Recommended approaches generally combine gentle cleansing, suitable moisturising, daily SPF, and one carefully chosen active ingredient. Strong actives should be introduced cautiously, particularly for sensitive or compromised skin.

Product choices should reflect individual needs, tolerance, age, lifestyle, and goals. Dry or reactive skin may need hydration and barrier repair, while oily or congested skin may benefit from salicylic acid. Retinoids or exfoliants can be added once or twice weekly if needed. When moving from a multi-step routine, remove products gradually and allow two to four weeks for adjustment. Professional advice can help streamline routines safely.

Side Screen offense pairs a big screener with a smaller ballhandler, creating penetration and post-up or shooting threats. NBA teams generally avoid switching because it can leave a smaller defender against the screener, preferring “Show & Recover.” The screener’s defender steps out to force the ballhandler wide while the on-ball defender fights over the screen; once guarding position is restored, the screener’s defender recovers and weakside defenders close out.

SOS defense varies by screen location. Above the free-throw line extended, defenders use an aggressive contact switch, force the ballhandler toward the sideline or corner, deny middle penetration, smother the stopped dribbler, front the rolling screener, and establish weakside “I” help positions. Below the line, defenders employ a baseline or corner trap, cover the screener with the low help defender, form a “Triangle I,” and close out after a pass.

All-Out SOS Disruption attacks before the screen develops. The point guard is forced toward the baseline and trapped, while teammates rotate to cover the roll and passing options. On a pass out, defenders rotate using the near-player concept, close out, deny return passes, and resume basic SOS principles. If the screener receives the ball on a baseline roll, defenders trap the post and rotate into help, denial, and fronting positions. All rotations occur as the pass leaves the passer’s hands.

Reports of unethical bank sales tactics and pressure on advisors reveal risks from incentive systems focused on revenue and production despite institutions’ client-first claims. The passage recommends tying advisor compensation to client satisfaction, rewarding advice not to buy products—potentially through wider use of base salaries—and requiring minimum educational qualifications. These changes could reduce complaints, improve asset retention and morale, strengthen the industry’s reputation, and support unbiased, high-quality advice. Advisors are urged to pressure financial institution leaders to replace sales-driven incentives with systems that reward client-first behaviour.

Consumer Reports tested 23 popular U.S. protein powders and ready-to-drink shakes, finding that more than two-thirds contained more lead per serving than its experts consider safe for daily consumption. Some contained 10 times that level, and contamination was higher than in its 2010 testing. Naked Nutrition’s Vegan Mass Gainer had 7.7 micrograms of lead per serving, while Huel Black Edition had 6.3 micrograms.

Plant-based powders averaged about nine times more lead than dairy proteins such as whey, potentially because plants absorb metals from soil and processing can concentrate contamination. Consumer Reports advised against daily use of most protein powders.

Protein powders are regulated as dietary supplements, with no federal lead limit or premarket FDA approval. Companies largely self-regulate, and NSF certification permits up to 10 micrograms of lead daily, compared with Consumer Reports’ concern level of 0.5 micrograms.

Martineau said most people can meet protein needs through whole foods. The recommended daily amount is 0.8 grams per kilogram of body weight, and most Americans already consume more than the recommended proportion of calories from protein.

The speaker praised a player’s timely goals and composure, described Arvi’s breakaway play and Pekka’s key saves, and credited a strong third period for closing out the game. He called the win an ideal birthday gift but emphasized returning to work. Team play, depth contributions, continued improvement, and stronger center play were identified as essential as the series becomes harder.

Intermediate attacking runs involve off-ball movement that creates opportunities for both the runner and teammates. Core principles include recognizing opportunities, choosing and timing runs, escaping defenders, receiving effective passes, and communicating.

Individual techniques include back-door runs, drifting, doubling back, delaying runs to avoid offside, recycling unrewarded runs, and setting up defenders by changing established patterns. Team-oriented runs create space by drawing defenders away and include decoy runs, dragging opponents, dropping the ball to a trailing teammate, and dummy runs.

Offensive switches exchange teammates’ positions and may be called verbally or occur naturally. Horizontal switches use crossing diagonal runs, while vertical switches exchange front-to-back positions. Players should communicate when switching back. In a cross-over exchange, a dribbler places the ball on a teammate’s matching foot before sprinting into space.

Players making effective runs must be ready to receive, anticipate their next action, and move toward passes to prevent interceptions.

Effective soccer communication relies on brief, clearly understood calls that quickly convey tactical information. Players without the ball—especially those behind it—often communicate because they have a broader view of play. Coaches should introduce age-appropriate terminology alongside relevant skills and tactics, while eventually teaching all players the full vocabulary.

The passage defines calls from introductory through advanced levels for receiving, passing, shooting, movement, defending, marking, support, positioning, offside awareness, transitions, set pieces, and time management. It also identifies specialized instructions used by defensive organizers and goalkeepers to coordinate defensive shape, assign opponents, manage walls, control the penalty area, and claim the ball.

Teams need not use every listed call and may select consistent, agreed-upon terms suited to their players. Higher-level teams may also use nonverbal signals, coded calls, and decoy communication. Players should listen to opponents’ calls, and distinct names or nicknames should identify teammates who share a name.

U.S. wages and benefits rose 2.6 percent in 2017, the fastest pace since 2015, despite slower fourth-quarter growth. Economists said pay should rise faster with unemployment at 4.1 percent. Hourly wages increased 2.5 percent, down from 2.9 percent in 2016.

The coach said a fire involving Danny caused only property damage, with insurance expected to cover it, and should not distract the team. Calgary played the style that made it the Western Conference’s best team, while his team lacked consistency, urgency, and proper respect for its opponent. He expects a strong response after reviewing the game and correcting the team’s mindset rather than making major tactical changes.

Marty played well and created chances, and the coach expects him to resume scoring consistently. He rejected labeling the next game a “must-win,” saying the team approaches every game intending to win. Calgary’s aggression and decision-making were not surprising, but his team responded too nonchalantly. The coach emphasized maintaining an even keel, learning from losses, and focusing on the next response. He also expressed confidence that Nikolai Khabibulin would rebound, be the team’s best player, and lead its response in the next game.

The study developed a simplified, potentially field-deployable metagenomic next-generation sequencing protocol for detecting SARS-CoV-2 in clinical throat swabs using Oxford Nanopore technology. It combined sample pretreatment, manual nucleic-acid extraction, random amplification, rapid barcoding, sequencing, and metagenomic analysis.

In pooled samples, DNase I treatment followed by 0.22-µm filtration substantially outperformed filtration, DNase treatment, or no pretreatment. The combined treatment increased SARS-CoV-2 BLAST hits from 31.8% without treatment to 99.9%, produced a 525-fold increase in mean viral reads per 100,000 reads, and achieved 99.3% reference-genome coverage after 20 hours. More than half of the genome was covered within 10 minutes. Apparent Orthohepevirus A hits from single pretreatments were judged false positives because reads mapped only to short genome regions.

Testing individual samples showed 85.8–100% genome coverage for samples with CT values of 30 or lower, compared with approximately 40–61% at CT values of 33 or higher. All 14 positive samples were identified as clade 21J Delta, while Pangolin sub-lineages were obtained for samples with CT values below 33. Reads also appeared in negative controls, possibly during demultiplexing, emphasizing contamination and interpretation risks.

The protocol avoids large equipment such as centrifuges, extraction robots, thermal cyclers, and Illumina sequencers. Its principal limitation is evaluation only with SARS-CoV-2; broader testing with other RNA and DNA viruses and sample types remains necessary.

A July 18, 2001 energy news digest covers California’s power crisis and national energy policy. California accelerated power-plant permitting, but only 2,500 of a targeted 5,000 megawatts were expected by July, making summer blackouts likely. PG&E sued California for compensation for wholesale electricity contracts seized by Gov. Gray Davis; estimates of their value ranged from about $150 million to $347 million. PG&E’s conservation rebate program awarded $7.6 million, with 29% of processed customers reducing usage by at least 20%.

Duke Energy reported a 27% increase in second-quarter profit, driven by trading and wholesale power. Davis used the energy crisis to increase his national political profile, blaming power companies and federal regulators while emphasizing environmental differences with President Bush. California lawmakers considered competing plans to prevent Southern California Edison’s bankruptcy, including purchasing transmission lines or financing debt through bonds and rate increases. A Chicago Tribune editorial argued that energy markets were easing gasoline, natural gas and electricity pressures and urged the Bush administration to combine expanded energy supply with conservation and environmental protection.

Over 60 per cent report worker shortages, prompting wage increases. Employment, labor costs and capital spending are expected to grow modestly, while material costs should rise slightly less than in 2017.

The FDA approved a second generic version of mifepristone, allowing three U.S. companies to produce the abortion pill despite opposition from anti-abortion groups and politicians. The approval is not expected to significantly affect access. Separately, Amgen said its cholesterol drug Repatha prevented cardiovascular deaths, heart attacks, and common strokes in a 12,000-patient trial, though full results were not released. Repatha generated $2.2 billion in 2024 sales, up 36%.

Gatwick recorded its busiest July, handling 4.7 million passengers, up 2.4%. Long-haul passengers rose 10.7% and cargo 20.4%, driven by routes including California and China. New services to North and South America, Taipei and Singapore were also planned.

James Walker Morales escaped Rhode Island’s Wyatt Detention Center by climbing a basketball hoop, cutting through fencing, crossing a razor-wire-covered roof and descending the building. Officers discovered him missing 3½ hours later, prompting a lockdown, security review and two officers’ administrative leave. Authorities tracked him toward Attleboro, finding bloody prison clothing and a suspected stolen car later recovered. Morales, held over alleged weapons theft, remained at large Monday.

Rockefeller researchers studying cell death in C. elegans discovered a “compartmentalized” process in the tail-spike cell. Its central body separates from its long extension, rounds up, and disintegrates, while the extension breaks into bead-like pieces or retracts into a ball for removal by a neighboring cell. A neuron was observed dying similarly, suggesting the process may occur in other animals. The team also found that the protein EFF-1 helps phagocytes seal their extensions around cell remnants, enabling rapid debris removal and offering insight into how phagocytes clear complex-shaped dying cells.

Second-quarter filings showed hedge funds shifting FAANG holdings. Third Point increased stakes in Facebook and Alphabet, while Omega Advisors reduced Facebook, Netflix and Amazon positions but retained Alphabet. Jana Partners increased its Whole Foods stake before profiting from Amazon’s acquisition deal. Facebook and Alphabet shares rose following Third Point’s investments.

A Lewisville mother earns money as a mystery shopper. Contrave, approved for certain overweight or obese patients, produced only modest additional weight loss in trials and may cause serious health risks. Consumer Reports recommends discussing alternatives with a doctor and prioritizing diet, exercise and intensive behavioral programs.

Apple Inc.’s fiscal 2017 Form 10-K describes a California-based company that designs, manufactures and markets mobile devices, computers, software, services and accessories. Its offerings include iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, operating systems, digital content services, iCloud, Apple Pay and AppleCare. The patent describes a heterogeneous, coarse-grained reconfigurable computing architecture intended to provide high-performance, energy-efficient execution of compute-intensive applications. Its hybrid threading fabric consists of arrays of configurable computing tiles connected through both a synchronous point-to-point mesh and an asynchronous packet network. Synchronous domains pipeline computations across tiles without intermediate queuing, while the asynchronous network carries data, continuation, completion, memory, and control messages.

Each tile includes configurable arithmetic, logical, multiply, shift, permutation, and conversion circuitry; local and configuration memories; synchronous inputs and outputs; asynchronous queues; and memory, thread, and flow-control circuitry. Separate instruction and “spoke” memories configure tile data paths, select current and subsequent instructions, designate synchronous inputs and outputs, and support dynamic reconfiguration and conditional branching.

Thread-control mechanisms support self-scheduling, ordered execution, data-dependency completion counts, loops and nested loops, private loop variables, and multiple thread-identifier types. Continuation, reenter, priority, and run queues govern execution readiness and priority. Loop tables specify subsequent threads, while loop counts and asynchronous completion messages track completion. Backpressure can halt packet output and tile execution when output queues reach specified thresholds.

The broader system may include configurable-circuit clusters, a hybrid threading processor, host and dispatch interfaces, memory interfaces, and a hierarchical interconnection network. Dispatch interfaces receive work descriptors, configure tiles, allocate identifiers, distribute arguments, track completion, and return results. Memory interfaces support loads, stores, and atomic operations. The disclosed methods cover configuration, conditional branching, flow control, thread ordering, dependency-based execution, loop management, synchronous-domain communication, and asynchronous messaging.

The MSPM0G3519/G3518/G1519/G1518 IOMUX selects digital I/O peripheral functions and controls output drivers, input paths, and shutdown wake-up logic; pin capabilities vary by device. An ARM-compatible two-wire SWD interface supports debugging.

The boot strap loader programs and configures devices through UART or I2C. It is enabled by default, protected by a user-defined 256-bit password, and can be disabled. A read-only, memory-mapped FACTORY region stores device capabilities, identification, hardware revision, and trim information. DEVICEID is at 0x41C40004 and USERID at 0x41C40008.

YbCu1.14Se2 was investigated as an exchange-disordered triangular-lattice magnet related to quantum spin-liquid candidates AYbSe2 and YbMgGaO4. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction found a P-3m1 structure with a well-ordered triangular lattice of magnetic Yb ions and disordered Cu occupancy of 56.6±0.7%, yielding YbCu1.14Se2. The resulting nonmagnetic-site disorder is expected to produce a distribution of magnetic exchanges.

Magnetic susceptibility indicates localized Yb3+ moments and antiferromagnetic exchange, with a low-temperature Weiss temperature of −17.2(5) K. Specific heat shows no magnetic-ordering anomaly between 100 mK and 10 K, but is sublinear from about 100 mK to 5 K and recovers roughly 85% of R ln(2) entropy by 10 K. AC susceptibility displays a frequency-dependent freezing peak near 0.1 K, characteristic of spin-glass behavior. No one-third magnetization plateau was observed, indicating departure from the ideal two-dimensional triangular Heisenberg model.

The combination of Cu disorder, absent magnetic order, substantial quantum fluctuations, sublinear specific heat, and low-temperature freezing resembles YbMgGaO4 and theoretical disordered triangular magnets. The authors propose that such behavior may be a universal feature of disordered frustrated systems and model the specific heat using a distribution of disordered quantum singlets.

Robert “Knobby” Knudsen received the Bridgestone Mark Messier Youth Leadership Award for his extensive work helping children, including founding Windsor’s Kids Skate for Kids program. His son accepted the award and recalled his father’s belief that improving a child’s life mattered more than material success.

Dustin Brown, Shane Doan and Ryan Callahan were announced as finalists for the Mark Messier Leadership Award, recognizing their on-ice leadership, professionalism and community work. Messier particularly praised Brown’s maturity, captaincy and charitable initiatives.

Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk argues the U.S. economy is accelerating despite repeated forecasts of a slowdown. Resilient consumer spending, stronger investment and stable housing support growth, while Atlanta Fed estimates point to 3.9% third-quarter GDP growth. Sløk attributes slower hiring to reduced immigration rather than broad weakness and warns that continued Federal Reserve rate cuts amid strong growth could revive inflation.

Morgan Stanley strategist Mike Wilson describes a transition from a three-year “rolling recession” to a “rolling recovery,” reflected more in stocks than employment. Recent ADP data showed job losses in September and declines in three of four months. Sløk says economists’ persistent, inaccurate slowdown predictions have damaged their credibility.

US$INR January futures are viewed bearish, with a sell range of 68.20–68.30, targets of 67.95/67.75 and stop-loss at 68.40. Indian bond yields recorded their biggest annual fall in eight years, while the rupee posted a sixth annual loss. Investors are advised to consult certified experts.

National Literacy Month highlights persistent reading inequities and the need for sustained support for effective local programs. In South Los Angeles, Partnership for Growth LA’s Read Lead Freedom Schools combine small classes, culturally relevant books, enrichment and civic projects. A 2023–24 pilot reported increased English proficiency, sharply reduced chronic absenteeism and improved student confidence, motivation and social-emotional growth. Nobel Peace Prize winner and ICAN executive director Beatrice Fihn warned that panic, carelessness, misunderstandings or bruised egos could trigger nuclear attacks destroying cities and killing millions. Fihn said nuclear risk is greater than at the Cold War’s end due to more nuclear-armed states, terrorism and cyberwarfare. ICAN advocates a treaty banning nuclear weapons.

Following a divisive political contest, citizens are urged to respect the lawful decision of the majority while protecting the equal rights of the minority. Political intolerance should be rejected, differences of opinion should not be mistaken for differences of principle, and Republicans and Federalists should unite around shared commitments to union and representative government. Free reason, rather than repression, should answer erroneous opinions.

The nation’s advantages require one further safeguard: a wise and frugal government that prevents people from harming one another, otherwise leaves them free to pursue industry and improvement, and does not unnecessarily burden labor.

He reports the lawful discharge of the temporary army and recommends improvements to the federal judiciary.

A treaty with Prussia has been ratified, while negotiations continue with Great Britain over an unresolved treaty provision and with France toward accommodation. Federal revenue has reached its highest level for an equivalent period, demonstrating national resources and the effectiveness of measures protecting commerce and public credit. Montgomery gas prices rose four cents to $2.18 per gallon, while the national average reached $2.40, its highest since September 2015. Analysts cited declining oil inventories, geopolitical tensions, increased summer demand and possible extended OPEC production cuts. GasBuddy expected prices may soon peak, while AAA forecast increases through September.

Zimbabwe’s Health Ministry estimates 44,586 female sex workers aged 15–49, including 12,800 in Harare and 6,800 in Bulawayo, excluding male sex workers and transactional sex. Their average HIV prevalence is 55 percent, compared with a 13 percent national average. The report aims to guide HIV funding and programmes. AIDS-related deaths fell from 278 daily in 2005 to 71 in 2016. Parliamentarian Ruth Labode warned that neglecting vulnerable key populations could undermine efforts to end HIV/AIDS by 2030.

AAA did not act in bad faith by failing to meet the claimants’ two-week settlement deadline because their counsel did not identify all potential heirs or lienholders, provide a release, or respond to AAA’s repeated inquiries. GoSun introduced the Fusion, a portable solar-electric oven designed to steam, bake, or roast indoors or outdoors, day or night. Its vacuum-insulated solar oven can operate through clouds and freezing temperatures, while a 150-watt, 12-volt electric heater enables cooking without sunlight and can run on a compact lithium-ion battery. The heater is claimed to be five times more efficient than a typical oven. The 10-pound, weatherproof Fusion reaches 350°F, has a 3.2-liter capacity, feeds five people, remains cool to the touch, and is built for rugged transport. GoSun launched a Kickstarter campaign offering deals to early backers. The company has sold more than 25,000 solar stoves across over 80 countries.

The passage proposes bivariate zero-inflated Poisson models for dependent count data with excess zeros. Counts are generated as \(X=WT\), where a common Bernoulli factor \(W\) creates simultaneous zero inflation with parameter \(\phi\), while \(T=(T_1,T_2)\) has Poisson margins with rates \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\). Dependence in \(T\) is introduced through comonotonic or counter-monotonic Poisson shocks controlled by \(\theta\), producing the positive-dependence BZIP+ and negative-dependence BZIP− models. Joint probability, distribution, and generating functions are derived for both classes.

Dependence arises from both the common inflation factor and latent shocks. Increasing \(\theta\) strengthens positive dependence in BZIP+ and negative dependence in BZIP−. Increasing \(\phi\) always raises correlation in BZIP− by increasing common zeros, but may raise or lower correlation in BZIP+. BZIP+ reaches the upper Fréchet–Hoeffding bound at \(\theta=1\); BZIP− reaches the lower bound at \(\theta=1\) only without zero inflation. Both families are ordered by positive quadrant dependence.

Parameters can be estimated using moments, maximum likelihood, or an EM algorithm. Moment estimators match marginal means and second moments and use covariance to estimate \(\theta\), but may violate parameter constraints in small or sparse samples. Maximum likelihood offers one-step and two-step implementations, with an explicit estimator for \(\phi\). The EM algorithm provides closed-form updates for \(\phi\) and marginal rates and requires univariate optimization for \(\theta\).

Simulations examined 72 scenarios across sample sizes, rates, inflation levels, dependence strengths, and dependence signs. Accuracy improved with sample size, while high zero inflation increased variability by reducing information about latent Poisson parameters. The two likelihood methods produced nearly identical results and generally lower root mean squared error than moment estimation. Negative-dependence models presented more numerical and initialization difficulties.

An application to 576 monthly Australian disaster records fitted BZIP+ to floods and storms and BZIP− to floods and bushfires. Both analyses indicated significant zero inflation and latent dependence, supporting the proposed models over independent or non-zero-inflated alternatives. The positive-dependence construction can also be extended directly to higher dimensions using multivariate comonotonic Poisson shocks.

The passage offers general essay-writing advice, including choosing an interesting topic, brainstorming, developing a thesis, using reliable sources, maintaining a formal tone, organizing by word count, and editing for errors. It notes that students may struggle with academic papers, limited time, motivation, concentration, and evaluating online sources. It also promotes professional essay-writing services, claiming expert writers can provide customized, original coursework while recommending tools such as Hemingway, FreeMind, and XMind.

Most Southeast Asian stock markets declined as investors awaited the U.S. Federal Reserve’s policy meeting and projections for future rate hikes. Thailand led losses amid weaker energy stocks, while Singapore and Indonesia also fell. Philippine shares recovered from early declines but closed marginally lower. Malaysia edged higher on financial and telecom gains. Vietnam rose for a sixth consecutive session, reaching its highest close since March 2007, supported by real estate and industrial stocks.
Hillview Middle School hosts an all-ages outdoor screening of “Sing” April 27 at 7:30 p.m. Food sales benefit LLS and JDRF. One adult is required per eight children.

The lecture extends temporal difference policy evaluation from discrete Markov chains to continuous domains using function approximation. Least-squares fitting with linear-in-parameter models can represent nonlinear functions through basis functions such as radial basis functions, barycentric interpolators, Fourier components, and polynomials. Unlike neural networks, linear approximators often permit direct analytic solutions and stronger convergence results.

Robot system identification can also be formulated as linear least squares because rigid-body dynamics are often linear in grouped physical parameters, despite being nonlinear in state. Accurate identification requires suitable basis functions and sufficiently rich excitation; unmodeled effects can be represented with additional basis terms.

For TD learning, the value function is parameterized by a linear approximator. Eligibility traces track each parameter’s recent contribution using the value estimate’s gradient, which equals the basis vector for linear models. This yields TD(lambda) with function approximation, with convergence results for linear approximators.

Standard TD updates use data incrementally and discard it. Least-squares temporal difference learning instead accumulates matrices from experience and directly solves for the steady-state parameter estimate. LSTD uses data more efficiently, avoids selecting a learning rate or initial parameter estimate, and can be adapted to incremental or periodic updates. Function approximation enables reinforcement-learning methods to scale beyond tabular systems, though strong theoretical results are largely limited to linear approximators.

The contracting parties guarantee one another’s territorial integrity and political independence under republican governments. They agree to settle territorial disputes amicably or through arbitration, submit unresolved disputes to international investigation before hostilities, and, with specified exceptions, pursue arbitration afterward. They also pledge to prevent hostile expeditions and arms shipments supporting insurrections against member governments. Ratifications are to be deposited with the Pan American Union in Washington, with provisions for entry into force, duration, and denunciation.

S. E. Mezes tells the Secretary of State that he will confidentially recast enclosed principles into a general plan without references to particular nations. Secretary of War Baker tells Walter Lippmann that he supports making postwar Germany livable for its people and the world, while requiring reliable assurances that access to resources will serve civilization.

A University of Edinburgh review found little consistent evidence that heavier biodegradable plastic bags are environmentally beneficial. Existing life-cycle and decomposition studies use varied protocols, produce inconsistent findings, and are often poorly defined, limiting their usefulness for policy and regulation.

The Trap play is a quick, downhill run scheme in which a pulling guard kicks out an interior defensive lineman. It is especially effective against aggressive pass rushers and can suit either a powerful fullback or a dynamic tailback. Its quick execution and deceptive backfield action give defenders little time to locate the ball. Angle blocks also make it suitable for smaller offensive linemen.

Trap is less effective against defensive fronts that squeeze interior gaps and prevent linemen from reaching linebackers. Against both 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, the guard pulls to kick out the first defensive lineman on or outside the opposite guard, while other linemen create an interior running lane and block second-level defenders. The fullback steps off the midline, takes the handoff, bends toward the kickout block, and runs vertically. The quarterback and tailback use perimeter action to misdirect defenders, while receivers engage the safeties.

Variations include a shotgun same-side Trap RPO, allowing the quarterback to throw a bubble or slant based on the nickel defender, and the Wing-T Trap, which mirrors Buck Sweep backfield action but gives the ball to a different runner.

Kinder Morgan rose after Canada agreed to buy its pipeline project. Bank of America and Petrobras fell amid lower interest rates and diesel subsidies, while ZTO Express, Booz Allen, American Woodmark, KB Home and American Water Works gained.

The passage says criminologists Gary Kleck and Marc Gertz estimated in the 1990s that Americans used guns defensively more than 2.2 million times annually. It reports that three unpublished CDC surveys from 1996–1998 produced a similar estimate of 2.46 million adult defensive gun users per year, suggesting defensive use occurred 3.6 times as often as criminal use. Kleck noted that the CDC never published or acknowledged these findings but did not accuse it of misconduct. Dean Weingarten suggested the results may have remained unpublished because they conflicted with the Clinton administration’s gun-control agenda. The author argues that the episode undermines gun-control claims, demonstrates the need to verify government information, supports private gun ownership, and highlights the importance of public education on gun policy.

Mitsui’s April-December net profit rose 64% to a record 376.8 billion yen, driven by higher iron ore and coking coal prices. It raised its full-year forecast to 440 billion yen. Itochu posted record profit but maintained its forecast, while Sojitz increased its annual outlook by 12%.

The President reviews U.S. foreign policy and urges national unity and cooperation between Congress and the executive. He describes strong alliances in Europe and Asia, improving but competitive relations with the Soviet Union, an opening with China, and U.S. efforts on Middle East peace and global issues including energy, food, trade, and the environment.

Focusing on the crisis in Indochina, he attributes South Vietnam’s deteriorating position to North Vietnamese violations of the Paris accords, reduced U.S. assistance, and a poorly executed South Vietnamese withdrawal. He requests $722 million in emergency military aid and an initial $250 million in economic and humanitarian assistance. He also seeks authority to use U.S. forces, if necessary, to evacuate Americans and endangered Vietnamese. He warns that aid to Cambodia may soon come too late.

The President argues that the United States must honor commitments, reassure allies, and maintain strong defense and intelligence capabilities. He calls for lifting the arms embargo on Turkey, supporting Greece, revising trade restrictions affecting friendly developing countries, and reconsidering sanctions that damaged trade and relations with the Soviet Union. He supports continued arms-control negotiations, stronger relations with China, renewed Middle East peace efforts, and cooperation on global challenges.

He concludes that American leadership, credibility, compassion, and unity are essential to world stability and asks Congress to help maintain a coherent national foreign policy.

Wayne Richert criticizes a six-and-a-half-hour Norfolk General Hospital emergency wait, blaming administrators rather than medical staff and urging doctors be authorized to call in additional help. Donna Clarke argues long-term care residents should receive free medications and questions whether newly announced provincial funding for care beds is politically motivated ahead of the June 7 election.

Peter DeBoer said each win brings his team closer to its goal and could shift the series. Returning veterans provided energy, while a rookie delivered an exceptional clutch performance. The team finally gained momentum after struggling to score first or win in overtime. DeBoer emphasized the players’ resilience, confidence, and desire to remain in Stanley Cup contention. He praised a veteran’s composure and legacy, called for more scoring, and said the power play created quality chances despite strong goaltending and penalty killing. The team must end its opponent’s streak to avoid elimination.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for dynamically replacing video content while preserving or modifying overlays generated by set-top boxes or client devices. A client device identifies the set-top box, fingerprints incoming video frames, matches them against reference fingerprints, and selects replacement content, such as substituting a local commercial for a national commercial.

Device-specific templates identify menus, notifications, picture-in-picture regions, cropped areas, and semi-transparent overlays. The client combines replacement and incoming video using masks, resizing, repositioning, cropping, filtering, or alpha blending so relevant interface information remains visible. Templates may be manually created or programmatically generated through regional and multi-frame analysis.

The system can detect channel changes, playback speed, pause, rewind, and fast-forward, adjusting or suspending replacement content accordingly. Components include fingerprint generators, a video identification system, a replacement content server, template databases, and client overlay modules implemented through hardware, software, or both.

KDKA-TV and WPXI-TV falsely reported that video showed 17-year-old Antwon Rose II firing a gun before he was fatally shot by Officer Michael Rosfeld and that gunshot residue was found on Rose’s hands. Allegheny County Police Superintendent Coleman McDonough denied both claims and warned media against using unverified sources. WTAE-TV did not air the false information.

KDKA later retracted the report, acknowledged its sources were incorrect and expressed regret. WPXI initially defended its reporting, citing multiple sources, but later apologized for pain caused to Rose’s family and the community. District attorney spokesman Mike Manko criticized local television media for repeatedly providing incorrect information and resisting corrections. The New Pittsburgh Courier argued that the stations failed to adequately question their sources and examine possible motives behind information portraying Rose negatively.

YouTube Red will debut four family-oriented series in spring: “Hyperlinked,” “DanTDM Creates A Big Scene,” “The Kings of Atlantis,” and “Fruit Ninja: Frenzy Force.” Additional shows will premiere throughout 2017. YouTube Kids will also become available on select internet-connected LG and Samsung Smart TVs.

The Kiss of Death is an S&P 500 sell signal triggered after the index falls from an all-time high below its monthly 21-EMA, rebounds above it, then drops below its recent low. It preceded major bear markets in 1969, 1973, 1978, 2001, and 2008, but produced a false signal in September 2022. The strategy sells when the signal occurs and re-enters when the index closes above its 10-month EMA. A backtest beginning in 1967, excluding dividends, showed higher compound annual growth and nearly half the maximum drawdown of buying and holding the S&P 500.

The passage describes the AGESA software interface, build environment, initialization stages, and host BIOS responsibilities. Errors other than SUCCESS and BOUNDS_CHK are logged in a circular buffer containing the 16 latest events, retrievable through AmdReadEventLog.

Support for 16-bit Real Mode is deprecated; the binary module operates in 32-bit protected mode. A host bridge calls the AGESA dispatcher with a function identifier, while AGESA call-outs return through a host-implemented router. The host must establish a valid stack, initialize standard headers, locate the binary image, implement required call-outs, and supply configuration structures. Binary-module and source-integration build methods are supported.

UEFI integration spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases. SEC establishes 32-bit execution and a stack. PEIMs initialize processors and memory, coordinate resets, and publish PPIs and memory-information HOBs. DXE performs late initialization, generates system tables, publishes the AgesaDxeProtocol, and may manage integrated-GPU VGA decoding. Platform option files, UEFI control files, build tools, and environment variables such as AGESA_ROOT and AGESA_OptsDir must be integrated into the host build.

Cache-As-RAM stack macros establish and remove pre-memory stacks. The host must not alter SS, ESP, cache controls, MTRRs, or APIC state when prohibited during initialization. PSP-equipped AArch64 APUs do not use the stack and early macros because the PSP initializes DRAM.

Service procedures create and release parameter structures, retrieve DIMM data-eye results, processor APIC and PCI addresses, current-core identity, execution-cache size, memory-device locations, and event-log entries, and update MMIO mappings. Most procedures require a stack; some require operational coherent HyperTransport links.

Published initialization entry points execute in boot order. AmdInitReset performs minimal processor and chipset initialization and allocates execution-cache regions under alignment, boundary, and capacity rules. AmdInitEarly performs full processor, HyperTransport, power-management, PCIe, graphics, and platform configuration before memory initialization. AmdInitPost initializes memory, configures interleaving, ECC, UMA, training, voltage, and related policies, transfers artifacts to main memory, and disables the pre-memory stack. Subsequent environment and mid-stage routines preserve HOB data, configure graphics and chipset resources, and run around PCI enumeration.

AmdInitLate generates operating-system data such as DMI, P-state, WHEA, CRAT, CDIT, ALIB, and IVRS tables using host-allocated buffers. The host must register generated ACPI tables and preserve required heap data. Ready-to-boot processing saves processor and silicon context for suspend. Resume procedures restore memory, processor state, PCI-related registers, and final silicon configuration before operating-system handoff. The host remains responsible for initiating suspend or restart and supplying preserved volatile and non-volatile context data.

Fair Isaac introduced a pricing model allowing mortgage lenders to obtain FICO scores through mortgage resellers rather than credit bureaus, aiming to eliminate markups and offer lenders more pricing and distribution choices. Fair Isaac shares rose more than 20%, while Experian, TransUnion and Equifax fell 4% to 10% amid concerns about their reduced role. Fair Isaac will offer both pricing models to the three bureaus on equal terms.

MSPM0C1105/6 are cost-optimized, ultra-low-power 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0+ MCUs operating up to 32MHz. They support 1.62V–3.6V, temperatures from -40°C to 125°C, up to 64KB flash and 8KB SRAM, with integrated analog, timers, DMA, and multiple communication peripherals.

Britain’s coffee market reached £3.4 billion in 2016 after rising 37 per cent in five years, with further growth forecast. Costa, the world’s second-largest coffee chain behind Starbucks, has more than 2,000 UK shops despite Britain ranking only 44th globally for per-capita coffee consumption.

To support expansion, Costa opened a roastery in Basildon, selected for its proximity to Tilbury Docks and London transport links. The facility quadruples annual roasting capacity from 11,000 to 45,000 tonnes, equivalent to 2.1 billion cups, and can receive 24 tonnes of beans per hour. Automated packing is expected to increase productivity by 25 per cent.

Beans imported worldwide arrive hard and whitish-green, then undergo cleaning, roasting, testing and packing. Brazil is the largest coffee producer and Vietnam the second largest; Vietnamese robusta beans contribute to Costa’s blend. Costa combines aromatic, acidic arabica with stronger, bitter robusta, changing source countries when seasonal quality declines.

Every incoming bag is sampled and inspected for defects before laboratory roasting and tasting. Around 8 per cent of beans are rejected annually. Colour, moisture and flavour are closely monitored to maintain consistency. Master of Coffee Gennaro Pellicia, whose tongue is insured for £10 million, oversees tasting and staff development.

The roastery uses solar energy, harvested rainwater and LED lighting, and is seeking final BREEAM “outstanding” certification. Costa also sources Rainforest Alliance Certified coffee. The site can train 3,000 baristas annually, has room for expansion and is designed for at least 30 years of operation.

Tesla Motors reported an immaterial error in its 2015 Form 10-K that overstated the Supercharger network’s cost and net book value. The correct net book value as of December 31, 2015 was $166.6 million. The error was confined to management’s discussion and did not affect consolidated financial statements or accompanying notes.

Researchers developed a molecular sensor that releases thyme-flavored thymol when influenza neuraminidase interacts with it. Intended for gum or lozenges, it could enable rapid, accessible screening before symptoms. In laboratory tests, the sensor released thymol within 30 minutes in saliva from flu patients and did not alter human or mouse cell function. Human clinical trials are planned in about two years. The technology has been patented with the European Patent Office.

Nominations are open for the 12th Harrogate Advertiser Business Awards, with entries due by noon on Monday, March 13, at harrogatebusinessawards.co.uk. Businesses may enter any of 10 categories covering company size, rural and family businesses, tourism, employment, websites, business personality and lifetime achievement. The lecture examines multi-stakeholder engagement in sustainable supply chains, using palm oil and GAR as the central case. Palm oil supply chains involve growers, mills, intermediaries, corporations, consumers, governments, investors, certifying bodies, NGOs, competitors, and affected local and international communities. Their complexity and limited transparency make it difficult to trace sources and practices.

Greenpeace’s campaign against Nestlé illustrates how NGOs may target prominent brands rather than distant suppliers, attracting publicity and consumer pressure that prompts companies to investigate their supply chains. Students proposed several strategies for GAR: collaborate with Greenpeace, treat it as an outsider while emphasizing industry self-regulation, or exceed baseline standards and offer a premium sustainable product. They also discussed publishing sustainability reports, working with technical NGOs such as the Forest Trust, and promoting standardized certification through the RSPO.

Key challenges include mixing certified and non-certified palm oil, uncertain certification costs, limited demand for certified products, and the financial burden on small farmers. Proposed responses included improving farmer productivity, education and training, financial incentives, third-party audits, land-use limits, and NGO or government support. The RSPO was characterized as a voluntary incentive, while mandatory Indonesian standards could provide an industry baseline.

GAR must decide whether to maintain higher anti-deforestation standards for niche sustainability markets or lower them to compete in cost-driven markets. Participants also emphasized proactive leadership, collaboration with stakeholders, innovation, risk mitigation, and communication through corporate strategy, sustainability departments, product labels, or public advocates.

The lecture described three broad partnership models: one-to-one partnerships, multiple specialized partners, and industry collaborations. Examples included Chiquita with the Rainforest Alliance, Dell with Goodwill for electronic waste collection, Walmart with the Environmental Defense Fund, and Starbucks with several organizations. Industry collaborations included the RSPO, Sustainability Consortium, Electronic Industry Citizenship Coalition, and Sustainable Apparel Coalition, which provide research, certification, training, measurement tools, and supply-chain guidance.

Effective partnerships require clear objectives, project design, defined company contacts, execution, and measurable outcomes. NGOs differ in approach: some offer technical collaboration, while others emphasize public pressure. Certification labels also vary greatly in rigor, with limited oversight and potential consumer confusion, although labels such as organic and Energy Star are widely recognized.

Pekkala stated that most Finns supported the democracies and increasingly favored a separate peace with the Soviet Union, views he said were shared by Mannerheim, many military figures, Social Democrats, and smaller parties, though not generally by Agrarians. From Sweden, Johnson reported that Finland’s military position was rapidly worsening. He warned that a Russian offensive and advance toward Sweden and Norway could provoke Swedish assistance to Finland, strengthen pro-German groups, create a major political crisis, and threaten Sweden’s coalition government. Soviet Minister Kollontay similarly feared the effects of a Russian advance on Sweden and considered a simple cessation of fighting the only hope for Russo-Finnish peace.

Four leading Baltimore County executive candidates—Democrats Vicki Almond, Jim Brochin and Johnny Olszewski Jr., and Republican Al Redmer Jr.—addressed real estate and development professionals. None endorsed impact fees on new construction, though they offered differing reasons. All acknowledged problems with the county’s cumbersome development approval process and supported making it smoother.

Olszewski and Redmer argued that rezoning should follow the county master plan, while Redmer also supported appeals for downzoned properties. Brochin suggested allowing the planning board to override County Council rezoning decisions. Almond emphasized that rezoning authority belongs to the council, not the executive.

Most candidates stressed development’s importance to economic growth and property tax revenue. Brochin differed by reiterating his pledge to end “pay-to-play politics” involving developer campaign contributions. The June 26 primary will also include Democrat Kevin Marron and Republican Pat McDonough, with the winner seeking to succeed County Executive Kevin Kamenetz.

The first trading day of the month is the first market trading session, which may differ from the first calendar day due to weekends or holidays. Backtesting SPY since 1993 showed an average close-to-close gain of 0.24% from the previous month’s final trading day, compared with 0.04% on an average day. February and July produced the strongest results.

The basic strategy was unstable, with most gains occurring before the 2008–09 financial crisis, making it unsuitable by itself. Adding a filter reduced trades by one-third and raised the average gain to 0.35%, with a 3% CAGR, 67% win rate, 2.5 profit factor, and 5% maximum drawdown. Selling at the first day’s open produced a 0.22% average gain, 3.7 profit factor, and 3% maximum drawdown. Another strategy buying at the first day’s close under one criterion averaged 1.1% across 61 trades.

The passage suggests that capital inflows from savers, pension funds, and automatic retirement contributions may contribute to the effect.

The paper studies profit maximization in repeated bilateral trade, where a broker seeks to maximize buyer payments minus seller payments while ensuring dominant-strategy incentive compatibility and individual rationality. Unlike Bayesian approaches, it does not assume known or independent valuation distributions and evaluates online algorithms against the best mechanism in hindsight.

In the stochastic i.i.d. setting with possibly correlated valuations, the authors provide a polynomial-time algorithm achieving nearly tight \(\tilde O(\sqrt T)\) regret. An \(\Omega(\sqrt T)\) lower bound establishes optimality up to polylogarithmic factors. The analysis also implies that approximately \(1/\varepsilon^2\) samples are both sufficient and necessary to learn an expected \(\varepsilon\)-optimal mechanism.

In the adversarial setting, no algorithm can obtain sublinear regret even relative to a \(2/3+\varepsilon\) fraction of optimal profit, demonstrating a separation between stochastic and adversarial models. Identifying intermediate models permitting no-regret learning remains open.

A correspondence with non-excludable mechanism design also improves the joint ads problem’s regret bound from \(O(T^{3/4})\) to \(\tilde O(\sqrt T)\).

The main technical challenges are the non-parametric mechanism space and potentially irregular profit functions. Although incentive-compatible, individually rational mechanisms admit a geometric representation through a monotone trade region and boundary-determined payments, standard fixed-discretization and uniform-convergence methods are insufficient.

The team’s ability to have fun while working hard contributed to its success. A fearless, durable shot blocker sets an example for teammates. Excitement grew upon arriving amid increased media attention, while a smooth, understated defenseman was praised as deserving his top-defenseman nomination.
Hawkin’s Bazaar’s Plymouth shop will close on February 4 after 10 years in the city. Its clearance sale offers discounts of 50 to 75 percent.

Mediation analysis examines variables linking interventions to outcomes, helping explain treatment mechanisms, refine interventions, and provide early indicators of success. Structural equation modeling (SEM) is commonly used for latent mediators because it accounts for measurement error and shared indicator variance. However, causal mediation with SEM assumes sequential ignorability, requiring adjustment for all mediator–outcome confounders, which is rarely achievable and can produce biased, poorly generalizable estimates.

Rank-preserving models using g-estimation offer an alternative based on randomized trials. They permit omitted covariates under a no-effect-modifier assumption, provided those covariates do not interact with treatment or mediator. Because these models had not incorporated latent variables, the authors introduce the Rank-Preserving Structural Equation Model (RAPSEM), combining rank-preserving models, factor score regression, and interaction corrections. RAPSEM is intended to estimate mediation effects despite measurement error and omitted mediator–outcome confounders.

The framework models a randomized binary treatment and latent mediator, outcome, and covariates measured through observed indicators. It targets the controlled direct effect of treatment while holding the mediator fixed and the controlled mediation effect of changing mediator levels while holding treatment fixed. The paper presents estimation assumptions and asymptotic properties, then evaluates RAPSEM against standard SEM and assesses its statistical power through simulations.

The speaker said the team played comfortably and believed sustained strong play would create scoring chances. He praised the goalie’s performance after a difficult year and expressed confidence that the team could even the series. He highlighted the team’s shared maturity, individual leadership and game-changing skill, especially Ryan Smyth’s work ethic and ability to score important goals. The opposing penalty kill has pressured aggressively, but the team remains confident its power play will contribute. Solid coaching, tactical adjustments and greater structure have driven playoff success. The team handled a frustrating disputed play by refocusing, believes it has not yet played its best, and hopes to join the organization’s celebrated past teams.

The passage presents former professor Robert Oscar Lopez’s rejection of academic freedom as an absolute good, arguing that tenure protects a select group while adjuncts remain vulnerable and ideological dissenters face persecution. It contends that academic freedom cannot be unlimited because institutions inevitably restrict certain views, and alleges that universities apply such restrictions unevenly against conservatives. Quoting Lopez, it describes higher education as politically biased, financially exploitative, and harmful to indebted students. The author advocates reducing college funding, layoffs, associate degrees, trade schools, and apprenticeships, noting that degree production exceeds the number of degree-requiring jobs. Because academia will continue to exist, the author argues that teaching should be governed by objective truth rather than academic freedom, and calls for substantial reform of higher education.

MADSEN Cycles designs customizable bucket bikes with a large rear bucket capable of carrying up to four children and cargo. The bucket includes removable bench seats and four seat belts. Accessories such as rain covers, frame-mounted front racks, and a padded middle seat add comfort, security, carrying capacity, and functionality for transporting children, pets, groceries, or drinks.

A cross-sectional study conducted from April to August 2021 assessed visceral leishmaniasis (VL) seroprevalence, associated factors, community knowledge and practices, and sand fly abundance in six kebeles of Denan district, southeastern Ethiopia. Among 187 participants tested using the direct agglutination test, 18 were positive, giving a seroprevalence of 9.63%. Multivariable analysis associated VL positivity with age, damp floors, outdoor sleeping, and sleeping outdoors near animal shelters.

Of the participants, 53.48% had heard of VL, 42% identified sand fly bites as the mode of transmission, and 89% knew at least one symptom. Although 78% described VL as treatable, only 36% considered it preventable and 44% believed untreated VL could be fatal. Preventive practices included bed-net use, insecticide spraying, smoking plant materials, and environmental cleaning.

Entomological sampling in four kebeles collected 823 sand flies representing 12 species. Sergentomyia species comprised most specimens, with S. clydie accounting for 50.18% of the total. Among Phlebotomus species, P. orientalis was most abundant and occurred mainly in termite mounds and forests; none were captured indoors. The study identified limited knowledge and unfavorable attitudes toward VL and recommended increased community awareness and further epidemiological and entomological research, particularly on P. orientalis.

The study examines whether transformers can learn transitive reasoning, formulated as connectivity prediction in directed graphs, from individual training examples rather than graph information supplied in prompts. It compares low-dimensional grid graphs, where connectivity can be inferred from node embeddings, with disconnected chain graphs, which lack similarly simple embeddings.

Transformers achieved near-perfect generalization on grid graphs but often struggled on disconnected chains. Increasing model size improved performance on grid graphs but did not provide comparable gains for disconnected chains. Increasing graph size maintained strong grid-graph performance and improved results on disconnected chains by providing more connected-node examples. Lower-dimensional grids were easier than higher-dimensional grids, while disconnected graphs with fewer chains were easier than those with many chains. For higher-dimensional grids and graphs containing many disconnected chains, increasing graph size was more beneficial than increasing model size.

Experiments used synthetic directed graphs, node-pair inputs labeled according to path existence, varying embedding dimensions, graph sizes, grid dimensions, and numbers of chains. The findings support the hypothesis that transformers learn connectivity more readily when graph structure permits a low-dimensional node-embedding heuristic. Future work could test whether similar capabilities arise for real-world knowledge and causal graphs.

Cincinnati beat No. 14 Iowa State, handing the Cyclones their first loss. The Bearcats built a 31-7 first-half lead and recovered a late onside kick after Iowa State pulled within eight. Cincinnati improved to 4-1 overall and 2-0 in the Big 12, while Iowa State fell to 5-1 and 2-1. The injury-depleted Cyclones were missing 16 players and their top two kickers.

Roy Allen Whisnant, charged with assaulting his brother-in-law with a deadly weapon and intent to kill, was appointed counsel after being found indigent. He initially pleaded guilty to misdemeanor assault with a deadly weapon but withdrew the plea after being told it waived his right to challenge his alleged unlawful arrest. The court denied requests to postpone trial so he could seek out-of-state witnesses and allow counsel more preparation time. Tried the next day, he was convicted of misdemeanor assault and sentenced to two years’ imprisonment. The court held that the prior guilty plea may have prejudiced jurors and that appointed counsel was entitled to reasonable time to investigate and prepare a defense. A new trial was ordered.

Jerome “Jay” Powell succeeds Janet Yellen as Federal Reserve chair amid strong US and global growth, low unemployment, rising wages, fiscal stimulus and inflation below the Fed’s two percent target. Yellen leaves after gradually raising rates five times and beginning to reduce the Fed’s bond holdings without disrupting markets. Powell’s central challenge will be deciding how quickly to raise rates as tax cuts and limited labor availability could increase wage and price inflation. Three rate hikes were projected for 2018, beginning as early as March, but stronger inflation could prompt four. More rapid increases risk unsettling markets and raising concerns about inflation or the recovery’s durability.

The Second Circuit affirmed summary judgment for Reisdorf Brothers on Patrick and Linda George’s federal environmental claims. The plaintiffs failed to present evidence of continuous or intermittent pollutant discharges required under the Clean Water Act; evidence concerning a 2009 chemical spill, fertilizers, pesticides, and molasses was either limited to past incidents or too speculative. Their newly raised storm-water claim was not properly pleaded. The Resource Conservation and Recovery Act claim also failed because plaintiffs neither alleged nor established violations of applicable federal open-dumping regulations. The district court acted within its discretion by declining supplemental jurisdiction over the distinct state adverse-possession claim and dismissing it without prejudice. It also properly denied Reisdorf attorney’s fees because the plaintiffs’ unsuccessful claims were not wholly baseless, frivolous, unreasonable, or pursued in bad faith.

The Supreme Court will consider whether 18 U.S.C. §§ 924(c) and 924(j) permit separate convictions and sentences for the same conduct. Barrett was convicted for participating in armed robberies culminating in a fatal shooting by a coconspirator.

Section 924(c) criminalizes using, carrying, or possessing a firearm to advance certain federal crimes, while Section 924(j) applies when such conduct causes death. Under established double jeopardy principles, separate punishments are generally presumed improper when one offense contains only a subset of another’s elements, unless Congress clearly indicates otherwise.

Barrett and the government agree that separate sentences are not permitted because neither provision clearly authorizes cumulative punishment. An appointed amicus defending the lower court’s contrary ruling argues that Section 924(c)’s requirement that its sentence run consecutively to “any other term of imprisonment” demonstrates congressional intent to allow separate punishment. The case follows an earlier Supreme Court decision holding that Section 924(c)’s mandatory minimums and consecutive-sentence requirement do not govern a Section 924(j) charge brought alone, while leaving the double jeopardy issue unresolved.

Phil Kessel scored twice with an assist, and Evgeni Malkin had two goals and two assists as the Pittsburgh Penguins defeated the Washington Capitals 7-4. Pittsburgh won its fourth straight game and seventh consecutive home game, moving within four points of division-leading Washington. Sidney Crosby extended his scoring streak to 11 games, while Matt Murray made 29 saves. Alex Ovechkin scored twice for Washington, raising his NHL-leading total to 32. The Penguins broke a 4-4 tie with three third-period goals and went 3-for-4 on the power play.

Vocational education and training (VET) assessment must address theoretical knowledge, technical skills, and workplace competence. Formative assessment uses immediate feedback, self- and peer assessment, multiple attempts, and teacher judgment to identify learning gaps and guide improvement. Although it can deepen learning and increase motivation, it requires time, spontaneous teaching, student participation, and additional teacher workload.

Academic assessment methods such as written tests may not adequately measure vocational learning. Competence-based education instead connects classroom theory with industry-standard workplace performance. It requires clearly defined tasks, standards, observable behaviours, and authentic evaluations, including assessments by workplace supervisors. This approach can improve student motivation and engagement.

Authentic assessment reflects workplace contexts and develops practical understanding rather than rote knowledge or isolated skills. However, contextualized assessment can reduce reliability and increase subjectivity. Clear procedures, workplace-linked tasks, rubrics, professional development, and calibration among teachers and industry experts can improve consistency. Workplace feedback also supports authenticity and industry relationships.

A comprehensive VET assessment program should combine written tests, technical skills assessments, workplace evaluations, process and product evaluation, and formative and summative methods. Assessment should occur before, during, and after learning and cover increasing levels of competence: knowing, knowing how, showing how, and performing authentic workplace tasks. Clearly communicated outcomes, vocational competencies, performance portfolios, and workplace evaluations can support deeper learning and student engagement.

The study developed a scale measuring prospective teachers’ attitudes toward values education through distance education. Following literature review, student compositions, expert review, and pilot testing, the scale was administered to 341 prospective teachers at Gazi University. Exploratory factor analysis produced a 36-item, two-factor structure: “Necessity and Usefulness” and “Feasibility,” explaining 63.286% of total variance. Reliability was high for both factors, with Cronbach’s alpha coefficients of .969 and .961. Because the scale lacked additivity, each factor should be evaluated separately rather than through a total score. Item analyses indicated adequate distinctiveness and internal consistency. The authors concluded that the scale provides valid and reliable measurements. Limitations included the predominantly female, single-university sample and the absence of a comparable external scale. Further confirmatory factor analysis, validity studies, and test-retest reliability assessments were recommended.

This PREVEND cohort study examined age- and sex-specific transitions between KDIGO kidney-risk stages and their association with new-onset heart failure. A multi-state model incorporated repeated eGFR and urinary albumin measurements, stage misclassification, heart failure, and death. Among 8,569 participants followed for a median of 12.6 years, 373 developed heart failure and 710 died beforehand.

Progression to higher KDIGO risk stages accelerated with age, particularly after age 50, and was generally faster in men. Younger participants and women were more likely to return from intermediate to low risk. Progression to intermediate risk occurred mainly between ages 60 and 70, while progression to high or very high risk increased mostly after age 70. Heart-failure rates rose exponentially with age and were lower in women.

Compared with low-risk participants, those at intermediate or high/very high risk had greater heart-failure risk. Relative risks declined with age, whereas absolute risk differences increased. Results remained similar after adjustment for smoking, hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, and diabetes. Misclassification was notable, particularly between intermediate and adjacent stages, but was lower when cystatin C-based rather than creatinine-based eGFR was used. Model calibration was excellent.

Strengths included repeated kidney measurements, accounting for misclassification and interval-censored transitions, and validated heart-failure outcomes. Limitations included enrichment for elevated urinary albumin, a predominantly Caucasian population, and reliance on the Markov assumption. The findings suggest that slowing kidney-risk progression in middle age may reduce new-onset heart failure.

Australian financial markets offer portfolio diversification and significant exposure to mining, energy, and commodity cycles. Investors can access them through US-listed ETFs, ADRs, international brokers such as Interactive Brokers, or stock CFDs. The iShares MSCI-Australia ETF (EWA) can serve as a proxy for Australian equities, while the Invesco CurrencyShares Australian Dollar Trust (FXA) provides AUD/USD exposure.

Backtests indicate that conventional mean-reversion, 200-day moving-average, and Golden Cross strategies have performed less effectively in Australia than in the US, possibly reflecting Australia’s commodity exposure. A tested Santa Claus seasonal strategy produced a 92% win rate since 1996, averaging 2.4% per trade, but traded only annually and returned 1.87% per year versus 7.34% for buy-and-hold.

Australia has more than 2,000 ASX-listed companies, plus ETFs, bonds, futures, and other securities. Its main exchange is the Australian Securities Exchange; the Sydney Stock Exchange also operates. Australian markets trade weekdays from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Australian Eastern Daylight Time, equivalent to 11:00 p.m.–5:00 a.m. GMT. Major Australian-dollar currency pairs are also tradable.

Defending a strong post player requires coordinated pressure, help defense, traps, and positioning before the catch. Defenders should force the player away from preferred areas and toward their weaker side. Full-court presses, adjusted 2-3 zones, and Diamond-and-One defenses can disrupt post play and create double or triple teams.

Indian press reports said Dabhol Power Company’s board authorized management to issue a preliminary notice terminating its power purchase agreement with Maharashtra State Electricity Board. The resolution passed six votes to one, with IDBI opposed and MSEB representatives barred from voting as interested parties. Authorization did not mean immediate termination; lender consent and a six-month consultation process could apply.

Maharashtra and the Centre sought an amicable settlement and tariff renegotiation, warning termination would impose substantial financial liabilities.

MSEB paid Rs 134 crore toward its March bill under protest while disputing Rs 12.64 crore. Maharashtra planned a committee to renegotiate the agreement under recommendations from the Godbole Committee.

Las Vegas gunman Stephen Paddock bought 1,000 tracer rounds, though investigators do not know whether he used them in the attack that killed 58 and injured nearly 500. He stockpiled 23 guns, modified 12 for continuous fire, requested a high-floor room and installed surveillance cameras. Authorities are investigating whether he considered other attacks, including a car bombing. Ammunition and explosive materials were found in his car. Justice Babatunde Quadri admitted EFCC evidence against Chinese national Li Ya Ping, accused of concealing $300,000 while attempting to fly from Abuja to Dubai without declaring it. EFCC detective Hassan Misau testified that customs intercepted Ping and transferred him, the money, passport, boarding passes and phone to the commission.

No. 22 Aledo leads Ryan 2-0 in Denton, Texas, after Ryan committed intentional grounding in its own end zone, resulting in a safety. Aledo is also No. 16 in the Massey Ratings, while Ryan remains outside the Top 25.

Ozzie made key saves despite the opponent creating more scoring chances than its low shot total suggested. Parental obesity can increase children’s obesity risk through biological changes in eggs and sperm, not just inherited DNA. Maternal BMI at conception and paternal BMI are associated with childhood weight, while having two obese parents further increases risk. Obesity alters sperm non-coding RNAs and egg metabolism and mitochondria, potentially affecting embryonic development and lifelong susceptibility to obesity and diabetes.

Research in mice suggests these effects may be reversible: exercise, healthier diets and some treatments improve egg or sperm quality and can prevent obesity transmission. Limited human evidence shows children conceived after maternal gastric banding were less obese than siblings conceived beforehand. Researchers therefore support healthier lifestyles and targeted interventions for both mothers and fathers before conception, alongside broader obesity prevention among adolescents and young adults.

Key sources for documenting U.S. policy toward the Soviet Union from January 1983 to March 1985 include Reagan Library White House and National Security Council files, Department of State Executive Secretariat and policy files, Moscow-Washington cable traffic, declassified National Security Decision Directives, and online materials maintained by the Office of the Historian.

To meet statutory requirements concerning major covert actions and intelligence activities, the volume explains how such operations were planned and approved. During the Truman administration, concern over Soviet “psychological warfare” led NSC 4–A in December 1947 to authorize peacetime covert operations under the Director of Central Intelligence. The CIA was selected partly because its unvouchered funds reduced exposure risks. Dissatisfaction at the Departments of State and Defense prompted NSC 10/2 in June 1948, which expanded the CIA’s responsibility from psychological to broader covert operations designed to conceal U.S. involvement and permit plausible denial.

Novo Nordisk plans to acquire Akero Therapeutics, developer of a MASH liver disease drug, for up to $5.2 billion. Other biotech news covers U.K. drug spending, drug pricing, research shifts, CRISPR, cannabis-related psychosis concerns, venture capital, and regulatory developments.

Amazon’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2017 reported Q2 net sales of $38.0 billion, up 25% year over year, while operating income fell from $1.3 billion to $628 million and net income declined from $857 million to $197 million. Operating cash flow for the trailing 12 months reached $17.9 billion. At June 30, Amazon held $13.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $8.2 billion in marketable securities. The passage provides troubleshooting, support, warranty, licensing, and disposal information for a SanDisk music player. Playback failures may result from missing device rights.
