Cornerbacks are defensive backs whose primary responsibility is covering opposing wide receivers in man or zone coverage. In man coverage, they must mirror receivers despite not knowing their planned routes, making the position difficult and vulnerable to costly mistakes. The name reflects their role protecting the outside portions, or “corners,” of the field. Teams usually deploy two cornerbacks, adding a third in nickel packages to cover slot receivers.

Successful cornerbacks require speed, agility, effective backpedaling, sharp changes of direction, and the ability to transition into a sprint. They also defend outside running plays by tackling runners or forcing them toward other defenders. Elite “lockdown corners” can neutralize top receivers without safety assistance, allowing defenses to pressure quarterbacks and build schemes around their coverage.

Notable cornerbacks include Deion Sanders, Charles Woodson, Mel Blount, Champ Bailey, Ty Law, and Darrell Revis. Sanders was a two-time Super Bowl champion, eight-time Pro Bowler, and 1994 Defensive Player of the Year. Woodson is the only defensive player to win the Heisman Trophy. Revis earned the nickname “Revis Island” for covering receivers independently. The passage states that 18 cornerbacks are in the Hall of Fame.

Nippon Express said an employee falsified inspection stamps on government-stockpiled rice repackaged after bags became wet or torn, affecting 266 bags. Fifteen 30-kilogram bags were shipped for livestock feed, with no reported health damage; remaining affected rice will be incinerated, and none entered human consumption. Mitsubishi, which subcontracted storage to Nippon Express, received a farm ministry improvement order and reported preventive measures.

Defending soccer goal kicks aims to win possession immediately in a dangerous area or prevent easy buildup and successful long kicks. Under Law 16, a goal kick is taken from within the goal area after an attacker last touches the ball before it crosses the defending team’s goal line. The stationary ball is in play once kicked and visibly moving. Opponents generally must leave the penalty area, though the kick may be taken before they do; interference before the ball is in play causes a retake.

Defenders should combine man-marking and zonal coverage, move aggressively to the ball, and transition quickly after gaining possession. Strikers restrict short options, midfielders challenge lofted balls, and backs support wider areas. If possession is not won, the team should press collectively in the opponent’s half while guarding against flick headers and fast breaks.

For players aged 10 and under, build-out lines often require opponents to retreat, allowing teams to develop play from the back. Recommended routines use a designated kicker, nearby dribbler, wide targets, and secondary receivers, emphasizing movement upfield along the sidelines and avoiding passes across one’s own goal. Players must be positioned and attentive before the kick.

For older youth, goal-kick patterns expand to multiple targets selected according to defensive coverage. Kicks may be played short of marked targets to create space, while midfield options require caution near the center. Coaches should practice from both sides, add defenders progressively, and teach receivers to attack the ball.

Adults may use short buildup, predetermined or deep targets, and directed lofted kicks; goalkeepers usually take the kick. Coaches should account for wind and field conditions, study opposing kickers’ range and tendencies, maintain sight of the ball, position midfielders effectively, and drill against all available goal-kick options.

NewMarket derives most of its revenue, profit, and cash flow from Afton Chemical, which produces fuel and lubricant additives. It has strong EBITDA margins, cash flow, returns on capital, and shareholder distributions, but limited analyst coverage and trading liquidity.

Industry 4.0, digitalization, and COVID-19 have increased demand for Education 4.0, which emphasizes personalized, blended, practical, interdisciplinary, and lifelong learning alongside digital, technical, and soft skills. Universities must adapt curricula and teaching methods to develop problem-solving, analytical thinking, communication, teamwork, self-management, and technology-related competencies.

The study surveyed 147 second-year engineering and technical management students at a Hungarian university in 2019 and 2021. It examined which skills students considered important for employability, international study, and higher education. Quantitative analysis included descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and decision-tree segmentation.

Overall, students prioritized problem-solving, specialization-related knowledge, and communication. Engineering students placed greater emphasis on specialized, technical, mathematical, and IT knowledge, while technical management students favored decision-making and analytical skills. Thus, the hypothesis that the groups had different skill priorities was supported. Both groups viewed individual abilities, professional commitment, and networks as major influences on career success, with no significant faculty difference; the second hypothesis was therefore rejected.

Students regarded improved foreign-language ability, networking, cultural adaptation, and exposure to foreign cultures as key benefits of international study. Engineering students valued new approaches to structuring and interpreting learning materials more strongly, while technical management students emphasized networking and adaptation.

Students generally identified job-related knowledge, digital literacy, and understanding others as important contributions of higher education. Faculty differences appeared in views on professional knowledge, quantitative analysis, teamwork, and self-understanding, so the third hypothesis was partly supported.

The study concludes that universities should integrate technical and soft-skill development, problem-based learning, international experience, and multidisciplinary collaboration into curricula. Its limitations include non-probability sampling, a relatively small sample, and participation from only two faculties at one university.

A cross-sectional study assessed lung function among adults with heroin use disorder receiving methadone at Muhimbili National Hospital’s medication-assisted therapy clinic in Dar-es-Salaam, Tanzania. Of 310 enrolled participants, 302 completed spirometry; their mean age was 42.8 years, 95.7% were male, 83.8% currently smoked cigarettes, 20.9% were underweight, 9.6% had HIV, and 32.8% reported previous pulmonary tuberculosis.

Lung function decline, defined as FEV1 below 70%, occurred in 28.5% of participants, at a mean onset age of 44 years. Possible restrictive disease affected 13.2%, obstructive disease 11%, and mixed abnormalities 4.3%. Underweight participants had higher odds of lung function decline than those of normal weight (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 4.73). HIV infection (aOR 2.61) and previous pulmonary tuberculosis (aOR 2.48) were also independently associated with decline. Cigarette, heroin, cannabis, and cocaine use measures and methadone dose were not significantly associated.

The study recommends routine lung-function screening in medication-assisted therapy clinics. Its main limitation was the absence of bronchodilator reversibility testing to distinguish asthma from COPD.

The Pennsylvania Superior Court affirmed Clay Williams’s sentence of life imprisonment without parole for first-degree murder, with concurrent sentences for robbery and carrying a firearm without a license. Evidence showed Williams attempted to rob Mizael Velez of a cell phone in a Philadelphia store, then shot and killed him with a shotgun. The passage introduces BALLAST, a Bayesian active learning method for sequential placement of free-floating ocean drifters. Unlike space-filling, expert-designed, or hand-crafted placement strategies, BALLAST accounts for Lagrangian observations by simulating hypothetical trajectories through time-dependent vector fields. It uses a spatio-temporal, vector-output Gaussian process with a temporal Helmholtz kernel and an information-theoretic utility function. An SPDE-based posterior sampling method is developed to improve computational efficiency, particularly for non-gridded observations.

The active learning framework selects drifter placement locations at predetermined times to maximize expected information gain about the full ocean-current vector field. The field is modeled over a finite time interval and rectangular spatial domain, with noisy velocity observations informing the Gaussian process posterior. The temporal kernel is Matérn 3/2, while the spatial Helmholtz kernel combines potential and stream-function kernels. Numerical results on synthetic and high-fidelity ocean-current models indicate that BALLAST improves sequential observer deployment.

Password protection stores non-volatile credentials and optionally a Force Erase Password for COP. Locked cards permit basic management commands but block data access and automatically relock after power-on. Lock/unlock uses a selected card in transfer state via single-block write.

The Fifth Circuit affirmed Joe Ezeokeke’s 138-month sentence for possession of cocaine with intent to distribute. His testimony, if believed, would have negated essential elements of the offense. The appellate court also held that his within-guidelines sentence was substantively reasonable because the district court considered his arguments for a lower sentence, and he failed to identify distinguishing mitigating factors or rebut the presumption of reasonableness. The unpublished opinion generally lacks precedential effect.

The passage examines slavery as an undertheorized foundation of pedagogy and uses Foucault’s panopticism to connect education, surveillance, extraction, and power. Foucault presents surveillance as inherent to teaching, particularly through examinations, records, and inscriptions that transform human experience into texts for classification, normalization, and control. Although his work largely neglects race-based slavery, its concepts can illuminate racial surveillance and educational inequality.

Historically, pedagogues in Ancient Greece were often enslaved people responsible for supervising and educating children. This relationship complicates modern definitions of pedagogy as merely the art or science of teaching. In the United States, racial chattel slavery restricted Black literacy while using surveillance, violence, recordkeeping, and productivity measurements to control enslaved people. At the same time, enslaved and formerly enslaved people pursued education through what Givens calls “fugitive pedagogy,” encompassing subversive practices developed against the criminalization and suppression of Black learning. Slavery also influenced American educational institutions, labor management, carceral schooling, and the school-to-prison pipeline.

The author introduces “surveillance textualization” to describe how surveillance inscribes experiences and actions into texts, and “surveillance pedagogy” to describe the monitoring and management of teaching and learning for academic, political, social, or economic purposes. Digitalization intensifies these processes by allowing learning-management systems and internet platforms to extract, store, analyze, and monetize personal data. Data-driven pedagogy can influence teacher and student behavior through opaque algorithms with limited oversight.

These developments reflect scientific management and support what Zuboff calls surveillance capitalism, in which personal experience becomes proprietary data used to predict and condition behavior for profit. Platforms such as Google collect educational data through cloud-based systems, blurring boundaries between education and commercialization. Artificial intelligence and language models further unite educational assessment with corporate data extraction.

The passage argues that contemporary digital surveillance rearticulates, without completely reproducing, historical practices associated with slavery. Surveillance pedagogy offers a framework for studying how texts, technology, teaching, capitalism, and unequal power intersect, while exposing continuities among master/slave, teacher/student, and capital/labor relations.

Northmont High School Student Assistance Counselor Sheree Coffman told the Northmont Rotary how the school identifies and supports students facing mental illness, substance abuse, family crises, relationship issues, and other challenges. Northmont emphasizes early intervention through universal, targeted, and individual programs, including U.N.I.T.Y. Day, Reality Club, Peer Facilitation, SADD, support groups, and an Alternative to Expulsion Program. U.N.I.T.Y. Day promotes understanding, acceptance, and belonging and has involved more than 400 students annually for the past three years.

This non-peer-reviewed study examined long-term visit-to-visit blood pressure variability and cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) among 1,284 Kailuan cohort participants. Blood pressure data collected from 2006–2022 were compared with MRI-detected white matter hyperintensities, lacunae, cerebral microbleeds, and perivascular spaces. cSVD was present in 69.3% of participants. Higher systolic blood pressure variability was associated with moderate cSVD burden and perivascular spaces, while higher pulse pressure variability was associated with moderate or severe burden, lacunae, and perivascular spaces. Associations differed by age and were more evident among participants with hypertension. In adults under 60, high pulse pressure variability was associated with severe cSVD, lacunae, and perivascular spaces. Results remained broadly consistent in sensitivity analyses. Limitations included one-time MRI assessment, possible reverse causation, and selection bias. The authors conclude that long-term blood pressure variability, particularly pulse pressure variability in younger adults and variability among people with hypertension, is a potential cSVD risk factor.

Bollinger Bands consist of a simple moving average and upper and lower bands based on price standard deviations, incorporating changing volatility. The article asks ChatGPT to create Bollinger Bands strategies and backtests its less commonly discussed squeeze strategy using Python. The strategy defines a squeeze when Bollinger Bands fall inside Keltner Channels, whose bands use twice the stock’s average true range. It buys and holds while the lower Bollinger Band is above the lower Keltner band and the upper Bollinger Band is below the upper Keltner band, selling when either condition fails. A backtest on unadjusted SPY data since 1993 produced low, erratic compounded returns and excessive drawdown. Adjusting for time in the market improved results and reduced drawdown only modestly. The strategy was considered unsuitable for live trading, although ChatGPT successfully performed the backtest.

Texas Instruments warns that improper ESD handling can degrade or destroy these precision integrated circuits. The April 2025 revision updates device features, variants, peripheral counts, operating modes, electrical and thermal specifications, memory endurance, timing, security, DMA, ADC, temperature sensor, UART, SPI, LFSS, and timer documentation. It adds preview package variants and notes targeted PSA-L1 certification. Mechanical and ordering information is subject to change; specified packages require appropriate thermal-pad soldering and board design. Preproduction parts may be incomplete, change, or be discontinued and are sold without warranties. Automotive-qualified MSPM0G3518-Q1 and MSPM0G3519-Q1 versions are available. TI provides resources “as is”; developers remain responsible for product selection, application design, validation, testing, and compliance.

Ocwen Financial settled with Connecticut, resolving 28 of 31 state regulatory actions over alleged servicing issues. The agreement restricts new servicing-rights acquisitions until April 30, 2018, requires migration from REALServicing to Black Knight’s platform, and adds Connecticut borrower communications, reviews and reporting. Noncompliance could trigger a $500,000 fine. Ocwen continues seeking resolutions with remaining regulators and attorneys general.

Hubble images show NGC 4536, 50 million light-years away in Virgo, rapidly forming stars from concentrated gas, possibly acquired through a galactic collision. Young stars emit ultraviolet light that illuminates nearby gas clouds.

Business Insider ranks Taylor Swift’s 20 best breakup songs, highlighting her portrayals of anger, regret, yearning, despair, confusion, catharsis, and recovery. The list spans her career, from early tracks like “Picture to Burn” and “Should’ve Said No” to three songs from “The Tortured Poets Department.” “Dear John” places near the top, while “All Too Well (10 Minute Version)” ranks first for its detailed depiction of heartbreak and enduring emotional impact.

Geologists from Queensland’s Department of Natural Resources and Mines and the University of Queensland found evidence of platinum, gold and rare earth elements in large geological pipes in western Queensland. The proposed Diamantina Minerals Province extends from central New South Wales to the Northern Territory. The pipes may contain minerals used in fuel cells, mobile phones, magnets and hybrid vehicle batteries, as well as diamonds. Officials said the under-explored area could create major economic and commercial opportunities amid predicted shortages of several rare earth elements.

At NATO’s spring session in Tbilisi, President Paolo Alli reaffirmed support for territorial integrity, praised Georgia’s military reforms and Euro-Atlantic integration, urged increased NATO spending and international unity, and addressed security challenges. The session planned a declaration supporting Georgia’s integration.

Gary Gensler marks Bitcoin’s 10th anniversary by reviewing its growth, mining activity, energy use, adoption, and associated ICO market while noting uncertainty about its future price, monetary policy, and volatility.

The lecture examines payment-system pain points, including numerous intermediaries and ledgers, high costs, delayed settlement, limited financial inclusion, cross-border friction, chargebacks, fraud, privacy concerns, cyberattacks, and identity theft. Blockchain could reduce verification and networking costs and support programmable payments, but faces challenges involving scalability, transaction costs, speed, interoperability, governance, regulation, liquidity, error resolution, and irreversible transactions.

Students debate whether immediate settlement is preferable to delayed settlement, which can protect consumers, correct errors, and support existing market practices. Blockchain may enable finality where desired, but legacy systems can also adopt faster settlement. Smart contracts offer conditional and automated payments, although similar functions may be possible without blockchain. Blockchain could therefore become either a payment infrastructure or merely a catalyst for incumbent systems to innovate.

A MasterCard employee argues that existing payment systems can provide blockchain’s proposed benefits and already possess critical acceptance and scale. Others note that blockchain may offer greater value in countries lacking reliable financial and legal infrastructure. India’s low-cost, real-time United Payment Interface illustrates that financial inclusion can also advance without blockchain. Adoption, local liquidity, and practical usability remain significant barriers, while censorship resistance can have both socially beneficial and harmful applications.

Payment-related blockchain businesses include BitPay, which converts cryptocurrency payments into fiat for merchants for a 1% fee, along with institutional services such as Ripple, R3, and Quorum. Incumbents are filing blockchain patents, possibly to pursue opportunities or create barriers to entry. Adoption remains limited, particularly in retail payments.

For cross-border transfers, cryptocurrency could serve as a bridge between two fiat currencies, potentially reducing intermediaries and settlement times. However, this requires two exchanges, sufficient liquidity, market makers, and management of volatility and transaction costs. It may offer more value for smaller remittances, less-liquid currency pairs, or weekend transactions than for major corporate currency transfers. The lecture concludes that each use case must be assessed to determine whether a consensus-based, append-only ledger and native token provide enough value to justify their risks and costs.

Kent McFarland of the Vermont Center for Ecostudies will discuss mercury along elevational gradients at Lyndon State College on February 15 at 4 p.m. The free weekly Natural Science seminars continue through May 3, covering environmental science, history, wildlife, archaeology, filmmaking, and botany.

Newlywed Sarah Illig was bitten on the arm by a nurse shark while swimming during a Caribbean resort attraction. Her husband, Evan Carroll, filmed her pulling away and escaping. Illig suffered flesh wounds but did not receive stitches and said the injury was healing without infection. She shared the footage and photos online. Such bites are considered extremely rare unless the sharks are provoked, and nurse sharks are not known to prey on humans.

Jonathan Quick said the team is focused on winning the next game despite the loss. He called the overtime stanchion bounce a tough break and noted that traffic, contact, missed calls, and offsides are part of hockey.

Tesla will file a proxy statement for a special stockholder meeting. The passage certifies official copies of records concerning the bark Cape Horn Pigeon, including an 1891 crew list and shipping papers authenticated by Secretary of State John Hay in 1900. The vessel was contracted for a whaling, walrusing, and trading voyage from San Francisco to the North Pacific, Arctic, or elsewhere, lasting no more than twelve months. Crew compensation was based on assigned shares, with obligations concerning freight, post-arrival service, advances, and trading. Seamen agreed to obey lawful commands, perform their duties, help secure and preserve cargo, and remain aboard unless granted leave. Shipboard regulations required daily log entries documenting misconduct, absences, drunkenness, unauthorized women aboard, and duty-related disabilities. Officers were responsible for enforcing these rules. Violations could result in forfeiture of pay, including twenty days for officers failing to remove unauthorized women, five days for participation or refusal to assist, and two days for drunkenness or each day of disability caused by intemperance or licentiousness.

Mr. Grew urged nations to support and allow the proposed World Organization to develop despite its imperfections, warning that another war could destroy peoples and civilizations. He also advocated strengthening the inter-American system before asking Mr. Rockefeller to preside.

Discussion then focused on Chile’s proposal that states should not be required to join military operations concerning remote regional disputes that did not threaten world peace. Ambassador Mora argued that populations would resist sending troops to distant conflicts, especially without participating in the decision. Dr. Pasvolsky replied that armed-force commitments would depend on later agreements and that the Security Council must determine whether disputes were local or global and which nations should assist. Mexico’s ambassador opposed regional determination of threats and favored Security Council selection of forces, preferably from uninvolved countries, citing the Saar plebiscite. He also questioned the political usefulness of continental divisions. Honduras supported extending inter-American solidarity worldwide. Mora left the issue open for later consideration, while Pasvolsky recommended further study of difficult new questions. The meeting then reviewed the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals and suggested amendments.

Novak Djokovic defeated Spanish qualifier Jaume Munar 7-6(1), 6-4, 6-4 in the French Open second round despite inconsistent serving and numerous errors. The 20th seed said he was dissatisfied with his performance but played well enough at key moments. Still adjusting after elbow surgery, a racket change and three service-motion changes this year, Djokovic acknowledged he remains below the level that brought him 12 Grand Slam titles. After several early tournament exits in 2018, he said he was determined not to give up. He next faces 13th-seeded Roberto Bautista Agut for a place in the last 16.

NVIDIA’s fiscal 2020 Form 10-K describes its GPU-based accelerated computing platforms serving Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive markets through GPU and Tegra Processor segments. The Czech crown rebounded from an 18-month low against the euro as the central bank’s commitment to cap it below 27 per euro expired. The bank could end its 3½-year weak-crown policy at any time, raising expectations of volatility after heavy intervention and extensive speculative crown positions. Forward rates also recovered. Czech bonds were mixed, while other Central European bond markets strengthened. The Hungarian forint firmed, the Polish zloty eased but remained near 17-month highs, and traders suggested funds withdrawn from crown positions could be reinvested elsewhere in Central Europe.

The New Jersey Superior Court considered whether sick pay and wages received for personal and family illness days must offset a plaintiff’s lost-wage recovery under N.J.S.A. 2A:15-97. The court held they are not collateral-source benefits because the employee earned them as compensation and exhausted benefits otherwise available for future use or retirement cash-out. Accordingly, recovering lost wages would not constitute duplicate recovery, and these payments cannot be deducted from any lost-wage award.

Nashville hosts a Stanley Cup Final game against Pittsburgh amid CMA Fest and widespread enthusiasm from the country music community. The NHL’s worldwide telecast will open with country star Luke Bryan performing from the rooftop of Tootsie’s Orchid Lounge.

The first speaker pledges to enforce the Taiwan Relations Act, treat Taiwanese officials with dignity, remove Carter administration restrictions not required by law, reject foreign interference in implementing U.S. laws, and consider the views of both China and Taiwan while prioritizing American interests. Bush rejects efforts to portray Ronald Reagan as likely to lead the country into war, calling that characterization a false and irresponsible distortion of Reagan’s views and record.

Large language models remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks that conceal malicious intent and bypass safety mechanisms. Existing input-only defenses often perform poorly against sophisticated attacks, while direct output inspection increases latency.

The proposed SafeBehavior framework applies hierarchical, human-inspired reasoning during inference. It has three stages: intention inference summarizes and screens a query for obvious risks; self-introspection evaluates the generated response and assigns confidence to guide acceptance, refusal, or revision; and self-revision rewrites uncertain responses to preserve user intent while meeting safety policies. The framework can terminate generation early when harmful intent is detected, reducing unnecessary computation.

SafeBehavior is evaluated against five optimization-based, contextual manipulation, and prompt-based attacks, including GCG, DeepInception, Papillon, PPPI, and IFSJ, and compared with seven defense baselines. The study reports strong robustness and adaptability across diverse threats.

Jailbreak attacks are categorized as white-box methods using gradients, logits, or fine-tuning, and black-box methods using templates, prompt rewriting, or LLM-generated attacks. Defenses are categorized as prompt-level techniques that detect or transform inputs and model-level techniques involving safety training, inference control, refinement, or proxy models. The defense objective is to preserve normal output quality, mitigate varied attacks without prior attacker knowledge, and maintain inference efficiency.

TI’s MSPM0C1105/MSPM0C1106 documentation states that prototype “X” devices are for internal evaluation only, may have higher or undefined failure rates, and should not be used in production; only qualified production devices are recommended. Device suffixes identify temperature range, package type, and distribution format.

TI provides LaunchPad development hardware, BoosterPack modules, software drivers, libraries, examples, cloud and offline tools, Resource Explorer, SysConfig, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, and an Arm-Clang compiler. Device-specific data sheets define pin functions, connections, and operating parameters. Support is available through TI E2E forums.

The September 2025 revision removed the DGS32 package, revised power modes, specifications, CPU and ADC information, added a DEGUGSS section, and updated identification tables. Packaging information includes thermal-pad soldering, optional vias, stencil guidance, and solder-coverage recommendations. Devices require ESD precautions.

Preproduction parts may lack completed qualification and can change or be discontinued. TI provides resources “as is,” limits warranties and liability, and assigns developers responsibility for product selection, design validation, testing, and regulatory compliance.

The passage argues that Ontario’s K–12 education system excludes disabled, racialized, and other marginalized students despite describing special education as inclusive. Historically, disabled students were institutionalized, segregated, or denied education; integration gained momentum during the 1960s through advocacy and legislation. Racialized students have also faced persistent discrimination and are overrepresented in certain special education categories, while multicultural and anti-racist policies have lacked consistent implementation.

Ontario uses Individual Education Plans, disability identification, multidisciplinary assessments, and placements ranging from regular classrooms with support to full-time special education classes. The passage contends that these processes rely partly on deficit-based understandings of disability and often exclude students from decisions about their education. It also rejects the view of students as “empty vessels,” emphasizing that knowledge develops through interaction and must account for students’ goals and circumstances.

Although Ontario’s Policy on Accessible Education for Students with Disabilities guarantees equal treatment and requires accommodation unless it causes undue hardship based on cost, funding, health, or safety, the passage argues that policy commitments are not consistently reflected in practice. Barriers include inadequate funding, inaccessible environments, lengthy accommodation procedures, stereotypes, large classes, limited resources, and insufficient teacher preparation concerning disability and inclusive education.

The passage recommends stronger and more accountable policies, increased funding, disability and intersectionality education for teachers, universal design for learning, and meaningful participation by disabled students and educators in policymaking. It also calls for accessibility policies supporting teachers with disabilities, whose experiences may positively influence disabled students. Genuine inclusion requires planning for diverse learners, valuing disabled students as capable participants, and translating written policy into classroom practice.

This qualitative study developed and validated a two-week, six-hour Critical Multicultural Education (CME) module for pre-service English teachers in Türkiye. Based on CME and critical language teaching, the module was created through brainstorming, expert and critical-friend feedback, and two implementation phases. It combined asynchronous preparation and reflection with synchronous instruction, discussions, multimedia materials, and critical lesson planning.

The initial version was tested online with 15 students from four universities and revised to improve sequencing, visual presentation, guidance, and task organization. The revised module was then delivered to 86 students at Çanakkale Onsekiz Mart University; ten participated in interviews analyzed through content analysis.

Participants reported more positive attitudes toward diversity, broader perspectives on social issues, and greater awareness of educational inequalities, ideologies, teaching’s political role, and critical material development. They also gained pedagogical resources, lesson-planning experience, and guidance for applying CME in English teaching. Challenges included limited time, dense content, teacher-centeredness, and insufficient attention to critical action.

The study concludes that the module achieved its introductory goals of raising awareness, curiosity, and attitudinal change toward CME. It recommends longer and more interactive implementation, integration of CME into teacher education courses and practicum, and further research across contexts. Limitations include the small interview sample, qualitative design, and short study period.

Pakistan’s higher education enrollment grew substantially after the Higher Education Commission was established in 2002, rising from about 2% in the early 2000s to 12.6% by 2021. Female participation also increased, narrowing the overall gender gap. However, access remains highly unequal by geography, income, gender, and institutional sector.

Using secondary data from government and independent sources, the study applies a distributive social justice perspective to examine enrollment across provinces, rural and urban areas, poverty zones, gender, and public versus private institutions. It finds that universities and enrollment are concentrated in urban, developed, and low-poverty regions. More than half of Pakistan’s districts lack college campuses, while rural and high-poverty areas have very limited access. Gender disparities remain particularly severe in poorer and less-developed regions.

The expansion of private universities has helped meet demand but has also intensified inequality because most are located in major cities and charge fees that are unaffordable for many low-income families. Public and private institutions also differ in quality and access to prestigious employment. Digital inequality and inadequate institutional support further disadvantaged low-income students during and after COVID-19.

Although Pakistan’s constitution, education policies, Vision 2025, and international commitments endorse equitable access, reforms have not sufficiently benefited historically marginalized populations. The study recommends opening well-funded public universities and skill-based community colleges in rural and high-poverty areas, regulating private institutions, expanding targeted scholarships and financial support, and addressing academic preparation barriers. It also calls for further research on institutional culture, admissions, vocational education, instructional quality, and other micro- and meso-level causes of inequality.

Apple reported issuing $8.5 billion of senior unsecured notes on May 11, 2020: $2.0 billion at 0.750% due 2023, $2.25 billion at 1.125% due 2025, $1.75 billion at 1.650% due 2030, and $2.5 billion at 2.650% due 2050. Interest is payable semiannually beginning November 11, 2020. Goldman Sachs, BofA Securities, J.P. Morgan, and Morgan Stanley represented the underwriters. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, note forms, and a legal opinion.

Abington Heights senior Theodore “Ted” Lambert has played cello since fifth grade and served as principal cellist in school and regional orchestras. His achievements include state PMEA rankings, performances with civic and philharmonic groups, teaching cello, and being named WVIA artist of the year. He also plays violin, performs classical and modern music at community events, and participates in academic competitions. Lambert plans to study chemical engineering at the University of Delaware while continuing to perform in chamber groups.

Digital leaders embed a data-centered culture into daily operations. They promote learning, thoughtful risk-taking, experimentation, long-term employee development, transparent data access, measurable objectives, and shared organizational goals. Data governance and controls support trust and safe use, while clear metrics provide teams with autonomy and flexibility. Leaders align goals through transparent, combined top-down and bottom-up processes, though some struggle to balance experimentation with deadlines or avoid excessive analysis.

Digital laggards emphasize short-term results, narrow training, risk avoidance, restricted data access, qualitative processes, and decisions based on authority or tenure. Their goals are often aspirational, poorly connected to strategy, and insufficiently grounded in data, creating organizational misalignment and discouraging innovation.

Case studies show that controlled experimentation enabled a pharmaceutical company to automate compliance checks in one-quarter of the previous time, while real-time reporting helped a retailer make faster decisions across business units. Research also found standardized APIs at 88% of digital leaders versus 27% of laggards.

Organizations commonly fall into four patterns: data novices lack both cultural and technical readiness; insight-ready firms support experimentation but lack advanced capabilities; tech-enabled firms have technology but discourage experimentation; and data-reliant firms overuse data at the expense of critical thinking. Strong data cultures require consistent beliefs, values, leadership support, skills, systems, and daily practices, with transformation occurring through deliberate, sustained effort.

The passage proposes five life challenges intended to foster empowerment and fulfillment: take a solo road trip to build independence and courage; pursue an entrepreneurial passion by starting a business; volunteer abroad while immersing yourself in another culture; confront a personal fear, such as skydiving or public speaking; and commit to a demanding physical goal suited to your fitness level. Each activity emphasizes pushing personal boundaries, learning from experience, and achieving lasting mental or physical growth.

The article traces the hockey lineage of 2010 Hobey Baker winner Blake Geoffrion through his father Dan, grandfather Bernie “Boom-Boom” Geoffrion, and great-grandfather Howie Morenz.

Born in Ontario in 1902, Morenz developed into a celebrated junior player known as “The Stratford Streak.” After Montreal Canadiens management discovered his speed and scoring ability, he signed with the team in 1923 and wore number 7. He immediately helped Montreal win a regular-season title and the Stanley Cup.

During eleven consecutive seasons with the Canadiens, Morenz became one of the team’s greatest stars. Despite his modest size, he was known for speed, scoring, physical play, and passion. He set a league record with 51 points in 1927–28 and won multiple Hart and Art Ross trophies and three Stanley Cups.

Financial pressures, declining performance, and changing ownership led Montreal to trade Morenz to Chicago in 1934. After unsuccessful periods with Chicago and the New York Rangers, he returned to Montreal when coach Cecil Hart was rehired.

On January 28, Morenz suffered a severely broken leg during a game against Chicago. Convinced he would never play again, he experienced declining physical and mental health and died following a heart attack on March 8. Thousands attended his funeral at the Montreal Forum, reflecting his enduring bond with Canadiens fans.

Amazon’s Q1 2022 net sales rose 7% to $116.4 billion, while operating income fell to $3.7 billion and net income shifted from an $8.1 billion profit to a $3.8 billion loss. The loss included a $7.6 billion valuation decline in its Rivian investment. AWS sales increased 37% to $18.4 billion and generated $6.5 billion in operating income, while North America and International recorded operating losses.

Operating cash flow was negative $2.8 billion for the quarter, and trailing-12-month free cash flow was negative $18.6 billion. At March 31, Amazon had $66.4 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, $410.8 billion in assets, and $134.0 billion in stockholders’ equity.

Amazon acquired MGM for approximately $6.1 billion net of cash acquired and repaid $2.5 billion of assumed debt. It repurchased $2.7 billion of stock under a new $10 billion authorization. Higher wages, transportation costs, supply-chain constraints, fulfillment inefficiencies, inflation, and changing post-pandemic demand pressured results. Changing server and networking equipment useful lives reduced quarterly depreciation by $973 million and benefited net loss by $769 million.

Jordan Montgomery threw four perfect innings to complete a combined no-hitter in the Yankees’ 3-0 win over Detroit. Although expected to return to Triple-A, the 24-year-old left-hander could earn a 2017 call-up or Opening Day bullpen role. Manager Joe Girardi praised Montgomery’s maturity and development while acknowledging uncertainty across the Yankees’ pitching staff. Montgomery, viewed long-term as a starter, said remaining with the major league club motivates him to improve.

WHO experts recommended that Dengvaxia be used only for people previously infected with dengue, requiring prior testing not yet available. WHO said earlier guidance acknowledged missing data and prompted Sanofi research showing increased severe-dengue risk among vaccinated people without prior exposure. Sanofi defended the vaccine’s safety and said no deaths resulted from it. The passage criticizes senators, particularly Franklin Drilon, for defending former President Benigno Aquino III amid 65 reported deaths and possible anti-graft charges. Drilon argued Aquino lacked malicious intent, relied on health officials, and that no conclusive evidence linked Dengvaxia to the deaths. The passage contrasts his position with WHO’s caution and argues that, as a senator, he should prioritize victims, parents, and the public interest.

LimeWire has evolved from a file-sharing service into an AI content creation and publishing platform. Its Studio supports image generation and editing through models including Stable Diffusion 2.1, Stable Diffusion XL, and DALL-E 2, with selectable styles, samplers, prompt guidance, and customization tools. LimeWire is developing its own AI model and plans to add music and video generation.

Published creations can automatically become NFTs on Polygon or Algorand and be shared publicly or with premium subscribers. Public NFTs can be discovered and traded, with creators receiving a 2.5% resale royalty. Creators can also earn advertising revenue paid monthly in LMWR cryptocurrency, which can be traded or used for AI prompts.

The free plan provides 10 credits, up to 20 daily images, and a 50% ad-revenue share. Premium plans cost $9.99 to $99 monthly, offering 1,000 to 11,250 credits, up to 2,000 to 22,500 image generations, 50% to 70% revenue shares, early model access, faster generation, creation history, no ads, and a Pro badge.

A Sunshine Coast woman was sexually abused and raped by her stepbrother from age eight to 16. She reported the abuse after joining the Australian Defence Force. The man pleaded guilty to nine child sex offences committed between ages 14 and 23. He was sentenced to five years in prison and made eligible for parole in August 2015.

The whitepaper was jointly produced by Microsoft Research Asia’s Societal AI team and computer and social scientists from industry and academia, with additional contributions from interns and a design team. It thanks collaborating researchers and acknowledges Lidong Zhou for his support and suggestions.

The author credits esthetician Renée Rouleau with identifying her melasma and its birth-control trigger, as well as diagnosing recurring desert breakouts as acne cosmetica caused by dry, windy conditions and oil-based foundation. Rouleau later recommended her Rapid Response Detox Masque for inflamed skin and hormonal acne. After testing it for a month, the author reports fewer breakouts and says it helps address clogged pores caused by hormones, travel, and sleeping in makeup. The lightweight gel mask contains tea tree oil, Chinese licorice, manuka oil, and a salicylic acid complex to combat bacteria, soothe inflammation, exfoliate, and reduce oil. It excludes parabens, synthetic fragrances and dyes, SD alcohol, and gluten. Rouleau recommends exfoliating first, applying the mask weekly for about 15 minutes, and rinsing it off easily afterward.

BusinessWeek reported that average CEO pay reached $13.1 million in 2000 despite weakening shareholder returns, though growth slowed as stock options lost value. Enron CEO Jeffrey Skilling received $72.5 million, while Kenneth Lay received $140.8 million.

India refused a $22 million payment claimed by Enron-controlled Dabhol Power, citing contractual penalties. Maharashtra’s Godbole committee recommended renegotiating both project phases and linking returns to a fixed rupee-dollar rate to reduce tariffs.

Cold weather was expected to strengthen U.S. utility earnings, including Enron’s. A California study alleged that public and private power suppliers earned excessive profits; Enron Energy Services was attributed $27.9 million.

Energy companies were developing wholesale power trading in France despite regulatory barriers and Electricité de France’s dominance. Enron was among regular participants.

Brazil’s integrated utility Copel was expected to attract strong privatization interest, with Enron listed among possible buyers.

This 2025 qualitative study examines Mexican higher education stakeholders’ views on online learning’s ability to expand access and improve quality. Mexico enrolled 5.2 million tertiary students in 2022–23, with 22% studying at a distance. Distance enrollment grew 150% between 2013–14 and 2022–23, compared with 18% for face-to-face learning; private institutions enrolled 69% of distance students.

Researchers conducted semi-structured interviews with 32 leaders, professors, and students from six public and private universities across five Mexican states. Participants reported that online learning increases flexibility and access, particularly for employed students and those with family responsibilities. However, inadequate internet connectivity, limited access to devices, institutional resource disparities, and rural–urban inequalities restrict participation. Some neurodivergent students and students requiring additional support also face difficulties.

Stakeholders identified quality concerns, including insufficient teacher preparation, varied digital proficiency, lower student engagement, communication and collaboration problems, academic-integrity risks, and the difficulty of teaching some practical subjects online. They emphasized ongoing pedagogical training, stronger technological infrastructure, and learning and mental-health support.

Participants generally viewed online learning as a useful complement rather than a replacement for in-person education. They valued its flexibility and support for international collaboration while favoring hybrid or mixed approaches. The study concludes that online learning could broaden Mexican higher education, but equitable access requires addressing digital, socioeconomic, institutional, and geographic disparities.

AMD’s March 2006 specification update documents numerous Revision A3 errata for the Geode CS5535 Companion Device. Affected areas include PIT/PIC interrupt behavior, legacy DMA, PCI and LPC transactions, IDE/UDMA and PRD handling, ACPI power management, GPIO, UART, USB, SMBus, keyboard emulation, clock gating, wake events, RTC memory, and timing compliance.

Reported effects range from negligible diagnostic or debug limitations to corrupted register writes, failed or discarded transactions, missed interrupts, unreliable wakeups, CRC errors, peripheral-access failures, and potential system hangs. Recommended mitigations include avoiding unsupported access patterns and modes, disabling affected clock-gating features, using correctly aligned PRD tables, sequencing IDE commands normally, trapping or replacing improperly sized ACPI accesses, using single-transfer DMA, applying software or external-circuit workarounds, and programming sleep delays below the PM_SED delay. Several issues have no resolution because they have little expected operational impact or require avoidance.

The lecture introduces linearized general relativity as one of three approaches to solving Einstein’s nonlinear field equations, alongside symmetric solutions and full numerical methods. In weak gravity, spacetime is treated as a small perturbation \(h_{\mu\nu}\) of flat spacetime, with all quadratic and higher-order perturbation terms neglected.

Lorentz transformations leave the flat background unchanged while transforming \(h_{\mu\nu}\) like a tensor field in special relativity. Indices on perturbations are raised and lowered using the flat metric, and the inverse spacetime metric is \(\eta^{\mu\nu}-h^{\mu\nu}\) to linear order. Infinitesimal coordinate transformations alter the metric perturbation but leave the linearized Riemann tensor unchanged, functioning as gauge transformations analogous to those in electromagnetism.

Linearizing the curvature tensors produces a complicated Einstein tensor. Introducing the trace-reversed perturbation and choosing Lorenz gauge, in which its divergence vanishes, reduces the Einstein field equations to sourced wave equations mathematically similar to those governing electromagnetic potentials.

For a static, nonrelativistic perfect fluid, the stress-energy tensor is dominated by its density component. The wave equation becomes a Poisson equation, relating the metric perturbation to the Newtonian gravitational potential and yielding the Newtonian-limit metric. This approximation underlies gravitational lensing, solar-system corrections, and descriptions of many binary systems. Rotating sources introduce mass-current contributions resembling magnetic fields and Lorentz-force effects, often called gravitomagnetism. The following lectures will address general dynamic solutions and gravitational radiation.

The disclosure describes a force transmission mechanism for teleoperated or manual surgical instruments that converts rotary input into translational movement of an actuation element controlling an end effector. A drive pulley transfers motion through one or two cables to a driven pulley, which moves a push-pull rod connected to jaws or another movable component. Cable routing, grooves, idler pulleys, and independently rotatable sheaves support alignment and pretensioning. Pulley dimensions and joint placement can provide application-specific mechanical advantage, including forces sufficient for clip appliers, forceps, or grippers. A ball joint permits rod translation while accommodating rotation of the instrument shaft and end effector. The mechanism may offer greater efficiency, range of motion, compactness, and reliability than toothed gear arrangements. The disclosed configurations and applications are exemplary and may be modified.

Clarkson College developed a college-wide interprofessional education model aligned with IPEC competencies, the Quadruple Aim, and NCICLE guidance. Its required, zero-credit online course combines four didactic modules with experiential events in knowledge, community, and service, accommodating clinical and nonclinical roles as well as on-campus and distance students.

Among 428 students completing the course and all assessments, 88.6% reported improved collaboration after the didactic modules. Of those reporting initial improvement, 93% perceived additional growth after experiential events; 56% of those initially reporting no growth improved afterward. Reflection analyses also identified positive experiences in teamwork, communication, collaboration, community awareness, and career preparation.

The model’s implementation and sustainability rely on institutional leadership, faculty and staff training, curriculum integration, ongoing assessment, experiential opportunities, and committee oversight. Outcomes indicate improved perceived interprofessional collaboration in clinical and nonclinical settings.

Enron’s financial crisis intensified as U.S. and U.K. energy companies reduced or restricted trading exposure following credit downgrades, falling shares, complex partnership disclosures and an SEC investigation. Enron said it would restate earnings from 1997 through the first half of 2001 and disclosed that former CFO Andrew Fastow may have received more than $30 million through partnerships doing business with the company.

Dynegy confirmed discussions about a possible combination but said no terms had been agreed. Reports described a potential $8 billion stock acquisition, supported by cash from ChevronTexaco, though concerns about Enron’s credit rating, debt and off-balance-sheet obligations complicated negotiations. Enron planned to meet creditors to discuss financing and merger plans.

Despite counterparties’ concerns, Enron said trading remained normal. Market participants emphasized Enron’s importance to energy-market liquidity, while FERC said it was monitoring the situation without intervening. Enron’s bonds rose on prospects of a Dynegy acquisition.

Wisconsin’s Department of Workforce Development awarded nearly $480,000 to seven projects training almost 600 Milwaukee residents for local jobs. Part of $4.5 million announced after Sherman Park unrest, the grants support training in community health, manufacturing, caregiving, construction, permeable pavement installation, machine operation, and call center/customer service work. Recipients include Milwaukee Area Health Education Center, Word of Hope Ministries, St. Ann Center, Employ Milwaukee, Grant Lakes Community Conservation Corps, Abaxent, and Enoch Solutions.

Mr. Solanko discussed restrictions on Finnish Legation personnel traveling outside Washington. Mr. Mikkola could return from New York as scheduled, while Attaché Wrede was ordered back immediately. Solanko compared the restrictions to those imposed on American personnel in Finland and raised concerns about delays in obtaining travel permission; the Department offered to expedite inquiries. He appeared surprised and once called the measures “prison regulations.” The Finnish Minister later argued that Helsinki restrictions applied equally to all diplomats because it was a special war area and requested relief from U.S. restrictions. A report on Finnish opinion from December 21, 1941, to January 4 found satisfaction over U.S. military reverses in East Asia, coupled with alarm over growing American cooperation with Britain and the Soviet Union.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. They operate from 4 V to 14 V and support switching frequencies from 100 kHz to 2 MHz. External gate drivers are recommended because switching and synchronous-rectifier outputs provide roughly 150-mA peak current.

Soft start is controlled by a capacitor on SS; regulation uses SS as the reference until it exceeds the 0.613-V reference. Synchronous-rectifier outputs activate after SS reaches 1 V. Switching frequency can be set by an RT resistor, an external 200-kHz-to-4-MHz clock at SYNC, or primary-secondary synchronization between two controllers. In primary-secondary mode, the secondary inverts the received clock, producing a 90° or 270° output phase shift.

Device variants provide single or dual primary and synchronous-rectifier outputs. OUTB and SRB are available only under specified device and 50%-duty-cycle configurations. Maximum duty-cycle options include 50%, 75%, and 100%, depending on the device and DCL connection. Dead time and leading-edge blanking are fixed on TPS7H5003-SP and externally programmable on other supported devices. Pulse skipping addresses minimum-on-time limitations and maintains transformer volt-second balance when dual outputs operate.

CS_ILIM supports PWM current sensing and overcurrent protection. At approximately 1.05 V, cycle-by-cycle limiting begins and charges the HICC capacitor. When HICC reaches 0.6 V, switching stops and SS discharges; restart occurs after HICC falls from 1 V to 0.3 V. The HICC capacitor sets limiting and restart delays, with 3.3 nF recommended as a minimum. The FAULT input stops switching above 0.6 V for the required pulse width and restarts through soft start after the signal falls below 0.5 V and a delay elapses. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C typical, with restart below 160°C typical.

Slope compensation, current-loop frequency compensation, and output regulation components are externally configurable. The design example describes a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull converter using GaN devices, including selection of timing, transformer, FETs, clamp, output filter, current sensing, protection, and compensation components. Example values include 205-kΩ RT, 33-nF soft-start capacitance, approximately 25-ns dead time, a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 0.47-µH output inductance, approximately 2.3-mF output capacitance, and a 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor.

Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high-current and high-dv/dt loops, reducing switch-node area, routing feedback and other sensitive signals away from switching traces, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, and using short, wide high-current traces. TI states that application guidance must be independently validated and that the resources and products are subject to applicable disclaimers and terms.

The TMS320DM8127 DaVinci is a programmable multimedia SoC integrating an ARM Cortex-A8 with NEON, a C674x floating-point DSP, HDVICP2 video acceleration, imaging and face-detection modules, and media-control subsystems. The ARM handles system control while the DSP and coprocessors process audio, video, and imaging workloads. On-chip memory includes ARM caches and RAM, DSP L1 memory and configurable 256KB L2 RAM/cache, with DSP accesses managed through a system MMU.

Peripherals include dual Gigabit Ethernet MACs, DDR2/DDR3 controllers, McASP and McBSP audio ports, DCAN, HDMI, PCIe, USB 2.0, GPIO, GPMC, I2C, SPI, UART, timers, MMC/SD/SDIO, camera and video interfaces, and configurable multiplexed pins. Hardware modules provide interprocessor mailboxes, spinlocks, interrupts, trace, boot configuration, and unified memory mapping. Development tools include ARM and DSP C compilers, a DSP assembly optimizer, and a Windows debugger interface.

The manual documents device architecture, pins, memory maps, operating conditions, power sequencing, clocks, timing, and peripherals. Revision updates cover supported operating points, pin-control functions, latch-up ratings, DDR3 speed support, voltage and clock changes, power sequencing, oscillator requirements, EDMA registers, and peripheral timing corrections.

The lecture examines black holes beginning with the Schwarzschild vacuum solution, which has mass despite a zero stress-energy tensor. The curvature singularity at \(r=0\) is physical, while \(r=2GM\) is a coordinate singularity. An infalling body crosses \(r=2GM\) in finite proper time but appears to approach it only asymptotically in Schwarzschild coordinate time.

Light emitted near \(r=2GM\) reaches distant observers with diminishing energy and increasingly separated pulses. At \(r=2GM\), the redshift becomes infinite, showing that Schwarzschild time fails there. Alternative coordinates clarify the geometry: tortoise coordinates stretch \(r=2GM\) to infinite coordinate distance; ingoing and outgoing null coordinates simplify radial light propagation; and Kruskal-Szekeres coordinates remove coordinate singularities everywhere except \(r=0\).

These coordinates reveal that \(r=2GM\) is an event horizon. After crossing it, every future-directed timelike or null trajectory moves toward smaller radius and cannot return. Events inside the horizon cannot causally influence the exterior. A spacetime with such a horizon is called a black hole.

The lecture also introduces other black-hole solutions. The Reissner-Nordstrom solution describes a charged black hole; if its charge exceeds its mass in the stated units, no horizon exists and the singularity is naked. The Kerr solution describes a spinning black hole, with angular momentum represented by the parameter \(a\); a horizon exists when \(a\leq GM\). Kerr spacetime is not spherically symmetric, and its spin distinguishes prograde from retrograde orbital behavior. The Kerr-Newman solution combines mass, spin, and charge.

The No-Hair theorem states that stationary black holes in three spatial and one temporal dimension are completely characterized by mass, spin, and charge and belong to the Kerr-Newman family. Since astrophysical charge is rapidly neutralized, Kerr describes observed black holes. During collapse or collision, gravitational and electromagnetic radiation remove structures incompatible with Kerr-Newman. This behavior, associated with Price’s theorem, leaves a stationary Kerr or Kerr-Newman black hole.

Italy reported that the Allies’ joint reply to President Wilson’s note had been agreed upon, pending Russian approval, and would be friendly but possibly omit detailed war aims. Greece submitted a conciliatory but indefinite preliminary reply, seeking assurances against encroachments, mixed inquiry commissions, and reparations. Allied conditions required Greek acceptance within 48 hours and execution within 15 days; the blockade would continue until fulfillment.

In France, Briand delivered the Allied reply, while Belgium submitted a separate note expressing gratitude for American aid and sympathy. The Allies planned publication on January 12, citing public expectations and difficulty maintaining confidentiality. Their reply praised the American peace initiative and supported a league of nations backed by enforceable agreements, but argued that lasting peace required settlement of the conflict through reparation, restitution, and guarantees against Central Power aggression.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture and TSMC’s 7nm process, targets AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. It contains 108 streaming multiprocessors, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1,555 GB/s, and a 40 MB L2 cache.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32, FP16, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. Compared with V100, A100 provides 2.5× FP16/FP32 and FP64 performance, while TF32 offers 10× faster processing than V100 FP32 operations. Fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity can double Tensor Core throughput by skipping zero values. A100 also supports simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution.

Memory improvements include a 192 KB combined L1 cache and shared memory per SM, 2.3× V100’s L2 read bandwidth, cache-residency controls, and compute data compression that can improve DRAM and L2 bandwidth by up to 4×. Asynchronous copy and barrier features reduce register use, overlap data movement with computation, and improve efficiency.

Multi-Instance GPU technology partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU instances with dedicated compute and memory resources, predictable performance, quality of service, and fault containment. Compute instances permit independent context execution and support Multi-Process Service workloads.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s aggregate bandwidth, twice V100’s total. A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, Magnum IO, InfiniBand, Ethernet, enhanced error handling, hardware JPEG decoding, optical-flow acceleration, improved atomic operations, and five NVDEC video decoders.

CUDA 11 supports A100 capabilities including Tensor Cores, sparsity, MIG, task graphs, asynchronous memory operations, cache controls, and cooperative groups. CUDA graphs reduce CPU launch overhead and inter-kernel latency by defining workflows once and executing them repeatedly.

The DGX A100 system combines eight A100 GPUs, provides up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, 4.8 TB/s aggregate bidirectional NVSwitch bandwidth, and up to 56 isolated GPU instances. It is designed to scale from individual workloads to clusters containing thousands of GPUs.

VentureWire’s October 5, 2000 issue reports extensive venture financing, acquisitions, launches, leadership changes, and fund activity. Broadcom agreed to acquire DSL chipmaker Element 14 for approximately $640 million in stock. Sony formed digital-media incubator 550 Digital Media Ventures with several hundred million dollars, while AC Ventures and Softbank launched the $100 million GameChange incubator network. Enterprise Investors raised an initial $200 million for a planned $300 million Central European fund. Productopia closed, and optical-networking company CyOptics secured $57 million.

Notable financings included Talisma’s $31.5 million first round, Cyclone Commerce’s $31 million Series B, NetScaler’s $35 million Series D, ePartners’ $35 million third round, and Actional’s $17.7 million second round. Paytrust and PayMyBills completed their merger alongside $20 million in financing.

Other developments included Amazon.com’s alliance with Ofoto, WatchGuard’s $66 million stock acquisition of Qiave, and Peopleclick’s acquisition of Claybrooke & Associates. New ventures and products included Contrado, CoreMatter’s eGiving Workplace, Wayfair.com, and network-storage provider Pyxsys. Electronics For Imaging created a $20 million imaging-technology fund, Far Blue approached a $14.6 million financing close, and Champions Sports launched Champions Tech Ventures.

Stafford Global offers online consultations and webinars for working professionals seeking undergraduate or postgraduate distance-learning programs. A University of Northampton MBA webinar was scheduled for 1 May 2018, with prior registration required.

The passage recommends nine podcasts for improving personal and business financial knowledge. Nick Loper covers side hustles and passive income; Farnoosh Torabi’s SO Money discusses finance, personal development, and business leaders; and Pat Flynn’s Smart Passive Income teaches low-resource business strategies.
