This multicenter prospective study evaluated the German 17-item Speech, Spatial and Qualities of Hearing Scale (SSQ17) for assessing hearing-related quality of life in unilateral Menière’s disease. Ninety-seven patients underwent vestibular assessment, pure-tone and speech audiometry, and completed the SSQ17.

Affected ears had substantially worse pure-tone thresholds and speech recognition than unaffected ears. The mean SSQ17 total score was 6.0, with scores of 5.3 for speech hearing, 5.1 for spatial hearing, and 7.2 for qualities of hearing. Scores did not differ significantly among diagnostic categories. The questionnaire demonstrated excellent internal consistency, with Cronbach’s alpha of 0.960 overall and 0.904–0.956 across subscales. SSQ17 scores generally decreased as pure-tone hearing impairment increased and rose with better speech recognition.

The findings support the SSQ17 as a viable patient-reported measure of hearing disability in advanced listening situations among patients with Menière’s disease, complementing clinical audiometric testing. However, it assesses only hearing-related disability and does not capture other major disease burdens, particularly vertigo.

This retrospective single-center study evaluated predictors of rebleeding among 226 adults admitted with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage to Rennes University Hospital from 2020–2022. Rebleeding occurred in 33 patients (15%). Admission blood pressure, Fisher grade, aneurysm location and size, and complication rates did not differ significantly between patients with and without rebleeding.

Time elapsed since initial symptoms was independently associated with rebleeding: each additional hour increased the odds by 0.7%. WFNS score was also an independent predictor. Two-thirds of rebleeding events occurred more than 24 hours after symptom onset. Rebleeding before aneurysm securing occurred in 9% of patients treated within 24 hours and 21% treated later. Patients with rebleeding also had substantially longer times from symptom onset to hospital admission.

Outcomes at one and six months were not significantly different overall, although patients without rebleeding more frequently achieved a Glasgow Outcome Scale score of 5 at six months. Limitations included the retrospective design, few rebleeding events, and a pragmatic rebleeding definition that could not always exclude other causes of deterioration. The findings support securing aneurysms as early as possible.

The passage describes SD Memory Card Physical Layer Specification 6.00 behavior for locking, commands, switching functions, addressing, timing, status, error handling, and performance.

Force erase preserves the secure area, maintains lock and temporary/group write protection during execution, then unlocks the card and clears those protections after erasing the user area. ACMD6 is rejected while locked, so bus width changes require an unlocked card. Locked cards accept only specified commands; hosts should avoid unsupported CMD42 parameters, force erase on permanently write-protected cards, and inappropriate force-erase protection on COP cards.

CMD55 marks the next command as application-specific. Defined legal ACMDs retain APP_CMD status; undefined legal commands are interpreted as regular commands, while illegal commands set an error. CMD6 switches or checks functions in six groups, including access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. Mode 0 queries support, readiness, and power consumption; Mode 1 changes functions. Invalid selections cancel switching, and busy functions should be checked with Mode 0. CMD6 returns a 512-bit status block and is mandatory for cards compliant with Version 1.10 or later. Power limits begin at 0.72 W and may be raised according to host supply and thermal capability.

High-Speed mode provides a 25 MB/s interface using a 50 MHz clock and is optional. CMD8, issued in Idle state before ACMD41, verifies host voltage compatibility and returns an echoed voltage range and check pattern. SDSC cards use byte addressing and CMD16-defined block lengths, whereas SDHC and SDXC use fixed 512-byte blocks and block addressing.

Hosts may vary or stop the clock subject to transaction and ACMD41 restrictions, including supplying eight clocks after transactions. Commands and most responses use CRC7; data uses CRC16. CRC failures and illegal commands leave card state unchanged and set status errors. Read, write, and erase operations have defined timeout rules, with write busy generally limited to 250 ms and certain SDXC cases permitting 500 ms.

Commands use fixed 48-bit formats and are organized into command classes. Responses include R1, R1b, R2, R3, R6, and R7 formats. Card information is exposed through Card Status, 512-bit SD Status, and Task Status. SD Status includes protected-area size, speed classes, allocation-unit information, erase timing, performance classes, and command-queue support.

Speed classifications support real-time recording. Defined methods include Speed Classes 2, 4, 6, and 10; UHS Speed Grades 1 and 3; and Video Speed Classes 6, 10, 30, 60, and 90. Allocation Units are divided into Recording Units, and performance requirements cover sequential writing, fragmented-area movement, reading, and file-system updates. SDXC differs by allowing larger allocation units, requiring recording to entirely free units, omitting move performance, using exFAT-related FAT, bitmap, directory, and continuous-information updates, and optionally using CMD20 for Speed Class control.

The article backtests calendar effects in the TLT ETF, which tracks 20-year Treasury bonds, primarily from 2004 to August 2021. It identifies weak performance during the first seven trading days of each month and stronger returns during the remainder. A strategy combining long end-of-month positions with short positions early in the month produced a 10.2% annual return and 24% maximum drawdown, compared with 3.8% and 48% for buy and hold. An improved short strategy returned an average 0.6% per trade, with 5.5% CAGR and a profit factor of 2. Investing from the close of the seventh trading day through month-end reportedly doubled buy-and-hold returns while maintaining roughly two-thirds market exposure. The article also explains that TLT prices and interest rates move inversely.

Scaling in means gradually building a trading position as new entry opportunities arise, following a predetermined plan rather than attempting to rescue a losing trade. Retail investors may buy as prices fall to reduce their average purchase price, day and trend-following traders may add to winning positions, and institutional traders may enter large orders gradually to limit market impact and avoid front-running.

The strategy offers flexible timing, potentially better average prices, reduced initial risk, and less slippage. However, it requires discipline and carries risks: investors may establish only part of their intended position before a rebound, while traders adding to winners may suffer losses after a sudden reversal.

Scaling in differs from doubling down and Martingale strategies. Doubling down adds to a losing trade in hopes of reaching breakeven, while Martingale doubles the size of each added trade. Scaling out is the opposite process, involving gradual exits to secure profits while retaining exposure to further gains.

Swing traders may scale in at potential reversal levels in mean-reversion strategies or add to profitable positions in trend-following strategies. The passage’s backtest produced a lower compound annual growth rate with scaling in but reportedly improved risk-adjusted returns and capital efficiency by reducing time in the market.

Digital laggards often fail to connect priorities, strategy, and team contributions, leading employees to deprioritize unclear objectives and pursue individual judgments. A data-driven culture improves vertical alignment through shared metrics and goals and horizontal alignment through common data models, transparency, and collaboration.

Digital leaders emphasize learning, transparent data access, clear metrics, and consistency among leadership beliefs, company values, and employee behavior. Laggards recognize the importance of data culture but face entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient leadership focus. Changing mindsets and behaviors requires compelling, widely understood reasons.

Strong data cultures support learning, risk-taking, transparency, measurement, and successful digital transformation. Organizations commonly fall into four patterns: data novices lack enabling culture and systems; insight-ready firms welcome experimentation but lack technical capabilities; tech-enabled firms possess technology but discourage experimentation; and data-reliant firms overuse data in ways that may inhibit critical thinking. Each can build on existing strengths through targeted action.

A Seattle Public Utilities study using four decades of rainfall data from 17 gauges found that extreme, long-lasting rainstorms have become more frequent and intense over the past 15 years, while the city’s typical drizzle and short showers have largely remained unchanged. A 24-hour storm producing 4 inches of rain, once classified as a once-in-a-century event, is now projected every 25 years; the new century-level threshold exceeds 5 inches.

SPU says the findings support residents’ observations and align with National Weather Service data. The utility will use the updated measurements to plan drainage and wastewater infrastructure, much of which was designed for a different climate. More intense storms can overwhelm combined sewage and stormwater systems, polluting waterways. Officials and meteorologists say the study highlights the need to prepare for flooding in Seattle and across Western Washington, while available science suggests climate change will bring continued long-term changes in extreme rainfall.

Enron neared a potentially record bankruptcy after Dynegy abandoned its acquisition, credit agencies downgraded Enron to junk status, and mounting debt obligations strained its limited cash. Senate Majority Leader Tom Daschle called for a congressional investigation. Enron’s European operations entered administration, while its extensive overseas assets and derivatives liabilities threatened to complicate any reorganization.

Energy exchanges restricted or suspended Enron trading, and EnronOnline reopened mainly to unwind positions. U.S. power and gas markets remained generally orderly, though British and German electricity markets experienced volatility. Trading shifted toward alternatives such as InterContinental Exchange.

Banks, utilities, energy companies, investment funds and other counterparties disclosed varying exposure to Enron. Treasury prices rose amid bankruptcy concerns, bank bonds weakened, and Enron shares and bonds reflected expectations of insolvency. Enron Metals attracted potential buyers, while the crisis delayed a Houston office project. NewPower, Reliant Resources and Williams said their financial positions or Enron-related exposure were manageable.

The 1942 Foreign Relations series comprises six numbered regional volumes and an unnumbered volume on China. Its Belgium section covers mutual-aid and military-service agreements, along with U.S.-British-Belgian negotiations concerning Belgian Congo trade. In March 1942, the State Department asked about stalled renewal talks for an expired Anglo-Belgian economic agreement and suggested possible U.S. participation. The U.S. Chargé reported delays caused by personnel changes, disputes over purchase prices, American competition, resistance from Congo trading interests, and Belgium’s failure to provide a comprehensive list of desired British goods. Growing wartime demand for Congo products prompted Britain to seek policy coordination with the United States.

NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2015 reported quarterly revenue of $1.153 billion, up 5% year over year, while net income fell to $26 million from $128 million. Six-month revenue rose 4% to $2.304 billion, and net income declined to $160 million from $265 million. Quarterly GPU revenue increased 9% to $959 million, driven by high-end gaming products, while Tegra revenue decreased 19% to $128 million. Gross margin was 55.0%.

Quarterly operating expenses rose 22% to $558 million, including $89 million of charges related to winding down Icera modem operations. NVIDIA expected another $15 million to $25 million of restructuring charges and said the plan would affect approximately 5% of its workforce. The company also recorded costs for recalling SHIELD tablets whose batteries could overheat.

At July 26, 2015, NVIDIA had $435 million in cash, $4.07 billion in marketable securities, $6.979 billion in assets, and $1.399 billion in long-term debt. Six-month operating cash flow was $409 million. NVIDIA returned $452 million to shareholders during the quarter through a $400 million accelerated share repurchase and $52 million in dividends. It also began constructing a new headquarters under an operating lease arrangement with up to $380 million in bank funding.

Inflammation is associated with depression through elevated cytokines and chemokines, altered neurotransmitter metabolism and neuroplasticity, and signalling pathways including NLRP3, NF-κB and P2X7R. Animal studies suggest that pharmacological interventions such as empagliflozin, calcitriol, natural extracts and nutritional supplements, and non-pharmacological interventions including acupuncture, exercise and photobiomodulation, may reduce neuroinflammation and depressive-like behaviours. However, most studies are short-term, small-scale and preclinical, leaving their long-term effects, safety, individual variability and clinical relevance uncertain.

This scoping review followed established frameworks and PRISMA guidance. PubMed was searched without date restrictions for randomized controlled trials involving anti-inflammatory strategies for depression. Of 1,057 screened articles, 11 studies published between 2008 and 2024 were included in the content analysis, collectively involving 907 patients. Interventions included fluoxetine, infliximab, ketamine, minocycline, celecoxib combined with vortioxetine, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and lacquer tree supplementation. Treatment lasted two to eighteen weeks. Examined inflammatory markers included CRP, high-sensitivity CRP, soluble TNF receptors, interleukins and TNF-α, although many markers were undetectable and definitions and measurement methods varied.

Anti-inflammatory strategies showed potential benefits in some patients, particularly those with elevated baseline inflammation. Higher CRP or TNF levels were associated with better responses to infliximab, while minocycline appeared more favourable among patients with high-sensitivity CRP levels of at least 3 mg/L. Some treatments reduced depressive symptoms, inflammatory markers, oxidative stress or body measurements. Nevertheless, responses varied substantially, celecoxib showed no superiority to placebo in one setting, and drug safety, testing costs and the lack of validated biomarkers limit clinical applicability.

The review identifies unresolved debates over single-target versus multi-target approaches and pharmacological versus non-pharmacological interventions. It recommends long-term follow-up, improved animal and clinical study designs, investigation of genetic, lifestyle and gut-microbiota differences, standardised inflammatory indicators, and research on combined interventions. Artificial intelligence and micro-robots are proposed as future tools for integrating patient data, monitoring inflammation and supporting personalised treatment, but these concepts remain prospective.

The authors conclude that pharmacological anti-inflammatory treatment of depression currently has limited research value and poor feasibility. They recommend greater emphasis on accessible non-pharmacological approaches such as exercise and positive thinking, alongside low-cost, broadly generalisable research.

A vehicle driving-assistance system uses cameras, radar, lidar, ultrasonic sensors, sensor fusion, and optional vehicle communications to detect surrounding objects and vehicles, including faster vehicles approaching from behind. To reduce rear-end collision risk, the system may warn the driver, recommend maneuvers, or autonomously accelerate to match the approaching vehicle’s speed and change lanes when sufficient space is available.

When passing a slower vehicle, the equipped vehicle may accelerate and enter an adjacent lane ahead of a faster rearward vehicle, then return to its original lane after completing the pass. If a faster vehicle approaches in the same lane, the system may move the equipped vehicle into an available adjacent lane or accelerate until a safe lane change is possible. These functions may operate autonomously in SAE Level 3 modes or with greater driver involvement in SAE Level 2 modes.

Maneuver decisions may consider vehicle speeds and distances, available space, traffic in multiple lanes, road exits, speed limits, driver comfort, travel time, safety benefits, and emergency-vehicle priority. Adaptive cruise-control speeds may also account for vehicle type, trailers, operating conditions, and driver-license restrictions. An electronic control unit processes sensor data, detects objects, controls vehicle motion, and may present alerts or exterior images on a display.

Mapbox provides geographic data for third-party apps and is expanding into self-driving car technology through partnerships with Microsoft, ARM and Intel’s Mobileye. Its Microsoft collaboration sends selected camera data to Azure for processing while showing drivers real-time road changes. ARM will optimize Mapbox software to recognize lanes, pedestrians and signs faster. Mapbox also developed in-car software that efficiently downloads Mobileye’s cloud-based road data, maintaining a map roughly 200 meters ahead as backup for onboard sensors. The company competes with Google Maps and HERE Technologies and has raised about US$228 million.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell architecture introduces advances in geometry, ray tracing, AI rendering, video, display, scheduling, and power efficiency. Mega Geometry uses triangle clusters and GPU-driven BVH construction to reduce processing and CPU overhead. Partitioned TLAS updates only changed scene partitions, while fast cluster generation supports real-time ray tracing of subdivision surfaces. Mega Geometry supports NVIDIA ray-tracing APIs and RTX GPUs from Turing onward.

Fourth-generation RT Cores add cluster compression and faster ray-triangle intersections. Blackwell also supports Linear Swept Spheres for strand rendering, providing about twice the speed and one-fifth the geometry memory of triangle-strip methods. SER 2.0 improves thread reordering efficiency and neural workload coherence.

The AI Management Processor uses a dedicated RISC-V processor to schedule GPU contexts, reduce CPU dependency and latency, and coordinate graphics and AI workloads. Video improvements include hardware 4:2:2 encoding and decoding, ninth-generation NVENC quality gains, faster sixth-generation NVDEC decoding, and multiple encoders and decoders on the RTX 5090. DisplayPort 2.1b supports up to 80 Gbps, enabling 8K at 165 Hz or 4K at 480 Hz with compression.

Blackwell Max-Q features finer power, clock, memory, and rail gating; clocks that adjust 1,000 times faster; and deep sleep entry ten times faster than Ada. These changes can reduce power consumption substantially in suitable workloads.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three generated frames per rendered frame. Its frame-generation model is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than the prior method. Transformer models replace CNNs for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability, motion detail, lighting, anti-aliasing, and reducing ghosting.

Blackwell enables developer-created neural shaders through Tensor Core access from graphics shaders. Applications include Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. These techniques approximate complex materials and lighting, compress textures, model subsurface scattering, and generate more natural-looking faces.

The flagship GB202 contains 92.2 billion transistors, up to 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, and 768 Tensor cores, and powers the RTX 5090. GB203 targets high-end products including the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti, while GB205 targets the RTX 5070 performance segment.

The £1,100 Marin Nail Trail 6 is an aluminium trail hardtail available with 27.5in or 29in wheels depending on frame size. Its 6061 hydroformed frame features a 68-degree head angle, 120mm RockShox Recon fork, short stem, wide handlebar, dropper-post routing and two bottle mounts. Components include a SRAM GX 1×11 drivetrain, Sunrace 11–42 cassette, Formula hubs, Marin rims, Schwalbe tyres and Shimano Deore hydraulic brakes.

The reviewer found the bike roomy, comfortable and stable, with predictable handling and a responsive alloy-frame feel. Its slender stays improve comfort and traction, while the component selection balances performance, durability and cost. It performed well on singletrack, everyday rides and casual trail exploration. The frame is also considered a strong platform for future upgrades. Overall, the Nail Trail 6 is described as attractive, versatile and enjoyable to ride.

The Woodland Trust recorded 42 indicators of spring at over 1,000 UK locations in early 2017. Sightings were later and fewer than in 2016 due to colder temperatures. Nature’s Calendar data helps researchers assess climate change’s effects on wildlife.

Kimberly Kirkwood forwarded a holiday chain email encouraging recipients to make a wish and resend the message. It claims wishes will come true within a number of minutes equal to the recipient’s age, promises rewards for forwarding it, and warns of bad luck for failing to do so.

San Diego Unified School District rescinded a resolution inviting Education Secretary Betsy DeVos after objections from the teachers’ union, parents and community partners. Union president Lindsay Burningham accused DeVos of seeking to undermine public education through vouchers and minimally regulated charter organizations. Board president Richard Barrera, who initially supported the invitation so DeVos could learn about district schools, withdrew his backing and called for defending public education.

Separately, protesters tried to block DeVos from entering a Washington school, an action condemned by American Federation of Teachers president Randi Weingarten, who encouraged DeVos to visit public schools. DeVos was confirmed after Vice President Mike Pence broke a Senate tie. At a White House session with parents and educators from varied school settings, President Donald Trump promoted school choice, while DeVos said she wanted to hear ideas for ensuring equal access to high-quality education.

The plaintiff moved to dismiss the defendants’ devolutive appeal, alleging incomplete transcripts, failure to include or cite all parties and a deceased defendant’s heirs, and acquiescence by several appellants. The court held that three partial transcripts filed under the same docket number collectively constituted a complete record, substantially complying with the law. Appellants were not required to name every appellee in their appeal petition; requesting citation of appellees was sufficient, with issuance and service being the clerk’s and sheriff’s duties. Any acquiescence by some appellants did not impair the appeal rights of those who had not acquiesced. The possible omission of the deceased defendant’s representatives likewise did not prejudice the remaining appellants and could still be raised appropriately. The motion to dismiss was denied with costs.

Six former detainees challenged Illinois counties’ practice, authorized by state law, of charging bail fees beyond required bail amounts. The district court dismissed the action for lack of standing and denied class certification as moot.

The Seventh Circuit reversed. The plaintiffs had standing to pursue individual § 1983 claims against Kane and DuPage Counties because they alleged monetary injuries directly traceable to those counties’ bail-fee policies and redressable through litigation. Even if class certification were inappropriate, the individual claims should not have been dismissed.

The court also reinstated the proposed class claims against Kane and DuPage Counties, finding no basis for dismissing them before conducting a Rule 23 analysis. As to 17 other counties, the court held that the plaintiffs might represent a class suing all 19 counties because the challenged fees arose from the same state statute. Although the plaintiffs had not adequately requested certification of a defendant class, a plaintiff class could potentially proceed against counties “juridically linked” by a uniform legal requirement.

The district court must determine on remand whether the proposed class satisfies Rule 23’s numerosity, commonality, typicality, adequacy, and applicable subdivision requirements, and consider the effects of related litigation. The appellate court concluded that neither standing doctrine nor Rule 23 automatically bars such a class action when the named plaintiffs suffered injuries under the same statute affecting unnamed class members.

The study demonstrates solid-state near-infrared-to-visible photon upconversion using a DIB-SQ:PCBM bulk heterojunction sensitizer coupled to a rubrene annihilator. Charge-transfer states, normally considered a loss pathway in photovoltaic systems, facilitate direct and PCBM-mediated triplet energy transfer to rubrene. Triplet-triplet annihilation then generates visible emission.

A 1:3 DIB-SQ:PCBM weight ratio maximized rubrene triplet population and light output. Doping rubrene with 0.5 vol.% DBP increased its photoluminescence and shifted emission from 562 to 605 nm. The optimized DIB-SQ:PCBM/rubrene:DBP system achieved a saturated upconversion quantum yield of 1.36% and a threshold intensity of 60.5 mW/cm² under 690 nm excitation. Transient spectroscopy identified charge-transfer states, PCBM and rubrene molecular triplets, and a rubrene triplet lifetime of about 1.4 μs. Magnetic-field measurements provided further evidence that the upconverted emission arose from triplet-triplet annihilation.

The results show that fullerene loading can tune charge-transfer-state formation and repurpose back-electron recombination to sensitize triplets. This approach may expand the range of low-band-gap materials suitable for solid-state photon-upconversion systems and optoelectronic devices.

Victor Wembanyama undertook an unconventional offseason after being diagnosed with a career- and life-threatening condition in his right shoulder. He said the traumatic experience motivated him to improve physically and mentally. His summer included soccer in Costa Rica and Tokyo, a 10-day Shaolin temple retreat in China, meditation, Kung Fu, chess, a NASA visit and time with Kevin Garnett.

At the Shaolin temple, Wembanyama woke at 4:30 a.m., followed a vegetarian diet, meditated and trained to improve strength, flexibility, balance and range of motion. Observers say he returned stronger, more controlled through physical contact and increasingly comfortable with his skills.

Wembanyama also worked with Hakeem Olajuwon during four 2½-hour sessions, developing a variation of Olajuwon’s “Dream Shake,” spin moves and a jump hook. Olajuwon emphasized using Wembanyama’s versatility efficiently across all five positions.

Away from training, Wembanyama helped organize Spurs fan supporter auditions and participated in a team visit to a Texas community affected by deadly flooding. He said he had maximized what he could accomplish during one summer and was ready to return to basketball.

Nearly 600 SUNY Oneonta students and staff attended a memorial for Daniel William Michaels, 18, who died Dec. 3. Attendees shared readings, memories and condolences for his family. More than $17,000 has been raised for a scholarship in his name.

IGP Ibrahim Idris warned Ekiti police officers against aiding politicians to manipulate the July 14, 2018 governorship election, stressing their duty to protect voters, observers and election materials impartially. Represented by ACP Abayomi Shogunle, he urged the public to report police involvement in rigging and said guilty officers could be dismissed and prosecuted. He cited punishment of officers accused of misconduct during the 2014 election and cautioned personnel against sacrificing their careers for politicians. Separately, protesting Mobile Policemen in Maiduguri accused Idris of corruption, inhumane treatment and selling promotions to connected individuals.

Denby reported that tensions among China, Japan, and Korea remained critical, though China favored conciliation and later indications suggested diplomacy might prevent conflict. British minister O’Conor and Viceroy Li sought U.S. leadership in urging the powers to ask Japan to withdraw its troops from Korea. Sill reported that a departing U.S. admiral left him vulnerable after he had promised the Korean King asylum; Gresham clarified that the United States would not intervene forcibly. Insurance Australia Group shares continued falling after a decline of more than 4%, reaching $8.07 amid scrutiny from the financial services Royal Commission. While no investigation findings directly concern IAG, scandals involving other insurers and reports of group counsel Chris Bertuch’s leave have weakened confidence. IAG recently agreed to a $525 million sale to two Asian companies and reported positive half-year results with a 7.7% dividend increase. Investors were advised to monitor future findings.

The Fresh Market appointed Yvonne Cowser Yancy senior vice president and chief human resources officer. With over 20 years of public- and private-sector HR experience, she will oversee employee benefits, recruitment, development, training, compensation, and wellness. Yancy previously led HR for the City of Atlanta and held roles at several Fortune 500 companies. She holds degrees from Georgia State and Northwestern and serves Atlanta civic organizations.

Japanese government bond prices fell with U.S. Treasuries as markets awaited the Bank of Japan’s April debt-buying plans. Some expect reduced purchases of shorter-dated bonds as the BOJ seeks to improve liquidity. Five- and 10-year JGB yields rose slightly.

Ángel Bracero, an independent contractor hired to transport rice, was injured when approximately thirty bags fell from a pile in S. Ramírez & Co.’s Ponce shop. The court found sufficient evidence that the defendant operated the Ponce branch and that Bracero was not subject to the Workmen’s Compensation Act.

The Supreme Court reversed the damages judgment. It held that res ipsa loquitur did not apply because Bracero and other workers had been removing bags, so the pile was not under the defendant’s exclusive control. It also found no proven negligence attributable to the defendant at the time of the accident.

Chief Justice Del Toro dissented, joined by Justice Hutchison. He concluded that testimony supported the trial court’s findings that the pile was improperly constructed, the defendant had been warned it might fall, and its inadequate attempt to prop it up demonstrated persistent negligence. He would have affirmed the judgment.

Tesla’s 2017 Form 10-K describes the company as a vertically integrated sustainable-energy business designing, manufacturing, selling, installing and servicing electric vehicles, energy storage products and solar systems. Its reportable segments are automotive and energy generation and storage. Tesla employed 37,543 full-time workers at year-end.

Tesla produced Model S, Model X and Model 3, beginning Model 3 deliveries in July 2017, and planned additional vehicles including Tesla Semi and a new Roadster. Vehicles were sold directly through company-owned stores and galleries, supported by service centers, mobile technicians and a growing global charging network. Tesla emphasized vehicle range, performance, energy efficiency, software updates and self-driving development.

Energy products included Powerwall 2 for homes and Powerpack 2 for commercial, industrial and utility applications. Tesla also sold and leased solar systems, offered power purchase agreements, and began producing and installing Solar Roof. Vehicle, solar and storage customers had access to various warranties and financing arrangements.

Manufacturing occurred primarily in California, the Netherlands, Gigafactory 1 in Nevada and Gigafactory 2 in New York. Gigafactory 1 produced battery cells, packs, energy storage products and Model 3 drive units in partnership with Panasonic. Tesla sourced thousands of parts globally, often from single suppliers, and used materials including aluminum, steel, lithium, nickel, cobalt and copper.

Government incentives included California manufacturing-equipment tax exclusions, Nevada incentives for Gigafactory 1, federal solar tax credits and tradable vehicle and renewable-energy credits. Tesla’s operations were subject to vehicle safety, battery transport, dealership, self-driving, energy storage, utility and solar regulations.

The filing identifies major risks including production and delivery delays, especially for Model 3; dependence on suppliers and Panasonic; difficulties scaling manufacturing, service and international operations; uncertain electric-vehicle adoption; cost overruns; reliance on a limited vehicle lineup; battery fires and material shortages; product defects and liability; regulatory restrictions; and intense competition across automotive, storage and solar markets.

WiseGuyReports announced “Gonorrhea - Pipeline Review, H2 2017,” covering therapeutics under development for the sexually transmitted bacterial infection. The report analyzes treatments by development stage, drug target, mechanism of action, administration route, and molecule type, while providing drug profiles, R&D histories, licensing details, news, and discontinued or dormant projects. Companies covered include Debiopharm International, Entasis Therapeutics, Merck & Co., and Recce. The guide is intended to support competitive analysis, R&D planning, partnerships, licensing, mergers and acquisitions, and portfolio strategy.

The speaker expresses confidence that the team can win by playing its best game at home. Proud of reaching this point in the Stanley Cup Finals, the team believes preparation, leadership by example, teamwork, and making every shift count will give it a good chance.

The S&P 500 gained 2.2% in July and 7.8% year to date, maintaining a healthy medium- and long-term uptrend despite an early-August decline. Seasonal increases in volatility and credit spreads, weakening short-term breadth, heavy technology exposure, and bearish divergence signal near-term risks. Global stocks remain ahead of US large caps, while frontier markets led July returns. US electricity demand reached a record high. The study introduces an evolutionary hypergame framework in which individuals possess heterogeneous subsets of cooperation, defection, and loner strategies. Behavioral adaptation occurs on two timescales: players rapidly select strategies through payoff-sensitive introspection, while strategy-set frequencies evolve more slowly through payoff-based competition. Pairwise interactions are modeled as Markov chains with unique stationary distributions at finite introspection strength, producing long-run payoffs used in replicator and spatial evolutionary dynamics.

Tournament and theoretical analyses show that weak introspection generally favors defection-containing sets or abstention. As introspection strengthens, players with the set {C, L} better sustain mutual cooperation and avoid exploitation by shifting to the loner strategy. Its performance also improves with the benefit-to-cost ratio, and sufficiently strong introspection allows it to outperform both unconditional defectors and {D, L} players.

In well-mixed populations, weak introspection leads to dominance by {D, L} when only two-strategy sets compete and by {L} when all seven possible sets compete. Stronger introspection shifts dominance toward {C, L}, producing higher-payoff cooperative equilibria. Spatial populations show similar overall patterns, though intermediate introspection can generate coexistence or temporary dominance by unconditional cooperators. At high introspection, {C, L} ultimately dominates. The results indicate that heterogeneous strategy access and introspective adaptation can substantially promote cooperation in both well-mixed and structured populations.

A sick Belfast woman asked Feeley’s Fish & Chip Shop to buy cold-and-flu tablets while delivering her food. The restaurant fulfilled the unusual request, shared it on Facebook, and drew widespread praise for its customer service. Feeley’s also offered her a free meal after her recovery.

Elon Musk said Tesla could help rebuild Puerto Rico’s power grid after Hurricane Maria, citing its renewable-energy projects on smaller islands. Governor Ricardo Rossello invited discussions, calling Puerto Rico a potential flagship project for Tesla technology. At the time, slightly more than 10 percent of residents had electricity. Tesla had already sent hundreds of Powerwall battery systems and planned further shipments. Musk referenced Tesla subsidiary SolarCity’s solar microgrid on Ta’u, American Samoa, which powers nearly all island needs and reduces diesel use.

Renault was expected to extend CEO Carlos Ghosn’s contract, while appointing a deputy or operating chief to handle operations, allowing him to strengthen Renault’s alliance with Nissan and Mitsubishi. The alliance sold 10.6 million vehicles after adding Mitsubishi, ranking second globally behind Volkswagen. Despite shared costs and technology, Renault-Nissan has faced rivalries, technology disputes and concerns about Renault’s influence over Nissan, raising questions about the alliance’s survival after Ghosn’s departure.

The passage specifies DM8127/DM814x power, reset, clocking, interrupt, peripheral, and interface requirements. Core voltage domains support independently selectable operating performance points and real-time Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling, subject to supported combinations, voltage-difference limits, and suspended DDR access during frequency changes. Adaptive Voltage Scaling is described but not supported. SRAM shutdown reduces leakage but erases stored data.

I/O groups support independently selected 1.8-V or 3.3-V supplies, while DDR interfaces support 1.5 V or 1.8 V. PHYs must enter power-down mode before their domains are switched off. Standby turns off switchable domains, runs the Cortex-A8 at its lowest frequency, and gates unused clocks. Defined power-supply sequencing, filtering, decoupling, and reset timing must be followed.

Reset sources include power-on, external and emulation warm, watchdog, software global cold and warm, test, and local resets. Their effects vary for emulation logic, EMAC, PCIe, boot-mode latching, and RSTOUT_WD_OUT. Most resets place I/O pins in high impedance. PCIe and EMAC support reset isolation under specified conditions.

Device clocks derive from DEV, optional AUX, SERDES, audio, and 32.768-kHz inputs through PLLs and dividers. DEV and AUX clocks may use crystals or 1.8-V LVCMOS sources. PLLs start in bypass mode and must remain within specified frequency limits.

The device provides ARM and DSP interrupt controllers, EDMA, advanced event triggering, trace, and JTAG. Peripheral sections describe DCAN, GPIO, GPMC/ELM, Ethernet/MDIO, and HDMI. Ethernet supports MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII with 3.3-V PHY interfaces. HDMI supports HDMI 1.3a, DVI, multichannel audio, and specified video modes; its TMDS pairs require controlled impedance, careful routing, paired vias, and low-capacitance ESD protection.

Gold prices have risen more than 50% over the past year to record highs, driven by recession fears, rate-cut expectations, dollar weakness and political uncertainty. UBS expects continued investment inflows, while Goldman Sachs forecast gold reaching $4,000 per troy ounce by mid-2026. Central banks are also expected to keep increasing gold holdings.

Higher material costs and tariffs are pressuring jewelry companies, particularly brands serving price-sensitive customers. Mejuri raised prices and introduced 10-karat products, while BaubleBar and Alexis Bittar emphasized gold-plated alternatives. Rowan also increased some prices while using gold coatings over surgical steel or titanium. Executives said consumers remain cautious and warned that sustained high gold prices could challenge companies unable to pass costs on to customers.

In 2011, Akamai was the world’s largest content delivery network, operating more than 100,000 servers across 78 countries and moving up to 30% of Internet traffic. Its decentralized infrastructure placed servers close to end users, improving speed and reliability for customers such as Apple, Amazon, Netflix, Microsoft, and government agencies.

As Akamai expanded internationally, its market share declined with distance from the United States. Local CDNs offered simpler, cheaper services tailored to domestic content, while major customers developed competing or in-house capabilities. Akamai held only about 10% of South Korea’s market, under 8% in China, and around 30% in India.

The company’s centralized approach contributed to these difficulties. Products, pricing, investments, and sales targets were largely determined at its Massachusetts headquarters, often without sufficient knowledge of local demand, labor conditions, network structures, competition, or brand awareness. Globally set prices limited responses to lower-priced competitors. Products developed or acquired in the United States were sometimes unnecessary abroad, as demonstrated when Akamai attempted to introduce mobile-content technology in Japan that had existed there for years. Local developments that could benefit the wider company were also overlooked.

Akamai reorganized in 2011 into product business units and three geographic theaters—Americas, EMEA, and APJ—to improve coordination and clarify customer ownership. However, product and pricing decisions remained global, and uncertainty persisted over responsibilities, particularly for multinational customers operating across several markets.

Vice president Charley Dublin and the international leadership team were tasked with proposing how, where, and how quickly Akamai should localize. They needed to balance local products, pricing, support, infrastructure, and market knowledge against centralized investment priorities and the global processes required to serve multinational customers.
The opponent’s strong, holding-style defense limited chances. Sammy Pahlsson scored the decisive goal, and the team aims to improve offensively when returning home.

Meta’s core social media business generates substantial cash flow and high returns, supporting major AI and innovation investments. This study assessed ex vivo susceptibility of Ugandan Plasmodium falciparum parasites to nine antimalarial drugs and examined genotype-phenotype associations involving 80 candidate resistance genes. Blood samples were collected from uncomplicated malaria cases in eastern and northern Uganda between July 2019 and June 2024; some analyses included samples collected since 2016.

Of 1,297 isolates collected, 1,114 were successfully evaluated. Most antimalarials retained potent activity, while quinine was less potent and pyrimethamine activity was poor. From 2016 to 2024, susceptibility increased markedly for chloroquine but decreased for dihydroartemisinin, lumefantrine, and mefloquine. Ring-stage survival assays frequently exceeded established artemisinin-resistance thresholds, although their clinical significance was uncertain.

Sequencing showed very low recent prevalence of PfCRT K76T and PfMDR1 N86Y mutations associated with chloroquine and amodiaquine resistance. Mutations associated with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance remained highly prevalent. The PfK13 C469Y and A675V artemisinin-resistance mutations were moderately prevalent and stable in northern Uganda but increased after 2021 in eastern Uganda.

PfK13 C469Y and A675V were associated with reduced susceptibility to dihydroartemisinin and lumefantrine in growth-inhibition assays, but not with ring-stage survival results. Wild-type PfMDR1 N86Y was associated with reduced lumefantrine and mefloquine susceptibility, while PfCRT K76T was linked to reduced chloroquine and amodiaquine activity. PfDHFR C59R and I164L were associated with progressively poorer pyrimethamine susceptibility. Potential additional associations included PfCARL D611N with lumefantrine and PfMDR1 Y500N with dihydroartemisinin.

Overall, malaria parasites remained mostly sensitive to commonly used drugs, but declining susceptibility to both components of first-line artemether-lumefantrine raises concern. Continued parasitological and genomic surveillance and policies limiting resistance selection and treatment failure were identified as priorities.

InVirtuoGen is a continuous-time discrete flow model for molecular generation that operates directly on fragmented SMILES. Unlike autoregressive and masked diffusion approaches, it refines all sequence positions simultaneously at every denoising step, enabling coordinated updates independent of sequence length. Its representation extends SAFE by decomposing molecules with revised BRICS, marking explicit attachment points, randomly shuffling fragments to reduce ordering bias, and tokenizing them with a 204-token vocabulary.

The model uses a diffusion transformer with bidirectional attention and was pretrained on roughly one billion molecules from ZINC and UniChem. It was evaluated on de novo generation, fragment-constrained design, PMO target-property optimization, and lead optimization. For de novo generation, finer simulation timesteps improved quality and diversity, and InVirtuoGen achieved a superior quality-diversity Pareto frontier over GenMol and SAFE-GPT. On fragment-constrained tasks, it produced competitive average quality and diversity and higher uniqueness, but lower validity than GenMol. These tasks require fixed fragment positions and therefore limit the model’s holistic refinement approach.

For property optimization, the framework combines a genetic algorithm with PPO adapted to discrete flows. The genetic algorithm recombines fragments from high-scoring molecules and applies mutation operators, while PPO estimates sequence probabilities through perturbed states and optimizes standardized oracle rewards. The passage reports state-of-the-art PMO results and improved lead-optimization performance over prior baselines.

Ontario’s Financial Accountability Office projects a $4 billion deficit in 2017-2018, rising to $9.8 billion by 2021-2022, despite the Liberal government’s balanced-budget claims. Moderate revenue growth, the Fair Hydro Plan and disputed pension accounting contribute to the outlook. The hydro plan alone is projected to add $3.2 billion to the deficit by 2021-2022.

Roffey secured a ten-wicket home victory over Cuckfield to remain joint top with Brighton & Hove after four games. Cuckfield were bowled out for 103, with Stuart Whittingham taking 4-35 and Rohit Jagota 3-17. Jagota then scored an unbeaten 64 and Theo Rivers 41 as Roffey reached 107 without loss in 20.4 overs. Captain Matt Davies praised the dominant team performance but urged Roffey to maintain standards and focus game by game. They next visit Ifield.

U.S. stocks edged lower after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates and outlined plans to reduce its $4.2 trillion securities portfolio. Weak oil prices pushed energy stocks down nearly 2%, while technology fell 1.2%. The Dow slipped 0.04%, the S&P 500 lost 0.38%, and the Nasdaq dropped 0.9%. Consumer prices unexpectedly declined in May, and retail sales posted their largest drop in 16 months. Alexion and H&R Block gained on corporate developments, while Biogen fell. Declining stocks outnumbered advancing issues on both major exchanges.

Flipkart co-founder Sachin Bansal is developing Billion, a budget private-label brand targeting shoppers in smaller Indian cities and towns. The brand spans electronics, appliances and accessories, with a low-cost smartphone also under consideration. The project is Bansal’s first major initiative since losing the CEO role in 2016 and uses a team largely outside Flipkart’s core organization. Billion aims to attract new customers, improve margins through private-label sales and differentiate Flipkart from Amazon India as online retail growth slows and Flipkart limits marketing spending while seeking profitability.

Following the Allied victory and Armistice, British, Japanese, Italian, French, Greek, and American leaders exchanged congratulations and praised their shared sacrifices for international freedom, democracy, independence, and civilization. Balfour, King Victor Emanuel, Wilson, Lansing, Lloyd George, and Polk emphasized stronger friendships and continued cooperation. Wilson welcomed close collaboration with French leader Clemenceau, while Lloyd George anticipated fruitful Anglo-American cooperation at the peace conference. The United States thanked Italy and Greece for their contributions and urged that wartime unity guide postwar reconstruction, including a new international order protecting the rights and security of small powers.
The team played with better energy but allowed neutral-zone odd-man rushes and suffered bad breaks. They must adjust defensively, stay resilient, and win the next road game in Detroit.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell architecture introduces hardware and software improvements for ray tracing, neural rendering, video, display, scheduling, and power efficiency.

Fourth-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput over the prior generation and add hardware support for Mega Geometry and Linear Swept Spheres. Mega Geometry enables full-fidelity ray tracing of highly detailed, dynamically changing geometry through cluster-level acceleration structures, batched GPU-driven BVH management, and partitioned top-level acceleration structures. It supports DirectX 12, Vulkan, and OptiX across RTX GPUs beginning with Turing, with additional Blackwell hardware optimizations. Linear Swept Spheres accelerate strand-like geometry such as hair, providing about twice the performance and one-fifth the geometry memory of triangle-based DOTS. Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 improves workload coherence, reduces reordering overhead, and accelerates divergent ray-tracing and neural-shading workloads.

The AI Management Processor is a programmable RISC-V GPU context scheduler that reduces CPU scheduling dependence, latency, and workload contention. It coordinates graphics and AI tasks, supports Windows Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling, and aims to improve frame consistency and responsiveness.

Blackwell adds hardware encoding and decoding for 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC video. Ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality, adds an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, and supports multiple encoders; the RTX 5090 includes three encoders and two decoders. Sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed. DisplayPort 2.1b with UHBR 20 provides up to 80 Gbps and supports 8K at 165 Hz or 4K at 480 Hz with display stream compression.

Power-efficiency features include finer clock, power, and rail gating; separate GPU-core and memory voltage rails; complete memory clock-tree gating; and clocks that adjust to workloads 1,000 times faster than previous architectures. Blackwell enters its deepest sleep state ten times faster than Ada, with cited power savings of up to 50% in small-language-model inference scenarios.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, capable of generating up to three frames per traditionally rendered frame. Its model is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and runs once per rendered frame. GPU-based Flip Metering improves frame pacing. Transformer-based models replace prior convolutional models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, improving temporal stability, motion detail, lighting quality, and artifact reduction.

Blackwell also expands neural shaders through Cooperative Vectors APIs for DirectX 12 and Vulkan, giving graphics shaders access to Tensor Cores. Applications include neural materials, neural texture compression, radiance caching, subsurface scattering for skin, and generative facial rendering. Neural texture compression can substantially reduce memory use, while Neural Radiance Cache estimates multi-bounce indirect lighting from partially traced rays.

The flagship GB202 GPU contains 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT Cores, and 768 Tensor Cores, and is used by the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 contains 45.6 billion transistors and 10,752 CUDA cores for the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 contains 31 billion transistors and 6,400 CUDA cores for the RTX 5070.

E. B. Woolf & Company sued Alfred Hamburger for commissions on the sale of his printing plant. The evidence supported findings that Hamburger employed the brokers and sold to a purchaser they procured, making them the efficient procuring cause despite interrupted negotiations. A broker earns commissions by producing a ready and willing purchaser or procuring the eventual sale. Because testimony placed customary commissions between 2.5 and 5 percent, the trial court erred by awarding less than either rate based on its own judgment rather than record evidence. Although plaintiffs had not preserved objections concerning damages, the Appellate Court could enter the proper judgment. The judgment was reversed and judgment entered for $750.

The global 3D animation market is projected to reach approximately USD 20.5 billion by 2022, growing at about 12% CAGR from 2016. Growth is driven by visual effects in movies, demand for 3D mobile applications, GPS mapping, gaming, architecture and education, while limited financing restrains the market. Media and entertainment is the fastest-growing end-user sector. North America leads the market, Asia-Pacific is expected to rise sharply, and Europe is growing through automotive and aerospace adoption. Segments include software, hardware, services and end-users.

The author argues that understanding Nigeria’s ethnic and political history is essential to nation-building and effective opposition. Nigeria is portrayed as a collection of distinct ethnicities shaped by colonial structures, regional divisions, religion, language and differing legal traditions. Ahmadu Bello, Nnamdi Azikiwe and Obafemi Awolowo represented broadly confederal, unitary and federal visions respectively, while political alliances frequently crossed regional and ethnic boundaries.

The passage traces how competition among parties, minority demands, the 1966 coup, state creation and successive civilian and military governments shaped political identities. It identifies several Northern traditions, including conservative oligarchs, nationalists, Aminu Kano’s radicals and Middle Belt nationalists. It argues that a Northern power oligarchy persists but does not represent all Northerners, many of whom have supported nationalist parties or opposed Buhari.

The author rejects assumptions of a unified South and warns against portraying all members of any ethnicity as sharing one agenda. Citing past electoral alliances and conflicts, the passage advocates a diverse, nationwide opposition rather than ethnic solidarity, superficial unity or party-centred mobilization. It concludes that Nigeria must recognize and understand its differences while building national political coalitions.

Youth suicide remains a major concern in China despite declining overall suicide rates. School-based gatekeeper programs train teachers, parents, peers, and staff to identify warning signs, communicate effectively, and refer at-risk students, but evidence regarding effects on suicidal and gatekeeper behaviors remains inconclusive. China lacks rigorously evaluated, culturally adapted programs for secondary-school teachers and parents, while parental migration, limited school mental health services, and shortages of qualified counselors create additional challenges.

This study used the Delphi method to support development of the first evidence-based, localized Chinese suicide gatekeeper training program. Initial content was derived from literature searches, consultations with school counselors and suicide-prevention experts, and working-group review. The proposed program covered adolescent suicide, suicide misconceptions, risk factors and warning signs, communication, risk assessment, safety planning, teacher- or parent-specific support and referral, and barriers to help-seeking and gatekeeper behavior.

Experts with relevant experience in crisis intervention, psychiatry, psychotherapy, psychology research, school counseling, or crisis-line work independently rated statements through two online rounds conducted from September to November 2022. Participants received group feedback, could revise ratings, and could propose additional statements. Items achieving substantial consensus were retained, while low- or conflicting-rated items were discarded. The study received approval from Tsinghua University’s institutional review board.

The lecture reviews Wald’s equality and stopping trials. A stopping trial \(J\) must be determined from observations available through trial \(n\); with IID variables of mean \(\bar X\) and finite \(E[J]\), Wald’s equality gives \(E[S_J]=\bar X E[J]\). For a renewal process, \(N(t)+1\), the index of the first arrival after \(t\), is a stopping trial, whereas \(N(t)\) is not. Applying Wald’s equality yields a lower bound on \(E[N(t)]\). The elementary renewal theorem states that \(E[N(t)]/t\) converges to \(1/\bar X\); its upper bound is established by truncating inter-renewal times.

Generalized stopping trials may depend on paired arrival and service variables. In a G/G/1 queue, the first arrival to an empty system begins a new busy period and acts as a renewal because subsequent inter-arrival and service times are independent of the past. Departures alone do not form a renewal process because servers may be idle. Renewal points must occur at arrivals to an empty system, not when the system first becomes empty.

Little’s theorem follows by equating the integral of the number of customers in the system with the sum of their waiting times. In time-average form, it gives \(\bar L=\lambda\bar W\), provided the relevant limits exist.

For an M/G/1 queue, the Pollaczek–Khinchin formula gives mean queueing delay as
\[
\bar W_q=\frac{\lambda E[V^2]}{2(1-\rho)},\qquad \rho=\lambda E[V].
\]
Delay grows as utilization approaches one and can be infinite when the service-time second moment is infinite. The derivation combines residual service time, independence of queued customers’ service times, and Little’s theorem.

The speaker is disappointed the coach chose another goalie but accepts the decision and will support Snowy and the team while preparing to play if needed. He says the coach regularly changes goaltenders after poor games, so he does not feel scapegoated. He acknowledges allowing a disappointing fourth goal but says the entire team played poorly against a strong opponent. He describes a supportive relationship with Snowy and emphasizes that necessary adjustments do not mean the team is panicking.

Authorities are investigating a fire that destroyed South Carolina Circuit Judge Diane Goodstein’s beachfront home on Edisto Island. At least three family members were injured after occupants jumped from the elevated first floor and were rescued by kayak. Goodstein’s husband, former state legislator Arnold Goodstein, was airlifted to a hospital. Goodstein recently temporarily blocked the state Election Commission from sharing voter registration information with the federal government, but the state Supreme Court reversed her order. An reported explosion may have resulted from the fire reaching nearby vehicles.

The study proposes generating and detecting effective magnetic monopoles on three-dimensional topological-insulator surfaces using scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy. A radially distributed electric field from the STM tip induces circulating Hall currents through the topological magnetoelectric effect, producing magnetic fields equivalent to a pair of opposite image monopoles. These fields interact with the orbital magnetic moments of image potential states (IPS), reducing their degeneracy and causing Zeeman-like energy-level splitting.

Experiments compared topologically trivial √3-Bi, two-dimensional topological-insulator Bi(110), and three-dimensional higher-order topological-insulator Bi(111). IPS peaks on √3-Bi and Bi(110) showed no comparable splitting, consistent with cancellation of surface currents in the two-dimensional limit. On Bi(111), IPS levels above the first state displayed sub-peak splitting, including two resolved components for the second level. The splitting lacked thickness and terrace-size dependence, which the authors use to exclude quantum-well, quantum-confinement, and symmetric–antisymmetric IPS explanations. Similar but smaller splitting was observed in seven-layer Bi₂Se₃.

The measured dependence of splitting on principal quantum number broadly matched an electron–dyon model in which orbital magnetic moments couple to the monopole field. Increasing tunneling current strengthened the tip electric field and changed the splitting according to the predicted field-emission relationship; extrapolation toward zero field caused the split levels to recombine. The authors conclude that these observations strongly support electric-field generation, detection, and manipulation of magnetic-monopole-like fields on three-dimensional topological-insulator surfaces.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell architecture adds hardware encoding and decoding for 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC video, balancing lower data requirements than 4:4:4 with twice the color resolution of 4:2:0. Ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality, introduces AV1 Ultra High Quality mode, and supports faster exports through multiple encoders. Sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed. DisplayPort 2.1b provides up to 80 Gbps and supports 8K at 165 Hz or 4K at 480 Hz with DSC.

Max-Q improvements include finer power, clock, memory, and voltage-rail gating; clocks that adapt to workloads 1,000 times faster; and deep sleep entry 10 times faster than Ada. These changes can reduce power use by up to 50% in a cited small-language-model inference example.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame. Its frame-generation model is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than the previous method. Enhanced Flip Metering improves frame pacing. Transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA use twice as many parameters as prior CNN models, improving temporal stability, motion detail, lighting, anti-aliasing, and reducing ghosting and denoising artifacts.

Blackwell introduces developer-created neural shaders through Tensor Core access in DX12 and Vulkan shaders. Applications include neural materials, neural texture compression, radiance caching, subsurface scattering for skin, and generative facial rendering. Neural texture compression reduces memory use and can provide up to seven-to-one compression over block-compressed formats. Neural Radiance Cache estimates multi-bounce indirect lighting from partially traced rays.

The flagship GB202 GPU contains 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, and a 512-bit memory interface; it underpins the RTX 5090. GB203 contains 45.6 billion transistors and 10,752 CUDA cores for the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 contains 31 billion transistors and 6,400 CUDA cores for the RTX 5070. NVIDIA states that specifications may change and products require customer testing for intended uses.

Janney Montgomery Scott raised Pacira Pharmaceuticals’ price target from $31 to $34 while maintaining a neutral rating. Across analysts, the stock had one sell, seven hold and seven buy ratings, with a consensus target of $63.58. Shares opened at $32.30, with a $1.21 billion market capitalization. Pacira reported quarterly EPS of $0.20, beating the expected loss of $0.02, while revenue rose 10% year over year to $68.4 million. The company had a 13.37% negative net margin and a 1.52% negative return on equity. Several institutional investors increased their holdings. Pacira develops, manufactures and commercializes products using DepoFoam drug-delivery technology, focusing primarily on non-opioid postsurgical pain control.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K on May 21, 2020, announcing financial results for the quarter ended April 26, 2020. The filing includes a press release and CFO commentary as exhibits, both furnished rather than filed under applicable securities laws. CFO Colette M. Kress signed the report.

The patent concerns image encoding and decoding using motion-vector refinement to improve inter-prediction compression efficiency and reduce computational complexity. A current block’s initial L0 and L1 motion vectors are refined through merge-mode-based or prediction-block-based methods, then used to generate a prediction block or encode motion-compensation information. Refinement may involve motion-vector differences within a search area, with mirroring or scaling based on picture-order-count differences between reference and target pictures. Magnitude, direction, pixel-unit, initial-vector, and method-availability information may be entropy-coded.

Prediction-block-based refinement may be restricted to bidirectional merge prediction, equal reference-picture POC differences, and blocks meeting specified size requirements. Search areas may extend from −2 to 2 integer-pixel positions horizontally and vertically. Blocks larger than 16 in either dimension may be divided into 16×16 sub-blocks for refinement. Candidate vectors can be evaluated using SAD, SATD, SSE, or MSE distortion measures.

The described encoder performs intra- or inter-prediction, residual generation, transformation, quantization, entropy encoding, reconstruction, filtering, and reference-picture storage. The decoder reverses these operations to reconstruct images. Images may be hierarchically partitioned into coding units using quad-tree, binary-tree, and ternary-tree structures, with partition signaling dependent on block size, depth, and permitted structures.

Inter prediction supports AMVP, merge, skip, and current-picture-reference modes. Motion information can be derived from spatially neighboring or temporally collocated blocks and may include motion vectors, reference-picture indices, prediction directions, and merge indices. Merge candidates are added to candidate lists according to predetermined availability and priority rules. The generated bitstream may be stored on a non-transitory recording medium or transmitted through wired or wireless media.

The passage argues that INF policy should prioritize NATO cohesion and U.S. credibility over missile numbers. Maintaining the zero-zero position too long could threaten alliance unity because the Soviets will not eliminate all SS-20s and key allies may resist deployment unless the United States narrows the negotiating gap. The United States should therefore offer flexible alternatives while retaining zero-zero as its ideal objective, preferably soon after the March 6 German election. A reasonable proposal could preserve deployment credibility, reduce SS-20s, strengthen NATO, and support broader U.S.-Soviet dialogue.

Shultz proposes intensified dialogue with Moscow to test Andropov’s intentions, promote allied unity, address arms control, regional conflicts, human rights, and cautiously improve bilateral economic relations, potentially leading to a summit. Clark expresses reservations, warning that piecemeal U.S. concessions might produce no meaningful Soviet response, weaken leverage, raise public expectations, increase pressure for further concessions, and undermine a firm policy, especially since Soviet activism is largely public propaganda while diplomatic dialogue is usually private.
GMR Infrastructure reported a Rs565.94 crore net loss for the December 2017 quarter, versus a Rs643.44 crore profit a year earlier, as operating income and expenses declined.

An inside day occurs when a trading bar’s high is below the previous bar’s high and its low is above the previous bar’s low, placing all price action within the prior range. It can occur across time frames and markets, with frequency affected by volatility, overnight gaps, and trading hours. Its opposite, an outside day, has both a higher high and lower low.

Backtests found that inside days alone poorly predict subsequent movements. Since 1993, SPY recorded 779 inside days, about 10% of sessions. Buying all inside days produced only modest gains. Adding a five-day RSI below 50 increased the average gain to 0.1% but remained untradeable. Another S&P 500 swing strategy generated 89 trades, averaging 0.45% with a 2.1 profit factor, but worked only in equities and performed oppositely in gold. Two consecutive inside days produced only 22 trades. Overall, additional variables are needed to make inside-day strategies potentially useful.

Google is testing Chrome’s first UI changes in two years through the Windows Canary build behind an experimental flag. Updates include near-rectangular tabs with rounded corners, a brighter active tab, a rounded address bar, and account-related interface elements. Internal Chromium documents reportedly show further changes, including moving the new-tab button left of the address bar. It remains unclear when these features will reach Chrome’s stable build; Canary version 68 is scheduled for production in late July.

Tesla’s unaudited Form 10-Q covers the quarter ended June 30, 2017. The company operates automotive and energy generation and storage segments.

Second-quarter revenue rose to $2.79 billion from $1.27 billion a year earlier, including $2.29 billion in automotive revenue and $286.8 million from energy generation and storage. Gross profit was $666.6 million. Tesla reported a $240.9 million operating loss and a $336.4 million net loss attributable to common stockholders, or $2.04 per share. For the first six months, revenue was $5.49 billion and the attributable net loss was $666.7 million.

At June 30, Tesla had $26.04 billion in assets, including $3.04 billion in cash, $2.44 billion in inventory, and $8.40 billion in property and equipment. Total liabilities were $19.46 billion, while stockholders’ equity was $5.11 billion. Debt principal totaled $8.10 billion. Tesla remained compliant with its debt covenants.

During the first half, operating activities used $270.0 million and investing activities used $2.14 billion, primarily reflecting $1.51 billion in property and equipment purchases. Financing activities provided $2.03 billion. Cash declined by $357.3 million.

Tesla acquired Grohmann Engineering in January 2017 for $109.5 million in cash to improve manufacturing speed and efficiency. It continued finalizing valuation estimates related to its November 2016 acquisition of SolarCity for $2.1 billion in stock.

In March 2017, Tesla issued $977.5 million of 2.375% convertible notes due in 2022 and raised approximately $399.6 million through a common-stock offering. It also exchanged $144.8 million of 2018 convertible notes for approximately 1.16 million shares.

The company held $603.5 million in customer deposits. Resale value guarantee liabilities totaled $2.72 billion, and the maximum potential repurchase obligation to leasing partners was $1.09 billion. Tesla identified dependence on predominantly single-source suppliers as a material risk.

Construction in progress included vehicle manufacturing equipment and Gigafactory projects. Tesla had capitalized $1.98 billion for Gigafactory 1. Its Buffalo manufacturing arrangement requires specified employment and investment milestones, with potential annual payments of $41.2 million for noncompliance.

Tesla disclosed securities, SolarCity acquisition, and government-related legal proceedings, stating that it intended to defend claims it considered without merit. As of July 31, 2017, 166,887,023 common shares were outstanding.

Heating oil is a low-viscosity crude-oil product used mainly to heat buildings. Demand rises in colder weather, making it seasonal, though the passage reports stronger futures performance from February through August, possibly because buyers prepare ahead of winter.

Heating oil futures are contracts to buy or sell a specified quantity at a future date and pre-agreed price. They trade as UHO on ICE Futures Europe and HO on CME Globex. Each contract represents 42,000 gallons, or 1,000 barrels, quoted in U.S. dollars per gallon. The minimum fluctuation is $0.0001 per gallon, equal to $4.20 per contract, and the block minimum is 25 contracts. ICE contracts are cash-settled, while CME contracts use physical delivery. Trading ends on the last business day before the contract month.

A trading strategy may combine technical and fundamental analysis, position sizing, and risk management. A cited backtest produced 168 trades, averaging $370 per trade, with a 2.02 profit factor and 59% win rate. Futures can be used for speculation, hedging, arbitrage, and portfolio diversification. Leveraged adverse price movements are identified as the primary risk.

Prices are influenced by weather, crude oil prices, refinery capacity, and alternative heating-fuel costs. The cited all-time high was $5.2215 per gallon in April 2022, and the low was $0.2920 in February 1999. Heating oil exposure is also available through CFDs and WisdomTree’s HEAT ETF.

Damages for a whaling vessel’s unlawful detention are direct losses, comparable to demurrage, rather than speculative profits. Unlike trading vessels, whalers depend on brief seasonal opportunities, so detention can eliminate an entire year’s returns and the crew’s lay-based compensation. The Cape Horn Pigeon’s detention caused an unprofitable voyage and left its crew indebted. Established practice values the lost use of fishing vessels according to their character and employment, using average catch as the best evidence. This measure compensates owners for the vessel, equipment, and crew devoted to whaling and includes the crew’s proportional losses. Similar reasoning appeared in the Williams case and the Costa Rica Packet arbitration, where the arbitrator recognized that unjustified detention caused Captain Carpenter to miss the best whaling season, while noting limits on proven subsequent losses.

Bottoms pled guilty to theft by receiving and financial transaction card theft and received ten years’ probation conditioned on restitution. The court properly continued the restitution hearing to secure victims’ attendance. However, restitution could cover only damages caused by the offenses charged, not all property taken during uncharged burglaries. The judgment was reversed and remanded for lawful resentencing; the remaining alleged error was moot.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that on June 4, 2018, it entered a definitive agreement to acquire GitHub for $7.5 billion. The filing includes a press release and investor presentation as exhibits. Microsoft and GitHub representatives planned to present transaction information to investors beginning that day.

Strength training builds muscle mass, strength and endurance, but poor technique, inadequate warm-ups, repetitive movements and lifting beyond current ability can cause injuries. Common problems include rotator cuff injuries, hamstring strains or tears, herniated discs, tendonitis, and tennis or golfer’s elbow.

Risk can be reduced by using correct form, maintaining good posture, stretching appropriately, limiting repetitive forceful movements, increasing workout intensity gradually and allowing sufficient recovery. Warm-ups raise heart rate and blood flow, preparing muscles for exercise; dynamic, full-range movements are recommended before training. Static stretches are more suitable during the cool-down, which helps regulate blood flow after exercise.

Do not exercise through pain. Stop, rest and seek medical advice if discomfort persists. Treatment may include rest, pain relief, physiotherapy, injections or surgery, depending on the injury and its severity. Ice, compression and elevation may help initially, while hydration and a good diet can support recovery. Consulting a qualified fitness instructor before beginning a new routine can help ensure exercises are performed safely and the programme is achievable.

Jonathan Toews and Patrick Kane said the team values goals from any player but expects its offensive leaders to contribute. They described the Stanley Cup Final as a competitive, evolving series requiring smarter two-way play, patience, puck possession and limiting Tampa’s speed and playmaking. Both welcomed returning home, where they expect strong fan support.

Toews praised Duncan Keith’s heavy workload and contributions in every situation, Corey Crawford’s accountability and ability to rebound, and Teuvo Teravainen’s continued development despite limited opportunities. Teravainen said he is learning from the team’s experienced players and is unconcerned about which opposing goaltender starts. The players expressed confidence in different line combinations and in supporting teammates receiving new opportunities. Kane said he will continue making the right play rather than focusing on increasing his shot total.

The speaker expects varied offensive and defensive matchups against the deep, skilled Devils but considers line matching less important than skating and executing the game plan. Discipline and special teams are vital, particularly early when referees discourage retaliation and stick fouls. Both teams have strong power plays and penalty killing, while success requires confidence, reading the defense and directing pucks toward Brodeur.

The team’s four lines contributed energy, net traffic and strong neutral-zone pressure, disrupting passes and containing the Devils outside. After narrowly avoiding a potential turning point, the team responded in the third period, with Sakic winning a key faceoff and Bourque scoring the winning goal. Leadership, tenacity, skill and experience helped the team overcome adversity. Nieminen and Hinote pressured the net effectively, and the speaker praised the officiating while stating that Adam Foote appeared to be a marked man.

Spin diffusion length is crucial for spintronic devices and can be strongly altered by electric-field-driven spin drift. Existing drift-diffusion models may be inaccurate in systems where spatial spin precession is important, while other approaches often use simplified Hamiltonians and scattering treatments.

The authors extend their ab initio spin-diffusion framework to electric fields along periodic directions using a covariant-derivative formalism.
