The system can include a gas source, humidification chamber, chamber and conduit heaters, inspiratory and optional expiratory conduits, patient interface, and temperature, flow, humidity, or ambient sensors. By determining whether incoming gas is ambient and relatively humid or compressed and dry, the controller adjusts operating parameters to provide desired humidity, improve comfort, and reduce condensation. User interfaces may request gas-source selection, display automatic determinations, verify user choices, and issue mismatch alerts. A safety or default mode may operate before configuration confirmation.

The MSPM0C1105/1106 integrate a calibrated ADC-connected temperature sensor, 32kHz low-frequency subsystem with RTC and independent watchdog, selectable 1.4V/2.5V or external voltage references, comparator, security firewalls, and CRC-16. Communications include three UARTs, I2C supporting up to 1Mbps and SMBus 3.0, and SPI supporting up to 16Mbits/s; interfaces include FIFOs and DMA support. Supervisory functions comprise independent and windowed watchdog timers. The RTC provides calendar, alarms, periodic interrupts, calibration, and temperature-drift compensation. General-purpose and advanced 16-bit timers support prescaling, synchronization, triggering, PWM, capture/compare, and fault handling.

IOMUX controls peripheral selection, signal paths, and shutdown wake-up. An Arm-compatible two-wire SWD debug subsystem supports peripheral debug behavior, mailbox communication, GPIO reuse, lockout, and password-authenticated debugging. Read-only factory memory stores device identification, capabilities, trim data, and calibration constants.

Typical designs should place 10µF and 0.1µF low-ESR decoupling capacitors near supply pins, connect NRST to a 47kΩ pullup and 1000pF pulldown capacitor, provide crystal capacitors where applicable, and use pullups with 5V-tolerant open-drain outputs. TI distinguishes experimental “X” parts from qualified “MSP” production parts and recommends only qualified devices for production. Revision A removed the DGS32 package, updated multiple specifications and CPU information, added DEBUGSS, and revised device-identification tables. Packaging guidance requires soldering thermal pads to the PCB and provides optional via and stencil recommendations.

Tesla introduced stripped-down Model Y and Model 3 Standard versions priced at $39,990 and $36,990, about $5,000 below Premium models but not enough to offset the canceled $7,500 federal tax credit. Analyst Joseph Yoon doubts the roughly 10 percent reduction will attract many new EV buyers, suggesting a price closer to $30,000 would be more compelling.

Cost reductions include fewer luxury materials and features. The Model Y Standard has smaller wheels, limited colors, no rear touchscreen, slower acceleration, and an estimated 321-mile range versus 363 miles for the Premium model. The Model 3 Standard also loses luxury touches and its rear touchscreen. Tesla’s supervised Full Self-Driving system remains available for an additional $8,000.

Tesla’s global sales are down 6 percent year over year. Musk has increasingly emphasized autonomous vehicles, robotics, and humanoid robots as the company’s future.

A Connecticut study combining genomic surveillance, epidemiological modeling, viral copy measurements, and vaccination metadata examined sequential Omicron lineage replacement from January 2022 to January 2023. BA.1 caused an estimated 1.5 million infections, while BA.2, BA.4, and BA.5 caused over 2.1 million combined infections; XBB caused about 0.4 million through January 2023. BA.1 replaced its predecessor fastest, while later replacements generally slowed as population immunity increased.

Variant fitness reflected differing combinations of intrinsic transmissibility and immune escape rather than a single determinant. BA.2 displaced BA.1 largely through higher viral copy numbers and transmissibility. BA.4 and BA.5 replaced BA.2 despite lower viral copy numbers, indicating a stronger role for immune escape. XBB combined extensive immune escape with higher viral copy numbers than late-stage BA.5. Vaccine-breakthrough analyses found significant evidence of enhanced immune escape for BA.1 compared with Delta, but results for later lineages were weaker or not statistically significant.

The authors propose a conceptual model in which successive lineages exploit changing antigenic and transmission niches created by vaccination, prior infections, and waning immunity. They conclude that linking genomic data with laboratory, clinical, and epidemiological information can help assess emerging variant fitness and inform surveillance for SARS-CoV-2 and other pathogens. Limitations include dependence on Connecticut’s population characteristics, selection of samples by diagnostic Ct thresholds, and use of Ct values as proxies for infectious viral burden.

GAO examined comprehensive support and improvement (CSI) schools, their improvement plans, and Department of Education oversight under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act. Using 2019–2020 federal data and a nationally generalizable sample of plans, GAO found that roughly 5,200 CSI schools served 2.5 million students and disproportionately enrolled low-income and Black students. These schools had substantially lower math and reading proficiency rates and slightly higher student-teacher ratios than other public schools.

GAO estimated that 42 percent of CSI plans appeared to address all three reviewed requirements: a school-level needs assessment, identification of resource inequities, and inclusion of evidence-based interventions. About 73 percent addressed needs assessments, 52 percent identified resource inequities, and 86 percent included at least one intervention. School and district officials reported difficulty understanding and implementing these requirements.

Education identified state compliance problems through routine and targeted monitoring, but allowed monitored states and districts to select plans for review. GAO recommended that Education independently select CSI plans to better assess state oversight. Education agreed and stated it would begin doing so in spring 2024.

Periyar University published its 2017 UG and PG examination results on periyaruniversity.ac.in and through affiliated colleges. Students can check results using their registration number and date of birth. Re-totalling and revaluation applications are accepted within 10 days, costing Rs 200 and Rs 250 respectively; answer-sheet copies cost Rs 250.

Japan’s high life expectancy and ageing population have prompted pension and employment reforms, but little is known about how older individuals perceive their survival prospects. Subjective Survival Probability (SSP) predicts mortality independently of self-rated health and may vary by gender, socioeconomic position, employment, and working conditions.

The study examines SSP among people aged 50 and older in Japan, distinguishing employment status from the nature and quality of work. Japanese policies have gradually raised pension eligibility from 60 to 65 and encouraged employers to retain older workers. Many companies use post-retirement non-regular contracts rather than raising mandatory retirement ages, while older people may also be self-employed, engaged in domestic work, or outside employment. The health implications of these late-career arrangements remain unclear.

The study also considers working time and job satisfaction. Japan has comparatively long working hours, while job satisfaction is associated with health, scheduling control, work-life balance, age discrimination, workplace support, earnings, and relationships with colleagues. Long hours appear particularly harmful to workers reporting low job satisfaction.

Identified research gaps include confusion between work and employment, inconsistent definitions of job satisfaction, and limited evidence on relationships among employment categories, job satisfaction, and SSP. The study investigates whether SSP differs by employment status, job satisfaction, working time, and employment category, and whether demographic, socioeconomic, and health adjustments alter these relationships.

Data come from four waves of the Japanese Study of Aging and Retirement, collected in 2007, 2009, 2011, and 2013 across ten cities. The dataset contains 16,932 observations from 7,082 respondents. SSP is measured through respondents’ estimated probability of surviving to specified ages from 75 to 110; responses cluster at selected percentages and vary most meaningfully around ages 80 to 95.

Telltale Games confirmed that an original IP remains in development, though it is not among its immediate projects and no genre or story details were revealed. Communications head Job Stauffer highlighted possibilities involving VR and streaming services. The company also plans to expand its narrative games beyond consoles, mobile devices, and PCs to services and devices already present in millions of homes, potentially including set-top boxes and streaming platforms. More details are expected during the summer. With up to 400 employees, Telltale can handle four projects simultaneously and is currently producing additional Game of Thrones, Minecraft, and Guardians of the Galaxy episodes, alongside several unannounced projects.

This study examined sodium homeostasis in structural connectivity hubs and epileptogenic regions in drug-resistant focal epilepsy using 7T anatomical, diffusion, and sodium MRI alongside stereoelectroencephalography. Analyses included 23 patients and 21 matched healthy controls. Structural connectomes defined hubs, while intracranial recordings classified brain parcels as epileptogenic, propagation, non-involved, or unexplored zones.

Patients had higher total sodium concentration (TSC) than controls across epileptogenic and non-epileptogenic regions. TSC was also higher in structural hubs than non-hubs in both groups and correlated with the extent of the epileptogenic network. The sodium signal fraction, f, did not differ globally between groups or between hubs and non-hubs. However, f was increased specifically within epileptogenic zones and reduced in other patient regions relative to controls. Epilepsy-related sodium changes did not depend on hub status. Ten of 23 patients had overlap between structural hubs and epileptogenic zones; sodium abnormalities were more pronounced in patients without such overlap, although group differences were not statistically significant.

The authors conclude that elevated TSC in hubs likely reflects regional microstructure or nonspecific loss of tissue integrity rather than epilepsy-specific hub vulnerability. Increased f within epileptogenic zones may indicate susceptibility to homeostatic failure associated with abnormal rhythm generation. Limitations include possible cerebrospinal-fluid partial-volume effects and difficulty separating hub status from anatomical location.

The lecture examines entry by allowing the number of firms to be determined endogenously. Potential entrants pay a sunk fixed cost, then compete through mechanisms such as Bertrand, Cournot, or search-based pricing. Backward induction determines post-entry profits and the equilibrium number of firms. Lower entry costs generally increase entry, while observed profits largely reflect how many firms the market can support rather than markups alone. In some models, larger markets support both more and larger firms.

For homogeneous goods, the first-best outcome has one firm pricing at marginal cost, while the second-best chooses the number of firms given equilibrium competition. Entry is generally excessive because an entrant captures sales from incumbent firms as well as generating additional output. This “business stealing” makes private entry incentives exceed social benefits, though integer constraints can produce one firm too few. In a linear Cournot example, only a small fraction of an entrant’s output represents added market output; the remainder displaces incumbent sales.

With differentiated goods, entry may be either excessive or insufficient. Business stealing lowers incumbent profits, while new products may raise consumer surplus through improved matches. In a Hotelling-circle example, equilibrium entry is twice the socially optimal level because all entrant demand is taken from existing firms, despite improved consumer-product matching. Insufficient entry is more plausible when new products generate substantial utility from close matches or serve consumers who otherwise would not purchase.

In vertical differentiation, Shaked and Sutton distinguish natural oligopoly from specialization. When one high-quality product is efficient for all consumers, only finitely many firms can survive even as entry costs approach zero. When different qualities are efficient for different consumer types, increasingly many specialized products can coexist as entry costs decline.

The lecture then discusses Jovanovic’s model of firm dynamics. Entrants do not initially know their permanent productivity and learn from noisy production outcomes. Firms with favorable beliefs produce more, while firms with unfavorable but uncertain beliefs produce little to gather information; firms with sufficiently unfavorable and precise beliefs exit. The model predicts that small firms grow faster but fail more often, large firms are more profitable, and concentration is correlated with both profit levels and profit dispersion because industries differ in realized firm costs rather than solely because competition affects markups.

Finally, Vellodi’s model applies this learning framework to rating intermediaries such as Amazon and Yelp. New firms may receive few customers and reviews, slowing learning about their quality and discouraging entry. Firms may price below cost to attract customers and obtain reviews. A consumer-oriented platform may optimally reveal ratings only partially, withholding some information about highly rated firms. This raises the relative value of achieving a moderately good reputation and strengthens new firms’ incentives to attract reviews and establish their quality.

IDT Corporation held its Q4 and full fiscal year 2025 earnings call on September 29, 2025. CEO Shmuel Jonas and CFO Marcelo Fischer were scheduled to discuss financial and operational results for the three- and 12-month periods ended July 31, 2025, followed by questions. The company cautioned that forward-looking statements involve risks and noted that referenced non-GAAP measures are reconciled to GAAP figures in its earnings release.

Tong Hâk rebels condemn Japanese and foreign influence, warn of national collapse, and call on millions of Koreans to unite, expel outsiders, and support loyal, patriotic leaders. They present their struggle as an obligation of loyalty, filial piety, and fidelity to the state. Japanese Consul Sugimura reports that Tong Hâk forces are traveling from Chulla Do and Kyung-sang Do toward Seoul and advises Japanese residents to prepare to evacuate women and children to Chemulpo. A message to Japanese merchants invokes Chinese moral principles, accuses Japan of interference, conflict, and murder, recalls Japan’s 1592 invasion of Korea, and urges the Japanese to choose peace rather than face divine condemnation and danger.

Britain’s first carbon-neutral new-build church opened in Walsingham in 2006, using solar panels, borehole heat exchange, and reused stone. A planned PassivHaus church in Sheffield featured solar design, insulation, and reclaimed materials but was abandoned because of funding constraints when the congregation bought a nearby nightclub instead. Britain still lacks a PassivHaus church, unlike the United States and Canada.

Canon’s EOS 77D adds a 24.2-megapixel Dual Pixel CMOS sensor, 45-point autofocus, 80D metering, optional beginner interface, and low-energy Bluetooth. Positioned between the T7i and 80D, it offers better build quality and a top display but lacks weather sealing. Canon also introduced a smaller, slightly heavier EF-S 18-55mm f4-5.6 IS STM kit lens compatible with the PZ-E1 power-zoom adapter. Available April 2017, the 77D costs $900 body-only, $1,050 with the 18-55mm lens, or $1,500 with the 18-135mm lens.

Via Browser is a lightweight, fast, stable, and customizable Android browser maintained by an active developer. It can be installed from Google Play and requires storage and location permissions, which the developer explains. Users can enter searches or URLs from the homepage, change the default Google search engine, and enable pull-to-refresh in settings. Privacy features include enabled Do Not Track and ad blocking, disabled location access, and an Incognito Mode. Its tab interface provides quick access to open tabs and easy closing. The author recommends Via for its balance of speed, features, simplicity, and low resource use.

Frank Schilbach introduces behavioral economics as integrating psychology and other disciplines into economics to make models more realistic, predictive, and useful for policy. His research examines how poverty-related conditions—including financial constraints, sleep deprivation, pain, substance abuse, depression, and loneliness—affect behavior and productivity.

Standard economic models commonly assume stable, well-defined preferences; utility maximization; narrow self-interest; perfect self-control; exponential discounting; risk aversion over final outcomes; Bayesian information processing; and no intrinsic preference for particular beliefs. Behavioral economics studies important deviations from these assumptions, such as unstable or context-dependent preferences, limited attention and memory, information-processing constraints, self-control problems, motivated beliefs, social influences, concern for others, and demand for commitment.

Examples include New Year’s dieting intentions that fade, avoidance of diagnostic information about incurable diseases, large differences in organ donation caused by opt-in versus opt-out defaults, medication reminders improving adherence, charitable giving, and failures to notice unexpected events when attention is directed elsewhere. These cases suggest that the standard “homo economicus” model may be excessively rational, selfish, and willful.

Economic models are deliberately simplified and should be tractable, insightful, generalizable, falsifiable, empirically consistent, and predictive. Behavioral economics does not replace standard economics; it seeks manageable modifications that better explain significant behavior while retaining core principles such as incentives, markets, data, and mathematical modeling. Evidence discussed shows that financial incentives can have stronger and more persistent effects than moral appeals.

Laptop use illustrates the policy implications. Although laptops can facilitate note-taking and choice, they can distract users and others, encourage temptation, consume cognitive resources, and exploit overconfidence in multitasking. Research cited found that allowing computers reduced test scores. The course therefore uses an opt-in laptop section designed to limit externalities while avoiding a complete ban.

The course covers time, risk, reference-dependent, and social preferences; emotions and projection bias; limited attention; beliefs, learning, and motivated information avoidance; mental accounting; malleable preferences; happiness and mental health; discrimination; defaults, nudges, paternalism, and ethics; and behavioral perspectives on poverty and possible psychological poverty traps.

Coach DeBoer described a major injury as catastrophic but ultimately beneficial because it forced him to evaluate the organization’s young players and depth, helping guide later acquisitions. He said his veteran players need tactical preparation rather than inspirational speeches in the Stanley Cup Final. Limited power-play opportunities have disrupted special-teams rhythm, so the team must attack more and draw penalties.

DeBoer praised Melker’s consistency, intelligence, effort and growing offensive confidence. He said leadership decisions were difficult because the roster contains many strong leaders, but players set aside egos and embraced an inclusive approach. Despite extensive travel, the resilient group has never used fatigue as an excuse. DeBoer also said his prior assumptions about the team lacking character or leadership proved unfounded, describing its leaders as among the most professional, hardworking and inclusive people he has coached.

Automatic Local bus clock gating can prevent an edge-configured PIC input from returning to Idle if its source remains high or cycles while the clock is off. Subsequent interrupts may be missed, potentially causing hangs or other unexpected behavior.

High Prairie Elementary students learned to access ebooks through Overdrive, while Grade 6M elected Shayla Grey class prime minister. Classes pursued gardening, biographies, family interviews, Famous Five research, reading sequencing, mechanics, number sense, science experiments and Christmas concert preparation. Kindergarten students exchanged postcards internationally. Grade 5’s behavior-reward book sale sold out, and students organized Remembrance Day activities, poppy sales, Christmas Shoebox collections and assemblies. Students also completed Students Against Drunk Driving holiday bags and began the annual kindness campaign.

The passage describes traditional Russian sunburn remedies. Sour cream, yogurt, and kefir are used for redness and dryness; egg whites, nettle decoction, and watermelon juice for pain; sea buckthorn oil for peeling and chafing; potatoes, carrots, and pumpkins for itching; and sauerkraut for swelling. Additional treatments include soda-water bandages, soaked oatmeal, and a sour cream–lemon juice mask. Vitamin-rich fruits such as kiwi, oranges, pineapples, and strawberries are also recommended.

The Supreme Court denied Google’s request to temporarily preserve its Play Store policies while it seeks review of an antitrust case brought by Epic Games. A 2023 jury found Google unlawfully maintained an app-store monopoly, and a district court ordered it to permit independent payment systems and, by July 2026, greater competition from other app stores. The 9th Circuit upheld the verdict and injunction. Google argued the changes posed security risks, while Epic said courts had already rejected those concerns. Google must allow developers to use alternative payment systems later this month, though broader Android changes could be avoided if the Supreme Court eventually hears the case and rules for Google.

Academic code violations remain high at Brown, with over half occurring in computer science. In 2015-16, 49 undergraduates and seven graduate students were charged, receiving outcomes ranging from no violation to suspension or dismissal. The Academic Code committee seeks more faculty members because of its caseload. Prevention efforts include a required online tutorial, syllabus standards, collaboration policies, quizzes and international student orientation presentations. Computer science uses MOSS to detect programming similarities, though violations often involve unauthorized collaboration rather than direct copying. Furnishing answers is another common offense, with both students punished. International and first-year students are slightly overrepresented, potentially reflecting differing educational systems and expectations. The University is considering an academic integrity panel or week and a student-led honor code system, while emphasizing education, accountability and long-term student success.

On April 16, 2020, NVIDIA and Mellanox received Chinese antitrust approval for NVIDIA Holdings’ proposed acquisition of Mellanox, following approvals from the European Commission and Mexico and expiration of the U.S. waiting period. The transaction was expected to close around April 27, 2020, subject to customary closing conditions.

The Rancho Bernardo Kiwanis Club celebrated 50 years of community service. Founded in 1967 with 30 charter members, it supports local school service groups, Scouts, hospitals, parks, Romanian orphanage projects and Ronald McDonald House. Its annual pancake breakfast typically raises about $20,000. A $160,000 bequest from organizer Franklin Lenfesty established its nonprofit foundation. The 40-member club, led by John O’Rourke, reports helping more than 800,000 children since its founding.

Amazon has reduced the three-camera Netgear Arlo security system from £409.99 to £249.99 for 19 March. The expandable system offers battery-powered waterproof cameras, motion alerts, night vision, remote viewing, one week of free online storage, and Android, iPhone, browser and Alexa compatibility.

A retrospective cardiac magnetic resonance study of 15 adults with excessive left ventricular trabeculation separately measured the central cavity, intertrabecular recesses, trabeculations, and compact wall. Intertrabecular recesses had a higher ejection fraction than the central cavity (61±17% versus 44±16%, P<0.001), a finding supported by four-chamber analyses of 30 cases. Standard methods that count trabeculations as blood or exclude recesses from the blood pool biased ventricular volume and ejection-fraction estimates toward reduced function. Contouring trabeculations halved the number of patients classified with severely reduced ejection fraction, while trabeculation extent did not correlate with total ejection fraction. The authors conclude that contouring may improve assessment and clinical management, but the small, single-center, imaging-focused study requires large-scale validation.

NVIDIA’s fiscal 2019 Form 10-K covers the year ended January 27, 2019. The company develops GPU and Tegra processor platforms based on a unified architecture, serving gaming, professional visualization, datacenter, and automotive markets. Its products include GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, DGX, GRID, DRIVE, Clara, SHIELD, and Jetson. NVIDIA emphasizes GPU-accelerated computing, CUDA, artificial intelligence, ray tracing, cloud gaming, high-performance computing, and autonomous vehicles.

NVIDIA uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on third parties for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, packaging, memory, and other components. It sells through partners and directly to cloud and enterprise customers. International sales represented 87% of fiscal 2019 revenue, while 46% of employees were outside the United States. NVIDIA had 13,277 employees, including 9,486 in research and development. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $7.42 billion at fiscal year-end.

The company faces intense competition, rapid technological change, cybersecurity threats, product defects, dependence on suppliers, demand forecasting and inventory risks, international and regulatory uncertainty, intellectual-property disputes, privacy and tax exposure, litigation, talent retention challenges, and potential business disruptions. Fiscal 2019’s second-half revenue was weaker than the first half, including prolonged channel inventory sell-through for mid-range gaming GPUs.

As of February 15, 2019, NVIDIA had 606 million common shares outstanding. Non-affiliate voting stock had an aggregate market value of approximately $146.66 billion on July 27, 2018. Through January 27, 2019, NVIDIA had repurchased 260 million shares for $7.08 billion and retained authorization for an additional $7.24 billion. Its Nasdaq-listed common stock trades under NVDA.

Only four members remain on the 26-person National Council on the Humanities after the Trump administration fired most members. All remaining members were appointed by Trump. The council advises the National Endowment for the Humanities chair on grants, policy and funding.

Lois Riess, 56, is in Texas custody after a national manhunt, accused of killing her husband, David Riess, in Minnesota and Pamela Hutchinson, a woman resembling her, in Florida. Authorities allege Riess stole $11,000 from her husband, befriended Hutchinson, killed her and assumed her identity.

Riess faces second-degree murder, theft, vehicle theft and identity-related charges in Florida, and felony theft in Minnesota, where a murder charge is pending. A Texas judge ruled she may be extradited to either state; Florida may proceed first because its case is further advanced.

Florida prosecutors would need a grand jury indictment for first-degree murder to seek the death penalty. Authorities may consider trial order because a Minnesota murder conviction could support Florida’s death-penalty case, while Minnesota prosecutors may oppose allowing capital punishment.

Riess also has a history of gambling and alleged financial misconduct. Court records say she transferred money from her disabled sister’s guardianship account and spent some at a casino, though she was not charged. While fleeing, she gambled in Iowa and Louisiana.

Harvey Ulfers was sentenced to 33 months for defrauding Deere & Company through undervalued scrap metal sales. He must pay a $111,602 fine and $259,132 restitution. Co-conspirator Patrick Williams received 27 months and similar restitution.

The President reports that federal authority and property had been seized across several Southern states, which declared secession and formed the Confederacy. His administration initially pursued peaceful measures, seeking only to retain federal property, collect revenue, and preserve the Union through time, discussion, and elections. After attempts to provision Fort Sumter prompted its bombardment and surrender, he concluded that force was necessary to preserve the government.

The administration called militia, blockaded insurgent ports, expanded the Army and Navy, and authorized limited suspension of habeas corpus during the rebellion. The President asks Congress to ratify these emergency actions and provide at least 400,000 men and $400 million to make the conflict brief and decisive.

He rejects “armed neutrality” by border states and describes Virginia’s alliance with the Confederacy and military preparations as requiring federal action while obligating protection for loyal Virginians. He argues that secession is neither constitutional nor peaceful: states possess only powers reserved under the Constitution, have no lawful status outside the Union, and cannot claim a governmental power to destroy the government itself. Permitting secession would also undermine national debts, territorial obligations, majority rule, and the endurance of any government.

The conflict is presented as a test of whether constitutional popular government can survive internal rebellion. The Union’s purpose is described as preserving a government that advances equal opportunity and rests on the authority of the people. The President praises the loyalty of common soldiers and sailors and maintains that election results must be changed through later elections, not armed revolt. After suppressing the rebellion, he pledges to act under the Constitution and laws, preserve state and individual rights, and restore loyal citizens’ protections. He concludes that employing war powers was a regrettable but unavoidable duty necessary to prevent the government’s destruction.

Halimat Oniru leads Haleem Group, an Abuja-headquartered dredging and road construction company operating in Lagos, Delta, Bayelsa and Cross River. The company has created thousands of jobs, while Oniru also supports humanitarian causes.

Two Oceans Restaurant, a voluntary WWF-SASSI member in Table Mountain National Park, has stopped selling West Coast Rock Lobster after depleting existing stocks because the species was red-listed as unsustainable. SASSI reports that less than 2% remains. SANParks TMNP fully supports the conservation initiative.

President Biden said the United States had made substantial progress against COVID-19 but faced continued pressure from the Delta variant and nearly 80 million unvaccinated eligible Americans. He emphasized that vaccines strongly protect against severe illness and outlined a six-part response plan.

The plan required employers with at least 100 workers to mandate vaccination or weekly testing, expanded vaccination requirements for healthcare workers, federal employees, contractors, and Head Start educators, and required paid time off for vaccination. Biden also urged vaccination or testing requirements at entertainment venues and called on medical professionals to contact unvaccinated patients.

The administration prepared to distribute booster shots once authorized by federal health agencies. To protect schools, Biden promoted vaccination for eligible children and adults around younger children, called for teacher and staff mandates, and supported masking, testing, ventilation, and distancing. He pledged federal support for school officials facing state opposition.

The plan increased rapid-test production, reduced retail test prices, expanded free pharmacy testing, funded nearly 300 million tests, and doubled fines for travelers refusing to wear masks. It expanded disaster loans for small businesses, doubled deployable military health teams, and increased shipments of monoclonal antibody treatments.

Biden also pledged an equitable response, continued international vaccine donations, and further pandemic preparedness planning. He concluded that vaccination, testing, masking, science, and collective action could reduce hospitalizations and deaths, keep schools and businesses open, and strengthen the recovery.

Blockchain is a cryptographically secured distributed ledger governed by consensus. Its peer-to-peer structure, immutability, transparency, and support for smart contracts can enable transactions without trusted intermediaries. Permissionless blockchains allow anonymous participation, while permissioned blockchains restrict nodes through central or consortium oversight. Although technical blockchain research is expanding, its business value and disruptive potential remain contested.

The study examines how blockchain companies create and capture value through digital business models. It combines value-chain, value-network, and value-shop configurations with value creation and capture concepts. Using interviews and archival data, researchers conducted exploratory case studies of five Chinese companies operating permissioned consortium blockchains without tokens.

The analysis identifies five blockchain-inspired business models:

- **Platformer:** ChainArchitect improves blockchain architecture and provides an open platform for third-party applications. It captures value by seeking to become a foundational standard but faces compatibility problems with existing infrastructure.
- **Disintermediator:** ChainFinance uses blockchain for interbank transfers and cash management, reducing clearing costs and dependence on incumbents. Its challenge is resistance from established participants.
- **Transformer:** ChainNova develops tailored applications, including agricultural traceability systems, and seeks to transfer solutions across industries. Variations in organizational practices limit transferability.
- **Mediator:** ChainSecurity applies blockchain to asset-backed securities, improving transparency, risk assessment, pricing, and transaction management. Adoption requires incumbents to accept new rules and routines.
- **Co-innovator:** ChainDraft jointly develops applications such as an electronic draft-management system and earns licensing revenue from its proprietary platform. High development and maintenance costs constrain small-scale adoption.

Value appropriation occurs at ecosystem, conventional value-chain, or individual-organization levels. The study concludes that blockchain may both disrupt intermediaries and improve existing value chains and practices. Its findings are limited by the five-company Chinese sample and the exclusion of value-delivery architecture and stakeholder-network dimensions; further studies across other companies and countries could refine the typology.

Amazon.com’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2021 reported quarterly net sales of $113.1 billion, up 27% year over year, operating income of $7.7 billion, and net income of $7.8 billion, or $15.12 per diluted share. Six-month net sales were $221.6 billion, operating income was $16.6 billion, and net income was $15.9 billion.

Quarterly segment sales were $67.6 billion for North America, $30.7 billion for International, and $14.8 billion for AWS. Segment operating income was $3.1 billion, $362 million, and $4.2 billion, respectively. Growth reflected increased unit sales, third-party seller activity, advertising, and AWS customer usage.

At June 30, 2021, Amazon had $360.3 billion in assets, $89.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, and $114.8 billion in stockholders’ equity. Long-term debt was $50.3 billion following an $18.5 billion senior-notes issuance. Six-month operating cash flow was $16.9 billion, while investing activities used $30.7 billion, including $24.2 billion in cash capital expenditures.

Amazon incurred approximately $1.5 billion of COVID-19-related costs during the quarter and expected sales growth to decelerate in Q3 2021. The company agreed to acquire MGM for approximately $8.5 billion. It also disclosed a €746 million Luxembourg data-protection fine, which it intends to contest, along with ongoing tax, antitrust, and other legal proceedings.

Parkinson’s disease ended Linda Ronstadt’s singing career and causes difficulties with speaking, traveling, and daily tasks, but she continues exercising and appearing at “A Conversation With Linda” events featuring archival material and audience questions. Diagnosed in 2013 after losing her ability to sing, she was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2014. Her chart-topping 1977 album *Simple Dreams* received a 40th-anniversary expanded edition with three live recordings. The album spent five weeks at Number One, sold more than 3.5 million U.S. copies in under a year, and produced hits including “Blue Bayou,” “It’s So Easy,” and “Poor Poor Pitiful Me.” It also won the Grammy for Best Recording Package.

This English cohort study assessed effectiveness of two BNT162b2 or ChAdOx1 COVID-19 vaccine doses over up to 50 weeks, using 12 consecutive four-week periods and risk-based age groups. It included approximately 2.0 million BNT162b2 recipients, 3.3 million ChAdOx1 recipients, and 1.2 million unvaccinated individuals.

Third-dose uptake reached at least 90% in the 65+, clinically vulnerable 18–64, and 40–64 groups. Consequently, later estimates for two-dose recipients were based on highly selected individuals. Marked changes in non-COVID-19 mortality hazard ratios suggested selection bias, potentially caused by delayed vaccination among people with recent infection, serious illness, or frailty. The study therefore did not interpret effectiveness beyond 26 weeks in these groups or separate omicron’s effects from those of third-dose uptake.

Among adults aged 18–39, third-dose uptake reached 73%, without evidence of increased non-COVID-19 mortality among those remaining with two doses. Protection against COVID-19 hospitalization waned approximately log-linearly and was negligible by weeks 35–38. Protection against a positive SARS-CoV-2 test waned approximately log-linearly through weeks 23–26 and appeared negligible earlier, although differences in testing behavior between vaccinated and unvaccinated people likely caused confounding. Waning did not appear affected by omicron.

The study concludes that high additional-dose uptake, delayed vaccination after infection or illness, and changing testing policies complicate estimates of long-term two-dose effectiveness. Future studies should examine why eligible people remain without additional doses and report non-COVID-19 outcomes to identify potential bias.

Kyle Busch overcame handling problems and a 16th-place start to win the Overton’s 400 at Chicago for Joe Gibbs Racing. He finished 12th in Stage 1 and 11th in Stage 2 as his team repeatedly adjusted the tight-handling No. 18 Toyota. Fast pit stops and improved performance moved him to the lead in Stage 3, and he held off Kyle Larson’s final-lap challenge by 1.162 seconds.

The victory was Busch’s fifth of the season, second at Chicago and 48th in 479 Cup Series races, tying Buck Baker for 14th on the all-time wins list. He led 59 laps and reached 190 total victories across NASCAR’s top three divisions. Aric Almirola won Stage 1, while Kevin Harvick won Stage 2. The next Cup Series race was scheduled for July 7 at Daytona International Speedway.

The application describes blockchain-based digital certificate management intended to reduce risks from a hacked, faulty, or malicious certificate authority (CA). A CA may issue a certificate and request its addition to a blockchain, but the certificate remains invalid until blockchain nodes complete consensus verification. Nodes broadcast verification results, and the request is accepted or rejected according to predetermined numerical or proportional thresholds. Similar consensus procedures govern certificate revocation lists, revocation records, and updates. Revocation lists can be stored in local node ledgers or constructed from accepted revocation records, allowing nodes to verify transaction participants’ certificates without remotely consulting the CA. The disclosed methods may reduce verification costs, improve transaction efficiency, and prevent unilateral CA actions from compromising blockchain security. Implementations include methods, apparatuses with receiving, determining, response, and transaction units, processor-and-memory electronic devices, computer-readable storage media, and systems combining these components.

President Donald Trump cited the attempted bombing near Manhattan’s Port Authority Bus Terminal as evidence that Congress should end “chain migration,” strengthen immigration enforcement, and address fraud and abuse. Suspect Akayed Ullah, a Bangladeshi permanent resident who entered the U.S. in 2011 on a family immigrant visa, allegedly detonated a crude device in a subway tunnel. Trump also called for the strongest legal penalties, including the death penalty where appropriate, for those convicted of terrorism.

The patent describes systems and methods for near-real-time analysis and forecasting of precipitation, fog, atmospheric water vapor, liquid water content, visibility, and runway visual range. It continues several earlier patent applications and relates to prior weather-forecasting patents and applications.

Existing fog detection commonly relies on direct observation or dedicated instruments with limited geographic coverage. Radio-frequency attenuation can indicate fog or atmospheric moisture but may be difficult to distinguish from rain or other interference. Current systems also struggle to process satellite microwave links, high-frequency vehicle sensor data, and rapidly changing weather, resulting in delayed or low-fidelity forecasts.

The described system asynchronously collects and preprocesses diverse data, including terrestrial and satellite microwave-link attenuation, radar, numerical weather prediction models, stationary and mobile sensors, maps, and ancillary runway data. Filters, transforms, and trained machine-learning models remove unreliable information and derive precipitation, water vapor, fog, and liquid-water estimates. Data from multiple sources may be blended to improve forecast accuracy and speed.

A parallel processing pipeline separates data collection from forecast cycles and supports forecast cadences as short as one minute. Four logical server components handle information collection and normalization, offline model and filter generation, modeling and prediction, and information distribution and alerts. Shared databases store collected, processed, generated, forecast, fog, precipitation, runway-visibility, and related data. Outputs include maps, reports, alerts, and user-requested forecasts for geographic locations, airports, or runways.

Forecast processing is organized into cadence series, cycles, and instances. Data is stored in geographically organized tile layers and tile stacks for collection, forecasting, and post-processing. Cadence instances may reuse prior or slowly changing data, incorporate newly collected information, and selectively update affected tiles rather than recomputing entire forecasts. A cadence manager compares collected data with earlier forecasts, propagates verified or changed tiles through dependent layers, and chooses between complete recalculation and incremental updates based on computational efficiency and data changes.

The system supports short-term high-resolution forecasts and longer-term forecasts. It can adapt cadence timing to weather conditions, classify storm tiles, use wind and atmospheric data to predict precipitation movement, calculate accumulations, and generate fog and runway-visibility forecasts. These forecasts may be updated as high-frequency observations arrive and used by airports, pilots, passenger airlines, and freight operators for planning and scheduling.

The Department of Transport warned that some commercial State company boards consider 2011 salary rates too low to attract or retain chief executives. Government reforms lowered executive pay, removed benefits such as car allowances and ended performance-related bonuses. Although agencies have complied, some CEOs whose contracts retain bonus clauses are threatening legal action for payment and back payments. The CEO of Dún Laoghaire Harbour Company has initiated High Court proceedings. Separately, Bus Éireann senior management pay is to be cut by 10 per cent.

The San Diego County Fair’s Western-themed exhibit highlights contemporary Kumeyaay culture through displays, photographs, maps and Wednesday performances of native-language songs by tribal members. The Kumeyaay presence aims to correct the misconception that the people no longer exist and educate visitors about their lives and traditions. The exhibit also examines myths about the Wild West and Hollywood’s portrayal of cowboys, while offering daily staged showdowns, variety shows and planned Kids’ Day crafts.

The MSPM0G3519/G3518/G1519/G1518 devices include independent and windowed watchdog timers, general-purpose and advanced timers, configurable analog and digital I/O, an Arm-compatible two-wire serial debug interface, and a UART/I2C boot strap loader protected by a 256-bit password. The bootloader is enabled by default, can be disabled, and may be invoked through hardware, blank-device detection, or software reset.

The independent watchdog uses a separate 32-kHz clock and offers eight periods from 2 ms to 2 hours, generating a POR reset if not serviced. The windowed watchdog provides eight selectable periods, reset or interrupt generation, automatic stopping in sleep mode, and interval-timer operation. Timer peripherals support programmable prescaling, multiple count modes, synchronization, cross-triggering, interrupt/DMA generation, and peripheral triggering. Advanced timers additionally provide complementary PWM, dead-band insertion, configurable fault handling, repeat counting, and extra capture/compare channels.

The IOMUX selects peripheral functions and controls output, input, and shutdown wake-up behavior. Enabling DAC_OUT connects it to PA15, so external signals on PA15 are not recommended during DAC use. The memory-mapped, read-only FACTORY region stores device capabilities, identification, hardware revision, and trim data.

Recommended hardware includes 10-µF and 0.1-µF low-ESR VDD decoupling capacitors, a 47-kΩ pullup and 10-nF capacitor on NRST, and a 0.47-µF VCORE capacitor. SYSOSC frequency correction requires an external 100-kΩ, 0.1% resistor. Five-volt-tolerant open-drain I/O requires pullups for high output and remains fail-safe without VDD.

TI distinguishes experimental “X” devices from qualified production “MSP” devices and recommends only qualified parts for production. Development resources include LaunchPad hardware, MSPM0 SDK, cloud tools, Resource Explorer, SysConfig, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, Code Composer Studio, IAR, Keil, TI Arm-Clang, and GNU Arm tools.

The April 2025 revision updates peripheral counts, package variants, electrical and thermal specifications, operating modes, memory endurance, security, timers, communications, and other device descriptions. Packaging data, assembly guidance, ESD precautions, support resources, and TI warranty and liability disclaimers are also provided.

This study evaluated the 17-item COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale–Modified (C19-YRSm), a patient-reported measure of Long Covid symptoms, functional disability, and overall health. Data came from 1,314 patients receiving care across 10 UK Long Covid services; 263 completed assessments at baseline and approximately 30 days.

The scale showed good convergent validity with the FACIT-Fatigue measure, distinguished between symptom-severity groups and patients with differing hospital or intensive-care admission histories, and demonstrated good internal and test-retest reliability. Its three subscales detected changes over time and were more responsive than the EQ-5D-5L health measure. Estimated minimally important differences were 2 points for symptom severity, 2 for functional disability, and 1 for overall health; estimated minimal clinically important differences were 4 points for symptom severity and functional disability. Confirmatory analysis provided some support for separate symptom-severity and functional-disability factors, although individual fit statistics did not consistently meet predefined thresholds.

The findings support the C19-YRSm as a brief, valid, reliable, responsive, and easily administered Long Covid measure for monitoring condition trajectories, evaluating interventions, informing clinical care, and supporting research and policy. Further work should confirm meaningful-change thresholds and examine whether item refinement could improve responsiveness.

Edmonton police seized $3.2 million worth of carfentanil, the department’s largest-ever seizure, after firefighters found suspicious powder in a vacant Parkallen basement suite on Jan. 28. Police recovered 16 kilograms of blue powder and additional pink powder containing carfentanil, plus 12 kilograms of suspected caffeine intended to dilute the drug. Police estimated the carfentanil could produce about 161,000 doses for street distribution. No arrests have been made, and investigators are seeking the basement tenant as a person of interest. Alberta Health Services condemned the building because of contamination risks. University students living upstairs were unaware of the suspected drug operation and had called firefighters.

Ethiopian-Irish actress Ruth Negga recalled resenting how teachers spoke to her while growing up in Limerick and longing for school to end. She described acting as freeing despite its rigorous structure and credited luck as an important factor in her career. Negga received her first Best Actress Oscar nomination for *Loving*, about the interracial couple whose convictions led the US Supreme Court to overturn laws against interracial marriage in 1967.

VentureWire’s May 30, 2001 newsletter reports executive appointments across technology companies in management, venture capital, business development, sales, operations, finance, product development, and human resources. Notable changes include new leaders at Solsoft, Gluon Networks, InfoImage, QED Solutions, and Corechange, while Real Media co-founder David Morgan plans to leave and start a software company. The newsletter also lists executive openings in analytics, marketing, sales, finance, engineering, product management, online learning, and venture capital across the United States and Europe.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K on July 26, 2022, announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2022. The related press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under the Securities Exchange Act. The report was signed by Chief Accounting Officer Alice L. Jolla.

The passage provides design guidance for a TPS7H500x-SP push-pull converter. The transformer uses a targeted 35% maximum duty cycle, a 2.5 turns ratio, and a 40-µH primary inductance, selected instead of the calculated 33 µH. Magnetizing current was initially targeted at 6% of output current.

Primary GaN FETs require margin above twice the input voltage; 170-V devices were selected for a 36-V maximum input. The synchronous rectifiers use 80-V GaN FETs despite an expected 20-V maximum stress. Parallel Schottky diodes can reduce soft-start current and dead-time reverse-conduction losses. An RCD clamp may limit switch-node overshoot, with final values optimized through testing.

The output stage uses a 0.47-µH inductor targeting 40% ripple. At least 1.3 mF output capacitance is required for ripple and transient limits, while approximately 2.3 mF was used to improve radiation-induced single-event transient mitigation. An optional secondary LC filter can further reduce ripple, with damping added if high-frequency peaking occurs.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins near 35 A, providing about 45% margin over the 24.25-A peak inductor current. A 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω sense resistor were selected. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover using 40.2-kΩ, 15-nF, and 47-pF components. Seven 330-µF capacitors provide about 2.3 mF, and a 102-kΩ slope-compensation resistor is used.

The controller operates from 4 V to 14 V and requires at least 0.1 µF of closely placed ceramic input bypass capacitance. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switching loops and switch-node area, keeping sensitive traces away from high-dv/dt signals and magnetics, placing bypass, filtering, sensing, and compensation components near relevant pins, and using short, wide high-current traces. CFP backside metallization should connect to AVSS through multiple vias.

A Regina father urged drivers to avoid splashing pedestrians after a vehicle drove through slush and drenched his wife and infant son. Regina and Saskatoon bylaws prohibit splashing pedestrians, but police said enforcement is difficult without a driver description, vehicle details and licence plate number. Marshall Pelletier expressed disappointment that the driver neither slowed down nor stopped and called for greater awareness around pedestrians.

The paper interprets statistical independence (SI) as the principle that random sampling yields representative samples. In Bell experiments, SI requires measurement settings to be independent of the measured systems’ states. Superdeterministic theories preserve locality by systematically violating this representativeness.

The authors identify three forms of superdeterminism: deterministic theories with fine-tuned initial conditions; deterministic or indeterministic statistical flukes; and “nomic exclusion,” where physical laws prevent combinations of settings and hidden states that would conflict with observed quantum predictions. They argue that superdeterminism therefore need not require determinism or fine-tuned initial conditions. They also maintain that retrocausal and invariant-set theories need not violate SI or be superdeterministic.

The paper further argues that superdeterminism can restrict free will under some compatibilist accounts, contains a conspiratorial element, and does not necessarily undermine scientific methodology. Nevertheless, the authors regard it as pre-scientific rather than scientific.

NVIDIA’s fiscal 2016 Form 10-K covers the year ended January 31, 2016. The Delaware corporation, headquartered in Santa Clara, California, had 542 million common shares outstanding as of March 11, 2016 and a non-affiliate market capitalization of approximately $9.92 billion as of July 24, 2015.

NVIDIA describes itself as a visual computing platform company serving Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter and Automotive markets through two reportable segments: GPU and Tegra Processor. Its brands include GeForce, Quadro, Tesla, GRID, DRIVE and SHIELD. The company uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on suppliers including Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Samsung for wafer production and independent subcontractors for assembly, testing and packaging.

Fiscal 2016 revenue was $5.01 billion, operating income was $747 million and net income was $614 million, or $1.08 per diluted share. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $5.04 billion. NVIDIA incurred $1.33 billion in research and development expenses and employed 9,227 people, including 6,566 in research and development. ASUSTeK accounted for 11% of fiscal 2016 revenue, while sales outside the United States and Other Americas represented 79%.

NVIDIA paid $213 million in dividends during fiscal 2016 and increased its quarterly dividend to $0.115 per share. Through January 31, 2016, it had repurchased 231 million shares for $3.85 billion, with $1.47 billion remaining authorized through December 2018. It intended to return approximately $1 billion to shareholders in fiscal 2017 through repurchases and dividends.

The company identified major risks including intense competition, rapid technological change, dependence on third-party manufacturers, product defects and manufacturing-yield problems, cybersecurity breaches, customer concentration, demand forecasting errors, international operations, intellectual-property disputes, acquisitions, fluctuating operating results, privacy regulation, headquarters construction, and substantial indebtedness. NVIDIA also noted that Intel’s final $200 million payment under a $1.5 billion patent cross-licensing agreement was received in January 2016, with related revenue recognition continuing through the first quarter of fiscal 2018.

The World Bank raised China’s 2025 GDP growth forecast from 4.5% to 4.8%, citing government stimulus, infrastructure investment, manufacturing support, stronger industrial output and improving exports and consumer sentiment. It expects growth to weaken in 2026 amid fiscal constraints, trade uncertainty, property-sector weakness, subdued consumption, local government debt, demographic pressures and declining productivity. Sustainable growth will require a gradual shift from state-led investment toward consumption, services, innovation, green industries and digital development.

Eisenhower accepts the Republican presidential nomination, thanks the convention, praises Vice President Nixon, and urges supporters to register and vote. He argues that the Republican Party is the “Party of the Future” because it follows enduring principles, addresses current and emerging problems, unites Americans, advances social justice through individual initiative and federal leadership, and remains dedicated to peace.

He cites farm policy, free collective bargaining, and limits on federal centralization as examples of principled government. He calls for attention to water, highways, health, housing, energy, urban development, and education rather than continued focus on Depression-era issues. He also highlights efforts against discrimination and programs assisting workers, older citizens, farmers, women, small businesses, and other groups.

Eisenhower identifies three requirements for peace: maintaining American moral, economic, and military strength; supporting collective security and cooperation among free nations; and cautiously expanding communication and exchanges with peoples under communist rule. He envisions technological and social progress within a peaceful world, achieved not through revolution or division but through free Americans working together with international partners. He concludes that faith, unity, sustained effort, and Republican principles can help create a future of prosperity, justice, goodwill, and lasting peace.

Joe Bryant’s Week 11 fantasy football report evaluates passing and rushing matchups as offensive locks, favorable, even, unfavorable, or heavily favoring defenses. Strong passing opportunities include Kansas City against San Francisco, Denver against Oakland, Jacksonville against Seattle, New Orleans against Carolina, San Francisco against Kansas City, and Indianapolis against the Jets. Difficult passing matchups include Tennessee against Baltimore, Philadelphia against Pittsburgh, Atlanta against Detroit, Baltimore against Tennessee, Cleveland against New England, Pittsburgh against Philadelphia, and Cincinnati against Dallas.

Favored rushing options include Oakland’s backs against Denver, Minnesota’s Robert Smith against Arizona, New England’s backs against Cleveland, Jacksonville’s Fred Taylor against Seattle, Cincinnati’s Corey Dillon against Dallas, and San Francisco’s Charlie Garner against Kansas City. Particularly difficult rushing matchups include St. Louis against the Giants, Chicago against Buffalo, Carolina against New Orleans, Tennessee against Baltimore, and Philadelphia against Pittsburgh. Injuries, uncertain workloads, and quarterback changes affect several recommendations.

The message concludes with a Veterans Day tribute describing veterans’ varied service, sacrifice, injuries, and often-unrecognized courage. It urges readers to thank those who served and includes a quotation crediting soldiers with protecting civic freedoms.

Researchers led by University of South Florida’s Dr. Davide Tanasi identified Italy’s oldest known olive oil residue in pottery fragments excavated at Castelluccio, Sicily, in the 1990s. Chemical analysis using Nuclear Magnetic Resonance, Gas Chromatography and Mass Spectrometry detected oleic and linoleic acids. The reconstructed 3.5-foot, multi-handled container and nearby utensils were dated to the Sicilian Early Bronze Age. The findings provide chemical evidence that systematic olive oil production in Italy began at least 700 years earlier than previously believed.

Jim Cramer reversed his bullish stance on Snap, citing backlash to Snapchat’s redesign, potential declines in user engagement and advertiser interest, and the stock’s high valuation. Shares lost gains made after strong fourth-quarter revenue growth amid criticism from celebrities, including Kylie Jenner. Cramer recommends avoiding the stock until the redesign’s impact is clearer, though he may buy at a lower price. Snap reports first-quarter results May 1.

David Luiz is holidaying in Dubai after injuries and limited playing time in Chelsea’s disappointing season cost him a place in Brazil’s World Cup squad. His future, and manager Antonio Conte’s, remains unclear despite Chelsea winning the FA Cup after finishing fifth in the Premier League.

During puberty and early adolescence, children develop identities separate from their parents while peer opinions and developmental changes may create insecurity, loneliness, academic problems, or depression. Parents should respond with patience, positive reassurance, nonjudgmental listening, and support rather than telling children how to think. Signs such as falling grades or withdrawal from favorite activities warrant professional help. School counselors can assist children and help parents understand and address these challenges.

Running backs are key offensive players whose primary responsibility is gaining yards on handoffs while protecting the football. Positioned behind or beside the quarterback, they must also block and catch passes. Effective running backs combine speed, agility, vision, strength, toughness, and receiving ability, typically with an athletic, well-built physique. Roles vary, including short-yardage specialists and versatile all-purpose backs. Notable running backs include Barry Sanders, Emmitt Smith, Walter Payton, Jim Brown, and Ladanian Tomlinson. Elite running backs contribute significantly by breaking tackles, evading and outrunning defenders, turning poor plays into major gains, and reliably running, blocking, and catching.

Chelsea manager Antonio Conte believes the media scrutinise his future more harshly than those of rival Premier League coaches. Despite winning the league and reaching the FA Cup final in his first season, Chelsea are now 18 points behind Manchester City and competing for a top-four finish. Amid rumours linking him with the Italy job, Conte reiterated his intention to remain in England and honour the final 18 months of his contract. Chelsea next face Watford after a 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth.

Unwanted gifts can be sold, traded or regifted. Platform choice matters: eBay and auction houses suit collectibles; Kijiji works well for electronics and heavy items; garage sales suit inexpensive household goods; and Bunz facilitates non-cash trades of clothing, cosmetics, furniture and decor. Clear, well-lit photos, condition abbreviations, searchable hashtags and engaging descriptions can improve online listings.

Prices should reflect comparable sold listings, condition, age and depreciation rather than the highest or lowest sale. Posting at popular times can improve results: Kijiji traffic rises in January, especially on weekends and Mondays, while Bunz activity peaks on Sundays. Furniture and home decor may sell well during late-summer student moves.

Gift cards can be sold through classified sites or services such as CardSwap, generally below face value. Regifting can save money but is appropriate only for new, packaged items the recipient would appreciate. Handmade, personalized or carefully selected gifts should not be regifted, and recipients should not know the original giver.

Will Ma introduces independent chip model (ICM) theory, which estimates tournament stack value under nonlinear payouts. Unlike cash games, winner-take-all events, or heads-up play, tournament decisions may prioritize survival and payout advancement rather than maximizing chip EV alone. ICM assumes a player’s chance of winning is proportional to their share of total chips, then recursively calculates probabilities of lower finishes. In a three-player example with payouts and stacks of 5-3-2, the shortest stack’s equity is 2.89 rather than 2 because it is guaranteed third-place money while retaining chances to finish higher.

ICM matters most near the payout bubble, at final tables, and in satellites. Big stacks generally have money EV below chip EV but can pressure smaller stacks, while small stacks have money EV above chip EV yet must call all-ins more cautiously. Thus, ICM does not simply require tighter play: players can shove more often when acting first but should call shoves less often. In extreme satellite or bubble situations, folding pocket aces can be correct.

Ma applies these principles while reviewing a final table. As a large stack, he avoids unnecessary confrontations with stacks that can eliminate him, pressures shorter stacks with frequent shoves, and analyzes opponents’ oversized all-ins as potentially justified by ICM. He reviews a jack-ten bluff-reraise where calling an ensuing shove required 33% equity by chip EV but 39.6% under ICM; estimated equity was insufficient, validating his fold.

The tournament reaches three-handed play, where short stacks increase the chip leader’s ability to shove broadly. Ma also discusses cooperative play against an all-in short stack, describing explicit cooperation as collusion. Once heads-up begins, ICM no longer applies, and he focuses on position, range construction, bluffing, postflop play, and exploitative adjustments. After several swings and favorable all-ins, he wins the tournament.

NASA launched Voyagers 1 and 2 in 1977 to study Jupiter and Saturn. Voyager 2 also visited Uranus and Neptune, while both probes collected data on 48 moons. Their missions later became interstellar; Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012. Both carry long-lasting Golden Records containing information about Earth and humanity.

Inverse PDE problems seek physical states from incomplete observations but are ill-posed and computationally demanding, especially across irregular geometries. Existing operator-learning and diffusion approaches largely focus on regular domains or forward tasks.

GeoFunFlow combines geometry-aware operator learning with generative modeling for reconstructing PDE-governed fields from sparse, noisy sensors. Its geometric function autoencoder uses a Perceiver module for variable-sized unstructured meshes and continuous field reconstruction, while a latent rectified-flow diffusion model performs conditional posterior sampling without explicit likelihoods or MCMC. The framework provides theoretical posterior-approximation guarantees and reports state-of-the-art accuracy and efficient inference on complex-geometry benchmarks.

The problem is formulated over families of bounded geometries, with physical fields constrained by geometry-dependent dynamics and observed through noisy point samples. Conditioning includes the geometry, sensor locations, and measurements, and the objective is to learn a conditional probabilistic operator over reconstructed fields.

A Chicago ordinance requires hotels to provide panic buttons protecting employees working alone in guest rooms. A union survey found 58% experienced guest sexual harassment, but only one-third reported it.

Researchers in Sweden and Finland developed CORE, a model estimating the 10-year risk of severe liver disease using age, sex, and routine AST, ALT, and GGT blood tests. Based on more than 480,000 Stockholm residents followed for up to 30 years, CORE distinguished those who developed severe liver disease from those who did not in 88 percent of cases, outperforming the FIB-4 method. Tests in Finnish and UK populations also showed high accuracy. A web calculator is available for primary care, potentially supporting earlier detection of cirrhosis and liver cancer. Further testing is needed in high-risk groups, including people with type 2 diabetes or obesity, along with integration into medical record systems.

The January 19, 1999 Option Investor Newsletter reported modest Dow gains and a record Nasdaq close driven by technology and Internet stocks. AtHome’s $7 billion Excite acquisition, rumors of a Compaq Internet purchase, and Microsoft’s better-than-expected earnings supported optimism. However, weak broader-market internals, high bullish sentiment, Greenspan’s upcoming testimony, Brazil’s financial problems, and Clinton’s State of the Union address created uncertainty.

The newsletter adopted bullish postures on the Nasdaq 100, hardware, and software sectors, remained neutral on most other indices and sectors, and rated oil and gas bearish. It advised protecting long positions because short-term indicators remained bearish.

Microsoft, Sun Microsystems, Dell, Cisco, AOL, AT&T, WorldCom, Nokia, Lucent, and other technology or telecommunications stocks were highlighted as call plays or earnings candidates. Ford was added as a new call play. Excite and BMC Software were dropped as put plays, while several existing puts were retained with tighter stops. Speculative combination plays were proposed for Premiere Technologies, Omnipoint, Secure Computing, and R. H. Donnelley.

Bernstorff reported that Wilson confidentially offered peace mediation without addressing territorial terms and requested Germany disclose moderate peace conditions. Wilson believed this could lead to early peace conferences and prevent further bloodshed. Bernstorff warned that immediate unrestricted U-boat warfare would make war with the United States unavoidable, while briefly delaying it and engaging Wilson could improve Germany’s diplomatic position and prospects for peace.

Sharp reported that French Socialist deputies endorsed Wilson’s Senate address, urging France and other belligerents to support negotiations based on popular will rather than force. The message also received approval from professional circles and broad French press support, although many maintained that peace should follow an Allied victory.

Amanda Nunes retained her UFC title by defeating Ronda Rousey at UFC 207, handing Rousey her second consecutive loss. Nunes blamed coach Edmond Tarverdyan for encouraging Rousey to view herself as a boxer rather than rely on her strong judo skills. Tarverdyan had previously faced criticism from Rousey’s mother, fans and pundits. After the fight, Rousey said she needed time to consider her future amid retirement speculation, while UFC president Dana White predicted Nunes’ popularity would grow.

California’s energy crisis intensified as rolling blackouts began earlier than expected and officials forecast at least 30 more blackout days during summer. High wholesale prices, limited supply, plant maintenance, transmission constraints and reduced Northwest hydropower contributed to the crisis.

The Public Utilities Commission proposed tiered rate increases beginning in June. About half of residential customers would be exempt, while heavier residential users could face increases up to roughly 60%; commercial and industrial users could face increases of 50% or more. Consumer and business groups criticized the proposal.

Gov. Gray Davis asked power generators to accept 70% of debts owed by Southern California Edison to help prevent bankruptcy. Generators offered mixed responses. Davis also sought legislative approval for the state’s proposed purchase of Edison’s transmission system.

The Legislature approved authorization for $13.4 billion in revenue bonds to repay state funds and finance electricity purchases. California had already spent more than $6 billion buying power. Meanwhile, declining technology-sector tax revenue reduced the projected state budget surplus by $3.4 billion, raising the prospect of spending cuts.

Congressional Republicans expressed concern that the Bush administration’s focus on long-term energy policy and limited immediate relief could create political risks in the 2002 elections.

Healthcare fraud and overutilization impose major costs on Medicare, while conventional detection relies on limited manual audits and datasets that emphasize overt fraud, contain severe class imbalance, and often lack procedure-level detail. This study developed a physician- and biller-labeled dataset of 663 ophthalmologists using 2015 Medicare billing data, including 200 overutilizers and 463 non-fraudulent providers. Features derived from 513 ophthalmology HCPCS codes and provider-level payment data captured service frequency, beneficiary proportions, and payment ratios.

Six machine-learning approaches were evaluated through repeated nested cross-validation. A stacking ensemble combining K-nearest neighbor, logistic regression, support vector machines, extreme gradient boosting, and multilayer perceptron performed best, achieving an AUROC of 0.907 and a Brier score of 0.109. At a probability threshold of 0.353, it achieved 0.850 accuracy, 0.886 specificity, 0.750 precision, and 0.763 sensitivity.

Applied to 2021 data, the model classified 1,457 of 17,013 Medicare ophthalmologists as likely overutilizers, an estimated rate of 8.6%. Their Medicare payment per patient was significantly higher than that of other ophthalmologists, and estimated annual losses from ophthalmology overutilization were $437.1 million. Extrapolating from ophthalmology’s Medicare budget share yielded an estimated $49.1 billion in annual Medicare losses. Predicted rates and losses varied by jurisdiction. Feature analysis identified Medicare payment per patient and excessive use of certain procedure codes as influential, while emphasizing that high code use alone does not establish fraud.

Limitations include the small, high-dimensional labeled dataset, reliance on model predictions rather than confirmed cases, difficulty distinguishing overutilization from intentional fraud, and the need for specialty-specific expert labeling. Manual audits and medical-record review remain necessary for validation.

In his final address to the assembly as U.S. president, Biden reflected on five decades of public service and argued that cooperation and optimism can overcome war, division, and global crises. He cited progress since the Cold War, reconciliation with Vietnam, opposition to apartheid, accountability for war crimes, efforts against violence toward women, ending the Afghanistan war, and rebuilding U.S. alliances.

Biden urged continued support for Ukraine until it achieves a just and durable peace under the U.N. Charter. He called for responsibly managing competition with China while cooperating on shared challenges and strengthening Indo-Pacific partnerships. In the Middle East, he condemned the October 7 Hamas attack and civilian suffering in Gaza, advocated a ceasefire and hostage deal, warned against wider regional war, supported diplomacy between Israel and Lebanon, and endorsed a two-state solution. He also called for constraining Iran and ending Sudan’s civil war and humanitarian crisis.

He highlighted U.S. investments in food security, global health, climate action, clean energy, infrastructure, COVID vaccines, and the response to mpox in Africa. He supported reforming and expanding the U.N. Security Council and strengthening the organization’s peacekeeping and diplomatic roles.

Addressing artificial intelligence, Biden emphasized its potential benefits and serious risks, calling for international standards that ensure safety, equitable access, human dignity, and protection against authoritarian abuse.

Biden said preserving democracy was central to his presidency and explained that he declined to seek another term because serving the people matters more than remaining in power. He concluded that democratic aspirations remain strong worldwide and that nations can meet current challenges by working together.
BSEB released BETET/BSITET 2011 Special Examination 2016 Paper I and II results and subject-wise answer keys on biharboard.ac.in. Candidates can access results using their 10-digit roll number.

By 2007, DeBeers faced growing competition from laboratory-grown diamonds while attempting to rebuild its image after decades of supply control, antitrust scrutiny, and involvement in the blood-diamond trade. Its share had declined from producing 45% and selling 80% of rough diamonds to producing 40% and selling 45%.

The diamond industry produced about $13 billion in rough stones and $62 billion in jewelry annually. Production was concentrated in seven countries, processing was dominated by low-cost Indian operations, and African producers increasingly sought to retain cutting, polishing, sales, and marketing activities. Industry participants also expanded vertically into mining and retail. The United States remained the largest diamond market, while demand grew rapidly in India and China.

DeBeers’s monopoly weakened during the 1990s as Russian, Australian, and Canadian diamonds escaped its control. Maintaining prices required costly purchases and stockpiling, while U.S. and European regulators challenged its practices. DeBeers subsequently adopted a demand- and brand-focused strategy, stopped acting as buyer of last resort, reduced stockpiling, emphasized conflict-free supply, restructured relationships with sightholders, introduced the Forevermark, expanded advertising beyond engagements, and entered retail through a venture with LVMH.
