It also settled U.S. price-fixing and consumer lawsuits and formed partnerships that moved diamond activities to Botswana and Namibia.

Synthetic diamonds were chemically identical to mined diamonds and sold for 15%–40% less, with especially large savings for colored stones. Producers promoted their financial, environmental, and conflict-free advantages. Annual synthetic sales were nearly $50 million and projected to exceed $2 billion by 2015. Production used high-pressure, high-temperature or chemical vapor deposition processes, though jewelry-grade stones larger than one carat remained unavailable. Synthetic diamonds also offered potential applications in semiconductors, optics, data storage, and biological devices, and already dominated industrial diamond markets.

The natural-diamond industry disputed terminology for lab-grown stones and feared parallels with cultured pearls. The Kimberley Process reduced conflict diamonds to about 1% of trade, though enforcement remained difficult and concerns about mining conditions persisted. DeBeers responded by funding detection research, supplying identification equipment, educating consumers about mining’s social benefits, and emphasizing natural diamonds’ age and uniqueness. The central dilemma was whether DeBeers should enter the synthetic market or rely on consumers’ continued preference for natural diamonds.

The statistical analysis plan describes demographic, baseline, efficacy, pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and safety analyses for a pediatric diabetes trial comparing dasiglucagon 0.6 mg, placebo, and GlucaGen®. Demographics, diabetes history, body measurements, medical history, and medications will be summarized by treatment. Medical history and adverse events will use MedDRA coding; medications will use WHODrug and ATC coding.

Primary efficacy is time to plasma glucose recovery, defined as the first increase of at least 20 mg/dL from baseline within 45 minutes without rescue intravenous glucose. Analyses will primarily use the full analysis set, with supportive per-protocol analyses. Kaplan-Meier methods and a log-rank test stratified by age group and injection site will compare dasiglucagon with placebo. Patients receiving rescue glucose or not recovering within 45 minutes are censored at 45 minutes in the primary analysis. Sensitivity analyses will apply alternative censoring approaches. Supportive analyses include stratified Wilcoxon testing, discrete-time Cox models, recovery histograms, and linearly interpolated recovery times.

Secondary endpoints are recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes and plasma glucose change from baseline at those times. Recovery rates will be compared using stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests, with Fisher tests if needed. Glucose changes will use analysis of variance adjusted for treatment, age group, and injection site. A hierarchical two-sided 0.05 testing procedure will control multiplicity for dasiglucagon-versus-placebo comparisons. GlucaGen comparisons are supportive and excluded from the hierarchy. Missing efficacy data will not be imputed, and no interim analysis is planned.

Plasma dasiglucagon, glucagon, and glucose concentrations and derived pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic metrics will be summarized by treatment and displayed in tables and concentration-time figures. Pharmacokinetic parameters will be calculated through noncompartmental analysis using Phoenix WinNonlin. Plasma glucose response will include area under the effect curve above baseline from 0 to 30 minutes. Rules are specified for sampling times, values below quantification limits, and missing measurements.

Safety analyses use the safety set and cover insulin administration, hypoglycemia induction, trial medication, rescue glucose, local tolerability, adverse events, laboratory tests, vital signs, physical examinations, ECGs, pregnancy tests, and immunogenicity. Treatment-emergent adverse events include new or worsened events after dosing; uncertain events are conservatively treated as treatment emergent. Event summaries include incidence, seriousness, relationship, severity, special-interest events, injection-site reactions, and deaths. ADA incidence combines treatment-induced and treatment-boosted cases among evaluable patients.

The appendices define formatting, rounding, derivations, missing-date handling, SAS programming and quality-control requirements, and planned tables, figures, and listings.

Violence-against-women services await Ontario’s election outcome amid demands for greater investment in sexual assault services, legal support, shelters and reproductive health. The passage cites recent killings and criticizes debates for largely neglecting gender equity and sexual violence, as well as a prospective premier’s remarks and responses. Ontario Thrive’s gender-equity survey received responses from every major party except the Progressive Conservatives. The passage links women’s safety to economic security, safe workplaces and transit, affordable child care, livable wages and inclusive education about consent and violence.

North Carolina child care academies operate in at least 11 counties, offering two- to six-week, low- or no-cost training to address early childhood educator shortages. Sixty percent of licensed providers statewide reportedly face staffing shortages, and more than a dozen additional community colleges are considering academies.

Two models exist. The classroom-ready model provides at least 20 hours of required health, safety, registration, and background-check preparation, qualifying graduates to work in licensed facilities but not as lead teachers. The teaching credential model adds child-development coursework equivalent to EDU 119. Graduates earn transferable EDU 3119 credit, qualify as lead teachers or elementary teaching assistants, and can continue toward an associate degree.

Programs are typically collaborations among community colleges, Smart Start partnerships, and resource and referral organizations. Costs, schedules, funding, and outcomes vary. Wayne County reported 63 graduates, with more than half entering child care or higher education; Johnston County reported 26 graduates, including 14 employed in child care; Stanly County had 13 graduates, with five to 10 finding jobs; and McDowell County had six credentialed graduates, four of whom entered classrooms. Durham’s bilingual, six-week program received 140 applications for 20 places.

The North Carolina House included $1.476 million for expansion, but it was excluded from subsequent legislation signed in August. Separately, state grants of up to $50,000 are available to as many as 10 colleges or universities offering academies from October 2025 through July 2026.

Tesla’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2019 reported revenue of $4.54 billion, up from $3.41 billion a year earlier. Gross profit was $565.7 million, operating loss was $521.8 million, and net loss attributable to common stockholders was $702.1 million, or $4.10 per share. Automotive revenue totaled $3.72 billion.

At March 31, Tesla had $28.91 billion in assets, $22.87 billion in liabilities, and $4.61 billion in stockholders’ equity. Cash and cash equivalents declined to $2.20 billion from $3.69 billion at year-end. Inventory increased to $3.84 billion. First-quarter operating, investing, and financing activities used $639.6 million, $305.8 million, and $653.0 million, respectively.

Vehicle pricing changes increased expected buyback-option exercises, reducing automotive revenue by $500.5 million, cost of sales by $408.8 million, and gross profit by $91.7 million. Tesla adopted the ASC 842 lease standard, recognizing $1.29 billion of right-of-use assets and $1.24 billion of operating lease liabilities while derecognizing build-to-suit assets and liabilities.

Total debt principal was $10.33 billion. Tesla repaid $920 million of 2019 convertible notes, expanded its revolving credit commitments to $2.43 billion, and obtained a China loan facility of up to RMB 3.50 billion for Gigafactory Shanghai.

Tesla operated automotive and energy generation and storage segments. It disclosed supplier concentration risks and ongoing litigation involving the SolarCity acquisition, Model 3 production statements, the 2018 CEO compensation award, and a potential going-private transaction.

Sheffield’s plan to fell 31 lime trees along Rivelin Valley Road is emerging as a new focus of opposition to its citywide tree-removal programme. The road’s 700 trees, planted over three-and-a-half miles in 1907, reportedly form the UK’s second-longest lime avenue. Campaigners argue the removals would create major gaps and primarily ease contractor Amey’s resurfacing work. The dispute stems from a reported £2bn, 25-year road-maintenance agreement signed in 2009. Residents await an independent panel’s report.

Former Infosys CFO V. Balakrishnan said Sebi should decide Infosys’ settlement application over Rajiv Bansal’s severance payment on legal merits, not the whistleblower’s emotions. The whistleblower alleged governance lapses and opposed settlement, seeking prosecution of management and the board. Infosys sought to resolve allegations that the payment lacked prior committee approval. The company had agreed to pay Bansal ₹17.38 crore in 2015 but paid only ₹5 crore. Former CFO T.V. Mohandas Pai supported settlement, while Balakrishnan demanded two board members resign.

Markets face seasonal weakness, thin liquidity, tax-loss selling and institutional rebalancing. Technical indicators suggest TLT could overcome resistance if yields fall, while a dollar below 98 would support commodities and energy-related materials. Weakening dollar, lower yields and rising gold generally indicate risk-off conditions. Growth and value continue to diverge. The content is educational, not trading advice, and financial trading carries substantial risk.

The government shutdown continues amid disagreement over extending enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits through 2025. Introduced during the Covid-19 pandemic, the credits increased aid for eligible recipients and expanded eligibility to higher-income people.

Effective February 1, 2017, Tesla Motors, Inc. amended its certificate of incorporation and bylaws solely to change its corporate name to Tesla, Inc. The Form 8-K includes the amendment certificate and amended bylaws as exhibits.
The dollar rebounded nearly 4% amid stronger rate-hike expectations and economic growth, breaking key technical levels. Its rally pressured crude oil below $50, benefiting consumers.

Apple discontinued the iPod nano and shuffle after retiring the iPod classic. Their lack of Apple Music compatibility hastened their decline, while Apple Watch became the smaller alternative. The iPod helped Apple evolve from a PC maker into a hardware, software, and services ecosystem.

British, Belgian, and American representatives informally discussed a draft agreement regulating Congo exports and essential supplies from September 1942 through December 1943. Issues included possible early revision after Belgian liberation, separate future price arrangements, Belgian access to dollars, shipping guarantees, and transition from the existing Anglo-Belgian agreement. Article 1 commits Belgium to make scheduled Congo exports available to British or American buyers.

Kerala’s budget allocates ₹970 crore to general education and ₹789 crore to higher education, funding school excellence, infrastructure, digitisation, computer labs, technical education, skills and facility upgrades.

OpenAI introduced parental controls for ChatGPT following a lawsuit alleging the chatbot harmed a California teenager who died by suicide. Linked parent-teen accounts can restrict sensitive content, features, storage and access times, while alerting parents to acute risks without revealing transcripts. OpenAI is also developing age prediction to apply stricter safeguards to minors amid growing regulatory scrutiny.

SCET organizes back-to-back dijet production in \(e^+e^-\) collisions into hard, collinear, and ultrasoft modes. Small hemisphere invariant masses select dijet configurations and establish the hierarchy of hard scale \(Q\), jet scale \(m\), and ultrasoft scale \(m^2/Q\). In the peak region the ultrasoft scale is comparable to \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}\), requiring a nonperturbative function; in the tail region it is perturbative, with power corrections governed mainly by \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}/\mu_s\).

After a field redefinition, collinear sectors decouple at leading power while ultrasoft Wilson lines encode long-distance communication between jets. Factoring the states, operators, momentum constraints, and hemisphere-mass measurements yields a cross section composed of a hard function, two jet functions, and a soft function. The soft function can further separate perturbative radiation from nonperturbative effects.

Thrust provides a one-variable projection of the hemisphere masses, with \(\tau=1-T\) approaching zero in the dijet limit. Its distribution contains a nonperturbative peak, a perturbative dijet tail, and a large-\(\tau\) region where additional jets become relevant.

The hard, jet, and soft functions naturally reside at different scales. Renormalization-group evolution between them resums logarithms of the scale ratios, including logarithms of \(m^2/Q^2\) or \(\tau\). The hard function renormalizes multiplicatively, while jet and soft functions obey convolution equations and contain delta and plus-distribution structures in perturbation theory.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K dated April 16, 2020, attaching its 2019 Letter to Shareholders as Exhibit 99.1 and an Inline XBRL cover page as Exhibit 104. Senior Vice President David A. Zapolsky signed the report.

Designs in Mind, a Community Interest Company, has taken a permanent lease on a Cross Street shop in Oswestry after a successful pop-up trial. Called Jolt, the shop sells colourful homeware and prints, mainly designed by members referred through a mental health scheme, and offers screen- and lino-printing workshops. The retail venture aims to generate public interest, challenge low expectations of its makers and reduce stigma around mental health. Halls Commercial welcomed the permanent opening as part of ongoing business growth in Oswestry.

The HHLL strategy is a price-action reversal method that identifies breaks in trend structure. In an uptrend, a higher high followed by a lower low may indicate a bearish reversal; traders may sell when price pulls back to the previous high. In a downtrend, a lower low followed by a higher high may signal a bullish reversal; traders may buy when price returns to the previous low.

The strategy relies on interpreting swing highs and lows: uptrends normally form higher highs and higher lows, while downtrends form lower highs and lower lows. The ZigZag indicator can illustrate these patterns but uses forward-looking elements and is unsuitable for backtesting or trading. Backtesting is difficult because identifying tops and bottoms involves discretion.

A simplified backtest using an outside-day criterion on Philip Morris produced 118 trades, a 9.8% compound annual growth rate, a 1.26% average gain per trade, and a 2.2 profit factor.

Texas accepted Congress’s September 9, 1850, proposals establishing its northern and western boundaries, relinquishing external territorial and federal claims, and creating a government for New Mexico. Its legislature approved the agreement on November 25, before the December 1 deadline, and ordered authenticated copies sent to the President and Texas’s congressional delegation. The President noted broad support in Texas and congratulated Congress and the country on a major measure of peace and conciliation. He stated that governments had been established across the territories acquired from Mexico and expressed confidence that Congress would enact further measures needed to strengthen the Constitution and Union.

Plymouth Studio School is likely to close in September 2018, three years after opening, following viability challenges and an Ofsted rating of “inadequate.” A final decision is expected from the Minister for Schools in July. The £4.2 million school, based near Plymouth Marjon University, provided academic qualifications and specialist sports training for students aged 14 to 19. Staff, pupils and parents have been informed, while the Regional Schools Commissioner will consult parents. Plymouth City Council says sufficient secondary-school places are available and will help pupils transfer. The school will also work with Careers South West to advise families, while HR specialists support staff. Headteacher Mark Cahill said some Ofsted concerns, including a safeguarding review, had already been addressed and teaching would continue during the transition.

The MAGIC and LST-1 Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescope systems on La Palma use automated On-Site Analysis (OSA) pipelines to provide next-day, high-quality processed data for alerts, scheduling, quality assurance, and rapid scientific analysis. MAGIC records up to 2 TB daily and processes data through high-level products using about 50 cores and 40 TB of storage. LST-1 records up to 30 TB daily and processes raw data to reconstructed events using 1,800 cores and over 5 PB of storage. Results are usually available before 14:00 local time.

Both pipelines transform raw camera data through calibration, image reconstruction, particle-parameter estimation, photon-candidate selection, and instrument-response production. Python scripts, scheduled jobs, key files, observatory databases, and batch systems coordinate processing. Work is divided into small observation units and parallelized using Torque for MAGIC and SLURM for LST-1. Completed products are merged, stored, checked, and transferred to off-site centres.

Web pages and email notifications support monitoring and human supervision. Failed processes may be retried and vetoed; automated error recovery currently exists only for MAGIC but is planned for LST-1. MAGIC additionally generates detection significance, spectra, light curves, and sky maps, capabilities being added to LST-1.

Operational experience shows that next-day analysis is necessary for rapid responses and problem detection, must integrate with databases and simulation tools, and should combine automation with human intervention and comprehensive error recovery. The systems have operated continuously for years and may serve as prototypes and test beds for future CTAO onsite pipelines.

BJP MP Shatrughan Sinha criticized his party after its Rajasthan bypoll defeats, saying voters had begun speaking clearly and describing losses in Ajmer, Alwar and Mandalgarh as a “triple talaq” to the BJP. Sinha, who joined Yashwant Sinha’s Rashtra Manch, has frequently differed with BJP leaders and said the party treated him like a stepson. Union Minister Babul Supriyo responded that Sinha should leave the BJP if he disliked it so much.

The speaker remains confident after one loss, citing a brief lapse against a strong, balanced opponent. The team aims to split the first two games, build on its strong second and third periods, avoid costly mistakes, and get scoring from all four lines.

Readers criticize Ontario hospital restructuring, declining access to family doctors and clinics, and systemic capacity shortages that have left emergency departments overcrowded, understaffed and frightening for patients and workers. One writer suggests ERs have become multipurpose “dumping grounds,” while another urges people to volunteer in an ER to witness the health system’s problems firsthand.

A separate letter condemns Ottawa’s open-box recycling system for allowing paper and plastic to scatter, proposing clear plastic bags like those used in Smiths Falls.

The Citizen also invites readers to nominate local “Capital Builders” who have improved the National Capital community, with selected nominations to be published by year’s end.

Fullbacks are physical, selfless players primarily used as blockers in two-back, pro-style offenses. Lining up beside or behind the quarterback, they block defensive linemen and linebackers in running and passing plays, especially at the second level. They occasionally carry the ball in short-yardage situations or catch short passes.

Typically around 5’11”–6’1” and 235–250 pounds, fullbacks are thickly built, tough, agile, and skilled in run blocking, pass blocking, and receiving. They are often less athletic than running backs but compensate with blocking ability and tenacity. The position’s name derives from early football’s rugby-influenced practice of naming backs by field depth. Other terms include “power back” and “blocking back.”

The spread offense has reduced fullback usage, particularly in college football, but the position remains important to traditional rushing attacks. Notable fullbacks include six-time Pro Bowler Mike Alstott, who scored 58 rushing touchdowns, and Larry Csonka, the Miami Dolphins’ all-time leading rusher with nearly 7,000 yards.

The President forwards the International American Conference’s recommendation for reciprocal commercial treaties with other American republics. Over 87 percent of their products already enter U.S. ports duty-free, limiting possible concessions. Improved steam transport, currency exchange, and rebates on raw materials could strengthen U.S. competitiveness. After pending tariff legislation, mutually advantageous trade expansion would be pursued through treaty powers.

NSC 10/2 established the CIA’s Office of Policy Coordination in 1948 to manage covert activities including propaganda, economic warfare, sabotage, subversion, support for resistance groups, and aid to anti-Communist elements, while excluding conventional armed conflict and espionage. Initially guided directly by State in peacetime and the military in wartime, the OPC was placed under stronger Director of Central Intelligence oversight in 1950. Its rapid growth during the Korean conflict made covert action a prominent and costly CIA function. Truman created the Psychological Strategy Board in 1951, while NSC 10/5 reaffirmed and expanded CIA authority, particularly over guerrilla warfare.

The Eisenhower administration imposed greater external coordination. NSC 5412 and its successors required consultation with representatives of State, Defense, and the President. By the end of Eisenhower’s presidency, the NSC 5412/2 Special Group had become the executive body reviewing and approving CIA covert-action programs, though the CIA retained substantial initiative.

Following the 1961 Bay of Pigs failure, the Taylor Report prompted the Special Group to assume greater responsibility for planning and review. In 1963 it adopted informal submission criteria based on risk, likelihood of success, exposure, political sensitivity, and cost, with the CIA using a $25,000 threshold.

SBI’s Ecowrap expects 2017-18 average CPI inflation at 4.8% with downward bias and below 4% until July, describing inflation fears as exaggerated. March wholesale inflation eased to 5.7% due to lower fuel prices and rupee appreciation. WPI has exceeded CPI since December 2016, a trend expected through the fiscal year’s fourth quarter.

A Seattle Uber driver returned a passenger’s purse after an officer texted that he could face arrest and vehicle impoundment, sending a selfie to verify his identity. The driver had demanded extra money despite the woman offering to pay his fare.

After a failed 2012 May Day general strike effort, activists planned new strikes against the Trump administration for Feb. 17, March 8, and possibly May 1. The Feb. 17 action called for withholding labor and spending, while the March 8 women’s strike sought an inclusive “feminism for the 99 percent” through demonstrations, walkouts, boycotts, and other locally appropriate actions.

Organizers drew inspiration from Europe, where 42 percent of 63 general strikes between 2000 and 2016 reportedly caused governments to alter or abandon contested proposals. Poland’s 2016 women’s strike helped defeat a proposed near-total abortion ban.

Recognizing that anti-strike laws, low union membership, and risks to vulnerable women make a traditional U.S. general strike unrealistic, March 8 organizers described their effort as a flexible “mass strike.” Support was being considered or offered by unions, Black Lives Matter affiliates, Palestinian rights groups, and the National Organization for Women. The passage argues that even limited participation could help Americans develop large-scale strikes suited to current conditions.

VentureWire People’s May 21, 2001 newsletter reports executive appointments across technology and biotechnology companies. Notable changes include Zeke Zeringue becoming Wellogix CEO, Mark Wright becoming EXP Systems CEO, and new sales, marketing, business development, finance, technology, and operations leaders at iTendant, Campus Pipeline, Metapa, New Edge Networks, Proteus, ImaRx, Fuegotech, Nishan, FirstLook, Synertech, IPWireless, JP Mobile, Metabolex, iUniverse, and Kiodex. The newsletter also lists executive searches in sales, finance, venture capital, project management, packaging, business development, technology development, and optical infrastructure. Nth Orbit, an eight-employee supply-chain technology company, is hiring in business development, marketing, sales, and engineering.

A collection of May 24–25, 2001 news reports focuses primarily on Enron’s political influence in Washington and its dispute over India’s $3 billion Dabhol power project.

Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Chairman Curtis Hebert said Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay offered continued support for his position if Hebert backed faster electricity deregulation and grid access. Lay disputed that account. Enron, a major Republican donor, also recommended candidates for commission vacancies and advocated energy policies reflected in the Bush administration’s report. Hebert was widely expected to be replaced as chairman by Pat Wood.

In India, the Maharashtra State Electricity Board sought to cancel its power-purchase agreement with Dabhol, alleging misrepresentation and failure to supply full capacity within three hours. Dabhol denied the board had that right and had already issued its own preliminary termination notice over unpaid bills. Negotiations were scheduled, although one former panel member questioned the negotiators’ authority. Reports also discussed possible government liabilities, a potential Enron stake sale, NTPC involvement, and Bechtel’s threat to withdraw unless paid.

Other reports covered criticism of political rhetoric during California’s energy crisis, declining approval ratings for Governor Gray Davis, modest U.S. stock-market gains, Portland General Electric’s increased earnings amid higher power costs, Australian investment plans in India, growing business-school interest in energy careers, and a federal hearing into allegations that El Paso manipulated California natural-gas prices.

The Flyers’ coach praised his team’s resilience, growth through adversity, and determination after losing the Stanley Cup Final. He congratulated the Chicago Blackhawks, describing them as fast, strong offensively, difficult to penetrate defensively, and deserving champions. He said Philadelphia created late chances but failed to capitalize, while Chicago’s young goaltender made important saves. He also commended Scott Hartnell and the productive line with Danny Briere and Ville Leino.

Before the elimination game, the coach emphasized channeling home-crowd energy without becoming nervous. Despite facing elimination for the sixth time, he expressed confidence in the team’s experience, leadership, and success at home. His message was to avoid pressure, focus solely on beating Chicago in that night’s game, and prepare to compete at the highest possible tempo.

The passage specifies SD Memory Card command behavior, state transitions, data transfer, protection, switching, and timing. SET_DSR configures card drivers, while CMD7 selects one card for Transfer State or deselects cards. Data communication is point-to-point with the selected card. CMD12 aborts reads or writes; writes must stop before deselection. Programming may continue after deselection, but reset commands terminate it and may damage data. DAT0 indicates busy status.

Read and write transfers are block-oriented and CRC-protected. CMD17 reads one block; CMD18 reads continuously until CMD12. Writes use CMD24, CMD25, and related commands. Invalid lengths, addresses, alignment, CRC, or write-protected regions produce errors or abort operations. Multiple-block writes are preferred for speed; ACMD23 pre-erases blocks, and ACMD22 reports successfully written blocks.

Erase uses CMD32, CMD33, then CMD38. Protected sectors remain intact. DISCARD may deallocate selected blocks, while FULE logically erases the entire user area. Both are limited to supporting SDHC/SDXC cards and unavailable through SPI. DAT0 remains low while these operations are busy.

Write protection includes a host-managed mechanical switch, optional internal protection, and password locking through CMD42. Passwords persist across power cycles, and locked cards allow only limited commands. Card Ownership Protection adds a Force Erase Password, COP Unlock, protected erase, and restrictions on clearing passwords. Ordinary Force Erase clears user data and the card password; FEP Force Erase requires the matching FEP and leaves the FEP stored.

CMD55 marks the next command as application-specific. CMD6 checks or switches functions including access speed, command systems, driver strength, and power limits. Mode 0 queries support and consumption; Mode 1 changes functions. Switch status reports supported, selected, and busy functions. High-Speed mode provides a 25 MB/s interface at 50 MHz and requires a one-to-one host-card connection.

CMD8 checks voltage compatibility during initialization. SDSC cards use byte addressing and configurable block lengths; SDHC and SDXC use 512-byte block addressing. Hosts may reduce or stop the clock under specified conditions but must provide eight clocks after transactions. Commands and responses use CRC7; data uses CRC16. Invalid CRC or illegal commands set status errors without changing card state.

Read timeout is generally up to 100 ms. Write busy is generally limited to 250 ms, with some SDXC cases allowing 500 ms and UHS-II Data Bursts allowing up to one second.

Amazon.com, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on October 27, 2016, announcing its third-quarter 2016 financial results. The filing incorporates a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. Chief Financial Officer Brian T. Olsavsky signed the report.

The Supreme Court’s October 2025 term will address major disputes involving presidential power, civil rights, social issues and criminal procedure. Cases include challenges to President Trump’s authority to impose tariffs and fire agency heads, while the administration has also requested review of Trump’s executive order restricting birthright citizenship.

The court will rehear a Louisiana redistricting case examining whether creating a second majority-Black congressional district violates the Constitution. The case could affect Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act and other federal laws imposing liability for racially disparate impacts.

Other cases concern Colorado’s ban on conversion therapy, Idaho and West Virginia laws barring transgender athletes from teams corresponding to their gender identities, and whether police need probable cause to enter a home under the emergency-aid exception. The term follows extensive emergency-docket activity in which the court frequently allowed Trump administration actions to proceed, generally through 6-3 rulings reversing lower courts.

The center leads and coordinates the offensive line, adjusting blocking assignments and pass protections based on the defense. Before each play, the center identifies defenders, communicates calls, and makes quick decisions informed by film study. Physical responsibilities include snapping to the quarterback, blocking interior linemen, reaching linebackers, pulling as a lead blocker, and picking up blitzes.

Located in the middle of the offensive line, centers are sometimes called its quarterbacks because they direct the other four linemen. Essential skills include football intelligence, leadership, agility, strength, blocking, and reliable shotgun and under-center snapping. Centers generally have thick, compact builds, commonly measuring 6’1”–6’4” and 310–325 pounds. Though often smaller or less athletic than other linemen, they compensate with toughness and physicality. Notable centers include Jim Otto and Mike Webster. The position is crucial to protecting the quarterback and supporting the running game.

The submission claims $45,000 on a prior item and $31,000 for the impressment of 31 American crewmen into Russian naval service. It describes their seizure, forced labor, mistreatment, abandonment at Vladivostok, and eventual return to their ship. Compensation is also sought for navigating a Russian schooner, at $10 daily for officers and $5 for men, characterized as analogous to salvage. Additional claims include $200 for provisions consumed by Russians and $210 plus $50 for crew support and related costs at Vladivostok. General expenses of $3,040 are requested, including documented expenditures and anticipated costs of proving the claim. The submission argues that Russia is internationally responsible for its subjects’ actions and should provide full restitution. It also seeks 6 percent annual interest from the seizure date, citing Bering Sea awards, including the Dolphin award of $31,484 plus $19,399.38 interest.

Microsoft’s Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended June 30, 2018. The company reported a $650.1 billion non-affiliate market value as of December 31, 2017, and approximately 7.67 billion outstanding shares as of July 31, 2018.

Microsoft develops software, services, devices, cloud solutions, games, advertising, and consulting services. Its strategy centers on reinventing productivity and business processes, building an intelligent cloud platform, and creating more personal computing. Key offerings include Microsoft 365, Office 365, Dynamics 365, LinkedIn, Azure, Windows 10, Surface, Xbox, and Bing. Microsoft announced plans in June 2018 to acquire GitHub for $7.5 billion.

The company reports through three segments:
- **Productivity and Business Processes:** Office, LinkedIn, and Dynamics products and services.
- **Intelligent Cloud:** Azure, server products, cloud services, consulting, and support.
- **More Personal Computing:** Windows, devices, gaming, and search advertising.

Microsoft distributes products through original equipment manufacturers, direct sales, distributors, resellers, digital marketplaces, and retail stores. It offers various volume licensing, subscription, partner, and cloud-service programs. No individual customer represented more than 10% of revenue during fiscal years 2016–2018.

Research and development expenses were $14.7 billion in 2018, representing 13% of revenue. Development focuses on cloud and AI, user experiences and devices, LinkedIn, gaming, and longer-term research. Microsoft held more than 53,000 issued and 29,000 pending U.S. and international patents. Its devices are primarily produced by third-party manufacturers, while regional operations centers and global datacenters support customers worldwide.

As of June 30, 2018, Microsoft employed approximately 131,000 people, including 78,000 in the United States and 53,000 internationally. Satya Nadella served as chief executive officer.

Major risks include intense competition; lower margins from cloud services and vertically integrated products; unsuccessful investments, acquisitions, or alliances; intellectual property disputes and impairment charges; cyberattacks, data breaches, service outages, and misuse of online platforms; regulatory scrutiny involving competition, privacy, trade, anti-corruption, accessibility, telecommunications, and artificial intelligence; compliance obligations under the EU General Data Protection Regulation; difficulty attracting and retaining employees; and potentially adverse litigation outcomes.

Palestine police arrested two suspects after about 30 unlocked cars were burglarized Tuesday. Authorities urged all victims to report rummaged vehicles and advised drivers to lock their doors. Police are seeking additional suspects.

The Burr Ridge Village Board adopted policies requiring a 20% minimum general fund reserve, balanced general fund spending, and limits on total expenses. Officials said the village already follows similar practices. The board also renewed administrator Douglas Pollock’s one-year contract with a 2% raise, bringing his salary to $174,000.

The disclosure describes waveguide devices and methods for producing substantially uniform output illumination by mitigating pupil-banding artifacts in near-eye displays, head-mounted displays, head-up displays, and related sensors. Banding occurs when light replicated through total internal reflection (TIR) produces gaps or overlaps between successive extractions, with severity depending on field angle, waveguide thickness, and input aperture. Acceptable spatial non-uniformity is described as below 20%, preferably below 10%.

The devices include an optical substrate, light source, input coupler, light extractor, and a debanding optic. The debanding optic shifts or reshapes the pupil so successive extracted beams integrate into a substantially flat illumination profile. Implementations include passive, multiplexed, stacked, or electrically switchable gratings; rolled grating K-vectors; spatially varied diffraction efficiency; refractive-index or gradient-index layers; partially reflecting or polarization-modifying layers; crossed-slant and fold gratings; variable-numerical-aperture microdisplays; tilted image generators; coupling prisms; and light-absorbing edge films. Some configurations satisfy a zero-banding geometric condition based on waveguide thickness \(D\), TIR angle \(U\), and an effective aperture of \(2D\tan(U)\).

Light sources may include lasers or LEDs, while image generators may incorporate microdisplays, collimation optics, beam splitters, filters, and despecklers. Input and output coupling may use prisms or holographic gratings, including Bragg and switchable Bragg gratings formed from holographic polymer-dispersed liquid crystal materials. Gratings may also provide two-dimensional pupil expansion and spatially varying extraction efficiency.

Color embodiments use stacked optical substrates with input stops in different planes. Dichroic outer portions shift the pupil to reduce color banding, while optional inner coatings compensate phase shifts. The disclosed method generates light, couples it into a substrate for TIR propagation, passes it through a debanding optic, and extracts it with reduced illumination non-uniformity.

Amazon.com filed a Form 8-K dated April 14, 2022, attaching its 2021 Letter to Shareholders as Exhibit 99.1 and the Inline XBRL cover page as Exhibit 104. Senior Vice President David A. Zapolsky signed the report.

High-performance computing (HPC) uses connected systems to process complex calculations in parallel. Four out of five surveyed industry decision makers consider it transformative for product and process innovation. HPC enables faster, higher-quality simulations, modeling, analysis, and optimization; supports more iterations and new tailored applications; and improves innovation and agility across value-creation processes. Over a quarter of surveyed enterprises already use professional HPC, while 39% are planning or piloting deployment. IDC expects HPC to replace multicore workstations for many demanding workloads.

VentureWire’s October 24, 2000 issue reports that FusionOne was nearing $100 million in financing; Vanguard Venture Partners closed a $240 million fund; Hotmail founders launched Web-server performance company Akamba; and online investment service StockPower ceased operations. Numerous technology, software, telecommunications and Internet companies announced financing rounds, including Rapid5 Networks with $53 million, OpenTable with $42 million and CoManage with $36 million. New ventures and products included Groove Networks, Latinanet’s planned video portal and HomeJupiter.com. M&A activity included IBM’s acquisition of OpenOrders, GetAsia’s purchase of three Filipino portals, and the planned Bidcom-Cephren merger into Citadon. Several companies announced board and executive appointments. STIVentures raised $50 million, Debis Capital Services launched a $63 million fund, and GoldenEgg Ventures and E-Street agreed to merge as Syntek Capital Group.

Matrimonial websites are replacing traditional matchmaking through relatives, community members, priests, and brokers. They offer online profiles and matchmaking tools that can reduce travel, time, costs, and effort. Their large databases provide broader choices, accessible websites and mobile apps, filtered searches based on specific preferences, and text or video communication. Many sites also offer wedding guidance, counseling, private profiles, anonymity, profile verification, and membership screening. Detailed profiles may include interests, background, occupation, location, residency status, and previous marriages, helping users compare potential partners before deciding whom to know better.

Larry Connors’ %b strategy is a mean-reversion approach based on Bollinger Bands. It buys at the close when price is above its 200-day moving average and %b remains below 0.2 for three consecutive days, then exits when %b closes above 0.8. Because Connors did not specify Bollinger Band parameters, the test used a five-day lookback and two standard deviations.

A portfolio test across 25 ETFs from 2000 through December 2020, limited to five simultaneous positions, produced 677 trades, a 75% win rate, 0.76% average gain per trade, a 1.9 profit factor, 4.84% CAGR, and 16% maximum drawdown, with 17% market exposure. Using a 10-day lookback increased CAGR to 8.2% and drawdown to 24%. The strategy showed good results, particularly in QQQ and SPY, but generated few trades. Further optimization and combination with other Connors strategies were not tested.

Carson High School’s 2018 Winterfest features Johnny Depp-themed activities, contests and a Feb. 10 dance. Underclass courts will be crowned Feb. 8, while the senior king and queen will be crowned Feb. 9.

Coach DeBoer discussed a key player’s difficult return from an Achilles injury and setback, saying his health makes him an important part of the team. He also described allowing veteran Henrik back into the lineup after Henrik insisted he was ready and could contribute.

Despite poor power-play results, DeBoer said the team continues creating quality chances and believes execution, rather than strategic change, is needed. He praised veteran leadership, professionalism among players removed from the lineup, and the calming influence of composed goaltending on a young defense.

DeBoer acknowledged the team’s tendency to start slowly but said it adjusts as series progress. He emphasized generating traffic and pucks around the opposing net, maintaining focus, and believing the team can win several consecutive games. He credited Quick for limiting scoring and said playoff success depends on which team executes best.

DLAA applies DLSS Super Resolution technology at native resolution to improve image quality, temporal stability, and motion detail. NVIDIA’s Blackwell architecture advances developer-created neural shaders, which use trained AI models to approximate complex graphics operations. Through the Cooperative Vectors API for DirectX 12 and Vulkan, Tensor Cores become accessible to pixel, ray-tracing, and other shaders.

Neural-shader applications include RTX Neural Materials for efficient film-quality materials, Neural Texture Compression for reduced memory use, Neural Radiance Cache for approximating multi-bounce indirect lighting, RTX Skin for real-time subsurface scattering, and RTX Neural Faces for generating more natural faces from rasterized images and pose data. Stochastic Texture Filtering reduces aliasing and moiré patterns and benefits from Blackwell’s improved point-sampling rate.

The flagship GB202 GPU contains 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA Cores, 192 RT Cores, 768 Tensor Cores, and a 512-bit memory interface, and powers the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA Cores, 84 RT Cores, 336 Tensor Cores, and a 256-bit interface, supporting the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 has 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA Cores, 50 RT Cores, 200 Tensor Cores, and a 192-bit interface, supporting the RTX 5070.

NVIDIA states that specifications may change, products require customer validation for intended uses, and the materials are supplied without warranties beyond applicable sales terms.

The passage specifies clocking, timing, electrical, routing, and peripheral requirements for TMS320DM814x/DM8127 devices. PCIe requires a low-jitter differential reference clock AC-coupled near the processor. Optional audio and 32.768-kHz reference inputs, selectable clock outputs, and multiple PLLs are supported. PLLs start in bypass mode and must be configured within reference, DCO, SYSCLK, and module-frequency limits; PLL_USB must operate at 960 MHz when USB is used.

Interrupt resources include the ARM Cortex-A8 AINTC, supporting up to 128 programmable requests, and the C674x DSP controller, combining up to 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts. EDMA supports 64 channels mapped to as many as 512 parameter entries.

Peripheral descriptions and timing data cover DCAN, GPIO, I2C, Ethernet, MDIO, GPMC, HDMI, HDVPSS, imaging, JTAG, trace, and DDR2/DDR3. Ethernet provides a three-port gigabit switch with two external ports supporting MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII, plus shared MDIO control. Its I/O requires 3.3-V-compatible PHYs. GPIO provides up to 128 configurable pins across four modules. The GPMC interfaces with NOR, NAND, SRAM, pseudo-SRAM, and custom logic, while the ELM locates BCH-coded NAND errors.

The HDMI 1.3a transmitter supports digital video, multichannel audio, DVI, DDC, and CEC. TMDS pairs require controlled impedance, careful differential routing, paired vias, and low-capacitance ESD protection. HDVPSS supports video capture, processing, composition, scaling, conversion, and digital or analog output. Video DAC traces must be short, isolated, impedance-controlled, and carefully matched.

The imaging subsystem supports parallel and CSI-2 camera inputs, ISP processing, cropping, compression, correction, scaling, and image statistics. DDR interfaces support DDR2 and DDR3 with 16- or 32-bit paths, two chip selects, and two PHY-equipped interfaces. Reliable DDR operation requires prescribed device placement, stackup, keepout regions, termination, bypassing, impedance, trace spacing, and skew control. Board-routing delays must be included in timing analysis, preferably using IBIS models, while DDR designs should follow TI’s routing-rule specifications.

Enron and Dynegy were renegotiating their proposed merger after Enron’s financial condition, share price and energy-trading business deteriorated. The original roughly $9 billion stock deal could be reduced by more than 40% to about $5 billion, with the exchange ratio falling from 0.2685 to below 0.15 Dynegy share per Enron share. Discussions also involved additional financing and extending Enron’s debt maturities.

Credit concerns caused many energy companies to limit or stop selling gas and power to Enron. A broker estimated its trading volume at about 25% of the previous month’s level, though Enron disputed that figure. Enron’s equity-trading unit was reportedly closing, affecting about 60 employees.

Banks sought up to $2 billion for Enron, but several investors declined to participate. Enron faced a $690 million payment, billions in upcoming obligations and potential rating downgrades, although Moody’s kept its rating at the lowest investment-grade level that day. Enron’s bonds and shares recovered somewhat on hopes of revised merger terms, but traders and analysts remained concerned the deal could collapse and lead to bankruptcy.

Employee and shareholder lawsuits added uncertainty, including claims over retirement-plan losses. Enron had also acknowledged overstating earnings by $586 million over four years. Its shares closed November 27 at $4.14, compared with $78 a year earlier, while Dynegy closed at $40.89.

More than 250 small earthquakes struck near the California-Mexico border beginning New Year’s Eve, unsettling Brawley residents. The strongest, magnitude 3.9, occurred beneath Brawley in the southern Brawley Seismic Zone, which connects the potentially damaging San Andreas and Imperial faults. Scientists initially monitored the swarm for the possibility of triggering a magnitude-5 or larger earthquake, but that risk had largely receded by Sunday night. The nearby Imperial fault caused destructive earthquakes in 1940 and 1979. Swarms in the northern seismic zone can raise the risk of major San Andreas earthquakes; a September swarm prompted a warning of increased chances of a magnitude-7 or greater event. Brawley’s last major earthquake was a magnitude 5.4 in 2012.

The Yankees host the Red Sox in Game 1 of the best-of-three AL Wild Card Series at 6:08 p.m. ET Tuesday, Sept. 30, at Yankee Stadium. Boston finished 89-73 and held a 9-4 regular-season advantage over New York, which finished 94-68 on an eight-game winning streak. The study introduces a coarse-grained rod-sphere model for nanoparticles grafted with polymers, such as PiPrOx, that can crystallize into rigid bundles. Each particle consists of a repulsive sphere tethered to a rigid five-bead rod. Three rod interaction patterns—lock-and-key, symmetric, and unspecific—represent different polymer crystallization modes.

Molecular dynamics simulations varied sphere-to-rod size ratio, temperature, and interaction type. Mesostructures were classified using the fraction of aligned rods and cluster dimensionality derived from gyration-tensor eigenvalues. Simulations produced three-dimensional bulk structures, bilayers, monolayers, ribbons, fibers, worms, stars, spherical clusters, gels, liquids, and dispersed states.

Increasing sphere size generally reduced assembly dimensionality because geometric hindrance frustrated growth: small or absent spheres allowed bulk structures, intermediate spheres favored sheets or one-dimensional assemblies, and large spheres produced finite clusters. Interaction specificity determined structural details. Lock-and-key rods formed bulk structures, bilayers, ribbons, and stars; symmetric rods also formed fibers, monolayers, and spherical clusters; unspecific rods assembled at higher temperatures and produced monolayers, worms, gels, liquids, and spheres.

Assembly proceeded through rapid aggregation, growth, and slower consolidation. Lock-and-key ribbons also twisted spontaneously into achiral double helices, with pitch decreasing as sphere radius increased. The model reproduced experimentally observed fibers and spherical aggregates of PiPrOx-grafted silica nanoparticles and predicted additional structures. Its limitations include simplified single-rod tethering and simulation times shorter than experimental assembly times.

Enron disclosed an informal SEC inquiry into transactions with partnerships formerly managed by CFO Andrew Fastow. The announcement intensified concerns over conflicts of interest, complex off-balance-sheet financing, unclear disclosures, and potential shareholder dilution. Enron shares fell about 21% to $20.65 after reporting a $618 million third-quarter loss, $1.01 billion in charges, and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. Moody’s placed Enron’s debt under review, while shareholders filed lawsuits alleging misleading statements and board misconduct. Enron said the transactions were reviewed, approved, and disclosed, and pledged full cooperation with the SEC.

The speaker accepts the presidency with humility, relying on fellow officials, the people, and Providence. He praises the nation’s prosperity and argues that its endurance depends on faithful adherence to constitutional principles, reciprocal concession, and equitable compromise. Reviewing past challenges—including debt, war, factional conflict, territorial expansion, and tensions between federal and state authority—he maintains that experience has demonstrated the strength of popular government and the people’s capacity for self-rule.

He calls for preserving constitutional and legal order, limiting federal action to national and foreign concerns, and reserving other powers to the states and people. On slavery, he pledges to oppose congressional abolition in the District of Columbia against slaveholding states’ wishes and any federal interference with slavery in states where it exists.

His foreign policy will seek friendship and equal commerce with all nations, avoid alliances and interference in foreign disputes, maintain neutrality, and defend national rights. He concludes by promising to preserve the country’s institutions, continue principles shared with his predecessor, faithfully serve the nation, and seek divine protection and peace.

Real Madrid conceded an 89th-minute equaliser to draw 2-2 at relegation-threatened Levante. Sergio Ramos and Isco scored for Real, while Emmanuel Boateng and debutant Giampaolo Pazzini replied. The result left fourth-placed Real 18 points behind Barcelona, with defensive errors and missed chances increasing pressure on Zinedine Zidane.

This non-peer-reviewed study used whole-blood RNA sequencing to compare 194 virally suppressed people living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy (ART) with 361 HIV-negative individuals. Among 20,211 genes, 566 were differentially expressed: 274 were upregulated and 292 downregulated. These genes were enriched in immune processes, including T-cell biology, cell migration, adhesion, calcium and PI3K signaling, and in cancer-related pathways.

Cell-type deconvolution found higher proportions of CD8+ and follicular helper T cells and lower proportions of naïve CD4+, resting memory CD4+, and resting mast cells in HIV-positive samples. Gene dysregulation occurred across multiple innate and adaptive immune-cell types.

Comparison with prior pre/post-ART data classified 234 differentially expressed genes as ART-affected and 332 as ART-unaffected. ART generally shifted expression toward, but did not fully restore, the HIV-negative state. Both groups contributed to immune- and cancer-related pathways, indicating that dysregulation was not solely attributable to ART.

Genetic analyses identified 258 genes with significant expression quantitative trait loci. Genomic regions surrounding differentially expressed genes showed heritability enrichment for several blood-cell and inflammatory traits, but not for HIV acquisition or the 12 cancers tested. Limited colocalization was observed with pancreatic cancer and lymphocytic leukemia signals.

Drug-target databases identified 111 differentially expressed genes targeted by approved or investigational compounds, including 11 genes in cancer pathways. The authors conclude that persistent gene dysregulation in treated HIV may help explain immune dysfunction and non-AIDS comorbidities and may provide pharmacological targets, while emphasizing the need for functional and cell-specific follow-up studies.

This case-control study examined lipid metabolism in 108 Thai university students, including 64 with simple dysmood disorder (SDMD), 47 of whom had first-episode SDMD, and 44 healthy controls. Participants with metabolic syndrome were excluded, and analyses adjusted for age, sex, BMI, subclinical metabolic syndrome, and medication use.

Compared with controls, SDMD and first-episode SDMD were associated with decreased lecithin-cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) activity and increased free cholesterol and ApoE. No substantial differences were observed in HDL cholesterol, ApoA1, reverse cholesterol transport, ApoB, or triglycerides. Depression severity, suicidal behaviors, brooding, and phenome scores correlated positively with free cholesterol and inversely with LCAT. Partial least squares analysis indicated that LCAT’s association with the depression phenome was mediated through free cholesterol and brooding rather than a direct effect.

Subclinical metabolic syndrome was associated with lower HDL cholesterol and reverse cholesterol transport and higher triglycerides, ApoE, ApoB/ApoA1, and atherogenicity indices. However, decreased LCAT and elevated free cholesterol remained present in SDMD patients without subclinical metabolic syndrome. Interactions between SDMD and subclinical metabolic syndrome further worsened several lipid measures.

The authors characterize SDMD and first-episode SDMD as pre-proatherogenic states distinguished from more severe major dysmood disorder by their lipid profiles. They propose lipid screening using LCAT, free cholesterol, and ApoE, while noting that prospective studies and analyses of additional lipids and LCAT genetic variants are needed.

Tesla’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2017 reports operations in automotive and energy generation and storage. Third-quarter revenue rose to $2.98 billion from $2.30 billion in 2016, while net loss attributable to common stockholders was $619.4 million, or $3.70 per share, versus income of $21.9 million. Nine-month revenue was $8.47 billion, with a $1.29 billion attributable net loss.

At September 30, Tesla had $28.11 billion in assets, including $3.53 billion in cash, and $21.93 billion in liabilities. Nine-month operating and investing cash outflows were $570.5 million and $3.46 billion, respectively, offset by $4.13 billion from financing. Property and equipment purchases totaled $2.63 billion.

Debt principal totaled $9.99 billion. During 2017, Tesla issued $977.5 million of convertible notes due 2022 and $1.8 billion of senior notes due 2025, while repaying or converting other obligations. The company reported compliance with all debt covenants.

Tesla acquired Grohmann Engineering for $109.5 million in cash to improve manufacturing speed and efficiency. It continued finalizing valuations related to its $2.1 billion stock acquisition of SolarCity. Inventory reached $2.47 billion, property and equipment totaled $9.39 billion, and customer deposits were $686.1 million.

Tesla expects to adopt new revenue-recognition rules in 2018, estimating a $550 million to $750 million increase to equity, and new lease-accounting rules in 2019. Identified risks include dependence on primarily single-source suppliers, uncertain warranty estimates, litigation, regulatory matters, and obligations related to solar incentives and Gigafactory 2 employment and investment targets.

The S&P 500 gained 2.2% in July and 7.8% year to date before falling 1.6% on August’s first day. Longer-term trends remain healthy, but weakening breadth, seasonal volatility and widening credit spreads signal short-term risks. Investors are increasingly concentrated in technology, while U.S. electricity demand reached a record high. Global stocks outperformed U.S. large caps, and July favored stocks over bonds. The professor demonstrates three experimental games used to measure social preferences. In the dictator game, one participant decides how to divide money or goods with a passive recipient. Variations use candy, apples, money, communication, different stakes, and differing levels of privacy, illustrating factors that may influence giving.

In the ultimatum game, a proposer suggests a division and a responder accepts or rejects it; rejection leaves both with nothing. Communication and publicity are varied. The strategy method elicits each participant’s proposed offer and minimum acceptable offer for all possible scenarios, allowing researchers to gather more information while implementing only selected outcomes.

In the trust game, an investor sends part of an endowment to a responder; the amount is multiplied, and the responder decides how much to return. Communication may enable promises but does not ensure they are truthful. The professor notes that the classroom demonstrations are less rigorous than formal experiments and says later classes will examine careful research and whether laboratory games predict real-world behavior.

Microsoft appointed Bradford L. Smith, 56, as President and Chief Legal Officer effective September 11, 2015. Smith joined Microsoft in 1993 and had served as General Counsel since 2002, most recently as General Counsel and Executive Vice President of Legal and Corporate Affairs.

The flea flicker is a football trick play disguised as a run. After receiving a handoff, the running back returns the ball to the quarterback, who looks for a downfield receiver. Receivers initially appear to block before beginning routes, exploiting defenders who react to the run.

The play is credited to Illinois coach Bob Zuppke, who used it against Penn in 1925 on a fake field goal and later claimed he first called it in 1910 at Oak Park High School. Zuppke compared its motion to a dog flicking away fleas.

A quarterback can be penalized for intentional grounding on a flea flicker because he relinquished possession before receiving the ball again and must throw toward an eligible receiver.

Michigan used the play for a touchdown against TCU in the 2022 College Football Playoff, with J.J. McCarthy finding Ronnie Bell after Bell disguised his route. A reverse flea flicker adds multiple handoffs and changes of direction before returning the ball to the quarterback, as demonstrated by Baker Mayfield and receiver Dimitri Flowers. A fake flea flicker instead remains a running play, with the runner pretending to toss the ball back so defenders move past him.

September’s household survey sharply contradicted the establishment survey’s reported 33,000 job loss. It showed employment rising by 906,000 to a record 154.3 million, unemployment falling to 4.2 percent, labor force participation reaching 63.1 percent, and hourly earnings increasing 2.9 percent. Economist Beth Ann Bovino said hurricane-related reporting problems may have distorted the establishment data, noting 1.5 million workers could not reach their jobs. Markets were largely unfazed, while possible revisions and historical post-hurricane rebounds supported a more positive labor-market outlook.

The Ordnance Factories Board successfully upgraded 130-mm field guns to 155-mm capability at its Nalanda facility and expects an Army order for 300 guns. The indigenous barrel replacement increases range from 27 km to 36 km and costs Rs 1 crore per gun, compared with Rs 15 crore for a new one.

The lecture examines solving large sparse linear systems by elimination, emphasizing how variable ordering affects “fill in,” where zeros become nonzeros during elimination. Matrix sparsity can be represented by a graph whose nodes correspond to rows and whose edges represent nonzero entries; eliminating a pivot removes its incident edges while connecting its neighbors.

Reordering equations and unknowns corresponds to applying compatible row and column permutations. Examples include red-black ordering, minimum-degree ordering, and nested dissection. Minimum degree greedily selects a node with the fewest connections, while approximate minimum degree is commonly used in MATLAB. Nested dissection repeatedly divides a graph using small separators, processes the separated regions first, and leaves highly connected separator nodes until last. It can be advantageous for very large or three-dimensional problems.

Bandwidth reduction does not necessarily minimize fill: moving a dense row toward the center may reduce bandwidth while creating additional nonzeros. Fill can be measured by factoring a matrix into \(LU\), or \(LL^T\) for symmetric positive-definite matrices using Cholesky factorization, and counting nonzeros in the factors with MATLAB’s `nnz`. Sparse-ordering methods are often evaluated experimentally by comparing fill and operation counts.

Starting to save and invest early can build lasting habits and increase long-term wealth through time and compounding. Regular contributions, reinvested interest or dividends, and separating savings from spending can strengthen results and reduce the temptation to spend. Reviewing variable expenses and creating a budget may identify additional money for investing.
