Common options include far-post corners for headers; near-post corners for volleys, headers, or redirects; medium corners aimed centrally; top-of-the-arc pull-backs for shots or passes; short corners intended to draw defenders outward; skip-header corners flicked across goal; and direct-score inswingers aimed into the goal. Floated corners can also test a goalkeeper’s ability to claim high balls.

Coaches should select plays based on players’ kicking, passing, heading, timing, and aggressiveness. Training should progress from minimal attackers without defenders to full game-like situations with live defenders. Players should learn every role, use signals, adjust for wind, avoid unnecessary goalkeeper involvement, time runs properly, and prepare for rebounds, clearances, offside situations, and counterattacks. The kicker must wait for the referee and cannot touch the ball again until another player does.

Osteoarthritis involves cartilage degradation and low-grade joint inflammation, but lacks approved molecular diagnostics. This study developed and validated a Fluorescent Immuno-Lectin Assay (FILA) using five lectins to characterize lubricin glycoforms in synovial fluid and plasma. FILA showed acceptable recovery, reproducibility, dilution linearity, and agreement with mass-spectrometric glycan measurements.

In matched samples from 19 osteoarthritis patients, lubricin glycoform concentrations were substantially higher in synovial fluid than plasma, and their glycosylation patterns differed. Plasma lubricin showed relatively greater sialylation and glycan complexity and less Tn-antigen than synovial-fluid lubricin.

Among plasma samples from osteoarthritis patients and controls, most lectin-binding glycoforms did not differ significantly. However, SNA-binding lubricin glycoforms were decreased in osteoarthritis, including a significant difference in the SNA/MGL ratio. This alteration alone was considered insufficient as an osteoarthritis biomarker.

Higher BMI correlated positively with Gal-3-, MAA-, and SNA-binding glycoforms, indicating increased sialylation and complexity. Age correlated negatively with MAA- and SNA-binding glycoforms and positively with MGL binding. The findings indicate that plasma and synovial-fluid lubricin differ in concentration and glycosylation, while plasma lubricin glycosylation is associated with osteoarthritis, age, and BMI.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that it issued an April 24, 2019 press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2019. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under the Exchange Act. Chief Accounting Officer Frank H. Brod signed the report.

Michael Barnard argues that worsening hurricanes, wildfires, sea-level rise, and extreme weather will increase voter acceptance of human-caused climate change. Migration from affected areas could disrupt established political patterns and reduce Republican support. He predicts Republicans will eventually lose power unless they abandon climate-change denial, though accountability may not occur in the next elections.

Crews removed Gainesville’s “Old Joe” Confederate statue after months of relocation efforts, returning it to the United Daughters of the Confederacy. In Tampa, vandals splashed red paint and wrote derogatory comments at a private Confederate memorial park. The incidents followed intensified national debate and violence surrounding Confederate monuments in Charlottesville, Virginia.

Europe will launch Sentinel-3B on Wednesday as the seventh satellite in the EU- and ESA-funded Copernicus Earth-monitoring constellation. Paired with Sentinel-3A, it will continuously track ocean and coastal conditions, including sea levels, temperatures, pollution, ice and vegetation, while also monitoring inland waters and wildfires. Copernicus provides free environmental and disaster-response data. The programme’s 2008–2020 budget is about €7.5 billion, while Brexit creates uncertainty over Britain’s future participation.

A longitudinal study assessed pneumococcal carriage and household transmission among 121 community-dwelling adults aged 60–86 from 61 households. Participants provided saliva every two weeks for 10 weeks during the 2020/2021 and 2021/2022 seasons. Culture-enriched saliva was tested by qPCR, with piaB used to define pneumococcal positivity; samples were also evaluated for serotypes and respiratory viruses.

Of 1,088 tested samples, 52 (4.8%) were pneumococcus-positive, and 27 participants (22.3%) were colonized at least once. Both household members carried pneumococcus in two households during season one and three during season two, but the study found no clear evidence of adult-to-adult transmission. Recent contact with children, particularly those younger than 10, was strongly associated with carriage and acquisition. Contact with children under five and aged 5–9 corresponded to prevalences of 14.8% and 14.1%, respectively. Daily or every-few-days contact was associated with higher prevalence than infrequent or no contact. Contact with children under 10 tripled the acquisition rate, while frequent contact increased it sixfold relative to no contact.

The estimated mean time to acquisition was 358 days, and detectable colonization lasted an average of 17.7 days. Carriage rates were similar across study seasons despite changing COVID-19 restrictions. Serotyping was limited by incomplete assay coverage, low bacterial abundance, and cross-reactivity with non-pneumococcal Streptococci.

The findings suggest children were the principal source associated with pneumococcal acquisition in these older adults. Adult vaccination may therefore primarily provide direct protection rather than substantially reducing transmission among community-dwelling adults. The study’s small, predominantly white and highly educated sample limits generalizability.
Geoff Cameron called Stoke’s home match against relegation-threatened Hull a must-win after five winless games. Stoke sit 13th, eight points above the drop zone; Hull are 17th.

The Triangle & Two defense uses three zone defenders and two aggressive “chasers” to deny key shooters passes and rebounds. The Double Stack offense counters by positioning posts at mid-post with shooters behind them, creating baseline space and screening advantages.

Shooters read defenders by popping out for jump shots, curling to the basket, fading to the corner, or back-cutting. Against switches, the ball handler feeds the screener posting against a smaller defender. Entry variations include crosses, fake crosses, and single/double screens. The offense can continue into base-screen or side-screen actions.

Success requires coordinated execution of screens and post-ups, defensive recognition, nonverbal communication, timing, and experience. Recommended preparation includes breakdown drills, shell drills, and scrimmaging. Teams should scout opponents’ screen and post defenses, monitor adjustments after substitutions and timeouts, vary alignments and entries, move players around, and target weak defenders.

A Milwaukee woman said intruders kicked in her front door around 11 p.m. on New Year’s Eve but fled when her alarm sounded, apparently realizing they had targeted the wrong house. Police reported similar incidents nearby. The damaged door was boarded up, and the woman plans to improve her home security.

A phase 2 multicenter trial found that adding abatacept to standard graft-versus-host disease prevention nearly eliminated severe acute GvHD after mismatched unrelated donor stem cell transplants. Among 43 patients, grade III-IV acute GvHD occurred in 3% by day 100, compared with 32% for calcineurin inhibitor/methotrexate controls and 22% for those also receiving anti-thymocyte globulin. At one year, overall survival was 85% and disease-free survival 79%, exceeding both control groups. Abatacept blocks activation of effector T cells implicated in GvHD while preserving immune reconstitution; no major uncontrolled infections or increased relapse occurred. A second randomized, double-blind cohort of 140 matched unrelated donor transplant patients had completed enrollment, with results pending.

Amazon’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2015 reported Q3 net sales of $25.4 billion, up 23% year over year, operating income of $406 million versus a $544 million loss, and net income of $79 million versus a $437 million loss. For the first nine months, net sales were $71.3 billion, operating income was $1.1 billion, and net income was $114 million.

Q3 segment sales were $15.0 billion for North America, $8.3 billion for International, and $2.1 billion for AWS. Segment operating income was $528 million, a $56 million loss, and $521 million, respectively. AWS sales rose 78%, primarily from increased customer usage.

Operating cash flow totaled $9.8 billion for the trailing 12 months, while free cash flow was $5.4 billion. At September 30, Amazon held $10.7 billion in cash and cash equivalents, had total assets of $56.2 billion, long-term debt of $8.2 billion, and stockholders’ equity of $12.4 billion.

Amazon acquired companies for $393 million during the first nine months and acquired Elemental Technologies in October for approximately $296 million. It reported $33.9 billion of contractual commitments and continued to contest patent, copyright, and tax proceedings, including an IRS transfer-pricing adjustment that could produce approximately $1.5 billion in additional federal tax.

The AEGEAN study randomized 1,162 subjects initiating apixaban for atrial fibrillation to Primary standard of care (SOC) or an Additional Educational Program. At 24 weeks, 1,054 subjects completed follow-up and 9.3% had discontinued. In Part 2, 524 subjects were assigned to Secondary SOC or continued education; 1,003 completed 48 weeks, with 4.5% discontinuing after Week 24.

Baseline characteristics were comparable across groups. Median age was 74 years, 59.9% were male, and 96.4% had atrial fibrillation. Hypertension, diabetes, and coronary or peripheral vascular disease were common risk factors. Drug exposure, interruptions, dosing, and compliance were similar among groups; mean compliance exceeded 95% through Week 24 and 94% at Week 48.

At 24 weeks, mean adherence was 91.64% with Primary SOC and 91.88% with additional education, with no significant difference. From Weeks 24–48, adherence ranged from 87.51% to 88.41% across the three groups, again without significant differences. Adherence declined significantly during later treatment periods in both original groups. Persistence was approximately 91% at Week 24 and 85%–88% at Week 48, without significant group differences. Fully adherent subjects decreased from approximately 27% at Week 24 to approximately 15% at Week 48.

Safety outcomes were generally similar among groups. Before Week 24, about 51%–52% reported adverse events, while bleeding occurred in 6.5%–9.0%. Between Weeks 24 and 48, adverse events occurred in 33.8%–40.8% and bleeding in 3.2%–4.1%. Overall, 24 deaths were reported, including one additional death without an associated fatal adverse event.

The study found high adherence and persistence through 24 weeks, sustained to 48 weeks, but the proactive educational program provided no additional benefit.

Wednesday’s notable moves included gains for H&R Block, Southern and Brookdale, while Biogen, GameStop, Citizens Financial, Synchronoss and Anadarko declined amid executive changes, economic data, falling yields, accounting errors and lower oil prices.

President Obama said Syria’s civil war had killed over 100,000 people and displaced millions, while the United States had provided humanitarian aid, supported moderate opposition groups, and pursued a political settlement. He argued that the situation changed after the Assad government allegedly used sarin gas on August 21, killing more than a thousand people, including hundreds of children. He cited videos, witness accounts, military preparations, rocket launches from regime-controlled territory, and biological samples as evidence.

Obama said chemical weapons violate international law and threaten U.S. security by weakening global prohibitions, encouraging dictators and terrorists, endangering regional allies, and undermining efforts to prevent other weapons of mass destruction. He therefore supported a targeted military strike intended to deter further chemical attacks and reduce Assad’s capacity to conduct them. He emphasized that the action would involve no U.S. ground troops, open-ended intervention, regime change, or prolonged air campaign.

Although he believed he had authority to order strikes, Obama sought congressional approval, arguing that democratic support would strengthen U.S. action. He acknowledged public exhaustion after Iraq and Afghanistan and addressed concerns about escalation, retaliation, extremists within the Syrian opposition, and America acting as the world’s policeman.

Obama also announced that emerging diplomacy might eliminate Syria’s chemical weapons without force. Russia had expressed willingness to pressure Assad, while Syria had admitted possessing chemical weapons and indicated it might join the Chemical Weapons Convention. Obama asked Congress to postpone its authorization vote while the United States pursued a verifiable agreement through talks with Russia, allies, and the U.N. Security Council. The military would maintain pressure and remain prepared if diplomacy failed. He concluded that limited action was justified to defend international law, protect civilians, strengthen global security, and uphold American leadership.

Several users reported that £3.99 Childs Farm Baby Moisturiser significantly improved psoriasis and eczema. Laura Gray claimed her psoriasis disappeared within 24 hours, while Paige Sweeney said her three-year-old daughter’s longstanding eczema improved within days after other treatments failed. Joanne reported that regular use cleared her one-year-old daughter Kelisha’s severe eczema within four weeks. Company dermatologist Dr Jennifer Crawley said regular moisturising can soothe, hydrate and help heal eczema-damaged skin, though the condition may fluctuate.

Apple filed a Form 8-K on April 28, 2021, reporting financial results for its second fiscal quarter ended March 27, 2021. The related press release was attached as Exhibit 99.1. Chief Financial Officer Luca Maestri signed the filing.

President Trump addressed senior military leaders, praising Secretary Hegseth, General Caine and the armed forces while advocating a “Department of War” focused on strength, merit, readiness and a warrior ethos. He claimed military recruitment and morale had reached record levels, promised more than $1 trillion in 2026 defense spending, a 3.8% service-member pay raise, nuclear modernization, the Golden Dome missile-defense system, additional ships and development of the F-47 fighter. He also urged faster weapons production and military procurement reforms.

Trump credited his administration with mediating several international conflicts and pursuing agreements in Gaza and Ukraine, arguing that military strength deters war. He discussed NATO burden-sharing, arms sales, tariffs and increased foreign investment, while criticizing the Biden administration, the media and political correctness.

He described illegal immigration, drug trafficking, crime and civil unrest as domestic security threats, praised military and National Guard deployments in Washington, D.C., and proposed using forces in other cities and creating quick-reaction units. He emphasized defending the homeland, combating cartels and maintaining overwhelming conventional and nuclear capabilities, concluding that the United States military is the world’s strongest fighting force.
Clinical trials show oral GLP-1 drugs help people with obesity lose weight without injections.

Legal experts Shane Kilcommins and Eimear Spain criticised the proposed Communications (Retention of Data) Bill 2017 for omitting Murray Report recommendations on protecting journalists’ sources and establishing an independent, resourced body to oversee service providers. The bill requires district court authorisation for data requests but lacks the recommended High Court approval and strict limits for accessing journalists’ data. It retains retrospective High Court reviews previously criticised as inadequate, though it expands requirements for prior judicial authorisation.

The season comes down to one final game. Home-ice advantage is considered less important than knowing what must be done and continuing the team’s season-long pattern of bouncing back. Both teams earned their place, while prior experience, the first goal, and momentum may or may not matter. Players face a mentally draining psychological roller coaster and need rest and preparation. Uncharacteristic penalties were attributed to excessive emotion, frustration, and opponents’ provocations. A player’s availability remains uncertain pending rest and a morning skate. Growing hatred between the teams is described as a normal result of a long, competitive playoff series.

The GHCB protocol enables SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests to communicate with a hypervisor through VMGEXIT. A guest handling a #VC disables interrupts and preemption, registers and clears the GHCB, supplies required state, marks valid fields, and invokes VMGEXIT. The hypervisor processes the exit, updates the GHCB, and resumes the guest. Software must protect GHCB access against interruption, and separate or saved GHCB state is recommended for NMIs.

Non-Automatic Exit events generate #VC exceptions. Guests inspect the error code, provide required state through GHCB fields, and process returned results. Both guest and hypervisor reset VALID_BITMAP before marking fields valid. Hypervisors can request exception injection or report malformed input and other errors through SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2. Unsupported events use an “Unsupported Event” exit code.

SEV-ES guests must avoid unplanned exits before entering long mode or 32-bit PAE because encrypted memory prevents GHCB communication. CPUID or GHCB information requests can determine SEV support and the encryption-bit position. Hypervisors must expose required CPUID properties identifying virtualization, SEV support, encryption-bit position, and physical-address reduction.

Defined NAE operations include I/O, MSR access, hypercalls, MMIO, page-state changes, SNP firmware requests, AP creation, doorbell registration, IPI delivery, timers, APIC ID retrieval, VMPL switching, trusted-I/O requests, Secure AVIC backing-page management, and termination. I/O and MMIO operations may use the GHCB shared buffer as decrypted storage and may require multiple VMGEXIT calls. Page-state-change requests support private, shared, PSMASH, and UNSMASH operations and track partial completion in shared structures.

SNP guest requests use shared request and response pages. The hypervisor translates their addresses, manages response-page ownership, returns firmware status, and may rate-limit requests. Extended requests can return certificate tables in contiguous shared pages. TIO requests similarly exchange trusted-device information, measurements, certificates, and attestation data. AP creation assigns VMSA pages to create, update, or remove vCPUs and supports vCPU hotplug.

The SNP secrets page reserves an area for communication between operating environments, including 64-bit VMPL request sequence numbers, an AP jump-table address, and guest-defined data. EFI firmware can communicate SNP secrets and CPUID pages through a defined configuration table.

Traditional AP startup is constrained because measured and encrypted register state cannot be changed by the hypervisor. APs may use initial measured state, reset-hold protocols, and an AP jump table. With SNP AP Creation, guests can provide VMSA pages and directly control AP state. Without this feature, vCPU hotplug is unsupported.

For NMIs, the hypervisor must not intercept IRET, must intercept #DB, and must wait for an “NMI Complete” VMGEXIT before injecting another NMI. Hardware debug-register virtualization may use VMSA state; otherwise, DR7 accesses are intercepted and emulated. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

Restricted Injection uses a shared, host-owned #HV doorbell page. Its PendingEvent field represents interrupt vectors, NMIs, machine checks, and whether another signal may be sent; NoEoiRequired provides an EOI optimization. The host emulates APIC presentation, acknowledgement, in-service, and EOI behavior, while the guest atomically retrieves and clears pending events and validates vectors. Guests halt with interrupts disabled and inspect doorbell state after resuming. Non-cooperative host behavior can deny service but should not corrupt guest state.

After nearly 40 years of chronic back pain, five spinal fusion surgeries and limited mobility, 77-year-old Deanna Conley received a spinal cord stimulator implant through Washington University Pain Management Center. Electrodes placed in the epidural space pulse to block pain signals to the brain. Following a one-week trial, patients may receive a permanent battery-powered implant, rechargeable through the skin and adjustable by wireless controller. Conley reported dramatic improvement, abandoning her walker and regaining daily activities. Dr. Michael Bottros described the procedure as relatively low risk and said nearly all of his 40 to 50 implant patients in the past year experienced remarkable results. Data indicate benefits can persist for five years, though longer-term outcomes remain under study.

Rory McKelvie, 19, was found dead in Biggar, Lanarkshire; police are not treating his death as suspicious. Before his death, he publicly discussed mental health struggles, saying a doctor told him his condition was not severe enough for support and to return near “breaking point.” He also said someone had prevented him from taking his life in November and urged others to seek support from friends and family. His mother, girlfriend and others paid tribute to him.

This study compared the race-adjusted 2009 and race-free 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine equations using Truveta electronic health records from about 8.08 million U.S. adults tested between 2016 and 2023. CKD was defined as two estimated GFR values below 60, measured 60–365 days apart. Outcomes included differences in CKD stages 3a–5 and timing of identification, with adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, and social determinants of health.

Approximately 1.24 million patients met CKD criteria under either equation. The 2021 equation identified CKD earlier in 24% of Black patients and 0.7% of non-Black patients. Staging discordance was concentrated in earlier disease stages and was substantially greater among Black patients. Nearly half of Black patients classified as stage 3a by the 2021 equation did not meet CKD criteria under the 2009 equation, while half classified as stage 3b by the 2021 equation were classified as stage 3a under the older equation. Black patients had 126 times the adjusted odds of an increased CKD stage under the 2021 equation compared with non-Black patients. Included social determinants were not significantly associated with increased staging.

The authors conclude that removing race from GFR estimation enabled earlier CKD identification and higher staging for many Black patients. Limitations include incomplete capture of care outside participating systems and use of a comorbidity index not validated for this population.

Donald Trump faced criticism after defending his writing ability in a tweet containing spelling and grammatical errors. Tony Schwartz, ghostwriter of *The Art of the Deal*, said Trump could neither write nor read well and had contributed little to the book. J.K. Rowling also mocked the tweet. Separately, Trump was criticized for initially denying a request to lower flags after a deadly Annapolis newsroom shooting, though he later ordered them lowered.

Clinton County tied for 64th among Site Selection magazine’s 2017 “Top 100 Micropolitans,” which recognizes regions securing investment and job-creating projects. Ohio led all states with 16 ranked micropolitans. Four county projects, submitted by the Clinton County Port Authority and vetted by JobsOhio and Site Selection, represented $70 million in investment, 150 new jobs and 400 retained jobs. One project is the Bright Farms facility under construction in Wilmington.

Arsene Wenger hopes to fit new signings Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Henrikh Mkhitaryan alongside Mesut Ozil and Alexandre Lacazette in Arsenal’s attack, reflecting the club’s attacking identity. However, he stressed the need to improve defensively and find balance. Wenger said Ozil’s new £350,000-a-week contract was cheaper than signing a comparable replacement and remained affordable without relying on credit. Aubameyang’s transfer depended on Borussia Dortmund finding a replacement, while illness left him uncertain to face Everton. Wenger offered Lacazette no guarantees, insisting all players must compete for their places.

Edmonton police charged blogger Barry Kent Winters, 62, with wilfully promoting hatred after years of complaints and a 13-month investigation. The rare Criminal Code charge received written consent from Alberta’s deputy attorney general. Winters’ blogs targeted numerous ethnic, religious and social groups, activists and public figures with racist and derogatory language, violent fantasies and allegations. Police said the blogs had thousands of readers and a growing audience; courts ordered them removed as a condition of pre-trial release.

The passage welcomes police action and praises complainants but questions whether criminal prosecution is the best response to hateful speech. It cites the prolonged prosecution of Jim Keegstra as an example of charges giving an accused person greater publicity and a platform to claim martyrdom. Constitutional law professor Eric Adams says some criminal limits on speech may be reasonable but require a very high threshold. The author concludes that although the blogs encouraged violence and incited hatred, prosecuting Winters could threaten free expression and potentially amplify rather than suppress hate.

Enron’s impending bankruptcy disrupted global energy markets after Dynegy abandoned its takeover and credit agencies downgraded Enron to junk status. Exchanges in Australia, Germany, Scandinavia and Britain suspended or restricted Enron, while Nord Pool closed its positions without losses. Enron stopped most new trading, failed to deliver gas to German utilities and faced European job cuts and asset sales.

Enron’s overseas assets and operations remained uncertain, including projects in Brazil, India, Japan and Europe. Potential buyers expressed interest in Wessex Water, British power and retail assets, metals trading, and Enron’s Nordic business. The Teesside power station continued operating normally.

Regulatory and legal scrutiny increased. The SEC promised a swift investigation into possible accounting violations, federal prosecutors sought to monitor the inquiry, and congressional committees planned hearings. Reports highlighted Enron’s undisclosed $50 million JEDI partnership investment in bankrupt Costilla Energy and the potential complexity of resolving billions of dollars in derivatives.

Insurers could face more than $3 billion in Enron-related losses, while utilities and banks disclosed varying exposures. Dynegy maintained that it could acquire Enron’s Northern Natural Gas pipeline and prevent the unit from filing bankruptcy without its consent, though Enron disputed the claim and Fitch kept Dynegy on negative rating watch because of likely legal challenges and potential liabilities.

The Higgs mechanism explains how gauge bosons and fermions can acquire mass without adding explicit mass terms that violate gauge invariance. It uses spontaneous symmetry breaking, in which a scalar field has a nonzero vacuum expectation value. In a simplified U(1) model, this produces a massive gauge boson and a massive scalar field. The massless Goldstone boson disappears in the unitarity gauge and becomes the longitudinal polarization of the massive gauge boson.

In the Standard Model, a complex SU(2) scalar field with four degrees of freedom spontaneously breaks the SU(2) × U(1) symmetry. Coupling this Higgs field to the gauge fields generates masses for the W⁺, W⁻, and Z bosons, determined by their coupling strengths and the vacuum expectation value. The photon has no mass term and remains massless. Three Goldstone bosons are absorbed as longitudinal components of the W and Z bosons, while one massive scalar Higgs boson remains. The mechanism was proposed in the mid-1960s, and the Higgs boson was discovered at the LHC in 2012.

DAVV mistakenly sent Corporate Accounts papers to centres for a BCom (Hons) third-semester Corporate Law exam, delaying the test by about 30 minutes while replacements arrived. Students alleged the December 18 Corporate Accounts paper was leaked, but university officials denied it was served and said another set could be used if necessary. DAVV also rejected colleges’ demand to restore semester examinations for BCom (Hons), stating that, without new higher education department instructions, the course would remain under the annual system introduced in 2017-18.

Paula and John Larison sued the Public Water Supply District after Mrs. Larison stepped on a water meter lid in their yard, causing it to slide off and her leg to fall into the meter well. She suffered serious injuries. A district employee had read the meter nine days earlier but could not specifically recall replacing the lid, although he testified that he routinely checked each lid for secure placement.

The trial court granted summary judgment to the Water District on all claims based on sovereign immunity and insufficient evidence. The Missouri Court of Appeals held that the dangerous-condition exception to sovereign immunity could apply. Circumstantial evidence created a genuine factual dispute over whether the employee negligently replaced the lid or whether another person or force later displaced it. Because credibility determinations belong to the jury, summary judgment was reversed on the operator-negligence and related loss-of-consortium claims.

The court affirmed summary judgment on the claim that the Water District knew or should have known of the dangerous condition because there was no evidence it had notice that this lid was unsecured or that mowing caused its displacement. It also affirmed dismissal of the res ipsa loquitur claim because the lid, located in the Larisons’ accessible yard and inspected only monthly, was not under the District’s exclusive control. The case was remanded solely on the operator-negligence theory.

Gold steadied near $1,247 an ounce after its largest weekly decline since May as markets awaited an expected Federal Reserve interest-rate increase and guidance on future policy. Higher rates typically pressure gold by strengthening the dollar and raising the cost of holding non-yielding bullion. Hedge funds and money managers sharply reduced net long gold and silver positions, with silver posting a record contraction. Silver, platinum and palladium prices also declined slightly.

The $7 billion Strategic National Stockpile stores medicines, vaccines, antidotes and emergency supplies at secret warehouses for rapid deployment during biological, chemical, radiological, nuclear, infectious disease and natural-disaster emergencies. Its inventory includes antibiotics, smallpox and anthrax vaccines, influenza antivirals and nerve-agent antidotes. Warehouses can dispatch 50-ton emergency packages within 12 hours, while nearly 2,000 Chempacks are positioned nationwide for quick access.

Created in 1999, the stockpile has expanded beyond terrorism preparedness to respond to emerging diseases and natural disasters. It supplied antivirals during the swine flu pandemic and medical equipment and vaccines after hurricanes in Houston and Puerto Rico. Its more than 133,995 pallets include enough smallpox vaccine for every American, though its growing needs have strained the CDC’s budget.

The Trump administration plans to transfer oversight of the $575 million program from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to the Department of Health and Human Services’ assistant secretary for preparedness and response in October. Supporters say consolidating product selection, purchasing and emergency response under one office will improve efficiency, coordination, visibility and funding advocacy.

Critics, including public health officials and bipartisan members of Congress, fear the shift could disrupt established federal, state and local distribution relationships and politicize purchasing. They warn biotechnology companies may lobby for costly specialized products at the expense of broadly useful supplies such as antibiotics, gloves, syringes and influenza vaccines. Lawmakers have urged HHS to preserve a strong CDC role and questioned whether the transfer will improve public safety. Officials say the change is unrelated to CDC performance and will not alter emergency response procedures.

This Australian population-wide study assessed audiovestibular conditions following COVID-19 vaccination using spontaneous adverse-event reports from Victoria’s SAEFVIC system and a self-controlled case series of general-practice data from the POLAR platform. Adults were evaluated for first presentations of hearing loss, vertigo, or tinnitus within 42 days after vaccination, compared with baseline periods.

Among eligible records, vertigo was most frequent, followed by tinnitus and hearing loss. Spontaneous reporting rates were higher after adenovirus-vector vaccines than mRNA vaccines, particularly after the first adenovirus-vector dose. The self-controlled analysis found increased relative incidence of vertigo following mRNA vaccination and tinnitus following both adenovirus-vector and mRNA vaccination. No increased incidence of hearing loss was identified after either vaccine type.

Spontaneous reports were more frequent among females, while general-practice data showed no significant difference between sexes. Results differed between datasets for vertigo: spontaneous reports were higher after adenovirus-vector vaccination, whereas the self-controlled analysis detected increased incidence only after mRNA vaccination.

Potential confounding factors included concurrent COVID-19 infection, incomplete vaccination records in general-practice data, reporting bias, and limited clinical detail in spontaneous reports. The authors concluded that healthcare providers should be aware of possible vertigo and tinnitus following vaccination while noting that causality remains difficult to establish.

During October’s Fire Prevention Month, fire departments emphasize knowing two exits, keeping doors and windows accessible, and teaching children how to respond to alarms. Families should leave immediately, remain outside, never re-enter for people, pets, or belongings, and rehearse home fire drills.
John Whitfield’s application to vacate a 1992 appellate decision based on ineffective assistance of appellate counsel was denied because he failed to establish his claim.

Adidas and Refinery29 created one custom UltraBOOST X shoe for each state, designed by female artists and auctioned to benefit Women Win. Georgia’s women’s size 8 shoe, designed by Lizzie Darden, uses a peach theme with pink-orange coloring, green laces, and a plastic leaf. At publication, its bid was $350, compared with $1,000 for Ohio’s buckeye-themed pair.

Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days offers discounts across nearly the entire Kindle lineup. The Kindle Colorsoft is recommended for colorful libraries, comics, and graphic novels, while its Signature edition adds wireless charging, automatic front-light adjustment, and twice the storage. The second-generation Kindle Scribe combines an e-reader and digital notebook with smooth writing and three-month battery life. The 2024 Kindle Paperwhite is the best all-around option, offering a larger screen and warm light; its Signature edition adds premium features. The base Kindle provides an affordable choice with responsive performance, dark mode, and a front light. For children, the Colorsoft Kids includes a cover and one year of Kids+ content, while the cheaper Paperwhite Kids includes a cover and six months of Kids+.

The court unanimously affirmed Vu Ngo’s conviction on three counts of first-degree robbery. His claim of discriminatory jury selection was unpreserved and not reviewed in the interest of justice. The court also upheld denial of suppression, finding that initial police questioning and the brief hospital detention were lawful and did not constitute a forcible seizure. After another officer arrived with information from a nearby robbery and homicide investigation, police had reasonable suspicion to detain Ngo for questioning and a showup identification.

NVIDIA reported that David M. Shannon, Executive Vice President, Chief Administrative Officer and Secretary, will retire at the end of 2016. Brian E. Cabrera will then lead the legal team, while NVIDIA recruits a human resources leader.

China promotes basic education groups to reduce disparities caused by the movement of strong teachers and students toward resource-rich schools and regions. Typically, a prestigious core school supports ordinary member schools by providing administrators, experienced teachers, training, coordinated research, curriculum development, resource sharing, and teacher rotation.

Government backing and unified management can improve member schools’ educational quality, standardize assessment, and narrow regional gaps. Groups may also increase teachers’ job satisfaction, professional knowledge, teaching skills, and opportunities for collaboration. Students gain access to varied courses, extracurricular activities, innovative teaching, and exchanges that support creativity, higher-order thinking, and community belonging. Expanding prestigious-school resources through groups can also reduce public anxiety and demand for selective school enrollment.

However, imposing core-school culture may erase the traditions and distinctive characteristics of ordinary schools. Differences in teacher ability, student competence, and local circumstances can make advanced methods difficult to apply. Core schools may also face reduced motivation because expansion disperses resources, requires substantial financial and human investment, and increases management and evaluation burdens.

Suggested improvements include establishing equal, democratic relationships among schools; creating a standing committee of member-school leaders; strengthening communication and shared decision-making; encouraging two-way teacher rotation and training; recruiting qualified teachers; and developing online platforms for shared courses. Government policy, operational funding, and incentives for educators serving disadvantaged schools are also recommended. Education groups represent contractual, deeper cooperation between prestigious and non-prestigious schools, but sustaining collaboration while preserving each school’s individuality requires further study.

Britain’s FTSE 100 closed 0.4% higher after Brexit was formally triggered, supported by sterling weakness and gains in export-focused firms. The index is over 16% above pre-referendum levels, while the domestic-focused FTSE 250 rose 0.1%. 3I Group surged following a Morgan Stanley upgrade, London Stock Exchange gained after EU regulators blocked its Deutsche Boerse merger, and miners benefited from higher copper prices. Gold miners, AA and Acacia Mining declined.

Jeff Dasovich’s confidential email on Enron’s proposed response to California’s electricity crisis was returned because one recipient address was unknown and relaying was denied. The message outlined plans to circulate proposed legislation, build a supporting coalition, and pursue public relations. Enron’s proposals addressed distributed-generation barriers, DWR credit risks under AB1X, an anticipated 5,000 MW summer supply shortage, increased generation, demand reduction, restoration of direct access and retail competition, and staged rate increases to restore utility solvency. Attachments contained proposed AB1X amendments and CPUC talking points.

2019 presidential aspirant Thomas Wilson Ikubese joined the Alliance for New Nigeria on May 29, 2018, after leaving the National Conscience Party over alleged over-taxation. His YesWeFit Revolutionary Movement aligned with ANN following its adoption by the Nigerian Intervention Movement. Ikubese plans to contest the 2019 presidential election under ANN, described as a “Third Force,” and urged supporters and other young aspirants to join the party and unite against President Buhari’s administration.

This cross-sectional study examined MRI-visible perivascular spaces (PVS), a component of the brain’s glymphatic waste-clearance system, in 467 people with epilepsy and 473 healthy controls. Epilepsy subtypes included temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis (TLE-HS), MRI-negative temporal lobe epilepsy, extratemporal focal epilepsy, and idiopathic generalized epilepsy. PVS were segmented from 3T T1-weighted MRI using the PINGU deep-learning algorithm, and regional PVS volume fractions were compared while adjusting for age and sex.

All epilepsy subtypes showed substantially higher PVS volume fractions and numbers in the basal ganglia than controls, with increases of approximately 101–140% and large effect sizes. This difference persisted without regional volume normalization. No adjusted differences were found between epilepsy and control groups in total white-matter PVS burden. Enlargement was primarily found in the basal ganglia excluding the thalami; adjusted thalamic differences were not significant.

TLE-HS showed greater contralateral PVS distribution in total white matter and several lobes, but most asymmetry comparisons between groups were not significant. No PVS measure was associated with illness duration. The cross-sectional design prevents determining whether enlarged basal ganglia PVS precede seizures or result from them. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify whether recurrent seizures impair glymphatic function or glymphatic impairment contributes to epilepsy.

The passage defines GHCB communication for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests. During negotiation, the hypervisor places protocol-version and encryption-bit information in the GHCB MSR/VMCB. The guest handles intercepted CPUID operations through #VC, determines the encryption-bit position, configures encrypted page tables, allocates a shared GHCB page, and registers its GPA before using VMGEXIT. SEV-SNP guests should rely on firmware-validated CPUID-page information.

For VMGEXIT, the guest disables interrupts and preemption, clears prior GHCB data, marks required fields valid, and supplies exit information. The hypervisor maps the GHCB, processes the request, returns state, and resumes the guest. Non-Automatic Exits generate #VC; guests identify the event from its error code, populate the GHCB, invoke VMGEXIT, process returned results, and exit through IRET. Both parties must reset and correctly set the VALID_BITMAP. Hypervisors report malformed input, requested exceptions, and other errors through SW_EXITINFO fields.

Defined NAE operations include instruction emulation, MSR and hypercall handling, MMIO through decrypted shared buffers, page-state changes, SNP firmware requests, certificate-returning extended requests, AP creation, doorbell registration, IPI delivery, timers, APIC-ID discovery, VMPL switching, trusted-I/O requests, Secure AVIC backing-page management, and guest termination. Page-state changes support private/shared transitions and SNP RMP hints, with progress recorded so interrupted operations can resume. SNP guest requests use shared request and response pages, require response-page ownership transitions, and may be rate-limited. Extended requests return GUID-identified certificate data in contiguous shared pages.

SEV-SNP AP creation uses guest-provided VMSA pages and can support vCPU hotplug. Without it, AP startup requires preserved initial register state, reset-hold protocols, and potentially an AP jump table communicated between firmware and the OS. Restricted Injection requires AP creation rather than reset-hold handling.

The SNP secrets page contains a guest-reserved area for 64-bit request sequence numbers, AP jump-table information, and guest-defined data. EFI firmware can expose SNP secrets and CPUID pages through a confidential-computing configuration table.

NMI handling uses an “NMI Complete” message. Debug-register virtualization is supported when enabled; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and emulated. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

Restricted Injection uses a shared, host-owned #HV doorbell page. Its PendingEvent field conveys interrupt vectors, NMI, machine-check, and signaling state; NoEoiRequired supports EOI without VM exit. The host emulates APIC presentation and service semantics, while the guest atomically acknowledges events, validates vectors, and either clears the EOI-assist field or performs a VMGEXIT APIC write. Guests should execute HLT with interrupts disabled and inspect doorbell state immediately after resuming.

A seven-judge Supreme Court Bench ruled that repeated re-promulgation of ordinances subverts democratic legislative processes and constitutes constitutional fraud. Presidential and gubernatorial satisfaction in issuing ordinances is subject to judicial review. The majority held that ordinances must be placed before the legislature, which must assess their necessity, validity and approval. Ordinances cease six weeks after the legislature reconvenes unless earlier disapproved. Rights and liabilities after expiry require interpretation. In the Bihar teachers case, the Court barred recovery of salaries already paid.

The study examines how digitalization and personalized online informal learning contribute to formal design education. Digital technologies have expanded education beyond conventional, teacher-centered settings by enabling global, collaborative, synchronous and asynchronous learning through multimedia, software, algorithms and virtual platforms. In design education, these tools support rapid iteration, computational thinking, collaboration and practical skill development.

Using a literature review and case studies, the research compares two synchronous computational-design programs: the five-day “Introduction to Computational Design” workshop and the 21-day “Sustainability through Computational Design” course. Both serve students and professionals, use Rhino and Grasshopper, and combine lectures, practice and discussion. The longer course additionally includes assignments, environmental analysis, collaborative work and jury evaluation.

Online informal programs provide focused, applied and multidisciplinary learning, convenient information access, discussion opportunities and professional networking. They can strengthen creativity, problem-solving, self-confidence and the ability to address social, environmental and aesthetic design concerns. Participants can personalize their learning environments and acquire skills that distinguish them professionally.

Limitations include restricted participation, economic and technological inequalities, software and internet requirements, inconsistent teaching and assessment methods, reduced physical interaction, isolation, and intensified competition. Certificates and learning outcomes are often excluded from formal transcripts, limiting recognition within compulsory education. The study argues that integrating structured informal programs and certificates into higher education could reinforce formal design education and expand personalized learning. Its conclusions are theoretical and limited by differences among organizations and instructors; experimental studies with students and professionals could provide more objective quantitative evidence.

University of Surrey researchers report that solar energy is now the cheapest large-scale power source, costing as little as £0.02 per unit in sunny countries. Global installed solar capacity exceeded 1.5 terawatts in 2024. Lithium-ion battery prices have fallen 89% since 2010, making solar-plus-storage systems competitive with gas plants and improving reliability. However, grid congestion can cause wasted energy when supply exceeds demand. Researchers identify smart grids, AI forecasting, regional connections, improved materials such as perovskite cells, sustained policy support, and international collaboration as essential for accelerating solar integration.

AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine provides optional SEV/SNP extensions for moving memory pages between physical memory tiers while preserving guest physical addresses. It requires IOMMU enablement and supports migrating pages undergoing DMA and SNP-protected guest pages inaccessible to the hypervisor.

TMPM offers commands for querying capabilities, moving I/O or hypervisor pages, moving SNP guest pages, and issuing no-ops. Commands use a separate ring buffer and can process up to 128 non-order-dependent page entries. Per-page and overall statuses report success, partial success, failure, or retry conditions. Pages generally require 4KB alignment; direct 2MB migration has command-specific limitations.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO coordinates with IOMMUs, pauses DMA, copies page contents, and updates host page-table entries. In SNP-enabled systems it applies only to hypervisor-owned pages. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages without supporting concurrent DMA: source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, destinations must be Pre-Migration, and their states are exchanged appropriately after migration.

Performance improves with batches of at least 16 pages and is highest with 128-page commands. Keeping the ring buffer populated and limiting interrupts also improves throughput. IOMMU structures, pinned vIOMMU storage, ring buffers, and argument pages are non-migratable.

The driver initializes, pauses, resumes, and shuts down the ring buffer through mailbox registers. Commands may execute asynchronously and in parallel, so completion order is not guaranteed. Shared interrupts report queue thresholds, empty queues, completion, command errors, invalid write pointers, and ring-buffer memory errors.

TMPM firmware can be reloaded only after operations stop and the ring buffer is dismantled. Reloaded firmware must be the same or newer version, and software must verify the ENGINE_READY status afterward. EPYC Family 19h reload uses a firmware image, reload header, and PSP mailbox command.

Errors are reported in commands, migration entries, status registers, or Machine Check Architecture. Hardware failures may leave an entire command’s pages unrecoverable, allowing software to attempt state preservation before reboot.

The work presents a correct-by-construction fault-tolerant voter for synchronous N-modular redundant measurement systems in avionics control applications. The voter selects a reliable input while handling measurement noise, transient faults, permanent faults, and limited changes between consecutive measurements. It may retain a previous output during transient failures, isolates units whose faults persist beyond a configurable limit, and avoids unnecessary switching of the prime input unit.

The fault model includes self-reported bad health and deviation faults exceeding a noise threshold, while excluding Byzantine faults. A simultaneous-fault hypothesis limits new faulty behavior per cycle, and reliable operation requires a minimum number of non-permanently faulty units. The output includes the selected reading, its age, a validity status—valid, unidentifiable, or not valid—and preserved state data.

Sixteen functional requirements define sound and complete fault identification, permanent-fault isolation, output generation, prime-unit switching, validity, and output-age limits. The paper derives theoretical limits for fault identification when the ground truth is unknown and provides tighter partial-classification rules that reduce erroneous isolation of healthy units. Output age remains bounded while minimum reliability assumptions hold.

The voter is modeled as a five-state transition system covering normal operation, transient prime-unit faults, operation with isolated units, temporary inability to identify a healthy replacement, and insufficient surviving units. Its configurable parameters include unit count, noise threshold, fault persistence limit, and maximum simultaneous faults.

The design and requirements are implemented and machine-verified in the Rocq theorem prover using higher-order logic and dependent types. Proofs are embedded in voter states and transitions. Verification of all requirements takes approximately 23 seconds on the reported system. The verified implementation extracts to 362 lines of OCaml, with a state transition taking about 3 milliseconds, and can also be extracted to Haskell or Scheme. Future directions include hierarchical redundancy management and verified fault handling for asynchronous distributed voting units.

The study developed and evaluated an integrated environmental education model based on multiple intelligences for expanded educational opportunity schools in Nakhon Pathom Primary Educational Service Area 2, Thailand. Data were collected through questionnaires, interviews, observation, SWOT analysis, and achievement assessments involving 364 junior high students, 44 teachers, three school directors, and a 30-student evaluation group.

Community environmental concerns included chemical residues from agriculture, water and air pollution, indiscriminate waste disposal, and cultural effects attributed to technological advancement. Teachers demonstrated higher overall environmental education learning levels than students, scoring 4.48 versus 3.95. Students showed particular needs in awareness, participation, skills, and evaluation ability.

The model incorporated nine forms of intelligence and emphasized community-based environmental study, awareness, knowledge, attitudes, practical skills, evaluation, and participation. SWOT analysis identified supportive school communities, stakeholder interest, sustainable development policies, and information technology as strengths or opportunities. Weaknesses and threats included industrial and household pollution, limited continuity of environmental education, urbanization, climate-related changes, and difficulties building conservation awareness.

The model’s process and outcome efficiency was 81.51/82.11, exceeding the specified 80/80 criterion. Expert assessment found high content validity and construct validity. Post-learning achievement was significantly higher than pre-learning achievement at the 0.05 level, while students reported high overall satisfaction with the model. Qualitative findings indicated that varied, practice-based group activities supported environmental understanding, critical thinking, participation, self-expression, and positive environmental values.

The study recommends integrating environmental education across subjects through real-world observation, practical problem-solving, and holistic learning activities. Future research should develop sustainable environmental education standards, curricula, and management approaches for schools.
A non-inverting comparator uses two resistors and VREF. Output switches high above VIN1 and low below VIN2; hysteresis equals VIN1 minus VIN2.

Doctors warned that eye cancer is often detected late, complicating treatment and risking blindness or death. India has few specialized facilities and only about 10–11 trained ocular oncologists. Retinoblastoma, affecting roughly one in 20,000 children under five, may cause squinting or a white pupil. Early detection can save both the child and eyesight.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that it issued a January 26, 2015 press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2014. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under the Exchange Act.

An anonymous 1893 notice condemns foreign religions as false, rebellious, disruptive of traditional propriety, ancestral rites, patriotism, and social order. It accuses religious leaders of hypocrisy, neglecting parents and funeral customs, unstable marriages, greed, exploiting students, and using preaching as a pretext for travel and book sales. The notice demands that they gather their possessions and leave, threatening an armed attack on a specified date if they refuse.

In a subsequent dispatch, Mr. Heard reports that Confucian followers in Seoul petitioned the king to suppress or exterminate the Tong Hâk for spreading corrupting false doctrines. Although there had been concern that Western religions might also be denounced, they were not included. The king replied that the government would handle the matter and advised the petitioners to study their own professed principles.

The strategy sells the S&P 500 after a 20% decline from its all-time high and buys after 18 consecutive closes above the 200-day SMA during a bear market, holding until the next bear market. Backtested from 1927, it produced 12 signals, reflecting 12 bear markets. Results included a 7.24% CAGR, 15.26 standard deviation, 0.24 Sharpe ratio, 60% maximum drawdown, 87.38% market exposure, and 8.28% risk-adjusted return. Excluding 1929, maximum drawdown fell to about 25%. Average returns after a signal were 9.54% at six months and 21.84% at one year, with positive 12-month returns after every signal. It outperformed the Golden Cross in absolute terms, but not risk-adjusted terms, generated fewer signals, and spent 30% more time invested. The backtest excluded dividend- and split-adjusted data.

St. George welcomed an 11-member delegation from sister city Ibigawa, Japan, continuing nearly three decades of cultural exchange. Four visitors, including elite runners Kenji Miyazaki and Mitsue Tomita, planned to compete in the 2017 St. George Marathon. Mayor Jon Pike and Vice Mayor Sunao Isaji exchanged ceremonial gifts during a luncheon, while delegates attended local events, stayed with host families and toured regional attractions. St. George planned to send officials and top runners to Japan in November for the 30th annual Ibigawa Marathon.
The player described scoring after a line change and passing sequence with Teemu, then said the team remained disciplined after a strong second period and scored again to secure the game.

Ola and Uber drivers in Delhi-NCR threatened a one-day strike over fares of Rs 6 per km and 25% company commissions, demanding fares near Rs 20 per km. The Delhi High Court barred two unions from disrupting cab services. The Sarvodaya Drivers’ Association planned a protest march and warned of an indefinite strike, while major autorickshaw and yellow-black taxi unions denied participating.
Rain Bird’s waterproof, submersible 9V WPX battery-operated irrigation controller supports 1, 2, 4 or 6 zones, offers LCD programming and zone-stacking, and operates up to two years.

Kuwait expects to complete cleanup of an oil spill near Ras al-Zour this week. No further oil patches were found, while the spill’s cause and size remain unknown. Khafji Joint Operations said its facilities were unaffected and initiated emergency measures and an aerial survey.

After a year of optimism driven by economic strength, corporate profits, tax cuts and deregulation, investors grew wary as stocks fell and Treasury yields rose. Strong wage growth raised inflation concerns and fears that central banks may withdraw the cheap money supporting markets since 2009. Low interest rates had encouraged investment in corporate assets to help companies raise capital, expand and hire.

A study spanning nearly 11,500 species and 270 million years found that birds and mammals adapted to temperature changes two to three times faster than reptiles and amphibians. Their ability to regulate body temperature and protect developing offspring likely helped them evolve and expand into colder regions. However, these historical adaptations occurred over millions of years and may not keep pace with rapid climate change. Animals also face pollution, hunting, habitat loss, and invasive species, contributing to extinction rates far above normal. Researchers hope the findings will clarify how long-term evolutionary patterns relate to present-day adaptation and help predict species’ responses to environmental pressures.

Market corrections—declines of 10% to 20%—have occurred about once a year since 1900, averaging a 13.5% drop and lasting 54 days. Fewer than one in five become bear markets, so selling during corrections can mean missing a rebound. Bear markets average a 33% decline, last about a year, and can be emotionally difficult, but historically they end.

From 1980 through 2015, the S&P 500 averaged a 14.2% intra-year decline yet produced positive annual returns in 27 of 36 years. This record suggests market declines are routine even amid wars, terrorism, and financial crises. Warren Buffett argues that U.S. population and productivity growth support continued long-term wealth creation. Investors should understand market behavior, remain patient, communicate with advisers during volatility, and accept responsibility for decisions rather than reacting fearfully to short-term declines.

The passage specifies SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guest-hypervisor mechanisms. Guests can request execution at another VMPL using VMPL-specific VMSAs and GHCBs; unavailable VMSAs require errors. SEV-TIO lets SNP guests bind trusted devices, validate device information and reports, configure MMIO and IOMMU, and exchange measurements, certificates, and attestation data through shared contiguous pages. Hypervisors must report required storage and validate page capacity.

Secure AVIC uses guest-owned APIC backing pages registered per vCPU. Guests may request termination and must report unsupported negotiated events. SEV-ES support is identified through specified CPUID properties.

Because encrypted, measured vCPU registers cannot normally be changed, AP booting requires predefined initial state, reset-hold protocols, and an encrypted, aligned AP jump table. SNP AP Creation instead lets guests create or update AP state using guest-supplied VMSA pages, supports Restricted Injection, simplifies AP parking, and enables vCPU hotplug.

NMI handling uses a guest “NMI Complete” message. Hardware debug-register virtualization may save state in the VMSA; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and emulated. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

With SNP Restricted Injection, host notifications use a shared #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. The host emulates APIC interrupt presentation, acknowledgement, in-service, and EOI behavior, while the guest atomically retrieves events, validates vectors, handles maskable and non-maskable events, and completes EOIs either by clearing the assist field or issuing an X2APIC EOI write. HLT handling must avoid missed interrupts, and malformed host behavior can cause guest denial of service but not guest-state corruption.
Two teens were arrested after a stolen-plate Subaru sped through Frankston roadworks and was pursued to Bayswater. A third person remains at large; one suspect was bitten by a police dog.

The invention concerns augmented-reality tracking for image-guided surgery. A healthcare professional wears a head-mounted display that overlays virtual patient anatomy and a surgical tool on the patient. A camera tracks patient and tool markers, potentially determining position and orientation from a single viewpoint without triangulation. When the primary camera loses sight of either marker, a processor uses data from another healthcare professional’s head-mounted camera or a stationary tracking device. Previously determined positions and inertial-measurement data may maintain alignment during occlusion. Multiple tracking sources may also be combined to improve tool-position estimates. The system may use high-speed cameras, reflective markers, infrared illumination, and computer-readable instructions implementing the tracking and image-generation methods.

The passage advocates moderate reform through government supervision rather than ownership of industry. Capital and labor combinations are considered necessary, but they should be rigorously regulated to prevent public harm. Laws indiscriminately prohibiting combinations are described as ineffective and damaging, particularly when railroad cooperation is needed for fair operation. Railroad agreements should be permitted if approved by the Interstate Commerce Commission and publicly disclosed, and Congress should amend laws that cannot be enforced without disrupting commerce.

Taxation should reflect the federal system: localities should tax real estate, states should tax franchises granted to intrastate corporations, and the national government should levy taxes that states cannot effectively impose. In addition to tariffs and excise taxes, the passage recommends graduated inheritance and, if possible, income taxes. Wealthy individuals should bear their proper share because they receive special benefits from government, but taxation must be administered with justice, moderation, and equal treatment of rich and poor.

Penn State will prohibit student-led trips by its Outing, Caving and SCUBA clubs after a risk assessment classified activities in remote areas as hazardous. Student leaders criticized the lack of consultation and questioned the rationale and higher cost of university-run alternatives. The university said student safety is its priority, the review was not prompted by injuries, and staff are discussing transitions and continued support with club leaders.

California’s $43 billion in long-term power contracts lost an estimated 15% in value as Western forward prices fell amid lower demand, conservation and a slowing economy. Sellers were unlikely to cancel favorable contracts, though California secured some June–September power at reduced prices.

Options volatility declined as investors sold contracts to generate income in an expected range-bound market. A large bullish Enron spread involved buying June 55 calls and selling June 50 puts while Enron shares rose to about $54.

Saudi Arabia selected eight international companies for three natural-gas projects requiring roughly $25 billion. ExxonMobil, Shell, BP and Phillips received South Ghawar stakes; ExxonMobil would lead the Red Sea project with Enron and Occidental; and Shell, TotalFinaElf and Conoco won Shaybah stakes. Leaders for South Ghawar and Shaybah were expected by June 5. The projects reopened Saudi energy development to substantial foreign investment and aimed to expand gas, electricity, desalination and petrochemical capacity.

Android 8.0 Oreo introduced system-level Picture-in-Picture (PiP) Mode, allowing supported apps to display video or navigation in a movable floating window while other apps are used. Supported apps included Chrome, Duo, Play Movies & TV, Maps, WhatsApp, YouTube, and VLC, though YouTube required a Red subscription.

To play YouTube in PiP through Chrome, open YouTube in desktop mode, play a video in full screen, reveal the navigation buttons, and tap Home. The floating window can be moved, paused, closed, expanded, or dismissed by dragging it downward. If PiP does not work, enable it under Settings > Apps & notifications > Advanced > Special app access > Picture-in-picture.

The radiation-hardness-assured TPS7H500x-SP family provides fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM control for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full bridge. Primary and synchronous-rectifier outputs have roughly 150-mA peak capability, so external gate drivers are recommended. OUTB and SRB operate only on supported devices with a 50% duty-cycle limit; synchronous outputs remain off during soft start until SS exceeds 1 V.

Dead time and leading-edge blanking are fixed at 50 ns typical on TPS7H5003-SP and programmable by external resistors on applicable devices. Pulse skipping addresses minimum-on-time issues when COMP is below 0.3 V and the previous duty cycle was below 25%. Equal pulse skipping between OUTA and OUTB preserves transformer volt-second balance. Depending on device, DCL selects 50%, 75%, or 100% maximum duty cycle.

CS_ILIM supports PWM generation and overcurrent protection. At 1.05 V, cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins and charges CHICC. When CHICC reaches 0.6 V, switching stops and soft start is discharged; operation restarts after CHICC falls from 1 V to 0.3 V. A minimum 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor is recommended. FAULT shuts down switching when its voltage exceeds 0.6 V for the required pulse width and restarts after the voltage falls below 0.5 V and an approximately 15-cycle delay. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C typical, with restart below 160°C.

Programmable slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle. The recommended compensation equals the inductor falling-current slope. The transconductance error amplifier supports Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation.

A synchronous push-pull TPS7H5001-SP design example uses 500-kHz switching, 5-V output, approximately 25-ns dead time, 50-ns blanking, 7.5-ms soft start, a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 170-V primary and 80-V synchronous GaN FETs, a 0.47-µH output inductor, and about 2.3 mF output capacitance. Overcurrent limiting begins near 35 A using a 7.5-Ω sense resistor, while Type 2A compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover.

The controllers require a regulated 4-V to 14-V supply and at least 0.1 µF of close ceramic input bypassing. Layout guidance emphasizes minimizing high-current and switching loops, separating analog and power grounds with a single connection, routing sensitive signals away from switch nodes and output-drive traces, placing bypass, filtering, sensing, and compensation components close to the controller, and connecting CFP backside metallization to AVSS through multiple vias.
Annual Fund gifts support the rule of law, independent courts, legal representation, bias reduction, access to justice, and rights protection.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2018 reported quarterly net sales of $61.1 billion, up 16% year over year, and net income of $13.8 billion, up from $11.0 billion. Diluted earnings per share rose to $2.73 from $2.10. Six-month net sales were $149.4 billion, with net income of $33.9 billion.

Quarterly iPhone revenue increased 14% to $38.0 billion as unit sales rose 3%; Services revenue grew 31% to $9.2 billion; Other Products grew 38%; iPad revenue increased 6%; and Mac revenue was flat. Sales increased across all geographic segments, led by Japan at 22% and Greater China at 21%. Gross margin was $23.4 billion, or 38.3%, compared with 38.9% a year earlier. Operating expenses rose to $7.5 billion.

At March 31, 2018, Apple had $367.5 billion in assets, including $45.1 billion in cash and equivalents and $222.2 billion in marketable securities. Total liabilities were $240.6 billion, including $109.9 billion of current and long-term debt. Six-month operating cash flow was $43.4 billion. Apple spent $32.9 billion on share repurchases and $6.5 billion on dividends during the period.

The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act reduced Apple’s federal tax rate and imposed a deemed repatriation tax. Apple recorded $9.3 billion of income tax expense for the six-month period, including a $2.6 billion provisional estimate related to the legislation. Its quarterly effective tax rate declined to 14.5%. Apple expected to place approximately €13 billion plus €1 billion of interest into escrow related to the European Commission’s Irish state-aid decision while appeals continued.

Apple had used $199.6 billion of its existing $210 billion repurchase authorization as of quarter-end. On May 1, 2018, its board authorized a new $100 billion repurchase program. The company also disclosed supply-chain concentration risks and ongoing VirnetX litigation involving verdicts of $440 million and $503 million, which Apple was challenging.

Ukraine signed an agreement with Bitfury Group to move government electronic data onto a blockchain platform, described by Bitfury as the largest government blockchain project to date. A pilot covering state registers, public services, social security, public health and energy is expected to launch late this year, followed by expansion into all areas, including cybersecurity. Ukraine aims to improve transparency, accountability and efficiency while becoming a leading blockchain nation. Bitfury previously piloted a blockchain land registry in Georgia.

Investors will focus on five themes: the Bank of England’s inflation and growth outlook amid sterling’s resurgence and rising bond yields; Australian and New Zealand policy meetings and Chinese economic data; a widening U.S. trade deficit and possible government shutdown; diverging U.S. and European earnings expectations; and emerging-market rate decisions, with possible cuts in Russia, hikes in Mexico and Romania, and unchanged rates but tougher messaging in India.

The Texas Supreme Court held that Mastin Latham’s 1839 instrument conveyed an absolute, unconditional one-half interest in the land to William F. Henderson rather than creating an executory contract. The stated consideration concerned services already performed, and the provision requiring equal division with Latham choosing a half was a partition arrangement, not a condition causing forfeiture. Even if treated as a subsequent condition, no authorized party properly enforced a forfeiture.

Thomas Henderson established a complete chain of title through a sheriff’s sale of William Henderson’s interest. Because the deed vested title, defenses based on stale demand, abandonment, or delay were inapplicable absent sufficient adverse possession.

The limitation defenses also failed. Ten years’ qualifying possession had not accrued, and Beaton lacked privity with the occupants whose possession he invoked. The five-year defense lacked evidence of tax payments. The three-year defense failed because the occupants held as Latham’s tenants rather than under Beaton’s asserted title or color of title; later-acquired title could not transform prior naked possession into qualifying possession. Defects in Beaton’s deed from Wood’s heirs further undermined his claim.

The judgment for the defendants was reversed, and the case was remanded to determine the parties’ respective partition rights more accurately.

HoopTactics presents baseline, sideline, and full-court out-of-bounds plays designed to create high-percentage shots with multiple options or flow into predetermined continuity. Teams should practice rare end-game full-court situations, including inbounding against pressure. Strategies include keeping plays simple, using the best inbounder and shooters, anticipating defensive tactics, and substituting appropriately. When possible, advance the ball and call timeout in the front court. When protecting a lead, use a baseline play to inbound safely and place the best free-throw shooters on the court.

The Seventh Circuit affirmed summary judgment against former Orland Park police officer Joseph McGreal. McGreal alleged that he was fired in retaliation for protected speech at a November 2009 village board meeting and that defendants intentionally inflicted emotional distress. The defendants maintained that he was terminated for misconduct, including lying under oath, insubordination, reckless conduct, violating a no-contact order, and obstructing an investigation.

The court held that McGreal provided no admissible evidence that defendants knew of his speech or that it motivated his termination. He also failed to show that the defendants’ stated reasons for firing him were pretextual; suspicious timing alone was insufficient. His emotional-distress claim likewise failed because he offered no evidence of extreme and outrageous conduct or severe distress and described his distress as “garden variety.”

Maddie Sabourin, an 18-year-old Georgia high school senior, learned she is a kidney match for her grandfather, Sam Senseney, 63, who has spent six years on the transplant list and undergoes dialysis three times weekly. After doctors initially considered her too young, she convinced them to allow the donation. Sabourin has promoted organ donation through pageantry and raised $7,500 for the American Kidney Fund. They will meet doctors next week to schedule surgery, hoped to occur within a month.

Kyle Freeland pitched 5 1/3 innings and doubled during a three-run fourth as the Colorado Rockies defeated the San Francisco Giants 11-4. Every Colorado starter recorded a hit, while David Dahl hit his first career pinch-hit homer during a four-run seventh. Trevor Story tripled, and Nolan Arenado, Gerardo Parra and Ian Desmond contributed RBI doubles.

Evan Longoria hit two solo homers and Buster Posey added another for San Francisco. Giants starter Jeff Samardzija left after one inning with shoulder tightness. Rookie Dereck Rodriguez, making his major league debut, allowed four runs in 3 1/3 innings before a Desmond line drive struck his shin. San Francisco committed four errors, including three by Kelby Tomlinson.

Giants pitcher Madison Bumgarner was scheduled for a second minor league rehabilitation start as he continued recovering from a broken hand.

Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF) co-founded crypto trading firm Alameda Research in 2017 and crypto exchange FTX in 2019 with Gary Wang. Nishad Singh led engineering at FTX while also working at Alameda; Caroline Ellison later led Alameda. FTX specialized in crypto derivatives and leveraged trading and issued its own token, FTT. By early 2022, it was the world’s second-largest crypto exchange, valued at $32 billion, with more than nine million customer accounts.

FTX claimed its automated risk-management system protected customers, while SBF promoted regulation and effective altruism. During the 2022 crypto downturn, FTX and Alameda financed distressed crypto businesses, strengthening SBF’s public image as an industry backstop.

According to regulatory complaints and guilty pleas, FTX secretly diverted billions of dollars in customer funds to Alameda. Wang and Singh altered software to give Alameda a nearly limitless credit line, permit negative balances, and exempt it from normal liquidation procedures. Customer funds were used for Alameda’s trading and loan repayments, venture investments, real estate, political donations, and personal expenditures. Alameda’s collateral included large quantities of illiquid, internally issued FTT tokens whose reported values were not supported by a broad market. Singh also admitted inflating FTX’s 2021 revenue by approximately $50 million and making illegal political contributions.

FTX’s collapse accelerated after CoinDesk published Alameda’s balance sheet on November 2, 2022, revealing heavy dependence on FTT.
