Body-camera footage from an August 19 mistaken-identity arrest shows former Grand Rapids Officer Kevin Penn pressing an AR-15 muzzle against a suspect’s head after the man was tasered. Another officer intervened, and police later reported Penn’s conduct. Kent County Prosecutor Chris Becker condemned the untrained technique but declined criminal charges. Penn resigned, while the suspect was charged with resisting arrest and released.

The European Central Bank is expected to keep interest rates at historic lows and maintain its €30 billion monthly bond-buying programme until September amid sluggish inflation and renewed economic risks. Inflation was 1.3 per cent in March, below the ECB’s target, while a stronger euro, potential US trade tariffs and slower business momentum pose concerns. Despite these risks, eurozone growth is forecast at 2.4 per cent in 2018, making abrupt policy changes unlikely. ECB President Mario Draghi may emphasize downside risks to curb expectations of an early rate increase, while pursuing a gradual exit from stimulus.

Magda Enriquez secretly joined Nicaragua’s Sandinistas in 1976, helped found their women’s association, AMNLAE, and later represented it on the Council of State. Raised in a prosperous family and educated in the United States, she studied journalism and economics before founding Nicaragua’s first school for children with intellectual disabilities. Discovering that malnutrition caused many disabilities led her to work in Managua’s slums and embrace liberation theology.

After police and landowners violently suppressed a 1978 peasant protest, poisoning children and leaving ten dead before treatment, Enriquez sought military training despite her earlier peace activism. Her political commitment ended her marriage, but she takes pride in balancing revolutionary work with raising five children and an adopted child, supported by neighbours, colleagues and the party.

Enriquez acknowledges that the revolution did not immediately eliminate women’s problems but believes it created opportunities to address them. She also participated in international delegations preparing Nicaragua’s election procedures, viewing democracy as a new experience for the country. Her public and family life is presented as challenging claims that women cannot reconcile political activity and motherhood.

Retirees and financially independent early retirees (FIRE) risk exhausting their portfolios because of unfavorable return sequences, excessive withdrawals, poor diversification, and unexpected market events. An example beginning in 2000 shows that withdrawing an inflation-adjusted 5% annually from a US large-cap portfolio depleted $1 million by 2017, as early losses and continued withdrawals prevented recovery.

Sequence risk means that the order of returns affects long-term compounding. A cited simulation of historical S&P 500 returns found widely varying 25-year outcomes despite strong average returns. Lower withdrawal rates substantially improved portfolio survival: 4% remained vulnerable, while 3% recovered after nearly failing in 2009.

The 4% rule, developed by William Bengen for conventional retirees, may be less suitable for FIRE participants because their longer retirement periods increase exposure to adverse events. Diversification across markets and asset classes can reduce risk, although historical correlations may change and backtests involve hindsight. Edward Thorp suggested a 2% inflation-adjusted spending limit for funds intended to last indefinitely.

The article concludes that retirement sustainability depends on conservative withdrawals, diversification, frugality, planning, and a substantial margin of safety.

Companies use experienced hosts and promoters to improve engagement at exhibitions and events. Professionate is an online event staffing platform connecting companies, recruitment agencies, and temporary workers worldwide. Employers can review candidate profiles, images, ratings, and reviews, while candidates can upload profiles, browse vacancies, and apply directly. The company also offers professional event hosting and promotion services in Dubai.

Police charged Jonathan Miles, 33, after allegedly finding marijuana plants, controlled substances and smoking devices in his home; he also allegedly cared for his daughter while impaired. Separate cases involved charges against Glen VanDerSchaaf for indecent assault, Tyran Ellis for corruption of minors, and Gilberto Isaac-Suarez following an alleged violent domestic break-in.

Seventy-five Hinsdale South High School seniors were named Illinois State Scholars, recognizing top academic achievement. Selection considers ACT/SAT scores, unweighted GPA and class size after junior year.

The U.N. warned that Yemen’s war and months of unpaid teacher salaries could prevent up to 4.5 million children from finishing the school year, increasing risks of child recruitment and early marriage. More than 166,000 teachers have not been paid since October. The salary crisis followed the government’s relocation of the central bank from Houthi-controlled Sanaa, amid mutual accusations over blocked payments and looting.

FDA approved a second generic version of mifepristone. Amgen reported that Repatha reduced combined risks of cardiovascular death, heart attacks, and strokes in a 12,000-patient trial, potentially supporting wider PCSK9 inhibitor use. The biotech roundup also highlights NIH efforts to reduce animal testing and industry policy developments.

This study compared self-reported PCL-5 and clinician-administered CAPS-5 PTSD assessments in 100 adults: 56 males and 44 females. Participants completed the PCL-5 before a trained interviewer administered the CAPS-5. Analyses examined sex, civilian versus military trauma, correlations between measures, predictive value, deviation from an ideal regression line, and diagnostic misclassification.

Overall PCL-5 and CAPS-5 scores were significantly correlated, but alignment was stronger for females (Rho=0.907) than males (Rho=0.655). CAPS-5 symptom severity did not differ significantly by sex or trauma type. Male scores deviated significantly from the ideal regression line, whereas female scores did not. PCL-5-based classifications disagreed with CAPS-5 classifications for 26.8% of males and 11.4% of females, most often because the PCL-5 indicated PTSD when the CAPS-5 did not.

Correlations were stronger among participants with civilian trauma (Rho=0.885) than military trauma (Rho=0.523), a pattern observed within both sexes, although only four females had military trauma. The findings suggest clinicians should consider sex and trauma type when interpreting PCL-5 results, particularly for male and military populations, and avoid relying solely on self-report measures.

Limitations included the sample size, the small number of females with military trauma, and recruitment limited to the southeastern region. Further research is needed to determine the causes of discrepancies and establish broader generalizability.

Channel 4’s documentary *The Super Orgasm* follows five women who report having dozens of orgasms in one sexual encounter. Experiments examining arousal, brain waves, and brain blood flow suggested the participants were easily aroused and maintained activity associated with multiple orgasms. However, the research involved few participants, lacked controls, and was not considered scientific.

Experts interviewed questioned whether “super orgasms” differ meaningfully from multiple orgasms. They emphasized that orgasm frequency, intensity, and patterns vary widely among women. Some experience separate peaks, while others have continuous waves of arousal. Although the featured women may easily experience numerous orgasms, experts described them as uncommon outliers and rejected the implication that all women could or should achieve 100 orgasms.

The Times reported that intercepted calls involved former Trump campaign chairman Paul Manafort and Russian intelligence officers. Manafort denied knowingly speaking with Russian intelligence or involvement with Russia’s government. U.S. intelligence concluded Russia sought to help Trump win the election, which Russia denied. Rep. Elijah Cummings called the report alarming. The report followed national security adviser Michael Flynn’s resignation over calls with Russia’s ambassador concerning sanctions. The White House maintained no evidence had changed Trump’s denial of campaign contacts with Russians.

Amazon is reportedly considering layoffs affecting up to 15% of its 10,000-plus-person PXT human resources division, with additional cuts possible in its consumer business. The total number and timing remain unclear, and Amazon declined to comment. The company is reducing employee costs while planning more than $100 billion in capital expenditures for cloud and AI infrastructure. CEO Andy Jassy has said AI-driven efficiencies will reduce Amazon’s corporate workforce. These proposed cuts are reportedly distinct from Amazon’s routine attrition process. Amazon previously eliminated at least 27,000 corporate jobs from late 2022 into 2023, but separately plans to hire 250,000 seasonal warehouse and logistics workers for the holidays.

American Surety Company filed an involuntary bankruptcy petition against John Jacob Beechwood. A jury found that Beechwood was insolvent and had committed acts of bankruptcy, including transferring his farm to his wife to hinder, delay, or defraud creditors. Beechwood claimed immunity as a farmer under the Bankruptcy Act.

Although Beechwood lived on an operating farm and participated in agricultural work during his leisure time, he had primarily worked as a lawyer and business executive, earning most of his income from employment and legal services. His farming activities produced substantially less income and were largely managed by an employed farmer. The court held that, when the acts of bankruptcy occurred, Beechwood was not personally deriving the principal part of his income from farming as required by the amended Act. His later full-time farm work did not alter his status on the relevant dates. The court rejected his cited precedents, denied the farmer defense, and directed entry of an order adjudicating him bankrupt.

Cover 3 is a common zone defense using four underneath defenders and three deep defenders. The cornerbacks cover the outside deep thirds, while the free safety covers the deep middle. Three linebackers and a rolled-down strong safety traditionally defend the hook, curl, and flat zones. Deep defenders prioritize staying above vertical routes, while underneath defenders force short throws that the defense can rally to tackle.

The scheme balances pass and run defense. Compared with Cover 2, it adds a third deep defender while allowing a safety to move near the line of scrimmage as an eighth run defender. Its balance makes it especially popular in high school and college football.

Cover 3 limits deep gains but is vulnerable to short passes in the flats, seam routes, four-vertical concepts, and perimeter runs. Four vertical routes can overload the three deep defenders, while seam routes create uncertain responsibilities near the hash marks. On perimeter runs, bailing cornerbacks and blocked safeties can expose the edge, requiring athletic defenders who can play effectively in space.

Variations include flipping the safeties’ assignments; fire-zone defenses that combine zone coverage with five or more pass rushers, sometimes dropping defensive linemen underneath; and Cover 3 Buzz, where the rolled-down safety covers the middle hook-to-curl area rather than the curl-flat. Pattern-reading systems such as Rip/Liz blend zone responsibilities with man-like reactions to routes, helping defend vertical and crossing concepts.

The lecture establishes sequential characterizations of continuity. For \(f:S\to\mathbb R\) and \(c\in S\):

- If \(c\) is not a cluster point of \(S\), every function \(f\) is continuous at \(c\).
- If \(c\) is a cluster point, \(f\) is continuous at \(c\) exactly when \(\lim_{x\to c}f(x)=f(c)\).
- \(f\) is continuous at \(c\) exactly when every sequence \(x_n\in S\) converging to \(c\) satisfies \(f(x_n)\to f(c)\).

The sequential criterion is proved in both directions, with the converse using contradiction: failure of continuity produces a sequence approaching \(c\) whose function values remain a fixed positive distance from \(f(c)\).

The lecture directly proves that sine is continuous using
\[
|\sin x-\sin c|\le |x-c|,
\]
then derives continuity of cosine from \(\cos x=\sin(x+\pi/2)\). It also presents a function distinguished by rational and irrational inputs that is discontinuous everywhere, using the density of rationals and irrationals to construct sequences approaching any real number with incompatible function values.

Continuity is preserved under sums, products, quotients when the denominator is nonzero, and compositions. These results follow from the corresponding sequence-limit properties. Consequently, power functions and polynomials are continuous, as is
\[
\frac{1}{3+\sin^4 x}.
\]

The next topics announced are the minimum and maximum theorems for continuous functions on closed bounded intervals and the intermediate value theorem.

The President transmits documents requested by the House concerning the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, including previously withheld instructions to U.S. commissioners. The commissioners were authorized only to secure Mexico’s ratification of the Senate-amended treaty, not to negotiate changes. Mexico approved the amended treaty before formally receiving the commissioners, relying solely on explanations previously supplied by the Secretary of State.

The subsequent protocol recorded conversations but neither government treated it as part of or a modification to the treaty. Its explanations affirmed that the amended ninth article protected the civil, property, and religious rights of inhabitants of ceded territories; deletion of the tenth article preserved valid Mexican land titles without reviving expired grants; and deletion of part of the twelfth article did not prevent Mexico from assigning its claim to the $12 million owed by the United States. Because these explanations accorded with the ratified treaty, the President deemed no further action necessary.

S. E. Mezes reported progress on “The Inquiry” and circulated a memorandum outlining research for a peace conference. Topics included war-breeding areas, national conditions and aspirations, international governmental arrangements, world organization, laws of war, reparations, international trade routes, diplomacy, and conference procedures. The Inquiry could assist with boundaries, governments, assessment of doubtful states, economic arrangements, minority protections, equal economic opportunity, international law, and diplomatic history. Required boundary work was identified for Poland, Alsace-Lorraine, Trentino, Trieste, Austria-Hungary, the Balkans, and Turkey; possible boundary work covered parts of Russia, Slesvig, Belgium, Luxemburg, Africa, and Latin America. Governments would need establishment in Poland and Austria-Hungary and might require attention in Russia, the Balkans, and Turkey. Other regional concerns included economic arrangements, state viability, and protections for minorities or weak peoples across Europe, Africa, Asia, the Pacific, and Latin America.

The address affirms America’s founding principles of equality, liberty, and collective self-government, arguing that each generation must adapt them to contemporary challenges. It calls for broad-based prosperity, a stronger middle class, modernized government and education, affordable health care, reduced deficits, and continued social protections. It urges action on climate change and leadership in sustainable energy, while advocating national security through military strength, law, diplomacy, alliances, and support for democracy and human dignity.

The speaker emphasizes unfinished work toward equal pay for women, equal treatment for gay people, accessible voting, immigration reform, and children’s safety. Rejecting political absolutism and delay, the address calls on citizens to participate through voting and public debate, act with common purpose, and preserve freedom and opportunity for future generations.

The report analyzes historical, current, and projected trends, revenues, growth, competition, risks, opportunities, policies, and economic factors in the global meat starter culture market. It segments products into maturation and surface starters and applications into meat, poultry, seafood, and others. Regional coverage includes the United States, China, Europe, Japan, Southeast Asia, India, and the rest of the world. It also examines production, pricing, supply, demand, technological developments, SWOT, investment feasibility, and leading manufacturers to support market participants and stakeholders.

On September 9, 2020, Amazon elected retired General Keith B. Alexander to its Board of Directors and Audit Committee. Alexander founded IronNet Cybersecurity and previously led U.S. Cyber Command and the National Security Agency. He received restricted stock units for 288 Amazon shares, vesting in three equal annual installments beginning November 15, 2021, subject to continued board service, and entered into Amazon’s standard director indemnification agreement.

The passage reports a Brazilian mouse study examining genetically modified Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) spore-crystals expressing Cry1Aa, Cry1Ab, Cry1Ac or Cry2A. Researchers found blood-cell changes, anemia, suppressed bone-marrow proliferation and abnormal lymphocyte patterns, with effects becoming more pronounced after 72 hours. Cry toxins reportedly caused adverse effects without alkaline activation, and the lowest tested Cry1Ab dose induced hypochromic anemia. The authors said the findings suggest possible hematological risks to vertebrates and called for further research before declaring Bt toxins safe for mammals. The passage also raises concerns about combined exposure to Cry toxins and glyphosate residues, criticizes biotechnology companies and regulators, and advocates GMO labeling, bans, consumer action and participation in protests against Monsanto.

December incentives on fuel-efficient vehicles include leases from $159 per month and discounts up to $18,100. Kia offers up to $5,000 off the 2017 Optima Hybrid, while the Optima Plug-In leases for $249 monthly and qualifies for government incentives. Hyundai’s Sonata Plug-In costs $289 monthly, and Chevrolet’s Volt leases for $273 with applicable tax credits and California benefits. Californians can save $18,100 on a Kia Soul EV+ or lease a base model for $159 monthly. Chevrolet Bolt EV leases start at $303 in select regions. Nationwide, the diesel Chevrolet Equinox LT receives a $4,000 discount and achieves 39 mpg highway. Southern California buyers can get $2,000 off the Toyota Yaris iA, reducing its price to about $15,000.

Progress Software held its Q3 fiscal 2025 earnings call on September 29, 2025. Investor relations chief Michael Micciche introduced CEO Yogesh Gupta and CFO Anthony Folger. The company said discussions of outlook, strategy, products, cost initiatives, and ShareFile integration were forward-looking and subject to risks. Financial figures were generally non-GAAP unless stated otherwise.

The paper proposes a computationally tractable Bayesian framework for community detection that avoids pre-specifying the number of communities and reveals hierarchical network structure. It recursively bipartitions a network using model-based MCMC inference and stops when a Bayes factor favors a model without further community structure.

The framework is demonstrated with stochastic block, edge exchangeable, and latent space models, allowing network properties to be represented through their likelihoods. For stochastic block models, the authors establish that recursive bipartitioning under Erdős–Rényi modularity is strongly consistent when the expected subnetwork degree divided by the logarithm of subnetwork size diverges, and weakly consistent when the expected degree diverges. No theoretical consistency guarantees are provided for the other two model classes, whose performance is instead evaluated through simulations.

The paper derives Gibbs-sampling procedures for each model, applies the method in simulation studies and to a stroke patient transfer network, and positions it as a more general and scalable alternative to direct Bayesian hierarchical modeling and recursive spectral clustering.

Founded by Herbert Henry Martyn in Cheltenham in 1888, H H Martyn & Co became a major centre of craftsmanship and engineering, employing over 1,000 people by 1910. Its work included furniture, stained glass, stone, plaster, ironwork, sculpture, cars, ships and aircraft. Notable commissions included Marble Arch’s gates, work for royal palaces, Selfridges’ frontage, House of Commons furnishings, the Cenotaph and fittings for more than 100 ocean liners, including the Titanic and Queen Mary.

During the First World War, aircraft production led to the creation of the Gloster Aircraft Company. Martyn’s also contributed to Sir Henry Segrave’s Golden Arrow land-speed car, manufactured Wolseley cars and developed the Unibus scooter. Between 1920 and 1937, it produced most of Britain’s commissioned decorative metalwork and later cast major sculptures.

Bought by Maples in the mid-1930s, the company gained military contracts during the Second World War but suffered after 1945. Declining British shipbuilding led Maples to sell its assets and close Martyn’s in 1971, though its work remains visible worldwide.

From 1826 onward, U.S. naval officers made friendly visits to Hawaii to address American deserters, claims, and relations. Captain Thomas ap Catesby Jones negotiated Hawaii’s first formal treaty with a foreign power in 1826, though the United States never ratified it. Later American vessels promoted peaceful relations and intervened on behalf of persecuted Catholic converts. In 1839, French commander Laplace threatened hostilities unless Hawaii protected Catholics and signed a commercial treaty; Hawaiian authorities complied, averting violence. British pressure also intensified after consul Richard Charlton’s complaints. In February 1843, Lord George Paulet seized the islands for Britain and forced King Kamehameha III to cede them. A commission then governed and exercised sovereign powers. U.S. Commodore Kearney protested the cession and infringements on American rights. After Rear-Admiral Thomas arrived and conferred with the King, Britain disavowed Paulet’s seizure and restored the Hawaiian flag on July 31, 1843.

Researchers found strong evidence that WASP-121b, a hot Jupiter about 880 light-years away, has a warm stratosphere. Hubble observations detected glowing water molecules indicating that temperatures increase with altitude, reaching about 4,500 degrees Fahrenheit (2,500 degrees Celsius). Nearly twice Jupiter’s size, WASP-121b orbits its star every 1.3 days.

The finding is considered the clearest evidence yet of an exoplanet stratosphere and demonstrates that distant planetary atmospheres can be analyzed in detail. Current technology favors studying large, extremely hot gas giants, but future observatories may enable similar analysis of smaller, cooler, Earth-like planets and their atmospheric molecules. The study was published in Nature.

Winthrop University will receive $1.1 million as part of a five-year, $20 million National Science Foundation award shared by 10 South Carolina institutions. The highly competitive MADE in SC initiative supports complex-materials research, including optical, magnetic, electronic and biomaterials. Winthrop’s funding will provide 36 summer student research experiences, conference support, faculty research funds, and $330,000 for equipment and upgrades. Faculty projects will examine nanoparticles, optical materials, supercapacitors, photocatalysis, proteins and other materials with potential applications in energy, water treatment, lasers and regenerative medicine. Researchers will also connect material synthesis with computer modeling to predict useful structures. The grant supports faculty including project director Maria Gelabert, Fatima Amir, Clifton Harris, Jason Hurlbert and Robin Lammi. Winthrop will additionally offer two-week summer workshops for regional high school teachers to expand materials-science education and outreach.

Average True Range (ATR) is a volatility indicator developed by J. Welles Wilder Jr. It is commonly used for stop-loss placement, position sizing, assessing market conditions, and identifying potential breakouts. ATR is typically calculated as a 14-day moving average of true ranges and can be computed in Python using pandas_ta. The article backtests a 14-day ATR strategy on unadjusted SPY data, holding the asset during high volatility and selling during low volatility. The strategy delivered better risk-adjusted performance than buy-and-hold but had a similar drawdown. Its results were not highly promising, though combining ATR with other indicators might improve them.

Coach Sutter said the emotional seven-game Chicago series, overtime periods, late travel, media obligations, and altered practice schedule contributed to fatigue. He noted lineup changes and several players experiencing their first Stanley Cup Final may have required adjustment. Kyle brought strong energy, but the team must improve and avoid repeatedly chasing leads. Sutter praised Mike Richards’ acceptance of roles, Jonathan’s focus, and a young player’s expanding responsibilities and potential. He emphasized learning ice-time management, shot selection, penalty killing, opponents, practice habits, and nutrition. He described Madison Square Garden as a distinctive venue and said the Kings receive strong attention in Manhattan Beach. During the first period, he adjusted combinations after recognizing that several players were struggling.

A University of Bristol study found that the chloroplast lineage separated from its closest cyanobacterial ancestor more than 2.1 billion years ago in low-salinity environments. About 200 million years later, chloroplasts formed an intimate symbiotic relationship with eukaryotic hosts. Marine algae diversified much later, around 800–750 million years ago. The findings suggest complex organisms such as algae first evolved in freshwater before colonizing marine environments and may improve understanding of early life and the carbon cycle.

NASA will broadcast a six-hour ISS spacewalk on August 17, beginning at 10:00 a.m. EDT. Expedition 52 cosmonauts Fyodor Yurchikhin and Sergey Ryazanskiy will exit around 10:45 a.m. to deploy five nanosatellites, including one testing a 3D-printed casing and another commemorating Russian space milestones. They will also collect exterior residue samples and install handrails and struts. It is Expedition 52’s only planned spacewalk and among the year’s longest.

The NHS Patient Charter combines patients’ legal rights, NHS pledges and patient responsibilities. It affirms care based on need and generally free at the point of use, with exceptions including some prescriptions, dentistry and eye care.

Patients have rights to equal access, appropriate treatment, waiting-time standards and alternatives when standards are missed. Care should be delivered by qualified staff in safe, clean, regulated settings, with suitable food, hydration and continuous quality improvement. Patients may access NICE-recommended treatments when clinically appropriate, receive routine vaccinations and expect local funding decisions to be fair, evidence-based and explained.

The Charter protects informed consent, refusal of treatment, clear information about risks and benefits, privacy and secure handling of health information. Patients may choose a GP practice, request a preferred doctor, compare services, participate in treatment and end-of-life decisions, and receive facts, an apology and support when mistakes occur.

Complaints must be acknowledged and properly investigated. Patients may escalate concerns to the Ombudsman, seek judicial review of unlawful decisions and claim compensation for negligent harm.

Patients are responsible for looking after their health where possible, respecting staff and others, following or discussing treatment plans, attending appointments, and participating in vaccination and screening. The Charter presents the NHS as a partnership based on fairness, trust, accountability and shared responsibility, particularly amid waiting lists, staffing shortages and financial pressures.

Anne-Marie D’Amico was among 10 people killed when a van struck pedestrians in Toronto; 15 others were injured. Police arrested 25-year-old Alex Minassian, who was due in court. Police said the attack appeared deliberate, but the motive remained unknown. Investigators continued identifying victims and seeking witnesses.

On February 8, 2022, NVIDIA, SoftBank, and SVF Holdco mutually terminated NVIDIA’s agreement to purchase Arm due to significant regulatory challenges. SoftBank and SVF Holdco will retain NVIDIA’s $1.25 billion prepayment, while NVIDIA will retain its 20-year Arm license. NVIDIA expects to record a $1.36 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal 2023.

A retrospective cohort study estimated outcomes and health-system costs for children admitted with clinical measles to Uganda’s Mulago National Referral Hospital in 2018. From 536 eligible charts, 267 were systematically sampled. Median patient age was one year, 63% were under one, and median hospital stay was four days.

Complications occurred in 69.3% of patients, most commonly severe pneumonia, gastroenteritis, and conjunctivitis. Thirty children (11.3%) died; most deaths occurred among infants, and 44% of those who died were not immunized.

Average direct healthcare cost per patient was US$33.13, including blood tests, radiology, treatment, and supplies. Average overhead cost was US$81.37, mainly for human resources, producing an estimated total cost of US$114.50 per case. Costs were significantly higher among males, patients with comorbidities, those hospitalized longer than 15 days, and those who died.

The study concluded that measles admissions involved frequent complications, high mortality, and substantial healthcare costs compared with vaccination costing less than one dollar. It recommended stronger measles immunization efforts. Limitations included reliance on clinical rather than laboratory diagnoses, retrospective records, exclusion of family and societal costs, and conduct at a single public referral hospital.

Neo-Nazi website the Daily Stormer lost domain registration services from GoDaddy after publishing an article attacking Heather Heyer, who was killed during the Charlottesville counterprotest, and celebrating her alleged killer. GoDaddy said the article could incite violence and violated its terms. The site transferred its domain to Google, which soon also canceled its registration for terms-of-service violations, though the site remained active at publication.

Neither company hosted the website’s data. Its host was concealed through Cloudflare, which had faced criticism for supporting the site and allegedly sharing complainants’ personal information with founder Andrew Anglin. Cloudflare called some sites’ content repugnant and said it was cooperating with law enforcement.

The Daily Stormer also claimed it had been hacked by Anonymous, but Anglin later said he had regained control. Separately, the Southern Poverty Law Center sued Anglin for allegedly coordinating harassment against Jewish real estate agent Tanya Gersh and her family. Anglin has not participated in the case, and his whereabouts remain unknown. A successful suit could allow seizure of his assets and potentially shut down the website.

The disclosure presents a recommendation-model training and recommendation system intended to improve top-N ranking performance while reducing training data volume, resource use, overfitting, and class imbalance. Sample sets contain positive and negative samples with user, object, and label features. Positive samples are added to a training set, while negative samples are selected according to probabilities calculated from one or more factors: differences between positive and negative estimated scores, distances between their feature vectors, and changes in ranking indicators after exchanging their rankings.

Negative-sample probabilities may be normalized by the maximum probability and compared with random numbers, or samples may be selected by probability ranking. The resulting training set is used with algorithms such as FTRL, logistic regression, or field-aware factorization machines to train a recommendation model. A trained model may generate estimated scores for later sampling and retraining, creating an iterative process.

During recommendation, the model calculates scores for candidate objects using user and/or object features, ranks the objects in descending score order, and recommends the first M objects. The disclosure also describes training and execution devices, processors, memories, storage media, computer-program products, and corresponding apparatus units implementing these methods.

Tests using a HUAWEI APPGALLERY dataset and ranking measures including NDCG@5, NDCG@10, P@5, and P@10 reportedly showed better results than training without sampling, random sampling, dynamic negative sampling, and optimized logistic-regression sampling.

Aqua Terra filed a preliminary prospectus across Canada, excluding Québec, for an initial public offering led by TD Securities, Canaccord Genuity and RBC Capital Markets. Share quantity and pricing remain undetermined, and completion is not assured. The offering is not registered or publicly available in the United States. Aqua Terra provides water disposal services to Canadian and U.S. onshore oil and gas producers, with infrastructure across seven hydrocarbon-producing regions in British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Texas and North Dakota.

The High/Low zone offense combines three-player perimeter passing with continuous interior high/low rotations. It can begin from multiple alignments, creates matchup problems through post movement, opens outside shots when defenses collapse, and uses weakside attacks, accurate passing, shooting, and offensive rebounding.

In the basic continuity, the point passes to a wing and moves opposite. The wing seeks the rolling post, short corner, or flashing high post. If no interior pass is available, a post steps out for ball reversal while another cuts, rolls, or flashes, continuing the action on the weakside. Post players may shoot, feed baseline cuts, pass inside, or kick and skip the ball to perimeter shooters.

Entry options include Dribble Clear, 1-4 Slice, Mid Screen, and Horns. These use back cuts, on-ball screens, dribble penetration, post rolls, and reversals to establish the continuity.

For late-clock situations or plays after timeouts, the offense can flow into specials. Pin Down uses two down screens for shooters with post-up options. Weakside Double creates a double screen, middle flash, lob opportunity, or corner kick-out. Vegas uses a high double screen to produce a skip pass, perimeter shot, post roll, or shooter popping out.

Major drugmakers are expected to meet Donald Trump Jr. and administration officials at a BlinkRx-hosted summit, raising concerns that companies are being steered toward the direct-to-consumer prescription service tied to Trump Jr. Separately, Pfizer’s private drug-pricing agreement with the administration has prompted other manufacturers to pursue deals, though their effect on U.S. prescription prices remains uncertain.

The paper presents a proof-of-concept for analyzing instant-messaging data in criminal investigations. It combines Neo4j knowledge graphs, Whisper speech-to-text transcription, a Named Entity Recognition and Linking pipeline, and semantic search through Neo4j and the DAVE faceted-search interface. Chat metadata, messages, audio transcripts, and extracted entities are integrated to support relational queries, keyword searches, entity filtering, visualization, and editable annotations.

The approach was tested on two investigations containing more than 2,500 chats and large volumes of messages and attachments. Whisper Large performed best in preliminary speech-recognition testing. Entity extraction enriched the graph and enabled additional search filters, although initial NER accuracy was unsatisfactory due to instant-messaging language characteristics and requires in-domain fine-tuning. Investigators valued graph visualizations, combined relational and textual search, audio transcription, and semantic browsing. Current limitations include entity-extraction quality, technical failures on very long chats, and the expertise needed for Neo4j queries. Future work includes improving the pipeline, developing simpler and conversational interfaces, and extending enrichment to images and videos. The system is intended to assist, not replace, investigators, with traceable results, human correction, restricted data access, and verification against original evidence.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU, based on the Ampere architecture and TSMC’s 7 nm process, targets AI and HPC workloads. Its implementation contains 108 streaming multiprocessors, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, five HBM2 stacks, and 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1,555 GB/s bandwidth.

Third-generation Tensor Cores provide twice the dense Tensor throughput per SM of V100 and support FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. TF32 accelerates FP32-based training without script changes, while FP16 and BF16 offer higher mixed-precision throughput. FP64 Tensor Cores deliver peak throughput of 19.5 TFLOPS. A100’s 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity compresses weights, reduces memory traffic, and doubles Tensor Core throughput by skipping zeros, with virtually no inference accuracy loss in evaluated networks after pruning and fine-tuning.

Each SM includes 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory. New asynchronous copy instructions transfer data directly from global to shared memory, reducing register use and allowing computation overlap. Hardware-accelerated asynchronous barriers support producer-consumer pipelines and synchronization among arbitrary thread subsets. Additional improvements include simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, faster atomic operations, warp-level reductions, and task-graph acceleration.

A100 has a 40 MB L2 cache, 6.7 times larger than V100’s, with 2.3 times its read bandwidth. L2 residency controls prioritize persistent data, while Compute Data Compression can improve DRAM and L2 bandwidth by up to four times and effective L2 capacity by up to two times. HBM2, L2, L1, and register files use SECDED ECC protection.

Multi-Instance GPU technology partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute, cache, memory-controller, and memory resources. This provides predictable quality of service, fault isolation, and support for VMs, containers, processes, and multi-tenant environments. Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances, support MPS, and migrated between compatible GPU Instances.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth per A100, twice V100’s aggregate bandwidth, with enhanced error detection and recovery. PCIe Gen 4 supplies 31.5 GB/s per direction on x16 connections and supports SR-IOV virtualization.

Other hardware includes five NVDEC video decoders, a five-core NVJPG JPEG decoder, and an optical-flow accelerator. CUDA 11 supports A100 features including new Tensor Core formats, sparsity, MIG, asynchronous operations, task graphs, cooperative groups, and L2 residency controls.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs, six NVSwitches, 4.8 TB/s aggregate bidirectional interconnect bandwidth, and up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance. MIG can expose up to 56 isolated accelerators per DGX A100. Its software stack includes CUDA, the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC software, deep-learning frameworks, TensorRT, RAPIDS, and HPC tools.

Charlie Tillett explains how startups should build financial projections to understand business assumptions, cash needs, pricing, costs, staffing, distribution, and growth. Financials serve as a company scorecard and help founders identify key operational drivers, even though projections will not be exact.

A business model can be viewed as an income statement expressed as percentages of revenue. It should include revenue, cost of goods sold, sales and marketing, R&D, general and administrative expenses, and operating profit or EBITDA. Founders should compare mature projections with similar companies, examine gross margins and revenue per employee, and estimate early years through detailed hiring and spending plans. Technology companies often spend 10%–20% of revenue on R&D and 5%–15% on G&A, while staffing commonly represents 50%–66% of expenses.

Sales forecasts should be constructed from the bottom up using factors such as sales staff, customer visits, conversion rates, and units sold rather than assuming a percentage of a large market. Models should use formulas wherever possible and include quarterly projections for sales, cost of goods sold, staffing, departmental expenses, capital spending, and cash. A practical estimate of required funding is cumulative operating losses plus capital expenses. Customer payment delays should also be reflected when estimating runway.

Distribution strategy can materially change revenue, expenses, and operating profit. Pricing should give customers enough benefit to justify adopting a product rather than capturing all the value created. Founders should build models themselves instead of relying on automated planning software, because the exercise develops understanding of the business. They should present one best estimate rather than multiple best- and worst-case plans.

Venture investors generally seek significant ownership, investments, and returns within five to seven years. Investor ownership equals the investment divided by the pre-money valuation plus the investment. Each financing round dilutes existing shareholders, and investors may also require preferred-share rights, board representation, and a 10%–20% employee option pool. Raising more capital than the market opportunity supports can create conflict because investors need a sufficiently large exit.

Equity should incentivize future work, so founders and employees should generally vest over three or four years. Suggested post-dilution equity ranges include approximately 5%–10% for CEOs, 1%–2.5% for vice presidents, 0.25% for senior managers, and 0.10% for senior individual contributors, with higher grants for founding team members. Tillett also recommends experienced financial leadership by the first venture round, arguing that a CFO can improve financing terms and reduce dilution.

UNC Chapel Hill reinstated professor Dwayne Dixon after a threat assessment found no basis to conclude he threatened the university community or violated policy. Dixon, active in counterprotests and gun-rights advocacy, was placed on leave following allegations and calls for his firing over past political affiliations.

The passage specifies SEV-ES and SEV-SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocols. Guests can use MSR-based requests before establishing a GHCB for CPUID values, SEV information, AP reset hold, GHCB address registration, page-state changes, VMPL switching, feature discovery, unregistration, and termination. CPUID requests return one register per VMGEXIT and exclude nonzero sub-leaves and function 0x0000000d.

SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB guest physical address before first use. They may request a hypervisor-preferred address, register another shared page, or unregister the current address. Negotiation examples describe obtaining protocol versions and encryption-bit positions, configuring encrypted page tables, allocating a shared GHCB, and registering it before VMGEXIT.

For non-automatic exits, hardware raises #VC with the VMEXIT code. The guest supplies required state and valid-bitmap bits in the GHCB, invokes VMGEXIT, processes returned state or errors, advances RIP, and returns via IRET. Interrupts and preemption should be disabled while manipulating the GHCB. Hypervisor errors may request exception injection or identify malformed input, unregistered addresses, invalid scratch buffers, missing fields, or invalid events.

Special NAE protocols cover port I/O, MSRs, hypercalls, MMIO, page-state changes, SNP firmware requests, extended requests returning certificate data, AP creation, restricted-injection doorbells, IPIs, timers, APIC ID discovery, VMPL switching, trusted I/O, Secure AVIC backing pages, and termination. Shared decrypted buffers support string I/O and MMIO. Page-state requests can make pages private or shared and provide PSMASH or UNSMASH hints, while progress fields permit interrupted operations to resume.

SNP guest requests use shared request and response pages, with the hypervisor translating addresses and managing response-page ownership around firmware calls. Extended requests may return GUID-indexed certificates. Trusted-I/O requests additionally exchange PCI, MMIO, device-state, measurement, certificate, and attestation information. Rate limiting may require guests to retry without issuing another request first.

The secrets page contains per-VMPL 64-bit request sequence numbers, an AP jump-table address, and guest-defined space. EFI firmware may communicate SNP secrets and CPUID pages through the specified confidential-computing configuration table.

AP startup cannot initially rely on hypervisor register modification because state is measured and encrypted. Reset-hold protocols and an AP jump table support subsequent INIT-SIPI handling. SNP AP Creation instead uses guest-supplied VMSA pages, supports immediate or INIT-triggered startup, and enables vCPU hotplug. Restricted Injection requires AP Creation rather than reset hold.

NMI handling uses a guest “NMI Complete” VMGEXIT. Debug-register virtualization is available when enabled; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and emulated. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

Restricted Injection uses a shared #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. The host presents APIC-like interrupt vectors or non-maskable events and signals #HV under defined conditions. The guest atomically clears and validates pending events, dispatches them, and completes EOI either by clearing the assist field or issuing an X2APIC EOI write. HLT is executed with interrupts disabled, and the guest checks pending events immediately after resuming.

Hetzner has connected directly to NAP Africa in Isando through a 10Gbps circuit, expanding its South African peering presence alongside NAP Africa Cape Town and JINX. More than 65% of its local traffic now passes through exchange points instead of transit links, contributing over 4Gbps weekly. Hetzner says settlement-free peering reduces connectivity costs and latency while improving resilience. The company hosts over 330,000 websites and peers with major local and international network operators. Its carrier-neutral Samrand data centre offers redundant 10Gbps transit and peering links, access to four international cable systems, and proximity to major fibre infrastructure. Hetzner invites other operators to establish peering connections.

The lecture reviews coding for bandwidth-limited additive white Gaussian noise channels, where nonbinary constellations, Euclidean distance, lattice coding, and shaping replace the binary codes and Hamming-distance methods used for power-limited channels. Lattice-constellation performance can be approximated by separating lattice coding gain from regional shaping gain, normalized by spectral efficiency.

An n-sphere minimizes normalized second moment and is therefore the optimal shaping region. Shaping gain is small in two dimensions—about 0.2 dB—but approaches a maximum of 1.53 dB as dimension increases. Practical methods such as shell mapping, used in V.34 modems, can obtain roughly 0.8–1 dB. Shaping is necessary for approaching the Shannon limit, though it cannot provide more than 1.53 dB.

Dense lattices include the two-dimensional hexagonal lattice, D4, E8, Barnes-Wall lattices, and the 24-dimensional Leech lattice. Their nominal coding gains increase with dimension, but their rapidly growing numbers of nearest neighbors reduce effective gain. Barnes-Wall lattices can be recursively constructed through partitioning and a “u, u plus v” method analogous to Reed-Muller codes. Even notable lattices such as the Leech lattice offer effective coding gains of only about 4 dB.

Trellis-coded modulation, introduced by Ungerboeck, expands the signal constellation and applies convolutional coding to subset labels created through set partitioning. A simple four-state, two-dimensional trellis code achieves a 3 dB coding gain and is decoded with the Viterbi algorithm. Larger partitions and trellises can provide approximately 5–6 dB. Four-dimensional schemes, including Wei’s code, reduce constellation expansion and were adopted in V.34 and ADSL standards.

Combining trellis coding with shaping still leaves performance roughly 2–3 dB from the Shannon limit. Higher-performance approaches include turbo codes, sequential decoding, multilevel coding, and bit-interleaved coded modulation. Multilevel coding can theoretically achieve aggregate channel capacity by coding each partition level separately. Bit-interleaved coded modulation pragmatically applies one binary capacity-approaching code across interleaved labeling levels and is used in wireless systems.

The lecture concludes that coding for traditional additive white Gaussian noise channels is mature and already close to Shannon limits. Remaining research includes iterative-decoding convergence, graph properties, algebraic code construction, multi-user and network channels, and data compression.

The gold/silver ratio measures how many ounces of silver equal one ounce of gold, calculated by dividing gold’s price by silver’s price using consistent units and currency. Traders often apply mean-reversion strategies: buying silver and shorting gold when the ratio is high, and reversing positions when it is low, through futures, options, or ETFs. Historically government-fixed, the ratio now floats widely; it averaged 47:1 in the 20th century and ranged mainly from 50:1 to 70:1 in the 21st, reaching 114.77 in 2020. Although 35 is generally considered low and 80 high, suitable thresholds require backtesting. The described GLD and SLV backtests produced erratic or flat results, finding no robust strategy or meaningful use as an equity-market risk indicator.

Deborah Jones opposes the proposed 35-storey Scott Road development, arguing it conflicts with the North Delta Area Plan’s six-storey guideline and policies on tree preservation, amenities, stormwater management and rainwater infiltration. She says the full-lot parking garage would eliminate groundwater recharge, harm Cougar Creek, increase flood and drought risks, and disqualify the project from incentives intended for low-impact development. Jones also warns that approval could encourage rezoning, land speculation and higher housing prices, while highrise condos may attract investors rather than residents. She suggests consideration only with major mitigation, including reducing the underground footprint and reserving at least 15 per cent of the site as fully permeable open space for large trees and infiltration. She further proposes requiring all multi-family developments to retain at least 15 per cent permeable land to support groundwater, urban forests, streams and climate resilience.

The lecture presents research on manufacturing polymer microfluidic devices through hot embossing and thermal nanoimprint lithography. Polymers are attractive because they are inexpensive, often transparent, mechanically tough, and suitable for rapid replication. Hot embossing heats a thermoplastic above its glass-transition temperature, applies and holds a load to fill stamp cavities, cools the material, and removes the stamp. Key variables include temperature, pressure, loading and hold times, polymer properties, substrate thickness, and feature geometry.

The research seeks computationally efficient models that predict replication quality across substrate, device-pattern, and individual-feature scales. A simplified linear-elastic model, using a temperature-dependent Young’s modulus and point-load response, closely matched measured topographies for PMMA while running far faster than detailed finite-element models. Carefully designed periodic test stamps containing channels and holes of varied sizes, densities, and orientations enabled rapid material characterization. Adding a linear viscous component approximately captured time-dependent polymer flow, though it underestimated filling of narrow features.

Experiments with PMMA and cyclic olefin polymers showed that feature penetration depends on temperature, force, hold time, feature size, density, and material behavior. A fractional-factorial study of TOPAS found temperature, force, and hold time significant, while loading time was not clearly significant. TOPAS also displayed strong orientation-dependent behavior attributable to material anisotropy.

Cooling and demolding are major challenges in microscale embossing. Differential thermal contraction can deform polymer features, shear material, or damage silicon stamps. Mold coatings can reduce friction but cannot eliminate contraction forces or mechanical locking. Demolding near the glass-transition temperature produced better feature geometry in PMMA, but required precise temperature control and rapid cooling to prevent recovery or overall part distortion.

The session concluded with project guidance: papers commonly run about six to eight pages, multiple optimization outputs can be combined using weighted objectives, and one-factor-at-a-time optimization can be compared with response-surface methods using existing experimental-design data.
Weston Public Library will offer free solar viewers, a pinhole projector workshop, and NASA’s livestream for the Aug. 21 eclipse, when Weston expects 70% coverage.

The speaker expects Dallas to respond strongly after losing Game 1 and emphasizes focusing on preparation rather than past results. Limiting time and space for skilled players such as Modano, Hull and Nieuwendyk requires coordinated defensive pressure. After a poor Game 2 marked by weak puck decisions, turnovers and failure to follow the game plan, the team still remained close. An apparent missed offside preceded a Dallas goal, but it was not blamed for the loss. With the series tied 1-1, the team plans to improve in Dallas without panicking. Players have only routine physical-series injuries, while Madden’s injury was less serious than feared. The speaker also discusses one player’s improved defensive responsibility, Brian’s strong overall play despite trying to do too much, the limited rivalry with Dallas, and the difficulty but positive significance of playing into June.

Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) supplies measurements to attestation managers through side-band/SPDM or in-band/DPE interfaces. AMD does not modify firmware protected by certain attestation schemes.

Update packages must verify compatible firmware and patch versions before execution and apply only if every component validates. Packages are non-persistent across reboots and may be applied during OS boot, after boot, or during operation. Files are versioned and can be applied sequentially.

SFS commands use a 2 MB-aligned memory region. The 4 KB TEE extended command buffer is followed by command output or the update package. A customer deployment agent creates the buffer, optionally adds a co-signing header and signature, appends the AMD package, and sends its physical address and command through the ASP TEE mailbox. Package memory is protected from non-ASP access.

Software checks whether SFS is enabled, waits for mailbox readiness, supplies the command-buffer address, issues the extended command, and polls for completion. The ASP then protects the memory, verifies optional customer and mandatory AMD signatures, executes the patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status.

Firmware-version queries use two contiguous 4 KB pages; the output page is initialized to C7h and must be HV-FIXED on SNP systems. Returned data includes API version, current SFS and system patch levels, and supported firmware version, type, and security patch-level entries.

Package names identify family, AGESA release, and a monotonically increasing number. Packages apply only to specified firmware and system patch-level combinations. Updates run alongside x86 and DMA traffic and aim to minimize disruption. SEV or SEV/ES virtual machines must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

CDC data show U.S. illnesses from mosquito, tick and flea bites have tripled since 2004. Venice faces mosquito risks from standing water in its canals, wetlands and residential yards, with West Nile Virus endemic in Los Angeles County. Mosquitoes transmit the virus from infected birds to humans and animals. About 80 percent of infected people have no symptoms; 20 percent experience symptoms such as nausea, rash and diarrhea, while fewer than one percent develop severe neurological disease. Los Angeles County West Vector manages standing water and mosquito breeding locally. Residents are advised to eliminate water that remains for more than five days and use recommended insect repellents, particularly outdoors between dusk and dawn.

SteelSeries Arctis GameBuds are discounted to $128 on Amazon. Designed for gaming and everyday use, they support Xbox or PlayStation versions and work with Switch, PC, and smartphones. Features include low-latency 2.4GHz audio, Bluetooth, active noise cancellation, game-specific equalizer presets, physical controls, and up to 10 hours of battery life or 40 hours with the case. Their portability, comfort, fit, and sound isolation also suit travel, exercise, and daily activities.

CBCT supports daily image guidance in radiotherapy but has artifacts, scatter, and inconsistent Hounsfield Units, while CT provides better soft-tissue contrast and dose-calculation accuracy but does not capture daily anatomical changes. Synthetic CT generation from CBCT aims to combine daily anatomy with CT-like image quality. Registration, GAN, CNN, transformer, hybrid, and diffusion approaches have been explored, but limitations include dependence on prior anatomy, training instability, hallucinations, limited interpretability, computational cost, and uncertain generalization.

The proposed EqDiff-CT framework uses a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model for head-and-neck CBCT-to-CT synthesis without deformable priors or adversarial training. It employs a time-conditioned, group-equivariant U-Net with C4 rotational symmetry, self-attention, and CBCT conditioning at every diffusion step. Training combines MSE and SSIM losses on predicted noise, while preprocessing and post-processing preserve Hounsfield Units. The model learns to reconstruct CT images by reversing a process that progressively adds Gaussian noise to reference CT slices.

Evaluation used an 80/20 patient-wise split of the SynthRAD2025 Head & Neck dataset, with slice- and volume-level metrics. The attention-enhanced model outperformed a diffusion model without attention and a CycleGAN baseline in SSIM, PSNR, MSE, and MAE, while preserving structures including the mandible, airway, and cervical spine.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2018 reported quarterly net sales of $53.3 billion, up 17% year over year, and net income of $11.5 billion, versus $8.7 billion. Diluted earnings per share rose to $2.34 from $1.67. Nine-month net sales were $202.7 billion and net income was $45.4 billion.

Quarterly growth was primarily driven by iPhone, Services and Other Products. iPhone revenue increased 20% to $29.9 billion, despite unit sales rising only 1%. Services revenue increased 31% to $9.5 billion, while Other Products grew 37%. iPad and Mac revenue each declined 5%. Sales increased across all geographic segments, led by 20% growth in the Americas and 19% in Greater China.

Quarterly gross margin was 38.3%, compared with 38.5% a year earlier. Research and development expense increased to $3.7 billion, and selling, general and administrative expense rose to $4.1 billion. The effective tax rate declined to 13.3% from 22.9%.

At June 30, 2018, Apple had total assets of $349.2 billion, including $32.0 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $211.8 billion in marketable securities. Total liabilities were $234.2 billion, including approximately $104.1 billion of term debt. Nine-month operating cash flow was $57.9 billion.

Apple repurchased $20.0 billion of stock during the quarter and authorized a new $100 billion repurchase program. It reduced its provisional expense related to U.S. tax reform from $2.6 billion to $900 million and estimated a $37.0 billion deemed repatriation tax payable. Apple also began funding escrow related to the European Commission’s €13 billion state-aid recovery decision, which it appealed.

Legal contingencies included patent litigation with VirnetX and a royalty dispute with Qualcomm. Apple stated that component sourcing, outsourced manufacturing, foreign exchange movements, competition and litigation could materially affect results.

James Harden recorded the NBA’s first 60-point triple-double, adding 10 rebounds and 11 assists as the short-handed Houston Rockets defeated the Orlando Magic 114-107. He broke Calvin Murphy’s franchise scoring record and scored six late points to secure the win. Houston played without Chris Paul and Trevor Ariza, while Eric Gordon left with back stiffness. Marreese Speights and Mario Hezonja led Orlando with 17 points each as the Magic lost their third straight game.

The study developed a model to interpret influenza A H5 RNA detections in wastewater by estimating contributions from humans, cow milk, poultry feces, and wildfowl feces. H5N1 outbreaks expanded from U.S. birds in 2022 to dairy cattle in 2024; by December 19, 2024, 865 dairy herds and 61 human cases had been reported, without reported or suspected human-to-human transmission. H5 RNA was detected in wastewater beginning in March 2024. Potential inputs include discarded infected milk, industrial dairy waste, human waste, and bird feces entering combined sewers or open treatment facilities.

Researchers retrospectively tested 110 wastewater-solids samples collected from September 2023 through May 2024 at a California treatment plant serving 750,000 people. Droplet digital RT-PCR measured total influenza A and H1, H3, and H5 RNA, with positive, negative, and internal controls. Samples with at least three positive droplets were considered positive.

The model used mass balance to estimate H5 RNA inputs required to produce measured concentrations. It accounted for RNA in wastewater solids and liquids, partitioning between phases, daily plant flow, and suspended solids. The objectives were to identify the first H5 detection during circulating human influenza and contextualize detections through theoretical source estimates.

Successful early offense and press breaks require precise execution, spacing, timing, footwork, and coordination. Coaches should teach players through the Whole-Part-Whole method: demonstrate responsibilities, walk through options and reads, use progressive one- through five-player drills, then practice live at game speed against motivated, challenging defense. Objectives include confidently attacking pressure, advancing the ball with controlled passes, handling double teams and outnumbered situations, flowing into early offense, and pursuing offensive rebounds. Teams should break on every possession, transition smoothly into continuity, scout defensive tactics, and remain alert to adjustments. Press-break work should be included in every practice to develop effective habits.

The goalie showed resilience after his first loss, responding with an outstanding game and consistently remaining calm after allowing bad goals. Bergeron and Ryan O’Reilly are described as hardworking, strong faceoff players who contribute on both sides of the puck. The teams share defensive, physical, forechecking styles and are difficult to play against, though their defensive units differ in size and mobility. Discipline requires playing physically but cleanly between whistles and avoiding post-whistle confrontations. The team’s identity centers on collective play, with no individual considered bigger than the team. Given scheduling and travel demands, two capable goalies are necessary, with usage depending on performance and circumstances.

The Justice Department’s hiring of assistant US attorneys has slowed sharply despite plans to add more than 400 lawyers. LinkedIn data showed about 42 new hires from January through August, less than half the number recorded during the same period in each of the previous four years, though the data is incomplete.

Current and former prosecutors attributed the slowdown to hiring freezes, budget constraints, higher pay costs, departures, declining applicant interest, low morale, and concerns about political pressure and ethically questionable cases. Some offices report significant staffing shortages, while offices including those in Philadelphia and southern Florida are now recruiting prosecutors.

The department appears to be maintaining hiring standards: many recent recruits attended top law schools or held prestigious legal jobs. Former prosecutors remain divided over recommending federal service. Some say most new attorneys will handle routine crimes under qualified leadership, while others warn that White House interference could involve prosecutors anywhere.

Researchers synthesized hydrogen-bonded metal inorganic-organic complex crystals ZnCl₂HIm₂ (MIOC-4) and ZnCl₂HbIm₂ (MIOC-7) by introducing chloride into ZIF-derived structures. MIOC-4 forms a stacked monoclinic network, while triclinic MIOC-7 has an interdigitated structure reinforced by extensive π–π interactions. Both crystals were melt-quenched into transparent amorphous glasses without ligand decomposition or coordination-bond breakage.

MIOC-4 and MIOC-7 melt at 440 and 508 K and have glass-transition temperatures of 282 and 359 K, respectively. MIOC-7’s greater thermal stability and higher glass-transition temperature were attributed to benzimidazole steric hindrance and its interdigitated structure. In situ X-ray diffraction showed that melting begins with slippage and distortion of hydrogen-bonded structures, followed by hydrogen-bond rupture and intermolecular disorder. During quenching, disordered N–H···Cl networks reform, while C–H···Cl bonds weaken or disappear.

Spectroscopic, NMR, and synchrotron X-ray analyses showed that vitrification eliminates medium- and long-range intermolecular order and disrupts π–π stacking while preserving intramolecular Zn–N, Zn–Cl, Zn–C, and ring correlations. The resulting glass contains short-range-disordered tetrahedral units and multiple frozen molecular conformations.

Mixed HIm/HbIm synthesis produced binary mixed-crystal systems with reduced melting points and composition-dependent glass transitions. The lowest melting point was 415 K for ZnCl₂HbIm₀.₄₉₈HIm₁.₅₀₂, while glass-transition temperatures increased approximately linearly from 282 to 360 K as HbIm replaced HIm. The design strategy was also extended by substituting Zn with Co or Cu and Cl⁻ with SCN⁻. Hydrogen-bond strength and network topology affected thermal behavior more strongly than metal-node identity.

MIOC-7 glass exhibited excitation-dependent photoluminescence ranging from blue to yellow, enhanced visible emission, and an internal quantum yield of 3.4%, compared with 1.2% for the crystal. These properties were linked to frozen tetrahedral conformations and slow molecular relaxation, indicating potential anti-counterfeiting applications.

The disclosure describes networked exercise systems that deliver live and recorded instructor-led classes to treadmills and other exercise machines. The systems support multimedia streaming, user-instructor and user-user communication, synchronized performance data, competition, leaderboards, social interaction, and gamification. Backend servers, recording studios, communications networks, and local digital hardware enable content creation, distribution, participation, and storage.

An example treadmill includes a deck, motor-driven incline mechanism, motor-driven continuous belt with slats and non-slip pads, support posts, crossbars, an adjustable display, sensors, controllers, and user controls. Two separate rotary controls can regulate different functions, such as belt speed and deck incline. Rotary controls may include rotatable outer portions, central input devices, tactile detents, visual indicators, audible feedback, sensors, and printed circuit boards. Their operation can vary according to rotation direction and speed. Alternative substantially linear or capacitive controls may also be used.

Sensors may measure machine settings and user performance, including speed, incline, load, distance, work, energy expenditure, heart rate, respiration, hydration, and calorie burn. Indicators can provide visual or audio exercise guidance. Additional features include trays, support handles, and a magnetic emergency-stop device that halts the belt when disconnected.

The display and user interface provide access to featured, scheduled, live, archived, and “just run” content. Users can filter classes by instructor, duration, type, music, body focus, or exercise. During classes, video may appear with overlaid metrics, timelines, scorecards, leaderboards, trends, and information about other participants. Touch, voice, gesture, or other input methods may control displayed content, account settings, profiles, and machine functions.

Socket 940 uses an LCP base and cover rated UL 94 V-0, with support structures protecting package pins and a seating-plane flatness below 0.25 mm. Cover thickness must not exceed 1.17 mm. A removable, residue-free overlay supports vacuum pick-and-place assembly.

Required markings include “SOCKET 940,” lever lock directions, pin A01 orientation, the supplier’s UL symbol, and lot traceability. Contacts use high-strength copper alloy plated with at least 1.27 µm nickel and 0.76 µm gold in mating areas; lubricants are prohibited there. SMT attachment uses 0.76 mm tin-lead solder balls, 0.64 mm PCB pads, solder barriers, and 0.20 mm ball-field coplanarity.

A stainless-steel lever enables tool-free actuation. Open-position insertion and extraction force must not exceed 2 kgf; closed-position extraction force must be at least 0.013 kgf per pin. Lever operation must require under 3.6 kgf, pin displacement must remain below 1.0 mm, and the socket must withstand 50 actuation cycles.

Sockets must have intact solder balls, contacts, plating, housing, tabs, latch, and lever. Each contact is rated for 1.5 A with under 30°C temperature rise. Initial and final resistance must not exceed 25 mΩ per contact. Electrical limits include under 4 nH single-pin inductance, under 1 pF capacitance, 100 Ω ±10% differential impedance, under 10 ps propagation skew plus measurement error, at least 650 Vac dielectric withstand, and at least 1000 MΩ insulation resistance.

Kentucky valedictorian Christian Bales and student council president Katherine Frantz delivered graduation speeches by bullhorn outside Holy Cross High School’s ceremony after the Diocese of Covington rejected them as late, political and inconsistent with Catholic teaching. Bales, who is gay but did not mention his sexuality in the speech, praised student activism and argued that young people can shape the world and should resist efforts to silence them. His speech cited Florida students advocating for stronger gun laws as an example of youth empowerment. Bales and his mother said the rejection ultimately amplified his message, drawing widespread media attention and support. He plans to attend the University of Louisville.

The speaker described supporting the overtime play that led to the deciding shot, emphasizing clean opportunities during a delayed penalty. He expressed excitement about returning to a supportive hockey town. He said the team must avoid penalties because the opponent’s elite power play requires intense, detailed defending, effective clears, and quick changes. Despite losing key players, he remains confident in the team’s depth.

The Average Directional Movement Index (ADX), developed by Welles Wilder, measures trend strength and uses DI+ and DI− to indicate bullish or bearish direction. It ranges from 0 to 100, is lagging, and was originally designed for commodity swing trading. Wilder classified readings below 15 as non-trending and above 20 as trending.

Backtests found that ADX performs reasonably but inadequately as a standalone strategy. A 10-day DI crossover on the S&P 500 produced a 5.4% CAGR, 0.42% average trade, and 1.71 profit factor. An optimized breakout strategy had a 3.03% CAGR and 13.76% drawdown, underperforming buy-and-hold’s 9.9% CAGR.

ADX added greater value as a filter for another indicator. Using short periods of 5–10 days and ADX limits around 30–40 increased profit factor from 2.15 to 2.6 while reducing market exposure from 24% to 7%. On Nasdaq, the combined strategy produced a 12.5% CAGR with 8% exposure. The article concludes that ADX is versatile and generally works better with other indicators, recommending independent backtesting.

Future Electronics and NXP will host a free i.MX RT Series Crossover Processor seminar in San Sebastian, Spain, on July 4, 2018. The workshop includes hands-on exercises featuring the Cortex-M7-based i.MX RT 105x processors, which offer real-time performance, MCU usability, implementation flexibility and affordability without integrated flash memory.

On October 7, 2016, NVIDIA entered a five-year unsecured revolving credit agreement with Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley MUFG Loan Partners and other lenders. NVIDIA may borrow up to $575 million for working capital and general corporate purposes through October 7, 2021, with up to $425 million in additional commitments subject to conditions. Loans bear interest based on adjusted LIBOR or an alternate base rate plus an applicable rate. The agreement includes customary covenants, default provisions and a debt-to-adjusted-EBITDA requirement. The obligations rank equally with NVIDIA’s other unsecured, unsubordinated debt.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture expands asynchronous computing by allowing concurrent RT Core and graphics or compute workloads, as well as two simultaneous compute workloads with configurable priorities. Its second-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection performance over Turing and add hardware acceleration for moving and deforming geometry, enabling ray-traced motion blur up to eight times faster. In a Blender test, an RTX 3080 rendered motion blur up to five times faster than an RTX 2080 Super.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, INT4, TF32, and BF16 operations. Fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity reduces weight storage and bandwidth while potentially doubling matrix throughput with virtually no inference-accuracy loss after pruning and fine-tuning. These Tensor Cores accelerate AI graphics functions including denoising and DLSS, whose enhanced scaling supports 8K gaming at 60 fps in some titles.

GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, transferring two bits per clock edge. It supports rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/s. Error Detection and Replay detects transmission errors during memory overclocking and retries affected transactions, causing performance to plateau before instability may occur.

RTX IO, used with Microsoft DirectStorage, enables compressed data to move from NVMe storage to the GPU for asynchronous decompression. It can reduce CPU work, improve I/O performance, loading times, asset streaming, and frame rates, while supporting large game and professional datasets.

Ampere GPUs support DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 4K at 120 Hz, and 8K at 60 Hz. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware decoding for formats including AV1, with up to 8K60 HDR playback at low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The data-center A40 provides 48 GB of memory, expandable to 96 GB through NVLink, PCIe Gen4, virtualization support, and improvements in FP32, ray tracing, and AI performance over the Quadro RTX 6000. The workstation RTX A6000 has 10,752 CUDA cores and 48 GB of GDDR6, also expandable to 96 GB. The RTX 3090 includes 24 GB of GDDR6X and targets creators, researchers, AI developers, and extreme gamers, while the RTX 3070 uses GDDR6 and omits NVLink.

A Stanford, Harvard and Census Bureau study of 20 million children found that black boys earn less than similarly situated white boys in 99 percent of U.S. neighborhoods. Black and Native American children had the lowest upward mobility, while white and Asian children had the highest. Among children raised in the bottom income fifth, 11 percent of white children reached the top fifth, compared with 2.5 percent of black children. Even black children from the wealthiest families earned 12.4 percent less than comparable white children. The black-white income gap was driven largely by men; after controlling for parental income, black women earned slightly more than white women. Neighborhoods matter, but affluent areas often showed larger gaps. Greater racial parity was associated with lower racial bias and more present black fathers in the community.

President Donald Trump announced an agreement under which Pfizer will lower U.S. drug prices, including offering existing medicines to Medicaid patients at the lowest prices available in other developed countries and extending similar pricing to new drugs for Medicare, Medicaid and commercial payers. Discounted direct purchases will be available through TrumpRx.gov, with many selected treatments reduced by 50% on average and up to 85%.

In exchange, Pfizer will receive a three-year exemption from pharmaceutical-specific tariffs if it further invests in U.S. manufacturing. The company plans to invest $70 billion in domestic manufacturing and research facilities. Pfizer shares rose more than 4% after the announcement.

Trump said his administration is pursuing similar agreements with other drugmakers and may impose tariffs if negotiations fail. Eli Lilly is also negotiating with the administration. Trump has separately announced a 100% tariff on branded or patented pharmaceutical imports, exempting companies building U.S. manufacturing plants.

The speaker celebrates Berlin’s reunification and honors Berliners’ courage in resisting division, tyranny, and the Wall. He pledges that a new American Embassy will stand in Berlin when it again becomes Germany’s governmental seat.
