Calling for renewed civil courage, he urges citizens to build a democratic, prosperous, and peaceful Europe based on free markets, cooperation, individual opportunity, and bridges rather than walls. He warns against racial, ethnic, and religious division, encourages young people to embrace tolerance and shape their future, and cites expanding democracy, economic reform, and NATO’s Partnership for Peace as signs of progress. Affirming enduring American support and military commitment to Europe, he presents the Brandenburg Gate as a gateway toward a Europe united in peace, freedom, and progress, concluding that Berlin is free.

The dividend-growth retirement portfolio gained 15% in 2016, including dividends and capital gains but excluding new contributions, outperforming the S&P 500’s 11.66% return every month. Of 27 beginning positions, 22 rose; Chevron, JPMorgan, AT&T, 3M and Aflac led gains, while Gilead Sciences, CVS Health, Starbucks, Coca-Cola and Target declined. The portfolio made one sale, exchanging Baxalta for Visa, and expanded to 35 companies by adding Visa, Cisco, Pepsi, Cummins, Honeywell, Qualcomm, Disney and V.F. Corp. Purchases averaged returns above 6%, with Boeing, Cisco and Microsoft performing especially well, while CVS purchases declined. The investor targets long-term annual returns of 6–8% and plans to continue buying dividend-paying companies below estimated fair value.

NVIDIA’s board appointed Tim Teter as senior vice president, general counsel and secretary, effective upon his expected employment start on January 23, 2017. Teter, 50, was previously a Cooley LLP partner focused on patent and technology litigation and formerly worked as a Lockheed engineer. He will assume legal department leadership from retiring chief administrative officer David M. Shannon.

Teter’s at-will offer includes an $850,000 annual salary, targeted annual incentive compensation of $250,000 beginning fiscal 2018, a conditional $450,000 first-anniversary bonus, and restricted stock units targeted at $5.8 million vesting over approximately four years. He may also participate in NVIDIA’s employee stock purchase plan and benefits programs and is expected to enter the company’s standard indemnity agreement.

The paper studies whether decentralized “win-stay, lose-shift” strategy updates can lead multi-agent reinforcement-learning systems from any initial strategy to an equilibrium. It introduces the grouped satisficing path, where a group retains its strategies if all members are best responding, generalizing classical satisficing paths.

Using topological properties of best responses, the paper characterizes local minima of the best-response group count and establishes a reduction from the original game to a sub-game. Its main theorem states that a finite-length grouped satisficing path from any initial joint strategy to an equilibrium exists when each strategy set is convex and compact, payoff functions are continuous and partially analytic, and every sub-game has an equilibrium.

Corollaries establish finite-length satisficing paths for continuous games under additional payoff conditions, finite N-player mixed-strategy games, and finite-state stationary or finite-step stochastic games. The results imply existence rather than specifying update algorithms. Open questions concern necessary and sufficient conditions, approximate best responses with positive error, and restrictions requiring non-best-responding players to choose nearby strategies.

WIRED highlights Prime-member Amazon Big Deal Days discounts under $100 for October 7–8. Tested picks span streaming devices, headphones, smart speakers, wireless chargers, security cameras, pet products, kitchen appliances, cleaning tools, bedding, personal-care items, gaming accessories, and toys. Featured deals include the Roku Streaming Stick 4K for $30, Ninja Blast blender for $50, several Belkin chargers, Eufy’s Indoor Cam S350 for $80, Instant Pot air fryers for $80, and Philips grooming products.

Virtual education offers flexibility, individualized pacing, broader course access, credit recovery, accommodations, parental engagement, and preparation for postsecondary learning. Challenges include internet access, motivation, isolation, delayed feedback, accommodations for special needs, student engagement, instructional quality, and teacher monitoring.

The study surveyed Indiana public-school superintendents and virtual program administrators during 2020–21 and conducted 11 follow-up interviews. Responses came from 96 superintendents and 36 program administrators, predominantly representing rural and smaller districts.

COVID-19 was the leading reason for implementing or maintaining virtual programs, followed by credit recovery. The most frequently reported benefits were maintaining enrollment during the pandemic, credit recovery, and learner flexibility. The principal challenges were student engagement, curriculum and instructional quality, staff professional development, and staffing.

Interviews showed that the pandemic accelerated technology initiatives and expanded some programs from secondary grades to K–12. District leaders linked virtual options to enrollment and funding retention. Teachers experienced stress, limited training, and rapid changes in responsibilities, although their technology skills improved. Students faced difficulties with motivation, time management, attendance, social-emotional well-being, and peer connection. Parental support was considered particularly important for younger students.

The study concludes that COVID-19 drove substantial growth in Indiana virtual education, while exposing challenges already associated with virtual programs. It recommends program design responsive to student and teacher needs, targeted professional development, and further research on effective virtual programs, students, and educators.

Kobe University researchers found that four orchid species germinated only near decaying logs and formed highly specific partnerships with wood-decaying fungi, which supply carbon absent from their dust-like seeds. Seedlings associated with nearly the same fungi found in adult orchids retaining coral-shaped rhizomes, while orchids without these structures may change fungal partners as they grow. Maintaining wood-decaying fungal partnerships may have facilitated the evolution of orchids that depend entirely on fungi instead of photosynthesis. The findings identify a carbon pathway from deadwood through fungi to orchids and suggest orchid conservation requires protecting deadwood and its fungal communities.

The study uses bibliometric analysis of open-access research published since 2019 to identify competencies required of future digital education transformation leaders. It links Thailand’s Education 4.0 transition with the national Digital Thailand 4.0 strategy and COVID-19-driven disruption.

Five core competencies emerge: digital literacy, digital readiness, digital culture, digital mindset, and digital leadership. Educators need technological knowledge and skills, cybersecurity awareness, readiness for new infrastructure and processes, confidence in digital tools, openness to innovation, ethical judgment, adaptability, collaboration, and data-driven decision-making. Leaders must establish clear strategies, support hybrid and project-based learning, build digital teams and ecosystems, protect data, empower practitioners, and develop educators through knowledge, skills, abilities, and practical experience.

The study emphasizes that digital transformation is irreversible and requires changes in organizational culture, teaching methods, infrastructure, and leadership. Technology cannot replace good teachers; educators must adapt digital practices to guide institutions, teachers, and students while supporting positive outcomes for society. The findings provide directions for further research on preparing future digital education transformation leaders.

The study uses documentary research, historical sources, interviews, observations, and audiovisual field data to examine Songyang Academy’s history and its relationship to general education.

Founded in 484 as Songyang Temple, the institution developed into a center of Confucian teaching during periods of political unrest. It became Taiyi School in 955 and flourished under Northern Song support through funding, facilities, classical texts, and prominent lecturers such as Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi. It later declined amid warfare and restrictions, briefly revived during the Ming and early Qing dynasties, and ultimately collapsed after the late Qing abolition of the imperial examination system.

Songyang Academy placed moral education, personality formation, practical learning, and the unity of knowledge and action at the center of education. It accepted students regardless of region or social status and promoted lectures, academic debate, independent reading, mutual questioning, critical thought, and teacher-guided learning. Its management combined educational and administrative leadership, with some students serving in assistant roles.

The article argues that these principles align with modern general education’s aim of developing knowledgeable, responsible, morally grounded, and well-rounded individuals rather than narrowly trained specialists. It concludes that Songyang Academy’s educational philosophy can inform contemporary reform through interdisciplinary learning, practical application, academic openness, personalized education, and integration of traditional moral principles with modern needs.

Texas Instruments provides TI E2E support forums and cautions that linked content is supplied as-is. LaunchPad, Code Composer Studio, TI E2E, Arm, and Cortex are identified as trademarks. The document warns that improper electrostatic-discharge handling can damage integrated circuits.

The April 2025 revision updates MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 device features, variants, peripheral counts, operating modes, electrical and thermal specifications, memory endurance, security, communications interfaces, timers, and other technical sections. It adds preview package variants, PSA-L1 certification targeting, DMA details, and revised ADC, temperature-sensor, oscillator, power, flash, and digital-I/O information.

Mechanical, packaging, soldering, ordering, material, RoHS, moisture-sensitivity, and part-marking information is subject to change. Preproduction parts are intended for evaluation and may lack completed qualification or warranties. Automotive-qualified MSPM0G3518-Q1 and MSPM0G3519-Q1 versions are listed.

TI supplies technical resources as-is, disclaims warranties, and assigns users responsibility for product selection, application design, validation, testing, and compliance. Use of the resources is limited to developing applications with the described TI products and remains subject to TI’s applicable terms.

The lecture covers theoretical models of protein folding and interlocked three-dimensional chains.

For protein folding, it introduces the HP model, where amino acids are represented as hydrophobic (H) or hydrophilic/polar (P) nodes on a lattice. A folding’s score is the number of nonconsecutive adjacent H-H pairs, reflecting the tendency of hydrophobic nodes to cluster away from water. Finding an optimal folding is NP-hard on both two-dimensional square and three-dimensional cubic lattices. A known polynomial-time approximation algorithm achieves a 1/3 approximation by exploiting the square lattice’s parity structure and arranging selected H nodes into patterns that create multiple H-H bonds. The lecture also discusses HP chains with unique optimal foldings: such examples exist for all even-length closed chains and all lengths divisible by four for open chains. Questions remain about other lengths, other lattices, relationships between H and P counts, and protein design—constructing a sequence whose unique optimal folding approximates a target shape.

The second topic concerns whether multiple chains with universal joints can interlock even when each chain is individually unlocked. This relates to Lubiw’s problem: determining how many vertex cuts are required to unlock an arbitrary three-dimensional chain with \(n\) bars. Known worst-case bounds are approximately \(n/4\) cuts from below and \(n/2\) from above. The lower bound comes from connecting multiple “knitting needle” locking structures, while the upper bound follows by cutting the chain into hairpins, which always separate.

Several separability and interlocking results are presented. Any finite collection of two-edge chains, or hairpins, is separable through a scaling argument. Two three-edge chains also separate, even with additional hairpins, as does a four-edge chain with any number of hairpins. Conversely, three three-edge chains can interlock, as can a three-edge chain with a four-edge chain. A two-edge hairpin can interlock with an eleven-edge chain, though optimality of this size is conjectural. Closed triangles can interlock with open four-edge chains, and closed four-edge chains can interlock with open three-edge chains; topological linking arguments establish these results.

Interlocked chains also support hardness constructions. They can form rigid infrastructure for computational gadgets used to prove that deciding whether one configuration of a three-dimensional chain can move to another is PSPACE-complete. However, determining whether a given chain can unfold to a straight configuration remains open.

E-minis are electronically traded futures contracts, generally one-fifth the size of standard contracts, covering indexes, commodities, currencies, and some stocks. Introduced by the CME in 1997, they provide retail traders with lower-capital access, liquidity, leverage, and nearly continuous trading. They can be used for speculation or hedging, but leverage magnifies both gains and losses.

Trading requires a futures brokerage account, knowledge of margins, order types, expiration, and risk management. Capital needs depend on the contract, exchange, and broker. For example, an S&P 500 E-mini valued at $200,000 may require a $10,000 maintenance margin, while the passage recommends budgeting $13,000–$15,000. Transaction costs generally range from $0.50 to $2.50 per contract plus applicable fees. At expiration, positions must be settled through delivery or an offsetting transaction.

A backtested S&P 500 E-mini mean-reversion-style strategy produced 163 trades from 2000–2021, averaging 0.89% per trade, with a 79% win rate and profit factor of 2. In 2022, 13 trades averaged 0.18%, compared with a 15% S&P 500 loss at the time.

The passage warns that futures are speculative, volatile, leveraged, and zero-sum. Scalping is discouraged because of intense competition, commissions, and slippage. Traders are advised to use a written, backtested plan, maintain discipline and records, and hold substantially more than the minimum margin. There is no legal daily trade limit, though brokers may impose restrictions.

The study examined attitudes toward inclusive education among 30 purposively selected elementary teachers from four public schools in Liloan District, Cebu, Philippines. Guided by behavioral, ecological, social learning, and legal frameworks, it used a descriptive-correlational design and a modified Scale of Teachers’ Attitudes Toward Inclusion. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics.

Most participants were female, married, aged 34–43, and had graduate-level units. Although teaching experience varied, 90% had only one to five years of experience with learners with special education needs, and 80% had attended only one or two inclusion trainings. Learning disabilities were the most common learner difficulty encountered.

Teachers showed generally positive attitudes toward inclusion’s advantages, professional considerations, and philosophical principles. They recognized its social benefits, equal-access principles, and need for differentiated instruction. However, they were less certain about academic effects and expressed concerns about large classes, preparation time, behavioral challenges, inadequate resources, scheduling, assistive technology, specialist access, and instructional materials. Logistical attitudes were neutral overall.

Statistical tests found no significant relationships between attitudes and age, marital status, education, teaching experience, number of learners, or learner disability. The study concluded that teachers shared broadly consistent positive foundations regardless of demographic background, but practical implementation required stronger support. It recommended sustained professional development, mentoring, smaller classes, additional qualified personnel, assistive technologies, adequate materials and budgets, collaboration with specialists and families, and continuous monitoring. These measures informed a proposed Teacher Inclusion Support Plan intended to translate positive attitudes into sustainable practices and reduce burnout risks as inclusive education expands.

The speaker considers the recognition a great honor despite missing a rookie trophy nomination. He delayed joining the Flyers to prepare mentally and physically, trained hard, and drew motivation from veteran teammates. After a slow first five games, improved confidence helped his performance.

Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School reopened two weeks after 17 people were killed, with about 50 uniformed officers, grief counselors, therapy animals and volunteers present. Some students found the security reassuring, while others, including student activist David Hogg, viewed the armed presence as disturbing. Backpacks were prohibited, the building where the shooting occurred remained closed, and classes began with the period underway during the attack.

Students described nervousness and emotional trauma but also resilience and pride in classmates advocating stronger gun laws. Dick’s Sporting Goods announced it would stop selling assault-style rifles and prohibit gun sales to anyone under 21.

Florida lawmakers advanced school-safety legislation that would raise the minimum age for long-gun purchases to 21 and potentially allow trained, deputized teachers to carry concealed weapons. The Broward superintendent and Hogg opposed arming teachers. The NRA’s Marion Hammer objected to new gun restrictions, while victim Alex Schachter’s father said the proposed measures were insufficient but might have saved his son.

The author’s 21-year-old daughter has the skills to become a strong literature professor, but the scarcity and worsening quality of full-time humanities jobs make graduate school an unattractive path. Higher education faces financial pressures, demographic decline, generative AI and political hostility, while related fields such as journalism and publishing have also contracted. The daughter is considering librarianship because information science offers more flexible opportunities, and the author encourages this option while seeking advice about viable careers for talented young people drawn to literary scholarship.

Vertical farming grows layered crops in controlled environments using methods such as hydroponics, aeroponics and aquaponics. Market growth is driven by food demand, population growth, reduced reliance on soil and water, technological adoption and pesticide-free production. High urban investment costs and artificial-lighting energy use constrain growth. The market is projected to reach about USD 6 billion by 2022, with a 21% CAGR from 2016–2022. North America holds the largest share, while Asia-Pacific is expected to grow rapidly due to urbanization, limited fertile land and investment.

Population growth and rising food demand are increasing cereal production and pesticide use, especially herbicides. Agricultural advances include crop protection, irrigation, soil management, GM technology, and improved farming techniques. Crop rotation supports soil fertility, limits erosion, improves yields, and reduces pest attacks, while excessive crop protection chemicals can harm health, the environment, and soil productivity. Herbicides dominate the grain and cereal crop protection market due to low costs and continued research. North America leads the market, while Asia Pacific is expected to expand rapidly. Global vendors compete through quality, innovation, price, and distribution, alongside numerous local and regional players.

The Appellate Division unanimously affirmed dismissal of Brian O’Loughlin’s defamation action against the Patrolmen’s Benevolent Association and its president, Phil Caruso. Caruso had described O’Loughlin and eight other officers as having “no feelings” and being “a disgrace” after they requested refunds of a $20 contribution for a memorial to officers killed in duty. O’Loughlin had proposed using the money for safety equipment instead. Applying factors distinguishing fact from opinion—including language, verifiability, context, and social setting—the court held that Caruso’s remarks were vague, subjective expressions of personal opinion that could not be proven true or false. The statements were not actionable mixed opinion because their basis—the officers’ refusal to contribute—was disclosed and not falsely represented.

Kayleigh Gray’s daughter Emilia was born at 27 weeks, weighing 1lb 11oz, and received months of care at Royal Preston Hospital’s neonatal unit. To thank the unit, Gray and her employer, Sign Build, donated 25 pairs of acrylic turtle doves, allowing parents to keep one while the matching dove stays with their baby.

Tesla’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2022 reported quarterly revenue of $21.45 billion, net income attributable to common stockholders of $3.29 billion, and diluted earnings per share of $0.95. For the first nine months, revenue was $57.14 billion, net income attributable to common stockholders was $8.87 billion, and operating cash flow was $11.45 billion.

At September 30, Tesla had $74.43 billion in assets, including $19.53 billion in cash and equivalents and $10.33 billion in inventory. Total liabilities were $33.30 billion, while stockholders’ equity was $39.85 billion. Debt and finance leases totaled $3.55 billion. Tesla converted approximately 75% of its digital-asset purchases into fiat currency, leaving digital assets with a carrying value of $218 million.

Tesla operates automotive and energy generation and storage segments. It cited continuing COVID-19, supply-chain, semiconductor, logistics and inflation pressures. An August 2022 three-for-one stock split was applied retroactively. The filing also discusses tax matters, stock-based compensation, debt, warranties, regulatory credits, operating commitments and litigation involving the SolarCity acquisition, the 2018 CEO performance award and director compensation.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K on August 15, 2019, announcing financial results for the quarter ended July 28, 2019. The filing includes a press release and CFO commentary as exhibits, both furnished rather than filed under securities laws. CFO Colette M. Kress signed the report.

A study examined how a 40 percent smaller NIH budget might have affected drug development. It identified grants in the bottom 40 percent of funding priority between 1980 and 2007 and traced their links to 557 drugs approved by the FDA from 2000 to 2023. More than half of those drugs were connected to research potentially at risk of losing funding.

Forty drugs had patents directly acknowledging NIH extramural funding, and 14 cited at-risk grants, including Cerdelga. Fifty-nine percent had patents citing NIH-supported publications, while 65 had patents whose citations were more than 25 percent linked to NIH research. Examples included Gleevec and Tarceva.

Drugs linked to at-risk research were not less important: 60 percent received FDA priority review, compared with 41 percent of unlinked drugs, and they had higher average market value. Researchers said the findings suggest major NIH cuts could substantially reduce medical innovation, while noting the analysis likely underestimates broader, indirect effects.

The speaker says the team must maintain its focus and mentality, treating the previous win as only another step toward winning the Stanley Cup. He praises an unheralded, old-school teammate and Marian, whose experience losing two Finals adds motivation and who has contributed greatly all season and playoffs. The team expects opponents to respond strongly and plans to keep pressuring their top players and goaltender.

Winning the Cup has been a lifelong dream, but players must control their excitement and save their energy for the game. Leadership comes from throughout the lineup, both in play and in the locker room, while discipline and avoiding frustration remain important. Winning matters regardless of venue, though the team wants its best performance at home. He also recognizes low-minute and replacement players for succeeding under pressure. Only 18% of U.S. workers are very confident about retirement security. The passage recommends three steps to improve preparedness: project retirement income from current savings and Social Security, review and minimize investment fees, and maintain an age-appropriate asset allocation.

Saving 10% of income may be insufficient because of healthcare costs, low interest rates, and longer life spans. Retirement calculators can estimate future savings and income; if combined savings and Social Security will not replace current income, contributions may need to increase.

Fees can substantially reduce investment balances. Investing $5,500 annually for 30 years at a 7% return would produce about $519,534 without fees, compared with about $308,467 with a 3% fee.

Asset allocation should balance growth and risk. One suggested formula is to subtract age from 110 and invest that percentage in stocks, while adjusting for individual circumstances and changing risk tolerance.

The Florida First District Court of Appeal affirmed AHCA’s dismissal of Glenwood Nursing Center’s administrative hearing request as untimely. AHCA’s complaint required Glenwood to request a hearing by June 14, 2010, but Glenwood filed on June 15 after obtaining counsel’s agreement to accept a late filing. Florida law required a Chapter 120 hearing request to be filed with the state agency’s clerk. Glenwood sent the letter to CMS and copied an AHCA field office manager, but did not file it with AHCA’s clerk. Accordingly, the April letter did not constitute a valid AHCA hearing request. The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies up to 2 MHz and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge.

When CS_ILIM exceeds 1.05 V, cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins and the HICC capacitor charges. At 0.6 V, soft-start discharges and switching stops; HICC is pulled to 1 V and then discharged until 0.3 V, when soft-start restarts. Slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle. The recommended compensation equals the inductor’s falling-current slope and is programmed by a resistor from RSC to AVSS. Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation may be used; Type 2A adds a high-frequency attenuation capacitor. Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical 175°C junction temperature and restarts below 160°C.

The synchronous push-pull design example uses the TPS7H5001-SP with GaN devices at 500 kHz. Selected values include a 205-kΩ timing resistor, 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback divider for 5 V output, approximately 25-ns dead time using two 20.5-kΩ resistors, 49.9-kΩ leading-edge blanking resistor, 33-nF soft-start capacitor for about 7.5 ms, transformer turns ratio of 2.5 and 40-µH primary inductance, 170-V primary GaN FETs, 80-V synchronous rectifier FETs, 0.47-µH output inductor, approximately 2.3 mF output capacitance, 7.5-Ω current-sense resistor, and 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor. The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require at least 0.1 µF of VIN bypass capacitance. Layout guidance emphasizes short high-current paths, minimized switch-node area and switching loops, separation of analog and power grounds with a single connection point, close placement of bypass, filtering, feedback, and compensation components, and separation of sensitive traces from high-dv/dt signals. CFP backside metallization should connect to AVSS through multiple vias. The passage introduces iMOOE, a physics-guided invariant learning framework for zero-shot out-of-distribution forecasting of PDE-governed dynamics without test-time adaptation. It identifies two domain-independent properties: invariant elementary physical operators and invariant composition relationships among operators, physical parameters, and forcing terms.

iMOOE combines parallel neural operator experts, derivative-selection masks, and a fusion network aligned with these invariances. Training uses prediction, cross-environment risk equality, high-frequency enrichment, and mask-diversity losses. The framework supports multiple neural operator backbones.

Experiments cover five simulated two-dimensional PDE systems, temporal extrapolation, and real-world sea-surface temperature forecasting. Reported results show state-of-the-art zero-shot performance, including average improvements of 40.21% in normalized MSE and 30.78% in Fourier RMSE across simulated OOD scenarios, plus gains in temporal extrapolation. Compatibility studies show improvements across FNO, DeepONet, VCNeF, and OFormer. Three operator experts performed best in sensitivity tests, while additional experts increased computation. The study is limited to a restricted variety of dynamics; future work targets irregular grids and broader real-world systems.

The Utah Court of Appeals affirmed summary judgment against Kari Baumann in her malpractice action against The Kroger Company and Dr. Gregory Tayler. Baumann failed to disclose expert witnesses by the stipulated deadlines. Because expert testimony was necessary to establish standards of care, breach, and causation, the district court excluded her late expert report under rule 26(d)(4) and ruled that she could not establish a prima facie case.

The appellate court declined to consider Baumann’s argument concerning an expert report for Dr. Tayler because she had not requested permission to submit one in district court and did not establish an exception to the preservation requirement. Regarding Kroger, the court rejected her argument that the discretionary sanctions of rule 16(d) should apply. It held that rule 26(d)(4), governing failures to disclose, controlled and generally requires exclusion unless the failure was harmless or supported by good cause. Baumann did not challenge the finding that she lacked good cause. The district court therefore did not abuse its discretion by excluding the report and granting summary judgment.

The lecture examines interacting Bose gases and methods for reducing difficult many-body Hamiltonians to solvable approximations. For homogeneous condensates, the Bogoliubov approximation replaces the macroscopically occupied zero-momentum operator with a number, producing noninteracting quasiparticles. Their dispersion is linear at low momentum and quadratic at high momentum. Sound propagation and stimulated two-laser scattering can measure these excitations. Interactions also cause quantum depletion, which is small in dilute atomic gases but large in liquid helium.

For trapped, inhomogeneous condensates, replacing the field operator by a macroscopic order parameter yields the Gross-Pitaevskii nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Its interaction term favors uniform density. The healing length characterizes how density adjusts near boundaries or nodes. When interaction energy dominates kinetic energy, the Thomas-Fermi approximation gives the density by inverting and filling the trapping potential. The Gross-Pitaevskii equation quantitatively describes condensate expansion and vortices. Rotation produces vortices with zero density at their centers; multiply charged vortices are unstable because separating them lowers kinetic energy, while repulsion organizes vortices into hexagonal lattices.

Optical lattices reduce kinetic energy and facilitate strongly correlated regimes. In the tight-binding limit, localized Wannier functions lead to the Bose-Hubbard model, characterized by nearest-neighbor tunneling energy \(J\) and on-site interaction energy \(U\). When \(U\) dominates, tunneling is suppressed and the system forms a Mott insulator with fixed occupation per site. When \(J\) dominates, atoms condense into the lowest quasimomentum state and form a superfluid.

A mean-field decoupling of the tunneling term introduces a superfluid order parameter. Perturbation theory around the insulating state determines whether nonzero superfluidity lowers the energy, producing a phase diagram of Mott-insulating lobes separated by superfluid regions. Experiments distinguish the phases through time-of-flight interference: coherent superfluids produce diffraction patterns, whereas Mott insulators expand without structure. Quantum gas microscopes can directly resolve site occupations.

A study of 2,066 18-year-old twins in England and Wales found that loneliness was associated with twice the likelihood of mental health problems such as depression and anxiety, a 38% higher unemployment risk, and more smoking and inactivity. The study developed a Pragmatic Trial Operations playbook within a Learning Health System framework to evaluate Ambient AI, a generative AI tool embedded in the Epic electronic health record to assist clinical documentation at UW Health. The playbook integrated governance, user experience, technical implementation, documentation compliance, and analytics through alpha testing and a beta pragmatic randomized clinical trial.

The alpha phase ran from June 24 to October 10, 2024, involving 20 providers, five specialties, 12 clinic locations, and 8,527 encounters. Iterative Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles, provider interviews, technical monitoring, and human-factors frameworks identified barriers involving workflow variability, organizational settings, provider and patient readiness, privacy concerns, and task suitability. Training, support, templates, and workflows were subsequently refined. Weighted median daily Ambient AI utilization was 65.4%.

Manual review revealed that removing visit diagnoses from AI-generated note templates reduced ICD-10 documentation accuracy from 79% before implementation to 35% afterward. A revised template restored accuracy to pre-intervention levels. Because coders spent 598.33 hours reviewing documentation, an automated large language model system was developed to flag higher-risk notes. Validation on 200 notes produced a mean Jaccard score of 0.54.

A real-time dashboard monitored utilization, consent compliance, provider feedback, documentation efficiency, work outside work, time in notes, and performance drift. Rolling difference-in-differences analyses found no substantial drift; observed averages included a 6.84-percentage-point decrease in utilization, a 0.33-hour increase in work outside work, and a 0.43-hour increase in time spent in notes.

The beta phase was designed as a 24-week, multisite, stepped-wedge trial of 66 providers across eight specialties in Wisconsin and Illinois. Providers were randomized into three waves transitioning to Ambient AI at six-week intervals. The primary evaluation uses the Professional Fulfillment Index to assess provider well-being, with additional operational and safety monitoring. The study presents the playbook as a scalable model for aligning rigorous evaluation with clinical operations during AI implementation.

The study presents DSCHECKER, an LLM-based approach for detecting and fixing API misuses in Python data science libraries. Such misuses are difficult to identify because API behavior may depend on dynamic properties of complex inputs such as DataFrames and arrays. DSCHECKER prompts off-the-shelf LLMs with API documentation directives and runtime variable information, then requests misuse classifications, explanations, and unified-diff patches.

The authors evaluated DSCHECKER using DSMISUSES, a curated dataset of 38 reproducible misuses and 38 corrected examples from NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, scikit-learn, and seaborn. Detection was measured using precision, recall, and F1-score; fixes were executed and manually assessed. An ablation study compared prompts containing no added context, data information, API directives, or both.

Providing both directives and data generally improved larger models, though results varied by model. Llama with the full zero-shot prompt achieved the highest overall detection F1-score of 61.18% and fixed 51.28% of misuses. Few-shot prompting significantly improved GPT-4o but slightly reduced llama’s detection performance and did not improve its fixing rate.

On 15 reproduced deep-learning API misuses, DSCHECKER achieved a 48% detection F1-score and a 26.67% fix rate. For cases with explicit directives, detection rose to 66.67%. On DSMISUSES, DSCHECKER achieved 46.15% recall with GPT-4o-mini, compared with 11.19% for LLMAPIDET, which fixed none of its detections.

An agentic version, DSCHECKERagent, autonomously requested documentation and runtime variable information. GPT-4o achieved a 48.65% detection F1-score and 39.47% fix rate, below the fully informed approach but indicating practical potential. Limitations include small datasets, three evaluated models, manual assessment, and possible nondeterminism. Future work includes improving information retrieval, validating tool calls, extracting relevant directives, and creating more machine-readable API documentation.

Camera-trap footage from a Malaysian durian orchard shows that island flying foxes pollinate durian flowers while feeding on nectar without damaging them, improving the crop’s reproductive success. The finding challenges bats’ negative reputation and highlights their role in supporting valuable tropical crops. Island flying fox populations are declining globally and are endangered in Malaysia because of hunting and habitat loss. Researchers emphasize that conserving nectar-eating bats is important for pollination, food security, and human well-being.

A Finnish study of 2,480 men followed for 22 years found that those with the highest blood levels of omega-6 linoleic acid had a 43 percent lower risk of premature death than those with the lowest levels. Higher levels were also associated with reduced cardiovascular mortality, but not cancer mortality. Linoleic acid is found mainly in vegetable oils, plant-based spreads, nuts, and seeds.

NVIDIA’s GA102 and GA104 GPUs extend the Ampere architecture across GeForce RTX 30-series, RTX A6000, and A40 products. Compared with Turing, GA10x delivers up to 1.7× faster raster graphics, 2× faster ray tracing, and 1.9× greater power efficiency at equivalent performance.

Manufactured on Samsung’s 8N process, the full GA102 contains 28.3 billion transistors, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second-generation RT cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor cores. Its Streaming Multiprocessors double peak FP32 processing by enabling both primary datapaths to execute floating-point operations. GA102 also increases L1/shared-memory capacity and bandwidth, relocates ROPs into Graphics Processing Clusters, and supports concurrent RT, graphics, and compute workloads.

Second-generation RT cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and add hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur. A new triangle-position interpolation unit enables accurate motion blur rendering up to eight times faster than Turing. Third-generation Tensor cores support structured sparsity, TF32, BF16, FP16, INT8, INT4, and binary precision. Sparsity can double matrix-processing throughput by skipping zero-valued weights, while DLSS uses Tensor cores to construct high-resolution images and enable 8K gaming.

GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, reaching data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/s. RTX A6000 and A40 instead use 48 GB of GDDR6, expandable to 96 GB by connecting two GPUs through third-generation NVLink. GA10x also supports PCIe 4.0, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4a, 4K at 120 Hz, and 8K at 60 Hz.

RTX IO works with Microsoft DirectStorage to move compressed assets directly from NVMe storage to the GPU for decompression. It can accelerate I/O by up to 100 times over hard drives and traditional APIs, reduce CPU utilization, shorten loading times, and improve asset streaming.

Fifth-generation NVDEC supports hardware decoding for formats including MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, HEVC, VP8, VP9, and AV1. GA10x is described as the first GPU family with hardware AV1 decoding, supporting up to 8K60 HDR with low CPU use. Seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding up to 4K in H.264 and 8K in HEVC.

The RTX 3090 includes 10,496 CUDA cores and 24 GB of GDDR6X and targets 8K HDR gaming and compute workloads. The RTX 3080 offers up to twice the RTX 2080’s performance, while the RTX 3070 rivals or exceeds the RTX 2080 Ti. The RTX A6000 combines 48 GB of GDDR6 with professional rendering, AI, and compute capabilities. The A40 offers similar core and memory capacity for data-center visualization, virtual workstations, and server workloads.

GA10x’s GDDR6X interface also includes Error Detection and Replay, which detects transmission errors and retries transactions. During memory overclocking, increasing retries causes performance to plateau, indicating the practical memory limit before instability.

Rice University and the Houston Museum of Natural Science have collaborated on space-science education since 1988. For the 2023–2024 Heliophysics Big Year, they expanded eclipse outreach through teacher training, websites, media, free animations, safety materials, viewing equipment, public events, and the fulldome show “Totality.”

Since 2021, eclipse animations were requested by 186 educators in 33 countries and received over 19,000 YouTube views. “Totality” and its Texas version were distributed to 200 sites in multiple formats and languages, generating more than 180,000 documented views. Teacher courses and workshops emphasized eclipse science and safety, reaching 5,104 educators through listed live events. Nearly one million eclipse viewers were distributed across Texas, alongside activities such as solar projectors, observation worksheets, and safety resources.

The partnership also supported Citizen CATE 2024, which used identically equipped volunteer teams at 35 primary sites to create continuous, polarized images of the April 8, 2024 solar corona. More than 250 participants contributed; over 80% of teams observed some or all of totality, and analysis remains underway.

Public eclipse events drew thousands, while media outreach reached additional audiences. The project also issued short-term space-weather forecasts and alerts, including accurate predictions during the May 2024 geomagnetic storm.

Overall, the partnership documented more than 250,000 views through teachers, museums, and planetariums, confirmed 5,405 teacher users, and estimated total reach above 1.5 million people. Survey respondents reported sharing materials with an average of more than 500 people each.

A collection of March 2001 articles examines California’s electricity crisis. Gov. Gray Davis proposed buying utility transmission lines, creating a public power authority and securing long-term electricity contracts, but critics questioned federal approval, costs, implementation delays and government operation of the system.

Experts warned of severe summer power shortages despite conservation and new generation. The Public Utilities Commission considered revising residential baseline allowances and extending temporary rate increases while defending its response to failed deregulation.

Cal-ISO alleged suppliers charged about $562 million above reasonable prices in December and January and requested federal review and refunds; generators denied wrongdoing. Lawmakers urged suppliers to forgive utility debts, while Enron executive Steven Kean saw no reason to do so. PG&E paid only $228 million of roughly $1.4 billion owed, alarming smaller suppliers and intensifying bankruptcy concerns.

California signed major long-term contracts with Calpine, while former regulator Elizabeth Moler advocated temporary federal wholesale price controls. Federal regulators remained skeptical of price caps and the proposed state transmission takeover.

Ventura police will review procedures after Anthony Mele was fatally stabbed in a crowded steakhouse. Chief Ken Corney said officers should have responded in person to earlier reports about suspect Jamal Jackson, who faces a murder charge. Residents criticized officials’ handling of homeless and mentally ill people.

The lecture revisits least-squares duality, showing that equality and optimality occur when \(b=Ax+w\), and poses a geometric identity involving distances from a point to a rectangle’s corners. It then introduces inverse problems, where small measurement errors can cause large solution errors. Examples include deriving velocity from noisy position data, seismology, medical imaging, gravitational measurements, scattering, coefficient recovery in differential equations, GPS velocity estimation, and genomics.

Many inverse problems can be expressed as first-kind integral equations and discretized into matrix problems, but finer discretization may worsen ill-posedness. Regularization improves stability by adding a positive identity term. Tikhonov regularization minimizes
\[
\|Ax-b\|^2+\alpha\|x\|^2,
\]
balancing fidelity against smoothing. If measurement noise has size \(\delta\), the noise-related error scales as \(\delta/\sqrt{\alpha}\). Choosing \(\alpha=\delta^{2/3}\) provides the stated balance: \(\alpha\) decreases as measurements improve without making the problem excessively sensitive to noise.

Mitch Larkin may add the individual medley to his Commonwealth Games trials schedule after winning the 400m IM at the Queensland titles in 4:20.45. However, the dual backstroke world champion remains focused on restoring his backstroke to world-class level. After earning 200m silver but missing the 100m podium at the Rio Olympics, Larkin changed coaches twice before joining Dean Boxall’s endurance-focused program. He says a difficult year has renewed his motivation for Olympic redemption.

Canon’s EOS M6 is an entry-level mirrorless camera with a 24.2-megapixel sensor, Digic 7 processor, optional viewfinder, pop-up flash and tilting 3.2-inch touchscreen. Shipping in April 2017, it starts at $780. Comparable Sony A5100 and A6000 models cost less, with the A6000 including a viewfinder, making the M6 difficult to justify.

Opioid misuse is associated with high overdose and mortality rates, and respiratory depression is a major risk of mu-opioid receptor (MOR) agonists. Naloxone reverses opioid effects and is used with buprenorphine to manage opioid use disorder. Although [11C]carfentanil ([11C]CFN) PET has extensively characterized brain MOR availability, including age- and sex-related differences, spinal cord and peripheral-organ studies remain limited.

Long axial field-of-view PET enables sensitive, dynamic whole-body imaging. This study presents the first human whole-body neuroreceptor PET investigation using [11C]CFN and evaluates the aorta and muscle as extra-central nervous system reference regions.

Healthy English-speaking adults aged 18–45 without psychiatric or substance use disorders underwent MRI and 90-minute dynamic PET imaging on the PennPET Explorer after [11C]CFN injection. Drug testing confirmed the absence of potentially interfering substances. PET/CT images were processed with PMOD, aligned with MRI and normalized to standard space. MOR distribution volume ratios were calculated for the bilateral amygdala, caudate, putamen, thalamus, and ventral tegmentum using the visual cortex as reference tissue and the Logan reference tissue model.

Arizona man Douglas Haig was charged with illegally manufacturing and selling armor-piercing ammunition to Las Vegas gunman Stephen Paddock. Forensic evidence linked Haig’s fingerprints and reloading equipment to cartridges found in Paddock’s hotel rooms. Haig, released on bail, faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine. Paddock killed 58 people and wounded hundreds at a music festival before killing himself.

On Aug. 21, a total solar eclipse will cross the United States from Oregon to South Carolina, the first coast-to-coast eclipse in 99 years and the first visible in the Lower 48 in 38 years. The roughly 60- to 70-mile-wide path of totality will pass through 14 states, with darkness lasting from under two minutes to a maximum of two minutes and 44 seconds in southern Illinois.

NASA, scientists, students, astronauts, aircraft and ships will observe the eclipse using balloons, satellites, telescopes and cameras. Numerous festivals and public events are planned, and large crowds are expected because about 200 million people live within a day’s drive of the path. A partial eclipse will be visible across a wider region, including parts of Canada, Central America and South America.

The full event will span about four hours, while the lunar shadow will cross the country in roughly 90 minutes at more than 1,500 mph. Temperatures may fall 10 to 15 degrees, and researchers will monitor plant and animal reactions. Eye protection is required during all partial phases, though not during the brief period of totality. Another eclipse will cross parts of North America on April 8, 2024.

Oncosec Medical shares fell 12.71%, closing at $1.58. Three analysts set an average 12-month target of $5.33, ranging from $5 to $6. Its average brokerage recommendation is 1, with three analysts rating it Outperform; the industry ranks 192 of 265. The stock’s 14-period ATR is 0.15, weekly volatility is 6.79%, monthly volatility is 8.05%, and RSI is 33.61. Oncosec has a $54.72 million market capitalization and 34.63 million outstanding shares. Previous trading volume was 4.56 million shares, compared with an average of about 2.4 million.

Colorado coach Deion Sanders, 58, underwent a procedure for recurring hereditary blood clots and hoped to return to practice the next day and coach against No. 22 Iowa State. Sanders experienced severe leg pain during a 35-21 loss at TCU. He previously had two left toes amputated after clot complications and underwent additional procedures in 2023. Sanders also received treatment for aggressive bladder cancer over the summer but said his current condition was unavoidable and expressed confidence in his recovery.

IDC’s white paper examines industrial simulation, modeling, data analysis, and high-performance computing (HPC), based on a 2021 survey of 200 manufacturing decision makers in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Manufacturers use these technologies to accelerate development, improve quality, reduce costs, support decisions, and enable digital products and business models. Deployment is expected to expand substantially, with 64% planning investments.

HPC enables faster, more accurate, and complex calculations, additional iterations, and new applications such as digital twins, virtual prototyping, design optimization, and high-performance data analytics. Among respondents, 81% view HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation. More than a quarter already use professional HPC infrastructure, while 39% are planning or piloting it.

Key obstacles include security risks, investment and operating costs, energy consumption, insufficient computing capacity, infrastructure complexity, availability, licensing, and limited expertise. Most HPC users prefer external infrastructure, including cloud and colocation services, rather than on-premises systems.

Public and hybrid cloud architectures are expected to become especially important because they offer scalability, flexibility, and access to capacity during peak demand. IDC recommends evaluating whether to build internal infrastructure or purchase HPC services, considering technical requirements, costs, agility, data protection, and workload intensity.

Rockefeller University researchers developed a chamber that kept a 0.5-millimeter slice of gerbil cochlea alive and functional outside the body. By reproducing its temperature, voltage, and fluid environment, they observed hearing mechanisms at subcellular resolution as sounds were played.

The team saw hair-cell ion channels add energy to vibrations and outer hair cells change shape through electromotility. They also directly confirmed that mammalian sound amplification depends on a Hopf bifurcation, a mechanical tipping point previously documented in bullfrogs and other animals. This supports a shared biophysical principle of hearing across species.

The ex vivo cochlea enables controlled study of specific cells and interactions, including targeted pharmacological experiments. Researchers hope it will clarify how hearing functions and fails, potentially supporting therapies for sensorineural hearing loss, for which no restorative drug has been approved.

The lecture defines additive energy \(E(A,B)\) in an Abelian group as the number of quadruples satisfying \(a_1+b_1=a_2+b_2\), equivalently \(\sum_x r_{A,B}(x)^2\). For one set, energy lies between roughly \(|A|^2\) and \(|A|^3\). If \(|A+A|\le k|A|\), Cauchy–Schwarz gives \(E(A)\ge |A|^3/k\), so small doubling implies large energy. The converse fails because a set may combine a highly structured subset with unstructured elements, producing both large energy and large doubling.

The Balog–Szemerédi–Gowers theorem remedies this failure: a set with large additive energy contains a polynomially large subset with small doubling. A stronger two-set version finds large subsets \(A'\subseteq A\) and \(B'\subseteq B\) whose sumset \(A'+B'\) is small. Ruzsa-type inequalities recover the one-set version from this statement.

The proof proceeds through a graphical version. For a dense bipartite graph \(G\) between \(A\) and \(B\), define the restricted sumset using sums across edges. If this restricted sumset is small, then large subsets \(A'\) and \(B'\) have a small unrestricted sumset. Large additive energy yields such a graph by retaining edges corresponding to popular sums: unpopular sums contribute little energy, while the popular sums form a dense graph with a small restricted sumset.

The graphical theorem uses dependent random choice. A path-of-length-2 lemma finds a large subset in which most vertex pairs have many common neighbors. After trimming low-degree vertices and refining both sides, a path-of-length-3 lemma produces large subsets \(A'\) and \(B'\) such that every pair between them is connected by many length-3 paths. Along each path, \(a+b\) can be represented as \(x-y+z\), where \(x,y,z\) belong to the restricted sumset. Counting these representations bounds \(|A'+B'|\) polynomially in the original parameters, proving the graphical and additive forms of the theorem.

Each digital I/O maps to a PINCM register for selecting its function. Only one IOMUX-managed digital function can connect to a pin simultaneously. For analog or other non-IOMUX functions, PINCM.PF and PINCM.PC should be 0. Non-IOMUX and digital functions may coexist if the designer ensures no contention.

The patent describes memory arrays with vertically alternating tiers of insulating material and memory cells. Each cell includes a transistor with a horizontally oriented channel between source/drain regions and one or more gates, plus a capacitor electrically coupled to one source/drain region. Vertical sense-line structures connect transistors across tiers, while vertical capacitor-electrode structures connect capacitor electrodes. Embodiments vary gate, channel, capacitor, and stacked-cell configurations. A fabrication method uses layered deposition, selective etching, gap filling, patterning, and conductive vias to form transistors, capacitors, access lines, sense lines, electrode structures, and staircase contacts.
XPIC clears the IRR bit late, causing duplicate CPU interrupts during AEOI. AEOI applies only to the master PIC and disables nested multilevel interrupts.

NVIDIA Ampere Tensor Cores add BF16, TF32, and FP64. BF16 and FP16 support mixed-precision neural-network training and provide 16 times FP32 throughput on A100 GPUs. TF32 enables default Tensor Core acceleration while accepting FP32 data, retaining FP32 range, and producing FP32 output.

The Louisiana Supreme Court declined Arthur Rhodes’s writ as untimely. His denied post-conviction application is final, and further state collateral review is barred unless a narrow statutory exception for successive applications applies. The district court must record a consistent minute entry.

The invention describes an automated storage, retrieval, and processing system using gantry conveyance systems, storage and destination bins, and programmable robotic devices. Selected bins are moved to a processing station, where a robotic arm uses an end effector to grasp objects from storage bins and place them into destination bins according to a manifest.

A perception system analyzes bin contents and identifies suitable grasp points. It favors flat surfaces, locations near an object’s center of mass, and features such as barcodes, while avoiding obscured or unstable points. Machine learning may correlate image features with successful and unsuccessful grasps. The end effector may approach normal to an object’s surface to improve grasping, particularly with vacuum tools.

Storage and destination bins may occupy separate, shared, intermingled, or dynamically assigned locations. Systems may use common gantries, multiple processing stations, multiple sources, and multiple floors. Computer systems continuously track each bin’s identity and location, coordinate motion devices, and direct object distribution. Completed destination bins may be transferred to output conveyors, staging areas, or shipment pallets.

The President stated that 653 troops, excluding marines stationed at the navy-yard, were assembled in Washington as a posse comitatus subordinate to civil authority. Their purpose was to preserve order, protect public property and government archives, and secure the President-elect’s inauguration amid widespread alarm and rumors. Although a House committee found no proof of a hostile secret organization, the House rejected a resolution calling for the troops’ immediate removal. The President maintained that precautionary action was justified and that the troops’ arrival restored comparative peace and security.

Startup owners seeking initial funding should focus on investor priorities: potential return on investment, equity terms, and possible mentoring or future investment rights. Founders should present themselves confidently, communicate persuasively, accept constructive advice, and demonstrate support from an experienced, proactive team. Evidence of market traction, such as revenue or customer satisfaction, strengthens credibility.

Investors may favor industries they know, emerging markets, market gaps, or disruptive ideas with strong growth potential. Founders should clearly explain market challenges and practical responses. A detailed business plan must include reliable data, realistic projections, competitive research, market threats and opportunities, and an understanding of the consequences of missing forecasts. Preparation, business knowledge, and clear communication can increase investor confidence and improve fundraising prospects.

President Biden presented the American Jobs Plan as a roughly $2 trillion, eight-year investment intended to rebuild infrastructure, create millions of well-paying jobs, strengthen unions and the middle class, address climate change, and improve U.S. competitiveness, particularly with China. He linked the proposal to the American Rescue Plan, citing vaccination progress, projected economic growth, and reduced child poverty.

The plan would modernize roads, bridges, airports, rail, transit, ports, electric grids, housing, and commercial buildings. It would replace lead water pipes, expand affordable high-speed internet, build electric-vehicle charging stations, support clean-energy manufacturing, improve climate resilience, and expand home- and community-based care. It would also increase non-defense research and development in areas including batteries, biotechnology, computer chips, and clean energy. Biden pledged to prioritize American companies, products, and workers while directing investment toward historically underserved communities.

Biden said the plan would support workers’ organizing rights and urged passage of the PRO Act. He proposed financing it by raising the corporate tax rate from 21 to 28 percent, establishing a 21 percent global minimum tax for U.S. corporations, discouraging offshoring, eliminating related deductions, and increasing IRS enforcement. He promised no federal tax increase for people earning under $400,000.

Calling infrastructure historically bipartisan, Biden invited Republican alternatives and negotiations while insisting action was necessary. He framed the plan as a test of whether democracy can deliver economic opportunity, national resilience, and long-term global leadership.

Bear markets are generally viewed as declines of at least 20%, though no official definition exists. They are typically shorter and steeper than corrections or bull markets, with heightened volatility and sharp rallies. The S&P 500 has traded above its 200-day moving average 70% of the time since 1960 and 85% since 2010.

During the 2000–2003 bear market, the dividend-adjusted S&P 500 fell 45% and did not reach a new high until late 2006. The Nasdaq declined more than 80% from March 2000 to October 2002 and took 15 years to recover.

The passage argues that bear markets create opportunities for investors to buy stocks more cheaply and for traders to benefit from increased volatility through long and short strategies. A mean-reversion strategy on QQQ produced average gains of 2.07% across 38 trades during the dot-com decline and 2.14% across 19 trades during the global financial crisis. Long-term investors are advised to continue adding positions, while those nearing retirement or withdrawals face greater concern. Bear markets are presented as a natural part of market cycles that may remove economic excesses and encourage innovation.

Hong Kong stocks ended slightly higher, with the Hang Seng up 0.2% and China Enterprises Index up 0.1%. Gains in Tencent, banks and shipping firms offset property-sector weakness amid tighter housing curbs and Moody’s warning of growing financial risks from a potential downturn.

The coach praised the team’s energy, speed, territorial control, scoring chances, net traffic and resilience despite an unsettled start and failure to find a third goal. He said the players defended well against offense generated below the goal line and remained aware of Burns’ ability to join the rush. He emphasized controlled emotion, trusted the team’s leadership and urged players to stay focused on routines and the immediate task despite the high stakes.

He described Sid as a force regardless of matchups and said Geno’s improving two-way play and scoring make the team harder to defend. Sergei was called invaluable for his relationship with the defense and the insights his recent playing experience provides. The coach also praised Matt’s performance, versatility, experience, composure and influence in the locker room, describing him as an extension of the coaching staff.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that it issued a July 20, 2017 press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2017. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under the Exchange Act.

European Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker said India’s 5.7% GDP growth should not be considered a slowdown compared with Europe’s 2%. The rate had fallen to a three-year low amid demonetisation and GST implementation. World Bank President Jim Yong Kim called it temporary, while BJP leader Yashwant Sinha urged corrective action.

β-Ga₂O₃ is promising for high-power, optoelectronic, and flexible devices because of its wide bandgap, high breakdown field, and mechanical flexibility, but its low thermal conductivity creates thermal-management challenges. Device fabrication and operation generate nonuniform strains and strain gradients that can significantly affect phonon transport.

The study combines a density-functional-theory-trained neuroevolution machine-learning potential, the phonon Boltzmann transport equation, and a strain-gradient scattering model to examine bulk, 10-nm, and 100-nm β-Ga₂O₃ under uniaxial and biaxial uniform strains and strain gradients at 300 K. The potential reproduces DFT energies, forces, phonon dispersions, lattice parameters, and experimental thermal conductivities. Boundary, isotope, three-phonon, and strain-gradient scattering are included, while four-phonon scattering is neglected due to its weak contribution.

Uniform strain substantially and anisotropically changes thermal conductivity, mainly by modifying intrinsic phonon lifetimes and three-phonon scattering rather than heat capacity or group velocity. It also strongly tunes thermal anisotropy. In contrast, strain gradients suppress conductivity more strongly while producing much smaller changes in anisotropy.

For 10-nm films, a uniaxial gradient of 0.6%/nm reduces conductivity along the three crystallographic axes by 31.8–36.6%, exceeding reductions from the corresponding 3% uniform tensile strain. Biaxial gradients produce reductions of 41.6–43.3%, about 1.5 times those under equivalent uniform strain. Ten-nanometer nanowires show reductions of 27–30%. Effects are weaker in 100-nm structures.

Strain gradients break translational symmetry, broaden phonon spectra, alter mode-frequency gaps, activate previously forbidden scattering channels, and expand phonon scattering phase space. Gradient-induced scattering particularly affects acoustic and low-lying optical phonons and can dominate total scattering below 10 THz. The findings show that strain gradients must be explicitly included in β-Ga₂O₃ thermal modeling and may enable thermal isolation without substantially changing designed directional heat pathways.

UCLA researchers found that lactate production regulates hair follicle stem cell activation and hair growth in mice. Genetically blocking lactate prevented stem cell activation, while increasing it accelerated activation and the hair cycle. Two topical experimental drugs also promoted lactate production and faster hair growth: RCGD423 activated the JAK-Stat pathway, and UK5099 blocked pyruvate from entering mitochondria. The findings may support development of hair-loss treatments, but both drugs have undergone only preclinical testing and have not been tested in humans or approved by the FDA. UCLA has filed separate provisional patents covering their use for hair growth.

Colgate-Palmolive’s outlook has improved as revenue and profit growth return, prompting an Argus upgrade and a $72 price target. Its forward price-to-earnings ratio is below 20, while analysts expect mid- to high-single-digit profit growth over the next three fiscal years. Colgate has raised its dividend annually since 1964 and currently yields about 2.6%.

However, the company faces long-term competitive risks. Its commoditized products historically relied on brand recognition and shelf-space control, but e-commerce enables smaller manufacturers and niche products to reach consumers more easily. Although Colgate retains loyal customers and time to adapt, the author argues its limited competitive moat and reduced growth potential make a valuation near 20 times earnings too high.

Officials raised the AJC Peachtree Road Race alert to Code Red due to dangerous conditions, advising runners to slow down and follow instructions. Temperatures were forecast in the upper 80s. The $70,000 prize purse was reserved for American athletes, with $10,000 awarded to each top male and female.
On Aug. 21, Columbia and the Midlands will experience daytime darkness within the total solar eclipse’s path of totality. WIS News 10 will air a preparation and safety special at 7:30 p.m.

The shallow cross passing concept combines a 10–12-yard basic route with a 3–4-yard shallow drag from opposite directions, stressing linebackers and providing answers against man and zone coverage. A flare route creates a triangle read, while post and go routes offer downfield options. Receivers continue moving against man coverage but may settle in open voids against zone.

The concept is effective against man, Tampa 2, and Cover 4. It is less effective against Cover 3, whose four underneath defenders provide a numerical advantage. It also gives quarterbacks quick options against blitzes or immediate pressure.

Quarterbacks first assess downfield routes, then progress through the post, drag, basic, and running back checkdown. Pre-snap, they evaluate the outside fade and identify man or zone coverage.

A bunch-set variation uses a post-out combination against two-high defenses, followed by the drag and basic routes. An empty-set post-wheel variation provides quick pressure answers and challenges one-high defenses; if defenders cover the glance and wheel, the drag can replace the departing safety and create space underneath.

Brea police are using a two-seat Polaris Gem electric vehicle to patrol downtown and The Tracks trail. Funded with Air Quality Management District money, it cost about $21,000. The vehicle travels up to 25 mph, has a 98-mile range, charges in six to eight hours, and can operate off-road.

The MSPM0C1105/1106 debug subsystem connects the ARM Serial Wire Debug interface to processor and device-state debugging, software communication through a mailbox, configurable peripheral behavior during debug, PMCU reset and mode requests, and security features such as SWD lockout and password authentication. SWD pins include default pull resistors and can be repurposed as GPIO.

A read-only, memory-mapped FACTORY region stores device capabilities, identification, hardware revision, and factory trim data. DEVICEID is at 0x41C4.0004 and USERID at 0x41C4.0008. Identification and revision information also appear in package markings.

Typical applications should use 10-µF and 0.1-µF low-ESR ceramic decoupling capacitors near VDD and VSS. NRST requires a 47-kΩ pullup resistor and 1000-pF pulldown capacitor. External crystals require bypass capacitors, while 5-V-tolerant open-drain I/Os require pullups for logic-high output.

TI distinguishes experimental “X” devices from fully qualified “MSP” production devices and recommends only qualified devices for production. Development resources include LaunchPad hardware, BoosterPack modules, software drivers, libraries, examples, cloud and offline tools, Resource Explorer, SysConfig, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, Code Composer Studio, and TI support forums.

The September 2025 revision removed DGS32 package information, updated multiple specifications and CPU features, edited ADC ENOB information, added the DEBUGSS section, and revised DEVICEID and USERID tables. Packaging drawings specify thermal-pad soldering, optional vias, stencil guidance, and solder coverage. TI warns that ESD can damage devices and provides technical resources “as is,” with developers responsible for component selection, design validation, testing, and compliance.

Digital communication uses a binary interface between source and channel coding, enabling standardization, layering, and no performance loss. Source coding converts waveforms into sampled analog sequences, quantizes them into finite alphabets with unavoidable distortion, and discretely encodes symbols for transmission over an assumed reliable binary channel.

Fixed-length coding assigns each of \(m\) source symbols a binary string of length \(l=\lceil\log_2 m\rceil\). Encoding blocks of \(n\) symbols reduces the rate toward \(\log_2 m\) bits per source symbol. Symbols’ identities have no inherent communication significance; only the number of distinguishable possibilities matters. Synchronization is assumed.

Variable-length coding assigns shorter codewords to probable symbols and longer ones to unlikely symbols. Because concatenated codewords have no separators, codes must be uniquely decodable, and buffering may be needed to reconcile variable output rates with fixed-rate channels. Prefix-free codes, in which no codeword prefixes another, are instantaneously and uniquely decodable and can be represented by binary trees.

The Kraft inequality states that prefix-free codeword lengths satisfy \(\sum_x 2^{-l(x)}\leq1\); conversely, any lengths satisfying it permit construction of a prefix-free code. Equality corresponds to a full code tree. The result follows by associating codewords with disjoint subintervals of \([0,1]\). Uniquely decodable codes also satisfy the inequality, though they need not be prefix-free.

The next topic is discrete memoryless sources: infinite sequences of letters selected independently and identically from a finite alphabet under a common, not necessarily uniform, probability distribution. This simplified model supports later study of entropy, optimal coding, dependent sources, Markov models, and more complex sources such as English text.

BG Group agreed to buy Enron’s offshore Indian oil and gas assets for $388 million, including interests in the Tapti and Panna/Mukta fields and the CB-OS/1 exploration block. The assets hold more than 170 million barrels of oil equivalent, and analysts generally viewed the price as favorable. Completion requires Indian government approval and agreement that BG will operate the fields; state-owned ONGC continued seeking operatorship, creating a potential obstacle. BG plans to expand production and strengthen its Indian gas business.

Enron was separately seeking to exit the troubled Dabhol Power Project, where it held a controlling stake. Dabhol had shut down amid tariff and payment disputes and defaulted on a $24 million interest payment to Indian lenders.

Elsewhere, Enron shares rose 9.4% during a broad technology-led U.S. market rally. Southern California Edison’s settlement with California would help repay debts owed to power suppliers, including Enron, while maintaining higher customer rates. Former Enron Energy Services vice chairman and Army Secretary Thomas White was appointed the Defense Department’s lead official for homeland security.

Learning assessment is well established in credit-bearing higher education but remains uncommon in noncredit continuing education, where satisfaction surveys are more prevalent. Noncredit programs include professional competency, career development, and personal enrichment activities. Their short duration, expert-led instruction, varied learner motivations, and limited institutional resources may constrain assessment, despite its potential to improve curricula, teaching, and learning.

Effective assessment begins with clear, measurable learning outcomes suited to course duration, learners’ prior knowledge, and program goals. Outcomes should be specific, achievable, relevant, time-bound, communicated early, and developed collaboratively with instructors. Learner feedback can also inform them.

End-of-course surveys can incorporate questions asking learners to rate their achievement or perceived gains. Retrospective pre-post questions are useful for short courses, although self-reports remain subjective. Repeated surveys can identify low perceived achievement and guide revisions to instruction, curriculum, and outcomes.

Direct assessment involves expert evaluation of learner products or performances. Short courses can add a few quiz-type questions to satisfaction surveys, scored simply as sufficient or insufficient. Medium-duration programs can use practical activities, role-plays, presentations, plans, demonstrations, or completed products aligned with learning outcomes. Assessments should be credible, trustworthy, fair, transparent, and beneficial to learners where possible. Measurement experts, instructors, or learners can help review clarity and alignment.

Assessment results can support course improvement, demonstrate program quality, inform personnel decisions, and justify resources. Digital credentials may motivate learners and require alignment between outcomes and direct assessment. The authors conclude that well-designed outcomes, learning-focused surveys, and direct assessments are feasible and worthwhile in noncredit continuing education.

Dairylea Cooperative appealed the denial of its application to quash a subpoena for corporate records in a grand jury investigation. The court held that the order was appealable and that Executive Law §63(3) authorized the Attorney-General to issue the subpoena because the Commissioner of Agriculture and Markets had requested the investigation. The order was affirmed without costs.

The application describes methods, apparatuses, communication nodes, and storage media for managing maximum power exposure in high-frequency mobile communications. A first communication node, such as user equipment, reports power parameters and/or uplink channel state information to a second node, such as a base station. Reportable information may include maximum power reduction, power headroom, power backoff, exposure energy, uplink duty cycle, alerts, reference signals, antenna groups, path loss, beam information, and quasi co-location information.

Reports may be periodic, semi-persistent, aperiodic, threshold-triggered, variation-triggered, timer-triggered, or configured by the base station. Power parameters may be associated with beams, antenna panels, reference signals, spatial relations, transmission occasions, and uplink power-control settings. Real or virtual power-headroom reports can identify candidate uplink beams and their associated power conditions.

The base station receives the report, determines beam-specific or antenna-group-specific power reduction, and schedules uplink transmission to reduce human exposure while maintaining transmission performance. The disclosed functionality may be implemented through software, hardware, processors with stored programs, or computer-readable storage media.

The lecture concludes Markov chains and introduces dynamic programming. For a transition matrix partitioned into transient and recurrent blocks, its determinant factors into the determinants of those blocks, so its eigenvalues are their combined eigenvalues; transitions from transient to recurrent states do not affect them. Left eigenvectors of recurrent blocks extend to the full matrix by adding zeros.

Markov reward models assign rewards to states or transitions. Expected aggregate rewards combine transient effects with a steady-state gain per step in ergodic chains. Expected first-passage times can be calculated by making the destination a zero-reward trapping state and solving linear equations for the remaining expected reward.

Dynamic programming considers finite-horizon decisions where each action determines an immediate reward and transition probabilities.
