Bellman’s algorithm works backward from a specified final reward: it solves the one-step problem, then recursively computes optimal expected rewards for longer horizons by maximizing immediate reward plus expected optimal future reward.

Power is a gap run play featuring a pulling backside guard, a kick-out block, back blocks, and double teams that concentrate blockers at the point of attack. It can be used from many personnel groups, formations, and offensive schemes. Its primary strengths are creating favorable blocking angles, double teams, and numerical advantages. Vertical double teams suit powerful lines, while horizontal combinations can help undersized lines.

Its main weakness is backside pursuit and penetration through the gap vacated by the pulling guard. Backside tackles must prevent edge defenders from turning the corner, while centers must correctly identify linebackers, especially against odd fronts, to avoid leaving an unblocked rusher.

Against both 3-4 odd and 4-3 even fronts, linemen use back blocks, combination blocks, hinges, and a pulling guard who targets the playside linebacker. The fullback generally kicks out the end defender, the tailback follows the pulling guard, the quarterback reverse-pivots for the handoff, and receivers push toward nearby safeties.

Variations include fullhouse Power, where one back arcs outside while another performs the kick-out, and same-side shotgun Power RPO, where the quarterback may throw a bubble or slant when the defensive box count or safety movement favors a pass.

The lecture examines the economics of green buildings through the “triple bottom line” of planet, people, and profit, emphasizing that private developers and investors require financial incentives to provide sustainable buildings. Millennium Partners illustrates how developers adapt projects to market and policy priorities, shifting from luxury, job creation, and wellness toward sustainability at Boston’s Winthrop Center.

Green buildings can benefit tenants through lower operating costs, improved health and productivity, and employee recruitment and retention. These benefits may increase tenants’ willingness to pay, rents, occupancy, and property values while reducing vacancies, depreciation, financing costs, and regulatory, market, and physical risks. Developers may then receive higher sale prices, although they must compare these gains with potentially higher construction or retrofit costs. Evidence reviewed in the lecture indicates average rent and sales premiums for green buildings, but results vary widely, and operating costs may rise or fall. Costs can decline through passive design, technological advances, accumulated expertise, and improved supply chains.

The market mechanism forms a chain from tenants to owners to developers: end-user demand supports owner cash flow and asset value, which encourages development. However, market failures can disrupt this process. Information asymmetry may prevent buyers from recognizing green-building benefits, reducing willingness to pay and discouraging legitimate green development. Surveys in China found that green-building residents and consumers given relevant information reported greater willingness to pay. Without credible signals, developers may engage in greenwashing, buyers may treat green and conventional buildings alike, and higher-quality projects may leave the market through adverse selection. Certifications such as LEED can reduce this information problem by helping buyers distinguish verified green buildings. Other market failures, including split incentives and externalities, are identified for later discussion.

South Dakota’s Board of Regents requested a plan to close Pierre’s jointly operated Capital University Center for consideration at its Oct. 3-5 meeting. Regents cited the need for an organized wind-down after extended discussion.

Bill Purswell was convicted of unlawfully transporting intoxicating liquor and sentenced to one year in prison. Officers hiding in a field near a social gathering testified that they saw Purswell carrying a jug containing whiskey and arrested him without a warrant. Defense witnesses disputed that he possessed the jug.

The court held that Purswell could not challenge the search of premises owned or possessed by another because protection against illegal search and seizure is personal to the injured owner or possessor. His warrantless arrest was lawful because officers witnessed conduct indicating a felony, and any contemporaneous search was therefore permissible. The officers’ evidence was properly admitted.

A general objection that the jury charge failed to state the applicable law was insufficient because exceptions must be specific. The charge adequately addressed transportation of liquor, presumed innocence, and reasonable doubt.

On rehearing, Purswell’s unsupported affidavit alleging that jurors considered his failure to testify did not establish misconduct. Because evidence heard on the new-trial motion was absent from the appellate record, the trial court’s ruling was presumed justified. The conviction was affirmed, and rehearing was denied.

Firefly Aerospace shares fell nearly 21% after its Alpha Flight 7 rocket exploded during a first-stage test in Briggs, Texas. No personnel were injured, and other facilities were unaffected. The company is assessing damage to the test stand. Firefly shares have declined more than 50% since last month’s Nasdaq debut.

Enron evolved from a debt-burdened pipeline company into a dominant energy trader after Ken Lay backed Jeff Skilling’s Gas Bank model. Skilling expanded trading into electricity, commodities, broadband, and other markets while promoting aggressive hiring, rapid profits, mark-to-market accounting, large bonuses, and forced employee rankings.

The company’s success produced a competitive, short-term culture that weakened teamwork and prioritized deals over customers, employees, and long-term assets. Costly international projects, failed water and telecommunications ventures, California energy-crisis criticism, accounting concerns, and the technology downturn damaged investor confidence.

Enron’s stock fell sharply in 2001, and Skilling resigned after six months as CEO, citing personal priorities. Lay returned, acknowledged morale problems, and said Enron would focus innovation more closely on its core business.

Goals are reportedly more likely during key five-minute periods: at the beginning of each half, after goals, penalty failures, serious fouls or dangerous play, before halftime, near full time, and around extra time. Psychological factors include excitement, poor preparation, complacency, anger, urgency, and defensive retreat. Coaches should prepare players to exploit or guard against these periods, especially preventing emotional letdowns, overconfidence, or discouragement after goals.

Q3 2025 commentary suggests municipal credit quality may begin weakening amid a government shutdown, slowing job growth, and mixed inflation, despite municipal bonds’ reputation as a safe, flight-to-quality asset. The Fed cut short-term rates in September, while many municipalities received upgrades for stronger reserves. The passage also profiles Cumberland Advisors co-founder David Kotok and lists several investment articles and municipal bond ETFs.

On October 29, 2001, Enron’s shares fell to multiyear lows after Moody’s downgraded its senior unsecured debt from Baa1 to Baa2, two levels above junk, and warned of further cuts. The company sought $1 billion to $2 billion in additional bank financing after drawing about $3.3 billion from existing credit lines to repay commercial paper. Analysts expected lenders to demand higher rates, collateral and stricter repayment terms.

Investor confidence had deteriorated following write-downs, a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity, disclosures involving partnerships managed by former CFO Andrew Fastow, and an SEC inquiry. European energy companies restricted dealings with Enron over credit concerns, potentially reducing market liquidity. Commentary questioned Enron’s asset-light trading strategy, financial transparency and ability to retain employees. Multiple shareholder lawsuits alleged conflicts of interest and losses related to partnership transactions involving broadband, water and other investments.

Separately, Moody’s reported worsening U.S. corporate credit quality, with downgrade reviews substantially outnumbering upgrade reviews.

Treetops, near Keynsham town centre, accommodates elderly people with dementia in three family-sized units. It offers individual named-carer support, family involvement, communal spaces and activities. Prospective residents should verify suitability and provided information.

The Arctic is an interconnected environmental, geopolitical, economic, and sociocultural system undergoing rapid change. Decisions in one area can create cascading effects across others, as illustrated by port expansion, shipping, resource development, and military activity. Traditional linear and discipline-specific approaches may overlook these interdependencies and produce unintended consequences.

Systems thinking offers a holistic educational framework that examines relationships, feedback loops, long-term patterns, underlying structures, and leverage points where targeted interventions can generate significant change. Applied to Arctic security education, it integrates fields such as governance, climate science, economics, military strategy, international relations, and Indigenous knowledge. It also supports anticipatory rather than reactive decision-making and consideration of second- and third-order consequences.

The proposed Systems Thinking Education Model has three components: core systems-thinking principles, educational leverage points, and structured learning and assessment strategies. Its leverage points include shifting mental models, improving information sharing, adapting policy and governance, encouraging behavioral and operational change, and responsibly applying emerging technologies. Intended competencies include interdisciplinary analysis, strategic foresight, adaptability, communication, and sustainable policy development.

Recommended instructional methods include concept mapping, simulations, wargaming, stakeholder role-playing, interactive case studies, and scenario-based problem-solving. Assessments should emphasize real-world application, reflective analysis, metacognition, and competency-based measures rather than knowledge retention alone.

The model is suited to online graduate education through asynchronous scenarios, digital simulations, multimedia cases, discussion forums, collaborative projects, and reflective exercises. Integrating systems thinking into Arctic security curricula can help professionals assess trade-offs, anticipate unintended effects, collaborate across sectors, and develop adaptive, sustainable responses to evolving regional challenges.

Newcomers to Canada can improve job-search success by networking and beginning their search before arrival. They should use job sites, attend free career workshops, pursue internships or volunteer roles, verify whether their credentials need updating, and strengthen English or French proficiency and business communication skills. Preparation can help candidates navigate an unfamiliar labour market and identify potential career paths.

The disclosure concerns improved autonomous radio-resource selection and sensing for sidelink transmissions, particularly LTE ProSe device-to-device and V2X communications. It reviews LTE architecture, resource structures, carrier aggregation, protocol layers, scheduling, ProSe communication, sidelink allocation Modes 1 and 2, and vehicular services involving periodic CAM and event-triggered DENM messages.

For autonomous Mode 2 allocation, devices sense scheduling assignments, resource reservations, and optionally received signal energy to predict usable future resources. Because sidelink devices operate half-duplex, they cannot sense while transmitting, creating incomplete information for certain future subframes.

The proposed procedure defines a sensing window before data arrival and a transmission window in which data must be sent. Candidate resources are divided into primary subframes, for which all corresponding sensing opportunities were used, and secondary subframes, for which sensing information is incomplete because the device transmitted during corresponding sensing subframes. Resources in primary subframes are preferred. Candidates within each category may be ranked separately using transmission delay and predicted energy, favoring shorter delays and lower energy. Energy prediction may use sensing subframes related through supported transmission periodicities, such as 100–1000 ms intervals.

If suitable unreserved resources are unavailable, a preemption procedure may select reserved resources based on factors such as received energy or priority. The approach can also apply to scheduling-assignment resources. A scheduling assignment may indicate resources reserved for future scheduling assignments, data transmissions, or both. The disclosed techniques may be implemented as transmitting devices, methods, systems, or computer programs.

Trump described US-Canada trade problems as less severe than those with Mexico and favored tweaks over an overhaul, sending USD/CAD to 1.3060 despite falling oil prices. Markets awaited Yellen’s testimony after US inflation expectations rose to 3%. Upcoming events included forecast increases in Chinese CPI and PPI and a Kuroda speech amid speculation about yield-curve control.

The creed urges soccer players to remain aware of the ball, teammates, opponents, and tactical options; communicate intelligently; report injuries; play hard without reckless fouls; support teammates; avoid retaliation and dissent; follow the referee’s whistle and game laws; learn from mistakes; prioritize team positioning and passing; and demonstrate fair play and sportsmanship on and off the field.

The course examines highly porous cellular materials, typically containing less than 30% solid, including honeycombs, foams, lattices, bone, tissue-engineering scaffolds, wood, bamboo, cork, plant tissues, and natural sandwich structures. It covers processing, structure, deformation, failure, mechanical modeling, material selection, and applications such as lightweight panels, energy absorption, thermal insulation, catalysts, medical implants, and tissue regeneration.

Honeycombs have two-dimensional prismatic cells, while foams have three-dimensional polyhedral cells that may be open or closed. Their properties depend on factors including solid volume fraction, cell geometry, and anisotropy. Structural analysis will be used to estimate stiffness, strength, fracture toughness, and other bulk properties. Natural examples include trabecular bone, wood, cork, palm stems, bamboo, leaves, skulls, plant stems, and animal quills, many of which use density gradients, sandwich arrangements, or cellular cores for mechanical efficiency.

Medical topics include osteoporosis-related reductions in bone density and strength, porous metal coatings for orthopedic implants, and scaffold mechanics. Studies described include cell-induced scaffold deformation, cell attachment in relation to surface area, and migration speed in relation to scaffold stiffness.

Students complete open-ended projects in pairs on cellular materials. Past projects addressed negative-Poisson-ratio honeycombs, osteoporosis, elephant-skull vibration, tissue-engineering scaffolds, and food foams.

Honeycombs can be produced through sheet expansion, corrugation, ceramic extrusion, casting, rapid prototyping, laser-based methods, or carbonized biological templates. Polymer foams are made by introducing and stabilizing gas bubbles through stirring or physical and chemical blowing agents; hollow spheres can also be bonded into syntactic foams. Metal-foam processes include stirring gas into molten aluminum, using titanium hydride, replicating polymer foams, vapor deposition, entrapped-gas expansion, bonding hollow spheres, and removing fugitive phases such as salt.

Gibson also outlines her education and career: civil engineering studies in Toronto, a Cambridge doctorate on cellular solids, work in Calgary’s oil industry, academic positions at the University of British Columbia and MIT, and a transition from civil engineering to materials as her research became more biomedical.

Several Supreme Court justices questioned whether Delaware procedures limiting medical malpractice lawsuits should apply in federal court. Justices Elena Kagan, Ketanji Brown Jackson, and Sonia Sotomayor argued that requirements such as filing an affidavit conflict with federal rules governing notice pleading, commencement of actions, and deadlines for answers. Defendants’ lawyer Frederick Yarger urged the court not to reject the entire state statute because portions might conflict with federal rules. Justice Neil Gorsuch questioned whether selectively applying its provisions would improperly rewrite Delaware law. Because Chief Justice John Roberts and Justices Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito said little, the court’s ultimate position remains unclear, though several justices appear likely to reject Delaware’s procedures.

The team must battle harder around the net, test the opposing goalie with elevated shots, and rebound after a disappointing loss. After two days to regroup and practice, they are ready and focused on scoring first.

Bank of Canada senior deputy governor Carolyn Wilkins expects Canada’s household debt-to-disposable-income ratio to stabilize gradually as credit growth slows and labour income rises. The ratio dipped slightly to 170.4 per cent in late 2017 after decades of growth. Wilkins noted debt financed assets such as housing, increasing net worth. The central bank considers household debt a major concern when raising interest rates, with governor Stephen Poloz estimating indebted households are 50 per cent more sensitive to rate changes.

Blair’s $250,000 transportation bond failed despite receiving 58.76% approval, short of the required 60%. The proposal would have purchased three buses. Municipal races favored John Womack, Jon Kidwell and Roberta Ellis, while school board results were reported across Caddo, Comanche and Cotton counties.

The study evaluates the usability of eight popular e-business websites operating in Saudi Arabia, an emerging online market. Sixty-five students trained in user-interface evaluation were divided into two groups examining four retail and four reservation websites. After 30-minute interactions, participants completed a questionnaire covering navigation, design, and content.

Ratings were generally positive, and results from both groups largely converged. However, participants identified weaknesses in internal and within-page navigation, sitemap availability, disappearing menus, orphan pages, Arabic-English interface consistency, layout simplicity, font-size consistency, icon labeling, contact information, content ordering, and display of the last update date. Reliability testing produced Cronbach’s alpha values of 0.66 for the retail group and 0.79 for the reservation group.

The study recommends user-centered and participatory design, task analysis, ethnographic research, and improved content development to strengthen customer engagement and trust. Its small sample and limited selection of websites restrict generalizability. Further qualitative and long-term quantitative studies are proposed to examine user feedback and the effect of usability improvements on customer behavior.

DAWN-PLASMA was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 multicenter trial evaluating convalescent plasma plus standard supportive care versus standard care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Participants were allocated 2:1 through a computerized system, while the trial statistician remained blinded until database lock. The study followed the Declaration of Helsinki, ICH Good Clinical Practice guidelines, ethics committee approvals, and informed-consent requirements.

The trial hypothesized that early administration of a high volume of plasma with high neutralizing-antibody titers would reduce mechanical ventilation. The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary and exploratory endpoints included clinical status, sustained improvement or live discharge, mechanical ventilation or death, thromboembolism, transfusion reactions, safety, quality of life, laboratory and vital-sign assessments, viral PCR, antibody measurements, and associations between antibody titers and clinical outcomes.

Eligible adults had confirmed or clinically supported SARS-CoV-2 infection and specified respiratory or imaging findings. Key exclusions included existing invasive or non-invasive mechanical ventilation, unacceptable safety risks, severe plasma allergy, treatment restrictions excluding ventilation or intubation, and recent anti-CD20 therapy.

Plasma recipients received 800–1000 mL in four units, beginning within 12 hours after randomization, with the second two-unit dose 24–36 hours later. Plasma titers below 1/160 were prohibited. Standard care followed evolving national and international guidance, with no restrictions on other therapies.

Five participants withdrew consent and one was a screen failure before intervention; all six were replaced. No participants were lost to follow-up after intervention. Sponsor monitoring assessed protocol adherence, GCP compliance, and data quality. Data were recorded in REDCap, laboratories underwent quality evaluation, and no quality audits or predefined quality tolerance limits were used.

Former Bengals starter Andy Dalton has been suggested as a possible replacement for struggling quarterback Jake Browning, who has 506 passing yards, three touchdowns and five interceptions in three games while filling in for Joe Burrow. Dalton played under Zac Taylor in 2019, is signed with Carolina through 2026 and would cost Cincinnati about $3 million for the remainder of his contract.

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court affirmed that Act 109 is constitutional and enforceable for nonsectarian nonpublic schools. It held that Lemon v. Kurtzman invalidated the Act only as applied to sectarian schools because public aid to them created excessive government-religion entanglement. The Act’s severability clause and Pennsylvania’s policy favoring severability permitted its continued application to nonsectarian schools, consistent with its purpose of supporting secular education. Subsequent legislation did not impliedly repeal Act 109 because it neither covered the Act’s entire subject matter nor irreconcilably conflicted with it. Finally, determining whether a school is sectarian does not create excessive entanglement, as the inquiry requires no extensive or continuing relationship with religious institutions. Justice Eagen dissented.

In a May 1980 interview, Ronald Reagan questioned President Carter’s response to the failed Iran hostage rescue mission. He described possible Soviet influence in Iran as a serious threat to the Middle East, the United States, and its allies, while noting uncertainty about Ayatollah Khomeini’s attitude toward Moscow. Accepting the Republican presidential nomination on July 17, Reagan made national security his highest priority and argued that lasting peace requires American strength, preparedness, good-faith negotiation, and resistance to forces threatening freedom. In a later address to veterans, he said those experienced in war understand that peace cannot be preserved through weakness. He warned that America’s defense margin was disappearing and rejected claims that military preparedness reflected militancy, quoting Will Rogers: “I’ve never seen anyone insult Jack Dempsey.”

Effective basketball press breaks rely on preparation, teamwork, spacing, controlled tempo, and exploiting the press’s weaknesses. All five players should participate rather than relying on one guard. The offense should look long first, short second, and middle third; advance with crisp passes; create leads; meet passes in a triple-threat stance; use the dribble sparingly; and attack outnumbered situations such as 2-on-1 and 3-on-2 opportunities. Reversal passes after double teams can create a 4-on-3 advantage, while a trailer maintains defensive balance.

Players should avoid sideline trap zones, one-handed, lob, bounce, telegraphed, or off-the-dribble passes. They should not pick up the dribble prematurely or force risky passes. Good shots, offensive rebounding, and immediate flow into early offense are emphasized.

Press breaks should use defined roles and flexible formations, and should be run consistently after made shots or free throws to prevent surprise. Instruction should follow a whole-part-whole progression: demonstrate responsibilities, walk through reads and counters, practice component drills, and finish with live, game-speed work against strong defense. Coaches should demand correct spacing, timing, footwork, and execution.

Objectives include developing poise, rapid controlled ball advancement, proper outlet decisions, responses to double teams, success in numerical advantages, offensive rebounding, and transition into early offense. Teams should scout defensive tactics, remain alert to adjustments, and make press-break practice an integral part of every session.

The study demonstrates coherent control of three nearest-neighbor spin-1/2 ^15N nuclei coupled to negatively charged boron vacancies in isotopically enriched hBN. Pulsed electron-nuclear double resonance selectively addresses four multi-nuclear hyperfine states and resolves three transitions whose inequivalent, magnetic-field-dependent energies arise from hyperfine-mediated electron–nuclear spin mixing. Fitted first-neighbor hyperfine tensor eigenvalues are −61.3, −121.6, and −63.7 MHz.

The same mixing enhances the nuclear g-factor, producing nuclear Rabi frequencies approximately 116 times greater than for isolated ^15N spins. Nuclear resonance linewidths reach 1.2 MHz, and Rabi coherence exceeds 10 μs, roughly two orders of magnitude longer than electron-spin coherence. Optical pumping, however, depolarizes the nuclei within 1 μs; this relaxation is tentatively attributed to the optically excited triplet state.

These results establish strongly coupled ^15N nuclei near boron vacancies as controllable quantum resources with rapid manipulation, spectral selectivity, and comparatively long coherence. Their properties, combined with hBN’s two-dimensional structure and integration compatibility, support potential applications in quantum sensing, memories, and nanoscale quantum devices.

Tesla’s unaudited Form 10-Q covers the quarter ended March 31, 2018. The company operates automotive and energy generation and storage segments.

First-quarter revenue rose to $3.41 billion from $2.70 billion a year earlier, while gross profit declined to $456.5 million from $667.9 million. Operating loss widened to $597.0 million, and net loss attributable to common stockholders increased to $709.6 million, or $4.19 per share, from $330.3 million, or $2.04 per share.

At March 31, 2018, Tesla reported $27.27 billion in assets, $21.55 billion in liabilities and $4.45 billion in stockholders’ equity. Cash and cash equivalents were $2.67 billion, inventory was $2.57 billion, and customer deposits were $984.8 million. Total debt principal was $10.47 billion, including $1.76 billion classified as current. Tesla stated it complied with all financial debt covenants.

Operating activities used $398.4 million in cash, investing activities used $728.6 million, and financing activities provided $371.7 million. Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash declined by $745.3 million to $3.22 billion.

Tesla adopted the ASC 606 revenue standard on January 1, 2018. The adoption reduced opening accumulated deficit by $623.2 million and changed certain vehicle sales with resale value guarantees from lease accounting to sales with rights of return. For the quarter, adoption increased reported automotive sales revenue by $299.0 million, reduced automotive leasing revenue by $164.9 million and reduced net loss by $36.3 million.

In February 2018, Tesla issued $546.1 million of automotive asset-backed notes and repaid $453.6 million under warehouse agreements. Stockholders approved a 20.3 million-option CEO performance award tied to market capitalization, revenue and adjusted EBITDA milestones. Tesla recorded $6.7 million of related stock-based compensation during the quarter.

Socket 940 uses an LCP UL 94 V-0 black base and natural or ivory cover. Cover thickness is limited to 1.17 mm and flatness to under 0.25 mm before and after reflow and testing. A removable, non-outgassing, residue-free overlay supports vacuum pick-and-place. Molded or applied markings identify the socket, lever positions, pin A01 orientation, UL approval, and lot traceability.

Contacts use high-strength copper alloy with at least 1.27 µm nickel plating and 0.76 µm gold on mating areas; lubricants are prohibited there. SMT attachment uses 0.76 mm tin-lead solder balls on 0.64 mm PCB pads, with a solder barrier and maximum 0.20 mm ball-field coplanarity.

A stainless-steel lever provides toolless actuation. Open-position insertion and extraction forces must not exceed 2 kgf; closed-position extraction force is at least 0.013 kgf per pin. Lever force is below 3.6 kgf, pin displacement below 1.0 mm, and durability is required through 50 cycles. Components must be free of functional or visible defects.

Each contact is rated for 1.5 A with under 30°C temperature rise. Initial and final LLCR must not exceed 25 mΩ per contact. Electrical limits include under 4 nH self-inductance, 3 nH ±10% loop inductance, under 1 pF capacitance, 100 Ω ±10% differential impedance, under 10 ps propagation skew plus measurement error, at least 650 Vac dielectric withstand, and at least 1000 MΩ insulation resistance.

North Carolina coach Bill Belichick accepted responsibility after a 38–10 loss to Clemson, citing defensive big plays, penalties and poor third-down situations. Clemson passed for 399 yards, while UNC managed 213 passing yards and converted 2 of 11 third downs. Belichick nevertheless praised his team’s effort and vowed continued improvement.

The 2018 ebook edition of the 1906 Foreign Relations of the United States preserves the printed volume’s content while offering search, bookmarking, offline access, and document-based citation. In his annual message, the President noted unprecedented prosperity and praised Congress but urged completion of pending legislation. He recommended prohibiting corporate political contributions and granting the federal government a limited right to appeal legal rulings in criminal cases without overturning acquittals on their merits. He argued that such appeals would resolve conflicting lower-court decisions and strengthen enforcement against wrongdoing by wealthy individuals and corporations while protecting workers’ legal rights.

Tesla’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2016 reported quarterly revenue of $1.27 billion, gross profit of $274.8 million, and a net loss of $293.2 million. Six-month revenue was $2.42 billion, with a $575.5 million net loss. At quarter-end, Tesla held $3.25 billion in cash, $11.87 billion in assets, and $9.31 billion in liabilities.

Tesla produced 18,345 vehicles in the second quarter and planned approximately 50,000 deliveries during the second half of 2016. It targeted Model 3 volume production in late 2017 and total annual vehicle production of 500,000 in 2018. Planned 2016 capital expenditures were approximately $2.25 billion.

A May 2016 stock offering generated approximately $1.7 billion. Customer deposits rose to $679.8 million, primarily due to Model 3 deposits. Tesla had incurred $430.7 million in Gigafactory costs and expected battery-cell production there to begin in the fourth quarter of 2016.

On July 31, 2016, Tesla agreed to acquire SolarCity through an exchange of 0.110 Tesla shares for each SolarCity share, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. After quarter-end, holders submitted conversion notices covering approximately $411 million of Tesla’s 2018 notes.

Russia denies responsibility for poisoning Sergei and Yulia Skripal, while Britain says evidence shows Russia continued producing and stockpiling the nerve agent Novichok. Russian officials suggested alternative blame and offered conditional cooperation. The passage urges intensified Western sanctions and legal reforms targeting assets held by Putin’s associates in Britain and America.

The ADS868xW uses independently configurable AVDD for internal circuits and DVDD for the digital interface. Proper decoupling improves PSRR: place 1µF capacitors close to supply pins and use at least 10µF near the supplies as specified. The device supports NAP and deep power-down modes for reduced consumption at lower throughput. Both require unlocking RST_PWRCTL_REG; NAP is controlled by NAP_EN and CONVST/CS, while PD powers down analog blocks but retains register contents and interface operation. Required wake-up times must elapse before new conversions.

PCB guidance includes separating analog and digital sections, using clean bypassed supplies, avoiding vias between pins and bypass capacitors, and connecting grounds through short, low-impedance paths. REFCAP requires 1µF and 10µF capacitors, with ESR below 0.2Ω for the 10µF capacitor; REFIO requires at least 4.7µF when using the internal reference.

TI provides documentation notifications and support forums, warns that ESD can damage the device, and supplies resources “as is.” Revision A changed ADS8685W and ADS8689W status from Advance Information to Production Data. Mechanical and ordering information may change without notice.

Clark County schools are determining how to use new state weighted funding for low-performing students who are learning English or living in poverty and do not attend schools receiving Zoom or Victory funds. Garside Junior High will receive more than $450,000 for 378 eligible students, potentially expanding tutoring and technology access. Clark County received over $34 million of Nevada’s $36 million allocation. Spending will be tracked and analyzed for its effect on student achievement.

Hyundai and Kia installed a vehicle-to-everything system along 14 kilometers of road in Hwaseong to support autonomous-driving research. The system enables real-time communication among vehicles, roads, traffic signals and pedestrians using relay stations and closed-circuit TVs. The companies will collect data through year-end to improve the system and prepare it for a state infrastructure project planned for highways in 2020.

Since becoming Speedy’s chief executive in 2015 after a profit warning, Russell Down has led a significant turnaround. He addressed unreliable asset data, declining revenue from smaller customers, excessive operating costs and equipment shortages caused by centralised testing and repairs. His strategy emphasised customer service, staff engagement, disciplined management, cost control and improved asset availability and utilisation.

For the six months to September, profits rose 58.8% to £10.8 million, while net debt fell and Return on Capital Employed improved. Speedy also resumed acquisitions, buying Prolift Access Limited and Platform Sales & Hire Limited to expand its powered-access fleet, increase product reach and better meet customer demand. With supportive banking partners, the company aims to deliver sustainable profitable growth.

Mastitis, the dairy industry’s costliest disease, causes mammary tissue damage, reduced milk production and treatment costs exceeding $400 per clinical case. Although antibiotics kill bacteria, they do not repair damaged tissue. Cornell researchers found that secretions from bovine mammary stem cells may promote tissue healing, blood vessel formation and cell migration, protect epithelial cells from bacterial toxins, and directly kill bacteria. The secretions were particularly effective against toxins from gram-negative bacteria, potentially complementing approved treatments that work better against gram-positive bacteria. Researchers plan to test the stem cell secretome in cows with mastitis.

Caitlin Bassett says the build-up to Sunshine Coast Lightning’s Super Netball grand final against Greater Western Sydney is unlike anything in her career. Playing her first national grand final, she has drawn on experienced teammates Geva Mentor and Laura Langman. Mentor has prepared to defend the Giants’ tall shooters, including 196cm Kristina Brice, by training against 215cm Queensland men’s player Junior Levi.

The study proposes periodically modulated coupled Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains for braiding topological edge-state pairs. Time-dependent interchain symmetry produces branch switching and protects sufficiently slow adiabatic evolution across transient gap closings, while inversion symmetry conserves parity. In a double-chain system, two edge-state pairs undergo Abelian exchange, enabling a particle at one chain end to transfer between the two ends of the other chain with a ratio controlled by an accumulated dynamical phase.

Extending to three coupled chains yields three edge-state branches with cyclic swapping and non-Abelian braiding. Different braid sequences produce different recipient chains, demonstrating sequence-dependent topological transport. For two identical bosons and a 50:50 transfer ratio, Hong-Ou-Mandel interference generates high-fidelity spatial NOON states whose chain location depends on the braid order. Photonic waveguide arrays are identified as a potential experimental platform.

The President submits the February 14, 1893 treaty annexing Hawaii for Senate ratification. He states that the treaty leaves detailed annexation issues for later settlement by the United States. He denies U.S. involvement in overthrowing the monarchy, attributes the crisis to Queen Liliuokalani’s policies and weak government, and argues that restoring her would be harmful. Of the remaining options—a U.S. protectorate or complete annexation—he favors annexation as best for Hawaiian and American interests and as a safeguard against control by another power. He urges prompt approval to preserve order under existing laws until Congress establishes a permanent government that protects the rights of natives, residents, citizens, and foreigners.

A police pursuit in City Heights ended after a wanted shooting suspect crashed through fences at Central Elementary School and a fire station. The armed suspect fled on foot but was arrested a block away.

A corner kick restarts play when a defender sends the whole ball over their own end line. Because it provides a set-play opportunity near goal, coaches should teach young players Law 17, correct technique, designated roles, and multiple kicking options.

Players should understand that the entire ball must cross the line, the kick is taken from the nearest corner arc, defenders remain at least 10 yards away, the corner flag cannot be removed, and the kicker cannot touch the ball again until another player does. Coaches should demonstrate proper ball placement, a roughly 45-degree run-up, and an instep drive into the field, then let every player practice.

A basic play uses three roles: the corner taker passes to a receiver five yards inside the field; a cover player guards against a miskick going out. The receiver turns toward goal while the other two players move deeper for a possible pass. Players should rotate through all roles.

Coaches should demonstrate and practice right- and left-footed kicks from both corners, later assigning players to positions and adding passive, then active, defenders. Additional passing options, offside instruction, and longer directed lofted kicks may be introduced as players improve. During games, officials indicate the correct corner, and the taker must wait until the referee is ready.

The passage argues that *Landor v. Louisiana Department of Corrections and Public Safety* challenges common narratives portraying Supreme Court religious-freedom cases as primarily partisan, majoritarian, and culture-war driven. Damon Landor, a Rastafarian prisoner, was forcibly shaved despite legal protections for his religious practice. He seeks monetary damages under RLUIPA, but a lower court ruled that the statute does not authorize them. The author contends that denying damages would leave prisoners with little effective relief and undermine the law.

More broadly, the passage notes that many significant religious-liberty rulings have been unanimous or nearly unanimous and have protected diverse minority faiths. It argues that most religious-freedom disputes concern practical accommodations rather than contentious social issues, and concludes that religious liberty is a foundational right belonging to all people.

U.S. stocks fell sharply Monday as Facebook’s 7.1 percent plunge over reports of improper access to more than 50 million users’ data triggered a broader technology selloff and privacy concerns. The Nasdaq dropped 2.09 percent, while the S&P 500 and Dow declined 1.44 percent and 1.23 percent, respectively. All major S&P sectors fell amid trade-war concerns, political uncertainty and anticipation of a likely Federal Reserve interest-rate increase. Other FAANG stocks also declined, while market volatility rose substantially.

The passage lists major late-1945 Truman administration statements on China, national defense, and European refugees, and describes postwar changes in the Department of State. Edward R. Stettinius Jr. resigned as Secretary of State and became U.S. representative to the United Nations; James F. Byrnes succeeded him. Joseph C. Grew resigned as Under Secretary and was replaced by Dean G. Acheson. Patrick J. Hurley resigned as Ambassador to China, and George C. Marshall was appointed presidential envoy there. Cordell Hull received the Nobel Peace Prize.

The Department recruited Foreign Service officers from the armed forces and assumed additional responsibilities. Executive Order 9608 transferred international information functions from the Office of War Information and Office of Inter-American Affairs to State. Executive Order 9621 abolished the Office of Strategic Services, transferring its research and analysis functions to State and remaining functions to the War Department. Truman directed State to lead development of a coordinated federal foreign-intelligence program.

A retrospective study analyzed 671 traumatic brain injury patients treated at a republic hospital from July 2017 to December 2018 to identify commonly reported risk factors. The sample included 459 men and 212 women, with a mean age of 46.0 years; 78.1% lived in cities and 21.9% in villages. Domestic accidents were the most frequent cause overall (43.8%) and for both sexes, followed by alcohol-related injury (20.7%), motor vehicle injury (16.5%), and criminal injury (11.2%).

Men experienced TBI at a younger mean age than women and had longer hospitalizations. Older age was directly correlated with hospitalization duration. The study reported increased TBI risk among village residents, while city residents affected by TBI were older. Most patients received conservative therapy; 198 required surgical treatment, most commonly wound debridement. The authors concluded that gender, age, residence, and injury cause were associated with TBI patterns and outcomes. The absence of a control group was identified as a limitation.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI), developed by Welles Wilder in 1978, is an oscillator ranging from 0 to 100 that measures average gains relative to average losses over a selected period. It is primarily used to identify overbought and oversold conditions, with common thresholds of 70 and 30.

The article’s backtests indicate that RSI works best as a mean-reversion indicator on stocks and stock indices, particularly with daily bars, short lookback periods of two to six days, and additional filters or indicators. More extreme thresholds, such as 15 and 85, suit shorter lookbacks. RSI generally performs less effectively on other assets, intraday data, forex, and commodity-related stocks.

A two-day S&P 500 strategy buying below 15 and selling above 85 achieved results slightly below buy-and-hold through November 2020 while spending 42% of the time invested and producing lower drawdown. A ten-day strategy performed worse. A QQQ backtest generated about 300 trades, a 0.82% average gain, a 71% win rate, and a 23% maximum drawdown. These tests excluded some trading costs where noted.

Combining 30-day and two-day RSI reduced market exposure but did not improve the tested S&P 500 strategy. Divergences are described as difficult to quantify and mainly identifiable in hindsight. RSI settings and thresholds should be backtested for each market, and risk management and confirmation tools are recommended. Cutler’s RSI uses a simple moving average instead of Wilder’s smoothed average, while Connors RSI combines three components.

Sodium cumenesulfonate is a water-soluble hydrotrope available in powder and liquid forms. It improves organic-matter solubility, ingredient compatibility, cloud point, and viscosity in aqueous formulations. Applications include detergents, cleaners, drilling and stimulation fluids, anti-caking and coupling agents, metal processing, oilfields, and hydrogen sulfide scavengers. Market demand is expected to benefit from industrialization and household detergent use in emerging economies, while volatile raw-material costs, declining research activity, and health risks from heavy exposure may hinder growth. Liquid sodium cumenesulfonate held a major market share in 2015 and was expected to remain dominant. Household applications also led in 2015, while industrial and institutional uses were projected to grow moderately.

Frost Brown Todd and Gibbons will merge in January as FBT Gibbons, forming an 800-lawyer firm with 25 offices and expanding Frost Brown Todd into New York and New Jersey. Robert Sartin will serve as chairman, while Adam Hall and Peter Torcicollo will be co-managing partners. Leaders will initially prioritize integration but may pursue further expansion. The firms reported revenues of $336.5 million and $115 million, respectively.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell architecture introduces finer-grained clock, power, and voltage-rail gating, including full memory clock-tree gating and separate controls for GPU cores and memory. Clock frequencies can adjust 1,000 times faster than previous architectures, while the deepest sleep state is entered 10 times faster than with Ada. NVIDIA reports power savings of up to 50% in a small-language-model inference example.

DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three frames per traditionally rendered frame. Its AI model is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and works with enhanced GPU-based frame pacing. Transformer models replace prior CNN-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, providing greater temporal stability, reduced ghosting, improved motion detail, and better handling of complex lighting.

Blackwell also supports developer-created neural shaders through Tensor Core access from graphics shaders using the Cooperative Vectors API for DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Applications include neural materials, neural texture compression, radiance caching, subsurface scattering for skin, and generative-AI face rendering. Neural Texture Compression reduced material memory in one demonstration from 1,110 MB to 333 MB, while Neural Radiance Cache approximates multi-bounce indirect lighting from partially traced rays.

The flagship GB202 GPU contains 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, and 768 Tensor cores, and powers the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 contains 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, and 10,752 CUDA cores for the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 contains 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, and 6,400 CUDA cores for the RTX 5070. NVIDIA states that specifications may change and disclaims warranties and liability beyond its sales terms.

Stephen Hawking, the renowned theoretical physicist, died after living with ALS for more than 50 years. Despite severe paralysis and reliance on an electronic voice synthesizer, he continued researching a unified theory reconciling relativity and quantum mechanics. His international bestseller “A Brief History of Time” and sequel “The Universe in a Nutshell” made complex cosmological ideas accessible. Hawking became a widely recognized scientific celebrity through television appearances and the film “The Theory of Everything.” His work, public profile and longevity inspired enthusiasm for science and demonstrated that severe disabilities need not prevent achievement.

Synaptics announced plans to mass-produce Clear ID, an optical fingerprint sensor embedded beneath bezel-less smartphone displays. The company claims it is twice as fast as 3D facial recognition, works with one touch, and enables unlocking from any angle. Synaptics argues that consumers prefer front-facing fingerprint authentication, though its market arrival remains uncertain.

Bemidji improved to 14-6 with a 77-45 win over Thief River Falls, leading 45-25 at halftime. Caden Rolfes scored 18 points, Linaes Whiting 17, Caleb Carlson 14 and Jeremy Beberg 10. Coach Travis Peterson praised the team’s sustained effort ahead of the section tournament.

After Kamehameha III’s death in 1855, his successor opposed a treaty providing increased annuities and Hawaiian admission as a U.S. state, causing it to fail. A reciprocity treaty concluded that year also failed Senate ratification. Civil War concerns later delayed renewed negotiations, though U.S. diplomatic representation was elevated in 1863. In 1867, U.S. and Hawaiian representatives concluded another reciprocity treaty. Secretary Seward authorized confidential discussions of annexation and stated that annexation should take precedence if it conflicted with reciprocity. Hawaiian concerns about the presence and alleged political interference of the USS *Lackawanna* delayed consideration until the ship departed. Hawaii ratified the treaty on July 30, 1867, but the U.S. Senate rejected it on June 1, 1870.

Florida State University President John Thrasher appointed a 15-member committee to review policies on campus names, statues and other markers amid national debates over Confederate symbols. Chief Diversity Officer Renisha Gibbs will chair the panel, which will seek community input and hold public meetings. The review follows calls to remove honors for Francis Eppes, whom activists describe as a slave owner and Confederate supporter.

The speaker pledges to preserve the Constitution and Union, restore harmony among the states, serve only one term, and uphold majority rule. He argues that territorial slavery should be decided through popular sovereignty, free voting, and Supreme Court judgment, while slavery within existing states remains under state authority. He urges an end to sectional agitation, warning that it threatens peace, security, prosperity, and the Union.

He emphasizes preventing government corruption, reducing the Treasury surplus through constitutionally authorized purposes such as debt repayment and naval expansion, limiting revenue to necessary expenses, and avoiding favoritism in tariffs. Public lands should primarily remain available to actual settlers at moderate prices, including immigrants who, once citizens, deserve equality with native-born citizens.

Advocating strict construction of federal powers, he nevertheless supports a military road to defend California and Pacific territories. In foreign affairs, he favors peace, commerce, friendship, noninterference, avoidance of entangling alliances, and reciprocal justice. Territorial expansion, he maintains, should occur only through purchase, voluntary union, or other means consistent with justice and honor.

Apple filed a Form 8-K reporting a February 16, 2016 underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs, Deutsche Bank Securities, J.P. Morgan Securities, and Merrill Lynch. Apple agreed to issue nine series of senior unsecured notes: two $500 million floating-rate series due in 2019 and 2021, and seven fixed-rate series totaling $11 billion, bearing interest from 1.300% to 4.650% and maturing between 2018 and 2046. Floating-rate interest is payable quarterly, while fixed-rate interest is payable semiannually. The notes were issued under Apple’s April 29, 2013 indenture and registration statement. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, note forms, legal opinion, earnings-to-fixed-charges computation, and related consent. CFO Luca Maestri signed the report on February 23, 2016.

Apple filed a Form 8-K on January 27, 2022, reporting financial results for its first fiscal quarter ended December 25, 2021. The filing includes the related press release as Exhibit 99.1 and Inline XBRL as Exhibit 104. CFO Luca Maestri signed the report.

A federal government shutdown has left essential aviation employees, including air traffic controllers and TSA agents, working without pay while many support staff are furloughed. Workers say air travel remains safe, but reduced staffing, financial stress, and halted projects may slow repairs and cause more delays and cancellations as the shutdown continues.

Employees also fear possible firings, weakened union protections, and consequences for necessary absences. Transportation officials say safety-critical positions are exempt from workforce reductions and that the FAA will reduce traffic when staffing is constrained. Union representatives reject organized sick-outs but warn some workers may be unable to afford commuting without pay.

Nearly 3,000 participants are expected for the 23rd BMO Okanagan Marathon in Kelowna. Events based at City Park include Saturday’s timed 5 km, kids’ activities and 1 km run, plus Sunday’s marathon, half marathon and 10 km races. The flat, fast marathon course follows Okanagan Lake and qualifies runners for Boston. New features include timing for the 5 km and an adult beverage garden. The event supports the Sunshine Foundation of Canada, involves more than 300 volunteers, and offers walk-up registration and package pickup from Oct. 6 to 8.

Modular containers require stable, documented APIs covering parameters, service calls, and exposed interfaces; even subtle changes in parameter meaning can be breaking. Dockerfiles can document ports, environment defaults, and standardized metadata labels.

The sidecar pattern augments an application container with reusable functionality. The ambassador pattern brokers external communication while keeping applications connected to a local interface. Ambassadors can route requests to sharded storage, discover services across environments, or split traffic for experiments. The adapter pattern converts heterogeneous application interfaces into standardized ones for monitoring, logging, and health checks. Examples include Prometheus exporters, Fluentd log normalization, and MySQL health-check adapters.

Multi-node microservice architectures divide applications into independently maintained, scaled components communicating through defined APIs. They improve team autonomy, reuse, reliability, and scaling flexibility, but make architecture and debugging more complex.

Replicated load-balanced services improve availability and horizontal scalability. Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching uninitialized instances, while session tracking can consistently route users to particular replicas. Application-layer proxies can add caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination.

Sharded services divide state among machines when data exceeds one machine’s capacity. Routing may be performed through client-side ambassadors or shared routing services. Effective shard keys must group equivalent requests, and consistent hashing limits remapping when shard counts change. Replicating shards improves resilience and permits independent scaling of heavily used shards.

Scatter/gather systems distribute portions of a request across multiple workers and combine their results, reducing computation time and supporting datasets distributed across shards. Excessive parallelism introduces overhead, straggler latency, and reliability risks, so replicated shards are used to improve availability and scaling. Event-driven, temporary computation is commonly implemented through function-as-a-service, often called serverless computing.

A New York panel unanimously recommended pausing Medicaid coverage of Sarepta’s Duchenne muscular dystrophy therapy Elevidys until the FDA updates its label with safety and trial data and the state evaluates a liver-failure risk mitigation regimen. Some patients under 21 may receive case-by-case coverage based on medical necessity. It remains unclear whether the recommendation will be adopted.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the 7nm Ampere GA100 architecture, targets AI, HPC, and data analytics in data centers, edge systems, and supercomputers. It contains 108 streaming multiprocessors, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, 40 GB HBM2 memory with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, and a 40 MB L2 cache.

A100 Tensor Cores support TF32, FP16, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. Compared with V100, A100 provides up to 2.5× FP16/FP32 mixed-precision and FP64 performance, while TF32 runs up to 10× faster than V100 FP32 operations. Its 2:4 structured sparsity feature can double Tensor Core throughput, yielding up to 20× improvements for some operations. Larger caches, compute-data compression, asynchronous memory copies and barriers, cache-residency controls, and task-graph acceleration further improve efficiency and programmability.

Multi-Instance GPU technology partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU instances with dedicated compute and memory resources, predictable performance, quality of service, and fault isolation. This supports multi-tenant environments, virtual machines, containers, workload migration, and improved utilization.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s aggregate bandwidth, twice V100’s total. A100 also supports NVSwitch, PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, Magnum IO, Mellanox InfiniBand and Ethernet, enhanced error containment, hardware JPEG decoding, optical-flow acceleration, improved atomics, and five video-decode units.

CUDA 11 supports A100 features including new Tensor Core formats, sparsity, MIG, asynchronous operations, task graphs, and L2 cache controls. The DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs, NVSwitches, high-speed networking, and NVIDIA’s software stack, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS in a 6U system and supporting up to 56 isolated GPU instances.

Anjuna police registered two unnatural-death cases involving tourists Pravin Sundaram, 28, from Tamil Nadu, and Abdul, reportedly from Kerala. Both died after being taken to private hospitals. Their bodies were sent to Goa Medical College for autopsies, with viscera preserved to determine the causes; police have not ruled out drug overdose. Investigators are questioning Sundaram’s friends and tracing the person who brought Abdul to hospital. Siolim MLA called for outdoor music parties and drug-related activities to be stopped.

Mothers and their children with Down’s syndrome created a Carpool Karaoke-style video for World Down Syndrome Day to challenge perceptions. Featuring Christina Perri’s “A Thousand Years” with Makaton signing, it surpassed 600,000 views and received support from Perri and James Corden.

The speaker says the team must move past its previous loss and focus on Wednesday’s decisive game, the biggest of their careers. Confidence comes from strong road performances throughout the season and playoffs. The team plans to play consistently by forechecking, getting pucks deep and toward the net, closing defensive gaps, and pressuring opponents. Despite quick third-period goals and a five-on-three score, the speaker felt the team played well overall, particularly at five-on-five, while both goaltenders made important saves. The extra rest and return of an important physical, goal-scoring teammate are welcomed.

Topshop removed till barrier displays nationwide after 10-year-old Kaden Reddick suffered fatal head injuries involving one at its Reading store. Police and Reading Borough Council are investigating, while supporting his family. The Reading branch remained closed after the incident.

The disclosure describes robotic- and navigation-assisted systems, tools, and methods for placing implants, particularly pedicle screws, in vertebrae through overlying soft tissue. A robotic manipulator aligns and advances a screw and coaxial sleeve along a planned insertion trajectory. The sleeve may remain closed during tissue penetration, then open through flexible distal tabs as the screw advances into bone and disengages from the sleeve.

Interchangeable working tools—including scalpels, probes, dilators, burs, drills, taps, and tap markers—connect to input devices through removable drive couplers. The couplers transfer rotational or translational forces, permit rapid tool changes, indicate insertion depth, and may allow surgeon-controlled movement while a robotic arm constrains tools to planned virtual boundaries. An elongate sleeve retracts tissue, prevents tissue ingress, provides a working channel, and may include spikes that engage bone to prevent lateral movement.

Navigation systems track anatomy and tools using detectable markers. Tap markers may remain secured in vertebrae during procedures that can move the anatomy, such as discectomy and cage placement. Removable tracking devices can then relocalize the vertebrae. A tracking device may include a ratcheting mechanism allowing its markers to rotate in one direction relative to a secured tool while preserving the tool’s position and orientation for navigation.

The FDA announced a nationwide crackdown on illegal sales of Juul e-cigarettes to minors at stores and online. Since March 2018, compliance checks found 40 violations, prompting warning letters and expectations of further enforcement. The agency also worked with eBay to remove Juul listings and requested documents from Juul’s manufacturer to determine why the nicotine-heavy products appeal to youth. Similar requests and actions are planned for other manufacturers and companies using misleading youth-oriented marketing. The Truth Initiative welcomed the action but urged faster regulation and removal of flavors that attract young people. The FDA is also pursuing education campaigns and assessing ways to make tobacco products less toxic, addictive and appealing.

The St. John’s Edge defeated the London Lightning 123-110 in Game 4, tying the National Basketball League of Canada Central Division final 2-2. Game 5 was scheduled for Thursday in St. John’s, followed by Game 6 Sunday in London.

After London built an early double-digit lead, St. John’s controlled the game, outscoring the Lightning 50-38 in the paint. London missed 13 free throws and struggled defensively. Charles Hinkle and Coron Williams scored 28 points each for the Edge, while Ryan Reid added 22. Royce White led London with 32 points and Ryan Anderson scored 21.

Lightning coach Keith Vassell accepted responsibility for preparation, adjustments and his limited use of the bench. Edge coach Jeff Dunlap credited lineup changes, including starting Alex Johnson. Vassell dismissed a third-quarter confrontation between White and Anderson as competitive frustration.

Separately, the league investigated a fan’s complaint alleging White used a homophobic slur during Game 3. Reports differed, and officials said they did not hear what was said.

The address presents the peaceful transfer of power as an opportunity for national unity, social progress, and global peace. It acknowledges American achievements in prosperity, science, civil rights, and education while warning of spiritual crisis, war, division, and unfulfilled lives. The speaker calls for quieter public discourse, responsive government, equal dignity for Black and white Americans, and cooperation between citizens and government to improve housing, education, cities, rural areas, the environment, and quality of life.

Internationally, the administration pledges open communication, negotiation, patient diplomacy, arms reduction, aid to the poor and hungry, and sufficient national strength. Peace is defined not as victory over others but as compassion, understanding, and self-determination. Drawing on Apollo’s view of Earth, the address emphasizes humanity’s shared destiny and urges people to move forward together with faith, purpose, caution, and hope.

The study examined Turkish teachers’ experiences with Turkish language courses and technological tools during COVID-19 distance education in Turkey. Using a qualitative case-study design, researchers conducted eight-question semi-structured interviews with 20 Turkish teachers teaching grades 5–8 in Hazro, Diyarbakır. Responses were analyzed descriptively and grouped by frequency.

Although 45% of teachers believed education progressed during the pandemic and 25% considered the progress insufficient, none regarded distance education as fully efficient. Most said learning outcomes were only partly achieved, primarily because students lacked internet infrastructure, phones, tablets, or computers. Other problems included irregular attendance, multiple school-age children sharing devices, limited parental support, interrupted connections, short lesson periods, and insufficient time to follow planned programs.

Teachers identified books and dictionaries, technological materials, and activities supporting reading, writing, listening, and speaking as key needs for Turkish lessons. Phones were the most commonly used communication tool, while WhatsApp was the most frequently used application, followed by Zoom and EBA. EBA and EBA TV were generally considered beneficial, though some teachers cited infrastructure limitations.

Participants said distance-education teachers should possess subject knowledge, communication and technology skills, plan materials in advance, use activity-oriented instruction, consider individual differences, and follow current developments. They recommended resolving infrastructure and material shortages, expanding and updating EBA, providing technology training, creating compensation programs, supporting reading, and using distance education alongside face-to-face teaching. They also proposed adapting education to regional conditions, strengthening cooperation among teachers, students, and parents, and revising post-pandemic learning objectives according to student needs.

A Las Vegas high school student says employment reversed his academic disengagement, helping him earn a 4.0 GPA while developing practical skills, confidence, and purpose. Research cited links youth jobs, internships, and apprenticeships to improved academic, social, and employment outcomes and reduced delinquency. However, such opportunities remain scarce, particularly for African American youth. The author urges governments to incentivize businesses, address transportation and scheduling barriers, and expand paid work-based learning to reconnect young people and benefit communities.

Apple filed a Form 8-K on August 1, 2017, reporting financial results for its third fiscal quarter ended July 1, 2017. The filing includes a press release and related data sheet as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2 and was signed by Chief Financial Officer Luca Maestri.

Diana Beresford-Kroeger, an Irish-born botanist and medical biochemist, lives with her husband Christian on 160 acres near Merrickville, where they created the Carrigliath arboretum and organic garden. Orphaned at 11, she spent three years with families who taught her traditional Irish knowledge about nature and life. After studying at University College Cork, the University of Connecticut, Carleton University, and the University of Ottawa, she pursued scientific and surgical research in Canada.

Concerned by local development and tree loss, Diana began documenting and preserving rare species. Her work expanded into books, international speaking, and the Canadian documentary “Call of the Forest: The Forgotten Wisdom of Trees,” which examines deforestation and climate change. Her proposed Bioplan encourages every person to plant one tree annually for six years; she estimates 50 billion trees could reduce atmospheric carbon dioxide from 400 to 300 parts per million. Through accessible science communication, she hopes to protect the environment for future generations.

The speaker describes a coach as tough, honest, hardworking and funny. He expects a difficult series against a deep, defensively strong opponent but is excited to pursue a shared championship dream. He praises Canadian hockey crowds, modern goalies’ athleticism and size, and his team’s scoring depth, including younger lines. He also argues that Giggy receives less recognition because he plays in a smaller media market.

Reports of Hindu girls being abducted, converted to Islam, and married to Muslim men have increasingly emerged in Pakistan’s Sindh province. Families and activists allege organized coercion targeting minors, while converted women, religious leaders, seminaries, and shrines often maintain that the women eloped and converted voluntarily. Courts generally rely on the women’s testimony, making coercion difficult to establish.

Lower-caste and low-income Hindus are particularly vulnerable because of poverty, discrimination, isolation, and rural feudal power structures. Religious institutions and politicians often support conversions, while seminaries and clerics also offer money and housing to converts. Mass conversions of Hindu families have also been reported.

A 2016 Sindh bill banning forced conversions and conversions before age 18 was abandoned after opposition from hardline religious groups. Activists have instead used laws prohibiting marriage under 18, but courts have still allowed some underage converts, including Ravita Meghwar, to live with their husbands.

The controversy has heightened insecurity among Pakistan’s Hindu minority. Some Hindu families are moving from villages to cities, while others are migrating to India. Activists connect the organized rise in conversions over the past 15 years to Pakistan’s broader Islamic nationalism and the legacy of General Zia-ul-Haq’s Islamization policies.

Combination defenses limit outstanding scorers’ touches and rely on timing and surprise. Common types include Box & One, with four zone defenders and one chaser; Diamond & One, which protects the middle but concedes corners; and Triangle & Two, designed for two scorers or tactical changes.

Saturday night remains a crucial ratings battleground for BBC1 and ITV because it attracts family audiences and demonstrates the BBC’s entertainment role. Yet launching successful programmes in this competitive slot is difficult, leaving schedules reliant on established shows such as Strictly, The X Factor and Casualty. Few entertainment formats have achieved lasting success, and little created in the past decade has broken through. Although Strictly and The X Factor revived Saturday television after Blind Date declined, both will eventually lose audiences. Broadcasters want original formats and talent, while producers stand to earn substantial rewards from international success. However, most new shows fail, and channel controllers must depend on instinct, producers’ records and hope.

Colony Northstar shares fell 2.3%, closing at $5.94. Five analysts set an average 12-month price target of $8.80, ranging from $6 to $10. Recommendations included one Buy, three Outperform, one Hold, and no Underperform or Sell ratings. The stock’s 14-period Average True Range was 0.3, with weekly volatility of 2.44% and monthly volatility of 3.81%. Its Relative Strength Index was 21.31, below the traditional oversold threshold of 30. Colony Northstar had a market capitalization of $3.32 billion and 558.38 million outstanding shares. Previous trading volume was 11.19 million shares, above the average of 8.14 million.

A study of 10.3 million opioid-prescription insurance claims found that pre-existing psychiatric and behavioral conditions and psychoactive medication use predicted long-term opioid use. About 1.7% used opioids for at least six months, with substantially higher risks among patients with mental health or substance use disorders.

The coach said Dallas played strong hockey for two periods but undermined itself in the third with correctable puck-support errors, odd-man rushes, and attempts to force big plays. Facing elimination, the team’s sole focus is winning the next game and returning home. He emphasized maintaining the system, defending with greater intensity, and avoiding frustration and individual play.

New Jersey’s speed without the puck, size, disciplined defense, and ability to reach loose pucks have given it a narrow but decisive advantage. The coach praised several opposing players, Larry Robinson’s coaching, and Fetisov’s influence on detailed defensive habits. He said shots are less important than scoring chances and that Dallas must eliminate easy opportunities.

He argued that emotional motivation must now come from the dressing room, particularly the captains and veteran leadership, while coaches concentrate on tactical guidance. Dallas must believe it can recover, accept the physical and mental demands, and raise its level rather than rely on past experience. He remained confident the team would respond strongly, while acknowledging that New Jersey has forced Dallas out of its preferred style.

Three chemists from UC Berkeley, Kyoto University and the University of Melbourne won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing metal-organic frameworks. These structures can harvest water, store toxic gases and hold large amounts despite their small size. More than 100,000 have been created.

The plaintiffs recovered the price of a horse selected, received, and used by the defendant before its return and subsequent death. The court rejected the defendant’s claims of a thirty-day trial, invalidity under the statute of frauds, and breach of warranty. Finding sufficient evidence of delivery and acceptance, the appellate court affirmed the judgment with costs.

The NPD Group identified five trends expected to shape Britain’s £57 billion foodservice industry in 2018. Click & collect could reduce waiting times, increase capacity, improve customer data and boost sales, but may require operational and layout changes. Investing in well-trained, retained staff can strengthen customer relationships, loyalty and profits. Loyalty schemes should become tiered and personalized, rewarding high-value customers with exclusive offers and occasional surprises. Operators must consistently deliver on brand promises across products, service and support to avoid losing customers and attracting social media complaints. Finally, authentic staff advice and customer data can provide personalized recommendations, helping customers choose and encouraging return visits. Success across these trends will depend on innovation and effective execution.

German Chancellor Angela Merkel agreed to establish asylum transit centers along the Austrian border after Interior Minister Horst Seehofer and Bavaria’s CSU demanded tougher immigration controls amid growing support for the far-right AfD. Migrants who previously applied for asylum elsewhere in the EU would be held in the centers and returned following agreements with relevant countries, or sent to Austria if no deal is reached. The plan has strained Merkel’s coalition, with the SPD objecting that transit centers were not included in its coalition agreement. Austria warned it could respond by expelling refugees, potentially threatening the EU’s internal open-border system. The dispute reflects broader European divisions over migration, as Italy, the Czech Republic, Poland, Hungary and Slovakia also resist accepting migrants from other EU countries.

It contains 108 streaming multiprocessors, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/s bandwidth, and a 40 MB L2 cache. Tensor Cores support TF32, FP16, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. Compared with V100, A100 provides higher dense and sparse computation throughput, including up to 2.5× FP64 and mixed-precision performance, while 2:4 structured sparsity can double Tensor Core throughput.

Third-generation NVLink supplies 600 GB/s total bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4, Magnum IO, InfiniBand, Ethernet, and NVSwitch support large multi-GPU systems. The DGX A100 system combines eight A100 GPUs, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and supporting up to 56 isolated GPU instances. Its NVLink, NVSwitch, InfiniBand, Magnum IO, NGC software, and cluster support enable deployment from individual workloads to large AI and HPC installations.

Amazon.com’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2020 reported Q3 net sales of $96.1 billion, up 37% year over year, operating income of $6.2 billion, and net income of $6.3 billion, or $12.37 per diluted share.
