The disclosure describes plasma substrate-processing systems and methods for creating arbitrarily shaped ion energy distribution functions (IEDFs) using shaped-pulse bias waveforms. Conventional RF bias produces two-peaked IEDFs because the plasma sheath voltage oscillates, while shaped pulses can keep substrate and sheath voltage nearly constant for most of each cycle, producing a monoenergetic IEDF.

IEDF shape is controlled by modulating the amplitude and frequency of negative voltage jumps applied to an electrode. Pulse amplitude determines ion energy, while the relative number or duration of pulses or bursts at each amplitude determines the corresponding ion fraction. Repeated pulse sequences can create single-, double-, triple-, or broader-peaked distributions.

Additional methods alter the voltage ramp during the ion-current compensation phase. Overcompensation uses a more negative slope, causing substrate-voltage magnitude and instantaneous ion energy to increase and producing a wider, double-peaked IEDF. Undercompensation uses a less negative slope, causing voltage magnitude and ion energy to decrease and producing a wider, single-peaked IEDF. A bias supply or controller stores and executes programs controlling these waveforms in a plasma-processing chamber.

The lecture develops binary detection by first reducing communication to a one-shot problem: one bit produces an observation corrupted by noise, and the detector maps that observation to one of two hypotheses. This simplification illustrates the theoretical method of solving a basic model before restoring practical constraints.

A maximum a posteriori probability (MAP) detector chooses the hypothesis with the largest posterior probability, thereby minimizing overall error probability. Using Bayes’ rule, binary MAP detection becomes a likelihood-ratio threshold test: compare the ratio of conditional observation densities with the ratio of prior probabilities. The likelihood ratio is a sufficient statistic because no other observation information is needed for the decision.

For binary antipodal signaling in additive Gaussian noise, zero and one are represented by \(+a\) and \(-a\). The Gaussian likelihood ratio simplifies to an exponential linear in the observation, so the log-likelihood test becomes a direct threshold comparison. With equally likely inputs, MAP reduces to maximum-likelihood detection, the threshold is centered between the signals, and the error probability is
\[
Q\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{2E_b}{N_0}}\right).
\]
Unequal priors shift the threshold toward the less probable hypothesis.

For arbitrary non-antipodal signal points, error probability depends only on their separation, while shifting both points away from the origin increases energy without improving detection. Such additional energy may support synchronization or pilot signals but does not reduce detection error.

The same principles extend to antipodal vectors in independent Gaussian noise. The log-likelihood ratio depends only on the inner product between the received vector and the transmitted signal vector. Thus, vector or waveform detection reduces to projecting the observation onto the signal direction, implemented for waveforms by a matched filter, followed by the same one-dimensional binary decision. Decision regions are separated by a plane perpendicular to the line joining the two signal vectors.

Volunteers in southern New South Wales and the ACT conduct late-winter platypus surveys to provide baseline data on the near-threatened species. Waterwatch has formally monitored the Upper Murrumbidgee River near Cooma for four years, with results suggesting local numbers are stable despite no platypus being seen during the latest survey. Platypus populations have declined across eastern Australia and Tasmania because of habitat changes, reduced river flows, exotic fish and discarded fishing equipment. Waterwatch encourages year-round reporting of sightings. Observers are advised to watch waterways in early morning or late evening during August and September, looking for ripples, bubbles, a rounded back and distinctive rings on the water.

The Princeton offense is an unstructured, team-oriented style developed and popularized by Pete Carril. It uses constant motion, spacing, passing, defensive reads, and counters—especially backdoor cuts—to create open shots. All five players participate and must shoot, pass, drive with either hand, understand the court, remain patient and unselfish, and maintain strong conditioning.

Players generally stay 12–15 feet apart and above the free-throw line except on basket cuts, spreading the defense and limiting help or double-teams. The offense can begin from various alignments and entries, then flow continuously through exchanges, screens, cuts, post actions, and renewed entries without resetting. Defensive overplays trigger back cuts or dribble clears, while sagging defenses are attacked through outside shooting, dribble handoffs, penetration, and kick-out passes.

Tempo is deliberately controlled, sometimes involving 15–20 passes per possession, while quick-break opportunities remain available. Post-ups often collapse the defense to create outside shots rather than serve as primary scoring options. Quick-hitting sets can be used late in possessions or after timeouts.

The system requires full coaching commitment but provides adaptability, daily practice of fundamentals, resistance to scouting, and preparation against pressure defenses. Its low-possession pace, constant movement, and threat of back cuts can create physical and psychological pressure, fatigue, frustration, rushed decisions, and defensive mistakes among opponents.

The team was outmuscled early in the second period but improved its work ethic late in the period and carried strong play into the third, tying the game before scoring quickly in overtime. NVIDIA’s Ampere-based GA102 GPU, manufactured on Samsung’s custom 8 nm process, contains 28.3 billion transistors. A full GA102 includes 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second-generation RT cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor cores. Compared with Turing, GA10x doubles peak FP32 processing and ray-triangle intersection throughput, adds concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute, and supports hardware-accelerated motion blur. Third-generation Tensor cores add TF32, BF16, and structured sparsity, which can double matrix throughput and accelerate AI workloads, denoising, and DLSS.

GA102 supports GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, reaching 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/s bandwidth. Third-generation NVLink can combine two 48 GB A40 or RTX A6000 GPUs into 96 GB of memory, while PCIe 4.0 doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth. Architectural changes include larger L1/shared memory, doubled shared-memory bandwidth, and moving ROPs into graphics processing clusters. Ampere GPUs are stated to be up to 1.9 times more power-efficient than Turing at equal performance.

RTX IO uses GPU-based asset loading and decompression with Microsoft DirectStorage to reduce CPU use and accelerate storage transfers. Display capabilities include DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1 for 4K at 120 Hz or 8K at 60 Hz. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware AV1 decoding up to 8K60 HDR, while seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The architecture powers GeForce RTX 30-series products and professional RTX A6000 and A40 GPUs. The RTX 3090 has 24 GB GDDR6X and targets creators, researchers, and gamers; the RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6. The A40 and RTX A6000 provide 48 GB GDDR6, virtualization support, and professional graphics, compute, AI, rendering, simulation, and data-center capabilities.

The Iowa Supreme Court affirmed dismissal of an action to enforce a New York deficiency judgment against James and Elizabeth Siver and prevent their property transfers to their sons as fraudulent. The Sivers counterclaimed that John Secor had induced the underlying land exchange through false representations about a farm’s condition, productivity, improvements, and value. The court found sufficient admissible evidence that the Sivers were materially misled and grossly overreached.

The court held that objections to witness competency must specifically identify the grounds of incompetency. A general assertion that a witness is “incompetent and unqualified” is insufficient. Although interested parties cannot testify against a deceased person’s administrator about personal transactions or communications with the deceased, they may testify about property descriptions, quality and value, reliance on representations, property conditions, and conversations between the deceased and another person. An objection addressing personal transactions does not necessarily cover personal communications.

The court also upheld taxing costs against the administratrix in her official rather than individual capacity, finding no demonstrated prejudice.

Justice Stevens dissented, joined fully by Justice Ladd and in conclusion by Justice Salinger. The dissent viewed the objections as sufficient to cover both transactions and communications and considered the Sivers’ testimony inadmissible because both participated in the relevant conversations with Secor.

A traditional Bulgarian and Turkish method ferments warmed cow’s milk with four live red wood ants in an ant mound overnight. Ant-associated bacteria produce lactic and acetic acids, while ants add formic acid; enzymes from both help thicken the milk into tangy, creamy yogurt. Live ants create better microbial and chemical conditions than frozen or dehydrated ants. Researchers caution against making it at home because live ants may carry parasites that can rarely cause liver or gastrointestinal disease.

Jara had served as deputy superintendent of Orange County Public Schools since 2012 and previously led Monroe County Public Schools in Florida. He said he would listen to the community and work with district staff to improve student achievement.

The divided board first rejected internal candidate Dr. Mike Barton by a 4–3 vote. Barton had strong support from meeting attendees, principals and community representatives, while trustees argued for two hours before approving Jara. Board Vice President Carolyn Edwards urged the community to give him a fair chance.

Jara was one of six finalists chosen after the district received 77 applications. The board hoped he would begin before outgoing superintendent Pat Skorkowsky retired at the end of June, subject to contract negotiations.

Socket 940 must display molded identification, lever lock/unlock indicators, pin A01 orientation, and a visible UL-approved supplier symbol. A visible lot traceability number may be inked, laser-marked, or impact-marked.

Contacts use high-strength copper alloy, plated with at least 1.27 µm nickel and, in mating areas, at least 0.76 µm gold. No lubricant is permitted on mating areas. SMT attachment uses 0.76 mm tin-lead solder balls on 0.64 mm PCB pads, with solder barriers and maximum field coplanarity of 0.20 mm.

A right-side stainless-steel lever enables tool-free actuation. Open-position insertion and extraction forces must not exceed 2 kgf; closed-position extraction force is at least 0.013 kgf per pin. Lever operation requires less than 3.6 kgf, pin displacement must remain below 1.0 mm, and the socket must retain integrity after 50 cycles.

Electrical limits include under 4 nH single-pin inductance, 3 nH ±10% loop inductance, under 1 pF capacitance, 100 Ω ±10% differential impedance, under 10 ps propagation skew plus measurement error, at least 650 Vac dielectric strength, and at least 1000 MΩ insulation resistance.

The lecture reviews Wald’s identity for random walks stopped upon crossing upper or lower thresholds. Applying Markov’s inequality yields an exponential upper bound on the probability that a negative-mean random walk crosses a positive threshold, governed by the second root of its log moment-generating function.

In binary hypothesis testing, the likelihood ratio summarizes all relevant observations and is therefore a sufficient statistic. The MAP rule compares it with a threshold determined by prior probabilities. For IID observations, the log-likelihood ratio is a random walk; under one hypothesis its associated second root is always 1. Fixed-sample tests trade off the two error probabilities, while sequential tests continue until the log-likelihood ratio crosses a preset positive or negative threshold. Such preset stopping rules are distinguished from selectively continuing experiments to obtain desired results. Sequential testing can achieve low error probabilities with fewer observations on average. Wald’s equality relates the expected stopping time to the expected stopped sum, including any threshold overshoot.

Differentiating Wald’s identity at zero produces Wald’s equality. A second derivative, under a zero-mean assumption, relates the expected squared stopped sum to the expected stopping time. For a symmetric simple random walk between thresholds, the expected stopping time equals the product of the thresholds’ magnitudes, illustrating the risks of “stop when ahead” gambling strategies.

A martingale is a sequence whose next conditional expected value, given its full past, equals its current value. Examples include zero-mean random walks, partial sums of dependent zero-conditional-mean increments, and products of independent unit-mean variables. A double-or-nothing product martingale shows that expectations and limits cannot always be interchanged: expected capital remains one at every finite time, but capital converges to zero with probability one. Submartingales have nondecreasing conditional expectations, while supermartingales have nonincreasing ones.

The lecture concludes with Jensen’s inequality: for a convex function, the function of a random variable’s expectation is no greater than the expectation of the function.

The command migrates up to 128 SNP guest pages within physical memory and may replace PAGE_MOVE. A 2M page must comprise contiguous 4K pages and be 2M-aligned; noncontiguous 2M migration is unsupported. CPU access must be blocked, and concurrent DMA may be aborted.

Source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, while destinations must be Pre-Migration. After copying, destinations inherit source states and sources become Pre-Migration. Firmware validates platform state, addresses, guest context, page sizes and states; obtains exclusive RMP access; invalidates and synchronizes the source TLB; copies data; and updates both RMPs. Failures return status codes.

An end command can mark completion of migration command sequences and optionally interrupt software. Command or list-entry errors may cause rejection or partial success. Ring-buffer errors appear in PM_STATUS, while hardware errors are reported through command status or MCA. Batch hardware failures may make all affected pages unrecoverable; software may save state, terminate VMs, stop TMPM operations, or reboot.

Action on Smoking and Health (ASH) argues that zero tobacco deaths should be the global goal. It portrays smokers as victims of an industry that markets intentionally addictive, deadly products, citing Sylvio’s fatal addiction. The Cape Town Declaration recognizes tobacco industry practices as human-rights infringements and has over 150 organizational endorsements. Founded in 1967, ASH advocates bold measures to achieve a tobacco-free world and eliminate preventable tobacco deaths.

Sydney maths teacher Eddie Woo rose to prominence through WooTube, a free YouTube channel created in 2012 to help an ill student. It now has more than 200,000 subscribers and 12 million views. In 2018, Woo was named Australia’s Local Hero and became one of 10 finalists for the Global Teacher Prize.

Woo remains at Cherrybrook Technology High School while serving as a NSW Department of Education “master teacher,” travelling across the state to mentor teachers and students and promote engaging approaches to mathematics. During a Riverina tour, hundreds of students and teachers attended his presentations, where he described maths as play, exploration and storytelling.

Education officials praise Woo’s ability to explain complex mathematics and reach students through technology. Despite growing fame and a busier schedule affecting his work and family time, Woo says sharing his enthusiasm for mathematics makes the effort worthwhile.

The IRS announced inflation-adjusted 2026 tax brackets and deductions to limit bracket creep. Standard deductions rise to $32,200 for joint filers, $16,100 for singles and $24,150 for heads of household. The 37% rate begins above $640,600 for individuals and $768,700 for couples. The estate tax exemption increases to $15 million, credit thresholds will be adjusted, and taxpayers aged 65 or older receive a new $6,000 deduction beginning in 2025. Analysts expect modest household relief without major federal revenue losses.

The Sansa Fuze is a portable audio/video player with a 1.9-inch color screen, FM radio, microphone, microSD/SDHC expansion, internal storage, and rechargeable battery. It supports music, audiobooks, converted videos and photos, voice and FM recording, playlists, slideshows, and customizable playback options. The manual explains charging, controls, computer connection, firmware updates, formatting, media transfer through Windows Media Player or Sansa Media Converter, playback, radio presets, and recording. Users must avoid disconnecting during data transfer, note that formatting erases content, and comply with copyright laws.

The New Jersey Supreme Court affirmed the denial of counsel fees and costs sought under the Anti-Injunction Act in two labor-related cases. In the arbitration case, the Act did not apply because the action primarily sought a declaration about whether a discharged employee’s grievance was arbitrable; the requested restraint was merely ancillary. In the strike case, although the Act applied and the injunction was reversed, fees were unwarranted because the Appellate Division had found a substantive basis for injunctive relief and reversed solely for procedural deficiencies not attributable to the company. The Act mandates costs and counsel fees when injunctive relief is denied or reversed on the merits because the employer’s action was wrongfully brought, not whenever reversal occurs for procedural reasons. The judgments were unanimously affirmed, with costs awarded to the respondent only in the arbitration case. Appellants could reapply for ordinary statutory trial-court costs as prevailing parties in that action.

Charlie Alliston, 18 at the time, struck 44-year-old Kim Briggs at nearly 20mph as she crossed Old Street in London in February 2016. Briggs suffered catastrophic brain injuries and died a week later. Prosecutors told the Old Bailey that Alliston was unlawfully riding a fixed-wheel track bicycle without a front brake and that crash reconstructions showed he could have stopped if one had been fitted. After the collision, Alliston posted online that Briggs was at fault and defended his own actions. The prosecution argued that riding the brakeless bike through a busy area was unlawful, dangerous and caused Briggs’s death. Alliston denies manslaughter and causing bodily harm by wanton or furious driving.

A Harvard poll found 65% of Americans aged 18-29 favored Democrats versus 33% favoring Republicans. Only 14% believed the country was headed in the right direction, while Trump’s approval stood at 25%. Most viewed internal forces as America’s greatest threats, and 61% supported stricter gun laws.

Huron County Acting CAO and County Librarian Meighan Wark proposed partnering with Central Huron on renovations to make Clinton Library accessible, improve services, and qualify it for accreditation. Although the Huron County Library system and 11 branches received accreditation in 2015, Clinton did not because of accessibility and space limitations.

Under the existing partnership, the county provides staff, materials, furniture, equipment, and services, while the municipality handles the building, maintenance, and utilities. Renovations would need to meet Ontario Public Library Guidelines, including requirements for adequate square footage, lower shelving, wider aisles, accessibility, attractive design, technology, storage, and flexible community space.

The county would assess required components based on the population served and work with the municipality to agree on space and service needs. An architect could then prepare draft plans for council and public review. Wark said having a shovel-ready project would improve prospects for provincial funding. If Central Huron commits to building changes, the county could invest in the library’s interior. Council plans to continue discussions with Wark.

Gamification applies game mechanics—such as goals, rules, competition, points, levels, feedback, and rewards—to education to strengthen motivation, engagement, strategic thinking, cooperation, and knowledge retention. Effective games require clear instructions, achievable tasks, immediate feedback, and enjoyable activities.

Four projects conducted at the University of Wrocław illustrated different applications. The location-based Kulturalny Wrocław game combined cultural education with information technology. Students solved location-related riddles and completed a crossword in teams. They valued outdoor learning, independence, social interaction, and memorable experiences, although some questioned whether it covered as much material as traditional classes. Its simple rules, low costs, and adaptable content supported its inclusion in the curriculum.

A five-day gamified career-management seminar used a science-fiction plot, missions, points, badges, prizes, and a game-based examination. Participants demonstrated high engagement, strong results, rapid group integration, self-diagnosis, and practical application of knowledge. However, instructors reported that designing the programme required substantial time, effort, testing, and resources, making repeated delivery or external funding preferable.

The Become an Entrepreneur location-based game required teams to complete entrepreneurship tasks, manage game money and obstacles, and pay simulated income tax. Participants praised its social, dynamic, outdoor, and educational qualities and its potential to develop teamwork and other soft skills. They expressed mixed views about competition, internet access, unfamiliar locations, weather dependence, and organisational challenges.

The LARP Spell of the Black Magic Master developed negotiation, communication, creativity, and group-management skills through role-play and team missions. Educational goals were achieved, but inexperienced participants had difficulty assuming roles, understanding complex rules, and integrating with unfamiliar teammates. Preparation and pilot testing were time-consuming.

Overall, educational games can successfully support academic learning when matched to students’ experience, subject matter, time, and available resources. Simple games with clear rules and strategic freedom are generally received best and can be integrated into curricula. Longer, more complex games are better suited to funded supplementary programmes and should be preceded by tutorials and socialising activities.

Preempt announced new integrations for its Behavioral Firewall to improve contextual threat detection and automated enforcement. Data integrations include Okta, Azure Active Directory and VPN gateways, while enforcement integrations include SecureAuth, RSA SecurID, Duo, Google Authenticator and HP Aruba ClearPass. The platform combines user and entity behavioral analytics with adaptive responses to detect suspicious internal activity and block, notify, redirect or challenge users in real time. Policies consider user roles, behavior and targeted assets, aiming to address attackers, malicious insiders and risky users without disrupting business operations.

Elijah Brown scored 27 points, including 17 of New Mexico’s final 19, as the Lobos defeated Boise State 78-73. New Mexico used an 11-0 first-half run and never trailed, then held off a late Broncos rally. Obij Ajet and Damien Jefferson each added 14 points, while Ajet recorded five blocks. Boise State’s Chandler Hutchison scored a career-high 31 points and James Reid had 18. The win moved New Mexico to 16-10 overall and 9-5 in the Mountain West, one loss behind conference leaders Boise State, Colorado State and Nevada. New Mexico played without injured forward Tim Williams. The Lobos next visit Fresno State, while Boise State hosts Wyoming.

This retrospective cohort study examined over 2.2 million U.S. inpatient pregnancy and postpartum hospitalizations from 2017–2019; 168,729 (7.4%) involved a mood disorder. Peripartum cardiomyopathy occurred more often among patients with mood disorders than those without (0.12% vs. 0.05%), as did composite adverse cardiac events (0.36% vs. 0.14%). After adjustment for demographic, clinical, and hospital factors, mood disorders remained associated with peripartum cardiomyopathy (adjusted odds ratio 1.36), composite cardiac events (1.57), and pulmonary edema (1.62), but not maternal mortality or other individual cardiac outcomes. The findings support further investigation of mood disorders as a potentially modifiable risk factor and suggest opportunities for coordinated mental health and cardiac screening. Limitations include reliance on ICD-10 codes, inpatient-only data, inability to establish causation, and absence of post-discharge outcomes.

Washington police will charge 12 Turkish security agents—seven with felonies and five with misdemeanors—over violence during President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s May visit. Two men were arrested on assault charges after Erdogan’s security forces violently broke up a protest outside the Turkish ambassador’s residence.

In card identification mode, the host resets, validates voltage, identifies each card, and requests its RCA using only its CMD line. CMD0 resets SD cards to Idle State, except inactive cards, while power-on places all cards in Idle State. Cards default to RCA 0x0000, 400 kHz, and specified driver strengths; UHS-II retains its Device ID. CMD8 verifies operating voltage and communication. Compatible cards echo voltage and check pattern; incompatible cards remain idle without responding. CMD8 is required before ACMD41 for SDHC/SDXC initialization.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture redesigns the streaming multiprocessor to execute FP32 and INT32 instructions concurrently, adds unified configurable L1/shared memory, and integrates Tensor and RT Cores. These changes deliver a stated 50% improvement in performance per CUDA core over Pascal. Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, and INT4 operations for training, inference, and neural graphics features such as DLSS, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Resolution.

Dedicated RT Cores accelerate bounding-volume hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, enabling substantially faster ray tracing than software execution on Pascal. Turing combines rasterization, ray tracing, AI, denoising, and BVH acceleration in a hybrid rendering model for real-time reflections, shadows, refractions, and ambient occlusion.

Turing also introduces GDDR6 memory, larger and faster L2 caches, improved compression, and approximately 50% higher effective bandwidth than Pascal in the cited comparison. Display and media features include DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, HDR processing, HEVC 8K encoding, expanded video decoding, and VirtualLink support for single-cable VR connections. NVLink replaces earlier SLI transfer interfaces on TU102 and TU104.

New graphics capabilities include mesh and task shaders, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering. These features reduce CPU and shading workloads, reuse shading results, support efficient rendering from multiple viewpoints, and improve VR through foveated rendering and expanded projection support.

The appellate court reinstated Hartford’s bad-faith settlement claims, finding sufficient evidence that General Accident’s delayed policy-limits offer prevented a potentially lower settlement and caused damages. Witness credibility and damages presented jury questions unsuitable for summary judgment. The court affirmed dismissal of Hartford’s claim alleging violations of Insurance Law § 2601.

A University of Rochester Medical Centre study in mice found that low alcohol doses, equivalent to about 2.5 daily drinks for a 70kg person, reduced brain inflammation and improved the glymphatic system’s removal of waste, including proteins associated with Alzheimer’s disease and dementia. Low-dose mice performed similarly to alcohol-free controls in cognitive and motor tests. Intermediate and high doses impaired glymphatic function, while prolonged high exposure increased inflammation and harmed cognitive and motor abilities. Glymphatic function recovered within 24 hours after moderate alcohol exposure ended. The researchers concluded that alcohol’s effects depend on dosage, with low doses potentially benefiting brain waste clearance and excessive consumption proving detrimental. The study was published in Scientific Reports.

Kentucky sophomore forward Wenyen Gabriel will remain in the 2018 NBA draft and begin his professional career rather than return for his junior season. Gabriel averaged 6.8 points and 5.4 rebounds, shot 39.6% from three-point range and led Kentucky with 40 blocks. His season highlight was scoring 23 points while making seven three-pointers against Alabama in the SEC Tournament semifinals.

Gabriel declared without an agent and received mixed feedback from NBA teams, though he was not invited to the scouting combine or ranked among ESPN’s top 100 prospects. Coach John Calipari praised his versatility and potential but acknowledged he must continue improving. Gabriel appears likely to begin his career overseas or in the NBA’s developmental league.

Kentucky has also lost several players to the draft or transfers. PJ Washington will return, while graduate transfer Reid Travis could join a crowded group of post players. Without Travis, Kentucky currently has no scholarship juniors or seniors.

The lecture presents trajectory optimization as policy search over parameterized open-loop controls. Shooting methods simulate trajectories and update parameters using gradients computed either by an adjoint backward pass or forward sensitivity propagation through real-time recurrent learning. The adjoint method uses less state but requires storing and traversing the trajectory; forward sensitivities carry a potentially large matrix but simplify endpoint constraints.

Sequential quadratic programming tools such as SNOPT generally outperform basic gradient descent by avoiding learning-rate tuning, converging faster, and efficiently handling control, state, and terminal constraints. Pendulum, cart-pole, and acrobot examples illustrate these methods.

Direct collocation optimizes both controls and states while imposing discretized dynamics as explicit constraints. It permits rapid cost and gradient evaluation, flexible initialization, and possible avoidance of some local minima. Its fixed-step discretization may be less accurate than shooting, though shooting can refine the result. Both approaches remain local optimization methods, but local minima are often acceptable when trajectories reach the goal. Future topics include feedback stabilization with LQR and iterative LQR trajectory optimization.

Modern defensive schemes require coaches to translate varied run-fit terminology into executable concepts tailored to personnel and philosophy. Run fits are influenced by post-snap front spacing and coverage. Even fronts leave a B-gap bubble, while odd fronts shift open gaps to the C gaps.

Spacing numbers indicate the number of defenders involved in the run fit against 12/21 personnel:

- **7-man spacing:** A light, out-gapped box commonly paired with middle-of-field-open coverage. Overhangs are pass-first, leaving an open gap. Defenses compensate through two-gapping, Tite fronts, stunts, or slants. Typical second-level techniques are “stack-track-fallback” against zone and “spill-overlap” against gap schemes.
- **8-man spacing:** A gapped-out box with equal defenders and offensive gaps, commonly paired with middle-of-field-closed coverage. Defenders generally use aggressive one-gap fits. Linebackers may use indicator fits based on tight-end movement against zone and “lever-spill-lever” against gap schemes.
- **9-man spacing:** A maxed-out or blitz fit, usually associated with Cover 0, featuring an extra run defender. First- and second-level defenders can attack their gaps aggressively, while an overhang or safety joins the fit.

These principles also apply to 3-4 defenses using odd or even spacing. In Tite/Mint fronts, a head-up nose may lag into the backside A gap while linebackers use stack-track-fallback. Overhang responsibilities can depend on running-back location: they may play the RPO and remain outside the fit or fill aggressively. Depending on spacing and philosophy, 3-4 defenses may use spill-overlap, lever-spill-lever, or one-gap fits.

A Norwalk, Iowa, family says an I-35 expansion project damaged their 68-year-old well, leaving them without clean water for two months despite assurances that construction would avoid it. Erin and Mark Paschell, who have two young children, must bring in water and cannot bathe their children or do laundry at home. After being told connection to Warren County’s rural water system could take 30–60 days, Mark and a contractor dug a 300-yard trench and installed a line themselves. The Iowa Department of Transportation says it is investigating and offered hotel accommodation until service is restored, along with reimbursement for cleaning supplies needed because of damage from dirty water.

Andrew Lo says financial markets remain fearful but interest rates are relatively low, liquidity support is active, and investors are largely waiting for clarity. He argues that greater pricing transparency for complex securities could improve liquidity and strongly opposes suspending mark-to-market accounting.

The lecture examines derivatives as tools for managing risks such as currency and commodity-price fluctuations. Hedging can stabilize cash flows and reduce financial distress, though shareholders could theoretically hedge independently. Derivatives can support risk management or cause harm depending on their use, while speculators provide counterparties for hedgers.

A forward contract is a customized, over-the-counter agreement to transact at a specified future date and price. It is binding, typically requires no initial payment, and begins with zero market value. Forward prices reflect market conditions and factors including storage and financing costs. Such contracts are illiquid and expose both parties to default risk as their value changes.

Futures contracts address these problems through standardized terms, exchange trading, daily mark-to-market settlement, collateral requirements, and a clearing corporation acting as intermediary. Daily payments limit counterparty exposure largely to one day’s price movement. Brokers issue margin calls when collateral falls below required levels and may close positions if funds are not supplied. Futures may involve physical delivery, but most participants use cash settlement. Forwards remain useful when customized quantities, dates, or established commercial relationships are important.

The lecture uses the dressed-atom picture to explain stimulated light forces. Diagonalizing the atom–laser interaction produces two dressed states split by the generalized Rabi frequency. In the strong-driving secular limit, population and coherence dynamics decouple, clarifying Mollow-triplet intensities and widths. Bare- and dressed-state descriptions provide complementary temporal and spectral pictures of spontaneous emission.

Atoms in the two dressed states experience equal and opposite forces. Their population imbalance produces an attractive force for red-detuned light and a repulsive force for blue-detuned light; on resonance, the average force vanishes. A finite delay in populations adjusting to a spatially varying field creates nonadiabatic friction, explaining cooling by blue-detuned light. Force reversals during transitions between dressed states generate momentum diffusion and heating, which can dominate photon-recoil heating in strong fields.

For atoms moving through a blue-detuned standing wave, transitions occur preferentially near potential maxima and place atoms near minima of the other dressed potential. Atoms therefore repeatedly climb potential hills before spontaneous emission lowers their energy, producing Sisyphus cooling. A perturbative treatment at large detuning derives transition rates, friction, and momentum diffusion, finding that the minimum temperature is comparable to the lattice depth. Thus two-level laser cooling alone cannot localize atoms in a lattice, and recoil heating ultimately prevents blue molasses from outperforming the Doppler limit.

The dipole force can also be understood through optical Bloch equations, dressed states, induced-dipole energy, or refraction. The refraction picture extends to dielectric particles and underlies optical tweezers used in biology and biophysics.

Child care academies in at least 11 North Carolina counties offer low- or no-cost, accelerated training to address early childhood educator shortages. Programs last two to six weeks and involve 20 to 64 hours of instruction, often through partnerships among community colleges, Smart Start agencies, and Child Care Resource and Referral organizations.

Two models operate statewide. Classroom-ready academies provide required health, safety, background-check, and registration preparation, qualifying graduates to work in licensed facilities but not as lead teachers. Teaching credential academies also cover EDU 119 content. Graduates earn transferable EDU 3119 continuing education credit, qualifying them as lead teachers or elementary teaching assistants and supporting further study toward an associate degree.

Programs operate in Buncombe, Cabarrus, Catawba, Davidson, Davie, Durham, Johnston, McDowell, Rowan, Stanly, and Wayne counties. Reported costs range from about $430 to $1,264 per student, funded through foundations, grants, and local partnerships. Programs in Wayne, Johnston, Stanly, McDowell, and Durham have placed graduates in child care jobs or higher education.

A $1.476 million expansion pilot passed the North Carolina House but was excluded from later legislation signed in August. Separately, the state Division of Child Development and Early Education is offering grants of up to $50,000 to as many as 10 eligible colleges or universities running academies between October 2025 and July 2026. More than a dozen additional community colleges are preparing programs or have expressed interest.

Florida Panthers coach Bob Boughner said injured goaltenders Roberto Luongo and James Reimer could return to practice and possibly the lineup next week. Luongo has missed 23 games with a lower-body injury, while Reimer has been sidelined with a groin injury. Backtests using Yahoo! Finance Bitcoin data from 2014 indicate a positive end-of-month effect. The strategy optimized entries before month-end and exits after the new month across 100 simulations. One formulation produced a 3.3% average gain per trade, 41.8% CAGR, 16% market exposure, and 25% maximum drawdown. Although partly curve-fitted, gains exceeded the 1.33% average for random periods of equal length. Adjusting entry timing and adding another variable reduced trades and CAGR but produced a smoother equity curve. The authors conclude the effect could support a turn-of-the-month strategy, though they do not disclose the improved rules.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies up to 2 MHz and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full bridge. External gate drivers are recommended because switching and synchronous-rectifier outputs provide roughly 150-mA peak current.

External synchronization requires RT floating and a 200-kHz to 4-MHz clock at SYNC, preferably 50% duty cycle, at twice the desired switching frequency. Two controllers can operate in primary-secondary mode for synchronized independent converters or an interleaved parallel converter. The secondary inverts the primary clock, producing a 90° or 270° output phase shift.

Available OUTA/OUTB and SRA/SRB outputs vary by device. OUTB is active only for TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP with a 50% duty-cycle limit; SRB is exclusive to TPS7H5001-SP under the same condition. Synchronous-rectifier outputs remain off during soft-start until SS exceeds 1 V. Programmable dead times are available on TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP, while TPS7H5003-SP uses a typical fixed 50-ns dead time. Leading-edge blanking is programmable on all devices except TPS7H5003-SP. Pulse skipping addresses minimum-on-time limitations and occurs when COMP is below 0.3 V at the clock edge and the previous duty cycle was below 25%.

Supported maximum duty-cycle settings are 50%, 75%, or 100%, depending on device and DCL configuration; TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50%. Current sensing through CS_ILIM controls PWM and overcurrent protection. At 1.05 V, cycle-by-cycle limiting begins and charges the HICC capacitor. When HICC reaches 0.6 V, switching stops and soft-start is discharged; restart begins after HICC falls from 1 V to 0.3 V. A minimum 3.3-nF HICC capacitor is recommended.

The FAULT pin enables external protections. A voltage above 0.6 V for the specified minimum pulse width shuts down switching; operation restarts after FAULT falls below 0.5 V, a delay of approximately 15 switching cycles, and soft-start. Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical 175°C and restarts below 160°C. Programmable slope compensation prevents subharmonic oscillation in peak-current-mode designs, with compensation equal to the inductor falling-current slope recommended. Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation may be used.

A TPS7H5001-SP synchronous push-pull GaN design example operates at 500 kHz and 5 V output. Selected values include 205-kΩ RT, 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback resistors, approximately 25-ns dead time using 20.5-kΩ resistors, 49.9-kΩ leading-edge blanking resistance, 33-nF soft-start capacitance, a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 0.47-µH output inductance, approximately 2.3-mF output capacitance, 7.5-Ω current-sense resistance, 3.3-nF hiccup capacitance, and 102-kΩ slope-compensation resistance. Primary and synchronous GaN FETs were rated at 170 V and 80 V, respectively.

The controllers require a regulated 4-V to 14-V supply and at least 0.1-µF VIN bypass capacitance. Layout guidance emphasizes short high-current paths, minimized switch-node area, separation of analog and power grounds with a single connection point, close placement of bypass, filtering, feedback, and compensation components, and routing noisy switching signals away from sensitive control traces. TI states that application guidance must be validated by customers and that its resources are provided subject to applicable disclaimers and terms.

A retrospective review examined 377 mechanically ventilated COVID-19 patients who underwent bedside, bronchoscopy-guided percutaneous tracheostomy at Jaber Al Ahmad Al Sabah Hospital, Kuwait, from March 2020 to March 2022. The protocol generally required at least seven days of intubation and specified ventilatory, laboratory, anticoagulation, staffing, and protective-equipment criteria.

Patients had a mean age of 56.2 years, mean BMI of 31.3, and mean interval from intubation to tracheostomy of 17.4 days. Diabetes and hypertension were the most common comorbidities. During tracheostomy, 29% were receiving ECMO and 23% dialysis.

Complications occurred in 85 patients (23%): 6% intra-operatively, 9% within seven days, and 7% later. Minor bleeding was most frequent, occurring in 14%. Nine tracheo-esophageal fistulae, eight wound infections, and one successfully ligated tracheo-innominate fistula were reported. No procedural deaths occurred.

After tracheostomy, 54% were weaned from sedation after a mean of 7.5 days, and 41% were weaned from mechanical ventilation after 12.9 days. Overall mortality was 63%, entirely attributed to COVID-19 complications; 37% were discharged, including 53 patients decannulated before discharge. Hypertension and age over 65 were significantly associated with increased mortality.

The authors concluded that percutaneous tracheostomy can be performed safely in COVID-19 patients and favored performing it soon after seven days of intubation, while acknowledging uncertainty about optimal timing. Limitations included no open-tracheostomy comparison group, follow-up only until discharge or death, incomplete post-discharge tracheostomy data, and no PCR testing of staff.

The speaker praises Republicans for supporting wartime presidential powers and military expansion despite partisan attacks, citing their patriotism in the Democratic-controlled 65th Congress. Bed Bath & Beyond operated 1,541 stores across the United States, Puerto Rico and Canada in November 2016, plus eight joint-venture stores in Mexico, under several retail brands. Its stock had fallen by roughly half from 2014–2015 highs, while revenue stagnated, margins declined and net income weakened. The company lacked pricing power and faced growing online competition, although its debt, liquidity and interest obligations were described as manageable.

The passage identifies four potential investment arguments. First, BBBY returns capital through dividends and extensive share repurchases, which could increase per-share value even without earnings growth. Second, acquisitions of One Kings Lane and PersonalizationMall.com were intended to expand its online furniture, décor and personalized-gift businesses. Third, the Beyond+ loyalty program, offering discounts and free shipping for an annual fee, received a favorable initial response and could improve customer retention. Fourth, the stock appeared undervalued based on a discounted cash-flow estimate of $54.17 per share, though a 40% safety margin implied a preferred entry price of $32.50.

The company remained exposed to macroeconomic conditions, including housing, unemployment and consumer spending, because many of its products are discretionary. The author expected a return to single-digit growth but would consider investing only around $32.50 per share.

Muriel Diaz, 90, trained as a nurse and midwife after studying music and art and teaching for 10 years. Inspired by a dream, she moved to Peru, where she married Alberto and lived for 32 years. For 18 years, she spent six weeks annually as the sole nurse at a remote jungle clinic, delivering babies and treating illnesses and snake bites without a doctor nearby. The couple moved to Penparc near Cardigan in 1995 because of escalating terrorism in Peru. For the past 20 years, Diaz has volunteered weekly at Cardigan’s Barnardo’s charity shop, repairing donated clothes to help raise money. She also enjoys landscape painting, learning Welsh and visiting friends and relatives in Peru.

Yale-New Haven Hospital sought summary judgment in three actions to collect unpaid medical bills. Defendants alleged that the hospital failed to provide required notice and free care under the Hill-Burton Act and Connecticut’s hospital bed funds statute, and counterclaimed under CUTPA.

The court held that intended beneficiaries may enforce both statutes and raise hospital noncompliance as a defense to collection. Alleged violations may also support CUTPA claims, regardless of whether the underlying statutes independently provide private actions. Whether the hospital’s conduct violated CUTPA presented factual issues for trial. The Hill-Burton Act did not preempt the state claims. The hospital’s motions for summary judgment were denied.

Joey Chestnut won his 11th Nathan’s Famous Mustard Belt by eating a record 74 hot dogs in 10 minutes. Officials initially counted 64 but corrected the tally after realizing he ate from two plates. Carmen Cincotti finished second with 64; Darron Breeden third with 43.

The ADS9803 is reset or powered down through pins or register fields; after power-up or reset, default registers must be initialized using prescribed writes while a free-running sampling clock is connected. User configuration includes analog input range, bandwidth, common-mode range, reference, output lanes, averaging, test patterns, correction codes, and data format.

Speed-boost mode samples one selected analog-input channel pair at up to 8 MSPS on every sampling clock while the other six channels remain idle. Normal data-interface specifications still apply.

The 16-bit registers use 8-bit addresses across three banks. Bank 0 is always accessible, while banks 1 and 2 are selected through register 0x03. SPI register reads and writes use 24-bit frames and require configuring read-enable and SPI-mode fields. Multiple devices can be connected in a daisy chain with shared CS and SCLK; the chain length excludes the first ADC, and operations require N × 24 clock cycles.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2-MSPS data-acquisition system with an integrated analog front end. In an ATE example, post-calibration TUE is 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. It offers low-noise bandwidth up to 22.7 kHz and wide bandwidth up to 700 kHz, with 99.95% full-scale settling in 7.5 µs for multiplexed signals.

The device uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies without a required power-up sequence. Recommended layout practices include close 0.1-µF bypass capacitors, short ground connections, nearby reference decoupling, and separation of analog paths from digital lines and noise sources. TI states that application guidance and resources are provided as-is, and users remain responsible for component selection, design validation, testing, and compliance.

Chargers Chairman Dean Spanos was leaning toward moving the team from San Diego to Los Angeles but appealed to the NFL for help staying. Cancer screening can detect cancer or pre-cancerous changes before symptoms appear, improving treatment success and survival. The NHS offers three main programmes:

- **Cervical screening:** Every five years for women and people with a cervix aged 25–64. It tests cervical samples for high-risk HPV. Positive results may require repeat testing, further cell analysis or colposcopy.
- **Breast screening:** Mammograms every three years for women and eligible people aged 50–71. Those over 71 may request continued screening, while younger people at higher risk should consult their doctor.
- **Bowel screening:** Every two years for people aged 50–74 using a posted faecal immunochemical test (FIT) to detect tiny amounts of blood. Positive results lead to an urgent colonoscopy. Screening beyond age 75 can be requested.

Screening is free, with invitations or kits usually sent by post. People who miss an invitation or believe they are overdue should contact their surgery or relevant screening service. Those without a permanent address can collect a FIT kit from their surgery.

Some screening, including prostate cancer checks, may be considered individually. People with symptoms should contact a doctor rather than wait for routine screening. Family history or other risk factors may justify earlier or additional testing. Women with neurofibromatosis type 1 are entitled to annual mammograms from age 40.

Private screening is also available based on personal choice or individual risk. Normal results can provide reassurance, while early detection may offer more treatment options and reduce deaths from breast, bowel and cervical cancers.

The lecture introduces fast Fourier transform algorithms for efficiently computing the discrete Fourier transform and inverse DFT. Direct computation requires approximately \(N^2\) complex multiplications and additions, making large transforms costly. For composite \(N\), FFT methods reduce computation; when \(N\) is a power of two, complexity is proportional to \(N\log_2N\).

The radix-2 decimation-in-time approach separates a sequence into even- and odd-indexed subsequences. Their \(N/2\)-point DFTs, denoted \(G(k)\) and \(H(k)\), are combined as
\[
X(k)=G(k)+W_N^kH(k).
\]
Periodicity allows each smaller DFT’s values to be reused. Recursively decomposing the \(N/2\)-point transforms into progressively smaller transforms until reaching two-point DFTs produces the computational savings.

The resulting flow graph consists of butterfly operations. Using \(W_N^{N/2}=-1\), each butterfly can be simplified to one multiplication by a power of \(W_N\), followed by an addition and subtraction, reducing multiplications. In the illustrated eight-point FFT, inputs appear in the reordered sequence \(0,4,2,6,1,5,3,7\), while outputs remain sequential. This input arrangement corresponds to reversing the bits of the binary index. Subsequent discussion will address memory organization and alternative FFT forms with differing advantages and disadvantages.

C.J. McCollum scored a career-high 43 points as the Portland Trail Blazers overcame a 14-point deficit to defeat the Minnesota Timberwolves 95-89. Portland, without Damian Lillard for a fourth straight game because of a sprained ankle, took control with a 32-15 third quarter. Mason Plumlee added 18 points and eight rebounds. Andrew Wiggins led Minnesota with 24 points, while Karl-Anthony Towns scored 11 on 3-for-15 shooting. Portland next visits Golden State, where Lillard could return, while Minnesota travels to Philadelphia.

Digital piracy has remained resilient despite technical, legal, and educational countermeasures, reducing industry revenues and pressuring firms to redesign distribution and monetization. Its appeal includes perceived free access, broad catalogs, fewer restrictions, and geographic availability, though it also entails inconsistent quality, technical effort, delays, and legal or moral costs.

Using archival data and nine expert interviews, the study examines how Spotify and Netflix use business models to compete with piracy. Their subscription-based streaming services combine affordable access, convenient interfaces, broad device compatibility, consistent quality, content recommendations, community features, and improved geographic availability. Spotify also offers an advertising-supported free tier. These features primarily outperform piracy through a better consumption experience rather than price or exclusive content.

The firms’ growing user bases improve personalization, network effects, bargaining power, and content offerings, creating reinforcing competitive advantages. The study concludes that digital technologies enable both piracy and effective responses to it. Firms can mitigate piracy by innovating across customer identification, engagement, monetization, and value-chain linkages, particularly by emphasizing accessibility, convenience, discovery, and social interaction. Although the findings may apply to books, games, and other digital content, industry differences and diversification require further study.

Sam’s Club will open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily following member feedback, significantly expanding Sunday hours. Plus members receive exclusive access from 8 to 9 a.m., while curbside pickup begins at 7 a.m. Holiday exceptions apply. Memberships remain cheaper than Costco’s, and both warehouse chains have reported strong results.

Indexed containers represent strictly positive indexed datatypes as functors between families of sets. They correspond closely to generalized polynomials, while offering practical advantages for concrete examples and proof-assistant formalization. A bounded vector illustrates the construction: shapes encode possible lengths and positions encode entries.

The work extends Uustalu’s characterization of monoid structures on non-indexed containers to indexed containers. It describes the monoidal structure corresponding to composition of container extents, adjusts the required data and equations for indexing, and proves that these structures correspond precisely to monad structures on indexed container functors. Unlike earlier work focused on Cartesian polynomial monads, it treats general monads. Examples include products of indexed container monads, indexed state and writer monads, and a free monad producing well-scoped λ-terms when applied to the family Fin.

The development is formalized in Cubical Agda, whose functional extensionality supports proofs of full faithfulness and combinatorial monoid equations, while allowing possible extensions to groupoids and higher-dimensional types.

For a fixed index set \(I\), an indexed container \(S\triangleleft P\) consists of shapes \(S:I\to\mathrm{Set}\) and indexed position families \(P\). Its extent is an endofunctor on \(\mathrm{Set}^I\), mapping a family \(X\) at index \(i\) to pairs of a shape \(s:S\,i\) and an indexed function from its positions to \(X\). Container morphisms map shapes forward and positions backward. Indexed containers and these morphisms form a category \(\mathrm{IC}_I\), and the extent operation defines a full and faithful functor from this category to the category of endofunctors and natural transformations on \(\mathrm{Set}^I\).

The team must get the puck deep, sustain its cycle game, and use its young forwards’ puck control. Ronnie Francis leads through hard work, class, professionalism, and intelligence rather than flashiness. The speaker describes a seven-year relationship with a coach involving criticism, growth, and mutual understanding. Playoff results do not always reflect performance, so players must persevere through adversity. The speaker says recent playoff goals are encouraging and acknowledges increased maturity despite earlier struggles.

Fred Puhn’s 1981 paperback explains suspension theory, chassis layouts, handling hardware, aerodynamic modifications, and brake setup in accessible language. The second-hand copy is in very good condition.

Szemerédi’s graph regularity lemma gives a universal approximate structure for large dense graphs by partitioning their vertices into boundedly many parts such that most pairs of parts behave randomly in a precise sense. For vertex sets \(X,Y\), their edge density is the number of edges between them divided by \(|X||Y|\). A pair \((X,Y)\) is \(\epsilon\)-regular if every \(A\subseteq X\) and \(B\subseteq Y\), each occupying at least an \(\epsilon\) fraction of its parent set, has edge density within \(\epsilon\) of the density between \(X\) and \(Y\). A partition is \(\epsilon\)-regular if the total weighted size of its nonregular pairs is at most an \(\epsilon\) fraction of all vertex pairs.

The lemma states that for every \(\epsilon\), there is a constant \(M\), depending only on \(\epsilon\), such that every graph has an \(\epsilon\)-regular partition into at most \(M\) parts. The bound is independent of the graph’s size. Sparse graphs satisfy the condition trivially, so the result is most useful for dense graphs. A stronger version guarantees an equitable partition, with part sizes differing by at most one, and allows a prescribed minimum number of parts.

The proof uses an energy-increment argument. The energy of a partition is a weighted mean of the squared edge densities between its parts and lies between 0 and 1. Convexity shows that energy never decreases when a partition is refined. If a pair is not \(\epsilon\)-regular, subsets witnessing its irregularity can be used to split both parts, increasing their contribution to energy by at least an \(\epsilon^4\)-weighted amount.

Starting from the trivial partition, all witnessing subsets for nonregular pairs are used simultaneously to refine the current partition. If a partition with \(k\) parts is not \(\epsilon\)-regular, this produces a refinement in which each original part is divided into at most \(2^k\) pieces, while total energy increases by at least \(\epsilon^5\). Since energy cannot exceed 1, the process stops after at most \(\epsilon^{-5}\) iterations, yielding an \(\epsilon\)-regular partition.

The resulting upper bound on the number of parts is an enormous tower of powers of two. A theorem of Tim Gowers shows that tower-type bounds are substantially unavoidable. To obtain equitable partitions, each refinement step can be followed by limited rebalancing; this may reduce energy slightly, but the net increment remains positive. Equitability cannot generally be imposed only after applying the lemma because \(\epsilon\)-regularity is not preserved under arbitrary refinement.
The Qnap TVS-x73 NAS comes in 4-, 6-, and 8-bay models, featuring an AMD quad-core APU, up to 64GB DDR4, M.2 and PCIe expansion, optional 10GbE, 1,172 MB/s throughput, and 4K playback with dual HDMI.

The Fifth Circuit upheld Mariano Del Cid-Mendez’s illegal-reentry conviction, rejecting his constitutional challenge to 8 U.S.C. § 1326(b) as foreclosed by binding precedent. However, it vacated his sentence because the district court applied mandatory Sentencing Guidelines later held unconstitutional in United States v. Booker, and the Government failed to prove the error harmless. The case was remanded for further proceedings.

Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull urged China to use its leverage to curb North Korea’s nuclear and missile threats. His comments followed a failed North Korean missile test and preceded US Vice President Mike Pence’s visit. China, pressured by Washington but wary of regime collapse, has toughened its stance by suspending North Korean coal imports.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 27, 2015 reported quarterly net sales of $49.6 billion, up 33% year over year, and net income of $10.7 billion, up from $7.7 billion. Diluted earnings per share rose to $1.85 from $1.28. For the first nine months, net sales were $182.2 billion and net income was $42.3 billion.

Quarterly growth was driven by iPhone 6 and 6 Plus, Mac portables, services and the Apple Watch launch. iPhone sales rose 59% to $31.4 billion, with units up 35% to 47.5 million. Mac sales increased 9%, while iPad sales fell 23% and units declined 18%. Greater China sales grew 112% to $13.2 billion. Gross margin was 39.7%, compared with 39.4% a year earlier.

At June 27, 2015, Apple had $273.2 billion in assets, including $202.8 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. Total liabilities were $147.5 billion, including $49.9 billion of long-term borrowings, and shareholders’ equity was $125.7 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow reached $67.8 billion.

During the first nine months, Apple repurchased $22.0 billion of stock, paid $8.6 billion in dividends and issued $21.3 billion of long-term debt. Its board increased the share-repurchase authorization to $140 billion, of which $90 billion had been used.

Apple identified risks involving foreign exchange movements, component supply concentration, outsourced Asian manufacturing, competition, pricing pressure, legal proceedings and tax investigations. The European Commission was investigating alleged Irish state aid, with an impact Apple could not estimate. A $533 million Smartflash damages award was vacated for retrial, while a Samsung judgment was reduced to approximately $548 million and remained subject to further proceedings.

Indian equity markets rose for a fourth consecutive week, supported by normal monsoon forecasts, strong IT earnings, positive global cues and expectations of healthy corporate results. The Sensex gained 0.65% to 34,415.58, while the Nifty50 rose 0.80% to 10,564.05. Lower wholesale inflation also supported sentiment.

Gains were limited by rising crude prices, a weaker rupee, banking-stock selling and expectations of a more hawkish RBI stance. The rupee fell 92 paise to 66.13 per dollar. Foreign institutional investors sold shares worth Rs 2,821.24 crore, while domestic institutions bought Rs 2,124.16 crore.

IT, metals, FMCG and realty led sectoral gains; PSU banks, energy and banking indices declined. TCS rose sharply after robust earnings, pushing its market capitalisation above Rs 6.50 lakh crore.

Southern Illinois defeated Evansville 73-61 after overcoming a nine-point first-half deficit and pulling away late. Ryan Taylor and Jaylon Brown each scored 19 points for Evansville, while Mike Rodriguez led Southern Illinois with 20. Evansville briefly regained the lead in the second half, but an 8-0 Salukis run gave them control, and their advantage reached 15 points. Southern Illinois improved to 11-8 overall and 4-2 in the MVC; Evansville fell to 10-9 and 1-5. Evansville also honored former head coach Jim Crews before the game and at halftime.

The study assessed the relative roles of nine age groups in four Omicron waves in France from March to December 2022 using publicly available ICU admission data. A relative risk statistic compared each age group’s share of admissions before and after each wave’s peak; higher values indicated greater depletion of susceptible individuals during the ascent.

The highest estimates were for ages 10–19 in spring, 0–9 in summer, 10–19 in autumn, and 30–39 in autumn–winter. Adults aged 40–49 also had a high estimate in spring, while those over 80 had a significantly elevated estimate during autumn–winter. Overall, the leading relative role shifted from children and younger adults toward adults aged 30–49 and those over 80.

The authors suggest increasing booster coverage among adults, possibly vaccinating children, and strengthening prevention among elderly people, including in long-term care facilities. Limitations include possible inconsistencies in infection detection and uncertainty about how closely the relative risk statistic reflects transmission roles.
About 400 Brentwood students were sent home after a 9-foot boa constrictor escaped its biology classroom enclosure. The snake was found beneath the floor wrapped around pipes.

Randall Margraves, father of three girls sexually abused by former sports doctor Larry Nassar, lunged at Nassar during a Michigan sentencing hearing after a judge denied his request to be alone with him. Deputies restrained Margraves, who later apologized. Judge Janice Cunningham declined to punish him for contempt but said assault cannot be answered with assault. Prosecutors also urged families to avoid violence. More than 30 victims had spoken during the hearing concerning Nassar’s work at a Michigan gymnastics club. In a previous case involving more than 150 victims, Nassar received up to 175 years in prison, in addition to 60 years for child pornography charges. Cunningham also criticized comments from Nassar’s attorney questioning the number of victims, noting Nassar had disavowed them.

An international team led by Harald Ebeling discovered eMACSJ1341-QG-1, a distant quiescent galaxy magnified 30 times by the galaxy cluster eMACSJ1341.9-2441 through gravitational lensing. The record magnification for this rare galaxy type enables detailed study of its stellar populations, undistorted shape, and properties. Because the galaxy stopped forming stars unusually early, it may offer clues about galaxy evolution. Follow-up observations are underway using telescopes in Chile and on Maunakea, with findings published in the Astrophysical Journal Letters.

Freeport High School recognized students in grades 9–12 for second-quarter High Honors and Honors. North Yarmouth Academy recognized students from The Forecaster’s coverage area in grades 5–12 for first-semester Highest Honors, High Honors and Honors.

Noozhawk founder Bill Macfadyen emphasizes the First Amendment’s importance, particularly freedom of the press, amid criticism of journalism. He says Noozhawk’s independent reporting and defense of the public’s right to know require substantial resources. Thanking advertisers and existing Hawks Club members, he asks the publication’s 21,000 daily readers to financially support expanded Santa Barbara County coverage. Contributions are not tax-deductible because Noozhawk is a for-profit business, but nearly all revenue is reinvested in its news product.

Aston Villa beat Burton Albion 3-2 for a sixth consecutive win, their best run since 1990. Scott Hogan, Albert Adomah and Jack Grealish scored, while an Ahmed Elmohamady own goal and Liam Boyce replied. Villa remain third, one point behind Derby County.

Virginia Chestnuts is a family-owned orchard in Nelson County, Virginia, operated by David and Kim Bryant. Seeking to revive a crop largely lost to blight in the early 1900s, the Bryants planted more than 1,600 blight-resistant American-Chinese hybrid trees after successful tests. Despite harsh weather and cicada damage, the orchard produced a bumper crop in 2015 and at least 3,000 pounds in 2017.

Harvested from mid-September through late October, the chestnuts are collected, sorted, washed, sanitized, dried, and refrigerated before delivery or shipment. Sold shelled or unshelled, they are roasted as snacks and used in breads, stuffing, beer, restaurant dishes, and desserts. Local bakers, brewers, distillers, chefs, and consumers have shown growing interest, driven partly by nostalgia. The Bryants also collaborate with four other Nelson County orchards and promote chestnuts through tastings, events, and social media.

A near-complete skull of Cifelliodon wahkarmoosuch, a small, hairy, egg-laying early mammal relative, was discovered in eastern Utah. Published in Nature, the finding suggests Pangea split about 15 million years later than previously believed, allowing animal migration into the Early Cretaceous. The fossil also indicates early mammal relatives were globally distributed and occupied diverse ecological niches. Found beneath a dinosaur foot fossil from Bureau of Land Management lands, the specimen is displayed at the Natural History Museum of Utah.

A four-year Michigan State University study compared adaptive multi-paddock (AMP) grass-fed cattle systems with grain-fed feedlots. AMP grazing potentially offset greenhouse gas emissions through soil carbon sequestration, while feedlots produced higher emissions, largely from fertilizer-related nitrogen. Feedlots were more productive, producing equal beef on half the land, though improved AMP management outperformed continuous grazing per unit of land. Researchers expect carbon sequestration rates to decline over time but believe managed grazing may offset methane for years. AMP grazing promotes plant recovery, deeper roots, soil organic matter and moisture retention. The study did not advocate one production method, instead identifying improvements for both systems, including reduced fertilizer use and cover crops in feed production. It concluded that environmental stewardship can coexist with cattle production, though AMP systems may imply lower per-capita beef consumption.

TI E2E support forums provide expert design assistance, while contributor-linked content is supplied “as is” and does not represent TI specifications or views. multiSPI and TI E2E are TI trademarks. Integrated circuits require ESD precautions because damage may range from performance degradation to complete failure.

Revision A, dated May 2025, changed ADS8685W and ADS8689W from Advance Information to Production Data. Mechanical, packaging, ordering, material, RoHS, finish, moisture sensitivity, reflow, and marking information is subject to change. Preproduction parts are experimental, may lack completed qualification, and are sold without warranties for early evaluation.

TI provides technical data and design resources “as is,” disclaims warranties, and limits use to developing applications with the described TI products. Developers are responsible for product selection, application testing, validation, and compliance with applicable requirements. TI’s liability for supplied material information is limited to the annual purchase price of the affected parts.

Mumbai Indians retained their playing XI, while Sunrisers Hyderabad made three changes: Shikhar Dhawan returned, Mohammad Nabi made his IPL 2018 debut, and Basil Thampi replaced Billy Stanlake, Ricky Bhui and Deepak Hooda. Stanlake was ruled out of the tournament with a fractured finger. Sunrisers entered after two successive defeats following three wins, while defending champions Mumbai had lost four of five matches and needed a win to improve their playoff prospects. Suryakumar Yadav had been Mumbai’s most consistent batter, with Jasprit Bumrah and Mustafizur Rahman leading the bowling. Kane Williamson had carried Hyderabad’s batting with 230 runs in five games, while Rashid Khan and Shakib Al Hasan were key middle-overs bowlers.

At Leander High School’s 2017 prom, winner Keilany Solano spontaneously gave her crown and sash to fellow nominee Abby Cano, a senior with Down syndrome known for spreading cheer. Solano said Cano deserved the honor and would be happier. Cano’s mother called the gesture amazing and said her daughter had consistently experienced kindness and respect throughout school.

Marvel’s Inhumans episode three, “Divide and Conquer,” airs on ABC at 9 p.m. ET. Following Maximus’s coup, Black Bolt, Medusa and the displaced Royal Family must reunite on Earth. Viewers without cable can stream ABC through Sling TV or DirecTV Now in supported U.S. markets. Sling costs $25 monthly with the required Broadcast Extra add-on and carries ABC in eight markets. DirecTV Now’s cheapest package costs $35 and offers ABC in 39 markets. Both services provide seven-day free trials and support desktop, mobile and various streaming devices.

Samsung Electronics was expected to beat fourth-quarter 2016 earnings forecasts, driven by recovering memory-chip demand. Operating income estimates ranged from $6.5 billion to $7.21 billion, up from $4.31 billion the previous quarter, despite the Galaxy Note 7 discontinuation. Guidance was due Friday.

Larry Connors’ Multiple Days Up/Down strategy applies mean reversion to ETFs. It buys an ETF above its 200-day moving average but below its 5-day moving average after declines on at least four of the previous five trading days. It sells when the ETF closes above its 5-day moving average and uses no stop-loss.

Tests on 20 original and five additional ETFs through December 2020 showed varying performance, with some ETFs apparently unsuitable for mean reversion. A portfolio test from 2000 to 2020 allowed five positions at 20% equity each, compounded without commissions or slippage. The strategy had the lowest profit factor among four referenced Connors mean-reversion strategies.

Trading only SPY and QQQ produced 287 trades, a 1.82 profit factor, 12% maximum drawdown, and 2.4% CAGR, with 7.7% market exposure. Short-side portfolio results were untradeable, though SPY and QQQ shorts achieved a 65% win rate and 0.68% average gain, with much of the profit occurring in 2008. The strategy may improve through asset-specific adjustments and optimization.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full bridge. Devices use a 1.23-V internal bandgap reference divided to 0.613 V for regulation, a transconductance error amplifier, resistor-divider output programming, and capacitor-controlled soft start.

Switching frequency ranges from 100 kHz to 2 MHz and can be set by an RT resistor, an external 200-kHz-to-4-MHz clock, or primary-secondary synchronization. Depending on the device and duty-cycle configuration, controllers provide one or two primary and synchronous-rectifier outputs, each with roughly 150-mA peak capability; external gate drivers are recommended. Programmable features include duty-cycle limits, dead time, leading-edge blanking, slope compensation, frequency compensation, and pulse skipping.

Protection functions include cycle-by-cycle current limiting, capacitor-programmed hiccup restart, external fault shutdown, and thermal shutdown at approximately 175°C with restart below 160°C. A design example describes a 500-kHz synchronous push-pull converter using GaN devices, including component selection for feedback, timing, transformer, FETs, filtering, current sensing, compensation, and protection.

The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require proper bypassing. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switching loops and switch-node area, isolating sensitive feedback and current-sense traces from noisy signals, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, and using short, wide high-current traces. TI states that application guidance must be independently validated and that provided resources are subject to applicable disclaimers and terms.

The Second Circuit affirmed the denial of Rodney Nicholson’s habeas corpus petition challenging his second-degree murder conviction. Nicholson argued that excluding Darnell Phelps’s hearsay confession and denying a new trial violated due process under Chambers v. Mississippi. Assuming Chambers applied, the court found no violation because Phelps’s confession lacked sufficient reliability: it contradicted his earlier denial of knowledge, could not be tested through cross-examination, may have been tailored to public forensic evidence, and did not necessarily exonerate Nicholson. An eyewitness identified Nicholson as the shooter, with some corroboration, and the jury credited her testimony. The court concluded that the state court did not abuse its discretion or deprive Nicholson of fundamental fairness.

Maria Sharapova lost her Wimbledon opener to 132nd-ranked qualifier Vitalia Diatchenko 6-7 (3), 7-6 (3), 6-4 despite repeatedly leading and serving for the match. It was Sharapova’s first opening-round Wimbledon defeat and only her second major-opening loss in 52 matches.

Seven top-10 seeds exited during the first two days, a professional-era record. Two-time champion Petra Kvitova, Caroline Garcia, Sloane Stephens, Elina Svitolina, Dominic Thiem, David Goffin and Grigor Dimitrov were eliminated or withdrew. Kvitova cited nerves and early-round pressure, while Sharapova mentioned the difficult clay-to-grass transition and poor decisions at crucial moments. Top-ranked Simona Halep said grass makes matches unpredictable; she, Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic advanced in straight sets.

Helping Hands Hawaii’s Ready to Learn program will hold its annual school supply drive from June 1 to July 31, 2017, providing free supply kits to low-income and homeless K–12 students. American Savings Bank branches will collect donations June 14 to July 14, with donations remaining on their respective islands. Supporters may donate supplies or money, organize drives, or volunteer to pack kits. Each kit is valued at about $10 and includes common classroom essentials. As of April 2017, the program had raised over $12,000 and assembled 3,115 kits, benefiting more than 6,000 students. Applicants must be referred by a case manager from a participating social service organization by June 23, 2017.

Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) and customer co-signing are disabled by default and require BIOS configuration.
