During early boot, BIOS may provide the AMD Security Processor (ASP) with a customer RSA public key. Co-signed packages are verified first against the customer key and then AMD’s key, enabling separation between test and production systems. Customers use 2048- or 4096-bit RSA keys with specified RSA-PSS schemes.

Patches verify applicable system patch levels and firmware versions before execution. Packages may modify registers, replace firmware images, or update firmware components. All package components must validate before any update is applied, and dependencies must be checked to avoid inconsistent firmware. SFS updates are non-persistent across reboots and may be reapplied during boot or system operation.

SFS commands use a 2 MB-aligned TEE extended command buffer. The deployment agent optionally appends a co-signing header and signature to the AMD package, then submits its physical address through ASP mailbox registers. The ASP protects the memory from x86 access, verifies customer and AMD signatures, executes the patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status. Firmware and patch versions can be queried through a two-page command buffer.

SEV updates are committed automatically and require reboot to revert. With SNP enabled, update pages must be marked HV-FIXED. Packages follow an AGESA-aligned naming scheme and apply only to specified firmware and patch-level combinations. Updates run alongside x86 and DMA traffic with minimal intended performance impact. SEV or SEV/ES virtual machines must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

Members of Congress continue receiving salaries during government shutdowns because the Constitution guarantees compensation and congressional pay is funded through mandatory spending. Rep. Angie Craig proposed temporarily docking lawmakers’ pay, though the money would be returned to comply with the 27th Amendment. Federal workers may miss paychecks during a prolonged shutdown but are guaranteed retroactive pay under a 2019 law. Funding expires Tuesday amid partisan disputes over Medicaid cuts and Affordable Care Act tax credits.

A pipe bomb strapped to 27-year-old Akayed Ullah exploded in a crowded subway passage near Times Square during Monday morning rush hour, injuring him and three others. Officials described it as an attempted terror attack and said Ullah was inspired by the Islamic State group but apparently had no direct contact with it. The low-tech device was attached with Velcro and plastic ties. All injuries were non-life-threatening. The blast prompted a large emergency response, evacuations, area shutdowns, and major subway, bus, and traffic disruptions around the Port Authority terminal. President Donald Trump was briefed on the incident.

Amazon.com filed a Form 8-K on April 29, 2021, announcing its first-quarter 2021 financial results. The filing incorporates a press release, information regarding non-GAAP financial measures, and an Inline XBRL cover page. CFO Brian T. Olsavsky signed the report.
The speaker praises an unnamed penalty killer’s defensive skill, Evgeni’s health and urgency, and Zetterberg’s consistency, intelligence, and all-around danger.

STAT’s Morning Rounds highlights that without congressional government funding by September 30, 2025, Medicare patients receiving hospital-level care at home must be discharged or returned to hospitals. The passage also lists recent health, medicine, biotech, and public-policy headlines.

Around 200 people gathered in Nottingham’s market square to remember 18-year-old student Mariam Moustafa, who died following an attack outside the intu Victoria Centre. Her family, friends, teachers and community members called for justice, an end to violence and solidarity across nationalities and backgrounds. The vigil was organised by Nottingham Stand Up To Racism and the Nottingham People’s Assembly.

The coach expressed confidence in his staff but emphasized that players determine outcomes on the ice. He praised the team for playing within its strengths, defending hard, simplifying the game, and making sacrifices such as taking hits and blocking shots. The team has improved through stronger effort, smarter play, and better execution rather than a new game plan. Players respect “Cully” and recognize the significance of their opportunity, but the group remains focused only on the next game. The coach stressed controlling what is controllable, following established routines, and maintaining commitment, discipline, and execution. Despite heightened scrutiny, players and coaches will rely on their usual process and aim to perform at their best.

Tesla delivered a record 497,099 vehicles in Q3 2025, up 7.4% year over year and exceeding forecasts, as U.S. buyers rushed to secure a $7,500 tax credit before its expiration. Incentives also boosted demand but may have pulled sales forward, complicating Tesla’s goal of 1.61 million annual deliveries. Sales weakened in Europe and the UK amid stronger competition. Investor reaction remained muted over sustainability concerns. Tesla also delivered a record 12.5 GWh of energy storage capacity, which could help offset slower automotive growth.

The National Beer Wholesalers Association launched DeliveringLocalJobs.com to highlight 135,000 beer distribution employees across all 50 states. These workers earn $11.2 billion in wages, contribute $70 billion to U.S. GDP, create nearly $180 million in community impacts and generate nearly $13 billion in tax revenue. Through videos, employee profiles and state economic data, the site showcases distribution careers, brand-building efforts and work with more than 5,000 brewers and importers.

Arizona Cardinals quarterback Carson Palmer, 37, revived his career after joining Arizona in 2013 and posted career highs during a 13-win 2015 season. His performance declined in 2016 as the Cardinals finished 7-8-1, raising questions about a rebound. Palmer said he evaluates his health and future after each season but intends to continue playing while healthy and enjoying the game. He believes reduced expectations and the team’s underdog status will ease pressure and allow greater focus on preparation.

Coach Sutter said no former teammate or player immediately compared to the player discussed. He described entering coaching after he could no longer play, advancing through the minors and organizational roles. He called Brown central to the team’s identity and praised his playoff success after a disappointing regular season. Sutter emphasized that championship opportunities are rare and require sacrifice. He expressed pride in his brothers’ six championships. He said home-game distractions provided an organizational lesson and stressed that his team responds rather than retreats. He praised special plays by Nash and Drew Doughty. Although the team’s core remained, he identified five significant players without Stanley Cup Final experience who still required evaluation. Sutter said he quickly moved past a Game 7 loss, selected lineups solely to maximize the chance of winning, and accepted the coaching role because he believed the team could contend for a championship.

The UC1825B-SP is a dual-output controller supporting push-pull, forward, half-bridge, and full-bridge converters, with voltage- or current-mode operation. Its sawtooth oscillator uses RT to set maximum duty cycle and CT to set frequency; recommended RT values are 1–100 kΩ, and duty cycles below 70% are discouraged. The reference push-pull design uses 215 kHz switching, 10-kΩ RT, 680-pF CT, 30% duty cycle, a 2.2 transformer turns ratio, 1.5 auxiliary-winding ratio, 120-µH primary inductance, and a 2.2-µH output inductor.

The design limits magnetizing current to 6% and employs an RCD switch-node clamp, with a recommended clamp factor of 1.5 and an initial 10% clamp-voltage variation. The output diode is rated at 60 V, while push-pull MOSFETs should be rated about 2.5–3 times the input voltage. Approximately 1145 µF of output capacitance, a 500-nH filter inductor, and a 0.5-Ω damping resistor reduce ripple. Type IIB compensation targets a 5-kHz crossover, and a current-sense resistor provides cycle shutdown near the CS pin’s 1-V threshold.

The controller operates from a regulated 10–30 V supply; remote supplies may require about 100 µF of additional bulk capacitance. PCB guidance emphasizes low-EMI inductors, short and thick power traces, separated signal and power grounds, ground planes, close bypass and compensation components, and unidirectional switching-current loops. VCC and VREF require direct high-frequency ceramic bypassing to their respective grounds. The device requires ESD precautions, and TI states that design resources are provided “as is” for skilled developers responsible for application validation and compliance.

Andy overcame injuries to become a key physical playoff contributor. Against Vancouver, the team must control emotions, withstand an aggressive start and remain focused despite the hostile crowd. A new Newfoundland team is expected to benefit from strong local hockey passion, attract fans and support the economy.

Microsoft reported fiscal 2023 second-quarter revenue of $52.7 billion, up from $51.7 billion a year earlier. Operating income declined to $20.4 billion from $22.2 billion, net income fell to $16.4 billion from $18.8 billion, and diluted earnings per share decreased to $2.20 from $2.48. For the six months ended December 31, 2022, revenue was $102.9 billion and net income was $34.0 billion.

Microsoft Cloud quarterly revenue rose 22% to $27.1 billion. Intelligent Cloud revenue increased to $21.5 billion, Productivity and Business Processes to $17.0 billion, while More Personal Computing declined to $14.2 billion. Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 31%; Windows OEM and Devices revenue each fell 39%, and Xbox content and services declined 12%.

At December 31, 2022, Microsoft had $364.6 billion in assets, $99.5 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments, and $183.1 billion in stockholders’ equity. Six-month operating cash flow was $34.4 billion. Microsoft repurchased $9.2 billion of shares during the first half and declared dividends totaling $1.36 per share.

Microsoft recorded $800 million in severance expense related to plans announced January 18, 2023, to eliminate approximately 10,000 jobs. A change extending server and network equipment useful lives from four to six years increased quarterly operating income by $945 million and net income by $768 million.

The company completed its $18.8 billion Nuance acquisition in March 2022 and continued seeking regulatory approval for its proposed $68.7 billion Activision Blizzard acquisition. Deloitte reported no material modifications were needed for the interim financial statements.

The Bollinger Band Squeeze is a breakout strategy that follows price direction after a low-volatility period. Bollinger Bands consist of a moving average and upper and lower bands based on standard deviations. Contracting bands indicate declining volatility and a potential breakout, while expanding bands reflect higher volatility.

Backtests across numerous assets and strategy variations produced little success. On Pepsi, the strategy returned 12.5% while invested 61% of the time, compared with a 14.8% buy-and-hold return. Consumer staples showed relatively better results, but the authors concluded that other indicators perform better and warned against relying on anecdotal evidence.

As a breakout approach, the strategy generally has a lower win rate and is vulnerable to whipsaws. Its effectiveness depends on the asset and market conditions; stocks tend toward mean reversion, while commodities behave differently. Traders may combine it with indicators such as RSI or IBS, but any version should be backtested for positive expectancy. Common mistakes include using a strategy without positive expectancy and failing to follow validated rules because of trading biases. Mechanical trading is suggested to reduce these problems.

Bollinger Bands were developed by financial analyst John A. Bollinger in the 1980s, reflecting his focus on volatility and adaptable trading bands.

Hammerson rejected Klépierre’s preliminary £4.88bn cash-and-share proposal, which valued it at 615p per share, saying it significantly undervalued the company. Hammerson shares rose about 25% to 545p following the news. The company remains committed to acquiring Intu Properties, expecting portfolio improvements and £25m in annual synergies. Although Hammerson trades below book value and offers a near-5% forward dividend yield, weakness in the retail property sector remains a concern, leading the author to avoid the shares for now.

Amid interrupted communications and fears surrounding the Tong Hâk movement, Augustine Heard reported uncertainty about the danger but believed the King was alarmed. After Heard advised Admiral Harmony that sending a ship would be prudent, the U.S.S. Petrel arrived at Chemulpo. Heard persuaded Commander Dayton to remain temporarily. Two Chinese ironclads and two Japanese warships were also present. Heard requested 600 cartridges for previously received rifles.

A royal order condemned people allegedly misled by heterodox ideas, directed authorities to arrest the movement’s leaders, prohibit its spread, disperse assemblies, and enforce the law under threat of punishment for official inaction. It urged peaceful conduct and declared that loyal subjects should uphold patriotism and filial piety, even sacrificing their lives for their King or parents during times of danger.

Dan Le Batard said the Heat believed LeBron James knew he was leaving and “checked out” during their 2014 NBA Finals loss, despite strong statistics. With James potentially leaving Cleveland and the Cavaliers facing long odds against Golden State, the passage questions whether a similar situation could arise in 2018.

Pedro Russell and fellow MBA graduates Garrison Jones and Stephen McGarvey founded GPS Partners, a search fund targeting for-profit medical technical schools. They identified MedPro Institute, a reputable vocational school near Boston founded by Dr. Samantha Hill, as a potential acquisition. MedPro offers medical assisting, phlebotomy, medical billing and coding, and dental assisting certificate programs, emphasizing practical training, small classes, high graduation rates, and strong job placement.

During due diligence, Russell found that MedPro relied mainly on word of mouth rather than advertising, presenting an opportunity to increase enrollment through greater visibility. However, he needed to understand how growth would affect costs. Major expenses included square-footage-based rent, daily cleaning fees, per-class instructor pay, salaries for two career services employees, fixed accreditation costs, disposable supplies, insurance with fixed and per-student components, usage-based internet fees capped monthly, and metered electricity.

Russell recalled that evaluating additional enrollment requires analyzing how costs respond to resource utilization and how resource usage changes with student volume. Cost-volume graphs could help visualize these relationships. GPS needed to assess whether MedPro could balance enrollment growth with financial sustainability before deciding whether to proceed with the acquisition.

Bitcoin rose about 2% Friday to $123,874, roughly 1% below its record high, and gained 12% for the week as investors sought decentralized assets during the U.S. government shutdown. Standard Chartered expects Bitcoin to reach a new high and eventually $135,000. Gold, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq also advanced.

Butterfield reported a strong first quarter of 2018, with core return on average tangible common equity rising to 24.3% and net interest margin increasing 18 basis points sequentially to 3.05%. Net interest income rose $3.8 million to $79.9 million, while non-interest income declined 6.1% from a seasonally strong fourth quarter. Core expenses were $76 million, and the core efficiency ratio was 62.3%, moving toward the bank’s 60% target.

Total assets reached approximately $11 billion, average deposits increased to $9.8 billion, and loans grew about $180 million to $4 billion, driven by a sovereign loan, U.K. residential mortgages, and commercial lending. Non-accrual loans declined to $42.4 million, while the net charge-off ratio was 2 basis points. The $4.5 billion investment portfolio remained predominantly AAA-rated.

The bank completed Deutsche Bank’s Global Trust Solutions acquisition, adding operations in Singapore and Mauritius and integrating businesses in Cayman, Guernsey, and Switzerland. Its planned acquisition of Deutsche Bank banking operations in Cayman and the Channel Islands is expected to close by year-end and could increase deposits by up to 20%. Management continues to seek disciplined acquisitions in offshore banking, trust, and wealth management.

The Basel III total capital ratio was 19.2%, and common equity represented 6.7% of assets. The board raised the quarterly dividend to $0.38 per share. No shares were repurchased during the quarter, though a repurchase authorization became effective April 1.

Management expects continued net interest margin support from rising rates and asset repricing, partly offset by lower-yielding U.K. mortgages and additional liquidity from acquisitions. Deposit pricing pressure remained limited. Expense levels should benefit from declining first-year compliance and other temporary costs, although acquired operations will add ongoing expenses.

The speaker regrets the play that contributed to the loss but refuses to dwell on it. RolI’s strong play and injury are unfortunate, yet they create an opportunity for another goaltender in the Stanley Cup Finals. Despite a rocky season and limited game action, the speaker trusts his preparation, confidence, teammates, and ability to regain game rhythm quickly. He believes either available goalie can win four games. RolI will continue helping by sharing observations about shooters and game tendencies.

Sen. Cory Booker campaigned in Alabama for Democratic Senate nominee Doug Jones, while also raising his profile among African-American voters who could be crucial in a potential 2020 presidential bid. Jones generally discouraged national Democrats from campaigning in the state, but welcomed Congressional Black Caucus members because his prospects depended partly on black turnout. Former Gov. Deval Patrick also appeared, while Sen. Kamala Harris supported Jones through fundraising and donations.

Deep South states play an important role in Democratic primaries because of their large black electorates and early voting dates. Hillary Clinton’s strong African-American support in 2016 produced substantial delegate advantages across the region, while Barack Obama similarly relied on black voters in 2008. Booker emphasized his family ties to Alabama and deflected calls of “Booker 2020,” noting his Senate reelection that year. Some Alabama voters praised his visit but said they would continue assessing him.

The Second Circuit reviewed an $89,841.75 income-tax deficiency assessed against the petitioner for 1931. The principal issue was whether preferred stock distributed as a dividend to common shareholders was exempt under section 115(f) of the Revenue Act of 1928, which stated that “a stock dividend shall not be subject to tax.”

The petitioner received preferred shares worth $629,125 in 1931. The Board of Tax Appeals held the distribution taxable. The Second Circuit reversed, reasoning that section 115(f)’s unqualified language, its legislative history, Treasury interpretations, and relevant decisions supported exemption of all stock dividends, including stock of a class different from the underlying shares. Congress later expressly taxed different-class stock dividends in the Revenue Act of 1936.

The court declined to treat $200,000 received from redemption of preferred shares as capital gain or as the equivalent of a taxable dividend because those issues were not properly raised, decided, or cross-appealed.

Judge L. Hand dissented. He argued that Congress exempted stock dividends only because it believed *Eisner v. Macomber* required exemption. Since preferred shares issued on common shares created substantially new rights and constituted income, he considered the distribution taxable and would have affirmed the Board.

Google canceled the Daily Stormer’s domain registration for violating policies against inciting violence, shortly after GoDaddy ordered the neo-Nazi site to leave over an article ridiculing Heather Heyer, who was killed protesting a Charlottesville white-nationalist rally. YouTube terminated the site’s channel for hate speech, while Facebook said it removes Daily Stormer links unless shared with clear condemnation. Other web-service companies distanced themselves, although the site’s actual host remained unclear. The actions reflect growing pressure on technology companies to balance free speech with restrictions on hateful or violent content.

The IRS furloughed about 34,000 workers during the government shutdown, closing most operations. Another 39,870 employees, or 53.6% of its workforce, remain working. Non-exempt employees entered unpaid, non-duty status beginning October 8, 2025, until further notice.

Whitmore secured a promissory note with a deed of trust. After his death, the creditor failed to present its claim within the statutory probate period but sought to sell the secured land. Whitmore’s executors obtained an injunction, which the defendants appealed.

The California Supreme Court held that failure to timely present a probate claim bars the remedy against the estate but does not extinguish the underlying debt. Because the debt remained unpaid, equity would not compel surrender of the security or prevent its sale without payment. The judgment was reversed with directions to sustain the defendants’ demurrer.

Justice Crockett, joined by Justice McKinstry, dissented. He argued that failure to present the claim eliminated the lien, and allowing enforcement of the trust deed would disrupt probate administration and prejudice creditors who timely presented claims.

Transport CS James Macharia blamed poor enforcement by NTSA and other agencies for disorder in Kenya’s boda boda industry. He said the ministry is collaborating with county transport committees and traffic authorities to implement existing regulations. Ruiru MP Simon King’ara proposed a dedicated motorbike safety authority, urged action against enforcement delays, opposed city-centre bans, and recommended benchmarking with Rwanda.

Matthew James Phelps, 29, faces first-degree murder charges after his wife Lauren, 29, was fatally stabbed at their North Carolina home on September 1. Phelps told 911 he had taken excessive Coricidin cough medicine, dreamed, and awoke covered in blood beside a knife, believing the medicine caused him to kill her. Investigators seized red-stained bedding, an empty Coricidin box, electronics, financial documents, a knife set and Lauren’s phone. Phelps, who had no criminal record, is being held without bail. The couple had been married less than a year.

The study reviews European public financing instruments for cleantech start-ups and SMEs, many linked to Horizon 2020. Financing commonly includes loans and equity, with some grants and guarantees, targeting fields such as energy efficiency, smart cities, ICT, renewable energy, and healthcare. Major managers include the EIB, EIF, EBRD, EUREKA, and European Commission. Instruments are benchmarked by funding metrics, eligibility, monitoring, and application processes. Many also provide coaching, advisory, commercialization, intellectual property, management, R&D, and acceleration support.

The speaker calls on Washington citizens to aid victims of catastrophic flooding in Johnstown, Williamsport, and nearby Pennsylvania communities. He emphasizes national brotherhood and charity, noting Jacksonville’s $2,000 contribution. Citing urgent reports of thousands left hungry, homeless, and penniless, he proposes committees to collect and quickly send food, gather clothing and bedding, and raise money for rebuilding homes. He urges the national capital to respond generously and notes that he has already sent his own subscription to Johnstown’s mayor.

The passage describes bonded optical devices for high-resolution displays in wearable electronics, augmented and mixed reality systems, projection systems, vehicle heads-up displays, smart watches, and phones. Monochromatic red, green, and blue microLED arrays are bonded to silicon, CMOS, TFT, glass, or other carrier elements containing circuitry that independently controls emitters. Direct or hybrid bonding can connect dielectric surfaces and conductive pads without adhesive through die-to-die, die-to-wafer, or wafer-to-wafer processes, enabling pixel pitches below 5 microns and potentially below 1 micron.

Separate monochromatic optical elements may be arranged parallel, angled, or laterally offset. Mirrors, beam splitters, lenses, and waveguides combine their outputs into a superimposed multicolor image delivered to a user. Optical elements may also be directly bonded or adhesively attached to waveguides. Pixel-isolation trenches can reduce optical crosstalk between individual pixels or pixel matrices, while processor circuitry controls brightness and image generation.

The disclosed configurations avoid separately placing millions of individual LEDs, potentially improving manufacturability. Proposed devices include independently controllable emitter arrays, processor backplanes, optical pathways, redirection elements, and optional red, green, and blue optical elements. Bond interfaces may include directly bonded dielectric regions and metal contacts, with surface activation, polishing, and annealing used to form covalent and metal-to-metal bonds.

Tennessee National Wildlife Refuge’s headquarters and Visitor Center will close August 21 for the solar eclipse. Visitors are directed to Cross Creeks National Wildlife Refuge for totality, lasting about 55 seconds. Staff will assist with parking and information. Viewing glasses, shirts, and water will be sold; visitors may bring picnics but must avoid blocking roads, gates, or fields.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture advances Turing with doubled peak FP32 throughput, larger and faster unified L1/shared memory, second-generation RT Cores, and third-generation Tensor Cores. Each SM can execute 128 FP32 operations per clock or 64 FP32 and 64 INT32 operations, while supporting concurrent graphics, compute, and ray-tracing workloads. Ampere GPUs are stated to be up to 1.9 times more power-efficient than Turing at equal performance.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and add hardware acceleration for ray-traced motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32, BF16, FP16, INT8, INT4, and structured sparsity, which can double matrix throughput by skipping zero values. These capabilities accelerate AI features such as denoising and DLSS, including 8K upscaling.

GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, reaching up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/s. RTX IO works with Microsoft DirectStorage to move compressed data from SSDs to GPU memory for GPU-based decompression, reducing CPU use and improving loading and streaming performance.

The architecture supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 4K at 120 Hz, and 8K at 60 Hz. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware AV1 decoding up to 8K60 HDR, while seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

Products based on GA10x include GeForce RTX 30-series GPUs, the data-center-focused NVIDIA A40, and the professional RTX A6000. The RTX 3090 includes 24 GB of GDDR6X, while the A40 and A6000 offer 48 GB configurations expandable to 96 GB through NVLink. GA10x also adds GDDR6X Error Detection and Replay to identify and retry faulty memory transmissions during overclocking.

William Brock was convicted of molesting three-year-old B.G. and sentenced to ten years at hard labor. B.G.’s mother testified that the child complained of pain, said Brock had touched her private area, and appeared frightened and withdrawn around him. A physician found vaginal redness and an abrasion likely caused by digital manipulation and ruled out self-infliction. Testimony established that Brock frequently supervised the child and that no other man had an opportunity to abuse her.

Brock appealed, arguing insufficient evidence and an excessive sentence. Applying the standard that evidence be viewed in the prosecution’s favor, the court found sufficient proof that Brock committed a lewd act for sexual gratification while exercising control or supervision over B.G. It also held that the trial court properly considered aggravating and mitigating factors, including the harm caused, the seriousness of the offense, and Brock’s lack of an apparent criminal record. Because the ten-year sentence was five years below the statutory maximum and within the trial court’s discretion, the conviction and sentence were affirmed.

The Colorado Supreme Court held that the district court lacked personal jurisdiction over defendants served in California under a rule permitting out-of-state service only on Colorado residents. Uncontroverted evidence showed the defendants had abandoned Colorado, settled in Ventura, obtained employment and California licenses, registered to vote, and intended to establish permanent residence there. Because plaintiffs failed to prove Colorado residency, the service was invalid. The Court exercised original jurisdiction, emphasizing its duty to prevent lower courts from proceeding without jurisdiction, and made the rule prohibiting further proceedings absolute.

This cross-sectional survey examined culturally sensitive mentorship needs among 133 entry-level occupational therapy students at one urban private university; 59 identified as historically underrepresented. Although 89.5% had experienced mentorship, only 34% currently had a mentor. Students valued mentors’ personality, relevant expertise, availability, shared interests, cultural humility, awareness of bias, empathy, anti-racism allyship, and guidance for handling discrimination and microaggressions. BIPOC students placed greater importance on mentors acknowledging bias, while Hispanic/Latinx students reported lower mentor effectiveness across cultural differences and in integrating personal and academic responsibilities.

Students also sought regular communication and practical support with clinical skills, certification preparation, networking, employment, work-life balance, confidence, and transitions into practice. The findings support flexible programs combining formal and informal mentorship, diverse mentor networks, cultural sensitivity training, and institutional resources. Such programs could strengthen belonging, resilience, inclusion, and professional preparation. Limitations include the single-institution, cross-sectional sample, lack of data on students’ program stage, and limited consideration of intersecting identities beyond race and ethnicity.

Centrica’s shares fell 35% over the past year, lifting its dividend yield to 8.6%. Despite regulatory uncertainty and business-model changes, its P/E ratio of around 10 and forecast 7% earnings growth may offer turnaround potential, though volatility and limited dividend growth remain risks. Ventilation supplier Volution reported 11.6% revenue growth and a 6.7% increase in adjusted operating profit to £18.3m, alongside its acquisition of New Zealand supplier Simx. Volution yields 2.2%, but strong dividend coverage and forecast profit growth could support faster payouts.

European markets reached record highs as the STOXX 600 rose about 0.5%, driven by steelmakers and banks. Proposed cuts to tariff-free steel import quotas boosted domestic producers, while stable bond yields and improving credit margins supported banks. Auto stocks lagged after BMW reduced its 2025 profit forecast due to U.S. tariffs and weaker Chinese demand. Expectations of future Federal Reserve easing strengthened risk appetite and helped gold exceed $4,000 per ounce. Analysts cited resilient industrial production and corporate earnings but warned that persistent inflation, trade tensions, or changing monetary policy expectations could pressure valuations.

The study examined pre-service teachers’ attitudes and opinions regarding the Research Methods in Education (RME) course and whether attitudes differed by department or grade level. Using a sequential explanatory mixed-method design, quantitative data were collected online from 190 Bayburt University Faculty of Education students in Turkish, English, and pre-school teaching programs. Qualitative data came from a focus group of 10 purposively selected participants.

The researcher developed a 21-item, five-point Likert attitude scale covering contribution to the profession, self-confidence, and contribution to daily and professional life. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported the three-factor structure, and the overall scale had a Cronbach alpha of .920. Because attitude scores were not normally distributed, Kruskal-Wallis H and Mann-Whitney U tests were used. Focus-group responses were analyzed through content analysis.

Attitudes did not differ significantly by academic department but differed by grade level, specifically between first- and fourth-year students, with fourth-year students having higher ranks. Contribution to daily life had the highest subdimension averages. In the focus group, nine of ten participants considered the course necessary, particularly for understanding scientific research, supporting other courses, graduate study, and professional projects. Participants reported personal, scientific-research, and professional gains. Six participants said course time was insufficient, while others emphasized the influence of teaching methods and problems involving software, materials, or licenses.

The study recommends providing prerequisite knowledge before RME, offering the course in the third or fourth year after measurement and evaluation, making it compulsory, and increasing its duration or dividing it into RME 1 and RME 2.

The Sensex slipped 12.31 points to 28,339.31, while Nifty fell 0.14% to 8,792. Five stocks reached new 52-week highs. AIA Engineering hit Rs 1,441 after reporting 17.6% profit growth and declaring a Rs 4 interim dividend, closing 2.02% higher. Alkem Laboratories, supported by a 24.9% profit increase and 30.1% growth in US sales, closed 2.03% higher at Rs 1,874. KEC International reached Rs 170 but closed 3.85% lower. Exide Industries touched Rs 218 before closing 0.81% down, despite receiving a buy rating with a Rs 230 target. Kalpataru Power Transmission rose to Rs 299.85 amid unusually high volumes but closed marginally lower at Rs 290.05.

In his final press conference, President George W. Bush thanked the press corps and reflected on his presidency. He said he would request the remaining $350 billion in financial rescue funds only if President-elect Barack Obama asked him to do so. Bush praised Obama, wished him success, and said he would largely withdraw from public attention after leaving office.

Bush supported a sustainable Gaza cease-fire requiring Hamas to stop rocket attacks and weapons smuggling, while affirming Israel’s right to defend itself and urging protection of civilians and humanitarian aid. He defended the two-state solution and said extremist violence remained a major obstacle to Middle East peace.

He identified an attack on the United States as the most urgent security threat and called North Korea and Iran continuing dangers. He urged the Republican Party to become more inclusive, compassionate, and open to differing views, particularly on immigration.

Defending his record, Bush cited the Iraq troop surge, tax cuts, and emergency actions to prevent financial collapse. He acknowledged setting aside free-market principles because advisers warned of a possible depression. He identified the “Mission Accomplished” banner, some rhetoric, and prioritizing Social Security over immigration reform as mistakes, while describing Abu Ghraib and the absence of Iraqi weapons of mass destruction as major disappointments.

Bush rejected claims that America’s moral standing had broadly declined, defended post-September 11 security policies, and opposed protectionism. He said New Orleans reconstruction remained incomplete but defended the federal rescue response to Hurricane Katrina. He described Obama’s election as evidence of racial progress while acknowledging more work remained.

Bush concluded by expressing disappointment with Washington’s hostile rhetoric and hoping Obama’s critics would treat him respectfully.

Shares of U.S. rare earth and critical mineral miners surged after China tightened export controls, including licensing requirements for products containing rare earths and those using Chinese extraction, refining or recycling technology. The restrictions came before an expected Xi-Trump meeting and intensified speculation that Washington will further invest in domestic supply chains. The Trump administration has already taken equity stakes in several miners, while industry leaders argue resilient supplies are vital to U.S. economic and national security.

Royal Rumble 2017 at San Antonio’s Alamodome aims to draw over 60,000 fans, with Goldberg, Brock Lesnar and John Cena confirmed. The Undertaker is expected, while Shawn Michaels may appear in a non-wrestling role. Confirmed matches include WWE Champion AJ Styles defending against Cena, who seeks a record-tying 16th world championship, and Universal Champion Kevin Owens facing Roman Reigns, with Chris Jericho suspended above the ring in a shark cage to prevent interference. Goldberg and Lesnar are announced for the 30-man Royal Rumble match, with Braun Strowman, The Undertaker and Finn Balor among other possible participants.

Bath Rugby fans faced days of travel disruption after their team’s 24-20 Champions Cup defeat by Toulon. Snow, ice and wind caused widespread flight cancellations and diversions across southern England and northern Europe, particularly affecting routes from Marseille, Nice and Amsterdam.

Supporters sought alternative routes through European cities or by train, often encountering further delays, cancellations and booking errors. Some had to take extra leave, extend pet or childcare arrangements, or risk missing the funeral of fellow supporter Mike Grice. Flights were diverted to Bournemouth and Cardiff, while rail problems also hindered journeys.

The Bath team returned to Bristol on a chartered flight on Sunday. Despite the disruption and match result, several stranded fans praised the players and Toulon supporters, while others made the most of extended stays in France.

Sergei Fedorov describes seven months away from hockey during prolonged contract negotiations. Selection for Russia’s Olympic team helped him regain physical and mental readiness. After receiving an offer from North Carolina, he hoped Detroit would match it because of his history with the Red Wings and attachment to the city. Detroit matched the offer, allowing him to reunite with teammates and begin rebuilding his relationship with fans. Despite exhaustion and travel from Japan, he returned immediately, recognizing that his priority was to play and perform well. He also recalls the inspiration of seeing Vladi at the Stanley Cup celebration, speaking to him in Russian and sharing the team’s joy with him.

On December 12, 2016, NVIDIA entered an agreement with Goldman Sachs to terminate 63,259,180.62 outstanding common-stock warrants issued under two 2013 transactions. NVIDIA will compensate Goldman with common shares, with the amount determined daily using volume-weighted average prices from December 13, 2016, through January 31, 2017. The shares are exempt from registration under Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act.

The Bank of England allocated £5.085 billion through its six-month repo operation, the highest since March 2020 and more than double the previous week. The increase reflects growing demand for central bank liquidity as the BoE unwinds quantitative easing and shifts banks from excess reserves toward secured borrowing. Demand remains far below the record £87.149 billion allotted through its seven-day facility.

Constraint Programming is effective for combinatorial problems but difficult to model manually, especially with global constraints. Constraint Acquisition automates model learning through passive examples, active oracle queries, or hybrid methods. Passive learning can over-fit limited examples, while active learning may require excessive queries. Existing hybrid approaches lack dedicated mechanisms for correcting over-fitted global constraints.

The proposed Hybrid CA with Refinement framework addresses this problem in three phases. First, passive learning detects candidate global constraints, including AllDifferent, Sum, and Count, from positive examples and removes fixed-arity candidates inconsistent with those examples. Candidates may still reflect coincidental patterns, such as an unnecessary diagonal AllDifferent constraint inferred from a few Sudoku solutions.

Second, Query-Driven Interactive Refinement evaluates global candidates using oracle interaction. Each candidate receives an initial confidence score from a pretrained machine-learning classifier. The system prioritizes low-confidence constraints, generates targeted queries, and updates confidence using Bayesian evidence. Constraints crossing an acceptance threshold are retained, while rejected constraints are removed. Subset Exploration attempts to preserve useful structure from rejected constraints by creating smaller-scope versions through removal of selected variables while retaining constraint type and parameters. Query budgets are dynamically allocated, pooled from accepted candidates, or transferred to generated subsets.

Third, an established active-learning algorithm uses the refined global constraints and pruned fixed-arity bias to learn remaining constraints and complete the model. The framework extends earlier hybrid and AllDifferent-focused work to additional global constraints while adding learned priors, adaptive budget management, and subset exploration. Reported experiments on diverse benchmarks found high accuracy and target-model coverage from limited examples with manageable query complexity.

The Keltner Channel, created by commodity trader Chester W. Keltner in the 1960s, is a volatility-based technical analysis tool for identifying trends, reversals, breakouts, and overbought or oversold conditions. It consists of a central moving average and upper and lower bands typically calculated by adding and subtracting a multiple of Average True Range (ATR). The bands expand and contract with volatility.

Unlike Bollinger Bands, which use standard deviation and respond more sharply to changes, Keltner Channels use ATR. Common settings include a 20-period exponential moving average and an ATR multiplier of 2, though settings should be adapted and backtested for each market and trading style.

Traders may use channel breaches for momentum or breakout trades, or trade against them as a mean-reversion strategy. The channels can also indicate support, resistance, entry, and exit areas in swing trading and scalping. A Bollinger squeeze within a Keltner Channel signals low volatility and possible consolidation before a breakout.

One S&P 500 backtest reported 288 trades, a 77% win rate, 6.3% CAGR, 15% market exposure, and a profit factor of 2. A momentum variation produced 143 trades and a 3.6% CAGR. Results vary with market conditions, discipline, risk management, and settings. Traders should avoid relying exclusively on the indicator and should combine it with broader market analysis and risk controls.

The study examined perceived research expectations for U.S. mathematics education faculty and how they vary by institution type, department, and time assigned to research. Researchers surveyed faculty identified through mathematics education publications; 404 complete responses from the target population were analyzed using frequencies, multinomial logistic regressions, and post-hoc comparisons.

Respondents typically devoted 20–40% of their time to research and were expected to publish an average of 1.64 papers annually. Research journal articles were consistently the most valued output. Books, chapters, practitioner articles, and conference proceedings generally counted somewhat, while textbook value lacked consensus. Presentations were commonly required, external funding was often valued, and professional development was generally neither required nor highly valued. First authorship was considered important.

Expectations differed most by Carnegie classification. R1 faculty typically devoted 40% of their time to research and were expected to publish 2.25 papers annually, compared with 1.5 at R2 institutions and 1 at other institutions. R1 faculty faced stronger expectations for presentations, external funding, and sole authorship, but non-journal publications were less valued. R2 institutions were most likely to state publication targets explicitly in written documents. Faculty at other institutions typically had lower research commitments and fewer funding expectations.

Each 10% increase in research time corresponded to 0.184 additional expected papers. Higher research commitments were associated with greater emphasis on funding and authorship and less value for books, practitioner articles, and professional development. Departmental differences were limited: mathematics departments expected 0.309 fewer papers than education departments, valued conference proceedings and funding more, and placed less emphasis on presentations, professional development, and first authorship.

The authors recommend clearer written expectations specifying publication quantities, the relative value of publication types and scholarly activities, and whether particular activities are required.

Government shutdowns have historically had limited economic and market effects, with estimated GDP losses of about 0.1 percentage point per week typically recovered later. However, President Donald Trump’s threat to make some federal furloughs permanent could worsen an already precarious labor market and create greater uncertainty.

A prolonged shutdown would shutter most Labor Department operations, potentially delaying or reducing the quality of jobs and inflation data. This could affect Social Security cost-of-living adjustments and leave the Federal Reserve more reliant on private data for monetary policy decisions. Economists generally expect a relatively mild overall impact, but furloughed federal employees and contractors could face significant financial hardship from missed income.

The study examines orbital and spin Edelstein effects in electron- and hole-doped monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides under a perpendicular gate field. The field, or equivalently a substrate, breaks horizontal mirror symmetry, producing in-plane chiral orbital and spin textures. An applied in-plane electric field then shifts the Fermi surface and generates orbital and spin magnetization.

A five-metal-d-orbital tight-binding Hamiltonian was derived through Löwdin downfolding and fitted to density-functional band structures for several Mo-, W-, and Nb-based dichalcogenides. Near band edges, the model reduces to combined Ising and Rashba terms. The Rashba coupling and Edelstein responses are approximately linear in the perpendicular field.

For hole doping, the Γ valley contributes much more strongly than the K/K′ valleys because of its larger electric-field coupling. Orbital contributions from the two spin-split valence bands add, whereas spin contributions largely cancel. Compressive strain raises the Γ-valley energy relative to K/K′, allowing holes to occupy it at lower concentrations and substantially enhancing both effects; about 1% strain is sufficient in MoS₂.

For electron doping, carriers occupy the K/K′ conduction valleys. The orbital Edelstein effect grows approximately linearly with electron concentration and is several times larger than the spin effect, whose contributions largely cancel between split bands. The calculated orbital susceptibilities are typically \(10^{-8}\)–\(10^{-7}\,\mu_B\,\mathrm{V}^{-1}\mathrm{m}\), exceeding values cited for other material systems. The results identify gated, doped monolayer TMDs as promising systems for studying orbital and spin Edelstein effects.

Boeing 737 MAX 8 crashes in Indonesia in October 2018 and Ethiopia in March 2019 killed 346 people. Both accidents involved MCAS, software designed to counter the aircraft’s tendency to pitch upward after larger engines were repositioned forward and higher on the low-slung 737 airframe.

Originally intended for rare high-speed conditions, MCAS was later modified to operate at low speeds, move the stabilizer more aggressively, activate repeatedly, and rely on a single angle-of-attack sensor. Although the MAX had two such sensors, warning indicators were optional and, because of a software error, the disagreement alert did not function without an additional purchased feature. The Lion Air aircraft’s sensor was incorrectly calibrated and supplied erroneous data to MCAS.

Boeing developed the MAX rapidly after Airbus’s A320neo threatened its market share. Employees described compressed schedules, strict budgets, hurried work, management pressure, and a culture that discouraged challenging decisions. These conditions followed broader changes after Boeing acquired McDonnell Douglas in 1997, including greater emphasis on shareholder value, outsourcing, layoffs, and business control over engineering.

Boeing characterized MCAS as a minor modification during FAA certification. It did not submit documents detailing significant changes to the system, and key FAA personnel were unaware of them. The FAA consequently gave MCAS limited scrutiny. Investigations later identified communication gaps, weak oversight, insufficient independence, and pressure from industry within the FAA.

To preserve a common pilot type rating and reduce airline costs, Boeing sought to avoid simulator training. Pilots received limited computer-based instruction, and many said they had not known about MCAS. Investigators found that inadequate manuals and training made proper responses more difficult.

After initially emphasizing maintenance and pilot error and declaring the MAX safe, Boeing began redesigning MCAS. Following the second crash, the aircraft was grounded worldwide for 21 months. The FAA authorized its return in November 2020 after changes and mandated simulator training. Boeing reorganized engineering and safety oversight and replaced senior leaders, including CEO Dennis Muilenburg.

The grounding caused order cancellations and substantial financial and reputational damage. Estimates included more than $21 billion in direct costs and $67 billion in lost aircraft sales. The disasters raised continuing questions about Boeing’s leadership and culture, employee accountability, regulatory independence, self-regulation, and prevention of future accidents.

Netflix’s “Unknown Number: The High School Catfish” follows Michigan teenagers Lauryn Licari and Owen McKenny as an unknown sender targets them with increasingly vulgar, personal and threatening messages, sometimes 30 to 40 daily. After local investigations fail for 18 months, the sheriff sends 720 pages of messages to the FBI, which conducts a forensic examination of Owen’s phone.

The author says the documentary could have explained cellphone forensics more thoroughly, including the differences between device data and cellular-provider records. He argues that phones contain extensive recoverable information, while provider records can help track movements through tower connections.

Reflecting on the documentary’s portrayal of technology’s harmful effects, the author supports Oklahoma’s “bell to bell” policy prohibiting cellphones, smartwatches and similar connected devices in schools during the 2025-2026 school year. He contends that student cellphone access can facilitate cybercrime, criminal cases and investigations that harm victims while potentially making many students suspects.

A South Carolina House panel advanced a pension bill addressing a $24 billion funding gap by raising employee contributions to 9 percent and employer contributions to 18.56 percent by 2023, prompting local-government objections. Another bill would recognize concealed weapons permits from all states despite differing training requirements. The Senate approved special Coastal Carolina University championship license plates, with profits funding scholarships; a similar Clemson plate is proposed.

Chelsea will face Barcelona in the Champions League last 16 after finishing second in Group C. Barcelona topped Group D with 14 points, conceding once. The legs will be played in February and March. Chelsea eliminated Barcelona 3-2 on aggregate in the 2012 semi-final. Lionel Messi is highlighted as Barcelona’s star player.

The Fabian Market Timing Model, developed by Richard Fabian in the 1960s, is a mechanical, long-term trend-following strategy for the S&P 500. It uses the index’s 39-week moving average, with signals confirmed by the Dow Jones Industrial Average and utilities sector moving averages to reduce false signals. Trades are executed weekly according to predetermined rules, emphasizing discipline over subjective predictions. Backtesting showed strong performance, low volatility, and limited maximum drawdown, although the high CAGR partly reflected a start after the dot-com peak. Over time, returns are expected to approach buy-and-hold results. The model’s central lesson is the importance of consistently following a chosen system through favorable and unfavorable periods.

A 19-year-old woman was sexually assaulted on a train to Taunton on April 8. Passengers intervened before the suspect left at Bridgewater. British Transport Police are appealing for witnesses and supporting the victim during the investigation.

Winter causes parking congestion around Kensington Park. Whangarei District Council warns drivers before issuing tickets for illegal or obstructive parking. Drivers should plan ahead, carpool, arrive early, or drop off players before parking elsewhere.

The speaker argues that the United States should help establish and guarantee a new international peace, but only under conditions consistent with American principles. The war’s settlement must serve justice and humanity rather than the immediate interests of belligerent nations. Lasting peace requires a universal covenant backed by an organized collective force stronger than any nation or alliance. The essential choice is between an unstable balance of power and a durable community of power based on common peace. Since both sides deny seeking to crush their opponents, the settlement should be a “peace without victory.” A victor’s imposed terms would create humiliation, resentment, and instability, while only peace among equals, founded on shared benefit and just treatment of territorial, racial, and national questions, can endure.

Researchers identified TRPM8 and TRPP3 receptors as potential therapeutic targets for increasing metabolism-boosting brown adipose tissue. In human bone marrow and belly fat precursor cells, both receptors were highly expressed during brown fat differentiation. Activating TRPM8 promoted browning, while inhibiting it impeded the process; disabling TRPP3 prevented brown, but not white, fat formation. The findings may support treatments for obesity, diabetes, and related metabolic disorders.

Tesla’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2021 reported quarterly revenue of $13.76 billion, gross profit of $3.66 billion, operating income of $2.00 billion and net income attributable to common stockholders of $1.62 billion, compared with $8.77 billion, $2.06 billion, $809 million and $331 million, respectively, a year earlier. Diluted earnings per share rose to $1.44 from $0.27.

For the first nine months of 2021, revenue was $36.10 billion and net income attributable to common stockholders was $3.20 billion. Operating cash flow totaled $6.91 billion, investing activities used $5.95 billion and financing activities used $3.95 billion.

At September 30, 2021, Tesla had $57.83 billion in assets, including $16.07 billion in cash and equivalents, and $29.34 billion in liabilities. Stockholders’ equity was $27.05 billion. Inventory was $5.20 billion, while property, plant and equipment totaled $17.30 billion.

Quarterly automotive revenue was $12.06 billion, energy generation and storage revenue was $806 million, and services and other revenue was $894 million. Tesla operates through automotive and energy generation and storage segments.

Tesla purchased $1.50 billion of bitcoin during the nine-month period. Its digital assets had a carrying value of $1.26 billion and fair value of $1.83 billion at quarter-end, after $101 million of cumulative impairment losses and $128 million of realized gains.

The company repaid or converted several debt instruments, including fully repaying $1.80 billion of 2025 senior notes. It reported $6.70 billion of unpaid debt principal and was materially compliant with all financial debt covenants.

Tesla cited continuing pandemic-related logistics and supply-chain challenges, including port congestion, supplier delays and semiconductor shortages. As of October 21, 2021, 1,004,264,852 common shares were outstanding.

The Jammu and Kashmir Public Service Commission kept the 2016 Combined Competitive Preliminary Examination result in abeyance and withdrew the main examination notification after candidates alleged inaccuracies, ambiguity, wrong options, and printing errors in question papers and answer keys. Although subject experts had reviewed earlier complaints before results were declared on April 23, 2017, further representations and information requests prompted the Commission to seek evaluation by independent third-party experts for all 23 subjects. Further action and a new main examination date will follow their report. Of 36,681 candidates who appeared, 6,925 had qualified. A revised result could exclude previously successful candidates and potentially lead to litigation and delays.

Ofsted rated Lyminster Primary School as requiring improvement after a May inspection, citing inconsistent teaching and previous Year 6 underachievement. However, inspectors praised headteacher Steven McGinley’s leadership, positive changes, improving governance, pupil conduct and some strong teaching. McGinley said the school already had plans to address identified weaknesses and was confident it would rapidly regain a “good” rating.

The study examines how dialogic educational ideals can be enacted in classrooms through qualitative analysis of two cases: a choir project in pre-service music teacher education and a discussion of fractions in an upper-primary mathematics class. Its framework combines epistemological dialogue, concerning subject knowledge, with ontological dialogue, concerning students’ lives, identities, and self-understanding. It also uses the concepts of Bildung, musicking, and mathematizing.

In the choir project, the teacher incorporated a student-selected song about life during the HIV/AIDS epidemic and shared her personal experience of losing her brother to AIDS. The case illustrates how musical participation can connect subject learning with existential meaning, relationships, and personal formation. In the mathematics case, students collaboratively discovered and tested possible patterns among fractions while the teacher openly acknowledged uncertainty. The discussion promoted reasoning, questioning, hypothesis formation, and shared inquiry.

Both teachers listened to students, allowed their contributions to shape activities, and accepted uncertainty about outcomes. Their practices supported participation, subject learning, personal development, and the formation of classroom communities. The analysis argues that epistemological and ontological dimensions interact in Bildung processes and that teachers must combine subject authority with openness, vulnerability, and genuine engagement.

The study also identifies tensions in dialogic pedagogy. Efforts to empower students may preserve teacher authority, privilege particular forms of participation, intrude on private experience, or promote predetermined values under the appearance of open dialogue. Dialogic teaching cannot guarantee democratic capacities through a direct cause-and-effect relationship. Nevertheless, the concepts used were found helpful for understanding how classroom practices may support participation, Bildung, and democratic citizenship.

PUBG’s Xbox One “Snipe City” event challenges players to collectively earn 400,000 kills with M24 and Kar98 rifles by July 10. Eligible participants receive clothing items and two Militia Crates if successful. Results arrive July 11.

The lecture develops gravitational radiation in linearized general relativity, where spacetime is treated as a small perturbation of flat spacetime. Of the ten metric perturbation degrees of freedom, six are gauge invariant and four are gauge freedoms. The transverse-traceless spatial perturbation \(h_{ij}^{TT}\) contains two independent radiative degrees of freedom corresponding to gravitational-wave polarizations.

For a wave propagating in the \(z\)-direction, \(h_{ij}^{TT}\) is orthogonal to that direction, symmetric, traceless, and described by two components, \(h_{xx}\) and \(h_{xy}\). A single freely falling body remains fixed in the chosen coordinates, showing that coordinate acceleration alone does not reveal a wave’s physical effect. Instead, gravitational waves are detected through their influence on separated bodies. They alter the round-trip travel time of light between freely falling objects and produce relative acceleration through geodesic deviation.

A ring of freely falling particles illustrates the two polarizations. The plus polarization alternately stretches one coordinate axis while squeezing the other. The cross polarization produces the same tidal pattern along axes rotated by 45 degrees. LIGO detects these effects by comparing laser-light travel times along perpendicular arms using interference.

To calculate radiation from a source, one may first solve the linearized Einstein equation in a convenient gauge and then extract the transverse-traceless part. In Lorentz gauge, the trace-reversed metric perturbation satisfies a wave equation sourced by the stress-energy tensor. Far from a compact source, the distance to different source points is approximated by a common radius. Using the tensor virial theorem, the spatial perturbation is expressed in terms of two time derivatives of the source’s quadrupole moment.

Projection tensors remove components parallel to the propagation direction and eliminate the trace. The resulting quadrupole formula states that \(h_{ij}^{TT}\) is proportional to Newton’s constant, inversely proportional to distance, and determined by the projected, traceless second time derivative of the source quadrupole moment. Missing powers of \(c\) make the measurable perturbation very small, although gravitational waves can carry substantial energy.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended April 1, 2023 reported quarterly net sales of $94.8 billion, down 3% year over year, and net income of $24.2 billion, versus $25.0 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.52. Services revenue rose 5% to $20.9 billion and iPhone revenue increased 2% to $51.3 billion, while Mac and iPad revenue declined 31% and 13%, respectively. Foreign currency weakness adversely affected sales.

For the first six months, net sales declined 4% to $212.0 billion, net income fell to $54.2 billion, and operating cash flow totaled $62.6 billion. Apple repurchased $38.1 billion of stock and paid $7.4 billion in dividends. Quarterly gross margin was 44.3%, while operating expenses rose to $13.7 billion, primarily from higher research and development spending.

At April 1, 2023, Apple had $332.2 billion in assets, $270.0 billion in liabilities, and $62.2 billion in shareholders’ equity. Cash and cash equivalents were $24.7 billion, total marketable securities were $141.6 billion, and term debt was $107.6 billion. Commercial paper declined to $2.0 billion.

Americas quarterly sales fell 8%, Greater China 3%, and Japan 7%; Europe rose 3% and Rest of Asia Pacific rose 15%. Apple announced new MacBook Pro, Mac mini, and HomePod products. The board later authorized an additional $90 billion share-repurchase program and increased the quarterly dividend to $0.24 per share. Apple reported no material changes in market risk, internal controls, critical accounting estimates, or risk factors.

Zacks Investment Research upgraded State Bank Financial Corporation (NASDAQ: STBZ) from “sell” to “buy,” setting a $30 price target representing 11.69% potential upside. Hovde Group separately downgraded the stock to “market perform” and lowered its target to $24.50. Overall, four analysts rated the stock “hold” and three rated it “buy,” with an average $25.25 target.

Shares opened at $26.86, with a $963.28 million market capitalization. Quarterly earnings were $0.34 per share, exceeding the $0.31 consensus estimate. Analysts forecast annual earnings of $1.33 per share. The company paid a quarterly dividend of $0.14 per share, equivalent to a 2.08% yield.

Two directors sold shares in November, while insiders retained 6.31% ownership. Hedge funds and institutional investors owned 81.81% of the stock. State Bank Financial provides community banking services to individuals and businesses in Georgia.

The lecture examines trabecular bone, osteoporosis modeling, metal foams for implants, and bone architecture in evolutionary studies. A whale vertebra, obtained as a relatively uniform source of trabecular bone, was proposed for cutting into cylindrical compression specimens.

Osteoporosis was modeled using two- and three-dimensional Voronoi honeycombs generated from separated random seed points. Finite-element calculations showed that structural randomness had little effect on elastic modulus compared with analytical models, but reduced compressive strength to roughly 60–80% of that of regular hexagonal honeycombs. This reduction was attributed to broader stress and strain distributions caused by variations in strut length and orientation. A strength minimum near 5% relative density was associated with interaction between elastic buckling and plastic yielding.

Bone loss was represented by either uniformly thinning struts or removing them. Removing struts caused much larger reductions in modulus and strength and eventually produced a percolation threshold, where the structure separated and its stiffness and strength became zero. Models adapted to vertebral trabecular architecture showed similar effects when longitudinal or transverse struts were thinned or removed. Three-dimensional structures required more material removal than two-dimensional ones to reach the percolation threshold.

Metal foams are being considered as porous implant coatings or components because bone can grow into them. Titanium and tantalum foams can be produced through replica, fugitive-phase, foaming-agent, gas-expansion, freeze-casting, and selective laser-sintering processes. Their mechanical behavior resembles that of other foams, though measured modulus and strength vary substantially with structure and manufacturing method.

The lecture also reviews mineralized structures in evolution. Early mineralized organisms commonly used calcium carbonate or silica, while true bone containing calcium phosphate appeared in ray-finned fish about 450 million years ago. Because bone architecture responds to mechanical loading, fossil trabecular patterns can help assess locomotion. Comparison of an approximately eight-million-year-old *Oreopithecus bambolii* ilium with human and non-human primate bones found several features more similar to humans, suggesting that the species was bipedal or spent some time moving bipedally. Bone quality can also decline through microcracking, in addition to strut thinning and loss.

Lagos and Ogun health workers are on high alert for Lassa fever. Ogun confirmed one isolated patient responding to treatment, with 66 contacts under surveillance. LUTH reported its cases and monitored contacts were doing well. Lagos previously confirmed five cases, two deaths, and 150 people under surveillance.

Asian shares fell as investors sold U.S. technology stocks amid concerns over Facebook’s improper user-data access, tighter regulation, U.S. protectionism and a potential U.S.-China trade war. Investors also awaited Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell’s first policy meeting, with a rate increase expected but uncertainty over future hikes. Japan’s Nikkei dropped 1 percent, while Wall Street’s S&P 500 and Nasdaq recorded their worst day in five weeks. Facebook fell 6.8 percent. Two-year Treasury yields reached a 9½-year high, while the dollar gained little. The euro rose on shifting ECB policy discussions, and sterling strengthened following agreement on a post-Brexit transition. Oil prices were nearly unchanged amid supply concerns and Saudi-Iran tensions.

Motorola’s rumored Moto Z2 Force may end Verizon exclusivity in 2017, potentially becoming available unlocked or through carriers such as T-Mobile and Sprint. Expected around June 2017, it follows the popular Moto Z Force, praised for its shatterproof display, larger battery, and comfortable design.
Wall Street headhunters advise candidates to be transparent and honest, and to specialize in an underrepresented niche or sector that the bank values and that offers growth opportunities.

Cleveland Central High School students presented the Purple Christmas Showcase at the Delta Arts Alliance, featuring photos, biographies, quotes and homecoming images created through the Cleveland Yearbook project. Since September, students have worked with project manager Charles Coleman to interview peers, teachers, residents and business owners about local history, culture and Cleveland’s future. The display remains open through Wednesday.

The Texas Court of Civil Appeals affirmed the divorce and award of custody of the parties’ two children to John Geesbreght but reversed and remanded the property division.

The court held that the Tarrant County trial court had jurisdiction over the divorce and children. Mary Lee had waived her jurisdictional objection by appearing in the Texas proceeding after her Illinois action was dismissed. The children’s legal domicile remained in Texas because both parents had established it there, John had not consented to a change, and Texas law gave both parents authority concerning domicile. Texas statutes also authorized personal jurisdiction based on the parties’ prior marital cohabitation and residence with the children in Texas.

The jury found that awarding John managing conservatorship served both children’s best interests. During deliberations, the trial court submitted supplemental questions defining a possessory conservator’s rights and asking what visitation rights Mary Lee should receive. The jury recommended all listed rights and unlimited visitation. The appellate court found no reversible error because these answers were recommendations rather than determinations of controlling issues, Mary Lee received possessory-conservator rights, and the custody findings were supported by the evidence.

The property division required retrial because the trial court valued John’s 50% interest in Emergency Medicine Consultants, a professional corporation, solely at its $16,000 book value. The corporation supplied physicians for hospital emergency rooms, generated substantial revenue, maintained multiple hospital contracts, and employed numerous physicians. Although goodwill personal to an individual physician generally is not divisible property, the corporation possessed goodwill independent of John personally. That goodwill could enhance the stock’s value by providing a purchaser an opportunity to retain the corporation’s contracts and established business reputation. The failure to consider it produced a grossly inadequate and clearly erroneous property award to Mary Lee.

The property retrial must address the parties’ property as it existed on August 30, 1977, the effective date of the affirmed divorce. Appellate costs were divided equally between the parties.

NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 29, 2018 reported second-quarter revenue of $3.12 billion, up 40% year over year, operating income of $1.16 billion, and net income of $1.10 billion, or $1.76 per diluted share. Gross margin rose to 63.3%. Six-month revenue was $6.33 billion, with net income of $2.35 billion and diluted earnings of $3.74 per share.

GPU quarterly revenue increased 40% to $2.66 billion, while Tegra Processor revenue rose 40% to $467 million. Gaming revenue was $1.81 billion, Datacenter $760 million, Professional Visualization $281 million, Automotive $161 million, and OEM and IP $116 million. Cryptocurrency-related OEM revenue declined substantially and was expected to become negligible. Operating expenses increased 33% to $818 million, reflecting investment in gaming, AI, and autonomous driving.

At quarter-end, NVIDIA had $12.88 billion in assets, including $7.94 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, and $4.09 billion in liabilities. First-half operating cash flow was $2.36 billion. The company returned $837 million to shareholders through $655 million in share repurchases and $182 million in dividends and intended to return $1.25 billion for fiscal 2019.

NVIDIA adopted a new revenue accounting standard, increasing opening retained earnings by $7 million, with no significant effect on reported first-half results. It reported ongoing patent litigation but recorded no related accrual because losses were considered possible rather than probable and could not be reasonably estimated. Management concluded that disclosure controls were effective, reported no material changes in internal controls or previously disclosed risk factors, and stated that existing cash and anticipated operating cash flows were sufficient for at least the next 12 months.
The Dallas Stars joined the Vegas Golden Knights in pregame tributes honoring Las Vegas shooting victims, a Stars staff member killed in a car wreck, and announcer Dave Strader.

The study externally validated a longitudinal Grade of Membership (L-GoM) model of Alzheimer’s disease progression in the community-based, multiethnic Predictors 3 cohort. The model uses fixed characteristics and time-varying clinical measures across 11 domains to represent patients as weighted combinations of four disease subtypes and predict survival and need for full-time care (FTC).

The analysis included 273 participants: 123 initially diagnosed with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and 150 with Alzheimer’s dementia. Predictions covering up to 7.5 years were compared with observed outcomes overall and across diagnostic and demographic subgroups. Survival predictions fit well for MCI cases and the 118 participants whose Alzheimer’s diagnosis remained consistent. FTC predictions were generally acceptable, although deviations occurred for some MCI observations and later follow-up among Alzheimer’s cases.

The model performed poorly for 32 participants whose Alzheimer’s diagnosis later reverted to non-dementia; their survival was higher and FTC need lower than predicted. Excluding these reverters improved model fit. Predictions were broadly consistent across sex and ethnicity, including the predominantly Caribbean-origin Hispanic sample, though the non-Hispanic nonwhite sample was too small for confident validation.

The findings support using the L-GoM model and its web-based calculator to predict survival and FTC needs among community-dwelling adults with Alzheimer’s disease or MCI from varied ethnic, linguistic, and socioeconomic backgrounds. Diagnostic misclassification can produce inaccurate predictions, and validation is still needed in additional minority populations and with biological measures not included in the current model.

Microsoft’s unaudited fiscal 2022 third-quarter revenue rose to $49.4 billion from $41.7 billion, operating income to $20.4 billion, and net income to $16.7 billion, with diluted earnings per share of $2.22. Nine-month revenue was $146.4 billion and net income was $56.0 billion. Microsoft Cloud quarterly revenue increased 32% to $23.4 billion, while all three operating segments reported revenue and operating-income growth.

At March 31, 2022, Microsoft had $344.6 billion in assets, $181.7 billion in liabilities, and $162.9 billion in stockholders’ equity. Nine-month operating cash flow was $64.4 billion; financing and investing used $45.6 billion and $20.6 billion, respectively.

Microsoft completed its $18.8 billion Nuance acquisition on March 4, 2022, and had agreed to acquire Activision Blizzard for $68.7 billion, subject to approvals and closing conditions. It repurchased $20.2 billion of shares during the first nine months and declared dividends totaling $1.86 per share. Deloitte reported no material modifications were needed for the interim financial information.

Fibonacci trading uses tools such as retracements, expansions, fans, and channels to identify potential support, resistance, entries, stops, and profit targets. Common retracement ratios include 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, and 78.6%. Expansions estimate the size of future trend moves, while fans provide dynamic support and resistance lines.

No single timeframe or retracement level is universally best; choices depend on trading style, market volatility, and backtesting. Higher timeframes, particularly daily charts, may suit technical analysis better.

The passage argues that Fibonacci trading lacks strong scientific and backtested evidence. A study by Clarissa Gunawan using Vanguard ETFs found that passive buy-and-hold strategies outperformed active Fibonacci strategies combined with moving averages, RSI, and ATR. Although Fibonacci tools may help mark support, resistance, and profit targets, the study recommends caution and confirmation with other indicators. The authors advise traders to backtest and use demo accounts, and generally favor other strategies over Fibonacci methods for day trading or crypto.

A Yale-Brookings analysis found no broad AI-driven disruption in the U.S. labor market, though targeted effects are emerging in software development, customer service, and creative work. Researchers attribute current hiring difficulties, including those facing recent graduates, mainly to a slowing economy, aging population, and reduced immigration. They stress that AI exposure may change tasks without eliminating jobs. Major displacement would likely occur only after companies redesign enterprise workflows around AI, a slow and uneven process whose systemic effects may take years.

U.S. wheat futures fell to a nearly three-week low on weak export demand and forecasts for rain in the southern Plains.
