In Gabon, an investigation highlighted trafficked children from Benin and Mali, including a girl rescued from forced marriage.

This study examined hippocampal perineuronal nets (PNNs), extracellular matrix molecules, glial cells, and synaptic markers in postmortem samples from subjects with substance use disorder (SUD), major depressive disorder (MDD), comorbid SUD/MDD, and controls. Rhesus macaques with or without one year of alcohol self-administration were also studied.

Subjects with SUD showed increased PNN densities in several hippocampal regions, including CA1, alongside increased parvalbumin, VAMP2, and chondroitin synthase 1 expression and decreased expression of the extracellular matrix proteases MMP9 and cathepsin S. WFA-labeled glial cells were increased in CA4 and the dentate gyrus. Cocaine history or presence at death affected several measures.

MDD generally produced different patterns, including reduced PNN density in CA1, increased WFA-glia in several regions, and increased parvalbumin, VAMP2, and cathepsin S expression. Comorbid SUD/MDD showed limited or opposing PNN changes, widespread reductions in WFA-glia, lower GFAP expression, and increased aggrecan and chondroitin synthase 1 expression.

Alcohol-exposed macaques had increased PNN densities across combined hippocampal subfields and specifically in CA1 and CA3, plus increased WFA-labeled glia in the dentate gyrus. The findings support a possible role for hippocampal PNNs and extracellular matrix changes in stabilizing contextual reward memories and cue-induced relapse. They also highlight the importance of MDD comorbidity. Limitations include polysubstance use, medication effects, postmortem tissue constraints, reliance on WFA labeling, and inability of qPCR to identify responsible cell types or functional activity.
The speaker views the Stanley Cup decider as an exciting opportunity, emphasizing that the team must move past previous losses and prepare to win the final game.

The Joseph Rowntree Foundation estimates that a couple with two children needs £40,000 annually for a reasonable lifestyle, while a single person needs £18,400. The passage argues that redistribution cannot raise 70% of households to this standard because only about 30% earn more than £40,000. It proposes reducing childcare and housing regulations, raising income tax and National Insurance allowances to £18,400, lowering government spending and taxation, and pursuing stronger economic growth.

The Education Department will halt two Obama-era rules scheduled for July 1 and convene committees to review them. One rule tied federal aid to graduates’ “gainful employment,” while the other established loan-forgiveness procedures for borrowers misled by colleges or affected by closures. The department will continue processing 16,000 existing claims. For-profit college representatives argue the rules are burdensome and have sued, while Democratic attorneys general and senators oppose the delay. Hearings are planned for July.

Culpeper defeated Courtland 2-1 in a nondistrict baseball game by capitalizing on seven Courtland errors, including five in the final two innings. Courtland pitcher Alex Kobersteen allowed only two hits, struck out nine and walked none, but both Culpeper runs were unearned. Defensive mistakes enabled Vincent Rivera to tie the game in the sixth and Hunter Bowers to score the winning run in the seventh. Culpeper pitcher Jake Dudley also threw a complete game, allowing two hits while recording nine strikeouts and three walks. Addie Burrow scored Courtland’s only run by stealing home. Both coaches emphasized Culpeper’s stronger defensive execution.

Etisalat Nigeria and 13 local lenders have not agreed on restructuring a $1.2 billion loan after a missed payment. Regulators favor a default deal over receivership, while Etisalat may consider selling its Nigerian stake after an agreement.

VentureWire’s November 30, 2000 issue reports that 724 Solutions agreed to acquire Tantau Software for about $375 million in stock; El Dorado Ventures formed a $250 million early-stage technology fund; MaMaMedia cut staffing to 15 employees; and iVMG appointed former Prodigy executive Samer Salameh as CEO. Numerous technology, healthcare, e-commerce, optical networking and business-services companies announced financing rounds, including E2O Communications’ $38.5 million, Medschool.com’s $26 million and Tapestria’s $25 million investment. Blackboard agreed to acquire campus commerce, identification and e-learning assets from iCollege. Crosspoint Venture Partners postponed a fund with commitments exceeding $1 billion, while Hyperion Partners raised $73 million toward a planned $100 million fund. The issue also covers product launches, executive and board appointments, venture-capital personnel changes, and corrections to previous reports.

Weak U.S. employment data, major downward revisions, political controversy at the Bureau of Labor Statistics, and Fed personnel changes increased rate-cut expectations. USD/JPY fell sharply, with support near 147.13 and 146.45; further losses could target 144.00–144.40.

Markets expect the Bank of England to cut rates by 25 basis points to 4.0% despite elevated inflation, as UK growth weakens and unemployment reaches 4.7%. GBP/USD remains bearish below resistance at 1.3360 and 1.3450–1.3500; a break under 1.3135 could target 1.3000.

BTC/USD declined alongside equities and found support around 112,000. A move above 117,260 could indicate renewed gains, while failure to hold 110,750 could expose 105,770–107,500. Economic uncertainty, tariffs, and concerns about Fed independence may continue weighing on sentiment. The passage also warns that trading financial instruments and cryptocurrencies carries substantial risk and that website data may be delayed or inaccurate.

Greek central bank chief Yannis Stournaras urged Greece and its lenders to conclude the bailout review by February’s end, warning delays could renew uncertainty, weaken banks and undermine a projected 2.7 percent economic recovery. Negotiations remain stalled over reforms, fiscal targets and IMF involvement, while household deposits have recently declined.
Researchers launched a study testing whether untaxed supplemental income for new mothers improves children’s emotional and brain development during their first three years.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced an agreement to build a Qatari Emiri Air Force facility at Mountain Home Air Force Base in Idaho. The facility will host Qatari F-15s and pilots for joint training with U.S. personnel. The announcement reflects deepening Trump administration ties with Qatar, which recently gifted the U.S. a Boeing 747 and received a security assurance from the president.

The offensive goal kick aims to retain possession and create an attack after the defending team wins the ball. It is awarded when an attacker last touches the ball before it crosses the defending team’s goal line. The stationary ball may be kicked by any player from anywhere in the goal area. It is in play once kicked and visibly moving; opponents should remain outside the penalty area until then, although the kicking team may choose to restart before they retreat. The original kicker cannot touch the ball again until another player does.

For players generally aged 10 and under, smaller fields and build-out lines help teams play safely from the back. Opponents retreat beyond the line, while the kicker may pass to a nearby dribbler or a wide target supported by a secondary receiver. Teams should move the ball wide and upfield, avoid passing across their own goal, ensure receivers are attentive, and keep a player in front of goal as protection if possession is lost.

For players aged 11 and above, the kicker chooses among progressively more advanced targets based on defensive coverage. Receivers should move decisively toward the ball, and coaches should practice setups from both sides while adding passive and active defenders.

Advanced teams may use short passes, predetermined targets, or deep kicks, usually taken by the goalkeeper. Deep kicks can create contested balls, so passes may instead be directed into space for a teammate to run onto. A goal kick is a direct restart, meaning it can score in the opposing goal without another touch. Wind and field conditions can significantly affect its outcome.

Global firms face rapidly changing regulations, rising penalties, reputational risks, and the challenge of balancing consistent oversight with local requirements. The passage argues that real-time monitoring, automated reporting, integrated governance, and audit readiness can turn compliance into a strategic advantage. StarCompliance’s Enterprise platform supports employee and firm compliance across areas including conflicts, accountability, registration, incident tracking, training, and sensitive-information oversight. The company, named Pan Finance’s Most Innovative Employee Technology Platform USA, also offers a free executive brief on managing non-compliance risks.

Finance Ministry-endorsed Project Sashakat proposes a five-pronged, time-bound strategy to accelerate bad-loan resolution. Loans above Rs 500 crore would use an AMC/AIF-led approach, while stressed accounts of Rs 50 crore or less would follow a templated SME process. Steering committees would handle accounts over Rs 50 crore within 90 days, with lead-bank resolutions approved by 66 percent of lenders. The plan encourages foreign capital and asset trading but rejects a state-owned “bad bank.”
South American anthuriums filter ammonia and xylene but may trigger allergies. They require indirect light, dampness, 18–21°C temperatures, winter misting, and annual repotting when young.

The report describes a longstanding U.S. policy opposing foreign aggression in Hawaii, protecting American commercial and strategic interests, and considering annexation a possible or preferred outcome. It cites proposed cession in 1851, an unfinished annexation treaty in 1854, and later support from officials including Seward, Johnson, Grant, Fish, and Blaine. After the 1875 reciprocity treaty, successive administrations sought exclusive U.S. commercial rights and supported Hawaii’s government while it protected American interests. If Hawaiian neutrality became impracticable, Blaine favored an “American solution.” The report also notes that formal U.S. representation began in 1820 with John C. Jones, appointed to oversee commerce, seamen, and broader American interests, with naval officers occasionally providing information and assistance.

Random walk theory holds that stock prices move unpredictably and independently of past prices, making technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysis ineffective. A random walk trading strategy therefore emphasizes passive investing and diversification across stocks or broad market index funds rather than market timing, based on an assumed 50% chance of prices rising or falling.

Although random walk theory views markets as random and the efficient market hypothesis argues that prices reflect all available information, both conclude that consistently outperforming the market is nearly impossible. Their assumptions may conflict and may not reflect recognizable market trends, behavioral patterns, or investors with long-term records of outperformance.

Burton Malkiel popularized random walk theory in his 1973 book *A Random Walk Down Wall Street*, building on ideas attributed to Louise Bachelier. A Wall Street Journal stock-picking experiment found professionals beat random dart selections but did not significantly outperform the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

Backtests using random entries produced positive results for the S&P 500 ETF SPY, with a 0.37% average gain per trade, a 1.7 profit factor, and a 13% maximum drawdown. The same approach performed poorly for the gold ETF GLD, averaging a 0.08% loss. The passage attributes SPY’s stronger result mainly to stocks’ long-term upward drift and advocates quantified, backtested trading rules.

The study uses a quasi-experimental approach to assess how in-person, hybrid, and online college teaching affected county-level COVID-19 cases and deaths. It matches similar colleges and counties, incorporates cellphone mobility data, varied reopening dates, and reweighting for colleges’ likelihood of selecting a modality. Addressing limitations of prior studies, including endogenous modality choices and testing effects, it finds that reopening—especially in-person instruction—increased cases and deaths over time.

President Harry S. Truman announces Germany’s unconditional surrender, honors Franklin D. Roosevelt and those who sacrificed their lives, and gives thanks to God. He cautions that victory is only half complete because the war against Japan continues, urging Americans to remain at their posts and work toward final victory and a lasting peace based on justice, law, and cooperation with allies. Truman proclaims May 13, 1945, a national day of prayer, thanksgiving, remembrance, and support for the continuing struggle.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K reporting that it published a press release on October 2, 2022, furnished under Items 2.02 and 7.01. The filing includes the press release as Exhibit 99.1 and was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn on October 3, 2022.

Which? says official fuel-economy figures often fail to reflect real driving, potentially obscuring annual fuel-cost differences of more than £800 between medium-sized hatchbacks. The New European Driving Cycle (NEDC), unchanged since 1997, lacks sustained motorway driving and allows practices that improve results, including eco modes, disabled accessories, removed equipment, high tyre pressures, lower test speeds and a 4% adjustment. Testing across different accredited laboratories also limits comparability.

The tougher Worldwide-harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) began replacing NEDC in September 2017, with all new UK cars required to use it by September 2018.

Which? tests vehicles consistently in one laboratory using WLTP cold- and hot-engine cycles plus sustained motorway driving. Cars remain in their default mode, accessories operate, tyres follow manufacturer specifications, and results are not adjusted. Hybrid testing accounts for battery charge and charging energy.

Tests also measure NOx, carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and particulate matter; heavily polluting vehicles cannot receive Best Buy status. Where laboratory NOx results appear suspicious, Which? uses portable equipment on real roads and penalises exceptionally high readings, while retaining laboratory tests for controlled comparisons. It publishes independent fuel-economy data for more than 700 vehicles and tests about 120 new cars annually.

Austria-Hungary faces severe postwar employment, supply, and financial problems that transit trade cannot solve. Allied assets include satisfying Bulgaria’s claims, Turkey’s military defeats and economic weakness, and German colonies and overseas exclusion as bargaining tools. Russia’s revolution threatens German domination through anti-capitalism, religious and nationalist sentiment, and its revolutionary example. Though used by Germany, the Vatican could assist the Allies if handled skillfully. American manpower and resources, combined with Entente forces, are presented as ensuring victory. Other advantages include popular desires for peace, rejection of old diplomacy and armed peace, support for a league of nations, and fears of social revolution and unmanageable war debts. German expansion, initially directed south and then southeast, now turns east toward opportunities in weakened Russia; Germany may therefore accept concessions elsewhere to secure control there.

Navient (NASDAQ:NAVI) shares rose 2.27%, closing at $13.51. Nine analysts project an average 12-month target of $16.89, with estimates ranging from $13.50 to $22. The stock’s average brokerage recommendation is 2.75 based on eight recommendations, while its industry ranks 138 of 265. Reported ratings include one Buy, three Outperform, five Hold, one Underperform, and no Sell recommendations. Navient’s 14-period Average True Range is 0.41, with weekly volatility of 2.72% and monthly volatility of 2.82%. Its Relative Strength Index is 51.03. The company has a $3.55 billion market capitalization and 263 million outstanding shares. Trading volume was 5.78 million shares, versus an average of approximately 2.8 million.

Scorpion envenomation is a potentially fatal emergency, particularly among children and in resource-limited settings. This prospective cross-sectional study described clinical features, outcomes, and fatality risk factors among patients admitted to Tesseney Community Hospital in western Eritrea from June 2019 through May 2020.

Among 165 patients, 51.5% were female, 61.8% were aged 15 years or older, and 57% lived in urban areas. Most stings occurred on the foot (64.8%), at night (62.4%), indoors (56.4%), and during summer (93%), especially September and October. Black scorpions were most frequently identified. The commonest manifestations were localized pain (70.3%), sweating (56.4%), vomiting (33.9%), paraesthesia (29.1%), relative bradycardia (24.8%), and restlessness (24.2%). By Abroug’s classification, 20.6% of cases were class I, 35.8% class II, and 43.6% class III. Children had more severe envenomation; 75% of children under five presented with class III symptoms.

Eight patients died, producing a 4.8% case-fatality rate. Six deaths occurred among class III cases, and five occurred in patients younger than 15 years. Age below 15 and lack of formal education were reported as possible factors associated with severity, while sex, scorpion colour, and number of stings were not significant risk factors.

Treatments included local anaesthesia, oral analgesics, diazepam, intravenous fluids, antibiotics, and, in moderate or severe cases, nifedipine and/or scorpion antivenom. Medication assessment was limited by shortages of antivenom and the unavailability of prazosin. Other limitations included data from one hospital, unrecorded community cases and post-discharge deaths, and uncertain scorpion-colour and rural–urban classifications.

The study recommends preventive education, prompt care-seeking, protective footwear, mosquito nets, safer firewood storage, improved surveillance, ecological research, updated treatment guidelines, and reliable provision of essential drugs, particularly for managing paediatric cases.

Scotiabank’s 1832 Asset Management will pay an $800,000 fine and $150,000 in investigation costs for providing advisers excessive promotional benefits between 2012 and 2017. Benefits included event tickets, electronics, food and entertainment. The firm began improving compliance practices last year.

Vodafone Ghana employee Eunice Ampomah-Manu helped save customer Andrew Kufuor after he suffered an attack during a routine call. She kept him on the line, contacted his wife, and later checked on him in hospital. Kufuor visited Vodafone to thank her, while CEO Yolanda Cuba emphasized the company’s commitment to customer care.

The President announces a special Advisory Commission on Civil Disorders, chaired by Illinois Governor Otto Kerner, to investigate recent urban unrest and recommend preventive measures. The FBI will continue investigating the riots and possible conspiracy.

He condemns looting, arson, and violence as crimes unrelated to civil rights protest, calling for swift enforcement by local, state, and, when necessary, federal authorities. He orders expanded riot-control training for the National Guard but argues that force alone cannot create lasting peace.

The long-term solution, he says, requires combating discrimination, poverty, slums, disease, inadequate education, and unemployment. He cites recent social legislation and urges further action on crime control, gun control, housing, education, and urban development, criticizing Congress for rejecting or reducing city programs.

He warns against racial hatred and emphasizes that most Black and white Americans are responsible citizens seeking safety and harmony. Calling for peaceful change, reconciliation, and personal responsibility, he proclaims July 30 a national day of prayer. He urges Americans to reject violence, aid its victims, rebuild trust between races, and pursue better jobs, housing, education, liberty, and justice.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that it issued a January 25, 2022 press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2021. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under the Exchange Act. The filing was signed by Chief Accounting Officer Alice L. Jolla.

The paper studies finitely generated Gorenstein-projective modules over the dual integers \( \mathbb Z[\varepsilon]=\mathbb Z[T]/(T^2) \), since classifying all modules over this ring is considered infeasible. It identifies \(G\text{-proj }\mathbb Z[\varepsilon]\) with categories of torsionless modules, perfect differential structures on abelian groups, and shift orbits of bounded complexes of free abelian groups, while noting that it lacks the Krull–Remak–Schmidt property.

Its main theorem establishes equivalences among the stable category of Gorenstein-projective modules modulo projectives, the stable category of submodules of finitely generated free modules, the orbit category \(D^b(\mathbb Z)/[1]\), and homotopy and stable categories of perfect differential structures. The result also extends to principal ideal domains.

These categories form a chain of dense functors from bounded complexes of free abelian groups to finite abelian groups. Quotients by shifts, projective-factorizing maps, and stalk-factorizing maps can be composed in any order, producing a cube whose faces are commutative squares.

Australia’s Nick Kyrgios will face American John Isner in the second singles match of their Davis Cup quarter-final in Brisbane, following Jordan Thompson’s opening match against Jack Sock. Kyrgios and Isner are tied with 218 ATP aces this season, while Isner leads their head-to-head record 2-1. Sam Groth and John Peers will play Sam Querrey and Steve Johnson in Saturday’s doubles. Thompson replaces Bernard Tomic, who declined to participate. Australia captain Lleyton Hewitt expressed confidence in Thompson after his two singles wins against the Czech Republic. Australia and the United States have won a combined 60 Davis Cup titles.

WIRED highlighted five stories: federal workers at the Small Business Administration were advised to use out-of-office messages blaming Democrats for the government shutdown, potentially conflicting with Hatch Act limits; Peter Thiel’s lectures about the Antichrist and global unification drew scrutiny given his influence and involvement in surveillance technology; Tesla reportedly encouraged drowsy drivers to use Full Self-Driving despite requiring constant driver attention; scientists created human eggs from skin cells and used them to form embryos, suggesting a possible future infertility treatment while raising ethical concerns; and OpenAI launched a standalone social video app powered by Sora 2.

OpenAI’s app resembles TikTok but contains AI-generated videos. Users can verify their identities to create digital versions of their appearance and voice, then place themselves in prompted scenarios. Controls can restrict who uses a person’s likeness, and the app blocks nudity and some romantic content. However, inconsistent handling of copyrighted characters and attempts to bypass safeguards for promotions or problematic videos may require continued moderation. Its long-term appeal and ability to compete with TikTok remain uncertain.

Global SARS-CoV-2 genomic surveillance is highly uneven: as of July 1, 2022, the United States and United Kingdom contributed 54.9% of GISAID sequences, while 10% of submitting countries produced 90.3%. Sparse, geographically concentrated data and delayed reporting can make country-specific regression estimates unreliable, particularly during early variant emergence.

The study developed a Bayesian hierarchical multinomial model that partially pools sequence information across countries and variants. It estimates country-specific variant prevalence and fitness, global fitness advantages, and associated uncertainty. Its mixed-effects structure accounts for geographic heterogeneity while shrinking weakly supported estimates toward shared means, reducing overfitting and enabling estimates in data-sparse settings.

Applied to SARS-CoV-2 data from April–July 2022, the model showed BA.4 and BA.5 replacing BA.2 at differing rates across countries. Estimated fitness advantages varied geographically, but global weekly fitness advantages relative to BA.2 were highest for BA.5, followed by BA.4 and BA.2.12.1; BA.1 was less fit than BA.2.

Retrospective comparisons with independent country-level multinomial models found that the multicountry model produced earlier, more stable fitness estimates and more accurate BA.5 prevalence predictions in Portugal. It could also estimate country-specific fitness before sufficient local observations were available.

The framework can be applied across pathogens and geographic scales and may support surveillance where sequencing is limited. It assumes random, unbiased sampling, accurate lineage assignment and collection dates, even within-country mixing, equal generation intervals, and constant relative fitness during the modeled period. The authors also developed a dashboard for global and local SARS-CoV-2 variant estimates.

IT-based simulation, modeling, digital twins, IoT data, visualization, and analytics can accelerate industrial development, reduce physical prototyping, improve optimization, and enable new products, services, and business models. However, growing computational complexity creates trade-offs between speed, accuracy, and cost; 42% of respondents said their simulations were outdated or inaccurate, while half reported excessive calculation times.

High-performance computing (HPC) addresses these constraints through parallel processing and specialized architectures. Among surveyed decision makers, 81% viewed HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation. More than a quarter already used professional HPC infrastructure, and 39% were planning or piloting deployment. HPC can improve calculation quality and speed, support more iterations, unlock new applications, and increase agility.

Most HPC users favor external infrastructure, cloud services, or colocation over on-premises systems. Key challenges include security, investment and licensing costs, energy consumption, insufficient computing capacity, downtime, scalability, and shortages of expertise. Public and hybrid cloud architectures and HPC as a Service can provide flexible capacity, cost optimization, modern technology, resilience, and support for distributed collaboration, though skilled personnel remain necessary.

IDC recommends establishing virtual product and manufacturing development, creating a holistic data strategy and single source of truth, selecting operating models based on utilization, budget, performance, flexibility, security, and skills, prioritizing scalability and energy efficiency, and using external expertise where needed. Findings derive from a December 2021 survey of 200 industrial decision makers at enterprises with over 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Prize in physics for demonstrating quantum tunneling and energy quantization in electrical circuits during the 1980s. Their experiments used chilled Josephson junctions containing billions of electrons, showing that quantum effects could occur in hand-sized devices rather than only individual atoms. Similar superconducting circuits later became qubits used in quantum computers. The three researchers share 11 million Swedish kronor, worth more than $1.1 million. Martinis also later led Google’s quantum computing effort.

The Open Source Definition emerged in February 1998, building on Richard Stallman’s “free software” advocacy and Netscape’s decision to release its source code. Christine Peterson proposed “open source” as a business-friendly term emphasizing source availability and user freedom without confusion over the word “free.” Bruce Perens adapted the Debian Free Software Guidelines into the OSD and described open source as a way to promote free software to businesses. The approach gained broad commercial acceptance: Apple, Amazon, Facebook, Google, Microsoft, Android, and iOS all rely to varying degrees on open source code. Microsoft notably shifted from hostility toward Linux to embracing open source. Red Hat’s Tim Burke said open source has moved beyond reproducing proprietary products and now leads technological innovation.

Enron’s shares fell to eight-year lows after Moody’s downgraded its long-term debt to Baa2 and reviewed its commercial-paper rating. Default-insurance costs doubled amid concerns over Enron’s liquidity, opaque affiliate transactions, $1.01 billion quarterly loss, $1.2 billion equity reduction, and SEC inquiry. Trading partners continued business with Enron but tightened exposure limits, while Enron sought additional bank credit.

New CFO Jeff McMahon said Enron aimed to expand forest-products trading and promote long-term price hedging, despite entrenched producer-publisher relationships and quality concerns. Separately, Germany’s cartel office threatened action against four utilities over allegedly unreasonable balancing-energy charges that disadvantaged competitors including Enron.

Apple filed amended Articles of Incorporation on August 3, 2020, increasing authorized common shares from 12.6 billion to 50.4 billion and providing for a four-for-one stock split effective at 5 p.m. Pacific daylight time on August 28, 2020. The Form 8-K was signed August 7, 2020.

Energy storage can support renewable energy by shifting electricity use across time, but its economic value depends on capital costs, charging costs and round-trip efficiency. Technologies suit different roles: lithium-ion batteries work well for small-scale distributed use, pumped hydro for large-scale grid management, and flywheels or capacitors for voltage and frequency control.

Lithium-ion costs have fallen substantially, but household batteries remain only marginally cost-effective under variable retail tariffs. A 7kWh system would need to cost below A$7,000 installed, while current costs are A$1,000–3,000 per kWh. Under a flat electricity tariff, batteries may need to fall to about A$300 per kWh. Claims that batteries reduce network costs depend on growing demand; with declining or flat demand, benefits are limited except in high-growth areas.

Pumped hydro costs about A$100 per kWh and already provides 1,500MW in Australia’s National Electricity Market, making it a cheaper, more controllable option where geography permits. However, distributed lithium-ion storage may ultimately prevail because of consumer behaviour rather than economics.

An Irish Times “Portrait Gallery” feature depicts 1951 Nobel physics laureate Ernest Walton working in a Trinity College Dublin laboratory. Described as quiet, shy and devoted to Ireland, Walton’s atom-splitting achievement at Cambridge’s Cavendish Lab receives understated treatment. Jack McManus’s photograph similarly gives equal prominence to Walton and the laboratory machine, contrasting with modern CERN publicity.

The TPS7H500x-SP push-pull converter design uses conservatively rated 80-V GaN synchronous rectifiers, with optional parallel Schottky diodes to reduce soft-start current and reverse-conduction losses. An RCD clamp limits switch-node overshoot and requires test-based optimization. The selected output inductor is 0.47 µH for 40% current ripple.

Output capacitance must satisfy both load-transient and voltage-ripple requirements, including derating for aging, temperature, and DC bias. Although calculations require at least 1.3 mF, approximately 2.3 mF was used to improve radiation-induced single-event transient mitigation. Seven 330-µF polymer tantalum capacitors provide this capacitance. An additional LC filter may reduce output noise, with its resonance placed above crossover frequency and below switching frequency and the bulk-capacitor ESR zero; damping may be added if high-frequency peaking occurs.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins near 35 A, providing about 45% margin over the 24.25-A peak inductor current. Primary current sensing uses a 1:100 transformer and a 7.5-Ω sense resistor. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover using 40.2-kΩ, 15-nF, and 47-pF components. A 102-kΩ slope-compensation resistor connects RSC to AVSS.

The controllers require a regulated 4-V to 14-V supply and at least 0.1 µF of ceramic VIN bypass capacitance placed close to the device. Layout guidance emphasizes separating sensitive feedback and analog-ground paths from switch nodes, magnetic components, high-current loops, and high-dv/dt signals; minimizing switching loops and switch-node copper; using short, wide high-current traces; placing bypass, filtering, compensation, and current-sense components near relevant pins; and joining analog and power grounds at one point. CFP backside metallization should connect to AVSS through multiple vias.

The document also provides application curves, layout examples, related evaluation and radiation reports, update-notification and support resources, ESD cautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, ordering, and legal information.
General on-field guidance helps new soccer players and coaches learn positioning, ball work, and team tactics.

Bernstorff reported that Germany would terminate the blockade if a conference could be arranged on reasonable terms. Ambassador Gerard received Germany’s submarine warfare note; Zimmermann said Germany hoped President Wilson would promote peace and remain quiet for two months while submarine warfare compelled England to seek terms. Greece announced that the Entente would permit essential food imports pending the blockade’s removal, while alleging that many rifles remained unaccounted for. Austria-Hungary asked the United States to preserve diplomatic relations and pressure the Entente to accept Wilson’s proposed “peace without victory.” It rejected the Entente’s alleged aim of dismembering Austria-Hungary and said submarine warfare could not be modified because consultation with allies was required and deployed submarines could not be recalled.

Bitcoin futures were set to begin trading on Cboe Futures Exchange, offering a regulated, cash-settled way to bet on or hedge bitcoin price movements without holding the cryptocurrency. The launch followed sharp price gains and extreme volatility. Financial institutions responded cautiously: some imposed high margins or prohibited short positions, while several banks and brokerages delayed offering or clearing the contracts. Analysts said futures could eventually improve price discovery and reduce volatility through institutional participation. However, concerns remained about inaccurate pricing, market manipulation, cybersecurity, fraud, margin defaults and systemic risks to clearing houses, particularly because the underlying bitcoin spot market is largely unregulated.

The Korean diet emphasizes whole, minimally processed foods, including vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, healthy fats, fermented foods such as kimchi, and varied side dishes. Portions are generally smaller than in Western diets, while processed foods, sugary drinks, unhealthy fats, and dairy are limited.

Its high-fibre, plant-based, low-calorie and low-saturated-fat approach, combined with physical activity, may support overall wellbeing, digestion and weight loss. It can be adapted for vegan, low-carbohydrate and gluten-free diets.

Potential drawbacks include high sodium from fermented foods and condiments, low calcium due to limited dairy, digestive irritation from spicy ingredients, and high carbohydrate intake from rice and noodles. Adjusting sodium, controlling portions and accommodating individual dietary needs may help maximize benefits.
The team hopes Horton recovers but must move forward, drawing confidence from rebounding after a Chicago loss. Despite a strong first period, unlucky bounces and late easy goals require adjustments.

Apple filed a Form 8-K on October 28, 2021, announcing financial results for its fourth fiscal quarter ended September 25, 2021. The related press release was attached as Exhibit 99.1. CFO Luca Maestri signed the report.

The MSPM0G3519/G3518/G1519/G1518 microcontrollers integrate power management, configurable clock sources up to 80 MHz, event routing, and a 12-channel DMA controller supporting transfers up to 128 bits and 64K transfer blocks. Memory includes dual-bank flash up to 512 kB, 16 kB data flash, and up to 128 kB SRAM split into protected and configurable banks. Flash supports ECC, 1 kB sectors, selected high-endurance sectors, and bank swapping for firmware updates.

The devices provide up to 93 GPIOs with low-power wake capability and configurable IOMUX functions. Analog resources include two 12-bit, 4-Msps ADCs with simultaneous sampling and hardware averaging; an internal temperature sensor; selectable 1.4 V or 2.5 V references; comparators; and a buffered 8- or 12-bit DAC with FIFO, calibration, triggering, and DMA support. DAC output uses PA15, where external circuitry should be avoided when DAC_OUT is enabled.

Security features include AES-128/256 acceleration, secure storage for four keys, configurable firewalls, CRC-16/32, and a 32-bit true random-number generator. Communications include UART with LIN support, I2C at up to 1 Mbit/s with SMBus 3.0 support, SPI at up to 32 Mbit/s on suitable pins, and CAN-FD at up to 5 Mbit/s. General-purpose and advanced timers provide capture/compare, PWM, synchronization, peripheral triggering, quadrature decoding, and fault handling.

The low-frequency subsystem contains an RTC and independent watchdog. The RTC supports calendar functions, alarms, periodic interrupts, and crystal calibration or temperature-drift compensation. Independent and windowed watchdogs supervise software execution. Debugging uses a two-wire serial-wire interface. A UART- or I2C-based boot strap loader supports password protection, optional disabling, hardware or software invocation, and automatic startup on blank devices.

Recommended hardware includes 10 µF and 0.1 µF VDD decoupling capacitors, a 0.47 µF VCORE capacitor, and a 47 kΩ/10 nF NRST network. SYSOSC frequency correction requires an external precision 100 kΩ resistor. Open-drain 5 V-tolerant outputs require pullups.

TI supplies development boards, SDKs, SysConfig, cloud and desktop tools, training, and support for Code Composer Studio, IAR, Keil, TI Arm-Clang, and GNU Arm toolchains. Experimental “X” devices are intended only for evaluation, while “MSP” devices are fully qualified. The April 2025 revision updates operating-mode details, peripheral counts, electrical specifications, memory endurance, security descriptions, and package variants.

Nike reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $11.72 billion, up 1% year over year and above the $11 billion expected, despite previously forecasting a mid-single-digit decline. Net income fell 31% to $727 million, or 49 cents per share, while gross margin dropped 3.2 percentage points to 42.2%, reflecting continued discounting and inventory-clearing efforts.

Under CEO Elliott Hill, Nike is pursuing a turnaround focused on wholesale, running and North America. Wholesale revenue rose 7% to about $6.8 billion, and North American sales increased 4% to $5.02 billion. However, Nike Direct sales declined 4% to about $4.5 billion, and China revenue fell 9%.

Inventories decreased 2% as Nike cleared older products. The company is also reorganizing teams by sport, emphasizing athlete consumers while retaining lifestyle products and seeking more female customers, including through the recently launched NikeSKIMS partnership. Finance chief Matt Friend cautioned that recovery progress would not be linear.

An international research team found live giant shipworms, Kuphus polythalamia, in a Philippine lagoon after decades of searching. The five-foot, shell-dwelling mollusks burrow in mud and consume hydrogen sulfide, which microbes in their gills convert into carbon, rather than eating rotting wood like their ancestors. Scientists are studying these microbes for potential antimicrobial substances. Many aspects of the animals’ life cycle, age and distribution remain unknown. The findings appeared in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

Miami Dolphins receiver Tyreek Hill dislocated his left knee during Monday night’s first win of the season. His leg twisted beneath him after a 10-yard third-quarter catch, and he was carted off after receiving an air cast. Hill remained hospitalized overnight for further tests but was reportedly in good spirits. He had six catches for 67 yards before the injury and entered the game as Miami’s leading receiver. Since joining the NFL in 2017, Hill has recorded a league-high 11,363 receiving yards.

This retrospective study developed a model to predict shunt-dependent hydrocephalus (SDHC) after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. Of 118 patients treated from 2013 to 2021, 109 were included after excluding eight early deaths and one case with incomplete data. All underwent aneurysm clipping or coiling, external ventricular drainage, and a subsequent drainage challenge; failed challenges or later hydrocephalus led to ventriculoperitoneal shunting.

Multivariate analysis identified three independent SDHC predictors: age ≥65 years (OR 3.94), surgical clipping rather than coiling (OR 4.36), and Hunt and Hess scale ≥3 (OR 3.59). A nomogram assigning one point to each factor had an AUC of 0.753 and showed adequate calibration. Aneurysm location, Fisher grade, and inflammatory blood ratios were not associated with SDHC in this cohort. The authors proposed the nomogram to support early risk assessment and clinical decisions. Limitations included the retrospective design and small sample, requiring prospective validation.

The DAX 40 comprises 40 major German companies listed in Frankfurt and has returned 5.36% annually since its 1988 inception. U.S. investors can access German large- and mid-cap stocks through the iShares MSCI Germany ETF (EWG), which charges a 0.50% expense ratio. Historical EWG returns since 1996 indicate its strongest performance occurred in the fourth quarter, while other months were largely sideways. A dividend- and split-adjusted backtest of investing only during the final three months reportedly outperformed buy and hold, though future continuation is uncertain.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data-acquisition system with an integrated analog front end. Speed-boost mode converts one selected analog-input pair on every sampling clock at up to 8MSPS while the other six channels remain idle; output-interface specifications remain unchanged.

Its 16-bit configuration registers use three banks and 8-bit addresses. Bank 0 is always accessible, while banks 1 and 2 are selected through register 0x03. SPI register writes and reads use 24-bit frames, with read access controlled by SPI_RD_EN and SPI_MODE. Multiple devices can be configured in a daisy chain sharing CS and SCLK; register operations require N × 24 clock cycles, and DAISY_CHAIN_LEN specifies the number of devices excluding ADC1. Registers configure operating modes, data formatting and averaging, test patterns, gain correction, channel bandwidth and power-down, output lanes, common-mode range, speed boost, and initialization.

For ATE applications, the ADS9803 provides a post-calibration total unadjusted error of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. It supports low-noise bandwidth up to 22.7kHz and wide bandwidth up to 700kHz; wide-bandwidth mode settles multiplexed signals to 99.95% full scale in 7.5µs. The device uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies without a required power-up sequence. Recommended layout practices include close 0.1µF bypass capacitors, short ground connections, and separation of analog and reference signals from digital lines and noise sources. TI states that application guidance and resources are provided as-is and that users are responsible for component selection, design validation, testing, and compliance.

Climate change is warming and reducing water in northern Rocky Mountain streams, allowing introduced rainbow trout to invade habitats of native cutthroat trout. The species interbreed, producing less-fit hybrids and permanently diluting cutthroats’ locally adapted genes. A study of hundreds of locations found widespread hybridization, especially where agencies historically introduced rainbows. Some states are removing rainbow trout to prevent the cutthroat species and its unique genetic traits from disappearing.

A nationwide study of Medicare beneficiaries linked long-term outdoor exposure to trichloroethylene (TCE), an industrial solvent and persistent pollutant, with a modestly higher risk of Parkinson’s disease. Researchers compared 221,789 adults over 67 diagnosed with Parkinson’s from 2016–2018 with more than 1.1 million people without the disease, estimating exposure from EPA data and residential ZIP+4 locations. After adjusting for factors including age, smoking and fine-particle pollution, those in the highest exposure group had a 10% greater risk than those in the lowest. Higher risks were also observed near some major TCE-emitting facilities. The study shows an association, not causation. Limitations include its focus on older adults and reliance on 2002 outdoor-air estimates that may not represent lifetime or indoor exposure.

Former INEC official Christian Nwosu told a Lagos Federal High Court that EFCC operatives coerced him into stating he received N30 million from former Petroleum Minister Diezani Alison-Madueke. He alleged that Usman Zakari threatened detention, dictated his statement, and escorted him to surrender N5 million. Nwosu also claimed prosecutor Rotimi Oyedepo urged cooperation and threatened conviction unless he surrendered property worth N30 million.

Sir John Deane’s sixth form college’s 35-member jazz collective performed 1960s soul and classic swing to a packed audience at the Macdonald Portal Hotel in Tarporley. The college’s next event features 14 students performing classical music at Arley Hall on February 9, with tickets costing £8 or £6 concessions.

A swimming advisory remained in effect at Port Stanley’s Little Beach due to elevated bacteria levels and risks of gastrointestinal illness and infection. The beach remained open because bacteria had not reached the closure threshold. Despite posted signs, some visitors continued swimming or had not noticed the warning. Advisories are posted on the Elgin St. Thomas Health Unit website.

State Street Corporation agreed to pay $5 million to settle U.S. Department of Labor claims that it underpaid 305 female employees and 15 Black vice presidents compared with colleagues in equivalent positions. The company denied the allegations but agreed to provide back pay and interest, while affirming its commitment to equal-pay practices. Its division commissioned New York’s “Fearless Girl” statue to promote women in leadership and a gender-diversity investment index. The settlement prompted criticism of the company for hypocrisy.

The Sansa Fuze supports transferring and playing music, audiobooks, podcasts, voice recordings, photos, and videos. Music may be copied by dragging MP3 or WMA files into the MUSIC folder or synchronized through Windows Media Player; Audible files require Audible Manager. Windows Media Player can organize libraries, create playlists, and synchronize them. Photos and videos require Sansa Media Converter, which can convert, crop, rotate, resize, and transfer files to internal memory or a microSD card.

Playback controls support navigation, volume adjustment, fast-forward, rewind, repeat, shuffle, equalizer settings, ratings, bookmarks, and Go Lists. Photos can be viewed individually or as slideshows with configurable shuffle, looping, duration, and music. The integrated FM radio, where available, supports tuning, up to 30 presets, automatic preset scanning, recording, regional settings, and mono or stereo modes. The built-in microphone can record voice, interviews, or speeches.

Content can be deleted directly from the player or through Windows Explorer. System settings include wallpaper color, list artwork, backlight timing, power saving, language, date and time, brightness, volume level, factory reset, device information, USB mode, formatting, and press-and-hold behavior. Formatting deletes all player content.

Supported audio includes MP3, WAV, WMA, secure WMA, and Audible formats; supported bit rates are 32–320 Kbps for MP3 and 32–256 Kbps for WMA. The player reads and writes microSD and microSDHC cards. A power reset is performed by holding the power switch upward for about 10 seconds. Firmware updates, support, and instructional videos are available through SanDisk.

SanDisk provides the original purchaser a one-year limited, nontransferable warranty, excluding misuse, unauthorized repairs, third-party products or software, and lost data. Remedies may include repair, replacement, or refund. The software license permits limited personal use with a SanDisk product and restricts modification, reverse engineering, redistribution, and hazardous applications. California law governs the agreement, with disputes assigned to courts in Santa Clara County.

Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology used machine learning and advanced simulations to identify the previously unresolved low-temperature structure of formamidinium lead iodide, a high-performing but unstable halide perovskite used in potential solar technologies. Their models simulated millions of atoms over much longer periods and showed that formamidinium molecules become trapped in a semi-stable state during cooling. Experiments with the University of Birmingham at −200°C confirmed the simulations. The findings could help researchers control perovskite materials and develop efficient, lightweight, flexible, and more durable solar cells and optoelectronic devices.

Coachella attendees used “Find My iPhone” to track Reinaldo De Jesus Henao, 36, who was arrested after security found more than 100 phones in his backpack. He faces grand theft and possession of stolen property charges.

In 2016, Norwich siblings Evan and Brynn Meek, ages 10 and 6, distributed 220 bagged lunches to homeless people in Manhattan. Norwich Police Officer Thomas Miller left after eight years to join the Syracuse Police Department. Miller and his K9 Nitro participated in community events, hospital visits and children’s demonstrations; Miller initially paid for Nitro’s training and food before Houndstooth Bakery and Boutique began donating her food. Tracy A. Price, 31, of Norwich, was arrested Aug. 16 on charges of torturing, injuring and neglecting a dog and was granted $750 bail.

A study suggests distraction through hobbies, education, or exercise can improve mood after a breakup but should be used sparingly because avoidance may hinder recovery. Focusing on an ex-partner’s negative qualities may also help people move on faster.
Clarke, Devoret and Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Physics Prize for circuit-scale quantum effects.

Wafa Yahia, the Syrian grandmother central to Hawaii’s lawsuit against President Trump’s travel ban, arrived in Honolulu after receiving US visa approval. Her son-in-law, imam Ismail Elshikh, argues the legal challenge enabled the family reunion. Hawaii Attorney General Doug Chin said the approval does not affect the ongoing lawsuit, while federal courts continue considering exemptions for relatives with bona fide US relationships.

Cuba marked the revolution’s 58th anniversary with a Havana military parade honoring Fidel Castro, who died in November. Tens of thousands marched, though soldiers carried no equipment. The tribute followed a law banning monuments or infrastructure named for Castro. Cuba enters 2017 facing economic contraction, Raul Castro’s planned departure, and uncertainty over improving US relations under President-elect Donald Trump.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that it issued a July 27, 2021 press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter and year ended June 30, 2021. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1, alongside the cover page interactive data file. The report was signed by Chief Accounting Officer Alice L. Jolla.

Vale’s stock conversion plan gained support from 84.4 percent of preferred shares, exceeding the required threshold. The company may list common shares on São Paulo’s Novo Mercado as early as 2017, aiming to broaden its investor base and improve governance. Vale will retain a government golden share and absorb former controller Valepar as part of a shift toward dispersed ownership. Shares rose following the announcement.

Pregnancy made the author’s usual stomach-sleeping impossible, while medical guidance limited safe positions and increased her anxiety about getting enough rest. After seeing a friend recommend the U-shaped Leachco pregnancy pillow, which allows users to turn over without repositioning it, she bought one. The pillow greatly improved her comfort by supporting side sleeping, remaining in place when she moved, and elevating her head during a cold. She began using it throughout her apartment and praised its washable cover. Downsides include its large size, a somewhat scratchy original cover, disruption of blankets, and the cost of softer replacement covers. Despite these issues, she considers it worthwhile and plans to continue using it after pregnancy, recommending it both to pregnant people and anyone seeking greater comfort.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K dated August 16, 2018, announcing results for the quarter ended July 29, 2018. The filing includes a press release and CFO commentary as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. These materials are furnished, not filed, and are not incorporated by reference into other SEC filings.

Commissioner.COM’s November 22, 2001 fantasy football report contains promotional offers, Week 11 NFL player updates, matchup evaluations, injury news, and start-or-bench recommendations. For “Luccis Losers,” it recommends starting Kurt Warner, Cris Carter, Duce Staley, and Marty Booker; treating Charlie Garner and Ike Hilliard cautiously; and reserving Alex Van Pelt, Mike Alstott, Az-Zahir Hakim, James McKnight, and Larry Parker. Cameron Cleeland is doubtful, Donald Hayes is expected to play despite bruised ribs, and Baltimore defensive end Michael McCrary will miss the season after knee surgery.

A study of 48,615 Omicron BA.1 genomes from England, global genomic data, epidemiological records, air travel, and human mobility examined BA.1’s spread from November 2021 through January 2022. Researchers inferred at least 6,455 independent introductions, about 70% of which produced no observable local transmission. Eight large transmission lineages accounted for over 60% of sampled English genomes, and early introductions—around 6% of all introductions—were linked to roughly 80% of reported BA.1 infections through January.

Importations increased approximately exponentially until mid-December despite restrictions on travel from southern Africa. Although many initial imports likely originated in South Africa, estimated importation intensity from the United States was about four times higher during the restriction period, reflecting growing US outbreaks and greater passenger volumes. The findings suggest targeted restrictions were largely ineffective because they began after local transmission and excluded secondary international hubs.

Greater London was central to BA.1’s initial domestic expansion, with substantial outward movement to the Midlands and northern England. Later, London’s contribution declined as mid- and long-distance spread increased from other regions. Spatial transmission was initially shaped by population size, geographic distance, and strongly directional movement from London; mobility patterns became more influential after 26 December.

Mobility across England declined by roughly 20–50% from mid-December to early January, coinciding with restrictions, holidays, and behavioural responses to rising cases. During early epidemic growth, trips between non-urban “home” areas and urban hubs decreased by an estimated 11.97% for each additional weekly COVID-19 case per 100 people at the hub. Shorter-distance travel was more affected.

The study concludes that introduction timing and human mobility strongly shaped BA.1 dissemination. Limitations include likely undercounting or aggregation of introductions and remaining geographic and temporal sampling biases. The authors emphasize integrating genomic, epidemiological, mobility, and behavioural data to prepare for future variants and emerging pathogens.

The TLV321/2x comparator family consumes 40 µA per channel and has 40 ns propagation delay. TLV321x devices use push-pull outputs, while TLV322x devices provide open-drain outputs that can be pulled up to 5.5 V independently of the supply.

Inputs operate from 200 mV below V– to 200 mV above V+, with current limited to 10 mA. Series input resistance is recommended for faults and transients. Unused inputs require at least 50 mV differential voltage and must not be tied together. The devices include 1.8 mV internal hysteresis; external positive-feedback hysteresis can reduce chatter near switching thresholds.

Push-pull outputs can source and sink current but must not be connected to other outputs or supply rails; unused outputs must float. Open-drain outputs support wired-OR operation and level translation. Recommended pull-up current is 100 µA to 1 mA, and unused outputs may float or connect to V–. Output shorts can cause thermal runaway, so current-limiting resistors are recommended where shorts are possible.

Internal ESD clamps limit input voltages to 0.2 V beyond the rails. Power-on reset holds outputs low for up to 32 µs after the supply crosses 1.65 V. Smaller overdrive voltages, especially below 100 mV, increase propagation delay.

A low-side current-sensing example triggers an alert when an amplified shunt voltage exceeds 1.1 V. High-speed PCB practices are required: place a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic bypass capacitor at each device, use solid grounding, minimize input-output coupling, and consider output damping or controlled-impedance routing. TI states that application guidance must be validated by customers and that devices require appropriate ESD handling.

The author accepts Amy Coney Barrett’s defense of originalism for argument’s sake and applies it to a Supreme Court challenge against Louisiana’s second majority-Black congressional district. The essay argues that the doctrine treating race-predominant districting as unconstitutional lacks support in the original public meaning of either the 14th or 15th Amendment. The 14th Amendment was not originally understood to regulate voting discrimination, while the 15th Amendment prohibits denial or abridgment of voting rights and does not clearly cover districting claims involving neither vote dilution nor restricted electoral participation.

Although stare decisis may preserve non-originalist precedents, the author contends that the racial-predominance doctrine is unworkable and conflicts with Voting Rights Act jurisprudence, which may require race-conscious districts to remedy minority vote dilution. An originalist court should therefore reconsider and discard that doctrine rather than weaken enforcement of Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act. Congress could separately prohibit race-based districting, but the Court should not create such claims and use them to restrict Congress’s enforcement authority. The author urges Barrett to address these originalism and precedent issues consistently with the principles stated in her book.

TI provides resources “as is” without warranties. Developers are responsible for product selection, application design, testing, compliance, and safety. Resource use is limited to developing applications with specified TI products. TI disclaims liability, requires indemnification, and applies its Terms of Sale.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture improves programmable shading, ray tracing, AI processing, memory, storage I/O, and efficiency over Turing. Each SM contains 128 CUDA cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation RT Core, 128 KB configurable L1/shared memory, and a 256 KB register file. Dual FP32-capable datapaths double peak FP32 throughput, while larger caches and doubled shared-memory bandwidth improve data access. Ampere GPUs are stated to be up to 1.9 times more power-efficient at equal performance.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput, support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute, and add hardware acceleration for motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores support additional data types, including TF32 and BF16, and structured sparsity that can double matrix throughput by skipping zero values. These capabilities accelerate AI graphics features such as DLSS, denoising, super resolution, and slow motion. DLSS and Ampere performance enable high-frame-rate ray-traced rendering, including 8K gaming in supported titles.

GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, reaching data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth up to 936 GB/s. Error Detection and Replay can detect and retry memory transmission errors. NVIDIA RTX IO, working with Microsoft DirectStorage, moves lossless decompression from CPUs to RTX GPUs, reducing CPU use and accelerating asset loading and streaming.

The architecture supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 4K at 120 Hz, and 8K at 60 Hz. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware decoding for formats including AV1, with support up to 8K60 HDR, while seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

Products based on GA10x include GeForce RTX 30-series GPUs and professional models. The RTX 3090 has 10,496 CUDA cores and 24 GB of GDDR6X memory; the RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6. The A40 targets data-center visual computing, while the RTX A6000 provides 10,752 CUDA cores and 48 GB of GDDR6, expandable to 96 GB using two cards with NVLink.

The United States reached the Davis Cup quarterfinals by defeating Serbia 3-0 after Ryan Harrison and Steve Johnson won the doubles, adding to singles victories by Sam Querrey and John Isner. Kazakhstan also swept Switzerland 3-0 and will face Croatia or Canada.

France led the Netherlands 2-1, while Croatia overcame a two-set deficit in doubles to take a 2-1 lead over Canada. Belgium failed to clinch against Hungary despite leading 2-0, losing a five-set doubles match. Spain led Britain 2-1, Germany held the same advantage over Australia, and Italy led Japan following doubles victories.

The paper adopts the UN definition of youth as ages 15–24 and defines skills development as encompassing technical and soft skills. Cooperative education, or co-op, is presented as experiential learning fully integrated into curricula through structured periods of academic study and paid workplace experience.

Nigeria’s youth unemployment rate, historically below many regions, rose above most regions by 2021 except South Asia and the Middle East and North Africa. Youth unemployment is generally higher than total unemployment, while youth employment-to-population ratios remain lower. Nigeria’s labor market is also characterized by informality, limited social protection, gender and regional disparities, and high unemployment among educated youth. In 2019, 28% of Nigerian youth were not in employment, education, or training, compared with 13% in OECD countries.

Co-op originated in industrialized countries and has also been implemented in South Africa and Namibia. Its core dimensions are curriculum integration, workplace-derived learning, and coordinated administration involving educational institutions, employers, and government. Models include alternating academic and work semesters, parallel schedules, and sandwich arrangements. Reported benefits include improved earnings, employability, career clarity, recruitment, curricula, institutional reputation, productivity, and school-to-work transitions. Evidence, primarily from developed countries, indicates higher employment and earnings and better alignment between graduates’ jobs and fields of study, though program effectiveness depends on design and implementation.

Nigeria has introduced initiatives including the Students Industrial Work Experience Scheme, SURE-P, and N-Power. Evaluations identify benefits but also challenges such as inadequate funding, weak supervision, poor placement matches, and complex administration. SIWES provides workplace exposure but is less integrated into academic schedules and employer-institution collaboration than co-op.

The paper proposes a federally supported alternating co-op model integrated with existing programs such as SIWES or N-Power. Governments could pilot the approach, provide public-sector placements, and offset costs through grants, budget allocations, or employer tax credits. Employers could help shape curricula to meet hard- and soft-skill needs. Students would complete multiple work terms and gain at least one year of career-related experience before graduation.

The paper concludes that co-op could strengthen collaboration among universities, employers, and governments and improve youth preparation for work, but cannot alone resolve unemployment. Broader policies addressing labor demand and economic, political, business, social, and cultural conditions are also necessary. Further research is recommended on governance, suitable models for different institutions and programs, and applications beyond tertiary education.
Euclid police are reviewing video of a white officer repeatedly punching a Black man during a traffic-stop struggle. The officer is on paid leave, and the NAACP seeks a federal investigation.

COVID-19 disrupted in-person education worldwide and prompted Turkey to introduce compulsory virtual education through EBA TV and other platforms. This transition created particular difficulties for students with disabilities in inclusive settings, including limited interaction, motivation, access to technology, individualized instruction, and implementation of Individualized Education Programs. This qualitative study examined primary school teachers’ perspectives on these students’ participation, responsibilities, monitoring, and challenges during virtual education, along with proposed solutions.

Using a phenomenological design, researchers conducted in-person, semi-structured interviews in 2021 with 10 general education primary school teachers from two provinces in Turkey’s Marmara region. Each teacher had at least one student with an officially diagnosed disability. Interviews lasted 28–35 minutes and were analyzed through content analysis. Six main themes and 15 subthemes were identified. Transcript reliability was 98%, and inter-coder reliability was 90.17%.

Teachers initially contacted and guided families, delivered courses through EBA or Zoom, and requested parental support. They also used WhatsApp, videos, virtual support instruction, and hybrid arrangements. Most students with disabilities participated regularly when they had parental assistance, adequate equipment, and independent connection skills. Others attended only core courses or could not participate because of parents’ illiteracy, limited technological skills, internet or device problems, medical advice, or preference for rehabilitation-center instruction.

Reported challenges included insufficient socialization, assignment-tracking difficulties, students turning cameras off, behavioral problems, low engagement with EBA TV, limited interaction and entertaining content, and heavy dependence on families. Large classes reduced teachers’ ability to support individual students and sometimes contributed to behavioral issues. Communication problems with parents and rehabilitation-center staff also hindered monitoring. Families’ inability to provide suitable study environments, low motivation, limited education, and financial or technological constraints further affected participation. Some teachers reported no major difficulties because families cooperated, maintained daily communication, and used EBA’s tracking and assessment functions.

Teachers addressed problems through individualized arrangements, family guidance, support sessions, home-study videos, frequent phone calls, and hybrid instruction. Their recommendations included strengthening teacher-parent cooperation, providing devices and internet access, supporting students’ social as well as academic development, keeping schools available for students with disabilities, expanding EBA support centers, coordinating with rehabilitation centers, improving technological infrastructure, and preparing accessible materials for teachers, parents, and students.

The study concluded that parental involvement, technological access, family circumstances, class size, and teacher-family cooperation strongly affected virtual participation and monitoring. It recommended further research involving students at different grade levels and institutions, comparisons between students with and without disabilities, and quantitative examination of factors influencing virtual education effectiveness. Ethics approval was received from Eskişehir Osmangazi University.

The Investors Intelligence Sentiment Index, developed by AW Cohen in 1963 and published by Chartcraft, surveys over 100 independent market newsletters weekly. It reports the percentages of investment advisors who are bullish, bearish, or expecting a correction. It also tracks stocks above their 10-week and 30-week moving averages to assess shorter- and longer-term market turns.

The index is widely used as a contrarian indicator because advisors have often been wrong at market turning points. Bullish readings above 55% indicate excessive optimism and may be negative for the market, while readings below 35% indicate excessive pessimism and may be positive. Weekly readings above 70% suggest overbought conditions, while those below 30% suggest oversold conditions.

Investor sentiment refers to investors’ overall market mood. Unlike the Investors Intelligence index, which surveys professional advisors and commentators, the AAII Sentiment Survey asks individual investors where they expect the market to head over the next six months. The Investors Intelligence index is available by subscription through Chartcraft’s website.

A homemade pipe bomb strapped to a man exploded or malfunctioned near New York City’s Port Authority and Times Square during Monday morning rush hour. The suspect was taken into custody. He and three others suffered non-life-threatening injuries. The blast prompted a major emergency response, evacuations and disruptions to subway and bus service.

Department of Education employees said their neutral shutdown out-of-office messages were changed without consent to language blaming Senate Democrats. Multiple sources told WIRED that employees who restored neutral wording saw it replaced again. Department of Labor employees also reportedly received suggested partisan language. Experts said the messaging could violate the Hatch Act, which limits federal employees’ political activity, and described it as coercive. The Education Department’s press email returned the same partisan message when WIRED requested comment.

Macmillan’s early-years reading season features six picture books. A 35th-anniversary gift edition of Rod Campbell’s lift-the-flap classic *Dear Zoo* follows a child seeking the perfect pet from a zoo. Catherine Rayner’s *Solomon and Mortimer* depicts two bored crocodiles whose attempt to surprise a hippo brings unexpected consequences. Paul Stickland’s republished *Ten Terrible Dinosaurs*, endorsed by the Natural History Museum, uses rhyme and a countdown from ten to one to teach numbers. In Julia Donaldson and Rebecca Cobb’s *The Everywhere Bear*, a classroom teddy falls from a backpack and journeys through a drain, the sea, a fishing boat, a lorry, a tip and a seagull while trying to return to Class One. Morag Hood’s *When Grandad Was a Penguin* combines surreal humour, a family relationship and a mystery about Grandad’s penguin-like behaviour. Lane Smith’s *A Perfect Day* contrasts several garden animals’ peaceful afternoon with a bear’s disruptive arrival, exploring differing perspectives through suspenseful illustrations.

The court affirmed Ronald Haynes’s conviction for third-degree criminal possession of a weapon following his guilty plea. Finding no nonfrivolous appellate issues, it granted assigned counsel’s request to withdraw. Haynes’s pro se claims were barred by his knowing, intelligent, and voluntary waiver of his right to appeal.
Lab tests suggest jostling air and methane microbubbles create tiny electrical sparks that may ignite methane, producing will-o’-the-wisps.

The Rotary Club of Lakewood and Rocky River honored winners of its annual student Speech, Music and Visual Arts Contest at Beck Center for the Arts. Lakewood High School’s Nicholas Cleary won speech; Rocky River flutist Angeliki Cintron won music; and Lakewood’s Elyza Mihalski won visual arts for “My Sisters.” More than 90 artworks from five high schools were submitted.

North Olmsted residents may purchase $75 engraved bricks for a new Fan Walk at the school campus by May 11. Free community meals are scheduled April 28 at Clague Road United Church of Christ and West Park United Church of Christ.

Lakewood City Schools received the NAMM Foundation’s Best Communities for Music Education designation for the second consecutive year, placing it among 4 percent of U.S. districts receiving the honor. The district offers K-12 music education, numerous ensembles and extracurricular groups, and scholarship support for private lessons.

Other community events include North Olmsted High School’s production of the Queen musical “We Will Rock You” April 27-29; Beck Center’s inclusive “Razzle Dazzle XVIII: Wide World of Sports” May 4-5; two blood drives honoring Dr. Steve Meadows; free genealogy assistance May 2 at Westlake Porter Public Library; and a May 5 volunteer cleanup at Kamm’s Corners ahead of the Hooley.

Additional events include Lakewood’s April 28 cleanup and Earth Day program, an American Legion Auxiliary rummage sale in Fairview Park, and the April 29 opening of the West Park Historical Society’s new office. Residents have also humorously decorated and named a traffic barrel marking a longstanding chuckhole near West 159th Street and Edgecliff Avenue.

Archaeologists in Mexico plan to clear Maya-sealed tunnels at Chichen Itza to seek an entrance to a hidden cenote beneath the El Castillo pyramid. Cenotes, the Yucatan’s only fresh-water sources, were spiritually significant entrances to the underworld where the Maya made offerings, including human sacrifices.

Scientist Rene Chavez Segura identified the cenote beneath El Castillo two years ago. Archaeologist Guillermo de Anda’s team expects the excavation to take about three months. Because known cenotes lie north, east, south and west of the pyramid, de Anda believes the hidden cavern may represent a fifth direction—the Maya’s symbolic center of the world—and could reveal more about their beliefs.

De Anda previously studied remains from Chichen Itza’s Sacred Cenote, finding that about 80% were children aged 3 to 11. Their bones and teeth showed anemia and malnutrition, but he says further research is needed to determine the circumstances and meaning of their placement there.
The New York court affirmed Enix Bussey’s convictions without opinion on October 16, 1947; all listed judges concurred.

The policy brief argues that the “out-of-school children” (OOSC) indicator inadequately measures educational exclusion because it focuses on formal enrollment, overlooks attendance and learning, and excludes informal and non-formal pathways such as madrasas, community-based programs, apprenticeships, radio, television, and online learning.

Afghanistan illustrates these limitations. Conflict, poverty, insecurity, gender disparities, geographic isolation, nomadic lifestyles, child labor, disabilities, inadequate infrastructure, and sociocultural tensions have restricted formal schooling. Enrollment data may also be unreliable because of chronic absenteeism, inaccurate population estimates, and ghost students and schools. The Taliban’s ban on girls’ secondary education has intensified exclusion, while alternative programs serving girls and other marginalized children remain unrecognized by OOSC measures.

The brief proposes replacing OOSC with an “out-of-education children” (OOEC) indicator that defines education as an activity occurring across an interconnected ecosystem. OOEC would measure formal, informal, non-formal, and technology-based learning, recognize culturally relevant pathways, reveal systemic barriers, and support more inclusive and resilient education systems. It could also reduce ideological conflicts caused by privileging formal schooling and help align education with local needs, global challenges, and SDG 4.

Implementing OOEC would require data systems that capture participation, curricula, learning experiences, educator competencies, costs, and outcomes across all pathways. Credentialing systems would need to validate diverse forms of learning and ensure their acceptance by higher education institutions and employers. Policymakers would also need to distribute resources more equitably and strengthen collaboration among governments, educators, researchers, communities, technology providers, and employers. The transition is presented as a catalyst for fundamentally reimagining education rather than merely changing a technical indicator.

Passport applicants must swear allegiance, provide a physical description, and submit a credible witness’s certification of identity and facts. Native citizens need this basic application; foreign-born applicants claiming citizenship through a native father must document his U.S. birth, residence, and citizenship. Naturalized citizens must provide naturalization records and details of emigration, residence, and naturalization. Special documentation applies to unmarried women, wives or widows of citizens, children claiming citizenship through a naturalized parent, and residents of U.S. insular possessions.

Passports expire after two years and require a new application. A passport may include an eligible spouse, minor children, and servant; others need separate passports. Professional titles are excluded. Officials may reject applications sought for improper purposes or failing to meet requirements. The passport fee was $1, with additional 50-cent fees for preparing duplicate applications and administering duplicate oaths.

AMD Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) enables selected high-priority firmware fixes to be applied at runtime without rebooting. Updates are distributed as cryptographically signed packages and are non-persistent, requiring reapplication after every reset.
