Packages may modify registers or SRAM, replace complete firmware images, or update firmware components.

SFS tracks the overall runtime patch level through the monotonically increasing SFS Patch Level (SFSPL), individual firmware versions and Security Patch Levels (SPL), and run-once changes through the monotonically increasing System Patch Level (SYSPL). Packages validate existing firmware versions, patch levels, and operational state before applying. Multiple packages must be applied sequentially, and updates proceed only if all package components validate.

The AMD Security Processor (ASP) verifies AMD signatures and executes packages. OEMs, ODMs, and customers may require co-signing by configuring BIOS settings and providing an RSA public key during early boot. Co-signed packages are verified first against the customer key and then AMD’s key. SFS and co-signing are disabled by default and require BIOS opt-in.

A customer-provided deployment agent places commands, packages, and optional co-signing data in aligned memory and communicates with the primary ASP through the TEE mailbox interface. The ASP protects the memory from x86 access, verifies signatures, runs the patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status. Version information, including firmware versions, SPL, SYSPL, and SFSPL, is available to the host OS.

SFS supports multi-socket systems and attestation interfaces. SEV updates are automatically committed against rollback; reverting them requires rebooting. SNP update pages must be HV-FIXED. Packages target specific firmware and system-level combinations and are designed to minimize performance impact. SEV or SEV/ES virtual machines may need restarting for SEV firmware updates, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

Patriarch Theophilos III said the Jerusalem Orthodox Church would appeal a court ruling upholding the 99-year lease of three East Jerusalem properties to settler-linked organization Ateret Cohanim. The church disputes the decade-old deal as illegal and calls the ruling politically motivated. Theophilos also warned of efforts to restrict Christian churches’ property rights and urged church and world leaders to respond.

The EU announced a €545 million renewable energy and electrification package for Africa under its Global Gateway initiative. Projects include transmission infrastructure in Côte d’Ivoire, rural electrification in Cameroon, wind and hydropower in Lesotho, and mini-grids in Madagascar. The program aims to expand electricity access, reduce fossil-fuel dependence, and potentially create 38 million green jobs by 2030.

Global Gateway, budgeted at €300 billion through 2027, also seeks to counter China’s $1.3 trillion Belt and Road Initiative and strengthen European access to Africa’s critical minerals. China remains a major investor, with $39 billion in African energy contracts in the first half of 2025 and sharply rising solar-panel exports.

Western initiatives also include G7-backed energy projects and the Lobito Corridor railway connecting Zambian copper and Congolese cobalt mines to Angola. Africa’s growing population, limited electricity access, fossil-fuel-heavy energy system, and mineral resources make it central to geopolitical competition and global decarbonization.

Photos document contestants’ correct and incorrect attempts, reactions, and celebrations during the third round of the Scripps National Spelling Bee in Oxon Hill, Maryland, on May 30, 2018. Participants ages 9 to 15 came from across the United States and South Korea.

S&P downgraded Bridgeview, Illinois, four notches to junk-level BB-minus, citing debt from its underperforming Toyota Park stadium, an approximately $256 million general obligation debt burden, and weak liquidity. The rating remains under review for further downgrade as Bridgeview considers restructuring $24.5 million in variable-rate bonds.

A take-a-knee chart helps football coaches determine when an offense leading late can safely run out the clock. In victory formation, the quarterback kneels after the snap, allowing the game clock to continue while resetting the play clock. Effective clock management requires coaches to practice late-game scenarios and understand timing rules. High school and college football generally use a 40-second play clock and lack the NFL’s two-minute warning. Incomplete passes stop the clock, potentially giving opponents time for a comeback.

GOLDWOOD emphasizes uncompromised quality, timely delivery, customer service, mutual trust, employee growth, and environmental safety. Based in Yamunanagar, Haryana, the company manufactures plywood, block boards, and flush doors for customers across India, aligning sustainable development with its business goals.

The 9 EMA strategy uses the 9-period exponential moving average to identify short-term trends. A price move above the EMA generates a buy signal, while a move below generates a sell signal. It can be applied to stocks, forex, commodities, options, and cryptocurrencies, and combined with indicators such as RSI, Bollinger Bands, MACD, volume, candlestick patterns, or longer-term moving averages.

Risk can be managed through stop-loss orders, position sizing, diversification, defined exits, limited leverage, and avoiding emotional trading. Backtesting showed stronger performance in trending assets than in mean-reverting markets. On Bitcoin, the crossover system produced 284 trades averaging 2.65% each, with a maximum drawdown of 83%. Adding a 200-day moving-average filter reduced trades to 153 and increased the average gain to 4%. Results on the S&P 500/SPY were poor, though the filter provided some improvement. The strategy is therefore presented as more suitable for assets displaying trends or short-term momentum.

ML²B is a multilingual benchmark for evaluating LLM-generated end-to-end machine-learning pipelines. It contains 30 Kaggle competitions—24 public and six private—covering tabular, text, and image tasks across 12 domains. Task descriptions were translated into 13 languages, producing 390 evaluation instances. Translations and standardized data cards were manually reviewed for clarity and information leakage.

The benchmark includes a pipeline for task preparation, isolated Docker execution, and code grading. Submitted code is executed directly using either a single-function or modular format. The modular format separates training, validation preparation, and prediction to reduce preprocessing leakage. Performance is measured through Kaggle leaderboard percentiles, enabling comparison across competitions with different metrics.

Evaluation of five LLM configurations using AIDE and ML-Master found 15–45% performance degradation on non-English tasks. English generally produced the strongest results, while Kazakh, Belarusian, and Romanian had poorer rankings and more non-functional code. Image categorization and text classification were comparatively stable, whereas tabular classification and regression showed greater cross-lingual instability. AIDE single models performed strongly in several English settings, while hybrid ML-Master systems often improved performance in difficult domains and non-English languages. No model was consistently best across all metrics and domains.

Common failures included missing training execution, improper data loading, inconsistent preprocessing, modified function signatures, global dependencies, and incompatible or nonexistent library calls. Static analysis flagged potential leakage in 61 of 554 modular submissions; after excluding likely false positives, 33 submissions, or 5.9%, remained potentially affected. Six private competitions help limit leakage from benchmark tasks appearing in LLM training data. Future work includes expanding private tasks, improving domain balance, strengthening code auditing, and developing multilingual alignment methods for low-resource languages.

The COVID-19 pandemic prompted Greece to implement distance education in preschool settings despite limited school infrastructure, unequal access to technology, and insufficient teacher training. Preschool education ordinarily emphasizes communication, social and motor skills, autonomy, and flexible, play-based learning. Distance education can be synchronous, asynchronous, or blended, but for young children it generally requires parental supervision and strong school-family cooperation.

The study examined kindergarten teachers’ views on distance education and its possible post-pandemic use. An online questionnaire was completed in May–June 2021 by 82 randomly selected kindergarten teachers from Greece’s Epirus region. Most participants were women, had over 15 years of service, and held a bachelor’s degree.

Before the pandemic, over three-quarters were little or not at all familiar with distance education, and 91.5% had never integrated it into teaching. During implementation, 64.6% preferred synchronous education. Webex was used by 88.9%, email by 60.5%, and other tools included e-class platforms, Viber, and Messenger.

Teachers were generally negative about integrating distance education into kindergarten. Around 90% believed it restricts psychomotor activities and requires adult supervision, while 86% considered it less effective than conventional education for developing social skills. Major reported barriers included children’s difficulty using technology independently, inadequate internet and device access, and deficient school infrastructure. Many teachers also doubted its effectiveness for individualized learning, student participation, critical thinking, blended learning, and inclusion of children with disabilities. About half considered it appropriate mainly when in-person attendance is impossible.

Teachers with advanced ICT certification reported greater prior familiarity with distance education than those without certification. No statistically significant relationship was found between years of service and ICT familiarity.

The study recommends improving technological infrastructure, teacher training, interactive resources, user-friendly platforms, and support for families. Because the research was limited to Epirus, its findings cannot be generalized safely to all Greek kindergarten teachers.

Mark Palmer forwarded a class-action complaint against major California electricity generators, noting a reporter said Enron’s suit would be similar. Filed by San Diego resident Pamela Gordon on behalf of approximately 1.2 million SDG&E customers, the complaint alleges that Reliant, Southern, NRG, Dynegy, AES, Williams, Duke, and others manipulated wholesale electricity markets beginning in May 2000.

The complaint claims defendants exploited confidential real-time generation and transmission data, withheld capacity, shifted sales from forward to real-time markets, exported and later resold power at inflated prices, coordinated outages, and aggravated transmission congestion. It alleges these practices produced artificial shortages, record prices, windfall profits, and roughly $4 billion in customer overcharges. It cites findings by FERC, CPUC, and CAISO that summer 2000 prices were unjust, unreasonable, or reflected substantial market power.

The action asserts antitrust, unfair competition, consumer-remedy, and unconscionability claims. It seeks class certification, treble or statutory damages, restitution, disgorgement of profits, interest, attorneys’ fees, and injunctions against market manipulation and unjust rates.

The Missouri Student Union held its annual Veterans Day wreath-laying ceremony, participating in the National Remembrance Day Roll Call for fallen MU student veterans. Keynote speaker and alumnus Col. Roderik Cox emphasized veterans’ commitment and challenged Hollywood stereotypes, describing them as ordinary professionals and students. MU Veterans Center director Robert Ross said the event honors sacrifice, promotes hopes for peace and shows appreciation for veterans, including more than 400 student veterans on campus. A reception followed at Memorial Union.

Effective law enforcement often depends on little-noticed legislation opposed by interested parties. The Government increasingly uses criminal proceedings in trust and interstate commerce cases after civil enforcement proved insufficient; despite some failures, fines and imprisonment have deterred offenders.

Judge Holt described a railroad rebate case as clear, flagrant, deliberate, and potentially capable of driving competitors out of business. He argued that such prolonged, secret discrimination by educated business leaders and a corporation entrusted with public privileges was especially serious. Because rebate prosecutions were rare due to difficulties obtaining evidence, Holt concluded that the penalty should reflect the offense’s gravity, with the corporation bearing the principal punishment because its traffic manager acted without personal gain and presumably followed company policy.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s 2018 Form 10-K describes operations across North America, International, and AWS. Amazon serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators through online and physical stores, devices, media, fulfillment, advertising, publishing, and cloud services. Whole Foods Market results have been consolidated since its August 2017 acquisition.

In 2018, net sales rose 31% to $232.9 billion, comprising $141.4 billion from North America, $65.9 billion from International, and $25.7 billion from AWS. Operating income increased to $12.4 billion, while net income reached $10.1 billion, or $20.14 per diluted share. Operating cash flow was $30.7 billion. At year-end, Amazon had $162.6 billion in assets, $50.7 billion in long-term obligations, and $41.3 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. It employed approximately 647,500 people.

North America and AWS generated 2018 operating income of $7.3 billion each, while International recorded a $2.1 billion operating loss. Cost of sales was $139.2 billion, fulfillment expense was $34.0 billion, and technology and content expense was $28.8 billion. Cash capital expenditures totaled $11.3 billion.

Amazon emphasizes customer focus, invention, operational excellence, long-term thinking, selection, price, convenience, and reliable fulfillment. Its financial focus is sustainable long-term free cash flow through sales growth, cost management, working-capital efficiency, and strategic investment.

Principal risks include intense competition, rapid expansion, fluctuating results, international regulation, fulfillment and data-center complexity, seasonality, acquisitions, foreign exchange exposure, dependence on key personnel, cybersecurity and system interruptions, inventory management, intellectual-property disputes, stock-price volatility, evolving regulation and taxation, supplier dependence, government contracts, product liability, payment processing, and fraudulent or unlawful seller activity.

Louisiana registered nurse Joy Williams will be featured in Worldwide Leaders In Healthcare. With over seven years’ experience, she earned practical nursing credentials in 2009 and a nursing bachelor’s degree in 2016. She belongs to two national nursing associations.

It emphasizes governance, security, explainability, privacy, access controls, and regulatory compliance. Passports expire two years after issuance and require a new application; certain naturalized citizens may use an old passport as naturalization evidence. One passport may include an applicant’s spouse, minor children, and eligible servant, but others require separate passports. Professional titles are excluded. Each citizen’s application requires a one-dollar fee by currency or postal money order; checks and drafts are rejected. The State Department does not obtain foreign visés, supplies application forms under stated limits, and may reject applications for improper purposes or rule violations. In U.S. insular possessions, applications go to the chief executive. Passports are limited to persons owing U.S. allegiance. Applications must be sworn, properly authenticated, and state birth, occupation, residence, temporary travel, and intent to return and fulfill citizenship duties.

Ray Dalio’s All Weather Portfolio is a diversified, defensive strategy using stocks, bonds, and commodities to perform across inflation, deflation, and stagflation. Its emphasis on diversification, low correlation, and risk balance aims to smooth returns and reduce drawdowns rather than maximize growth.

A backtest from July 2007 produced a 4.5% CAGR without dividends, compared with 6.7% for the S&P 500, but followed a smoother path. The portfolio’s maximum drawdown was 17% during the financial crisis, approximately 6% during the 2020 Covid-19 selloff, and about 12% in 2022. Leveraging it 1.5 times increased CAGR to 6.5% and maximum drawdown to 25%, excluding leverage costs.

The portfolio tends to outperform when stocks struggle and underperform during equity bull markets. It may suit conservative investors, retirees, and FIRE participants, while younger investors may prefer greater stock exposure. Rebalancing once or twice annually is suggested, preferably in a tax-deferred account. Future performance is not guaranteed.

Small-group differentiation tailors content, learning processes, products, assessments, and environments to students’ readiness, interests, abilities, linguistic needs, and cultural backgrounds. It may benefit students at all achievement levels and is increasingly relevant as U.S. schools become more culturally, linguistically, and academically diverse.

A systematic review of literature published from 2000–2023 examined differentiation, student diversity, and learning outcomes in elementary and higher education. The research was guided by constructivist and sociocultural theories, which emphasize active knowledge construction, prior experience, social interaction, collaboration, and teacher scaffolding.

Effective differentiation involves flexible goals and materials, ongoing assessment, appropriately challenging experiences, collaboration, and student responsibility. Small groups can support personalized instruction, skill reinforcement, discussion, peer relationships, engagement, and gradual progression to more complex tasks. Teachers may use instructional-level resources, visuals, verbal scaffolding, open-ended questions, reflection exercises, and individual or group assessments. Groups can become student-led when learners are ready.

Implementation differs by setting. Elementary students generally require greater teacher guidance and foundational instruction, while higher education emphasizes specialized content, independence, choice, and self-directed learning. Inclusive and culturally responsive materials may support linguistically and culturally diverse students, including international graduate students.

Challenges include large classes, limited planning time, insufficient administrative support, changing student groups, and the need to understand students’ prior knowledge, interests, strengths, disabilities, and learning needs. Differentiation is especially important given substantial numbers of English-language learners and students receiving special education services.

The review found limited empirical research comparing differentiated or small-group instruction across settings or linking it with test scores, benchmarks, and learning outcomes. It recommends longitudinal research following students from elementary through higher education and studies examining outcomes associated with visual, auditory, kinesthetic, and read/write learning styles.

The 4-3 defense uses four defensive linemen, three linebackers, and four defensive backs, emphasizing smaller, athletic front-seven players. Developed in the NFL by Tom Landry, modernized by Jimmy Johnson, and later associated with Tampa Bay’s “Tampa 2,” it traditionally features two 5-technique ends, a 1-technique nose guard, and a crucial 3-technique defensive tackle.

The ends control one gap and contain the quarterback; the nose guard handles the strong A gap and double teams; and the 3-technique creates interior pressure. The Sam, Mike, and Will linebackers decrease in size and increase in athleticism from strong side to weak side. The Mike must defend both run and pass, while the Will is typically the most athletic.

The scheme is strong against the run because it places seven defenders in the box and assigns each defender a gap. Four defensive backs also permit varied coverages. However, spread formations can pull linebackers from the box, create coverage mismatches, and force defenses into nickel personnel. Offenses also attack the edges with outside-zone concepts and additional blockers.

Common pressure packages include a Will edge blitz and a zone blitz in which a defensive end drops into coverage while the Sam and Mike rush. Common coverages include Tampa 2, where the Mike drops into the deep middle between two safeties, and Cover 3, featuring three deep defenders.

Notable users include the early-2000s Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the 2006 NFC champion Chicago Bears under Lovie Smith, and Montini Catholic High School under Mike Bukovsky, which achieved multiple Illinois state championships and runner-up finishes.

The paper presents the Atlas of Human-AI Interaction, an open-source framework that uses large language models to synthesize empirical findings from human-AI interaction research. Addressing fragmented literature and limitations of topic-, citation-, and keyword-based reviews, the Atlas maps findings as cause–relationship–effect triplets in a navigable knowledge graph.

The authors collected 1,888 abstracts from ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, Springer Nature Link, and ArXiv. Claude Opus 4.1 identified extractable empirical findings in 1,124 papers, producing 2,037 findings. Entities were normalized, embedded, merged for synonymy, and semantically clustered before graph construction. The resulting graph contains 1,310 nodes and 3,908 edges. A web interface provides three complementary modes: a 3D Graph View for exploring themes and gaps, a Cause-Effect View for tracing relationships, and a Paper View for reviewing individual studies.

Analysis identified clusters involving human stakeholders, AI technologies, and concepts, with substantial research attention on educational contexts, explanation and trust, design, decision support, and human-AI feedback loops. Network analysis found 126 research communities and highlighted large language models, generative AI, trust, chatbots, and autonomous agents as major opportunities for cross-community synthesis. Proposed research directions include universal LLM interaction patterns, generative-AI collaboration models, transferable trust mechanisms, unified agent-interaction theory, and cross-domain testing frameworks.

A study with 20 human-AI interaction experts found that the Atlas supported landscape visualization, relationship discovery, and research-gap identification. Participants valued spatial exploration, rapid validation of relationships, and interdisciplinary discovery. However, they requested deeper paper information, broader and historical coverage, temporal analysis, clearer relationship interpretation, and stronger support for technical or mathematical research. The authors position the Atlas as an exploratory complement to, rather than replacement for, existing literature-review workflows.

Future work includes continuous publication updates, richer relationship types, improved extraction and verification, contradiction resolution, and more advanced network analysis.

Please, Continue (Hamlet), created by Yan Duyvendak and Roger Bernat, stages Hamlet’s trial for Polonius’s murder using real judges, lawyers and courtrooms, with actors portraying Hamlet, Ophelia and Gertrude. After legal arguments and forensic evidence, 12 audience members deliberate as a jury. Performed internationally since 2011, each production follows its host country’s laws and is limited to jurisdictions with jury systems.

Inspired by Guantanamo trial transcripts and research into criminal trials, the work places a fictional Hamlet scenario within a real legal process. It incorporates details from an actual case involving a young man accused of killing his girlfriend’s father. The creators’ opposing views of that defendant prompted them to design a performance exposing similar disagreements among audiences. Duyvendak says participants often change their opinions repeatedly, gaining a stronger appreciation of the justice system’s complexity and the difficulty of judging human actions.

This study systematically reviewed metaverse research in education using 270 English-language Scopus journal articles published from 2015 to July 2024. Following PRISMA standards, it applied descriptive bibliometric analysis and VOSviewer to examine publication trends, geographic productivity, influential journals and articles, and keyword patterns.

Publications began appearing in 2020, increased sharply from 2022, and peaked at 131 in 2023; 91 had been published by July 2024. South Korea produced the most articles and citations, while China and the United States were also highly productive, and the United Kingdom ranked prominently in citations. IEEE Transactions on Learning Technologies published the most articles, while Sustainability received the most citations. The most cited article was Dwivedi et al.’s 2022 multidisciplinary examination of metaverse challenges, opportunities, and research priorities.

The most frequent keywords were “metaverse,” “virtual reality,” “education,” “augmented reality,” and “artificial intelligence.” Research primarily addressed two areas: using metaverse technologies to create immersive educational environments and examining students’ and teachers’ perceptions and adoption. Studies reported applications in medical training, virtual universities, educational games, collaborative learning, and teacher preparation. Perceived usefulness, ease of use, enjoyment, and innovativeness were identified as important adoption factors, with attitudes generally positive.

Potential future topics include extended reality, blockchain, sustainability, and gamification. The review identified limited longitudinal evidence on long-term effectiveness, scalability, and adaptability, as well as geographic concentration in East Asia and the United States. It recommends longitudinal and cross-cultural research across traditional, online, and hybrid educational settings.

Security researcher Michael Myng found a disabled-by-default keylogger, described as a debug trace, in Synaptics touchpad drivers on more than 450 HP device models. HP quickly released patches and urged affected users to install them. This was HP’s second keylogging vulnerability that year, following a similar issue involving debugging code in Conexant audio drivers.

The appellate court held that the damages instructions improperly treated mortality-table life expectancies as fixed facts, rather than questions for the jury, and misstated recoverable benefits. The instructions also wrongly permitted consideration of a child’s loss of parental love, assumed college expenses without sufficient evidence, and failed to exclude grief and sorrow. Recoverable damages were limited to reasonably expected pecuniary benefits, including the monetary value of parental care, nurture, and education, but not society, companionship, or affection.

The court found no evidentiary basis for requested issues concerning sole proximate cause or a new and independent cause. It also held that appellees’ counsel improperly criticized appellants for introducing admissible divorce records and that the trial court should have instructed the jury to disregard those remarks. Effective transition defense begins with disciplined offense: protect the ball, select balanced shots, rebound aggressively, and maintain defensive coverage. After missed shots, turnovers, or blocks, players must sprint ahead of the ball while maintaining vision, protect the basket, pressure the ball handler, deny outlets, and force extra passes so teammates can recover.

Players should be trained to defend breakaways and outnumbered situations. Defenders must contain rather than gamble, communicate, prevent layups and second chances, and rebound before counterattacking. In 2-on-1 situations, defenders buy time and anticipate passes; in 3-on-2 situations, they use tandem positioning, pressure the ball, and rotate according to pass direction.

After missed shots or free throws, the nearest defender jams the rebounder, another denies the primary ball handler, and remaining defenders sprint back and match up. Outlet pressure, sideline influence, pass denial, and optional traps can slow penetration and disrupt early offense. Similar recovery principles apply after turnovers and blocked shots.

Coaches should scout opponents’ transition tendencies, require every player to sprint back, and incorporate transition defense into practices and scrimmages. Teaching objectives include awareness, sound offensive decisions, offensive rebounding, defensive balance, outnumbered defense, and determined recovery. The passage recommends the whole-part-whole teaching method and breakdown drills such as full-court one-on-one, three-on-two/two-on-one, and continuous transition exercises.

Johns Hopkins and Mayo Clinic researchers developed a guideline to eliminate CK-MB blood testing for suspected heart attacks. Peer-reviewed evidence and professional guidelines conclude that cardiac troponin is more sensitive and predictive, while CK-MB adds no diagnostic value. Nevertheless, a 2013 survey found that 77 percent of nearly 2,000 U.S. laboratories still used CK-MB. The report recommends hospitalwide education, removing CK-MB from routine order sets, adding computerized ordering alerts, and measuring test use and patient outcomes. It is the first implementation guide from the High Value Practice Academic Alliance, whose future guides will address other unnecessary tests and treatments.

The passage specifies SEV-ES and SEV-SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block protocols for non-automatic exit events. Guests and hypervisors must mark supplied GHCB fields in VALID_BITMAP, clear the bitmap before each exchange, and protect VMGEXIT processing by disabling interrupts and preemption. SW_EXITINFO fields communicate results and errors; nonzero SW_EXITINFO1[31:0] indicates an error.

Guests may handle #VC-triggering instructions or para-virtualize them and invoke VMGEXIT directly. IO, MSR, and MMIO operations require instruction decoding and appropriate GHCB state. String I/O and MMIO may use decrypted shared buffers and multiple VMGEXIT calls.

Page State Change events let guests request private/shared page transitions and SEV-SNP RMP operations, including optional PSMASH and UNSMASH hints. Progress fields support interruption and resumption, while reason codes report invalid structures, state conflicts, overlap, or other failures.

SNP Guest Request events use shared request and response pages to access firmware. Extended requests may return GUID-indexed certificate data, including VCEK and VLEK certificates. Hypervisors validate buffer sizes, return required page counts when insufficient, preserve firmware return codes, and may rate-limit requests. SNP TIO requests similarly exchange trusted-device information, measurements, certificates, and attestation reports through shared data pages.

Additional NAE events support AP creation and removal, VMPL changes, #HV doorbell registration, IPI delivery, timer emulation, APIC ID enumeration, Secure AVIC backing pages, and guest termination. AP creation uses guest-provided VMSA pages and can support vCPU hotplug. Unsupported events use the Unsupported Event exit code.

SEV-ES guests identify support through hypervisor-provided CPUID properties. Traditional AP startup is constrained because measured encrypted register state cannot be modified; alternatives include predetermined reset vectors, AP Reset Hold, AP jump tables, or SNP AP Creation. Without SNP AP Creation, vCPU hotplug is unsupported.

For NMIs, the hypervisor intercepts #DB rather than IRET and waits for an “NMI Complete” message before injecting another NMI. Debug-register virtualization may be hardware-backed; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and emulated. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

Restricted Injection uses a shared #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. The host presents maskable vectors, NMIs, and machine checks through this page and signals #HV when required. Guests atomically acknowledge events, validate vectors, and perform implicit or explicit EOI processing. HLT is executed with interrupts disabled, after which pending events are examined. Non-cooperative host behavior can cause guest denial of service, while non-cooperative guest behavior does not compromise host integrity.

Compass Minerals remains rated “Buy” due to rising salt and plant nutrition revenue and volumes, cost reductions, improved cash flow and EBITDA, and below-peer valuation multiples. The study tests observational estimates of infall velocity in prestellar cores using hydrodynamic simulations combined with time-dependent chemistry and radiative transfer. A collapsing 5 M⊙ Bonnor–Ebert sphere was evolved for 0.87 Myr, chemically post-processed, and used to generate synthetic emission profiles for several molecular tracers and aperture sizes.

Infall velocities were calculated with the Myers et al. (1996) two-slab method using optically thick, self-absorbed CS and HCO+ lines paired with thinner tracers. Although the core’s density and velocity profiles evolved rapidly between 0.81 and 0.87 Myr, synthetic line profiles changed little between these times and varied more strongly with aperture size.

All line-based estimates fell significantly below the true mass-weighted infall velocities of 0.153 and 0.228 km s−1. CS produced estimates reaching roughly half the true value, while HCO+ sometimes underestimated it by an order of magnitude. The discrepancy arises because constant-velocity models do not represent realistic radial velocity profiles: self-absorption generally originates in slower outer regions rather than near the inner peak velocity. Consequently, mass-accretion rates derived from these methods may also be underestimated by up to an order of magnitude.

In the simulations, velocity dispersions from optically thin lines were within a factor of two of the mass-weighted infall velocity and may provide better estimates in isolated cores, though this may not apply to turbulent environments.

William O’Neill developed CANSLIM as seven criteria for identifying strong stocks based on earnings, growth, new developments, supply and demand, market leadership, institutional sponsorship, and market direction. Some criteria are difficult to quantify, making implementation and backtesting demanding.

Investor’s Business Daily applies the methodology through its computer-ranked IBD 50 list, available mainly to subscribers. Backtests since 2003 indicate CANSLIM has beaten the S&P 500, with one report showing an 18% compound annual growth rate versus 9%. However, its small-cap bias, high volatility, substantial drawdowns, and weak performance in bearish and recent markets complicate those results.

The method is primarily intended for long-term investing in fundamentally strong stocks that are trending upward. Risks include volatility, capital loss, and companies failing to meet expectations. O’Neill’s *How to Make Money in Stocks* is identified as the main resource.

The speaker felt the team controlled the latest win, crediting Rucchin’s two goals, Jiggy’s play, and a strong overall performance. After struggling offensively earlier in the finals, he was pleased to contribute and emphasized maintaining the same preparation and approach. He leads primarily by example rather than speaking in the dressing room. He viewed the first two New Jersey losses as uncharacteristic but deserved, saying Anaheim regained its pace at home and now must improve on the road. He described the long series as intense and increasingly antagonistic but typical of playoff hockey. Although winning the Stanley Cup would mean a great deal, his focus remained on preparing for the next game.

Peter Crouch’s widely shared joke about the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge presenting their third child prompted a sharp reply from his wife, Abbey Clancy. Investors are buying exchange-listed closed-end equity mutual funds trading below NAV because of poor liquidity. Buyers holding until maturity can redeem at NAV, benefiting from the discount and any investment gains. Discounts vary with time to maturity and tax implications; schemes cited trade about 6–10% below NAV. However, opportunities can be difficult to find because many funds trade rarely. Experts suggest targeting schemes with assets above Rs 250 crore, which may have more investors and trading activity.

The talented Warriors often overcame halftime deficits through strong third quarters, including major comebacks against Houston in Games 6 and 7 of the Western Conference finals. However, their ability to “flip a switch” failed in Games 2, 4 and 5 amid defensive problems, poor shooting and turnovers. Analysts Mark Jackson and Jeff Van Gundy praised Golden State’s talent, adjustments and composure but warned that repeatedly falling behind is dangerous and could eventually cost the team. Similar comeback patterns have produced dramatic results elsewhere in sports, but successful endings cannot be guaranteed.

Airbus’s Project Vahana aimed to develop a clean, autonomous, helicopter-style airborne taxi to reduce road congestion and infrastructure costs. The company planned a functional prototype by 2017 and short-haul service by 2021. Other flying-vehicle initiatives included Uber’s proposed VTOL network, Urban Aeronautics’ Cormorant passenger drone, AeroMobil’s land-and-air vehicle, and startups backed by Skype’s co-founder and Google co-founder Larry Page.

Fired Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael Ben’Ary said a false social media post apparently prompted his dismissal while he was prosecuting a 2021 Afghanistan airport bombing that killed 13 U.S. service members and 160 Afghan civilians. A letter bearing his signature accused Justice Department leaders of prioritizing punishment of President Trump’s perceived enemies over national security. Pro-Trump commentator Julie Kelly had suggested Ben’Ary was allied with former Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco and resisted indicting former FBI Director James Comey.

Aspen is replacing its Fourth of July fireworks with a 15-minute show featuring 50 drones due to wildfire risks and Colorado fire restrictions. The drones will display patriotic colours accompanied by music. Officials hope drone shows can offer a safer alternative amid increasing fire dangers.

Jio announced offers for Samsung Galaxy J2 2018 and Galaxy J7 Duo, including Rs 2,750 cashback through 55 vouchers. J2 buyers receive 100GB additional data with Rs 198 or Rs 299 plans, while J7 Duo buyers receive double daily data. Valid until September 30, both phones are sold online and offline. The J2 has a 5-inch display and 2GB RAM; the J7 Duo has a 5.5-inch display and 4GB RAM.

The passage states that U.S. national debt surpassed $21 trillion, increasing by $73 billion in one day, $215 billion in February, and more than $1 trillion over six months despite positive economic conditions. It argues that debt is growing faster than the economy: national debt rose 6% in the previous year compared with 4.4% nominal GDP growth. From 2008 to a decade later, GDP increased 36%, from $14.5 trillion to $19.7 trillion, while debt rose 123%, from $9.4 trillion to over $21 trillion. The author rejects claims that debt does not matter because much is owed domestically, warning that default could harm Social Security, banks, and the Federal Reserve, and urges readers to recognize possible future consequences and prepare accordingly.

Seattle Children’s Pediatric Advanced Care Team offers journaling sessions to help parents express difficult emotions. Meagan Holt, whose 3-year-old daughter Madeline has life-threatening Zellweger Syndrome, says writing provides relief and helps her cope. The donation-funded program can foster calm, empowerment and acceptance.

Amazon.com filed a Form 8-K on October 27, 2022, announcing its third-quarter 2022 financial results. The filing includes the related press release, information concerning non-GAAP financial measures, and the Inline XBRL cover page. CFO Brian T. Olsavsky signed the report.

The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau finalized rules requiring payday and auto title lenders to verify borrowers can repay loans within 30 days and limiting repeated account debits. Consumer advocates say such loans trap borrowers through rollovers, high fees and interest rates exceeding 300 percent; a CFPB study found over 80 percent were rolled over or followed by another loan within two weeks. Industry representatives warn the rules could restrict credit and drive borrowers toward unregulated lenders. The CFPB estimates loan volume could halve and many stores could close. The rules are scheduled for 2019 but face possible reversal by congressional Republicans seeking to weaken the CFPB and Dodd-Frank. A Pew poll found 70 percent of surveyed adults favored greater payday-lender regulation.

The patent describes a micro light-emitting-diode device and manufacturing method designed to provide reliable electrical connections between luminous bodies and electrodes. The device includes a thin-film-transistor substrate, alternating first and second diode electrode lines, a first passivation pattern, cylindrical micro LEDs, and first and second bridge patterns connecting opposite semiconductor ends of the LEDs to respective electrodes. Each micro LED contains an inorganic light-emitting material with sequential p-type, intermediate, and n-type semiconductor layers surrounded by an insulating protective layer.

The micro LEDs and first passivation pattern have aligned sidewalls forming substantially continuous planes. This reduces steps along the bridge patterns and minimizes connection breakage. Barrier ribs and reflective electrode materials may improve light efficiency, while additional passivation layers insulate and protect components.

A display embodiment includes multiple light-emitting units controlled by scan, data, power-supply, and timing circuits. Each unit may use three switching transistors, a storage capacitor, and multiple aligned micro LEDs.

Manufacturing includes forming electrodes, depositing a first passivation layer, placing and electrically aligning micro LEDs between electrodes, and depositing a second passivation layer. A single mask process with two etching stages forms the passivation patterns: a longer, relatively anisotropic first etch removes most material, while a shorter, more isotropic second etch using an oxygen-containing additive gas aligns the passivation and LED sidewalls. Separate mask processes then form the first bridge, an insulating third passivation layer, and the second bridge.

Thursday’s MLB wild-card round features three winner-take-all Game 3s, only the second time three such playoff games have occurred in one day. Detroit must improve with runners in scoring position after stranding a franchise postseason-record 15 runners in Game 2. Cubs-Padres is expected to be a low-scoring bullpen battle, with starters Jameson Taillon and Yu Darvish likely on short leashes. Boston needs pitching length after using six relievers in Game 2 against the Yankees’ potent lineup.

Happy Home Furnishers is closing its Neath town-centre store after 33 years, citing anti-social behaviour, limited free parking and rising business rates. Director Mike Semmens said street works disrupted trade and a council-installed bench attracted drinking, fights and other disorder, deterring customers and forcing staff to clean hazardous waste. Other traders reported similar problems, particularly in summer, though some said the impact was limited.

Neath Council said the street improvements benefited the town, the bench was intended for people with mobility issues and was removed after misuse. It is working with police and partners to reduce anti-social behaviour. The council also highlighted a 600-space car park, some free parking and regeneration events.

Semmens said business rates had increased substantially, although Neath was no worse than other towns. The Welsh Government said relief schemes support small and medium-sized businesses. Happy Home Furnishers will continue operating elsewhere and may seek another Neath location.

African countries were urged at the 18th VADA Forum in Lilongwe to use modern technology and electronic fiscal devices to improve VAT compliance and revenue collection. Officials highlighted challenges from cash-based economies, tax-evasion schemes and informal business practices. VADA’s 10 member countries share solutions to strengthen domestic revenue mobilization, while providing technical support to at least 12 non-member countries.

The Ravens traded pass rusher Odafe Oweh and a 2026 fifth-round pick to the Chargers for safety Alohi Gilman, freeing about $8 million in cap space. Oweh, who has no sacks through five games after recording 10 last season, addresses Los Angeles’ need for an edge rusher. Gilman adds experience to a Baltimore defense allowing an NFL-worst 35.4 points per game and ranking 31st against the pass. The Ravens are 1-4, tied for the worst start in franchise history.

Sarcomas are genetically and clinically diverse, with limited responses to chemotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI), creating a need for predictive biomarkers. Researchers analyzed pretreatment transcriptomes from 67 patients with more than 10 sarcoma subtypes enrolled in three ICI combination trials, then assessed findings in 190 TCGA sarcoma samples.

Tumors separated into immune-hot and immune-cold groups based on inferred immune-cell infiltration. Immune-hot tumors had greater immune-cell abundance, higher checkpoint-gene expression, lower tumor purity, and better ICI outcomes. Their objective response rate was 30% versus 8.1% for immune-cold tumors, while median progression-free survival was 3.65 versus 1.7 months. These groups broadly corresponded to previously reported sarcoma immune classes.

Expression models identified transposable elements (TEs) and the chromatin-interacting transcription factor IKZF1 as predictors of immune type. Six TE subfamilies and IKZF1 showed greater expression in immune-hot tumors. Higher TE scores and IKZF1 expression correlated with cGAS-STING, type I and II interferon, antigen-processing, CD8+ T-cell effector, and PD-L1 activity. Both were associated with longer progression-free survival; high IKZF1 expression also corresponded to a significantly higher response rate. Conditional-independence analysis supported a model in which IKZF1 regulates TE expression, which then influences immune type, although functional validation is required.

In the TCGA validation cohort, tumors again separated into immune-hot and immune-cold clusters. Immune-hot status, high TE scores, and high IKZF1 expression were associated with immune-pathway activity and longer overall survival.

The study proposes pretreatment immune status, TE expression, and IKZF1 as potential biomarkers for ICI outcomes and suggests that pharmacologically de-repressing TEs could help convert immune-cold tumors to immune-hot states. Limitations include the small, heterogeneous treatment cohort, differing ICI regimens, differences between the study and validation cohorts, polyadenylated RNA selection, and analysis of epigenetic genes largely as independent factors.

The President clarifies that his earlier message did not deny Congress’s constitutional authority to regulate the custody, location, removal, and disposition of public money and property. He claims no executive authority over such assets except as granted by law and requests that this clarification be entered with the original message in the Senate journal.
The figures show perspective, front, back, side, top, and bottom views of two analytical instrument embodiments. Features depicted in broken lines are excluded from the claimed design.

The lecture reviews scalar-field propagators as heuristic particle transition amplitudes and field correlation functions. Feynman propagators are time-ordered, while retarded, advanced, Feynman, and anti-time-ordered Green functions correspond to different contour prescriptions around poles. Equivalent \(i\epsilon\) prescriptions shift poles slightly off the real frequency axis while keeping the integration contour fixed.

In free field theory, vacuum \(n\)-point functions factor into sums over products of two-point functions because creation and annihilation operators must pair. Composite operators such as \(\phi^2\), Hamiltonian density, and the stress tensor can be singular when fields are multiplied at the same point, requiring renormalization.

Interactions can be introduced by adding nonlinear terms, such as a \(\lambda\phi^4\) term, to the free scalar Lagrangian. Unlike quadratic mass terms, nonlinear terms produce interacting fields and nonlinear equations that cannot generally be solved exactly. For small coupling \(\lambda\), the theory can instead be treated perturbatively.

Scattering experiments probe particle interactions. The S-matrix gives transition amplitudes between asymptotically free initial states at \(t=-\infty\) and final states at \(t=+\infty\). It is infinite-dimensional because particle numbers and momenta can vary continuously. For a free theory, \(S\) is the identity; with weak interactions it is written \(S=1+iT\). Momentum conservation allows the interaction term to be separated into a total-momentum delta function and a nontrivial scattering amplitude. Since time evolution is unitary, the S-matrix is unitary, and Hamiltonian symmetries constrain its matrix elements. The LSZ theorem relates scattering amplitudes to time-ordered correlation functions in the interacting vacuum. The next lecture will introduce path integrals as a method for treating interactions.

The study explores physics teachers’ scepticism toward physics education research and its practical value. It used interviews with 13 German teachers to develop attitude categories, followed by a survey of 174 German and Austrian teachers.

Interviews revealed three generally positive and four generally sceptical attitudes. Most participants valued personal teaching experience over research, considered findings difficult to implement, or criticized cooperation between researchers and schools. Nevertheless, many also regarded physics education research as relevant to teaching.

Survey analysis identified four dimensions of scepticism: research’s relevance to individual teachers, feasibility of findings, relevance to teaching generally, and cooperation between research and schools. Four teacher profiles emerged: the Sceptical Ones (14%), who questioned research’s value and applicability; the Uncertain Ones (27%), who held mostly neutral or unclear views; the Undersupplied Ones (41%), who valued research but found its findings insufficiently applicable and poorly aligned with practice; and the Research Advocates (18%), who viewed research positively while still criticizing research–school cooperation.

Among the examined professional variables, only frequency of reading instructional journals significantly predicted profile membership. Teaching experience, teacher education pathway, school type, and doctoral degree did not. All profiles expressed some scepticism about cooperation between research and practice.

The findings suggest that physics teachers are not generally sceptical, but notable concerns exist about applicability, communication, and researchers’ understanding of classroom needs. The authors recommend stronger integration of research into teacher education and professional development, closer researcher–teacher collaboration, and improved communication of findings. Limitations include small or convenience samples, possible participant self-selection and response effects, probabilistic profile assignment, and imprecise measurement of journal-reading frequency.

Retired civil litigator Marcel Strigberger recounts decluttering law books purchased more than 50 years ago. He revisits memorable contract, property and damages concepts and cases, but decides they have little practical value after his 42-year career and places most books in recycling. He later regrets discarding one property-law volume after seeing a used copy listed online for more than C$1,000. He keeps one five-inch-thick book because it serves as a useful reading stand when he works standing up.

Amazon.com filed a Form 8-K reporting that it announced third-quarter 2018 financial results on October 25, 2018. The filing includes the earnings press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. CFO Brian T. Olsavsky signed the report.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K on March 19, 2020, furnishing a same-day press release under Regulation FD. The filing includes the press release as Exhibit 99.1 and an interactive data file as Exhibit 104. Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn signed the report.

The application describes sidelink positioning methods and apparatuses intended to improve terminal positioning accuracy and reduce latency compared with core-network-controlled positioning. A network device configures first and second terminal devices with sidelink positioning reference-signal resources, sequences, measurement reporting methods, and optional terminal information. The terminals exchange reference signals over a sidelink and measure angle of arrival, receive-to-transmit time differences, or both.

Measurement values may be reported directly between terminals through a PC5 interface or to the network device through a Uu interface. The first terminal or network device determines the first terminal’s relative or absolute position using these measurements and the second terminal’s position, orientation, speed, or measurement time information. Some implementations use bidirectional measurements, while others use a single reference signal or measurement. A second terminal may perform measurements for a first terminal that does not support sidelink reference-signal measurement.

The positioning process may be initiated by a position-information request and hosted by the network device without core-network control. Because nearby terminal devices serve as positioning references and measurements need not traverse the core network, the method is presented as improving accuracy and reducing latency.

The disclosure covers implementations for LTE, 5G NR, V2X, IoT, and later communication systems. It also provides terminal-side and network-side apparatuses, processors, memories, communication interfaces, chips, computer programs, computer-readable storage media, and communication systems configured to perform the methods.

In June 2014, Hertz announced it would restate three years of financial results because of broader-than-expected accounting problems, prompting questions about whether depreciation of its large rental fleet contributed to the issues.

The U.S. car rental industry generated about $36 billion in 2013 and was dominated by Enterprise, Avis Budget, and Hertz, which together held 71% market share. Hertz operated nearly 12,000 locations across 145 countries, employed more than 30,000 people, and maintained over 700,000 vehicles. Acquisitions and new brands expanded Hertz into budget leisure rentals, China, commercial fleet leasing, and equipment rental.

Hertz reported record revenue and EBITDA in 2013. From 2011 to 2013, revenue rose roughly 30% to $10.8 billion, while net income attributable to Hertz more than doubled to $346.2 million. Depreciation averaged about 25% of expenses, and revenue-earning equipment represented more than half of total assets.

Depreciation depends on estimated useful lives and residual values. Hertz depreciated rental equipment using the straight-line method over estimated holding periods, reviewing rates quarterly based on expected disposal values, market conditions, vehicle characteristics, usage, and other external factors. Its estimated useful-life range for cars widened from 5–16 months in 2006–2008 to 4–36 months in 2013. Meanwhile, U.S. purchases of program cars—vehicles covered by manufacturer repurchase or guaranteed-depreciation arrangements—declined from 61% of purchases in 2006 to 18% in 2013, increasing the share of vehicles subject to residual-price risk.

An analyst assembled Hertz and Avis data from 2006–2013 to assess whether fleet depreciation had significance for Hertz’s accounting problems. Over that period, Hertz’s gross revenue-earning equipment increased from $10.9 billion to $18.0 billion, while related depreciation expense rose from $1.8 billion to $2.4 billion.

Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike urged the United States to establish a visa office in Port Harcourt and pursue investment partnerships in agriculture, oil and gas, and industrialization. During a visit by US Ambassador William Symington, Wike accused the NDDC of corruption, financing political ambitions, neglecting proposed state projects, and failing to contribute N900 million toward a Mother and Child Hospital despite the state paying N800 million. He also called for the cleanup of Ogoni land and greater governmental focus on governance.

The speaker emphasizes staying focused as the team returns home, noting that outside expectations and distractions do not decide games. Philadelphia has performed well on the road, while Detroit also understands the importance of winning away from home. Several players have prior experience in similar situations.

Success requires a complete game rather than merely a strong opening. Consecutive penalties strain the team, limit use of the bench, and create territorial pressure, though the speaker says the team generally avoided retaliation and foolish penalties. Close games can change through a single mistake, penalty, or bounce, making sustained discipline essential.

Mike and Chris have formed a strong goaltending tandem. Mike is described as confident, resilient, and able to recover quickly from goals or difficult games. The speaker does not dwell on historical droughts, believing players are focused on the present.

The speaker defends a missed scoring attempt as the correct play against an aggressive goaltender. He also discusses player development, roster moves, defensive pairings, and the contributions of experienced players. Fetisov and Konstantinov have worked well together, while Murphy fits with Lidstrom because both handle the puck effectively. Strong forward coverage has also supported the defense.

The team plans to stay away from home the night before the next game to reduce distractions and maintain its routine. The building’s cooling system is expected to keep the ice suitable.

Reflecting on a previous loss to New Jersey, the speaker says Detroit was then a different, more offensively oriented team that became frustrated by limited shots. New Jersey was stronger defensively, received excellent goaltending, and benefited from experienced additions. Current players have gained experience from that series.

Kirk Maltby earned a role on the left wing through speed and defensive commitment despite the organization’s abundance of right wings. His scoring chances previously did not convert, but they are now going in.

AI could augment cognition, learning, creativity, productivity, and skill development, but over-reliance may weaken critical thinking, knowledge retention, and work satisfaction. Mitigation includes delegating only non-essential tasks, promoting active learning and critical problem-solving, and designing AI as a thought partner rather than a replacement. Personalized learning, interactive assessment, and reduced emphasis on memorization could broaden intellectual development, requiring coordination between developers and educators.

LLMs may alter the social division of labor by expanding access to knowledge, blurring job boundaries, and challenging the role of specialized workers and the middle class. AI may accelerate gig work and flexible collaboration, improving efficiency while risking instability, inadequate protections, excessive workloads, and inequality. Institutional reforms, tailored welfare systems, equitable AI access, education, new industries, and employment opportunities are needed. AI may also enable individuals to participate in dynamic, network-based, and cross-organizational innovation.

In social science, AI and LLMs can expand data access, automate analysis, simulate demographic behavior, code text, and assist in developing hypotheses and theories. However, generated data may misrepresent people, underrepresent minorities, reinforce stereotypes, and enable misinformation. Effective use requires balancing cost and data quality, applying alignment and watermarking, maintaining human oversight, and combining AI search with human interpretation and intuition.

AI governance faces misinformation, deepfakes, bias, discrimination, safety concerns, inconsistent national rules, industry-government communication gaps, and risks discovered only during real-world use. Governance should protect rights, inclusion, safety, transparency, and accountability while supporting innovation. The passage calls for global and cross-sector cooperation, forward-looking regulation, and combined top-down and bottom-up mechanisms through which developers, researchers, users, companies, and governments report risks, investigate them transparently, and update rules promptly.

Coach Vigneault said the team must turn the page after the loss and make adjustments. He described the opponent as highly skilled, structured, physical, experienced and disciplined, with few obvious weaknesses. Every player must bring his “A game,” combining execution, compete level and adherence to the plan; a “B game” will not be enough. The team played well early but struggled against a strong third-period push, while its goaltender kept the game close. Vigneault said speed is among the team’s strengths and must be better utilized. He praised Johnny’s consistency, Rick’s two-way play and scoring opportunities, and a defenseman whose stamina and performance have improved throughout the playoffs.

The TLV32xx comparator family has 1.8 mV internal hysteresis and push-pull TLV321x or open-drain TLV322x outputs. Unused inputs must not be tied together; they require at least 50 mV differential voltage within the specified input range. Push-pull outputs can source and sink current but must not connect to other outputs; unused outputs remain floating. Open-drain outputs support pull-ups from 0 V to 5.5 V, logic translation, and wired-OR operation; recommended pull-up current is 100 µA to 1 mA. Output shorts can cause thermal runaway, so current-limiting resistors are recommended where shorts are possible.

Inputs and outputs include rail-connected ESD protection. Inputs are limited to 0.2 V beyond the rails, and clamp current should remain at or below 10 mA. The power-on-reset circuit holds outputs low for up to 32 µs after the supply crosses 1.65 V.

Comparator output state depends on the relationship between input and reference voltages. Propagation delay increases with smaller overdrive, especially below 100 mV. External positive-feedback hysteresis can reduce chatter near the switching threshold and adds to internal hysteresis.

For low-side current sensing, an amplifier boosts shunt voltage before comparison with an overcurrent threshold. High-speed outputs require careful PCB layout, minimized input-output coupling, and a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic bypass capacitor placed directly at each device. Series resistors can limit input current or damp output ringing. Devices support single or split supplies, provided inputs remain within their recommended range. TI states that application guidance must be independently validated and that the devices require appropriate ESD handling.

CPRE Bedfordshire disputes Central Bedfordshire Council’s plans for 44,000–55,000 homes by 2035, saying Freedom of Information data shows about 60% would accommodate newcomers and that development would harm countryside and strain infrastructure. The assessment identified a need for 32,000 homes, with the council adding 7,400 for Luton residents and up to 20% contingency. The council says government planning rules require housing forecasts to account for migration, population change and affordability.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that on October 20, 2016, it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2016. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act.

Woodstock grief specialists advise bereaved people to plan holiday activities around their tolerance, limit events, have an exit strategy, acknowledge emotions, share memories, practice self-care, and balance new traditions with old ones. The peer-led Surviving Suicide Grief Support Group meets twice monthly at Smith-LeRoy Funeral Home beginning in January; advance registration is required. Additional grief programs include “Understanding Your Grief” in Woodstock beginning April 4 and an eight-week “Healing Journey Through Grief” program in Ingersoll from Feb. 1 to March 22.

The passage urges creation of a Cabinet-level commerce secretary with broad authority over interstate corporations, citing expanding labor, capital, corporate, and international business concerns. It advocates reciprocity with Cuba, emphasizing close political and economic ties, mutual interests, and support for the new republic. It also announces a reciprocal trade convention with Great Britain concerning Newfoundland. The passage favors arbitration over warfare when practical, praises the Hague tribunal, and highlights its successful use by the United States and Mexico. Congress is asked to consider Hawaiian fire claims favorably. Finally, the passage supports immediate construction of an isthmian canal at Panama, notes efforts to secure title and Colombia’s consent, and calls for the project to continue across successive administrations.

President Andrew Johnson submitted correspondence concerning General Ulysses S. Grant’s departure as Secretary of War ad interim. Johnson accused Grant of having agreed either to retain the office while Edwin Stanton’s claim was judicially tested or to resign early enough for Johnson to appoint a replacement. He argued that Grant instead intended from the beginning to prevent Stanton’s exclusion and later assumed an insubordinate position by interpreting presidential instructions concerning War Department orders.

Five Cabinet members provided recollections of the January 14 meeting. Generally, they supported Johnson’s account that Grant had initially believed Stanton would need court action to regain office and had promised notice if his view changed. They also recalled Grant explaining that he later concluded the Senate’s action restored Stanton automatically, that remaining might expose him to penalties, and that he failed to meet Johnson before the Senate acted because of other engagements and an expectation that action would not occur so quickly.

Grant denied intending to disobey any lawful, direct presidential order. He said Johnson’s instruction concerning orders issued through Stanton was ambiguous, so he interpreted continued departmental practice as evidence of presidential authorization until otherwise instructed. Grant cited requests from the Treasury and Post Office Departments that Stanton transmitted to him as evidence that other Cabinet officials continued recognizing Stanton’s authority.

Advocacy is a professional responsibility in special education and should be integrated throughout teacher preparation rather than taught as a standalone lesson. A model undergraduate inclusive education course develops advocacy through policy analysis, reflections, case research, debates, role-based writing, and a persuasive TED Talk and paper. Scaffolded assignments, feedback, and active learning help students practice argumentation, critical thinking, communication, and engagement with opposing perspectives. Such preparation equips future special educators to address inequities, navigate systemic barriers, collaborate with professional networks, influence policy, and advocate effectively for students with disabilities.

North Carolina fell to 2-3 after a 38-10 loss to Clemson, dropping to 0-3 against Power 4 opponents. Coach Bill Belichick blamed poor execution, concentration and coaching but said no structural or personnel changes were planned. While the program described the season as a rebuilding campaign, players rejected that framing and emphasized winning now.

The professor compares near-certain, gradual climate change with the low daily but catastrophic cumulative risk of nuclear war. He identifies fear and distrust as central drivers of nuclear buildup and highlights two major pathways to war: accidental escalation between the United States and Russia through early-warning failures or cyberattack, and escalation from conventional conflict between India and Pakistan. North Korean use is considered less likely.

Cold War arsenals grew to tens of thousands of weapons despite early scientists imagining 100 weapons per side as the worst case. Arms-control agreements later reduced inventories, but the United States and Russia retain roughly 1,500 strategic warheads each, with many missiles on rapid-launch alert. The professor argues that deterrence has contributed to non-use but also creates instability, enables brinkmanship, requires rationality, and cannot deter terrorists.

The Non-Proliferation Treaty limits acquisition of nuclear weapons while obligating established nuclear powers to pursue disarmament. Although fewer countries acquired weapons than once predicted, tensions persist because nuclear states have not provided disarmament timetables or fulfilled other commitments. Iran’s enrichment program is suitable for weapons production, but the professor favors continuing the interim agreement because Iran remains under extensive inspections and states that it does not seek weapons.

Obama’s record is described as mixed: the Prague speech, New START Treaty, inspections, and nuclear-security efforts were positive, while continued hair-trigger alert, weapons modernization, limited engagement with North Korea, and stalled negotiations with Russia were criticized. The professor distinguishes necessary maintenance from modernization and argues that risk minimization—not complete risk elimination—should guide consideration of nuclear abolition. Conventional precision systems such as Global Strike may eventually replace some nuclear roles but could preserve aggressive military postures.

Medical students face substantial stress, burnout, and psychological distress, intensified during COVID-19. This study explored Dubai medical students’ experiences with a six-hour, curriculum-based resilience course grounded in constructivist experiential learning and covering stress, mindfulness, coping, emotional intelligence, and self-regulation.

Researchers conducted a phenomenological thematic analysis of reflective essays from 37 fourth-year medical students at Mohammed Bin Rashid University of Medicine and Health Sciences. Three interlinked themes emerged: awareness, application, and appraisal. Students viewed resilience as a learnable, continuously developed capacity relevant to academic performance, clinical practice, mental health, and patient care. They reported applying mindfulness, meditation, reflection, exercise, cognitive reframing, social support, self-care, gratitude, and spiritual practices. Reported barriers included scepticism, limited time, effort, competing priorities, and difficulty changing habits.

Students generally valued the course, associating it with greater self-awareness, emotional regulation, confidence, healthier coping, reduced stress, and improved relationships and learning. The study supports contextualized resilience training within medical curricula, particularly when designed for self-directed, experiential learning. Limitations include its single-institution cohort, reliance on self-reported reflections, possible social desirability bias, and lack of validated pre- and post-intervention measures.

Avoyelles Parish was projected to spend $8,123 per student in 2017-18, second-lowest among Louisiana’s 69 public school districts. Local revenue accounted for $2,102 per student, also second-lowest, while state funding provided 74.15 percent of its total. Louisiana districts averaged $9,015 per student. The Minimum Foundation Program directs more state aid to poorer districts and adjusts funding for student needs, floods, and small districts. Lawmakers requested a study of actual education costs and potential funding sources by February 2018.

Community-based organizations such as summer camps, mentoring programs, sports leagues and after-school clubs can complement families and schools in addressing urgent youth mental health needs. Because young people already form trusted relationships in these settings, trained staff can recognize distress, provide basic support and connect youth with professionals without turning programs into clinics. However, many workers currently handle crises without sufficient resources, training or institutional support. The authors urge funders to help organizations develop protocols and resource directories, train staff, establish partnerships and referral systems with mental health providers, and address frontline worker stress and burnout. Investing in this infrastructure could create a stronger, more sustainable network of mental health support.

Top stories include continued debate over investigations into Trump administration ties to Russia; possible changes to Israeli-Palestinian peace policy; an arrest following Kim Jong Nam’s death; NATO talks; cracks at California’s Oroville Dam; widespread risky driving; a Boeing union vote; laser-marked produce in Sweden; Kate Upton’s third Sports Illustrated swimsuit cover; and German shepherd Rumor’s Westminster victory.

President Ford’s 1976 EO 11905 replaced the 40 Committee with the Operations Advisory Group (OAG), required formal review of covert actions, and prohibited political assassinations and domestic intelligence involvement. Under President Carter, Hughes-Ryan requirements remained, while the Special Coordination Committee for Intelligence (SCC–I) replaced the OAG, retaining similar procedures and membership. EO 12036 reaffirmed the SCC–I and made the Attorney General and Office of Management and Budget director full members.

The SCC–I created the Special Activities Working Group to review covert-action proposals, but it gradually fell out of use and was supplanted by an interagency group chaired by David Aaron. The Carter administration also used “worldwide” presidential findings for lower-risk, broadly directed covert operations. CIA-drafted and State Department-cleared “Perspectives” supplied detailed policy guidance, while riskier activities required separate findings or Memoranda of Notification. From 1978, worldwide activities were authorized as line-item additions to an existing finding.

Oclaro shares fell 0.99% to a latest closing price of $9.04. Thirteen analysts set an average 12-month target of $9.27, ranging from $6.50 to $11.25, with an average brokerage recommendation of 2.38. Recommendations included 2 Buy, 3 Outperform, 9 Hold, and none for Underperform or Sell. The stock’s ATR-14 was 0.29, weekly volatility 2.50%, monthly volatility 3.07%, and RSI 55.48. Oclaro had a $1.53 billion market capitalization and 169.6 million outstanding shares. Previous trading volume was 1.62 million versus a 5.58 million average.

The introductory real analysis lecture presents two goals: developing proof-reading and proof-writing skills, and proving statements about real numbers, functions, and limits. It defines sets, the empty set, membership, subsets, equality, proper subsets, unions, intersections, differences, complements, and disjointness, alongside standard number systems and their inclusions. A first major course goal is to define the real numbers rigorously.

The lecture explains theorem and proof structure, then proves one of De Morgan’s laws by showing mutual set inclusion. It introduces the well-ordering property of natural numbers and uses contradiction to prove mathematical induction. Induction is then applied to establish the finite geometric-series formula and the inequality \((1+c)^n \ge 1+nc\) for \(c\ge -1\).

New computer modeling and analysis of decades of observations indicate that Uranus emits about 15% more energy than it receives from the Sun, overturning conclusions based largely on Voyager 2’s single 1986 heat measurement. Researchers modeled reflected sunlight and emitted heat using data on Uranus’ atmosphere, clouds, hazes, and seasonal changes. The planet generates less internal heat than Neptune but is not heatless as previously believed. Better measurements could clarify Uranus’ formation, evolution, possible collision history, and similarities to many Uranus-sized exoplanets.

Ahead of Super Bowl LII between the Patriots and Eagles, the author encourages Steelers fans to support Philadelphia and invites readers to a game thread and possible contest. Weekly questions ask readers to predict next season’s playoff teams, Kirk Cousins’ 2018 destination, Nick Foles’ completions, the coin-flip result, Rob Gronkowski’s receiving yards, a combined game statistic, and Alan Faneca’s Hall of Fame selection.

The previous week’s responses covered Le’Veon Bell’s contract prospects, preferred Senior Bowl players for Pittsburgh, interest in the XFL, Pro Bowl fantasy points, and the longest Pro Bowl touchdown. Rashaan Evans was the most desired Senior Bowl prospect. Chris Boswell provided the Steelers’ only fantasy points, while Ben Roethlisberger’s 79-yard pick-six was the longest touchdown.

The final leaderboard is led by Alan Tman with 48.5 points, followed by Darth Blount 47 with 43.5 and DirtDawg1964 with 43. The NFL will also announce its Hall of Fame class and major awards; Tom Brady’s MVP win was reportedly revealed early.

Researchers developed and externally validated logistic regression, random forest, and boosted-tree models to predict pulmonary restriction using demographic, anthropometric, and spirometric data. Development included 42,462 pulmonary function tests from one academic health system; external validation included 24,524 tests from another. Restriction was defined as total lung capacity below the lower limit of normal using current reference equations.

The random forest model performed best overall. In external validation, its negative predictive value was 88.3%, compared with 72.7% for using the forced vital capacity lower limit of normal (FVC LLN). Its sensitivity was higher than FVC LLN interpretation (83.3% versus 46.0%), but its specificity was lower (82.9% versus 94.4%).
