It excluded the need for static lung-volume measurements in fewer tests than the FVC LLN (56.7% versus 78.4%). The model showed excellent discrimination but poor calibration, and performance declined from development to external validation.

Performance disparities remained but were reduced. Among non-Hispanic Black patients, negative predictive value was 74.6% for the random forest model and 49.5% for FVC LLN; among non-Hispanic White patients, it was 90.9% and 79.6%, respectively. Decision-curve analysis favored the random forest model across most assessed thresholds.

Limitations included use of academic health-system data, possible ascertainment bias, poor external calibration, limited racial and ethnic diversity, and an equity assessment based only on performance comparisons. Overall, machine-learning models improved the accuracy and equity of excluding restriction from spirometry compared with FVC LLN, while recommending static lung-volume measurement more often.

The lecture examines competition, fairness, and regulation in digital platform markets. Industrial organization increasingly addresses both excessive cooperation—such as data pooling, common ownership, and algorithmic collusion—and insufficient cooperation involving access to essential platform facilities.

Digital platforms connect consumers with in-house and third-party merchants or applications. Concerns include behavioral manipulation, self-preferencing, contestability, fair access, and compensation. The traditional Chicago School argument holds that platforms benefit from offering rich ecosystems because they can charge consumers more. Three factors undermine this argument: consumer prices may be constrained at zero despite an optimal negative price; platforms may disadvantage third parties to prevent future platform entry or protect their core business; and zero lower bounds may allow applications to earn supranormal profits.

Although platforms resemble public utilities through network effects and low marginal costs, conventional utility regulation is difficult because platforms operate globally, evolve rapidly, and have uncertain investment histories and boundaries. The European Digital Markets Act addresses platform contestability and fairness through designation thresholds, obligations toward third-party merchants, interoperability, portability, and substantial self-enforcement. Limited regulatory resources and uncertainty over technical standards complicate implementation.

Contestability may be promoted through multihoming, data portability, interoperability, and allowing merchants to direct customers toward alternative channels. However, entry can be deterred by fixed costs, network effects, incumbent responses, or acquisitions of potential competitors. Acquisitions may suppress competition without benefiting consumers.

The lecture then develops an access-pricing model for hybrid platforms containing both in-house and superior third-party applications. Applications receive ancillary benefits from advertising, data, merchant fees, or repeat customers, creating negative opportunity costs. Zero lower bounds prevent firms from subsidizing users through negative prices because bots or fake users could exploit those payments.

If access charges are too low relative to ancillary benefits, platforms prefer non-price foreclosure, such as disadvantaging rivals in rankings. If charges are too high, third-party applications are squeezed and may face price foreclosure. Between these extremes lies a region where the Chicago School logic holds and changes in access charges do not affect allocation or profits. The model indicates that an unregulated platform would choose a high charge that squeezes a superior third-party application, while the optimal regulated charge equals the ancillary benefit and is not zero. Because regulators cannot easily observe that benefit, practical regulation requires simple mechanisms for eliciting information and rules that limited regulatory staffs can implement.

Cox challenged a district judge’s authority to grant pharmacist P. H. Bell a liquor permit at a term subsequent to the one for which the application was filed. The court held that statutory directions to hear liquor-permit applications promptly are not mandatory and do not limit a court’s general discretion to manage its docket. If an application cannot be heard during the first term and no vacation hearing is scheduled, adjournment does not automatically dismiss it or remove jurisdiction; it continues to the next term. Courts are presumed to have valid reasons for postponement absent contrary evidence. Because the later hearing was regular and the remonstrants failed to appear independently of the county attorney, the certiorari proceeding was dismissed.

Asian markets remained unsettled ahead of planned U.S. tariffs on $34 billion of Chinese goods and expected retaliation from Beijing. Asia-Pacific shares edged up 0.1%, while Japan’s Nikkei fell 0.5%. Wall Street declined, led by technology stocks, with Facebook, Tesla and Micron posting sharp losses. Micron fell after a Chinese injunction blocked its chip sales, also pressuring Japanese chip-related shares.

The yuan stayed near an 11-month low despite China’s central bank pledging stability, while the Mexican peso surged following spending assurances from the newly elected president. Major currencies were mostly steady, with the euro retaining gains after Germany’s coalition resolved a migration dispute. Oil rose after a larger-than-expected decline in U.S. stockpiles, while copper remained near nine-month lows amid concerns that trade tensions could weaken global growth.

The January 2017 Dugan Stock Scoring System ranked non-REIT and non-MLP companies from David Fish’s 684-company “All CCC” list. Candidates had to rank in the top half and meet thresholds for yield, market capitalization, valuation, payout ratio, dividend growth, projected EPS growth, debt-to-equity ratio and Dugan Score. The system evaluates stock quality across risk, value, past performance and expected future performance, emphasizing current conditions and future prospects rather than historical returns. Scores also receive small adjustments based on three brokers’ sector-weighting recommendations. Applying the 2017 formula and filters produced 21 companies. The information is educational, not investment advice, and the author disclosed holdings in PRU, AIZ, MGA, BBY, HBAN, DOW, ADM, CSCO and RAI.

The Care Quality Commission rated East of England Ambulance Service NHS Trust as Requires Improvement overall after a March inspection. Its caring services were rated Outstanding, while safety, effectiveness, leadership and responsiveness required improvement. Inspectors noted progress in safeguarding, understanding of the Mental Capacity Act and incident reporting, but found failures to meet national response standards, winter-related serious incidents, low staff morale and disengagement between frontline staff and senior management.

Required improvements include emergency response times, consistent procedures, risk-register reviews, and better mentoring and support. The CQC is monitoring progress with NHS Improvement and will reinspect. Chief Executive Robert Morton welcomed recognition of improvements and staff’s outstanding care, while acknowledging pressures and challenges across the trust’s 7,500-square-mile area. He said leadership development and £11.5 million in additional funding would support further improvement.

Temple Grandin will discuss livestock handling and animal behavior from 7–9 a.m. Feb. 23 at Tehama District Fairground in Red Bluff. Sponsored by agricultural organizations, the breakfast costs $15. Contact Josh Davy at 527-3101.

Coach DeBoer said the team has overcome difficult playoff situations before and can rebound after securing its first win. He saw no need for lineup changes made out of panic, noting the team created quality chances but was stopped by Los Angeles’ goaltender. He emphasized scoring first, improving offensive production, and managing frustration. DeBoer praised the officiating and both teams’ discipline, discussed adjustments to travel and the unusual start time, questioned a momentum-changing call involving a lost puck, and said he was not disappointed because his team competed until the final buzzer.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture enables single-GPU real-time ray tracing through dedicated RT Cores, RTX software, filtering algorithms, enhanced Tensor Cores, and advanced shading. It supports Microsoft’s DirectML and DXR APIs and inherits Volta CUDA enhancements. The flagship TU102 powers the GeForce RTX 2080 Ti and Quadro RTX 6000.

Israel and Canada signed a modernized free trade agreement replacing their 1997 pact. The revised deal will eliminate duties on thousands of additional products and add chapters on labor, environment, gender, small and medium-sized enterprises, corporate social responsibility, and improved dispute settlement. Ministers Francois-Phillippe Champagne and Eli Cohen said it would expand market access, strengthen economic ties, increase competition, and support prosperity. The agreement aims to double bilateral trade and will take effect after ratification by both countries’ parliaments.

A Danish study of 4,741 mothers found that children of older mothers had fewer behavioural, social and emotional problems at ages seven and 11, but not 15. Researchers linked this to older mothers’ psychological maturity, emotional stability, tolerance and less punitive parenting, independent of socioeconomic factors. However, later motherhood carries increased risks of miscarriage, premature birth and deformities.

Apple’s unaudited Form 10-Q covers the quarter ended March 30, 2019. Quarterly net sales declined 5% year over year to $58.0 billion, reflecting lower iPhone sales, partially offset by growth in Services and Wearables, Home and Accessories. Net income fell to $11.6 billion from $13.8 billion, while diluted earnings per share decreased to $2.46 from $2.73. Six-month net sales were $142.3 billion and net income was $31.5 billion.

At March 30, 2019, Apple reported $342.0 billion in assets, $236.1 billion in liabilities and $105.9 billion in shareholders’ equity. Six-month operating cash flow was $37.8 billion. Apple repurchased $32.2 billion of stock during the six-month period, including $24.0 billion in the second quarter, and paid second-quarter dividends and dividend equivalents of $3.4 billion. The board subsequently increased the share-repurchase authorization from $100 billion to $175 billion.

Apple introduced updated iPad, iMac and AirPods products and announced Apple News+, Apple Card, Apple Arcade, a redesigned Apple TV app and Apple TV+. The company also disclosed litigation, tax, supply-chain and market risks, including settlements with Qualcomm and ongoing VirnetX matters.
Scientists created functional human egg cells by fusing skin cells with empty eggs and inducing meiosis. The proof-of-concept eggs formed early embryos and may eventually help treat infertility.

Tesla’s 2018 Form 10-K describes the company as a vertically integrated sustainable energy business that designs, manufactures and sells electric vehicles, energy storage systems and solar products. Its two reportable segments are automotive and energy generation and storage. As of December 31, 2018, Tesla had 48,817 full-time employees.

Tesla produced the Model S, Model X and Model 3, while planning Model Y, Tesla Semi, a pickup truck and a new Roadster. It was expanding Model 3 production and international deliveries, targeting production in Shanghai by the end of 2019. Vehicles were sold directly through Tesla’s stores, galleries and online channels and supported by company service centers, Mobile Service technicians, Superchargers and Destination Chargers.

Energy products included Powerwall 2 and Powerpack 2 battery systems, traditional solar systems and Solar Roof. Tesla sold, leased and financed certain products and offered warranties covering vehicles, batteries, energy storage systems, solar installations and Solar Roof.

Manufacturing occurred primarily in Fremont, Lathrop, Tilburg, Gigafactory 1 in Nevada and Gigafactory 2 in Buffalo. Gigafactory Shanghai began construction in January 2019. Tesla relied on hundreds of global suppliers, often single-source suppliers, and partnered with Panasonic for battery cells and solar products.

Tesla identified core capabilities in electric powertrains, battery packs, power electronics, vehicle engineering, manufacturing, software and self-driving technology. Autopilot provided driver-assistance features, while drivers remained responsible for vehicle control.

The company competed with established and emerging vehicle, energy storage and solar businesses. It received government incentives and generated tradable regulatory credits, while operating under vehicle safety, battery transport, dealership, energy and solar regulations.

Key risks included production and delivery delays, failure to meet Model 3 volume and cost targets, limited high-volume manufacturing experience, supplier dependence, component or raw-material shortages, product defects, servicing constraints, uncertain electric-vehicle demand, international expansion challenges, regulatory restrictions, and inability to achieve targeted manufacturing costs and profitability.

Niu Technologies’ stock surged in 2025 amid strong recent growth, but several factors could disrupt the growth already reflected in its valuation. The author believes growth may be insufficient to justify the rally and assigns NIU a neutral hold rating. The author reports no financial position or business relationship with the company.

During cold and flu season, nutritious food supports immune function, energy, recovery, and long-term health alongside rest and hydration. A varied range of colourful fruits and vegetables provides vitamins, minerals, micronutrients, and prebiotic fibre; vitamins A and C, magnesium, and zinc help regulate immunity. Protein supports growth, repair, oxygenation, digestion, hormones, T cells, and antibodies, while insufficient intake can weaken disease defences and reduce energy. Herbs and spices such as ginger and turmeric contain antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, or antibacterial compounds, while coriander, mint, and basil also provide antioxidants. Probiotics from fermented foods support gut health, digestion, nutrient absorption, and immunity. Nuts and seeds supply minerals, fatty acids, and vitamin E, which aids cell repair after infection. These food groups can be incorporated into a balanced daily diet.

This PRISMA-guided meta-analysis examined 13 studies from eight countries, published between January 2015 and July 2024, on AI-related educational technologies. Studies were identified through Google Scholar, ERIC, and Scopus and included applications such as chatbots, generative AI, online learning, virtual reality, learning management systems, and AI platforms.

Using a random-effects model, the analysis found a significant positive overall effect on educational outcomes (effect size 0.86, 95% CI [0.45, 1.27], p < 0.0001). Chatbots and generative AI produced the largest effect (1.02, 95% CI [0.45, 1.59], p < 0.0001). Learning management systems and AI platforms also had a significant positive effect (0.62, 95% CI [0.03, 1.21], p < 0.05). Online learning and virtual reality showed a positive effect of 0.79, but the confidence interval included zero (95% CI [-0.04, 1.62], p < 0.07).

Substantial heterogeneity occurred across analyses (I² 54.03%–93.23%), and publication bias was reported, indicating that outcomes varied by educational context, implementation approach, technology, and student characteristics. Experimental analyses using Naive Bayes-, TF-IDF-, and BERT-based methods, plus a hybrid fixed- and random-effects model, also yielded positive overall effects between 0.84 and 0.88.

The study concludes that AI technologies can improve educational outcomes, particularly chatbots and generative AI, but implementation should account for context and student needs. It recommends larger samples, diverse designs, longer interventions, further validation of the novel analytical methods, and cautious policy development.

Fredrik underwent X-rays after missing several shifts, with a report expected later that day. The coach attributed the loss to a poor start, inaccurate passing, turnovers, weak shot selection and insufficient offensive execution, while rejecting blame on any single player or line. He said Carolina’s speed, defensive pressure, faceoff strength and quick puck movement created difficulties. Special-teams play produced an ice-time imbalance that limited effective players, requiring possible lineup and unit adjustments. Detroit also needed to improve forechecking, zone entries and puck placement. Although the second game was considered crucial to evening the series, the coach said past playoff comebacks had no bearing on the next game.

The Akindele case highlighted widespread sexual harassment in Nigerian institutions. OAU dismissed the professor after finding him guilty of soliciting sex from a student. Other institutions are urged to protect students, investigate abuses, punish offenders, and uphold ethical conduct.

Three youths were killed during a military operation in Shopian that damaged a mosque and homes, prompting protests in which civilians were injured. Two soldiers were killed and others injured in separate attacks, while train services remained suspended. Kashmiri resistance leaders opposed efforts to alter Jammu and Kashmir’s disputed status or Article 35A. A civilian injured in a Srinagar explosion also died.

Tom Evans said his terminally ill 23-month-old son, Alfie, continued breathing unassisted for nine hours after life support was withdrawn at Alder Hey Children’s Hospital. Evans claimed doctors initially withheld oxygen, water and food but later provided oxygen and water after discussions. He said Alfie remained stable but needed further life support. Alfie’s mother, Kate James, praised him in a Facebook post.

Enron disclosed an informal SEC inquiry into related-party transactions involving partnerships formerly managed by CFO Andrew Fastow. The partnerships conducted complex financing and hedging transactions with Enron, raising conflict-of-interest, valuation, accounting and disclosure concerns. Enron said the arrangements were reviewed, approved and properly disclosed, and pledged full cooperation.

The inquiry followed Enron’s $1.01 billion third-quarter charge, $618 million loss and $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity associated with unwinding financing arrangements. Analysts criticized the company’s limited and unclear disclosure. Enron shares fell about 21% to $20.65 amid concerns about management credibility, possible further write-offs, shareholder dilution and obligations linked to off-balance-sheet vehicles such as Marlin and Whitewing. Moody’s placed Enron’s debt under review, though it remained investment grade.

Shareholders filed lawsuits alleging fiduciary breaches and securities-law violations. Reports also highlighted substantial institutional ownership, including Janus’s 5.71% stake, and uncertainty over whether trust assets could repay billions of dollars in financing without stock issuance or asset sales.

This Mendelian randomization study evaluated whether genetically determined pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) causally affects cardiovascular disease risks and whether hypertension mediates these effects. Eleven independent genetic variants associated with PAT were selected from genome-wide association studies; all had adequate instrument strength. Cardiovascular outcome data came primarily from UK Biobank, FinnGen, MEGASTROKE, and the IEU OpenGWAS project.

Greater genetically determined PAT was associated with increased risks of overall cardiovascular disease, heart failure, hypertension, coronary heart disease, ischemic heart disease, ischemic stroke, and venous thromboembolism. No significant associations were found for cardiac arrhythmias, atrial fibrillation, aortic aneurysm, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, myocardial infarction, stroke subtypes, or subarachnoid hemorrhage. Sensitivity analyses generally supported the main findings and found no substantial heterogeneity, horizontal pleiotropy, or outlying variants.

Two-step Mendelian randomization indicated that hypertension partly mediated associations between PAT and heart failure, coronary heart disease, ischemic heart disease, and ischemic stroke, with mediated proportions ranging from 13.23% to 19.18%.

The findings suggest PAT may be a therapeutic target for several cardiovascular diseases and that antihypertensive strategies may provide additional benefits, particularly for people with obesity and greater PAT accumulation. Limitations include restriction to European participants, possible sample overlap, limited case numbers for some outcomes, inability to conduct multivariable analyses, and potential residual bias or pleiotropy. Further research is needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms and associations with other cardiovascular diseases.

“Russian math” is a rapidly growing form of after-school enrichment in the United States. The Russian School of Mathematics serves 22,000 students at 40 locations, while smaller programs such as Brighton’s Studio of Engaging Math also thrive. Classes generally emphasize early algebra and geometry, reasoning, critical thinking, and understanding why methods work rather than relying solely on memorization and drills.

The movement grew partly through Soviet-trained immigrants. Russian School of Mathematics co-founder Inessa Rifkin opened the program in 1997 after concluding that her son lacked expected math skills. Soviet educational traditions included strong teacher training, detailed textbooks, and elite math and physics schools. American programs adapt these traditions through small, ability-based groups, puzzles, manipulatives, and engaging problems.

Parents enroll children because they want greater challenges, preparation for technology-related futures, or alternatives to public-school curricula. Weekly instruction can cost about $2,000 annually, prompting concerns about pressure to participate and widening gaps between families that can and cannot afford enrichment. Schools may also struggle when some students have already learned new material, and teachers report possible overconfidence among participants.

Although honors math enrollment has increased in places where Russian math is popular, available data do not establish causation. Researchers say the methods have not been extensively studied. Supporters nevertheless report that students become more comfortable confronting difficult problems and more willing to think through them.

The patent describes immune effector cells, including T and NK cells, engineered to express chimeric antigen receptors while having reduced or eliminated Tet1, Tet2, or Tet3 expression or function. Tet disruption, particularly Tet2 inhibition, is proposed to lower 5-hydroxymethylcytosine levels and enhance CAR-cell proliferation, cytokine production, degranulation, stem-cell-memory phenotype, and therapeutic efficacy.

Tet inhibition may use CRISPR/Cas9, zinc-finger nucleases, TALENs, meganucleases, siRNA, shRNA, dominant-negative proteins, small molecules, or CAR integration into a Tet gene. The disclosure covers CARs targeting CD19 and numerous other tumor antigens, with various antigen-binding, transmembrane, primary signaling, and costimulatory domains. It also provides vectors, gene-editing systems, manufacturing methods, ex vivo or in vivo Tet-inhibitor treatment, and combined administration of engineered cells and Tet inhibitors.

The cells and methods are intended to treat diseases associated with tumor-antigen expression, including hematologic malignancies and solid cancers. Patient data showed clonal expansion of CD19 CAR T cells containing a CAR insertion between Tet2 exons 9 and 10, fusion transcripts predicted to disrupt Tet2 function, and defective DNA demethylation. Additional experiments evaluated Tet2 knockdown or editing, 5-hydroxymethylcytosine reduction, T-cell phenotypes, CAR expression, proliferation, cytokine production, genomic accessibility, and editing outcomes.

A South African woman declared dead after a crash was found alive hours later in a mortuary refrigerator. Two other occupants died. Distress Alert said paramedics detected no breathing or pulse and followed procedures. The woman was hospitalized, and the ambulance company launched an investigation.

The speaker says the team must maintain its successful road-playoff mindset, expect a desperate opponent energized by its crowd, and establish its own game early. The extra day provides valuable rest and an unusual opportunity to practice adjustments. Improvement should begin with winning more faceoffs, maintaining possession, staying patient under pressure, and executing plays cleanly. Everyone is dealing with injuries, but players are prepared to contribute or have replacements step in. Past playoff experience helps the team avoid looking ahead despite its home success. Playing more aggressively and confidently, as in the previous game’s third period, should create more chances. The speaker also praises a versatile teammate whose effort and small contributions are being rewarded, as well as an intense former-player coach whose recent experience and attention to offensive details help players in every role.

Cruzin’ for Life’s free, wheelchair-accessible van transported more than 2,600 Mission Hope Cancer Center patients and traveled over 34,000 miles during its first year. The service helps patients across several Central Coast communities attend treatments when other transportation is unavailable. The nonprofit raised funds to retrofit the $69,000 van, aided by a $36,000 donation from Santa Maria Energy, and supports operations through annual fundraisers. Patients can request rides directly or receive referrals from nurses and social workers. Driver Chris Magana stocks comfort supplies for passengers. With Marian Regional Medical Center diagnosing more than 700 new cancer cases annually, officials expect continued demand and may consider adding a second van if funding permits.

San Juan Mayor Carmen Yulin Cruz called revised Hurricane Maria death estimates “a day of collective mourning” and accused Puerto Rico’s government of misrepresenting the toll. Harvard researchers estimated 4,645 excess deaths from Sept. 20 through Dec. 31, potentially more than 70 times the official count of 64, though the estimate ranged from 793 to 8,498. Cruz criticized President Trump for not apologizing for the lost lives and said Puerto Rico remained unprepared for another hurricane season. She uses the number 4,645 and the phrase “NEVER AGAIN” as reminders of the victims.

The study developed a rapid, low-depth metagenomic next-generation sequencing workflow combining HostEL, which depletes human nucleic acids using nuclease-coated magnetic beads, and AmpRE, a single-tube library preparation method for both DNA and RNA. The workflow detects bacteria, fungi, and DNA and RNA viruses while reducing preparation time, sequencing depth, and cost.

In spiked plasma, HostEL preserved microbial composition and enabled detection of all ten tested bacterial and fungal species down to 70,000 cells/mL. HostEL-treated samples achieved 96% sensitivity and specificity, compared with 82% sensitivity and 97% specificity without treatment. Clinical validation using 42 plasma samples produced 93% agreement with molecular diagnostic results for samples with Ct values below 33. Comparable performance was observed on iSeq 100, shortened simulated iSeq runs, and MiniSeq, with total turnaround times ranging from approximately 13 to 27 hours.

The workflow’s limitations include reduced detection at low pathogen loads, inability to detect parasites, and validation using limited pathogen diversity, specimen types, and sample numbers. Paths Diagnostics, whose shareholders include several authors, licensed the HostEL and AmpRE intellectual property and partially funded the study.

Celtic’s 2-1 comeback victory at Ibrox put them 19 points ahead of Rangers with a game in hand, their biggest projected gap in 91 years. In 1925-26, Celtic finished 20 points ahead under today’s scoring system. Celtic could surpass that record with nearly half the season remaining.

Backtests using Yahoo Finance data from 2007 suggest NIFTY 50 has a positive end-of-month effect comparable to that observed in US stocks. The proposed strategy buys at the close of the fifth-last trading day of each month and sells at the close of the second trading day of the next month. It produced a 10.5% CAGR, exceeded buy-and-hold performance while maintaining 30% market exposure, and had a 26% maximum drawdown. Although partly curve-fitted and based on a short dataset, results remained reasonably robust when entry and exit dates were varied by several trading days.

Jim Montgomery begins his first full season coaching the St. Louis Blues after guiding them to the playoffs following a midseason takeover. The Blues open Oct. 9 at Enterprise Center and play seven of their first 11 games at home. Their schedule includes 26 Central Division games, an Olympic break from Feb. 5–25, and a demanding closing stretch against Colorado, Winnipeg, Chicago, Minnesota and Utah. Key questions include defensive improvement, development of young forwards, adaptation to Montgomery’s system and performance against division rivals, all of which could determine whether St. Louis earns a playoff berth.

June 4, 2001 reports linked Enron to several political and international energy issues. White House adviser Karl Rove disclosed substantial Enron and other corporate stock holdings while awaiting authorization to divest; other administration officials also had financial ties to energy companies.

Saudi Arabia signed agreements worth at least $25 billion with nine international oil companies, including Enron, to develop natural gas fields, power plants, pipelines and desalination projects—the sector’s first major foreign investment since 1975.

In India, Enron’s Dabhol Power project remained in dispute with Maharashtra’s electricity board over unpaid bills, pricing and contract termination. Indian and foreign lenders planned talks in Singapore, with local creditors seeking to preserve the project while some foreign banks favored withdrawal. Rating agencies cited fiscal reform concerns and the Dabhol dispute when assessing India’s investment climate, though some analysts considered Fitch’s negative outlook unjustified. Power Minister Suresh Prabhu said India would honor international contracts while reforming electricity distribution, tariffs and state utilities.

Nigeria’s president accused Enron of poor performance, excessive pricing and failure to meet obligations on a Lagos power project. In Britain, Enron and Powergen completed the first brokered post-NETA gas-electricity “spark spread” trade. Enron Japan’s chief said Japan remained committed to electricity deregulation, but genuine competition had not yet emerged.

Commentary criticized energy companies and wasteful consumption, while another editorial argued high prices would stimulate supply, efficiency and an eventual energy glut.

On May 2, 2016, NVIDIA announced a settlement with Samsung resolving all pending intellectual property litigation in U.S. courts, the International Trade Commission, and the Patent Office. Each company will license a small number of patents to the other, without broad cross-licensing or other compensation.

TrackR unveiled three Bluetooth tracking products ahead of CES. The colorful TrackR pixel and credit-card-shaped wallet 2.0 use smartphone apps and a crowdsourced GPS network to locate items, with replaceable batteries lasting about a year. The TrackR atlas maps trackers to specific rooms and supports Amazon Alexa. Prices are $24.99, $29.99, and $39.99, respectively, with spring launches expected.

Lightning is not attracted to metal or water; strike locations are primarily influenced by height, pointed shape and isolation. Metal-roofed vehicles offer protection through their roof and sides, not rubber tires. Lightning can strike up to 10 miles from a storm and repeatedly hit the same tall, isolated object. Trees are unsafe shelters because they are likely targets and can conduct electricity nearby. Most leisure-activity lightning deaths occur on or near water, not among golfers.

Thinking Machines Lab, cofounded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati and other OpenAI veterans, has launched Tinker, an API that automates much of the infrastructure required to fine-tune frontier AI models. It currently supports Meta’s Llama and Alibaba’s Qwen through supervised and reinforcement learning, while allowing users to control training data and algorithms and download resulting models.

Beta testers said Tinker simplifies reinforcement learning while retaining substantial tunability. Access applications open Wednesday, with the API initially free and expected to become paid later. The company currently vets users and plans automated safeguards against misuse.

Thinking Machines Lab raised $2 billion in seed funding at a $12 billion valuation. Murati says Tinker aims to broaden access to advanced AI research and counter the trend toward increasingly closed commercial models.

The study reviews links between drama-based pedagogy and STEAM education and reports a qualitative pilot study involving 19 first-year female university students at ELTE University in Budapest. Drama is presented as a participatory, reflective teaching approach that can integrate cognition and emotion, support subject connections, and develop creativity, communication, collaboration, confidence, problem-solving, and critical thinking. STEAM similarly connects academic content with authentic problems through interdisciplinary, arts-based learning.

Participants completed two group activities: representing a butterfly’s life cycle through silent movement and portraying India’s caste system through improvised or scripted scenes. Researchers used participant observation, detailed field notes, and student reflections. Findings were organized around creativity, collaboration, problem-solving and thinking skills, and motivation. Students produced varied artistic interpretations, worked supportively in groups, showed enthusiasm, and reported preferring active, creative learning to teacher-led explanations. Language barriers and uneven participation during preparation were observed, although all students performed.

The study concludes that drama can make STEAM learning enjoyable, increase engagement, confidence, concentration, and understanding, and allow students to express ideas through realistic or imaginative interpretations. Implementation may be hindered by limited time, teacher experience and confidence, curriculum requirements, classroom management difficulties, resource needs, and students’ willingness or ability to participate. The authors caution that the small, demographically narrow sample and participants’ limited experience with STEAM and drama-based pedagogy prevent definitive or broadly generalizable conclusions. The findings are preliminary and require validation through further research.

The application describes autonomous vehicles with multiple independent control systems. A primary autonomous vehicle control subsystem uses diverse sensors and processing resources to plan routes and trajectories and control propulsion, steering, braking, shifting, lighting, and other functions. Independent auxiliary control units provide redundancy for predefined safety conditions, system malfunctions, or events the primary system may miss or mishandle.

Auxiliary units may use dedicated sensors, communication buses, logic, power sources, and vehicle interfaces. They can monitor hazards such as imminent collisions, lane occupancy, cross-traffic, traffic signals, roadway hazards, internal malfunctions, or failure of the primary control system. Based on current or planned vehicle locations, they generate predefined vehicle responses, including braking, steering, stopping, maintaining a lane, changing lanes, pulling roadside, or activating lights. Their outputs may directly override primary commands, receive physical priority at vehicle interfaces, or be sent to the primary system for trajectory verification and replanning.

The auxiliary units can continuously evaluate trajectories supplied by the primary system and return alerts, hazard data, warnings, or recommended actions. Responses may be fixed or adjusted in type, magnitude, or duration according to sensor input and may continue until a hazard clears or the vehicle reaches a safe state. The units may be designed with reliable hardware, firmware, or software architectures, parallel redundancy, predetermined reliability metrics, or Automotive Safety Integrity Level requirements. The disclosed method operates the primary system while independent auxiliary units monitor conditions and either command vehicle interfaces directly or provide priority input to the primary system.

Amazon.com’s 2021 Form 10-K reports operations across North America, International, and AWS, serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, and advertisers. Amazon emphasizes customer focus, invention, operational excellence, and long-term thinking. It employed approximately 1.608 million full- and part-time workers at year-end.

Amazon’s businesses include online and physical retail, third-party seller services, subscriptions, advertising, electronic devices, media content, publishing, fulfillment, and cloud computing. Its markets are intensely competitive, with selection, price, convenience, service quality, speed, and reliability among key factors.

Major risks include competition, international expansion, fluctuating demand, fraud, intellectual-property disputes, foreign exchange movements, rapid growth, fulfillment and data-center operations, cybersecurity, system interruptions, personnel retention, supplier dependence, acquisitions, inventory, payments, stock volatility, regulation, litigation, taxes, product liability, and government contracts.

For 2021, operating activities provided $46.3 billion in cash, investing activities used $58.2 billion, and financing activities provided $6.3 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $96.0 billion at year-end. Cash capital expenditures were $55.4 billion, primarily supporting fulfillment capacity and technology infrastructure, including AWS.

Amazon operated approximately 605.4 million square feet of leased and owned facilities, including offices, stores, fulfillment facilities, and data centers. Researchers developed and externally validated deep learning biomarkers that detect extra-prostatic extension (EPE) and seminal vesicle invasion (SVI) from pretreatment prostate MRI to improve risk stratification for localized prostate cancer.

The primary cohort included 820 Yale patients with biopsy-confirmed prostate cancer treated by surgery or radiation; 612 were assigned to training and 208 to internal testing. External testing used 65 community-hospital patients and 41 patients from the public Prostate-Dx dataset. Ground-truth EPE and SVI labels were based on pathology or radiology reports and expert review. Overall, 24.4% of patients developed biochemical recurrence (BCR).

On the Yale, community-hospital, and Prostate-Dx test sets, EPE model AUCs were 0.719, 0.743, and 0.611, respectively; SVI model AUCs were 0.724, 0.678, and 0.775. Both ground-truth findings and model-derived biomarkers were associated with BCR. Patients classified as EPE- or SVI-positive had lower five-year BCR-free survival after either surgery or radiation.

Combining the two biomarkers improved prognostic performance. Five-year BCR-free survival was 79.3% for patients with neither biomarker, 65.6% for those with one, and 60.0% for those with both. The combined biomarker also distinguished recurrence risk within Gleason score groups and among some patients without pathologically confirmed EPE or SVI.

Integrating the biomarkers into NCCN risk groups reclassified 26.4% of patients and increased the C-index from 0.592 to 0.617. Integration with UCSF-CAPRA increased the C-index from 0.592 to 0.614. Interpretability analyses indicated that model features localized to clinically relevant anatomy and were associated with EPE, SVI, and established risk factors.

Limitations included the absence of overall and prostate cancer-specific survival analyses, no comparison with tissue-based genomic classifiers, and underrepresentation of African American patients. The authors conclude that these MRI biomarkers may improve treatment personalization, while further validation in larger and more diverse cohorts is needed.

The President informs Congress that Britain rejected arbitration of its boundary dispute with Venezuela and challenged the applicability and international legal status of the Monroe Doctrine. He argues that the doctrine remains essential to U.S. peace, safety, institutions, and rights, and applies when a European power extends its control over territory claimed by an American republic. After years of unsuccessful efforts to secure arbitration, he recommends that Congress fund an executive commission to investigate the evidence and determine the rightful boundary between Venezuela and British Guiana. If the commission’s findings are accepted, he maintains that the United States should resist by every means Britain’s appropriation or governance of territory determined to belong to Venezuela, despite the serious consequences such action might entail.

Michael Flynn resigned after reports that he discussed U.S. sanctions with Russia’s ambassador before Trump’s inauguration. Acting Attorney General Sally Yates warned White House Counsel Donald McGahn that Flynn’s misleading account left him vulnerable to Russian blackmail. Reports said Trump knew about the calls weeks before Vice President Pence, who publicly defended Flynn.

Trump responded by condemning intelligence leaks, media coverage, and allegations of Russian connections. Critics argued Flynn may have acted with high-level backing, while lawmakers from both parties increasingly supported investigations into possible ties between Trump’s administration and Moscow and Russian interference in the 2016 election.

The passage suggests Flynn and McGahn could become important witnesses. If Flynn testified that Trump knew of or authorized the conversations, it could implicate the president in inappropriate pre-inauguration communications and in allowing officials to make inaccurate public statements.

The Power Offense, widely used in the NBA, frees shooters through baseline crosses and down screens while attacking both sides of the defense. Wings cross beneath the basket, curl around post players’ screens, and seek open shots, post feeds, or rolling screeners. Players counter defensive tactics with curls, basket cuts, fades, back cuts, screen-and-rolls, post or wing isolations, and screen slips.

The offense emphasizes aggressive offensive rebounding, using inside positioning and two weakside rebounders. Automatic counters include fake crosses, misdirection, back-cut or direct-post entries, and dribble drives against overplayed passing lanes.

If the initial action fails, continuity options include motion, side screens, drive-and-kick action, and triangle-post play. A Single/Double variation allows a primary shooter to choose between single and double baseline screens.

Successful execution requires coordinated screening, post play, timing, nonverbal communication, and defensive recognition. Recommended instruction includes breakdown drills, scrimmaging, and individual skill development. Teams should scout defensive tendencies, prepare appropriate counters, monitor in-game adjustments, vary alignments and entries, target weak defenders, and use side screens late in the shot or game clock.

Northeast Mississippi celebrated several achievements last week. Parkway Elementary volunteer Karmel Davis was named Tupelo Public School District’s 2017 Parent of the Year. Corey Crayton, her daughter and grandson received a three-bedroom Habitat for Humanity home funded by HomeStretch Furniture after completing required sweat equity. The overtime loss was difficult after sustained effort, but the team remains excited and ready to regroup for the next game. Both goalies played exceptionally well, and the team plans to adjust its approach, learn from missed opportunities, and avoid dwelling on the defeat.

The Supreme Court’s October 2025 term will address major disputes involving presidential power, civil rights, social issues and criminal procedure. Cases include challenges to President Donald Trump’s authority to impose tariffs and remove independent agency officials. The administration has also asked the court to review Trump’s executive order restricting birthright citizenship, which lower federal courts have found unconstitutional.

The court will rehear a Louisiana redistricting case concerning whether creating a second majority-Black congressional district violates the 14th or 15th Amendments. The case could affect Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act and other civil rights laws that permit liability based on racially disparate effects without proof of discriminatory intent.

Other cases concern Colorado’s ban on conversion therapy, Idaho and West Virginia laws barring transgender athletes from teams corresponding to their gender identities, and whether police need probable cause to enter a home under the emergency-aid exception. These cases follow extensive summer emergency-docket activity in which the court repeatedly allowed challenged Trump administration actions to proceed, generally through 6-3 rulings.

The passage describes reset, clocking, interrupts, debugging, peripheral capabilities, and electrical/timing requirements for TMS320DM814x devices.

Software Global Warm Reset generally matches External Warm Reset and is initiated through the PRM_RSTCTRL register. Local resets affect only selected modules, while simultaneous reset requests are handled by priority. PCIe and EMAC support reset isolation under specified software and register controls. Reset behavior includes RSTOUT_WD_OUT signaling, power-domain warm and cold resets, and most I/O pins entering Hi-Z except designated emulation, isolated EMAC, and reset-status pins. After reset, the Cortex-A8 executes internal Boot ROM code, which configures boot-related pin multiplexing.

Device clocks originate from DEV and optional AUX references using crystals with internal oscillators or external 1.8-V LVCMOS clocks. DEV is normally 20 MHz, with conditional support for 20–30 MHz; AUX supports 20–30 MHz. PCIe requires a low-jitter, AC-coupled differential SERDES clock. Optional audio and 32768-Hz references and two selectable clock outputs are supported. The device contains 12 top-level and four embedded PLLs, which start in bypass mode and must remain within specified frequency and module-clock limits.

The ARM Cortex-A8 interrupt controller handles up to 128 programmable-priority requests. The C674x DSP controller combines up to 128 events into 12 prioritized CPU interrupts and supports multiplexed event sources.

Peripheral features include:
- Two CAN 2.0A/B interfaces.
- EDMA with up to 64 channels and 512 parameter entries.
- Advanced Event Triggering, real-time trace, and IEEE 1149.1 JTAG debugging.
- A three-port gigabit Ethernet switch supporting MII, GMII, RMII, RGMII, QoS, flow control, and shared MDIO management of multiple PHYs.
- Four 32-channel GPIO modules, providing up to 128 GPIO pins and configurable interrupt generation.
- GPMC interfaces for NOR, NAND, SRAM, pseudo-SRAM, and custom logic, plus BCH-based error location.
- An HDMI 1.3a transmitter supporting digital video, multichannel audio, DVI, DDC, and CEC. TMDS routing requires controlled impedance and careful PCB layout.
- HD video processing with capture, display pipelines, scaling, de-interlacing, compositing, format conversion, graphics layers, and analog and digital outputs.
- Four I2C modules supporting 10–400 Kbps, multimaster operation, 7- and 10-bit addressing, and 32-byte FIFOs.
- An imaging subsystem with parallel and CSI-2 camera inputs, image processing, correction, scaling, compression, cropping, and exposure, focus, flash, and shutter controls.
- Two DDR2/DDR3 interfaces supporting 16- or 32-bit paths, two chip selects, devices from 64 Mb to 4 Gb, and interleaving.

The passage also provides register listings, PCB-layout guidance, signal-reference conventions, and detailed electrical and timing specifications. Board-routing delays must be considered, IBIS analysis is recommended where applicable, and clocks and control signals must transition monotonically.

AI is reshaping drug patent law, raising unresolved questions about whether AI can be an inventor and how predictive technology affects what qualifies as obvious to a person skilled in the field. Future litigation is expected to clarify these issues.

DHS proposed replacing “duration of status,” which lets international students remain in the U.S. until completing their studies, with a four-year limit requiring extensions. The rule would also bar students from changing majors or transferring institutions. DHS says it seeks to reduce F- and J-visa overstays, while critics argue existing monitoring is sufficient and overstay rates are overstated.

Higher education institutions, researchers, hospitals and business leaders warned that many undergraduate, doctoral, medical and research programs exceed four years. Extensions could be costly, uncertain and slow, increasing administrative burdens and potentially preventing students from completing degrees or research. Critics said the rule could deter international enrollment, harm U.S. research and industry, and disrupt health care by affecting roughly 17,000 J-1 physicians, many of whom work in high-need specialties and underserved communities.

DHS received more than 15,700 comments by Sept. 29 and must review them before deciding whether to proceed. Few comments supported the change, generally citing competition with Americans for jobs and college places. The Council for Christian Colleges and Universities suggested limiting the policy to institutions with admission rates below 30 percent.

On August 17, Russian cosmonauts Fyodor Yurchikhin and Sergey Ryazanskiy will conduct a spacewalk from the ISS, deploying five nanosatellites, collecting residue samples, and installing handrails and struts. The mission will be Yurchikhin’s ninth and Ryazanskiy’s fourth spacewalk, and the 202nd supporting station assembly and maintenance.

Stenabolic (SR9009) is a synthetic, orally taken Rev-ErbA ligand developed by the Scripps Research Institute under Professor Thomas Burris. By activating Rev-Erb proteins, it may affect circadian rhythms, metabolism, fat storage, macrophages, and muscle mitochondria. Reported effects include increased endurance, strength, energy expenditure, and fat and glucose burning. In mouse studies, SR9009 increased running distance and duration by 50%. Studies also reported reductions in triglycerides, cholesterol, fatty acids, glucose, insulin, and the proinflammatory cytokine IL-6. The compound has gained popularity among athletes despite being a recent pharmacological development.

Lung cancer mortality remains high because early disease is often asymptomatic and screening is limited. This review examined recent U.S. clinical research on biomarkers for early lung cancer detection. Evaluated approaches included volatile organic compounds, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), miRNAs, DNA methylation markers, isocitrate dehydrogenase, combined risk scores, and Ga-Alfatide II PET/CT imaging.

ctDNA showed 80% sensitivity and 96% specificity, while Ga-Alfatide II imaging showed approximately 86% sensitivity and 85% specificity. Volatile organic compounds had 80% sensitivity and specificity. Although selected miRNAs had sensitivities of 93–96%, their specificities were only 23–33%. Combined scores, methylation markers, and IDH-based screening also lacked consistently high sensitivity and specificity. The review identified ctDNA as potentially suitable for broader screening and Ga-Alfatide II imaging as potentially appropriate for patients at high risk or suspected of having lung cancer, though neither confirms diagnosis.

Early detection, smoking cessation, reduction of modifiable risks, and improved screening could reduce mortality. Further research should refine biomarkers, evaluate treatment response, expand demographic analysis and literature sources, and investigate immunotherapy, chemotherapy, and combination treatments. Limitations included restricting articles to recent U.S. studies, variation in cancer types studied, possible diagnostic errors, and biases within the reviewed research.

This qualitative phenomenological study examined 16 early childhood teachers in Ankara—eight bilingual teachers from private bilingual preschools and eight monolingual teachers from state preschools—to explore views on bilingualism and bilingual education. Semi-structured interviews were analyzed through content analysis, producing five themes: benefits, bilingual children in monolingual schools, program structure, implementation challenges, and developmental effects.

All participants regarded bilingualism as advantageous, associating it with stronger communication, self-confidence, career prospects, cultural awareness, cognitive development, and global citizenship. Bilingual teachers more often warned that attendance at monolingual schools could lead children to lose a language or cultural identity, whereas some monolingual teachers emphasized improved proficiency in Turkish.

Teachers had limited knowledge of bilingual program models but generally believed school personnel should use both languages effectively and that environments should include bilingual materials and stimuli. Reported challenges included inadequate teacher proficiency, shortages of qualified staff and resources, children’s uneven language abilities, family attitudes, cultural conflicts, and difficulties balancing both languages in curricula. Participants agreed that parental support is important, though bilingual teachers more strongly encouraged using the second language at home.

Views differed on bilingual children’s developmental and social outcomes. Teachers cited possible benefits in confidence, communication, cultural awareness, and cognition, but also risks such as peer rejection and difficulty integrating when children lack proficiency in the community’s dominant language.

The study recommends professional development, bilingual teacher certification, stronger curricula and resources, parental guidance, and strategic expansion of bilingual schools in Türkiye. Its findings are limited by the small, Ankara-based sample, restricted school settings, participant differences, and reliance on self-reported perspectives.

The study compared primary care physicians’ electronic health record and interoperability experiences across the 2021 National Electronic Health Records Survey (NEHRS), 2022 American Board of Family Medicine Continuous Certification Questionnaire (CCQ), and 2022 UCSF Physician Health IT Survey. The surveys used different recruitment strategies and had response rates of 18.2%, 100%, and 3.6%, respectively. Respondents also differed substantially in age, practice setting, practice size, and metropolitan location.

All surveys found limited EHR satisfaction, substantial after-work documentation, and persistent interoperability problems. About one-quarter of physicians were very satisfied with their EHR, roughly three-quarters documented for at least one hour after work daily, and about 20% often had access to information from patients’ outside healthcare encounters. Epic users generally reported better experiences, while private-practice physicians were less likely to have external patient information available.

However, most survey questions produced statistically significant differences. CCQ and NEHRS respondents reported better interoperability than UCSF respondents, while NEHRS respondents reported the highest EHR satisfaction. CCQ respondents reported both more after-work documentation and greater ease of documentation. Differences generally persisted after stratification by age, EHR platform, and practice type, suggesting that respondent composition alone did not explain them.

The authors conclude that sampling and response differences, including possible response bias in voluntary surveys, may meaningfully affect policy findings. Mandatory recertification surveys such as the CCQ may offer more representative and reliable supplementary data but cover only individual specialties and may encourage rapid responses. Question and response-option differences also limited comparisons. Augmenting NEHRS with certifying-board data could improve information available to policymakers, though further research across other medical specialties is needed.

A multicentre randomised controlled trial evaluated PrAISED, a 12-month, dementia-specific programme combining tailored exercise, functional activities, risk management, environmental assessment and carer involvement. Participants were 365 adults over 65 with mild cognitive impairment or dementia, randomly assigned to PrAISED or a limited falls-prevention intervention. PrAISED participants received a median of 31 therapy sessions and reported about 121 minutes of exercise weekly.

At 12 months, PrAISED did not improve activities of daily living, physical activity, balance, mobility, quality of life or most other health outcomes. Falls and injurious falls did not differ significantly between groups. Underpowered analyses suggested possible benefits in specific cognitive domains, while two measures favoured controls. More adverse events were reported in the intervention group, likely partly reflecting greater therapist contact; none was treatment-related. Results remained consistent across sensitivity analyses, including analyses addressing COVID-19 disruptions.

The intervention was well received and delivered with reasonable adherence and fidelity, but the participant population lacked diversity. The findings add to evidence that exercise and functionally oriented rehabilitation do not substantially alter cognitive or functional decline in early dementia or mild cognitive impairment. Future support may need to emphasise adapted or supported functioning, practical problem-solving, personhood, inclusion, emotional support, carer support and enjoyable activity rather than restoration of independence.

Pocatello-Chubbuck School District will use three diverse focus groups to advise trustees on controversial high school boundary changes. Meetings will be public. Trustees delayed the decision for more feedback after enrollment and socioeconomic disparities prompted ending school choice.

Microsoft’s Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended June 30, 2015. As of December 31, 2014, common stock held by non-affiliates was valued at approximately $365.3 billion; 7.998 billion shares were outstanding on July 27, 2015.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower people and organizations through a “mobile-first, cloud-first” strategy. Its research and development priorities are reinventing productivity and business processes, building an intelligent cloud platform, and creating more personal computing. Key offerings include Windows, Office 365, Azure, Dynamics, Skype, OneDrive, Bing, Xbox, Surface, Lumia phones, advertising, consulting, and support services. Windows 10, launched in July 2015, was intended to provide a unified, continuously updated platform across devices.

The company reported six operating segments: Devices and Consumer Licensing, Computing and Gaming Hardware, Phone Hardware, Devices and Consumer Other, Commercial Licensing, and Commercial Other. The Nokia Devices and Services business acquired in April 2014 was included in Phone Hardware, while Mojang, developer of Minecraft, was acquired in November 2014. Microsoft competes with companies including Apple, Google, Amazon, Sony, Nintendo, Samsung, IBM, Oracle, SAP, Salesforce.com, VMware, and numerous software, hardware, cloud, advertising, and open-source providers.

Microsoft operates worldwide, with offices in more than 100 countries, regional operations and global data centers. Phones were manufactured mainly in Vietnam, while most other hardware was produced by third-party manufacturers. Products and services were distributed through OEMs, distributors, resellers, online channels, wireless carriers, and Microsoft stores under multiple licensing and subscription programs.

Research and development expense was $12.0 billion in 2015, $11.4 billion in 2014, and $10.4 billion in 2013, equal to 13% of revenue each year. Microsoft held more than 57,000 issued U.S. and international patents and over 35,000 pending patents. As of June 30, 2015, it employed approximately 118,000 people, including 60,000 in the U.S. Management approved eliminating up to 7,800 positions during fiscal 2016, primarily in Phone Hardware.

Principal risks included intense competition; execution challenges in cloud services and Windows 10; uncertain returns from investments, acquisitions, and alliances; impairment of goodwill and intangible assets; intellectual-property disputes and piracy; cyberattacks, data breaches, outages, and infrastructure failures; regulatory, antitrust, anti-corruption, trade, privacy, and tax exposure; difficulty attracting employees; litigation; hardware supply and quality problems; currency and international operational risks; and catastrophic or geopolitical disruptions. In fiscal 2015, Microsoft recorded $5.1 billion of goodwill impairment and $2.2 billion of intangible-asset impairment in Phone Hardware.

The district court granted Garlock’s unopposed summary judgment motion and dismissed Steven Gittens’s ADA disability-discrimination complaint with prejudice. Despite two warnings and an extended deadline, Gittens filed no response or requested extension. The court found dismissal warranted under Rules 41(b) and 16(f) for failure to prosecute and obey scheduling orders, concluding that his noncompliance was willful, further delay would prejudice Garlock, and lesser sanctions would be ineffective.

The court also deemed Garlock’s factual assertions admitted under Rule 56 and local rules. Gittens’s lower-spine injury imposed a 25–30-pound lifting restriction, preventing him from performing certain punch-press positions, but he remained employed in welding and light-duty jobs. The court held that this restriction and inability to perform particular jobs did not substantially limit a major life activity or employment generally, so Gittens was not disabled within the ADA’s meaning and failed to establish a prima facie case. It further found that Garlock provided legitimate, nondiscriminatory reasons for reassigning him and that no evidence showed pretext or discriminatory animus.

Linux Foundation news highlighted Linux’s widespread adoption, $14.5 billion in project value, Hart’s Gold membership and healthcare API platform, a free open-source management publication, and 11 new Cloud Native Computing Foundation members.

Justice should be swift, orderly, and governed by law rather than mob violence. Denying education to any class ultimately harms the whole population; public and industrial education, including that offered at Hampton and Tuskegee, can reduce criminality, improve race relations, and benefit both Black and white communities. Inflammatory rhetoric that encourages or excuses lynching intensifies racial hostility and may contribute to further violence, while lawful punishment is presented as the only lasting response to serious crime.

Similarly, demagogues who incite class hatred against the wealthy undermine legitimate efforts to regulate corporations and correct abuses. Sensationalism, slander, and agitation weaken moral judgment, foster corruption and disorder, and can provoke reactions that reverse genuine reforms and allow old abuses to return. Progress requires resolute but measured reform, rejecting both those who manipulate popular passions for political power and those who exploit others for financial gain.

The passage includes a U.S. passport application, oath of allegiance, applicant description, supporting affidavits, and a passport requesting protection for its bearer. Each faced debt, deficits, limited borrowing options, and heavy taxation. Safety outcomes were similar across groups at 24 and 48 weeks. Before Week 24, adverse events affected about 51–52% of subjects; between Weeks 24 and 48, rates were 33.8–40.8%. Serious adverse events, discontinuations, and bleeding rates were comparable, with three fatal bleeding events overall. Twenty-four deaths and one additional death without an associated adverse event were reported. No pregnancies or concerning hepatic or renal laboratory signals occurred. Adherence and persistence remained high, but additional education provided no benefit.

The bankruptcy court considered whether the Smiths’ amended Chapter 13 plan complied with statutory requirements concerning claim treatment, good faith, and disposable income. The trustee objected that the plan favored Chrysler over NBD Bank, understated income, reserved excessive funds for emergencies, and excluded profit-sharing benefits.

The court found that paying Chrysler’s claim in full did not unfairly discriminate because the debtors had purchased the vehicle five months before bankruptcy and made no payments. However, Chrysler was entitled only to the 3.9% contract interest rate, not the proposed 8%. The court also found that the debtors proposed the plan in good faith, including their treatment of the vehicle debt, corrected omission of insurance values, and deferral of Mrs. Smith’s profit-sharing distribution.

Undisbursed or deferred benefits in Mrs. Smith’s ERISA-qualified profit-sharing plan were excluded from the estate and were not disposable income. The court could not compel her to elect a cash distribution. Any cash distribution actually received during the plan, net of taxes and penalties, must be paid to creditors. Voluntary paycheck contributions to retirement or 401(k) plans must cease and be devoted to plan payments.

The court partially sustained the trustee’s objection and confirmed the modified plan. Monthly payments were increased from $1,733.33 to $1,808.33; excess overtime income must augment payments; and the debtors must provide pay stubs and year-to-date earnings every six months. The modified plan satisfied the Bankruptcy Code’s requirements regarding unfair discrimination, good faith, and disposable income.

The “Single/Double” offense attacks a Triangle & Two defense by using coordinated screens to free shooters from aggressive pass-denial chasers. Either shooter can initiate the action while the opposite shooter forms a double screen. Shooters use fakes and choose single or double screens based on defensive positioning, while screeners seal defenders, post up, roll to the basket, or pop out for shots.

The offense can flow into base-screen or side-screen actions, creating options such as lob, drop, kick-out, and roll passes when defenders help or rotate. Successful execution requires screening, strong post play, defensive recognition, communication, timing, coordination, and experience. Preparation includes breakdown drills, scrimmaging, scouting defensive techniques and matchups, monitoring adjustments, varying alignments and entries, and attacking weaker defenders. In the Triangle & Two defense, three players guard zones while two chasers deny designated opponents passes and rebounds.

A report linked South Korea’s falling fertility rate to rising education and labor participation among married women. Fertility dropped from 2.1 in 1984 to 1.6 in 1987 and reached 1.24 in 2015. Married women’s labor participation rose from 39 percent in 1974 to 53 percent in 2012.

The goalie described making a crucial breakaway save and emphasized how timely saves build confidence and improve anticipation. He acknowledged the playoffs’ emotional ups and downs, dissatisfaction with his first two Finals performances, and stronger recent games.
