The ScottishPower Foundation donated £95,220 to Sussex Wildlife Trust’s 50th-anniversary programme at Woods Mill. The funding will enable 1,300 additional participants, ten wildlife identification courses, training for 250 wildlife champions, and a young naturalists club. It will also support habitat improvements, better path access and a kestrel nesting-box camera. Woods Mill opened to the public in 1968. The foundation has donated more than £1 million to UK charitable projects this year.

The study investigated Greek primary teachers’ views on STEM education and the conditions required for its effective implementation. STEM education is presented as an interdisciplinary, inquiry-oriented approach connecting school learning with real-life problems while developing scientific thinking, critical thinking, collaboration, creativity, communication, and problem-solving.

Participants were 114 public-school teachers in Attica, Greece. Data were collected from March to May 2022 through a questionnaire and 27 structured interviews. Limited convenience sampling restricted generalization.

Most teachers considered students’ scientific thinking very or extremely important, particularly for solving everyday problems, fostering inquiry and critical thinking, improving social skills, supporting experiential and interdisciplinary learning, and acquiring knowledge. Teachers also viewed STEM education as attractive, practical, collaborative, and capable of connecting scientific methodology and technology with daily life. Some believed it could reduce educational inequalities by increasing participation among students with learning, language, or social disadvantages.

Despite valuing core STEM practices, teachers reported few classroom opportunities for students to undertake investigations, test predictions, make measurements, analyze data, explain findings, or present results. Only 20–30% expressed strong confidence in teaching science effectively, compared with approximately 30–40% for mathematics. Technology and engineering are not taught as separate subjects in Greek primary schools.

The principal barriers were insufficient teacher training and educational materials, inadequate infrastructure and equipment, limited teaching time, and STEM’s unclear position in the curriculum. Teachers primarily requested practical and experiential training, sample lessons, manuals, continuing guidance, peer collaboration, suitable equipment, increased funding, and curriculum reorganization.

Teachers generally supported STEM education but described its introduction in Greek compulsory education as rushed, stressful, and insufficiently organized. The study concludes that successful implementation requires teacher preparation, resources, institutional support, and adequate timetable allocation rather than reliance on teachers’ individual efforts.

During construction of Amsterdam’s North/South subway line, archaeologists excavated 700,000 discarded objects from two sites in the Amstel riverbed. The finds, ranging from Neolithic stone axes to cellphones, document everyday life before and throughout Amsterdam’s development as a trade center. Many objects were well preserved in mud and silt nearly 40 feet below the surface. The €6 million “Below the Surface” project displays 10,000 items at Rokin station, offers photographs and data for about 30,000 objects online, and produced a catalog featuring 13,000 photographs for city schools.

Dalhousie researcher Nancy McLean found native bees comprise over half the bees on P.E.I. blueberry flowers and likely perform most pollination because they are highly efficient, adapted to blueberries and tolerant of Maritime weather. She encourages farmers to support native bees with preferred plants instead of importing costly honey bees, which may carry parasites.

Steven Kean congratulated Jeffrey McMahon on stirring change after a Modern Metals article examined Enron’s controversial expansion into steel trading. Enron proposed forward contracts, hedging products and selective physical holdings to reduce price volatility and inventory risk. Industry responses ranged from support for improved pricing and contract enforcement to concerns about low fixed prices, profiteering, delivery reliability, product complexity and distributors losing inventory control. Other attached reports covered Northern Natural Gas’s pipeline sale, speculation about Enron’s role in copper stock increases, Enron’s sale of its Paladin Resources stake, and its expected participation in new coal futures trading.

In a farewell to Cabinet and White House staff, the President thanks them for their dedicated public service and urges them to serve his successor. He praises the administration’s integrity, accepts responsibility for its mistakes, and emphasizes that government service offers a cause greater than personal gain. Recalling his parents’ perseverance and Theodore Roosevelt’s recovery from profound loss, he argues that character and greatness emerge through hardship. He encourages staff to remain proud, continue serving, resist discouragement and hatred, and depart with hope, humility, gratitude, and faith.

The lecture develops tools toward Freiman’s theorem. Ruzsa’s modeling lemma first transfers a positive proportion of a small-doubling set into a small cyclic group while preserving bounded additive relations.

Bogolyubov’s lemma states that if \(A\subseteq \mathbb F_2^n\) has density \(\alpha\), then \(2A-2A\) contains a subspace of codimension less than \(1/\alpha^2\). Although \(A+A\) need not contain such a subspace, repeated addition smooths the set. The proof uses convolution and Fourier analysis: large Fourier coefficients form a small set by Parseval’s identity, while Fourier inversion shows that the convolution supported on \(2A-2A\) is positive on their orthogonal complement.

For \(A\subseteq \mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\), subspaces are replaced by Bohr sets. The analogous lemma shows that \(2A-2A\) contains a Bohr set of width \(1/4\) and dimension below \(1/\alpha^2\). The Fourier proof is essentially unchanged, with the Bohr condition ensuring nonnegative real contributions from large Fourier coefficients.

The lecture then uses geometry of numbers to show that every Bohr set of dimension \(d\) and width \(\epsilon\) contains a proper generalized arithmetic progression of dimension at most \(d\) and size at least \((\epsilon/d)^d n\). A lattice associated with the Bohr frequencies is constructed, and Minkowski’s second theorem bounds its successive minima. These minima provide progression generators and lengths; lattice estimates establish containment, size, and properness. Together with Ruzsa’s covering lemma, these results supply the main ingredients for completing Freiman’s theorem.

The SUSHI study developed and tested an online version of the validated Social Inclusion Questionnaire User Experience (SInQUE) for collaborative care planning in mental health supported accommodation. The tool assesses nine areas of social inclusion, identifies up to three priorities, generates reports, and tracks changes over repeated assessments without storing identifying service-user data.

Conducted in an inner London borough, the study included lab testing with six staff members and five months of field testing. Interviews involved 12 additional staff and 12 service users. Usage was also monitored in two areas where the tool was introduced without implementation support. Interview data informed an intervention-context-actor-mechanism-outcome logic model.

Participants generally considered the SInQUE user-friendly, quick, comprehensive, collaborative, and relevant. They suggested it could prompt personal conversations, clarify service-user priorities, support targeted care planning, strengthen staff–service-user relationships, and identify service gaps. Minor changes improved wording, guidance, score presentation, and supporting materials. Some staff worried that personal questions could feel intrusive, but service users did not report similar concerns.

In the participating borough, 27 staff registered, 17 used the tool, and 30 assessments were completed with 28 service users—just over 10% of the supported accommodation population. Uptake was highest in supported housing and lower in residential care and floating outreach services. In areas without an implementation strategy, one staff member registered but no assessments were completed. Leadership endorsement, technical guidance, and organisational support appeared important for implementation.

Limitations included low uptake, testing in one borough, no female service-user interviewees, participant self-selection, limited representation from some accommodation types, and insufficient time to assess long-term outcomes or repeated assessments.

The study concluded that the SInQUE is potentially acceptable and useful, particularly in supported housing, but requires active implementation support. Further research should examine non-use, other settings and populations, longer-term uptake, implementation methods, and effects on social inclusion, care planning, and mental health outcomes.

Before COVID-19, Japanese universities lagged in educational ICT use because of traditions favoring classroom instruction, limited adult enrollment, distance-learning credit limits, and low use of learning management and file-sharing tools. The pandemic forced a rapid shift online: by June 2020, about 90% of universities offered remote classes, while 60% offered no face-to-face instruction.

MEXT temporarily relaxed the 60-credit limit for remote learning but later encouraged a return to face-to-face classes because students reported limited interaction and poor online quality. By fall 2022, 99.8% of universities conducted more than half their classes face-to-face. Revised standards retained remote-credit limits while permitting exceptions for universities with effective quality assurance. Government initiatives also supported digital innovation, educational-data sharing, online inter-university cooperation, and use of the national “My Number” system, though data-linking errors raised privacy and public-trust concerns.

Faculty rapidly adopted hybrid, high-flex, and remote teaching despite limited prior experience. Online instruction created difficulties in communication, practical training, assessing understanding, supporting students, managing group work, and addressing instructors’ limited computer literacy. Universities responded by sharing examples of effective distance-learning practices. The pandemic challenged assumptions that university education must occur face-to-face, although broader cultural change remains uncertain.

Digital tools increased assignments and students’ out-of-class study time, potentially supporting the required credit system, under which one credit represents 45 hours of study. However, students traditionally study little outside class because they take many courses, undertake job hunting and graduation research, and participate in other activities. Online workloads were also widely viewed as excessive. Effective reform may require combining ICT-based learning management and improved materials with fewer course credits and university-wide curriculum management.

Lifelong learning remains weakly institutionalized. Distance degree programs primarily serve adult learners and had begun digitalizing before the pandemic, but their separation from regular programs limited wider use of their expertise. Traditional non-degree public lectures were rarely offered remotely, while newer vocational certificate programs became more digitalized, partly because they target employed adults. Overall, digitalization expanded access, made learning more visible, and created opportunities for adult learners, but further infrastructure, institutional and cultural reform, quality improvement, and protection of students’ personal information remain necessary.

NVIDIA’s A100 GPU, based on the Ampere architecture, improves compute, memory, scalability, virtualization, and programmability over V100. Third-generation Tensor Cores share data across all 32 warp threads, increase matrix-multiply dimensions per instruction, and reduce instructions and register accesses. New asynchronous copy instructions transfer data directly from global memory to shared memory, while asynchronous barriers support efficient pipelines. Shared memory rises to 164 KB per SM.

A100 provides 1,555 GB/s HBM2 bandwidth, 2.3 times V100’s L2 read bandwidth, and a 40 MB L2 cache. Cache-residency controls retain frequently reused data and reduce DRAM traffic, while Compute Data Compression further improves bandwidth and effective capacity. CUDA 11 exposes asynchronous copies, barriers, Tensor Cores, sparsity, CUDA Graphs, MIG, and L2 residency controls. CUDA Graph optimizations reduce CPU launch costs and inter-kernel latency, while Cooperative Groups adds asynchronous-copy and hardware-accelerated reduction support.

Multi-Instance GPU technology partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute, cache, memory-controller, and DRAM resources. This provides predictable performance, quality of service, security, and fault isolation for VMs, containers, processes, and multiple tenants. GPU Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances, support MPS, execute and context-switch independently, and be migrated between compatible instances to consolidate workloads or service hardware.

Third-generation NVLink doubles the signal-pair rate and expands A100 to 12 links, providing 600 GB/s aggregate bandwidth. PCIe Gen 4 supplies 31.5 GB/s per direction over x16 and supports SR-IOV. A100 also strengthens fault attribution, isolation, containment, and recovery for shared and clustered environments.

Additional hardware includes five NVDEC video decoders, a five-core NVJPG JPEG decoder, an optical-flow and stereo-disparity accelerator, and faster global-memory atomics—11 times V100 throughput for FP16 and 2.7 times for FP32.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs, six NVSwitches, 4.8 TB/s total bidirectional interconnect bandwidth, and up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance in 6U. MIG can provide up to 56 isolated accelerators per system. Its software stack includes CUDA 11, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC software and models, and support for deep learning, inference, analytics, and HPC workloads.

A100 supports fine-grained structured 2:4 sparsity, balancing sparse computation across nodes while reducing compute and memory requirements. NVIDIA reports virtually no accuracy loss across evaluated neural networks after fine-tuning.

Michael Dell says the AI data-center boom remains strong because customers are immediately deploying infrastructure and face computing demand limited mainly by power availability. Dell Technologies’ server-networking business grew 58% last year, while the company raised forecasts for annual revenue growth to 7%–9% and earnings-per-share growth to at least 15%. Its stock has risen 39% this year amid broader gains for AI infrastructure suppliers. Although market observers warn that valuations are stretched and vulnerable if AI disappoints, Dell sees no current signs of excessive data-center construction.

Siddharth Agrawal has spent 18 years managing Silkasia, his family’s garment and home-textile export business. He researches native Indian cattle, invests in rooftop farming and start-ups, and mentors entrepreneurs. With his wife Vrinda, he developed women’s clothing brand Mayori. He also leads TiE Rajasthan and belongs to several business networks.

Concomitant medications and diabetes treatments will be coded using WHODrug Global and ATC classifications, listed in detail, and summarized by treatment, ATC level 2, and preferred name. Medications ending before first investigational product administration are prior; ongoing or later-starting medications are concomitant. Ambiguous incomplete dates are classified conservatively as concomitant.

Primary efficacy analysis uses the full analysis set, with supportive per-protocol analyses. The primary endpoint is time within 45 minutes to a plasma glucose increase of at least 20 mg/dL from baseline without rescue IV glucose. Baseline is generally the last non-missing value before dosing. Analyses adjust for age group and injection site, use observed data without imputation, and include no interim analysis.

Dasiglucagon 0.6 mg and placebo are compared through hierarchical two-sided testing at 0.05: time to recovery, recovery within 30, 20, 15, and 10 minutes, then glucose changes at those times. Testing stops after the first nonsignificant comparison. GlucaGen comparisons are supportive and excluded from this hierarchy.

Time to recovery is analyzed with Kaplan-Meier methods and a stratified log-rank test. Patients receiving rescue IV glucose or not recovering within 45 minutes are classified as not recovered and censored at 45 minutes. Sensitivity analyses use no censoring after rescue or censor at rescue administration. Supportive analyses include stratified Wilcoxon testing, recovery histograms, discrete-time Cox models when assumptions permit, subgroup homogeneity models, and linearly interpolated recovery times.

Secondary recovery rates are compared using Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests stratified by age and injection site, with Fisher testing if required. Glucose changes are analyzed by ANOVA with treatment, age group, and injection site. Rescue-time glucose values replace scheduled values when rescue occurs earlier.

Pharmacokinetic analyses describe dasiglucagon and glucagon concentrations and derive noncompartmental metrics using Phoenix WinNonlin. Sampling times, below-quantification values, and missing values follow specified handling rules. Plasma glucose pharmacodynamics include area under the effect curve above baseline from 0–30 minutes. Concentrations and metrics are summarized and graphed by treatment.

Safety analyses use the safety set and cover insulin use, hypoglycemia induction, trial medication, rescue glucose, injection-site tolerability, adverse events, laboratory tests, vital signs, ECGs, and immunogenicity. Treatment-emergent adverse events include events beginning after dosing or worsening during the study; uncertain partial dates are treated conservatively. Events are coded with MedDRA, summarized by treatment, system organ class, preferred term, causality, severity, seriousness, and special categories. Missing causality is treated as related if unresolved; missing severity is not imputed.

Laboratory, vital-sign, and ECG data are summarized descriptively, including reference-range categories and changes from baseline. QTcF thresholds and changes are tabulated. Anti-drug antibody incidence includes treatment-induced and treatment-boosted cases among evaluable patients; no inferential testing is planned.

The SAP adds sensitivity and supportive primary analyses and revises secondary endpoint terminology. Appendices specify table, figure, listing, derivation, formatting, missing-date, SAS programming, validation, quality-control, and documentation requirements, along with planned outputs.

Vladimir Putin won a fourth presidential term with authorities reporting more than three-quarters of the vote, extending his rule for six years. Critics described the election as predetermined and alleged pressure on government employees, harassment of monitors, ballot stuffing and isolated violence. Putin’s campaign emphasized Russia’s resilience despite Western sanctions and portrayed accusations over a former spy’s poisoning and U.S. election interference as parts of an anti-Russian campaign. Opposition leader Alexei Navalny was barred from running, while divisions persisted among opposition figures. Asked whether he might change the constitution to remain in power beyond the new term, Putin said he had no such plans yet.
Alabama voters face a special Senate election between Democrat Doug Jones and Republican Roy Moore, who denies sexual misconduct allegations involving teenage girls.

The Dark Cloud Cover is a bearish reversal candlestick pattern appearing after an upward price swing. It consists of a bullish candle followed by a bearish candle that opens above the prior close but closes below the bullish candle’s midpoint, indicating a possible shift toward bearish sentiment.

Traders may use it to close long positions or initiate short sales, especially during rallies in bearish markets. Confirmation may come from subsequent price action, resistance levels, moving averages, MACD, or RSI. The strategy can be applied to stocks, Forex, commodities, and cryptocurrencies across short or long timeframes, though shorter periods may produce more false signals.

The pattern is a warning rather than a guaranteed reversal. Traders should consider market conditions, news, fundamental analysis, stop-loss levels, and other risk-management methods. Backtesting with clearly defined rules can help evaluate performance, but results vary by market, timeframe, and parameters and do not guarantee future returns.

Thousands of Armenian-Americans marched in Los Angeles to commemorate an estimated 1.5 million Armenians who died under the Ottoman Empire beginning in 1915 and to demand Turkey recognize the deaths as genocide. Turkey attributes them to civil war and unrest. Demonstrators honored ancestors and emphasized preventing future atrocities. The marches followed Armenian Prime Minister Serzh Sargsyan’s resignation after anti-government protests. Kim Kardashian West praised the peaceful demonstrations.

News reports from Nov. 16–18, 2001 focused on Enron’s financial collapse, proposed acquisition by Dynegy, asset sales and investor concerns. Enron’s stock had fallen about 90% amid an SEC investigation, earnings restatements, partnership-related liabilities and reduced confidence in its accounting. Dynegy’s proposed transaction was valued at roughly $24 billion in stock and assumed debt, with provisions allowing withdrawal under certain circumstances. Enron secured a $550 million pipeline-backed loan, while Chairman Kenneth Lay declined a potential $60.6 million severance package.

Investors awaited Enron’s third-quarter regulatory filing for details about debts, partnerships, legal liabilities, layoffs and restructuring. Pension funds considered lawsuits, while employees criticized retirement-plan losses after executives had sold substantial holdings. Commentaries linked Enron’s problems to hidden debt, executive incentives, deregulation, weak oversight and inadequate diversification.

Potential buyers, including WestLB, reportedly considered acquiring Enron’s Wessex Water unit, valued near £1 billion. Aquila limited trading with Enron in case Dynegy abandoned the acquisition.

Broader financial coverage reported rising stocks and falling bonds following improved economic indicators. Energy analysts remained optimistic about long-term energy stocks despite weak oil prices and volatility. Other articles emphasized diversification, regular saving and investor skepticism after market losses.
Jokes and missed shots keep players relaxed despite elimination pressure. The team remains focused on winning one game at a time.

Tesla Motors’ Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2015 reported quarterly revenue of $936.8 million, up from $851.8 million a year earlier, while gross margin declined to 24.7% from 29.6%. Quarterly net loss widened to $229.9 million from $74.7 million. For the first nine months, revenue was $2.83 billion, net loss was $568.3 million, operating cash outflow was $494.7 million, and capital expenditures were $1.22 billion.

At September 30, Tesla had $7.55 billion in assets, $6.19 billion in liabilities, $1.31 billion in stockholders’ equity, and $1.43 billion in cash and equivalents. Inventory rose to $1.29 billion, while property, plant and equipment increased to $3.10 billion. An August stock offering generated approximately $738.3 million net.

Tesla began Model X deliveries and Tesla Energy production during the quarter, had delivered almost 90,000 vehicles cumulatively, and planned to unveil Model 3 in early 2016 for late-2017 deliveries. It projected 2015 deliveries of 50,000–52,000 vehicles and approximately $1.7 billion in capital expenditures. Model X production faced supplier and ramp-up uncertainties, particularly involving second-row seats.

The company continued expanding manufacturing, stores, service centers, Superchargers and the Nevada Gigafactory. It expected existing liquidity and projected operating cash flows to support operations for 12 months. Key risks included production delays, supplier concentration, resale guarantees, leasing residual values, foreign exchange movements, Gigafactory execution and ongoing litigation.

Manny’s possible return from injury would provide an emotional boost because his leadership and contributions have been important to the team’s success. He remained involved during recovery. The speaker also said close teammates can easily tell him and his sibling apart, unlike some coaches.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2016 reported net sales of $78.35 billion, up 3% year over year, while net income declined to $17.89 billion from $18.36 billion. Diluted earnings per share rose to $3.36 from $3.28. Gross margin decreased from 40.1% to 38.5%, and operating income fell to $23.36 billion.

iPhone sales increased 5% to $54.38 billion on 78.3 million units. Mac sales rose 7% to $7.24 billion, and Services revenue increased 18% to $7.17 billion. iPad sales declined 22% to $5.53 billion, while Other Products fell 8% to $4.02 billion. Regional sales increased in the Americas, Europe, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific, but declined 12% in Greater China.

At December 31, 2016, Apple had $331.14 billion in assets, including $246.09 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. Total liabilities were $198.75 billion, including $10.49 billion of commercial paper and $77.06 billion of term debt. Operating activities generated $27.06 billion in cash; investing used $19.12 billion and financing used $12.05 billion.

Apple repurchased $10.85 billion of common stock and paid $3.13 billion in dividends and equivalents during the quarter. Of its $175 billion share-repurchase authorization, $144 billion had been used. The company anticipated approximately $16 billion in fiscal 2017 capital expenditures.

Research and development expense increased to $2.87 billion, while selling, general and administrative expense rose to $3.95 billion. Apple expected second-quarter gross margin of 38% to 39%.

Apple appealed the European Commission’s state-aid decision concerning Irish taxes, which announced recovery of up to €13 billion plus interest. Apple expected to place the amount calculated by Ireland into escrow pending appeals. The filing also described supply-chain concentration, litigation, tax, currency, interest-rate and other business risks.

The document standardizes the 4 KB, decrypted Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) and required Non-Automatic Exit behavior so SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests can interoperate with supporting hypervisors while exposing only necessary guest state. The GHCB largely mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save-state format and is located through a non-interceptable MSR. Its lower address bits support an MSR protocol for version negotiation, feature discovery, CPUID requests, GHCB registration, page-state changes, VMPL changes, and termination.

Protocol Version 2 adds SEV-SNP support and a 52-bit hypervisor feature bitmap. Later revisions add 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, expanded error reporting, APIC ID retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, SEV-ES page-state changes, confidential-computing EFI data, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, VLEK identification, and GHCB unregistration. SEV-SNP guests must register each vCPU’s shared GHCB guest physical address before first use and may request a preferred address or unregister it.

For Non-Automatic Exits, hardware raises a #VC exception. The guest identifies the event, populates required GHCB fields and validity bits, executes VMGEXIT, and processes the hypervisor’s returned state or error. Interrupts and preemption should be disabled while manipulating the GHCB. Defined operations include I/O, MSR access, hypercalls, MMIO, page-state changes, SNP firmware requests, certificate retrieval, AP creation, Restricted Injection doorbells, IPIs and timers, APIC ID lists, VMPL switching, trusted-I/O requests, Secure AVIC backing pages, and termination.

Page-state-change requests can make pages private or shared and provide PSMASH or UNSMASH hints. SNP guest requests use shared request and response pages, with retry and rate-limiting provisions. Extended requests can return GUID-identified certificates, while SEV-TIO requests can return device measurements, certificates, and TDISP attestation reports.

The specification defines GHCB negotiation and VMGEXIT workflows, SNP secrets-page sequence-number storage, and an EFI configuration table for communicating SNP secrets and CPUID pages. It also specifies SMP boot procedures, AP reset holding, AP jump tables, and SNP AP creation. SNP AP creation enables vCPU hotplug; traditional SEV-ES operation does not.

Restricted Injection uses a shared #HV doorbell page containing pending-event and EOI-assist fields. It defines host and guest behavior for presenting, acknowledging, prioritizing, and completing interrupts and non-maskable events. Secure AVIC uses private per-vCPU APIC backing pages registered with the hypervisor.

Debug-register virtualization is supported when enabled by hardware; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and emulated. System Management Mode and nested virtualization are not supported.

The Jonathan Hunt Chapter of the Daughters of the American Revolution honored eight high school seniors selected for citizenship qualities. Students submitted applications and essays about America’s role in advancing freedom. Five attended a tea, received recognition items, and the overall winner earned a monetary award.

STAT’s D.C. Diagnosis newsletter covers federal health policy, including a potential government shutdown and Democrats’ push to extend enhanced ACA subsidies. The page also lists recent reporting on pharmaceuticals, biotech, women’s health, drug trials, vaccines, dementia, and federal health agencies.

Standard accretion-disc models struggle to explain AGN spectral complexity and rapid variability. Fairall 9, a minimally absorbed Seyfert 1 monitored for about 1,000 days by Swift and other observatories, provides a test of connections between its UV-emitting disc and X-ray corona.

The study divides the Swift campaign into segments and analyses time-averaged spectral energy distributions, power spectra, Fourier-resolved lags, and coherence. SED modelling indicates a substantial rise in optical/UV disc emission, consistent with a roughly 40–50% increase in global mass-accretion rate. Total coronal X-ray power remains nearly constant, while the X-ray spectrum softens, consistent with increased cooling by disc seed photons. The inferred inner accretion structure may also evolve.

Fourier analysis using Gaussian Process regression shows steeply declining high-frequency UV variability but relatively flat X-ray variability, suggesting distinct intrinsic variability sources. During the sharp brightening, the UV coherently leads the X-rays at low frequencies, consistent with an inward-moving change associated with increased accretion. Outside this phase, the UV and X-rays are only moderately or weakly coherent, with variable lags.

An analytic model represents observed emission as combinations of intrinsic disc and coronal variability, disc seed photons entering the corona, X-ray reverberation from the disc, and EUV reprocessing by a wind or broad-line region. It can broadly reproduce the observations if the disc and corona vary intrinsically and partly interfere, while remaining linked through seed photons and reprocessing. Segments after the rise may share the same underlying stochastic process, whereas the rising phase likely reflects a structural change.

The results suggest Fairall 9’s inner accretion flow evolves on observable timescales much shorter than predicted by standard viscous-disc theory. Such evolution complicates averaging timing measurements across different campaign segments and motivates models with modified disc structures or instabilities.

Argentine defender Federico Allende admitted repeatedly jabbing Estudiantes strikers with a needle during Sport Pacifico’s 3-2 cup upset, claiming teams must “play dirty” to beat bigger clubs. Colombian striker Juan Otero said he complained during the match. Pacifico president Hector Moncada said the incident tarnished the club’s work and vowed to expel Allende.

Jalen Carey’s commitment joined Darius Bazley and Buddy Boeheim in Syracuse’s promising 2018 basketball recruiting class, potentially its best in seven years. The article compares it with top classes in program history using contemporary recruiting rankings, not player outcomes.

Jane Goodall, the pioneering primatologist and conservationist, died in her sleep of natural causes at 91 while touring California. Beginning fieldwork in Tanzania’s Gombe reserve in 1960, she gained chimpanzees’ acceptance and documented their toolmaking, personalities, warfare, and other behaviors previously considered uniquely human. She earned a Cambridge doctorate in ethology in 1965 despite lacking a bachelor’s degree.

Goodall faced sexism and scientific criticism but continued her research with support from the National Geographic Society. She married wildlife photographer Hugo Van Lawick, with whom she had a son, and later married Tanzanian national parks director Derek Bryceson.

In 1977, she founded the Jane Goodall Institute to protect chimpanzees and their habitats, later adding the Roots & Shoots youth program. She advocated for improved treatment of laboratory chimpanzees and became an internationally recognized conservation leader. Her honors included appointment as a UN Messenger of Peace, Dame of the British Empire, and member of the French Legion of Honor.

In July 1889, Robert W. Wilcox and Robert Boyd led an unsuccessful Hawaiian insurrection involving about 100 adherents. U.S. sailors and marines landed with permission to protect life and property, returning to their ship after order was restored. The supreme court subsequently ruled that the King’s official actions were subject to cabinet direction. Hawaii was invited to the 1890 International American Conference, but its delegate arrived after adjournment. King Kalakaua visited the United States in December 1890 and died in San Francisco on January 20, 1891; Liliuokalani was then proclaimed Queen. Minister Stevens reported concerns that she sought to replace constitutionally protected ministers with supporters. The supreme court later ruled that Kalakaua’s cabinet ceased to exist upon his death, and a generally satisfactory new cabinet was appointed. After the prince consort died in August 1891, Hawaii pursued revision of its U.S. reciprocity treaty because removal of the sugar tariff threatened island interests. A special envoy was appointed, and a treaty-favorable legislature was elected in February 1892.

Churchill High School senior Deanthony Gordley earned his diploma after losing both parents and experiencing homelessness for seven months. A stranger temporarily housed him, and NEISD connected him with the McKinney Vento Homeless Project, which, along with local families and his school, provided support. Gordley hopes his achievement inspires others to persevere. He also shares his experiences through singing, dancing, and rapping, with songs available on iTunes.

The paper applies Bacchi’s “What’s the Problem Represented to be?” framework to public and freedom-of-information documents concerning South Australia’s 2018 “World Class” education policy. Influenced by McKinsey, New Public Management and the Global Education Reform Movement, the policy aimed to make the state’s public education system “world class” by 2028 using standardised-test results and McKinsey’s Universal Scale.

The analysis finds that the Department represented school improvement as requiring centralised authority, consistent messaging, measurable targets and reduced educator autonomy. NAPLAN became a proxy for international assessments, while schools were ranked by performance. Lower-performing schools, often serving disadvantaged communities, received greater bureaucratic scrutiny through dashboards, Education Directors, prescribed priorities and curriculum materials. The authors argue that this approach privileged centralised data and bureaucratic knowledge over educators’ professional judgement, local circumstances, equity and broader social and democratic purposes of education.

The paper reports that after four years, South Australia’s PIRLS performance declined, its PISA equity gap widened, and problems included absenteeism, disengagement, lower retention and reduced school certification. It acknowledges that schools may resist or adapt policy implementation.

As an alternative, the authors propose a “Beyond World Class” framework based on professional trust, democratic policymaking, equity, inclusion, local knowledge and collaboration across system levels. Aligned with the Alice Springs Declaration, it would treat partnerships as policy advisers, support contextual approaches to teaching and wellbeing, and use educators’ knowledge in policy design, evaluation and school improvement.

A randomized controlled trial evaluated eight-week mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) with or without group psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy (PAP) in 25 physicians and nurses with COVID-19-related depression and burnout. Participants received MBSR alone or MBSR plus 25 mg psilocybin, group preparation and integration sessions.

At two weeks, MBSR+PAP produced a significantly greater reduction in depressive symptoms than MBSR alone: QIDS-SR-16 scores decreased by 7.26 versus 2.66 points. MBSR+PAP also showed greater improvements in depersonalization, demoralization, and connectedness at two weeks, and emotional exhaustion at six months. Depression differences were not significant at six months. All study-related adverse events were mild or moderate; no serious adverse events, emergent suicidality, or self-injurious behavior occurred. Attendance and retention indicated feasibility.

The small, predominantly white and female sample, lack of blinding or placebo, unequal intervention experiences, and inclusion of participants with prior psychedelic use limited generalizability and interpretation. The authors conclude that MBSR combined with group PAP appears safe, feasible, and potentially effective, but larger, more diverse, placebo-controlled studies are needed.
Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi won the 2025 chemistry Nobel for metal-organic frameworks that trap substances.

Polar metals combine a polar crystal structure with metallic conductivity, preventing electric-field reversal of polarity because mobile electrons screen internal fields. Distortive polar metals undergo symmetry-lowering transformations that create domains and boundaries, including head-to-head (H-H) and tail-to-tail (T-T) configurations associated with structural “bound charge.”

This study identifies Mn₅Al₈ as a metallic distortive polar metal. Off-stoichiometric Mn₅₁Al₄₉ undergoes a first-order, martensitic transition near 880°C from cubic γ-brass, space group I¯43m, to polar rhombohedral γ₂, space group R3m. Resistivity measurements and density-functional calculations confirm metallic behavior. The transformation produces four polar variants arranged in rank-2 laminate twins, commonly forming a herringbone microstructure with mixed {100} and {110} boundaries.

Electron microscopy, diffraction, and qualitative 4D-STEM differential phase-contrast mapping revealed H-H and T-T boundaries forming a recurring interlocking-Y pattern. Surface measurements showed contrasting behavior between boundary types. Low-voltage electron microscopy and electrostatic force microscopy indicated variations consistent with differing carrier concentrations or work functions. Preferential copper deposition and oxidation occurred along H-H boundaries but were inhibited at T-T boundaries, suggesting electron enrichment and depletion, respectively. Magnetism and elastic strain did not account for the observed pattern, although the underlying mechanism remains unresolved.

A database survey identified at least 134 compounds composed solely of metallic elements in polar space groups, about 20% of which undergo symmetry-lowering transitions into polar structures. These findings suggest that metallic distortive polar metals and their domain boundaries constitute a broader, largely unexplored materials class with potentially functional surface and electronic properties.

Following its $1.1 billion acquisition of stablecoin startup Bridge, Stripe is launching Open Issuance, a service enabling businesses to create and manage interoperable stablecoins while retaining yield from reserves such as Treasury bills and bank deposits. Stripe believes stablecoins can improve global money transfers and storage through fast, low-cost blockchain transactions.

A new U.S. regulatory framework signed in July has encouraged corporate experimentation with stablecoins. Stripe expects Open Issuance to simplify adoption and enable conversions among stablecoins, dollars, and customer points or balances. Initial users—Phantom, Hyperliquid, and MetaMask—are all crypto companies, however, leaving uncertain when non-crypto businesses will adopt the technology. Stripe expects merchants to play a central role in bringing stablecoins to mainstream consumers.

The 3-2 zone drops the point defender to the free-throw line, allowing wings to deny passing lanes and helping protect the high post. It concedes outside shots to the point guard but can shift to a 1-2-2 or 1-3-1 against strong shooters. A tall, athletic wing may interchange with the point, improving high-post defense and weakside rebounding. The alignment also supports fast breaks. As the ball moves to a wing or corner, the nearest wing or baseline defender pressures it, the point protects the elbow, high post, or low post, and other defenders rotate into the middle, basket, corner, or weakside baseline areas.

Stock trading strategies use defined rules to buy and sell stocks or ETFs, usually over shorter periods than long-term investing. Major approaches include day trading, swing trading, momentum, scalping, trend following, arbitrage, event-driven trading, sector rotation, pair and market-neutral trading, technical analysis, seasonality, overnight trading, mean reversion, and oscillator trading.

Effective strategies require research, disciplined execution, risk management, timing, and accounting for volatility, commissions, spreads, and slippage. Technical indicators include moving averages, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and stochastic oscillators. Backtesting evaluates quantified rules against historical data, though past performance does not guarantee future returns. Algorithms can automate predefined rules, accelerate execution, reduce human errors, and manage numerous trades and strategies.

Diversification across stocks, sectors, assets, timeframes, and strategies can reduce risk, particularly from unexpected news and company-specific events. Concentrating on a single stock may provide specialized knowledge but exposes retail traders to substantial losses, bankruptcy risk, limited opportunities, and scaling difficulties. The passage therefore favors diversified portfolios and multiple quantified strategies over single-stock trading or intuition.

Day trading closes positions within one session and is described as highly difficult, with many traders losing money. Swing trading holds positions for days or weeks. Momentum and trend-following strategies seek continuing price movements, while mean reversion anticipates returns toward historical averages. High-frequency trading, arbitrage, and statistical arbitrage are presented as more suitable for institutions.

Beginners are advised to establish an account and financial plan, learn market analysis, practice with a simulator, avoid speculative tips, and manage risk. Strategy selection should reflect personal objectives, mindset, and risk capacity.

Cierra Dillard scored 22 points as 11th-seeded Buffalo upset third-seeded Florida State 86-65, reaching its first women’s NCAA Tournament Sweet 16. Buffalo shot 47.4% and limited Florida State to 33.8%, including 3 of 25 from three-point range. The Bulls will face defending champion South Carolina in Albany.

A collection of May 11–13, 2001 news reports covers Enron-related energy issues and Houston business developments. California universities prepared for rolling blackouts during final exams amid a contract dispute with Enron Energy Services. In India, officials and Dabhol Power Company began talks over unpaid bills, high electricity prices, contract renegotiation and possible third-party power sales. Maharashtra State Electricity Board said it could not acquire another 15% of Dabhol because of financial stress. Enron was also reportedly considering leaving the Dolphin gas pipeline project between Qatar and the United Arab Emirates.

Oregon Congressman Peter DeFazio proposed that the state purchase Enron-owned Portland General Electric to stabilize rates, but state legislators and regulators expressed skepticism. Other reports discussed criticism of British Telecom’s credit downgrade, Houston’s potential benefits from nanotechnology, a business-led plan to improve Houston’s education, economy and quality of life, and the growth of Star Fleet Entertainment Yachts.

The global organic pigments market is forecast to grow about 4.5% through 2022, driven by demand from paints and coatings, plastics, textiles, printing inks, and other applications. Growth factors include cost-effectiveness, shade consistency, solvent stability, and non-toxicity. Asia-Pacific is expected to remain the largest and fastest-growing market, led by China, while North America and Europe compete in value and volume. The report segments the market by pigment type, natural or synthetic source, application, and region. It analyzes pricing, supply chains, competitive forces, regulations, macroeconomic indicators, and developments such as mergers, alliances, and new products. Key companies include BASF, Dow Chemical, Huntsman, Cabot, Clariant, Evonik Degussa, DuPont, and DIC.

West Midlands house prices rose 7.1% over the year to December, adding about £12,000 to reach an average £181,000. UK prices increased 7.2%, led by England at 7.7%. Within the West Midlands, growth ranged from 10.4% in Wyre Forest and Kidderminster to 3.1% in South Staffordshire. PwC forecast UK house price growth would slow to between 2% and 6% in 2017.

Nahant’s April 29 Town Meeting will consider 41 articles, including a proposed Ambulance Enterprise Fund funded through fees. The Finance Committee opposes the measure, citing questionable resident benefits, spending concerns, and no urgency. Selectmen are divided over whether fees could deter emergency calls. Members will also consider reversing a 2008 decision to sell Coast Guard Housing land for condominiums and authorizing sale of the four-acre parcel and 12 homes; the committee recommends postponement. It also supports funding for drainage repairs, two Public Works trucks, and pumping station maintenance.

Markets shifted decisively risk-off after a week of earnings, economic data and policy uncertainty. Major indexes fell 2.2%–4.2%, forming bearish engulfing patterns at record highs as volume, market breadth and most sectors weakened. Strong earnings and upward estimate revisions failed to sustain buying, while Amazon was punished for less impressive results.

GDP grew 3%, above the 2.5% forecast, but tariff-driven import volatility complicated interpretation and personal spending remained weak. Payrolls increased by 73,000 versus 100,000 expected, with unusually large downward revisions to prior months. The unemployment rate edged to 4.2% as the labor force contracted.

The Fed maintained a patient, data-dependent stance amid inflation, tariff and labor-force uncertainty, despite two dissenting votes. Markets assigned more than 75% odds to a September rate cut and expected three cuts by January, while bond prices signaled concern about slowing growth. Political developments—including tariffs, tensions with Russia, the dismissal of the Bureau of Labor Statistics commissioner and a Fed governor’s resignation—added uncertainty. Short- and intermediate-term indicators remained risk-off, though longer-term earnings expectations continued to improve.
UNMC’s Children’s Dental Day provides free treatment and oral-health education to Nebraska children. Since 2001, the program has delivered more than $3 million in dental care.

The passage argues that Western mainstream media’s anti-Trump coverage and portrayals of political violence may have contributed to radicalizing James Hodgkinson, who shot five people at a Republican baseball game and later died after police intervention. Hodgkinson, a Bernie Sanders supporter, had expressed hatred toward Trump and Republicans and followed anti-Trump media. While acknowledging that most viewers remain peaceful, the passage compares alleged media incitement to extremist propaganda and calls for equivalent scrutiny and condemnation.

NVIDIA’s February 8, 2018 Form 8-K reports the release of financial results for the quarter and fiscal year ended January 28, 2018. Exhibits include the earnings press release and CFO Colette M. Kress’s commentary. The materials are furnished, not filed, under applicable securities laws.

The invention concerns a grid-based storage system in which robotic load handlers travel on perpendicular rails above stacked containers. Uprights and grid members form a framework that also routes services such as power, data communications, lighting, water, gases, heating, cooling, and sensing equipment. These services enable monitoring and control of the framework, containers, and their contents.

Sensors, cameras, data loggers, and communication systems may continuously detect structural defects, misalignment, fire, smoke, heat, gases, and container conditions while the system operates. Services can connect to containers through physical, releasable, or non-contact methods, including conductive contacts, induction, and telescopic connections. Connections between stacked containers may distribute power or data throughout a stack.

Fluid systems may target individual containers or areas with water, nutrients, carbon dioxide, or fire-suppressant gases, reducing damage compared with warehouse-wide deployment. Container identification systems allow specific containers to be monitored, treated, or controlled. The framework may also support permanent or temporary partitions to create different temperature or atmospheric zones and isolate incidents such as fires or spills. Overall, the system is intended to improve monitoring, reliability, control, and operational efficiency in dense automated storage installations.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, simultaneous-sampling 20-bit SAR data-acquisition system supporting single-ended or differential bipolar inputs. It provides up to 2 MSPS per channel in normal operation and up to 8 MSPS for one selected channel pair in speed-boost mode. Each channel includes ±18 V clamp protection, a programmable-gain amplifier, selectable low-pass-filter bandwidth, a high-speed ADC driver, and constant 1 MΩ input impedance. A common-mode rejection circuit supports voltages up to ±12 V.

The device operates from 5 V and 1.8 V analog supplies, includes a 4.096 V low-drift reference, and supports an external reference. Conversion data can use straight-binary or two’s-complement formatting. Its source-synchronous output interface supports two or four lanes in SDR or DDR modes, with 20-bit results transmitted MSB-first in 24-bit packets. Multiple devices can be synchronized using shared sampling-clock and synchronization signals.

Additional functions include simple and moving averaging, output randomization to reduce data-interface interference, fixed, ramp, and alternating test patterns, and programmable input range and bandwidth per channel. Configuration uses banked 16-bit registers accessed through SPI, including support for multi-device daisy chains. A free-running sampling clock and prescribed register initialization are required after power-up or reset.

For ATE applications, the device offers low-noise bandwidth up to 22.7 kHz and wide bandwidth up to 700 kHz, with 99.95% full-scale settling in 7.5 µs. Post-calibration total unadjusted error is specified as 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. Recommended layout practices include close supply and reference decoupling and separation of analog paths from digital noise sources.

Defenders should practice disciplined free-throw box outs, stepping up the lane with feet together and hands raised while maintaining inside position and ensuring the shooter is covered. Strong rebounders may be pinched by two defenders, with the maximum permitted defenders placed along the lane. After allowing an offensive rebound, defenders should intensify efforts to prevent scoring. Teams should also practice assignments and early push-outs for both made and missed free throws.

Mineral companies owe more than $42 million in delinquent taxes to 12 Wyoming counties, largely because bankruptcies leave counties behind secured creditors. Campbell County is owed over $26 million, while Sheridan County is owed about $7.46 million, primarily by Storm Cat Energy and Summit Gas Resources.

County mineral taxes are collected after delays of up to 18 months, allowing companies time to reorganize, transfer property or enter bankruptcy. State severance taxes, due within two months, have far fewer delinquencies. Unpaid county taxes reduce funding for schools and public services; several Sheridan County educational institutions are owed substantial sums.

Recovering delinquent taxes requires costly legal action. The Powder River Basin Resource Council recommends monthly tax collection, perpetual liens, a state fund to assist counties in bankruptcies, and tax-debt checks before asset transfers. Previous legislative proposals failed, though another bill is planned. State officials report major corporations generally pay taxes on time, while the council argues proactive policy changes could address the problem.

Amazon’s unaudited Q1 2021 Form 10-Q reported net sales of $108.5 billion, up 44% year over year, and net income of $8.1 billion, versus $2.5 billion in Q1 2020. Operating income rose from $4.0 billion to $8.9 billion. North America, International, and AWS sales were $64.4 billion, $30.6 billion, and $13.5 billion, respectively. Operating cash flow was $4.2 billion, while investing and financing used $8.7 billion and $3.5 billion. At March 31, Amazon had $323.1 billion in assets, $103.3 billion in stockholders’ equity, and $73.3 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. The company incurred approximately $2.0 billion in COVID-19-related costs. Q2 guidance projected sales of $110 billion to $116 billion and operating income of $4.5 billion to $8.0 billion.

A Cherokee County community will honor school leader Maleka Johnson, who died when a tour boat exploded in the Bahamas. Her husband, Tiran, suffered severe leg injuries during their 15th-anniversary trip. Their 12-year-old son, Cameron, was with family in Tennessee, where relatives are now supporting him and preserving memories of his mother.
Figures 1–9 show perspective, elevation, plan, and exploded views of an under-sink organizer with a sliding storage basket. Broken lines indicate portions excluded from the claimed design.

The newly elected President expresses gratitude and acknowledges the office’s grave responsibilities. He pledges to uphold the Constitution, follow judicial decisions and early presidential practice, and appoint officials distinguished by honesty, capacity, fidelity, and integrity. His administration will serve the entire country, maintain effective armed forces, and preserve republican principles. Foreign policy will emphasize neutrality, peaceful relations, and diplomacy before force while protecting national rights. He will recommend constitutional measures supporting agriculture, commerce, manufacturing, infrastructure, public-debt reduction, official accountability, and economical spending, while respecting Congress’s legislative authority. He urges cooperation among government branches, reconciliation of conflicting interests, preservation of the Union, moderation, justice, liberal principles, and broad national patriotism.

Votes are being counted for by-elections in four Lok Sabha and 10 Assembly constituencies. Attention centres on Kairana, where BJP candidate Mriganka Singh faces an RLD candidate backed by the BSP, SP and Congress. Maharashtra’s Palghar and Bhandara-Gondia contests involve the BJP, Shiv Sena, NCP and Congress.

US stock options generally expire at the close on the third Friday monthly, with holiday adjustments. Backtests show the S&P 500 has above-average returns during OPEX week, averaging 0.2% per trade since SPY’s inception, though the effect has weakened recently and varies by month. The tested strategy buys at the week’s open and exits at the OPEX-day close.

OPEX day alone produced negative average returns, even with a 50-day moving-average filter. The following week also underperformed a random week: a strategy buying SPY at the OPEX Friday close and selling the next Friday generated a 1.5% CAGR while invested about 22% of the time. Results varied substantially by month; August averaged a 0.55% weekly gain, while September averaged a 0.94% loss with a 25% win rate.

The effect is attributed to declining open interest, hedging, delivery obligations, imbalances, and pin risk near expiration. The article concludes that the OPEX-week effect exists but is not independently tradeable without additional parameters. Similar consistent effects were not found in tested European futures markets.

After winning his third London Marathon title, Eliud Kipchoge visited Tottenham Hotspur, meeting Victor Wanyama, coach Mauricio Pochettino and players. Newly crowned World Marathon Majors champion, Kipchoge was expected to target Dennis Kimetto’s world record in Berlin.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed Noe Martinez Paredes’s guilty-plea conviction and 57-month sentence for a methamphetamine and heroin distribution conspiracy. Its independent review found no arguable grounds for relief, and it granted counsel’s motion to withdraw.

After a strong, physical Game 1 in which many shots found the net, the speaker expects the opponent to respond with its best effort. His team must start disciplined, remain physical, create chances at the net, and recognize that the series effectively resets with each game. He praises Jason’s growing leadership, comfort in New Jersey, and support for teammates. He also expects Belfour, one of the NHL’s best goalies, to rebound rather than surrender after a difficult game. The team’s young scorers are competitive, share strong chemistry, and protect each other. Winning the opener provided a lift and preserved home-ice advantage, but it will mean little without another strong performance in Game 2.

This retrospective study analyzed 1,383 noma patients treated at Nigeria’s Noma Children’s Hospital between 1999 and 2024 to estimate incidence and describe clinical presentation in northern Nigeria. Patients ranged from 8 months to 80 years, with a median age of 6; 54.2% were male. Acute disease accounted for 67.3% of cases, predominantly gangrene, while 32.7% had arrested noma. The cheeks were the most commonly affected sites.

Using the WHO estimation method and 2006 census data, the study estimated 62,067 new cases and an overall incidence of 114.5 per 100,000 population. Incidence was 120.7 per 100,000 among males and 108.1 among females. Annual incidence ranged from 0.2 to 21.3 per 100,000, averaging 4.4. Incidence was highest among children under five and was greater for gangrene than oedema or acute necrotizing ulcerative gingivitis. Sokoto had the highest state incidence, while Adamawa had the lowest; Kebbi recorded the highest incidence among young adults.

The findings support increased awareness and screening to identify reversible early-stage disease. Limitations included absent data from six eligible states or territories and a lack of detailed risk-factor analysis.

The disclosure describes secure, zero-knowledge sharing and storage of encrypted user data, particularly medical information. Client devices retain encryption keys while servers store or transmit encrypted data without access to plaintext. A layered key hierarchy derives keys from passwords or security-question answers to decrypt master and data-encryption keys, enabling credential recovery without exposing underlying data. Public/private keys support encrypted sharing between individuals, while shared data key hierarchies permit authorized groups to access and propose edits to shared copies. Owners may accept changes or revoke users by regenerating shared keys. Keys and credentials are discarded from memory when no longer needed, and sensitive keys are not stored unencrypted in non-volatile memory. The techniques may operate through applications, browsers, peer-to-peer protocols, cloud servers, messaging links, or printer drivers.

The Senate approved the Philippine Identification System Act with a 17-2 vote. It would assign citizens and foreign residents a PhilSys Number integrated across government identification systems, with the Philippine Statistics Authority managing the registry. Barbeque Nation filed for an IPO comprising a Rs 200 crore fresh issue and sale of 61.79 lakh shares. Fresh proceeds will fund new restaurants, loan repayment and corporate purposes. The company operated 81 restaurants across 42 Indian cities and one in Dubai as of June 2017.

Telstra CEO Andy Penn faces pressure to provide positive news at the company’s investor day after falling shares, an effective earnings downgrade, and an S&P rating cut. Expected dividend reductions and declining NBN compensation threaten earnings, though UBS and Morgan Stanley recently offered more positive assessments.

Researchers isolated two bacterial strains from chardonnay and cabernet sauvignon grape leaves that can degrade guaiacol, a major volatile phenol associated with wildfire smoke taint in wine. In laboratory tests, both strains reduced guaiacol to barely detectable levels within 96 hours. Scientists also identified the gene responsible for degradation; deleting it prevented one strain from consuming guaiacol. The bacteria did not grow on similar smoky compounds, indicating that additional microbes may be needed to address other contributors to smoke taint. This targeted microbial approach could avoid drawbacks of activated-charcoal filtration, which can remove desirable wine components such as color, but further research is required.

The lecture explains corporate carbon footprinting through a fictional chair manufacturer, WidgetCo. Carbon footprints require defining organizational and operational boundaries, gathering activity data, applying emissions factors, and deciding which indirect activities to include. Calculations commonly multiply energy or fuel consumption by emissions factors. Transportation may use fuel consumption or ton-miles, but aggregated weights and distances must not simply be multiplied because this can greatly overstate emissions.

Carbon footprints generally cover six Kyoto gases expressed as carbon dioxide equivalents. Scope one includes direct emissions from owned or controlled facilities and vehicles; scope two covers indirect emissions from purchased electricity; scope three includes other indirect emissions, such as outsourced transportation, business travel, product use, and disposal. Scope one and two are normally required under the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, while scope three is generally optional.

Organizational boundaries may use equity share or financial or operational control. For WidgetCo’s 50-50 Shanghai joint venture, this could mean accounting for 50%, 100%, or none of its emissions, depending on the selected method and control. Consequently, reported totals varied substantially even though actual supply-chain emissions did not change.

Data collection is often manual and difficult, involving multiple facilities, systems, units, and departments. Common problems include missing values, inappropriate aggregation, inconsistent emissions factors, unit conversion errors, and changing factors or corporate structures. Companies may track both absolute emissions and emissions per unit and may need to restate prior years for consistent comparisons.

Disclosure is increasingly driven by investors and business customers. Transparency can help explain higher reported emissions, especially when competitors use narrower boundaries. Corporate comparisons may be misleading because outsourced activities often fall outside scope one and two. FerretCo appeared cleaner partly because it used contract manufacturing, while WidgetCo owned manufacturing operations.

Broader value-chain standards seek to include emissions from raw materials through product use and disposal. Product carbon footprints focus on one product across its full life cycle and support carbon labeling. The following class applies life-cycle assessment to product-level environmental comparisons.

The study investigated barriers to distance education in university mathematics teaching after Turkish universities returned online following the February 2023 earthquake. It drew on literature categorizing barriers as technological, individual, pedagogical, and student-related, alongside frameworks distinguishing external barriers, teachers’ beliefs, and instructional design challenges.

Using Q methodology, researchers examined the views of 13 mathematics education faculty members from Turkish universities in the Marmara region. Participants ranked 50 statements derived from more than 300 e-learning studies and then commented on their strongest choices. Principal component analysis with Varimax rotation identified three perspectives: student-related, technology-related, and pedagogical barriers.

Six participants primarily emphasized student-related barriers, including weak engagement, reluctance to participate or assume responsibility, distraction, insufficient preparation, and limited interaction. Five participants emphasized technology and resource barriers, particularly inadequate access to digital libraries and restrictions affecting participation. The remaining perspective focused on pedagogical barriers specific to mathematics, such as unreliable online assessment, difficulties representing mathematical concepts, limitations of graphics tablets compared with blackboards, and reduced opportunities for deep thinking and sharing solutions.

Across all participants, curriculum and content barriers received the highest average score, followed by teacher-related, technology and institutional, and student-related barriers. The most discriminating statements concerned limited faculty feedback, inadequate digital-library access, and unreliable online assessment. Participants generally agreed that students were reluctant to respond to teachers and participate in lessons.

Faculty members reported substantial distance-education experience gained during COVID-19 and generally expressed confidence in using it. However, all argued that distance education alone was unsuitable for mathematics education. They favored blended, hybrid, or HyFlex models combining online and face-to-face teaching. The study concluded that its findings broadly aligned with existing barrier frameworks, while also identifying barriers arising from the distinctive pedagogy and curriculum of mathematics. Teacher-related barriers did not emerge as a separate factor.

Montclair State University celebrated mascot Rocky the Red Hawk’s 16th birthday with campus dancing, free bagels, candy, cupcakes and a Student Center party. Campus organizations offered gifts, photo booths and prizes, while Rocky posed and danced with students. The event included donations for a local food pantry, remarks from President Susan Cole, birthday cake and raffles for university merchandise, a bookstore gift card and parking passes. Students praised Rocky for bringing joy to campus and uniting the university community.

Ajay Bodke of Prabhudas Lilladher remains positive on Indian equities, citing recovering corporate earnings, fading GST and demonetization disruptions, comparatively sound macroeconomic conditions, expected 7.5% GDP growth, and crude oil prices projected at $60–70 per barrel. He expects the RBI may struggle to maintain a neutral monetary stance amid global tightening and domestic fiscal concerns.
