Retail investors need not fear the 10% long-term capital gains tax because equities remain an inflation-beating asset class; he suggests market declines can offer buying opportunities. He notes the Sensex has historically delivered substantially better returns than gold and expects financial-asset inflows to rise as inflation remains contained. Insurance and retail-focused private BFSI companies are identified as promising medium- to long-term sectors.

The Legislative Analyst’s Office said Gov. Jerry Brown’s proposed one-year contract granting 27,000 correctional employees a 5 percent raise lacks evidence of recruitment or retention problems. The office cited growth in entry-level staffing, stable mid-career employment, declining external job opportunities and wage growth exceeding inflation since 2001. The contract requires union and legislative approval. The administration estimates it will cost $338 million over two years, though overtime and pension expenses could raise costs. Unlike recent multi-year agreements, the simpler contract does not reduce health or future pension benefits or add retiree health deductions.

A study in Antiquity concludes that a mass grave beside St. Wystan’s church in Repton, Derbyshire, contains more than 250 members of the Viking Great Heathen Army from the winter of 874. Earlier radiocarbon dates suggesting older remains were distorted by the Vikings’ seafood-rich diet; correcting for this “marine reservoir effect” aligned the bones with the invasion’s chronology. Burials included women, injured warriors, weapons, a Thor’s hammer pendant, a boar’s tusk, and four apparent child sacrifices. The findings support accounts of the army’s invasion, conflict with Mercia and Wessex, and settlement in England, while highlighting the need to adjust radiocarbon dating of human bones for marine diets.

Bodycam footage shows Wildwood police confronting 20-year-old Emily Weinman on a New Jersey beach over suspected underage drinking. She passed a breathalyser, but officers continued questioning her about unopened alcohol and requested her surname, which she refused to provide. The encounter escalated, with an officer saying he struck and “slammed” her after alleging she tried to kick them, though this was not visible in the footage. Weinman accused officers of hitting, choking and pulling her hair. The incident prompted conflicting public reactions and an investigation; the officers were reassigned to desk duty. Weinman was charged with assault, resisting arrest, obstruction, disorderly conduct and possessing alcohol as a minor.

The March 2006 specification update documents numerous errata for AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device silicon revision A3. Issues affect PIT/PIC interrupt behavior, legacy DMA, UART and LPC access, PCI and I/O addressing, IDE/UDMA and PRD handling, ACPI/PMC registers and wake events, GPIO, USB clock gating, keyboard emulation, SMBus, RTC RAM, thermal alarms, and sleep controls. Consequences range from negligible debug-only effects and timing deviations to lost interrupts, invalid data, failed transfers, register corruption, and system hangs.

Recommended mitigations include avoiding unsupported access sequences and illegal addresses; waiting for DMA completion before UART access; using single-transfer rather than block or demand DMA; disabling affected clock-gating features; using correctly ordered IDE operations and DWORD-aligned PRDs; restricting ACPI/PMC accesses to supported widths; applying software traps or read-modify-write operations; using PWRBTN# or external circuitry for S3 wakeup; and programming sleep delays below PM_SED. Several issues have no operational impact or no available resolution. Issue numbering is nonsequential because resolved items were omitted.

Camp America offers people over 18 opportunities to work at summer camps across the USA and travel afterward, regardless of qualifications, though skills such as tennis coaching, horse riding and lifeguarding are especially valued. More than 8,000 places are available, with applications shared among 1,000 camps and UK recruitment fairs held in January and February. Camp work is fast-paced and includes supervising children through daily activities, meals and rest periods. The £599 package covers application fees, medical insurance, return flights and a 30-day travel period. Participants also receive $650–$1,200 in pocket money and can develop skills useful for future careers.

Authorities offered a $50,000 reward and expanded a nationwide search for Steve Stephens, 37, accused of posting Facebook video of himself fatally shooting Robert Godwin Sr., 74, at random in Cleveland. Stephens said he had “snapped,” blamed a former girlfriend and cited gambling and relationship problems, but police said his motive remained unknown. His cellphone was last detected Sunday near Erie, Pennsylvania, while reported sightings elsewhere were unconfirmed. Investigators said Godwin was the only victim linked to Stephens despite his claim of killing more than a dozen people. Police spoke with Stephens by phone and urged him to surrender. Friends, colleagues and his former girlfriend described him as kind or respectful, though he had filed for bankruptcy and reportedly struggled with gambling. Godwin’s family and community held a vigil, remembering the father of 10 as gentle and harmless.
Agriculture and fertiliser shares rose after the government increased paddy’s minimum support price by a record Rs 200 per quintal and approved MSPs for 14 kharif crops.

Aarhus University researchers, working with Arla, examined whether concentrating raw milk on farms through reverse osmosis affects quality. The process could reduce water transport and save resources. Tests found no negative effects on bacterial counts, free fatty acids, or protein breakdown, and concentrated milk was suitable for cheese and milk powder. Powder quality and shelf life matched products made from ordinary milk, though concentrated milk coagulated about ten minutes later in cheese production. Commercial viability depends largely on herd size, distance to dairies, energy use, equipment investment, and handling requirements. Farmers have shown interest, while dairies remain cautious about costs and processing implications.

Nested virtualization is unsupported under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP. SNP RestrictInjection limits hosts to #HV doorbells. Common host-notification formats support OS-level dispatch, while driver-specific virtualization messages retain flexible communication paths.

The study compares interdisciplinarity in highly impactful medical journals—defined as the top 10% by annual SCImago Journal Rank—with less impactful journals. It constructs cosine-normalized co-occurrence networks from second-level disease-related MeSH terms assigned to PubMed articles published in 1999, 2010, and 2022. To control for sample-size differences, impactful-journal networks are compared primarily with less-impactful networks based on June publications. Network measures assess knowledge integration, compactness, clustering, mixing, centrality, and core structure.

Less impactful journals consistently showed greater average node strength, network density, and compactness, indicating more interdisciplinary knowledge integration. Impactful-journal networks had higher modularity and were more compartmentalized, while clustering coefficients and negative strength assortativity were similar across journal groups. Both groups contained stable inner cores centered on communicable and sexually transmitted diseases, immunologic deficiency syndromes, genital diseases, and urogenital neoplasms.

Neoplasms by site ranked highest in both node strength and betweenness. Infections, nervous-system diseases, and neoplasms were consistently the most prominent broad categories. Infection research emphasized within-category integration, whereas nervous-system and cancer research more strongly connected distinct knowledge areas; cancer-related research was identified as the main driver of interdisciplinarity.

Positive and negative difference networks showed only a weak tendency for strong differences to be adjacent, but their differences formed topic clusters. These areas of relative prominence changed substantially over time, unlike the stable shared core of medical knowledge. Stronger links in impactful-journal networks also tended to produce stronger differences, following power-law relationships.

The authors conclude that highly impactful medical journals publish relatively more discipline-based research. They suggest peer-review practices and evidence, reporting, and guideline systems favor tightly specified, discipline-anchored studies over complex interdisciplinary work. Accommodating interdisciplinary evaluation within existing compliance structures is proposed as a potential remedy.

The British Foreign Secretary agrees with President Wilson’s desire for an early, lasting peace but argues that peace depends on correcting defective international conditions. He supports the Allied territorial proposals, including ending Turkish rule over alien peoples, citing Turkey’s German-backed aggression and massacres in Armenia and Syria. However, territorial changes alone cannot prevent renewed war if Germany retains its militarized political system, armaments, and methods of surprise attack. International treaties and laws are also insufficient without enforcement, since Germany rejected peace-oriented arbitration efforts and violated its pledge to defend a country it invaded and mistreated. Lasting security therefore requires more than territorial rearrangements or solemn agreements.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig was fired from Florida’s Southern District after conservatives publicized blog posts attributed to him criticizing President Donald Trump. Rosenzweig, who joined the office in 2020 and handled economic crimes, allegedly called Trump “mentally unfit” and “an institutional terrorist.” The Justice Department has also fired three prosecutors in the district who worked with former special counsel Jack Smith. Smith recently criticized dismissals of career officials and politically motivated prosecutions. Separately, Virginia U.S. Attorney Erik Siebert left after Trump pressured him to indict Letitia James and James Comey.
A thermal alarm triggers Faulted Standby and power removal, but cannot be detected there. The system periodically powers up and returns to Standby if the alarm remains asserted.

Choosing a content marketing partner resembles dating: seek someone whose strategy aligns with your goals, interview multiple candidates, verify claims through references and measurable results, clearly define your needs, and begin with a trial period. The right provider should produce effective content, simplify your workload, and be enjoyable to work with.

CompareCards highlights credit cards offering introductory 0% APR periods, generally lasting 12 to 21 months, for purchases, balance transfers, or both. Featured cards from Bank of America, Capital One, Citi, Discover, and others offer combinations of cash back, travel points, welcome bonuses, no annual fees, and category-based rewards. Regular variable APRs apply after promotional periods, and balance transfers may incur fees or exclusions.

The passage advises that low-interest cards can reduce borrowing costs, particularly for existing balances or large purchases, but notes differences between fixed and variable APRs. Introductory rates eventually revert to standard rates, making long-term terms important. Cardholders who pay balances fully and on time generally benefit most.

CompareCards states that its editors evaluate more than 100 cards from over 50 issuers using a data-driven rating system. The site receives compensation from listed companies but says this does not affect ratings or reviews. Applicants should verify current terms through each card’s application.

New York Attorney General Schneiderman announced the arrests of Guilderland Town Judge Richard Sherwood and financial adviser Thomas Lagan for allegedly stealing $4 million from family trusts they managed. Both face felony charges of grand larceny, fraud and criminal possession of stolen property following a multi-agency investigation.

The article argues that gold’s rally has not been confirmed by silver or mining stocks, with the GDXJ showing limited strength and remaining below its April closing high. It interprets miners’ underperformance as an early signal of a broader precious-metals decline. A play-action pass is designed to resemble a running play but always results in a pass. The quarterback fakes a handoff, often bootlegs, and searches for a receiver downfield. Its purpose is to draw linebackers and safeties toward the line of scrimmage, creating open space behind them.

Successful play action requires the entire offense to sell the run. The quarterback must execute a convincing handoff motion, while the offensive line initially blocks as if for a run before shifting to pass protection. Receivers commonly use crossing, drag, post, and other deeper routes to exploit vacated areas.

Play action is especially effective after establishing a strong running game or in situations where defenses expect a run, such as short-yardage, goal-line, and red-zone plays. Some professional teams use play action on 30–40% of passes.

Common concepts include the double post, which sends two receivers deep on post routes to challenge man coverage or a single safety, and Bubble Y Over, which combines short swing and bubble routes with deeper go, post, and crossing routes.

Unlike play action, a run-pass option allows the quarterback to choose after the snap between handing off and making a quick pass based on the defense’s reaction. In play action, the run is only a deception, and all intended outcomes are passes.

The lecture reviews plasma spectroscopy equilibria and X-ray imaging. Complete thermodynamic equilibrium has Boltzmann state populations, a common temperature for electrons, ions, and radiation, and balanced opposing processes, but is rarely realized. Local thermodynamic equilibrium assumes an optically thin plasma where collisions dominate excitation and de-excitation; the Saha equilibrium then relates temperature, electron density, ionization potential, degeneracy, and ion populations. Coronal or collisional-radiative equilibrium applies mainly to low-density, optically thin plasmas: collisions excite atoms, while spontaneous radiation de-excites them before another collision occurs. Non-LTE modeling requires identifying and solving for all relevant processes, though dominant mechanisms can sometimes justify neglecting others.

Spectroscopic modeling starts with plasma density and temperature, selects an appropriate equilibrium, calculates ionization and excitation populations, determines transition strengths, predicts spectra, accounts for radiation transport, reflections, and detector response, and compares results with measurements. Density and temperature may be iteratively adjusted. Strong, isolated, identified spectral-line ratios can estimate relative ion populations and temperature, especially in optically thin plasmas, though line identification, impurities, opacity, and line-integrated measurements create uncertainty and non-unique solutions.

X-ray spectroscopy is useful for hot plasmas and features strong, narrow characteristic lines. Highly ionized atoms may be described as helium-like or lithium-like according to their remaining electrons. K-shell transitions end at \(n=1\): K-alpha is \(n=2\) to \(n=1\) and is generally strongest, while K-beta is \(n=3\) to \(n=1\). L-shell transitions end at \(n=2\). These lines identify elements, ionization states, temperatures, and plasma impurities. Material absorption edges, including K and L edges, enable filters that select spectral regions.

Because ordinary lenses cannot focus X-rays, pinhole imaging uses geometric projection, producing inverted, magnified images. Resolution is limited by geometric blur, which decreases with pinhole size, and diffraction blur, which increases as the pinhole shrinks, creating an optimal size. Bent crystals can both select a wavelength and focus it, enabling monochromatic imaging, but are expensive.

X-ray detectors include time-integrated film, reusable laser-read image plates, time-gated cameras, and streak cameras. Film offers high resolution but no time information. Image plates store excitation in metastable states for later scanning. Time-gated cameras capture short intervals but are costly. Streak cameras record one spatial dimension over time and are fast, though their response can be nonlinear and difficult to quantify.

The Federal Circuit affirmed a $250,000 award under the Public Safety Officers’ Benefits Act to the estate of Christine Roberts, whose son, Sheriff Harold Presley, died in the line of duty. Roberts survived her son and filed a benefits claim but died before the Bureau of Justice Assistance completed processing and payment.

The majority held that eligibility is determined when the public safety officer dies. A beneficiary’s right vests upon surviving the officer’s death and is not lost through later death before agency processing or payment. The court rejected the government’s interpretation requiring beneficiaries to remain alive until payment, finding it contrary to the statute and implementing regulations. It also declined to defer to a 2006 regulation limiting payment to living payees.

Judge Prost dissented, arguing that the statute is silent or ambiguous about whether estates may receive benefits. She would have deferred to the Bureau’s regulation permitting payment only to living recipients, reasoning that this interpretation preserves benefits for surviving statutorily designated beneficiaries rather than estates.

Industry 4.0 makes information technology essential for productivity, customer service, and competitiveness. Indonesian digital startups are growing rapidly but often lack profitable management and effective business models. The study examines the Lean Canvas as a tool for creating sustainable digital startup strategies.

Using a descriptive qualitative method, researchers interviewed 120 startup founders, project managers, coworkers, and customers through purposive sampling and semi-structured interviews. Observations provided secondary data, while source triangulation supported validity.

The Lean Canvas structures a startup model around customer segments, value propositions, channels, customer relationships, revenue streams, key resources, key activities, partnerships, and cost structure. Its implementation involves identifying target customers and problems, validating solutions, developing unique value, selecting customer channels, defining revenue and costs, establishing performance metrics, and creating advantages competitors cannot duplicate.

The resulting “Beautiful Memories” model targets people organizing weddings, birthdays, graduations, and other events. It connects customers with photographers, video editors, decorators, and souvenir suppliers without restrictive packages. Its proposed value includes convenient service discovery and provider certification, promoted through social media, with revenue based on a 10% fee from each service order.

Resolute Marine Energy (RME), founded by Bill Staby in 2007, developed Wave O™, a wave-powered reverse-osmosis desalination system for coastal communities with scarce freshwater and weak or nonexistent electric grids. RME targeted South Africa, where millions lived in water-stressed areas and diesel-powered desalination was costly. Its proposed pilot in Ugu could produce water using submerged wave energy converters, hydraulic equipment, and standard desalination components.

Wave O™ was designed to be modular and scalable. One converter could serve about 850 people, while a 25-unit plant could serve approximately 21,400. RME estimated water costs of $1–$2 per cubic meter, compared with $3–$8 for some diesel-dependent communities. By 2012, RME had filed several provisional and international patent applications and had received most of its funding from U.S. government agencies.

RME signed preliminary agreements with Ugu and South Africa’s Council for Scientific and Industrial Research. The Development Bank of South Africa expressed interest in funding local pilot costs, while RME sought $6 million from impact investors for further testing and deployment. If successful, Ugu planned to purchase the first system.

RME considered three commercialization strategies. The first would generate electricity to run an existing desalination plant. It was technically simpler and eligible for U.S. grants, but offered lower margins, greater competition, energy-conversion losses, and limited bargaining power. The second would directly use hydraulic power for desalination. It promised lower production costs, higher water-based margins, greater efficiency, and fewer competitors, but required private financing, untested technology, and a desalination partner. The third was a vertically integrated “black box” producing both water and electricity. It offered control over the full value chain and additional innovation opportunities but required more capital, time, expertise, and local market capabilities.

RME also explored wave-generated electricity for remote Alaskan communities as a grant-funded learning opportunity, although management questioned whether pursuing electricity and water simultaneously might concern investors. The company’s central decision was whether to position itself as an energy company, a water company, or an integrated provider while satisfying stakeholders, attracting investors, and preserving a viable exit strategy.

The AEGEAN study found high apixaban compliance and adherence among subjects initiating therapy for atrial fibrillation, with no significant benefit from an additional educational program. Compliance exceeded 95% through Week 24 and 94% at Week 48 across groups. Mean adherence at 24 weeks was 91.64% with primary standard of care (SOC) and 91.88% with education; from first dose to Week 48, it was 89.52% and 90.93%, respectively. Adherence declined significantly during later treatment periods in both groups.

Persistence was approximately 91% at Week 24 and 85%–88% at Week 48, without significant group differences. Full adherence declined from about 27% at Week 24 to about 15% at Week 48. Sensitivity analyses supported these findings. Most subgroup analyses showed no significant interaction, although interactions from Weeks 24–48 were observed by atrial fibrillation type and sex.

Safety outcomes were similar between groups. Before Week 24, adverse events occurred in about 51%–52% of subjects, serious adverse events in 12%–15%, and bleeding events in 6.5%–9.0%. Between Weeks 24 and 48, adverse events occurred in 33.8%–40.8%, while bleeding occurred in 3.2%–4.1%. Major and fatal bleeding events were uncommon. Overall, 24 deaths were reported, no pregnancies occurred, and laboratory review identified no clinically concerning hepatic or renal signal.

CoSn₂ single crystals exhibit metallic resistivity with a slope change below 25 K, without corresponding specific-heat or magnetic anomalies. Susceptibility remains paramagnetic from 2–300 K. Synchrotron single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals weak commensurate superlattice reflections and a transition from tetragonal I4/mcm symmetry to an acentric monoclinic C2-related superstructure, with doubled a and c axes and minimal lattice distortion. Angle-dependent magnetoresistance similarly changes from nearly fourfold symmetry above 40 K to twofold symmetry below 20–25 K.

Phonon calculations show no imaginary frequencies, indicating dynamic stability of the high-temperature structure. Electronic-structure calculations identify possible Fermi-surface nesting and susceptibility maxima capable of producing an electronically driven instability that breaks rotational symmetry and couples weakly to the lattice. Polarization-dependent ARPES reveals orbital-selective anisotropy and a reduction from fourfold to twofold intensity symmetry, suggestive of electronic nematicity, though further investigation is required to establish its origin.

ARPES measurements broadly agree with density-functional calculations and identify anisotropic type-I and type-II band crossings belonging to a continuous nodal loop in the kx–kz plane. Spin-orbit coupling opens only a very small gap. The combined structural, transport, susceptibility, and spectroscopic results position CoSn₂ as a nonmagnetic nodal-line semimetal displaying low-temperature symmetry breaking with weak structural distortion and a probable electronically driven contribution.

The preprint proposes an interpretable causal Bayesian network as a complementary tool for diagnosing Alzheimer’s disease (AD), including early- and late-onset cases. Unlike previous models, it distinguishes suspected disease from formal diagnosis and updates probabilities as risk factors, symptoms, cognitive and biomarker tests, competing conditions, and functional independence become known.

The model follows validated diagnostic criteria and medical reasoning patterns. Its structure and parameters combine literature estimates, expert judgement, U.S. census data, and the National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center dataset. It includes AD risk factors, manifestations, treatments, complications, depression, other dementias, and reversible causes of cognitive impairment.

Internal validation matched the estimated general-population AD prevalence of 3.336%. Clinical scenarios demonstrated probability updating, explaining-away effects, and backward reasoning. For example, positive cerebrospinal-fluid biomarkers increased suspected AD probability from 65% to 95%, while identifying another dementia reduced AD probability in a separate scenario.

The model can operate with incomplete information, supports “what-if” analyses, and provides visible justification for predictions. However, it should be used cautiously alongside clinical evaluation. Limitations include broad aggregation of non-AD conditions, selection bias in the dataset, uncertain rates of missed or incorrect diagnoses, manually judged parameters, omitted causal relationships and variables, and uneven sample sizes. Proposed future work includes separately modelling common dementias and reversible conditions, improving definitive-diagnosis data, expanding early-onset and disease-management components, and developing a research model for preclinical AD.

The Missouri court affirmed judgment for the defendant in Susan Ann Vansickle’s malicious-prosecution action arising from her arrest for obstructing a highway. Evidence of the arresting officer’s insulting conduct was properly excluded because the defendant had not instigated it. A later trespass judgment and county-court proceedings concerning a new road were also irrelevant to probable cause when prosecution began.

Verbal directions from the county court, though legally ineffective to establish the road, were admissible to show the defendant road overseer’s good faith and absence of malice. The defendant could testify about his intentions and lack of ill feeling.

Probable cause requires that the prosecutor actually believe the accused guilty and have reasonable grounds supporting that belief; Hickman v. Griffin was overruled on this point. Voluntarily waiving preliminary examination and entering a recognizance constituted prima facie evidence of probable cause. Malicious prosecution requires both malice and lack of probable cause; malice is not legally inferred from lack of probable cause alone. The jury instructions, considered together, were sufficiently favorable to the plaintiff. Napton, J., dissented regarding the probable-cause standard, and Henry, J., disagreed that waiver of examination should establish probable cause.

The Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine provides optional extensions to SEV and SNP for moving memory pages between physical locations while preserving guest physical addresses. It supports migration of pages targeted by concurrent DMA and SNP-protected guest pages inaccessible to the hypervisor. TMPM availability is indicated by the ENGINE_READY status bit and requires IOMMU enablement.

Commands are submitted through a dedicated ring buffer and can process up to 128 pages. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates hypervisor or default pages, coordinates with IOMMUs, pauses DMA, copies data, and updates host page-table entries. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages from Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid state to destinations in the new Pre-Migration state; afterward, destinations inherit source states and sources become Pre-Migration. Guest migration does not support concurrent DMA. PM_GET_CAPABILITIES reports firmware capabilities and versions, while PM_NOOP can mark the end of a command sequence.

Pages generally require 4 KB alignment; host page-table entries require 8-byte alignment. Direct PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migration of 2 MB pages is unsupported, while guest 2 MB pages must be aligned and physically contiguous or split into 4 KB pages. Some structures cannot be migrated, including IOMMU data structures, private vIOMMU page tables, pinned buffers, ring buffers, and argument pages.

Commands may complete successfully, partially successfully, or fail entirely. Per-page status identifies individual results, including retryable RMP exclusivity conflicts. Parallel execution means command order is not guaranteed. Better performance is achieved with at least 16 pages per command, with maximum performance at 128 pages, a continuously populated ring buffer, and limited interrupt requests.

The driver initializes ring-buffer addresses, size, thresholds, interrupts, and IOMMU PAGEMIGRATION_EN bits. Processing can be paused while in-flight commands finish and later resumed. Shared interrupt sources report queue thresholds, empty queues, completion, errors, invalid write pointers, and ring-buffer memory failures.

Firmware reload requires paused operations, ring-buffer teardown, and preferably disabled IOMMU page-migration bits. Reload firmware must be the same or a newer version. Drivers must verify ENGINE_READY afterward. EPYC Family 19h is identified by FW_VER_Major 71.

Format, migration-entry, ring-buffer, and hardware errors are reported through command, entry, status-register, or Machine Check Architecture mechanisms. Hardware failures may leave all pages in a command unrecoverable and can require saving state, terminating virtual machines, or rebooting.

The study investigated pedagogical approaches for integrating education for sustainable development into South Africa’s Technology curriculum. Using experiential learning theory, it examined teachers’ sustainability knowledge, curriculum opportunities, and teaching methods.

A qualitative case study involved eight Grade 7–9 Technology teachers from Mpumalanga’s Ehlanzeni District. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations, then analysed using inductive content analysis and triangulation.

Teachers understood sustainable development as preserving resources, reducing technology’s environmental harm, using renewable energy, meeting societal needs, and drawing on indigenous practices. They identified opportunities to teach sustainability through recycling, responsible technology use, renewable energy, design, investigation, and practical projects. Collaborative learning was viewed as particularly useful for knowledge sharing, problem-solving, creativity, cross-cultural learning, and environmental stewardship.

However, classroom observations showed limited integration of sustainability concepts. Teaching relied mainly on demonstrations and lectures, with little collaborative or experiential learning. Lessons rarely connected environmental, social, and economic dimensions of sustainability, even when addressing recycling or biodegradable materials.

The study recommends integrating sustainability throughout the Technology curriculum rather than treating it as a separate topic. Teachers should use collaborative, investigative, context-based, and hands-on approaches; incorporate indigenous knowledge; promote responsible resource use and sustainable design; and engage learners in real-world environmental challenges. The study was limited to eight teachers in two circuits of one district and used only qualitative methods. Further research should include additional regions, educational phases, and mixed qualitative and quantitative approaches.

This phase 4 prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial will evaluate Thai cannabis oil in 90 women aged 18–70 with metastatic breast cancer receiving chemotherapy at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital, Thailand. Participants with Edmonton Symptom Assessment System scores of at least 3 will be assigned equally to Ganja Oil, Metta Osot, or placebo, taken nightly for 90 days.

The study will assess whether cannabis oil improves chemotherapy-related symptoms and quality of life while monitoring adverse effects. Blood, saliva, stool, and skin samples will be collected at baseline and day 90; clinical assessments will occur at enrollment, shortly after treatment begins, day 30, and day 90. Participants will then be monitored for withdrawal symptoms for one month.

Secondary objectives include examining bacterial and fungal microbiome diversity, cytokines, bacterial translocation markers, and metabolites before and after treatment. Pharmacokinetic measures, including maximum concentration and time to maximum concentration, and pharmacogenetic profiles will also be studied. Analyses will follow an intention-to-treat approach, with microbial diversity assessed using Shannon, Chao 1, and Jaccard indices.

The trial was approved in December 2022 and was scheduled to begin recruitment around January 2023. It is funded by Thailand’s Thai Traditional Medical Knowledge Fund.

Soccer position numbering began in 1920s England with players numbered 1–11 from goalkeeper through defenders, halfbacks, and forwards in a 2-3-5 formation. The 1950s W-M formation repositioned inside forwards and the center halfback while retaining numbers, producing enduring terms such as “Number 9” for a central striker and “Number 10” for a scoring playmaker. From the 1960s, tactical experimentation, overlapping roles, Total Football, and player-selected jersey numbers weakened fixed number-position associations. In 2012, U.S. Soccer introduced a standardized 4-3-3 system: 1 goalkeeper; 2, 3, 4, and 5 defenders; 6, 8, and 10 midfielders; and 7, 9, and 11 forwards. It also established technical, tactical, physical, and mental position profiles. Related terms include “False 9” for a striker who drops into midfield and “Double-9s” for paired central strikers.

Jonathan Huberdeau scored with 7.7 seconds remaining to give the Florida Panthers a 3-2 win over Detroit. Aleksander Barkov and Aaron Ekblad also scored for Florida, while Harri Sateri made 26 saves. Danny DeKeyser scored both Red Wings goals, and Petr Mrazek stopped 30 shots.

A punter helps flip field position after an offense fails to advance, aiming for punts with sufficient distance, hang time, accuracy, spin, and touch so coverage teams can stop opponents deep in their territory. Punters need leg strength for long kicks and precision for placing short punts inside the 20-yard line. They may also run or throw on fake punts and commonly serve as holders for field goals and extra points.

Typical skills include accuracy, coordination, flexibility, creativity, and lower-body power. Punters generally have slim builds, measuring about 5'10"–6'2" and 180–210 pounds. Notable punters include Shane Lechler, who holds the stated NFL record of 47.6 average yards per punt, and Ray Guy, a first-round draft pick who helped the Oakland Raiders win three Super Bowls. Though often overlooked, punters are important because field position affects an opponent’s likelihood of scoring and can influence a defense’s confidence and game momentum.

Studies show millennials generally save well for retirement, often starting younger than Generation X, with many saving over 10% of their salaries and some accumulating at least $100,000. However, they tend to invest more conservatively than older generations, holding larger shares in cash, bonds and other stable investments. Many find stock-market investing intimidating, partly because they experienced the 2008–09 financial crisis.

Avoiding stocks could threaten millennials’ long-term retirement security because historical stock-market returns have substantially exceeded money-market account returns, despite periods of severe losses. Financial experts advise viewing investment risk within the broader context of life decisions and accepting some risk to pursue long-term goals. Millennials interested in investing can begin with simple retirement portfolios or use robo-advisors for investment selection and management.
