The disclosure describes a cloud microservices architecture that abstracts hardware and software implementations behind a standardized API. Microservice-capable resources—including software, CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, resource pools, ASICs, and hardware accelerators—register their functions, interfaces, connection capabilities, configuration data, performance attributes, and load information with a service discovery function and catalog.

Applications request functions without specifying implementation details. A microservices driver queries the catalog, selects or provisions an appropriate instance based on availability, performance, locality, priority, and load, maps generic API calls to native invocations, and establishes communication through message forwarders. New instances may be spawned or configured dynamically, including programming FPGAs using stored gate configurations.

Multiple microservices can be chained so outputs pass directly between instances rather than repeatedly returning to host software. Path identifiers, unified addressing, shared buffers, RDMA, REST APIs, PCIe, memory-mapped I/O, and other access methods support local or remote execution. Message forwarding can transform messages, manage queues, enable zero-copy transfers, track completion, and support dynamic load balancing. The architecture aims to reduce latency and overhead, improve portability and scalability, enable autoscaling, and transparently use optimized data-center resources.

Google laid off more than 100 employees in design-related roles within its cloud unit, including user experience research and platform teams. Some design teams were halved, with many U.S.-based roles affected. Certain employees have until early December to find another internal position. The cuts come as Google prioritizes AI investment and seeks greater efficiency.

Micro E-mini S&P 500 Index futures (MES), launched by CME Group in 2019, are one-tenth the size of E-mini contracts and track the S&P 500. Each contract equals $5 times the index value, has a minimum fluctuation of 0.25 index points worth $1.25, and is cash-settled. Quarterly contracts expire in March, June, September, and December, with trading ending at 9:30 a.m. ET on the third Friday of the contract month.

MES trades electronically on CME Globex from Sunday evening through Friday, with daily maintenance breaks. Traders need a funded futures brokerage account and can use leverage, which increases potential losses. CFDs offer similar exposure without fixed expiration dates.

MES strategies may combine technical and fundamental analysis, entry and exit rules, position sizing, and risk management. The passage references a paywalled mean-reversion strategy backtested on continuous, back-adjusted E-mini data using daily closing prices, without risk-management parameters. Historically, S&P 500 futures have performed better in winter and spring than in summer.

The contract’s reported all-time high was 4808.25 in January 2022, while its low since inception was 2174.00 in March 2020. As of December 9, 2022, it traded at 3959.50, making one contract worth $19,797.50. MES can be used for speculation, portfolio diversification, or equity-market hedging.

Janata Congress Chhattisgarh announced 11 candidates early for next year’s 90-seat assembly elections. Ajit Jogi said six sitting MLAs and several core committee members had also been selected but would be named later. He said the timing allowed candidates to prepare. The BJP dismissed JCC as Congress’s “B team” and targeted over 65 seats. Jogi identified farmers, women, unemployment and Naxalism as major issues, while observers linked the announcement to his caste-certificate controversy.

China’s official manufacturing PMI rose to 49.8 in September, beating expectations of 49.6 and marking its strongest reading since March, though remaining in contraction. RatingDog’s manufacturing PMI reached 51.2, above the 50.2 forecast. Official non-manufacturing PMI slipped to 52.9, while RatingDog’s services PMI fell to 50. Manufacturers faced weak domestic demand, higher U.S. tariffs and trade disruptions. An October Politburo meeting is expected to indicate Beijing’s policy response to the third-quarter slowdown.

Reports focused on Enron’s political influence, energy deregulation and President George W. Bush’s energy plan. Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay presented Vice President Dick Cheney with proposals opposing wholesale electricity price controls, promoting open transmission access and reducing barriers to new infrastructure. Bush’s plan reflected several priorities Enron supported. Enron had contributed heavily to Bush’s campaigns, cultivated bipartisan political relationships and advocated nominees to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission who favored competitive electricity markets.

Bush’s plan emphasized expanded oil, gas, coal and nuclear production, new power plants, pipelines and transmission lines, while offering conservation tax credits. Traditional energy, construction and labor interests generally expected benefits, while critics said the plan provided little immediate price relief, insufficient support for renewable energy and inadequate attention to climate change. California officials and environmental groups strongly opposed it.

Japanese utilities rejected Enron’s proposal to separate electricity generation and transmission, warning it could weaken supply responsibility and create California-style failures. Enron argued liberalization would increase competition and reduce costs.

Other reports said Enron leased substantial office space in Mumbai and planned to withdraw from the Dolphin gas project, where it held a stake and was responsible for pipeline construction, gas marketing and project management.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K on November 15, 2018, reporting results for the quarter ended October 28, 2018. Exhibits include its third-quarter fiscal 2019 earnings press release and CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress. The materials are furnished, not filed, under applicable securities laws.

Wickes, B&Q and Homebase will operate reduced hours over Christmas and New Year, with customers advised to check local store finders. Wickes closes on Christmas Day, opens 10am–5pm on Boxing Day, 6am–4pm on New Year’s Eve and 10am–4pm on New Year’s Day. B&Q closes on Christmas Day and generally opens 10am–4pm on Christmas Eve, Boxing Day, New Year’s Eve and New Year’s Day, with regional exceptions. Homebase closes on Christmas Day, opens 7am–5pm on Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve, 10am–5pm on Boxing Day and 10am–4pm on New Year’s Day, when Scotland and Eire stores close. Argos customers should check its store locator.

The MOVE Index, known as the bond market’s VIX, measures U.S. interest-rate volatility using implied volatility from one-month OTC options. Created by Merrill Lynch in 1998 and acquired by ICE in 2019, it has averaged about 85 since 2000. It recently surged amid Federal Reserve rate increases and banking concerns.

Unlike high VIX readings, elevated MOVE levels generally do not signal attractive buying opportunities and generate few bond-trading signals. A strategy backtested from 2002 held TLT when MOVE was below its historical mean and sold when it exceeded the mean. The strategy produced modest, relatively steady growth and reduced maximum drawdown to about half that of buy-and-hold, helping particularly in 2022 but reducing returns in 2008. The passage concludes that MOVE effectively indicates bond-market volatility but is not clearly useful as a standalone bond-trading indicator.

NVIDIA’s Compensation Committee adopted its Fiscal Year 2022 Variable Compensation Plan on March 15, 2021. Eligible executive officers may receive cash payments based on achievement of specified fiscal 2022 revenue goals, with threshold, base, and stretch levels. Participants generally must remain employed through the payment date. Base-plan target awards are: CEO Jen-Hsun Huang, $2 million (200% of salary); CFO Colette Kress, $300,000 (33%); Ajay Puri, $650,000 (68%); Debora Shoquist, $250,000 (29%); and Timothy Teter, $250,000 (29%). Fiscal 2022 ends January 30, 2022.

NatWest and The Future Laboratory identified eight rising UK fraud trends after more than £100m in banking fraud occurred in early 2017. Schemes include smartphone malware, fake discounted World Cup tickets, personalised social-media scams, “Brexit-proof” investments, money mules, fake wedding services, dating-app catfishing and solicitor impersonation. Consumers should verify information requests directly, update security software and avoid unknown links, files and contacts.

California expanded state control over electricity after deregulation left utilities financially distressed. Gov. Gray Davis authorized state power purchases, long-term contracts worth $45 billion to $50 billion, borrowing, emissions exemptions, new energy agencies and proposed transmission acquisitions. Critics warned of reduced oversight, costly contracts, conflicts of interest and long-term economic burdens, while Davis said intervention had lowered prices and secured supply.

Legislators remained divided over rescuing Southern California Edison. Competing plans differed over purchasing its transmission system, repaying utility debt and preserving customers’ ability to buy power from alternative suppliers. Consumer and business groups opposed proposed costs and restrictions. PG&E, already bankrupt, received court approval for management bonuses.

Davis dedicated a 90-megawatt Otay Mesa peaker plant built in 90 days, the first of 10 planned facilities. Separately, officials investigated energy consultants’ stockholdings in power companies and delayed financial disclosures.

Southern California Edison recruited churches to enroll low-income customers in a program offering 20% discounts and exemptions from rate increases. About 62% of an estimated one million eligible customers participated.

The Bush administration promoted its national energy plan while emphasizing conservation more than previously, though critics questioned its relevance to Western states.

California consumers awaited a decision on another possible rate increase to support a proposed $13.4 billion bond issue. Officials said an increase might not be necessary as power costs declined and revenue improved, but did not rule one out.

Pakistan’s inflation indices are expected to be rebased by June 2018 and operational in fiscal year 2018-19, replacing the outdated 2007-08 base. Delayed by the population census, the process uses surveys and industrial data. PBS also plans separate rural, urban and total CPI measures to address urban bias.

Soccer vision—the ability to see, interpret, anticipate, and respond to positioning and movement—is essential for passing, attacking, defending, and quick decision-making. Ball skills alone are insufficient without spatial awareness. Players can improve vision through practice, familiarity with teammates, and related activities involving angles and strategy.

Four fundamentals are emphasized: remain aware of every player’s position by constantly scanning; raise the head quickly after controlling the ball and keep the eyes, head, and body moving; recognize peripheral events, anticipate primary and secondary options, and monitor threats; and communicate useful information through team-standard verbal and nonverbal signals. Players should notice teammates making runs, avoid tunnel vision, and reposition based on potential dangers.

Coaches can support vision by teaching players to take the first touch away from the body and receive passes with the foot opposite the pass’s direction. A suggested drill uses two differently colored teams in a grid, requiring players to scan before receiving and pass only to the other color, progressing from two-touch to one-touch play without calling for the ball. Visualization may also help improve on-field vision.

Gianluca Vialli says Juventus must prevent Barcelona and the Camp Nou crowd from gaining momentum in their second-leg clash. Recalling Chelsea’s 5-1 extra-time defeat at Barcelona in 2000, he warned that an inflamed atmosphere can transform the match. Vialli praised Juventus’ stability, confidence and European stature, while identifying Sergio Busquets and an angry Lionel Messi as major threats. He called Juve’s first-leg display nearly perfect and said effective transitions, ruthless counterattacking and another strong performance from Gianluigi Buffon will be crucial.

Hucknall and Linby Dolphins finished fifth among eight teams at a 55-race novice gala despite injuries and illness. Katie Hill earned three runner-up finishes, while the boys’ U10 medley relay won its event.

Mats Zuccarello said the team played two good games despite mistakes and overtime setbacks. Confident in the group’s depth and leadership, he emphasized learning from past series, focusing on the next game, using home support, and winning two straight to even the series.

A Citizen experiment found that academics who submit work to predatory publishers or conferences may have their contact details and even unpublished submissions circulated among other scammers. OMICS International accepted bogus papers about underwater birds and flying pigs for conference presentation fees. Afterward, unrelated journals solicited full articles based on the fake bird abstract. Other publishers referenced a nonexistent paper previously submitted to test another website and repeatedly addressed the reporter as “Dr. Spears1,” apparently copying his Twitter username. The experiment suggests that interacting once with predatory publishers can result in prolonged targeting by similar operators.

VentureWire’s June 6, 2001 edition reports that Napster licensed MusicNet’s platform and catalog; Comdisco Ventures CEO James Labe resigned amid restructuring; Charter Growth Capital became Focus Ventures; and optical networking firm Movaz raised $62 million.

Other financing included rounds for InsureZone, Mergermarket, Clustra, Screentec, AtriCure, OmniCluster, DataCert, Alloptic, GotMarketing, and several others. Alien Technology was also seeking strategic partners for a planned $40 million round.

WhatsHotNow.com, Hologix, TerraShare, Ditto.com, and The Dock ceased or began winding down operations, while Hiwire cut 17 employees. MetaTV acknowledged criminal allegations against CEO Ranjit Singh Sahota and placed co-founder Andrew Lev in charge of daily operations.

Corporate developments included eToll becoming FastForward, the launch of Workadia with $16.7 million, and acquisitions or mergers involving SetNet, Torque Systems, Omnicom Group, Employment Wizard, and CareerSite. The newsletter also covers board appointments, executive changes, venture-capital hires, and corrections concerning Optium and iWitness.

The S&P 500 fell 3.33% from Thursday’s record high over two sessions and lost 2.36% for the week, though futures indicated a roughly 0.5% rebound. Investor sentiment improved slightly, while the VIX rose to 21.90. Crude oil declined after OPEC+ announced a sixth consecutive monthly production increase, amid tariff uncertainty and concerns about weakening demand. The outlook suggests the rebound may be temporary within a broader consolidation or downtrend, with earnings, low volatility, seasonal weakness, and stretched valuations supporting careful or defensive positioning.

European shares rose despite Britain formally triggering Brexit, with the STOXX 600 gaining 0.4 percent to a nearly 16-month high and Germany’s DAX approaching its record. Daimler and upgraded auto suppliers lifted automotive stocks. London Stock Exchange and Deutsche Boerse gained after EU regulators blocked their proposed merger. Banks underperformed amid expectations that ECB monetary easing would continue, though Deutsche Bank rose on optimism over its capital increase. Engie and 3I Group advanced following analyst upgrades. Scout24 fell after weak results and guidance, while Aurelius plunged more than 35 percent as investors remained unconvinced by its response to a short-seller report.

Chesterfield residents sent messages of support to Craig Burr, 33, after he threatened to jump onto the A617 Hasland bypass. He was taken to hospital and released before discussing his mental health struggles with the Derbyshire Times, which runs the You Are Not Alone campaign. Burr thanked supporters for their kind words. NHS guidance advises seeking help from a GP, trusted person or immediate-support helpline. Around one in four UK residents experiences a mental health problem annually, while about one in eight affected adults receives treatment.

XLP, the Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR Fund, tracks large, low-volatility consumer staples companies in the S&P 500 and is rebalanced quarterly. The passage argues that XLP is an underused but effective trading vehicle because it has few sudden moves, tends toward mean reversion, supports short strategies, and provides diversification through lower correlation with ETFs such as QQQ and SPY. A backtest of three short strategies produced 418 trades, a 75% win rate, an average gain of about 0.4% before costs, and a 2.35 profit factor. Although mean-reversion strategies can suffer occasional large losses, XLP’s low-volatility holdings have limited such outcomes in the reported results.

Holik was considered a needed, pressure-tested addition whose return helped New Jersey reach the Stanley Cup Finals. Despite losing, the team remained confident after overcoming adversity in earlier series. Playing in the opponent’s difficult building and adjusting to the ice could affect their speed, but they believed they could succeed. The speaker described being surprised by a hard, rising shot that beat his glove. Although the opponent had momentum and a strong home record, New Jersey aimed to regain home-ice advantage by winning one game while maintaining respect for its opponent.

Effective diversification requires selecting assets based on how they respond to risks and align with financial goals, investment horizons, and liquidity needs. Common mistakes include excluding major holdings such as provident funds or stock options when assessing asset allocation; owning so many investments that quality, returns, costs, and monitoring suffer; and buying products without understanding them. Financial advisers or mutual funds can help address limited expertise, but investors should still understand available assets.

Diversification must also support specific goals. For example, retirement portfolios may need income-generating assets, while excessive exposure to long-term products and real estate can create liquidity problems. Asset allocations should be reviewed and rebalanced periodically because differing returns cause them to drift. Investors may also diversify within asset classes, such as across equity sectors and market capitalizations or debt issuers’ credit profiles and tenors, though related subcategories may move similarly.

From January 2010 to August 2012, buying weakness or selling strength based on SPY’s last trading hour appeared effective. Trades entered at the next open and exited at 11:30. Buying at the prior close produced similar returns but larger drawdowns, while targets and stop-losses did not improve results.
AOL Instant Messenger will be discontinued December 15, reflecting changing communication habits. Users shared nostalgic memories and usernames on social media with the hashtag #AIMmemories.

Apple appointed Monica Lozano to its Board of Directors effective January 4, 2021, and assigned her to the Audit and Finance Committee. She will receive a $100,000 annual retainer, participate in the Non-Employee Director Stock Plan, and received 281 restricted stock units. Apple reported no transactions with Lozano requiring disclosure under Regulation S-K.

The DAWN-PLASMA study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 multicenter trial comparing standard supportive care plus convalescent plasma with standard care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Conducted under ethical and Good Clinical Practice guidelines, it used a 2:1 randomization ratio. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary and exploratory endpoints assessed clinical status, ventilation, hospitalization, mortality, thromboembolism, transfusion effects, antibody titers, safety, quality of life, laboratory findings, vital signs, and viral and immune measures.

Eligible adults had confirmed or clinically supported SARS-CoV-2 infection and respiratory disease indicators. Patients already receiving mechanical ventilation, facing unacceptable safety risks, having severe plasma allergy, treatment restrictions excluding ventilation, or recent anti-CD20 therapy were excluded.

Plasma recipients were intended to receive four units totaling 800–1000 mL, beginning within 12 hours of randomization, with neutralizing antibody titers of at least 1/160. The statistician remained blinded until database lock.

Between May 2, 2020 and January 26, 2021, 499 patients were assessed and 489 randomized: 326 to plasma and 163 to control. Six randomized patients were excluded from the Full Analysis Set because of absent confirmed infection or immediate consent withdrawal. The Per Protocol Set excluded 26 plasma patients receiving fewer than four units and three control patients receiving plasma before Day 30.

Among plasma recipients, median time to first transfusion was five hours and median administered volume was 884 mL. Of administered units, 80.7% had antibody titers of at least 1/320; 294 patients received all four units. Baseline characteristics and concomitant COVID-19 therapies were similar between groups.

Wound Care Advantage, Dr. David G. Armstrong, the Southwestern Academic Limb Salvage Alliance and Gen1 Research launched Advanced Discovery, a research alliance focused on improving wound care through evidence-based studies. The alliance will evaluate diagnostic and treatment methods using an international network of wound and hyperbaric treatment centers, with Gen1 providing administrative and research infrastructure.

Advanced Discovery will give approved manufacturers access to de-identified clinical data from more than 42,000 patients and 880,000 wound assessments collected over 16 years, supplemented by SALSA’s global academic affiliations. Its goals include improving healing outcomes, preventing amputations and reducing treatment costs. Chronic wounds affect about 5.7 million U.S. patients and cost the healthcare system more than $20 billion annually.

Wound Care Advantage manages outpatient wound care and hyperbaric centers, SALSA contributes specialized limb-salvage expertise, and Gen1 provides coordinators, analytics and research management software.

CompareCards highlights partner credit cards offering introductory 0% APR periods of 6 to 18 months on purchases or balance transfers, followed by variable APRs generally ranging from 17.99% to 28.99%. Featured cards provide cash back, travel points or miles, sign-up bonuses, and in many cases no annual fee. Balance-transfer fees and eligibility terms vary. The site explains fixed and variable APRs, notes that promotional rates revert after introductory periods, and says its data-driven ratings cover over 100 cards from more than 50 issuers. Although it receives compensation from listed companies, it states this does not affect reviews.

The study developed UZEP, a cloud-based distance education platform designed to help higher education institutions rapidly transition to online teaching during emergencies such as Covid-19. Implemented through an Education as a Service model, UZEP requires no university-owned infrastructure, supports integration with university management systems, scales to demand, and complies with personal-data protection requirements.

UZEP combines a learning management system, BigBlueButton-based virtual classrooms, online examinations, homework and project assessment, digital material sharing, announcements, surveys, and reporting. Its examination module supports several question types, randomized question sets, monitoring measures, and up to 10,000 simultaneous students.

Using a developmental research model, the platform was deployed at 12 Turkish universities beginning in fall 2020. Between October 2020 and February 2021, it served 78,732 users and supported 13,180 courses, 11,314 exams, and 358,657 exam sessions. Feedback from experts, pilot users, administrators, lecturers, and students informed continuing improvements.

Evaluations found UZEP easy to learn, quickly deployable, integrated, scalable, and suitable for users with limited technical skills. Lecturers rated its virtual classroom component highest, while students reported above-midpoint satisfaction. Compared with Moodle, edX, and Google Suite, UZEP performed strongly as an integrated emergency higher-education platform but lacked social networking, collaboration, advanced analytics, and some reporting and assessment capabilities. Planned improvements include communication tools, interactive materials, enhanced reporting, and artificial intelligence for examination security and assessment. Limitations include reliance on self-reported questionnaires, comparison with only three other platforms, and evaluation during unusually high pandemic demand.

Plumbers Local 93 benefit funds sued Waterworks under ERISA to compel an audit, claiming the company was bound by a collective bargaining agreement. The parties disputed whether a 2004 meeting created an agreement: the union representative denied promising Waterworks exemption from the CBA, while Waterworks’ president asserted that contributions for specified employees would not bind the company further. Waterworks later submitted unsigned contribution reports and payments consistent with CBA terms. The court found genuine factual disputes over the meeting and whether Waterworks’ conduct demonstrated intent to accept the CBA. The LMRA’s prohibition on payments absent a written agreement did not resolve those factual issues. Both summary judgment motions were denied.

The disclosure describes apparatus and methods for assessing tissue viability and burn depth by measuring electrical characteristics, particularly capacitance, and converting them into sub-epidermal moisture (SEM) values. Because wound appearance may not reliably reveal damage, SEM measurements can distinguish low-moisture necrotic tissue from surrounding edema and more viable tissue.

Electrode arrays placed over wounds can form physical or virtual capacitive sensors. Drive circuits, processors, and stored instructions analyze measurements, compare them with thresholds or data linking capacitance or SEM values to burn depths, and identify boundaries between tissue types. Flexible substrates may include LEDs, marking elements, or perforations to display or physically mark boundaries. Alternatively, a camera and projector can record measurement locations and project tissue-condition indicators onto the patient.

For third-degree burns, the described model includes a central necrotic zone with reduced moisture, a zone of stasis with decreased perfusion and elevated risk, and an outer hyperaemic zone with better perfusion and healing prospects. SEM patterns, peak values, changes from normal tissue, and repeated measurements may indicate damage depth, progression, or recovery. Measurements can also be evaluated through regional delta values, thresholds, trends, and quality metrics.

The methods may be applied to burns, cuts, ulcers, gangrene, and similar injuries. Periodic SEM assessment can monitor healing after wound closure, evaluate therapies, guide treatment adjustments, and identify incomplete recovery or recurrence risk.

The Court immediately and temporarily suspended attorney E. Nkem Odinkemere from practicing law, restrained disbursement of his New Jersey attorney-account funds without court approval, prohibited him from practicing during suspension, and ordered compliance with rules governing suspended attorneys.

The disclosure describes methods for reducing wireless transmission latency, particularly in 5G systems, by enabling a wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) to determine transmission parameters and prepare protocol data before receiving a transmission grant. Parameters such as modulation and coding scheme, transport-block size, resource range, power, timing, TTI duration, HARQ behavior, quality of service, and spectrum operating mode may be signaled, configured, or autonomously determined in advance.

A WTRU may monitor and blindly decode downlink control information (DCI), then derive data-transmission parameters from decoding characteristics such as CRC length, aggregation level, control-channel elements, DCI format, or robustness level. These characteristics may indicate reliability, latency, best-effort service, QoS, spectrum mode, or HARQ feedback timing. Network configuration may define mappings between decoding and transmission parameters.

To reduce post-grant processing, the WTRU may incrementally segment, assemble, encode, and modulate fixed-size data blocks as higher-layer data arrives. Data-block sizes may be configured, signaled, derived from physical-layer parameters, or selected according to traffic, buffering, padding, channel conditions, and service type. After receiving a grant, the WTRU may select prepared blocks, create or update headers, add padding or control information, complete physical-layer processing, and construct a transport block matching the grant.

Prepared blocks may be selected using flow or logical-channel restrictions, arrival order, priority, time-to-live, QoS, relationships between blocks, or minimization of the difference between grant and transport-block sizes. A WTRU may signal intended data-block or transport-block sizes through scheduling requests, buffer status reports, random access, control information, or CRC values.

Transport blocks may contain multiple data blocks with individual CRCs. ACK/NACK decisions may depend on the number or ratio of erroneous blocks, allowing retransmission of an entire transport block or selected blocks. Aggregated data-block status reports may provide rapid feedback across one or more transmission intervals.

The described 5G framework supports multiple waveforms, spectrum operating modes, bandwidths, TTI lengths, duplexing schemes, fragmented spectrum, network- and WTRU-based scheduling, low-latency and high-reliability services, machine-type communications, and varied radio-access and core-network architectures.

Former Army pilot and mechanical engineer Sungi Cho founded P6 Gear after developing the $10.99 Warbelt Hanger to improve military gear storage. He later launched the MOLLE Backer, a universal equipment-mounting base sold for $10.99 per two-pack, attracting military, outdoor, and trade customers.

While pursuing an MBA at MIT Sloan, Cho operated 15 printers and employed two students at $20 per hour. Backer sales stabilized at 1,800 units monthly, produced by 10 printers. Monthly Backer labor totaled 56 hours: 40 for printer operation, nine for assembly, and seven for fulfillment.

Cho considered outsourcing production through injection molding. Compared with 3D printing, injection molding offered stronger, more uniform parts, lower PETG and scrap costs, and capacity of 200 units per hour. However, the manufacturer charged $0.75 per unit, excluding insert assembly, and required at least eight production hours. Injection molding also required an $11,487 steel mold, while each printer cost $1,716. Shared per-unit costs included $0.48 for inserts, $0.50 for screws, and $0.11 for packaging. Cho needed to evaluate the financial and non-financial implications of switching production methods.

NVIDIA’s fiscal 2022 Form 10-K covers the year ended January 30, 2022. The company, headquartered in Santa Clara, develops accelerated computing platforms combining GPUs, networking, systems, software and services. It reports Graphics and Compute & Networking segments and targets Gaming, Data Center, Professional Visualization and Automotive markets.

NVIDIA’s technologies support computer graphics, AI, high-performance computing, autonomous vehicles, robotics, simulation and virtual worlds. Its offerings include GeForce, NVIDIA RTX, CUDA, DGX, BlueField, Omniverse and DRIVE platforms. The company uses a fabless manufacturing model relying on external foundries, component suppliers and contract manufacturers.

NVIDIA terminated its proposed acquisition of Arm due to significant regulatory challenges and expected a $1.36 billion fiscal 2023 first-quarter charge for the signing prepayment. Fiscal 2022 demand exceeded supply in several areas, disrupting historical seasonal patterns.

The company had 22,473 employees in 32 countries, including 16,242 in research and development. Its environmental goal is to match all global office and data-center electricity use with renewable energy by fiscal 2025.

As of March 11, 2022, 2.51 billion common shares were outstanding. Non-affiliate voting stock had an estimated market value of $467.25 billion on July 30, 2021.

Major risks include rapidly changing markets, intense competition, inaccurate demand forecasting, semiconductor supply constraints, dependence on third-party manufacturing, product defects, international operations, climate change, unsuccessful investments or acquisitions, regulatory requirements, cryptocurrency-related demand volatility and cybersecurity incidents. In February 2022, criminal actors accessed NVIDIA’s network, obtained proprietary information and leaked some source code; NVIDIA responded with security, investigative and law-enforcement measures.

EEM options can provide exposure to rising and falling markets but involve significant risks, including market losses, time decay, volatility, liquidity constraints, leverage, and margin calls. Common strategies include calls, puts, covered positions, straddles, strangles, collars, and butterfly spreads. Traders can assess pricing, risk, and potential returns using the Black-Scholes model, option delta, technical analysis, fees, and commissions. Risk management includes position sizing, hedging, maintaining sufficient margin, and backtesting strategies. Broker costs, deposits, margin requirements, liquidity, spreads, expiration dates, and taxes vary. Traders should choose a reputable broker, understand option pricing and chains, and avoid leverage when inexperienced.

Eastern New England is forecast to receive more snow, with Maine, New Hampshire and Vermont expecting nearly a foot or more in mountains. Connecticut will likely receive only a dusting as two systems phase offshore too late.

Unknown artist or album labels usually indicate missing ID3 or WMA metadata, which can be entered through the song’s computer properties. The Sansa Fuze supports microSD and microSDHC cards and can be reset by holding the power button up for about 10 seconds.

SanDisk provides technical support by phone, online request, email, and its website, which also offers videos and firmware updates. The product has a one-year limited, nontransferable warranty for the original purchaser, subject to proof of purchase and exclusions for misuse, unauthorized changes, accidents, third-party products, and software. SanDisk may repair, replace, or refund covered products but disclaims responsibility for lost data and limits liability to the purchase amount where permitted.

The software license permits personal executable use with a SanDisk product on one device at a time. Modification, reverse engineering, source-code discovery, redistribution, and separation into components are restricted. Software is provided without warranties, and users assume performance and repair risks. The license may transfer only with the integrated SanDisk product and agreement. Breach permits immediate termination. The software is unsuitable for high-risk activities, and the agreement is governed by California and applicable U.S. federal law.

South Korea restored 46 public services after a suspected battery explosion caused a fire at a Daejeon government data centre, disrupting hundreds of platforms. Of 647 affected systems, 551 are being restarted, though passport, welfare and administrative services remain impaired. President Lee Jae Myung called for stronger safeguards, backup systems and disaster preparedness to address vulnerabilities in the country’s digital infrastructure.
Amazon.com disclosed that Rosalind G. Brewer resigned from its Board of Directors, effective February 16, 2021. She informed the company on January 26, 2021.

The ANC Free State provincial congress remained delayed amid legal disputes. A court ordered 29 branch meetings to be rerun; 28 were completed and one was underway. The congress will elect leaders, with Ace Magashule expected to seek re-election, while challenger Thabo Manyoni was not expected to attend.

MetSoc of CIM announced its 2018 awards recognizing achievements in metallurgy and related fields. Recipients include Sam Marcuson, Priti Wanjara, Jun Song, Xinjin Cao, Georgios Kolliopoulos and Shauna Litke. The Innovation Award went to the Canadian-developed Acousto Ultrasonic-Echo testing technique by Dr. Afshin Sadri and Hatch’s NDT team. Awards will be presented October 15, 2018, at COM 2018 in Columbus, Ohio.

Antipsychotics improve psychiatric outcomes but commonly cause metabolic syndrome, including weight gain, glucose dysregulation and dyslipidaemia, increasing cardiovascular disease, diabetes and premature mortality risks. Non-modifiable risk factors include age, gender, ethnicity and family history, while modifiable factors include diet, physical activity and related behaviours. Existing non-pharmacological interventions show limited clinical efficacy, uncertain sustainability and barriers to patient engagement; their optimal timing and healthcare setting remain unclear.

This scoping review will map evidence on determinants of antipsychotic-induced metabolic syndrome among community-dwelling adults, interventions used to prevent or treat it, and preferred delivery contexts. Following Joanna Briggs Institute and PRISMA-ScR guidance, researchers will search multiple databases and grey literature for qualitative, quantitative, mixed-method and evidence-synthesis studies. Two reviewers will independently screen initial records; full texts and extracted data will receive sample checks. Findings will be narratively synthesised, with research types categorised by evidence level rather than formally appraised for quality. Patients, carers and other stakeholders will contribute through consultation. The review will identify knowledge gaps, inform future behavioural-intervention research, and be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and conferences.

This retrospective study evaluated whether diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps could predict TERT promoter mutation status in glioblastoma using a 50-layer residual convolutional neural network. The cohort included 266 adults with primary glioblastoma, including 147 with DWI data; 142 patients had TERT mutations and 124 were wild-type.

Conventional structural MRI performed poorly, with accuracies near 50–52% and AUCs of 0.527–0.571. ADC maps achieved 78.63% accuracy and an AUC of 0.865, while combined DWI and ADC data achieved the best slice-based performance at 85.20% accuracy and an AUC of 0.934. Patient-based accuracy was 86.6% in the 30-patient test group. Using the entire tumor as the region of interest outperformed tumor-core and enhanced-tumor regions.

Age, necrosis volume, and tumor location were associated with mutation status, but an SVM using these characteristics achieved only 70.91% accuracy and did not improve the DWI/ADC model. The authors conclude that combined DWI and ADC imaging may support noninvasive preoperative prediction of TERT promoter mutations. Limitations include the small sample, retrospective design, reliance mainly on cross-sectional slices, and restriction to WHO grade IV glioblastoma.

The Colorado Court of Appeals affirmed summary judgment for Shelter Mutual Insurance Company. Breit, injured in an automobile accident with damages exceeding $200,000, received the third party’s $100,000 policy limit and sought another $100,000 by stacking underinsured motorist coverage from two Shelter policies.

The court held that Shelter’s policy provisions unambiguously limited total liability under multiple policies issued by Shelter to the highest limit of any single policy. The general “Other Insurance” clause did not conflict with this anti-stacking provision because it addressed allocation among different insurers, while the anti-stacking clause governed multiple policies issued by the same insurer. The court distinguished Compton v. State Farm and followed Thompson v. Shelter Mutual Insurance Co.

The reasonable expectations doctrine did not apply because the policy language was neither ambiguous nor conflicting, and an expectation that stacking was permitted would not be reasonable. The court also declined Shelter’s request for appellate attorney fees, finding the appeal was not frivolous.

Iranian President Hassan Rouhani warned that Iran could abandon the 2015 nuclear deal within hours if Washington continued imposing sanctions. He accused President Donald Trump and the United States of repeatedly breaking promises and being unreliable partners, amid mutual allegations that missile activity and sanctions violated the agreement’s spirit.

The ADS868xW family comprises 16-bit SAR ADCs with integrated analog front ends, programmable gain, ADC drivers, precision references, alarms, and multiSPI interfaces. Programmable high and low input alarms use independent thresholds and common hysteresis; fixed AVDD alarms trigger above approximately 5.3 V or below 4.7 V.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI, dual-SDO, source-synchronous transfer, and multi-device daisy chains. Communication uses 32-bit input/output shift registers. In a daisy chain, devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, pass data serially between devices, and optimally use 32 × N clock edges for N devices.

Three operating states are supported: RESET, acquisition (ACQ), and conversion (CONV). The active-low RST pin can perform an application reset or power-on reset. The device acquires inputs in ACQ, begins conversion on a CONVST/CS rising edge, ignores further transitions during conversion, and returns to ACQ when finished.

Data-transfer frames begin when CONVST/CS falls and end when it rises. A 32-clock frame accepts a valid 32-bit command; shorter frames cannot write but can read selected most-significant output bits. In longer frames, the final 32 input bits form the command. Commands support byte and half-word reads and writes, plus bit-set and bit-clear operations. Read results appear in the following frame. Output can contain conversion or register data, fixed test patterns, device address, input range, AVDD and input alarm flags, parity, and zero padding.

Four SPI modes are selectable. Read operations can use single or dual SDO lines or source-synchronous protocols with internal or external output clocks. Dual-SDO operation outputs two bits per clock and reduces the required number of clock cycles.

Nine configuration registers control device identification, reset and power, input and output protocols, output formatting, input range and reference, alarm status, and alarm thresholds. Writes to protected reset and power-control fields require a 69h key.

An example industrial design combines the ADS8681W with an eight-channel differential multiplexer for programmable voltage, current, or temperature inputs. The ADC supports signals up to ±12.288 V, bandwidth up to 400 kHz, settling below 5 µs to 1% accuracy, and safety monitoring. Programmable alarm hysteresis can reduce false triggering in thermistor-based temperature monitoring.

Separate AVDD and DVDD supplies require local decoupling. NAP and deep power-down modes reduce consumption at low throughput; power-down retains registers and keeps the interface active. PCB guidance recommends separating analog and digital routing, short low-impedance grounding, and close placement of specified AVDD, DVDD, REFCAP, and REFIO capacitors.

The Trump administration shifted day-to-day management of career and technical education programs from the Education Department to the Labor Department while retaining Education’s oversight authority. Responsibilities include distributing more than $1 billion in Perkins funding, monitoring compliance, and assisting states and schools.

Administration officials and supporters say the change could better align education with employer needs, reduce bureaucracy, improve accountability, and connect more young people to jobs. Alabama workforce officials cite their state’s efforts to coordinate education, apprenticeships, and regionally valuable credentials as a potential model.

Critics, including congressional Democrats and CTE advocates, question the transfer’s legality and warn that staffing shortages could disrupt federal guidance, particularly for serving students with disabilities and ensuring equitable access. They also fear the Labor Department’s emphasis on employment and short-term credentials could steer students toward low-paying jobs with limited advancement rather than using CTE as a path to further education and lifelong opportunity. Supporters counter that the Labor Department has relevant apprenticeship experience and could better evaluate whether programs improve employment outcomes and meet workforce needs.

This withdrawn, non-peer-reviewed study compared six machine-learning models for pancreatic cancer diagnosis using a synthetic dataset of demographic factors, clinical risks, and symptoms. Test accuracy was similar across models at 76.05%–76.35%, but sensitivity was extremely low. SVM had the highest sensitivity at 1.90%; Random Forest and Decision Tree detected no positive cases. SuperLearner achieved the highest precision at 66.67% but only 0.42% sensitivity. The study attributes these results largely to class imbalance and recommends resampling, cost-sensitive learning, threshold tuning, feature engineering, explainability tools, multimodal data, and validation with real-world clinical datasets.

British Columbia’s Ministry of Education will fund a $28.5-million replacement for Walnut Park Elementary in Smithers. The existing school is over 50 years old, sits on unstable land and would cost more to upgrade than replace. The new two-storey, LEED Gold building will support modern collaborative and project-based learning, accommodate 440 students and include StrongStart and neighbourhood learning centre spaces. It will be built beside the current school, which will be demolished after students relocate. Construction is expected to begin next spring, with opening targeted for the 2020-21 school year. The Province will provide up to $27.6 million, while School District 54 will contribute $900,000.

Cervical cancer disproportionately affects low- and middle-income countries, where access to precancer treatment is limited. Self-administered intravaginal 5-fluorouracil (5FU) may offer an accessible alternative or adjunct to provider-administered ablation and excision.

A Phase I pilot trial in Kisumu, Kenya, enrolled 12 women living with HIV who had received treatment for high-grade cervical precancer. Participants self-administered two grams of intravaginal 5FU every other week for eight doses. Acceptability was assessed through questionnaires and in-depth interviews. All participants completed treatment, with adherence supported for 96% of doses; adverse events were primarily mild, with no grade III or IV events.

Although some women initially reported anxiety, fear, difficulty measuring doses, limited anatomical knowledge, or challenges using applicators and tampons, education and repeated clinic support increased confidence. Side effects included vaginal discharge, itching, burning, and discomfort during urination. Condom requirements, partner negotiation, abstinence, tampon costs, and limited privacy in crowded homes were additional concerns.

All participants ultimately considered 5FU safe, were confident they had used it correctly, and preferred it over their prior ablation or excision procedures. They valued reduced pain and fear, convenience, privacy, minimal disruption of daily activities, and the ability to administer treatment at home at night. The study found high acceptability but was limited by its small, single-site sample. Larger randomized studies are needed to assess efficacy and implementation in varied settings.

The Indiana Supreme Court held that David Shaner's wrongful-death claim for survivor damages following his wife Laura's death did not abate when he died intestate without heirs. Indiana’s wrongful-death and survival statutes preserve a properly accrued claim regardless of whether an heir exists, and Bemenderfer v. Williams does not impose an heir requirement. The Court reversed partial summary judgment for the defendants but remanded for the trial court to determine whether a legal representative or successor to David, rather than Laura’s estate, is the proper party to continue the claim.

CompareCards highlights credit cards offering 0% introductory APR periods of 6–21 months, cash back or travel rewards, and sign-up bonuses. Featured issuers include Discover, Bank of America, Citi, Capital One, and Wells Fargo, with varying post-promotional APRs, transfer fees, reward rates, and annual fees. The site says it uses data-driven ratings, although it receives compensation from listed companies, and advises applicants to verify current terms before applying.

Pupils aged eight to 10 from Richardson Dees Primary School have transformed an unused rooftop at The Forum shopping centre into a garden with flowers, fruit, vegetables and herbs. The produce will be shared with pupils and families. The project promotes gardening skills, healthy eating, responsibility, confidence and decision-making while strengthening the centre’s partnership with the school.

The configurable active-high ALARM output supports input-voltage and AVDD monitoring. Input thresholds are user-programmable; AVDD thresholds are 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Both alarms default to enabled but can be independently disabled. Active and tripped flags are updated after each conversion; active flags clear after conversion, while tripped flags clear when ALARM_REG is read. Alarm status is available through the pin, ALARM_REG, or appended output data.

The S&P 500 gained 2.2% in July and 7.8% year to date, maintaining a healthy longer-term uptrend despite an early-August decline. Seasonal increases in volatility and credit spreads, weakening short-term technical indicators, and growing technology concentration signal potential risks. Frontier markets led July returns, while stocks rose and bonds fell overall. U.S. electricity demand reached a record high. Investing.com warns that trading carries substantial risk and its market data may be delayed or inaccurate.

Tyreek Hill returned to the Dolphins’ facility three days after season-ending surgery on his dislocated left knee, encouraging teammates during a meeting. Miami plans to replace his production collectively, with Jaylen Waddle leading the receiving group and other players receiving expanded roles. Coach Mike McDaniel expressed confidence that the team can respond to Hill’s absence through group execution.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un is portrayed as seeking sanctions relief, economic development and international legitimacy while remaining unwilling to abandon nuclear weapons until his regime’s security is assured. His meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping and South Korean President Moon Jae-in have demonstrated diplomatic skill and helped repair ties and advance peace discussions. However, references by US officials to Libya’s denuclearisation heightened Kim’s concerns about regime change, contributing to uncertainty over his planned summit with US President Donald Trump. Although Kim has expressed openness to “complete denuclearisation,” its meaning and conditions remain unclear.

Apple’s board appointed Alex Gorsky as a director on November 9, 2021, increasing the board from eight to nine members. Gorsky will serve on the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, receive a $100,000 annual retainer, and was granted 486 restricted stock units. Apple amended its bylaws accordingly.

A Russell 2000 Death Cross occurs when its 50-day moving average falls below its 200-day moving average and is commonly considered bearish. Rob Hanna’s study identified 25 such events since 1988; the S&P 500 rose during the following year in 21 cases, or 84%, including a gain exceeding 60% in 2020. However, sizable drawdowns occurred even in winning cases. The most recent Death Cross was in 2022, after which the S&P 500 fell. Hanna concluded that the signal is imperfect but potentially useful for monitoring downturn risk. Because the Russell 2000 tracks more volatile small-cap stocks, the signal may be less reliable for the S&P 500.

John Mellencamp performed “Easy Target,” a song about racial inequality, on “The Late Show” and then knelt with a raised fist in support of Black Lives Matter. He said kneeling protests social injustice but was politicized by the Trump administration.

Rick Langenberg previews Super Bowl 52 between the New England Patriots and Philadelphia Eagles after Denver’s disappointing season. Local contributors largely predict another Patriots championship, citing Tom Brady, Bill Belichick, experience, and consistency. Others favor Philadelphia’s offense, defense, and Nick Foles to produce an upset. Predicted scores range from decisive New England victories to close Eagles wins, while readers are encouraged to watch at local bars, casinos, lounges, and eateries.

The Ichimoku trading strategy uses five components—Tenkan-Sen, Kijun-Sen, Senkou Span A, Senkou Span B, and Chikou Span—to identify support and resistance, trend direction, momentum, and potential entry or exit points. Senkou spans form a cloud: price above it indicates an uptrend, while price below indicates a downtrend. Cloud thickness may reflect volatility. Tenkan-Sen and Kijun-Sen crossovers provide bullish or bearish signals, while the Chikou Span can confirm or precede trend breakouts.

Traders may use individual signals or combine them, such as requiring both a crossover and cloud breakout. The indicator can be applied across timeframes and assets, but strategies should be backtested and forward-tested.

The presented backtests found that the strategy reduced time in the market and avoided much of the drawdowns, including a drawdown for MDY of less than half that of buy-and-hold. However, it generally underperformed risk-adjusted buy-and-hold returns. Its principal risk is that signals may be inaccurate or unreliable.

The S&P MidCap 400, ticker MID, is a market-cap-weighted index tracking 400 mid-sized U.S. companies, generally with market capitalizations of $3.6–$13.1 billion. It was formed in 1991 and rebalanced quarterly. Its reported historical low was 119.43 in June 1991 and high was 2925.93 in November 2021. The index tends to perform better in winter and spring than in summer and fall.

E-mini S&P MidCap 400 futures, ticker EMD, trade on CME Globex and allow hedging or speculation on the index. Each contract equals $100 times the index value, is financially settled, and has a minimum fluctuation of 0.1 index point, or $10, for outright Globex trading. Quarterly contracts are listed for March, June, September, and December, with trading generally ending at 9:30 a.m. ET on the third Friday of the contract month. Settlement uses cash based on the index’s special opening quotation. The BTIC block minimum is 50 contracts.

Trading runs Sunday through Friday from 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET, with a daily maintenance break. Futures require a broker with CME access and are leveraged, making adverse price movements a major risk. CFDs offer an alternative without fixed expiry dates but generally track the index rather than futures.

Prices are affected by component stocks, interest rates, economic news, and the U.S. dollar. ETFs tracking the index include IJH and SPMD, while EWMC tracks an equal-weighted version. Backtests found one volatility strategy performed poorly and an overnight strategy produced decent results, though both performed better on SPY or QQQ.

Following the Great Recession, U.S. casual dining remained pressured by reduced consumer spending, though investors anticipated renewed demand by 2016. The restaurant industry was projected to generate nearly $800 billion in sales, equal 4% of GDP, and employ almost 10% of Americans.

Bloomin’ Brands began with Outback Steakhouse in 1988 and went public in 2012. By June 2016, it owned 1,335 and franchised 166 restaurants across Outback, Fleming’s, Bonefish Grill, and Carrabba’s. About 85% were in the United States, and nearly two-thirds operated under Outback.

The passage compares Bloomin’ with 13 publicly traded restaurant companies spanning casual dining, fast casual, and fast food. As of August 15, 2016, Bloomin’ had a $2.2 billion market capitalization, a trailing P/E of 40.2, a forward P/E of 12.6, and forecast long-term EPS growth of 12.1%. For the trailing period, it reported $4.319 billion in revenue, $171 million in operating income, $60 million in net income, and EPS of $0.48. At June 30, 2016, it had $2.784 billion in assets, $2.451 billion in liabilities, and $333 million in shareholders’ equity.

Microsoft reported fiscal 2023 first-quarter revenue of $50.1 billion, up 11%, and operating income of $21.5 billion, up 6%. Net income fell 14% to $17.6 billion, reflecting a prior-year $3.3 billion tax benefit; diluted EPS was $2.35. Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 24% to $25.7 billion. Intelligent Cloud revenue increased 20%, Productivity and Business Processes 9%, while More Personal Computing was nearly unchanged. Azure and other cloud services grew 35%, while Windows OEM revenue declined 15%.

Operating cash flow was $23.2 billion. At September 30, 2022, Microsoft held $107.3 billion in cash, equivalents, and short-term investments, with total assets of $359.8 billion and stockholders’ equity of $173.6 billion. Extending server and network equipment useful lives from four to six years increased quarterly operating income by $1.1 billion and net income by $859 million.

Microsoft completed its $18.8 billion Nuance acquisition in March 2022 and expected its proposed $68.7 billion Activision Blizzard acquisition to close in fiscal 2023, subject to approvals.

Enron appointed experienced trader James Fallon to lead Enron Broadband Services as Kenneth Rice moved to a corporate role. The broadband unit, which lost $102 million in the second quarter, was being restructured, folded into Wholesale Services, and reducing staff amid falling bandwidth prices. Enron maintained that bandwidth trading had long-term potential despite weak market liquidity.

EnronOnline CEO Greg Piper predicted continued volume growth from its $3.5 billion in daily trades. The platform planned expansion in products including metals, steel, weather, petrochemicals, and plastics, while retaining its model in which customers trade directly with Enron.

Rep. Henry Waxman urged the White House to seek a Justice Department review of senior adviser Karl Rove’s contacts with Enron, Intel, and General Electric while he owned their stock. The White House said Rove followed ethical guidelines. Officials also opposed releasing details about his stock acquisitions and tax-deferred divestiture.

Mississippi regulators approved Calpine’s proposed $450 million Lowndes County power plant, though environmental permits remained pending amid concerns about water and gas supplies. Enron already operated a plant nearby.

Texans contributed nearly $500,000 through Chase branches to Red Cross relief efforts following Tropical Storm Allison, supplementing major corporate donations, including from Enron.

In India, Maharashtra’s planned judicial inquiry into the Dabhol power project faced difficulties because the Supreme Court had previously opposed reopening the project’s validity. Critics cited delays and favored arbitration. The state also faced potential embarrassment from its 1997 defense of Dabhol Phase II and efforts to demonstrate that its electricity board could absorb the project’s power. Maharashtra separately cleared a Rs 350 crore overdraft after receiving Rs 750 crore from the central government.

A University of Liverpool study of 38 healthy adults found that higher musical aptitude correlated with lower hallucination proneness and greater corpus callosum integrity. Statistical analysis suggested this brain microstructure mediated the relationship, indicating musical training could potentially help counter hallucination predisposition, though further research in psychosis patients is needed.

South Sudan nonprofit GAIS urged the government to restrict imported seeds after FAO allegedly imported 100 metric tons into Gbudue despite GAIS bidding to supply locally produced maize seeds. FAO said it supports local growers through transparent procurement and seed fairs, has previously assisted GAIS, and invited registered local suppliers to bid this year. It said the government waived import restrictions for 2018 because conflict, displacement and low production had reduced domestic seed supplies. FAO plans to distribute 5,000 metric tons of seed nationwide this year, up from 2,000 metric tons last year.

The Rhode Island Supreme Court affirmed Andrew A. Bucci’s conviction for furnishing legal advice while suspended from practicing law. Bucci had advised Robert Oliva about pending criminal charges through recorded meetings and telephone conversations, discussing grand jury procedure, searches, litigation strategy, restitution, and representation by another attorney. The court found ample evidence that Bucci provided information intended to guide Oliva’s actions and continued managing the litigation despite arranging for another attorney to appear in court.

The court rejected Bucci’s argument that the state had to prove he received a pecuniary benefit, holding that G.L. 1956 § 11-27-10 contains no such requirement. It also held that a Superior Court may impose a greater sentence following a trial de novo in Rhode Island’s two-tier court system. Bucci’s challenge to the six-month sentence could not be considered on direct appeal because he had not first sought relief in Superior Court under Rule 35. His appeal was denied, the conviction affirmed, and the case returned to Superior Court.

Assam AHSEC’s 2018 Class 12 results were scheduled for release on May 31 at 9:30 am. Students could check results at ahsec.nic.in, resultsassam.nic.in, examresults.net, via designated SMS services, or through apps after preregistration. Exams ran from February 23 to March 22. Candidates needed at least 20 marks in each subject to pass, while scores of 70 percent or higher earned distinction. About 2.5 lakh candidates appeared the previous year across Arts, Science and Commerce.

The lecture contrasts poker tournaments with cash games. Tournaments have fixed buy-ins, rising blinds, elimination, fixed losses, higher variance, limited table choice, and a survival-oriented strategy. Cash games allow players to join, leave, or rebuy at fixed stakes and often emphasize table selection and targeting weaker players. Tournaments offer broader stack-size situations, are easier to analyze with less metagame, and generally cost less in casino fees. Despite these differences, skill largely transfers between formats.

Preflop hand equities fall into rough categories. A higher pair against a lower pair is about an 80/20 favorite; a pair against one overcard or a dominating hand is around 70/30; two overcards against a pair can approach 50/50; and with four different cards, the hand containing the highest card is often near 60/40. Suitedness improves weaker hands more than strong hands because it creates additional ways to catch up.

Tournament players should not be overly reluctant to move all-in preflop. With antes, stacks below roughly 12 big blinds should generally be played by shoving or folding; without antes, the threshold is closer to 10. Small-blind shoving ranges can be wider because only one opponent remains and postflop positional disadvantage disappears. In an example with 15 big blinds, equilibrium play has the small blind shoving about 66.8% of hands and the big blind calling about 38.5%. Players may deviate exploitatively: shove more when opponents call too little and tighten when they call too much.

All-in ranges widen with later position and shorter stacks, though position often matters more than stack size. Suited connectors depend more on fold equity and stack size, while unsuited high-card hands depend more on having fewer players left to act. Small pairs and weak aces can be suitable shoves because they are difficult to play postflop at shallow depths. However, a very short player in the blinds reduces the value of stealing because that player is likely to call.

Players should also call all-ins when pot odds justify it. Preflop hands often retain at least 30% equity, and after raising with an effective stack of 12 big blinds or less, folding to a shove is often a larger mistake than calling. With only four big blinds after posting the blind, nearly any two cards may be playable.

For reraises, a default size is about 2.5 times the original raise, with larger sizing out of position. If a reraise would commit more than roughly a quarter of the stack, moving all-in is generally preferable. Calling an existing raise can be reasonable when deep because reraising gives the original raiser an opportunity to shove. Against limpers, add approximately one big blind to the normal raise size for each limper.

The lecture emphasizes that routine preflop decisions, correct all-in ranges, stack awareness, pot odds, and simple probability calculations are more important to tournament profitability than occasional elaborate bluffs.

The 60/40 portfolio allocates 60% to equities and 40% to bonds, aiming to balance growth and risk through their typically low or negative correlation. It can be built with broad stock and bond ETFs or purchased as a managed fund, with international assets providing additional diversification.

Vanguard reports an average annual return of 8.8% since 1926. However, rising inflation in 2022 caused both stocks and bonds to fall, producing a 17.77% year-to-date loss by September 17. Historically, such declines have been infrequent and often followed by recoveries. Since January 2010, the maximum drawdown was 21.85% in March 2020, with recovery occurring within 79 trading sessions.

The passage argues that the strategy remains viable despite lower expected returns and near-term challenges. Market timing is considered ineffective, while patience and continued diversification are emphasized. Alternatives include an 80/20 stock-bond allocation, the All-Weather Portfolio, trend-following strategies, gold, small cryptocurrency allocations, international equities, tail-risk strategies, and Thomas Carlson’s “Defense First” approach. Trend-following is highlighted as a potentially useful hedge because its return pattern differs from stocks and bonds.

Asian shares edged higher for a fourth session as optimism over global growth and strong Chinese credit data outweighed expectations of a U.S. rate hike. Wall Street also gained, led by technology and energy stocks. Investors awaited Federal Reserve and European Central Bank meetings, with the Fed potentially raising growth and rate projections while the ECB maintains a low-rate stance. Despite widening U.S.-German yield spreads, the dollar remained weaker this year. Bitcoin hit record highs, gold stayed subdued, and Brent crude rose following a temporary North Sea pipeline shutdown.

The lecture examines supply-side modeling, the BLP random-coefficients demand model, Nevo’s cereal-market study, and the common ownership hypothesis.

In static competition models, firms may own multiple products and maximize total portfolio profits. Combining an ownership matrix with demand-derived price derivatives produces first-order conditions that can be inverted to recover marginal costs from estimated demand, observed prices, and an assumed conduct model. Flexible marginal costs can rationalize any conduct assumption, limiting testability. Parametric cost functions and supply-side moment conditions can instead restrict demand estimates, improve precision, and permit tests of competing conduct models. Joint demand-and-supply estimation is efficient when the conduct assumption is credible.

BLP applies a random-coefficients model to U.S. automobile data from 1971–1990. Instrumental variables produce more negative price coefficients than OLS because unobserved quality is associated with higher prices. Supply-side restrictions help identify heterogeneous preferences. The model finds significant variation in tastes and generates more plausible substitution patterns than simple logit: consumers substitute mainly among similarly positioned cars, low-end buyers respond more strongly to a fixed price increase, and buyers of expensive cars are less likely to choose the outside option. Limitations include ignoring durable-good dynamics, used-car market responses, dealerships, negotiated transaction prices, and financing or insurance.

Nevo studies why ready-to-eat cereals have high observed margins. The concentrated industry contains many products owned by a few firms, making multiproduct pricing and cannibalization important. His demand model includes product fixed effects, consumer demographics, and random coefficients. Because fixed effects absorb much product-characteristic variation, he uses prices in other markets and regional cost variables as instruments, though these may be invalid if correlated demand shocks exist. Demographic interactions explain much preference heterogeneity.

Nevo compares observed accounting markups with markups implied by alternative conduct assumptions. His preferred random-coefficients specification rejects full collusion among the included brands but cannot reject either brand-level competition or profit maximization under actual ownership. A simple logit model yields lower markups and different conclusions, demonstrating the importance of realistic substitution patterns. The analysis depends on accounting costs being an appropriate benchmark and does not model advertising or product characteristics as strategic choices.

The common ownership hypothesis argues that diversified institutional investors holding shares in competing firms may encourage firms to internalize rivals’ profits and soften competition. Institutional ownership and implied cross-firm profit weights have increased over time, including among major cereal producers. Backus, Conlon, and Sinkinson test this hypothesis by combining cereal demand estimates, alternative conduct assumptions, flexible marginal-cost functions, and supply-side overidentifying restrictions. Their non-nested tests reject common ownership, perfect competition, and full monopoly in favor of own-profit maximization. The result is a case study rather than evidence for the entire economy, and the broader hypothesis remains disputed partly because a mechanism through which institutional investors reduce competition has not been clearly established.

This study examined whether group-based brain parcellations bias estimates of functional connectivity differences between people with early psychosis and healthy controls. Using Human Connectome Project–Early Psychosis data, researchers compared standard Schaefer cortical parcellations with individualized parcellations generated by the Group Prior Individualized Parcellation algorithm. The final sample included 112 patients and 55 controls.

Individualization reassigned over 40% of cortical vertices and produced slightly more functionally homogeneous regions. Both methods identified widespread lower functional connectivity in patients, but group-based parcellations yielded larger case-control differences and approximately 9% more dysconnected edges. The methods differed on 643 identified edges and produced notable regional differences, including in medial frontal and insular areas. However, conclusions at the level of seven canonical functional networks were largely consistent across methods. Parcel-size changes did not significantly differ between patients and controls.

The findings indicate that group-based parcellations may inflate functional connectivity differences by failing to account for individual variation in brain organization. Individualized parcellations produced more conservative and refined estimates of dysconnectivity, particularly at edge and regional levels, while broad network-level findings remained robust. Limitations included use of a relatively low-resolution cortical surface, medication exposure among some patients, and clinical heterogeneity within the psychosis group.

Japanese mobile game Travel Frog has become popular in Taiwan, with players caring for an independently traveling pet. Psychologists attribute its appeal to desires for companionship, altruistic connection, relaxation and a simpler life. Despite being available only in Japanese, the game prompted a 70-fold increase in related online searches and a 60 percent rise in domestic sales of frog-themed products.

Coach Quenneville described the playoffs as demanding and unpredictable, praising players’ preparation, conditioning, competitiveness, and mutual support. He discussed uncertain player availability, confidence that top players will eventually score, defensemen’s heavy ice time, and line changes intended to improve balance and production. He emphasized disciplined penalty killing and avoiding penalties against a strong power play. Quenneville also praised his captain’s leadership in major games, said both finalists faced challenges after seven-game series, and expected improved play in the next game.

Stress and grief after a loved one’s death can harm health by weakening immunity, disrupting sleep and eating, causing symptoms to be ignored, and occasionally triggering heart attacks or broken heart syndrome. Studies indicate increased mortality after losing a longtime spouse, though apparent links may be coincidental, especially among older people with existing illnesses. Former President George H.W. Bush, 93, was hospitalized with sepsis after Barbara Bush’s funeral, but he also had Parkinson’s disease and a history of infections. Doctors said stress or delayed attention to symptoms might have contributed but could not establish a cause. Deaths such as those of Johnny Cash and Debbie Reynolds were attributed to serious pre-existing medical conditions despite public speculation about broken hearts.

Protesters disrupted Jacob Rees-Mogg’s scheduled speech at the University of the West of England in Bristol, prompting scuffles among attendees. Footage showed the Conservative MP attempting to calm and reason with opposing groups. Witnesses said five or six masked protesters entered shouting accusations including “fascist” and “racist” before security escorted them out about 10 minutes later.

Rees-Mogg said he was neither injured nor physically threatened. He defended lawful protest but criticized attempts to prevent debate, changing his planned remarks on politics and conservative principles to discuss free speech. The event later resumed normally.

UWE Bristol condemned the protesters’ conduct, saying they were believed not to be students and lacked tickets. Police were called, while security and officers remained for the speech. The university praised Rees-Mogg’s composure and said it would work with police to identify those involved.

Syrian forces seized al-Sukhna, Islamic State’s last major Homs town, while advancing toward Deir al-Zor province. Islamic State is also losing territory to the U.S.-backed SDF, which is focused on capturing Raqqa.

School shootings and other emergencies create fear, communication failures, traffic problems, and difficulties reuniting families. Although police and schools conduct lockdown drills, planning cannot cover every situation. Families should decide how children will get home, who may pick them up, and what to do if roads, phones, and electricity fail during a natural disaster. Schools should also develop broader emergency exercises, including unscheduled closures and disaster drills, because preparation can save lives.

Google added NHL and NBA playoff updates to Search and Play Newsstand, including team posts, headlines, scores, analysis and videos. MLB team content is available only in Search. Powered by Posts on Google, the English-language features are rolling out globally, with team information available in the U.S. and Canada.

The lecture reviews numerical methods as layered applications of linear algebra. Solving linear systems with Matlab backslash typically costs order \(n^3\), though forming Jacobians may dominate at order \(n^2\). Ill-conditioned matrices can produce widely varying solutions, and nonlinear root-finding, minimization, constrained optimization, and implicit ODE methods repeatedly invoke linear solves. Their performance depends strongly on iteration counts, initial guesses, time steps, and function-evaluation costs; continuation and homotopy can improve convergence.

Functionals take functions as inputs, as in root-finding, gradients, Jacobians, and density functional theory. Numerical integration is connected to interpolation and basis functions: sampled values are fitted by an approximating function that can be integrated analytically. Interpolation uses as many parameters as data points, while fewer parameters may be preferable for noisy data. Basis functions should be linearly independent or orthogonal to avoid singular systems.

Polynomials are convenient but can oscillate severely. Monomial bases often become poorly conditioned, while Lagrange and Newton polynomial bases provide computational advantages. Gaussian quadrature chooses points and weights to integrate polynomials through degree \(2n-1\) exactly, achieving higher-order accuracy than common Newton–Cotes rules. Comparing Gaussian and higher-point quadrature estimates can provide an error indication.

Multidimensional integration nests one-dimensional quadratures, causing function evaluations to grow exponentially with dimension. This “curse of dimensionality” makes high-dimensional integrals computationally prohibitive and motivates methods with better scaling.
