The FBI later confirmed it was investigating possible links between Russia and Trump associates.

Former BBC weather team leader Bill Giles criticised the corporation’s new weather graphics as unclear and less useful than the previous maps. He said the smaller, zoomed-out UK view makes local details and temperatures difficult to see, although forecast accuracy remains reliable. Giles recommended Channel 5’s clearer graphics but said its forecast is too short. The BBC defended its new design as more realistic.

The EU is preparing action against Italy over its broad use of “golden power” laws to influence banking mergers. Brussels argues the interventions restrict cross-border consolidation, distort competition and deter investment. Proposed measures could require narrower veto powers, clearer national-security justifications and greater transparency. Italy maintains the framework protects economic sovereignty and strategic assets.

Ascension Health and Providence St. Joseph Health are discussing a nonprofit merger that would create the largest U.S. hospital chain, with 191 hospitals, operations in 27 states and $44.8 billion in annual revenue. Talks remain unresolved amid broader healthcare consolidation, policy changes and rising drug prices.

iCVS is a mechanistic cardiovascular model designed to infer hidden physiological states in critically ill patients using routinely available arterial and venous pressure waveforms, plus age and weight. It combines a one-chamber heart, arterial and venous compartments, peripheral resistance, autonomic regulation, and non-autonomic vascular modulation. Five observables—mean arterial and venous pressures, heart rate, peripheral resistance, and pulse pressure—are extracted across fast and slow timescales and used to estimate 15 hidden parameters through constrained nonlinear optimization.

The model represents hypovolemic shock through intravascular volume loss, distributive shock through reduced non-autonomic vascular resistance, and cardiogenic shock through reduced contractility. Applied in five-minute segments to data from 10 pediatric intensive-care patients, iCVS identified bleeding, distributive shock, cardiac dysfunction, combined shock states, and stable controls in agreement with clinical assessments. Reconstructed observables correlated with measurements at 0.71–0.94.

The study demonstrates potential for real-time bedside decision support but requires prospective validation in larger, more diverse cohorts and defined diagnostic thresholds. Limitations include noisy clinical recordings, simplifying assumptions, and omission of factors such as positive-pressure ventilation, pericardial effusion, heart-chamber interactions, and separate pulmonary and systemic circulations. Future work may combine iCVS with machine learning to guide fluid and inotropic treatment.

China’s debt may be as high as 328% of GDP, driven by post-crisis stimulus, loose state-bank credit and shadow banking. Although its closed capital account limits conventional crisis channels, high internal debt may prolong economic burdens, capital misallocation and pressure for drastic policy intervention.

China also faces risks as a major overseas creditor. Loans to Venezuela, Argentina, Pakistan and Belt and Road infrastructure projects in Kenya, Laos and Sri Lanka may prove difficult to repay and can generate political resentment or demands for write-offs. The passage compares this lending surge with the 1970s buildup preceding Latin America’s 1980s debt crisis: abundant capital financed questionable projects and ultimately created unserviceable debt. If Chinese-funded projects fail to generate adequate returns and political changes interrupt repayment, China could be left holding extensive unenforceable debt.

The ADS9803 uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies without a required power-up sequence; VDD_1V8 and IOVDD may share a 1.8V supply. Each supply pin should have a nearby 0.1μF ceramic bypass capacitor without intervening vias. Reference capacitors should be close to REFIO and REFM, with short ground-plane connections. Board layouts should separate analog and reference paths from digital lines and noise sources.

TI provides development tools, documentation-update notifications, and TI E2E support forums. The device requires appropriate ESD precautions. Mechanical, packaging, orderability, material, RoHS, reflow, and marking information may change. Preproduction parts are experimental and sold without warranties. TI resources are provided “as is” for skilled developers, who remain responsible for product selection, design validation, testing, compliance, and resulting liabilities.

India’s mobile customer base rose 0.51%, or 6 million, to 1.19 billion in June. Reliance Jio gained the most subscribers, adding 6 million. Wireless tele-density was 92.12, broadband connections reached 300.84 million, and fixed-line subscribers fell to 24 million.

Dietitians recommend balancing enjoyment of Diwali foods with realistic planning, portion control and healthier ingredient choices. Use smaller plates, eat mindfully, and favour high-fibre foods, vegetables, wholegrains, lentils, chickpeas and lean grilled proteins. Replace ghee, butter and coconut oil with small amounts of unsaturated oils; choose tofu over paneer; reduce salt; and bake foods instead of frying them.

Limit mithai and refined sugar. Homemade desserts allow healthier substitutions such as fruit, dates, dried fruit, low-fat milk and whole wheat flour. People with diabetes should combine simple carbohydrates with protein, healthy fats and fibre, monitor blood sugar more frequently, and watch for symptoms of high levels.

Limit sugary, high-calorie and alcoholic drinks, particularly sweet cocktails and mixers. Drink water, stay physically active, and avoid skipping meals, which can encourage overeating and disrupt blood sugar management. Family support, including alternative gifts and cooking healthier dishes together, can make these changes easier.

The speaker defends the Payne tariff as a substantial, though incomplete, downward revision consistent with Republican protectionism: rates should cover differences between domestic and foreign production costs while allowing reasonable profits, but should not be so excessive as to encourage monopoly. Of 2,024 dutiable items under the Dingley law, 654 were reduced, 220 increased, and 1,150 unchanged. Reduced duties applied to roughly $5 billion in consumption, largely necessities, while increases applied to about $879 million, much of it luxuries.

The speaker acknowledges that the unchanged wool schedule violated the platform’s principle and notes disputed treatment of cotton, crockery, paper, lumber, and other products. Nevertheless, he considers the bill the best Republican tariff enacted, citing major reductions in metals, hides, leather goods, coal, lumber, oil products, and other necessities. He rejects claims that recent increases in living costs were primarily caused by tariffs.

He signed the bill because defeating it would have prolonged economic uncertainty, disrupted party unity, and endangered other legislation. The law also created tools against discriminatory foreign tariffs, imposed a 1 percent corporate excise tax above a $5,000 exemption, established limited free trade with the Philippines, and funded tariff administration. A newly appointed tariff board will gather impartial data on production costs and tariff effects before any future revision, which he argues should wait until the law has operated for several years.

At a Super Bowl news conference, halftime performer Justin Timberlake initially said his 3-year-old son would never play football, then clarified he would support him in sports or the arts while prioritizing his character. The comment came amid concerns about football-related brain injuries. Timberlake also said he has made peace with Janet Jackson over their controversial 2004 halftime performance.

Closed-cell foams are widely used for thermal insulation because their high gas volume fraction and small cells reduce heat transfer. Foam conductivity comprises conduction through the solid and gas, convection within cells, and radiation. Gas conduction usually dominates; low-conductivity blowing gases improve insulation but gradually diffuse out as air enters, increasing conductivity. Convection is negligible for typical foams because it becomes important only at cell sizes around 20 millimeters or larger. Radiation increases as relative density decreases and as cell size grows, while solid conduction increases with density, producing a minimum overall conductivity at an intermediate density.

Steady-state conduction follows Fourier’s law, while transient conduction depends on thermal diffusivity, defined as thermal conductivity divided by density and specific heat. Aerogels have lower conductivity than closed-cell foams because their pores can be comparable to or smaller than air’s mean free path, but they are extremely weak and brittle.

A foam’s specific heat and thermal expansion coefficient equal those of its solid material. Foams resist thermal shock better than solids because their much lower elastic modulus reduces stresses caused by sudden surface-temperature changes. Modeling open-cell foams indicates that their critical temperature change before cracking or spalling exceeds that of the parent solid by a factor related inversely to the square root of relative density.

PDP-Laban secretary-general Pantaleon Alvarez said presidential aide Bong Go and several lawmakers and officials were being considered for the party’s 2019 Senate slate. Party president Aquilino Pimentel III said Go had a slot if he chose to run. The elections were viewed as crucial to maintaining the party’s political dominance.
Amazon.com reported that Thomas O. Ryder will retire from its Board of Directors effective December 31, 2021. He notified the company of his decision on November 10, 2021.

A pragmatic, two-stage adaptive randomized trial evaluated auricular acupuncture (AA) and peripheral acupuncture (PA), each combined with usual care, against usual care alone for acute musculoskeletal pain in a U.S. academic emergency department. English-speaking adults with new acute pain or exacerbations of chronic pain lasting seven days or less were eligible. The primary outcomes were feasibility, acceptability, safety, and change in pain one hour after treatment.

From February 2020 to May 2021, 236 patients were randomized: 84 to AA plus usual care, 84 to PA plus usual care, and 68 to usual care alone. Participants had a mean age of 46.1 years; 53.6% identified as Black and 7.2% as Hispanic. More than 95% completed the one-hour assessment, meeting the feasibility goal.

At one hour, estimated pain reductions were 2.1 points for AA plus usual care, 1.6 points for PA plus usual care, and 0.5 points for usual care alone. The two acupuncture approaches did not differ significantly. Both acupuncture groups reported high satisfaction, averaging 4.4 on a five-point scale. Opioid and non-opioid medication use was lower in acupuncture groups after baseline and at discharge, but these differences were not statistically significant. Pre-existing chronic pain did not affect treatment response.

Adverse events were uncommon, with no serious events. Reported effects included transient needle-site pain, bleeding or bruising, headache, and brief anxiety.

Limitations included the single urban site, English-only enrollment, treatment by licensed acupuncturists, and inability to blind participants. The study concluded that auricular and peripheral acupuncture were feasible, acceptable, safe, and effective for acute musculoskeletal pain in the emergency department, warranting further multisite research and implementation evaluation.

Jonathan Toews expects a difficult Stanley Cup Final against an experienced, deep and disciplined Boston team. He says Chicago must prepare well, start strongly, create traffic and rebounds against Boston’s goaltender, avoid unnecessary post-whistle confrontations, and prioritize smart team play over risky individual moves. Despite limited scoring, Toews remains confident and focuses on contributing defensively and leading unselfishly. He respects Jaromir Jagr and Boston’s sweep of Pittsburgh but believes previous results no longer matter. Having won the Cup before, Chicago is determined to prove it can contend every year and capitalize on another championship opportunity.

Apple filed a Form 8-K on January 29, 2019, reporting the release of financial results for its first fiscal quarter ended December 29, 2018. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. CFO Luca Maestri signed the report.

The patent describes a blockchain-based platform for offering, purchasing, managing, and reselling tokenized securities representing transferable equity. Investors register through a graphical interface, undergo accreditation and compliance checks, review required documents, accept contractual terms, and transfer cryptocurrency or fiat currency into escrow. The platform synchronizes accreditation data, maintains investor whitelists and blacklists, records document hashes and transactions on an immutable ledger, and releases securities tokens and payment when specified conditions are met.

Tokenized securities may remain nontransferable during prescribed rest periods before secondary trading. The system supports bids, asks, transfers, vesting, conversions, capitalization management, documents, communications, analytics, and regulatory enforcement. Offering entities may update documents and terms, reverse transactions, burn unsold tokens, restrict noncompliant investors, and calculate tax information. Described smart contracts include transferable, proxy, escrow, aggregate, and related contracts. “BITE” tokens may represent stock, options, warrants, convertible notes, restricted stock units, or employee stock options, with conversion, dividend, financing, and liquidity-event rights. The platform may operate through cloud-based servers, user devices, accreditation services, blockchain oracles, digital wallets, and public or private blockchains, including Ethereum.

Airbus Helicopters may close its Ghimbav manufacturing base and move production, possibly to Poland, unless Romania commits to buying at least 16 H215M helicopters. The maintenance base would remain unaffected. Romania has also developed ties with Bell, which seeks an order for 45 attack and transport helicopters.

The S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.4 per cent to 6183.4 amid rising trade tensions and financial-sector losses. Major banks declined, while AMP dropped 3 per cent on potential regulatory and legal costs. Broker downgrades sent Platinum Asset Management down 8.9 per cent and Magellan Financial down 8.8 per cent.

El estudio analiza lingüísticamente la expresión de emociones en 798 tuits de Acciona e Iberdrola publicados entre abril y junio de 2016. Mediante análisis del discurso, clasifica los mensajes como informativos o emocionales, distingue emociones descritas y evocadas e identifica categorías semánticas y metáforas conceptuales.

La mayoría de los tuits presenta contenido emocional, principalmente de valencia positiva. El orgullo es la emoción más frecuente en ambas cuentas, seguido del interés, la alegría, la felicidad y la confianza; las emociones negativas —miedo, preocupación, tristeza e ira— son escasas. Los mensajes evocativos recurren, entre otros recursos, a imperativos, preguntas retóricas, exclamaciones, emoticonos y hashtags.

Las metáforas se concentran en la alegría-felicidad-optimismo, el orgullo y la confianza. En Iberdrola, la felicidad se conceptualiza mediante la luz, la energía, el sol, el calor y el movimiento, mientras que el color verde representa identidad corporativa y orgullo. En Acciona, la sostenibilidad, la innovación y los logros empresariales evocan confianza y orgullo. Estos dominios metafóricos se vinculan con la misión, visión y valores de cada compañía, reforzando su identidad organizacional.

El estudio concluye que el microblog corporativo constituye un corpus válido para investigar las emociones en las organizaciones y propone incorporar estos recursos al español de los negocios y a la enseñanza de español con fines específicos.

Two US books challenge moral panic about children online. In *Screenwise*, Devorah Heitner advises parents not to panic, to prioritize parent-child relationships, examine their own screen use, avoid oversharing, and seek children’s permission before posting photos. In *Worried About the Wrong Things*, Jacqueline Ryan Vickery argues that debate focuses too narrowly on pornography, predators, and cyberbullying while overlooking unequal technology access. Based on fieldwork at a diverse Texas school, she finds that poorer students depend more on filtered school computers. Vickery recommends emphasizing young people’s online opportunities and agency rather than treating them primarily as passive victims.

This two-center retrospective study developed a fully automated machine learning tool to predict 1-year overall survival in pediatric diffuse midline glioma using multisequence MRI at diagnosis and after radiation therapy. The system used transfer learning for tumor-core and whole-tumor segmentation, extracted radiomic features, and applied a linear support vector machine. It was trained and validated on 53 patients from Children’s National Hospital and externally tested on 16 patients from Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia.

Automatic segmentation showed mean Dice scores of 0.91 for tumor core and 0.88 for whole tumor internally, and 0.74 and 0.86 externally. Survival prediction achieved 77–85% accuracy, with post-radiation data generally improving accuracy and sensitivity. More homogeneous whole-tumor intensity on baseline T2 FLAIR and a larger post-radiation tumor-core-to-whole-tumor ratio were associated with survival under one year.

The tool may support standardized risk stratification, treatment-response monitoring, clinical decisions, and multi-institutional trials. Limitations include small cohorts and possible radiomic variation from differing scanners and imaging protocols; the findings require validation in larger datasets.

Historical comparisons offer little reliable guidance on how U.S.-North Korea tensions might affect stocks. While peace in the early 1990s coincided with rising valuations, markets have reacted inconsistently to other conflicts, including the Korean and Vietnam wars and recent fighting in Afghanistan and Syria. The 1990s bull market likely reflected the internet’s emergence and falling interest rates more than a “peace dividend.” The Dow’s recent decline after President Donald Trump’s North Korea remarks may therefore reflect investor concern about his unpredictability rather than expectations of imminent war. The retreat could also be part of a broader reversal of the post-election “Trump trade,” with investors increasingly focused on Trump’s mindset.

Indian benchmarks declined, with the Sensex down 253 points to 32,923 and Nifty down 101 to 10,094, amid energy-stock losses and a widening current account deficit. Asian markets also fell ahead of a potential US rate hike. Technical indicators showed oversold conditions, with Nifty support at 9,900–10,000 and Nifty Bank support near 24,000. Stock calls included buys on National Aluminium, Mahindra & Mahindra, Jagran Prakashan and Just Dial, and a sell on Indiabulls Housing Finance.

Wafra Investment Advisory Group maintained 167,141 Marsh & McLennan shares worth $11.24 million in the third quarter. Several other investors modestly increased holdings, while institutional investors and hedge funds owned 83.81% of the company.

Marsh & McLennan traded at $67.59, with a $34.85 billion market capitalization. Quarterly earnings were $0.69 per share, exceeding estimates by $0.01, while revenue of $3.14 billion fell below expectations. Analysts forecast annual earnings of $3.37 per share. The stock had a consensus “Buy” rating and a $69.44 target price.

Chairmen Alexander Moczarski and Peter Zaffino sold 8,850 and 21,087 shares, respectively. Corporate insiders owned 1.51% of shares. Marsh & McLennan provides professional services through Marsh, Guy Carpenter, Mercer and Oliver Wyman Group.

A pipe bomb strapped to 27-year-old Akayed Ullah exploded in a crowded subway passage near Times Square during Monday morning rush hour, injuring him and three others. All injuries were non-life-threatening. Mayor Bill de Blasio and Police Commissioner James P. O’Neill called it an attempted terror attack. Officials said Ullah, a Brooklyn resident possibly of Bangladeshi descent, was inspired by the Islamic State group but apparently had no direct contact with it. The low-tech device was attached with Velcro and plastic ties. The blast prompted a major emergency response, evacuations, area shutdowns, and subway and bus disruptions around the Port Authority terminal. President Donald Trump was briefed.
Bayshore Petroleum announced director C.F. Cheng’s immediate resignation to pursue other business interests. The company expects to replace him soon in connection with anticipated financing.

As of April 10, foreign investors had sold South Korean shares for six consecutive sessions, totaling a net 353.6 billion won. April 10 net sales were 54.0 billion won by foreigners and 4.5 billion by institutions, while retail investors bought 6.5 billion won.

Associated Press interviews with 29 Rohingya women and girls who fled Myanmar to Bangladesh found consistent accounts of systematic gang rape by Myanmar security forces, often accompanied by killings, beatings and village destruction. Survivors, aged 13 to 35, described attacks from October 2016 to September involving men typically wearing military uniforms. Their testimony supports the U.N.’s assertion that rape was used as a “calculated tool of terror” against the Rohingya.

Doctors and aid workers reported treating numerous sexual violence survivors, including children, and believed many attacks remained unreported. Myanmar’s military did not respond to AP requests, while a military investigation denied the assaults and Aung San Suu Kyi’s government dismissed reports as false.

One survivor, F, said soldiers raped her, killed her husband and burned her home. She later discovered she was pregnant. Months afterward, armed men attacked her again and killed members of the family sheltering her. She escaped to Bangladesh, where she planned to keep the baby, her only remaining family.

The coach said Anaheim’s playoff record deserves respect, but his experienced team is focused on winning rather than merely participating. Joe’s injury remains day to day, and lineup decisions will be made after further meetings. He expects competitive games with chances for both teams and emphasized staying composed regardless of events.

He said players and coaches must continually learn, and the team must move beyond its emotional recent victory to prepare for the next challenge. Anaheim’s longer rest could briefly affect its start but may also leave players healthier. Jeff has fit in well, while Oleg experienced recurring injury problems.

The coach expressed confidence in Marty’s ability to ignore distractions and praised both teams’ goaltending. He wants more scoring production and said his team must find ways to undermine the opposing goalie’s confidence. He stressed starting early, avoiding panic, and recovering the emotion needed to meet Anaheim’s strong playoff starts.

“Pound Cake” attacks a Box-and-One defense by isolating the star player against the chaser in the post, where pass-denial specialists may be less effective and the 2-1-2 alignment limits help. If no shot develops, the star can use baseline screens, curl or back cut to the basket, fade to the baseline, exploit switches through a screener’s roll, or pop outside for a one-on-one opportunity. Ball reversals and post flashes create additional feeding angles.

Supporting players space the floor, cut when defenders help, and receive drop or kick-out passes. Other options include screener pops, guard basket cuts, and double mid-screens that create matchup problems and outside shots.

Successful execution requires coordinated screening, post play, defensive recognition, communication, timing, and experience. Recommended preparation includes breakdown drills, shell drills, scrimmaging, scouting defensive tendencies and matchups, monitoring adjustments, varying alignments and entries, and targeting weaker defenders. In a Box-and-One, four defenders play a box zone while the chaser aggressively denies one opponent the ball and rebounds.

Technology stocks led U.S. markets lower Tuesday as Alphabet fell 3.9% on concerns about rising costs, prompting declines across other FAANG shares. Apple dropped amid warnings from suppliers about weaker smartphone demand. The Nasdaq fell 0.60%, the S&P 500 declined 0.20%, and the Dow lost 0.37%. The 10-year Treasury yield briefly reached 3% for the first time since 2014, adding pressure. Industrial shares also weakened: Caterpillar reversed earlier gains, Lockheed Martin fell after maintaining its cash-flow outlook, and 3M plunged after trimming its forecast. Despite market declines, 77% of reporting S&P 500 companies had exceeded profit estimates, raising projected first-quarter earnings growth to about 21%.

Defence Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said her ministry would assist efforts to rescue over 1,500 Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims stranded in Nepal by bad weather; two pilgrims had died. Tamil Nadu opened a Delhi control room to support returning pilgrims, including about 19 from the state.

Zacks Investment Research upgraded Liberty Global PLC from hold to buy with a $35 price target, citing DOCSIS 3.1 services, its Vodafone Netherlands joint venture and acquisitions as growth drivers. Risks include European economic pressures, competition, currency exposure and integration challenges. Among analysts, twelve rate the stock buy, one hold and one sell, with a consensus target of $43.85. Shares opened at $30.59, giving the company a $27.72 billion market capitalization. Executives Bryan H. Hall and Paul A. Gould recently purchased shares, while company insiders own 3.93% of the stock. Several institutional investors increased their holdings, and hedge funds and institutions own 23.48%. Liberty Global operates cable services in 14 countries, connecting about 25 million customers to more than 47 million television, broadband and telephony subscriptions.

The Supreme Court will consider whether a trial judge may prohibit a criminal defense lawyer from discussing a client’s ongoing testimony during an overnight recess. David Villarreal, convicted of murdering his boyfriend and sentenced to 60 years, argues that such an order violated his Sixth Amendment right to effective counsel.

Supreme Court precedents permit banning lawyer-client contact during a brief recess but prohibit a total ban during an overnight recess. State supreme courts have generally allowed overnight restrictions limited to testimony, while several federal appeals courts recognize a right to discuss ongoing testimony overnight. The Texas Court of Criminal Appeals upheld the restriction in Villarreal’s case.

Villarreal argues that separating testimony from other trial advice is impractical, chills candid counseling, and threatens attorney-client privilege. Texas maintains that limited restrictions are workable and protect against improper management of testimony. The United States supports Texas, arguing such orders can protect trials’ truth-finding function and are historically consistent with the Sixth Amendment. The decision may clarify permissible limits on lawyer-client consultations during trial recesses.

The Cape Horn Pigeon was released from Russian detention too late to resume whaling in the Okhotsk Sea or elsewhere during the 1892 season. Its owners, officers, and crew sought indemnity for lost operations, consumed supplies, forced service transporting a Russian vessel, imprisonment, maintenance, communications, legal assistance, transportation, and proceedings. The captain estimated damages at $49,500 and submitted claims in September 1892. In 1893, the United States requested an investigation. Russia’s commission found no basis for confiscation, attributed the arrest to a misunderstanding, and ordered release. Russia considered the $45,000 lost-whaling claim excessive but proposed $2,500 compensation. The United States formally presented the indemnity claims in June 1894. After repeated requests, Russia replied in October 1895, seeking vouchers for $3,400 in claimed expenses.

Frequent wheezing, coughing and breathlessness may indicate COPD, diagnosed primarily through pulmonary function testing. Causes can include premature birth, uncontrolled asthma, environmental exposure and genetics, not only smoking. Untreated COPD damages lungs, while breathing and conservation exercises can help diagnosed patients manage symptoms and slow worsening.
The power-play goal hurt momentum, but continued pressure, persistence, and tiring heavily used defenders could create third-period opportunities despite Patrick’s strong saves.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that on January 30, 2019, it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2018. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under the Securities Exchange Act.

During the NHL’s centennial celebrations, more than four million fan votes selected the Edmonton Oilers as the greatest NHL team ever. Led by Wayne Gretzky, Paul Coffey and other Hall of Famers, the Oilers dominated the regular season and playoffs, defeated the Philadelphia Flyers to win a second consecutive Stanley Cup, and saw Gretzky earn the Hart and Conn Smythe trophies.

Nike unveiled Nigeria’s 2018 World Cup campaign and kits, with the home jersey featuring bright green, white and black chevrons inspired by the 1994 strip. Mirror Football ranked it best among 20 revealed jerseys. Nike denied claims of three million pre-orders, stating no pre-order option existed and the jersey would be released in June.

Tesla appointed Dave Morton as Chief Accounting Officer effective August 6, 2018. Formerly Seagate Technology’s CFO, Morton will receive a $350,000 annual salary and a $10 million equity grant vesting over four years. His employment is at will, with eligibility for standard employee benefits.

Early offense has three phases: an initial push before the defense organizes, a continuous flow into an early set, and a continuity offense if no advantage develops. Teams should transition between phases without hesitation, seeking numerical advantages, mismatches, and quality shots.

Effective early offense begins with disruptive defense, forced turnovers or rushed shots, authoritative rebounding, and quick, safe outlet passes. Players should push the ball on every possession, run wide lanes, advance into the front court within 3–5 seconds, keep their heads up, minimize dribbling, pass ahead, and finish outnumbered situations. If the initial attack fails, teams should exploit defensive disorganization before moving into continuity play.

As the shot clock winds down, players should remain poised and involve their best offensive players. They should aggressively pursue offensive rebounds and assume every shot may miss. Success requires strong conditioning, rapid transition—especially against zones—and disciplined execution during the scoring phase, where many turnovers occur.

The President described Soviet threats to end Western rights and access in West Berlin as a worldwide challenge to freedom. He affirmed that the United States, Britain, France, and NATO would uphold their legal rights and commitments to West Berlin, while remaining willing to negotiate peaceful arrangements consistent with freedom, security, and international agreements.

To strengthen military readiness, he requested an additional $3.247 billion for the armed forces, an increase in Army strength to about one million, larger Navy and Air Force personnel levels, expanded draft calls and reserve activation authority, retention or reactivation of ships and aircraft, improved airlift and sealift, and $1.8 billion for conventional weapons and equipment. He emphasized the need for flexible forces capable of responding without choosing only between humiliation and nuclear war.

He also requested $207 million for civil defense, including identifying and supplying fallout shelters and improving warning and detection systems. The new requests totaled $3.454 billion, raising annual defense spending to $47.5 billion and contributing to an estimated deficit exceeding $5 billion. He said the recovering economy could bear the cost but pledged spending restraint, closure of tax loopholes, a balanced future budget, and possible tax increases if necessary.

The President called for NATO unity, continued assistance to developing nations, disarmament efforts, economic progress, and education. He warned that weakness and disunity could lead to war, but stressed that the United States sought peace without surrender. He concluded that there was no quick solution and asked Americans for perseverance, support, advice, and prayers.

Dennis Waldron sued Ball Corporation and others after they obtained his deceased wife’s medical records using a previously signed medical reimbursement form, despite his refusal to authorize release. Ball sought the records to defend a workers’ compensation claim by Waldron’s coworker, who had the same rare leukemia and alleged workplace toxins contributed to both illnesses.

The court affirmed summary judgment dismissing claims for conversion, fraud, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and invasion of privacy. Conversion failed because Waldron had no possessory interest in the records, which belonged to the medical providers. Fraud failed because Ball disclosed that it would continue seeking the records, and alleged misrepresentations were made to hospitals rather than Waldron. Although the court did not condone defendants’ method of obtaining the records, their conduct was not sufficiently extreme or outrageous to support intentional infliction of emotional distress. The privacy claim also failed because New York recognizes only a statutory privacy right concerning use of a person’s name or image for advertising or trade, which was not involved. CPLR 4504 protects patient confidentiality among designated health professionals but creates no private cause of action.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 28, 2015 reported quarterly net sales of $58.0 billion, up 27% year over year, and net income of $13.6 billion, up from $10.2 billion. Diluted earnings per share rose to $2.33 from $1.66, while gross margin increased to 40.8%. Six-month net sales were $132.6 billion and net income was $31.6 billion.

Quarterly iPhone sales rose 55% to $40.3 billion on 61.2 million units, while iPad sales fell 29% to $5.4 billion on 12.6 million units. Mac sales increased 2% to $5.6 billion, and Services sales rose 9% to $5.0 billion. Greater China sales grew 71% to $16.8 billion; Japan sales declined 15%.

At March 28, 2015, Apple held $193.5 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, including $171.3 billion held by foreign subsidiaries. Total assets were $261.2 billion, shareholders’ equity was $129.0 billion, long-term debt was $40.1 billion, and commercial paper outstanding was $3.8 billion. Six-month operating cash flow was $52.8 billion.

During the quarter, Apple repurchased $7.0 billion of common stock and paid $2.7 billion in dividends. It issued U.S. dollar- and Swiss franc-denominated debt, while its $90 billion share-repurchase authorization had been utilized by $80 billion.

Apple cited foreign-currency weakness, component and manufacturing concentration, competition, product transitions, legal proceedings and tax investigations as risks. A jury awarded Smartflash approximately $533 million against Apple, which Apple was challenging without recording a loss accrual. Apple also had $19.0 billion in manufacturing and component commitments and $5.1 billion in future operating lease payments.

The global drone payload market is projected to grow from $4.28 billion in 2016 to $13.54 billion by 2023, at a 17.8% CAGR. Growth drivers include sensor advancements, increased defense spending, lower camera prices, environmental applications, and military cost efficiency. Security, privacy, regulation, and design complexity may constrain growth. Synthetic Aperture Radar is expected to lead components due to defense use. North America is projected to dominate, while Asia Pacific should grow moderately. The report covers commercial and defense applications, major regions, market trends, forecasts, competitive analysis, and key industry participants.

Kuwaiti preacher Mubarak al-Bathali claimed Mohamed Salah’s Champions League final shoulder injury was divine punishment for breaking his Ramadan fast. Salah changed his fasting plans after consulting Liverpool staff. Al-Bathali said breaking the fast for the match was unjustified, while praising Salah and urging repentance.

In April 1983, Secretary of State George Shultz proposed intensifying dialogue with Moscow to counter increased Soviet activism under Andropov and test whether improved U.S.-Soviet relations were possible. He argued that fundamental differences and Soviet military power made an amicable breakthrough unlikely, but firm U.S. policies might induce changes in Soviet behavior. Shultz cited progress through rearmament, stronger alliances, ideological competition, and arms-control proposals. He expected Soviet diplomatic offensives in Europe and Asia and recommended greater U.S. diplomatic and public activism. Preconditions included rebuilding U.S. strength, revitalizing alliances, stabilizing relations with China, pursuing regional peacekeeping, and continuing ideological competition. Dialogue would probe Soviet flexibility, preserve U.S. influence, prevent allied divisions, and sustain domestic and allied support. It should address Soviet military buildup, expansionism, and human rights violations without lowering basic U.S. requirements for improved relations.

The study used a single-group posttest design to evaluate an eight-week activity-based amateur guitar program during the Covid-19 pandemic. Five volunteers aged 18–33 with no previous guitar instruction received individual online lessons totaling 16 hours. The curriculum covered major and minor scales, open and barre chords, chord transitions, and arpeggios through introduction, development, and evaluation stages adapted from the 5E model.

Three field experts approved the program’s content and level. Students completed a 10-question theoretical test and a 10-item performance assessment. Performance was evaluated by three experts using criteria for pitch and duration accuracy, tempo, technique, and musicality. Final scores weighted theoretical knowledge at 40% and performance at 60%.

The students’ theoretical scores were 80–100, with a mean of 92. Their final achievement scores were 91, 89.2, 95.5, 93.6, and 98.8, producing a class average of 93.6. All five students were classified as “very good.” The study concluded that activity-based lesson plans produced successful outcomes for this study group and may support engagement, theoretical learning, performance, and academic achievement in amateur guitar education.

A Digital Business Ecosystem (DBE) combines an economic community of interdependent organizations with a self-organizing digital infrastructure. Its lifecycle comprises formation, evolution, and dissipation. Formation is crucial because entities identify opportunities, select partners, collaborate, negotiate, and establish contracts.

The paper focuses on negotiation during DBE formation and proposes Contract Net with Quality Protocol (CNQP), an extension of the FIPA Contract Net Protocol. Standard CNP organizes negotiation through task identification and announcement, contractor evaluation and bidding, bid evaluation, contract award, execution, reporting, and termination. CNQP adds participant evaluation of the announcer and announcer evaluation of participants. These assessments consider reliability, trust, reputation, transaction history, resources, and current quality.

Quality evaluation increases negotiation time through interactions with a Quality Backbone Engine. However, the authors argue that it can reduce uncertainty, execution risks, resource overhead, and transaction failures by identifying suitable entities and strengthening confidence among business partners. CNQP retains CNP’s lightweight, flexible, and straightforward structure with minor message modifications. Future work will apply the protocol to negotiations between business entities using service-level parameters and develop the quality evaluation mechanism further.

Authorities identified James T. Hodgkinson, 66, of Belleville, Illinois, as the gunman who fired on Republican lawmakers practicing baseball in Alexandria, Virginia. He died after a shoot-out with Capitol Hill police. Hodgkinson frequently posted sharp criticism of President Donald Trump, Republican politicians, income inequality and campaign finance, and belonged to several anti-Republican Facebook groups. He strongly supported Senator Bernie Sanders, apparently volunteered for his 2016 presidential campaign and praised Sanders as understanding the working class. Sanders condemned the shooting as a “despicable act.” Hodgkinson had owned a home inspection business whose license expired in 2016. Earlier battery and property-damage charges against him were dismissed, while he pleaded guilty to speeding in 2007.

Baskin Financial Services increased its TransCanada stake by 2% in the third quarter to 199,992 shares valued at $9.5 million, representing 2.5% of its portfolio. Other institutional investors also expanded or initiated positions, with institutions owning 51.44% of the stock. TransCanada shares traded at $45.15, with a $36.12 billion market capitalization and a 52-week range of $28.40 to $48.52. The company announced a quarterly dividend of $0.4221 per share, equivalent to a 3.74% yield. Analysts gave TransCanada a consensus “Buy” rating and an average target price of $61.50. TransCanada operates natural gas pipelines, liquids pipelines and energy businesses.

The author disputes Education Minister Mitzie Hunter’s claim of commitment to rural students, arguing that provincial funding models pressure local boards to close schools despite higher rural education costs and long bus rides. Hunter criticizes Conservative leader Patrick Brown’s proposed moratorium as limiting local decision-making, but the author says ministry policies dictate those decisions. Two Georgian Bay-area schools were temporarily saved through community, private-sector, municipal and developer support, without assistance from the ministry or school board.

Offensive tackles are the outermost two of five offensive linemen, responsible for executing run- and pass-blocking schemes. They often face elite pass rushers one-on-one, protect the quarterback’s pocket, and create running lanes by blocking defensive linemen and linebackers. The left tackle has particular importance because they protect a quarterback’s blind side.

Success requires blocking technique, footwork, hand placement, coordination, agility, strength, and strong football awareness to respond to defensive formations, blitzes, and movement. NFL offensive tackles are generally 6 feet 3 inches to 6 feet 8 inches tall, weigh 300–340 pounds, and combine a thick build with functional athleticism and lateral mobility.

The position’s name reportedly originated when outside defenders commonly tackled ball carriers on outside runs. Standard abbreviations include OT and T, while linemen may be nicknamed hogs, bruisers, bulldozers, or big uglies. Notable offensive tackles include Jonathan Ogden, Anthony Munoz, and Joe Thomas.

The Justice Department formed a national task force of prosecutors to investigate Enron’s collapse and possible accounting fraud, while the SEC, Labor Department and congressional committees pursued separate inquiries. Enron welcomed the centralized investigation. The White House faced scrutiny over six meetings between Enron representatives and Vice President Cheney or his energy-policy staff, while officials considered policies to protect workers and pensioners from similar failures.

Enron prepared to auction its energy-trading business, with Citigroup and UBS among reported bidders, despite creditor concerns about valuation, liabilities and distribution of proceeds. A federal judge declined to freeze $1.1 billion allegedly earned by 29 Enron officers and directors through stock sales, citing insufficient evidence they would conceal assets. Another bankruptcy order allowed Enron to reject leases and contracts with 10 business days’ notice.

Cape Cod lawmakers are seeking a legislative oversight hearing into how the criminal justice system handled Thomas Latanowich, who is charged with murdering Yarmouth K-9 Sgt. Sean Gannon while officers served an arrest warrant. Latanowich had a lengthy criminal record, and a prior domestic violence case involving Gannon’s testimony was dismissed after the alleged victim declined to cooperate. Lawmakers want to identify possible systemic lapses, while Trial Court leaders said they would participate.

A study of 1,856 adults with a lifetime history of psychosis found cannabis use rose nearly 10% five years after states legalized recreational marijuana, with the increase emerging primarily after retail commercialization. Usage became more widespread but not more frequent among individual users.

Medical professionals warn that THC, particularly in high-potency products, can induce or exacerbate psychosis. Previous studies associate cannabis use with earlier onset, worse prognosis, more severe symptoms, greater disability, lower medication adherence, and more hospital admissions. However, the study did not assess cannabis potency or determine whether increased use worsened participants’ mental health.

Researchers suggest potency caps and health warnings could reduce harms, noting only two states require warnings linking high-potency cannabis to psychosis. Limitations included overrepresentation of women, self-reported diagnoses, and unavailable treatment histories. The biological mechanism linking cannabis and psychosis remains uncertain.

James Lovelock’s 1970s Gaia hypothesis proposes that interactions between living organisms and inorganic processes help keep Earth habitable. Researchers from the universities of Exeter, Lincoln and Southampton suggest “sequential selection” explains this stability: destabilising conditions are short-lived, while stable systems persist and acquire further stabilising traits through “selection by survival alone.” The mechanisms could help explain Earth’s long-term habitability, assess the likelihood of complex life elsewhere, and clarify responses to climate change and extinction events. The study was published in Trends in Ecology and Evolution.

Former President George H.W. Bush, 93, was hospitalized in Houston after an infection spread to his blood following Barbara Bush’s burial. His spokesperson said he was “responding and recovering.” Melania Trump offered prayers. Bush has previously been hospitalized for pneumonia and chronic bronchitis.

Tamiflu use has risen. Seek medical advice for illness lasting several days or fever above 102°F. A flu kit may include sanitizer, masks, decongestants, pain relievers, and water. Flu shots remain available at pharmacies.

Verdad Research analyzed nearly 30,000 stocks from 2005–2023 and found that U.S. hard-to-borrow stocks generally underperformed over 3-, 6-, and 12-month periods, unlike comparable stocks in Japan and Europe. However, exploiting this tendency may be impractical because shares can be difficult to locate and borrowing fees can be high.

Short selling requires borrowing shares through a broker, selling them, and returning them after repurchase. Selling without locating shares is prohibited. Stocks become hard to borrow because of limited supply, high short-selling demand, regulatory restrictions, elevated loan fees, and locate requirements. Fees can range from 1% to 50%.

Large, stable, liquid stocks usually have lower borrowing costs, while small, volatile, illiquid stocks cost more. Fees also fluctuate with market conditions. GameStop’s average fee rose from about 1% in January 2019 to 34% in January 2021 amid increased short interest and a short squeeze. Short selling is risky because potential losses are unlimited.

The federal judiciary will use court fee balances and other funds not dependent on new congressional appropriations to maintain paid operations through Oct. 17 during the government shutdown. Judges will continue receiving constitutionally protected salaries. Most proceedings and deadlines will continue, though some civil cases involving unavailable executive-branch attorneys may be delayed; at least 10 district courts have postponed some matters. The Supreme Court will similarly use nonannual funds during a short-term lapse. Once funding runs out, courts will operate under the Antideficiency Act: staff supporting essential constitutional duties may work without pay, while others may be furloughed. Each court and federal defender’s office will determine necessary staffing.

A trading time frame includes both a trade’s expected duration and the bars used, ranging from ticks and minutes to years. The passage recommends daily bars as a versatile starting point because they simplify backtesting, may reveal market inefficiencies, and reduce intraday noise. However, traders should select time frames suited to their goals, strategies, and available edge.

Different participants use different horizons: day traders typically hold positions for minutes or hours, swing traders for days or weeks, trend followers for days to months, and investors for years or decades. Strategies can combine time frames, such as weekly bars for identifying trends and daily bars for entries.

Trading across multiple time frames and asset classes can improve capital use, reduce correlations, and diversify risk. Gains from short-term strategies may offset losses in long-term positions, potentially smoothing performance and limiting drawdowns. Although daily bars are recommended, losses remain inevitable, and no single time frame is universally best.

Researchers studying mice identified peroxisomes as a backup heat source in brown fat when mitochondrial heat production is impaired. Container patterns provide modular ways to extend applications and build distributed systems. An ambassador can split traffic between services, using IP hashing for consistent user experiences and weighted routing for experiments.

The adapter pattern modifies an application container’s interface to meet common operational conventions without changing the application itself. Adapters can expose standardized monitoring metrics, redirect or normalize logs, and implement rich health checks. Examples include a Prometheus exporter for Redis, Fluentd plugins for Redis and Storm logging, and a separate MySQL health-check container. This separation supports reuse, independent updates, dedicated resources, and shared expertise.

Microservices divide applications into independently maintained components communicating through defined APIs. They improve team autonomy, release agility, reliability, and independent scaling, but make debugging and system design more difficult. Distributed patterns help standardize their architecture.

Replicated load-balanced services use identical servers behind a load balancer for availability and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching instances before initialization is complete. Session-tracked services route a user consistently to one replica, preferably using cookies or headers for external traffic. Application-layer tiers can add caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination. A demonstrated Kubernetes architecture uses replicated application, Varnish cache, and nginx SSL layers connected by Services.

Sharded services divide requests or state among specialized replicas when data exceeds one machine’s capacity. Sharded caches improve memory utilization but make failures and upgrades more consequential because each request maps to a specific shard. Replicating each shard improves availability and supports independent scaling of hot shards. Shard routers may run as ambassadors or shared services. Effective sharding depends on deterministic, uniform keys and may use consistent hashing to minimize remapping when shard counts change.

Scatter/gather distributes parts of a request across multiple workers and combines their results, reducing processing time through parallelism. It can also shard data across workers. Excessive parallelism introduces overhead, straggler latency, and availability risks because completion depends on all required responses. Replicating each shard improves reliability, scaling, and upgrade safety.

Function-as-a-service provides event-driven, automatically scaled execution and simplifies deployment, but enforces stateless, network-based decoupling that complicates monitoring and debugging. It is poorly suited to long-running background work, applications requiring substantial in-memory data, or sustained workloads where per-request pricing becomes costly. Suitable patterns include request or response decoration, such as adding API defaults, and asynchronous event handling, such as sending two-factor authentication codes.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the 7 nm Ampere GA100 architecture, for AI, high-performance computing, and data analytics. A100 includes 108 streaming multiprocessors, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1555 GB/s bandwidth, and a 40 MB L2 cache.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32, BF16, FP16, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. Compared with V100, A100 provides higher mixed-precision and FP64 performance, while 2:4 structured sparsity can double Tensor Core throughput by skipping zero values. Additional improvements include simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, asynchronous memory copies and barriers, cache-residency controls, compute-data compression, hardware JPEG and video decoding, and an optical-flow accelerator.

Multi-Instance GPU technology partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU instances, each with dedicated compute and memory resources, predictable performance, fault isolation, and quality of service. Compute instances further divide resources and allow independent context execution.

Third-generation NVLink supplies up to 600 GB/s total GPU interconnect bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4 provides 31.5 GB/s per direction for x16 connections. CUDA 11 supports Ampere features including sparsity, task graphs, asynchronous operations, cooperative groups, MIG, and L2 cache controls.

The DGX A100 system combines eight A100 GPUs, delivers up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, and can provide as many as 56 isolated accelerators through MIG. It uses NVLink, NVSwitch, Mellanox networking, Magnum IO, and NVIDIA’s software stack to scale AI and HPC workloads from individual instances to large clusters.

The lecture reviews numerical optimization, emphasizing that assignments should focus on numerical methods rather than unresolved engineering definitions. Steepest descent follows the negative gradient toward local minima, with step sizes estimated using quadratic Taylor expansions. It always moves downhill but may converge slowly, fail on flat landscapes, or continue indefinitely when no minimum exists.

Symmetric positive-definite linear systems \(Ax=b\) can be formulated as minimizing a quadratic objective. Conjugate gradient improves on steepest descent by selecting conjugate directions that preserve earlier minimization. It can solve an \(n\)-variable system in at most \(n\) iterations and requires only matrix-vector products, but applies directly only to symmetric positive-definite matrices. Related Krylov subspace methods address broader systems.

For nonlinear optimization, Newton-Raphson applies the inverse Hessian to the gradient. It converges quadratically near a critical point and solves quadratic objectives in one step. However, it requires solving linear systems, encounters problems with singular Hessians, and may approach maxima, saddle points, or asymptotes when the Hessian is not positive definite.

Trust-region methods combine Newton-Raphson’s speed with steepest descent’s downhill behavior. They accept Newton steps when these remain within a trusted radius and reduce the objective; otherwise, they use steepest-descent or boundary-limited steps. The trust-region radius grows or shrinks according to how accurately the quadratic approximation predicts improvement. MATLAB uses such heuristic methods, including dogleg trust-region steps, to solve nonlinear equations and minimization problems.

Williams %R is an oscillating, mean-reversion indicator developed by Larry Williams. Backtests on the S&P 500 ETF SPY found the best results with a two-day lookback. A comparable RSI strategy returned a lower 7.3% CAGR, though the difference could reflect chance. Another Williams %R strategy using a second indicator achieved a 13.4% CAGR on QQQ, 14% market exposure, a 3.2 profit factor, and a 20.5% maximum drawdown. This study examined associations between hypertension, current blood pressure, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) leakage using a sensitive dynamic contrast-enhanced 7 Tesla MRI protocol. BBB leakage rates and blood plasma volume fractions were measured in grey and white matter regions. Cerebral small vessel disease markers and cardiovascular risk factors were also assessed. Hypertension status was not significantly associated with BBB leakage after adjustment for age and sex. However, higher systolic, diastolic, and mean arterial pressure were associated with greater leakage in cortical grey matter, while diastolic and mean arterial pressure were also associated with leakage in total grey matter. No significant associations occurred in white matter or deep grey matter. These relationships generally remained after adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors, medication, and cerebral small vessel disease burden.

Hypertensive patients had higher blood plasma volume fractions in grey matter, but these measures were not associated with current blood pressure. Leakage was higher in men than women. Patients whose blood pressure was normalized with antihypertensive medication showed lower grey-matter leakage than patients with currently elevated blood pressure, although subgroup sizes were small.

The findings indicate that current blood pressure, rather than hypertension status alone, is associated with subtle BBB leakage, particularly in cortical grey matter. The study investigated early changes in participants without known cerebrovascular disease, but was limited by its sample size, low cerebral small vessel disease burden, and use of 30-minute rather than 24-hour blood pressure monitoring. Larger or longitudinal studies were recommended to clarify medication effects.

The study examined dropout tendencies among students at Turkish public universities using Tinto’s Theoretical Dropout Model. Survey data were collected during 2023–2024 from 1,061 preparatory and undergraduate students selected through simple random sampling. Princeton-led researchers reported in Nature that ATP-dependent ISWI chromatin remodelers use the nucleosome’s negatively charged “acidic patch” to regulate access to genetic information. High-throughput screening involving tens of thousands of biochemical measurements showed that remodelers outside the ISWI family also use this feature, suggesting it may be broadly required for chromatin remodeling. Chemical modifications near the acidic patch can enhance or inhibit ISWI activity and produce distinct effects on other chromatin-interacting proteins. The resulting data provide a resource for studying how chromatin modifications regulate ISWI functions. Because acidic-patch mutations occur in some human cancers, the findings may also support research into potential therapeutic targets.

Andrew Lo explains modern portfolio theory using expected return, volatility, and covariance. Combining imperfectly correlated securities creates a bullet-shaped set of portfolio opportunities. Rational investors who prefer higher returns and lower risk select portfolios on its upper branch, the efficient frontier. Diversification generally improves the risk-return trade-off, and adding securities cannot make investors worse off because they may assign new securities zero weight. Correlations below one can provide diversification benefits, while negatively correlated stocks with positive expected returns are rare.

Combining any risky portfolio with a risk-free asset produces a straight risk-return line. The best such line is tangent to the efficient frontier, and its tangency portfolio offers the highest expected excess return per unit of volatility. This measure—the portfolio’s expected return minus the risk-free rate, divided by its volatility—is the Sharpe ratio. Investors with different risk preferences choose different positions along the tangency line: conservative investors hold more Treasury bills, while risk-tolerant investors may borrow to invest more in the tangency portfolio. This analysis assumes equal borrowing and lending rates and stable portfolio parameters.

Indifference curves describe how much additional expected return an investor requires for greater risk. Although investors differ in risk aversion, mean-variance investors all prefer positions on the tangency line. Performance beyond this baseline is called alpha and can be used to assess whether investment managers add value.

In equilibrium, if all investors hold combinations of Treasury bills and the tangency portfolio, aggregate demand must equal the supply of assets. Consequently, the tangency portfolio must be the market portfolio: all assets held in proportion to their market capitalizations. Broad market indexes such as the S&P 500 or Russell 2000 can serve as approximations.

For efficient portfolios, expected return equals the risk-free rate plus a premium determined by portfolio volatility relative to market volatility and the market’s excess return. For any individual security or portfolio, Bill Sharpe’s broader relationship replaces relative volatility with beta. Beta equals the covariance of the asset’s return with the market return divided by the market return’s variance. Thus, the equilibrium expected return, or appropriate discount rate, equals the risk-free rate plus beta multiplied by the market risk premium. This makes covariance with the market, rather than total volatility, the relevant measure of risk for determining the cost of capital.

Belarusian out-of-school education combines Soviet traditions with EU lifelong-learning principles. Its development progressed from early literacy programs, through a Soviet system emphasizing labor, practical training, career choice, and talent identification, to a post-Soviet model focused on individual development and mental health.

The 2011 Education Code defines out-of-school education as part of lifelong learning and guarantees broad access, government funding, institutional resources, and activities supporting intellectual, moral, physical, creative, vocational, and social development. Additional regulations emphasize patriotism, civic and environmental education, healthy lifestyles, safety, leisure, career preparation, and psychological support.

By the end of 2021, Belarus had 318 institutions: 185 comprehensive and 133 specialized. Specialized institutions included regional study tours, ecosystem protection, physical training, science and technology, professional training, and art. Public institutions are popular because of lower fees, qualified staff, stability, and their role in academic competitions that can facilitate university admission. About one-third of Belarusian children and adolescents participate, although private providers are increasingly entering the market.

The system prioritizes four abilities: mastering information technology, developing a social personality, functioning in a multicultural world, and sustaining lifelong learning. Institutions provide age-specific technology courses, sports and volunteer activities, cultural exchanges, safety education, and vocational experiences. Identified limitations include inadequate funding and equipment, unequal access to paid technology programs, insufficient publicity, limited attention to small-group interpersonal skills, and multicultural activities that are often brief.

Overall, Belarus uses legislation, public institutions, and clearly defined educational objectives to integrate physical, social, technological, cultural, and vocational development. The passage presents this experience as potentially useful for improving China’s public out-of-school education policies and resource allocation.

On “Jeopardy!,” three contestants left the football category until last and failed to answer any of its five questions. Host Alex Trebek jokingly remarked that they were big football fans and suggested going to commercial. The passage also reports that several Philadelphia Eagles players experienced illness before the Super Bowl in Minneapolis, with Ronald Darby and Timmy Jernigan missing a media session and Mychal Kendricks later attending.

John M. B. Sill described Japan as favoring Korean independence from Chinese suzerainty and reforms promoting peace and prosperity. Foreign representatives proposed simultaneous Japanese and Chinese troop withdrawals. Japanese representative K. Otori referred the proposal to his government while affirming support for peace. Yuan Shi-Kai reported that China intended to withdraw after Korean rebels dispersed but would not do so unless Japan also withdrew, citing the 1885 Tien-Tsin agreement. Japan had rejected simultaneous withdrawal. At a June 26, 1894 audience, Otori said Japanese troops had been sent to protect Japan’s legation and subjects and assist Korea if necessary. He praised restored order and emphasized the historical friendship and mutual dependence of Japan and Korea.

University of Oxford researchers detected hydrogen sulphide in Uranus’s cloud tops using infrared observations from Hawaii’s Gemini North telescope, confirming earlier theories. Unlike Uranus, Jupiter and Saturn have ammonia clouds, a difference that may reveal how and where the planets formed. Uranus’s extreme atmosphere would kill humans before the rotten-egg smell mattered.

Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon said stock markets could face a drawdown within 12 to 24 months after AI enthusiasm drove heavy investment and record highs. Comparing the trend with the dotcom era, he warned that markets often outpace a technology’s potential and that some deployed capital will fail to generate returns. The killing of Kim Jong Nam at a Malaysian airport, allegedly by North Korean female agents using a sprayed toxin, renewed attention to poison as a stealthy murder weapon. Common poisons include ricin, thallium, arsenic, strychnine, cyanide and potassium, each causing different symptoms and acting at varying speeds. Though slow poisons can aid escape, toxic compounds may be difficult to handle and conceal. Poisoning has long featured in literature, historical debate and political assassination. Notable modern cases include Georgy Markov’s 1978 ricin killing, Alexander Litvinenko’s 2006 radioactive poisoning, the 1995 Tokyo sarin attack and the 2004 killing of Indonesian activist Munir Said Thalib.

Cameroon plans to restore 12 million hectares of deforested land by 2030 while strengthening protection of existing forests. The Congo Basin initiative involves 183 organizations, including local councils, NGOs and businesses, with annual government funding for councils and vulnerable chiefdoms. Cameroon has more than 23 million hectares of forest but lost 777,000 hectares between 2001 and 2015, half since 2012. Officials say restoration will support communities, climate resilience and economic development. Environmental experts welcome the project but stress that conserving indigenous forests should remain the priority because they store more carbon, support greater biodiversity and provide essential services such as drinking water and hydroelectric power. The government says it has reinforced forest governance and sanctions, though efforts to curb forest loss have had limited success.

CME lean hog futures fell about 3% Friday as abundant U.S. supplies pressured cash markets. October hogs closed at 59.175 cents per pound and December at 60.925 cents, both sharply lower. ZnSe-WSe₂ and ZnSe-MoSe₂ core-shell nanowires were fabricated by chemical vapor deposition growth of ZnSe nanowires, reactive DC magnetron sputtering of WO₃ or MoO₃ precursor layers, and subsequent selenization. MoSe₂ shells were produced at 600–650°C and WSe₂ shells at 700–750°C, with a 20-minute reaction time.

TEM showed that lower selenization temperatures produced thin, conformal layered shells: approximately two MoSe₂ layers below 2 nm at 600°C and three WSe₂ layers around 2 nm at 700°C. At 650°C for MoSe₂ and 750°C for WSe₂, shells became discontinuous and formed protruding crystals. XRD, XPS, and Raman spectroscopy confirmed wurtzite ZnSe cores and successful conversion of the oxide precursors into MoSe₂ and WSe₂ without detectable residual oxide. Raman and photoluminescence measurements indicated that the ZnSe cores remained structurally intact and identified optical features associated with ZnSe and the diselenide shells.

The morphology change was attributed to temperature-dependent growth mechanisms. At lower temperatures, predominantly solid-state reactions between selenium species and oxide coatings yielded smoother shells governed by precursor thickness. At higher temperatures, oxide evaporation, gas-phase reactions, and redeposition promoted crystalline island growth. Uniform shells may benefit electronic and optoelectronic applications, while protruding crystals may offer greater surface area for catalysis. The approach may extend to other semiconductor nanowire and layered-material heterostructures.

CompositesWorld’s 2017 Carbon Fiber conference will take place Nov. 28-30 in Charleston, South Carolina. The author thanks family and mentors. Modern applications require high availability, reliability, and rapid scaling, making distributed systems widespread but difficult to build. The President urged Congress and the public to act immediately against inflation through a coordinated economic program. Proposals included expanding food production, reviewing regulations that raise food prices, monitoring exports, reducing foreign oil dependence, increasing domestic energy production, improving automobile fuel efficiency, and developing alternative energy sources.

He called for stronger antitrust enforcement, regulatory reform, inflation-impact statements for government actions, and voluntary rather than compulsory wage and price restraint. To increase capital and employment, he proposed investment tax credits, tax changes supporting equity investment, and liberalized capital gains treatment.

Measures for those most affected by inflation included extended unemployment benefits, a temporary Community Improvement Corps, and tax relief for low- and middle-income households. He also sought broader federal mortgage purchases, reforms for thrift institutions, passage of trade legislation, and international economic cooperation.

To finance the program, he proposed a one-year 5 percent surcharge on corporate and upper-level individual incomes, generally excluding families earning below $15,000, while rejecting a gasoline tax increase. He requested a $300 billion federal spending target and reductions across agencies, including defense.

Citizens were asked to reduce food waste, drive and heat less, share resources, and join the voluntary “WIN” mobilization. He described inflation as the nation’s foremost public enemy and appealed for discipline, sacrifice, and joint action by government and the public.

EduVidQA addresses the lack of interaction in online educational lectures by evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for answering student questions. A survey of 52 STEM students found that 67.9% wanted to ask questions while watching educational videos, but only 17% posted content-related questions, motivating an expert-level question-answering system.

The dataset contains 5,252 open-ended question-answer pairs from computer science and AI lectures: 270 expert-curated real-world pairs and 4,982 synthetic pairs generated from 197 videos. Real questions were extracted from YouTube comments, temporally grounded, and answered or corrected by domain experts without LLM assistance. Synthetic pairs were generated from annotated NPTEL transcripts, filtered for timestamps and contextual dependence, tagged by Bloom’s Taxonomy, and divided into 3,908 training and 1,074 test pairs. Human review indicated high question naturalness and answer soundness.

A student preference study identified clarity as the most valued answer quality, while encouraging critical thinking and using pedagogical techniques were also considered relevant. These qualities informed LLM-based evaluation metrics validated against human annotations. Benchmarking covered six open- and closed-source video and vision-language models using conventional text metrics, FactQA precision and recall, and qualitative measures.

Fine-tuning smaller open-source models on synthetic data consistently improved quantitative and qualitative performance. Fine-tuned models with 7–13 billion parameters performed comparably to, and sometimes better than, larger closed models. Among evaluated open models, mPLUG-Owl3 8B and LLaVA-13B performed strongest, while GPT-4o led among closed models on parts of the real-world evaluation. Nevertheless, all models retained substantial room for improvement.

Limitations include restricted participant demographics, a small computer-science-focused real-world dataset, reliance on LLM-based qualitative evaluation, and compute-constrained model selection. The authors caution that synthetic data and expert annotation may introduce bias and emphasize that automated systems should complement rather than replace human educators.
The judgment is affirmed based on President Judge Griffith’s opinion. The appellant must appear before the lower court and remain committed until completing any unperformed sentence.

At the September 10, 1892 seizure, Joseph and William R. Wing of J. & W. R. Wing were the Cape Horn Pigeon’s agents and managing owners. Ownership was divided among several Massachusetts parties, with transfers since the vessel’s 1887 register documented by customs certificates and exhibits. All owners were native American citizens domiciled as stated. The bark carried a captain and 30 officers and crew, whose compensation consisted of shares of net voyage proceeds, including recoveries replacing catch. Some crew claims were assigned to the owners after advances, and most seamen owed more in advances and ship charges than their pay because little oil was obtained. Built in Dartmouth in 1854 for whaling, the 201.42-ton bark had always conducted that business. J. & W. R. Wing fitted her out at San Francisco in December 1891 for a year-long whaling voyage in the Japan and Okhotsk seas. She had no sealing equipment, preservation materials, or intention to take fur seals or assist sealing.

The paper addresses memory inflation and contextual degradation in long-running Low-Code/No-Code agents. It proposes a hybrid architecture comprising working memory, episodic memory for time-indexed interactions, and semantic memory for generalized knowledge. Its “Intelligent Decay” mechanism scores episodic memories using weighted recency, task relevance, and user-assigned utility, then retains, deletes, or consolidates them into semantic summaries.

A timeline-based Human-in-the-Loop interface enables non-technical users to view memory status and mark entries for retention, forgetting, or consolidation. This is intended to improve transparency, control, trust, and memory quality.

In a simulated 500-turn software project-planning task, the system was compared with a 10-turn sliding window and basic retrieval-augmented generation. It achieved a 92.5% task completion rate, versus 65.2% and 81.4%, respectively. It also recorded a 0.94 consistency score, a 1.2% contradiction rate, and an average cost of 890 tokens per turn, 22% lower than basic RAG. Simulations indicated that indiscriminate memory addition caused declining performance, while the hybrid approach maintained or improved performance over time.

Limitations include the need to tune decay parameters and reliance on consistent, high-quality user feedback. Proposed future work includes autonomous parameter calibration, structured pruning, multimodal and procedural memory, integration with stateful agent frameworks, adaptive optimization, and specialized deployment.

Carroll County’s school board asked commissioners to reconsider moving the school system’s Central Office from Westminster to the former North Carroll High School. Superintendent Stephen Guthrie said the noncentral location could increase travel by roughly 50 percent in miles and 30 percent in time, raising operating costs and potentially requiring cuts or additional funding.
