The board will send commissioners another letter detailing projected annual costs. Commissioner Richard Weaver defended the approved budget, saying the county had considered broader needs and provided all available resources.

The passage specifies SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guest–hypervisor communication mechanisms. AP Creation events let SNP guests create, update, remove, or immediately run vCPUs using guest-prepared VMSA pages, enabling alternative AP boot and vCPU hotplug. Related events support APIC ID discovery, execution at different VMPL levels, Secure AVIC backing-page registration, and guest termination.

With Restricted Injection, guests use a shared #HV doorbell page for pending interrupts and non-maskable events, #HV Send IPI for interprocessor interrupts, and #HV Timer for emulated APIC timers. Doorbell configuration supports preferred-address retrieval, setting, querying, and clearing. Host and guest must follow defined atomic acknowledgement, interrupt-priority, EOI, signaling, and validation rules. Guests should execute HLT with interrupts disabled and inspect pending events after resuming.

SEV-TIO allows SNP guests to bind trusted devices, validate device information and reports, configure MMIO and IOMMU state, and receive measurements, certificates, and attestation reports through shared contiguous data pages. The hypervisor validates page capacity and reports required storage.

SEV-ES guests identify support through specified CPUID properties. Because measured and encrypted vCPU registers cannot ordinarily be changed, traditional INIT-SIPI AP startup requires predefined initial state, reset-hold protocols, and AP jump tables. SNP AP Creation simplifies this process and is required with Restricted Injection.

NMI delivery uses an “NMI Complete” message rather than IRET interception. Hardware debug-register virtualization is supported when enabled; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and emulated. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported. Unsupported negotiated events must produce an “Unsupported Event” VMGEXIT.

After Liberty Media acquired Formula 1 in 2016, CEO Chase Carey, CCO Sean Bratches, and motorsport director Ross Brawn sought to transform it from a traditionally managed motorsport into a global entertainment brand. By 2019, attendance reached 4.2 million, cumulative television audience rose to 1.9 billion, and digital engagement expanded, though unique television viewers declined.

Formula 1 combines elite racing, automotive technology, extensive data analysis, and complex team strategy. Its main stakeholders are the teams, regulator FIA, and Formula 1’s commercial organization. Revenue primarily comes from broadcasting, race-promotion fees, advertising and sponsorship, hospitality, and other services. Team budgets varied widely, contributing to prolonged dominance by Mercedes, Ferrari, and Red Bull and financial pressure on smaller teams.

Liberty inherited an organization with limited marketing, research, digital infrastructure, and fan engagement. New leadership established functions in these areas and adopted five priorities: improve competition and team relations, upgrade events, engage fans through traditional and digital platforms, expand the brand, and grow in markets such as China and the United States. Initiatives included social media, streaming, esports, fantasy leagues, fan festivals, exhibitions, podcasts, personalized content, and Netflix’s *Drive to Survive*. Research on viewership, social media, spectators, and event movement informed broadcasting, marketing, sponsorship, and scheduling decisions.

A central problem remained weak on-track competition. Aerodynamic turbulence made close following and overtaking difficult, while large spending disparities reinforced dominance by the wealthiest teams. Proposed 2021 regulations included a $175 million budget cap and redesigned cars intended to support closer racing and greater unpredictability. Formula 1 expected stronger competition to improve fan engagement and commercial performance.

The organization also faced obligations as an automotive technology platform. Formula 1, FIA, and participating teams committed to carbon neutrality by 2030 amid climate change and industry transition. Its continuing challenge was balancing commercial growth, fan expectations, team and driver interests, competitive racing, technological leadership, and environmental relevance.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture improves video encoding quality and enables 4K streaming with lower CPU use. It supports VirtualLink, which combines display, data, and power for VR headsets through one USB-C connector. TU102 and TU104 GPUs replace earlier SLI interfaces with higher-bandwidth NVLink, supporting two-way SLI and advanced display configurations.

Turing introduces real-time ray tracing through dedicated RT Cores, which accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection tests. Combined with rasterization, denoising, and NVIDIA RTX software, this hybrid rendering approach produces physically correct reflections, refractions, shadows, ambient occlusion, and indirect lighting. Turing achieves over 10 Giga Rays per second and approximately ten times Pascal’s ray-tracing performance.

NGX uses Turing Tensor Cores and pretrained deep neural networks for graphics features. DLSS renders with fewer samples and reconstructs target-resolution images with quality similar to TAA while reducing shading work; DLSS 2X approaches 64-times supersampled quality. Other NGX functions include image inpainting, interpolated slow-motion video, and AI-based image or video upscaling.

Additional graphics features include Mesh Shading, which reduces CPU draw-call bottlenecks and supports efficient geometry processing and level-of-detail selection; Variable Rate Shading, which adjusts shading rates by region for content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering; Texture Space Shading, which decouples visibility and appearance sampling and reuses shading results; and Multi-View Rendering, which processes up to four hardware views per pass for VR, shadows, and multiple object instances. Turing also expands DirectX 12 resource binding and heap support.

Turing’s VR improvements combine VirtualLink, Multi-View Rendering, foveated rendering, Texture Space Shading, and RT Core-accelerated VRWorks Audio. TU104 contains up to 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, while TU106 contains 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores but lacks NVLink and SLI. Tesla T4 uses TU104 for inference workloads.

The architecture combines rasterization, ray tracing, AI, integer processing, and simulation. NVIDIA’s RTX-OPS metric weights these workloads according to estimated frame-time usage. Real-time ray tracing is enabled collectively by hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH acceleration, and RT Cores.

Medical oxygen is essential for many acute and chronic conditions, but COVID-19 exposed major global supply inequities. In Peru, the pandemic revealed longstanding regulatory, logistical, and governance weaknesses amid a fragmented health system, regional disparities, political instability, and high excess mortality.

The study used a problem-based political economy analysis combining 13 stakeholder interviews with reviews of academic literature, grey literature, policies, and health-system reports. Researchers identified seven relevant academic articles, 87 grey-literature documents, and 23 policies.

Peru’s pre-pandemic requirement that medical oxygen exceed 99% purity restricted competition and concentrated government contracts among a few large suppliers, despite the availability of 93% oxygen standards. Production was concentrated near the central coast, leaving Andean and jungle regions dependent on inadequate distribution systems. During COVID-19, authorities underestimated demand, responded slowly, and took seven months to formally lower the purity standard. Fragmented procurement, weak coordination, political turnover, absent centralized leadership, and limited data on oxygen demand, production, equipment, and distribution worsened shortages. Scarcity contributed to inflated prices and informal sales of unsuitable or stolen cylinders.

Civil society, religious organizations, academia, and private companies helped address shortages by donating oxygen, cylinders, and plants. By the pandemic’s end, 496 plants had been installed, but bureaucratic approval problems, unclear ownership, insufficient training, staff turnover, missing replacement parts, and absent maintenance plans limited sustainability. Nearly 200 plants later became unused, broken, or abandoned, while many facilities returned to purchasing cylinders from major suppliers. Although maintenance funding was allocated, implementation remained limited.

Interviewees generally considered Peru insufficiently prepared for another health emergency. The study recommends establishing a National Oxygen System integrating demand and supply monitoring, forecasting, centralized coordination, equitable distribution, quality control, equipment inventories, maintenance funding, infrastructure, and trained personnel. A coordinated national framework could reduce reliance on external suppliers, sustain oxygen infrastructure, and improve preparedness for future crises.

Researchers using 3D modeling and field experiments found that Rapa Nui islanders likely transported moai upright by pulling ropes to rock them in a zig-zag motion. Models identified wide D-shaped bases and forward leans that enabled movement. Eighteen people moved a 4.35-ton replica 100 meters in 40 minutes. The island’s 4.5-meter-wide, concave roads may have stabilized the statues during transport. The findings support earlier experiments, challenge theories involving prone transport on wooden devices, and highlight the engineering skill of Rapa Nui’s people.

This scoping review mapped methods used to measure socioeconomic status (SES) in health research across sub-Saharan Africa. Five databases were searched for English-language publications from January 2012 to June 2024. Following duplicate removal and two-stage screening, 65 articles covering 22 countries were included.

Most studies were research articles, with cross-sectional and cohort designs predominating. South Africa, Kenya, and Ghana were the most represented countries. SES assessment and maternal and child health were the leading research themes.

The review identified 41 SES measures across 11 categories. Asset-based wealth indices were most common, accounting for 61.9% of measures, followed by indices incorporating education, health, and living standards. Common indicators included household assets, housing conditions, utilities, land, livestock, transportation, education, employment, income, health, and perceived social standing. Principal Component Analysis was the predominant method for calculating asset-based wealth indices, used independently in 57.7% of cases and with other methods in 9.6%.

The diversity of SES measures and methodologies limits study comparability and continent-wide conclusions. Income-based measures may be difficult to apply where informal employment is widespread, while asset-based and multidimensional measures may better identify disadvantaged groups in some contexts. The review recommends greater standardization of SES measurement across Africa while retaining flexibility for local contexts. Limitations included no thorough quality appraisal, methodological heterogeneity, and the possibility that relevant literature was missed.

Sudan, the world’s last male northern white rhinoceros, was euthanized at Kenya’s Ol Pejeta Conservancy at age 45 after a severe leg infection left him unable to stand. Captured in 1975, he lived in a Czech zoo before moving to Kenya in 2009 with females Najin and Fatu, but they never reproduced. Northern white rhinos, once widespread in parts of Africa, became extinct in the wild because of war and poaching. The two surviving females cannot carry calves, so scientists hope to collect their eggs, fertilize them with preserved sperm, and implant embryos in southern white rhinos. However, egg collection has never been performed on rhinos and could endanger the remaining females.

This study developed and tested a maternal vulnerability segmentation tool (MVST) to identify underserved pregnant women in Oromia, Ethiopia, and examine associations between vulnerability and use of antenatal care and health-facility delivery. Baseline data came from a 2024 community-based quasi-experiment. Researchers screened 1,614 households, identified 1,189 eligible pregnant women, and analyzed service-use outcomes among a sample of 470.

An initial 20-item questionnaire covered economic, social, information, and service-access factors. Factor and reliability analyses produced a four-item tool for combined urban-rural settings and a six-item tool for rural settings. Relevant factors included residence, housing materials, women’s and household mobile-phone ownership, distance from health facilities, and women’s and husbands’ education. Both versions had acceptable model fit and internal reliability.

Higher vulnerability scores were associated with fewer antenatal care visits and lower health-facility delivery. Institutional delivery declined from an intersecting vulnerability score of three, while antenatal care declined from one or more vulnerability points. Regression analysis also showed that women with greater vulnerability were less likely to receive antenatal care or deliver in health facilities.

The MVST is intended as a practical population-segmentation device for frontline health workers, enabling targeted and potentially cost-saving interventions rather than serving as an intervention itself. Its applicability may be limited beyond the study areas because vulnerability varies by social, cultural, environmental, and pregnancy-stage contexts. Further research should validate the tool across settings and test it against maternal and child health outcomes.

The SPREAD offense is a 3-2, no-post motion system requiring all players to pass, handle, cut, and read defensive overplays. After passing, players cut to the basket, then clear to corners if not receiving the ball while teammates fill vacated positions. Overplayed players immediately back cut rather than fight pressure. Ball handlers use triple-threat position, drive when defenders overplay passing lanes, and kick out against help defense. Corners may initiate back-door plays through the middle when wings are denied or the shot clock is low.

A study of 549 participants from 29 countries found that smileys in formal work emails reduced perceptions of the sender’s competence without increasing perceived warmth. Recipients also provided less detailed, content-related responses to emails containing smileys. Unlike smileys, photographs of smiling senders increased perceived competence and friendliness. When the sender’s gender was unknown, smiley use made recipients more likely to assume the sender was a woman. Researchers recommend avoiding smileys in initial workplace interactions.

US labor-force participation among young adults without college degrees has declined more sharply than among graduates, while about 12% of 18- to 24-year-olds are disconnected from work and school. Experts attribute the trend to limited access to well-paying jobs, stigma against non-degree and blue-collar work, mental-health and substance-use challenges, isolation, and family support that allows some to avoid undesirable employment. Some gig workers may also be missing from official statistics. Proposed responses include education programs combining coursework with internships or apprenticeships and efforts to improve perceptions of trades and other non-degree careers, though experts say reconnecting older disengaged adults will be difficult.

Legal scholar Deepa Das Acevedo argues that tenure protections have eroded through decades of legislation, university policies and intentional attacks on academic labor. Recent rapid disciplinary actions against faculty over social media posts following Charlie Kirk’s killing illustrate universities’ increasing willingness to disregard established due-process procedures.

Das Acevedo identifies two enduring justifications for tenure: compensating academics for lower earnings and career hardships through employment security, and protecting academic freedom. She says current controversies over public speech, alongside growing economic pressure on universities and faculty, reinforce both purposes.

She disputes claims that tenure reduces productivity, noting that limited empirical research does not support the stereotype, though output may temporarily rise before tenure and level off afterward. Anecdotes about unproductive professors may reflect cognitive bias rather than broader evidence.

Tenure does not make professors immune from dismissal. As a form of just-cause employment, it permits discipline or termination for sufficiently serious misconduct, including predatory behavior, plagiarism or research misrepresentation. Failure to act against misconduct generally reflects institutional choices rather than tenure restrictions.

Tenure typically requires reasons, notice and faculty-informed procedures before termination. However, universities largely control whether these processes are maintained, changed or ignored, making tenure and academic freedom increasingly dependent on institutional willingness to honor them.

A quality improvement project explored trainee and trainer perspectives on regional teaching for Stage 1 anaesthetists across five UK hospital trusts following the 2021 curriculum change. Six trainees and eight trainers participated in focus groups, with transcripts analysed thematically.

Participants described Stage 1 training as demanding and uncertain, involving varied trainee needs, clinical competency, examinations and career development. Teaching differed substantially among hospitals, creating perceived unfairness, gaps in learning and competition between sites. Barriers to a regional programme included travel, space, funding, rota coordination, differing educator compensation, group size and quality assurance.

Despite these challenges, trainees and trainers generally supported regional teaching. Expected benefits included standardised, exam-focused education, wider curriculum coverage, shared teaching expertise, improved fairness, reduced isolation and greater networking. Participants emphasised the need for experienced coordination, continuous feedback, high-quality teaching and adaptation over time.

The findings prompted a deanery-wide trainee survey, investigation of teaching and study-budget policies, and engagement of consultants to lead teaching. Limitations included the small trainee sample and possible interviewer-related bias. The study concludes that a well-executed regional programme may reduce disparities but requires sustained engagement and investment.

RWE Supply & Trading expects to double or triple LNG derivatives trading from 1.5 million tonnes in 2017 to manage physical cargo price risks. The statistical analysis plan specifies treatment-group tables, listings, and figures using ICH conventions, primarily two-sided tests at the 0.05 significance level. Continuous variables will use descriptive statistics; categorical variables will use counts and percentages. Analyses will use SAS 9.4 or higher, with Phoenix WinNonlin 6.4 or higher for pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic analyses. Prespecified analyses are a priori; analyses after unblinding are exploratory and labeled post hoc.

Treatment groups are dasiglucagon, GlucaGen, and placebo. The safety set includes randomized patients receiving at least one dose, the full analysis set uses randomized treatment assignments, and the per-protocol set excludes relevant protocol deviations. The primary analysis uses the full analysis set, supportive analysis uses the per-protocol set, and safety analyses use the safety set.

The primary endpoint is time within 45 minutes to a plasma glucose increase of at least 20 mg/dL from baseline without rescue intravenous glucose. Secondary endpoints include recovery within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes and glucose changes from baseline at those times. Baseline is generally the last non-missing value before dosing. Analyses adjust for age group and injection site, use observed data without imputation, and include no interim analysis.

Dasiglucagon versus placebo testing follows a hierarchical sequence across the primary and secondary endpoints to control type I error. GlucaGen comparisons support study validity but are outside this hierarchy. Time to recovery will be analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and a stratified log-rank test; rescue-treated patients and those not recovered will be censored at 45 minutes in the primary analysis. Sensitivity analyses apply alternative rescue-glucose censoring, while supportive analyses include stratified Wilcoxon tests, Cox models where assumptions permit, recovery histograms, and linearly interpolated recovery times. Recovery rates use stratified Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests, with Fisher tests if necessary; glucose changes use analysis of variance.

Pharmacokinetic analyses summarize dasiglucagon and glucagon concentrations and derived metrics using noncompartmental methods. Pharmacodynamic analyses summarize plasma glucose and calculate area under the effect curve above baseline from 0 to 30 minutes. Rules address sampling times, values below quantification limits, and missing observations.

Safety analyses cover exposure, insulin and hypoglycemia induction, rescue glucose, local tolerability, treatment-emergent adverse events, laboratory tests, vital signs, ECGs, pregnancy testing, and immunogenicity. Adverse events are coded with MedDRA and summarized by treatment, relationship, severity, seriousness, and category. Anti-drug antibody incidence includes treatment-induced and treatment-boosted cases.

Appendices define presentation standards, derivations, conservative handling of incomplete dates, SAS programming validation and quality-control procedures, and planned tables, figures, and listings.

Neonatal jaundice commonly results from bilirubin accumulation and is usually self-limiting, but severe cases can cause neurological injury or death. To investigate its genetic basis, researchers conducted genome-wide association studies using neonatal, maternal, and paternal genomes from nearly 30,000 Norwegian families, with replication in 6,902 Danish neonates.

Two neonatal loci reached genome-wide significance: the UGT1A gene region and an X-chromosome locus near CHRDL1. A missense variant affecting UGT1A4, rs6755571, was associated with a five-fold lower jaundice risk in Norway and replicated in Denmark. Family analyses indicated a neonate-only effect. Colocalization suggested the association may involve increased intestinal UGT1A1 expression rather than altered UGT1A4 activity. The CHRDL1-region association also appeared driven by neonatal alleles and replicated in Denmark, although its mechanism remains unclear.

The maternal GWAS identified UGT1A, the X-chromosome locus, and the ABO region. The ABO association was largely explained by maternal-fetal blood-group incompatibility, which increased jaundice risk. The protective UGT1A4 variant remained effective despite ABO incompatibility, though its effect was stronger in full-term and post-term births.

Genetic effects differed substantially between neonatal jaundice and adult bilirubin levels. Adult-associated variants at UGT1A and SLCO1B1 showed little or distinct association in neonates. An adult bilirubin polygenic score predicted neonatal jaundice mainly through chromosome 2, which contains UGT1A. These findings suggest age-, tissue-, and context-specific mechanisms of bilirubin clearance, potentially emphasizing intestinal UGT1A1 activity in neonates. The study was largely limited to Nordic European ancestry, and the biological mechanisms require further investigation.

Art teacher Kenneth Hobbs unveiled the second panel of Lawton High School’s 22-foot cafeteria mural. Funded by the class of 2014, it depicts the school, “Hanta Yo!” sign, a Wolverine, and the 1993 National Wrestling Champions, continuing the historical and athletic timeline begun in 2010.

The passage describes a hard-sided, collapsible shelter or camper designed to combine portability with weather protection, security, insulation, and climate control. Rigid roof, floor, and folding wall panels transition between an expanded living or sleeping enclosure and a compact, weather-tight, lockable case. Folded units may be transported on roof racks, in pickup beds, on trailers, with detachable wheels, or by vehicles ranging from bicycles to cars.

Shelters may use insulated composite panels, sealed joints, windows, doors, locks, solar panels, batteries, electronics, plumbing, heating, cooling, and internal fixtures. Configurations range from low sleeping shelters to full-height campers with kitchens, bathrooms, seating, and movable bed platforms. Bed systems may be raised to provide standing space or lowered for sleeping without removing fixtures beneath them.

Wall panels may be bi-fold or multi-fold and connect to the roof, floor, or an intermediate structural connector through hinges, latches, and weather seals. Opening and closing may be manual or assisted by motors, pistons, pulleys, springs, or other mechanisms. In the collapsed configuration, the roof and floor enclose the folded walls, mattress, and fixtures. Various dimensions, materials, shapes, mounting arrangements, and interior layouts are described, along with methods for transporting, expanding, using, and collapsing the shelter.

Pivot points are price levels based on the previous day’s high, low, and close, used to identify potential support, resistance, and trade entry or exit points. Invented by floor traders, they are objective, quantifiable, versatile, and easy to use but lag price and produced low win rates in the authors’ tests. Six strategies were backtested on one-minute S&P 500, Nasdaq, Russell 2000, and USD/CHF data from 2010 onward. None was consistently tradeable alone, though some ideas may warrant further day-trading research. Lewis Borsellino reportedly used pivot points daily but did not explain his methods.

Federal policy seeks to reduce minority overrepresentation in special education, requiring reporting and remedial funding when significant disparities occur. However, the cited study found no evidence that racial, ethnic, or language minorities were disproportionately overidentified as disabled. After adjusting for socioeconomic status, academic achievement, behavior, and other factors, Black and Hispanic children were generally less likely than otherwise similar White children to receive several disability classifications. Children from non-English-speaking households were less likely to be identified with learning, speech, or language impairments. Disability identification was more strongly associated with academic achievement, behavioral self-regulation, and externalizing behavior. The study concludes that minority students are comparatively underrepresented in special education across elementary and middle school. The author argues that policies intended to prevent discrimination may further reduce minority access to services and asks who is harmed when children who could benefit from special education are mainstreamed.

Limiting opponents’ puck possession, forechecking, and time in the defensive zone is key. Mike and Joe Nieuwendyk are dangerous players who require reduced space and time; Brett’s possible absence would help.
The appellate court affirmed the Kitsap County Superior Court judgment in Belcher v. Kitsap County.

Thames Centre councillor Kelly Elliot is urging the Thames Valley District School Board to adopt a defibrillator policy after West Nissouri Public School fundraising secured a device and maintenance funding. The board declined installation, citing the need for a board-approved device and training, and has not commented.

More than 80% of Minnesota public school districts offer mental health services, often supplemented by nonprofits providing specialized support. Know the Truth uses peer specialists with personal addiction-recovery experience to help students affected by substance use. Specialist Tiffany White offers individual and group support, emphasizes harm reduction, and builds trust by sharing her own recovery story. Her work is funded through contracts and grants, though federal cuts eliminated her position at one school.

Restoration for All supports African immigrant and refugee students through culturally informed therapy, screenings, suicide monitoring, peer support and mind-body practices. The organization also trains educators to understand trauma, refugee experiences and cultural differences that can lead to students being misunderstood or inaccurately diagnosed. State grants have enabled it to expand services in several Minnesota communities.

South Korea’s spy agency suspects two female North Korean agents poisoned Kim Jong Nam, the estranged half-brother of leader Kim Jong Un, at Kuala Lumpur International Airport. U.S. sources also believed North Korean assassins were responsible. South Korean lawmakers said Kim Jong Un had issued a standing assassination order and that a 2012 attempt had failed. Malaysian police said Kim, traveling under the name Kim Chol, died en route to hospital while preparing to fly to Macau. An autopsy was underway, and the cause of death remained undetermined. Airport footage reportedly showed a woman involved, while unconfirmed media reports said two women attacked Kim with a poisoned needle and fled. Kim had lived largely abroad and publicly opposed his family’s dynastic rule.

No. 16 Miami defeated Clemson 81-57 as senior Adrienne Motley scored 15 points and passed Octavia Blue for seventh on the program’s all-time scoring list with more than 1,724 points. Jessica Thomas scored 18 and reached 1,200 career points, while Laura Cornelius added 14. Miami led most of the game, built a 48-30 halftime advantage and outscored Clemson 17-4 in the third quarter. The Hurricanes improved to 19-6 overall and 8-5 in the ACC during their annual Play4Kay game. They next face No. 14 Duke.

The lecture introduces the stress-energy tensor as a relativistic description of matter’s energy and momentum. For dust, the number four-vector combines rest number density with four-velocity and obeys a covariant conservation law. Multiplying particle four-momentum by the number vector gives the dust stress-energy tensor,
\(T^{\alpha\beta}=\rho_0 u^\alpha u^\beta\).
Its components represent energy density, energy flux, momentum density, and momentum flux. Energy density is neither a Lorentz scalar nor a four-vector component because it transforms with two Lorentz factors.

The stress-energy tensor is symmetric: energy flux equals momentum density, while spatial symmetry is physically motivated by showing that unequal off-diagonal stresses would produce divergent angular acceleration in an infinitesimal material element. Its vanishing spacetime divergence expresses covariant conservation of energy and momentum; choosing a reference frame separates this into distinct energy- and momentum-conservation equations.

A perfect fluid has no energy flow in its rest frame, no viscosity, and isotropic pressure. Its rest-frame tensor is diagonal with energy density and three equal pressure components. Covariantly, it is constructed from the fluid four-velocity, metric, energy density, and pressure. Dust is the zero-pressure special case. Because relativistic gravity cannot select only energy density, the entire stress-energy tensor must source gravity, with spacetime geometry providing the corresponding tensorial left-hand side.

Additional examples include a point particle, whose stress-energy tensor uses a spacetime Dirac delta function along its worldline, and the electromagnetic field. The electromagnetic tensor contains electric and magnetic energy density, the Poynting vector as energy flux, and generally anisotropic spatial stresses.

The lecture concludes by beginning a transition toward curvature through flat spacetime in curvilinear coordinates. Polar-coordinate basis vectors are coordinate-dependent and not necessarily normalized, so transformation matrices can contain entries with different dimensions and the metric acquires nonconstant functional components.

Texas faces Colorado after a major loss to Oklahoma, with its Big 12 South prospects potentially at stake. Colorado has beaten Texas six consecutive times and has not lost to the Longhorns in Boulder since 1941.

Coach Mack Brown named Major Applewhite the sole starting quarterback, with Chris Simms reserved for emergencies. Freshmen Roy Williams and B.J. Johnson were promoted to starting receiver roles, Kenny Hayter is expected to receive more carries, and defensive tackle Shaun Rogers is expected to return. Offensive coordinator Greg Davis is reassessing play-calling, penalties and the team’s commitment to a balanced offense. Chip Brown identifies offensive leadership, motivation and consistency as Texas’ primary concerns but says a win could restore the Longhorns’ position in the conference race.

U.S. stocks rebounded Wednesday on hopes Italy could avoid new elections. Banks, energy firms and small companies led gains. Major indexes rose 0.9%–1.5%, while yearly performance ranged from the Dow’s 0.2% decline to Nasdaq’s 8.1% gain.

A Salvadoran woman fled toward Houston after her 19-year-old daughter and 15-year-old son disappeared in a gang-controlled town. She and her partner were detained shortly after crossing into Texas, separated, and subjected to deportation under the Trump administration’s zero-tolerance policy. She was returned in chains to El Salvador while her partner remained detained.

Although President Donald Trump portrayed undocumented immigrants as gang threats, U.S. statistics showed only 0.09 percent of people detained in fiscal 2017 belonged to Central American gangs. Migration from El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras has risen substantially, with researchers saying most migrants are fleeing violence.

MS-13 and Barrio 18 control many Salvadoran working-class neighborhoods, extorting residents, killing those who resist, and targeting people suspected of rival affiliations. Government crackdowns have failed to halt gang growth, while police, soldiers and clandestine groups also contribute to threats and violence. Because El Salvador is small and gang territories are widespread, internal relocation offers little safety. An estimated 90 percent of deportees attempt migration again within days.

The returned woman said she feared going back to her home and was uncertain whether she would try to migrate again. Asked who awaited her there, she replied, “No one.”

Valencia resident Travis Phippen, wounded in the Las Vegas mass shooting that killed his father, John Phippen, filed a civil lawsuit against gunman Stephen Paddock’s estate in Clark County, Nevada. The suit seeks control and preservation of Paddock’s financial accounts, property and other assets. Paddock killed at least 59 people and wounded 527 at the Route 91 Harvest festival. Three other Santa Clarita Valley residents remained hospitalized and were reportedly recovering.

Transactions included leases for the Law Office of Peter D. Baron; Jersey Mike’s, Hand and Stone Massage, and Fortunoff Bedding; Hartford Fire Insurance and Hollander Legal Group; and SCH Sheet Metal. Marbai Profit Sharing purchased a mixed-use Miller Place property for $850,000.

Scale AI cofounder Alexandr Wang urges teenagers to spend thousands of hours “vibe-coding,” using natural-language prompts and experimentation with AI software tools. He argues that early, intensive AI experience could create career advantages comparable to those gained by Bill Gates and Mark Zuckerberg during the rise of personal computers. Wang, who became a self-made billionaire at 25, now leads Meta’s AI operations and superintelligence team. His advice comes as automation reduces some technology jobs and increases demand for AI skills.

More than 600 people have signed a petition opposing Alyn Family Doctors’ proposal to close its Gresford Health Centre branch and move patients to Llay and Rossett. The practice says staffing shortages leave no viable alternative for maintaining safe care across three sites and has asked Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board to consider the closure. Patients fear longer journeys, greater difficulty securing appointments and added pressure from proposed housing developments. The health board is supporting a consultation, with feedback accepted at surgeries, by post or email.

Fourteen Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust staff recreated a 1927 photograph of Hallam Hospital nurses to mark the NHS’s 70th anniversary. The original was among historic images discovered in a broom cupboard and preserved by trainer Sue Woodcock. The photographs will be displayed at Sandwell Hospital during an anniversary tea party.

Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi won the 2025 Nobel Prize in chemistry for developing metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), porous molecular structures capable of storing gases and other chemicals. Applications include collecting water from air, capturing carbon dioxide and extracting PFAS. Robson pioneered hole-filled crystalline structures by combining copper ions with organic compounds. Kitagawa created MOFs that absorb methane, nitrogen and oxygen, while Yaghi developed an exceptionally stable framework with enormous surface area. The three scientists share 11 million Swedish kronor, worth more than $1.1 million.

During an in-match penalty kick, defenders other than the goalkeeper must remain at least 10 yards from and behind the penalty mark, outside the penalty area and arc, and inside the field. They may enter only after the kicker touches the ball and it clearly moves forward. Early entry results in either allowing a scored goal or retaking a missed kick.

Defenders should quickly claim legal positions, hold ground without displacing opponents, and prepare to pursue any save, block, or rebound. Because the kicker may play the ball again after another player touches it—but not after only striking the post or crossbar—defenders must reach loose balls before attackers and clear them safely. If the goalkeeper secures or defenders clear the ball, the team should immediately counterattack through designated outlet players.

Defenders must also recognize rare “tap” penalties, in which the kicker moves the ball forward for a teammate to shoot. Training should rehearse positioning, competing legally for space, following rebounds, clearing blocked shots, transitioning to attack, and defending tap penalties. These procedures apply to match penalties, not shoot-outs, where follow-up play is prohibited.

The incoming chief executive expresses gratitude for public confidence, acknowledges the office’s responsibilities, and promises accountable service. He credits self-government, constitutional institutions, capable representatives, and an intelligent and virtuous citizenry for the nation’s prosperity, territorial growth, individual rights, successful defense, and political stability.

He urges preservation of the Union through public education, constitutional government, and protection against foreign threats. He supports coastal and frontier fortifications, moderate but effective land and naval forces, and a well-organized militia. He also advocates constitutionally authorized roads and canals to strengthen interstate ties, government support for domestic manufacturing, friendly and liberal relations with Indian tribes, responsible use of abundant national revenues, early repayment of the national debt, and strict oversight of public funds.

Peace, national harmony, and fair relations with other nations are presented as essential to continued prosperity. The speaker pledges to preserve republican principles, protect independence and liberty, promote the Union’s interests, learn from previous administrations, and rely on cooperation among government departments and divine protection.

The disclosure describes a gaming machine, control method, and program that synchronize game-event displays with background-music beats. The machine includes displays, speakers, storage, a controller, player controls, lighting, payment-related units, and other interfaces. Storage holds BGM sound data, tempo data containing beat timing, event sounds, graphics, reel layouts, paytables, and rhythm patterns.

During play, the controller outputs BGM, determines event timing from tempo data and, where applicable, the timing of player input. It dynamically configures animation so events appear at selected beat-aligned times. Event sounds and illumination may also occur at those times. Rhythm patterns can define the sequential timing of multiple related events.

In a video-slot embodiment, symbols are arranged on virtual reel strips and displayed in a grid. After a player initiates a game, reel stopping positions are randomly determined. The controller obtains the current BGM frame count, identifies a future on-beat frame, assigns beat-aligned stopping times to the reels, and generates spin-and-stop animations that reach the predetermined symbols at those times. Reel length may be modified without changing spin speed. Winning is then determined from displayed symbol combinations, and any applicable award is paid.

Alternative processing uses stored rhythm patterns to stop successive reels according to a defined sequence while maintaining alignment with the BGM. In bonus games, the controller may randomly select a scenario, determine beat-aligned timing for object movements or other events, generate corresponding animations, and display and pay the resulting outcome.

The technique can synchronize randomly occurring or player-triggered events, reel operations, bonus animations, sounds, and lighting with BGM beats. It may be applied beyond slot games to video card games, bingo, keno, wheel games, pachinko, and pachinko slot machines.

VentureWire’s November 7, 2000 issue reports Broadcom’s planned acquisition of processor-chip developer SiByte for up to $2 billion in stock; Alta Partners’ $275 million–$325 million third fund; Furniture.com’s shutdown and dismissal of 76 employees after failing to raise capital; and eStellarNet’s $30 million first institutional financing.

Numerous technology companies announced funding rounds, including Dotcast and Stellcom at $60 million and $50 million, respectively; Colorado MicroDisplay at $35 million; Centric Software, Frictionless Commerce, and eStellarNet at $30 million each; and Magma Design Automation at $28 million. Several venture firms also launched or raised funds targeting technology investments in the United States, Israel, India, Asia, and Europe.

Other developments included layoffs at Divine interVentures, Foodoo.com’s closure, new product launches and corporate renamings, and acquisitions. Sonus Networks agreed to acquire telecom technologies for more than $451 million, while InfoSpace acquired Locus Dialogue for approximately $128 million. The issue also reports executive and board appointments, including new CEOs at Disappearing Inc., Bridgewater Systems, IP Globalnet, and Adwise.

At Puerto Cortés in Honduras, Sergio Romero visits the Avontuur, a 97-year-old schooner that transports small cargo under sail. Unlike modern freighters burning bunker fuel, the vessel crossed from Europe through the Caribbean using wind power.
The speaker says the team must play cohesively and turn talk into action. Despite injuries, players remain motivated by their goals, and others have proven capable of stepping up.

Andrew Lo uses auctions of an iPod and an autographed book to illustrate how limited information affects valuation. He relates this to the government takeover of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, whose mortgage-market role, financial distress, and uncertain securities threatened wider market disruption. Government backing protected their obligations and counterparties but exposed taxpayers to costs and possible inflation, while shareholders lost most of their investments.

The lecture then defines an asset as an ordered sequence of present and future cash flows, which may be positive, negative, or zero. Asset value depends on the timing of those cash flows and can be represented by a value operator, often supplied by market prices.

Cash flows at different dates are treated like different currencies and must be converted into a common unit before being combined. Net present value converts future cash flows into present dollars using market-derived exchange rates or discount factors. Under certainty and without conversion frictions, an asset’s value equals the sum of its discounted cash flows. The interest rate, or opportunity cost of capital, unifies these conversions: a cash flow received after \(t\) periods is discounted by \(1/(1+r)^t\). This framework supports investment decisions and prepares for later analysis of annuities, perpetuities, inflation, uncertainty, and fixed-income securities.

Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) can detect pathogens without prior assumptions while simultaneously identifying antimicrobial resistance, virulence, and functional genes. Unlike culture-dependent diagnostics, it may detect novel or slow-growing organisms more rapidly, but routine clinical adoption remains limited.

This qualitative study explored views on clinical mNGS among ten infectious disease diagnostic stakeholders across six English regions. Semi-structured interviews conducted in 2021 were analysed using an interpretive phenomenological approach. Five themes emerged: diagnostic choice, infrastructure, open data sharing, COVID-19, and communication.

Participants viewed mNGS as a valuable addition to existing diagnostic tools rather than a universal replacement. Major barriers included cost, insufficient evidence of cost-effectiveness, slow turnaround times, unequal access between hospitals, centralised sequencing services, limited laboratory and digital infrastructure, workforce shortages, inadequate bioinformatics training, accreditation difficulties, workflow standardisation, and challenges storing and clinically interpreting genomic data. Open data sharing could strengthen surveillance and research but conflicts with patient confidentiality.

Participants supported local or decentralised sequencing to improve turnaround times and reduce reliance on empirical treatment. They also emphasised equitable funding, clinically actionable reporting, stronger business cases, and improved communication within and between hospitals and among healthcare, academia, industry, manufacturers, and funding bodies.

COVID-19 demonstrated the public health value of sequencing, increased its visibility, and expanded manufacturing capacity and access to platforms and reagents. Participants considered this experience a model for wider implementation.

The study concludes that successful routine adoption of mNGS requires attention to cost, speed, infrastructure, training, accreditation, data governance, and collaboration. Its findings were geographically diverse but did not represent Southwest or Northeast England.

Gary Allen Darnell, 45, a registered sexual predator, was arrested in Grafton after allegedly offering fishing poles to children near a river. He was charged with felony loitering within 500 feet of a park. Jersey County prosecutors said they will seek maximum penalties if he is convicted.

A Dueitt Middle School teacher was placed on administrative leave after allegedly calling African American students “cotton pickers.” Students corroborated the allegation, prompting Spring ISD to remove the teacher and launch an investigation. Parent Roshonda Davis praised the district’s response.

Berkshire Hathaway sold 10.6 million General Electric shares in the second quarter of 2017, exiting an investment originating from a roughly $3 billion financial-crisis loan that ultimately generated more than $1 billion in profit. The sale coincided with GE’s leadership transition from Jeff Immelt to John Flannery amid investor pressure, concerns about profit targets and a nearly 20% share-price decline. Berkshire also bought Synchrony Financial shares and increased holdings in Bank of New York Mellon and Apple while retaining stakes in Bank of America and Goldman Sachs. Other filings showed Appaloosa Management exited an S&P 500 ETF, Soros acquired over $1 billion in a Nasdaq-100 ETF, and Viking Global bought 12.3 million Wells Fargo shares despite the bank’s continuing regulatory and consumer-lending problems.

CUPA-HR examined Title IX staffing in higher education amid changing federal regulations. Title IX personnel oversee compliance, address sex discrimination and sexual misconduct, support campus safety and equity, and educate campus communities. Most are located in human resources (29%) or student affairs-related departments (28%), followed by compliance and diversity, equity, and inclusion offices (11% each).

Between 2019-20 and 2023-24, institutions with at least one dedicated full-time Title IX position increased from about one-third to 43%, while the reported workforce grew 38%, from 542 to 746 positions. Nevertheless, 56% of institutions still lack a dedicated full-time position, often assigning Title IX duties to employees with broader responsibilities. In 2023-24, 31% of institutions had a full-time head of Title IX compliance, 12% had a deputy head, and 16% had an investigator. Seventeen percent employed two or more dedicated Title IX staff.

Dedicated staffing was most prevalent at doctoral institutions: 64% had at least one Title IX position, compared with 45% of baccalaureate, 39% of master’s, and 19% of associate’s institutions. Thirty-six percent of doctoral institutions had multiple positions, versus fewer than 12% in other classifications.

Women held 77% of Title IX positions, compared with 62% of higher education professional positions overall. Black women represented 13% of Title IX staff, more than twice their 6% representation among professionals generally. Median salaries were $96,714 for heads, $84,931 for deputies, and $75,000 for investigators, all above the $66,000 median for higher education professionals. Women and people of color in Title IX roles had median pay comparable to or exceeding White men.

The report recommends reassessing Title IX officers’ responsibilities and resources, increasing dedicated staffing where needed, and monitoring legal and regulatory developments to maintain compliance with prevailing requirements.

Whitman Howard raised Produce Investments’ target price from GBX 210 to GBX 240 while maintaining a buy rating. Shore Capital and Numis Securities also reiterated buy ratings, with Numis setting a GBX 286 target. Shares rose 0.54% to GBX 187. The company declared a GBX 5.03 dividend payable December 5. Produce Investments grows, sources, packs and markets potatoes, daffodil bulbs and flowers.

Amazon entered a 364-day unsecured revolving credit agreement on November 18, 2022, with JPMorgan Chase Bank as administrative agent and other lenders. The facility provides up to $10 billion and may be extended for another 364 days. Initial interest is SOFR plus 0.45%, with a 0.05% fee on undrawn commitments. Borrowings will support general corporate purposes, including potential commercial paper notes. The agreement contains customary terms and defaults but no financial covenants.

The German Ambassador reported Germany’s willingness to confidentially state peace terms, including restoring Belgium with limited German travel rights, preserving neutral buffer states, French independence and coastline, restoring Russian territory, properly treating Serbia and Romania, and indemnifying Belgium. He said Britain hesitated to disclose terms because its maximum allied demands were impractical while minimum British terms risked allied disagreement, but American pressure might prompt disclosure.

Greece welcomed the U.S. peace initiative, emphasizing its severe suffering despite neutrality, including foreign occupation, disarmament, blockade, and threats of starvation. Although unable to participate fully because of restricted communications and unresolved difficulties, the Greek Government expressed strong support for peace efforts and readiness to cooperate in future action securing stable peace, state rights, sovereignty, and independence.

Marines tested Instant-Eye surveillance drones before Task-Force-Southwest’s Afghanistan deployment, while 2nd Law Enforcement Battalion completed grenade training for an upcoming exercise. The Marine Corps also awarded 91-year-old Lee Anderson a Purple Heart for injuries sustained at Iwa Jima 72 years earlier.

SOS side-screen defense varies by screen location. Below the free-throw line, defenders trap the ballhandler before the screen is set, force play toward baseline or corner checkpoints, deny return passes, front or double-team the post, and rotate into helpside “I” positions. On passes out of the trap, defenders close out using SET, SNUGGLE, FRONT, or SMOTHER techniques and establish final matchups.

Above the free-throw line, defenders execute an aggressive contact switch. The screener’s defender bumps and hedges into the ballhandler’s path, while the original defender positions inside the screener. The new on-ball defender denies middle penetration and quick shots, then smothers the ballhandler; the other defender denies or fronts the rolling screener, while teammates maintain weakside “I” positions.

The “All Out” disruption traps the point guard before a screen or pass, forcing the offense out of planned routes. Defenders then rotate by the near-player concept, deny return passes, protect post rolls, and apply standard SOS principles. Secondary traps are used when the ball reaches a rolling post, with subsequent rotations determined by passes, drives, and post entries. All rotations occur as the ball leaves the passer’s hands.

His Majesty requests formal recognition by the United States of his Kingdom as a sovereign, independent state, noting that prior agreements with foreign naval officers lacked governmental sanction despite tacit recognition through consuls and official dealings. He cites major reforms over twenty-three years, including a written language, widespread education, a constitutional representative monarchy, civil and criminal laws, an annual legislature, courts, jury trials, and protection of foreign persons and property. He argues that independence also benefits commercial nations because the islands are a center for whaling, lie on major routes between America and Asia, and provide advantageous vessel repairs and supplies.

Three University of Dayton students reported a naked man entering their bedrooms early Wednesday through windows or an unsecured door. One said he tried to restrain her before she escaped. The suspect, described as a white man in his mid-20s with curly brown hair, remains under investigation.

This study examines kindergarten teachers’ views on visual arts in early childhood education, including their developmental value, teaching approaches, integration into curricula, and associated challenges. Prior research identifies visual arts as supporting children’s creativity, imagination, emotional expression, communication, socialization, intellectual development, motor skills, self-esteem, cooperation, and inclusion. Effective teaching requires developmentally appropriate activities, varied materials, supportive environments, teacher training, and opportunities for independent exploration.

The study surveyed 65 public and private kindergarten teachers in Piraeus using a 21-item questionnaire. Most participants were women, held four-year degrees, had one to five years of experience, and lacked specialized visual-arts training. Data were analyzed using SPSS and thematic analysis.

Most teachers considered visual arts crucial to early childhood education and reported positive effects on creativity, imagination, intellectual development, emotional expression, social interaction, and social skills. Children’s interest and participation in art activities were generally rated high. Teachers favored free exploration, group teaching, guided discovery, varied materials, and positive feedback. Most considered visual arts satisfactorily integrated into the curriculum.

The primary reported challenges involved classroom and child management, including limited concentration, difficulty handling tools, insufficient cooperation, large classes, inadequate time, materials, equipment, and space. Suggested responses included individualized guidance, patience, rewards, role assignment, games, online demonstrations, varied techniques, continuous feedback, and flexible teaching.

The study concludes that demographic factors did not significantly influence teachers’ views. Despite broad recognition of visual arts’ importance, effective implementation requires specialized professional development, adequate resources, dedicated spaces, and support for classroom management. Limitations include electronic voluntary sampling, restricted participation to Piraeus, and limited capacity to explore perceptions in depth compared with qualitative interviews.

Hampton and Newport News police apprehended a 15-year-old after a January 31 armed robbery at a Tinee Giant. Officers found him near the suspect’s Ford SUV with a handgun and outstanding juvenile petitions. He faces firearm, concealed weapon and tobacco charges, but none directly related to the robbery.

A Sarasota couple was arrested after accepting an internationally shipped package containing carfentanil, a synthetic opioid the DEA says is 10,000 times stronger than morphine. Detectives also found over 7 grams of fentanyl, other drugs and paraphernalia. Both face drug charges; Trisha Steffes also faces an oxycodone possession charge.

Amazon selected Fidelity Investments as the new recordkeeper for its 401(k) Plan. A blackout period, expected from January 2 through the week of January 12, 2020, will restrict participant exchanges, asset allocation changes, loans, withdrawals, and distributions during the transition. Amazon also notified Section 16 officers and directors that they would face related restrictions on trading company equity securities acquired through employment or service.

The patent describes a display device with crack- or defect-sensing lines extending around the display area and, in some embodiments, through a bendable area. These lines connect input pads to switching elements and data lines used to detect cracks by observing resistance-dependent pixel illumination. Static-electricity discharge elements, such as capacitors, transistors, or diodes, are connected to the sensing lines, preferably in a central circuit area. They store or discharge accumulated static electricity, protecting sensing circuits and reducing leakage currents and false defect indications. Capacitors may connect between test data lines or between a test data line and a separate connection wire, and may comprise multiple sub-capacitors corresponding to sub-wires. Matching resistors balance normal voltage drops. During testing, intact sensing lines produce uniform low-gray pixels, while damaged or disconnected lines create visible white lines. The disclosure also details flexible substrates, switching and lighting circuits, OLED layer structures, encapsulation, touch conductors, and alternative circuit and bending-area arrangements.

Critics argue colleges lack viewpoint diversity, but definitions vary across organizations, governments and conservative commentators. The Trump administration has demanded greater diversity while offering nine universities federal grant advantages for adopting policies including bans on race- and sex-based hiring and admissions, tuition freezes, limits on international enrollment, standardized testing and a campus “marketplace of ideas.” It has also considered evaluating institutions’ “patriotic” education when awarding discretionary grants. Research indicates students may pay more to attend colleges where fewer peers oppose their political beliefs, potentially encouraging institutions to market their intellectual environments. The passage warns that tying federal funding to a political agenda could replace genuine plurality with education aligned to White House priorities.

Corey Perry’s major-junior success and prior playoff experience helped prepare him for intense situations. Though not flashy, he is effective with the puck, slippery around defenders and highly skilled. Extra players practice with the main group to support team-building and learn the expectations and lifestyle surrounding playoff pressure. An injured player remains doubtful pending medical clearance and evaluation of his hand and game readiness.

The coach emphasized strong starts, anticipating Ottawa’s physical pace and home-crowd energy. Players are urged to remain emotionally steady through success and adversity, briefly process each result, then focus on the next game. The team relies on committed leadership, collective play and players willing to sacrifice for one another. With the Stanley Cup opportunity potentially rare—even for veterans such as Teemu Selanne—the group must work hard, follow its system, stay mentally strong and respond to the game as it unfolds.

The address reports national prosperity, abundant harvests, growth in agriculture, manufacturing, commerce, and navigation, and rising public confidence and credit. Rapid subscription to the Bank of the United States is cited as evidence of confidence and community resources.

On the western frontier, peace efforts and provisional treaties with Indigenous nations were pursued before military operations were authorized against hostile groups. Kentucky militia expeditions achieved some success, while peace offers continued and some individuals accepted United States protection. The address recommends impartial justice, regulated land transfers and commerce, efforts toward civilization, and penalties for violations of Indigenous rights and treaties. Treaties with the Cherokees and Six Nations are submitted for Senate ratification.

Implementation of the distilled-spirits duties is described, including administrative arrangements and localized discontent caused by novelty and misunderstanding. Possible revisions consistent with the law’s purpose are encouraged.

A permanent federal district along the Potomac, including Alexandria and Georgetown, has been established, and a city planned. Census returns indicate a population near four million. Loans were completed or initiated in Holland, while domestic and state debt subscriptions largely fulfilled legislative objectives. Existing revenues appear sufficient without new burdens, though Congress must fund the coming year and address remaining debt.

Congress is urged to consider the militia, arsenals, fortifications, postal services and roads, a mint, uniform weights and measures, and the sale of federal lands pledged toward repayment of the public debt.

Alexander Zverev overcame Dusan Lajovic 2-6 7-5 4-6 6-1 6-2 in three hours, 24 minutes to reach the French Open third round, continuing his pursuit of a first grand slam quarterfinal. Lajovic struggled physically late, while Zverev found greater authority despite fatigue.

Grigor Dimitrov and Kei Nishikori also recovered from 2-1 set deficits to win five-set matches. Dimitrov defeated Jared Donaldson, who used underhand serves while apparently cramping, and Nishikori beat Benoit Paire. Dominic Thiem led Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-2 2-6 6-4 when darkness stopped play.

World No. 1 Simona Halep recovered from losing the opening set to defeat Alison Riske 2-6 6-1 6-1. Petra Kvitova and Elina Svitolina advanced in straight sets.

Novak Djokovic defeated qualifier Jaume Munar 7-6 6-4 6-4, saying he was gradually rebuilding confidence following elbow surgery and diminished motivation. Marco Cecchinato ended Marco Trungelliti’s run in straight sets.

Parents and caregivers can foster children’s curiosity and conversation by asking varied, open-ended questions, engaging seriously with children’s questions, modeling their own thought processes, demonstrating how to find unknown answers, and listening attentively while seeking clarification. These practices show genuine interest, normalize uncertainty and build confidence in asking and answering questions.

Foreign Relations editors have complete access to retired State Department records and special access to restricted materials at the Reagan Library and other agencies. State Department files from 1981–1989 selected for preservation will eventually be transferred to the National Archives and made accessible after declassification and processing. Although all published material is declassified, some excerpts come from documents that remain partly classified. Research also used records scanned through the Remote Archive Capture project, whose scanning methods sometimes made the status of attachments uncertain.

Documents are arranged chronologically by Washington time, with conversations dated by when they occurred. Originals are reproduced as closely as possible, preserving spelling, punctuation, abbreviations, marginalia, and formatting, while silently correcting obvious typographical errors. Bracketed text identifies corrections, additions, unrelated omissions, or still-classified material. Withheld documents and omitted passages are accounted for. Initial footnotes provide source, classification, distribution, drafting, background, and readership information.

The disclosure addresses wireless channel-status signaling after beam failure recovery in high-frequency 5G systems. A UE may temporarily decode PDCCH or PDSCH transmissions by assuming a quasi-co-located relationship with the newly selected recovery beam and reusing its spatial receive filter until updated transmission configuration indication states arrive. Alternatively, the UE may disregard prior QCL relationships and rely only on channel-specific reference signals until receiving updated configuration. Methods cover TCI-state mapping, predetermined TCI values, control/data channel relationships, access-node updates, and implementation in UEs, base stations, and computing systems. These techniques identify usable reference signals after recovery while reducing signaling overhead and improving communication performance.

This cross-sectional study examined physical activity and self-esteem among 10th- and 11th-grade students at Capa Science High School in Istanbul. Of 278 eligible students, 225 participated; 16 were excluded from metabolic equivalent analyses due to zero scores. Physical activity was measured using the IPAQ-SF, self-esteem using the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale, and height, weight, BMI, and school success were self-reported.

Participants were 71.6% male and 27.6% female. According to IPAQ-SF, 23% were inactive, 61.7% minimally active, and 15.3% health-enhancing physically active. Higher physical activity scores were weakly positively correlated with higher self-esteem. Students reporting regular exercise had higher self-esteem than those who did not. Males had higher physical activity and self-esteem scores than females. Higher self-esteem was also associated with greater self-reported school success and height, but not with BMI category. Dormitory residents had higher physical activity scores.

The findings apply to a selective science high school population and may not represent other students or regions. The cross-sectional design does not establish causality, and some measures relied on self-reports. Further research is needed to investigate causal mechanisms and sociocultural influences on the relationship between physical activity and self-esteem.

U.S. stocks were mixed after the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by a quarter-point to 1%-1.25% and said it would begin gradually reducing its $4.5 trillion balance sheet this year. The S&P 500 fell 0.4%, the Dow was nearly flat after reaching an intraday record, and the Nasdaq dropped 0.9%. Energy and materials led declines, while consumer staples and utilities gained.

Weak May inflation and retail-sales data pushed Treasury yields and the dollar lower. Oil futures fell 3.7% to $44.73 a barrel after data showed a smaller-than-expected decline in crude supplies and increases in gasoline inventories and production. Gold rose 0.6%.

Fed Chair Janet Yellen maintained that inflation should reach 2% next year. Among individual stocks, Tesla gained 0.6%, H&R Block rose 9%, and Alexion Pharmaceuticals climbed 8.7%, while oil-related shares posted steep losses. European stocks slipped, and Asian markets finished mixed.

The ADS868xW provides programmable input and AVDD alarms. Input alarm thresholds and hysteresis can support NTC thermistor temperature monitoring, where properly adjusted hysteresis reduces false alarms caused by noise near threshold limits.

The device uses independent AVDD and DVDD supplies. Recommended decoupling includes capacitors close to supply pins; proper decoupling improves power-supply rejection. Two low-power modes are available: NAP mode, which reduces internal power between conversions, and power-down mode, which disables analog blocks while retaining register contents and interface activity. Both require register configuration and specified wake-up delays.

PCB guidance includes separating analog and digital sections, routing sensitive analog signals away from digital noise, using clean, well-bypassed supplies, connecting grounds through short low-impedance paths, and placing specified ceramic capacitors close to AVDD, DVDD, REFCAP, and REFIO without intervening vias where directed.

The document lists related TI resources, update notifications, support forums, trademarks, and ESD precautions. Revision A changed ADS8685W and ADS8689W from Advance Information to Production Data. Mechanical, packaging, material, and ordering information may change. TI provides resources as-is, assigns application selection and validation responsibility to developers, limits permitted use, and applies its sales terms and warranty disclaimers.

A Toronto study of blood samples from more than 2,800 people found evidence that celiac disease affects about one per cent of the population, with roughly 90 per cent of potential cases undiagnosed. The autoimmune disease causes gluten-triggered intestinal inflammation and may impair nutrient absorption. Diagnosis is difficult because symptoms overlap with other conditions, and antibody tests can produce false positives. Testing and confirmatory duodenal biopsies should occur while patients consume gluten to avoid false negatives. Researchers cautioned that the study did not distinguish latent from active disease and may not represent all of Canada. They also noted that many people follow costly, potentially less nutritious gluten-free diets without confirmed celiac disease. The research was federally funded, and lead researcher Ahmed El-Sohemy disclosed ties to a nutritional genetic-testing company.

Schneider Electric introduced a prefabricated Edge Module for scalable, autonomous telco edge deployments. The turnkey system integrates power, cooling, software and IT components, supporting single- or three-phase power, up to 48 kW, N+1 cooling and configurable racks. EcoStruxure software enables metering, remote monitoring and control for “lights out” operation, while optional locks, cameras, lighting and card readers provide security. The module aims to standardize remote edge endpoints across locations as demand grows from 5G, IoT, autonomous vehicles and other data-intensive technologies.

The passage defines pin-state abbreviations and describes boot configuration pins multiplexed with GPMC functions. At reset, BTMODE pins select XIP pin-mux options, Ethernet PHY modes, and ARM Cortex-A8 boot configurations. After reset, these pins operate as GPMC multiplexed data/address signals. Reserved pins require proper reset handling. Internal pull states indicate pulldown, pullup, or disabled defaults.

The plaintiffs, classified as alien enemies during World War I, sought recovery of property seized by the Alien Property Custodian under the Trading with the Enemy Act. The court held that Public Resolution No. 53 postponed such recoveries while Germany remained in arrears on specified obligations. Relying on Cummings v. Deutsche Bank, it concluded that Congress could suspend the statutory recovery right because it had been granted as a matter of grace. The plaintiffs’ claim that the property was illegally seized did not distinguish their case from precedent involving unlawful withholding. The dismissal was affirmed.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for updating open-loop basal insulin parameters using automated insulin delivery records and closed-loop glucose-control outcomes. An artificial pancreas application calculates total basal and bolus insulin delivered during a selected period, determines the basal proportion, and compares it with a safety threshold. If the proportion exceeds the threshold, the system calculates a modified average basal dosage for a subsequent period and instructs a wearable pump to deliver it. Thresholds may vary based on clinical data, activity, insulin-delivery history, and time spent in hypoglycemia.

Calculations may exclude basal insulin delivered near meal boluses because post-bolus effects can affect glucose measurements and basal recommendations. Basal adjustments may use fixed modification values or coefficients and may be repeated periodically as insulin needs change. Rather than recommending a constant rate, the system may divide a day into time segments and apply clustering algorithms to delivery history to generate time-dependent basal profiles.

The drug-delivery system may include a wearable pump, continuous glucose monitor, personal diabetes management device, smart device, wireless communications, memory, processors, and cloud services. Artificial pancreas or automated insulin delivery software may run on one or more components, use glucose and user information to determine insulin delivery, maintain delivery histories, and transmit pump-control signals. The techniques may also support open-loop delivery through devices such as smart pens or syringes and may be implemented in hardware, software, or non-transitory computer-readable media.

OpenAI unveiled an Apps SDK that lets developers embed third-party applications directly within ChatGPT, aiming to make it a platform or chat-driven operating system. Demonstrations included Canva creating business materials and Zillow displaying and filtering home listings. Distribution is initially limited to major partners, while future plans include app monetization and instant checkout within ChatGPT.

OpenAI also introduced AgentKit for building AI agents and made its Codex coding model generally available, alongside Slack integration, an SDK, and usage analytics. The company is competing with Google, Anthropic, Amazon, Meta, and DeepSeek for developers while expanding its models, APIs, agent tools, and data-center infrastructure. OpenAI says its broader goal is to develop a “super assistant” that guides users across apps and websites rather than keeping them exclusively within ChatGPT.

U.S. stocks fell sharply Friday as strong employment and wage growth fueled inflation and interest-rate concerns, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to its highest since January 2014. The Dow dropped 665.75 points, or 2.54%, its largest point decline since December 2008. The S&P 500 lost 2.12% and Nasdaq fell 1.96%, giving major indexes their worst weekly losses in two years. All S&P sectors declined, led by technology, while volatility reached its highest level since November 2016. Exxon, Chevron, Alphabet and Apple fell following disappointing results or outlooks, while Amazon gained after strong earnings. Despite the rout, some market participants viewed the decline as an overdue pullback rather than the end of the bull market.

Tail risk refers to rare, extreme outcomes occurring more frequently than a normal distribution suggests. Left-tail events can cause severe portfolio losses, particularly with leverage or negatively skewed strategies. Hedging aims to limit losses, support long-term survival, and reduce behavioral mistakes during market declines.

Suggested hedges include out-of-the-money put options, foreign assets, cash and bonds, Cambria’s TAIL ETF, diversified portfolios such as Ray Dalio’s All Weather Portfolio, and trend-following strategies. These may reduce drawdowns and perform well during crises but generally lower long-term returns through ongoing insurance costs. Cambria’s TAIL ETF gained during several market selloffs but had negative returns since inception through the period discussed. The appropriate balance between protection and returns depends on individual circumstances and preferences.

Champions League holders Real Madrid drew Paris Saint-Germain in the last 16. Other ties include Chelsea-Barcelona, Basel-Manchester City, Bayern Munich-Besiktas, Juventus-Tottenham, Sevilla-Manchester United, Porto-Liverpool and Shakhtar Donetsk-Roma. Matches run from February 13 to March 14.

Artificial intelligence, particularly generative and agentic AI, is transforming legal practice. Generative AI creates content such as documents and legal arguments, while agentic AI analyzes information, makes predictions and offers recommendations.

AI can help lawyers review documents, conduct legal research, draft materials, communicate with clients, brainstorm and manage workflows. Tools including Vincent AI, Copilot, ChatGPT, built-in legal software features and custom systems can improve efficiency and client service. Examples include identifying useful deposition quotes, researching legal issues, drafting motions and client responses, and providing automated legal assistance.

AI is not appropriate for every task, and work requiring nuanced judgment or creative problem-solving may remain better suited to humans. Lawyers should assess whether AI is the best tool for a particular job and use paid versions when entering client information. A subsequent column will address effective AI integration and future developments.

The Minnesota Wild signed Kirill Kaprizov, 28, to an NHL-record eight-year, $136 million extension through 2033-34. Beginning next season, the deal carries a record $17 million annual value and includes substantial signing bonuses in its first four years.

Kaprizov recorded 25 goals and 31 assists in 41 regular-season games in 2024-25 despite missing 40 games with a lower-body injury requiring surgery. Over five Wild seasons, he has 185 goals and 386 points, holds several franchise single-season records, and won the 2020-21 Calder Trophy. He added nine points in Minnesota’s six-game playoff loss to Vegas.

The agreement followed prolonged negotiations in which Kaprizov rejected a $16 million annual offer. It will be among the NHL’s final eight-year extensions because the new collective bargaining agreement will reduce maximum contract terms. Minnesota has gone 10 consecutive seasons without winning a playoff series.
