A Tom Thomson sketch once given as a gag gift sold for $481,250 at Heffel’s Toronto auction. The 118-work sale raised $14.1 million, led by Paul-Emile Borduas’s “Figures schematiques” at a record $3.6 million. Works by Lawren Harris, A.J. Casson, Jack Bush and Jean Paul Lemieux also exceeded estimates or set records.

Photographer Mark Bickerdike documented young and adult musicians attending 10-week RockJam courses at Ricky’s School of Rock in Linthwaite. Over several years and around 50 gigs, he photographed pupils learning songs and performing for family and friends. Founder Ricky Comiskey said the courses built confidence and inspired many pupils to form bands, including Bickerdike’s son Tom, who joined Fading Sunlight. Comiskey praised the photographs for chronicling participants’ development.

The thesis examines digital services in event management and proposes a mobile application offering event information and sensor-based services, such as locating facilities and viewing stages through drone cameras.

It distinguishes e-business, which encompasses electronically supported business processes, from e-commerce, which concerns online buying and selling. Digital business creates new value by connecting people, businesses and things. Benefits include efficiency, reduced bureaucracy and cloud-based infrastructure, while risks include market consolidation, income disparity and cybersecurity threats. Common protections include antivirus software, firewalls, encryption and digital certificates. Relevant technologies include cloud computing, Web 2.0, the Internet of Things and mobile systems.

Researchers evaluated 200 event-management websites—17 Croatian and 183 from eight other countries—between August 1 and September 15, 2017. Each site was assessed against 103 Boolean criteria covering content, social networks, public relations and support, multimedia and mobile technologies, user experience and technical specifications.

Foreign websites commonly provided terms and conditions, privacy policies, newsletters, social-media links and customer support. Facebook, Twitter and LinkedIn were the most prevalent social networks, while all foreign sites had blogs, though only 78% were current. All used photos and logos; 86% used animations and 19% used video. Among foreign sites, 78% loaded within three seconds, 73% had homepages under 5 MB and 56% achieved performance scores above 80%. All used HTML and Java, while only 4% used HTTPS.

The results indicate substantial room for improvement among Croatian organizations: the highest-ranked Croatian website placed 40th, and the lowest placed last. Recommended priorities include faster loading, removal of unnecessary content, stronger social-media activity, better mobile support, more independent applications and effective multimedia use. The study was limited to selected countries; future research should examine customer perspectives and relationships between marketing and event-management strategies.

Southwest Airlines employee asked UC Berkeley basketball coach Lindsay Gottlieb to prove she was the mother of her biracial 1-year-old son, requesting a birth certificate and later a Facebook post despite his passport. Gottlieb called the incident demeaning and suspected race, rather than their different surnames, prompted the questioning. Southwest apologized for her discomfort and said its policy requires verifying that lap children are under two, though domestic travel does not require matching surnames. The airline said it would reinforce proper policy with the employee. Social media reactions were divided; model Chrissy Teigen defended such checks as precautions against child trafficking.

Nigeria’s annual inflation fell to 16.25% in May 2017 from 17.28% in April, while monthly inflation rose to 1.88%. Food inflation eased slightly to 19.27%, with higher prices for meat, cereals, fish, potatoes, dairy products, eggs and vegetables.

OPEC and non-OPEC producers plan to announce a strategy in June for eventually ending supply cuts, though UAE Energy Minister Suhail al-Mazroui stressed the pact would not necessarily end then. The agreement cuts supply by about 1.8 million barrels daily to support prices. Russia favors a clear, gradual withdrawal to avoid market deficits, rapid price increases and higher U.S. shale output. Russian Energy Minister Alexander Novak said exiting could take three to six months, depending on market conditions and crude demand.

The VIX measures implied volatility in S&P 500 index options and usually moves inversely to the stock market. As a mean-reversion indicator, a rising VIX may signal an opportunity to buy stocks, while a falling VIX may suggest selling. One tested strategy buys SPY or ES when VIX crosses its upper Bollinger Band and exits after two rising days. Although simple VIX strategies may work, traders should conduct their own backtesting because the indicator and market are complex.

Box reported a smaller-than-expected quarterly loss, revenue of $140.5 million, and billings of $116.7 million, all beating estimates. It added 3,000 paying customers and issued second-quarter guidance above forecasts. Despite strong results, shares fell 4.6% after hours.

The paper presents an exact algorithm for computing Nash equilibria in multiplayer imperfect-information games. It generalizes the sequence-form representation to multiple players, formulates equilibrium conditions as a nonlinear complementarity problem, and converts them into a quadratically constrained feasibility program solvable with nonconvex quadratic optimization.

Using Gurobi, the method outperformed a direct mixed-integer bilinear formulation on tested random multiplayer strategic-form games. On reduced three-player Kuhn poker, after removing dominated actions, it computed an essentially exact equilibrium in 2.47 seconds, with maximum deviation gain of \(1.4\times10^{-17}\). Gambit’s only successful applicable method, logit quantal-response-equilibrium tracing, took 43 seconds and produced an approximation with maximum deviation gain of \(1.667\times10^{-5}\).

The new method could not solve full three-player Kuhn poker within 24 hours, whereas logit tracing solved it in several minutes. The results indicate that removing dominated actions can substantially improve performance. The proposed approach is best suited to exact equilibrium computation in smaller games, while logit QRE tracing may be more scalable for moderate games and iterative self-play methods remain practical for very large games despite lacking convergence guarantees.

Cette étude qualitative examine les défis anticipés et les besoins de formation de 18 futurs enseignants québécois d’éducation physique et à la santé, répartis en quatre groupes de discussion. Les principaux défis généraux relevés sont la gestion de classe et le manque de motivation des élèves. Concernant spécifiquement la motivation, les participants mentionnent l’hétérogénéité des capacités, intérêts et personnalités, la conception d’activités motivantes, l’engagement des élèves, la gestion des élèves désengagés et les différences entre les sexes.

Les participants souhaitent apprendre à intégrer les stratégies motivationnelles à leur planification, obtenir des exemples concrets de mise en œuvre et bénéficier de davantage d’occasions de pratique. L’étude recommande d’établir des liens explicites entre les processus motivationnels et les contenus déjà enseignés, notamment la planification, l’évaluation, la didactique et la gestion de classe. Elle souligne aussi l’importance d’adapter les activités aux besoins psychologiques d’autonomie, de compétence et d’appartenance des élèves, ainsi que de favoriser un climat axé sur la progression personnelle.

Les résultats suggèrent que les programmes québécois actuels ne répondent pas pleinement aux besoins exprimés, particulièrement pour développer la nouvelle compétence professionnelle liée au soutien de la motivation à apprendre. L’échantillon restreint et exclusivement québécois limite toutefois la représentativité des conclusions.

The lecture develops the AdS/CFT operator–field mapping. Boundary operators correspond to bulk gravity fields with matching quantum numbers, while boundary values of bulk fields act as sources deforming the boundary theory.

In semiclassical gravity at large \(N\), Newton’s constant is small. After canonical normalization, nonlinear bulk interactions are suppressed by powers of the gravitational coupling, so leading fluctuations can be treated as free fields. For a massive scalar in AdS, the near-boundary solution has two behaviors:
\[
\phi(z,x)\sim A(x)z^{d-\Delta}+B(x)z^\Delta,
\]
with \(\Delta\) determined by the bulk mass. Stability requires real exponents, giving the BF bound; unlike Minkowski space, AdS permits some negative mass-squared values because curvature prevents constant modes.

Boundary conditions select the modes used in canonical quantization. In standard quantization, the \(B\)-mode is normalizable and the \(A\)-mode is treated as non-normalizable. When both are mathematically normalizable, alternative quantization can interchange their roles. Normalizable modes represent states in the boundary theory, while non-normalizable modes determine sources and therefore deform the theory itself. Solutions differing only in normalizable modes describe different states of one theory; those differing in non-normalizable modes describe different theories.

A scaling argument shows that, in standard quantization, \(\Delta\) is the scaling dimension of the dual operator and satisfies the scalar mass–dimension relation. Massless scalars correspond to marginal operators, negative mass-squared fields to relevant operators, and positive mass-squared fields to irrelevant operators. Alternative quantization assigns dimension \(d-\Delta\).

Bulk gauge fields correspond to conserved currents of dimension \(d-1\), while metric perturbations correspond to the stress tensor of dimension \(d\). Finally, the boundary generating functional equals the gravity partition function with specified non-normalizable boundary data. In the semiclassical limit, the gravity path integral is evaluated by the saddle-point approximation using the Euclidean action of the classical solution satisfying those boundary conditions.

QuantifiedStrategies.com offers TradingView strategies translated into Pine Script upon request. Users can browse available strategies, select desired ones, and subscribe for availability notifications. The site notes that trading involves risk and past performance does not guarantee future results.

Thomas Scullun contracted to command the American whaling bark Cape Horn Pigeon, receiving one-twelfth of the voyage’s net proceeds. The vessel, carrying 44 men, cleared San Francisco on December 7, 1891, for a whaling voyage. Scullun swore that its cargo manifest was complete, lawful, and intended for whaling. On August 20 (September 10), 1892, Russian naval Lieutenant von Cube encountered the vessel near the Sea of Okhotsk. Suspecting from its log and charts that it had entered Aniva and Patience bays, where foreign fishing was prohibited, he took it to Vladivostok for investigation. Although the commission found that the vessel had navigated within Russian territorial waters, it found no grounds for confiscation, deemed the arrest a misunderstanding, and promptly returned the vessel to its owners.

Dusty Baker supports former Giants second baseman Jeff Kent’s Hall of Fame candidacy. Despite 377 home runs, eight 100-RBI seasons and the 2002 NL MVP award, Kent has received about 15 percent of votes, far below the 75-percent election threshold. Kent suggested advanced metrics and media friction may be factors.

Former Burlington College president Carol Moore blamed the school’s closure on a $10 million land purchase championed by Jane Sanders despite low enrollment and a $4 million budget. Federal authorities are examining whether Sanders accurately represented donations securing the loan. Moore also criticized an agreement with a woodworking school connected to Sanders’ stepdaughter, Carina Driscoll.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth summoned hundreds of generals and admirals worldwide to advocate reshaping a military he described as soft and “woke.” New York Times Pentagon reporter Greg Jaffe discusses the speech.

The patent application describes an auditory-based digital assistant for media exploration, particularly on devices with limited or no displays. The assistant can refine media searches from speech received during playback, combine spoken responses with related media, offer alternatives until non-affirmative responses reach a threshold, then request further input, and merge multiple present users’ preference profiles to select media.

These methods are implemented through electronic devices, processor-executable programs, and non-transitory storage media. They aim to provide flexible, natural interactions, reduce repeated inputs and user mistakes, improve content selection, and lower power use. The described system may use client-server or standalone architectures and supports varied devices, networks, sensors, audio interfaces, touch controls, applications, contextual information, and event-handling components.

In Simmonds v. Simmonds, decided March 9, 1904, the appellee recovered 117½ acres in Bell County and rents. His title rested on a duplicate headright certificate issued to Willard Chamberlain, the resulting state patent, an 1850 transfer executed by Louis C. Clemons as Chamberlain’s agent to Joseph P. Sneed, and Sneed’s 1860 deed to appellee. Appellant presented no paper title, relying on alleged defects in appellee’s proof and the ten-year limitations statute.

The court held that the certificate transfer was admissible as an ancient instrument because it was genuine, more than thirty years old, came from proper custody, had long supported a claim of title, and bore no suspicious circumstances. These facts also created a conclusive presumption that Clemons had authority to act for Chamberlain. The transfer sufficiently identified Chamberlain’s one-third-league headright certificate despite omitting its number and date.

The court properly excluded a Land Office copy of a third party’s affidavit claiming ownership of the certificate and evidence of a later augmentation certificate, which did not undermine identification of the transferred certificate. It also properly refused evidence of appellant’s reputation for truth and honesty because conflicting testimony alone did not place his character at issue. Finding the jury instructions proper and the evidence sufficient, the court affirmed the judgment.

Configure the circuit to output logic high when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1 V. Use a low-ESR 0.1-µF ceramic bypass capacitor close to each device’s supply and ground pins. Maintain stable, low-noise supplies, solid grounding, and recommended input ranges. Minimize input-output coupling, place input resistors near the device, and optionally add a series output resistor below 100 Ω to reduce ringing.

Qualcomm accidentally revealed the Asus Zenfone AR ahead of CES 2017. It would be the second consumer Google Tango smartphone and the first to support both Tango augmented reality and Google’s Daydream View virtual reality headset. The phone uses a Snapdragon 821 processor, while leaked renders were posted by Evan Blass. Pricing and availability remained unknown. Asus also teased another Zenfone possibly featuring the Snapdragon 835.

The IMF urged Ukraine to reform its loss-making pension system, which supports 30 percent of the population. Mission chief Ron van Rooden said Ukrainians retire about five years earlier than the EU average and suggested limiting early retirement and pursuing employers that evade pension taxes. Ukraine, seeking $4.5 billion in IMF funding, has resisted raising retirement ages because of public and parliamentary opposition. The country needs financial assistance while recovering from recession and conflict-related economic damage.

The 20-day exponential moving average strategy buys when price rises above the 20 EMA and sells when it falls below, using recent prices to identify short-term swings. A backtest on SPY produced low CAGR despite roughly 70% market exposure and a significant drawdown. Adding an undisclosed indicator improved risk-adjusted performance to nearly match buy-and-hold CAGR, though drawdown remained unchanged. The basic strategy performed better on Bitcoin from 2014 onward, attributed in the passage to Bitcoin’s periodic momentum.

Iron sulfate heptahydrate, or ferrous sulfate heptahydrate, copperas, or green vitriol, is a water- and acid-soluble co-product of titanium dioxide manufacturing and can also be obtained by cooling hot sulfate solutions. It contains 18%–20% iron and up to 3% free acid; its crystals may clump, create dust, and release acidic liquid that damages storage containers. It is used to treat iron deficiency and iron chlorosis, purify water and sewage, prevent eutrophication, reduce chromium ions in cement, and supply iron in agriculture. Historical uses include textile dye fixation, leather blackening, and ink production.

NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the 7nm Ampere GA100 architecture, targets AI and HPC workloads. The A100 implementation includes 108 streaming multiprocessors, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, five HBM2 stacks, 40 GB of memory, and 1,555 GB/s bandwidth. Its 40 MB L2 cache is 6.7 times larger than V100’s, while combined L1 cache and shared memory reaches 192 KB per SM.

Third-generation Tensor Cores provide twice the dense Tensor throughput per SM of V100 and support FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. A100 delivers up to 312 TFLOPS of dense FP16/FP32 mixed-precision performance and 19.5 TFLOPS of FP64 performance. TF32 accelerates FP32-based AI training without script changes, while FP16 or BF16 mixed precision provides higher throughput. Fine-grained 2:4 structured sparsity compresses weights and doubles Tensor Core throughput by skipping zero values, with NVIDIA reporting virtually no inference-accuracy loss after pruning and fine-tuning across evaluated networks.

Memory and execution improvements include direct asynchronous copies from global to shared memory, hardware-accelerated asynchronous barriers, L2 residency controls, compute-data compression, simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, improved atomic operations, and hardware warp reductions. CUDA 11 exposes these capabilities and supports CUDA Task Graphs, which define workflows once and execute them repeatedly, reducing CPU launch overhead and grid-to-grid latency. A100 hardware further accelerates graph launches and dependency handling.

Multi-Instance GPU technology partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances. Each instance receives dedicated compute resources and isolated memory-system paths, providing predictable quality of service, fault isolation, and support for virtual machines, containers, and multiple users. Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances and support Multi-Process Service functionality.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth per A100, twice V100’s total. PCIe Gen 4 supplies 31.5 GB/s per direction for x16 connections and supports SR-IOV. Additional hardware includes five NVDEC video decoders, a five-core NVJPG JPEG decoder, an optical-flow accelerator, ECC protection, and enhanced error detection, containment, and recovery.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs, six NVSwitches, 4.8 TB/s aggregate bidirectional interconnect bandwidth, and up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance. MIG can expose up to 56 isolated accelerators in one DGX A100. The system uses NVIDIA’s CUDA, container, NGC, deep-learning, inference, analytics, and HPC software stack and can scale to large clusters.

Amazon’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2019 reported net sales of $59.7 billion, up 17% from $51.0 billion in Q1 2018. Operating income increased from $1.9 billion to $4.4 billion, while net income rose from $1.6 billion to $3.6 billion. Diluted earnings per share increased from $3.27 to $7.09.

North America sales rose 17% to $35.8 billion and operating income doubled to $2.3 billion. International sales increased 9% to $16.2 billion, while its operating loss narrowed from $622 million to $90 million. AWS sales grew 41% to $7.7 billion and operating income increased to $2.2 billion. Growth reflected increased unit sales, third-party seller activity, advertising, and AWS customer usage.

Operating cash flow was $1.8 billion for the quarter and $34.4 billion for the trailing twelve months. Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow increased to $23.0 billion. Q1 investing cash outflow was $8.1 billion, largely reflecting securities purchases and acquisitions, while financing cash outflow was $2.4 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $37.0 billion at March 31, 2019.

Total assets were $178.1 billion, liabilities included $63.7 billion of current liabilities and $33.3 billion of long-term lease liabilities, and stockholders’ equity was $48.4 billion. Amazon adopted new lease guidance, recognizing approximately $21 billion of operating lease assets and liabilities. Total contractual commitments were $131.3 billion, and unsecured senior notes outstanding totaled $24.3 billion.

The company disclosed ongoing tax disputes, indirect-tax claims, sanctions-related reviews, and patent litigation, stating that outcomes could materially affect particular periods. Amazon said operating cash flows, available investments, and borrowing arrangements were expected to meet anticipated operating cash needs for at least twelve months.

Damian Lillard scored 32 points and became the fastest player in Portland franchise history to reach 10,000 career points, but Toronto defeated the Trail Blazers 130-105, ending their four-game winning streak. DeMar DeRozan led Toronto with 35 points and matched his career high with six 3-pointers. The Raptors made a season-high 19 3-pointers, led 74-52 at halftime and improved their NBA-best home record to 20-4. CJ McCollum scored 21 and Jusuf Nurkic 20 for Portland. Toronto has beaten Portland six straight times.

The 1825 treaty between Russia and Great Britain protected navigation, fishing, and trade with Indigenous peoples throughout the Pacific, subject to specified restrictions. The Paris arbitration tribunal found that although Russia’s 1821 ukase claimed jurisdiction 100 Italian miles from its shores in the Bering Sea, subsequent treaties limited jurisdiction to cannon-shot range, and Russia exercised no exclusive sealing rights beyond territorial waters before Alaska’s cession. The passage argues that because the tribunal treated the Bering Sea as part of the Pacific, the same reasoning applies to the Okhotsk Sea. Citing F. de Martens and Vattel, it states that seas connected to oceans remain open to all nations, even when surrounded by one state, and that no state may claim expansive seas, restrict peaceful fishing and navigation, enforce its laws against foreign vessels, or treat ice as territory.

Harvey Weinstein was indicted on first- and third-degree rape and first-degree criminal sexual act charges involving two women. He declined to testify before the grand jury on his lawyers’ advice, citing insufficient preparation time. Manhattan District Attorney Cyrus Vance Jr said the case would be tried in court, not through the press.

Coach Quenneville discussed lineup adjustments, player matchups, and the importance of balanced play with and without the puck. He praised Johnny’s all-zone impact despite reduced scoring, Dunks’ conditioning and ability to handle heavy minutes, and Bolly’s defensive reliability, offensive skill, and comfort with greater responsibility. He emphasized contributions across four lines, improved defense, strong goaltending, and team consistency.

Quenneville described Chicago as a special sports city and expressed appreciation for the Blackhawks organization. He acknowledged coaching’s limited job security and reviewed the team’s progress, adversity against Detroit, and improvement through the playoffs. He said extra rest was beneficial before a busy schedule and noted concerns about two overtime too-many-men penalties.

He praised Corey’s consistency, composure, and development as a top goaltender, as well as his supportive partnership with Ray Emery. Quenneville also commended Shaw’s competitiveness and willingness to play near the net, discussed contact with other Chicago coaches, and highlighted the team’s ability to generate momentum even when offensive production was limited.

The lecture explains the asymptotic equipartition property (AEP) for discrete memoryless sources. For long sequences, the sample average of the negative log probability approaches entropy. Consequently, the typical set has probability approaching one, contains approximately \(2^{nH(X)}\) sequences, and each typical sequence has probability approximately \(2^{-nH(X)}\). This establishes entropy as the fundamental source-coding rate: rates near \(H(X)\) are achievable with rare failures, while rates below \(H(X)\) yield error probability approaching one.

Because memoryless sources are limited models, the lecture introduces Markov sources, where transitions depend on the preceding state and outputs label state transitions. Ergodic Markov chains are accessible, aperiodic, stationary, and have unique steady-state probabilities approached from any initial state. Their coding performance is governed by conditional entropy \(H(X\mid S)\). Using separate single-symbol prefix codes may provide little compression for small alphabets, but block coding can approach \(H(X\mid S)\), and rates below it are unattainable asymptotically.

The lecture then presents Lempel–Ziv universal compression, which requires no predefined probability model and asymptotically matches the best coding rate for a Markov source while also adapting to other statistical structures. LZ77 maintains a sliding window of previously encoded symbols, finds the longest match for the upcoming string, and transmits the match length and location. Match lengths use a unary-binary prefix-free code, while locations require \(\log W\) bits for window size \(W\). Typical-set reasoning suggests a match length near \(\log W/H(X\mid S)\), producing an asymptotic rate near \(H(X\mid S)\). Larger windows improve matching but require more processing and adapt more slowly when statistics change.

Speaking at West Point near the end of his presidency, President Bush emphasized the Commander in Chief’s responsibility and the continuing need for U.S. global leadership after the Cold War. Although democratic governments and arms-control agreements had reduced major threats, he warned that dictatorships, weapons of mass destruction, regional aggression, and terrorism remained dangers. He rejected both isolationism and the role of America as universal policeman, advocating leadership through diplomatic, economic, moral, and, when necessary, military means.

Bush cited Kuwait, Iraq, Somalia, Panama, and the Philippines as examples of U.S. action, while explaining restraint in the former Yugoslavia. He argued that decisions to use force require case-by-case judgment rather than rigid rules. Force should serve significant interests, be effective when alternatives are inadequate, remain limited in scope and duration, and offer benefits proportionate to costs. Military operations should have clear, achievable missions, realistic plans, withdrawal criteria, and broad international participation when possible, though the United States may sometimes act alone.

He stressed that effective leadership requires congressional and public support, allied military and financial contributions, and capable forces prepared for varied contingencies. He praised the U.S. military’s strength, training, merit-based advancement, discipline, diversity, compassion, and volunteer character, crediting service members for success abroad.

Addressing the cadets, Bush described military service as an honorable commitment to duty, sacrifice, and purposes beyond personal interest. He connected their choice with broader traditions of public service and recalled enlisting in the Navy on his eighteenth birthday during World War II. He concluded that the cadets were entering a promising new world whose development would require their leadership and service.

The lower 32 kB flash supports higher endurance for EEPROM emulation. Erase limits count sector or bank erases; word lines require erasure after maximum writes. Programming times end when completion flags are set.

The article traces Enron’s transformation from a debt-burdened pipeline company into a dominant energy trader under Ken Lay and Jeff Skilling. Skilling introduced the Gas Bank, expanded trading into electricity and other commodities, and promoted rapid growth, aggressive hiring, large performance bonuses, and forced employee rankings. Enron later pursued online trading, broadband, international power projects, and water privatization while using extensive mark-to-market accounting and booking projected profits upfront.

The company’s culture increasingly emphasized immediate profits, internal competition, secrecy, and dismissing low-ranked employees. Costly international projects, California’s energy crisis, the telecommunications collapse, criticism of Enron’s accounting, and doubts about its earnings weakened investor confidence. Enron’s stock fell sharply in 2001, and Skilling resigned after six months as CEO, citing personal sacrifices and family priorities. Lay returned as CEO, pledged to focus innovation closer to Enron’s core business, and acknowledged that its performance-review system had damaged morale.

Vertex Resource Group acquired an Edmonton-area hydro-vac services business for $4.3 million. The deal, closed June 30, 2018, adds 11 units, doubles Vertex’s hydro-vac fleet, expands services into Edmonton’s municipal and utility markets, and is expected to generate approximately $5 million in annual revenue. The acquired company’s management and operators joined Vertex. Revenue expectations are forward-looking and subject to risks and uncertainties.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture introduces major improvements in memory, storage I/O, graphics, AI, professional computing, displays, and video processing. GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling to transmit two bits per clock edge, with Maximum Transition Avoidance encoding and additional signal-training techniques improving reliability. At up to 19.5 Gbps, it provides 936 GB/s peak bandwidth on the GeForce RTX 3090.

NVIDIA RTX IO works with Microsoft DirectStorage to transfer compressed data from NVMe SSDs to GPUs for asynchronous, GPU-based lossless decompression. This reduces CPU utilization, improves I/O performance, accelerates loading and asset streaming, and benefits games and professional workloads involving large datasets.

Ampere provides up to twice the performance in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Second-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection performance and support motion blur, while third-generation Tensor Cores use structural sparsity to increase effective throughput. The RTX 3090 includes 24 GB of GDDR6X memory, while the RTX 3070 uses GDDR6 and lacks NVLink.

The data-center-oriented NVIDIA A40 offers up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to five times the AI throughput of the Quadro RTX 6000, or ten times with sparsity. It includes 48 GB of memory, expandable to 96 GB through NVLink, PCIe Gen4, virtualization support, and compatibility with NVIDIA EGX. The RTX A6000 similarly offers 48 GB of GDDR6, expandable to 96 GB, for professional rendering, AI, and scientific workloads.

Ampere supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 4K at 120 Hz, and 8K at 60 Hz. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware decoding for codecs including AV1, enabling up to 8K60 HDR playback with low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

Error Detection and Replay protects GDDR6X transfers by retrying corrupted transactions. During overclocking, increasing retries reduces useful bandwidth and causes performance to plateau before instability, helping users identify memory limits. NVIDIA states that specifications may change, products require suitability testing, and the materials are provided without warranties.

Addressing the Foreign Service Institute, the speaker defines diplomacy’s central task as building peace through reason, moderation, and international cooperation. Europe’s recovery since 1945 is attributed to common action, interdependent institutions, and collective security, particularly through NATO.

NATO is described as a living institution that must adapt through consultation among its members rather than through isolation or dismantlement. Its integrated military strength and political unity have deterred war by demonstrating collective readiness and making aggression too costly. Independent national action and loosely coordinated forces contributed to two world wars, while collective action has maintained Atlantic security since 1945.

The United States remains committed to strengthening NATO with its allies and hopes withdrawn members will resume mutual responsibilities. Atlantic unity, grounded in shared values, economic and military strength, and peaceful purpose, also offers hope for reconciliation between Western and Eastern Europe. The speaker urges future diplomats to preserve human solidarity, reject destructive national rivalries, and promote unity as the foundation of security and welfare.

On June 24, 2020, Tesla entered a 90-day agreement under which CEO Elon Musk will personally provide up to $100 million in directors’ and officers’ indemnity coverage when Tesla cannot indemnify claims. Tesla will pay Musk $972,361, potentially adjusted based on a discounted, prorated market insurance quote. During this period, Tesla will evaluate longer-term coverage options.

The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card is designed for paying down debt or financing large purchases. It offers 0% introductory APR for 21 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74%. It has no annual fee and includes up to $600 in cellphone protection, subject to a $25 deductible.

The card offers no ongoing rewards, charges a 5% balance-transfer fee with a $5 minimum, and has a 3% foreign transaction fee. Applicants are generally recommended to have good or excellent credit, though approval is not guaranteed. Motley Fool Money named it its Best 0% Intro APR Card of 2025 and notes that advertiser compensation may influence offer placement but not product ratings or recommendations.

Sony confirmed the Xperia XZ Premium will receive Android Oreo later in 2017, adding the 3D Creator scanning app, smile-detecting predictive capture, and a 10-frames-per-second burst mode with autofocus tracking. No exact release date was announced.

Microsoft’s fiscal 2019 Form 10-K describes its mission to empower people and organizations through software, cloud services, devices, business applications, gaming, advertising, and consulting. Its strategy centers on productivity and business processes, intelligent cloud and edge platforms, and personal computing, supported by investments in AI, mixed reality, IoT, cloud infrastructure, research, and product development.

Microsoft reports three segments: Productivity and Business Processes, including Office, LinkedIn, and Dynamics; Intelligent Cloud, including Azure, server products, GitHub, and enterprise services; and More Personal Computing, including Windows, Surface, Xbox, and search advertising. Products are distributed through OEMs, direct sales, distributors, resellers, digital marketplaces, and retail stores under varied licensing and subscription programs.

Microsoft completed its GitHub acquisition in October 2018 and continues integrating cloud, AI, collaboration, security, and developer tools. It employed approximately 144,000 full-time workers as of June 30, 2019, including 85,000 in the United States.

The filing identifies risks involving intense competition, cloud execution, acquisitions, cybersecurity, privacy, harmful online content, AI and IoT, service outages, product quality, supply chains, intellectual property, litigation, regulation, anti-corruption compliance, and uncertain returns on investments. As of December 31, 2018, non-affiliate market value was $769.6 billion; 7.64 billion shares were outstanding as of July 29, 2019.

The work establishes a fine-grained hierarchy of quantum replica advantage. For any integer \(k\ge2\), estimating nonlinear observables such as \(\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{k}O)\) can require exponentially many samples when measurements jointly access fewer than \(k\) replicas, while \(k\)-replica measurements achieve constant sample complexity for constant \(k\). For estimating \(\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{k+1}O)\), \(k\)-replica protocols require \(\Omega(\sqrt d/(k\varepsilon^{1/(k+1)}))\) samples under stated conditions, whereas \((k+1)\)-replica protocols use \(O(k/\varepsilon^2)\). A \(\lceil(k+1)/2\rceil\)-replica protocol achieves \(\widetilde O(\max\{k\sqrt d/\varepsilon,k/\varepsilon^2\})\), showing the \(\sqrt d\) dependence is optimal.

The main lower-bound tool is an indistinguishability principle for Haar-assembled ensembles—mixtures and tensor products constructed from independent Haar-random states. Such ensembles are difficult for single-replica protocols to distinguish from their averages. The proof uses Haar integration, permutation operators, concentration of measure, one-sided likelihood ratios, and product-structured POVMs.

Hard instances are built from probability distributions whose moments agree through degree \(k\) but differ at degree \(k+1\). Their associated Haar-random state mixtures have matching \(k\)-copy averages and are therefore hard for \(k\)-replica protocols to distinguish, while their \((k+1)\)-degree properties differ. Chebyshev polynomials provide the required moment gap.

The principle also yields lower bounds for spectrum and rank testing. If two spectra agree on moments through degree \(k\) and each has at most \(m\) nonzero entries, \(k\)-replica spectrum testing requires \(\Omega(\sqrt d/(m\sqrt{\ln m}))\) samples. Rank testing and estimation of noninteger powers \(\operatorname{tr}(\rho^\alpha)\) consequently acquire unavoidable dimension-dependent lower bounds under bounded-replica measurements.

Open directions include improving error dependence, identifying the precise error threshold between hard and easy regimes, extending indistinguishability results to Haar-random unitary conjugations of fixed spectra, and finding tasks that remain exponentially hard when protocols are constrained by working-qubit capacity even with sequential state resetting.

AGNC Investment is presented as a leading mortgage REIT with a 14%+ yield. Recent and expected Fed rate cuts may lower financing costs and increase mortgage-backed securities valuations. AGNC reported its third consecutive quarter of positive net interest income in Q2 2025 and trades above book value. The author maintains a bullish rating, owns AGNC and Annaly securities, and notes the article reflects personal opinion rather than investment advice.

A penalty-kick shoot-out determines the winner of a match tied after regulation and any extra time when competition rules require one. Under IFAB Law 10, eligible players are generally those on the field when play ended. Teams alternate five kicks from the penalty mark, unless an insurmountable lead is reached earlier. If still tied, equal pairs of kicks continue in sudden death until one team scores and the other misses.

The referee selects the goal when necessary, conducts coin tosses for the goal and kicking order, enforces Laws 10 and 14, and records results. Each eligible player must kick before anyone takes a second kick. If teams have unequal numbers because of dismissals or injuries, the larger team reduces its eligible participants accordingly. Eligible players may act as goalkeeper; an injured goalkeeper may be replaced under specified substitution rules. A kick ends when the ball’s motion is complete and may count after rebounds involving the goalkeeper, posts, or crossbar.

Shoot-out goals are recorded separately from individual statistics, such as 1-1 (4-3). Coaches should understand competition modifications, select and rank likely kickers, practice the complete procedure under pressure, analyze opponents, prepare goalkeepers, and ensure preferred kickers remain on the field. During and after the shoot-out, coaches should maintain calm, support players, preserve morale, and review performance for future improvement.

Andrea Conti’s agent said the Atalanta wing-back only wants to join Milan and urged the clubs to negotiate. He argued coach Gian Piero Gasperini should not block Conti’s desired transfer, citing the player’s professional and economic ambitions.

A loaf-sized, remote-controlled swimming robot will inspect Fukushima Dai-Ichi’s Unit 3 containment vessel in July. Equipped with cameras, lights and a radiation detector, it will assess structural damage and search radioactive water for melted fuel. Developed by Toshiba and a government institute, the probe follows earlier robots that failed due to damage and extreme radiation. Its findings are intended to support safe fuel removal and long-term decommissioning.

Patrick Sutherland challenged the denial of parole, arguing that the Board relied on erroneous criminal-history information from his presentence report. Because he had not timely disputed or sought correction of that report and did not refute the incident before the Board, he could not contest the Board’s reliance on it. The court found that the Board considered the required statutory factors and that its decision was not irrational. The dismissal of Sutherland’s petition was affirmed without costs.

Coach Vigneault expressed disappointment after a hard-fought Stanley Cup Final loss in which all three games at the venue went to overtime. He praised his team’s effort and both goaltenders, saying the group gave its best and would reflect before deciding what comes next. Before another game, he emphasized focusing on the opportunity, improving from the previous performance, maintaining more puck possession through quick north-south play, and trusting a power play that had generated good chances but failed to finish.

Malawi Health Equity Network urged the government to deploy internal auditors to all 28 district councils, citing research showing their absence undermines financial management and accountability. The study also identified poor coordination between councils, NGOs and civil society organizations, as well as the exclusion of rural communities from annual budget preparation. MHEN called for joint planning, shared responsibilities and rural representation on budget committees. Government analyst Yohanne Nyanja confirmed that auditor deployment plans were advanced and said councils must support auditors rather than view them as investigators. The K7 million research project, supported by Mamaye, included training council members in budget tracking and transparency.

The address calls the 1970s a decade of reform, peace, and improved quality of life. It identifies ending the Vietnam War through a just peace as the foremost foreign-policy goal. Under a new doctrine, other nations should assume primary responsibility for their defense and development while the United States honors treaty commitments, strengthens partnerships, and pursues negotiations with the Soviet Union and Communist China.

Domestically, the President urges government reform rather than simply expanding existing programs. Priorities include replacing the welfare system with income support, job training, and work incentives; returning federal power to states and citizens through “New Federalism”; and expanding voting, employment, and ownership opportunities. He advocates balanced budgets to control inflation, stronger legislation and federal support against crime, and increased cooperation with state and local law enforcement.

The address also presents environmental protection as a major concern. Proposed measures include a $10 billion clean-water program, preservation of parks and open spaces, stricter automobile pollution standards, comprehensive environmental regulations, and incorporating pollution-control costs into goods. Economic growth should be redirected toward improving life rather than abandoned.

A national growth policy is proposed to balance urban and rural development, rebuild old cities, assist new cities, and reverse rural decline. Looking toward the nation’s 200th anniversary, the President envisions reduced hunger and poverty, better housing, transportation, health, and education, controlled inflation and crime, cleaner air and water, expanded parks, continued space exploration, and peace. He concludes that material progress must be accompanied by moral leadership, idealism, public participation, and service to liberty, opportunity, progress, and peace.

Santa Cruz County supervisors selected Assistant County Administrative Officer Carlos Palacios to replace retiring administrator Susan Mauriello. Palacios, 55, previously served 19 years as Watsonville city manager and will become the county’s first Latino top administrator. He will oversee 2,400 employees and a $720 million budget, earning a $263,057 base salary.

Coach DeBoer said playing at home offers advantages but also distractions that require focus. He expects the team to improve after adjusting to Pittsburgh’s speed and wants better support, more puck possession and stronger attacking play. Lineup decisions will be made on game day, while one unnamed player missed time for maintenance. DeBoer emphasized that the series is not over until a team wins four games, citing the character and leadership required to reach the finals. He identified Crosby, Kessel and Malkin as major matchup challenges and said Pittsburgh’s quality means momentum will shift, requiring patience and an avoidance of frustration.

The President submits a preliminary report by James Bronson Reynolds and Charles P. Neill describing revolting, unsanitary, and dangerous conditions in Chicago stockyards and packing houses. Existing law and inadequate funding prevent effective federal inspection of prepared meat products entering interstate commerce, leaving trade open to diseased or spoiled meat and providing no means to address alleged misuse of chemicals and dyes.

He urges immediate legislation authorizing the Department of Agriculture to inspect and supervise meat production “from the hoof to the can,” regulate sanitary conditions, and cover products entering interstate commerce. He proposes funding inspections through a fee of no more than eight cents per slaughtered animal to prevent inadequate appropriations from undermining enforcement. Although investigations into chemical adulteration and the reuse of tainted or returned products remain unfinished, he warns that abuses will recur without legislation. He recommends enactment of the Beveridge amendment.

Nassim Nicholas Taleb is a statistician, mathematician, philosopher, trader, investor, and author focused on randomness, uncertainty, human bias, antifragility, decision-making, and tail risk. His *Incerto* series includes *Fooled by Randomness*, *The Black Swan*, *Antifragile*, and *Skin in the Game*. Taleb argues that forecasting is unreliable, rare events have disproportionate effects, and success is often mistakenly attributed to skill rather than luck.

After trading at investment banks, Taleb reportedly profited substantially from options during the 1987 crash. He later co-founded Empirica Capital with Mark Spitznagel and became an adviser to Spitznagel’s Universa Investments, which specializes in tail-risk protection.

Taleb’s barbell strategy combines mostly low-risk assets with a small allocation to high-risk, high-reward positions, avoiding moderate-risk investments. It seeks stability while retaining the potential to profit greatly from extreme events. Applications include stocks, bonds, options, and futures. Selling naked calls represents the opposite approach because it produces frequent small gains but exposes investors to potentially unlimited losses.

Taleb defines antifragile systems as those that benefit from volatility, shocks, and disorder, unlike robust systems that merely withstand them. He emphasizes preparedness over prediction, decentralization, limiting the risk of ruin, learning through trial and error, and ensuring decision-makers bear the consequences of their choices. *Skin in the Game* argues that incentives and risks should be aligned and that actions and personal stakes are more meaningful than stated opinions.

Armed police detained a 26-year-old man after reports he threatened two people with a firearm at Shackleton Court in Newton Heath. Officers surrounded and searched the tower block for several hours, with negotiators reportedly involved. The suspect was arrested and remained in custody.

Donald Trump said U.S.-Canada trade would only be “tweaked,” but Canada’s greater dependence on U.S. trade makes even small changes consequential. Despite an encouraging White House meeting, concerns remain over agriculture, softwood lumber, and whether U.S. deregulation and tax cuts could weaken Canadian competitiveness. Interim Conservative leader Rona Ambrose supported Justin Trudeau’s decision to avoid confrontation. Trudeau maintained a respectful diplomatic distance, prioritizing protection of the vital trade relationship. Trump described Canada as a friend, neighbour, and ally, while both governments emphasized cooperation on trade, energy, security, alliances, and fighting ISIS. They also announced a council supporting women entrepreneurs and business leaders.

Initial coin offerings (ICOs) raise funds by selling crypto tokens, often before a network or product is functional. The concept originated with J.R. Willett, who proposed building applications and fundraising mechanisms on Bitcoin. ICO activity surged from June 2017 to June 2018, raising about $25 billion—roughly 20%–30% of annual global venture capital—before declining sharply.

ICOs commonly fund network development, retain tokens for promoters, permit token transfers, and establish scarcity through supply policies. Many offerings are based only on ideas, lack published source code, and rely on expectations of token appreciation. Simple Agreements for Future Tokens formalize future delivery when tokens are not yet usable, partly in an attempt to address regulatory concerns.

ICOs should be evaluated by examining whether blockchain and a native token are necessary, the white paper and source code, the project team, venture-capital involvement, community interest, monetary policy, token ownership, distribution methods, competition, and technical challenges. Token valuation is difficult because future utility is often unclear; despite risk and uncertainty suggesting discounted prices, tokens were frequently sold at premiums.

ICO proceeds are generally recorded as current or deferred revenue, and sometimes as liabilities. Revenue models may rely on the initial sale, retained tokens sold later, transaction-related income, or tokens circulating among network users. In the United States, most ICOs were described as noncompliant securities offerings regulated by the Securities and Exchange Commission, though regulation varies by jurisdiction.

By the third quarter of 2018, ICO funding had fallen 78% from the previous quarter to $1.8 billion. Around 80%–85% of offerings used Ethereum, 76% were based only on ideas, few had usable code, and many raised little or failed quickly. Most tokens provided access to network goods or services rather than company ownership, although tokens can be structured with voting, governance, dividend, or cash-flow rights. The lecture predicted continued contraction of ICO activity and failure rates exceeding 90%–95%, while allowing that native tokens could retain limited value for launching and motivating networks.

A&O Shearman associate Ashley Hollis won “Big Brother” after posing as a social media marketing manager to avoid becoming a target. Inspired by Elle Woods, she used legal skills to anticipate arguments and craft her final speech. Hollis plans to share much of the $750,000 prize with her parents and may buy a home.

Libyan National Army forces lost four men and had 10 wounded in December amid continued clashes in Benghazi’s Khreibish district, despite declaring victory in July. The fighting forms part of Libya’s broader post-2011 conflict.

Tharisa announced a phased transition from 15 years of open-pit operations to underground mining, beginning with the west mine as surface resources decline. Management said the long-planned shift supports an integrated mining complex designed to extend value from platinum group metals and chrome production. The company highlighted its resilience through volatile markets and 11 consecutive profitable years.

The study examines a dialogic emergency remote education activity developed during the COVID-19 pandemic for 19 Brazilian physics teacher-education students. Grounded in Freirean critical pedagogy and Cultural-Historical Activity Theory, it aimed to increase students’ awareness of social contradictions while teaching scientific communication.

Using Discord, students discussed difficulties with remote education and the disputed reopening of schools, researched scientific and government sources, evaluated information, and collaboratively produced an infographic presenting benefits and risks of returning to face-to-face classes. Discord’s text and voice channels enabled students to move independently among groups, review discussions, share resources, organize meetings without the teacher, and divide tasks according to their abilities.

The authors found that combining a socially relevant theme, Freirean dialogue, collaborative production, and students’ familiarity with Discord supported participation, autonomy, agency, and connections between personal experiences and broader sociopolitical issues. They conclude that the activity fostered collective problem-solving and more complex awareness of the relationship between individual concerns and systemic social contradictions.

This study used bibliometric and factorial analyses to examine research on STEAM education combined with gamification. A Scopus search conducted on October 23, 2023, identified 34 English-language documents published from 2017 to 2023. Publication output increased over this period, particularly from 2020 onward, indicating growing scholarly interest.

The literature associates gamification with increased student motivation, engagement, collaboration, satisfaction, and academic performance, although outcomes vary by personality, design, context, and duration. Computer science accounted for 37.7% of publications and social sciences for 20.5%. Thailand led in publications and citations, while Bulgaria, Italy, and Malaysia were also major contributors. Leading authors included Kummanee, Nilsook, Wannapiroon, Lee, and Piriyasurawong.

Frequently occurring keywords were “gamification,” “STEAM,” “STEAM education,” and “computational thinking.” Country-link analysis identified Malaysia and Singapore as having the highest total link strengths, while Germany, Latvia, Norway, and France were prominent in collaborative research. Factorial and hierarchical clustering grouped topics into educational methodologies and interaction tools, student-centered learning environments, and educational technologies and engagement strategies. Overall, the study maps publication trends, influential works, authors, countries, collaborations, keywords, and conceptual relationships in this emerging research field.

CEO Fran Horowitz transformed Abercrombie & Fitch by replacing command-and-control management, improving clothing quality, and prioritizing a durable lifestyle brand over trendiness. Abercrombie sales nearly doubled to $2.6 billion from 2019 to 2024, while combined sales with Hollister are expected to exceed $5 billion this year. To sustain growth, the company is expanding partnerships, including selling Abercrombie Kids at Macy’s and becoming the NFL’s first fashion partner. Horowitz says the NFL deal can increase brand awareness and better serve female fans with more sophisticated team merchandise.

The DAWn-Plasma study was an ethics-approved, multicenter, randomized, open-label phase 2 trial comparing standard care plus high-titer convalescent plasma with standard care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19 who were not receiving mechanical ventilation. Participants were allocated 2:1; the plasma regimen comprised four units totaling 800–1000 mL, administered soon after randomization.

Between May 2020 and January 2021, 499 patients were assessed and 489 randomized. The Full Analysis Set included 320 plasma recipients and 163 controls after six exclusions. Median time to first transfusion was five hours, and 91.9% of plasma-group patients received all four units.

At Day 15, the proportion alive without mechanical ventilation was similar between groups: 83.7% with plasma versus 84.1% with control (odds ratio 0.99; p=0.976). No statistically significant differences were found in mortality or any secondary endpoint at Days 15 or 30. A prespecified analysis found an interaction between the primary endpoint and age.

Adverse-event rates were also similar. Adverse events occurred in 28.13% of plasma recipients and 30.06% of controls; serious adverse events occurred in approximately 20.6% of each group. Transfusion-related effects occurred in 6.0% of plasma recipients, with no reported TRALI cases. Fourteen treatment-related adverse events and seven treatment-related serious adverse events were reported.

Neutralizing-antibody titers increased by Day 6, but this was not influenced by plasma treatment. Higher baseline and Day 6 titers correlated with better outcomes. Overall, early administration of high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not alter the clinical course of hospitalized COVID-19 or improve measured outcomes.

The paper studies whether formulas of the modal µ-calculus (µML) can be defined or separated by formulas of propositional modal logic (ML). An ML-separator for µML formulas φ and φ′ is an ML formula ψ such that φ entails ψ and ψ entails ¬φ′. Definability is the special case of separating φ from ¬φ. The problems are considered over all models, words, binary trees, and trees of bounded or unbounded outdegree, including finite-model restrictions.

The main complexity results are:
- Over all models, ML-definability and ML-separability are ExpTime-complete.
- Over words, both problems are PSpace-complete.
- Over binary and unrestricted trees, both are ExpTime-complete.
- Over d-ary trees for d ≥ 3, definability is ExpTime-complete while separability is 2-ExpTime-complete.

Constructed separators have single-exponential size over words, double-exponential size over all models and binary trees, and triple-exponential size over d-ary trees for d ≥ 3. The word construction is optimal; under mild assumptions, the binary and unrestricted-tree constructions are also optimal.

ML has the Craig interpolation property over all models, words, and binary trees, but not over trees of outdegree bounded by d ≥ 3. Thus, the modal logic K ⊕ altd has Craig interpolation exactly when d ≤ 2. Over higher-arity trees, determining whether two ML formulas admit a Craig interpolant is coNExpTime-complete.

The graded setting is also examined. For graded µ-calculus formulas, definability and separability by graded modal logic are ExpTime-complete. Definability by ordinary ML remains ExpTime-complete, while ML-separability becomes 2-ExpTime-complete.

The technical framework uses pointed Kripke structures, bisimulations, bounded bisimulations, parity-game semantics, and nondeterministic parity tree automata. Non-separability at modal depth n is characterized by the existence of models satisfying the two formulas that are n-bisimilar. Automata-theoretic pumping arguments then reduce unbounded consistency questions to bounded-depth tests.

Over all models, separators can be constructed in doubly exponential time through bounded-depth uniform consequences. Over words, separability is reduced to checking whether the intersection of two regular prefix languages is infinite, yielding a PSpace decision procedure. If a separator exists over words, one can be constructed in exponential time, matching the exponential succinctness gap between µML and ML.

The disclosure describes electronic gaming systems, methods, and storage media implementing stop-based bonus games. A base-game outcome may trigger a bonus wheel that can lead to a secondary jackpot wheel containing jackpot and non-jackpot stops. When a non-jackpot stop is selected, its credit or other prize may be awarded and the stop subsequently replaced with a jackpot award, increasing future opportunities to win a jackpot. These upgraded associations may persist across base-game plays or player sessions and may reset or decrease after a jackpot is awarded.

The bonus construct may use wheels, reels, dice, or grid-based treasure maps. Trigger events can include base-game outcomes, other bonus-game outcomes, or player inputs. Awards may include progressive or fixed jackpots, credits, multipliers, wild symbols, free games, additional selections, or no-value outcomes. Implementations may visually update newly converted stops and support multiple jackpot levels.

The systems may operate on standalone or networked electronic gaming machines with processors, memory, displays, player interfaces, credit-input mechanisms, random number generators, ticketing, player tracking, and gaming-related servers. An example uses a bonus wheel with inner credit-prize stops and outer feature stops that may activate separate GRAND, MAJOR, MINOR, or MINI jackpot wheels.
Some dogs’ irresistible attraction to toys may parallel human behavioral addictions.

Muskogee veteran Rodney Orton relies on a mobility scooter because breathing problems limit his walking. When his 15-year-old scooter stopped working, the VA scheduled an evaluation six weeks later. After Problem Solver Travis Guillory contacted the VA, staff found a suitable scooter in local inventory and delivered it to Orton’s hospital room the next morning.

A Hubble image shows the filamentary Tarantula Nebula and bubble-like Honeycomb Nebula. Research suggests the Honeycomb’s unusual shape results from interactions between older and newer supernovae and its viewing angle. Hubble is a NASA-ESA project launched in 1990.

A Stanford study tested whether appealing vegetable names influenced college students’ choices. Identically prepared vegetables received indulgent, basic, health-positive, or health-restrictive labels. Among nearly 28,000 dining-hall patrons, indulgently labeled vegetables were chosen 25% more often than basic versions, 35% more than health-positive versions, and 41% more than restrictive versions. Students also served themselves larger portions.

The findings suggest taste-focused descriptions may encourage healthier eating more effectively than emphasizing nutrition or restrictions. An IFIC survey similarly found taste influenced 84% of food purchases, compared with 63% for healthfulness. This approach could be used at home by giving vegetables appetizing descriptions. Suggested dishes include grilled carrots with chipotle-lime aioli, nacho-cheese kale chips, chili-lime sweet corn salad, rosemary sea-salt-and-vinegar beet chips, cauliflower fried rice, and green beans with blue cheese and walnuts.

Browns coach Kevin Stefanski said no single factor will determine whether Shedeur Sanders earns the backup quarterback job behind rookie starter Dillon Gabriel. Stefanski emphasized long-term player development and avoiding roles players are not ready for, suggesting Sanders remains in development. Receiver Jerry Jeudy praised Sanders’ professionalism and preparation. Sanders will likely remain the emergency third-string quarterback while competing with Bailey Zappe for the backup role.

The article offers five strategies for Abalone: begin defensively rather than rushing to attack, plan moves to avoid vulnerabilities, secure the board’s centre for mobility, shift to offense when appropriate, and divide opposing counters into smaller groups that can be pushed toward the edge. Players should remain alert to counterattacks.

The March 2006 specification update documents numerous errata for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3. Issues affect PIT and PIC behavior, legacy DMA, UART and LPC access, PCI and I/O addressing, IDE/UDMA operations, ACPI power management, GPIO, USB, SMBus, keyboard emulation, clock gating, wake events, and suspend recovery.

Several failures can hang the system or disrupt operation, including I/O cycles at addresses 10000h or higher, byte accesses to ACPI PM1_STS and PM1_EN, misaligned ATAC PRDs, certain LPC synchronization patterns, and missed PIC interrupts when automatic clock gating is enabled. Other defects can cause discarded accesses, invalid read data, register corruption, missed ASMIs or wake events, incorrect CRCs, failed DMA or UDMA transfers, and unavailable peripheral functions.

Recommended workarounds include avoiding unsupported command sequences and illegal addresses; using DWORD-aligned PRDs; completing PRD tables before DMA; disabling clock gating for affected PIC, UART, USB, and GLIU domains; avoiding UART or LPC I/O during block or demand DMA; using single-transfer DMA; restricting PMC and ACPI register access sizes; using normal IDE command-before-bus-master ordering; preventing host termination during UDMA reads; using PWRBTN# or external circuitry for S3 wake events; and programming Sleep control delays below PM_SED. Some debug-only or rarely used features have no operational impact and no resolution. External protection is required because CS5535 USB pins do not meet the cited USB 1.1 over-voltage specification.

A spring 2025 study at a large public university compared three approaches to teaching electric potential and equipotential lines in a non-calculus introductory physics course: traditional physical equipment, a pre-built AI-designed simulation, and student development of simulations through prompting, testing, and refining generative AI. Students participated in only one approach. All groups addressed common learning objectives and completed five conceptual questions and an attitude survey after the laboratory; midterm and final performance were also examined.

Students in the AI-engagement group used Claude AI to generate an interactive simulation, validate its technical operation and physical accuracy, and improve it through independently written prompts. The pre-built simulation group explored the same physics content with an existing digital tool, while the physical group mapped equipotential lines using conductive solution, electrodes, and multimeters.

Because assessment data were not normally distributed, researchers used nonparametric analyses. Immediate conceptual performance differed significantly across groups, with a strong effect. Both simulation groups performed significantly better than the traditional physical-laboratory group, while the AI-generated and pre-built simulation groups did not differ significantly. No significant differences appeared in overall midterm or final-exam performance, indicating that the immediate conceptual advantage did not persist after subsequent lectures, homework, reviews, and peer instruction.

Laboratory type was significantly associated with responses to all five attitude questions. Students in both simulation groups reported more favorable attitudes than those using physical equipment regarding comparison with the previous lab, ease of use, support for understanding, enjoyment, and willingness to repeat the activity. The pre-built simulation group rated the lab more positively than the AI group only on comparison with the previous week’s lab. Students sometimes reported frustration when fixing either AI simulations or physical equipment, though concerns that learning was impaired were associated more clearly with physical equipment.

The study concludes that prompting, validating, and refining AI-generated simulations can support immediate conceptual understanding as effectively as using a vetted pre-built simulation and more effectively than the traditional physical activity studied. AI-based work may also offer opportunities to practice model development, validation, and debugging, although modeling skills were not directly assessed. Pre-built simulations provide rapid visualization and conceptual exploration, while physical equipment remains important for experimental skills and engagement with material phenomena.

Limitations include differences in abstraction among the activities, restrictions imposed by the AI platform’s free tier, occasional need for technical assistance, examination of only one physics topic, and a largely life-science student population at one institution. The authors recommend selecting among AI-generated simulations, pre-built simulations, and physical equipment according to specific learning objectives and call for further research on effective implementation across topics, populations, and educational contexts.

Electroweak unification combines weak and electromagnetic interactions despite their different strengths and coupling structures. Projecting particle spinors into left- and right-handed components allows the weak vector-axial current to be written as a vector current, while the electromagnetic current separates into left- and right-handed terms.

Left-handed neutrinos and electrons are organized into weak-isospin doublets. Charged weak currents rotate neutrinos into electrons and vice versa, while the third isospin component produces a neutral current. Introducing hypercharge adds the right-handed contributions needed for the neutral interaction.

The gauge fields consist of an isospin triplet \(W_1, W_2, W_3\) and a hypercharge singlet \(B\). The \(W^+\) and \(W^-\) bosons are linear combinations of \(W_1\) and \(W_2\). Mixing \(W_3\) and \(B\) through the weak mixing angle produces the photon and \(Z\) boson. Their couplings relate to the electromagnetic coupling, yielding a consistent framework containing \(W^+\), \(W^-\), the photon, and the \(Z\) boson.

This cross-sectional study assessed Alzheimer disease (AD) plasma biomarkers in 1,067 Amish adults from Ohio and Indiana, averaging 81.2 years of age. Researchers measured Aβ40, Aβ42, Aβ42/Aβ40, total tau, p-tau181, Aβ42/total tau, and Aβ42/p-tau181 and examined their relationships with clinical diagnosis, cognitive preservation, APOE status, and biomarker-derived clusters.

Participants with AD had higher p-tau181 and lower Aβ42/p-tau181 than cognitively unimpaired participants, while amyloid biomarkers and total tau did not differ significantly across diagnostic groups. Adjusted analyses found no overall significant biomarker associations with AD, but higher p-tau181 was strongly associated with AD among APOE ε4 carriers. Cognitive preservation was associated with lower p-tau181 and higher Aβ42/p-tau181 after excluding mild cognitive impairment. Models using all biomarkers or Aβ42/p-tau181 best distinguished AD from cognitive unimpaired status, with an area under the curve of 0.83.

Clustering based on Aβ42/Aβ40 and p-tau181 identified subgroups with differing amyloid and tau profiles. The high-risk subgroup had lower Aβ42/Aβ40, higher p-tau181, more APOE ε4 carriers, and more participants with AD. A three-cluster analysis further separated low-, moderate-, and high-risk biomarker patterns.

Limitations included the population’s limited representativeness, absence of imaging or cerebrospinal-fluid confirmation, possible diagnostic misclassification, and the cross-sectional design. The findings support p-tau181, Aβ42/Aβ40, and Aβ42/p-tau181 as promising non-invasive indicators, but longitudinal validation is needed.

The “Triangle Rotation” offense attacks a Triangle & Two defense by exploiting typically weak triangle-zone rotations. Three players rotate clockwise or counterclockwise, while two shooters become options if inside action fails. Key actions include point-guard penetration to an elbow, an opposite-elbow pop-out, a baseline cut, a weakside lob, and side screens for shooters. Success depends on simple execution, zone-attack fundamentals, defensive recognition, communication, timing, and coordinated play. Teams should practice through drills and scrimmages, scout defensive schemes and matchups, monitor adjustments, vary alignments and entries, and target weak defenders. In a Triangle & Two defense, three players guard zones while two chasers aggressively deny designated opponents passes and rebounds.

The patent describes deuterated heterocycle-fused gamma-carbolines designed to limit N-dealkylation, alpha-oxidation, and carbonyl-reduction metabolism while retaining antagonism of 5-HT2A receptors, serotonin transporter inhibition, and modulation of dopaminergic signaling. The compounds contain a trideuterated N-methyl group, a dideuterated adjacent methylene, or both, and may be provided as free bases, pharmaceutically acceptable salts such as tosylates, or substantially pure stereoisomers.

Pharmaceutical forms include immediate-, sustained-, and delayed-release compositions; injectable polymeric depot formulations releasing drug over approximately 14–180 days; and osmotic-controlled oral delivery systems. Proposed uses include treatment or prevention of schizophrenia and residual psychotic symptoms, depression, anxiety, sleep disorders, agitation, aggressive behavior, post-traumatic stress disorder, impulse-control disorders, dementia-associated symptoms, Parkinson’s disease-related conditions, and dyskinesia. The compounds may be administered alone or with agents including antipsychotics, antidepressants, hypnotics, Parkinson’s therapies, cholinesterase inhibitors, and NMDA receptor antagonists.

Examples describe synthesis of compounds deuterated at the N-methyl group, adjacent methylene, or both. Mouse studies found lower relative amide-metabolite formation for three deuterated compounds than for the non-deuterated Formula Q compound, while receptor-binding profiles remained substantially similar. In rats, oral administration of Example 2 produced comparable parent-drug exposure but approximately half the exposure to metabolite Q-1 and a 55% decrease in relative metabolism compared with Formula Q. Intravenous dosing produced little Q-1 formation for either compound. In dogs, sublingual Example 2 produced about 72% greater parent exposure than Formula Q, with the amide metabolite undetectable; subcutaneous administration produced comparable parent exposure and undetectable amide metabolite for both compounds.
