Venture capital is appropriate for only a minority of startups, and raising it does not determine a company’s quality. Entrepreneurs should remain capital- and dilution-efficient, choose investors carefully, and ensure that all parties share a definition of success.

Accelerators vary in services and involvement. Bolt, for example, supports hardware startups through funding, engineering resources, product development, team building, and financing guidance. Beyond formal services, accelerators can provide motivation and peer learning.

Convertible notes offer quick, inexpensive interim financing and usually convert into equity during a later funding round. However, they remain debt until conversion, potentially giving creditors significant control if a company fails. They are generally more suitable for smaller bridge rounds than large financings. Equity financing may better align investor and founder interests.

Funding amounts vary widely, from no outside capital to very large rounds. Entrepreneurs should raise only what is appropriate for their plans because excessive capital creates pressure for rapid growth and large exits, reducing flexibility. Investors also face pressure to deliver returns to their own funders.

The panel advised entrepreneurs to obtain mentors, check investor references, seek strong introductions, and begin investor conversations early. Productive investors ask questions and listen rather than merely lecture. Founders should examine how investors behave during difficult periods, follow-on financing, management changes, and exits.

Potential mismatches include raising more money than a market opportunity supports, accepting strategic investors whose priorities may later diverge, and giving numerous small investors unanimous decision rights. Strategic relationships should be evaluated for long-term alignment because personnel and corporate priorities can change.

Entrepreneurs should identify and eliminate their largest risks quickly and economically. If success depends on a major partner, they should understand that partner’s long-term interests, begin discussions early, ask questions without prematurely selling, and use experienced advisers for complex negotiations.

DS-STAR is a multi-agent framework that generates Python solutions for data science tasks involving heterogeneous files such as CSV, JSON, Markdown, and unstructured text. It first uses an analyzer agent to create descriptions of each file’s structure and content. A planner then proposes one executable step at a time, a coder implements and executes the cumulative plan, and an LLM-based verifier judges whether the plan and results sufficiently answer the query. If insufficient, a router either adds a step or truncates the plan at an erroneous step before regeneration. Additional modules debug failed scripts, retrieve relevant files from large data collections, and format final outputs.

Using Gemini-2.5-Pro, DS-STAR achieved 45.24% hard-task accuracy on DABStep, compared with 41.01% for the best alternative; 44.69% on KramaBench, compared with 39.79%; and 38.5% overall on DA-Code, compared with 37.0%. In KramaBench’s oracle setting, where relevant files were supplied, accuracy reached 52.55%.

Ablations showed that removing the analyzer reduced DABStep hard-task accuracy from 45.24% to 26.98%, while removing the router reduced it to 39.95%. Hard DABStep tasks required an average of 5.6 rounds versus 3.0 for easy tasks, and higher refinement limits improved accuracy. DS-STAR also produced promising results with GPT-5. Future work proposes incorporating human experts into the framework.

SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification 6.00 defines SD card interfaces, capacities, voltages, form factors, performance modes, protocols, initialization, data transfer, protection, and maintenance features. Mc-EX extends the physical layer for mobile-commerce command packets, while SDIO modifications are specified separately.

Cards are classified as SDSC up to 2 GB, SDHC above 2 GB through 32 GB, and SDXC above 32 GB through 2 TB. Hosts supporting higher capacities must also support lower-capacity cards. Standard cards operate at 2.7–3.6 V; UHS-II additionally uses 1.70–1.95 V on VDD2. Standard, miniSD, and microSD form factors are defined; standard cards measure 24 × 32 mm and are 2.1 or 1.4 mm thick. Cards may be read/write or fixed-content ROM and contain user and authenticated protected areas.

Bus modes range from Default Speed at 12.5 MB/s and High Speed at 25 MB/s through UHS-I SDR50, DDR50, and SDR104 at up to 104 MB/s. UHS-II modes include FD156, optional HD312, FD312, and FD624, reaching 624 MB/s. UHS-I uses 1.8 V signaling in SD mode and requires a voltage-switch sequence; it is unavailable in SPI mode. UHS-II hosts support both legacy SD and UHS-II interfaces and initialize through PHY, device initialization, enumeration, configuration, and SD-TRAN stages.

Speed Classes 2, 4, 6, and 10 specify corresponding minimum MB/s performance; Class 0 has no specified performance. Application Performance Classes define random and sustained sequential performance. Cache, self-maintenance, command queue, low-voltage initialization, and higher-speed UHS-II features are also defined.

Communication is host-controlled using broadcast or addressed commands, responses, and block data transfers. Commands use 48-bit tokens with CRC7; responses are 48 or 136 bits; data uses CRC16. Transfers may use one or four data lines and single or multiple blocks. Initialization uses CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3 to reset cards, verify voltage, establish capacity and readiness, obtain identification, and assign relative addresses. CMD7 selects a card for transfer.

Read, write, erase, discard, and full-user-area logical erase operations include CRC, status, sequencing, busy signaling, and error handling. Multiple-block writes and optional pre-erasure improve performance. Write protection includes a host-enforced mechanical switch, internal protection, and password locking through CMD42. Card Ownership Protection adds a Force Erase Password, COP unlocking, protected erase, and password-management rules. ROM cards reject write and erase commands and full-size ROM cards lack a write-protect switch.

“Sell the rip” means closing a long position or opening a short position when an asset appears overvalued, anticipating mean reversion or a correction. It is primarily a short-term strategy suited to overbought assets and stocks with weak fundamentals, but may be unsuitable for long-term investments or high-growth stocks. Short-selling carries substantial risk because prices can continue rising.

Traders may identify overbought conditions using RSI, stochastic, Williams %R, Internal Bar Strength, Bollinger Bands, moving averages, and other momentum or oscillating indicators. An RSI-based SPY backtest produced 391 trades, a 0.61% average gain, a 75% win rate, and a 1.6 profit factor, but had excessive drawdowns. Revised exit criteria reduced holding periods and drawdowns while increasing trade frequency, despite lowering average gain to 0.48%. The approach performed well on the S&P 500 over the past three decades but was less effective before the 1990s and may fail in trend-following markets such as commodities.

The Scripps National Spelling Bee nearly doubled in size through a wild-card program, prompting longtime pronouncer Jacques Bailly to share duties with associate pronouncer Brian Sietsema. Sietsema, a Greek Orthodox priest, former linguistics professor and former Merriam-Webster pronunciation editor, pronounced words for about 180 contestants. More than 500 spellers competed in preliminary rounds, with 41 semifinalists selected partly through a challenging written spelling and vocabulary test.

Among the competitors, multisport athlete Rebekah Zeigler advanced beyond her previous onstage best by correctly spelling “yarrow.” Reagan Remmers was reinstated after spelling “balaclava” as “Balaklava,” a Ukrainian city, because judges had not identified the homonym. Daniel Doudna of Alaska deliberately paused after each letter while spelling “quietude,” explaining that slower spelling helps him avoid mistakes.

A chronological bibliography lists major 1945 U.S. foreign-policy statements by Presidents Roosevelt and Truman, Secretaries Stettinius and Byrnes, Under Secretary Grew, and Cordell Hull. Topics include Yalta and Potsdam, the United Nations Charter and San Francisco Conference, Germany’s and Japan’s surrenders, the atomic bomb and atomic energy, wartime aid, postwar economic peace, foreign ministers’ meetings, world cooperation, and China policy. Citations primarily reference the Department of State Bulletin and Truman’s Public Papers.

The defense has performed well all season, with the top four handling difficult minutes and Matt Irwin and Yannick Weber also making important contributions. Working with experienced players such as Shea provides daily lessons in preparation, practice, and conduct. Coaching experience has also shaped playoff routines, including gathering on off days to meet, reset, and move forward. The team earned its position through both good and difficult periods, which helped form its identity. While players, coaches, and staff enjoy the opportunity to play hockey in June, they remain focused on the daily work required. Both finalists are hungry to win the Cup, and success will depend on being prepared and willing to do whatever is necessary.

Amazon completed its acquisition of Whole Foods Market on August 28, 2017. Whole Foods became a wholly owned Amazon subsidiary, with eligible outstanding shares converted into the right to receive $42.00 cash each. Equity awards were converted to cash based on the merger consideration, while options and stock appreciation rights with exercise prices at or above $42.00 were canceled without consideration. Total consideration was approximately $13.55 billion, financed through previously disclosed debt financing. Amazon planned to file required Whole Foods financial statements and pro forma financial information by amendment within 71 days after the report’s required filing date.

Colorado’s Prescription Drug Affordability Board set a $600-per-unit payment ceiling for Amgen’s arthritis drug Enbrel, applying to government agencies and commercial health plans covering state residents. The limit equals about $30,350 annually per person, versus roughly $53,000 paid by the average Colorado insurance plan in 2023.

The Martingale trading strategy doubles position size after each loss so one eventual win can recover prior losses and earn the initial stake. Originating in gambling and based on equal-probability outcomes, it assumes sufficient capital and eventual mean reversion. However, prolonged losses cause rapidly increasing exposure, severe drawdowns, or total capital loss. Stocks can fall to zero, making the method especially dangerous, though broad-market index ETFs are presented as less likely to do so.

Martingale differs from double-down trading, which adds the original position size, and from planned averaging down or scaling in. A cited SPY benchmark produced 409 trades, a 0.64% average gain, 8.68% annual returns, and a 23% maximum drawdown. Modifying equity exposure using RSI thresholds as a simple Martingale method produced an undesirable result despite the same trade count and average gain. The passage does not recommend Martingale, instead favoring diversified, uncorrelated strategies and careful risk management.

Turkey planned to extend its state of emergency from April 19 for three months, pending parliamentary approval, citing terrorism threats and the alleged coup organizers. Emergency rule began after the failed July 2016 coup and allows the government to bypass parliament and restrict rights.

Generative AI increases the potential for personalized learning, but realizing it requires changes to pedagogy, assessment, school organization, and especially prescribed curricula. Despite repeated reforms and technological adoption, schools largely retain a centuries-old structure in which institutions determine what, how, where, and with whom students learn.

The article identifies curriculum as education’s central organizing element. It translates societal expectations into required content, shapes teaching, assessment, policy, scheduling, and teacher training, and has increasingly restricted student autonomy through standards and testing. In the AI age, fixed curricula may limit access to expanding knowledge and may not remain relevant to students’ future needs.

The authors propose a balanced curriculum that divides learning time between system-prescribed content and student-directed learning. The balance should vary according to students’ age, experience, ability to manage autonomy, and available support. Teachers would become coaches, facilitators, project managers, and social-emotional supporters, while schools would revise schedules, classes, facilities, and assessments.

Using panarchy theory, the article describes education as a nested system of classrooms, schools, districts, and larger jurisdictions. Its adaptive cycle includes growth, conservation, release, and reorganization. Education has demonstrated resilience and adaptability by absorbing innovations without altering its core structure, but may lack the transformability needed to respond to AI and societal change.

The authors distinguish tiny classroom innovations, small school programs, large system policies, and transformational models such as Montessori and democratic schools. They recommend introducing autonomous learning subsystems within existing public schools rather than transforming entire institutions at once. Successful subsystems could gradually influence higher system levels.

Examples include China’s Innovation, Creativity, and Entrepreneurship Education program, which allocated about one-third of curriculum time to personalized, product-oriented, and globally connected learning, and related initiatives in Australia. Some programs expanded, while others ended or remained extracurricular. The article concludes that protected subsystems may allow transformative educational ideas to survive, be tested, spread, and eventually reshape the broader system.

A New York Times survey found widespread dissatisfaction among responding federal judges with the Supreme Court’s emergency docket decisions involving President Donald Trump’s second-term policies. Of 65 judges, 47 said the docket was used inappropriately, while 48 said lower courts lacked sufficient guidance. Of 54 respondents, 42 said the decisions harmed public perception of the judiciary.

The survey included 28 Republican-appointed and 37 Democratic-appointed judges. At least seven of roughly 20 relevant emergency orders lacked reasoning, and nearly all benefited Trump, enabling major policy actions. Some judges described the orders as arbitrary and demoralizing, though one Trump appointee praised them. The Times acknowledged respondents may not represent the judiciary. A Volokh Conspiracy critique argued the survey may overrepresent judges predisposed to oppose the rulings.

The ADS868xW multiSPI interface supports four SPI protocols for reads and writes, defaulting to SPI-00-S after power-up or asynchronous reset. Protocol selection uses SDI_MODE bits, with the initial configuration write performed through SPI-00-S; valid writes require at least 32 SCLK cycles. Read options include single- or dual-SDO SPI and source-synchronous protocols. Source-synchronous operation outputs a data-aligned clock on RVS and supports internal or external clock sources. Dual-SDO mode uses SDO-0 and the configurable ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin.

Nine four-byte configuration registers control device identification, reset and power management, SDI and SDO protocols, output formatting, input range and internal reference, and alarm flags, thresholds, and hysteresis. Protected reset and power-control writes require writing 69h to address 05h first. Output data can include device address, alarm flags, range settings, parity, conversion data, or test patterns.

The ADS868xW integrates a 16-bit SAR ADC, analog front end, programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, and precision reference. An example industrial input module combines the ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 differential multiplexer to measure configurable voltage, current, or temperature inputs. The device supports programmable input and AVDD alarms; adjustable hysteresis improves immunity to noise near alarm thresholds.

Separate AVDD and DVDD supplies require local decoupling. The device provides NAP and deep power-down modes for reduced consumption. Recommended PCB practices include separating analog and digital routing, using short ground paths, placing bypass capacitors close to supply and reference pins, and avoiding vias between pins and capacitors. The document also provides support, revision, packaging, ESD, and legal information.

The Dolphins earned their first win by beating the Jets but lost star receiver Tyreek Hill to a feared season-ending dislocated left knee. Darren Waller caught two touchdowns in his first game since January 2024, suggesting a larger offensive role. The Jets fell to 0-4 after committing three turnovers and 12 penalties, despite rushing for 197 yards. Justin Fields scored on a 43-yard run but struggled through the air.

Apple filed a Form 8-K on July 28, 2022, announcing financial results for its third fiscal quarter ended June 25, 2022. The related press release was filed as Exhibit 99.1, with Inline XBRL as Exhibit 104. CFO Luca Maestri signed the report.

Astronomer Hector Socas-Navarro proposes searching for advanced extraterrestrial societies by detecting vast swarms of geosynchronous satellites around distant planets. During a planetary transit, such a satellite “necklace” could cause slight dimming of the host star before and after the planet passes, especially when viewed edge-on. Unlike searches for radio or laser signals, this method requires no synchronization or deliberate alien communication, and satellites might remain long after their creators disappeared. Astronomers could test the idea using existing exoplanet observations without new telescopes or experiments. Although success is uncertain, the approach is relatively easy to attempt.

IMI plc received a consensus “Hold” rating from 18 research firms: two sell, 12 hold and four buy. The average 12-month target price was GBX 1,027.29. BNP Paribas raised its target to GBX 1,400 with an “outperform” rating, while other cited brokers maintained neutral or overweight ratings. IMI opened at GBX 1,216, with a GBX 3.29 billion market capitalization. The UK engineering company designs, manufactures and services products controlling fluid movement across critical, precision and hydronic engineering segments.

China reduced the US dollar’s weighting in its trade-weighted foreign-exchange basket from 26.4 to 22.4 percent and expanded the basket from 13 to 24 currencies from 2017. The first adjustment since the basket’s 2015 launch aims to shift attention from the yuan-dollar exchange rate. The yuan fell about seven percent against the dollar in 2016, its largest annual decline since 1994. The change came amid concerns over future China-US trade relations under Donald Trump, who accused China of currency manipulation. Chinese officials said the yuan remained stable and attributed its weakness to a strong dollar, which continues to dominate real trade.

Police and Crimestoppers are warning about counterfeit banknotes during the festive shopping season, when fraudsters often target busy shops, temporary staff and the public. In the first half of 2017, more than 237,000 fake notes, notionally worth over £4.88 million, were removed from UK streets. Counterfeiting harms businesses, charities, schools and individuals and is linked to organised crime. Crimestoppers and the Bank of England launched the Banknote Checking Scheme to train cash-handling businesses. Information about counterfeiters can be reported anonymously to Crimestoppers.

The article examines whether dance education can integrate social studies and support holistic development in U.S. schools. Standardised assessments such as PISA and NAEP emphasise separate academic subjects, marginalise dance, and discourage interdisciplinary education. Social studies promotes civic competence through concepts including culture, identity, environments, governance, global connections, and civic practices, while dance education encompasses creative, performative, responsive, and contextual learning.

A literature review found that testing influences education policy, arts educators usually initiate curricular integration, and dance education varies substantially in interpretation and implementation. Research also indicated that dance can connect students with culture, heritage, identity, community, civic life, and historical contexts.

A survey of 91 graduates of U.S. dance education programmes examined whether their curricula included social studies concepts. The strongest reported emphases were individual development and identity (97%), people, places, and environments (94%), and time, continuity, and change (75%). Governance and civic ideals received the least attention, both at 44%. Open-ended responses showed that concepts were incorporated either explicitly through content such as cultural dance forms and geography or implicitly through pedagogy involving inclusion, cooperation, authority, empathy, and classroom rules.

The findings suggest that dance educators can integrate social studies when they adopt a holistic view of curriculum and pedagogy, but they often work without adequate guidance. The study recommends less prescriptive dance curricula, greater professional development, and policy support for interdisciplinary arts education. Its scope was limited by a small U.S.-only sample and predominantly binary survey questions. Further international and in-depth research is proposed. The UNESCO Framework for Culture and Arts Education is identified as potential policy support for integrating arts, culture, social studies, sustainable development, and peace.

Cheltenham Town face interest from an unnamed League Two club in influential midfielder Harry Pell, 26. Pell, under contract until 2019, nearly joined Blackpool for £200,000 last summer but rejected personal terms. The versatile, 6ft 5in player joined Cheltenham in 2015 and has made more than 120 starts.

Zimbabwe’s veterinary department faces prolonged FMD vaccine shortages, allowing infections to spread across several provinces, with active cases in Chipinge South, Mwenezi, Chivi and Chiredzi. Control efforts are weakened by severe staffing, funding, logistical and infrastructure deficiencies, livestock movement violations, poor animal identification and limited stakeholder cooperation. Lost boundary fences have undermined control zones, expanding the cattle population requiring vaccination. Effective containment requires movement controls, rapid detection, quarantine and regular vaccination every six months, or every four months after outbreaks.

GSK named chief commercial officer Luke Miels as CEO effective Jan. 1, replacing Emma Walmsley. During Walmsley’s tenure, GSK spun off Haleon and focused on specialty medicines and vaccines, though investors questioned its strategy amid patent and vaccine challenges. AstraZeneca plans to list ordinary shares on the New York Stock Exchange while retaining listings in London and Stockholm, giving U.S. investors easier access. The move comes amid criticism of the U.K.’s pharmaceutical pricing and commercial environment and U.S. pressure involving tariffs and drug pricing.

Arnoldi iteration constructs an orthogonal basis for Krylov subspaces. For symmetric matrices, its Hessenberg matrix becomes symmetric tridiagonal, enabling efficient approximation of low eigenvalues through Ritz values from a small leading submatrix.

Conjugate gradients applies to symmetric positive definite systems. It recursively chooses approximations in Krylov subspaces so that residuals are mutually orthogonal and correction directions are orthogonal in the \(A\)-inner product. Each cycle requires one sparse matrix-vector multiplication, two inner products, and a few vector updates. Its convergence depends on the condition number, with faster convergence for better-conditioned matrices.

The method can also be viewed as minimizing the quadratic energy
\[
E(x)=\tfrac12 x^T A x-b^T x,
\]
whose gradient is \(Ax-b\); its minimum solves \(Ax=b\). Unlike steepest descent, which repeatedly follows residual directions and may progress slowly across elongated level sets, conjugate gradients adjusts each new search direction to be \(A\)-orthogonal to previous directions, improving progress.

For matrices that are not symmetric positive definite, conjugate gradients may fail. Minimum residual methods instead choose a Krylov-subspace approximation minimizing \(\|b-Ax_k\|\). Using an Arnoldi basis converts this into a small least-squares problem, but the general Hessenberg matrix is not tridiagonal, so Arnoldi requires more work and lacks short recurrences. For large symmetric positive definite systems, choosing between conjugate gradients and reordered direct elimination depends on numerical experiments.

Stone tools found at Attirampakkam in southeast India date from 385,000 to 172,000 years ago, challenging beliefs that such technology arrived after 140,000 years ago. The discovery may indicate earlier migration from Africa, but without human remains, researchers cannot identify the toolmakers or determine whether the technology reflected local or African influences.

VentureWire’s September 19, 2000 issue reports that Internet television network Pseudo.com ceased operations and laid off 175 employees after failing to secure funding or a buyer. Broadbase Software agreed to acquire Servicesoft for approximately $645 million. Enfrastructure launched with over $100 million, Interregnum opened a $105 million IT fund, and Q9 Networks raised $26.5 million.

Numerous technology companies announced venture financing, including Darwin Networks ($91 million), IPG Photonics ($75 million), Wheelhouse ($52 million), Everdream and Nishan Systems ($50 million each), Onehealthbank.com ($42 million), CosmoCom ($40 million), MobileSys and StorageWay ($36 million each), and Portera ($35 million).

RightWorks named former Baan CEO Mary Coleman as chief executive. Other developments included company launches, renamings, board and executive appointments, and acquisitions by Optical Solutions, Symposium, and ConsumerSearch.com. Corrections clarified funding amounts for Global Factory and NewsMarket and Peter Trost’s position at BrannRMG.

Nebraska editorials highlight investments in education, history and tourism. The University of Nebraska-Lincoln is expanding agricultural and environmental research through new facilities, interdisciplinary initiatives and partnerships, amid rising enrollment and substantial research spending. Buffalo County Historical Society opened the 6,000-square-foot Family History Center at Trails & Rails Museum to preserve collections, welcome visitors and support exhibits, while seeking funds for a second phase. Lincoln Public Schools is urged to preserve Nebraska’s lowest student-teacher ratios among large districts, particularly to support low-income, minority, refugee and immigrant students, despite budget concerns. In Alliance, Carhenge—once threatened by zoning officials—has become a prominent folk-art attraction and a focal point for visitors viewing the August 21 total eclipse, illustrating the tension between regulation and creativity.

The disclosure describes a cloud-based industrial data services platform that registers industrial assets, hierarchical asset models, owners, and available data-service applications. Users select applications that direct gateway devices to collect industrial data from model-referenced tags for cloud processing.

Industrial devices support configurable basic information data types (BIDTs), including State, Rate, Odometer, and Event tags. Each BIDT includes values and metadata defining attributes such as states, limits, units, data sources, rollover values, time intervals, update rates, and event conditions. External systems can discover these tags and retrieve their data and metadata.

Gateway devices collect BIDT data and organize it through user-defined asset models representing plants, production lines, machines, equipment, and devices. Different models can provide role-specific or destination-specific views. Application servers may aggregate models from multiple gateways or facilities into plant or enterprise models, then generate contextualized graphical presentations using suitable widgets, historical trends, event logs, and hierarchical navigation.

The architecture supports on-premise and cloud deployments. Cloud-based application servers can receive modeled data through secure channels managed by a gateway registry that authenticates registered hardware and issues temporary communication certificates. The system is intended to simplify scalable collection, contextualization, visualization, processing, and controlled sharing of industrial data.

The President approves the act regulating the counting of electoral votes for the term beginning March 4, 1877, viewing it as a constitutional and orderly means to resolve the unprecedented disputed presidential election. The measure assigns Congress responsibility for single returns and establishes a tribunal for double returns, whose decisions stand unless both Houses agree otherwise. Although limited to the recent election and possibly imperfect, the act provides a definite legal process, reduces the danger of irregular conflict, and supports peaceful acceptance of the lawful result. The President also urges future permanent legislation for similar disputes, noting that uncertainty has disturbed public harmony and economic activity. Believing the bill will restore confidence and ensure an unquestioned presidential title, he signs it.

The study evaluated neural operator models for identifying combined causes of thoracic aortic aneurysms from image-derived aortic dilatation and distensibility. Researchers generated 500 synthetic aneurysm cases using finite-element growth and remodeling simulations with spatially varying combinations of compromised elastic fiber integrity and dysfunctional cellular mechanosensing. Four architectures—CNN-DeepONet, FNN-DeepONet, UNet, and Laplace Neural Operator—were trained on either dilatation alone or dilatation plus distensibility, using grayscale or heat maps.

Most models predicted both insults within 10% relative error. Adding distensibility reduced errors by roughly half across all architectures and helped distinguish aneurysms with similar maximum dilatation but different underlying mechanisms and mechanical properties. Input map format generally had little effect. UNet achieved the highest overall accuracy, with errors near 2% when using both dilatation and distensibility, while Laplace Neural Operator performed poorly with dilatation alone. The findings support full-field measurements of aortic geometry and mechanics over reliance on maximum diameter alone and suggest UNet-based models could aid personalized, image-based aneurysm risk assessment. Limitations include synthetic data, a single initial geometry and parameter set, simplified cylindrical anatomy, and exclusion of unstable growth, dissection, and rupture.

A cross-sectional study at ACS Medical College and Hospital in Chennai examined antimicrobial resistance in 346 clinical specimens collected from November 2023 to May 2024. Cultures and antibiotic susceptibility testing were performed using standard biochemical methods and Kirby–Bauer disk diffusion under CLSI guidelines.

Of 346 samples, 264 (76.3%) showed bacterial growth; 75.4% of positive cultures were Gram-negative. Urine was the most common specimen among positive cultures (40.2%), followed by wound/pus (29.9%) and sputum (24.6%). E. coli was the most frequently isolated organism (28.8%), followed by Klebsiella spp. (26.9%), Staphylococcus spp. (13.2%), and Pseudomonas spp. (9.5%). E. coli predominated in urine, Klebsiella in sputum, Staphylococcus in wounds, and Salmonella in blood. Adults older than 45 comprised 56.6% of participants.

Among 76 E. coli isolates, resistance was particularly high to cefoperazone/sulbactam and chloramphenicol (97.4%), cefotaxime (92.1%), cefuroxime (93.4%), and polymyxin B, vancomycin, linezolid, and ceftazidime with clavulanate (98.7%). Amikacin and gentamicin showed the highest sensitivity rates, at 71.1% and 63.2%, respectively.

The study recommends multidisciplinary antimicrobial stewardship, regular resistance surveillance, evidence-based local treatment guidelines, diagnostic testing, provider education, restrictions on non-prescription antibiotic sales and self-medication, decision-support tools, accountability, and ongoing evaluation. Limitations include the short duration, small sample, cross-sectional and context-specific design, absence of clinical outcome and comorbidity data, and limited focus on hospital-acquired and rural infections.

The Sixth Circuit affirmed the judgment, finding no error in the trial court’s instruction regarding an inconsistency between an interrogatory answer and the general verdict, and concluding that substantial evidence supported the jury’s verdict.

The SanDisk Sansa Fuze is a portable audio/video player with a 1.9-inch color display, FM radio where available, built-in microphone, internal storage, and microSD/microSDHC expansion. It supports MP3, WAV, WMA, secure WMA, Audible audiobooks, podcasts, converted videos, and converted photos. Its rechargeable, nonreplaceable battery provides up to 24 hours of audio or five hours of video playback under specified conditions.

The manual explains charging and computer connection, power controls, resetting, thumbwheel navigation, media transfer through drag-and-drop, Windows Media Player, Audible Manager, and Sansa Media Converter. It covers music and audiobook playback, playlists, ratings, repeat, shuffle, equalizer settings, video bookmarks and brightness, photo slideshows, FM presets and recording, and voice recording. Content can be deleted directly or through a computer. Formatting erases all stored content, and disconnecting during data transfer may damage the device.

System settings include wallpaper, artwork display, backlight, power saving, language, date and time, brightness, volume, USB mode, factory reset, formatting, and press-and-hold behavior. Firmware updates, troubleshooting, support resources, and technical-support contact details are provided.

SanDisk offers the original purchaser a one-year limited warranty under stated conditions, with repair, replacement, or refund as possible remedies. The software license permits limited personal use with a SanDisk product and restricts modification, reverse engineering, redistribution, and hazardous applications. Warranty and liability limitations apply. Users are responsible for complying with copyright and intellectual-property laws.

The paper examines relationships between digitalization, sustainable development, and national culture in 28 EU countries. Digitalization is measured through the Digital Economy and Society Index (DESI), while sustainability is assessed using indices covering economic, social, and environmental dimensions. Hofstede’s cultural dimensions are included to evaluate cultural relationships with digitalization. Pearson and Spearman correlations are calculated using data from 2014–2017.

DESI correlates strongly and positively with competitiveness, innovation, entrepreneurship, GDP, contributions to humanity, and the Sustainable Development Goals Index. Digitalization is also positively associated with social indicators, including human wellbeing. However, it has a negative relationship with environmental wellbeing, while some environmental measures show no statistically significant relationship.

Cultural analysis shows that digitalization is negatively correlated with power distance and uncertainty avoidance, and positively correlated with individualism and indulgence. Long-term orientation and masculinity show no significant relationship. The findings indicate that national culture is related to digitalization and may inform macromarketing approaches to technological change.

The study concludes that digitalization significantly correlates with sustainable development, particularly its economic and social components, while environmental performance is comparatively neglected. Limitations include DESI’s restriction to EU countries, incomplete or developing sustainability measures, and reliance on Hofstede’s cultural framework. Further research could include broader country samples, alternative cultural models, development levels, and policy-oriented macromarketing tools.

Ari Ne’eman contrasts the Kennedy family’s historical disability-policy achievements with Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s promotion of unproven links between autism, vaccination, and acetaminophen.

Ne’eman recounts a 1963 visit by President Kennedy’s disability panel to the Soviet Union, where political doctrine constrained research into intellectual disability. Soviet officials rejected genetic and socioeconomic explanations, encouraged physiological diagnoses, and reported much lower prevalence than the United States. The delegation ultimately found that differing diagnostic practices, rather than actual impairment rates, likely explained the disparity.

The author argues that rising U.S. autism diagnoses similarly reflect broadened diagnostic criteria, substitution for previous labels such as intellectual or learning disability, and improved access among racial, socioeconomic, and gender groups. He cites research showing that increased use of autism classifications corresponded with declines in other disability categories.

Ne’eman contends that the Trump administration disregards these explanations by treating autism as a recent epidemic and allowing political ideology to shape public-health claims. He also criticizes proposed reductions to the Developmental Disabilities Act and Medicaid cuts, which fund services for autistic people and others with disabilities.
More than 50 people escaped unharmed after a UPS fire engulfed Scope Hospital in Lucknow. ICU patients were transferred, and officials ordered a fire-safety compliance probe.

The Houston Astros beat the Chicago White Sox 7-1 for their sixth straight win, completing a three-game sweep with a 27-2 scoring advantage. Jose Altuve’s go-ahead single sparked a five-run seventh inning, Lance McCullers Jr. allowed one run in six innings, and Evan Gattis hit his first homer of the season. Chicago lost its seventh consecutive game. White Sox reliever Danny Farquhar remained in critical but stable condition after collapsing during Friday’s game.

Defending champions India face Bangladesh in the Champions Trophy semi-final at Edgbaston on 15 June. Both teams feature strong batting and varied bowling attacks. The match begins at 3 PM IST, with television coverage on Star Sports Network and online streaming on Hotstar.

Joe Hadzima presents legal issues startups should identify and discuss with advisers, emphasizing that outcomes depend on specific facts and changing laws. He organizes the discussion around intellectual property, legal entities, people, and financing.

Intellectual property can support competitive advantage, fundraising, and business credibility. Trademarks identify the source of goods or services; copyrights protect expression but generally belong to the author unless created by an employee or assigned; trade secrets require confidentiality; and patents provide a time-limited right to exclude others from making, using, selling, importing, or distributing an invention. Patentability generally requires novelty, usefulness, eligible subject matter, adequate disclosure, and non-obviousness. Public disclosure or sale can jeopardize rights, especially outside the United States. Provisional applications can establish an early filing date while delaying the cost of a full application. Startups should prioritize commercially valuable patents and ensure that inventors assign rights to the company.

MIT’s Technology Licensing Office manages university-owned intellectual property arising from funded research or significant use of MIT resources. Startups may obtain options or licenses, sometimes exchanging equity for upfront fees. License revenue is distributed among operating costs, patent expenses, inventors, departments, and MIT.

Technology startups seeking financing commonly use Delaware corporations. Early incorporation and stock issuance can reduce personal liability and avoid tax problems under Internal Revenue Code Section 83. An S corporation election may provide pass-through taxation while eligibility lasts. Founders should address equity division, governance, transfer restrictions, intellectual-property ownership, departures, and team responsibilities early.

Employee compensation may include restricted stock, incentive stock options, or non-qualified options. Equity plans commonly use four-year vesting with a one-year cliff, while considering departures, misconduct, changes of control, and repurchase rights. Startups should not assume equity automatically motivates employees.

Securities offerings generally require registration or an exemption, and improper offers can create criminal or personal liability. Business plans should avoid directly offering a stated ownership percentage for investment.

Financing instruments include common stock, convertible notes, and convertible preferred stock. Convertible notes can postpone valuation decisions. Investors commonly seek preferred returns, protection against dilution, governance rights, and an exit strategy. Liquidation preferences determine payment priority, while participating preferences can provide investors both repayment and equity participation. Anti-dilution provisions adjust conversion rights after lower-priced issuances; full-ratchet protection is especially unfavorable to entrepreneurs, while weighted-average adjustments are more typical.

Toronto homeowners are cashing out after steep price gains and moving to cheaper cities for larger homes, reduced debt and retirement savings. Sarah Blakely sold her renovated Toronto house for more than $1 million and bought a larger Ottawa home, expecting to live mortgage-free.

Toronto agent Josie Stern says the market is cooling as buyers await possible government affordability measures and sellers receive fewer high bids. Still, the Greater Toronto Area’s average sale price reached $916,567, up 33.2 per cent year over year, and the market remains favourable to sellers.

Departing Toronto residents have helped drive price increases in surrounding communities such as Hamilton-Burlington, while buyers are also considering farther markets, including Nova Scotia. Vancouver experienced a similar migration, though luxury demand weakened after British Columbia introduced a foreign buyers’ tax.

Agents caution that hot markets can shift. While some recommend selling before a correction, Stern warns that owners who cash out may regret it if prices continue rising and they cannot afford to buy back into the market.

LeBron James is a four-time NBA champion, four-time MVP and 19-time All-Star who became the league’s highest-earning player and a billionaire through NBA salaries, endorsements and investments. His business interests include Nike, Blaze Pizza, Lobos 1707 tequila, Fenway Sports Group, Canyon Bicycles, Uninterrupted, SpringHill and Manhattan real estate.

James spends heavily on luxury homes, vehicles, family gifts and maintaining his body, while describing himself as frugal about smaller expenses. His philanthropy includes Akron’s I Promise School, college funding through the LeBron James Family Foundation and support for voting initiatives.

Although James has hinted at retirement, an October 2025 announcement teased as “The Second Decision” was ultimately a Hennessy advertisement. He is 41, in the final year of his Lakers contract, and fulfilled his goal of playing alongside his son Bronny in October 2024.

Apple filed a Form 8-K on January 27, 2021, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for its first fiscal quarter ended December 26, 2020. The release is attached as Exhibit 99.1, with Inline XBRL included as Exhibit 104. CFO Luca Maestri signed the filing.

St. Jude researchers identified the kinases Mst1 and Mst2 as regulators of dendritic cell subsets that activate T cells against cancer and infections. Using the NetBID systems biology algorithm to integrate gene-expression and proteomics data, they found that Mst1/2 and the Hippo signaling pathway control dendritic cell function.

CD8α+ dendritic cells, which prime CD8 T cells, were more metabolically active than CD8α- cells. Manipulating their metabolism altered their function and T-cell priming. Mst1/2 also used the NF-κB pathway to stimulate production of interleukin-12, supporting CD8α+ dendritic cell activity and CD8 T-cell responses. The findings suggest potential strategies for treating cancer or immune disorders by modifying dendritic cell activity. Researchers said NetBID could also identify hidden drivers, therapeutic targets, and biomarkers in other biological datasets.

Roman pottery found on Chapel St Leonards beach, following discoveries of a Roman coin and brooch fragment, may indicate a submerged Roman site nearby. Experts previously believed a lost settlement, tower or fort was near Skegness. Lincolnshire County Council urges residents to report coastal archaeological finds for recording.

The Federal Circuit reversed the district court’s denial of Hilite’s motion for judgment as a matter of law in Melchior’s patent-infringement suit involving hydraulic cam phasers that use torque reversals to adjust engine valve timing.

The court held that claims 22–25 of the ’017 patent were anticipated by the prior-art Danckert patent. Melchior’s expert conceded that Danckert disclosed every limitation except an asserted requirement for “direct transfer in a closed line.” The court concluded that this feature was not present in the claim language, claim construction, specifications, or jury instructions and therefore could not distinguish Danckert.

The remaining asserted claims of the ’506 and ’254 patents were held obvious over Danckert in view of Shirai. Shirai disclosed the rotary cam-phaser and complementary sub-chamber features absent from Danckert, and Melchior did not challenge Hilite’s rationale for combining the references beyond the rejected “direct transfer” argument. The court declined to address infringement and other appealed issues.

Judge Newman concurred only in the judgment of no liability. She concluded that substantial evidence supported the jury’s finding that Danckert did not anticipate the claims, but found insufficient evidence of infringement because the parties stipulated that operation with the external oil pump supplying oil was noninfringing, and Melchior failed to show that the accused devices sealed off the pump during transitional operation.

The passage examines the 2018 Baku Declaration of the Non-Aligned Movement and the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting Communiqué, focusing on their implications for India and the Global South. Both documents oppose protectionism, support multilateral trade and address the Doha Development Round. The author argues, however, that neither adequately challenges structural inequalities in global economic governance, unequal North-South trade, debt dependence or limited market access.

The Baku Declaration reaffirms policy autonomy, South-South cooperation and support for Palestinian self-determination. It condemns Israeli occupation, settlements, violence against Palestinians and measures altering the occupied Syrian Golan. It also promotes tolerance, diversity, human rights and opposition to discrimination. The passage questions India’s commitment to NAM principles and notes criticism of the Modi government’s treatment of minorities and Dalits.

The CHOGM Communiqué seeks expanded intra-Commonwealth trade while recognizing the debt, financing, climate and financial-access problems confronting small and vulnerable states. It supports international action for refugees and migrants, condemns violence against the Rohingya and calls for their safe, dignified return to Myanmar under UNHCR oversight. The passage contrasts this position with India’s resistance to obligations toward Rohingya refugees.

The author concludes that, despite useful commitments on refugees, occupation, crimes and intolerance, both documents insufficiently address fundamental economic challenges. The forthcoming NAM summit is presented as an opportunity for Global South countries to pursue alternative strategies on trade, technology, markets, currencies and autonomous policymaking.

The passage specifies SD Memory Card command behavior, protection, switching, status, timing, and performance.

Card Ownership Protection (COP) uses CMD42. COP Unlock enables CMD42 version 2.0 operations; cards without COP reject requests and set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED. A Force Erase Password (FEP) may be set, replaced, or cleared using correctly sized data blocks and matching old credentials. Setting FEP disables ordinary Force Erase and password reset, while clearing it restores those functions and disables COP operations. With FEP set, a card starts locked after reset and requires COP Unlock before other CMD42 operations. Ordinary Force Erase clears card data and PWD registers and unlocks the card, but is blocked when FEP is set. FEP Force Erase requires a matching FEP, erases card data and PWD registers, unlocks the card, and preserves FEP. CMD42 errors set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED; password lengths must be 1–128 bits. Locked cards reject ACMD6 and most commands.

CMD55 causes the next command to be interpreted as an application-specific command when defined. Repeated CMD55 commands preserve this behavior for the command immediately following the last CMD55. Undefined or illegal ACMDs follow specified status and error handling, with special rules for ACMD41.

CMD6 checks or switches card functions. Defined groups include Access Mode, Command System, Driver Strength, and Power Limit. Mode 0 reports support, readiness, selected functions, and maximum current or power; Mode 1 performs switching. Invalid selections cancel switching, while busy functions retain their current setting. Function 0 is the default and 0xF preserves the current function. CMD6 returns a 512-bit status block. Power Limit defaults to 0.72 W and may be raised according to host power, thermal, connector, and card requirements.

High-Speed mode provides a 25 MB/s interface using a 50 MHz clock and is optionally selected through CMD6. Command-system switching changes the interpretation of reserved commands. CMD8 checks host voltage compatibility for Version 2.00 or later cards and returns an R7 response echoing voltage and check pattern when accepted.

SDSC cards use byte addressing and CMD16-defined block lengths; SDHC and SDXC use 512-byte block addressing and fixed 512-byte memory-access blocks. Hosts may alter or stop the clock subject to transaction-completion rules. CRC7 protects commands and most responses, while CRC16 protects data blocks. CRC or illegal-command errors leave card state unchanged and set corresponding status bits.

The passage defines read, write, erase, and busy timeouts; four command types; 48-bit command formatting; command classes; response formats; card, SD, and task status; and UHS-II command differences. It also defines Speed Class, UHS Speed Grade, and Video Speed Class methods. Performance is organized around Allocation Units and Recording Units, with write, move, read, fragmentation, and FAT-update behavior used to characterize real-time recording performance.

Norwegian schools often use digital technology only at a basic level despite strong infrastructure and curricular requirements for digital competence. Research suggests technology and flipped learning (FL)—where students study concepts before class and use class time for active learning—may improve motivation, engagement, collaboration, and learning in physical education (PE) and physical education teacher education (PETE), although evidence in PETE remains limited.

This qualitative study examined 22 Norwegian PETE students’ perceptions of FL. Across two semesters, students completed 11 flipped lessons in practical dance and theoretical motor learning units. They watched 10–20-minute instructional videos before participating in student-centred classroom activities. Group interviews were analyzed using constructivist grounded theory methods.

Five themes emerged: expectations, simple input, deep learning, a supportive learning environment, and challenges. Videos clarified learning expectations, encouraged preparation through peer pressure, and were perceived as more accessible and efficient than assigned readings. Students reported stronger understanding because they could pause, repeat, and revisit content, then discuss and apply it in class. Advance preparation reduced uncertainty, particularly in dance, and supported active participation and collaboration. Challenges included technical difficulties, increased time demands, and the inability to ask teachers immediate questions while preparing.

Overall, students viewed FL as useful and motivating, reporting greater class engagement and improved learning. They also considered it a potential tool for their future PE teaching. The study was limited by its initial focus on motivation and learning and by collecting data from one institution. Further research should examine digital technology implementation in PETE and how teachers’ technological, pedagogical, and content knowledge affects school PE.

Peter Joseph Saville, a Worthing dentist who cared for thousands of patients over four decades, died peacefully at home on June 27, aged 90. Born in Ilford in 1928, he studied dentistry at Guy’s Hospital and served as an Army dental surgeon in Cyprus and Egypt before moving to Worthing with his wife, Josephine, in 1954. He later established his practice in West Park Lane.

Saville was active in local hockey, golf, tennis and squash, helping found the Manor Sports Club’s squash section and serving as Worthing Hockey Club president. A devoted Catholic, he was a Eucharistic minister, Lourdes carer and pilgrim, longtime Catenian Association member, and charity supporter. His family remembered him as kind, selfless and joyful. He is survived by Josephine, six children and eight grandchildren. His funeral will be held at Saint Mary of the Angels on July 12, followed by burial at Durrington Cemetery.

The Alabama Supreme Court answered a certified Eleventh Circuit question, holding that an insurance policy covering constitutional or civil-rights violations is neither ambiguous nor illusory merely because it defines insured employees as those acting within the scope of their duties.

Janice Shrader and Debra Livingston alleged that Attalla police officer Fletcher Mallard and bailiff Barnie Gilliland sexually abused them while they were detained. After settling their claims, they sought coverage under the City of Attalla’s Employers Mutual Casualty Company linebacker policy. A federal district court ruled that the policy did not cover the conduct because it fell outside the employees’ scope of duties.

The Court held that its earlier Titan decisions did not control. Titan I concerned conflicting provisions covering intentional offenses while excluding intended injuries, and Titan II relied solely on law-of-the-case principles. Neither resolved the relationship between civil-rights coverage and a scope-of-duties limitation.

The Court explained that conduct under color of state law may occur either within or outside an employee’s scope of employment. Because some civil-rights violations can satisfy both standards, the scope limitation does not eliminate civil-rights coverage or make it illusory. The limitation is also not inherently ambiguous, and insurers may lawfully provide narrow coverage. Therefore, the policy must be enforced as written.

Nobel laureate Peter Agre will give a free public lecture on science advocacy, human rights, diplomacy and global disease May 9 at the University of Louisville. The Johns Hopkins professor discovered aquaporins and has led scientific diplomacy visits to several countries to promote collaboration and reduce tensions.

Historical evidence cited suggests U.S. stocks have often performed reasonably well and shown lower volatility during wars, particularly when conflicts occurred abroad. During World War II, the market fell nearly 20% after Pearl Harbor but recovered within months, and the Dow gained more than 60% in real terms before the war ended. A study of U.S. stocks from 1890 to 2017 found war periods had less volatility, with higher defense spending associated with lower volatility.

Markets may initially decline as they anticipate conflict, then recover as war is discounted and government spending increases economic activity. However, wars fought on home soil can cause severe infrastructure damage, market closures, nationalization, and major investor losses, as illustrated by Germany, Russia, and Ukraine-related events.

Gold often rises during uncertainty and anticipated monetary expansion, while commodities such as oil may benefit from disrupted supply chains. Nevertheless, commodities have been difficult to predict and have delivered poorer long-term returns than stocks. Overall, market effects differ substantially depending on whether war occurs domestically or abroad.

The study demonstrates a chirality-selective nanoscale thermal switch using ferromagnetic [Co/Pt] multilayers coupled to chiral α-SiO₂. Laser-induced demagnetization generates chiral phonons in [Co/Pt], with angular momentum determined by magnetization direction. These phonons transfer energy and angular momentum into α-SiO₂, where heat transport is enhanced when phonon angular momentum matches the material’s chirality.

Time-resolved magneto-optic Kerr measurements found that reversing magnetization changes α-SiO₂’s apparent thermal conductivity by about 7%, or 0.7±0.1 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. The response reverses between left- and right-handed α-SiO₂, while amorphous non-chiral SiO₂ shows negligible dependence. The thermal on/off ratio is approximately 1.07 at room temperature under direct optical excitation, falling to 1.02 with an Al transducer that weakens demagnetization.

First-principles-based molecular dynamics simulations reproduce chirality-dependent heat propagation and attribute it to angular-momentum-polarized acoustic phonon branches in α-SiO₂. Heat-transfer efficiency depends on phonon rotation, frequency, group velocity, density of states, and integrated angular momentum.

Cooling enhances switching performance: the on/off ratio reaches about 1.2 at 50 K, roughly four times the room-temperature contrast, because reduced phonon-phonon scattering improves angular-momentum transport. The results establish a magnetic-field-controlled thermal diode and switch in an electrically insulating chiral material.

The Economist’s “Carrie Bradshaw index” ranks major US cities by studio affordability, comparing median wages with the salary needed to keep rent below 30% of gross income. Of the cities assessed, 59 were broadly affordable, down from 62 last year. Coastal cities were least affordable, led by New York, while Sun Belt and Midwestern cities generally ranked better. High demand, low vacancies, population growth, and limited housing construction contributed to unaffordability.

The study examined whether short-term outdoor temperature drops were associated with worsening COVID-19 during the 2022 Omicron wave in Tomsk, Russia. It proposed that infection compromises airway epithelium, making it more vulnerable to cooling, which may reduce antiviral responses and mucociliary clearance.

Daily temperatures and COVID-19 hospitalizations from January through March 2022 were analyzed using a case-crossover approach, with hospitalization and pneumonia serving as proxies for disease severity. The authors identified 14 periods when temperature fell by more than 3°C; all were associated with hospitalization spikes after 1–2 days. Temperature was characterized as the primary trigger in eight periods and an additional factor in six. Of 17 hospitalization surges, three were attributed to other factors.

The study lacked direct severity measurements and acknowledged that weather, pollution, physiological, social, and behavioral factors may overlap. It recommends further mechanistic research on humidity, airway supersaturation, air pollution, and mathematical analysis of interacting influences. The authors suggest temperature forecasts could help anticipate hospitalization increases and support timely healthcare preparation.

Successful school-based mental health programs rely on family-school-community collaboration, involvement from existing school staff and teachers, and integration of community-based clinicians into school culture. Programs should adapt to local needs while making services visible, accessible and less stigmatized.

Minnesota developed a nationally recognized model that uses insurance and state funding to support clinicians’ counseling and collaboration with teachers and schools. Baltimore expanded school-based care after transportation, childcare and stigma limited attendance at outside appointments. Its providers promote services through classroom presentations, social media and events. Both models reflect work pioneered by the University of Maryland, emphasizing that children are more likely to receive care when providers work where students are. Minnesota’s programs now receive private and public insurance funding plus $20 million from the state.

Jaime Smith’s guide for prospective transfer students is praised as clear, organized and practical, with case studies reflecting varied student backgrounds. Aimed mainly at community college students transferring to four-year institutions, it advises preserving syllabi and textbook information, choosing withdrawals over failing grades when appropriate, prioritizing institutional fit over prestige, researching housing costs, and distinguishing university admission from admission to a major.

The reviewer recommends consulting community college transfer advisers because websites may not clarify articulation agreements, credit limits, elective status, scholarships or differing course requirements. The main criticism is Smith’s vague treatment of whether students should complete an associate degree before transferring. Degree completion may be required for statewide general education transfer agreements, reduce credit loss, address concerns about low grades or dual-enrollment courses, and provide a credential if bachelor’s studies are interrupted. Despite this omission, the book is considered accessible and useful for its intended audience.

Voluntary medical male circumcision reduces heterosexual HIV acquisition risk, but sex before the recommended 42-day healing period can cause complications and increase HIV transmission risks. Using self-reported data from four Rakai Community Cohort Study rounds, researchers assessed early sex resumption among recently medically circumcised Ugandan men aged 15–49 from 2013–2020.

Early sex resumption declined from 45.1% in 2013–2015 to 14.9% in 2018–2020. Across pooled adjusted analyses, it was more common among men aged 25–44, currently or previously married men, those with multiple recent sexual partners, and those with primary rather than post-primary education. HIV status and occupation were not independently associated with early resumption. The authors suggest targeted counseling for married men, their female partners, men with multiple partners, and men with lower education. Limitations included reliance on self-reports and inability to determine HIV status at circumcision.

A Phase 1/2 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study evaluated mifepristone in 32 non-treatment-seeking individuals with alcohol use disorder. Participants received mifepristone 600 mg/day or placebo for seven days, followed by yohimbine, alcohol-cue exposure, an alcohol prime, and open-bar self-administration; treatments were separated by a three-week washout.

Mifepristone co-administered with yohimbine and alcohol produced no serious adverse events and did not alter alcohol pharmacokinetics or subjective stimulation and sedation. Compared with placebo, it lowered diastolic blood pressure and attenuated alcohol craving and urge during the first cue trial, while reducing cue-elicited salivation during both trials. It increased cortisol, but cortisol did not mediate reductions in craving, urge, or salivation.

Family history density of alcoholism moderated some effects. Participants with high family history density reported greater craving and urge, while mifepristone significantly reduced these outcomes mainly among those with low family history density. Salivation decreased in both family-history groups. Mifepristone did not significantly reduce alcohol consumption in either the laboratory or outpatient settings.

The study supports the safety of mifepristone with yohimbine and alcohol and provides preliminary evidence that it may reduce stress- and cue-induced alcohol craving independently of cortisol increases. Limitations included the absence of a yohimbine-placebo condition, no measurement of mifepristone blood concentrations, and low female enrollment. Higher-dose studies are recommended to identify treatment-response biomarkers and likely responders.

Ronald E. Gabler appealed his aggravated-assault conviction and the denial of his amended motion for a new trial. Evidence showed that after following his estranged wife to Thomas Duff’s home, Gabler encountered Duff, repeatedly struck, bit, choked, kicked, and stomped him, then dragged him into Duff’s house and photographed him. Duff suffered facial injuries requiring emergency helicopter transport, intensive-care monitoring, surgery, and hospitalization. The court found the evidence sufficient to support the conviction.

Gabler alleged ineffective assistance because trial counsel did not investigate Duff’s medical records or interview his physicians and failed to object to testimony concerning Gabler’s character. Applying the two-part Strickland test, the court found counsel’s decision not to pursue medical evidence was reasonable trial strategy intended to avoid emphasizing Duff’s injuries while advancing a mutual-combat defense. The omitted medical evidence would not likely have changed the verdict and contained potentially damaging references to head injury, concussion, contusions, monitoring, and plastic surgery. The State was not required to prove life-threatening injuries, and the jury could find that Gabler’s fists were used as deadly weapons.

The court also found no prejudicial deficiency regarding character testimony because Gabler introduced extensive character evidence and insisted, against counsel’s advice, on calling a minister whose cross-examination disclosed prior allegations of abuse. The denial of a new trial was affirmed.

The lecture introduces loop diagrams and quantum fluctuations beyond tree-level QED. Unlike tree diagrams, whose internal momenta are fixed by external momenta, loops contain free internal momenta integrated over all values. These integrals commonly diverge at high energies and momenta, reflecting extrapolation of QED to arbitrarily short distances.

In the late 1940s, Feynman, Schwinger, and Tomonaga developed renormalization methods to remove these divergences and obtain physically sensible predictions. Freeman Dyson later simplified and disseminated these methods. Although initially regarded as mathematical tricks, renormalization gained a physical basis through Ken Wilson’s later work on the renormalization group.

Loops represent vacuum fluctuations and modify electron and photon propagators and the electron-photon vertex. Consequently, the physical electron mass, charge, and fields differ from the bare parameters and fields in the QED Lagrangian. Electron self-energy shifts the propagator pole and changes its residue. Photon corrections preserve its zero mass because of gauge invariance but renormalize the field strength. Vertex corrections renormalize charge in a manner consistent with gauge symmetry and also generate the electron’s anomalous magnetic moment.

Taking the nonrelativistic limit of the Dirac equation yields the Pauli equation and predicts an electron magnetic-moment factor \(g=2\). Loop corrections make \(g\) slightly larger. Schwinger’s 1948 calculation found the leading correction proportional to \(\alpha/(2\pi)\), agreeing closely with experiment. Higher-order calculations involve rapidly increasing numbers of diagrams, while measurements reach precision near \(10^{-12}\), demonstrating QED’s strong agreement with nature.

This study analyzed bulk RNA sequencing from 38 granulomatous myositis (GM) muscle biopsies and compared their transcriptomic profiles with other inflammatory, genetic, and normal muscle samples. Spatial transcriptomics, immunohistochemistry, pathway analysis, and machine-learning models were also used.

GM showed strong activation of the IFNγ pathway, high type II HLA expression, and increased macrophage, CD4 T-cell, B-cell, plasma-cell, immunoglobulin, cytokine, chemokine, and checkpoint-related markers. IL1B, TNF, TGFB1, and their associated pathways were elevated. Structural muscle and mitochondrial markers were reduced. Spatial analysis localized key inflammatory features, including IFNγ signaling and IL1B, TNF, and TGFB1 production, to non-caseating granulomas.

Researchers identified 1,293 specifically upregulated and 256 specifically downregulated GM genes. These gene sets correlated strongly with transcriptomic markers of inflammation, muscle differentiation, mitochondrial function, and muscle atrophy. Upregulated genes were predominantly associated with highly active, terminally differentiated macrophages in granulomas. CHIT1 was the most significantly upregulated gene, with protein expression confirmed in granulomas and giant cells.

Machine-learning classifiers based on the GM-specific gene sets distinguished GM from other muscle conditions. The best-performing support vector machine achieved an area under the ROC curve of 99.6% and accuracy of 98.6%.

The findings identify potential diagnostic and disease-monitoring markers and inflammatory pathways that may inform therapeutic research. Limitations included the absence of infectious or genetic granulomatous muscle diseases and protein-level validation only for CHIT1.

This retrospective study compared REM sleep microstructure in 20 patients with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD), 20 with Parkinson’s disease and RBD (PD+RBD), and 20 matched controls using polysomnography. Researchers assessed phasic REM sleep, sawtooth waves (STW), REM sleep without atonia, and NREM-to-REM transitions.

Patients with iRBD had a higher phasic REM sleep proportion and more REM sleep without atonia than the other groups. Patients with PD+RBD had less and shorter REM sleep, longer REM latency, and lower-density, shorter STW bursts. Both patient groups showed STW spectral shifts toward higher frequencies. NREM-to-REM transitions progressively lengthened from controls to iRBD and PD+RBD, while transition-event sequences also differed. The findings indicate that RBD involves REM sleep abnormalities beyond loss of muscle atonia and dream enactment. Limitations included small samples, medication use in the PD+RBD group, heterogeneous recordings, and the absence of a PD group without RBD. Longitudinal research is needed to assess whether these features predict disease progression or conversion to α-synucleinopathies.

Elina Svitolina won the 2017 Rogers Cup in Toronto, defeating Caroline Wozniacki 6-4, 6-0 after beating four top-ten opponents. She dropped only one set in five matches and lost six games across her final two matches, despite fatigue, hot conditions and playing three matches within roughly 30 hours.

The victory was the 22-year-old Ukrainian’s fifth title of 2017 and her second Premier final win over Wozniacki that year. It also made her the first woman to win three Premier 5 titles in one season and improved her 2017 finals record to 5-0. Svitolina credited experience, persistence, positivity and managing pressure for her success.

Although the title raised her world ranking to fourth, Svitolina emphasized taking one tournament and match at a time. She acknowledged having nerves but said athletes must learn to manage them and find a comfortable competitive mindset. Looking ahead to Cincinnati and the US Open, she viewed her form and mental strength positively while remaining focused on her own expectations and goals rather than others’ assessments.

The lecture reviews control of the double integrator \(q̈=u\), contrasting manually chosen linear feedback with bounded minimum-time bang-bang control. Pontryagin’s minimum principle verifies local optimality along trajectories, while dynamic programming recursively defines optimal cost-to-go functions.

Taking the continuous-time limit of dynamic programming yields the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, which provides sufficient conditions for optimality when the value function is smooth. Applying it to linear dynamics with quadratic state and control costs produces the linear quadratic regulator. Assuming a quadratic value function leads to the Riccati equation; solving it determines the optimal feedback \(u=-R^{-1}B^TSx\). Finite-horizon gains vary with time, while the infinite-horizon solution is the Riccati equation’s steady state.

For the double integrator, the resulting LQR controller produces stable, oscillatory convergence to the origin. LQR offers systematic tuning through state-cost matrix \(Q\) and control-cost matrix \(R\), and extends to complex linear systems or local linearizations.

HJB requires differentiable value functions, making it unsuitable at discontinuities arising in bang-bang minimum-time control. Pontryagin’s principle remains applicable there because it evaluates local optimality along individual trajectories. Both analytical approaches become difficult for nonlinear dynamics, motivating later numerical algorithms based on these foundations.

Energy Central’s January 25, 2002 newsletter highlights Enron’s collapse, including Ken Lay’s resignation, congressional hearings, Andersen’s document destruction, regulatory investigations, lawsuits, employee retirement losses, and allegations of hidden losses and market manipulation. Other coverage includes PG&E’s bankruptcy restructuring, utility regulation, power pricing and projects, environmental and nuclear issues, renewable-energy developments, corporate earnings, and international energy markets.

Canadian studies involving 459 heterosexual university students found a correlation between higher facial width-to-height ratios and stronger sex drives and more permissive attitudes toward infidelity, particularly among men. Researchers measured faces and surveyed participants about sexual desire and fidelity. However, the findings do not establish that wide-faced people are more likely to cheat, and the studies’ small, unusually young sample limits firm conclusions. Critics caution against using appearance to judge potential partners.

Its contents begin with diplomatic correspondence concerning the Chinese-Japanese War, dated 1893–1894, primarily involving Seoul, Peking, and Washington.

Emma Watson received ELLE’s Woman of the Year award for acting and gender-equality campaigning. Other winners included Debbie Harry, Riz Ahmed, Sasha Lane, and Christine and the Queens. Beth Ditto, Thandie Newton, and Vivienne Westwood also attended the London ceremony.

Hedge funds are privately offered investment pools managed for accredited investors and institutions, typically requiring high minimum investments. They trade relatively liquid assets and may use short selling, leverage, derivatives, and complex risk-management techniques. Unlike private equity funds, they are generally open-ended, allowing periodic investments and withdrawals.

Common hedge fund strategies include long/short equity, event-driven, global macro, relative value, fixed-income arbitrage, trend following, and merger arbitrage. Strategies may be systematic, discretionary, concentrated, or diversified. Niche funds focus on areas such as real estate, insurance-linked instruments, or cryptocurrencies.

Many hedge funds seek market-neutral returns by combining long and short positions. Long/short equity involves buying undervalued stocks and selling overvalued ones, while merger arbitrage exploits pricing differences surrounding acquisitions. Diversifying among strategies with low correlations can smooth returns and reduce drawdowns; correlation between strategies may be more important than individual backtest performance.

Operating like a “one-man hedge fund” requires adequate capital, professional planning, record-keeping, access to multiple asset classes, diversification, and sustained effort. Hedge fund advantages include potential higher returns, professional management, diversification, and access to unique investments. Risks include illiquidity, leverage, counterparties, strategy failure, high fees, and performance restrictions.

Minimum investments commonly range from $100,000 to $500,000. Hedge funds typically report quarterly and may have tax implications requiring professional advice.
