VentureWire’s October 18, 2000 issue reports major technology financing and acquisitions. Jamcracker raised over $100 million; Edgix secured $50 million; KnowledgeNet raised $30 million; Broadbeam obtained $29 million; and CoVia raised over $25 million. Broadcom agreed to acquire Allayer for about $264 million, while SonicWall agreed to buy Phobos for $258.9 million.

Other coverage includes numerous early- and later-stage investments, product launches and company renamings. Wine.com, Tellium, SimplyDone, Provider HealthNet Services, and Mass Medium announced acquisitions. Several technology companies appointed directors and executives, including new leaders at How2TV, APPower!, Impower, Evoke, UpShot, Rebel.com, The Deal, Sakonnet Technology, and eBizJets.

In venture capital news, Delta Ventures launched a $60 million Israeli fund, Velocity Capital raised $7 million for early-stage Northwest companies, and Nash, Sells & Partners announced its renaming as Sovereign Capital and plans for a new fund. Ignition, SSM Ventures, Bay Partners, and Anila Fund also announced senior personnel appointments.

Trust Co. of Vermont increased its United Technologies position by 2.3% in the third quarter, holding 115,963 shares worth $11.78 million. The stock represented 1.5% of its portfolio and was its 14th-largest position. Other investors also modestly increased holdings, while institutional investors and hedge funds owned 78.26% of the company.

United Technologies traded at $109.62, with a $90.26 billion market capitalization. Quarterly earnings were $1.76 per share, exceeding the $1.67 estimate, while revenue rose 4.1% to $14.40 billion. Analysts projected annual earnings of $6.60 per share. The company paid a $0.66 quarterly dividend, equivalent to a 2.41% yield.

Analysts assigned a consensus “Hold” rating and an average price target of $112.82. Director Brian C. Rogers purchased 5,000 shares for $539,700, while Vice President Robert J. Bailey sold 967 shares for $102,946.82. United Technologies provides technology products and services to global building systems and aerospace industries.

The passage calls for expanded defense research, restored U.S. intelligence capabilities, fewer congressional restrictions on covert actions, and broader international broadcasting to promote American ideals and counter communist propaganda. It advocates strengthening NATO and relations with Japan and other allies, improving policy consultation, and creating a North American Accord to combine continental resources, technology, and capital. Military strength is described as essential but a last resort, while Carter administration policies are criticized as weak and unpredictable. An editorial note recounts a May 1, 1980, interview with presidential candidate Ronald Reagan following the failed Iran hostage rescue. Reagan argued that the hostages and the region’s strategic situation were inseparable, warning that their continued detention threatened the United States and Americans serving abroad.

The study examines how ultraviolet femtosecond-laser irradiation modifies 190 nm-thick niobium films by forming laser-induced periodic surface structures (LIPSS). Films and transport bridges were fabricated, patterned at varying pulse energies, and characterized using electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, resistivity, SQUID magnetometry, magneto-optical imaging, and time-dependent Ginzburg–Landau simulations.

Increasing pulse energy produced quasi-one-dimensional ripples with a period of about 260 nm, accompanied by reduced film thickness, increased grain size near ripple peaks, and lattice compression. Fully formed LIPSS reduced the superconducting critical temperature by approximately 0.3 K and the upper critical field by about 50 mT, independently of ripple orientation.

LIPSS created anisotropic flux pinning. Critical currents were higher parallel than perpendicular to the ripples, with optimized films outperforming pristine samples mainly below about 100 mT and between 6 and 8 K. The anisotropy developed with ripple formation and approached unity near the upper critical field. Simulations attributed this behavior to vortices preferentially occupying thinner ripple valleys, which impede motion across the corrugations. Thickness variations below 100 nm approximately doubled the current capacity along the channels. The results establish correlations between laser-processing conditions, microstructure, superconducting parameters, and anisotropic critical-current behavior, supporting laser patterning as a method for fabricating superconducting circuit elements.

PHIVE is an unsupervised, physics-informed variational autoencoder developed for rapid metabolite quantification and uncertainty estimation in high-resolution whole-brain MRSI. Its convolutional encoder estimates metabolite amplitude, frequency, phase, and damping, while a physics-based decoder reconstructs spectra. A five-model ensemble estimates aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty, and a conditional spline baseline permits adjustable flexibility without training separate networks.

The framework was evaluated against LCModel using 7T MRSI data from 12 healthy subjects: eight provided 122,473 training spectra and four provided 39,051 test spectra. PHIVE generated metabolite maps broadly similar to LCModel, with strong positive correlations across six metabolite ratios. It generally produced lower coefficients of variation, particularly for Glx and mIns, although mIns estimates were significantly higher and tCho and mIns showed greater discrepancies. Baseline stiffness affected metabolites differently, especially mIns.

PHIVE processed a whole-brain dataset in 6 milliseconds, compared with approximately two hours for LCModel. It remained robust across varying signal-to-noise ratios and produced CRLB, epistemic, and aleatoric uncertainty maps, with greater uncertainty in low-SNR regions.

Limitations include the absence of ground-truth concentrations, a small sample, no separate frequency-correction step, reduced specificity for some metabolites, limited interpretability, and lack of longitudinal validation. The study concludes that PHIVE offers rapid, uncertainty-aware MRSI quantification but requires validation across larger and more diverse datasets.

Knees experience lifelong wear and tear, but injury risk can be reduced through healthy weight management, regular activity, strong supporting muscles, and flexibility exercises. Strengthening the hamstrings, quadriceps, glutes, and hip flexors supports the knees, while stretching improves motion and balance. Low-impact cardio such as cycling and swimming promotes circulation without excessive joint impact.

Persistent pain or limited mobility should be assessed by a physiotherapist. Tailored strengthening and flexibility exercises can aid recovery, prevent recurrence, restore movement, and sometimes delay or avoid surgery. Recommended exercises include quadriceps extensions, bridges, wall squats, calf and quadriceps stretches, and knee-to-chest stretches. Pain should not be ignored, though appropriate movement can prevent stiffness and compensation-related damage.

Knee surgery is most common among people over 50, with osteoarthritis a leading cause. When physiotherapy cannot rehabilitate severe damage, surgery may improve motion and quality of life, although it carries risks such as infection and deep vein thrombosis. More than four in five total knee replacements and seven in ten partial replacements last 25 years. Regular physiotherapy after surgery can accelerate recovery and protect the replacement.

Actors Daisy McCrackin and Joseph Capone were allegedly kidnapped from McCrackin’s Los Angeles home by Keith Andre Stewart, Johntae Jones and Amber Neal. Capone was pistol-whipped, stripped and held without food in a bathtub for 30 hours, while McCrackin was forced to obtain at least $US10,000 for his release. She escaped after being returned home and alerted police. The three suspects face 17 charges, including kidnapping, firearm assault, grand theft, mayhem, conspiracy and methamphetamine possession for sale. Stewart and Jones could receive life without parole; Neal faces up to life imprisonment.

Invictus MD Strategies received $5.78 million from the exercise of 4.35 million warrants and 337,500 options during its fiscal year beginning February 1, 2018. The proceeds will support construction and operations, with cannabis production capacity projected to grow from 56,000 square feet to 262,000 by year-end 2018 and 846,000 by year-end 2019. The company has approximately 9.9 million warrants and 9.4 million options outstanding, potentially generating another $34.6 million. It also granted 120,000 five-year incentive stock options at $1.50 per share. Invictus operates or invests in cannabis production, vaporizer technology, and fertilizer businesses. Its production forecasts are subject to construction, regulatory, market, and operational risks.

The passage warns that democracy is threatened equally by violent demagogues who incite mobs against the rich and corrupt reactionaries who enable exploitation by the wealthy. Both disregard others’ rights and may unite against efforts to ensure equal justice. It urges limits on railroad employees’ working hours, broader adoption and enforcement of the eight-hour day where conditions permit, and summer half holidays for government employees. It also supports investigation into child and women’s labor, emphasizing their broad effects on national home life. While states must address child labor individually, a federal investigation could inform the public and encourage unified action. Congress should immediately enact a strict child-labor law for the District of Columbia and the Territories.

The Education Department restarted loan forgiveness for eligible income-based repayment borrowers with 25 years of on-time payments. Processing may be delayed by furloughs, potentially exposing borrowers to taxes after the federal exemption expires Dec. 31.

Wall Street Week reviewed a turbulent 2000 in which the Dow fell just over 6%, the S&P 500 lost more than 10%, and the Nasdaq plunged over 39%, ending more than 51% below its March peak. The economy’s growth slowed, unemployment remained near 4%, oil prices retreated from September highs, the dollar strengthened, and the trade deficit headed for another record.

Panelists identified corporate earnings, consumer confidence, mutual-fund flows, interest rates, and the dollar as key issues for 2001. Brian Rogers expected corporate profit growth of 5–7% and Federal Reserve rate cuts totaling 50–75 basis points. Barbara Marcin did not predict a recession but remained concerned about weakening consumer confidence. Louis Holland saw a greater than 50% chance of recession and believed the Fed might cut rates by half a point. Elizabeth Dater emphasized interest rates, capital preservation, and the risk that a weaker dollar could reduce foreign investment.

Their 2000 portfolios outperformed major indexes: Rogers gained 42.5%, Marcin more than 40%, Holland more than 28%, and Dater more than 7.5%. For 2001, all four projected higher year-end Dow closes, while their Nasdaq forecasts varied. Their recommendations included technology, telecommunications, financial, consumer, industrial, energy, and healthcare stocks. Dater allocated 25% to three-year Treasury notes, with the remainder divided among established companies. The transcript also listed 2001 market forecasts and investment selections from 22 panelists.

The 4-Verticals concept sends four receivers vertically to stretch defenses horizontally and vertically, create one-on-one matchups, and exploit zone voids while allowing a relatively quick throw. It works well against man coverage by targeting favorable matchups and against Cover 3 by looking off the free safety and attacking seams above the linebackers. It is less effective against Cover 4 and soft zones, especially on third-and-long; horizontal concepts may be preferable.

Against two-high defenses, the tight end and slot occupy designated hashes, outside receivers run go routes, and the running back checks protection before releasing. Against one-high defenses, the slot occupies the seam, while outside receivers may convert go routes into comebacks if they lack separation at 15 yards.

The quarterback must identify safeties, man or zone coverage, and favorable matchups before the snap, avoid staring down receivers, then target a downfield matchup or zone void before checking down to the running back. Variations from 3x1 and empty formations preserve receiver landmarks while isolating receivers, influencing the free safety, or adding a shallow crossing route against blitzes and deep coverage.

This study examined behavioural changes across behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), semantic dementia (SD), and intermediate presentations using informant questionnaires, neuropsychological testing, and structural MRI. Participants included 47 people with FTD—26 with bvFTD and 21 with SD—and 18 age-matched controls.

Both bvFTD and SD showed broad behavioural impairment compared with controls, although changes were generally more severe in bvFTD. No behaviours were significantly more prevalent in SD, indicating quantitative rather than qualitative differences between the syndromes. Principal component analysis identified three behavioural dimensions: apathy, challenging behaviours, and impairment in activities of daily living. Apathy and challenging behaviours were greater in bvFTD, while activities of daily living did not differ significantly between FTD subtypes.

Semantic memory and executive-function measures discriminated bvFTD from SD more accurately than behavioural measures, achieving 95.1% accuracy when combined. Patient self-ratings of apathy differed substantially from caregiver ratings, particularly in bvFTD, supporting the clinical importance of informant reports.

MRI showed predominantly prefrontal atrophy in bvFTD and bilateral anterior temporal lobe atrophy in SD, with anatomical overlap between syndromes. Greater apathy was associated with poorer executive function and anterior cingulate cortex atrophy. Impaired daily functioning was associated with overall disease severity. Behavioural changes were not associated with semantic knowledge or anterior temporal lobe volume in the questionnaire-based analyses.

The findings support viewing FTD as a graded clinical and anatomical spectrum rather than as strictly separate categories. They also support conceptualising left- and right-predominant SD as variants of one disorder. The authors recommend semantic-memory and executive-function testing for diagnostic discrimination and emphasise that the cross-sectional design, incomplete coverage of possible behaviours, caregiver-rating influences, and participants’ disease duration limit the conclusions.

Brent Honeywell allowed four hits and struck out seven without a walk over six innings as Triple-A Durham shut out Columbus, 11-0. Pitching coach Kyle Snyder praised the Rays’ No. 2 prospect’s body control, adjustments, pitch command and two-strike execution. Since his promotion from Double-A Montgomery, Honeywell has a 4.22 ERA, 1.32 WHIP and 71 strikeouts in 11 starts. Brad Boxberger struck out all three batters in the seventh, while Ryne Stanek and Adam Kolarek completed the shutout. Rehabbing catcher Wilson Ramos went 1-for-3, and Shane Peterson finished a triple short of the cycle with two RBIs.

Founded in 2004, Yunnan Lucky Air grew rapidly as a low-cost carrier serving tourist routes from Kunming. By 2007, it carried 1.2 million passengers, earned US$104.3 million in operating revenue, and achieved profitability. Its Southwest-inspired model used one aircraft type, coach-only service, simple pricing, and short point-to-point routes. However, government controls over fuel, landing fees, aircraft leasing, taxes, routes, and fares limited its cost advantage to about 5% below the industry average.

China’s expanding aviation market attracted growing competition, including numerous low-cost entrants. Lucky Air therefore sought advantages beyond price, particularly through e-commerce. Yet Chinese airline tickets were still predominantly sold through agents, while limited Internet and credit-card penetration, security concerns, expensive payment systems, and regional disparities constrained online purchasing. Although Lucky Air offered fully online booking, payment, validation, refunds, discounts, travel information, blogs, and loyalty points, direct consumer purchases represented only 1% of total ticket sales.

Western airlines demonstrated that e-commerce could reduce service costs, improve customer relationships, increase purchases, and build loyalty through online communities, reviews, self-service, alternative payments, and targeted services for corporate travelers, students, and loyalty-program members. Lucky Air had to decide whether to invest scarce resources in becoming an online travel leader, develop bundled tour packages like Spring Airlines, or pursue other strategies while responding to regulatory changes, infrastructure expansion, and intensifying competition.

Lattice Semiconductor is showing an early revenue rebound driven by data centers, though automotive and industrial demand remains weak. Management sees opportunities in high-end data-center chips, robotics, vision systems, and security. Inventories are normalizing, cash generation is strong, debt is absent, and Q3 guidance indicates further growth. Despite a $70 price target, the stock remains rated HOLD due to its high valuation and limited margin of safety.

Researchers from Texas A&M University, the Western Australian Museum and the University of Washington identified a new clingfish genus and species from two museum specimens collected off Southern Australia in 1977. Named the duckbilled clingfish (Nettorhamphos radula), the finger-sized fish has a broad, flat snout and an estimated 1,800–2,300 backward-pointing teeth, about 10 times more than other known clingfish.

Because dissection could damage the only known specimens, researchers used CT scanning and 3-D printing to examine their skeletons and jaw structures noninvasively. The fish’s unusually wide, long upper jaw and numerous conical teeth distinguished it as both a new species and genus. The discovery highlights the scientific value of museum collections and digital imaging methods. The findings were published in Copeia, with support from the National Science Foundation.

During Lehigh’s Dec. 12–20 finals period, crowded libraries and limited private study spaces increase student stress. Students seek alternatives in cafes and academic buildings, citing distractions and unfairly saved seats in Fairchild-Martindale Library. Lehigh addresses demand by extending building hours, keeping FML open continuously from Dec. 11 to Dec. 20, and offering reservable study rooms through the Center for Career and Professional Development. Students said classrooms and reserved rooms provide quieter, more reliable study environments.

The President announced that 100,000 additional American troops would leave South Vietnam between May 1 and December 1, bringing total withdrawals since he took office to 365,000. He said his Vietnamization policy had strengthened South Vietnamese forces, reduced American troop levels and casualties, and enabled faster withdrawal without jeopardizing remaining forces.

He defended operations in Cambodia and Laos, arguing that they disrupted enemy bases and supply lines, weakened North Vietnamese offensive capacity, and demonstrated that South Vietnamese troops could fight effectively without American advisers. He maintained that American involvement was ending and that total withdrawal could be achieved through Vietnamization, though he preferred an earlier negotiated settlement.

The President renewed calls for a cease-fire, peace conference, withdrawal of outside forces, political settlement, and immediate release of all prisoners of war. He rejected setting a fixed withdrawal date, saying it would weaken negotiations, endanger remaining troops, and reduce South Vietnam’s chance to determine its future.

He defended American service members against broad condemnation based on individual atrocities and praised their sacrifices and humanitarian work. He framed his policy as an effort to end the war honorably, preserve trust in America, heal domestic divisions, and create lasting peace. Citing declining troop levels and casualties, he asked Americans to judge his policy by its record and reaffirmed his pledge to end American involvement.

Tesla Motors’ 2015 Form 10-K describes its electric vehicles, energy storage products, manufacturing, sales and service operations, technology, regulatory environment, competition and risks. Tesla produced the Model S and began Model X deliveries in 2015, while planning to unveil Model 3 in 2016 and begin production in late 2017. It also launched Powerwall and Powerpack products under Tesla Energy.

Tesla operated company-owned sales and service locations and a global charging network, including 584 Supercharger stations at year-end. Manufacturing occurred primarily in California, Nevada and the Netherlands. The Nevada Gigafactory was intended to integrate battery production, reach full capacity in 2020 and support approximately 500,000 vehicles annually. Tesla relied on more than 350 suppliers, with many components sourced from single suppliers.

As of December 31, 2015, Tesla had 13,058 full-time employees. Its major risks included production delays, uncertain demand, Gigafactory execution, product defects, supplier dependence, battery safety, cost increases, currency fluctuations, resale guarantees and leasing exposure, intense competition, regulatory restrictions on direct sales, international expansion challenges, reduced government incentives, and difficulty retaining key personnel.

The Trump administration’s 2018 Nuclear Posture Review calls for modernising US nuclear command systems, the nuclear triad, aircraft and infrastructure while developing flexible, low-yield weapons to strengthen deterrence. Planned measures include modifying some submarine-launched ballistic missile warheads, pursuing a nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile and maintaining the ability to deploy nuclear bombers and dual-capable aircraft worldwide.

President Donald Trump said the strategy seeks to make nuclear use less likely while deterring strategic attacks against the US and its allies. The policy maintains commitments to arms control, non-proliferation, the nuclear testing moratorium and prevention of nuclear terrorism. It also states the US will not threaten compliant non-nuclear parties to the Non-Proliferation Treaty with nuclear weapons.

Defence Secretary Jim Mattis cited expanding Russian and Chinese nuclear capabilities, particularly Russia’s reliance on nuclear escalation, as challenges to US superiority. The report also identifies North Korea and Iran as concerns but does not mention Pakistan. US officials reaffirmed extended nuclear deterrence commitments to European, Asian and Pacific allies and stressed cooperation, joint exercises and tailored assurance strategies.

Canada’s federal government agreed to give provinces and territories 75 per cent of legalized marijuana tax revenue under a two-year deal, replacing an initially proposed 50-50 split. Ottawa will retain 25 per cent, capped at $100 million annually, with excess revenue going to provinces and territories. Municipal allocations will be determined with provincial or territorial governments, despite cities seeking one-third of revenues for policing and administrative costs.

Ottawa expects marijuana taxes to generate up to $400 million during the first two years, although annual revenue could eventually reach $1 billion. Provinces may impose additional markups. Governments will review the framework in December 2018 and reconsider the approach after two years.

Finance ministers also discussed equalization payments, the Canada Pension Plan, the global economy and improved corporate-ownership information sharing to combat tax evasion, money laundering and terrorist financing.

ANU and the Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris studied alumino-silicate glass used in mobile screens. Experiments and modelling showed sodium and potassium form clusters or channels rather than distributing randomly, while calcium and magnesium also affect flexibility and fracture resistance. These microscopic arrangements could help manufacturers develop more shatter-resistant screens. The research comes amid durability concerns about glass smartphones and continued industry work on foldable displays.

The statistical analysis plan specifies descriptive ECG summaries by treatment and visit, including overall interpretations, ECG parameters, QTcF thresholds above 450, 480, and 500 ms, and postbaseline increases above 30 and 60 ms.

Antidrug antibody occurrence will be summarized descriptively without statistical testing. Overall ADA incidence includes treatment-induced cases among baseline-negative patients and treatment-boosted cases with at least fivefold titer increases. The denominator comprises evaluable patients with at least one reportable postadministration sample, including relevant unscheduled visits.

Protocol changes include rewording the primary efficacy analysis, adding sensitivity and supportive analyses, and changing secondary efficacy timing terminology from “within” to “at” specified minutes.

Presentation standards define formatting, decimal precision, percentages, P values, footnotes, source information, figures, listings, date and time formats, and sorting. Missing or incomplete dates use conservative assumptions. Calculations cover durations, unit conversions, temperature, BMI, and change from baseline.

SAS quality control requirements address program structure, documentation, logs, output review, dataset validation, data verification, listings, figures, and retention of QC records. Pinnacle 21 validation is required, and selected source data and derived values must be spot-checked.

Planned outputs cover patient disposition, demographics, diabetes and medical history, medications, glucose recovery and sensitivity analyses, adverse events, insulin and rescue-glucose use, ECGs, laboratory tests, pregnancy, local tolerability, vital signs, immunogenicity, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and patient listings. Primary glucose-recovery analyses include summary tables, Kaplan–Meier curves, Cox models, linear interpolation, and recovery at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes. Adverse-event outputs include treatment-emergent events, special-interest events, injection-site reactions, drug-related events, severity, causality, serious events, and relevant listings or narratives.

Scientists increasingly argue that ultraprocessed foods—industrial products made from concentrated sugars, fats and additives—can trigger cravings, loss of control, tolerance and withdrawal resembling substance use disorders. Studies report changes in brain reward systems involving dopamine, serotonin and opioids, while surveys estimate food addiction criteria are met by about 14 percent of adults and 12 percent of children.

Ultraprocessed foods account for more than half of average U.S. calorie consumption. Although definitions vary, the NOVA system classifies foods by processing level, while “hyperpalatable” describes especially appealing combinations of fat, sugar and salt. Researchers emphasize that these categories overlap but are not identical.

Questions remain about which foods are addictive, who is most vulnerable and how their effects compare with other addictive substances. Researchers also note that limited access, cost and preparation demands can make minimally processed foods difficult to choose.

Responses include proposed school restrictions, clearer warning labels, taxes, marketing limits and healthier product reformulation. Chile’s regulations on packaged foods have been associated with reduced household purchases of sugar, salt, saturated fat and calories from warning-labeled products. Advocates argue that policy should address food design and availability rather than relying solely on individual restraint.

The dollar rose broadly Monday as traders reversed bearish positions amid reduced U.S.-North Korea rhetoric and calls for a peaceful resolution. The dollar index gained 0.3 percent, while the currency strengthened against the yen and Swiss franc. Rising U.S. and global stocks also supported the rebound. Investors awaited Tuesday’s U.S. retail sales report for indications about inflation.

Saskatoon staff recommend a $1.2-million, two-year plan to remove and replace about 1,000 black ash trees damaged by European cottony ash psyllids. Insecticide treatments have only delayed or failed to slow tree decline. The first-year cost of $757,000 would come from reserve funds, while funding for the $423,000 second year remains unidentified. Ash species comprise about 27 per cent of the city’s 105,000-plus trees. Residents can identify infestations by white cotton, curled or discoloured leaves, and tiny light-green insects.

The president pledges to continue his predecessor’s reforms against abuses by railroad and industrial combinations while providing lawful businesses greater certainty. He proposes amendments to antitrust and interstate commerce laws, federal supervision of railroad securities, and reorganization of enforcement agencies.

He calls for prompt tariff revision to secure adequate revenue and appropriate protection, recommending a graduated inheritance tax if customs duties cannot eliminate the deficit. He supports economy without undermining necessary government functions, including agricultural research, business regulation, conservation, waterways, the Panama Canal, and national defense.

The address advocates a prepared army, strong navy, improved fortifications, arbitration and peaceful diplomacy, while maintaining the capacity to defend American rights and interests. It urges federal authority to enforce treaty protections for foreign nationals, monetary and banking reform, postal savings banks, expanded foreign trade, free trade with the Philippines under specified limits, and subsidized steamship links with South America.

The president supports completing the Panama Canal as a lock canal under the existing organization and reports favorable progress in Puerto Rico and the Philippines. He seeks greater political tolerance and national unity in the South. Regarding Black Americans, he affirms constitutional voting protections, educational and economic advancement, sympathy against racial injustice, and careful discretion in federal appointments.

On labor, he supports employer liability, compensation for injured government workers, child-labor restrictions, arbitration, and railway safety measures. He defends judicial injunctions against unlawful conduct in labor disputes and opposes secondary boycotts, while favoring statutory safeguards against abuse of temporary restraining orders. He concludes by requesting public support and divine aid.

Physicists developed a method to self-organize immiscible oil, water, and alcohol droplets into uniform multilayer patterns. By confining liquids in droplets or thin straws, de-mixing moves inward from the edge, producing stripes determined by wave speed and segregation time rather than droplet size. Adjusting these parameters enables control of emulsion structure and step-wise release of inner droplets. The technique could support more sophisticated pharmaceuticals and cosmetics, including manipulation of water- and oil-soluble medicines.

South Africa is expected to retain Moody’s investment-grade rating following Cyril Ramaphosa’s succession of Jacob Zuma, which strengthened the rand and business confidence. Moody’s rates the country one step above junk and will announce its decision Friday, while S&P and Fitch already classify its debt as junk. Risks include weak growth, missed budget targets and plans to permit property expropriation without compensation, which critics warn could deter investment. A downgrade could exclude South Africa from major bond indexes, trigger up to 100 billion rand in outflows and raise borrowing costs. Analysts expect Moody’s to wait for evidence of fiscal performance and policy implementation before considering a later downgrade.
OnePlus is rolling out Android Nougat with OxygenOS 4.0 to the OnePlus 3 and 3T, adding redesigned menus, multi-window, direct replies, and enhanced Doze.

Antimicrobial resistance prediction from whole-genome sequencing is limited by gene-based searches, order-agnostic machine learning, and the data demands of Transformers. The study introduces AMR-EnsembleNet, which averages predictions from a lightweight sequence-aware 1D convolutional neural network and XGBoost. The CNN learns local SNP motifs, while XGBoost captures non-local feature interactions.

The framework was evaluated on 809 *E. coli* isolates containing 60,936 ordered SNP features and resistance labels for ciprofloxacin, cefotaxime, ceftazidime, and gentamicin. Models were trained using stratified splits and class weighting and assessed with accuracy, Matthews correlation coefficient, macro F1, precision, recall, and resistant-class F1.

AMR-EnsembleNet matched the best ciprofloxacin accuracy at 0.9630, achieved the strongest overall cefotaxime results with 0.8086 accuracy and 0.8611 resistant-class recall, and produced the best Matthews correlation and macro F1 for highly imbalanced gentamicin data. Random Forest performed best for ceftazidime, though the ensemble balanced weaknesses in its component models.

SHAP analysis mapped influential SNPs to known resistance-associated genes, including *gyrB*, *marR*, *rpsL*, *parC*, *ampC*, *acrD*, and *ftsI*, supporting the biological relevance of the predictions. The authors conclude that combining local sequence modeling with feature-based learning provides robust AMR prediction and propose future work on minimum inhibitory concentration regression, transcriptomic integration, and deeper CNN explainability. Code and data sources are publicly available.

The Fifth Circuit affirmed Jose Verastegui’s guilty-plea convictions and concurrent 120-month sentences for firearm possession by a felon and unlawful reentry. Although the advisory range was 63–78 months, the district court properly imposed an upward departure because his criminal history category understated his conduct and a variance under 18 U.S.C. § 3553(a). The appellate court found no abuse of discretion or unreasonable sentence. Verastegui’s guideline challenge and constitutional challenges to 18 U.S.C. § 922(g) and 8 U.S.C. § 1326(b) were foreclosed by binding precedent and raised only to preserve them for further review. The unpublished opinion has limited precedential effect.

Enjifit launched its free iOS workout partner app on July 3, 2018. It connects nearby users, personal trainers, and nutritionists based on fitness goals and interests, offering messaging, workout reminders, session postings, and user filters. Trainers can purchase PRO subscriptions to promote services. Founded by Nicole Garcia in New York City, Enjifit plans an Android release.

Milky Tea’s HyperBrawl Tournament entered Steam Early Access in June 2017. The arena game combines high-speed handball with PvP combat, offering 10 warriors, 10 weapons, six arenas, eight skill-building mini-games, unlockable content, and local or online 1v1 and 2v2 multiplayer for up to four players.

The study investigates liquid-assisted capillary densification and thermal annealing as scalable methods for strengthening electrospun polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofiber yarns. Loosely assembled yarns were rolled with water or ethanol, dried, and optionally annealed at 110°C. Their tensile behavior and microstructure were evaluated using micro-tensile testing, SEM, Fourier analysis, and OrientationJ measurements of fiber alignment and planar packing density.

Liquid treatment compacted and aligned fibers, improving interfiber adhesion and load transfer. Water-treated yarns generally achieved greater strength and load capacity than ethanol-treated yarns, attributed to stronger capillary driving forces and slower evaporation; ethanol-induced fiber swelling may reduce intrinsic fiber performance. Annealing promoted partial fusion at fiber junctions, increasing stiffness and strength but reducing ductility. As-spun yarns showed lower modulus and strength but could sustain much larger strains through fiber sliding and progressive disengagement.

Mechanical performance increased strongly as yarn diameter decreased. Yarns below 10 μm approached reported single-nanofiber properties, reaching approximately 1.1 GPa modulus and 30 MPa peak stress. Comparisons within diameter groups and among segments cut from the same parent yarn confirmed that treatment-related gains were not solely caused by diameter shrinkage. Water treatment increased peak load by about 70% relative to untreated segments, while subsequent heating did not significantly increase peak load.

Peak load correlated positively with alignment (R²=0.68) and packing density (R²=0.75). A combined regression improved R² to 0.80, indicating complementary contributions. A stochastic mean-field constitutive model incorporating distributed recruitment and failure, fiber orientation, elastic-perfectly plastic behavior, load-transfer efficiency, and post-failure retention reproduced the observed deformation regimes. Its inferred packing–alignment parameter closely matched SEM-derived measurements (R²=0.91), linking processing, microstructure, and mechanical response.

Pepsi Nigeria’s No Shakin’ Carry Go campaign will send 10 fans on an all-expenses-paid, three-day VVIP trip to Dubai’s One Africa Music Fest in November, including opportunities to meet Pepsi-affiliated artists.

The nuclear force binds nuclei and is the residual strong interaction between quarks in different nucleons. Its study relies on nucleon-scattering experiments, nuclear binding energies and precise masses, and nuclear structure measurements such as energy levels, spin, parity, and magnetic and quadrupole moments.

Experimental results show that the nuclear force depends on nucleon separation, spin, and angular momentum, including spin-orbit and tensor components. It is short-ranged, becoming negligible beyond about 2 femtometers, and strongly repulsive below about 0.5 femtometers. Nearly constant binding energy per nucleon indicates that nucleons interact primarily with immediate neighbors, while nuclear densities show that nucleons are densely packed.

After electromagnetic effects are removed, the nuclear force appears charge independent, with no significant dependence on whether interacting nucleons are protons or neutrons. This property can be studied through mirror nuclei, which exchange proton and neutron numbers while retaining the same mass number. Mirror pairs generally show similar Coulomb-corrected binding energies and excitation levels, and stable mirror nuclei can help investigate corresponding unstable nuclei.

Gary Gensler outlines finance’s central role in pricing, allocating, and transferring money and risk through intermediaries. Key functions include investment, credit, payments, liquidity, market making, and risk transformation. Major sectors include commercial and investment banking, insurance, asset management, collective investment vehicles, exchanges, and clearinghouses. Primary markets issue new securities, while secondary markets facilitate later trading.

Ledgers record economic activity and financial relationships and underpin all financial institutions. Payment and settlement systems authorize, clear, record, and finalize transfers by updating ledgers. Blockchain may offer faster final settlement and immutable records, though its complexity is most relevant when recording valuable assets.

Financial regulation has existed for thousands of years and focuses mainly on financial stability, consumer and investor protection, and, increasingly, illicit activity. Regulation changes over time, often tightening after crises and easing later. Financial institutions’ leverage and maturity transformation support economic activity but can also create instability and bank runs.

Finance has long evolved alongside technology, from physical money and checks to computers, cryptography, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, biometrics, open APIs, automation, and blockchain. Established institutions may adapt slowly because of legacy systems, creating targeted opportunities for technological disruptors.

Credit is borrowing value with an agreement to repay. Debt forms a substantial part of modern economies, with US debt distributed across government, commercial, financial, and household sectors. US corporate financing relies heavily on securities markets, while household debt is dominated by mortgages and student loans.

Major financial risks include market, credit, underwriting, liquidity, funding, settlement, model, operational, cyber, legal, compliance, and reputational risks. Liquidity, funding, settlement, and failed correlation models are especially important during crises. The 2008 crisis reflected weak mortgage underwriting, predatory lending, easy credit, derivatives, leverage, poor risk management, and asymmetric incentives. Government intervention prevented broader collapse, but assistance favored major institutions more than homeowners.

The disclosure describes training and using a machine-learned model that estimates a scene’s depth map from a single color image. Training data may include monocular video, stereoscopic image pairs, or both. Images are processed by depth and pose models, then projected into synthetic frames. Model parameters are refined by minimizing per-pixel photometric reconstruction error between synthetic and captured images.

An input-scale, occlusion- and motion-aware loss function may select the minimum reconstruction error among projections from adjacent video frames or stereoscopic views. This reduces errors caused by occluded, disoccluded, and out-of-view pixels. Depth features may be upsampled to input-image resolution before frame synthesis to reduce texture-copy and depth-upsampling artifacts. A mask may exclude apparently static features, such as objects moving with the camera, from loss calculations. A hybrid architecture can share a depth encoder with a pose decoder to reduce computation.

After training, the model receives an image, optionally with camera intrinsics, and outputs a depth value for each pixel. The model may operate on a client device or through other computing systems.

An exemplary application is a location-based parallel reality game whose virtual geography corresponds to real-world geography. Client devices capture images, determine location, estimate scene depth, and display virtual content integrated with real-world imagery. Depth information can control virtual-object scale, movement, and occlusion relative to real objects. A game server hosts game state, distributes content, trains or supplies the depth model, and may manage commercial features, data collection, events, and location verification. User location and personal information are collected only after notice and consent and may be processed to remove identifying information.

NASA’s New Horizons, which flew by Pluto in 2015, was scheduled to encounter Kuiper Belt Object 2014 MU69 on Jan. 1, 2019. Located about 1.6 billion km beyond Pluto, MU69 would be the most distant and primitive object visited by a spacecraft. It was selected for its scientific value and relatively low fuel requirements. Observations suggested it could be an elongated object or a close/contact binary.

A public naming campaign involving 115,000 participants and 34,000 suggestions selected the nickname “Ultima Thule,” meaning beyond the known world. The nickname reflects the unprecedented nature of the mission but is not permanent. After the flyby determines whether MU69 is a single body, binary pair, or multiple objects, NASA and the New Horizons team will propose a formal name to the International Astronomical Union.

Attacking runs are off-the-ball movements into open space that help a teammate advance the ball, create passing opportunities, or produce shots. Effective runs require players to recognize or create open space, choose an appropriate route, separate from defenders, time movement to avoid offside, receive a well-placed pass, and communicate.

Common runs include bending, checking, diagonal, hooking, inside, lateral, onside, outlet, sideline, straight, through, and wide runs. Selection should maximize attacking progress while enabling the ball carrier to complete the pass. Attackers can escape markers through feints, sudden direction changes, or sprints, exploiting their initial head start and defenders’ need to react.

Runs and passes must coordinate in direction, pace, location, and timing. Runners should complete initiated runs because passers target the anticipated space. Communication may progress from verbal calls to hand signals and eye contact.

Coaching can begin with cones representing defenders, followed by practicing individual runs, adding passes, stationary defenders, restricted movement, supporting attackers, and full play. Coaches should reward good runs with passes, discourage ball-hogging and ball-watching, encourage continued movement after passing, and teach support runs. Advanced players may establish predictable patterns before changing direction to deceive defenders.

The “Clock” offense attacks a Diamond-and-One defense by placing the star player in the middle and treating the defense like a 1-3-1 zone. It seeks open shots, layups, putbacks, and one-on-one post opportunities against the chaser, who may be more prepared for pass denial than post defense.

Its basic rotation begins with a wing-to-corner pass followed by a basket cut, while perimeter players rotate. The corner can return the pass, feed the star when the middle defender helps, or reverse the ball to attack the weak side. If the middle defender covers a wing, the star rolls to the basket. This pass-and-cut sequence continues whenever the ball reaches a corner.

Wings may also dribble-clear the corner, causing the corner player to back cut and exchange roles. If neither the cutter nor post is available, the ball is reversed for a weak-side attack.

When the star receives the ball at the high post, an inside triangle forms. The star can drive either direction, pass to players positioned at the low post or short corner, or kick the ball outside for a shot or penetration. A baseline player may flash into the middle if other options are unavailable.

The inside triangle creates a three-on-two offensive rebounding advantage on outside shots, with an optional back screen on the star’s defender. Successful execution requires screening, post play, defensive recognition, communication, timing, practice, scouting, and varying alignments to target weaker defenders.

Education initiatives often stall because institutions invest heavily in programs and policies but neglect narratives that help communities understand them. Without clear framing, reforms are interpreted through existing distrust of top-down control, data practices, and technology replacing teachers.

The authors recommend treating narrative development like product research: frame the intended story, test it with communities, refine it through co-design, and scale it with practical tools and training. Leaders should emphasize shared values, use concrete metaphors, explain how changes produce benefits, center teachers and students, and directly address risks such as privacy, bias, and misuse. They should avoid crisis, blame, and “silver bullet” framing.

Trust also depends on who shapes the narrative, whose voices are prioritized, how benefits are distributed, and whether results are reported transparently. Building and testing narratives alongside education innovations can make new approaches more understandable, trustworthy, and adoptable.

Output capacitance is determined by the greater requirement from load-transient voltage deviation and output-ripple calculations. At least 1.3 mF is required, accounting for aging, temperature, and DC-bias derating; the space-grade example uses approximately 2.3 mF for radiation-induced single-event transient mitigation. An optional secondary LC filter can reduce ripple, with its resonance above crossover frequency but below switching frequency and the bulk-capacitance ESR zero; damping may address high-frequency peaking. Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins near 35 A, providing about 45% margin over the 24.25-A peak inductor current. Primary-side sensing uses a 1:100 current-sense transformer and a calculated sense resistor.

Quantum-correlated phonon pairs are promising resources for hybrid quantum networks but remain difficult to generate optically because of weak single-photon optomechanical coupling. The proposed protocol uses effective high-order nonlinearity in an optomechanical crystal nanobeam cavity. Simultaneous pulses at frequencies ωa±ωm induce Stokes and anti-Stokes interactions, producing degenerate correlated phonon pairs through an optomechanical spontaneous four-wave-mixing process analogous to spontaneous parametric down-conversion. A second red-detuned pulse retrieves the pairs, whose quantum correlations are verified using the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.

Using exome data from 454,803 UK Biobank and 173,585 Geisinger participants, researchers identified CHIP in 27,331 and 12,877 individuals, respectively. CHIP prevalence reached about 15% by age 75 and was associated with older age and heavy smoking. DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1, PPM1D, and TP53 were the most frequently mutated genes.

A genome-wide association study identified 27 common-variant loci associated with CHIP, including 24 novel loci, while exome-wide analyses found significant rare variants at three loci and burden associations involving ATM, CHEK2, CTC1, CLPTM1L, and KDELC2. Gene-specific analyses revealed shared, distinct, and opposing genetic effects among CHIP subtypes. TCL1A variants increased DNMT3A-CHIP risk but reduced risk for TET2-, ASXL1-, and other CHIP subtypes. Missense variants in PARP1 and LY75 were associated with reduced DNMT3A-CHIP risk.

CHIP was distinct from mosaic chromosomal alterations, although carriers were enriched for them. CHIP shared several germline risk factors with mosaic loss of the Y and X chromosomes. Rare-variant analyses also identified novel associations for mosaic alterations and telomere length.

Phenotypic associations varied by CHIP subtype. High-variant-allele-fraction CHIP was associated with COVID-19 hospitalization and severe infection, cardiovascular disease, blood cancers, lung cancer, prostate cancer, and all-cause mortality. Blood-cancer risk was substantially higher for myeloid than lymphoid cancers, with TET2 carriers showing the greatest blood-cancer risk. DNMT3A mutations did not predispose to lymphoid cancer unless accompanied by additional CHIP mutations. Lung-cancer risk remained elevated among both smokers and non-smokers.

The cardiovascular association was weaker than previously reported and was largely driven by TET2-CHIP. A previously reported protective cardiovascular effect of an IL6R variant among CHIP carriers appeared in the first 50,000 UK Biobank samples but not in the full cohort. Overall, the findings characterize CHIP as a collection of genetically and clinically distinct somatic mutation subtypes.

Defending the Power Offense requires disrupting continuous baseline and down screens, protecting against low-post mismatches, and rebounding effectively. NBA teams generally prefer “show and recover” rather than switching: defenders guarding screeners step out to force shooters wide, then quickly recover to deny the screener in the post, while perimeter defenders chase shooters and pressure the ball. Weakside defenders pack toward the ball, and teams may trap post mismatches.

The “All Out SOS Disruption” strategy initiates pressure by forcing the point guard toward the sideline, preferably to the weak hand, and trapping the wing receiver. Defenders may invert positions to keep bigger players inside, use contact switches and tight denial positions against baseline and down screens, and rotate to deny post entries and reversal passes. When the trapped player passes out, defenders immediately rotate, pressure the new ballhandler toward the baseline, front the post, and establish helpside positions. Subsequent drives, post passes, and screening actions are handled through prescribed traps, rotations, and basic SOS defensive rules.

Since Florida’s 2023 takeover of New College, spending has risen to roughly $134,000 per student while graduation and retention rates have fallen and the college has dropped nearly 60 places in national liberal arts rankings. The TPS7H500x-SP radiation-hardness-assured PWM controllers use fixed-frequency peak-current-mode control and support space-grade DC-DC topologies including buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge, with switching frequencies up to 2 MHz and external gate drivers.

A TPS7H5001-SP synchronous push-pull GaN converter example operates at 500 kHz and 5 V output. Selected values include a 205-kΩ timing resistor, 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback divider, approximately 25-ns dead time, 49.9-kΩ leading-edge blanking resistor, 33-nF soft-start capacitor for about 7.5 ms, 2.5 transformer turns ratio, and 40-μH primary inductance. The design uses 170-V primary and 80-V synchronous-rectifier GaN FETs, a 0.47-μH output inductor, and approximately 2.3 mF output capacitance for ripple, load-transient, and radiation-induced transient mitigation. Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins near 35 A using a 7.5-Ω sense resistor. Type 2A compensation targets 10 kHz with 40.2-kΩ, 15-nF, and 47-pF components; slope compensation uses 102 kΩ.

Controllers require a regulated 4-V to 14-V supply and at least 0.1-µF ceramic input bypassing. Layout guidance emphasizes short switching loops, minimized switch-node copper, separated analog and power grounds joined at one point, wide high-current traces, nearby bypass and compensation components, filtered current sensing, and separation of sensitive traces from switching signals. TI states that application guidance must be validated by customers and provides related evaluation, radiation, support, revision, packaging, ESD, and legal information.

The study applies a sub-pixel shift-and-add algorithm to electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) patterns captured with a 256×256-pixel Timepix-based direct electron detector. Multiple patterns from semiconductor-grade single-crystal silicon were registered using image transformations and combined to reconstruct a super-resolution pattern. Experiments compared this method with longer single-frame exposures, frame integration, camera retraction, and simulated diffraction patterns.

The direct detector operated in electron-counting mode at 20 keV with a 19.4 keV energy threshold. Pattern quality was assessed through a signal-to-noise metric derived from two-dimensional Fourier-transform radial profiles. Longer exposures and frame integration improved quality, but the signal-to-noise ratio plateaued near 30. The shift-and-add method increased the ratio from approximately 30 to 70 at an effective one-second exposure and produced more high-frequency information than an equivalent-dose single pattern.

The reconstructed pattern reproduced features observed in camera-retracted data and simulations, including higher-order Laue zone rings, zone poles, and fine band structures. Tenfold up-sampling produced a 2560×2560-pixel representation, although no information was added beyond the original frequency domain.

The method requires patterns sharing a common orientation and lattice but could potentially use large grains, precise stage movements, or detector-plane movements. It may also be applicable to indirect detectors, subject to their information limits. Without hardware modification, the approach more than doubled signal-to-noise and may support pattern indexing, strain and lattice-rotation measurements, unit-cell determination, centrosymmetry evaluation, and pseudosymmetry-related indexing.

Astronomers discovered MOA-2016-BLG-227Lb through gravitational microlensing observations begun by the MOA collaboration in May 2016 and supplemented by several telescopes. Its radius and orbital period remain undetermined. Keck images detected excess flux near the target, but Bayesian analysis considering possible contamination indicated that much of it was unlikely to originate from the lens star. Researchers recommended further observations with Hubble, Keck adaptive optics, and future telescopes to better characterize the system.

Red Same, Red Opposite, and Red Rover are SOS half-court defensive disruptions used briefly to change tempo, create easy baskets, disrupt set offenses, and limit penetrating point guards. They differ primarily in the initial trapping defender. X1 pressures O1 toward the sideline hash mark, where a second defender creates a hard trap, while the remaining defenders form Triangle “I” denial and help positions.

When O1 passes from the trap, defenders rotate to the nearest offensive players as the ball leaves the passer’s hands. The closing defender directs O2 toward a sideline, corner, or baseline checkpoint; X1 denies the return pass; other defenders deny the post and high-post players or provide helpside support.

In Red Mid Same, X3 joins X1 in the trap. In Red Opposite, X2 traps with X1. In Red Rover 4 and Red Rover 5, designated defenders X4 and X5, respectively, trap with X1. Subsequent assignments adjust accordingly.

All basic SOS rules remain active. If O2 penetrates to the free-throw-line extended, the defense transitions to coach-selected Base Go I or Base Go Red rotations. A low-post feed can trigger Post Front trap rotations.

The report examines newcomer education in California using state data, district interviews, literature, and practitioner experience. Newcomers—recent arrivals to U.S. schools—often have limited English proficiency, socioeconomic disadvantages, interrupted schooling, trauma, and unmet material or social-emotional needs. Unlike other vulnerable student groups, they lack dedicated statewide safeguards and supports. Schools frequently lack funding, expertise, curricula, data, and community partnerships, contributing to poor graduation, dropout, and college or career readiness outcomes, particularly for high school arrivals.

Federal rulings require meaningful and appropriately supported public education for English learners and immigrant students regardless of legal status. However, many districts may not meet federal standards for effective language programs because of inadequate staffing and resources.

In 2020–21, California enrolled 151,996 Title III immigrant students, representing 2.5 percent of K–12 enrollment. Fifty-eight percent attended schools in Alameda, Santa Clara, Los Angeles, Orange, or San Diego counties. Sixty-seven percent were socioeconomically disadvantaged, while needs varied substantially among districts. Spanish was the home language of 43 percent; newcomers showed considerable linguistic diversity. Only 19 percent were in high school, and newcomers were less concentrated in charter schools. California lacks statewide data on students with interrupted formal education, though Oakland Unified demonstrates a local system tracking arrival year and interrupted schooling.

California ranks below many states in education funding and had the nation’s highest student-to-teacher ratio in 2021. The Local Control Funding Formula provides added support for high-needs students, but newcomers receive no extra funding for qualifying as both low-income and English learners. State programs include the $5 million annual CalNEW program and the Opportunities for Youth pilot. Federal Title III funding is limited and uneven: in 2022–23, 77.6 percent of newcomers received no Title III Immigrant Student Program support because eligibility depended on district enrollment growth. Refugee programs support qualifying populations, but many students fleeing dangerous conditions are ineligible.

Effective education includes specialized newcomer instruction, flexible schedules, extended learning time, integrated language and academic content, translanguaging, collaboration, oral-language development, trained teachers, additional planning time, welcoming environments, cultural orientation, social activities, robust intake procedures, appropriate placement, and transcript recognition. Existing curricula and standardized assessments often inadequately address newcomers’ needs or growth. Outside-school partnerships are also important for family engagement, legal assistance, housing, food, health care, and mental health services.

The report recommends collaborative action across education, social services, nonprofits, philanthropy, and government. Proposed state actions include dedicated newcomer leadership, formal collaboration between education and social-service agencies, national partnerships, distinct statewide data for newcomers and students with interrupted schooling, continuation of the Opportunities for Youth initiative, revised funding for students arriving after census day, inclusion of newcomers in instructional frameworks, investment in open curricula and research, and advocacy for stronger federal data, resources, coordination, and more equitable Title III funding.

Backtesting applies trading strategies to accurate, representative historical data to assess potential profitability, risk, and resilience without risking capital. Reliable tests should cover varied market conditions, delisted assets, transaction costs, slippage, leverage, latency, and other asset-specific factors. Traders can reduce overfitting and bias through diverse datasets, out-of-sample testing, sensitivity analysis, forward testing, scenario analysis, and paper trading. Metrics such as net profit, Sharpe ratio, profitability, and maximum drawdown support evaluation and risk management. Tool selection should consider usability, customization, data quality, integration, and analytical capabilities. Backtesting can refine strategies across equities, derivatives, forex, futures, options, CFDs, and cryptocurrencies, but each market presents distinct data, volatility, pricing, execution, and psychological challenges. Results must be continually reviewed alongside current market analysis because historical success cannot guarantee future performance.

The disclosure describes dry, self-supporting electrode films for energy storage devices containing active material, a fibrillizable binder such as PTFE, and a microparticulate non-fibrillizable binder, preferably CMC, with particle sizes of about 0.5–40 μm. The smaller binder particles are intended to improve material distribution, mechanical strength, processability, consistency, and reduce holes, cracks, and surface pits. Solvent-free fabrication methods include high-shear processing or jet milling of the non-fibrillizable binder, nondestructive mixing with active materials, fibrillizing structural binder, and calendering the mixture into a free-standing film.

In an example, jet milling reduced CMC median particle size from approximately 70 μm to 10 μm. Graphite anodes containing 96 wt.% graphite and 4 wt.% binder achieved similar capacities but higher first-cycle efficiency with milled CMC: 90.9% versus 90.2%. Milled CMC also eliminated observed film defects and increased tensile strength from 0.936 N to 1.74 N at comparable film thicknesses. The films may be incorporated into electrodes, lithium-ion batteries, capacitors, and other energy storage devices.

The 3-3-5 is a high-risk, high-reward defense using three defensive linemen, three inside linebackers, and five defensive backs. Also called the 3-5-3 or 3-3 stack, it emphasizes speed, athleticism, pressure, flexible fronts, and disguised coverages. It can serve as either a base defense or sub package.

Its primary strengths are versatility and the ability to present the same pre-snap formation while using Cover 1, Cover 3, or varied blitzes. Linebackers and overhang defenders can rush from different positions, while defensive linemen can slant or pinch. Common pressures include the Sam Blitz, which sends a stack linebacker off the edge, and the SAW Blitz, which creates a Bear front with five rushers.

The defense is vulnerable along the edges, particularly against Buck Sweep and outside zone plays, where blockers may create numerical advantages. Passing attacks can target seams, especially with four vertical routes against Cover 3. Trips formations can reduce the defense to five box defenders and weaken the single-receiver side.

In Cover 1, corners and overhangs cover receivers man-to-man, a linebacker covers the back, another may act as a middle-field “rat,” and the free safety provides deep help. In Cover 3, the corners and free safety divide the deep field, overhangs cover the flats, and linebackers handle curl and hook zones.

Joe Lee Dunn is credited as the defense’s inventor. Coaches associated with it include Matt Campbell, Tony Gibson, Tim Racki, and Jeff Tumpane.

NVIDIA’s RTX Blackwell architecture for GeForce RTX 50-Series GPUs introduces GDDR7 memory with always-enabled single-bit error correction, Enhanced CRC, and Error Detection and Replay. Fifth-generation Tensor Cores add FP4 and FP6 support alongside existing formats, reducing AI model memory needs and improving performance. For example, FP4 lowers FLUX.dev memory use from over 23GB to under 10GB.

Fourth-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput and add hardware optimized for Mega Geometry and Linear Swept Spheres. Mega Geometry enables full-fidelity ray tracing of highly detailed, dynamically changing geometry through cluster-level acceleration structures and partitioned top-level acceleration structures, reducing BVH construction work and CPU overhead. Linear Swept Spheres accelerate strand-like geometry such as hair while using less VRAM. Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 improves thread coherence and neural-shading performance.

A dedicated RISC-V AI Management Processor moves GPU-context scheduling from the CPU to the GPU, aiming to reduce latency, improve multitasking, and coordinate AI and graphics workloads. Blackwell also adds hardware encoding and decoding for 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC video. Ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality, while sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed. RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders. DisplayPort 2.1b provides up to 80 Gbps and supports 8K at 165Hz or 4K at 480Hz with compression.

Max-Q improvements include finer clock, power, and rail gating; independently controlled GPU-core and memory power rails; clocks that adjust 1,000 times faster; and sleep entry up to 10 times faster than Ada. The passage reports power savings of up to 50% in a small-language-model inference example.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame. Its frame-generation model is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than the prior method. GPU-based Flip Metering improves frame pacing. Transformer models replace CNNs for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, using twice as many parameters to improve temporal stability, motion detail, lighting, anti-aliasing, and ghosting.

Blackwell expands neural shaders through Cooperative Vectors APIs for DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Applications include neural materials, texture compression, radiance caching, subsurface scattering with RTX Skin, and generative facial rendering with RTX Neural Faces. Neural Texture Compression can provide up to 7:1 VRAM compression over block-compressed formats, while the cited materials demo reduces memory use from 1,110MB to 333MB.

U.S. adults generally consume more protein than recommended, but dietary guidelines often treat unequal protein sources as equivalent. Animal foods typically provide more complete, digestible essential amino acids than plant foods, resulting in greater muscle protein synthesis. Older adults are particularly vulnerable to inadequate high-quality protein and related muscle loss.

Experts propose guidelines based on essential amino acids and tailored to demographic needs. Plant-based diets can still meet protein requirements through larger portions, complementary foods such as beans and rice, and preparation methods including soaking, sprouting and fermentation. Younger adults can generally replace some animal protein with plant protein, while older adults, athletes, and pregnant or lactating individuals may require more. Reducing meat can also benefit health and the environment.

A survey of 2,000 British adults found that the average person wakes three times nightly, while one in 10 wakes seven to 10 times. Common causes include toilet trips, snoring, lack of bed space, discomfort, nightmares, tossing and turning, sleep talking, phone use, reading or television, and anxiety. Psychologist Robert Stewart said sleep quality depends on pre-bed habits and sleep cycles. He recommended limiting food, drink and screens before bed, maintaining a regular bedtime, and reducing environmental disturbances with measures such as earplugs or a comfortable mattress.

New York’s early intervention providers, who serve about 70,000 children from birth through age 3 with developmental delays and disabilities, have not received a substantive pay increase in three decades. Many are independent contractors paid state-set fees that have declined in nominal and inflation-adjusted terms; a standard visit averaged $79 in 1994 and $69 in 2022. Providers also perform extensive uncompensated work, including travel, planning, reporting and handling cancellations.

Low pay, administrative burdens and reimbursement delays have driven therapists and special education teachers to better-paying jobs, reducing access to timely services, especially in rural areas. A 2024 state-authorized 5% increase for in-person services remains pending federal approval, while a 4% increase for underserved areas has been approved but not implemented. Telehealth rates were cut to help fund the proposed increase, prompting virtual providers to quit.

Families report months without services and developmental regression among children. Similar workforce and compensation problems exist in other states, including Illinois, where provider numbers have fallen. Advocates warn that Medicaid cuts could further restrict funding and access. Despite increased caseloads, reporting requirements and stagnant compensation, veteran teacher Emily Lengen plans to remain because of her commitment to children and families.

Principal risks include production and launch delays, failure to achieve manufacturing cost or volume targets, inaccurate demand forecasts, insufficient delivery, service, charging or installation capacity, limited consumer adoption of electric vehicles, supplier disruptions, regulatory restrictions, intense competition and difficulties expanding international manufacturing. Tesla specifically depends on successfully sustaining and expanding battery-cell, pack and drive-unit production at Gigafactory Nevada.
