UBS Warburg’s proposed acquisition of Enron’s energy-trading business involved no upfront cash. Enron and creditors would receive 33% of pretax profits for at least two years, with potential reductions later. UBS was expected to hire most trading employees and pay rent for Enron office space, subject to bankruptcy-court approval.

Other reports covered Enron’s political connections, government contacts before bankruptcy, Andersen’s destruction of documents, and losses suffered by employees and investors. Enron’s collapse prompted energy companies to reduce debt, sell assets and raise equity amid tighter credit standards. In India, the cash-strapped Dabhol Power Company faced possible closure and further layoffs, while BG Group continued renegotiating its proposed purchase of Enron’s Indian oil and gas assets.

Anthropologist Donald Blakeslee identified carved limestone boulders in a Kansas backyard as centuries-old Wichita Nation sacred shrines. Water poured into holes and basins flows through miniature channels, reflecting Wichita beliefs in three interconnected realms and water’s spiritual role. Nearby depressions may have held water women drank while praying for successful pregnancies. Springs, caves, and pools were considered sacred portals where people could communicate with spirits. Wichita leader Gary McAdams said water was used for transformation, baptism, prayer, preparation for major undertakings, and cleansing after deaths. Blakeslee hopes the carvings can reveal more about lost Wichita mythology.

The state cabinet formed an 11-member committee to study liquor policies in six states and report within three months. No final decision on prohibition has been made. The government will not open new outlets but will operate unsold shops among the existing 712.

Animal partnerships can be unusual and unequal. Pearlfish shelter inside sea cucumbers, emerging at night to hunt; some parasitise their hosts by eating their gonads. Gobies protect pistol shrimp, which maintain shared burrows, clean parasites from the fish and respond to their danger signals, creating a mutually beneficial relationship. In contrast, threatened arid bronze azure butterfly larvae chemically mimic queen ants, causing bearded sugar ants to shelter them in their nurseries, where the larvae consume ant babies for nutrition.

The media roundup covers several Enron-related developments. Sycamore Networks sharply reduced its revenue forecast as major customer Williams shifted some business to rivals amid Sycamore product delays; Enron Broadband’s purchases also remained well below a previously announced potential $200 million agreement. Enron’s Dabhol Power Company called an April 23 lenders’ meeting amid payment and contractual disputes with Maharashtra authorities, arbitration notices, and uncertainty over the project’s second phase. Enron-owned Azurix planned to sell its American and German operations before potentially selling Wessex Water. Bandwidth trading faced weak demand, excess capacity, falling prices, credit concerns, and unresolved contract standards, prompting Enron to cut broadband jobs and network spending. Separately, northwestern U.S. aluminum smelters faced prolonged closures because of proposed Bonneville Power Administration restrictions and price increases, while McCook Metals pursued a turbine power project with Enron. Nevada’s utilities regulator sought to delay Sierra Pacific Resources’ proposed $3.1 billion purchase of an Oregon utility from Enron because of pending state legislation.

The strategy rotates monthly between SPY and TLT, investing in whichever ETF performed better during the prior month and holding it for one month. It applies momentum, which has historically worked best over one- to 12-month periods, and sector rotation. TLT may act as a safe haven during stock-market weakness, though it does not reliably hedge tail risk. A backtest from 2003, with dividends reinvested and excluding taxes, slippage, and commissions, produced a 9.2% CAGR. Maximum drawdown was 22% before 2022 but reached 41% when both SPY and TLT declined sharply. Entries and exits occurred at each month’s close.

Moldova’s economy grew 1.1% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2025, reversing a 1.2% first-quarter contraction. Construction, energy and ICT drove the rebound. The central bank cut its benchmark rate to 6% to support lending and demand. The EBRD forecasts 1.5% growth in 2025 and 3.8% in 2026, conditional on reforms and international support. Inflation, fiscal constraints, currency volatility, weak external demand and regional uncertainty remain risks. Sustained growth depends on financing, structural reforms and economic diversification.

The article surveys results connecting transformer expressivity with logic, automata, and circuit complexity. It models transformers as sequence-to-sequence computations combining piecewise-linear functions with attention, distinguishes softmax, unique hard attention (UHAT), and average hard attention (AHAT), and discusses masking, positional embeddings, and precision. Transformers with chain-of-thought are excluded, though they are known to be Turing-complete.

UHAT with positional embeddings is strictly contained in AC0, so it cannot express PARITY or MAJ. It can express first-order logic with unary numerical predicates, while masked UHAT without positional embeddings coincides with first-order logic and star-free languages. UHAT with positional embeddings contains all regular languages in AC0 and can recognize palindromes. Verification of masked UHAT without positional embeddings is decidable and EXPSPACE-complete.

AHAT can recognize MAJ and is upper-bounded by TC0. Counting LTL with unary numerical predicates is expressible by AHAT with positional embeddings, while its fragment Kt[#] is expressible by masked AHAT without positional embeddings. NoPE-AHAT recognizes exactly permutation-invariant languages with semi-algebraic Parikh images; consequently, checking its language for nonemptiness is undecidable.

Hard attention remains an imperfect approximation of practical softmax attention. Softmax transformers with positional embeddings can express PARITY, and uniformly attentive AHAT models can be simulated by softmax transformers. Softmax models can therefore recognize Kt[#] languages and permutation-invariant languages with semi-algebraic Parikh images.

Expressibility does not ensure trainability. PARITY is expressible by softmax transformers but difficult to train, possibly because of its sensitivity to individual symbol changes, unlike MAJ. A formalized version of the RASP-L conjecture links length generalization to limit transformers and Kt[#], excluding PARITY while admitting MAJ. The article highlights unresolved questions about softmax expressivity, AHAT characterization, and which concepts support length generalization.
The Ninth Circuit dismissed the appeal by stipulation of counsel and ordered the mandate issued immediately.

New York City’s Department of Education spends $25,087 per student, up 40 percent since 2008-09 and the highest among the nation’s 100 largest school systems in fiscal 2015. Of its $23.4 billion budget, 30.3 percent went to employee and retiree benefits and 23.4 percent to teacher salaries.

Critics cite growing pension obligations, waste, weak oversight, a $100 million pool of educators without permanent posts, and the $784 million Renewal Program for struggling schools. A comptroller’s review also questioned documentation and results for $350 million spent on school broadband.

Despite higher spending, standardized performance changed little from 2009 to 2015. Fourth-grade math and reading scores declined, while eighth-grade scores rose modestly but remained below national averages. Although the 2016 graduation rate reached 72.6 percent, only half of graduates were considered ready for college or careers. A 2014 union contract raised top teacher pay from $100,000 to $119,000 and included retroactive raises.

The lecture examines persistent gender gaps in employment, wages, promotion, and task allocation. Although women’s labor-market outcomes improved through expanded education, technological change, shifts toward service work, regulation, and competition, women still earn roughly 20%–30% less than men after accounting for work time and education. Studying these differences matters for fairness, economic efficiency, and understanding how preferences and identities develop.

Technological measures can reduce discrimination but are incomplete. Goldin and Rouse found that blind orchestra auditions increased impartiality and women’s representation, though estimates were sometimes imprecise and multistage selection complicated analysis. Algorithms may reproduce biases in the human decisions used to train them, but fairness objectives can potentially reduce those biases.

Discrimination may reflect preferences or beliefs. Bertrand and Mullainathan found that otherwise identical applications with white-sounding names received 50% more callbacks than those with African-American-sounding names. Sarsons found that physicians responded differently to surgeons’ outcomes: women were punished more after adverse events and rewarded less after good outcomes. Negative outcomes also reduced referrals to other female surgeons, potentially limiting opportunities to correct mistaken beliefs.

Gender identity norms can also shape labor-market behavior. Bertrand and colleagues found fewer couples immediately above the point where wives earn half of household income. Proposed mechanisms included marriages not forming, increased divorce, wives reducing market work, and wives performing more unpaid household and childcare work. Kleven and colleagues found that after a first child, women experienced a long-run earnings penalty of nearly 20% and an hours penalty of about 10%, while men’s outcomes changed little. Gender-neutral tenure-clock extensions reduced women’s tenure rates and increased men’s, suggesting formally neutral policies can have unequal effects. Experiments with MBA students indicated that single women reported lower career ambition when responses might be observed by single male peers.

Women also undertake more nonpromotable work. Field and laboratory studies found women were more likely to volunteer or invest in tasks benefiting a group but not themselves. Gender differences disappeared in single-sex groups, suggesting expectations matter. Women were asked more often because they were more likely to comply: 76% invested when asked, compared with 51% of men. This interaction between women’s responses and others’ requests may amplify unequal task allocation and hinder promotion.

The ADS868xW transitions from acquisition to conversion on the rising edge of CONVST/CS and ignores further transitions until conversion completes. The host detects completion through an RVS low-to-high transition or by waiting for the maximum conversion time.

Data-transfer frames begin when CONVST/CS falls and end when it rises. During a frame, SCLK shifts commands into the input register and output data through SDO pins. A 32-clock frame accepts a valid 32-bit command. Short frames cannot perform writes but can read selected output MSBs; in long frames, the final 32 input bits form the command.

The device supports byte and half-word register operations, including read, write, bit-clear, and bit-set commands. Half-word commands ignore the address LSB. Read results appear in the following frame; otherwise, output normally contains the latest 16-bit conversion result. Configurable output fields include device address, input range, supply and input alarms, parity, and fixed test patterns.

The multiSPI interface supports four standard SPI modes, single- or dual-SDO output, and source-synchronous protocols using RVS as the output clock. Source-synchronous operation can use internal or external clocks. Dual-SDO mode transfers two bits per launch edge and reduces the required clock cycles.

Nine configuration registers control device identification, reset and power, input and output protocols, output formatting, input range and reference, and alarm flags, thresholds, and hysteresis. Protected power-control writes require a 69h key.

The ADS868xW integrates a 16-bit SAR ADC, differential analog front end, programmable gain, driver, and precision reference. An example industrial design combines the ADS8681W with an eight-channel differential multiplexer for voltage, current, or temperature measurements. Programmable alarms and hysteresis support threshold monitoring while reducing false triggers.

The device uses separate AVDD and DVDD supplies and requires nearby decoupling capacitors. NAP and deep power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput rates while requiring specified wake-up delays. PCB guidance recommends separating analog and digital routing, short low-impedance grounds, clean bypassed supplies, and closely placed reference capacitors.

The 3 Days Down Overnight Trading Strategy buys SPY at the close after three consecutive declining days and exits at the next day’s open. Since 1993, the backtest produced 661 trades, a 0.13% average gain, 65% win rate, and 8% maximum drawdown, excluding slippage and commissions. Exiting at the next close increased average gain to 0.24% and produced a 5% CAGR with 8% market exposure, but reduced the win rate to 61% and increased drawdown to 17%. The strategy also works on QQQ and many stocks, though less effectively. A March 2022 modification reduced exposure and drawdowns, reporting a 0.35% average gain, 60% win rate, and 10% drawdown. During the 2022 bear market, it made 35 trades averaging 0.3%.

In 1886 the United States successfully opposed a Hawaiian loan managed by an English syndicate, citing privileges under the reciprocity treaty. In 1887 Secretary of State Bayard also withheld approval from a proposed Hawaiian-Samoan political alliance. Britain later proposed that the United States, Britain, and Germany guarantee Hawaiian neutrality and equal harbor access. Bayard declined, arguing that existing U.S.-Hawaiian treaties already protected Hawaiian sovereignty, prohibited territorial cessions without U.S. consent, and maintained port accessibility. Meanwhile, Britain protested the United States’ exclusive use of Pearl River Harbor as a coaling and repair station, warning that preferential foreign concessions threatened Hawaiian independence. The Hawaiian and U.S. governments maintained that the concession transferred neither territory nor jurisdiction, granted no exclusive commercial rights, and would end with the 1875 treaty.

Index Markets Research’s report analyzes the global Polyolefin (POF) Shrink Film market by size, volume, revenue, trends, growth drivers, constraints, opportunities, manufacturing costs, production capacity, and competitive strategies. It covers North America, China, Europe, Southeast Asia, Japan, and India from 2012 to 2022, including forecasts. Products are divided into general and cross-linked films, while applications include food, beverages, industrial packaging, pharmaceuticals, and consumer goods. The report evaluates major manufacturers, market shares, segmentation, production technology, raw material sources, and R&D status. It also includes SWOT, investment feasibility, project returns, development trends, emerging segments, and recommendations for companies and new entrants.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture improves GPU memory, display, rendering, AI, and VR capabilities. Its GDDR6 subsystem delivers 14 Gbps signaling and 20% better power efficiency than Pascal’s GDDR5X, while larger L2 caches and enhanced lossless compression provide about 50% higher effective bandwidth. The display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDR, and two 8K 60 Hz displays; updated NVENC and NVDEC units add 8K HEVC encoding and expanded video decoding. USB-C and VirtualLink combine VR display, data, and power in one connector, while second-generation NVLink increases two-GPU SLI bandwidth.

Dedicated RT Cores accelerate bounding-volume hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray tracing at over 10 Giga Rays/sec—about ten times Pascal’s software performance. Turing combines ray tracing, rasterization, denoising, and AI in a hybrid rendering model for reflections, shadows, ambient occlusion, and other effects. Tensor Cores support NVIDIA NGX features including DLSS, inpainting, interpolated slow motion, and AI-based image upscaling. DLSS is trained against 64-times supersampled reference images and can provide TAA-like quality with less shading work.

Additional graphics features include Mesh Shading to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks, Variable Rate Shading to adjust shading rates by content, motion, or viewer focus, Texture Space Shading to reuse shading computations, and Multi-View Rendering for multiple viewpoints in one pass. Turing also expands DirectX 12 resource binding and heap support.

The TU104 GPU contains up to 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, while TU106 contains 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores but lacks NVLink and SLI. Products include the GeForce RTX 2080, RTX 2070, Quadro RTX 5000, and Tesla T4. NVIDIA defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric combining weighted Tensor, FP32, ray-tracing, and INT32 throughput.

Jon Jones and trainer Mike Winkeljohn favor a lucrative Brock Lesnar fight over facing heavyweight champion Stipe Miocic. Jones cited Lesnar’s greater public appeal, stylistic advantages and potential benefit to MMA. Winkeljohn said Miocic is the harder opponent and Jones should gain weight and develop skills before fighting him.

Long Covid causes varied, often disabling symptoms and may disproportionately affect deprived and ethnic minority communities, despite their underrepresentation in post-COVID services. This NIHR STIMULATE-ICP study co-produced a community-based approach with a Community Advisory Board to identify people with probable but undiagnosed Long Covid and explore barriers, stigma and support needs.

Researchers recruited participants through community organizations in Camden, Merton and Derbyshire. Twenty-three adults without a known clinical diagnosis completed semi-structured interviews, which were thematically analysed. Four themes emerged: uncertainty and limited Long Covid awareness; barriers to healthcare engagement; stigma and discrimination; and sources of support.

Participants often did not recognize their symptoms as Long Covid, doubted their own experiences or attributed symptoms to ageing, menopause, stress or existing conditions. Healthcare interactions sometimes reinforced these doubts. Help-seeking was inhibited by concerns about burdening the NHS, medication, parenting judgments, appointment access and dismissal. Fluctuating, multisystem symptoms also complicated recognition and care.

Participants reported perceived age, gender, weight and health-related discrimination, alongside dismissal by healthcare professionals, employers and others. Anticipated disbelief or judgment discouraged disclosure and care-seeking, while internalised stigma included shame, reduced self-worth and comparisons with people who recovered quickly. These experiences reflected layered stigma and forms of epistemic injustice involving difficulty interpreting symptoms and reduced credibility assigned to patients’ accounts.

Nearly half sought support outside the NHS through private care, alternative therapies, supplements, behavioural changes or healthcare professionals among family and friends. Participants valued peer, community, social-prescribing, employment and financial support. They wanted accessible appointments, more time with clinicians, attentive listening, appropriate referrals and dedicated Long Covid services that could sometimes be accessed without a GP.

The study concludes that co-designed active case finding can identify probable undiagnosed Long Covid. Greater awareness, stigma reduction, recognition of lived experience, early signposting and accessible support are needed. Alternative diagnoses remain possible, and younger adults were not represented.

The speaker emphasizes collective commitment, puck awareness, positioning, and anticipation in all situations. In the playoffs, teams must manage emotions, regroup after losses, and focus on the next game, while the finals naturally bring greater intensity. His power-play role may differ, but every player must contribute. He praises a steady defenseman for improving offensively, playing heavy minutes, and sharing his dedication to fitness. He is also willing to take faceoffs when needed. Defending requires tracking quick opponents who move the puck effectively. Reaching the finals is especially meaningful given Slovakia’s small NHL presence, though he wishes for better game results. His first televised final was Pittsburgh against Minnesota.

A prolonged heat wave is breaking records across Canada, the United States, Europe and the Middle East. Montreal reached 37 C and reported 11 heat-related deaths, while Ottawa recorded a humidex of 47. The northeastern U.S. issued heat warnings, Denver tied its 40 C record, and at least one U.S. death was reported. Scotland recorded an all-time high of 33.2 C, while southern Russia reached 37 C. In Oman, temperatures stayed above 42.6 C for 51 hours, setting a record for the highest nightly low. Climate scientist Blair Feltmate linked the heat waves’ duration and severity to climate change.

The Oppo R15 and Vivo X21 launches suggest possible OnePlus 6 features because the BBK Electronics brands often share similar designs. Leaks indicate the OnePlus 6 may adopt a 6.28-inch-style 19:9 notched display, resembling the Oppo R15, while using a Snapdragon 845 processor. The Vivo X21 UD also raises the possibility of an under-display fingerprint sensor. Some details, including camera orientation, may differ.

The double-down trading strategy adds a position equal to the initial losing position after the price falls, lowering the average entry price and allowing an earlier breakeven if the price reverses. Unlike planned scaling in, doubling down is often unplanned. It also differs from Martingale, which repeatedly adds increasingly larger positions, and from the repair strategy, which uses call options.

Backtests suggest doubling down may suit mean-reverting assets but not trending assets. On SPY, the tested double-down rules produced 236 trades averaging a 0.97% gain, compared with 518 trades averaging 0.56% under the initial rules. On the trend-oriented junk-bond ETF HYG, average losses worsened from 0.19% across 275 trades to 0.22% across 125 trades.

The strategy can cause substantial losses if prices continue falling, and one major loss may be ruinous. Traders should assess market conditions, recovery potential, risk management, and probability of success rather than focus on average entry price. Doubling down is rarely part of a rational trading plan and is often driven by anchoring or trading bias.

A December 31, 1842 presidential message transmitted correspondence with Hawaiian agents and addressed U.S. commerce and diplomacy in the Pacific. It described Hawaii as increasingly civilized, strategically important for provisioning trans-Pacific and American whaling vessels, and governed by a weak but peaceful administration seeking education and social improvement. The United States sought no exclusive control but supported Hawaiian independence and prosperity, warning that foreign colonization or overthrow of the native government would prompt dissatisfaction and possible remonstrance. The President recommended funding the U.S. consul to assist American citizens and address Hawaiian complaints. The message also noted that Britain’s treaty ending military operations in China opened four ports—Amoy, Foo-Choo-Foo, Ningpo, and Chinghai—to British merchants. Because the treaty neither admitted nor excluded other nations, the United States would need to seek its own commercial arrangements with China.

A low-side current-sensing circuit uses an amplifier to increase the shunt-resistor voltage drop and a high-speed comparator to issue a logic-high alert when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1 V. Because fast output transitions can cause supply ringing, false triggers, or oscillation, each device requires a low-ESR 0.1-µF ceramic bypass capacitor placed directly between V+ and ground. Stable, low-noise supplies, solid grounding, and separation of input and output traces are recommended. Series resistors, controlled-impedance traces, and back-termination can reduce ringing on long routes. The device supports single or split supplies, provided inputs remain within the recommended range; with split supplies, the low output approaches V− rather than ground.

TI provides update notifications and E2E support resources. Devices require ESD precautions, and mechanical, packaging, and ordering data may change. TI supplies technical resources “as is,” assigns application selection, design, validation, testing, and compliance responsibilities to developers, limits resource use to applications involving the described products, and applies its Terms of Sale and warranty disclaimers.

The MSPM0C1105/1106 include an independent watchdog timer with a 25-bit windowed counter, LFOSC clocking, programmable divider, eight periods, and POR reset capability. A windowed watchdog provides reset or interrupt generation, selectable periods, automatic stopping in sleep, and interval-timer operation.

RTC_B uses a 32kHz clock and supports calendar counters, binary or BCD formats, leap-year correction from 1901 through 2099, customizable and periodic alarms, standby interrupts, ±240ppm calibration and temperature compensation, and GPIO clock output.

General-purpose timers provide 16-bit counting, prescaling, quadrature encoding, synchronization, cross-triggering, and peripheral triggers. Advanced timers add clock doubling, repeat counting, shadow registers, asymmetric PWM with dead-band insertion, fault handling, and additional capture/compare channels.

IOMUX selects digital peripheral functions and controls output drivers, inputs, and shutdown wake-up logic. An Arm-compatible two-wire SWD interface supports processor and device-state debugging. DEBUGSS includes configurable peripheral behavior during debug, a software mailbox, SWD pin reassignment, lockout, and password-authenticated debugging.

A read-only FACTORY memory region contains device capabilities, identification, revisions, and trim data. DEVICEID is at 0x41C4.0004 and USERID at 0x41C4.0008.

TI recommends 10µF and 0.1µF low-ESR ceramic VDD decoupling capacitors near the pins, a 47kΩ NRST pullup with a 1000pF pulldown capacitor, crystal bypass capacitors where applicable, and pullups for 5V-tolerant open-drain outputs.

“X” identifies experimental devices intended for internal evaluation, while “MSP” identifies fully qualified production devices. TI provides development boards, SDKs, cloud and offline tools, SysConfig, training, GUI tools, documentation, and support forums. The September 2025 revision removed DGS32 package information, updated specifications and identification tables, revised CPU and ADC information, and added DEBUGSS. Mechanical and packaging data remain subject to change, and appropriate ESD precautions are required.

Christmas Bird Counts enlist volunteers of all skill levels to record birds within designated circles, contributing to a century-long population database. Sheridan’s count is Dec. 14; Story-Big Horn’s is Dec. 23. Feeder and backyard watchers are also needed.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture improves graphics, ray tracing, AI, memory, I/O, and media processing over Turing. GA102 contains up to seven GPCs, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA cores, 112 ROPs, a 384-bit memory interface, and 6 MB of L2 cache. Each SM includes 128 CUDA cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation RT Core, and 128 KB of configurable L1/shared memory. Dual FP32-capable datapaths double peak FP32 throughput, while expanded cache and shared-memory bandwidth improve graphics and compute performance.

Third-generation NVLink provides up to 112.5 GB/sec bidirectional bandwidth between two GPUs and can combine two A40 or RTX A6000 GPUs for 96 GB of memory. PCIe 4.0 doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth and supports up to 64 GB/sec through a x16 slot.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput, support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute, and add hardware acceleration for motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32, BF16, FP16, INT8, INT4, and structured sparsity, which can double matrix throughput by skipping zero-valued elements. These capabilities accelerate DLSS, denoising, AI inference, and other neural-network workloads. Ampere GPUs are stated to be up to 1.9 times more power-efficient than Turing at equal performance.

GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling to transfer two bits per clock edge, reaching up to 19.5 Gbps and 936 GB/sec of memory bandwidth. RTX IO, integrated with Microsoft DirectStorage, enables compressed data to move from NVMe storage to GPU memory for GPU-based decompression, reducing CPU use and accelerating asset loading.

The architecture supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 4K at 120 Hz, and 8K at 60 Hz. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware AV1 decoding up to 8K60 HDR with low CPU utilization, while seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

The A40 targets data-center visualization, compute, AI, virtualization, and remote workstations, with 48 GB scalable to 96 GB through NVLink. The RTX A6000 provides 48 GB for professional desktop workloads, while the RTX 3090 offers 24 GB GDDR6X for creators, AI developers, data scientists, and gamers. Error Detection and Replay protects GDDR6X transfers during memory overclocking by retrying failed transactions.

The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card is aimed at consumers paying down debt or financing large purchases. It offers 0% introductory APR for 21 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74%. It has no annual fee and includes up to $600 in cellphone protection, subject to a $25 deductible.

Drawbacks include no ongoing rewards, a 5% balance-transfer fee with a $5 minimum, and a 3% foreign-transaction fee. Applicants are generally recommended to have good or excellent credit, though approval is not guaranteed. The card may suit those who can use the full interest-free period, but alternatives may be preferable for ongoing rewards, lower transfer fees, or international travel.

Motley Fool Money states that advertiser compensation can affect product placement and coverage but not ratings or recommendations.

Apple entered an underwriting agreement with Goldman, Sachs & Co. on September 10, 2015, to issue €1 billion of 1.375% senior unsecured notes due January 17, 2024, and €1 billion of 2.000% senior unsecured notes due September 17, 2027. Interest is payable annually. The notes rank equally with Apple’s other unsecured, unsubordinated debt and were issued under its 2013 indenture and Form S-3 registration statement. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, note forms, legal opinion, and earnings-to-fixed-charges calculation.

Changes to the FAFSA have complicated colleges’ sharing of student financial information with scholarship providers because some data now comes directly from the IRS and is subject to stricter privacy rules. Confusion has led many financial aid offices to restrict access, delaying scholarship decisions and disbursements. A NASFAA survey found 58 percent of respondents would share federal tax data with scholarship organizations with student consent, while 22 percent would never do so; 22 percent had ended or modified outside data-sharing agreements.

Native Forward Scholars Fund said these delays left students starting classes without knowing their award amounts and placed added burdens on Native students, for whom financial constraints are a major barrier. Other providers reported difficulty obtaining cost-of-attendance, aid and unmet-need information.

New Education Department guidance confirms that colleges may share FAFSA tax data with scholarship providers when students consent, while two designated organizations may receive it directly without consent. However, forthcoming security standards remain undefined, and providers say the guidance offers little immediate relief. They are calling for streamlined student-consent procedures and standardized, secure data-sharing systems.

Tariffs rarely create monopolies, but duties should be reduced when they harm competition; the anthracite coal tariff should be removed to aid the public during crises. Monetary legislation should promote an elastic circulation, largely supplied by banks, that meets legitimate commercial and industrial demand, ensures interchangeability of money, and maintains convertibility into gold without reconstructing the entire financial system. Congress should also pass an appropriate immigration law. Capital and labor organizations can both benefit or harm society, so criticism should target misconduct rather than organizations themselves. Employers and workers must obey the law, respect individual freedom and others’ rights, deal fairly, and align their interests with the public good. Mutual understanding should replace hostility and distrust. Political class animosity threatens national welfare; citizens should be judged by individual merit and honorable conduct, not wealth, occupation, creed, birthplace, or class. National powers should be exercised according to these principles.

Researchers found that Apple had granted Uber’s iPhone app a unique entitlement enabling screen recording even when other apps were active. Uber said the permission supported Apple Watch map rendering and was no longer connected to its code; newer app versions removed it. No evidence indicates Uber misused the capability. The discovery raised concerns given Uber’s privacy record and ongoing negotiations after losing its London operating licence.

In September 1945, Colonel Alfred McCormack became Special Assistant to the Secretary of State for Research and Intelligence. Executive Order 9630 abolished the Foreign Economic Administration, transferring specified functions and responsibility for most foreign surplus property disposal to the State Department, while assigning remaining duties to other federal agencies. The passage catalogs 1945 government statements and documents concerning Lend-Lease extension, operations, discontinuance, and postwar reconstruction; Bretton Woods institutions, foreign investment, and Export-Import Bank policy; and international trade policy. On December 27, Treasury Secretary Fred M. Vinson signed the agreements establishing the International Monetary Fund and International Bank for Reconstruction and Development on behalf of the United States.

Nuclear binding energy is the difference between the summed masses of a nucleus’s constituent protons, neutrons, and electrons and the measured nuclear mass. Average binding energy per nucleon is generally 7.5–9 MeV and peaks near iron, allowing energy release through fusion of lighter nuclei and fission of heavier ones.

The semi-empirical Weizsäcker formula, also called the liquid-drop model, describes binding energy using five terms. The dominant volume term is proportional to mass number and contributes about 16 MeV per nucleon, indicating a short-range nuclear force. The surface term reduces binding because surface nucleons have fewer neighbors. The Coulomb term accounts for electrical repulsion among protons. An asymmetry term penalizes unequal neutron and proton numbers based on the Pauli exclusion principle. A pairing term favors even numbers of protons and neutrons and gives the least favorable energy when both numbers are odd. Together, these terms reproduce the binding-energy curve and its maximum near iron.

Medical professionals warn that drinking more than one glass of wine nightly may indicate chronic alcoholism. Daily alcohol consumption increases risks of pancreatitis, liver disease, obesity, dementia and cancers. Drinkers are advised to have several alcohol-free days weekly and consume no more than two standard drinks on most days. Older adults may be particularly unaware of alcohol units, while cheap supermarket alcohol and greater disposable income are linked to rising misuse. A full-strength beer or restaurant wine serving often exceeds one standard drink, and the daily limit cannot be averaged across a week.

U.S. imports from China reached $9 million in some years, while direct exports to China in 1841 totaled $715,000 in domestic products and $485,000 in foreign merchandise, excluding goods routed through other countries. China’s treaty with England and the opening of new ports were expected to improve foreign commercial access, though labor costs and established habits might limit rapid demand growth. President John Tyler recommended funding a well-qualified commissioner in China to protect American citizens, property, and commercial interests and communicate with Chinese authorities. Separately, representatives of King Kamehameha III stated that Hawaii had followed an 1826 agreement with the United States for sixteen years despite receiving no confirmation of its ratification or approval.

In soccer, an overlap sends an unmarked player from the back into attack. Typically, a wing fullback runs outside and beyond a midfielder near the sideline, creating space or freeing another attacker if covered. The overlapping player may receive the ball, approach the end-line, and cross, or return the ball to the midfielder. Unlike a vertical offensive switch, the midfielder remains in attack. An underlap uses an inside run toward the center, often leading to a shot. Both runs require adequate space, and the defender eventually returns to position. Coaches can vary overlaps and underlaps but should avoid them when extra attackers create congestion. “Overlap” may signal or identify the run, and a back-heel pass can support it.

The Washington Supreme Court affirmed dismissal of Ross Nelson’s action seeking specific performance of a 1892 agreement to purchase Puyallup allotment land from John and Chekudakai Salerhand. The court held that restrictions on alienation in the federal patent were valid despite the land being granted for consideration, because federal policy treated Indians as government wards and sought to protect them from improvident transfers. The Bland Act’s grant of citizenship did not impliedly repeal those restrictions. Washington’s statute removing restrictions required congressional consent, and Congress’s March 3, 1893 act continued restrictions for ten years on allotted lands not selected for sale. Because the Salerhands’ agreement preceded removal of the restrictions, it was void and could not support Nelson’s claim.

The passage examines how the Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming products, competition, and business models while creating a new productivity paradox: technology investment and consumer benefits may grow without corresponding gains in measured GDP. Internet-enabled free services, consumer surplus, disruptive innovations, and online piracy generate “uncaptured GDP,” defined as utility and happiness beyond monetized economic value.

An empirical analysis of 500 global ICT firms from 2005–2016 finds that sales are associated with R&D investment, but high-R&D firms increasingly experience declining marginal ICT productivity. The number of firms in this position rose from 16 in 2005 to 25 in 2016. The study attributes this decline to ICT’s two-faced nature: new functionality can raise technology value, while Internet characteristics such as free availability, easy copying, and standardization reduce prices.

In response, leading firms seek self-propagating functionality development through sophisticated digital business strategies and soft innovation resources, including changing consumer preferences, sleeping or untapped resources, trust, past experiences, memory, and future aspirations. The study reviews Samsung, Intel, Google, Microsoft, Huawei, Apple, and Amazon as examples of firms shifting toward IoT-oriented, disruptive models. It also identifies broader transitions from mechatronics to software, software to networks, networks to combined digital and physical operations, and commodities to culture.

The paper recommends that ICT firms integrate ICT and business strategy, recognize dependence on uncaptured GDP, develop trust-based disruptive models addressing social demand, and use soft innovation resources effectively. Future research should examine additional firms, Amazon’s high digital value despite limited R&D, novel business concepts, strategic road maps, and GDP’s limitations in measuring the digital economy.

The US government has auctioned the 106-meter superyacht Amadea, seized in Fiji in 2022 from a sanctioned Russian oligarch. The buyer and sale price remain undisclosed. Once valued at $300 million and later appraised near $230 million, the yacht cost taxpayers almost $1 million monthly to maintain. Its ownership remains disputed: Eduard Khudainatov, whom a judge deemed a straw owner, has appealed the forfeiture and called the auction premature. The unresolved litigation may discourage the new owner from taking the yacht into international waters.

Rigel Pharmaceutical shares rose 0.25% and closed at $4.01. Six analysts have an average 12-month price target of $5.83, ranging from $5 to $7. Recommendations comprise one Buy and five Outperform ratings, with no Hold, Underperform or Sell ratings. The stock’s ATR-14 is 0.24, weekly volatility 6.91%, monthly volatility 6.13%, and RSI 46.26. Rigel has a $599.66 million market capitalization and 149.54 million outstanding shares. Previous trading volume was 2.33 million shares, above the 1.42 million average.

The team prioritizes winning regardless of location and expects little home-ice advantage against Carolina. Players are enjoying the rare atmosphere while remaining focused, relying on experience and preparing to play hard against an opponent they know will not quit.

The article rigorously analyzes direct and inverse problems for an SEIR-like COVID-19 model with a time-dependent transmission rate. The model contains nine compartments: susceptible, exposed, vaccinated, asymptomatic, mildly infectious, severely infectious, critically infectious, recovered, and deceased. Transmission rates for asymptomatic, severe, and critical cases are fixed proportions of the mild-case transmission rate, which is estimated from observed incidence. Other parameters describe vaccination, disease progression, recovery, hospitalization, ICU admission, and death.

Assuming continuous, strictly positive parameters and nonnegative initial populations, the analysis proves that susceptible and exposed populations remain positive, all other compartments remain nonnegative, and total population is conserved. The ordinary differential equation system has a unique nonnegative solution on any finite interval and, when parameters are bounded, on the infinite interval.

The parameter-to-solution map is defined on transmission functions in the Sobolev space \(H^1\) bounded below by a positive constant. Its domain is shown to be nonempty, closed, convex, and weakly closed. The map is well defined, injective, continuous in the \(H^1\) norm, sequentially weakly closed, and Fréchet differentiable in the domain’s interior. Its derivative is characterized through a linearized ODE system. The broader study applies Tikhonov regularization to establish existence, stability, and convergence for estimating transmission rates from reported daily infections and includes a numerical example using real data.

Enron-related reports from April 7–8, 2001 covered several developments. Enron Energy Services signed a long-term agreement worth over $600 million to manage electricity supply and upgrade equipment at more than 1,250 J.C. Penney locations. Enron planned to eliminate about 250 jobs, or 20% of its broadband unit, after completing its fiber-optic network amid weak demand for streaming media. Its failed online movie partnership with Blockbuster was cited as an example of difficulties facing media and distribution convergence.

In India, Maharashtra declined to pay electricity bills from Enron’s Dabhol Power Company, prompting arbitration. State political leader Sharad Pawar urged Dabhol to lower its tariffs and advocated a negotiated solution, warning that the project’s second phase was unaffordable.

In Florida, Enron requested a one-month delay in a Pompano Beach vote on rezoning land for a proposed 510-megawatt power plant, saying it wanted an air permit first. Opponents called the request a tactic to disrupt protests.

PG&E’s bankruptcy caused stock declines among utilities, lenders, insurers and power suppliers, including Enron. PG&E listed Enron Canada as an unsecured creditor owed about $28 million. Other items included Enron’s sponsorship of a Houston Earth Day festival and references to its discontinued broadband movie-delivery venture.

The speaker welcomes foreign representatives to the Pan-American Exposition, praising expositions for recording progress, spreading knowledge, encouraging competition, and advancing art, science, industry, and invention. He argues that modern transportation and communication have connected nations, expanded trade, reduced isolation, and strengthened opportunities to resolve international disputes through arbitration.

Noting unprecedented American prosperity and industrial growth, he emphasizes the need to protect savings, strengthen the commercial system, and find foreign markets for surplus production. He advocates reciprocal trade arrangements, selective tariff adjustments, friendly commercial relations, expanded American steamship service and merchant marine, an Isthmian canal, and a Pacific cable.

He identifies the exposition with the pan-American movement and hopes its influence will promote greater commerce, peaceful achievement, mutual respect, confidence, and lasting friendship among nations.

The Buffalo goalie is focused solely on winning four games and bringing the Stanley Cup to Buffalo. He respects Dallas goalie Eddie Belfour, despite competing with him as Chicago’s backup seven years earlier, but is concentrating on Dallas’s scoring threats rather than the opposing goalie. He feels healthy and ready after a lighter practice. He expects teammates and referees to handle opponents who target or provoke him, allowing him to regain focus quickly. He also admired a former Russian national-team goalie as a child but said that goalie worked mainly with Belfour in Chicago and spent little time coaching him.

Washington University researchers identified peroxisomes as a backup heat source in mouse brown fat. Through the protein ACOX2, peroxisomes metabolize certain fatty acids, generating heat when mitochondrial heat production is impaired. Mice lacking ACOX2 had poorer cold tolerance, insulin sensitivity, and weight control, while elevated ACOX2 improved these measures. Researchers are exploring dietary and drug-based activation of this pathway, but its effectiveness in humans remains untested.

Liverpool beat Roma 5-2 at Anfield in their Champions League semi-final first leg. Mohamed Salah scored twice against his former club without celebrating, then assisted goals for Sadio Mane and Roberto Firmino. Firmino added a second goal, taking both him and Salah to 10 goals in the European campaign, while Salah reached 43 in all competitions.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain left on a stretcher after injuring his left knee, further limiting Liverpool’s midfield options. Roma started strongly and maintained an open approach, but Liverpool overwhelmed their defence before tiring late on. Roma scored twice in the final 10 minutes, leaving Liverpool with a three-goal advantage but keeping the tie alive ahead of the second leg in Rome.

Kyocera’s DuraForce PRO won an iF Design Product Award in the Industry/Skilled Trades category after being honored at the CES Innovation Awards. The military-grade rugged phone features a Super Wide View HD action camera, fingerprint scanner, IP68 waterproofing and Military Standard 810G protection. It is available from Verizon Wireless, AT&T and Sprint.

U.S. new-home sales rose 4% in March to an annual rate of 694,000, driven by a 28.3% surge in the West. First-quarter sales were 10.3% above 2017 levels despite rising mortgage rates. The median new-home price increased 4.8% to $337,200 amid record-low existing-home listings.

RTX Neural Texture Compression uses neural shaders to reduce texture memory while improving visual quality; a cited demo drops material usage from 1,110 MB to 333 MB. Stochastic Texture Filtering reduces aliasing and moiré patterns and benefits from Blackwell’s improved point-sampling rate. Neural Radiance Cache trains small networks during gameplay to infer multi-bounce indirect lighting from partially traced rays, improving performance, lighting quality, and adaptability. RTX Skin brings ray-traced subsurface scattering to real-time rendering, while RTX Neural Faces generates natural-looking faces from rasterized faces and pose data using models trained on varied offline imagery and optimized with TensorRT.

Blackwell GPUs target several graphics segments. The flagship GB202 contains 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, and a 512-bit memory interface, and powers the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores, and a 256-bit interface, powering the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. NVIDIA states that specifications may change, products require customer validation for intended applications, and the materials are provided without warranties. © 2025 NVIDIA Corporation.

JAMB is considering a mock exercise before its examination while testing new processes and ICT facilities. Registrar Ishaq Oloyede said hitches were expected but manageable, and innovations would curb illegal operators defrauding candidates. A stakeholder retreat in Abeokuta was organized to critique the board’s processes and planned facilities.

Hammes Company’s five-story, 94,000-square-foot Milwaukee headquarters is under construction at 210 E. Knapp St., with completion expected later this year. The privately financed project will replace a vacant site but has drawn mixed reactions over its Jefferson-inspired classical design. Critics have challenged its architectural quality, while Mayor Tom Barrett and Alderman Nik Kovac praised the masonry design and integrated 360-stall garage. Designed by DGP Architects and Eppstein Uhen Architects and built by Miron Construction, the $27 million to $30 million building will house about 80 Hammes employees in 36,000 square feet, with remaining office and commercial space available for lease. Hammes bought the 1.5-acre site for $1 million in 2015 and plans a second five- to eight-story office building of 90,000 to 100,000 square feet.

Enron CFO Andrew Fastow’s LJM2 partnership earned millions from Enron transactions, including over $7 million in management fees and about $4 million in capital gains. The arrangements raised conflict-of-interest concerns amid Enron’s $618 million quarterly loss, $1.01 billion write-off, $1.2 billion shareholder-equity reduction and falling stock price. A shareholder lawsuit alleged Enron’s board lost at least $35 million by permitting Fastow to manage related partnerships.

The New Power Company amended its Enron netting agreement through January 4, 2002, reducing cash-collateral requirements by allowing certain receivables and inventory as collateral while it sought asset-backed financing.

Enron also faced criticism for opaque accounting and paid Quinn Gillespie $525,000 for lobbying focused on energy deregulation. Separately, Enron Metals planned European staffing cuts of 10%–20%.

The Bombay High Court scheduled December hearings on Enron-promoted Dabhol Power Company’s challenge to the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission’s jurisdiction in its dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended September 29, 2018. Apple designs, manufactures and markets devices including iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, AirPods and HomePod, along with operating systems, software, digital content, cloud, payment and support services. Apple sells worldwide through direct channels and third-party carriers, wholesalers, retailers and resellers. Created in 2003, the S&P 500 Equal Weight Index contains the same companies as the traditional S&P 500 but assigns each a 0.2% weight at quarterly rebalancing. The traditional index weights companies by market capitalization, giving mega-cap stocks and their sectors greater influence. Equal weighting determines sector exposure by the number of constituent companies and may reduce the impact of downturns in large technology stocks.

The Invesco RSP ETF tracks the equal-weight index, while SPY tracks the market-cap-weighted index. Historically, RSP has outperformed SPY, though not during the last decade. A $10,000 investment in 2004 reportedly grew to $60,000 in RSP versus $55,000 in SPY over 18 years with dividends reinvested. The passage attributes this advantage to faster growth among smaller companies, while noting RSP’s higher expense ratio and greater return differences during turbulent periods.

Government fishery improvement initiatives may aid frozen seafood expansion. The report covers frozen seafood and meat, ice cream and desserts, ready-to-eat meals, and processed fruits and vegetables across major Thai cities and distribution channels. It recommends developing healthy convenient meals, improving cold-chain maintenance, expanding product ranges, maintaining quality standards, promoting healthy products, and collaborating with end users.

Choked gamma-ray bursts may occur when relativistic jets launched during core-collapse supernovae fail to escape the hydrogen-rich envelopes of Blue or Red Supergiants. Although gamma-ray emission is suppressed, jet-driven cocoons and shocks may produce X-ray, ultraviolet, and optical transients, accelerate particles, and generate TeV–PeV neutrinos that escape with little attenuation.

The study uses 2.5D relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations to examine jet propagation, cocoon dynamics, shock formation, and choking. Stellar density profiles combine power-law and polytropic terms. A separate set of 39,000 one-dimensional jet-head calculations found breakout time to scale linearly with stellar radius and provided estimates for choking time and maximum engine duration. Simulated jets are defined by luminosity, opening angle, enthalpy, magnetization, and engine duration. Shock cells are identified through converging flow, pressure jumps, aligned temperature and density gradients, and relativistic Mach numbers above one.

A detailed simulation considered a 15-solar-mass, 50-solar-radius Blue Supergiant and a weakly magnetized jet with luminosity \(10^{51}\) erg s\(^{-1}\), initial Lorentz factor 7, and five-second engine activity. By five seconds, the jet head reached about 0.03 stellar radii and formed external cocoon, termination, and internal collimation shocks. After engine shutdown, the head continued forward without choking during the 30-second simulation, while the collimation shock faded and cocoon expansion became more isotropic. The cocoon shock accelerated along the declining density gradient, leaving it and the residual termination shock as the main dissipation and potential particle-acceleration sites. The jet is estimated to choke roughly one minute after launch.

Future work will examine Blue and Red Supergiants across multiple jet luminosities, Lorentz factors, and viewing angles to predict neutrino and reprocessed-photon spectra, light curves, and detectability.

This cross-sectional study examined predictors of intended compliance with COVID-19 preventive measures among 15,131 adults residing in Spain during the first-wave lockdown. Data were collected through an online, non-probabilistic survey from May 15 to June 5, 2020, covering sociodemographic, behavioral, cognitive, social, affective, and personality variables.

Self-efficacy and expected outcomes were the strongest predictors of post-confinement preventive intentions. Other predictors included general adherence, information level, previous preventive behavior, perceived vulnerability, trust in scientists, and social norms. Perceived pandemic severity modified the effects of infection-avoidance behavior and perceived vulnerability of others. Regional differences were small but significant: intentions were highest in the Canary Islands and lowest in Aragón and the Balearic Islands. Personality variables contributed little after sociodemographic adjustment.

Limitations included online, non-probabilistic sampling, possible underrepresentation of people without internet access, cross-sectional timing, and low reliability for some measures. The findings support strengthening self-efficacy, providing clear and consistent public communication, and adapting health strategies to regional disparities.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation in a hybrid rendering model. Its GDDR6 memory subsystem, larger and faster L2 caches, and improved lossless compression provide approximately 50% more effective bandwidth on the RTX 2080 Ti than the Pascal-based GTX 1080 Ti.

Turing’s display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDR, and dual 8K displays at 60 Hz using Display Stream Compression. Enhanced NVENC and NVDEC units support 8K HEVC encoding and expanded video decoding, while VirtualLink combines display, power, and USB data for VR headsets through one USB-C connector. TU102 and TU104 replace prior SLI interfaces with higher-bandwidth second-generation NVLink.

Dedicated RT Cores accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, enabling ray tracing at over 10 Giga Rays per second—about ten times Pascal’s software-based performance. Hybrid rendering uses rasterization where efficient and ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. Denoising reduces the number of rays required. Turing supports NVIDIA RTX, OptiX, Microsoft DXR, and planned Vulkan ray-tracing APIs.

NGX uses Turing Tensor Cores and pretrained neural networks for graphics functions. DLSS generates target-resolution images with quality similar to TAA while requiring roughly half the shading work; DLSS 2X approaches 64× supersampling quality. Other NGX features include AI-based inpainting, slow-motion frame interpolation, and image or video super-resolution.

New graphics capabilities include Mesh Shading, which reduces CPU draw-call bottlenecks and supports efficient geometry and level-of-detail processing; Variable Rate Shading, which varies shading rates by region or primitive for content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering; Texture Space Shading, which decouples visibility and appearance sampling and reuses shading results; and Multi-View Rendering, which supports up to four hardware views per pass. Turing also expands DX12 resource binding and heap support.

The TU104 contains up to 3,072 CUDA cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, and is used in products including the RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. Tesla T4 uses 2,560 CUDA cores and 320 Tensor Cores. TU106 contains 2,304 CUDA cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores and powers the RTX 2070, without NVLink or SLI support.

NVIDIA defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based hybrid-rendering metric combining weighted Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations. For the RTX 2080 Ti, the stated calculation yields 78 RTX-OPS. NVIDIA attributes practical real-time ray tracing to hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH acceleration, and dedicated RT Cores.

Cats’ tail movements must be interpreted with overall body language: tapping may indicate attention or dreaming, whipping may signal nervousness or aggression, and position can suggest friendliness, relaxation, or defensiveness. “Zoomies” may result from arousal, frustration, fear, pent-up energy, or insufficient stimulation.

The paper proposes a weighted expectation-maximization algorithm for estimating transition probability matrices in Markov cohort-state-transition models when data have unequal observation intervals or missing transitions. Unlike the existing method that combines estimated one-step transition counts uniformly, the approach assigns weights selected through grid search to minimize variance in a chosen output, such as transition probabilities, confidence intervals, or the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER). Uncertainty is estimated using bootstrap samples.

A three-state fictitious model comparing “SuperDrug” with placebo used one-, two-, and three-month transition counts and optimized weights across 5,000 bootstrap samples. The method reduced ICER variance by 15.2% and increased the probability of cost-effectiveness at £20,000 per QALY by three percentage points, while producing similar mean ICERs. It did not necessarily make the treatment appear more cost-effective.

The authors conclude that optimized weighting is feasible without significant estimation bias when transition-count matrices come from the same or similar studies. Pooling dissimilar sources may introduce bias or non-unique estimates. They recommend assessing pooling feasibility, comparing weighted and uniform methods for precision and accuracy, validating weights, and using one method as the base case and the other for scenario analysis. Validation with clinical-trial and real-world data is needed.

The lecture reviews minimum-distance decoding for equiprobable signals over an AWGN channel and the union bound estimate, which approximates error probability using minimum distance and the average number of nearest neighbors.

Effective coding gain measures a signal set’s improvement over a baseline at a fixed error probability, set here to \(10^{-5}\). In the power-limited regime, the baseline is 2-PAM. A constellation is characterized by nominal coding gain,
\[
\gamma_c=\frac{d_{\min}^2}{4E_b},
\]
and average nearest neighbors per information bit, \(K_b\). The rule of thumb is
\[
\gamma_{\text{eff}}\approx\gamma_c(\mathrm{dB})-0.2\log_2K_b.
\]
Both 2-PAM and 4-QAM have zero effective coding gain. A selected four-point subset of a three-dimensional cube has about 1 dB gain.

Orthogonal signal sets have equidistant points, nominal coding gain \(\frac12\log_2M\), and \(M-1\) nearest neighbors. Their effective coding gain approaches 11.2 dB, the Shannon limit, as dimension increases. However, their spectral efficiency approaches zero sharply, and Hadamard-transform decoding has complexity exponential in the number of information bits. Simplex sets subtract the mean from orthogonal sets, while bi-orthogonal sets add each signal’s negative; both share similar practical drawbacks.

In the bandwidth-limited regime, M-PAM is the baseline. The nominal coding gain is
\[
\gamma_c=\frac{d_{\min}^2(2^\rho-1)}{6E_s},
\]
with a corresponding nearest-neighbor adjustment.

The next chapter introduces binary block codes: \(K\) input bits map to \(N\) coded bits, followed by binary signaling. This separation is suitable for binary signaling, with at most about 0.2 dB loss in the power-limited regime, but is not generally optimal for nonbinary signaling.

The S&P 500 fell 2.36% last week and more than 3% from Thursday’s record high, with a Monday rebound expected. Investor sentiment improved slightly, but rising volatility, stretched valuations, seasonal weakness, earnings, tariffs, and weak economic data raise correction risks. Oil declined after OPEC+ approved another production increase, though potential U.S. sanctions on Russian crude could offset excess supply. The article recommends careful position management and potentially more defensive positioning.

The lecture develops SCET calculations with rapidity divergences, which require an additional regulator and scale \(\nu\) alongside dimensional regularization and \(\mu\). For the massive Sudakov form factor, collinear modes favor \(\mu\sim m,\nu\sim Q\), while soft modes favor \(\mu\sim\nu\sim m\). Renormalization therefore occurs in two-dimensional \((\mu,\nu)\) space. Evolution is path-independent because the two scales are independent, imposing consistency relations among hard, collinear, and soft anomalous dimensions. Their combined scale dependence cancels in physical observables.

The same framework applies to small-transverse-momentum Higgs production, where collinear and soft modes generate rapidity divergences. Factorization involves a hard function, transverse-momentum-dependent gluon PDFs, and a soft function, with evolution in both \(\mu\) and \(\nu\). Jet broadening in electron-positron dijet production provides another SCET-II example.

The lecture then examines Drell–Yan production in several kinematic regimes. Inclusive Drell–Yan factorizes into a hard function and ordinary PDFs, subject to ensuring Glauber exchanges do not contribute. Near threshold, energetic radiation is suppressed, producing a hard function, PDFs, and a soft function whose evolution sums logarithms of \(1-\tau\). For isolated Drell–Yan, restrictions on hemisphere momenta permit collinear initial-state radiation and ultrasoft radiation, yielding a SCET-I factorization theorem with hard, soft, and beam functions.

Beam functions describe both the incoming proton and perturbative initial-state jet radiation. They are proton matrix elements that measure both large and small momentum components. When the jet scale is perturbative, beam functions match onto ordinary PDFs through perturbative coefficients. They commonly appear in exclusive hadron-collision processes with specified jet multiplicities.

The speaker considered the hit legitimate but expressed concern for Horton and support for Aaron. He emphasized moving forward in the finals, improving player movement on the power play, and preventing special teams from shifting momentum. He expressed confidence that the close, hardworking team would bounce back.

The guide describes optional SEV and SNP extensions using AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine. TMPM offloads copying pages and updating virtual-to-physical mappings, requires IOMMU enablement, can pause DMA during migration, and can migrate protected guest pages inaccessible to the HV/OS.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates DMA-targeted pages and requires the relevant IOMMU host page-table entry. It supports hypervisor-state pages in SNP systems and default pages in non-SNP systems. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages from Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid states to destinations in the new Pre-Migration state. Afterward, sources enter Pre-Migration state and destinations inherit source states.

Commands can migrate up to 128 nonadjacent pages, potentially across multiple guests. PM_SUCCESS means all pages migrated, PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires checking per-page statuses, and other command errors mean no migrations occurred. PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE operations may be retried after conflicts are resolved.

Performance improves with at least 16 pages per command and peaks at 128. Keeping the ring buffer populated and limiting interrupts is recommended. IOMMU structures, vIOMMU private mappings and pinned storage, ring buffers, and argument pages are non-migratable. Host software must avoid concurrent modification of referenced IOMMU page-table entries during TMPM operations.

The euro edged up against the dollar while trading remained subdued ahead of U.S. tariffs on $34 billion of Chinese goods, due July 6, and expected Chinese retaliation. The yuan gained 0.8 percent, extending its recovery after China’s central bank pledged to monitor currency fluctuations and maintain stability. Investor caution and the U.S. Independence Day holiday limited market moves, while Asian and European stocks declined. The yen strengthened on safe-haven demand. Investors also awaited Federal Reserve minutes and U.S. jobs data. Elsewhere, the Australian dollar rose after solid retail sales figures, and the Mexican peso rallied after President-elect Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador sought to reassure investors.

Blackwell is optimized to improve neural shader performance and efficiency, advancing GPU shading beyond fixed-function pipelines and programmable vertex, pixel, geometry, compute, and ray-tracing shaders. Its launch introduces developer-created neural shaders, some compatible with earlier-generation GPUs.

Wauwatosa East High School celebrated 77 years of theater with the opening of its renovated Dale K. Hidde Theatre and Encore! Encore!, a production conceived by Jennifer Lato, Amanda Marquardt and Kate Sarner. Featuring a large orchestra, extensive sets, costumes and choreography, the show revisits numbers from past productions including How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying, Sweet Charity, Jekyll and Hyde, Tarzan, Beauty and the Beast and West Side Story. Students participated in all aspects of production. The program highlights the school’s commitment to arts education and the range of disciplines involved in theater. The May 8, 2001 State Bar of Michigan e-Journal summarizes decisions across several practice areas. Courts upheld dismissal of a Title VII retaliation claim for lack of causal connection; reinstated riot charges against defendants accused of violent conduct toward police; vacated one felony-firearm conviction while permitting retrial under another predicate offense; denied transferring a juvenile prosecution to adult court; and upheld defendants’ waiver of attendance at voir dire. Other rulings affirmed termination of parental rights under statutes found constitutional and compliant with Indian Child Welfare Act notice requirements; held that a remittitur-or-new-trial order was not appealable; found private landowners lacked standing to enforce a township ordinance; and prohibited deducting estimated environmental cleanup costs from condemnation compensation. The issue also contains fields-of-practice listings, classified advertisements, job openings, archived journals, and contact information.

Both are expected to recover fully. Police arrested a 12-year-old girl, who is being held without bail and faces two felony firearm charges. Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 25, 2016 reported quarterly net sales of $42.4 billion, down 15% year over year, and net income of $7.8 billion, down from $10.7 billion. Diluted earnings per share fell to $1.42 from $1.85. Nine-month net sales were $168.8 billion and net income was $36.7 billion.

Quarterly iPhone sales declined 23% to $24.0 billion, with units down 15%. Mac sales fell 13%, while iPad revenue rose 7% despite a 9% unit decline. Services revenue increased 19% to $6.0 billion. Sales declined across most regions, particularly Greater China, down 33%, while Japan rose 23%. Gross margin decreased to 38.0% from 39.7%, partly due to foreign-exchange effects, lower sales and fixed-cost leverage.

At June 25, 2016, Apple had $305.6 billion in assets, including $231.5 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. Total liabilities were $179.1 billion, including $12.5 billion of commercial paper and $72.4 billion of term debt. Nine-month operating cash flow was $49.7 billion. Apple spent $23.7 billion repurchasing shares and $9.1 billion on dividends and dividend equivalents during the period.

The board increased the share-repurchase authorization to $175 billion, of which $127 billion had been used. Apple identified foreign-exchange exposure, component and manufacturing concentration, litigation, tax audits and an unresolved European Commission state-aid investigation as risks. Management expected fourth-quarter gross margin of 37.5%–38.0% and stated that existing liquidity was sufficient for operating needs over the next 12 months.

The study presents a multi-criteria integer model for locating ambulance stations while balancing population coverage within short and intermediate travel times and guaranteeing coverage within a legal maximum. The model assigns weighted demand points to open stations, includes fixed locations and a specified number of stations, and maximizes coverage within two response-time thresholds.

The model was applied to outdated ambulance stations in Southwest Germany. In one study area, four locations were selected from 17 candidates while accounting for 13 fixed neighboring stations. The area included 70 municipalities, over 450,000 inhabitants, and 20,444 road segments. Travel times were calculated using an OpenStreetMap road network and ambulance-specific speed profiles. Thresholds of 5, 10, and 15 minutes were used, with 15 minutes representing the legal maximum.

Using the ε-constraint method, the researchers identified 16 Pareto-optimal solutions. Maximizing five-minute coverage concentrated stations in urban areas, while maximizing ten-minute coverage distributed them more evenly, often in rural areas. Moving away from either extreme could substantially improve the other objective with only a small initial loss.

The static model assumes ambulances are present at their stations, so its solutions served as an initial decision-support stage and were subsequently evaluated by experts and discrete-event simulation. Future extensions could incorporate investment costs, multiple vehicles, multiple coverage, and simultaneous optimization of station locations and service provision.

A short squeeze occurs when a heavily shorted stock unexpectedly rises, forcing short sellers to repurchase borrowed shares. Their buying can accelerate the increase, create margin calls, and cause potentially unlimited losses because stock prices have no theoretical ceiling. Short selling is also difficult because assets generally appreciate over time, though short strategies may provide portfolio diversification.

Short squeezes are rare, random, and difficult to predict or backtest. High short interest or a high short-interest ratio may be necessary conditions, but tests found no evidence that they form a viable long strategy; highly shorted stocks generally underperform those with low short interest. Squeezes usually last two to four weeks or less than a month, depending on short volume, trading volume, short-interest ratio, and broker actions.

Notable examples include Volkswagen and GameStop. In early 2021, GameStop rose dramatically, causing major losses for short hedge funds. The passage states that natural short squeezes are legal, but manipulating a stock’s price or availability to cause one is illegal, as are naked short sales.

An exit strategy involves monitoring price momentum and short interest, using stop-loss or trailing-stop orders, and leaving before a rapid reversal after the squeeze peaks.

The study compared convalescent plasma plus best supportive care with standard care, assessing WHO clinical status, mechanical ventilation or death, sustained improvement or discharge, and intensive care outcomes. Intent-to-treat analyses used multiple imputation and regression models, adjusted for study period and site, with treatment effects reported using 95% confidence intervals.

Taylor Swift’s songwriting frequently draws on literature to explore love, reputation, isolation, betrayal, aging, and survival. Her songs reference or parallel works by Robert Frost, Shakespeare, Pablo Neruda, Lewis Carroll, Nathaniel Hawthorne, F. Scott Fitzgerald, Kurt Vonnegut, Charles Dickens, J.M. Barrie, Sylvia Plath, Charlotte Brontë, Jean Rhys, William Wordsworth, Daphne du Maurier, Emily Dickinson, Virginia Woolf, and Samuel Taylor Coleridge. Some connections are explicit, such as “Love Story,” “The Great Gatsby” references, and the Coleridge symbolism in “The Albatross”; others are thematic or speculative. Her newest single, “The Fate of Ophelia,” rewrites Ophelia’s tragic end in “Hamlet,” portraying love as rescuing the narrator from loneliness, deception, and emotional collapse.

This study analyzed brief resting-state stereo-EEG recordings from 43 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy to identify seizure-onset zones (SOZ) and predict treatment outcomes. Directional connectivity, cross-frequency interactions, 1/f power slopes, and balanced random forest models were evaluated using artifact- and spike-free interictal recordings.

Information flow predominantly traveled from non-SOZ to SOZ regions across multiple frequencies. SOZ electrodes had more negative 1/f power slopes than non-SOZ electrodes, suggesting lower excitability. Greater within-frequency information-flow asymmetry between SOZ and non-SOZ was associated with seizure freedom. Random forest models predicted SOZ with 85% accuracy and an AUC of 0.94. Seizure outcomes were predicted with 77% accuracy using clinician-identified SOZ and 72% using model-estimated SOZ.

The findings suggest that resting-state connectivity may supplement conventional prolonged ictal monitoring for SOZ localization and outcome prediction. Limitations include reliance on clinically defined SOZ, short recording segments, and omission of clinical variables from prediction models. Prospective validation and further study of behavioral-state effects are needed.
