Plasma glucose is measured pre-dose and through 45 minutes, with a 60-minute sample for patients weighing at least 21 kg. The pharmacodynamic endpoint is the area under the effect curve above baseline from 0–30 minutes, calculated in SAS. Concentrations, baseline changes, pharmacodynamic metrics, and mean and individual time-concentration curves will be summarized by treatment.

Safety analyses use the safety set and cover insulin use, hypoglycemia induction, trial medication, rescue glucose, injection-site tolerability, adverse events, laboratory tests, vital signs, ECGs, and immunogenicity. Time to first post-treatment IV glucose infusion is summarized descriptively without censoring or statistical testing.

Treatment-emergent adverse events include new or worsened events after dosing. Events are coded using MedDRA version 21.0 or higher and summarized by treatment, system organ class, preferred term, causality, and severity. Missing causality is treated as related if unresolved; missing severity is not imputed. Summaries include special-interest events, injection-site reactions, serious events, drug-related events, and deaths.

Laboratory data are listed with reference-range flags and summarized descriptively by treatment and time point, including changes from screening to follow-up. ECG analyses include overall interpretation, parameter summaries, QTcF thresholds above 450, 480, and 500 ms, and postbaseline increases above 30 and 60 ms. ADA incidence combines treatment-induced and treatment-boosted cases among evaluable patients and is analyzed descriptively without statistical testing.

Protocol-analysis changes include revised primary efficacy wording, added sensitivity and supportive analyses, and revised secondary efficacy terminology. Planned outputs include efficacy recovery analyses, Kaplan–Meier curves, safety tables, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic summaries, figures, and listings. Programming specifications define formatting, rounding, sorting, missing-date handling, derivations, and unit conversions. SAS quality control covers program and log review, output validation, dataset structure, source-data verification, figure checks, and documentation.

The President urges Congress to address the Treasury’s worsening condition, restore federal credit, and provide adequate funding for public obligations and national defense. The Treasury faces an estimated $14 million deficit; even proposed Treasury notes and a pending loan would leave a $2.5 million shortfall. Temporary measures are deemed insufficient amid stagnant trade and declining revenue prospects.

He recommends increasing import duties, potentially above 20 percent on selected goods, both to raise revenue and incidentally protect manufacturing. Because higher duties would suspend distribution of public-land sale proceeds to the States, he argues that restoring federal credit must take priority. Continuing distribution while borrowing to pay public debt would weaken creditor security.

Citing depressed American credit, banking difficulties, foreign debts, speculation, and state repudiation of contracts, he proposes funding nearly $15 million in debt and pledging public-land proceeds for interest and repayment. He maintains that sound federal finances are essential to stabilizing state credit, currency, business, and public confidence, and calls for decisive congressional action grounded in good faith and fiscal punctuality.

The paper introduces variadic nominal anti-unification, combining support for variable binding with variadic expressions to identify structural similarities and differences. Its terms distinguish bindable atoms, individual variables, and hedge variables representing finite term sequences. Freshness constraints and atom permutations support capture-avoiding substitution and equivalence modulo renaming of bound atoms.

The VNAU algorithm computes generalizations of terms-in-context using rules for elimination, decomposition, abstraction, solving, merging, and narrowing. It also records differences and substitutions that reconstruct the original terms. Restricting generalizations to a finite atom set avoids the absence of least general generalizations caused by arbitrarily added freshness constraints. The paper proves termination, soundness, and completeness for these finite-atom generalizations.

Code-clone examples show that the method can recognize similarities despite renamed local variables, changed types, deleted statements, and altered argument lists. The resulting store describes differences and reconstruction mappings, while freshness constraints identify atoms forbidden from missing positions. However, exhaustive hedge decomposition creates substantial nondeterminism, produces multiple incomparable least general generalizations, and offers limited control over selected similarities. A rigidity function is proposed to improve efficiency and control generalization granularity, particularly for clone detection, though the framework also applies to program analysis, refactoring, symbolic reasoning, linguistics, and mathematics.

The lecture contrasts Riemann and Lebesgue integration and explains why measure theory is useful in communication theory, Fourier analysis, and random processes. Riemann integration partitions the time axis, while Lebesgue integration partitions function values and measures the set of times falling within each value range. Whenever a Riemann integral exists, the Lebesgue integral gives the same value, but Lebesgue integration also handles some irregular functions that are not Riemann integrable.

Lebesgue measure assigns an interval its length, makes the measure of a countable union of disjoint intervals the sum of their measures, and assigns measure zero to sets coverable by intervals of arbitrarily small total length. The rational numbers between zero and one form a countable dense set of measure zero. A Cantor-like construction also demonstrates that an uncountable set can have measure zero.

A function is measurable when the set of times at which its values fall within any specified interval is measurable. For a nonnegative measurable function, increasingly fine value quantization produces increasing integral approximations, so its Lebesgue integral is either finite or infinite rather than undefined. A function equal to one on rational points and zero on irrational points is not Riemann integrable, but its Lebesgue integral is zero because the rationals have measure zero.

An \(L^1\) function is measurable and has a finite integral of its magnitude; an \(L^2\) function is measurable and has a finite integral of its squared magnitude, interpreted as energy. Functions may belong to either, both, or neither class. Over a finite interval, every \(L^2\) function is also \(L^1\). These definitions extend to complex functions when their real and imaginary parts are measurable.

For finite-duration \(L^1\) or \(L^2\) functions, Fourier coefficients exist and are finite. Fourier series need not converge pointwise to a function at every discontinuity, but for \(L^2\) functions they converge in the mean: the energy of the difference between the function and its finite Fourier approximation approaches zero. Conversely, any coefficient sequence with finite energy corresponds to an \(L^2\) function in this limiting sense.

An arbitrary \(L^2\) function can be divided into finite time segments, with each segment expanded as a Fourier series. This yields a double expansion in orthogonal, time-limited complex exponentials and provides a conceptual basis for applications such as voice compression, where signals are processed in short intervals. The lecture concludes by introducing Fourier transform relationships, which map between time and frequency representations and will be developed further.

Marshall University Joan C. Edwards School of Medicine, Marshall Health and Cabell Huntington Hospital welcomed four board-certified, fellowship-trained assistant professors in internal medicine. Infectious disease specialists Peimei He and Elie Khalil focus on chronic and atypical infections and immunocompromised patients. NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation in a hybrid rendering model while improving inference, graphics, memory, video, display, and VR performance.

The Turing-based Tesla T4 targets data-center, enterprise, and edge inference. It includes 2,560 CUDA cores, 320 Tensor Cores, 16 GB of memory, and 320 GB/s bandwidth, supporting FP32, FP16, INT8, and INT4. NVIDIA reports up to 40 times higher inference performance and more than 50 times greater energy efficiency than CPU-based inference. T4 accelerates workloads including image classification, video analytics, language processing, speech recognition, and search.

Turing introduces GDDR6 memory with 14 Gbps signaling and improved power efficiency, larger and faster L2 caches, and enhanced lossless compression. Together, these provide approximately 50% higher effective bandwidth than Pascal in the cited comparison. Enhanced display and video engines support DisplayPort 1.4a, 8K at 60 Hz, HDR, HEVC 8K encoding, additional HEVC and VP9 decoding formats, and higher-quality streaming with lower CPU use. USB-C and VirtualLink combine VR headset power, display, and data into one connector, while second-generation NVLink increases GPU-to-GPU bandwidth for two-way SLI.

Dedicated RT Cores accelerate bounding-volume hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection tests, enabling real-time ray tracing on a single Turing GPU. NVIDIA describes hybrid rendering as using rasterization where efficient and ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. Denoising and BVH structures reduce required rays and intersection tests; Turing is stated to achieve over 10 Giga Rays per second and roughly tenfold faster ray tracing than Pascal.

Turing Tensor Cores support NVIDIA NGX deep-learning graphics features. DLSS uses trained neural networks to generate target-resolution images with reduced shading work, while DLSS 2X targets quality approaching 64-times supersampling. Other NGX functions include content-aware inpainting, interpolated slow-motion video, and AI-based image or video upscaling.

Additional features include mesh and task shaders for efficiently rendering many complex objects; Variable Rate Shading for content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering; Texture Space Shading for reusing shading results; and Multi-View Rendering for rendering several viewpoints in one pass. Turing also expands resource binding and heap support.

TU104 powers products including GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. TU106 powers GeForce RTX 2070 and includes RT and Tensor Cores but lacks NVLink and SLI. NVIDIA proposes RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric combining weighted Tensor, FP32, ray-tracing, and INT32 operations.

NVIDIA states that specifications may change, disclaims warranties and certain liabilities, and places responsibility on customers to verify product suitability.

The guide describes optional SEV and SNP extensions for page migration using AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine. TMPM support is identified through the ENGINE_READY status bit and requires IOMMU enablement. It enables software to move pages between memory tiers while preserving guest physical addresses, safely pausing concurrent DMA and migrating protected SNP guest pages inaccessible to the HV/OS.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates DMA-targeted or hypervisor-state pages and requires the relevant IOMMU host page-table entry. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages from Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid states to destinations in the new Pre-Migration state. After migration, source pages enter Pre-Migration state and destinations inherit source states.

Commands can migrate up to 128 nonadjacent pages, including pages from multiple guests. Per-page statuses identify partial success and retryable conflicts such as PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE. Commands with at least 16 pages improve bandwidth, while 128-page commands provide maximum performance. Keeping the ring buffer populated and limiting interrupts also improves throughput.

IOMMU data structures, vIOMMU private mappings, pinned backing buffers, ring buffers, and argument pages cannot be migrated. Host software must prevent concurrent changes to referenced page-table entries.

Firmware reload requires pausing operations, dismantling the ring buffer, and preferably disabling IOMMU PAGEMIGRATION_EN bits. Reload firmware must be the same or a newer version, and software must verify ENGINE_READY afterward. Reload procedures vary by EPYC family, identified through PM_GET_CAPABILITIES; Family 19h uses FW_VER_Major 71. Debugging single commands can be facilitated by keeping the ring-buffer tail no more than one command ahead of the head.

The speaker urges fair treatment and naturalization opportunities for Japanese immigrants, arguing that justice toward foreign nationals is essential to American commerce, humanity, and international standing. Congress should strengthen federal civil and criminal laws so the national government can enforce treaty rights and prevent local violence against aliens from provoking international conflict.

In Cuba, an insurrection overwhelmed the existing government, whose president resigned after requesting American intervention. To prevent chaos and possible European involvement, the United States sent naval forces and officials to seek a settlement. When negotiations failed and Cuba’s government ceased functioning, a provisional government was established under the Piatt amendment, supported by American troops. Insurgents disarmed, existing personnel and laws were largely retained, and the provisional administration planned to restore order, hold elections, and inaugurate a new government. Peace returned, allowing the sugar-cane harvest to proceed.

The ADS8681W/ADS8685W/ADS8689W use synchronous, 32-bit input commands for byte or half-word register operations. Half-word commands ignore the address LSB and operate on 16 bits. Commands execute on the rising edge of CONVST/CS. Output in the following frame may be a fixed pattern, register data, or the latest 16-bit conversion result. Optional output flags include device address, input range, supply and input alarms, and parity.

The multiSPI interface supports four legacy SPI modes for writes and reads, single- or dual-SDO output, and source-synchronous protocols using RVS as the output clock. SPI-00-S is the default after power-up or reset; other modes are selected through SDI_CTL_REG. Valid writes require at least 32 SCLK cycles. Source-synchronous operation can use an internal or external clock.

Nine configuration registers control device identification, reset and power, input and output protocols, output formatting, input range, and alarm thresholds and status. Writes to protected reset and power-control bits require writing 69h to address 05h first.

The ADS868xW integrates a 16-bit SAR ADC, analog front end, programmable gain, ADC driver, and precision reference. An example industrial design combines ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 for software-configurable voltage, current, or temperature inputs. Programmable input alarms support high and low thresholds and hysteresis to reduce false triggering.

Separate AVDD and DVDD supplies require local decoupling. NAP and deep power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput rates while retaining configurable wake-up behavior. PCB guidance includes separating analog and digital routing, using short ground paths, placing bypass capacitors close to supply and reference pins, and avoiding vias between pins and capacitors.

The study examined knowledge, attitudes, educational integration, and programming support related to artificial intelligence in Hungarian education. Interviews involved 14 high school teachers and university lecturers, while 53 university students completed questionnaires.

Participants knew a broad range of AI applications, with ChatGPT, Copilot, DALL-E, Midjourney, and Bard/Gemini mentioned most often. They used AI for debugging, explaining steps, finding information, accelerating development, generating code and practice tasks, and summarizing material. Reported advantages included saving time, immediate answers, faster debugging, greater opportunities for creative work, and easier self-learning. Risks included cheating, excessive reliance, reduced learning effectiveness and critical thinking, legal concerns, incorrect responses, and the need for sufficient prior knowledge. Overall, 91% viewed integrating AI into education positively.

Programming experiments compared Gemini, ChatGPT, and Microsoft Copilot. For beginner tasks involving programming theorems, their overall accuracy was 64%, 92%, and 74%, respectively. None achieved complete accuracy. In four complex tasks, all eventually completed HTML, JavaScript, and JavaScript/PHP tasks, often after feedback or additional prompts. Only ChatGPT completed the longer C programming task; Gemini and Copilot provided partial solutions and advice.

The study concludes that AI can support teaching and learning through preparation, task generation, practice, assessment, debugging, and development. ChatGPT produced the most correct responses, but errors and incomplete answers frequently required additional prompts. AI was considered useful when users had critical thinking skills and basic subject knowledge, but insufficiently reliable for learners unable to identify mistakes.

Casey Paul Baumgart pleaded guilty to grievous bodily harm after kicking and breaking his cousin’s leg during a drunken altercation in Maryborough. He recorded .142 for drink driving and received an 18-month wholly suspended prison sentence.

The study examines how users employ prompting strategies, how ChatGPT adapts communication styles to prompts and issue controversy, and how its responses affect AI perceptions and issue-specific attitudes. It frames prompting as a behavioral indicator of AI literacy and second-level digital inequality.

Researchers conducted a 3-by-2 experiment involving health, science, and policy issues categorized as controversial or non-controversial. A nationally representative sample of 937 U.S. adults interacted with ChatGPT for at least five turns. Of the submitted conversations, 747 valid and relevant chats were analyzed. Communication styles were classified as self-revealing, information-seeking, fact-oriented, action-seeking, and cognitively complex. Researchers also measured citations, structural elements, and eight prompting strategies.

Only 19.1% of users employed at least one prompting strategy, with usage associated with education and party affiliation. Issue controversy affected ChatGPT’s communication styles, including action-seeking and cognitive complexity, and its citation counts, while users’ communication styles remained consistent across controversy levels. More cognitively complex responses were viewed less favorably but were associated with more positive issue-related attitude changes.

Gold rallied as the USD Index declined, but remained below resistance and resembled its 2011–2013 pattern. Silver and mining stocks showed little strength, with the GDXJ’s weak response interpreted as confirmation of a bearish precious-metals setup. The USD Index’s inverse head-and-shoulders breakout was described as being verified, with a potential rise to at least 101.3. Stocks paused near short-term support after breaking below a rising support line, signaling possible further declines. The author compares the combination of resilient gold, a rising dollar, weakening stocks, and underperforming miners to 2008. The passage also includes promotional material, reader criticism, and trading-risk disclosures.

The President urged the United States to join other nations in guaranteeing lasting peace through universal self-determination, avoidance of entangling alliances, collective protection, government by consent, freedom of the seas, and reduced armaments limited to maintaining order. He described these as both American and universal principles.

Italy’s foreign minister received the address without apparent hostility but considered it idealistic, difficult to implement, and lacking a specific plan for a peace-preservation league. The Swiss minister praised it highly. Spain’s minister said the address made a better impression than the earlier peace note and expressed willingness to cooperate, provided Spain was consulted in advance and treated as a leading neutral with a distinctive position. Hungary’s Count Tisza welcomed continued exchanges with the United States but said lasting disagreement remained because the opposing powers sought to dismantle Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire. He also claimed Austria-Hungary strongly fulfilled the President’s principles concerning nationality, religious liberty, and development.

Three-year-old Liam Radcliffe left Barassie early years nursery in Ayrshire unnoticed, passing through two doors and an unlocked gate before walking half a mile home along a busy road. His mother, Sarra Reid, returned him to the nursery and discovered staff had not realized he was missing for up to 20 minutes. Following the incident, nursery officials said the main door would be alarmed, the gate padlocked and an additional staff member provided. South Ayrshire Council confirmed the security changes. Reid said Liam would soon move to another nursery because she had lost confidence in the facility.

BG Group agreed to acquire Enron’s offshore Indian oil and gas assets for $388 million, including interests in the Tapti, Panna/Mukta and CB-OS/1 fields, with reserves exceeding 170 million barrels of oil equivalent. Analysts viewed the price as favorable, but the deal required Indian government approval and agreement from partners over BG becoming operator. BG planned further investment and possible production expansion.

Enron was separately seeking to exit its troubled 65% stake in the Dabhol power project amid payment disputes, shutdowns and a $24 million interest-payment default by Dabhol Power to Indian lenders.

Other Enron mentions included a 9.4% stock-price rise, Southern California Edison’s debt to power suppliers including Enron, and former Enron Energy Services vice chairman Thomas White’s appointment as the Defense Department’s homeland-security liaison.

The TPS7H500x-SP radiation-hardness-assured PWM controllers support space-grade DC-DC topologies including buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge at frequencies up to 2 MHz. They use fixed-frequency peak-current-mode control and require external gate drivers.

The FAULT pin enables external protections. A voltage above 0.6 V for the specified minimum pulse width shuts down switching and discharges soft-start; operation restarts after FAULT falls below 0.5 V and a delay of about 15 switching cycles. Internal thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C and restarts below 160°C.

Slope compensation prevents subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle. The recommended compensation equals the inductor falling-current slope and is programmed with a resistor from RSC to AVSS. Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation may be used; Type 2A adds a high-frequency noise-attenuation capacitor.

A synchronous push-pull design example using TPS7H5001-SP and GaN devices operates at 500 kHz and produces 5 V. Selected values include a 205-kΩ timing resistor, 25-ns dead time, 49.9-kΩ leading-edge-blanking resistor, 33-nF soft-start capacitor, 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 0.47-µH output inductor, and approximately 2.3 mF output capacitance. The design uses 170-V primary and 80-V synchronous-rectifier GaN FETs, a 7.5-Ω current-sense resistor, 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation, and a 102-kΩ slope-compensation resistor. Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins near 35 A.

The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require at least 0.1 µF of input bypass capacitance. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switch-node and high-current loops, isolating sensitive traces from switching signals and magnetics, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, and using short, wide high-current traces. TI states that application guidance must be validated by customers and warns that the devices require ESD precautions.

The disclosure describes computer-implemented systems and methods for automating orthodontic treatment planning using patient dentition data and dental professionals’ preferences. A treatment-planning engine creates and maintains a database linking users, textual key preferences, and corresponding clinical behaviors, then applies matching behaviors when generating patient-specific treatment plans and appliance schedules.

Preferences may be extracted from current or historical treatment instructions through machine-learning text classification, similarity searches such as Damerau-Levenshtein distance, and statistical analysis of consistent clinical behavior over time. Identified preferences may be manually verified before inclusion. Statistical clustering can distinguish recent or multiple behavior patterns and account for changing preferences.

Generated plans may be reviewed and modified by users, with modifications used to update the preference database. Monitoring tools compare automatically applied behaviors with accepted plans, report positive, negative, and neutral outcomes, and identify outdated or incorrect preferences. The Affordable Care Act changed nearly every part of the U.S. health system. BioRecall is a cross-sectional pilot study designed to supplement Finnish biobank genetic, biological, and clinical data with lifestyle and environmental information for research on non-communicable diseases and gene-environment interactions. The Central Finland Biobank will invite 1,386 previously genotyped adult donors with type 2 diabetes who consented to recontact.

Participants will provide electronic consent and complete a 30–40-minute REDCap questionnaire through the secure MyBiobank portal. It covers physical activity, diet, alcohol, anthropometrics, weight-loss history, smoking, substance use, medical history, women’s health, employment, emotional state, sleep, socioeconomic background, and residential environment. Postal codes will enable linkage with open-source environmental and socioeconomic data. Participants will receive automated feedback comparing selected lifestyle measures with national recommendations.

Survey responses will be pseudonymously linked to biobank records, while researchers remain unaware of participant identities. Participant and non-participant characteristics may be compared using pseudonymized data. Collected data will be returned to the biobank with consent and made available for approved research through Fingenious.

Data collection is scheduled to begin in February 2025. No formal sample-size calculation or detailed statistical analysis plan was prepared because the primary aim is to test the operational model. The approach is electronic, scalable, and potentially suitable for longitudinal monitoring, but the pilot is limited to one regional biobank, has a restricted sample size, relies on a lengthy self-report questionnaire, and does not collect wearable data. If successful, it may expand to other donors and Finnish biobanks. The study received ethics and biobank approval; patients and the public were not involved in its design.

The course has no textbook, recitations, or exams. References and materials will be posted online, and office hours are Monday from 3:30 to 4:30, with other meetings available. Grades comprise five biweekly problem sets worth 75% and an 8–10-page final project on holographic duality worth 25%. The flexible syllabus spans gravity, string theory, and quantum field theory, with substantial independent reading expected.

The lecture introduces holographic duality: quantum gravity in a dynamical spacetime can be equivalent to a nongravitational quantum field theory on a fixed spacetime. The two sides describe the same quantum system but require a dictionary connecting their quantities. This equivalence suggests that gravity and spacetime can emerge from nongravitational degrees of freedom, an idea related to earlier proposals comparing gravity with effective descriptions such as hydrodynamics.

Gravity differs from other interactions because quantum gravity lacks a precise formulation, while electromagnetic, weak, and strong interactions are described by gauge theories. A graviton is a massless spin-2 particle, raising the question of whether it could emerge as a composite state in ordinary field theory.

The Weinberg–Witten theorems constrain this possibility. A theory with a Lorentz-covariant conserved current cannot contain charged massless particles with spin greater than one-half, while a theory with a Lorentz-covariant conserved stress tensor cannot contain massless particles with spin greater than one. These results apply to elementary and composite particles. They remain compatible with QED, Yang–Mills theory, and general relativity because the relevant particles are neutral or the required covariant conserved currents or stress tensors do not exist.

The theorems rule out emergent gravity within the same spacetime as an ordinary Minkowski-space quantum field theory. Holographic duality avoids this restriction because gravity emerges in a different, typically higher-dimensional spacetime. The lecture concludes with a kinematic proof using Lorentz symmetry, helicity states, rotation properties, and matrix elements of conserved currents and stress tensors.

NVIDIA’s A100 GPU uses third-generation Tensor Cores to accelerate GEMM operations central to AI and HPC. Its 108 streaming multiprocessors contain 432 Tensor Cores, delivering up to 312 TFLOPS of dense mixed-precision FP16/FP32 performance. A100 supports FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. TF32 enables Tensor Core acceleration for FP32-based AI training without script changes, while FP16 or BF16 mixed precision provides higher throughput. FP64 Tensor Core support delivers up to 19.5 TFLOPS and 2.5 times V100’s FP64 performance.

A100 introduces 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity, allowing two nonzero values per four entries. Sparse matrix instructions skip zero values, doubling Tensor Core throughput. NVIDIA’s pruning and fine-tuning method reportedly achieves virtually no inference accuracy loss across evaluated networks.

Memory and execution improvements include 40 GB of HBM2 with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, a 192 KB combined L1/shared-memory subsystem, compute data compression, simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, and ECC protection. Asynchronous global-to-shared-memory copies, asynchronous barriers, increased thread-level data sharing, cache-residency controls, and reduced instruction and register-access requirements improve Tensor Core utilization and strong scaling.

Multi-Instance GPU technology partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory resources, predictable performance, fault isolation, and quality of service. Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances and support MPS, virtual machines, containers, migration, and multi-tenant workloads.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s aggregate bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4 supplies 31.5 GB/s per direction for x16 connections and supports SR-IOV. Additional hardware includes five JPEG decoders, five NVDEC units, an optical-flow accelerator, and faster FP16 and FP32 atomic operations.

CUDA 11 supports A100 features including new Tensor Core formats, sparsity, MIG, CUDA Graphs, asynchronous copies and barriers, L2 residency controls, and accelerated cooperative-group reductions. CUDA Graph optimizations reduce CPU launch overhead and inter-kernel latency.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs, six NVSwitches, 4.8 TB/s bidirectional interconnect bandwidth, and up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance. It can expose up to 56 isolated accelerators through MIG and is supported by CUDA, container tools, NGC software, AI frameworks, inference platforms, analytics libraries, and HPC software.

Researchers developed a DNA-PAINT super-resolution microscopy method that visualizes individual strands in DNA origami nanostructures. Results showed that assembly remains robust across varying physical conditions, including formation speed, but staple incorporation efficiency depends on target position, and not all sites are occupied. Adding excess staple strands can improve incorporation. The method can guide optimization of DNA nanostructures and may enable quantitative measurement of labeling efficiency in antibodies, cellular proteins, and nucleic acids.

Sony prepared to launch the $599 PlayStation 3 in November 2006 amid intense competition. Microsoft had sold nearly four million Xbox 360 consoles after launching a year earlier, while Nintendo’s $249.99 Wii targeted a broader audience with motion controls. The PS3 also served as a comparatively inexpensive Blu-Ray player, making Sony’s console strategy part of its standards battle against Toshiba and Microsoft’s HD-DVD format.

The video game industry had evolved through Atari’s late-1970s dominance and 1983 collapse, Nintendo’s tightly controlled revival of the market, and Sony’s successful entry with the PlayStation in 1994. Sony used 3D graphics, lower-cost CDs, and a broad game library to capture 60% of the U.S. market by 1999. The DVD-capable PlayStation 2, launched in 2000, later attained a 55% console-market share and sold more than 100 million units worldwide.

Console manufacturers generally sold hardware at or below cost and earned money through software royalties. Rising game-development costs and dependence on blockbuster titles drove publishers to acquire independent studios and intellectual property. Online connectivity also became central to competition. Microsoft offered the unified, broadband-only Xbox Live service, Nintendo’s Virtual Console emphasized downloadable classic games and other services, and Sony’s PlayStation Network supported online play, communication, purchases, and licensees’ own servers.

Sony and Microsoft continued targeting core male gamers with powerful hardware, while Nintendo sought to expand the market across ages and genders through simple games and intuitive controls. Nintendo’s strategy had already succeeded with the DS and Nintendogs.

The industry also faced criticism over violent content. The self-regulatory ESRB ratings system gained adoption but was criticized for relying on publisher-supplied clips rather than full gameplay. State restrictions were rejected on First Amendment grounds, while proposed federal legislation sought to prohibit minors from buying mature-rated games.

Analysts differed on Sony’s prospects. One forecast projected that PS3 would hold just over half of next-generation consoles through 2010, but Sony faced the Xbox 360’s head start, the Wii’s lower price, high PS3 production losses, and declining profitability in Sony’s game business.

The paper combines dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) with Gaussian process regression to model noisy, nonlinear, high-dimensional dynamical systems. DMD approximates the infinite-dimensional Koopman operator in a finite basis, enabling spectral analysis, forecasting, simulation, control, and dimensionality reduction. Kernel methods provide nonparametric, interpretable function spaces with convergence and consistency guarantees, while Gaussian processes add probabilistic predictions and model-selection tools.

The proposed Gaussian Process DMD gives a Bayesian interpretation of the embedded Perron–Frobenius operator and modifies Extended DMD to learn from noisy measurements while estimating uncertainty in multi-step forecasts. It integrates hyperparameter optimization, sparse dictionary learning, and measurement noise within one framework. To reduce the cubic costs of Gramian inversion and eigendecomposition in kernel DMD, the work applies variational free energy methods using pseudo-inputs, seeking a balance between computational complexity and generalization.

The formulation treats the embedded Perron–Frobenius operator as a random operator acting on RKHS representations of probability distributions. Training data are implicitly lifted through feature maps, target observations include isotropic Gaussian noise, and an operator-valued kernel handles the infinite-dimensional output space. The method is presented as a special case of EDMD and therefore retains some of its limitations.

The paper studies modal extensions of lattice-based semantics, interpreting necessity primarily as the greatest lower bound of formula values across accessible worlds. This framework supports classical, intuitionistic, fuzzy, relevant, and paraconsistent logics and aims to facilitate communication between worlds governed by different logics through a shared lattice order.

A normal modal extension is regular—so necessity means truth in all accessible worlds—exactly when the designated values form a filter whose greatest lower bound is designated. For finite lattices, regularity is equivalent simply to the designated set being a filter. Infinite lattices can yield non-regular extensions, including examples involving fuzzy semantics and non-principal ultrafilters.

The paper connects modal validity with lattice properties. The formula \((\Box\varphi \lor \Box\psi)\to\Box(\varphi\lor\psi)\) is valid on every frame exactly when the designated set is implicative. For strictly deductive implication, axiom K is valid on every frame exactly when the lattice is linear outside the designated filter. When implication is defined by \(\neg x\lor y\), anti-monotonicity, involutivity, down-distribution, and implicativity provide a corresponding characterization of axiom K.

An application to twist algebras derived from Boolean algebras shows that axiom K is valid precisely when the designated set contains all relevant values whose first coordinate is \(1\). The paper concludes by highlighting cross-logical communication and the finite-model property as directions for further research.

The study develops an Atomic Cluster Expansion machine-learning potential for YBa₂Cu₃O₇−x, trained on density functional theory data covering equilibrium structures, defects, disordered configurations, oxygen Frenkel pairs, and transition states. The dataset contains 1,368 configurations and 545,267 atoms. The potential achieves energy and force RMSEs of about 10 meV/atom and 70 meV/Å and improves upon a Buckingham+Coulomb potential in reproducing lattice behavior, defect formation energies, and oxygen migration barriers.

Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations reproduce the orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition near 800 K, compared with approximately 1,000 K experimentally. The transition occurs through oxygen migration from CuO-chain O1 sites, and partly apical O4 sites, into interstitial O5 sites between chains. This redistribution disorders the basal-plane oxygen sublattice, removes long-range chain order, and makes the crystallographic a and b directions equivalent.

Calculations show that thermal expansion lowers oxygen Frenkel-pair formation energies. Because these energies remain positive around the simulated transition temperature, the transition is identified as entropy-driven but facilitated by lattice expansion. Differences from experiment are associated with oxygen loss in heated samples, which is absent from fixed-composition simulations. The potential enables detailed simulations of oxygen diffusion and defect behavior in YBCO, with possible applications to radiation damage and annealing, though future work must address variable oxygen content and longer experimental timescales.

Ion trapping differs from neutral-atom trapping because Coulomb forces provide much deeper confinement. Since static electric fields cannot confine ions in every direction, ion traps generally use dynamic methods. Penning traps combine electrostatic axial confinement with magnetic-field-induced cyclotron motion, while widely used Paul or RF traps rapidly alternate confinement and anti-confinement. In RF traps, micromotion causes ions to experience a net restoring force; its kinetic energy appears as the effective trapping potential.

Both ions and neutral atoms support precision clocks, quantum information, and quantum simulations. For ion-based quantum computation, single-qubit operations use Rabi rotations, while two-qubit operations can use the Cirac–Zoller controlled-phase gate. This scheme transfers one ion’s qubit state into the shared center-of-mass vibrational mode, which acts as a data bus. A conditional phase operation is then applied to another ion before the vibrational information is transferred back. Together with single-qubit rotations, controlled-phase operations can construct a CNOT gate and enable universal quantum computation.

The Cirac–Zoller gate clearly illustrates ion-based quantum logic but requires cooling the center-of-mass motion to its ground state and becomes slower as systems scale. Other gate designs relax these limitations.

The article reviews how artificial intelligence affects inclusive education. Inclusive education seeks equitable, accessible learning for all students, regardless of disability, background, ethnicity, or ability, and requires curriculum adaptations, supportive environments, suitable infrastructure, trained educators, and collaboration among families, schools, communities, and policymakers.

AI can support inclusion through personalized and adaptive learning, rapid feedback, assistive technologies, accessible resources, continuous assessment, administrative automation, and improved communication. Tools such as text-to-speech, speech-to-text, writing aids, chatbots, virtual assistants, and accessible digital materials may increase engagement, motivation, participation, and academic performance. However, effective outcomes depend on thoughtful implementation, cultural context, teacher and student acceptance, and educator involvement in designing and evaluating AI tools. AI can support but not replace human educators, whose guidance, creativity, emotional support, and understanding of complex experiences remain essential.

Barriers include inadequate educator training, inaccessible or incompatible materials, overcrowding, insufficient infrastructure and resources, discriminatory labeling, weak stakeholder support, and resistance to technology. AI also presents risks involving biased data and curricula, privacy and security, costs, job losses, excessive technological dependence, reduced human interaction, and possible physical effects.

The non-empirical study reviewed literature from September 2023 to March 2024 using PRISMA guidelines and three scholarly databases. Its limitations include the absence of fieldwork and empirical data, limited database coverage, and insufficient attention to minority and marginalized groups.

The article recommends inclusive syllabi, Universal Design for Learning, accessible synchronous and asynchronous materials, professional development, child-centered teaching, safe learning environments, active student participation, and policies that integrate AI and accommodate special needs.

This study examined racial differences in associations between blood pressure (BP) and longitudinal cognitive decline among 2,284 Black and White adults aged 55 or older from three harmonized aging cohorts. Participants were classified as having normal, high, or variable systolic BP and completed repeated assessments of global cognition and five cognitive domains. Mixed-effects models adjusted for age, sex, education, diagnosis, and multiple comparisons.

Cognition declined over time across groups. Decline rates generally did not differ by race among participants with normal BP. White adults with high BP showed faster decline than Black counterparts in global cognition, processing speed, semantic memory, and working memory. White adults with variable BP declined faster than Black adults with variable BP in global cognition and all five domains. Results remained consistent after accounting for cohort effects and alternative model specifications, and exploratory analyses indicated that lower baseline cognitive scores did not explain the reduced association between BP and cognitive change among Black adults.

The authors discuss autonomic regulation, chronic stress, and allostatic load as possible explanations but note that these require further study. Limitations include BP categorization based on annual measurements and the absence of detailed medication adherence and medication-use histories. The findings indicate greater susceptibility to cognitive decline associated with elevated or fluctuating BP among older White adults than older Black adults and support targeted interventions addressing BP and cognitive health.

Most Southeast Asian stock markets fell on April 6 amid fears of capital outflows after Federal Reserve minutes indicated policymakers may begin reducing the central bank’s $4.5 trillion balance sheet later in the year. Investors were also cautious before the Trump-Xi meeting. Indonesia bucked the trend, closing at a record high as financial stocks gained. Philippine shares fell 0.3%, led by financial and property stocks, while Singapore and Malaysia also declined slightly. Vietnam and Thailand were closed for holidays.

U.S. economic data weakened as July added 73,000 jobs and prior months were revised down by 258,000. Meanwhile, strong corporate results lifted estimated S&P 500 second-quarter earnings growth to 11.2%. After July’s gains, seasonal weakness, high valuations, tariffs, and technical resistance may pressure markets, though the slowdown may not become a recession.

In Wiechmann v Wiechmann, the defendant appealed a divorce judgment granting shared legal custody while awarding the plaintiff physical custody of the two older children and the defendant physical custody of the younger twins. Although a custody specialist recommended that the defendant receive custody of all four children, the trial court found the parents essentially equal under the statutory best-interest factors, except that maintaining a stable, satisfactory environment slightly favored the plaintiff.

The Court of Appeals affirmed. It held that courts should seriously consider sibling bonds and the possible harm caused by separation, and that keeping siblings together will usually serve their best interests. However, the best interests of each individual child ultimately control. The trial court properly applied the statutory factors and did not commit legal error or palpably abuse its discretion by separating the siblings under the custody arrangement.

At the 2018 Scripps National Spelling Bee, 113 contestants were returning competitors, including 41 finalists. Erin Howard, 13, prepared for her third appearance by studying several hours daily, focusing on trademarked words after misspelling “Klydonograph” in 2017. Cameron Keith, 12, studied up to nine hours on weekends and said experience made him calmer in competition. Four-time participant Naysa Modi, 12, also spent hours reading, typing and being quizzed. The spellers and their families described years of intense preparation and personal sacrifices. While the contestants hoped to win, they also valued their love of language, increased confidence and stronger family relationships.

AMD Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) securely applies non-persistent runtime updates to selected AMD firmware, modules, and register settings without BIOS reflashing or system resets. It excludes x86-executed BIOS components and run-once boot code. Updates target specific firmware and patch levels, must be reapplied after reboot, and are intended as interim measures between BIOS releases.

AMD signs every package; customers may require co-signing by configuring BIOS and supplying a public key during early boot. The AMD Security Processor verifies applicable versions and signatures, protects package memory, executes the patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status. SFS tracks overall, system, firmware, and security patch levels while preventing rollback through monotonically increasing values.

Customers are responsible for enabling SFS, validating patches, managing co-signing keys, and providing a deployment agent. Packages apply sequentially and only after complete validation. They may replace firmware images, update portions of firmware, or modify registers and SRAM. Updates are designed to minimize operational impact, though some SEV virtual machines may require stopping and restarting.

FCA data found 70% of adults planning to access defined contribution pensions within two years had not been asked by providers about their plans, while 67% had received no provider advice. Among those without advice, 40% preferred making their own decisions. The state pension was expected to be the largest retirement income source by 33%, and 44% had a good idea of their annual retirement income.

Taxify will launch in Sydney on Tuesday, offering half-price fares for one month. Its first Australian operation has registered more than 4,000 drivers and charges 15 per cent commission. Founded in Estonia in 2013, the app operates in 20 countries with four million users. Holiday surge pricing will be capped at 1.5 times standard fares.

Marco Gonzales allowed no earned runs over 6 2/3 innings as the Seattle Mariners beat the Texas Rangers 2-1, their ninth win in 10 games and MLB-leading 16th one-run victory. Gonzales extended his scoreless streak to 19 1/3 innings. Seattle scored twice in the sixth after Rougned Odor’s defensive miscue, with Nelson Cruz and Kyle Seager delivering RBI singles. Texas scored its lone run on a passed ball. Alex Colome pitched a scoreless eighth in his Mariners debut, and Edwin Diaz earned his 19th save. Newly acquired Denard Span went 0 for 4. Seattle expected Jean Segura to return Tuesday and Dee Gordon on Thursday, while Texas infielders Elvis Andrus and Adrian Beltre took ground balls before the game.

The Covid-19 pandemic accelerated the shift from face-to-face to distance education, highlighting the need for adaptable, effective digital learning systems. This literature review examines artificial intelligence-assisted education, including machine learning, deep learning, algorithms, neural networks and Intelligent Education Systems (IES).

AI can support personalized teaching, assessment, student services, data management, educational games and administrative decision-making. IES typically combine domain, pedagogy and learner models to adapt instruction through analysis and feedback. Proposed formats include AI-supported human teaching, face-to-face teaching delivered by AI, and AI-based simulation education. These systems may use supervised, human-defined algorithms or unsupervised deep learning in which AI develops curricula and teaching methods.

Potential learning environments range from classrooms with virtual or robotic teachers to augmented-reality simulations accessed through devices or possible future neural-computer integration. AI-based education may improve personalization, motivation, learning performance, efficiency and access while reducing costs and training risks. It could serve many learners simultaneously and offer experiences unavailable in conventional classrooms.

However, the passage identifies concerns about machine control, privacy, cyberattacks, manipulation, social isolation, psychological effects, confusion between virtual and real environments, adaptation difficulties and educator unemployment. Computers have not reached human mental capacity, but continued technological progress makes expanded educational use plausible. The authors conclude that AI-based education requires broader research and serious ethical, social and philosophical discussion.

State officials broke ground on the $220 million Mauka Concourse at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport. Scheduled for completion by late 2020, it will add larger-aircraft gates and 260,000 square feet of passenger facilities as part of a $1.3 billion modernization project.

Audi, BMW, Volkswagen and Volvo have discontinued several manual-transmission models in their local ranges, largely because of weak market demand as buyers prefer automatics. Some manual variants remain available, while Porsche has committed to manuals and Jaguar South Africa recently added manual F-Type versions.

This retrospective cohort study used All of Us survey and electronic health record data to predict healthy aging from social determinants of health. Healthy aging was defined using age, modified Charlson comorbidity index, cognitive impairment, and assisted-living status. Among approximately 99,936 adults aged 50 or older, 44% met the primary healthy-aging definition. Logistic regression, multilayer perceptron, and XGBoost models were evaluated; oversampled XGBoost performed best, with AUROCs of 0.795 in the primary cohort and 0.862 in the secondary cohort. Its predictive values and accuracies were similar across race and gender groups. Health insurance type was the strongest predictor, followed by employment status, substance use, and insurance coverage. Limitations included the healthy-aging definition, potential volunteer selection bias, limited generalizability, and unmeasured confounding.

Research suggests that improving classroom air quality through portable filters and better ventilation can raise test scores, reduce absenteeism, and improve health at relatively low cost. Following a California gas leak, schools receiving air purifiers saw math gains equivalent to about three months of learning, with similar English improvements, while equipment and operating costs were approximately $30 per student. Other studies cited found reductions in student absences and illness-related daycare absences, though further research is needed.

Cleaner air may support cognition, reduce respiratory infections, allergies, and asthma triggers, and particularly benefit low-income students attending older schools or those near pollution sources. Portable purifiers also require less staffing and infrastructure than interventions such as smaller classes or tutoring.

Schools are encouraged to reactivate pandemic-era devices or pilot purifiers, targeting sufficient clean-air delivery with low noise, while tracking academic, attendance, health, and teacher outcomes. Philanthropists, advocates, and researchers could fund equipment, establish standards, lower purchasing costs, and conduct larger randomized trials.

Index Markets Research’s Global Plastic Granules Market report analyzes market size, trends, drivers, dynamics, segmentation, growth, revenue forecasts, manufacturing costs, production capacity, and competitive conditions. It covers key players including Dar Al Khaleej Plastics, Nahata Plastics, Vanshika Plastic Industry, Balaji Plastic, Navkar Industries, Shakti Plastic Industries, and Wiwat Plastic. Segmentation includes commercial, government, and personal sectors; product types such as PP, HDPE, PPCP, LLDPE, LDPE, and others; and applications including plastic products, clothing, and others. Regional analysis covers North America, China, Europe, Southeast Asia, Japan, and India, with production, consumption, revenue, market share, and growth data from 2012 to 2022. The report also includes historical and prospective market value and volume, player strategies, SWOT analysis, investment feasibility, development trends, product specifications, production methods, cost structures, and recommendations for companies.

The Cincinnati Bengals will start newly acquired quarterback Joe Flacco against the Green Bay Packers. Cincinnati traded a 2026 fifth-round pick to Cleveland for Flacco and a 2026 sixth-round selection.

Flacco, 40, began practicing Wednesday and will take all starting repetitions. He faced Green Bay in Week 3, leading Cleveland to a 13-10 win, and played against Cincinnati in Week 1.

The Bengals made the change after losing three straight games with Jake Browning starting in place of injured Joe Burrow, who is recovering from surgery for turf toe. Browning will return to the backup role. Coach Zac Taylor said there is no timetable for Burrow’s return.

Cincinnati hopes Flacco’s experience and recent preparation for Green Bay will help end its skid and maintain playoff contention.

Iamgold shares were unchanged in the latest session, closing at $4.90. Thirteen analysts set an average 12-month price target of $7.65, ranging from $6.25 to $9.05. The company’s average brokerage recommendation is 2, with an industry rank of 194 out of 265. Analyst ratings include 3 Buy, 6 Outperform, 6 Hold, 2 Underperform and no Sell recommendations.
