Australian ecosystems are undergoing sudden, potentially irreversible shifts as gradual climate change combines with increasingly frequent and intense extreme weather. Despite their adaptation to climatic variability, even largely undisturbed systems are losing resilience as recovery intervals shorten.

Recent examples include kelp forests becoming seaweed turfs after a 2011 marine heatwave, wildfire destruction of Gondwanan refugia, Murray River floodplain forest dieback after prolonged drought, alpine forests converting to shrubland after repeated fires, arid-zone population booms and collapses following extreme rain, and extensive mangrove dieback after a weak monsoon. Only the Murray River forests had substantial prior human disturbance.

Ecosystem collapse can result from a single extreme event, accumulated gradual decline, repeated events that prevent recovery, or interacting climatic pressures. Consequences include losses of biodiversity, fisheries, forest resources, carbon storage, pasture quality, tourism, and water quality and supply. Collapse is difficult to predict, while interventions such as assisted recolonisation, reseeding, and fire protection are costly, uncertain, and less likely to succeed as extreme events become more frequent. Nonetheless, the growing risk to apparently healthy ecosystems may make inaction more dangerous than intervention.

El neuromarketing aplica técnicas neurocientíficas al estudio de la conducta del consumidor y se utiliza en el sector audiovisual para analizar contenidos, promociones y bloques publicitarios. Aunque internacionalmente diversas empresas de entretenimiento ya recurren a estos servicios, su implantación en España es todavía incipiente.

El estudio analizó la situación del neuromarketing audiovisual español mediante 18 entrevistas a consultoras, representantes del sector, neurocientíficos y académicos. Los entrevistados confirmaron la viabilidad de estudiar al consumidor audiovisual, pero señalaron limitaciones éticas, dificultades para interpretar y aplicar los datos, problemas de representatividad de las muestras y la necesidad de equipos multidisciplinares formados en neurociencia, psicología, ingeniería, marketing y comunicación.

Las cinco consultoras españolas estudiadas habían trabajado para la industria audiovisual, que representaba, en promedio, el 33% de su actividad y el 38% de su facturación. Sus servicios se concentran en el análisis de contenidos y la mejora de la eficacia publicitaria. El crecimiento reciente ha sido notable, aunque limitado a pocos clientes. Las principales barreras son el desconocimiento, la desconfianza, la mala praxis, la escasa cultura innovadora, el precio y la falta de resultados directamente aplicables.

Atresmedia y Mediaset España son los principales grupos que emplean estas metodologías. Mediaset las aplica a ficción y publicidad, mientras Atresmedia mantiene su uso principalmente en bloques publicitarios tras encontrar dificultades para interpretar resultados sobre contenidos. TVE abandonó experiencias similares por motivos económicos. Las productoras muestran interés, pero sus bajos presupuestos y la falta de personal especializado dificultan la inversión.

Se prevé una evolución positiva, condicionada por el desarrollo y la estandarización tecnológica, una mejor interpretación de datos, menores costes, avances científicos y la demostración del retorno de la inversión. La consolidación del sector también requiere mayor transferencia entre universidad y empresa y respuestas más ajustadas a las necesidades audiovisuales.

Virginia defeated North Carolina 71-63 to win the ACC Tournament at Barclays Center. The tournament also featured North Carolina’s rivalry win over Duke, standout play from Duke’s Marvin Bagley III, and Clemson’s NCAA Tournament-bound season. Barclays Center expressed interest in hosting the event again.

Institute manager Kevin Deery expressed frustration after a third consecutive draw, saying his side deserved to beat Larne but lacked luck and missed several chances. He blamed poor decision-making in both penalty areas for Larne’s unusual free-kick goal and Institute’s failure to score beyond two own goals in 180 minutes. Despite sitting below their desired position, Deery remains confident in his players, with Institute still in the top six and 13 games remaining.

IES Holdings has nearly doubled year to date, outperforming infrastructure peers and the Russell 2000. Despite residential weakness, data-center projects are boosting other divisions. Backlog exceeds $2 billion, growing over 20% annually, alongside stronger cash flow and record cash balances. However, the stock appears overextended, with a weak free-cash-flow yield and increased insider selling, supporting a wait-for-a-pullback view.

Former Maui County Councilmember and 2018 mayoral candidate Mike Victorino struck two teenagers crossing West Papa Avenue on April 13. Police said alcohol and speed were not factors, and Victorino remained at the scene. Both teenagers sustained nonlife-threatening injuries. Police reported they were outside a crosswalk, while the older teen’s mother said her son claimed they were in one.

The study simulates replacing ICE vehicles with four BEV models using one year of anonymized telematics data from 10,441 drivers in Asti, Italy. After cleaning, the dataset contains 10.1 million trips covering nearly 98.9 million km. Each recorded trip is replicated while updating battery state of charge according to vehicle- and road-specific consumption.

Four charging policies are assessed: workplace AC charging, low-state-of-charge AC charging, overnight AC charging, and low-state-of-charge DC fast charging. Workplace-only charging performs worst, enabling 64%–88% of trips on average. Fast charging performs best: all models except the Fiat 500e exceed 98% average feasible trips, while the Audi A6 e-tron is suitable for 95% of users and enables 72% to complete every trip. Overnight charging with the Fiat 500e is suitable for 35% of users and maintains average post-trip charge above 70%. Charging frequency varies substantially by policy, with low-charge-threshold policies requiring fewer sessions than overnight charging.

Current BEVs can meet many users’ needs but not those of the entire population; even the best combination is insufficient for 5% of users. Limitations include fixed consumption and charging rates, assumed charger availability at every eligible parking event, omitted costs, and analysis of only one region.

A February 6, 2002 media roundup reports expanding investigations into Enron’s collapse. William Powers testified that executives knew partnerships concealed losses, inflated earnings and enriched insiders, while controls and oversight failed. Congressional committees subpoenaed Kenneth Lay; Jeffrey Skilling planned to testify, while Andrew Fastow was expected to invoke the Fifth Amendment absent immunity. Arthur Andersen faced criticism over auditing and document destruction. Other reports covered reduced bankruptcy financing, broadband-unit back taxes, disputed stadium naming rights, a Spanish regulatory inquiry, employee retirement losses, whistleblowing, weakened investor confidence in corporate accounting, and commentary and satire about Enron’s broader impact.

Linebackers require toughness, athleticism, intelligence, and versatility. Positioned 3–5 yards behind the defensive line, they often organize the defense, relay coaching calls, stop runs, rush passers, and cover receivers or zones. Their name reflects their original role backing the defensive line in run support. Positions include Sam, Mike, Will, and Jack.

Key skills include vision, agility, tackling, strength, explosiveness, block shedding, change of direction, violent hands, and sustained effort. Typical estimates range from 5'10" to 6'5" and 215–255 pounds with a lean-muscular build.

Notable linebackers include Hall of Famers Ray Lewis, Chuck Bednarik, and Lawrence Taylor, all recognized for major championships and individual honors. Although inside linebackers have declined in NFL value as passing offenses emphasize edge rushers and defensive backs, versatile linebackers remain valuable because they can defend the run, rush the passer, and play man or zone coverage, creating flexibility and favorable matchups for defenses.

On October 22, 2001, Enron shares fell about 21% after the SEC requested information on related-party transactions involving partnerships formerly run by CFO Andrew Fastow. Enron pledged cooperation and said its board, auditors and attorneys had reviewed and approved the disclosed arrangements. The partnerships were linked to a $35 million charge, a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity and concerns about conflicts of interest, debt ratings and potential shareholder dilution. Shareholders filed derivative and class-action lawsuits alleging fiduciary breaches and securities fraud.

Broader U.S. markets rose on stronger-than-expected corporate earnings despite anthrax concerns and weakening economic indicators. Separately, UniPrime signed a letter of intent for an interest in an Enron-owned wind park ground lease in California.

The Canadian dollar rose to nearly 75.50 U.S. cents Wednesday as strong economic data increased expectations of a Bank of Canada interest-rate hike. The loonie had previously fallen from a rapid January rise to 72.73 U.S. cents on May 4. Its movements largely reflect oil prices and the Canada-U.S. interest-rate gap, both of which have recently pressured it downward. However, first-quarter economic growth of 3.7 per cent, stronger employment and business investment indicate recovery from the oil-related recession. Recent Bank of Canada comments suggest monetary tightening may come sooner than expected, though Governor Stephen Poloz highlighted export challenges, signalling concern about excessive currency strength. CIBC now forecasts a rate increase in the fourth quarter rather than 2018.

Colorado State University officials reviewed feedback from the first two on-campus football games. Student leaders plan to rebrand the underused tailgating lot and add pregame programming. Attendance was 37,583 for the opener and 27,038 for the second game. Initial stadium-entry and concession congestion improved by game two. Transportation planning was largely successful: transit carried 7,000 attendees at the opener, exceeding the projected 5,000, while bicycles and MAX service were popular. Hooker reported 50 vehicles were towed from campus lots each game weekend, with a similar number towed from nearby neighborhoods.

Allen Iverson told ESPN that his 2013 divorce from Tawanna Turner marked his lowest point and prompted deep self-reevaluation. After retiring that year, he reconciled with Turner and recognized alcohol as a source of negative experiences while rebuilding his marriage. Discussing his memoir “Misunderstood,” Iverson also reflected on his difficult childhood, career, maturation, family responsibilities and influence on younger NBA players’ self-expression.

The study examined whether role-taking and literacy interventions reduce demographic and appearance-based biases in trust and risk-taking during social engineering scenarios. An online mixed-factorial experiment involved 139 Arab participants assigned to persuader, persuadee, literacy, or control groups. Participants evaluated 16 personas varying in age, gender, ethnicity, and attire before and one week after interventions involving role-taking scenarios or educational materials.

Repeated-measures analyses found no significant intervention effects on trust, risk-taking, or word-of-mouth behavior across persona characteristics. Bayes Factors generally supported the absence of an effect. Issue involvement changed significantly, though post hoc comparisons found no differences between specific groups. Self-esteem moderated changes in trust toward casually versus formally dressed personas, with a small effect.

The findings supported the null hypothesis, suggesting brief interventions did not alter reliance on demographic and appearance cues. Participant feedback nevertheless described the activities as engaging and reflective. Limitations included imagined rather than real-world scenarios, possible social desirability and recall effects, and limited emotional engagement from static comic-based simulations. The study concludes that deeply ingrained biases may require longer-term, immersive, interactive approaches such as games or virtual reality.

The Great Southern Storm named a 45-player colts squad for next month’s carnival in Kulin. Glynn Verbruggen replaces long-serving coach Phil Gilbert and will assess players during two training sessions and upcoming local matches before selecting the travelling team. The squad includes State 16 members Heath Spinks and Jacob Blight, plus eight players with State Country colts experience. North Albany has the largest representation with 12 players. Training will be held at Railways on June 4 and 11 from 5.30pm.

Chipotle launched queso on Sept. 12 to boost sales, but customers criticized its taste and prices, including $6.25 for large chips and queso. A spokesman said tests showed increased visit likelihood and prices would remain because the dip uses real, whole ingredients.

The central issue is whether Germany can organize Middle Europe’s resources and manpower through control of the Poles, Czechs, South Slavs, and Bulgaria, thereby becoming Europe’s dominant power. The United States should not oppose regional economic or cultural integration itself, but should dismantle imperial control by ruling groups in Berlin, Vienna, Budapest, Sofia, and Constantinople. Their alliance rests on shared interests in subjugating nationalities, preserving German-Magyar dominance, exploiting Bulgarian grievances, maintaining Turkish integrity, and managing wartime debts to Germany.

The strongest leverage against Germany is economic: exclusion from raw materials, markets, and communications could obstruct industrial recovery and demobilization, threatening unrest, financial ruin, and continued hardship. Combined with the prospect of international cooperation, this pressure could secure concessions, especially during prolonged peace negotiations.

In Austria-Hungary, Czech and South Slav nationalism and potential Polish reorganization could weaken existing political coalitions. Meanwhile, the emperor and ruling groups seek to preserve the empire through no annexations, disarmament, and a league of nations guaranteeing the status quo. The proposed policy is to encourage nationalist discontent without permitting Austria-Hungary’s complete dismemberment, while offering its rulers security in exchange for independence from Berlin and participation in a league of nations.

The paper constructs strong pseudorandom unitaries in the quantum Haar random oracle model. Its construction,
\[
G^U(1^\lambda,k)=X_{k_3}U_\lambda X_{k_2}U_\lambda X_{k_1},
\]
uses two Haar-oracle queries and \(O(\log^{1+\epsilon} n)\) random bits while remaining secure against polynomially many forward and inverse queries.

The proof replaces Haar-random unitaries with Ma and Huang’s path-recording isometries, which record oracle interactions in relation databases. An approximate isometry \(S\) merges the two independent databases of the ideal experiment into the real experiment’s combined database while simulating compatible keys. Query-by-query operator-norm bounds show that applying \(S\) before or after each forward or inverse oracle query produces negligibly close states.

The analysis proceeds through hybrids: it uses Haar-measure invariance to rebalance the real oracles, replaces Haar unitaries with path-recording operators, modifies those operators to decouple their left and right databases, applies \(S\) to transition to independent databases, and finally returns to two independent Haar-random unitaries. Additional simplifications use unnormalized operators shown close to isometries. The work addresses a gap left by earlier results establishing pseudorandom primitives in QHROM and forward-only pseudorandom unitaries in the inverseless QHROM.

Texas will replace STAAR in 2027-28 with three shorter tests administered at the beginning, middle and end of the school year. Schools may select TEA-approved national assessments for the first two, while TEA will create the final test. Results must be released within about two days, and practice tests for grades 3-8 will be banned.

Supporters say the overhaul will monitor academic growth, reduce testing time and ease pressure. Critics fear it may increase stress if all three exams follow STAAR’s restrictive protocols, while the high-stakes end-of-year test continues to heavily influence school accountability ratings. A required study of testing’s role in ratings is not due until 2029-30, and TEA need not implement its findings.

Educators and parents want teacher input, less restrictive testing conditions and access to assessments such as MAP, which many districts already use to measure growth. They argue that relaxed administration is essential to reducing anxiety and that school ratings should reflect accomplishments beyond standardized tests.

Energy Central’s August 25, 2000 forum asks whether federal policy should encourage natural-gas exploration and production on federal lands and the continental shelf amid projected demand and record winter prices. Responses are due September 15.

Published responses to the previous question debate whether generators manipulated California electricity markets and whether price caps should protect consumers. Opinions vary: some allege collusion or withholding, while others attribute price spikes to hot weather, fuel costs, limited generation and transmission, regulatory design, and supply-demand imbalances. Many oppose caps as discouraging investment, conservation, and new capacity; others support temporary or cost-based caps. Proposed solutions include expanding generation and transmission, improving demand management, encouraging competition, reforming market rules, or re-regulating the industry.

LAPIS is an MLIR-based compiler framework designed to combine performance, portability, and productivity for computational science and AI/ML. It addresses two challenges: creating an extensible, performance-portable compiler based on Kokkos concepts, and efficiently integrating C++ scientific applications with Python-based ML code. LAPIS compiles native Python ML functions into Kokkos-based C++ that can be integrated directly into scientific applications.

The framework accepts high-level MLIR, generally conforming to the linalg-on-tensors contract, through torch-mlir or MPACT. It lowers programs through platform-agnostic intermediate representations and a custom Kokkos dialect, then emits portable parallel C++ or supports further architecture-specific lowering. Its principal additions to MLIR include the Kokkos dialect, mappings for Kokkos Kernels linear algebra operations, accelerator-oriented lowering passes, a Kokkos-inspired memory model with DualView support, and a C++ emitter.

The Kokkos dialect represents portable execution and memory abstractions, hierarchical parallel loops, reductions, synchronization, and dense matrix operations such as GEMM and GEMV. LAPIS maps parallel loop nests to Kokkos policies according to nesting depth, estimates team and vector parameters using compile-time or runtime information, and inserts synchronization where needed. For sparse CSR-like traversal, it estimates inner-loop parallelism from the average entries per row.

The authors demonstrate lowering sparse and dense linear algebra operations and coupling scientific computing with SciML and image-processing workloads. Tests on AMD MI300A and NVIDIA H100 GPUs and Intel Granite Rapids CPUs reportedly match hand-optimized implementations. Compared with related compilers such as TACO, COMET, Triton, DISTAL, SpDISTAL, and LegateSparse, LAPIS emphasizes automatic end-to-end performance portability and easier extension to new architectures.

Paul Clement is set to become Swansea manager after Bayern Munich allowed him to hold talks. He is expected to sign until 2019 and receive a £30 million transfer budget. Swansea, 19th in the Premier League after conceding 44 goals in 19 games, dismissed Bob Bradley following a 4-1 defeat to West Ham. Neil Taylor said players would support Clement’s efforts to avoid relegation.

The State Bar of Michigan’s May 23, 2001 e-Journal summarizes decisions in bankruptcy, constitutional law, civil rights, criminal law, employment, family law, insurance, litigation, municipal law, torts, and real property. Key rulings include: states ceded sovereignty over bankruptcy discharge matters, defeating Tennessee’s immunity claim in In re Hood; rejection of an unsupported racial-discrimination claim; affirmance of several criminal convictions and suppression rulings, while reversing dismissal of charges for delayed discovery; affirmance of three parental-rights terminations; enforcement of an ordinary insurance loss-payable clause; approval of striking an untimely supplemental witness list; reinstatement of a zoning variance denial based on self-created hardship; and affirmance of tort rulings involving the fireman’s rule, insufficient negligence evidence, an open and obvious hazard, and employee defamation damages. The issue also contains legal practice listings, classified advertisements, employment opportunities, bar events, archives, and subscription and contact information.

A federal judge dismissed Drake’s defamation, harassment and deceptive-acts lawsuit against Universal Music Group, ruling Kendrick Lamar’s “certified pedophile” lyric in “Not Like Us” was nonactionable opinion made during a heated rap battle. Drake plans to appeal.

Springfield police officer Conrad Lariviere faces disciplinary review after posting “Hahahaha love this” about Heather Heyer’s death during a white nationalist rally protest in Charlottesville. Police Commissioner John Barbieri launched an internal investigation, and Mayor Domenic Sarno condemned the comment. Lariviere apologized, calling it a stupid comment, and denied being racist or wanting anyone murdered.

Video output signals carry the eight MSBs: G/Y/YC lines provide green, Y/luma, or multiplexed Y/Cb/Cr data; B/Cb/C lines provide blue, Cb, or multiplexed chroma data and are unused in BT.656 mode. Pin-state and internal-pull abbreviations describe default reset behavior.

Williams & Connolly said hackers used a zero-day vulnerability to access a small number of attorney email accounts. The firm found no evidence that confidential client data was extracted from other systems and said it blocked the suspected nation-state-affiliated attacker. Mandiant recently warned that Chinese government-linked hackers were targeting law firms for national security and trade information.

The 1956 Hungarian revolt became a nationwide challenge to Soviet control. Communist leader Mátyás Rákosi had eliminated political opposition and imposed collectivization and rapid industrialization, contributing to economic failure and public discontent. De-Stalinization, Yugoslavia’s independent Communism, and political change in Poland encouraged Hungarian dissidents. After Rákosi was replaced by Erno Gero, a student manifesto demanded nationalist Communism, neutrality, and Soviet withdrawal. A Budapest rally on 23 October escalated when state security police fired on demonstrators, prompting revolutionary councils across Hungary.

The government requested Soviet intervention while restoring Imre Nagy as prime minister. Initial Soviet military action intensified resistance, but Soviet representatives subsequently confirmed Nagy, replaced Gero with János Kádár, withdrew tanks, and promised Hungarian sovereignty. These concessions concealed preparations for invasion. With international attention diverted by the Suez Crisis, around 250,000 Soviet troops and 2,500 armoured vehicles surrounded Budapest and attacked on 3–4 November. Hungarian resistance was largely defeated by 14 November and ended by 30 November. About 25,000 Hungarians and 7,000 Soviet soldiers were killed.

The DAWN-PLASMA study was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 multicenter trial evaluating convalescent plasma plus standard supportive care versus supportive care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Participants were allocated 2:1. The primary endpoint was the percentage alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary and exploratory endpoints included clinical status, sustained improvement or discharge, ventilation or death, thromboembolism, transfusion reactions, antibody titers, safety, quality of life, laboratory data, vital signs, and viral PCR.

Eligible adults provided informed consent, had confirmed or clinically supported SARS-CoV-2 infection, and met respiratory or imaging criteria. Exclusions included existing mechanical ventilation, unacceptable safety risks, severe plasma allergy, treatment restrictions excluding ventilation or intubation, and recent anti-CD20 therapy.

Patients assigned plasma received 800–1000 mL in four 200–250 mL units. The first two units were administered within 12 hours of randomization when possible, followed by two units 24–36 hours later. Plasma required neutralizing-antibody titers of at least 1/160.

Five patients withdrew consent and one had a non-COVID diagnosis before intervention; all six were replaced. No participants were lost to follow-up after intervention. Ethics committees approved the protocol and consent documents, and the study followed Declaration of Helsinki and ICH Good Clinical Practice guidelines.

Indianapolis Public Schools is seeking public input on a task force proposal to close three high schools by 2018-2019. Enrollment has fallen from 109,000 students in 1967 to 30,000, leaving all seven high schools under capacity. The report recommends operating four schools for flexibility. Public meetings will continue through May, administrators may recommend closures in June, and the board will vote in September.

CEMEX evolved from a small Mexican cement company into a publicly traded global building-materials leader with 65,000 employees, operations in 50 countries, and $21.7 billion in 2007 revenue. Its expansion culminated in major acquisitions of Southdown, RMC, and Rinker, although leverage from the $15.3 billion Rinker purchase contributed to financial pressure during the 2008 downturn.

CEMEX’s international growth relied on engineering, information technology, operational discipline, transparency, and acquisition integration. Its “CEMEX Way” standardized processes, technology, and organizational structures while preserving local operational flexibility. Post-merger integration teams spread established practices, catalogued acquired companies’ methods, and adopted superior ones across the corporation. An estimated 70% of CEMEX practices originated from acquisitions, while integration time fell from 25 months for its 1992 Spanish acquisitions to under five months for Southdown.

Internationalization began after Mexico’s economic opening and increased foreign competition. CEMEX divested unrelated businesses, developed export terminals, and introduced CEMEXNET and an executive information system. Its 1992 acquisition of Spain’s Valenciana and Sanson responded to competitive threats, provided access to cheaper capital, and produced substantial efficiency gains. CEMEX also learned from Spanish operations, notably adopting petroleum coke as fuel. Difficulties integrating a Colombian acquisition later taught the company to balance standardization with learning from acquired firms.

CEMEX expanded through Latin America, the Caribbean, Asia, Europe, and the United States. It applied its integration process to its own Mexican operations in 1996, identifying $85 million in savings. It also developed branded bagged cement for individual homebuilders and used regional cement trading to balance demand and improve capacity utilization.

Strategic reframing helped CEMEX enter new markets and businesses. Viewing the United States regionally supported the Southdown acquisition, while emphasizing return on investment rather than margins increased the appeal of ready-mix concrete and aggregates. The 2005 acquisition of decentralized, financially weak RMC diversified CEMEX geographically and by product. Despite initial market concern, CEMEX exceeded promised synergy savings within a year. Its 2007 Rinker acquisition posed a different challenge because Rinker already had stronger learning processes and cultural integration.

The cement industry remained highly localized because of transportation costs, despite increasing global consolidation. Cement was more profitable and capital-intensive than ready-mix concrete, while consumption patterns differed between developing markets dominated by bagged cement and developed markets emphasizing bulk purchases, logistics, and timely delivery.

Coppin State University, a historically Black institution in Maryland, has sharply increased enrollment through Expand Eagle Nation, which offers in-state tuition to students from 41 states and territories without an HBCU, plus Washington, D.C. Students from qualifying areas rose from 81 in 2023 to 195 in 2024 and 416 this fall, while total enrollment increased 26 percent.

The university promoted itself through school visits, advertising, community college transfer partnerships and outreach organizations. Officials say the initiative has expanded Coppin’s name recognition locally and nationally and diversified a student body once drawn mainly from within 50 miles.

Coppin prepared for growth by expanding courses and faculty, constructing a dorm and using supported off-campus housing. Its efforts coincide with colleges seeking wider recruitment amid projected demographic declines and increased interest in HBCUs. Affordability is also a factor: Coppin says it is Maryland’s least expensive institution. One challenge has been persuading families that the discounted tuition offer is genuine.

Remote sensing change detection supports urban planning, disaster assessment, surveillance, and resource management. Traditional methods are sensitive to seasonal, lighting, and shadow variations, while deep-learning approaches improve accuracy but face limitations involving long-range context, scarce data, annotation costs, and multimodal fusion.

The proposed Language-Guided Change Detection model, LG-CD, integrates visual and textual information. A pretrained SAM2 encoder extracts hierarchical multi-scale features from bi-temporal images and is fine-tuned using lightweight convolutional adapters. Adapter outputs from both images are concatenated into fused visual features. CLIP encodes natural-language prompts into word-level and global embeddings. The Text Fusion Attention Module uses visual features as queries and word embeddings as key-value pairs in multi-head cross-attention, directing attention toward relevant changing regions. A visual-semantic fusion decoder then combines visual and semantic information through cross-attention to generate change masks.

The approach aims to improve semantic understanding, detection accuracy, robustness, generalization, and adaptability across datasets by exploiting SAM2’s transferable visual representations and contextual guidance from natural language.

The Democratic takeover of Congress and the presidency represents more than partisan victory; it reflects a national demand for reform and restoration. While praising the country’s wealth, enterprise, moral strength, and government, the speaker condemns waste, exploitation, human suffering, resource depletion, and the use of government for private interests.

The proposed reforms include fairer tariffs, banking and currency changes, greater opportunity for labor and capital, conservation of natural resources, improved agriculture and infrastructure, and protections for public health, food safety, and working conditions. Government must uphold justice, equality of opportunity, property, and individual rights while preventing industrial and social forces from harming people.

Reform should proceed carefully, factually, and step by step, restoring rather than destroying the economic system. The occasion is presented not as a partisan triumph but as a dedication to justice and humanity, requiring counsel and support from honest, patriotic, and forward-looking citizens.

The White House said it was not defending Roseanne Barr’s racist tweet, which led ABC to cancel her sitcom. However, Trump and press secretary Sarah Sanders argued ABC owed the administration an apology for derogatory comments about Trump. Sanders cited remarks by several media figures as evidence of a double standard and said Trump was calling out media bias. She also criticized networks for not airing Trump’s remarks about legislation intended to help terminally ill patients access not-yet-fully-approved treatments.

Kyle Shanahan said minicamp practice was balanced, with the offense starting well and the defense responding strongly in the red zone, while both units still had areas to improve. He values input from his father, who informally studies film and offers ideas but is not part of the staff. Shanahan said this support helps as he balances head-coaching and offensive responsibilities. During the upcoming break, he plans to disconnect and spend time with his family. He also emphasized play-action as central to creating explosive plays, easing pressure on quarterbacks and offensive linemen, and keeping defenses honest.

A federal judge dismissed Spencer Elden’s lawsuit alleging that Nirvana’s 1991 album cover constituted child pornography. The judge found that, aside from nudity, the image lacked sexually suggestive or lascivious elements and compared it to a family photo of a nude child bathing.

District and Sessions Judge Nasir Khan Yousafzai sentenced Shehzado to death and fined him Rs. 200,000 for murder. Brothers Ajab Khan and Fateh Khan received 25 years and Rs. 200,000 fines each; Dilbar Khan received 25 years and a Rs. 105,000 fine.

California lawmakers considered competing plans to prevent Southern California Edison’s bankruptcy, including purchasing transmission lines, backing part of its $3.5 billion debt, or imposing monthly ratepayer charges. Consumer and business groups criticized aspects of the proposals.

PG&E sued California for compensation for long-term electricity contracts seized by Gov. Gray Davis in January. The state acknowledged compensation was owed but sought judicial determination of the contracts’ value.

California sold surplus electricity at substantial losses after cooler weather reduced demand, though officials defended prior purchases as protection against shortages. Contra Costa County approved up to $1.7 million in energy-efficiency upgrades for nine buildings. Consumer prices rose 0.2% in June as electricity costs increased while other energy prices declined. Duke Energy reported a 27% quarterly profit increase, driven by trading and wholesale power operations.
Estimating quantum-state moments determines Rényi entropies and supports measures of entanglement, coherence, and randomness certification.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. Devices operate from 4 V to 14 V and generally require external gate drivers.

The EN pin supports direct VLDO connection, external sequencing signals, or resistor-divider-programmed undervoltage lockout. UVLO should be approximately 75% or less of input voltage to ensure reliable startup. An internal 1.23-V reference produces a 0.613-V error-amplifier reference. A 470-nF REFCAP capacitor is required. Output voltage is programmed by a resistor divider, preferably using resistors with 1% or better tolerance. A capacitor on SS controls soft start; synchronous-rectifier outputs activate after SS exceeds 1 V.

Switching frequency can use an internal oscillator, external synchronization, or primary-secondary operation. An RT resistor programs 100-kHz to 2-MHz switching; SYNC outputs twice that frequency. External synchronization requires RT floating and a 200-kHz to 4-MHz clock with 40%–60% duty cycle. Two controllers can synchronize independent converters or operate an interleaved converter, with corresponding outputs shifted by 90° or 270°.

Available primary and synchronous-rectifier outputs vary by device, have approximately 150-mA peak capability, and generally require external drivers. Dead time and leading-edge blanking are programmable on selected devices. Pulse skipping addresses minimum-on-time limitations when COMP is below 0.3 V and the previous duty cycle was below 25%. Depending on device and DCL configuration, maximum duty cycle is 50%, 75%, or 100%.

CS_ILIM provides peak-current PWM control and overcurrent detection. At approximately 1.05 V, cycle-by-cycle limiting begins and the HICC capacitor controls delay and restart timing. External FAULT activation above 0.6 V stops switching; operation restarts after the fault clears and a delay expires. Programmable slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle. Type 2A or Type 2B compensation can be connected at COMP. Thermal shutdown occurs near 175°C, with restart below 160°C.

A 500-kHz synchronous push-pull GaN design example selects a 205-kΩ RT resistor, 5-V feedback divider, approximately 25-ns dead time, 49.9-kΩ blanking resistor, 33-nF soft-start capacitor, 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 0.47-µH output inductor, about 2.3-mF output capacitance, 7.5-Ω current-sense resistor, and 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor.

Layout guidance emphasizes short high-current and switching loops, minimized switch-node area, separated analog and power grounds joined at one point, close bypass and compensation components, protected feedback and current-sense routing, and adequate grounding of CFP backside metallization.

The speaker was surprised and grateful that coach Pat returned him to the lineup after two weeks, and he focused on contributing alongside hardworking teammates. He plans to discuss his future with his family, noting the victory could be a fitting way to leave. He praised the team’s three championships in nine years and its foundation for next season. He credited Pat’s demanding, focused coaching and refusal to allow complacency throughout a difficult season.

Cervical cancer is a malignant disease of the cervix, caused in almost all cases by cancer-causing human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly types 16 and 18. HPV is sexually transmitted, and vaccines can prevent infection with common cancer-associated types.

Precancerous cervical lesions usually have no symptoms but can be detected through Pap smears and treated before becoming invasive. Early cancer may also be symptomless; later signs include bleeding after sex, abnormal vaginal bleeding, foul-smelling discharge, pelvic pain, weakness, anaemia, weight loss, and loss of bladder or bowel control. Confirmation requires a cervical tissue biopsy and histology, while imaging may help determine the stage.

Early-stage cervical cancer can be cured using radical surgery or radiotherapy. Late-stage disease is generally managed with radiotherapy, sometimes combined with chemotherapy, to prolong life rather than cure it. Prognosis depends on the stage, cancer type, and tumour size, with late presentation associated with poor survival.

Nigeria has a high cervical cancer burden because it lacks structured screening programmes. The passage cites about 15,000 diagnoses and 10,000 deaths annually, with cervical cancer ranking behind breast cancer in incidence among Nigerian women and possibly first in cancer deaths.

Regular screening is encouraged, generally every three years during reproductive age and every five years later. Additional risk factors listed include multiple sexual partners, smoking, early sexual contact, and birth-control pill use. Women may become pregnant during early, symptomless disease.

An analysis by Notre Dame law professor Derek Muller found that 92.45% of 2023–2024 campaign contributions from lawyers and staff at 100 top-grossing and 50 larger plaintiffs-side firms went to Democrats, up from a 6-to-1 Democratic advantage in 2017–2020. Contributions totaled about $52 million for Democratic-affiliated groups and $4 million for Republican-affiliated groups. Cleary Gottlieb had the highest Democratic share at 99.7%, while Nelson Mullins had the lowest at 66.4%.

U.S. stock futures rose as strong earnings and rebounding oil prices supported sentiment, though North Korea tensions, France’s election and uncertainty over Trump’s growth agenda limited risk-taking. About 75% of reporting S&P 500 companies beat expectations, with quarterly profits estimated up 10.8%. Qualcomm gained after beating estimates, while eBay fell on weak guidance. Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures rose 0.2%, 0.28% and 0.32%, respectively.

The lecture introduces post-flop poker strategy through example hands. Players should evaluate entire hand ranges rather than specific holdings and generally check to the preflop aggressor, whose range is typically stronger. Post-flop bets should usually serve as either value bets with strong hands or bluffs with weak hands that can make better hands fold; medium-strength hands are often best checked. Typical bet sizes increase from roughly half-pot on the flop toward larger fractions on later streets, while very small bets can unnecessarily enable check-raises.

Continuation betting depends on board texture, opponents, and hand strength. Coordinated flops and multiway pots are poor bluffing situations. When facing bets, players should fold most missed hands and weak or vulnerable draws, especially out of position. Calling is preferable with many medium-strength hands because raising often folds weaker hands while retaining stronger ones. With deep stacks, raising and committing all chips generally requires about two pair or better, though strong one-pair hands may suffice on safer boards. Shallower effective stacks justify committing with weaker holdings. Position, opponent range, board texture, and effective stack size materially affect every decision.

Leading into the preflop aggressor can be appropriate when the flop favors the caller’s range, but balancing leads and checks is difficult, making it an advanced and optional strategy.

The lecture distinguishes direct equity from implied and reverse implied odds. Speculative suited and connected hands can profit from future betting when they make strong hands, while weak, difficult-to-play holdings may be folds despite adequate immediate equity. Set mining relies on deep stacks and winning a large pot after flopping three of a kind, though its effectiveness declines against players capable of folding strong one-pair hands.

Draws are useful both for implied odds and as bluffs. Effective bluffs generally have substantial outs against calling hands, rather than being unsupported attempts with no improvement potential. Bluffing decisions should also consider what strong hands the player can credibly represent. When later cards strengthen the opponent’s likely range, fail to improve the bluffer, or undermine the represented range, abandoning the bluff is appropriate.

Ottawa’s coach said the team is better than it showed in the first two games but must prove it at home. Anaheim outpositioned Ottawa, capitalized on mistakes, controlled faceoffs and loose pucks, and limited offensive pressure through disciplined defense. Ottawa needs fewer turnovers and risky passes, better puck possession, speed, forechecking, faceoff support, and adjustments to Anaheim’s defensive system.

The young goaltender has generally played well and given Ottawa opportunities to win, while the team has barely tested Giguere. Several forwards, including Alfredsson, Jason and Comrie, must return to their earlier playoff form. Anaheim’s Pahlsson line and Rob Niedermayer were praised for their physical play, puck protection and effectiveness. Ottawa plans to use its energetic fourth line more and hopes an emotional home crowd will provide a lift. Chris Neil missed practice because his wife was having a baby.

Artificial intelligence is increasingly influencing higher education, affecting teaching and learning, research, institutional management, and external relationships. The paper examines this influence through document analysis using B-ON and SCILIT, complemented by the authors’ reflexivity as experienced university teachers.

AI-oriented higher education differs from traditional models in its pace of technological adoption, data-based governance, personalized training, and collaborative, traceable research. Applications include adaptive and personalized learning, tutoring, automated grading, predictive analytics, plagiarism detection, translation, virtual assistants, research data analysis, administrative automation, accessibility tools, and virtual reality. These tools may improve accuracy, speed, feedback, student support, resource recommendations, and institutional efficiency while freeing staff for more complex tasks.

Implementation also presents challenges involving equitable access, disability inclusion, bias, privacy, data security, ethics, teacher preparation, student learning styles, costs, organizational resistance, policy transparency, monopolization, and AI’s inability to account fully for emotions or think beyond its programming. AI may also alter teachers’ roles, academic work, student selection, learning locations, and educational programs.

The paper argues that integration should be participatory and institution-wide. Stakeholders need AI literacy to evaluate, communicate with, and use AI critically and effectively. Teachers require competencies in AI-supported learning, research, data analysis, human-resource management, and critical assessment. Higher education must adapt while preserving academic freedom and encouraging discussion, action research, and further investigation into appropriate AI use.

Darren Osborne, 48, received a life sentence with a minimum term of 43 years for murdering Makram Ali and attempting to murder nine others by driving a van into worshippers near Finsbury Park mosques in June 2017. Prosecutors said Osborne had been “brainwashed” into Islamophobia; he also claimed he wanted to kill Sadiq Khan and Jeremy Corbyn. Ali’s family welcomed the guilty verdict and remembered him as peaceful and innocent. Police said Osborne failed to divide communities, highlighting the unity shown across Finsbury Park and the UK.

The appellate court affirmed Washington’s convictions and sentences for second-degree murder and related offenses. His challenges to detective testimony and the jury’s consciousness-of-guilt instruction were unpreserved and meritless because evidence supported an inference that he evaded police. The prosecutor did not change the prosecution’s theory during summation, consistently identifying Washington as the gunman; principal or accomplice status did not affect liability. Because Washington raised no independent challenge to his separate guilty-plea murder conviction, that judgment was also affirmed.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for synchronizing a rotating LIDAR sensor with one or more rolling-shutter cameras to improve sensor fusion. Camera sensing rows are aligned with the LIDAR’s rotation axis and exposed sequentially in an order and timing corresponding to the LIDAR’s beam emission, pointing direction, rotation direction, and speed. Exposure periods may overlap, and camera fields of view may overlap to reduce temporal or spatial misalignment.

A controller coordinates LIDAR rotation, pulse emission, camera exposure, and pixel readout so image pixels can be associated with LIDAR data collected at similar times and viewing directions. Cameras may be arranged in a ring or use a curved image sensor around the rotation axis. The synchronized data can combine camera information, such as color, with LIDAR information, such as distance, depth, texture, or reflectivity, to generate representations including colored three-dimensional point clouds. The concepts may also apply to other active and passive sensors, including RADAR, SONAR, microphones, and environmental sensors.

Quantbot Technologies increased its Zoe’s Kitchen stake by 114.5% in the second quarter to 17,056 shares valued at $203,000. Several other institutional investors also raised or acquired holdings. Director A. Alexander Taylor II purchased 3,100 shares for $39,897, while insiders owned 3% of the company.

Analysts gave Zoe’s Kitchen a consensus “Hold” rating and a $17.55 target price, with two sell, seven hold and three buy ratings. Shares opened at $12.39, compared with a 12-month range of $10.77 to $27.41, and the company’s market capitalization was $242.04 million.

Quarterly earnings were $0.06 per share, exceeding the $0.02 consensus estimate. Revenue rose 12.1% year over year to $74.30 million but missed estimates of $75.11 million. The company reported a negative 0.07% net margin and negative 0.27% return on equity. Analysts projected annual earnings of negative $0.09 per share.

Major hedge funds reduced healthcare holdings in the second quarter despite the sector’s 6.7 percent gain, amid fading Republican efforts to replace the Affordable Care Act. Jana Partners exited nine healthcare companies, while Third Point cut stakes in Humana and Baxter. Hedge funds overall gained 1 percent, trailing first-quarter returns. As energy stocks fell 7 percent with oil prices, Third Point, Jana Partners and Omega Advisors exited multiple energy positions. Regulatory filings reveal trades with a 45-day delay and may not reflect current holdings.
Facebook is rolling out Trending News on iOS and Android, ranking widely shared stories and offering headlines, videos, photos, and related posts from multiple sources through the Explore tab.

The lecture examines discrete symmetries and fermionic path integrals. In quantum mechanics, parity and charge conjugation are implemented by unitary operators, while time reversal must be anti-unitary. Its anti-linearity sends \(i\) to \(-i\), allowing a time-reversed wavefunction to satisfy the Schrödinger equation with reversed time.

For a complex scalar field, parity and time reversal reverse spatial momentum, while charge conjugation exchanges particles and antiparticles. Discrete transformations may include phases constrained by applying the transformation twice; for parity, the phase is \(\pm1\), distinguishing scalars from pseudoscalars.

For Dirac fields, discrete transformations also act on spinor components through matrices. Parity invariance requires a matrix commuting with \(\gamma^0\) and anticommuting with spatial \(\gamma^i\), so it is proportional to \(\gamma^0\). Charge conjugation uses a matrix \(C\) relating \(-\gamma^{\mu T}\) to \(\gamma^\mu\); its existence follows from the equivalence of gamma-matrix representations. The time-reversal spinor matrix is similarly related to \(C\) and \(\gamma^5\). Parity and time reversal are independent discrete transformations, not connected by Lorentz boosts.

The lecture then introduces fermionic path integrals. Because fermionic fields obey anticommutation relations, their classical path-integral analogues are Grassmann variables, which anticommute and square to zero. Functions of one Grassmann variable contain only constant and linear terms; functions of several variables terminate after each variable appears once. Left and right differentiation can differ by signs.

Grassmann integration is defined by linearity, vanishing integrals of total derivatives, \(\int d\theta=0\), and the normalization \(\int d\theta\,\theta=1\). Consequently, integration over one Grassmann variable equals differentiation. Grassmann differentials anticommute with other Grassmann variables, and under \(\theta'=a\theta\), the measure transforms as \(d\theta'=a^{-1}d\theta\), opposite to ordinary-variable integration.

A modified Google Camera app enables HDR+ on certain Snapdragon-powered Android phones. Amazon is refunding questionable solar-eclipse glasses. HBO refuses hackers’ ransom demands despite further leaks, including unreleased “Curb Your Enthusiasm” episodes. Waymo patented technology that softens vehicle exteriors during imminent pedestrian collisions, though it remains only a patent.

The invention concerns a coil-less atomizer for electronic cigarettes using one or more electrically conductive woven fiber tubes as both heating and liquid-wicking elements. Each tube has a hollow interior and porous walls that transport liquid from a reservoir to a higher-resistance heating section through capillary action. Tubes may be C-, L-, or U-shaped, use materials such as carbon fiber, metals, ceramics, polymers, or composites, and have conductive coatings or selectively modified resistance.

Electrical power is supplied through leads or surface contacts. The heating section, typically positioned between lower-resistance conductive sections, heats and vaporizes transported liquid when activated by control electronics responding to an airflow sensor or manual switch. Air passes around the heating section and carries the resulting aerosol to the mouthpiece.

Multiple tubes may be parallel, touching, or have different diameters to improve liquid flow, supply additional liquid, or provide staged aerosol production. Tube sections may also vary in diameter, including a larger central heating section designed to limit overfilling. Liquid reservoirs may hold free-flowing liquid, liquid stored in porous material, or both.

A manufacturing method mounts woven fiber tubes on a support board, masks the intended heating section, and applies a conductive material to exposed portions to lower their resistance. The resulting atomizer can be compact, wickless, mass-produced at low cost, and manufactured with controlled electrical resistance. Embodiments include disposable, rechargeable, refillable, and replaceable cartridge-based electronic smoking devices.

Oliver Stone’s *Wall Street*, released shortly after the 1987 market crash, remains a defining film about finance because it combines a rags-to-riches story, the Hero’s Journey, and a cautionary fairy tale. Bud Fox rises from low-level broker to wealth and status through Gordon Gekko, reflecting fantasies of effortless success. The film also serves as a vivid time capsule of 1980s Wall Street culture, marked by excess, corporate raiders, fashion, and technology. Its greatest strength is Michael Douglas’s Oscar-winning portrayal of Gekko, a charismatic embodiment of financial ambition and greed who became an enduring cultural icon and career inspiration for some finance professionals. Memorable phrases such as “Greed is good,” together with the film’s moral complexity and period detail, have sustained its influence and reputation.

Apple’s August 17, 2022 Form 8-K reports approval of an Executive Cash Incentive Plan for designated executives and employees. Cash awards depend on performance goals and periods established and evaluated by the Board’s Compensation Committee; awards generally are forfeited if employment ends before payout unless the Committee decides otherwise.

Apple also adopted amended bylaws effective August 17. Changes address notice requirements for Board meetings, shareholder director nominations and proposals, proxy solicitations, shareholder meetings and written consents, emergency Board procedures, and related disclosure requirements. The filing includes the amended bylaws and incentive plan as exhibits.

Access Cardiosystems and its investors sued founder Randall Fincke for securities violations, fiduciary breaches, and related claims. Earlier rulings established that Access owned the disputed intellectual property, Fincke breached fiduciary duties, and he violated Massachusetts securities law by falsely stating in an October 2002 Business Plan that patent counsel had advised that Access’s product infringed no known patents.

The court denied Fincke’s motion to reconsider, finding that patent counsel had provided no such advice, formal or informal, and that the statement was objectively false and material.

To recover under Massachusetts General Laws ch. 110A, § 410(a)(2), the investors had to link particular securities sales to the misstatement. The court found their testimony that every later investment relied on the Business Plan not credible. It concluded that only Joseph Zimmel’s October and November 2002 stock purchases, totaling $1.5 million, were made “by means of” the Business Plan. April 2003 investments arose from a new company document, negotiations, financial needs, and governance changes; later advances were not shown to involve securities sales connected to the misstatement.

The court awarded Zimmel $1.5 million plus six percent interest from May 25, 2007, and costs. It also awarded Access $281,534.62 for Fincke’s fiduciary breaches, plus twelve percent interest from July 6, 2004, and costs. Federal postjudgment interest applies to both awards.

Amazon.com’s 2016 Form 10-K describes operations across North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS), serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators. Amazon emphasizes customer focus, invention, operational excellence, and long-term thinking. Its offerings include retail marketplaces, Prime, electronic devices, digital content, fulfillment, advertising, publishing, and cloud computing. At year-end 2016, Amazon employed approximately 341,400 people.

Net sales increased 27% to $135.99 billion in 2016, comprising $79.79 billion from North America, $43.98 billion from International, and $12.22 billion from AWS. Operating income rose to $4.19 billion, with North America and AWS generating $2.36 billion and $3.11 billion, respectively, while International recorded a $1.28 billion loss. Net income was $2.37 billion, diluted earnings per share were $4.90, and operating cash flow reached $16.44 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $26.0 billion. Amazon had 477.2 million shares outstanding as of January 25, 2017, and had never paid cash dividends.

Amazon identifies major risks involving intense competition, rapid expansion, new products and markets, fluctuating results, international regulation, fulfillment and data-center operations, seasonality, acquisitions, foreign exchange, cybersecurity, system interruptions, inventory, intellectual property, taxation, supplier relationships, government contracts, product liability, payments, and seller misconduct. The company operated approximately 172.2 million leased square feet and 7.2 million owned square feet of facilities at year-end 2016.

The Ohio Supreme Court upheld R.C. 3105.03’s requirement that divorce plaintiffs reside in Ohio for at least one year before filing. Although durational residency laws may require strict equal-protection review when they penalize interstate travel, the court held that delaying access to divorce does not impose the same penalty as denying welfare or voting rights. Divorce was characterized as neither a basic necessity nor, under the facts, an urgent need.

The court found that Ohio has a compelling interest in regulating marriage and divorce for its residents and preventing nonresidents from using its divorce laws. Because domicile depends partly on a person’s subjective intent to make Ohio a permanent home, the one-year period was deemed the least restrictive practical means of establishing genuine residency. The requirement also permits time for reconsideration and possible reconciliation, does not prevent migration into Ohio, and exempts alimony-only actions addressing immediate support needs.

The constitutional issue was not moot despite the appellant’s later satisfaction of the residency period because dismissing could create difficulties in regaining jurisdiction over the appellee. The judgment was affirmed. Justice Schneider concurred based on the case’s particular facts but stated that reconsideration might be appropriate where grounds for divorce arise after a spouse establishes Ohio residence.

Evelyn Montiel balanced high school success with long hours supporting her family’s East Oakland ice cream business. Determined to become her family’s first college graduate, she initially attended an East Coast college but dropped out after depression and a difficult start. Students Rising Above helped her transfer to the University of Southern California, secure internships, and prepare for work. After graduating during the recession, she returned to the family business because of limited job opportunities. SRA later connected her with an investment firm interview that launched her finance career. She now works as a broker at a Silicon Valley startup while remaining closely connected to her family, business, and East Oakland community.

The BIRDS workshop aims to connect digital library and GLAM professionals, who possess domain knowledge but may lack technical resources, with computational researchers who may be unfamiliar with practical library challenges. It seeks to foster collaborations that develop innovative, effective access systems while respecting constraints such as limited computing capacity and restrictions on external services.

Designed as an interactive, in-person, full-day event at TPDL, the workshop requires no paper submissions. Its program includes introductions, a keynote presenting successful practitioner-researcher collaboration, scientific speed-dating, a diverse panel, guided breakout discussions, and closing summaries. Discussion topics may include large language models, OCR, interface evaluation, and novel access paths.

The workshop’s goals include identifying shared challenges, exploring computational solutions, providing a forum for early ideas and ongoing work, establishing a recurring workshop series, and producing a SIGIR Forum report. It targets practitioners, researchers, students, and library representatives, with approximately 25 participants expected. Organisers Christin Katharina Kreutz and Hermann Kroll bring experience in information access, user behaviour, digital libraries, workshop organisation, and collaborations with library institutions.

Retired Justice Anthony Kennedy’s memoir reflects on judicial humility, integrity, and the possibility of error. He rejects both strict originalism and pragmatism as insufficient, arguing that constitutional interpretation can improve without changing the Constitution. Kennedy discusses major cases involving campaign finance, same-sex marriage, presidential elections, flag burning, and abortion, emphasizing legal reasoning over personal or political preferences. He recounts Antonin Scalia’s eventual apology for the personal tone of his same-sex marriage dissent and rejects the label “swing justice,” saying cases, not he, shifted.

Kennedy also argues that presidents should defer properly to Supreme Court rulings and opposes courtroom cameras because they could distort arguments. He describes a chilling conversation with Vladimir Putin about capital punishment, the vandalism of his family home after he declined to lower a Manson family member’s bail, and his view that his children’s rock music was avant-garde and excessively loud.

The Simons Observatory uses over 67,000 transition-edge sensor detectors, including nearly 31,000 on its large-aperture telescope (LAT), read out through SMuRF microwave frequency multiplexing. The LAT’s room-temperature electronics and coaxial transmission lines are exposed to diurnal temperature changes that can alter cable properties and produce phase drifts resembling detector signals.

Researchers measured this effect using off-resonance pilot tones that pass through the readout system without interacting with microwave resonators. Data from 290 tones over 22.6 hours showed phase-delay changes correlated with ambient temperature but limited to a few picoseconds per daily cycle. An analytical conversion based on resonator calibration and measured SQUID response translated these drifts into inferred detector noise-equivalent currents.

During a representative 40-minute telescope scan, the calculated phase-drift noise was smaller than overall on-sky detector noise and remained within the readout noise budget. The study concludes that temperature-induced phase drift in the LAT’s warm RF cables is not expected to significantly affect detector performance or telescope mapping speed.

VentureWire’s September 26, 2000 issue reports extensive venture financing, product launches, acquisitions, appointments and fund developments. Major deals include Chiaro Networks raising over $100 million, Novalux securing $109 million, Nexsi and Netigy each raising $75 million, and Predictive Networks obtaining $45 million. Sun Microsystems launched a $50 million Asia-Pacific investment program expected to support $250 million in co-investments. Bertelsmann and iSyndicate formed an equally owned European content-syndication venture, while online jewelry retailer Miadora shut down. Other developments include three acquisitions, several board and executive appointments, Venturelab Partners’ $100 million second fund, and Net Value Holdings’ renaming as Stonepath Group. Corrections clarified Sharing Technologies’ $15 million financing sources and epipeline.com’s investors.

The Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian describes electron–photon interactions that modify molecular electronic structure in optical cavities. Sinc functions provide an orthonormal, systematically improvable real-space basis suited to nonlocal coupling. Although direct two-electron integrals scale as O(N⁴), rapidly decaying off-diagonal elements permit sparse or low-rank approximations.

The Wham play resembles Trap, but a tight end or fullback pulls to kick out a defensive lineman instead of a guard. It creates quick, unexpected blocking angles and serves as a complementary change-up. However, it is complex and time-consuming to install, requiring coordinated front identification and a sufficiently powerful blocker. Teams often use specific formations to produce predictable defensive fronts.

Against 3-4 Odd and 4-3 Even fronts, linemen secure gaps, double-team interior defenders, and climb to linebackers while the tight end blocks the edge. The fullback identifies and kicks out the first defensive lineman outside the center. The tailback runs inside the kickout block behind a second-level block, while receivers account for safeties and cornerbacks.

Variations include a Gun H-Back Wham RPO, where the fullback blocks the nose tackle and the quarterback may throw a slant or bubble, and Shotgun Influence Wham, which uses a pulling guard to influence a defensive tackle before the fullback traps him.

The DAWN-PLASMA study was a multicenter, randomized, open-label phase 2 trial comparing standard care plus high-titer convalescent plasma with standard care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Participants were allocated 2:1; the plasma group received four units totaling 800–1,000 mL, generally beginning within 12 hours of randomization. The primary endpoint was survival without mechanical ventilation at Day 15.

Between May 2020 and January 2021, 489 patients were randomized; the Full Analysis Set comprised 320 plasma recipients and 163 controls. Survival without mechanical ventilation at Day 15 was similar between groups: 83.7% with plasma and 84.1% with standard care (odds ratio 0.99; p=0.976). No statistically significant differences were found in mortality or other secondary outcomes at Days 15 or 30.

Adverse events occurred in 28.13% of the plasma group and 30.06% of controls. Serious and fatal adverse-event rates were also similar. Treatment-related events occurred in 12 plasma recipients, including seven serious events. Transfusion-related effects were reported in 19 plasma recipients, with no reported transfusion-related acute lung injury. Laboratory measures and vital signs showed no meaningful between-group differences.

Neutralizing-antibody titers increased by Day 6, but the intervention did not influence this increase. Higher baseline and Day 6 titers correlated with better outcomes. Overall, early administration of high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not alter the clinical course of hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

Santa Barbara County sheriff’s detectives are investigating a Tuesday robbery at Summerland Antique Collective. A man threatened and duct-taped two female employees, stole cash and merchandise, and fled. The employees were found after about 20 minutes and had no apparent serious injuries.

Using nationally representative 2009–2020 NHANES data, researchers examined empirical dietary patterns among 32,498 US adults and their associations with cardiovascular disease (CVD), socioeconomic vulnerability, and Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) participation. Principal components analysis identified four patterns: American; Prudent; Legume; and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy. The American pattern was most common and had the lowest Healthy Eating Index score, while Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy had the highest.

After adjustment for demographic factors, adults with CVD were more likely than those without CVD to follow the American pattern. Greater socioeconomic vulnerability was associated with greater alignment with American and Legume patterns and lower alignment with Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy patterns. SNAP participants were more likely to follow the American pattern and less likely to follow the Prudent pattern than income-eligible non-participants and SNAP-ineligible adults. Some associations varied by race and ethnicity, although CVD-related associations did not.

The findings were generally unchanged in sensitivity analyses. Limitations included the cross-sectional design, reliance on self-reported conditions and social factors, and dietary assessment based on up to two 24-hour recalls. The study concludes that nutrition initiatives for people with or at risk for CVD should account for naturally occurring dietary patterns and socioeconomic differences.

Iqaluit-Tasiluk MLA George Hickes said Nunavut civil servants have the right to speak with MLAs and should not face intimidation or retaliation from senior government managers. Hepatitis C virus (HCV) can cause cirrhosis, liver cancer, morbidity, and mortality. The study evaluated household HCV transmission, associated risk factors, and awareness among household members of HCV-positive patients attending CUSP in Huye District, Rwanda.

Using a descriptive cross-sectional design, participants were screened with an HCV antibody rapid test, with reactive results confirmed by ELISA. Questionnaires assessed risk factors and awareness. Although the planned sample was 180, 148 participants from 30 families were tested. Data were analyzed using Excel and SPSS.

Sixteen participants tested positive, giving an HCV prevalence of 10.8%. HCV positivity was significantly associated with HBV history, HIV history, and unprotected sex. Blood transfusion showed no significant association. Awareness was low: 139 participants gave incorrect answers about HCV transmission, but awareness was not significantly associated with test results.

The study recommends early screening of household members, follow-up and treatment of HCV-positive patients, and education about transmission and risk factors. Its cross-sectional design could not establish whether infections originated within households. Phylogenetic and nationwide studies were recommended to clarify transmission origins and broaden assessment.

The passage introduces Construction Defining Functionality (CDF), a framework for analyzing computational problems through three structural spaces: syntactic definitions, semantic configurations, and logical outcomes. These are connected by mappings from syntax to semantics, semantics to logic, and syntax directly to logic. CDF distinguishes generative internal structure from observable behavior and evaluates whether these mappings are stable and compositionally coherent.

A mapping is stable when output complexity grows polynomially relative to input complexity and explosive when growth exceeds polynomial bounds. A CDF structure is compositionally coherent when the direct syntax-to-logic mapping equals the composition of the syntax-to-semantics and semantics-to-logic mappings. The framework classifies structures as ComCDF when coherent and stable, ExpCDF when incoherent or unstable, and Semi-ExpCDF in intermediate cases.

CDF formally represents a function using its iterative syntactic orbit, input-output relations, and proof or computation trees. Linear and fixed-input recursive functions illustrate stable mappings, while variable inputs may produce increasingly complex structures. The passage compares such instability to expanding search spaces in NP problems.

The framework contrasts 2SAT and 3SAT. It characterizes 2SAT clauses as reducible to local binary implications, enabling implication-graph methods, compositional reasoning, and polynomial-time solution. It characterizes 3SAT clauses as involving non-local ternary dependencies that cannot be reduced to binary implications. According to the passage, these dependencies cause exponential growth in semantic configurations, unstable logical reasoning, and computational intractability. It concludes that 3SAT’s semantic explosion arises intrinsically from its clause-level syntax and claims that polynomial stabilization would require changing the problem’s structural identity.

An open-label randomized trial in western Cambodia compared 14-day primaquine regimens totaling 3.5 mg/kg and 7.0 mg/kg for preventing Plasmodium vivax recurrence. All participants received seven days of artesunate and were relocated to a malaria-free area for 90 days. Among 156 allocated patients, 119 with normal G6PD activity were randomized to low-dose primaquine, high-dose primaquine, or no primaquine; 37 G6PD-deficient patients received no primaquine.

By day 90, recurrence occurred in 81.4% of patients receiving no primaquine, 24.4% receiving 3.5 mg/kg, and 4.7% receiving 7.0 mg/kg. High-dose primaquine had a significantly lower recurrence risk than low-dose treatment, with a hazard ratio of 0.17. Its advantage remained evident through day 180.

Both primaquine regimens were well tolerated in G6PD-normal patients, with no serious adverse events or severe anaemia. Increased methaemoglobin was more frequent with high-dose treatment but was clinically silent and resolved after treatment. Limitations included the small, below-target sample, single-centre open-label design, controlled treatment conditions, and inability to distinguish relapses from recrudescence definitively. The study supports recommending 7.0 mg/kg primaquine for G6PD-normal patients with P. vivax infections acquired in Cambodia and potentially elsewhere in Southeast Asia.

A 2,100-year-old chalk bowl fragment engraved with the Hebrew name “Hyrcanus” was discovered in 2015 beneath Jerusalem’s Givati parking lot, near an ancient mikvah complex and the Akra fortress. The holiday effect is a stock-market calendar anomaly involving returns around non-weekend market holidays. Proposed causes include lower liquidity, holiday optimism, limited macroeconomic news, and pre-holiday risk reduction. S&P 500 backtests found the strongest tradeable effects around Independence Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas, while Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Presidents’ Day, Memorial Day, and Labor Day showed weak or absent effects. Retail stocks also performed strongly around Thanksgiving.

Post-holiday SPY tests from 1993 examined holding periods of one to five days. Holding over holidays produced no gains, but the second day afterward performed better. A strategy combining holiday timing with another variable generated 100 trades, a 0.56% average gain, 71% win rate, profit factor of 4, and 3.5% annual return while invested 1% of the time. Holiday effects are generally small and not guaranteed, but may supplement other trading strategies.

Bollinger Bands are a volatility indicator created by John Bollinger, typically comprising a 20-period simple moving average and upper and lower bands set two standard deviations away. Widening bands indicate rising volatility, while contracting bands signal low volatility and possible consolidation. Prices near the upper or lower bands may indicate overbought or oversold conditions, though band breaches can also signal trend continuation.

Trading approaches include squeezes, breakouts, %B, band walks, bounces, double or triple bands, bandwidth analysis, RSI divergence, reversals, and volatility contraction. Settings can be adjusted by changing the moving-average period, standard deviations, or average type. Shorter periods generate more signals and false positives; longer periods reduce noise.

Bollinger Bands should be combined with price analysis and indicators such as RSI, MACD, or stochastic oscillators. Risk controls include confirmation, stop-loss orders, position sizing, and diversification. Limitations include delayed or false signals, equal weighting of old and recent data in the SMA, and an inability to predict extreme market events.

Tests described found some profitability in mean-reverting stocks and promise for gold breakouts, but no useful strategies for stock indices. Results vary by asset, timeframe, and settings; no single configuration or companion indicator works best across all markets.

A report by economists Lucas Chancel and Thomas Piketty finds that Indian income inequality rose rapidly from the 1980s. The top 1% income share fell from under 21% in the late 1930s to 6% in the early 1980s, then climbed to 22%, its highest level since 1922. Inequality declined under strong regulation and progressive taxation from the 1950s to 1970s but reversed with pro-business policies. Since liberalisation, growth has disproportionately benefited the top 10%, particularly the top 1%, rather than the middle 40%.

Amazon is developing an AI chip to improve Alexa amid strong Echo sales, high-profile advertising and planned integrations. Other reports cover CES devices, speaker price wars, Apple delays and an Alexa malfunction that played loud music overnight.

Daily water intake is given as 6–8 glasses, or 1.2 liters, with some obtained from food. Drinking excessive amounts quickly can dilute blood salt, causing lethargy, light-headedness and, rarely, death; drinking according to thirst is advised. A 12-week study of 48 adults aged 55–75 found that participants drinking two cups before meals lost 15.5 pounds on average, compared with 11 pounds for others. Replacing sugary, high-calorie drinks with water may also support weight management.
