Teams should prepare for defensive, even, and offensive jump balls. In defensive situations, players should anticipate the opposing jumper’s direction, rotate early, deny passes, box out, maintain contact, and protect the basket. Defensive, diamond, and “Y” alignments provide varying levels of backcourt protection, with the “Y” using two defenders back against a superior jumper.

Even jump balls require inside position, coordinated clockwise or counterclockwise rotations, and predetermined signals. Success depends on anticipation, aggressiveness, and determination.

With a height advantage of at least six inches, teams can use set offensive plays while preserving defensive balance. Players generally tip toward the tallest teammate, then transition into a set or motion offense if no immediate shot develops. Offensive options include Possession, Double Tap, Post Split, Jumper Fly, Forward Fly, Spread, Tandem, and Loop, using tips, screens, cuts, passes, and drives to create scoring opportunities.

AMD’s SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block specification may be reviewed only to design products interfacing with AMD products or to provide feedback. AMD retains all intellectual-property rights, prohibits copying or redistribution, provides the specification “as is,” disclaims warranties and liability, restricts safety-critical uses, may freely use voluntary feedback, and requires export-law compliance. California law governs disputes, which must be heard in Santa Clara County.

The specification standardizes communication between hypervisors and guests using Secure Encrypted Virtualization–Encrypted State (SEV-ES) or Secure Nested Paging (SEV-SNP). These features encrypt guest register state and classify VM exits as Automatic Exits, which expose no guest register state, or Non-Automatic Exits, for which guests selectively share state through the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB).

The GHCB is a 4 KB decrypted, shared page whose layout partly mirrors the SEV-ES VMCB save-state area. Guests expose only state required for a VMGEXIT. Protocol version 2 adds SEV-SNP support and hypervisor feature advertisement. Later revisions add 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, VLEK support, APIC ID retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, page-state changes, an EFI confidential-computing blob protocol, SEV trusted I/O, Secure AVIC, revised error reporting, and GHCB unregistration.

The GHCB MSR protocol supports version negotiation, encryption-bit discovery, pre-GHCB CPUID requests, AP reset hold, GHCB address registration, page-state changes, VMPL switching, feature queries, unregistration, and termination. SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB guest physical address before first use; registration replaces any previous address, and optional unregistration reports success, absence, or failure.

For Non-Automatic Exits, guests handle a #VC exception, place required state in the GHCB, mark valid fields in VALID_BITMAP, and invoke VMGEXIT. Hypervisors process the request, return state or errors, and resume the guest. Interrupts and preemption should be disabled while accessing the GHCB, with separate or preserved GHCB state recommended for NMI contexts.

Defined operations include I/O and MSR handling, hypercalls, MMIO access through decrypted buffers, private/shared page-state transitions, SNP guest and extended certificate requests, AP creation, restricted-injection doorbells, IPIs and timers, APIC ID lists, VMPL switching, SEV-TIO requests, Secure AVIC backing-page registration, and guest termination. Guest-request interfaces use shared pages, and rate limiting is recommended to prevent excessive synchronous SNP firmware requests.

SMP booting requires alternatives to hypervisor modification of encrypted AP register state. SEV-ES can use reset vectors, AP reset hold, and AP jump tables. SEV-SNP can use guest-created VMSA pages through the AP Creation event, enabling vCPU hotplug. Restricted Injection requires AP Creation and uses shared #HV doorbell pages for host notifications.

The specification defines NMI completion signaling, hardware-debug virtualization behavior, and restricted-injection doorbell data modeled on APIC behavior. System Management Mode is unsupported in this version, and nested virtualization is unsupported under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP.

Merck CEO Ken Frazier resigned from Trump’s American Manufacturing Council to oppose intolerance and extremism after the Charlottesville white supremacist rally. Trump criticized Frazier over drug prices before explicitly denouncing neo-Nazis and the KKK. The study introduces Doublethink, a Bayesian model-averaging method for identifying direct non-genetic risk factors in high-dimensional biobank data. It converts model-averaged posterior odds into asymptotically valid adjusted p-values, enabling simultaneous control of Bayesian false discovery rate and frequentist familywise error rate. It also permits post-hoc testing of arbitrary variable groups without inflating these error rates.

Doublethink was applied to COVID-19 hospitalization in UK Biobank using logistic regression and Markov chain Monte Carlo. The analysis included 1,917 cases, 200,000 down-sampled controls, and 1,912 pre-2020 variables. At posterior-odds and adjusted-p-value thresholds of 10 and 10−3.3, respectively, nine individual variables were significant. These included unspecified dementia, acute lower respiratory infection, tendency to fall, carer support, number of treatments or medications, and history of psychoactive substance abuse. Educational qualifications showed protective direct effects.

Grouping correlated variables recovered signals diluted at the individual-variable level. Significant predefined groups included age, sex, deprivation, and physical or occupational therapy. Post-hoc groups identified signals related to obesity, deprivation, kidney disease, ethnicity and pollution, and poor physical health. The analysis supported direct effects for established categories including age, sex, obesity, socioeconomic status, smoking, lung disease, alcohol intake, general comorbidity, kidney disease, and educational attainment. It found no significant direct effects for diabetes, cardiovascular disease, or hypertension, though indirect effects were not excluded. Psychiatric disorders, infection, dementia, and aging showed strong evidence despite receiving relatively limited attention in 127 reviewed UK Biobank COVID-19 studies.

The method evaluates direct rather than total effects, so results cannot predict intervention effects and depend on the included variables, data preparation, and prior assumptions. Additional limitations include possible selection bias, unmeasured confounding, measurement error, large-sample approximations, and substantial computational demands: the analysis required approximately 3,500 CPU hours. Interactions, nonlinear effects, rare variables, and some exposures could not be investigated. The authors conclude that Doublethink offers a systematic exposome-wide framework for model-averaged discovery while linking Bayesian and frequentist hypothesis testing.

A public inquiry into the Grenfell Tower fire, which killed 72 people, began with personal tributes from survivors and victims’ relatives. Inquiry chairman Martin Moore-Bick said understanding the victims and their families’ suffering should precede examination of building materials, regulations and fire spread.

Ahmed Elgwahry described hearing his mother and sister die by phone. Other relatives recounted seeing evidence of victims’ terror, losing children during the evacuation and suffering pregnancy loss after the fire. Their testimonies emphasized demands for accountability and answers.

Criticism focused on the local council’s failure to heed safety warnings, the building manager’s installation of flammable insulation and cladding, officials’ failure to implement earlier safety recommendations, and fire authorities’ instructions for residents to remain in their apartments. Families argued these failures, along with inequalities between rich and poor, contributed to the disaster.

The global industrial hybrid stepper motors market is forecast to exceed $1 billion in revenue by 2022. Growth is driven by rising demand for automated industrial equipment, while competition from servo and conventional stepper motors remains a challenge. Trends include miniaturization, robotic design advances, and IoT-enabled motors. Key vendors include AMETEK, MinebeaMitsumi, Moons’, Nidec, and Schneider Electric.

Software patterns evolved from Knuth’s general-purpose algorithms through object-oriented design patterns and reusable open source components. For distributed systems, patterns provide reusable blueprints, shared terminology, accumulated experience, and common components that improve reliability and development efficiency.

Containers establish boundaries for resources, ownership, and concerns. Multiple containers on one node can share resources as a tightly grouped pod. Three principal single-node patterns are described:

- **Sidecar:** A secondary container augments an application container. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service, synchronizing configuration, monitoring processes, and updating application code from Git. Effective sidecars should be parameterized, expose stable APIs, and include clear documentation and metadata.
- **Ambassador:** A container brokers communication between an application and external services. It can route requests to storage shards, discover services across environments, or split traffic for experiments while keeping routing logic separate from application code.
- **Adapter:** A container transforms an application’s interface into a standard one. Examples include exporting Redis metrics to Prometheus, normalizing logs with Fluentd, and providing richer database health checks.

Multi-node microservice architectures divide applications into independently maintained services connected through formal APIs. They support team autonomy, independent scaling, and agility, but make architecture and debugging more difficult. Distributed patterns help standardize these systems.

Replicated, load-balanced services use interchangeable instances for availability and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching unprepared instances, while session tracking can consistently route users to particular replicas. Additional replicated layers may provide caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination.

Sharded services divide state among replicas, with routing logic directing each request to the appropriate shard. Sharding increases storage capacity and cache utilization but makes failures more consequential because requests mapped to a failed shard miss the cache. Replicating each shard improves resilience, supports scaling, and reduces disruption during failures or upgrades.

A 2017 survey of 462 people found 79 per cent rated Regina Police Service quality very good to excellent and over 80 per cent viewed it as honest. Nearly 25 per cent, particularly Indigenous respondents, considered it ethnically insensitive.

Dividend yields above 6% can indicate cut risk, but the passage assesses two stocks yielding a forecast 7.1%. Taylor Wimpey plans a £450m total dividend for 2017, supported by £511.6m of 2016 free cash flow and strong housing demand. SpaceX will launch an unmanned Dragon cargo spacecraft from Kennedy Space Center at 12:31 p.m. ET, delivering 6,400 pounds of supplies to the ISS. The first stage is expected to land for reuse. This is NASA’s final mission using a brand-new Dragon before switching to flight-proven craft.

Diffusion models and flow matching are special cases of learning stochastic dynamics between distributions. The Schrödinger bridge problem seeks a stochastic process connecting two distributions while minimizing KL divergence from a reference process. Iterative proportional fitting (IPF) solves this by alternating forward and reverse half-bridge updates, but existing variants require samples from both endpoint distributions.

The authors extend IPF to settings where one or both endpoints are specified only by unnormalised densities or energy functions. Their method uses off-policy reinforcement-learning losses and stabilization techniques from diffusion samplers. It reportedly learns low-cost data-to-energy and energy-to-energy bridges comparable to oracle data-to-data IPF, improves data-to-data IPF by learning both drift and diffusion coefficients, and enables scalable, data-free image-to-image translation by transporting generative-model priors to latent-space posteriors.

Formally, a Schrödinger bridge minimizes process-level KL divergence to a reference process subject to prescribed initial and final marginals. For an Itô SDE reference, the solution is also an SDE with the same diffusion coefficient, reducing inference to optimizing its drift. As diffusion vanishes, the problem approaches dynamic optimal transport with squared-Euclidean cost; with positive diffusion, its endpoint coupling is entropy-regularized optimal transport.

Overnight trading buys at the close and sells at the next open or close, seeking short-term stock-market edges. SPY backtests since 1993 found potential edges in Turnaround Tuesday, holidays, month-end, weekday patterns, mean reversion, options expiration, breakouts, and gaps. Reported strategies generally produced average gains of 0.2%–0.55% per trade, with win rates around 57%–70%. A combined portfolio also performed well, including out of sample from 2018, though backtests remain approximations.

Effective portfolios combine numerous uncorrelated strategies across asset classes, time frames, and approaches such as mean reversion, trend following, momentum, seasonality, and short strategies. Avoiding overlapping signals and severe drawdowns can improve compounding and risk-adjusted returns. Short strategies may reduce portfolio risk even when weak independently, but short selling and low-win-rate trend following are difficult. Practical drawbacks include executing trades at the close, often requiring automated or mechanical trading.

Baseline out-of-bounds defense differs from standard half-court defense because the ball begins behind the defense and offensive players often cut directly toward the basket. The defense has a temporary 5-on-4 advantage but must prevent quick lobs, cuts, screens, and overloads.

Four defensive approaches are presented:

1. **Jam:** Initially protect the middle, then aggressively smother opponents without switching, deny lane cuts, disrupt screens, pressure the inbounder after three counts, and match up once the ball enters play.
2. **Jump Switch:** Aggressively switch screens and deny passing lanes and rolls to the basket. This option is especially useful with fewer than five seconds remaining.
3. **Trap:** After protecting the basket and pressuring the inbounder, follow the inbound pass and double-team the receiver while other defenders assume helpside positions and rotate on subsequent passes.
4. **Combination defenses:** Use Box-and-One, Diamond-and-One, or Triangle-and-Two alignments to deny selected players while maintaining zone coverage. The alignment depends on whether the offense uses a one- or two-guard front.

All methods emphasize alertness, middle protection, pass denial, aggressive pressure, proper rotations, and preventing second-chance shots.

This multicentre study examined the molecular features of chronic neuropathic pain using excised Morton’s neuroma tissue from 22 adults and unaffected nerve tissue from 11 controls. Clinical pain phenotyping was combined with bulk RNA sequencing, gene-expression analyses, cell-type deconvolution, and immunofluorescence.

Morton’s neuroma and control nerves showed clear transcriptomic separation, with 3,349 differentially expressed genes: 1,461 upregulated and 1,888 downregulated. Upregulated pathways primarily involved immune and inflammatory responses, while downregulated pathways included myelination, axon guidance, neurogenesis, and nervous-system development. Co-expression analysis linked a defence-response module positively and a neurogenesis module negatively with paroxysmal pain, although only the defence-response association remained significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons.

Deconvolution indicated higher proportions of macrophages and memory B cells, but lower CD4+ helper T-cell proportions, in Morton’s neuroma. Macrophage proportions correlated with paroxysmal pain severity. The macrophage-associated genes MARCO, CD163, and STAB1, characteristic of an M(GC) glucocorticoid-stimulated subset, were upregulated and positively associated with paroxysmal pain and paraesthesia; MARCO showed a nominally significant correlation with paroxysmal pain.

Histological analyses confirmed demyelination and increased intraneural T-cell, CD163+, and CD163+MARCO+ macrophage densities in Morton’s neuroma. Overall CD68+ macrophage density did not differ significantly between groups but correlated with burning pain. Axonal β-tubulin III levels were not significantly different, although lower staining correlated with greater pain.

The findings associate chronic Morton’s neuroma with persistent intraneural inflammation, altered nervous-system development pathways, and demyelination. Limitations included varied control nerve locations, sex imbalance, small sample size, human tissue variability, and limited tissue for validation.

The speaker described a close, one-goal hockey game decided after an early penalty, saying the team missed key second-period chances and must capitalize against opponents who allow few opportunities. The team will not change its style but must skate faster, use last-change matchups better, and avoid leaving position to make hits. Speed, rather than physical play, was credited as a major factor in earlier playoff victories over Detroit, Vancouver, and San Jose.

The speaker said previous losses sometimes helped the team prove itself and improve, and the current series remains a game-by-game challenge. Line combinations were adjusted to improve matchups against opposing players, while several individual players were praised for strong play and major contributions. The speaker also discussed limited between-period instruction, players receiving treatment and refocusing, relationships among general managers and coaches, draft and free-agent preparations, and operating within fixed financial limits when deciding whether to retain players.

The speaker credits team unity, defensive depth and shared enthusiasm for individual success. Facing New Jersey requires respecting its depth, speed and power forwards while emphasizing positioning, containment, stick awareness and simple play over unnecessary physical battles. Ray Bourque and other veterans provide valuable lessons and help distribute responsibilities, keeping players fresher. Returning to the finals after a long absence reflects the league’s competitiveness and the importance of health, emotion, confidence, experience and determination. Although reaching this stage feels especially rewarding after sustained pressure and expectations, the team recognizes that the job is unfinished and must approach the next game from scratch.

Syria’s High Negotiations Committee seeks direct Geneva talks focused on forming a transitional governing body with full powers and excluding President Bashar al-Assad. A May 26–27, 2001 media roundup focused on Enron, California’s energy crisis, the Dabhol power dispute in India, Saudi gas projects, and energy regulation.

Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay privately presented prominent Californians with a plan advocating further deregulation, higher or market-based rates, conservation incentives, utility debt repayment by consumers, and an end to price-gouging investigations. Senator Dianne Feinstein sought hearings into possible improper ties between federal energy regulators and private companies after reports that Lay discussed supporting FERC Chairman Curtis Hebert if he backed Enron’s deregulation views. Both sides disputed tariffs, plant performance, unpaid bills, penalties, and the validity of their power purchase agreement while pursuing termination or rescission measures. Small-sided soccer games use fewer than 11 players per team on reduced fields, giving individuals more ball touches. In practice, formats typically range from 3v3 to 9v9 and develop tactical decision-making and technical skills under limited time and space. Themes include attack, defense, possession, passing, movement, shooting, transitions, support, crossing, switching play, and goalkeeping. Player numbers, field size, and complexity increase with age.

Competitive small-sided games provide an age-appropriate progression from U6 through U12. U.S. Soccer’s 2017 Player Development Initiatives established national standards involving fewer players, smaller fields, goals and balls, shorter games, and age-specific rules. These standards aim to increase meaningful participation, learning, decision-making, and consistent development nationwide.

From U9, build-out lines encourage possession and playing from the back, restrict opponents during goalkeeper possession and goal kicks, and define where offside begins. There is no offside before U9, and headers, goalkeeper punts, and drop kicks are prohibited. Additional standards cover field markings, substitutions, equipment, officials, restarts, free kicks, throw-ins or kick-ins, goal kicks, and corner kicks.

Dr. Pasvolsky said “peace-loving states” emphasized the organization’s peace objective. Initial membership would be settled in the Charter, while new members would be admitted by the Assembly upon Security Council recommendation, with both judging whether applicants were peace-loving. The Economic and Social Council’s position under the Assembly could later change.

On Chapter V, Mexico proposed three Assembly delegates per country, though Ambassador Castillo Nájera considered more potentially necessary; other commentaries opposed limits. Pasvolsky defended dividing responsibilities between organs for effective action. The Assembly could discuss peace and security issues and make recommendations, but the continuously operating Security Council would hold primary responsibility for action. He stressed that the organization’s success required most nations to support its principles and develop stable relations; otherwise, both the Assembly and Security Council would be ineffective.

The patent disclosure describes metal-assisted delayed fluorescent emitters using benzo-imidazo-phenanthridine and analogues for full-color displays and lighting. Their small singlet–triplet energy gap enables thermally assisted delayed fluorescence alongside phosphorescence, supporting high internal quantum efficiency and short lifetimes. The author examines psychiatry through the cases of a pregnant, suicidal girl, her grandmother, and her own depression diagnosis. The girl was detained after seeking an abortion but released after a second psychiatrist found no mental disorder. The author’s grandmother underwent involuntary ECT and multiple medication trials, sometimes worsening her condition. The author argues that psychiatric diagnoses often label behaviours without identifying underlying causes, are influenced by culture and politics, and rely partly on trial and error. While acknowledging that psychiatric intervention can sometimes be appropriate, she maintains that mental illness remains poorly understood and psychiatry should not be assumed to meet the same evidentiary standards as other medical fields.

The passage describes analyte monitoring systems, particularly one-piece devices that avoid separate packaging, sterilization, and user assembly of sensors and electronics. Conventional systems often sterilize sensors and sharps with radiation and electronics with gaseous chemicals because radiation can damage electronics while chemicals such as ethylene oxide can damage sensor chemistry.

The disclosed system includes a sensor applicator, cap, and preassembled sensor control device. The control device contains an electronics housing, biological sensor, sharp and sharp hub. A collimator inside the cap defines a sterilization zone receiving the exposed sensor and sharp. It focuses radiation, including electron-beam or low-energy X-ray irradiation, on these components while shielding sensitive electronics. Internal shields may provide additional protection.

Seals around the sharp hub, electronics housing, collimator, and sterilization-zone opening create a sterile region encompassing the sensor, sharp, and selected housing portions. The collimator may have conical, frustoconical, cylindrical, or polygonal passages and may be made from dense polymers or metals. It can be internal, external, or used with another collimator. External sterilization assemblies similarly direct radiation toward components requiring sterilization while shielding radiation-sensitive components.

The monitoring system places a sensor beneath a user’s skin with a retractable introducer and secures the control device using an adhesive patch. Sensor electronics process analyte data and communicate with reader devices, remote terminals, trusted computer systems, or networks through wired or wireless links. The system can monitor glucose and numerous other analytes or drugs.

Compared with two-piece architectures requiring users to combine separately sterilized components, the one-piece architecture arrives assembled in a sealed package. This reduces components, packaging, process steps, waste, contamination risk, and potential user error.

JM Smucker sued Trader Joe’s, alleging its frozen crustless peanut butter and jelly sandwiches copy trademarked Uncrustables features, including crimped edges and blue packaging, causing consumer confusion. Brewers outfielder Jackson Chourio exited Milwaukee’s 9-3 NLDS opener against the Cubs after injuring his hamstring while beating out an RBI single. The lecture presents a SNARG construction from two primitives: batch arguments (BARGs) and somewhere extractable, or somewhere statistically binding, hash functions.

A BARG succinctly proves that many NP instances are valid. Its semi-adaptive soundness requires a cheating prover to choose before seeing the CRS which instance location will be false, though the instances themselves may be chosen afterward. BARGs for index languages allow verification from a succinct description of the instances, with runtime depending only logarithmically on their number.

A somewhere extractable hash supports succinct hashes and local openings. Its key hides a designated index, while that index is statistically binding: even an unbounded adversary cannot open it to both bits. Index hiding extends computational binding to every index. Repetition gives binding and extraction at multiple locations, with hash size growing accordingly.

The hash can be constructed using bounded-depth homomorphic encryption. A basic encrypted-index tree is insufficient because malicious openings may contain malformed ciphertexts. Using separate keys across tree levels and homomorphically decrypting and re-encrypting ensures ciphertexts along an opened path are well formed, establishing binding.

For the SNARG, the prover evaluates every wire of the verification circuit and hashes all wire values. It then supplies a BARG proving that, for every circuit gate, valid hash openings exist for its input and output wires, that these values satisfy the gate, and that the circuit’s output is one. The SNARG proof consists of the hash value and BARG proof. The verifier checks only the BARG. Because the gate statements form an index language with a succinct description, verification need not scale linearly with the circuit size; its dependence can be polylogarithmic, apart from reading the original input.

The Inquiry is compiling coordinated newspaper analyses, treaty obligations, declarations, national biographies, and briefs on subject nationalities, mostly for completion by mid-January or February 1. Existing resources include charts comparing fourteen international organization plans and tracing major international events since 1870. For Poland and the Baltic provinces, Austria-Hungary, the Balkans, Turkey in Asia, and Central Africa, researchers are gathering concise histories, authoritative sources, accounts of racial participation and restrictions, political organizations, and government structures. The study examines optical-cavity coupling to quantum-critical magnetic systems, primarily the transverse-field Ising model. When cavity photons couple directly to the critical order parameter, quantum-critical fluctuations reduce the critical light–matter coupling for a superradiant phase transition to zero at the matter quantum critical point. Large-spin analysis and one-dimensional density matrix renormalization group calculations yield qualitatively consistent phase diagrams and distinct scaling regimes across ordered, critical, and disordered phases.

Critical matter–photon mixing produces intrinsic two-mode squeezing and light–matter entanglement stronger than in the standard Dicke model. At the quantum critical point, the minimum quadrature variance vanishes more rapidly and the conjugate variance, proportional to quantum Fisher information, diverges more strongly. If photons instead couple to a noncritical spin component, ferromagnetism and superradiance compete; the critical coupling remains finite, reaches a minimum near the matter critical point, and a tricritical point separates discontinuous and continuous transitions. Analysis of a ferromagnetic XY model further supports the general role of critical fluctuations in facilitating superradiance. Candidate experimental materials include CoNb₂O₆, LiHoF₄, and CrI₃, and the framework may extend to driven-dissipative systems.
On July 25, 1977, the court unanimously denied Harry H. Boddie’s application for a writ of habeas corpus.

The Jammu and Kashmir Assembly witnessed protests and an opposition walkout over alleged attacks on Kashmiri students outside the state, including two students assaulted in Haryana. The government said Haryana police had filed an FIR, arrested three people, and coordinated with Jammu and Kashmir officials. Opposition members accused the government of failing to prevent such incidents and warned they could increase alienation. They also questioned an all-party meeting on panchayat elections, claiming decisions had already been made; the government said its outcome would be considered by the cabinet. Legislators also praised Army and Air Force rescue efforts after three soldiers died in an avalanche in Gurez.

American drug suspect Christian Beasley escaped Bali’s overcrowded Kerobokan prison by sawing through a ceiling and scaling a wall. Another American inmate was caught attempting to escape. Authorities are investigating possible guard involvement. The prison houses nearly 1,600 inmates despite a 300-person capacity and previously saw four foreign prisoners escape in June.

The invention describes a Reconfigurable Power Station (RPS) that autonomously extends the operating range of unmanned aerial vehicles by exchanging depleted swap cartridges for energized cartridges. The system can support multiple UAV types and sizes and may also apply to ground, underground, surface, underwater, and space vehicles.

The RPS communicates with a Universal Integrated Swap system aboard a UAV, evaluates cartridge status and vehicle information, authorizes landing, and guides the UAV using a dynamic terminal landing system with scalable visible or non-visible markers. After landing, the station may mechanically secure and electrically power the UAV. Sensors locate the cartridge receptacle, and a swapping mechanism removes the depleted cartridge, places it in a modular power bay for storage or replenishment, retrieves a compatible energized cartridge, and installs it in the UAV.

Modular power bays can hold cartridges of different types and sizes, including batteries, fuel cells, fossil fuels, hybrid power media, or other payloads. Cartridges may contain connectors, data storage, identifying markers, locking features, and health, compatibility, ownership, or payload information. A central processor coordinates communications, cartridge selection and exchange, power distribution, environmental controls, system monitoring, data storage, and safety functions.

The station may use grid, generator, solar, or internal power and can operate locally or remotely through wired or wireless communications. It may download mission or payload data, assess environmental and flight-readiness conditions, manage landing queues for multiple UAVs, and clear serviced vehicles for departure.

Former Cubs pitcher Ryan Dempster feels pride and gratification in Kyle Hendricks’ success because Chicago acquired Hendricks when it traded Dempster to Texas in 2012. Hendricks later won an ERA title, helped clinch the NLCS, started Game 7 of the Cubs’ World Series victory and earned a Game 1 postseason start against Washington. Dempster, who had no-trade rights, rejected an Atlanta deal before accepting the Rangers trade. He views Hendricks’ rise as especially meaningful because Dempster himself was once a Class A prospect traded for a veteran.

The collection highlights Enron’s November 2001 financial crisis, proposed acquisition by Dynegy, regulatory uncertainty, investor concerns over undisclosed debt, and efforts to sell assets including Wessex Water and its Dabhol power stake. An opinion article argues that despite transparency and conflict-of-interest concerns, Enron contributed innovations in deregulated energy markets, customized contracts, networks, risk controls, and corporate culture.

Fortune warns that companies face up to $65 billion in repayments on zero-coupon convertible bonds after falling stock prices made conversion unlikely. Enron was classified as particularly risky. Other reports describe record corporate bond issuance driven largely by refinancing, weak brokerage stock portfolios, and strong but volatile Russian fund performance. Indian power-sector coverage discusses Dabhol due diligence, litigation, and broader structural and pricing problems.

Orbitronics uses electrically generated orbital angular momentum through effects such as the orbital Hall and orbital Rashba-Edelstein effects. Experiments commonly detect orbital torque after orbital angular momentum is converted to spin in a ferromagnet or an added conversion layer. Other approaches include magnetoresistance, reciprocal orbital pumping and THz emission, orbital Hanle magnetoresistance, and direct imaging through dichroism, magneto-optical methods, or electron microscopy. Quantitative interpretation remains difficult because generation, interface transport, spin conversion, spin transport, and torque transfer are hard to separate.

CuOx has been identified as a strong orbital-angular-momentum source, producing enhanced torques when Pt converts orbital currents into spin currents. Experiments also report orbital transport over longer distances than spin transport, strong dependence on ferromagnetic material and crystal symmetry, and orbital torques in antiferromagnets, two-dimensional systems, and perpendicular ferromagnets. Reciprocal pumping and transport reciprocity remain unsettled. In two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides, the orbital Hall effect may better describe orbital transport than the valley Hall effect and may have topological characteristics.

Theory describes orbital texture as broadly present even without spin-orbit coupling, allowing orbital Hall and interfacial orbital Rashba-Edelstein effects in many solids. Major unresolved questions concern torque magnitude and orbital relaxation. Experiments indicate orbital relaxation lengths longer than spin relaxation lengths, despite strong crystal-field coupling that should efficiently dissipate orbital angular momentum. Conflicting calculations predict either long-range orbital torque or extremely short orbital diffusion lengths.

Potential applications include MRAM, oscillators, random-number generators, logic devices, unconventional computing, and THz emitters. Orbital torque could enable low-resistivity light metals, but practical devices require higher torque efficiency, compatibility with high tunneling magnetoresistance, shorter diffusion lengths, low write current and resistance, endurance, thermal robustness, manufacturability, and scalability. Orbitronics may benefit from abundant materials, crystal and interface engineering, robustness to magnetic perturbations, and coupling to photons and phonons, though its generation, transport, interface behavior, and spin conversion remain incompletely understood.

HHH defended excluding women from the Greatest Royal Rumble, citing cultural differences and arguing WWE can promote change through engagement. He highlighted WWE’s first women’s match in Abu Dhabi and said discussions were underway in hopes that women could compete in Saudi Arabia within the next few years.

On April 26, 1879, President Rutherford B. Hayes warned against unauthorized settlement in Indian Territory, which was legally reserved for Indian tribes and authorized persons. Violators would be promptly removed by Indian Department agents, with military assistance if necessary, to enforce federal laws and protect tribal and U.S. interests.

WHO reported 503,484 suspected cases and 1,975 deaths from Yemen’s waterborne disease outbreak. Although transmission slowed since early July, about 5,000 people remain affected daily. War-damaged infrastructure, poor sanitation, limited clean water and healthcare shortages have worsened the epidemic. WHO urged payment for health workers and a political solution to the conflict.

The coach said the team has managed frustration by refocusing after each shift and adhering to its game plan despite two losses to Detroit. Detroit’s stronger net-front presence, success in loose-puck battles, and scramble goals have been the main differences. Although his team has generated more shots and chances, it must drive the net, create second opportunities, protect its own crease, and maintain composure. Guest lecturer Jason Ku discusses representational origami as both art and an algorithmic design discipline, comparing origami designers and folders to musical composers and performers. He focuses on works generally made from a single uncut square and intended to represent recognizable subjects.

Akira Yoshizawa, described as the father of modern origami, pioneered creating original models and using wet-folding to produce curved, expressive forms. Traditional origami styles emphasize precise straight creases, clean polygons, flat folding, and grids based on angles such as 22.5 or 45 degrees. Nontraditional styles rely more heavily on wet-folding, curved tension folds, texture, and subjective shaping. Artists discussed include Hideo Komatsu, David Brill, Michael LaFosse, and Eric Joisel, whose sculptural and expressive work often depicts human figures and incorporates extensive shaping and texture.

Modern realism combines structural complexity with free-form shaping. Robert Lang pioneered algorithmic origami design, codified tree theory, and developed TreeMaker. His work demonstrates precise proportions, complex insects, tessellations, and modular forms. Brian Chan applies tree theory, color changes, and detailed texturing to complex single-sheet subjects, including a rose with its stem, anime characters, a kraken attacking a ship, and the MIT seal. Satoshi Kamiya combines crisp geometric folding with detailed three-dimensional shaping; one highly complex dragon required about a year to fold and contains thousands of scales.

Ku explains tree theory as a process of reducing a subject to a stick figure that specifies flap lengths and connectivity, converting that tree into an origami base, and shaping the base into the final model. Artistic judgment is especially important when choosing which features to represent, determining proportions, allocating paper, and shaping the result.

Uniaxial bases have flaps aligned along a common axis and hinged perpendicular to it, allowing their projection to form a one-dimensional tree. Circular regions correspond to leaf flaps, while constant-width strips called rivers separate portions of a model and correspond to branch edges. A space allocation maps uniquely to a tree, but one tree can have multiple space allocations. Central flaps use more paper and can provide bulk, while edge or corner flaps are better suited to thin features.

Crease patterns can be analyzed through hinge creases to recover their underlying trees. Extra paper can provide flap thickness, broad structures such as butterfly wings, toes, texture, or scales. Kamiya’s dragon illustrates how pleating compresses textured regions while preserving the model’s overall long form.

Ku demonstrates TreeMaker by defining a crab’s legs, claws, eyes, body, and relative edge lengths; scaling circles to avoid overlap; managing active paths and constraints; imposing symmetry; and triangulating polygons. He then presents a manually designed crab using 22.5-degree folding, geometric surface design, an underbelly, texture, and later shaping. He closes by recommending Robert Lang’s *Origami Design Secrets*, the documentary *Between the Folds*, online forums, and MIT’s OrigaMIT club.

NVIDIA’s A100 GPU targets AI, HPC, analytics, and data-center workloads. It includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1555 GB/s bandwidth, over 1.7 times V100, and a 40 MB L2 cache with 2.3 times V100’s L2 bandwidth. SECDED ECC protects HBM2, caches, and register files. Programmable cache residency and Compute Data Compression can improve effective DRAM bandwidth, L2 bandwidth, and cache capacity.

A100 has 108 SMs and third-generation Tensor Cores supporting larger operations, improved thread-level data sharing, structured sparsity, and substantially fewer instructions and register accesses. Asynchronous global-to-shared memory copies, asynchronous barriers, and 164 KB of shared memory per SM improve data movement and help sustain Tensor Core utilization. CUDA 11 supports these capabilities, along with accelerated task graphs, cooperative groups, and persistent L2 caching.

Multi-Instance GPU partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute and memory resources, including GPCs, SMs, L2 slices, memory controllers, and frame-buffer capacity. MIG provides predictable performance, quality of service, fault isolation, and support for VMs, containers, processes, MPS, migration, and multiple users or tenants. GPU Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances for simultaneous, independently context-switched workloads.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth per A100, twice V100’s aggregate bandwidth. A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4 at 31.5 GB/s per direction for x16 connections, SR-IOV, enhanced fault detection and containment, five NVDEC units, a five-core NVJPG decoder, an optical-flow accelerator, and improved FP16 and FP32 atomic throughput.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs, six NVSwitches, and high-speed networking, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS and 4.8 TB/s aggregate bidirectional GPU interconnect bandwidth. MIG enables up to 56 isolated accelerators per DGX A100. Its software stack includes CUDA 11, the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC software, deep-learning frameworks, inference, analytics, and HPC tools.

A100 also supports 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity, intended to reduce computation and memory traffic while preserving balanced workloads and, in evaluated networks, producing virtually no accuracy loss after fine-tuning.

Cosmetic tooth bleaching is a growing $3.2 billion global industry with numerous products that can confuse consumers. Whitening products are considered cosmetics and do not require FDA approval, though the FDA has not found currently marketed ingredients unsafe. The ADA seal indicates independent review for safety and effectiveness; only one over-the-counter bleaching product currently carries it.

Over-the-counter products can work when used as directed but may cause temporary tooth sensitivity or gum inflammation and generally take two to six weeks. Custom dentist-made trays cost about $400 and provide a more precise application, while in-office bleaching costs over $1,000, uses higher peroxide concentrations, and produces faster, more dramatic results. Insurance rarely covers these cosmetic procedures.

Dentists recommend an examination before bleaching because discoloration may indicate cavities or other problems. Surface stains from foods, drinks, and smoking may improve with cleaning, while bleaching can lighten deeper age-related stains by two to seven shades. Discoloration caused by trauma, tetracycline, or excess fluoride is permanent and may require crowns or veneers. All bleaching results are temporary and require touch-ups. The ADA says there is no evidence that remedies such as charcoal, baking soda, or lemon juice whiten teeth.

The oil-laden Barge New London, pushed by the Tug Ocean Prince, struck a charted rock outside the Hudson River channel and caused a major oil spill. The district court denied exoneration but limited Red Star’s liability to the tug’s value and capped federal cleanup liability at $100 per gross ton. It dismissed claims against the United States and found Pittston, the barge owner, not responsible.

The Second Circuit held that Red Star was not entitled to limitation. Red Star knew pilot Reimer lacked Hudson River experience but failed to appoint a captain, inform experienced pilot Kiernan of Reimer’s inexperience, or require a proper lookout. These management failures rendered the tug unseaworthy and constituted negligence within Red Star’s privity and knowledge. The absence of a lookout also violated a statutory duty and could have contributed to the casualty because a lookout could have identified the visible Con Hook Light in time to avoid the rock.

The court further found Red Star’s combined omissions amounted to willful misconduct under the federal water-pollution statute, removing the statutory cap on cleanup costs. It affirmed dismissal of claims against the United States because the available buoy was the best practical aid during ice season and any government negligence was not the proximate cause.

The judgment was reversed insofar as it limited Red Star’s liability, affirmed otherwise, and remanded for judgments awarding Pittston and the United States their damages.

The FDA indicated it would approve Epidiolex, a purified cannabidiol medicine, for seizures associated with rare, severe Lennox-Gastaut and Dravet syndromes in patients aged 2 and older. Three studies provided substantial evidence of effectiveness, with risks considered acceptable given the life-threatening nature of the disorders. Manufactured by GW Pharmaceuticals under strict standards, Epidiolex is 99 percent pure CBD, contains no THC, and differs from dispensary products or smoked marijuana. Experts emphasized consistent pharmaceutical quality and reported major improvements in some severely affected children. While unsubstantiated CBD products are widely marketed for other conditions, Epidiolex underwent required testing. Doctors are also interested in researching CBD for autism, anxiety, and inflammatory and autoimmune disorders.

The Single/Double offense, common in NBA playbooks, frees a strong shooter through coordinated single and double baseline screens while attacking both sides of the defense. The shooter cuts toward the basket, then chooses either screen as another wing moves opposite. Defensive reactions determine counters: curls or basket cuts against trailing defenders, fades or back cuts against overplays, post or wing isolations against switches, and slips or lobs against show-and-recover coverage. Ballhandlers may drive when passing lanes are overplayed.

Screeners also create scoring opportunities by breaking double screens into down screens, back screens, rolls, slips, pop-outs, and lob actions. Similar reads and counters apply to down screens. Defensive switching can produce post mismatches against smaller defenders or wing isolations against larger, less mobile defenders.

If the initial action does not create a shot, the offense can continue through motion, side screen-and-roll, or drive-and-kick actions. It also supports strong post play and offensive rebounding, with inside positioning and two weakside rebounders.

Successful execution requires precise timing, coordination, nonverbal communication, defensive recognition, and proficiency in screening, using screens, posting up, and rebounding. Teaching should include breakdown drills, scrimmaging, and individual skill development. Teams should scout defensive tendencies, prepare appropriate counters, vary alignments and entries, target weak defenders, and use side screens late in the shot or game clock.

Trapped-ion quantum computers offer long coherence and high-fidelity gates but are limited by relatively slow motion-mediated entanglement. Electrons could enable much faster gates because of their lower mass, though existing electron-trap proposals require cryogenic cooling and lack integrated control of individual spins and collective states.

The paper proposes simultaneously trapping laser-cooled Ca ions and quasi-free electrons in the same space using a two-frequency planar Paul trap. A Ca+ ion would be Doppler-cooled and photoionized, producing a Ca2+-electron system. The electron’s states progress from ion-bound states through transitional Rydberg-like states to trap-induced states above the ionization threshold, where their spectrum approaches that of a harmonic oscillator. Tunable transitions between these states may support quantum computing, photon counting, spin manipulation, ion coupling, and radio-frequency-to-optical conversion.

The two-frequency trap uses separate high-frequency electron and lower-frequency ion signals whose trapping-field centers should overlap. Optical transitions provide cooling, ionization, state control, recombination, and detection through electromagnetically induced transparency. The planar ring-electrode design is intended to support scalable fabrication, photonic and electronic integration, symmetric confinement, reduced heating, and trapping about 1 mm from the electrodes. Its parameters prioritize electron-state separation while retaining enough volume for sympathetic cooling of Ca2+ by Ca+ ions.

The disclosure describes ultrasonic fingerprint sensing systems positioned beneath displays, including OLED and flexible OLED displays. The sensors transmit ultrasonic waves through the display and detect reflections from fingerprint ridges and valleys to generate biometric images for authentication.

Proposed devices integrate an ultrasonic sensor with combinations of non-porous light-blocking layers, grounded electrical shielding layers, reworkable adhesives, mechanical stress-isolation layers, and high- or low-acoustic-impedance materials. These layers lie in the acoustic path while reducing optical transmission, electromagnetic interference, thermal variation, mechanical stress, acoustic loss, and display distortion. Detachable adhesives permit sensor replacement or refurbishment. Foam or air backing layers may reflect acoustic energy and protect the sensor.

The sensor may include pixel circuits on glass, plastic, silicon, stainless steel, or flexible substrates; a piezoelectric transmitter, receiver, or transceiver layer; and electrodes. Piezoelectric materials may include PVDF, PVDF-TrFE, PZT, or aluminum nitride. Flexible implementations can span substantially the entire active display area, enabling authentication anywhere on the display.

Manufacturing methods include laminating or bonding functional layers to a display and attaching the ultrasonic sensor beneath them. Implementations support receiver-up or receiver-down orientations and may include protective housings, edge seals, flexible printed circuits, stiffeners, acoustic matching layers, and processing systems for controlling the sensor and converting reflected signals into fingerprint images. The technology is applicable to mobile, wearable, automotive, computing, and other electronic devices.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell architecture introduces scheduling, media, display, power-efficiency, neural-rendering, and AI graphics improvements. Its AI Management Processor coordinates workloads to reduce response latency and prioritize game-engine tasks, improving frame consistency and quality of service.

Blackwell adds hardware encoding and decoding for 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC video, which retains twice the color resolution of 4:2:0 while requiring two-thirds the data of uncompressed 4:4:4. Ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR and adds an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode. The RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders, delivering over 50% faster exports than the prior generation. Sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed. DisplayPort 2.1b with UHBR 20 provides up to 80 Gbps and supports 8K at 165 Hz or 4K at 480 Hz with Display Stream Compression.

Max-Q improvements include finer clock, power, and rail gating; independent core and memory voltage control; and complete memory-clock-tree gating. Clock frequencies can adapt to workloads 1,000 times faster than previous architectures, while the deepest sleep state is entered 10 times faster than on Ada. Combined improvements can reduce power consumption by up to 50% during small-language-model inference.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame. Its frame-generation model is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and runs once per rendered frame. Enhanced Flip Metering moves frame pacing to the display engine. Transformer-based models replace CNNs for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA, using twice as many parameters to improve temporal stability, motion detail, lighting, anti-aliasing, and reduce ghosting and denoising artifacts.

Blackwell also supports developer-created neural shaders through Tensor Core access from graphics shaders using Cooperative Vectors APIs for DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Applications include neural texture compression, neural materials, radiance caching, skin rendering, and generative neural faces. Neural texture compression reduces memory use and can provide up to seven-to-one compression over block-compressed formats. Neural Radiance Cache estimates multi-bounce indirect illumination from partially traced rays, improving lighting quality and performance.

A small study comparing 12 boys aged around 10, 12 untrained men and 13 male endurance athletes found that boys’ muscles resisted fatigue during high-intensity cycling similarly to endurance athletes and recovered even faster. Researchers attributed this to children’s less-developed anaerobic systems, which produce less lactic acid, and their faster clearance of lactic acid from the blood. The findings do not mean children are as fit as elite athletes, but suggest their recovery patterns resemble them.

The results may help tailor youth training toward skills, strength and sprint ability rather than aerobic fitness, and favor stop-start play over adult-style deliberate exercise. Researchers also found that muscle-level aerobic fitness declines from childhood into adulthood. Further research could investigate whether these changes are related to increased risks of diseases associated with physical inactivity and aging.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data-acquisition system with configurable straight-binary or two’s-complement output. It supports differential or lower-power single-ended free-running sampling clocks; stopping the clock invalidates output data and clocks. SMPL_SYNC synchronizes channel sampling and frame alignment across multiple devices.

The device includes a low-drift internal reference, filtered with a 10µF REFIO capacitor, and supports an external reference when the internal reference is disabled. Its source-synchronous interface offers two or four lanes in SDR or DDR mode. Each 20-bit result is transmitted MSB-first in a 24-bit packet with six trailing zeros. Data and frame clock frequencies depend on sampling rate, lane count, and data-rate mode.

Features include output randomization using a PRBS bit or conversion-result LSB, simple and moving averaging, and fixed, ramp, or alternating test patterns configurable separately for channels 1–4 and 5–8. Speed-boost mode samples one selected channel pair at up to 8MSPS while the other six channels remain idle.

Reset or power-down restores default registers, and initialization requires prescribed register writes with a free-running clock. Configuration uses three banks of 16-bit registers addressed through 24-bit SPI frames. SPI supports register reads, writes, and multiple-device daisy chains.

The ADC provides low-noise bandwidth up to 22.7kHz and wide bandwidth up to 700kHz. In an ATE example, it achieves 0.0015% total unadjusted error at 25°C ±5°C after calibration and 99.95% full-scale settling in 7.5µs in wide-bandwidth mode. It uses AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies without a required power-up sequence. Recommended layout practices include local bypassing, short reference and ground connections, and separation of analog paths from digital noise.

The President describes the Cuban war as a prolonged humanitarian, commercial, and security crisis affecting the United States. Spanish reconcentration policies devastated agriculture, displaced more than 300,000 people, and caused widespread starvation and death. American relief efforts delivered nearly $200,000 in aid, while diplomatic attempts to secure mediation, an armistice, home rule, and an end to reconcentration failed to achieve peace.

The President rejects immediate recognition of Cuban belligerency or independence, arguing that neither would end the conflict and that Cuba had not yet demonstrated stable, secure statehood. He instead considers intervention justified by humanitarian suffering, threats to American citizens and property, damage to commerce, mounting government expense, and danger to national peace. The destruction of the USS *Maine*, attributed by an American inquiry to an external mine without assigning responsibility, further demonstrated Cuba’s intolerable insecurity.

Concluding that Spain could not suppress the insurrection and that continued warfare would bring only exhaustion and destruction, the President asks Congress to authorize measures, including military and naval force, to end hostilities and establish a stable Cuban government. He also requests continued food relief funded partly by Congress. A late Spanish decree suspending hostilities is presented for congressional consideration, with intervention remaining contemplated if it fails.

Goal-of-care (GOC) discussions improve serious-illness care but are often documented inconsistently across electronic health record notes. Researchers developed an NLP classifier to identify GOC discussions in general inpatient notes from patients with advanced illnesses at five University of Pennsylvania Health System hospitals.

The dataset contained 400 Advance Care Planning notes and 376 general notes. Annotators labeled individual utterances, revealing substantial class imbalance: general notes contained 109 positive and 24,174 negative utterances. Researchers compared passive and active learning using logistic regression, regular expressions, transformer models, and ensembles.

The best system was a five-classifier ensemble using weighted-average predictions and active learning. It achieved moderate F1 scores of approximately 0.56 for utterances and 0.63 for notes. It identified 13 of 18 test notes containing GOC discussions while incorrectly flagging 13 notes. Active learning improved precision and required annotation of 3,200 additional utterances, or 30% of the unlabeled general-note set. Training on all available examples generally did not outperform active learning.

Performance was limited by utterance-level classification, lack of surrounding context, and a restricted active-learning pool containing few positive examples. The authors consider the classifier suitable for production-supported clinician review and plan further testing on a much larger pool of notes. The annotated clinical notes are not publicly available because they contain protected health information; code and models are available on reasonable request.

The “Diamond & One” defense uses four zone defenders and one chaser who denies the opponent’s primary scorer. It is most effective against odd or one-guard fronts, protects the middle well, but concedes corners; teams can switch to a Box & One if corners become problematic. X5 stays between the ball and basket near the low post, X1 protects the high post, and wing defenders cover from the free-throw-line extensions to the corners, rotating according to ball position. Against an odd front, defenders force ball handlers toward sideline or baseline pressure points while weak-side players protect rebounds and passing lanes. The alignment also supports double-teaming a strong post player: the chaser denies the post, X5 joins the double team, and outside defenders anticipate passes from the trap. The chaser’s strong denial is intended to limit the star scorer and disrupt offensive plays and continuities.

The lecture develops matching, renormalization-group running, and power corrections in heavy quark effective theory (HQET). One-loop heavy-quark wave-function renormalization is calculated using dimensional regularization, MS-bar, Feynman gauge, and a parameterization suited to integrals containing both linear and quadratic momentum denominators. The resulting renormalization differs from full QCD because HQET uses a heavy-quark propagator.

Heavy-to-light currents acquire a nonzero anomalous dimension below the heavy-quark mass, unlike the corresponding partially conserved current in full QCD. This anomalous dimension is independent of the current’s spin structure, consistent with heavy-quark spin symmetry. For heavy-to-heavy currents involving velocities \(v\) and \(v'\), the anomalous dimension depends nontrivially on \(w=v\cdot v'\), which is fixed by external kinematics but can vary across a process. Renormalization-group evolution resums logarithms separated between HQET Wilson coefficients and scale-dependent matrix elements, with evolution stopped where perturbation theory remains reliable.

Matching full QCD onto HQET requires accounting for vertex corrections, wave-function residues, and operator structures. A vector current can match onto two HQET currents because the velocity \(v^\mu\) supplies an additional vector. Matching can be simplified by using dimensional regularization for both ultraviolet and infrared divergences: on-shell HQET loop graphs become scaleless, while their infrared divergences cancel those of the full theory, leaving the finite full-theory terms as matching coefficients.

Power corrections arise as an expansion in \(1/M_Q\). Integrating out the suppressed heavy-field component yields two first-order operators: a kinetic-energy term and a chromomagnetic term. The kinetic term breaks heavy-flavor symmetry but preserves spin symmetry, while the chromomagnetic term breaks both.

A bottom-up operator analysis must impose power counting, gauge invariance, discrete symmetries, and reparameterization invariance. Reparameterization invariance reflects the freedom to shift a small momentum contribution between \(M_Qv\) and the residual momentum. It restores invariance under small boosts and relates different orders in the expansion. This symmetry fixes the kinetic operator’s Wilson coefficient to one to all perturbative orders, provided the regulator and scheme preserve the symmetry. The chromomagnetic coefficient is not similarly constrained and has a nonzero anomalous dimension.

The course’s second half shifts from block codes toward convolutional codes and codes on graphs, which enable capacity-approaching performance with lower-complexity decoding. Shannon showed that random codes can approach capacity, and random linear codes permit polynomial-complexity encoding. However, maximum-likelihood decoding of block codes generally has exponential complexity. Algebraically decodable codes such as Reed-Solomon and BCH codes have polynomial decoding complexity but do not reach capacity.

A rate-1/2, constraint-length-2 convolutional encoder was introduced. It maps each input bit and two previous bits to two output bits:
\(y_{1k}=u_k+u_{k-2}\) and \(y_{2k}=u_k+u_{k-1}+u_{k-2}\), over \(F_2\). The encoder combines linear time-invariant structure with a four-state finite-state structure. This combination supports low-complexity decoding through the Viterbi algorithm.

Convolutional codes were defined using Laurent sequences: binary sequences with a definite starting time but potentially infinite duration. Their D-transforms are generating functions \(\sum_k u_kD^k\). Laurent sequences form a field because addition, convolutional multiplication, and inverses are well-defined. Rational sequences, expressible as ratios of polynomials, are exactly eventually periodic sequences. Restricting encoder impulse responses to causal rational sequences guarantees finite-state realizations.

For the example encoder, the impulse responses are \(g_1(D)=1+D^2\) and \(g_2(D)=1+D+D^2\), giving \(y(D)=u(D)g(D)\). Equivalent encoders generate the same code and differ by multiplication by an invertible rational causal sequence. A canonical polynomial encoder can be obtained by clearing denominators and removing common factors, producing a feedback-free realization with minimal constraint length.

The example code is linear, so its minimum distance equals the minimum nonzero output weight. Its free distance is five: every finite nonzero path begins with output weight two, adds at least one more unit, and ends with output weight two. The four-state transition diagram confirms this result. Future topics include trellis diagrams, catastrophic encoders, and the Viterbi algorithm.

In Ward v. Yorba, both parties claimed title to Los Angeles property through competing proceedings. After negotiations and legal advice, Yorba agreed to pay Ward $4,750 for Ward’s interest, paying $100 initially. The written contract mistakenly required Ward to convey perfect title, although testimony showed the parties intended only a transfer of Ward’s existing interest. Yorba later refused to pay the balance, arguing mistake and inadequate consideration after learning his own title was superior.

The court upheld reformation and specific enforcement of the contract. Clear evidence supported the finding that the writing did not express the parties’ actual agreement. Yorba knew the material facts concerning both titles and acted on counsel’s advice, so his mistaken assessment of their legal strength did not qualify as a factual mistake under Civil Code section 1577. The agreement also had sufficient consideration because Ward surrendered his disputed claim, possession, and related litigation concerning property worth $9,000. The judgment awarding Ward $4,650 plus interest and costs, and the order denying a new trial, were affirmed.

TMPM format, content, and migration-list errors are reported in commands or entries, possibly causing rejection or partial success. Ring Buffer errors use PM_STATUS. Hardware errors use command status or MCA; failures may render batch pages unrecoverable, allowing software to save state.

Apple options allow traders to speculate on or hedge movements in Apple stock through calls, which provide a right to buy, and puts, which provide a right to sell at a specified strike price before expiration. Prices depend on the underlying stock, time to expiration, volatility, interest rates, dividends, corporate news, and macroeconomic conditions.

Strategies include buying or selling calls and puts, covered calls, protective puts, straddles, strangles, and delta hedging. Options offer leverage and flexibility but involve substantial risks, including rapid losses, time decay, market risk, and potentially unlimited losses from naked short calls. Apple options are described as highly liquid, volatile, competitive, and generally more complex than trading Apple stock.

Trading costs include contract prices, brokerage commissions, taxes, transaction fees, and slippage. Profits are generally subject to capital gains taxes, while the applicable rate depends on the investor’s circumstances. Available orders include market, limit, stop, and stop-limit orders, though stop orders may be bypassed by sudden price movements.

Traders can evaluate options using technical, fundamental, and options analysis tools, including charting software, financial reports, Black-Scholes models, Monte Carlo simulations, and backtesting. American-style options may be exercised before expiration, whereas European-style options may be exercised only at expiration. The passage recommends limit orders for entry and exit, emphasizes quantitative backtesting and risk preparation, and advises most traders to consider trading Apple stock before attempting options.

Researchers identified 2-methylisocitrate (2-MiCit), a metabolite produced by tumor-associated bacteria, that enhances the colorectal cancer drug 5-fluorouracil. Screening in microscopic worms showed that E. coli produces the molecule, while computer modelling indicated that microbiomes from cancer patients could also generate it. Tests in human cancer cells and a fly model found potent anti-cancer effects and extended fly survival.

2-MiCit inhibits a mitochondrial enzyme, disrupts cancer-cell metabolism, damages DNA, and activates pathways that reduce cancer progression. Combined with 5-fluorouracil, it killed significantly more cancer cells than either compound alone. Researchers also developed a synthetic version with greater cancer-killing potency. The findings suggest that metabolites from tumor-dwelling microbes could support new treatments, improve existing chemotherapy, and contribute to personalized medicine.

The speaker values veteran teammates as role models for younger players and credits demanding coach Hitchcock with fostering his growth. The team prioritizes winning over individual scoring, with everyone contributing as needed. This qualitative case study examined AI integration throughout a university-level Digital Photography in Nature course at a public university in eastern Turkey. Guided by TPACK, constructivist learning theory, and the MRK instructional design model, it investigated the experiences of one instructor and 38 associate-degree students. Data came from semi-structured interviews and were analyzed through content analysis, producing five themes and 17 codes.

The instructor integrated tools including ChatGPT, Claude, Flikia AI, Krea AI, and Gamma App into flipped-classroom, project-based, and collaborative activities. AI supported course planning, learner analysis, personalized feedback, photography analysis, content creation, and assessment. Weekly assignments involved analyzing composition, lighting, exposure, focus, and other technical elements. The instructor reported improvements in students’ technical proficiency, academic language, personalized learning, engagement, and assessment efficiency.

Students described AI as an assistant, guide, or teacher that improved technical knowledge, provided rapid and detailed feedback, saved time, increased convenience, and raised awareness of AI tools. By the course’s end, all participants were actively using AI tools, and some had adopted them in other courses.

Reported disadvantages included passivity, overreliance, reduced independent research, possible constraints on originality, misinformation, contradictory responses, and uncritical acceptance of AI feedback. Infrastructure problems, unequal access to devices and premium services, connectivity issues, and AI hallucinations also hindered implementation. Participants emphasized that AI should supplement rather than replace instructors and human judgment.

The study concludes that AI can support personalized, adaptive, and efficient learning when integrated through a clear pedagogical framework. It recommends AI-literacy training, reflective assignments, human-led feedback, critical verification of outputs, ethical guidance, equitable technological access, educator professional development, and continued monitoring. Limitations include its focus on one course, institution, and instructor; reliance on qualitative data; and absence of a control group.

The Allies deplore wartime suffering but deny responsibility, attributing the conflict to deliberate German and Austro-Hungarian aggression. They welcome assurance that the American communication was unrelated to the Central Powers’ proposal, while rejecting any equivalence between the belligerent groups. Citing invasions, atrocities, submarine attacks, deportations, and other abuses, they argue that the Central Powers defied humanity and international law. Their war aims include restoring and indemnifying Belgium, Serbia, and Montenegro; evacuating and repairing occupied Allied territories; reorganizing Europe around national rights, security, liberty, and protected borders; returning seized territories; liberating subject nationalities; ending Ottoman domination in Europe; and resisting Prussian militarism. They deny seeking the destruction of the German people and seek peace founded on liberty, justice, and faithful observance of international obligations.

Orochi is presented as a versatile foundational model for low-level biomedical image processing, addressing restoration, super-resolution, registration, and fusion within a unified framework. It targets limitations of specialist models involving sequential tasks, related degradations, and the high computational costs of large, multi-channel biomedical datasets.

The model is trained on over 100 terabytes of raw, unlabeled data from more than 100 studies, spanning 2D–5D imaging modalities. Random Multi-scale Sampling converts regions of interest at different scales into training patches or volumes. Task-related Joint-embedding Pre-training jointly reconstructs task-specific degradations to learn their interrelations, rather than relying on masked image modelling. Orochi combines Mamba blocks for linear-complexity long-range modelling with a hierarchical, patch-merging structure inspired by Swin-Transformer.

A three-tier post-training framework supports full fine-tuning, replacement-head fine-tuning, and lightweight depth-wise separable convolution tuning. The authors report that the lightest option achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art specialist models while reducing training and inference costs. Orochi is intended to provide efficient, unified biomedical image-processing functionality suitable for platforms such as ImageJ and napari.

The invention describes an automated storage, retrieval, and processing system that moves selected storage bins by controlled conveyors to processing stations. A programmable robotic device travels along a gantry, uses perception and an end effector to select, grasp, and transfer objects into linearly arranged destination bins according to a manifest. The system tracks bin identities and locations, supports returning partially processed bins, and removes completed or empty bins using conveyors or displacement mechanisms. Perception-based grasp selection evaluates object visibility, flat surfaces, surface normals, barcodes, and prior grasp outcomes, with machine learning used to improve selections. Embodiments may include gravity-fed conveyors, standardized box-tray assemblies, multiple storage rows, and parallel processing stations under centralized computer control.

The North Carolina Court of Appeals vacated a preliminary injunction barring Paul Alton Vaughn from operating a used car lot allegedly violating Knightdale’s zoning ordinance. Although the interlocutory appeal was reviewable because the injunction affected Vaughn’s substantial right to operate his business, Knightdale failed to prove irreparable harm. Its verified complaint was the only evidence presented and contained only conclusory assertions that the violation impeded enforcement of zoning goals. A preliminary injunction requires a likelihood of success and specific facts showing probable substantial, irreparable injury or necessity to protect rights during litigation. Municipal authority to enforce ordinances through injunctions does not eliminate Rule 65’s evidentiary requirements, and the availability of injunction as an ultimate remedy does not establish entitlement to preliminary relief. Judges Phillips and Parker concurred.

Japan urged Korea to modernize its government, education, laws, finances, agriculture, and commerce to preserve independence and strengthen relations between the two countries. Korean minister Ye Sung Soo subsequently asked the United States to help resolve the crisis after Japan refused to withdraw its troops and pressed for political reforms. With both Chinese and Japanese forces remaining in Korea, he requested international efforts to prevent conflict and secure their rapid withdrawal.

The swinging gate is an unconventional special-teams formation, typically used for two-point conversions, that lets an offense quickly run or pass against an unprepared defense or shift into a standard kicking formation. Kicking personnel remain on the field, with linemen detached to one side and the kicker eligible as a receiver. Common plays include a side snap to a runner behind the offensive line and a quick screen pass to the formation’s opposite side.

The formation aims to exploit defensive confusion and steal extra points, often after a team’s first touchdown. It is uncommon after NFL touchdowns because extra points are snapped from the 15-yard line, eliminating a practical kicking threat from the formation.

Defenses should match personnel rather than merely numbers, placing linemen and linebackers against blockers and athletic defenders in open spaces. Against heavy or balanced versions, safeties protect the alleys near the snapper, while cornerbacks prioritize pass coverage and assist against runs after confirming the play.

U.S. margin debt reached a record $665.7 billion in January, fell to $645.1 billion in February, and remained nearly unchanged in March. FINRA warned that investors may underestimate margin risks, including forced portfolio liquidations during falling markets. Margin debt amplifies gains by creating buying liquidity and accelerates declines through forced selling. Although it remained 55% above its July 2007 peak, its 12-month growth slowed substantially by March. Previous major margin-debt spikes preceded crashes, but the passage suggests the current correction could unfold gradually because of slow Federal Reserve tightening and abundant market liquidity.

Secondary endpoints assess ≥20 mg/dL plasma glucose increases within 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes using actual sampling times. Patients receiving rescue IV glucose before recovery are nonresponders.
