The statistical analysis plan defines adverse-event causality as not related, unlikely, possible, or probable; possible, probable, and unresolved missing assessments are analyzed as related. Severity is mild, moderate, or severe, with missing severity retained. Adverse events are summarized by treatment-emergent status, special interest, injection-site reaction, relationship, seriousness, death, MedDRA system organ class, preferred term, and severity. Patients are counted once per category, while total events are also reported.

Laboratory parameters are summarized by treatment, visit, reference-range status, and change from screening to follow-up. Hematology, biochemistry, coagulation, urinalysis, pregnancy tests, alcohol tests, vital signs, physical examinations, and ECGs are tabulated or listed as specified. QTcF summaries include values above 450, 480, and 500 ms and postbaseline increases above 30 and 60 ms.

Immunogenicity is analyzed descriptively without statistical tests. Overall ADA incidence combines treatment-induced ADA and treatment-boosted ADA, defined as a fivefold or greater post-dose titer increase, among evaluable patients with reportable post-dose samples.

Efficacy outputs include plasma glucose recovery analyses, Kaplan–Meier curves, sensitivity analyses concerning rescue intravenous glucose, recovery at 10–30 minutes, glucose changes, and pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic summaries and figures.

Missing or incomplete dates are handled conservatively, generally classifying uncertain adverse events as treatment-emergent. Standard formulas cover durations, unit conversions, BMI, and change from baseline.

Appendices specify table, figure, and listing formats; rounding, sorting, source documentation, SAS programming standards, validation, log and output review, dataset checks, patient spot-checks, figure verification, and retention of quality-control records. Protocol changes include rewording the primary efficacy analysis, adding sensitivity and supportive analyses, and revising secondary efficacy timing terminology.

Football formation terminology varies among coaches, but generic names describe how offensive players align. Basic formations include the run-oriented I formation, split backs, and balanced run-pass Twins alignments. Modern spread offenses commonly use Ace, Trips, Empty, Quads, and Bunch formations to distribute receivers, create favorable matchups, and challenge defensive coverage while retaining running options.

Shotgun and Pistol describe backfield alignments rather than all eleven players. In shotgun, the quarterback receives an airborne snap several yards behind center; in Pistol, the running back aligns directly behind the quarterback, supporting downhill runs while preserving shotgun passing advantages. Single Back generally describes one running back behind a quarterback under center.

Older formations remain more common at lower levels. The Wishbone, Flexbone, Double Wing, T, Wing-T, Power I, and Single Wing emphasize rushing, misdirection, option plays, additional blockers, and play-action opportunities. Some are also used near the goal line.

Gadget formations create unfamiliar defensive problems. The Wildcat uses a non-quarterback taking the snap and often an unbalanced line. Emory and Henry spreads players into separate groups across the field. The Swinging Gate is generally used for two-point attempts after touchdowns. Unbalanced formations place four or more ineligible players on one side of the center, strengthening one side of the running game and potentially confusing defenses.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture introduces hybrid rendering, combining rasterization with ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, and ambient occlusion. Dedicated RT Cores accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection tests, while denoising reduces required rays. Turing delivers over 10 Giga Rays per second and approximately tenfold faster ray tracing than Pascal.

Turing Tensor Cores support NVIDIA NGX, a deep-learning stack for graphics features including DLSS, inpainting, slow motion, and super-resolution. DLSS is trained against 64-times supersampled reference images and provides image quality comparable to temporal anti-aliasing with less shading work.

Other architectural features include Mesh Shading to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks; Variable Rate Shading for content-, motion-, and gaze-based shading optimization; Texture Space Shading to reuse shading results; and Multi-View Rendering for efficient rendering from multiple viewpoints. Turing also supports improved resource binding, VirtualLink connectivity, and accelerated ray-traced audio for virtual reality.

The TU104 GPU includes up to 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, while TU106 includes 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores. Tesla T4 uses TU104 with 2,560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores. NVIDIA defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based metric combining weighted Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations.

Ray tracing casts rays through image pixels into a scene, using surface intersections to calculate lighting and color. BVH structures reduce intersection tests, while refitting updates existing structures efficiently. Together, hybrid rendering, BVH acceleration, denoising, and RT Cores enable real-time ray-traced effects on a single Turing GPU.

Gold remained steady in New Delhi at Rs 28,300 per 10 grams amid scattered jeweller demand and closed global markets. Silver fell Rs 100 to Rs 39,300 per kg, while February gold futures rose 0.30 percent.

Studies link regular volunteering among adults over 50 to lower risk of high blood pressure, reduced stress, loneliness and depression, and improved cognitive health. Virginia Cooperative Extension will offer a five-week, 30-hour Master Food Volunteer training beginning April 18 at Brambleton Center. The $90 fee includes materials and lunches; need-based scholarships are available. Applications are due April 3 through Kim Butterfield at 540-772-7524.

SEV-TIO lets SEV-SNP guests bind trusted passthrough devices into private address space. Guest or VMPL0 firmware configures device information, validates reports, and sets up MMIO and IOMMU. TIO requests include unencrypted PCI, MMIO, and TDISP status data; optional shared contiguous pages return measurements, certificates, and attestation reports, with nonce-based freshness support.

Secure AVIC uses a private APIC backing page per vCPU, which guests can register or unregister. Termination requests provide reason codes and optional unsupported-feature information, while unsupported non-automatic exits use the “Unsupported Event” code.

SEV-ES guests identify support through hypervisor-provided CPUID properties. Because measured and encrypted vCPU registers cannot normally be changed, AP booting requires predefined initial state, reset-hold protocols, and an AP jump table. The SEV-SNP AP Creation feature instead allows guests to create or update AP VMSA pages, supports restricted injection, simplifies AP control, and enables vCPU hotplug.

For NMIs, the hypervisor intercepts #DB rather than IRET and waits for an “NMI Complete” message before injecting another NMI. Hardware debug-register virtualization may save and restore state through the VMSA; otherwise, DR7 accesses are intercepted and emulated. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

With SNP Restricted Injection, host notifications use a shared #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields. PendingEvent represents interrupt vectors, NMIs, machine checks, and signal suppression. The guest configures the page through VMGEXIT and accesses it unencrypted. The host emulates APIC ready, acknowledgement, in-service, priority, and EOI behavior, signals #HV when needed, and supports implicit EOIs through NoEoiRequired. Guests atomically retrieve and clear pending events, validate vectors, dispatch maskable and non-maskable events appropriately, and perform implicit or explicit EOIs. HLT handling uses disabled interrupts and post-HLT examination of doorbell state to avoid missed events. Non-cooperative behavior can cause denial of service but should not compromise host integrity or guest state.
Vincent Bolloré expects sole control of Vivendi after its April 25 shareholder meeting. His 20.65% stake provides 29% of voting rights. The European Commission has until April 24 to approve.

Weak U.S. employment data and substantial downward revisions increased expectations of dovish Federal Reserve policy, while President Trump’s firing of the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ CEO and Fed board member Adriana Kugler’s resignation added uncertainty.

BTC/USD found support near 112,000 after declining with equities. A break above 117,260 could signal renewed gains, while failure to hold 110,750 may expose 105,770–107,500. Economic, tariff and Federal Reserve independence concerns remain risks.

Duke extended men’s basketball coach Jon Scheyer’s contract through the 2030-31 season, adding two years to his previous deal. Scheyer has won 89 games in three seasons, reaching the 2024 Elite Eight and last season’s Final Four while winning both 2024-25 ACC titles. Duke has secured three No. 1 recruiting classes in four cycles and sent nine players to the NBA during his tenure. Despite losing all five starters to the NBA, Duke is expected to begin the season ranked in the top 10.

Mick Schumacher says he is not ready for Formula One and must first prove himself in European Formula 3. After failing to win a Formula 4 title, he aims to improve consistency, learn, and lead the rookie rankings. He has no fixed F1 plan but appreciates interest from Mercedes and Ferrari and is adapting to media attention.

The invention concerns phase-stable colloidal polysaccharide suspensions containing biotechnologically produced, never-dried α(1→3)-glucan. A moist press cake containing 4–80% polysaccharide solids is diluted to a suspension concentration of 0.01–50% and mechanically comminuted using a low-shear dispersing unit such as an Ultraturrax mixer or colloid mill. Chemical or enzymatic pretreatment, dissolution, precipitation, high pressure, and high shear are unnecessary, reducing energy use and avoiding solvent residues. Optional high-pressure homogenization can slightly improve homogeneity.

The glucan preferably constitutes 80–100% of the polysaccharide and has a weight-average degree of polymerization of 200–2,000. Other polysaccharides and additives may be incorporated. The resulting nonfibrillar, three-dimensional networks are phase-stable, shear-thinning, water-binding, thickening, and film-forming. Potential applications include paper and packaging coatings, barrier layers, molded bodies, viscosity modification, binders, nonwovens, flushable wipes, food, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics.

Suspensions may be dried by spray drying, freeze drying, or supercritical drying to produce powders, hybrid particles, or aerogels. Spacers can reduce hydrogen bonding and improve redispersibility.

Experiments showed that never-dried glucan formed uniform, stable suspensions using low-shear equipment, including pilot-scale colloid milling. Additional high-pressure homogenization produced little viscosity change. In contrast, previously dried linear or branched glucans showed phase separation, low water retention, and little viscosity increase despite repeated homogenization. Increasing solids concentration increased viscosity and reduced water retention. The suspensions produced continuous, adherent films on glass and polyester and displayed dense film structures and three-dimensional spongy networks. Stable suspensions containing up to 10% glucan and spray-dried particles in the micrometer range were also demonstrated.

Virgin Galactic’s VSS Unity completed its second rocket-powered test flight from Mojave Air and Space Port on May 29, 2018. Its motor fired for 31 seconds, reaching supersonic speed and 114,500 feet—above April’s 84,271 feet—before gliding to a landing. The flight advanced testing toward commercial space tourism operations.

The passage specifies mechanical, material, marking, actuation, durability, inspection, and electrical requirements for Socket 940 and its 940-pin ceramic µPGA package. The socket supports lidded and lidless packages; the lidless package thickness is at least 2.20 mm. Its LCP base and cover have a UL 94 V-0 rating, and the package-seating plane and cover require flatness below 0.25 mm. A removable overlay supports vacuum pick-and-place without outgassing or residue.

Required markings include “SOCKET 940,” lever lock directions, package pin A01 orientation, the supplier’s UL symbol, and lot traceability. Contacts use high-strength copper alloy, with at least 1.27 µm nickel plating and 0.76 µm gold on mating areas. Tin-lead solder balls are 0.76 mm in diameter, require 0.20 mm coplanarity, and mount to 0.64 mm PCB pads.

A stainless-steel lever enables tool-free actuation. Open-position insertion and extraction forces must not exceed 2 kgf; lever force must remain below 3.6 kgf, and pin displacement below 1.0 mm. The socket must retain integrity after 50 actuation cycles and have no specified visual defects.

Each contact is rated for 1.5 A with under 30°C temperature rise. Initial and final resistance must not exceed 25 mΩ per contact. Requirements also include inductance below 4 nH, capacitance below 1 pF, differential impedance of 100 Ω ±10%, signal skew below 10 ps plus measurement error, dielectric withstand of at least 650 Vac, and insulation resistance of at least 1000 MΩ.

Newly elected State Quad senators and some resident assistants say UAlbany students need clearer information about asbestos than existing door notices and housing documents provide. Residential Life says low-crystallite asbestos has been present in some dorm ceiling insulation for decades and is harmful through long-term exposure when disturbed; officials report no recent ceiling disturbances. Some students have mistaken falling paint for asbestos debris.

Facilities Management proposed adding asbestos FAQs to the university website. Older, unrenovated campus buildings contain asbestos, while some quads have undergone or are scheduled for abatement; State Quad renovations are not yet planned.

Anonymous RAs alleged housing directors discouraged asbestos discussions to avoid panic, which Residential Life denied. Officials said RAs should refer questions to supervisors because they lack professional expertise, while some RAs advocated earlier, more prominent education for residents.

The Charlottesville attack renewed questions about how educators should confront racism and white supremacy. Derek Weimer, who taught suspect James Alex Fields Jr., said Fields was interested in Hitler and white supremacy and that he felt he had failed to redirect him. Facing History and Ourselves encourages teachers to examine historical moral choices and use current events as teachable moments. Suggested classroom resources include identity charts, diverse books, age-appropriate lessons on bias and social justice, historical materials about Charlottesville and Confederate monuments, and curricula addressing racism, civil rights, stereotyping, bullying, trauma and media literacy. Educators also created the #CharlottesvilleCurriculum hashtag to share responsive teaching resources.

Strix reported mixed first-half 2025 results. Billi maintained double-digit growth, supported by new products and geographic expansion. Management planned to provide further business details before a Q&A session.

The parties’ 2003 custody agreement gave the father sole custody of their two daughters, with maternal visitation subject to the children’s wishes, while requiring him to foster their relationship with the mother. In 2004, the father moved the daughters to Florida without informing the mother and repeatedly obstructed communication and visitation. Family Court found multiple intentional violations of the custody order but initially declined to change custody.

After prolonged proceedings, Family Court found that the father had alienated the daughters from their mother and that this constituted changed circumstances. Nevertheless, it denied the mother custody, continued visitation subject to the children’s wishes, granted unrestricted remote communication, and suspended the mother’s child support payments.

The appellate court affirmed the denial of custody of the younger daughter because the limited record did not establish that a change was in her best interests. However, it held that visitation should not depend on the 15-year-old daughter’s wishes because she appeared subject to undue influence and likely would benefit from a relationship with her mother and younger siblings. The matter was remitted for immediate consideration of court-ordered visitation based on updated hearings. The suspension of child support was affirmed.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 26, 2020 reported net sales of $111.4 billion, up 21% year over year, and net income of $28.8 billion, up from $22.2 billion. Diluted earnings per share rose to $1.68. Sales increased across all product categories and geographic segments, led by 57% growth in Greater China and 41% growth in iPad sales. Gross margin was 39.8%.

Apple generated $38.8 billion in operating cash flow, repurchased $24.0 billion of stock, and paid $3.6 billion in dividends and equivalents. At quarter-end, it held $195.6 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, had $107.0 billion in term debt, and reported total assets of $354.1 billion and shareholders’ equity of $66.2 billion.

The quarter included launches of the iPhone 12 lineup, M1-powered Macs, iPad Air, AirPods Max, HomePod mini and Apple Fitness+. COVID-19 continued affecting stores, offices and operations. Apple also disclosed ongoing tax, competition and patent proceedings, supply-source concentrations, and $8.1 billion in long-term unconditional purchase obligations.

SPARK, a three-year autism research study, aims to test families of 50,000 people with autism spectrum disorder to identify genetic markers and improve understanding of inherited and newly occurring traits. Unlike studies requiring intact biological families, SPARK accepts any family structure. Participants can submit at-home cheek swabs arranged online or attend assisted testing events, and each family receives a $50 gift card. More than 25,000 people with autism and their families were participating by early April. Rush University Medical Center oversees the Chicago-area effort. Researchers may group and re-contact participants with particular chromosomal abnormalities to study treatment effectiveness. Secure data will also be available to unaffiliated researchers. Although the findings could reveal prenatal indicators or individual genetic predispositions, organizers emphasize that the study seeks understanding, not prevention.

Microsoft reported $443 million in accrued legal liabilities and approximately $1.6 billion of additional reasonably possible adverse outcomes. Deloitte’s review found no material modifications necessary for the interim financial statements to conform with U.S. GAAP.

This systematic literature review examined definitions, effects, and influencing factors of digital leadership in education. Following PRISMA guidelines, researchers searched Scopus, Web of Science, and EBSCO and conducted citation searches, selecting 39 empirical English-language articles.

Only 11 studies defined digital leadership, often using related terms such as technology leadership and e-leadership. Existing definitions commonly emphasized technology integration but overlooked interaction, followers, educational context, organizational change, or environmental factors. The review characterizes digital leadership as a dynamic, evolving practice that integrates technology, fosters supportive organizational culture, and adapts to technological, organizational, and environmental changes.

Twenty-eight studies addressed effects. Most focused on teachers, particularly technology integration, ICT competence, professional development, engagement, innovation, and job satisfaction. School-level effects included improved administration, teaching quality, digital transformation, resource management, and digital culture. Only one study examined student academic performance, leaving effects on creativity, digital literacy, lifelong learning, and digital security underexplored.

Ten studies analyzed influencing factors. Internal factors included age, gender, technology use, professional and administrative experience, qualifications, digital literacy, technology acceptance, self-efficacy, and change-management skills. External factors included infrastructure, school culture, technical supervision, policies, training programs, and the COVID-19 pandemic. Future research should examine these interacting factors, followers’ participation, organizational culture, multicultural teams, lifelong learning, and data security.

The author recommends using existing private channels, especially Shultz-Gromyko exchanges, to test Soviet intentions before intensifying bilateral relations. With little room for major compromise on arms control or regional issues, expanded dialogue could create false expectations, encourage concessions, and weaken firm U.S. positions. The author opposes proposed initiatives on Afghanistan, Soviet participation in Namibia/Angola discussions, and restoring the Joint Commercial Commission, favoring private trade and engagement through frontline African states. Dialogue should cover Soviet internal conduct, human rights, and arms control, with INF negotiations serving as a test of Soviet willingness to accept reductions, equality, verification, and compliance. Broad dialogue at all governmental levels and summitry would primarily benefit Moscow unless the Soviets first demonstrate a major reduction of threats. A subsequent memorandum agrees that Soviet leadership changes may intensify challenges to U.S. interests but raises questions about significantly expanding U.S.-Soviet dialogue.

Fitch assigned expected ‘BB(EXP)’ ratings to Telenet subsidiaries’ new senior secured Term Loans AH and AI, subject to final documentation. Secured debt is rated one notch above Telenet’s issuer rating, with an ‘RR2’ recovery rating.

Constraints include Telenet’s relatively high leverage target. Fitch assumes stable 2017 revenue, mid-single-digit EBITDA growth and capital expenditure near 24% of sales. Downgrade risks include stronger competition, greater market-share or EBITDA losses, FFO-adjusted net leverage consistently above 5.25x, fixed-charge coverage below 2.5x, or higher leverage targets. An upgrade is unlikely without a more conservative financial policy. Liquidity is supported by EUR120 million of internal cash flow, EUR400 million of undrawn facilities and no debt maturity before 2022.

The Passing Game is an unstructured, team-oriented basketball offense based on purposeful movement, passing, off-ball screens, spacing, cuts, and rebounding rather than fixed plays. It involves all five players, can use multiple alignments, and is effective against person-to-person and zone defenses. Its continuous, unpredictable motion can control tempo, create open shots, and make scouting difficult, but selfish play, poor defensive reads, impatience, weak off-ball skills, and offensive rebounding can disrupt it.

Success requires accurate passing, 12–15-foot spacing, shot discipline, triple-threat positioning, limited dribbling, strong screening, purposeful cuts, post play, offensive rebounding, and reading defensive reactions. Players should back cut against overplay, attack mismatches, meet passes, use screens correctly, and select shots within their abilities.

Variations include three-player high/low, four-out single or rotating post, and five-player motion offenses. Screen options include popping, replacing, slipping, rolling, curling, fading, and back cutting. Against zones, teams should pass sharply, use fakes and skip passes, attack gaps and the weak side, penetrate selectively, push in transition, and pursue rebounds.

The system requires unselfish players and a coaching commitment to teaching fundamentals while accepting less direct control. Its patience and constant motion can pressure opponents mentally and physically, expose weak defenders, create backdoor opportunities, and produce a stable offense.

TV presenter Keith Chegwin died aged 60 at home on December 11 after a long battle with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), surrounded by his wife Maria, daughter Rose and son Ted. His family thanked Severn Hospice and requested privacy. IPF progressively scars and stiffens the lungs, reducing their ability to take in oxygen. About 6,000 people are diagnosed annually in the UK, mostly men and people over 70. Possible contributing factors include acid reflux, viruses and exposure to workplace dust. Symptoms include breathlessness, persistent coughing, fatigue, and clubbing of the fingers and toes.

College football targeting occurs when a player aims at an opponent with forcible contact beyond a legal tackle, block or play on the ball, particularly against a defenseless player. The NCAA penalty is 15 yards and automatic disqualification. First-half fouls remove the player for the rest of the game; second-half fouls also trigger a first-half suspension for the next game. Three targeting fouls in one season result in a one-game suspension, with another suspension for each additional foul.

Unlike the NCAA, the NFL classifies similar contact as unnecessary roughness against a defenseless player and does not require automatic disqualification unless the action is flagrant.

The NCAA adopted targeting in 2008 for player safety. Automatic disqualification and related suspensions were added in 2013, while video review became mandatory in 2019. Controversial incidents involving Texas-Arizona State and Clemson-Ohio State illustrated ongoing uncertainty over enforcement.

The player said readiness depends on the coach, praised the team’s play despite tough calls, and expected a fast, skilled opponent. The team focused on each shift and the game at hand, came back successfully, and remains committed to finding different ways to win without giving up.

Facebook shares fell 6.8%, their largest percentage decline in four years, erasing nearly $40 billion in market value amid U.S. and U.K. scrutiny over Cambridge Analytica’s unauthorized retention of user data. Analysts viewed the episode as a significant public-relations and regulatory risk but differed on its business impact. Wells Fargo and GBH Insights remained bullish, citing privacy upgrades and potential investments in security, screening and artificial intelligence. Pivotal Research expected little near-term advertiser impact but warned of systemic and regulatory risks, while Stifel said necessary security changes could reduce engagement and monetization. The controversy also weighed on Twitter, Snap, Alphabet and broader technology indexes, with the Nasdaq falling 1.8%.

Adm. Harry Harris, originally nominated as U.S. ambassador to Australia, will instead become ambassador to South Korea because of challenges on the Korean Peninsula. Australia has lacked a U.S. ambassador since September 2016, with Jim Caruso serving as chargé d’affaires. Foreign Minister Julie Bishop said Washington would prioritize a replacement, while Australian commentators and politicians expressed concern about the prolonged vacancy, with some calling it evidence of Australia’s low priority or the Trump administration’s ad hoc decision-making.

The author describes founding a successful supplement company as a teenager and later launching the nootropic Excelerol. In 2010, he listed Excelerol on Amazon, solicited honest reviews from subscribers, and quickly gained reviews and sales without advertising. Although Amazon initially generated new customers and revenue, policy changes increasingly favored buyers, while sellers faced product restrictions, account suspensions, limited support, and loss of control over customer relationships and listings. These risks even created a market for suspension insurance. After five years learning to navigate Amazon’s marketplace, the author formed a team that advises startups and Fortune 500 companies on Amazon strategy.

In 2016, the Rams traded six draft picks to Tennessee, including two first-rounders, for the No. 1 pick and two later selections. Los Angeles drafted quarterback Jared Goff, who rebounded from a difficult rookie season to make the 2017 Pro Bowl. Subsequent moves also yielded Pro Bowl return specialist Pharoh Cooper, Temarrick Hemingway and Mike Thomas.

The Titans converted the Rams’ picks through additional trades into Corey Davis, Jack Conklin, Austin Johnson, Derrick Henry, Jonnu Smith, LeShaun Sims and Kalan Reed. Conklin earned All-Pro honors, while Henry, Davis and Smith became starters or prospective key contributors.

The completed trade has no definitive winner: the Rams obtained a potential franchise quarterback and two Pro Bowlers, while Tennessee gained greater depth and four starters. The passage gives Los Angeles a slight edge based on Goff’s development and its earlier division title, but notes that Tennessee’s ultimate return depends on the health and performance of players including Davis, Conklin and Henry.

The Vintage Optical Shop, a U.S. online retailer of authentic vintage eyewear from the 1850s to the 1980s, offers new email subscribers a one-time $20 coupon for their next purchase. Subscribers also receive updates about arrivals, sales, specials, and coupons. Its inventory includes cat-eye eyewear, Pince Nez and Windsor glasses, safety goggles, and John Lennon glasses. Customers can subscribe, browse products, review FAQs, or submit queries at vintageopticalshop.com.

Will Ma analyzes a deep-stacked cash-game hand using combinatorial range analysis. Holding eight-seven suited, the player calls preflop, calls bets on a ten-eight-six flop and queen turn, then bluffs after an ace river and an opponent’s check. Ma explains calling versus raising, bet sizing, polarized river ranges, implied odds, position, showdown value, and the value of arranging bets to avoid difficult all-in decisions. By reconstructing the opponent’s range across each action and counting possible card combinations, he concludes the river bluff is highly profitable because the opponent folds more than half the time and checking wins infrequently.

Ma then discusses why poker can offer substantial money: widespread overconfidence, gambling and emotional-control problems, the game’s rapid strategic evolution, and difficulty avoiding results-oriented thinking. He emphasizes honest assessment of ability, controlling tilt, accepting variance, and focusing on decision quality rather than short-term outcomes. He notes that confidence is necessary for risk-taking but must be balanced against overconfidence.

For further study, Ma recommends online resources such as CardRunners, Two Plus Two forums, and Twitch streams, while noting that poker books can quickly become outdated. Suggested books include *Small Stakes Hold ’em*, *Harrington on Hold ’em*, *Kill Phil/Kill Everyone*, *Every Hand Revealed*, *The Mathematics of Poker*, and *Building a Bankroll*.

During questions, Ma recommends the MIT Poker Club for continued play, taking breaks during severe downswings, seeking candid feedback from skilled friends, and generally playing tightly against recreational casino players. He says poker remains worthwhile for those who enjoy its mathematics and decision-making, even when money is not the primary motivation.

The speaker celebrates a team-focused championship victory over a strong opponent, crediting veteran leaders, coaches, scouts, ownership, and teammates. He highlights Patrick Roy’s mentorship and calls him the best goalie of all time. Winning for Ray Bourque was especially meaningful, and seeing Joe Sakic hand Bourque the Cup was emotional. He also expresses pride in bringing Denver a local championship and looks forward to celebrating with family and friends.

President Trump accused major homebuilders of withholding 2 million empty lots and urged Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to spur construction. Libertarian housing scholar Bryan Caplan rejected the comparison to OPEC, arguing that restrictive zoning, lengthy approvals, and local opposition—not builder collusion or financing—are the main barriers to housing supply. Industry data show 64% of single-family builders report a shortage of buildable lots, constraining entry-level construction and increasing prices. Caplan said financing incentives may boost building in lightly regulated markets such as Texas but would have little effect in cities like San Francisco without zoning reform. He welcomed Trump’s attention to the housing shortage but said progress requires confronting regulatory restrictions rather than blaming builders.

Emma Stone agreed to become Louis Vuitton’s face for two years in a deal reportedly worth $6 million to $10 million. Ryan Gosling declined similar offers. Stone also described enjoying the weightlifting and protein-heavy training used to portray Billie Jean King in “Battle of the Sexes.”

The study examines coarsening of phase-separated DNA nanostar droplets in a three-dimensional self-stirring fluid composed of extensile microtubule bundles and ATP-powered kinesin motors. Active flows advect droplets and accelerate collision-driven coalescence relative to passive Brownian diffusion, while Ostwald ripening remains comparatively slow.

Active and passive droplets showed similar mean-radius growth exponents, βR≈1/3, but different droplet-number exponents: γN≈−1.65 for active fluids and −0.89 for passive fluids. Passive coarsening remained self-similar, whereas active systems increasingly contained many small droplets alongside a few exceptionally large ones. These exponents were insensitive to ATP concentration and confinement-controlled active length scale.

Active droplets moved ballistically over short times and diffusively over longer times. Their effective diffusivity was independent of droplet size and determined by active-flow speed and velocity-correlation length, unlike passive droplets governed by the Stokes–Einstein–Sutherland relation.

Hydrodynamic and particle simulations reproduced the experiments. Simulations of self-propelled, diffusive, subdiffusive, and superdiffusive droplets showed that coarsening behavior depends on collision dynamics rather than whether motility is active or passive. The collision-kernel scaling exponent k emerged as the unifying control parameter, with k=3−(m+2)/α, where m describes size-dependent diffusivity and α the anomalous-diffusion exponent. Positive k favors collisions between large droplets, causing broadening size distributions, loss of self-similarity, and a nonlinear relationship between βR and γN.

The framework may apply to biological condensates and other volume-conserving aggregation processes. Open questions include finite-size effects, behavior when droplets approach or exceed the active length scale, shear effects, and the possible role of Ostwald ripening in systems with broad droplet-size distributions.

A Pepperdine student recounts studying abroad in Buenos Aires and initially worrying about facing racism and discrimination. Instead, he experienced hospitality from police, strangers and Argentine friends, and felt appreciated rather than singled out because of his ethnicity. Although people of African descent were uncommon in the city, he formed immediate bonds when meeting them. Sprint and The Sprint Foundation will provide free devices and wireless service to 180,000 low-income students in over 1,300 schools across 32 states during the first year of the five-year 1Million Project. Researchers analyzed whole-blood RNA sequencing from 390 rare-disease participants and familial controls using FRASER and FRASER2 to identify transcriptome-wide splicing outliers. Forty individuals had excess outliers by at least one metric. Outlier genes were enriched for OMIM disease genes and genes associated with developmental delay and intellectual disability, although batch effects influenced some measurements.

Focusing on intron retention in minor intron-containing genes identified five individuals with a distinct minor-spliceosome signature. Four had rare biallelic pathogenic or likely pathogenic RNU4ATAC variants, compatible phenotypes, and substantially more affected genes than the rest of the cohort, supporting diagnoses of RNU4atac-opathy. The fifth had rare compound heterozygous RNU6ATAC variants, similar clinical features, and extensive overlap in affected genes with the RNU4ATAC cases. RNU6ATAC was therefore proposed as a candidate disease gene, but additional cases and functional evidence are required.

Larger sample sets increased detection sensitivity, while FRASER2 detected all five minor spliceopathy cases with lower specificity. The study concludes that biologically coherent, transcriptome-wide splicing patterns can aid rare-disease diagnosis, variant interpretation, and discovery of candidate gene-disease relationships rather than being dismissed solely as technical noise.

NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU introduces major compute, memory, virtualization, interconnect, and programmability improvements over V100. SECDED ECC protects HBM2, L2 and L1 caches, and register files. Its 40 MB L2 cache is 6.7 times larger than V100’s, provides 2.3 times the read bandwidth, supports programmable residency controls, and uses compression to improve DRAM and L2 bandwidth by up to fourfold and effective L2 capacity by up to twofold. The 1555 GB/s HBM2 subsystem supplies over 1.7 times V100’s bandwidth.

A100 has 108 SMs and third-generation Tensor Cores supporting larger operations, increased thread-level data sharing, fewer instructions and register accesses, and mixed-precision performance up to 16 times standard FP32 FMA. Asynchronous global-to-shared memory copies, asynchronous barriers, and 164 KB maximum shared memory per SM improve data movement and pipeline efficiency. CUDA 11 exposes these features alongside task-graph acceleration, cache-residency controls, cooperative groups, sparsity, and MIG management.

Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) can partition one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances, each with dedicated compute and memory-system resources. This provides predictable throughput, latency, quality of service, fault isolation, and error containment for VMs, containers, processes, and multiple tenants. GPU Instances consist of GPU slices containing a Sys Pipe, GPC, L2 slice group, and frame-buffer allocation, and may be subdivided into Compute Instances. MIG supports Linux, containers, Volta-style MPS, independent context switching, and migration of virtual GPUs between compatible instances.

Third-generation NVLink doubles the signal-pair data rate to 50 Gbit/s and gives A100 twelve links totaling 600 GB/s, compared with V100’s six links and 300 GB/s. It adds stronger error detection and recovery, non-posted writes, and improved small-transfer efficiency. PCIe Gen 4 supplies 31.5 GB/s per direction over x16 and supports SR-IOV. A100 also adds enhanced fault attribution and containment, a five-core NVJPG engine, an optical-flow and stereo-disparity accelerator, five NVDEC units, and higher atomic-operation throughput.

A100’s structured 2:4 sparsity balances work while reducing computation and memory traffic, with evaluations reporting virtually no accuracy loss across tested networks. The architecture targets strong scaling for deep learning by accelerating fixed-size workloads and reducing execution, launch, synchronization, and memory overheads.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs, six NVSwitches, 4.8 TB/s aggregate bidirectional interconnect bandwidth, up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, and eight 200 Gb/s InfiniBand adapters in a 6U system. MIG can expose up to 56 isolated accelerators per DGX A100. Its software stack includes CUDA 11, the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC containers and registries, deep-learning frameworks, TensorRT, RAPIDS, and HPC tools, and supports scaling from individual workloads to large clusters.

AGESA is an AMD BIOS procedure library supporting multiple products. The document defines its host-wrapper interfaces, boot-time entry points, configuration structures, build methods, execution requirements, error reporting, UEFI integration, and platform customization.

Public entry points use the “Amd” prefix, while host call-outs use “Agesa.” The interface is intended to remain stable across processor generations. Initializer functions allocate and populate parameter structures with defaults; the host supplies required values, optionally changes others, calls the main function, checks status, and releases storage. Errors are reported through status codes and a 16-entry event log.

AGESA supports source integration and separately built binary modules. Binary images contain identifying headers, module information, dispatcher offsets, relocation data, size, and checksum. The host locates and relocates the image, creates standard headers, and invokes functions through a bridge and dispatcher. Call-outs return to host services through a router. Binary execution requires 32-bit protected flat-address mode, identity mapping if paging is enabled, and a valid stack.

Platform build options reside primarily in `<Plat>Options.c`. Technology code and generated default tables are compiled separately, allowing selected procedures to be linked. Build controls support generic makefiles, UEFI descriptors, and vendor-specific formats. Integrated Debug Services macros can be compiled out entirely.

Boot entry points correspond to reset, recovery, initialization, OS boot, and suspend restoration stages. Hosts must use only published functions and must not alter cache controls during Cache-As-RAM operation. Stack services establish and remove pre-memory stacks; AArch64 systems with the Platform Security Processor instead use PSP-initialized DRAM.

UEFI support spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases. PEIMs coordinate processor, memory, and reset initialization and publish PPIs and memory information. DXE performs late initialization, creates system tables, and publishes a protocol for table access.

Service procedures create and release structures, read event logs, identify processors and memory locations, query PCI/APIC addresses and execution-cache size, retrieve DIMM data-eye results, and update MMIO mappings. Major initialization procedures perform reset-time processor setup, early processor and HyperTransport configuration, power-management setup, memory initialization, training, interleaving, ECC, UMA, voltage, and graphics-related configuration.

The article argues that mainstream climate education emphasizes scientific knowledge, technological solutions, sustainable development, and carbon reduction while neglecting colonial histories, Black and Indigenous knowledge systems, historical responsibility, and reparative justice. It critiques UN development frameworks and “green” solutions that can perpetuate extraction, dispossession, ecological destruction, and unequal power relations, particularly in the Global South.

Using Said’s contrapuntal reading, the authors examine dominant and marginalized narratives in climate education. They define “climate coloniality” as the continuing influence of colonial power structures, racial capitalism, unequal consumption, and extractive development on climate impacts, governance, and proposed solutions. Former colonies and marginalized communities often experience the greatest climate harms despite contributing least to greenhouse gas emissions. Technological responses such as lithium mining and carbon-offset land acquisition may reproduce colonial patterns.

The authors propose “decolonial educational ecologies” as an alternative. This approach centers historically marginalized knowledge, cosmologies, local contexts, and relationships between humans and more-than-human beings. It incorporates decolonial, anti-colonial, feminist, anti-racist, and anti-capitalist critiques while questioning Eurocentric universalism, anthropocentrism, modernization, limitless growth, and technological solutionism.

Decolonial educational ecologies encourage students to investigate whose knowledge is recognized, who sets agendas, and how extraction, exploitation, displacement, and ecological violence underpin modernity. They emphasize critical inquiry, distributive justice, reparations, restitution, and locally situated adaptation rather than universal solutions. The article concludes that climate education should challenge colonial hierarchies, recover marginalized histories and practices, and support alternative social and ecological relations without presenting decoloniality as a universal cure.

Public higher education funding remains shaped by historic discrimination and exclusion. Flagship universities often receive substantially more state funding per student than institutions serving larger shares of low-income, Black, Hispanic, Native American, and other marginalized students. Funding gaps persist because most states rely on “base plus” appropriations tied to previous budgets rather than formulas reflecting current institutional and student needs.

Historically, community colleges, HBCUs, and women’s colleges developed within systems that restricted access to elite institutions. These schools frequently received less support, and current funding practices continue aspects of that legacy. Flagships now educate only 16 percent of public university students but receive nearly 40 percent more state funding per student than other four-year institutions. Open-access universities, attended by many Pell-eligible and marginalized students, spend far less on education-related services than highly selective research universities.

The passage distinguishes equity—distributing available funds according to relative need—from adequacy—providing enough funding for institutions to fulfill their missions. Increasing overall appropriations without equitable distribution can widen existing disparities. Free college addresses student prices but not institutional resources, while outcomes-based funding may disadvantage underfunded institutions that lack the upfront resources needed to improve results.

Drawing on K–12 funding practices, the report proposes allocating funds according to student and institutional need and accounting for outside revenue such as tuition, endowments, and alumni donations. Education and student support funding should be separated from research, health care, and agricultural allocations. Equity reforms should precede adequacy efforts so future funding increases reach institutions with the greatest needs. The report concludes that systemic reform, rather than simply adding money to existing mechanisms, is necessary to create fairer educational opportunities.

The disclosure describes instruments, systems, and methods for drilling, cutting, or driving implants into tissue while measuring working-tool torque, force, power, energy, and depth in real time. A controller processes sensor signals and presents results through an integrated or external wired or wireless interface. Drilling or insertion energy may indicate regional tissue strength, bone density, screw pullout strength, and potential construct strength, including information relevant to osteoporosis and implant selection.

The instrument may include rotational and axial motors, interchangeable working tools, torque and axial-force sensors, and a guide harp that controls tool exposure and measures penetration depth. Multiaxis torque sensing can identify changes in tissue layers, cortical contact, and skiving, allowing tool redirection. A drop in power may indicate breakthrough and trigger an alert or automatically stop tool rotation or guide withdrawal, reducing inadvertent plunge and injury.

Real-time guidance may reduce reliance on depth gauges, trial-and-error implant sizing, repeated radiographs, fluoroscopy, and associated delays, costs, radiation, and complications. The instrument may also provide irrigation, automated alerts, tool identification and usage tracking, removable components for sterilization, and various electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, or manual drive options. User feedback can be graphical, numerical, auditory, visual, or tactile and may indicate torque, applied force, depth, energy, power, and whether operating pressure is appropriate.

Solution-processed laser diodes remain challenging because high current densities cause carrier imbalance, heating, and material degradation. The study reports a continuously electrically driven polariton laser based on a solution-grown CsPbBr3 microplate embedded in an optical microcavity and contacted by chemically inert single-walled carbon nanotube electrodes.

The initial metal-semiconductor-metal Schottky diode was converted into a rectifying p-i-n structure through electric-field-induced ionic redistribution. A two-stage cooling protocol spatially froze this structure at 8 K, improving balanced carrier injection and preventing continued junction propagation. Under forward bias, tunneling produced currents up to four orders of magnitude higher than in the unmodified cryogenic device.

Angularly and polarization-resolved electroluminescence measurements confirmed strongly coupled exciton-polariton modes. At a threshold current of 60 µA and 3.95 V, corresponding to approximately 2.8 kA cm−2, emission intensity increased by more than two orders of magnitude, accompanied by linewidth narrowing and energy blueshifts, indicating polariton lasing. The emission was spatially localized, and carrier densities remained about two orders of magnitude below the CsPbBr3 Mott density. Above threshold, emission saturation and additional blueshifts were attributed to Joule heating. The results demonstrate continuous direct electrical pumping of a solution-processed perovskite polariton laser diode.

Robert Epstein argues that the human brain does not operate like a computer: it does not store, retrieve, or process symbolic representations, memories, rules, images, algorithms, or programs. Humans are born with senses, reflexes, and learning mechanisms, and experiences change the brain in ways that enable later behavior without storing copies of those experiences.

The information-processing metaphor arose after computers were invented, following earlier metaphors that compared intelligence to spiritual, hydraulic, mechanical, electrical, and telegraphic systems. It became central to cognitive science through figures such as George Miller and John von Neumann and now dominates scientific and popular accounts of intelligence. Epstein calls its logic faulty because the fact that computers are intelligent information processors does not mean all intelligent entities process information.

A drawing exercise involving a dollar bill illustrates his claim: people reproduce it poorly without an exemplar despite repeated exposure. Epstein argues that prior experience changes the brain’s capacity to visualize or reproduce something but does not create a stored image. Recall is therefore less accurate than recognition, and learning reflects orderly neural change rather than information storage and retrieval.

Anti-representational researchers offer explanations of behavior without computation. For example, a baseball player may catch a fly ball by moving to maintain a constant visual relationship between the ball and surroundings, rather than calculating its trajectory through an internal model.

Epstein rejects predictions that minds could be uploaded to computers. Each brain changes uniquely according to its structure and life history, so even identical experiences affect individuals differently. A complete neural snapshot would be meaningless without the living body and possibly the person’s developmental and social history. He concludes that the information-processing metaphor has distorted neuroscience, encouraged unrealistic projects and promises, and should be abandoned in favor of studying humans as organisms.

The study examines whether papers that create structural “knowledge gaps” in scientific concept networks generate greater long-term impact than other conceptual recombinations. Using 34,363,623 journal and conference papers from Microsoft Academic Graph published between 1900 and 2020, the authors model level-3 research fields as concepts connected when they first co-occur. Persistent homology identifies new concept links that create topological holes, classifying papers as gap openers, non-gap openers with novel pairs, or non-gap openers without novel pairs.

Gap openers constitute 0.84% of papers, compared with more than 25% for non-gap openers with novel pairs and over 70% for papers without novel pairs. Their prevalence varies by discipline and declined after 1930. Gap-opening papers connect newer, less established concepts, cite fewer prior works, exhibit greater recombinational novelty, and more often use language associated with creation and innovation.

Regression analyses controlling for team size, references, year, and discipline show that gap openers are 1.58 times more likely than papers without novel pairs to rank among the top 1% most cited and score 1.4 percentage points higher in disruption percentile. Associations with Nobel-winning work are positive but statistically insignificant. Gap openers receive 6.11% fewer citations within five years but 31.39% more within twenty years, with their citation disadvantage turning positive after eight years. They also display stronger delayed-recognition patterns. Novel combinations that do not open gaps show smaller or no advantages.

Gap-opening papers are produced by teams that are smaller, younger, fresher, and more geographically proximate. The findings indicate that topologically significant knowledge gaps, rather than novelty alone, are associated with greater disruption, delayed recognition, and long-term scientific influence. The authors suggest that short-term evaluation metrics may undervalue such work and that computational gap detection could inform research funding and strategy.

The ambassador pattern separates application logic from communication concerns. Applications connect to localhost while an ambassador handles sharding, service discovery, brokering, or traffic splitting. Kubernetes examples use StatefulSets, Services, ConfigMaps, twemproxy, and nginx to implement sharded Redis or Memcached services and controlled experiments.

The adapter pattern converts heterogeneous application interfaces into standardized ones for monitoring, logging, and health checks. Examples include Prometheus exporters for Redis, fluentd plugins for normalizing Redis and Storm logs, and a separate MySQL health-check container. Separate adapters improve modularity, resource isolation, reuse, and maintainability without modifying third-party images.

Microservices divide applications into independently maintained components communicating through defined APIs. They support team autonomy and independent scaling but complicate architecture and debugging. Replicated load-balanced services improve availability and horizontal scale, with readiness probes preventing traffic from reaching uninitialized instances. Session tracking can use IP-based or application-level affinity, while caching and SSL termination may be added as separate replicated layers using Varnish and nginx.

Sharded services divide state or requests among specialized replicas, enabling datasets larger than one machine can hold. Sharded caches improve memory utilization but can suffer performance degradation when shards fail or change. Replicating each shard improves resilience and permits independent scaling of hot shards. Effective sharding requires deterministic, uniform keys and may use consistent hashing to minimize remapping during resizing.

Scatter/gather distributes each request across multiple workers and combines their partial results, reducing processing time and supporting distributed search. Sharding allows it to handle datasets exceeding one machine’s capacity, while shard replication improves availability and scalability. Excessive parallelism introduces overhead and amplifies slow-node and failure risks because completion depends on all required responses.

Function-as-a-service simplifies deployment, automatic scaling, and recovery through stateless, event-driven functions. Its strong decoupling can hinder monitoring and debugging, and it is poorly suited to long-running background work, applications requiring substantial in-memory data, or sustained high request volumes. FaaS works well for transformations such as decorating HTTP requests or responses, and open-source implementations on orchestrators can retain its development model while using virtual-machine pricing.
