The combination of resilient gold, a strengthening dollar, falling stocks and weak miners is compared with 2008.

The passage also promotes Investing.com’s stock screener, includes critical reader comments, related financial headlines, and warnings that trading financial instruments and cryptocurrencies involves substantial risk and that website data may be inaccurate or delayed.

The President argues that congressional Reconstruction has failed, left Southern states under military rule, excluded Virginia, Mississippi, and Texas from representation, damaged racial relations, and disrupted national prosperity. He urges repeal or revision of Reconstruction measures, the Tenure of Office Act, and laws restricting presidential military authority and state militias, advocating a return to constitutional government.

He warns that federal spending has risen far faster than population, reaching an estimated $372 million in 1869, while postwar expenditures and debt remain exceptionally high. He calls for retrenchment, reduced military costs, prudent taxation, and a definite plan to repay the national debt. He proposes applying the current 6 percent interest payments toward principal, contending this could eliminate the debt within sixteen years and eight months while fairly compensating creditors.

The message advocates restoring specie payments and a uniform currency. It describes nearly $700 million in paper circulation as depreciated relative to gold and silver, urges government and national banks to make notes convertible into specie, and recommends excluding paper notes below $20 after resumption.

Departmental reports cover public lands, pensions, patents, Indian reservations, transcontinental railroad construction, and proposed reductions in Army and Navy forces. Postal expenditures exceeded revenue, largely because service was restored and expanded in former insurgent states, while new international agreements reduced overseas postage costs.

Foreign affairs remained generally friendly, though disputes arose involving Paraguay and detained United States citizens. The administration pursued mediation in South American conflicts, assistance after earthquakes, treaties concerning trade, naturalization, consular powers, extradition, and claims, and negotiations over an isthmian canal. The President supports peaceful acquisition or incorporation of neighboring territories, including the Danish West Indies, possible annexation of the Dominican republics, and eventual Hawaiian admission, while opposing unlawful expeditions.

Finally, he renews proposals for direct popular election of the President, Vice-President, and senators; a clear presidential succession rule; presidential ineligibility for a second term; and limited terms for federal judges. He concludes by urging Congress to preserve the Union, uphold the Constitution, restore prosperity, and promote peace.

The Simons Observatory in Chile uses small- and large-aperture telescopes to study the cosmic microwave background across six frequency bands. This work characterizes 25 production Ultra-High-Frequency detector modules operating at 220/280 GHz, from which 19 will be deployed.

Each module contains 1,720 antenna-coupled transition-edge sensor bolometers, 36 dark calibration devices, and microwave SQUID multiplexed readout circuitry. Laboratory testing measured resonator performance and detector yield, critical temperature, resistance, saturation power, noise, time constants, and optical efficiency.

An average 86% of resonator channels passed operational cuts, while readout noise peaked at 35 pA/√Hz. The average operable detector yield was 83%, with all modules exceeding the 70% baseline target. Median saturation powers were 24 and 26 pW at 220 and 280 GHz, respectively. Median dark noise-equivalent powers were 39 and 42 aW/√Hz, with about 89% of detectors meeting noise requirements. Median optical efficiencies were 0.62 and 0.63, and expected photon noise indicates background-limited on-sky performance.

Two modules were rejected for unsuitable saturation power, and one was excluded because post-fabrication thermal re-annealing produced unusually low optical efficiency. Overall, 23 modules met saturation-power requirements, exceeding the 19 needed. Thirteen modules have already been deployed, and six more are planned for the large-aperture telescope upgrade.

The lecture proves an \(\Omega(\log n)\) cell-probe lower bound per operation for dynamic connectivity, even when every connected component is a path and algorithms may be randomized. The graph consists of a \(\sqrt n \times \sqrt n\) grid whose consecutive columns are joined by perfect matchings representing permutations. Bulk updates replace a matching, while “verify sum” queries test whether a prefix composition of permutations equals a supplied permutation. Each bulk operation corresponds to \(\Theta(\sqrt n)\) ordinary edge updates or connectivity queries.

The hard operation sequence follows bit-reversal order. A balanced binary tree is built over time; bit reversal ensures that indices updated in any node’s left subtree interleave with indices queried in its right subtree. The proof shows that information about random permutations introduced on the left must be conveyed to queries on the right. Summing this communication over the tree’s logarithmically many levels yields the desired lower bound without double counting, since each read is charged to the lowest common ancestor of its read time and last write time.

The argument is information-theoretic. The random update permutations under a subtree require \(\Omega(l\sqrt n\log n)\) bits to encode, where \(l\) is the number of leaves. For ordinary prefix-sum queries, encoding the memory cells read on the right and written on the left permits simulation of the queries and reconstruction of all left-side updates. Therefore, the intersection of those read and write sets must contain \(\Omega(l\sqrt n)\) cells.

Verify-sum queries are harder because the queried permutation is itself unknown during decoding. The decoder tries every possible permutation and selects the unique one returning yes. Incorrect simulated queries may access cells outside the actual read set, so the encoding additionally stores a compact separator distinguishing cells read only on the right from cells written only on the left. Such separators can be represented using succinct perfect hashing.

The resulting encoding bound implies either many cross-subtree reads or already enough total reads and writes within a subtree. Combining these cases across the balanced tree gives \(\Omega(\log n)\) time per original insertion, deletion, or connectivity query. The technique also yields update-query tradeoffs and establishes optimality for structures such as link-cut and Euler-tour trees.

In a cash sale, possession without payment does not transfer title. Because the defendant neither paid nor tendered payment and showed no waiver of the cash condition, the plaintiff retained title. The directed verdict for the plaintiff and dismissal of certiorari were proper. Judgment affirmed.

The free Fantastic Fountain Square Home Tour will run June 16–17, 2018, from noon to 5 p.m. in Indianapolis. It will showcase newly constructed homes and floor plans from several builders, including properties on Woodlawn, Cottage and Laurel streets. Food, maps, guided tours and prizes will be available.

The Washington Court of Appeals affirmed Vernon Clausing’s convictions for unlawful delivery and possession with intent to deliver legend drugs. After losing his medical license, Clausing continued distributing Soma and Nubain, claiming recipients had valid prescriptions. The court held that legend drugs delivered pursuant to prescriptions must first be dispensed by a licensed practitioner, though delivery itself may be performed by another person. The challenged jury instructions accurately stated the law, and the charging document sufficiently alleged the offenses without prejudicing Clausing. Instructions concerning valid prescriptions, labeling, and dispensing did not reduce the State’s burden of proof. Testimony that revocation invalidated prior prescriptions lacked explicit legal support, but any error was harmless because Clausing produced no prescription or records supporting his defense. The prosecutor’s closing remarks were supported by the testimony and evidence and did not constitute misconduct.

April 10, 2001 reports focused on Enron’s dispute with Maharashtra over unpaid bills for the $3 billion Dabhol power project. Dabhol invoked political force majeure, potentially allowing contract termination, while India agreed to conciliation. Maharashtra’s electricity board had not paid since December, disputed federal payments totaling $48 million, reduced purchases because of high rates, and imposed a performance penalty. Analysts proposed restructuring Dabhol as a failed business model, while Karnataka rejected Enron power as too expensive.

Other reports said E.ON planned to acquire Powergen for €8.2 billion and assume €7.1 billion in debt, creating the world’s second-largest utility and supporting U.S. expansion. American Airlines acquired bankrupt TWA’s assets for $742 million plus $3.5 billion in debt, becoming the world’s largest carrier.

In Houston, a citizens board selected Montgomery Watson over Enron affiliate Azurix to negotiate a water-plant contract potentially worth $150 million, citing its lower bid and financial considerations despite City Hall’s preference for Azurix.

President Buhari said Nigerians were reporting improved electricity supply, citing 5,222.3 MW delivered by December 2017 and generation capacity above 7,500 MW. Meanwhile, Daura faced a 10-day blackout after a windstorm toppled a new power tower and 16 poles. KEDCO promised restoration within 48 hours. Similar infrastructure damage has caused prolonged outages elsewhere, including Lagos and Ondo.

This study investigated thalamic local field potentials (LFPs) as internal biomarkers for closed-loop deep brain stimulation (DBS) in 34 patients with essential tremor, multiple sclerosis, or Parkinson’s disease. LFPs from VIM/VOP DBS leads and hand accelerometry were recorded during tremor assessment, including testing at several DBS frequencies in 16 participants.

Tremor showed moderate correlations with theta- and alpha-band LFP power but a strong correlation with peak LFP–acceleration coherence. Postural tremor could be decoded from LFPs with an area under the curve of approximately 0.7, including during DBS. High-frequency stimulation near 130 Hz reduced low-frequency LFP power relative to baseline.

Signal processing included DBS artifact removal, spectral and coherence analyses, regression, classification, and repeated-measures testing. A computational thalamus model containing 5,000 neurons across VC, VIM, and VOP examined the biophysical basis of LFPs. Simulated low-frequency power varied substantially with electrode location, tremor-cell distribution, and the proportion of tremor cells, potentially explaining participant variability and the moderate association between spectral power and tremor.

The paper introduces the **popular dimension** to address cases where no single popular matching exists. A matching is popular if the total weight of agents preferring it to any alternative is at least the weight preferring the alternative. A **popular winning set** is a collection of matchings whose best outcome for each agent is at least as popular as every individual matching; the popular dimension is the minimum size of such a set.

The framework covers house allocation, marriage, and roommates problems under strict preferences or ties, with either unweighted or weighted agents. Popularity lies between Pareto and core stability and is stronger than the analogous Condorcet winning-set condition.

The main results are:

- **House allocation:** The popular dimension is exactly 2 in all four preference and weighting cases. A polynomial-time algorithm constructs a top-choice \((1,2)\)-matching and decomposes it into two matchings forming a popular winning set. A three-agent, two-house example establishes the lower bound.
- **Marriage:** With unweighted agents and strict preferences, the dimension is 1 because stable matchings exist and are popular. If weights or preference ties are allowed, the dimension is between 2 and 3. The lower bound follows by reductions from house allocation, while the upper bound follows from the general roommates result.
- **Roommates:** With unweighted agents and strict preferences, the dimension is exactly 2. A polynomial-time greedy algorithm orders agents and constructs two alternating matchings; a charging argument proves their popularity. With weights or ties, the dimension is between 2 and 3.
- **General roommates upper bound:** The instance is converted into a house allocation instance. Two auxiliary matchings are produced, merged into a graph of maximum degree 3 whose components contain at most one cycle, and then edge-coloured with three colours. The resulting three matchings form a popular winning set in polynomial time.

These upper bounds also imply that the Condorcet dimension is at most 3 for the three matching settings studied. The remaining open problem is whether the popular dimension is 2 or 3 for marriage and roommates instances with weights or ties. The authors conjecture that it is exactly 2 for the marriage problem, even when both weights and ties are allowed.

Industrial enterprises increasingly need high-performance computing (HPC) as simulation, modeling, and data analysis become more complex. Half of surveyed decision makers report calculations taking too long, while 42% use outdated or inaccurate simulations. Demand for high-performance calculations is expected to rise from 8% currently to almost half of respondents within two years.

HPC enables faster, more complex calculations, additional iterations, improved results, new applications, and greater innovation and agility. Eighty-one percent view HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation. More than a quarter already use professional HPC infrastructure, while 39% are planning or piloting it.

External infrastructure is preferred: 87% of HPC users use or plan cloud-based services, and 74% use or plan colocation facilities. Key challenges include security concerns, cited by 72%; energy consumption and sustainability, cited by 58%; limited expertise, affecting 42%; and costs, capacity, availability, scalability, and infrastructure complexity.

Public and hybrid cloud architectures are expected to become especially important. HPC as a Service can provide scalable performance, flexible operating costs, access to current technology, improved collaboration, and support for HPC-based business models. However, skilled personnel remain necessary to configure systems, program calculations, and interpret results.

IDC recommends integrating virtual development into digital transformation, establishing a unified data strategy, selecting operating models according to utilization, budget, performance, flexibility, security, and skills, prioritizing scalability and energy efficiency, and using external expertise where necessary. The findings are based on a December 2021 survey of 200 decision makers at industrial enterprises with over 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

The study examines how climate change affects K–12 internally displaced learners in lower- and middle-income countries. Using a literature review of 73 academic and grey-literature sources, it combines a Human Rights-Based Approach to education with Education in Emergencies research to assess immediate, indirect, and long-term effects.

Climate-related disasters disrupt schooling through damaged infrastructure, displacement, poverty, food insecurity, health problems, psychological trauma, and reduced learning capacity. In new locations, displaced learners face additional financial, administrative, linguistic, cultural, technological, and discriminatory barriers. Host education systems often lack adequate resources, data, preparedness, psychosocial support, and inclusive policies. Girls experience heightened risks because of household responsibilities, gender bias, financial prioritization of boys, safety concerns, early marriage, and limited opportunities to return to school.

The study recommends scalable financial assistance, simplified enrollment and documentation processes, stronger academic and mental health support, improved data systems, and gender-responsive policies. It identifies research gaps concerning climate displacement within Education in Emergencies, long-term educational outcomes, and proactive policy responses. It argues for climate-specific education policies integrated with broader adaptation strategies and for long-term systemic approaches that recognize education as a human right and a component of climate resilience.

After becoming PayPal’s CEO in 2015, Dan Schulman established a mission to democratize financial services and promote universal financial health. However, internal studies revealed that many hourly and entry-level employees were financially insecure despite receiving market-rate compensation. Nearly two-thirds of surveyed customer service employees ran out of, or nearly ran out of, money between paychecks, while some could not afford PayPal’s health insurance or routine emergencies.

PayPal created estimated net disposable income (eNDI), measuring pay remaining after taxes and typical living costs. Findings showed that half of global customer service employees retained only 4–6% of monthly pay after basic expenses. In response, a cross-functional committee developed a four-part Employee Financial Wellness Initiative for lower-paid employees: wage increases where appropriate; a 60% reduction in U.S. healthcare premiums and company-funded health reimbursement accounts; equity grants for employees who previously lacked stock awards; and financial education, digital tools, and confidential coaching. PayPal adjusted compensation for promoted employees to prevent losses in benefits.

The initiative, announced in October 2019, cost tens of millions of dollars in its first year. Leadership and the board supported it as consistent with PayPal’s mission and potentially beneficial through lower turnover, greater productivity, stronger engagement, and improved customer service. During the Covid-19 pandemic, PayPal avoided pandemic-related layoffs, provided remote-work equipment and stipends, and offered crisis leave. It later introduced early wage-access platforms, additional equity grants, and further remote-work stipends.

By 2021, surveys and operating measures indicated improvement. Customer service turnover fell from 19.4% in 2019 to 7.3% in 2020, engagement rose, productivity and customer loyalty improved, and 76% of surveyed employees intended to remain at PayPal for at least five years, versus 51% in 2018. U.S. hourly and entry-level employees’ minimum eNDI reached 11%, with a global target of 20%.

PayPal viewed employee financial health as part of multistakeholder capitalism, alongside commitments to inclusion, pay equity, racial justice, and women’s economic empowerment. It partnered with nonprofit organizations to encourage other companies to assess and improve worker financial wellness; by the end of 2021, 11 companies had joined the initiative.

In Mock v. Watson, a widow sought one-third of her deceased husband’s real estate despite claims that the land was needed to pay estate debts. The court held that her statutory interest was not subject to those debts and could be set apart before their payment.

Under Code § 2440, the widow’s interest attaches when the husband owns the land during marriage and becomes vested upon his death. Because the husband cannot defeat that interest by conveying the property without her relinquishment, it never becomes part of the estate available to creditors. Sections 2387 and 2391 authorize sale only of the estate’s remaining interest in the land. Section 2441 merely prevents the widow from receiving more than her lawful one-third share in a manner prejudicing creditors, while § 2451 protects a replacement homestead from the widow’s own debts, not her husband’s. The judgment ordering her interest admeasured and set apart was affirmed.

The study presents two all-optical thermometry methods using photoluminescence from silicon-vacancy centers and Raman signals from fluorescent microdiamonds. Nine temperature-dependent spectral features were measured from eight approximately 1-µm diamonds between 25 and 85 °C. Models were trained on subsets of diamonds and tested on previously unseen diamonds to obtain generalized accuracy and resolution.

The multi-feature regression (MFR) model uses linear regression with exhaustive feature selection. Its best feature set comprised the SiV zero-phonon-line wavelength and linewidth plus the diamond Raman linewidth. With only 3–4 calibration diamonds and temperature points, MFR achieved approximately 1.7 K accuracy and 1.2 K·Hz⁻¹/² resolution, improving accuracy by about 26% over the best single-feature model.

The two-stage multi-feature regression (2SMFR) combines partial least squares, Lasso regression, and spline-based bias correction. With seven diamonds and seven temperature points, it achieved 0.7 K accuracy, 0.6 K·Hz⁻¹/² resolution, and 0.04 K⁻¹ sensitivity. These values represent improvements of about 70%, 50%, and sevenfold, respectively, over the best single-feature model. However, 2SMFR requires larger calibration datasets, while MFR gains become marginal beyond a few calibration diamonds or temperatures.

Both methods automatically select useful features and can accommodate different instruments and calibration resources. Performance generally improves with more training data. The models assume approximately linear feature–temperature relationships over the studied range, and predictions outside the calibration range may be unreliable.

A self-driving Uber vehicle killed pedestrian Elaine Herzberg, 49, in Tempe, Arizona, while operating with a human safety driver. Uber suspended autonomous vehicle testing across the U.S. and Canada and is cooperating with police. The first fatality involving a fully autonomous test vehicle could affect development and regulation of the technology.

Dabhol Power Company’s board authorized management to issue a preliminary notice terminating its power purchase agreement with Maharashtra State Electricity Board, though termination was not immediate and could require lender consent and a six-month consultation period. International lenders generally supported withdrawal, while Indian lenders, Maharashtra, and the Centre favored renegotiation. MSEB paid Rs 134 crore of its March bill under protest, disputing Rs 12.64 crore. Officials cited potential termination liabilities of up to Rs 2,840 crore for the Centre, while Maharashtra planned a committee to renegotiate the project’s high tariffs.

Thai Prime Minister Prayuth Chan-ocha said Thailand has no trade with North Korea and complies with U.N. resolutions. U.S. envoy Joseph Yun is expected in Bangkok to seek greater pressure on Pyongyang over its nuclear and missile programs. Thailand previously reported a 94% annual decline in bilateral trade.

Following the September 11 attacks, U.S. energy companies heightened security, evacuated offices, and largely halted power, gas, oil, and bandwidth trading while maintaining essential energy deliveries and production. Oil, natural-gas, and gasoline prices rose amid fears of supply disruption and panic buying, though producers reported adequate supplies and OPEC indicated readiness to increase output. Enron resumed limited North American gas and power trading on September 12 through EnronOnline and telephone systems. Companies also reviewed security for South Asian operations. Separately, Enron’s Dabhol project in India faced debt-repayment difficulties, construction delays, and a continuing payment dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board.

HDFC Mutual Fund will wind up HDFC FMP 378D March 2014 (1), subject to unit-holder approval. After two maturity extensions, net assets fell below Rs 10 crore, making the scheme unviable. Its corpus is invested in cash and cash equivalents.

Josephine Slosson held a testamentary power of appointment over a trust created by her father. Her will directed payments to specified beneficiaries and creditors, with the balance passing to her surviving issue per stirpes. The court held that this constituted a valid exercise of the power, preventing her three children from electing to take under their grandfather’s will, because the alternative gift applied only if she failed to dispose of the fund by will. The beneficiaries’ interests and payments of $24,840 to creditors were therefore subject to transfer tax. Because the children had not renounced their maternal legacies, the consequences of renunciation were not considered. However, $682.04 advanced by Alice Slosson to settle claims was improperly included in her taxable bequest because the decedent owed her nothing at death. The tax order was modified by deducting that amount and otherwise affirmed.

The quarterback is football’s offensive leader and is widely viewed as the sport’s most important position because the player handles the ball on every play and directs the offense. Responsibilities include receiving the snap, communicating plays, ensuring correct formations, reading defenses, calling audibles, passing, handing off, and occasionally running. Quarterbacks must thoroughly study playbooks, scouting reports, and opponents while inspiring teammates’ confidence.

Important quarterback qualities include football intelligence, decision-making, passing accuracy, leadership, footwork, athleticism, and arm strength. Accurate throws help receivers maintain momentum, avoid defenders, and reduce injury risks. Although quarterbacks were traditionally expected to be tall and strong, modern players vary considerably in size, speed, and athletic ability, with coaches designing systems around their strengths.

The name “quarterback” originated from early formations in which the player stood a quarter of the way back from the running back, with a fullback between them. Other terms include signal caller, field general, gunslinger, and “QB.”

The passage identifies Otto Graham, Peyton Manning, Dan Marino, Joe Montana, and Tom Brady among the greatest quarterbacks, citing their championships, records, production, and leadership. Because quarterbacks control possession, find receivers, protect the football, and initiate nearly everything an offense does, their performance strongly affects the entire team.

Options expire when contracts become void and can no longer be exercised. In the US, expiration occurs on the third Saturday of the month, generally at 11:59 a.m. EST, while trading and exercise instructions usually end on the preceding Friday, or Thursday if Friday is a holiday.

Large-cap stocks with actively traded options often experience higher returns, trading volumes, and volatility during expiration week. Expiration of stock options, stock index futures, and stock index options together occurs quarterly in March, June, September, and December.

Strategy development involves researching models, backtesting them across at least 15 years or multiple market cycles, and forward-testing promising models. Presented stock and ETF backtests found average gains of 0.3% per expiration week for SPY, about 0.7% per trade for an undisclosed XLV strategy, 0.46% for a 24-hour SPY strategy, and 0.18% across 306 intraday short trades on SPY. Expiration days showed slightly higher volatility than ordinary trading days, particularly quarterly combined-expiration days.

Carol Christ, 73, became UC Berkeley’s first female and oldest chancellor as the university faced sexual harassment scandals, a $110 million deficit, free-speech conflicts, housing shortages and strained relations with state lawmakers. A former Berkeley professor, department chair, provost and Smith College president, Christ said her priorities include increasing Black student representation, addressing sexual misconduct, promoting civil debate, expanding student housing, reducing the deficit through philanthropy and administrative cuts, improving financial transparency, and rebuilding campus community. She plans to make 2017–18 a “free speech year” featuring debates between people with opposing views. Christ also wants to collaborate with Berkeley and Oakland on housing, homelessness and safety before considering construction at People’s Park. She said her long connection to and affection for Berkeley motivated her return.

The UC1825B-SP is a high-frequency PWM controller supporting current- or voltage-mode systems, input feed-forward, protection features, jitter-free logic, undervoltage lockout, and high-current totem-pole outputs.

Players described a fiery playoff opponent, emphasized staying positive after improved first-period play, and believed there was time to recover. One player recalled unexpectedly joining Detroit from Toronto before the deadline and credited Jimmy Devellano, Scotty Bowman, the team’s Russian players, and the entire roster for a Stanley Cup victory. He called it a total team effort and said Detroit improved throughout the playoffs, ultimately sweeping the series by consistently outplaying its opponents.

An 11-year study of 33,908 Norwegian adults found that people reporting no exercise were 44 percent more likely to experience depression than those exercising one to two hours weekly. Researchers estimated that modest exercise could have prevented 12 percent of depression cases, suggesting one hour per week may provide significant protection.
Irish soccer player Megan Connolly posted a viral video of her frightened reaction to a Myrtle Beach ride, accompanied by teammate Dallas Dorosy’s laughter and the Fray’s “How To Save A Life.”

Zimbabwean nurse and epidemiologist Chenai Mathabire received an International AIDS Society prize for research showing that a rapid tuberculosis urine test could be implemented in health centers in Malawi and Mozambique. After nursing in Zimbabwe and South Sudan with Doctors Without Borders, she joined the two-year study in 2015.

Tuberculosis is a leading killer of HIV-positive patients, but standard cough tests and chest X-rays can take days or longer to produce results, while costs and transportation barriers may prevent follow-up care. The rapid test delivered results within an hour, could be administered after a few hours of staff training, and was considered easy to interpret. It allowed sick patients to begin treatment the same day and was accepted by patients.

The findings prompted some Doctors Without Borders-supported health centers to adopt rapid testing and could encourage broader use. Mathabire continues working for the organization and is considering further HIV and tuberculosis research.

A soccer penalty kick is awarded for a direct-free-kick offense by a defender inside their penalty area. The ball is placed on the penalty mark, the kicker is identified, and the goalkeeper must remain between the posts with at least part of one foot on, behind, or aligned with the goal line when the ball is kicked. Other players must remain outside the penalty area and arc, behind the mark, and at least ten yards away. The kicker must wait for the referee’s signal and kick the ball forward. After striking a post or crossbar, the kicker cannot touch it again until another player does; after a goalkeeper save, the kicker may immediately play the rebound.

Coaches should select primary and alternate kickers before matches based on demonstrated confidence, preparation, and scoring success. Kickers should develop and consistently practice a complete routine, including ball placement, mental preparation, starting position, run-up, plant-foot placement, strike, follow-through, and response to rebounds. They should remain calm, block distractions, visualize success, and avoid changing their intended kick at the last moment.

Common techniques include inside-foot, instep-drive, and instep-face kicks. Accuracy with sufficient pace is essential. Lower corners are generally recommended because they reduce the risk of shooting over the goal, while upper corners are harder for goalkeepers to reach but easier to miss. Feinting during the run-up is permitted, but feinting after completing it is prohibited.

Practice should occur regularly on relevant playing surfaces, initially using targets and later goalkeepers, distractions, fatigue, referees, and game-like situations. Advanced preparation may include scouting goalkeeper habits, mastering at least two kicks, disguising the designated kicker, modifying approaches, or using a rare two-player “tap” penalty. Coaches are responsible for preparing the whole attacking team, while kickers should report any lack of confidence without criticism.

B.C. Liberal leader Andrew Wilkinson blamed Premier John Horgan and gas taxes for rising fuel costs, urging tax relief for drivers. Horgan attributed a nine-cent overnight increase to supply constraints and company profits, not taxation, and called for greater domestic refining and federal scrutiny.

Google’s Project Fi added three compatible phones: the $199 Moto G6, $740 LG G7 ThinQ and $899 LG V35 ThinQ. The expansion broadens Fi’s limited device lineup, but the absence of Apple and Samsung phones remains a major obstacle to customer growth. Launched in 2015, Fi charges $20 monthly for calls and texts plus $10 per gigabyte of data up to 6GB, refunding unused data. In the U.S., it automatically connects through T-Mobile, Sprint, U.S. Cellular or Wi-Fi; overseas, it uses Three. Google has not disclosed subscriber numbers, citing only a healthy user base and high satisfaction. Analyst Roger Entner said limited handset choice and minimal promotion have caused the service to languish amid increased competition from unlimited wireless plans.

Apple filed a Form 8-K on October 27, 2022, reporting that it issued a press release detailing financial results for its fourth fiscal quarter ended September 24, 2022. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1, with Inline XBRL cover-page data as Exhibit 104. CFO Luca Maestri signed the filing.

John F. Kennedy accepts the Democratic presidential nomination, pledging to uphold the party platform, civil and economic rights, church-state separation, and independent decision-making regardless of his religious affiliation. He praises fellow Democratic leaders and contrasts his party’s vision with Richard Nixon and Republican policies.

Kennedy argues that the nation faces urgent international and domestic challenges, including Communist expansion, nuclear danger, poverty, racial discrimination, inadequate education and health care, agricultural disruption, urban crowding, automation, and declining moral and intellectual purpose. He calls for a new generation of vigorous, creative leadership rather than complacency or attachment to the status quo.

He presents the “New Frontier” of the 1960s as a set of challenges requiring courage, innovation, sacrifice, and public commitment. Americans, he says, must decide between progress and mediocrity, national greatness and decline, while proving that a free society can compete with Communism. He closes by asking for voters’ help and expressing faith that renewed strength will enable the nation to meet the test and prevail.

North Tyneside Council unanimously approved progressing the North of Tyne devolution deal with Newcastle and Northumberland. The agreement includes an elected mayor, £600m in funding over 30 years and a projected 10,000 jobs. Mayor Norma Redfearn said councils south of the Tyne could seek government approval to join after the authority is established, while criticising their withdrawal from an earlier seven-council proposal. Newcastle leader Nick Forbes rejected claims the authority would be under-powered, saying its per-capita investment exceeds some other deals and includes health, disability support and housing measures. The combined authority was planned for summer 2018, with mayoral elections in May 2019, though a vote to split the existing North East Combined Authority was postponed until mid-April.

Coach Bylsma restored the team’s confidence and introduced a helpful philosophy, contributing to its playoff run. A successful five-game road trip and trades for Billy and Adams marked the season’s turning point. The speaker hopes to receive a championship ring but values few other mementos. Sid leads through disciplined, team-focused play at both ends of the ice. Jordan combines offensive talent with responsible two-way play, while other skilled leaders can suddenly dominate and consistently compete hard. The organization’s sustained success is considered remarkable, especially after losing significant players following the previous year’s Cup run.

Plymouth Studio School is expected to close in September 2018, pending government approval, after operating at about half its 300-student capacity and being deemed financially unviable. The £4.2 million sports-focused free school opened in 2015 and currently has 155 students. An upcoming Ofsted report rates it “inadequate” and identifies fundamental areas requiring improvement, despite some progress by current management. MP Johnny Mercer expressed disappointment but said his priority was preventing disruption to pupils’ education. The local authority is consulting families and says surplus secondary school places can accommodate affected students. The school would be the 19th studio school to close nationally.

The Texas Court of Civil Appeals affirmed a judgment denying damages arising from a 1955 head-on collision. The jury found that Wilson negligently drove into the western lane, causing the collision, and that his negligence was the sole proximate cause. It found no relevant negligence by King.

Appellants challenged the omission or form of several jury issues and alleged improper closing argument. The court held that objections to the jury charge were waived because appellants neither timely objected nor properly submitted written requested issues to the court and opposing counsel. Their earlier informal memorandum of possible issues did not satisfy procedural requirements.

Appellants also failed to object when appellee’s counsel argued that the $55,000 sought exceeded what an ordinary person might earn in a lifetime. Because any harmful effect could have been cured by an instruction, the argument was not incurably prejudicial and could not support reversal without a timely objection. Finding no reversible error, the court affirmed the trial court’s judgment.

Students must read Mankiw chapter 10 and prepare homework on how monetary and fiscal policy shift IS-LM curves, identify a recent example, recommend policies for Southeast Asia, compare IMF recommendations, and complete two textbook problems. Class will discuss shifts affecting Europe, the United States, Japan, and Indonesia during the 1997–98 crisis.

Optional readings cover France’s 35-hour workweek, a Latin American stock-market rally, and Japan’s economic stagnation. France’s shorter-workweek law produced mixed results: some firms increased productivity and flexibility, but job creation remained uncertain amid opposition over costs, wage freezes, working conditions, and competitiveness. Latin American markets rose on foreign investment, reduced concern about U.S. interest rates, stronger commodity and export prospects, and expectations of renewed regional growth, though external rate increases and stalled Brazilian reforms remained risks. Japan’s downturn was attributed mainly to policy failures after the asset bubble, unresolved bad loans, fiscal tightening, and a credit crunch, compounded by globalization, population aging, and technological change. Government stimulus offered temporary relief, but lasting recovery required financial, corporate, and systemic reform.

California Assembly Republican Leader Chad Mayes faced calls to resign after supporting an extension of the state’s cap-and-trade program with seven other Republicans. Mayes defended the vote as demonstrating Republican commitment to climate policy while preventing stricter regulations. Conservative critics called it a betrayal that aided Democrats, raised business costs and disregarded most of his caucus.

Republican officials, activists and donor groups urged Mayes to step down or face a 2018 primary challenge. His leadership can be ended only by his 25-member caucus, where Assemblyman Jay Obernolte mounted an internal challenge. Other Republicans supporting the legislation also encountered protests and constituent anger.

The conflict threatened party fundraising arrangements and undermined hopes that the bipartisan climate deal would broaden support for California’s environmental policies. It also reflected longstanding tension within the state’s shrinking Republican minority between gaining influence through cooperation with Democrats and adhering to conservative positions.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell architecture can reduce power use by up to 50% in small-language-model inference through higher performance, lower-power transitional states, and faster entry into deep sleep.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame. Its AI model is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and works with enhanced GPU-based frame pacing. New transformer models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA use twice as many parameters as prior CNN models, improving temporal stability, motion detail, lighting, anti-aliasing, and reducing ghosting and denoising artifacts.

Blackwell expands neural rendering through Tensor Cores accessible from graphics shaders via Cooperative Vectors APIs for DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Neural-shader applications include:
- RTX Neural Materials for approximating complex, layered materials.
- Neural Texture Compression, demonstrated reducing material memory from 1,110 MB to 333 MB.
- Neural Radiance Cache for estimating multi-bounce indirect lighting from partially traced rays.
- RTX Skin for real-time ray-traced subsurface scattering.
- RTX Neural Faces for generating more natural faces from rasterized inputs and pose data.

The flagship GB202 GPU contains 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor Cores, and a 512-bit memory interface, and powers the GeForce RTX 5090. GB203 contains 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA cores, and a 256-bit interface for the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 contains 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA cores, and a 192-bit interface for the RTX 5070.

NVIDIA states that specifications may change, provides the materials without warranties, restricts use in safety-critical applications, and places responsibility for suitability and testing on customers.

Pragyan ’18 began on March 1 with chief guest Dr BN Suresh. The festival featured lectures from experts, technology workshops, a large student-run human library, and exhibits including Hyperloop India, InMoov, KalamSat, ISRO displays, and Ugears. Shadow dance, ventriloquism, cardistry, mentalism, hypnosis, and stand-up comedy performances complemented the technical events.

May 23, 2001 news reports focused on the dispute among Enron-promoted Dabhol Power Company (DPC), the Maharashtra government and Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB). Madhav Godbole resigned as chairman of the panel renegotiating DPC’s power purchase agreement after Nationalist Congress Party leader Sharad Pawar criticized negotiators’ “negative approach.” Chief Minister Vilasrao Deshmukh refused to accept the resignation and asked Godbole to continue, while Pawar said his remarks did not represent the government. The scheduled renegotiation meeting was cancelled.

The dispute centered on unpaid electricity bills, high tariffs and DPC’s preliminary termination notice. Maharashtra considered issuing its own termination notice, while Enron warned it could seek substantial damages. MSEB’s advocate general supported its Rs 401 crore rebate claim against DPC for failing to meet declared power availability. The Centre adopted a wait-and-watch policy pending conciliation.

Indian lenders faced significant exposure through loans and guarantees, prompting falling share prices and concern that DPC loans could become non-performing assets. Some lenders considered skipping a June meeting in Singapore. Indian power companies showed little interest in buying DPC at prevailing tariffs. Enron reportedly appointed advisers to value its Indian businesses, potentially preceding an exit.

The Godbole Committee report criticized failures of governance, due diligence, competitive bidding and project assessment. Other reports discussed employee protests, Enron’s willingness to consider solutions involving creditworthy power buyers, and its withdrawal from Qatar’s Dolphin natural-gas project.

The 2017 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons for highlighting nuclear weapons’ humanitarian consequences and promoting a treaty-based ban. ICAN helped drive the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, adopted by 122 nations, which prohibits activities including development, testing, production, acquisition and stockpiling. The five permanent UN Security Council members did not join negotiations. The Nobel Committee cited growing nuclear tensions and proliferation risks. ICAN said nuclear weapons endanger humanity and urged all nations to reject them, while chief executive Beatrice Fihn said the prize strengthened awareness of the treaty and the campaign for abolition.

The University of Maine canceled its annual AFLOAT offshore wind summit, citing changing federal policies and priorities after a $12.5 million federal grant was suspended. It has no plans to revive the event but will continue its grant project and hold private meetings with industry, research and government leaders.

Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell and Shimon Sakaguchi won the 2025 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine for discoveries concerning regulatory T cells, or T-regs. Sakaguchi identified T-regs in 1995. Brunkow and Ramsdell studied mutations linked to fatal autoimmune disease in mice and related disorders in people. T-regs calm immune responses, prevent attacks on the body and help avoid fetal rejection during pregnancy. Their failure can cause autoimmune disorders and damaging inflammation. Researchers are investigating their use against immune-related diseases and cancer.

The TPS7H500x-SP push-pull converter design uses approximately 25-ns dead time with 20.5-kΩ resistors, 50-ns leading-edge blanking with 49.9 kΩ, and a 33-nF soft-start capacitor for about 7.5 ms. The transformer uses a 2.5 turns ratio and 40-µH primary inductance, targeting a 35% maximum duty cycle. Primary and synchronous-rectifier GaN FET ratings are 170 V and 80 V, respectively. An RCD clamp may limit switch-node overshoot and requires test optimization.

The output stage uses a 0.47-µH inductor and approximately 2.3 mF capacitance, exceeding the calculated 1.3-mF minimum to improve radiation-induced transient mitigation. An optional secondary filter can further reduce ripple. Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins near 35 A using a 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω sense resistor. Other selected values include a 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation targeting 10 kHz with 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF, and a 102-kΩ slope-compensation resistor.

The controllers require a regulated 4-V to 14-V supply and at least 0.1-µF ceramic input bypassing. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switching loops and switch-node area, keeping sensitive traces away from noisy signals and magnetics, using short and wide high-current paths, and placing bypass, filtering, sensing, and compensation components close to the controller. CFP backside metallization should connect to AVSS through multiple vias. Documentation also covers support resources, ESD precautions, revision history, packaging information, and TI warranty limitations.

Arthur Heine moved to dismiss a bigamy indictment, arguing that his second marriage was void because a justice of the peace performed it when he was 19. His first marriage remained legally valid at the time. New York Domestic Relations Law §11 authorized only specified officials to solemnize marriages involving a party under 21. Courts had disagreed over whether violating this provision merely prohibited the officiant’s conduct or invalidated the marriage. Relying on Caplan v. Caplan and De Martino v. De Martino, the Kings County Court concluded that the statutory requirements were mandatory and that a marriage performed by a justice of the peace when either party was under 21 was invalid. Because Heine’s second marriage was void, the court granted his motion to dismiss the bigamy indictment.

Darfon America showcased upgraded H200 and H300 energy storage systems and the H5001 hybrid inverter at Intersolar North America 2018. Improvements include expanded battery options and capacity, easier installation, enhanced security, improved temperature control and overload handling, and an optional generator start-up kit. The products are available through authorized distributors. Darfon Electronics manufactures power supplies, inverters, energy storage systems and installation solutions in-house.

The Federal Reserve raised short-term interest rates by a quarter point to 1%–1.25%, its third increase since December, citing continued U.S. economic strength. It upgraded growth and unemployment forecasts but lowered its 2017 inflation projection to 1.6%. Unemployment reached 4.3% in May, while jobs grew for 80 consecutive months. The Fed also plans to begin gradually reducing its $4.5 trillion asset holdings, initially by $10 billion monthly, if economic conditions develop as expected. Most officials anticipate at least one more rate increase this year.

Christmas Day, a US federal holiday since 1870, is not a trading day in US markets. Adjacent days may be trading days depending on weekends, while bond markets close at 2 p.m. before Christmas. Weekend holidays are observed on Friday or Monday.

Backtests indicate a Santa Claus rally—stronger stock performance in late December and early January—across the S&P 500, Germany’s DAX proxy EWG, Euro Stoxx 50 ETF FEZ, emerging markets fund FEMKX, and India’s NIFTY 50. S&P 500 strategies since 1960 produced average gains of 0.7% to 1.6% per trade, with win rates of 66% to 72%. EWG and FEZ averaged 2.1% and 1.5%, respectively, both with 81% win rates. Emerging markets averaged 2.7%, while NIFTY averaged 1.2%, though its backtest had only 14 observations and used a non-tradable cash index as a proxy.

Recent returns weakened in several markets. Suggested explanations include fund rebalancing, limited macroeconomic news, positive turn-of-the-month effects, and reduced selling during holidays. Past results do not guarantee continuation.

The speaker is excited to play in a hostile hometown environment but aims to treat it like any other road game. Feeling confident at the net, they credit strong team play and stress maintaining focus, matching Edmonton’s effort, and finishing the job while enjoying support from teammates.

Drew Doughty said the team is not discouraged despite losing two straight and believes the games could have gone either way. He credited the opponent’s execution and said his team must adjust, create traffic, pursue rebounds and score “dirty” goals against Marty. Doughty acknowledged that players were distracted and nervous with family, friends and the Cup present, but said they learned to prioritize the team and will be better prepared. He added that the Cup’s presence provides motivation and praised his communication, accountability and strong on- and off-ice relationship with defensive partner Rob.

Volkswagen’s U.S. unit asked a Virginia judge to delay upcoming consumer fraud trials for at least six months, arguing that a plaintiffs’ lawyer’s televised comments linking company-sponsored diesel tests on monkeys to Hitler and the Holocaust could prejudice jurors. Lawyer Michael Melkersen called the request a delaying tactic. The first trial, involving a North Carolina owner of a 2014 diesel Jetta, was scheduled for Feb. 26. Volkswagen has committed more than $25 billion to resolve U.S. diesel-emissions claims, but about 2,000 owners opted out of settlements and are seeking additional compensation. Early verdicts could influence remaining cases.

James Madison returned the internal improvements bill unsigned, arguing that Congress lacked constitutional authority to fund roads, canals, and navigation improvements. He rejected deriving such power from the commerce, necessary and proper, or common defense and general welfare clauses, warning that broad interpretation would effectively grant Congress unlimited legislative authority, undermine state powers, and weaken judicial enforcement of federal boundaries. State consent could not confer powers absent from the Constitution. Although recognizing the projects’ national value, Madison maintained that preserving the defined division of federal and state powers required withholding approval and suggested pursuing a constitutional amendment.

Scalping seeks frequent small profits from price changes lasting seconds to minutes. The article argues that most scalpers lose money because they compete with better-capitalized, lower-latency institutions and high-frequency traders while facing market noise, limited profitable opportunities, commissions, bid-ask spreads, and slippage.

Short-term backtests often fail to reflect real trading because execution costs, randomness, and fill difficulties are hard to model. Automation is considered necessary, but requires specialized software and infrastructure and introduces operational errors and potential losses. Scalping also creates significant stress from constant market monitoring and rapid execution.

A real-world example describes a trader who invested in software, data, and exchange co-location but was outpaced by competitors, eventually losing heavily and quitting. The article recommends seeking quantified strategies on longer time frames, which offer larger potential profits per trade and more robust backtesting. It suggests stocks and indices may provide better opportunities than forex and notes that diversified long-term investing in mutual funds may offer better odds of reasonable success than trading.

The TMS320DM814x integrates an ARM Cortex-A8 subsystem, C674x DSP, multimedia accelerators, memory-management hardware, interprocessor communication modules, and extensive peripheral interfaces. The Cortex-A8 subsystem includes NEON SIMD, VFPv3 floating point, separate L1 caches, debug and trace support, a 32KB embedded trace buffer, an interrupt controller, an embedded PLL, and direct connections to DDR and other modules. Its AINTC prioritizes peripheral requests and generates IRQ or FIQ, although general-purpose devices do not support FIQ generation.

The C674x DSP provides eight functional units, 64 general-purpose registers, parallel fixed- and floating-point processing, complex and Galois-field multiplication, compact instructions, software-pipelined loops, exception handling, privilege modes, protected local-memory pages, and a free-running timestamp counter. Its memories include L1 program/cache and unified L2 RAM/cache with error protection.

C674x MDMA accesses pass through the system MMU for address remapping and ARM-memory protection. EDMA transfer controllers may also use the MMU. Multimedia functions include a media controller, HDVICP2 video acceleration for major codec standards, and face detection and tracking for QVGA grayscale images. The device also provides 128 hardware spinlocks and mailbox queues for communication among the ARM, DSP, and media controller.

A unified memory map covers on-chip memories and peripherals, with extended TILER addressing for rotated and mirrored framebuffer views. Detailed pin tables define multiplexing, electrical characteristics, reset pulls, supply voltages, and functions for boot configuration, DDR2/DDR3, Ethernet, GPIO, GPMC, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, JTAG, SD, SPI, clocks, timers, UART, USB, digital and analog video, and power connections. Boot-mode pins are sampled at reset and subsequently serve GPMC functions. Several interfaces require external pullups, specific reset behavior, unconnected unused pins, or mandatory power supplies even when their associated peripheral is unused.

NATO’s 2017 annual report highlighted stronger deterrence, defense spending, deployments and international cooperation. The alliance stationed multinational battle groups in the Baltic states and Poland, expanded its Black Sea presence, strengthened cyber defenses, joined the anti-ISIS coalition, deepened EU cooperation and admitted Montenegro.

European and Canadian members increased defense spending for a third consecutive year, adding $46 billion since 2014 and investing more in equipment, operations and exercises. NATO deployments grew to over 23,000 troops by the end of 2017.

Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg identified Russia’s military actions, election interference, nuclear modernization and alleged nerve-agent attack in Britain as major threats. He said NATO sought neither a new Cold War nor an arms race but would maintain conventional and nuclear deterrence.

NATO also increased its Afghanistan training mission from 13,000 to about 16,000 personnel, supported Afghan-led peace negotiations, trained Iraqi military instructors and planned expanded training and regional support in Iraq, Jordan and Tunisia.

Amazon’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2019 reported Q2 net sales of $63.4 billion, up 20% year over year, operating income of $3.1 billion, and net income of $2.6 billion, or $5.22 per diluted share. Six-month net sales were $123.1 billion, operating income was $7.5 billion, and net income was $6.2 billion.

Q2 segment sales were $38.7 billion for North America, $16.4 billion for International, and $8.4 billion for AWS. Segment operating results were $1.6 billion, a $601 million loss, and $2.1 billion, respectively. AWS sales grew 37% year over year.

For the first six months, operating cash flow was $11.0 billion, while investing and financing activities used $15.7 billion and $4.5 billion. At June 30, Amazon had $191.4 billion in assets, $22.6 billion in cash and equivalents, $18.8 billion in marketable securities, $23.3 billion in long-term debt, and $53.1 billion in stockholders’ equity.

Amazon adopted new lease accounting guidance, recognizing approximately $21 billion in operating lease assets and liabilities. The filing also describes tax disputes, patent litigation, contractual commitments of $134.6 billion, and other contingencies.

QuantifiedStrategies.com provides over a thousand free articles, hundreds of videos, trading courses, and backtested strategies based on statistics rather than opinions. Topics include trading psychology, risk-adjusted returns, money management, orders, position sizing, candlestick patterns, seasonality, indicators, backtesting, algorithmic trading, and multiple strategy types across stocks, forex, futures, and options.

First-quarter GAAP diluted EPS rose 143% to $2.58, primarily because of a $336 million litigation reserve reversal following a favorable court ruling. Fiscal 2017 profit was expected to approach or surpass previous records.

Becton produces medical products including insulin syringes, IV catheters, specimen-collection equipment, and surgical products. Identified risks include manufacturing disruptions, higher interest rates, and competition from more advanced products. The author considers the dividend safe despite its 1.6% starting yield and discloses a long position in BDX.

The study uses CASTEP density functional theory with GGA-PBE and PBEsol to predict the structural, electronic, mechanical, thermal, and optical properties of three previously unstudied o-MAX phases, Mo₂A₂AlC₃ (A = Zr, Nb, Ta). All adopt a hexagonal P6₃/mmc structure. Negative formation energies, absence of imaginary phonon frequencies, and satisfaction of elastic stability criteria indicate chemical, dynamical, and mechanical stability.

Band structures and finite density of states at the Fermi level confirm metallic behavior, with major contributions from Mo-4d orbitals. Density-of-states, charge-density, and Mulliken analyses identify mixed covalent, ionic, and metallic bonding, including strong Mo–C interactions. Mo₂Nb₂AlC₃ has the strongest calculated bonding, greatest stiffness, highest fracture toughness, and greatest machinability, while Mo₂Ta₂AlC₃ has the lowest Young’s modulus. Elastic criteria classify all three compounds as brittle and mechanically anisotropic.

Calculated Vickers hardnesses are 6.025, 6.277, and 6.224 GPa for the Zr-, Nb-, and Ta-containing phases, respectively. Their melting temperatures are 2064–2237 K, Debye temperatures are 526–634 K, and minimum thermal conductivities are 0.74–0.90 W/m·K. Thermal expansion coefficients range from 9.90×10⁻⁶ to 11.47×10⁻⁶ K⁻¹. These thermal properties, together with fracture toughness values of 2.59–2.78 MPa·m¹/², support potential use as thermal barrier coatings.

The compounds show high infrared reflectivity and generally exceed 44% reflectivity across visible to near-ultraviolet ranges, indicating potential for thermal-barrier and solar heat-shielding coatings. Overall, the calculations identify Mo₂Zr₂AlC₃, Mo₂Nb₂AlC₃, and Mo₂Ta₂AlC₃ as stable metallic o-MAX phases with promising high-temperature coating applications.

Celtic’s Ibrox victory demonstrated their superiority over Rangers and highlighted the clubs’ widening financial and sporting gap. The author argues Rangers chairman Dave King has failed to provide manager Mark Warburton with promised investment, while recruitment mistakes and reliance on veterans Clint Hill and Kenny Miller have compounded the problem.

Celtic, strengthened by Brendan Rodgers and successful signings such as Moussa Dembele and Scott Sinclair, have Champions League revenue and potential transfer income available. The author urges Rodgers to invest from a position of strength, both to sustain domestic dominance and build a team capable of competing more effectively against leading European clubs. Celtic should use their current financial advantage ruthlessly, avoiding the missed opportunity to establish lasting superiority after Rangers’ 2012 collapse.

It examines market drivers, constraints, risks, opportunities, trends, policies, technologies, competition, PEST, Porter’s Five Forces, SWOT, and investment feasibility.
