Tesla reported that Jerome Guillen, President of Tesla Heavy Trucking, departed the company effective June 3, 2021. The Form 8-K was signed by Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn on June 7, 2021.

Cowen shares rose 19% after CEFC China agreed to buy a 20% stake for $100 million, provide $175 million in debt financing and appoint three directors. The transaction, subject to approvals, was expected to close by third-quarter 2017.

India’s trucking industry is expected to change substantially by 2027, driven by population growth, urbanisation, rising freight demand and government policies. The nationwide introduction of BS IV and accelerated shift directly to BS VI will challenge manufacturers while creating opportunities for suppliers. The Goods and Services Tax is expected to reduce state-border delays, encouraging long-distance transport and demand for faster, more powerful trucks supported by improved infrastructure.

Domestic manufacturers will likely face stronger competition from established and prospective global OEMs. The government’s Automotive Mission Plan II aims by 2026 to place India among the world’s top three automotive industries, expand exports, increase the sector’s GDP contribution and create millions of related jobs. International fleets, advanced connectivity and full-service packages are also expected to become more prominent.

Unpredictable government actions remain a challenge for industry planning. By 2027, Indian trucks are expected to be larger, faster, stronger, more connected and efficient, while electric and autonomous trucks remain many decades away.

The paper proposes a philosophical framework for ethical, humanizing use of generative AI across online, blended, and in-person education. Anders’s concept of the “Promethean discrepancy” highlights the gap between technological capabilities and humans’ ability to grasp their consequences. Foucault’s “regimes of truth” illuminates how corporations and AI systems can shape knowledge while reproducing errors, hallucinations, biases, and commercial interests. Freire’s concepts of conscientization and humanization support using technology critically to strengthen dialogue, agency, and social transformation.

The authors combine Bloom’s Revised Taxonomy with Arendt’s hierarchy of labor, work, and action. Although AI can perform tasks across Bloom’s cognitive levels, that taxonomy does not address educational purposes or ethical consequences. Arendt’s framework supplies this direction by distinguishing repetitive labor and consumption from durable work and public action intended to influence the world.

The resulting framework places AI use on a spectrum from consumptive labor to humanizing action. AI-generated work falls toward the consumptive end when it lacks personal relevance, contains errors, or requires little thought. Ethical use moves toward humanizing action when students critically assess AI, connect learning to their perspectives, engage with others, and apply knowledge meaningfully. AI should reduce routine burdens without replacing human judgment, dialogue, creativity, or agency.

Illustrative activities include evaluating local political issues and candidates before developing civic action plans, and using AI as a Socratic questioner to support individualized research and community outreach. The paper concludes that educators and instructional designers must continually redesign teaching, learning, and assessment as AI develops, prioritizing critical reflection, human agency, and meaningful action rather than efficiency or content production alone.

The passage describes methods and apparatus for managing reduced processing time in low-latency wireless systems using configurable or short transmission time intervals (TTIs). A wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) may determine and report processing capabilities based on criteria such as TTI length, transport block size, channel or transmission type, timeline, numerology, coding, waveform, and resource allocation. Processing capabilities may include limits for timing advance, receive-transmit time difference, processing time, TTI length, transport block size, or scheduling and HARQ timelines.

A network may configure these capabilities, and the WTRU may calculate processing headroom by comparing a current processing value with its capability. Reports or actions may be triggered when thresholds are crossed, uplink transmissions are suspended or dropped, or processing limits are violated. Actions may include limiting timing advance, suppressing transmissions, stopping time-alignment timers, flushing HARQ buffers, prioritizing transmissions, or sending error or headroom reports.

For uplink grants and HARQ acknowledgments, the WTRU may determine whether sufficient processing time exists between downlink reception and the scheduled uplink transmission, accounting for timing advance. It may transmit only when the available time meets a capability-based threshold.

The passage also outlines example LTE, NR, and WLAN communication architectures, WTRU components, timing relationships, HARQ operation, timing-advance procedures, receive-transmit timing differences, and time-alignment timers. Shorter TTIs reduce latency but also reduce available processing time, particularly when timing advance causes uplink transmission to begin earlier.
An 80-year-old patient was treated on the floor at Gujranwala DHQ Hospital due to unavailable beds. Separately, PML-N workers celebrated Yaum-e-Takbeer and praised Nawaz Sharif.

The disclosure describes devices and methods for executing computational primitives on embedded systems using a processor, streaming engines, memory, and a matrix multiplication accelerator (MMA). The MMA uses multiplier, multiplicand, and result buffers, including ping-pong buffering, and can load, store, and execute in one cycle through an LSE instruction. Configurable components support input and output data types, fixed-point precision, lookup-table expansion, row offsets, and elementwise ReLU.

Streaming engines transfer formatted, multidimensional data streams from cache according to programmable addressing sequences. Processor control software configures the streams, MMA formatting, offsets, nonlinearities, and instruction sequences. Processor-side formatting can provide zero padding, value replication, identity matrices, linked operations, seam or stride removal, and transposition.

The MMA implements primitives by expressing them as matrix operations. Examples include batched small and tiled large matrix multiplication, pointwise multiplication, matrix addition, vector-matrix multiplication, vector summation, affine transformations, two-dimensional convolution, row and column permutation, matrix assignment, and transpose. Small operations may be batched by placing matrices diagonally or block-diagonally in buffers. Large matrices are divided into tiles and processed while loading and storing data in parallel.

Two-dimensional convolution is converted into matrix multiplication using tiled feature maps and filter matrices. Streaming configurations support large or small feature-map tiles, strides, seam removal, and optional output padding.

The device also supports small and large complex FFTs, discrete cosine transforms, one-dimensional convolution and correlation. Small FFTs use DFT matrix multiplication; large FFTs combine column FFTs, twiddle-factor multiplication, row FFTs, and transposition. Large convolutions divide filters into smaller fragments, process shifted inputs, and combine results.

Alternative implementations may use host processors, various processor types, and MMA buffers of different dimensions.

Gunmen attacked U.N. peacekeeping sites in Timbuktu and Douentza, Mali, killing seven mission employees, a Malian soldier and a U.N. peacekeeper, while injuring eight others. U.N. forces killed eight attackers. Mission chief Mahamat Saleh Annadif called both incidents terrorist attacks. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned them, warning that attacks on peacekeepers may constitute war crimes. The U.N. is investigating a possible connection.

Apple narrowly surpassed Samsung in fourth-quarter smartphone sales, shipping 77 million iPhones for 17.9 percent market share versus Samsung’s 76.8 million and 17.8 percent. Apple benefited from holiday demand, while Samsung suffered from the Galaxy Note7 recall and brand damage. Samsung could regain the lead following its March flagship launch, as customers may await Apple’s anticipated 10th-anniversary iPhone in September. Samsung still led annual market share, 20.5 percent to Apple’s 14.4 percent. Chinese vendors Huawei, Oppo and BBK ranked third through fifth, respectively, after displacing Apple and Samsung in China and expanding internationally with feature-rich phones.

Arizona ammunition dealer Douglas Haig was charged with illegally manufacturing armor-piercing bullets after unfired rounds bearing his fingerprints were found in Las Vegas gunman Stephen Paddock’s hotel room. Court records do not indicate whether the ammunition was used in the attack that killed 58 people. Haig said he sold Paddock 720 tracer rounds weeks earlier after meeting him at a gun show and noticed nothing suspicious. His identity became public after it was mistakenly left unredacted in court documents, leading to media attention and death threats. Haig has since closed his ammunition business.

The passage outlines NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the 7 nm Ampere GA100 architecture, for AI, HPC, and data analytics workloads. Its third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32, FP64, BF16, FP16, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. Fine-grained structured sparsity can double Tensor Core throughput.

A100 includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, cache residency controls, and compute data compression. Multi-Instance GPU technology securely partitions one GPU into up to seven isolated instances with dedicated memory-system resources, predictable performance, and fault isolation.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4 offers 31.5 GB/s over x16 connections and supports SR-IOV. A100 also works with NVSwitch, Magnum IO, and Mellanox InfiniBand and Ethernet technologies for multi-GPU and multi-node scaling.

Additional features include improved error containment, asynchronous memory copying and barriers, and hardware acceleration for CUDA task graphs. CUDA 11 supports these capabilities, which aim to improve programmability, utilization, scalability, latency, power efficiency, and workload isolation in cloud data centers, clusters, edge systems, and supercomputers.

The Treasury Department recommended rolling back parts of Obama-era financial regulations to encourage economic growth and public offerings. Proposals include repealing Dodd-Frank’s CEO-worker pay-gap disclosure, allowing companies to privately gauge investor interest before IPOs, raising the annual crowdfunding limit from $1 million to $5 million, and harmonizing derivatives oversight. Republicans and business groups supported the plan, while Democrats and consumer advocates warned deregulation could weaken post-crisis safeguards. Most changes could be implemented by regulators, as broader congressional repeal efforts have stalled.

NIST revised its password guidance, recommending long, simple, memorable phrases instead of frequent changes, special characters, and mixed-case requirements. Adviser Paul Grassi says longer passwords are harder to crack and easier for users to remember. Passwords need not expire because users often make predictable minor changes. Password managers remain useful for generating random passwords but are not required for security.

Stack procedures are supplied as macro-included native assembly code that the host must call. The host defines the execution environment and includes the source locally. These segment-independent routines establish or destroy the stack in stackless mode and can be integrated into assembly or, carefully, C files.

Static benchmarks, data contamination, overfitting, and complex AI mechanisms limit evaluation of general-purpose AI on unforeseen tasks. Future benchmarking should dynamically generate samples, vary task difficulty, and analyze individual capabilities, while adapting psychometric principles for AI. Evaluations should also consider cultural and ethnic values and human-defined safety principles. The DyVal framework addresses these needs by generating low-duplicate, uncertain, on-the-fly samples across complexity levels. It uses computable directed acyclic graphs, with variables and operators representing task entities and relationships, to produce replicable samples with guaranteed ground truth for tasks such as mathematical and logical reasoning.

Raja Jackson, 25, son of retired MMA fighter Quinton “Rampage” Jackson, faces felony battery causing serious bodily injury and misdemeanor battery charges over an August assault at a Los Angeles professional wrestling event. Video showed Jackson slamming wrestler Stuart “Syko Stu” Smith and continuing to strike him after he appeared unconscious. Jackson had earlier said he wanted revenge following a promotional altercation in which Smith hit him with a beer can. Smith reported jaw and head injuries, a lip laceration and lost teeth. Jackson was arrested in September and could face up to four years in prison, potentially increased by a sentencing enhancement. His father condemned his actions.

The study assessed early childhood education in 71 Anganwadi Centers across 25 villages in Mewat, Haryana, using observations, checklists, photographs, and interviews with Anganwadi workers. Most centers lacked safe infrastructure, sanitation, electricity, water, furniture, learning materials, and play equipment. Only 23 centers had safe buildings, three had functional toilets and clean drinking water, and none had mats, desks, or chairs.

Many workers did not meet educational prerequisites and lacked knowledge of school readiness, developmental domains, curriculum, assessment, recordkeeping, and parental involvement. Most relied on repetition and memorization rather than activity-based teaching, while infrequent training and limited community support constrained their work.

The study concludes that rural early childhood education faces interconnected challenges involving infrastructure, educator capacity, socioeconomic conditions, language and culture, parental engagement, and weak monitoring. It recommends standardized essential facilities, adequate learning resources, systematic worker training, stronger assessment and oversight, greater parental awareness, and coordinated action by governments, communities, NGOs, and corporate partners to improve quality and equity in preschool education.

The passage lists errata for AMD Geode CS5535 Revision A3, covering PIT, PIC, DMA, IDE/UDMA, USB, UART, LPC, PCI, power management, clock gating, GPIO, SMB, and debug functions. Notable issues include incorrect PIT and DMA behavior, system hangs from debug-port or invalid I/O accesses, missed interrupts with automatic clock gating, inaccessible UARTs during block or demand DMA, inadequate USB over-voltage protection, PRD prefetch hazards, and UDMA CRC corruption. Recommended mitigations include avoiding unsupported command sequences and illegal addresses, disabling affected features, waiting for DMA completion, defining PRD tables before operations, using external USB protection, and enabling UDMA I/O blocking. ATAC SSMI during DMA generates the expected notification but fails to block IDE I/O; this has no stated operational impact.

LLMs are increasingly used as synthetic respondents and agents in social research, sometimes reproducing survey patterns, experimental effects, and social interactions. However, their probabilistic text generation does not constitute Bayesian inference or sampling from a human population. Outputs arise from static learned weights and decoding methods, without explicit posterior beliefs or calibrated uncertainty.

Repeated LLM queries may violate exchangeability and the martingale property required for coherent Bayesian prediction. Their predictions can depend on generation order and drift as synthetic outputs are added to context, a phenomenon termed “introspective hallucination.” Studies also identify artificially low response variance, misaligned coefficients, position effects, and weaker performance on interactions, novel contexts, and identity-sensitive interventions. Fine-tuning and alignment may improve task-specific mimicry while reducing statistical coherence and generalizability.

LLMs appear predictive largely because they interpolate patterns contained in extensive training data. Scaling, prompting, fine-tuning, and behavioral alignment can strengthen this capability, but success within a domain does not establish a general model of human behavior. A universal “homo silicus” is therefore unlikely; domain- and task-specific agents are more plausible.

Researchers should treat synthetic agents as conditioned, high-capacity predictors rather than calibrated population samples. Their outputs should be validated against human data by subgroup, with dispersion, calibration, and distribution shifts explicitly reported. Synthetic data should preferably augment rather than replace human evidence, including through instrument pretesting, failure detection, sample allocation, and sensitivity analysis. Individual- or task-anchored agents can improve fidelity but remain limited to their validated domains.

Recommended safeguards include independent sampling, avoidance of self-conditioning, randomized order, fixed decoding settings, stress tests across prompts and contexts, out-of-distribution evaluation, confidence intervals that account for human-model mismatch, and limits on effective synthetic sample size. Full reproducibility requires disclosure of prompts, scripts, model versions, decoding parameters, seeds, ordering checks, ensemble procedures, and observed failures.

LLM agents may support near-term prediction, sensitive research, and counterfactual exploration, but their black-box uncertainty and lack of demonstrated Bayesian coherence require narrow claims, transparent validation, and models tailored to specific social questions.

Gary Ackerman’s final “Friday Burrito” of 2000 reviews California’s electricity crisis and argues that the industry needs clearer public messaging focused on consumers’ concerns about rising bills. He proposes emphasizing new generation, greater provider choice, and a reliable provider of last resort.

The newsletter criticizes Senator Steve Peace’s response to high power prices and discusses Kaiser Aluminum’s decision to resell electricity and close a smelter. It examines Southern California Edison CEO John Bryson’s call to re-regulate electricity, explaining how utility undercollections, credit downgrades, and delayed payments threaten Northwest power suppliers and California’s market. It also notes that the CPUC reopened PG&E and Edison rate-stabilization applications.

Federal Energy Secretary Bill Richardson ordered out-of-state suppliers, BPA, and WAPA to provide power to California. The order increased imports but potentially reduced Northwest hydro reserves and affected salmon. Questions remained about payment terms and prices.

WPTF supported the Power Exchange’s emergency request to replace the ISO’s $250/MWh cap on adjustment bids with a mechanism supporting forward transactions; the ISO opposed the request. Correspondents endorsed stronger public relations efforts promoting competition and consumer value.

The next WPTF general meeting was scheduled for February 8–9, 2001, in Scottsdale, Arizona. The newsletter concludes with election-themed humorous poems and Ackerman’s reflection on a meaningful conversation with his son during a drive to hockey practice, followed by holiday wishes.

Toll purchased a Denver property from Mrs. McKenzie, unaware that her minor daughters owned a half interest inherited from their father. Casey had created the defective record title by replacing an unrecorded deed to McKenzie with a backdated deed to Mrs. McKenzie. After Toll learned this, Casey and Mrs. McKenzie agreed to perfect his title through probate and guardianship proceedings at their expense. Although those proceedings differed from the agreement’s literal terms, the court found they validly conveyed the minors’ interests and would provide Toll a merchantable title.

The court held, however, that Casey, who caused the complication and had not fully performed his obligations, could not foreclose until the title issues and related expenses were resolved. Both judgments were affirmed as modified. Toll was ordered to pay Casey the mortgage balance with six percent interest, less Casey’s obligations under the agreement, after which Casey must release the trust deed. Costs were allocated among Toll, Mrs. McKenzie, and Casey. On rehearing, the foreclosure case was remanded to implement the modified judgment, with any necessary extension limited to thirty days; rehearing was otherwise denied.

The 6-quart Instant Pot Ultra is on sale for the first time for $120 at Amazon and Sur La Table, down from $150. Compared with DUO models, it adds an “Ultra” setting for customized temperature, pressure, and cooking time, along with status information and a quick-release button. It also includes nine preset cooking options. Prices may change.

Orthopaedic surgeon Dr Sushrut Babhulkar and MAFSU veterinarians plan to fit Sahebrao, an eight-year-old tiger at Nagpur’s Gorewada Rescue Centre, with a prosthetic front-left paw, potentially a world first for a tiger. The paw was amputated after a 2012 poachers’ trap injury. Doctors will first evaluate and treat a painful neuroma, using portable X-rays to minimize stress, before fitting an infection-resistant silicone prosthesis sourced with help from Germany’s AO Foundation.

Hydrogen peroxide is presented as a versatile household product with 13 uses: diluted as a weekly mouth rinse; mixed with water to lighten hair; applied as ear drops; used to wash produce; combined with baking soda to whiten teeth, clean stovetops, cookware and cutting boards; poured into toilet bowls; used to disinfect toys and reusable bags; diluted for a foot soak; applied cautiously to stains; and used in diluted form to soak plant seeds. Produce should be rinsed thoroughly, mouth rinsing should be limited, and fabrics should be spot-tested because peroxide may cause stains.

Micro E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures (MNQ) provide exposure to the Nasdaq 100 Index at one-tenth the size of E-mini contracts. Traded electronically on CME Globex, each contract equals the index value multiplied by $2. Contracts expire quarterly in March, June, September, and December and are cash-settled based on the index’s special opening quotation, typically on the third Friday.

The minimum price fluctuation is 0.25 index points, worth $0.50 per contract; calendar spreads have a $0.10 tick value. Trading generally runs Sunday evening through Friday evening, with daily maintenance breaks. There is no block-trade eligibility.

Trading requires a funded futures-broker account and involves significant leverage risk, as losses are based on the contract’s index value rather than deposited margin. CFDs offered by some brokers differ because they can trade indefinitely without contract expiration.

A trading strategy may use technical and fundamental analysis, defined entry and exit points, position sizing, and risk management. The passage describes a proprietary backtest using continuous, back-adjusted CME data and daily closing prices but does not disclose its rules. It states that futures performed better in spring and fall than in winter and summer.

Reported historical levels are a low of 6,628.75 in March 2020 and a high of 16,676.50 in November 2021. Prices are affected by major index components, macroeconomic reports, interest-rate policy, economic conditions, and sociopolitical events.

Former Trump aide Sebastian Gorka endorsed John McCann in New Jersey’s 5th District Republican primary, praising his support for Trump’s “America First” agenda. McCann faces Steve Lonegan, a former Trump critic who now supports him. The winner will challenge Democratic Rep. Josh Gottheimer.

Muhammad Iqbal Khan recalls his son Mashal as an exceptional student who loved learning. Four days before his death, Mashal criticized problems at Abdul Wali Khan University, including administrative vacancies, fees, and teachers holding multiple posts. His father says university staff framed him. On April 13, 2017, students chased Mashal before he was shot and killed; several suspects were later arrested. Khan calls for justice and political unity so students can attend school without fear. Though no government representative visited him, he finds hope in public demonstrations affirming Mashal’s innocence and wants his son’s memory to endure.

UnitedHealth Group appointed Duke Health chief data scientist Michael Pencina as its chief AI scientist. Pencina has advocated greater oversight and transparency for health care AI and co-founded the Coalition for Health AI, which develops standards for testing and oversight.

Accern rated Celyad’s media sentiment somewhat positive at 0.19, with an impact score of 45.69 indicating coverage was unlikely to affect its share price soon. Piper Jaffray maintained a buy rating and raised its target to $49, while BidaskClub and ValuEngine rated shares hold. Celyad fell 5.15% Friday to $60.70, with a $578.19 million market capitalization. The Belgium-based company develops stem cell therapies for cardiovascular disease, including C-Cure.

Bayern Munich players selected 99-rated versions of themselves for FIFA 18’s featured Squad Battle, alongside Messi, Brazilian Ronaldo, Vieira, Matthaus, Maldini, Alaba and Neuer, creating a formidable Ultimate Team lineup.

Leveraged ETF trading is a short-term strategy using funds that employ debt and derivatives to amplify an index’s daily returns, commonly by 2:1 or 3:1. Inverse ETFs gain when the tracked index declines. Leverage magnifies both profits and losses, while fees, transaction costs, daily rebalancing, and volatility decay generally make these funds unsuitable for long-term holding.

Day trading or short-term swing trading is presented as the most effective approach. Risks may be managed through diversification across traditional, leveraged, and inverse ETFs, as well as stop-loss orders, though alternatives may be preferable. Traders should examine fund components, tracked indexes, market conditions, liquidity, and volatility. Performance and risk can be evaluated with measures such as the Sharpe ratio, Jensen’s alpha, and the appraisal ratio.

For US taxpayers, short-term profits are generally taxed as ordinary income, while holdings exceeding one year receive long-term capital-gains treatment; individual circumstances depend on domicile and should be reviewed with a tax adviser.

A backtest showed a leveraged QLD strategy producing higher average gains and annual returns than an unleveraged QQQ strategy, but not double the performance because of time decay. QLD also suffered losses exceeding 35% during the financial crisis. A less robust strategy produced a maximum drawdown above 55%, illustrating that leveraged ETFs can rapidly erase gains and create psychologically difficult losses. The central warning is that leverage can force traders to abandon otherwise effective strategies during severe drawdowns.

The passage highlights seven Indian entrepreneurs and their app-based start-ups. Sachin and Binny Bansal founded Flipkart, later acquired by Walmart and valued at USD 15 billion. Vijay Shekhar Sharma launched Paytm in 2011; it gained momentum during the 2016 demonetization and was valued at USD 9.4 billion. Kunal Behl and Rohit Bansal developed Snapdeal after starting the coupon business MoneySaver; Snapdeal was valued at USD 6.5 billion. Former Microsoft employee Bhavish Aggarwal built Ola Cabs into a major affordable transport service, valued at USD 5 billion in 2015. Deepinder Goyal and Pankaj Chaddah created Zomato by digitizing restaurant menus; it operated in about 23 countries and was valued at USD 1 billion in 2016. College dropout Ritesh Aggarwal founded OYO Rooms, valued at USD 250 million. Shashank ND founded healthcare platform Practo, which operated in 15 countries, listed medical providers and stored patient records, and was valued at USD 650 million.

Kanawha County deputies arrested Zachary Steele, 21, after he allegedly assaulted his father, stole his parents’ vehicle, fled police, and threatened himself and a police K9 with a knife. A deputy incapacitated him with a less-lethal bean bag. Steele faces domestic battery and fleeing charges.

Namibia’s defence ministry said temporary furloughs and utility savings address budget cuts while prioritizing training and transport. Seventy percent of troops remain active, with furloughed personnel recallable if needed, ensuring security and sovereignty.

JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon, a longtime Bitcoin critic, said blockchain technology is “real” and that stablecoins and JPMorgan’s deposit token could have practical uses. The bank operates Kinexys, a private, permissioned blockchain intended to improve transactions such as intraday repos. However, Dimon said blockchain has limitations, will not replace every system, and can be “a solution looking for a problem.” He declined to comment on Bitcoin.

The TLV322x open-drain output supports external pull-ups from 0 V to 5.5 V, logic-level translation, and OR’ing multiple outputs. TI recommends 100 µA to 1 mA pull-up current. Lower resistance improves rise time but increases low-level voltage and power; resistance above 1 MΩ increases RC rise time. Outputs must not be shorted directly to voltage sources; use current limiting if shorts are possible. Unused outputs may float or connect to V−.

Inputs and outputs include rail-referenced ESD protection. Inputs should remain within 0.2 V of the rails, with clamp current limited to 10 mA. TLV321x power-on reset holds outputs low for up to 32 µs after the supply crosses 1.65 V.

A comparator outputs low or high according to the relationship between input and reference voltage; swapping inputs reverses the logic. Propagation delay varies by transition and increases at low overdrive, especially below 100 mV. External positive-feedback hysteresis can prevent chatter near the switching threshold and adds to the device’s 1.8 mV internal hysteresis. Inverting configurations use three resistors, while non-inverting configurations use two resistors and a reference voltage.

A low-side current-sensing example uses an amplifier and comparator to assert a high alert above 1.1 V. Supply pins require closely placed, low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic bypass capacitors. Inputs must remain in range for single or split supplies. Layout should minimize input-output coupling, use solid grounding, and may employ output series resistance or controlled-impedance traces to reduce ringing.

TI states that application guidance and linked resources are provided as-is; users are responsible for component selection, design validation, testing, compliance, and ESD-safe handling.

One Nation leader Pauline Hanson announced conditional support for the Federal Government’s media ownership reforms, potentially ending a political deadlock. The changes would abolish rules limiting cross-media ownership and preventing one TV broadcaster from reaching more than 75 per cent of Australians. In return, the Government agreed to investigate the ABC’s balance and regional commitment, seek disclosure of staff remuneration above $200,000, and provide an additional $12 million for community radio. Labor and the Greens oppose the reforms, arguing they would reduce media diversity. The legislation is expected before Parliament this week.

A June 4, 2001 collection of Enron-related reports covers corporate, energy and international developments. Disclosures showed White House adviser Karl Rove held substantial stock in Enron and other major companies affected by administration policies while awaiting authorization to divest. Other senior officials also had financial ties to energy companies.

Saudi Arabia signed agreements worth at least $25 billion with nine international oil companies, including Enron, to develop natural gas fields, power plants, pipelines and desalination projects. The deals marked the sector’s first major foreign investment since nationalization in 1975.

Enron’s $2.9 billion Dabhol power project faced escalating disputes with Maharashtra’s electricity board over unpaid bills, high power costs and contract termination. Indian and foreign lenders planned talks in Singapore, while rating agencies warned the dispute could damage India’s investment climate. India’s power minister pledged to uphold contracts and pursue reforms involving private sales, utility restructuring, tariff changes and reduced distribution losses.

Other reports criticized Enron’s role in California’s energy crisis and its performance on a Nigerian power project. Spectron brokered a UK gas-electricity “spark spread” deal between Enron and Powergen. Enron Japan’s chief said genuine competition remained absent from Japan’s partially deregulated electricity market and that prices were substantially higher than in the United States.

Technology Education Corporation (TEC) appealed judgments awarding three former students $5,225 each for breach of educational-service contracts. The students contracted with Paraprofessional Institutes of Ohio, whose school assets were later sold to Educational Leadership Corporation (ELC) and then to TEC. They alleged misrepresentation of the course of study and placement services.

The appellate court considered whether TEC could be liable solely as a successor corporation. Although successor corporations may be liable when they assume liabilities, participate in a merger, continue the seller’s corporate entity, or engage in a fraudulent transaction, none applied here. The incorporated asset purchase agreement expressly excluded liabilities arising before TEC’s purchase, except specified liabilities that did not include student contracts. Knowledge of pending litigation did not imply assumption of liability, and the parties were free to allocate liabilities contractually.

TEC also was not a mere continuation of ELC. Although school operations continued, no evidence showed common stockholders or directors, or that TEC was not a separate corporate entity. Providing the same services alone was insufficient.

The court further found that, even if successor liability applied, the students had not proved their contractual claims; the trial court had summarily imposed liability while deciding TEC’s motion to dismiss. The appellate court sustained TEC’s assignments of error, reversed the judgment, and remanded the case for further proceedings.

Across Phases 1–3, injection-site and systemic reactions within seven days of BNT162b1, BNT162b2, or BNT162b2SA vaccination were generally mild or moderate, short-lived, and well tolerated. Injection-site pain was the most common local reaction; tiredness and headache were the most common systemic events. Findings after booster doses were similar to those in the larger Phase 2/3 population.

Phase 1 doses of 10, 20, and 30 µg were well tolerated, except 100 µg BNT162b1, which was stopped after Dose 1 because of reactions. The 30-µg BNT162b2 dose was selected for Phase 2/3. In Phase 2/3, fewer than 1% of participants left because of medical problems, and most problems were mild or moderate.

Serious medical problems were uncommon, with no single event affecting at least 1% of any group. Researchers considered most serious problems unrelated to vaccination, although a small number in participants aged 16 years or older were considered potentially related. No vaccine-related serious problems occurred among participants aged 12–15 years.

No deaths occurred in Phase 1. During Phase 2/3, 85 participants initially receiving BNT162b2, 62 initially receiving placebo and later BNT162b2, and 23 receiving placebo before any BNT162b2 died from various causes; researchers did not consider the deaths caused by BNT162b2. No deaths occurred among BNT162b2-naive Phase 3 participants receiving BNT162b2SA.

U.S. stocks rose after ADP reported 263,000 private-sector jobs added in March, exceeding forecasts of 187,000. The Nasdaq briefly reached a record high, while the Dow gained 0.84%, the S&P 500 0.67%, and the Nasdaq 0.53%. All major S&P sectors advanced, led by financials and technology. Investors awaited Federal Reserve meeting minutes and a meeting between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. Amazon hit a record high, and Panera Bread surged after JAB Holdings announced a $7.16 billion acquisition.

The Chande Momentum Oscillator (CMO), introduced by Tushar Chande in 1994, measures momentum by comparing the sums of recent higher and lower closes:

CMO = 100 × (SHc − SLc) / (SHc + SLc)

It ranges from −100 to +100. Positive values indicate strength and negative values weakness, depending on trend direction. Readings above +50 suggest overbought conditions, while readings below −50 suggest oversold conditions. Divergences between price and CMO swings may signal reversals, and a 9-period moving average can serve as a signal line.

The CMO cannot reliably identify the main trend, so it is best combined with trendlines, moving averages, price action, or other indicators. Traders can use it to identify the end of pullbacks, support momentum strategies, or trade range boundaries in sideways markets. Its signals are trend-dependent and may be unreliable in volatile, directionless markets or during strong trends when extreme readings persist.

Suitable periods and timeframes depend on the asset, strategy, and trading style and should be determined through backtesting. A backtest on dividend-adjusted SPY using a 9-day CMO and a maximum five-day holding period produced high risk-adjusted returns and lower drawdown than buy-and-hold; longer holding periods reduced returns.

Germany, France, Britain, Spain and Italy warned the Trump administration that proposed U.S. tax measures could violate treaties, discriminate against foreign companies and breach World Trade Organization rules. Their finance ministers objected to taxes on multinational affiliate payments and cross-border financial transfers, as well as a Senate provision favoring U.S. exporters. The warning came as Congress worked to reconcile competing tax bills.

Students at Atlanta’s Ron Clark Academy celebrated after learning they would see “Black Panther.” Teachers will incorporate the film and comics into lessons on imperial history, African art, math, science and physical education. A video of the students dancing during the announcement went viral on Twitter.

The patent describes techniques for preventing ransomware from encrypting files by using an endpoint agent to monitor file-system activity in protected directories. A mini filter driver injects virtual honeypot files and folders into directory-query results, placing them near the beginning and end so ransomware is likely to target them before genuine files. When accessed, virtual entries are redirected to a small set of actual forged files stored in a dedicated location.

The agent monitors operations such as opening, deleting, renaming, writing to, or changing information for honeypot files, as well as enumerating honeypot directories. Unauthorized or dangerous activity can trigger policy-based responses, including denying access, terminating the associated process, generating alerts, notifying users, or logging activity. Legitimate processes may be exempted through configurable exception lists, and honeypot entries can be hidden from users by recognizing shell-based directory requests.

Honeypot file names, types, contents, sizes, dates, protected paths, exceptions, and responses are configurable through policies and management interfaces. The virtual approach uses minimal storage, avoids residual files across protected directories and mounted volumes, and reduces maintenance overhead while increasing the probability of stopping ransomware before it encrypts genuine files. The techniques may be implemented across desktop, mobile, and server operating systems.

Research Report Insights forecasts the global corrugated packaging market to grow at a 4% CAGR from 2014 to 2020, reaching US$173.6 million. Growth is driven by rising e-commerce, industrial production, shipments, population, incomes, and demand from medicine, rubber, food, consumer durables, and petroleum industries. Corrugated packaging is favored for its low cost, sustainability, reliability, and easy handling, but low durability and slow adoption in some industries constrain growth. Products include liner board, container board, sheets, and boxes, with A, B, C, E, and F flute types. Major production centers include China, India, Japan, the U.S., several European countries, Brazil, and Turkey. Leading companies are pursuing expansion in emerging markets amid substantial merger and acquisition activity.

Sterling traded narrowly but rose 0.2 percent against both the dollar and euro ahead of Britain’s formal triggering of Article 50. Analysts viewed the move as largely symbolic, saying the EU’s response, negotiations and UK economic performance would matter more. Strong inflation, possible Bank of England rate increases and dollar weakness recently supported the pound, though it remains nearly 20 percent below its pre-Brexit level. Retail customers were nervous, while companies had increased hedging. Risks included a hard, prolonged Brexit, economic weakness and a possible second Scottish independence referendum.

This study maps primary science education research through bibliographic coupling and co-word analysis of 2,295 English-language Web of Science publications using VOSviewer. Primary science education supports curiosity, critical thinking, scientific literacy, and STEM interest, but faces limited resources, insufficient teacher preparation, rigid curricula, and unequal digital access.

Five intellectual clusters were identified: technology-enhanced instruction using augmented and virtual reality; equity, engagement, and teacher competence; cognitive and metacognitive supports; dialogic and integrative pedagogy; and artificial intelligence, computer science, and computational thinking. Co-word analysis similarly highlighted scientific discourse and literacy, teacher beliefs and professional development, achievement and conceptual change, and technology integration in STEM. Overall, research is shifting toward student-centered, inquiry-based, digitally mediated, and equity-oriented approaches.

The study proposes the DIG-EDU-QUEST framework, integrating culturally responsive inquiry, pedagogical practices, technological affordances, and sociocultural equity. It emphasizes dialogic teaching, teacher development, meaningful technology use, inclusive curriculum design, and policy support. Remaining gaps include culturally responsive computational thinking, teacher identity in reform, equitable digital access, and scalable interventions in resource-constrained settings. Future research should incorporate qualitative methods and broader, multilingual databases to improve global representation.

The human microbiota consists of trillions of bacteria and other microbes that support digestion, metabolism, immunity and inflammation. Disruption of gut microbiota may contribute to conditions including asthma, obesity, colitis and colon cancer. Research shows that microbiota composition and activity follow daily circadian rhythms and may also influence the host’s rhythms.

In mice, microbial metabolites circulating in the blood changed throughout the day and altered liver gene expression and metabolism. Antibiotics and changes in feeding times modified these patterns. Gut microbiota also affected the liver’s ability to process acetaminophen, with overdose toxicity varying by time of day. These findings suggest medication timing could influence effectiveness and side effects.

Advances in DNA sequencing, analytics and computing enabled researchers to study complex microbial communities, whose members often depend on one another. The findings may be relevant to people taking long-term antibiotics and shift workers eating at biologically unusual times, potentially linking microbiome disruption with obesity and metabolic syndrome.

Under GST, e-way bills are required for goods consignments exceeding Rs50,000 to curb tax evasion. The GST Council exempted 153 items, including LPG for households, PDS kerosene, food products, animals, jewellery, currency and household effects. Exemptions also cover non-motorised transport and certain port transfers. The system, expected after NIC software is ready, requires shipment details and enables tax officials to track goods after states dismantled border checkposts.

Center for Diagnostic Imaging Miami offers imaging and preventive screening services using advanced technologies under board-certified physicians, radiologists and technicians. Services include X-rays, PET/CT, CTA, MRI, ultrasound, mammography and nuclear medicine. Its Total Body Scan combines CT imaging of the head, neck, chest, abdomen and pelvis with cardiac calcium scoring and a physician consultation within 24–48 hours. The center also provides screenings for breast, ovarian and prostate cancers and nuclear medicine tests for cardiac, bone and thyroid evaluation.

Multi-organ imaging genetics integrates AI-derived quantitative endophenotypes with genetic data to support aging, disease, and precision-medicine research. Progress has been driven by large multi-omics datasets such as UK Biobank and FinnGen, open access to GWAS summary statistics through public platforms, and computational methods including LDSC and Mendelian randomization.

Previous work generated 2,024 multi-organ AI endophenotypes: 2,003 brain structural covariance patterns, nine neuroimaging measures of heterogeneity across four brain diseases, and 12 biological age gaps across nine organ systems. Their UK Biobank GWAS statistics were released through the MEDICINE portal. FinnGen and the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium also publicly released extensive disease-related GWAS results.

This study uses UK Biobank, FinnGen, and consortium resources to characterize the genetic architecture of the 2,024 endophenotypes and 525 disease endpoints with more than 5,000 cases. These include 521 FinnGen endpoints and Alzheimer’s disease, ADHD, bipolar disorder, and schizophrenia from the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium. It also systematically benchmarks and compares genetic statistical methods.

Massachusetts probation officials seek clarification on Michelle Carter’s stayed sentence, including how monitoring and potential violations should be handled during her appeal. A hearing is scheduled for August 21; Carter is excused from attending.

Energy Central’s January 30, 2002 newsletter compiles electric power and gas industry news. Major topics include Enron’s restructuring under acting CEO Stephen Cooper, investigations into its collapse and political influence, energy-market oversight, utility mergers, deregulation, pricing, transmission projects, renewable energy, environmental regulation, corporate financial results, and international energy developments. Other highlights include plans for a common New York–New England electricity market and World Energy Solutions reporting over $250 million in 2001 online energy transactions.

Police negotiators spent several hours persuading a distressed man to leave the Cambridge Mill roof while officers controlled roads and crowds. The man moved around the roof, apparently seeking an escape route, before approaching negotiators and surrendering as onlookers applauded. Items he discarded, some suspected stolen, were recovered nearby. He was taken to Cambridge Memorial Hospital for a mental health assessment, with charges pending. Restaurant staff later assessed damage, possible theft and how he entered, while management thanked emergency services for ensuring a safe outcome.

The passage argues that existing employers’ liability laws are inadequate because workers and their families should not bear the costs of unavoidable industrial injuries and deaths. The full trade risk should fall on employers, who can incorporate it into production costs, and federal protections should include employees in navy yards and arsenals.

It also supports compulsory federal investigation of labor disputes. From 1881 to 1900, strikes and lockouts displaced millions of workers and caused an estimated $450 million in losses to employees and employers, alongside substantial public hardship. A neutral federal commission on conciliation and arbitration could reduce misunderstandings, encourage settlements, protect both sides from stronger opponents, and represent the public interest. Its decisions would not be legally binding but could mobilize public opinion, allowing reform to proceed cautiously.

Kapil Sibal forgave Arvind Kejriwal and Manish Sisodia after they apologized for baseless allegations against him and his son. The allegations had prompted Amit Sibal to file a defamation suit against Kejriwal.

After ratifying a reciprocity treaty, Hawaii’s King sought a commercial treaty with Japan, opposed by the U.S. minister as harmful to American trade. In 1868, President Johnson argued that reciprocity would stabilize Hawaii and preserve it from foreign control until its people voluntarily sought U.S. annexation. Reports described growing annexation sentiment in Honolulu, though Secretary Seward postponed consideration because of Reconstruction. The United States also unsuccessfully protested the importation of laborers into Hawaii, which continued under foreign influence. In 1871, Minister Henry A. Pierce urged renewed consideration of annexation, describing it as Hawaii’s likely political destiny. President Grant confidentially sent Pierce’s dispatch to the Senate, requesting its views without offering his own recommendation.

Clemson food scientist Paul Dawson found that double-dipping transfers substantial bacteria into shared dips. Double-dipped water contained 1,000 more bacteria per milliliter. Salsa initially had about 1,000 bacteria per milliliter, five times more than chocolate syrup or cheese dip, though acidity reduced its count after two hours. Single-dipped samples showed no bacteria. Double-dipping can spread mouth bacteria and diseases, including flu, herpes, and Legionnaires’ disease.

Longtime Circle K cashier Eric Whitcomb, 49, was fatally shot near his Lake Elsinore store early Wednesday as his shift ended. The motive remains unknown, and the gunman is at large. Authorities are reviewing surveillance footage, while Circle K is cooperating with the investigation. A GoFundMe was created for Whitcomb’s family.

An active weather pattern brings snow, wintry mix and rain Tuesday, followed by arctic air with highs mainly in the 20s and 30s and lows in the single digits and teens. Another chance of snow arrives Friday, with partly sunny conditions Saturday and milder weather Sunday.

In 2015, Quest Diagnostics hired MaryAnn Camacho to lead its National Customer Service organization, which had been consolidated from 20 regional call centers into facilities in Lenexa, Kansas, and Tampa, Florida, plus remote staff. The consolidation reduced regional expertise and created incompatible processes and systems, while most experienced regional representatives declined to relocate.

The centers handled about 55,000 calls daily, mainly requests for test results. Performance problems included waits exceeding two minutes, low first-call resolution, high labor costs, inconsistent information, and lost customers. Sixty percent of representatives left within their first year, costing Quest up to $10.5 million annually. Across Quest, employee turnover generated an estimated annual loss of $50–70 million.

Representatives received six weeks of training, but understaffing sometimes prevented hands-on coaching. Regional differences made call routing difficult, while supervisors spent long hours covering absences, answering escalated questions, and resolving employee and customer problems. Unplanned absenteeism reached 12.4%, and many supervisors and representatives lacked adequate preparation.

Quest’s leadership identified four immediate priorities: step-based pay, career paths, supervisor development, and improved workforce planning. Camacho began by observing operations and interviewing employees. The specification describes SD card interfaces, operating modes, initialization, data transfer, protection, and command behavior.

- In UHS-II mode, unused SD interface lines must not be driven by the card and must be held at defined levels by the host. UHS-II initialization includes PHY initialization, device initialization, enumeration, configuration, and SD-TRAN initialization.
- ROM cards are read-only devices, excluding write-protected writable cards. They treat write and erase commands as illegal, may optionally support CMD42 and security commands, and full-size ROM cards have no write-protect switch.
- UHS-I supports DS, HS, SDR104, and DDR50 modes, reaching 104 MB/s with an SDR104-capable host and UHS104 card. UHS-I requires SD mode and 1.8 V signaling for SDR50, DDR50, and SDR104. ACMD41 negotiates support, CMD11 performs voltage switching, ACMD6 selects 4-bit mode, and CMD6 selects driver strength, speed mode, and power limit. CMD19 provides tuning.
- UHS-II modes include FD156, optional HD312, FD312, and FD624, with maximum throughput up to 624 MB/s. Hosts supporting UHS-II must also support the legacy SD interface and fall back to it if UHS-II signaling is not detected within the timeout.
- Application Performance Classes specify minimum random and sequential performance. Cache, self-maintenance, command queueing, and low-voltage initialization are defined as optional performance-related features.
- Hosts control all communication using broadcast or addressed commands. Cards operate in identification mode until assigned an RCA, then enter data-transfer mode. Initialization uses CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3. CMD8 verifies interface voltage, while ACMD41 negotiates voltage, capacity, power, and 1.8 V support.
- Reads and writes use block-oriented transfers with CRC protection and generally support blocks up to 512 bytes. CMD12 stops multiple-block transfers. Write buffering may allow new blocks while earlier blocks are programmed, with DAT0 indicating busy status.
- ERASE uses CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38. DISCARD may deallocate selected blocks and is supported only by SDHC and SDXC outside SPI mode. FULE logically erases the entire user area and has similar restrictions.
- Write protection includes a host-managed mechanical switch, optional internal protection, and password locking. CMD42 manages passwords, locking, unlocking, and force erase.
- Card Ownership Protection adds a Force Erase Password and COP-specific CMD42 functions. With FEP set, COP Unlock is required after reset, ordinary force erase and password clearing are disabled, and authenticated FEP Force Erase is available.
- CMD55 marks the following command as application-specific. CMD6, mandatory for Version 1.10 and later cards, selects access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit while the card is in Transfer State.

The Money Flow Index (MFI) is a momentum indicator combining price and volume to measure money flowing into and out of a security. It ranges from 0 to 100 and identifies overbought, oversold, and potential reversal conditions. Common thresholds are above 80 for overbought and 20 or below for oversold, though traders may adjust them. Bullish and bearish divergences between price and the MFI can also signal reversals.

The default lookback is 14 days. Longer periods produce fewer, potentially more reliable signals, while shorter periods generate more signals and false positives. Optimal settings depend on the market and strategy and should be determined through backtesting. Signals generally work better in range-bound markets; in trending markets, traders are advised to use them in the trend’s direction.

A strategy combining MFI extremes with bullish or bearish engulfing patterns was tested. Since 2000, Pepsi produced 581 trades, a 0.42% average gain, 71% win rate, 1.8 profit factor, and 10.4% annual return while invested 39% of the time. SPY achieved a 10.6% CAGR while invested 35% of the time. A combined Pepsi-SPY portfolio returned 15% annually with 48% market exposure. The strategy performed poorly on gold.

This bibliometric content analysis examined 273 full-text studies on modern physics education in Turkey published between 2000 and 2023. Using the Modern Physics Education Publication Classification Form, researchers analyzed publication characteristics, topics, objectives, methods, samples, interventions, data collection and analysis, validity, reliability, findings, discussions, and recommendations. Most studies were Turkish-language articles published through Tübitak Ulakbim, with research concentrated between 2010 and 2019 and declining in recent years. Common topics included atoms, the photoelectric effect, relativity, nuclear energy, and the Compton effect. Studies frequently investigated instructional effectiveness and students’ cognitive and affective characteristics. Quantitative research favored quasi-experimental and survey designs, while qualitative research mainly used case studies. Purposive sampling was common, undergraduate education students were the largest participant group, and samples typically contained 31–100 people. Interviews, tests, questionnaires, and scales were widely used; frequency and percentage analyses, t-tests, and content analysis predominated. Many studies inadequately reported sampling, intervention duration, validity, reliability, or research design. Instructional methods and materials generally improved achievement, understanding, problem-solving, and attitudes, although misconceptions and negative responses persisted. Textbooks and curricula were often criticized for unclear, unsuitable, or insufficient content and continued reliance on classical physics perspectives. Discussions were commonly supported by literature but often lacked adequate explanation. The study recommends broader topics, larger samples, mixed and qualitative methods, varied analyses, enriched interventions and materials, longer durations, stronger validity and reliability reporting, and curriculum and textbook development reflecting modern physics philosophy.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for automatically recognizing objects, particularly products, in video or image content and presenting related information to viewers. A media device or server selects frames according to an adjustable frame-selection rate, partitions selected frames into image blocks, and uses machine-learning algorithms to identify regions containing potential products. Likelihood metrics, based partly on the frame-selection rate and recognition error rates, are compared with thresholds to determine recognition accuracy. Analysis may iteratively focus on smaller regions, use stored-image matching, or incorporate accompanying audio. Frame rates, partitions, parameters, and thresholds may be adjusted through user feedback, accuracy analysis, or updates shared among devices and servers to balance accuracy and computational efficiency.

The system may include media devices, content, product, and merchant databases, a media server, and a network. Product and merchant databases can provide descriptions, prices, brands, inventory, store locations, payment methods, and purchase links. Recognized products may populate title profiles, lists, widgets, or digital shopping carts displayed alongside or overlaid on content.

Shopping carts can be populated in real time, after a delay, or from prior recognition results. They may provide recommendations, merchant links, advertisements, and direct or third-party purchasing options. Product selection and ranking may be personalized using viewer transaction data, browsing history, social-media data, communications, viewing history, stated preferences, sizes, colors, brands, and price ranges. Users may correct erroneous recognition, identify products manually, adjust frame-selection rates, and interact through touchscreens or external devices. Implementations may use hardware, software, or non-transitory computer-readable media containing processor-executed instructions.

Altermagnetism is a compensated magnetic phase that breaks time-reversal symmetry while preserving its combination with crystallographic symmetries, producing momentum-dependent spin splitting and nodal structures without spin-orbit coupling (SOC). Using group theory and density functional theory, the study identifies and quantifies real-space atomic magnetic multipoles in MnF₂, CrSb, and KMnF₃ by projecting spin densities onto tesseral harmonics.

In MnF₂, the lowest uncompensated collinear multipole is an octupole, consistent with d-wave altermagnetism, while higher-order 32-poles also occur. In g-wave CrSb, collinear dipoles and octupoles cancel, leaving a 32-pole as the lowest uncompensated collinear multipole. Although both materials have collinear atomic dipoles, SOC generates smaller noncollinear spin-density components with symmetry-allowed octupoles and 32-poles. These noncollinear multipoles grow linearly with SOC strength, whereas SOC modifies collinear multipoles only quadratically.

In KMnF₃, fluorine-octahedral rotations remove anti-translation symmetry and convert the magnetic state from antiferromagnetic to altermagnetic. The resulting uncompensated 32-pole increases linearly with the octahedral rotation angle, while the dipole density remains nearly constant.

The identified multipoles constrain macroscopic response tensors, including piezomagnetism and second-order magnetoelectric effects. The results emphasize that noncollinear spin density, higher-order multipoles, SOC, and structural distortions are important for describing altermagnets and predicting their observable responses.

Both teams have defended well collectively, including goaltending and shot blocking. Momentum can shift quickly and must be earned every shift. ECB policymakers said eurozone prospects had improved but support should remain, amid uncertainty over France’s election and potential bond-market turmoil.

This study used CiteSpace 6.2.R2 to analyze research trends connecting open and vocational education in China and other countries from 2012–2023. Chinese literature came from CNKI, while international literature came from Web of Science. Analyses covered keyword networks, timelines of research hotspots, and citation bursts.

Chinese research primarily emphasized the integrated and coordinated development of open and vocational education. After 2016, attention shifted from separate development models toward integration involving teaching models, curricula, practical instruction, credit recognition, and institutional coordination. Since 2018, terms related to integration and coordinated development have shown strong citation bursts.

Research outside China focused more on adult education, vocational training, lifelong learning, and online learning than on the direct relationship between open and vocational education. Since 2018, studies increasingly examined online learning for adult vocational learners, including motivation, self-regulated learning, digital literacy, blended learning, technology, and personality. From 2020, online learning and vocational education and training received especially strong attention.

The study concludes that regional priorities differ: China emphasizes institutional integration, whereas other countries emphasize adult skills development and technology-supported learning. It recommends further quantitative and visual research on integration practices, policy frameworks, industry collaboration, technological innovation, and the use of big data and statistical models.

The invention provides multiple-factor verification for computer-vision-driven interactions by combining at least two complementary monitoring systems with a verification system. It is primarily described for retail applications such as automatic or expedited checkout, where independently generated evaluations of selected items or customer activity are compared to identify discrepancies, improve accuracy, reduce adversarial vulnerabilities, and determine whether checkout should proceed or require alternative handling.

Monitoring systems may include computer vision, RFID or radio-frequency tags, smart shelves and scales, user applications, smart carts, point-of-sale systems, customer-profile prediction, and security-tag barriers. Computer-vision systems may identify and track people, products, interactions, gestures, and events using distributed cameras and other sensors. Systems may operate as primary or secondary monitors, exchange roles by location or condition, provide full or partial coverage, and generate outputs such as virtual carts, candidate items, behavioral assessments, confidence scores, or historical risk predictions.

The method executes separate monitoring systems, generates independent evaluations, determines their alignment, and triggers actions based on that alignment. Alignment may involve comparing checkout lists, verifying a subset of selected items, evaluating confidence levels, identifying discrepancies, or incorporating customer history. Resulting actions may permit, halt, or modify checkout; alert or direct workers to inspect customers or specific products; update customer profiles; control alarms or barriers; recommend operational changes; or provide training feedback to improve monitoring systems.

Example implementations include validating computer-vision checkout with RFID tags or smart shelves, using computer vision to detect errors or theft at point-of-sale systems, verifying customer-entered purchases in applications or smart carts, combining computer vision with security barriers, and using historical profiles to adjust confidence thresholds. The approach may improve reliability, reduce unnecessary inspections and false alarms, support user coaching, detect manipulation or shoplifting, and enable monitoring systems to improve through operational feedback.

The 1-3-1 zone is a versatile defense suited to matching up, disrupting passing lanes, and trapping. It spreads the offense and encourages vulnerable cross-court or corner passes. Its main weaknesses are corner shots and rebounding, particularly on the weak side. All defenders must move together, anticipate passes, and remain active with extended arms.

Personnel typically includes a strong rebounder on the left wing, a quick baseline defender covering corner to corner, and possibly a tall player at the top. As the ball moves, the point defender covers the ball or ball-side elbow, wings alternate between pressure and weak-side support, the baseline defender covers corners, and the middle defender stays between the ball and basket to protect post areas and stop penetration.

Adjustments address skip passes, closeouts, and role exchanges between baseline and middle defenders. The compact “Three in a Line” variation keeps a large defender near the basket while wings cover corners.

The alignment supports hard or soft traps, especially in corners where sidelines and baselines restrict the ball handler. Trappers should pressure without fouling or reaching, trace the ball with both hands, and force difficult passes. Off-ball defenders deny post and sideline options, anticipate passes, and prepare for transition opportunities. The defense can extend into quarter-court, half-court, or full-court pressure.

Missouri legislation could offer free online courses to K-12 public school students as early as next summer if signed by Gov. Eric Greitens. Districts or charter schools would pay, expanding access to courses unavailable in rural or financially troubled schools. Critics cite poor performance among full-time virtual students and fear expansion into virtual charter schools. Schools and the state education department would oversee course quality and publish annual outcome data. Enrollment requests could be denied based on a student’s educational interests, with appeals handled locally and then by the state.

The study assessed cardiovascular disease risk through lipid profiles among HIV-positive patients receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART) at the University Teaching Hospital of Butare, Rwanda. HIV infection and ART are associated with lipid abnormalities—including elevated total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol and triglycerides, and reduced HDL cholesterol—which may increase cardiovascular risk despite ART’s substantial reduction of HIV-related morbidity and mortality.

A cross-sectional study was conducted from January to February 2021. It included 150 HIV-positive participants on ART and 49 HIV-negative controls. Participants with hepatitis B or C, abnormal thyroid hormones, pregnancy, hypertension, kidney disease, diabetes, alcoholism or obesity were excluded. Serum total cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL and LDL were measured spectrophotometrically. Data were analyzed using SPSS, with P≤0.05 considered statistically significant.

Among the ART group, 51 participants were male and 99 female, with ages ranging from 29 to 75 years and a mean age of 49.4 years. Most received first-line ART (72%), while 26% received second-line and 2% third-line treatment. Hypertriglyceridemia occurred in 48 participants (32%), low HDL levels in 29 (19.3%), elevated LDL in 12 (8%), and elevated total cholesterol in 23 (15.3%). Most lipid abnormalities occurred among participants receiving first-line regimens.

Compared with controls, ART recipients showed significant differences in triglycerides (P=0.046), LDL (P=0.039), HDL (P=0.021) and total cholesterol (P=0.045). No control participant had high triglycerides, while 89.8% had normal triglyceride levels.

The study concluded that HIV-positive patients receiving ART had significant lipid-profile changes associated with cardiovascular risk. It recommends routine lipid-profile assessment for people living with HIV, broader studies in other Rwandan health facilities, and additional cardiovascular testing such as troponin, creatine kinase-MB, C-reactive protein and electrolytes. Findings may support health policies for early cardiovascular disease detection, prevention and management among ART recipients.

A giant teddy bear called Big Ted visited Warwick East State School for students’ last day, delighting children and staff. Part of a Blackbird and Finch promotion, the bear also appeared at local events and shopped at the Uber Markets.

The application describes screen display methods, apparatuses, electronic devices, storage media, and program products for managing multiple application interfaces. When one application is displayed full screen and another appears as a floating window, an operation on the full-screen interface may automatically minimize the floating window into a floating ball, application icon, contact avatar, or video pop-up window. If an edit box gains focus, other interfaces may be minimized and positioned away from the cursor; when focus is lost, they may be restored. Operating a floating interface may display it full screen while minimizing the original full-screen interface and other floating windows.

For interfaces initially displayed side by side without overlap, an operation on one interface may maximize it and minimize the other. Losing edit-box focus or operating the minimized interface may restore split-screen display. The methods support multiple floating windows and user-adjustable window size, shape, location, transparency, and content arrangement. An Android-based implementation may use touch-event processing and the window manager to adjust interface parameters. The electronic device may include processors, memory, a display, communications modules, sensors, cameras, audio components, and related hardware and software layers. The approach reduces the operations needed to minimize obstructing interfaces and facilitates input and viewing.

Other work included roofs, fencing, concrete, paint, walkways and storage. About $88 million remains for future plumbing, drinking fountains, windows, doors and upgrades at additional schools.

Random numbers are essential in cryptography for key generation, encryption, and decryption, requiring unpredictability and robustness. Software pseudorandom number generators use deterministic mathematical models and seeds, making sequences vulnerable if the seed and model are discovered. Hardware generators use physical hardware sources, producing less predictable numbers better suited to cryptography. AMD “Zen” processors include a cryptographic coprocessor for secure random-number generation, accessible through the AMD Secure RNG library’s software API.

Stan Bowman and coach Joel Quenneville credit organizational stability, strong leadership, coaching, player development, depth, and a resilient veteran core for the team’s sustained success and return to the final. They praise Jonathan Toews’s competitiveness, preparation, accountability, leadership, and ability to excel in crucial moments.

Bowman acknowledges future salary-cap-driven roster changes but expects the main players to return and younger players such as Saad and Teravainen to assume larger roles. He says injuries, including Patrick Kane’s absence, prompted others and newly acquired players to contribute, while roster depth gave coaches flexibility.

Quenneville emphasizes the team’s ability to recover from injuries, losses, and other difficult moments. Both describe Brad Richards as an experienced center who improved as he adapted to the system, gained playing time with Kane, and provided offensive skill and defensive reliability.

Bowman says young players generally need gradual development, often in the American league, before taking major NHL roles. Experienced players handle difficult matchups while younger players adjust to the league. Although Tampa’s run is respected and available information is being studied, the immediate outcome will depend on execution.

The announcement followed Turkey’s capture of Afrin after a nearly two-month offensive. Kurdish forces withdrew with fleeing civilians and vowed guerrilla resistance, while the EU and United States expressed humanitarian concern and reports emerged of looting by Turkish-backed rebels. Ankara considers the YPG an extension of the PKK. Turkey plans to establish governing structures in Afrin and allow some Syrian refugees in Turkey to return.

The team remains behind in the series, but the victory created momentum, with the next game crucial to getting fully back into contention. The passage argues that Russia could not claim sovereignty over the open waters of the Okhotsk Sea, citing an arbitration decision rejecting British sovereignty over the broad Bay of Fundy. Russian notices, diplomatic correspondence, and official publications also acknowledged that Russian jurisdiction extended only through ordinary territorial waters. Evidence showed the Cape Horn Pigeon was seized beyond even Russia’s former claimed boundary and had not reentered Russian waters after leaving Vladivostok. Russia did not defend the seizure as enforcement of exclusive fishing rights, but attributed it to the commander’s suspicions. Consequently, Russia assumed responsibility for resulting damages unless it established a wrongful act by the vessel’s occupants within Russian jurisdiction.

United Airlines beat Q1 2017 earnings estimates and maintained strong Q2 guidance despite a passenger-removal scandal. It projected PRASM growth of up to 3% and pre-tax margins of 10%–12%, despite higher costs. The article considers the stock undervalued at about 8.7 times forward earnings and expects earnings growth as costs normalize. The author disclosed a long position in UAL and emphasized that investing carries risks.
The speaker says prior success can be built on, talk is over, and the team must play its game. Home ice drives momentum, demanding solid play.

This cross-sectional study evaluated the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio (P/C ratio) as an indicator of kidney damage in adults with urinary tract infections. Eighty patients were recruited at Padmashree Diagnostics, Bangalore; after excluding those with low urinary creatinine or no proteinuria, 46 remained for analysis. Their mean age was 38.11 years, and 67% were female.

Participants were classified by P/C ratio as Stage I (<15 mg/mM; 12 patients), Stage II (15–50 mg/mM; 16), or Stage III (>50 mg/mM; 18). Mean urinary creatinine declined across stages and was significantly below the reference interval. Mean urinary protein increased from 2.6 mg/dL in Stage I to 48.5 mg/dL in Stage III, while the mean P/C ratio rose from 9.0 to 180.6 mg/mM. Stage III urinary protein elevation was statistically significant.

The findings showed an association between UTIs and proteinuria and identified the spot P/C ratio as a reliable marker for assessing UTI-associated renal impairment. Longitudinal studies were recommended to evaluate prognostic and therapeutic significance.

TSLA options grant the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell shares at a specified price by a certain date. They offer leverage, portfolio hedging, speculation, and potential profits but involve complexity and the risk of substantial or complete losses.

Common strategies include long calls, long puts, covered calls, and spreads. Strategy selection should reflect risk tolerance, investment goals, market outlook, potential returns, and associated risks. Available orders include market, limit, and stop orders.

The passage emphasizes backtesting and quantified analysis to identify trends, entry and exit points, and possible statistical advantages. It recommends having a clear trading plan, avoiding overtrading and discretionary judgments, and using risk-management measures such as stop losses and profit-taking. Fees depend on the broker and may include commissions, platform, regulatory, and margin charges. Liquidity varies by contract, expiration, volume, and premium, while tax treatment depends on the trade and country and may require professional advice.

Amazon elected Daniel P. Huttenlocher to its Board and Leadership Development and Compensation Committee effective September 7, 2016. He received restricted stock units for 1,131 shares, vesting in three equal annual installments beginning November 15, 2017, subject to continued service, and entered into the company’s standard director indemnification agreement.

Ernesto Guevara, Che Guevara’s youngest son, runs La Poderosa Tours with his wife, offering six- or nine-day Harley-Davidson motorcycle tours of Cuba. Costing about $3,000 to $6,000, the tours attract international enthusiasts, including growing numbers of Americans.
