From April 2017 to April 2018, Employment Minister Patty Hajdu’s department developed speaking points and media guidance on Canada Summer Jobs eligibility. New rules required applicants to attest respect for human rights, including reproductive, gender-diverse and transgender rights, to prevent funding organizations with conflicting mandates or projects. Officials said religious groups faced the same criteria and were not assessed on beliefs. Religious organizations objected to the wording, but no change was promised. Justice Hyeladzira Nganjiwa failed to stay his trial on 14 charges involving alleged $260,000 fraud, N8.6 million corrupt enrichment and false information. He pleaded not guilty and received bail. His lawyer sought suspension pending an appeal challenging the lower court’s jurisdiction.

A study found that grape-derived polyphenols may help treat depression by targeting inflammation and synaptic dysfunction, mechanisms not specifically addressed by current antidepressants. In mice, two compounds—dihydrocaffeic acid and malvidin-3′-O-glucoside—promoted resilience against stress-induced depression-like symptoms by modulating systemic inflammation and brain synaptic plasticity. Researchers suggest these compounds could become therapeutic agents for some people with depression and anxiety.

Japan’s Financial Services Agency conducted a surprise inspection of cryptocurrency exchange Coincheck after hackers stole $530 million. The regulator said it had identified security flaws before the theft, which prevented Coincheck from receiving full operating approval. The exchange stored coins in an internet-connected “hot wallet” and lacked multi-signature security. Inspectors examined customer compensation, finances, system management and consumer protection. Coincheck promised to repay about $425 million, though regulators had not confirmed it had sufficient funds. The FSA ordered Coincheck to report on the breach and prevention measures and required all Japanese exchanges to review system risks. Police and international authorities are investigating the theft involving NEM cryptocurrency. The hack intensified scrutiny of Japan’s cryptocurrency regulation amid broader regulatory concerns and falling bitcoin prices.

Published by Johns Hopkins University Press, the journal will support Creighton’s Center for Henry James Studies while offering students research and learning opportunities.

The disclosure describes autonomous vehicle systems using a machine-learned yield model. Sensor and map data feed perception and prediction systems that identify objects, estimate their states and trajectories, and generate features such as relative position, required acceleration or deceleration, traffic-signal timing, available intersection space, and temporal traffic gaps. The yield model processes these features to recommend yielding, proceeding, stopping, or selecting a particular gap.

A motion-planning system converts yield decisions into trajectories, potentially using scenario controllers, gap penalties, cost functions, and iterative optimization. The model can also prevent gridlock by assessing whether sufficient space exists to exit an intersection. Vehicle controllers execute selected plans through steering, braking, and acceleration controls.

The model may use decision trees, random forests, neural networks, or other machine-learning architectures. It can be trained through supervised learning on labeled real-world or simulated driving logs. Labels may be assigned manually or automatically by comparing the scores of yielding, stopping, and gap-traversal outcomes.

The approach is intended to improve safety, comfort, adaptability, scalability, processing speed, and memory efficiency while reducing reliance on manually designed rules. Models may operate onboard or through networked computing systems and can be retrained as new data or autonomy-system improvements become available.

The President explains his veto of a public-works appropriation bill by arguing that the Constitution grants Congress no general authority to establish a system of internal improvements. Because the federal government possesses only delegated powers, broad phrases such as “general welfare” cannot override the Constitution’s enumerated powers. Improvements may be federally funded only when necessary to execute specific powers, including military, naval, postal, commercial, or public-property functions.

A general federal program covering roads, canals, railroads, harbors, education, hospitals, and similar projects would greatly expand federal spending, employment, patronage, and political influence while weakening state action and private enterprise. The authority over federal sites and “needful buildings” likewise permits only facilities required for expressly granted federal functions.

Historical practice supports federal construction of lighthouses, beacons, buoys, and some navigation aids, though the constitutional boundary for river and harbor improvements remains unsettled. Early Congresses generally limited navigation spending to marking hazards, while broader improvements began in 1824. Federal statutes and Supreme Court decisions extended maritime jurisdiction to navigable interstate and foreign waters, including lakes and inland rivers, but this jurisdiction does not itself establish unlimited improvement authority.

The President urges caution because river and harbor appropriations can exceed constitutional limits, produce inadequate benefits, and favor local interests at national expense. The passage describes container-based patterns for distributed systems. The ambassador pattern separates application logic from communication logic. A client-side ambassador can route requests to storage shards, broker environment-specific services, or split traffic between production and experimental systems while applications connect to localhost. Examples use Kubernetes, Redis, twemproxy, nginx, and ConfigMaps. Client-side ambassadors simplify backend services but complicate client deployment; centralized routing services have opposite trade-offs.

The adapter pattern modifies an application’s interface to conform to common operational standards. Separate adapter containers can translate monitoring metrics, normalize logs, redirect file output to stdout, or provide rich health checks without modifying third-party application images. Examples include adapting Redis metrics for Prometheus, using fluentd plugins for Redis and Storm logs, and adding query-based MySQL health monitoring. This modularity enables independent updates, resource isolation, reuse, and shared operational knowledge.

Microservices divide applications into independently maintained components communicating through defined APIs. They improve team autonomy, release agility, reliability, and independent scaling, but make architecture and debugging more complex. Distributed patterns provide reusable approaches to these challenges.

Replicated load-balanced services use interchangeable instances for availability and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching instances before initialization. Session tracking can consistently route users to particular replicas, preferably through application-level identifiers when external addresses are affected by network translation. Additional replicated layers can provide caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service defense, and SSL termination.

Sharded services divide state or requests among specialized replicas when data exceeds one machine’s capacity. Sharded caches improve memory utilization but make individual shard failures more consequential. Replicating each shard improves availability and permits independent scaling of hot shards. Effective sharding requires deterministic, uniform functions and carefully selected keys. Consistent hashing limits remapping when shard counts change. Routing may use per-client ambassadors or shared routing services, with trade-offs in deployment complexity, scaling, latency, and network traffic.

Scatter/gather systems send work to multiple nodes in parallel and combine partial results, reducing processing time or searching data distributed across shards. Excessive parallelism introduces request overhead, slow-node effects, and reduced reliability because completion depends on all required responses. Replicating each shard supports failures, upgrades, and greater capacity.

Function-as-a-service provides event-driven, automatically scaled execution and shortens deployment from source code to running service. Its strong decoupling promotes modularity but complicates observability, dependency analysis, and debugging. FaaS is poorly suited to long-running background work, applications requiring substantial in-memory data, or sustained traffic where per-request pricing may become inefficient.

Research suggests outdoor light exposure reduces children’s risk of developing myopia, while near work, computer use and television are not important causes. Myopia occurs when the eye grows too long to focus distant light properly, requiring lifelong corrective lenses and potentially increasing the risk of serious eye disease later in life.

A 20-year study of 4,979 children found that children with two myopic parents and little outdoor time had about a 60 percent chance of needing glasses. Spending roughly 14 hours outdoors weekly lowered this risk to about 20 percent. However, outdoor time has little or no effect on myopia progression in children who already wear glasses.

The leading explanation is that bright outdoor light stimulates retinal dopamine, promoting normal eye growth. Exercise and vitamin D are other proposed factors. Children should still use sunscreen and sunglasses to limit ultraviolet exposure.

The lecture introduces link-cut trees for maintaining a dynamic forest of rooted, unordered trees. They support creating vertices, linking a root beneath a node in another tree, cutting a node from its parent, finding a tree’s root, and aggregating values such as minima, maxima, or sums along root-to-node paths. The presented version achieves \(O(\log n)\) amortized time per operation using splay trees.

The represented forest is decomposed into preferred paths determined by recent accesses. Each preferred path is stored as an auxiliary splay tree ordered by node depth. Auxiliary trees are connected through path-parent pointers representing nonpreferred edges. An access operation makes the root-to-node path preferred and moves the accessed node to the root of the overall auxiliary-tree structure by repeatedly splaying nodes, removing obsolete preferred edges, and joining path segments.

Other operations reduce largely to access. Finding a root accesses a node and locates the leftmost node in its auxiliary tree. Path aggregation uses subtree information maintained in auxiliary trees. Cutting accesses the node and removes its left subtree connection, while linking accesses nodes in separate trees and joins their auxiliary structures.

The analysis uses heavy-light decomposition. An edge is heavy when its child subtree contains more than half the nodes of its parent’s subtree; otherwise it is light. Any root-to-node path contains at most \(O(\log n)\) light edges. This bounds preferred-child changes by \(O(\log n)\) amortized per operation, initially yielding an \(O(\log^2 n)\) bound. Applying the splay-tree access lemma makes the costs telescope, improving the total to \(O(\log n)\) amortized time per operation. A more complicated worst-case \(O(\log n)\) version directly maintains heavy-light paths with weight-balanced trees.

The paper investigates how early-stage startups develop Internet-of-Things systems. IoT development combines software, hardware, connectivity, data, and domain expertise, creating challenges not fully addressed by traditional software engineering methods, particularly for resource-constrained startups.

Researchers conducted an exploratory multiple-case study of eight IoT startups selected from 241 candidates. Data included 12 semi-structured interviews with founders, executives, and engineers, supplemented by documents and public information. Thematic analysis used four SEMAT Essence elements: team, system, work, and way of working.

Most startups lacked all required competencies and relied on consultants, component and cloud-service providers, contractors, and manufacturers. Software development was the dominant internal engineering competence. Their systems pursued Internet-centric, thing-centric, or combined value propositions and began development from either application or perception layers.

Three types of minimum viable products were identified: “looks-like” MVPs that simulate the final experience; functional “works-like” MVPs demonstrating capabilities; and quality-focused MVPs emphasizing performance, scalability, security, integration, and testing. Startups generally progressed from simulated prototypes toward functional and quality-oriented systems, although development durations varied considerably.

Common working practices included in-house design, outsourced implementation and manufacturing, rapid prototyping, reuse of ready-made hardware and software components, and iterative or Agile development. Tools such as 3D printing, CAD, Arduino, and Raspberry Pi accelerated prototyping. Hardware development required longer cycles, made frequent releases costly, and introduced vendor, platform, and competence dependencies. Agile practices were applied situationally rather than systematically.

The findings are limited by small case numbers, reliance on one interview for most cases, and concentration on Pakistani and Scandinavian startups with bootstrap financing. The study concludes that IoT startups favor speed through rapid prototyping, iteration, reuse, and outsourcing, while hardware complexity requires adaptations to software-oriented startup methods.

Postpartum vaginal bleeding occurs after both C-sections and vaginal deliveries because the placental site continues to bleed and shed tissue, called lochia, as the uterus returns to its pre-pregnancy state. Bleeding may resemble a heavy period with small clots for several days, should gradually lessen, and usually ends within four weeks. Contact a physician if it lasts beyond six to eight weeks, soaks a pad hourly for two hours, includes large clots, or accompanies fever, rapid heartbeat, shortness of breath, dizziness, or lightheadedness. After a C-section, limit activity, avoid heavy lifting and certain activities, stay hydrated, and eat healthy meals.

The Commodity Channel Index (CCI) is a momentum oscillator comparing a security’s current price with its average price over a selected period. Readings above +100 are generally considered overbought and below −100 oversold, though reversal levels vary by security. CCI can also signal emerging trends and bullish or bearish divergences, but divergence is only a warning of possible change.

CCI is calculated from typical price—the average of high, low, and close—its moving average, and mean deviation. It was introduced in 1980 for commodities and later adopted for stocks and ETFs. Similar indicators include RSI, ROC, Stochastics, and MACD.

The passage states that CCI works best for mean-reverting assets, particularly stocks and partly bonds, using daily bars and short lookbacks of about five to nine days. Its advantages are quantifiable identification of overbought and oversold conditions. Its limitations include lagging price, weak trend detection, no precise entry timing, and prolonged extreme readings.

A backtest on SPY selected a nine-day lookback, buying below −90 and selling when the close exceeded the previous day’s high. It produced a profit factor near 1.8, an average gain of 0.55% per trade, and a 23% maximum drawdown, though the strategy may be curve-fitted. The passage concludes that short-term oversold signals in stocks are the best CCI approach, while noting that other indicators, including RSI, may perform better.

Pneumococcal disease causes substantial global morbidity and mortality, particularly among young children, adults aged over 65, and people with underlying conditions. Pre- and post-marketing data identified no unexpected safety concerns. A registered phase 4 randomized, double-blind, active-controlled noninferiority trial compared its immunogenicity, tolerability, and safety with Pneumovax in Chinese children, adults, and elderly people.

HPC as a service (HPCaaS) enables manufacturers to scale computing resources, avoid large upfront infrastructure investments, and develop data-based products, services, and business models. Respondents also view HPCaaS as a means to outsource infrastructure operations or use HPC without building their own systems. IDC recommends establishing virtual product and manufacturing development, adopting a holistic data strategy and single source of truth, and selecting an HPC operating model based on utilization, budget, performance, flexibility, security, and available skills. The findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 technology decision-makers from industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Inflation is a broad rise in prices that reduces a currency’s purchasing power. Major causes include rapid money-supply growth, excess demand, higher production costs, and expectations of continued inflation.

High inflation generally increases stock-market volatility and hurts stocks in the short term. Consumers have less money to spend and invest, businesses face higher input and borrowing costs, and central banks may raise interest rates. Excessive rate increases can contribute to recession and market declines. Over time, however, companies may pass higher costs to consumers and stocks may resume rising.

Value stocks may outperform during inflation, while highly valued growth stocks and dividend-paying stocks can become less attractive. Potential inflation investments include diversified index funds, stocks, bonds, commodities, gold, real estate, REITs, and Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities. TIPS are government-backed bonds whose payments reflect inflation changes.

A described S&P 500 backtest based on inflation and interest rates produced poor results, supporting the conclusion that stocks perform poorly during high inflation, at least in the short term.

The Second Circuit reversed and vacated a preliminary injunction preventing H. P. Hood from supplying dairy products to Grand Union and Finast warehouses for transshipment into Jackson Dairy’s exclusive distribution territory. Jackson alleged that the arrangement breached its distributorship agreement and disrupted customer relationships and delivery routes.

The court held that preliminary relief requires irreparable harm plus either likely success on the merits or serious questions and a balance of hardships favoring the applicant. Jackson failed to show irreparable injury because lost sales, profits, customers, and route disruptions could be adequately compensated through calculable monetary damages. The court did not address Hood’s remaining arguments or whether permanent injunctive relief might later be justified by other evidence.

Judge Mansfield concurred but preferred reversal based on Jackson’s failure to show a contractual violation. He found that Hood had no contractual duty to prevent independent customers from transshipping products into Jackson’s territory and that no evidence showed Hood controlled, encouraged, or participated in the chains’ conduct.

A treaty with Nicaragua is submitted to the Senate for ratification, providing for a canal connecting the Atlantic and Pacific. The canal is presented as essential to U.S. national unity, defense, commerce, and prosperity because existing sea routes are lengthy and hazardous and railways cannot fully meet transportation needs.

The treaty respects Nicaraguan sovereignty and does not contemplate U.S. territorial acquisition or political control. Nicaragua would provide the territory and the United States the financing. The canal would be open peacefully to all nations on equal terms, with possible preferential tolls for the two countries’ coastal trade. Railway and telegraph lines could also be constructed, and the United States would lend Nicaragua $4 million for related internal improvements.

The proposed route uses Lake Nicaragua and the San Juan River, requiring locks and between 43½ and 53½ miles of canal excavation. It would offer sailing vessels a route from New York to San Francisco ten days shorter than the Panama route.

The canal is expected to expand trade with South America and Asia, strengthen commerce between U.S. coasts, reduce transportation costs and discriminatory practices, and shorten major voyages. Its commercial traffic and lower construction costs are expected to make it remunerative, although national benefits are considered more important than investment returns. Congress is urged to approve the treaty, provide legislation for prompt construction, recognize citizens who performed preliminary work, and consider using the Army Engineer Corps to build the canal.

Bibliotherapy uses selected texts, reading, and discussion to help readers address developmental, academic, behavioral, or mental health concerns. Its central processes include identification, catharsis, insight, and sometimes universalization. Educational bibliotherapy differs from targeted clinical bibliotherapy and may use self-help texts, fiction, poetry, social stories, shared reading, writing, or online discussion. Appropriate book selection should consider goals, age, developmental level, relevance, engagement, and cultural context.

This systematic review followed PRISMA-P and examined 35 peer-reviewed studies published from 2006–2021. The studies used varied quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods, preventing meta-analysis. Overall, findings associated bibliotherapy with improvements in socio-emotional behavior, academic skills, self-esteem, hope, resilience, anxiety, depression, and some stress outcomes. It also helped readers reflect on problems, discuss trauma, and develop socially appropriate behaviors. However, some outcomes were nonsignificant, and students sometimes found sessions boring.

Practitioners reported limited awareness, formal training, time, resources, and reader engagement. The review was also limited by small samples, restricted institutional settings, incomplete methodological reporting, varied interventions, and possible cultural differences. The authors conclude that bibliotherapy may support diverse educational goals, but clearer definitions, stronger evidence, improved training, and a unified framework are needed.

VN-HGCN is a heterogeneous graph convolutional network designed to capture long-range information without predefined meta-paths or deep layer stacking. It adds type-level virtual nodes, randomly connects original nodes to virtual nodes of the same type, and links all type-level virtual nodes through a central node. This structure reduces the maximum path between any two original nodes to four hops. Virtual nodes are initialized from connected-node feature means, while drop-edge is used to reduce overfitting.

The model projects different node types into a shared feature space, performs normalized node-level aggregation, and applies attention-based type-level aggregation to update embeddings. Its stated time complexity for \(N\) layers is \(O(N|A|(|V|+|E|))\). The virtual-node strategy can also be incorporated into existing heterogeneous graph models.

Experiments on ACM, DBLP, and IMDB node-classification datasets compared VN-HGCN with meta-path2vec, HAN, MAGNN, HGT, HetSANN, SimpleHGN, ie-HGCN, and a virtual-node variant of ie-HGCN. Across training ratios from 20% to 80%, VN-HGCN achieved the best results in most settings, including 17 of 24 Macro-F1 and Micro-F1 comparisons on ACM and DBLP. Adding virtual nodes improved ie-HGCN particularly at lower training ratios and increased sensitivity to perturbations from distant nodes, indicating stronger long-range information propagation.

Parameter analysis found stable performance across hidden dimensions and numbers of type-level virtual nodes. Performance improved from two to four layers but declined beyond four, consistent with over-smoothing. The authors conclude that virtual nodes provide a simple, adaptable approach to long-range heterogeneous graph learning, while noting that complete resolution of over-smoothing, scalability to large datasets, and dataset-specific selection of virtual-node counts require further study.

Cleveland engineering and construction manager Khalil Ewais attempted to resign in 2015, citing low pay and responsibilities beyond his job description, but withdrew after supervisors promised staffing changes and continued consideration of a raise. Federal agents later searched City Hall, seizing records concerning Ewais’s side business, Pioneer Engineering, several properties and Burton Scot Contractors. Authorities have not disclosed the investigation’s purpose. Ewais stated in a 2017 internal audit that he had no business or financial interests involving the city and said Pioneer work would not interfere with his city duties. Planning records showed Pioneer sought approval to pave two parking lots at addresses included in the seizure. Burton Scot, awarded at least $7.4 million in city paving contracts over three years, said it would cooperate with investigators.

SimulRAG is a simulator-based retrieval-augmented generation framework for long-form scientific question answering. It addresses two challenges: translating between textual questions and numerical simulator inputs and outputs, and updating long answers with fine-grained control. Its retrieval interface uses simulator handbooks and an LLM to extract parameters, execute simulations, and convert outputs into textual context.

The generation method produces diverse answers, decomposes them into deduplicated atomic claims, and selectively verifies claims against simulation results. Selection combines claim-level uncertainty estimation with simulator boundary assessment (UE+SBA), which filters claims that simulators cannot verify. Verified claims are retained, corrected, or left unchanged depending on their alignment with simulation evidence, while low-confidence claims may be removed.

The authors construct climate-modeling and epidemiology benchmarks containing 200 free-form questions each. Ground-truth answers are based on simulator outputs and human verification. Experiments using GPT-4o and Claude-3.5 Sonnet compare SimulRAG with input- and output-layer RAG baselines. SimulRAG generates 30.4% more unique true claims and achieves 16.3% higher factuality than the best baselines. UE+SBA consistently outperforms random, verbalized-uncertainty, and uncertainty-only claim-selection methods across F1, AUPR, and AUROC metrics. Boundary assessment filters 34.5% of climate claims and 41% of epidemiology claims on average, reducing unnecessary verification. Using a 45% verification budget produces performance comparable to verifying all claims. A stated limitation is the assumption that questions relate to available simulators; future work could detect question-simulator relevance automatically.

Post-cardiac-surgery hyperglycemia is common and associated with adverse outcomes, while standardized insulin protocols may cause both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia. Researchers developed GLUCOSE, a distributional offline reinforcement-learning model that recommends personalized hourly regular-insulin doses during the first postoperative day.

GLUCOSE was developed using 6,148 cardiac-surgery patients from MIMIC-IV and externally validated using 649 patients from eICU-CRD. It evaluates more than 70 clinical features, including current and recent glucose levels, weight, vasopressor use, mechanical ventilation, and SOFA scores. The model used conservative Q-learning with Implicit Quantile Networks to represent uncertainty in patient outcomes.

Estimated performance was significantly better than observed clinician performance in internal testing and external validation. Time in the target glucose range of 70–180 mg/dL was highest when administered doses matched GLUCOSE recommendations. Compared with endocrinologist recommendations, GLUCOSE had lower dosing error than treating clinicians and performed comparably to intensivists and nurse practitioners. Blinded expert assessment rated its safety, effectiveness, and acceptability as comparable or superior to human dosing policies.

Limitations include the retrospective design, restriction to the first postoperative day, omission of explicit dietary data, and exclusion of many external-dataset patients with ambiguous medication records. Prospective studies and randomized controlled trials are needed to evaluate clinical effectiveness and safety.

A forwarded October 2001 essay by Arundhati Roy argues that the U.S.-led bombing of Afghanistan is another act of terror that will kill civilians, worsen hunger, fuel anger and create future terrorists. Roy criticizes the absence of UN authorization, Western governments’ histories of warfare and support for armed groups, the Northern Alliance’s record, food airdrops as inadequate publicity gestures, expanding surveillance and restrictions on civil liberties, and limited independent media access. She portrays both the Taliban and U.S. policy as forms of fundamentalist hegemony, while linking the war to defense-industry and oil interests, including prospective Central Asian pipelines. Although she says the September 11 perpetrators must be brought to justice, she questions whether war can achieve that goal and calls for an immediate end to the bombing.

USD/CAD remains neutral within 1.2968–1.3211. Breaking 1.3387 would favor gains beyond 1.3598, while falling below 1.2968 would signal bearishness. Longer term, the corrective pattern could target 1.2075 if 1.2460 breaks.

An analysis of 2023–2024 campaign contributions by attorneys and staff at the 100 top-grossing U.S. law firms and 50 larger plaintiffs-side firms found that 92.45% went to Democrats. Democratic-affiliated groups received about $52 million, compared with $4 million for Republican-affiliated groups, a shift from a 6-1 ratio in 2017–2020 to roughly 12-1. Cleary Gottlieb had the highest Democratic share at 99.7%, followed by Fried Frank at 99.4% and Mintz Levin at 99.1%. Nelson Mullins had the lowest Democratic share among top-grossing firms at 66.4%, followed by Lewis Brisbois at 77.3% and Ogletree Deakins at 81.5%.

The Missouri Court of Appeals affirmed an order requiring Max Gibson to specifically perform a property settlement agreement with his former wife, Annetta, and to pay her attorney fees and costs. The agreement required Max to secure future maintenance payments through a life insurance trust. After the parties substituted whole life policies for term insurance, Max created a trust retaining his right to use or encumber the policies’ cash value. The court held that deleting this provision enforced, rather than altered, the agreement because allowing Max to deplete the cash value could impair Annetta’s security.

The court also found that Annetta pleaded and enforced the same agreement. Venue was proper in Platte County because the parties had contractually agreed that the court handling their dissolution would retain jurisdiction to interpret and enforce the agreement. Filing a claim against Max’s estate was not an adequate legal remedy because it was less certain and effective than specific performance. Finally, Annetta was entitled to attorney fees and costs under the agreement’s indemnification provision because Max had failed to perform and she was the successful litigant.

The address describes postwar social and economic readjustment as a major test of civilization, emphasizing that all groups must share its burdens. Although the United States has recovered comparatively well, coal and railway strikes hindered progress, while agricultural distress remains a national concern.

Congress is urged to expand farm land, production, and livestock credit through Federal land banks and to improve transportation. The address calls for coordinating railways, waterways, sea carriers, and motor trucks; consolidating railway facilities; pooling freight cars; reducing costs on farm products and basic commodities; and securing fair returns on railway investment. Government operation is rejected. An impartial, enforceable labor tribunal connected with the Interstate Commerce Commission is proposed to resolve major railway disputes and prevent service disruptions while protecting workers’ wages, conditions, and individual rights.

The new tariff is defended as protection for American living standards, with flexible duties intended to support industry, prevent consumer exploitation, and preserve beneficial trade. International cooperation is endorsed without accepting foreign burdens, dictatorship, alliances, or supergovernment.

Domestic concerns include revolutionary advocacy, divided national loyalties, disrespect for law, and widespread violations and corruption surrounding prohibition. Strict enforcement and cooperation between Federal and State governments are recommended.

The address supports alien registration, overseas immigration screening, Americanization and education of immigrants, Federal educational assistance, and constitutional amendments authorizing child-labor regulation and restricting tax-exempt securities. It also recommends reclamation, forest protection, study of fuel problems and price spreads, cooperative purchasing, integrated power development, and plans to mobilize national resources for future defense.

Internationally, the address highlights naval limitation, the four-power Pacific pact, peaceful consultation, mediation of disputes, and conferences among Central American nations. It concludes that the United States should defend its rights, respect those of others, promote peace and rehabilitation through moral influence, and avoid assuming responsibilities that belong to other nations.

The “Chase” offense attacks a Box-and-One defense by exploiting the chaser’s limited post-defense preparation and isolating the star player in the middle with four outside feeders. Its primary action uses a high-post back screen and dribble penetration to create space for the star. If unavailable, options include screen-and-roll action, a base screen, weakside two-player action, give-and-go cuts, high-post screens, and back cuts through double screens that flow into single/double continuity.

Effective execution requires coordinated screens, strong post-ups, defensive recognition, timing, communication, and experience. Recommended preparation includes whole-part-whole teaching, breakdown drills, shell drills, and scrimmaging. Teams should scout opponents’ screen and post defenses, identify matchups, monitor adjustments after substitutions and timeouts, vary alignments and entries, and attack weaker defenders. In a Box-and-One, four defenders guard zones in a box while a chaser aggressively denies one opponent passes and rebounds.

Valtteri Bottas topped the dry but occasionally damp practice session ahead of Lewis Hamilton and Sebastian Vettel, despite crashing at Spoon, damaging his front wing, floor and right rear, and ending his running early. Kimi Raikkonen later caused a second red flag by crashing heavily at Degner.

Limited running from the previous day contributed to a busy session. Mercedes set its fastest times on soft tyres, while Red Bull’s Max Verstappen and Daniel Ricciardo finished fourth and fifth, both more than 0.8 seconds off the pace. Esteban Ocon, Nico Hulkenberg, Fernando Alonso, Sergio Perez and Jolyon Palmer completed the top ten.

Alonso received a 25-place grid penalty after an engine change prompted by a hydraulic leak, joining Carlos Sainz and Bottas in receiving penalties. Vettel tested the gearbox involved in his earlier post-race collision with Lance Stroll. Sainz was also shown running a red light when the second stoppage ended, potentially attracting stewards’ attention.

A New York Times report revealed Rose McGowan’s 1997 $100,000 settlement with Harvey Weinstein following a hotel-room episode and detailed Ashley Judd’s harassment allegation. Weinstein denied the settlement constituted admission and announced leave from his company.

The 52-week high strategy buys stocks trading near their highest closing price of the past year, based on research suggesting they outperform stocks farther from their highs. The 52-week range spans the highest and lowest closing prices over that period; intraday breaches do not establish new highs or lows unless confirmed at closing.

Traders use these levels as resistance and support, indicators of momentum, and tools for assessing bullish sentiment. The percentage off the 52-week high is calculated as:

(Current Price − 52-week High) / 52-week High

Backtests cited found evidence of the effect in individual stocks, including one strategy that beat the S&P 500 over two decades. However, the article’s SPY-based tests produced unattractive results. It suggests the market-cap-weighted S&P 500’s concentration in large stocks may explain why the individual-stock effect was not replicated.

The US Energy Department approved nearly $67 million for 85 nuclear research projects to improve safety, efficiency and energy independence. Funding includes over $31 million for 32 university-led projects and $6 million for reactor safety and performance research at 19 universities.

Dietitian Samantha Rigoli rejects no-fruit trends, emphasizing that fruit is nutrient-dense and rich in antioxidants, vitamins, and phytonutrients. Though fruit contains carbohydrates and natural sugars, it differs nutritionally from calorie-dense cookies. Those losing weight may choose lower-glycemic fruits, but Rigoli recommends eating fruit daily.

The NHS Constitution, also called the Patient Charter, sets out patients’ legal rights, NHS pledges and patient responsibilities. It upholds healthcare based on need and generally free at the point of use, with some exceptions.

Patients have rights to equal access, appropriate treatment, waiting-time explanations and alternatives, safe and regulated care, qualified staff, privacy, valid consent and clear information. NICE-recommended treatments should be available when clinically suitable, while other funding decisions must be fair, evidence-based and explained. Patients may choose a GP practice, participate in treatment decisions and receive openness, an apology and support when care goes wrong.

Complaints must be acknowledged and investigated, with options to approach the Ombudsman, seek judicial review or claim compensation for negligence. NHS organisations must continually improve care and consider community health needs.

Patients are responsible for looking after their health where possible, respecting staff and others, following or discussing treatment plans, attending appointments, and participating in vaccination and screening. The Charter presents the NHS as a partnership based on fairness, trust, accountability and shared responsibility, particularly amid waiting lists, workforce shortages and financial pressures.

The Cahokia Creek Watershed Planning project aims to address stormwater, flooding and water-quality issues in two western Madison County watersheds, including Indian Creek and Canteen Creek near Glen Carbon and Edwardsville. HeartLands Conservancy gathered public input at January open houses to identify priorities such as flood-prone areas, inadequate infrastructure, pollution, mining-related subsidence and poor conditions for recreation and wildlife. The resulting plans will help seek funding for infrastructure and land-management projects affecting residential and agricultural areas. The effort is part of Madison County’s stormwater planning and involves the county, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and HeartLands Conservancy.

California’s recreational cannabis rollout produced lower-than-expected early sales amid complex regulations, slow municipal licensing, widespread local retail bans, limited legal product availability, and heavy taxes. Experts estimated that 85–90 percent of the previous industry remained unlicensed, encouraging continued black-market purchases. Some warned of a crisis, while others noted that Colorado also initially missed revenue projections before its market stabilized and later exceeded them.

TaintDroid addresses sensitive-data exfiltration by Android applications through dynamic taint tracking. Traditional Android permissions regulate access to devices and resources but cannot specify which data may be transmitted. Simply preventing applications from having both sensitive-data and network access would break legitimate applications and would not prevent side channels, application collusion, or deceptive IPC use.

TaintDroid designates sensors, identifiers, contacts, and similar data as sources and the network as the principal sink. It represents up to 32 taint sources with a 32-bit vector. As Dalvik instructions execute, taint moves with assignments and is combined through bitwise unions for operations involving multiple inputs. Arrays, IPC messages, and files each receive one conservative aggregate tag, potentially overestimating taint but avoiding leaks. File tags persist in metadata. Native methods require manually defined propagation policies, although simple signatures can be handled automatically.

Taint tags are stored near local variables, arguments, fields, and arrays to improve cache efficiency. At network interfaces, TaintDroid detects tagged outgoing data and can block it, alert users, or apply another policy. Evaluation found applications transmitting locations, phone numbers, and other information without adequately informing users. Reported overhead was approximately 3–5% additional memory and 3–29% CPU.

TaintDroid does not prevent initial compromise, side channels, or implicit flows in which sensitive values affect control flow rather than direct assignments. Tainting the program counter during sensitive branches can detect some implicit flows but may produce false positives. Lower-level x86 or ARM tracking covers native and arbitrary software but is expensive, difficult to implement correctly, and vulnerable to “taint explosion,” where excessive propagation makes most data unusable.

More expressive information-flow languages can let programmers define labels, channels, and policies, enabling compile-time detection of many leaks. Static checks are preferable because runtime failures can themselves become covert channels.

The lecture also describes TightLip, a legacy-system approach using doppelganger processes. It creates scrubbed copies of sensitive files, runs a duplicate process on scrubbed data, and compares its system calls with those of the original. Divergence followed by external output may indicate sensitive-data dependence. TightLip requires file-specific, reliable scrubbers but needs only minor operating-system changes and adds roughly the cost of another process.

A 10-year-old PGI schoolgirl reported an alleged abduction attempt by youths in a black car. Police found no witnesses but lodged a precautionary DDR. Following a similar recent incident, the school requested regular PCR patrols.

Long COVID includes new, returning, or ongoing health problems lasting at least four weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Although vaccines are highly effective against infection and severe outcomes, vaccinated people may remain susceptible to infection and long COVID. Healthcare workers face increased occupational exposure, and evidence suggests additional vaccine doses may reduce long COVID prevalence.

This case-control study examined epidemiological data and risk factors for long COVID among healthcare workers aged 18 years or older at Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein in Brazil from March 1, 2020, to July 15, 2022. Symptomatic workers received free RT-PCR testing, and those with confirmed infection were followed for 180 days. Cases had symptoms arising during or after infection, persisting beyond four weeks, and not explained by another diagnosis; symptoms included general, respiratory, cardiac, neurological, digestive, joint, and muscle complaints. Workers recovering within four weeks were controls. Diagnostic confirmation used RT-PCR on nasopharyngeal swabs.

Alabama faces more showers and thunderstorms today as deep tropical moisture and saturated ground increase flash-flood risks, especially across central counties. A flash flood watch remains through 7 p.m. Storms will be more scattered Thursday, with possible small hail and gusty winds in north Alabama. Friday through the weekend will bring partly sunny skies, scattered afternoon storms and highs near 90. Early next week should be drier before rain chances rise later. No Atlantic tropical storms are expected within seven days.

The lecture reviews biomimetic cellular structures that replicate or draw design inspiration from nature. Examples include silicon carbide ceramics templated from wood, 3-D-printed fiber-reinforced honeycombs with wood-like fiber orientation, tantalum foams resembling trabecular bone, tissue-engineering scaffolds mimicking extracellular matrices, and lightweight sandwich structures comparable to leaves and bird skulls. Palm-inspired concrete structures use density gradients, though concrete requires reinforcement under tensile loads.

Plant stems, porcupine quills, hedgehog spines, toucan beaks, and feather quills combine dense outer shells with foam or honeycomb cores. These cores resist local shell wrinkling and reduce weight for a given buckling load. Engineering analogues include fiber-reinforced structures modeled on horsetail stems and extruded metal structures made by removing aluminum wires from a copper matrix.

The class then reviews foam energy absorption. Energy-absorption diagrams are derived from stress-strain curves by plotting absorbed energy against stress for different densities and strain rates. Optimal points occur near the onset of densification. A bicycle-helmet problem is discussed using peak stress, assumed velocity, strain rate, and absorbed energy per unit volume. Another problem identifies transitions between linear elasticity, the stress plateau, and densification for open-cell aluminum foam.

The test covers foam thermal conductivity, trabecular bone, sandwich panels, and energy absorption. Students may bring one sheet and should know key modulus and strength equations for open-cell foams. Remaining classes include a talk on becoming a professor and project collection.

News reports from November 22, 2001 focused on Enron’s worsening liquidity crisis, collapsing share and bond prices, and uncertainty surrounding Dynegy’s proposed acquisition. Enron secured a three-week extension on a $690 million payment and accessed the remaining $450 million of a $1 billion credit line, while negotiating to restructure $9.15 billion due by the end of 2002. Its shares closed at $5.01, down 94 percent for the year. Analysts warned that a credit downgrade, withdrawal of bank support, or failure of the Dynegy deal could lead to bankruptcy.

Enron employees suffered severe retirement losses because its 401(k) plan was heavily invested in company stock and temporarily frozen during the price collapse. A class-action lawsuit alleged Enron inflated its share price and breached fiduciary duties. Meanwhile, some senior executives had earned substantial sums by exercising stock options.

Enron reviewed its Japanese operations as its yen-denominated bonds pressured investors and money market funds. Potential sales included its stake in India’s Dabhol power project and Wessex Water in Britain. Investors holding Enron and partnership bonds also faced steep losses as prices fell sharply amid concerns about off-balance-sheet debt and Enron’s ability to meet obligations. Broader stock markets declined before Thanksgiving because of profit-taking, weak technology news, and economic uncertainty.

U.S. stocks stayed near record highs Wednesday while Treasury yields and the dollar rose after stronger-than-expected retail sales and inflation data. Consumer prices increased 2.5 percent annually in January, the highest rate since March 2012, supporting Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen’s case for gradual interest-rate increases. The 10-year Treasury yield reached 2.50 percent. Higher yields weakened dividend-focused utility, real-estate and telecom stocks. European markets were mixed, while major Asian indexes gained. Oil prices were little changed, and gold slipped slightly.

Belgium’s controversial 18-10 win over Spain secured Romania’s automatic qualification for the 2019 Rugby World Cup. World Rugby is reviewing the appointment of Romanian match officials after Spanish players confronted them following the game. Spain will face Portugal, with the winner playing Samoa; that series loser will join Canada in November’s four-team repechage. The Africa Cup runner-up and the Asia 2–Tahiti winner will complete the field. The round-robin winner enters Pool B with New Zealand, South Africa, Italy and Africa 1. Canada entered the repechage after losses to the United States and Uruguay.

NVIDIA reported results from its May 23, 2017 annual stockholders meeting. He says the bruise is minor and he is ready to play, praises developing young talent, and emphasizes simple, strong plays despite unpredictable bounces.

Gray Davis’ threats to seize plants or impose a windfall profits tax. He questioned several officiating decisions but emphasized that the team did not play well enough to win, particularly in generating offense, recovering pucks and preventing second chances. He said playoff motivation comes from pursuing the Stanley Cup and supporting teammates, while distinguishing between players who are hurt but can play and those who are injured.

The team must believe it can win despite missing key players, though replacing defenders such as Z and Griz would require better boxing out, puck support and contributions from others. Because the opponent is a big, heavy team, Z’s absence would be significant. If two defensemen are unavailable, the team may use seven defenders or insert a less experienced player situationally.

The coach said line changes are possible but could disrupt existing chemistry. Krejci and Jake need to adjust how they generate offense, with Jake needing to use his speed and play more inside. After the loss, the team must respond by improving details, limiting rebounds and second chances, and using speed, forechecking and effort to create inside opportunities.

This retrospective study compared REM sleep microstructure in 20 patients with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD), 20 with Parkinson’s disease and RBD (PD+RBD), and 20 matched controls using polysomnography.

Compared with controls and PD+RBD, patients with iRBD had a higher proportion of phasic REM sleep and more REM-sleep arousals. REM sleep without atonia was highest in iRBD, followed by PD+RBD and controls. Patients with PD+RBD had shorter and less abundant REM sleep, longer REM latency, shorter REM bouts, and lower density and duration of sawtooth waves. Both patient groups showed altered sawtooth-wave spectral characteristics, with relatively less low-frequency activity than controls.

NREM-to-REM transitions progressively lengthened across groups: controls had the shortest median transitions, followed by iRBD and then PD+RBD. Atonia generally began first in controls, whereas sawtooth waves more often appeared first in both patient groups.

The findings indicate that REM sleep abnormalities in RBD extend beyond loss of muscle atonia and dream enactment to phasic activity, sawtooth waves, and sleep-stage transitions. Limitations included small groups, medication use among patients with PD, heterogeneous recordings, lack of a PD group without RBD, and cross-sectional analysis. Longitudinal research is needed to assess whether these features predict progression to α-synucleinopathies.

China’s first-quarter 2017 GDP grew 6.9%, exceeding expectations and the government’s 6.5% target, but the passage questions the reliability and significance of official GDP and industrial production data. March industrial production rose 7.6%, its highest rate since January 2015, alongside renewed export growth. The author speculates that earlier production figures may have understated economic weakness and argues the March increase could be temporary, as occurred in March 2016.

Retail sales rose 10.9% in March, near their average since the 2014 slowdown. State-owned fixed-asset investment grew 13.6% in the first quarter, private investment 7.7%, and total investment 9.2%, remaining subdued and below earlier years despite stimulus.

The passage presents China as having stabilized after monetary pressures rather than restored durable growth. It argues that stronger GDP and production figures have not been matched consistently across other indicators or the global economy. Industrial production’s rise would be meaningfully positive only if it began sustained acceleration, which the author considers unlikely given weak investment, uneven statistics, and previous short-lived rebounds.

The Delaware Supreme Court reversed a Superior Court judgment affirming the Industrial Accident Board’s denial of workers’ compensation benefits to PNC employee Cheryl Tickles. Tickles arrived about an hour before her shift to work overtime, entered Building 103 of PNC’s Bellevue Complex to use an employee-only ATM for lunch money, and then slipped on ice in the adjoining PNC parking lot while returning to her ride to Building 400, where she worked. Her injuries later required shoulder surgery and caused approximately twelve weeks of total disability.

The Board denied benefits because Tickles had not begun work and was engaged in a personal errand. The Superior Court agreed. The Supreme Court held that the parking lot qualified as PNC’s premises despite Tickles working in another building, noting the operational relationship between the buildings and employees’ customary travel between them. It also held that using the employer-provided ATM shortly before work was a reasonably necessary act of personal convenience undertaken in preparation for the workday and therefore incidental to employment. Tickles was injured at her workplace and during the course of employment, making her eligible for benefits. The case was remanded for further proceedings consistent with the opinion.

Soccer coaches should prepare players for varied field, weather, equipment, ball, officiating, and perimeter conditions while conducting pre-match inspections to identify hazards or determine whether a field is unplayable.

Artificial turf produces faster ball movement and can become dangerously hot. Natural surfaces vary with grass length, hardness, moisture, slope, crowns, dirt, uneven ground, repairs, and debris, affecting traction, bounce, and passing. Wet fields make balls skip, while puddles stop them; substantial standing water, extensive ice, protruding sprinkler heads, split artificial-turf seams, pitching mounds, or unsafe rocks may render fields unusable. Players should choose suitable cleats and adjust technique accordingly.

Field dimensions vary, requiring changes in fitness, passing weight, timing, crossing, and tactics. Long or wide fields generally demand stronger passes, while short or narrow fields favor earlier, lighter passes and small-group play.

Severe storms and blizzards justify cancellation. Lightning requires immediate evacuation to cars or buildings, with at least 30 minutes after continued thunder before resuming. Cold requires appropriate clothing; heat and humidity require hydration, monitoring, and possible postponement or abandonment. Rain, snow, wind, dew, fog, frost, sunlight, shadows, glare, floodlight failure, and darkness can alter visibility, ball behavior, and safety.

Players should adapt to referee interpretations, continue playing until the whistle, and never assume offside will be called. Perimeter hazards include advertising boards, fences, drainage ditches, tracks, sidewalks, spectators, thrown objects, crowd noise, and overhanging branches. Players should avoid unsafe collisions and use nonverbal communication when necessary.

Goals must be securely anchored and structurally sound. Dangerous corner flags, damaged nets, defective or waterlogged balls, extra balls, and incorrect ball sizes require attention. Multiple game balls should match in size, model, and pressure.

Players must understand field markings and adapt to missing, multiple-colored, nonparallel, or wavy lines, with cones, saucers, or paint used when appropriate. Coaches should practice under varied conditions, teach proper clothing and hydration, know local rules, inspect fields before games and practices, and use field disadvantages strategically when choosing ends.

The speaker praised Paul’s leadership and competitiveness after returning from a concerning hit to score a crucial goal. Following difficult years, the team now has an opportunity to win the Stanley Cup and earn respect for the organization. The overtime victory boosted confidence, and the team looks forward to the next game despite another long flight.

The lecture develops models for honeycomb mechanics. For brittle hexagonal honeycombs under in-plane compression, cell-wall fracture occurs when bending stress reaches the modulus of rupture; the crushing plateau stress scales with the wall strength and \((t/l)^2\). In-plane compression may therefore fail through elastic buckling, plastic yielding, or brittle crushing.

In tension, elastic moduli remain unchanged, elastic buckling does not occur, and the plastic plateau stress is approximately the same as in compression. For brittle honeycombs containing cracks much larger than the cell size, fracture toughness is derived by combining the crack-tip stress field with cell-wall bending. Unlike previously derived properties, toughness depends on cell size.

Triangular honeycombs behave primarily as pin-jointed trusses with axial member forces. Their modulus scales as \(E_s(t/l)\), compared with \(E_s(t/l)^3\) for bending-dominated hexagonal honeycombs, making triangular structures much stiffer.

Out-of-plane loading causes cell walls to extend, contract, or shear rather than bend. The out-of-plane Young’s and shear moduli scale linearly with \(t/l\), producing strong anisotropy relative to in-plane properties. Two out-of-plane Poisson’s ratios equal that of the solid, while the reciprocal ratios are small for thin walls.

Out-of-plane compression may cause elastic plate buckling, axial yielding, plastic buckling, or brittle crushing. Approximate elastic and plastic buckling strengths are obtained using plate-buckling and work-balance methods. For defect-free brittle walls, tensile strength, fracture toughness, and crushing strength scale with relative density and the corresponding solid properties.

The lecture concludes by introducing wood and cork as natural honeycombs whose density dependence and anisotropy can be analyzed using these models.
Moody’s says Saudi Arabia’s stable A1 rating reflects strong finances, reserves and liquidity, despite oil dependence, challenging reforms, a 2017 contraction and large deficits.

Lake Havasu City is Arizona’s hottest place, reaching a state-record 128 degrees on June 29, 1994, second in the United States only to Death Valley. Many of Arizona’s highest temperatures occur along the Colorado River, including in Bullhead City, Parker, Willow Beach and Yuma. State Climatologist Nancy Selover attributes western Arizona’s extreme heat to isolation from monsoon circulation, dry air, intense sunshine, rocky terrain that retains heat, hot western winds and little irrigated agriculture. The Colorado River provides limited cooling, while higher elevations and monsoon moisture moderate temperatures elsewhere in Arizona.

Robert A. Maclam sued Marquette for injuries sustained after tripping over poultry crates obstructing a sidewalk. The court held that Marquette’s charter exempted the city from liability for obstructions negligently left by property owners or occupants. This special charter provision was neither superseded by the general state liability statute nor repealed by a later local act because both laws could operate without conflict. The exemption was also valid local legislation, not unconstitutional class legislation. The directed verdict and judgment for the city were affirmed.

The passage argues that forex trading should generally be avoided because it is highly risky and difficult to trade profitably. Its primary concern is leverage: brokers may offer leverage of up to 50 times a trader’s deposit, meaning a 2% adverse move can eliminate the account. Leverage magnifies both gains and losses and makes surviving the learning process difficult.

Other cited disadvantages include volatile and unpredictable exchange rates, the lack of long-term wealth-building benefits found in stocks, and forex’s zero-sum nature. Currency prices reflect numerous economic and market participants, making reliable forecasting difficult. Erratic movements can also undermine risk-management systems.

Additional risks include scams, fraudulent or unsupported strategy claims, broker insolvency, counterparty default, and comparatively limited regulation. Round-the-clock trading may encourage overtrading, while the market may attract impulsive gamblers with limited capital. Systematic forex strategies reportedly have high failure rates during testing and often stop working quickly. Many advertised strategies rely on anecdotal evidence rather than backtesting. The passage recommends carefully reconsidering forex trading and views stocks as offering more robust and profitable opportunities.

Brazil, Latin America’s largest economy, has established stock and commodity markets regulated by the Brazilian Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM). Tradable assets include stocks, REITs, funds, ETFs, agricultural commodities, derivatives, currencies, and bonds. Strategies include day and swing trading, value investing, momentum, trend following, technical and fundamental analysis, options, contrarian, and algorithmic trading. Technical tools include moving averages, RSI, Bollinger Bands, Fibonacci tools, and candlestick patterns, while fundamental analysis uses financial statements, ratios, and macroeconomic indicators.

Investment timing depends on economic indicators, politics, industry performance, and global conditions. Agricultural commodities and the technology, healthcare, and consumer goods equity sectors have shown profitability or growth, though market conditions vary. Key risks include volatility, instability, currency movements, regulation, taxation, limited transparency and liquidity, and company-specific problems. Leverage can increase gains and losses, requiring risk management.

Trading may incur capital gains tax, dividend income tax, VAT on brokerage fees, IOF on currency transactions, and other taxes. The presented backtest produced 250 trades, averaging 0.75% per trade, with a 67% win rate, 19% maximum drawdown, and 2.1 profit factor.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines redesigned streaming multiprocessors, unified configurable L1/shared memory, larger L2 caches, GDDR6, improved compression, and concurrent integer and floating-point execution. These changes deliver higher bandwidth, lower latency, and a reported 50% improvement in delivered performance per CUDA core over Pascal. Turing Tensor Cores support FP16, INT8, and INT4 operations for training, inference, and neural graphics. Tesla T4 uses 2,560 CUDA and 320 Tensor Cores, provides up to 130 INT8 TOPS and 260 INT4 TOPS, and offers substantially higher inference performance and energy efficiency than CPU-based systems.

Dedicated RT Cores accelerate bounding-volume hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, enabling real-time ray tracing through a hybrid pipeline combining rasterization, ray tracing, AI, simulation, and denoising. Turing reportedly performs ray tracing about ten times faster than Pascal. NVIDIA NGX uses Tensor Cores for features including DLSS, InPainting, AI Slow-Mo, and AI Super Rez. DLSS uses neural networks trained against 64-times supersampled reference images to provide image quality comparable to temporal anti-aliasing with less shading work.

Other graphics capabilities include mesh and task shaders, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering. These technologies reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks, vary shading rates by content, motion, or gaze, reuse shading computations, and render multiple viewpoints efficiently. Turing also supports bindless resources and flexible resource heaps.

Display and media improvements include DisplayPort 1.4a, dual 8K displays at 60 Hz, HDR processing and tone mapping, HEVC 8K encoding, expanded HEVC and VP9 decoding, and improved streaming quality. USB-C and VirtualLink combine display, data, and power for VR headsets. NVLink replaces earlier SLI transfer interfaces on TU102 and TU104, while TU106 lacks NVLink and SLI.

TU104 contains up to 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores; TU106 contains 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores. Turing’s memory subsystem uses 14 Gbps GDDR6 with 20% better power efficiency than Pascal’s GDDR5X, while larger caches and improved compression provide approximately 50% higher effective bandwidth.

The speaker says the team must ignore past results and distractions, prepare for the next Stanley Cup Final game from the opening shift, and play hard. After retiring, he spent a year away from hockey before accepting Jacques Lemaire’s invitation to coach. Winning the Cup as an assistant and seeing veteran players’ happiness made coaching rewarding and motivated him to continue.

He describes coaching as an emotional but fulfilling profession centered on teaching, improving players’ abilities, helping them handle adversity, and keeping the game enjoyable. He confirms an unnamed player was slightly stiff but skated well and was fine.

Regarding an earlier incident, he rejects retribution and emphasizes winning, discipline, and focus. Because the opponent has a strong power play, the team must avoid needless penalties and cannot rely on repeatedly killing penalties or scoring shorthanded. He declines to reveal planned matchups.

Wall Street indexes suffered their worst week in two years as rising bond yields and inflation concerns outweighed strong corporate profit expectations, pushing the S&P 500 down 3.9 percent. However, the index remained up 3.3 percent for the year after gaining 19.4 percent in 2017. Analysts sharply increased earnings forecasts following the reduction in the U.S. corporate tax rate from 35 to 21 percent. Estimated first-quarter S&P 500 profit growth rose to 17.7 percent, while projected 2018 growth climbed to 18.2 percent. Overall 2018 earnings are expected to reach about $155 per share. Improving global growth and a weaker dollar are also supporting U.S. companies. Whether the market downturn continues may depend partly on upcoming earnings reports, following disappointing results from Apple, Alphabet, ExxonMobil and Chevron despite stronger-than-expected fourth-quarter results overall.

Pfizer’s agreement with the Trump administration to lower drug prices has pressured other major pharmaceutical companies to pursue similar deals. Some firms that received Trump’s demands for lower prices hope to announce agreements with the White House as soon as this week, though timing may change.

US officials told CNN that Trump campaign and business associates had frequent communications with Russians known to US intelligence, prompting concern due to their frequency, senior-level involvement and concurrent Russian cyberactivity against Democratic organizations. Trump and Obama were briefed. Investigators had not determined the conversations’ intent and were examining possible coordination over damaging information about Hillary Clinton. The contacts were intercepted through routine intelligence collection.

The U.S. Embassy in Nigeria shared photos of Folake, a woman living with HIV whose health improved after receiving antiretroviral treatment through PEPFAR at a Lagos treatment site. The World AIDS Day post emphasized that HIV/AIDS is not necessarily a death sentence. Forum responses largely praised her transformation, stressed treatment adherence and testing, and criticized stigmatizing remarks.

Nashville sought stronger offense while relying on goaltending and defense, making trades for players such as James Neal, P.K. Subban and Ryan Johansen. Management emphasized honest player evaluation, organizational fit and communication, while acknowledging that trading longtime players such as Shea Weber can be difficult. Despite major defensive trades, strong scouting and drafting allowed the team to retain one of the league’s best defenses.

The organization credits patient development with the Milwaukee Admirals as central to its success. Pekka Rinne, Roman Josi, Ryan Suter and Weber all developed there, while Milwaukee players provided important depth during injuries and the playoffs.

Subban improved after injuries and an adjustment period, contributed significantly, and aligned with the organization’s goal of winning the Stanley Cup. Nashville also worked closely with him, his family and representatives to support his off-ice activities and prevent misunderstandings. More broadly, management believes acquired players succeed when their skills are embraced, roles are clearly defined and communication continues.

Scout Lucas Bergman strongly advocated drafting Patric despite injury and skating concerns. Management expressed deep appreciation for the franchise’s success and praised Nashville’s enthusiastic fans, loud arena, game presentation and atmosphere inside and outside Bridgestone Arena.

The Michigan Supreme Court granted mandamus directing the Livingston County circuit judge to dismiss an action for lack of personal jurisdiction. Plaintiffs initially filed in chancery and served the Brennens in Washtenaw County. After determining that the agency-contract dispute had an adequate legal remedy, the court transferred the case to its law side. Michigan law required service in the county where a transitory law action was brought, or where a defendant resided. The transfer statute did not make out-of-county chancery service effective for the subsequent law action. The Brennens’ appearance and answer in chancery, counsel’s comments concerning transfer, and discussion of pleading deadlines did not waive their right to challenge jurisdiction after the declaration at law was filed. Their motion to dismiss was therefore well founded.

Harvey Weinstein was indicted by a New York grand jury on first- and third-degree rape and first-degree criminal sex-act charges involving two women. Manhattan District Attorney Cyrus Vance said the ongoing investigation moves Weinstein closer to accountability and urged additional accusers with relevant information to come forward.

Defense attorney Ben Brafman said Weinstein would plead not guilty, seek dismissal of the indictment and expected acquittal. Weinstein declined to testify before the grand jury after prosecutors denied a requested postponement, which Brafman said left insufficient preparation time. Brafman also argued that one accuser had maintained a consensual relationship with Weinstein after the alleged 2013 attack and blamed political pressure for the indictment.

Weinstein, who denies non-consensual sex, surrendered to police Friday and was released on $1 million bail, restricted to New York and Connecticut.

Sudden Unexpected Death in Epilepsy (SUDEP) is strongly associated with poorly controlled generalized tonic-clonic seizures, particularly nocturnal seizures followed by prone positioning. Respiratory dysfunction, impaired arousal, central apnea, and autonomic instability can lead to death within minutes, making rapid intervention essential.

The study developed Korus, a twin XL autonomous repositioning mattress comprising 32 individually controlled inflatable cells, pressure sensors, networking components, and machine-learning software. Its 1,152-node pressure-sensing surface uses a Random Forest classifier to identify prone, supine, left, and right positions. A mobile app displays position, supports individualized model training, and controls cell inflation.

Eighteen control subjects enrolled, with 10 undergoing formal testing. The cells reached 14-inch inflation within seven seconds and had a 1,000-pound-per-cell capacity. Manual repositioning from prone succeeded in all 10 tested subjects, averaging 21.75 seconds. Prone-position detection accuracy was 96.8%, while overall position accuracy was 92.4%. During sleep recordings, Korus identified the correct position 97.3% of the time; errors primarily involved confusing supine with lateral positions, with no false prone detections. One subject was excluded because bent-leg sleeping positions were absent from training data.

The system demonstrated body-position recognition and repositioning, but further work is required to improve mapping, computation, biomechanics, autonomous operation, and seizure detection. Korus may also integrate with wearable seizure detectors.

The invention describes a landing device that enables camera-free delivery drones to land at destinations. A landing portion uses multiple infrared cameras to determine a drone’s position, remotely guides authorized drones during landing, and measures distance to control descent speed. Movable plates help receive, secure, and center packages. An opening-and-closing mechanism protects equipment from weather and ultraviolet exposure, while an ascending/descending mechanism transfers delivered packages from a rooftop landing area to a residential space.

A management system coordinates delivery requests, drones, routes, packages, batteries, weather data, warehouse controls, and household controls. Drones navigate autonomously by GPS or beacons until near their destination, transmit identification information, and surrender control to the landing device only when authorized. After releasing a package, the drone returns to the warehouse.

Alternative configurations include a simplified enclosed landing device, integration with ventilation or smoke-exhaust systems, local weather observation, emergency landing support, portable disaster-relief landing stations, falling-drone warnings, and alerts for approaching camera-equipped drones. Additional proposals address battery monitoring, accident-recording black boxes, preflight package and safety checks, designated flight routes, beacon base stations, and coordinated defenses against unauthorized drones, including warnings, flight restrictions, observation, blocking, and interception.

NVIDIA’s fiscal 2021 Form 10-K describes a Santa Clara-based accelerated computing company serving Gaming, Professional Visualization, Data Center, and Automotive markets through unified GPU, networking, systems, and software platforms. NVIDIA reports Graphics and Compute & Networking segments, invested more than $24 billion in research and development since inception, and acquired Mellanox in fiscal 2021.

NVIDIA agreed to acquire Arm from SoftBank in a transaction valued at $40 billion, subject to regulatory approvals and other closing conditions. The company expected closing in the first quarter of calendar 2022.

NVIDIA uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on external foundries, component suppliers, and contract manufacturers. Its markets are intensely competitive, with rivals including AMD, Intel, major internet companies, semiconductor suppliers, networking vendors, and companies developing internal processors.

As of January 31, 2021, NVIDIA employed 18,975 people in 29 countries, including 13,532 in research and development. Its workforce was 80% male and 20% female; Black or African American and Hispanic or Latino employees represented 6% of its U.S. workforce. Offices largely closed in March 2020 because of COVID-19, with remote-work support and safety protocols implemented.

Major risks include rapid technological change, competition, dependence on third-party manufacturing, supply constraints, inaccurate demand forecasts, product defects, cybersecurity incidents, business disruptions, COVID-19 impacts, regulatory and geopolitical changes, and failure to realize anticipated benefits from acquisitions. NVIDIA had 620 million common shares outstanding on February 19, 2021, and non-affiliate voting stock had an aggregate market value of approximately $241.21 billion on July 24, 2020.

Harav Aaron Brafman, longtime Menahel of Yeshiva Derech Ayson–Yeshiva of Far Rockaway, died on Erev Shabbos, 19 Av 2017, at age 73. Born in 1944, he studied and taught at Yeshivah Torah Vodaath for more than 20 years and was a close student of Harav Yaakov Kamenetsky, Harav Gedaliah Schorr and Harav Avrohom Pam. He married Susie Schwartz in 1964 and became Menahel of Yeshiva of Far Rockaway in 1970. Known for his dedication and accessibility, he built close relationships with generations of students, taught local community members and raised funds for those in need. After declining health, he was buried at Eretz HaChaim cemetery in Beit Shemesh. He is survived by his wife, siblings, eight children and many grandchildren.

California avoided predicted summer blackouts through reduced electricity use, mild weather, new generation and market controls, improving Gov. Gray Davis’s political outlook despite weak approval ratings. Davis still faced challenges including Southern California Edison’s proposed rescue, PG&E’s bankruptcy, state power-purchase costs, budget pressures, drought and criticism of his extensive executive actions.

Lawmakers debated whether rescuing Edison or allowing bankruptcy would better protect ratepayers. The proposed plan included $2.9 billion in bonds backed by business customers and a state option to buy transmission lines. Consumer groups opposed the measure, while creditors warned inaction could lead to bankruptcy.

Other reports described stable public-power utility credit, Williams’s $591 million claim in PG&E’s bankruptcy, California’s short-term borrowing needs, unmet infrastructure investment, and concerns that the state’s roughly $45 billion in long-term electricity contracts could exceed market prices through 2010. Davis’s reelection prospects benefited from substantial campaign funds, Republican candidates’ weaknesses and California’s increasingly Democratic electorate.

The course examines the evolution of proof systems in computer science from the mid-1980s onward. Requirements include scribe notes, one problem set, and recommended readings. Topics include interactive and doubly efficient proofs, the GKR protocol, PCPs, multiprover proofs, IP = PSPACE, cryptographic soundness, Fiat–Shamir, batch proofs, and SNARGs.

Classical NP proofs allow polynomial-time verification of language membership. Interactive proofs add interaction and verifier randomness; without randomness, interaction offers no advantage because the prover could provide the full transcript.
