Randomness alone yields the class MA, which is not known to differ from NP. As an example, randomized verification can check whether \(C=AB\) for \(n\times n\) matrices in quadratic time by evaluating the matrices on a vector of powers of a random field element. If the matrices differ, acceptance occurs with probability at most roughly \(n/|F|\).

An interactive proof involves a potentially unbounded prover and a polynomial-time randomized verifier. Completeness requires high acceptance probability for true statements, while soundness limits acceptance of false statements against any prover. Constant completeness and soundness gaps can be amplified through repetition. Shamir’s result \(IP=PSPACE\) demonstrates that interactive proofs can establish membership in any PSPACE language to a polynomial-time verifier.

The lecture introduces the sum-check protocol. Given a multivariate polynomial \(f\) of individual degree at most \(d\), a subset \(H\) of a finite field \(F\), and a claimed value \(\beta\), the prover seeks to establish
\[
\sum_{(h_1,\ldots,h_m)\in H^m} f(h_1,\ldots,h_m)=\beta.
\]
In each round, the prover sends a univariate polynomial obtained by summing over all remaining variables while leaving one variable open. The verifier checks its degree and consistency with the preceding claim, then selects a random field element. After \(m\) rounds, the verifier directly evaluates \(f\) at the resulting random point.

The protocol has perfect completeness. For soundness, a false initial claim forces the prover to submit an incorrect polynomial, while final acceptance requires consistency with the true polynomial. Moving from an incorrect to a correct polynomial succeeds at any round with probability at most \(d/|F|\), since distinct degree-\(d\) polynomials agree at no more than \(d\) points. A union bound gives soundness error at most \(md/|F|\), reducible by using a sufficiently large extension field. The protocol uses \(O(m)\) rounds and communication proportional to \(md\) field elements. Its importance comes from polynomials’ error-correcting properties and from low-degree extensions that encode many other problems as polynomial claims.

The PGA848 is a high-voltage, high-bandwidth programmable-gain instrumentation amplifier with a single-ended output and eight binary gain settings from 0.5V/V to 100V/V. Its DA_IN– and DA_IN+ pins provide access to the output difference amplifier, allowing external capacitors for noise filtering or customized attenuation. The internal resistor network offers 0.01% matching and at least 80dB CMRR, but resistors have ±15% absolute variation. Leakage can degrade CMRR, and the pins must not source or sink current.

The device operates with input-stage supplies above ±4.5V and output-stage supplies above ±2.25V. Its input range extends to within 3V of either supply. Supplies above 40V total, or ±20V, can permanently damage the device.

A typical application drives a 16-bit, 1MSPS ADS8860 SAR ADC using ±15V input-stage supplies and a 5.3V output-stage supply. Three filters address EMI/RFI, amplifier bandwidth and ADC charge kickback. A 75pF feedback capacitor produces a nominal 318kHz cutoff, changing to 277kHz with resistor tolerance; the circuit remains flat within –0.1dB to 41kHz. The ADC reference is 5V, while the PGA848 REF pin is buffered at 2.5V using an OPA192 and precision divider.

Recommended PCB practices include matched differential paths, close 0.1µF low-ESR supply bypass capacitors, separation of input traces from supply and output traces, minimized leakage and parasitic capacitance around DA_IN pins, ground-plane keep-outs beneath inputs, few thermal junctions, and distance from heat sources. TI provides simulation tools and related documentation, while emphasizing ESD precautions, application validation, and stated warranty limitations.

Enrique Marquez Jr., 25, agreed to plead guilty to federal charges for acting as a straw buyer of two rifles used by Syed Rizwan Farook and Tashfeen Malik in the 2015 San Bernardino attack, which killed 14 and injured 22. He also admitted conspiring with Farook in unexecuted 2011–2012 plans to attack Riverside City College and freeway traffic. Prosecutors found no evidence Marquez participated in or knew beforehand about the 2015 attack. In custody since December 2015, he faces up to 25 years in federal prison.

Motley Fool Money highlights the no-annual-fee Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card, which offers unlimited 2% cash rewards, a $200 bonus after $500 in purchases within three months, and 0% introductory APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers. Afterward, a variable APR of 18.99%, 23.99%, or 28.99% applies. Additional benefits include up to $600 in cell phone protection, subject to a $25 deductible, and Visa Signature concierge service. Approval is most likely for applicants with good or excellent credit.

Alternatives include Capital One Quicksilver, offering unlimited 1.5% cash back, travel rewards, welcome bonuses, and a 15-month 0% introductory APR; and a Citi card offering up to 2% cash back, a $200 bonus, and an 18-month balance-transfer APR offer.

Motley Fool Money receives partner commissions that may affect offer placement but says compensation does not influence ratings. It does not cover every available offer, and recommended credit scores do not guarantee approval.

Using Gaia’s initial data release and RAdial Velocity Experiment measurements of more than 200,000 shared stars, University of Toronto astrophysicists calculated that the Sun orbits the Milky Way’s center at 240 km/s. The team analyzed stellar velocities relative to the Sun, identifying a velocity distribution linked to stars scattered into chaotic halo orbits near the Galactic center. Combining the Sun’s calculated speed with proper-motion measurements of Sagittarius A*, they estimated the Solar System’s distance from the Galactic center at 7.6–8.2 kiloparsecs, or about 24,788–26,745 light-years. This narrowed previous estimates, which ranged from 7.2 to 8.8 kiloparsecs. The researchers expected later Gaia data releases to further improve the precision of both the Sun’s velocity and its distance from the Galactic center.

Venezuelan TPS holders urged the Supreme Court to preserve a federal judge’s ruling blocking the Trump administration from ending their protected status. DHS Secretary Kristi Noem terminated Venezuela’s 2023 TPS designation and its extension through October 2026. Challengers argued she lacked legal authority and acted partly from racial animus.

U.S. District Judge Edward Chen initially blocked the termination, but the Supreme Court paused that preliminary order. Chen later issued a final ruling that Noem acted unlawfully, and the 9th Circuit declined to stay it. The administration returned to the Supreme Court, arguing lower courts had defied its earlier order. Challengers responded that the prior stay applied only to preliminary relief, while Chen’s final judgment relied on different statutory authority, a more developed record, and a new claim. They warned that reversing the ruling would severely harm TPS holders and their families.

The coach called the season phenomenal despite the painful Stanley Cup Final loss, acknowledging the opposing team was better and deserved to win. He praised his players for their hard work, confidence, resilience, and unity throughout an unexpected run, as well as the staff’s contributions. He also thanked the team’s outstanding fans for their consistent support and said the group would appreciate its accomplishments more after the disappointment subsided.

Bitcoin fell below $8,000 after Indian Finance Minister Arun Jaitley pledged measures against cryptocurrencies used for illicit financing or payments. India has repeatedly warned that digital currencies lack official backing and resemble Ponzi schemes, while reported bank-account suspensions at exchanges have increased uncertainty.

India represents 2%–3% of global cryptocurrency trading but has significant growth potential. Industry participants said government scrutiny followed bitcoin’s surge to nearly $20,000 and worried regulation could hinder the market. Others argued cryptocurrencies are too established to outlaw and said regulation may be welcome. India has formed a committee to study cryptocurrencies and will await its report before acting, while also considering blockchain technology for digital payments.

Costamare’s share price fell sharply from 2014 to 2016 amid weak global trade but appears to be recovering as shipping fundamentals improve. The company owns and charters 71 containerships and has recently chartered 16 ships, with none laid up. Management cited rising charter rates, a low 1.8% idle fleet, and an order book below 13% as evidence of tightening supply and demand. Costamare has $1.2 billion in contracted revenue, primarily from major charterers, with an average remaining charter duration of about three years. It is pursuing newbuilding and secondhand vessel opportunities. Cash totals roughly $219 million, while net debt has declined from $1.7 billion in 2013 to $1 billion. The author believes the improving market and strengthened balance sheet could support future operations and share-price gains and discloses a long position in Costamare.
The time off allowed preparation for the next game. The team is focused on avoiding a return to Dallas while trailing and may adjust against strong shot blockers.

Tesla’s 2020 Form 10-K describes two business segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. Tesla designs, manufactures, sells and leases electric vehicles, including Models 3, Y, S and X, and develops planned vehicles such as Cybertruck, Tesla Semi and Roadster. It also offers solar systems, Solar Roof, Powerwall, Powerpack and Megapack, supported by proprietary battery, software, charging and driver-assistance technologies.

Tesla sells directly through its website and company-owned locations and operates service centers, Mobile Service and charging networks. Manufacturing occurs at facilities in California, Nevada, New York and Shanghai, with factories under construction in Berlin and Texas. The company had 70,757 full-time employees at year-end. As of February 1, 2021, 959,853,504 common shares were outstanding, and non-affiliate holdings were valued at $160.57 billion on June 30, 2020.

Major risks include COVID-19 impacts, production and construction delays, uncertain demand, intense competition, supplier and battery-cell constraints, international regulatory complexity, product defects and liability, financing risks, and challenges expanding sales, delivery, service, charging and installation capacity.

John Ternus, Apple’s 50-year-old senior vice president of hardware engineering, is increasingly viewed as the likely successor to CEO Tim Cook, particularly after former contender Jeff Williams stepped down from operational duties. Apple has raised Ternus’s public profile and expanded his influence over product road maps, features, and strategy.

A mechanical engineering graduate of the University of Pennsylvania and former competitive swimmer, Ternus worked at Virtual Research Systems before joining Apple in 2001. He became vice president of hardware engineering in 2013 and later assumed responsibility for iPhone hardware. His work spans the iPad, iPhone, AirPods, Macs, Apple Silicon transition, and Apple Vision Pro.

Ternus’s age, technical background, institutional experience, and standing with Cook and Apple loyalists reportedly appeal to the board. His possible promotion would continue Apple’s practice of selecting internal leaders while emphasizing technical innovation as the company confronts challenges in artificial intelligence, mixed reality, and products beyond the iPhone. Succession planning has gained urgency amid potential turnover among other senior executives, while Cook has offered mixed signals about retirement and may eventually become chairman.

Amazon.com’s 2022 Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022. Amazon is organized into North America, International, and AWS segments and serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, content creators, and advertisers. Its offerings include online and physical stores, third-party seller services, subscriptions, electronic devices, media content, advertising, fulfillment, and cloud-based compute, storage, database, analytics, and machine-learning services.

Amazon emphasizes customer focus, invention, operational excellence, and long-term thinking. It competes globally across retail, cloud computing, logistics, electronics, media, grocery, and advertising, primarily on selection, price, convenience, quality, speed, and reliability. Fourth-quarter sales are historically higher due to seasonality.

As of December 31, 2022, Amazon employed approximately 1.541 million full- and part-time employees. It operated 611 North American and 32 international physical stores and approximately 661.4 million square feet of leased and owned facilities. Andrew Jassy served as President and CEO, Jeffrey Bezos as Executive Chair, and Brian Olsavsky as CFO.

Major risks include intense competition, international operations, expansion into new products and markets, demand variability, inventory and fulfillment challenges, data breaches, system interruptions, labor constraints, supplier dependence, acquisitions, payment processing, foreign exchange fluctuations, evolving regulation, litigation, taxation, product liability, and government contracting requirements.

Amazon focuses financially on sustainable free cash flow, sales growth, operating efficiency, inventory turnover, technology investment, and management of shareholder dilution. Cash provided by operating activities increased from $46.3 billion in 2021 to $46.8 billion in 2022. Cash used in investing activities declined from $58.2 billion to $37.6 billion, while financing activities provided $9.7 billion in 2022. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities declined from $96.0 billion at year-end 2021 to $70.0 billion at year-end 2022.

Inclusive education is a global educational goal emphasizing quality education that meets every child’s needs, often in regular schools. Myanmar has strengthened disability rights and inclusive education policies since ratifying the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2011, but enrollment among children with disabilities remains comparatively low.

This study examined education for visually impaired children in Yangon through interviews, focus groups, observations, and document reviews at two special schools and two connected regular schools. Students receive primary education in special schools and then attend regular schools with nondisabled students from lower secondary education onward. The study describes this arrangement as “limited inclusive education in phases.”

Special schools provide Braille instruction, mobility and daily-life training, computer skills, supplementary academic support, teachers experienced with visual impairment, and a secure environment among peers. Regular schools help visually impaired students develop social and communication skills and allow nondisabled students to learn about disability and provide peer support.

Limitations include inadequate communication between special- and regular-school teachers, regular teachers’ dependence on special-school expertise, bullying and teasing, limited friendships between students with and without disabilities, and poor public awareness of educational opportunities and special schools. Special and regular schools are also governed by different ministries, contributing to weak coordination.

The study concludes that Yangon’s phased system effectively uses existing resources and addresses a broad range of student needs, but requires stronger cooperation, teacher training, information exchange, and activities promoting inclusion. Rather than adopting an unprepared one-track model, countries—especially low-income countries—should develop inclusive education systems suited to their resources and contexts.

This volume outlines diplomatic papers on World War I peace efforts and neutral rights in 1917. Part I covers Allied and Central Powers’ responses to peace proposals, President Wilson’s durable-peace address, German peace terms, proposed assurances against Austria-Hungary’s dismemberment, Mexican peace initiatives, Greece, and Germany’s constitutional struggle. Part II addresses unrestricted submarine warfare, submarine incidents, the U.S. severance of relations with Germany, the Zimmermann telegram, attacks on ships, merchant-ship armament, relations with other Central Powers and European neutrals, and the U.S. declaration of war on April 6. It also covers neutral and captured American seamen and Latin American responses, including diplomatic breaks or war declarations against Germany, proposed regional conferences, ship sinkings, seizures of German vessels, and support for U.S. naval forces.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2-MSPS data-acquisition system with an integrated analog front end. SMPL_SYNC aligns channel selection and frame clocks across multiple devices sharing identical sampling signals. Its internal low-drift reference can be filtered with a 10-µF REFIO capacitor or disabled for an external reference.

The source-synchronous interface supports two or four lanes in SDR or DDR modes. Conversion results are sent MSB-first in 24-bit packets. Features include output randomization to reduce ground-bounce interference, simple and moving averaging, fixed, ramp, and alternating test patterns, and a speed-boost mode providing up to 8 MSPS for one selected channel pair.

Configuration uses 16-bit registers across three banks through SPI. Devices can be connected in a daisy chain, with each ADC adding a 24-clock delay. Reset or power-down restores default registers, and initialization requires specified register writes with a free-running sampling clock.

The device offers low-noise bandwidth up to 22.7 kHz and wide bandwidth up to 700 kHz. In an ATE example, calibrated TUE is 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C, while wide-bandwidth mode settles to 99.95% full scale in 7.5 µs. Separate AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD supplies require local decoupling, careful grounding, and separation of analog paths from digital noise.

The disclosure describes a real-time “neural bridge” that measures neural activity, removes artifacts, extracts signal features, and uses trained decoders to identify intended movements and effort. A body-state model, sensor feedback, and individual activation profiles guide continuously updated electrical stimulation of muscles or control of targets such as prosthetics, wheelchairs, cursors, exoskeletons, remote devices, and robotic arms. Multiplexed stimulation can interleave noninterfering signals to produce simultaneous, compound, or rhythmic movements.

Neural activity may be recorded through EEG, ECoG, or implanted electrode arrays. Decoders are trained with movement cues and machine-learning methods, while feedback may be provided through stimulation and graphical body representations. The system can compensate for changing joint positions, electrode movement, and differences among users.

Experiments showed close correspondence between measured and actual hand positions. In a quadriplegic participant, decoded cortical signals, a virtual central pattern generator, and neuromuscular electrical stimulation enabled thought-controlled thumb flexion, extension, and rhythmic wiggling. Reported movement accuracies were 84.6%–91.5%, with 77.4% overall accuracy across movement and rest states.

Microsoft disclosed an August 1, 2016 underwriting agreement to issue seven series of senior unsecured notes: $2.5 billion at 1.100% due 2019; $2.75 billion at 1.550% due 2021; $1.5 billion at 2.000% due 2023; $4 billion at 2.400% due 2026; $2.25 billion at 3.450% due 2036; $4.5 billion at 3.700% due 2046; and $2.25 billion at 3.950% due 2056. Interest is payable semiannually beginning February 8, 2017. The notes may be redeemed under specified circumstances and will rank equally with Microsoft’s other unsecured, unsubordinated debt. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, supplemental indenture, note forms, and legal opinions.

Iran’s parliament initially approved a bill allocating over $260 million each to its ballistic missile program and Quds Force in response to new US sanctions. The government-backed measure also mandates strategies addressing US human rights violations and assisting sanctioned Iranians. It requires further parliamentary and clerical approval.

Blackwell reduces dynamic and leakage power through rapid clock-tree gating, GDDR7 memory clock gating, and separate GPU-core and memory voltage rails enabling workload optimization and frame-level shutdowns.

The lecture reviews full factorial experimental design, showing how coded factor levels and contrasts estimate main and interaction effects for \(2^k\) designs. Equivalent regression models use product columns for interactions, while ANOVA and F-tests determine whether estimated effects are significant relative to experimental noise. Replication provides estimates of process variance and supports residual analysis; residuals should have zero mean, roughly constant variance, and approximate normality.

A sheet-metal bending example illustrates fitting main and interaction effects from replicated data. All tested terms were significant. Model adequacy can be evaluated by adding replicated center points or other intermediate settings to test for curvature and distinguish lack of fit from replication noise. Discrete factors may prevent true center-point testing.

The lecture also introduces nuisance factors, randomization, blocking, and confounding. Runs can be arranged so nuisance effects are confounded with less important interactions rather than main effects. This principle leads to fractional factorial designs, which reduce experimental runs by accepting ambiguity among selected effects.

The 3-4 defense uses three down linemen, four linebackers, and four defensive backs, typically two cornerbacks and two safeties. Its large defensive linemen often control two gaps, while hybrid outside linebackers can rush the passer or drop into coverage. The balanced formation allows varied pressure and coverage disguises.

Its primary strength is versatility. Both outside linebackers can create a five-man rush, while two-high safety alignments can shift into Cover 1, Cover 2, Cover 3, or Cover 4. Blitzes such as the weakside edge blitz and Crossfire disguise post-snap pressure and coverage responsibilities.

The defense can struggle against spread formations. When outside linebackers cover receivers, only five defenders may remain in the box against five blockers and a running back. Trips formations can also force safeties or linebackers into difficult coverage matchups against slot receivers. The 3-3 stack developed partly to address these issues.

Common coverages include Cover 4, which protects deep and underneath areas but is vulnerable in the flats, and Cover 2 Man, which uses man coverage beneath two deep safeties.

Bill Parcells, Bill Belichick, Nick Saban, and Kirby Smart are prominent users of 3-4 variants. Their coaching tree has produced numerous NFL Super Bowl and college national championship victories.

A Berliner Testament appoints spouses as sole heirs and children as final heirs, providing financial security to the surviving spouse. However, its provisions are strongly binding and generally cannot be changed unilaterally, even after changed relationships or a spouse’s death. Clauses may provide flexibility. Inheritance-tax allowances should also be considered, as distributing an estate among multiple heirs may use them more effectively. Legal advice is recommended.

The Neofoot study assessed whether newborn foot length could identify low birth weight (LBW) and preterm birth (PTB) in resource-limited settings in Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. This prospective diagnostic accuracy study enrolled 342 stable newborns assessed within 72 hours of birth. Birth weight was measured twice using electronic scales, gestational age was estimated from menstrual dates or antenatal ultrasound, and right foot length was measured twice with a plastic ruler. Nine trained volunteers also measured 123 babies.

Among participants, 72 babies (21.1%) had LBW and 25 (7.3%) were preterm. Mean foot length was 7.8 cm. A foot length below 7.7 cm was the optimal threshold for both outcomes. For LBW, sensitivity was 84.7%, specificity 69.6%, positive predictive value 42.7%, and negative predictive value 94.5%. For PTB, sensitivity was 88.0%, specificity 61.8%, positive predictive value 15.4%, and negative predictive value 98.5%. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 87.0% for LBW and 85.8% for PTB.

The mean difference between researcher and volunteer measurements was 0.07 cm, with 95% limits of agreement from −0.55 to +0.70 cm; 7.3% of paired measurements fell outside these limits. Limitations included measurements up to 72 hours after birth, lack of blinding to newborn clinical status, digit preference, and conduct in one province. The study concluded that newborn foot length is a simple, feasible method for identifying LBW and PTB, while further implementation research should address training, measurement errors, referrals, and health outcomes.

The study estimates mortality attributable to SARS-CoV-2 in India using WHO-compliant verbal autopsies of deaths reported in the Consumer Pyramids Household Survey from 2018–2021. Of 30,447 reported decedents, 22,178 verbal autopsies were completed; after excluding deaths before 2018, the final sample contained 20,453 people. Physicians assigned ICD-10 causes of death. Statistical weights adjusted for survey sampling, delayed death reporting, and non-response.

India’s annual all-cause death rate in 2020–2021 was estimated to be 81.19% higher than in 2018–2019. SARS-CoV-2 accounted for 17.93% of deaths and 33.15% of excess deaths during the pandemic. Cardiovascular disease accounted for 27.18% of all deaths and 23.15% of excess deaths, while respiratory deaths declined by an amount equal to 1.52% of excess deaths. SARS-CoV-2 mortality peaked around the end of the 2020 lockdown and after the second wave in 2021, accounting for nearly 35.8% of deaths in April 2021.

SARS-CoV-2 death rates increased with age and were highest among people over 80, although most deaths occurred among those aged 61–80. Rates were higher, but not significantly, among females, urban residents, and the highest income quartile. More total deaths occurred in rural areas because their population was larger. State-level excess death rates varied substantially.

Limitations include possible misclassification involving ICD-10 codes U07 and U08, imperfect adjustments for delayed reporting and non-response, uncertainty in assigning a single cause of death, and lack of validation for the modified verbal-autopsy procedure used to identify SARS-CoV-2 deaths.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture improves graphics, ray tracing, AI, memory, storage I/O, display, and video performance over Turing. The RTX 3080 can render a cited frame in 6.7 ms, aided by doubled FP32 capability, second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, improved caching, concurrency, and GDDR6X memory.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection throughput and add hardware acceleration for moving and deforming geometry. A new Interpolate Triangle Position unit uses ray timestamps to determine geometry positions, enabling ray-traced motion blur up to eight times faster than Turing; an RTX 3080 measured up to five times faster than an RTX 2080 Super in a Blender demo.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support additional data types, including TF32 and BF16, and structured sparsity that can double matrix throughput by skipping zero values. DLSS uses neural networks to combine information from multiple frames, improving image quality and performance and enabling 8K ray-traced gaming at high frame rates on supported hardware.

GDDR6X uses PAM4 signaling to transfer two bits per clock edge, reaching 19.5 Gbps and up to 936 GB/s. Error Detection and Replay identifies and retries faulty memory transfers during overclocking.

RTX IO, working with Microsoft DirectStorage, moves lossless asset decompression from CPUs to GPUs. It is intended to reduce CPU utilization, accelerate loading and streaming, improve frame rates, and support larger game and professional datasets.

Ampere supports DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, including 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz under specified compression or pixel-format conditions. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware AV1 decoding up to 8K60 HDR with low CPU usage, while seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

For professional and data-center workloads, the A40 and RTX A6000 provide accelerated graphics, ray tracing, AI, virtualization, and large memory capacities. The A40 includes 48 GB of memory, expandable to 96 GB through NVLink, while the RTX A6000 offers 48 GB and professional rendering and compute capabilities.

Delta expects premium-cabin revenue to surpass coach sales for at least one or two quarters next year. Last quarter, premium ticket revenue rose 9% to nearly $5.8 billion, while main-cabin revenue fell 4% to just over $6 billion. CEO Ed Bastian reported no slowdown in premium demand as airlines add more upscale seats.

Former Langley City mayor and one-term Liberal MLA Peter Fassbender is considering running for mayor again, with a decision expected by early August. Fassbender served as mayor before winning Surrey-Fleetwood in 2013 and holding several provincial cabinet posts. Two incumbent city councillors have also declared mayoral campaigns.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is a momentum indicator ranging from 0 to 100 that measures gains and losses to identify overbought, oversold, reversal, and pullback conditions. Standard thresholds are typically 70 and 30, while day traders may use shorter time frames and more extreme levels such as 85 and 15. RSI can support mean-reversion, momentum, and divergence strategies, but settings should reflect the asset, market trend, time frame, risk tolerance, and trading goals.

Contracts for Difference (CFDs) allow traders to speculate on asset price movements without owning the underlying stocks, commodities, currencies, or indices. Profit or loss depends on the difference between opening and closing prices, and CFD trading is zero-sum and often leveraged.

Backtests cited include a SPY strategy producing 313 trades averaging 0.86% per trade but with severe drawdowns. A modified two-day RSI strategy generated 355 trades averaging 0.67%, with smaller, smoother drawdowns. Trading profitability also depends on spreads and brokers. Effective RSI-based CFD trading requires backtesting, combining RSI with other indicators where appropriate, monitoring divergences, adapting thresholds and time frames, and managing risks including leverage, commissions, slippage, taxes, and potential losses.

Humans have long used caffeine and nicotine to improve focus; caffeine blocks sleep-promoting adenosine, while nicotine mimics acetylcholine to activate attention-related brain areas. Current research includes Tim Tully’s effort to develop a memory-enhancing drug by studying people with exceptional memories and manipulating CREB activators, which has produced fruit flies with photographic memories. Other projects seek genes associated with intelligence for possible genetic enhancement, though hundreds may be involved and success is uncertain. Researchers are also developing deep brain stimulation devices that monitor neural activity and electrically correct abnormal patterns linked to panic attacks, depression, or psychosis. These technologies remain in development and raise concerns about potential misuse.

The Supreme Court will review whether a Texas man’s plea-agreement waiver bars him from appealing a mandatory mental-health-medication condition imposed at sentencing. Hunter pleaded guilty to aiding and abetting wire fraud and received 51 months in prison, three years of supervised release, and over $235,000 in restitution. The 5th Circuit dismissed his appeal based on the waiver, despite the trial judge telling him he could appeal. Hunter argues other federal appeals courts permit similar constitutional challenges. Arguments are likely early next year, with a decision by summer.

The Colorado Supreme Court affirmed a directed verdict awarding real estate brokers their commission. The brokers fulfilled their duty by producing Mrs. Tallman as a purchaser, regardless of whether the other parties were bound by or ratified the sale contract. Any variance between the pleadings and proof did not affect substantial rights. The rejected instructions concerned immaterial issues, and any errors in refusing to strike replication allegations were harmless.

Yankees rookie Cam Schlittler pitched eight scoreless innings with 12 strikeouts, five hits and no walks in an AL Wild Card game against Boston, setting an MLB first. Scout Matt Hyde called the performance “unbelievable” and “surreal.”

The study compared methods for annually forecasting fatal opioid overdoses at the census-tract level to support geographically targeted public health interventions. It analyzed 1,620 Massachusetts tracts using 2001–2021 data and 1,328 Cook County, Illinois, tracts using 2014–2023 data. Predictors included prior overdose counts, location, time, and optional Social Vulnerability Index features.

Models ranged from simple baselines—zero predictions, previous-year counts, and historical averages—to weighted averages, Poisson regression, gradient-boosted trees, Gaussian processes, Bayesian spatiotemporal models, spatially lagged negative binomial regression, and CASTNet. Performance was assessed using mean absolute error, root mean squared error, and a new intervention-focused metric, percentage of best possible reach (%BPR). %BPR measures how many deaths occurred in the model’s K recommended tracts relative to the maximum attainable with perfect hindsight; evaluations assumed K=100.

Model rankings differed by metric. In Massachusetts, Bayesian spatiotemporal models achieved stronger %BPR than a Gaussian process despite similar or better error-based performance by both. In Cook County, Poisson regression with vulnerability features had higher %BPR than gradient-boosted trees despite worse error metrics. Selecting models by %BPR could identify 18 additional annual deaths in Massachusetts and 15 in Cook County compared with selections based on error metrics.

Simple historical-average models performed competitively with complex models in both locations. In Massachusetts, weighted historical averages were within two annual deaths of the leading method; in Cook County, the best Bayesian model reached less than one additional annual death compared with the historical average. The authors therefore recommend tuned historical-average baselines in future forecasting studies and intervention-aware evaluation metrics when models guide resource allocation.

Limitations include evaluation in only two jurisdictions, incomplete Cook County medical examiner coverage, use of a fixed 100-tract intervention budget, BPR’s emphasis on overall burden rather than rapidly increasing risk, and a limited covariate set. The study provides open-source modeling software, preprocessing code, and processed Cook County data.

MSPM0G3519/3518 and MSPM0G1519/1518 MCUs provide five decreasing-power modes: RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN. RUN executes code; peripheral interrupts can wake SLEEP, STOP, and STANDBY. SHUTDOWN disables both power domains and permits wake through NRST, SWD, or selected IO logic-level matches. PD1 powers the CPU, memories, and high-performance peripherals in RUN and SLEEP, while PD0 supports low-power peripherals through STANDBY.

The PMU supplies and supervises core power, offering programmable brown-out monitoring, mode-aware regulation, and parity-protected trim. The clock module includes internal and external low- and high-frequency sources, SYSPLL outputs up to 80 MHz, and clocks distributed according to operating mode.

The DMA controller has six full-featured and six basic channels, supports transfers from 8 to 128 bits, blocks up to 64K transfers, configurable triggers, channel cascading, ping-pong buffering, and stride operation. The event manager routes peripheral events to the CPU, DMA, or other peripherals through static and programmable paths.

Memory includes dual-bank flash up to 256/512KB plus 16KB data flash, ECC, 1KB sectors, selected high-endurance sectors, and bank swapping for firmware updates. Up to 128KB SRAM is divided into two 64KB banks; Bank 0 has ECC or parity and remains available through STANDBY, while Bank 1 is configurable and available through STOP. Both lose contents in SHUTDOWN. SRAM supports configurable read-write and read-execute partitions.

Up to 93 GPIO pins support atomic set, clear, and toggle operations, low-power wakeup, and configurable multiplexing, drive strength, speed, and pulls. Analog capabilities include two 12-bit, 4Msps ADCs with hardware averaging, internal temperature and supply channels, selectable internal or external references, a temperature sensor, comparators, and a buffered 8- or 12-bit DAC with calibration, FIFO, DMA, and hardware triggering.

Security features include AES-128/256 acceleration, protected storage for four keys, configurable firewalls, CRC-16/32, and a 32-bit true random-number generator. A math accelerator offloads 32-bit calculations.

Communication peripherals include UART with LIN support, I2C through 1Mbit/s with SMBus 3.0 and low-power wake, SPI up to 32Mbit/s on supported pins, and CAN-FD up to 5Mbit/s. The low-frequency subsystem contains RTC_B and an independent watchdog. Additional peripherals include a windowed watchdog and general-purpose and advanced timers supporting capture/compare, PWM, synchronization, DMA and ADC triggering, quadrature decoding, and fault handling.

Debugging uses a two-wire SWD interface. The boot strap loader programs or configures memory through UART or I2C, supports a 256-bit password, and can be invoked by pins, blank-memory detection, or software. Factory memory stores device identification and trim data.

Recommended implementation includes 10µF and 0.1µF VDD decoupling capacitors, a 47kΩ NRST pullup with 10nF capacitor, and a 0.47µF VCORE capacitor. Optional SYSOSC frequency correction requires a precision 100kΩ resistor. Open-drain IOs require external pullups.

TI provides LaunchPad hardware, SDKs, SysConfig, training, cloud tools, Code Composer Studio, and support for IAR, Keil, TI Arm-Clang, and GNU Arm toolchains. The April 2025 revision updates operating-mode functionality, peripheral counts, electrical specifications, SRAM and flash descriptions, security features, and package options.

The speaker accepts national leadership with gratitude, humility, and a heightened sense of responsibility amid unprecedented global conflict and domestic difficulties. He recalls the country’s prosperity under republican institutions, peace, commerce, manufacturing, public works, and debt reduction. Although the United States observed justice and impartial neutrality, belligerent powers imposed unlawful measures against it. He pledges to pursue peace, neutrality, diplomacy, national independence, union, constitutional government, states’ and individual rights, religious liberty, press freedom, fiscal economy, debt repayment, limited standing forces, a strong militia, economic improvements, science, education, and existing plans concerning aboriginal neighbors. Drawing encouragement from predecessors, citizens, public representatives, and divine guidance, he expresses confidence that national unity will protect the country’s honor and interests.

Traditional definitions of bear, bull, correction and crash markets rely on arbitrary percentage thresholds that do not meaningfully help investors manage risk or deploy capital. A more useful framework combines long-term market performance, economic trends, volatility and investor psychology. Secular bull markets typically last 10 to 20 years, supported by economic growth and investors’ increasing willingness to pay more for earnings. Secular bear markets feature economic challenges, greater volatility and declining earnings multiples. Historical bull markets, including 1982–2000, were driven more by expanding price-to-earnings ratios than by profit growth. Investors should therefore focus on the direction of valuation multiples and the psychology driving markets rather than fixed percentage definitions.

Montecito Union School District agreed to pay $7.5 million to two brothers, now 65 and 68, who alleged former superintendent and principal Stanford Kerr sexually abused them in the 1970s. The settlement, reached before a scheduled 17-day trial, equals about 40% of the 350-student district’s 2025-26 budget. The district admitted no liability and lacked insurance coverage for the period.

The brothers sought $35 million and filed suit in 2022 after California’s Assembly Bill 218 removed the statute of limitations for childhood sexual abuse claims against public agencies. Kerr, who died in 2013, was never criminally charged. A third plaintiff previously settled similar allegations for $1 million.

Superintendent Anthony Ranii said the risk of a larger jury award threatened district operations. Costs will be managed through a hiring freeze, reductions through natural attrition, and redirected capital-repair funds, while avoiding layoffs. The settlement follows stalled legislation that would have restored a statute of limitations. California districts face potentially billions of dollars in similar claims and sharply rising insurance costs.

President Trump’s threatened 100% tariffs on branded pharmaceuticals did not begin as announced. The White House said it would prepare tariffs for companies that neither expand U.S. infrastructure nor reach drug-pricing agreements, without providing a timeline. Administration officials are contacting pharmaceutical executives nearly daily, seeking deals and U.S. investment ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Requests include increased production from Eli Lilly and Pfizer and a possible U.S. headquarters for AstraZeneca.

Deutsche Bank is seeking to sell its 8.8 percent stake in Dubai-based Abraaj, viewing it as non-core amid its own restructuring and Abraaj’s investor dispute. Sources said a sale has become more urgent but could require a steep discount, while valuation is complicated by undisclosed debt. Abraaj faces an investigation by four investors over alleged misuse of money from a $1 billion healthcare fund, which it denies. The firm is considering asset sales to ease cashflow pressures and has cut jobs, reorganized management, suspended investments and released investors from capital commitments. Two senior executives have also resigned.

The passage specifies host BIOS and UEFI requirements for integrating AGESA software. The host must establish a valid stack, initialize standard headers, locate binary entry points, call AGESA through dispatchers and bridge routines, and implement a call-out router that maps function identifiers to host services. Calls use a 32-bit protected-mode flat-addressing model where specified.

UEFI execution spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases, with separate libraries, build targets, drivers, and compiler tools. SEC establishes 32-bit C execution and Cache-as-RAM using AMD-provided stack macros. PEIMs coordinate processor, memory, and reset initialization and publish PPIs and memory-information HOBs. DXE performs late initialization, publishes generated tables through a protocol, and can control integrated-GPU VGA decoding.

Integration requires platform option files, UEFI control files, environment variables such as `AGESA_ROOT` and `AGESA_OptsDir`, and build selection by platform solution, build method, and features. AGESA may be built as binary modules through a common dispatcher or integrated directly from source. The host must not alter stack registers or cache controls during Cache-as-RAM operation.

AMD-provided stackless assembly procedures establish and remove the pre-memory stack. They initialize processor caches, divide stack space among cores, configure MTRRs where applicable, create the SEC-to-PEI handoff structure, and later disable Cache-as-RAM after memory becomes available. AArch64 APUs with a Platform Security Processor do not use these early stack macros because the PSP initializes DRAM.

Utility services create and release AGESA parameter structures, retrieve DIMM data-eye results, processor APIC and PCI addresses, execution-cache size, current core identity, memory-device location for an address, MMIO mappings, and event-log entries. Most services require an established stack; some also require operational coherent HyperTransport links.

Published initialization entry points execute in boot-time order. Reset initialization performs minimal processor and chipset setup and allocates constrained execution-cache regions. Early initialization configures HyperTransport, processor power management, PCIe topology, graphics, platform characteristics, and VRM properties. Post initialization discovers and initializes memory, applies memory, ECC, interleaving, UMA, voltage, training, and refresh options, transfers artifacts to main memory, and disables the pre-memory stack. Environment initialization moves HOB and artifact data into host-controlled permanent storage. Graphics initialization runs after PCI resource allocation and before video BIOS execution. Late initialization creates operating-system information tables such as DMI, P-state, WHEA, IVRS, CRAT, CDIT, and ACPI data.

Ready-to-boot processing saves silicon context for suspend, separating critical nonvolatile data from other restorable data. Resume entry points restore memory, processor state, silicon registers, and final operating-system handoff state in sequence. The host remains responsible for detecting resume, restoring MTRRs where required, supplying saved-context locations, and initiating suspend or operating-system restart.

Required host call-outs include main-memory buffer allocation and deallocation. Allocated buffers must meet requested sizes, return usable addresses and handles, and persist as reserved runtime memory when the heap status requires it. Creation and release operations must be paired, and failure to provide required call-outs or preserve AGESA artifact data can cause initialization errors.

This study compared Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) with an explainable convolutional neural network (CNN) for detecting technical and procedural outliers in multicenter plantar pressure data. Experts labeled 1,031 samples from 703 subjects, including 798 valid recordings and 233 outliers across four categories: general acquisition errors, double-foot captures, inverted orientations, and incorrect side annotations. Synthetic augmentation produced a final dataset of 2,798 samples.

SPM used affine registration, pixel-wise nonparametric testing, and cluster-based correction. The CNN incorporated foot-side metadata and used SHAP to explain pixel contributions. Both approaches were evaluated through nested stratified cross-validation with subject-level grouping.

The CNN outperformed SPM, achieving mean F1 and Matthews Correlation Coefficient scores of 0.99 and 0.96, compared with 0.93 and 0.78 for SPM. SPM frequently missed incorrect side annotations and misclassified valid pathological feet as outliers, likely because of pixel-level deviations and registration difficulties. The CNN performed least accurately on the heterogeneous general acquisition error category.

Sixteen plantar-pressure experts evaluated correctly classified explanations. Both SPM and SHAP explanations were rated positively for clarity, correctness, usefulness, relevance, understandability, trustworthiness, and completeness, with no significant differences. SPM was descriptively perceived as simpler. Experts reported relatively high agreement between approaches and most often preferred SHAP explanations (43.48%), followed by SPM (34.78%), both together (17.39%), or neither (4.35%).

The findings support automated, explainable quality control for plantar pressure data, with the CNN providing superior detection performance. Limitations include synthetic outliers, possible registration errors, reliance on SHAP, and the exploratory human evaluation. Future work could examine deformable registration, regional pressure measures, more realistic synthetic data, alternative explainability methods, and refined user-evaluation protocols.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K dated February 11, 2015, reporting that it issued a press release and CFO commentary on financial results for the quarter and fiscal year ended January 25, 2015. The materials are furnished as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2 and are not deemed filed under specified securities laws. CFO Colette M. Kress signed the report.

Defending the High Post Split Offense requires guarding the high post, disrupting guard splits, countering down screens, and protecting the low post. In the basic NBA “Show & Recover” strategy, perimeter defenders sag toward the high post to prevent handoffs and drives, while the post defender protects the basket and pressures the high-post player toward a weak-hand corner. Against down screens, defenders show to force shooters wide, chase them, then recover to deny passes and prevent mismatches rather than switch. Once the ball reaches a wing, defenders pressure the ball, defend or deny the low post, and pack the weak side.

The aggressive SOS strategy begins by forcing the ballhandler toward the sideline and denying the high-post entry. Defenders switch on guard splits and down screens, use contact to impede shooters, and assume strong pass-denial positions. Wing passes trigger double-team traps, with other defenders rotating to front the post and occupy help positions. Defenders must rotate as passes leave the trap. Post entries are trapped with corresponding weakside rotations, while standard SOS rules apply if screening action begins.

The speaker described his baby’s birth as amazing, then discussed teammates rallying after Dino suffered an elbow to the head. He said high-tempo hockey incidents happen but expected the league to review the hit.

The speaker says his knee feels strong and the MCL has healed well, though another painless tear will require surgery after the series. A brace will help. After rapid rehabilitation, he is ready and eager to return for tomorrow’s game and hopes another player recovers quickly.

The “Flash/Back Door” offense attacks the vulnerable middle of a Box-and-One defense by flashing a baseline post player inside. The post can shoot, feed a wing’s back cut, or initiate high/low action. If no shot develops, the offense flows into Single/Double Screen continuity. Variations include baseline screens for the star player and a point back-door entry.

Successful execution requires coordinated screens, post-ups, defensive recognition, communication, timing, and practice through breakdown drills and scrimmages. Teams should scout defensive screen and post coverage, monitor adjustments, vary alignments, and target weak defenders. A Box-and-One uses four zone defenders and one aggressive chaser dedicated to denying a designated opponent the ball.

The Supreme Court will hear on August 17 Lt Col Prasad Shrikant Purohit’s bail plea and a victim’s father’s challenge to Sadhvi Pragya Singh Thakur’s bail in the 2008 Malegaon blast case. The Bombay High Court had granted Thakur bail but rejected Purohit’s application.

H. B. Fuller VP Traci L. Jensen sold 5,397 shares at an average $58.40, totaling $315,184.80. The stock opened at $56.81, with a $2.87 billion market capitalization and a 52-week range of $41.52–$58.74. Quarterly earnings of $0.65 per share missed estimates by $0.02, while revenue of $562.87 million exceeded expectations. Analysts forecast fiscal-year earnings of $2.59 per share. The company declared a $0.15 quarterly dividend, equivalent to a 1.06% annual yield. Analysts’ consensus rating was “Hold,” with a $57.40 price target. Institutional investors owned 92.37% of the stock, with several firms increasing holdings. H. B. Fuller manufactures and markets adhesives, sealants and other specialty chemicals.

NVIDIA’s May 7, 2015 Form 8-K reports first-quarter fiscal 2016 results for the period ended April 26, 2015. It also announces the board-approved wind-down of Icera modem operations in the second quarter of fiscal 2016 while remaining open to a sale. If no sale occurs, NVIDIA expects $100 million to $125 million in restructuring charges, primarily during fiscal 2016. Exhibits include the earnings press release and CFO commentary.

The study examines teachers’ knowledge, attitudes, concerns, and readiness regarding metaverse integration in education. The metaverse can provide immersive, collaborative, personalized, and risk-free learning experiences, but requires reliable infrastructure, accessible devices, suitable content, and teacher training. Potential limitations include technical difficulties, increased mental effort, health effects, data security, unequal access, and uncertain learning advantages over traditional media.

Researchers surveyed 333 teachers in Türkiye using a 28-question online questionnaire and thematic and descriptive analysis. Teachers reported moderate knowledge of the metaverse, while 78.1% had experienced related environments, mainly virtual reality or three-dimensional virtual worlds. They generally viewed educational use positively and were willing to adopt it and receive training.

Frequently identified benefits included engaging materials, opportunities to apply knowledge, experiential learning, exposure to new technologies, and fewer educational constraints. Major concerns included technical problems, addiction and other psychological effects, inequality of opportunity, data security, insufficient teacher readiness, preparation difficulties, physical discomfort, and cost.

Teachers considered information technology, physics, biology, chemistry, and mathematics especially suitable for metaverse applications, particularly for visualizing abstract concepts, conducting experiments, supporting collaboration, and creating realistic environments. However, they judged teachers, parents, schools, and the broader education system largely unprepared, while viewing students as relatively more ready. Most expected widespread implementation within ten years, particularly within three to five years.

The study concludes that the metaverse could create dynamic, interactive, and secure educational experiences, including simulations and virtual field trips. Successful implementation requires gradual adoption, robust infrastructure, professional development, age-appropriate content, behavioral guidelines, stakeholder cooperation, user feedback, and attention to physical and psychological health.

Young people choosing college courses should recognize that career plans can change and technological advances will reshape many industries. They should develop valuable, specialized skills that increase their earning power, whether employed or self-employed. Employers generally seek maximum work for minimum cost, so workers must ensure their expertise is properly rewarded. No job will be enjoyable every day, and work may sometimes primarily support the more important parts of life outside employment.

Grand Erie and Brant-Haldimand-Norfolk Catholic school board officials are discussing merging high school sports across Brantford, Haldimand and Norfolk into one league, potentially by 2019-20. Currently, most teams compete only within their counties. The proposed district-wide association would standardize schedules, rules and championship opportunities for public and Catholic students. No decision or formal timeline has been established, and further meetings are planned. Increased travel costs and time, particularly for schools at opposite ends of the district, remain key concerns to be considered.

LUKB Disease Trajectory (LUKB DT) is an R Shiny web tool integrated into the LUKB platform for identifying disease trajectories from electronic medical records. It accepts participant IDs, diagnoses, dates, exposures, prevalence thresholds, study periods, and adjustment variables, and can run locally for secure analysis without extensive programming.

The workflow first uses Cox regression with time-varying exposure to identify diseases associated with increased risk. Binomial tests then detect temporal disease pairs and determine directionality. Conditional logistic regression validates pairs using matched case-control datasets, after which confirmed pairs are concatenated into trajectories.

Using UK Biobank ICD-10 data, the authors examined trajectories following COVID-19. The source dataset contained 6,166,668 records from 446,995 individuals. The analysis included 183,386 individuals, 8,411 COVID-19 cases, and 274 diseases. Cox regression identified 90 diseases associated with COVID-19. Of 8,010 possible disease pairs, 2,410 showed temporal associations, 527 passed directionality testing, and all 527 were validated. Trajectories mainly linked COVID-19 to viral agents, viral pneumonia, respiratory failure, healthcare-associated conditions, and other medical care. Immune-related diseases were not identified, possibly because UK Biobank ICD-10 data incompletely captured COVID-19 cases and related conditions.

The full analysis took 55 minutes using eight computing cores. Limitations include dependence on processed diagnostic records and the construction of trajectories by concatenating statistically supported pairs rather than directly observing complete patient trajectories. The authors recommend comprehensive, representative datasets and advise using the results primarily to investigate disease risk factors and mechanisms rather than for patient clustering. The work is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed.

Scotland will abolish local authority burial and cremation fees for anyone under 18, supported by £500,000 in government funding. The agreement with Cosla standardizes policies across councils and aligns Scotland with England. The Church of Scotland welcomed the change, saying it would ease unexpected financial pressure on bereaved families.

NVIDIA appointed Stephen C. Neal to its Board on March 30, 2019. He received 1,419 restricted stock units vesting semi-annually over three years, 139 units vesting May 15, 2019, a $10,890 cash retainer, and an indemnity agreement. The Form 8-K was signed April 1, 2019.

Children with developmental language disorder, autism, or migration-related language challenges often need tailored support. Speech-language therapists and educators may struggle to provide frequent, varied, and consistent examples of targeted morphological structures during interactive, game-based interventions. Existing robot-assisted language learning systems offer scalability but are often limited by rigid programming, speech-recognition errors, and difficulties managing natural interaction and turn-taking.

The multiprofessional research team developed TalBot, which combines ChatGPT with the Furhat conversational robot. Co-designed and tested with 13 preschool children with language vulnerabilities and seven educators, TalBot leads a word-guessing game, generates clues, provides feedback, manages turns, displays appropriate expressions, redirects unrelated dialogue, and interprets some mispronunciations or speech-recognition errors. Personal-data risks were reduced by discouraging disclosure and limiting third-party processing mainly to temporary voice recognition.

The researchers propose extending TalBot to morphological learning. An LLM could rapidly generate adaptable linguistic material, repeatedly model targeted grammatical forms, and demonstrate intervention strategies for educators. The robot may reduce the cognitive and time demands associated with producing varied, structured language input in real time.

Planned development includes laboratory co-design, preschool field studies, and a feasibility study involving children with clinically significant language vulnerabilities. Researchers will compare robot- and educator-led 15-minute sessions, quantify targeted morphological forms, assess whether observing the robot affects educator performance, analyze interactions and interviews, and measure children’s skills before and after intervention. User experiences and emotional responses will be monitored throughout.

Remaining concerns include data protection, EU AI Act requirements, long-term developmental effects, institutional resistance, children’s sustained participation, and robot costs. The long-term goal is a robust, adaptive LLM-based intervention for teaching morphological structures across languages, developed collaboratively with children and educators and potentially informing lower-cost alternatives.

AGESA integration requires the host environment to establish a stack and implement a call-out router that dispatches binary-module requests to host procedures. UEFI support spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases, with phase-specific libraries, build tools, drivers, PPIs, protocols, configuration files, and environment variables.

The SEC phase establishes 32-bit execution and Cache-as-RAM stacks using AMD-provided macros. Hosts must enable CAR before AmdInitReset, avoid modifying stack registers or cache controls while CAR is active, and use the supplied procedures to create and remove pre-memory stacks. AARCH64 APUs with a Platform Security Processor instead rely on the PSP to initialize DRAM.

PEI modules initialize processors and memory, publish completion PPIs and memory information, and coordinate reset requests. The DXE driver performs late initialization, generates AMD data tables, and publishes a protocol for accessing them. A separate driver controls iGPU VGA decoding through PCI I/O requests.

AGESA supports binary-module and source-integration build methods. Platform defaults and customizations are defined through platform option files, while UEFI control files and variables identify source and option directories.

Provided service procedures create and release parameter structures, retrieve DIMM data-eye results, processor APIC and PCI addresses, execution-cache size, current-core identity, and memory-device location. Other services update MMIO mappings and read event-log entries. Most require an established stack; several also require operational coherent HyperTransport links.

Paramount Skydance owner David Ellison praised CBS News while saying it must rebuild trust and avoid political alignment. He rejected claims that CBS News would become aligned with Trump but did not specify needed improvements. His appointment of The Free Press founder Bari Weiss as CBS News editor in chief has raised questions because of her commentary-focused background. Ellison said CBS News should appeal to center-left and center-right Americans, though its future direction remains unclear.
Emirates reversed its decision to discontinue the Hindu meal option after negative customer feedback, saying it would retain the choice for Hindu passengers.

The push-pull converter uses Type 2A compensation with a 10-kHz crossover target and 16.2-A/V power-stage transconductance. Seven parallel 330-µF capacitors provide approximately 2.3 mF with 0.86-mΩ equivalent ESR. Selected compensation values are 40.2 kΩ for RCOMP, 15 nF for CCOMP, and 47 pF for CHF; tuning during testing may improve performance. A 102-kΩ resistor from RSC to AVSS sets slope compensation.

TPS7H500x-SP controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V. The supply should be regulated and bypassed with at least 0.1 µF from VIN to AVSS, preferably using nearby X5R-or-better ceramic capacitors. Bulk capacitance is advised for remote supplies.

Layout guidance emphasizes separating sensitive feedback and control signals from switch nodes, magnetic components, and high-dv/dt traces; minimizing switching loops and switch-node copper; separating analog and power grounds with a single connection point; and using short, wide high-current traces. Bypass, filtering, compensation, and current-sense components should be placed close to their associated pins. CFP backside metallization should connect to AVSS through multiple vias.

The document includes application curves, CFP and TSSOP layout examples, related evaluation and radiation reports, support and update resources, ESD precautions, revision history, and mechanical, packaging, and ordering information. The August 2024 revision released QMLP options for TPS7H5002-SP, TPS7H5003-SP, and TPS7H5004-SP. TI states that resources are provided “as is,” may change without notice, and remain subject to applicable terms and disclaimers.

US payrolls rose by 200,000 in January, exceeding forecasts, while annual wage growth reached 2.9 per cent, its fastest pace since 2009. Unemployment remained at 4.1 per cent. The data strengthened expectations of a March Federal Reserve rate increase and raised the possibility of more than three hikes in 2018. Treasury yields climbed, with the 10-year exceeding 2.8 per cent and the two-year reaching its highest level since September 2008.

FERC extended NYISO’s Automated Mitigation Procedures through April 30, 2002, rather than the requested October 31 extension. NYISO must file by March 1 a comprehensive mitigation proposal effective May 1. It must refine mitigation by zone, hour, and bid size; assess treatment of new generation and energy-limited resources; coordinate existing mitigation measures; consider must-run rules consistent with PJM and ISO-NE; and collaborate toward a unified Northeast mitigation plan. Enron had opposed the extension.

Cover 2 is a zone defense with five underneath defenders and two safeties dividing deep coverage. In a 4-3 defense, the cornerbacks cover the flats, the Sam and Will linebackers cover hook/curl zones, the Mike covers the middle, and the safeties cover deep halves.

The coverage protects short routes while retaining deep support. Its zone structure lets defenders observe receivers and the quarterback. Hard cornerbacks help stop quick passes, screens, and outside runs because they remain near the line while safeties protect deep routes.

Cover 2 is vulnerable to multiple vertical routes, especially four-vertical and trips formations, which strain the two safeties. It can also leave limited defenders in the box or weak-side running lanes, creating opportunities for large gains if blocks are successful.

Variations include “Switch,” where cornerbacks cover deep halves and safeties cover flats, and disguising Cover 2 from a one-high safety alignment.

Dr. Harris L. Rittenberg’s Jacksonville family practice has served children and adults for over 50 years. The practice emphasizes personal, advanced dental care and continuing education. Dr. Rittenberg participates in the AACD’s domestic violence victim program, and Dr. Brittany Jones recently joined the team.

Ryan Carter said the team must learn from the loss, improve puck execution, avoid turnovers and defensive mistakes, and play its own game. Despite poor play, they had a chance to win. He emphasized forechecking, limiting the goaltender’s involvement, staying positive, and using timely hits to generate momentum.

Leicester manager Craig Shakespeare said the 4-2 defeat at Everton, his first in charge, would not undermine confidence before Wednesday’s Champions League quarter-final against Atletico Madrid. He made five changes due to a congested schedule but said the team still aimed to win. Shakespeare blamed poor defending at set pieces for Everton’s decisive goals and confirmed captain Wes Morgan would miss the Madrid match with a back injury.

Lowe’s will leave NASCAR after 18 seasons, ending its longtime sponsorship of Jimmie Johnson’s No. 48 team. Johnson said a new sponsor could accompany him through his remaining “handful of years” in Cup racing. Though he expects to leave NASCAR eventually, he plans to continue racing and is interested in events including Le Mans, the Rolex 24 and potentially the Indianapolis 500.

WhatsApp provides free cross-platform messaging with videos, photos, sound clips, emoticons, personalized backgrounds, and automatic contact integration. The strategy buys the S&P 500 ETF SPY at the close when the index opens at a five-day low and closes above its opening price, then sells at the next day’s open. Overnight S&P 500 returns historically average 0.04%. From 2005 onward, the strategy reportedly averaged 0.26% per trade, or 0.17% excluding an October 2008 outlier.

This study used VOSviewer co-occurrence analysis to examine author-supplied keywords from 1,076 Information Systems Education Journal articles published between 2003 and 2024. Articles were divided into five eras, and term maps grouped frequently co-occurring keywords into topical clusters.

The 2003–2007 era emphasized curriculum, assessment, accreditation, ethics, pedagogy, and other foundational IS education topics. From 2008–2012, research broadened toward pedagogy and student issues, including mentoring, retention, women, minorities, social networking, and outsourcing. The 2013–2017 era featured cybersecurity, big data, analytics, pedagogy, and renewed curriculum assessment. During 2018–2022, business and data analytics formed separate clusters, while COVID-19-related concerns such as attendance and attentiveness appeared; cybersecurity, pedagogy, online learning, and IS curriculum remained prominent. In 2023–2024, topics consolidated into three clusters—pedagogy, analytics, and artificial intelligence—although this era contained only two years of data.

Across the eras, pedagogy maintained the highest overall prominence, analytics rose from a middle-ranked topic to first, and assessment, programming, and cybersecurity declined or disappeared from the latest period. The number of clusters peaked at 12 in 2008–2012 and fell to three in 2023–2024. The full-network analysis identified nine clusters and showed sustained emphasis on pedagogy and curriculum.

The authors describe this as the first known analysis of ISEDJ’s complete available corpus. Limitations include reliance solely on author-supplied keywords, possible bias toward period-specific terminology, and distortion from special issues. Future research may incorporate titles and abstracts and allow the data to define eras rather than using predetermined five-year periods.

Apple filed a Form 8-K on July 26, 2016, reporting the release of financial results and related data for its third fiscal quarter ended June 25, 2016. The press release and data sheet were attached as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. The report was signed by Chief Financial Officer Luca Maestri.

New York’s Excelsior Scholarship offers tuition-free SUNY or CUNY attendance to qualifying residents, but covers only tuition after other aid, excluding fees, housing, books and other expenses. The program has increased student interest in public colleges and intensified competition for smaller private institutions.

Private colleges argue that their education may still offer greater value despite higher costs. In response, schools including Canisius, Roberts Wesleyan, Le Moyne and St. Bonaventure have reduced tuition, expanded scholarships, guaranteed four-year graduation, or added internships and mentoring. Some administrators favor expanding the existing Tuition Assistance Program instead, saying Excelsior disadvantages private schools and may be financially unsustainable.

Students and families continue weighing cost against academic programs, campus atmosphere, personal attention and overall fit. Private colleges remain economically important in New York, enrolling nearly 500,000 undergraduates and directly employing about 180,000 people.

The disclosure presents an image-processing method, apparatus, electronic device, and storage medium for placing models, such as advertisements, into videos. A target three-dimensional model is positioned on a selected plane in a first video frame, with model-surface feature points aligned to that plane. Their world and pixel coordinates are used to calculate the first frame’s camera pose. The target plane is then tracked across subsequent frames using homography matrices, enabling feature-point coordinates and camera poses to be determined for each frame. The placeholder model is replaced with a target model, projected into all frames according to the calculated poses, and synthesized into a target video.

The target plane may be selected manually or identified using a trained neural network. Model pose adjustment may also be manual or AI-assisted. Camera poses may be calculated using camera intrinsic parameters and a perspective-n-point algorithm. Plane tracking can optimize each frame’s homography from the previous frame and exclude occluded pixels.

The method avoids full three-dimensional scene reconstruction, does not require large parallax, and can operate without relying on image feature extraction. It is described as reducing computation while improving speed, convenience, accuracy, applicability, and placement quality. Corresponding software or hardware modules implement video acquisition, model placement, coordinate and pose determination, plane tracking, projection, and video synthesis. Data and processing may also use blockchain storage and nodes.

Supporters say revisions would reduce uncertainty and tailor oversight, while consumer advocates warn they could revive pre-crisis risk-taking. Weapons expert John Schilling said the failure suggested an early-stage test of a new or underdeveloped missile, possibly one displayed at Pyongyang’s military parade.
