The lecture introduces blockchain’s technical foundations through Bitcoin. Its core components are cryptography, consensus mechanisms, and transaction ledgers. Key design features include timestamped append-only logs, block headers, Merkle trees, public and private keys, digital signatures, Bitcoin addresses, proof of work, nodes, network communication, and a native currency that incentivizes mining.

Hash functions map data of any size to fixed-size outputs. Secure hashes are deterministic, efficient, one-way, collision-resistant, and sensitive to small input changes. Bitcoin uses SHA-256 to link blocks and secure data. Merkle trees compress transaction data into a root hash stored in each block header. Headers also contain the previous block’s hash, timestamp, difficulty target, nonce, and version. Lightweight nodes can store headers rather than the full transaction history.

Asymmetric cryptography generates linked public and private keys. Private keys create digital signatures, while public keys verify them without revealing the private key. Secure random-number generation is essential when creating keys. Bitcoin addresses are derived from public keys through multiple hashing and encoding steps.

Bitcoin addresses the double-spending problem by maintaining an ordered transaction ledger without a trusted central authority. Miners perform proof of work, receive newly created bitcoin, and often join mining pools. Bitcoin’s supply is capped at 21 million, with mining rewards declining over time. Changes to its decentralized software require consensus among network participants.

The offside trap is a defensive maneuver in which all back defenders move upfield together just before a forward pass, attempting to leave attackers offside. If successful, it can win possession through an offside violation without a tackle; if unsuccessful, it may leave the goalkeeper exposed. Changes in offside interpretation and increased use of short passing have made the tactic riskier.

Effective execution requires mature, knowledgeable players, precise timing, coordination, communication, sufficient field space, and a disciplined defensive line. One designated defender—usually a central back—must decide when to call the trap using a clear verbal or non-verbal signal. At the signal, every defender must sprint forward three to five yards in unison. A single defender remaining behind can keep attackers onside and defeat the trap.

The tactic is generally more suitable against teams using predictable through balls than opponents employing quick short passes and fast, skillful strikers. Flat-back formations support it better than stopper-sweeper systems. It may be used during normal play or free kicks, with midfielders sometimes covering the vacated space.

Teams should practice varied situations repeatedly before using the trap in games. Coaches must weigh its benefits against the risk of conceding, scout opponents, protect signals from detection, and avoid overuse because opponents may adapt and beat it.

Asia-Pacific equities rose in April on stronger risk appetite, easing geopolitical concerns and robust corporate earnings. Regional shares neared a two-year high, led by India’s 20% gain. New Zealand and India had the highest valuations, while South Korea and Hong Kong were cheapest.

Enron replaced CFO Andrew Fastow with former treasurer Jeff McMahon to restore investor confidence amid an SEC inquiry into partnerships Fastow managed that conducted complex, off-balance-sheet transactions with Enron. The arrangements raised conflict-of-interest, disclosure and liability concerns and contributed to a $35 million loss and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity.

Enron shares fell 17% to $16.41 on October 24 and had roughly halved since its October 16 earnings report, while other energy-trading stocks also declined. Analysts downgraded Enron, citing unclear financial disclosures, potential debt and equity obligations, credit-rating risks and uncertainty about further losses. Enron denied wrongdoing and maintained that its operations and liquidity remained sound, but analysts said Fastow’s departure alone would not resolve the company’s credibility problems.

Air cargo containerization enables rapid intermodal transport without repeatedly unloading goods. Commercial airlines and military forces use customized containers, with passenger aircraft carrying them on lower decks and cargo aircraft using both decks. Market growth is driven by demand for faster global transport and lightweight, durable containers meeting IATA load requirements. Economic slowdowns and rising aviation fuel costs restrict cargo flights and hinder growth. Increasing commercial cargo fleets and military demand may create future opportunities. The market is segmented by refrigerated and non-refrigerated containers, aircraft type, end user, and geography. Aircraft categories include narrow-body, wide-body, very large, and military aircraft, while end users are commercial airlines and defense forces. Major vendors operate across North America and Europe.

This protocol outlines a systematic review of how hospital Rapid Response Team (RRT) services are introduced or redesigned and how implementation success is measured. RRTs respond to cardiac arrests and acute patient deterioration, but their names, staffing, leadership, resources, activation criteria, and service models vary considerably. Increasing demand and limited guidance on adapting services motivate the review.

The review will include prospective and retrospective observational cohort studies involving new RRT services or service redesign, without restrictions on publication status, language, year, comparator, or reported outcome; studies that cannot be translated into English will be excluded. Searches will cover Medline, CINAHL, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, reference lists, conference abstracts, and expert consultation.

Two independent reviewers will screen studies, assess full texts, and extract data, with disagreements resolved through discussion or a third reviewer. Extracted information will include study and team characteristics, reasons and methods for implementation, implementation time frames, communication and simulation techniques, and quantitative or qualitative outcome measures. Risk of bias will be assessed in duplicate using the JBI critical appraisal checklist.

The primary outcome is a description of implementation methods. Secondary outcomes include reasons for change, implementation duration, and measures used to evaluate success. Findings will be synthesized mainly narratively, with simple statistics on implementation methods. Anticipated limitations include study heterogeneity and limited research on service implementation and change management. Ethical approval is unnecessary because only published studies will be reviewed. Results will be presented at scientific meetings and submitted to a peer-reviewed journal. The review has no external funding.

Equity represents corporate ownership and provides value through dividends—cash or stock—and capital gains. Growth companies often reinvest earnings rather than pay dividends. Unlike bonds, common stockholders are residual claimants: bondholders receive promised payments first, while equity holders receive any remaining value and have unlimited upside. Limited liability restricts investors’ losses to their investment, encouraging entrepreneurship, innovation, and capital formation. Voting rights and access to public markets also enable large-scale investment.

Short selling improves market efficiency by allowing negative information to affect prices. Equity securities trade in primary markets when first issued and in secondary markets afterward. Primary-market activity, including IPOs, is strongly influenced by business and credit cycles. Secondary-market volume has expanded through internet trading, electronic communications networks, electronic order routing, and other technologies, making trading faster, cheaper, and easier.

The Dividend Discount Model values stock as the present value of all expected future dividends, discounted using rates reflecting the risks of each cash flow and general market conditions. Equity valuation is more complex than bond valuation because both future cash flows and risk-adjusted discount rates are uncertain. Market prices establish appropriate returns by comparing investment opportunities and their risks.

With constant dividends and a constant discount rate, stock value is \(D/r\). Higher expected dividends increase price, while higher interest rates reduce it. If dividends grow perpetually at rate \(g\), value is \(D/(r-g)\), requiring \(r>g\). Prices can change sharply when expectations about growth change. Rearranging the model shows that the required return equals dividend yield plus expected growth, so company value reflects both current payouts and future growth opportunities.

These simplified formulas describe steady states. Companies with changing, zero, or negative dividends require forecasts of individual cash flows, potentially using separate annuity calculations for different periods. Such forecasts are difficult and inaccurate. Companies generally avoid raising dividends unless they expect to sustain them because dividend cuts signal financial trouble, though temporary suspensions or extraordinary dividends may occur. Cost of capital is important to managers allocating funds and to investors comparing expected returns, while financing choices depend on internal funds, borrowing costs, debt risk, and market conditions.

A geoarchaeological study of Karnak Temple analyzed 61 sediment cores and thousands of pottery fragments to reconstruct 3,000 years of landscape change. The site was regularly flooded before about 2520 BCE, suggesting occupation began during the Old Kingdom. Karnak developed on high ground created between two Nile channels, which later diverged and silted up, allowing expansion. Ancient Egyptians may also have filled channels with desert sand to create building land. Researchers suggest the island setting could have influenced Karnak’s location because it resembled creation myths describing primeval land emerging from water. Further studies are planned across the Luxor floodplain.

In 2006, SunPower CEO Tom Werner faced questions about solar-industry growth, competition, and whether the company’s efficiency advantage could become enduring. Interest in solar power was rising because of energy-independence goals, fossil-fuel pollution, and climate-change concerns. Although photovoltaics supplied only 0.04% of global electricity, demand expanded rapidly amid subsidies, carbon trading, and private investment.

Solar-cell efficiencies had risen from below 4% in the 1950s to 10–20% in 2006. PV power remained substantially more expensive than conventional generation, but annual industry growth averaged 41% from 2003 through 2006 and was projected at 40% through 2011. Japan and Germany led production, while China became the third-largest producer in 2006. Global demand reached 2,500 MWp that year, concentrated particularly in Germany and Japan.

The industry value chain comprised silicon, wafers, cells, modules, and installation. Rapid growth created a silicon shortage, driving up silicon, wafer, cell, and module prices, though planned capacity expansion was expected to ease shortages around 2008. Installation markets ranged from residential roofs to large commercial facilities, with costs varying by location and application. Government support—including rebates, feed-in tariffs, renewable-energy mandates, and tax incentives—was critical to demand, though analysts expected the industry could operate without subsidies by 2012 if costs fell and production scaled.

Founded in 1987 by Stanford professor Richard Swanson, SunPower initially pursued solar concentrators before shifting toward high-efficiency cells. Projects for Honda’s solar race car and NASA’s Helios aircraft pushed the company toward commercial manufacturing. A 2001 partnership with Cypress Semiconductor supplied manufacturing expertise and capital. SunPower began commercial production in 2004 and went public in 2005. Revenue increased from $6 million in 2004 to $78.8 million in 2005 and was projected above $220 million in 2006; the second quarter of 2006 was its first profitable quarter.

SunPower expanded from cells into modules, wafers, silicon supply, ingots, and installation, including its $335 million acquisition of PowerLight. Its back-contact cell design delivered the highest commercially available efficiency in 2006 and improved appearance, space utilization, and installation economics. However, its manufacturing process required roughly twice as many steps as conventional production and higher capital spending. The company targeted cell efficiency of at least 22% by early 2007 while reducing silicon use and wafer thickness.

Competitors included established manufacturers Sharp, Q-Cells, and REC; thin-film producer First Solar; rapidly expanding SunTech; and business-model innovator Citizenre. SunPower therefore had to decide how to balance module pricing, process improvements, vertical integration, and continued innovation while preserving its technological lead.

Microsoft’s Cortana voice assistant works on Windows 10 desktops, laptops, tablets, and phones, integrates with the Edge browser, and searches local and cloud files. It offers dedicated-button activation, Android and iOS availability with reduced efficiency, personalized voice recognition, entertainment features, and location-based reminders. Updates continue to expand its capabilities.

The passage argues that Chinese family education has overindulged children while prioritizing grades, discipline, and academic competition over character, independence, interests, and moral development. It contrasts perceptions of Chinese and American schooling, concluding that children should be free to develop individual abilities rather than be constrained by parents, teachers, and society. Reported consequences of examination-oriented education include weak household skills, emotional and behavioral problems, poor adaptability, and difficulty coping with adversity.

Proposed improvements include equal access to higher education, guidance in discovering personal interests, learning to give and contribute to society, spending time in nature, and participating in manual labor and sports. The passage places moral behavior above scientific knowledge and recommends drawing on traditional Chinese moral education, which emphasizes virtue, self-cultivation, knowledge combined with practice, and harmony between humanity and nature.

Parents are presented as children’s first educators. Shared travel, outdoor activities, play, singing, and conversation can strengthen trust, improve communication, and reduce the generation gap. Religious education, particularly Buddhist teachings, is described as providing love, ethical standards, purpose, self-awareness, and positive thinking. The passage also stresses mothers’ influence on children and calls for greater attention to women’s role in family education. Overall, it advocates combining humanity, morality, parental guidance, traditional values, faith, practical abilities, and personal development in modern Chinese education.

The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card is aimed at consumers paying down debt or financing large purchases. It offers 0% introductory APR for 21 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers made within 120 days, followed by a variable APR of 16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74%. It has no annual fee and includes up to $600 in cellphone protection, subject to a $25 deductible.

Drawbacks include no ongoing rewards, a balance transfer fee of 5% or $5 minimum, and a 3% foreign transaction fee. Applicants are generally recommended to have good or excellent credit, though approval is not guaranteed. The review considers it a strong option for maximizing interest savings but less suitable for ongoing rewards or international use.

Former Ford CEO Mark Fields said US automakers expanded electric-vehicle production without adequately considering consumer demand, which developed more slowly than expected. He said some EV investments have become burdens as near- and medium-term adoption forecasts decline. One automaker announced a $1.6 billion charge to realign EV capacity with demand after federal incentives expired. Industry views differ: one executive predicted US EV sales could halve, while another argued the market could continue growing without subsidies.

The team stayed mentally tough, composed and disciplined, generating more traffic, screens and rebounds around the net before winning on a rebound in overtime. Players adjusted to injuries and shifting wing assignments, with one player finding extra effort despite heavy minutes. Toni Lydman chose to play after consulting trainers and testing himself in warmup, while another player remained in protocol. The speaker praised the team’s special teams but said improved five-on-five play was essential. He emphasized taking the playoffs game by game, recovering and reloading, and declined to revisit the previous day’s comments, saying his focus was game day.

NVIDIA entered an underwriting agreement with Goldman Sachs on March 26, 2020, to issue $5 billion of unsecured senior notes: $1.5 billion at 2.850% due 2030, $1 billion at 3.500% due 2040, $2 billion at 3.500% due 2050, and $500 million at 3.700% due 2060. Net proceeds were approximately $4.97 billion and are intended for general corporate purposes, potentially including debt repayment.

Interest is payable semiannually beginning October 1, 2020. NVIDIA may redeem the notes before maturity under specified terms. Following both a change of control and qualifying credit-rating downgrades, NVIDIA must offer to repurchase affected notes at 101% of principal plus accrued interest. The notes rank equally with other unsecured, unsubordinated debt but are subordinate to secured debt to the extent of collateral and structurally subordinate to subsidiary liabilities. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, indenture documents, note forms, and a legal opinion.

The article backtests two trend-following strategies and one momentum strategy on BTC-USD using Yahoo Finance data from 2015 to April 2021, excluding commissions, slippage, and taxes. Simple moving-average approaches outperformed Bitcoin buy-and-hold while reducing exposure to severe downturns. A short exponential average performed best below 20 days, with the five-day version producing a 145% CAGR. A 100-day/250-day moving-average crossover returned a 115% CAGR versus 94% for buy-and-hold, though its maximum drawdown reached 65% in 2018. A strategy buying when Bitcoin’s close exceeded its close 25 days earlier also beat buy-and-hold and reduced drawdown despite a low win rate. The article concludes that Bitcoin’s large price swings support trend-following and momentum strategies, while noting that past recoveries and future performance are not guaranteed.

The ADS8681W/ADS8685W/ADS8689W are 16-bit SAR ADCs with integrated analog front ends, programmable gain, ADC drivers, references, filtering, protection, alarms, and multiSPI interfaces. Each analog input has at least 1MΩ resistive impedance, independent of sampling and signal frequency, allowing many sources to connect directly. Matching source resistance on AIN_P and AIN_M helps preserve DC accuracy.

Internal overvoltage protection uses input resistors and antiparallel diodes. With AVDD at 5V, properly configured inputs withstand up to ±20V; with AVDD floating, protection extends to ±15V. External protection remains necessary for surge, ESD, and EFT events. Higher source impedance can expand protection limits but increases gain error and noise.

The PGA converts single-ended or differential inputs, adjusts common mode, and supports selectable ranges through RANGE_SEL[3:0], defaulting to ±3V × VREF. A second-order antialiasing low-pass filter has a typical 500kHz cutoff. An integrated high-bandwidth, low-noise buffer drives the ADC sample-and-hold network.

The device supports an internal or external 4.096V reference. The internal reference is enabled by default and requires at least 4.7µF from REFIO to REFGND. REFIO must not directly drive external loads. Solder reflow and mechanical or thermal stress can shift its factory-trimmed value; placing the device in the second reflow pass reduces repeated exposure. External-reference mode uses REFIO as an input and requires at least 10µF plus a nearby 1µF capacitor on REFCAP. The reference buffer’s typical and maximum temperature drifts are 0.5ppm/°C and 2ppm/°C.

Both bipolar and unipolar inputs produce straight-binary output, with LSB size equal to full-scale range divided by 2¹⁶. Input alarms use programmable high and low thresholds with hysteresis. AVDD alarms have fixed typical thresholds of 4.7V and 5.3V. Active flags clear after conversion unless the condition persists; tripped flags clear when ALARM_REG is read. Alarm status can appear on a pin, in registers, or in output data.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI, dual-output SPI, source-synchronous transfers, and daisy chains. Devices exchange 32-bit frames; short frames cannot perform writes but may read selected output bits, while long frames use the final 32 input bits as the command. Daisy chains require optimal frames of 32 × N clocks and reduce throughput as device count increases.

Operational states are RESET, ACQ, and CONV. Reset can perform application or full power-on initialization. Conversions begin on a CONVST/CS rising edge and use an internal clock. Nine configuration registers control identification, reset and power, protocols, output formatting, input range, reference selection, and alarms.

The output word normally contains the latest 16-bit conversion, but it can return register data or fixed test patterns and append device address, range, alarm, and parity fields. Four SPI clock modes are supported; SPI-00-S is the reset default.

NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput. Recommended layout separates analog and digital routing, uses short ground paths, and closely places supply and reference decoupling capacitors. An example industrial module combines an ADS8681W with an eight-channel differential multiplexer to measure standard voltage and current ranges, with software-configurable channels and settling to 1% accuracy in under 5µs.

Microsoft reported results from its December 13, 2022 annual shareholders meeting. Of 7.46 billion eligible shares, 6.41 billion were represented. Shareholders re-elected all 12 directors, approved executive compensation with 88.84% support, and ratified Deloitte & Touche as fiscal 2023 auditor with 95.37% support. Six shareholder proposals—addressing diversity and inclusion, hiring people with arrest or incarceration records, retirement fund climate investments, government use of Microsoft technology, military products, and tax transparency—were rejected.

The speaker viewed his increased scoring chances as positive despite failing to capitalize and hoped to convert in the next game. He said playoff hockey requires disciplined play and contributions from different players. He described the opponent as fast, hardworking, and effective around the puck. Although his performance fluctuated across series, he felt it was improving. He praised veteran Dave for adapting to a defensive role, continuing to score, working hard, and leading through actions. The team plans to pressure and wear down opposing defensemen by playing below the circles, cycling, and avoiding turnovers.

After a strong game despite early penalties, the team remains focused on the work ahead and expects Jersey to respond forcefully. Practices emphasize recovery, while playoff success depends on limiting top scorers, taking away space, applying back pressure, and defending aggressively at the blue line.

UC San Diego engineers developed proof-of-concept ultrasound-powered nanorobots that remove bacteria and their toxins from blood. Gold nanowires coated with fused platelet and red blood cell membranes bind pathogens such as MRSA, neutralize bacterial toxins, and resist biofouling. Ultrasound propels the robots without chemical fuel at speeds up to 35 micrometers per second. In contaminated blood samples, five minutes of treatment reduced bacteria and toxins threefold compared with untreated samples. Researchers aim to use the platform broadly for detoxifying biological fluids, with future work involving animal tests and biodegradable alternatives to gold.
The court discharged a late motion to annul a reference after impartial referees had examined all evidence and agreed on their report without misconduct or refusal to hear testimony.

The Minnesota Timberwolves host the NBA-leading Houston Rockets on Sunday, with both teams on the second night of back-to-backs. Minnesota is sixth in the tightly contested Western Conference after losing 117-101 to San Antonio. Karl-Anthony Towns, averaging 25.5 points over six games, scored 23, while Andrew Wiggins added 21.

Houston improved to 55-14 with a 107-101 win over New Orleans behind James Harden’s 32 points. The Rockets have won 21 of their last 22 games and lead Golden State by 2½ games for the conference’s top seed, despite scoring under 110 points in five straight games. Houston has defeated Minnesota three times this season, each by 18 points, and has won five consecutive meetings and 17 of the last 19.

Stifel downgraded GrubHub from Buy to Hold while raising its price target to $110, citing a balanced risk-reward profile after the stock’s 200-percent annual gain. The firm raised 2019 estimates based on expected benefits from Yum! Brands and smaller-city expansion but said GrubHub’s valuation is elevated. Shares fell 1.6 percent Monday morning.

Kansas City Chiefs general manager Brett Veach enters his first draft in charge without a first-round pick but with one second-rounder and two third-round selections. Since replacing John Dorsey, Veach has improved salary-cap flexibility and aggressively traded picks and players, acquiring Reggie Ragland, Cam Erving, Kendall Fuller and additional draft capital while dealing Alex Smith and Marcus Peters.

With a deep offense strengthened by Sammy Watkins, Kansas City is expected to prioritize defensive needs, particularly pass rusher and cornerback, though it may also add receivers or offensive linemen to support new starting quarterback Patrick Mahomes II. Local prospects Dorance Armstrong and D.J. Reed could be options.

Recent Chiefs drafts produced Pro Bowl players Marcus Peters, Tyreek Hill and Kareem Hunt, along with Mahomes and Chris Jones. Defensive selections KeiVarae Russell and Tanoh Kpassagnon have been less successful, while late-round picks Hunt and Hill became major contributors.

The Nobel Prizes, established by Alfred Nobel and first awarded in 1901, became science’s most prominent honors by recognizing major discoveries regardless of nationality. Their narrow categories and three-person limit, however, exclude many scientific fields and contributors to collaborative work.

Prize recipients disproportionately are white men from wealthy regions with strong research funding. Women and people of color face barriers to accessing prestigious institutions and leading laboratories, while prizes often recognize lab heads rather than other major contributors. Selection can take decades and involves worldwide nominations and committee review intended to reduce bias, but the Nobel Foundation remains constrained by Nobel’s will.

Despite these limitations, scientists argue that the prizes demonstrate science’s impact, encourage public interest and give winners a platform to discuss their research.

North Carolina regulators are considering testing backyard vegetables near Chemours’ Fayetteville plant for GenX and related chemicals after a Dutch study found such compounds in about 40% of food samples near another Chemours factory. Officials have not decided whether or how to conduct testing, which could later expand to commercial agriculture. Fish-testing results near both plants are expected within months. GenX replaced PFOA in 2009 and has shown toxic effects in animals, but its human effects remain unknown and no federal health standards exist. Nearby residents have raised concerns about contaminated wells, plants, fish and venison. GenX was also detected in treated drinking water serving about 200,000 people in Wilmington, downstream from the Fayetteville plant.

The TPS7H500x-SP radiation-hardness-assured PWM controllers use fixed-frequency peak-current-mode control for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. Output voltage is programmed through a VSENSE resistor divider referenced to 0.613 V; 1%-or-better resistors are recommended. An SS capacitor controls gradual startup, with synchronous rectifier outputs enabled after SS exceeds 1 V.

Switching frequency can be set from 100 kHz to 2 MHz using an RT resistor, synchronized to a 200-kHz-to-4-MHz external clock applied at twice the desired switching frequency, or shared between primary and secondary controllers. Primary-secondary operation supports synchronized independent converters or parallel interleaved phases, with a 90° or 270° phase shift between corresponding outputs.

Depending on the device, controllers provide OUTA, OUTB, SRA, and SRB outputs with approximately 150-mA peak capability; external gate drivers are recommended. Dead time and leading-edge blanking are fixed or resistor-programmable by device. Pulse skipping addresses minimum-on-time limitations and occurs when COMP is below 0.3 V and the previous duty cycle was below 25%. Configurable maximum duty cycles include 50%, 75%, and 100%, subject to device support.

CS_ILIM provides PWM current sensing and overcurrent protection, with a nominal 1.05-V threshold. Sustained overcurrent invokes cycle-by-cycle limiting and capacitor-controlled hiccup shutdown and restart. FAULT permits external protection functions, while thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C and restarts below 160°C. Programmable slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation, and Type 2A or Type 2B compensation can stabilize the control loop.

A TPS7H5001-SP synchronous push-pull GaN design example uses 500-kHz switching, 5-V output, 25-ns dead time, approximately 50-ns blanking, 7.5-ms soft start, a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 0.47-µH output inductance, and about 2.3 mF output capacitance. It sets overcurrent near 35 A and uses Type 2A compensation with a 10-kHz crossover target.

The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V. Layout guidance emphasizes short high-current paths, minimized switch-node area, separation of analog and power grounds, careful routing of feedback and sensitive signals, close placement of bypass and compensation components, and adequate filtering of current-sense signals.

NFL kickers are pressure-tested specialists responsible for extra points, field goals, kickoffs, onside kicks, and occasionally replacing injured punters. Extra points are worth one point, field goals three, and NFL kickers are generally expected to make about 90% and 80% of these attempts, respectively. Their accuracy can determine close games and influence coaches’ fourth-down decisions.

Kickoffs require power and directional accuracy to produce touchbacks, avoid dangerous returners, and support coverage. Onside kicks demand touch, accuracy, and luck to create recovery opportunities. Placekickers typically have slim builds, lower-body strength, flexibility, consistent technique, and accuracy.

Notable kickers include Justin Tucker, identified as the most accurate ever and holder of the 66-yard field-goal record; Hall of Famer Morten Andersen, who made 565 career field goals; and Adam Vinatieri, the NFL’s all-time leading scorer with 2,673 points and record holder for 44 consecutive field goals. Reliable kickers reduce pressure on offenses and defenses, improve special-teams performance, and can decide wins or losses.

VentureWire’s May 31, 2001 edition reports major venture funds and financing activity. Insight Capital Partners closed a $740 million software-focused fund; Rho Ventures closed a $435 million fund; and MMC Capital announced a $250 million technology fund. Whitney & Co. plans to spin off its Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London offices after its fifth fund closed below target.

Quake Technologies raised $30 million for optical-networking chips. Other financings included $30 million for Neurotech, $21 million for OmniSonics Medical, $4.5 million for Arexis, $4.2 million for Atherotech, $3.2 million for Remedyne, $3 million for SpeedGreetings, and $1.7 million for Tools for Health. Toppan Printing invested $5 million in E Ink, while Fractus secured a commitment of up to $4.3 million from 3i.

PaperExchange closed its physical European operations. Softbank and Scientia Health Group formed Scientia Japan, Eqvitec Partners and IT Provider established an alliance, and Incyte and Iconix agreed to develop a chemogenomic information product.

Acquisition activity included Bertelsmann’s purchase of MyPlay, TMP Worldwide’s acquisition of FlipDog.com, BuildOnline’s purchase of iScraper Germany, Metavante’s acquisition of CyberBills, and Outtask’s acquisition of Upright Software. UsherPro and Season Ticket Networks merged to form Season Ticket Solutions.

Cervalis launched managed hosting services, while Data Downlink renamed itself Alacra. Several companies announced new directors and executives, including Enanta Pharmaceuticals, Polexis, and Ardent Pharmaceuticals. Royal Bank Capital Partners added two professionals to its $100 million Energy Fund team.

Backtests on SPY, GLD, and TLT examined trades entered after two consecutive daily bars with higher highs and higher lows and exited after 1–10 bars. The pattern produced weak short-term returns: SPY and GLD gains were below comparable random periods, while TLT had negative short-term returns and average two-week performance. Using three or four consecutive days did not improve results. The pattern appears to indicate short-term reversal but is insufficient as a standalone long or short trading signal.

The patent disclosure describes deep learning systems for splice-site classification and aberrant-splicing detection in genomic sequences. Convolutional and atrous convolutional neural networks classify nucleotides as donor sites, acceptor sites, or non-splicing sites using surrounding sequence context. Atrous convolutions provide large receptive fields with relatively few parameters and capture long-range dependencies; implementations also use residual blocks, skip connections, batch normalization, ReLU layers, one-hot encoding, pooling, and dimensionality-altering convolutions.

SpliceNet variants process contexts ranging from 40 to 5,000 nucleotides on each side, with non-exponentially changing dilation rates and varying convolution-window sizes. Models are trained on labeled donor, acceptor, and non-splicing examples and output normalized triplet scores for each target nucleotide.

For aberrant-splicing detection, reference and variant sequences are processed separately, and position-wise differences in splice-site scores are compared with a selected threshold. Variants exceeding the threshold are classified as causing aberrant splicing and therefore pathogenic; those below it may be classified as benign. The disclosure includes system, method, server-deployment, and computer-readable-medium implementations, along with background on neural-network training and incorporated patent applications and technical references.

Twelve contestants remain in “Dancing with the Stars” Season 34 after Corey Feldman and Jenna Johnson, and Baron Davis and Britt Stewart, were eliminated during Week 2. Gymnast Jordan Chiles is the only athlete left entering Episode 3’s “TikTok Night.” Results combine judges’ scores and public-vote percentages equally. Viewers may cast up to 10 votes per couple through each voting method during the live Eastern and Central time-zone broadcast.

The coach said the team is focused on its own preparation rather than analyzing an injured opponent. Players are relaxed, enjoying the moment and ready for another elimination game, with the goal of producing their best performance of the series. After a six-hour flight, practice was limited to loosening up rather than systems work. An injured teammate remains an important part of the group; his equipment and sweater were brought to honor his contributions and desire to play. The coach praised veteran leadership and its impact on younger players, while emphasizing that coaches and management have fostered a committed but positive atmosphere. The team has identified what it must improve from its previous game and plans to make those adjustments.

High-κ dielectrics require both high permittivity and wide band gaps, but machine-learning predictions of ionic dielectric contributions have been less accurate than electronic contributions. The study developed a joint model that separately predicts Born effective charge tensors using an E(3)-equivariant graph neural network and phonon force constants using a pretrained machine-learning potential, then analytically combines them to calculate ionic dielectric tensors.

Trained on first-principles data for 928 oxides, the Born effective charge model achieved an average R² of 0.982. SevenNet provided the most accurate force constants among four tested potentials. The resulting joint model predicted ionic dielectric tensors with R² of 0.843 and RMSE of 0.129, substantially outperforming a direct model with R² of 0.418 and RMSE of 0.260.

The framework screened 8,717 nonmagnetic, nonmetallic oxides from the Materials Project. After filtering for dynamical stability, predicted dielectric properties, band gaps, and first-principles validation, 38 previously unknown high-κ candidates met the final figure-of-merit threshold. Twelve exceeded KTaO₃, the best-performing oxide in the training set. Ionic contributions accounted for more than 90% of total permittivity in all qualifying training and screened oxides. Ten identified candidates had previously been synthesized, and reported dielectric constants for five agreed with predictions. Most candidates contained empty-d-shell transition metals and flexible oxygen-octahedral frameworks. The authors propose extending the method to non-oxides and finite-temperature calculations.

University of Edinburgh researchers identified 287 genetic signals linked to male pattern baldness by studying DNA from more than 52,000 mostly middle-aged men in the British BioBank. Forty signals were on the X chromosome, inherited by men from their mothers, while others were distributed across the genome. Genetic patterns were only somewhat predictive of hair loss severity, and researchers said accurate individual forecasts remain distant. However, the findings may improve understanding of hair loss, identify those at greatest risk, and reveal potential targets for intervention. Male pattern baldness affects about 80 percent of men by age 80.

The speaker credits strong team defense for two successful games and shutouts, emphasizing focus over personal achievements. A key late-second-period save preserved momentum. Despite the series lead, the games remain close, and the team expects a major challenge in Anaheim, where the opponents will be eager to rebound and apply pressure.

U.S. mortgage applications fell 0.8% in the week ended March 24, declining for a second week despite lower borrowing costs. The average 30-year conforming mortgage rate dropped to 4.33% from 4.46% as Treasury yields declined. Refinancing applications fell 2.9%, and their share reached the lowest level since October 2008. Purchase applications rose 1.2%, while the share of adjustable-rate mortgage applications declined to 8.5%.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the 7nm Ampere GA100 architecture, for AI, HPC, and data analytics. A100 contains 108 streaming multiprocessors, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, and a 40 MB L2 cache. Its Tensor Cores support TF32, FP16, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary formats. Compared with V100, A100 provides higher throughput, including 2.5× FP16 mixed-precision and FP64 performance, while 2:4 structured sparsity can double Tensor Core throughput.

Multi-Instance GPU technology partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU instances with dedicated compute and memory resources, predictable quality of service, and fault containment. Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4 offers 31.5 GB/s per direction for x16 connections. A100 also supports Magnum IO, Mellanox InfiniBand and Ethernet, SR-IOV, enhanced error handling, hardware JPEG and video decoding, optical-flow acceleration, and improved atomic operations.

CUDA 11 exposes Ampere features including task graphs, asynchronous global-to-shared-memory copies, asynchronous barriers, L2 cache residency controls, and cooperative-group reductions. These features reduce launch overhead, memory traffic, latency, register use, and software complexity.

The DGX A100 system combines eight A100 GPUs through NVLink and NVSwitch, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, 4.8 TB/s total bidirectional GPU interconnect bandwidth, and up to 56 isolated accelerators through MIG. It supports NVIDIA’s software stack, NGC, Kubernetes, Slurm, DeepOps, and large-scale expansion through Mellanox networking and Magnum IO.

Retired civil litigator Marcel Strigberger humorously recounts decluttering law books purchased more than 50 years ago. He revisits memorable contract, property and damages cases before recycling most volumes, later regretting that one property book could be worth over $1,000. He kept one five-inch-thick book because it serves as a useful reading stand when working at his desk.

Federal, state, and nonprofit grants have strengthened Mercy University’s School of Education through mentoring, curriculum innovation, professional learning, career preparation, and partnerships serving diverse PK–12 communities.

The five-year, $2.8 million GRAD-PRO grant expands graduate opportunities for Hispanic and other underserved students in health sciences, education, and business. It supports scholarships, experiential learning, stackable credentials, faculty mentoring, retention, and career alignment. Activities include mental-health programming for educators and a Faculty Mentoring Fellowship focused on inclusive, evidence-based mentorship.

A three-year BranchED grant is transforming teacher preparation through district partnerships, curriculum review, data-informed instruction, coaching, and customized professional development. In partnership with the Public Schools of the Tarrytowns, Mercy exceeded first-year expectations by completing all required outcomes. Its final phase emphasizes sustaining collaborative practices and educational equity.

The National Science Foundation-funded MISTI program prepares mathematics and science teachers for high-need schools. Scholars receive coursework, school observations, social justice seminars, yearlong student teaching, certification support, faculty mentoring, and continued coaching during their early teaching careers. Research indicates that intensive mentoring, cohort support, and long-term assistance promote teacher retention in high-need schools.

The six-year STEM Master Teaching Fellowship supported 14 PK–12 teachers from four high-need districts in becoming STEM leaders. Fellows completed graduate coursework and led projects including enrichment programs, community gardens, and professional development for colleagues. The initiative also strengthened faculty expertise and produced publications and conference presentations.

A five-year, $687,500 New York State grant supports an advanced ESOL certificate addressing New York City’s shortage of teachers for multilingual learners. Candidates receive clinically integrated coursework, mentoring, classroom observations, professional development, and post-completion support.

Together, these grants have enhanced teacher preparation, faculty development, school partnerships, educational equity, and support for educators serving diverse students.

Education Minister Mailis Reps authorized state-run upper secondary schools in Viimsi and Rapla, opening leadership recruitment ahead of their September launch. Both construction projects have completed architectural competitions and entered detailed planning.

A CORAF report found that the three-year SRI-WAAPP project increased rice yields and farmer incomes across 13 West African countries. Involving more than 50,000 farmers at over 1,000 sites, the project promoted the System of Rice Intensification, an adaptable approach designed to reduce inputs while raising production. An independent five-country evaluation reported yield increases of 54 percent in irrigated systems, 65 percent in rainfed lowlands, and 153 percent in rainfed uplands, alongside a 41 percent average income increase. During 2015–2016, project sites produced over 20,000 additional tons of milled rice, valued at about US$10 million.

The report argues that wider adoption could advance regional rice self-sufficiency, but practices must be adapted to local environmental and socioeconomic conditions. SRI’s labor effects vary, and concerns were raised about potential burdens on women and impacts on landless laborers. The project introduced labor-saving weeding technology and used regional collaboration among farmers, researchers, and extension staff to accelerate innovation, adaptation, and adoption.
The passage contrasts machine translation’s practical value with its lack of language understanding, questioning whether high-quality translation can rely solely on decoding.

Sanergy, founded by three MIT Sloan students, addresses poor sanitation in Nairobi’s slums through an integrated model covering waste collection, treatment, and reuse. Its nonprofit Fresh Life arm franchises hygienic toilets to entrepreneurs, landlords, and schools, while Sanergy crews collect waste daily. The waste is processed into Evergrow organic fertilizer, sold by the for-profit Farm Star brand.

By 2015, Fresh Life operated 615 toilets serving about 32,000 people, with ambitious expansion targets. Farm Star sold 118 tons of fertilizer and also planned substantial growth. Achieving these goals required stronger sales, marketing, fundraising, and stakeholder engagement.

Communications manager Medora Brown was tasked with developing a social media strategy despite limited funds, staff, and uncertainty about return on investment. Kenya’s expanding technology sector, Internet access, mobile-phone ownership, and social media use offered opportunities, but adoption differed substantially among Sanergy’s audiences. Farmers were increasingly active on Facebook and WhatsApp, while slum residents and Fresh Life franchisees used social media infrequently because of limited access and cost.

Fresh Life relied primarily on personal contact, events, referrals, SMS, and door-to-door promotion because trust and behavior change were essential to recruiting franchisees and customers. Farm Star saw greater social media potential: Facebook advertising generated several dozen relatively inexpensive leads, while WhatsApp and SMS-based learning supported consultative selling and farmer engagement. However, sales conversions remained unknown.

Sanergy’s corporate communications focused on attracting foundations, major donors, and investors through its blog, email, speaking engagements, personal networks, and media coverage. Advisors encouraged a broader thought-leadership program, though company leaders doubted social media could secure large donations.

Brown needed to determine suitable platforms and content for each brand, adapt blog material efficiently, establish performance metrics, and assess whether social media could build the trust needed among customers, farmers, franchisees, investors, and donors.

Five days after Stephen Paddock killed 58 people and wounded hundreds at a Las Vegas music festival, investigators said they still lacked a motive despite pursuing 1,000 leads. The FBI planned billboards requesting public information.

Authorities examined Paddock’s politics, finances, mental health, medications, social behavior, possible radicalization, cruises, contact with prostitutes and a cryptic note. Investigators found no evidence of an accomplice but sought anyone who knew of the plot beforehand. His girlfriend, Marilou Danley, said she noticed no signs of violence and knew nothing of his plans.

Authorities said Paddock meticulously prepared, obtaining an upper-floor hotel suite overlooking the festival, stockpiling 23 guns and installing surveillance cameras. He had also booked rooms overlooking music festivals in Chicago and Las Vegas. His arsenal included 1,000 tracer rounds, though it was unclear whether he used them during the attack.

This systematic literature review examined trends in robotic coding research in science education from 2015–2022. Searches of WOS and Scopus initially identified 74 studies; after applying criteria for relevance, language, publication type, empirical design, and quality, 15 peer-reviewed articles were analyzed using content analysis and expert review.

The studies primarily addressed cognitive skills, especially 21st-century abilities such as communication, problem-solving, scientific creativity, and cognitive processing, alongside computational, algorithmic, and mathematical thinking. Research also examined integrating robotic coding into science and engineering using tools such as Arduino and tablets. Affective outcomes focused on students’ interest, motivation, and opinions.

Common recommendations included integrating robotic coding across STEM subjects, educational settings, teacher training, and different learning levels; studying varied coding programs and teaching methods; and conducting larger, deeper studies using diverse data-collection tools and considering gender. Future research should also investigate underexamined 21st-century skills, psychomotor and affective characteristics, curriculum development, code literacy, and additional tools such as Scratch, Alice, MIT App Inventor, and Microsoft Small Basic. In-service robotic coding training for teachers is recommended.

The review was limited to 15 full-text articles indexed in WOS and Scopus and published between 2015 and 2022. Future reviews could examine other fields, periods, databases, or use meta-synthesis and meta-analysis.

System Management Arts sought revision under Federal Rule 54(b) of an earlier decision denying partial summary judgment on whether Avesta’s “Delphi” software constituted prior art invalidating Smarts’ patents. Smarts relied on newly discovered evidence that corroborating witness Igor Klener had invested in Avesta, anticipated its IPO, and had friendships with Avesta executives, allegedly making him biased. Klener denied receiving any reward for his declaration and stated that the investment invitation preceded his knowledge of the lawsuit.

The court held that the motion was timely and procedurally proper under Rule 54(b), but denied it on the merits. Patent invalidity must be established by clear and convincing evidence, and testimony concerning prior use generally requires corroboration. Under the applicable “rule of reason,” however, an interested corroborating witness’s testimony is not automatically inadequate. Bias, relationships, elapsed time, and competing interpretations of the evidence affect credibility and evidentiary weight, which are matters for the jury. Because the new evidence did not eliminate genuine factual disputes regarding Delphi’s status as prior art, revision of the prior decision was unwarranted.

Following the Charlottesville protests, the Twitter account @YesYoureRacist asked users to identify participants photographed at the rally, which featured racist and white nationalist messages. The account grew to 271,000 followers and was described as “naming and shaming” attendees through social media.

Its followers identified several participants, including Cole White, whose employer, Top Dog in Berkeley, announced that he no longer worked there and rejected the actions in Charlottesville. The account also identified Peter Cvjetanovic, who defended promoting “White, European culture” but objected to being labeled “angry torch guy,” and James Allsup, a Washington State University student whose posts encouraged others to attend the rally. Followers subsequently contacted the university president about Allsup. The account also received media credit for identifying men in widely circulated photographs and finding an image of the driver who killed a protester.

The City and State appealed confirmation of 1515 Broadway’s consummated Chapter 11 reorganization plan, challenging tax exemptions for partnership restructuring, a possible future foreclosure or sale, and the purchase of leased land. The court held that failure to obtain a stay does not automatically moot an appeal; each claim depends on whether effective relief remains possible without disrupting the reorganization. The City’s challenge to the partnership restructuring was moot because that transaction was integral to the completed plan and could not be altered without affecting the settlement. However, the challenge concerning a future sale or foreclosure was not moot because the transaction and distribution of proceeds had not occurred. The State’s Gains Tax claims were also not moot because controlling Second Circuit law changed after confirmation, and tax liability for the land purchase had not been considered. The motion to dismiss was therefore denied, subject to these limitations.

Software engineering supports systematic, efficient software development and maintenance. Requirements engineering defines system services and constraints, distinguishing functional requirements, which specify actions the software must perform, from non-functional requirements (NFRs), which describe qualities such as usability, security, speed, reliability, and maintainability.

The study proposes extracting potential NFRs by clustering semantically similar words from functional requirements. It evaluates semantic similarity measures and clustering techniques, using Normalized Google Distance, average-linkage clustering, text semantic similarity, and an NFR traceability matrix. A post-pruned decision tree classifier categorizes instances according to feature values.

Using an IVR dataset, the method classifies null and non-null functions by combining an NFR matrix with a decision tree. Compared with an existing method using only the NFR matrix, the proposed approach reportedly achieves higher accuracy and lower execution time in Python testing. The study concludes that null functions reduce project efficiency and that combining the NFR matrix with decision-tree classification improves their identification.

Smoky River FCSS seeks parents with babies aged 2–4 months in October for the 2017–2018 Roots of Empathy school program. Classroom baby visits teach children to understand feelings, encourage positive social behavior, and reduce aggression. Contact Crystal at 780-837-2220 or youthsrfcss@live.com.

At a Lodhran school ceremony, PML-N leader Rana Muhammad Tariq Khan urged civil-society support for government-school students and pledged a water pump, furniture and co-curricular assistance. An education official highlighted free education, infrastructure and stipends.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture introduces hybrid rendering that combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation. Dedicated RT Cores accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, while denoising reduces required rays. Turing can exceed 10 Giga Rays per second, approximately ten times Pascal’s software ray-tracing performance, enabling real-time shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections.

The NGX neural graphics stack uses Turing Tensor Cores for AI-based graphics features. DLSS produces image quality similar to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work, while DLSS 2X approaches 64-times supersampled quality. Other NGX functions include content-aware inpainting, interpolated slow motion, and image or video super-resolution.

Additional Turing features include Mesh Shading to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks; Variable Rate Shading for content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering; Texture Space Shading to decouple and reuse visibility and shading computations; and Multi-View Rendering for efficiently producing multiple viewpoints in one pass. These technologies improve performance in complex scenes, VR, stereo rendering, and shading workloads.

TU104 includes up to 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, while TU106 includes 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores. Products based on these chips include the GeForce RTX 2080, RTX 2070, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. Turing also supports VirtualLink, enhanced VR audio, expanded resource binding, and a workload-based RTX-OPS metric combining Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 utilization.

Studies link excessive social media use to poorer emotional well-being. Passive Facebook “lurking” may foster envy, unrealistic comparisons, and mood deterioration, while teens using social media over two hours daily face a higher chance of mental illness. However, platforms can provide access to mental health services. Researchers recommend limiting use and prioritizing active connection over passive browsing.

Markets shifted decisively risk-off after a week of earnings, economic data, Fed policy, tariffs, and political developments. Major indexes fell 2.2%–4.2% from record highs, forming bearish engulfing patterns as volume, market internals, transports, retail, and most sectors weakened.

Second-quarter earnings remained strong: 82% of reporting S&P 500 companies beat earnings estimates and 79% exceeded revenue estimates, while upward earnings revisions increased. However, investors sold into positive results amid doubts about continued growth and limited new buying.

GDP grew 3%, above the 2.5% expectation, but tariff-driven import volatility distorted the figure, while weak personal spending indicated softer demand. Payrolls rose by 73,000 versus 100,000 expected, with unusually large downward revisions to prior months. Unemployment edged to 4.2% as the labor force contracted.

The Fed maintained a patient, data-dependent approach amid inflation, tariff, and labor-force uncertainty, despite two dissenting votes. Markets placed the probability of a September rate cut above 75% and anticipated three cuts by January. Bond prices strengthened, reflecting expectations of lower rates and economic slowing.

President Trump dismissed the Bureau of Labor Statistics commissioner, announced nuclear submarine deployments following Russian comments, advanced tariff actions, and gained another potential Fed appointment after Governor Adriana Kugler’s resignation. The outlook remained longer-term positive but short-to-intermediate-term risk-off.

Benchmarks shape language-model development, but structural issues such as redundancy and uneven data distributions can distort aggregate scores. The authors introduce HARMONY, an entropy-based metric for assessing benchmark reliability by measuring how uniformly model performance is distributed across semantic subdomains.

The evaluation pipeline partitions benchmark data into semantic clusters, measures model performance within each cluster, and computes HARMONY for each benchmark-model pair. High HARMONY indicates that aggregate accuracy reflects broad, consistent competence, while low HARMONY suggests that dominant subdomains or performance disparities obscure model strengths and weaknesses. The authors recommend reporting HARMONY alongside accuracy.

Formally, a benchmark is partitioned into disjoint semantic subsets using a similarity function. Each subset receives a size weight, and model performance is compared with the weighted mean through smooth proximity scores. The study maps 19 multiple-choice question-answering benchmarks across five model families in a HARMONY mean-variance plane to characterize benchmark reliability.

The study developed a semi-empirical Bayesian shrinkage method to improve sex-specific Mendelian randomization analyses when one sex has a substantially smaller genome-wide association study sample. Motivated by the Million Veteran Program, where about 10% of participants are female, the method adaptively borrows information between male and female groups while accounting for observed differences in genetic variant effects. Its adaptive posterior mean estimator is used to calibrate variant-exposure effect estimates before applying existing two-sample Mendelian randomization methods.

Simulations modeled female and male exposure samples of 2,000 and 20,000 individuals, respectively, and balanced outcome samples. Adaptive shrinkage generally reduced mean squared error in female-specific causal estimates, including when variant effects differed by sex or female instruments were weak. Fixed-effects meta-analysis performed best when genetic effects were similar across sexes but performed poorly under substantial differences. MR-RAPS generally performed at least as well as the other evaluated methods and controlled Type I error near nominal levels in most settings. Larger female samples reduced the benefit of borrowing information, but shrinkage did not reduce estimation efficiency.

The method was applied to Million Veteran Program genome-wide association results for obstructive sleep apnea, insomnia, short sleep, long sleep, and daytime sleepiness, and All of Us data for cardiovascular-related outcomes. Using raw sex-specific instrument selection, significant associations included insomnia with chronic kidney disease and long sleep with hypertension in females, and short sleep with coronary artery disease in males. Adaptive instrument selection additionally identified associations of obstructive sleep apnea with type 2 diabetes and hypertension in females, and with chronic kidney disease and heart failure in males. A significant sex difference was found for obstructive sleep apnea’s effect on chronic kidney disease, with a stronger effect in males. Long sleep showed higher risks of several cardiovascular-related outcomes in females but protective associations in males. These sex-difference results were nominally significant, but none of the reported false-discovery-rate-adjusted values was below 0.05.

Limitations included unavailable independent sex-specific sleep datasets for instrument selection, sensitivity to instrument-selection strategy, difficulty accounting for correlation between shrinkage-based male and female causal estimates, and restriction to individuals of European ancestry.

Patient advocacy groups asked the U.K. antitrust regulator to investigate major drugmakers and their lobbying organization for suspected coordinated efforts to raise medicine prices. The complaint follows a dispute over mandatory NHS rebates, which increased from 10% to 23%. AstraZeneca, Merck, and Eli Lilly subsequently halted or canceled research and manufacturing investments totaling $2.6 billion.

The work introduces and experimentally demonstrates a dynamically controllable dark-fringe x-ray interferometer for Mössbauer science. Unlike conventional crystal interferometers requiring Angstrom-level stability, it uses two co-propagating, polarization-distinguished pathways through two ^57Fe-enriched α-iron targets inside a crossed polarimetry setup.

The targets’ magnetizations are oriented at opposite angles, producing destructive interference and ideally zero transmission for identical targets. Multiple-scattering pathways and radiative coupling between the targets cancel, leaving only two single-scattering pathways associated with polarization-changing scattering in either target. Their distinct intermediate polarizations allow individual addressing and potential study of polarization-dependent phase shifts.

A piezoelectric transducer displaces one target, imposing a phase shift determined by displacement relative to the x-ray wavelength. This enables continuous, dynamic control of the relative phase and transmitted intensity. Event-based detection measured responses to sudden displacements for about 7.5 μs, roughly 50 nuclear lifetimes. Demonstrated applications include nanosecond-scale control of transmitted x-ray intensity and measurement of relative target displacements on x-ray-wavelength and nanosecond scales by tracking mechanically induced wave propagation and reflection for more than 10 μs.

This electronic edition of the 1919 Paris Peace Conference volume in the Foreign Relations of the United States series preserves the printed content while providing search, bookmarking, offline access, and media-neutral document citations. Its preface explains that the records were published during World War II to support planning for a just and stable postwar order by examining the Paris settlement of 1919 and avoiding its pitfalls. The volume addresses a gap in the Foreign Relations series by presenting official American conference records, supplementing an extensive but incomplete body of memoirs, document collections, histories, and bibliographies.

Computing evolved from purpose-built machines to programmable, time-sharing, networked client-server systems and, by the early 2000s, large-scale distributed systems. Properly structured distributed systems offer greater reliability, scalability, and organizational benefits but are harder to design, build, and debug. Growing demand has increased the need for specialized tools and practices, with containers, images, orchestration, reusable patterns, and components providing a foundation for reliable systems.

Penn Medicine researchers found that a single psilocybin dose reduced pain, anxiety, and depression-like behaviors for nearly two weeks in mice with chronic pain. Psilocybin activated serotonin receptors and affected the anterior cingulate cortex, which processes pain and emotions; spinal cord injections did not produce similar effects. The findings suggest potential for non-addictive, non-opioid therapies, but safety, effectiveness, dosing, and long-term benefits require further study.

The Regional Theatrical Youth Camp runs June 19–30, 2017, offering two age divisions for participants ages 5–18. Level II includes 50 training hours and a role in “Bye, Bye Birdie, Jr.” Public performances are scheduled after camp, including a second show July 2. Registration information is available at (931) 628-8277.

The President urges bipartisan cooperation to sustain prosperity, preserve peace, invest in America’s future, and substantially reduce the federal deficit without raising taxes. His budget would use increased revenues from economic growth to fund priorities while cutting the deficit by nearly 40 percent. He proposes two-year budgets, a presidential line-item veto, required congressional votes on rescissions, and a balanced-budget amendment.

His agenda emphasizes low taxes, economic growth, individual choice, opposition to discrimination, support for families and faith, and private-sector solutions where effective. Proposed investments include increased funding for scientific research, NASA and space exploration; a permanent research-and-development tax credit; lower capital-gains taxes; urban enterprise zones; and education reforms rewarding excellent schools and teachers, promoting science and mathematics, expanding magnet schools, and encouraging alternative teacher certification.

He requests increased funding for drug enforcement, treatment, prevention, border security, prosecution, and prisons, alongside $1.6 billion for AIDS education and research. Environmental proposals include stronger clean-air legislation, acid-rain reductions, clean-coal funding, conservation, penalties for ocean dumping, delayed offshore lease sales pending environmental review, and tougher toxic-waste enforcement.

Social priorities include expanded Medicaid coverage for pregnant women near poverty, targeted child-care tax credits, adoption incentives, full Social Security funding, and greater assistance for homeless people. He also supports a Puerto Rican referendum, urgent savings-and-loan reform protecting insured depositors, and expanded cleanup of nuclear weapons facilities.

On defense, he proposes a one-year real spending freeze tied to a comprehensive deficit agreement, followed by increases above inflation, while reviewing strategy and reforming Pentagon procurement. Internationally, he advocates cautious engagement with the Soviet Union, continued military strength, the Strategic Defense Initiative, bans on chemical weapons, nuclear nonproliferation, democracy in Central America, strong alliances, freer trade, and cooperation with Europe and Pacific nations.

He concludes by calling for national service, educational involvement, inclusion of disabled Americans, support for farmers and service members, personal responsibility, perseverance, and congressional negotiation.

Baltimore County schools increasingly use television studios for student-produced announcements, class assignments and programs. At Lansdowne High School, students gain hands-on production experience by broadcasting daily announcements and creating a monthly variety show. About 100 of the county’s 161 schools have studios, roughly half with digital recording capabilities.

Officials and educators say studio work develops teamwork, communication, creativity, critical thinking and public-speaking skills while preparing students for growing demand for online video production. Studios can also provide artistic and technological outlets and serve as instructional tools beyond morning broadcasts.

Expansion depends on school-level funding because no central funding exists. Basic live-streaming equipment costs about $400, while complete digital studios can cost $15,000 to $18,000. Staff advisers now qualify for extra-duty compensation, though inadequate classroom projectors and speakers can limit access to live broadcasts. Hillcrest Elementary recently converted library storage into a student-operated studio, while Arbutus Middle established one with surplus equipment in an unused office.

The lecture develops renormalization group evolution for the weak Hamiltonian describing \(b\to c\bar u d\). Operator and Wilson-coefficient running are equivalent because their scale dependence must cancel, leaving the Hamiltonian independent of \(\mu\). In the \(+\!/\!-\) basis, the lowest-order equations decouple. Changing integration variables from \(\mu\) to \(\alpha_s\) using the beta function yields solutions involving ratios of couplings at different scales raised to anomalous-dimension-dependent powers.

Matching at a scale \(\mu_W\sim M_W\) supplies boundary conditions, while evolution to \(\mu_b\sim M_b\) sums leading logarithms of \(M_W/M_b\). This separates high-scale physics into Wilson coefficients and low-scale physics into operator matrix elements. Renormalization group improvement can generate a significant coefficient for an operator whose tree-level matching coefficient vanishes. For processes such as \(B\to D\pi\), using coefficients and operators at the \(b\)-quark scale avoids large logarithms in low-energy matrix elements.

At leading-logarithmic order, tree-level matching and one-loop anomalous dimensions are required. Next-to-leading-logarithmic accuracy requires one-loop matching and two-loop anomalous dimensions; generally, running must be computed one perturbative order higher than matching.

One-loop matching is obtained by subtracting renormalized effective-theory amplitudes from full Standard Model amplitudes. Their infrared dependence must agree, confirming that the effective theory contains the correct low-energy degrees of freedom. The difference isolates short-distance contributions to Wilson coefficients. Effective-theory calculations simplify multiscale problems and use renormalization group equations to infer logarithmic terms that would require higher-loop full-theory calculations.

Beyond leading order, matching coefficients, anomalous dimensions, Wilson coefficients, and operator matrix elements depend on the renormalization scheme, although physical products such as \(C(\mu)O(\mu)\) are scheme independent. Consistent use of one scheme is therefore essential. Higher-order dimensional-regularization calculations also require careful treatment of \(\gamma_5\) and evanescent operators, which vanish in four dimensions but are needed in \(d\)-dimensional operator bases.

Amazon.com filed a Form 8-K reporting its third-quarter 2015 financial results on October 22, 2015. The filing includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. Chief Financial Officer Brian T. Olsavsky signed the report.

Columbia researchers developed a silicon photonics chip that converts one powerful multimode laser into a frequency comb with dozens of stable, evenly spaced light channels. A locking mechanism cleans the laser’s noisy output, after which the chip’s nonlinear optical properties split it into multiple wavelengths. Each wavelength can carry a separate data stream through the same fiber, potentially replacing racks of individual lasers in data centers while reducing cost, space, and energy use. The compact, high-power source could also support LiDAR, sensing, optical clocks, spectrometers, and quantum devices.

Uber board member David Bonderman resigned after joking that more women on the board would mean more talking, calling his remark “careless, inappropriate and inexcusable.” The comment came during a meeting about an investigation into Uber’s workplace culture. His departure followed CEO Travis Kalanick’s leave of absence, executive Emil Michael’s resignation and the firing of 20 employees after a separate harassment investigation.

Paul Tudor Jones said current markets resemble late 1999, citing technology rallies, speculation and AI financing deals. Unlike then, current easing monetary policy and a 6% budget deficit could fuel a more explosive surge before a painful correction. He believes the bull market has room to run and favors gold, cryptocurrencies and Nasdaq technology stocks through year-end.

Hereditary angioedema (HAE) causes recurrent swelling and is commonly linked to SERPING1 mutations causing C1 inhibitor deficiency or dysfunction. Delayed or incorrect diagnosis is frequent and can lead to unnecessary procedures, increased burden, and potentially fatal laryngeal attacks. Because urine is noninvasively collected and may reflect systemic and local pathological changes, the study used urinary proteomics to investigate HAE and identify diagnostic biomarkers.

Distinct urinary protein profiles were found among type 1 HAE, type 2 HAE, and healthy controls. Enriched processes included complement and coagulation cascades, cell adhesion, immune response, proteolysis, and bradykinin catabolism. A panel comprising C1-INH, KNG1, and EGF was identified as a promising noninvasive diagnostic tool.

The discovery cohort included 20 adults with HAE and 29 healthy controls; an independent validation cohort included 24 type 1 patients and 18 controls. First-morning urine samples underwent data-independent acquisition proteomics, bioinformatics analysis, and parallel reaction monitoring validation.

Diffusion Pharmaceuticals shares rose 6.56%, closing at $0.65. One analyst set a 12-month price target of $89.30. The company’s 14-period Average True Range was 0.12, with weekly volatility of 8.70% and monthly volatility of 10.55%. Its Relative Strength Index was 31.95, near the traditional oversold threshold of 30. Diffusion had a $9.8 million market capitalization and 15.07 million outstanding shares. Previous trading volume was 2.24 million shares, compared with a stated average of approximately 722.78 million.

A hard ferromagnetic sphere of radius roughly 24–30 µm was magnetically levitated in a cylindrically symmetric type-I superconducting lead trap at 4.2 K. Meissner repulsion passively confined its translational and polar rotational motion, while residual horizontal fields produced azimuthal libration. SQUID-based detection and synchronous feedback through driving coils accelerated the magnet from libration into continuous rotation and controlled its speed.

Free spin-down followed an exponential decay under viscous gas damping. The measured decay rate was approximately linear with helium pressure and agreed with the free-molecular gas-damping model after accounting for gauge sensitivity and thermomolecular gradients. This enabled pressure measurements on the cryogenic side of the chamber. The rotor operated as a pressure sensor from about \(10^{-3}\) to \(10^{-8}\) mbar. At the lowest effective pressure, the damping rate was \(4.75\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\), corresponding to a decay time of about 24 days and a quality factor of \(1.33\times10^{13}\).

The maximum demonstrated rotation frequency was 2.3 MHz, or 138 million rpm, for a magnet of approximately 30 µm radius. SQUID bandwidth limited further acceleration, while the estimated material-breaking limit was around 5.5 MHz. A weaker spectral peak was attributed to precession of the spinning axis; its frequency varied inversely with spin frequency, broadly matching the proposed image-field model.

The system requires no active translational stabilization and uses synchronous driving with relatively low heating, allowing cryogenic operation. Proposed applications include pressure sensing, gyroscopes, gravimetry, material studies, torque magnetometry, searches for ultralight dark matter, gravitational tests, and studies of rotational quantum effects.

Applied Materials presented a slide deck at Semicon West 2025. Seeking Alpha’s transcripts team published it as part of its expanding coverage. An accompanying chart spans October 3–8, 2025, with values from 210.99 to 226.321.
Everi seeks to refinance $335 million in notes and its term loan, forecasting Q1 revenue of $233–238 million, EBITDA of $52–54 million, and a $4–6 million loss.

Former NFL quarterback and Fox Sports analyst Mark Sanchez faces a Level 5 felony battery charge after an altercation with a 69-year-old truck driver in Indianapolis. Prosecutors upgraded the charge after learning the driver suffered serious injuries; Sanchez also faces three misdemeanors and potentially additional charges.

According to an affidavit, Sanchez confronted the driver at a hotel loading dock. The driver used pepper spray and then stabbed Sanchez, saying he feared for his life as Sanchez continued advancing. Sanchez suffered multiple torso wounds, while the driver sustained a facial laceration. Both were hospitalized, and Sanchez was stable Monday. His court hearing was rescheduled to Nov. 4.

NIST’s revised guidelines recommend long, simple, memorable passwords using phrases, lowercase letters and common words.
