The document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for interoperability between SEV-ES or SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors. These technologies encrypt guest register state, while the GHCB selectively exposes state needed to process Non-Automatic Exits (NAEs). The GHCB is a 4 KB decrypted page modeled partly on the SEV-ES VMCB save-state area. Protocol version 2 adds SEV-SNP support and a 52-bit hypervisor feature bitmap; later revisions add 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, VLEK certificates, APIC ID retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, page-state changes, SEV-TIO, and Secure AVIC.

The GHCB MSR protocol supports version negotiation, early CPUID access, encryption-bit discovery, AP reset hold, GHCB GPA registration and unregistration, page-state changes, VMPL switching, feature queries, and termination requests. SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB GPA before first use. During VMGEXIT, guests and hypervisors identify valid GHCB fields through a bitmap and may report malformed input, missing registration, invalid shared buffers, or unsupported requests.

Defined NAE operations include I/O, MSR and VMMCALL handling; MMIO access through decrypted buffers; private/shared page transitions; SNP guest and extended certificate requests; AP creation; restricted-injection doorbells, IPIs, and timers; APIC ID lists; VMPL switching; trusted-I/O requests; Secure AVIC backing pages; and termination. SNP firmware requests use shared request and response pages, support error reporting and rate limiting, and may return certificates, measurements, or attestation reports.

SMP booting requires alternatives to conventional register modification because measured encrypted vCPU state cannot be changed directly. Mechanisms include reset-hold protocols, AP jump tables, and SNP AP Creation using guest-provided VMSA pages. AP Creation can support vCPU hotplug, whereas traditional SEV-ES booting cannot. NMI handling uses an “NMI Complete” VMGEXIT message. Debug-register virtualization is supported when enabled by hardware; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and emulated. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

Restricted Injection limits the host to notifying guests through a shared #HV doorbell page. Its common fields describe pending interrupt vectors, NMI or machine-check events, suppression of further signals, and EOI assistance. Guests execute HLT with interrupts disabled and inspect doorbell state after resuming. The host must emulate APIC interrupt lifecycle behavior, present the highest-priority ready interrupt, signal #HV when required, track acknowledgments and in-service state, and determine whether an explicit EOI is necessary.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K dated June 26, 2020, announcing a strategic change in retail operations, including closure of Microsoft Store physical locations. The related press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1. Chief Accounting Officer Frank H. Brod signed the report.

Individual soccer defending requires quickly reaching the ball carrier after getting goal-side and adopting a balanced stance. Depending on teammates’ positioning, the defender either engages aggressively or stalls the attack until support arrives. Aggressive actions include intercepting passes, tackling as the opponent receives the ball, getting between opponent and ball, and preventing the opponent from turning toward goal.

To delay an attack, defenders should remain goal-side, maintain proper distance and balance, avoid overreacting to feints, block passes or shots, give ground carefully, restrict the dribbler’s vision, jockey them toward unfavorable areas, shepherd them toward the sideline, and steal poorly controlled balls. Near shooting range or the penalty area, defenders must stop retreating, hold their ground, and tackle when appropriate.

Because the on-ball defender is focused on the opponent, teammates must provide verbal guidance. Calls such as “contain,” “delay,” “jockey,” and “stand him up” instruct the defender to avoid tackling while the defense reorganizes. “Challenge,” “tackle,” and “take him” indicate that support has arrived and the defender may attempt to win the ball. If beaten, the defender must immediately chase and switch roles if a teammate confronts the dribbler.

Coaching should progressively teach positioning, stance, movement, all defensive techniques, field awareness, and communication, beginning slowly without a ball, then adding the ball and increasing speed. Beginning players require substantial individual instruction and competent demonstrations.

The lecture examines reverse logistics through ReCellular and Whirlpool. ReCellular collects, refurbishes, and resells used phones. Students debated whether demand from developing markets and late technology adopters could sustain the company despite rapid product evolution, declining margins, changing donation behavior, and dependence on one product category. Unlike specialized ReCellular, GENCO handles diverse products and partners primarily with retailers.

Whirlpool’s options under proposed extended producer responsibility regulations were to oppose regulation, join an industry-funded organization (IFO), or establish its own closed-loop system. Opposition was supported by existing appliance recycling rates of roughly 95%, though concerns included commodity-price changes and improper handling of mercury and refrigerants. An IFO could provide economies of scale and lower implementation risk, while a closed loop could strengthen customer loyalty, control costs, recover materials, and potentially make Whirlpool an industry leader.

Estimated IFO costs ranged from $24 million to $35 million. The lecture compared approximate reverse distribution costs of $80 per unit before scrap recovery, or $47 after recovery, with forward distribution costs of about $70 per unit. Reverse logistics costs more because collection networks are not optimized. A Whirlpool closed loop could use returning delivery trucks, but retailers would need incentives, tracking systems, packaging solutions, storage space, and additional handling capacity. Whirlpool ultimately pursued a closed-loop approach, although its initial implementation was more expensive than expected, with the possibility of later becoming an IFO.

The class concluded by discussing student projects comparing sustainability practices across companies and industries, including apparel, electronics, automobiles, and tobacco, with attention to business models, regulation, life-cycle impacts, operational improvements, and carbon offsets.

Average personal debt grew by £560 in early 2017, rising to about £930 for single parents with children. True Potential found 15% of people, and 20% of single parents, borrowed to cover household necessities. Average debt was £1,797, peaking among 45- to 54-year-olds and North East households. Couples without dependents borrowed least. Other causes included career changes, new jobs and parental leave. True Potential warned that easy credit and poor understanding of borrowing costs risk a debt crisis.

The speaker argues that age matters little in modern hockey, where knowledge, positioning, puck decisions, and sacrifice outweigh speed or individual skill. He is proud to have overcome doubts that a team could win in the playoffs with him, but emphasizes that team victory matters more than personal goals. Despite playoff soreness and injuries, he remained able to play. He expected to re-sign with Dallas, but delays and budget issues limited his options. After urging his agent to contact Detroit, he joined the team and feels extremely fortunate about the outcome.

Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease associated with systemic inflammation and comorbidities including depression, obesity, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and hypertriglyceridemia (HTG). This study examined whether depression, obesity, and HTG jointly influence their association with RA and whether these relationships vary by inflammatory status.

Researchers analyzed nationally representative 2007–2010 NHANES cross-sectional data because these cycles included C-reactive protein (CRP) measurements. Among 4,136 eligible adults aged 18–79, 305 self-reported RA. Depression was defined as a PHQ-9 score of at least 10, obesity as BMI of at least 30 kg/m², and HTG as serum triglycerides of at least 150 mg/dL. CRP levels were categorized as low, medium, or high.

RA was more prevalent among older adults, women, and lower-income participants. It was significantly associated with hypertension, stroke, HTG, depression, diabetes, and obesity. Participants with RA had higher PHQ-9 scores, BMI, triglycerides, and CRP levels than those without RA. RA prevalence increased progressively with CRP level.

Depression and obesity were individually associated with higher RA prevalence, whereas HTG alone was not. RA prevalence among participants with depression increased substantially when obesity or HTG coexisted. This synergistic association depended on CRP level and was strongest at medium CRP levels of 1–3 mg/L. Obesity intensified the depression–RA association across all CRP categories, while HTG’s effect was prominent mainly at medium CRP levels. Statistical tests supported these associations.

Because the data were cross-sectional, the study could identify associations but not causality or increased risk of developing RA. Other limitations included self-reported RA, insufficient participants with all three comorbidities, and CRP’s lack of specificity. The authors recommend longitudinal studies and measurement of broader inflammatory markers to clarify underlying mechanisms and suggest incorporating these comorbidity interactions into RA prediction models.

The disclosure describes methods for reducing wireless device power consumption by controlling uplink transmissions when a device uses enhanced coverage, which may require many repeated transmissions. Enhanced coverage may be identified through coverage levels, modes or classes, repetition counts, signal strength, or signal quality across technologies including LTE, NB-IoT, and EC-GSM-IoT.

Two solutions are presented. In the first, an application obtains radio-coverage information from a modem and decides whether to transmit, retain, or discard data. In the second, the application instructs the modem to conditionally transmit specific or future data. Information and instructions may be exchanged through AT commands or other APIs, including solicited queries and automatic notifications when coverage changes.

Transmission restrictions may depend on data type, QoS, priority, bit rate, elapsed time, attempt count, device movement or location, battery level, connection to external power, and combinations of these factors. Exceptions may permit emergency or critical data, transmission after a waiting period, reporting when a device becomes stationary, or sending data when battery power is very high or nearly exhausted.

Restriction parameters may be predefined by manufacturers, users, or standards, derived from network signaling, or configured by the network. Configuration can be carried in NAS, RRC, system-information, bearer-context, USIM toolkit, or device-management messages. The described mechanisms may apply to selected applications, ports, bearers, logical channels, traffic classes, or all uplink data.

The disclosure also describes corresponding network-node and user-equipment components. A similar approach may control mobile-terminated messages, with an application server using network-provided coverage information and related criteria to decide whether to forward data.

The paper investigates knowledge graph embeddings (KGEs) for ontology alignment, addressing their limited systematic use compared with large language model approaches. It formulates alignment as link prediction over a unified repository of source and target ontology triples, enabling joint learning of structural and semantic representations.

The proposed Graph Embedding Aligner is integrated into the modular OntoAligner Python library and consists of parser, encoder, and aligner stages. The parser extracts RDF-style metadata and class membership information. The encoder converts ontology triples from IRIs to natural-language text and merges them into a triple factory. The aligner uses PyKEEN to train KGE models with negative sampling, extracts normalized entity embeddings, and ranks source-target pairs using cosine similarity. Postprocessing enforces one-to-one mappings and removes matches below a predefined confidence threshold.

The framework supports 17 KGE models selected for their use in ontology alignment or broader knowledge graph tasks. These include translation-based, convolutional, bilinear, complex-valued, graph convolutional, hyperbolic, quaternion, and spatial models such as TransE, TransR, DistMult, ComplEx, RotatE, ConvE, CompGCN, MuRE, QuatE, and BoxE. The work aims to enable comparative evaluation of KGE approaches and support scalable, semantically grounded ontology alignment.

The speaker has a sore leg after another player fell on it but feels better after treatment and hopes to play in the next Stanley Cup Finals game. He says Calgary must control its energy, remain disciplined, and deliver its best effort against a strong Tampa team. He found watching the previous game from the dressing room frustrating and emphasizes that momentum, the opening draw, and sustained effort may determine the outcome. He praises Calgary’s fans and says he spends most of his time at home with his newborn.

Information systems research has shifted from positivist, technologically deterministic approaches toward human and social factors, mixed methods, and an understanding of IS as emerging through users’ ongoing adaptation of technology and processes. The paper connects this shift with complexity science and User Experience (UX), emphasizing that information systems are dynamic, nonlinear, irreversible, and continually evolving.

Complexity theory describes complex adaptive systems as open, far from equilibrium, self-organizing, historically dependent, and characterized by emergent properties. Unlike merely complicated systems, they cannot be fully understood by analyzing separate components. Although computers are complicated, incorporating human use makes information systems complex. Their outcomes cannot always be predicted from initial conditions, and their processes have an irreversible “arrow of time.”

UX extends traditional usability beyond measurable task performance to subjective concerns such as motivation, expectations, satisfaction, look, and feel. Contemporary systems therefore require multidisciplinary approaches combining numerical usability measures with attention to experiential and contextual human behavior.

The paper critiques approaches that separate human and technological subsystems or treat user requirements as independent starting points. It argues that information systems themselves alter organizational conditions and user requirements, making hierarchical decomposition inadequate compared with self-organization and networked interaction.

A partnership between the University of Salford and Sigma Ltd aims to examine real-world, non-reversible user experiences and how time and irreversibility affect design, usability, complexity, and success. The paper concludes that continual adaptation and flexibility should be incorporated into future information-system design.

DomeShelter Australia’s Container Mounted DomeShelter™ is a relocatable, weather-resistant shelter designed for Australian Wind Regions A–D. Its steel frame attaches to containers by welding, bolting or Twistlock. The CMDS protects goods, livestock and venues from rain, UV, heat and moisture, serving industrial, agricultural, events and tourism applications.

Economic data showed slowing momentum, with July adding 73,000 jobs and prior months revised down by 258,000, though June data was largely positive. Meanwhile, strong corporate results lifted projected S&P 500 second-quarter earnings growth to 11.2% and sales growth to 5.6%. After July’s 11th consecutive positive year, August through October historically produce weaker returns. The S&P 500 reached its 9.1% average annual return amid resistance, high valuations and a negative equity risk premium. AI-related stocks have supported the market, but continued economic weakness could drive volatility and create opportunities later in the year.

DAWN-PLASMA was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 multicenter trial comparing standard care plus high-titer convalescent plasma with standard care alone in hospitalized adults with COVID-19. Conducted under ethical and Good Clinical Practice guidelines, it randomized 489 patients 2:1 between May 2020 and January 2021. Plasma recipients were intended to receive 800–1000 mL in four units, beginning shortly after randomization. The primary endpoint was survival without mechanical ventilation at Day 15; secondary and exploratory endpoints assessed clinical status, ventilation, hospitalization, mortality, safety, laboratory findings, antibody titers, viral PCR, and quality of life.

The primary full analysis excluded six randomized patients. Baseline characteristics and concomitant therapies were similar between groups. Plasma was first administered a median of five hours after randomization, with a median volume of 884 mL; 91.9% received all four units. At Day 15, the proportion alive without mechanical ventilation did not differ between plasma and control groups: 83.7% versus 84.1% (odds ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.59–1.68; p=0.976). Per-protocol results were similar.

The match-up zone combines person-to-person and zone principles through assignment rules that prevent offensive alignments from splitting defenders, help counter overloads, and may confuse opponents. Its success depends on knowledgeable players and communication. Though generally passive and permissive of perimeter movement, it can incorporate aggressive traps and dictate whether opponents use one- or two-guard fronts.

Basic assignments place X1 on the point or right-side guard, X2 on the first player left of X1, X3 on the first player right, X4 on a second perimeter or baseline player, and X5 on the center or right baseline player. Assignments adjust for 2-3, 1-3-1, 1-2-2, and 1-4 offensive alignments and may be tailored to personnel.

Cutters are usually denied for three steps before the defender switches with a weakside teammate. On some cuts, defenders stay with their players while interchanging positional roles. Against various alignments, defenders use switches, interchanges, help positions, elbow drops, ball pressure, and post-pass denial to handle point cuts, wing cuts, baseline cuts, flashes, post rolls, and high-post movement. Similar-sized defenders can interchange rather than switch, simplifying matchups and confusing the offense.

The rules extend to half- and full-court trapping, especially when the ball enters corner trap zones. Traps may be used after timeouts, on free throws, or when trailing late, through quarter-court, half-court, and full-court pressure schemes.

Analyses of school districts nationwide and 2025 Mississippi test data found that schools strong in reading generally also perform well in math and science. Of identified district outliers, 140 excelled across subjects and grade levels, while only 14 excelled in one subject but underperformed in another. Mississippi school-level reading and math scores had a 0.87 correlation, and growth rates were similarly related: none of the 50 schools with the greatest reading gains fell below average in math growth. Florida showed comparable patterns. However, proficiency is associated with socioeconomic status, and results may depend on how states measure growth.

The passage presents reusable patterns for designing containerized distributed systems. On a single node, separating applications into containers improves resource isolation, team ownership, reuse, testing, deployment, and reliability. Kubernetes pods support tightly coupled containers sharing resources.

Three single-node patterns are described:

- **Sidecar:** augments an application container, such as adding HTTPS to a legacy service, synchronizing configuration, monitoring processes, or updating code from Git. Reusable sidecars should be parameterized, expose stable APIs, and include clear metadata and documentation.
- **Ambassador:** brokers communication between an application and external services. It can route requests to storage shards, discover environment-specific services, or split traffic between production and experimental versions.
- **Adapter:** converts an application’s interface into a standard form, enabling consistent monitoring, logging, and health checks without modifying the original container.

Multi-node systems commonly use microservices, which divide applications into independently maintained and scaled components with defined APIs. This improves agility, reliability, and scaling but makes architecture and debugging more difficult.

Replicated load-balanced services provide redundancy, availability, and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching uninitialized instances, while session tracking can consistently route a user to one replica. Additional replicated layers may provide caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination.

Sharded services divide state among machines when one machine cannot hold or serve all data. Sharded caches improve memory utilization but can lose capacity or performance when a shard fails. Replicating each shard increases resilience and permits independent scaling. Requests are assigned through deterministic, uniform sharding functions based on carefully selected keys. Consistent hashing limits remapping when the number of shards changes.

NVIDIA’s combined L1 data cache and shared memory architecture improves performance and simplifies programming. A100 increases capacity to 192 KB/SM from V100’s 128 KB/SM, providing low-latency, high-bandwidth access for streaming and frequently reused data.

The disclosure describes a plumbing device that measures and controls fluid flow from a single installation point while minimizing pressure loss. Most fluid travels unobstructed through a main channel, while a known proportion passes through a parallel bypass containing a flowmeter. A rotating wheel monitored by two movement sensors detects flow direction and backflow, enabling calculation of net flow and detection of very small leaks.

The device may include a solenoid shut-off valve, temperature sensor, upstream and downstream pressure sensors, microcontroller, and network-connected transceiver. Flow and temperature data can be processed locally or remotely and compared with recorded fluid-usage signatures to identify individual appliances, total consumption, abnormal usage, deterioration, overuse, pipe breaks, and leaks. Signatures may be created through supervised or unsupervised data collection and analyzed using pattern recognition, statistical classification, or machine-learning algorithms.

When unexplained flow is detected without a recognized appliance signature, the system can temporarily close the valve and compare upstream and downstream pressures. No pressure drop or a large drop associated with normal use causes the valve to reopen; a low-to-medium drop indicates leakage and can keep the valve closed. The system can account for baseline leakage, automatically stop abnormal flow, and notify a user’s mobile device through a remote server. Potential applications include monitoring appliance efficiency, abnormal prolonged water use, occupancy patterns, and public-restroom maintenance needs.

Crystal morphology strongly affects the safety and performance of energetic materials. Smooth, near-spherical PETN and RDX crystals are less shock-sensitive than needle-like crystals, while morphology also influences packing density, detonation velocity, and pressure. Existing Wulff-based BFDH, surface-energy, and attachment-energy models deviate from experimental morphologies, depend strongly on selected crystal planes, neglect edge and corner effects, and cannot provide intermediate growth dynamics or kinetic parameters.

The authors introduce an open-source kinetic Monte Carlo method, implemented in the Python package cgkmc, that predicts crystal morphology from intermolecular interaction parameters. The crystal lattice is represented as a weighted, undirected graph whose nodes indicate occupied or vacant lattice sites and whose edges encode interaction energies. Coordination numbers identify surface sites eligible for molecular adsorption or evaporation. Adsorption rates depend on diffusivity, solubility, surface density, and crystal radius, while evaporation rates are calculated using harmonic transition-state theory. A dynamically updated rate prefactor balances average adsorption and evaporation at a user-specified crystal size. A residence-time algorithm then simulates crystal growth through adsorption and evaporation events. Applied to PETN, the method shows excellent agreement with attachment-energy predictions and experimental observations.

The disclosure describes systems and methods that pause potentially risky actions involving untrusted emails, domains, links, attachments, or embedded code and prompt users to proceed or return and review their actions. Unlike technologies that automatically remove threats, the system preserves user choice while providing real-time phishing-awareness training and recording responses for analysis, reporting, and targeted education.

A device driver detects application processes, and a user console may inject a monitoring library into selected email clients, browsers, document readers, and other applications. The library detects URL access and related actions, pauses execution, and communicates with the console through shared memory. The console resolves shortened or encoded URLs, queries a server to determine whether a domain is trusted, untrusted, or unknown, displays an appropriate notification, and then resumes or cancels the action based on the user’s response. Browser-based email may be monitored through injected code or an extension communicating with the operating system through an intermediary application.

Company administrators can independently configure notifications for different user groups, including titles, text, buttons, help links, checkboxes, colors, and element visibility. Clients retain local settings and transmit a settings hash with server queries. If it differs from the server hash, updated settings and the new hash are returned and stored before notification display; update dates may alternatively be compared.

The system can monitor simulated and actual phishing activity, collect risky-behavior data, customize training, and support configurable actions such as ignoring, reporting, prompting, or preventing user activity. It may be delivered as software as a service and operate across varied client, server, network, cloud, and computing environments.

The Mid Screen offense, widely used in NBA and WNBA basketball, places an on-ball screen near the center of the floor while shooters occupy the wings, limiting help defense and creating quick scoring options. The point guard drives off a high-post screen and may attack the basket, pull up if the defender goes under, pass to the rolling or posting screener, or kick out to open shooters.

Execution depends on coordinated defensive reads by the ballhandler and screener. Counters include driving when defenders chase over, kicking out when wing defenders help, dropping the ball to the post when baseline defenders help, driving opposite against early cheating, throwing a lob when the screener’s defender overplays, and shooting when defenders go under. Against switches, offenses can exploit inside or outside mismatches; against anticipated switches, the screener can slip to the basket. Show-and-recover or trapping defenses can be attacked by stretching defenders, rolling or popping the screener, cutting to the basket, and moving the ball quickly through passes.

If the initial action fails, the offense can reverse the ball into motion, single/double screens, flex continuity, inside-triangle action, side screens, or post isolation. Variations include screen-and-pop, Horns with two high screeners, a 1–4 low alignment, high-post isolation, and a two-player passing game.

Successful installation requires defensive recognition, communication, timing, experience, fundamental skills, breakdown drills, and scrimmaging. Coaches should scout expected coverages, teach appropriate counters, monitor defensive adjustments, vary alignments and entries, and target weak defenders. Teams must also prepare to defend Mid Screens because of their widespread use.

SAE defines five levels of self-driving capability. Levels 1 and 2 automate acceleration, braking and some steering but require full attention. Level 3 permits limited hands-off driving with rapid takeover required. Level 4 allows longer takeover times and can stop safely if necessary; Waymo already operates limited Level 4 cars. Level 5 requires no driver. BMW expects Level 3 in 2021, Level 4 infrastructure by the mid-2020s, and Level 5 near the decade’s end.

Casey Mittelstadt could join Rochester for the regular season and playoffs on an AHL or amateur tryout contract. Buffalo prefers a tryout followed by an NHL deal beginning in 2018-19, while Mittelstadt could instead sign immediately, burn a contract year, and forfeit NCAA eligibility.

Soccer teams need a practiced corner-kick defense that players implement immediately. Every player should understand their role, react quickly, communicate, attack the ball aggressively, follow the goalkeeper’s commands, clear the ball high, far and wide, and transition rapidly into attack. Defenders should maintain basic principles such as goal-side positioning, preventing bounces, covering, blocking shots and winning second balls.

Three main systems are described:

- **Zone defense:** Players protect assigned areas and clear balls entering them. It is easy to teach and encourages movement away from goal, but opponents can overload zones and defenders may hesitate over responsibility. A basic setup assigns the goalkeeper the central six-yard area, players to each post, several defenders across the six-yard line and penalty area, one player to disrupt the kicker or short corner, and a striker positioned for a counterattack.
- **Man-to-man defense:** Each defender marks an attacker, staying goal-side and able to see both player and ball. It prevents zone overloads but can force defenders toward their own goal, require hurried matchups, and create risks if defenders lose their marks.
- **Mixed defense:** Players guard the posts and six-yard zones while others mark attackers individually. The passage cites a study indicating this approach may concede the fewest corner-kick goals.

Training should progress from positioning drills to actual kicks, varied deliveries and full opposition, emphasizing concentration and communication. Coaches may assign duties based on height, jumping, aggression and marking ability, scout opponents, adjust plans between games, and provide an outlet for fast counterattacks. The goalkeeper remains in charge, while defenders must move forward promptly after clearances. Practice should continue until responses become intuitive.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for long-term detection of abnormal cardiac activity using cardiac data, such as ECG or PPG, together with motion data, such as accelerometer measurements. Data may be collected by wearable devices, including smart watches, and supplemented with medical history and demographic information.

The method divides data into time windows, preprocesses signals, calculates signal-quality indices, selects high-quality channels, extracts cardiovascular features, and transforms cardiac or motion data into tensors. A trained deep-learning architecture—including a convolutional neural network, bidirectional recurrent neural network, and attention network—classifies windows or periods as normal, abnormal, noisy, or other specified classes. Attention scores can identify windows containing abnormalities and support estimates of abnormal-activity burden. Results may be compiled into reports for clinicians. The disclosure covers corresponding computer-readable media, processor-based systems, sensor configurations, communications, and computing implementations.

JPMorgan Chase has deployed its proprietary generative AI platform to 200,000 employees as part of an approximately $18 billion technology investment. More than 175 AI applications support customer service, research, credit assessments, onboarding, fraud detection and risk management, reducing analysis time and repetitive work. Key challenges include regulatory compliance, transparency, bias, security, legacy infrastructure and adoption costs, particularly under market stress and tighter regulation.

Wandera’s analysis of 50,000 moderately to heavily used iPhones and iPads found iOS 11 reduced average battery life from 240 minutes on iOS 10 to 96 minutes, with older devices affected more. Although some users reverted to iOS 10.3.3, Wandera advised against this due to security risks. Apple’s iOS 11.0.1 update improved battery life to 159 minutes. Users can conserve power by restricting background app refresh and location access or enabling low power mode.

The passage presents a synchronous 5-V GaN push-pull converter design using the TPS7H5001-SP. It operates at 500 kHz with a 205-kΩ timing resistor, 25-ns dead time, 49.9-kΩ leading-edge blanking resistor, and 33-nF soft-start capacitor providing approximately 7.5 ms. The transformer uses a 2.5 turns ratio and 40-μH primary inductance. Selected components include 170-V primary GaN FETs, 80-V synchronous rectifier FETs, a 0.47-μH output inductor, and approximately 2.3 mF of output capacitance for ripple, transient, and radiation-induced SET mitigation.

Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins near 35 A using a 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω sense resistor. The design uses a 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation targeting 10 kHz, compensation values of 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF, and a 102-kΩ slope-compensation resistor. Component values, RCD clamping, filtering, and compensation may require optimization during testing.

TPS7H500x-SP controllers require a regulated 4-V to 14-V supply and at least 0.1-μF ceramic input bypassing. Layout guidance emphasizes short, wide high-current paths; minimized switching loops and switch-node area; separation of analog and power grounds with a single connection point; close placement of bypass, filtering, sensing, and compensation components; and isolation of sensitive traces from high-dv/dt signals. The passage also lists related documentation, revision updates, ESD precautions, package information, and TI warranty and usage disclaimers.

This retrospective cohort study examined incident hypertension after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) among 2,514 patients who delivered at two southeastern U.S. academic health systems during 2014–2017 and had blood pressure measured 15–90 days postpartum. Cox models evaluated associations between postpartum blood pressure, clinical factors, and subsequent hypertension diagnosis.

Forty percent of otherwise eligible patients lacked a documented 15–90-day postpartum blood pressure check, and only 20% were checked within 14 days. At 15–90 days, 55% had blood pressures in Stage 1 or Stage 2 hypertension ranges. Overall, 315 patients (13%) subsequently received a hypertension diagnosis.

Higher systolic blood pressure at the postpartum visit was associated with incident hypertension: 140 versus 120 mmHg had a hazard ratio of 1.70 (95% CI, 1.37–2.12). Severe preeclampsia/eclampsia versus gestational hypertension (HR 1.49, 95% CI, 1.15–1.94) and age 35 versus 25 years (HR 1.46, 95% CI, 1.16–1.83) were also associated with greater risk. Modeled 12-month hypertension risk was 4.7% at 110/65 mmHg and 13.0% at 140/90 mmHg. Results were similar when analyses were restricted by provider specialty.

The findings support more consistent postpartum blood pressure screening, early cardiovascular risk management, and interventions addressing barriers to follow-up. Limitations included retrospective data, possible missing outside care, selection differences, reliance on diagnostic codes, and uncertain generalizability beyond the U.S. South.

The speaker described creating a scoring chance, recovering defensively on two-on-ones, and improving consistency against Dallas as the series progressed. Although pleased with the Devils’ progress, he emphasized that they must avoid complacency and try to finish the series Thursday. He signed with New Jersey partly because he believed the team could reach this stage, drawing on experience from consecutive finals in Finland. Dallas presents challenges through speed, cycling, support, and finding open space. The Devils have improved line changes and communication throughout the playoffs while treating defense as a group responsibility. He also praised a veteran player for preparing well and increasing his contribution during the playoffs.

More than 250 Connaught Public School students played tunnel ball for nearly 30 minutes, attempting to surpass the 120-player world record pending Guinness verification. The Hintonburg event also raised $10,000 for playground, basketball court, soccer field, tree and yard improvements.

Several billionaire executives reject conventional work-life balance. Jeff Bezos prefers “work-life harmony,” arguing professional and personal well-being reinforce each other. Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman, Scale AI cofounder Lucy Guo, LinkedIn cofounder Reid Hoffman, and Alibaba cofounder Jack Ma contend that building exceptional companies requires extremely long hours and major sacrifices. Zoom CEO Eric Yuan says work and life cannot truly be balanced, though he prioritizes family during conflicts. Guo similarly advises maintaining some time for friends and family despite working 90-hour weeks.

On Oct. 29, 2001, Enron’s shares fell to multiyear lows after Moody’s downgraded its senior unsecured debt to Baa2, two levels above junk, and warned of further cuts. Enron sought an additional $1–2 billion in bank credit after drawing roughly $3.3 billion to repay commercial paper. Disclosures involving partnerships formerly managed by CFO Andrew Fastow, related write-downs and a $1.2 billion equity reduction prompted an SEC inquiry, investor distrust and concerns about liquidity. Analysts expected lenders to demand higher rates and collateral, while some European energy firms restricted trading with Enron. Commentary questioned Enron’s asset-light strategy, financial disclosure and ability to retain employees. Shareholders also filed lawsuits alleging conflicts of interest and losses involving partnership transactions. Separately, Moody’s warned that overall U.S. corporate credit quality would continue deteriorating into early 2002.

U.S. consumer confidence rose to 128.7 in April from 127.0 in March, nearing February’s 18-year high. Strong labor conditions, tax cuts, reduced stock volatility and easing trade-war fears supported confidence. However, analysts warned sluggish real income growth could limit consumer spending despite upbeat surveys.

NEC’s Satellite Operation Center will begin full operations in April, initially operating the ASNARO-2 radar satellite using GroundNEXTAR and a secure data center. NEC and JEOSS plan to distribute ASNARO-2 images starting in September.

Seattle and King County home prices and rents have risen sharply amid limited inventory and strong sales. A ValueInsured survey reported that 71% of Washington homeowners feared a housing bubble, but its small sample limits the finding. Real estate experts said strong credit, down payments and homeowner equity make a 2008-style collapse unlikely, though prices and inventory may eventually level out. A city comparison showed wide affordability differences, with estimated required household incomes ranging from $7,359 in Detroit to $226,577 in San Francisco; Seattle required about $106,709.

AMD’s CS5535 revision A3 has several documented issues:

- Reading Port 60h can incorrectly clear AuxOutputFull, potentially confusing USB keyboard/mouse PS/2 emulation; use separate interrupts.
- IDE tACK settings do not alter UDMA timing, which remains 30 ns and meets requirements.
- WORD-aligned PRDs can hang ATAC; drivers should use DWORD alignment.
- The LPC controller may abort transactions with delayed SYNC patterns, particularly through LPC-to-ISA bridges; a PLD workaround is available.
- SMB NEGACK behavior is inconsistent; clear it using two specified writes to SMB_STS.
- GLPCI’s retry counter includes unrelated PCI retries, potentially ending retries early.
- After suspend, atomic GPIO High Bank writes clear unselected bits; use read-modify-write.
- CS5535 SMBus data hold time is discussed against the 300 ns SMB 2.0 minimum.
- LOWBAT_FLAG may not be set after an abnormal standby, preventing later detection; no resolution is provided.
- Excessive sleep-control delays can prevent SLEEP_X/SLEEP_Y deassertion and PCI/IDE recovery; program these delays below PM_SED.

SN NEXT No. 1 McEachern visited Harrison in Kennesaw, Georgia, for an 8 p.m. kickoff. Both teams entered 5-0 after bye weeks. McEachern sought to strengthen its case for The Sporting News High School Football Top 25, while Harrison aimed to boost its profile with an upset.

Former FDA vaccine regulator Peter Marks, ousted by RFK Jr., joined Eli Lilly Research Laboratories to oversee molecule discovery and infectious diseases. The move drew criticism over the revolving door between regulators and industry.

The radiation-hardness-assured TPS7H500x-SP family provides fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM control for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies up to 2 MHz and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full-bridge. Type 2A or 2B frequency compensation may be used; Type 2A adds a high-frequency noise-attenuation capacitor. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C and restarts power-up below 160°C.

A synchronous push-pull TPS7H5001-SP design example uses GaN devices, 500-kHz switching, 5-V output, approximately 25-ns dead time, 50-ns leading-edge blanking, and 7.5-ms soft start. Selected values include a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 170-V primary GaN FETs, 80-V synchronous rectifier FETs, a 0.47-µH output inductor, and approximately 2.3-mF output capacitance. Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins near 35 A using a 7.5-Ω sense resistor and 1:100 current-sense transformer. Type 2A compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover using 40.2-kΩ, 15-nF, and 47-pF components; slope compensation uses 102 kΩ.

The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require at least 0.1 µF of input bypass capacitance. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switching loops and switch-node area, keeping sensitive signals away from noisy traces, placing bypass and compensation components close to the controller, and using short, wide high-current traces. TI states that application information must be validated by customers and provides related evaluation, radiation, support, packaging, and revision documentation.

Astronomers and citizen scientists using LOFAR discovered RAD J131346.9+500320, the most distant and powerful known odd radio circle. Located at redshift 0.94, it consists of two intersecting radio rings and is the first ORC identified through citizen science and with LOFAR. The study suggests ORCs may arise from galactic superwinds rather than black hole or galaxy mergers.

The RAD@home collaboration also found two giant radio galaxies with rings associated with bent or extended jets. All three objects lie in massive galaxy clusters, indicating that interactions between relativistic magnetized plasma and surrounding hot plasma may shape these structures. Future radio and optical surveys are expected to reveal more ORCs and clarify their formation and evolution.

The news digest covers Enron’s bankruptcy, regulatory contacts, asset sales and international operations, alongside U.S. energy policy. Enron planned to rebuild around profitable pipelines and power plants, sell weaker assets, retain employees and adopt a new name. FERC disclosed 25 contacts with Enron officials but denied improper influence. BG Group planned to increase Indian investment to $1.3 billion after acquiring Enron assets, while disputing offshore field management rights. Enron Japan’s limited assets might leave creditors unpaid. U.S. agencies had provided $1.2 billion in loans to Enron-related overseas power projects. The Senate prepared to debate energy legislation involving Arctic drilling, conservation, fuel economy and electricity regulation. California considered delaying its MTBE ban over potential gasoline shortages and inadequate ethanol infrastructure.

Precise ring-buffer halting requires the target command to be last in the queue; precise error halting requires queuing one command at a time. Interrupt status can be cleared only when the buffer is empty or processing is paused. With SMEE or SME-MK, software encodes encryption information in valid system physical addresses, and firmware selects appropriate keys.

PM_GET_CAPABILITIES reports firmware capabilities and versions. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO processes 1–128 entries, moving 4 KB hypervisor-owned or non-SNP pages, including pages used by DMA devices, while updating IOMMU host page-table entries. Software must prevent CPU access and, where required, prepare IOMMU entries and invalidate ATS mappings. Firmware validates addresses and page states, obtains exclusive RMP access when enforced, invalidates CPU and IOMMU TLBs, flushes DMA, copies data with appropriate encryption, updates mappings, and clears migration state. Direct 2 MB migration is unsupported; pages must be split into 4 KB pages.

PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST processes 1–128 SNP guest pages. DMA is unsupported, CPU access must be prevented, and RMP enforcement is required. Source pages must be Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid, destinations must be Pre-Migration, and page sizes must match. Firmware validates the guest context, obtains exclusive RMP access, invalidates CPU TLB entries, copies data, and updates source and destination RMP states. Physically contiguous, aligned 2 MB pages are permitted; noncontiguous ones must be split.

Command, migration-entry, ring-buffer, and hardware errors are reported through command or list statuses, PM_STATUS, or MCA. Batch hardware failures can make up to 128 pages unrecoverable; software should preserve state and determine whether to stop operations, terminate VMs, or reboot.

In Windows 10, change mouse pointer size and color through Settings > Ease of Access > Mouse, or search for “Mouse Pointer.” Options include small, medium, or large sizes and white, black, or background-inverting colors. For additional shapes and sizes, use Control Panel > Mouse > Pointers.

To close all Safari tabs on an iPhone, press and hold the Tabs icon, then select “Close xx Tabs.” If the tab overview is already open, press and hold “Done” for the same option. Restarting Safari will not close tabs because the browser remembers them.

Canadian Pacific Railway says operational changes in Vancouver and North Dakota will cut cross-border container transit to Detroit to five days, up to 48 hours faster than Canadian National Railway. The faster, seamless Chicago route could lower shipping costs and increase competitive pressure on CN.

Louisiana sued the Citizens’ Bank’s Banking Department for a banking-license tax. The bank’s president objected that no corporation existed under that name and that he lacked authority to represent it. The court found that only the Citizens’ Bank of Louisiana was expressly authorized to sue and be sued; neither the 1853 statute nor the related compact created a separate corporate banking department. Because the state intentionally sued the department rather than the bank, the error was not merely a misnomer. Questions concerning corporate existence and estoppel required proceedings against the Citizens’ Bank itself. Limiting its decision to defective citation, the court reversed the judgment and dismissed the suit as a nonsuit. Justice Monroe dissented, and rehearing was denied.

NASA’s Dawn spacecraft captured the closest-ever images of Ceres, revealing detailed views of sodium carbonate deposits in the 50-mile-wide Occator Crater. After entering a lower orbit in June, Dawn approached within about 22 miles of the surface. Images taken June 14 and June 22 show Vinalia Faculae, Cerealia Facula, and a nearby mound. The deposits, discovered in 2015, are the largest carbonates found beyond Earth, but their origin—whether from shallow mineral-rich water or deeper brines—remains uncertain. Dawn’s extended mission uses gravity measurements and spectrometers to investigate Ceres’ interior and composition. Launched in 2007, Dawn orbited Vesta before reaching Ceres in 2015. Nearing the end of its fuel supply and mission, the spacecraft will remain in orbit rather than crash, preventing contamination of Ceres.

The passage presents a control-theoretic approach to budget pacing in real-time advertising auctions. Pacing systems adjust spending to follow desired plans despite stochastic traffic, noisy signals, auction dynamics, and changing market conditions. The authors propose a Bucketized Hysteresis Controller (BHC), provide a framework for parameter selection, and validate it through real-world auction experiments, emphasizing improved accuracy for small-budget campaigns.

Ads submit bids calculated as the maximum bid multiplied by event probability. A pacing multiplier, \(\lambda \in (0,1]\), rescales these bids to influence auction win rates and spending. Because auction conditions change, \(\lambda\) must be updated periodically to keep spending aligned with campaign budgets.

The production baseline uses multiplicative \(\lambda\) updates and an adaptive step size. A fluctuation factor derived from recent pacing history distinguishes stable trends from oscillatory behavior, increasing the step size during stable movement and reducing it when oscillation is high. No update occurs when delivery is within a tolerance range.

BHC instead divides normalized delivery error into predefined bands with associated gains. It determines adjustment direction from the error sign, applies larger steps for large errors to accelerate convergence, and smaller steps for minor errors to improve stability. This multi-step quantized design is inspired by bang-bang control and gain scheduling.

Euro zone stocks reached their highest in over a year after manufacturing activity grew at its fastest pace in more than five years. Italy’s FTSE MIB and Germany’s DAX posted notable gains, while lower-rated euro zone government bond yields fell. Thin holiday trading contributed to volatility. The euro weakened below US$1.05 as the dollar resumed its rise, supported by expectations of U.S. rate increases and fiscal expansion. Markets showed little reaction to an Istanbul nightclub attack that killed 39, though the Turkish lira slipped near record lows amid security and tourism concerns. China’s manufacturing expanded for a fifth month but slowed more than expected. The yuan had lost almost 7 percent in 2016, while bitcoin rose above US$1,000 for the first time since late 2013.

Roger Poole advises anglers to reassess river conditions, swims, tactics and baits when the coarse-fishing season reopens after the spawning close season. Natural food is plentiful, so experimentation is recommended. Early-season prospects include tench in ponds, chub near river margins and cover, and dace, roach and perch using light float tackle. Feeder or ledger tactics on the Arun may catch bream, chub or barbel.

Petworth and Bognor Angling Club encourages young people to take up fishing and maintains still waters and stretches of the Rother and Arun. National Fishing Month, running July 27 to September 2, supports more than 250 UK events for adults and children, with backing from the Environment Agency and fishing trade. Children under 16 are eligible for a free fishing licence.

NEC Display extended warranties from three to five years at no extra cost for four professional 24/7 signage models: P404, P484, P554, and P703. Coverage begins with first shipments for the first three models and for P703 purchases made on or after August 1, 2017.

Guyana’s Office of Climate Change opened a three-day Greenhouse Gas Inventory workshop to prepare the Third National Communication due to the UNFCCC in 2019. The workshop aims to strengthen technical and institutional capacity, integrate climate priorities into national development, and establish a pool of local experts able to compile, review and edit emissions inventories and other climate reports. Later activities will address mitigation, baseline assessment, vulnerability and adaptation. National Project Coordinator Marlon Velloza said the inventory will identify major emissions sources and net sinks, support Guyana’s green agenda, and raise awareness of climate risks such as flooding, health threats, livelihood losses and food insecurity. India-based experts Anit Garg and Indu Murthy are conducting sessions remotely, with participants expected to gain practical experience and potentially receive certification.

Nashville police arrested Travis Reinking, suspected of killing four people with an assault rifle at a Waffle House, without firing shots. James Shaw Jr. had disarmed Reinking, who fled and was found more than 24 hours later with a handgun and ammunition. The passage contrasts police restraint in Reinking’s arrest with killings and violent arrests of unarmed Black people, arguing that race affects U.S. policing. It also describes Alabama officers violently arresting Chikesia Clemons, an unarmed Black woman involved in a dispute over plastic utensils at another Waffle House.

The May 16, 2001 ISDA press report covers derivatives regulation, markets, accounting, trading infrastructure and documentation. Witnesses urged the IRS to apply Congress’s broader risk-management standard to hedging rules, including commodities, weather, energy and insurance-related transactions. BIS reported that outstanding OTC derivatives grew only 1% in the second half of 2000 to $95.2 trillion, while gross market value rose 24% to $3.2 trillion.

Federal Home Loan Bank of New York implemented Principia Partners’ system for FAS 133 compliance. FASB also proposed guidance allowing qualifying option-value changes to remain in other comprehensive income until the hedged transaction affects earnings. UK regulators defended the proposed 15% “w charge” on credit derivatives, while the UK Treasury proposed allowing building societies to use credit derivatives solely for risk management.

Former CFTC chairman Philip McBride-Johnson warned that regulatory and margin costs could limit single-stock futures. CME and CBOE, with limited CBOT participation, announced a separately regulated, electronic joint venture for such products.

Heavy credit-linked note issuance and offsetting default-swap sales widened the negative basis between swaps and bonds, creating arbitrage opportunities. Lightrade planned to expand its neutral bandwidth pooling-point network across the United States.

ISDA finalized a restructuring supplement to its 1999 Credit Derivatives Definitions. It generally limits deliverable securities following restructuring to maturities under 30 months after the restructuring date or to the extended maturity of the restructured loan.

Napheesa Collier suffered Grade 2 tears to three ankle ligaments and a shin muscle in a collision, requiring at least six weeks of recovery. The Mercury eliminated the Lynx in Game 4, while Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve received a one-game suspension for reacting to the injury-causing play.

The Horns Offense uses high-post screens that can create layups, open shots, or mismatches. Defenders should influence the ballhandler toward the weaker screener, weak hand, or sideline while using strong fundamentals against penetration, post play, and kick-out passes.

In the NBA “show and recover” strategy, the on-ball defender fights over the screen as the screener’s defender steps out to force the ballhandler wide. Help defenders cover the roll and deny passes before everyone recovers to their assignments.

The “SOS” disruption strategy traps the point guard before the initial screen or pass, forcing the offense out of planned routes. Help defenders cover the rolling screener and passing options. On a pass out of the trap, defenders rotate as the ball leaves the passer’s hands, reestablish ball pressure, denial positions, helpside alignment, and low-post coverage. Baseline drives and post entries trigger designated trap rotations.

University of Alabama student Kelsey Hall promised to wear a Christmas tree costume to class if her post received 1,000 retweets. After quickly receiving 30,000, she fulfilled the pledge but found the resulting attention stressful and said she would reconsider future social media challenges.

The passage promotes Maxwell Chan and SkyBlue Cross’s “Functional Food Therapeutic Lifestyle Change Intervention Program” for high cholesterol. It argues that conventional treatment focuses on lowering cholesterol with lifelong statin use rather than addressing individual causes involving lifestyle, genetics, environment, and organ functions. The promoted program claims to identify and treat 14 types and underlying causes of high cholesterol through personalized, natural, food-based interventions without side effects. It also advertises Chan’s book, “Naturally Balanced Your Cholesterol Level,” and related websites.

Matthew Hatfield hosted VirginiaPreps.com’s High School Sports Talk from the Nike Elite Youth Basketball League event in Hampton, featuring basketball players, journalists, callers and officiating supervisor Bryan Kersey.

Alpha Theory identifies investor biases through deviations from risk-reward-based position sizing. Managers often fail to reduce positions after price gains, scale too slowly into high-conviction opportunities, hold positions without explicit price targets, and overdiversify into lower-return names. The firm recommends re-underwriting positions at critical probability-weighted return levels and applying disciplined, optimal sizing. Its research found disciplined managers and larger holdings outperform, while concentrated portfolios generated 2.2% more alpha than diversified ones. In 2016, clients could have improved returns by 5.1% using suggested optimal position sizes, though not every position could be sized accordingly.

Showstoppers Theatre presents “Foiled Again!,” a children’s musical melodrama directed by founder Radu Azdril. Performances are at La Colina Junior High School on Friday, Saturday, June 28 and June 29. Admission is free for children 12 and younger; general tickets cost $7.

Internal Bar Strength (IBS) is a mean-reversion indicator calculated as (Close−Low)/(High−Low). It ranges from zero to one: low values suggest short-term bullish conditions, while high values are considered bearish. Backtests indicate IBS has performed well for decades on individual stocks and broad stock indices, particularly SPY and QQQ, but poorly on commodities, metals, and commodity-heavy markets.

IBS strategies generally buy weakness and sell strength. One modified SPY strategy achieved a 15.3% CAGR while invested 36% of the time, with a 74% win rate, 22% maximum drawdown, and 1.7 Sharpe ratio. Nasdaq results were also strong.

Performance tends to improve during volatile bear markets, when large upward moves occur more frequently. Volatility and moving-average filters improved some results, although small parameter changes produced variability and increased curve-fitting risk. Combining IBS with other indicators may also enhance performance.

A key weakness is execution: trades need to be entered near the close. Delaying entry until the next day’s open significantly reduces returns. The authors use IBS in swing trading alongside other indicators and emphasize adapting strategies to each market rather than expecting universal effectiveness.

After watching construction of the original Tappan Zee Bridge in 1950, the author describes crossing the newly opened first span of the Governor Mario M. Cuomo Bridge and attending a presentation by project director and structural engineer Jamey Barbas. The 3.1-mile crossing includes a 2,230-foot elevated main span, eight 419-foot towers, and cable stays supporting more than 74 million pounds. It is designed to last 100 years without major maintenance and includes bicycle and pedestrian lanes, viewing platforms, and extensive educational outreach. Construction used the massive “I Lift NY” floating crane, modular components, and river-based concrete plants that eliminated 20,000 truck trips. Labor agreements, environmental studies, and contingency planning supported the project. About 7,000 people contributed nearly nine million work hours, following more than one million design hours.

A fake WhatsApp link claiming PM Narendra Modi is offering Rs. 500 mobile recharge asks users for personal and telecom details, then directs them to share it with 15 friends. The site disclaims telecom affiliations and may be a phishing attempt. Users are advised not to click, share, provide information, or download software from such links.
