Gross margin increased to 56.7%, and operating income rose to $176 million. GPU revenue increased 5% to $940 million, Tegra revenue rose 4% to $145 million, and licensing-related revenue was $66 million.

Operating cash flow was $246 million. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $4.79 billion, while long-term debt was $1.39 billion. NVIDIA returned $99 million to shareholders through $53 million in repurchases and $46 million in dividends. The board expanded repurchase authorization to $2 billion, raised the quarterly dividend to $0.0975 per share, and increased planned fiscal 2016 shareholder returns to $800 million.

NVIDIA announced plans to wind down or sell its Icera modem operations, estimating restructuring charges of $100 million to $125 million if no sale occurs. It also continued patent litigation involving Samsung and Qualcomm. Management found disclosure controls effective and reported no material changes in internal controls, market risks, or previously disclosed risk factors aside from Icera-related risks.

Zach Parise said the team must focus on winning tonight and extending the series to New Jersey. He emphasized creating more offensive-zone pressure, obstructing Jonathan Quick’s vision, and generating rebounds. Parise credited the opposing defense for limiting entries, boxing players out, and allowing Quick to see shots. He said lineup changes could provide a different element, despite strong playoff performances from other players. The team has worked hard but needs better puck movement, fewer turnovers, and greater pressure. He added that past comebacks show a recovery is possible, noting all three games were close and the margin for error is slim.

The 2-1-2 zone is a compact variation of the 2-3 defense that protects the middle and positions big players near the basket for rebounding. It is vulnerable to outside shooting, so it is mainly used against poor shooting teams or high-post offenses. The athletic middle defender covers the high post, fronts the low post, and stays between the ball and basket. The two quickest outside defenders move together, pressure the ball, protect the elbows, and deny passes from corners. Baseline defenders cover corners, protect the blocks, and establish weakside rebounding position. When the ball enters the middle, defenders collapse to pressure the handler and prevent high-low post passes.

Markets shifted decisively risk-off after a week of earnings, economic data, monetary policy and political developments. Major indexes fell 2.2%–4.2%, forming bearish engulfing patterns at record highs as volume, market internals and most sectors weakened.

Second-quarter earnings were generally strong: 82% of reporting S&P 500 companies beat earnings estimates and 79% exceeded revenue estimates. Earnings revisions also improved. However, investors sold into positive results amid concerns about slowing growth and limited new buying.

GDP grew 3%, above the expected 2.5%, but tariff-driven import volatility distorted the data, while weak personal spending indicated soft demand. Nonfarm payrolls rose by 73,000 versus 100,000 expected, and prior months received unusually large downward revisions. The unemployment rate increased slightly to 4.2%, while the labor force contracted.

The Federal Reserve maintained a patient, data-dependent stance amid tariff-related inflation uncertainty and labor-force changes. Markets assigned more than 75% odds to a September rate cut and anticipated three cuts by January. Bond prices strengthened as economic slowdown concerns increased.

President Trump dismissed Bureau of Labor Statistics Commissioner Erika McEntarfer, announced nuclear submarine deployments following Russian comments, pursued tariff agreements and postponements, and gained another opportunity for a Fed appointment after Governor Adriana Kugler’s resignation. Short- and intermediate-term indicators remained risk-off, although longer-term earnings expectations continued to improve.

AMZN options can be used to speculate on stock movements, hedge positions, leverage capital, and potentially limit risk. Strategies include buying calls or puts, writing covered or naked options, and spread trading. Calls generally gain value as AMZN rises, while puts gain value as it falls; sensitivity is measured by delta. Strike prices and expiration dates determine exercise rights and potential payoffs.

Key risks include leverage, total premium loss, expiration, limited liquidity, margin calls, and potentially substantial or unlimited losses from naked options. Spreads can reduce risk by combining options with different strikes or expirations.

Trading generally requires options knowledge, sufficient capital, and a broker margin account; many brokers require a $2,000 minimum deposit. Costs may include premiums, commissions, exchange, clearing, and platform fees. Available orders include market, limit, and stop orders. Expirations may be weekly or monthly, commonly on the third Friday.

Higher AMZN volatility generally increases option premiums. Tax treatment depends on the trade and holding period, and investors are advised to consult a tax accountant. Platform selection should consider fees, execution speed, reliability, and research tools. Quantified analysis can help identify trends, entry and exit points, and potential profit or loss.

The lecture examines experimentation and robust design, contrasting factorial methods with adaptive one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT) experimentation. R.A. Fisher challenged earlier preferences for simple experiments by developing randomized factorial designs, which improve estimation efficiency by evaluating multiple factors simultaneously. Fractional factorial designs reduce the number of trials but confound some main effects and interactions, creating risks when interactions are significant.

Robust parameter design seeks control-factor settings that reduce sensitivity to uncontrolled noise factors. Taguchi promoted crossed arrays of control and noise factors, but these experiments can become large, and combined-array refinements may fail in some cases. Despite this, orthogonal-array methods remain embedded in industrial programs such as Six Sigma.

An investigation of an agricultural-equipment manufacturer found that many planned robust-design experiments were never completed. This motivated research into adaptive OFAT methods, where each factor is changed sequentially and retained or reversed according to observed improvement. Across 66 chemical, mechanical, and electrical systems, adaptive experiments often matched or outperformed fractional factorial designs when experimental error was moderate or interactions were substantial. Mathematical analysis indicated that adaptive OFAT cannot separately estimate interactions, but can still exploit important ones and approach strong outcomes with relatively few trials. For seven two-level factors, eight adaptive trials achieved about 80% of the maximum attainable improvement, compared with 128 trials for a full factorial design.

Starting points mattered more than factor ordering. Informed starting points substantially improved results and could preserve adaptive OFAT’s advantage under high experimental error. Tests involving sheet-metal spinning and paper airplanes supported these findings. Ensembles of multiple adaptive experiments also outperformed larger fractional factorial designs and showed robustness to experimental error.

Adaptive methods are most suitable when experiments can proceed sequentially and the primary objective is immediate improvement. Parallel experiments, delayed measurements, time trends, or a need for precise, reusable effect estimates favor factorial designs. The lecture also argues that organizations may gain more by conducting many streamlined robustness studies than a few expensive ones, especially when they are uncertain where major quality problems lie.

The concluding discussion addressed course logistics and problem-set questions involving regression terms, interactions, covariance, noise propagation, ANOVA, and preparation for the upcoming quiz.

A teardown of Google Wallet v20 suggests upcoming security changes, though findings are speculative and may not be released. The app may add fingerprint unlocking, replace its dedicated Payments PIN with a Google Account PIN used across other Google services, and allow users to disable PIN access entirely. These changes could reduce friction and the number of PINs users must remember. The Google-signed APK, version 20.0.158862257, can upgrade the existing app.

Frickley Athletic manager Spencer Fearn added midfielders Jason Yates, Josh Nodder and Danny Patterson for 2017-18, praising their work rate, versatility, goals and experience. Defender Joe Austin, wide player Tom Dugdale and utility man Danny Swales also joined. Tyler Williams will remain, while striker Jacob Hazell returns after a successful spell at Scarborough and could partner Gavin Allott. Hazell previously scored more than 20 goals as Frickley finished seventh in the Premier.

The passage studies ground states of classical bilinear-biquadratic Heisenberg and XY models on a partially anisotropic triangular lattice composed of isosceles triangles. Each triangular plaquette has two bilinear couplings, \(K\) and \(L\), and two biquadratic couplings, \(A\) and \(B\). Reducing the problem to one plaquette enables construction of global ground states for various lattices.

The three interspin angles \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) occupy a tetrahedral domain defined by geometric inequalities. Its vertices represent collinear configurations, while edges and faces represent coplanar ones; interior points correspond to noncoplanar states. The plaquette energy is minimized over these regions. Analytical stationarity conditions are derived for interior, face, edge, and vertex configurations.

The resulting configurations include ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, canted ferromagnetic, spiral, and noncoplanar phases. Their energies and existence conditions are tabulated. For interior noncoplanar states, the angles satisfy
\(\cos\alpha=K/(2A)\) and \(\cos\beta=\cos\gamma=L/(2B)\).
Ground-state phase diagrams are presented for several values of \(A\) with \(L=1\), distinguishing Heisenberg and XY models and marking continuous and discontinuous transitions.

A KPMG survey of 130 leaders at large U.S. organizations found AI agent deployment rose from 11% to 42% in six months, while employee resistance fell from 47% to 21%. Workers increasingly view AI as an enabling tool, but its immaturity requires human oversight, critical thinking and adaptability, contributing to “cognitive fatigue.” Most leaders believe conventional KPIs and ROI measures fail to capture AI’s full value, instead tracking productivity, profitability and quality. AI is also reshaping entry-level work and recruiting, with 56% of leaders expecting changes within a year and younger workers needing greater skepticism toward technology.

Bank of New York Mellon reduced its Greenlight Reinsurance holdings by 8.7% in the second quarter, selling 18,470 shares and retaining 193,448 shares valued at $4.04 million. Other institutional investors increased their positions, while institutions and hedge funds collectively owned 45.43% of the company.

Analyst ratings varied between sell, hold and buy. Greenlight Reinsurance shares opened at $22.30, with a market capitalization of $832.70 million. The company reported a quarterly loss of $0.96 per share, beating estimates by $0.04, on revenue of $121.48 million. Analysts projected annual earnings of $0.68 per share.

Director Leonard R. Goldberg completed two reported share sales, and insiders sold 6,468 shares worth $147,928 over three months. Insiders owned 21.81% of the company. Greenlight Capital Re categorizes its underwriting operations into frequency and severity business.

Costco members can buy gold, silver, and platinum online or at select warehouses, subject to availability and purchase limits. Executive members receive 2% rewards on most purchases, including precious metals. Online orders typically arrive within three to five days. In stores, shoppers complete a merchandise pickup slip and pay with staff assistance. Precious metals cannot be returned or receive price adjustments. Buyers are cautioned against interest-bearing financing and advised to consider long-term holding because resale can be difficult and costly.

Offensive guards line up between the center and tackles and play crucial roles in both running and passing offenses. They block powerful defensive tackles and blitzing linebackers, prevent interior pressure on quarterbacks, communicate against defensive stunts and blitzes, establish double teams, and pull laterally to block defenders and create running lanes. The position requires intelligence, toughness, strength, quickness, agility, footwork, hand placement, and sound technique.

Guards generally have sturdy, compact builds, typically measuring 6 feet 3 inches to 6 feet 5 inches and weighing 300–320 pounds. Common abbreviations are G, LG, and RG, while offensive linemen may be nicknamed hogs, bruisers, bulldozers, big uglies, or monsters. The origin of the term “guard” is unclear but dates to early football. Notable guards include Larry Allen, an 11-time Pro Bowl selection and Super Bowl champion, and John Hannah, a seven-time All-Pro inducted into both the College and Pro Football Halls of Fame.

SanDisk grants users a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use the bundled software in executable form for personal use on one computer or device at a time. SanDisk and its licensors retain ownership. Users may not modify, reverse engineer, decompile, rent, embed, separate, disclose, or create derivative works from the software. Permitted copies must remain unmodified and include all notices and the agreement.

The software is provided “as is” without warranties, and users assume all risks and repair costs. SanDisk and its licensors exclude liability for indirect or consequential damages, with total liability limited to the amount paid for the software. Government use is subject to restricted-rights provisions. SanDisk may terminate the license for violations, requiring destruction or deletion of all copies.

The software is not intended for hazardous or fail-safe applications. California and U.S. federal law govern the agreement, with disputes subject to courts in Santa Clara County, California. Users must comply with export laws. The device must not be discarded with unsorted household waste; local return and collection systems should be used.
Nathaniel Atkins’s application to vacate an appellate decision based on ineffective assistance of counsel was denied because he failed to establish that claim.

The American Red Cross blood supply remains depleted after March storms canceled more than 270 blood drives nationwide, leaving over 9,500 donations uncollected. Connecticut lost 1,287 donations from 39 cancellations. The Red Cross urges donors to schedule appointments when travel is safe.

Acordis Technology & Solutions will sponsor and attend the Jewish Federation of Broward County’s Men’s Nite Out on May 9, 2018, at The Signature Grand in Davie, Florida. Featuring speaker Reggie Jackson, the event offers professionals networking, dinner and refreshments.

Early offense has three phases. **Early Push** advances the ball into the offensive area within two to four seconds, before defenders organize, creating mismatches, open space, and outnumbered situations. Coaches should explicitly teach breakaways and 2-on-1, 3-on-1, 3-on-2, and 3-on-3 attacks. Players should pass ahead, minimize dribbling, finish layups, avoid charges, block defensive pursuit, rebound misses, and retain trailer and safety coverage. Objectives progress from layups in breakaways and 2-on-1s, to creating smaller numerical advantages in 3-on-1 and 3-on-3 situations; 3-on-2 attacks generally seek an open jumper and putback.

**Early Flow** begins when transition produces no immediate shot or advantage. The offense moves directly into secondary or set actions without pulling the ball out, preventing the defense from becoming organized. Flow actions can exploit isolations and two- or three-player games and can also function as half-court offenses. Their effectiveness depends on execution and spacing.

**Continuity** maintains uninterrupted offensive movement, court balance, rebounding position, and controlled late-clock opportunities. Examples include Flex continuity, which uses baseline and down screens in “pick the picker” action; Passing Game continuity, emphasizing continuous movement, screens, penetration, and cuts; Mid Screen continuity, using a central on-ball screen for drives, pull-ups, rolls, pops, and kick-outs; Side Screen continuity, creating similar reads from wing ball screens; and the Inside Triangle Game, which relies on interior screening, wing shooting, reversals, post feeds, back screens, and skip passes.

The Commonwealth Fund ranked New Jersey’s healthcare system 25th nationally in 2018, down two places and behind all other Northeastern states. The state performed well in access to care, children’s coverage, employee-based insurance payments, and infant mortality, but needs improvement in preventive care, elderly hospital readmissions, and treatment costs.

The North Dakota Supreme Court reversed an order suppressing evidence obtained after Denise Hahne failed to stop at a sobriety checkpoint and was found intoxicated. The district court had concluded motorists lacked a safe, legal way to avoid the checkpoint. The Supreme Court held that checkpoints need not provide an avoidance route as a matter of law, though avoidability may be considered when assessing intrusion on motorists’ liberty. It remanded for determination of whether the checkpoint was constitutionally reasonable under the applicable balancing test.

The article examines how first-year architectural design education at BUU Faculty of Architecture may inform STEM education. Its framework connects STEM, project-based learning, design studios, technical drawing, reflective practice, and real-world problem solving. Architectural studios emphasize learning by doing, open-ended design problems, iterative development, visual communication, instructor criticism, and reflection in action.

Using ethnographic research, the first author observed a 30-student architectural design class over four weeks and interviewed eight volunteers. Observation notes and interviews were analyzed through coding, categorization, thematic analysis, theoretical triangulation, and comparison with related studies.

Four prominent elements of architectural design education emerged: confronting open-ended problems, deepening understanding of problem situations, gaining experience in presentation techniques, and engaging with a culture of criticism. Students researched real sites and community needs, developed drawings and models, repeatedly revised designs, and defended their decisions before instructors and juries. They reported difficulties with model-making, drawing, presentations, time, motivation, and the iterative invention process.

Through analogical inference, the study proposes six implications for STEM education: students should independently pursue open-ended problems from beginning to end; project work should receive greater curricular importance and serve as a graduation qualification at high-school and undergraduate levels; problems should be authentic, sustainable, and economically meaningful; younger students should physically engage with relevant materials and tools even without producing final products; technical drawing and graphic communication should be taught more broadly; and undergraduate STEM projects should adopt stronger practice-oriented structures, including critique and jury-based assessment.

The team maintained its game plan, stayed composed despite trailing, kept shooting, and eventually scored. Players viewed Dr. McMullen’s potential team sale as a business matter and remained focused on hockey. Facing the same player twice created some uncertainty.

The OECD warned that threatened trade barriers and persistently high oil prices could undermine global growth, investment, jobs, confidence, and household incomes. It lowered its 2018 global growth forecast to 3.8 percent, while predicting 3.9 percent in 2019.

The 13/48 strategy uses exponential moving average crossovers: a 13-period EMA crossing above the 48-period EMA signals a buy, while crossing below signals a sell. As a momentum strategy, it performs better in trending markets but may generate unreliable signals in sideways or choppy conditions. Backtesting on the S&P 500 cash index from 1960 showed 66% market exposure and a 5.1% annual return, compared with 7.2% for buy and hold, excluding reinvested dividends. Its risk-adjusted return was slightly better at 7.8%. The strategy remains vulnerable to whipsaws and lagging signals and is not a guaranteed path to profits.

Alan Brister sought refunds of amounts the IRS applied from his 1989–1992 overpayments toward liabilities arising from reversed withholding credits for 1985 and 1986. Although the 1993 adjustments occurred beyond the usual three-year limitation period, the Government argued that 26 U.S.C. § 6501(c)(1) permitted assessment at any time because Brister filed false returns intending to evade tax.

Brister had reported that Solar Roofing withheld $10,435.50 in 1985 and $5,231.42 in 1986, although those amounts were never paid to the IRS. He prepared or directed preparation of the supporting W-2 forms as a means of collecting debts he believed Solar Roofing owed him. Despite knowing the company lacked funds, lacked authorization for the withholding, and had not filed corresponding forms with payment, Brister claimed and received refunds. He later prepared amended returns removing the disputed withholding but delayed filing them and did not pay the amounts owed.

The court found by clear and convincing evidence that Brister, an accountant familiar with the relevant requirements, knowingly filed false returns. It also held that his conduct demonstrated intent to evade tax, even though the improper credits increased refunds rather than directly reducing tax otherwise payable. Therefore, § 6501(c)(1) removed the limitations bar, making the IRS’s 1993 adjustments proper. Judgment and costs were awarded to the United States.

Fiat–Shamir can be unsound in the random-oracle model when the underlying public-coin protocol has non-negligible soundness error: a cheating prover repeatedly queries the oracle until receiving a favorable challenge. Sequential repetition reduces interactive soundness error to negligible levels but remains vulnerable because the prover can preserve successful partial transcripts and extend them with constant expected overhead.

For constant-round public-coin protocols with negligible soundness error, Fiat–Shamir is sound in the random-oracle model. The proof converts a polynomial-time Fiat–Shamir adversary making at most \(q\) oracle queries into an interactive cheating prover. The prover guesses which oracle query will appear in the adversary’s accepted transcript, embeds the verifier’s challenge as that query’s response, and simulates all other oracle answers randomly. For a three-message protocol, this loses roughly a factor of \(q\); with \(c\) verifier messages, the loss is roughly \(q^c\). Thus constant rounds preserve non-negligible cheating probability and yield a contradiction. More rounds may still work under stronger soundness guarantees or round-by-round soundness, as with GKR.

This theorem establishes random-oracle soundness for the constant-round, negligible-error Kilian–Micali protocol. However, random-oracle security does not guarantee security under any explicit hash-function family. The random-oracle model is therefore a sanity check rather than a standard-model proof, though the lecture notes that practical failures generally arise from implementation issues rather than the model itself.

Sequential repetition of the Hamiltonian-cycle protocol remains zero knowledge because its transcripts can be simulated one round at a time. Parallel repetition is different: a malicious verifier may choose all challenges jointly as a function of all commitments, preventing separate simulation. A 2019 result showed that this specific parallel protocol is not zero knowledge by proving Fiat–Shamir soundness for it under a cryptographic assumption. If a simulator existed, choosing the verifier’s challenges through the sound Fiat–Shamir hash would let the simulator produce an accepting transcript for some false statement, contradicting soundness. More generally, an interactive proof for which Fiat–Shamir is sound cannot be zero knowledge against that Fiat–Shamir-based verifier.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K on August 3, 2017, announcing early adoption, effective July 1, 2017, of new FASB standards for revenue recognition and leases. Beginning with the quarter ending September 30, 2017, financial information would reflect the standards with prior periods adjusted.

The revenue standard, adopted retrospectively, materially affected income statements and balance sheets but not cash flows. Key changes include recognizing most Windows 10 revenue upon billing and delivery and certain commercial software license revenue at contract execution. Accounting for hardware, Office 365, LinkedIn, and professional services remained substantially unchanged.

The lease standard materially affected balance sheets through recognition of operating-lease right-of-use assets and liabilities but did not materially affect income statements or cash flows. Restated fiscal 2016 and 2017 financial information was provided in Exhibit 99.1.

This qualitative case study examined faculty and student views on how distance education affects equality of educational opportunity. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 21 faculty members and 26 students who had experienced distance education, and responses were analyzed through content analysis.

Participants identified flexible learning pace, freedom from time and place limitations, free access to courses, easier access to information, and varied resources as contributions to equality. Reported inequalities included limited financial means, inadequate technology and internet access, unsuitable learning environments, differing digital competencies, and increased achievement gaps among students.

Suggested improvements included assessing learner characteristics, expanding access to technology, strengthening internet infrastructure, improving digital literacy, allocating public funding for technological access, and providing students with greater faculty guidance. The study concludes that distance education can both reduce and reinforce educational inequality depending on learners’ resources, competencies, and access to infrastructure.

Artificial intelligence is reshaping higher education through personalized learning, intelligent tutoring, predictive analytics, automated assessment, research support, administrative services, and improved accessibility. Adoption is growing rapidly: 86% of surveyed students use AI academically, although implementation varies by region because of differences in infrastructure, funding, expertise, and policy readiness.

Institutions are responding through faculty training, AI-related curricula, literacy programs, ethical guidelines, and government frameworks. Examples include Squirrel AI’s adaptive learning in China, Arizona State University’s predictive analytics, and Australian AI-literacy initiatives. However, only 20% of surveyed universities meet student expectations for AI integration.

AI can tailor instruction, identify at-risk students, provide immediate feedback, automate routine work, analyze large research datasets, support round-the-clock student services, and enable international collaboration through translation. It also supports simulations, creative production, career preparation, peer learning, lifelong education, and accommodations for learners with disabilities or neurodiverse needs. Applications span performing arts, sciences, medicine, business, and liberal arts.

Tools have differing strengths: ChatGPT supports writing and brainstorming; Bard emphasizes real-time research and data; and Gemini uses emotional cues for counseling, psychology, communication, and creative work. Combining tools can provide discipline-specific educational experiences.

Major risks include academic dishonesty, inaccurate or biased outputs, privacy and security concerns, unclear authorship, faculty resistance, overdependence on AI, and unequal access. Biased algorithms may reinforce inequalities, while limited infrastructure can widen the digital divide. AI-based emotional support may also weaken independent decision-making and interpersonal skills if students become reliant on it.

The paper recommends treating AI as a complement rather than a replacement for educators. Institutions should expand faculty training, student participation, infrastructure investment, interdisciplinary research, and international cooperation. They should also establish transparent policies addressing academic integrity, consent, data protection, algorithmic fairness, and accountability. Future developments may include emotional-recognition systems, immersive virtual and augmented reality, and real-time translation, but equitable and responsible adoption requires collaboration among educators, policymakers, technologists, students, and industry.

Entanglement is defined as a non-factorizable state of two physically distinct subsystems that can be separately addressed, manipulated, and measured. A single photon distributed between two modes may represent entangled modes but not entanglement as a usable resource. Photons are well suited for entanglement because they can be separated, while bound electrons in helium cannot be independently accessed. Standard maximally entangled two-qubit states are the four Bell states.

Entangled states exhibit non-local correlations and are fragile against decoherence. Their degree of entanglement can be measured by tracing out one subsystem and calculating the von Neumann entropy of the resulting reduced density matrix. Bell states yield a completely mixed reduced state with entropy one, while factorized pure states yield zero entropy.

Entanglement purification probabilistically converts multiple copies of a weakly entangled pure state into Bell states. Alice and Bob apply controlled-NOT operations to paired copies and measure target qubits; a specified outcome leaves the remaining qubits maximally entangled. The optimal success probability corresponds to the entanglement measured through reduced-state entropy. Producing many identical prepared states does not violate the no-cloning theorem, which prohibits copying an unknown arbitrary state.

For atoms, one proposed approach is photodissociation of a suitable diatomic molecule into two spin-entangled atoms. Another probabilistic method uses photons emitted by separate atoms. The photons are mixed at a beam splitter so their origins cannot be determined. Hong-Ou-Mandel interference ensures identical photons leave together, whereas detections at both outputs indicate distinguishable polarizations. Combined with polarization manipulation, such measurements can project the atoms into an entangled state.

Chris Lattner, creator of Apple’s Swift language and former leader of Tesla’s Autopilot program, joined Google Brain. His experience and following could support Google’s push to attract AI talent and use artificial intelligence and machine learning to strengthen its cloud division against Amazon Web Services.

Commissioner.COM’s Nov. 25, 2001 fantasy football report includes promotional offers, NFL injury updates, Week 11 lineup recommendations, and the Luccis Losers–Team Chick matchup. Key updates: Muhsin Muhammad and Reggie Wayne were expected to miss games; Warrick Dunn and Mark Brunell were expected to start; Olandis Gary was out for the season; Terrell Davis targeted a Dec. 2 return; and Az-Zahir Hakim was questionable. Recommended starts included James Allen, Rod Smith, Marshall Faulk, Kurt Warner, Marvin Harrison, Corey Dillon, and Ahman Green. The featured matchup showed both teams at 0.0 points.

The paper develops quasi-Monte Carlo methods for uncertainty quantification in a nonlinear tumor-growth model governed by a semi-linear parabolic reaction-diffusion PDE. Diffusion and proliferation coefficients are modeled as random fields, while treatment effects represent chemotherapy and radiotherapy. The authors establish well-posedness and parameter-dependent bounds for general random fields, derive novel parametric regularity bounds for uniform random fields, and prove QMC error estimates. The analysis exploits the fact that solutions remain between zero and one when the initial tumor fraction does, addressing difficulties caused by the non-monotone logistic term and time dependence. Numerical experiments confirm the theory and include a realistic log-normal test case on a complex brain domain. Spatial and temporal discretization errors are not analyzed.

Scotty must decide how long to continue coaching given the family sacrifices involved, though he is expected back next year. His exceptional passion, energy, and constant engagement with hockey explain his success.

In May 2007, Deputy Mayor for Education Victor Reinoso had to recommend a chancellor to lead Washington, DC Public Schools as Mayor Adrian Fenty prepared to assume control of the system. DCPS had 55,000 students and 150 schools, with half failing federal standards despite high per-student spending. The district suffered from administrative bloat, patronage, underinvestment in instruction, deteriorating facilities, declining enrollment, and frequent leadership turnover.

Reinoso, an MBA and former consultant, joined the school board in 2004 after observing dissatisfaction with neighborhood schools. He campaigned on data-driven management, measurable outcomes, and facilities improvements. On the board, he became frustrated by consensus-driven decision-making, particularly Superintendent Clifford Janey’s decision to recommend closing six schools after indicating that 20 needed closure. Reinoso concluded that mayoral control offered a faster route to reform.

After Fenty’s November 2006 election, Reinoso became deputy mayor for education. He assembled a flat, project-oriented team, commissioned the Parthenon Group to assess DCPS, and helped draft takeover legislation. Parthenon found DCPS ranked last among 11 reviewed districts in fourth- and eighth-grade reading and math achievement. It identified persistent problems involving accountability, teaching quality, management, special education, facilities, and community responsiveness.

The DC Public Education Reform Act, passed in April 2007, made DCPS subordinate to the mayor, assigned daily management to a mayor-appointed chancellor, reduced the school board’s authority, shifted facilities management outside DCPS, separated state and local education responsibilities, and coordinated child services across agencies. The administration was required to demonstrate results within five years.

Reinoso sought a courageous, entrepreneurial chancellor willing to rethink public education, reject incremental reform, focus on teaching and student achievement, and maintain high expectations. Candidates included Rudy Crew, an experienced superintendent with a record of aggressive reforms in New York and Miami; Michelle Rhee, founder of The New Teacher Project, who emphasized teacher quality and criticized union staffing rules but had little teaching experience and no school-administration background; and incumbent Clifford Janey, an experienced educator with ambitious plans but a cautious approach.

Shortly before the recommendation deadline, Reinoso faced criticism for using unattributed material from another district’s education plan. Setting the controversy aside, he had to choose a leader capable of disrupting DCPS without destabilizing it.

Mesh is a short-to-intermediate Air Raid passing concept widely used across football. It creates natural picks and confusion, enabling receivers to keep moving against man coverage or settle into open areas against zone. It offers answers against Cover 2, 3, and 4 but can struggle against zone blitzes or simulated pressures that challenge five-man protection and require quick decisions.

The base design uses shallow and deep drag routes, backfield arrow and flare routes, and a corner route. Against man, drag runners stay moving; against zone, they settle in coverage voids. The quarterback may select the corner route pre-snap based on space or matchup, then progresses from flare to shallow drag, deep drag, and fullback arrow regardless of the defensive look. Because five eligible receivers release, the quarterback must anticipate pressure and deliver quickly.

Popular variations include “mesh rail,” which makes the running back’s vertical rail route the primary option and adds a sit route, and another variation emphasizing an 8–10-yard sit route as a stationary zone target. Against man, the sit runner instead helps create natural picks. Mesh can also be adapted to formations such as the single wing and combined with smash principles.

Channel 4 chief executive Alex Mahon called the broadcaster’s 28.6% gender pay gap “unacceptable” and pledged improvement. Although women comprise 59% of staff, they hold only 34 of the 100 highest-paid positions, while the organisation’s lower half is 66% female. Mahon aims for a 50:50 gender split in the top 100 jobs by 2023. Channel 4’s gap exceeds the 17.4% national average, ITN’s 19.6%, and the BBC’s 10.7%. Gender pay inequality has faced increased scrutiny following disclosures of BBC salaries and Carrie Gracie’s resignation.

Culp reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2017 sales of $77.4 million, essentially unchanged year over year. Pretax income declined 2.3% to $7 million, including about $250,000 in plant relocation costs, while net income rose to $6.2 million, or $0.49 per diluted share, aided by a lower tax rate.

Full-year sales declined 1.1% to $309.5 million, but pretax income reached a company record of $29.7 million. Net income increased to $22.3 million, or $1.78 per diluted share, and adjusted EBITDA rose 7% to $40.1 million. Operating cash flow increased to $33 million and free cash flow to $18 million. Culp ended the year with $54.2 million in cash and investments and no outstanding credit-line balance. The board approved a special dividend of $0.21 per share.

Mattress fabric annual sales rose 2.4% to a record $190.8 million, while operating income increased 11% to a record $29.4 million. Culp invested approximately $38 million in this segment over three years. North Carolina expansion and consolidation projects were substantially complete, with anticipated annual savings of about $1 million beginning in the second half of fiscal 2018. The company also expanded Canadian operations, planned to relocate mattress-cover production in North Carolina, and expected its Haiti joint venture facility to begin operating during the second quarter.

Upholstery fabric annual sales fell 6% to $118.7 million amid weak residential furniture demand, while operating income remained near the prior year at $11.1 million. Favorable Chinese currency movements and stronger hospitality and performance-fabric margins supported results. China-produced fabrics represented 92% of upholstery sales, and hospitality accounted for about 10%. Culp is exploring hospitality acquisitions and said it was cautiously optimistic about completing one or possibly two during fiscal 2018.

Mattress-industry disruption, particularly changes involving Mattress Firm and SSB, was expected to pressure near-term demand. For the first quarter of fiscal 2018, Culp projected overall sales comparable to the prior year, slightly lower mattress fabric sales and operating income, and slightly higher upholstery sales and operating income. Pretax income was forecast at $7.8 million to $8.4 million, including approximately $300,000 in relocation expenses. Management expected operating results to improve in the second half as restructuring benefits emerged, with fiscal 2018 capital spending comparable to fiscal 2017 and another solid year of free cash flow.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that on February 26, 2020, it issued a press release updating revenue guidance for its More Personal Computing segment for the quarter ending March 30, 2020. The press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Exchange Act.

A 34-year-old Mission man was arrested after allegedly driving recklessly and causing multiple collisions at a Maple Ridge strip mall, injuring a woman and her son. He faces impaired driving, hit-and-run and dangerous driving causing bodily harm charges and was released pending a court appearance.
The speaker was disappointed not to score initially but believed he was playing well otherwise. He stayed positive, kept working, and prioritized winning over personal scoring.

CTPNet is a framework for multivariate long-term time-series forecasting that jointly models inter-channel, intra-subsequence, and inter-subsequence dependencies. Channel-wise representation learning uses temporal-query multi-head attention; downsampling divides residual-enhanced inputs into periodic subsequences; an encoder maps them into a hidden space; and efficient Transformer-based trend-wise and periodic-wise modules capture local trend structures and global periodic dynamics. A decoder and inverse downsampling reconstruct the forecast.

The forecasting task predicts the next \(L_{out}\) time steps from \(L_{in}\) historical observations while minimizing error against target values. Downsampling uses the smallest inherent period to preserve temporal information, whereas temporal queries may use longer periods to capture long-range variation; both can be selected using autocorrelation. Experiments across multiple benchmark datasets and prediction horizons report state-of-the-art performance, with CTPNet recording 54 first-place results in the presented comparison.

The document standardizes the 4 KB decrypted Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) used by SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests to selectively share register state with hypervisors during Non-Automatic Exits. It defines protocol negotiation, feature advertisement, GHCB registration, VMGEXIT handling, required state, error reporting, secrets-page fields, and EFI communication of SNP secrets and CPUID pages.

Version 2 adds SEV-SNP support and optional feature advertisement. Later revisions add 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, enhanced error reporting, APIC ID retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, SEV-ES page-state changes, trusted I/O, Secure AVIC, and GHCB unregistration. Defined operations include CPUID exchange, page-state changes, SNP guest and certificate requests, AP creation, doorbell registration, IPIs, timers, VMPL switching, termination, and TIO requests.

The specification covers GHCB negotiation and usage, MMIO and MSR exits, SMP booting, AP reset and jump tables, NMI handling, debug registers, and restricted interrupt injection through a shared #HV doorbell page modeled on APIC behavior. SEV-SNP GHCB addresses must be registered per vCPU, with optional per-VMPL registration. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported. Restricted Injection requires host notifications through #HV, with defined pending-event, EOI, HLT, host, and guest behavior.

The technology improves sealing in high-pressure flow devices handling corrosive or abrasive fluids, including plug valves and hydraulic-fracturing fluid ends. Conventional designs mount seals on replaceable components so they contact the device body, causing body erosion, leakage, costly repairs, and downtime.

The disclosed design instead mounts seals or springs in grooves or recesses formed in the body, with the seals extending against mating components such as valve inserts, retaining nuts, plugs, valve seats, stuffing-box sleeves, flanges, or manifolds. This transfers erosion from the body to components that are less complex and less expensive to repair, resurface, coat, or replace. Disposable liners and erosion-resistant treatments may further extend service life.

Fluid-end embodiments include intersecting conduits connecting an internal chamber to external surfaces, concentric endless grooves or recessed corners for radial, axial, or crush seals, a reciprocating plunger, and a stuffing-box sleeve overlying a sealing recess. A breather opening may vent trapped air during sleeve installation. The principles may also be applied to other high-pressure flow devices and closure configurations.

From April 1, Scotland will criminalize disclosing or threatening to disclose private intimate images without consent, with penalties of up to five years’ imprisonment. The law addresses growing online sharing enabled by smartphones and social media and forms part of wider efforts to combat abuse, harassment and sexual violence.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver said the 2026 All-Star Game will remain at the Clippers’ Intuit Dome despite an investigation into whether the team circumvented salary-cap rules involving Kawhi Leonard’s $28 million endorsement deal with Aspiration. Clippers owner Steve Ballmer invested $50 million in Aspiration, which partnered with the team. Potential penalties include fines, voided contracts and lost draft picks. The Feb. 15 game is expected to feature a new U.S.-versus-international format.

Matthew Shashy, 29, received four years’ probation after a federal jury convicted him of interfering with Maxwell Air Force Base personnel. In January 2017, he fired three shotgun rounds toward a base entrance after spray-painting anti-government graffiti. He fled, later barricaded himself at home, and eventually surrendered. Authorities found firearms, ammunition, anti-government literature, and evidence linking him to the shooting.

The Louisiana Supreme Court affirmed Ray Jones Jr.’s first-degree murder conviction and life sentence without probation, parole, or suspension for killing his infant son.

Jones challenged the admission of three inculpatory statements and a restriction on cross-examination. The court found his hospital statements voluntary, unsolicited, and not products of police interrogation, so Miranda warnings were unnecessary. It also held that his police-station confession, made after requesting counsel, was not elicited through interrogation because the detective’s remarks about the baby being in heaven were consolatory rather than reasonably likely to provoke an incriminating response. Jones had voluntarily changed his mind and confessed. Even if that statement was improperly admitted, the error was harmless beyond a reasonable doubt because earlier statements and other evidence overwhelmingly established guilt.

The trial court also properly excluded a hypothetical question to Jones’s psychiatrist about potentially inaccurate family information because no evidence showed that such information had been supplied, making the question irrelevant. Both assignments of error lacked merit.

A mobile agricultural machine actively maps ground terrain using a pose sensor that periodically determines geographic position and orientation. Machine dimensions and sensor pose are used to define a virtual point cloud, attached to the machine, whose points estimate the ground surface beneath and around it. Elevation values are generated for the points and correlated with cells in a georeferenced map.

Each elevation estimate receives a confidence weight based on its distance from the pose sensor. As the machine moves, repeated estimates for each map cell are aggregated, allowing nearer, higher-confidence measurements to refine earlier estimates. Map layers may store average elevation, confidence, sample count, and elevation variance. The point cloud’s resolution, dimensions, and offset may be configured, including extension ahead of or beside the machine to support future passes.

The resulting terrain data can predict ground elevation ahead of the machine and generate control signals for subsystems such as harvester header height, sprayer boom height, propulsion, steering, crop-volume estimation, communications, and operator interfaces. Maps may be stored, shared with remote systems, merged with prior maps, and implemented through local, mobile, networked, or remote-server computing architectures.

A NIAID-funded Phase 2 trial found that adding 16 weeks of omalizumab to oral immunotherapy improved desensitization in children with multiple food allergies. Of 48 participants aged 4–15, 83% receiving omalizumab could consume at least two grams of two or more allergenic foods after 36 weeks, compared with 33% receiving placebo. The omalizumab group also experienced fewer adverse events during early treatment. The findings suggest omalizumab may safely accelerate desensitization, but larger studies are needed.

Generative AI challenges traditional higher education assessments by producing sophisticated text, answering multiple-choice questions, and evading unreliable detection tools. It also offers opportunities for personalized feedback, authentic assessment, and development of critical thinking, problem-solving, and workplace-relevant AI literacy. Institutions can mitigate AI use through invigilated, practical, oral, or live assessments, or integrate it through activities such as critiquing AI output, generating cases, debating with AI, and comparing human and AI content.

A UK postgraduate immunology course redesigned a traditional essay assessment to include ChatGPT-generated outlines, training in AI use and academic integrity, peer evaluation, and subsequent independent essay writing. Among 20 surveyed students, 57.9% had used generative AI, only 5% were very confident using it, and 30% would use it in their studies. Students valued AI for planning, drafting, summarizing, research, revision, and proofreading but identified problems with accuracy, outdated information, unverifiable sources, superficiality, and limited critical thinking. Only 26% considered using AI in assessments plagiarism, while 37% disagreed and 37% were unsure. Students found AI-generated outlines useful starting points but generic and insufficiently detailed.

The case study indicated that integrating AI supported learning about its capabilities and limitations. The paper recommends holistic integration rather than replacing traditional assessment or educators, alongside training for students and staff, transparent and ethical AI use, and redesigned assessments emphasizing higher-order cognition, authenticity, diversity, and academic integrity.

Brookfield Infrastructure Partners has delivered 20% annualized returns since 2008, with adjusted AFFO rising from $352 million in 2012 to $926 million. It currently yields 4% versus a 5.84% AFFO yield, retaining cash for growth while also issuing units. Brookfield targets 6–9% annual distribution growth through same-store growth, reinvestment, and asset rotation, though currency effects, low inflation, and future crises may challenge this target. The elevated unit price enables accretive capital issuance but makes growth dependent on market valuation. Despite likely lower future returns, the author considers BIP’s distribution safe and expects roughly 6% growth, supporting an estimated 10% total return.

Credit bureaus began by tracking borrowers for lenders. Today, companies such as Equifax collect extensive financial data without consumers opting in, making disengagement difficult, while lawmakers have struggled for decades to regulate the industry.

Archaeologists failed to find an Easter Rising rifle believed to have been dropped beside Dublin City Hall by Irish Citizen Army rebel Willie Halpin while evading British soldiers. The Dublin City Council-funded excavation uncovered roof fragments, including one with a bullet hole, milk bottles, pottery and other debris. Archaeologist Franc Myles suggested the rifle was likely recovered during inspections in the years after the Rising. Lord Mayor Nial Ring, who supported the search with Halpin’s family, said the investigation was worthwhile despite the disappointment.

This study examined Mauritian education and industry leaders’ understanding of micro-credentials, their integration into higher education credit systems, and their professional value. Micro-credentials certify competencies gained through focused learning experiences and may support upskilling, reskilling, lifelong learning, employability, and alignment between education and workplace needs. However, their adoption faces barriers including inconsistent definitions, limited leadership knowledge, uncertain employer recognition, assessment reliability, and difficulties mapping them to formal qualifications.

Researchers conducted semi-structured interviews with ten leaders from public and private higher education institutions and four industry leaders in Mauritius. Participants generally understood micro-credentials as short, competency-based learning units requiring formal assessment, although views differed regarding their relationship to badges, attendance certificates, and formal qualifications.

Most participants supported a flexible hybrid model linking micro-credentials to existing academic credits while allowing separate use for continuing professional development. They believed micro-credentials could provide personalised learning paths and respond rapidly to industry skill demands, with information technology suggested as a possible starting area. Nevertheless, participants favoured phased implementation, experimentation, and quality assurance because recognition remains uncertain and rapid integration could disrupt existing systems.

Education and industry leaders generally regarded micro-credentials as an important, though not necessarily dominant, part of higher education’s future. They stressed that credentials must be verifiable, competency-focused, assessed reliably, and comparable across institutions. Employer acceptance would also require job requirements to shift from conventional degrees and diplomas toward competency profiles.

The study recommends integrating micro-credentials into an adaptable national qualifications framework through recognised learning pathways, university credit mapping, reliable assessment, and quality standards. A unified framework should allow micro-credentials to accumulate toward recognised qualifications while accommodating different fields and levels. Collaboration among institutions, regulators, and employers is considered essential for academic recognition, industry acceptance, employment, and career development.

Vanguard Mid-Cap Growth ETF’s holdings imply a $145.80 target price, representing 9.77% upside from $132.83. Notable holdings include Sensata Technologies, with 11.37% projected upside; Global Payments, 10.34%; and Markel, 10.26%. The passage cautions that high targets may reflect optimism or outdated assumptions and require further investor research.

John Knight left $5.25 million to LHSC’s ovarian cancer research team in tribute to his wife, Mary, who died from the disease in 2008. The donation will fund specialized researchers, equipment and international collaborations focused on understanding ovarian cancer growth and metastasis, particularly given the lack of early screening tools. Victoria Hospital named its A-block first-floor lobby the Mary and John Knight atrium in recognition of the gift.

Former Facebook executive Chamath Palihapitiya expressed guilt over helping build tools he says damage social cohesion through addictive feedback loops, misinformation, and reduced cooperation. Sean Parker similarly warned of social media’s effects on relationships, productivity, and children. Despite concerns, Palihapitiya believes Facebook does substantial good and funds structural reforms.

GPT-5’s launch faced livestream glitches, inaccurate charts, complaints about its unfriendly behavior, and criticism that it failed to meet OpenAI’s heightened expectations despite improved performance.

Tanzania launched the Tanzania Business Clinic to accelerate improvements to the business climate by offering companies and sectors expert guidance on challenges, policies and regulations. Headquartered in Dar es Salaam, it will operate through Small Industries Development Organisation offices nationwide. The initiative supports a regulatory reform blueprint scheduled for implementation in 2018/19, including proposed amendments to tax, import, immigration, labour, social security and environmental laws. The reforms follow Tanzania’s ranking of 137th among 190 economies in the World Bank’s Doing Business 2018 report. The government aims to attract private investment, change regulators’ attitudes, promote local raw-material processing, create jobs and develop industries including textiles, pharmaceuticals and cooking oil.

Soccer players use hand signals, gestures, eye contact, head movements, and ball actions to communicate during play. Signals can initiate set pieces, corners, free kicks, and throw-ins; request passes, runs, substitutions, or specific ball placement; organize defensive walls and coverage; direct teammates upfield; and identify planned tactics such as corner types or offside traps. Teams and coaches may establish customized signals, especially when crowd noise makes verbal communication difficult.

On May 24, 1870, President Ulysses S. Grant warned against illegal military expeditions from U.S. territory against Canada. Participants would lose government protection, and federal officers were ordered to prevent the expeditions and arrest those involved.
Eleven-year-old Damian Sunderland suffered life-threatening facial injuries in a relative’s dog attack. He faces months of reconstructive surgery, including skin grafts and lip recreation.

Julia Banks, who won the multicultural Melbourne seat of Chisholm for the Liberals in 2016, faced questions over possible dual Greek-Australian citizenship. Many local voters were initially unaware, while several said they would consider candidates on merit or continue supporting the Liberals in a potential byelection. Monash University lecturer Zareh Ghazarian said a byelection would likely favour Labor in the marginal seat, which Banks won by 2,154 votes after a 2.84 per cent swing, ending almost 20 years of Labor control. Labor expressed confidence it could regain Chisholm in a tight contest, potentially campaigning on housing affordability, mortgage stress and renter security. More candidates could increase voting volatility.

VentureWire’s May 22, 2001 issue reports that Kodiak Venture Partners closed a $290 million early-stage fund; Mercury Interactive acquired Freshwater Software for $147 million; Celetron raised $48 million; and TVM held a €70 million first close for a life sciences fund targeting $219 million.

Numerous companies announced financing, including Lawson Software with $40 million, NuVasive with $29.3 million, SeeCommerce with $27.4 million, NetContinuum with $26 million, FlightTime and MiFund with $25 million each, and ViAir and Cambridge Broadband with $15 million each.

AgWeb cut 36% of its staff, Ironmax cut about 30%, and Rx.com ceased daily operations and prescription fulfillment. Realm Connect adopted a new name, while Nextira Federal launched operations. Acquisitions included Blink.com buying BookmarksPlus, Everstream acquiring The MusicBooth for $10 million in stock, Primus acquiring AnswerLogic for approximately $3 million in stock, and MindArrow agreeing to buy Control Commerce.

The issue also covers board and executive appointments, a University of Pittsburgh–Redleaf technology funding program, venture-capital personnel changes, and corrections concerning Broadview Capital Partners and Porivo Technologies.

Poor document management can cost businesses time, money and customers through inaccessible files, inefficient paper storage and printing, wasted supplies, and exposure of sensitive information. Although 40% of business processes remain document-driven, a Xerox survey found that improving document management can enhance workflow, productivity and business growth. Businesses should begin by tracking printing costs. Cloud-enabled printers and multifunction printers can scan, share and print documents through cloud services, email and business applications, while customized workflows support mobile access and multiple destinations. Printer controls can require PINs, track usage, restrict colour printing and protect confidential documents. Automatic toner alerts can also prevent shortages and unnecessary purchases.

This qualitative study examined the effectiveness of distance-mode Physical Education teacher training at North-West University, South Africa. Data came from open-ended questionnaires completed by 17 third-year education students and semi-structured interviews with four lecturers.

Participants generally reported accessible, professional lecturers whose enthusiasm strengthened students’ knowledge, confidence, and motivation. Course content also improved students’ perceptions of Physical Education and its role in learners’ holistic development. Videos supported practical learning by demonstrating movements repeatedly, but insufficient video guidance, lack of physical contact, and delayed feedback limited skills development.

Additional obstacles included students’ limited foundational knowledge, technological skills, and internet access, as well as administrative delays and errors involving assignments. Recommendations include more face-to-face contact, technological training, greater use of videos and other practical media, improved online interaction, and stronger university administration and management systems.

U.S. passports certify citizenship and may be issued only to citizens, but issuance is discretionary; denial does not itself negate citizenship. Applicants must establish citizenship, U.S. domicile, and a genuine intention to return and fulfill civic duties. Expatriation involves abandoning allegiance to become a permanent resident and citizen elsewhere and is determined from each case’s circumstances. Even without established expatriation, permanent foreign residents are ineligible. Prolonged residence abroad creates a presumption of intent to remain, especially when applicants sever U.S. ties, establish foreign homes and careers, or fail to honor stated plans to return. Continuing family or property ties, health or financial obstacles, and work advancing legitimate American enterprises may favor issuance. Americans living in countries where the United States exercises extraterritorial jurisdiction may receive continuing passport protection if their activities are legitimate and do not harm diplomatic relations. The Department also recognized inherited U.S. citizenship rights within certain American communities in Turkey operating under extraterritorial privileges.

Mud Bay, a Pacific Northwest pet-store chain founded by Elsa Wulff in 1988 and later led by her children Lars and Marisa, differentiated itself through natural dog and cat products, knowledgeable staff, consultative service, low everyday prices, and a mission centered on animal health, customer happiness, and company strength.

By 2014, Mud Bay had strong sales but low margins and 48% employee turnover. Its leadership launched a “Good Jobs Vision” aimed at making employees—known as Muddies—better paid, trained, empowered, and invested in the company while improving productivity and customer experience. The five-part strategy called for investing in staff; offering fewer products at lower prices; standardizing processes and fostering continuous improvement; cross-training and operating with staffing slack; and partnering with animal-welfare organizations.

From 2014 to 2017, Mud Bay raised average hourly store wages from $12.12 to $15.06, increased the share of employees working at least 30 hours from 69% to 82%, improved health benefits, introduced an Employee Stock Ownership Plan and assistance program, and expanded training and leadership development. It reduced its assortment, created employee-heavy category teams, lowered prices, standardized some delivery and operational processes, combined store-lead roles, and expanded animal-welfare activities.

Progress was uneven. Mud Bay struggled to standardize inventory, hiring, staffing, and scheduling; establish a formal continuous-improvement system; create sufficient slack; and execute all planned initiatives. Although employees retained broad authority to help customers, much operational improvement remained directed from the home office.

Between 2014 and 2017, sales grew 70%, comparable-store growth averaged above 9%, sales per labor hour increased, employee turnover fell to 31%, and employees acquired 4.8% ownership. Customer reviews remained highly favorable, and Mud Bay’s prices averaged about 7% below PetSmart and Petco by 2018. However, lower prices, higher compensation and benefits, home-office growth, and new stores reduced margins; net profit margin declined from 2.18% in 2014 to 1.99% in 2017.

While preparing the 2018 budget, COO Tracy Yamane proposed closing stores at 8:00 p.m. instead of 9:00 p.m. Monday through Saturday. She argued this would improve employees’ quality of life, eliminate short turnarounds between closing and opening shifts, increase midday staffing overlap, and save labor during slow evening periods. Marisa supported the proposal, but Lars worried about customer inconvenience and lost sales. The planning team reviewed store sales by half-hour before deciding.

A phase 2/3 observer-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled Indian study evaluated two doses of SII-NVX-CoV2373 in 920 children aged 2–17 years. Participants were assigned 3:1 to vaccine or placebo, with safety monitored through 180 days and immune responses compared with vaccinated Indian adults.

Fourteen days after dose two, anti-spike IgG and neutralizing antibody responses in both pediatric age groups were non-inferior to adult responses and were higher in younger participants. Seroconversion exceeded 98%, and antibody levels remained substantially above baseline at day 180, although they had declined. The vaccine also generated responses against Delta, Omicron BA.1, and Omicron BA.5 variants.

Solicited reactions, mainly injection-site pain, tenderness, headache, fatigue, and fever, were more frequent with the vaccine than placebo. Almost all adverse events were mild, began within one day, lasted one to two days, and resolved without sequelae. Two serious adverse events occurred among vaccinated adolescents, but neither was considered vaccine-related. No adverse events of special interest were reported.

The study did not assess vaccine efficacy and excluded participants with known previous COVID-19, but the authors concluded that SII-NVX-CoV2373 was safe, well tolerated, and highly immunogenic in children aged 2–17 years. The study was funded by Serum Institute of India; several authors were employees of the vaccine manufacturer, Novavax, or 360biolabs.

The passage specifies SD card interfaces, initialization, commands, transfer modes, protection, and performance features. UHS-I operates only in SD mode, normally uses 1.8V signaling and 4-bit transfers, and requires host/card agreement through ACMD41 followed by CMD11 voltage switching. CMD6 selects bus speed, driver strength, and power limits; CMD19 supports sampling-point tuning. Returning from 1.8V signaling to 3.3V or SPI requires a power cycle.

UHS-II hosts support both legacy SD and UHS-II interfaces. After power-up, lane signaling determines whether initialization proceeds through UHS-II or falls back to SD. UHS-II initialization comprises PHY initialization, device initialization, enumeration, configuration, and SD-TRAN initialization. Defined modes include FD156, optional HD312, FD312, and FD624; FD624 reaches 624 MB/s. Application performance classes, caching, self-maintenance, command queuing, and low-voltage initialization are also described.

SD initialization begins with CMD0, followed by CMD8 to verify interface conditions and ACMD41 to establish voltage, capacity support, and readiness. CMD8 is mandatory before ACMD41 for SDHC and SDXC cards. After initialization, CMD2 retrieves identification and CMD3 establishes the relative card address. Cards then move from identification mode to data-transfer mode, where CMD7 selects one card.

Read and write operations use block transfers with CRC protection. CMD12 stops multi-block transfers. Multiple-block writes are preferred for speed, and ACMD23 may pre-erase blocks. Erase, DISCARD, and Full User Area Logical Erase use CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38 sequences. DISCARD and FULE apply only to SDHC and SDXC cards and are unavailable through SPI.

Write protection includes a host-managed mechanical switch, optional internal protection, and password locking through CMD42. Card Ownership Protection adds a Force Erase Password, COP unlocking, protected force erase, and restrictions on clearing passwords. Locked cards accept only specified commands, and ACMD6 cannot change bus width until the card is unlocked.

CMD55 marks the following command as application-specific. CMD6 checks or switches function groups, including access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. Mode 0 queries capabilities; Mode 1 changes functions. Function changes normally take effect within eight clocks, while invalid selections cause no change.

A city court reserved until tomorrow its order on Shashi Tharoor’s anticipatory bail plea in Sunanda Pushkar’s death case. Delhi Police argued he might flee, influence witnesses or harm the investigation, while his lawyers cited his cooperation and the completed probe. Summoned to appear July 7, Tharoor is the sole accused, charged with cruelty and abetment of suicide, but has not been arrested.

ITV cycling presenter Matt Barbet’s Home Roads podcast launches on iTunes and Acast on June 8. Barbet rides guests’ familiar local routes while discussing their cycling careers and personal lives. Initial episodes feature Alex Dowsett, Sarah Storey, Nicolas Roche and David Millar, with later guests including Ben Saunders, Simon Warren, Simon Mottram and Philippa York.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell architecture introduces the AI Management Processor (AMP), a programmable RISC-V GPU context scheduler that reduces CPU dependency, latency, and scheduling overhead. Compatible with Windows Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling, AMP coordinates concurrent AI and graphics workloads, improves frame consistency, prioritizes game-engine work, and reduces response times for language models.

Blackwell adds hardware encoding and decoding for 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC video. The ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality by 5% BD-BR PSNR and includes an AV1 Ultra High Quality mode offering another 5% improvement. RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders, enabling exports over 50% faster than the prior generation and four times faster than RTX 3090. Sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed. DisplayPort 2.1b with UHBR 20 provides up to 80 Gbps and supports 8K at 165 Hz or 4K at 480 Hz using display stream compression.

Max-Q improvements include finer clock, power, and voltage-rail gating; independent GPU-core and memory power control; and full memory-clock-tree gating. Accelerated frequency switching adjusts clocks 1,000 times faster than previous architectures. Blackwell enters its deepest sleep state ten times faster than Ada, contributing to power savings of up to 50% in a small-language-model inference example.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, which can generate three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame. Its frame-generation model is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and runs once per rendered frame. Enhanced Flip Metering moves frame pacing to the display engine. Transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA use twice as many parameters as prior CNN models, improving temporal stability, motion detail, anti-aliasing, lighting, and reducing ghosting and denoising artifacts.

Blackwell enables developer-created neural shaders by exposing Tensor Cores through Cooperative Vectors APIs for DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Applications include neural materials, texture compression, radiance caching, subsurface scattering through RTX Skin, and generative facial rendering through RTX Neural Faces. Neural Texture Compression can provide up to 7:1 VRAM compression over block-compressed formats; one demonstration reduced material memory from 1,110 MB to 333 MB. Neural Radiance Cache infers multi-bounce indirect illumination from limited path-traced rays.

The flagship GB202 GPU contains 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, and a 512-bit memory interface, and powers the RTX 5090. GB203 contains 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA cores, and a 256-bit interface, supporting RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 contains 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA cores, and a 192-bit interface for RTX 5070. NVIDIA states that specifications may change and disclaims warranties and liability subject to its sales terms.

Researchers found that New Caledonian crows and kea parrots selected appropriate tools more successfully after previously exploring them. Birds played with blocks and ropes differing in colour, weight and pattern before using them in tasks to retrieve rewards. The results suggest they incidentally learned object properties through play, a form of latent learning, rather than explicitly seeking information or changing how they explored objects after discovering their use as tools.

Irish software engineer Joan Jordan, 45, struggled to find work after being diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2010, following paralysis on one side of her body. After repeated rejections, she returned to work eight years later in a 15-hour weekly role with the European Patients’ Academy. Jordan also wrote “huManS Multiple Sclerosis,” featuring advice from people living with MS. For World MS Day, she is speaking at Trinity College as MS Ireland launches a report recommending stronger research collaboration, data sharing, patient involvement, funding, and dissemination of findings.
