The 200-day moving average (DMA) is a trend-following indicator calculated from an asset’s average closing price over the previous 200 trading days. Prices above it generally indicate an uptrend; prices below it indicate a downtrend. The article uses the simple moving average because results differ little from the exponential version.

The strategy’s main benefits are simplicity, trend identification, lower drawdowns, and protection during major bear markets. It helped investors exit before substantial declines in 2007–09 and during the 2020 oil-price collapse. Long-term S&P 500 testing showed returns close to buy-and-hold with substantially lower drawdowns, although taxes and trading costs may apply.

Its principal weakness is frequent whipsaws when markets rise without major recessions. From March 2009, the strategy produced an 8.5% compound annual growth rate versus 12.8% for buy-and-hold, while reducing maximum drawdown from 34% to 19%. Since 1960, the S&P 500 crossed above the average 187 times, but only 28% of trades were profitable, with as many as nine consecutive losses.

Jeremy Siegel’s variation buys at least 1% above the average and sells at least 1% below it. It slightly outperformed the basic version and improved risk-adjusted returns, though transaction costs reduced absolute performance. Overall, the 200-day moving average is useful for filtering noise and managing risk, but it is not consistently superior to buy-and-hold and should be evaluated through backtesting.

Saskatchewan Roughriders return specialist Christion Jones has practised as an emergency defensive back ahead of Thursday’s game against Hamilton. Jones, who trained at receiver and defensive back at Alabama, said he is prepared to contribute wherever needed and has discussed the transition with receiver-turned-cornerback Duron Carter. Listed as a backup receiver and experienced at tailback, Jones values his versatility. He ranks third in the CFL in punt- and kickoff-return averages and leads the league with 531 combined yards despite not playing offence. Head coach and GM Chris Jones said the team has limited his offensive and defensive workload to protect his return performance, but would use him at defensive back if necessary.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU increases memory performance with 1555 GB/s HBM2 bandwidth, 2.3 times V100’s L2 read bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, residency controls, and Compute Data Compression. Cache controls retain reusable data and reduce DRAM traffic, while CUDA 11 supports persistent L2 allocation, asynchronous memory copies, hardware barriers, task graphs, and accelerated cooperative operations.

A100’s Multi-Instance GPU capability partitions one GPU into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute, cache, memory-controller, and DRAM resources. Instances provide predictable performance, quality of service, fault isolation, and support for VMs, containers, processes, MPS, and migration between compatible instances. Compute Instances can further subdivide GPU resources and execute contexts independently.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s total A100 bandwidth, while PCIe Gen 4 supplies 31.5 GB/s per direction over x16 and supports SR-IOV. Additional features include improved error containment, five hardware JPEG decoder cores, an optical-flow accelerator, five NVDEC units, and atomic-operation throughput gains over V100.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs, six NVSwitches, up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance, and 4.8 TB/s aggregate bidirectional interconnect bandwidth. MIG enables up to 56 isolated accelerators per system. Its software stack includes CUDA 11, the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC containers and models, and support for deep learning, inference, analytics, and HPC applications.

A100 also supports fine-grained structured sparsity. Pruning removes low-contribution weights or connections, potentially reducing computation, memory bandwidth, and inference latency. NVIDIA’s 2:4 structured sparsity balances work across compute resources and is described as producing virtually no accuracy loss across evaluated neural networks.
Camel engravings at Jebel Misma indicate human presence in the once-verdant Nefud region over 12,000 years ago.

The application describes address obfuscation for memory devices to improve resistance to wear-out attacks and conceal wear-leveling patterns. A configurable mapping function converts logical addresses from access commands into physical memory addresses. For each address bit, selectable operations—including pass-through, inversion, XOR, XNOR, and address swapping—may determine corresponding physical-address bits.

Mapping functions may differ across devices, dies, arrays, or time and may be selected using random numbers, unique identifiers, manufacturing settings, schedules, or trigger events such as booting, access thresholds, or detected attacks. Data may subsequently move among physical cells under a wear-leveling procedure while logical addresses remain fixed. Varying the initial mapping changes observable failure patterns, making reverse-engineered wear-leveling information less useful for attacking other memory entities or the same entity later. A security key may enable direct addressing for testing. Controllers select mappings, receive logical-address access commands, determine physical addresses, and access the corresponding data.

Mario Batali took leave from his businesses and was removed from ABC’s “The Chew” after four women accused him of sexual misconduct. Batali apologized, acknowledged that much of the alleged behavior matched his past actions, and accepted responsibility.

The author argues that schools overemphasize broadly defined skills such as critical thinking, communication and metacognition while neglecting knowledge in history, geography, science, mathematics, languages, literature and the arts. Critical thought, reading comprehension and informed evaluation require substantial background knowledge stored in long-term memory; internet searches cannot replace sustained study, as illustrated by the specialized mathematics needed to understand string theory and the cultural knowledge needed to understand cricket references.

The passage links the retreat from content requirements to grade inflation, declining test performance and reduced graduation testing. It presents high-quality, knowledge-rich instructional materials as a countertrend, though some approved curricula lack coherent, sequential content. AI may support knowledge acquisition but can also weaken rigorous curricula. The author concludes that diminished knowledge instruction particularly harms poorer students and that knowledge is essential not only for practical skills but also for examining and understanding human life.

Using nationally representative 2021 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Survey data, this study examined sociodemographic factors associated with insecticide-treated net (ITN) ownership and use among children under five and pregnant women. Data covered 13,727 households and 14,476 women aged 15–49 and were analyzed using chi-square tests, odds ratios, and 95% confidence intervals.

Overall, 56% of households owned at least one ITN, but only 25% had enough nets for all members, assuming two people per net. Ownership was significantly higher among rural households, households in the North West and North East, and those in lower wealth quintiles.

About 41% of children under five slept under an ITN the preceding night. Use was significantly associated with age, residence, geopolitical zone, and household wealth, but not sex. Younger children, rural residents, children in the North West and North East, and those from poorer households were more likely to use ITNs.

Among pregnant women, 49.6% slept under an ITN. Usage was highest in the North East and North West and increased as household wealth decreased. Women with no or primary education had higher odds of ITN use than women with education beyond secondary level, while rural–urban differences were not statistically significant.

Although Nigeria has improved ITN use over the past decade, ownership declined from 69% in 2015 to 56% in 2021, and usage remains below the national target of 80%. The study recommends addressing regional and socioeconomic disparities through expanded distribution, healthcare access, health education, ongoing monitoring, and adaptive interventions.

HMD Global had not released Nokia 8 kernel modifications 136 days after promising them, despite GPLv2 requirements. Although the locked bootloader limits custom ROM development, the delay drew criticism from developers and risked damaging goodwill toward the company.

The SanDisk Sansa Fuze is a portable audio/video player with a 1.9-inch color screen, FM radio where available, microphone, microSDHC expansion, internal storage, and a rechargeable nonreplaceable battery. It supports music, audiobooks, podcasts, converted videos and photos, voice recording, FM presets and recording, playlists, slideshows, bookmarks, ratings, shuffle, repeat, and equalizer settings.

Users should avoid high-volume listening, hazardous headphone use, moisture, forced connectors, battery damage, and improper disposal. The player connects and charges through USB; files can be transferred through Windows Explorer, Windows Media Player, Audible Manager, or Sansa Media Converter. Disconnecting during transfers may damage the device, while formatting deletes all content.

Controls include a power switch, hold lock, thumbwheel, playback buttons, and reset by holding the power switch for about ten seconds. Settings cover display, wallpaper, backlight, power saving, language, date and time, brightness, volume, USB mode, formatting, and factory reset. Firmware updates, troubleshooting resources, technical support, and how-to videos are available through SanDisk.

SanDisk provides the original purchaser a one-year limited warranty under stated conditions. Warranty remedies may include repair, replacement, or refund, but exclude lost data and certain damages. The software license permits limited personal use with a SanDisk product and restricts modification, reverse engineering, redistribution, and hazardous applications.

The lecture revisits hinged dissections, their construction, motion, applications, and higher-dimensional generalizations. No general software currently exists for animating hinged dissections, making animation tools, slender-adornment refinements, and new dissection designs possible projects. Greg Frederickson’s books and examples provide many designs but limited theory.

Universal hinged dissections for polyominoes, polyiamonds, and related polyforms can be proved inductively. Each basic tile is divided into hinged pieces with hinges accessible on every edge. A spanning tree of a target shape permits removing and reattaching leaf tiles while reconnecting hinge cycles. Open chains of slender pieces can move continuously; some constructions require refinement. Similar methods extend to compatible copies of arbitrary shapes and to three-dimensional polyforms.

Physical implementations include salt-actuated mesoscale dissections, DNA origami, chains of ball-and-socket units, and reconfigurable robots. Connected chains preserve wiring, power, and communication during reconfiguration, unlike modular robots that repeatedly attach and detach. Hinged dissections have also inspired transformable furniture and architectural concepts.

A classical rectangle-to-rectangle dissection overlays angled tessellations and supports the general polygon-dissection construction. Related overlay methods produce square-to-equilateral-triangle dissections, including Dudeney’s hinged design. Frederickson proposed furniture-oriented variants emphasizing one large supported piece.

The general conversion of a dissection into a hinged dissection may require at least exponentially many pieces because successive hinge adjustments repeatedly refine existing pieces. For grid-based polygons, a pseudopolynomial bound can be obtained by triangulating through grid points, converting each polygon into chains of equal-area triangles, preserving hinges during triangle-to-triangle transformations, and using hinge-moving gadgets and pseudocuts without deeply nested refinement.

In three dimensions, equal volume alone does not guarantee a dissection. Dehn showed that matching Dehn invariants is also necessary; Sydler later proved that equal volume and equal Dehn invariant are sufficient in 3D, with a similar result in 4D. The invariant sums, over all edges, tensor products of edge lengths and dihedral angles considered modulo rational multiples of pi. Conditions for dimensions five and higher remain unknown. Equality of Dehn invariants is decidable, but efficient algorithms for testing equality or constructing dissections are not known.

Non-Automatic Exit events are exits not handled automatically. Under SEV-ES they cause a #VC whose error code identifies the VMEXIT. The guest places required state in the GHCB, marks valid fields, invokes VMGEXIT, and processes hypervisor results after resumption. Both parties must clear and set VALID_BITMAP appropriately; SW_EXITCODE and exit-information fields form the minimum exchange. Interrupts and preemption should be disabled while updating or reading the GHCB, and NMI handling may require a separate or saved GHCB.

The GHCB protocol defines required NAE support, state exchange, error reporting, and special handling for events including I/O, MSR accesses, hypercalls, MMIO, page-state changes, SNP firmware requests, AP creation, restricted-injection services, APIC ID discovery, VMPL changes, trusted I/O, Secure AVIC, and termination. Guests may handle #VC or paravirtualize faulting operations. Unsupported negotiated events use the Unsupported Event exit code.

I/O and MMIO operations may require decrypted shared buffers referenced through SW_SCRATCH and multiple VMGEXIT calls. Page-state changes use shared structures containing up to 253 requests and support private, shared, PSMASH, and UNSMASH operations, with progress fields enabling interruption and resumption. SNP guest requests use shared request and response pages; extended requests can return GUID-indexed certificates. TIO requests similarly exchange measurements, certificates, and attestation data. Hypervisors must report required buffer sizes when supplied pages are insufficient.

AP Creation can create, update, or destroy vCPU state using guest-provided VMSA pages. Restricted Injection adds GHCB operations for registering a #HV doorbell page, sending IPIs, and emulating APIC timers. APIC ID List returns assigned APIC IDs in shared contiguous pages. Secure AVIC permits registering private APIC backing pages. Termination requests carry reason codes and optional feature information.

Guests identify SEV-ES through specified CPUID properties. Traditional AP booting is complicated because measured encrypted register state cannot be modified by the hypervisor. Without SNP AP Creation, initial register state, reset-hold protocols, and an encrypted AP jump table are used; vCPU hotplug is unavailable. SNP AP Creation allows guest-supplied VMSAs, simpler AP startup, and vCPU hotplug.

For NMIs, the hypervisor must not intercept IRET, must intercept #DB, and relies on an NMI Complete message before injecting another NMI. Debug-register virtualization may be hardware-backed; otherwise DR7 is intercepted and cached. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

Restricted Injection uses a shared #HV doorbell page containing PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired. The host presents APIC-like interrupt vectors and non-maskable events, while the guest atomically acknowledges events and performs implicit or explicit EOI processing. HLT is executed with interrupts disabled, and the host re-enters the guest when events are pending. Guests must validate vectors and treat improper host behavior as denial of service rather than trusted state.

NVIDIA’s fiscal 2023 first-quarter revenue rose 46% year over year to $8.29 billion, while net income declined 15% to $1.62 billion and diluted earnings per share fell 16% to $0.64. Results included a $1.35 billion charge following termination of the Arm acquisition due to regulatory challenges. Gross margin increased to 65.5%, and operating income declined 4% to $1.87 billion.

Gaming revenue increased 31% to $3.62 billion, Data Center rose 83% to $3.75 billion, and Professional Visualization grew 67% to $622 million. Automotive revenue declined 10% to $138 million, while OEM and Other fell 52% to $158 million, primarily reflecting lower cryptocurrency mining processor revenue.

At May 1, 2022, NVIDIA had $45.21 billion in assets, including $20.34 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, and $10.95 billion in long-term debt. Operating cash flow was $1.73 billion. NVIDIA returned $2.10 billion to shareholders through repurchases and dividends, and its board authorized repurchases of up to $15 billion through December 2023.

The company reported continued supply and logistics constraints, long manufacturing lead times, uncertain cryptocurrency-related demand, inflationary pressures, COVID-19 disruptions in China, and impacts from the war in Ukraine. Outstanding inventory purchase and long-term supply obligations totaled $9.59 billion. NVIDIA stated it had sufficient liquidity for foreseeable operating requirements.

Ray Lewis, Brian Urlacher and Randy Moss entered the Pro Football Hall of Fame on their first ballot, while Terrell Owens made it on his third. Brian Dawkins, Bobby Beathard, Jerry Kramer and Robert Brazile completed the eight-person class.
The cheering showed support before Detroit. The speaker aims to gain ground and responds to each puck carrier’s tendencies rather than categorizing players.

The speaker enjoyed joining the intense physical battle and described helping create two goals. He prioritizes team victories over personal points and is focused on winning the next home game. He appreciates his family attending the Stanley Cup Finals and praises Cory as an underrated teammate who moves the puck well and creates plays.

University of Queensland researchers found that Black, Western Green, and Jameson’s mamba venoms attack two nervous-system targets. They first cause limp paralysis through postsynaptic toxicity; after antivenom treats this effect, presynaptic toxicity may emerge, causing painful spasms and spastic paralysis. This explains why some patients initially improve before developing uncontrolled spasms. Venom effects also varied geographically, particularly between Black Mamba populations in Kenya and South Africa, complicating treatment. Researchers called for specialized antivenoms that address the full range and regional variation of mamba venom activity.

Birmingham City’s ten most memorable away days featured crucial wins, dramatic comebacks and strong travelling support. Highlights included Championship survival secured at Bristol City in 2017 through Che Adams’ goal and at Bolton in 2014 through Paul Caddis’ stoppage-time equaliser. Promotion was clinched at Reading in 2009. Other notable results were derby victory at Wolves, emphatic wins over Fulham, Derby, Crystal Palace and Shamrock Rovers, and a late 3-2 triumph at Tottenham. The standout European trip saw about 8,000 supporters travel to Belgium in 2011, where Chris Wood’s 100th-minute winner made Birmingham the first English team to beat Club Brugge away.

This systematic review examines AI applications in higher education assessment, grading, and feedback through the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge framework. It reviewed 20 studies identified through five academic search engines using predefined inclusion, exclusion, quality-assessment, and PRISMA procedures.

The literature indicates that AI can automate large-scale assessments, improve grading speed and consistency, reduce educators’ workloads, and provide timely, personalized feedback and adaptive learning pathways. AI-driven systems may support student engagement, self-regulated learning, instructional planning, and standardized assessment across institutions. Adoption remains emerging in African contexts, including Zambia, where AI may help address large classes, resource constraints, and inconsistent assessment practices.

Persistent challenges include algorithmic bias, data privacy, transparency, infrastructure and training limitations, academic integrity, and uncertainty about AI’s ability to assess creativity, critical thinking, and other subjective qualities. The review concludes that AI should complement rather than replace educators’ judgment. Effective implementation requires pedagogical alignment, diverse training data, transparent governance, professional development, continued validation, and collaboration among educators, technologists, and policymakers.

Researchers analyzing 39 fossils from 560-million-year-old rocks off Newfoundland conclude that remains previously considered decomposed organic matter may represent early spongelike animals. The creatures had pores, vertical fingerlike tubes, and bodies up to 53 centimeters long, suggesting they were filter feeders that lived atop other organisms. Their punklike appearance inspired a name honoring Sex Pistols singer John Lydon, while also referencing the Beothuk word for gooseberry. Researchers say the organism may be related to modern sponges and could help clarify early animal evolution.

Best Buy’s Techtober sale discounts the Acer Swift 16 AI by $450 to $800. It includes 16 GB of RAM, 1 TB of storage, a 16-inch 2,880 × 1,800 OLED display with a 120-Hz refresh rate, and an Intel Core Ultra 7 256V processor. Testing delivered 13 hours of YouTube playback. The 0.79-inch-thick laptop is less portable than the $900 Lenovo Yoga Slim 7i Aura Edition. Techtober runs through October 12.

The U.S. Department of State disapproved Mr. Allen’s request that the American consul-general in Shanghai assist in surrendering Kim Ok-kiun’s murderer to Korean justice, stating that U.S. consular jurisdiction extended only to American citizens.

Mr. Sill reported that Korean rebels defeated government troops near Chon-ju, captured their weapons, and seized the undefended provincial capital. He warned that the rebellion was expanding, the Korean Government lacked adequate means to restore order, and Americans in Seoul could face danger. Admiral Skerrett, whose squadron was largely assigned to the Bering Sea, could not immediately send a vessel to Chemulpo but promised one when possible. British, French, Chinese, and Japanese vessels had already been dispatched there.

After an appeal from the Korean King, China sent 1,500 troops, with plans to increase the force to 2,225, and ordered three warships to Chemulpo. China assured Japan and Russia that the troops would be withdrawn after hostilities ended and invited Japan to send gunboats to protect its subjects.

@ThingsExpo’s January 2017 posts cover IoT, M2M, WebRTC identity management, data platforms and monetization, software for connected devices, blockchain, mobile transformation, Scrum, Microsoft, election data science, and 2017 technology predictions. Onalytica ranked @ThingsExpo among leading IoT and M2M brands and Carmen Gonzalez as a top M2M influencer. Several posts promote the June 6–8, 2017 @ThingsExpo and Cloud Expo in New York. Other articles discuss connected-home communications, real-time IoT analytics, data ownership and surveillance risks, the Web platform’s importance, and Matrix’s open standard for IP messaging and VoIP.

In his inaugural address, the President urges Americans to confront the national crisis with courage, declaring that “the only thing we have to fear is fear itself.” He describes widespread unemployment, lost savings, collapsing markets, foreclosures, reduced incomes, and failed financial leadership, while emphasizing that the nation still possesses abundant resources.

He calls for replacing selfish monetary values with honesty, public service, productive work, and social responsibility. His immediate priority is employment through direct government recruitment and projects supporting natural resources. Additional measures include improving agricultural prices, preventing farm and home foreclosures, reducing government costs, coordinating relief, supervising transportation and utilities, regulating banking, credit, and investment, and establishing sound currency.

Domestic economic recovery must precede international trade reform, though he supports international economic cooperation and a “good neighbor” policy respecting other nations’ rights and agreements. He asks Americans to accept shared discipline and sacrifice under vigorous leadership.

While hoping Congress and the Executive can act through normal constitutional processes, he states that if Congress fails during the emergency, he will seek broad executive authority comparable to wartime powers. He concludes that the people have demanded direct action and expresses confidence in democracy, national unity, moral values, and divine guidance.

The MACD and RSI strategy combines two momentum indicators to analyze trends and price movements. MACD, calculated from 12- and 26-period exponential moving averages with a 9-period signal line, is mainly used for trend analysis. RSI oscillates between zero and 100, with readings above 70 traditionally considered overbought and below 30 oversold.

Traders may use MACD to identify the overall trend and RSI to identify price swings or mean-reversion opportunities. One example buys when MACD rises above its signal line while RSI rises from oversold territory; the opposite conditions can signal a short trade. Custom settings and additional filters may also be used.

A backtested strategy incorporating MACD, RSI, and a mean-reversion filter performed best for semiconductors. On SMH from 2001 onward, it produced 235 trades, an average gain of 0.88% per trade after stated costs, and a 73% win rate.

The combination may provide confirmation, but critics consider it redundant because both indicators measure momentum. MACD can whipsaw in range-bound markets, and RSI may generate more false signals. Effectiveness varies by rules, parameters, markets, and assets, so clear rules and backtesting are essential.

Nifty50 gained 29.65 points, or 0.28%, amid consolidation and rollover-driven short covering. Resistance is expected at 10,650–10,695, with support at 10,585 and 10,510. RSI and MACD remain bullish, but Nifty has not broken out of its trading range. Low India VIX and elevated put-call ratio may limit gains and increase profit-taking risk, warranting caution.

On April 20, 2010, explosions aboard Transocean’s Deepwater Horizon rig killed 11 workers and injured 17. The rig, leased by BP to drill the Macondo well in the Gulf of Mexico, sank two days later. By the time the well was capped on July 15, nearly five million barrels of oil had spilled, making it the largest marine oil spill then recorded in U.S. waters.

BP had grown through mergers, decentralization, workforce reductions, and cost cutting. Its “asset federation” model gave site managers substantial autonomy and tied compensation to performance, while providing limited incentives to share risk-management practices. Despite publicly emphasizing safety and environmental responsibility, BP had experienced major incidents, including the 2005 Texas City refinery explosion and the 2006 Prudhoe Bay spill. Investigations identified maintenance cutbacks, weak process-safety leadership, and confusion between personal safety performance and process safety.

The Macondo project was hazardous, over budget, and behind schedule. The Deepwater Horizon also had extensive unresolved maintenance problems, including disabled alarms and unreliable drilling-control computers. Closing the well involved multiple companies and recently appointed BP managers. Several disputed decisions favored faster or less costly procedures: BP selected long-string casing, which provided fewer barriers against gas flow; used six centralizers despite Halliburton modeling that recommended 21 and warned of severe gas-flow risk; circulated drilling mud for only 30 minutes rather than completing a full circulation; and canceled a cement bond log that could have detected channeling and cement failure. No stop-work order was issued while suitable centralizers were obtained.

The spill caused extensive environmental damage across all five Gulf States, harming wildlife, wetlands, fisheries, tourism, and coastal businesses. BP suffered major financial and reputational losses, while the federal deepwater-drilling moratorium reduced employment, investment, and oil production. BP established a $20 billion claims facility, which had paid more than $3.6 billion by February 2011.

As of early 2011, investigations continued and involved parties disputed responsibility. The case concludes that BP’s organizational structure, contractor relationships, incentives, communication, and repeated preference for cost reduction and expediency over caution may have contributed to the disaster.

A January 19, 2001 news compilation focuses on California’s power crisis and Enron-related developments. California’s two largest utilities, Pacific Gas & Electric and Southern California Edison, accumulated more than $11.5 billion in power-related debt because regulated retail rates remained below soaring wholesale costs. Both defaulted on obligations and faced possible bankruptcy. California authorized $400 million for emergency power purchases and considered multiyear contracts and utility debt refinancing. Federal Energy Secretary Bill Richardson ordered electricity and natural-gas suppliers to continue serving California through January 23. Rolling blackouts were avoided that day, though the state maintained its highest power alert and faced possible fuel disruptions.

President-elect George W. Bush opposed wholesale electricity price caps. Enron chairman and Bush adviser Ken Lay also opposed caps, arguing California should purchase needed power and expose consumers to price signals. The crisis prompted investors to reassess utilities as higher-risk investments following sharp stock and bond losses.

Separately, Enron Energy Services signed a 10-year agreement to manage electricity and natural-gas purchases for 53 Owens-Illinois facilities in 20 states, covering more than $2 billion in projected purchases. EOTT Energy Partners, whose general partner is an Enron subsidiary, declared a quarterly distribution of $0.475 per common unit. Enron remained active in the expanding bandwidth market, where quoted routes increased from two to ten. Pennsylvania regulators rejected GPU Energy’s comparison of its financial problems with California’s crisis, citing differences in generation supply, plant ownership, and contracting rules.

After Trump reversed his pledge to label China a currency manipulator, analyst Sean King suggested he might reconsider withdrawing from the Trans-Pacific Partnership. Japan and the remaining 10 nations are pursuing the pact without the U.S., while its text remains valid until February 2018.

The lecture examines limited attention and its effects on decision-making. Change-blindness, gorilla, and dichotic-listening experiments show that people can direct attention toward instructed tasks but often miss other information, especially when distracted. Attention may also be reduced by environmental conditions, competing tasks, worries, poor sleep, noise, poverty, and temptations.

Inattention can persist even in high-stakes settings. EntreMed’s stock price rose sharply when old cancer-treatment news reached the New York Times front page, despite earlier publication in Nature and the Times. Investors also confused the video-conferencing company Zoom with an unrelated company having a similar name and ticker.

Chetty and co-authors measure inattention to sales taxes, which are usually added only at checkout. In a California grocery-store experiment, selected products displayed both pre-tax and after-tax prices. Making taxes salient reduced sales by 8.8%. Combined with estimated price elasticity, this implied that consumers reacted to sales-tax changes about one-quarter as strongly as to ordinary price changes. Evidence from beer purchases similarly showed strong responses to salient excise taxes but little response to less-visible sales taxes. Such inattention may reduce tax-induced distortions when taxes primarily raise revenue, while taxes intended to discourage harmful behavior should be salient.

The lecture also discusses how existing beliefs shape attention and learning. People may overlook relevant evidence when a possible cause is absent from their mental model, as with food-related headaches or doctors historically overlooking handwashing as a cause of childbed fever.

A study of experienced Indonesian seaweed farmers illustrates this mechanism. Farmers understood line spacing but largely ignored pod size and did not know their current or optimal pod size. Merely participating in trials varying pod size had insignificant effects, while receiving summarized trial results and recommendations substantially changed farming practices. The findings show that people may fail to learn from available information when they do not consider it relevant, potentially producing persistent errors and large welfare losses.

Undefeated Mississippi State (8-0) visits No. 25 Cincinnati (7-2) Tuesday at BB&T Arena in Kentucky. Key factors include Cincinnati’s turnover problems against MSU’s improved defense, the Bearcats’ advantage in offensive rebounding, and Mississippi State’s deeper rotation. The Bulldogs force 17 turnovers per game but face a major step up after playing one of Division I’s weakest schedules. Eli Wright returns from suspension, giving MSU its first full roster this season.

The flexbone is a run-heavy system derived from the wishbone and built around option plays, misdirection, and spreading defenders across the field. It moves two running backs, called A-backs, near the line of scrimmage to increase running and passing threats. Successful personnel include a decisive, mobile quarterback; a powerful, athletic B-back; versatile A-backs; strong-blocking receivers; and intelligent, athletic offensive linemen.

Its strengths include unfamiliarity for modern defenses, ball control, long possessions, multiple potential ball carriers, assignment confusion, and the ability to physically wear down opponents. Its weaknesses are limited high-volume passing, difficulty overcoming late deficits, extensive practice requirements, and vulnerability in bad weather because option exchanges demand precise timing and ball security.

Common formations include the balanced double slot, trips, and receivers-over alignments, each designed to influence defensive positioning and create advantageous space. Major running plays include the triple option, where the quarterback chooses among a fullback dive, keeper, or A-back pitch; the midline option, which reads an unblocked defensive tackle; and the rocket toss, a quick outside pitch to a motioning A-back. Passing concepts include the play-action wheel route, toss boot, and four verticals, often exploiting defenses focused on stopping the run.

Navy, Army, and Air Force traditionally use versions of the flexbone. Paul Johnson employed it at Georgia Southern, Navy, and Georgia Tech, whose 2009 team won the ACC championship. Harding University won the 2023 Division II national championship using a version, and the offense remains common in high school football, particularly at smaller schools.

Jeff Carter and Drew Doughty described their goals as efforts to get shots through traffic, with Dustin Penner screening Martin Brodeur. Carter called his first playoff overtime goal a special moment that secured a two-game series lead. Doughty said the team must reset for Los Angeles, learn from the opening games and treat the return home as a new series. Both expect New Jersey to play desperately, while acknowledging Los Angeles has not yet played its best hockey. Carter said familiarity with Brodeur and the Devils helps, and Doughty anticipated an increasingly loud home crowd.

The Larry Swedroe Portfolio uses evidence-based investing to balance long-term growth and risk. It allocates 30% to equities—15% US small-cap value, 7.5% international small-cap value, and 7.5% emerging markets—and 70% to intermediate bonds. Swedroe favors low-cost passive index funds, broad diversification, a long-term perspective, and periodic rebalancing, typically annually or after a 5% allocation deviation.

His value strategy uses bottom-up analysis to identify undervalued companies with strong balance sheets, consistent earnings, and capable management while avoiding overpayment. Small-cap value stocks may offer higher potential returns and diversification but also greater volatility and loss risk.

A backtest beginning in 2012 produced a 3.71% annual return, below historical returns. Over an earlier 30-year period, the portfolio reportedly returned 6.28% annually with 5.46% standard deviation, aided by falling interest rates. Its large bond allocation means it is expected to underperform stocks over time but may appeal to risk-averse investors.

Berkshire Hathaway began repurchasing shares in 2011 at up to 110% of book value, but bought only $67 million. Raising the limit to 120% in 2012 enabled approximately $1.3 billion in repurchases. No shares were repurchased from 2013 through 2016, although prices approached the threshold several times. The author argues that the unchanged limit has become increasingly conservative because book value does not reflect growing unrecorded gains in Berkshire’s controlled businesses. Despite Buffett’s view that purchases at or below 120% materially benefit continuing shareholders, the author believes repurchases should be considered if Berkshire’s price-to-book ratio again reaches the low-to-mid 120% range.

Facing declining attendance, Germany’s Protestant church is experimenting with social media. At Magdeburg’s Walloon Reformed Church, worshippers tweet prayers and reactions during services while posts from across Germany appear on a screen. Pastor Ralf Peter Reimann hopes this will engage people who live online and encourage communication among believers. The approach echoes how printing-press pamphlets rapidly spread Martin Luther’s Reformation ideas and fostered public debate 500 years ago. Reactions are mixed: some participants welcome sharing prayers online, while others find Twitter distracting or exclusionary and prefer traditional services and hymn singing.

European stocks headed for a fifth consecutive decline and their biggest weekly loss since November 2016, pressured by rising bond yields, a stronger euro and disappointing bank earnings. Germany’s exporter-heavy DAX fell more than 5% in eight sessions, turning negative for the year.

Deutsche Bank shares dropped after a larger-than-expected 2017 loss, while Caixabank and Sabadell declined following mixed results. Technology stocks were also in focus after earnings updates from major U.S. companies.

Investors awaited U.S. payroll data, while Bank of America Merrill Lynch’s “Bull & Bear” indicator issued a sell signal. Analysts warned that rising yields could increase funding costs and force leveraged trades to unwind, though strong global growth and profit expectations continued to support the equity outlook.

Danny Langston was injured in Florida while riding in a vehicle owned by George Johnson, Jr. and allegedly negligently driven by Fred Johnson with the owner’s consent. The trial court granted summary judgment to Johnson and his surety, Personal Service Insurance Company, finding the Ohio-issued bond covered only Johnson’s personal acts.

The appellate court held that Florida tort law governs the owner’s liability because the accident occurred in Florida. Under Florida’s dangerous instrumentality doctrine, Johnson could be personally liable for negligence by a permissive driver. Ohio law governs the bond, which secures judgments arising from the ownership, maintenance, or use of a motor vehicle. Accordingly, Personal Service could be liable, up to the bond’s limits, if Langston obtains a judgment against Johnson. The court reversed the summary judgment and remanded for further proceedings.

Pain Association Scotland will deliver a free five-week chronic pain self-management course in Montrose from May for Angus residents aged 18 or over. Weekly two-and-a-half-hour sessions will cover understanding pain, stress, pacing, flare-ups, relaxation and medication through interactive discussions. The course aims to improve coping skills and quality of life but does not replace medicine or provide direct pain relief. To book, call 01307 474889 or email achppatientcourses.tayside@nhs.net.

U.S. homebuilder sentiment fell three points to 68 in April, below forecasts but still indicating favorable conditions. Current sales, six-month expectations and buyer traffic declined. Nevertheless, new-home sales remained robust, supported by low mortgage rates and a strong job market, with February sales up nearly 13 percent year over year.

NVIDIA’s A100 GPU introduces third-generation Tensor Cores, new numerical formats, structured sparsity, expanded memory systems, Multi-Instance GPU capabilities, and faster interconnects for AI and HPC workloads. TF32 operates by default for deep-learning training, while FP16 or BF16 mixed precision provides maximum throughput. For HPC, A100 supports IEEE-compliant FP64 Tensor Core operations, reaching 19.5 TFLOPS and up to 2.5 times V100’s FP64 performance. In iterative-refinement tests, TF32 provided the fastest and most robust mixed-precision results, with a 2.0× geometric-mean speedup over an FP64 solver.

A100’s 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity retains two nonzero values per four entries. Pruned weights are compressed, reducing footprint and bandwidth by half, while Sparse MMA instructions skip zeros and double Tensor Core throughput. NVIDIA’s dense-training, pruning, and fine-tuning process produced virtually no inference-accuracy loss across evaluated networks.

The GPU combines 192 KB of L1 cache and shared memory per SM, supports simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, and includes 40 GB of HBM2 delivering 1,555 GB/s. Its 40 MB L2 cache is 6.7 times larger than V100’s and provides 2.3 times its bandwidth. Compute Data Compression can improve DRAM and L2 bandwidth by up to fourfold. SECDED ECC protects HBM2, caches, and register files.

A100 improves Tensor Core efficiency through broader warp-level data sharing, fewer instructions and register accesses, asynchronous global-to-shared-memory copies, asynchronous barriers, and increased shared memory. CUDA 11 supports these capabilities, along with task-graph acceleration, L2 residency controls, Cooperative Groups, sparsity, and MIG.

MIG partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory paths, predictable performance, quality of service, and fault isolation. Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances and support MPS, virtual machines, containers, migration, and multi-tenant operation.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s aggregate bandwidth, double V100’s total. A100 also supports PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, enhanced error isolation, hardware JPEG decoding, optical-flow acceleration, improved atomics, and five NVDEC units.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs, six NVSwitches, 4.8 TB/s bidirectional interconnect bandwidth, and up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance. MIG enables up to 56 isolated accelerators per system. Its software stack includes CUDA 11, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC resources, and optimized software for deep learning, inference, analytics, and HPC.

Accounts of children raised by animals are often apocryphal or fraudulent, but several remain intriguing. Jean de Liège reportedly lived alone in Belgian woods for sixteen years, emerging speechless, highly sensitive to smells, and allegedly covered in hair, though this claim lacks evidence and may reflect hypertrichosis. In 1672, Nicholas Tulp described an Irish teenager supposedly raised among sheep who bleated, ate grass and hay, and displayed sheep-like behavior. A nineteenth-century Texas legend tells of a “Wolf Girl” orphaned in infancy, later seen living with wolves, captured, and escaping after wolves approached her confinement. She was allegedly observed again seven years later with two pups before disappearing permanently. The passage suggests maintaining an open mind about whether such feral people might still exist.

Apple’s closed iOS platform trades some innovation and flexibility for stronger security, though it remains vulnerable to malware and attacks. iOS 10.3.1 protects data through passwords, PINs, fingerprints, two-factor authentication, optional erasure after ten failed logins, and iCloud backups. Built-in anti-malware, frequent security updates, and an exclusive app store reduce infection risks. Find My Phone lets users locate, lock, or erase stolen devices through iCloud, while permission controls restrict applications’ data access. Although iOS had more publicly disclosed vulnerabilities than Android in 2015, most Apple devices receive regular patches. Android’s varied manufacturers, customized hardware, and modified operating-system versions create fragmentation that makes security updates more difficult, while Apple controls both its hardware and software.

The paper examines how an Australian university addressed limited arts preparation among primary pre-service teachers by introducing an Arts Specialism in 2019. Using Stephen J. Ball’s education policy sociology framework, it analyses contexts of influence, policy text production and policy practice, supported by critical discourse analysis.

Arts education is widely recognised for supporting creativity, cultural literacy, learning and wellbeing, yet teacher education programmes often allocate insufficient curriculum time and provide inadequate specialist preparation. Government requirements for primary teaching specialisations, advocacy from professional organisations and collaboration with arts stakeholders supported the development of the specialism.

The programme comprises four courses covering dance, drama, media arts, music and visual arts, building on a compulsory foundation course. It emphasises experiential “making and responding,” digital technologies, culturally responsive pedagogy, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander arts, school-based projects and partnerships with arts organisations. Across the suite, students receive 600 hours of arts education through coursework, practical projects, placements, presentations and reflective assessment.

Implementation required negotiation over staffing, costs, timetabling and equitable coverage of five arts subjects. COVID-19 also prompted online delivery and community-based projects. Pre-service teacher feedback indicated increased confidence, pedagogical knowledge, interdisciplinary understanding and appreciation of arts education.

The Arts Specialism, approved by the Australian Institute for Teaching and School Leadership, offers a model for improving generalist teachers’ arts competencies and bridging policy and practice. Persistent challenges include curriculum time, resources, staffing conditions and competing programme demands. The paper recommends wider institutional adoption, stronger policy and industry support, continued stakeholder collaboration, and longitudinal research into graduates’ careers and school-based arts implementation.

October 2025 features a supermoon and two meteor showers. On October 6, the full moon may appear up to 14% larger and 30% brighter because it coincides with perigee. The Draconids, produced by debris from comet 21P Giacobini-Zinner, peak around October 8 and may yield up to 10 meteors per hour, though moonlight could hinder viewing. The Orionids, caused by Halley’s Comet debris, peak October 21 at about 20 meteors per hour. A new moon will provide dark viewing conditions, especially before midnight through 2 a.m.

For NMI injection, the hypervisor must intercept #DB rather than IRET and rely on the guest’s “NMI Complete” VMGEXIT message before injecting another NMI. A guest may set the trap flag before IRET, handle the resulting #VC/#DB intercept, clear its per-CPU NMI state, and send completion.

SEV-ES hardware supporting DebugVirtualization saves and restores debug registers through the VMSA, allowing debug-register intercepts to be cleared. Without this support, DR7 reads and writes must be intercepted; the guest caches written values and returns them on reads without updating actual DR7.

SMM is unsupported in this specification version, and nested virtualization is unsupported under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP.

SNP Restricted Injection limits the host to #HV doorbell notifications. The shared, host-owned doorbell page contains PendingEvent, identifying interrupts, NMI, #MC, and signaling state, plus NoEoiRequired for optimized end-of-interrupt handling. Doorbell pages are configured through GHCB VMGEXIT requests and accessed by guests with C=0.

Guests should execute HLT with interrupts disabled and inspect doorbell state immediately after resuming. Hosts must emulate APIC interrupt presentation, acknowledgement, in-service, priority, and EOI behavior. Guests acknowledge events by atomically exchanging PendingEvent with zero, validate vectors, and either clear NoEoiRequired atomically or issue an explicit X2APIC EOI through VMGEXIT. Non-maskable events must remain dispatchable when EFLAGS.IF is zero. Non-cooperative behavior may cause denial of service or lost notifications but must not compromise host integrity.

Amid renewed tensions on the Korean Peninsula, veterans and experts debated Canada’s potential role. Korean War veteran John Bishop doubted Canada could influence events, while former ambassador Marius Grinius argued that Canada weakened its position by cutting diplomatic ties with North Korea under a “controlled engagement” policy. North Korea’s nuclear and missile tests, U.S. military actions and hostile rhetoric have heightened fears of conflict. Veteran Doug Finney and scholar Tina Park urged Canada to act, citing widespread humanitarian suffering in North Korea, Canada’s wartime legacy and its commitment to preventing crimes against humanity.

Last-shot basketball situations require preparation, composure, simple execution, and getting the ball to the best player, who should never inbound. Teams should read the defense, exploit overplay, pursue offensive rebounds, and practice timed scenarios while maintaining strong conditioning.

Holding for the final shot with under 30 seconds is recommended when the score margin is under eight points. Players should be positioned by 10 seconds, initiate the play at eight, and shoot with three to five seconds remaining. Controlling the final possession of one period and the first of the next can create a major scoring swing.

Essential skills include long skip, baseball, and semi-hook passes; half-court shooting; tipping; offensive rebounding; and intentionally missing free throws while ensuring the ball hits the rim. Teams should preserve and track timeouts, use one with one to three seconds remaining, advance the ball toward half court before calling timeout when possible, and consider quick counter breaks before the defense sets.

Additional guidelines include attacking in line with the basket, counting down from the bench, confirming correct clock operation, practicing plays from both sides, designating a skilled inbounder, and tailoring plays to the ball’s location and time remaining. With very limited time, use predetermined inbound plays and minimal passes; with more time, push the ball upcourt and execute a rehearsed play through the best player.

The exponential moving average (EMA) gives greater weight to recent prices than the simple moving average, making it more responsive but still a lagging indicator prone to false signals. SPY backtests suggest short-period EMAs work best for mean-reversion, while long-period EMAs favor trend-following. A 5-day mean-reversion strategy produced a 7.41% CAGR, and a 200-day trend-following strategy returned 7.84% with a 25.94% maximum drawdown. Buying below the 50-day EMA and exiting after 200 days yielded 10.17% per trade. EMA settings should be selected through backtesting and may be combined with other indicators or used to identify trends, support, and resistance.

April the giraffe’s Animal Adventure Park livestream became YouTube’s second-most-watched live channel, attracting over 232 million views and 1.2 million simultaneous viewers when she delivered her calf.

Taylor Swift has set records across awards, charts, streaming, and touring. She became the youngest writer-performer of a No. 1 Hot Country Songs track and, at the time, the youngest CMA entertainer of the year and Grammy album-of-the-year winner. She later became the first artist to win album of the year four times and holds records for American Music Awards, Billboard Digital Song Sales No. 1s, Grammy song-of-the-year nominations, and occupying the entire Billboard Hot 100 top 10. “All Too Well (10 Minute Version)” became the longest No. 1 song. “The Life of a Showgirl” and “The Fate of Ophelia” broke single-day streaming records, while the Eras Tour became the highest-grossing music tour at $2 billion. Swift’s estimated net worth reached $1.6 billion in 2024.

The lecture reviews permutation matrices, which reorder rows through left multiplication and columns through right multiplication by the transpose. Their transpose is also their inverse. Such reordering can reduce numerical error through pivoting or minimize fill-in in large sparse systems.

A Plinko model illustrates diffusion using a sparse matrix with off-diagonal entries of one-half. Repeated multiplication spreads probability among neighboring cells and can approach a uniform distribution. A distribution unchanged in direction by a matrix transformation is an eigenvector; its scaling factor is the corresponding eigenvalue.

Eigenvalues satisfy \(Aw=\lambda w\). Nontrivial eigenvectors require \(A-\lambda I\) to be singular, so eigenvalues are roots of the characteristic polynomial \(\det(A-\lambda I)=0\). Diagonal and triangular matrices have their eigenvalues on the diagonal. Real matrices may have real or complex eigenvalues, with complex values occurring in conjugate pairs. The determinant equals the product of eigenvalues, while the trace equals their sum.

Eigenvectors lie in the null space of \(A-\lambda I\) and can be found using Gaussian elimination. Algebraic multiplicity counts repeated eigenvalue roots; geometric multiplicity is the dimension of the associated null space and cannot exceed algebraic multiplicity. A matrix has a complete set of eigenvectors when these multiplicities agree for every eigenvalue.

With a complete eigenvector set, \(A\) can be diagonalized as \(A=W\Lambda W^{-1}\). This eigendecomposition simplifies solving linear systems and decouples linear ordinary differential equations. For symmetric matrices with normalized eigenvectors, \(W^{-1}=W^T\). Matrices lacking a complete eigenvector set require alternatives such as Jordan normal form, Schur decomposition, or singular value decomposition.

A systematic review examined papers published from 2000–2017 in leading Information Systems journals using terms related to digital business strategy, digital transformation, and business digitalization. From 292 initial articles, title, abstract, keyword, and full-text screening produced 28 articles. These were coded following Wolifswinkel’s guidelines to identify dimensions, attributes, and themes.

Publication activity increased after 2009, particularly in 2016. Research focused mainly on automotive, banking, telecommunications, healthcare, oil and gas, and manufacturing, with most studies conducted in the United States and Europe and fewer in Asia, the Middle East, Latin America, and Africa.

The review identified 12 dimensions of digital transformation, six of digital business strategy, and ten of organizational capabilities. All three concepts share external collaboration through digital-platform ecosystems. Digital transformation and digital business strategy share technology use and structural change; digital transformation and organizational capabilities share digital leadership, agile and scalable operations, digitally enabled customer service, and digital artefacts; digital business strategy and organizational capabilities share dynamic capabilities.

The proposed framework presents digital transformation as digital business strategy in action, enabled by continuously developed and reconfigured organizational capabilities. It emphasizes external collaboration, updated digital leadership skills, flexible operations, customer-value analysis, digital processes, data-handling infrastructures, and adaptable products and services. The study argues that competitive digital strategy initiatives and market-aligned organizational capabilities support digital transformation and improved performance. The framework is intended to guide executives, consultants, and Information Systems researchers in selecting capabilities for effective digital transformation rather than concentrating only on technology investment.

The paper studies allocating finite resources across multiple periods with stochastic, potentially correlated demands to maximize expected revenue. It formulates a static convex optimization problem whose allocations depend only on marginal demand distributions. Using KKT conditions, optimal allocations are expressed through demand quantiles and efficiently computed by bisection on a dual variable.

Because the static policy cannot use temporal correlations or newly observed demands, the authors propose a shrinking-horizon sequential heuristic. At each period, it allocates resources for the current period, conditions future demand distributions on observed demands, and re-solves the remaining allocation problem. The method requires conditional quantile functions and applies to any demand model providing them. For independent demands, it reduces to the static solution.

Experiments use jointly log-normal synthetic demands, with an oracle allocation as a noncausal upper bound and a roll-forward rule as a causal baseline. Under independent demands, static and sequential policies produce identical results. With correlated demands, the sequential policy consistently earns more revenue than the static and roll-forward methods across horizons from 20 to 200 periods, approaches oracle performance, and generally has lower revenue variance. Future work will combine allocation with online learning of demand distributions and examine the importance of distributional accuracy.

Foreign Relations editors have full access to retired State Department records and special access to restricted materials at the Reagan Library and other agencies. Department files from 1981–1989 and permanently preserved office files will eventually become available through the National Archives after declassification and processing. Although all published material is declassified, some comes from documents that remain partly classified or unavailable in full. Reagan Library collections include major foreign-affairs records from White House offices and federal agencies. Some research used records scanned through the Remote Archives Capture project; incomplete scanning sometimes made attachment status uncertain, noted as “Not found attached.”

Documents are arranged chronologically by Washington time, with memoranda of conversation dated by the conversation. Originals are reproduced as closely as possible, preserving spelling, punctuation, capitalization, abbreviations, marginalia, and original ellipses, while silently correcting obvious typographical errors. Editorial headings are supplied, and bracketed text identifies corrections, additions, unrelated omissions, or classified material. Withheld text and documents are accounted for by location, length, and, where possible, nature.

The passage specifies SD Memory Card write, erase, protection, command, switching, CRC, timing, and addressing behavior.

Block writes use per-block CRC; failed CRC data is discarded. Write commands reject invalid block lengths, addresses, misalignment, or protected areas and set corresponding status bits. SDHC/SDXC memory transfers use fixed 512-byte blocks and block addressing, while SDSC uses byte addressing and CMD16-defined lengths. Multiple-block writes are preferred for speed. ACMD23 can pre-erase blocks, and ACMD22 reports successfully written blocks after an error. Cards signal programming busy by holding DAT0 low; hosts may poll with CMD13, deselect with CMD7, and interleave writes among cards.

Erase ranges are set by CMD32 and CMD33, followed by CMD38. Sequence errors reset the operation, and protected sectors remain intact. DISCARD deallocates selected blocks and leaves their contents undefined; FULE logically erases the entire user area. Both require support checks, are limited to SDHC/SDXC, and are unavailable through SPI. DISCARD has a 250 ms busy timeout; FULE has a one-second timeout.

Write protection includes a host-managed mechanical switch, optional internal protection, and password locking. CMD42 manages passwords, locking, unlocking, password clearing, and force erase. Passwords persist across power cycles, and cards with passwords automatically lock after power-up. Card Ownership Protection adds a Force Erase Password, COP Unlock, protected force erase, and restrictions on clearing passwords or using ordinary force erase. Incorrect parameters or passwords set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED. Force erase removes user data and the normal password but not the secure area; FEP Force Erase retains the FEP. Locked cards accept only specified commands, and bus-width changes are rejected.

CMD55 marks the next command as application-specific. Defined legal ACMDs retain APP_CMD status; undefined commands may be treated as regular commands, while illegal commands report errors. CMD6 checks or switches functions, including access speed, command systems, driver strength, and power limit. Mode 0 queries support, readiness, and power use; Mode 1 performs switching. Invalid selections cancel switching, and busy functions must not be changed. High-Speed mode provides a 25 MB/s interface using a 50 MHz clock and requires a one-to-one host-card connection.

CMD8 checks voltage compatibility during initialization. The host may vary or stop the clock subject to transaction-completion and ACMD41 requirements. CRC7 protects commands and most responses; CRC16 protects data, separately on each data line in wide-bus mode. CRC or illegal-command errors prevent execution and set status bits.

Read operations generally use a 100 ms timeout. Writes normally use up to 250 ms busy time, with specified SDXC cases allowing 500 ms; UHS-II data bursts may remain busy for one second. Commands are fixed 48-bit words and organized into command classes, with mandatory and optional support depending on card version, capacity, and features.

Research across more than 150 firms found that technological maturity correlates with stronger three-year revenue and enterprise-value growth. Digital leaders include both digital natives and successfully transformed traditional enterprises, while laggards often retain legacy infrastructure and practices.

Four cultural traits distinguish organizations with strong data cultures: a growth mindset toward learning and responsible risk-taking; transparent data sharing that creates common context; employee empowerment to examine data and measure performance; and shared, objective targets that align teams while allowing autonomy. Leaders reinforce these traits through daily operations, broad skill development, experimentation, governed data access, realistic metrics, and goals clearly connected to strategy.

Digital laggards generally emphasize short-term needs, narrow training, risk avoidance, restricted and siloed data, intuition or seniority-based decisions, unrealistic objectives, and process compliance. These practices can reduce trust, discourage measurement, misalign teams, and inhibit innovation. Cultural transformation remains difficult even for leaders, particularly when balancing experimentation with regulation, deadlines, excessive analysis, and appropriate use of human judgment.

Data-driven culture supports both vertical alignment with company goals and horizontal collaboration across functions. Organizations commonly fit four patterns: data novices lack both enabling culture and systems; insight-ready firms support learning but lack technical capabilities; tech-enabled firms have technology but discourage experimentation; and data-reliant firms overuse data at the expense of critical thinking. Each can build on existing strengths through targeted cultural and technical changes.

The article examines how anti-Critical Race Theory policies in Idaho, Utah, and Arizona affect Native content in teacher education. Drawing on stories, interviews, observations, and research at predominantly white institutions and K–12 schools, the authors apply Tribal Critical Race Theory and the concept of “colonial unknowing.”

They argue that U.S. education has historically omitted or distorted Native histories, sovereignty, knowledge, and contemporary presence. Although some states require Native history instruction, implementation, funding, professional development, and tribal partnership remain limited. Anti-CRT measures further discourage educators from discussing colonization, racism, land dispossession, and culturally sustaining pedagogy.

The authors’ experiences illustrate three effects: continued silencing of Native perspectives, ongoing invisibilization of Native peoples, and resistance to culturally sustaining teaching. Examples include administrators using anti-CRT legislation to halt tribal history training, states disregarding Native history mandates, curricula portraying Native peoples mainly as historical, and teacher candidates resisting discussions of colonialism and racial inequality.

The article concludes that teacher education remains shaped by settler-colonial assumptions and white-centered narratives. It calls for critical democratic education that accurately teaches Native histories and contemporary realities, recognizes tribal nationhood and sovereignty, and prepares educators and students to support democracy and tribal sovereignty.

Sven Henrich agrees with Alan Greenspan that stock and bond markets are in bubbles. He highlights a technical ratio between the 10-year Treasury yield and the S&P 500, which broke a long-term support trend after the 2016 U.S. election and may be forming a multi-year head-and-shoulders pattern. Rising yields alongside falling stocks are driving the ratio lower and could indicate that the rally since early 2016 was a blow-off top. Although Henrich does not predict an immediate collapse, he warns that continued yield increases could produce a prolonged bear market with significant consequences. Bulls need yields to decline or stabilize, though the ratio is nearing critical short-term support.

He recalls that both sides sought to avoid war, yet one chose war rather than preserve the Union while the other accepted it rather than let the nation perish. The article tests a gold trend-following strategy from 1971 using a 12-month simple moving average. It holds gold above the average and cash below it. In the backtest, $100,000 grew to $10 million versus $4 million for buy-and-hold, across 26 trades, excluding commissions and slippage. Similar results occurred with 200–250-day averages. The strategy’s advantage came primarily from avoiding major drawdowns. Gold can be traded through ETFs or futures, though results may differ from spot-price tests. Historical performance offers no guarantee of future results.

The lecture identifies control—especially periodic motion and impacts—as the central challenge in walking robotics. Stable limit cycles are illustrated with the Van der Pol oscillator, whose trajectories converge to a periodic orbit without synchronizing in phase. Poincaré sections convert continuous-time limit-cycle stability into discrete-time fixed-point stability; locally, stability requires the eigenvalues of the Poincaré map’s gradient to have magnitude below one.

Historical walking studies include Muybridge’s animal photography, McMahon’s ballistic walker model, and McGeer’s passive dynamic walkers, which walked down slopes without motors or controllers. The rimless wheel captures essential passive-walking dynamics: gravity adds energy while inelastic ground collisions dissipate it, producing a stable rolling limit cycle when gains and losses balance. Its collision map reduces velocity by a factor of cosine of twice the inter-leg angle, and its behavior can be analyzed analytically through a Poincaré map, including rolling and standing fixed points and their attraction basins.

Ground impact is presented as the dominant energy loss in walking, with appropriately timed push-off potentially improving efficiency. More complex passive models include the compass gait and walkers with knees. These can exhibit stable limit cycles but generally have smaller attraction regions than the rimless wheel. The next lecture will address optimization and control methods for hybrid walking dynamics.

The study analyzed 8,338,877 responses from the U.S. COVID-19 Trends and Impact Survey to estimate county-level mask-wearing from September 2020 through May 2021. Researchers used Bayesian binomial regression to address small county samples, reweighted responses by age, sex, and education, and estimated response bias by comparing self-reported vaccination with county vaccination data. This correction assumed masking and vaccination responses were similarly biased.

Bias-corrected masking varied substantially across counties and was positively associated with population density. Median masking exceeded 0.8 in urban counties but was below 0.6 in the most rural counties. Masking peaked in January 2021 and fell sharply by May, coinciding with rising vaccination, declining infections and concern, relaxed CDC guidance, and removal of many mask mandates; causality was not assessed. Community-reported masking closely approximated corrected self-reported estimates, suggesting community-focused questions may reduce response and social-desirability bias.

The authors conclude that fine-scale behavioral data can support geographically targeted public health measures and disease models better than state or national aggregates. Limitations include unmeasured biases, exclusion of minors, reliance on Facebook users, limited samples, and the untested assumption that vaccination and masking reports share equivalent bias. Accordingly, precise county estimates should be interpreted cautiously, with emphasis placed on relative spatial and temporal trends.

Drug-resistant gram-negative bacteria, particularly carbapenemase-producing organisms carrying KPC or MBL enzymes, present major treatment and infection-control challenges. This study assessed the Disk Potentiation Test (DPT) for detecting these enzymes among 147 imipenem-resistant gram-negative isolates collected at Evercare Hospital, Dhaka, from January to June 2020. KPC was detected using phenylboronic acid and MBL using EDTA.

All isolates were resistant to imipenem, with resistance most frequent among patients over 60, males, and ICU patients. Of the isolates, 39 (26.53%) carried KPC, 66 (44.89%) carried MBL, and 36 (24.49%) carried both; 78 showed neither enzyme. KPC and MBL were most prevalent in ICU isolates. Acinetobacter baumannii was the predominant organism carrying both enzymes, followed by Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Escherichia coli. Tracheal aspirates contained the most isolates with both enzymes. Most resistant isolates had imipenem MICs of at least 16 µg/ml.

The findings support DPT as an accessible phenotypic approach for identifying KPC and MBL and emphasize the need for antimicrobial stewardship, surveillance, and infection-control measures, particularly in ICUs.

Kenneth Kaylor appealed a dissolution judgment requiring rehabilitative alimony, child support, housing expenses, a car, insurance, and children’s medical costs. His approximately $2,000 monthly net income would be reduced to about $600 before several additional obligations. Although his minority interest in an insurance agency might be valuable, it was not readily marketable. The ordered payments plus Sharon Kaylor’s income also exceeded her stated expenses by $175 monthly. The appellate court held that the financial award exceeded Kenneth’s ability to pay, reversed and remanded the financial provisions for reconsideration based on Sharon’s needs and Kenneth’s resources, and affirmed the remainder of the judgment.

The passage describes AGESA host procedures for early processor initialization and related services. A stackless assembler routine allocates per-core Cache-as-RAM stack space, maps it globally, configures x86-64 MTRRs, creates a UEFI handoff structure, and handles real or protected mode. A corresponding BSP-invoked routine disables pre-memory stacks after DRAM and stack relocation are available, flushes caches, and disables CAR mode on all cores. AARCH64 APUs with PSP instead rely on the PSP to initialize DRAM.

AmdCreateStruct allocates and initializes parameter structures using pre-memory heap, post-memory DRAM, or host-provided storage. It requires an established stack, and allocated structures must later be released.

Additional stack-dependent services return a DIMM’s normalized read or write data-eye bitmap, determine an x86-64 processor core’s APIC address and presence, and report per-core cache capacity available for code execution before main memory becomes available. Status codes indicate success, warnings, allocation failures, unknown processor families, or initialization errors.

The coach plans to build on improved late power plays while managing defensemen’s minutes through fresher players and shorter, more frequent shifts. Pushing offensively led to positional mistakes against Detroit.
