Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. Subjects’ median age was 74; 59.9% were male. Mean BMI was 28.7 and MMSE 28.3. Most had atrial fibrillation (96.4%), hypertension (87.2%), and mean CHADS2-VASc score of 3.6.

The speaker credited teammates for creating his goal, reflected on a difficult summer, and expressed gratitude for a chance to pursue the Stanley Cup. He said the team’s confidence has grown but emphasized taking one game at a time. Manny’s advice helped him focus on simple, direct hockey.

Vietnamese higher education comprises public and private institutions overseen by the Ministry of Education and Training and other governing bodies. Before COVID-19, digitalization varied widely: a few universities integrated digital technologies, while many lacked infrastructure, funding, digital skills, online-learning expertise, and consistent governance. Learning management systems were common, but distance education, digital materials, and shared resource repositories remained limited.

COVID-19 accelerated online and blended learning and increased acceptance of educational technology. Government programs through 2030 prioritize digital management, distance-learning platforms, online programs and assessments, digitized materials, shared data warehouses, and individualized learning technologies. Regulations now permit portions of regular bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral programs and assessments to be delivered online.

Most institutions have since developed platforms supporting teaching, learning, administration, and student services, though implementation remains uneven. National education databases and management systems support information sharing, enrolment, and evidence-based decision-making. Digital repositories include electronic lectures, theses, question banks, e-books, private-sector platforms, and emerging open online courses. Challenges include costs, copyright, cybersecurity, inconsistent systems, database coordination, material quality, and unequal institutional capacity.

The paper recommends clearer policy guidance and evaluation frameworks, national training and policy dissemination, targeted government funding for infrastructure and cybersecurity, partnerships with private and international organizations, and leadership development. Institutions should train lecturers in intellectual property, online pedagogy, digital tools, personalized learning, and mentoring, while providing students with digital-skills training and expanded paperless administrative services.

The passage describes electrical characteristics, architecture, peripherals, operating modes, application guidance, and support information for Texas Instruments MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontrollers.

The devices use an Arm Cortex-M0+ CPU operating from 32 kHz to 80 MHz, with instruction prefetch/cache, SysTick, an eight-region memory protection unit, and interrupt management. Five power modes—RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN—use two power domains to balance functionality and consumption. Clock sources include internal and external low- and high-frequency oscillators and a 32–80 MHz system PLL.

Memory features include up to 256/512 kB dual-bank flash, 16 kB data flash, and up to 128 kB SRAM divided into protected and unprotected banks. Flash supports ECC, 1 kB sectors, selected high-endurance sectors, and bank swapping for firmware updates. SRAM supports configurable read-write and read-execute partitions.

Analog functions include two 12-bit, 4-MSPS ADCs with simultaneous sampling, hardware averaging for 14-bit effective resolution, internal temperature and supply channels, and internal or external references. The VREF module provides selectable 1.4 V and 2.5 V references and requires appropriate decoupling. The device also includes comparators with reference DACs and a buffered 8-/12-bit DAC with calibration, FIFO, DMA, and hardware-trigger support. DAC_OUT connects internally to PA15, so external circuitry on that pin should be avoided when DAC_OUT is enabled.

Digital and communication peripherals include up to 93 GPIOs, configurable IOMUX, DMA, an event-routing fabric, UART, I2C with speeds through 1 Mbit/s, SPI through 32 Mbit/s on suitable pins, timers, RTC, independent and windowed watchdogs, and CAN-FD on MSPM0G351x devices. Security functions include AES-128/256 acceleration, secure storage for four keys, configurable firewalls, CRC-16/32, and a true random-number generator.

The boot strap loader supports UART or I2C programming, password protection, optional disabling, hardware invocation, blank-device startup, and software entry. Serial Wire Debug provides debugging access. Factory memory contains read-only device identification, capabilities, and calibration data.

Recommended hardware includes 10 µF and 0.1 µF VDD decoupling capacitors, a 47 kΩ NRST pullup with a 10 nF capacitor, and a 0.47 µF VCORE capacitor. An external precision resistor is required when using the SYSOSC frequency-correction loop. Open-drain 5 V-tolerant outputs require pullups.

The April 2025 revision updates device variants, electrical and timing specifications, operating-mode tables, memory descriptions, peripheral counts, analog specifications, and security details. TI provides development boards, SDKs, SysConfig, Code Composer Studio, third-party toolchains, documentation, and support resources. Experimental “X” devices are intended only for evaluation, while “MSP” devices are fully qualified for production.

Curriculum literacy involves understanding, evaluating, adapting, and implementing curricula, teaching methods, materials, and outcomes. It supports teachers’ pedagogical effectiveness, technology integration, student success, equity, and responsiveness to individual learning needs.

The study used thematic content analysis to examine accessible, peer-reviewed English and Turkish articles retrieved from Scopus using “curriculum literacy.” After excluding six unrelated studies, 29 original articles were analyzed by year, topic, country, discipline, keywords, methods, samples, and themes.

Research attention shifted from curriculum literacy and social studies education in 2010–2015, to activity theory and culture in 2015–2020, and to dyslexia, diagnosis, empowerment, artificial intelligence, and digital tools in 2020–2025. Studies were concentrated in social sciences, with limited representation in psychology, arts, computing, engineering, mathematics, and other fields. Australia and the United States produced the most studies, followed by Türkiye and South Africa.

Findings indicate a positive but weak relationship between digital literacy and curriculum literacy. Curriculum literacy can help teachers use materials effectively, improve pedagogical practices, support student participation, and address cultural, contextual, and individual needs. However, inadequate teacher training, limited time, bureaucratic barriers, and frequent curriculum changes hinder its development.

The study recommends expanding curriculum literacy training in teacher education, providing digital resources and support, encouraging interdisciplinary and international research, integrating innovative technologies, and designing more equitable and inclusive educational programs.

Tube UK supplied ten audio systems for Manchester Day 2017, covering five carnival floats and five city-centre stages. A nine-person crew deployed six vans of equipment, completing installation by midday and dismantling immediately after events ended. Four floats used battery-powered systems, while Graham Massey’s float used an onboard generator. D&B systems and Yamaha consoles supported commentary and music stages across Albert Square, Exchange Square, St Anne’s Square and Cathedral Gardens. The largest system served more than 2,000 people at the Cathedral Gardens finale featuring world music and cross-cultural performances.

Nasdaq 100 E-mini futures are electronically traded, leveraged contracts tracking the Nasdaq 100, an index dominated by large non-financial technology companies. Introduced in 1999, they trade on CME Globex under the symbol NQ and may be used for speculation or equity-market hedging.

Each cash-settled contract equals the index value multiplied by $20 and expires quarterly in March, June, September, or December. The minimum fluctuation is 0.25 index points, worth $5, for outright Globex trades. Regular trading runs from Sunday at 6:00 p.m. to Friday at 5:00 p.m. ET, with a daily one-hour break. Final settlement normally occurs on the third Friday of the contract month.

Trading requires a funded futures-broker account with CME access. Strategies may use technical and fundamental analysis, defined entry and exit points, position sizing, risk management, hedging, arbitrage, or spread betting. A referenced volatility strategy was backtested on daily, continuous, back-adjusted CME data without stops, but its rules and results were not disclosed. Historically, the futures tended to perform better in spring and fall than in winter and summer.

Prices may be affected by Federal Reserve decisions, component-stock prices, economic news, and the US Dollar Index. Leverage amplifies losses from adverse price movements. The passage reports an all-time low of 797.50 on October 3, 2002, and a high of 16,676.50 in November 2021. CFDs differ because they can be held indefinitely and represent agreements with brokers rather than expiring futures contracts.

Federal authorities charged 29-year-old Jonathan Rinderknecht with intentionally starting a New Year’s Day fire that allegedly smoldered underground before reigniting in high winds and devastating Los Angeles’ Pacific Palisades. The Jan. 7 blaze killed 12 people and destroyed more than 6,000 homes and buildings. Investigators cited his knowledge of the ignition site, conflicting location claims, 911 calls, online inquiry about cigarettes causing fires, and possession of a lighter. Rinderknecht was arrested in Florida and faces charges including malicious destruction by fire. Authorities excluded cigarettes, fireworks, lightning and power lines as causes. A separate review found outdated policies, inconsistent practices and communication problems delayed evacuation warnings.

Pets at Home’s Burton branch will hold an autism-friendly hour before opening on Sunday, October 8, as part of a National Autistic Society initiative involving more than 340 stores. Lights will be dimmed, sounds reduced and staff given autism information. The initiative aims to reduce sensory overload, which causes 64% of autistic people surveyed to sometimes avoid shops.

A bear trap is a bullish pattern in which price briefly breaks support during an uptrend, encouraging traders to short before reversing upward and continuing the prior trend. Retail traders may suffer losses when short positions or stop-loss orders are triggered during the reversal. Potential warning signs include bullish divergence in indicators such as RSI or MACD, breaks below support that quickly reverse, trading volume, and positive fundamental news.

The passage attributes bear traps partly to liquidity providers or market manipulators creating selling pressure before buying at lower prices. It also identifies FOMO, impulsiveness, crowd-following, and excessive reliance on price movements as factors that make retail traders vulnerable. Traders are advised to consider technical indicators, company fundamentals, broader market conditions, and risks; remain disciplined; and backtest strategies.

The MSPM0C1105/1106 are ultra-low-power 32-bit microcontrollers based on the Arm Cortex-M0+ core, operating at up to 32 MHz from 1.62 V to 3.6 V across –40°C to 125°C. They provide up to 64 KB flash, 8 KB SRAM, internal 32 MHz and 32 kHz oscillators, DMA, CRC-16, configurable clocks, and RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN power modes.

Integrated peripherals include a 12-bit ADC supporting up to 1.6 Msps, temperature sensor, configurable internal or external voltage reference, comparator with 8-bit DAC, RTC, independent and windowed watchdogs, advanced and general-purpose 16-bit timers, three UARTs, two I2C interfaces, one SPI interface, GPIO, and serial-wire debugging. Communication peripherals support protocols including LIN, IrDA, DALI, Manchester, smart card, SMBus, and PMBus.

Each digital pin is configured through a PINCM register. The IOMUX permits one managed digital function per pin, while compatible analog or wake inputs may operate concurrently if the designer prevents contention. Certain GPIOs can wake the device from SHUTDOWN, while all GPIOs support wake-up from higher-power low-power modes.

Flash supports 1 KB sectors, with up to 100,000 program/erase cycles in the lower 32 KB and up to 10,000 elsewhere. SRAM is retained through STANDBY but lost in SHUTDOWN.

Recommended hardware includes 10 µF and 0.1 µF low-ESR VDD decoupling capacitors placed near the device, a 47 kΩ pullup and 1000 pF pulldown on NRST, appropriate external crystal capacitors, and pullups for 5 V-tolerant open-drain outputs. NRST must remain pulled high for startup.

Henrico County Economic Development Authority director Gary McLaren said Facebook’s planned $750 million data center at White Oak Technology Park will benefit the county. Infrastructure developed for a former semiconductor plant provides excess water and sewer capacity, extensive fiber-optic connections, and redundant power supplies suited to data centers.

Henrico already hosts numerous data centers but cut taxes on computers and related equipment to compete with Northern Virginia’s established industry clusters. Although existing data centers also benefited, McLaren said Facebook’s investment more than offsets the lost revenue, while declining to provide proprietary financial details. Facebook also received an $863,000 water-sewer connection credit from previously allocated development incentives, which McLaren said creates no new taxpayer liability.

Henrico hopes the project will attract additional data centers as suitable Northern Virginia locations and electricity capacity become more constrained. McLaren said the county’s ability to fast-track projects was an important factor in Facebook’s decision.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture improves effective memory bandwidth by about 50% over Pascal through GDDR6 and enhanced lossless compression. Its display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, dual 8K displays at 60 Hz, HDR processing, tone mapping, and USB-C output. Updated NVENC and NVDEC units add 8K HEVC encoding, bitrate savings, broader decoding support, improved streaming quality, and lower CPU use. VirtualLink combines display, power, and USB data for VR headsets through one USB-C connector. TU102 and TU104 replace earlier SLI interfaces with second-generation NVLink, supporting two-way SLI and higher-bandwidth display configurations.

Turing introduces RT Cores for real-time ray tracing and Tensor Cores for AI workloads. RT Cores autonomously accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, allowing shading processors to perform other work. Combined with hybrid rasterization/ray tracing, denoising, acceleration structures, NVIDIA RTX software, DXR, OptiX, and related APIs, Turing can produce real-time reflections, refractions, shadows, and ambient occlusion. Turing is described as achieving over 10 Giga Rays per second and roughly ten times Pascal’s software ray-tracing performance.

NVIDIA NGX uses pretrained deep neural networks and Tensor Cores for graphics features. Deep Learning Super-Sampling renders with fewer samples and infers target-resolution images, providing quality similar to temporal anti-aliasing with less shading work; DLSS 2X targets quality approaching 64-times supersampling. Other NGX functions include image inpainting, interpolated slow-motion video, and AI-based image or video enlargement.

Additional graphics features include Mesh Shading, Variable Rate Shading, Texture Space Shading, and Multi-View Rendering. Mesh Shading introduces task and mesh shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks, process many objects efficiently, select levels of detail, and manipulate geometry. Variable Rate Shading controls shading rates by 16-by-16-pixel regions for content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading separates visibility from appearance sampling and reuses shaded texels across pixels, views, or frames. Multi-View Rendering supports four hardware views per pass and enables more efficient stereo, wide-field VR, shadow, and multi-instance rendering.

TU104 contains up to 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and one x8 NVLink connection, and is used in products including the GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. Tesla T4 uses 2,560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores. TU106, used in the GeForce RTX 2070, contains 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but lacks NVLink and SLI. NVIDIA defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based hybrid-rendering metric combining weighted Tensor, FP32, ray-tracing, and INT32 operations.

The document concludes that real-time ray tracing results from combining hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH acceleration, and RT Cores. It also states that specifications may change, products require suitability testing, and NVIDIA limits warranties and liability.

The lecture reviews the absolute-value criterion for sequence convergence and the squeeze theorem, then uses the binomial theorem and elementary inequalities to prove three limits: \(1/n^p\to0\) for \(p>0\), \(p^{1/n}\to1\) for \(p>0\), and \(n^{1/n}\to1\). The last proof sets \(x_n=n^{1/n}-1\) and uses a binomial coefficient term to show \(0\le x_n\le\sqrt{2/(n-1)}\).

For a bounded sequence \((x_n)\), the lecture defines
\[
\limsup x_n=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{k\ge n}x_k,\qquad
\liminf x_n=\lim_{n\to\infty}\inf_{k\ge n}x_k.
\]
The tail suprema form a bounded decreasing sequence, while the tail infima form a bounded increasing sequence, so both limits exist and \(\liminf x_n\le\limsup x_n\).

Examples show that \((-1)^n\) has limsup \(1\) and liminf \(-1\), whereas \(1/n\) has both equal to \(0\). The sequences of tail suprema and infima need not themselves be subsequences of the original sequence.

Every bounded sequence has subsequences converging respectively to its limsup and liminf. This is proved by choosing sequence terms increasingly close to the relevant tail supremum or infimum and applying the squeeze theorem. Consequently, every bounded sequence has a convergent subsequence, establishing the Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem.

Finally, a bounded sequence converges if and only if its limsup equals its liminf. When they are equal, the sequence is squeezed between its tail infima and suprema; when the sequence converges, subsequences approaching the limsup and liminf must converge to the original limit. Thus the limit, limsup, and liminf all coincide.

This single-center retrospective Chinese study compared tenecteplase with alteplase for acute ischemic stroke treated within 4.5 hours. It included 120 patients receiving tenecteplase and 144 receiving alteplase. Baseline characteristics were generally comparable, although hyperlipidemia and atrial fibrillation prevalence differed.

Tenecteplase was associated with shorter onset-to-treatment, door-to-needle, and door-to-puncture times. More tenecteplase patients met targets of door-to-needle within 45 minutes and door-to-puncture within 120 minutes. Regression analysis identified tenecteplase as an independent predictor of achieving both workflow targets.

At 24 hours, neurological improvement was more frequent with tenecteplase than alteplase (64.17% versus 50%), and tenecteplase independently predicted improvement. Symptomatic and overall intracranial hemorrhage rates did not differ significantly between groups. Higher baseline NIHSS predicted hemorrhage, while atrial fibrillation predicted any intracranial hemorrhage. Tenecteplase patients also had shorter hospital stays.

The findings suggest that tenecteplase offers early clinical and workflow advantages with safety comparable to alteplase. Its rapid single-injection administration may reduce treatment and transfer delays. Limitations include the single-center, retrospective, nonrandomized design, early outcome assessment, and predominance of mild-to-moderate strokes. Larger multicenter studies with longer follow-up are needed.

The Sandwich Islands’ strategic Pacific position made their potential transfer to another maritime power unacceptable to the United States. Hawaii’s political decline, local support for annexation, and its value as a commercial stopping point prompted requests for detailed information on its population, trade, resources, industry, and debt. The American representative was instructed to avoid committing the government while discreetly assessing Hawaiian officials’ views on annexation.

After King Lunalilo died without naming a successor in February 1874, unrest followed the legislature’s election of David Kalakaua. At Hawaiian authorities’ request, American naval forces landed to protect government institutions and suppress rioters. British forces also intervened without initial authorization, later formalized through an antedated request. Both forces withdrew on February 20. Later that year, Kalakaua visited the United States to encourage reciprocity negotiations, receiving official courtesies and transportation, despite opposition from British and French commissioners.
Maikel Kieftenbeld’s red card against Bristol City was overturned on appeal, allowing the Birmingham City midfielder to avoid a three-match ban and face Bolton Wanderers.

Amid escalating tensions in Korea, Japan told the United States that its troops were needed to maintain order, secure Korean independence, and compel administrative reforms addressing corruption and oppression. Japan denied territorial ambitions and said it would withdraw only after future stability was assured. China, described by the U.S. chargé at Peking as conciliatory, sought peaceful settlement through foreign good offices and requested that the United States urge the powers to press Japan to withdraw. The United States expressed sympathy for Korea, concern over possible war, and willingness to offer neutral good offices, but stated that action protecting Japanese interests in China required Chinese assent and declined to join Great Britain or other powers in a joint intervention.

The study examines digitalization in education, accelerated by technological development and COVID-19-related remote work and learning. Digital education uses technology to support online, hybrid, personalized, collaborative, and interactive learning, but also requires digital competence, updated content, cybersecurity, and equitable access.

Using a qualitative design, researchers collected semi-structured interview responses from 20 private-sector education expert-managers; five were also interviewed through Zoom. Data were analyzed through content analysis.

Participants identified major challenges including technological and financial limitations, unsuitable or insufficient digital content, resistance to change, limited digital literacy, distraction, unequal opportunities, and difficulties combining work with training. Organizations adapted through online and hybrid training, digital platforms and academies, training videos, workshops, projects, and technological tools.

Reported benefits included access independent of time and location, time and cost savings, broader participation, equal opportunity, personalized learning pace, increased accessibility, and expanded e-learning content. Negative effects included concentration problems, reduced interaction, difficulty conducting practical activities, lower event efficiency, cyberbullying, assessment problems, cheating, and perceptions that digital education is less effective than face-to-face instruction.

Participants generally defined digitalization through technological opportunities and easy access. The study concludes that educational organizations must adapt, create suitable digital content, and use tools such as virtual reality and gamification. However, it is considered premature to fully digitalize education, and face-to-face learning is expected to remain alongside digital approaches.

The disclosure describes channel state information (CSI) reporting for beam operation in wireless networks, including LTE and 5G NR. A user equipment (UE) is configured with at least two CSI reference-signal resources, measures them, generates multiple CSI reports—including at least one based on multiple resources—and reports at least one CSI. CSI may include channel quality, precoding matrix, rank, precoding type, and CSI-RS resource indicators.

The approach addresses high-frequency systems where narrow, high-gain beams and multiple transmission/reception points are needed for coverage, reliability, and throughput. It supports analog, digital, and hybrid beamforming and scenarios using multiple beams or transmission points to send identical or different data.

The passage also describes MIMO transmitter, receiver, and communication-device architectures and summarizes 3GPP procedures for periodic and aperiodic CSI reporting. These procedures define CSI processes, reference and interference-measurement resources, reporting modes, triggering, timing, wideband and subband feedback, and dependencies among CQI, PMI, RI, CRI, and PTI. Aperiodic reports are generally triggered through uplink control information and sent on PUSCH, while periodic reports are configured by higher layers and sent on PUCCH according to specified periods and offsets.

The study presents an end-to-end superconducting-material discovery workflow combining guided DiffCSP generation, machine-learning screening, DFT calculations, and experimental validation. A foundation model pretrained on more than two million crystal structures was fine-tuned on approximately 7,200 conventional superconductors and used to generate 200,000 candidates conditioned on target critical temperature. Guidance shifted generated properties toward targets within the training range but failed to extrapolate to 110 K.

After relaxation, deduplication, and screening for metallicity, thermodynamic and dynamical stability, and superconducting propensity, 773 of 34,027 unique structures had DFT-calculated critical temperatures above 5 K and energies within 200 meV/atom of the convex hull. The 2.3% hit rate was about 135 times that of an element-substitution baseline and 2.8 times that of a prior generative approach. Most candidates were ternary or quaternary compounds.

Eighteen candidates were selected for arc-melting synthesis. Nine showed superconductivity above 4.2 K, but measured critical temperatures were lower than predicted. X-ray diffraction generally showed that the predicted ordered structures had not formed; samples instead consisted mainly of disordered body-centered-cubic solid solutions or mixtures of known phases. The authors identify incomplete reference convex hulls, sparse chemical-space data, and failure to account for disorder and synthesizability as major limitations. Proposed improvements include experimental active learning, local DFT refinement, practical multi-objective constraints, disorder-aware screening, and alternative generative and guidance methods.

New Brunswick will operate 20 recreational marijuana stores in 15 communities under CannabisNB, an NB Liquor subsidiary. Buyers must be 19, public smoking will be banned, possession limited to 30 grams outside the home, and cannabis stored securely at home. Stores were selected using demographic and market data.

Zimbabwe Yadzoka/Mayibuye iZimbabwe launched a campaign encouraging Zimbabweans abroad to return and register for the 2018 election, claiming the Zanu PF government sought to suppress diaspora voting. Leader Victor Chimhutu said mobilisation would begin in selected European, North American and African cities, alongside global protests against President Robert Mugabe. He urged those unable to return to support mobilisation inside Zimbabwe and called for opposition parties to form a coalition to challenge Zanu PF.

Crook County Medical Services District is adding a wheelchair-accessible patient transport van, family rooms for end-of-life care, and renovated emergency and imaging facilities. The van was funded through a grant and family trust donation, while patient families funded the new family rooms. Supported by the USDA and Sundance State Bank, renovations are expected to begin this month and finish by September. Two former operating rooms will house new CT and X-ray equipment, and the current X-ray room will become a modern trauma room. The equipment, funded through a Helmsley Foundation grant, will improve imaging and reduce patient exposure. The district’s nursing home also received a Women’s Choice Award as one of America’s Best for Extended Care, based on federal survey data, staffing, quality, infections, and other measures. The recognition followed another strong annual survey in which the facility successfully met new rules.

Rent-A-Center shares rose 3.63%, closing at $9.99. Seven analysts set an average 12-month target of $10.79, ranging from $5 to $15. The stock’s average brokerage recommendation is 2.5, based on eight recommendations, while its industry ranks 183 of 265. Ratings include three Buys, five Holds, one Underperform, and no Outperform or Sell ratings. Its 14-period ATR is 0.42, with weekly volatility of 3.80% and monthly volatility of 4.72%. The RSI is 58.84. Rent-A-Center has a market capitalization of $567.33 million and 56.79 million outstanding shares. Previous trading volume was 1.01 million shares, below the average of 1.71 million.
Self-reported memory and focus difficulties among U.S. adults ages 18 to 39 nearly doubled from 2013 to 2023, for unknown reasons.

This study used bibliometric analysis to examine 487 English-language Web of Science articles published between 1980 and 2023 on mathematics and mathematics education in special education. Using bibliometrix and R, it analysed publication growth, authors, journals, keywords, citations, and collaboration networks.

Publications increased notably in 2017 and 2020, with an annual growth rate of 7.56%. The articles appeared across 120 sources, involved 1,093 authors, averaged 24.94 citations, and contained 17,813 references. Most were published in special education journals, particularly the *Journal of Special Education* and *Remedial and Special Education*. Bouck Ec was identified as an influential author. “Students,” “mathematics,” and “children” were the most prominent keywords, reflecting studies’ frequent focus on student and child participants.

Author collaboration across groups was limited. The United States had the strongest international cooperation network, followed by the United Kingdom, while the University of Florida, Purdue University, and Vanderbilt University were prominent institutional collaborators.

The study recommends expanding research participation to teachers and families, examining teachers’ mathematical and pedagogical knowledge, using digital tools and artificial intelligence, strengthening international and institutional collaboration, and incorporating disciplines such as psychology, educational technology, and linguistics. Findings are limited to Web of Science records and the selected search terms and software.

Amazon’s two best-selling espresso machines, the Ninja Luxe Cafe Premier and Breville Barista Express, are each $100 off ahead of Prime Big Deal Days on October 7-8. The beginner-friendly Ninja includes a 25-setting grinder, built-in scale, milk steaming, and cold brew and drip coffee options, at its lowest observed price. The durable, easy-to-use Breville combines a built-in grinder with reliable espresso extraction, though its sale price remains above its previous $550 low.

JAXA launched the world’s smallest orbit-capable rocket from Kagoshima, carrying a three-kilogram Earth-imaging satellite. The mission tested affordable micro-satellite launches amid growing private-sector demand, following a failed 2017 attempt caused by a short circuit.

Two Hamilton schools and a daycare recorded excessive lead in water tests; officials said corrective measures, including bottled water and filters, were implemented. Provincewide, more than 640 schools and daycares failed required tests over two years. Lead exposure can harm children’s intellectual development, and new sampling rules may increase failures.

Australian financial intelligence agency AUSTRAC is suing Commonwealth Bank of Australia over nearly 54,000 alleged breaches of anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorism financing rules, potentially exposing the bank to billions of dollars in fines. The case cites Chinese national Jizhang Lu, who pleaded guilty to laundering A$3.2 million for an alleged international drug syndicate through meat exporter CC&B International. Lu delivered cash to CC&B in exchange for receipts documenting fake meat purchases, after which the money was deposited with CBA. AUSTRAC alleges A$17.7 million in criminal proceeds was deposited on CC&B’s behalf between February and August 2015. Lu was jailed for two years, while two CC&B employees were also charged and a company director left Australia. CBA plans to contest the lawsuit, attributing most alleged breaches to an ATM coding error while acknowledging other serious allegations.

SynDoc is a hybrid framework for zero-shot key information extraction from domain-specific visually rich documents. It combines a discriminative vision-language model, called the warmer, with a generative multimodal large language model (MLLM). Its synthetic-data workflow uses OCR or PDF parsing, MLLM-generated semantic and spatial question-answer pairs, and quality verification for meaningfulness and answer consistency.

The warmer is adaptively trained to learn document text, visual, layout, structural, and domain-specific features. It uses grid matching, span-based question answering, and entity retrieval. During recursive inference, warmer-retrieved entities are added to the MLLM prompt, and outputs from both models are repeatedly cross-fed until predictions stabilize.

Experiments used FormNLU, CORD, Ephoie, and FUNSD, evaluated primarily with Averaged Normalized Levenshtein Similarity. Proprietary MLLMs generally outperformed open-source models, with Gemini serving as SynDoc’s main generator. Adding warmer guidance generally improved zero-shot results on domain-specific datasets, while sometimes introducing noise on the cross-domain FUNSD benchmark. Bounding-box guidance, top-k retrieval, structural adaptation, prior MLLM outputs, and recursive inference often improved performance. Meaningfulness verification consistently helped adaptive tuning, whereas consistency verification could be harmed by OCR errors. Top-3 retrieval produced substantial gains over top-1, while gains from top-5 were limited.

Recursive inference improved both warmer retrieval and generated answers, though optimal iteration counts varied by model and dataset. Open-source models generally required more iterations than Gemini, and OCR-challenging datasets benefited from additional iterations. SynDoc showed robust domain-specific performance, but further improvements are needed for cross-domain generalizability and robustness.

- **ISDA Master Agreements:** Smaller, non-rated derivatives customers should prioritize liquidity by limiting dealers’ early-termination rights. Key negotiation points include narrow cross-default definitions, appropriate thresholds, cross-acceleration requirements, limits on credit events and additional termination events, prompt termination payments, and adequate cure periods.

- **Brazilian energy crisis:** Brazil ordered government offices to reduce electricity consumption by 10% and anticipated rationing due to low hydroelectric reservoirs and long-term underinvestment. Partial deregulation, delayed privatizations, currency risks, and insufficient transmission capacity hindered investment. Some companies developed private generation, while Petrobras expanded thermal projects amid operational and environmental controversies.

- **Merchant banking capital rules:** Financial-industry groups criticized proposed Federal Reserve and Comptroller rules imposing graduated capital charges on financial holding companies’ nonfinancial investments. They favored internal risk models, exemptions or grandfathering for existing and small-business investments, and narrower treatment of mixed-activity companies.

- **Swap spreads:** Analysts expected U.S. dollar swap spreads to narrow further as the yield curve steepened, while euro spreads could remain stable or widen near term because anticipated European rate cuts were already priced in. Longer-term euro fundamentals could support renewed narrowing.

- **Federal debt paydown:** Alan Greenspan said sustained budget surpluses could reduce publicly held Treasury debt to an irreducible minimum. Debt reduction could lower interest rates and increase investment, productivity, and income, but government accumulation of private assets could distort capital allocation. He expected markets to develop alternatives to Treasuries for benchmarks, hedging, and low-risk investment. The Federal Reserve was considering alternative assets, collateral, and lending mechanisms while consulting market participants and Congress.

- **Enron weather note:** Enron offered an Internet-traded structured note tied to weather in 19 U.S. cities and promised a secondary market. The product targeted institutional and speculative investors seeking returns with low correlation to equities.

After a long path to the NHL, the goalie values reaching the Stanley Cup Finals and wants to capitalize on the opportunity. He credits supportive coaches who introduced techniques without forcing him to change his unconventional style. A year earlier, he was recovering from hip surgery and focused only on rehabilitation. Although uncertain before the playoffs whether the team could reach the Finals, he believed it had potential. Throughout the season and playoffs, the team proved resilient and battle-tested, repeatedly finding different ways to win despite deficits, lost leads, and difficult games.

Nova Scotia is seeking public feedback on setting the legal cannabis age at 19, Crown corporation sales, permitted use locations and drug-impaired driving. The survey runs until Oct. 27 as provinces prepare for federal legalization by July 1, despite concerns about the timeline.

The lecture reviews Fiat–Shamir transformation, which removes interaction by replacing verifier challenges with a hash function. Although the Kilian–Micali protocol is sound in the random-oracle model, proving soundness for explicit hash functions is difficult. The lecture focuses on a parallel-repeated, zero-knowledge Hamiltonicity protocol and a 2019 result by Canetti, Lombardi, and Wichs showing Fiat–Shamir soundness in the standard model for a suitable commitment and hash function.

In the Hamiltonicity protocol, the prover commits to a randomly permuted graph and responds either by opening a Hamiltonian cycle or by revealing the permutation and nonedges. A single execution has soundness error one-half, so it is repeated in parallel with fresh permutations. The commitment is implemented using public-key encryption, with a trusted common reference string supplying a correctly generated public key. Its secret key acts as a trapdoor that reveals which verifier challenge would let a cheating prover succeed.

The central construction uses fully homomorphic encryption, which permits circuit evaluation on encrypted data. The Fiat–Shamir hash key contains an encryption of a circuit, and evaluation homomorphically computes that circuit on the prover’s first message. In the security proof, the encrypted circuit is replaced with a special circuit that uses the commitment trapdoor to find the unique bad challenge, decrypts it, and flips a bit. Consequently, the resulting hash output cannot equal the bad challenge. Semantic security ensures an efficient cheating prover cannot distinguish this special encrypted circuit from the original one.

Because the special circuit contains the fully homomorphic encryption secret key, the presented proof assumes circular security: encryptions of the secret-key bits are indistinguishable from encryptions of zeros. The lecture notes that later lattice-based work removes this circular-security requirement. The technique supports noninteractive zero-knowledge proofs and extends beyond Hamiltonicity to protocols such as sum-check, GKR, SNARGs, and batch arguments.

The lecture develops spacetime models for static, spherically symmetric compact bodies with perfect-fluid interiors and vacuum exteriors. Using Schwarzschild coordinates, the radial coordinate is chosen as an areal radius, so spheres have area \(4\pi r^2\), though radial proper distance is generally not \(r_2-r_1\). Isotropic coordinates are presented as an alternative.

Solving the vacuum Einstein equations shows that the exterior metric functions satisfy \(\phi=-\lambda\). Matching the large-radius, nonrelativistic limit to Newtonian gravity fixes the integration constant and yields the Schwarzschild metric. Birkhoff’s theorem states that this metric describes the vacuum exterior of any spherically symmetric body, even when the body varies in time while preserving spherical symmetry. Such variations produce no gravitational waves, and the exterior depends only on the mass and distance from the center.

For the interior, the body is modeled as a static perfect fluid with radius-dependent density and pressure that vanish outside its surface. Defining a mass function gives
\[
m(r)=\int_0^r 4\pi r'^2\rho(r')\,dr'.
\]
This gravitational mass differs from the proper-volume-integrated baryonic mass, with their difference interpreted as gravitational binding energy.

Combining the Einstein equations with local stress-energy conservation produces coupled equations for the mass, metric potential, and pressure gradient. With a central density, an equation of state relating pressure and density, and surface matching conditions, these equations determine the interior spacetime. The relativistic hydrostatic-equilibrium equation is the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equation, used to construct static, spherically symmetric relativistic stellar models.

The author raises Netflix’s price target from $144.46 to $160.73 but downgrades the recommendation from High Conviction Buy to Buy because upside is more limited. Netflix remains suitable as a long-term holding for investors able to withstand volatility, though near-term expectation risk is elevated.

The central issue is international subscriber growth, particularly whether Netflix guides to at least 52 million international members by Q2 2017. With few other growth drivers after prior price increases and migration to higher-tier plans, revenue expectations depend heavily on international additions. The author raises the fiscal-year revenue estimate from $10.9 billion to $11.285 billion, slightly above the $11.23 billion consensus, and increases diluted EPS expectations from $0.97 to $1.16. Profitability appears easier to improve than revenue because content costs are projected to grow more slowly than sales. Potential competition from Apple does not materially change the investment thesis.

The April 16 reports cover energy-market developments involving Enron and other power companies. Competing bandwidth-trading agreements reflect disagreement between firm and best-efforts contracts. Sierra Pacific shares fell 8.3% after it suspended its dividend amid high wholesale power costs, while its purchase of Enron’s Portland General remained delayed. California’s energy crisis prompted investigations and lawsuits alleging market manipulation by largely unmonitored wholesalers, though companies denied wrongdoing. Independent power producers expected strong first-quarter earnings from elevated energy prices and trading activity despite unpaid California debts and possible refunds. Seattle City Light spent a record $92 million on power in March, including $25.5 million from Enron, as drought and soaring market prices drove rate increases.

West Midlands Police created a 24-hour task force after 28 recent home burglaries involving tens of thousands of pounds in jewellery. Victims were threatened or assaulted, including a newborn threatened in Balsall Heath and women held at knifepoint. One arrest has been made. Police urged jewellery owners to secure valuables and report suspicious people or vehicles.

Cisco announced webcast participation in two San Francisco investor conferences: CEO Chuck Robbins at Goldman Sachs on February 16, 2017, and SVP/GM David Goeckeler at Morgan Stanley on February 28. Webcasts will be available through Cisco Investor Relations.

Aspetuck Land Trust offers three April guided walks: a hawk walk at Trout Brook Valley on April 22, a spring wildflower hike there April 23, and a stone walls walk at Poindexter Preserve April 29. Reservations are required; each hike is limited to 30 participants.

Update packages must match a system’s specific firmware and patch levels. Updates run alongside x86 and DMA traffic with minimal performance impact. Most require little or no OS quiescence, though SEV or SEV/ES virtual machines must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates; SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

A randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated SA58, a broad-spectrum anti-COVID-19 monoclonal antibody nasal spray, as post-exposure prophylaxis among healthy adults in Beijing exposed to SARS-CoV-2 within 72 hours. Participants self-administered SA58 or placebo 5–6 times daily. The trial ended early after COVID-19 restrictions were lifted.

Of 1,634 randomized participants, 1,222 received treatment and were followed: 901 received SA58 and 321 placebo. After excluding baseline RT-PCR-positive participants, efficacy analysis included 824 SA58 recipients and 299 placebo recipients. Symptomatic laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 occurred in 7 SA58 recipients and 14 placebo recipients, corresponding to an estimated efficacy of 80.82% (95% CI 52.41%–92.27%). SARS-CoV-2 infection occurred in 32 participants in each group, giving an estimated efficacy of 61.83% (95% CI 37.50%–76.69%). All sequenced infections were Omicron BF.7. No severe COVID-19 cases or deaths occurred.

Adverse events were reported by 25% of SA58 recipients and 22% of placebo recipients. All were grade one, with no serious adverse events, adverse events of special interest, withdrawals, or deaths. Common events included nasal dryness, runny nose, fever, nasal congestion, headache, cough, and throat dryness, with no significant group differences.

The findings suggest SA58 may safely reduce symptomatic COVID-19 and SARS-CoV-2 infection after early exposure. Limitations included the short follow-up, early termination, small sample size, predominantly young and healthy workforce, and isolation practices that may have reduced transmission. Further evaluation in larger studies and high-risk populations was recommended.
