Mesh Shading adds Task and Mesh Shaders using cooperative thread models, reducing CPU draw-call bottlenecks, supporting dynamic level of detail, and enabling real-time rendering of many complex objects. Variable Rate Shading independently controls shading rates for 16×16-pixel regions and supports content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading decouples visibility from appearance sampling, stores and reuses shading results, and can improve stereo VR rendering. Multi-View Rendering processes up to four hardware views per pass and supports VR, shadow maps, and multiple object instances.

Turing also expands DX12 resource binding and heap support. Its VR features include VirtualLink, Multi-View Rendering, foveated rendering, and RT Core acceleration for VRWorks Audio.

The full TU104 contains 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, 13.6 billion transistors, and one x8 NVLink connection. Tesla T4 uses a TU104 configuration with 2,560 CUDA Cores and 320 Tensor Cores. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, contains 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, 36 RT Cores, and 10.8 billion transistors, but lacks NVLink and SLI.

NVIDIA defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based hybrid-rendering metric combining weighted Tensor, FP32, ray-tracing, and INT32 operations. The document concludes that hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH algorithms, and RT Cores collectively make real-time ray tracing practical on Turing GPUs.

Autoliv plans to spin off and list its electronics business, which develops radar, vision and driver-assistance systems, in the third quarter of 2018. Its airbags and seatbelts business will retain the Autoliv name. Shares have risen 20% since September.

Apple filed a Form 8-K dated October 27, 2015, reporting the issuance of a press release and data sheet covering financial results for its fourth fiscal quarter ended September 26, 2015. The documents are attached as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. CFO Luca Maestri signed the report.

British police declared a major incident after a man and woman in their 40s were found unconscious in Amesbury following suspected exposure to an unknown substance. Both remained critically ill in Salisbury hospital. Counterterrorism officers joined the investigation because of the recent Novichok poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal nearby. Authorities cordoned off locations and increased patrols, while officials said no significant public health risk was believed to exist. Testing was underway to identify the substance.

PPP official Taj Haider said Bilawal Bhutto Zardari would begin an aggressive Punjab election campaign in South Punjab, addressing rallies in major cities. He urged authorities to ensure fair polls and said PPP had supported democratic continuity despite alleged past rigging.
The figures show multiple views of a portable fan; broken lines indicate portions excluded from the claimed design.
SpaceX launched NASA’s TESS aboard a Falcon 9 on April 18 from Cape Canaveral to search nearby stars for exoplanets suitable for follow-up observations.

The Amazon’s 2024 fire season was its most destructive in over two decades, affecting 3.3 million hectares and releasing an estimated 791 million tons of carbon dioxide—roughly Germany’s annual emissions and seven times the prior two-year average. For the first time in the 2022–2024 analysis, fire-driven forest degradation surpassed deforestation as the region’s main source of carbon emissions. Extreme drought linked to climate change, forest fragmentation, and land-use mismanagement likely contributed. Brazil recorded its highest emissions from forest degradation, while fires affected over 9% of Bolivia’s remaining intact forests. Researchers combined satellite monitoring systems with Monte Carlo simulations to detect damage and estimate emissions. The study urges coordinated fire reduction, stronger forest protections, support for local and Indigenous stewardship, and climate finance addressing degradation as well as deforestation.

Dell Technologies will expand Salesforce’s cloud CRM, sales, and marketing tools to nearly 40,000 sales employees and provide global customer contact centers access to the AI-powered Service Cloud Einstein. The companies will use Dell Boomi to share cloud data, supporting Dell’s approximately 200,000 channel partners. The agreement extends their decade-long relationship, which also includes Salesforce using Dell EMC infrastructure and Dell laptops. Salesforce has ranked as IDC’s leading CRM provider for four consecutive years.

Canada’s S&P/TSX composite reached a record high Wednesday, driven by gains in energy, financial, technology and health-care stocks following Senate passage of the cannabis bill. U.S. indexes were mixed. The Canadian dollar fell to a one-year low amid U.S. rate and trade concerns, while oil rose and gold and copper declined.

Tuberculosis remains a major global cause of death, particularly among people living with HIV. Zambia is among the 30 countries with the highest TB burden, with severe cases and most TB-related deaths managed at secondary and tertiary hospitals.

This retrospective audit reviewed 74 TB-related mortality files from patients aged at least 16 years who died at Kitwe Teaching Hospital between June 2018 and June 2019. Thirty files were excluded because death occurred within 24 hours of admission or TB lacked clear confirmation. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, radiological and HIV-related data were analyzed.

Among the reviewed deaths, 67.6% were male, the mean age was 39.2 years, 83.8% lived in high-density residential areas and 81.1% were HIV-positive. Common presentations included cough (41.9%), fever (40.5%), diarrhea (29.7%), productive cough (27.0%), headache (21.6%) and shortness of breath (16.2%). Admission findings included elevated mean pulse rate, while measurements before death showed lower mean arterial pressure and persistent respiratory abnormalities. Anemia affected 39.2% of patients. Laboratory findings also indicated hypoalbuminemia, renal dysfunction and abnormal liver enzymes, suggesting multi-organ involvement.

The audit identified male sex, age below 50 years, HIV infection, high-density residence and unstable hemodynamics as prominent features among inpatient TB deaths. Limitations included retrospective reliance on incomplete or missing records. The authors recommend improved early recognition of clinical instability, particularly among young and middle-aged HIV-positive males, and a prospective study to identify mortality predictors and assess malignancy as a contributing factor.

The patent describes an orthopedic surgical ecosystem using mixed, virtual, augmented, and extended reality for patient-specific joint repair. It supports preoperative planning, implant and instrument selection or manufacture, intraoperative guidance and tracking, postoperative monitoring and analysis, predictive analytics, and surgical education. Patient imaging generates three-dimensional anatomical models and surgical plans that clinicians can review, modify, and visualize relative to actual anatomy. Wearable or handheld visualization devices use displays, cameras, depth and motion sensors, voice, gaze, and gestures to present and manipulate virtual models and procedural guidance. Applications include shoulder and ankle arthroplasty, bone preparation, implant placement, tool identification, range-of-motion assessment, remote collaboration, workflow checklists, and AI-assisted diagnosis and surgery recommendations.

Uzbekistan’s sum gained about 9% against the dollar on the black market amid expectations of exchange-rate liberalisation. Authorities ended mandatory foreign-currency sales by exporters, while full convertibility and unified rates remain pending. Currency controls have been cited as a major barrier to foreign investment.

The passage references memory maps for L4 peripheral domains and interconnect documentation. The DDR DMM TILER provides an additional 4-GB range using a 33rd address bit for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views; the full range is limited to HDVPSS and ISS, while other masters can access one view through the base-map 512-MB TILER region. Terminal-function tables document pin names, multiplexing, ball numbers, types, pulls, supplies, control registers, and deselected states. Boot configuration pins sample BTMODE settings at reset for GPMC and reset-output behavior, then operate as GPMC data/address pins.

The speaker said defensive mistakes caused an early deficit, despite strong offensive pressure and a promising third period. Returning to play felt good, and line changes helped create chaos. With each team winning at home, the team looks forward to returning to Chicago, tightening its defense, and matching its third-period intensity. The opponent was described as deep, fast, and difficult to handle, but the team remains confident after adversity.

Plex is launching free podcast support in beta on iOS, Android, Roku, and Plex Web, without requiring Plex Pass or a media server. Features include podcast recommendations, home-screen access, playback controls, and variable speeds. Updated mobile apps add customizable screens, tabs, and default locations for content across multiple Plex servers.

The Boring Company sold 20,000 $500 novelty flamethrowers, but customs objections prompted Elon Musk to consider renaming them. The propane-torch-like devices shoot flames under 10 feet and include serial numbers and free fire extinguishers.

Passive investing has grown since the 2008/09 financial crisis because it requires limited time and effort, reduces costs and cognitive mistakes, and can provide satisfactory retirement returns. Vanguard, founded by passive-investing pioneer John Bogle, manages more than $6 trillion and is popular for its low costs, straightforward strategies, and broad selection of stock and bond funds.

Eight highlighted retirement options are four LifeStrategy funds—Income, Conservative Growth, Moderate Growth, and Growth—and four Target Retirement funds—Income, 2040, 2050, and 2060. LifeStrategy funds invest in four underlying Vanguard funds, with allocations ranging from bond-heavy income portfolios to stock-oriented growth portfolios. Target Retirement funds provide diversified stock and bond exposure and become more conservative as retirement approaches. The dated funds eventually align with the Target Retirement Income Fund, generally within seven years after their target dates.

A five-fund Vanguard Retirement Portfolio was backtested from 2007 to 2023 using buy-and-hold investing with annual rebalancing and dividend-adjusted prices. Its value increased from $10,000 to $23,317. Returns were lower than the S&P 500 Total Return Index because of bond allocations. Investors are advised to review each fund’s prospectus to determine whether it matches their goals.

The speaker accepts the presidency with humility and faith, praising national progress while warning that disregard for law threatens self-government. He calls for reform of the federal justice system, vigorous enforcement of the Eighteenth Amendment, citizen cooperation against illegal liquor, and a national commission to investigate enforcement and court procedures.

He supports regulation rather than government ownership of private enterprise, federal cooperation with state, local, and private welfare efforts, broader educational opportunity, and organized public health services. Internationally, he rejects imperialism, supports disarmament, arbitration, judicial settlement of disputes, and practical efforts toward lasting peace while avoiding binding political commitments such as League of Nations membership.

He emphasizes responsible party government, requests a special congressional session on agricultural relief and tariff changes, and identifies mandates including constitutional integrity, economy, business regulation, government reorganization, public works, and welfare programs. He affirms equality of opportunity, ordered liberty, honest government, education, religious tolerance, strong homes, and peace, concluding with confidence in the nation and a request for public and divine assistance.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K reporting that it released third-quarter 2017 financial results on November 1, 2017. Its shareholder letter for the quarter ended September 30, 2017, was posted online and attached as Exhibit 99.1. CFO Deepak Ahuja signed the report.

Italy’s business lobby, Confindustria, lowered its 2025 growth forecast amid U.S.–EU tariffs, a strong euro and expected export stagnation through 2026. It sees domestic investment as the main growth driver, with household consumption offering limited support. The government is expected to revise its forecasts accordingly. Confindustria warned that trade disputes, geopolitical uncertainty, public debt and EU budget constraints threaten recovery, emphasizing the need for productivity and competitiveness reforms.

The “Back Cut” offense attacks a Diamond & One defense’s weaknesses in the corners and middle, creating open shots, layups, and offensive rebounds while using baseline screens to free the star player. Its sequence includes post entries, wing and baseline back cuts, weak-side back screens, corner shots or drives, and single/double-screen actions. If defenders anticipate the screens, the star can reverse direction for an open shot while a screener rolls to the basket. Effective execution requires coordinated screening, strong post play, defensive recognition, nonverbal communication, timing, and experience. Preparation should include isolation drills and scrimmaging. Teams should scout defensive tendencies and matchups, recognize in-game adjustments, vary alignments and entries, and target weak defenders. In a Diamond & One, four defenders play zone while a fifth denies passes to the opponent’s leading scorer.

The patent describes a controllable nanosecond pulsed electric field (nsPEF) generator for electrotherapy, particularly tumor treatment. NsPEF pulses can induce apoptosis in tumor cells while limiting thermal effects on surrounding tissue and may stimulate an immune response.

The system includes a controller, adjustable power supply, pulse generator, user interface, therapeutic electrode, and sensors. Users may specify pulse amplitude, width, frequency, quantity, polarity, rise and fall times, or treatment limits such as tissue temperature, energy, and average power. Feedback signals representing voltage, current, pulse characteristics, tissue temperature, electrode conditions, or other parameters allow the controller to adjust power-supply and pulse-generator control signals. Control may use PID methods, lookup tables, or fixed-step adjustments.

The pulse generator uses a Marx-switch stack architecture containing serially connected semiconductor switches, including MOSFETs, within each stage. This permits stage charging voltages above an individual switch’s rating while using relatively few stages, providing high voltage, low impedance, high current, adjustable pulse duration, and improved efficiency. Multiple generator circuits may be connected in parallel to increase current or in series to increase voltage. Transformer-coupled drivers electrically isolate and synchronously control the switches, while diodes, snubbers, clamps, and overcurrent circuits provide decoupling and protection.

Pulse duration generally follows the control pulse duration, although transformer saturation can limit excessively long output pulses. Example outputs include approximately 15 kV, 50 A pulses lasting 15 or 30 nanoseconds.

Suction, needle, and two-pole electrodes may position tumors between opposing polarities and deliver pulses through tumor tissue. Electrodes can incorporate voltage, current, and temperature monitoring and may be adapted for percutaneous or endoscopic use.

Described feedback methods repeatedly generate and measure pulses, compare measured characteristics with desired values, and modify control settings. Adjustments can regulate pulse amplitude and width, verify generator charge voltage, or reduce voltage, frequency, or pulse width when tissue temperature, delivered energy, or average power approaches specified limits.

Senator Leila de Lima rejected Francis Tolentino’s allegations of fraud in the 2016 Senate election, saying a recount in his chosen pilot precincts found no irregularities or vote recovery. De Lima, who placed 12th ahead of 13th-ranked Tolentino, accused him of delaying his electoral protest through unnecessary procedures and seeking former elections chief Andres Bautista as a hostile witness. She dismissed Tolentino’s comparison to Juan Miguel Zubiri’s 2011 resignation, arguing that Aquilino Pimentel III’s earlier protest was supported by recount results. De Lima urged Tolentino to accept his defeat and stop pursuing what she called a baseless protest.

Care Compliance Expert aims to improve elder and dementia care by promoting higher care standards and greater attention to health and safety in care homes. The company says quality treatment can improve residents’ mood and quality of life. It provides professional advice across several areas and consults with governmental organizations on regulatory changes.

Authorities are investigating a fire that destroyed South Carolina Circuit Judge Diane Goodstein’s beachfront home on Edisto Island and injured at least three family members. Officials found no evidence that the fire was intentionally set or that a prefire explosion occurred. Occupants escaped by jumping from the elevated first floor and were rescued by kayak. Goodstein’s husband, Arnold Goodstein, 81, was airlifted to a hospital. Goodstein recently temporarily blocked the state Election Commission from providing voter registration data to the federal government, but the South Carolina Supreme Court reversed her order.

SpaceX plans to launch NASA’s first mission using a previously flown Falcon 9 and Dragon capsule, carrying nearly 5,000 pounds of supplies to the International Space Station. NASA says the inspected recycled booster poses similar risks to a new one. The launch also marks the reopening of rebuilt Launch Complex 40, damaged in a 2016 explosion.

Lexington County authorities are seeking a woman suspected of making more than 60 baseless 911 calls between March 25 and April 14, mostly from the Saint Andrews area. Officials say the calls delay genuine emergencies and endanger officers and drivers. Anonymous tips may be submitted to Crimestoppers by phone or text.

Scientists documented the first modern case of rapid “river piracy” at Canada’s Kaskawulsh glacier. In May 2016, a 30-metre canyon formed at the glacier’s end, redirecting most meltwater from the Slims River toward the Alsek River and Pacific Ocean rather than the Bering Sea. The once-deep, swift Slims became shallow and nearly still, while the Alsek grew deeper and faster. Researchers ruled out rainfall changes and calculated only a one-in-200 chance that the glacier retreat and rerouting occurred naturally without human-caused global warming. Outside scientists described the study, published in Nature Geoscience, as significant evidence of climate change’s widespread and surprising effects.

CPI(M) leader Prakash Karat described Tripura’s February 18 election as nationally significant and expressed confidence in an eighth Left Front government. He accused the BJP-IPFT alliance of conspiracy and criticized BJP governance, communal unrest, cow-protection harassment and pro-corporate policies. Karat praised Tripura’s Left Front government as clean, pro-people and protective of tribal rights and social harmony.

France reached the World Cup quarter-finals after a 4-3 victory over Argentina, driven by 19-year-old Kylian Mbappé’s two goals and earned penalty. Antoine Griezmann, Olivier Giroud and Paul Pogba helped create opportunities, while Benjamin Pavard scored a memorable long-range goal. France next face a more defensively robust Uruguay side led by Luis Suarez and Atlético Madrid defenders Diego Godin and Jose Maria Gimenez, who have conceded only once in four matches. Edinson Cavani’s probable injury absence weakens Uruguay’s attack, but their playing and defensive style is expected to remain largely unchanged. France enter the match as favourites to reach the semi-finals.

Fort Bend ISD crews and contractors worked overnight to repair air conditioning problems at Quail Valley Elementary and Marshall High School following a hot three-day weekend. Marshall students said Tuesday was unusually warm, prompting some to gather in the cooler cafeteria while fans were placed in hallways. The district restored cooling by Wednesday. Despite discomfort, students noted it was a half-day near the end of the school year.

TI recommends close placement of 10µF and 0.1µF VDD decoupling capacitors, a 47kΩ/10nF NRST network, an optional precision 100kΩ resistor for SYSOSC frequency correction, a dedicated 0.47µF VCORE capacitor, and pullups for 5V-tolerant open-drain outputs.

MSP devices are qualified production parts; X-prefixed devices are experimental and unsuitable for production. TI provides development hardware, SDKs, cloud tools, SysConfig, training, GUI tools, IDEs, compilers, documentation, update notifications, and support forums. Appropriate ESD precautions are required.

The April 2025 revision updates device variants, peripheral counts, operating modes, electrical and thermal specifications, memory endurance, timing, analog characteristics, security features, and peripheral descriptions. Mechanical, packaging, ordering, soldering, and material information may change. TI provides resources “as is”; developers remain responsible for product selection, design validation, testing, and regulatory compliance.

Night or overnight trading means holding positions from the market close until the next day’s open, unlike after-hours trading. Since 1993, virtually all S&P 500 gains have occurred overnight, while repeatedly holding from open to close produced no return. The average overnight S&P 500 gain is 0.04%. Gold shows a similar 0.03% overnight gain, while gold miners have displayed an even stronger overnight tendency and poor daytime returns.

The passage attributes the overnight bias mainly to inflation, earnings growth, and compensation for overnight risk. However, the average edge alone may not cover commissions and slippage, so effective trading rules and backtesting are necessary. A previously published strategy remained profitable out of sample despite flat years, and a portfolio of three 24-hour strategies produced 950 trades averaging 0.33% each. The article concludes that overnight stock strategies offer reasonable risk and reward but are unlikely to generate substantial wealth.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K reporting that it released financial results for the quarter and year ended December 31, 2019. Its Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2019 Update, dated January 29, 2020, was posted online and attached as Exhibit 99.1. CFO Zachary J. Kirkhorn signed the filing.

Two oral GLP-1 drugs showed weight-loss benefits in clinical trials involving people with obesity. A 25-milligram dose of semaglutide produced an average body-weight reduction of nearly 14 percent among more than 300 participants over 64 weeks. Orforglipron, a small-molecule drug developed by Eli Lilly, led to about 11 percent average weight loss at the highest dose among more than 3,000 participants over 72 weeks.

Unlike most injectable GLP-1 medications, the daily pills require neither needles nor refrigeration and may be easier and cheaper to manufacture and distribute. Side effects included nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and constipation, generally fading over time. Researchers observed no liver toxicity, though larger, longer-term studies are needed to establish risks and benefits. The drugs could become available by 2026, depending on FDA approval, and may improve access for people unable to obtain current GLP-1 treatments.

Dengue lacks effective direct-acting antivirals, while available vaccines provide uneven protection across viral serotypes. AT-752 is an oral guanosine nucleotide prodrug that is metabolized to AT-9010, an inhibitor of dengue virus RNA polymerase with pan-serotype antiviral activity.

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1 study evaluated single ascending doses of 250–1500 mg and multiple doses of up to 750 mg three times daily in 65 healthy subjects. AT-752 was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events or adverse-event-related discontinuations. Treatment-emergent adverse events were mild or moderate and resolved by study completion; gastrointestinal events occurred mainly at higher doses.

AT-281, the parent prodrug, was rapidly eliminated, while AT-273, a surrogate marker for intracellular AT-9010, had a 15–25-hour half-life and accumulated with repeated dosing. Steady state was largely reached by Day 3. The 750 mg three-times-daily regimen maintained AT-273 trough concentrations above the in vitro 90% effective concentration for dengue replication. Pharmacokinetics were comparable between Asian and predominantly Caucasian cohorts. Food delayed and reduced peak concentrations of several analytes but had little effect on total exposure, indicating AT-752 may be taken with or without food.

These safety and pharmacokinetic findings support further clinical evaluation and dose selection for AT-752 as a potential dengue treatment. The study was funded by Atea Pharmaceuticals.

Paleontologist Ashley Leger monitors Los Angeles Metro Purple Line construction for fossils, as required by California environmental laws. Since the extension began in 2014, crews have uncovered Ice Age remains from rabbits, mastodons, camels, bison and horses. The most significant discovery was the intact skull of a juvenile Columbian mammoth, excavated over 15 hours with both tusks attached. Named Hayden, the rare specimen is being studied and displayed at the La Brea Tar Pits and Museum. Construction continues elsewhere during excavations, with transit workers assisting scientists. Similar urban projects have uncovered fossils and historical artifacts in San Diego and near Boston.

The provisional government in Cuba will end after peaceful elections and inauguration. The United States hopes Cuba will preserve justice, order, prosperity, and independence, but warns that fraudulent elections or recurring insurrection could require renewed American intervention to protect life and property. Cubans are urged to ensure orderly government, rights, and freedom from rebellion.

The Third International Conference of American Republics met in Rio de Janeiro from July 23 to August 29. It harmoniously addressed trade, communication, freer intercourse, and mutual understanding, completing its work more efficiently than previous conferences. Brazil and Rio were thanked for their hospitality. The Secretary of State attended and then visited Brazil, Uruguay, Argentina, Chile, Peru, Panama, and Colombia, carrying a message of peace, friendship, and cooperation that received an enthusiastic response.
Wall Street stocks fell as healthcare companies and banks declined. Goldman Sachs, Johnson & Johnson and Cardinal Health dropped, while Treasury bond prices rose.

NTT Docomo installed smartphone wipes in some restrooms at Tokyo Narita International Airport until March 15. The wipes advertise its Wi-Fi and translation app while addressing phone hygiene concerns highlighted by studies finding fecal germs and high bacteria levels on phones.

The Supreme Court allowed Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook to remain in office while it considers in January 2026 whether President Donald Trump has legal cause to remove her. Trump alleges Cook committed mortgage fraud, which she denies; she has not been charged. The decision preserves Cook’s participation in upcoming interest-rate meetings and leaves intact an injunction blocking her dismissal during her lawsuit. The case could affect the Federal Reserve’s independence from political interference.

The March 2011 earthquake, tsunami, and Fukushima nuclear emergency devastated Japan and severely disrupted its automotive industry. About 80% of Japanese automotive plants initially suspended production, while overseas factories faced shortages because they depended partly on Japanese components. Nissan sustained damage at six facilities, and around 50 critical suppliers were impaired.

Japanese manufacturers had historically adopted just-in-time production, reducing inventories but increasing vulnerability when material or information flows were interrupted. Nissan differed from Toyota’s closely controlled supply chain by using a decentralized regional structure combined with strong central coordination during crises. Its simplified product line, flexible organization, diverse leadership, and crisis-oriented culture supported rapid responses.

Following financial difficulties and its 1999 alliance with Renault, Nissan developed a formal risk-management system emphasizing early risk identification, preventive measures, business continuity planning, seismic reinforcement, and disaster simulations. Its emergency plan prioritized human life, prevention of further damage, rapid recovery, business continuity, and community support.

Within 15 minutes of the earthquake, Nissan activated its Global Disaster Control Headquarters and later formed a Recovery Committee. Its response centered on four practices: sharing information globally by bringing regional staff to Japan; allocating scarce components to higher-margin products; adjusting production based on inventories and anticipated bottlenecks; and empowering managers to make rapid decisions. Nissan used in-transit inventory to gain time, obtained alternative supplies and air freight, rescheduled vacations, and continually revised production plans.

Nissan’s localization strategy and supply-chain flexibility helped insulate it from some constraints affecting competitors. In 2012, it announced plans to raise localized vehicle production in the Americas from about 70% to 90% by 2015 and reduce Japanese components used in North America. It also sought greater visibility beyond first-tier suppliers and stronger business continuity plans covering second- and third-tier suppliers.

The articles describe California’s escalating 2001 electricity crisis. Gov. Gray Davis pursued long-term power contracts, conservation, new generation and purchases of utility transmission lines, including a possible $7 billion-plus deal with PG&E. Critics questioned contract secrecy, above-market prices, unresolved reimbursement of state power purchases and whether sufficient electricity would be available for summer. The state had spent billions buying power and planned a $10 billion bond issue, but revenue constraints raised concerns about rate increases, the budget and California’s credit rating.

PG&E and Southern California Edison faced nearly $13 billion in debt after wholesale costs rose above regulated retail rates. Nonpayment prompted El Paso Energy to close six cogeneration plants producing about 175 megawatts. Analysts and lawmakers debated price caps, retail rates, conservation incentives, faster plant construction and alternative-energy payments. A bill to lower alternative-power prices stalled over unequal payment provisions.

Utilities sought layoffs and relaxed service standards, while regulators considered potential effects on outage restoration, meter reading and customer service. Municipal utilities, including Sacramento’s SMUD, sought exemption from PG&E-directed rolling blackouts, arguing they had secured supplies and conservation measures.

Officials approved a temporary 51-megawatt peaker plant at San Francisco International Airport, while Contra Costa County explored additional sites amid environmental and community opposition. Separate hearings considered PG&E’s proposed $91 million Tri-Valley transmission upgrade. One commentary also cited a broader estimated $90 billion infrastructure gap and advocated coordinated regional planning, demand management and realistic pricing.

Thermoelectric performance requires high power factor and low thermal conductivity, but these properties are coupled. N-type Bi₂Te₃₋ₓSeₓ alloys particularly face strong anisotropy and intrinsic defects. This study used scalable melting–hot pressing followed by annealing to decouple carrier and phonon transport.

Bi₂Te₂.₆Se₀.₄ was identified as the optimal composition. Annealing at 723 K for 100 h caused Te(Se) volatilization and cation-vacancy formation, reducing carrier density from 3.02 × 10¹⁹ to 2.43 × 10¹⁹ cm⁻³ while increasing mobility to 295.97 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹. The resulting Seebeck coefficient and power factor improved. Volatilization-induced point defects and pores increased phonon scattering, lowering room-temperature lattice thermal conductivity to 0.48 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹.

The annealed sample achieved a room-temperature ZT of 0.78, a peak ZT of 1.06 at 373 K, and an average ZT of 0.99 over 300–423 K. Annealed samples prepared by either hot pressing or spark plasma sintering consistently outperformed unannealed counterparts. The method offers a practical route to n-type Bi₂Te₃-based materials for thermoelectric cooling and chip-level thermal management.

Schaeffler created the 1,180-hp electric Audi RS3 4ePerformance using four Formula E motors, all-wheel drive, torque vectoring, and 64-kWh batteries. It reaches 124 mph in seven seconds. Audi is shifting toward practical electric models, while growing manufacturer participation and electric-car launches may strengthen Formula E’s marketing importance.

The study addresses limitations in ISO 25023 accessibility metrics by developing a classification, mathematical model, and evaluation methods focused on users with visual impairments. It divides accessibility into perceptiveness, operability, understandability, and localization. These subproperties are measured through weighted attributes including alternative text, color contrast, subtitles and audio descriptions, keyboard and structured navigation, clear instructions, input assistance, error-message support, and language availability.

The methodology was applied to the Vasyl Stefanyk Precarpathian National University website using automated tools and expert-derived weighting coefficients. The portal received an overall accessibility score of approximately 0.68, classified as “excellent” on the proposed scale. Strong results included keyboard navigation, clear instructions, color contrast, and error-message support. Major weaknesses were the absence of subtitles, audio descriptions, and input assistance, along with limited alternative text and structured navigation.

The proposed approach provides quantitative accessibility assessment, identifies areas for improvement, and supports compliance with ISO 25023 and WCAG requirements.

The Supreme Court agreed to hear five cases during its 2025-26 term. One challenges Hawaii’s 2023 law barring concealed-carry permit holders from bringing handguns onto publicly accessible private property without owners’ affirmative permission and into designated “sensitive places.” Challengers argue the law violates the Second Amendment and that the 9th Circuit improperly relied on post-Reconstruction firearms regulations rather than founding-era history.

Two cases concern claims under a 1996 federal law allowing U.S. nationals to sue over property confiscated by Cuba. Exxon Mobil seeks compensation from Cuban state-owned companies for property seized in 1960, while Havana Docks seeks to sue cruise lines that used confiscated docks between 2016 and 2019.

Another case involves a Michigan estate seeking the difference between a foreclosed home’s alleged fair market value and unpaid taxes, arguing that receiving only the auction-sale surplus violated the Fifth and Eighth Amendments.

The court will also decide whether federal transportation law bars a state negligence claim against a broker accused of selecting an unsafe motor carrier or driver.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K on May 25, 2022, reporting the release of financial results for the quarter ended May 1, 2022. Exhibits include the fiscal 2023 first-quarter earnings press release and CFO commentary by Colette M. Kress. The materials are furnished rather than filed under applicable securities laws.

Kit Kat’s November 14, 2001 social update promotes the November 30 grand opening of Boaka Bar at 1010 Prairie, featuring complimentary food, champagne, martinis, DJs and visual entertainment. It also lists numerous Houston-area nightlife, music, dining, networking, charity and sports events through New Year’s Eve, along with venue details, prices, schedules, contacts and promotions.

HIV disproportionately affects minoritized populations because of social and structural determinants such as racism, stigma, economic conditions, housing instability, transportation, and healthcare access. These factors also create inequities in access to and adherence with prevention and treatment interventions, including pre-exposure prophylaxis and antiretroviral therapy. Structural interventions targeting policies, environments, social determinants, and service delivery may help reduce these disparities, but their implementation in the United States remains understudied.

This systematic review will identify determinants, implementation strategies, adjunctive interventions, and literature gaps related to implementing structural interventions for HIV evidence-based interventions. Searches conducted across multiple databases from May to July 2024 identified 8,098 records before deduplication. Eligible studies must focus on HIV/AIDS, have at least half their sample in the United States, include original behavioral or social science research, assess implementation outcomes, and examine interventions that alter external conditions or target social determinants.

Natural language processing screened 8,092 titles and abstracts across five eligibility domains, identifying 405 records for inclusion and 4,285 for further inspection. Trained reviewers will conduct duplicate title, abstract, and full-text screening, followed by data extraction. Determinants will be coded using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research, while implementation strategies and adjunctive interventions will be classified using ERIC, the Theoretical Domains Framework, and COM-B. Analyses will examine intervention types, populations, settings, outcomes, health equity, effectiveness, and research gaps.

Results will be disseminated through papers, conferences, and an interactive literature dashboard. Title and abstract review is underway; analyses are planned from June 2025 through June 2026, with dissemination from fall 2025 through fall 2026.

Public agricultural lands should be reserved for resident settlers, while laws enabling acquisition by nonsettlers should be reformed. Western grazing lands require different acreage standards from fertile homesteads, and unlawful fencing of public land should be stopped. Congress should address these issues, possibly through an expert commission. Alaska needs liberal land and homestead laws promoting permanent settlement, protection of forests, game, and salmon fisheries, regulated timber use, congressional representation, and direct investigation of its needs. Indian policy should aim at gradual absorption while recognizing differences among tribes. Advanced tribes on fertile land may receive individual allotments, but others should not be forced into unsuitable arrangements; on prairie lands, pastoral village life may be preferable to isolated farming.

An experiment found that 6-year-olds performing repetitive tasks worked harder and stayed more focused when pretending to be Batman or Dora the Explorer, while those focused on themselves took more breaks.

Mod-Cam is the first-light and commissioning receiver for the 6-meter Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope and a testbed for Prime-Cam instrument modules. Its modules use large arrays of superconducting kinetic inductance detectors (KIDs), whose resonant frequencies respond to both absorbed radiation and bath-temperature fluctuations.

The study characterized Mod-Cam’s cryogenic performance, detector-stage stability, and thermal responsivity for aluminum and titanium-nitride KIDs in the 280 GHz module. A dilution refrigerator cools the detector stage to approximately 100 mK, while a PID-controlled heater stabilizes its temperature. Measurements were primarily conducted in a dark, cold-load configuration. Temperature was recorded at 10 Hz for eight hours, and detector responsivity was measured by varying the bath from 96 to 105 mK and tracking resonant-frequency shifts.

The 100 mK stage exhibited an RMS temperature fluctuation of \(3.2\times10^{-5}\) K. Measurements of 2,409 aluminum and 1,886 titanium-nitride detectors yielded median thermal responsivities of \(1.995\times10^{-4}\) K\(^{-1}\) and \(-6.081\times10^{-4}\) K\(^{-1}\), respectively. Using previously measured optical responsivities, the resulting equivalent optical-power fluctuations at a 5 pW load were 0.20 fW for aluminum and 0.11 fW for titanium nitride, corresponding to 0.0040% and 0.0023% of the incident power. At 9 pW, they were 0.27 fW and 0.13 fW.

These results show that cryogenic thermal fluctuations contribute negligibly to detector noise, validating Mod-Cam’s thermal design and control system. Future work will directly measure optical responsivity using a cryogenic blackbody source.

This study examined self- and other-oriented mentalization, attachment insecurity, and personality pathology within DSM-5’s Alternative Model of Personality Disorders. The sample included 109 psychiatric inpatients and community participants aged 18–47; 54% met criteria for a personality disorder. Mentalization, attachment, personality functioning, and maladaptive traits were assessed through interviews, self-reports, and a performance-based social cognition task.

Self-mentalizing deficits strongly predicted impairments in both self and interpersonal functioning and all five maladaptive trait domains: Negative Affectivity, Detachment, Antagonism, Disinhibition, and Psychoticism. Correct other-mentalizing predicted fewer interpersonal functioning difficulties but did not significantly predict maladaptive traits when self-mentalizing was considered. Models explained 18%–55% of outcome variance.

Attachment anxiety predicted Criterion A impairments and generally all Criterion B traits, while attachment avoidance was associated primarily with Detachment. Correct other-mentalizing weakened the relationship between attachment anxiety and interpersonal impairment and between attachment avoidance and Detachment. Hypermentalizing intensified interpersonal impairment associated with attachment anxiety, while undermentalizing and nonmentalizing intensified Detachment associated with attachment avoidance. Self-mentalizing moderated associations between attachment anxiety and both Negative Affectivity and Detachment.

The findings indicate that self-mentalizing has a broad association with personality pathology, whereas other-mentalizing relates more specifically to interpersonal functioning and Detachment. The authors suggest prioritizing self-mentalizing while tailoring other-mentalizing interventions to interpersonal and attachment-related difficulties. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, small heterogeneous sample, unassessed comorbid disorders, and differing assessment methods.

Finder.com’s survey found that 78.3% of respondents, representing 192 million Americans, admitted making financial mistakes. The most common regret was overspending on shopping, vacations, dining, and other entertainment, cited by nearly 64%. Women reported this more often than men and were also more likely to regret allowing a partner to control family finances. Men more frequently regretted bad investments and excessive gambling.

About 20% of both men and women regretted dropping out of college. Bureau of Labor Statistics data showed college dropouts had lower median wages and higher unemployment than bachelor’s degree holders.

Financial regrets also varied by generation. Millennials most frequently reported overspending on fun, while baby boomers were most likely to regret bad investments. Other regrets included expensive weddings, online scams, and having children. The passage emphasizes recognizing triggers, researching education and career choices, and learning from past financial mistakes.

The Missouri Supreme Court will consider whether the Missouri Human Rights Act’s ban on sex discrimination covers sexual orientation and gender identity, issues not explicitly named in the law and treated inconsistently by lower courts.

In one case, transgender student R.M.A. sued the Blue Springs school district after being denied access to boys’ restrooms and locker rooms. His attorneys argue gender identity is a protected sex-related trait. The district contends the law does not mention gender identity and that school districts cannot be sued as “people” under the act. Lower courts dismissed the case.

The second case involves gay state employee Harold Lampley, who alleged mistreatment for not conforming to male stereotypes, and co-worker Rene Frost, who alleged retaliation because of their friendship. The Human Rights Commission rejected their complaints as sexual-orientation rather than sex discrimination, but an appeals court ruled that mistreatment for perceived insufficient masculinity can constitute sex discrimination. The state argues Lampley alleged only sexual-orientation discrimination and that courts cannot add protections absent from the statute.

Denmark’s Systemic Risk Council urged restrictions on interest-only and variable-rate mortgages for highly indebted borrowers in Copenhagen and Aarhus to protect financial stability. The government has three months to adopt the recommendation or publicly justify rejecting it.

MIT’s Advanced Data Structures course covers temporal and geometric data structures, dynamic optimality, memory hierarchies, hashing, integers, dynamic graphs, strings, and succinct structures. The lecture introduces pointer machines, whose constant-size nodes contain data or pointers and are manipulated relative to a root.

Temporal data structures include persistence, where past versions remain accessible, and retroactivity, where past operations can be changed. Four persistence levels are described: partial persistence permits updates only to the latest version; full persistence permits updates to any version, forming a version tree; confluent persistence combines versions, forming a DAG; and functional data structures prohibit modifying existing nodes.

Any pointer-machine data structure with constant in-degree and out-degree can be made partially or fully persistent with constant amortized time overhead and constant additional space per change. Partial persistence stores back pointers and a bounded list of timestamped field modifications. When this list fills, a new node is created, current modifications are applied, and incoming pointers are recursively updated. A potential-function argument establishes constant amortized overhead.

Full persistence additionally maintains version ancestry using a tree linearized through beginning and ending markers in an order-maintenance structure. Full modification lists are split between nodes, and pointers are recursively updated; amortized analysis again yields constant overhead. Partial persistence can be deamortized to constant worst-case slowdown, while doing so for full persistence remains open.

Confluent persistence is harder because versions form a DAG and operations can create exponentially large conceptual structures. A general method incurs overhead related to effective version depth, and whether constant time and space overhead can be achieved when queries are also charged remains open. Under the restriction that merged versions share no nodes, logarithmic overhead is possible using techniques including link-cut trees and fractional cascading.

Functional techniques include path copying for balanced binary search trees, functional deques with constant-time concatenation, and persistent tries. Several questions about efficient splitting, concatenation, confluence, and the gap between functional and ordinary data structures remain open.

The work introduces an active-learning queue-prioritization algorithm for generative scientific screening workflows. A retrained surrogate model predicts candidate properties and uncertainty, while customizable acquisition functions reorder generated candidates according to exploitation, exploration, and multiple design objectives. This aims to reduce evaluation of unreasonable candidates, improve surrogate models, and prevent generative-model decay caused by iterative retraining on poor outputs.

The method is demonstrated for generating metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for carbon capture. DiffLinker generates organic linkers, molecular dynamics simulations assess internal strain, and XGBoost predicts strain for prioritization. Additional objectives include synthesizability and similarity to known MOF linkers. Tests show that active learning improves identification of stable MOFs across fine-tuning settings, offsets model decay, and supports multi-objective prioritization. A weak-exploration upper-confidence-bound strategy provides the best combined stability discovery and prediction accuracy. Among 1,000 candidates, active-learning prioritization yields an average of 604 high-performing candidates versus 281 without it, while adding approximately 0.6%, and less than 1% overall, computational overhead.

The speaker is doubtful to play tonight despite daily improvement since being injured against Ottawa two weeks ago. He will know after skating, does not want to hinder the successful team, and feels proud, included, and ready to celebrate with teammates.

Jim Cramer reversed his bullish view on Snap after its controversial redesign drew user and celebrity criticism, raising concerns about declining engagement and advertiser departures. Although fourth-quarter revenue rose 72% and shares initially surged over 40%, those gains disappeared. Cramer now considers the stock expensive and risky but may buy at a lower price. Snap will report first-quarter results May 1; Wall Street expects a $0.17 adjusted loss per share on $243.85 million in revenue.

Markets face seasonal weakness, thin liquidity, tax-loss selling and institutional rebalancing. TLT shows a bullish divergence despite resistance and a mean-reversion sell signal; further yield declines and weaker dollar performance could support stocks and commodities. Growth continues to outperform value, while rising gold and falling yields may signal risk-off conditions. The passage also promotes Investing.com’s stock screener and warns that trading financial instruments and cryptocurrencies carries substantial risk and that website data may be inaccurate or delayed.

Professor Noelle Selin explains mercury’s global transport, accumulation in food chains, neurological and cardiovascular risks, and major sources, including coal combustion, products, industrial processes, and artisanal gold mining. She describes the development of the 2013 Minamata Convention, emphasizing how domestic regulations, national interests, limited enforcement, industry participation, and developing-country capacity shaped negotiations. The treaty addresses emissions, trade, products, waste, mining, and mercury phaseouts, but is expected mainly to prevent future increases initially. Selin highlights regulatory leadership by the EU and US, the importance of capacity building and safer technologies, and the treaty’s broader political signal against mercury use.

Researchers led by Dr. Shinichi Furuya demonstrated that pianists can alter piano timbre through precise key manipulation. Using the Hackkey non-contact sensor system, they measured all 88 keys at 1,000 frames per second and 0.01 mm resolution while 20 internationally renowned pianists performed intended timbres such as bright, dark, light, and heavy.

In listening experiments with 40 participants, intended timbres were consistently recognized regardless of musical experience, though pianists showed greater sensitivity. Differences remained perceptible after controlling for volume and tempo. Statistical analysis identified movement features—including acceleration during escapement and variations in hand synchronization—that contributed to timbre. Experiments varying individual features provided evidence of a causal relationship between key movement and perceived timbre.

Published in PNAS, the findings could support evidence-based music education, injury prevention, neuroscience research, rehabilitation, skill transfer, and human-interface design by making previously tacit performance techniques measurable and teachable.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of Florida’s Southern District was fired by email while observing Rosh Hashanah after conservatives publicized past blog posts attributed to him criticizing President Donald Trump. Rosenzweig, who joined the office in 2020 and handled complex economic crimes, allegedly called Trump “mentally unfit” and “an institutional terrorist.” He is among dozens of federal prosecutors reportedly dismissed for perceived conflicts with Trump or his agenda. The Justice Department also fired three Southern District of Florida prosecutors who had worked with former special counsel Jack Smith. Smith recently criticized dismissals of career public servants, attacks on the rule of law and politically motivated investigations. Days later, Virginia U.S. Attorney Erik Siebert left after Trump pressured him to indict Letitia James and James Comey.

Tennessee middle schooler Keaton Jones went viral after his mother shared a video describing the bullying he faced. Celebrities, including LeBron James and Mark Ruffalo, publicly supported him and condemned bullying.

As high street banks continue closing branches, mobile-only firms such as Atom Bank, Monzo and Revolut are growing. A Which? survey of 9,076 members found over half of under-40s would consider a mobile-only account, but interest dropped sharply among older respondents. Branchless banking may offer competitive savings rates, yet Atom Bank’s app crash highlighted the risks of lacking in-person service. Customers concerned by closures cited difficulties with online banking, cash deposits and resolving problems, while others supported alternatives such as enhanced ATMs, shared facilities and mobile branches.

North American stock markets declined Friday. The S&P/TSX composite fell 81.78 points to 15,694.52, while the Canadian dollar edged up to 79.70 cents US. U.S. indexes also slipped after nonfarm payrolls fell by 33,000 in September amid hurricane disruptions, though wages rose a stronger-than-expected 0.5 per cent, lifting the dollar. Declines in Costco, technology and energy shares weighed on markets. The TSX will close Oct. 9 for Thanksgiving, while U.S. markets remain open.

A confidential memorandum proposes preparing U.S. peace negotiators through secret, concise studies by selected experts in history, commerce, international law, disarmament, guarantees, arbitration, and political institutions. Articles of 10,000–15,000 words, supported by indexed documentary and statistical appendices, would be centrally assigned, reviewed, printed, and organized under one director.

A separate memorandum raises questions about U.S. involvement in European boundaries and colonial redistribution; appropriate grounds for territorial settlements; the roles of race, language, religion, nationality, prior affiliation, conquest, and colonization; and conditions governing colonial possessions.

Colonel E. M. House tells Secretary Lansing that President Wilson discussed the proposed work with him. House expects to visit Washington, welcomes Lansing’s advice, and praises the memorandum as helpful for planning an organization.

The lecture examines digital identity and blockchain applications. Identity is discussed as a contextual aggregation of attributes, while credentials and attestations allow third parties to verify claims. Identity and access management systems provide authentication and authorization through users, service providers, identity providers, and certificate authorities. Public-key cryptography and digital signatures secure websites, although current password recovery and identity verification remain imperfect.

Major identity-management problems include data breaches, identity theft, forged credentials, privacy risks, and difficulties updating personal information. Estonia’s e-identity system and India’s Aadhaar biometric identification system demonstrate large-scale digital identity without blockchain. Aadhaar has improved access to services but has also experienced breaches, errors, and public controversy.

Self-sovereign identity would give individuals greater control, direct access, portability, and interoperability of identity attributes. Blockchain could reduce verification costs and fraud, improve provenance and privacy, and decentralize public-key infrastructure. However, distributing personal information across nodes creates privacy concerns, immutable records may conflict with deletion rights, attributes must be updated, private keys can be stolen or lost, and adoption requires cooperation from governments and businesses. Storing hashes rather than personal data may address some concerns.

Numerous digital identity initiatives exist, including token-funded projects, Bitnation, the Distributed Identity Foundation, the World Wide Web Consortium, and MIT’s blockchain-backed diplomas. Gensler concludes that blockchain may suit some identity applications, but many projects remain experimental, face policy and economic barriers, and must be evaluated critically rather than accepted as either universal solutions or mere hype.

This methodology paper describes KaviKrishna’s community-based participatory research approach to tuberculosis control in rural Northeast India. It combines Indigenous Knowledge Systems, temple-based communication networks, telemedicine, trained community volunteers, clinical monitoring, nutritional support, and laboratory research. Since 2010, the program has screened 300 pulmonary TB cases and 500 suspected cases and maintains longitudinal follow-up data.

Laboratory methods include sputum processing and culture, drug-susceptibility testing, PCR differentiation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis from non-tuberculous mycobacteria, whole-genome sequencing, lineage and mutation analysis, minimum inhibitory concentration and killing assays, and detection of viable but non-culturable bacteria. Clinical studies also collect blood and bone marrow to investigate dormant MTB within mesenchymal stem cells and its possible role in reactivation and multidrug resistance. Mouse studies found viable dormant MTB in lung and bone-marrow stem-cell populations and observed reactivation following coronavirus-induced stress.

Preliminary findings identified circulating MTB lineages and rpoB and rpoC mutations in MTB recovered from stem-cell populations of relapsed, sputum-negative patients, suggesting the stem-cell niche as a potential site for studying MDR evolution. The authors propose that integrating community participation, Indigenous networks, patient-specific surveillance, and molecular analysis could complement existing TB-control programs. Patient follow-up data are provided as supplementary material, and sequencing data are available under NCBI accession PRJNA1054003.

Insecticides India plans to invest Rs 200 crore over three years to expand plants in Gujarat and Rajasthan, adding two synthesis facilities and an export-oriented unit. It expects 10–15 percent revenue growth this fiscal, supported by normal monsoons and new product launches. Fiscal 2017-18 net profit rose 41 percent to Rs 83.97 crore, while total income reached Rs 1,109.63 crore.

Defendants Antonio Vasquez and Hector Perez were charged after allegedly attempting to steal a chained bicycle with bolt cutters but abandoning the effort following a conversation with a third person. The jury acquitted them of attempted petit larceny and resisting arrest but convicted them of possessing burglar’s tools. They sought to set aside the conviction, arguing that renunciation should also apply to the possession charge because they abandoned their intent to commit larceny. The court held that Penal Law § 40.10 limits renunciation to specified offenses, including criminal attempts, and does not authorize it as a defense to possession of burglar’s tools. Although troubled that the statute provided defendants little benefit for abandoning the theft, the court concluded that any expansion of the defense was for the Legislature and denied the motion.

The Supreme Court said the CBI-led MDMA investigation into the wider conspiracy behind Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination had made little progress and could be “endless.” It added the Centre as a party to convict A G Perarivalan’s plea seeking suspension of his life sentence until the probe into the belt bomb is completed, and scheduled a January 24 hearing. Perarivalan, convicted of supplying batteries allegedly used in the bomb, said he had served 26 years and that Tamil Nadu had decided to release him. His death sentence was commuted in 2014 due to delays in deciding his mercy plea.

OSCAR is a one-shot, multi-label causal discovery framework for high-dimensional event sequences. It uses two pretrained Transformer-based autoregressive density estimators to identify each label’s Markov Boundary through conditional mutual information testing and to quantify whether events increase or inhibit label likelihood. Its GPU-parallelized design is independent of event and label cardinality, enabling sequence-specific causal analysis in minutes. Theoretical identification relies on temporal precedence, bounded lagged effects, causal sufficiency, and perfect modeling of the joint distribution.

OSCAR was evaluated on vehicle diagnostic data containing 29,100 event types, 474 defect labels, and sequences averaging about 150 events. On 50,000 samples, it achieved 55.26% precision, 31.37% recall, and 40.02% F1 in 11.7 minutes. Five local structure-learning baselines failed to produce Markov Boundaries within a three-day timeout. The framework provides interpretable causal subgraphs that may support diagnostic rule refinement, though evaluation is affected by changing expert-defined rules and approximately 12% missing Markov Boundary rules.

The ambassador pattern separates application logic from external communication concerns. Applications connect to localhost while an ambassador discovers and brokers services, routes requests, or splits traffic between production and experimental systems. Request splitting can direct a percentage of users to an experiment or duplicate traffic to test a new service without affecting production responses. Nginx can implement weighted experiments, with IP hashing maintaining consistent user experiences.

The adapter pattern modifies an application’s interface to match standardized operational interfaces. Separate adapter containers can normalize monitoring metrics, redirect or transform logs, and provide rich health checks without modifying third-party application images. Examples include adapting Redis metrics for Prometheus, using Fluentd plugins to collect Redis or Apache Storm logs, and exposing application-specific MySQL query checks through an HTTP health interface. This modularity supports independent updates, resource isolation, reuse, and shared operational knowledge.

Multi-node distributed systems use loosely coupled components communicating through network APIs. Microservices divide functionality into independently maintained and scaled services, improving team autonomy, release agility, and scaling flexibility. Their disadvantages include harder debugging, architecture, communication, and coordination. Reusable distributed-system patterns help address these challenges.

Replicated load-balanced services use interchangeable servers behind a load balancer. Stateless services require multiple replicas for availability, safe upgrades, and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching instances before initialization completes. Session-tracked services consistently route a user to one replica, using IP-based affinity internally or application-level mechanisms such as cookies externally. Consistent hashing limits remapping when replica counts change.

Application-aware proxy layers can add caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination. Separate replicated caching tiers can use memory more efficiently than per-application sidecars. Rate limits may vary by identity and return HTTP 429 responses. Nginx can terminate SSL before forwarding traffic through a Varnish cache to application servers.

Sharded services assign subsets of requests or state to different replicas and are commonly used when data exceeds one machine’s capacity. Sharded caches improve memory utilization because each key is stored on one shard, but shard failures reduce hit rates and may overload backend services. Replicating each shard improves availability, supports upgrades, and permits independently scaling hot shards. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, use keys that reflect response identity, and employ consistent hashing to minimize remapping during resizing. Routing may be implemented by per-pod ambassadors or shared routing services, with trade-offs between deployment complexity, scaling, latency, and network usage.

Scatter/gather distributes each request across multiple workers, then combines partial results. It accelerates independent computations and can search document indexes by intersecting or uniting worker results. Sharding workers allows processing datasets larger than one machine. Excessive parallelism introduces request overhead and increases sensitivity to slow or failed workers because overall latency and availability depend on all required responses. Replicating each shard improves reliability, scale, and upgrade safety.

Function-as-a-service provides event-driven, automatically scaled execution with minimal deployment artifacts. Functions encourage stateless, modular designs but can complicate monitoring, dependency analysis, debugging, long-running background processing, and workloads requiring substantial in-memory data. Per-request pricing is beneficial for intermittent traffic but may become uneconomical under sustained load. FaaS decorator functions can transform HTTP requests or responses, such as supplying default API values, while remaining independently scalable.

Despite disappointment after losing two third-period two-goal leads, the team remains positive and believes it can compete and win. The players must learn from their mistakes, follow a chosen game plan, stick to their systems, and focus solely on responding in the next must-win game. Playing at home with supportive fans is expected to provide a boost.

South Carolina Republican Trey Gowdy, known for his self-deprecating humor and friendship with Sen. Tim Scott, announced in January 2018 that he would leave Congress and return to law, where fairness is rewarded. After gaining prominence through the partisan Benghazi hearings, Gowdy increasingly departed from Republican positions. He defended Robert Mueller’s Russia investigation, disputed claims that Russia did not seek to harm Hillary Clinton’s candidacy, and argued that the Steele dossier was not central to several aspects of the investigation. Although he supported Andrew McCabe’s firing, Gowdy warned President Trump against dismissing Mueller and advised him to act innocent if no collusion occurred.

The Trump administration will allow U.S. businesses citing religious or moral objections to deny employees contraception coverage, reversing an Obamacare provision. Reproductive rights advocates condemned the policy, while conservative Christian activists praised it. The government estimates 120,000 women will lose coverage, and California’s attorney general pledged a legal challenge.

Apple filed a Form 8-K on January 28, 2020, reporting that it issued a press release announcing financial results for its first fiscal quarter ended December 28, 2019. The release was attached as Exhibit 99.1, with Inline XBRL included as Exhibit 104. CFO Luca Maestri signed the filing.

The ADS868xW uses a multiSPI interface supporting standard SPI and source-synchronous data transfers with single- or dual-SDO output. The host always sees a 32-bit input/output shift register. Devices can operate individually or in a daisy chain; an optimal daisy-chain frame contains 32 × N SCLK capture edges for N devices.

The device has RESET, acquisition (ACQ), and conversion (CONV) states controlled by RST and CONVST/CS. RESET can perform an application reset or full power-on reset. ACQ captures the analog input, while CONV begins on a CONVST/CS rising edge and uses an internal clock. Conversion completion is indicated by RVS or by waiting for the maximum conversion time.

A transfer frame starts when CONVST/CS falls and ends when it rises. A 32-clock frame accepts a valid 32-bit command; shorter frames invalidate writes but can read selected output bits, while longer frames use the final 32 input bits as the command. Read responses occur in the following frame and can contain register data, fixed patterns, or the latest 16-bit conversion result. Optional output fields include device address, input-range flags, supply and input alarms, and parity.

Nine configuration registers control identification, reset and power modes, input and output protocols, output formatting, input range and reference, and alarm thresholds and status. Supported read/write commands operate on bytes or half-words; half-word commands ignore the address LSB.

The device supports four SPI clock-polarity/phase combinations, source-synchronous output using internal or external clocks, and configurable bus width. It provides NAP and deep power-down modes for reduced consumption.

The application example combines an ADS8681W with an eight-channel differential multiplexer for industrial voltage, current, and temperature inputs. Features include programmable gain, integrated reference and driver, overvoltage protection, and programmable alarms with hysteresis. Recommended design practices include separate analog and digital routing, close supply and reference decoupling, short ground paths, and appropriate ESD precautions.

The author counters bearish warnings amid record equity highs using Ray Dalio’s bubble framework, arguing that patient, low-action strategies have historically outperformed more exciting approaches. The passage promotes Envision Early Retirement’s research, model portfolios, and risk-management services. The author discloses positions in referenced tickers and states that the article reflects personal opinions, is not investment advice, and offers no guarantee of future results.
