For large sparse matrices, direct elimination can be too costly, while sparse matrix-vector multiplication is fast, motivating iterative methods for solving \(Ax=b\). Preconditioning uses a simpler matrix \(P\) resembling \(A\). Examples include Jacobi’s diagonal preconditioner, Gauss-Seidel’s triangular preconditioner, successive overrelaxation, and incomplete LU, which limits fill-in.

The stationary iteration has error equation
\[
e_{k+1}=(I-P^{-1}A)e_k.
\]
Convergence is controlled by the iteration matrix \(M=I-P^{-1}A\): its spectral radius, the largest eigenvalue magnitude, must be below one, and determines the asymptotic convergence rate.

For the one-dimensional tridiagonal matrix with diagonal entries 2 and adjacent entries \(-1\), Jacobi uses \(P=2I\). Its iteration eigenvalues are cosines, so convergence occurs but is slow because the spectral radius approaches one as \(1-O(n^{-2})\). Consequently, roughly \(n^2\) iterations may be required for a fixed error reduction. High-frequency error components decay quickly, while low-frequency components persist. Residuals may therefore become small faster than solution errors.

Weighted Jacobi, particularly with weight \(2/3\), improves damping of high-frequency errors but does not resolve slow low-frequency convergence. Gauss-Seidel uses newly computed values immediately, reduces storage, and effectively squares Jacobi’s eigenvalues, making a step comparable to two Jacobi steps, but it still requires order \(n^2\) iterations. Multigrid addresses persistent low-frequency errors by transferring them to coarser grids, while conjugate gradients are recommended for symmetric positive definite systems.

The speaker congratulates Scotty Bowman and says watching Detroit raise the Stanley Cup should motivate his team. Although disappointed by four straight losses, including three one-goal games, he is proud of the team’s rapid progress and believes it will learn from the experience.

Detroit held slight advantages across many areas, particularly Finals experience, resilience, goaltending, veteran defense and four strong forward lines. The speaker praises Steve Yzerman as a deserving playoff MVP and says Olaf Kolzig was crucial to his own team reaching the Finals. He also commends Detroit’s emotional tribute to injured teammate Vladi and his masseur.

The speaker appreciates growing local interest in hockey and rejects suggestions that his team should be embarrassed. He regrets not fully convincing the players they could beat Detroit but believes the series taught them about sacrifice, composure, simplicity and the extra effort required to win. He expects the team to return stronger.

This phenomenological study examined 45 pre-service teachers’ views on a special education course delivered remotely at a private university in 2022–2023. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews. Although more than half reported satisfaction with distance delivery, 58% preferred traditional education, citing greater effectiveness, quality, interaction, and comprehensibility. Distance education offered flexibility, recorded lessons, home comfort, individualized learning, lower costs, and opportunities to develop technological skills. However, internet connectivity, system failures, insufficient devices and materials, limited technical support, distraction, and difficulties in practical courses reduced its effectiveness. Most participants considered attendance important for learning and achievement, though some opposed compulsory participation because of unequal access to technology or the availability of recordings. Most recommended distance education, particularly for employed learners or compulsory situations. Participants proposed improving digital systems and internet infrastructure, expanding technical and material support, and providing free internet access.

The April 16, 2001 news compilation covers Enron and broader energy, technology and labor issues. Sierra Pacific suspended its dividend amid high Western power costs but continued pursuing Enron’s Portland General Electric despite financing and regulatory obstacles. British offshore wind projects, involving Enron and other major energy companies, reflected growing investment in renewables, while rising natural-gas prices and subsidies improved prospects for solar and wind power in California.

Internet rumor boards were accelerating corporate responses to layoff reports; Enron publicly denied broadband layoffs and said employees had been reassigned. Technology stocks rallied before major earnings reports despite weak economic indicators. Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay criticized the Bush administration’s retreat from global-warming action, while Enron executive Thomas White was expected to be selected as Army secretary.

In India, a Maharashtra committee warned that Enron’s costly Dabhol project threatened the state electricity board and recommended renegotiating tariffs, removing dollar linkage and restructuring payments. Trade unions made Dabhol and globalization central issues in a planned statewide strike.

Other reports addressed online movie piracy using DivX, the end of Enron and Blockbuster’s video-delivery talks, and the restart of Enron’s 15,000-barrel-per-day MTBE plant in Texas.

MLPs outperformed the S&P 500 in 2016, with the Alerian MLP Index returning 18.3% and the equal-weight AMZE returning 22.5%. December gained 4.4%, extending positive quarterly and monthly streaks amid rising oil and natural gas prices. Smaller MLPs rallied strongly, while Enterprise Products Partners underperformed the index for the first time since 2009. Global Partners led the sector for a second week; SunCoke Energy Partners was the top-performing distribution-paying MLP for the year, while Ferrellgas Partners was the biggest loser. General partners and midstream corporations underperformed MLPs. Plains GP Holdings filed to sell up to $500 million in common units, and Shell Midstream Partners announced acquisitions of minority interests in three Gulf of Mexico pipeline assets at a 7.7x EBITDA multiple.

A Reversal Day occurs when a stock or market index changes direction after an extended trend. A bullish reversal follows a downtrend, potentially making a lower low before closing above the previous day’s high. A bearish reversal follows an uptrend, potentially making a higher high before closing below the previous day’s low.

Reversals may result from shifts in market sentiment, economic conditions, company news, technical patterns, or political and geopolitical events. Potential signals include changes in price direction, heavy trading volume, moving averages, RSI, Bollinger Bands, MACD divergences, and breaks of support or resistance. Stocks, currencies, commodities, and bonds can all reverse, though their primary drivers differ.

Two reversal strategies were backtested on gold ETF GLD using exits after 1–25 trading days. The bullish strategy produced generally favorable profit factors, with the highest average gain of 2.02% after 24 trading days, but generated few trades. The bearish strategy produced losses, attributed to gold’s upward overnight drift, and performed substantially worse than the bullish strategy. The results suggest that Reversal Day patterns may have merit when combined with trend, volume, technical indicators, and relevant market news.

Health savings accounts (HSAs), attracting renewed Republican interest as an Affordable Care Act alternative, allow tax-free investment growth and withdrawals for approved medical expenses. They are limited to people with high-deductible health plans, and only about 20 million of 176 million insured Americans participated in 2015.

Participation is constrained by limited disposable income and psychological barriers to saving. Behavioral research suggests people respond strongly to potential financial losses, while automatic enrollment with an opt-out option could increase participation. People with HSAs use less health care, but their health outcomes remain unclear: one study found lower prescription costs but more emergency room visits, especially among lower-income families.

Saving appropriate amounts is also difficult because medical prices are hard to determine. HSAs may benefit people who can cover daily expenses and still save, but are less practical for those already struggling with insurance costs or lacking emergency savings.

The S&P 500 Information Technology sector represents over a quarter of the index’s market capitalization and includes software, technology services, hardware, semiconductor, and chip-equipment companies. Major tracking ETFs are VGT and XLK. Its five largest stocks listed are Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Broadcom, and Adobe, though sector leadership changes frequently.

Two mean-reversion XLK strategies were backtested. The first produced 245 trades, a 0.96% average gain, 10% CAGR, 18% maximum drawdown, 71% win rate, and 3.1 profit factor while spending 12% of the time invested. The second produced 212 trades, a 1.05% average gain, 9.5% CAGR, 15% maximum drawdown, 70% win rate, and 2.85 profit factor with 10% market exposure. NVIDIA’s Turing architecture adds native HDR processing and tone mapping, improved NVENC/NVDEC video support—including HEVC 8K encoding—and higher streaming quality with lower CPU use. VirtualLink combines display, data, and power for VR headsets through one USB-C connector. TU102 and TU104 replace earlier SLI interfaces with second-generation NVLink, supporting two-way SLI and higher-bandwidth display configurations.

Turing introduces RT Cores that accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing. Combined with rasterization, denoising, NVIDIA RTX software, and compatible APIs, these cores enable real-time hybrid rendering of reflections, refractions, shadows, and ambient occlusion. The passage reports over 10 Giga Rays/sec and roughly tenfold faster ray tracing than Pascal.

NGX uses Turing Tensor Cores and pretrained neural networks for graphics features. DLSS produces image quality similar to temporal anti-aliasing with less shading work, while DLSS 2X approaches 64-times supersampled quality. Other NGX capabilities include AI-based inpainting, slow-motion frame interpolation, and image or video super-resolution.

Additional graphics features include task and mesh shaders for reducing CPU draw-call bottlenecks; Variable Rate Shading for content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering; Texture Space Shading for decoupling and reusing shading computations; and Multi-View Rendering for up to four hardware views per pass. Turing also expands DX12 resource binding and heap support.

The full TU104 contains 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and one x8 NVLink link. Tesla T4 uses a reduced TU104 configuration for inference. TU106, used in GeForce RTX 2070, contains 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores but lacks NVLink and SLI. NVIDIA defines RTX-OPS as a workload-weighted combination of Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations.

The passage argues that Morgan Tsvangirai, once crucial to Zimbabwe’s opposition and successful in challenging Robert Mugabe, has become a liability following electoral defeat, party divisions and illness. It urges him to support leadership renewal by stepping aside for a stronger MDC Alliance leader while continuing in an advisory role.

Cocoa futures are standardized derivatives to buy or sell cocoa at a pre-agreed price and future date. They trade on ICE under symbol CC and CME Globex/NYMEX under CJ. Each contract represents 10 metric tons, quoted in U.S. dollars per metric ton. The minimum fluctuation is $1 per metric ton, or $10 per contract. Contracts expire in March, May, July, September, and December.

CME contracts are financially settled, while ICE contracts involve physical delivery through designated U.S. port warehouses. The ICE block minimum is 100 contracts. Futures can be traded through a funded futures brokerage account, while cocoa CFDs are broker agreements based on price differences and do not require delivery.

Cocoa futures strategies may use fundamental and technical analysis, market timing, position sizing, and risk management for speculation or hedging. A cited backtest made 96 trades, with a 2.3 profit factor and 74% win rate. Cocoa has historically performed better in summer and poorly in spring and fall.

As of November 25, 2022, cocoa traded at $2,484 per metric ton, making one contract worth $24,840. Trading Economics data lists an all-time high of $5,379 in July 1977, while TradingView data since 1979 shows a low of $707 in December 2000 and a high of $3,775 in March 2011.

Key risks include leveraged losses, adverse price movements, limited liquidity, and wide spreads. Cocoa exposure is also available through the iPath Bloomberg Cocoa Subindex Total Return ETN (NIB), which tracks cocoa futures with three expiration dates.

For Fire Prevention Week, Montecito fire crews plan to teach 800 local children emergency preparedness through Oct. 14. Lessons include fire response, smoke safety, hazard identification, 9-1-1 calls, and home evacuation. Activities scheduled Oct. 3-6 were canceled due to predicted bad weather and will be rescheduled; later events remain scheduled.

They also criticize the program’s perceived liberal political bias and request ideologically diverse alternatives. The authors oppose creating a PWR minor, saying resources should instead improve existing instruction. They propose allowing experienced writers to place out and replacing current courses with a standardized, source-based curriculum designed by senior humanities professors and taught by existing PWR faculty.

Ottawa police say a woman feigning car trouble near Innes and O’Toole roads lured a Good Samaritan to a vehicle, where she and two male accomplices assaulted him and stole his wallet. The injured victim was hospitalized, and the trio fled with cash in an older dark-coloured sedan. Police are seeking information.

They called for redesigning business processes, increasing board diversity, and rejecting men’s avoidance of meetings with women. Megan Smith emphasized that women of color remain the most excluded, amid an absence of Black speakers.

Burnout is an occupational phenomenon linked to chronic workplace stress, emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced personal accomplishment. Prison officers are particularly vulnerable because of demanding workloads, irregular hours, institutional pressures, and limited stress-management resources.

This descriptive cross-sectional study assessed burnout, associated factors, and coping strategies among general-duty officers at Ghana’s Nsawam Medium Security Prison. Using proportionate stratified random sampling, 266 officers were recruited; 243 completed questionnaires were analyzed. Data were collected from February to May 2023 using instruments adapted from the Maslach Burnout Inventory–Human Services Survey, Work Environment Scale, and Coping Methods Checklist.

Participants had a mean age of 32.4 years; 68.3% were male, 57.6% single, 60.9% had under five years of service, and 78.2% were junior officers. Overall burnout prevalence was 9%. High emotional exhaustion affected 42.0%, high depersonalization 32.5%, and low personal accomplishment 68.7%. Shift allocation was significantly associated with emotional exhaustion, while junior rank was associated with depersonalization. Female officers had higher burnout than males; adjusted analysis showed males had 69% lower odds of burnout. Officers with diploma or certificate qualifications had 89% lower odds than those with postgraduate degrees.

The most commonly perceived causes were irregular shifts (71.6%), heavy workload (49.0%), and inadequate training and development opportunities (47.7%). Although many officers reported teamwork, pride, control, and acceptance by colleagues, substantial proportions reported an unsupportive workplace culture, inadequate recognition and feedback, limited trust in superiors, and penalties exceeding rewards.

Talking to colleagues was the leading coping strategy (62.5%), followed by anticipating off-duty periods (60.1%), talking to family (54.3%), and withholding thoughts and feelings (42.1%). Alcohol use was least reported at 29.2%. The study recommends attention to shifts, workload, training, development opportunities, and workplace support to reduce burnout.

Expected to use the 7 Series-derived CLAR platform, it may feature a 600-plus-horsepower twin-turbo V8 and adaptable all-wheel drive. Its live sessions support synchronized music listening, video, photos, chat, and audio commentary for selected friends or the wider community. Vertigo legally pays royalties for shared songs, with payments increasing as subscribed listeners join. StockX expanded its streetwear marketplace by adding authenticated BAPE and PALACE products, following earlier Supreme and Kith offerings. At launch, it planned to list more than 4,000 BAPE products dating to 2010 and over 3,000 PALACE products. Scotty Newman leads BAPE operations, while Kenny Locklier manages PALACE curation. Brazilian stocks rose Thursday as Vale gained up to 4.9% after record first-quarter iron ore output, despite a quarterly decline. Usiminas advanced after returning to profit amid signs of industrial recovery. The real remained volatile alongside other Latin American currencies as geopolitical tensions and European election uncertainty weighed on risk appetite, though favorable polling for French centrist Emmanuel Macron eased some concerns.

Thailand recorded 390 road deaths during Songkran’s “seven deadly days,” an 11 per cent decline from the previous year after a junta road-safety campaign. Drunk driving caused 28 per cent of accidents, while authorities seized 5,600 motorcycles and 1,800 cars from intoxicated drivers. Junta chief Prayut Chan-O-Cha said further improvement was needed. President Donald Trump warned Iran against restarting its nuclear program as he met French President Emmanuel Macron to discuss preserving the 2015 nuclear agreement. Trump criticized the deal for excluding Iran’s ballistic missiles and regional activities, while Iran threatened to expand its nuclear work and possibly leave a nonproliferation treaty if the United States withdrew.

The study evaluated a streamlined workflow combining optical genome mapping (OGM), Bionano Access, and Variant Intelligence Applications (VIA) for analyzing and reporting cytogenomic variants in myeloid malignancies. Current cytogenetic methods often require multiple tests, specialized manual interpretation, and provide limited resolution, while OGM can detect balanced structural rearrangements and copy-number changes in a single assay.

Ten retrospective cases—nine acute myeloid leukemia and one myelodysplastic syndrome/neoplasm—were independently reviewed five or six times by technologist-director teams. VIA was configured with customized views, filters, classifications, guideline annotations, and reporting tools. Reviews included quality checks, variant prioritization, classification, director confirmation, and report generation.

OGM detected all findings identified by standard-of-care karyotyping and/or FISH. Four cases were negative by both approaches, while six contained reportable variants. Guideline-associated Tier 1A findings were unanimously identified and classified. OGM also revealed additional variants not reported by standard testing in five of six positive cases, including large copy-number losses, trisomy 8, small deletions, chromosomal gains, and complex rearrangements. Classification and reporting of non-Tier 1A variants varied among reviewers.

Average technologist review times were 25.2 minutes for negative cases, 28.5 minutes for simple cases, and 47.3 minutes for complex cases. VIA often reduced review time by approximately 50% compared with Bionano Access alone. The authors conclude that OGM with Access and VIA can consolidate cytogenomic testing, improve resolution and efficiency, support standardized interpretation, and generate reports from a single assay.

A football holder catches the long snap and quickly positions the ball exactly as the kicker prefers, including proper angle and laces facing away. The role requires soft hands, fast reactions, consistency, precision, and calmness under pressure. Holders work closely with long snappers and kickers to create a repeatable rhythm for field goals and extra points. They may also pass, hand off, or run during fake kicks. Teams often use punters, backup quarterbacks, or receivers as holders, and there is no standard body type or consensus ranking of the best players at the position. Though rarely recognized and lacking official NFL statistics, holders can determine whether scoring opportunities succeed, particularly when handling poor snaps or making rapid adjustments.

The address presents America’s 1941 task as protecting the nation and its institutions from external disruption. It argues that democracy has survived domestic crisis through decisive action while preserving constitutional government, civil rights, and free elections. Democracy endures because it draws on individual initiative, majority will, and the pursuit of human progress.

The nation requires material well-being, an informed mind, and, above all, the enduring spirit and faith of America. Rooted in centuries of aspirations for freedom and expressed in foundational American documents, this spirit demands broader security, opportunity, and knowledge while rejecting both undeserved poverty and self-serving wealth. Invoking Washington’s warning that liberty and republican government depend on the American people, the address calls for sacrifice in national defense, steadfast protection of democracy, and continued forward movement despite unprecedented dangers.

The disclosure describes operating a hybrid electric gas turbine engine during descent and other low-power modes. The engine includes two compressor-turbine spools, a geared fan, an electric motor/generator, energy storage, and a controller. Electric assistance permits the engine to be undersized for takeoff or climb and optimized for cruise efficiency.

During descent, the controller reduces or stops core operation by limiting fuel or airflow, optionally maintaining a minimum temperature to prevent thermal cycling. Aircraft systems are then powered electrically, with an electric compressor replacing insufficient engine bleed air. The fan may windmill, driving the low-speed spool and motor/generator to produce electricity for immediate use or storage. Alternatively, stored energy can drive the motor and fan to provide conventional descent thrust or overcome engine drag. These measures reduce fuel consumption and emissions while decoupling aircraft-system operation from engine output.

The study examines how digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth affect sustainable supply chain performance through brand image and supply chain image in Indonesian ICT companies. Researchers distributed 568 questionnaires to employees involved in product distribution across randomly selected regional clusters, obtaining 315 valid responses. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling.

Results supported all seven hypotheses. Digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth positively affected brand image; brand image positively affected supply chain image; and supply chain image positively affected sustainable supply chain performance. Brand image mediated the relationships of digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth with supply chain image, while supply chain image mediated the relationship between brand image and sustainable supply chain performance. The model explained 82.3% of the variance in sustainable supply chain performance and met reported reliability, validity, and predictive relevance criteria. The study concludes that Indonesian ICT companies should use e-commerce practices to improve digital customer experience, electronic word of mouth, brand image, and supply chain performance.

An IDC survey of 200 manufacturing decision makers in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland found that IT-based simulation, modeling, data analytics, and high-performance computing (HPC) are increasingly important for innovation, product quality, faster development, cost reduction, sustainability, and new digital business models.

Simulation and analytics are already widely used in product development, production planning, and quality management, with deployment expected to reach up to 90% in some areas within two years. However, fragmented data and departmental silos limit their value. IDC recommends a holistic data strategy and a shared “single source of truth” across the product life cycle and partner ecosystem.

Growing computational complexity creates trade-offs between speed and accuracy: half of respondents said calculations take too long, while 42% use outdated or inaccurate simulations. HPC addresses these constraints through parallel processing, enabling faster, more detailed calculations, additional iterations, new use cases, and greater agility. Four in five respondents viewed HPC as a game changer, while 64% planned investments in modern simulation, modeling, and high-performance analytics.

Most HPC users favor external infrastructure, cloud services, or colocation rather than on-premises systems. Key challenges include security, investment and licensing costs, energy consumption, insufficient computing capacity, system availability, complexity, and shortages of relevant expertise. Public and hybrid cloud architectures can provide scalability, flexible peak capacity, access to current technology, and operating-cost-based pricing, although trained personnel remain necessary.

IDC recommends evaluating on-premises, cloud-based HPC as a Service, and hybrid models according to utilization, budget, performance, flexibility, security, energy efficiency, and available skills. Enterprises should also use external expertise where needed and treat simulation, analytics, digital twins, and HPC as foundations for integrated development, operational improvement, collaboration, and new data-based products and services.

AMD’s March 2006 specification update for the Geode CS5535 Revision A3 documents numerous silicon issues and workarounds. Automatic clock gating can prevent edge-triggered PIC interrupts, GLIU statistics ASMIs, UART CEIR operation, and USB register reads; affected clock domains should remain enabled. Interrupt or SSMI failures may cause hangs, missed events, or unreliable I/O trapping.

ATAC, ACC, IDE, and DMA issues include PRD prefetch hazards for 4-byte-aligned tables, CRC corruption in UDMA writes following a host-terminated UDMA read, failure when IDE bus mastering precedes PIO or ATAPI commands, hangs with non-DWORD-aligned PRDs, and unreliable LPC block or demand DMA. Recommended measures include defining PRDs before operations, keeping audio PRD changes two entries ahead, blocking UDMA host terminations, using normal PIO-before-bus-master sequencing, DWORD-aligning ATAC PRDs, and using single-transfer legacy DMA.

ACPI and power-management defects include hanging byte accesses to PM1_STS and PM1_EN, corruption from byte or word PMC writes, unavailable GPIO wake events from S3, missing LOWBAT_FLAG after abnormal standby, and failure to deassert sleep controls when their delays exceed PM_SED. Workarounds include avoiding byte accesses, trapping incorrectly sized accesses, using PWRBTN# with optional external circuitry, and programming sleep delays below PM_SED.

KEL defects prevent CmdData from distinguishing writes to ports 060h and 064h, alter HCE state in Snoop mode, and incorrectly clear AuxOutputFull on port 60h reads. Software must use trap information, save and restore HCE state, and use interrupts for PS/2-emulated USB keyboard and mouse handling.

Other issues include incorrect RTC CMOS reads after specific extended-port writes, LPC transaction aborts with delayed SYNC responses, inconsistent SMB NEGACK behavior, excessive SMBus timing noncompliance, premature PCI retry termination, GPIO high-bank atomic-write corruption after suspend, unsupported PIC polling, and a possible simulated PCI back-to-back read failure with no expected real-world impact. IRDY# and DEVSEL# have a guaranteed 1.5 ns tVAL rather than 2 ns; small capacitors may be added if problems occur.

A December 2000 McKinsey update reviews global electricity-sector privatization and restructuring from June through November 2000. Governments facing rising demand and limited funds were opening generation to foreign investors, unbundling state utilities, introducing wholesale and retail competition, and developing regional transmission links. Some international investors shifted toward lower-risk U.S. and European markets.

Europe’s liberalization was driven by the EU Directive, with varying progress in customer choice, utility separation, privatization, trading markets, and consolidation. Central and Eastern European countries pursued reforms and asset sales, often under IMF pressure or in preparation for EU membership. Asian governments resumed restructuring after the financial crisis, though independent producers continued facing contract, guarantee, and utility-solvency problems. Latin American privatizations slowed because of economic instability, ownership restrictions, droughts, and political difficulties, while transmission investment increased. African and Middle Eastern countries increasingly allowed private generation, but most had not advanced beyond independent power projects; drought and subsidized tariffs remained obstacles.

The passage contrasts the postwar hopes of 1945 with the fear and division of 1953. It states that the United States and other free nations pursued cooperation, national self-determination, disarmament, and peaceful development, while Soviet policies emphasized military power, subversion, and domination. This prompted free nations to arm themselves and unite, creating a costly arms race that diverts resources from food, housing, education, infrastructure, and health.

Following Stalin’s death, the new Soviet leadership is presented with an opportunity to demonstrate peaceful intentions through concrete deeds rather than rhetoric. Proposed steps include an honorable Korean armistice followed by free elections in a united Korea, an end to attacks in Indochina and Malaya, an Austrian treaty, the release of prisoners, a free and united Germany, and independence for Eastern European nations.

The passage also proposes limiting armed forces and military production, establishing international control of atomic energy, restricting destructive weapons, and enforcing agreements through United Nations inspection. Savings from disarmament could support global aid, reconstruction, trade, and development. The United States declares its readiness to cooperate but asks whether the Soviet Union will promote genuine peace in Asia, permit nations to choose their governments, and accept effective disarmament controls. Peace, it concludes, must be proven through deeds and could replace fear and armament with freedom, prosperity, and international cooperation.

A federal judge dismissed Spencer Elden’s lawsuit over Nirvana’s 1991 album cover, ruling that the image of him nude as a baby underwater was not child pornography. Judge Fernando Olguin found no sexually suggestive elements or intent to elicit a sexual response, comparing the image to a family photo of a nude child bathing.

Cloud-based high-performance computing (HPC) provides flexible access to current analysis methods and hardware, faster calculations, deeper data insights, and opportunities for data-driven products, services, and business models. It can also improve energy efficiency, scalability, agility, and cost effectiveness while reducing dependence on on-premises infrastructure.

IDC considers simulations, modeling, and data analytics essential for manufacturing innovation, productivity, sustainability, supply-chain optimization, and digital transformation. Effective use requires integrated, high-quality data serving as a single source of truth across the product lifecycle.

IDC recommends establishing virtual product and manufacturing development, creating a holistic data strategy, selecting an appropriate on-premises, cloud, or hybrid HPC model, and considering performance, flexibility, security, scalability, energy efficiency, costs, and available skills. Enterprises lacking specialist expertise should engage service providers or ecosystem partners.

The findings are based on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 technology decision-makers at industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Saskatoon’s Myrna LaPlante, whose aunt Emily Osmond disappeared in 2006, opposes replacing chief commissioner Marion Buller despite the Assembly of First Nations’ call for her resignation. LaPlante said her family trusts the current inquiry and would withdraw its story from the public record if the commission were reset. She supports extending the inquiry’s November 2018 deadline by two years, citing the scale of its mandate and staffing needs. Other Saskatchewan families support Buller’s resignation. Lillian Ewenin criticized communication, scheduling and support at Saskatoon hearings, saying families felt unsafe and stories were missed. Danielle Ewenin said the inquiry failed to address community-wide trauma holistically.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced to life in prison for the 2014 murder of her former son-in-law, Florida State University law professor Dan Markel, plus 30 years for conspiracy and solicitation. She maintained her innocence and denied knowing beforehand about the murder-for-hire plot, prompting Judge Stephen Everett to cite her “utter lack of remorse.” Prosecutors said Adelson plotted with her son, Charlie Adelson, to kill Markel so his ex-wife, Wendi Adelson, could move with their children to South Florida. Charlie Adelson, Katherine Magbanua and one hit man were convicted of murder; another pleaded guilty to second-degree murder. Wendi Adelson has not been charged. Donna Adelson’s husband, Harvey, also told the court she was innocent.

Sony’s A7R III firmware update fixes the “Set File Name” function and improves camera stability. Installation issues affect macOS High Sierra, which is unsupported, rather than Sony’s software. Users can install the update on macOS 10.10–10.12 or run Windows on their Mac as a workaround.

The July 31 IEP news digest focuses on energy policy and California’s electricity crisis. Reports criticize Gov. Gray Davis’ $43 billion in long-term power contracts and proposed Southern California Edison rescue, while detailing possible conflicts of interest involving advisers and spokesman Steve Maviglio’s energy-stock holdings. The SEC reportedly opened a preliminary insider-trading inquiry, five consultants were dismissed, and consultants Chris Lehane and Mark Fabiani waived state compensation. Other coverage addresses reduced federal power refunds, San Francisco public-power ballot measures, Texas deregulation, Baltimore Gas and Electric’s proposed restructuring, and broader causes and financial consequences of California’s crisis.

Rising mortgage rates make borrowing power increasingly important. Borrowers can improve qualification by paying off debts, since lenders calculate debt-to-income ratios using monthly payments rather than interest rates; ratios above 50 percent may be challenging. A co-signer can add borrowing capacity but becomes equally liable and generally can be removed only through refinancing or selling. Switching among Freddie Mac, Fannie Mae, conventional, or FHA programs may affect approval, with refinancing possible later. Larger down payments may help, though often less than debt reduction. Changing to a salaried or W-2 job before applying may also help when employment remains in the same or a similar field. These options should be reviewed with a loan officer and researched for individual circumstances.

NVIDIA’s fiscal 2023 third-quarter revenue was $5.93 billion, down 17% year over year. Net income fell 72% to $680 million, diluted earnings were $0.27 per share, and operating income declined 77% to $601 million. Data Center revenue rose 31% to $3.83 billion, while Gaming fell 51% to $1.57 billion and Professional Visualization fell 65% to $200 million. Gross margin declined to 53.6%, primarily due to a $702 million inventory charge.

For the first nine months, revenue increased 9% to $20.92 billion, but net income decreased to $2.95 billion from $6.75 billion. NVIDIA recorded a $1.35 billion charge after terminating its Arm acquisition due to regulatory challenges. It generated $3.39 billion in operating cash flow and returned $9.29 billion to shareholders through repurchases and dividends.

At October 30, 2022, NVIDIA had $13.14 billion in cash, equivalents and marketable securities, $40.49 billion in assets, and $10.95 billion in debt. Inventory rose to $4.45 billion. U.S. export restrictions affected sales of certain advanced products to China, though alternative-product sales largely offset the third-quarter impact. NVIDIA cited demand uncertainty, excess inventory, supply commitments, macroeconomic conditions, China lockdowns, cryptocurrency changes and export controls as ongoing challenges.

Singapore’s special education evolved from a pre-2004 dual system, in which welfare organizations operated separate special schools, toward a national continuum emphasizing inclusion. Following government commitments in 2004, Enabling Masterplans, ratification of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, and compulsory education requirements expanded support. About 80% of students with special needs now attend mainstream schools.

Teacher preparation has broadened through Special Educational Needs Officers, special-needs training for mainstream teachers, compulsory pre-service coursework, and diploma, advanced diploma, master’s, and doctoral pathways. Collaboration among the Ministry of Education, National Institute of Education, schools, and social service agencies has supported consistent implementation.

Remaining issues include lower salaries and shorter training for special-school teachers, limited mainstream options for students requiring greater support, and the absence of an undergraduate special education degree. Current reforms emphasize holistic education, stronger school partnerships, career development, and greater inclusion of students with disabilities.

A 1968 study found that doctors often disagreed when diagnosing stomach ulcers from X-rays and even contradicted their own diagnoses of duplicate images. A simple computer algorithm based on doctors’ descriptions of their methods outperformed every doctor studied. However, questions remain about how conflicting medical advice was translated into the model and how images were coded for computers. The findings suggest algorithms may apply expert-derived rules more consistently than individuals, while raising questions about experts’ future role as artificial intelligence increasingly generates its own rules from data.

United Way of Northwest Illinois will launch Carroll County’s Imagination Library on March 28, 2018, providing books to children from birth through age five with community partners.

Rare wave-like Asperitas clouds were seen over Bristol, Thornbury, Filton and Monmouthshire on Monday morning. Recently added to the International Cloud Atlas, their formation remains uncertain, with theories linking them to thunderstorms or changing wind direction.

Which? found lenders were quicker to raise mortgage costs than savings rates after the Bank of England increased the base rate from 0.25% to 0.5% in November. Of 327 instant-access savings accounts and ISAs, 48% saw no change within five weeks, while 21% received the full increase. Meanwhile, 53% of standard variable-rate mortgage providers raised rates by year-end, and fixed-rate averages also increased. UK Finance said rates reflect multiple factors and customers can compare and switch products.

The S&P 500 mean reversion strategy uses Internal Bar Strength and Relative Strength Index criteria to generate signals. Backtests on SPY since January 2000 assume full-equity compounding without taxes and evaluate win rates, drawdowns, and annual returns. The article also compares results when the strategy’s parameters are reversed.

The lecture reviews PDE modeling and introduces probability. Homework 7 requires solving drug diffusion from a patch into a flowing fluid using both COMSOL and a finite-volume code. The drug’s low diffusivity creates a small characteristic length, large Peclet number, and sharp concentration gradients, especially near the upstream patch edge. Students should test mesh refinement, domain height, convergence, and physical plausibility rather than trust numerical outputs. Finite-volume methods balance fluxes across control-volume boundaries, handle wall and concentration boundary conditions, and produce a linear, sparse system. Sparse solvers, including MATLAB backslash with appropriate settings or conjugate-gradient methods such as BiCGSTAB, may be suitable. Adaptive meshes can improve accuracy but are prone to coding errors.

For time-dependent PDEs, the CFL number relates time-step size, velocity, and spatial mesh size. It should generally remain near or below one so material does not move across multiple cells in one time step. Refining spatial resolution therefore also requires smaller time steps, greatly increasing computational cost.

The probability discussion emphasizes that measurements and physical systems fluctuate, while continuum equations generally describe averages. Repeated measurements produce distributions rather than exact values, so results may be reported with averages and error bars. The lecture introduces event probabilities, joint and conditional probabilities, correlations, and the need to avoid double counting when combining events. Bayes’ theorem relates the probability of one event given another to the reverse conditional probability and prior probabilities. For continuous variables, probability densities integrate to one, have inverse units of the variable, and assign nonzero probability to ranges rather than exact values. Cumulative distributions give the probability that a variable is below a specified value.

Hickory Tussock Moth caterpillars, found around Belleville from July to September, have venomous hairs that can cause skin redness, burning, swelling, pain and, rarely, headaches, nausea or allergic reactions. Contact areas should be washed and treated with calamine lotion or cortisone; serious reactions require medical attention. Experts advise observing but not touching them, noting they are not a major health hazard and use their hairs defensively.

The MSPM0C1105/1106 include a 32-kHz low-frequency subsystem with RTC and independent watchdog; configurable internal or external voltage references; comparator; firewalls and CRC-16 security; UART, I2C, and SPI interfaces with FIFO/DMA support; independent and windowed watchdogs; general-purpose and advanced timers; configurable I/O; and Arm-compatible two-wire serial debugging with security and mailbox features. The RTC supports calendar functions, alarms, periodic interrupts, calibration, temperature-drift compensation, and clock output. Factory memory provides read-only device identification, capabilities, and trim data.

Typical applications should use 10-µF and 0.1-µF low-ESR decoupling capacitors near VDD/VSS. NRST requires a 47-kΩ pullup and 1000-pF pulldown capacitor. External crystals require bypass capacitors, while 5-V-tolerant open-drain I/O requires pullups for logic-high output.

TI provides development hardware, software, cloud tools, configuration utilities, training, documentation, and support forums. Experimental “X” devices are intended only for internal evaluation, while “MSP” devices are fully qualified for production. The September 2025 revision removed DGS32 package information, updated several specifications and CPU features, revised ADC ENOB information, added DEBUGSS, and updated device-identification tables. The report analyzes the global nuclear medicine market by manufacturers, regions, product types, applications, and sales channels. Market size grew annually by 6.27%, from $3.5 billion in 2013 to $4.2 billion in 2016, and is projected to reach $5.89 billion by 2021. Covered companies include GE Healthcare, Bracco Imaging, Mallinckrodt, Lantheus Medical Imaging, and Bayer. The report includes pricing, revenue, costs, margins, consumption, regional development, SWOT, feasibility, and return analyses.

Options trading in META involves contracts granting the right to buy or sell META or other assets at a predetermined strike price before expiration. Calls provide buying rights; puts provide selling rights. Traders may choose different strikes, expirations, and strategies, including calls, puts, covered or naked writing, straddles, strangles, and spreads.

The passage states a $100 minimum account deposit, though broker requirements may vary, and a minimum trade size of one contract. Orders specify the asset, option type, expiration, strike, and contract quantity. Brokers typically provide options chains, watch lists, charts, technical indicators, market analysis, educational resources, demo accounts, and risk-management tools such as stop losses and trailing stops.

Leverage may range from 1:1 to 1:100, increasing both potential profits and losses. Margin requirements depend on leverage, asset type, and broker policies. Brokers may charge commissions, financing, slippage, and inactivity fees.

Options trading is speculative, highly leveraged, and can cause substantial losses, particularly when shorting options. Investors should use caution, trade only money they can afford to lose, and backtest strategies where possible, although differing strikes and expirations make options backtesting difficult.

D-branes become dynamical through massless scalar fields arising from open-string quantization. Their mass is the vacuum energy of all open-string fields on the brane. Summing worldsheet vacuum diagrams with boundaries shows that, at weak string coupling, the leading disk contribution scales as \(1/g_s\), so a D\(p\)-brane tension scales as \(T_p\propto [g_s(\alpha')^{(p+1)/2}]^{-1}\), up to a numerical constant.

The interaction between two D-branes can be represented by a cylinder. Viewed in one direction, it is tree-level closed-string exchange; viewed in the other, it is a one-loop open-string vacuum diagram. This channel duality connects gravitational closed-string processes with open-string gauge dynamics and motivates holographic duality. Topological counting also gives \(g_s\propto g_o^2\), where \(g_o\) is the open-string coupling.

At low energies, D-brane gauge fields and transverse scalar fields are described by an effective action whose completion for constant fields or slowly varying derivatives is the Dirac–Born–Infeld action. It combines a nonlinear extension of Maxwell theory with the relativistic volume action of a moving brane. The transverse scalars are massless because placing a brane breaks translation symmetry; they are Goldstone bosons and cannot have an ordinary potential.

For \(N\) coincident D-branes, open strings carry endpoint labels \(i,j\), so every excitation becomes an \(N\times N\) matrix. String joining produces matrix multiplication, and the resulting world-volume theory has \(U(N)\) gauge symmetry. Its low-energy dynamics is Yang–Mills theory with matrix-valued gauge and scalar fields, with \(g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2\propto g_s(\alpha')^{(p-3)/2}\).

Separating branes stretches strings between them, giving those strings masses equal to their tension times separation. In field-theory terms, scalar expectation values break \(U(N)\) through the Higgs mechanism. Separating branes into stacks of sizes \(n_1,n_2,\ldots\) leaves \(U(n_1)\times U(n_2)\times\cdots\), while strings connecting different stacks become massive.

S&P Global Platts will launch prices for marine gasoil and diesel capped at 0.1% sulphur on June 1, 2017, across several Asian ports. The move reflects tightening global sulphur limits and rising demand, including six-fold Singapore sales growth over three years.

The Gann Fan, developed by W.D. Gann, is a technical analysis tool that plots nine diagonal lines from significant price highs or lows to identify potential dynamic support, resistance, breakouts, and reversals. Its central 45-degree 1:1 line represents one unit of price movement per unit of time; other angles include 2:1, 3:1, 4:1, 8:1 and their inverses. Price above the 1:1 line may indicate bullish conditions, while a break below may suggest bearish conditions.

Traders may use Gann Fans for trend-following, reversal, forex, entry, exit, and price-target decisions, preferably alongside trend lines, moving averages, multiple timeframes, and other indicators. Risk management should include clear entry and exit points, stop-loss orders, position sizing, and risk-reward ratios.

Unlike Fibonacci fans, which use Fibonacci ratios, Gann Fans express price-to-time relationships. Their signals are not consistently accurate, and the method is subjective. The passage states that meaningful backtesting is difficult without strict, objective rules and recommends testing strategies before use, noting that past performance does not guarantee future results.

Eric Hirsch will step down as EdReports CEO at the end of the school year after leading the instructional-materials reviewer since its 2014 founding. Under Hirsch, EdReports completed more than 1,100 reviews and became influential in state and district curriculum decisions by emphasizing alignment between curricula and standards and involving teachers in reviews.

His departure follows changes to EdReports’ scoring process, expansion into pre-K materials, and criticism that its reviews were slow to reflect reading reforms and overemphasized standards alignment. Updated criteria now give greater attention to phonics, fluency and phonemic awareness.

As the board searches for a successor, experts say EdReports must address artificial intelligence, support for students below grade level, and connections between core curricula and supplemental materials. Hirsch also highlighted evidence that adopting strong curricula alone is insufficient because materials, teacher training and assessments are often misaligned, curricula may be diluted, and many districts do not pilot or evaluate materials before broad adoption.

Cover 1, or “man-free,” assigns man coverage to receivers while a free safety patrols deep and, sometimes, another defender covers the low middle. It enables defenses to support the run, blitz, bracket receivers, and challenge offenses to throw vertically. Alignment leverage can funnel routes toward or away from middle-field help.

Offenses should attack perimeter matchups beyond the free safety’s reach. Effective tactics include pick plays that create natural collisions, double moves such as sluggo and hitch-and-go routes, and routes that let receivers catch the ball in motion, including crossers, wheels, and outs. Slot fades can also isolate inside receivers while quarterbacks hold the safety with their eyes. Examples from Ohio State, Oklahoma, Georgia, and red-zone concepts illustrate bubble-go combinations, slot fades, out-and-up routes, goal-line motion, and scissors or snag-wheel combinations, though some featured defenses changed coverage after the snap.

Christine Milligan was surprised that her family could revoke the organ donation decision made by her daughter, Cassidey Ouellete, who died in a car accident before her 20th birthday. Ontario’s Trillium Gift of Life Network allows families to prevent donation if a registered donor later expressed regret. Families overturned decisions in about 10 per cent of cases in 2016, often because organ retrieval delays withdrawing life support.

Trillium encourages people to discuss donation wishes with relatives. Milligan instead supports reviving a 2012 private member’s bill that would permit only donors to revoke registration and automatically register Ontario residents as donors unless they opt out. Trillium CEO Ronnie Gavsie opposes presumed consent, citing public preference for opt-in donation and research finding no evidence that presumed consent increases donor numbers. Milligan hopes renewed legislation will be named “Cassidey’s bill.”

Motley Fool receives partner compensation, which may affect offer placement but not product ratings, and does not cover every available offer.

Fifth-generation farmer Steve Mitchell uses innovation and social media to grow The Buffalo Farm near Kirkaldy, promoting products, farm life and buffalo meat’s health benefits. Winning the 2016 Meat category at the Scotland Food & Drink Excellence Awards for buffalo fillet steak strengthened the brand’s credibility and opened doors with larger customers. The 2018 awards are seeking entries from innovative, enterprising and quality-focused Scottish food and drink businesses and individuals.

Edmonton officials reported $4.2 million in operating savings and a 68 per cent reduction in sand use from a calcium chloride road-treatment pilot. Chemical engineer Arthur Potts warned the substance could cause substantial corrosion to vehicles, concrete and bridges, potentially costing vehicle owners far more than the city saved. He criticized the city for not testing the chemical and corrosion inhibitor under local conditions. Officials seek to continue the program and purchase specialized equipment but have not disclosed costs. Environmental and collision impacts remain unclear after one year; stormwater monitoring results are expected in October.

An AI tool called Waldo scanned more than 430,000 cannabis-related Reddit posts and flagged over 28,000 as potentially describing harmful or unexpected side effects. Researchers verified that 86 percent of a 250-post sample represented problematic experiences. Trained on posts previously reviewed by humans, Waldo produced fewer false positives than ChatGPT but did not outperform human reviewers. Researchers say social media monitoring could help health agencies identify adverse effects among people who lack medical access or knowledge of official reporting systems. However, Waldo’s effectiveness for other products remains uncertain, and any future use would require caution, ethical oversight and privacy protections.

The speaker praises a player’s positioning and decision-making, and describes Carolina as family-friendly with growing public support for the team. Winning is seen as essential to building recognition and expanding hockey in southern markets. He highlights increased scoring, comeback opportunities, youth participation, and his experience coaching children in Tampa. Misunderstandings in South America portrayed the Monroe Doctrine as asserting U.S. superiority or a protectorate, hindering relations, investment, and trade. Secretary Root’s mission sought to dispel this view. At the Rio conference, he declared that the United States sought peace, respected the equal sovereignty and independence of all nations, claimed no privileges denied to other American republics, and favored shared prosperity, cooperation, justice, disarmament, and prevention of international wrong. His remarks were widely acclaimed and endorsed as reflecting American sentiment.

Argentina’s former foreign minister, Doctor Drago, similarly described U.S. policy as opposing European oppression without seeking dominance. Root received honors and hospitality throughout South America, including recognition in Buenos Aires of American figures associated with South American independence and Brazil’s naming of the conference building “Palacio Monroe.” The passage concludes by recalling concerns raised in 1905 about foreign powers using armed force to collect debts from American republics, potentially leading to lasting territorial occupation.

The note traces how U.S. work has been classified by skill and examines whether “unskilled” status reflected job content, worker identity, or low entry barriers. In 1917, Alba Edwards divided occupations into six socioeconomic groups. “Skill” initially described manual work, while professional and managerial roles were distinguished by property, education, and executive ability. Laborers and servants were labeled “unskilled,” meaning their jobs supposedly required little training, judgment, or dexterity. Classification was also influenced by whether women, children, and minority workers performed the work.

In 1930, 28% of workers held “unskilled” jobs, including farm, factory, servant, and other labor. African Americans were disproportionately represented. By the 21st century, skill was commonly measured through education, experience, and job content, with “skilled” often meaning work requiring education beyond high school. In 2018, over half the U.S. labor force held jobs typically requiring a high school education or less, with a median annual wage of $33,473.

Historically, farm labor relied heavily on enslaved Africans, sharecroppers, convict labor, immigrants, and children. Mechanization sharply reduced agricultural employment, but many crops still required workers’ judgment and manual labor. Factory industrialization similarly drew women, children, immigrants, and African Americans into repetitive, hazardous, low-paid jobs. Automation, offshoring, and production changes later reduced manufacturing employment, while prison labor and garment sweatshops preserved some extremely low-paid production work.

Domestic service declined as household technology advanced, but service employment expanded in retail, restaurants, childcare, and elder care. These jobs often combined low wages and unstable schedules with physical, cognitive, and interpersonal demands. Digital platforms created gig work in transportation, delivery, household services, and online microtasks, often using algorithmic management and independent-contractor arrangements. Warehousing, content moderation, and other contracted work also involved strict quotas, injury risks, or psychological harm.

Education and training did not consistently improve job quality, and access to programs such as the G.I. Bill was unequal. Government regulation, worker organization, and employer practices produced some improvements. The Fair Labor Standards Act established minimum wages, a 40-hour week, and child-labor restrictions, while the National Labor Relations Act protected unionization. However, agriculture, domestic work, tipped work, and independent contractors were excluded from major protections. Union organizing secured wage and workplace gains, but union membership fell substantially after its mid-century peak.

Some employers improved wages, productivity, and job quality by investing in workers and redesigning operations. Examples included Ford’s wage increase, Toyota’s worker-involvement system, and service companies using the “Good Jobs Strategy.”

During COVID-19, nearly 70% of essential workers held jobs categorized as “unskilled.” Many worked in healthcare, food, agriculture, transportation, warehousing, and services for low wages and without remote-work options or adequate protection. The pandemic highlighted that workers long treated as low-status—disproportionately immigrants, women, and people of color—performed work essential to the economy. The note concludes that the central future-of-work challenge is job quality rather than automation-driven job loss.

Hascall Steel Company is a U.S. steel service center with over 45 years of experience. It supplies and processes diverse steel products for customer specifications, including coils, sheets, cold reduced, blanked, slit, coated, and rolled steel. Trained technicians and an in-house laboratory conduct quality testing. The company aims to offer cost-effective solutions, shorter lead times, and reduced supply chain costs.

The United States withdrew from U.N. negotiations on a nonbinding global migration compact, arguing that the process could undermine national sovereignty, immigration law and border enforcement. The compact sought international cooperation on issues including refugee assistance, migrant children’s education and prevention of labor exploitation.

The U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops expressed disappointment and urged reconsideration, saying participation would allow the country to shape the agreement. Pope Francis called for nations to welcome, protect, promote and integrate migrants and refugees. Catholic leaders emphasized that nations have a right to regulate borders but also obligations to protect migrants’ human rights and support the universal common good.

Supporters of the withdrawal argued that the compact’s broad language could interfere with U.S. laws and transfer authority to international bodies. U.N. officials maintained that countries would retain sovereignty over implementation. Other critics warned that withdrawal eliminated U.S. influence over the negotiations and argued that global migration requires international cooperation, particularly from wealthy countries with greater capacity to assist refugees.

A white van mounted the sidewalk near Yonge Street and Finch Avenue, striking pedestrians while travelling south and zigzagging at high speed. Witnesses described multiple casualties and said the driver appeared to target people deliberately. Police arrested the driver and seized the van, but said the motive remained unknown. Officers and bystanders provided emergency aid as hospitals received numerous patients, including several in critical or serious condition. Police closed a large section of Yonge Street, requested witness information and advised the public to avoid the area. Public Safety Minister Ralph Goodale said available information indicated no national-security connection or increased public risk. Transit service was temporarily disrupted, emergency support was arranged for residents, and a makeshift memorial formed near Finch.

The U.S. government shutdown has worsened a longstanding air traffic controller shortage, requiring about 13,000 controllers to work without pay and prompting absences, flight delays, and staffing cuts of up to 50% in some areas. At the start of 2025, 285 of 313 air traffic control facilities were below FAA-recommended staffing levels.

The shortage stems partly from lengthy, costly, and rigorous training, pandemic-era training pauses, retirements, and high attrition. Controllers must retire by 56, while applicants must be U.S. citizens under 31 and meet education, experience, medical, security, testing, and language requirements. Fewer than 10% of applicants are accepted for training, which can take several years.

Controllers face long hours, unpredictable shifts, and mental health concerns but earn an average annual salary of $144,580. The profession is projected to grow 3% from 2023 to 2033, with about 2,200 openings annually.

Tesla announced on February 28, 2019 that its standard Model 3 was available for $35,000, offering 220 miles of range, while a $37,000 Standard Range Plus offered 240 miles and upgraded features. To reduce prices by about 6%, Tesla planned to shift global sales online, close many stores, and retain some as galleries and information centers. Customers could return vehicles within seven days or 1,000 miles for a full refund. Tesla also planned increased service investment and firmware upgrades improving Model 3 range, speed, and power. The company did not expect profitability in the first quarter of 2019 but considered second-quarter profitability likely.

Indian Railways will implement a “no bill, your food is free” policy by March 31 on trains where meals are sold separately, aiming to prevent overcharging. IRCTC is publicising the measure and deploying 120 inspectors, with plans to expand checks across trains. More than 7,000 overcharging complaints were recorded between April and October last year. Railways has terminated two catering contracts and fined caterers about 5,000 times, while the CAG has recommended stronger controls against overcharging.

The judgment was reversed and a new trial ordered because no decision supported the judgment and the plaintiff’s accounting evidence was improperly restricted. Another justice must assess credibility and make findings. Costs will abide the event.

Researchers created nanoscale, resealable polymer packets that release contents when exposed to specific light wavelengths. Light changes linking molecules, softening an inner glassy layer; removing light resolidifies and reseals it. Made from biocompatible polyethylene oxide and polylactic acid, the packets could enable targeted drug delivery or controlled release of fertilizers and cleanup chemicals. The team is exploring materials responsive to pressure and chemical cues while using molecular simulations to study the mechanism. The research appeared in Nature Chemistry.

The S&P 500 closed near a record 6,715, with elevated valuations, technology weakness, Federal Reserve policy, and government shutdown developments fueling caution. The index remains above 6,620 support as investors debate whether the rally is sustainable or approaching bubble conditions.

It excludes third-party software or components, misuse, improper installation, unauthorized repair, modification, accidents, and failure to follow instructions. Warranty service requires contacting SanDisk and returning the product prepaid in tamper-resistant packaging with tracking. SanDisk may repair, replace, or refund the product. It disclaims responsibility for lost data, uninterrupted operation, consequential damages, and high-risk uses; liability is limited to the amount paid, subject to applicable law.

The device uses Microsoft WM-DRM to protect licensed content. If its security is compromised, Microsoft may revoke its ability to obtain new secure-content licenses without affecting unprotected content.

The software license permits personal use of executable software on one computer or device at a time. Users may not modify, reverse engineer, decompile, rent, disclose, separate, or embed the software. A maternal and newborn health training intervention used a Training of Trainers cascade to develop sustainable local training capacity in Palghar District, Maharashtra, during 2019–2022. Eight experienced trainers from an earlier Pune pilot supported 32 selected Palghar master trainers through screening, adult-learner-centered and simulation-based training, staggered induction, supervised practice, virtual quality assessments by UK experts, and refresher sessions.

The Palghar trainers subsequently trained 505 public health providers. Among 463 providers with complete assessment data, post-training scores improved significantly for clinical knowledge, abdominal palpation, newborn resuscitation, and eclampsia management. Interviews and observations indicated that master trainers gained clinical competency, confidence, leadership opportunities, recognition, and motivation, while applying standardized case management, referral, and participatory teaching practices.

The study found that careful trainer selection, extended supervision, peer learning, quality control, and hybrid in-person and virtual training supported standardized delivery and continued learning during the COVID-19 pandemic. It recommends longer training timeframes, supportive health-system conditions, refresher training, and formal opportunities for trainers. Further evaluation of long-term competency retention, application to care, and costs is needed.

At a February 13, 2017 town hall meeting in Nevis, Minister Mark Brantley said the three-party Team Unity coalition had created unprecedented cooperation between the Federal Government and Nevis Island Administration. Launched in 2013 under Timothy Harris, the coalition won the February 2015 election.

Brantley said Nevis received $62.2 million from the Sugar Industry Diversification Foundation in less than two years for infrastructure, energy, healthcare, sports, water and other projects. He contrasted this with 2013, when the foundation spent $95.47 million entirely in St. Kitts. Nevis also received $51.16 million in federal budgetary support, compared with $17.3 million from 2006 to 2015, bringing total funding under Team Unity to $113.36 million. He credited Premier Vance Amory’s discussions with Harris and said the funding demonstrated the coalition’s commitment to equal access to national resources for citizens of both islands.

NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU introduces mixed-precision acceleration, structured sparsity, expanded memory and cache, improved data movement, GPU partitioning, and faster interconnects for HPC and AI. CUDA 11’s TCAIRS solver uses formats including TF32, which achieved the most robust mixed-precision convergence across 37 tests, a 2.0× geometric-mean speedup over FP64, and up to 4× on large complex matrices.

A100’s 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity retains two nonzero values per four entries. Sparse Tensor Core instructions skip zeros, doubling compute throughput, while compressed weights halve storage and bandwidth requirements. NVIDIA’s train-prune-fine-tune process produced virtually no inference accuracy loss across evaluated vision and language networks. Third-generation Tensor Cores also reduce instructions and register accesses through broader warp-level data sharing, while asynchronous copies and barriers improve data-fetch pipelines.

The GPU combines 192 KB of L1 cache and shared memory per SM, supports simultaneous FP32 and INT32 execution, and includes 40 GB of HBM2 delivering 1,555 GB/s. Its 40 MB L2 cache is 6.7× larger than V100’s and provides 2.3× higher bandwidth. L2 residency controls prioritize reusable data, while compute data compression can improve DRAM and L2 bandwidth by up to 4×. SECDED ECC protects HBM2, L2, L1 caches, and register files.

Multi-Instance GPU technology partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory-system resources, predictable quality of service, and fault isolation. Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances, support MPS, VMs and containers, and can be migrated between compatible instances to consolidate workloads or service hardware.

Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth per A100, twice V100’s total. PCIe Gen 4 supplies 31.5 GB/s per direction on x16 connections and supports SR-IOV. Other additions include hardware JPEG decoding, five NVDEC units, an optical-flow accelerator, and faster FP16 and FP32 atomic operations.

CUDA 11 supports Tensor Cores, sparsity, MIG, CUDA Graphs, asynchronous global-to-shared memory copies, asynchronous barriers, L2 residency controls, and enhanced Cooperative Groups. CUDA Graphs reduce repeated CPU launch and inter-kernel overhead, while A100 hardware accelerates dependency handling and reductions.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs, six NVSwitches, 4.8 TB/s aggregate bidirectional interconnect bandwidth, and up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance in a 6U system. MIG can expose up to 56 isolated accelerators per DGX A100. Its software stack includes CUDA, the NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC software, and optimized frameworks for deep learning, inference, analytics, and HPC.

T-Tamer is a model-agnostic framework for managing bi-objective trade-offs, such as accuracy versus latency or cost, in cascaded inference. It represents sub-model routing and stopping as Markovian costly exploration over directed acyclic graphs, where nodes are models and edges encode precedence, dependencies, and inspection costs. A tunable weighted objective combines model loss and exploration cost.

The work distinguishes no-recall policies, which must return the latest inspected model, from recall policies, which may select any previously inspected model. It proves that no-recall strategies cannot achieve any constant-factor approximation to the offline optimum, even for two bounded random variables. For recall-based inference, T-Tamer uses dynamic programming to compute an optimal dynamic-index policy that determines whether to stop and which model to inspect next.

The policy is online-optimal and polynomial-time computable for directed lines, their transitive closures permitting ordered skips, and directed trees. Preprocessing requires \(O(n|V|^2T)\) time for lines and trees and \(O(n^2|V|^2T)\) for transitive closures; inference takes \(O(n)\) time per input.

Experiments on synthetic data and early-exit vision and NLP workloads using VGG, BERT-base, and GPT-2 show favorable accuracy–latency trade-offs. Reported examples include reducing latency to 45% with less than 7% accuracy loss and reductions of up to 90% on language-model workloads.

He is described as hardworking, intelligent, quiet, helpful, and an elite Russian hockey player who excelled in major competitions. The speaker links Russian hockey’s struggles to younger generations lacking his influence.

In 1900, the United States and Russia agreed to arbitrate indemnity claims arising from Russian arrests and seizures of American vessels: the Cape Horn Pigeon, James Hamilton Lewis, C. H. Cold dark matter (CDM) explains extensive astrophysical evidence for missing mass and successfully models large-scale structure and cosmic microwave background fluctuations, but unresolved small-scale problems and the absence of confirmed weakly interacting massive particle detections motivate alternatives such as axions, primordial black holes, warm or self-interacting dark matter, and modified gravity.

Coordination, reproducibility, and open data are increasingly important across astronomy, particle physics, and astroparticle physics. European initiatives including EOSC, OSCARS, and ESCAPE provide FAIR data, software, storage, and analysis infrastructure. ESCAPE’s Dark Matter Test Science Project (TSP) supports cross-experiment workflows through its Data Lake, software repository, and Virtual Research Environment.

The TSP currently emphasizes particle and astroparticle experiments: ATLAS collider searches for dark matter mediators and semi-visible jets; DarkSide direct detection using liquid argon; Fermi LAT gamma-ray searches; and KM3NeT and CTA neutrino and gamma-ray studies. It provides reproducible analyses, experimental exclusion curves, instrument-response tools, and reusable software such as the Baler data-compression package. No new signals were reported in the described ATLAS searches, while other workflows constrain dark matter interaction properties or assess detector sensitivity.

Astrophysical observations could extend these services. Gravitational lensing can constrain subhalo abundance, density profiles, warm-dark-matter particle masses, and self-interaction cross-sections. Dwarf spheroidal galaxies offer low-background targets for indirect gamma-ray searches, although inferred constraints depend on uncertain dark matter density distributions and velocity-dependent particle interactions.

Existing tools include pyHalo and lens-modeling software for simulating halo substructure, GAMBIT for global statistical fits combining particle, astrophysical, and cosmological data, and plotting resources such as AxionLimits and the Dark Matter Limit Plotter. The review encourages incorporating astronomical constraints into the TSP to improve communication, reproducibility, and joint interpretation across disciplines.

Knees experience lifelong wear and tear, but healthy habits can reduce injury and later surgery risk. Persistent knee pain that restricts mobility should be assessed by a physiotherapist. Suggested exercises include quadriceps strengthening, bridges, wall squats, calf and quadriceps stretches, and knee-to-chest stretches. Pain should not be ignored, although appropriate movement can prevent stiffness and compensatory damage. Online physiotherapy may offer greater convenience.

Knee surgery is most common among people over 50, with osteoarthritis a leading cause, although genetics also contribute. When physiotherapy cannot rehabilitate severe damage, surgery can improve quality of life and movement but carries risks including infection and deep vein thrombosis. Modern knee replacements often last decades: more than four in five total replacements and seven in ten partial replacements last 25 years. The ADS8681W/ADS8685W/ADS8689W support standard SPI, daisy-chain, dual-SDO, and source-synchronous multiSPI communication. A standard interface uses CONVST/CS, SCLK, SDI, and SDO-0. In a daisy chain, devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, connect serially through SDI and SDO-0, use identical configurations, and optimally transfer 32 × N clock edges for N devices; throughput decreases as device count increases.

The devices operate in RESET, acquisition (ACQ), and conversion (CONV) states. The active-low RST pin can initiate either an application reset or power-on reset. In ACQ, the analog input is acquired; a CONVST/CS rising edge starts conversion. Conversion uses an internal clock, ignores further CONVST/CS transitions until completion, and returns the device to ACQ. Completion can be detected through RVS or by waiting for the maximum conversion time.

Data-transfer frames begin when CONVST/CS falls and end when it rises. A 32-clock frame accepts a valid 32-bit command. Short frames cannot perform writes but can read selected output MSBs. In long frames, the final 32 input bits form the command. Register reads appear in the next frame; otherwise output normally contains the latest 16-bit conversion result. Configurable output fields include device address, input range, supply and input alarms, parity, or fixed test patterns.

Four SPI modes are supported, selected through SDI_CTL_REG; SPI-00-S is the reset default. Readout can use single or dual SDO lines or source-synchronous operation, where RVS supplies an output clock based on either the external or internal clock. Dual-SDO operation outputs two bits per launch edge and requires fewer clock cycles.

Nine configuration registers control device identification, reset and power modes, input and output protocols, output formatting, input range and reference, and alarm status and thresholds. Writes to protected reset and power controls require writing 69h to address 05h first.

The ADS868xW integrates a 16-bit SAR ADC, differential analog front end, programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, and precision reference. An example industrial design combines ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 for programmable voltage, current, or temperature inputs. Programmable input-alarm thresholds and hysteresis help prevent noise-related false triggering.

Separate AVDD and DVDD supplies require local decoupling. NAP mode reduces acquisition-state power, while power-down disables analog blocks but retains registers and interface operation. PCB guidance includes separating analog and digital routing, using short ground paths, and placing specified supply and reference capacitors close to device pins.
