The disclosure concerns absorbent cores for hygiene products such as diapers, incontinence products, sanitary napkins, and panty liners. The cores contain substantially interconnected channels designed to distribute body fluids faster and more uniformly than surrounding absorbent structures, improving absorption, dryness, comfort, fit, and perceived performance.

The channels extend longitudinally and laterally through at least part of the crotch region. Preferred configurations include U-shaped, funnel-shaped, V-shaped, semi-hourglass, or related geometries, with a closed end near the back and diverging open ends near the front. Channel width may narrow toward the connecting portion to promote fluid transport. Channels are preferably substantially free of three-dimensional absorbent material and superabsorbent polymer, while surrounding regions contain fibrous absorbent material and dispersed superabsorbent particles. Multiple concentric or disconnected channels may also be used.

The core may comprise absorbent material between two nonwoven webs bonded within the channels. Different bonding strengths across a channel can allow selected bonded regions to separate as nearby absorbent material swells while maintaining channel integrity. Channels may remain visible before and after use and become more visible when wet.

An acquisition and distribution layer may be positioned above the core. Fluid distribution may improve when channel terminal or connecting portions extend beyond the layer’s edges, while also reducing material use.

The manufacturing process uses a mold with a three-dimensional insert shaped as the inverse of the desired channels. Vacuum draws absorbent material around the insert, leaving its surface substantially clear and forming channels free of absorbent material. Nonwoven layers are then applied and optionally adhesively bonded into a laminate.

AMD Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) enables runtime firmware updates. The AMD Security Processor (ASP) verifies AMD signatures on boot firmware and every SFS package. OEMs/ODMs retain responsibility for firmware update trust and may require customer co-signatures. During early boot, BIOS can provide a customer RSA public key; the ASP then requires both customer and AMD signature verification. Co-signing uses 2048- or 4096-bit RSA-PSS keys, whose maintenance is the customer’s responsibility.

SFS and co-signing are disabled by default and must be enabled through BIOS configuration. Updates run only at runtime, do not persist across warm or cold reboots, and must be reapplied after each boot. Multiple packages are applied sequentially, including across multi-socket systems. Each package validates applicable firmware and patch levels and applies nothing unless all components validate successfully. Packages can modify registers or values, replace complete firmware images, or update firmware portions.

The deployment agent places commands and packages in specified aligned memory, optionally adds a customer co-signing header and signature, and submits the physical buffer address through the ASP mailbox interface. The ASP protects the package memory, verifies customer and AMD signatures, executes the patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status. Version-query commands report base firmware, SFS and system patch levels, and supported firmware versions.

SEV updates are automatically committed against rollback and require reboot to revert. SNP update pages must be HV-FIXED. Attestation data is provided through appropriate managers, while some attestation schemes may prevent particular updates.

Packages are aligned to AGESA releases and apply only to specified firmware and patch-level combinations. Updates run alongside x86 and DMA traffic with minimal intended performance impact. SEV or SEV/ES virtual machines may need stopping and restarting for an SEV firmware update, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

The passage formulates the empirical stochastic inverse problem (eSIP): inferring a probability distribution of unobservable physical parameters from repeated observations of quantities of interest produced by a process model. Because the observation map is generally not one-to-one, multiple parameter values can produce identical data, so the inverse problem has multiple solutions.

A Bayesian approach selects a unique posterior conditioned on a prior distribution. Using disintegration of measures, the posterior is constructed from conditional probability measures concentrated on generalized contours containing all parameters that yield the same observation. Under stated measurability, smoothness, rank, and density assumptions, each prior with a density determines a unique posterior density explicitly from the observed-data density, the prior density, and its push-forward. The posterior density is almost everywhere continuous under general conditions. The posterior associated with a uniform prior has maximum entropy and treats indistinguishable points on each contour equally.

For empirical data, the paper develops an importance-sampling estimator that is asymptotically unbiased and strongly consistent, with asymptotic variance and error estimates. An exponential-decay example illustrates how observation time changes generalized contours and posterior distributions. The resulting posterior is a distribution rather than a point estimate and can identify low- or high-probability parameter regions and support forecasting of new quantities of interest.

The eSIP models stochastic output as arising from randomly varying physical parameters across repeated trials, rather than observational noise around one true parameter value. It differs from conventional Bayesian inverse problems, model calibration, and methods for longitudinal single-trial data. The paper develops the theoretical solution, entropy and continuity properties, random-sampling and accept-reject numerical methods, examples, and supporting proofs.

AMD AGESA documentation defines published firmware entry points, parameters, dependencies, status codes, host call-outs, and platform customization controls. Only published functions are guaranteed stable; internal procedure names should not be used.

Boot procedures perform staged processor, chipset, graphics, PCIe, and memory initialization from reset through OS handoff. Reset initialization establishes minimal processor operation and up to three flash-ROM execution-cache regions, subject to alignment, address, boundary, and cache-capacity rules. Later stages complete processor and HyperTransport initialization, configure power management, initialize main memory, transfer temporary artifact data to permanent buffers, configure display hardware, and generate ACPI, DMI, P-State, WHEA, IVRS, CRAT, and CDIT tables. BSP and AP cores perform distinct tasks, and many procedures require a stack and uninterrupted inter-core communication.

Memory configuration includes interleaving, ECC, timing, frequency, power-down, training, refresh, voltage, UMA, context restoration, AMP overclocking, DIMM-type support, and memory limits. Post-memory processing enables system memory caching, clears execution-cache MTRRs where appropriate, and prepares processors for host control.

Suspend and resume interfaces save critical and noncritical silicon context, restore memory from self-refresh, reload registers, and prepare for OS re-entry. The host environment initiates suspend or restart and supplies the saved-context locations.

Required host functions allocate, locate, and deallocate memory buffers; initiate warm or cold resets; read DIMM SPD data; and dispatch tasks to application processors. Optional hooks support IDS data, alternate heap placement, memory timing and voltage adjustments, external Vref, resume customization, video BIOS reposting, FCH customization, PCIe clock requests, and memory testing.

Customization is provided through platform build settings, post-creation parameter changes, IDS controls, and call-outs. Build options remove unused code such as DIMM types, ECC, interleaving, training, ACPI tables, processor families, sockets, Connected Standby, or S3 support. Build configuration elements describe motherboard limits and features, including VRM capabilities, CPU frequency limits, PCI MMIO, IO APICs, ACPI content, P-State behavior, C-states, Connected Standby, Core Performance Boost, hybrid boost, and core leveling.

HF-band RFID and NFC transfer data and power through inductive coupling, but readers often use maximum magnetic-field strength, oversupplying passive transponders and increasing mobile-device battery drain. The article investigates dynamic field-strength scaling during card detection, communication, and operation with multiple transponders.

Its PTF-Determinator method estimates the power transfer function (PTF) during card detection by varying reader power, checking transponder responses, collecting reader and transponder parameters, and approximating their physical relation. The resulting PTF enables the reader to regulate transmitted power. A digital-business-card case study also restricts maximum transmission distance and cuts power when that limit is exceeded.

Simulation with improved scaling hardware reduced transmission energy by up to 80%, while measurements on existing hardware showed a 26% reduction. Cutting power beyond the permitted distance reduced transmission energy by up to 75%. Based on smartphone measurements, the method could reduce battery drain by up to 13%, or 39% when transactions beyond the maximum distance are prevented. Future work will improve physical-relation approximation and examine dynamic scaling during communication and with multiple transponders.

The Trump administration’s “Make Our Children Healthy Again Strategy” calls for increasing breastfeeding through WIC, other supportive policies and a safer donor human milk supply, but does not propose federal paid parental leave.

Although 84 percent of U.S. parents initiate breastfeeding, fewer than 40 percent of infants receive human milk at age one, and 60 percent of breastfeeding parents stop earlier than intended. Experts attribute this decline to structural barriers, including inadequate leave, limited health coverage, insufficient workplace accommodations and disparities affecting low-income parents, rural residents and women of color.

A National Academies report recommends better coordination of postpartum services, expanded professional training, and broader insurance coverage for breastfeeding support. Research cited in the passage associates paid leave with higher breastfeeding initiation and duration; California’s paid-leave policy increased breastfeeding duration and the likelihood of continuing for six months.

Experts also emphasize enforcing workplace protections, addressing maternal health disparities, preserving food and health assistance, and coordinating federal and state programs. WIC is considered a key channel because it serves nearly half of U.S. infants. Donor milk can support premature and medically fragile infants and help parents transition to breastfeeding, but advocates seek additional federal funding to expand awareness, donations and access.

The 4-2-5 defense combines elements of the 4-3 and 3-3-5, using four defensive linemen, two linebackers, and five defensive backs. It maintains six defenders in the box while supporting pass coverage, relying on athletic personnel, pressure, and a versatile hybrid Sam linebacker or Rover who can cover, rush, and defend the run.

Its strengths include flexibility against spread formations, compatibility with numerous coverages, and varied blitz packages. Common tactics include six- or seven-man Cover 0 pressures, while typical coverages include Cover 4 and Cover 3 Sky from a two-high safety shell. Its weaknesses are an unbalanced alignment, vulnerability opposite the Sam, dependence on the weak safety to fill running lanes and cover, and smaller personnel that may struggle against large offensive lines and backs. Offenses commonly attack the weak side with plays such as buck sweep or outside zone.

Gary Patterson used the 4-2-5 to produce highly ranked defenses at TCU, including three consecutive national defensive leads and five overall. Greg Etter also employed it successfully at Carthage College, where his defenses ranked prominently in interceptions, turnovers, and other defensive categories.

The speaker praised a player’s puck handling, skating, physicality and composure, and said Detroit’s goalie has proven he can handle pressure and win. Playing in Pittsburgh will require an even better, patient and disciplined road performance because of the loud arena and strong home team. The challenge of repeating as champions and Hossa’s determination have motivated the team, while his return to face his former club adds pressure and excitement. Success will depend on managing the puck and ice, avoiding penalties and post-whistle incidents, limiting quality opportunities, and showing greater will. The team values character, sacrifice and collective success over individual statistics. Previous results do not create momentum; momentum develops during games through important penalty kills, hits and strong shifts. The speaker also praised the team’s elite two-way players for contributing offensively and defensively, particularly in difficult matchups against Crosby.

Severe storms moved into Houston, threatening damaging winds, quarter-size hail, heavy rain and isolated tornadoes. Areas from Conroe to Wharton faced greatest concern, with the worst weather expected east of Houston by 9 a.m.

Algoma Public Health’s “Get Active Algoma” GooseChase contest encouraged community activities away from screens. Running March 19–May 31, 2018, participants completed missions for prize-draw entries, including a $600 bike voucher.

Sleep problems disproportionately affect older adults with chronic conditions, low socioeconomic status, and limited health literacy. This study evaluated a personalized sleep psychoeducation module within a mobile chronic disease self-management app for adults aged 40 or older with chronic conditions and health literacy at or below an eighth-grade level.

The module, offered at third-, sixth-, or eighth-grade reading levels, provided tailored information based on participants’ insomnia, depression, and stress assessments. It covered sleep stages, chronic disease effects, sleep hygiene, sleep logs, and sleep restriction. Assessments occurred at baseline, immediately after intervention, and three months later.

Of 286 participants, 195 had insomnia scores of at least 8 and were included in the analysis. Eighty-six percent identified as Black, Indigenous, or People of Color, and 61% reported annual incomes below $10,000. Participants generally had basic health literacy, elevated stress and depression scores, and substantial sleep disturbance. Sleep disturbance was associated with hypercholesterolemia, depression, other nervous conditions, and bipolar disorder.

Socioeconomic status, health literacy, and number of health conditions were significantly associated with sleep quality. Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores improved by an estimated 0.85 points, representing a statistically significant small-to-medium intervention effect. The findings suggest that brief, personalized sleep information at appropriate reading levels may modestly improve sleep and could serve as an initial stepped-care intervention.

Limitations include reliance on one self-reported sleep measure, possible effects from other app modules, limited generalizability beyond predominantly low-income and minoritized participants, and the modest effect size.

Adoree’ Jackson said the Titans had never practiced their final offensive play, while coach Mike Mularkey said they had practiced it previously, though not that week. The fourth-down pass targeted Jackson, a rookie cornerback with no career receptions. The article questions using him instead of the team’s established pass-catchers in a crucial situation.

Appalachian State freshman Max Correa, a biochemistry major with no ties to Kansas, launched a campaign for Kansas governor after discovering the state has no age requirement for candidates. Correa acknowledges his youth and lack of political experience but says they provide a fresh perspective and help him appeal to younger voters. His platform incorporates Jewish concepts, including tikkun olam to address legislative conflict and kibbutz-inspired communities where students could work toward college tuition. He also proposes reducing opioid deaths by offering state-owned properties to pharmaceutical companies to lower Narcan production costs. If elected, Correa plans to leave Appalachian State, move to Topeka and study part-time at the University of Kansas. Political science professor William Hicks supports young people’s political involvement and questions arbitrary age requirements for office.

Minnesota Lynx star Napheesa Collier accused WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert of negligent leadership, citing officiating, player compensation and the league’s overall direction. Collier alleged Engelbert dismissed officiating complaints and said young stars should be grateful for the league’s platform and media-rights deal. Engelbert said she respected Collier but was disheartened by her characterization of their conversations.

Collier, vice president of the WNBA Players Association and co-founder of Unrivaled, spoke as players negotiate a new collective bargaining agreement that could lead to a 2026 work stoppage. Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve supported Collier’s leadership. Collier said she was unconcerned about possible fines for her remarks.

British expatriate Daniel Jones, 31, received a one-year suspended sentence in Siem Reap for using photos deemed pornographic to promote a pool party. Jones denied any sex or nudity occurred and apologised, but was convicted under Cambodian decency laws. Having served nearly two months on remand, his remaining sentence was suspended. His lawyer may appeal.

Kay Frazier, 50, died after surgery for a severe blood clot blocking blood flow to her brain. The procedure ruptured an artery, and she died two days later. The cause of the clot is unknown. Frazier had married Nebraska prisoner Gary Frazier after exchanging thousands of letters. The coroner has not yet returned a verdict.

The lecture examines pleat folding, where alternating mountain and valley creases create three-dimensional forms. A prominent example uses concentric squares and diagonal creases to produce a saddle-like model traditionally called a hyperbolic paraboloid. Such forms arise from equilibrium between creased regions that prefer to remain bent and uncreased paper that prefers to remain flat. Simulations using spring approximations reproduce physical models and support sculptures built from 3D-printed joints and aluminum rods. Related work includes polyhedral assemblies of multiple saddle forms, circular pleats, self-folding structures, and paper models enclosed within blown-glass vessels.

Despite its appearance, the standard concentric-square crease pattern cannot properly fold into a nonflat form with every crease bent between 0 and 180 degrees. Additional diagonal creases are required. A zigzag triangulation can produce a saddle-like structure, although one central diagonal must be removed. Its construction proceeds outward from a folded central square by locating each new vertex through intersections of three spheres. Interval arithmetic provides error bounds and verifies examples with up to 100 rings for numerous fold angles. Another triangulation works only for limited angles and ring counts. The successful triangulated model closely resembles, but does not exactly match, a mathematical hyperbolic paraboloid.

The impossibility proof relies on properties of intrinsically flat, piecewise-smooth paper. Gaussian curvature remains zero under folding, so smooth regions are locally planar or bend in only one direction and consist of straight ruling segments. A region without creases and with a polygonal boundary must remain planar, while a straight crease folded by a proper angle must remain straight. Consequently, every interior face of a straight-line crease pattern remains rigid. These results show that concentric square, hexagonal, octagonal, and similar pleated patterns cannot fold properly without extra diagonals.

The lecture also discusses unresolved inflation problems involving pillows, tea bags, and Mylar balloons. Any polyhedron can have its volume increased, but the maximum-volume form and its likely curved, rippled limit remain unknown. It concludes with ongoing efforts to reconstruct and analyze David Huffman’s curved-crease origami, including designs using circular, parabolic, and elliptical creases, to document his methods and identify their underlying mathematics.

President Van Buren transmitted further correspondence concerning Alexander McLeod’s detention for alleged involvement in the 1837 destruction of the steamboat Caroline. British minister H.S. Fox regretted the President’s refusal to release McLeod, warned of serious consequences, and defended the Caroline’s destruction as necessary self-defense against a vessel engaged in hostile activity. Secretary of State John Forsyth replied that evidence of the alleged outrage and a demand for redress had already been submitted to the British Government, making further discussion improper, and suggested Fox lacked access to the collected testimony.

Micro E-mini futures, launched by CME Group in 2019, are one-tenth the size of corresponding E-mini contracts. They trade electronically on CME Globex and generally settle financially, making futures more accessible to retail traders with limited capital while enabling speculation, diversification, hedging, and more precise risk management.

Initially offered for the S&P 500, Dow, Nasdaq 100, and Russell 2000, Micro E-minis now cover assets including bitcoin, copper, crude oil, Treasury yields, and foreign exchange. Contract terms, seasonality, and price drivers depend on the underlying asset.

For Micro E-mini S&P 500 futures, each contract equals $5 times the index value. The minimum fluctuation is 0.25 index points, worth $1.25, or 0.05 points and $0.25 for calendar spreads. Quarterly contracts are listed for five consecutive quarters and terminate at 9:30 a.m. ET on the third Friday of the contract month. Trading generally runs Sunday through Friday with a daily break.

Trading requires a funded futures brokerage account and margin. CFDs may provide an alternative without fixed expiration dates. Futures leverage creates substantial risk: losses are based on the full contract value rather than deposited margin. Traders should use defined entry, exit, position-sizing, and risk-management rules and backtest strategies before trading.

Stochastic Texture Filtering introduces randomness into texture sampling to reduce aliasing and moiré patterns and can provide higher-order filtering from one point sample. It benefits from Blackwell GPUs’ doubled point-sampled texture filtering rate.

Neural Radiance Cache uses real-time-trained neural networks to infer multi-bounce indirect lighting from rays traced for only an initial bounce, improving global illumination quality and performance while adapting to game scenes. RTX Skin brings ray-traced subsurface scattering into real-time games to render translucent materials such as skin. RTX Neural Faces uses a TensorRT-optimized generative AI model, trained on varied images, to produce natural-looking faces from rasterized faces and 3D pose data.

Blackwell GPUs target multiple graphics segments. The flagship GB202 has 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, 768 Tensor cores, and a 512-bit memory interface; it powers the GeForce RTX 5090. High-end GB203 has 45.6 billion transistors, 84 SMs, 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 RT cores, 336 Tensor cores, and a 256-bit interface; it powers the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. Performance-segment GB205 has 31 billion transistors, 50 SMs, 6,400 CUDA cores, 50 RT cores, 200 Tensor cores, and a 192-bit interface; it powers the RTX 5070.

NVIDIA states that specifications may change, provides the materials without warranties, limits liability, restricts use in safety-critical applications, and places responsibility for suitability and testing on customers. © 2025 NVIDIA Corporation.

Retired Toronto civil litigator Marcel Strigberger recounts decluttering law textbooks purchased more than 50 years ago. He reviews memorable contract and property-law cases and concepts, questioning their practical relevance after decades of practice before recycling most volumes. He later regrets discarding one property book after finding a used copy listed online for more than C$1,000. Strigberger keeps one five-inch-thick legal volume because it serves as a useful reading stand when he works standing up.

The teams are closely matched in style, with an emotional game expected. The speaker’s team must correct errors and improve intensity. After creating chances only in the final seven minutes, they intend to avoid a defensive shell, win battles, involve defensemen, and drive the puck and players to the net.

The speaker says opponents deliberately fell on him and pushed teammates onto him, creating danger. He wants teammates to clear space and be more aggressive around Eddie, but not retaliate illegally, and believes referees should penalize such actions. He expects similar tactics in upcoming games. At home in Buffalo, he plans to play the puck more aggressively because he feels comfortable and finds the ice and board bounces more predictable than in Dallas. Despite postgame fatigue, his groin feels fine. The team intends to remain physical while making smarter decisions.

An international team used Bell’s test to verify nonclassical quantum correlations in a superconducting processor containing up to 73 qubits. By measuring energies below classical limits, with a difference of 48 standard deviations, they certified large-scale quantum behavior. They also demonstrated genuine multipartite Bell correlations involving all qubits in systems of up to 24 qubits. The approach could support improved quantum communication, cryptography, and algorithms.

Advanced attacking runs require players to anticipate play, observe defenders, and create opportunities several passes or minutes ahead. Individual runs include blind-side, inverted, overlap or underlap, third-attacker, late, and deep-lying runs, as well as movements intended to draw defenders out and create space.

Planned runs are prepared for specific situations, including set plays, receiving crosses, and fast breaks following turnovers. Fast breaks typically involve a midfielder becoming available for an initial pass and another attacker sprinting toward the sideline or goal.

Effective runs depend on avoiding offside, choosing the correct timing, showing patience, and remaining unpredictable. Supporting runs help retain possession through back-pass and square-pass options or by switching the ball across the field to change the point of attack.

A successful attacking run also requires a completed pass. Although only one runner can receive the ball, all players should complete their runs because play determines the recipient. Attackers should study opposing defenders’ individual tendencies and overall team tactics to improve their decisions.

Honor launched the Honor 9i in India for Rs. 17,999. A rebranded Huawei Maimang 6/Nova 2i, it features a metal unibody, 5.99-inch Full HD+ 18:9 FullView display, front 13MP+2MP and rear 16MP+2MP dual cameras with portrait mode, Kirin 659 processor, Android Nougat-based EMUI, 4GB RAM, 64GB storage, fingerprint sensor and 3,340mAh battery. Initial indoor camera and performance impressions were positive, though further testing was deemed necessary.

A paper in Climate Change argues that Iceland’s devastating Eldgjá eruption of 939–940 CE may have encouraged Christianisation. The eruption produced the Common Era’s largest known lava flood, while ash reduced sunlight, lowered temperatures, and hindered agriculture. Researchers contend that volcanic imagery in the 10th-century Völuspá drew on firsthand memories of Eldgjá to portray pagan gods and traditions as doomed. They suggest these memories helped catalyse Iceland’s gradual conversion, officially dated to 999/1000 CE. Later accounts of the conversion also connected volcanic events with religious debate.

The President assumes office amid economic depression, unemployment, industrial disruption, and fiscal strain. He advocates careful reform of coinage, banking, and currency laws, possibly through a bipartisan commission, while preserving currency stability, government credit, and parity between silver and gold. He supports international bimetallism through cooperation with major commercial powers.

He calls for strict economy, reduced expenditures, adequate revenue, debt retirement, and continued support for pensioners. Rejecting routine reliance on loans, he urges protective tariff legislation to eliminate deficits, support American labor and industry, strengthen government credit, and preserve the gold reserve. He also favors expanded trade reciprocity to open foreign markets without harming domestic employment.

The address emphasizes relief for farmers and workers, restoration of business confidence, equal rights, respect for law, fair elections, judicial justice, and opposition to lynching. It pledges enforcement of laws against monopolistic combinations, improvement of immigration and naturalization laws, expansion of education, genuine civil-service reform, and restoration of the American merchant marine.

In foreign affairs, the President supports peace, non-interference, national honor, protection of American rights, avoidance of conquest, and arbitration, urging Senate approval of the arbitration treaty with Great Britain.

Because the Treasury requires immediate action, he announces an extraordinary congressional session for March 15, 1897. He concludes by welcoming declining sectional divisions, promoting national unity and cooperation, and pledging faithfully to preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution.

Medical student mistreatment is common and associated with psychological distress, burnout, reduced empathy, and career regret, yet it is frequently unreported. This single-site qualitative study used peer-led, semi-structured interviews with 21 medical students who described 34 mistreatment incidents; 12 were reported and 22 were not.

Four groups of factors shaped reporting decisions: personal, situational, structural, and climate. Personal concerns included retaliation, effects on grades or careers, lack of perceived benefit, and a sense of justice or desire to protect others. Situational factors included the perceived severity and clarity of mistreatment, validation from confidants, bystander reactions, and perceptions of the perpetrator. Structural barriers included uncertainty about reporting procedures, lack of feedback, prior institutional inaction, and expectations that reports would not produce meaningful consequences. Climate factors reflected medicine’s hierarchy and a culture in which mistreatment was viewed as expected, leaving students feeling powerless.

Only personal and situational factors sometimes encouraged reporting; most factors discouraged it. A sense of justice was a distinctive motivator, while passive bystanders negatively affected reporting. The authors recommend accessible and transparent reporting systems, anonymous mechanisms for reporting retaliation, prompt institutional responses, bystander training focused on senior personnel, and leadership-driven cultural change.

Limitations include recruitment from one institution, volunteer self-selection, a higher reporting rate than the broader medical student population, and a predominance of incidents from clinical settings. Further research should examine mistreatment climate and witness influence.

The October 19, 2000 Haas Alumni Jobs bulletin lists openings at Kaiser Permanente, the University of Michigan, United Nations Foundation, Micron Technology, Informatica, PG&E, Blue Shield of California, ePocrates, iVenturi, Extensity, Fremont Group, Research Dog, and an online comparison-shopping service. Positions span business analysis, finance, accounting, fundraising, communications, corporate development, marketing, strategy, healthcare data, economics, sales, and market research. Expanded postings provide responsibilities, qualifications, compensation or benefits where available, and application contacts. Haas also offers alumni career assistance and invites employers to submit openings. Energy Central’s January 24, 2002 newsletter covers 78 electric-power articles, with extensive reporting on Enron investigations, Arthur Andersen subpoenas and document destruction, bankruptcy proceedings, political scrutiny, and financial fallout. Other topics include Long Island electricity competition, proposed utility rate cuts, nuclear-waste standards, energy legislation, power projects, renewable energy, environmental regulation, utility earnings, international energy markets, gas-industry developments, and California load forecasts.

Darren respectfully protected Nick without escalating the situation. Enthusiastic fans can establish a well-supported hockey market, as happened with the Stars in Dallas, and the same is hoped for here. Successful teams also need physical, defensively strong players who can score and contribute off the ice.

The Nation should retain its remaining coal lands, allowing private extraction under royalties while regulating consumer prices, transportation rates, and fair competition. Coal, like forests, should remain public property and be managed for public benefit.

Congress has advanced federal oversight of interstate corporations through railway rate, pure food, and meatpacking laws. Their operation should be assessed before expansion, though packing-house labels should eventually carry dates and packers should bear inspection costs. The interstate commerce law has coincided with increased railroad earnings and numerous voluntary reductions in freight and passenger rates.

Further federal control will ultimately be necessary because separate state laws cannot effectively regulate interstate corporations. Expanded oversight should address overcapitalization, require disclosure of ownership and business interests, and prevent favored individuals from gaining excessive profits at others’ expense. Consolidation should be regulated rather than prohibited. Effective government regulation can remedy genuine abuses, reduce demands for socialism or public railway ownership, and preserve individual initiative. Unregulated competition can itself destroy competition by allowing dominant individuals or corporations to subordinate all rivals.

Crystal Palace fought back from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 at home with Leicester City. Robert Huth and Jamie Vardy put Leicester ahead before Yohan Cabaye replied and Christian Benteke headed a 70th-minute equaliser. Palace remained above the relegation zone with 35 points from 32 games, two behind Leicester. Manager Sam Allardyce praised Palace’s improved resilience.

Delta reported record revenue and earnings above forecasts, driven by premium and corporate travel. Premium-seat revenue rose 9% to nearly $5.8 billion, while main-cabin sales fell 4% to about $6 billion. Delta expects premium-seat sales to surpass main-cabin sales in 2026, earlier than previously forecast. Adjusted quarterly revenue reached $15.2 billion and EPS was $1.71; full-year adjusted EPS is projected near $6. Executives credited wealthy consumers, capacity management, coastal-market investments, and premium lounges for the shift. Delta shares rose as much as 6%, while analysts viewed the results as evidence of resilient travel demand and improving airline fundamentals.

Meb Faber’s S&P 500 trend-following strategy buys when the index crosses above its 200-day moving average and sells when it falls below, relying solely on price. Testing since 1960 indicates the approach avoided much of the 2008–09 financial crisis and reduced exposure during the 2020 COVID-19 downturn. A monthly version using a ten-month moving average turned $100,000 into $4.7 million, excluding dividends, with a 6.3% CAGR and 26% maximum drawdown, compared with 7% growth for buy-and-hold. The strategy offers a simple way to limit major drawdowns while maintaining reasonably competitive long-term returns.

Printed Circuit Broker Elmatica is establishing a temporary South African department after a 245 percent sales increase and demand for technical support. Country Manager Mikael Jansson has relocated temporarily, with a permanent local team planned.

The $1.8 billion Las Vegas stadium project exceeded minority hiring and small-business subcontracting goals. Minorities, women and veterans completed 54 percent of 80,000 work hours through March, surpassing a 38 percent target. Qualified small businesses received $91 million, or 18 percent, of $509 million in subcontracts, exceeding the 15 percent goal. About 225 workers have been hired, with 500 expected by fall. The 65,000-seat stadium remains scheduled for completion in summer 2020.

Michelle Bishop’s research explores what education grounded in Indigenous knowledges could look and feel like on D’harawal Country in south-west Sydney. Rejecting school reform as its starting point, it prioritises Indigenous education sovereignty in response to the systemic harm, racism, assimilation and dispossession associated with colonial schooling.

The study involved 35 anonymous survey respondents and face-to-face yarns with more than 15 Indigenous people connected to the local community. Indigenous futurities, resurgence and envisioning provided decolonising approaches for collectively imagining education beyond current systems, guided by ancestors, future generations, Country and community self-determination.

Bishop uses “layering the vision” to combine participants’ multiple perspectives without reducing them to demographics or statistics. Participant anonymity is protected by withholding exact numbers and amalgamating quotations within fictionalised characters. Participants who wished to be identified were represented separately through intergenerational letters.

Story is used as an Indigenous, relational and accessible method of presenting findings, maintaining participant voices while challenging conventional academic structures. The story “Our Education, Our Way” incorporates 58 direct and indirect participant quotations. It depicts community members discussing the limitations of mainstream schooling and envisioning Aboriginal-controlled education centred on culture, identity, belonging, relationships, language, storytelling, Elders, Country and Indigenous knowledge. Their vision includes responsive learning based on learners’ needs, equality and respect, community participation, cultural confidence, literacy and numeracy without sacrificing identity, and education that empowers future generations.

Congress should fund stronger antitrust enforcement under the Attorney-General rather than use tariff reductions against trusts, since such reductions would not affect many large corporations and could harm weaker domestic competitors. Trust regulation should remain separate from tariff revision. Economic policy should preserve a stable protective-tariff system, avoid abrupt changes that disrupt business, maintain American competitiveness, and protect workers’ wages and living standards. Necessary tariff adjustments should reflect changing national needs and may be pursued through reciprocity treaties, direct legislation, or selective duty reductions. Changes should follow careful, business-focused investigation by practical experts, potentially through a commission that would assess tariff schedules and recommend revisions without undermining prosperity or established economic policy.

Motley Fool Money highlights the no-annual-fee Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card, which offers unlimited 2% cash rewards, a $200 bonus after $500 in purchases within three months, and 0% introductory APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers. Afterward, a variable APR of 18.99%, 23.99%, or 28.99% applies. Additional benefits include up to $600 in cell phone protection and Visa Signature concierge service. Approval is most likely for applicants with good or excellent credit.

Alternatives include Capital One Quicksilver, offering unlimited 1.5% cash back, enhanced travel rewards, welcome bonuses, and 15 months of 0% introductory APR; and a Citi card offering up to 2% cash back, enhanced Citi Travel rewards, a $200 bonus, and an 18-month balance-transfer introductory APR.

Motley Fool Money receives advertising compensation, which may affect offer placement but states that it does not influence product ratings. Not all available offers are included, and recommended credit scores do not guarantee approval.

Dollar-cost averaging (DCA) invests capital gradually over time, while lump-sum investing deploys it at the earliest opportunity. Scale-in strategies follow the same principle as DCA. Although DCA can reduce fear, behavioral mistakes, and the effects of market volatility, studies cited indicate lump-sum investing outperforms it most of the time because markets generally rise and idle cash loses value to inflation.

Backtests used $60,000 and S&P 500 returns from January 2000 through December 2019. A lump-sum investment grew to $193,157, with a 6.02% CAGR and a maximum drawdown of 55%. DCA produced a 5.5% CAGR, benefiting from continued investment during market declines. When the sequence of returns was reversed—placing 2010–2019 returns before 2000–2010—the lump-sum CAGR changed only slightly to 5.93%. However, the DCA ending value fell from $173,949 to $87,396, and its CAGR declined from 5.5% to 1.9%.

The article concludes that DCA is highly exposed to sequence-of-returns risk, particularly when markets rise while much capital remains uninvested. It recommends lump-sum investing when spare capital is available, while acknowledging DCA’s behavioral and volatility-smoothing benefits.

The passage identifies nine Vanguard ETFs for broad diversification across U.S. and international stocks, real estate, and corporate, domestic, international, and global bonds: VTI, VT, VXUS, VNQ, VNQI, VTC, BND, BNDX, and BNDW. Vanguard, founded by passive-investing advocate John Bogle, is presented as a leading provider of low-cost index funds.

A diversified portfolio combining these ETFs was backtested from 2007 to 2023 using a buy-and-hold strategy with annual rebalancing and dividend-adjusted prices. An initial $10,000 grew to $19,318, though returns were below the S&P 500, partly because of bond allocations. The passage emphasizes drawdowns when assessing risk.

Passive strategies minimize trading, typically through index funds or ETFs, and are popular for their low costs, simplicity, and historically competitive returns. Investors should review each fund’s prospectus to determine whether it suits their goals.

The paper examines historical, theoretical, ideological, and institutional relationships among English as a Second Language (ESL), Bilingual Education (BE), and World Language Education (WL). Although these fields share language-learning goals, they developed separately within U.S. contexts shaped by settler colonialism, forced assimilation, English-only policies, national security priorities, and unequal access to bilingualism. The authors emphasize the question of “language for whom,” noting that minoritized learners have often faced subtractive English instruction while English-speaking students receive enrichment through world languages.

Using Valdés’ framework of language curricularization, the authors analyze how theories and ideologies shape program goals, materials, assessments, learner labels, and teacher qualifications. They argue that monolingual and native-speaker ideals remain influential despite multilingual perspectives emphasizing dynamic bilingualism and translanguaging.

At their Chicago institution, enrollment overlap among ESL, BE, and WL programs prompted a three-phase curricular redesign. First, an ESL methods course shifted from a monolingual sheltered-instruction model to equity-oriented translanguaging pedagogy applicable across educational settings. Revised outcomes, activities, and assessments emphasize learners’ linguistic repertoires, culturally responsive teaching, multiliteracies, differentiation, and multilingual assessment.

Second, the authors created a combined ESL and WL methods course focused initially on Chinese language teaching. Delivered bilingually in Chinese and English, it prepares teachers to serve English speakers, Chinese-speaking English learners, bilingual students, and heritage speakers across program models. Candidates examine second- and foreign-language learning, culture, professional standards, learner profiles, field experiences, and inclusive curriculum design.

A planned third phase will connect WL and BE teacher preparation. It will emphasize candidates’ linguistic histories, critical consciousness, ideological clarity, equity issues in dual-language education, and critical analysis of bilingual programs. Candidates will examine how policies, traditions, theories, and ideologies influence program elements and design bilingual instructional units.

The authors advocate disciplinary border-crossing rather than merging all language teacher education into one pathway. They recommend historically informed, culturally and linguistically responsive preparation grounded in a heteroglossic view of language, translanguaging, multilingualism, antiracism, critical consciousness, and attention to each learner’s linguistic profile.

Microsoft’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2015 reported quarterly revenue of $21.7 billion, operating income of $6.6 billion, and net income of $5.0 billion, compared with $20.4 billion, $7.0 billion, and $5.7 billion, respectively, a year earlier. Total liabilities were $86.6 billion, debt was $31.8 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $90.1 billion. Nine-month operating cash flow was $22.3 billion. Commercial operating income increased to $6.2 billion; Devices and Consumer operating income declined to $1.7 billion. Microsoft completed its $9.4 billion acquisition of Nokia’s Devices and Services business purchase-price allocation and acquired Mojang for $2.5 billion.
