Microsoft described its strategy as focusing on productivity and platforms for a mobile-first, cloud-first world, with investments in digital work and life experiences, cloud infrastructure and services, and devices and operating systems.

AGESA’s binary build model routes all call-outs through a host-implemented router whose address is stored in the standard header. The router maps function identifiers to host procedures and passes function-specific data and configuration pointers. UEFI integration spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases, using phase-specific libraries, drivers, build tools, control files, platform option files, and environment variables.

The host must establish Cache-as-RAM and stack support before early initialization, avoid modifying stack registers or cache controls during the pre-memory period, and later disable the pre-memory stack. Platform Security Processor–enhanced AArch64 APUs initialize DRAM without these stack macros. AGESA provides services for structure allocation and release, event-log access, MMIO mapping, processor and memory address identification, cache sizing, and DIMM data-eye retrieval; these generally require an established stack.

Initialization entry points proceed through reset, early processor and interconnect setup, memory initialization, environment configuration, graphics setup, late table generation, ready-to-boot state saving, and resume restoration. PEIMs coordinate processor, memory, and reset initialization through PPIs and HOBs. DXE drivers perform late initialization, publish generated tables through a protocol, and control functions such as integrated-GPU VGA decoding.

Platform configuration covers processor power management, VRMs, PCIe topology, graphics, display, chipset controllers, memory timing and interleaving, ECC, UMA, training, refresh, voltage, and performance policies. Memory initialization brings DRAM online, transfers artifacts from pre-memory storage, configures cache mappings, and prepares processor cores for host control. Late initialization generates operating-system tables such as DMI, P-State, WHEA, IVRS, CRAT, CDIT, and ACPI data.

Suspend support saves critical and noncritical silicon context into nonvolatile or retained storage. Resume procedures restore memory, processor state, PCI-related registers, and final silicon configuration before operating-system handoff.

Required host call-outs include allocating and deallocating post-memory buffers and initiating warm or cold resets. Buffer call-outs must cooperate through shared handles, support persistent runtime allocations when indicated, and return defined AGESA status values.

MIT’s 6.451 is a mathematically rigorous coding course focused on approaching capacity over the additive white Gaussian noise channel. It requires 6.450 or equivalent preparation and uses instructor-developed notes rather than a textbook. Weekly problem sets emphasize learning and count for 15% of the grade; a two-hour midterm counts for one-third and the final for one-half. The course is videotaped for OpenCourseWare, and TA Ashish Khisti will teach lectures two through four.

Topics include algebraic block, convolutional, tail-biting, capacity-approaching, low-density parity-check, lattice, and trellis codes, along with decoding algorithms. Greater emphasis will be placed on modern capacity-approaching codes and, if time permits, band-limited channels.

The central engineering problem is maximizing digital data transmission through a specified channel. An additive white Gaussian noise channel is characterized by bandwidth \(W\) and signal-to-noise ratio \(P/(N_0W)\). Shannon capacity is \(C=W\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR})\), below which arbitrarily low error probability is theoretically achievable through sufficiently long coding, although Shannon’s proof is not constructive. Coding introduces constraints across long symbol sequences to increase distances between valid transmissions.

The lecture contrasts deep-space, telephone-line, and wireless channels. A telephone channel example with 3,700 Hz bandwidth and 37 dB SNR has an estimated capacity above 42,000 bits per second, while simple uncoded 32-QAM might provide about 15,000 bits per second. Wireless channels add time variation and fading, which this course does not cover.

The first homework reviews decibels, Euclidean signal sets, QAM constellations, and spherical shaping. Decibels represent multiplicative factors as \(10\log_{10}\alpha\); a factor of two is approximately 3 dB.

Using orthonormal pulse-amplitude modulation and matched filtering, a continuous-time AWGN channel can be converted without loss into a discrete-time model \(Y_k=X_k+N_k\). A bandwidth of \(W\) corresponds to approximately \(2W\) real symbols or \(W\) complex symbols per second, with the same SNR. Spectral efficiency is \(\rho=R/W\) bits per second per Hertz, equivalent to bits per two real dimensions. The capacity condition becomes \(\rho<\log_2(1+\mathrm{SNR})\).

Weber State University canceled its annual Unity Conference, themed “Redacted: Navigating the Complexities of Censorship,” after presenters were directed days beforehand to remove references to DEI, diversity, equity and inclusion. Faculty members, including psychology professor Sarah Herrmann, withdrew rather than alter their research presentations.

Officials said the conference, formerly called the Diversity Conference, was organized by the Student Access and Success division and therefore subject to Utah’s HB 261. Unlike academic events, its programming could not endorse certain claims about identity, power structures or legislation. Organizers canceled the conference after participants raised concerns, while acknowledging that the rules had not been clearly communicated earlier.

Critics, including faculty and the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression, highlighted the irony of censoring a conference about censorship. A faculty and staff union held an alternative event, but attendees were also told to comply with HB 261.

Faculty described broader legislative pressure on Utah public universities, including budget cuts and scrutiny of programs and speech involving LGBTQ+, ethnic, women’s and gender studies. Weber State is considering placing future Unity Conferences under Academic Affairs or a college, which would make them exempt from HB 261’s restrictions.

Evercore will release second-quarter 2018 financial results on July 25, 2018, followed by an 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time conference call led by senior executives and a question-and-answer session. Telephone replay will be available for one week, while the webcast will remain archived on Evercore’s website for 30 days.

Winter fishing targets include offshore sailfish, dolphin, wahoo and kingfish, using live bait, kite fishing, flat lines and deep rods. Inshore, anglers can find jacks, tarpon and spawning sheepshead near the inlet, beaches and ICW; shrimp and clams are recommended for sheepshead.

October 2001 reports focused on Enron’s financial strain, opaque partnerships and falling stock. Enron said asset sales could help repay roughly $3.3 billion in investment-vehicle notes, but acknowledged a worst-case $1 billion stock issuance that would dilute shareholders. Executives asserted sufficient liquidity and defended CFO Andrew Fastow while declining detailed discussion of SEC-reviewed partnership transactions. Analysts criticized inadequate disclosure, and shares closed at $19.79 after steep declines. Other reports covered a requested $750 million loan, shareholder litigation, possible tax refunds, Indian energy investments and unrelated market, shipping and economic-stimulus developments.

Michael Gayed’s strategy rotates weekly between SPY and XLU based on their past performance. Rotation systems seek to benefit from changing asset or sector leadership and are often used in trend-following and seasonality strategies.

Utilities are selected because of their low beta, risk-aversion, and interest-rate sensitivity. They tend to outperform when interest rates fall or volatility rises and underperform when rate expectations increase. During the 2008 crash, XLU fell 45.2% from its peak versus 54.61% for SPY.

Gayed reported 13.1% annual compounding since 1929. From 1999 to the paper’s March 2014 publication, the strategy returned 6.7% annually versus 4.6% for buy-and-hold. Since publication, it has lagged SPY, returning 5.1% annually versus 10.4%, and its post-2021 drawdown was similar to SPY’s. The passage concludes that it may be too soon to determine whether the strategy has stopped working.

The April 23, 2001 news compilation highlights energy and financial developments involving Enron and other companies. PG&E’s utility entered Chapter 11 after wholesale electricity prices surged while retail rates remained capped. Critics attributed the crisis partly to CEO Robert Glynn’s support for deregulation, rapid expansion, costly acquisitions and losses outside California.

Tri-State proposed a $1.3 billion, 1,200-megawatt coal-fired plant in Bent County, Colorado, citing lower generation costs and improved pollution controls. Environmental opponents argued that cleaner alternatives, including a nearby Enron wind project, were preferable.

Saudi Oil Minister Ali al-Naimi planned to meet U.S. Energy Secretary Spencer Abraham to discuss oil prices after OPEC production cuts. Enron and other energy companies were also potential participants in Saudi gas projects.

Enron-controlled Dabhol Power Company and its lenders scheduled London meetings amid Maharashtra State Electricity Board payment defaults totaling 2.26 billion rupees. DPC sought lender approval before considering a termination notice for its $2.9–$3 billion, 2,184-megawatt Maharashtra project. Maharashtra wanted India’s federal government to assume electricity purchases.

Developers reportedly planned to halve Karnataka’s proposed 1,000-megawatt Mangalore power project because of lower demand and the state electricity board’s weak finances. Separately, India’s ONGC disputed Enron’s claim of substantial gas reserves at the Tapti Moon Prospect after a $15 million drilling effort.

Spain planned to revise electricity-market rules to improve transparency, competition and access for entrants such as Enron, challenging the dominance of Endesa and Iberdrola.

Eilish McCready, 25, founded Glasgow’s Fearless theatre school to help children build confidence, social skills and communication through small, inclusive drama classes without auditions or end-of-year performance pressure. The school welcomes confident and shy children, as well as those with additional needs such as autism.

McCready, who experienced performance pressure as a child, wanted classes to focus on personal development. Sessions begin with a “Fearless shake” to release nerves and worries, and she says participants have shown increased confidence.

Lizanne Conway said the classes have helped her autistic sons Rudy and Carl develop confidence, social interaction, awareness of personal space and communication in a safe, supportive setting. She praised staff for being inclusive and caring while maintaining clear rules and boundaries.

Lisa Byrne said her previously shy daughter Rua has become comfortable singing in front of others, dressing up in public and creating her own YouTube channel after attending Fearless. Classes are held at Studio 93 in Glasgow.

A study found that online media and AI systems portray women as younger and less experienced than men, particularly in prestigious occupations. Researchers analyzed nearly 1.4 million images and videos, online text, human perceptions and ChatGPT outputs. Images, videos and language models associated younger women with lower-status jobs and older men with authoritative roles.

In an experiment, viewing occupational images shifted participants’ age estimates: female workers were perceived as about two years younger, while male workers were perceived as more than half a year older. ChatGPT similarly generated younger, less experienced resumes for female names across 54 occupations and then ranked them lower than male resumes. It also scored young men below young women.

These patterns conflict with U.S. Census data showing male and female employees are roughly the same age. Researchers warn that AI can inherit and intensify intersecting age and gender biases, potentially reinforcing workplace discrimination and the glass ceiling.

Game is offering a 500GB Xbox One S with Forza Horizon 3, Tekken 7, Halo 5, and Gears of War 4 for £249.99. The items cost £297.10 separately on Amazon UK, representing a £47.11 saving. The Xbox One S received a 4/5 review for its compact design, 4K upscaling, HDR support, and UHD Blu-ray playback. All four included games were also highly rated, scoring between 4/5 and 5/5.

The address reports continued national prosperity and implementation of prior legislation. Measures were adopted to preserve peace with Indigenous nations, protect settlers and treaty rights, and establish trading houses and military posts. A Creek land purchase failed, but existing agreements were reaffirmed.

The United States took possession of several posts evacuated by Britain. Commissions began work on the St. Croix boundary and claims involving captured property, though some British appointments remained outstanding. Under the Spanish treaty, arrangements proceeded for boundary surveys and withdrawal from posts, but no Spanish commissioner had been named to address American claims. Agents were appointed to protect American seamen. Negotiations with Algiers appeared likely to succeed, American prisoners were freed, and treaties with Tunis and Tripoli were being pursued.

The address urges gradual creation of a navy to protect commerce and neutrality, limited public manufacture of essential military supplies, and public support for agricultural improvement. It renews proposals for a national university and military academy to promote national unity, governmental knowledge, and military expertise. It also recommends revising federal officers’ compensation so public service is not effectively restricted to the wealthy.

French cruisers and agents were inflicting serious damage on American trade in the West Indies. Despite troubling communications from France, the government remained committed to friendship while defending national rights and honor; further details were reserved for a special message.

Federal revenues were improving, and Congress was urged to accelerate repayment of the public debt during peacetime. The address also calls for an effective militia and stronger harbor defenses. Concluding his final appearance before Congress, the speaker celebrates the success of the government and expresses hopes for the nation’s lasting liberty, virtue, happiness, and stability.

Researchers are developing methods to convert grape pomace, the wine industry’s roughly 14 million tons of annual waste, into antioxidants, oils, dietary fibers and other commercial products. Pomace can pollute water, acidify soil and attract pests, but it contains valuable antioxidants such as proanthocyanidins, anthocyanins and ellagic acid. Changmou Xu’s team is optimizing technologies to extract safe nutrients while removing pesticides. They are studying pomace polyphenols against foodborne pathogens and testing dietary effects in sows and piglets. In foods such as mayonnaise and ranch dressing, extracted phenolic compounds inhibited lipid oxidation and extended shelf life, while earlier research reduced acrylamide formation in potato chips by 60 percent. The researchers aim to make these natural antioxidants perform comparably to EDTA, supporting consumer demand for natural ingredients.

The Rams requested permission to interview Jaguars interim coach Doug Marrone, who went 1-1 after replacing Gus Bradley. Marrone previously improved Buffalo from 6-10 to 9-7 before opting out of his contract. Jacksonville may also consider retaining him permanently.

Cassini completed the first of five close Saturn flybys before its planned September 15 plunge, ending a 20-year mission. The passes will make it the first Saturn atmospheric probe, collecting data on cloud-top conditions, temperature, auroras, vortexes, chemical composition and the planet’s day length. Cassini spent 13 years at Saturn and completed 127 Titan flybys. Running low on fuel, it will be deliberately destroyed to prevent a possible collision with Titan or Enceladus, potential habitats for microbial life. A final Titan encounter on September 11 will direct Cassini toward Saturn.

The disclosure describes smart ultrasonic and electrosurgical devices integrated into an interactive surgical system. An ultrasonic device’s control circuit measures transducer impedance, compares it with stored reference values, classifies the result, characterizes the end effector’s state or function—or contacted tissue—and adjusts applied power accordingly. Related controls address tissue identification, blade temperature, articulation losses, instability, capacitive coupling, and energy modality.

The broader system connects intelligent instruments, visualization and robotic systems, modular energy generators, smoke evacuation, suction/irrigation, displays, processors, and storage through a surgical hub. Modular docking enclosures provide shared power, data, and fluid management and support communication among ultrasonic, bipolar, and monopolar generators. A surgical data network links operating-room devices to local computers and cloud-based resources for real-time processing, analytics, control, and information display, with the stated goals of improving surgical outcomes, reducing costs, and improving patient satisfaction.

Hurricane Harvey may have damaged up to a dozen Texas Gulf Coast wildlife habitats, including marshes, nesting sites and coastlines. Officials are assessing impacts. Endangered whooping crane habitat was damaged, and possibly only 10 of 60 prairie chickens survived. Oyster beds and marine mammals were also affected, while shrimp and crabs largely survived.

Tesla faced severe financial pressure in 2017–2018 as it spent heavily to expand Model 3 production while generating generally negative operating cash flow. Founded in 2003, the company developed the Roadster, Model S, Model X, and mass-market Model 3, alongside battery, solar-energy, and driver-assistance products. It acquired SolarCity for about $2.1 billion in 2016.

Tesla repeatedly financed growth through equity and debt. Its share count nearly doubled during the eight years after its 2010 IPO, while long-term debt exceeded $10 billion, including SolarCity obligations. From 2015 to 2017, assets rose from $8.1 billion to $28.7 billion, but liabilities increased from $7.0 billion to $23.0 billion. In 2017, Tesla reported $11.8 billion in revenue, a $1.6 billion operating loss, and $471 million in interest expense.

Model 3 production began in July 2017 but repeatedly missed forecasts. Reaching 5,000 vehicles per week was considered essential for positive cash flow. As cash burn accelerated, one analyst estimated Tesla could require more than $10 billion in external capital and refinancing by 2020. Musk nevertheless stated that Tesla would not need an equity or debt raise in 2018 beyond standard credit lines, leaving its survival dependent on balancing capital needs with investor willingness to provide funding.

The study evaluated BNT162b1, BNT162b2, BNT162b2SA, placebo, and booster doses, initially under observer-blinded conditions and later partly open-label. It ran at 153 locations in six countries from 29 April 2020 to 10 February 2023. Participants were healthy people aged 12 years or older without prior COVID-19 infection or vaccination when enrolled. Phase 1 included 195 participants, while Phase 2/3 included 46,406; an additional 333 participants were assigned BNT162b2SA in Phase 3.

In Phase 2/3, two 30-µg doses of BNT162b2 were 95% effective at preventing COVID-19 from seven days after Dose 2 through 3 December 2020 among participants aged 16 years or older, regardless of past infection. Booster BNT162b2 produced immune responses against the original strain comparable to those after Dose 2. BNT162b2SA produced immune responses against the Beta variant comparable to BNT162b2 responses against the original strain.

Temporary lymphocyte reductions occurred in a few Phase 1 participants shortly after Dose 1 and generally returned to normal within days. Injection-site reactions and systemic events were generally short-lived and mild or moderate. Injection-site pain, tiredness, and headache were most common. All tested 10-, 20-, and 30-µg doses were well tolerated, but the 100-µg BNT162b1 dose was stopped after Dose 1 because of reactions. BNT162b2 at 30 µg was selected for Phase 2/3.

Few participants discontinued because of medical problems, and serious medical problems were uncommon. Researchers generally did not consider serious events related to study vaccines, although some temporary serious events in participants aged 16 years or older were considered potentially related. No Phase 1 participants died. In Phase 2/3, deaths occurred from varied causes and were not considered caused by BNT162b2. No deaths occurred among BNT162b2SA recipients who had not previously received BNT162b2.

Amazon.com reported first-quarter 2015 net sales of $22.7 billion, up 15% from $19.7 billion in 2014, or 22% excluding foreign-exchange effects. Operating income rose to $255 million from $146 million, while a $57 million net loss compared with net income of $108 million. Diluted loss per share was $0.12.

North America sales increased 24% to $13.4 billion, with segment operating income of $517 million. International sales declined 2% to $7.7 billion but rose 14% excluding currency effects; its operating loss widened to $76 million. AWS sales increased 49% to $1.6 billion, and operating income rose to $265 million.

For the trailing 12 months, operating cash flow increased to $7.8 billion from $5.3 billion, and free cash flow rose to $3.2 billion from $1.5 billion. First-quarter operating, investing, and financing cash outflows were $1.5 billion, $1.8 billion, and $652 million, respectively. At March 31, Amazon held $13.8 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities. Total assets were $50.1 billion, long-term debt was $8.3 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $10.9 billion.

Operating expenses increased to $22.5 billion, reflecting higher fulfillment, marketing, technology, content, and administrative costs. Stock-based compensation was $407 million. Amazon acquired companies for $341 million, primarily to obtain technologies and expertise.

Amazon changed its reportable segments to North America, International, and AWS. It disclosed ongoing patent, employment, and tax proceedings, including contested proposed tax adjustments from U.S. and French authorities and a European Commission investigation involving Luxembourg. The company stated that legal and tax outcomes remain uncertain.

Natural gas settled at $3.27/MMBtu, constrained by a descending wedge as North American oversupply offset strong U.S. export demand. Seasonal weakness and Canadian supply disruptions sustained volatility.

Plasma diagnostics infer properties such as density, temperature, velocity, and magnetic fields through plasmas’ effects on light, probes, and other phenomena. Because these relationships are often unintuitive, the course assumes prior plasma physics knowledge, particularly electromagnetism, plasma waves, Landau damping, and material from 22.611.

Diagnostics are essential to plasma experiments and fusion development. ZETA researchers initially misidentified anisotropic neutrons from MHD instabilities as thermonuclear fusion, prompting development of Thomson scattering. That technique later confirmed kiloelectron-volt temperatures in Soviet tokamaks, accelerating worldwide tokamak adoption. Similarly, the National Ignition Facility initially lacked sufficient diagnostics to explain its poor performance; improved measurements enabled greater physical understanding and accompanied eventual ignition.

Experimentalists need diagnostics and uncertainty estimates, computational researchers use them to validate and compare simulations, and theorists need them to assess experimental claims and formulate testable predictions. Although complete particle positions and velocities would be impractical, useful measurements include distribution functions, their moments—such as density and average velocity—and magnetic fields.

Real diagnostics are limited: measurements are sparse in space and time, often line-integrated, filtered by instrument response, and dependent on imperfect physical models such as atomic data. Optical measurements may combine emission and absorption from regions with different plasma conditions along one sightline.

The course emphasizes enduring physical principles rather than changing hardware implementations. An in-class survey illustrated the wide ranges of plasma temperature, density, and magnetic field studied in tokamaks, inertial fusion, pulsed-power systems, thrusters, accelerators, and low-temperature plasmas. Mentioned diagnostics included Langmuir and magnetic probes, spectroscopy, bolometry, neutron and X-ray detectors, interferometry, electron cyclotron emission, shadowgraphy, Faraday rotation, and Thomson scattering.

U.S. markets fell sharply Tuesday as the 10-year Treasury yield reached three per cent and company-specific concerns weighed on investors. Canada’s S&P/TSX declined 75.06 points, cushioned by gains in gold and materials, including Barrick Gold. The Canadian dollar, gold and copper also rose slightly.

The study introduces an ascending-descending method for identifying public transit mode hierarchies from passenger travel patterns without assuming spatial homogeneity. Transfers before and after half of a trip’s total distance are classified as ascending and descending, respectively. Transfer-rate matrices quantify directional tendencies, while normalized hierarchy measures rank modes from 0 to 1. Interzonal and intrazonal trips can be analyzed separately.

The method was applied to 10,264,700 T-money trip chains recorded in the Seoul Metropolitan Area on November 12, 2019. Modes included walking, community bus, urban bus, intercity bus, light rail, and metro. Within Seoul, ascending and descending hierarchies showed no significant differences, with the order progressing from walking through community bus, urban bus, light rail, and metro. For trips between Seoul and Gyeonggi or Incheon, community bus ranked lowest, followed by urban bus, light rail, metro, and intercity bus. Including intercity buses relatively lowered the hierarchy values of several other modes. The hierarchy of intercity buses, metro, and urban buses also varied by region, demonstrating that the method captures relative and regional differences among transit modes.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture introduces GDDR6 memory at 14 Gbps, larger and faster L2 caches, improved compression, and approximately 50% higher effective bandwidth than Pascal. Its display and video engines support DisplayPort 1.4a, dual 8K displays at 60 Hz, HDR processing, HEVC 8K encoding, improved decoding, and higher-quality streaming. USB-C and VirtualLink consolidate VR display, data, and power into one connection, while second-generation NVLink increases two-GPU SLI bandwidth.

Turing enables hybrid rendering by combining rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation. Dedicated RT Cores accelerate bounding-volume hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, delivering over 10 Giga Rays per second and roughly ten times Pascal’s software ray-tracing performance. Denoising and hybrid rendering reduce required ray counts while supporting realistic reflections, shadows, refractions, and ambient occlusion.

NGX uses Tensor Cores and pretrained neural networks for graphics features including DLSS, inpainting, slow motion, and image or video super-resolution. DLSS targets image quality similar to temporal anti-aliasing with substantially less shading work, while DLSS 2X approaches 64-times supersampled quality.

Other architectural features include Mesh Shading to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks; Variable Rate Shading for content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering; Texture Space Shading to reuse shading results; and Multi-View Rendering for up to four hardware views per pass. Turing also expands DirectX 12 resource binding and heap support.

TU104 includes 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, while TU106 includes 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores but lacks NVLink and SLI. Products include the RTX 2080, RTX 2070, Quadro RTX 5000, and Tesla T4. NVIDIA defines RTX-OPS as a workload-weighted metric combining Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations.

The passage criticizes Ontario Premier Kathleen Wynne’s statement urging young people and minorities to vote because older white people otherwise would. It argues the remark stereotypes voters by age and race, assumes opposing interests, and uses identity politics to increase turnout by demonizing another demographic. Commentators quoted describe the statement as socially divisive and potentially grounds for workplace human-rights complaints. The author acknowledges that voting participation rises with age and may be lower among visible minorities, but says Wynne should encourage all groups to vote rather than disparage older white voters.

The study assessed whether self-archiving could broaden access to clinical trial results from German university medical centers. Using Unpaywall and Shareyourpaper, it analyzed 1,897 publications from trials completed between 2009 and 2017 and published between 2010 and 2020.

Overall, 54% of publications were openly accessible: 23% gold, 7% hybrid, 16% bronze, and 8% exclusively green open access. Open accessibility increased from 50% in 2010 to 73% in 2020. The remaining 871 publications, or 46%, were closed access.

For 736 closed-access publications, representing 85%, Shareyourpaper identified permission to archive an accepted or published version in an institutional repository. Most permissions covered accepted manuscripts after a 12-month embargo. Only 143 of 879 publications that were either self-archived or eligible for self-archiving were available exclusively through repositories, indicating 16% realized green open access.

The findings show substantial unused potential for self-archiving to improve compliance with WHO guidance that clinical trial results should be openly accessible where possible. The automated approach could support institutional repositories and targeted interventions by libraries or research organizations. Limitations include reliance on the accuracy of Unpaywall and Shareyourpaper, exclusion of some non-repository platforms, uncertainty about some permissions, and assumptions used to estimate realized green open access. Code and data are openly available through GitHub and Zenodo.

Sixteen-year-old Bradd Rudolph drove through an inadequately marked rural “T” intersection and into Bayou Bartholomew, drowning two back-seat passengers, including 15-year-old Michael Hill. Hill’s father sued the Morehouse Parish Police Jury, alleging it knew the intersection was dangerous but failed to maintain additional warning signs. Evidence showed parish officials had previously installed double-arrow signs that were repeatedly removed or damaged and had not been replaced for three months.

The trial court assigned 80% fault to Rudolph, who was speeding and had consumed alcohol, and 20% to the police jury. It awarded $150,000 in general damages and $7,937.64 in special damages, reduced by the police jury’s fault percentage.

The appellate court affirmed the finding that the police jury’s failure to provide adequate warning was a substantial cause of the accident. However, it amended fault allocation to 65% for Rudolph and 35% for the police jury, finding 35% the lowest reasonable allocation to defendants. The general damages award was affirmed as within the trial court’s discretion. Rehearing was denied.

Amazon.com filed a Form 8-K on January 28, 2016, announcing its fourth-quarter and full-year 2015 financial results. The filing incorporates a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. CFO Brian T. Olsavsky signed the report.

Global stocks mostly rose after Federal Reserve chair Janet Yellen said U.S. interest rates could increase as soon as March, citing stronger employment and modestly higher inflation. European and most Asian markets gained, while Shanghai and India declined. Bond yields, bank shares and the dollar rose. Chinese inflation increased, raising concerns about possible monetary tightening, though analysts saw no immediate policy change. U.S. and Brent crude prices fell.

Renewed psychedelic research supports drug-facilitated psychotherapy. Across six Phase II trials, 54% of MDMA-assisted therapy patients no longer met PTSD criteria. Phase III findings confirmed safety, efficacy, and significant PTSD symptom reduction versus placebo with therapy.

The Bank of England will retain the £5 polymer note and issue the £10 note despite tallow concerns. Following a petition, it will consult on plant-based alternatives for the £20 note and future production.

Browns coach Kevin Stefanski has not decided whether rookie Shedeur Sanders will back up starter Dillon Gabriel after Cleveland traded Joe Flacco and a sixth-round pick to Cincinnati for a fifth-round pick. Sanders is listed second on the unofficial depth chart, while Bailey Zappe could be promoted. Stefanski emphasized player development and said the decision would come later in the week. Deshaun Watson remains on the physically unable to perform list while rehabilitating his Achilles injury.

Ireland’s exposure to dollar and sterling movements affects tourism, trade, industries and households. A strong euro has encouraged record US tourism but deterred UK visitors. Sterling weakened from 76 to about 91 pence per euro after Brexit, while the euro rose from $1.05 to $1.18 amid expectations of tighter ECB policy. Future rates remain highly uncertain due to ECB decisions and Brexit. Weak sterling benefits Irish importers from the UK, who should hedge to preserve gains, but harms UK-facing exporters and the car industry through cheap second-hand imports. Tourism firms have few practical hedging options, while exporters can reduce exposure by incurring costs in sterling.

Digital laggards restrict and silo data, rely on individual judgment and tenure, use data to justify existing decisions, and often lack resources for data-driven practices. Only 27% have standardized APIs enabling interdepartmental data flow, compared with 88% of digital leaders. Their aspirational, poorly understood goals discourage measurement, promote qualitative proof of effort and process adherence, and can stifle innovation and strategic alignment.

Digital leaders provide transparent data access, use measurable objectives and continuous tracking, and combine quantitative evaluations with broader feedback. Clear goals allow employees flexibility, experimentation, and autonomy. A retail company illustrated this approach by replacing quarterly reporting with sales dashboards updated three times daily, enabling faster decisions across inventory, marketing, and supply chains.

Leaders also use transparent, jointly developed objectives to connect individual and team work to organizational strategy, creating vertical and horizontal alignment. However, excessive demands for quantitative analysis can delay simple decisions and weaken intuition.

Strong data cultures emphasize learning, risk-taking, transparency, measurement, and consistency between leadership beliefs, company values, and employee behavior. Cultural transformation remains difficult because entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient leadership focus impede change. Organizations commonly fall into four patterns: data novices lack both cultural and technical enablement; insight-ready firms support experimentation but lack analytical capabilities; tech-enabled firms possess technology but discourage innovation; and data-reliant firms overuse data at the expense of critical thinking. Each can build on existing strengths through targeted improvements.

Gary Gensler introduces MIT’s “Blockchain and Money” course, which examines whether blockchain could catalyze change in finance. Blockchain is described as a cryptographically secured, time-stamped, append-only database that moves data over decentralized networks. Its foundations include hash functions, digital signatures, and consensus protocols; Bitcoin combined earlier innovations to enable peer-to-peer electronic cash without a trusted intermediary.

The course considers blockchain’s potential to alter finance, which moves, allocates, and prices money and risk. Opportunities include reducing verification and intermediary costs, improving payment systems, and expanding financial inclusion. Major obstacles include limited scalability and performance, privacy and security concerns, interoperability, governance, uncertain commercial uses, and unsettled public policy. The course will compare permissionless systems such as Bitcoin with permissioned systems controlled by known participants.

Gensler emphasizes neutral, critical analysis rather than cryptocurrency investment advice. Students will examine minimalist and maximalist perspectives, assess technology, markets, law, and social norms, and distinguish evidence from hype. The course begins with blockchain fundamentals, moves to economics, and then studies financial applications such as payments, central bank digital currencies, trading, venture capital, and initial coin offerings.

Assessment includes class participation, two individual critical-reasoning papers, and a team project proposing a financial use case. Upcoming topics include the roles and history of money, fiat currency, ledgers, and Bitcoin’s place within electronic finance.

A University of Michigan study of more than 2,000 older Americans found that 21% of women and 10% of men in their 50s and early 60s met standardized criteria for ultra-processed food addiction, compared with 12% of women and 4% of men aged 65 to 80. Criteria included cravings, unsuccessful attempts to reduce consumption, withdrawal symptoms, and avoiding social activities.

Researchers suggested that early exposure to widely marketed ultra-processed foods, including diet products promoted to women in the 1980s, may help explain generational and sex differences. Addiction was substantially more common among participants who described themselves as overweight, reported fair or poor mental or physical health, or experienced social isolation. The researchers warned that today’s children and adolescents, who consume even more ultra-processed foods, could face higher addiction rates later in life and emphasized the potential importance of early intervention.
Apple Inc. reported that Bob Iger resigned from its Board of Directors on September 10, 2019. The Form 8-K was signed by Katherine Adams and dated September 13, 2019.

Qarlinngua, meaning “like pants” in Inuktitut, is a more than 50-metre-tall natural sea arch about 80 to 90 kilometres southwest of Arctic Bay, Nunavut. Its remote location on Baffin Island’s uninhabited Brodeur Peninsula, accessible only by a four- to five-hour boat trip during a brief ice-free period, has left it little known and led some viewers to doubt photographs were genuine.

Geologists identified the formation as layered sedimentary rock shaped by wind and water erosion, with erosion-resistant quartz possibly helping it remain standing. The surrounding Paleozoic rocks are estimated to be 250 to 600 million years old. Increased open water may accelerate erosion, though estimates of the arch’s remaining lifespan range from decades to thousands of years.

Local hunters regularly pass Qarlinngua, while Arctic Bay Adventures has taken tourists there during limited access periods. Nunavut tourism officials, previously unaware of the formation, plan to discuss promoting it to visitors.
The court affirmed, with costs, a judgment for New York City against Collis P. Huntington, relying on the trial judge’s opinion.

North Korea displayed new intercontinental and submarine-launched ballistic missiles during celebrations marking Kim Il-sung’s 105th birthday and warned it could retaliate against nuclear attacks. Amid speculation of another nuclear test, China cautioned that conflict could erupt at any moment and leave no winner.

This study examines career-transition adaptation and its effects on Indonesian civil-servant lecturers and education personnel who assume additional campus management roles. Such transitions create dual responsibilities, often shifting lecturers’ focus from teaching and research toward administration and reducing individual performance. Education personnel also face uncertainty following bureaucratic reforms and mismatches between functional positions, education, competence, and actual work.

Using an interpretive, qualitative grounded-theory approach, researchers conducted semi-structured interviews with lecturers and education personnel from different types of state universities. Informants were selected through snowball sampling. Interview and document data were coded with NVivo through open, axial, and selective coding, producing eight main categories: situation, self, support, strategies, behavior, role, learning, and perception.

Findings support Schlossberg’s four transition factors—situation, self, support, and strategies—and identify additional dimensions involving new tasks, personal strengths and weaknesses, and organizational support. These factors interact reciprocally. Informants assessed new duties, their capabilities, and support from family, colleagues, and organizations before choosing strategies such as seeking information or taking direct action.

Career transitions produced changes in behavior, roles, learning, and perceptions. Reported effects included burnout, motivation changes, competence demands, self-discipline, new identities, and expanded family and community roles. Time management and managerial competence were important because participants performed functional and leadership duties simultaneously. Unlike Schein’s theory that individuals have one principal career anchor, participants relied on both competence and managerial anchors.

The study concludes that organizational support did not fully match expectations, although family and colleagues provided meaningful support. Dual roles often forced participants to prioritize organizational responsibilities, contributing to declining performance in their primary lecturer or functional positions. The government is advised to consider competence and educational background when assigning functional positions. Limitations include the institutional focus, qualitative design, omission of demographic factors, and potential researcher bias.

The player felt comfortable returning despite concerns about being hit from behind into the boards. He played well before tiring and cramping in the third period, possibly from dehydration and travel, but felt fine the next day. A CT scan reviewed by team doctors showed sufficient healing three and a half months after the injury; they said his current risk would not differ significantly by September. The scan was arranged after another player’s injury created a possible opening in the lineup, and his family and team supported the decision. He does not intend to change his playing style and hopes to contribute to a team filled with accomplished players. Looking ahead to a Stanley Cup-deciding home game, he said the team must improve its execution, effort, and passion, sustain a strong start for the full game, and benefit from rest, routine, and home support.

NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2020 reported quarterly revenue of $3.87 billion, up 50% year over year, and net income of $622 million, up 13%. Diluted earnings per share were $0.99. Six-month revenue was $6.95 billion and net income was $1.54 billion.

Quarterly Graphics revenue increased 16% to $2.09 billion, while Compute & Networking revenue rose 130% to $1.78 billion. By market, Gaming revenue was $1.65 billion, Data Center $1.75 billion, Professional Visualization $203 million, Automotive $111 million, and OEM and Other $146 million.

NVIDIA completed its $7.13 billion acquisition of Mellanox on April 27, 2020. Mellanox contributed approximately 14% of quarterly revenue and more than 30% of Data Center revenue. Acquisition-related inventory and intangible-asset charges reduced quarterly gross margin to 58.8%. Operating expenses rose 67% to $1.62 billion.

At July 26, 2020, NVIDIA had $25.18 billion in assets, $11.27 billion in liabilities, and $13.91 billion in shareholders’ equity. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $10.98 billion. Long-term debt was $6.96 billion following $5 billion of notes issued in March 2020.

NVIDIA stated that COVID-19 adversely affected several industries, including automotive and professional visualization, and could negatively affect demand, supply chains, logistics, and component availability. The company had 617 million common shares outstanding as of August 14, 2020.

Tropical Depression 02W made landfall in the eastern Philippines on April 15, 2017, then weakened while crossing several regions. NASA’s Terra satellite observed its elongated cloud remnants over the South China Sea on April 17. The system moved west, with wind shear and dry air expected to prevent re-intensification.

This study used bibliometric analysis to examine mathematics anxiety research in mathematics education from 2013–2023. Scopus searches were filtered by subject area, keywords, language, open-access status, and article type, leaving 324 journal articles for analysis with VOSviewer and Biblioshiny.

Publications generally increased over the decade, peaking at 56 articles in 2022. Mathematics anxiety remained the dominant theme and was linked to psychological and cognitive factors, including motivation, self-efficacy, gender, achievement, mathematical skills, understanding, and problem-solving. Social sciences and psychology produced the largest shares of research.

Frontiers in Psychology published the most articles on the topic, while Garcia-Santillan was the most productive author with 10 publications. The United States produced the most research and had the broadest international collaboration network, Germany received the most citations, and the University of Barcelona was the most relevant affiliation with 23 documents. Collaboration among authors was generally limited.

The study concludes that mathematics anxiety research has expanded across disciplines and educational levels. Its limitations include using only Scopus-indexed, open-access journal articles and excluding other document types and databases.

A May 25, 2001 media compilation focuses on Enron’s political influence, California’s energy crisis, and the Dabhol power dispute in India. FERC Chairman Curtis Hebert alleged Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay linked company support to favorable deregulation policies; Lay disputed that account. Reports said Hebert might be replaced by Pat Wood, an Enron-backed candidate. In India, Maharashtra’s electricity board sought to cancel Dabhol’s power-purchase agreement amid unpaid bills, disputed penalties, high tariffs, and performance complaints, while Enron contested the cancellation and negotiations continued. Other reports covered possible project buyers, Bechtel’s threatened withdrawal, Australian energy investment, Portland General Electric’s higher revenues and costs, energy-sector recruitment, market gains, and allegations that El Paso manipulated California natural-gas prices.

The application describes a detection-model training method, apparatus, storage medium, and terminal device intended to improve performance across differing image domains, such as medical images from different hospitals. An initial model combines a detection model with an adaptive domain-classification model. Training samples include source-domain images labeled with target-object information and domain identifiers, and target-domain images labeled only with domain identifiers.

The detection model predicts whether a target object is present and may also determine its type and location. The adaptive model classifies each image’s domain using shared extracted features. Loss functions compare predictions with object and domain labels, and model parameters are iteratively adjusted until convergence or a preset number of adjustments. A gradient-inversion module may create an adversarial relationship that encourages feature extraction to remove domain-specific differences.

In a colorectal-polyp example, labeled images from existing sources are combined with unlabeled images from a new hospital. This permits target-domain images without physician-provided polyp labels to contribute to training, increasing usable sample size and improving cross-domain detection. The final model determines whether a new image contains a lesion and, when present, its type and location. The disclosed apparatus implements these functions through model-determining, sample-processing, loss-calculation, adjustment, and detection units.

Teams should prepare for defensive, even, and offensive jump balls. In defensive situations, players should anticipate the tip by watching the jumper’s eyes and hands, rotate early, deny passes, box out, and maintain contact. Box, diamond, single-back, and “Y” alignments use coordinated rotations and one or two defenders protecting the basket, especially against superior jumpers.

Even jump balls require inside position, boxing out, anticipation, aggressiveness, and predetermined clockwise or counterclockwise rotations to attack open spots.

With a height advantage of at least six inches, teams can use set offensive plays, generally tipping forward to the tallest player while preserving defensive balance. If no immediate shot develops, the team should enter its normal offense. Options include simple possession tips, Double Tap, Post Split from diamond or box formations, Jumper Fly, Forward Fly, Spread, Tandem, and Loop. These plays combine directed tips, screens, cuts, passes, and drives to create scoring opportunities while designated players remain back for defensive protection.

Developers of ICE-monitoring and documentation apps removed from Apple’s App Store are appealing the decisions and pursuing possible legal action. Eyes Up, ICEBlock, and DEICER remain accessible through alternatives including Google Play and websites. Apple reportedly cited guidelines against content targeting protected or vulnerable groups, while Attorney General Pam Bondi claimed such apps endanger ICE officers. Google has also removed ICE-monitoring apps and considers ICE officers a vulnerable group.

Legal experts told WIRED the apps publish constitutionally protected information about public events. Critics also noted that Apple, Google, and Waze offer crowdsourced police-sighting features. Digital rights researchers said the removals demonstrate the risks of centrally controlled platforms, particularly Apple’s closed ecosystem, where the company serves as the sole gatekeeper. Apple, Google, the White House, and ICE did not provide comments to WIRED.

Alberta Education Minister David Eggen said parents may be allowed to pay school bus fees despite Bill 1, which eliminated fees for students living at least 2.4 kilometres from their designated school. Rocky View Schools faces a $1 million transportation shortfall and has considered longer commutes, changed bell times and relocated stops. Board chair Todd Brand said many parents prefer paying previous fees and the district will consult the ministry before making a decision.

Shohei Ohtani started Game 1 of the 2025 NLDS for the Dodgers against Phillies ace Christopher Sanchez, marking Ohtani’s first postseason pitching appearance. Ohtani posted a 2.87 ERA with 62 strikeouts over 47 innings in 14 regular-season games. Manager Dave Roberts hoped he could pitch into the seventh inning. Ohtani retired Philadelphia’s first three batters but struck out in his first at-bat. The October 4 game at Citizens Bank Park aired on TBS and truTV and streamed on HBO Max.
