Preproduction parts are experimental, may lack complete testing or qualification, may change or be discontinued, and are intended only for early internal evaluation without warranties. Material information may rely on third parties and may exclude proprietary details; TI’s related liability is limited to the annual purchase price of affected parts. Technical and design resources are supplied “as is” without warranties. Developers are responsible for product selection, application design, validation, testing, standards compliance, safety, security, and regulatory requirements. Resources may be used only to develop applications using the specified TI products, and no additional intellectual-property licenses are granted. TI products remain subject to applicable Terms of Sale.

Digital leaders view sensible risk-taking, deliberate experimentation, continuous feedback, and data as essential for adapting and competing. They value experiments for both results and learning while avoiding excessively costly risks through careful planning. They also invest in long-term employee development, particularly critical thinking, problem-solving, statistics, and design thinking.

The $170 Jabra Elite 65t are among the first earbuds to integrate Alexa through Amazon’s mobile accessory kit. Alexa initially works only with Android, with iOS support planned, but lacks many smart-speaker capabilities. It cannot initiate calls, send messages, provide navigation, support reminders, or voice-control popular music services such as Spotify. Amazon Music is supported, though controls are limited, while timers and alarms produce no notifications. Alexa does provide access to skills, basic translation, multi-room audio, package tracking, and particularly effective voice shopping.

The earbuds can answer calls, but microphone performance suffers in traffic and wind. Google Assistant and Siri offer stronger messaging, notification, and navigation features, and users can switch assistants through Jabra’s Sound+ app.

The Elite 65t provide excellent sound, a comfortable and secure fit, and a HearThrough mode for ambient sound. However, their five-hour battery plus 10 additional hours from the case trails competing earbuds, and they lack a lost-device tracker. Overall, the earbuds offer strong audio quality, but Alexa’s limited mobile functionality undermines hands-free use for calls, music, reminders, and navigation.

The Supreme Court considered whether double jeopardy bars separate convictions and sentences under 18 U.S.C. §§ 924(c) and 924(j) for the same conduct. Section 924(c) covers firearm use connected to violent or drug-trafficking crimes, while Section 924(j) applies when such firearm use causes death.

The parties agreed that cumulative punishment for greater and lesser-included offenses generally requires clear congressional authorization. Debate centered on whether Section 924(c)(1)(D)(ii), which requires consecutive sentences notwithstanding other laws, demonstrates that intent. Barrett and the federal government argued it does not establish separate offenses, while court-appointed attorney Charles McCloud maintained that its language, statutory structure, and purpose indicate Congress intended cumulative punishment.

The government instead emphasized Section 924(c)’s requirement that its sentence be imposed “in addition to” punishment for the underlying violent or drug-trafficking offense. It argued that this language does not extend to Section 924(j), which contains no comparable authorization. Justice Neil Gorsuch questioned the basis for requiring clear congressional intent, but the issue was not briefed and appeared unlikely to feature prominently in the court’s decision.

The speaker welcomes Winnipeg’s new NHL team, praising its passionate fans, MTS Centre, and organization under Mr. Chipman. He recalls playing amid “white out” crowds and chants for the Jets. He distinguishes Henrik and Daniel by appearance, speech, and Henrik’s more outspoken personality. Against goalie Thomas, he emphasizes studying tendencies, getting shots through, choosing between shooting for rebounds and back-door passes, and targeting available corners while respecting Thomas’s ability.

Willis Eschenbach analyzed Mauna Loa Observatory solar-radiation data from about 1980 onward to assess atmospheric clarity and the effects of the El Chichon and Pinatubo eruptions. Outside the two-year periods following these eruptions, maximum sunlight showed little change, suggesting atmospheric clarity at Mauna Loa remained broadly unchanged.

During both post-eruption periods, maximum and average solar radiation followed nearly identical patterns despite differences between the eruptions. Average downwelling radiation was about 24.5 W/m² lower than during non-volcanic periods. Eschenbach calculated that cloud changes offset roughly 7 W/m² of the expected reduction, consistent with his theory that clouds rearrange to oppose changes in forcing.

Despite the sustained radiation decrease, temperature records from Mauna Loa, Hilo, Molokai, Barber’s Point, and Lihue showed no evident cooling associated with either eruption. Wind-speed differences were within the data’s uncertainty. Eschenbach said he did not know why Hawaiian temperatures remained unchanged, but proposed that climate-system responses tend to restore prior conditions. His method compared ten-minute direct and diffuse solar measurements during volcanic and non-volcanic periods.

Energy sector trading provides diversified exposure through individual stocks or ETFs such as XLE and VDE. The S&P 500 energy sector includes oil and natural gas exploration, refining, distribution, equipment, materials, and service companies. As of July 18, 2022, the sector’s one-year return reached 52.81%, versus about -9.28% for the S&P 500.

The five largest sector stocks listed are Exxon Mobil, Chevron, ConocoPhillips, EOG Resources, and Schlumberger, though rankings can change. Energy trading is difficult because commodity prices depend heavily on unpredictable macroeconomic factors.

One short-term XLE strategy recorded 198 trades, a 0.61% average gain, 65% win rate, 13% maximum drawdown, and 2.1 profit factor. Another recorded 335 trades, a 0.21% average gain, 59% win rate, 8% maximum drawdown, 1.75 profit factor, and 3% annual return. The strategies’ rules were not disclosed. Their primary potential benefit is diversification from broader market movements.

Country musician Charlie Daniels called the Las Vegas mass shooting an anomaly and argued that fear should not deter concertgoers. The Oct. 1 attack during Jason Aldean’s Route 91 Harvest performance killed 58 people and injured more than 500, prompting debate over gun control and country music’s ties to the National Rifle Association. Daniels supports regulating bump stocks but opposes broader gun restrictions, saying politicians often misunderstand firearms and that stricter laws could leave people defenseless. His comments contrast with Rosanne Cash’s call for country musicians to oppose the NRA. Daniels is scheduled to headline an Oct. 21 show at Cary’s Booth Amphitheatre.

Schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD) affects approximately 1% of the global population, but diagnosis remains symptom-based because no widely applicable objective biomarkers exist. Resting-state functional connectivity MRI classifiers face challenges involving accuracy, generalisability, repeated-session variability, and disorder specificity. This study sought to develop a clinically applicable SSD classifier and examine whether its functional connections could serve as trait, state, or staging markers.

Researchers used harmonised multisite datasets, with 1,015 participants for classifier development and 683 for independent validation. They generated 100 sparse LASSO classifiers, applied spatial averaging and a voting method, tested specificity across psychiatric disorders, and examined symptom severity, disease stage, and laterality.

Functional-connectivity diagnostic effects were significantly correlated across the independent datasets. The LASSO classifiers achieved 79.6% accuracy and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.876 in the discovery dataset. In validation, they achieved 77.3% accuracy, 0.824 AUC, 69.2% sensitivity, and 81.1% specificity. Performance varied by site, with reduced sensitivity at JHU, whose early-stage SSD participants showed distributions between chronic-stage SSD and healthy controls.

Forty-seven functional connections contributed above chance to classification, and group relationships were reproduced for 44 of them in validation. Voting classifiers significantly improved sensitivity but not specificity; their validation AUC of 0.841 did not significantly differ from LASSO. Voting also reduced performance disparities across disease-severity groups, though results could be partly influenced by age. LASSO performance was unaffected by assessed confounders. Important functional connections showed hemispheric laterality imbalances, except in the cerebellum.

Snap and Francis were convicted and fined $50 each for unlawfully shooting and wounding a mare trespassing in an oat field protected by an insufficient fence. The court held that landowners may remove trespassing livestock using necessary force or seek compensation for damages, but may not unnecessarily injure the animal. The conviction and judgment were affirmed.

Old paper £10 notes will cease to be legal tender on 1 March but can later be exchanged at banks, building societies, post offices or the Bank of England, possibly with ID. The Jane Austen polymer replacement entered circulation in September 2017 and offers greater durability, security and accessibility. A polymer £20 note is planned for 2020, with no update planned for the £50 note.

AMD re-enters the high-end graphics card market with the Radeon RX Vega 64 and Vega 56, competing respectively with Nvidia’s GTX 1080 and GTX 1070. AMD does not position Vega 64 against the GTX 1080 Ti, leaving Nvidia likely ahead in single-card performance. Vega 56 costs $400, below the GTX 1070’s cited US price, though UK pricing is less favorable. AMD’s advantages include support for three-card CrossFire on its 64-lane X399 platform and the cheaper, widely available FreeSync ecosystem. Enhanced Sync improves FreeSync and non-FreeSync monitor experiences, while AMD says it has worked to improve minimum frame rates.

Toronto’s financial sector declined after February highs, with Canada’s five largest banks falling 4.6%–7.5% and selected small-cap lenders dropping as much as 28%. The author compares ten financial companies using beta, earnings yield, dividend yield, payout ratio, and dividend history.

The big five banks offer dividend yields of 3.4%–4.4% and have not reduced dividends in over a decade. First National, Home Capital, and Equitable Group have cut dividends, while Atrium Mortgage Investment and MCAN Mortgage have maintained or increased them and yield above 7%.

MCAN ranked first overall, followed by Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and Atrium. Equitable ranked last because it had the highest beta and lowest dividend yield. Small-cap lenders may provide higher yields and lower price volatility, but they have lower trading liquidity and less diversified business models than major banks. The author holds Atrium, CIBC, TD, and Bank of Nova Scotia.

The Hawk offense combines wing isolation, a high-post shuffle cut, and a weakside post-up. Like the UCLA offense, a guard cuts off a high-post back screen, creating layup or post-up opportunities.

The basic NBA “show and recover” defense avoids switching a big defender onto a guard. Against wing penetration, weakside defenders sag to help, then recover. On the shuffle cut, the cutter’s defender forces the cut behind the screen while a weakside defender shows to force the cutter wide, then recovers. The original defender takes a shorter route to regain position and deny the post pass. Similar show-and-recover tactics defend the subsequent down screen, followed by aggressive on-ball pressure, pass denial, and weakside interior help.

The “SOS” disruption strategy traps the ballhandler near the sideline because the off guard’s low-post cut makes ball reversal difficult. The high-post defender joins the on-ball defender in the trap while teammates switch, deny passes, front post players, and occupy helpside positions. If the ball escapes cross-court, defenders rotate as the pass is released and match up using the near-player concept. Contact switches counter both the shuffle cut and down screen. Once matched up, SOS principles apply, including “Base Go Red” rotations against baseline penetration and “Post Trap” rotations against post entries.
Jane Goodall’s legacy includes chimpanzee stories and enduring skeletons; she died October 1 at age 91.

A safety is a defensive back positioned deep as the last line of defense against major passing or rushing plays. Safeties protect against passes, support run defense, create turnovers, make tackles, and communicate coverage adjustments. Quarterbacks monitor their positioning to identify defensive weaknesses.

Free safeties typically roam the middle without a specific assignment, provide deep coverage, and rely on speed. Strong safeties generally play closer to the line, tackle more often, defend the run, and may cover running backs, tight ends, slot receivers, or zones. Alternative names include “Rover” for a strong safety and “Star” for an extra safety in specialized packages.

Effective safeties must be quick, athletic, strong tacklers, capable in man and zone coverage, and skilled communicators with a broad view of the field. Their coverage abilities have become increasingly important as football has grown more pass-oriented.

Notable safeties include Troy Polamalu, Ed Reed, Ken Houston, Steve Atwater, Ronnie Lott, Brian Dawkins, Emlen Tunnell, Larry Wilson, and Sean Taylor. Great safeties strengthen the entire defense by limiting throwing areas, supporting cornerbacks, forcing turnovers, stopping first downs, and preventing touchdowns. Because mistakes can leave no backup defender, positioning, leadership, and communication are critical.

Residents of San Andrés Hueyapan, Morelos, face heightened stress from Popocatépetl’s renewed activity following the September 19 earthquake, which severely damaged the town and destroyed many homes. Authorities advised nearby communities to prepare for a possible eruption. Although residents traditionally view the volcano, called Don Goyo, as less frightening than earthquakes, recent eruptions and tremors have increased anxiety. Ashfall was reported in Tetela del Volcán and Zacualpan de Amilpas. Despite losing part of her home and workshop, resident Araceli Soberanes Estrada continues weaving clothing.

Backtests indicate positive futures-expiration-week effects for DAX 40 and Euro Stoxx 50, whose contracts expire on the third Friday of March, June, September, and December. DAX 40 averaged a 0.39% gain with a 57% win rate, versus 0.12% in a random week. Euro Stoxx 50 averaged 0.3% with a 54% win rate, versus 0.18% randomly. December performed best for both, while Euro Stoxx 50 recorded a substantial average loss in June. The week after DAX 40 expiration averaged a 0.1% loss with a 47% win rate. That test used 100% margin, investing at expiration Friday’s close and selling one week later, without commissions or slippage. Expiration weeks are more volatile due to “pin” risk.

Sean “Diddy” Combs was sentenced in Manhattan to 50 months in prison and fined $500,000 after being convicted on two Mann Act counts for transporting sex workers across state lines for “freak offs.” The jury acquitted him of sex trafficking and racketeering conspiracy, rejecting prosecutors’ claims that women were coerced.

Prosecutors sought at least 135 months, while defense attorneys requested no more than 14 months. Combs apologized to his victims and family, calling his conduct “disgusting, shameful, and sick.” Judge Arun Subramanian said Combs had physically, emotionally, and psychologically abused women and praised those who testified against him. Combs continues to face civil lawsuits alleging sexual assault, rape, drugging, and violence, which he denies.

The Second Circuit affirmed Samuel Israel III’s conviction and twenty-year sentence. It held that Judge McMahon did not abuse her discretion by declining to recuse herself because her retention of the case, a docketing error, comments concerning an adjournment, and recusal from a related bankruptcy case did not indicate actual or apparent partiality. The court also rejected Israel’s sentencing challenges, finding no bias, no basis for a downward departure for medical needs, and no error in the credit awarded for cooperation. Given the duration of Israel’s criminal conduct and the amount of money involved, the sentence was within the permissible range.

The report proposes the “Hope Initiative” to protect and sustain education for Arab children affected by conflict, using Syria as its main example. Conflict, displacement, poverty, damaged schools, scarce resources, inadequate teacher training, and psychological trauma have deprived millions of children of consistent, quality education. Syrian children face school dropout, interrupted learning, limited materials and infrastructure, child labor, language and registration barriers, and insufficient psychosocial support.

Using interviews, a case study, and an online survey, the researchers examined educational experiences in war zones. Ahmed, a Syrian child, studies only a few hours weekly in an unsafe, poorly equipped communal space while balancing farming and caregiving. Interviews similarly identified destroyed schools, repeated relocation, anxiety, concentration difficulties, textbook shortages, unreliable electricity and internet, and community-led learning efforts.

The report recommends immediate emotional and academic support, safe temporary learning spaces, regular tutoring, mobile education units, materials, and psychological services. Its long-term proposal is an integrated regional system that anticipates crises, maintains education during conflict, supports vulnerable children, strengthens resilience, and prepares communities for recovery and peace-building.
The UC1825BEVM-CVAL uses an RCD switch-node clamp. A recommended Kclamp of 1.5 limits overshoot to about 50%; component starting values depend on transformer parasitics and voltage variation.

U.S. stocks rose Monday, led by technology and semiconductor shares, despite shutdown risks and energy-sector weakness. A shutdown could delay economic data and complicate Federal Reserve decisions, increasing volatility. Investors still expect a modest rate cut, though stronger data and hawkish remarks have reduced expectations for aggressive easing. Congressional negotiations are likely to shape near-term market sentiment.

The Great Barrier Reef recovered from five major die-offs over 30,000 years by migrating seaward or landward as sea levels changed. Fossil cores show it moved between 20 centimetres and 1.5 metres annually. Researchers warn this adaptability may be insufficient against today’s faster warming, acidification, bleaching and other stresses. Past deaths resulted from air exposure, rising seas and sediment deposits. A 2016 heatwave killed nearly a third of its coral. Bleaching deprives corals of food, increases disease risk and threatens reefs that support about a quarter of ocean life.

The Supreme Court reversed the Eighth Circuit and held that Brooks was entitled to journeyman machinist seniority at North Little Rock dating from November 3, 1955. Brooks’s railroad apprenticeship had been interrupted by military service, after which he completed training in 1958 and received seniority from that date. The District Court found that advancement from apprentice to mechanic was automatic in practice and that, absent military service, Brooks probably would have completed training and become a journeyman at North Little Rock in 1955. Applying Tilton v. Missouri Pacific Railroad Co., the Court ruled that uncertainty about future labor demand could not defeat a veteran’s statutory seniority rights. The case was remanded for proceedings consistent with the opinion.

Americans spent over $100 billion on summer vacations last year, while experts say travel can reduce stress and health risks and improve energy and relaxation. To control costs, travelers recommend setting a budget based on available funds, comparing prices through travel websites, and seeking hotel and fuel deals. Use credit cards without foreign transaction fees, carry a backup card, and manage overseas phone charges. Travel during the offseason, book transportation and lodging early, consider trip insurance, monitor airline newsletters for short-lived offers, and seek local discounts through information centers, hotels, newspapers, and city passes.

Russian journalist and Kremlin critic Arkady Babchenko appeared alive at a Kiev news conference after Ukrainian authorities staged his reported murder to disrupt an alleged Russian assassination plot. Babchenko apologised to his wife, friends and family, who were not told about the operation.

Ukrainian Security Service chief Vasyl Gritsak said Russian security services allegedly paid a Ukrainian citizen $40,000 to organise the killing. The suspect, who allegedly hired an acquaintance as the gunman, was detained. Gritsak said the assassination was part of a broader plan involving weapons, explosives and terrorist attacks in Ukraine.

Babchenko said authorities had known about the contract on his life for two months and approached him one month earlier. The war reporter fled Russia in 2017 after receiving threats linked to his criticism of the Kremlin, including its annexation of Crimea and support for separatists in eastern Ukraine.

The PGA848 front end driving an ADS8860 uses ±15V supplies, a 5V ADC reference, and three filters for EMI/RFI reduction, bandwidth control, and SAR ADC charge kickback. A 75pF feedback capacitor provides nominal 318kHz bandwidth, falling to 277kHz with resistor tolerance, while maintaining –0.1dB flatness to 41kHz. C0G capacitors minimize distortion.

The PGA848 REF pin is set to 2.5V using a precision divider from the REF6250 and an OPA192 buffer. A dual-feedback network and 20Ω isolation resistor provide an 86° phase margin; altered bypass capacitance requires simulation and verification of greater than 60° margin.

Nominal performance uses ±15V input- and output-stage supplies. Supplies above 40V total permanently damage the device. Recommended PCB practices include symmetrical input paths, local 0.1µF low-ESR bypass capacitors, separation of sensitive and noisy traces, minimized leakage, parasitic capacitance, vias, thermal junctions, and exposure to heat sources.

TI provides PSpice for TI and free TINA-TI simulation tools, related documentation, update notifications, and TI E2E support. Integrated circuits require ESD precautions. Mechanical and ordering data may change. Preproduction status, RoHS, finishes, moisture sensitivity, and markings are defined in ordering information. TI supplies resources “as is”; developers remain responsible for product selection, design validation, testing, and regulatory compliance.

The ARM Cortex-A8 subsystem controls device configuration, subsystems, peripherals, and external memory. It supports ARMv7, Thumb2, JazelleX, Media Extensions, AINTC, NEON SIMD, VFPv3, separate L1 caches, and a 128-bit interconnect. Designed for multitasking, it provides memory management, debugging, and ETM tracing through a 32KB system-level Embedded Trace Buffer.

The disclosure concerns silicone elastomers containing dispersed hydrophilic, oxidized carbon black particles. The particles are treated with silicone-compatible dispersants bearing carbon-black-affinic amino, acrylate, or epoxy groups, optionally during size reduction, then mixed with hydrophobic silicone pre-polymers and cured by addition or condensation. Dispersants may partially envelop the particles, converting them to hydrophobic, silicone-affinic particles while limiting aggregation.

Preferred dispersants include amino-silicones, silicone-acrylates, and silicone-epoxies with sufficient siloxane content for miscibility in the silicone matrix. Their concentration and functional-group content are balanced to promote dispersion without impairing curing. Curing may employ catalysts, cross-linkers, accelerators, retardants, volatile solvents, or hydrophobic fumed silica network formers.

The carbon black may be characterized by acidity, oxygen and volatile-matter content, negative zeta potential, Raman D/G-band ratios, and epoxy, hydroxy, or carboxylic surface groups. Treated particles commonly have low-micron or submicron sizes, with Dv90 generally no greater than 5 µm. Resulting compositions may contain substantial carbon black concentrations while retaining adequate mechanical integrity and substantially uniform particle distribution.

The disclosure also covers curable and cured compositions, articles containing them, and definitions and measurement methods for dispersibility, miscibility, hydrophobicity, particle size, and carbon-black properties. Potential uses rely on carbon black’s mechanical reinforcement, thermal or electrical conductivity, pigmentation, and radiation absorption, including printing-system transfer members, sealants, electronic devices, and medical or temperature-resistant applications.

The Blue Ridge Poison Control Center warns of increased spring exposure to poisonous plants, mushrooms, spiders, and snakes. It advises avoiding self-treatment, wearing protective clothing, checking boots, and remaining alert outdoors.

President James Madison, responding to Congress, designated the third Thursday of August 1812 as a national day of public prayer and humiliation, seeking forgiveness, divine protection and guidance during war, national unity, justice among nations, and the restoration of peace.

Southern California will be mostly sunny Wednesday and Thursday, with morning coastal low clouds and fog. An excessive heat watch is in effect Friday morning through Saturday evening across all listed zones. Friday highs range from 85–91°F at beaches to 107–115°F in inland valleys and 111–117°F in deserts. Temperatures ease gradually after the weekend. A high surf advisory covers Orange and San Diego County coastal areas from Wednesday evening through Friday evening. Mountain and some desert areas have slight chances of weekend or early-week thunderstorms.

A study announced by Miami-Dade Mayor Carlos Gimenez estimated PortMiami’s economic impact at over $41 billion, with 300,000 related jobs and $288 million in 2016 state and local taxes. The port handled 8.9 million tons of cargo and a record 5.1 million cruise passengers. The Miami Herald questioned whether the study inflated figures, which Gimenez defended. A planned $247 million Royal Caribbean terminal is projected to generate $500 million annually.
IT Central Station reviewers praise Exadata’s smart scans and Vertica’s columnar storage, but criticize Exadata patching and Vertica documentation; a report provides detailed comparisons.

The U.S. added 200,000 jobs in January, while unemployment remained at 4.1 percent. Average hourly wages rose 2.9 percent year over year, potentially reflecting a tightening labor market and minimum-wage increases in 18 states affecting 4.5 million workers. Employers added 2.1 million jobs in 2017, similar to 2.2 million in 2016. African-American unemployment rose from 6.8 percent in December to 7.7 percent, though it has declined substantially since 2010. Economists cautioned against attributing trends to presidential policies or relying on one monthly report because estimates are revised and have a margin of error of about 100,000 jobs. December’s estimate was raised to 160,000 jobs, while November’s was lowered to 216,000.

Coronation Street’s storyline about Aidan’s suicide is praised for sensitively portraying loved ones’ anger, disbelief and sadness. The writer recalls surviving a teenage suicide attempt while struggling with sexuality. Their friend Cheryl describes the lasting trauma of her husband John’s suicide at 31 aboard a cruise ship 33 years ago. With no note, warning signs or known depression, she continues to question why it happened and lives with enduring sadness and anger. The writer reflects on the devastation suicide leaves behind.

The author argues that IEX has failed to become a disruptive stock exchange, capturing less than 3% of trading volume because of a split identity. “IEX One” uses its speed bump to improve execution for large buy-side market orders but remains dependent on the SEC’s national market system, much like traditional exchanges. The speed bump effectively imposes an implicit cost benefiting market orders over resting orders, limiting IEX to a small niche.

“IEX Two” represents the broader ambition to serve all traders and unify the market. According to the author, achieving this requires abandoning reliance on the speed bump, balancing buy- and sell-side interests, delivering liquidity, and bypassing the national market system, which protects exchanges from service-based competition. Market dominance would also require support from brokers and traders for an alternative trading vehicle.

The Pakistan Super League will hold a new draft on Feb. 22 to replace foreign players unwilling to attend the March 5 final in Lahore over security concerns. The PCB promised top-level security, backed by Pakistan’s army chief, but a recent bombing and a FICA travel warning raised doubts. PSL chairman Najam Sethi said several foreign players remained willing to participate, viewing the final as a step toward bringing international cricket back to Pakistan.

After her 20-year marriage ended at age 49, the author realized she knew little about the couple’s accounts, investments, insurance, or major purchases. With support from a friend and a financial planner, she gathered financial documents, created budgets, and developed a retirement plan. Having spent years as a stay-at-home mother, she also secured a job providing steady income and health insurance, remaining there for seven years. Since her divorce, she has learned to manage major purchases, home repairs, and financial decisions independently. Although she regrets not participating more in earlier financial decisions, she is now confident in her career and financial future and plans to pursue retirement on her own terms.

The study examines barriers to women’s education in rural Pakistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir, where female literacy is 51.9% nationally and 40.8% in rural areas, compared with 73.3% for men. Using open-ended surveys and thematic analysis, researchers collected responses from literate and illiterate women. Both groups considered women’s education necessary and expressed hope for the future.

Major barriers include poverty, household workloads, poor time and resource management, patriarchal attitudes, limited family support, illiterate parents, early marriage, religious misconceptions, inadequate transport, distant and insufficient schools, weak infrastructure, language difficulties, outdated curricula, technical limitations, and shortages of qualified teachers. Women are often prioritized below boys, restricted from traveling or working, and expected to focus on domestic duties and childcare.

The study recommends awareness seminars involving parents and women, educational programming through media and social platforms, legislation supporting compulsory female education, and expanded open and distance learning opportunities.

The author praises Maine’s inland wilderness and supports retaining the Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument designation. Created from a private donation of more than 87,000 acres and backed by a $40 million private endowment, the monument is presented as preserving natural resources while promoting tourism, investment, and economic growth in rural Maine. The author criticizes Gov. Paul LePage’s effort to revoke the designation and notes that Sens. Susan Collins and Angus King and Rep. Chellie Pingree support retaining it. Interior Secretary Ryan Zinke is visiting the monument as part of a review, and the author hopes his experience canoeing and meeting local businesspeople will convince him of its cultural, environmental, and economic value.

The CAG’s 2015/16 report found widespread procurement and project-management violations, including poorly managed contracts, noncompetitive purchases, delayed projects, unauthorized procurement and transactions without valid or legally vetted contracts. It also reported weak asset management, including 37 dilapidated buildings across 12 Tanzanian embassies and ten undeveloped plots intended for embassies abroad.

ESPN grew from a 1979 startup into Disney’s major profit engine through advertising and affiliate fees paid by cable and satellite operators. Its expansion was driven by premium sports rights, particularly the NFL; competition from satellite providers; additional ESPN channels; extensive news programming; and strong cross-platform branding. Disney acquired 80% of ESPN through its 1996 merger with Capital Cities/ABC, while Hearst retained 20%.

By the early 2010s, ESPN received more than $7 monthly from over 100 million subscribers, whether they watched or not. By 2023, cable and satellite subscriptions had fallen to about 70 million, while sports-rights costs continued rising. Broadband, streaming, changing consumer preferences, and competition from media and technology companies weakened ESPN’s traditional business model.

Disney acquired streaming technology provider BAMTech and launched ESPN+ in 2018 as a supplementary direct-to-consumer service. By 2024, ESPN+ had about 25 million subscribers and average monthly revenue per user of $6.30. Disney planned to offer ESPN’s flagship networks directly to consumers in 2025. Disney, Fox, and Warner Bros. Discovery also announced Venu Sports, a jointly owned streaming bundle scheduled for fall 2024.

These initiatives marked ESPN’s transition from a stable business-to-business model centered on affiliates and advertisers toward a consumer business requiring subscriber acquisition, retention, first-party data, product innovation, and profitability. Streaming provides direct customer relationships and enhanced viewing capabilities but introduces volatility, churn, high costs, and potential harm to ESPN’s remaining linear business.

The broader sports-media market includes incumbent media companies, technology firms, sports properties, distributors, and fans. Amazon, YouTube, Apple, Netflix, and social platforms participate with differing objectives, while leagues seek to balance reach, revenue, and relevance. U.S. sports-rights spending reached $25.57 billion in 2023 and was projected to exceed $30 billion by 2025. Cable operators increasingly prioritize broadband, reconsider video services, and integrate streaming products into distribution agreements.

Fans have gained more choices in access, content, and services, but face fragmentation, discoverability problems, subscription limits, and potentially substantial costs. A sample package combining internet, premium cable, Peacock, Amazon Prime, and ESPN+ totaled $251 monthly. Piracy and varying levels of fan interest further complicate the market.

Disney began separately reporting ESPN’s finances in 2023. In the quarter ending March 30, 2024, ESPN Domestic generated $3.866 billion in revenue, up 4%, while operating income fell 9% to $780 million because of additional programming costs and fewer affiliate subscribers. ESPN’s future depends largely on managing sports-rights obligations, replacing declining affiliate revenue with profitable subscriptions, selecting economically sustainable rights, and becoming a leading digital sports platform.

Competitive Capabilities International and R&G Global Consultants partnered to develop Stable Operations TRACC, a data-driven continuous improvement product for manufacturing and supply chains. It aims to create a 15–20% capacity increase within six months while addressing capacity utilization, service delivery and CAPEX avoidance. First deployed by Cargill, the product combines analytics, TRACC methodology, maturity roadmaps and blended learning to scale and sustain operational improvements across multiple sites.

An offensive switch in soccer is an exchange of positions between two attacking teammates to confuse defenders and create passing opportunities. Switches may be called verbally or occur naturally, with or without ball possession. In a basic lateral or horizontal switch, players make crossing diagonal runs toward opposite sidelines, temporarily assuming each other’s roles. In a vertical switch, players exchange positions back-to-front or front-to-back toward opposite goal lines. Unlike an overlapping run, a vertical switch involves an actual positional exchange. Switches can create uncertainty in 2 v 1 or 2 v 2 situations and are usually used in the opponents’ half. Afterward, players may verbally coordinate returning to their original positions by saying “Switch back” or “Switching back.”

Tesla appointed Joseph Gebbia to its Board of Directors effective September 25, 2022. Gebbia has no reportable related-party transactions and is eligible for standard outside director compensation, but waived cash compensation until further notice and equity compensation until July 2023. He was not appointed to any board committees. Tesla announced the appointment in a September 28 blog post attached to the Form 8-K.

At NVIDIA’s May 20, 2015 annual meeting, stockholders elected all 12 director nominees to one-year terms, approved executive compensation on an advisory basis, and ratified PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as the independent accounting firm for the fiscal year ending January 31, 2016. The Form 8-K was signed May 26, 2015, by Rebecca Peters.

Tropical Storm Nate is strengthening in the western Caribbean and moving toward the southeastern United States. West Tennessee will remain mild and dry Friday night, but could receive heavy rain Saturday evening through Sunday morning if Nate follows its forecast path. Severe weather risk is low, and the projected path has shifted east.

LifeCLEF 2014 evaluated content-based plant identification under realistic, socially sourced conditions. Its PlantCLEF dataset contained 60,962 images representing 19,504 observations of 500 European tree, herb, and fern species, contributed by 1,608 users. Images covered seven views—entire plant, fruit, leaf, flower, stem, branch, and leaf scan—and included contextual and social metadata. Key innovations were multi-image observation queries, image-quality ratings, the branch category, and expansion to 500 species.

The task required systems to rank species for observations comprising one or more images of the same plant. The dataset was divided into 47,816 training and 13,146 test images. Evaluation used the inverse rank of the correct species, averaged by plant and user to reduce contributor-related bias. A secondary metric evaluated individual-image predictions.

Ten of 74 registered research groups submitted runs. Methods included Fisher vectors, convolutional neural networks, bags of visual words, local and global descriptors, shape analysis, support vector machines, nearest-neighbor classifiers, random forests, and metadata processing.

IBM AU achieved the highest observation-level score, 0.471, by combining Fisher vectors, a convolutional neural network, and segmentation. Its Fisher-vector and combined runs occupied the top three positions. PlantNet’s feature-matching approach ranked next, scoring 0.289. Results indicated that implementation, parameter tuning, color descriptors, and observation-aware validation could substantially affect performance. Metadata was rarely beneficial; Miracl’s textual and structural metadata reduced performance relative to its visual method.

Combining multiple images from one observation generally improved identification compared with single-image results, though gains were modest. Leaf scans and flowers were the easiest categories, while branch images were generally more difficult. IBM AU performed particularly well on branches, while shape-focused methods reduced the gap on leaf scans. CNN performance was strongest for flowers, a category with relatively abundant training data.

The task demonstrated progress in scaling plant-recognition methods to more species and varied plant organs, while concluding that deployment across thousands of species remained difficult. A possible future extension was identification across approximately 5,000 species in the French flora.

An EF-0 tornado with 75 mph winds damaged a mile-long path near Broad Run in Fauquier County on August 11. It lasted two minutes and caused no injuries. Four days earlier, an EF-1 tornado struck Salisbury, Maryland, also without injuries.
With the team needing a win, the speaker urges aggressive play without fearing mistakes, continued shooting despite blocks, and seeking a fortunate bounce.

MatterMech is a benchmark for evaluating large language models’ ability to reason about physicochemical mechanisms in nanomaterial synthesis. It contains 4,800 MCQ and text-infilling questions across eight subdomains, derived from approximately 17,000 papers. Questions were generated with Claude-3.5-Sonnet, refined through a Worker–Reviewer–Critic multi-agent system to reduce hallucinations, and quality-checked through human evaluation. MatterDB supplements the benchmark with 31,735 papers linking extracted synthesis mechanisms to academic sources.

Evaluation of 14 models showed stronger performance on multiple-choice reasoning than precise text infilling. Qwen-Max achieved the highest MCQ accuracy at 61.99%, while Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct led text infilling at 35.25%. Larger models generally performed better. Reasoning-focused models were competitive on MCQs but often weaker at reproducing exact domain terminology. Performance varied moderately across subdomains, with polymer questions strongest and semiconductor questions weakest in MCQs.

Multi-agent refinement improved semantic alignment with source documents, and human ratings averaged about 4 out of 5 for logic, distractor quality, and question clarity. Principle-guided prompting outperformed automatic chain-of-thought prompting, improving accuracy, reducing output length, and increasing stability. The study concludes that current LLMs reason logically but struggle to combine conceptual knowledge with principle-based reasoning reliably enough for scientific hypothesis generation. Limitations include the absence of expert annotations during benchmark construction and the dataset’s static representation of an evolving field.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 29, 2019 reported quarterly net sales of $53.8 billion, up 1% year over year, and net income of $10.0 billion, down from $11.5 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $2.18. Growth in Services and Wearables, Home and Accessories offset lower iPhone sales; foreign currency weakness adversely affected revenue.

For the first nine months, net sales were $196.1 billion and net income was $41.6 billion. Operating activities generated $49.5 billion in cash. At quarter-end, Apple had $322.2 billion in assets, $225.8 billion in liabilities, $96.5 billion in shareholders’ equity, and $210.6 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities.

Apple repurchased $49.2 billion of stock during the nine months, while its authorized repurchase program increased to $175 billion. Outstanding term debt totaled $98.3 billion. The filing also describes accounting-policy changes, financial instruments, tax matters, legal proceedings, supply risks and geographic segment results.

The passage describes TMS320DM81xx device memory addressing, pin functions, boot configuration, multiplexing, and electrical connection requirements. The TILER provides an additional 4-GB address range through a 33rd address bit for rotated or mirrored frame-buffer views; the full range is limited to HDVPSS and ISS, while other masters can access one view through the base-map 512-MB TILER region.

Terminal-function tables document signal names, package pins, pin types, internal pull states, supply voltages, multiplexed functions, control registers, and de-selected input states. Covered interfaces include boot/GPMC, DDR2/DDR3 controllers, EMAC, GPIO, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, reset/JTAG, SD, SPI, clocks, timers, UART, USB, digital and analog video, and power supplies. DDR data strobes synchronize transfers, while many DDR pullups or pulldowns change state when reset is released. Interface-specific requirements include external pullups for I2C, required supply connections even for unused modules, and prescribed handling of unused analog or reserved pins.

At reset de-assertion, BTMODE[15:0] values are sampled and stored in CONTROL_STATUS. BTMODE[4:0] selects an ordered sequence of boot modes; BTMODE[15:11] configures GPMC CS0 defaults; BTMODE[9:8] selects the Ethernet PHY mode during EMAC boot; BTMODE[10] selects GPMC XIP pin options; and BTMODE[7:5] is reserved and should be pulled down. Boot tables identify pins configured for XIP, NAND, I2C EEPROM, MMC/SD, SPI, EMAC, PCIe, and UART booting.

Pin multiplexing is controlled individually through PINCNTL1–PINCNTL270 MUXMODE fields. A zero MUXMODE generally tri-states the pin; inputs are usually routed to all sharing peripherals, although some de-selected inputs receive fixed values. Multimuxed functions may be routed to multiple pins with different timing characteristics.

Unused signal pins may generally remain unconnected unless specified otherwise, but inputs must not float. Internal or external pull resistors should establish valid levels, with external resistors strongly recommended for undriven boot pins. Resistor selection must account for leakage, logic thresholds, drive strength, supply and component tolerances, and other pulls. Typical guidance is 1 kΩ to oppose an internal pull and 20 kΩ to complement one or provide a pull where internal pulls are disabled, subject to application verification.

Dr. Edith Mbagwu recommends using SMART goals to support realistic, sustainable weight loss. Goals should be specific about exercise and diet, measurable through motivating assessments, attainable, realistic given available resources and time, and time-based. She advises periodically reassessing goals, setting smaller milestones, and avoiding unhealthy expectations. Quantizing the Dirac field with ordinary commutators produces bosonic symmetry and a Hamiltonian unbounded below. Replacing commutators with anticommutators yields a positive Hamiltonian and fermionic creation and annihilation operators. Each fermionic mode can be occupied only once, reproducing the Pauli exclusion principle.

The field expansion gives particle and antiparticle states with momentum, two spin polarizations, equal mass, and spin one-half. A conserved U(1) Noether charge assigns opposite charges to these states after subtracting an infinite vacuum constant, explaining their particle–antiparticle interpretation. Applied to electrons, the theory predicts the positron, later observed in cosmic rays. More generally, the spin-statistics theorem associates half-integer-spin fields with anticommutation relations and Fermi-Dirac statistics, while integer-spin fields use commutators and Bose-Einstein statistics.

Dirac-field two-point functions can be expressed by applying the operator \(i\partial\!\!\!/ + m\) to corresponding scalar-field correlators. Fermionic time ordering introduces a minus sign when operator order is exchanged, and the momentum-space Feynman propagator is the matrix inverse of the Dirac operator with the usual epsilon prescription.

The lecture concludes by introducing ways to reduce the four-complex-component Dirac spinor: chiral fermions use two complex components, while Majorana fermions use four real components.

The study examined difficulties in university foreign-language education after the Covid-19 pandemic forced a shift from face-to-face to distance learning. Distance education may be synchronous, asynchronous, or hybrid and offers flexibility, accessibility, reduced geographical and temporal limitations, and recorded lessons. Its disadvantages include technical barriers, limited interaction and feedback, security concerns, low participation, and difficulty teaching and assessing practical skills. These limitations are particularly relevant to language learning, which requires dialogue, imitation, repetition, and development of listening and speaking skills.

An online survey was completed by 294 undergraduate and graduate students studying German or English in spring 2020–2021. A 53-item scale assessed six categories of distance-education problems. Microsoft Teams and Zoom were the primary virtual-classroom platforms.

Internet and computer problems were rated highest, particularly connection interruptions, freezing, and poor connectivity. Student-related problems were also substantial, led by lack of motivation and low active participation. Course-content issues centered on insufficient mutual communication, while measurement problems included difficulty assessing skill-based learning. Teacher-related and software-related problems were rated comparatively low, although monotonous delivery was the leading teacher issue.

Male students reported more student-related problems than female students, but no other gender differences were found. Results did not differ between German and English students. Students without training in distance-education software experienced more software-related and overall problems. Those lacking a private study room or home internet connection reported greater problems across all categories.

Students viewed distance education as unsuccessful and less effective than face-to-face foreign-language teaching, citing inadequate materials, problematic assessment, limited participation, insufficient preparation, and inadequate knowledge of relevant programs. The study recommends training students in self-discipline, responsibility, planning, and software use; training teachers in virtual instruction, assessment, materials, communication, and classroom management; and adopting a hybrid model for foreign-language education.

This exploratory study examined whether a mitochondrial polygenic score (MGS) and lifestyle or environmental factors influence Parkinson’s disease age at onset (AAO). It included 9,745 patients from AMP-PD, Fox Insight, and a Tunisian Arab-Berber cohort: 486 with LRRK2-associated Parkinson’s disease (LRRK2-PD) and 9,259 with idiopathic Parkinson’s disease (iPD). A harmonized MGS based on nine mitochondrial-function-related SNPs was analyzed alongside smoking, caffeine consumption, and pesticide exposure using regression and Kaplan-Meier methods; p-values were not corrected for multiple testing.

Higher MGS was associated with earlier AAO in LRRK2-PD, with each 1% score increase corresponding to approximately one month earlier onset. This association was stronger among European/White patients and weaker among Tunisian Arab-Berber patients. No overall MGS-AAO association was found in iPD.

Smoking was associated with later AAO in iPD but not LRRK2-PD. Black tea consumption was associated with later onset in LRRK2-PD, while coffee was associated with later onset in iPD. Caffeinated soda was associated with earlier onset in both groups. Workplace pesticide exposure was associated with earlier onset in iPD but not LRRK2-PD.

In LRRK2-PD, MGS interacted with coffee and caffeinated soda consumption. Patients with high MGS who consumed coffee or caffeinated soda had median onset approximately six and 11 years earlier, respectively, than consumers with low MGS. In iPD, high MGS interacted with caffeinated soda consumption and workplace pesticide exposure, corresponding to earlier onset. These iPD interactions persisted when analysis was restricted to European/White Fox Insight participants. No interactions were found for smoking, tea, caffeine dosage or duration, pesticide exposure duration, or pesticide exposure in LRRK2-PD.

Limitations included differing genotyping methods, use of only nine of the original 14 MGS variants across cohorts, questionnaire-related exposure uncertainty, population-specific effects, and incomplete environmental data. The findings indicate that mitochondrial genetic burden is associated with earlier onset in LRRK2-PD and that caffeine-related consumption and pesticide exposure may modify MGS effects in LRRK2-PD and iPD.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for periodic beam-failure measurements in beamformed wireless communications, particularly 5G NR. A user equipment determines measurement-period duration using the periodicities of beam-failure detection reference signals (BFD RSs) actually used to assess radio-link quality, such as CSI-RS, synchronization-signal, or PBCH blocks quasi co-located with reference signals of monitored control-channel receptions. The duration may be based on the shortest or longest relevant periodicity and a specified time value, ensuring that measurement periods contain an assessed BFD RS.

During each period, the UE monitors relevant BFD RSs and reports a beam-failure instance when all measured signals fail a specified signal-quality or block-error-rate threshold. A physical-layer entity may report instances and related BFD RS information to a higher-layer entity, such as MAC. After a specified number of consecutive instances, the UE may declare beam failure, identify a candidate beam, and send a beam-failure recovery request.

Using all configured BFD RSs to set measurement periods can create periods containing no RS assessed by the UE, causing counters to reset and failures to be missed. The disclosed approach excludes unassessed BFD RSs when determining periodicity. If no BFD RS is transmitted during a period, such as because it overlaps control signaling, the UE may ignore that period when updating the consecutive-failure counter or treat it as a beam-failure instance rather than resetting the counter. The methods may be implemented by processors and memory in UEs, base stations, and communication systems.

The ADS8681W/ADS8685W/ADS8689W use CONVST/CS to delimit data-transfer frames. Frames with 32 SCLK cycles accept a valid 32-bit command; shorter frames act as NOP writes but can return valid leading output bits, while longer frames use the last 32 input bits. Read results appear in the following frame, while writes execute at the CONVST/CS rising edge. Output can contain conversion or register data, fixed patterns, device address, range and alarm flags, parity, and zero padding.

The multiSPI interface supports four standard SPI modes, single- or dual-SDO output, and source-synchronous protocols using internal or external clocks. SPI-00-S is the power-up default. Nine configuration registers control identification, reset and low-power functions, input/output protocols, output formatting, input range, and alarm thresholds and status.

The devices integrate a 16-bit SAR ADC, analog front end, programmable gain amplifier, driver, and reference. An example industrial design combines the ADS8681W with an eight-channel differential multiplexer for programmable voltage, current, or temperature inputs. Programmable input and AVDD alarms support adjustable thresholds and hysteresis.

AVDD and DVDD require appropriate local decoupling. NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput rates while retaining specified wake-up requirements. PCB guidance recommends separating analog and digital routing, short low-impedance grounding, clean supplies, and closely placed reference and supply capacitors.
The labor department is preparing aid for an estimated 17,000 workers who could be displaced by Boracay’s proposed closure, including job fairs, skills training, and worker profiling.

MOTO is a three-layer framework for systematically mapping local transition-state networks around an energy minimum. It combines a multi-objective explorer that optimizes diversity, feasibility, and minimum-mode separability; a bilayer minimum-mode-following kernel using Hessian–vector products with Lanczos or LOBPCG eigensolvers; and deterministic bidirectional descent to verify saddle connectivity and identify connected minima.

In atomistic spin benchmarks, Hessian–vector-product methods closely matched explicit-Hessian eigenmodes while substantially reducing memory use and runtime. The implementation scaled to \(10^6\) spins, computing the two lowest-curvature modes with under 1 GB incremental memory and 0.5 seconds wall time. On a \(70\times70\) spin system, it used approximately 0.01% of the explicit-Hessian method’s incremental peak memory and achieved a tenfold speedup. Both L-BFGS and conjugate-gradient outer optimizers converged to index-1 saddles.

Applied to a DFT-parameterized Pd/Fe/Ir(111) model, MOTO mapped networks around a Néel skyrmion and an antiskyrmion, identifying twelve index-1 saddles and up to 32 transition channels. The mechanisms included meron- and antimeron-mediated duplication, chiral-droplet formation, bi-antiskyrmion formation, annihilation, and boundary-defect-induced changes in topological charge.

The same workflow was transferred to a Cartesian Ni heptamer on Ni(111), where it recovered low-barrier edge, corner, and concerted multi-atom rearrangements and certified their connectivity. This demonstrated applicability across differentiable spin and atomic potential-energy surfaces without changing the algorithmic core.

Limitations include dependence on physically appropriate masks and objectives, sensitivity to eigensolver and line-search parameters, and difficulties near degenerate curvature modes. Proposed improvements include multidimensional minimum-eigenspace following, preconditioning, automated parameter selection and stopping criteria, and integration with two-ended path solvers.

The passage challenges James Damore’s claim that women’s underrepresentation in technology reflects innate, fixed biological differences. Research indicates that men and women are more similar than different, cognitive traits exist on spectra, and brains combine characteristics traditionally labelled male and female. Brain plasticity shows that experience and training can alter brain structure and performance, including spatial cognition. Gender gaps in spatial skills have narrowed, disappeared, or reversed across times and cultures. Stereotypes, expectations, and perceived social status can affect anxiety, performance, brain activity, and grey matter. Conversely, empowerment and changes in mindset can reduce stereotype threat and performance anxiety. The author concludes that workplace environments and diversity training can alter abilities and outcomes that Damore treated as biologically unchangeable.

Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson suffered a hamstring injury in the third quarter of Baltimore’s Week 4 loss to Kansas City and did not return. Reports initially estimated a two-to-three-week absence, later describing him as week to week. Jackson missed consecutive practices and was considered doubtful for Week 5 against Houston, while his Week 6 availability was also uncertain. Coach John Harbaugh said Jackson could not have reentered the game. Another report said he may remain out until after Baltimore’s Week 7 bye.

Hospital-at-home programs nationwide are reducing or stopping admissions as a Medicare waiver permitting inpatient care in patients’ homes approaches its Sept. 30 expiration amid a possible government shutdown. CMS instructed providers to discharge or return Medicare patients to hospitals by midnight Tuesday unless Congress acts.

UMass Memorial, which treats about 20 home-hospital patients daily, paused admissions despite overcrowding in its facilities. Hackensack Meridian discharged all participants, ChristianaCare stopped admitting Medicare patients, and Mass General Brigham reduced its census from 60 to 40. National capacity is estimated at roughly 1,000 beds, concentrated in areas facing severe capacity constraints.

Hospital-at-home care is not a complete answer to crowding but helps free beds for urgent cases. Repeated short-term extensions have discouraged investment and created recurring disruption. A bipartisan five-year extension is under consideration, while experts argue a longer authorization is necessary to evaluate and shape a permanent program.

Following the November 11, 1918 armistice, President Wilson declared that America’s objectives had been achieved and called for supporting just democracy through example, counsel, and aid. Edward House praised Wilson, while Secretary Lansing congratulated Britain and France on their victory and valor. France, Japan, and Greece celebrated the armistice, honored American contributions and wartime sacrifices, and expressed hopes for peace, freedom, national unity, and a Society of Nations. Wilson also praised British Prime Minister Lloyd George’s approach to the difficult postwar tasks ahead.

The team needs to calm down after taking four consecutive penalties and return to its usual style. Strong penalty killing has relied on coaching adjustments, patience, coordinated pressure, hard battles, and smart defensive outlet plays. The opponent’s power play is dangerous because of its talented, hardworking players and depth. The key for the next game is to avoid penalties.

This study examined perceptions of ICT and Computer-Assisted Language Learning (CALL) integration in an EFL initial teacher education program at a university in southern Vietnam. Using Hong’s framework and a convergent mixed-methods design, researchers surveyed 67 final-year pre-service teachers, conducted a focus group with six of them, and interviewed three teacher educators.

Pre-service teachers reported substantial opportunities to develop CALL-related knowledge, particularly in finding online resources, creating digital teaching materials, using word-processing software, and presenting multimedia lessons. Opportunities were more limited for supervising online learning, selecting personalised online exercises, using mobile devices, and troubleshooting digital equipment. ICT was used mainly for resource discovery, lesson archiving, information exchange, and developing teaching materials. Some participants nevertheless considered the program’s technology content outdated or superficial.

ICT integration was constrained by educators’ limited confidence, knowledge, skills, time concerns, and resistance to change; pre-service teachers’ attitudes and engagement; unreliable internet, outdated equipment, and slow technical support; and the absence of formal institutional policies or guidelines. Educators wanted further professional development and clearer implementation requirements.

The study concludes that learning opportunities, infrastructure, professional development, administrative support, and consistent CALL policies are interdependent contributors to effective technology integration. Its findings are limited by the small sample, single institution, lack of educator assessment data, and absence of curriculum analysis.

Senator William Flinn’s will created life-income trusts from his residuary estate and allowed five years for administration. After stocks were transferred to the trustee and sold, life tenants and remaindermen disputed entitlement to post-death undistributed earnings.

The court held that, absent clear testamentary language selecting a later date, the intact value of trust assets is fixed at the testator’s death. The trusts and life tenants’ income rights became effective then; delaying them until estate settlement would permit an unlawful accumulation of income. Accordingly, the life tenants were entitled to relevant earnings accruing after Flinn’s death.

Stocks owned by Booth & Flinn Company were treated differently because the corporation was a separate legal entity, despite Flinn’s controlling ownership. Their intact value was therefore fixed when the company distributed them to the executors in January 1925, not at Flinn’s death.

The court also accepted averaging Gulf Oil’s annual earnings on a daily basis to estimate earnings accrued before Flinn’s February 1924 death, since no more accurate method was offered. The lower court’s decree was affirmed with the modification concerning the Booth & Flinn stocks, at the estate’s cost.
The order dismissing John Gracy’s habeas corpus writ and remanding him was affirmed. Four judges concurred, while Justice Manning dissented.

A study explored integrating Sibelius music notation software into a traditionally taught general music education course at a Caribbean university. Using a mixed-methods phenomenological design, researchers collected questionnaire and assignment data from 24 pre-service early childhood and primary teachers. Most participants reported enhanced understanding, 67% supported continued technology use, and 75% wanted further training, although many preferred traditional instruction or felt uncomfortable using the software during practicum. Twenty students submitted a composition assignment, completed overall with 90% accuracy. The study concluded that music software can be integrated relatively easily and positively affect learning outcomes. It recommended gradual continued use, progressive training, technology-based practicum criteria, and technology-focused final assessments.

The article argues that global citizenship education, while promoting human rights, environmentalism, social justice, multiculturalism and transnational participation, inadequately explains international conflict, security concerns, interstate cooperation and citizens’ influence on foreign policy. Recent tensions involving China and Russia’s war against Ukraine highlight the need to supplement it with theories of international politics.

Three perspectives are proposed. Realism views international relations as anarchic, with states prioritising security, survival and relative power; cooperation remains subordinate to national interests. Regionalism explains cooperation through shared benefits, especially economic integration, while recognising that states remain central actors. Institutionalism shows how international organisations, treaties and established practices create predictability and facilitate cooperation, although their authority is limited and major security issues may be settled outside them. The war in Ukraine illustrates both the importance of NATO and the EU and the limitations of the UN.

International cooperation depends on state interests and the nature of the problem. Global public goods may require action by one capable state, participation by every state, or cumulative efforts from many states. Coordination around common technical and regulatory standards can also produce benefits. Examples such as European integration, ozone protection and Norwegian-Russian fisheries management demonstrate that cooperation can succeed without a shared global citizenship identity.

The article recommends broadening global citizenship education to include military and economic security, power relations, national foreign policy and the conditions under which states cooperate. Young people should learn how states pursue security, prosperity, status and values through negotiation, information, economic measures and military power. Citizen engagement should include NGOs and transnational platforms but also democratic efforts to influence national foreign policy. Teaching should incorporate history, propaganda, misinformation and differing national contexts while addressing conflict carefully and highlighting successful examples of peace and cooperation.

The writer plans to retain a 1pm reporting target after readers favored accuracy over speed. The discussed company’s shares rose 17% to 145p, valuing it at £188.2m; the writer holds a short position. CEO Oozi Cats resigned immediately after an independent review confirmed a US indictment had been knowingly concealed from advisers. The writer criticizes the board and advisers for failing to investigate Cats’s background earlier.

Astronomers used JWST and archival Hubble images to identify the progenitor of Type II supernova SN2025pht in spiral galaxy NGC 1637, about 40 million light-years away. It is JWST’s first confirmed detection of a supernova progenitor and the first identified in mid-infrared light.

The progenitor was a massive red supergiant radiating roughly 100,000 times more light than the Sun. Dense surrounding dust made it appear over 100 times dimmer in visible light, explaining why it was absent from pre-explosion Hubble images but visible to JWST. The star was the reddest and dustiest red supergiant yet observed exploding as a supernova.

The findings support the idea that red supergiants frequently explode but often escape detection because thick dust obscures them. Unexpectedly, the star’s circumstellar dust was carbon-rich rather than dominated by oxygen-rich silicates, possibly because convection brought carbon from its interior to the surface. Researchers are now seeking similar stars, with future observations from the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope expected to aid the search.

The UAE’s Mars 2117 Project aims to establish the first inhabitable human settlement on Mars by 2117 through international scientific collaboration and faster transportation. It follows the UAE’s planned 2021 Mars probe mission. Announced by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum, the project seeks to advance science, technology and youth knowledge. SpaceX founder Elon Musk has separately proposed Mars colonisation using reusable transport while reducing travel costs.

NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended April 30, 2017 reported revenue of $1.94 billion, up 48% year over year, and net income of $507 million, up from $208 million. Diluted earnings per share rose to $0.79 from $0.35, while gross margin increased to 59.4% from 57.5%. Operating income was $554 million, and operating expenses increased 18% to $596 million.

GPU revenue grew 45% to $1.56 billion, driven by gaming, datacenter and professional visualization. Tegra Processor revenue rose 108% to $332 million, supported by gaming platforms, Nintendo Switch modules and automotive products. By market, gaming generated $1.03 billion, datacenter $409 million, professional visualization $205 million, automotive $140 million, and OEM and intellectual property $156 million.

At quarter-end, NVIDIA held $6.21 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, with total assets of $9.41 billion and shareholders’ equity of $6.13 billion. Operating activities generated $282 million; investing activities generated $754 million; and financing activities used $813 million, including $605 million for convertible-note repayments and $82 million in dividends.

NVIDIA intended to return $1.25 billion to shareholders during fiscal 2018 through dividends and share repurchases. It had authorization to repurchase up to $2.73 billion through December 2020. The company reported $1.98 billion of long-term debt and $215 million of convertible short-term debt.

NVIDIA continued construction of a new headquarters under an off-balance-sheet lease arrangement with up to $380 million in bank funding. It also faced patent litigation from Polaris Innovations but recorded no related liability because losses were considered possible rather than probable. Management concluded that disclosure controls were effective, with no material changes in internal control or previously reported risk factors.

The study introduces the “Simplified Egg and Changing Yolk Model” to explain ventricular repolarisation and ECG T-wave morphology. It represents the heart as an asymmetric egg-shaped muscle mass centred on Wilson’s Central Terminal (WCT), with repolarisation expanding outward like a growing yolk. Each ECG lead records the net difference between signals moving toward and away from it.

In the model, balanced signals produce the isoelectric ST segment. When repolarisation enters the asymmetric “T-zone,” an imbalance generates the T-wave. Electrically inert damaged regions alter this balance, reproducing ST depression, ST elevation, and higher, flattened, inverted, or biphasic T-waves. Their timing and morphology depend on damage location, severity, hypertrophy, ion imbalance, heart orientation, and lead direction.

The model proposes that repolarisation begins with the Q-wave and continues through the T-wave, treating the ST segment and T-wave as one process. It questions interpreting ST depression and elevation alone as specific indicators of ischemia or infarction and recommends considering damage location alongside other investigations.

The authors identify limitations in corrected QT (QTc) measurement, including formula variability and difficulty locating the T-wave end. They recommend the QTp interval, measured from Q-wave onset to T-wave peak, as a clearer and potentially more reliable measure for arrhythmia risk and medication effects. Future work will incorporate coronary artery distributions, investigate U-wave origins, apply the model to atrial repolarisation, and validate QTp across populations and settings.

Gbenga Ogundele, 58, and his wife, Mojisola Popoola, 42, of Laurel, Maryland, were sentenced to 234 months and 18 months in federal prison, respectively, followed by three years of supervised release, for wire fraud and money-laundering conspiracies involving an online dating scam. Ogundele was also convicted of aggravated identity theft. From 2011 to 2015, conspirators formed online romantic relationships with vulnerable victims and used false stories to obtain payments ranging from $1,720 to $50,000, channeling millions through “drop accounts” and concealing the funds through transfers and checks. Ogundele was ordered to forfeit about $2.2 million; Popoola must forfeit about $165,000 and pay $34,100 in restitution. Co-conspirator Victor Oloyede also received 234 months, while Babatunde Popoola received 12 years. Three others pleaded guilty to money-laundering conspiracy.

The disclosure describes methods and systems for creating virtual game environments from three-dimensional scans of real-world scenes. Users arrange physical objects, scan them with a capturing device, and generate digital representations that are converted into virtual toy construction models. Conversion rules translate detectable properties such as shape, dimensions, color, texture, and recognized object identity into virtual features, themes, behaviors, and game-controlling elements.

Known physical objects may be identified through image processing, visible markers, RFID, Bluetooth, or similar technologies. Stored object data can provide accurate virtual representations, attributes, animations, themes, and functionality. Recognized objects may be removed from scanned geometry, replaced with library models, or used to modify surrounding virtual areas. Virtual characters and objects can move within and interact with the resulting environment.

The disclosure also presents computational methods for converting surface meshes into voxel representations. Points distributed across each surface element are mapped to voxels, with surface attributes transferred to voxel attributes. A restricted color-search method efficiently selects the closest color from a predetermined palette. Voxel models can then be converted into virtual construction models composed of standardized, interconnectable elements.

Interactive game systems may combine a depth-sensitive camera, processor, storage, and display, optionally in a mobile device. Augmented-reality overlays can assist targeting and scanning. Games may operate cyclically: users create an environment, play game segments, receive rewards or tasks, modify physical models, and begin another cycle. Physical toy characters and tools may also unlock corresponding virtual characters, abilities, and equipment.

Ipswich striker Martyn Waghorn credits Sunderland legend Kevin Ball with reviving his career as a teenager by teaching him football’s fundamentals. Waghorn, who left Sunderland goalless in 2010, has since scored 87 career goals and returns to the Stadium of Light aiming to beat his former club.

A woman with multiple sclerosis says Delta employees tied her tightly to a wheelchair with a dirty blanket in Amsterdam because a chair with proper straps was unavailable, leaving bruises. Delta apologized and offered 20,000 SkyMiles, but her family seeks policy changes for handling passengers with disabilities.

The application describes novel triazine-containing compounds represented by Chemical Formula 1 and organic light-emitting devices incorporating them in one or more organic layers, particularly electron transport layers. The compounds allow varied aryl, heterocyclic, linker, and substituent groups and may be synthesized through coupling reactions. OLEDs may use normal or inverted structures and include hole injection, hole transport, light-emitting, electron transport, electron injection, and blocking layers. Preparation examples produced numerous compounds, which were tested in OLEDs against seven comparative electron-transport materials. At 10 mA/cm², devices using the disclosed compounds showed driving voltages of 3.76–3.91 V and current efficiencies of 5.19–5.46 cd/A, compared with 3.96–4.13 V and 4.89–5.18 cd/A for comparative devices. The disclosed compounds provided lower driving voltage, higher current efficiency, and longer lifetime.

The article examines leaders of education-related undergraduate programmes in English further education colleges using Hodgson and Spours’s four-layer lifelong learning ecology. Policy initiatives, widening participation, local employer links, higher education partnerships, professional practice and learners’ community contexts shape this provision.

The study used a 2020 questionnaire completed by 70 programme leaders and 11 follow-up interviews, focusing primarily on 14 questionnaire respondents and four interviewees from further education colleges. Most college programme leaders entered their roles through informal or internal routes. All reporting qualifications held master’s degrees, but fewer held doctorates or Higher Education Academy fellowships than university-based leaders. Opportunities for research, scholarship and higher education-specific professional development were constrained by workload and limited institutional support.

College programmes generally had smaller teams and cohorts than university programmes, leaving leaders with extensive teaching, management and administrative duties. Their poorly defined roles encompassed three main responsibilities: meeting colleges’ and higher education partners’ organisational requirements, supporting students academically, and responding to pastoral needs. Leaders managed recruitment, quality assurance, programme partnerships and mixed-level teaching while fostering undergraduate identities and supporting diverse, often non-traditional students. Flexible, local provision enabled progression into degrees and teacher training, but could conflict with institutional systems designed for further education students.
