The article characterises programme leaders as a “keystone species” anchoring local learning ecologies through specialised knowledge, close student relationships and commitment to widening participation. However, macro-level policy, partnership requirements and internal demands can overshadow student support and scholarly development. It proposes improved “sightlines” through greater access to research, academic communities, employer partnerships and networks with other colleges and universities. Such support could strengthen programme leaders’ ability to sustain, develop and innovate undergraduate provision in further education.

The “Give & Go” isolation offense uses a 2-1-2 spread, keeps control with the two best ball handlers, and positions the post weakside. A passer cuts hard to the basket; if no pass is available, the ballhandler dribbles out and repeats the action. Overplayed wings back cut, while soft or obstructive defense can be attacked with drives, spin moves, or behind-the-back dribbles. The post or weakside players provide pressure-release passes and may initiate further Give & Go action. Weakside players can exchange positions or use down and back screens to occupy sagging defenders. Screens must be stationary to avoid moving-screen fouls.

Leam Richardson dismissed the brief tunnel clash between Wigan’s Ivan Toney and Fleetwood’s Nathan Pond as harmless pushing and shoving, saying both later laughed about it. Toney could start against AFC Fylde in Tuesday’s FA Cup replay, alongside other squad players, as manager Paul Cook balances fielding a strong team with resting regulars. Victory would secure a third-round trip to Premier League Bournemouth, but Richardson stressed Wigan must first overcome a difficult Fylde side.

GPS-guided truck traffic through Ponca, Arkansas, has risen from about six unfamiliar trucks annually to at least six daily, leading to repeated crashes on steep, winding Arkansas 43. Seven trucks wrecked on a 2-mile stretch north of Ponca in 2½ years, often after drivers underestimated the 1,300-foot descent and lost their brakes. Some drivers suffered minor injuries, and an earlier fatal crash spilled diesel into the Buffalo River. Residents and businesses fear for motorists, pedestrians and tourists visiting the Buffalo National River and Boxley Valley. The Arkansas Highway and Transportation Department plans signs warning that the next 3 miles are crooked and steep, while officials continue evaluating the problem. An alternate-route warning is considered impractical because it would need to begin about 25 miles away in Harrison.

This unreviewed protocol describes a Danish register-based cohort study of trends in revision surgery for periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) after primary total hip arthroplasty. It will compare debridement, antibiotics and implant retention (DAIR), one-stage exchange, and two-stage exchange, and assess the risk of a second revision after each approach.

Using Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register data from public and private departments, the study will include adults undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty from 1995 to 2022. Hemiarthroplasty and simultaneous bilateral arthroplasty will be excluded. PJI revisions will be grouped by timing: within four weeks, four to twelve weeks, or more than twelve weeks after primary surgery.

Annual revision trends and causes will be reported. Second-revision risk will be analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for calendar time, age, and sex, and presented with Kaplan–Meier plots. Strengths include broad inclusion criteria, analysis of multiple revision methods, and long-term registry data. Limitations include incomplete reporting by some private clinics, surgeon-reported PJI diagnoses, the observational design, and limited applicability outside Denmark. No external funding was received; study costs are limited to investigator salaries paid by the orthopedic department.

Australia dominated the Philippines in a 2019 FIBA World Cup qualifier, leading 79-48 before a bench-clearing brawl and eventually winning by default, 89-53. Australia’s size, defense, passing, and shooting overwhelmed Gilas, which struggled offensively and committed 18 turnovers.

The confrontation began after RR Pogoy shoved Daniel Kickert, who retaliated, triggering punches, thrown chairs, and bottles. Although Philippine coach Chot Reyes cited alleged Australian aggression during warm-ups, the article argues that such circumstances did not excuse the Philippine team’s escalation and poor judgment.

Australia apologized for its role, while the Samahang Basketbol ng Pilipinas apologized for breaching Filipino hospitality and affirmed that violence has no place in sports. The article calls for accountability, restraint, further action beyond apologies, and recognition that forthcoming FIBA sanctions and the incident’s international impact could damage Philippine basketball’s reputation.

The patent describes a battery-powered floor cleaner with a wheeled base, pivoting steerable body, supply and recovery tanks, vacuum source, cleaning-fluid nozzle, suction inlet, handle controls, and brushroll. Component placement maintains the center of gravity behind the handle axis across varying tank levels for balance and control.

The recovery tank includes a removable cover, inlet duct, splash-reducing baffle, filter, guided shutoff float, and removable perforated strainer. The strainer fits around and engages the inlet duct, separates debris from recovered fluid, and has a handle protected from splashing. The float travels along the inlet duct and closes the suction outlet when fluid exceeds a desired level. Tank retention features maintain sealing when the cleaner body flexes.

A linkage permits the body to pivot for reclining and steering while keeping the base on the floor. Internal passages separate fluid tubing from electrical wiring. The brushroll may use hydrophobic textile fibers, including flexible fine fibers for wiping and larger helical fibers for agitation and vibration reduction.

A one-hand removable brushroll cover uses opposed, spring-biased latch actuators. The cover carries the distribution nozzle and mates with fluid couplings on the base. Cleaning fluid is sprayed visibly in front of the base, with lights providing illumination or operating-status indications.

Two squeegees direct surface fluid toward the suction inlet and remove fluid and debris from the brushroll. An optional secondary nozzle wets and cleans the brushroll. Rollers support the base, and an alternative raised cover edge exposes the brushroll for cleaning low vertical surfaces such as baseboards.

The Break, a longtime Five Points South restaurant and billiards hall, will be demolished for high-rise apartments. Some residents hope the development revives the area’s declining nightlife, while others criticize rising rents and want more affordable housing. No closure date has been announced.

Neiman Gracie criticized Dillon Danis for trash talking without professional MMA experience. Their proposed Bellator 180 fight was declined because Danis prioritized the IBJJF World Championship, so Gracie will face Dave Marfone on June 24.

This study examined teachers’ views of culturally responsive practices in the Turkish education system using Q methodology. Twenty-one public-school teachers from Denizli, Mardin, Erzurum, and Şanlıurfa ranked 30 statements about cultural diversity in education. Principal component and varimax analyses identified three perspectives—unification, student support, and teacher support—accounting for 35%, 16%, and 8% of variance, respectively. Seventeen participants loaded significantly on these factors.

Teachers generally viewed cultural diversity as valuable and accepted within the education system while recognizing persistent inequalities. Consensus was strongest, though often neutral, regarding cultural competence, general cultural practices, and students’ academic and social development. Major disagreements concerned measures against discrimination, whether different cultures are perceived as threats, and whether classrooms reflect society’s cultural diversity. Participants declined to explain their strongest rankings, preventing analysis of extreme statements.

The study concludes that Turkey has taken initial steps toward culturally responsive education but lacks sufficient student and teacher support, inclusive curricula, teaching materials, and systematic implementation. It recommends culturally responsive education workshops, stronger pre-service and professional teacher development, classroom support for free cultural expression, broader research, and dissemination of knowledge about different cultures. Limitations include participants’ reluctance to elaborate and their geographic concentration. No conflicts of interest or financial support were reported.

The patent describes electronic devices with display and touch-sensor layers extending beneath transparent and opaque enclosure surfaces. Devices may include phones, tablets, watches, computers, wearables, and other electronics. Transparent walls can cover displays and touch sensors, while opaque walls can support touch-only input. Sensors may cover front, rear, side, or inactive display areas, enabling gestures and controls without obstructing displayed images.

Enclosures may have planar, sloped, or curved walls. Display and touch layers can be rigid, flexible, attached with adhesive, deposited as coatings, or integrated on a shared substrate. Touch sensing may use capacitive, resistive, acoustic, force-based, or light-based technologies, while displays may use LCD, electrophoretic, plasma, organic light-emitting diode, discrete LED, electrowetting, or other pixel technologies.

Foldable configurations may use flexible transparent wall portions connecting planar sections, with continuous display and touch layers spanning fold regions. Devices may have one or multiple bend axes and hinges formed from flexible materials, accordion structures, or pivoting members. Stress-tolerant features—including thinned substrates, serpentine or redundant conductive traces, neutral-plane adjustment layers, and crack-resistant conductive materials—can reduce bending damage.

Fabrication methods include molding transparent walls, depositing and patterning sensor or display structures, laminating flexible layers onto planar and curved surfaces, applying protective hard coatings, and bending initially planar structures into curved forms. The described structures and methods may be used individually or in combination.

Progressive, the fourth-largest U.S. auto insurer, reported strong February 2018 results. Net earned premiums rose 19% year over year to $2.20 billion, while year-to-date premiums increased 18% to $4.89 billion. All business lines grew by at least 16%. The February combined ratio improved 2.6 percentage points to 87.8%, reflecting stronger underwriting profitability, although net income declined 4% to $129 million.

Personal, commercial motor, and property businesses all reported combined ratios below 91%. The company is considered capable of achieving its 2018 target of a group combined ratio below 95%. Progressive also recognized $70 million in additional premiums after expanding commercial auto coverage for an Uber subsidiary into three more states.

The company raised net proceeds of $1.08 billion through senior notes and preferred shares for general corporate purposes. The author expects book value to grow more than 10%, 2018 EPS to reach the upper end of a $2.50–$4.30 estimate, and the annual dividend to range from $0.76 to $1.85 per share. Estimated intrinsic value is approximately $48 based on current metrics and $50–$54 using projected 2018 figures. Despite strong growth and operating performance, the author considers Progressive slightly overvalued but believes existing shareholders can reasonably retain their shares.

A US study of more than 10 million students over 13 years found that each half-degree rise in annual average temperature corresponded to a 1% fall in exam scores, with air conditioning reducing the effect. UK students may be vulnerable because exams occur in June, when temperatures can exceed 21C, and schools often lack air conditioning. Changing exam timing or the academic year would disrupt institutions following the September-to-July calendar. However, annual grade boundaries adjust to average performance, limiting long-term disadvantage from unusually hot summers.

Gary Antonacci’s dual momentum strategy combines absolute momentum—an asset’s price performance over time—with relative momentum—its performance against peers. It buys the strongest asset among those with positive absolute momentum and, where short selling is practical, sells the weakest asset among those with negative momentum. Momentum research cited in the passage suggests the effect is strongest over periods of one to 12 months.

Signals are identified by calculating each asset’s rate of change and then ranking comparable assets. In bullish markets, the strategy favors leaders with positive absolute and relative momentum; in bearish markets, it may short the worst performers or move into bonds. Examples favor the S&P 500 over gold when both rise but the index gains more, and short crude oil when it falls more than natural gas.

The approach originated with relative-momentum research by Jagadeesh and Titman and was extended by Antonacci to include absolute momentum, aiming to reduce volatility. It can be applied to individual securities, futures, ETFs, and sector rotation, though Antonacci’s research favors geographically diversified equity ETFs with monthly evaluation and rebalancing.

Antonacci’s Global Equities Momentum model rotates among U.S. stocks, non-U.S. stocks, and bonds. One ETF backtest using SPY, EFA, and AGG produced a 6.75% annual return with a 30% maximum drawdown, versus 9.2% and roughly 55% drawdown for the S&P 500. Results were hypothetical and excluded some real-world costs. The strategy may underperform in strong bull markets or rapid rebounds but is presented as offering lower volatility and better protection in bear markets.

Hervey Bay dive operators disagree over the tourism impact of the ex-HMAS Tobruk landing on its starboard side after scuttling. Dive Hervey Bay owner Glenn Bowman said limited accessibility for general divers could halve projected income and reduce local spending. Hervey Bay Dive Centre owner Ed Gibson said the wreck remains accessible and tours can be adjusted, predicting tourism will thrive. Both agreed the dive would be spectacular. Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service said the wreck is in the correct restricted area and is undergoing safety inspections before the government reviews options and works with commercial operators.

The advance-decline (A/D) indicator is a market breadth measure tracking the cumulative difference between advancing and declining stocks. Its formula adds the current day’s advancing stocks minus declining stocks to previous net advances. A rising A/D line indicates strengthening market momentum, while a falling line suggests weakening momentum. Divergence between the indicator and a stock index may signal a potential reversal.

Advance/decline distribution includes the number and trading volume of rising and falling stocks. The Advance/Decline Volume Line similarly tracks the cumulative difference between advancing-stock and declining-stock volume, indicating buying or selling pressure.

The NYSE A/D line measures advancing versus declining NYSE-listed stocks. A strategy backtested with the NYSE indicator on the SPY ETF produced 229 trades, an average gain of 0.6%, and a profit factor of 1.55. Results were inconsistent, and multiple strategy versions failed to produce a satisfactory system. The article concludes that other oscillating indicators, such as RSI, Williams %R, or IBS, may be preferable.

Generative AI is transforming sectors such as finance, healthcare, and education but creates risks including misinformation, deepfakes, bias, discrimination, and regulatory uncertainty. Existing government rules and corporate AI principles seek to protect rights, safety, transparency, and accountability, yet differing national regulations, limited government-industry communication, and rapidly emerging risks complicate compliance and oversight.

The passage recommends forward-looking, human-centered governance that balances innovation with risk mitigation. It calls for collaboration among policymakers, industry, and academia, combined with bottom-up participation from developers, users, and communities. Governments and companies should establish transparent channels to report and investigate problems, promptly update regulations and guidelines, and use social-computing methods to identify the regulatory needs of specific communities.

A July 2001 energy news roundup focuses on failed negotiations over California’s demand for $8.9 billion in electricity-overcharge refunds. Federal mediator Curtis Wagner suggested refunds closer to $1 billion and limited calculations to sales since October 2000. Gov. Gray Davis said California would pursue the remaining claims in court, while generators disputed the state’s analysis.

Other reports cover Calpine’s $355 million purchase of natural-gas reserves; Edison International’s improving finances but uncertain utility rescue; concerns about California’s overloaded transmission grid; limited federal energy legislation; Texas officials’ claims that their electricity market would avoid California-style problems; and strong power-plant construction demand reported by Shaw Group.

A separate report describes California shepherds’ isolated working conditions, low pay, inadequate housing, and proposed state legislation requiring rest periods and basic amenities.

The team needs more aggressive offense and net pressure, but Detroit has effectively blocked shooting lanes and defended the crease. Both goaltenders and defenses have played well, though Ronnie Francis nearly scored. Enthusiastic home fans create the NHL’s loudest atmosphere and energize the players.

Global Ferronickel unit PGMC renewed a contract to supply Guangdong Century Tsingshan Nickel with 1.5 million wet metric tons of nickel ore at prevailing 2018 prices. Global Ferronickel’s 2017 income reached P779.7 million, while revenues rose 54% to P5.8 billion.

The passage reviews business ventures launched by wealthy or famous women, many of which suffered substantial losses despite personal wealth and outside investment. Millie Mackintosh closed her fashion company after losses and debts of £548,000. Ella Mills closed two of three delis after first-year losses of £723,811, while her separate Deliciously Ella business earned a £545,497 profit. Trinny Woodall’s cosmetics company reported a £70,089 loss after an initial profit but received £2.7 million from investors. Petra and Tamara Ecclestone’s accessories and haircare businesses accumulated multimillion-pound debts and losses. Alexa Chung’s fashion company lost £1.5 million in one year but secured nearly £3 million from friends. Kate Rothschild wound up her record label after it accrued debts, while Sadie Frost and Jemima French’s lingerie company was dissolved following years of mounting losses; their Floozie swimwear remained on sale.

Eurozone stocks fell Friday amid euro strength and anticipation of US jobs data. Frankfurt’s DAX dropped 1.7%, Paris’s CAC 40 lost 1.6%, and the STOXX 600 declined 1.4%. Deutsche Bank plunged 6.21% after reporting losses linked to US tax reforms.

NVIDIA filed a Form 8-K dated February 9, 2017, announcing financial results for the quarter and fiscal year ended January 29, 2017. The filing includes a press release and commentary from CFO Colette M. Kress as exhibits. These materials are furnished, not filed, under applicable securities laws.

This May 2018 ebook reproduces *Foreign Relations of the United States, Diplomatic Papers, 1942, Volume II, Europe*. The portable, searchable edition preserves the printed volume’s content and supports offline access, bookmarking, and note-taking. Document numbers are recommended for citations because ebook pagination differs from print.

The series constitutes the official record of U.S. foreign policy. Its selection and editing follow security requirements and principles of historical objectivity, requiring major policy documents and relevant supporting materials without concealing policy defects. The Historical Office prepared the volume under G. Bernard Noble and E. R. Perkins, with designated compilers covering Finland, France and North Africa, Greece, and the remaining sections. The Division of Publishing Services handled copyediting, proofreading, and indexes.

Salem residents sought bottled water as far away as Woodburn after officials announced cyanotoxins from an algae bloom had contaminated the drinking water. Neither Salem nor Oregon emergency officials planned water distribution sites, while local stores reported shortages and awaited shipments. Officials advised young children, pregnant or nursing women, people with certain health conditions, pets and other sensitive groups not to drink tap water and to use bottled water for food and beverages. Fresh test results were expected Thursday. Several nearby communities were also affected.

Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson’s 2022 investiture occurred three months after she began serving on the Supreme Court. Federal courts warned that a government shutdown could quickly restrict lower-court operations, while the Supreme Court would continue using permanent funds. As Chief Justice John Roberts marked 20 years leading the court, upcoming cases involve elections, free speech, and executive authority, amid criticism over the court’s reputation.

State attorneys general urged federal support for challenging a 2008 ruling barring the death penalty for child rape when the victim survives. Former Michigan athletes plan to appeal the dismissal of their name, image, and likeness lawsuit. Venezuelans asked the court to preserve their protected status, while the Trump administration sought review of birthright citizenship.

The justices met to consider petitions before the 2025–26 term. The passage also recounts Chief Justice Warren Burger’s extensive communications with President Nixon, despite Burger later writing the unanimous decision requiring Nixon to release his tapes.

A town-commissioned study says relocating Vegreville’s 236-job federal immigration processing centre to Edmonton could reduce the town’s population by 420, eliminate 130 local students, lower home prices by 30 per cent and increase unemployment. The mayor and workers’ union oppose the planned 2018 move.

Karnataka’s education department plans to cancel government school summer camps because of funding shortages and teachers’ involvement in SSLC evaluation and election work. Launched in 2017-18, the free programme taught Mathematics, Science, language skills and extracurricular activities while providing meals. Last year, camps served classes 5 and 6 students at 7,049 schools, mainly in drought-hit taluks.
Brendon Naidoo, accused of defrauding people through a foreign-exchange trading scheme, was granted R50,000 bail. He must report to Sandton Police Station twice weekly and return to court on May 5.

American football offenses aim to advance the ball into the end zone or field-goal range, with each position performing specialized duties. The quarterback leads the offense, distributes the ball, reads defenses, and may change plays through audibles. Running backs primarily carry the ball but may also catch passes and block. Tight ends combine receiving and blocking responsibilities; attached tight ends often provide a vertical passing threat, while “sniffers” or H-backs frequently move before the snap and block like fullbacks.

The five-player offensive line consists of two tackles, two guards, and a center. Linemen block defenders to protect the quarterback or create running lanes. Tackles play outside, with the left tackle commonly protecting a right-handed quarterback’s blind side. Guards line up beside the center, participate in double-team blocks, and may pull across the formation. The center snaps the ball, directs blocking awareness, and alerts teammates to defensive threats.

Wide receivers run routes, catch passes, create separation, and may block. X receivers are generally larger, physical players aligned on the line of scrimmage. Z receivers usually align behind the line and often emphasize speed. Slot receivers line up inside, seeking openings underneath and across the middle against safeties or linebackers.

Cornell researcher Adam Anderson and co-author Daniel H. Lee found that people can identify six basic emotions from the eyes alone. Participants evaluated eye expressions paired with mental-state words across 600 trials. Narrowed eyes, which improve visual discrimination, were linked to states such as disgust, suspicion and disapproval, while open eyes, which increase visual sensitivity, were associated with fear, awe and curiosity. Eye openness was the feature most closely tied to interpreting mental states, while surrounding features indicated whether emotions were positive or negative. Comparisons showed that eyes conveyed emotions more robustly than the nose or mouth. The findings support Darwin’s theory that facial expressions originated as adaptive sensory responses before evolving into social communication.

The paper studies learning minimal Linear Temporal Logic on finite traces (LTLf) formulas that separate positive from negative traces. LTLf learning supports applications in software specification mining, control and robotics, and artificial intelligence, but is computationally difficult and existing tools struggle with formulas larger than about 15 nodes.

The proposed framework combines bounded enumeration of LTLf formulas with Boolean Set Cover. It first uses the VFB algorithm, which performs bottom-up combinatorial search, evaluates formulas efficiently through characteristic bit tables, and removes observationally equivalent formulas. After reaching a fixed size threshold, it treats generated LTLf formulas as weighted atoms and searches for larger separating formulas using only conjunctions and disjunctions. This reduces evaluations from characteristic tables to vectors, lowering time and memory requirements.

Boolean Set Cover seeks a minimum-weight positive Boolean formula whose interpretation contains every positive element and no negative element. The problem is NP-complete, though the existence of any solution can be checked polynomially. The framework further prunes formulas using domination, which permits replacing a formula with another of no greater weight that correctly classifies a superset of elements. Because exhaustive domination testing is quadratic, an approximate heuristic examines only promising candidates.

The Boolean Set Cover solver uses beam search, retaining a fixed number of high-scoring formulas at each weight. A divide-and-conquer procedure recursively splits positive or negative examples when the solver fails, ensuring a valid solution whenever one exists, though not necessarily a minimal one.

The authors implement the framework in the CPU-based tool Bolt and consolidate more than 15,000 benchmark tasks across ten families. Experiments report that Bolt solves 14,374 of 15,595 tasks, compared with Scarlet’s 11,468, while producing smaller formulas and lower average runtime. A GPU algorithm solves more tasks on the subset it supports, while Bolt remains competitive in runtime and formula size. Ablation experiments show that Boolean Set Cover enables solving more difficult tasks with little loss in formula size. The framework may also apply to specification languages involving conjunctions and disjunctions, including regular expressions, Boolean circuits, and bit-vector programs.

John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics for experiments demonstrating macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in superconducting electric circuits.

Job interviews range from banal to elaborate. Self-described “disruptors” favor eccentric activities, riddles and unconventional questions over traditional ones; candidates are advised to respond assertively when invited to ask questions.

End a job interview promptly and confidently with a handshake and brief farewell. Avoid lingering, self-promotion, appearing desperate, or asking when a decision will be made. Strong candidates focus on the opportunity, ask necessary questions, and convey confidence.

Construction began on Fort Buford near the Missouri and Yellowstone rivers in 1866. Soldiers faced poor food, scurvy, disrupted steamboat supplies, boredom, alcohol problems, and mental illness. A report criticized the cooking but praised the post library’s 1,100 books and periodical subscriptions. Sitting Bull surrendered to military officials there in 1881, the fort’s final year as a military post. A museum opened in the former headquarters in 1963, and additional parts of the post were later restored.

This non-peer-reviewed study assessed antimicrobial-resistant Enterobacteriaceae in untreated wastewater from metropolitan and non-metropolitan areas of Western Uttar Pradesh, India, during 2020–2021. Fifteen wastewater samples yielded 150 isolates: 93 E. coli, 36 K. pneumoniae, 12 other Enterobacteriaceae, and nine unidentified mixed isolates. Susceptibility to 19 antibiotics across eight classes was evaluated using disc diffusion, VITEK2, and confirmatory tests for extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL), carbapenem, and colistin resistance.

Of the isolates, 111 (74%) resisted at least one antibiotic, while 88 of these resistant isolates (79.3%) produced ESBL. Multidrug resistance was observed particularly in E. coli and K. pneumoniae, with K. pneumoniae showing significantly higher prevalence across zones. Carbapenem resistance among Enterobacteriales was 36.05%, and colistin resistance occurred in K. pneumoniae and other Enterobacteriaceae, but not E. coli. Zone 1 had the highest overall multidrug resistance, though total zonal differences were not statistically significant.

The authors associate the wastewater resistance burden with extensive antibiotic use and inadequate wastewater treatment during the COVID-19 pandemic. They recommend periodic surveillance of Indian wastewater and receiving waters, molecular characterization of resistance genes, improved wastewater infrastructure, and policies addressing antimicrobial resistance in both metropolitan and non-metropolitan areas.

The Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed Anthony Davis’s and Eric Simmons’s convictions for Class A felony conspiracy to deal more than three grams of cocaine and Davis’s forty-year sentence. Evidence showed they participated in transporting, preparing, and selling cocaine from a Marion apartment. Although each of two controlled purchases involved less than three grams, their combined weight exceeded three grams, the transactions occurred close together, and the broader conduct supported an agreement to deal that amount. Simmons’s acquittal on a separate dealing charge was not irreconcilable with his conspiracy conviction because the State alleged and proved other overt acts. Davis had only one charge at trial, so inconsistent verdicts were impossible. Any improper sentencing aggravators were harmless because Davis’s extensive criminal history, including recent drug convictions, independently supported the enhanced sentence.

Deutsche Telekom, Nokia and the Hamburg Port Authority will test 5G applications across Hamburg’s 8,000-hectare port. Using an antenna on the Hamburg television tower, trials will cover traffic-light management, real-time environmental sensor data and virtual reality infrastructure monitoring. Multiple network slices will be tested under live industrial conditions to assess adaptation to differing application requirements.

Flippy, a $60,000 burger-flipping robot developed by Miso Robotics, has begun working at a Caliburger restaurant in Pasadena. It can grill 150 burgers per hour but still requires humans to place patties, add cheese and toppings, and wrap orders. Equipped with sensors, cameras, interchangeable tools and artificial intelligence, Flippy can improve its technique and may eventually cook other foods. Miso and Caliburger describe it as a tool to assist, rather than replace, kitchen workers. Caliburger has six months of exclusive use and plans possible U.S. expansion after testing, while a McKinsey report identifies fast food as highly vulnerable to automation.

Engineer John Essey uses connected devices and sensors to automate and monitor his home. Carnegie Mellon researcher Gierad Laput’s team developed a single wall-mounted sensor that detects environmental signals such as vibrations, sounds and light, allowing a computer to identify activities and appliance use. The technology could support domestic and commercial monitoring while avoiding the expense and incompatibility of smart appliances or the clutter of multiple sensors. Security expert Bruce Schneier warns that Internet-of-things companies may collect data to drive sales and that device makers do not sufficiently prioritize security. He argues that increasingly capable connected systems could make harmful actions more precise and damaging.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 26, 2021 reported quarterly net sales of $81.4 billion, up 36% year over year, and net income of $21.7 billion, compared with $11.3 billion. Diluted earnings per share rose to $1.30 from $0.65. Growth occurred across all product, service and geographic categories; iPhone sales increased 50% to $39.6 billion, while Services rose 33% to $17.5 billion.

For the first nine months, net sales totaled $282.5 billion and net income was $74.1 billion. Operating cash flow reached $83.8 billion. At quarter-end, Apple had $329.8 billion in assets, $265.6 billion in liabilities and $64.3 billion in shareholders’ equity. It repurchased $65.5 billion of stock during the nine-month period, including $22.5 billion in the third quarter.

Apple introduced new iMac, iPad Pro, Apple TV 4K, AirTag and Apple Podcasts Subscriptions offerings. The filing also discusses COVID-19 uncertainty, supply concentration, derivatives, debt, taxes and pending legal matters.

Vermont prosecutors dismissed attempted murder and aggravated assault charges against 18-year-old Jack Sawyer, accused of planning a mass shooting at Fair Haven Union High School. The state Supreme Court ruled that preparation alone did not establish an attempted crime, making the charges untenable. Sawyer, who pleaded not guilty, still faces criminal threatening and dangerous-weapon charges. Prosecutors allege he documented plans, bought a shotgun and ammunition, and discussed the plot online, but he had not visited the school or town. His bail is $100,000 with strict release conditions. The case prompted Vermont to enact significant gun restrictions, though they cannot apply retroactively to Sawyer.

The speaker credits playoff success to focusing on one game at a time, especially with only two wins needed. He praises a teammate’s disciplined play, effort, and leadership. He says poor ice and glass conditions discourage him from leaving the net to play the puck. He values sharing the Stanley Cup with loved ones and charitable causes, recalling a rewarding visit to a children’s cancer hospital. He also emphasizes closely guarding a talented opponent. Compared with an earlier playoff run centered on defense, the current team has greater offensive skill, though timely saves remain essential. Despite being well positioned to advance, he expects the next game against an experienced, resilient opponent to be the playoffs’ toughest challenge yet.

U.S. stocks rose sharply on October 22, 2001, supported by better-than-expected corporate earnings despite anthrax concerns and weakening economic indicators. The Dow gained 1.9% and the Nasdaq 2.2%.

Enron shares fell about 21% to $20.65 after the SEC requested information on related-party transactions involving partnerships run by CFO Andrew Fastow and other executives. Enron pledged cooperation, stating that its board, auditors and attorneys had reviewed and approved the arrangements. Investors remained concerned about conflicts of interest, reduced shareholder equity, potential dilution, affiliated-company liabilities and Enron’s recent $618 million quarterly loss following $1.01 billion in charges.

Shareholders filed derivative and class-action lawsuits alleging that Enron’s board breached fiduciary duties and that company officials concealed material information. The partnerships allegedly cost Enron more than $35 million, while unwinding arrangements involving 55 million shares reduced shareholder equity by $1.2 billion. One analyst estimated dismantling additional affiliated companies could cost up to $3 billion.

Separately, UniPrime Capital signed a letter of intent for a partial interest in an Enron Wind Development ground lease covering more than 3,000 acres in California’s Tehachapi Valley.

The passage provides hardware design, reset, clocking, interrupt, peripheral, and timing guidance for TI TMS320DM814x devices.

- PLL and analog supplies require nearby filtering, preferably ferrite beads and capacitors forming Pi filters. Use small 0.1-µF decoupling capacitors, no larger than 0402, plus periodic bulk capacitors, while avoiding excessive capacitance that disrupts power sequencing.
- Reset sources include power-on, external and emulation warm, watchdog, software global cold and warm, test, and local resets. POR resets the entire chip; warm resets preserve selected logic. Reset isolation is supported for PCIe and the EMAC switch. Most I/O pins enter Hi-Z during reset, and the ARM Cortex-A8 subsequently executes Boot ROM code.
- Device clocks derive from DEV, AUX, SERDES, audio, and 32.768-kHz sources. DEV and AUX clocks may use crystals or 1.8-V LVCMOS inputs. DEV is normally 20 MHz; AUX supports 20–30 MHz. PCIe requires a low-jitter differential SERDES clock. All PLLs start in bypass mode and must remain within specified frequency limits.
- Interrupt handling includes an ARM AINTC supporting up to 128 requests and a C674x controller combining up to 128 events into 12 prioritized CPU interrupts.
- Timing specifications exclude PCB routing delays; TI recommends accounting for routing and using IBIS models. Clock and control transitions must be monotonic.
- Peripheral sections describe DCAN, EDMA, advanced event triggering, trace, JTAG, GPIO, GPMC/ELM, HDMI, HDVPSS, video DACs, Ethernet, MDIO, and I2C. EDMA supports 64 channels and 512 parameter entries. GPIO provides up to 128 configurable pins. GPMC interfaces with NOR, NAND, SRAM, and related devices.
- The three-port gigabit Ethernet switch supports MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII, with 10/100/1000-Mbps operation and shared MDIO control. Its I/O requires 3.3-V PHY interfaces.
- HDMI supports HDMI 1.3a and DVI 1.0, multichannel audio, and video up to specified 1080p formats. TMDS routing requires controlled impedance, matched differential routing, paired vias, and low-capacitance ESD protection.
- HDVPSS provides video capture, processing, composition, scaling, format conversion, HDMI, digital video outputs, and analog video. Video DAC traces must be short, isolated, impedance-controlled, and carefully matched.
- Four I2C modules support 10–400 Kbps operation, 7- and 10-bit addressing, multimaster modes, noise filtering, and 32-byte FIFOs.

Since 2000, only 12 albums have spent at least 10 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard 200. Taylor Swift and Morgan Wallen each have three albums on the list, while Adele has two. Adele’s “21” led for 24 weeks. Wallen’s “One Thing at a Time” became the chart’s longest-leading country album, and Swift’s “The Tortured Poets Department” totaled 17 weeks at No. 1.

Clio acquired legal research platform vLex for $1 billion, expanding its legal practice and law firm management capabilities. The company, valued at $3 billion last year, has also acquired ShareDo and Lawyaw. CEO Jack Newton discusses Clio’s future, AI and the Oct. 16–17 Clio Cloud Conference in Boston.

The passage describes reset, clocking, interrupt, peripheral, and timing features of the TMS320DM814x device. PCIe and EMAC switch reset isolation allow selected subsystems to avoid or independently undergo reset, with software procedures required for PCIe idling, local reset, hot reset, and bus re-enumeration. Power domains have dedicated warm and cold resets. Most I/O pins enter Hi-Z during reset, subject to exceptions for emulation, isolated EMAC, RSTOUT_WD_OUT, and DDR pins.

Device clocks derive from DEV and optional AUX inputs using crystals or 1.8-V LVCMOS sources. The PCIe PHY requires a low-jitter differential clock. The device includes selectable clock outputs and multiple PLLs, which start in bypass mode and must remain within specified frequency and power limits. Interrupt facilities include the ARM AINTC, supporting up to 128 programmable requests, and the C674x controller, combining up to 128 events into 12 prioritized CPU interrupts.

Peripheral descriptions cover DCAN, EDMA, advanced event triggering, trace, JTAG, Ethernet, MDIO, GPIO, GPMC/ELM, HDMI, HDVPSS, video DACs, I2C, imaging, and DDR2/DDR3. The three-port gigabit Ethernet switch supports MII, GMII, RMII, and RGMII, while MDIO manages multiple PHYs. GPMC interfaces with NOR, NAND, SRAM, pseudo-SRAM, and custom logic; ELM locates BCH-based NAND errors. HDMI supports HDMI 1.3a, DVI, multichannel audio, and specified TMDS PCB routing. The imaging subsystem supports parallel and serial camera inputs, image processing, and sensor control. Two DDR interfaces support 16- or 32-bit paths, multiple memory capacities, two chip selects, and DDR2/DDR3 PHYs.

The passage also provides register listings, electrical and timing requirements, PCB-routing guidance, reset timing, clock-transition criteria, and interface-specific timing for these subsystems. Board delays must be considered, with IBIS analysis recommended where applicable.

Dolphins receiver Tyreek Hill suffered a dislocated left knee after being tackled by Jets cornerback Malachi Moore in Week 4. He was carted off, hospitalized overnight and scheduled for further imaging and evaluation. Coach Mike McDaniel confirmed the injury is season-ending, and Hill is not expected to return in 2025. The full recovery timeline depends on the extent of ligament or tendon damage and whether surgery is required.

The Secretary preferred keeping INF and START negotiations in Geneva but was open to discussing them with Dobrynin. Dobrynin proposed reviewing bilateral agreements by status and exploring cooperation on security and regional issues. Both sides supported continued nonproliferation talks and possible confidence-building measures, while differing on the value of further Middle East discussions. The Secretary insisted that Poland, Kampuchea, Afghanistan, Central America, and human rights, including Soviet Jewry, remain on the agenda. Dobrynin argued that human rights cases were easier to resolve amid improved relations and criticized the Jackson Amendment’s effect on Soviet emigration. They agreed to prepare lists of bilateral agreements for a future meeting.

In a memorandum to President Reagan, Clark said prospects for constructive change in US-Soviet relations were uncertain because of new Soviet leadership and limited US efforts to test them. He argued that Reagan’s first two years had restored US defenses, allied confidence, economic strength, and international credibility after perceived decline. Clark judged that this strengthened position might encourage the Soviets to negotiate limits on the US military buildup. Based on Soviet history and recent military setbacks, he concluded that the Soviets would not risk military conflict with the United States.

The Green Bay Packers agreed to a deal with veteran tackle Byron Bell, who has played for Carolina, Tennessee and Dallas. Bell adds competition at right tackle as Bryan Bulaga recovers from a torn ACL. Jason Spriggs and Kyle Murphy are also returning from injuries, making Bell a potential starter for the season opener.

UFC 216 in Las Vegas features Tony Ferguson against Kevin Lee for the interim lightweight title, with the winner potentially facing Conor McGregor to unify the division. Flyweight champion Demetrious Johnson will pursue a record 11th consecutive title defence against Ray Borg. The event follows a mass shooting that killed 58 and injured nearly 500; UFC pledged $1 million to victims and their families.

The study examines how science education contributes to citizenship education in Turkey through analysis of the national science curriculum and semi-structured interviews with eight experienced science teachers. Citizenship education is presented as preparation for informed, responsible, and active democratic participation, while science education supports this goal through scientific literacy, socio-scientific issues, environmental awareness, values, and critical-thinking skills.

Turkey’s 2018 science curriculum emphasizes scientific, technological, and environmental literacy, sustainable development, social responsibility, and skills such as inquiry, observation, problem-solving, and evidence-based reasoning. However, it does not explicitly connect these elements to citizenship education. Teachers most strongly associated citizenship with scientific literacy, society, and the environment. They viewed scientific knowledge and inquiry as essential for understanding daily life, health, safety, climate change, pollution, pandemics, and other socio-scientific issues. They also identified values such as responsibility, respect, compassion, patriotism, and scientific integrity as relevant to citizenship.

Teachers reported that science education’s citizenship potential is limited in practice by overcrowded classrooms, inadequate laboratories and materials, curriculum shortcomings, students’ preparedness, communication difficulties, and an exam-oriented system that prioritizes test performance over experiments, discussion, and real-life problem-solving.

The study concludes that science education can strengthen citizenship knowledge, skills, attitudes, and values, but its role should be defined more explicitly. It recommends greater emphasis on scientific literacy, critical thinking, inquiry, debate, democratic participation, socio-scientific topics, environmental education, sustainability, hands-on learning, and teacher training, particularly in support of the Sustainable Development Goals.

Medina City School District’s May 8 ballot includes a permanent 5.2-mill levy replacing an expiring 5.9-mill operating levy. Supporters say homeowners would pay the same amount, with a separate bond expiration slightly reducing tax bills. The levy would maintain programs, restore high school French and fund free districtwide all-day kindergarten. Kids First Medina organized a rally attended by school and city officials, educators, students and parents.

After many years, the speaker is excited and nervous to reach this point. Championship feelings remain unchanged since childhood, while the team maintains its normal routine, stays even-keeled, and avoids mental exhaustion from overthinking.

Out-of-bounds situations require preparation for baseline, sideline, and full-court inbounding. The primary objective is to inbound successfully, then get the ball to the best players for a high-percentage shot. Plays should be simple, practiced, and executed with vision, communication, timing, precise cuts, screens, and passes. Players should anticipate defensive tactics, use safety outlets, and exploit automatic reads such as basket cuts, give-and-go actions, and lob passes.

Teams should scout opponents’ defensive approaches and ensure players understand throw-in rules. The designated inbounder has five seconds to release the ball and cannot touch it again before another player does. Except after a made basket, the inbounder must remain near the designated spot. After a made basket, the inbounder may run the baseline, including after certain defensive infractions or an immediate timeout. Passes into the backcourt are permitted without an over-and-back violation. The ball cannot be thrown over the backboard or directly into the basket. A defender touching the ball across the out-of-bounds vertical plane while it is held by the inbounder commits a technical foul. Coaches should test players’ rule knowledge rather than assume understanding.

APU’s Feb. 10 GIG formal dance at La Cañada Flintridge Country Club featured a “La La Land” theme, semi-formal attire and two distinct dance floors: one with a DJ playing current hits and another with a live jazz combo. Organized by the Office of Communiversity, the $20 event welcomed singles, couples and groups while emphasizing safety and organization. Additional attractions included free digital cartoons, professional photography, a grand piano, outdoor seating and views of Los Angeles. Students praised the venue, varied music, activities and dual ambiances, describing the evening as classy, memorable and among APU’s best dances.

Neutrino oscillations are studied using neutrinos from the Sun, atmosphere, accelerators, nuclear reactors, supernovae, and potentially Big Bang relics. Experiments vary source-to-detector distance, neutrino energy, flavor sensitivity, and accessible mass range.

Early solar-neutrino experiments, including Homestake, detected fewer electron neutrinos than theoretically expected. The SNO experiment measured the total neutrino population through neutral scattering and found agreement with predictions, showing that neutrinos changed flavor rather than disappeared. Atmospheric neutrinos, produced mainly through pion, kaon, and muon decays, also showed a deficit of muon neutrinos dependent on energy and direction.

Accelerator experiments use a nearby detector to measure the initial neutrino flux and a distant detector to observe flavor appearance or disappearance. Results such as those from T2K provide clear evidence of oscillation. Reactor experiments study electron-antineutrino disappearance, typically through inverse beta decay, and can directly observe survival probability as a function of distance divided by energy. Many major advances across these experimental approaches occurred during and after the 2000s.

AI literacy and educational robotics can support personalized learning, feedback, digital competence, algorithmic thinking, inclusion, and social, cognitive, linguistic, psychomotor, and technological development. This study examined how future preschool and primary school teachers perceive robots and their educational roles.

Using a mixed-method Draw-And-Answer Test, researchers analyzed drawings and open-ended responses from 143 final-year University of Belgrade students in 2024. After excluding 22 responses containing misconceptions, the final sample comprised 75 future preschool teachers and 46 future primary school teachers. Two evaluators achieved a Pearson correlation of 0.99 in coding the responses.

Among the 121 accurate representations, 98 participants had encountered robots in person, 21 through media, and two had no prior experience. The 22 misconceptions mainly represented robots as ordinary electrical appliances, with smaller numbers depicting stick figures, virtual-reality equipment, or avatars.

Animal-shaped robots were the most common accurate depiction, especially Bee-Bot, followed by typical robots and mechanical objects; humanoid robots were rare. Most robots were shown without emotion, while positive expressions appeared primarily on animal-shaped robots. Educational functions were most frequently identified, followed by assistive functions. Future preschool teachers emphasized educational uses, while primary school teacher students gave similar importance to educational and assistive roles.

Most respondents first encountered robots at the Faculty of Education. Their reasons for selecting particular robots were chiefly cognitive, including practicality and ease of educational use, followed by affective interest and behavioral experience. Future preschool teachers showed more consistent conceptions than future primary school teachers.

The study recommends more frequent, purposeful integration of educational robots and continued curriculum development for future teachers. Effective use depends on teacher competence, robot quality, appropriate teaching strategies, accessibility, physical safety, and privacy protection. Robot use alone does not guarantee educational innovation.

Education 4.0, shaped by artificial intelligence, machine learning and other digital technologies, requires education to shift from rote learning toward personalized, competency-based learning and skill-based assessment. India’s National Education Policy 2020 supports games and gamification as innovative approaches to teaching, learning and assessment.

Digital game-based learning can develop cognitive and non-cognitive skills, provide immersive and multimodal experiences, encourage problem-solving and decision-making, and improve motivation and academic achievement. Educational digital games may include role-playing, puzzles, simulations, quizzes and multiplayer games. Customized games aligned with learning outcomes can also serve as behavioral and learner-centered assessment tools.

Stealth assessment measures competencies during gameplay without interrupting learning. It uses digital traces generated by learners and AI-based machine-learning algorithms to evaluate skills such as problem-solving, creativity, attention, persistence and critical thinking. It can provide immediate feedback, adapt challenges to learner competency, reduce test anxiety and assess both procedural and declarative knowledge.

Effective stealth assessment depends on evidence-centered design, machine-learning algorithms, formative assessment and feedback. Evidence-centered design identifies competencies, relevant gameplay indicators and tasks that produce reliable evidence. Digital-game assessment may either embed assessment activities within games or analyze game logs afterward. Developing these systems requires collaboration across education, psychology, technology, programming and related disciplines.

Challenges include limited teacher adoption, difficulty developing customized games, possible cognitive overload, inappropriate difficulty levels, and concerns about games’ neurological effects. The validity, reliability and educational effectiveness of digital game-based learning and assessment remain insufficiently established and require extensive technological and educational research.

An Ernakulam court convicted migrant labourer Muhammed Ameerul Islam of raping and murdering a 30-year-old Dalit law student at Perumbavoor on April 28, 2016. He was found guilty of murder, rape and causing death during rape, but acquitted of evidence-destruction and SC/ST Act charges. Sentencing was scheduled for the following day. Islam was arrested in Tamil Nadu 50 days after the crime following an extensive investigation involving over 100 police personnel.

Amazon entered a three-year, unsecured $3 billion revolving credit agreement on May 20, 2016, replacing its 2014 facility. The initial rate is LIBOR plus 0.60%, with a 0.05% fee on undrawn funds; no borrowings were outstanding. At its May 17 annual meeting, shareholders elected all director nominees, ratified Ernst & Young LLP as auditor, and rejected proposals on sustainability reporting, human rights, and political contributions.

A penalty kick during play is a restart; once the kicker touches the ball and it clearly moves forward, the ball is live and players may pursue saves, blocks, or rebounds. Before the kick, all players except the kicker and goalkeeper must remain at least 10 yards from and behind the penalty mark, within the field, and outside the penalty area. Attacking players should position promptly without displacing opponents and must not enter the penalty area or arc before the ball is kicked.

All attacking players should follow up the kick. The kicker may play the ball again only after another player touches it, such as the goalkeeper, but not after a rebound directly from the goal frame. Teammates should pursue rebounds without hesitation and avoid overrunning the ball. If the goalkeeper secures possession, attackers must immediately defend against a counterattack. Attacking-team procedural violations result in a retake if a goal is scored or generally an indirect free kick if it is not.

Governments are increasingly regulating artificial intelligence, but AI policy remains largely absent from computer science curricula. The paper argues that developers need policy literacy to translate abstract and sometimes conflicting requirements into technical practices.

The United States lacks comprehensive federal AI legislation and has relied mainly on non-binding frameworks and executive orders. Federal policy shifted from President Biden’s emphasis on safe, secure, trustworthy AI to President Trump’s focus on global AI dominance, economic competitiveness, and national security. By contrast, the EU AI Act establishes a broad, risk-based regulatory system, prohibiting certain practices and imposing additional oversight, transparency, copyright, and training-data requirements on high-risk and general-purpose AI.

The authors identify three major policy implications: rapid regulatory change, difficulty translating non-technical goals into technical controls, and cross-border effects such as EU rules influencing global corporate practices. Developers must understand technical limitations, adapt to changing requirements, and communicate realistic expectations to policymakers.

To integrate AI policy into computing education, the paper proposes a framework with three perspectives—socio-political, translational, and technical—and three dimensions: scope, power, and agency. Guiding questions examine policy requirements, affected jurisdictions and groups, creators and beneficiaries, implementation responsibilities, technical safeguards, practitioner influence, and conflicts between policy expectations and technical limitations. The framework is designed to support adaptable classroom discussions and assignments. Future work could develop targeted curricular activities and apply requirements-engineering methods to translating policy principles into technical specifications.
Nigerians abroad sent $21.9 billion home in 2017, up 12% from $19.64 billion in 2016, according to the World Bank. The total was Sub-Saharan Africa’s highest.

An Italian man, Luca Traini, 28, allegedly drove through Macerata shooting African migrants, injuring six, one seriously, in what police called a racially motivated attack. He also fired at Democratic Party offices without causing injuries and was arrested wearing an Italian flag after reportedly making a fascist salute. Traini had unsuccessfully run for the anti-immigration Northern League in local elections. The attack followed the discovery of 18-year-old Pamela Mastropietro’s dismembered body and the arrest of Nigerian asylum seeker Innocent Oseghale. Northern League leader Matteo Salvini condemned the shooting but blamed mass immigration for tensions, while Democratic Party leader Matteo Renzi and Prime Minister Paolo Gentiloni urged calm and rejected hatred and violence. Leftist politician Laura Boldrini accused Salvini of inciting hatred and whitewashing fascism.

Weak US employment data and major downward revisions increased expectations of dovish Federal Reserve policy. USD/JPY fell 2.25%; support lies near 147.13 and 146.45, while recovery above 147.80 could restore upside momentum. Markets expect the Bank of England to cut rates by 25 basis points to 4.0% despite inflation near twice its target and unemployment at 4.7%. GBP/USD remains pressured, with resistance at 1.3360 and support at 1.3135. Bitcoin declined alongside equities and found support near 112,000; a break above 117,260 could signal renewed gains, while falling below 110,750 may expose the 105,770–107,500 zone. The passage also promotes Investing.com stock-screening tools and warns that financial and cryptocurrency trading carries substantial risk, website data may be inaccurate or delayed, and advertisers may compensate the site.

Rutgers historian Mark Bray plans to relocate temporarily to Spain with his family after receiving death threats and having his home address posted online. Bray, author of a 2017 book about antifa, faced renewed attacks from far-right influencers and a student petition following President Donald Trump’s executive order seeking to designate antifa as a domestic terrorist organization.

Bray said threats intensified after posts by influencers including Jack Posobiec, Milo Yiannopoulos, and Andy Ngo, as well as a Change.org petition promoted by a Rutgers chapter of Turning Point USA and covered by Fox News. Messages included a threat to kill him in front of students and another listing his address. The petition’s organizer later said she opposed threats, doxxing, and harassment.

Bray and his family were initially unable to leave when their United Airlines reservation disappeared after airport check-in and security clearance. They were rebooked for another flight. DHS said it was not tracking any related action by TSA or Customs and Border Protection, while United did not comment.

Rutgers said it was gathering information, and Bray reported the threats to university and local police. He expects to remain in Spain through the academic year and teach remotely. Bray said he publicized the situation to defend academic freedom and dissent.

On April 7, 2015, NVIDIA’s Compensation Committee adopted its Fiscal Year 2016 Variable Compensation Plan. Eligible executive officers may earn cash bonuses based on achievement of specified fiscal 2016 revenue targets, subject to threshold and maximum levels and generally continued employment through payment. Target awards were: CEO Jen-Hsun Huang, $1 million (100% of base salary); CFO Colette Kress, $275,000 (35%); Ajay Puri, $475,000 (54%); David Shannon, $200,000 (25%); and Debora Shoquist, $150,000 (21%). A multiscale framework was developed to connect atomic interactions at GaN–liquid Ga interfaces with facet-dependent epitaxial growth rates. Molecular dynamics simulations showed that liquid Ga forms ordered interfacial layers whose structure and charge depend on GaN polarity. Charge redistribution is largely confined to the first two layers, while density oscillations extend farther into the liquid.

Metadynamics calculations found that these ordered Ga layers govern nitrogen adsorption and migration. Liquid Ga lowers N-adatom migration barriers relative to a clean GaN surface, producing a “Ga lubrication” mechanism. Migration barriers were approximately 0.56 eV at Ga-polar interfaces and 0.34 eV at N-polar interfaces, compared with about 1.1 eV on a clean Ga-polar surface. Step edges introduced additional Ehrlich–Schwoebel barriers above 0.6 eV that can hinder adatom descent.

Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations predicted rough, island-like growth at high nitrogen flux and diffusion-controlled, layer-by-layer growth at lower flux. Estimated experimental MBE fluxes are substantially below the simulated low-flux case, indicating that practical self-catalyzed GaN growth should occur through diffusion-limited step flow.

A parameter-free transport model combined interfacial free-energy profiles, simulated nitrogen diffusivity, and nitrogen solubility in liquid Ga to predict facet-normal growth rates. The predicted rates ranged from 0.01 to 0.04 nm/s and reproduced experimental facet trends. MBE experiments on partially nitridated Ga/GaN particles, analyzed by electron microscopy, showed multiple wurtzite and zinc-blende orientations and morphology changes from rounded droplets to faceted particles. Wurtzite m-planes grew faster than basal planes, while zinc-blende Ga-polar (111) was predicted to grow faster than N-polar (111), with (001) intermediate.

The results indicate that GaN growth is limited by nitrogen transfer and controlled primarily by the interfacial free-energy landscape because nitrogen has very low solubility in liquid Ga. The workflow is intended to be transferable to other low-solubility crystal-growth systems. Limitations include omission of impurities, possible machine-learning potential inaccuracies, simplifying assumptions in the one-dimensional steady-state model, neglected interfacial and droplet effects, and experimental averaging across multiple facets.

In soccer, the second defender supports the first defender by positioning goalside, behind, and toward the field’s center, at enough distance to react if the first defender is beaten. This positioning encourages the attacker toward the sideline. The support defender uses a proper defensive stance, avoids overrunning play, adjusts with movement, and communicates because the first defender is focused on the ball. Calls such as “support” confirm cover; “jockey,” “delay,” or “contain” instruct the first defender to control the attacker while teammates recover; and “tackle” authorizes a challenge. Training should progress from stationary positioning to movement, half-speed communication, and full-speed practice. If the first defender is beaten, the support defender generally takes over, possibly through a defensive switch.

The ADS868xW family integrates a 16-bit SAR ADC, programmable-gain analog front end, ADC driver, second-order antialiasing filter, and buffered voltage reference. The PGA supports programmable bipolar and unipolar input ranges through RANGE_SEL_REG; its default range is ±3 × VREF. The low-pass filter has a typical 500-kHz cutoff and consistent performance across ranges.

The device supports an internal factory-trimmed 4.096-V reference or an external 4.096-V reference, selected by INTREF_DIS. Internal-reference operation requires at least 4.7 µF between REFIO and REFGND, while REFCAP requires at least 10 µF plus a nearby 1-µF capacitor. Reference outputs must not directly drive external loads. Soldering and repeated reflow can shift the internal reference, so placing the device in the second reflow pass minimizes thermal stress. The reference and buffer operate from –40°C to +125°C; typical buffer drift is 0.5 ppm/°C and maximum drift is 2 ppm/°C.

Single-ended and differential inputs support bipolar and unipolar ranges, with straight-binary output. LSB size equals full-scale range divided by 2^16. Input alarms use programmable high and low thresholds with common hysteresis, while AVDD alarms use fixed typical thresholds of 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Active flags update each conversion and clear after conversion unless the condition persists; tripped flags clear after ALARM_REG is read. Alarm status can be provided through the multifunction pin, registers, or appended output flags.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI, dual-SDO, source-synchronous operation, and multi-device daisy chains. Devices appear to the host as 32-bit input-output shift registers. Daisy chains share CONVST/CS and SCLK, require identical configuration, and optimally use 32 × N clocks for N devices, with throughput decreasing as device count increases.

The device operates in RESET, acquisition, and conversion states. The active-low RST pin can issue an application reset or power-on reset. Conversions begin on a CONVST/CS rising edge and use an internal clock. Data frames begin when CONVST/CS falls and end when it rises. A 32-clock frame accepts a valid command; shorter frames invalidate writes but can read selected output bits, while longer frames use the last 32 input bits.

Nine configuration registers control identification, reset and power, input and output protocols, output formatting, range and reference selection, and alarm thresholds and status. Output words can contain conversion or register data, fixed patterns, device address, range, alarm flags, and parity. Four standard SPI modes are supported; dual-SDO operation halves the clock cycles required to transfer a given number of bits. Source-synchronous modes output a data-aligned clock on RVS.

The device offers NAP and deep power-down modes. NAP is entered after conversion while CONVST/CS remains high; power-down disables analog blocks while retaining registers and an active interface. AVDD and DVDD are separate supplies and require local decoupling. PCB guidance includes separating analog and digital routing, using short low-impedance grounding, and placing supply and reference capacitors close to device pins.

An example industrial module combines the ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 differential multiplexer to measure standard voltage and current inputs, including ranges up to ±10 V and 0–20 mA. The integrated PGA, driver, reference, alarms, protection, and enhanced SPI simplify industrial data-acquisition designs.

At Mobile World Congress, the EU-funded Graphene Flagship showcased technologies intended to address 5G development challenges through strong industry-academic collaboration. RWTH Aachen University and AMO GmbH demonstrated flexible, printed graphene microwave transmitters and receivers for Wi-Fi, millimeter-wave systems, and base-station backhaul. Chalmers University and APR Technologies developed a miniature graphene-based cryogenic cooling pump with no moving parts. Using alternating hot and cold graphene patches to compress gas, it could cool satellite systems and 5G base-station receivers to improve signal clarity.

This study compared air- and bone-conduction auditory brainstem response (ABR) and auditory steady-state response (ASSR) thresholds in infants aged 0–6 months with normal hearing or ABR-confirmed conductive hearing loss. Fifty of 64 recruited infants completed testing. Thresholds at 500 and 2000 Hz were measured, with tympanometry and otoacoustic emissions used as cross-checks. Conductive loss occurred only at 500 Hz.

At 500 Hz, air-conduction ABR and ASSR thresholds and air-bone gaps were significantly higher in infants with conductive hearing loss, while bone-conduction thresholds did not differ between groups. Mean air-bone gaps for normal-hearing and conductive-loss groups were 15 and 36 dB for ABR and 12 and 21 dB for ASSR, respectively. ABR and ASSR thresholds and air-bone gaps were poorly correlated, and ASSR showed greater variability and more overlap between groups. Minimum normal ASSR intensities were 40 dB HL for 500-Hz air conduction, 30 dB HL for 500-Hz bone conduction, and 40 dB HL for both modes at 2000 Hz.

Under the study parameters, ABR identified mild low-frequency conductive hearing loss more reliably than ASSR. ASSR criteria achieving high sensitivity had poor specificity. The findings support continued use of ABR as the diagnostic standard in early hearing detection programs. Further ASSR research is needed across larger samples, multiple frequencies, and varying degrees of conductive hearing loss.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture introduces hybrid rendering that combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI, and simulation. Dedicated RT Cores accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, while denoising reduces required rays. This enables real-time ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, with Turing delivering over 10 Giga Rays per second and roughly ten times Pascal’s software ray-tracing performance.

Turing Tensor Cores support NVIDIA NGX, a deep-learning graphics stack unavailable on earlier architectures. Its features include DLSS, which uses trained neural networks to produce image quality comparable to temporal anti-aliasing with less shading work; AI-based inpainting; interpolated slow-motion video; and image or video super-resolution.

Other architectural features include Mesh Shading, which replaces CPU-intensive per-object draw calls with cooperative Task and Mesh Shaders; Variable Rate Shading, which adjusts shading rates by region for content-adaptive, motion-adaptive, and foveated rendering; and Texture Space Shading, which decouples visibility and appearance sampling so shading results can be reused spatially and temporally. Multi-View Rendering processes geometry once for multiple viewpoints, improving stereo VR, wide-field headsets, shadows, and instancing. Turing also supports expanded DX12 resource binding, VirtualLink over USB-C, and RT Core-accelerated VR audio.

The TU104 GPU contains up to 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, and 48 RT Cores, and is used in products including the GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. TU106 contains 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, and powers the GeForce RTX 2070 without NVLink or SLI. Tesla T4 uses a reduced TU104 configuration optimized for inference.

NVIDIA defines RTX-OPS as a workload-based hybrid-rendering metric combining weighted Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 throughput. Ray tracing itself casts rays through image pixels, using BVH structures to reduce intersection tests. Hybrid rendering, denoising, BVH acceleration, and RT Cores collectively make real-time ray tracing practical on Turing GPUs.

The study examines global, African regional, and Ethiopian legal frameworks supporting inclusive education and assesses awareness among educational leaders in Addis Ababa resource centers. Inclusive education seeks equitable participation and meaningful learning for all students, including those with disabilities, and depends on leaders understanding relevant policies.

Using a qualitative case-study design, researchers purposively selected 15 Ministry of Education experts, principals, itinerant teachers, and general teachers from three resource centers. Data from semi-structured interviews and document reviews were analyzed thematically, with participant consent, pseudonyms, and transcript validation used for ethical protection.

Reviewed global frameworks included the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Convention on the Rights of the Child, Salamanca Statement, Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, Marrakesh Treaty, and Sustainable Development Goals. African frameworks included the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights, African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child, and African Disability Protocol. Ethiopian frameworks included the Constitution, Proclamation No. 1263/2021, Education and Training Policy 2023, Education Sector Development Plan VI, Special Needs/Inclusive Education Strategy, and National Children’s Policy.

The legal environment generally supports inclusive education, but awareness differs substantially. Ministry experts and itinerant teachers demonstrated relatively strong knowledge, attributed to specialized education and training. School principals had limited familiarity with specific global, regional, and national frameworks, often citing insufficient training and competing administrative responsibilities. General teachers supported inclusion through compassion and classroom adjustments but generally lacked knowledge of its legal and policy foundations. Participants also noted Ethiopia’s absence of a dedicated stand-alone inclusive education policy.

The study concludes that policy awareness is essential for effective leadership and implementation. It recommends regular policy-focused professional development, integration of inclusive education frameworks into teacher and leadership curricula, alignment of local practices with international and regional standards, and Ministry monitoring of practitioners’ policy awareness.

Yoga can improve breathing, concentration, flexibility, balance, strength, injury prevention, recovery and mental calmness. Choosing a suitable practice depends on individual goals, needs and training schedules. Hatha is an umbrella term for posture-based yoga, while common styles include rigorous, fixed-sequence Ashtanga; variable, breath-linked Vinyasa; alignment-focused and prop-supported Iyengar; heated Bikram and hot yoga; long-held Yin poses; slower Restorative yoga; and gentle, meditative Kripalu.

Specialized classes for runners, cyclists and other athletes address activity-specific stresses, muscle imbalances and injury risks. Athletes who train intensely may benefit from gentler therapeutic styles, while others should choose practices that complement their activities. Yoga styles differ substantially and offer distinct benefits.

The Executive submits an agent’s report on Texas but has taken no steps toward recognizing its independence. Although Congress previously favored recognition once Texas demonstrated a functioning independent government, recognition is a delicate act that may provoke war, particularly when the former sovereign still claims control. The United States has traditionally avoided interference and recognized new governments only after their independence was firmly established.

Texas has expelled Mexican authority, defeated its army, and organized a government, but Mexico is preparing another invasion. Recognition should therefore await evidence that Texas can permanently maintain its sovereignty. Additional caution is required because many Texans are connected to the United States, Texas has adopted a similar government, and it intends to seek admission to the Union after recognition. Premature action could appear designed to facilitate American acquisition of disputed territory.

The President recommends maintaining the current position until Mexico or a major foreign power recognizes Texas, or events conclusively establish its independence. Because recognition could lead to war, he considers consultation with Congress prudent and promises to cooperate with whatever measures Congress adopts after careful deliberation.

Classical Maxwell solvers model complex nanostructures but cannot capture quantum effects such as photon correlations and entanglement. Exact quantum methods are difficult to integrate with Maxwell solvers and become computationally prohibitive for large systems, while semiclassical approaches may inadequately represent nonclassical statistics. Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) offer a means to model fluctuations, correlations, and noise beyond average dynamics.

The authors introduce an SDE-based stochastic Bloch-vector approach that avoids wave-function unraveling, phase-space representations, and operator-valued noise. It connects quantum-emitter dynamics to spatiotemporally resolved classical electromagnetic fields and is intended for integration with finite-difference time-domain Maxwell solvers. The approach is validated using the Mollow spectrum of a strongly driven two-level system, whose triplet structure and sideband correlations provide benchmarks for open quantum-system modeling and applications in photon and entangled-state generation.

Conventionally, master equations yield Fokker–Planck equations with symmetric, positive-semidefinite diffusion matrices factorized to define SDE noise. The proposed method extends this framework to complex, non-symmetric diffusion matrices, interpreted as cross-covariances between coupled stochastic processes. This extension aims to include asymmetric noise correlations arising from noncommuting quantum operators.
