Saudi Arabia approved the University of New Haven’s plan to open a Riyadh branch campus next fall, potentially making it the first foreign university to do so. The university hopes to enroll 13,000 undergraduate and graduate students within a decade, exceeding its U.S. enrollment. The coeducational, English-language campus would include colleges focused on business and digital innovation, engineering and advanced manufacturing, and arts and applied sciences, along with preparatory, ESL, executive education and micro-credential programs.

University leaders said the campus would support Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 economic diversification goals and meet demand for skilled workers. New Haven has worked with Saudi partners since the late 1990s, including educating members of the royal family and helping modernize King Fahd Security College. That partnership drew criticism after Saudi agents killed journalist Jamal Khashoggi in 2018, but the university continued it.

The university still needs approval from its accreditor, the New England Commission of Higher Education.

NASA Glenn’s Glenn Extreme Environments Rig recreates Venus’s extreme heat, pressure, and carbon dioxide atmosphere to study materials and technology. An 80-day experiment significantly altered rock and mineral samples, while a durable computer chip operated for 21 days, demonstrating that electronics could support longer Venus missions. Venus has lead-melting temperatures, pressures 100 times Earth’s, and acidic clouds; earlier Soviet probes survived only minutes to hours. Scientists believe Venus underwent a runaway greenhouse effect that boiled away its oceans. Although its surface is uninhabitable, its upper atmosphere has Earth-like temperatures and pressures, potentially allowing floating vessels or cities, despite concentrated sulfuric acid clouds. Researchers say exploring Venus could clarify planetary climate development and possibly reveal microbial life in its upper atmosphere.

The President transmits departmental reports responding to the Senate’s resolution. Upon taking office, he retained California’s existing military commandant as acting civil governor pending congressional action, without granting new authority or compensation. He sent officials to California and New Mexico to gather information and implement the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo.

He encouraged both territories to draft constitutions and seek statehood but instructed federal officers not to influence elections, conventions, or domestic institutions. He lacks information about California laws or territorial censuses. Early statehood, he argues, would reduce national conflict over involuntary servitude by allowing each state to determine its domestic policies.

California has prepared a constitution, partly through efforts begun under the previous administration, and he recommends admission if it meets constitutional requirements. Congress must resolve New Mexico’s disputed boundary with Texas; establishing a territorial government beforehand could improperly favor one claim. He considers immediate territorial government unnecessary because existing Mexican municipal laws and federal military protection remain effective.

He opposes imposing conditions on California’s domestic institutions, asserting that states retain self-government and may amend their constitutions after admission. He expects New Mexico eventually to seek statehood and urges Congress to avoid unnecessary controversy, geographical divisions, and threats to national unity.

The document standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for interoperability between SEV-ES or SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors. These technologies encrypt guest register state, while GHCB provides a decrypted 4 KB page through which guests selectively expose state needed to process Non-Automatic Exits via VMGEXIT.

Version 2 adds SEV-SNP support and a 52-bit hypervisor feature bitmap. Subsequent revisions add 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, enhanced error reporting, APIC ID retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, SEV-ES page-state changes, confidential-computing EFI communication, SEV-TIO, Secure AVIC, and GHCB unregistration. The GHCB MSR protocol supports version negotiation, pre-GHCB CPUID requests, feature discovery, page-state changes, VMPL switching, GPA registration, and termination.

SEV-SNP guests must register a shared GHCB GPA before first use and may request a preferred address or unregister it. VMGEXIT processing requires valid-field bitmaps, protected GHCB access, and defined error handling. Supported operations include I/O, MSR and hypercall handling, MMIO, private/shared page transitions, SNP firmware requests, certificates, AP creation, restricted-injection doorbells, IPIs, timers, APIC ID lists, TIO requests, Secure AVIC backing pages, and termination.

SMP booting cannot rely on hypervisor modification of measured registers. SEV-ES uses initial register state, AP reset hold, and AP jump tables; SEV-SNP can use guest-supplied VMSA pages through AP Creation, enabling vCPU hotplug. NMI handling uses an explicit “NMI Complete” VMGEXIT. Hardware debug registers may be virtualized when supported; otherwise DR7 accesses are intercepted and cached. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

Restricted Injection limits host notification to a shared #HV doorbell page containing pending interrupt or non-maskable-event information and EOI assistance. The guest configures this page through GHCB requests, accesses it unencrypted, and follows special HLT behavior with interrupts disabled. The host must emulate APIC interrupt priority, acknowledgment, in-service, and EOI semantics while controlling #HV signaling through the doorbell state.

Maya Kodes, an interactive real-time holographic pop star created by Montreal’s Neweb Labs, has released a dance-pop single, recorded an EP, performed 30 concerts and gained 5,500 Facebook followers. A 360-degree livestream EP launch is scheduled for June 13, with touring and simultaneous performances planned.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K reporting that it issued a January 26, 2017 press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2016. The press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under the Exchange Act.

Mac Otakara claims Apple’s tenth-anniversary iPhone may feature a polished stainless-steel frame between glass panels, an under-display Touch ID sensor, and vertically arranged dual cameras for virtual or augmented reality. The report, allegedly based on testing documents, remains unconfirmed.

A small study found that women preferred the body odor of men who ate more fruits and vegetables, while high-carbohydrate diets produced less appealing odors. Researchers assessed participants’ diets through skin carotenoid measurements and questionnaires, then asked women to rate sweat collected from exercise-worn T-shirts. Meat consumption did not affect attractiveness but made odor more intense. Earlier research also linked non-meat diets with preferred male odor. Diet affects body odor indirectly: sweat itself is odorless until skin bacteria metabolize its compounds. The study did not examine odor preferences among same-sex couples.

U.S. Treasury prices fell and yields rose after September data showed 2.9% wage growth despite a hurricane-related loss of 33,000 jobs. Unemployment fell to a 16-year low of 4.2%. Traders viewed wage gains as inflationary, increasing expectations for a December Federal Reserve rate rise to 88%. Yields later pared gains amid concerns over Catalonia and upcoming Treasury auctions. Some analysts warned that hurricane disruptions may have distorted wage data by disproportionately affecting lower-paid hourly workers.

A UCLA study estimates that meat-based food and waste from America’s 163 million dogs and cats generate carbon emissions equivalent to 64 million tons of carbon dioxide annually, or 13.6 million cars. Pets account for an estimated 25–30% of the environmental impact of U.S. meat consumption. The researcher urged owners to consider this impact but did not recommend vegetarian diets. A livestock-emissions expert noted that pet food largely uses animal byproducts that might otherwise be discarded. While some studies and owners report dogs can thrive without meat, veterinarians warn that plant-based diets—especially for cats—may lack essential nutrients such as taurine. A 2015 study found many vegetarian pet foods failed labeling standards, with some deficient in critical amino acids.

Mike Modano’s ligament injury could not worsen, so playing depended on whether he could shoot, pass, take faceoffs, and fully handle his normal responsibilities. Although his offense could be replaced temporarily, his defense, penalty killing, leadership, and situational play would be greatly missed. A supportive wrist-and-finger brace allowed him to play effectively, with some faceoff difficulty.

Ed Belfour overcame defensive attitudes and trust issues stemming partly from a serious back injury. After extensive rehabilitation and daily maintenance, his physical condition and relationships with coaches and teammates improved.

Buffalo’s Satan and Sanderson created pressure, while Curtis Brown was considered a key performer. The team maintained that Dominik Hasek should not be hit while controlling the puck, but could not obstruct opponents pursuing a loose puck or use his stick outside the crease without challenge.

Hull was listed day to day with a groin injury, with Sydor and other reserves considered as replacements. Strong penalty killing restored confidence, while passionate defense, shot blocking, hard work, and two upcoming rest days helped secure the performance. Some penalties resulted from excessive emotion. Veteran players were praised for their pride, competitiveness, and willingness to accept major roles regardless of age.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter-point to 1–1.25 percent, its fourth increase in 18 months, and projected another hike this year. Credit card rates, home equity lines and some adjustable-rate mortgages typically rise alongside the Fed rate, increasing borrowing costs. Consumers with poor credit may also pay more, particularly for used-car financing.

Fixed mortgage and auto loan rates have changed little because long-term mortgages generally track 10-year Treasury yields rather than the Fed’s rate. Savings rates have risen only slightly on average, though some smaller banks and high-yield CDs offer better returns.

Higher U.S. rates can attract overseas investment, strengthen the dollar, make U.S. exports more expensive and draw capital from developing countries. Retirees holding bonds are advised to maintain balanced fixed-income portfolios rather than react to individual rate increases.

The white paper examines how IT-based simulation, modeling, data analysis, and high-performance computing (HPC) support manufacturing innovation. It draws on a December 2021 survey of 200 decision makers from manufacturing enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Manufacturers use these technologies to accelerate product development, reduce costs, improve decisions, enhance quality, and prevent defects. Deployment across product development, production planning, and quality management is expected to reach as high as 90% within two years, while 64% plan related investments. Integrated data sources and a shared information base are considered necessary to overcome silos and support collaboration.

Technologies including virtual prototyping, digital twins, IoT data, high-performance data analytics, visualization, AR/VR, and machine learning enable new products, services, and business models. However, increasingly complex calculations strain conventional infrastructure: 42% of respondents use outdated or inaccurate simulations, and half report excessive calculation times.

Four out of five respondents view HPC as a game changer because it enables complex calculations, faster and more numerous iterations, improved results, new applications, and greater innovation and agility. More than a quarter already use professional HPC infrastructure, while 39% are planning or piloting it.

Most HPC users favor external infrastructure: 87% use or plan cloud or other external services, 74% use or plan colocation, and 43% use or plan research partners. Only 6% currently operate on-premises HPC. Major challenges include security concerns, cited by 72%, as well as investment, licensing and operating costs, energy consumption, sustainability, and the need for regular infrastructure modernization.

This study evaluates machine-learning potentials for material surfaces using models trained from scratch (TS), zero-shot pretrained Universal Interatomic Potentials (ZS), conventional fine-tuning (FT), and multi-head fine-tuning (MHFT). The MACE-MP-0a-small model was selected as the foundation model after benchmarking several pretrained potentials on diatomic energy curves.

Tests covered unary Au, binary RuO₂, and ternary BiVO₄ surface datasets. Across all systems and training-set sizes, FT consistently produced lower energy and force errors than TS and required substantially less data to reach comparable accuracy. For Au, fine-tuning with 40 configurations reduced ZS errors from 14.8 to 4.3 meV/atom for energies and from 74.7 to 37.4 meV/Å for forces. TS models trained on 2,000 Au configurations performed similarly to or worse than FT models using 40–200 configurations. Diatomic tests showed that TS models frequently generated unphysical short- or long-range interactions, while FT generally preserved more realistic potential shapes.

For RuO₂, FT again outperformed TS, although force errors were larger than for Au. For BiVO₄, FT achieved the lowest force RMSE, 0.17 eV/Å, compared with 0.24 for TS and 0.42 for ZS, while reducing high-error outliers. The foundation model’s prior exposure to high-force bulk configurations helped FT remain reliable in unstable atomic environments absent from the surface training data.

Conventional FT caused catastrophic forgetting: a model fine-tuned on Au performed worse than ZS on Ag, Cu, Pt, and Ir surfaces and substantially degraded bulk-data accuracy. MHFT, which trained simultaneously on Au surface and sampled bulk data, improved generalization. Surface-energy RMSE across the four metals was 27 meV/Å² for ZS, 88 for FT, and 16 for MHFT. MHFT preserved bulk capabilities better than FT but required roughly 100 times more training time and slightly reduced Au-specific accuracy.

The results support FT for data-scarce, specialized surface predictions and MHFT when retaining bulk performance and broader transferability is important. MHFT additionally requires alignment of computational conditions and energy references between datasets.

The NHL expansion draft will let the Vegas Golden Knights select one unprotected player from each existing team. Teams may protect either 11 position-specific players or eight skaters and a goalie, subject to eligibility rules. Readers can propose Calgary Flames protections and predict Vegas’s selection.

The study examines whether earnings press-release text predicts announcement-day stock returns. It analyzes 134,354 releases from 2006–2023 using rolling, look-ahead-free models based on LDA, BERT, MPNET, and FinBERT, while controlling for earnings surprises.

Textual “soft” information and earnings surprises provide similar explanatory power. FinBERT performs best, raising regression \(R^2\) from 3.3% with earnings surprises alone to 4.4%; its text signal accounts for 52% of normalized SHAP importance. Online LDA offers greater topic interpretability, highlighting financial performance and sector-specific news. Topic analysis suggests managers discuss internal financial factors more positively when results are favorable and external sector factors more negatively when results disappoint.

Soft information does not explain returns before publication, indicating little average evidence of leakage. Because most releases occur outside trading hours, their information is incorporated by market open. Long-short strategies initiated after opening generate no sustained profits and primarily incur transaction costs, supporting market efficiency.

If press releases and earnings surprises are available before release, combining them substantially improves identification of extreme performers. Precision for selecting the top ten best- or worst-performing stocks rises from 0.25–0.36 using either signal separately to 0.44–0.52 when the signals agree, emphasizing the cybersecurity importance of unreleased earnings information.

The article examines trauma-informed human rights education (TIHRE) in higher education through an interdisciplinary literature review. Traditional human rights education often emphasizes legal norms while avoiding politically sensitive or emotionally challenging histories, despite the prevalence of lived and intergenerational trauma among students. TIHRE seeks to reduce retraumatisation and secondary or vicarious trauma while promoting dignity, inclusion, wellbeing, agency and advocacy.

Drawing on SAMHSA’s principles of safety, trustworthiness, transparency, peer support, collaboration, empowerment, choice, and recognition of cultural, historical and gender issues, the article makes three main recommendations. First, educators should clarify their values, biases, motivations and lived experiences to develop an authentic, respectful and self-aware teaching persona. Building rapport, learning students’ names and creating mutually respectful relationships support trust and resilience.

Second, trauma-informed principles should shape curriculum and lesson design. Human rights education should integrate learning about, through and for human rights; use co-creation, project-based learning, skills development and reflective practice; and provide meaningful opportunities for advocacy and action. Educators should avoid graphic or exploitative content, warn students about potentially distressing material, offer wellbeing check-ins, maintain flexibility and avoid romanticising trauma or resilience.

Third, TIHRE should use dialogic teaching that treats learners as equals, develops critical thinking and communication skills, and creates safe opportunities to discuss difficult issues. Engagement with survivors, practitioners and peers can connect academic knowledge with lived experience and foster community, healing and hope. Overall, TIHRE aims to move learners and educators from avoidance and apathy toward informed human rights advocacy while placing dignity, agency and wellbeing at the centre of learning.

Notre Dame received two gifts totaling $205 million. Matthew and Joyce Walsh donated $150 million to the School of Architecture, which will be renamed for them. Francis and Kathleen Rooney provided another gift to endow an institute promoting scholarship and dialogue on American democracy.

North Park Elementary reopened a week after Cedric Anderson killed his estranged wife, teacher Karen Smith, and 8-year-old Jonathan Martinez before killing himself. Another student was wounded. Families and community members welcomed returning students, while officials increased security, provided counselors and emphasized healing and commitment to students.

The compilation highlights Enron’s involvement in several October 2000 stories. Three inexperienced entrepreneurs won Strategic Petroleum Reserve oil contracts but needed substantial financial guarantees. Enron discussed backing Renard Euell’s three-million-barrel award, including a required $93 million letter of credit, but no agreement was completed before the deadline. Euell and Lance Stroud forfeited their awards, while Ronald Peek transferred his interest to Hess Energy Trading.

Enron Broadband Services also participated in a $26 million financing round for digital asset management company Artesia Technologies.

Houston coverage examined a proposed publicly financed downtown basketball arena. Supporters, including Enron Chairman Kenneth Lay, argued it would promote development and strengthen Houston’s economy. Critics questioned taxpayer subsidies and projected benefits. Separate articles endorsed the proposal and compared its public costs with arena deals in other cities, noting that Houston’s planned subsidy exceeded those in several larger or comparable markets.

Apple’s February 13, 2018 annual shareholder meeting elected eight directors and approved Ernst & Young as auditor, executive compensation, and the amended Non-Employee Director Stock Plan. Shareholder proposals on proxy access amendments and a human rights committee were rejected. The Form 8-K was signed February 14, 2018, by General Counsel Katherine Adams.

The passage argues that Apple should let users teach Siri new words, pronunciations, nicknames, meanings, and alternative commands. Such features could personalize interactions and, through aggregated machine learning, expand Siri’s vocabulary and capabilities. Siri currently supports limited nickname functions through contacts but often misinterprets natural requests. The proposed learning system could enable customized actions and more complex searches, such as finding photos containing a particular person photobombing the user.

Backtests from January 2015 to September 2021 examined RSI in cryptocurrency trading. RSI measures the speed and magnitude of price movements on a 0–100 scale. Mean-reversion strategies—buying at low RSI readings and selling at high readings—produced weak results with few trades for Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Dogecoin. In contrast, momentum strategies performed better, particularly with short RSI periods. A Bitcoin strategy using five-day RSI crossings above and below 50 achieved a reported 122% CAGR versus 101% for buy-and-hold, with 39% drawdown versus 83%. The passage concludes that RSI appears useful for crypto as a momentum indicator, but not as a mean-reversion indicator.

Arkansas sought U.S. Supreme Court approval to execute Don Davis after state stays. A federal appeals court reinstated eight planned executions, ruling that midazolam did not create undue severe pain.

Twenty-seven days into Kilauea’s eruption, fast-moving lava from Fissure 8 threatened homes in Leilani Estates, Lanipuna Gardens and Kapoho, advancing at about 600 yards per hour. Lava fountains exceeded 200 feet, while volcanic glass fibers known as “Pele’s hair,” sulfur dioxide emissions and vog created additional hazards. About 22 fissures have opened since May 3, destroying at least 40 homes, covering more than 2,000 acres and forcing about 200 people into shelters. Volcanic haze traveled roughly 4,000 miles to Guam, reducing visibility and posing risks to people with respiratory conditions despite lacking toxic chemicals. Officials expected the haze to dissipate temporarily but return while the eruption continued. The USGS also warned against roasting marshmallows over volcanic vents because emitted gases could contaminate them.

Amsterdam’s Buiksloterham district is pursuing experimental, inclusive docklands regeneration based on sustainability and circular-economy principles. Its central project, De Ceuvel, is a temporary co-working and cultural hub built from renovated houseboats on a polluted former shipyard. Phytoremedial plants will clean the soil over ten years, preparing the site for future use at lower cost than mechanical removal.

De Ceuvel reduces waste through wormeries, composting toilets, fertiliser extraction, gardens, aquaponics and renewable energy. Solar-powered offices trade surplus-energy rewards through the local cryptocurrency Jouliettes, which may become a wider currency. Other initiatives include biogas production, a floating B&B and self-built eco-homes. The project emerged after the financial crisis halted conventional luxury development, offering an alternative intended to restore the land without pricing out local people or destroying the community.

Peel Regional Police believe three men filmed assaulting a 29-year-old autistic man at Square One’s bus station in Mississauga on March 13 are originally from British Columbia’s Lower Mainland and recently travelled to the Greater Toronto Area. A tip came from Western Canada, prompting police to seek wider circulation of the surveillance video around Vancouver, Surrey, Abbotsford and Richmond. The video has received more than 300,000 views. All three suspects are described as South Asian men, about 5-foot-10, wearing black clothing. The victim remains shaken, and police continue supporting him and his family. Anyone with information is asked to contact Peel police, local police or Crime Stoppers.

SpinGPT is an LLM-based agent designed for three-player Spin & Go poker tournaments, where incomplete information, changing player counts, stack sizes, and non-linear chip values complicate traditional poker strategies. It uses Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and a two-stage pipeline: supervised fine-tuning on 320,000 professional decisions from 8,800 high-stakes games, followed by offline reinforcement learning with ORPO using 270,000 solver-generated hands mixed with 50,000 human hands.

SpinGPT-SFT achieved 80% exact accuracy and 86% macro F1 on professional data. After reinforcement learning, SpinGPT recorded 79% exact accuracy on professional data with improved bet-sizing error, and 72% exact and 78% tolerant accuracy on solver data. In gameplay, a heuristically patched SpinGPT-SFT achieved 13.4 ± 12.9 BB/100 against Slumbot over 30,000 hands. SpinGPT then beat SpinGPT-SFT by 13.2 ± 7.24 BB/100 over 10,000 duplicate hands, indicating substantial improvement from reinforcement learning.

Limitations include mismatched benchmark formats, costly evaluations, deep-stack errors, and occasional numerical mistakes typical of language models. Proposed improvements include stronger foundation models, higher-quality data, retrieval of GTO charts, deeper reasoning methods, opponent adaptation, explainability, and tighter integration with poker solvers.

A global learning crisis, worsened by school closures, climate change, conflict and economic slowdown, costs an estimated US$129 billion annually. Youth unemployment approaches 30 percent in lower-income countries, while 20 percent of youth globally were not in employment, education or training in 2023, two-thirds of them young women. Employers report major skills shortages, and educational mismatch affects two-thirds of young adult workers in lower-income countries.

GPE supports inclusive education systems that combine foundational literacy, numeracy and socio-emotional learning with creativity, critical thinking, collaboration, adaptability and practical workplace skills. It uses policy advocacy, financing, knowledge investments and public-private partnerships to align curricula with labor-market needs. Initiatives include education financing in Lesotho, foundational learning investment in Ghana, a competency-based curriculum in Kenya, and socio-emotional and creativity training in El Salvador. In 2024, 20 active GPE grants focused on employment-related skills.

The passage identifies habits said to undermine weight loss: drinking from plastic bottles, eliminating sweets or carbohydrates entirely, avoiding healthy fats, emotional eating, consuming store-bought protein bars, energy drinks, meal replacements, or liquid calories, and eating sweets outside pre-workout periods. It recommends fruit, whole grains, nuts, coconut water, real food, and balanced proportions of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins. Other advice includes practicing self-forgiveness, avoiding discouraging social influences, measuring success by adherence to routines rather than scale readings, sleeping at least seven hours, avoiding excessive calorie restriction, gradually changing the diet, varying exercise weekly, and choosing a weight-loss routine suited to one’s body type, metabolism, and health status.

The MACD histogram shows the difference between the MACD and signal lines. Bars above zero indicate bullish momentum, bars below zero indicate bearish momentum, and their height reflects momentum strength. A crossover strategy buys when the histogram moves above zero and sells when it moves below. The described mean-reversion strategy enters at the close and exits when the close first exceeds the previous day’s close, with reversed rules for shorts. Across 77 liquid ETFs, it generated 6,669 trades, with long positions outperforming shorts. A backtest on the 2x leveraged Nasdaq-100 ETF QLD produced 85 trades, a 2.2% average gain, 10.4% annual returns, 5% market exposure, and a 19% maximum drawdown.

Feature phones remain popular as secondary devices and as alternatives for reducing smartphone use. Options include the Rs 799 Intex Yaari for basic calls; sub-Rs 1,000 dual-SIM Micromax X408; Rs 1,200 Samsung Guru E1200 with flashlight; and durable Rs 1,310 Nokia 105. The Rs 2,536 Nokia 216 adds a camera, MP3 player, internet access, torchlight, and long battery life. Samsung Metro 350 offers a 2MP camera and 1200 mAh battery for Rs 2,780. Premium choices include the stylish Nokia 230 at Rs 4,799 and the forthcoming Nokia 3310, expected around Rs 4,000.

Onesmo Rupil began using drugs at 17 and was dismissed from the University of Dodoma in 2013 for poor performance linked to substance abuse. His heroin addiction led him to steal students’ laptops to finance the habit, resulting in arrests and imprisonment. He began recovering while detained in Dodoma and later attended rehabilitation centres in Dar es Salaam. Now recovered, he manages Philimisana Foundation Sober House in Mwanza, which accommodates about 30 young people.

Rupil attributes his addiction partly to limited parental care and a lack of personal principles, rather than peer pressure alone. He says marijuana is the most commonly used drug locally, while heroin and cocaine are less affordable. Psychiatrist Kassian Nyandindi says marijuana’s THC can damage brain connections and contribute to mental disorders. Research cited in the passage estimated that 550,000 people had been affected by drug abuse, with about 25,000 addicts nationwide and only 3,500 receiving treatment at four methadone hospitals in Dar es Salaam. HIV prevalence among drug users was reported at 20–50 percent.

The team expected a difficult Stanley Cup Finals after a tough Colorado series but rejects fatigue as an excuse. New Jersey is balanced, defensively strong, quick in transition and has a line with strong chemistry that must be contained through effective matchups chosen by the coaching staff. The team expects a tight, low-scoring series requiring battles for every inch. It must spread out scoring, get more pucks to the net and create opportunities. Despite New Jersey’s confidence after beating Philadelphia, the players remain confident, recognize the urgency of the next game and expect to respond with a desperate effort.
