NASA’s Suomi NPP satellite captured an infrared image of aurora borealis across northern Canada on Dec. 22. Auroras form when charged solar-wind particles interact with Earth’s magnetic field and atmospheric gases, producing colored light. Major displays follow an approximately 11-year solar cycle.

The SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 defines SD Memory Card architecture, interfaces, protocols, commands, registers, electrical characteristics, performance classes, and operating procedures. It covers SD, SPI, UHS-I, UHS-II, low-voltage interfaces, command queues, cache, self-maintenance, application performance, security, write protection, and mechanical form factors.

SD cards may be read/write or ROM and provide user and protected areas. Capacity classes are SDSC up to 2 GB, SDHC above 2 GB through 32 GB, and SDXC above 32 GB through 2 TB. Speed classes specify minimum performance from Class 2 through Class 10. Bus modes range from Default Speed at 12.5 MB/s to UHS-I SDR104 at 104 MB/s and UHS-II FD624 at 624 MB/s.

Communication is host-controlled through broadcast or addressed commands, responses, and block-oriented data transfers protected by CRC. Cards operate in identification and data-transfer modes. Initialization uses commands including CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3 to reset cards, validate voltage, determine capacity, obtain identification, and establish relative addresses. UHS-I uses a 1.8 V signaling switch and may require tuning through CMD19; UHS-II has separate detection, initialization, enumeration, configuration, and SD-command transport stages.

The specification also describes read and write operations, erase, locking, card states, error handling, timing, power-up, registers, extension functions, and SDIO compatibility. SDIO cards retain mechanical, electrical, signaling, power, and software compatibility with SD Memory Cards while adding I/O capabilities.

Nintendo announced Mario Kart Tour, a smartphone app scheduled for release between April 2018 and March 2019. No gameplay details were provided. It follows Nintendo mobile titles including Super Mario Run, Animal Crossing: Pocket Camp and Fire Emblem Heroes.

Malaria control in Africa is threatened by emerging Plasmodium falciparum resistance to artemisinin-based combination therapies. This study assessed artemisinin and partner-drug resistance markers in a low-transmission area of Choma District, southern Zambia, using samples collected through health-center and community surveillance from 2018–2023.

Of 570 samples tested with a 24-locus deep-sequencing panel, 540 were successfully sequenced at one or more loci. The WHO candidate artemisinin-resistance marker Pfk13 P441L occurred in 6% of 501 successfully assessed samples. Its annual prevalence rose from 0% in 2018 to 7.2% in 2023, peaking at 9.3% in 2022, and it was detected at all four health centers. Both the six-year and 2023 prevalences exceeded the WHO’s 5% threshold for concern. Pfk13 A578S, which is not associated with artemisinin resistance, was detected in three samples in 2023.

Pfmdr1 Y184F prevalence was 41% without temporal change, while wildtype Pfmdr1 N86, associated with possible reduced lumefantrine susceptibility, occurred in all samples. P441L and Y184F co-occurred in two samples, and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance markers were highly prevalent.

The emergence of P441L in Zambia adds to detections across several African countries, but its origin and resistance implications remain unclear. Study limitations included missing loci, incomplete Pfk13 coverage, and variable sample sizes. The authors call for therapeutic efficacy and ex-vivo studies, whole-genome sequencing, and routine national and multinational molecular surveillance.
The team aims to rebound on the road, regain home-ice advantage, and execute its counteracting style after failing to match the opponent’s expected intensity.

This study examined factors attracting and retaining special education teachers in rural remote Midwestern districts. Of 155 surveys, 93 complete responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlations, t-tests, and thematic analysis. Participants identified four primary factors: financial incentives, administrative, collegial, and community support; job-related conditions; and rural recruitment initiatives.

Support was the most frequently cited retention factor, while financial incentives were the leading attraction factor. Teachers emphasized competitive salaries, health insurance, tuition assistance, loan forgiveness, housing, and bonuses. They also recommended reducing paperwork and caseloads, providing relevant professional development and resources, improving work-life balance, developing Grow Your Own programs, and holding career fairs led by rural educators. Greater perceived support and job satisfaction were significantly associated with plans to remain, while experienced teachers reported less support.

The authors conclude that combined, intentional strategies are needed rather than isolated incentives. Limitations include self-reported data, a small and minimally diverse geographic sample, and primarily descriptive analysis. Future research should examine practical methods for strengthening support, satisfaction, professional development, work-life balance, and continuing financial incentives.

Tyreek Hill underwent successful surgery to repair a dislocated left knee and multiple torn ligaments, including his ACL. Agent Drew Rosenhaus said Hill will not need another operation and aims to return for the start of the 2026 season. Hill sustained the season-ending injury during Miami’s 27-21 victory Monday. BAE Systems agreed to sell Qatar 24 Typhoon fighter jets with training and support for £5 billion, part of a £6 billion defense deal also including MBDA missiles and British-made Raytheon guided bombs. Qatar becomes the ninth country to buy the aircraft.

The MSPM0G3519/G3518/G1519/G1518 devices include analog, communications, timing, security, debugging, and low-power peripherals.

- The temperature sensor produces a voltage linear with device temperature and connects internally to an ADC channel. Factory memory contains a device-specific calibration value measured in 12-bit mode using the 1.4-V internal reference.
- VREF provides selectable 1.4-V and 2.5-V internal references and supports an external reference. A decoupling capacitor is required on the VREF pins.
- Comparator outputs support timer blanking, low-power wakeup, and advanced-timer fault handling. DAC_OUT shares PA15 with comparator inputs, so external circuitry on PA15 should be avoided when DAC_OUT is used.
- The buffered DAC supports 8- or 12-bit output, self-calibration, binary and two’s-complement formats, programmable sampling, FIFO, DMA, and hardware triggering.
- Security functions include AES-128/256 acceleration, firewalls, storage for four AES keys, and CRC-16/CRC-32. The TRNG generates a new 32-bit value every 128 TRNG clock cycles. AESADV supports multiple encryption modes, 128- and 256-bit keys, and operation in RUN and SLEEP. The keystore securely supplies stored keys to the AES engine.
- MATHACL provides hardware-accelerated 32-bit mathematical functions.
- UART peripherals support asynchronous communication, configurable parity and baud-rate oversampling, LIN, separate transmit/receive FIFOs, DMA, and loopback. I2C supports 7- and 10-bit addressing, controller and target modes, rates through 1 Mbit/s on supported IOs, SMBus 3.0, DMA, filtering, low-power wakeup, and eight-entry FIFOs.
- SPI supports controller and peripheral operation, rates up to 32 Mbit/s, programmable 4- to 16-bit controller frames and 7- to 16-bit peripheral frames, PACKEN, DMA-capable FIFOs, and TI, Motorola, and Microwire formats. Rates above 16 Mbit/s require HSIO pins.
- CAN-FD supports CAN 2.0A, CAN 2.0B, and ISO 11898-1:2015 CAN-FD through 5 Mbit/s, with configurable FIFOs and dedicated transmit and receive buffers.
- LFSS_B uses a typical 32-kHz clock and contains RTC_B and an independent watchdog. RTC_B provides calendar functions, alarms, periodic interrupts, leap-year correction, and crystal calibration and temperature compensation up to ±240 ppm. IWDT_B provides eight periods from 2 ms to 2 hours and generates a POR reset if not serviced. WWDT supports eight periods, reset or interrupt generation, sleep-mode stopping, and interval-timer operation.
- General-purpose and advanced timers support programmable counting, prescaling, synchronization, cross-triggering, interrupts, DMA, and peripheral triggers. Advanced timers additionally provide complementary PWM, dead-band insertion, repeat counting, fault handling, and internal capture/compare channels.
- IOMUX selects digital IO functions and controls drivers, inputs, and SHUTDOWN wakeup. SWD provides a two-wire ARM-compatible debug interface.
- The boot strap loader programs and configures the device over UART or I2C. It is protected by a user-defined 256-bit password, can be disabled, and can be invoked through pins, blank reset-vector detection, or software.

A proper one-on-one defensive stance helps a soccer defender react quickly, control an attacker’s direction, avoid being beaten, and prepare to tackle. The defender generally places one foot forward and one back, stays balanced on the balls of slightly bent legs, and keeps bent arms somewhat outward. On the field’s right side, the left foot typically leads; on the left side, the right foot leads, encouraging attackers toward the sideline. Central defenders choose based on play. Training should cover stance and movement at right, center, and left positions, progressing from slow movements without a ball to faster ball work. Defenders should monitor their position relative to the goal and avoid using their arms to block opponents.

Fisher sought an accounting from Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Beane for $6,500 paid in commodity transactions with Fuller, Rodney & Co., alleging that Merrill Lynch succeeded to or merged with that firm. Merrill Lynch’s assumption of one lease and admission of two Fuller partners did not establish a merger or assumption of Fuller’s obligations. The decree granting summary judgment and costs to Hargrave was affirmed.

The Iso play is a simple, downhill running scheme common in I-formation and pro-style offenses. It uses a fullback to isolate and block a linebacker while offensive linemen execute base blocks and double teams at the point of attack. The tailback takes one step before running vertically behind the fullback.

Iso’s strengths are its speed, simplicity, and consistent yardage potential for teams with a powerful tailback and linemen capable of sustaining one-on-one blocks. Its main weakness is dependence on personnel, particularly large, strong offensive linemen and a rugged fullback.

Against 3-4 and 4-3 fronts, linemen establish inside leverage through drive or combination blocks, with double-team blockers advancing to linebackers. The tight end blocks the playside edge defender, receivers target safeties, and the quarterback reverse-pivots for the handoff. The fullback locates the open playside gap and blocks the relevant inside or middle linebacker, while the tailback follows his leverage.

Variations include Shotgun Iso, which gives spread offenses a downhill run and may accompany an RPO, and Weakside Iso, which can provide more favorable double-team angles and assigns the fullback to an outside linebacker.

The study reviews administrative, instructional, transformational, distributed, transactional, ethical, contingent and participative leadership in education. Administrative leadership provides clear structures but may restrict creativity and adaptability. Instructional leadership prioritizes teaching and learning but can be hierarchical and overlook student well-being and other school activities. Transformational leadership promotes shared vision, innovation and development, though efforts to change staff attitudes may become authoritarian. Distributed and participative leadership strengthen collaboration, trust, shared responsibility and teacher engagement, but may create conflicts, communication problems and slow decision-making. Transactional leadership uses authority and rewards to support performance but may weaken morale, innovation and long-term development. Ethical leadership emphasizes justice, respect, honesty and accountability, although differences in ethical perspectives can cause conflict. Contingent leadership enables principals to adapt their behavior to changing circumstances.

Because no single model can address all contemporary educational challenges, the study recommends a synthetic, flexible approach. Combining managerial stability, transformational innovation, distributed and participative collaboration, ethical integrity, contingent adaptability and transactional operational tools can improve school effectiveness, responsiveness and educational quality.

The SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 defines mandatory, recommended, and optional provisions; card capacities, voltages, form factors, interfaces, registers, commands, and transfer protocols. SDSC supports up to 2 GB, SDHC more than 2 GB through 32 GB, and SDXC more than 32 GB through 2 TB. Cards may be read/write or ROM, use standard, miniSD, or microSD form factors, and contain user and protected areas.

SD communication is host-controlled and uses commands, responses, and block data protected by CRC. Cards support single- or multiple-block transfers over one or four data lines. Defined bus modes range from Default Speed and High Speed through UHS-I modes up to 104 MB/s and UHS-II modes up to 624 MB/s. UHS-I uses 1.8 V signaling after a voltage-switch sequence and supports SDHC and SDXC cards. UHS-II adds a second-row interface, initialization, enumeration, configuration, and SD-command transport while retaining legacy SD-bus compatibility.

Initialization uses CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3 to reset cards, verify voltage, establish operating conditions, obtain identification, and assign relative addresses. Data-transfer mode permits one selected card at a time. Read, write, erase, discard, and full-user-area logical erase operations have defined command sequences, error handling, busy signaling, and capacity or interface restrictions.

Five Speed Classes specify minimum sustained performance from unspecified Class 0 through Class 10 at 10 MB/s. Application Performance Classes define minimum random and sequential performance. Optional performance features include cache, self-maintenance, and command queuing.

Protection mechanisms include a host-managed mechanical write-protect switch, internal write protection, security-protected areas, and password locking through CMD42. Card Ownership Protection adds a Force Erase Password, COP unlocking, protected password management, and alternate force-erase behavior. ROM cards reject write and erase commands and full-size ROM cards lack a write-protect switch.

The lecture reviews infinite-dimensional orthonormal expansions, where successive projections converge to the component of a vector within the spanned space and the residual is orthogonal to every basis function. Complete orthonormal sets span \(L_2\), and Schwarz’s inequality ensures finite inner products. Fourier, sinc-based, and prolate spheroidal expansions illustrate these ideas; prolate spheroidal functions optimize energy concentration within specified time and frequency intervals.

Communication systems are then described through layered processing: sources are converted to binary data, discrete encoders map bits into symbols, signal constellations assign numerical values, and modulators convert signal sequences into waveforms. Layering allows source and channel functions to be designed separately. Delay and attenuation are treated independently through timing recovery, link budgets, and signal-to-noise ratios.

Pulse-amplitude modulation maps symbols to equally spaced real signals, usually centered at zero, then forms a waveform by weighting shifted copies of a pulse \(p(t)\). Larger constellations carry more bits per signal but require rapidly increasing energy when minimum signal spacing is fixed by noise considerations.

At the receiver, filtering with \(q(t)\) produces a composite response \(g(t)=p(t)*q(t)\), followed by sampling. Nyquist’s necessary and sufficient condition for avoiding intersymbol interference is \(g(kT)=\delta_k\). In frequency terms, aliased spectral components must sum to a rectangle of width \(1/T\). A sinc response meets the criterion with minimum bandwidth but decays slowly and requires impractical delay. Wider-band responses with band-edge symmetry provide faster time decay. Raised-cosine filters are a common practical choice satisfying the Nyquist criterion while controlling excess bandwidth.

The passage describes methods and apparatus for improving localization of electronically generated binaural sound, particularly when a visible or known sound source is within one meter of a listener. Near-field HRTFs can vary significantly, require substantial processing, and provide unreliable localization. Instead, sound may be convolved with far-field HRTFs corresponding to a location behind, in front of, near, or along a line from the listener to the sound source. Visual association and adjusted volume can cause the listener to perceive the sound as originating from the source despite its actual convolved location.

Applications include telephone and video calls, augmented or virtual reality, advertisements, games, intelligent assistants, and multiple displayed speakers. Voices can be processed to distinct far-field coordinates behind corresponding images, with localization updated as the listener, device, image, gaze, or head orientation changes. Sound may also be convolved to multiple or varying points, while listener feedback helps determine an effective localization distance.

The system can switch between externally localized binaural sound and internally localized mono or stereo sound in response to detected actions or device states. Triggers include rotating or moving a portable device, changing head orientation or gaze, facial detection or absence, covering a camera or sensor, detecting light or darkness, changing listener distance, connecting headphones, or entering a low-battery state. Other responses may include muting, adjusting volume, pausing sound, or ending or holding a call. Sensors such as cameras, accelerometers, gyroscopes, proximity sensors, and biometric sensors detect these conditions.

Examples show listeners using smartphones, laptops, displays, headphones, earphones, and wearable devices. A processor continually selects or updates HRTFs so sound remains aligned with a device or displayed image, even though the actual localization coordinates may lie in empty space behind it at a far-field distance.

The paper develops a probabilistic computational model of implicature comprehension based on relevance theory and implements it in ProbLog. Relevance theory distinguishes explicatures, derived by contextually developing an utterance’s logical form, from implicatures, supplied as contextual premises or conclusions. Communication is treated as intention attribution: ostensive utterances create expectations of optimal relevance, balancing cognitive effects against processing effort.

Comprehension follows a heuristic that tests interpretive hypotheses in order of accessibility and accepts the first that satisfies relevance expectations. Explicit content, contextual assumptions, and implicit conclusions are adjusted in parallel rather than sequentially. Strong, specific relevance expectations support strong implicatures; less specific expectations may produce weak implicatures or explicatures alone.

Using an example in which Mary indirectly declines coffee by rejecting energizing drinks, the model represents encyclopaedic knowledge as probabilistic graphs and links utterances, concepts, explicatures, and implicatures through Bayesian inference. Interpretive hypotheses are evaluated by whether they satisfy relevance expectations, the Kullback–Leibler divergence between prior and posterior probability distributions over communicated assumptions, and the size of their ProbLog Herbrand bases as an approximation of processing effort. The resulting optimization model rejects hypotheses that fail relevance expectations, prefers smaller Herbrand bases when KL measures are equal, and otherwise selects the hypothesis with the highest KL measure.

The model focuses on audience comprehension and requires experimenters to construct candidate interpretations manually. Future extensions could address speaker reasoning, metacognition, higher-level explicatures, irony, quotation, and reported speech or thought.

Rutile RuO₂ has been proposed as an altermagnet, but recent calculations and bulk measurements indicate no intrinsic compensated magnetic order. Exchange-bias shifts in RuO₂/ferromagnet heterostructures have nevertheless been cited as evidence of antiferromagnetism or altermagnetism.

This study examined epitaxial TiO₂/RuO₂/Fe/Ru heterostructures using SQUID magnetometry, polarized neutron diffraction and reflectometry, atom probe tomography, high-resolution transmission electron microscopy, electron energy-loss spectroscopy, and X-ray characterization. Neutron diffraction detected no antiferromagnetic ordering in sputtered RuO₂, placing an upper limit of 0.01 μB per Ru atom on a possible sublattice moment. Polarized neutron reflectometry instead identified field-history-dependent canted, uncompensated moments at the RuO₂/Fe interface.

Chemical and structural analyses showed that this interface contains a reduced Ru region, an oxidized Fe gradient extending into RuO₂, and a reaction layer containing detectable magnetite, Fe₃O₄. Such an interlayer can pin Fe moments and produce exchange bias. Fe-based heterostructures exhibited hysteresis-loop shifts below roughly 50 K, while comparable RuO₂/Ni structures showed no significant exchange bias. TiO₂/Fe/Ru controls lacking RuO₂ also displayed a smaller bias, attributed to Fe oxidation through the Ru cap. Time-dependent magnetization measurements further indicated distinct oxidation behavior at the RuO₂/Fe interface.

The results establish that exchange bias in incoherent RuO₂/Fe heterostructures arises from a magnetically active, chemically intermixed iron-oxide interlayer rather than intrinsic antiferromagnetic or altermagnetic order in RuO₂. Exchange bias or related magnetotransport behavior alone therefore should not be treated as evidence of altermagnetism in RuO₂.

MIT’s Underactuated Robotics course requires familiarity with differential equations, linear algebra, and MATLAB, but not prior robotics coursework. It studies robots that exploit natural dynamics rather than overriding them through high-gain control.

ASIMO illustrates conventional conservative control: although technologically advanced, its stiff, bent-knee walking consumes about 20 times a human’s energy, is relatively slow, and struggles with unknown or uneven terrain. Passive dynamic walkers show that gravity and mechanical dynamics alone can produce more natural, efficient walking. Similar contrasts appear between conservatively controlled aircraft and birds capable of stalled, highly maneuverable flight. Albatrosses, falcons, bats, and trout further demonstrate efficient and agile use of environmental dynamics.

Robot motion is modeled by nonlinear second-order equations relating joint positions, velocities, accelerations, and control inputs. A system is fully actuated when its controls can produce accelerations in every direction; feedback linearization can then cancel nonlinear dynamics and replace them with simpler desired dynamics. A system is underactuated when this is impossible, formally when the control-input mapping lacks full rank.

Lagrangian mechanics provides a procedural method for deriving robot equations from kinetic and potential energy. Rigid-body manipulators commonly follow equations containing inertial, Coriolis, gravitational, and control terms. A two-link arm with motors at both joints is fully actuated; removing one motor creates the underactuated Acrobot, which requires dynamic energy pumping to swing upward.

Walking, jumping, flying, and non-force-closure manipulation are inherently underactuated because some motions cannot be directly controlled. The course progresses from pendulums, cart-poles, and Acrobots to walking robots, higher-dimensional systems, impacts, uncertainty, and unknown models. Its computational methods include analytical and numerical optimal control, dynamic programming, policy search, reinforcement learning, numerical optimization, and motion planning.

Educational pacifism argues that mass formal schooling causes pervasive, often normalized harm despite education’s presumed benefits. Harm occurs when students’ important interests are worsened and includes personal violence as well as systemic structural, objective, and symbolic harms. Authoritarian hierarchies, coercion, testing, surveillance, competition, standardized curricula, and economic conditioning can undermine autonomy, motivation, creativity, privacy, well-being, and social mobility.

Drawing on Kant’s principle that people must be treated as ends rather than merely as means, educational pacifism holds that harming innocent students is morally unjust. Most students are illegitimate targets of harm, and schooling’s harms exceed legitimate guidance. Because peaceful educational alternatives exist, mass schooling cannot be defended as a necessary last resort. The position does not claim that all schooling is always harmful or should be abolished, but that it significantly harms many students.

Montessori’s philosophy broadly aligns with educational pacifism. She viewed education as the means to lasting, positive peace and criticized schooling that suppresses children’s natural activity, autonomy, and development through domination, competition, rewards, punishments, and preparation for social and economic subordination. Montessori education instead emphasizes respect, freedom with guidance, harmonious activity, internal motivation, and peaceful social reform.

Contemporary Montessorians should therefore reject harmful and paternalistic practices while protecting student agency. However, some Montessori schools reproduce conventional testing, timetabling, coercion, hierarchy, segregation, and weak implementation. Authentic Montessori practice can offer a nonharmful alternative to mass schooling only when its commitments to peace, liberty, justice, and student autonomy are consistently maintained.

Jeff Davis Parish began school Friday after summer preparations, including campus improvements, streamlined processes, bus driver training and staff planning. Educators evaluated students to tailor instruction while meeting state requirements. The parish’s 92.5% on-time graduation rate ranks fourth statewide, up three percentage points.

Metagenomic binning clusters fragmented DNA sequences by genome of origin. Existing methods use deterministic embeddings derived from k-mer profiles or large language models, but cannot adequately represent sequences shared across genomes or distinct sequences with similar k-mer profiles.

The work proposes UNCERTAINGEN, a lightweight probabilistic embedding framework that maps each DNA fragment to a distribution rather than a fixed point. Its contrastive-learning formulation derives non-Euclidean distances from probability distributions and provides closed-form expected pairwise likelihoods for scalable optimization. Theoretical analysis characterizes ambiguity through covariance terms and argues that probabilistic embeddings expand latent-space capacity and improve fragment distinguishability. Experiments on real metagenomic datasets reportedly outperform deterministic k-mer and language-model embeddings.

The approach builds on efficient self-supervised binning methods. Each sequence is divided into two halves to form positive pairs, while halves from different sequences form negative pairs. Their k-mer profiles pass through a shared neural network trained to place positive pairs nearby and negative pairs farther apart; resulting embeddings are subsequently clustered by species. Unlike prior probabilistic embedding research using heuristic divergences or variational formulations, this framework emphasizes model-capacity results independent of specific data-generating parameters.

The speaker credits an early power-play goal and Donovan’s follow-up with restoring confidence after a poor previous game. He describes Jarome as a natural leader whose captaincy represents the next step in his development, and explains the team’s green hard-hat tradition for recognizing overlooked contributions, such as Saprykin blocking a shot that led to a goal.

Defensively, the team aims to limit St. Louis’s time and space and disrupt him physically. Kiprusoff’s consistent play and strong response after allowing six goals demonstrated mental strength. Victories over Colorado after the All-Star break convinced the team it could beat elite opponents.

The players emphasize overcoming fatigue collectively and adjusting their breakouts because opponents aggressively pressure the boards and sustain their forecheck. Suggested alternatives include using the middle, skating the puck out, and chipping it high off the glass.

The speaker rejects the idea that the team depends solely on Jarome, stressing teamwork and the development of young players such as Leopold, Kobasew, and Lombardi. Darryl improved accountability, prevented prolonged slumps, demanded mental and physical toughness, and reinforced belief in reaching the playoffs. Quiet veteran leaders, including Gelinas and Yelle, also strengthened the group. Darryl’s acquisitions, including Kiprusoff and three late-season additions, are praised despite budget constraints.

Saving penalty kicks is difficult, with fewer than 15% saved, about 80% scored, and roughly 5% missed. Goalkeepers must understand Law 14: remain between the posts facing the kicker, avoid unfair distraction, and keep part of one foot touching, aligned with, or behind the goal line until the ball is kicked. Violations may result in a retake, warning, or caution.

Coaches should provide dedicated training, appropriate equipment, positive support, and clear expectations. Modern instruction generally favors “read and react” over guessing, partly because many penalties are struck down the middle. Goalkeepers should practice observing cues such as ball placement, gaze, approach angle, run-up, plant foot, hips, chin, body lean, dominant leg, and kneecap position. Research on opponents’ recent penalties and tendencies can also inform decisions.

Preparation should include confidence, focus, emotional control, visualization, positive self-talk, controlled breathing, consistent pre-shot routines, agility, reaction time, diving, and footwork. During a kick, goalkeepers should remain calm, locate the goal’s center, adopt a balanced ready position, resist diving early, watch for stuttered approaches, read selected cues, react quickly, and use proper diving technique. Catching is preferable; otherwise, the ball should be deflected safely away.

Because an in-game penalty is a restart, play continues after rebounds or saves. Goalkeepers must recover immediately, prepare for follow-up shots, organize defenders, or launch a fast break. Teammates should cover rebounds, provide outlets, and avoid celebrating while the ball remains live. Attempts to unsettle kickers must comply with the law, and coaches should prepare goalkeepers for all post-kick outcomes.

This scoping review examined barriers and facilitators to belonging in graduate occupational therapy, physical therapy, and medical education. Of 202 identified studies, nine met inclusion criteria. Qualitative analysis identified three main influences: environment, relationships, and personal factors. Inclusive, accessible spaces and institutional cultures aligned with students’ values supported belonging, while limited representation, inaccessible environments, bias, and discriminatory practices undermined it. Positive faculty mentorship and peer relationships reduced loneliness and imposter syndrome and supported mental health, learning, and professional identity. Students’ prior experiences, identities, perceived acceptance, and confidence in their academic abilities also shaped belonging, particularly for historically minoritized students.

The review recommends that occupational therapy programs evaluate physical spaces, teaching practices, policies, and institutional climates; strengthen peer and faculty mentorship; address bias and microaggressions; support affinity groups and research opportunities; and connect students with community resources. Further longitudinal and multi-program research is needed to examine belonging specifically in occupational therapy education and develop an educational theory of belonging. Limitations include possible omitted studies, author bias, lack of evidence-quality assessment, and the subjective nature of belonging.

Nick Mathewson presents Tor as an open-source anonymity network supported by roughly 6,000 volunteer relays and used by individuals, researchers, companies, and law enforcement for privacy, while acknowledging criminal use. He distinguishes anonymity from unlinkability and unobservability, defining anonymity as preventing observers from linking particular users to activities.

Tor prioritizes practical, low-latency use such as web browsing. Clients construct circuits through multiple relays, negotiate separate symmetric keys with each relay, and apply layered encryption. No relay should know both the user and destination, though an attacker observing both ends may correlate traffic through timing and volume. Tor’s large, shared user base is important because “anonymity loves company.”

Tor relays TCP stream contents rather than raw IP packets or application-specific protocols. Directory authorities jointly vote on available relays and publish signed consensuses, limiting network-capture and partitioning attacks but retaining centralized trusted components. Applications, especially browsers, must also be modified to prevent identifying leaks such as fonts, window sizes, cookies, and cache information.

Abuse remains difficult to prevent because useful services can also be misused. Websites often block Tor through IP-based controls, while proposed alternatives include anonymous credentials and accounts that impose resource costs without exposing identity. Mathewson advises users whose freedom is at stake to employ redundant protections rather than relying on any single security product.

Hidden services provide responder anonymity by letting a service and client communicate through separate Tor paths, directory records, introduction points, public keys, and end-to-end encryption. Proposed key blinding would reduce directory enumeration attacks.

Major threats include unencrypted application traffic, traffic tagging, denial-of-service attacks, implementation errors, and end-to-end correlation. Defenses include encryption, integrity checking, failure-rate monitoring, higher-capacity relays, improved scheduling, and careful cryptographic validation. For censorship resistance, Tor uses bridges and pluggable transports whose traffic transformations are changed faster than many censors can block them.

Future work includes redesigning hidden services, modernizing cryptography, improving path selection and congestion control, combining high- and low-latency traffic, scaling beyond tens of thousands of nodes, exploring peer-to-peer directory designs, and developing evidence-based padding and traffic-analysis defenses.

Los Angeles County agreed to pay nearly $12 million to the family of cyclist Milton Olin Jr., who was fatally struck by an on-duty sheriff’s deputy. Family attorneys allege the deputy texted his wife and used his patrol computer shortly before the crash, and they are urging prosecutors to reconsider the case based on newly uncovered cellphone records.

Actress Allison Mack was released on a $5 million bond to house arrest while awaiting trial on sex trafficking and conspiracy charges. Prosecutors allege she recruited women into a secret society within Keith Raniere’s Nxivm organization, where women were branded, blackmailed, restricted and forced to have sex with Raniere. Mack pleaded not guilty and is barred from contacting Nxivm associates. Both sides are discussing a plea. Raniere, held without bail, denied harming anyone.

The Supreme Court declined to hear several appeals, including Alex Jones’ challenge to liability arising from Sandy Hook defamation claims and Colorado parents’ challenge to school practices concerning children’s gender identities. Justice Samuel Alito, joined by Justices Clarence Thomas and Neil Gorsuch, agreed the Colorado case was procedurally unsuitable but emphasized the national importance of parental-rights questions.

The court also rejected a case seeking to limit Section 230 immunity for Grindr after an anonymous plaintiff alleged the app connected him with adults who raped him when he was 15. It denied review in a Georgia death penalty case involving alleged juror misconduct; Justice Sonia Sotomayor, joined by Justices Elena Kagan and Ketanji Brown Jackson, dissented.

The justices further declined a challenge by California property owners seeking jury trials before county fines. Gorsuch agreed with the denial but suggested reconsidering precedent holding that the Seventh Amendment jury-trial right does not apply to states.

The court requested the solicitor general’s views in cases involving New Mexico’s restrictions on organizations claiming Affordable Care Act exemptions and bankruptcy protections for nondebtors.

This study developed a world model-based reinforcement learning framework for autonomous mechanical thrombectomy navigation across five tasks and ten patient-specific vascular anatomies. Simulations used clinically based guidewire and guide-catheter models, two-dimensional device-tip tracking, and patient-derived vessel meshes. Single-task Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) agents generated initial replay data, while multi-task SAC and model-based TD-MPC2 agents were trained and evaluated.

Single-task SAC achieved 82–100% success across tasks. In multi-task evaluation, TD-MPC2 significantly outperformed SAC, achieving a mean success rate of 65% versus 37% and a mean path ratio of 73% versus 47%. Improvements were particularly significant for the A2R, A3L, and A3R tasks. TD-MPC2 also required fewer exploration steps but produced longer procedure times across all tasks.

The findings demonstrate the feasibility of using one model-based agent for multiple endovascular navigation tasks across varied patient anatomies. However, TD-MPC2’s 65% success rate remains inadequate for clinical deployment, with left-sided tasks showing lower performance. Future work should improve generalization and planning efficiency, incorporate larger and more diverse datasets, model vessel deformation and contact forces, use differentiable physics, compare image-based approaches, and validate performance in vitro.

Western aversion to eating insects reflects their unsettling familiarity, appearance, abundant food alternatives, and digestibility concerns. Yet about two billion people regularly consume at least 1,900 edible, nutritious species, which provide protein, fiber, healthy fats, vitamins, and minerals more sustainably than other animal proteins. Research found most primates retain genes producing an enzyme that breaks down insect exoskeletons, while cooking also makes them easier to digest. In 2017, roasted, chili-lime-seasoned grasshoppers proved unexpectedly popular at Seattle Mariners games.

The report analyzes the global household sewing machines market from 2013–2023, including historical data for 2013–2017 and forecasts for 2018–2023. It examines production, consumption, revenue, pricing, profit, trade, growth drivers, challenges, and market trends across North America, Europe, China, Japan, the rest of Asia-Pacific, and Latin America. Segments include mechanical and electronic machines for home and light-commercial applications. It also profiles major manufacturers, including Brother, Singer, Janome, Necchi Macchina, Bernina International, Union Special, Merrow, AMF Reece, Consew, YAMATA, Elna International, SVP Worldwide, and Henderson Sewing, covering products, sales, revenue, prices, gross margins, and competitive developments.

LG’s G7 ThinQ flagship targets South Africa’s competitive premium smartphone market. It features Gorilla Glass 5, slim bezels, a bright display, AI-powered camera modes, dedicated Google Assistant and Lens access, a Snapdragon 845 processor, 4GB RAM, expandable 64GB storage, dual 16MP rear cameras and an 8MP front camera. It launches in early June from about R13,999.

The bankruptcy court granted summary judgment to Wells Fargo Bank and Dynamic Management against contractor SCS General Contractors. SCS sought payment for unpaid construction work on three Mississippi Barnhill’s restaurants, asserting equitable liens against Barnhill’s leaseholds and landlords’ fee interests and alleging Dynamic was Barnhill’s alter ego.

The court held that any prepetition equitable lien on the leaseholds terminated when Barnhill’s became a debtor-in-possession with bona fide purchaser status. SCS had neither perfected a mechanic’s lien nor received a security interest and was not a party or third-party beneficiary to the leases. No lien attached to the landlords’ fee interests because Mississippi law required their written consent, which was absent. The court ordered the escrowed sale proceeds released to Wells, while preserving SCS’s unsecured bankruptcy claim.

The court also found SCS produced no admissible evidence establishing the elements required to pierce Barnhill’s corporate veil and hold Dynamic liable. Dynamic’s evidence showed it neither controlled Barnhill’s nor contracted with or paid SCS. The court dismissed SCS’s claims against Dynamic, denied SCS’s request for additional discovery, and granted Spirit Finance Corporation’s unopposed motion to dismiss.

The U.S. Department of Education is reconsidering the Institute of Education Sciences, which plays a key role in evaluating public education and supporting states and districts. Knowledge Alliance recommends prioritizing urgent state and local research needs, improving coordination and infrastructure, and helping practitioners apply evidence effectively. Proposed steps include establishing shared learning agendas, accelerating research and study approvals, using rapid-cycle surveys, modernizing data collection, and restarting Regional Education Laboratories and Comprehensive Centers. The administration could also use artificial intelligence, social media, professional networks, and coaching to deliver actionable information to educators. Requiring practitioner-focused implementation resources and recognizing effective evidence use could further address the gap between research and classroom practice. Collaborative, strategic reforms could make federal education research more efficient, responsive, accountable, and beneficial to students, educators, and families.

The team surrendered third-period leads through soft defensive play against Detroit. Despite the loss, there were positives and confidence in rebounding at home. The goalie made strong saves and was not faulted.

The University of North Texas will hold fall 2017 commencement ceremonies Dec. 15–16 at the UNT Coliseum and Murchison Performing Arts Center in Denton. More than 3,400 students are expected to receive degrees, including 2,731 undergraduate, 615 master’s and 72 doctoral candidates. Bachelor’s ceremonies run Friday and Saturday, while the combined master’s and doctoral ceremony is at 7 p.m. Friday. Eligible graduates attending the New Orleans Bowl may join a special ceremony at 6:15 p.m. Friday at the Hilton New Orleans Riverside. Coliseum and Murchison ceremonies will be livestreamed.

Microsoft reported the expiration and settlement of debt exchange offers. On March 17, 2021, it issued $6.25 billion of 2.921% senior unsecured notes due 2052 and $1.934966 billion of 3.041% senior unsecured notes due 2062. Interest is payable semiannually beginning September 17, 2021. Microsoft revised its March 16 press release to correct the 2062 notes amount from $1.934476 billion.

The Supreme Court appointed senior counsel Amarendra Sharan as amicus curiae to examine petitioner Pankaj Phadnis’s material alleging a larger conspiracy behind Mahatma Gandhi’s assassination, while noting it appeared insufficient for a fresh inquiry. Phadnis challenged the Bombay High Court’s rejection of his plea, arguing the Supreme Court never reviewed the case on merits and alleging British Secret Service involvement and an historical cover-up.

Strength training builds muscle mass, strength and endurance, but poor technique, inadequate warm-ups, repetitive movements and lifting beyond current ability can cause injuries. Common problems include rotator cuff injuries, hamstring strains or tears, herniated discs, tendonitis, and tennis or golfer’s elbow.

Risk can be reduced by maintaining good form and posture, stretching appropriately, warming up with dynamic full-range movements, cooling down with static exercises, increasing workout intensity gradually and allowing adequate recovery. Do not exercise through pain; stop, rest and consult a doctor if symptoms persist. Qualified fitness instructors can help create an achievable programme and ensure exercises are performed correctly.

Treatment depends on the injury and its severity. Rest, gentle exercise during recovery, painkillers, physiotherapy, injections or surgery may be recommended. Ice, compression and elevation can help initially with many sports injuries, while hydration and a good diet may support recovery. Urgent medical help may be necessary for warning signs associated with a herniated disc.

Amazon.com’s 2017 Form 10-K describes operations across North America, International, and AWS, serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators. Amazon acquired Whole Foods Market on August 28, 2017, operated 472 Whole Foods stores at year-end, and employed approximately 566,000 people.

2017 net sales were $177.9 billion, operating income was $4.1 billion, and net income was $3.0 billion, or $6.15 per diluted share. Operating cash flow reached $18.4 billion, while investing activities used $27.8 billion, largely reflecting acquisitions and capital expenditures. Amazon held $31.0 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities and issued $16.0 billion of senior unsecured notes, primarily to finance the Whole Foods acquisition.

Amazon emphasizes customer focus, invention, operational excellence, long-term thinking, selection, price, convenience, and sustainable free-cash-flow growth. Its principal risks include intense competition, rapid expansion, international regulation, fulfillment and data-center operations, seasonality, acquisitions, currency fluctuations, cybersecurity, system interruptions, inventory management, intellectual property disputes, evolving regulation, taxes, supplier dependence, product liability, payment processing, and seller misconduct. The company also faced ongoing U.S. and European tax disputes.

Amazon’s common stock trades on Nasdaq under “AMZN.” It had 484.1 million shares outstanding as of January 24, 2018, had never paid cash dividends, and reported no unresolved SEC staff comments.

Five-year-old Angel, who has rare CLOVES syndrome, was brought from Pakistan to Australia by humanitarian Moira Kelly 18 months ago. The condition caused her feet to become severely enlarged, leaving her in constant pain and barely able to walk. Initially too malnourished for surgery, she is now preparing for a free double amputation in Melbourne by Professor Tony Pennington. Angel understands she will lose her feet and lower legs but looks forward to wearing shoes and dancing.

At Tesla Motors’ May 31, 2016 annual meeting, stockholders elected Brad W. Buss and Ira Ehrenpreis as Class III directors for three-year terms. They approved PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as the independent auditor for fiscal 2016 and rejected a stockholder proposal concerning supermajority voting provisions. The Form 8-K was signed by General Counsel Todd A. Maron on June 3, 2016.

The Centre empowered CGST officers to verify all transitional credit claims, regardless of whether taxpayers are administered by central or state authorities. Taxpayers claimed Rs 1.6 lakh crore in pre-GST credits, though preliminary enquiries found only 5-7% invalid. CBEC said only authorities with jurisdiction and historical records could conduct verification. Experts warned the move could prompt Centre-state litigation. CBEC also plans to amend the CGST Act to exclude credits for previously paid cesses, including Swachh Bharat and education cesses, while experts noted the need to address accumulated credits.

West Virginia Attorney General Patrick Morrisey renewed a partnership with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission to identify recalled non-food products in stores and verify recall notices. Investigators have conducted over 40 compliance checks since 2015 and plan 25 additional searches.

Tesla Motors filed a Form 8-K reporting that it issued a press release on October 2, 2015, furnished under Items 2.02 and 7.01. The release is attached as Exhibit 99.1 and is not deemed filed under the Exchange Act unless specifically incorporated by reference. General Counsel Todd A. Maron signed the report.

A media digest highlights several Enron-related stories. Three inexperienced entrepreneurs won rights to Strategic Petroleum Reserve oil but needed large letters of credit. Lance Stroud and Renard Euell failed to secure financing and forfeited seven million barrels; Euell blamed Enron after partnership discussions ended without an agreement. Ronald Peek successfully transferred his three-million-barrel interest to Hess Energy Trading, reportedly earning substantial money.

Artesia Technologies raised $26 million from Warburg Pincus Ventures and strategic investors including Enron Broadband Services. The digital asset manager planned European expansion and increased sales and marketing staffing.

Houston articles debated a proposed publicly financed downtown basketball arena. Supporters, including Enron Chairman Ken Lay and the Houston Chronicle editorial board, argued it would retain the Rockets, improve entertainment options, support downtown development and enhance the city’s appeal. Critics characterized the estimated $125 million to $175 million public contribution as corporate welfare, questioned projected economic benefits and noted that Rockets owner Leslie Alexander could gain substantial new revenue. Comparisons with recently built NBA arenas found Houston’s proposed public subsidy larger than those in four of seven cities studied, though other cities provided indirect incentives such as land condemnation and development rights. The arena proposal was scheduled for a Nov. 7 vote.

Police arrested Jason A. Clifford, 37, after he allegedly forced entry into a southeast Portland apartment complex while threatening residents with a slungshot. He faces burglary, weapons, menacing, coercion and theft charges. Two others were arrested on outstanding warrants but were not believed involved.

The CCAT Collaboration is constructing the six-meter Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope in Chile, with observations planned for 2026. Its Mod-Cam testbed and Prime-Cam science receiver will use large arrays of kinetic inductance detectors for broadband and spectroscopic observations.

The study characterizes flexible stripline circuits that connect cryogenic detectors to room-temperature readout electronics. Mod-Cam uses six 46 cm assemblies, while Prime-Cam will support three readout harnesses for approximately 100,000 detectors. Prime-Cam’s redesigned striplines use thinner copper and longer paths between temperature stages to reduce heat transfer.

Measurements yielded a copper residual resistance ratio of approximately 120, consistent with high-purity OFHC copper. Direct thermal-conductivity measurements agreed with calculated values. Despite containing three times more striplines, one Prime-Cam harness is estimated to impose less thermal loading at 4 K than Mod-Cam because of the revised geometry.

Room-temperature transmission tests found that the striplines met crosstalk requirements, with inter-channel signals at least 50 dB below transmission. Elevated crosstalk originated primarily in the SMP-SMA transition printed circuit boards, especially between closely spaced traces sharing a board. A redesigned PCB buries signal traces between ground planes; simulations predict crosstalk no greater than −57 dB across the full board, about a 20 dB improvement.

The results support flexible striplines as a robust, scalable readout solution for large detector arrays and guide fabrication of optimized Prime-Cam assemblies.

The author expects AMD shares, trading near $10 within a roughly $9.30–$15.13 range, to benefit from its April 2018 earnings report and proposes three options strategies expiring May 4. Buying a $10 call for about $0.60 provides upside exposure with a maximum $60 loss, compared with purchasing 100 shares for $1,000. A $10–$12 call spread reduces the cost to $0.50 per share and offers a maximum $1.50-per-share profit if AMD reaches $12, but caps further gains. Selling a cash-covered $10 put for $0.56 either produces $56 if it expires worthless or results in purchasing 100 shares with an effective $9.44 cost basis. Combining the put with the call spread generates a net $0.06 credit but requires accepting shares at $10 if AMD falls below that price. The author favors cash-covered puts and covered calls for disciplined entry and exit points, while acknowledging capped profits and downside exposure. The bullish outlook is based on AMD’s product line, processor demand, potential market-share gains, and the possibility of a short squeeze involving nearly 182 million shares. The author disclosed long positions in AMD, Intel, and Nvidia.

The passage documents AGESA host-environment integration, build configuration, initialization entry points, stack management, UEFI drivers, service routines, and required call-outs.

Binary AGESA calls are routed through a host-implemented call-out router whose address is stored in the standard header. The router maps function identifiers to host procedures and passes function-specific data and configuration pointers. Most procedures require a host-established stack and use 32-bit protected-mode flat addressing.

UEFI execution spans SEC, PEI, DXE, and runtime phases. SEC establishes 32-bit execution and Cache-As-RAM stack support. PEIMs initialize processors and memory, publish coordination PPIs and memory-information HOBs, and manage reset requests. DXE performs late initialization, publishes generated tables through a protocol, and can control integrated-GPU VGA decoding. Build control files, platform option files, tools, and environment variables such as `AGESA_ROOT` and `AGESA_OptsDir` must be integrated into the host build system.

AGESA supports binary-module and source-integration build methods. Platform defaults are customized through `<plat>Options.c`. During Cache-As-RAM operation, the host must not modify stack registers or cache controls. Stackless assembly macros establish and remove pre-memory stacks on x86-64 processors; PSP-equipped AArch64 APUs instead initialize DRAM.

Utility procedures create and release parameter structures, read event logs, allocate MMIO ranges, identify processors and memory locations, obtain APIC or PCI addresses, retrieve execution-cache size, and report DIMM data-eye results. Structure allocation may use pre-memory heap, post-memory DRAM, or host-provided storage.

Published boot entry points perform reset-time processor setup, early processor and interconnect initialization, memory initialization, environment transition, graphics configuration, late table generation, suspend-state saving, and resume restoration. Generated data can include DMI, P-state, WHEA, CRAT, CDIT, IVRS, and other ACPI tables. Configuration structures expose processor, power, VRM, memory, graphics, PCIe, display, FCH, UMA, ECC, interleaving, training, and related platform controls.

The host must implement essential call-outs for allocating and deallocating main-memory buffers and initiating warm or cold resets. Runtime allocations must persist in reserved memory when indicated. Only published entry functions are guaranteed to remain available; reliance on internal procedure names is discouraged.

President Donald Trump will direct U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer to assess whether China’s trade practices warrant a Section 301 investigation over forced technology transfers and intellectual property theft. Such an investigation could take a year and potentially result in tariffs or other restrictions, though officials said negotiations could resolve the dispute and no decisions had been made about using World Trade Organization procedures. The administration said the trade action was unrelated to efforts to secure China’s help in curbing North Korea’s nuclear missile program, despite Trump previously linking his approach to trade with Beijing’s cooperation on North Korea. The European Union, Japan, Germany and Canada have also raised concerns about Chinese intellectual property theft.

Graph limit theory provides analytic objects representing limits of graph sequences, analogous to completing the rational numbers with the reals. For example, the minimum 4-cycle density among graphs of edge density \(p\) is approached by quasirandom graph sequences and represented by the constant graphon \(p\).

A graphon is a symmetric measurable function \(W:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]\). A finite graph becomes a graphon by partitioning \([0,1]\) according to its vertices and filling each resulting square with the corresponding adjacency-matrix entry. Graphons can represent limits such as half graphs or quasirandom graphs. However, visual convergence alone is unreliable because vertex rearrangements can change adjacency-matrix pictures, as illustrated by checkerboards representing complete bipartite graphs.

Graph homomorphism density \(t(H,G)\) is the proportion of vertex maps from a fixed graph \(H\) to \(G\) that preserve edges. For large target graphs, these densities have the same limits as subgraph densities. For graphons, \(t(H,W)\) is defined by integrating a product of \(W\)-values, one factor for each edge of \(H\). This agrees with the graph definition when \(W\) is the graphon associated with \(G\).

A sequence of graphs or graphons is defined to converge when \(t(H,\cdot)\) converges for every finite graph \(H\). To describe convergence metrically, the lecture introduces the cut norm, which maximizes the absolute integral of a function over measurable rectangles. The cut distance between graphons minimizes the cut norm of their difference over measure-preserving rearrangements. This accounts for vertex relabeling and more general splitting and rearrangement, and also permits comparison between graphs of different sizes through their associated graphons. Edit distance is unsuitable because independent random graphs with density \(1/2\) remain far apart despite approaching the same graphon limit.

Three central results are stated: convergence of all homomorphism densities is equivalent to being Cauchy in cut distance; every convergent graph or graphon sequence has a graphon limit; and the space of graphons, identifying graphons at cut distance zero, is compact. This compactness is closely related to Szemerédi’s Regularity Lemma, while constant graphons connect the theory to quasirandom graphs.

Violet Brown, a Jamaican born March 10, 1900, was believed to have become the world’s oldest living person after Emma Morano’s death. Researchers said Brown had credible birth documentation, though Guinness World Records had not confirmed the title. The 117-year-old former sugarcane farmer attributed her longevity to hard work and Christian faith. She lives with her 97-year-old son, rests most of the day, and can walk short distances.

A UC Davis study of 50,921 California firearm deaths from 2000–2015 found gun deaths declined, largely because of reduced gang violence and fewer homicides of Black men. Firearm homicide rates fell from 4.19 per 100,000 in 2000 to 3.13 in 2014, then rose slightly in 2015. The study recorded 24,922 homicides and 23,682 suicides. California and private foundations have recently increased funding for gun-violence research amid longstanding federal funding restrictions.

WIRED reviews white-noise and sound machines for adults, children, pets, travel, and home use. These devices may offer white, pink, brown, fan, nature, and other sounds; pink and brown noise are described as less grating than pure white noise. For babies, machines should remain below recommended volume levels and more than 200 centimeters from the sleeping area.

The compact LectroFan Classic offers fan and colored noises, adjustable volume up to 85 decibels, and a 60-minute timer. The Snooz and Yogasleep Dohm generate sound with real fans and emphasize simple operation. Hatch models combine sound, lighting, clocks, app controls, and child-oriented routines, though subscriptions are needed for full content. Portable options from Momcozy, ErgoPouch, Babelio, and Yogasleep add features such as night-lights, Bluetooth, clips, rechargeable batteries, and timers, with varying sound quality and durability.

Smart speakers can also play ambient and sleep sounds through voice commands, routines, apps, or streaming services. A regular fan provides consistent noise and cooling, but dedicated machines offer greater sound variety. Buyers wanting overnight playback should verify that a device supports continuous operation rather than only timed shutoff. WIRED says recommendations are editorially independent despite affiliate compensation, and tested products are donated to local communities afterward.

The Inverted Hammer is a single-candle pattern with a small lower body, little or no lower shadow, and a long upper wick. It usually forms during a downward price swing and can signal that buyers are gaining strength, potentially leading to a bullish reversal. If a similar formation occurs at the top of an upswing, it may be called a Shooting Star.

The pattern should not be used alone. Traders are advised to consider market trends, support levels, moving averages, momentum oscillators, volume, and confirmation signals. It may support trend-following swing trades or mean-reversion strategies, particularly when occurring near support or during oversold conditions. Suggested risk controls include position sizing, diversification, stop-loss orders below the swing low, and profit targets near resistance or based on a 2:1 reward-to-risk ratio.

The passage notes that results depend on market context. Backtests on the S&P 500 found 132 occurrences since 1993, win ratios of 53–65% for exits after 1–10 days, a reported 70% overall win rate, and an average gain of 0.36% per trade. However, the pattern ranked 39th among 75 candlestick patterns and may behave bearishly in overbought conditions. Its disadvantages include subjectivity, unclear or false signals, and inconsistent suitability across timeframes.

European shares rebounded Monday after their worst weekly losses of the year, driven by easing geopolitical concerns and banking gains. RWE, Danone, Standard Life Aberdeen and Fiat Chrysler rose, while Ladbrokes Coral fell. Earnings favored energy and basic materials, while consumer cyclical and industrial firms largely missed expectations.

A McKinsey update reviewed electricity-sector privatization and restructuring worldwide from June to November 2000. It reported expanding foreign investment, utility unbundling, wholesale and retail competition, privatization, independent power projects, and regional transmission links, while noting regulatory, financial, political, and drought-related obstacles across Europe, Asia-Pacific, Latin America, Africa, and the Middle East.

Mark Schroeder considered the EU overview useful but identified errors and omissions: Spain’s power pool is not mandatory for domestic generation owners; Denmark has more than two generators because municipalities own substantial capacity; transitional anti-competitive arrangements in the Netherlands were omitted; and Poland, described as the most progressive former Communist country, was absent from the Central and Eastern Europe discussion.

Digital laggards often set aspirational goals unsupported by data, leading employees to avoid measurement, rely on “best effort,” prioritize process compliance, and resist adaptation. Their goals may lack clear links to strategy, causing misalignment and reinforcing a “culture of genius” in which individuals pursue their own priorities.

Digital leaders use transparent, data-driven objectives and metrics to connect employee and team work with company strategy. Shared goals, developed through combined top-down and bottom-up processes, support vertical and horizontal alignment while allowing flexibility and innovation. However, excessive demands for quantitative analysis can slow simple decisions and weaken intuition and critical thinking.

Strong data cultures emphasize learning, risk-taking, transparency, measurement, accessible data, and consistency between leadership beliefs, company values, and employee behavior. Cultural transformation is difficult because entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient leadership focus can obstruct change, but both traditional and digitally native firms can improve.

Organizations commonly fall into four patterns: data novices lack enabling culture and systems; insight-ready firms support experimentation but lack analytical capabilities; tech-enabled firms have technology but discourage experimentation; and data-reliant firms overuse data. Each can build on existing strengths through targeted action toward a stronger data culture.

PSA testing and mpMRI have limited specificity and sensitivity for prostate cancer, while biopsies are invasive. This study evaluated rapid point-of-care detection of circulating YAP1 nucleic acid and androgen receptor AR-FL and AR-V7 mRNA using RT-pHLAMP on a handheld ion-sensitive field-effect transistor Lab-on-Chip device.

TRIzol LS extraction enabled detection of low-abundance nucleic acids from patient plasma. In 13 evaluable samples, YAP1 was detected by RT-qPCR in 62%; benchtop RT-pHLAMP results agreed with RT-qPCR in 12 of 13 samples and were obtained within 12 minutes. AR-FL RT-pHLAMP showed complete concordance with corresponding RT-qPCR. Dual-well Lab-on-Chip detection of YAP1 and AR-FL was fully concordant with benchtop assays, generally within 15 minutes after extraction. YAP1 presence was associated with higher cancer stage and higher initial PSA. AR-FL amplification and AR-V7 were found only in high-risk or metastatic patients; AR-V7 was detected in one metastatic sample.

The findings support rapid multiplexed prostate cancer prognostic testing, but the small cohort and point-of-care incompatibility of the current TRIzol extraction require further development and validation.

NVIDIA’s A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere GA100 architecture and TSMC’s 7nm process, targets AI, HPC, and data analytics. It contains 54.2 billion transistors, 108 streaming multiprocessors, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, 40 GB HBM2 memory, 1,555 GB/s memory bandwidth, and a 40 MB L2 cache.

Third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32, FP16, BF16, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary operations. Compared with V100, A100 provides up to 10 times faster TF32 processing, 2.5 times higher FP16/FP32 and FP64 performance, and up to 20 times faster sparse TF32 or INT8 operations. Its 2:4 structured sparsity feature can double Tensor Core throughput by skipping zero values.

Multi-Instance GPU technology partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU instances, each with dedicated compute and memory resources, predictable performance, fault isolation, and quality of service. This supports multi-tenant cloud environments, virtual machines, containers, and smaller workloads while improving utilization.

A100 also introduces third-generation NVLink with twelve links and 600 GB/s aggregate bandwidth, PCIe Gen 4, SR-IOV, asynchronous memory copy and barriers, L2 residency controls, compute data compression, task-graph acceleration, improved error containment, hardware JPEG decoding, optical-flow acceleration, five NVDEC units, and faster atomic operations. CUDA 11 exposes these capabilities and reduces programming complexity.

DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs, NVSwitch, Mellanox networking, and NVIDIA’s software stack. It delivers up to 5 PFLOPS, supports as many as 56 isolated GPU instances, and can scale from individual workloads to clusters containing thousands of GPUs.

The paper studies optimal pricing for a monopolist selling one indivisible item that becomes worthless at a fixed expiration time. The seller is time-sensitive, while buyers are temporally neutral and may delay purchasing to obtain lower prices, balanced against the risk that another buyer buys first.

The market is modeled as a finite-horizon Stackelberg game. The seller commits at time zero to a continuous, non-increasing public price schedule. Buyers arrive according to a Poisson process, have independently and uniformly distributed private valuations, observe the full schedule, and choose target purchase times. The earliest target determines the sale time and price; otherwise, the item expires unsold.

To address buyers’ two-dimensional private information—valuation and arrival time—the paper introduces Value-Based Threshold strategies, which map valuation to a target purchase time. It derives necessary conditions, including an ordinary differential equation, for a candidate equilibrium and sufficient conditions for verifying existence, uniqueness, and resistance to unilateral deviations. Unlike earlier work that formally established equilibrium only for two discrete valuation types, this framework covers continuously distributed valuations.

The pricing analysis considers two stylized regimes. In thin markets, infrequent arrivals create little competitive risk, encouraging buyers to wait for the lowest price. A constant price eliminates expected discounts, induces immediate take-it-or-leave-it decisions, and produces a unique equilibrium. In thick markets, frequent arrivals make preemption likely, causing buyers to behave myopically and purchase when price reaches their valuation. The resulting near-optimal policy is a linear discount schedule whose rate depends on the seller’s time sensitivity; it also induces a unique equilibrium among fully strategic buyers.

Numerical simulations support the near-optimality of these policies and show that optimal schedules shift with seller time sensitivity: patient sellers use end-loaded quasi-auctions, moderately sensitive sellers use constant prices, and impatient sellers use front-loaded linear discounts.

The toss play is an outside run in which the quarterback pitches to a tailback moving toward the defense’s edge. It is simple to install, quickly gets the ball to the perimeter, and can consistently gain yardage with a fast tailback and athletic offensive line. Its effectiveness declines without suitable personnel, and edge or corner blitzes can disrupt it immediately.

Against 3-4 and 4-3 fronts, offensive linemen generally use reach and combination blocks to secure outside leverage and advance to linebackers. The fullback leads toward the nearest unblocked defender, while the tailback follows and reads the block. The quarterback reverse-pivots, pitches, and boots opposite; receivers block the most dangerous perimeter defenders.

Variations include the Flexbone or “Rocket Toss,” where a motioning wingback receives the pitch while quarterback action toward the fullback delays defenders, and the Single Back Toss G Pull, where the playside guard pulls around the tight end as the lead blocker. Each version aims to deliver the ball to an athletic runner on the edge before the defense can respond.

In his final State of the Union address, the President described persistent domestic and international challenges alongside national strengths such as economic growth, democracy, exploration, public judgment, and commitment to justice. He cited achievements including Medicare, expanded voting and civil rights, federal education aid, Head Start, conservation, job training, 3.3 percent unemployment, and 8.5 million new jobs over five years.

He urged Congress to fulfill existing commitments through expanded model cities and housing programs, an urban development bank, higher Social Security benefits, maternal and child healthcare, protection from catastrophic illness, continued antipoverty efforts, and $3.5 billion for job training. He also advocated enforcing fair housing protections, extending the Voting Rights Act, funding state and local crime reduction, licensing and registering firearms, reorganizing the postal system, adjusting congressional salaries, and adopting random draft selection.

The President reported increased social spending, projected federal surpluses of $2.4 billion and $3.4 billion, and supported temporarily extending the surtax while resisting inflation. He noted record wages, profits, economic growth, and a 1968 balance-of-payments surplus.

Internationally, he called for ratifying the nuclear nonproliferation treaty, resuming missile limitation talks with the Soviet Union, adequately funding aid to developing nations, supporting European unity, maintaining liberal trade, strengthening the international monetary system, and seeking peaceful agreements with the Soviet Union. He expressed hope for peace through the Paris talks while honoring American forces in Vietnam, and supported a settlement based on the U.N. Security Council resolution in the Middle East.

Concluding, he reflected on his congressional and presidential service, thanked leaders of both parties, asked Congress to support President-elect Nixon, and expressed hope that their shared work would make the country more just and preserve liberty.

Diane David appealed the dissolution judgment awarding Joseph David the marital farm and assigning her his pension, 401(k), and personal property. The Missouri Court of Appeals found no abuse of discretion in awarding Joseph the farm, despite Diane’s primary physical custody and the children’s attachment to the property, because Joseph was better equipped to farm its tillable acreage. The court also held that the parties had not formed a binding agreement requiring equal property division and that Diane’s separate teacher retirement account could be considered without being assigned as marital property. Her claim regarding taxes and penalties from liquidating retirement assets was rejected because she had not raised it at trial.

However, the trial court incorrectly calculated Diane’s awarded assets as $62,781 rather than $59,182, increasing the actual disparity between the parties’ distributions. Because the appellate court could not determine whether the trial court would have made the same division using the correct figure, it vacated the judgment and remanded for reconsideration of the property distribution and any related adjustments.

Compass Minerals International went public on December 12, 2003, after two years as a stand-alone company owned by Apollo Management. CEO Michael Ducey faced the challenge of meeting investor expectations while positioning a salt company whose major opportunities and risks included stable demand, operational execution, environmental concerns, and potential new uses for salt mines.

Salt was primarily used in the United States for highway deicing and in chemical, food-processing, water-treatment, and agricultural applications. It was produced through rock mining, mechanical evaporation, or solar evaporation, with brine cheapest, rock salt generally the least expensive dry form, and vacuum-pan salt the purest and most costly. Highway deicing represented about one-third of U.S. consumption and caused substantial yearly demand fluctuations. Since the 1970s, U.S. production averaged roughly 40 million metric tons annually, with recent average prices near $25 per metric ton.

The capital-intensive industry had consolidated substantially. By the early 2000s, 29 firms owned 66 U.S. dry-salt establishments. New mines and evaporation plants required large investments, while production costs depended on deposit depth and thickness. High transportation costs made plant location important, especially in highway deicing. Customers generally purchased through annual or multiyear contracts.

Growing road-salt use increased chloride concentrations in soils, streams, groundwater, and freshwater ecosystems. Researchers found toxic concentrations in some urban and rural watersheds and warned that impacts could persist for decades. Road salt was not regulated as a freshwater pollutant in the United States, but possible regulation threatened future demand.

Compass subsidiary North American Salt was the third-largest U.S. salt producer. General trade products generated just over half its revenue, while highway deicing represented about 40% of 2002 salt sales. Compass operated rock, solar, and evaporated-salt facilities across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom, supported by approximately 75 distribution depots. Its largest facility was the Goderich, Ontario rock-salt mine, with annual capacity of 6.5 million tons.

Ducey emphasized safety, workforce training, variable compensation, and strong execution. Compass also faced substantial debt but showed improved operating performance before the IPO. Its strategic question was how to present a compelling investment case while managing regulatory risks and pursuing emerging uses such as document storage and nuclear-waste disposal.

The “Box and One” combines four defenders in a box zone with a chaser who aggressively denies the opponent’s star player passes and rebounds. Baseline defenders X4 and X5 shift like a 1-2-2 zone, while outside defenders X1 and X2 shift like a 2-3 zone. Against even or odd fronts, defenders force the ball away from the chaser’s side, toward sidelines and baselines, while rotating to protect the low post, elbow, free-throw line, and weak-side rebound areas. The chaser maintains denial throughout, supported from both sides if the assigned opponent receives the ball. Effective denial limits the star scorer and disrupts the offense’s set plays and continuities.
