Tesla’s 2016 Form 10-K describes two business segments: automotive, and energy generation and storage. Tesla designs, manufactures and sells electric vehicles and energy-storage systems and, following its November 2016 acquisition of SolarCity, provides solar products and electricity. Its vehicles included Model S and Model X, while lower-priced Model 3 volume production and deliveries were planned for the second half of 2017. Tesla also offered Powerwall 2, Powerpack 2 and planned to begin producing and installing solar roofs in 2017.

Tesla sold vehicles directly through company-owned locations and online. At year-end 2016, it operated 265 sales and service locations, 135 service locations, 790 Supercharger stations and more than 7,110 destination wall connectors. Manufacturing occurred primarily in California, Nevada, the Netherlands and New York. Gigafactory 1 was intended to integrate battery-cell, pack and drive-unit production, with projected capacity supporting approximately 500,000 vehicles annually by 2020.

Tesla emphasized proprietary battery, power-electronics, software, dual-motor and Autopilot technologies. All vehicles began receiving hardware intended for full self-driving capability in October 2016, though drivers remained responsible for vehicle control. Tesla provided vehicle, battery, energy-storage and solar warranties and offered financing, leasing and solar agreements.

The company competed with established and emerging automotive, energy-storage, utility and solar businesses. It relied on regulatory credits, tax incentives and renewable-energy programs while remaining subject to vehicle safety, battery transport, dealer, utility and energy regulations.

As of December 31, 2016, Tesla had 17,782 full-time employees and SolarCity had 12,243. Tesla’s non-affiliate market value was approximately $24.7 billion at June 30, 2016, and 161.7 million common shares were outstanding on January 31, 2017.

Principal risks included production and delivery delays, particularly for Model 3; dependence on single-source suppliers; Gigafactory expansion challenges; uncertain electric-vehicle adoption; manufacturing costs; product defects and liability; lithium-ion battery fires or shortages; rapid international growth; regulatory restrictions; and intense competition from better-resourced companies.

The article demonstrates how to backtest a SPY trading strategy in Python using pandas for data analysis, yfinance for historical Yahoo Finance data, and matplotlib for charts. It calculates simple and exponential moving averages, removes rows lacking indicator values, and generates a regime signal of 1 when SPY’s closing price exceeds both averages and 0 otherwise. Signals are applied from the following day because they are generated at the close. Daily SPY returns are calculated and compounded only during invested periods. The strategy produced accumulated returns of 804.82%, compared with 1505.31% for buy and hold, meaning it underperformed.

The passage describes the Texas Instruments TMS320DM8127 DaVinci digital media processor. It combines an ARM Cortex-A8 control processor with a code-compatible C674x floating-point DSP. The DSP provides configurable 32KB L1 program and data memories, 256KB L2 RAM/cache with error protection, eight functional units, 64 registers, parallel arithmetic and multiplication capabilities, compact instructions, software-pipelined loops, exception handling, privilege modes, and a time-stamp counter. DSP external memory accesses pass through the system MMU, which provides address translation and protects ARM memory regions.

The Cortex-A8 subsystem supports ARMv7, Thumb2, JazelleX, media extensions, NEON, VFPv3, separate instruction and data caches, interrupts, debugging, trace buffering, and direct DDR access. Other device functions include dual DDR2/DDR3 controllers, EDMA, Ethernet, PCIe, USB, HDMI, video input/output, audio ports, GPIO, GPMC, I2C, SPI, UART, timers, SD interfaces, video acceleration, face detection, spinlocks, mailboxes, and unified memory mapping. The HDVICP2 accelerator supports major MPEG, H.264, VC-1, RV, AVS, and VP6/VP7 codecs.

The passage also lists revision changes covering operating points, voltages, clock frequencies, DDR3 support, pin multiplexing, RXACTIVE control, power sequencing, oscillator timing, EDMA registers, peripheral timing, and latch-up specifications. Extensive terminal-function tables document package pins, multiplexed functions, boot configuration, electrical supplies, reset behavior, and internal pullup or pulldown settings.

The #HV doorbell page aligns with APIC behavior for guest interrupt handling. It defines a 16-bit PendingEvent field in bytes 0–1 and NoEoiRequired in byte 2; bytes 3–63 are reserved, while the remainder is virtualization-stack-defined. The backing page must be host-owned, and guest accesses must use C=0.

The Crude Oil Friday Seasonality Strategy buys at Thursday’s close, anticipating a Friday price increase. Historical data from April 2006 to the present shows it performs better when Thursday is a down day, particularly when USO falls at least 0.75 times its 25-day average high-low range. Buying every Thursday is not recommended. The strategy produced a 56.96% profit and loss result across 98 trades, with 60 winners and an average profit of 0.58% per trade. Other weekdays displayed more random patterns.

Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) requires customers using co-signing to provide a 2048- or 4096-bit RSA public key before BOOT_DONE; it cannot later be changed. Customers sign AMD update packages using RSA-PSS with SHA-256 for 2048-bit keys or SHA-384 for 4096-bit keys.

Packages validate applicable system patch levels, firmware versions, dependencies, and all components before applying. They may modify registers, complete firmware images, or firmware portions. Packages are non-persistent across reboots and may be reapplied during boot or system operation. AMD SFS automatically commits SEV updates, preventing rollback; reverting requires reboot. SNP update pages must be marked HV-FIXED.

SFS commands use a 2 MB-aligned memory region. The 4 KB TEE_EXT_CMD_BUFFER is followed by command output or the update package, including optional customer co-signing headers and signatures. A customer deployment agent constructs the buffer and communicates its physical address through ASP mailbox registers.

The ASP protects package memory from x86 access, verifies optional customer and mandatory AMD signatures, executes the patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status. Firmware-version queries use two contiguous 4 KB pages and report API, patch, system patch, firmware version, and security patch information.

Package names identify processor family, AGESA release, and a monotonically increasing package number. Packages apply only to specified firmware and patch-level combinations. Updates run alongside x86 and DMA traffic with minimal expected performance impact. SEV or SEV/ES virtual machines must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

The ADS868xW family comprises single-channel, 16-bit SAR ADC data-acquisition devices operating from a 5V analog supply. They support differential or single-ended bipolar and unipolar inputs up to ±12.288V through nine programmable ranges. The integrated analog front end includes ≥1MΩ input impedance, a programmable gain amplifier, a 500kHz second-order antialiasing filter, a high-speed ADC driver, and input overvoltage protection up to ±20V when powered and ±15V when AVDD is floating.

A factory-trimmed, temperature-compensated 4.096V internal reference is provided, while an external 4.096V reference can also be used through the internal buffer. Conversion results use straight-binary format. Floating analog inputs produce invalid conversion data but do not damage the device.

The multiSPI interface supports four standard SPI modes, single- or dual-SDO output, source-synchronous transfers using internal or external clocks, and multi-device daisy chains. Transfers use a 32-bit shift register; valid writes require at least 32 clocks, while shorter frames can read selected output bits. Output data can include conversion results, register data, device address, input-range information, alarm flags, and parity.

Programmable alarms monitor analog-input thresholds with hysteresis and AVDD against fixed 4.7V and 5.3V limits. Active flags clear after conversion if the condition ends, while tripped flags remain until the alarm register is read.

Operational states include RESET, acquisition, and conversion, with programmable NAP and power-down modes. Nine configuration registers control reset, power, SPI protocols, output formatting, input range, reference selection, and alarms.

An example industrial design combines the ADS8681W with an eight-channel differential multiplexer for PLC, DCS, or data-acquisition inputs. Recommended implementation practices include matched source impedances, symmetric differential routing, supply and reference decoupling, separation of analog and digital routing, and external surge, ESD, and EFT protection.

Biocon India grew from an enzyme manufacturer founded by Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw in 1978 into an 800-employee pharmaceutical group with US$75 million in annual revenue by 2003. Its “earn as you learn” strategy used existing capabilities to enter generic drugs and establish Syngene, a contract research organization serving international pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies.

India’s pharmaceutical industry benefited from patent and price-control policies, rapid domestic and export growth, skilled low-cost scientists, a diverse population, government biotechnology support, and increasing global outsourcing of research, clinical trials, and manufacturing. Clinical research offered particular potential because trials represented a large share of drug-development costs. However, Indian firms faced intense competition, regulatory concerns, and doubts among multinational clients about outsourcing sensitive work.

Biocon’s success rested on fermentation expertise, patented technology, expansion into generic statins, and a collaborative, nonhierarchical culture emphasizing trust, accessibility, scientific talent, merit, and team performance. Syngene extended the company’s research capabilities and began developing the infrastructure needed for original drug discovery.

In 2000, Biocon created Clinigene to supply clinical laboratory services, bio-equivalence and bio-availability studies, hospital coordination, and eventually broader clinical-trial services. Clinigene filled a missing link in Biocon’s ambition to become a fully integrated drug discovery and development company, though Biocon’s own molecules were still years from requiring trials. It therefore needed external clients to sustain itself.

Clinigene faced strategic risks despite strong market growth. Its existing services occupied low- to medium-value segments, while moving into higher-value data management and advanced trials required substantial investment. Rapid success could make Clinigene larger than its parent, divert resources, require more formal structures, and weaken Biocon’s collaborative culture. Clinical trials also created financial, ethical, legal, and reputational risks, especially regarding informed consent, poor or illiterate participants, and perceptions that Western companies were exploiting Indian subjects.

Mazumdar-Shaw had to choose among aggressively expanding Clinigene, limiting it initially to safer lower-value services until Biocon’s own molecules were ready, or acquiring an external clinical-services organization that could remain culturally separate. The central question was how Biocon could expand while balancing growth, integration, culture, market positioning, ethics, and risk.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture introduces performance and feature improvements for gaming, professional visualization, data centers, displays, video processing, and AI. Second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, doubled FP32 processing, structural sparsity, and GDDR6X memory provide up to twice the performance in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI.

RTX IO, integrated with Microsoft DirectStorage, transfers compressed data from NVMe SSDs directly to GPUs for asynchronous lossless decompression. This reduces CPU workload and I/O overhead, improves loading and streaming, limits stutter and object pop-in, and benefits games and professional workloads involving large models, textures, and datasets.

The A40 data-center GPU provides 48GB of memory, expandable to 96GB through NVLink, PCIe Gen4, virtualization support, and professional graphics, compute, and AI acceleration. The RTX A6000 similarly offers 48GB of GDDR6 memory, scalable to 96GB, for rendering, simulation, AI, and large professional datasets. The RTX 3090 includes 24GB of GDDR6X memory, while the RTX 3070 exceeds the previous-generation RTX 2080 Ti in performance.

Ampere GPUs support 4K at 120Hz, 8K at 60Hz, DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, Display Stream Compression, and HDCP. Fifth-generation NVDEC supports hardware decoding for major codecs, including AV1 at up to 8K60 HDR with low CPU use. Seventh-generation NVENC enables high-quality, low-latency hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

Error Detection and Replay detects and retries GDDR6X transmission errors, helping users identify overclocking limits through plateauing performance. NVIDIA states that specifications may change, products require customer validation for intended uses, and the materials are provided without warranties.

The disclosure describes portable ground stations that extend the operating range of vertical-takeoff aerial vehicles by providing landing, protection, and charging. Each station includes a protective casing and an extendable landing pad that transitions between an open landing configuration and a closed configuration containing the vehicle. An elevator may raise or lower a base platform, while folding flaps, telescoping wings, or triangular panels expand the landing area. Closing components may center a landed vehicle before retracting it into the casing.

Charging terminals may be embedded in the platform, folding panels, casing walls, or top closure to contact corresponding vehicle terminals. Power may come from batteries, fuel cells, photovoltaic panels, wind turbines, mains electricity, or other sources. The casing may be lockable, resistant to motion, transparent to navigation signals, and configured with windbreakers.

Visual patterns or infrared, radio-frequency, LED, audio, ultrasonic, and other beacons may guide vehicles toward the station and landing point. Networks of stations and vehicles may be coordinated by a control server through wired or wireless communications, supporting multiple vehicles and potentially continuous operation. Modular additions may provide transportation, mounting, suspension, carrying, communications, sensing, weather monitoring, radar, night vision, or extra battery capacity.

The described operating method deploys stations across a required range, opens and raises a landing platform, guides an aerial vehicle to land, centers it, retracts it into the casing, and charges it. Multiple structural configurations and combinations of these features are contemplated.

Relations with most Indigenous tribes remain friendly, though violence continues in the Upper Mississippi, Lakes, and Missouri regions. The address reports schools intended to promote civilization and proposes voluntary relocation westward under organized civil governments, rejecting forced removal as unjustifiable.

General Lafayette’s national reception is praised, and Congress is asked to provide for him in recognition of his Revolutionary services and sacrifices. The address concludes by emphasizing constitutional limits, cooperation between state and federal governments, national unity, defense, internal improvements, vigilance against foreign and domestic dangers, and gratitude for public confidence.

Mali’s gold exports and production are declining as major legacy mines close or wind down. Morila is scheduled to close in 2019, Yatela has ended production, and negotiations to extend Sadiola’s life appear stalled. Sadiola’s owners—IAMGOLD and AngloGold Ashanti, each holding 41 percent, and Mali’s government with 18 percent—propose investing $380 million to modify its plant for hard-rock processing, accessing 3.4 million ounces of proven and probable reserves and extending operations by about 10 years.

Sadiola has operated since 1997, but depletion of soft-rock deposits has reduced annual production from 600,000 ounces in 2000 to under 200,000 ounces. The mine employs about 1,000 people, 93 percent of them Malians. Expansion could preserve and increase employment, raise government revenue, and add infrastructure, including a connection to Mali’s power grid.

Industrial gold production rose slightly from 46.5 tonnes in 2015 to 46.9 tonnes in 2016, while exports fell from 70 to 67 tonnes. Production was expected to decline to 45 tonnes, with no new mines anticipated before 2018. Gold accounts for about 25–30 percent of government revenues. With elections approaching, uncertainty over Sadiola is being closely watched as a test of Mali’s investment climate.

The study presents the first near-infrared spectra of cryogenic grain mixtures of water ice, epsomite, and halite relevant to Europa’s surface. Using the nitrogen-purged CRONOS laboratory facility, researchers measured pure materials and 50/50 volume mixtures across four grain-size ranges, generally at 100–120 K. They compared laboratory spectra with linear and intimate mixture models based on Hapke radiative transfer theory and published optical constants.

Water ice showed characteristic absorption bands at 1.25, 1.5, 1.65, and 2.0 µm, with larger grains producing lower reflectance and saturated features. Cryogenic epsomite displayed numerous absorption features absent under ambient conditions, while halite showed a feature near 1.95 µm attributed to adsorbed water. In mixtures, water ice generally dominated the spectra; halite-water mixtures were nearly indistinguishable from pure water ice, and fine grains exerted disproportionately strong spectral influence.

Linear and intimate models reproduced water-ice spectra comparably, usually within about 5–10%, though neither consistently matched both continua and absorption features. Epsomite models showed larger discrepancies because published cryogenic optical constants may instead represent ambient conditions or because laboratory epsomite partly dehydrated. Consequently, model fidelity for epsomite mixtures remained inconclusive.

The results indicate that spectra of equal-volume mixtures do not necessarily lie midway between their constituent spectra and that observations may be biased toward smaller grains. Quantitative spectral mixture analyses using optical constants are therefore recommended for determining Europa’s surface composition, abundances, and grain sizes from Europa Clipper and JUICE data. The authors plan to derive updated epsomite optical constants in future work.

After seven or eight months in Quebec, the speaker feels at home and looks forward to sharing the nearby game with family. The team’s success is attributed to preparation, resilience, hard work, and creating its own luck. They expect a desperate, intense opponent at home and plan to approach the game one shift at a time. Confident playing either home or away, the team intends to impose its physical, fast style and follow the coach’s game plan. Despite an expected loud atmosphere, the focus will be on weathering the crucial first ten minutes, quieting the crowd, and playing their game.

NVDA options can provide leveraged exposure to stock-price movements, with buyers’ losses limited to the premium paid, though options remain complex and carry stock-price, time-decay, volatility, and liquidity risks. Strategies include calls, puts, covered calls, straddles, strangles, spreads, collars, and hedges; selection depends on goals, risk tolerance, and the strategy’s risk-reward profile.

Option values are influenced by NVDA’s stock price, time to expiration, implied volatility, market sentiment, and dividends. Higher implied volatility generally raises premiums. Rising stock prices typically increase call values and reduce put values, while falling prices have the opposite effect. Dividends generally lower call prices and raise put prices.

Analysis may combine quantitative and qualitative methods, using pricing models such as Black-Scholes, technical analysis, software, and relevant news. Risk can be managed through protective puts, stop-loss orders, hedging, diversification, and position sizing. Margin requirements and trading costs vary by option type, with writing options generally requiring more margin than buying them. NVDA options are described as typically liquid. Tax treatment depends on the investor’s circumstances, and professional advice is recommended. Practical experience and a strong understanding of option pricing are emphasized.

The President informed the Senate about alleged forcible resistance in Boston to federal law enforcement. Although official information remained incomplete and disputed, he condemned the incident as an unexpected violation of federal authority, while asserting that it did not represent the general sentiment of Boston or Massachusetts.

He reviewed federal laws requiring marshals to obtain temporary detention facilities when states deny use of their jails. Massachusetts legislation enacted in 1843 barred state officials and facilities from assisting in fugitive-slave cases. The President maintained that such state laws could not diminish Congress’s constitutional duty and authority to enforce the return of persons bound to labor. If the Massachusetts marshal had not secured a detention facility, he would be directed to do so promptly.

The President transmitted related affidavits, proclamations, departmental instructions, and communications. He also recommended clarifying federal law so militia could be called to execute laws without a prior proclamation, and suggested clarification concerning presidential use of the Army and Navy and marshals’ authority to summon organized militia. He pledged to execute federal laws and suppress forcible opposition.

In a separate proclamation dated April 25, 1851, the President warned against a planned military expedition from the United States to invade Cuba, then a Spanish colony. He declared such activity illegal, punishable by fines and imprisonment, and said participants would forfeit claims to government protection. Citizens and federal officers were urged to prevent the expedition and arrest offenders.

The 2018-19 Union Budget contained no separate allocation for women, unlike previous years, and critics argued it largely addressed women within traditional household and economic roles rather than tackling barriers to employment or changing development patterns.

Economists highlighted the National Health Protection Scheme, offering Rs 5 lakh annual insurance to 10 crore vulnerable families, as potentially improving women’s access to treatment. However, concerns included uncertain implementation, weaknesses seen in earlier insurance schemes, inadequate preventive healthcare, and insufficient funding. Health-sector allocations rose only 2.7 percent, while their share of the total Budget fell from 2.4 to 2.1 percent. Funding for the National Health Mission also declined by 2.1 percent.

Support for micro, small and medium enterprises, including Rs 3,794 crore for credit and subsidies and expanded corporate tax reductions, could benefit women employed or self-employed in small industries. Sanitation investments were also viewed as potentially improving women’s health.

Negative developments included reduced maternity entitlement funding, with Rs 2,400 crore allocated against an estimated central commitment of Rs 8,000 crore. The expanded Ujjwala LPG scheme was criticised because many beneficiaries could not afford replacement cylinders. Overall, experts found mixed potential benefits but little substantially new for women, with most initiatives continuing existing approaches and programmes.

Chelsea and Real Madrid could rival Tottenham for Ajax defender Davinson Sanchez, valued at £40m. Tottenham reportedly plan a £28m opening bid, while Ajax want a new contract. Sanchez is said to want Premier League and Champions League football.

Shares of Walgreens, CVS Health and Rite Aid fell about 5% after reports that Amazon was considering selling prescription drugs online. Leerink said Amazon was exploring the market and would likely enter drug distribution within two years. Amazon declined to comment.

Lincoln argues that slavery agitation has intensified and that the nation cannot remain permanently divided between slave and free states. He contends that the Nebraska Act, the Dred Scott decision, and political endorsements formed a coordinated process expanding slavery: opening territories to it, denying federal and territorial power to exclude it, and potentially preparing a future Supreme Court ruling against state exclusion of slavery.

He criticizes “popular sovereignty” as ineffective under Dred Scott and warns that public indifference to whether slavery is accepted or rejected could make slavery lawful nationwide. Lincoln rejects Senator Douglas as a reliable opponent of slavery because Douglas professes neutrality toward its expansion and has not joined Republican principles. He urges Republicans to entrust their cause to committed opponents of slavery, remain united, overthrow the governing political power, and prevent slavery’s nationwide legalization. He concludes that Republican victory is ultimately assured if they stand firm.

The Tenth Circuit affirmed Henry J. Adams III’s 140-month sentence for armed bank robbery. Adams helped plan the robbery, recruited a driver, acted as lookout, assisted the escape plan, and expected compensation. The court held he was not substantially less culpable than the other participants and therefore did not qualify for a minor-participant offense-level reduction.

Although the advisory guidelines range was 84 to 105 months, the district court imposed an upward variance based primarily on Adams’s extensive and escalating criminal history, repeated recidivism, the seriousness of the offense, deterrence, public protection, and rehabilitation. The appellate court determined that the sentence was a variance under 18 U.S.C. § 3553(a), not a guidelines departure, and found it substantively reasonable. Adams’s comparison of his sentence with a codefendant’s did not establish an unwarranted nationwide sentencing disparity.

USB-C and USB-A describe connector shapes, not speed or capability. USB-C is smaller, reversible, and supports advanced features such as USB Power Delivery and DisplayPort Alternate Mode. Devices using compatible ports remain limited by the slowest component, including cables.

USB4 exclusively uses USB-C and initially offered 20–40 Gbps speeds. USB4 Version 2 can potentially reach 120 Gbps but remains uncommon. USB 3.x naming is inconsistent, so checking stated speeds is more reliable: USB-A tops out at 20 Gbps, while older standards range from 10 or 5 Gbps down to USB 2.0’s 480 Mbps.

USB-PD enables charging up to 240 watts under USB-PD 3.1, though ports, chargers, cables, and devices must support the required wattage. DP Alt Mode carries audio and video over USB-C. USB4 requires it and uses DisplayPort 2.0, supporting higher display resolutions and refresh rates than DisplayPort 1.4.

Thunderbolt uses USB-C but enforces stricter certification. Thunderbolt 4, based on USB4, supports up to 40 Gbps, 100-watt charging, DisplayPort 2.0, and two 4K displays at 60 Hz, including over cables up to two meters. Thunderbolt 5 raises bidirectional bandwidth to 80 Gbps, reaches 120 Gbps for display output, supports expanded multi-display configurations, and delivers up to 240 watts.

To obtain expected performance, every component must meet the required specifications. Users should preferably use supplied cables and compare explicit speed and wattage ratings rather than USB version labels.

The study examines positive, neutral, and negative value loads in prose reading texts from Turkish primary-school textbooks for grades 2–4. Using OCR and text-processing tools, researchers created a database of 3,637 unique words. Three applied-linguistics experts classified words by internal meaning, consulting dictionaries and comparison methods. Overall, 172 words (4.72%) conveyed positive values, 159 (4.37%) negative values, and 3,306 (91.43%) neutral values. Grade-level results similarly showed about 5% positive, 4.5% negative, and 90% neutral transfer, with no observable relationship between grade level and value load. The authors conclude that standards for presenting value-related vocabulary are lacking and recommend classifying words by conveyed values, increasing positive-value vocabulary, using corpus-based textbook preparation, and digitizing textbooks to support further comparative research.

Nannette Perkins, 40, was arrested at her Taylorsville home after a tip identified her as the suspected pajama-wearing robber in at least six Salt Lake City-area bank robberies, including five within two hours. She remains jailed pending a court appearance.

The stick concept is a quick-game passing play used in West Coast, Air Raid, and other offenses. Five eligible receivers release downfield, giving the quarterback options on both sides. The tight end commonly runs the primary stick route, adjusting against coverage: versus man, he runs a speed out after five vertical yards; versus zone, he settles in an open area.

The quarterback identifies the flat defender before the snap and reads his post-snap movement. If that defender stays inside or honors the tight end, the quarterback throws the arrow route; if he widens with the arrow, the quarterback targets the stick route. A backside slant/arrow combination provides an answer against blitzes or favorable matchups, while the Z receiver runs an outside-release go route.

Stick works well against man, Cover 3, and Cover 4. It is less favorable against Cover 2 because the cornerback can undercut the arrow route, though a sideline “hole shot” to the Z receiver is possible with sufficient arm strength and anticipation.

Variations include a condensed 2x2 formation, where outside receivers run stick routes and slots run arrows, with the running back as a check-down; and “Sticko,” a double-move counter featuring the tight end vertically, a delayed slot slant, and a backside sluggo.

Student newsrooms serve as essential local news sources for campus communities, informing students about issues, events, and diverse perspectives. Their removal would worsen news deserts and limit students’ ability to make informed decisions, challenge their beliefs, and prepare for civic and professional life. Amid increasing media consolidation and declining local news, preserving student journalism is presented as vital to educating future generations.

UOB strategists expect GBP to grind toward 1.3040/45, with resistance at 1.3060. Although the bearish phase remains intact, weak downward momentum makes a near-term fall to 1.2900 unlikely. Support lies at 1.2975 and 1.2939.

The passage explains how to build and backtest an RSI reversal strategy using TradingView and Pine Script. The example trades DOT on a five-minute chart with a 14-period RSI, entering long when RSI rises above 35, entering short when it falls below 65, and closing positions when RSI crosses 50.

Users add RSI through the Indicators menu, adjust its settings, and create a strategy in the Pine Editor. Pine Script’s built-in `ta.rsi`, conditional statements, `strategy.entry`, and `strategy.close` functions implement the rules. User inputs can make the RSI period and overbought or oversold thresholds adjustable from the strategy settings.

After adding the script to the chart, TradingView reports metrics including equity, net profit, drawdown, win rate, Sharpe ratio, average risk-to-reward, and individual trades. Standard backtests are limited by candles displayed on the chart. Pro or higher accounts can use deep backtesting across available historical data and selected date ranges. Trade data can be exported as CSV, although this option is unavailable to free users.

The passage cautions that RSI alone does not perform consistently and may benefit from additional indicators or criteria.

The address presents domestic and foreign-policy priorities while asserting that the United States remains strong despite economic, security, and international challenges. Domestically, it calls for accelerated and permanent tax reductions, elimination of dividend double taxation, spending restraint, private retirement accounts for younger workers, Medicare reform with prescription-drug coverage, medical liability reform, energy independence, cleaner technologies, faith-based service initiatives, mentoring for disadvantaged children, addiction treatment, restrictions on abortion, and a ban on human cloning.

The speaker proposes $1.2 billion for hydrogen-powered vehicle research, $400 billion over ten years to strengthen Medicare, and $15 billion over five years for an international AIDS relief plan focused on Africa and the Caribbean. The plan aims to prevent infections, provide treatment, and care for patients and orphans.

On national security, the address describes efforts against Al Qaeda, expanded homeland protections, a proposed $6 billion Project BioShield, and a new center to integrate terrorist-threat information. It identifies regimes seeking weapons of mass destruction as the gravest danger, supports peaceful pressure on Iran and North Korea, and focuses extensively on Iraq.

The speaker accuses Saddam Hussein’s government of violating disarmament obligations, concealing chemical, biological, and nuclear programs, obstructing inspectors, abusing Iraqi citizens, and supporting terrorists. He announces that evidence will be presented to the United Nations and states that, if Iraq does not fully disarm, the United States will lead a coalition to do so. While emphasizing the costs of war and a preference for peace, the address pledges decisive military action if necessary, humanitarian aid for Iraqis, and continued confidence in American resolve, freedom, and faith.
Cancer-cell mitochondria enter neighboring fibroblasts, promoting growth and altering gene activity.

The lecture introduces a course connecting extremal graph theory and additive combinatorics. Schur’s theorem states that every finite coloring of the positive integers contains a monochromatic solution to \(x+y=z\). Its infinitary and finitary forms are shown equivalent through restriction and diagonalization. Schur used the theorem to prove that, for any exponent \(n\), Fermat’s equation has nontrivial solutions modulo every sufficiently large prime, ruling out a proposed modular strategy for Fermat’s Last Theorem.

Schur’s theorem is proved using Ramsey’s theorem for triangles: every sufficiently large complete graph whose edges receive finitely many colors contains a monochromatic triangle. Ramsey’s theorem is established by induction on the number of colors. Given a coloring of integers, coloring edge \(ij\) by the color of \(j-i\) turns a monochromatic triangle into a monochromatic solution of \(x+y=z\). This illustrates how translating additive problems into graph theory provides greater flexibility.

The lecture then surveys additive combinatorics. Van der Waerden’s theorem guarantees arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions. The Erdős–Turán conjecture, proved by Szemerédi, asserts that every positive-density set of integers contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. Roth proved the three-term case using Fourier analysis. Other approaches include ergodic theory, higher-order Fourier analysis, graph and hypergraph regularity, and the Polymath project. A recurring theme is decomposing mathematical objects into structured and pseudorandom parts.

Extensions include multidimensional Szemerédi theorems for finite constellations, polynomial Szemerédi theorems for polynomial patterns, and the Green–Tao theorem that primes—and relatively dense subsets of primes—contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. Ergodic methods often provide qualitative results without quantitative bounds, while combinatorial approaches can yield explicit bounds.

The course will next study extremal graph theory, beginning with Mantel’s theorem and questions about graphs in which every edge lies in exactly one triangle. Such questions connect to Roth’s theorem and bounds for sets avoiding three-term arithmetic progressions, where substantial gaps and open problems remain. Course assignments include collaborative lecture notes and contributions to Wikipedia.

American Mint offers a 24k gold-layered Band of Brothers Men’s Ring honoring American service members. Available in sizes 8–14 with a jeweler’s box, it costs $129.90 for a limited time while supplies last.

Since January 2000, a compounded QQQ mean-reversion strategy reportedly achieved a 12.34% CAGR, high profit factor, and lower drawdown than buy-and-hold. Trades exit when the close exceeds the previous high or close. Future performance remains uncertain.

The London breakout strategy trades price moves above or below the Asian session’s range, generally within the first three hours of the London session. Traders go long on upward breakouts and short on downward breakouts, based on the London session’s high liquidity and volatility. The Asian range can be defined using session highs and lows or candle opening and closing prices; breakouts may begin during the preceding Frankfurt hour.

Custom London breakout indicators can display entry, stop-loss, and take-profit levels and may be automated. A backtest on EUR/USD found that buying breakouts above the range lost money, while buying breakouts below the low produced average gains near zero. The passage concludes that additional parameters or risk management would be needed and expresses skepticism about the strategy and forex trading generally.

Typical session hours are 8:00 AM–5:00 PM GMT for London, 8:00 PM–8:00 AM GMT for Asia, and 8:00 AM–5:00 PM EST for New York, subject to daylight-saving and local market adjustments.

Freelance science writer and amateur astronomer David Dickinson describes the anticipation surrounding the August 21 total solar eclipse, whose 70-mile-wide path crosses the United States from Oregon to South Carolina. Millions are expected to watch, while dedicated eclipse chasers, or “umbraphiles,” have planned for decades and may travel based on weather conditions.

Dickinson, who previously witnessed partial and annular eclipses but never totality, plans to observe 107 seconds of totality from North Carolina. He notes that clouds could obstruct the event and intends to focus on experiencing it rather than photographing it.

Directly viewing the sun during partial phases can seriously damage eyesight. Observers should use approved ISO 12312-2 solar glasses, properly filtered equipment, or a pinhole projector; only during totality may the sun be viewed unprotected.

Total eclipses occur because the sun is about 400 times larger than the moon and roughly 400 times farther from Earth. As the moon recedes, total eclipses will eventually cease in about 600 million years. The next total solar eclipse crossing the United States will occur April 8, 2024.

The study developed strategies for excellence in vocational institutions under Thailand’s Office of the Vocational Education Commission amid technological disruption, workforce shortages, and skills mismatches. Using a two-phase research and development methodology, researchers surveyed 206 respondents from institutions nationwide, analyzed needs through the modified priority needs index and SWOT analysis, examined three exemplary institutions, and obtained evaluations from nine experts.

Current management conditions were rated high and desired conditions highest. The overall needs index was 0.179, with curriculum development ranked highest, followed by cooperation networks, personnel, teaching management, graduate quality, and administration.

The resulting framework comprises vision, mission, objectives, strategies, and indicators. Its six strategies are: improving professional management; developing competency-based curricula to international standards; elevating teaching and learning; developing teachers and staff as specialized professionals; building comprehensive workforce-development networks; and producing high-competency graduates. Proposed methods emphasize digital administration and learning platforms, industry-aligned curricula, active learning, professional certification, dual vocational education, partnerships, ethical development, and upskilling.

Experts rated the strategies’ overall suitability and feasibility at the highest level. The study recommends prioritizing competency-based curriculum development, adapting implementation to each institution’s context, and integrating strategies with existing plans. Future research should develop curriculum models linking professional competencies with qualifications and examine digital-content production and internationally recognized competency standards.

California’s Department of Fish and Wildlife re-approved Newhall Ranch after certifying additional environmental analysis addressing greenhouse gas emissions and protection of the endangered unarmored three spine stickleback, as ordered by the California Supreme Court. Developer Newhall Land revised its mitigation plan with 13 measures intended to achieve net-zero emissions; state air regulators found an adequate basis for no net additional emissions. Construction changes will avoid water contact, eliminating previously approved fish collection and relocation measures. The 15,000-acre, nine-phase project could include 12,000 homes and 11.5 million square feet of commercial and industrial space. Los Angeles County supervisors are expected to consider re-approval of its first two villages.

A Nigerian bank support worker warned of ATM fraud in which scammers transfer money from stolen phones or hacked accounts into victims’ accounts and ask them to withdraw it. When the original account holder reports the theft, recipients may have their accounts frozen, BVNs flagged, and face arrest. The banker cited an 18-year-old forced at gunpoint to withdraw ₦40,000 and an adult who unknowingly withdrew ₦50,000 for a scammer. The public was advised to reject all requests to receive transfers for ATM withdrawals.

The study evaluated the maturity of English-language PubMed publications on healthcare AI from 2019–2021 using a validated BERT classifier and manual annotation of specialties, countries, data types, model types, and diseases. The classifier achieved 99% accuracy, with F1 scores of 93% on the test set and 91% in prospective validation.

Only 385 of 7,062 publications were classified as mature models. Reported maturity rates were 6.01% in 2019, 7.7% in 2020, and 1.81% in 2021. Radiology consistently produced the most mature models, while pathology, ophthalmology, and gastroenterology also ranked highly in individual years. COVID-19 publications had maturity rates of 4% in 2020 and 1.6% in 2021.

Mature publications were geographically concentrated, particularly in the United States and China, with South America, Eastern Europe, and Africa underrepresented. Image data appeared in approximately 88–89% of mature publications, whereas text and tabular data were less common. Deep learning was the leading model type, used in 62–71% of mature publications, followed by traditional machine learning.

The findings identify gaps across specialties, data types, and regions and suggest opportunities to increase mature healthcare AI research through greater use of heterogeneous datasets, diverse models, infrastructure, and global resources. Limitations included reliance on PubMed, English-language publications, and exclusion of conference abstracts.

Tesla entered an underwriting agreement on February 13, 2020, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley to sell 2.65 million common shares publicly. Underwriters fully exercised an option for 397,500 additional shares. The offering closed February 19, generating approximately $2.31 billion in net proceeds. Tesla and qualifying security holders waived certain registration rights related to the offering. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, waiver, legal opinion, and offering press release.

Bar Harbor Bankshares reported 2016 net income of $14.9 million, including $2.7 million in acquisition and system-conversion charges. Assets rose to $1.8 billion, loans increased 14 percent, and non-interest income grew 38 percent.

The passage studies antiferromagnetic domain-wall dynamics driven by spin-orbit torque. Antiferromagnets offer potential advantages over ferromagnets because they produce no stray fields, withstand moderate external fields, and support fast Newtonian and relativistic dynamics. The authors identify steady precession, constant-velocity propagation not obtained through a simple Lorentz transformation, and periodic motion between two positions when spin polarization has both in-plane and perpendicular components. Damping-induced breaking of Lorentz invariance is included, along with the magnetic moment generated by time-dependent Néel order.

The model is an antiferromagnetic spin chain with exchange, Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, perpendicular anisotropy, damping, and spin torque from polarized electrons. Although most cases neglect the DM interaction, its effects are discussed. A continuum approximation based on tetramers yields an extended nonlinear sigma model for the Néel vector. The tetramer formulation gives magnetization proportional to the cross product of the Néel vector and its time derivative; total magnetization follows by spatial integration. Numerical results come from discrete-spin simulations using 14,200 lattice sites.

For spin-current polarization perpendicular to the plane and no DM interaction, simulations beginning with a static Néel domain wall approach a steady state in which all spins precess around the polarization axis at constant angular frequency. Using spherical coordinates and separating spatial and temporal dependence, the continuum equations predict a transient term that decays through damping and a stable long-time precession frequency \(\omega=-\beta/\alpha\), determined by the ratio of spin torque to damping.

The study examines MnBi₂Te₄/(Bi₂Te₃)ₙ superlattices grown by the Inverted Vertical Bridgman Method and links melt dynamics, manganese distribution, layer stacking, and magnetic behavior. Four ingot sections showed distinct structures despite identical starting composition. Near the initial growth region, turbulent flow supported pure MnBi₂Te₄ and closely spaced septuple layers with high Mn content, producing antiferromagnetic transitions at 26 and 13.5 K. Farther along, MnTe precipitation reduced Mn concentration and introduced Bi₂Te₃ quintuple layers. Samples with septuple layers separated by 4–5 or 7 ± 2 quintuple layers displayed ferromagnetic behavior near 9–11 K; Mn depletion reduced magnetization and anisotropy.

Four growth regimes were identified: turbulent flow, rapid MnTe precipitation, stationary flow, and cessation of flow. The transition from turbulent to stationary flow caused MnTe precipitation and reduced average Mn content from about 14 to 7 at.%. During stationary growth, diffusion-limited competition among MnBi₂Te₄ layer edges generated ordered alternating layers. Septuple-layer spacing increased as MnTe supersaturation decreased. When flow ceased, purely diffusive transport increased Mn incorporation but also promoted defects, Mn depletion within septuple layers, and stacking disorder. Magnetic resonance measurements supported the SQUID results, with stronger anisotropy in the more structurally ordered ferromagnetic sample.

The findings establish that melt composition and flow govern septuple-layer spacing, structural quality, and magnetic phase. Closely spaced, Mn-complete layers favor antiferromagnetism, whereas wider spacing and Mn-deficient layers produce ferromagnetic signatures. Controlled growth conditions may therefore enable tuning of magnetic topological materials.

Young African entrepreneurs are using technology to make agriculture more sustainable, resilient and profitable amid climate change. In Rwanda, Jean Bosco Nzeyimana’s Habona employs 25 youths to convert organic waste into fuel briquettes and fertiliser, reducing emissions and restoring soil quality. Malawi’s Pilirani Khoza sponsors female science students who train rural women farmers in irrigation, drought- and flood-tolerant crops, tree planting and soil-water conservation. Kenya’s Brian Bosire developed a handheld soil sensor that provides farmers with crop and input advice through mobile phones; his company aims to reach 200,000 farmers.

These initiatives, showcased at the 2017 Young Africa Works Summit, seek to improve food security, employment and climate resilience. U.N. official Richard Munang said agriculture can reduce poverty faster than other sectors because it employs nearly two-thirds of Africa’s population. He advocated developing the full agricultural supply chain through technology, logistics, clean energy, processing and market access to create jobs and income.

The Supreme Court considered whether the federal government can be sued when postal workers intentionally fail to deliver mail. Texas landlady Lebene Konan alleged that workers withheld mail as racial harassment. A lower court dismissed her claims under the Federal Tort Claims Act’s postal exception, but the 5th Circuit allowed them to proceed, finding that intentional nondelivery is not mail “loss,” “miscarriage,” or “negligent transmission.”

Several justices questioned whether “loss” covers intentional conduct, while others worried that permitting such claims could trigger numerous lawsuits over delayed or missing mail. Konan’s attorney argued that intentional nondelivery claims are rare and difficult to establish. Some justices also warned that broad immunity could cover deliberate destruction of mail-in ballots or Social Security checks. A decision is expected by early July.

Staff at Aiken County’s Silverbluff Audubon Center support the Philadelphia Eagles because a pair of bald eagles has nested there since 1994. After initially failing to appear, an eagle was spotted soaring nearby. Staff joked that the national symbol also connects with Patriots fans, making either Super Bowl outcome acceptable.

Enron’s delayed third-quarter filing widened its loss to $664 million, or 87 cents per share, and warned that a credit downgrade could require repayment or collateral for a $690 million note by late November. A further downgrade could trigger $3.9 billion in additional obligations, while falling asset values could cause a $700 million fourth-quarter charge. Enron faced $9.15 billion in obligations through 2002 against about $1.75 billion in available cash and credit.

Arthur Andersen had not completed its review, and Enron’s internal investigation remained ongoing. The company had restated prior profits downward by $586 million and increased previously reported debt. Representative John Dingell requested an investigation of Andersen’s Enron and Waste Management audits.

Bankers questioned whether Dynegy might abandon its proposed acquisition under a material-adverse-change clause, while shareholder litigation also threatened the deal. Enron sought financing, asset sales, debt restructuring and extensions to preserve cash. Other reports noted Kenneth Lay relinquishing severance, the Conoco-Phillips merger strengthening Houston’s energy-sector prominence, and ChevronTexaco increasing expected merger savings.

Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN) comprises autosomal-dominant cancer syndromes MEN1, MEN2, and MEN4, associated respectively with pathogenic variants in MEN1, RET, and CDKN1B. This study assessed MEN-linked variants in Indian populations using IndiGen, ClinVar, and Mastermind data and ACMG/AMP classification guidelines.

Researchers identified 1,324 unique variants across the three genes and created MAPVar, a searchable database containing 3,280 ACMG-classified variants: 1,094 pathogenic/likely pathogenic, 1,591 benign/likely benign, and 595 variants of uncertain significance. Analysis of IndiGen data identified two likely pathogenic RET variants and estimated that approximately 1 in 341 Indians may carry a MEN-linked pathogenic RET mutation. One variant was found in Jammu and Kashmir and another in Odisha; the latter occurred at a significantly higher frequency in IndiGen than in examined global datasets.

MAPVar analysis of the GUaRDIAN endocrine cohort identified five unique pathogenic variants among seven patient cases, involving RET or MEN1. The researchers also developed a multiplex sequencing panel covering all coding regions of RET, MEN1, and CDKN1B through 38 amplicons in two pools. Testing across 72 patients with endocrine disorders identified pathogenic MEN1 mutations in three cases provisionally diagnosed with acromegaly, pheochromocytoma, or insulinoma.

The study concludes that MEN, particularly RET-associated disease, warrants further investigation in India. MAPVar and the sequencing panel are intended to support variant interpretation, carrier detection, and early, accurate, cost-effective genetic diagnosis.
All four analysts predict Dariush to beat Dunham, citing superior all-around and ground skills and Dunham’s wear. Three expect a unanimous decision; one predicts a second-round submission.

VOT targets Tibet on shortwave frequencies 11.510, 9.510 and 15.565 MHz, requiring frequent retuning. ASIASAT 7 carries its 24-hour C-band “MOMO” audio service, alternating 30-minute Mandarin and Tibetan broadcasts.

Radford University selected two finalists for Vice President for Student Affairs, a position held on an interim basis by Susan Trageser since Dr. Irvin Clark’s departure in spring 2017. Both candidates attended campus forums in September.

Dr. Thomas C. Segar, Vice President for Student Affairs at Shepherd University, has more than 26 years of experience. His priorities include student success, belonging, social justice, experiential learning, strong services, institutional pride, and proactive advising.

Dr. Ann Marie Klotz, Dean of Students at the New York Institute of Technology, emphasized mentorship, particularly for first-generation students, based on her own experience. She advocates adaptable, student-centered universities, supportive campus communities, and greater use of social media to share Radford’s story. Both candidates expressed enthusiasm about joining Radford.

Australia and Germany finished Day 1 of their 2018 Davis Cup tie level at 1-1 in Brisbane. Alexander Zverev survived a five-set challenge from teenager Alex de Minaur before Nick Kyrgios beat Jan-Lennard Struff 6-4, 6-4, 6-4. Christa Goldblatt of Crossborder Energy circulated R. Thomas Beach’s rebuttal testimony on behalf of Indicated Electric Generators supporting the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement in a California natural gas restructuring proceeding.

Beach responds to Southern California Generation Coalition and The Utility Reform Network testimony supporting their Post-Interim Settlement Agreement. He argues that their proposal improperly defers unbundling SoCalGas intrastate transmission. He maintains that PG&E and SoCalGas have faced similar access and conflict-of-interest issues, their backbone systems serve comparable functions, and statewide consistency favors applying the PG&E Gas Accord model to SoCalGas.

Beach contends that PG&E’s city-gate market has reduced transportation costs for electric generators without requiring customers to hold capacity or pay demand charges. He says SCGC and TURN overlook competitive city-gate benefits, a projected $3 million annual reduction in electric-generation rates beginning in 2002, greater rate stability, and reduced customer exposure to transmission and storage cost risks.

He argues that SCGC and TURN overstate demand-charge impacts by assuming generators contract for unrealistic amounts of firm capacity and neither release excess capacity nor use alternatives. The Comprehensive Settlement offers a partially volumetric firm rate, interruptible service, capacity trading, and city-gate purchases. Recalculating SCGC and TURN’s study using interruptible service, Beach estimates annual fixed costs would rise by 0.6%, rather than as much as 20%.

Beach also disputes claims that city-gate markets would create bottlenecks, manipulation, plant closures, or reliability problems. He cites excess SoCalGas backbone and storage capacity, capacity-holding limits, priority open seasons for end users, and SoCalGas’s incentive to sell unused capacity. He recommends adoption of the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement.

Escalating nuclear threats between Donald Trump and Kim Jong-un triggered a global market sell-off and renewed volatility. A mouse study suggests black tea may support weight loss by altering gut bacteria, increasing microbes linked to lean body mass and reducing those associated with obesity. Combining black and green tea may offer complementary benefits.

The goalie adjusted to Zdeno’s large screen by directing shots from the sides for better visibility. Both goaltenders made key saves in a tight game that seemed likely to extend into overtime. The embassy assesses Andropov’s foreign policy as a continuation of Brezhnev’s hard line, despite greater vigor and intelligence and a continuing Soviet dependence on relations with the United States. U.S. policy should prioritize security and reducing the risk of nuclear war, combining arms control with adequate defense rather than expecting arms control to sustain the entire bilateral relationship.

Arms control, especially intermediate-range nuclear forces (INF), is presented as the best available means to improve relations and counter growing European perceptions of U.S. rigidity. The telegram argues that the U.S. zero-zero INF position has nearly exhausted its usefulness and should change. It describes Soviet strategy as seeking to prevent NATO deployment without eliminating Soviet SS-20 missiles, using incremental negotiating concessions and propaganda to influence Western European, particularly German, opinion. Without a new U.S. initiative, the NATO deployment schedule could be endangered.

The planned deployment of 572 ground-launched cruise missiles and Pershing II missiles was primarily intended to reassure Europeans that the United States would respond to a nuclear attack on Europe as an attack on itself. The number was set below projected SS-20 warheads but high enough to establish U.S. credibility.

The Grand River Conservation Authority will spend $1.8 million over five years to digitally map Grand River floodplains and most Speed and Conestogo river floodplains using LiDAR. Detailed 3D maps of land and riverbeds will replace decades-old plastic-sheet maps and integrate with U.S. Army Corps of Engineers software for near-real-time flood forecasts. The system will help identify threatened properties and improve emergency notifications. The long-planned project reflects changes in river conditions and was not prompted by June’s unexpected flooding.

The Government is consulting on stronger action against irresponsible directors following failures such as Carillion and BHS. Proposals include reversing asset stripping to recover money for workers, disqualifying directors who sell struggling companies and expanding Insolvency Service powers. Ministers say reforms would increase accountability, while opposition figures welcomed stronger protections but criticised delayed government action.

Although many U.S. institutions prioritize global citizenship, only about one percent of higher-education students study abroad. Virtual global learning improves access, but travel-based programs offer distinctive intercultural, academic, personal, and professional benefits. Financial, administrative, and logistical barriers limit expansion, creating a need for sustainable and replicable program models.

The article proposes designing education abroad programs around three interdependent drivers: curricular, operational, and financial logistics. Curricular objectives and measurable learning outcomes should guide decisions about credits, assessment, location, activities, duration, institutional alignment, and program differentiation. Operational planning must address leadership, risk management, travel timing and organization, transportation, lodging, partner coordination, communication, meals, entertainment, emergencies, student preparation, wellbeing, and problem support. Financial planning should ensure income meets expenses while accounting for faculty and staff compensation, external services, projects, coordination, tuition, student fees, scholarships, grants, sponsorships, and partner contributions.

Programs may be led by external organizations, faculty, or students. Faculty-led models can rely on student payments, generated revenue, corporate donations, grants, or combinations of these sources. External providers reduce faculty workload but generally increase student costs, potentially limiting participation. Student-led programs are commonly non-credit club activities funded through donations and student activity fees.

No single model suits every program. Faculty should adapt or combine models according to learning objectives, destinations, risks, constraints, and resources. Revenue-generating community engagement and corporate sponsorship can reduce costs, dedicated staff can ease faculty workload, and carefully delegated student responsibilities can support professional development. Sustainable global learning depends on balancing academic quality, operational feasibility, financial viability, institutional support, and equitable access.

This qualitative case study examined how advanced technologies may transform the management and delivery of open and distance education. Four Anadolu University academics with at least 20 years of field experience participated in semi-structured interviews, which were analyzed through content analysis and researcher triangulation.

Participants identified artificial intelligence, blockchain, metaverse, virtual and augmented reality, brain-computer interfaces, and brain chips as influential technologies. Expected educational changes included adaptive learning, personalized and synthetic content, AI teaching assistants, simulations, recognition of prior learning, virtual learning environments, and automated assessment. Managerial effects included improved planning, supervision, decision-making, anomaly detection, reduced hierarchies, horizontal or networked organizational structures, and AI participation at multiple management levels.

The technologies may require substantial initial investment but could later reduce labor, time, errors, and costs while increasing productivity and profits. Participants also anticipated job displacement, especially among entry-level white-collar and technologically unprepared workers, alongside new employment for technologically skilled personnel. They emphasized cost-benefit analysis, accurate and current AI training data, human oversight, and balanced investment in technology and human resources.

Potential sociocultural effects included lifestyle and communication changes, increased screen dependence, reduced physical interaction, virtual addiction, psychological and biological problems, and the emergence of “meta-culture” spanning physical and virtual societies. These developments may require new legal, ethical, and rights frameworks.

The study recommends developing and testing AI assistants and managers, blockchain-based certification and recognition systems, adaptive AI content, metaverse teaching systems and virtual identities, and further research on brain-computer interfaces and brain chips. Larger qualitative and quantitative studies across different institutions, disciplines, and regions are also recommended.

John Bryant, a pro se Sing Sing inmate, sued DOCS, Sing Sing, and Officer Hanser Hernandez under 42 U.S.C. § 1983, alleging constitutional violations arising from a roughly twenty-day prison lockdown prompted by Hernandez’s false ammunition report. Bryant alleged extensive cell confinement, searches, property interference, and denial of services, medical access, recreation, communications, meals, and religious activities. He also challenged inmate compensation and collective-bargaining restrictions, seeking injunctive relief.

The court adopted the magistrate judge’s recommendation and dismissed DOCS and Sing Sing because, as arms of New York State, they are protected by Eleventh Amendment immunity and are not “persons” subject to suit under § 1983. New York had not consented to federal suit, and Congress had not abrogated its immunity. The claim against Hernandez could proceed, subject to proper service, whose status Bryant was ordered to report by June 29, 2001.

Engineers developed a rapid optical flow-cytometry technique to screen the crystalline structure and properties of natural and synthetic proteins, including sequences produced inside living bacteria. Using femto- and picosecond lasers with time-domain thermo-transmission, the method analyzes proteins in milliseconds without significantly heating samples, altering their structure, or killing cells. Proof-of-concept research showed it can identify and separate selected proteins, including variants adapted from water-resistant squid ring teeth proteins. A Defense University Research Instrumentation Program grant will support equipment for higher-throughput screening. The Army Research Office supported the work.

The document describes neural modulation systems and methods, particularly spinal cord stimulation, that use electrode fractionalization and target multipoles to create broad, substantially linear electric fields over neural tissue. A programming system determines anodic and cathodic current distributions across electrodes, including directional, percutaneous, paddle, or multiple leads. Target poles may be progressively stacked away from a center, with outer poles receiving higher fractionalization, to increase and widen the first-order voltage gradient while reducing the second-order gradient.

The approach is intended to preferentially modulate dorsal horn or dorsal root neural elements while minimizing activation of dorsal column fibers. This may provide pain relief with reduced or absent paresthesia, including sub-perception therapy. Modulation may use varied frequencies, pulse patterns, duty cycles, amplitudes, widths, electrode configurations, and current or voltage regulation.

Programming interfaces may allow users to adjust field orientation, focus, length, width, spread, and therapy strength; identify pain areas or draw anatomical target regions; and automatically determine or move target multipoles within an electrode array. Flanking electrodes may shape fields, dampen edge effects, or steer current. Search heuristics and forward/inverse modeling may optimize pole number, position, amplitude, orientation, focus, spread, and electric-field magnitude.

The described systems may include implantable or external waveform generators, leads and electrodes, clinician programmers, remote controls, trial modulators, telemetry, storage, safety controls, and graphical user interfaces. Calibration may account for electrode-tissue coupling and patient perception thresholds. Mathematical models, transfer matrices, objective functions, and least-squares optimization may determine electrode fractionalizations that approximate desired constant-voltage or constant-electric-field distributions.

Players’ children enjoy opportunities to skate. Tomorrow’s game is considered crucial, but the team must focus on execution rather than consequences. The paper proposes a methodology for assessing the probability of failure before e-commerce interactions in digital business ecosystems. A trusting agent evaluates a probable trusted agent against interaction-specific criteria using a FailureLevel scale. Because risk changes over time, analysis divides the relevant period into non-overlapping time slots covering pre- and post-interaction phases. Pre-interaction FailureLevels are derived from relevant past interactions or trustworthy, time-appropriate recommendations, weighted by criterion significance and recency. Post-interaction FailureLevels are predicted from earlier values using a Gaussian distribution, producing probabilities for each failure level. An example compares two logistics agents and demonstrates how predicted levels can support selection. Assessing the consequences of failure, the other component of risk, is left for future work.

Kazakhstan’s education programs sought to expand inclusive schooling and ensure equal, accessible, quality education for students with disabilities. Inclusive education requires responsive systems, equal access, social inclusion, appropriate teacher training, accessible environments, technology, stakeholder cooperation, and curricula tailored to individual needs. COVID-19 forced a broad shift to distance education, creating both technological opportunities and challenges, particularly for students with special needs.

This qualitative case study examined special education teachers’ views of distance education for students with disabilities in Kazakhstan. Ten teachers working with students in grades 5–8 who had hearing, speech, visual, or mild intellectual disabilities participated voluntarily. Data were collected through 30–35-minute online semi-structured interviews and analyzed thematically.

Teachers used online lessons, video sharing, homework, online activities, and mobile applications. Seven preferred formal education, two viewed formal and distance education similarly, and one preferred distance education. Six considered distance education insufficient for meeting students’ individual learning needs, while three found it partly sufficient and one sufficient. Reported barriers to family participation included high anxiety, limited technology, poor communication, and inadequate online family education. Teachers also described teacher–student and peer interaction as weak, time-limited, low-quality, or disorganized.

The study concludes that formal education was generally preferred and that distance education inadequately addressed individual needs and interaction. It recommends diversifying technology-based teaching methods, improving infrastructure, developing individualized learning content, providing online family seminars, and organizing regular technology-supported social activities to strengthen teacher, student, and peer relationships.

The Tax Court considered whether six $3,000 noncharitable gifts made by checks delivered in December 1980, but paid in January 1981, were completed upon delivery. The estate argued that payment related back to delivery, while the Commissioner maintained that the decedent retained control because she could stop payment.

The court declined to apply the relation-back doctrine, previously applied to charitable contributions. The estate failed to prove unconditional delivery, particularly because the checks remained uncashed for 35 days and were presented only when additional checks were delivered. The record also lacked evidence concerning the reason for delay, available account funds, and donative intent.

Under Oklahoma law, delivery of a personal check neither assigns bank funds nor prevents the drawer from stopping payment. Because the donees provided no consideration, they were not holders in due course and could not compel payment if the decedent stopped the checks. Accordingly, the decedent retained dominion and control until the bank paid the checks in January 1981. The gifts were therefore completed in 1981, not 1980.

Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and epilepsy have a bidirectional association involving network hyperexcitability, cognitive impairment, and faster disease progression. This study analyzed transcriptomic data from three AD cohorts and brain regions to examine epilepsy-causing genes in a severe AD subtype characterized by synaptic plasticity dysfunction (SPD).

Of 105 epilepsy-associated genes, 45 were dysregulated in the Knight ADRC cohort, 67 in MSBB, and 41 in ROSMAP. Sixteen were shared across all cohorts; 15 were consistently downregulated, while CERS1 was upregulated. Nine shared genes—ARHGEF9, GABRA1, GABRB3, GABRG2, GRIN2A, HCN1, NECAP1, SCN1A, and SCN8A—were mainly synaptic and highly expressed in neurons. Enrichment analyses identified glutamatergic, GABAergic, dopaminergic, ion-channel, synaptic-transmission, and circadian pathways associated with epilepsy.

In ROSMAP, dysregulation of epilepsy-associated genes was concordant in early and late AD but more pronounced at later stages. Twenty-three genes were downregulated and two, CERS1 and WWOX, were upregulated; GABRG2, HCN1, and PRICKLE1 showed the strongest downregulation. The findings indicate that epilepsy-causing genes are disrupted across AD stages and correlate with disease progression, although whether epilepsy or AD pathology occurs first remains uncertain.

The study concludes that shared genetic and pathophysiological mechanisms may underlie epilepsy and AD, particularly altered synaptic function, neuronal excitability, GABAergic and glutamatergic signaling, sodium channels, and ceramide metabolism. These shared pathways may offer therapeutic targets and support early detection, epilepsy management, phenotype-based stratification, and personalized treatment in AD.
