In his farewell address, the President thanks Congress and the public for their cooperation and service, wishes his successor peace and prosperity, and reflects on America’s global power and responsibility. He argues that national policy must balance security, economic priorities, individual duties, immediate needs, and future welfare.

He warns that the permanent military establishment and arms industry could acquire unwarranted influence and endanger liberties and democratic processes, requiring oversight by an informed citizenry. He also cautions that federal funding could dominate scholarship and that public policy could become captive to a scientific-technological elite.

The President urges Americans not to consume future generations’ resources or jeopardize their democratic inheritance. He advocates disarmament, equal international cooperation, and resolving disputes through reason rather than warfare. Although disappointed that lasting peace remains distant, he notes that war has been avoided and pledges continued private efforts toward peace. He closes by expressing hope for freedom, opportunity, responsibility, relief from poverty, disease, and ignorance, and global peace founded on mutual respect and love.

Amazon received a patent for a delivery drone system that could release selected components during malfunctions or hazardous weather to prevent an uncontrolled crash. A continuously updated “fragmentation sequence” would consider flight conditions, terrain, component cost, weight and drag, directing parts toward safer locations such as water, forests or open fields. Components could be detached using mechanisms including latches, springs, compressed gas or small explosive charges, altering the drone’s descent and trajectory. The patent does not guarantee Amazon will implement the system, but it acknowledges the need to address possible catastrophic drone failures.

This prospective single-site observational study examined genetic variants and plasma cytokines as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers of aggressive cerebral cavernous malformation (CCM), defined by hemorrhage or epilepsy. Among 103 patients, 70 were symptomatic, including 48 with hemorrhage and 22 with seizures without bleeding; 44 had multifocal or familial CCM.

PTPN2 rs72872125 CT and VDR rs7975232 CC genotypes were more frequent among asymptomatic patients. PTPN2 CT was associated with higher IL-10 and lower IL-18 and IFN-γ levels, while carrying a VDR rs7975232 C allele was associated with lower IL-27 and IL-23. A diagnostic model combining PTPN2 rs72872125 CC with plasma GM-CSF distinguished symptomatic from asymptomatic patients with an AUC of 0.663, 41.3% sensitivity, and 85.7% specificity, performing better in familial disease and infratentorial lesions.

Of 42 patients followed for four years, four developed symptomatic events. FCGR2A rs1801274 GG was independently associated with these events and showed AUCs of 0.796 overall and 0.875 after propensity matching. Structural analysis indicated that this variant substitutes arginine for histidine at position 131. VDR rs731236 AA was associated with later symptom onset, whereas VDR rs11568820 CC was associated with earlier onset.

The authors propose that inflammatory and immune mechanisms may influence CCM behavior and that these genetic and cytokine markers warrant further investigation. The study is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture introduces performance and feature improvements across gaming, professional visualization, AI, and data-center workloads. Third-generation Tensor Cores support 2:4 structured sparsity, compressing weights by 2x and doubling effective math throughput while evaluations showed virtually no inference-accuracy loss after pruning and fine-tuning. Enhanced DLSS combines information from multiple frames to improve image quality and performance, enabling ray-traced 8K gaming at 60 fps in supported titles.

GA10x GPUs use GDDR6X memory developed with Micron. Its PAM4 signaling transmits two bits per clock edge and, with Maximum Transition Avoidance encoding and other signal-integrity techniques, supports rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/sec. Error Detection and Replay detects transmission errors during memory overclocking and retries transactions, causing performance to plateau as errors increase.

RTX IO works with Microsoft DirectStorage to enable GPU-based loading and lossless decompression of assets. It can accelerate I/O by up to 100 times over hard drives and traditional storage APIs, reduce CPU utilization, improve frame rates and loading times, and support rapid asset streaming. It also benefits professional workloads involving large rendering, CAD, visualization, and virtual-reality datasets.

The NVIDIA A40 combines second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, PCIe Gen4, 48 GB of memory, virtualization support, and optional 96 GB combined memory through NVLink. It targets visual computing, AI, simulation, rendering, and virtual workstations in data centers. The RTX A6000 similarly provides 48 GB of GDDR6, expandable to 96 GB with NVLink, for large professional datasets and rendering workloads.

Ampere supports DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, including 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz under specified compression or pixel-format requirements. Fifth-generation NVDEC hardware decodes MPEG-2, VC-1, H.264, HEVC, VP8, VP9, and AV1. GA10x is described as the first GPU family with hardware AV1 decoding, supporting playback up to 8K60 HDR with low CPU use. Seventh-generation NVENC provides hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC while reducing CPU demands.

Overall, GA10x offers up to 2x improvements in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. The RTX 3090 includes 24 GB of GDDR6X and targets creators, researchers, developers, and extreme gamers, while the RTX 3070 uses GDDR6 and is described as faster than the RTX 2080 Ti. NVIDIA states that specifications may change and disclaims warranties and liability beyond its applicable terms.

Connecticut municipal advocates asked Gov. Dannel Malloy for relief from state mandates and reforms to control local costs amid a prolonged budget stalemate. COST and CCM proposed changes to municipal pensions, binding arbitration, prevailing-wage thresholds, service-sharing rules and land-transfer fee allocations. Malloy supported easing regulations as towns face potentially reduced aid during an estimated $3.5 billion state deficit. CCM’s Joe DeLong said municipalities were not seeking unchanged aid levels, but Senate President Martin Looney disputed that claim, saying it misrepresented local leaders’ positions. Advocates argued outdated pension contribution rates and wage requirements increase costs and discourage consolidation and inter-town cooperation.

The study developed a teacher education course integrating collaborative inquiry and panoramic cameras to improve TESs’ ability to diagnose student learning problems and design instructional activities. Effective diagnosis requires observing student behavior across teaching activities, linking evidence to learning objectives, and using findings to revise instruction. Collaborative inquiry supports this process through lesson preparation, classroom observation, evidence analysis, post-lesson discussion, and instructional adjustment, while panoramic cameras enable repeated review of student actions, conversations, and worksheets.

From September 2022 to January 2023, 22 TESs completed a five-week preparation stage and four three-week collaborative inquiry cycles in junior high school classrooms. Participants alternated between teaching and observation roles, recorded selected students’ performance, reviewed panoramic footage, discussed learning problems, and revised lesson plans. Diagnostic ability was assessed through 76 observation records, while perceived instructional design capability was measured with a 12-item pre- and post-test questionnaire.

Observation scores increased across the four cycles, from an average of 0.47 in the first cycle to 1.88 out of 2 in the fourth. Initially, TESs focused mainly on teacher behavior and lacked specific evidence about student learning. Guidance emphasizing learning objectives and evidence across multiple activities improved their diagnostic accuracy. Questionnaire results showed statistically significant gains in lesson preparation, connecting student learning with classroom practice, and revising lesson plans after discussion.

The study concludes that the semester-long model was feasible and improved TESs’ diagnostic abilities and perceived instructional design capabilities. Its effectiveness was attributed to collaborative reflection, evidence-based observation, and panoramic video review. However, the study could not determine whether TESs’ proposed instructional strategies effectively resolved student learning problems, partly because of their limited teaching experience.

Social media platforms increasingly use artificial intelligence to moderate hate speech, extremism, misinformation, nudity, and other prohibited content. AI can recognize offensive language, images, and symbols across languages, but its accuracy depends on context and training data. Outdated or biased algorithms have misidentified people, censored legitimate identity terms, and spread human biases embedded in shared datasets.

AI also struggles to determine intent, causing platforms to remove educational, historical, journalistic, or anti-hate content containing otherwise prohibited imagery. Consequently, human moderators remain necessary to verify violations. AI is most effective as an initial screening tool that identifies and prioritizes posts for review, helping moderators work faster and at greater scale. While it has also helped identify suicidal tendencies and prompt emergency responses, experts say fully automated moderation remains distant. The rapid development of moderation technology additionally raises concerns that ethical standards and laws are not keeping pace, potentially increasing demand for expertise in humanities and ethics.

Methane bubbles in shallow muddy aquatic sediments form from microbial decomposition, grow by consuming dissolved methane, displace pore water, and fracture the sediment beyond pore scale. In consolidated cohesive muds, large bubbles behave as Mode I gas-filled cracks governed by Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics (LEFM).

The presented three-dimensional finite-element model couples methane diffusion, gas accumulation, sediment elasticity, and fracture propagation. It begins with a 4 mm penny-shaped bubble seed in a symmetric sediment domain and simulates growth until a mature, closed-tail, inverted teardrop shape develops, indicating the onset of ascent. Dissolved methane transport is modeled with specified concentration and no-flux boundary conditions. Methane entering the bubble obeys conservation, Henry’s law, and the ideal-gas relation, producing internal pressure that elastically expands the cavity against overburden and gravitational stresses.

Fracture growth occurs when the maximum Mode I stress intensity factor exceeds sediment fracture toughness. Local propagation increments vary with the squared ratio of local to maximum stress intensity, with the greatest increment at the bubble head. Mesh deformation, smoothing, and occasional remeshing track the evolving bubble surface. The model is implemented in COMSOL Multiphysics using coupled solute-transport and force-equilibrium equations with refined meshes near the bubble.

Simulations use conditions representative of Eckernförde Bay. Validation against analytical solutions across varying fracture toughness shows good agreement in mature bubble shape, size, and opening. Lower fracture toughness produces smaller, flatter bubbles, while higher toughness produces larger, more inflated bubbles. The model applies only to individual bubbles; upscaling bubble characteristics to the effective properties of gassy mud remains undeveloped but is needed for acoustic applications, geohazard assessment, and methane-flux estimates.

The disclosure describes computer-based systems and methods for orthodontic treatment planning and appliance manufacturing. Patient tooth positions, movement constraints, and malocclusions are measured to generate and evaluate multiple branched treatment plans. Plans may address open bite, crossbite, protrusion, molar and canine class relationships, overjet, extractions, spacing, and interproximal reduction through successive interim tooth positions. A dental professional selects a plan, after which movement stages, appliance models, and fabrication instructions are generated. Patient-removable appliances progressively reposition teeth and may incorporate attachments or auxiliary components. Appliances can be fabricated directly through additive or subtractive manufacturing, indirectly by thermoforming, or through combined techniques using various rigid and elastic materials. Data processing systems, scanners, simulation tools, and remote fabrication equipment may support treatment design, force modeling, appliance geometry selection, manufacturing, and post-processing.

Users may not modify, reverse engineer, decompile, rent, embed, disclose, or separate the software. Permitted copies must remain unmodified and retain notices and the agreement.
