At September 30, Tesla had $29.26 billion in assets, $23.41 billion in liabilities, $4.51 billion in stockholders’ equity, and $2.97 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Nine-month operating activities generated $863.2 million, investing activities used $1.97 billion, and financing activities generated $686.1 million. Total debt principal was $10.90 billion.

Tesla adopted ASC 606 on January 1, 2018, changing revenue recognition for certain vehicle sales with resale guarantees and reducing opening accumulated deficit by $623.2 million. The adoption increased reported nine-month net income by $216.5 million relative to prior accounting.

Tesla operates automotive and energy generation and storage segments. Third-quarter automotive revenue was $6.10 billion, energy generation and storage revenue was $399.3 million, and services and other revenue was $326.3 million. Inventory totaled $3.31 billion, property and equipment totaled $11.25 billion, and customer deposits totaled $905.8 million.

Tesla remained dependent on largely single-source suppliers and reported compliance with all financial debt covenants. As of October 26, 2018, 171,732,775 common shares were outstanding.

Diana Containerships reported a quarterly loss of $0.66 per share, beating the $0.77 loss estimate, while revenue of $5.40 million missed the $7.50 million estimate and fell 63.8% year over year. Renaissance Technologies increased its stake by 94.4% to 231,485 shares. Zacks upgraded the stock from “sell” to “hold.” The company owns containerships and operates them through subsidiary UOT.

The President reports that the United States remains stable, prosperous, peaceful, and neutral amid foreign conflicts. Relations with Great Britain, France, Mexico, Brazil, and most European and American states are generally amicable. He describes efforts to uphold neutrality by halting aid to a German warship, suppressing an expedition against Cuba, and avoiding involvement in European wars. He urges settlement of claims against Portugal and Venezuela, stronger laws against abduction and the African slave trade, and continued support for independent nations and friendly relations throughout the Americas.

He advocates internationally protected, equally accessible transportation routes across Central America, including a proposed Nicaragua canal and crossings at Panama and Tehuantepec. He also supports the independence of the Sandwich Islands.

Treasury figures show receipts of about $59.7 million and expenditures of $57.6 million, with a projected two-year deficit of about $16.4 million stemming from the Mexican War and territorial acquisitions. He recommends borrowing to cover the deficit, strict economy, tariff revision using specific duties to increase revenue and encourage domestic industry, and possible modification of the subtreasury system.

For California, New Mexico, and Oregon, he recommends civil organization, favorable consideration of California statehood, avoidance of sectional disputes, improved customs and postal services, coastal surveys, lighthouses, expanded Indian agencies, a California branch mint, land-title commissions, public-land surveys, mineral exploration, and liberal land policies. He proposes surveying possible routes for a transcontinental railroad before deciding whether government support is appropriate.

Additional recommendations include an agricultural bureau, continued river and harbor improvements, expansion of western military forces, retirement systems for disabled Army and Navy personnel, naval reorganization, improved Pacific mail service, uniform five-cent letter postage, legislation for the Seventh Census, and attention to Washington, D.C.

The President emphasizes that Congress holds legislative authority, while the Executive may recommend but not dictate policy. He promises limited use of the veto, urges each branch to remain within its constitutional sphere, and identifies preservation of the Union as essential to national liberty and future prosperity.

The AMD Geode CS5535 Revision A3 errata lists defects affecting clocks, DMA, UART, LPC, PCI, IDE, USB, ACPI, interrupts, SMB, GPIO, power management, and timing. Detailed issues include PIT behavior deviations, a system-hanging GLIU debug port, incorrect PIT mode 3 loading, duplicate interrupts with PIC auto-EOI, improper DMA priority rotation, thermal-alarm standby recovery limitations, and Sleep Clock dependencies. Recommended mitigations include completing PIT latch commands before read-back, avoiding the debug port and unsupported PIT behavior, and enabling Sleep Clock in the PMC when related sleep options are used.

Roanoke College transformed wood from its historic, storm-damaged Bittle tulip poplar into the Bittle Tree of Life Cross for Antrim Chapel during its 175th anniversary year. Designed by Reverend Chris Bowen and retired professor George Arthur, the cross symbolizes the College’s roots in founder David Bittle’s vision and the future growth of its students.

This French retrospective study evaluated COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) in hospitalized patients with hematological malignancies. From May 2020 to April 2021, 112 patients received four high-titer CCP units; 83 had B-cell lymphoid neoplasms, 19 multiple myeloma, and 10 myeloid neoplasms. Most were seronegative at transfusion, and 72% had previously received anti-CD20 or anti-CD19 therapy.

By day 7, CCP transfusion was associated with reduced temperature, C-reactive protein, ferritin, and fibrinogen, alongside increased PCR cycle-threshold values. Reported adverse events were three allergic reactions and two transient increases in oxygen requirement. Overall 90-day survival was 64.9%, including 77.5% for B-cell lymphoid neoplasms, 36.8% for plasma-cell neoplasms, and 20% for myeloid neoplasms. Older age, hypertension, and severe COVID-19 independently predicted lower survival, while previous B-cell-depleting therapy was associated with better survival among CCP recipients.

A propensity-score comparison of CCP-treated and untreated patients with B-cell neoplasms sought to address indication and immortal-time biases. In the main analysis of 147 anti-CD20-pretreated patients alive 16 days after hospitalization, CCP was associated with a 63% reduction in the risk of death; sensitivity analyses estimated reductions of 40%–63%.

The authors conclude that CCP may benefit patients with B-cell lymphoid malignancies, particularly those previously treated with anti-CD20 antibodies and unable to mount a humoral response. Limitations include the retrospective, nonrandomized design, differences between cohorts, lack of viral-strain data, and limited applicability to later variants. Confirmation in a randomized prospective trial is needed.

Welsh abuse survivors May Baxter-Thornton and Emma Lewis have joined IICSA’s victims and survivors panel. They will advise on engaging Welsh survivors, represent their experiences and help improve child protection. The inquiry has operated in Wales since November 2016, meeting survivors and experts across several locations.
The Louisiana Supreme Court granted review in Robert Daniel Chappuis v. Sears Roebuck & Co., ordering the Court of Appeal to provide the case record and notify counsel.

Steve Yzerman and coach Jon Cooper describe the Tampa Bay Lightning’s rise without a fixed timeline, emphasizing drafting, patient player development, strong character and limited reliance on trades or free agency. They credit the organization’s scouts, development staff, veterans and stable ownership, along with foundational players Steven Stamkos and Victor Hedman. Cooper says young players such as Tyler Johnson, Ondrej Palat and Nikita Kucherov benefited from developing together in the minors and learning through adversity. Both highlight Stamkos’s growth into a selfless, well-rounded captain and the team’s resilience throughout the playoffs. Yzerman adds that sustained success and attracting free agents require a credible, winning program, while his playoff role is mainly to support the coaches and players.

Electric Resistance Welding (ERW) pipes transport petroleum, gas, vapor, and liquids under varying pressures. Produced efficiently from hot-rolled coil, they offer low cost, material savings, consistent wall thickness, and controlled burr removal. Meeting API or GB/T9711.1 standards, ERW pipes are widely used in industry and urban gas networks.

Beth Utton argues that health care is a human right and supports Medicare for all as a less costly, care-focused alternative to profit-driven private insurance. Bonnie New criticizes a headline and settlement concerning a teenager killed by police, emphasizing that the teen was driving a stolen car toward an officer. She argues the officer acted in self-defense and calls for greater respect for police.

The March 28, 2001 media digest highlights Enron and energy-market developments. Viacom abandoned plans to split off Blockbuster after improved market share, revenue and cash generation. President Bush nominated Patrick Wood and Nora Brownell to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission amid debate over intervention in California’s electricity crisis.

Enron awarded Chairman Kenneth Lay a $7 million bonus for strong 2000 performance. CEO Jeffrey Skilling projected 2001 revenue of $160–170 billion, supported California’s electricity rate increase as a step toward reducing shortages, and said Texas was better prepared for deregulation. Texas companies were recruiting customers for a June pilot program ahead of full deregulation in January.

Enron submitted plans for a large LNG-fired power plant and terminal in northern Japan, targeting construction in 2004 and operations from 2007. It also planned an Indian wind-power subsidiary but withdrew from bidding for a stake in Karnataka’s Vijayanagar project, citing the power sector’s lack of economic viability. Enron held a stake in a project intended to supply Qatari gas to the United Arab Emirates.

Other reports covered India’s proposed restrictions on state borrowing from multilateral agencies, criticism of California electricity rate increases, Britain’s new electricity-trading system, and efforts by U.S. companies to expand private export financing through the Export-Import Bank.

Deloitte found growing consumer confidence in autonomous vehicles: 49% considered them unsafe, down from 73% the previous year. Brand trust influenced confidence, with 51% trusting traditional carmakers to implement the technology versus 21% trusting technology companies. Consumers remained reluctant toward electric vehicles, citing range, price and charging infrastructure, though 37% were attracted by lower running costs. Customer service also remained important, while the UK government continued investigating autonomous vehicle safety.

New Jersey Governor Chris Christie signed legislation strengthening protections for people with developmental disabilities and increasing family involvement in care. Prompted by Stephen Komninos’ 2007 death in a group home, the law permits twice-yearly unannounced inspections, requires rapid injury notification to guardians, and mandates family meetings at least twice annually.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for identifying audio content through a networked playback device. While playing received digital audio through wired speakers, the playback device sends part of the audio data to an identification system, receives associated information or metadata, and forwards it to a control device. This approach can identify content when metadata is absent without requiring the control device to capture and digitize played audio through a microphone.

A control device may command identification during playback, receive the results, retrieve additional metadata from a specified network location, and display information such as track, artist, album, or release date. Identification may occur periodically, after detected discontinuities, or when existing metadata lacks a category. The playback device may decode audio, convert sample rates, select data from different processing stages, or isolate frequency ranges to meet identification-system requirements.

The described operating environment includes networked playback devices, controllers, audio sources, playback zones, synchronized groups, queues, and wired or wireless interfaces. Playback devices may be paired, consolidated, or dynamically grouped across rooms and can obtain content from local storage, line-in connections, other network devices, or Internet services. Implementations may use processors, circuitry, firmware, software, and non-transitory computer-readable media.

The Browns are considering Baker Mayfield alongside Sam Darnold, Josh Allen and Josh Rosen for the No. 1 NFL draft pick. General manager John Dorsey said accuracy, arm strength and winning are key criteria. Mayfield won the 2017 Heisman after throwing for 4,627 yards and 43 touchdowns.

Jefferies raised Ferguson Plc’s price target from GBX 5,170 to GBX 5,240 while maintaining a hold rating. Other analysts set targets ranging from GBX 4,700 to GBX 5,600. Three analysts rate the stock hold and four rate it buy, producing an average buy rating and GBX 5,265.71 target. Shares rose 0.68% to GBX 5,200, valuing the plumbing, heating and building-materials distributor at GBX 13.17 billion.

The presidential election cycle theory holds that U.S. stock market performance follows a four-year pattern linked to presidential terms, though the passage presents differing descriptions of which years perform best. Yale Hirsch’s research identifies the pre-election year as strongest and the election year as second strongest, while midterm years tend to be weak until the fourth quarter and experience greater volatility.

Since 1952, the S&P 500 averaged a 12.5% gain in election years with an incumbent seeking reelection, compared with 6.7% across all election years and a 1.5% loss in open-field elections. Historical analysis also found below-average stock and bond returns before presidential elections, while stocks often performed better following midterms. Political party control generally did not predict broad market performance.

Election-related uncertainty can particularly affect healthcare, energy, and trade-sensitive sectors because policy depends on both the president and Congress. Major economic shocks can disrupt historical patterns, and the theory does not reliably predict every cycle. The passage recommends monitoring policy effects, remaining invested, and maintaining a rebalanced portfolio rather than reacting broadly to election volatility.

The disclosure describes thin directional illumination and display systems for 2D, autostereoscopic 3D, multi-user, and privacy applications. Unlike spatially multiplexed displays, which can suffer reduced resolution, flicker, and crosstalk, time-multiplexed systems direct full-resolution sequential images into separate viewing windows.

The proposed display combines an array of light sources, an imaging directional waveguide, a transmissive spatial light modulator, polarisers, and passive or switchable retarders. A stepped waveguide guides light toward a reflective end, then extracts the returning light through angled features. Different source positions produce corresponding output directions and viewing windows. Curved extraction features or reflective ends may provide optical power, while source control permits observer tracking, stereoscopic viewing, separate images for multiple viewers, and restricted privacy viewing.

Additional polarisers and retarders—including crossed A-plates, C-plates, O-plates, and switchable liquid-crystal retarders—control off-axis luminance. These components can reduce image visibility to off-axis observers while substantially preserving head-on brightness and enabling switching between narrow privacy and wide-angle modes. Correcting passive retarders may limit color variation, and independently addressable or patterned regions may provide different privacy levels or camouflage effects.

A control system may synchronize the light sources, spatial light modulator, and retarder voltage; adjust privacy according to observer or snooper location; and temporally display secondary images that obscure stray-light versions of the primary image. Applications include automotive displays designed to reduce reflections in windows or windscreens. The disclosure also covers related non-directional backlights, reflective polarisation-recycling structures, multiple retarder layers, and combinations intended to improve efficiency, privacy, viewing freedom, resolution, and device thinness.

Intel’s Management Engine (ME) is a closed-source microcontroller embedded in many Intel CPUs, connected to storage, networking, and other peripherals, and active even when the computer is off. Originating alongside technologies such as TPM and Active Management Technology, it runs Minix and supports remote management functions.

Researchers Mark Ermolov and Maxim Goryachy demonstrated a local exploit at BlackHat Europe that enables arbitrary code execution on ME versions above 11 through physical access and a USB device. Although the exploit does not work remotely and excludes Macs, the passage warns that other vulnerabilities may affect earlier versions.

Intel provides a tool to detect ME, while System76, Dell, and some manufacturers offer systems, firmware, or instructions to disable it. No universal method exists because implementations vary, and removing valid firmware causes shutdown after 30 minutes. The me_cleaner tool instead disables most ME functionality while preserving computer operation. The passage characterizes the current physical-access threat as limited but argues that ME’s privileged access and unauditable code create significant security concerns, particularly if a remote exploit is eventually developed.

This literature review analyzes Christian and global education management through Mortimer J. Adler’s perennialism and posthumanism, using Adler’s works and recent studies on philosophy, Christian education, and educational management. Adler emphasizes enduring values, rational development, democracy, freedom, and education beyond employment preparation. His concept of docility means temporarily suspending judgment before trusted educational authority while retaining critical thought, skepticism, and intellectual responsibility.

The study presents posthumanism as an unfinished, context-dependent critique of human supremacy and explores human dependence on technology and ecosystems. It also reviews Christian educational management involving family health, spirituality, moral and character education, cross-cultural learning, business ethics, institutional transformation, and disaster resilience.

The researchers argue that education should empower women, avoid blaming or treating children as incomplete adults, and hold teachers, parents, and governments responsible for educational failures. Educational management should extend beyond administration and immediate achievement to cultivate timeless values, conscience, critical reflection, and learners’ sustained intellectual development.

VentureWire People’s May 30, 2001 newsletter reports executive appointments across technology and venture-backed companies. Major changes include Robert de Monts becoming Solsoft chairman and CEO; David Morgan leaving Real Media to launch an audience-data software company; Jo Anne Heywood Miller becoming Gluon Networks president and CEO; and new presidents at InfoImage, QED Solutions, and Corechange. Additional appointments span venture capital, business development, sales, marketing, operations, finance, product development, and human resources at firms including Partech, BitFlash, Riptech, PurpleYogi, OptiMight, CryoCor, OutStart, NetByTel, and Converge.

The newsletter also lists executive searches for senior analytics, marketing, advertising sales, product management, engineering, finance, sales, online learning, and venture-capital roles in the United States and Europe. Proteus of Washington is seeking its first vice president of sales and marketing to build and lead its sales team.

Nicola Sturgeon called Theresa May’s 8 June snap election an extraordinary U-turn and political miscalculation designed to exploit Labour’s disarray, increase the Conservative majority, pursue a hard Brexit and deepen cuts. She said Scotland should reject the Conservatives and reinforce the mandate for another independence referendum. SNP deputy leader Angus Robertson framed the election as a choice between the SNP and Tories. Scottish Conservative leader Ruth Davidson said a Tory vote would support strong Brexit leadership and oppose a second referendum.

Genworth Financial shares fell 0.37%, closing at $2.70. Two analysts set a 12-month consensus target of $3, while five recommendations rated the stock Hold. Its 14-period ATR was 0.1, with weekly volatility of 2.81% and monthly volatility of 3.58%. RSI stood at 42.86. Genworth had a $1.39 billion market capitalization and 515.35 million outstanding shares. Previous trading volume was 2.14 million shares, below the 3.43 million average.

President Rutherford B. Hayes proclaimed that domestic violence obstructing laws along West Virginia’s Baltimore and Ohio Railroad must cease. Citing the governor’s request and constitutional authority, Hayes warned against aiding the unrest and ordered participants to disperse peacefully by noon on July 19, 1877.

Ed Sachse, 56, is president of property services at Kennedy Wilson, overseeing brokers and 21 million square feet of U.S. commercial and residential properties. He began as a teenager running a window-washing business in Detroit, then studied accounting at Michigan State University and worked for Arthur Andersen. After moving to Los Angeles, he joined Douglas Emmett and became chief financial officer of Camden Financial.

Wanting to make deals, Sachse became a commercial property broker at Coldwell Banker. An early success selling an empty school to the Simon Wiesenthal Center helped launch his brokerage career. After improving operations at a client’s strip mall, he founded his own property management and brokerage company in 1993.

In 2001, Sachse was diagnosed with stage 4 non-Hodgkin lymphoma. He continued working through six years of treatment, including a bone marrow transplant and two stem cell transplants. The Great Recession later forced his company to cut staff. Seeking new business, he approached Kennedy Wilson in 2009; the firm instead offered to acquire his company, and he accepted.

Sachse lives in Pacific Palisades with his wife, Julie, and has two grown children. He enjoys hockey and playing guitar in a garage band.

Venezuelan Temporary Protected Status holders asked the Supreme Court to preserve a federal judge’s ruling blocking the Trump administration from ending their protections. DHS Secretary Kristi Noem terminated Venezuela’s 2023 TPS designation and its extension through October 2026. Challengers argued that she lacked statutory authority and acted partly from racial animus.

U.S. District Judge Edward Chen initially blocked the termination, but the Supreme Court paused that preliminary order in May. Chen later issued a final ruling that Noem had acted unlawfully, and the lower courts declined to stay it. The administration returned to the Supreme Court, arguing that those courts disregarded the justices’ prior order. The challengers responded that the earlier stay applied only to preliminary relief, while Chen’s final judgment relied on different statutory authority, a more developed record, and a new claim.

Sheffield Lord Mayor Magid Magid called Donald Trump a “wasteman,” declared him banned from the city and named July 13 Mexico Solidarity Day ahead of the US president’s visit. Wearing a sombrero and an anti-Trump T-shirt, Magid said he wanted to show solidarity with Mexicans and criticized Trump’s Muslim ban, withdrawal from the Paris climate agreement, embassy move to Jerusalem, detention of children at borders and defense of white supremacists. The 28-year-old Somali-born Green Party politician is Sheffield’s youngest Lord Mayor. He also criticized Theresa May for welcoming Trump and said Sheffield celebrates its differences.

The invention improves the field of view and wavelength range of optical waveguide displays. Conventional waveguides use diffractive gratings to inject image-bearing light for propagation by total internal reflection, but their acceptance angles vary with wavelength, causing light outside permitted angles to escape and reducing the field of view, particularly for colors other than the grating’s tuned wavelength.

The proposed apparatus coats external waveguide surfaces responsible for internal reflection with a positive-index material, preferably a metamaterial, having a refractive index substantially equal to or below 1.0 at optical wavelengths. This lowers the critical angle for total internal reflection, allowing a wider range of incident angles and wavelengths to remain guided. An input diffractive part directs display light into the waveguide, while an optically coupled output diffractive part releases it for viewing. Conjugated input and output gratings may reduce geometric distortion and chromatic dispersion.

Preferred metamaterials include periodic conductive mesh structures containing magnetic resonators, or arrays of parallel conductive nanowires. Their geometry can be optimized to produce refractive-index values between approximately zero and one. The coating may also protect waveguide surfaces and exposed gratings from damage and contamination while optically mimicking air when its index is approximately one.

The design can be applied to multilayer waveguides having separate gratings tuned to different colors. Intermediate metamaterial layers may bind and protect component waveguides while improving total internal reflection, and outer protective layers may provide strength, shock absorption, rigidity, or scratch resistance. Coating may be omitted over input and output regions, or windows may be formed, to reduce attenuation by the metamaterial.

The MSPM0C1105/1106 CPU subsystem uses a 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0+ running up to 32 MHz, with instruction prefetch, a two-line cache, 24-bit SysTick, and an NVIC with four priority levels. Five power modes—RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN—use two power domains to balance performance and consumption. SHUTDOWN disables both domains and permits limited wake sources.

The PMU supplies and supervises core power, while the clock module provides internal and external low- and high-frequency oscillators and distributes clocks to the processor and peripherals. DMA supports two full-feature channels and one basic channel, transfers up to 64K elements, peripheral triggers, channel cascading, stride, gather, and ping-pong buffering. An event manager routes interrupts, DMA triggers, and peripheral-to-peripheral events.

Flash supports 1KB sectors, with selected regions rated for up to 100,000 program/erase cycles. SRAM offers zero-wait-state access, 1KB-resolution write protection, retention through STANDBY, and loss in SHUTDOWN. Up to 45 GPIO pins are supported, including wake, FastWake, filtering, and configurable IOMUX functions.

Analog capabilities include a 12-bit ADC operating at up to 1.6 Msps with internal temperature, supply-monitoring, and signal-chain channels; selectable 1.4V or 2.5V references; external reference support; a calibrated temperature sensor; and a comparator with wake and timer-fault integration. Security features include code and data firewalls and CRC-16.

Communication peripherals include three UARTs with LIN support, I2C supporting rates through 1 Mbps and SMBus 3.0, and SPI supporting up to 16 Mbit/s. Independent and windowed watchdog timers supervise execution. The RTC provides calendar, alarm, periodic interrupt, calibration, and temperature-drift compensation functions. General-purpose and advanced 16-bit timers support prescaling, triggering, synchronization, PWM, capture/compare, encoder input, and fault handling.

Debugging uses a two-wire Arm SWD interface with configurable peripheral behavior, mailbox communication, lockout, and password authentication. Factory memory contains read-only device identification, capabilities, and calibration data.

Recommended application connections include 10µF and 0.1µF VDD decoupling capacitors, a 47kΩ NRST pullup with a 1000pF capacitor, crystal capacitors where applicable, and pullups for 5V-tolerant open-drain outputs. TI distinguishes experimental “X” devices from qualified “MSP” production devices and advises using only qualified devices in production.

La-Z-Boy outperforms Stanley Furniture on 12 of 14 compared factors. It has higher revenue, earnings, profitability, institutional ownership and analyst upside, while paying a $0.44 annual dividend yielding 1.6%. Stanley Furniture has a lower price-to-earnings ratio, greater insider ownership and lower volatility but reports negative earnings and margins and pays no dividend. La-Z-Boy manufactures and retails residential furniture through multiple brands and an extensive store network. Stanley Furniture designs, markets and sources wood residential furniture, primarily from Southeast Asia, selling through retailers and interior designers worldwide.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said AI-generated video feels more lifelike and emotionally resonant than still images, prompting intellectual property holders to seek stronger restrictions. Following viral unauthorized Sora videos featuring characters such as SpongeBob and Pikachu, Altman announced plans to give rights holders more granular control over character generation. He said most rights holders are interested in participating but want guardrails, and predicted they may eventually push for their content to appear in more AI videos to strengthen fan connections.

Scientists are progressing toward understanding and manipulating human memories. Research on “face cells” and the learning-related protein CREB suggests that activating specific neurons before learning could determine where memories are stored. Memory reconsolidation during recall may provide an opportunity to alter or implant memories. MIT researchers led by Dr. Susumu Tonegawa created an artificial association between a harmless situation and fear, then later reversed a negative reaction into a positive one, approaching the possibility of implanting and erasing memories.

The paper presents a real-time face anonymization system for AI-supported scientific education that protects student identities while preserving visible instruments, hand movements, and experimental procedures. It combines BOTSort tracking and Gaussian blurring with MSFF-YOLOv8, an enhanced YOLOv8 architecture that improves multi-scale feature fusion and small-object detection. Contour-Adaptive Occlusion Refinement (CAOR), applied during training-data preparation, expands instrument–face boundaries toward the face center to reduce accidental blurring of occluding equipment.

The authors created a dataset from 51 experimental videos, including 1,049 annotated images and labels for faces, instruments, and operator poses. Performance was measured using processing speed, Sensitive Object Blur Accuracy, and Over Blur Rate. MSFF-YOLOv8 with CAOR at 1920-pixel input achieved 0.9602 accuracy and 0.0159 over-blur rate on the full dataset, while processing 1080p video at 22.67 frames per second. It outperformed original YOLOv8, SAM, and Edge-SAM, including on heavily occluded videos. Further research is needed to improve precise edge classification during real-time inference.

After a minor scratch, the author developed sepsis, spent three months in a coma and a year recovering. Sepsis affects more than 30 million people annually, kills about 6 million, and leaves 40% of survivors with lasting symptoms. It occurs when the body’s response to infection becomes uncontrolled, rapidly causing organ failure. Warning signs include pale or mottled skin, severe breathlessness, shivering or muscle pain, lack of urination, nausea and vomiting; emergency services should be contacted immediately. There is no specific cure, though antibiotics may treat the original infection and research into metformin and gene therapy appears promising. Public and professional awareness remains limited, while diagnosis is difficult. In the short term, greater recognition of symptoms and protocols such as Sepsis6 could save lives and reduce harm.

The speaker dismisses outside perceptions, emphasizing that the team earned its Stanley Cup opportunity by defeating three strong opponents. He calls Mike Peca hockey’s best all-around player, joking about their linemates. The team’s success is attributed to a physical style and large, strong, mobile forwards who forecheck effectively. The long break allowed players to relax before rebuilding focus in Dallas. Despite lacking Stanley Cup experience, the team gained confidence by overcoming adversity in earlier rounds and expects to respond well without being unusually nervous.

SD Memory Cards provide secure, high-capacity storage for consumer audio and video devices, using mutual authentication, encryption, and optional standards-based security while allowing non-secure user-content access. SDIO Cards add low-power, high-speed I/O and optional storage while maintaining SD compatibility and safe behavior in unsupported hosts. Communication uses a low-voltage 9-pin interface operating up to 208 MHz.

A trade deficit shifts demand abroad, potentially increasing U.S. unemployment unless offset by budget deficits or asset bubbles. The dollar’s reserve status does not require trade deficits, since other reserve-currency economies avoid them. China and South Korea accumulate dollars partly to keep their currencies competitive, a policy the author says could be challenged. The passage also disputes criticism of China’s technology-transfer requirements, arguing that U.S. companies voluntarily accept these conditions to access China’s market and are capable of protecting their own interests.

The lecture reviews renewal theory and applies it to countable-state Markov chains. The strong law for renewals gives an almost-sure long-run renewal rate of \(1/\bar{x}\), while the elementary renewal theorem gives the same rate in expectation. Blackwell’s theorem provides finer asymptotic behavior: for an arithmetic renewal process with span \(\lambda\), the probability of a renewal at a sufficiently large allowable time approaches \(\lambda/\bar{x}\). In the non-arithmetic case, expected renewals over an interval of fixed length \(\delta\), divided by \(\delta\), approach \(1/\bar{x}\); the order of limits in \(t\) and \(\delta\) cannot be interchanged.

For an arithmetic renewal process, the joint limiting distribution of age \(Z(t)\) and duration \(\widetilde X(t)\) is determined by the inter-renewal distribution. The limiting duration distribution is size-biased:
\[
P(\widetilde X=k)\to \frac{kP(X=k)}{\bar{x}},
\]
so its expected value is \(E[X^2]/E[X]\). The limiting age distribution is based on the complementary distribution of \(X\), and its expected value differs from the continuous-time sample-path average because age can be zero at integer observation times.

Countable-state Markov chains can behave differently from finite-state chains. In a two-sided random walk, probabilities spread across states as time grows, so each individual state’s probability approaches zero and no steady-state probability distribution exists. With equal upward and downward probabilities, return to the starting state occurs with probability one despite zero limiting state probability. A birth-death chain on nonnegative integers remains concentrated near zero when downward drift dominates, escapes toward infinity when upward drift dominates, and returns with probability one but lacks a steady-state distribution in the balanced case.

Recurrence is defined by eventual return to a state with probability one. First-passage probabilities \(f_{ij}(n)\) describe reaching state \(j\) for the first time at step \(n\), and their cumulative limit determines whether eventual passage is certain. Returns to a recurrent state form a renewal process. Communicating states are either all recurrent or all transient. A recurrent state may have finite or infinite expected return time; finite mean permits positive steady-state probability, while infinite mean yields zero state probability and no steady-state distribution.

In HS mode, codes are read individually. The ADS7828 holds the clock LOW after receiving the read-address byte until conversion completes. A repeated START after reading keeps the device in HS mode, while a STOP returns it to F/S mode.

JD Wetherspoon plans a 1,600sq-metre Dublin city-centre gastropub linking a former bank and Baptist chapel on Lower Abbey Street. A full drinks and restaurant licence was granted, subject to planning permission, with opening expected between 2019 and 2022. The chain, known for cheap deals, has raised drink prices in recent years.

The passage presents a mean-reversion strategy for QQQ using the two-day Relative Strength Index, entering when RSI(2) is below 10 and exiting when the closing price exceeds the previous day’s high. The strategy returned 10.01% versus 6.39% for buy-and-hold and performed well during four bear markets. Lowering the entry threshold to 5 increased average gains but reduced total returns because of fewer trades. Adding a second, unspecified indicator improved results: approximately 12.7% CAGR, 14% market exposure, 232 trades, 75% winners, a profit factor near 3, 19.5% maximum drawdown, and a 2.85 Sharpe ratio.

This September 2022 ebook edition of *Foreign Relations, 1981–1988, Volume I* provides searchable, portable, offline access while preserving the printed edition’s content. Document numbers are recommended for citations. The *Foreign Relations of the United States* series documents major U.S. foreign policy decisions and diplomatic activity under statutory standards of comprehensiveness, accuracy, objectivity, and timely publication. Relevant government entities must provide records, most of which are declassified and available at the National Archives.

The BGF China Flexible Equity Fund provides access to both onshore and offshore Chinese equities through one strategy. Managed by Helen Zhu and supported by 10 China-focused analysts, it holds 20–50 companies selected from over 4,300 stocks. Its flexible, long-only, fundamentals-driven approach invests across markets, sectors, company sizes and factors to exploit valuation differences, market cycles and sector opportunities.

Brad Vis will again represent the Conservatives in Mission-Matsqui-Fraser Canyon after narrowly losing to Liberal Jati Sidhu in 2015. Vis criticized Liberal spending and highlighted challenges facing seniors and young homebuyers. Conservatives plan outreach across the sprawling riding before next year’s election.

An Alberta Education survey of nearly 10,000 respondents, half teachers, found support for emphasizing practical skills, literacy and numeracy in a planned K-12 curriculum overhaul. Most believed draft plans promoted basic skills, critical thinking and student success, though some misunderstood the high-level documents. Social studies drew strong debate, including concerns about political viewpoints, civic literacy, Indigenous content, global history and active citizenship. Other respondents questioned social justice in music and cultural perspectives in math. Alberta Teachers’ Association president Greg Jeffery said curriculum development was progressing well but emphasized careful implementation and teacher preparation. The government aims to complete the K-4 curriculum by December and higher grades by 2022, but has not announced when it will enter classrooms.

A data-driven culture aligns organizations vertically by connecting individual and group objectives to company goals, and horizontally through shared data models and transparent access that support collaboration. Digital leaders emphasize learning, data transparency, clear metrics, and consistency among leadership beliefs, company values, and employee behavior. Digital laggards often struggle to translate stated ambitions into practice because of entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient leadership focus. Changing mindsets and behaviors is often the hardest part of digital transformation and requires compelling, well-understood reasons.

Technologically mature firms demonstrate stronger data cultures by promoting learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement in both values and daily practices. Organizations generally fall into four patterns: data novices lack supporting culture and systems; insight-ready organizations encourage experimentation but lack analytical capabilities; tech-enabled organizations possess technology but discourage risk-taking; and data-reliant organizations may depend on data so heavily that critical thinking suffers. Each can build on existing strengths and target specific improvements.

The study examined Turkish tour-guiding students’ perceptions of emergency distance education (EDE), introduced during Covid-19 as a temporary transfer of face-to-face teaching online. Using a qualitative phenomenological design, researchers collected questionnaire and semi-structured interview data from 81 students enrolled in face-to-face programs at three Istanbul universities during 2022–2023. Thematic content analysis identified perceptions of both educational modes, EDE’s sufficiency, practical adequacy, advantages, disadvantages, and differences from face-to-face education.

Students generally considered EDE insufficient for tour-guiding education because of inadequate vocational practice, limited communication, and motivation problems. Most viewed distance education as unsuitable for developing field experience, public speaking, body language, foreign-language use, and interpersonal skills. Reported disadvantages included technical problems, low attendance, reduced concentration, weak socialization, and predominantly one-way communication.

Nevertheless, students recognized advantages such as effective time management, access from any location, lower costs, recorded lessons, opportunities to repeat material, and easier access to resources. Most reported understanding distance courses, with associate-degree students indicating higher comprehension than undergraduates. However, 59.2% considered distance education practically inadequate, and 81.4% perceived clear differences between distance and face-to-face education. Face-to-face teaching was preferred for its efficiency, interaction, socialization, concentration, and opportunities for self-expression.

The findings reveal a dilemma: students valued EDE’s convenience and flexibility but preferred face-to-face education for practical and communication-based learning. The study suggests that hybrid approaches, stronger communication systems, and practice-oriented online activities could improve distance tour-guiding education. Its findings are limited to EDE experiences among tour-guiding students in Türkiye and have restricted generalizability because of the exploratory qualitative design.

The speaker felt personally strong but acknowledged that the Devils outplayed and outskated his team, especially in the second period. He credited Jeff Friesen’s patience, speed and scoring moves while explaining that traffic and rebounds limited his ability to stop the goals. He said the defeat was unrelated to time off and emphasized that his team must use its speed, shoot more, create traffic, match the Devils’ intensity and improve collectively. Despite the Devils’ greater experience, he viewed the loss as a learning opportunity and urged his team to respond in the next game without excuses. He also praised Patrick as possibly the greatest goaltender and said any decision he makes must be respected.

This study examined relationships between multilingual learning and cultural awareness among Indonesian university students using an embedded mixed-methods design. Quantitative survey data came from 388 randomly selected students across six universities, while qualitative data involved 60 participants. Variables covered multilingual competence, learning processes, psychological factors, social interaction, cultural knowledge, cultural participation, sociocultural context, and attitudes toward cultural learning.

Participants represented diverse ethnic and linguistic backgrounds. Indonesian was the dominant mother tongue, while Javanese, Bugis, and Makassarese were the most frequently studied regional languages. English was the leading foreign language studied, followed by Korean and Arabic. Formal instruction predominated for Indonesian and foreign languages, whereas regional languages were mainly learned independently.

Pearson correlation analysis found significant positive relationships among all multilingual-learning variables and among cultural-awareness variables. Multilingual competence, learning processes, psychological factors, and social interaction were also significantly associated with cultural knowledge, participation, sociocultural context, and attitudes toward cultural learning. The strongest reported cross-domain relationships involved multilingual competence and sociocultural context, and social interaction and attitudes toward cultural learning.

Qualitative findings identified strategies including culturally inclusive curricula, educator training, technology-supported and self-directed learning, community engagement, intercultural collaboration, and accessible language-learning resources. The study concludes that integrating multilingual and culturally responsive approaches in Indonesian higher education can support inclusive learning and prepare students to participate in culturally diverse communities.

The lecture examines auctions as price-setting mechanisms in government procurement, financial markets, spectrum allocation, and online advertising. It begins with the independent private values model, where risk-neutral bidders independently observe their own values.

In second-price sealed-bid auctions, bidding one’s true value is weakly dominant: deviations either do not affect outcomes or risk winning above one’s value or losing a profitable purchase. Seller revenue equals the expected second-highest value. Oral ascending or button auctions produce the same outcome when bidders withdraw at their values, though they reveal less information about the highest bidder’s valuation.

In first-price sealed-bid auctions, winners pay their bids, so bidders optimally shade bids below their values, balancing higher surplus against a lower probability of winning. With uniformly distributed values, a bidder bids \((n-1)/n\) of their value. More generally, the equilibrium bid equals the expected second-highest value conditional on the bidder having the highest value.

The revenue equivalence theorem states that, under symmetric independent private values, any mechanism that allocates the object to the highest-value bidder and gives the lowest-value type zero surplus generates expected revenue equal to the expected second-highest value. It also gives bidders identical expected utility across such mechanisms. This result can help solve other formats, including all-pay auctions.

Revenue equivalence may fail when bidders are risk-averse, values are correlated, or allocation need not always occur. Risk aversion makes first-price auctions generate more revenue than second-price auctions, while positively correlated values favor second-price auctions. In second-price auctions, the optimal reserve price equals the single-buyer monopoly price regardless of the number of bidders. Reserve prices can reduce welfare, discourage costly entry, and face commitment problems.

Common-value auctions create a winner’s curse because winning indicates that rivals had lower estimates of the object’s shared value. Rational bidders account for this by bidding based on expected value conditional on winning.

Hendricks and Porter study US offshore oil leases. Drainage tracts adjacent to existing wells are more productive and profitable than wildcat tracts but attract fewer bidders because incumbents possess superior information. Their model predicts mixed strategies, more frequent incumbent participation, incumbent profits, approximately zero entrant profits, and incumbent bids increasing with tract value and observable signals. Data from 114 drainage tracts broadly support these predictions, suggesting asymmetric information and fear of the winner’s curse deter outside bidders. Joint bidding and incumbent advantages may also increase competition for initial wildcat leases by making their associated future drainage opportunities more valuable.

Seventy-seven-year-old Jeong-Suk Cha provides most of the round-the-clock care for her 48-year-old son Alex, who has cerebral palsy, spinal cord damage and almost no mobility. Despite help from family, friends and personal support workers, the physically demanding work has injured and exhausted her.

Alex has waited 13 years for a place at London’s Participation House, which has 40 spaces and 60 to 90 people waiting. Ontario had 9,700 developmentally disabled adults awaiting residential care, while regional officials acknowledged lacking complete data on demand and capacity. A $100-million class-action lawsuit alleges the province administers support wait lists inconsistently and unreasonably.

Alex’s sister Jin spends about two hours daily coordinating his care and has created detailed instructional binders for support workers. As their mother ages, the family is campaigning for appropriate residential housing. The offered alternative is long-term care with seniors, which Alex strongly rejects, writing that he would rather die than go there.

Amazon.com’s 2015 Form 10-K describes operations across North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). Amazon serves consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators through retail, marketplace, cloud computing, publishing, advertising, devices, and related services. Its strategy emphasizes customer focus, innovation, operational excellence, and long-term thinking.

For 2015, net sales rose 20% to $107.0 billion, operating income reached $2.23 billion, and net income was $596 million, compared with a $241 million loss in 2014. Operating cash flow increased to $11.9 billion. Segment sales were $63.7 billion for North America, $35.4 billion for International, and $7.9 billion for AWS; respective growth rates were 25%, 6%, and 70%. Foreign exchange movements reduced reported 2015 sales by $5.2 billion.

Amazon employed approximately 230,800 people at year-end. It operated about 130 million leased and 5 million owned square feet of facilities. The company had $19.8 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities and considered operating cash flow, available balances, and credit sufficient for anticipated needs over the following 12 months.

Major risks included intense competition, rapid expansion, international regulation, foreign exchange fluctuations, fulfillment and data-center operations, seasonality, inventory management, cybersecurity and system interruptions, acquisitions, intellectual property disputes, taxation, supplier dependence, payment processing, product liability, and fraudulent or unlawful seller activity. Amazon reported no unresolved SEC staff comments, no dividends, and no issuer share purchases.

Suzanne Nimocks forwarded a December 2000 McKinsey update on electric-power privatization and restructuring worldwide. Governments facing rising demand and limited funding were increasingly opening generation to foreign investment, unbundling state utilities, introducing wholesale and retail competition, and pursuing privatization. Some international investors were shifting toward lower-risk U.S. and European markets.

European liberalization was driven by the EU Directive, with countries progressing at different rates through customer choice, grid access, utility consolidation, asset sales, and independent market operation. Central and Eastern European countries pursued restructuring and privatization to attract capital and support prospective EU membership, often under IMF or development-bank pressure.

Asian reforms resumed as economies recovered, though independent producers continued to face disputed power-purchase agreements, weak government guarantees, insolvent utilities, and regulatory uncertainty. Latin American privatization restarted more slowly after economic and currency disruptions; drought, hydroelectric dependence, ownership limits, and political instability constrained investment. African and Middle Eastern governments increasingly permitted private generation, while broader privatization remained limited. Regional transmission projects were advancing in Africa, the Middle East, Central America, and parts of Asia.

The paper proposes a method for estimating, before interaction, the probability that a trusting agent in a digital business ecosystem will not receive the full benefit of resources invested with a probable trusted agent. Risk combines the probability and consequences of failure.

A trusted agent’s “FailureLevel” represents the extent to which desired outcomes may not be achieved under specified context and criteria. Time is divided into non-overlapping slots across pre- and post-interaction phases to reflect risk’s dynamic nature. Pre-interaction FailureLevels are derived from past interactions or recommendations; these levels are then used to predict probabilities for every possible FailureLevel in post-interaction slots.

The Amount Invested Curve (AIC) represents the probability of a net financial amount being invested and remaining at stake throughout a time slot, accounting for cumulative and progressive investments. The Factual Amount Invested Curve (FAIC) extends the AIC by incorporating the trusted agent’s FailureLevel through convolution, showing the increased investment probability required to achieve the same outcomes.

The Loss of Resource Benefit (LORB) index is the ordinate of the FAIC at the endpoint of the AIC. It indicates the probability that the trusting agent will not obtain the expected benefit from its invested resources. This measure can support informed selection among probable trusted agents alongside broader risk analysis.
Philadelphia’s energetic arena can benefit the home team. The goalie remains calm despite opponents’ pressure and has consistently made crucial saves.

The Brunswick school board began the process of placing a 10-year, $4.67 million emergency levy renewal on the May ballot, with no tax increase. It authorized up to $10 million in notes for a new middle school and other property improvements, and revised fiscal 2018 appropriations after grant and fund increases. The district received donations supporting student programs, special education and overdue lunch fees. The board honored Lisa Durichko as she ended 12 years of service. An executive session produced no action. Organizational and regular meetings are scheduled for Jan. 8 and Jan. 22.

This May 2018 ebook reproduces the 1917 Supplement 1 of *Foreign Relations of the United States*, preserving the printed edition while offering search, bookmarking, note-taking, and offline access. Document numbers are recommended for citations because they remain consistent across formats. The volume primarily covers U.S. neutrality before April 6, 1917, but extends later for continuing issues and related diplomatic developments involving Latin America, China, Siam, and Liberia. Editorial brackets identify supplied text, corrections, omissions, or garbled wording; parentheses generally originate in the documents or reflect proposed telegram decodings. File translations were revised against original-language texts or other versions while avoiding significant changes to texts used by officials.

The Shuffle offense, originating with Bruce Drake at Oklahoma, uses constant five-player movement, rotation, passing, screening and rebounding to create high-percentage shots while limiting defensive help. It requires little dribbling and suits teams lacking height because every player rotates through each position.

Its continuity centers on reversal passes and rub cuts off post screens, with options to feed the cutter, pass to a post popping off a down screen, or find a corner player flashing into the middle. If these options fail, players screen and reverse the action to the opposite side.

Players read defensive reactions and counter by cutting over or under screens, attacking switches, bumping back for shots, or using post-up opportunities. The corner player alternates among rebounding, flashing and screening duties. Defensive overplay is countered through wing back cuts, dribble clears, point backdoors and lob passes to a fronted post.

The AEGEAN study compared standard care with an additional education program for adherence to apixaban, measured electronically in patients with atrial fibrillation. Of 1,162 randomized subjects, 1,054 completed 24 weeks and 1,003 completed 48 weeks. Baseline characteristics were comparable across groups.

At 24 weeks, mean adherence was 91.64% with standard care and 91.88% with education, with no significant difference. From weeks 24–48, adherence was 87.59% in primary standard care, 87.51% in secondary standard care, and 88.41% with continued education, also without significant differences. Adherence declined significantly over time in both original groups. Persistence was approximately 91% at 24 weeks and 85%–88% at 48 weeks, with no significant group differences. Compliance exceeded 95% through week 24 and 94% at week 48.

Safety outcomes, including adverse events, serious adverse events, discontinuations, and bleeding, were generally similar between groups. Overall, 24 deaths and three fatal bleeding events were reported. The study concluded that adherence and persistence were high through 24 weeks and sustained through 48 weeks, but proactive education provided no additional benefit.

The player said he capitalized on a scoring chance, credited his development in Finland, and felt ready for the NHL. After the Sharks’ first Finals win, he urged more shooting and sustained effort. He chose San Jose because of its early interest, leadership, and opportunities for young players.

NVIDIA reported that its subsidiary exercised an option to purchase its new Santa Clara campus property from Wachovia for approximately $350 million, terminating related lease and financing agreements. Construction was substantially completed October 31, 2017, and the purchase was expected to close in fiscal 2018’s fourth quarter. NVIDIA also furnished its third-quarter and first-nine-month fiscal 2018 results, including a November 9, 2017 press release and CFO commentary.

Scientists from MIT and the University of Cambridge found that the Phoenix cluster’s central black hole may recycle 10-million-degree gas into cold fuel for star formation. ALMA observations revealed cold-gas filaments extending 20,000 light years from the black hole and closely aligned with hot-gas bubbles mapped by NASA’s Chandra X-Ray Observatory. The findings may explain why the cluster’s central galaxy produces about 1,000 stars annually and offer insight into how supermassive black holes and host galaxies evolve together. The study was published in the Astrophysical Journal.

TDSAT temporarily barred penalties against Bharti Airtel and Idea Cellular for failing to meet Trai’s tariff-reporting requirements and stayed clauses concerning reporting and significant market power. Trai may still seek details of customer-retention discounts. New rules require operators to report tariffs within seven working days, disclose segmented offers, and treat discounts as new tariffs. Violations can draw daily penalties, while predatory tariffs by operators with at least 30% market share can attract fines up to Rs50 lakh per plan per circle. Airtel, Idea and Vodafone have challenged the rules.

Shared distributed-system patterns accelerate learning and give developers a common vocabulary. Standard names and definitions prevent wasted debate over identical concepts known by different terms, enabling faster discussion of implementation. The container community’s adoption of “sidecar” illustrates how shared terminology allows developers to focus immediately on applying a concept to solve problems.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPUs introduce PCIe 4.0, redesigned graphics processing clusters, increased ROP counts, and streaming multiprocessors with 128 CUDA cores, second-generation RT Cores, third-generation Tensor Cores, and 128 KB unified L1/shared memory. Dual FP32-capable datapaths double peak FP32 throughput over Turing, while larger caches and doubled shared-memory bandwidth improve graphics and compute performance. Ampere GPUs are stated to be up to 1.9 times more power-efficient than Turing at equal performance.

Second-generation RT Cores double ray-triangle intersection throughput, support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute, and add hardware acceleration for motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores support TF32, BF16, FP16, INT8, INT4, and structured sparsity, which can double matrix throughput by skipping zero-valued weights. These capabilities accelerate AI features including DLSS, denoising, RTX Voice, and 8K rendering.

GA10x introduces GDDR6X memory using PAM4 signaling, reaching data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth up to 936 GB/s. RTX IO, working with Microsoft DirectStorage, enables GPU-based asset loading and lossless decompression, reducing CPU workload and improving loading, streaming, and I/O performance.

Display capabilities include DisplayPort 1.4a and HDMI 2.1, supporting 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz under specified compression or pixel-format conditions. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware AV1 decoding up to 8K60 HDR, while seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.

Products based on GA10x include the GeForce RTX 30 series, NVIDIA A40, and RTX A6000. The A40 targets data-center visualization, compute, AI, and virtualization, while the A6000 provides 48 GB of GDDR6 memory, expandable to 96 GB through NVLink. The RTX 3090 includes 24 GB of GDDR6X memory and targets creators, researchers, developers, and extreme gamers. Error Detection and Replay technology helps identify unstable GDDR6X memory overclocks by retrying failed transmissions and exposing performance plateaus.

Five Gor Mahia players—Kenneth Muguna, Meddie Kagere, Musa Mohammed, Jacques Tuyisenge and George Odhiambo—were shortlisted for the 2017 Kenyan Premier League MVP award. Other contenders are Massoud Juma, Patrick Matasi and Lawrence Juma. Following postponement of KPL’s awards, the Sports Journalists Association of Kenya will hold its sponsored Football Gala on December 18. Eight categories include MVP, Golden Glove, Defender, Midfielder, Golden Boot, Young/New Player, Coach and the special SJAK Award. Prize details remain unannounced.

This preprint examined whether placental biomarkers measured during the first and second trimesters were associated with retained placenta or postpartum hemorrhage requiring transfusion (RP/PPH). Using NuMoM2b data, researchers analyzed 2,192 nulliparous participants with singleton pregnancies; 67 experienced RP/PPH.

Participants with RP/PPH had higher second-trimester levels of soluble endoglin, β-hCG, inhibin A, PAPP-A, and sFlt-1, as well as higher first-trimester sFlt-1 and sFlt-1/PlGF ratios. PlGF did not differ between groups. RP/PPH was also associated with preeclampsia, cesarean birth, and instrumental delivery. Among participants without preeclampsia, second-trimester β-hCG, inhibin A, PAPP-A, and sFlt-1 remained significantly elevated in those who developed RP/PPH; no biomarkers significantly distinguished RP/PPH among participants with preeclampsia. Changes between trimesters also varied by preeclampsia status.

The findings suggest that early-pregnancy placental biomarkers, particularly second-trimester angiogenic markers, warrant further study as potential predictors of postpartum bleeding risk. Limitations include the absence of direct blood-loss measurements or a general PPH diagnosis, only 67 RP/PPH cases, overrepresentation of adverse pregnancy outcomes, and lack of adjustment for other demographic, pregnancy, and labor factors.

The Steelers won eight straight, including a 39-38 victory over Baltimore, but four of their last five wins were by three points or fewer. They host New England in Week 15, potentially for the AFC’s top seed, without injured linebacker Ryan Shazier and facing MVP-level quarterback Tom Brady.

Retired Boynton Beach firefighter-paramedic Luis Garcia spent nearly $40,000 of his savings on 800 doses of naloxone, or Narcan, to combat opioid overdoses. Through his South Florida Opioid Crisis Mortality Reduction Project, he travels Florida training residents, business owners and law enforcement officers to administer the drug and distributes it for free.

At a Stuart community event, Garcia provided about 50 doses after offering 30-minute training sessions. He said he responded to roughly 3,000 overdoses during his career and has revived five of six people he assisted in the past 18 months. Garcia prioritizes businesses with high customer traffic and police agencies that do not carry Narcan.

Most major Treasure Coast law enforcement and emergency agencies carry the medication. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office used it 62 times while responding to 153 overdose cases in 2017. Community organizers and attendees emphasized reducing stigma, increasing awareness and treating addiction as a widespread issue.

U.S. home prices rose 0.9% during the latest quarter and 6.1% year over year, the strongest annual growth since February 2015, despite the winter slowdown. Quarterly growth was 0.8% in the Midwest, 0.7% in the Northeast, and 1.0% in both the South and West. San Jose and Hartford recorded 0.3% quarterly declines, while Portland led growth near 2%; eight major metros grew at least 1.5%.

Clear Capital reported that 16 of the 50 largest metropolitan markets had surpassed housing-bubble peak prices. Together with smaller record-setting markets, they represented about one-third of national housing stock. Another 5% was within 5.8% of 2006 prices. Although 2017 annual growth was projected to moderate to 2–3%, continued gains could leave nearly 40% of homeowners who bought at the market peak above water by year-end. Clear Capital said reduced negative equity could bring more homeowners and demand into the market.

A late surge in London Stock Exchange listings has raised hopes of an IPO revival after only three listings accounted for 2% of Europe’s IPOs earlier in 2025. Recent and potential offerings include Beauty Tech Group’s £300 million debut, Princes Group and Shawbrook, which could be valued at up to £2 billion. Activity spans consumer goods, fintech and real estate. Analysts say sustained recovery depends on strong demand, first-day trading and post-listing performance. Norway’s Visma is also reportedly considering a major London float in 2026.

SD cards contain a user area and an authenticated protected area. Capacity classes are SDSC up to 2 GB, SDHC above 2 GB through 32 GB, and SDXC above 32 GB through 2 TB. Hosts supporting higher-capacity cards must also support lower-capacity cards. Speed Classes 0, 2, 4, 6, and 10 specify minimum performance from unspecified to 10 MB/s.

Host-controlled communication uses commands, responses, and block data transfers over SD, SPI, UHS-I, or UHS-II interfaces. Commands and responses use the CMD line; data may use one or four DAT lines. Transactions include CRC protection, card addressing, single- or multiple-block operations, busy signaling, and defined packet formats. Cards provide identification, addressing, configuration, status, and operating-condition registers and can be reset by power cycling or CMD0.

UHS-I supports up to 104 MB/s and uses 3.3 V or 1.8 V signaling in DS, HS, SDR104, and DDR50 modes. It applies to SDHC and SDXC cards, requires SD mode for 1.8 V operation, and uses initialization, voltage-switching, driver-selection, bus-width, and tuning commands. UHS-II adds a second-row interface and supports modes from FD156 through FD624, reaching 624 MB/s. Hosts may fall back to the legacy SD interface if UHS-II initialization is not detected.

Card initialization uses CMD0, CMD8, ACMD41, CMD2, and CMD3 to reset cards, verify voltage, establish capacity and signaling support, obtain identification, and assign relative addresses. Identification and data-transfer modes are separate. CMD7 selects one card for transfer. Reads and writes are block-oriented, normally using blocks no larger than 512 bytes, with CRC checking and stop-command support. Multiple-block writes are preferred for speed, and pre-erasing may improve performance.

Erase operations use CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38. DISCARD permits deallocation with unspecified resulting contents, while FULE logically erases the full user area; both are limited to SDHC and SDXC and are unavailable through SPI. Cards indicate write, erase, discard, or FULE activity through DAT0 busy signaling.

Protection mechanisms include a host-managed mechanical write-protect switch, optional internal protection, and password locking through CMD42. Card Ownership Protection adds a Force Erase Password, COP unlocking, protected force erase, and restrictions on clearing passwords. Force Erase removes stored data and the card password; setting a Force Erase Password disables ordinary Force Erase and password clearing.

ROM cards are read-only, reject write and erase commands, optionally support locking or security commands, and lack a write-protect switch. Application Performance Classes specify random and sequential minimums. Cache, self-maintenance, command queuing, and low-voltage initialization are also defined as performance or interface features.

Oversold markets or stocks have fallen significantly over a defined period. Objective measures such as the Relative Strength Indicator (RSI) can identify these conditions; the example defines oversold as a 3-day RSI below 20. Because markets often exhibit mean reversion, sharp declines may be followed by short-term rebounds, though long-term returns tend toward averages and reversals are not guaranteed.

A backtest on the S&P 500 from 1985 used a strategy of buying at the close when the 3-day RSI was below 20 and selling when the close exceeded the previous day’s high. Reported results included an average gain of 0.64% per trade, a 75% win rate, approximately 7.6–7.7% CAGR, a 26% maximum drawdown, and a 2.4–2.5 profit factor. The passage reports either 448 or 484 trades. Dividends were excluded, and the strategy performed less effectively before 1990. Markets were also reportedly less prone to mean reversion before S&P 500 futures began in 1982, so the pattern may not persist indefinitely.

Robert Putnam popularized “social capital,” especially through *Bowling Alone*, linking civic-group participation to economic, social, and political performance. His earlier work contrasted civically engaged northern Italy with southern Italy’s history of autocratic rule and mafia dominance. Social capital has two principal definitions: participation in civic organizations, favored by Putnam, and generalized trust, which may improve economic performance by lowering transaction costs. A 1996 study found economic growth associated with generalized trust but not civic membership. Another distinction separates “bridging” social capital, which builds cooperation across groups, from “bonding” social capital, which strengthens solidarity within groups, sometimes against outsiders. Putnam also reported that ethnic diversity and fragmentation often do not increase social capital, a finding adopted by some ethnocentrists and nationalists despite his own support for diversity.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K on April 26, 2021, announcing that its financial results for the quarter ended March 31, 2021, were posted on its website. The First Quarter 2021 Update is attached as Exhibit 99.1. CFO Zachary J. Kirkhorn signed the report.

This study reviewed the first year of COVID-19 vaccination in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), from April 2021 to March 2022, using Ministry of Health and WHO-African Region data. The campaign prioritized healthcare workers, people with comorbidities, and adults aged 55 or older, aiming to vaccinate at least 20% of the population by the end of 2021.

Only 16 of 26 provinces began vaccination during the first year. By March 2022, approximately 5.7% of the population had received at least one dose and 1.03% was fully vaccinated. Coverage varied substantially by province, with Kasai Oriental reporting the highest full-vaccination coverage and Equateur the lowest. Functional vaccination sites increased over time but remained unevenly distributed, with Kinshasa consistently having the most sites. Men outnumbered vaccinated women in every province except Kasai Oriental.

Among priority groups, 8,302 healthcare workers and 46,495 older adults completed their primary series. Janssen was the most frequently used vaccine, followed by Moderna and Pfizer, while AstraZeneca was least requested. Compared with other Central African countries, the DRC had the lowest proportion receiving at least one dose and administered only 8% of received doses.

Challenges included vaccine hesitancy, safety concerns and communication surrounding AstraZeneca, competing disease outbreaks, shortages and strikes among healthcare workers, logistical problems, short vaccine shelf lives, expiring doses, and difficulties reaching priority groups. The study recommends stronger health systems, community and religious engagement, and integration of COVID-19 vaccination with other primary healthcare services. Limitations included aggregated data, difficulties identifying priority-group denominators and vaccination histories, and limited national generalizability.

The First Circuit dismissed the government’s interlocutory appeal for lack of jurisdiction under 18 U.S.C. § 3731. Defendants Philip Watson and Shane O’Hearn were charged in connection with a 1997 assault and robbery. Anthony Spera, a key government witness, was deported to Italy after immigration officials overlooked the prosecutor’s request to preserve his availability. Shortly before trial, the government sought a continuance to arrange Spera’s return or depose him abroad. The district court denied the requests, citing the case’s age, Speedy Trial Act concerns, government negligence, and the likely six-to-twelve-month delay.

Section 3731 permits government appeals from pretrial orders suppressing or excluding evidence, but not from all interlocutory rulings. Although the denial of a continuance impeded the government’s ability to obtain and use Spera’s testimony, the orders were case-management decisions intended to prevent further delay, not evidentiary rulings directly excluding testimony. Their effect on evidence gathering was incidental and therefore insufficient to establish appellate jurisdiction.

Michael Gayed proposed the lumber/gold ratio as a risk-on/risk-off indicator. Lumber reflects housing, construction, consumer spending, and the business cycle, while gold offers diversification, low correlation with stocks and bonds, and value preservation. Gayed invested in stocks during risk-on periods and long-term Treasuries during risk-off periods. A modified backtest used WOOD as a lumber proxy and GLD for gold. Rotating between SPY and TLT produced 11.4% annual returns since 2008 and a 2.2% average gain per trade, but suffered a 35% drawdown amid the 2022–23 bond collapse. Replacing TLT with GLD reduced annual returns to 8.7%. The large drawdown could make the strategy difficult for investors to maintain.

The speaker thanked Grand Forks Air Force Base personnel for supporting national security and flood-stricken communities. After touring the devastation and meeting regional officials, the speaker praised residents, rescue workers, local leaders, and organizations for their courage, cooperation, and community spirit.

Federal actions included authorizing FEMA to cover 100 percent of direct federal emergency assistance, extending disaster coverage to 18 additional Minnesota counties and 53 South Dakota counties, and requesting another $200 million from Congress. If approved, total requested disaster assistance for North Dakota, South Dakota, and Minnesota would reach $488 million.

The speaker acknowledged immediate needs for shelter, income, sanitation, and temporary housing, as well as the emotional strain likely to follow the disaster. Residents were urged to support one another. FEMA Director James Lee Witt was assigned to lead an interagency task force developing a long-term rebuilding plan. The speaker pledged continued federal support and emphasized that the communities’ people, faith, and spirit could endure floods, fire, and blizzards.

Tesla’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2019 reports:

- Second-quarter revenue of $6.35 billion, gross profit of $921 million, operating loss of $167 million, and net loss attributable to common stockholders of $408 million, or $2.31 per share.

ReplayTV shifted from manufacturing digital recorders to licensing technology, cut non-core staff, and replaced CEO Kim LeMasters with founder Anthony Wood. NetCom Technologies raised $75 million, while Access Point Telecommunications laid off 35% of employees after abandoning plans to build its own network. Numerous companies secured funding, including Financial Technologies International with $52.75 million, MortgageRamp with $50 million, NetSchools and Vector with $30 million each, Medsite.com with $28 million, Currenex with $27.6 million, Magnifi with $25 million, and MindSHIFT with $21 million. VitaGO announced restructuring focused on Germany and planned to discontinue Italian operations.

New offerings included Kasna’s Central and Eastern European trade portal, Cuantra’s Latin American transportation marketplace, a wireless-payment joint venture between Redpacket and Pocketpass, and BuzzBack’s online research product.
