This Foreign Relations volume documents U.S.-Soviet relations from January 1983 to March 1985 within a four-volume Reagan-era subseries. Editorial annotations supplement official records with related documents, public statements, memoirs, and firsthand accounts. The Advisory Committee oversees compilation and declassification processes, while the Department of State conducted review under applicable security standards. Review from 2015 to 2019 withheld one document fully and made excisions in 33 others.

The volume examines implementation of Reagan’s NSDD 75 agenda covering arms control, human rights, regional issues, and bilateral relations. It focuses on policymaking by George Shultz, William Clark, Robert McFarlane, Jack Matlock, the National Security Council, and the Department of State, as well as discussions with Soviet officials Anatoly Dobrynin and Andrei Gromyko. It also documents U.S. assessments of Soviet leaders Yuri Andropov and Konstantin Chernenko despite the absence of meetings with Reagan.

Hola Publishing International expanded its Spanish-language imprint into Mexico, offering affordable print-on-demand publishing and global distribution. Authors and organizations can order 25 to 1,000 locally produced books instead of traditional minimums of 2,000. Services cover paperback, hardcover, and e-books, with authors retaining all rights. Local production reduces shipping costs and enables a 60-day print turnaround. The company serves self-published authors, corporations, government bodies, nonprofits, universities, and educational institutions.

The article argues that gold’s rally remains technically constrained while silver and mining stocks have failed to follow, suggesting a possible broader precious-metals decline. It says the USD Index’s inverse head-and-shoulders breakout is being verified and could support a rally to at least 101.3. Stocks are described as pausing after breaking support and failing to exceed previous highs, which the author views as bearish. The combination of resilient gold, a strengthening dollar, weakening stocks, and underperforming miners is compared with 2008. The page also includes promotional material, critical reader comments, and disclosures warning of substantial trading risks and potentially inaccurate market data.

The disclosure describes augmented and virtual reality systems requiring accurate, low-latency localization of users’ heads, handheld controllers, and other physical objects. A head-mounted display, local processing module, sensors, and optional cloud resources coordinate virtual content with real-world environments and maintain a shared world model.

Localization may combine electromagnetic emitters and coil sensors, inertial measurement units, cameras, depth sensors, GPS, SLAM, and sensor fusion. Compact electromagnetic tracking configurations can place an emitter in a handheld controller and sensors on a headset or belt pack, using reduced duty cycles, multiplexing, dynamic tuning, noise cancellation, calibration, and multiple coils to conserve power and improve accuracy. Vision-based tracking extracts image features, creates and updates 3-D map points, estimates head pose, and divides processing into tracking, low-latency mapping, optimization, and cleanup stages.

Other embodiments use stacked waveguides to present content at different apparent depths, retrieve virtual content by decoding QR codes or accessing network locations, and share content between users through activation gateways and credentials. The described hardware can include speakers, cameras, processors, storage, quick-release connectors, wireless links, and local or cloud-based computation. Numerous applications are identified across gaming, navigation, communication, education, work, shopping, healthcare, entertainment, and collaborative experiences.

Amazon’s May 22, 2019 annual shareholder meeting elected all ten director nominees. Shareholders ratified Ernst & Young LLP as independent auditor for fiscal 2019 and approved executive compensation in an advisory vote. All twelve shareholder proposals were rejected, covering food waste, special-meeting thresholds, government technology use, product and employment reports, independent board leadership, climate change, board ideology, gender pay reporting, executive compensation metrics, and vote-counting practices.

At American University, the speaker calls world peace humanity’s most urgent task, arguing that nuclear war is irrational and that peace must be pursued through practical agreements, evolving institutions, mutual tolerance, and peaceful dispute resolution. Americans should reject assumptions that war is inevitable, reconsider distorted views of the Soviet Union, recognize shared interests in avoiding devastation, and seek communication and arms control while protecting vital interests and alliances.

The speaker advocates strengthening the United Nations, respecting national self-determination, establishing direct communication between Moscow and Washington, and pursuing staged disarmament. He announces forthcoming high-level Moscow discussions on a comprehensive nuclear test-ban treaty and declares that the United States will not conduct atmospheric nuclear tests unless other states resume them.

Peace abroad must also be supported by freedom and equal rights at home. Government institutions and citizens share responsibility for protecting those rights and respecting the law. Although treaties cannot guarantee absolute security, effective agreements offer fewer risks than an uncontrolled arms race. The United States will remain prepared but will work toward a world where the weak are safe, the strong are just, and policy follows a strategy of peace rather than annihilation.

SOS disruption defense directs wing ball handlers toward corner or baseline checkpoints to deny middle penetration, weakside reversals, and operating space. Off-ball defenders deny first passes, front posts, and occupy Helpside I positions.

Three baseline responses are used:
- **Straight SOS:** The on-ball defender contains and smothers a dribbler who stops before the baseline checkpoint; the low help defender may fake a trap.
- **Base Go I:** Penetration inside the checkpoint triggers an automatic trap by the low Helpside I defender. The remaining defenders rotate into Triangle I positions, deny nearby passes, and rematch when the ball leaves the trap.
- **Base Go Red:** A predetermined early sideline trap begins when the ball enters below the free-throw-line extended area. The nearest defender traps while teammates rotate into Triangle I, then close out, deny passes, front the post, and restore matchups after an outlet pass.

Against side screens, SOS switches aggressively above the free-throw line to prevent shots and middle penetration. Below it, defenders trap the ball handler before the screen is established. Off-ball defenders rotate into high and low Helpside I positions and deny or front the screener’s roll. Outlet, skip, and low-post passes prompt coordinated closeouts, denials, post traps, and matchup recovery.

The all-out variation traps the point guard before a screen or pass, disrupting planned routes. Secondary traps may occur on baseline rolls or post entries. Throughout all schemes, rotations happen as the pass leaves the passer’s hands, and standard SOS fundamentals resume once defenders are matched up.

Just Patios offers durable, customisable galvanised and Colorbond carports designed to protect various vehicles from Australia’s harsh weather. Its Flat/Skillion, Raised Flyover and Gable designs can be freestanding or house-attached. Builders tailor installations to each property and assist with council regulations. He also cited contagion risks in emerging markets, particularly Turkey, Argentina and Brazil, while noting selective opportunities. Economist Paul Krugman warned of a self-reinforcing emerging-market currency and corporate debt crisis.

NVIDIA’s Turing architecture introduces dedicated RT Cores that autonomously accelerate Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection tests, freeing streaming multiprocessors for shading and compute work. Combined with hybrid rendering, denoising, and BVH acceleration, they enable real-time ray tracing. Turing achieves over 10 Giga Rays/sec, approximately ten times Pascal’s software ray-tracing performance.

Turing also introduces NVIDIA NGX, a deep-learning graphics stack using Tensor Cores and pretrained neural-network services. Its features include DLSS, which produces TAA-like image quality with roughly half the shading work; DLSS 2X, which approaches 64-times supersampled quality; AI-based inpainting; interpolated slow-motion video; and image or video super-resolution. DLSS networks are trained against high-quality 64-times supersampled reference images.

Mesh Shading replaces parts of the traditional geometry pipeline with cooperative Task and Mesh Shaders. It reduces CPU draw-call bottlenecks, supports dynamic level-of-detail selection and geometry manipulation, and enables substantially more objects to be rendered in real time.

Variable Rate Shading independently controls shading rates for 16-by-16-pixel regions without changing visibility rates. Its applications include content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading further decouples visibility from appearance sampling, stores shading results in texture space, and reuses them spatially, temporally, or across stereo views.

Multi-View Rendering processes geometry once for multiple viewpoints or instances, supporting four hardware views per pass and up to 32 through APIs. It expands Pascal’s stereo-rendering capabilities and supports canted VR displays, multiple shadows, and varied character poses. Other Turing features include bindless resource views, flexible resource heaps, VirtualLink over USB-C, and RT Core-accelerated VR audio.

The TU104 GPU contains up to 48 SMs, 3,072 CUDA Cores, 368 Tensor Cores, 48 RT Cores, and second-generation NVLink. It is used in products including GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. TU106 contains 36 SMs, 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but lacks NVLink and SLI support.

Turing’s hybrid-rendering model combines rasterization, ray tracing, AI, and simulation. NVIDIA’s workload-based RTX-OPS metric weights Tensor, FP32, RT, and INT32 operations according to representative usage.

Ray tracing casts rays from the camera through pixels into a scene to calculate reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. BVHs reduce intersection testing by organizing geometry in hierarchical bounding boxes, while denoising produces higher-quality results from fewer rays. Turing applies these techniques to physically accurate shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections, overcoming limitations of shadow maps, screen-space methods, and static probes.
Figures 1–8 show perspective, front, rear, side, top, and bottom views of a desk lamp design. Dashed or broken lines indicate portions excluded from the claimed design.

The work introduces a local Boltzmann Generator architecture for equilibrium sampling of large crystalline materials. Traditional Boltzmann Generators can produce independent samples and estimate free energies but have struggled to scale beyond several hundred particles because of high training costs and low sampling efficiency.

The proposed method combines graph neural networks with augmented coupling flows. It learns transformations from local particle environments, models displacements from ideal crystal lattices, and scales linearly with system size when the number of neighbors is fixed. Models require only the target potential energy during training, not target-distribution samples. Auxiliary variables preserve three-dimensional environmental information and permit exact joint likelihood evaluation; physical marginal densities can be obtained through an inverse flow pass. The architecture also supports conditioning on box shape, thermodynamic variables, and interaction parameters.

Models trained on small systems transferred to systems exceeding 1,000 particles. For monatomic-water ice and Lennard-Jones crystals, generated radial distribution functions and energy distributions closely matched molecular dynamics results. Local models trained faster and achieved higher effective sample sizes than global attention-based architectures. For example, a local ice model converged in about four GPU days, compared with more than 330 GPU days reported for a global model on a larger training system.

Using targeted free energy perturbation, the models produced accurate Helmholtz and Gibbs free energies. Ice free energies agreed with molecular-dynamics and MBAR references to within \(10^{-3}k_BT\) per particle for systems up to 1,000 particles, while marginal estimates remained accurate at 1,728 particles. The method captured small free-energy differences between cubic and hexagonal ice and between FCC and HCP Lennard-Jones crystals, including dependence on interaction cutoff.

Conditioning on the Stillinger–Weber three-body strength enabled one model to cover parameterizations associated with germanium, silicon, and monatomic water and to compare diamond cubic, β-tin, and BCC structures. Temperature- and box-conditioned models also reproduced the silicon diamond-cubic/β-tin coexistence line in close agreement with MD+MBAR.

The authors conclude that local augmented flows reduce training costs, improve sampling efficiency, transfer across system sizes, and amortize calculations across thermodynamic conditions and interaction parameters. Future work includes liquid phases and broader chemical generalization.

In his inaugural address, President Biden celebrates the peaceful transfer of power and democracy’s resilience after violence at the Capitol. He calls for national unity to confront the pandemic, unemployment, racial injustice, political extremism, systemic racism, climate change, inequity, and threats to truth and democracy. He urges Americans to reject division, political violence, and manufactured falsehoods while treating one another with dignity, humility, and respect.

Biden pledges to govern for all Americans, defend the Constitution and democracy, restore alliances, and lead internationally through example. TQQQ options offer leveraged exposure to Nasdaq-100 price movements through calls and puts. Available contracts include American- and European-style options with varying strike prices and expirations. Common strategies include buying calls or puts, writing covered calls or puts, and combining these approaches.

Options can provide higher potential returns, hedging, and flexibility but are speculative, complex, and carry substantial loss risk due to leverage, volatility, market shifts, contract terms, and expiration. Strategy selection should reflect market conditions, investment goals, risk tolerance, liquidity, time horizon, and capital at risk. Backtesting, diversification, cautious leverage, stop-loss orders, and investing only affordable losses are emphasized.

Fair value may be estimated with the Black-Scholes model, supplemented by fundamental, technical, and quantified analysis. Trading costs vary by broker and may include commissions, contract fees, and slippage. Minimum capital and regulations concerning leverage, margin, stop losses, and hedging depend on the broker and jurisdiction. Profits are generally subject to capital gains tax, though investors should consult qualified brokers and tax specialists.

A review of 10 trials involving 77,917 high-risk participants found that omega-3 supplements did not significantly reduce deaths from heart disease, nonfatal heart attacks, strokes, or procedures to reopen clogged arteries. Participants, averaging 64 years old, were followed for 4.4 years and generally received omega-3 supplements or placebo for at least one year. Small apparent reductions in some coronary outcomes could have occurred by chance. Researchers said the findings do not support American Heart Association guidance recommending supplements for patients with prior coronary heart disease. Limitations included varied trial designs and missing data on smoking and cancer history. Other experts noted that omega-3 supplements are inexpensive and generally safe, and suggested consuming fatty fish or supplements may offer benefits beyond cardiovascular health.

The disclosure presents techniques for low-latency, scalable gate control, shared physical links among multiple time-sensitive applications, and energy-efficient communication in time-aware networks. Applicable settings include industrial automation, IoT, telecommunications, data centers, vehicles, audiovisual systems, power grids, and robotics.

Precision Time Protocol and generalized PTP synchronize clocks across time-aware systems. Grandmaster clocks are selected through algorithms such as the best master clock algorithm, while relay instances compensate for link and residence delays and propagate timing information. TSN standards provide synchronization, resource management, reliability, traffic shaping, and scheduled transmission.

Scheduled traffic uses traffic-class queues, each controlled by a transmission gate. A gate control list specifies when queues open or close and can coordinate frame preemption. Frames are transmitted according to selection algorithms such as strict priority, credit-based shaping, or enhanced transmission selection, provided their gates are open and sufficient transmission time remains.

Conventional TSN network interface controllers store large, duplicated gate control lists in on-chip memory. This consumes silicon area and power, limits scalability and timing precision, and can require more than a millisecond to program—longer than some industrial cycles.

The proposed architecture instead stores gate control-list banks in host memory and retains only small control registers and a prefetch buffer in the network controller. A dedicated DMA or RDMA channel prefetches list entries, while the controller parses upcoming operations and fetches packet data before gates open. Alternating banks permit one list to execute while another is updated. This approach reduces on-chip memory, power use, programming latency, and silicon area while supporting larger lists and sub-nanosecond scheduling resolution.

For devices hosting multiple talker applications, the disclosure proposes presenting one physical end station as a virtual bridge connected to multiple virtual single-talker end stations. Centralized network management can discover and configure these virtual elements using existing TSN mechanisms. A configuration service and gate control engine then apply the resulting configuration to the shared physical interface and coordinate workloads to limit interference.

University at Albany chemists synthesized manganese diboride, a boron-rich compound that is over 20% more energetic by weight and about 150% more energetic by volume than aluminum used in solid rocket boosters. It remains stable until exposed to an ignition agent such as kerosene, potentially allowing rockets to carry less fuel and more equipment or samples.

Researchers produce the compound by heating pressed manganese and boron powders to 3,000°C with an arc melter, then rapidly cooling the material. This creates an overcrowded, asymmetrical atomic structure that stores substantial potential energy. Computer models identified subtle structural deformation as the source of this stored energy, which is released during ignition.

Previously difficult to produce despite interest dating to the 1960s, manganese diboride can now be experimentally studied. Related boron structures may also support more durable automotive catalytic converters and catalysts for breaking down plastics.

Boscov’s achieved record sales in 2017 despite widespread department store closures, including Bon-Ton and Sears in the Wyoming Valley Mall. Customers credit its loyal staff, personal service, convenient location, sales and hometown atmosphere. Its downtown Wilkes-Barre store increased physical-store sales and supports nearby businesses. Barry “The Hatchet” Vagnoni, an Eagles fan since 1954, hosts large game-day gatherings with his wife, Dawn, in their 2,000-square-foot, memorabilia-filled “locker room” in Reading, Pennsylvania. The space has a 35-foot bar, 16 televisions and strict family-friendly rules requiring Eagles gear. Vagnoni leads cheers, changes costumes and plays a drum while Dawn handles food, guests and photos. For Super Bowl LII against the New England Patriots, the couple expected more than 100 fans, a band, dancers and extensive free food and drinks. A trading gap is an untraded price range between one period’s close and the next opening, usually caused by news or market imbalances. Gaps occur across time frames but are most common overnight. Major types include common, exhaustion, runaway, and breakaway gaps.

Traders may fade a gap by trading against its direction or follow it by trading with its direction. Stocks generally show greater mean reversion than other asset classes. Smaller gaps are more likely to fill, while larger gaps fill less often or take longer.

Using 25 years of S&P 500 E-mini futures data, same-day fill rates were 59% for bullish and 61% for bearish gaps at a 0.1% threshold. At 0.5%, rates fell to 43% and 42%; at 1%, they were 28% and 33%. A high fill rate does not necessarily ensure profitability because large losses can outweigh frequent small gains.

Simple gap strategies tested on futures data generally produced negative or weak returns. Adding filters improved one example to 0.06% per trade but remained insufficiently profitable. A swing strategy holding positions overnight averaged about 0.48% per trade with a 1.8 profit factor, while longer-term SPY testing averaged around 0.5%.

Gap trading has become less profitable as competition, computing power, and trader participation have increased. Effective strategies may require additional filters or fewer trades, increasing curve-fitting risk. Reliable data is essential for backtesting, and predicting gaps in advance is described as nearly impossible.

Smart beta ETFs have attracted substantial assets, but many advisors lack familiarity. A 2018 FTSE Russell survey found 79% of U.S. advisors were aware of smart beta, while 35% were very familiar. Education remains a key barrier, alongside U.K. concerns about performance and track records.

Bayard received an “unmodified” audit rating, indicating sound finances, despite two minor findings: a $700 deficit caused by budgeting in a new federal grant fund and $64 in mileage calculation errors.

The City Council unanimously supported Santa Clara’s effort to manage historic Fort Bayard, though Councilor Zeke Santa Maria questioned the village’s capacity and resources. Santa Clara’s plan seeks to restore the deteriorating property, promote economic development and rent office space to the U.S. Forest Service. Chamber Director Scott Terry said the village wants Bayard’s support, not funding, and argued immediate action is necessary to save the buildings.

The council also received an update on restoring Bayard’s historic train depot. The city owns the building, but the railroad owns the land beneath it, and officials are working to resolve the issue.

Wrestling legend Ric Flair, 68, was hospitalized for monitoring and faced “tough medical issues,” his representative said. Mick Foley and Eric Bischoff offered support. Flair debuted professionally in 1972 and entered WWE’s Hall of Fame in 2008.

The Wells Fargo Reflect® Card offers 0% introductory APR for 21 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by a variable APR of 16.99%, 23.49%, or 28.74%. It has no annual fee and includes up to $600 in cellphone protection, subject to a $25 deductible. However, it offers no ongoing rewards, charges a 5% balance-transfer fee with a $5 minimum, and imposes a 3% foreign-transaction fee. Motley Fool Money discloses that advertiser compensation can affect offer placement but says it does not influence product ratings or recommendations.

Xu Yan, wife of detained Chinese rights lawyer Yu Wensheng, said police prevented her from leaving her Beijing neighbourhood without explanation. Yu was detained after advocating constitutional reform and charged with inciting subversion. His detention is part of a crackdown on legal activists and harassment of their families.

Horses4Heroes has opened registration for Las Vegas camps for children ages 5–13 at its Equestrian Center in Floyd Lamb Park. Saturday camps run through May 19, Spring Break Camp runs March 26–30, and 10 weeks of weekday summer camp begin May 29. Activities include horseback riding, animal interactions, park tours, outings, bowling, karate and water slides. Reduced rates are available for military members, veterans, first responders, teachers and nurses. Teen volunteers ages 14–17 may earn community service hours. Camp proceeds support animal care and scholarships. Registration is available at horses4heroes.myonlinecamp.com. The nonprofit also provides lessons, workshops and other equestrian programs, including free workshops for community members facing challenges.

The President returns without approval a bill doubling Andrew J. Hill’s pension, noting that the Pension Bureau recently found his existing pension commensurate with his disability. He argues that Congress should rarely override the Bureau through special legislation, since frequent intervention may encourage weak claims, discredit the established review system, and foster prejudice against deserving veterans. Of nearly 240 special pension bills recently submitted, 232 included claims denied for insufficient evidence, preexisting or post-service disabilities, disabilities not incurred in duty, lack of legal authorization, or claims never presented to the Bureau. He approved 81 cases with insufficient testimony, while other bills, estimated to cost over $35,000 annually, will become law without his approval because time prevented full review. The returned bill also incorrectly names the beneficiary as Andrew J. Hill, while records identify him as Alfred J. Hill.

Education requires comprehensive renewal because society, technology, and learners are changing rapidly. Schools should remain focused on developing the whole person while critically evaluating change. Millennials, Generation Z, and Generation Alpha form a Net generation with distinct goals, motivations, and ways of processing information, requiring learner-centred, blended, and non-formal approaches.

Physical and cyber worlds increasingly overlap, while artificial intelligence, robots, intelligent agents, and hybrid entities perform cognitive and psychomotor activities. Successive waves of technological innovation—from steam power and electricity to computing, the Internet, and generative AI—have transformed work, society, and education through “creative destruction.” The sixth wave emerged through advances in transformer architecture, large language models, and generative AI.

Education initially responded to generative AI with denial, criticism, and concern before moving toward acceptance. Web 4.0-based generative AI is expected to affect economies, politics, cultures, work, and knowledge production rapidly. This raises unresolved questions about teachers, educational content, knowledge, and assessment.

The passage proposes a shift from digital pedagogy, where technology is treated as a tool, to generative pedagogy, where generative AI functions as a partner. Teachers will no longer be the sole authorities or carriers of knowledge; their role will increasingly emphasize relationships, values, and the affective domain. Education must prepare for human–AI symbiosis through a rapid transition to this new pedagogical model.

Xiaomi’s Mi 8 models feature Snapdragon 845 chips, 6GB RAM, 6.21-inch AMOLED displays, dual-frequency GPS, dual 12-megapixel rear cameras and AI photography tools. The 1,799-yuan Mi 8 SE uses Snapdragon 710 and has a 3,120mAh battery.

The Mid Screen, in which a big player screens for a smaller ballhandler, is widely used and can create penetration, post mismatches, or outside shots. NBA teams generally avoid switching and instead use “Show & Recover.” The on-ball defender pushes the ballhandler toward the sideline while the screener’s defender steps out to impede progress. Help defenders deny passes and protect against the roll. Once the original defender recovers, the big defender returns to the post, and the defense matches up with denial and weakside help positions.

An alternative, “All Out SOS Disruption,” traps the point guard before the screen develops, forcing the offense out of its planned action. Help defenders rotate to cover the rolling post and passing options. When the ball leaves the trap, defenders rotate using the near-player concept, deny return passes, close out aggressively, and reestablish SOS positioning. Subsequent baseline drives or post entries trigger designated trap rotations.

Reports suggest Nintendo may end NES Classic Mini production, with final shipments expected by April or May. A NeoGAF member claiming to work for a Nordic retailer said Nintendo confirmed production had ended, while a Norwegian retailer indicated similar final shipments. It remains unclear whether the reported stock ending applies only to Norway or worldwide.

ChatGPT is an OpenAI language model that can assist traders by analyzing sentiment from financial news and social media, generating technical indicators, coding trading strategies and algorithms, and producing forecasts from historical data. Traders can specify a platform or programming language, compile and debug the generated code, and backtest strategies before cautiously testing them with small amounts in live markets.

ChatGPT does not provide guaranteed profitable strategies or automate trading by itself. Its outputs may contain errors, inaccurate predictions, overconfident claims, biases, or unusable code. Therefore, traders should validate its insights with other sources, check code for bugs, backtest generated strategies, and combine its output with their own knowledge and methods.

In an example, ChatGPT created logical rules and Amibroker code for an RSI-based mean-reversion strategy, but the strategy generated few trades and the code contained many errors. The passage concludes that ChatGPT is useful for ideas and hints but cannot be expected to produce consistently correct results. It also describes AI pattern trading as using algorithms to identify recurring market patterns, offering speed and adaptability while facing unpredictable market conditions and algorithmic bias.

Cell2Text is a multimodal generative framework that converts single-cell RNA-sequencing profiles into natural-language descriptions of cell type, tissue, disease, developmental stage, and pathway activity. It uses a frozen Geneformer encoder to retain gene-level embeddings, a lightweight adapter to project them into language-model space, and an instruction-tuned Llama-1B or Gemma-4B decoder. The language models are adapted through full fine-tuning or LoRA.

The authors constructed a dataset of one million CELLxGENE cells from 7,331 donors, covering 783 cell types, 347 tissues, 128 diseases, and 34 Hallmark pathways, with donor-level train, validation, and test splits. Cell2Text was evaluated on text quality and classifications parsed from generated descriptions. Fully tuned models achieved BioBERT semantic F1 scores above 93.9%. Gemma-4B reached 77.83% cell-type accuracy and 73.04% tissue accuracy, while Llama-1B achieved 77.84% disease accuracy; these models generally outperformed Geneformer linear-head and LightGBM baselines. Ontology-based PageRank evaluation gave Gemma-4B an 85.62% cell-type similarity score, indicating biologically related predictions even when labels were incorrect. For pathway identification, Cell2Text surpassed the linear-head baseline but remained below LightGBM on several metrics. Overall, the results suggest that generating descriptions can produce rich, interpretable cellular representations while retaining competitive classification performance.

Bandai Namco announced Super Robot Wars X for PS4 and Vita, launching March 29, 2018 in Japan and April 26 in Southeast Asia with English subtitles. Japan receives a Premium Edition and early-purchase bonuses.

The November 9, 2000 Haas Alumni weekly bulletin lists 20 job opportunities, primarily in California, Texas, Chicago, New York and the Southwest. Roles include CEO, senior vice president/general manager, CIO, business manager, nonprofit project manager and CFO, investment analysts, marketing and product managers, contracts manager, financial consultant, technology equity research associate, CPA, consultants and software-related positions. Employers include Applied Materials, BRIDGE Housing, Public Advocates, AXA Rosenberg, NetCurrents, SmartForce, McGraw Hill, Vividence, UCSF, Hewlett-Packard, Wedbush Morgan Securities, Aetna and Extensity. The bulletin provides detailed responsibilities, requirements, compensation information and application contacts for many roles. It also announces a Women in Leadership Conference on November 11 and a Big Game barbecue on November 18. Haas notes that listed employers and search firms have not been researched and advises alumni to investigate them.

The volume documents Secretary of State George Shultz’s bureaucratic struggle to implement NSDD 75’s four-part agenda, gain regular access to President Reagan, and preserve dialogue with the Soviet Union despite opposition and crises in 1983. Shultz and NSC adviser Jack Matlock promoted communication amid the KAL 007 downing, Reagan’s Strategic Defense Initiative, INF missile deployments, the Soviet “War Scare,” and Able Archer. After the Soviet withdrawal from INF negotiations, the administration spent 1984 developing a framework for renewed arms-control talks, with SDI remaining a central dispute. In January 1985, Shultz and Gromyko agreed to three-track Nuclear and Space Talks covering START, INF, and Defense and Space. The documents trace competing agency positions and show arms control taking precedence over other agenda areas. The acknowledgments credit archival, intelligence, defense, editorial, review, and declassification staff who supported the volume.

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study examined whether oxytocin selectively enhances responses to gentle stroking that targets C-touch fibers and whether intranasal and oral administration produce similar effects. Of 180 healthy Chinese adults, data from 171 were analyzed after participants received 24 IU intranasal oxytocin, oral oxytocin, or placebo. Participants experienced gentle stroking and medium-pressure massage while behavioral ratings, plasma oxytocin, physiological responses, and cortical activity measured by functional near-infrared spectroscopy were recorded.

Both administration routes increased plasma oxytocin, although the initial increase was greater after intranasal treatment. Intranasal and oral oxytocin selectively increased the perceived pleasantness of gentle stroking but not medium-pressure massage. Neither route affected ratings of arousal, intensity, willingness to pay, heart-rate variability, or skin conductance. Both routes also enhanced responses to gentle stroking in the medial and mediolateral orbitofrontal cortex and posterior superior temporal sulcus, while producing no significant neural effects during medium-pressure massage. Neural response patterns distinguished each oxytocin group from placebo but not intranasal from oral administration.

Post-treatment plasma oxytocin increases correlated with pleasantness ratings and mediolateral orbitofrontal activity during gentle stroking. Mediation analyses indicated that plasma oxytocin changes mediated the behavioral effects of both administration routes, but not their neural effects. The findings suggest that exogenous oxytocin selectively facilitates hedonic and cortical responses to C-touch-fiber stimulation through primarily peripheral mechanisms. Limitations included the superficial cortical coverage of functional near-infrared spectroscopy, the controlled and relatively unnatural touch setting, lack of direct pressure measurement, and limited blood-sampling frequency.

The disclosure describes a smart gateway platform for industrial IoT analytics. Users select a model template associated with a business objective, such as reducing downtime, improving quality, increasing throughput, or optimizing energy use. Templates encode domain expertise by identifying relevant industrial data and defining correlations or causal relationships among data inputs. Users map these inputs to actual industrial-device tags, producing a customized analytic model.

The platform collects only the mapped data, normalizes disparate formats, contextualizes raw data, adds modeling and AI metadata, synchronizes related values, and organizes data according to asset or enterprise hierarchies. It can process both conventional tags and contextualized smart tags representing states, rates, cumulative quantities, and events. The resulting structured data is sent to AI, machine-learning, or statistical analytics systems operating at device, edge, enterprise, or cloud levels.

By constraining analysis to relevant, pre-modeled data, the platform seeks to reduce storage and processing requirements, shorten time to actionable insights, and limit spurious correlations compared with unconstrained big-data analysis. Analytic results may generate visualizations, predictions, recommendations, notifications, or automated control actions that modify industrial-device or system operation.
A 29-year-old Essex man was charged with impaired driving after crashing into a gas meter on Ridge Road, causing a leak. He was uninjured and is scheduled to appear in Windsor court June 13.

The nation enjoys abundant harvests, flourishing commerce, strong revenue, and peaceful foreign relations. Negotiations with Britain cover commerce and unresolved issues, while the existing convention is extended for at least eight years. Relations with Spain remain unsettled over claims, boundaries, and Florida, where weakened Spanish authority enabled lawlessness, attacks, and the Seminole conflict. U.S. forces suppressed Amelia Island and pursued hostile groups into Florida; Pensacola and St. Marks were taken after alleged Spanish assistance to them, but their restoration was ordered to preserve friendly relations. Related documents will be submitted to Congress.

South American conflicts with Spain continue, and the United States is advised to maintain its existing policy. Relations with France, Russia, and other powers remain friendly. Treasury receipts, customs revenue, and public-land sales are strong, with a surplus expected after debt payments. Congress is invited to consider further protection for domestic manufactures.

Fortifications, coastal surveys, naval depots, and naval expansion are progressing. Treaties with several Indigenous tribes produced extensive territorial cessions, and further negotiations continue. New frontier posts are intended to improve security and promote federal control and the transformation of Indigenous communities.

Illinois has joined the Union, strengthening the federal system, western development, commerce, and national cohesion. Congress is also asked to consider improved governance for the District. The address concludes with gratitude for national blessings.

A Nature study led by University of Texas at Austin researchers warns that hundreds of built and proposed Amazon hydroelectric dams could trap nutrient-rich sediments, disrupt river and floodplain dynamics, threaten biodiversity and food supplies, and alter climate patterns as far as the Gulf of Mexico. South American developers have proposed 428 dams, with 140 built or under construction. Researchers created the Dam Environmental Vulnerability Index to measure risks from land-use change, erosion, pollution, sediment trapping and river-system disruption. The Marañon, Ucayali and Madeira rivers were identified as especially vulnerable. Two recently built Madeira dams coincided with a 20 percent decline in average sediment concentration, while 25 more are planned upstream. The Tapajós and its tributaries could also become extensively impounded if 90 proposed dams proceed. Researchers argue that cumulative sediment losses could damage wetlands, forests, fisheries and coastal mangroves while affecting rainfall, storms and regional climate.

The paper addresses unstable robot motion caused by inconsistencies between successive environment maps in partially observed, unstructured terrain. It extends the deterministic Kinodynamic Efficiently Adaptive State Lattice planner to compute edge costs using multiple temporally sampled world hypotheses while requiring final trajectories to remain collision-free in the latest map.

Four methods are examined. Valid in Every Hypothesis avoids obstacles in all maps but is overly conservative. Per-Edge Hypothesis reroutes invalid edges for each map but is computationally impractical. Goal-Edge Hypothesis delays rerouting until reaching the goal but concentrates search near the goal. Goal-Edge Graph Revision Hypothesis (GEGRH) adds graph revision to focus search at points where map hypotheses diverge.

Experiments used 221 planning problems from unmanned ground vehicle field data, with two or three successive maps, ARA* search, and a one-second planning limit. Compared with Valid in Every Hypothesis, GEGRH reduced average planning time by 15.4% with two hypotheses and 29.27% with three. It reduced path duration by 6.64% and 18.72%, respectively. GEGRH generally produced less conservative trajectories, though rerouting overhead sometimes caused suboptimal results within the time limit. Future work includes adding more hypotheses, considering non-binary map differences, varying cost functions, and incorporating hypothesis certainty.

President Trump condemned racism, white supremacists, neo-Nazis, the KKK and other hate groups following deadly violence in Charlottesville. The statement came after bipartisan criticism of his earlier attribution of blame to “many sides” and nearly 48 hours of silence. Trump later criticized Merck CEO Ken Frazier for resigning from his manufacturing council over Trump’s initial response.

Microsoft’s fiscal 2020 second-quarter Form 10-Q reported revenue of $36.9 billion, up 14% year over year; operating income of $13.9 billion, up 35%; net income of $11.6 billion, up 38%; and diluted earnings per share of $1.51, up 40%. Six-month revenue was $70.0 billion, operating income $26.6 billion, and net income $22.3 billion.

Quarterly segment revenue was $11.8 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $11.9 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $13.2 billion for More Personal Computing. Commercial cloud revenue rose 39% to $12.5 billion, with Azure revenue up 62%, Office 365 Commercial up 27%, LinkedIn up 24%, and Windows OEM up 18%; Xbox content and services revenue declined 11%.

At December 31, 2019, Microsoft had $282.8 billion in assets, $134.3 billion in cash, equivalents, and short-term investments, $172.7 billion in liabilities, and $110.1 billion in stockholders’ equity. Six-month operating cash flow was $24.5 billion. Microsoft repurchased $8.6 billion of shares and declared dividends totaling $1.02 per share during fiscal 2020’s first half.

Following their 2025 playoff elimination by Toronto, the Yankees could pursue trades and roster changes. Steven Kwan is predicted as a potential 2026 leadoff hitter, while Josh Naylor could play first base, potentially replacing Trent Grisham and Paul Goldschmidt. Most core players are expected to remain.

Gartner analysts Stephen Kleynhans and Michael Silver argue that Microsoft is making Windows 10 Pro unsuitable for enterprises by limiting its support and enterprise management features. While Enterprise and Education editions received extended 24-month support for several releases and can purchase an additional 12 months, Pro remains limited to 18 months. Gartner recommends that businesses using Pro monitor Microsoft’s policies and budget for Enterprise, as Pro is increasingly positioned for “pro-sumer” and small-business users.

Bridgewater Associates founder Ray Dalio recommends allocating up to 15% of portfolios to gold, calling it a strong diversifier and hedge against monetary debasement and geopolitical uncertainty. Gold surpassed $4,000 an ounce after rising more than 50% this year amid fiscal deficits and global tensions. Dalio compared current conditions—high inflation, government spending and debt—to the early 1970s, arguing debt instruments may not effectively preserve wealth.

The divisional Australian patent application describes novel ionizable cationic lipids, including Formula (I) compounds and their salts, tautomers, prodrugs, stereoisomers, isotopically labelled forms, and metabolites. These lipids can combine with neutral or charged lipids, steroids such as cholesterol, and polymer-conjugated lipids such as PEGylated lipids to form lipid nanoparticles for delivering therapeutic agents, particularly nucleic acids.

The nanoparticles are intended to protect nucleic acids from serum degradation, promote cellular uptake and intracellular delivery, support systemic or local administration, improve in vivo activity and tolerability, and increase therapeutic index. Payloads may include mRNA, antisense oligonucleotides, plasmid DNA, siRNA, miRNA, miRNA inhibitors, cDNA, multivalent RNA, and related nucleic acids. Applications include inducing desired protein expression, increasing endogenous protein expression through miRNA inhibition, suppressing target genes or proteins, expressing transgenes, co-delivering different nucleic acids, and treating or preventing diseases associated with infectious entities or protein insufficiency.

The passage details structural variations and representative compounds within Formula (I), along with compositions containing therapeutic agents and optional excipients. Lipid nanoparticles may encapsulate nucleic acids fully or partially and commonly have mean diameters of about 30–150 nm.

Methods for producing, purifying, and modifying mRNA are described, including in vitro transcription, removal of double-stranded RNA contaminants, 5′ capping, polyadenylation, modified nucleosides, and untranslated-region optimization. Preparation methods for oligonucleotides and plasmid DNA are also outlined.

The compositions may be formulated in solid, liquid, semisolid, or aerosol dosage forms and administered through oral, topical, transdermal, inhaled, parenteral, sublingual, buccal, rectal, vaginal, intranasal, intravenous, intraarterial, subcutaneous, intramuscular, intradermal, or intraperitoneal routes. Dosage depends on the therapeutic agent, patient, administration method, and condition being treated.
John Howendobler was jailed after reporting that he choked his wife shortly before 1:30 a.m. Friday. His wife said he awoke suddenly, apparently from a bad dream, and began choking her.

Liverpool Instagram jewellery brand Say It With Diamonds has opened its first city-centre store in Cavern Walks. Founded in 2016 by Charlotte Donoghue and Steph Porter, the company offers affordable luxury jewellery, including engagement and wedding rings and its popular initial necklaces. After strong online growth and attracting celebrity clients, the founders hope the shop will support further expansion.

Mental health care is often neglected in low- and middle-income countries until conflict draws international attention. In South Sudan, its only mental health facility lacked adequate medication, care and funding before civil war prompted support for traumatized civilians. Untreated mental disorders are linked to physical illness and substance abuse, further straining fragile health systems. Low-income countries average one psychiatrist per two million people and devote less than one percent of health budgets to mental health, often prioritizing institutions over prevention and community outreach. The passage calls for increased funding, professional training, community-based services and efforts to reduce stigma, emphasizing that mental health treatment is a human right essential to development and should not depend on conflict.

President Donald Trump announced a deal for AstraZeneca to offer discounted prescription drugs through TrumpRx and provide Medicaid prices comparable to the lowest charged internationally. The UK-based pharmaceutical company also pledged $50 billion for US research, drug development, and manufacturing over five years. The agreement follows a similar deal with Pfizer involving reduced prices and a three-year tariff exemption.

Shriram Transport Finance said promoters are discussing repayment with SVL Group amid concerns over an Rs 870 crore guarantee for debentures maturing in June 2019. Its shares fell 11.83%, while the company said alternate settlement mechanisms were available.

Veeco Instruments published a slide deck for its Axcelis Technologies M&A call. The passage also describes Seeking Alpha’s transcript coverage, lists investment articles, and references a September 29–October 3, 2025 chart.

Britain’s Co-operative Group lost £132 million in 2016 after valuing its 20% stake in the struggling Co-operative Bank at nil. Despite the write-off, operating profit rose 32% to £148 million, supported by growth in supermarkets, funeral services and insurance. Supermarket like-for-like sales increased 3.5%, while food prices began rising after two years of declines. The group is sourcing more British products to meet customer demand and reduce exposure to import costs. The bank remains for sale.

Matthew Lane, a 19-year-old Massachusetts college student, pleaded guilty to hacking education technology company PowerSchool and stealing sensitive records belonging to more than 60 million students and 10 million educators. Prosecutors say Lane and an unnamed co-conspirator demanded about $2.85 million in Bitcoin to prevent the data from being published. The breach cost PowerSchool more than $14 million, including ransom and identity-protection expenses.

Federal prosecutors seek seven years in prison, more than $14 million in restitution and describe Lane’s conduct as sophisticated and part of cybercriminal activity dating to 2021. Investigators say he used stolen credentials, foreign servers, VPNs, anonymized communications and cryptocurrency tools. About $3 million remains unaccounted for, while Lane returned roughly $160,000.

Cybersecurity firm Cyble linked Lane to several online aliases associated with attacks on educational, government and corporate targets, including the Massachusetts Interscholastic Athletic Association, foreign entities and private companies. Cyble concluded the PowerSchool breach was an escalation of years of activity rather than a first offense. Prosecutors also allege Lane and a collaborator previously extorted a telecommunications company.

Friends, neighbors and a former professor described Lane as quiet, introverted, skilled at programming and interested in gaming. Online, however, accounts linked to him adopted conspicuous personas and boasted about hacking. Investigators may have identified him partly after an account previously protected by a VPN connected from his family home.

PowerSchool initially denied being a ransomware victim but later acknowledged paying an extortion demand. Some school districts subsequently received additional ransom threats involving the stolen records. PowerSchool says it notified customers, provided updates and continues cooperating with districts and law enforcement. Lane is scheduled for federal sentencing.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 29, 2018 reported net sales of $84.3 billion, down 5% year over year, and net income of $20.0 billion, compared with $20.1 billion. Diluted earnings per share rose to $4.18 from $3.89. Product sales declined to $73.4 billion, while services sales increased to $10.9 billion.

iPhone sales fell 15% to $52.0 billion, reflecting lower unit sales across all geographic segments. Mac sales rose 9%, iPad 17%, Wearables, Home and Accessories 33%, and Services 19%. Americas sales increased 5%, while Europe declined 3%, Greater China 27%, and Japan 5%; Rest of Asia Pacific rose 1%. Foreign-currency weakness adversely affected sales.

Gross margin was $32.0 billion, or 38.0% of sales, compared with 38.4% a year earlier. Operating expenses increased to $8.7 billion, including $3.9 billion in research and development. Operating income declined to $23.3 billion. The effective tax rate decreased to 16.5% from 25.8%.

At quarter-end, Apple had $373.7 billion in assets, $255.8 billion in liabilities and $117.9 billion in shareholders’ equity. Apple repurchased $8.2 billion of stock and paid $3.6 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents.

Apple adopted new standards covering revenue recognition, financial instruments and intra-entity asset transfers. It reported $12.0 billion of commercial paper and $103.8 billion of term debt. The company identified supply concentration, foreign exchange, litigation and other business risks, including disputes involving VirnetX, Qualcomm and iPhone performance management. Dobbins together in the backfield. Linebacker Chris Worley is probable, while Dre’Mont Jones and Erick Smith will miss the game; Antonio Williams is questionable.

The patent describes sustainable molded-fiber containers intended to replace single-use plastics in food, beverage, horticultural, shipping, and utility applications. Products are vacuum formed from fiber-and-water slurries, then wet-pressed or dry-cured. A closed-loop system recirculates slurry and monitors chemical additives.

Slurries may use softwood, bagasse, bamboo, corrugated-container fiber, or newsprint, combined with additives providing moisture, oil, and vapor resistance, dry and wet strength, rigidity, color, and chemical retention. Formulations are tailored for produce containers, microwave- and oven-safe food containers, meat trays, beverage lids, and non-food packaging. Surface coatings, fiber refining, and reduced porosity can further improve barrier performance.

Structural features such as rolled edges, skirts, shelves, ribs, and varied wall angles increase rigidity and help maintain strength under moist conditions. Directional spray nozzles remove excess fiber around mold inserts to create larger ventilation holes without modifying existing molds. Beverage lids may incorporate zero or negative draft locking rings; a mold with a pneumatically extended retractable piston releases such lids after pressing.

The disclosure also provides manufacturing methods and preferred additive ranges for specific products, including moisture-resistant produce containers, low-porosity coated containers, microwavable containers with moisture and oil barriers, meat trays, beverage lids, and shipping components. The described technologies may also be adapted to other fiber-based manufacturing methods, including 3D printing.

The South Dakota Department of Agriculture asks producers who suspect dicamba-related crop damage to complete its online Dicamba Damage Survey. Results will help evaluate statewide impacts. Producers may also complete the survey at the department’s Dakotafest booth in Mitchell, Aug. 15–17.

Founded in 2010, Spartan Race became a leading obstacle course race provider, reporting one million participants at about 130 events across more than 25 countries in 2016. Unlike competitors emphasizing accessibility, fun, or teamwork, Spartan focused on timed competition, individual athleticism, varied race distances, and penalties for failed obstacles. After raising $15 million in private equity, founder and CEO Joe De Sena considered an initial public offering in 2017 and questioned how the new revenue recognition standard would affect Spartan’s financial statements and reported growth.

The standard requires companies to identify contracts and performance obligations, determine transaction prices, allocate prices among multiple obligations, and recognize revenue when each obligation is satisfied. Contracts require agreement, commercial substance, specified payment terms, and probable collection. Transaction prices must account for discounts, refunds, variable consideration, delayed payment, and noncash compensation. Product revenue is recognized when customers obtain control, while service revenue is recognized upon completion or over the service period.

Spartan’s revenue sources include walk-up and advance race entries, annual race passes, merchandise, sponsorship agreements, trainer certification programs, and international licensing. These activities involve differing terms, including complimentary volunteer entries, nonrefundable purchases, race deferrals, merchandise returns, multi-period sponsorship services, renewable certifications, royalties, and sales of obstacles or logistical services to international licensees. De Sena sought guidance on how the standard would affect the amount and timing of revenue reported for these varied activities.

Philadelphia City Council will consider amended bills authorizing the $500 million “Rebuild” project to renovate up to 200 parks, recreation centers and libraries over seven years. The revisions strengthen local, women and minority hiring. Work depends on resolving legal challenges to the beverage tax financing it.

McLaren’s new 4.0-liter twin-turbo M840T V8 succeeds the 3.8-liter M838T and will debut in the 720S, producing 720 PS (710 bhp). McLaren says the 720S reaches 200 km/h in 7.8 seconds and completes a quarter mile in 10.3 seconds. The engine offers improved power, torque, response, efficiency, emissions, and reduced turbo lag. Full specifications are due in March.

NVIDIA’s fiscal 2018 third-quarter revenue rose 32% year over year to $2.64 billion, operating income increased 40% to $895 million, and net income grew 55% to $838 million, or $1.33 per diluted share. James Hodgkinson, 66, of Belleville, Illinois, shot Rep. Steve Scalise and several others during Republican lawmakers’ baseball practice in Alexandria, Virginia. Hodgkinson died after a police shootout. Scalise remained in critical condition after surgery, while other victims included a Capitol Police officer, staffer and lobbyist. The FBI investigated Hodgkinson’s motives, social media and associates. Rep. Claudia Tenney later received a threatening email referencing additional targets.

The ADS7828 SAR converter is sensitive to power, reference, ground, and digital-input transients during conversion. Use a clean, well-bypassed supply, placing a 0.1µF ceramic capacitor near the device and adding 1µF–10µF when supply-connection impedance is high. External-reference noise, especially when tied to the supply, directly affects digital results; line-frequency variation may be difficult to filter. Connect GND to a clean, preferably analog, ground away from digital processors.

Preproduction parts may be experimental, incompletely qualified, subject to change or discontinuation, and sold without warranties. The speaker says Calgary has become more defensive, while his team remains focused on its own approach, maintaining momentum and responding well after losses. Special teams are especially important in a low-chance series, though the team has struggled recently despite scoring a key goal. He describes the league as increasingly defensive, with better goaltending making goals difficult, but says each team must follow its own concept. He declines to discuss injury updates. He praises a player who progressed from uncertainty in the minor leagues to a trusted, defensively responsible NHL contributor with untapped offensive potential. He also expresses concern about blows to the head against defenseless players. With the series tied, he views Game 5 simply as the next step toward four wins.

Henry Grivi sought mandamus compelling the Los Angeles Superior Court to remove a presiding judge’s report from the McAdoo divorce case. The report criticized Grivi for bypassing established trial-setting procedures and taking the case directly to a visiting judge, although it acknowledged that the irregularity did not affect the divorce decree. The court held that while the presiding judge could investigate rule violations and potentially initiate contempt or disciplinary proceedings, the report concerned counsel’s conduct rather than issues in the divorce action. Because it resulted from an ex parte administrative investigation without notice or jurisdiction over Grivi, it could not properly be filed in that case. A peremptory writ ordering its removal was issued.

Andrew Ladd was an effective, rugged playoff player in Carolina. Dustin Byfuglien’s size, scoring and net-front presence pose a challenge, though the team’s defense has performed well. Previous coaching experience can help prepare a roster with limited finals experience. Repeated setbacks since Christmas strengthened the players’ belief in one another, leaving them unlikely to be overwhelmed.

The coach expressed gratitude to Paul and the organization for the opportunity to return after a year out of work. Mike Richards leads by example through toughness, effort and decisive plays. Chicago is dynamic, quick in transition and confident in its system, requiring careful puck management. Philadelphia feels prepared for the series. Its goaltending has succeeded by committee: Ray Emery played well when healthy, Brian Boucher posted strong numbers, and Michael Leighton returned from injury without losing form.

The passage describes targeted cancer-detection assays that analyze abnormal DNA methylation patterns in cell-free DNA. Large panels of oligonucleotide probes capture converted cfDNA from genomic regions that are differentially hypermethylated or hypomethylated in cancer versus non-cancer samples. Regions and probes are selected using methylation rarity, cancer and control sample counts, CpG density, overlap, tiling, and off-target criteria. Captured fragments are sequenced, and methylation-derived feature vectors are evaluated by trained classifiers to determine cancer presence, stage, type, or tissue of origin. The disclosure also covers assay-panel design, probe synthesis, PCR-based enrichment, classifier training, diagnostic and treatment methods, numerous probe and performance specifications, and genomic regions identified in Lists 1–8. Definitions address methylation, CpG and UpG sites, methylation vectors, anomalous patterns, and cancerous and non-cancerous samples.

A reconfigurable hardware switch uses ingress and egress pipelines containing a parser, match-action unit (MAU), and deparser. The parser separates packet headers from payload and places header fields potentially used or modified by the MAU into a primary packet header vector (PPHV). Unused fields are placed into a secondary packet header vector (SPHV), which bypasses the MAU and goes directly to the deparser. The MAU matches PPHV fields against exact or ternary tables, performs actions such as modifying headers, selecting ports or queues, sending packets to a controller, or dropping packets. The deparser reconstructs each packet from the processed PPHV, unprocessed SPHV, and payload, then sends it to the queuing system or out of the switch.

A control-plane compiler generates parser and MAU configuration data from switch-programming code, parse graphs, and control and table-flow graphs. This data identifies packet formats, parsing paths, participating fields, register placement, and match-action behavior. Separating participating from nonparticipating fields conserves MAU resources, simplifies wiring, and allows parsing deeper into packets—including long or multilayer tunnel headers—without increasing the data sent through the MAU.

E-mini S&P 500 futures are CME-traded derivatives tracking the S&P 500 index. Introduced in 1997, they are one-fifth the size of standard S&P 500 futures and are widely used for speculation, hedging, arbitrage, and spread trading. Each contract equals the index value multiplied by $50 and is financially settled in cash using special opening index quotes.

Contracts trade electronically on CME Globex from Sunday through Friday, generally 6:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. ET, with a daily one-hour break. Quarterly contracts cover March, June, September, and December. Trading normally ends at 9:30 a.m. ET on the third Friday of the contract month.

The minimum price fluctuation is 0.25 index points, worth $12.50, for outright Globex trading. BTIC, TACO, and calendar spreads have a 0.05-point minimum, worth $2.50. There is no block-trade eligibility.

Trading requires a funded futures brokerage account and margin. Leverage creates significant risk because losses are based on full contract value rather than deposited margin. CFDs may offer similar exposure but, unlike futures, do not have fixed expiration dates.

The passage describes a paywalled mean-reversion strategy backtested on daily, continuous, back-adjusted CME data without risk-management parameters. It also states that futures historically performed better in winter and spring than summer. Reported extremes were 665.75 in March 2009 and 4808.25 in January 2022.

Poland plans to invest 20 billion zlotys ($5.5 billion) to connect its fuel pipeline network to NATO’s Central Europe Pipeline System. The project will add about 300 kilometres of infrastructure and new storage facilities, improving military supply security and readiness. NATO has committed 60 million zlotys for planning and design. Construction will take several years and may face coordination, regulatory, delay, and cost risks.

Fifth Third Bank will acquire Comerica in a $10.9 billion all-stock deal, creating the ninth-largest U.S. lender with about $288 billion in assets. Pending regulatory approval, the merger is expected to close in early 2026 and expand Fifth Third’s presence in Florida, Arizona, California and the Southeast. Comerica shareholders will receive nearly 1.9 Fifth Third shares per share, valued at about $82.88 and representing a 20% premium. Supporters cite greater scale and stronger commercial, payments and wealth management operations, while critics warn of increased systemic risks from banking consolidation.

The lecture reviews Poisson processes as arrival processes with IID exponential interarrival times, equivalent representations through interarrival times, arrival epochs, and counting processes. Their memoryless property implies that the waiting time from any fixed time to the next arrival remains exponential. Counts over disjoint intervals are independent and depend only on interval length, while \(N(t)\) has Poisson PMF \(e^{-\lambda t}(\lambda t)^n/n!\). Equivalent definitions use stationary independent increments together with either Poisson counts or small-increment probabilities.

Independent Poisson processes with rates \(\lambda_1\) and \(\lambda_2\) combine into a Poisson process of rate \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2\). Conversely, independently assigning each arrival of a rate-\(\lambda\) process to two outputs with probabilities \(p\) and \(1-p\) produces independent Poisson processes with corresponding rates. Combining and splitting can simplify queueing problems; for a last-come, first-served queue with arrival rate \(\lambda\) and service rate \(\mu\), service completes before interruption with probability \(\mu/(\lambda+\mu)\).

Non-homogeneous Poisson processes have time-varying rates. Counts remain Poisson, with parameters determined by the total arrival rate over an interval, though interarrival times are no longer IID exponential.

Conditioned on exactly \(n\) arrivals by time \(t\), the ordered arrival epochs have joint density \(n!/t^n\) over \(0<s_1<\cdots<s_n<t\). They are distributed like the order statistics of \(n\) IID uniform random variables on \([0,t]\). Consequently, the first arrival has complementary distribution \((1-s/t)^n\) and mean \(t/(n+1)\).

The lecture ends with the apparent paradox that an arbitrary observation time tends to fall within an interarrival interval longer than the mean \(1/\lambda\), because longer intervals occupy proportionally more time and are therefore more likely to contain the observation point.

A Death Cross occurs when a short-term moving average, usually the 50-day, falls below a long-term average, usually the 200-day. Distributed-system patterns capture prior experience, establish shared terminology, and enable reusable components that improve consistency, quality, and development speed. Containers support these patterns by defining resource, ownership, and responsibility boundaries. Even on one machine, separating an application into focused containers enables resource isolation, modular team ownership, reuse, independent deployment, and easier testing.

Three single-node patterns are presented:

- **Sidecar:** A companion container augments an application while sharing resources such as networking, filesystems, or process namespaces. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service, synchronizing configuration, monitoring processes, and updating application code from Git. Reusable sidecars should be parameterized, expose stable APIs, and include clear documentation and metadata.
- **Ambassador:** A container brokers communication between an application and external services. It can route requests to sharded storage, discover environment-specific services, or split traffic between production and experimental versions.
- **Adapter:** A container transforms an application’s interface into a standard form. Uses include converting metrics for Prometheus, normalizing logs with fluentd, redirecting logs to standard output, and providing richer health checks without modifying the original application.

Multi-node patterns build loosely coupled distributed systems from networked components. Microservices divide applications into independently maintained services with defined APIs, improving team autonomy, release agility, reuse, and independent scaling. Their disadvantages include more difficult debugging, coordination, and architecture.

Replicated load-balanced services use interchangeable instances behind a load balancer to provide availability and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching instances before initialization. Session-tracked services route a user consistently to one replica, often through hashing, cookies, or headers. Additional replicated layers can provide caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination.

Sharded services divide state among machines, with a router directing requests to the appropriate shard. Sharded caches improve memory utilization by avoiding duplicate cached data, but shard failures can reduce capacity and increase latency. Replicating each shard improves resilience and supports independent scaling. Shard routing may use per-client ambassadors or a shared routing service, with trade-offs in deployment complexity, scalability, latency, and network use. Effective sharding functions must be deterministic and distribute requests uniformly.

The passage specifies SD Memory Card physical-layer behavior, commands, states, data transfers, protection, switching, timing, and error handling.

CMD19 tuning consists of consecutive executions without intervening commands; 40 executions must complete within 150 ms, excluding host processing time. During card identification, the host remains at identification frequency, then may switch frequencies in Data Transfer Mode. CMD7 selects one card for Transfer State and deselects others; addressed data communication is point-to-point.

CMD12 can abort read and write transfers. Completed writes move to Programming State when successful or Transfer State when failed. DAT0 indicates busy status. Programming restricts parameter-setting and read commands, while deselection can move a busy card to Disconnect State without terminating programming or erase. Reset commands terminate active programming and may destroy data. ACMD6 selects 1-bit or 4-bit bus operation, but locked cards reject it.

Reads and writes use block-oriented transfers with CRC protection. Maximum memory-access block size is 512 bytes, with partial-block and alignment behavior determined by card capabilities. CMD17 reads one block; CMD18 reads continuously until CMD12. Writes with invalid CRC are discarded. Multiple-block writes are preferred for speed, and ACMD23 may pre-erase blocks. ACMD22 reports successfully written blocks after errors.

Erase operations use CMD32, CMD33, then CMD38. Protected sectors remain intact. DISCARD uses CMD38 argument 00000001h, may partially or completely deallocate blocks, is limited to SDHC/SDXC outside SPI, and has a 250 ms busy timeout. FULE uses argument 00000002h to logically erase the full user area, is similarly limited, and has a one-second timeout. Unsupported DISCARD or FULE requests execute ERASE.

Write protection includes a host-managed mechanical switch, optional internal protection, and password locking. CMD42 manages passwords, locking, unlocking, clearing passwords, and force erase. Passwords are nonvolatile, and cards with passwords set lock after power-up. Card Ownership Protection adds a Force Erase Password, COP Unlock, protected force erase, and restrictions on clearing passwords. With FEP set, ordinary force erase and password clearing are disabled; FEP Force Erase requires the correct FEP and erases user data and PWD while retaining FEP. Errors set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED.

CMD55 marks the next command as application-specific. CMD6 checks or switches function groups, including access speed, command systems, driver strength, and power limits. Mode 0 queries support, busy status, and power consumption; Mode 1 changes functions. The default power limit is 0.72 W. High-Speed mode provides a 25 MB/s interface using a 50 MHz clock and requires one-to-one host-card signaling.

CMD8 checks whether Version 2.00-or-later cards support the host voltage and echoes a check pattern. SDSC cards use byte addressing and CMD16-defined block lengths, while SDHC/SDXC use 512-byte block addressing and disable partial or misaligned memory access.

Hosts may vary or stop the clock, subject to transaction-completion and ACMD41 requirements. Commands, responses, and data use CRC7 or CRC16 protection. CRC failures and illegal commands do not change card state and set status errors. Read timeout is generally capped at 100 ms; write busy is generally capped at 250 ms, though specified SDXC cases may extend to 500 ms.

The UC1825B-SP PCB layout should minimize noise and EMI. Route feedback traces directly and away from inductors and power traces, preferably on the opposite PCB side with a separating ground plane. Place ceramic input, feed-forward, and compensation capacitors close to the IC; surface-mount parts are recommended.

Keep high-current traces short, direct, and thick, with at least 15 mils per ampere. Place inductors, output capacitors, and diodes close together. Connect relevant grounds directly to a ground plane, using separate power and signal areas where appropriate. For multilayer boards, use approximately one standard via per 200 mA and arrange switching loops in the same direction to prevent magnetic-field reversal.

The 2-A peak output drivers require a designated power-ground area for PGND and high-di/dt currents. Connect VCC bypassing, MOSFET sources, input return, and bulk input capacitor to power ground; connect only these items there. Bypass VREF and analog circuitry to signal ground. Clamp outputs to VCC and PGND with high-current Schottky diodes.
