It advises comparing providers’ services and prices, reading customer reviews, requesting quotes, and contacting writers before choosing a service. Customers provide assignment requirements online, and the company completes the work remotely.

A 2008-to-present backtest of the NIFTY 50 cash index bought at the second Friday’s December close and exited on the new year’s first trading-day close. It produced a 1.2% average gain, 71% win rate, profit factor of 6, and 7% maximum drawdown, suggesting a Santa Claus Rally effect. The non-tradable cash index served as a proxy.

This study evaluated first-phase left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF-1) as an echocardiographic marker of cardiac dysfunction and coronary stenosis severity in patients with coronary heart disease whose conventional LVEF exceeded 50%. LVEF-1 measures left ventricular volume change from aortic valve opening to peak aortic flow velocity relative to end-diastolic volume.

From June 2021 to June 2023, 207 patients undergoing first-time coronary angiography for chest pain were classified as having mild (73), moderate (39), or severe (95) stenosis. As stenosis severity increased, LVEF-1 and global longitudinal strain decreased, while conventional LVEF did not differ significantly. LVEF-1 correlated negatively with Gensini score (r=-0.694) and B-type natriuretic peptide (r=-0.244), as well as several coronary risk factors.

LVEF-1 independently predicted stenosis of at least 50% and at least 70% after adjustment for clinical and laboratory variables. It had a greater diagnostic area under the ROC curve than global longitudinal strain, E/e′, LVEF, and left ventricular diastolic dimension. A 27.9% cutoff predicted stenosis ≥50% with 82.8% sensitivity and 83.6% specificity; a 26.9% cutoff predicted stenosis ≥70% with 89.5% sensitivity and 83.9% specificity.

Among 82 patients receiving PCI, LVEF-1 and global longitudinal strain increased and E/e′ decreased by postoperative day four, while LVEF showed no significant early change. Greater Gensini scores and larger stent diameters independently influenced LVEF-1 improvement.

The authors conclude that LVEF-1 may provide a simple, sensitive indicator of coronary stenosis-related cardiac dysfunction and early recovery after PCI. Limitations include the small sample, multicenter measurement differences, absence of coronary functional and microcirculatory assessments, and possible medication effects.

The Steelers unveiled 1978-inspired throwback jerseys commemorating the 40th anniversaries of their Super Bowl XIII and XIV victories. Replacing the “bumblebee” uniforms for at least two seasons, the jerseys feature block numbers and sleeve stripes and will debut against Cleveland in Week 8.

BNT162b2 and BNT162b2SA produced antibody responses considered comparable across specified doses and virus strains. In previously vaccinated participants without prior COVID-19, a BNT162b2 booster produced responses to the original strain comparable to those after Dose 2, while a BNT162b2SA booster produced comparable responses against the Beta variant. Among previously unvaccinated participants, two BNT162b2SA doses produced comparable Beta-variant responses. Researchers considered these findings unlikely to be due to chance.

Temporary lymphocyte-count reductions occurred in a few Phase 1 participants shortly after Dose 1 and generally returned to normal within days. Injection-site reactions and systemic events were usually mild or moderate, short-lived, and well tolerated. Injection-site pain, tiredness, and headache were most common.

Phase 1 doses of 10, 20, and 30 µg were generally well tolerated, except 100 µg BNT162b1, which was stopped after Dose 1 because of reactions. BNT162b2 at 30 µg was selected for Phase 2/3. In Phase 2/3, fewer than 1% discontinued because of medical problems, with similar numbers in vaccine and placebo groups.

Serious medical problems were uncommon, and no single serious problem occurred in at least 1% of participants. Researchers generally did not consider serious problems related to study vaccines, though some temporary events in participants aged 16 or older were considered possibly related.

No one died in Phase 1. During Phase 2/3, 85 participants initially receiving BNT162b2, 62 initially receiving placebo and later BNT162b2, and 23 receiving placebo before any BNT162b2 died from varied causes; researchers did not attribute the deaths to BNT162b2. No deaths occurred among Phase 3 participants receiving BNT162b2SA without previous BNT162b2.

On February 25, 2019, Amazon elected former PepsiCo CEO and chairman Indra K. Nooyi to its board and Audit Committee. She received restricted stock units for 549 Amazon shares, vesting in three equal annual installments beginning May 15, 2020, subject to continued board service, and entered into the company’s standard director indemnification agreement.

Stocks represent company ownership and can provide long-term price appreciation, dividends, and increased ownership through buybacks, but they carry substantial loss risk and require diversification. Bonds are loans to companies or governments, generally pay fixed interest, mature on set dates, and usually rank ahead of shareholders in bankruptcy. Their rates vary with maturity, credit quality, and risk.

Historically, stocks have outperformed bonds, while bonds—especially sovereign bonds—have often reduced portfolio volatility and losses during market turmoil. Corporate bonds may remain vulnerable in recessions due to credit risk and sentiment. A 60% stock and 40% bond portfolio produced lower returns than an all-stock portfolio but experienced less volatility and smaller drawdowns. The appropriate allocation depends on factors such as risk tolerance, investment horizon, and proximity to retirement.

The “Sell in May and go away” strategy proposes investing in stocks from November through April. A related international strategy alternated between countries experiencing winter, using equally weighted ETF portfolios. Backtesting with growth, drawdown, and volatility measures found that this approach did not perform as expected.

Digital leaders treat data transparency, shared access, governance, measurement, and learning as central to decision-making and organizational alignment. Leadership sponsorship, standardized infrastructure, clear metrics, and shared goals support collaboration, experimentation, autonomy, and risk-taking while controls protect privacy and prevent misuse. Standardized APIs enable cross-department data flow at 88% of digital leaders versus 27% of laggards.

Digital laggards commonly restrict and silo data, use burdensome access processes, favor individual judgment and tenure, and employ data mainly to justify prior decisions. Their objectives are often aspirational, unclear, and weakly connected to strategy, leading employees to avoid measurement, emphasize process and effort, and struggle to innovate or coordinate.

Data-driven objectives can align organizations vertically with company strategy and horizontally across teams. However, leaders may still have inconsistent data attitudes or demand excessive analysis that slows simple decisions and weakens intuition.

Successful transformation requires changing entrenched beliefs and behaviors, aligning leadership values with daily practices, and combining technological capability with a culture of transparency, learning, measurement, and experimentation. Organizations commonly fall into four patterns: data novices, insight ready, tech enabled, and data reliant. Each can build on existing strengths and target remaining cultural or technical gaps.

European stocks rose Monday in thin holiday trading, led by banks. The Stoxx Europe 600 gained 0.5% after a 1.2% decline in 2016. Italian banks advanced following reports that suspended lender Monte dei Paschi would issue €15 billion in debt to improve liquidity and confidence. German banks also gained. Italy’s FTSE MIB rose 1.3%, Germany’s DAX 0.9%, Spain’s IBEX 0.4%, and France’s index 0.2%.

Motley Fool Money highlights the no-annual-fee Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card for unlimited 2% cash rewards, a $200 bonus after $500 in purchases within three months, and 0% introductory APR on purchases and qualifying balance transfers for 12 months. Afterward, a variable APR of 18.99%, 23.99%, or 28.99% applies. Additional benefits include up to $600 in cell phone protection, subject to a $25 deductible, and Visa Signature concierge service. Applicants generally need good or excellent credit.

Alternatives include Capital One Quicksilver, offering unlimited 1.5% cash back, select travel rewards, welcome bonuses, and a 15-month introductory APR period; and a Citi card offering up to 2% cash back, a $200 bonus, and an 18-month balance-transfer offer.

Motley Fool receives partner commissions that may affect offer placement and coverage but says compensation does not influence ratings. Approval is not guaranteed, and consumers are advised to choose cards suited to their needs.

The disclosure describes muscle-targeting compositions, particularly engineered recombinant adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors designed to address the limited non-liver tropism, toxicity risks, manufacturing challenges, and cross-species variability of conventional AAVs. Targeting moieties contain short peptide n-mer motifs, including RGD and non-RGD motifs, that may be displayed externally on engineered AAV capsids. Motifs may be inserted at specified capsid positions, including between amino acids 588 and 589 of AAV9 or analogous positions in other AAV serotypes.

The engineered particles can carry therapeutic or gene-modifying cargo, including transgenes, antisense oligonucleotides, morpholinos, peptides, RNAs, CRISPR-Cas components, and mini- or micro-dystrophin genes. Potential applications include muscular dystrophies, neuromuscular diseases, cardiomyopathies, glycogen-storage diseases, expanded-repeat diseases, cancers, autoimmune diseases, viral diseases, and progeroid diseases.

Also described are vector systems, capsid polypeptides, producer cells, pharmaceutical formulations, kits, and treatment methods involving administration to subjects. Capsid libraries may be generated and selected using tissue-specific promoters and mRNA-based screening across species. Presented experiments compare MyoAAV with AAV9 and AAV8, including muscle transduction, biodistribution, gene-expression kinetics, DMD correction, and integrin-mediated entry. MyoAAV is reported to transduce mouse and human primary myotubes 50–100 times more effectively than AAV9.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies up to 2 MHz and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge.

TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP provide independently programmable primary-to-synchronous and synchronous-to-primary dead times through PS and SP resistors; TPS7H5003-SP has a fixed 50-ns typical dead time. Floating PS/SP pins produce an 8-ns typical minimum, while programmed resistors should be 10 kΩ to 300 kΩ. Leading-edge blanking suppresses current-sense transients after output turn-on. It is fixed at 50 ns for TPS7H5003-SP and resistor-programmable on other devices, with LEB requiring 10 kΩ to 300 kΩ.

Pulse skipping addresses minimum-on-time problems at high frequency. It occurs when COMP is below 0.3 V at the clock rising edge and the previous duty cycle was below 25%. With a 50% duty limit and both primary outputs active, equal pulses are skipped to preserve transformer volt-second balance. Depending on the device and DCL connection, maximum duty-cycle limits are 50%, 75%, or 100%.

CS_ILIM senses primary current for PWM control and overcurrent protection. Outputs turn off when sensed peak current reaches COMP/2, including a 150-mV offset. At 1.05 V on CS_ILIM, cycle-by-cycle limiting begins and CHICC charges. When HICC reaches 0.6 V, soft start discharges and switching stops; restart occurs after HICC rises to 1 V and subsequently discharges to 0.3 V. CHICC controls limiting and restart delays, with at least 3.3 nF recommended. The FAULT input shuts down switching above 0.6 V after its minimum pulse width and restarts through soft start after the signal falls below 0.5 V and a delay of approximately 15 switching cycles.

Programmable slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle; compensation equal to the sensed inductor-current falling slope is recommended. Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation may be connected to COMP. Thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C typical and restarts below 160°C typical.

A TPS7H5001-SP synchronous push-pull GaN design example uses 500-kHz switching, 5-V output, approximately 25-ns dead time, 50-ns leading-edge blanking, 7.5-ms soft start, a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 170-V primary and 80-V synchronous GaN FETs, a 0.47-µH output inductor, approximately 2.3 mF output capacitance, and overcurrent limiting near 35 A. Type 2A compensation targets 10-kHz crossover.

The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require at least 0.1 µF VIN bypassing. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing high-current and switching loops, isolating sensitive traces from switch-node and gate-drive signals, placing bypass, filtering, sensing, and compensation components close to their pins, and using multiple AVSS vias for CFP backside metallization.

A Michigan family filed a police report and plans to sue after their five-year-old alleged two Highview Elementary educators repeatedly taped his mouth shut and discarded his lunch. One substitute assistant was removed. The district denied knowledge of earlier incidents, while police investigate. His mother says he will not return unless the second accused teacher is fired.

Builder Eric Woodward is creating a temporary public park on his vacant Fort Langley property after cancelling a mixed-use boutique hotel project amid a Township dispute. Planned features include gathering and play areas, picnic spaces and outdoor ping pong. Major work is expected by early July, addressing concerns about the prominent site’s long-term appearance.

Microsoft’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended December 31, 2020 reported quarterly revenue of $43.1 billion, operating income of $17.9 billion, and net income of $15.5 billion, up from $36.9 billion, $13.9 billion, and $11.6 billion, respectively, a year earlier. Diluted earnings per share rose to $2.03 from $1.51. Six-month revenue was $80.2 billion and net income was $29.4 billion.

Quarterly segment revenue was $13.4 billion for Productivity and Business Processes, $14.6 billion for Intelligent Cloud, and $15.1 billion for More Personal Computing. Commercial cloud revenue increased 34% to $16.7 billion; Azure revenue grew 50%, Xbox content and services 40%, LinkedIn 23%, and Office 365 Commercial 21%.

At December 31, 2020, Microsoft had $304.1 billion in assets, $132.0 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments, $173.9 billion in liabilities, and $130.2 billion in stockholders’ equity. Six-month operating cash flow was $31.9 billion. Microsoft repurchased $11.0 billion of shares and declared dividends of $1.12 per share during the six-month period.

Microsoft agreed to acquire ZeniMax Media for $7.5 billion in cash, subject to closing conditions and regulatory review. Extending server and network equipment useful lives increased six-month operating income by $1.7 billion and net income by $1.4 billion. Microsoft noted continued COVID-19-related benefits to cloud, PC, productivity, and gaming demand, alongside weakness in transactional licensing.

This prospective cohort study assessed whether circulating indole 3-acetate (3-IAA) predicted chemotherapy response or survival in 124 patients with borderline resectable or locally advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Serum 3-IAA was measured before chemotherapy; 35 participants provided follow-up samples. Outcomes included radiologic and CA19-9 response, surgical resection, and overall survival.

Median pretreatment 3-IAA was 290 ng/mL and correlated positively with age, but not tumor diameter or CA19-9. Concentrations did not differ significantly by chemotherapy regimen, treatment response, subsequent resection, or one-year survival. Follow-up concentrations increased nonsignificantly after chemotherapy. Median survival was 499 days, with no significant survival differences across 3-IAA quartiles. Pretreatment 3-IAA was not associated with survival in univariable analysis or after adjustment for age, performance status, CA19-9, and tumor classification.

These findings do not support 3-IAA as a predictor of chemotherapy response or overall survival in non-metastatic, borderline resectable or locally advanced disease. Differences from prior findings in metastatic disease may reflect patient populations, tumor characteristics, assay differences, or optimistic discovery-cohort results. The authors recommend technical and clinical validation in geographically distinct metastatic cohorts before controlled trials aimed at increasing circulating 3-IAA.

Researchers from McGill University and the University of Toronto propose understanding gaslighting as a learning process based on prediction error minimization. Gaslighters violate expectations, then attribute the resulting surprise to targets’ supposed inability to perceive reality accurately. Repeated manipulation can lead targets to internalize this belief. Because people rely on trusted, close others to shape their sense of self and reality, the model suggests anyone could be vulnerable when trusting the wrong person. Lead author Willis Klein said future research could examine whether attachment styles or trauma affect susceptibility, validate the model, and improve support for victims.

Reagan transition records describe a November 1980 interim foreign policy advisory board established to monitor international developments before inauguration and a December 1980 State Department transition report prepared under the Office of Executive Branch Management. The records identify board and transition-team members, attached materials, and missing meeting minutes.

An editorial note recounts Ronald Reagan’s November 20, 1975 announcement challenging President Gerald Ford for the 1976 Republican presidential nomination. Reagan cited concerns about the economy, government, foreign energy dependence, declining military superiority, and détente. He argued that unresponsive Washington leadership was the root problem and called for government that listened to and relied on citizens. He rejected continued “business-as-usual” and advocated progress, truth, hope, and restoring confidence in American life.

Sea of Thieves had Rare’s highest launch-month sales since NPD tracking began in 1995. It was March’s second-best-selling game and 2018’s eighth best-selling title to date, excluding Game Pass downloads. It was also the year’s highest-ranked platform exclusive at that point.

On April 27, 2018, Amazon amended its unsecured revolving credit agreement, increasing borrowing capacity from $3 billion to $7 billion and extending its term to April 27, 2021. The company also established a $7 billion commercial paper program for unsecured notes maturing within 397 days. Borrowings and note proceeds are intended for general corporate purposes, with the credit facility potentially backing the notes.

U.S. stocks fell Tuesday as the 10-year Treasury yield reached 3 percent for the first time in four years, raising concerns about corporate borrowing costs and prompting possible shifts from equities to bonds. The Dow declined for a fifth consecutive session, while technology and industrial shares led losses. Alphabet, Facebook, 3M, Caterpillar, Apple and Lockheed Martin fell despite generally strong earnings, as investors focused on rising expenses, weaker margins, higher steel costs and disappointing outlooks. Although 77.1 percent of reporting S&P 500 companies beat estimates, investors questioned whether gains were sustainable. Consumer confidence rebounded in April. Oil briefly exceeded $75 a barrel before reversing as U.S. and French leaders sought to resolve differences over Iran. Declining stocks outnumbered advancing issues on both the NYSE and Nasdaq.

The study addresses domain shift and limited data in neuroimaging by transferring features learned from 40,000 UK Biobank structural MRI scans to the smaller OASIS-3, IXI, and ABIDE datasets. Simple Fully Convolutional Networks were pretrained for age or sex prediction, then adapted by retraining the classifier and fine-tuning the full model.

Pretrained features remained reusable across scanners but were highly task-specific. Transfer learning substantially outperformed elastic net regression for age and sex prediction and generally surpassed training from scratch. Age mean absolute errors were 3.25 for OASIS, 5.65 for IXI, and 1.70 for ABIDE; sex accuracies were 92.6%, 90.3%, and 75.7%, respectively. Reinitializing parameters with pretrained scaling did not reproduce these gains, indicating that feature reuse, rather than parameter scaling, explained improved performance.

Benefits depended on similarity between source and target data. Fine-tuning was especially useful for ABIDE, whose age range and scanner characteristics differed substantially from UK Biobank, although negative transfer occurred for ABIDE sex prediction. With very small datasets, retraining only the classifier could reduce overfitting. Transfer learning also accelerated convergence. The authors propose UK Biobank as a potential pretraining resource for neuroimaging while noting limitations involving scanner variation and transfer to disease-specific tasks.

The study addresses Turkish citation intent classification by introducing the first large-scale, publicly available dataset for the task. The dataset contains 2,650 annotated citation sentences extracted from 723 Computer Science research articles, using five Web of Science categories: Background, Basis, Support, Differ, and Discuss. Annotation combined academic expertise with LLM-assisted classification to resolve missing or ambiguous labels.

Experiments evaluated GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Gemini 2.5 Pro using in-context learning, automated prompt optimization, and ensemble methods. Manual prompt performance varied substantially, demonstrating sensitivity to prompt design. DSPy optimization with MIPROv2 and Chain of Thought achieved 86.5% accuracy. Few-shot experiments showed that adding examples did not consistently improve results: Gemini 2.5 Flash peaked at 89.1% with one example, while GPT-4o performed best at 88.4% without examples.

Ensemble approaches produced the strongest results. Majority voting reached 90.2% accuracy, logistic-regression stacking reached 91.0%, and an XGBoost stacked meta-model achieved 91.3%. Key challenges included severe class imbalance favoring Background, difficulty distinguishing semantically similar categories, especially Support and Differ, and inconsistent LLM predictions. Proposed future work includes hierarchical classifiers, targeted or synthetic augmentation of rare classes, and broader citation context and document metadata.

The team is focused on resting, preparing, and playing well as it tries to close out the Stanley Cup Finals. Clinching is difficult because the opponent faces elimination and will not surrender. Players must manage the emotions surrounding the potential championship while remaining businesslike and focused on their on-ice responsibilities. An injured teammate’s possible return would provide a boost, but he will not play if he is a liability. Experienced players are helping teammates understand the stakes without looking beyond the game. Winning at home brings greater expectations and a more hectic atmosphere, while winning on the road offers less pressure and a quieter celebration, but either would be enjoyable.

Teuvo Teravainen says staying calm helps him play better. He describes his athletic family, the team’s confidence in overcoming deficits, and a comeback win after Tampa Bay’s strong start. He says his goal excited fans in Finland, appreciates having an experienced mentor who is like a second father, and credits hard work, skating, skill, and self-belief for overcoming doubts about his size. Antoine Vermette calls the playoffs an exciting opportunity and emphasizes bringing their best game, persevering through adversity, and trusting the team’s experience. He describes Tampa Bay as fast and skilled, stresses puck possession, positioning, skating, and pressure, and praises Teravainen as a smart, skilled player with strong vision and an active stick.

Veteran forwards Ryan Malone and Brian Gionta are potential candidates for the 2018 U.S. Olympic men’s hockey team, which will lack active NHL players. Malone, a 2010 silver medalist, joined the AHL’s Iowa Wild after a two-year retirement. USA Hockey is also monitoring unsigned 2006 Olympian Gionta, who likely must join a non-NHL club. The roster will be named around Jan. 1.

Research by Ross Levine and colleagues found that easier borrowing conditions encourage businesses to invest more in reducing pollution by increasing loan availability and lowering financing costs. Such investments can reduce fines, improve worker health and productivity, and enhance corporate reputations.

The researchers examined bank deposit windfalls generated by fracking-related mineral lease payments. They focused on non-gas-producing counties served by banks that received these funds elsewhere, isolating credit effects from fracking activity. Benzene levels fell 26% in counties with the largest credit gains compared with the average county, while other toxic pollutants also declined.

EPA data further showed that companies whose primary lenders received shale-related deposit increases reduced toxic emissions more than comparable companies, earned better environmental ratings, and spoke more publicly about green issues. The study does not assess fracking’s environmental effects but uses the boom to examine how increased credit supply affects environmental performance.

Calgary single mother Shauna Sinfield’s car was stolen with her 12-year-old son Caden’s hockey gear inside. Sinfield, who has multiple sclerosis and a fixed income, estimates replacing the equipment will cost $1,500–$2,000. Police consider recovery unlikely. A GoFundMe had raised $685 toward a $3,000 goal by Tuesday.

Media industry observers expect David Ellison, backed by his father Larry Ellison, to bid for Warner Bros. Discovery after acquiring Paramount, though no offer exists and Ellison has declined to discuss plans. A merger could combine streaming services, studios, sports rights, cable channels, and administrative functions, creating a larger competitor to Netflix, Disney, and Amazon. Political ties could reduce antitrust concerns, while Larry Ellison and potentially Apollo could help finance a purchase of WBD, valued around $44 billion with roughly $35 billion in debt. WBD CEO David Zaslav may seek to preserve the company’s independence, but prior restructuring plans failed to significantly boost its stock. A deal would further consolidate Hollywood, reducing the number of buyers for creators.

This week’s top posts cover DomTerm’s browser-based interface, the history and meaning of open source and container runtimes, Christine Peterson coining “open source software” 20 years ago, and an Ontario school program using Linux to preserve over 200 computers. Opensource.com also marks its eighth anniversary.

The playoffs are getting tougher, and the team must better read officiating, stay active on the penalty kill, and work through adversity. They are generally satisfied with their systems and game plan against Detroit. Despite missed chances and unfavorable bounces, strong defense remains the priority. Playing at home is especially energizing because of the passionate fans.

Fourth-grader Lexi Bergeron sells handmade fidget toys to help pay school lunch debts in Grand Haven, Michigan. After exceeding Ferry Elementary’s $188 debt, her family’s fundraiser aims to raise $2,200 for the entire district.

The team’s mediocre second period and lapses proved costly despite a strong third-period push. Both goaltenders played well, while missed opportunities and unfavorable bounces contributed to the loss. Returning home, where the team has played comfortably, they must maintain consistency for 60 minutes, work harder around the net, avoid discouragement, and build on recent home performances.

Researchers identified two bacterial strains on grape leaves that degraded guaiacol, a major smoke-taint compound, to barely detectable levels within 96 hours. The bacteria did not consume similar smoky compounds, indicating other strains may be needed. This targeted microbial approach could preserve wine qualities better than activated-charcoal filtering, but further research is required.

The paper introduces edit distances for constructible \( \mathbb{R}^d \)-persistence modules and proves that they coincide with the interleaving distance. Persistence modules are treated both as functors from posets to finite-dimensional vector spaces and as graded modules; for \( \mathbb{R}^d \)-modules, constructibility is equivalent to finite presentability.

Two categories of indexing posets are used: finite join-semilattices embedded in \( \mathbb{R}^d \), and finite \(d\)-grids. Their morphisms are monotone maps admitting right adjoints. A morphism between constructible persistence modules is induced by such a Galois connection and compatibility of the restricted modules. The edit distance is the infimum of the summed distortions of morphisms along finite edit paths.

The main theorem states that, for either category and any constructible \( \mathbb{R}^d \)-persistence modules \(M,N\),
\[
d_I(M,N)=d_{\mathrm{Ed}}(M,N).
\]
One inequality is established by showing that a single edit of distortion \(\epsilon\) produces an \(\epsilon\)-interleaving. The reverse inequality uses finite presentations of interleaved modules, a cost assigned to bijections between presentations, and an “easy-edit lemma” showing that sufficiently small presentation changes yield edits of no greater cost. An interpolating family of presentations and a finite-cover argument then bound edit distance by interleaving distance.

The edit distance is universal among pseudometrics bounded by the cost of a single edit. Consequently, stability under the interleaving distance is equivalent to stability under the edit distance, and single-edit stability suffices to establish interleaving stability. Computing the edit distance is NP-hard because of its equality with interleaving distance.

The metric space’s path components are represented by free modules, distinguished by their eventual vector-space dimension. Compared with earlier work based on Galois insertions, the new framework permits arbitrary edit sequences and applies to constructible multiparameter modules for every \(d\), rather than only one-parameter modules.

The appendices compare two notions of constructibility and establish their equivalence after adjoining a bottom element. They also relate constructibility to finite presentations and examine preservation of constructibility under cokernels.

The Department of Education will hold its first School Safety Conference at Okkodo High School beginning June 26. About 400 support staff will receive training on law enforcement and legal issues, school climate, drugs and alcohol, crises, and mental health, including bullying, suicide, and sexual identity. DOE reported 352 campus drug cases in 2015-2016 and is increasingly emphasizing treatment and group therapy over discipline.

Plasmodium vivax and P. ovale can persist as dormant liver-stage hypnozoites that later activate, causing relapsing infections. Radical cure requires 8-aminoquinolines, which can cause haemolysis in people with G6PD deficiency. Hypnozoite activation is poorly understood; proposed mechanisms include an intrinsic clock and external triggers such as seasonal changes, mosquito bites, fever, inflammation, and haemolysis.

The study developed analytical likelihoods for an “exponential clock” model in which each hypnozoite activates independently at a constant rate without external triggers. The model also represents variation in infectious-bite timing, sporozoite inoculum size and development, and age-related anti-disease immunity. It predicts that relapse rates increase with hypnozoite burden, inter-relapse intervals lengthen as the reservoir is depleted, hypnozoite burdens are highly variable in low-transmission settings, and symptomatic relapse varies nonlinearly with age.

The model was fitted to the 1993–1995 SPf66 vaccine trial on the Thailand-Myanmar border. The trial followed 1,344 children aged 2–15 daily for 21 months; the vaccine had no clinical efficacy. After excluding likely treatment failures, 2,504 symptomatic vivax infections and 1,164 symptomatic falciparum infections occurred over 1,988 person-years, including 293 mixed infections. Individual children experienced up to 13 vivax and seven falciparum episodes.

The estimated average hypnozoite carriage duration was 171 days, with a half-life of 118 days. The estimated successful sporozoite inoculum was 6.9 per infective bite, including 2.7 hypnozoites. Relapsing infections were estimated to outnumber primary infections by 3.4 to one, implying that about 75% of observed symptomatic vivax infections were relapses. Higher-than-expected vivax rates followed falciparum monoinfections treated with artesunate alone, consistent with external triggering. Mefloquine provided sufficient exposure to eliminate emerging relapses for approximately one month, potentially masking triggering effects because most falciparum episodes received artesunate-mefloquine.

Jack Wilshere has met West Ham manager Manuel Pellegrini about a potential move after leaving Arsenal over limited playing opportunities. Fenerbahce reportedly offered a larger deal, but Wilshere’s London-based family and hopes of an England recall may favor remaining in the Premier League.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting switching frequencies up to 2 MHz and topologies including buck, flyback, forward, push-pull, and full bridge.

The CS_ILIM pin senses primary-side current for PWM control and overcurrent protection. Outputs turn off when sensed current reaches the COMP-derived threshold. Exceeding the nominal 1.05-V current-limit threshold initiates cycle-by-cycle limiting. Continued overcurrent charges the HICC capacitor until switching stops; the capacitor then controls the non-switching interval before soft-start is retried. A minimum 3.3-nF HICC capacitor is recommended, and sufficient margin should be maintained between normal peak current and the trip point.

The FAULT input supports external protections. A voltage above 0.6 V for the specified minimum pulse width shuts down switching and discharges soft-start. After FAULT falls below 0.5 V, restart occurs following a frequency-dependent delay. Internal thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C and restarts below 160°C.

Slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation above 50% duty cycle. It is programmed with an RSC-to-AVSS resistor; compensation equal to the sensed inductor-current falling slope is recommended. The controller’s transconductance error amplifier supports Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation, with Type 2A adding high-frequency noise attenuation.

A synchronous push-pull GaN design example uses 500-kHz switching, 5-V output, approximately 25-ns dead time, 50-ns leading-edge blanking, 7.5-ms soft-start, a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 0.47-µH output inductance, and about 2.3 mF output capacitance. It selects 170-V primary and 80-V synchronous-rectifier GaN FETs, begins current limiting near 35 A using a 7.5-Ω sense resistor and 1:100 current-sense transformer, and uses Type 2A compensation with 40.2-kΩ, 15-nF, and 47-pF components.

The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require at least 0.1 µF of input bypass capacitance. Layout guidance emphasizes separating analog and power grounds, minimizing switching loops and switch-node area, routing sensitive signals away from noisy traces, placing bypass, filtering, and compensation components close to the controller, and using short, wide high-current traces.

Investors speculated the Czech National Bank could remove its cap keeping the euro above 27 crowns, prompting a nine-month high in currency hedging costs amid fears of a sharp appreciation. Britain’s statistics agency is examining ways to identify recessions earlier after delays and underestimation during the 2008 downturn, though post-Brexit GDP estimates have avoided major revisions.

Global markets reversed early gains after Federal Reserve minutes raised concerns over stock valuations and indicated its $4.5 trillion balance sheet could shrink this year. Delays to U.S. tax reform and caution before President Trump’s summit with China’s President Xi added pressure. Wall Street, Treasury yields, the dollar, oil and volatility fell. Most Asian markets declined except Shanghai, while European stocks were expected to open lower ahead of economic data, ECB speeches and the Czech central bank meeting.

The article advocates an ecological, sociocultural perspective on foreign-language education, arguing that classroom learning must be understood within broader school, socioeconomic, linguistic, cultural, and national contexts. Focusing mainly on state education in Malaysia and Thailand, it examines why English-language policy intentions often diverge from educational outcomes, particularly among disadvantaged rural and low-income learners.

National curricula commonly prescribe communicative language teaching, extensive classroom use of English, and proficiency targets linked to the Common European Framework of Reference. However, achievement data show persistent socioeconomic and urban-rural inequalities. In Malaysia, English proficiency is associated with urban residence and higher socioeconomic status, while rural learners generally perform less well. Similar divisions exist in Thailand and other Asian contexts. National-language identities and limited everyday use of English further restrict opportunities for meaningful communication in English.

Teacher proficiency is frequently blamed for weak outcomes. Assessments found substantial numbers of Malaysian and Thai teachers below designated proficiency targets, including teachers assigned to English despite training in other subjects. The article argues that standardized language tests alone do not measure teachers’ pedagogical effectiveness or how they use English to support learning. Such assessments can also undermine professional identity by disregarding teaching experience, classroom performance, and teachers’ own educational backgrounds.

Teachers report that prescribed communicative approaches often conflict with classroom realities, including large mixed-ability classes, low student proficiency, limited resources, examination pressures, ambitious syllabuses, and students’ preference for national or local languages. Indigenous Malaysian learners face additional difficulties when curricula assume literacy and language backgrounds they do not possess. Even academically successful students may lack confidence using spoken English because communication in English can be socially unnecessary or discouraged.

The article concludes that curriculum development should begin with analysis of local sociolinguistic, sociocultural, socioeconomic, and educational conditions. Policymakers should consult schools, teachers, students, and communities before setting curricula and proficiency goals. Effective English programmes require alignment between intended outcomes and education systems’ actual capacity to achieve them, rather than attributing implementation failures primarily to teachers.

The team must play patiently, simplify its hockey, limit neutral-zone speed, and improve shooting execution against blocked lanes. Ward played well after a long absence, but frustration hurt the team, which hopes to rebound next game.

NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 27, 2019 reported quarterly revenue of $3.01 billion, down 5% year over year, and net income of $899 million, down 27%. Diluted earnings were $1.45 per share. Nine-month revenue was $7.81 billion and net income was $1.85 billion. Quarterly Gaming, Data Center, Professional Visualization, Automotive, and OEM revenue totaled $1.66 billion, $726 million, $324 million, $162 million, and $143 million, respectively. Gross margin rose to 63.6%, while operating expenses increased 15% to $989 million. NVIDIA held $9.77 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities and generated $3.30 billion in nine-month operating cash flow. The company planned to acquire Mellanox for approximately $6.9 billion, subject to regulatory approval, with closing expected in early 2020. NVIDIA paid $292 million in dividends during the first nine months and had $1.99 billion in long-term debt.

Yuk Bui Yee was charged in a 13-count indictment arising from six alleged extortion incidents at three Chinese restaurants over two months. He sought separate trials for each incident, arguing the offenses were joined only because they were similar under CPL 200.20(2)(c), which permits discretionary severance. Prosecutors contended they were joined under CPL 200.20(2)(b), which applies when evidence of one offense would be material and admissible at trial for another and does not permit severance.

The court explained that CPL 200.20(2)(b) incorporates the evidentiary principles associated with People v Molineux. Although the incidents did not collectively establish a common scheme or plan, they shared a distinctive method: the perpetrator spoke Mandarin, demanded money for his “brothers,” and claimed affiliation with the “Eagles” gang. These similarities made evidence of the offenses relevant to identity. Evidence of the earlier incidents was also potentially admissible to establish knowledge and criminal intent in later incidents because the alleged demands were not necessarily unequivocally extortionate.

The court found all counts properly joinable under CPL 200.20(2)(b) and denied the motion to sever, while noting that the trial judge could later reconsider the admissibility of particular evidence based on developments at trial.

A UK Biobank analysis of 451,355 adults examined cardiovascular biomarkers and outcomes by ethnicity-adjusted BMI category and diabetes status. Diabetes was present in 4.9% of participants, most of whom were overweight or obese. Cardiovascular imaging included carotid intima-media thickness, arterial stiffness, left ventricular ejection fraction, and cardiac contractility.

Higher BMI was associated with adverse metabolic and cardiovascular measures regardless of diabetes, although cardiovascular abnormalities progressed less clearly with BMI among participants with diabetes because substantial abnormalities were already present at normal weight. Within each BMI category, diabetes was associated with worse cardiovascular phenotypes. Adiposity measures correlated more strongly with cardiovascular biomarkers than diabetes duration or HbA1c, but all correlations were modest.

Over 5.3 million person-years of follow-up, there were 29,931 deaths, including 5,831 cardiovascular deaths, as well as 7,179 non-fatal myocardial infarctions and 3,469 non-fatal ischaemic strokes. Event rates increased with BMI and were substantially higher with diabetes. Compared with normal-weight participants without diabetes, adjusted cardiovascular mortality was elevated among obese participants without diabetes and even higher among normal-weight participants with diabetes; risk increased further with overweight or obesity in diabetes.

The findings indicate that obesity and diabetes are independently and additively associated with cardiovascular disease and mortality. The high risk among normal-weight people with diabetes may involve visceral adiposity, suboptimal conventional risk-factor control, and other unidentified factors. Limitations include observational design, incomplete imaging data, survivor and selection bias, limited diabetes-type stratification, and recruitment before widespread use of newer diabetes treatments.

The Education Department continued negotiated rule making during the government shutdown on student-loan changes under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, with another session scheduled for Nov. 3–7. Participants expressed cautious optimism but reached no consensus.

The main dispute concerned which postbaccalaureate programs qualify as professional degrees, whose students may borrow up to $200,000, compared with $100,000 for graduate programs. The department initially proposed limiting eligibility to 10 programs listed in the Higher Education Act. After objections about legal risks and effects on high-cost, high-demand fields, it proposed a one-year expansion covering programs meeting specified standards that institutions had designated as professional before July 4, 2025. Committee members questioned the proposal’s clarity, breadth, cost and usefulness as a long-term solution. Other alternatives were submitted but received limited public discussion.

The shutdown reduced transparency because the department’s website was not updated with proposals and meeting materials, leaving committee members to inform constituents. Officials said documents could not be posted until the government reopened.

Negotiators also discussed repayment changes taking effect July 1, 2026. Most income-driven plans will end except the new Repayment Assistance plan, while existing borrowers may apply for Income-Based Repayment before the deadline. Parent PLUS borrowers could face a lengthy process requiring consolidation, enrollment in Income-Contingent Repayment and one payment before applying for IBR. Consumer representatives sought simplification, but the department’s plan was not amended.

Severe weather season began slowly in North Texas, Oklahoma, and Kansas. North Texas reported four tornadoes, while Oklahoma and Kansas recorded none. However, tornado activity can increase sharply in May across Oklahoma and Texas.

Bear Grylls criticised schools for prioritising league tables over preparing children for adult life, arguing that persistence and determination matter more than top exam grades. He said his own determination helped him pass SAS selection despite not excelling academically, while praising Eton for positive memories and friendships. Grylls also doubted Donald Trump would suit a wilderness adventure, saying survival requires humility, and hoped the president had more important priorities.

This Chinese study examined cross-sectional and longitudinal relationships between arterial stiffness, measured by brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV), and renal function, assessed by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and microalbuminuria. The cross-sectional analysis included 67,060 adults, while 12,324 had follow-up data.

After adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors, eGFR was negatively associated with baPWV. Higher baseline baPWV predicted incident chronic kidney disease (CKD); participants in the highest baPWV tertile had an adjusted hazard ratio of 2.17 compared with the lowest tertile. Conversely, lower eGFR predicted arterial stiffness, with an adjusted hazard ratio of 1.21. Cross-lagged analysis showed that the association from baseline eGFR to follow-up baPWV was stronger than that from baseline baPWV to follow-up eGFR, indicating that declining kidney function preceded increased arterial stiffness.

The findings support a bidirectional association between CKD and arterial stiffness, with renal decline appearing temporally earlier. Limitations include estimating renal function from serum creatinine rather than the reference technique and deriving the population primarily from central China. The authors reported no conflicts of interest, and funders had no role in the study.

Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev said Russia’s economy is entering growth. Industrial output rose 1.3 percent, agriculture grew 5 percent, and agricultural machinery production increased 60 percent. He highlighted agriculture’s export potential and links between agricultural growth and machine-building.

This case study examined whether spinal cord stimulation (SCS) providing sensory feedback from a missing foot alters walking-related muscle activity in a woman aged 60–65 with a unilateral transtibial amputation. Three epidural SCS leads were implanted near T12–L2 for 84 days. During laboratory walking sessions, stimulation was triggered during prosthetic-limb stance and modulated by plantar pressure. Electromyography and motion capture assessed muscle activity and gait kinematics.

Muscle activation patterns with and without SCS at Day 63 were highly similar. However, compared with Day 30, residual-limb tensor fasciae latae and vastus lateralis activity increased by Day 63. Co-contraction of residual-limb knee antagonist muscles decreased significantly over time, with a further slight reduction during stimulation. Increased tensor fasciae latae activity corresponded with greater pelvic obliquity range of motion and residual-limb pelvic drop. Some improvements remained when stimulation was off, suggesting a possible rehabilitative effect, although additional participants are needed for confirmation.

The findings indicate that repeated laboratory exposure to SCS-mediated sensory feedback may improve dynamic knee and hip stability during walking without disrupting gait-cycle duration or limb alternation. Interpretation is limited by the single participant, incomplete electromyography data, and stimulation being delivered only in the laboratory.

Anyone, including visitors, contractors and Defense Department civilians, may dine at more than 1,600 Exchange restaurants worldwide. They may also purchase food and beverages at 300-plus Express locations if consumed on the installation. Amazon.com filed a Form 8-K dated July 25, 2019, announcing its second-quarter 2019 financial results. The filing incorporates a press release as Exhibit 99.1 and information regarding non-GAAP financial measures as Exhibit 99.2. CFO Brian T. Olsavsky signed the report.

The study introduced SCIseg, an open-source deep-learning model that simultaneously segments the spinal cord and T2-weighted hyperintense lesions in spinal cord injury MRI. It used 231 scans from 191 patients across three sites, incorporating varied scanners, resolutions, orientations, treatment stages, and traumatic or ischemic lesions. Training combined region-based nnUNet segmentation, active learning, and multi-site data expansion.

SCIseg achieved mean Dice scores of 0.92 for spinal cord and 0.60 for lesion segmentation. The 3D model significantly outperformed its 2D version, while active learning improved agreement between automated and manual lesion measurements. Performance was lower for scans affected by metal artifacts and heterogeneous injury phases. Automatically derived lesion biomarkers were statistically comparable to manual measurements and showed similar correlations with clinical scores. The model also produced reasonable segmentations in unseen degenerative cervical myelopathy cases.

Limitations include training only on T2-weighted images and treating lesions as single entities without separating edema and hemorrhage. The authors propose incorporating additional MRI contrasts, finer lesion labels, and more degenerative cervical myelopathy data. SCIseg is available through the Spinal Cord Toolbox, with code and processing resources publicly released.

The group remains calm and focused ahead of Sunday, relying on the same disciplined, mentally tough approach used throughout the playoffs. They aim to start better, sustain their game plan, wear down the opposition, and expect both teams’ best efforts. The team plans to remain aggressive against dangerous skilled players while maintaining normal routines. Playing at home amid enthusiastic fans is considered special, and the team hopes to deliver a strong performance.

Athletes Unlimited (AU), founded by Jon Patricof and Jonathan Soros, launched in 2020 to create a new model for professional sports centered on player empowerment, innovative competition, social impact, and long-term financial sustainability. Beginning with softball, AU expanded within three years to women’s volleyball, lacrosse, and basketball, involving more than 200 athletes. It secured major broadcast partnerships, raised $30 million in 2022, and was named one of Fast Company’s most innovative sports companies in 2023.

AU sought to address persistent problems in women’s professional sports, including underinvestment, limited media exposure, low pay, inadequate facilities, and unstable leagues modeled after established men’s sports. Research indicating that modern fans increasingly follow individual athletes, value organizational missions, and consume sports across multiple platforms informed AU’s approach.

AU seasons generally last five weeks at a single venue, reducing travel costs. Teams are redrafted weekly, and individual leaderboards award points for both personal performance and team victories. Leading players become captains who draft teams and determine starters. The model aims to preserve team incentives while building interest around individual athletes.

Players help govern each league through five-member Player Executive Committees. These committees participate in decisions involving competition formats, schedules, venues, uniforms, recruitment, sponsorships, policies, and social initiatives. Players receive base compensation, performance bonuses, and shares in a Profit Participation Plan providing rights to future distributions. AU also offers professional training conditions, meals, laundry, childcare, paid parental leave, pregnancy accommodations, and control over pregnancy disclosure.

Organized as a public benefit corporation, AU balances investor returns with stakeholder and social interests. Under its “Mission Equity” structure, investor returns are capped; after those targets are met, at least half of surplus funds go to players, with the remainder supporting mission-aligned programs. Athletes promote chosen nonprofits, participate in youth clinics, and support civic initiatives such as Power in My Voice.

AU emphasizes professional broadcasting and athlete storytelling to build awareness and loyalty. A 2022 fan survey found that most respondents engaged through television or streaming, valued AU’s support for women’s sports and player ownership, and viewed its approach as innovative and more exciting than existing leagues. However, broadcast availability remained a concern.

Despite rapid growth, AU faced unresolved questions about economic sustainability, scaling, expansion into additional sports, balancing broadcast investment with in-person experiences, increasing revenue and sponsorship, and preserving its player-driven mission while reaching broader audiences.

The CAT offense counters traps, double teams, and zone presses using a 2-1-2 spread, sharp passing, and a skilled triple-threat middle player. Baseline players back cut when the ball enters the middle. The post receives facing the basket and rolls or back cuts when passes reach corners, then resets or interchanges positions. Trapped players use skip passes toward the opposite corner. Dribble penetration should be limited to drive-and-kick escapes while maintaining ball and clock movement.

The disclosure describes allocating wireless resource units in a multiple-BSSID network through trigger frames. A transmitted BSSID and multiple non-transmitted BSSIDs may share an access point, operating class, channel, access mechanism, and antenna connector while serving different groups of stations.

An access point uses association identifier values derived from a group-AID mapping in a traffic indication map’s partial virtual bitmap to allocate random resource units. In trigger frames sent from the transmitted BSSID, an AID matching a non-transmitted BSSID’s index allocates resources to its associated stations, AID 0 allocates resources to stations associated with the transmitted BSSID, and AID 2045 allocates resources to unassociated stations. For frames sent from a non-transmitted BSSID, AID 0 identifies its associated stations and AID 2045 identifies unassociated stations. Trigger frames may also assign dedicated resource units to individual stations.

Management frames may advertise the multiple-BSSID set, BSSID indices, queued traffic, and random-access contention parameters. Stations decode these mappings and contend for eligible random resources, including through opportunistic backoff procedures.

Resource allocation may prioritize BSSs based on station counts, traffic types and priorities, security, access privileges, device types, quality-of-service parameters, latency requirements, and other factors. Selectively allocating resources to particular BSSs may improve wireless-medium utilization, efficiency, and fairness compared with allocating equal resources across all BSSs. The disclosure also describes corresponding access points, stations, processors, memory, software modules, and computer-readable media implementing these operations.

Tight ends are versatile offensive players who run mostly short-to-medium routes, provide red-zone receiving targets, and block defensive linemen and linebackers in running and passing plays. Their size, strength, athleticism, and ability to line up in multiple positions create difficult matchups for defenses. The name originated when players positioned close to the formation were distinguished from “split ends” aligned farther outside; “TE” is the standard abbreviation, while an H-back is a tight end positioned behind the line outside an offensive tackle. Typical tight ends are estimated at 6'3"–6'8" and 240–270 pounds, requiring strong hands, speed, route-running, blocking, and physicality. Notable tight ends include Tony Gonzalez, Rob Gronkowski, Antonio Gates, and Shannon Sharpe. Their combined receiving and blocking abilities allow offenses to use more formations and schemes.

Artists best serve democratic society by remaining independent rather than becoming instruments of propaganda or ideology. He envisions an America that balances strength with restraint, wealth with wisdom, protects natural and historic beauty, expands cultural opportunities, rewards artistic achievement, and earns respect for its civilization as well as its power.

Guangdong Province is experiencing China’s largest recorded chikungunya outbreak, with more than 4,000 confirmed cases since late July. Shunde District in Foshan accounts for over 3,600 cases, with infections also reported in Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, and Macao.

Chikungunya is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes and causes fever, severe joint pain, headache, rash, muscle aches, and swelling. It rarely causes death but may lead to prolonged pain, fatigue, and arthritis-like symptoms. No specific antiviral treatment or licensed vaccine exists; care focuses on rest, hydration, and pain relief.

Authorities are urging residents to eliminate standing water and mosquito breeding sites. Climate change, urbanization, global trade, and international travel are contributing to the spread of mosquito-borne diseases. Recommended measures include genomic surveillance, community participation, repellents, screens, protective clothing, and international coordination.

On World No Tobacco Day, Coalition for Tobacco Control–Pakistan urged the government to prioritize health, strictly enforce tobacco-control laws, implement the delayed 85 percent pictorial health warning on cigarette packs, and raise tobacco taxes. Officials said tobacco contributes to non-communicable disease deaths, with 108,800 tobacco-associated deaths in Pakistan and more than seven million globally each year. WHO reports that over 80 percent of smokers live in low- and middle-income countries, while tobacco costs countries $1.4 trillion annually in health care and lost productivity. CTC-Pak criticized Pakistan’s low-tax third tier for making cigarettes cheaper and more accessible, including to youth. The coalition, comprising over 250 civil society organizations, said Pakistan still needs stronger policies to meet its WHO tobacco-control obligations.

Standard variance components models may inadequately capture gene and isoform expression because cis-SNPs often have stronger effects than trans-SNPs, and genetic correlations can differ between SNP sets. To overcome limitations of existing methods, the authors implemented a minorization-maximization algorithm in Julia for maximum likelihood and restricted maximum likelihood estimation of multivariate linear mixed models with multiple phenotypes and variance components. Applied to PsychENCODE data, the method jointly modelled gene isoforms and partitioned genetic variance and covariance between cis- and trans-SNPs. Local variants showed sparse but large expression effects, while distal variants had small individual but large collective effects. Cis-SNPs showed greater shared genetic influence on isoform expression than trans-SNPs. Isoform-level analyses detected more genetic signals than gene-level analyses, including signals associated with psychiatric disorder risk.

GameStop’s 4,400-plus U.S. stores will each receive at least five $300 Nintendo Switch consoles by August 15, available no later than August 16. They are in-store only; online sales remain limited to bundles shipping in September.

SoDaDE is a data-driven solvent fingerprint designed to improve molecular modelling, particularly for solvent selection in the Catechol Benchmark. It uses a transformer trained on the Spange dataset of 191 solvents and up to 12 properties. Training data are augmented by shuffling property-value pairs, while masking enables property prediction and handles missing values. Inputs combine solvent type, ChemBERTa fingerprints, property labels, and numerical values.

The final model has five layers, 16 attention heads, and a dimension of 64. It achieved a normalized validation MSE of 0.107. On a five-solvent property-prediction test set, SoDaDE obtained an average MSE of 0.170, compared with 0.335 for Gaussian processes, 0.550 for random forests, and 4.23 for property averages.

For the Catechol Benchmark, SoDaDE representations were combined with temperature and residence time to predict starting material and product percentages. Without fine-tuning, SoDaDE achieved MSEs of 0.0029 on the full mixture dataset and 0.0044 on single-solvent data; with fine-tuning, results were 0.0026 and 0.0044. These results surpassed ACS, DRFP, fragprint, Spange, RXNFP, and ChemBERTa representations. Similar tuned and untuned performance suggests the fingerprint captures general solvent features, demonstrating that effective representations can be learned from small datasets.

The Trump administration postponed threatened 100% tariffs on branded drug imports. It will prepare tariffs for companies that neither build U.S. infrastructure nor reach drug-pricing agreements, but provided no new timeline.

MMFP-Tableau is a secure health data integration and visualization platform developed at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia for primary mitochondrial disease. It combines clinical and research data from EPIC, REDCap, spreadsheets, surveys, and laboratory records. Alteryx automates extraction, cleaning, transformation, coding, and analysis, while Tableau provides role-based, interactive dashboards.

The platform integrates real-time data from more than 2,000 individuals, supporting patient- and cohort-level queries without requiring advanced informatics expertise. Human Phenotype Ontology and diagnostic codes standardize phenotype data. Applications include cohort characterization, clinical trial eligibility screening, genotype-phenotype mapping, medication trend analysis, risk-factor assessment, biospecimen tracking, and review of laboratory, hospitalization, and patient-reported outcome data.

Iterative review by clinicians, researchers, analysts, and scientists improved data quality, visualization, and structured clinical documentation. The system reduces manual chart review, duplication, data loss, and disconnected workflows while maintaining controlled access behind an institutional firewall. Limitations include difficulty extracting non-discretized data, separately stored imaging, scanned PDFs, and external institutional records, as well as performance issues caused by large volumes of live data. The framework is scalable and potentially transferable to other diseases, cohorts, and health systems.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell architecture introduces ninth-generation NVENC encoding with improved AV1 and HEVC quality, 4:2:2 support, and AV1 Ultra High Quality mode. The RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders, while sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed. DisplayPort 2.1b enables up to 80 Gbps bandwidth, supporting 8K at 165Hz or 4K at 480Hz with DSC.

Blackwell’s Max-Q improvements include fine-grained clock, power, memory, and voltage-rail gating; clocks that adjust 1,000 times faster; and low-power states entered more quickly. Its deepest sleep state is entered ten times faster than Ada’s, contributing to observed power savings of up to 50% in small-language-model inference.

DLSS 4 adds Multi Frame Generation, producing up to three additional frames per rendered frame. Its frame-generation model is 40% faster, uses 30% less VRAM, and employs enhanced display-engine Flip Metering. Transformer models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA use twice as many parameters as prior CNN models, improving temporal stability, motion detail, lighting, anti-aliasing, and artifact reduction.

Blackwell also introduces developer-created neural shaders through Cooperative Vectors APIs for DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Applications include neural materials, texture compression, radiance caching, subsurface scattering through RTX Skin, and generative facial rendering through RTX Neural Faces. Neural Texture Compression can substantially reduce memory use, while Neural Radiance Cache approximates multi-bounce indirect lighting from limited traced rays.

The flagship GB202 GPU contains 92.2 billion transistors, 192 SMs, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, and 768 Tensor cores. GB203 contains 45.6 billion transistors and 10,752 CUDA cores, while GB205 contains 31 billion transistors and 6,400 CUDA cores. These chips underpin the RTX 5090, 5080, 5070 Ti, and 5070 products.

The lecture introduces stability, causality, linear constant-coefficient difference equations, and frequency response for discrete-time linear shift-invariant systems.

A system is stable if every bounded input produces a bounded output. For a linear shift-invariant system, stability is equivalent to its unit sample response being absolutely summable. Such a system is causal if its unit sample response is zero for negative indices. Causality is useful to identify but need not always be imposed, since noncausal systems can be useful.

Linear constant-coefficient difference equations express outputs through delayed inputs and outputs. Zeroth-order equations directly match the convolution sum, with coefficients forming the unit sample response. Higher-order equations require boundary or initial conditions. For the first-order equation \(y(n)-ay(n-1)=x(n)\), causal boundary conditions produce \(h(n)=a^n u(n)\), which is stable when \(|a|<1\). Noncausal boundary conditions produce \(h(n)=-a^n u(-n-1)\), which is unstable for \(|a|<1\). Thus, a difference equation alone does not uniquely specify a system; appropriate boundary conditions are also required.

Complex exponentials are eigenfunctions of linear shift-invariant systems. An input \(e^{j\omega n}\) produces an output \(H(e^{j\omega})e^{j\omega n}\), where
\[
H(e^{j\omega})=\sum_n h(n)e^{-j\omega n}
\]
is the frequency response. Its magnitude determines the amplitude change of a sinusoidal input, while its phase determines the phase shift.

For the causal first-order system with \(h(n)=a^n u(n)\) and \(|a|<1\), the frequency response is
\[
H(e^{j\omega})=\frac{1}{1-ae^{-j\omega}}.
\]
Discrete-time frequency response is a continuous function of \(\omega\) and is periodic with period \(2\pi\), because discrete-time complex exponentials repeat when frequency changes by integer multiples of \(2\pi\). The next lecture extends these ideas to the discrete-time Fourier transform.

House of Fraser’s annual pre-tax profit rose from £1.3 million to £3.4 million, while revenue remained flat at £1.3 billion. Online sales increased 16.1%, but the retailer warned of continued market volatility. It will discontinue five underperforming brands and recently opened its first standalone Chinese store in Nanjing.

The lecture introduces plasma self-emission as a diagnostic spanning radio frequencies to gamma rays. Radiation can cool plasmas while revealing their spatial, temporal, and spectral properties. Its transport is often non-local and complex because emission, absorption, and re-emission transfer energy through the plasma.

Spectral radiance evolves along a path according to the radiation transport equation, balancing emissivity against absorption determined by opacity. Optical depth is the path integral of opacity and distinguishes optically thin, transparent systems from optically thick, opaque ones. For homogeneous conditions, the equation has an analytic solution combining attenuated incident radiation with locally emitted radiation that may subsequently be absorbed. Emissivity and opacity depend on frequency and position, while simplified treatments assume straight paths, isotropic emission, and independent frequencies.

In the optically thick limit, radiation approaches blackbody emission. Equating this with the transport solution yields Kirchhoff’s law, linking emissivity and opacity: strongly emitting regions also strongly absorb. Calculating plasma emission generally requires quantities such as temperature, density, and sometimes magnetic-field direction.

Optical absorption is distinguished from wave cutoff. Absorption gradually attenuates an oscillating wave, whereas cutoff produces reflection and an exponentially decaying evanescent field beyond a critical surface. Evanescent waves can cross a sufficiently narrow forbidden region and resume propagation.

The lecture then explains why accelerated charges radiate. A stationary charge has no Poynting flux, while a uniformly moving charge carries its electromagnetic fields without producing far-field radiation. Acceleration creates outward electromagnetic energy flow. The full single-charge field contains near-field and far-field terms: near-field power decreases with distance, while far-field power propagates with constant total power through expanding spheres. Applying this to plasmas requires solving particle motion and integrating over the velocity distribution; later lectures will use quoted results for mechanisms including cyclotron radiation, Bremsstrahlung, recombination, and bound-electron emission.

Seventh grader Calvin Alexander of Caddo Middle Magnet won the Northwest Louisiana regional spelling bee for the second consecutive year by spelling “nectarivorous.” The 20-round LSUS and KTBS-sponsored competition featured 22 spellers, with Rosetta Schultz finishing second. Alexander advances to the 2018 Scripps National Spelling Bee near Washington, D.C., receiving an expenses-paid trip and other prizes. The Bee aims to improve students’ spelling, vocabulary, English usage, public speaking and performance under pressure.

The DuBard School was one of four U.S. schools recognized by IMSLEC for multisensory structured language education. Its accredited DuBard Association Method teaches reading, speaking and writing, with the school serving as its national training site.

The head and shoulders pattern is a technical chart formation comprising three price highs separated by two lows, with the middle high forming the “head” above two “shoulders.” It is considered a bearish reversal signal, typically after an uptrend. A neckline connects the intervening lows, and the pattern is confirmed when price breaks below it. Traders may close long positions or sell short, sometimes placing a stop-loss above the right shoulder. A target can be estimated by projecting the head’s height below the neckline.

The inverse pattern consists of three lows, with the middle low deepest, and signals a potential bullish reversal. It is completed when price breaks above the neckline connecting the intervening highs. Suggested stop-loss locations include below the right inverse shoulder or at the neckline.

The pattern is difficult to define objectively for software backtesting. Thomas Bulkowski’s study of more than 15,000 formations across 500 stocks reported a 93% success rate for 431 head and shoulders examples, defining failure as a decline of less than 5% below the neckline before reversal. The average decline was 23%. His inverse-pattern research indicated few false signals and potential returns of 20–30% within 73 days. He found that volume and neckline direction generally did not determine results, though inverse breakouts should occur on high volume.

The authors caution that Bulkowski’s research used after-the-fact analysis and state that they could not create a fully quantified strategy. A 1995 Federal Reserve Bank of New York report also found statistically significant profits from technical analysis, including head and shoulders strategies.

The Base Cross offense challenges defenses with a strong inside game, quick reversals, and down screens. In the Basic NBA Show & Recover strategy, defenders avoid switching when a smaller player screens for a post. The screener’s defender shows to force the post high and wide, allowing the post defender to recover, while weakside defenders pack the lane. Defenders pressure the ball, deny post position, and recover after passes.

The All Out SOS strategy disrupts the offense by trapping the wing ball handler before a post entry. It uses a Hi-Lo Switch: defenders switch when the post cuts low but not when the post cuts high. On passes out of traps, nearby defenders rotate immediately, deny return and post passes, force the ball toward sideline or corner checkpoints, and establish help positions and box pressure.

Giving career advice to adult children is difficult because they need independence while still facing workplace challenges. Expert Ruth Nemzoff recommends three principles: recognize how personal experiences shape advice, tailor communication to the individual child and their circumstances, and consider current workplace and economic conditions.

Parents should first ask whether the child wants advice or only to vent. They should approach the discussion with curiosity, ask nonjudgmental questions, acknowledge that the child knows the situation best, and share their own career mistakes to create an equal, productive exchange.

Rather than dictating solutions, parents can help identify the problem and the next practical step, such as arranging an introduction for an informational interview. They may also suggest consulting an objective third party, career adviser, or therapist when serious issues are involved. Ultimately, parents should not expect their advice to be followed or resent their child for ignoring it.

The paper introduces automatic detection of “hype”—hyperbolic or subjective language used to promote scientific research—as an NLP task focused on biomedical texts. Hype may bias research evaluation, create unrealistic expectations, and erode public trust, but identifying it is context-dependent because potentially promotional adjectives can also have neutral or technical meanings.

Using NIH grant abstracts, the authors selected 11 novelty-related adjectives and randomly sampled 550 sentences. They developed six annotation criteria covering positive value judgments, hyperbole, gratuitous wording, amplification, adjective coordination, and broader promotional context. Three researchers annotated the data; discussion resolved 106 of 119 disagreements, producing 537 sentences, of which 392 were labeled Hype and 145 Not Hype. Groundbreaking, revolutionary, unparalleled, and unprecedented were always classified as hype, while emerging and latest were especially difficult to judge.

The authors evaluated traditional classifiers, pretrained language models, large language models, and an uninstructed human baseline. Traditional methods performed below the human baseline, with GloVe plus SVM achieving 0.796 accuracy. Finetuning substantially improved language-model performance: BERT achieved the best accuracy at 0.861, exceeding the human baseline of 0.824. GPT-4o-mini performed approximately on par with the human evaluator, whereas Llama 3.1 Instruct performed poorly. Biomedical pretraining did not improve results.

The findings suggest that formal guidelines can support reliable human annotation and that trained models show promise for hype detection. Limitations include subjective judgments, focus on one adjective category, a small English-language biomedical dataset, restricted computing resources, and uncertain applicability to other disciplines or languages. Future work will refine and expand the guidelines, lexicon, dataset, and human evaluation, and develop tools for flagging or editing promotional scientific language.
