UCLA’s offense gained 430-plus yards against Penn State, while its quarterback rushed for 150 yards and three touchdowns. Penn State’s projected playoff prospects, Big Ten title odds and expected record fell sharply.

Florida beat Texas 29-21 as its quarterback completed 21 of 28 passes for 298 yards and two touchdowns. Texas dropped to 20th in SP+, with a projected 7-5 record and difficult SEC games remaining. Alabama defeated Vanderbilt after the Commodores squandered scoring opportunities with turnovers, keeping the Crimson Tide well positioned in the SEC race. Miami beat Florida State, whose turnovers and reduced quarterback effectiveness effectively ended its ACC title and playoff hopes.

Texas Tech remained the Big 12 favorite after dominating Houston and has a 36% chance of finishing 12-0. Cincinnati entered the conference race by handing Iowa State its first loss, while BYU stayed unbeaten. Baylor, Kansas and TCU also remained contenders.

SP+ rewarded strong performances by UCLA, Florida, Northwestern, Notre Dame and Old Dominion, while Penn State suffered the largest cited decline. UCLA’s quarterback led the weekly Heisman-style rankings. Other notable results included dramatic late victories by Baylor, Arkansas State, Georgetown, West Liberty, Wisconsin-Oshkosh, Wisconsin-La Crosse and Augustana. Western Carolina’s quarterback completed an NCAA-record 46 consecutive passes.

Researchers Michelle Munson and Sarah Narendorf argue that mental health providers should understand how marginalized young adults interpret the causes, meaning, and treatment of their conditions. These narratives—shaped by factors such as stigma, poverty, discrimination, trauma, and genetics—strongly influence treatment engagement and self-care.

Using in-depth interviews and qualitative analysis, researchers found that young adults’ transitions can be either painful or hopeful depending partly on how mental health systems communicate with them. They recommend collaborative care in which professionals respect patients’ knowledge and adapt treatment to individual narratives. Current studies are testing whether narrative types persist across populations, change over time, and relate to health behaviors. The researchers also advocate provider training, cultural humility, replicated studies, and technology-based interventions, noting that many marginalized young adults avoid care because they do not feel heard, respected, or understood.

BBC Radio 4 presenter Anita Anand was temporarily removed from Any Answers because her public support for equal pay conflicted with BBC impartiality rules ahead of a discussion on the corporation’s gender pay dispute. Julian Worricker replaced her, and she is expected to return. Critics argued the decision implied women affected by pay discrimination could not be impartial. The BBC said editors assess such cases individually when staff publicly campaign on topics they may cover.

The NRA accused YETI of ending business with its foundation, prompting boycott calls and videos of supporters destroying YETI products. YETI said it had instead eliminated outdated discount programs for several organizations while offering an alternative customization program, calling the NRA’s statement inaccurate. The company also reaffirmed its support for the Constitution and Second Amendment.

Sixteen-year-old Murad Rahimov, an aspiring astronaut from Uzbekistan, received a private tour of NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center after an NPR listener learned of his ambitions. Astrophysicist Jeremy Schnittman showed Murad and his mother spacecraft testing facilities, a laser laboratory, and research on black holes, while discussing Einstein and time travel.

Murad immigrated to the United States in 2010 without speaking English and is now an accelerated high school student taking AP courses. After his family became U.S. citizens, he felt his goal of working for NASA was more attainable. His mother, Limara, also described feeling newly rooted in the country. Murad hopes to attend Caltech, lead a Mars mission, and continue pursuing his ambitions despite others urging him to choose a more conventional career.

Jonathan Toews said winning the Stanley Cup at home or on the road makes no difference; the team must ignore surrounding excitement and focus on its job. He described the playoffs as a fast-moving journey defined by adversity, togetherness and meaningful games, and said the team tends to improve as series progress. He praised Joel for managing matchups, lineups and individual performances, while crediting experienced players for preparing properly, recovering and staying healthy.

Brad Richards said repeated championship experience helps players remain comfortable, focused and prepared without needing speeches. He emphasized patience and smart puck management against an opponent expected to regain belief once play begins. He also praised a veteran teammate’s offensive, defensive and leadership qualities.

Kris Versteeg called the playoff run difficult, noting Tampa Bay’s playmaking ability and the expectation of close games. He was encouraged by his new line’s chemistry and said players outside the lineup must remain confident and ready to contribute when given an opportunity.

The message reviews an eventful year marked by national prosperity, a financial panic, diminished political partisanship, and the seizure of the U.S.-registered steamer Virginius by Spain. Most foreign relations remained friendly. Spain agreed to return the Virginius and surviving passengers and crew, salute the U.S. flag, investigate and punish unlawful violence, and provide appropriate indemnities after 53 people aboard were executed in Cuba. Naval forces were placed on a war footing during negotiations. The message attributes Cuba’s instability partly to slavery and expresses hope for its abolition.

American participation in the Vienna exposition produced numerous awards, and a U.S. representative attended an international conference on protecting inventions. Slight progress was reported against the Chinese coolie trade. The Geneva arbitration award was received from Britain and invested in a $15.5 million U.S. bond, with a commission recommended to compensate specified losses caused by Confederate vessels. U.S.-British boundaries were being surveyed, while a mixed commission awarded Britain $1,929,819 in gold and dismissed other claims. Congress was urged to fund this award and establish a court for alien claims arising from the insurrection.

Other foreign matters included neutrality in the Netherlands-Acheen war, renewed Mexican claims proceedings, Venezuelan obligations, proposed judicial reforms in Ottoman and Egyptian territories, Santo Domingo’s request for a U.S. protectorate, and several newly proclaimed treaties. Congress was asked to clarify expatriation, foreign marriage, nationality, and the status of children born abroad to American parents.

Proposed constitutional amendments would permit the President to veto portions of legislation, prohibit most legislation during Congress’s final 24 hours, and restrict extraordinary sessions to subjects submitted by the Executive.

Federal receipts were $333.7 million and expenditures $290.3 million, but declining revenue following the panic threatened a deficit. Economy was urged in public buildings, local river and harbor projects, fortifications, and claims arising from the rebellion. The message advocated eventual specie payments, an elastic currency, limits on speculative use of deposits, bank reserve reforms, clearinghouses, and possible adjustments to national-bank circulation. It also recommended tariff codification, additional mints, expanded domestic shipping, improved inland waterways, and exploration of the Amazon and Madeira Rivers.

Congress was urged to strengthen coastal armament and reopen Army staff promotions. The Navy had repaired six wooden ships and was completing eight new sloops of war. Postal revenues reached nearly $23 million against expenditures of about $29.1 million. Recommendations included expanded free delivery, revised postage and postmaster compensation, postal savings depositories, and consideration of postal telegraphs.

Justice Department concerns included the collapse of jury trials in Utah, involuntary bankruptcy during financial stringency, and fraudulent or stale claims against the Government. The Indian policy of concentrating tribes on reservations, promoting self-support, and punishing threats to peace would continue; a territorial government for Indian Territory was proposed.

Public-land disposal and surveys increased, Russian immigration was encouraged, pension rolls reached 238,411, and stronger safeguards against pension fraud were requested. A census in 1875 and possibly every five years was recommended. The message supported federal contributions to Washington improvements, a national university in the capital, enforceable civil-service rules, Colorado statehood, an irrigation canal east of the Rocky Mountains, general amnesty for remaining former Confederates under disability, and stronger protection of civil rights for formerly enslaved people.

Folate-rich foods include asparagus, broccoli, citrus fruits, legumes, avocado, lady’s finger, nuts and seeds, cauliflower, beetroot, carrots, and corn. A cup of boiled asparagus provides 33% of daily folate needs, avocado 28%, and broccoli, cauliflower, and beetroot about 14% each. Other notable amounts include 50 mcg per orange, 103 mcg per half-cup of cooked lady’s finger, and 34 mcg per cup of cooked corn.

Several deals announced Monday indicate renewed consolidation among junior gold miners after a slow period. Hecla Mining proposed a US$462-million cash-and-share acquisition of Klondex Mines, which would add three Nevada mines and raise Hecla’s annual gold production to about 370,000 ounces. Alio Gold proposed a $128-million acquisition of Rye Patch Gold, creating a company producing an estimated 165,000 ounces annually and strengthening Alio’s finances. Anaconda Mining also offered 14 cents per share for Maritime Resources. Canada recorded six metals and mining mergers so far in 2018, compared with 19 at the same point in 2017. Industry participants expect further consolidation as junior miners seek diversification, lower risk and reduced capital costs.

Four Hungarian women describe growing acceptance and influence in winemaking. Zita Kovács overcame early prejudice and is now respected as a winemaker while contributing creatively to labels and wine names. Zsófi Laposa says technology helped open the physically demanding, formerly male-centred profession to women, who bring gentleness and uniqueness. Krisztina Csetvei combines winemaking with motherhood, taking her daughter Panna to tastings and naming a rosé after her. Andi Gere jointly manages her family winery with her father and believes women add elegance, grace and variety to Hungarian wines.

This study benchmarked 15 two-sample Mendelian randomization methods using GWAS summary statistics and real-world genetic datasets. Performance was assessed by type I error control under population stratification, pleiotropy, and family-level confounding; accuracy of causal-effect estimates; replicability; and power. Instrument-selection thresholds and data preprocessing choices were also examined.

MR-APSS, Egger, and weighted-mode generally controlled type I errors across confounding scenarios and instrument thresholds, while CAUSE often produced deflated p-values and performed poorly under strong population stratification. The other 11 methods frequently showed inflated type I errors, particularly with population stratification and looser instrument thresholds. Using family-based GWAS data produced well-calibrated p-values for all methods, supporting its usefulness in mitigating family-level confounding.

For six same-trait exposure–outcome pairs with true causal effects of one, MR-APSS generated the most accurate estimates and maintained confidence-interval coverage across thresholds. Weighted-mode performed comparably at its default stringent threshold. Most other methods became biased toward zero as weaker instruments were included, indicating sensitivity to weak-instrument and selection bias.

In analyses of LDL cholesterol and coronary artery disease using six GWAS datasets, CAUSE and MR-APSS showed the greatest replicability across studies and thresholds, although CAUSE’s p-values disagreed with its confidence intervals. Larger GWAS sample sizes improved consistency and detection across methods.

The study recommends using negative controls, evaluating multiple instrument-selection thresholds, and testing independent data sources. Limitations include potentially coexisting confounders, limited positive controls, inability of same-trait analyses to assess pleiotropy, and exclusion of individual-level MR methods. MAF thresholds and same-ancestry LD reference panels generally had little effect.

MSPM0C1105/6 are cost-optimized, ultra-low-power 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0+ MCUs operating up to 32MHz, with up to 64KB flash and 8KB SRAM. They support 1.62–3.6V and –40°C to 125°C, integrating an oscillator, DMA, CRC, analog peripherals, timers, watchdog, UART, SPI, and I2C. TI provides development kits, SDK, examples, training, and support.

India’s 21 state-run banks posted a record combined loss of 853.7 billion rupees in 2017/18 as stricter central bank rules increased bad-loan provisions. Fourth-quarter losses reached 626.81 billion rupees, while gross non-performing loans rose 15% to 8.96 trillion rupees. The losses may limit growth funding despite New Delhi’s two-year, 2.11 trillion-rupee recapitalization plan and upcoming Basel III capital requirements.

Congress leader Pusa died at 63, leaving a wife and three children. A former Nagaland minister and four-term legislator, he was buried in Viswema after a funeral attended by prominent political leaders.

Detroit is described as the strongest opponent yet, with powerful offense, elite goaltending, strong special teams and skilled faceoff players. The speaker says his team must adapt to strict officiating, avoid unnecessary penalties, make smarter power-play decisions, improve faceoffs and generate more offense. Detroit’s line led by Kris Draper requires particular attention, while its top defenseman is praised for positioning and puck movement. The team is focusing on the next game despite family, ticket and other distractions, and expects an exceptionally loud home crowd. The speaker also jokes about his increasingly unmanageable playoff beard.

The disclosure describes articles that use optical elements to produce structural color through scattering, refraction, reflection, interference, or diffraction rather than solely through pigments or dyes. Applications include footwear, apparel, sporting equipment, containers, electronics, and eyewear. In footwear, optical elements may be attached to uppers, soles, cushioning bladders, or foam and displayed through openings or transparent components.

Optical elements may contain single- or multilayer reflectors or filters, protective and polymeric layers, textured surfaces, and primer layers. Layer materials, thicknesses, refractive indices, and arrangements can be selected to produce desired colors. Textured micro- or nanoscale features can modify optical effects through their dimensions, shapes, spacing, and orientation. Primer layers may include paints, inks, polymers, metals, oxides, pigments, or dyes and can further alter the resulting color.

Structural colors may be single-hued, multihued, angle-independent, highly iridescent, or limited in iridescence, with matte, glossy, or metallic appearances. Color variation may be evaluated at multiple viewing or illumination angles using CIELAB, CIELCH, or PANTONE systems. Optical and supporting layers may be deposited through vapor deposition, sputtering, wet chemistry, printing, coating, or related processes.

The articles and layers may use thermoplastic or thermoset polymers, including polyurethanes, polyesters, polyethers, polyamides, polyolefins, polycarbonates, and copolymers. The disclosure particularly discusses thermoplastic and elastomeric polyurethanes, their thermal and mechanical properties, and their use in textured surfaces, coatings, adhesives, and article components.

A Zillow analysis of homes sold or listed for rent from June 2017 through May 2018 found that U.S. homes with central air conditioning sold for 2.5% more on average, about $5,486, while rentals commanded 2.8% more, or roughly $40 monthly. San Antonio had the highest home-sale premium at 5.8%, followed by Cincinnati at 5.7%. New York, Las Vegas and Phoenix had the highest rental premiums. Nationwide, 66.1% of sold homes and 54.7% of rental listings had air conditioning. Zillow controlled for property characteristics and location across the 35 largest metropolitan areas.

A survey of 100 financial services professionals found that over 80% expect commercial blockchain adoption by 2020, while more than half are investing or planning to invest in 2017. Average investment is about $1 million. Banks favor private blockchains and prioritize payments, identity management, clearing, credit and loan syndication.

Gov. Kay Ivey announced the voluntary Alabama Sentry Program, allowing trained, locally approved administrators at schools without resource officers to access securely stored firearms during active-shooter incidents. Participants or school boards must provide approved weapons, ammunition and bulletproof vests. Ivey described the program as an interim security measure while pursuing more school resource officers. State law enforcement and education officials endorsed the program as a way to improve school safety without new funding.

IWM options trading involves calls, which grant rights to buy shares, and puts, which grant rights to sell shares, at agreed prices before expiration. Options provide leverage, speculation, and hedging but can result in total investment loss; short calls may carry unlimited risk.

Available orders include market, limit, stop, and trailing stop orders. Strategies include buying calls or puts, covered calls, protective puts, spreads, straddles, and butterfly spreads. Contract selection should consider duration, expiration, and strike price.

Investors should research underlying assets and contracts, monitor relevant news and economic data, use technical indicators, and backtest strategies. Risk controls include stop-loss orders, diversification, position limits, and allocating no more than 10% of a portfolio to options.

Requirements and costs vary by broker. Investors generally need sufficient funds and a margin account, while minimum balances are commonly around $2,000. Margin trading and short selling are allowed but involve substantial risk. Commissions, other fees, and capital-gains taxes may apply. The passage advises beginners to avoid options trading and emphasizes understanding contracts and risks before committing funds.

The Bank of England warned that AI stock valuations resemble dot-com-era levels and may be detached from fundamentals. Gains concentrated among major U.S. technology firms, alongside power, semiconductor and data-infrastructure constraints, could increase the risk of a sharp correction and global volatility. While the UK financial system remains broadly stable, its openness leaves it exposed to U.S. market shocks. The IMF has raised similar concerns about inflated AI-linked asset prices.

Plum School District will begin preliminary 2018-19 budget discussions early, hoping to avoid a third consecutive tax increase while carrying more than $4 million in debt. Its current $66 million budget raised property taxes without cutting programs, and the district approved a $5.6 million bond. Officials will also discuss recruiting tuition-paying Chinese students, elementary construction, consolidation, redistricting and the process for closing Regency Park Elementary School.

The passage describes systems and methods for tracing blockchain asset flows and managing cryptocurrency transaction risk for anti-money laundering, counterterrorism financing, fraud detection, and blockchain forensics. Transaction and off-blockchain data are combined with intelligence labels, entity information, address clustering, and machine-learning behavior classifications.

An auto-tracing system receives source, intermediate, and destination addresses plus parameters such as direction, time range, transaction value, and maximum hops. AI graph-search algorithms identify asset paths and generate interactive visualizations, destination statistics, suspicious-address reports, and alerts. Suspicious activity may trigger transaction blocking, asset freezing, or account suspension; normal transactions may be approved.

Risk engines classify behaviors and assign scores using blockchain activity, external information, graph connectivity, and time decay. AutoML pipelines preprocess labeled data, extract features, train and evaluate models, select a model, and deploy it for prediction. Supported approaches include decision trees, regression, neural networks, gradient boosting, random forests, and support vector machines. The solution may support multiple blockchains, fiat transactions, exchanges, KYC mappings, and real-world entity information.
The Eighth Circuit docketed and dismissed Pink C. Jenkins’s appeal against the United States on the appellee’s motion and with the appellant’s consent.

Pump-and-dump schemes involve promoters acquiring assets, often penny stocks or low-volume cryptocurrencies, then inflating prices through false or misleading claims. As rising prices trigger fear of missing out, promoters sell to late buyers, causing prices to collapse and leaving most participants with losses.

Such schemes occur mainly in OTC penny stocks and unregulated crypto markets, while regulation, enforcement, and larger company sizes make them less common on major exchanges. A German study found nearly 6% of sampled investors participated in at least one scheme, with an average return of -28%. Pump-and-dumps are described as illegal in regulated stock markets, immoral, and difficult to identify beforehand. Investors are advised to avoid sudden, unsupported price increases, exercise caution in OTC markets, and use legitimate, systematic, long-term approaches.

Orbital ATK’s Q2 2017 sales rose 3% to $1.12 billion, slightly exceeding estimates. Adjusted earnings of $1.56 per share beat expectations, but GAAP earnings fell 3% as operating margin declined to 12.2%. Free cash flow shifted from positive $107.2 million a year earlier to negative $55.8 million.

Management expects faster revenue and earnings growth and significant free cash flow in the second half. Strong bookings increased firm backlog 10%, prompting higher full-year guidance of $4.6 billion to $4.65 billion in sales and earnings of $5.95 to $6.25 per share. Free cash flow guidance remained $250 million to $300 million.

Argus Research upgraded the stock from hold to buy with a $120 target, citing expected cash-flow milestones, increased defense spending, and valuation. However, the author considers the stock too expensive after a 44% annual rise, given its earnings and cash-flow multiples and projected 10% annual profit growth.

The disclosure describes methods, apparatuses, and systems for paging in beam-based wireless communications. High-frequency beamforming requires paging across multiple beams or ports, while idle user equipment cannot predict beam scheduling, making LTE-style discontinuous reception difficult.

A first communication node calculates a second node’s paging occasion and transmits paging downlink control information and/or a paging message within it. The paging occasion comprises resources for one or more preset beams or ports and may correspond to a synchronization-signal burst set or other sweeping resources. The second node independently calculates the same occasion and receives the paging information.

Paging occasions may be determined from parameters including the discontinuous reception cycle, paging transmission interval, number of paging transmissions, device identifier, and paging-occasion offset. These parameters determine starting radio-frame and, when necessary, subframe positions. The nodes may also configure or exchange quasi-co-location information linking paging-related signals with sweeping signals or channels, enabling the terminal to determine reception resources and beams.

The disclosure also provides corresponding base-station and terminal apparatuses, a communication system, computer-readable storage media, and computer programs. The proposed mechanisms are intended to support reliable beam-swept paging while enabling energy-saving discontinuous reception for idle terminals.

Sean “Diddy” Combs was sentenced to four years and two months in prison and fined $500,000 after being convicted under the Mann Act for transporting girlfriends and male sex workers across state lines for drug-fueled sexual encounters. Having already served a year, he could be released in about three years. Combs was acquitted of sex trafficking and racketeering charges. Trial testimony included allegations of violence, threats, sexual assault and coercion. Before sentencing, Combs apologized for his “disgusting, shameful” actions and requested leniency, while prosecutors emphasized his years of violence and control. Six of his seven children appealed to the judge for mercy.

This qualitative study proposes “whole human pedagogy,” a decolonial framework for education abroad that treats students as integrated beings whose bodily, emotional, relational, and meaning-making knowledge matters. Derived from hooks’ engaged pedagogy, Thompson’s tenderness pedagogy, experiential learning, and decolonial theory, the framework has four tenets: embodiment, emotions, belonging, and becoming.

Seventeen practitioners from U.S.-based undergraduate education abroad organizations participated in semi-structured interviews in Fall 2023. Participants viewed whole-human approaches as central to their work. Embodiment involved sensory, place-based, physical, mindful, and identity-related learning. Emotions included normalizing culture shock, accepting discomfort, and using structured reflection. Belonging emphasized nonhierarchical facilitator relationships, reciprocity, trust, vulnerability, and collaborative learning communities. Becoming focused on transformation, self-knowledge, self-sufficiency, and finding purpose.

Findings provide preliminary support for whole human pedagogy as a framework centered on collaboration, presence, mutuality, creativity, and wellbeing. It challenges dominant Euro-U.S. educational values by including forms of knowledge often excluded from academia. The framework may guide program design and assessment, professional development, and future research on holistic education abroad.

Amazon announced new hardware featuring Alexa+, including Echo speakers and displays powered by AZ3-series chips, Omnisense sensors, improved audio, cameras, and support for Alexa Home Theater. Alexa+ offers conversational, contextual assistance, is free for Prime subscribers and costs $20 monthly for others.

Three third-generation Kindle Scribe models include the first color Scribe, faster performance, lower writing latency, cloud file integration, AI notebook search, and spoiler-free reading tools.

Amazon also introduced faster Fire TVs with Omnisense and Dialogue Boost, plus a $40 Fire TV Stick 4K Select powered by its new Vega operating system.

New Ring cameras use Retinal 2K or 4K image processing and add Familiar Faces, customizable Alexa+ Greetings, and Search Party, which uses participating neighborhood cameras to locate lost dogs. Ring customers may voluntarily respond to law-enforcement footage requests. Blink also received 2K cameras and an Arc accessory combining two cameras for 180-degree coverage.

NGC 5949 is a nearby barred spiral dwarf galaxy about 44 million light-years away and one-hundredth the Milky Way’s mass. Discovered by William Herschel in 1801, it helps astronomers investigate dwarf galaxies and unresolved dark matter and “missing satellites” problems.

When Jill Medvedow became director of Boston’s Institute of Contemporary Art in 1998, the museum had limited funding, low attendance, no permanent collection, weak public visibility, and an inadequate converted police-station facility. Seeking to make contemporary art accessible and relevant to broader audiences, she established a planning group that recommended expanding education, considering a collection, growing attendance, and finding a new location.

Medvedow pursued waterfront property as both an audience draw and a symbol of expanded horizons. In 1999, the ICA won rights to Parcel J on South Boston’s Fan Pier after presenting plans for a publicly oriented museum and demonstrating financial viability. She built support among residents, politicians, artists, donors, and business leaders while continuing exhibitions and public-art programming. The ICA hired development leadership, launched an initially underfunded capital campaign, and added prominent financial and business figures to its board.

Through a public selection process, the ICA chose Diller + Scofidio, an architecture firm that had never completed a U.S. building. Construction required numerous government approvals and faced setbacks, including the surrounding property’s sale, contractor problems, and delays. The new $51 million ICA opened on December 10, 2006, attracting more than 8,000 visitors that day.

The campaign ultimately raised over $75 million, exceeding its $62 million goal. First-year attendance surpassed 280,000, above the 200,000 needed to break even, and combined attendance in 2008 and 2009 exceeded 450,000. Shepard Fairey’s 2009 exhibition alone attracted 130,000 visitors despite his arrest outside its opening celebration. Medvedow’s transformation of the ICA relied on disciplined organizing, public outreach, coalition-building, and repeated financial, architectural, and institutional risks.

In 1892, U.S. Minister Stevens reported political instability in Hawaii, hostility toward the heir, growing support for U.S. annexation, dissatisfaction with Queen Liliʻuokalani’s government, and recurring revolutionary plans. He advocated either annexation or closer U.S. control through a customs union, cable connection, permanent possession of Pearl Harbor, and an implied protectorate. Naval reports corroborated his accounts, culminating in news of the peaceful revolution and the Queen’s dethronement in January 1893. The report characterizes U.S. policy toward Hawaii from 1820 to 1893 as friendship and protection, opposition to foreign intervention, and occasional consideration of annexation. The appendix provides selected correspondence, excludes minor private claims, and notes uncompleted treaties and additional Navy Department records.

Theratechnologies agreed with underwriters led by RBC Capital Markets to offer US$50 million of convertible unsecured senior notes due June 30, 2023, with an option for an additional US$7.5 million. The notes bear 5.75% annual interest and are convertible into common shares at US$14.85 per share. They may be redeemed after June 30, 2021, subject to specified trading-price conditions.

Proceeds will fund US$23.85 million in payments under the amended EMD Serono Termination Agreement, Trogarzo’s approval and commercialization in Europe and other jurisdictions, general corporate purposes, and potential acquisitions. The offering, expected to close around June 19, 2018, requires regulatory approvals. It will be offered through a Canadian prospectus and potentially a U.S. private placement. The securities are not registered under U.S. securities laws. Completion and use-of-proceeds statements are subject to assumptions, risks, and uncertainties.

The Supreme Court rejected Varun Thakur’s plea to cancel anticipatory bail for Ryan International School’s owners in his son Pradyuman’s murder case. The CBI cleared the arrested bus conductor and accused a class 11 student.

Container design patterns provide modular ways to extend and connect applications. Sidecars augment colocated application containers, enabling HTTPS termination, dynamic configuration, process monitoring, Git-based deployment, and other reusable functions without modifying legacy code. Effective sidecars require configurable parameters, stable APIs, and clear image documentation.

Ambassador containers broker external communication. They can route requests to sharded storage, discover environment-specific services, or split traffic between production and experimental implementations. Adapter containers normalize application interfaces for monitoring, logging, and health checks, allowing heterogeneous or third-party software to work with common operational tools.

These single-node patterns support reuse and separation of concerns but may be less tailored or efficient than application-specific code. They also form building blocks for multi-node microservice architectures, whose independent components and formal APIs improve team autonomy, scaling, and reliability while making design and debugging more difficult.

Replicated load-balanced services provide redundancy and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching instances before initialization, while session tracking consistently routes a user to one replica. Layered replicated services can add caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination.

Sharded services divide state among machines when one machine cannot hold or serve all data. Routing may occur through client-side ambassadors or shared proxy services. Sharded caches use memory more efficiently than replicated caches but can lose capacity when a shard fails; replicating each shard improves resilience and supports scaling hot shards. Effective sharding depends on deterministic, uniform key selection and consistent hashing, which limits remapping when shard counts change.

The scatter/gather pattern distributes portions of a computation across multiple replicas, then combines their partial results, reducing request-processing time through parallelism across machines.

President Trump denied a New York Times report that he watches four to eight hours of television daily. The Times stood by its article, citing interviews with 60 advisers, associates, friends and members of Congress. His denial followed criticism of other media outlets for publishing “fake news.”

Education researchers are cautiously optimistic that the Trump administration may rebuild parts of the Institute of Education Sciences after extensive staffing, contract and grant cuts. The Education Department plans to reinstate some research contracts, temporarily restore 10 regional education labs, seek public input on modernizing IES and hire staff for National Assessment of Educational Progress work. Researchers also view Amber Northern’s appointment to advise Secretary Linda McMahon on reforming IES as encouraging.

However, severe staffing shortages, including the reduction of the National Center for Education Statistics from about 100 employees to three, continue to threaten research quality, data collection and reporting. Experts worry that new data demands, reduced NAEP reporting and cuts to supporting databases could undermine future assessments. While some believe research programs and regional labs should be redesigned to produce clearer results, they argue that federal education research remains essential amid declining test scores. Ongoing uncertainty over funding, staffing and policy continues to disrupt researchers and universities.

The Ultimate Oscillator is a momentum indicator developed by Larry Williams in 1976. It measures buying pressure across short-, medium-, and long-term periods, typically 7, 14, and 28, to reduce premature overbought readings and false divergence signals associated with single-timeframe oscillators.

Buying pressure equals the close minus the lower of the current low or prior close. True range equals the higher of the current high or prior close minus the lower of the current low or prior close. Ratios of summed buying pressure to summed true range are calculated for each period, weighted 4:2:1, and scaled from 0 to 100. Readings below 30 are considered oversold and those above 70 overbought.

Trading signals rely on price-indicator divergence. A buy signal requires bullish divergence beginning below 30 and a rise above the divergence high; opposite conditions produce a sell signal. Rising values indicate stronger buying pressure, while falling values indicate weakening momentum.

A default SPY strategy buying below 40 and selling above 50 performed poorly. However, optimization of the three periods produced generally strong results. One example generated 355 trades, a 0.77% average gain, 78% win rate, 2.5 profit factor, and 25% maximum drawdown. The passage characterizes the oscillator as a consistent mean-reversion indicator across varied settings.

Lava from Hawaii’s Kilauea volcano crossed Highway 132, destroyed utility equipment and caused extended power outages in coastal communities. Officials reported 71 homes destroyed, with the number expected to rise, along with more than 400 utility poles. Residents near Kapoho were ordered to evacuate amid possible isolation, and one trapped person was rescued. Since the May 3 eruption began, 24 fissures have opened, thousands of residents have been displaced, and ash, volcanic glass and gases have prompted health warnings. Lava also covered two monitored wells at a geothermal plant, though officials reported no dangerous gas releases.

Meb Faber’s Tactical Asset Allocation strategy is an active trend-following, market-timing approach covering equally weighted U.S. stocks, foreign stocks, U.S. bonds, U.S. REITs, and world commodities. Each category can be represented by a diversified, liquid index ETF; 20% is allocated to each asset when signaled, otherwise held in cash. Bonds, REITs, and commodities improve diversification through lower correlation with stocks. A 16-year backtest reported a maximum drawdown of 13.24%, substantially below typical passive-portfolio drawdowns. The timing model can also be applied to other asset classes and ETFs.

The Minnesota Court of Appeals reviewed an order increasing Richard Berg’s child support from $145 to $258 per month for each of two minor children, based on his net monthly income rising from $1,246 to $1,721. Nancy Berg’s employment income had also increased since the divorce. The trial court found Richard’s increased income made the original support terms unreasonable and unfair and applied the statutory guideline level of $516 monthly. Although the appellate court considered the amount within the trial court’s discretion, it held that the findings did not adequately explain the reasons for the modification under Moylan v. Moylan and relevant statutes. The case was remanded for complete, specific factual findings supporting the increase.

Automation threatens millions of jobs, including 3.5 million U.S. truck drivers, as autonomous vehicles, AI, and robots expand into transportation, law, hospitality, journalism, and other fields. The World Economic Forum predicts the Fourth Industrial Revolution will eliminate over five million jobs within five years.

The passage examines human augmentation as a possible response. Neural lace technology could integrate electronic mesh with the brain, improving its ability to receive, process, and communicate information. Researchers have injected electronic mesh into mice’s brains, while Elon Musk has promoted neural lace as a way for humans to remain competitive with AI. However, functional versions remain years away.

Physical augmentation through powered or soft exosuits could combine human intelligence and adaptability with robotic strength and precision. Systems developed by SuitX, Harvard, Hyundai, and the U.S. Army can reduce physical strain, assist people with disabilities, and help soldiers and laborers perform demanding tasks. Such technology may preserve human roles in unstructured work that robots cannot yet automate.

Workers can also improve employability by developing creativity, technical knowledge, and skills for working alongside machines. However, these strategies may be more accessible to knowledge workers than physical laborers, and some professions may still disappear. Narrow AI currently performs specialized tasks, but artificial general intelligence capable of matching broad human intellectual abilities would create far greater uncertainty.

Major-General Qassem Soleimani said Iran’s Revolutionary Guards were ready to prevent regional oil exports if U.S. policy halted Iranian oil sales. President Hassan Rouhani had suggested disrupting neighboring countries’ shipments, while Iranian officials have previously threatened to block the Strait of Hormuz.

The Canadian dollar held near C$1.2857 per U.S. dollar as investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s expected rate increase and a speech by Bank of Canada Governor Stephen Poloz. The currency had fallen 1.3 percent the prior week following the central bank’s dovish tone. Speculators reduced bullish Canadian-dollar positions. Oil prices edged higher, while Canadian government bond prices rose slightly across a flatter yield curve. NAFTA negotiators were set to hold limited talks in Washington the following week.

BidaskClub upgraded Rapid7 from “hold” to “buy.” Across analysts, the stock has two sell, one hold and eight buy ratings, with an average “Buy” rating and a $20.19 consensus price target. Rapid7 closed Friday at $18.47, near its one-year high of $18.65, with a market capitalization of $796.26 million. Rapid7 provides analytics for cybersecurity and IT operations.

The University of Agriculture Faisalabad approved Rs3.28 billion in non-development accounts for 2015-16. The university reported 48 new degree programs, enrolment exceeding 25,000, Rs700 million in financial assistance and a Rs2.5 billion research portfolio. Vice Chancellor Dr Iqrar Ahmad urged greater agricultural research investment, reduced wheat irrigation, and modern handling, storage and processing to address water scarcity, malnutrition, low productivity and 40 percent post-harvest losses.

Amazon’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2017 reported Q3 net sales of $43.7 billion, up 34% year over year, and net income of $256 million, compared with $252 million in 2016. Nine-month net sales rose 27% to $117.4 billion, while net income declined to $1.18 billion from $1.62 billion. Operating income fell to $347 million for Q3 and $1.98 billion for nine months.

Q3 segment sales were $25.4 billion for North America, $13.7 billion for International, and $4.6 billion for AWS. Segment operating results were income of $112 million, a loss of $936 million, and income of $1.17 billion, respectively. Higher fulfillment, technology, content, and marketing spending reduced consolidated operating income.

At September 30, Amazon had $115.3 billion in assets, $12.8 billion in cash and equivalents, $24.7 billion in long-term debt, and $24.7 billion in stockholders’ equity. Nine-month operating cash flow was $6.1 billion, investing outflow was $25.8 billion, and financing inflow was $12.5 billion.

Amazon acquired Souq for approximately $579 million and Whole Foods Market for approximately $13.2 billion. Whole Foods contributed $1.3 billion in sales and $21 million in operating income after its August 28 acquisition. Amazon issued $16.0 billion of senior notes, primarily to finance the transaction.

The company disclosed $116.5 billion in contractual commitments, ongoing tax disputes and legal proceedings, and planned adoption of new revenue, lease, income-tax, and restricted-cash accounting standards. It stated that existing liquidity, operating cash flow, and available borrowing capacity should meet anticipated operating needs for at least 12 months.

Emperor penguins are classified as near-threatened, with one study projecting a 19 percent population decline by 2100. A new remote-monitoring system combines minute-by-minute colony photographs with weather data, enabling online observation. It found penguins huddling in warmer conditions, possibly indicating reduced body fat and food scarcity linked to sea-ice loss, though commercial fishing may also be responsible. Experts praised the system as cost-effective for Antarctic research.

President Donald Trump said the U.S. will impose an additional 100% tariff on Chinese imports and export controls on all “critical software” starting Nov. 1, 2025. The measures respond to China’s planned restrictions requiring licenses for certain products containing Chinese rare earths or made with related Chinese technology. China supplies about 70% of global rare earths, which are essential to automotive, defense and semiconductor industries. Trump also suggested canceling a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Chinese imports already face an estimated 40% effective U.S. tariff rate.

India urged the UN Secretariat to disclose serious misconduct cases involving UN personnel and instances where immunity blocked prosecution. Legal adviser Yedla Umasankar criticised the UN for allegedly hesitating to waive immunity and requested data on waiver requests, refusals, consultations, and prosecution referrals. His request excludes member-state diplomats. Although the UN publishes data on sexual misconduct in peacekeeping and has identified accused personnel’s nationalities since 2015, it lacks a comprehensive public record of misconduct across the organisation. Umasankar cited jurisdiction, sovereignty, immunity, and countries’ willingness or ability to prosecute as obstacles, noting that the UN cannot conduct criminal prosecutions itself.

A double bottom is a bullish reversal chart pattern consisting of two swing lows near the same support level, separated by a swing high. The swing high forms resistance called the neckline, and the pattern is complete when price closes above it, ideally with increased volume.

The pattern typically appears during a downtrend or prolonged pullback and may signal the end of a decline. Aggressive traders may enter near the second low after reversal signals, while conservative traders wait for a confirmed neckline breakout. Profit targets can be estimated by projecting the pattern’s height above the neckline. Stop losses may be placed near the pattern’s midpoint or below the pattern.

Double bottoms are difficult and time-consuming to quantify and code. Thomas Bulkowski’s manually identified study of 500 stocks over five years found that 68% of formations reached their targets. However, the findings may be affected by survivorship bias, the late-1990s bull market, the short study period, and human interpretation. The passage favors fully quantified rules and backtesting over reliance on these statistics.

Richard Mosse’s three-year project *Heat Maps* documents refugee camps across Europe, North Africa and the Middle East amid an increasingly politicized displacement crisis affecting 65.3 million people. Using a military-grade thermal surveillance camera, Mosse renders people as anonymous, grey biological traces, reflecting how Western governments represent refugees and implicating viewers in dehumanizing policies.

The large panoramas combine nearly a thousand frames and occupy a space between surveillance, art and ambiguity rather than presenting exact reality. Mosse deliberately repurposes technology designed for surveillance and weapons targeting to challenge perceptions of refugees. The project applies a distancing effect that makes familiar subjects strange and demands renewed engagement.

Access restrictions, border controls and technically complex equipment repeatedly hindered production, including at Berlin’s Tempelhof Airport, the Calais Jungle and in Mali. Although the camera concealed identities, Mosse acknowledged that long-range observation still involved a degree of privacy violation. He witnessed horrific conditions but maintained that art, while not necessarily politically committed, can remain culturally resonant and iconic.

A host-terminated UDMA read can leave corrupted state, causing subsequent UDMA writes to continue an old CRC after device termination and generate errors. UDMA writes are therefore generally unusable. The resolution is to use the UDMA I/O blocking feature controlled by bit 8 of the ATAC Error MSR.

Mark Palmer forwarded Enron colleagues a California class-action complaint against major electricity generators and traders, noting a reporter expected a forthcoming suit against Enron to resemble it. Plaintiff Pamela Gordon alleged the defendants manipulated California’s wholesale electricity market beginning in May 2000 by exploiting confidential real-time data, withholding capacity, exporting and reselling power, coordinating outages, and creating transmission congestion. The complaint claimed these practices inflated prices, tripled some SDG&E customer bills, produced billions in profits, and caused approximately $4 billion in overcharges. Representing roughly 1.2 million SDG&E customers and other purchasers, Gordon asserted antitrust, unfair competition, consumer-protection, and unconscionability claims. She sought class certification, damages including treble damages, restitution, disgorgement, interest, legal costs, and injunctions against continued market manipulation and unreasonable rates.

The court fined Pomeroy $1,000 for each of six offenses and the New York Central and Hudson River Railroad Company $18,000 for each of six crimes, totaling $6,000 and $108,000 respectively. The passage criticizes overturning judgments for technical errors unrelated to substantial justice and proposes allowing reversals or new trials only when an error caused a miscarriage of justice. It opposes abolishing injunctions in labor disputes, arguing they remain necessary against violence and intimidation but should not prevent peaceful, lawful efforts by workers or improperly benefit corporations. Because preliminary injunctions can effectively decide labor disputes and cause irreparable harm, judges should exercise this power carefully. Both failure to use injunctions when necessary and their oppressive use deserve condemnation. Judges should resist public pressure and special interests when justice requires, but their exceptional and largely unreviewable authority should remain open to public scrutiny and criticism.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed dismissal of antitrust and related California-law claims brought by Innofood and Sea Breeze against Mitsubishi entities and Mexico’s majority-owned salt producer, ESSA. Plaintiffs alleged that ESSA breached distribution agreements and resumed selling Mexico’s sea salt exclusively through Mitsubishi.

The court held that the act of state doctrine barred the suit. ESSA’s conduct constituted an official sovereign act because Mexico owns and controls ESSA, Mexico’s Constitution places sea salt under state ownership, and decisions governing the large-scale exploitation and distribution of national natural resources are inherently sovereign. The relevant decisions and contractual breach occurred in Mexico.

All five claims challenged ESSA’s exclusive distribution arrangement and would require a United States court to judge the validity of Mexico’s policy for disposing of its salt resources. The requested injunction would effectively direct Mexico to alter how it allocates and profits from those resources.

The additional Sabbatino factors also favored applying the doctrine: the record showed no international consensus prohibiting such resource-distribution arrangements; judicial intervention could interfere with foreign relations; and Mexico’s government continues to exist. The court declined to decide whether a commercial exception to the doctrine exists because ESSA’s actions involved powers peculiar to sovereigns rather than purely commercial conduct.

Sea Breeze’s temporary corporate suspension did not require dismissal because California restored its corporate status during the appeal. The Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act did not remove jurisdiction because its commercial-activity exception applied. The holding was limited to this challenge to Mexico’s policy concerning essentially its entire salt output and did not broadly immunize all foreign state-owned enterprises.

The President accepts office with humility, anxiety, and awareness of his limited civil experience, trusting that patriotic motives will excuse any shortcomings. He invokes divine guidance for the new government and expresses gratitude for the peaceful establishment of American independence and constitutional government. Rather than recommend specific measures, he trusts Congress’s talents, integrity, and patriotism to pursue national interests without prejudice or faction. He emphasizes the connection between virtue, liberty, and public prosperity, and notes Congress’s responsibility to consider constitutional amendments while preserving effective government and protecting individual rights and public harmony. He declines personal compensation beyond necessary official expenses and concludes by praying for wisdom and moderation in governing.

Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) is a frequent complication of advanced liver disease and may worsen after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) placement. This prospective multicenter study used untargeted metabolomics to analyze hepatic and peripheral vein plasma collected before and after TIPS from 22 participants, who were monitored for HE for up to one year.

The largest metabolomic changes occurred in peripheral blood between immediately post-TIPS and discharge, with bile acids contributing substantially. Greater pre- to post-TIPS hepatic-vein metabolome dissimilarity was associated with subsequent HE, suggesting that patients with less preexisting intrahepatic shunting may face higher post-TIPS HE risk. More severe HE was associated with larger decreases in bile acids and glycerophosphocholine. Three conjugated hydroxylated bile acids measured immediately after TIPS were inversely associated with later HE severity. In two participants readmitted for HE, these bile acids were low during HE and increased following treatment.

Chemical proportionality analysis identified post-TIPS fluctuations in glycerophosphocholine and bilirubin-related metabolites, including changes consistent with altered biliverdin oxidation-reduction. Bile acid ratios changed comparatively little, suggesting TIPS primarily affected their overall abundance rather than relative composition.

The findings indicate that intrahepatic shunting and changes in bile acids, glycerophosphocholines, and bilirubin-related compounds may help predict or explain post-TIPS HE. Limitations include the small cohort, incomplete metabolite coverage and annotation, limited readmission samples, and lack of paired microbiome analysis. Larger studies are needed to validate these metabolites as biomarkers or therapeutic targets and to develop noninvasive measures of intrahepatic shunting.

James T. Hodgkinson, 66, wounded House Majority Whip Steve Scalise and several others during a Republican congressional baseball practice in Alexandria, Virginia, before police fatally shot him. Armed with a rifle and handgun, Hodgkinson had apparently lived in a van in northern Virginia since March after leaving Illinois.

He was frequently seen alone at a nearby YMCA and restaurant. Acquaintances described him as quiet and generally calm. Authorities were investigating his activities, motive, and weapons. Hodgkinson had posted grievances about President Donald Trump and Republicans, supported Bernie Sanders, and frequently wrote newspaper letters concerning income inequality.

Victims included Scalise, congressional aide Zack Barth, two Capitol Police officers, and a former congressional aide. Barth was expected to recover fully, while the officers suffered relatively minor injuries.

Hodgkinson had previously run a home-inspection business and had a history of arrests. A 2006 battery case involving a shotgun was dismissed. In March, police questioned him after he fired about 50 rifle rounds into a cornfield near homes, but filed no charges because his firearms documentation was valid.

High-quality large-area hBN is difficult to assess because antiparallel domains on high-symmetry growth substrates form grain boundaries, while conventional microscopy has limited sampling areas and Raman spectroscopy cannot resolve orientational polarity. The study demonstrates interferometric second-harmonic generation (SHG) polarimetry as a non-destructive, scalable method for imaging hBN domains and evaluating crystalline quality.

SHG is coherent and sensitive to crystal orientation: fields from antiparallel domains are out of phase and interfere destructively. Ten types of continuous monolayer or few-layer CVD-grown hBN were compared with mechanically exfoliated references using SHG, Raman spectroscopy, optical microscopy, and atomic force microscopy. CVD samples showed SHG intensities ranging from about 0.1% to 100% of the monolayer reference, spanning three orders of magnitude, whereas Raman intensity varied only fourfold. Raman linewidths were generally two to three times those of references.

Dual-polarization SHG imaging mapped domain orientations and revealed sample-dependent structures, including randomly oriented crystallites, apparently unidirectional domains separated by weak-SHG boundaries, and domains associated with varying thickness or stacking. Orientational spread correlated positively with Raman linewidth and ranged from about 0.1° in exfoliated hBN to approximately 5° in commercial CVD material. SHG intensity and orientational spread were more sensitive to disorder than Raman metrics.

Numerical mixed-domain simulations showed that ordinary orientational disorder could not explain the large SHG suppression. Introducing antiparallel UP and DOWN domains reproduced the observed reductions through destructive interference, with nearly balanced populations producing losses of several orders of magnitude. Interferometric SHG measurements directly detected π phase shifts between antiparallel regions, including domains smaller than the roughly 1 μm² probing area. Boundary regions could retain substantial Raman intensity while exhibiting strongly reduced SHG, indicating nanoscale antiparallel domains.

The combined metrics—Raman intensity and linewidth, SHG intensity, orientational spread, and interferometric phase—provide a quantitative framework for assessing hBN crystallinity. Antiparallel domains and boundaries were pervasive across multiple CVD growth methods, including films appearing unidirectionally aligned. The approach enables wide-area, high-throughput structural characterization and is applicable to other non-centrosymmetric two-dimensional materials, including transition metal dichalcogenides.

The passage presents container and distributed-system design patterns. Adapter containers can expose incompatible applications through standard interfaces without modifying their images. Examples include exporting Redis metrics to Prometheus, normalizing Redis and Storm logs with Fluentd, redirecting file logs to stdout, and providing rich database health checks for MySQL. This modular approach improves reuse, maintenance, sharing, and independent updates.

Microservices divide applications into independently maintained components communicating through defined APIs. They improve team autonomy, release agility, reliability, and independent scaling, but make architecture and debugging more complex. Distributed patterns provide reusable approaches to these challenges.

Replicated load-balanced services use interchangeable replicas for availability and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes prevent traffic from reaching instances before initialization. Session tracking routes a user consistently to one replica, preferably through cookies or headers for external clients. Application-layer proxies can add caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination. Caches are often best deployed as a separate replicated tier rather than as sidecars, while nginx can terminate SSL before forwarding traffic through Varnish to application servers.

Sharded services assign subsets of requests or state to different replicas and are commonly used when data exceeds one machine’s capacity. Sharded caches improve memory utilization but make individual shard failures more consequential. Replicating each shard improves availability and permits independent scaling of hot shards. Effective sharding requires deterministic, uniform functions and carefully selected keys. Consistent hashing limits remapping when shard counts change. Routing may use per-pod ambassadors or shared routing services, with trade-offs in complexity, latency, and scaling.

Scatter/gather distributes parts of a computation to multiple leaves and combines their partial results at a root, reducing processing time. It can also search sharded datasets larger than one machine can hold. Excessive parallelism introduces request overhead and amplifies slow-node, failure, and tail-latency problems because completion depends on all required leaves. Replicating each shard improves reliability, scaling, and upgrade safety.

Function-as-a-service simplifies deployment and automatic scaling of event-driven, stateless code. Its limitations include difficult debugging, forced network communication, external state storage, bounded runtimes, poor suitability for long-running processing or memory-heavy services, and unfavorable costs under sustained load. Suitable patterns include request or response decorators, asynchronous event handlers such as two-factor authentication, and event pipelines such as user signup or build workflows. FaaS enables small, independent handlers while requiring careful monitoring and architecture.

Perplexity AI has made its Comet browser free worldwide after initially offering it to Perplexity Max subscribers for $200 per month. Comet can search the web, organize tabs, draft emails and assist with shopping. The move comes amid competition from Google, OpenAI and Anthropic. Perplexity also offers Comet Plus, featuring content from publishing partners including CNN, Condé Nast and The Washington Post, and plans a mobile version and multitasking Background Assistant.

Awards may include cash, stock, or performance stock, with stock awards issued under designated Microsoft stock plans.

Exelon is expanding a Delmarva Power pilot job-placement partnership with The Precisionists to Atlantic City Electric and Pepco, aiming to provide steady work for dozens of autistic adults. Twelve participants currently contribute skills such as strong attention to detail. Worker Kaylin Morris said the program ended a three-year job search and emphasizes employees’ abilities over social barriers associated with autism.

John LeClair said the team was flat, made poor decisions, failed to skate and pursue loose pucks, allowing the opponent to play effectively. Although low puck movement was adequate, opportunities were limited. He expects simple corrections rather than major changes and stressed avoiding a 0-2 deficit without panicking.

Nigeria’s internet users rose from 28 million in 2012 to 103 million in May 2018, highlighting the internet’s growing importance for good governance. At the 2018 Nigeria Internet Governance Forum, NCC Executive Vice Chairman Umar Danbatta said three additional infrastructure companies awaited approval, bringing the total to seven to expand broadband penetration under the National Broadband Plan. Speakers also emphasized ICT’s expected role in the 2019 elections and the need for secure cyberspace. NCC data showed MTN, Airtel and Globacom gained subscribers in December 2017, while 9mobile lost users. Despite cost, scalability, power and education barriers, internet growth was described as positive.

The speaker emphasized maintaining focus amid increased media and time demands during the finals. He praised Scott Stevens’ dedication, physical play and endurance, while noting that roster protections make sustained success difficult. Home ice offers matchup advantages, but Dallas has shown it can win anywhere and poses a major power-play threat through Hull, Modano and Zubov.

The team remains businesslike and focused on winning the Cup, approaching the series one game and shift at a time. Challenging confident opponents early and scoring first can provide momentum. Recent scoring from hardworking players, strong chemistry among Sykora, Elias and Arnott, favorable bounces, solid skating and timely saves from Marty contributed to a win, but the speaker expected Dallas to respond strongly. He sought favorable defensive matchups against Modano while expressing confidence in multiple pairings and lines.

The AMD Geode CS5535 Revision A3 specification update identifies multiple hardware errata and workarounds:

- UART accesses during block or demand legacy DMA may be discarded or return all ones. Wait for DMA completion or use single-transfer mode.
- LPC-to-memory software DMA does not write data but has no operational impact; avoid this diagnostic combination.
- PCI I/O addresses at or above 10000h can hang the system. ATAC and Diverse Device LBARs must also remain below 10000h.
- The USB interface requires external over-voltage protection.
- PIC edge interrupts may be missed when automatic Local-bus clock gating occurs while an interrupt remains high, potentially hanging the system. Disable automatic clock gating.
- ATAC and audio PRD prefetching can fetch part of the next unaligned PRD. Define ATA PRDs before starting UDMA and keep live audio PRD changes at least two entries ahead.
- A host-terminated UDMA read can leave corrupted state that causes CRC errors in a subsequent UDMA write. Enable ATAC UDMA I/O blocking.
- ATAC SSMI during DMA generates status but does not block IDE I/O; do not use the feature.
- GLIU statistics-counter ASMIs may be lost when domain-zero clock gating is enabled; keep that clock active.
- Byte accesses to ACPI PM1_STS and PM1_EN can hang. Use WORD or DWORD accesses, or BIOS emulation.
- BYTE and WORD writes to PMC registers can corrupt current or future register contents. Use SMI traps to control access sizes.
- KEL cannot distinguish ports 060h and 064h through CmdData; use processor trap information. Snoop mode also changes HCE state, requiring software save and restore.
- Simulated back-to-back PCI memory reads can misaddress the second read, but no real-world impact is expected.
- Standard 8259 PIC polling mode is unsupported.
- UART CEIR mode fails with automatic clock gating; disable gating for UART domains.
- IRDY# and DEVSEL# have a guaranteed 1.5 ns tVAL rather than 2 ns, though failures are not expected. Small capacitors may correct edge timing if needed.
- Simultaneous IRQ and SSMI events can allow trapped I/O to complete before SSMI handling. Use the Geode GX processor for SSMIs.
- IDE UDMA fails if bus mastering is enabled before the PIO command packet. Drivers must issue the PIO command first.
- Most GPIO wake inputs do not work from ACPI S3; use PWRBTN# and external logic when multiple wake sources are needed.
- Certain consecutive extended-write and legacy-read RTC CMOS operations return incorrect data; no resolution is provided.
- LPC I/O is unreliable during block or demand DMA; use single-transfer mode.
- USB controller clock gating can cause register-read failures; disable it.
- An unexpected IDE interrupt during bus-master operation resets the engine; this was observed with one CD-ROM firmware revision.
- KEL AuxOutputFull may clear on port 60h reads; use interrupts for USB keyboard and mouse PS/2 emulation.
- ATAC PRDs must be DWORD-aligned to avoid hangs.
- LPC transactions may abort with delayed SYNC patterns; a programmable logic device workaround is available.
- SMB NEGACK behavior is inconsistent; clear it with two specified SMB_STS writes.
- GLPCI retry counting includes unrelated bus retries; increase or disable the retry limit.
- After suspend, atomic writes to GPIO high-bank feature registers clear unselected bits; use read-modify-write.
- LOWBAT_FLAG may not record low-battery entry into abnormal standby; no resolution is provided.
- Sleep-control delays must be shorter than PM_SED to ensure wake signals and PCI/IDE inputs are restored.

Lothar Matthaeus said Neymar should reduce his theatrics to improve his FIFA player of the year prospects, while Ronaldo dismissed the criticism. Wimbledon player Kyle Edmund joked about tensions with his Swedish coach before England’s World Cup quarterfinal against Sweden. Real Madrid denied reports of agreements to sign Kylian Mbappe or Neymar from Paris Saint-Germain. Russian police briefly detained activists protesting political repression and seeking Ukrainian filmmaker Oleg Sentsov’s release. James Rone lost fingers while descending from a back hoe at an Indiana sewer project and sued Boncar Construction. The appellate court held that Rone waived review of the dismissed Illinois Structural Work Act claim by abandoning his earlier appeal. It also ruled that disputed inferences concerning communication signals, proximate cause, and contributory negligence were properly submitted to the jury. The refusal of Rone’s proposed agency and shared-fault instructions was not error because other instructions adequately covered those issues. The judgment for Boncar was affirmed.

Weak US employment data and political uncertainty increased expectations of dovish Federal Reserve policy. USD/JPY fell sharply, with support near 147.13 and downside risk toward 144.00–144.40. The President informs Congress that Texas intends to extend jurisdiction, potentially by force, over territory east of the Rio Grande claimed as part of New Mexico. He states that Texas has no lawful authority beyond its boundaries and that federal law authorizes and obliges the President to use militia or military forces if necessary to prevent powerful combinations from obstructing federal laws or treaty protections.

Under the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, inhabitants of Mexican-held New Mexico at the treaty’s signing are guaranteed liberty, property, and religious rights. Until competent authority establishes a definitive boundary, the Executive must regard and protect as New Mexico all territory then occupied as such. The Executive cannot determine the disputed boundary or establish a territorial government; those powers belong to Congress.

To prevent conflict and enable government in New Mexico, the President urges Congress to settle the Texas–New Mexico boundary immediately, preferably with Texas’s consent. He suggests Congress may offer Texas fair compensation for surrendering its claim and argues that prompt, amicable settlement would promote domestic tranquility, harmony, and attachment to the Union.

Stockholm recorded 10.3C on New Year’s Eve 2016, its warmest in at least 157 years. Eskilstuna and Adelsö reached a Swedish record of 10.4C, surpassing the 1972 mark. SMHI forecast below-freezing temperatures nationwide by Monday.

Balyasny Asset Management acquired 401,837 Avis Budget Group shares worth about $10.96 million in the second quarter, representing roughly 0.49% ownership. Parallax Volatility Advisers, Voya Investment Management, Bain Capital, Ontario Teachers Pension Plan Board and Dimensional Fund Advisors also increased or initiated positions.
