The stock had a consensus “Buy” rating and average $35.89 price target.

Insiders sold 185,708 shares worth about $6.88 million during the quarter. Avis Budget Group provides vehicle rental and car-sharing services through brands including Avis, Budget, Zipcar, Payless, Apex, Maggiore and France Cars.

The AEGEAN study found high apixaban compliance, adherence, and persistence among subjects initiating therapy for atrial fibrillation, with no significant benefit from an additional proactive educational program. At 24 weeks, mean adherence was 91.64% with primary standard of care (SOC) and 91.88% with the educational program; persistence was 91.7% and 91.3%, respectively. At 48 weeks, adherence and persistence remained comparable across primary SOC, secondary SOC, and continued educational-program groups, although adherence declined significantly during later treatment periods.

Drug exposure, interruptions, dosing, and dose modifications were similar between groups. Mean compliance exceeded 95% through Week 24 and 94% at Week 48. Fully adherent subjects decreased from approximately 27% at Week 24 to approximately 15% at Week 48, without significant group differences. Most subgroup analyses showed no significant interaction, though interactions were observed from Weeks 24–48 by atrial fibrillation type and sex.

Safety outcomes were generally similar between groups. Before Week 24, adverse events affected 51.2% of primary SOC subjects and 52.0% of educational-program subjects; bleeding occurred in 6.5% and 9.0%, respectively. Between Weeks 24 and 48, adverse events occurred in 33.8%–40.8% and bleeding in 3.2%–4.1% across groups. Major bleeding was uncommon. Twenty-four deaths were reported, including three fatal bleeding events, and no pregnancies or concerning hepatic or renal laboratory signals were identified.
The figures show multiple views of a gaming machine design; dashed lines indicate portions excluded from the claimed design.

Augustine Heard reported unrest surrounding the Tong Hâk, a religious sect whose founder was executed in 1864. About forty members petitioned the King to rehabilitate their founder and permit their religion, possibly also seeking the expulsion of foreigners. The King rejected them and threatened punishment. Anti-foreign placards later ordered American missionaries and Japanese residents to leave, while a violent Tong Hâk manifesto called for foreigners’ extermination.

Chinese official Yuan promised to protect foreigners and maintain order, with two Chinese warships expected at Chemulpo. Korean authorities increased patrols, reportedly made arrests, and received petitions demanding punishment of the sect. The Japanese consul warned citizens to prepare women and children for evacuation, though his information came only from rumors, and some Japanese families moved to Chemulpo. Despite agitation, no serious incident occurred and most foreigners remained relatively unconcerned. A British cruiser briefly visited Chemulpo, with its captain promising to return within forty-eight hours if summoned by telegraph.

Retired Toronto civil litigator Marcel Strigberger humorously recounts decluttering law books purchased more than 50 years ago. He revisits memorable contract, property, damages and maritime cases before recycling most volumes, later regretting that one property book could be worth over C$1,000. He kept one five-inch-thick book because it serves as a useful stand at his desk.

The Amoeba defense, developed by UNLV coach Jerry Tarkanian, is an aggressive trapping match-up zone run from a 1-1-3 alignment. It pressures the ball while four defenders zone, requiring quick guards and aiming to create steals and transition baskets. The point guard initially pressures near midcourt, while teammates protect the high post, wings, and basket. On wing or corner entries, defenders rotate to pressure the ball, front the post, deny return and lob passes, and form helpside “I” alignments. Optional traps occur when a pass enters the corner or a wing begins dribbling, with remaining defenders forming a Triangle “I.” Players also rotate on passes out of traps, skip passes, reversals, and guard-wing interchanges. Against a two-guard front, X1 and X2 match up; a high-post entry triggers a triple team while wing passing lanes are denied.

Opening range breakout (ORB) strategies enter trades when prices move above or below a range established shortly after the market opens. They aim to exploit volatility caused by overnight news and market activity near the open and close.

Backtests on S&P 500 futures found that basic ORB strategies produced very small average gains, low win rates, and worse results for downside breakouts. Tests on Nasdaq, gold, silver, and oil futures were similarly negative. Reasons include false breakouts, overnight sessions capturing much of the gains, rapid competition from computerized trading, and daily highs or lows often occurring before breakout entries.

Adding logical filters based on daily or weekly data may improve results. One undisclosed strategy combining one-minute bars with a daily filter produced 198 trades, a 0.27% average gain, a 65% win rate, and a profit factor of 2. Strategy optimization may help identify opportunities, including in individual stocks, but traders should avoid curve fitting and ensure robustness. Overall, ORB strategies are less effective than they once were, particularly for heavily traded futures and ETFs.

The speaker says he has recovered, feels fresh, and will play tomorrow after finding it difficult to miss playoff games. He credits last year’s championship experience and the team’s depth, noting that players such as Helm, Filppula, Samuelsson, Cleary, and Franzen have stepped up when others were unavailable. He expects an interesting series against an experienced opponent with similar depth and strong top players. Although he still feels nervous before playoff games, he says experience helps him stay focused and composed. The opportunity to win the Stanley Cup, especially for teammates who have not won before, provides motivation. He does not expect fatigue to be significant but emphasizes short shifts and using the full bench. He also praises Johnny for playing with maturity, poise, and increasing confidence in his first playoffs before undergoing surgery.

ADP reported 32,000 private nonfarm jobs lost in September, the largest decline since June 2020. The six-month average fell to 23,000. Education and Health Services gained 33,000 jobs, while Leisure and Hospitality lost 19,000.

Utah anti-police brutality groups condemned a prosecutor’s ruling that Officer Clinton Fox was legally justified in fatally shooting Patrick Harmon, a 50-year-old Black man, in Salt Lake City on Aug. 13. Harmon fled while officers attempted to arrest him on outstanding warrants after a bicycle stop. Body-camera footage shows Fox shooting Harmon at close range, though it does not clearly capture a knife or alleged threats.

District Attorney Sim Gill said slowed footage showed Harmon pivoting toward officers, while two officers reported hearing threats to stab or cut them. A knife was found near Harmon’s body. Gill concluded that the close distance, footage and knife made Fox’s fear of serious injury or death reasonable.

Black Lives Matter organizer Lex Scott called the shooting murder and demanded Gill’s resignation. About 50 protesters, including Harmon’s relatives, had demanded release of the footage. Salt Lake NAACP president Jeanetta Williams said the group would seek more information before deciding how to respond.

Momentum investing buys stocks with the strongest recent performance and periodically rebalances, based on the hypothesis that 3–12 months of historical strength may persist for another 3–12 months. Research cited in the passage found that a small minority of stocks generated overall market gains, supporting a defensive focus on strong stocks while avoiding weak ones.

A monthly S&P 500 momentum backtest using a moving-average crossover and cash-index data from 1960 to February 2023 grew $100,000 to $5.575 million. It returned 6.6% annually versus 7% for buy-and-hold, while being invested 69% of the time and limiting maximum drawdown to 26% versus 55%. The claimed risk-adjusted return was 9.5%. Average losses were below 5%, while average winners approached 25%. Simple moving averages outperformed exponential ones in testing.

Globe and Mail social media editor Kiran Rana describes social media’s dual impact: it rapidly spreads news and supports movements such as #MeToo, but also fosters misinformation, echo chambers and personal attacks. She worries Facebook’s algorithm may deepen polarization and cites an investigation into the sale of fake followers as evidence that online influence and personas can be deceptive.

The newsletter also profiles Brock University professor Veena Dwivedi, an Indo-Canadian scientist who overcame racism, sexism and repeated underestimation of her abilities. She now runs a brain-and-language laboratory, mentors women in STEM and advises others to remain visible, find supportive people and persevere.

LifeShare Community Blood Services is urging northeast Ohio residents to donate blood after winter weather, low temperatures and flu reduced donations. The region needs 40,000 units annually; Type O is currently most critical, though all types are accepted. Eligible donors may be as young as 16 with parental consent, weigh at least 110 pounds and be healthy. Mobile drives are scheduled Feb. 3 in Avon Lake and Feb. 4 in Amherst, Elyria and Grafton. Permanent locations operate in Elyria and Lorain.

Using Veterans Health Administration electronic health records, researchers compared 198,938 Veterans with PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection with 992,036 matched uninfected Veterans through one year of follow-up. Outcomes were documented suicide attempts and self-directed violence, analyzed using an emulated trial design.

Within one year, 3,078 cohort members had a suicide attempt and 2,887 experienced self-directed violence. Compared with uninfected Veterans, infected Veterans had higher one-year risks of suicide attempts (hazard ratio 1.41) and self-directed violence (1.38). Risks were greatest during the first 30 days after infection, with hazard ratios of 2.54 and 1.94, respectively, but remained elevated through one year. Relative risks were higher among Veterans without prior documented suicide attempts or self-directed violence, while analyses of those with prior events were limited by small samples. Sensitivity analyses produced similar findings.

Reported suicide deaths did not differ significantly between groups, though causes of death were unverified. Limitations included possible ascertainment bias, undetected infections among comparators, and unobserved confounding. The findings support early and continued monitoring and suicide-prevention efforts following SARS-CoV-2 infection.

Overbought markets have risen significantly over a defined period, often measured with indicators such as RSI. Backtesting indicates that overbought conditions are associated with below-average or negative returns over the following few days, but returns tend to revert toward long-term averages over time. Thus, overbought conditions are considered short-term bearish signals rather than predictors of long-term weakness. Mean reversion describes the tendency of strong deviations from a trend to reverse toward the historical average. Media coverage may intensify market sentiment by encouraging FOMO during rallies or panic during declines. Although overbought conditions may suggest a correction, the results do not necessarily provide a tradeable short-selling strategy.

Pakistan and Afghanistan held their first Joint Working Group meeting in Kabul, attended by a senior Pakistani delegation led by Foreign Secretary Tehmina Janjua. Pakistan proposed five groups covering security, intelligence, military cooperation, trade, refugees and connectivity. Officials supported an Afghan-led peace process, bilateral dispute resolution and improved US relations based on mutual respect, while rejecting violence and terrorism in Afghanistan.

European officials are negotiating a major pharmaceutical policy overhaul addressing medicine access, industry investment, shortages, antimicrobial resistance, compounding, environmental impacts, and hospital-made drugs. Meanwhile, U.S. telehealth has evolved into a major marketing channel for prescription and compounded medications, including treatments for weight loss, sexual health, acne, and birth control. A Colorado panel also made a first-in-the-nation decision to limit health-plan payments for a costly Amgen arthritis drug.

William C. Smith, 42, pleaded not guilty to murdering Willard Higgins Jr., 40, following a Friday altercation in Troy. Bond was set at $500,000. Higgins later died at Kettering Hospital after breathing difficulties, a heart attack and brain bleed. An autopsy is underway.

A 2015 survey found 70 per cent of Fiji’s kawakawa and donu breeding sites had declined or disappeared, while catches also fell 70 per cent. The 4FJ Campaign urges people not to eat, buy or sell the fish during their June–September breeding season, receiving strong public and cross-sector support.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K announcing that its financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2020 were posted on its website on July 22, 2020. The Second Quarter 2020 Update was furnished as Exhibit 99.1. Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn signed the report.

Israel and Myanmar signed an education cooperation agreement to teach the Holocaust, anti-Semitism, racism, intolerance and xenophobia, jointly review textbooks concerning each other’s history, establish reciprocal studies programs and expand academic cooperation. The agreement drew criticism amid Israel’s killing of Palestinian protesters and allegations of Myanmar’s ethnic cleansing of Rohingya Muslims. The passage also cites Israel’s continued arms sales to Myanmar, Myanmar’s support for the US embassy opening in Jerusalem, Israeli policies accused of discriminating against non-Jews, and the revocation of Aung San Suu Kyi’s US Holocaust Memorial Museum award. Online critics expressed skepticism that the textbook review could enable historical revisionism.

VentureWire’s November 15, 2000 issue reports extensive private-company financing, deals, personnel changes, and venture capital activity. Advanced Technology Ventures is raising an $800 million fund, Qualcomm committed $500 million to Qualcomm Ventures, and IP Communications secured $312 million in equity and debt. Numerous technology firms announced funding, including Video Networks at $66 million, Cinta at $36 million, RichFX and Autodaq at $33 million each, and Requisite Technology at $30 million. Foodbuy.com ended California operations and cut 22% of its workforce; Drinks.com laid off about 40 employees and may close, while WebTaggers shut down for lack of funding. Other developments include ING’s partnership and investment in PayPal, several acquisitions and mergers, executive appointments, new venture funds and offices, and corrections to prior reports concerning Avolo, Malibu Networks, and Telespree.

The court reversed the order requiring Jane Kursa to provide a further bill of particulars. Although condemning her delays, it held that defendants failed to seek relief within CPLR 3042(d)’s 10-day period or allege special circumstances excusing their delay. The motion was denied without costs.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. Switching frequency ranges from 100 kHz to 2 MHz. Internal oscillator mode uses an RT resistor and outputs a synchronized clock at twice the switching frequency; external synchronization requires RT floating and a 200-kHz to 4-MHz clock. Two controllers can operate in synchronized primary-secondary or interleaved configurations, with a 90° or 270° output phase shift.

Depending on the device, controllers provide one or two primary and synchronous-rectifier outputs, each with roughly 150-mA peak capability, so external gate drivers are recommended. Dead time and leading-edge blanking are fixed or resistor-programmable by device. Pulse skipping addresses minimum on-time constraints and preserves transformer volt-second balance with dual outputs. Maximum duty-cycle options include 50%, 75%, or 100%, depending on device and DCL configuration.

Current sensing controls PWM and overcurrent protection. At 1.05 V on CS_ILIM, cycle-by-cycle limiting begins; continued overcurrent charges the HICC capacitor, stops switching, and later initiates soft-start restart. The FAULT input supports external protection, while thermal shutdown stops switching above 175°C and restarts below 160°C. Programmable slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation, and Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation is supported.

A synchronous push-pull design example uses the TPS7H5001-SP at 500 kHz with GaN devices, including selected values for oscillator timing, feedback, dead time, blanking, transformer, switches, filtering, current sensing, hiccup timing, compensation, and slope compensation. The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require proper bypassing. Layout guidance emphasizes short high-current paths, minimized switch-node area, separated analog and power grounds, careful routing of sensitive signals, close placement of bypass and compensation components, and noise filtering at CS_ILIM.

Blue Bird posted record Q3 sales and strong margins, supported by bus volumes, pricing, resilient demand, and a 3,900-unit backlog. Despite tariff uncertainty and short-term EV risks, facility investments, product innovation, and federal EV funding support long-term growth. The author maintains a Buy rating based on valuation, demand, and margin expansion, while disclosing a possible BLBD position within 72 hours.

Russia acknowledged that seizure of the bark Cape Horn Pigeon was unjustifiable and that indemnity was due, but rejected compensation for loss of the vessel’s, equipment’s, and crew’s services during detention. The claimants later submitted all expenses in a detailed damages bill. In 1899, the United States offered to settle for $42,000 without prejudicing the claimants’ rights if refused. Russia rejected the compromise and renewed its $2,500 offer.

The claimants argued that the Okhotsk Sea’s size prevented exclusive occupation and that Russia had never publicly prohibited navigation, fishing, or whaling beyond ordinary jurisdictional waters. They cited treaties with the United States and Great Britain, longstanding foreign whaling activity, and affidavits. The arresting commander allegedly claimed the sea was closed and ordered seizures of whaling vessels. The passage contends such a claim conflicted with international law and the 1824 treaty guaranteeing navigation, fishing, and access in the Pacific, subject to specified conditions.

Stocks, bonds, and commodities fell sharply Friday, with major indices dropping about 2 percent and the Dow losing over 600 points. Strong wage growth raised fears of inflation and faster interest-rate increases. Analysts largely viewed the overdue correction as a return to normal volatility, not broader economic trouble.

The adapter pattern uses companion containers to extend applications without modifying their images. Fluentd adapters can normalize Redis slow-query and Apache Storm logs, while health-check adapters can run diagnostic database queries and expose HTTP health endpoints. This modular approach improves reuse, sharing, and independent maintenance.

Microservices divide applications into small processes communicating through defined APIs. They support smaller teams, independent releases, reliability, and service-specific scaling, but make architecture and debugging more complex. Distributed design patterns help standardize these systems.

Replicated load-balanced services use interchangeable replicas for availability and horizontal scaling. Stateless services should generally have at least two replicas, and readiness probes should prevent traffic from reaching instances before initialization completes. Session-tracked services route a user consistently to one replica, commonly through application-level identifiers and consistent hashing.

Application-layer proxies can add caching, rate limiting, denial-of-service protection, and SSL termination. Caches are often best deployed as a separate replicated tier rather than as sidecars because fewer, larger caches avoid duplicate data and improve hit rates. Varnish can provide caching and throttling, while nginx can terminate SSL. Kubernetes Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, and Secrets can implement these layered architectures.

Sharded services partition requests or state among specialized replicas and are generally used when data exceeds one machine’s capacity. Sharded caches improve memory utilization but become dependent on individual shards, so failures or upgrades can reduce performance. Replicating each shard improves availability and permits independent scaling of hot shards. Sharding functions should be deterministic and uniform, use carefully selected keys, and often employ consistent hashing to minimize remapping during resizing. Routing can use per-pod ambassadors or shared routing services, with trade-offs in complexity, latency, and scaling.

Scatter/gather distributes each request across multiple workers, then combines partial results. It can reduce processing time and support large, sharded datasets, such as document search. However, request overhead, slow “straggler” workers, and failure probability increase with the number of leaves. Replicating each shard improves availability, scalability, and upgrade safety.

Function-as-a-service executes stateless functions in response to events and automatically handles deployment, scaling, and restarts. It simplifies development but complicates monitoring, dependency analysis, state management, long-running processing, memory-heavy workloads, and sustained high-volume economics. Suitable patterns include request or response decorators, asynchronous event handlers such as two-factor authentication, and event pipelines such as user signup or software delivery workflows.

Distributed ownership requires selecting a process to own a task. A singleton avoids election complexity and can achieve reasonable availability under a container orchestrator, which restarts failed or unhealthy containers and moves workloads after machine failures. Its limitations include downtime during failures and upgrades because old and new versions cannot run simultaneously.

NVIDIA’s Blackwell architecture adds hardware ray-intersection support for Linear Swept Spheres, improving hair rendering speed and reducing geometry memory use. Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 improves thread coherence, neural shading, and path-tracing efficiency. A programmable RISC-V AI Management Processor moves GPU-context scheduling from the CPU to the GPU, reducing latency and coordinating graphics and AI workloads.

Blackwell adds hardware encoding and decoding for 4:2:2 H.264 and HEVC video. Ninth-generation NVENC improves AV1 and HEVC quality, while sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed. RTX 5090 supports three encoders and two decoders. DisplayPort 2.1b provides up to 80 Gbps, supporting 8K at 165 Hz or 4K at 480 Hz with compression.

Max-Q improvements include finer power, clock, memory, and voltage-rail gating; clocks that adapt 1,000 times faster; and sleep entry up to 10 times faster than Ada. These changes can reduce power consumption by up to 50% in the cited small-language-model inference example.

DLSS 4 introduces Multi Frame Generation, generating up to three additional frames per rendered frame. Its model is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than the prior method. Hardware Flip Metering improves frame pacing. Transformer-based models for Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA use twice as many parameters and improve temporal stability, motion detail, lighting, anti-aliasing, and ghosting.

Blackwell introduces developer-created neural shaders through Cooperative Vectors APIs for DirectX 12 and Vulkan. Applications include Neural Materials, Neural Texture Compression, Neural Radiance Cache, RTX Skin, and RTX Neural Faces. These techniques approximate complex material behavior, compress textures, infer indirect lighting, simulate subsurface scattering, and generate more natural-looking faces.

The flagship GB202 GPU contains 92.2 billion transistors, 192 streaming multiprocessors, 24,576 CUDA cores, 192 RT cores, and 768 Tensor cores, and powers the RTX 5090. GB203 contains 45.6 billion transistors and 10,752 CUDA cores for the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti. GB205 contains 31 billion transistors and 6,400 CUDA cores for the RTX 5070. NVIDIA states that specifications may change and disclaims warranties and liability under the listed conditions.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for a diabetes management partner interface that enables an analyte sensor system to communicate flexibly with display devices, insulin delivery devices, other medicament delivery devices, and remote servers. After authorization, partner devices may access or modify configuration parameters based on requirements involving battery capacity, accuracy, communication protocols, regulation, and operating time.

Configurable parameters include wireless connectivity, device permissions, whitelists and timeouts, advertisement structures, connection models, calibration and factory codes, analyte data, bolus calculations, alerts, security, privacy, power management, and server services. The system may select operating modes for partner-only, display-only, or combined configurations; adjust device access; accept selected connection requests; switch between intermittent and continuous connections; and restore previous settings when leaving a partner-specific mode.

Partner authorization and requirements may be obtained or updated through display devices and servers. Display applications may exchange pairing, analyte, dosage, medicament-delivery, status, and alert information with partner applications. Alerts may be configured across primary and secondary notification devices. The system may also combine analyte data with delivery-device information, including reservoir changes, pump rewind, priming, cannula fill, and fluid pressure, to assess device operability. These features address interoperability and synchronized communication among devices from different manufacturers while supporting automated or manual insulin delivery.
The team is excited, rested, healthy except for Dwayne’s injury, and confident that executing its game plan and playing well Saturday will bring the desired result.

This study examined long-term stimulant effects on brain development through a 4-year naturalistic follow-up of a randomized methylphenidate trial involving stimulant-naive males with ADHD. Pharmacological MRI measured resting relative cerebral blood flow (rCBF) and responses to an acute methylphenidate challenge. The final sample included 32 adolescents and 24 adults.

No evidence showed that stimulant use caused age-dependent changes over time in resting rCBF or methylphenidate response, and initial methylphenidate versus placebo allocation had no lasting effects. However, greater stimulant use was associated with lower thalamic resting rCBF in adults and lower medial prefrontal cortex response in adolescents. These associations existed before treatment and were unrelated to ADHD symptom severity. Whole-brain responses corresponded with noradrenaline transporter distribution but not dopamine receptor or transporter distributions.

The findings do not support persistent stimulant-related alterations in dopamine-system development over four years. Limitations included participant attrition, assumed prescription adherence, different MRI scanners, a restricted sample size, and inclusion of males only. Larger longitudinal studies are recommended to assess pharmacological MRI’s potential for optimizing ADHD treatment.

Linguistics researcher Martin O’Leary created charts showing how seemingly unrelated words share ancient Proto-Indo-European (PIE) roots. PIE, thought to have originated north of the Caspian Sea and spoken between roughly 4,500 and 2,500 BC, developed into more than 440 modern languages. Examples of cognates include “architect” and “dachshund,” derived through separate branches from “teks” (“to weave”); “science” and “sh*t,” from “sek”; and “blue,” “phlegm,” and “flamingo,” from “bhel” (“to shine”). Because no PIE texts survive, linguists have struggled to reconstruct the language. O’Leary’s charts attracted thousands of retweets and enthusiastic responses.

The specification standardizes the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) for interoperability between SEV-ES or SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors. These technologies encrypt guest register state; for Non-Automatic Exits, guests selectively expose required state through a 4 KB decrypted GHCB page. Version 2 adds SEV-SNP support, hypervisor feature advertisement, protocol enhancements, and optional capabilities including restricted injection, AP creation, APIC ID retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, trusted I/O, Secure AVIC, page-state changes, and GHCB unregistration.

The GHCB MSR protocol supports version negotiation, encryption-bit discovery, early CPUID requests, feature queries, GHCB GPA registration, page-state changes, VMPL switching, and termination requests. SEV-SNP guests must register a GHCB GPA before first use and may request a preferred address or unregister it. Guests must protect GHCB access against interruption, mark valid fields in a bitmap, and handle hypervisor errors or requested exceptions.

The document defines automatic and non-automatic exit handling, VMGEXIT processing, MMIO, MSR, I/O, hypercalls, SMP booting, interrupts, and page-state transitions between private and shared states. It also defines the SEV-SNP secrets-page reserved area, including 64-bit request sequence numbers, and an EFI configuration table for communicating secrets and CPUID pages.

SNP Guest Request enables firmware requests through shared request and response pages, with error reporting, sequence-number handling, and recommended rate limiting. SNP Extended Guest Request additionally returns GUID-identified certificate data, including VCEK and VLEK certificates, across contiguous shared pages and reports the required page count when supplied storage is insufficient.

The lecture develops coherent, or collective, Thomson scattering, where the scattering-vector wavelength exceeds the Debye length and samples collective plasma motion. Relevant modes include ion acoustic and electron plasma waves, whose frequencies are much lower than the laser frequency. Plasma fluctuations continually supply such modes, and scattering transfers energy and momentum to them. Spectra contain broadened pairs of ion-acoustic and electron-plasma-wave peaks; thermal effects and the detector’s finite angular collection range contribute to broadening.

The derivation first relates scattered power to electron-density fluctuations through the spectral density function \(S(k,\omega)\). Unlike the incoherent treatment, particle positions are retained, allowing phase differences and interference among scattered fields. The resulting power includes scaling factors for laser intensity, geometry, density, and scattering volume, while all spectral shape information resides in \(S(k,\omega)\).

Density fluctuations are then calculated using a test-particle treatment. Each electron or ion perturbs the surrounding plasma through shielding. Thomson scattering remains from electrons: electrons directly contribute and repel other electrons, while ions contribute indirectly through the electrons attracted around them. Electron-ion cross terms vanish because the particles do not generally occupy the same locations. Sums over individual particles are replaced by smooth velocity distribution functions using the Klimontovich distribution.

The general spectral density contains an electron term and a sum over ion species, each weighted by plasma susceptibility and permittivity. The electron distribution is evaluated at the mode phase velocity \(\omega/k\), as are the ion distributions. Peaks occur as the permittivity approaches zero, corresponding to the plasma’s normal modes. The low-frequency “ion feature” still results from electron scattering around moving ions, not direct ion scattering.

To calculate susceptibilities, the lecture linearizes the collisionless Vlasov equation. A collisionless treatment can apply even to a collisional plasma when the scattering wavelength is much shorter than the mean free path. The susceptibility for an arbitrary distribution requires a Landau-contour integral with a pole at \(v=\omega/k\). For Maxwellian distributions, it can be expressed using the Debye length, the coupling parameter, species properties, and a tabulated complex function related to the plasma dispersion and complex error functions. Experimental spectra are typically fitted by varying model plasma temperature and density until the calculated \(S(k,\omega)\) matches the measured spectrum.

Webster Elementary dedicated two recycled-material “buddy benches” and planted a tree in memory of former music teacher Robert Pickell, who died in July after falling through his roof. More than 100 staff, students, friends and relatives attended. Students shared goodbye messages and recalled his care and influence. The benches symbolize Pickell’s commitment to friendship and recycling, while a memorial plaque will eventually be placed on the tree.

A cross-sectional study examined associations between personal health literacy, school health literacy environments, and health outcomes among 7,264 teachers from 11 urban and rural schools in Zhengzhou, China. Participants completed validated measures of personal and organizational health literacy and reported health status, health-compromising behaviours, health service use, and healthcare costs.

Teachers averaged 75.17/100 for personal health literacy and 25.30/32 for school health literacy environment. Overall, 56.9% had problematic or inadequate health literacy, while 31.0% perceived their school environment as supportive of health literacy. Poor health status was reported by 15.0%, at least one health-compromising behaviour by 75.2%, health service use by 82.4%, and annual out-of-pocket healthcare costs of at least RMB 1,000 by 60.7%.

After adjustment, inadequate personal health literacy was associated with higher odds of poor health, health-compromising behaviour, health service use, and higher healthcare costs compared with excellent literacy. A non-supportive school health literacy environment was also associated with higher odds of all four outcomes. Health literacy varied by characteristics including school type, age, marital status, teaching duration and subject, health awareness, chronic conditions, and insurance type.

The convenience sample, self-reported measures, and cross-sectional design limit generalizability and prevent causal conclusions. The findings support interventions combining individual health literacy education with organizational changes in schools, tailored to specific teacher subgroups.

Massachusetts General Hospital’s Pre-Admission Testing Area (PATA) conducted required preoperative assessments for surgical outpatients. Although committed to patient safety and high-quality care, the clinic faced persistent inefficiencies, long waits, staff overtime, inconsistent patient selection, and incomplete work-ups. Patients averaged about 2.5 hours per visit, sometimes exceeding four hours, despite receiving only 80–90 minutes of provider contact.

PATA had 12 exam rooms and served about 55 patients daily with five laboratory technicians, five nurses, and eight anesthesiologists. Patients progressed through check-in, vital signs and an EKG, a nursing assessment, an anesthesiologist’s examination, blood collection, and check-out. Manual scheduling and tracking, variable examination times, lunch-hour staffing reductions, missing records, unclear provider assignments, and uneven patient arrivals created delays. Patients were generally served by arrival order rather than appointment time.

Limited capacity allowed PATA to evaluate only about 65% of surgical outpatients, prioritizing patients considered medically complex. However, unclear criteria and differing surgeon judgments sometimes sent healthy patients to PATA while sicker patients were assessed in the operating room on surgery day. These same-day work-ups contributed to delayed surgeries, staff overtime, possible cancellations, lost revenue, and an estimated 57,000 minutes of annual operating-room productivity loss.

Previous proposals for another clinic or broader perioperative reforms failed because of financial, political, cultural, and space constraints. PATA generated no separate revenue, making additional resources difficult to justify. In 2008, anesthetist-in-chief Dr. Jeanine Wiener-Kronish formed a task force led by executive director Susan Moss. An MBA intern later gathered operational data through interviews, observation, time studies, and workflow mapping, confirming that patients spent more time waiting than receiving care.

After receiving a patient complaint, the task force considered extending clinic hours and spacing appointments farther apart, adding staff and rooms, reducing patient volume, or improving operations with existing resources. Moss requested detailed analysis of these alternatives, including responsibilities, technology use, and existing process assumptions, before deciding on changes.

Edinburgh-based Vert Rotors has developed VERT.500, a scaled-up oil-free compressor offering clean air, energy efficiency and low noise. Created with the Advanced Manufacturing and Automation Centre, it targets hospitals, food businesses and electronics manufacturers, potentially reducing noise-protection costs, electricity bills and CO2 emissions. The firm previously focused on compact compressors, including one for Scotland’s emerging space industry.

The ADS7828 captures the selected analog input on a typical 25pF sampling capacitor; input charge depends on conversion rate. It supports an internal 2.5V or external reference. Lower reference voltages reduce LSB size and increase offset, gain, and noise errors when expressed in LSBs, though Gaussian noise can be reduced by averaging.

The device operates as an I²C slave in standard, fast, and high-speed modes through open-drain SDA and SCL lines. Transfers use START and STOP conditions, byte-wise data, and acknowledgment bits. Addressing uses the factory-set prefix 10010, two pin-selected address bits, and an R/W bit, allowing up to four devices on one bus. Command-byte settings control channel selection, converter operation, and internal-reference power.

Conversion results are 12-bit words transmitted in two bytes. Repeated START conditions support efficient continuous conversions. In high-speed mode, the ADS7828 may hold SCL low until conversion completes; using STOP returns it to standard/fast mode.

The internal reference defaults off and requires adequate settling time after activation for 12-bit accuracy. External references must also be settled. Clean, well-bypassed power, a suitable ground layout, and careful control of reference noise and switching transients are recommended for optimum performance.

TI states that product, material, packaging, and design information may change, provides resources “as is,” limits warranties and liability, and assigns application selection, validation, compliance, and safety responsibilities to developers.

Veteran leadership provides comfort and direction. The team emphasizes communication, speed, trust, and effort while keeping a sacrificing teammate involved through skates, conversations, and his observations.

The S&P 500 fell 3.33% from Thursday’s record high before futures indicated a roughly 0.5% Monday rebound. Investor sentiment improved slightly, but the index’s reversal, rising VIX, seasonal weakness and stretched valuations suggest a deeper correction remains possible. S&P 500 futures faced resistance at 6,330 and support at 6,280. Oil declined after OPEC+ announced a sixth consecutive monthly production increase, while possible U.S. sanctions on Russian crude could offset additional supply. Weak jobs and PMI data and trade-tariff uncertainty raised fuel-demand concerns. Upcoming earnings and macroeconomic risks may favor careful position management and defensive positioning.

Interfacial mobility governs microstructural evolution but is difficult to connect reliably between atomistic simulations and continuum models, especially when solute drag introduces memory effects. Standard molecular dynamics methods—capillary fluctuations and driven steady-state motion—assume Markovian, memory-free dynamics. However, multiple atomic relaxation times can produce persistent sub-diffusion, particularly at low temperatures and in solute-containing interfaces, complicating mobility extraction.

The study adapts generalized memory-based methods to a simplified kinetic Monte Carlo model of interface migration with interacting solute. It demonstrates limitations of the capillary fluctuation method, proposes mobility extraction from mean boundary motion, and applies a time convolutionless propagator to model memory-influenced dynamics. The computationally efficient two-dimensional lattice model permits control of boundary stiffness, solute binding, and diffusion kinetics.
Experienced players must keep the team focused for a difficult road game in Calgary. The team succeeds by battling hard, following its game plan, and avoiding distractions.

The passage argues that female genital mutilation (FGM) may occur in North America, citing charges against a Detroit doctor and an Ontario Human Rights Commission report indicating evidence of the practice in Canada and of girls being sent abroad for it. It describes FGM as a cultural practice and form of child abuse, including infibulation and requests for reinfibulation after childbirth. Medical experts quoted oppose performing nonessential genital mutilation under cultural accommodation. The author concludes that FGM is not a Canadian value and supports screening prospective citizens for acceptance of the practice.

Retail listings suggest Intel may mark the 8086 processor’s 40th anniversary with the Core i7-8086K, featuring six cores, 12 threads, 12MB L3 cache, and a 5GHz maximum clock speed. Its specifications closely resemble the Core i7-8700K but offer 300MHz more speed. The overclockable, potentially speed-binned chip could provide greater performance and overclocking headroom. It is expected to cost around $480, about $100 more than the Core i7-8700K and less than many pre-binned alternatives.

The memorandum predicts that peace will emerge gradually amid continued hostilities and intensifying German propaganda designed to divide Allied nations and their domestic political groups. Germany has maintained military unity in Central Europe while exploiting disagreements among the Allies.

Allied responses include suppressing views receptive to German concessions, a temporarily effective but costly approach that deepens class divisions, encourages violence, and obstructs constructive international policy. An alternative, represented by the President’s reply to the Pope, emphasizes broadly accepted aims, rejects divisive purposes, strengthens Allied unity, and pressures Central Europe toward concessions.

Political tensions prevent European Allies from openly debating peace terms. Territorial discussions would weaken morale, reduce the war to national ambitions, and split the coalition. The primary objective remains defeating the German army or pressuring Germany to reject its ruling groups; specific peace terms are secondary.
Baking soda reacts with acids; baking powder combines soda with dry acid. Powder lasts 3–12 months, while sealed, cool soda lasts indefinitely. Bubbling tests usability.

Researchers tested 105 pet dogs’ reactions when favored toys were inaccessible or competed with food puzzles, and how quickly dogs calmed after toy removal. Thirty-three displayed addictive-like traits, such as persistent focus on unavailable toys and ignoring food. Behavioral biologist Stefanie Riemer suggests the dogs seek the excitement of play rather than the toys themselves. These behaviors were more common among terriers and shepherds, breeds valued for motivation, focus and perseverance. An unpublished survey of roughly 1,600 dogs estimated that about 3 percent showed addictive-like toy behavior. Researchers caution against directly equating these poorly understood behaviors with human addiction while emphasizing play’s value to dog-human relationships.

MIT Sloan’s Women in Management club spent 11 months organizing its sold-out 2013 conference, “Dare to Fail,” for 500 attendees. Despite leadership tensions, speaker cancellations, slow ticket sales, operational problems, and sponsorship challenges, the team confirmed 15 speakers and raised $38,000 to cover costs.

The day before the conference, forecasts predicted a potentially severe Boston snowstorm, though its timing and snowfall remained uncertain. Speakers planned to attend, but attendees and sponsors expressed concerns, MIT had not announced whether it would close, and vendor setup would soon create substantial financial liabilities. Rescheduling was deemed impractical. The leadership team had to choose among canceling before setup, holding a shortened conference with concurrent sessions, or delaying the decision until forecasts and travel information became clearer, while considering safety, finances, reputation, and the conference’s legacy.

The study evaluates national and municipality-level non-pharmaceutical interventions during the Netherlands’ first COVID-19 wave. It develops an agent-based SEIR framework representing about 17 million residents through 170,721 agents across 11 demographic groups and 380 municipalities. Using demographic, mobile-phone mobility, contact-mixing, hospitalization, and seroprevalence data, the model creates hourly contact patterns and reproduces national hospital admissions and the epidemic’s spread from the south through western cities toward the north.

Mobility reductions contributed most to epidemic control; without them, hospital admissions were predicted to approximately double. Behavioral changes also had substantial effects, while the relatively late school closure had little impact. Simulated municipality-level interventions showed a trade-off between health and societal burdens. A 0.33% local infection-prevalence threshold produced 410 additional hospital admissions compared with national restrictions while allowing 167 municipalities to delay interventions, yielding 36 million additional intervention-free person-days; about 6% of municipalities never required interventions. At a 0.1% threshold, admissions increased only slightly, and 18 municipalities remained intervention-free for more than five weeks. Less affected municipalities were mainly rural, isolated areas in the north and east.

The results suggest that locally tailored interventions, supported by timely infection monitoring, could reduce societal burdens with limited additional hospitalizations, even in a densely populated, highly connected country. Limitations include omission of household structure, incomplete movement itineraries, assumed day-to-day mobility variation, nationally averaged mobility changes, and reliance on pre-pandemic mobile-phone data. The framework may be adapted to other countries and policy questions if similarly detailed data are available.

Federal Reserve officials largely supported further interest-rate cuts in September amid growing concern about labor-market weakness. The FOMC voted 11-1 to cut the federal funds target range by 0.25 percentage point to 4%-4.25%. Projections showed a 10-9 split, with a narrow majority favoring quarter-point cuts at both remaining 2025 meetings. Officials differed over how restrictive policy remained, while Governor Stephen Miran preferred a half-point cut and a more aggressive easing path. Participants expected inflation to move toward the 2% target and generally viewed tariff-driven price increases as temporary. The government shutdown could complicate upcoming decisions by halting key data collection and releases on inflation, employment, and consumer spending.

Amazon added Outlook.com calendar support to Alexa, enabling voice-based event review and creation. Apple Calendar remains unofficially supported through a GitHub skill. Amazon Tap also gained hands-free Alexa activation and spatial perception while retaining about eight hours of battery life.

A Boeing-funded study suggests passengers seeking to avoid colds or flu should choose a window seat and remain seated, reducing contact with people moving through the cabin. Researchers observed passenger movement and tested surfaces and air on 10 flights but found none of 18 tested viruses and saw only one coughing passenger, limiting broad conclusions. Modeling estimated that one hypothetical infectious aisle-seat passenger would infect an average of one person among about 150, with the 11 closest passengers at greatest risk. Aisle passengers moved most often, while window passengers moved least. Independent experts called the study novel but cautioned that its small size prevents general conclusions about disease transmission on airplanes.

Comcast received a consensus “Buy” rating from 23 brokerages, with an average 12-month price target of $79.31. Several firms upgraded the stock or raised targets, including Jefferies, Deutsche Bank, Instinet, Macquarie and RBC Capital Markets.

Insiders sold 229,839 shares worth $17.17 million during the latest quarter and own 1.27% of the company. Institutional investors, which own 82.03%, reported several new or increased positions.

Comcast shares opened at $75.71, with a market capitalization of $179.87 billion and a 12-month range of $56.59 to $76.87. A 2-for-1 stock split was scheduled for February 20.

Quarterly earnings were $0.89 per share, exceeding the $0.87 estimate. Revenue rose 9.2% year over year to $21 billion, above expectations of $20.67 billion. Analysts projected full-year earnings of $3.75 per share. Comcast increased its quarterly dividend from $0.14 to $0.1575, equivalent to $0.63 annually and a 0.83% yield.

Comcast’s primary businesses are Comcast Cable and NBCUniversal, whose operations include cable networks, broadcast television, filmed entertainment and theme parks.

The paper introduces LLM-proposed Open Taxonomy (LOT), an inductive method for identifying and interpreting reasoning differences between large reasoning models. LOT uses an LLM to derive natural-language features from paired reasoning traces, annotate other traces as feature vectors, and train a logistic classifier to identify their source models. Misclassified samples prompt iterative expansion of the taxonomy. It supports binary presence-of-reasoning and frequency-based bag-of-reasoning encodings.

Applied to 24,444 traces from 12 open-source models across science, mathematics, and coding datasets, LOT achieved 80–100% classification accuracy when models differed substantially in scale, base family, or specialization. For models of varying parameter sizes, it outperformed few-shot prompting, VML, and a fixed human-defined taxonomy by average margins of 23.8%, 19.6%, and 11.7%, respectively. Frequency-based encodings were particularly useful for distinguishing models using similar strategies at different rates.

LOT found that smaller Qwen3 models more often showed redundant evaluation, circular reasoning, theory switching, and incorrect application of scientific principles, while Qwen3-32B more reliably recalled relevant knowledge, checked method applicability, and maintained coherent stepwise analysis. Models sharing a base family were generally harder to distinguish. Domain specialization also affected reasoning: Seed-Coder-8B sometimes wrote and simulated Python functions for mathematics problems, unlike Qwen3-8B.

On GPQA-Diamond, identified behaviors correlated with answer correctness. A test-time intervention that summarized, modified, and re-expanded reasoning traces improved smaller Qwen3 models’ accuracy by 3.3–5.7%, although Qwen3-1.7B was harmed by summarization. Limitations include uncontrolled differences in model training, possible taxonomy variation across random seeds, incomplete coverage of reasoning differences, reliance on one annotator model, and limited evidence connecting model attributes causally to reasoning patterns.

Researchers analyzed daily growth lines in fossilized embryonic teeth to determine dinosaur egg incubation periods. Protoceratops embryos incubated for nearly three months, while Hypacrosaurus embryos took six months. These periods are longer than previously expected and more similar to primitive reptiles than modern birds, suggesting birds evolved faster incubation after diverging from other dinosaurs. Long incubation exposed dinosaur eggs and parents to extended risks from predators, starvation and environmental disruption. Combined with slow maturation and high resource needs, this may have limited dinosaurs’ ability to reproduce and recover after the end-Cretaceous extinction, while birds’ shorter incubation enabled faster reproduction. The study examined embryos from Mongolia’s Gobi Desert and Alberta’s Devil’s Coulee nesting site.

SOS pressure defense addresses the growing challenge posed by stronger, faster, and more skilled offensive players. Designed to complement any defensive system, it emphasizes fundamentals, clear communication, motivation, pride, desire, and intensity.

Its six key elements are:

1. Defensive skills progress from basic one-on-one positioning and movement to five-on-five team pressure, supported by daily reinforcement.
2. Consistent S-O-S action words guide on-ball defense—SET, ON, SMOTHER—and off-ball defense—SNUGGLE, OFF, STRIKE.
3. Defenders direct opponents toward checkpoints at least 18 feet from the basket, reducing high-percentage shooting opportunities.
4. Aggressive switching on on-ball and off-ball screens is encouraged to reduce confusion and disrupt screening offenses.
5. Transition defense begins with immediate backcourt pressure after a rebound, including denying passing lanes, pressuring dribblers, and directing ballhandlers to low-percentage areas.
6. Every defender receives a specific role, enabling coordinated team pressure that dictates offensive action, creates turnovers, blocks passing lanes, forces difficult shots, and strengthens rebounding.

The system is presented as an equalizer for offensively outmatched teams and an advantage for teams of any skill level.

President Trump issued an executive order on Jan. 20 ending birthright citizenship for virtually anyone born in the United States, prompting nationwide federal court challenges. The administration initially asked the Supreme Court only to restrict universal injunctions, not decide the order’s legality. In a 6-3 ruling, the court rejected universal injunctions while allowing lower courts to consider narrower relief.

Lower courts subsequently blocked the order. Judges Deborah Boardman and Joseph Laplante certified affected classes and found the order likely unconstitutional, while another judge maintained nationwide relief for challenging states. A divided 9th Circuit panel ruled that the order contradicts the Fourteenth Amendment’s plain language.

The administration has now asked the Supreme Court to review the 9th Circuit ruling and Laplante’s decision. It did not seek expedited consideration. If four justices agree to hear the cases, arguments will likely occur in 2026, with a decision expected by late June or early July.

The coach praised players’ playoff commitment, forechecking and willingness to work in gritty areas, particularly Brett Hull, whom he called the team’s unsung hero. Facing elimination, the team’s motivation comes from wanting to continue playing together rather than external factors. Its leaders supply energy, while the coaches reflect on strengths and possible changes.

He acknowledged the team has benefited from favorable playoff circumstances and must capitalize because another championship opportunity is not guaranteed.

Both teams have shown determination and no willingness to quit. The goaltending performances by Eddie and Martin Brodeur were described as exceptional. The coach said the team has learned to win, lose and remain united, while rediscovering its hunger. Langenbrunner’s return and interchangeable energy forwards could help, but the series has become primarily a mental challenge.

The passage describes techniques for routing IPsec traffic through an Internet-based overlay network used as an optimized WAN. Customer-premises routers initially resolve a service hostname through DNS and establish an IKEv2-authenticated outer IPsec tunnel to a selected overlay edge region, called an NEdge. Because corporate DNS resolution may select an edge based on the resolver’s location rather than the router’s location, the selected edge performs a secondary authoritative DNS lookup using the router’s IP address. If another edge is more appropriate, the original edge sends an IKEv2 redirect, causing the router to establish a new tunnel to that edge.

The active edge may subsequently perform periodic DNS lookups to verify that it remains suitable. If it is no longer appropriate, it intentionally drops responses to the router’s liveness probes. This causes the router to treat the tunnel as unavailable and select an alternate route or perform another hostname lookup. The overlay infrastructure can transport traffic over multiple paths, remove duplicate packets, apply network address translation, and use existing routing and loss-mitigation capabilities. The described functions may be implemented as processor-executable software on standard computing systems.

WORD and BYTE writes to PMC registers can cause local or cross-register corruption because shadow registers update operational registers at 32-bit granularity and retain inactive-byte data. ACPI registers permit such accesses; proprietary registers require DWORD access. An SMI I/O trap can control ACPI register accesses.

The lecture examines government policy toward behavioral agents. Traditional rationales for intervention include externalities, inequality, insufficient competition, public goods, innovation, and macroeconomic stabilization. Behavioral policy instead addresses “internalities,” where people fail to account fully for effects on their future selves. Paternalism attempts to influence conduct for people’s own good rather than to address externalities.

Intervention may be warranted for self-control problems, limited attention, memory failures, misinformation, overconfidence, and discrimination, but not necessarily for nonstandard preferences or motivated beliefs. Hard paternalism restricts choices or substantially changes prices through mandates, bans, subsidies, or taxes. Libertarian or soft paternalism influences behavior while preserving choice, while asymmetric paternalism seeks to help people making mistakes without harming those already optimizing.

Arguments against paternalism include limited government knowledge, heterogeneous preferences, distorted choices, inefficiency, corruption, regulatory capture, slippery-slope concerns, and the intrinsic value of freedom. Arguments for it emphasize preventable mistakes, the costs of evaluating complex choices, and inexpensive opt-out policies. Popular examples include Social Security, Medicare, safety regulation, mandatory education, cigarette taxes, retirement-plan defaults, and calorie disclosures. Policies vary considerably in popularity and implementation across jurisdictions.

Nudges such as automatic retirement enrollment, court-date reminders, and household energy comparisons can affect behavior cheaply, but they do not always work. Government nudge-unit results tend to be smaller than published academic findings, potentially because of publication bias or implementation difficulties. Some people dislike nudges and may be willing to pay to avoid them, so opt-outs can help respect preferences.

The Save More Tomorrow plan is presented as successful libertarian paternalism. Employees voluntarily commit portions of future pay raises to retirement savings, contributions rise automatically, and participants may leave at any time. The plan uses present bias, loss aversion, reference dependence, and defaults to increase saving without immediate pay cuts.

Markets may offer products that help consumers, but firms can also target and exploit naive consumers, who may not recognize their need for assistance. Regulation can address exploitation through disclosure requirements, advertising restrictions, and interest-rate caps. Firms and governments can also create “sludges,” using behavioral techniques or administrative burdens to obstruct beneficial choices. Identifying and removing such obstacles may be as important as implementing nudges.

The lecture concludes that psychological factors matter in economic decisions. Soft paternalism can improve welfare, but nudges may fail, backfire, or reduce welfare, so policies should be evaluated carefully and allow opt-outs where appropriate.

The Wisconsin Court of Appeals affirmed Andrew Sabo’s convictions for possessing cocaine with intent to deliver and being a felon in possession of firearms. Sabo argued that evidence seized from his residence should be suppressed because the search-warrant affidavit lacked probable cause, contained false statements warranting a Franks-Mann hearing, and relied on an informant whose identity should have been disclosed.

A citizen informant reported seeing Sabo, known as “Drew,” loading a firearm and packaging cocaine at his Milwaukee residence. Officer Rodolfo Ayala identified Sabo, confirmed his felony record and probation status, and observed him at the reported address. A search found firearms, ammunition, suspected cocaine, marijuana plants, drug paraphernalia, packaging supplies, surveillance equipment, and cash.

The court concluded that the informant’s firsthand, specific observations and Ayala’s independent corroboration established reliability and probable cause. Alleged inaccuracies concerning Sabo’s nickname, the firearm’s color, and other omitted details did not substantially show deliberate falsehood or reckless disregard for the truth. Claims connecting the affidavit to an allegedly false 911 call were also insufficient and relied on a caller the trial court found less credible.

Because the affidavit was sufficient and the informant reasonably considered credible, the trial court properly denied suppression, a Franks-Mann hearing, and disclosure of the informant’s identity.

Mercedes chief Toto Wolff believes driver rivalry, including stress and tension, can help sustain the team’s success. Hamilton and Bottas enjoyed a controversy-free season while securing Mercedes’ fourth consecutive constructors’ championship, unlike Hamilton’s bitter rivalry with Nico Rosberg. Astronomers observed Cha 1170-7626, a rogue planet about 600 light-years away, accumulating gas and dust at a record 6 billion metric tons per second. Estimated at five to 10 times Jupiter’s mass, it grew up to eight times faster from late June through August than in April and May. Telescope observations also showed increased heat, brightness and water vapor. The prolonged growth spurt resembles behavior previously observed only in young stars, suggesting a starlike formation process. Researchers plan further observations to determine whether such bursts recur and how common they are among rogue planets.

Reinaldo De Jesus Henao, 36, was arrested at Coachella after festival-goers traced missing phones. Police allegedly found over 100 stolen devices in his backpack. Charged with grand theft and receiving stolen property, he was released on $10,000 bail.

The lecture examines exact solutions of nonlinear PDEs, chiefly Burgers’ equation. For inviscid Burgers’ equation with a unit delta-function initial source, the solution consists of a fan \(u=x/t\) followed by a shock, with zero elsewhere. Conservation of total mass places the shock at \(X(t)=\sqrt{2t}\). The solution satisfies both the shock jump condition and the entropy condition, which distinguishes valid shocks from expansion fans.

For Burgers’ equation with viscosity, introducing the integral of \(u\) and then applying an exponential change of variables converts the nonlinear equation into the linear heat equation. Taking viscosity to zero produces the inviscid solution; the limiting integral is dominated by the point minimizing a particular expression involving the initial data and \((x-y)^2/(2t)\). This yields an explicit minimization formula that correctly generates shocks, fans, shock speeds, and entropy-satisfying solutions.

The lecture also discusses the Korteweg–de Vries equation, a nonlinear dispersive equation associated with shallow water waves. Numerical experiments showed that traveling waves called solitons can interact and then re-emerge with their original shapes. This suggested hidden linearity and led to the discovery that KDV is completely integrable, with infinitely many conserved quantities. Other integrable nonlinear equations include nonlinear Schrödinger equations.

Navier–Stokes equations are not known to be completely integrable, and the existence of three-dimensional solutions for all time remains unresolved. Recent numerical experiments reportedly ruled out one proposed finite-time blow-up scenario.

Chelsea manager Antonio Conte urged his players to focus on beating Huddersfield rather than their upcoming Champions League tie with Barcelona. After losing 1-0 to West Ham, Conte said Chelsea must improve results and fight for Champions League qualification, conceding that defending their Premier League title is unrealistic. The passage argues that Oklahoma quarterback Baker Mayfield was the best quarterback prospect in the 2018 NFL draft based on analytics, despite debate about his personality, arrest, height, college offense, and playing style. Pro Football Focus unanimously ranked Mayfield atop the class, citing his performance under pressure and accuracy at short, intermediate, and deep levels. He completed 38 of 67 passes traveling at least 20 yards, substantially outperforming Josh Allen, while radar data showed his pass velocity was only slightly below Allen’s. Football Outsiders’ QBASE rated Mayfield its fourth-highest quarterback prospect since 1997. Concerns included his sub-6-foot-1 height, tendency to hold the ball and take unnecessary sacks, and transition from Oklahoma’s Air Raid offense. Nevertheless, reports suggested he would likely be selected among the top five picks because of his accuracy, composure under pressure, and arm strength.

AOL Instant Messenger, active since 1997, will shut down permanently on December 15, 2017. Once a leading U.S. messaging service, AIM declined as cell phone texting and social media platforms became widespread.

The speaker is focused on the Stanley Cup Finals after accepting the league’s decision regarding a recent incident. He plans to be more careful around the goalie and avoid penalties. He discusses several players’ different strengths, including puck movement, net traffic, and poise. Away from the rink, he focuses on family and managing his fantasy baseball team.

Earth’s total solar eclipses result from the moon being about 400 times smaller than the sun but also 400 times closer, allowing it to cover the sun and reveal its corona. As the moon moves away about 1.5 inches annually, this alignment is temporary; in roughly 600 million years, total solar eclipses will cease.

Theresa May reportedly planned to seek Cabinet backing at Chequers for a soft Brexit maintaining EU product and agricultural standards, easing goods trade and collecting EU customs tariffs while allowing independent trade deals. Freedom of movement would end, though EU citizens could receive preferential access to live and work in Britain in exchange for better European access for UK services. The proposals intensified Conservative divisions. Phillip Lee accused Brexiteers of planning a leadership coup, while William Hague warned Cabinet members against resigning or demanding a clean break, arguing that failure to compromise could lead Parliament to impose a more diluted Brexit.

The Colorado Supreme Court reviewed an order requiring personal-injury plaintiffs to disclose therapists’ notes and records to YMCA. The plaintiffs had sought damages for mental suffering and psychiatric care after four-year-old Erin Bond was severely injured in an accident involving a YMCA truck.

By placing their mental conditions at issue, the plaintiffs waived physician-patient and psychologist-patient privileges. However, evidence showed that disclosure of confidential therapy communications could harm their treatment and cause embarrassment or oppression. The district court considered YMCA’s need to defend against the claims but failed to balance it against the plaintiffs’ confidentiality and treatment interests as required under C.R.C.P. 26(c).

The Supreme Court made its rule absolute and remanded for reconsideration under the proper balancing standard. It did not determine that disclosure was necessarily improper, noting that the district court could use measures such as in camera review, court-appointed experts, or tailored protective orders.

NeuroAdapter is an end-to-end brain-decoding framework that conditions a pretrained Stable Diffusion model directly on parcel-wise fMRI embeddings, avoiding intermediate image or text embedding spaces that may create information bottlenecks and reduce interpretability. Cortical fMRI data are parcellated, projected into tokens, and integrated through trainable cross-attention modules while the remaining diffusion model is frozen. Training uses stochastic fMRI-token dropout and min-SNR loss weighting. During evaluation, a brain encoder selects from candidate reconstructions based on correlation between predicted and measured fMRI activity.

The accompanying Image-Brain BI-directional framework (IBBI) analyzes cross-attention throughout diffusion. Its brain-directed view estimates each cortical parcel’s relative contribution, while its image-directed view maps where selected brain regions direct attention in reconstructed images. Parcel masking further examines the effects of specific regions.

NeuroAdapter was evaluated on NSD, NSD-Imagery, and Deeprecon using eight image-quality metrics. It achieved competitive performance against embedding-aligned methods, particularly for high-level semantic measures, while showing more modest low-level improvements because it lacks a dedicated low-level latent-feature pathway. It generalized to mental imagery and disjoint test categories, capturing category information and properties such as shape, orientation, and color. Interpretability analyses showed distinct spatial attention patterns for face-, body-, scene-, and word-selective regions; masking high-level regions substantially altered semantic content, whereas masking low-level regions did not.

The authors note variability caused by stochastic diffusion and argue that image-quality metrics alone may not establish faithful brain decoding. They propose interpretability as a complementary means of understanding interactions between neural activity and image generation.

At the 2017 Teen Choice Awards, Zendaya urged young people to stay educated, pay attention to injustice, use their voices, think independently, and recognize their power as future leaders to improve the world.

Doctors determined Erik’s healing had progressed as far as possible, clearing his return after a final consultation. The team was outskated, lost battles, took undisciplined penalties, and failed to create traffic or get shots through. With one Stanley Cup game remaining at home, the coach stressed relying on veteran experience, restoring the team’s skating style, and offering no excuses despite Doug’s absence. He praised the returning player’s courageous, physical effort and expected Joe to perform strongly despite lingering effects from knee surgery. Both finalists were described as well-conditioned, with execution, special teams, and disciplined play expected to matter more than atmosphere or adrenaline.

The patent describes systems for managing cloud-hosted virtual desktop resources. A service provider monitors client connections, disconnections, and inactivity, then applies default, administrator-defined, or user-defined policies to determine whether and when to shut down underlying virtualized computing instances. Activity may be detected through session gateways, protocol agents, operating-system events, or network traffic patterns.

When an instance is shut down, associated storage volumes and user data may remain maintained but detached. Upon reconnection, the same or another computing instance can be started and the volumes reattached, restoring the desktop environment and applications. Historical usage patterns and machine-learning models may predict shutdown and restart times, balancing fast reconnections against minimizing unused active resources. Connection status and active-resource periods may also support differentiated billing.

The system may operate in multi-tenant provider networks using virtual machines, storage virtualization, public and private IP addressing, virtual private networks, and overlay networking. Program Execution Service components manage remote sessions, user profiles, desktop images, persistent stores, backups, resource placement, and failure recovery.

The Sansa c200 uses a rechargeable lithium-ion battery and includes a Hold switch to disable controls and a Record button for microphone recording. It connects to a computer through USB and appears as an additional drive. Music and other files can be transferred in MTP or MSC mode; photos require Sansa Media Converter, which supports JPEG, TIFF, PNG, BMP, and GIF. Files may be deleted through the computer’s file browser, and the player should be safely removed after file or firmware operations.

The player supports music, voice and FM recordings, photos, slideshows, and FM radio. Playback controls provide track navigation, repeat, shuffle, equalizer settings, and a GoList. Radio features include tuning, scanning, presets, and broadcast recording. Settings cover backlight, contrast, power timers, connection mode, device information, and factory reset. Supported audio formats include MP3, WAV, WMA, and secure WMA; unsupported formats must be converted. MTP is used to synchronize media with Windows XP and Windows Media Player 10.

Technical support is available through SanDisk by telephone, online request, or email. The one-year limited warranty applies to the original purchaser, excludes third-party software and damage caused by misuse, improper installation, unauthorized repair, modification, or accident, and may provide repair, replacement, or refund. SanDisk disclaims responsibility for lost data and limits liability as permitted by law.

The software license permits limited personal use on one computer or device. Modification, reverse engineering, unauthorized distribution, and disclosure of proprietary information are prohibited. The software is provided without warranties, is not intended for high-risk activities, and the agreement is governed by California and United States law. The device must not be discarded with unsorted household waste; local return and collection systems should be used.

Apple Inc.’s 2022 Form 10-K covers the fiscal year ended September 24, 2022. Apple designs and sells smartphones, computers, tablets, wearables, accessories and related services, including advertising, AppleCare, cloud, digital content and payments. Direct and indirect channels represented 38% and 62% of 2022 net sales, respectively. Apple had approximately 164,000 full-time-equivalent employees.

The company identifies risks from economic conditions, COVID-19, geopolitical and trade disputes, intense competition, supply constraints, outsourced manufacturing, product defects, cybersecurity incidents, regulation, litigation, currency movements, credit exposure and tax changes. Most hardware manufacturing is outsourced to partners primarily in Asia.

As of March 25, 2022, stock held by non-affiliates had an aggregate market value of approximately $2.83 trillion. Apple had 15.9 billion shares outstanding on October 14, 2022. In litigation with Epic Games, the district court ruled for Apple on nine of ten Epic claims and Apple’s breach-of-contract claims, while issuing an injunction concerning certain App Store guidelines; appeals were pending. Apple’s common stock trades on Nasdaq under AAPL.

InfoWorld provides promotional and usage guidelines for Technology of the Year Award winners. Companies may be referenced in award publicity, while proprietary information will not be disclosed. Physical awards and reprints may be ordered from YGS Group, which sets production costs. Winners may purchase a license to use the award logo, which cannot be altered, distorted, combined with other elements, or placed too close to company or product names.

Press materials must use the full name “InfoWorld Technology of the Year Awards,” identify the publication initially as “IDG’s InfoWorld,” and accurately name any subsidiary receiving an award. An approved quote from Executive Editor Doug Dineley may be used; modifications require approval. The annual awards are selected by InfoWorld editors and reviewers from products tested during the previous year and recognize innovative IT products.
