The three-member LakeSmart Team is delivering its summer Dock Talk program and attending Kenora’s weekly Matiowski Farmers’ Market to promote healthy lake ecosystems. The LOWDPOA initiative provides guidance on shoreline landscaping, septic systems, invasive species, safe refueling, and the Clean, Drain and Dry boating program. The team will also give scheduled presentations, join IISD Experimental Lakes Area tours, and offer presentations to lake groups upon request.

The passage highlights United Nations efforts to expand access to clean water and improve water management. Examples include UNMISS creating a clean-water system in South Sudan, UNICEF raising restaurant donations for children without water access, a Singapore university developing water-harvesting technology, and UNHCR funding standpipes serving about 800 people in Kyrgyzstan. It also describes UN efforts to coordinate water-related sustainable development goals through an inclusive dialogue. General Assembly President Miroslav Lajčák warned that future wars could concern water and urged action to prevent conflict and treat water appropriately.

The 2018 Chevrolet Equinox’s available 1.6L turbo-diesel engine achieves 6.0 L/100 km highway fuel consumption in the FWD model. The GM-developed engine produces 240 lb-ft of torque, supports B20 biodiesel, and includes stop/start technology. The compact SUV also offers expanded cargo space, connectivity and safety features. Canadian pricing starts at $27,145, while turbo-diesel models start at $35,645, including destination charges.

The Put-Call ratio is a sentiment indicator calculated by dividing traded put options by call options, using either volume or open interest. Calls provide the right to buy shares at a predetermined price within a set period, while puts provide the right to sell and can serve as protection against falling prices. High Put-Call readings generally indicate fear, while low readings suggest complacency, though appropriate levels vary by market and indicator. Because markets may revert toward their mean, extreme readings are often treated as contrarian signals.

Put-Call ratios exist for indices and individual stocks and are available through many trading platforms and exchanges, although free downloadable data can be difficult to find. The article’s S&P 500 backtest produced unimpressive performance; one example showed an average 6.36% gain after 115 days, excluding dividends. The authors consider the Put-Call ratio inferior to other sentiment indicators, such as the VIX, and recommend independently backtesting trading methods.

Artificial intelligence (AI), encompassing machine learning and deep learning, uses reliable data to generate insights and support decisions across sectors, including education. AI applications should be assessed for transparency, accuracy, reliability, safety, fairness, privacy, security, non-discrimination, and alignment with human values.

Higher education institutions can implement AI by defining objectives aligned with institutional goals, investing in infrastructure and cybersecurity, training faculty and staff, conducting pilot projects, establishing governance policies, promoting personalized learning, using predictive analytics, collaborating with technology providers, evaluating outcomes, and involving students. Responsible integration requires ethical oversight, data protection, bias audits, human supervision of critical decisions, transparency, equitable access, and continuous evaluation.

Potential benefits include personalized and adaptive learning, immersive virtual and augmented reality experiences, increased engagement, intelligent tutoring, real-time feedback, consistent grading, improved accessibility, academic and career guidance, data-informed decisions, and greater administrative efficiency. AI may also reduce costs by automating grading, scheduling, admissions, and record management.

Challenges include implementation and maintenance costs, unequal access, faculty resistance, algorithmic bias, data privacy risks, dependence on technology, cybersecurity threats, reduced human interaction, cheating, and possible teacher job displacement. Because biased data can produce biased outcomes, institutions should maintain human oversight and update quality assurance processes to include AI ethics.

Successful adoption requires clear goals, suitable infrastructure, ongoing educator training, flexible platforms, and regular feedback from students and teachers. AI is expected to expand personalized learning, automated assessment, predictive analytics, administrative automation, and assistive technologies, while prompting changes in assessment, institutional roles, curricula, and public education about AI.

The passage recommends clear policies, ethical safeguards, privacy protections, and guidelines against misuse rather than outright institutional bans. It also presents the author’s view that students should avoid AI in school and coursework to preserve analytical and critical-thinking skills, while allowing carefully evaluated use in research. Overall, AI offers transformative opportunities in higher education, but its value depends on balanced, inclusive, and accountable implementation.

Touch Football Australia and the NRL will launch the nationally broadcast NRL Touch Premiership on May 18. Elite men and women, including Ipswich players, will represent teams aligned with six NRL clubs in curtain-raisers over seven rounds. Jillaroos star Ali Brigginshaw said the partnership would raise touch football’s profile, create pathways between codes and let players participate year-round, though her contract may prevent her competing.

To replace an HDD with a SanDisk SSD, shut down the computer, disconnect power, and remove a notebook battery. For notebooks, transfer any HDD brackets or adapters, align and connect the SSD in the SATA drive bay, reassemble the bay, replace the battery and power cable, and restart. For desktops, open the case, disconnect and remove the HDD, install the SSD—using a 3.5-inch mounting adapter if required—connect SATA data and power cables, close the case, and restart. The old HDD may be retained as a backup.

Harvey Weinstein was indicted in Manhattan on rape and criminal sex act charges involving two women. Weinstein denied the allegations and declined to testify before the grand jury, saying he lacked preparation time and that political pressure made indictment inevitable. District Attorney Cyrus Vance defended the process and expressed confidence in the evidence. Weinstein, free on $1 million bail with electronic monitoring, is accused of a 2013 hotel-room rape and forcing former actress Lucia Evans to perform oral sex in 2004. Dozens of other women have accused him of misconduct. Vance previously faced criticism for declining to prosecute Weinstein over a 2015 groping allegation, prompting a state investigation into his handling of that case.

Leapfrog’s spring Hospital Safety Grades showed broad patient-safety improvements. Five hospitals earned an “A” after previously receiving an “F,” while 46 earned their first “A” since grading began in 2012. Of roughly 2,500 hospitals, 30% received an “A,” 28% a “B,” 35% a “C,” 6% a “D,” and 1% an “F.” Hawaii, Idaho, Rhode Island, Massachusetts, and Virginia had the highest percentages of “A” hospitals. Maryland improved to three “A” hospitals, and Washington, D.C., gained its first in five years. Forty-nine hospitals have maintained an “A” in every grading cycle. The peer-reviewed, publicly available grades are updated twice yearly.

The disclosure describes techniques for reducing power consumption in near-eye VR, AR, and MR displays while maintaining perceived image quality. A controller determines a maximum-luminance location based on the user’s field of view or gaze, typically near the foveal axis, and independently drives OLED, AMOLED, micro-LED, or other light sources according to their distance from that location. For the same input display value, sources nearer the maximum-luminance location emit at higher luminance than more distant sources. Display zones may use different mappings between input values and luminance ranges, with transitions limited to reduce noticeable differences.

An eye-tracking subsystem may illuminate and image the eye, identify features such as the pupil, iris, corneal reflections, and corneal position, and determine gaze direction through calibrated feature-, appearance-, interpolation-, or model-based methods. The resulting gaze data can dynamically shift the high-luminance zone as the eye moves.

The described artificial-reality system may include a head-mounted display or glasses, display electronics and optics, waveguides, sensors, tracking modules, a console, and controllers. Display controllers may generate luminance maps using lookup tables and send driving instructions through timing, gate, and source drivers. Lowering peripheral-zone luminance can reduce display power with minimal or no effect on user experience; example reductions range from about 5% to 40%.

The Boathouse at City Point will open June 17 on Hopewell’s riverfront. The fourth Central Virginia location will include indoor, patio and event spaces, offer coastal dishes with locally sourced ingredients, and serve lunch and dinner daily plus Sunday brunch. Officials consider it a cornerstone of riverfront revitalization.

Madison Realty Capital provided JDS Development Group a $137 million construction loan to fully finance Monad Terrace, a 59-residence waterfront development in South Beach designed by Jean Nouvel with Kobi Karp Architecture. Residences range from two to five bedrooms and 1,453 to 5,350 square feet, featuring private elevators, custom interiors, terraces, gardens, reflecting pools and climate-resilience measures, including elevating the building 11.5 feet. Sales average nearly $2,000 per square foot, with a penthouse under contract at $2,700 per square foot. Construction was underway, with completion projected for fall 2019. Douglas Elliman Development Marketing manages sales and marketing, while JLL arranged the financing.

Glibc 2.28 development includes clean GNU/Hurd support without out-of-tree patches, following numerous Hurd-related commits. GNU Guix can run on Android devices, though installation requires significant effort. Node.js 10.0 is expected to support npm 6, whose major update introduces new security features for developers working with open-source code.

The PGA848 input circuitry operates linearly within 3V of either supply while maintaining strong common-mode rejection. Its valid common-mode range depends on common-mode and differential input voltages, gain, and reference voltage.

A typical application drives an ADS8860 16-bit, 1MSPS SAR ADC using ±15V input-stage supplies and a 5.3V output-stage supply. A REF6250 provides the 5V ADC reference, while a precision divider and OPA192 buffer generate a 2.5V midscale voltage for the PGA848 REF pin. Three filters address EMI/RFI, bandwidth, noise, ADC charge kickback, settling, and distortion. The nominal bandwidth is 318kHz, potentially decreasing to 277kHz with feedback-resistor tolerance, while maintaining –0.1dB flatness to 41kHz. Stability should exceed 60° phase margin when reference-load components are modified.

Nominal performance is specified at ±15V supplies. Output-stage supplies must remain within input-stage supply levels, and supplies above 40V permanently damage the device. Recommended PCB practices include matched input paths, close 0.1µF supply bypass capacitors, separation of sensitive and noisy traces, minimized leakage and parasitic capacitance, limited thermal junctions, and separation from heat sources.

Large-\(N\) gauge-theory expansions share the topology-based structure of string perturbation theory when the string coupling is identified with \(1/N\). Single-trace operators correspond to string or glueball states, while Feynman diagrams of fixed genus can be viewed as discrete triangulations of string worldsheets. The large-\(N\) limit then corresponds to classical, tree-level string theory, with higher-genus terms representing quantum string loops.

Establishing an explicit gauge/string correspondence is difficult because Feynman amplitudes are products of propagators rather than recognizable string actions, the appropriate target space and worldsheet theory are unknown, and a continuum worldsheet geometry is expected to emerge only from complicated diagrams dominating at strong coupling. This program works more explicitly for simpler matrix integrals and matrix quantum mechanics. Fundamental-representation fields introduce surfaces with boundaries and open strings, while \(SO(N)\) or \(Sp(N)\) theories require non-orientable surfaces and strings.

A direct four-dimensional string description of large-\(N\) QCD fails: ordinary strings are quantum mechanically consistent only in critical dimensions, and compactifying a consistent higher-dimensional string theory to four dimensions produces a massless spin-2 particle absent from QCD. Holography instead suggests that a four-dimensional gauge theory may correspond to a gravitational string theory with one additional noncompact dimension.

Requiring a five-dimensional metric to preserve four-dimensional Poincaré symmetry gives a warped form depending only on the extra coordinate. If the field theory is scale invariant, that symmetry fixes the warp factor and yields anti-de Sitter space. Thus a large-\(N\) conformal field theory in \(D\) dimensions, if it has a string description, should correspond to string theory in \(AdS_{D+1}\), with \(1/N\) related to the string coupling. Maldacena supplied explicit examples in 1997, and Witten subsequently connected them to the holographic principle.

The lecture then begins the string-theory derivation. A string worldsheet embedded in a target spacetime inherits a metric, and its Nambu–Goto action measures worldsheet area. Introducing an auxiliary worldsheet metric rewrites this square-root action as the polynomial Polyakov action. Quantizing the string therefore becomes equivalent to quantizing two-dimensional gravity coupled to \(D\) scalar fields, integrating over both embeddings and worldsheet metrics.

TeraWulf is shifting from bitcoin mining to AI-focused digital infrastructure, supported by expanded Fluidstack contracts and a $3.2 billion Google commitment. The company targets $760 million in annual revenue and plans to expand power capacity to 1,150 MW by 2030, potentially raising annual revenue to $1.5 billion. The author considers WULF attractively valued but discloses no position and emphasizes investment risks.

Britain’s regulator Ofqual proposed a record £175,000 fine for exam board OCR after a 2017 Romeo and Juliet question mistakenly described Tybalt as hating the Capulets rather than the Montagues. The error affected grading and was deemed damaging to public confidence.

Using airborne lidar, archaeologists identified more than 60,000 previously unknown Mayan structures beneath Guatemala’s Petén jungle, including homes, fortifications, causeways and a seven-story pyramid. The technology creates three-dimensional maps by measuring laser pulses reflected through dense vegetation. Findings suggest the Maya controlled extensive territories with sophisticated trade networks, large-scale food production and water-management systems. Researchers said earlier population estimates may have been three to four times too low, with 10 million to 15 million people potentially living in the region, including swampy areas once considered uninhabitable. Archaeologists said analyzing the extensive data could take decades and significantly alter understanding of Mayan civilization and complex tropical societies.

Steven Kean asks how important defending the Export-Import Bank is to Enron. Enron and other major exporters were lobbying Congress against a proposed 25% budget cut, while the White House characterized the bank as corporate welfare; Enron received $135 million in Ex-Im financing in fiscal 2000. Other reports cover Enron’s Houston office tower, Dutch gas-market trading, California power contracts and unpaid supplier bills, doubts over Sierra Pacific’s acquisition of Portland General Electric, and falling U.S. natural-gas prices.

“The Last Three,” a 5m bronze sculpture of the remaining Northern White Rhinos, was unveiled in New York to highlight their impending extinction. Critic Jerry Saltz condemned the work, prompting social media debate. The three related zoo survivors were moved to Kenya’s Ol Pejeta sanctuary in 2009; poachers likely killed the last wild members 12 years ago.

The disclosure describes AI-based image encoding and decoding intended to reduce bitrate for high-resolution images. An encoding apparatus determines whether to down-scale an original image using a first deep neural network (DNN), encodes the resulting lower-resolution image with a conventional frequency-transform codec, and transmits image data plus AI data describing whether and how AI down-scaling was performed.

A decoding apparatus conventionally decodes the image data, then uses the AI data to determine whether to up-scale the decoded image through a jointly trained second DNN. AI up-scaling occurs when the image was AI down-scaled and the required DNN and settings are available. Otherwise, the decoded image may be output directly, up-scaled by a display device, or processed through legacy scaling. Systems without AI capabilities remain compatible by processing only the conventional image data.

The AI data may identify resolution changes, target resolution or quality, codec type, bitrate, encoding parameters, or appropriate DNN settings. DNN settings may control layer structures, filter kernels, and parameters, and may vary by image, frame, user settings, or display capabilities. The up-scaling DNN may combine convolution-layer output with a bypass-scaled image and may also use pixel-position or encoding information. The down-scaling and up-scaling DNNs are jointly trained using image-quality loss so that reconstructed images more closely match original images.

This cross-sectional analysis examined whether the BCHE-K variant affects age at Alzheimer disease diagnosis among APOE4 carriers. The study included 45 patients aged 50–74 with cerebrospinal fluid biomarker-confirmed mild Alzheimer disease; 33 carried APOE4 and 16 carried BCHE-K.

Among APOE4 carriers, BCHE-K carriers were diagnosed an average of 6.4 years earlier than noncarriers (60.6 versus 67.0 years; P < .001). Their baseline age was also 6.2 years younger, with slightly greater amyloid and tau accumulation. BCHE-K had no comparable influence among APOE4 noncarriers. APOE4 carriers generally showed greater amyloid pathology and a more limbic-amnestic phenotype.

Regression analyses associated amyloid pathology with APOE4 status, larger ventricular volume, less synaptic injury, and less tau. Tau pathology was associated with greater neuroaxonal damage, synaptic injury, and glial activation. The authors propose that APOE4 and BCHE-K may influence early Alzheimer phenotypes through cholinergic signaling and glial function.

The study was limited by its small, potentially unrepresentative clinical-trial sample, cross-sectional design, restricted age range, and retrospective age-at-diagnosis assessment. Findings should not be extrapolated to patients over 75 and require confirmation in larger prospective longitudinal studies. The work is a non-peer-reviewed preprint based on a study funded by Biogen and designed and executed by Ionis.

Smith County legal notices for the week of May 31, 2018 include requests for information about a 2000 Chevy Silverado and a 1999 Suzuki; probate land auctions for the estates of Alfred Gene Stewart Jr. on June 23 and Betty Rose Drake on June 9; creditor notices for the estates of Leon Dewayne Barnes, Nellie Belle Hunter, and Sarah Kaye Stallings; publication orders concerning an adoption and termination-of-parental-rights case involving Jason Rodgers and a dependency-and-neglect case involving Danny Lee Brown; and trustee sales of properties at 217 College Avenue East on June 13 and 9 Hills Dale Lane East on June 21. The passage also links to the Town of Gordonsville budget and South Side Utility District water reports for three districts.

The lecture examines structures tailored to finite impulse response (FIR) systems. FIR filters can use direct, transposed, or cascade forms, but conventional parallel forms do not apply because FIR systems have no poles.

Linear-phase FIR filters have symmetric impulse responses, allowing paired input samples to share coefficients. This reduces the number of multiplications by approximately half while retaining the same number of delays. Transposing the resulting structure provides another linear-phase implementation.

Frequency-sampling structures express an FIR system using discrete Fourier transform coefficients, which are samples of its frequency response. The structure combines a common factor with parallel recursive sections whose poles cancel corresponding zeros, leaving an overall FIR response. Although pole-zero cancellation and finite-register effects are drawbacks, this form can reduce computation when many frequency samples are zero and can efficiently share components among multiple equal-length filters in a filter bank.

Practical structure selection depends on delays, multiplications, modularity, and finite-register-length effects. Arithmetic rounding produces output noise, while coefficient quantization changes pole locations. Pole sensitivity increases when clustered poles are implemented through higher-order polynomials, making direct forms more sensitive than cascade or parallel forms using low-order sections. Even among second-order implementations, direct and coupled forms produce different grids of realizable pole locations because they quantize different coefficient parameters.

Ultralight backpacking prioritizes carrying less to travel farther, faster, and more comfortably. It is defined here as having a base weight of 10 pounds or less, excluding worn clothing and consumables; lightweight is 15 pounds or less, while “super ultralight” targets 5 pounds.

The first step is to remove nonessential items while ensuring warmth, comfort, food, and safety. After eliminating unnecessary gear, focus on reducing the weight of the shelter, sleep system, and backpack, choosing the pack after determining the size of the other equipment. Experimenting with alternatives such as tarps, cowboy camping, and quilts can reveal what is genuinely needed.

Ultralight backpacking is ultimately a flexible philosophy rather than a strict weight limit. Simple routines, such as eating away from camp and carrying gear that is easy to pack, can improve safety and mobility. Beginners may not immediately reach 10 pounds, and needs vary by trip. Continued experimentation generally lightens packs by identifying unused equipment and removing obstacles to enjoying the outdoors.

Researchers investigated whether a highly transmissible or virulent RSV variant caused the unusually early, severe U.S. surge in autumn 2022. Sequencing 105 diagnostic specimens from Greater Boston produced 54 near-complete and 23 partial genomes. Among 77 genomes, 91% were RSV-A and 9% RSV-B; near-complete genomes were genotypes GA2.3.5 or GB5.0.5a. RSV-A comprised at least 10 distinct lineages with common ancestors dating to 2014–2017, while RSV-B lineages had a latest estimated common ancestor in 2019. Several Massachusetts lineages were also identified in Washington. Genetic divergence matched expected evolutionary rates rather than the accelerated evolution observed in major SARS-CoV-2 variants. The findings indicate that numerous pre-existing RSV lineages, not one newly emerged highly transmissible lineage, drove the surge. The authors recommend investigating non-viral factors, including pandemic-related changes in immunity and RSV circulation.

Seven months after disclosing treatment for alcohol addiction, Ben Affleck was photographed smiling and appearing upbeat at a reported Los Angeles outpatient treatment centre. In March, Affleck said rehab was the first of many steps toward recovery and expressed gratitude for support from family, friends and co-parent Jennifer Garner. He also said he wanted to be the best father possible and show his children there is no shame in seeking help.

International law generally prohibits searching or arresting foreign ships on the high seas, except suspected pirates, and requires compensation for unjust arrest. The Cape Horn Pigeon was seized by Russian agents while whaling 125 miles from Russian land and taken to Vladivostok. Although a Russian commission claimed the vessel had entered Russian waters, no supporting evidence was presented, and innocent passage through territorial waters was well established. The commission found no basis for confiscation, acknowledged that the arrest resulted from a misunderstanding, returned the vessel, and offered indemnity. The seizure allegedly violated treaty and international-law rights and ended the voyage, harming the owners, officers, and crew. They claimed $45,000 for lost vessel service, calculated from average prior catches minus the current catch. The loss was characterized as direct because the season and crew engagements prevented resuming the voyage. Arbitration decisions involving the Betsey and Neptune supported awarding expected profits from voyages unlawfully interrupted.

The study examined US death-certificate data from 2014–2020 to assess whether cancer increased COVID-19 mortality. Researchers modeled expected weekly mortality and compared it with observed deaths during 2020, considering underlying-cause and multiple-cause coding for six cancer categories and several chronic diseases. National patterns were supplemented with analyses of New York, California, and Texas, which experienced differently timed COVID-19 waves.

Underlying-cause cancer deaths did not increase notably during 2020, but multiple-cause cancer mortality rose modestly during pandemic waves. Nationally, there were approximately 12,000 excess cancer deaths, a statistically significant 2% increase over baseline. Hematological cancers had the largest increase at 5%, while pancreatic and lung cancers showed no excess. New York’s spring wave produced an 8% rise in multiple-cause cancer mortality, including increases of 8% for colorectal, 13% for hematological, and 15% for breast cancer. Cancer increases in California and Texas were generally small and statistically insignificant.

By comparison, diabetes and Alzheimer’s mortality rose substantially and tracked COVID-19 waves. Multiple-cause mortality increased 39% for diabetes and 31% for Alzheimer’s nationally.

A demographic model projected mortality under the assumption that chronic conditions did not independently increase COVID-19 risk. It incorporated population age, size, baseline mortality, SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence, and age-adjusted infection-fatality ratios. Observed cancer mortality was generally more consistent with this null hypothesis than with a model in which cancer doubled COVID-19 fatality risk. Differences between cancer and other chronic diseases could largely be explained by demographic factors and competing mortality risks. Particularly lethal cancers, such as pancreatic and lung cancer, had high baseline mortality and small populations at risk, limiting detectable COVID-19-related increases.

The findings do not support the hypothesis that cancer-related immunosuppression protected patients from severe infection; hematological cancers were the most affected cancer category. Coding changes shifted some deaths from cancer as the underlying cause to COVID-19 as the underlying cause, making multiple-cause records important, but adjusted cancer excess mortality remained modest.

Limitations included uncertainty in model inputs, large state-level confidence intervals, lack of data beyond 2020, and reliance on mortality rather than hospitalization, morbidity, or Long COVID. Longer-term effects from disrupted cancer diagnosis and treatment were not assessed.

The passage argues that interdisciplinary music education connects music with mathematics, language, science, technology, psychology, arts, and social studies, supporting cognitive, academic, emotional, social, and creative development. Research cited links music education to improved memory, problem-solving, analytical thinking, language skills, mathematical understanding, communication, collaboration, and cultural awareness.

The qualitative study combined a literature review, content analysis, and a single-participant case study involving a social studies teacher studying music at a Fine Arts Faculty. A semi-structured interview examined the participant’s experiences, perceived deficiencies in music education, and views on curricula and workshops.

The participant reported inadequate foundational music preparation, assumptions by instructors that students already possessed basic knowledge, and insufficient practical and interdisciplinary instruction. Suggested improvements included preparatory classes differentiated by prior education; practical teaching of music theories and methods; creative drama, media literacy, material design, psychology, speech, dance, music-and-movement, and workshop courses; micro-teaching and simulated lessons; learning-style assessments; and instruction in instruments such as bağlama, piano, guitar, and ukulele. The participant also emphasized presentation work, practical teaching experience, repertoire development, and strategies for teaching when instruments or resources are unavailable.

The study concludes that interdisciplinary basic music education is necessary for well-rounded learning and should be embedded in curricula and education policies. It recommends strengthening collaboration between music and other disciplines, improving teacher competencies, expanding practical workshops and research, and designing programs in consultation with teachers.

Nabors Industries sold Quail Tools for more than its purchase price and plans to use the proceeds to reduce debt by 25%. Its key U.S. and Saudi markets appear near cyclical lows. Although shares have risen 70% from recent lows, the author believes historical valuations suggest further upside. The author holds no current position but may buy Nabors securities and states the article is opinion, not investment advice.

Environmental crises, resource scarcity, climate change, and pollution have increased international attention to environmental education and sustainable development. Major milestones include the 1972 UN Conference on the Human Environment, the 1975 Belgrade environmental education workshop, the 1992 Earth Summit and Agenda 21, and the UN Sustainable Development Goals.

Environmental education is an interdisciplinary, lifelong process that develops environmental awareness, knowledge, attitudes, skills, responsibility, participation, and evaluation abilities. It seeks to change behavior, promote stewardship, prevent and solve environmental problems, and support harmonious coexistence with nature. The Belgrade Charter emphasizes natural and human-made environments, lifelong learning, interdisciplinary study, active problem-solving, global and regional perspectives, future challenges, and the environmental impacts of development. Environmental education should be integrated across school subjects and supported through formal, non-formal, classroom, and outdoor learning. Outdoor environmental activities can strengthen knowledge, skills, attitudes, and meaningful participation, including among learners with disabilities.

The environment includes natural and human-made, living and non-living, visible and invisible, tangible and intangible elements. Environmental knowledge covers natural resources, social conditions, environmental technology, waste, and pollution. Environmental components have unique characteristics, are interdependent, form ecosystems, produce chain reactions when disrupted, vary in resilience, and change over time.

Sustainable development means improving present conditions and meeting current needs without reducing future generations’ ability to meet theirs. Its principles include economic growth, fair income distribution, quality of life, continued progress, protection of future resources, and action beginning with individuals and communities. Environmental sustainability underpins social and economic goals, including climate action.

Proposed methods for sustainable environmental development include reducing energy use and waste, conserving resources, protecting environmental quality, adopting clean technologies, recycling, strengthening community responsibility, and using science, technology, education, law, economic measures, and environmental management systems such as ISO 14000. Environmental management aims to meet human needs while conserving resources and stabilizing environmental quality.

Examples include a community collaborative learning project, Thailand’s Huai Sai development initiative, natural capital accounting cooperation with UNEP, and a national ecosystem assessment focused on marine and coastal biodiversity. These initiatives emphasize environmental knowledge, community participation, scientific assessment, policy development, and behavioral change as foundations for long-term economic, social, and environmental sustainability.

Foreigners entered a bivouac despite warnings and were eventually escorted out after giving their names. In diplomatic correspondence, Japanese minister K. Otori demanded that British consul-general C. T. Gardner retract reports that Otori had sought the dismissal of Korea’s naval instructor, which Otori denied. Gardner advised him to seek information through usual channels. Another statement outlined proposed reforms with deadlines ranging from ten days to two years.

U.S. Secretary Gresham reported worsening tensions in Korea and a possible Sino-Japanese war. Korea sought U.S. intervention, saying Chinese and Japanese troops threatened its independence after an internal revolution had been suppressed. China favored mutual troop withdrawal, while Japan refused and demanded political changes before withdrawing. Korea proposed a neutral-power conference and repeatedly requested American diplomatic assistance. The United States expressed sympathy and offered friendly influence but maintained impartial neutrality and rejected joint intervention with other powers.

Anton Shekhovtsov’s book “Tango Noir” examines Russia’s cultivation of Western far-right activists to portray the West as chaotic and Russia as an alternative global power. The strategy echoes Soviet tactics, including KGB operations intended to provoke fears of a Nazi resurgence in West Germany.

After Russia’s 2008 invasion of Georgia produced a public-relations setback, the Kremlin intensified its information war. RT became a major platform for fringe activists and employed tactics Shekhovtsov calls “nudge propaganda,” “narrative laundering” and selective sourcing. Far-right groups also supported Russia’s annexation of Crimea through election-observer missions, strengthening ties with Kremlin officials.

Shekhovtsov describes Putin’s system as competing clans and interconnected “operators,” including sympathetic foreign groups, activists, think tanks, oligarchs, diplomats and United Russia figures. These networks sought influence in Austria, Italy, France and Germany. Results have been limited: efforts supporting Marine Le Pen failed, Russia remains unpopular, Western sanctions persist and relations with the United States have not significantly improved. However, Russian tactics continue to evolve, with emerging evidence that paramilitary groups may be assisting Europe’s far right and encouraging violence.

These stackless assembler procedures use register passing to initialize and later remove a pre-memory, cache-based stack on all processor cores. Initialization divides and globally maps stack regions, configures x86-64 MTRRs, sets SS:ESP according to processor mode, and creates UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF. It may return success, a stack-reentry warning, or a fatal unknown-family error. AARCH64 PSP systems instead initialize DRAM. Removal occurs once main memory and a relocated stack are available, disables CAR without changing MCRRs, and preserves EBX.

The study assessed Faculty of Industrial Education students’ readiness, expertise, and needs for creating educational multimedia. Multimedia was defined as integrating text, images, sound, animation, video, and newer technologies such as augmented reality, virtual reality, and the metaverse to support engaging and effective learning.

Using interviews, literature review, and an online survey, researchers examined teaching contexts and multimedia skills among a randomly selected sample of 124 students in several engineering and technical education programmes. Students showed high readiness to create multimedia, most commonly using notebooks and smartphones. Their overall multimedia expertise was rated high (mean 3.51), while their need for multimedia learning materials was rated at the highest level (mean 4.62). Expertise was comparatively lower in areas including copyright and educational metaverse creation, where learning needs were greater.

The findings indicate that students are more confident in areas where they have prior experience and require targeted resources in less familiar areas. The study recommends strengthening future teachers’ technological and multimedia production abilities. Its limited sample size and population diversity constrain generalisability and suggest a need for broader future research.

A May 24, 2001 news compilation focuses largely on California’s energy crisis. Gov. Gray Davis considered paying businesses to use highly polluting backup diesel generators during severe shortages, drawing environmental and public-health objections. Davis also planned longer advance notice of blackouts and was scheduled to meet President George W. Bush amid disputes over federal price controls.

California regulators reported evidence that generators manipulated plant output to maximize prices, while energy companies cited legitimate operational and financial reasons. Reliant offered lower electricity prices if pollution restrictions were eased, and El Paso Merchant denied manipulating natural-gas prices.

Other reports examined the potential impact of Sen. James Jeffords leaving the Republican Party, declining public approval of officials’ energy responses, Antonio Villaraigosa’s legislative career, and a commentary criticizing California officials’ attacks on Texas energy companies.

Florida International University reopened Monday after a pedestrian bridge collapsed four days earlier, killing six people, including student Alexa Duran. The university planned a moment of silence and a Wednesday vigil. Authorities recovered four vehicles and five victims’ remains, while a sixth victim died at the hospital. Federal investigators continued gathering evidence, and nearby Southwest Eighth Street remained closed indefinitely.

Teacher Caroline Hope, 37, died in Glasgow after contracting E. coli during colon cancer surgery in Turkey. Family and friends raised over £31,000 for her medical evacuation to Scotland. Her mother thanked donors and hospital staff, saying Caroline was grateful to return home.

North Carolina’s 140-parts-per-trillion GenX health goal aims to prevent non-cancer effects, including endocrine disruption, thyroid disease and reproductive problems. Cancer evidence remains limited. A GenX forum is scheduled August 16 at UNCW’s Lumina Theater.

Texas A&M’s Christian Kirk poses a major challenge for favored Alabama as an elite receiver and returner. In two games against Alabama, he has 16 catches for 148 yards, a receiving touchdown and a 68-yard punt-return score. Alabama defenders emphasized tracking Kirk and tackling effectively to limit his explosive plays.

Hong Kong and Singapore have seen a sharp rise in initial coin offerings after China and South Korea banned them in September. Companies are relocating token sales to these loosely regulated markets to reduce legal risks. Chinese firms such as Xender and South Korean companies including Bithumb and Zikto are pursuing ICOs through Singapore-based entities. Industry figures attribute much of the increase to restrictions in the issuers’ home countries.

The RIAA has certified 179 songs diamond, requiring at least 10 million equivalent sales and streaming units plus an artist or label application. Elton John’s “Something About the Way You Look Tonight / Candle in the Wind” was the first, certified in 1997, while Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” was the most recent on September 15, 2025. Drake leads artists with 10 diamond singles, followed by Post Malone with nine; Rihanna holds the female-artist record with seven. The chronological list spans releases from Queen, Michael Jackson, and Whitney Houston to The Weeknd, Katy Perry, Bruno Mars, and other contemporary artists.

Russian cosmonauts Alexander Misurkin and Anton Shkaplerov completed a record 8-hour, 13-minute Russian spacewalk to replace an obsolete electronics box and upgrade an International Space Station communications antenna. The antenna remained operational but became stuck 180 degrees beyond its intended position, prompting Russian officials to assess whether further action was needed. The discarded 60-pound electronics box was safely thrown away and will eventually burn up in Earth’s atmosphere. The spacewalk exceeded the previous Russian record but remained shorter than NASA’s nearly nine-hour world record.

If a SanDisk SSD is not recognized, disconnect other USB devices because the computer may not supply enough power. Clone the existing HDD to the SSD using preferred cloning software, selecting the internal drive as the source and the SSD as the destination. After cloning, shut down the computer, disconnect power, and remove a notebook battery. For notebooks, transfer required brackets or adapters, align and connect the SSD in the SATA drive bay, reassemble, and restart. For desktops, open the case, disconnect and remove the HDD, install the SSD—using a 3.5-inch mounting adapter if required—and reconnect SATA data and power cables. The old HDD may be retained as a backup. Installation videos, SSD information, and warranty details are available on SanDisk’s website.

Bills running back James Cook has 401 rushing yards, five touchdowns and three consecutive 100-yard games after signing a $48 million contract. Josh Allen said the deal may have helped Cook play more freely, calling him an “all-time teammate” who deserved his contract. Buffalo is 4-0 and can improve to 3-0 in the AFC East by defeating the Patriots in Week 5.

Apple’s fiscal first-quarter 2020 net sales rose 9% year over year to $91.8 billion, while net income increased to $22.2 billion and diluted earnings per share reached $4.99. Growth was driven primarily by iPhone, Wearables, Home and Accessories, and Services; Mac and iPad sales declined. Americas and Europe sales grew 12% and 14%, respectively, while Japan declined 10%.

Gross margin was $35.2 billion, or 38.4% of sales, and operating income was $25.6 billion. Operating cash flow totaled $30.5 billion. At December 28, 2019, Apple reported $340.6 billion in assets, $207.1 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, $251.1 billion in liabilities, and $89.5 billion in shareholders’ equity.

Apple repurchased $20.0 billion of stock and paid $3.5 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents. It had $103.1 billion in outstanding term-note principal and $5.0 billion in commercial paper. The company adopted new lease and hedging standards, recording $7.5 billion of right-of-use assets and $8.1 billion of lease liabilities upon lease-standard adoption. Disclosed contingencies included tax, competition, iPhone performance-management, and VirnetX matters.

Trump administration directives, Education Department reductions, rescinded guidance, proposed 2026 budget cuts, and immigration enforcement fears are disrupting services for more than 5 million English learners in public schools. Schools have canceled teacher training, closed or consolidated newcomer centers, suspended hiring, reduced translation, tutoring, family engagement, adult ESL classes, supplies, and other support.

Advocates warn that Oklahoma could lose $6.4 million and Virginia $17.5 million, affecting multilingual learners and broader school resources. Reduced federal monitoring may leave states responsible for ensuring legal obligations are met.

Educators report that immigrant students and families increasingly avoid questions or decline services because they fear identification and deportation. One Texas district consolidated newcomer programs after enrollment fell from 250 students across nine high schools to fewer than 30, reassigning most teachers. An Indianapolis school reported only two newcomers this year, compared with 10 previously.

Teachers and researchers say cuts eliminate trusted staff and programs that help immigrant families navigate schools, obtain language assistance, and acclimate. They also fear losing bilingual educators recruited from immigrant communities, worsening staffing shortages and reducing academic opportunities.

The Gold Overnight strategy seeks to capture overnight price movements by buying gold futures, GLD, GDX, or GDXJ at the market close and selling at the next open. Such movements may reflect changes in global economic conditions, interest rates, political events, and market sentiment.

Backtests showed GDX averaging a 0.12% overnight gain, compared with a 0.09% average intraday loss. GLD produced an 8.4% annual overnight return versus 8.2% for buy-and-hold, averaging 0.04% per trade, while its average intraday gain was nearly zero. These small gains may not be directly tradable.

An incubated long overnight strategy recorded 741 trades averaging 0.17%, or 0.11% since 2012. An incubated GDX short overnight strategy recorded 205 trades averaging 0.7%. Both use three variables.

The strategy involves substantial risk and volatility because gold prices are unpredictable and influenced by numerous external factors. Execution requires defined entry and exit rules, market analysis, discipline, patience, emotional control, stop-loss and profit-taking orders, cautious leverage, appropriate position sizing, a risk-reward framework, and diversification. The authors consider commodities, including gold and gold miners, harder to trade than stocks because strategies may lose effectiveness and are generally less robust.

The passage introduces the May 2018 ebook edition of the 1894 Foreign Relations of the United States, designed to preserve original content while enabling offline access, search, bookmarking, and note-taking. It recommends citing persistent document numbers rather than page numbers. Included are 1893 messages from President Benjamin Harrison and Secretary of State John W. Foster transmitting to the Senate an uncompleted 1854 treaty draft with Hawaii, related correspondence, and a report covering United States–Hawaiian relations from 1820 to 1893.

Research from Yale’s Budget Lab and the Brookings Institution found no discernible U.S. job disruption linked to AI since ChatGPT launched in November 2022. Occupational shifts largely began earlier, and employment changes do not correlate clearly with AI exposure, automation, or augmentation. Recent graduates face somewhat greater difficulty finding work, but the data does not establish AI as the main cause. Researchers cautioned that the analysis has a small sample and is not predictive; future effects may emerge as AI improves and companies integrate it more effectively.

Some companies, including Shopify and Cloudflare, are expanding internships, viewing AI as a tool that can increase new hires’ contributions. Other AI developments include Meta’s plan to use AI chatbot conversations for personalized ads and recommendations, without an opt-out for users; Thinking Machines Lab’s launch of Tinker for creating customized frontier models; and OpenAI’s release of Sora 2, which generates video, audio, and user “cameos” but requires copyright owners to opt out.

Periodic Labs raised $300 million and recruited researchers from major AI companies to develop AI-assisted scientific discovery using robotic experiments. Meanwhile, 72% of S&P 500 companies disclosed AI-related risks in 2025, up from 12% in 2023. Reputational and cybersecurity concerns were most frequently cited, with particularly sharp increases in financial services, health care, and industrial companies.

Stroke treatment is time-sensitive. The American Stroke Association’s FAST mnemonic identifies major warning signs: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, and Time to call 911. Call even if symptoms disappear, and note when they began. Another mnemonic, STR, advises asking the person to Smile, Talk, and Raise both arms; difficulty with any action warrants an emergency call.

Enron faced intensified scrutiny over complex off-balance-sheet partnerships and management-linked transactions. A $35 million purchase from Chewco Investments, managed by former Enron executive Michael Kopper, appeared connected to transactions that kept substantial JEDI partnership debt off Enron’s balance sheet. The SEC opened a formal investigation, while questions arose about the adequacy and clarity of Enron’s disclosures and auditor Arthur Andersen’s oversight.

Short seller James Chanos identified warning signs in Enron’s filings, including low returns, related-party dealings, insider stock sales and dependence on investor trust. Enron’s shares had fallen 86% during 2001. The AFL-CIO and other shareholders called for broader governance reforms and review of insider transactions.

Facing credit downgrades and declining confidence, Enron considered asset sales. Its Indian subsidiary began valuing the Dabhol power project ahead of possible contract termination, while lenders examined bids for Enron’s 65% stake. Enron also discussed selling its 50% interest in a Korean natural-gas venture with SK Corp.

SOS low-post defense prioritizes aggressive post fronting to limit interior passes, touches, and shots. The post defender occupies the passing lane, maintains physical contact, and pushes the opponent toward the three-second area. On lob passes, the low Helpside I defender double-teams while teammates rotate to deny passes, cover open players, and restore matchups. All rotations begin as the ball leaves the passer’s hands.

The main trapping options are:

- **Base Go:** The primary low-post double team. The post defender forces the receiver toward the baseline, and the low Helpside I defender rotates along the baseline to trap.
- **Go Top:** A secondary option used when fronting is difficult or the post tends to turn toward the middle. The post defender forces middle, where the high Helpside I defender traps.
- **Go Wing:** Used when the wing is a poor outside shooter or the post defender is caught behind. The wing defender follows the entry pass to double-team the post.
- **Hold:** Designed to prevent open three-point shots. The post defender plays one-on-one with three-quarter denial while the other defenders stay home and aggressively deny kick-out passes.
- **Yo-Yo:** When the wing passer is not an outside threat, that defender may sag into a post double team, then close out quickly if the ball returns to the wing.

After passes out of traps, defenders close out, deny return passes, protect Helpside I positions, front the post, and direct ball handlers toward sideline, corner, or baseline checkpoints. Sound individual post defense remains essential and is supplemented by coordinated traps.

From 1881, U.S. officials maintained that Hawaii could not grant other powers privileges reserved to the United States under the 1875 treaty and pledged support for Hawaii’s treaty obligations. Blaine described Hawaiian neutrality as essential to American Pacific interests and stated that, if neutrality became impracticable, the United States would seek an American solution. In 1883, however, the United States declined Hawaii’s request to protest British and French territorial expansion in Polynesia. Negotiations extended the reciprocity treaty for seven years and granted the United States exclusive access to Pearl River Harbor for a coaling and repair station. Although concluded in 1884, the convention was not ratified until 1887 because of U.S. sugar-industry and congressional opposition; Britain also opposed it. General Schofield had recommended acquiring Pearl River Harbor in 1873. Beginning in 1884, proposals considered an ocean cable linking Australia, Hawaii, and North America. Hawaiian legislation authorized a subsidy, while disputes arose over U.S. or British Columbian landings and exclusive privileges. In 1891–92, the U.S.S. Albatross surveyed a cable route from Monterey Bay to Honolulu.

On World Wetlands Day, Beignet, a permitted pet nutria and educational mascot in South Louisiana, did not see his shadow, predicting a hurricane-free season. Meanwhile, Punxsutawney Phil predicted six more weeks of winter.

Children’s mobile phone ownership varies widely by country, age and culture. Sara Zaske’s daughter rarely wanted a phone while attending school in Berlin, where few classmates owned smartphones, but requested one after becoming the only fourth-grader in her California class without one. Her parents plan to provide a flip phone before allowing a smartphone in high school.

Studies reported that 46% of European children ages 9 to 16 owned smartphones, with differences in school restrictions, classroom use and affordability. In the United States, 45% of children ages 10 to 12 had smartphones with service plans, while 42% of children 8 and younger owned tablets. Smartphone ownership reached 72% among South Korean children ages 11 to 12. Ownership and access also varied across Taiwan, Turkey, South Africa, Ghana, Malawi and Australia, generally increasing with age and over time.

The American Academy of Pediatrics says there is no single right age for a child’s first phone. It recommends avoiding regular digital media for children younger than 18 to 24 months except video chatting, limiting screen time for ages 2 to 5 to one hour daily, monitoring content, and keeping screens away from meals and the hour before bedtime.

The author describes cryopreservation, in which bodies are treated with antifreeze and stored in liquid nitrogen at -196C in hopes of future revival. About 2,000 people have paid for the procedure, including whole-body or head-only preservation, while celebrities have expressed interest. Citing the lack of scientific support for reviving frozen brains or bodies, the author argues that cryonics companies exploit fear of death through deceitful and extortionate promises of immortality.

Since 1900, the ten best-performing stock markets have been Australia, the United States, South Africa, New Zealand, Denmark, Sweden, Canada, Finland, Switzerland, and the Netherlands. Australia ranked first, delivering real annual returns above 6.5% in U.S. dollars. Dividends accounted for 53% of its total market gains, while its banking sector, service economy, commodity exports, regulatory environment, and limited World War II damage also supported performance.

The United States returned about 6.5% annually after inflation, turning $1 invested in 1900 into $3,806 by 2019. South African stocks averaged 7.2% locally and 6.4% in U.S. dollars, while New Zealand returned 6.4%. Denmark ranked fifth despite prolonged poor performance during much of the twentieth century.

From 1900 to 2019, global stocks produced real annualized returns of 5.2%, compared with 2% for bonds and 0.8% for Treasury bills. Stocks benefited from economic rebuilding, productivity growth, technological innovation, and lower interest rates. Their advantages include potential returns, inflation protection, dividend income, liquidity, ownership, diversification, and low starting costs.

However, only a small fraction of stocks generated overall market gains, while most underperformed Treasury bills. Markets also experience frequent and sometimes severe declines, and past performance does not guarantee future results.

International Development Secretary Penny Mordaunt became the first minister to use sign language in Parliament. She highlighted London’s upcoming Global Disability Summit, organised with Kenya and the International Disability Alliance, which aims to promote inclusion and support for disabled people in poorer countries.

South Korean prosecutors raided Korean Air’s headquarters while investigating alleged tax evasion, embezzlement and breach of trust involving Chairman Cho Yang-ho and his family. Authorities are examining inheritance taxes, overseas assets and suspicious financial flows. The investigation follows controversies involving Cho’s daughters and public pressure that prompted him to leave a leadership role at affiliate Jin Air.

In 1999, Robin Chase and Antje Danielson conceived Zipcar as a technology-enabled car-sharing service offering urban residents convenient access to vehicles. Drawing on her quantitative training, entrepreneurial network, advisers, and lessons from existing car-sharing organizations, Chase developed the company’s team, technology, operations, financing, and pricing model. Zipcar launched in Cambridge and Boston in June 2000 with four cars, emphasizing a smart, urban brand and direct customer communication.

Despite favorable press, growing membership, and plans to close a $1.3 million funding round, October data revealed that Zipcar’s business model was not viable. Vehicle utilization and revenue per trip were roughly half Chase’s projections, largely because daily rentals represented more revenue than expected at an underpriced rate. The analysis indicated that daily prices needed to rise 20% for the company to break even. Chase faced opposition from colleagues who feared that changing promised prices would appear deceptive, alienate customers, and jeopardize financing, while maintaining existing prices would leave the company financially unsustainable.

Montreal topped the 2017 QS Best Student Cities ranking, displacing Paris after four years, while London rose to third. Rankings assess university quality, affordability, student facilities, desirability, employer access, international character, tolerance, pollution and safety.

Canada’s bilingual education, desirability and growing international enrolment may help it gain students amid concerns over US entry rules. Vancouver ranked 10th and Toronto joint 11th. Germany also placed two cities in the top 10, supported by tuition-free education for overseas students.

Seoul rose to fourth, leading five Asian cities in the top 20. Kuala Lumpur and Surabaya were most affordable, while Stockholm and New York were most expensive. The ranking highlights intense competition for international students, who contribute nearly $36 billion annually to the US economy.

The team believes it has played well despite unfavorable bounces and misleading scores. It plans to create more traffic, capitalize on chances, and keep pushing shift by shift. Players remain confident they can overcome the opponent’s outstanding goalie through hard work and teamwork.

The United States supports France’s recovery of Alsace-Lorraine as important to French recovery and ending German militarism, but would not insist if France accepted a compromise. Italy merits border adjustments balancing defense and nationality; Trieste should remain commercially free with cultural autonomy, while broader Adriatic ambitions lack justification. A Balkan settlement should reject the Treaty of Bucharest, restore Serbia and Montenegro, evacuate occupied states, and balance national and economic interests through impartial inquiry. Tentative proposals include returning Bulgarian areas, restoring specified Bulgarian boundaries and Aegean access, providing Serbia access through Saloniki, further studying Macedonia, and questioning Albanian independence. Economic prosperity is considered central to Balkan stability. An independent democratic Poland should be established with boundaries balancing national and economic needs and adequate maritime access. Complete Polish unification is considered impractical, while dependence on German waterways, vulnerability to Germany, and tensions among Poles, Ruthenians, and Jews make democratic government essential.

Lincolnshire County Council leader Martin Hill urged health bosses to publish future service plans after ULHT was rated “requires improvement” and remained in special measures, despite 72% of inspected areas receiving “good” ratings. He cited recruitment, children’s services and concerns at Lincoln and Boston. The delayed £1.2 million STP is expected in 2019. Lincoln was rated “requires improvement,” Boston “inadequate,” and Grantham and Louth “good.”

Consilium Software announced worldwide availability of UniRSM on Cisco SolutionsPlus as a replacement for Cisco’s end-of-sale Remote Silent Monitoring product. Designed for Cisco Unified CCE and Packaged CCE, UniRSM enables supervisors to remotely monitor and coach contact center agents by dialing in from any phone without connecting to the Cisco network. Improvements include architecture without RTSP reliance, whisper coaching, multiple-call monitoring, high availability and failover, Cisco VVB support, web-based reporting and administration, and Windows and Linux compatibility. Developed with Cisco product engineering participation, UniRSM is available through Cisco Commerce and the Global Price List. SolutionsPlus allows customers to order approved, tested third-party products through Cisco sales teams and partners, while vendors provide service and support.

The team needs greater initiative, especially on the penalty kill, by disrupting Carolina’s forecheck and entries rather than allowing extended offensive-zone setups. Improvements in blocked shots, giveaways, takeaways, and other small details are considered essential. Players should avoid trying to do too much in the Stanley Cup Finals and instead trust their normal games. Rem’s recovery and contribution were described as meaningful. The team also aims to limit opponents’ advantages on faceoffs, particularly on home ice.

U.S. stocks continue rising on AI and technology gains, but record valuations and market concentration are increasing investor caution. The S&P 500 is up about 15% this year and the Nasdaq nearly 19%, while the S&P’s forward price-to-earnings ratio of 23 exceeds its 10-year average of 18.7. The IMF and Jamie Dimon warn of correction risks, though Goldman Sachs cites strong earnings and productivity. High call-option volumes signal exuberance. Federal Reserve easing expectations and softer inflation support optimism, while upcoming earnings and central bank guidance may determine whether valuations are sustainable.

An informal review of 13 CFD brokers found that 62% to 82% of retail CFD traders lose money, with Interactive Brokers reporting the lowest proportion. CFD trading is generally unprofitable for most participants, though a minority of disciplined traders may profit through effective risk management, lower transaction costs, and proven strategies.

CFDs are leveraged derivatives in which gains correspond to another party’s losses. Leverage magnifies both profits and losses, while spreads, overnight fees, widening spreads during volatility, illiquidity, and price gaps increase costs and risks. Many CFD traders are undercapitalized, inexperienced retail participants without trading plans. The passage concludes that these factors make consistent CFD profitability unlikely.

Trump’s recognition of Jerusalem as Israel’s capital was condemned internationally and by the Arab League. An interviewed expert argued that the United States was never neutral, while Trump sought support from Jewish Zionists within the American establishment. The expert described the Arab League as weak and expected an Islamic summit in Istanbul to clarify regional responses. Trump’s decision was portrayed as exposing the Israeli-Palestinian peace process as a sham, though it had not yet produced major changes on the ground. The passage highlights Palestinians’ limited residency rights in Jerusalem, which can be revoked. It also notes UN Security Council Resolution 478 rejected Israel’s 1980 Jerusalem law and East Jerusalem’s annexation. The expert considered the two-state solution nearly dead and advocated equal rights in Palestine.

The patent application describes systems and methods for protecting and managing enterprise data, particularly changed-block tracking (CBT) for incremental and differential backups in cloud or virtualized environments that lack native CBT support, such as OpenStack. Images of a virtual machine disk generated at different times are compared to identify changed blocks and create a location map. A virtual server agent uses the map to extract and back up those blocks in a format supported by the information management system, reducing processing and storage requirements compared with full-disk comparisons or backups.

The broader information management system may include client computing devices, primary and secondary storage, a centralized storage manager, application-specific data agents, media agents, virtual machines, hypervisors, and communication networks. The storage manager coordinates operations, policies, scheduling, monitoring, recovery, indexing, retention, reporting, and resource allocation. Data agents process application data for protection or restoration, while media agents manage data transfer, indexing, and access to secondary storage. Components may be distributed, consolidated, scaled, load-balanced, or configured for failover.

Primary data is live production data stored in native formats, while secondary copies support recovery, compliance, analysis, retention, and storage management. Information management operations include full, differential, incremental, synthetic full, file-level, volume-level, and block-level backups; archives; snapshots; replication; deduplication; auxiliary copies; restoration; and information lifecycle or hierarchical storage management. Secondary copies may be compressed, encrypted, deduplicated, indexed, stored remotely or on lower-cost media, and retained according to policies.

The Ravens fell to 1-3 after a 37-20 loss to the Chiefs, putting their playoff hopes in danger. CBS Sports’ John Breech graded Baltimore an “F,” criticizing a defense that did not force a punt until the fourth quarter. Lamar Jackson committed two turnovers before leaving with a hamstring injury. Baltimore, third in its division, needs a rapid turnaround and two wins before its bye week to reach 3-3 and remain competitive.

Tarik Skubal tied Detroit’s postseason record with a career-high 14 strikeouts, allowing one run and three hits over 7⅔ innings as the Tigers beat Cleveland 2-1 in Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series. Detroit’s bullpen escaped a tense ninth inning, putting the Tigers one win from advancing to the division series. Cleveland’s two errors contributed to both unearned Detroit runs.

Investigating officer Sergeant Marlon Appollis told the Western Cape High Court that he found no suicide note, object to stand on, footprints or fingerprints supporting the initial belief that Susan Rohde hanged herself in a Spier hotel room in July 2016. He found a note suggesting her husband, Jason Rohde, was involved in an extramarital affair. After an autopsy indicated Susan died from manual strangulation, Appollis changed the case to murder and identified Rohde as a possible suspect. Rohde, who denies murdering his wife and staging her suicide, had returned to Johannesburg before becoming a suspect. The trial was postponed to allow the defence to prepare for evidence concerning whether the bathroom door hook could support Susan’s approximate weight of 51kg.

Amazon entered an amended and restated credit agreement with JPMorgan Chase Bank and other lenders on June 23, 2020, extending its revolving credit facility through June 23, 2023. Borrowings will support general corporate purposes, including backing notes issued under Amazon’s commercial paper program. The agreement replaces the prior April 27, 2018 agreement and is filed as Exhibit 10.1.

Tesla filed a Form 8-K on October 23, 2019, announcing financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2019. Its Third Quarter 2019 Update was posted online and attached as Exhibit 99.1. CFO Zachary J. Kirkhorn signed the report.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, supporting buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies. Their transconductance error amplifier compares VSENSE with the lower of SS or the 0.613-V reference; output voltage is programmed by a resistor divider. A capacitor on SS controls gradual startup, with synchronous rectifier outputs activating above 1 V.

Switching frequency can be set from 100 kHz to 2 MHz by an RT resistor, synchronized to an external 200-kHz-to-4-MHz clock, or shared between primary and secondary controllers. In primary-secondary operation, the secondary inverts the clock, producing a 90° or 270° output phase shift. Primary and synchronous-rectifier outputs have about 150-mA peak capability, so external gate drivers are recommended.

Depending on device, dead time and leading-edge blanking are fixed or resistor-programmable. Pulse skipping addresses minimum-on-time limitations when COMP is below 0.3 V and the preceding duty cycle is below 25%. Supported maximum duty-cycle settings are 50%, 75%, or 100%; OUTB and SRB operate only with compatible devices at the 50% setting.

CS_ILIM provides peak-current control and overcurrent detection. At 1.05 V, cycle-by-cycle limiting begins and charges the HICC capacitor; reaching 0.6 V stops switching and discharges SS, followed by a timed restart when HICC falls to 0.3 V. External faults above 0.6 V also stop switching, with restart after the fault clears and an approximately 15-cycle delay. Thermal shutdown occurs at 175°C and restart at 160°C. Programmable slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation, while Type 2A or 2B compensation can stabilize the control loop.

A TPS7H5001-SP synchronous push-pull GaN design example uses 500-kHz switching, 5-V output, approximately 25-ns dead time, 50-ns leading-edge blanking, 7.5-ms soft start, a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 0.47-µH output inductance, and about 2.3 mF output capacitance. It selects 170-V primary and 80-V synchronous GaN FETs, a 7.5-Ω current-sense resistor for roughly 35-A limiting, a 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, Type 2A compensation, and a 102-kΩ slope-compensation resistor.

The controllers operate from 4 V to 14 V and require at least 0.1 µF input bypassing. Layout guidance emphasizes short high-current loops, minimized switch-node copper, separation of analog and power grounds with a single connection point, close placement of bypass, sensing, and compensation components, and routing sensitive signals away from switching outputs, magnetics, and SYNC.

This study sequenced and characterized 12 SARS-CoV-2 genomes from patients in Esteio, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, collected between April and June 2021, and compared them with genomes from state and global databases. Ten samples belonged to lineage P.1 and two to P.1.17, both within the Gamma variant. Across the 12 genomes, 68 nucleotide substitutions were identified, including 36 nonsynonymous mutations. Several mutations were reported for the first time in Rio Grande do Sul; NSP3:D1208A was newly reported in Brazil, and NSP12:I136V had not previously been described in GISAID.

Analysis of 4,706 state genomes collected from March 2020 through May 2022 showed successive predominance of B.1.1.33, Zeta, Gamma, Delta, and Omicron lineages. Gamma represented 57.1% of sequenced genomes in 2021, Delta 32.3%, and Omicron exceeded 90% between January and April 2022. Sequenced genomes represented approximately 0.19% of reported state cases. Phylogenomic analyses supported distinct clades for major variants and placed all 12 study genomes within Gamma.

Selection analyses of the E, M, and N structural proteins found no positively selected sites in E, two in M, and 14 in N. Negative selection affected two E sites, 12 M sites, and 46 N sites. Protein-stability modeling indicated that selected mutations could have stabilizing or destabilizing effects; M:H125L/Y and N:D63Y produced the largest predicted stabilizing changes, while most evaluated C-terminal N mutations were destabilizing. The authors conclude that further studies are needed to determine how these structural changes affect SARS-CoV-2 host interactions.

Wisconsin’s frack sand industry has rebounded as domestic crude production increased, reviving idled mines and strengthening demand. New Texas mines will add competition, but analysts expect growing demand and differences in sand quality to protect Wisconsin’s market. Northern white sand prices may rise 10–12 percent this year.

Stanford researchers developed “biofilm lithography,” using genetically engineered E. coli that secrete a sticky protein under blue light to create patterned biofilms overnight. The method produces designs at 25-micrometer resolution and offers speed, simplicity, and compatibility with surfaces including closed microfluidic devices. It may help researchers study spatial interactions within bacterial communities and develop synthetic communities, biomaterials, microfluidic systems, or biofilm circuits. Sharp patterns observed during testing suggested bacteria continually attach to and detach from culture surfaces rather than freely swimming throughout the dish. The team is working to pattern multiple bacterial strains simultaneously, including studying how biofilm bacteria share antibiotic resistance.

This protocol describes a three-arm randomized controlled trial evaluating Digital-MindCAN, an eight-week, real-time videotelephony mindfulness psychoeducation program tailored to cancer survivors in Singapore. The study will recruit 150 adults aged 21–65 with stage 0–III cancer who completed curative treatment between two weeks and two years earlier. Participants will be assigned equally to Digital-MindCAN plus standard care, Palouse Mindfulness plus standard care, or a wait-list control.

Both interventions comprise eight weekly 90-minute group sessions and daily home practice. Digital-MindCAN integrates cancer-specific education with mindfulness practices, while Palouse Mindfulness provides general stress reduction without cancer-specific content. The study will assess whether Digital-MindCAN is superior to wait-list control and non-inferior to Palouse Mindfulness.

Primary outcomes are objective and subjective stress. Secondary outcomes include psychological well-being, relaxation, mindfulness, resilience, depression, and anxiety. Data will be collected through questionnaires, skin temperature, heart rate, oxygen saturation, practice records, and post-intervention focus groups. Psychological outcomes will be assessed at baseline, after sessions four and eight; objective stress and relaxation will be measured around intervention sessions.

Quantitative analyses will use intention-to-treat methods, covariance analysis, and repeated-measures analysis of variance. Focus-group data will undergo realist analysis. The study received ethical approval and is registered as ISRCTN10756933. Positive findings could support incorporating Digital-MindCAN into standard cancer-survivor care and testing it in other institutions or digital formats.

The team improved its defensive quickness, net-front protection, composure, and puck movement after rushing plays and being outplayed previously. Dallas’s heat and westward travel were viewed as potential advantages. A scoring play developed through patience at the blue line, allowing teammates to drive toward the net for a shot and tip. The team expects the same line matchup for the rest of the series and believes it can manage it better in Dallas. Embarrassed by its prior performance, the team responded without blaming individuals, focusing instead on personal responsibility, emotion, urgency, skating, and checking.

The study examined preschool teachers’ views and classroom practices concerning sensory education. Using a qualitative phenomenological design, researchers conducted semi-structured, 30-minute interviews with 20 preschool teachers selected through maximum-diversity sampling. Content analysis produced 81 codes organized into nine categories and three themes: the importance of sensory education, its relationship with the preschool curriculum, and related difficulties and limitations.

Teachers considered sensory education essential in early childhood and beneficial across developmental areas. They recommended planned activities, suitable materials, enriched environments, early intervention, play-based experiences, family support, and teacher training. Although teachers reported incorporating visual, auditory, tactile, musical, artistic, experimental, dramatic, and balance activities into daily routines, most focused on five senses rather than all seven, and some confused “sense” with “emotion.”

Participants generally believed the preschool curriculum contained sensory-related outcomes and concepts but did not address sensory education clearly or sufficiently. They evaluated activities mainly through observation, developmental forms, questions, children’s responses, and family cooperation. Family participation included seminars, individual meetings, classroom or home activities, and stronger parent-teacher communication.

Major barriers included inadequate materials, unfavorable school and classroom conditions, limited time, and insufficient teacher competence in addressing sensory integration problems. Most teachers wanted additional training. The study recommends in-service training, occupational therapist support, better-equipped classrooms, greater coverage of sensory education in undergraduate programs, and jointly developed sample activities.

CMD42 requires sufficient block length and valid password parameters; otherwise results are undefined or errors occur. Password length must be 1–128 bits. Execution errors set LOCK_UNLOCK_FAILED, while CARD_IS_LOCKED reflects the resulting lock state, observable through CMD13.

An MRI indicated a third-degree, or slightly less severe, MCL injury expected to heal relatively quickly. The goalie injured his knee when a collision at the net wedged him against the post, but said the play was not a penalty and defenseman Mark Andre was not at fault. Though frustrated to miss time during the Stanley Cup playoffs, he remains confident in goalies Ty and Jussi, plans to support them with tailored advice, and believes the team will rally around the adversity.

Agilent Technologies shares rose about 22% in a month, but the author rates them “avoid” because their valuation appears optimistic relative to modest revenue and earnings growth.
