Positives include shareholder-friendly management, dividend growth, a shrinking share count, manageable debt, substantial cash, and improved recent results. However, projected 6% dividend growth implies an estimated four-year annual return of only 6.7%, which the author considers inadequate given risks from fluctuating customer research budgets, economic conditions, government policies, and spending priorities.

The technical outlook would turn bearish below $58.50, with a potential decline to $53 and a stop-loss above $60.50. Agilent trades at a 15% premium to the overall market and near the high end of its recent range despite limited growth. The author may initiate a short position using put options.

External Affairs Minister Sushma Swaraj sought a report from India’s High Commission in Pakistan after Sikh leader Charnjit Singh was shot dead in Peshawar. Singh, an interfaith activist and Taliban critic, was reportedly killed in a targeted attack. Sukhbir Singh Badal urged India to raise concerns about Sikh safety with Pakistan.

The speaker credited a comeback win to confidence, momentum and improved third-period play but stressed that the team had skated poorly, taken too many penalties and must improve throughout a seven-game Stanley Cup Final. The goaltender played outstandingly, while the disputed penalty shot remained unclear after video review. The team believes in continuing to attack when trailing, using its offensive depth and never quitting, though it cannot depend on repeated comebacks.

The opponent was described as physical, talented and defensively strong, with effective goaltending and penalty killing. Preparation included studying its systems, special teams, forecheck and faceoffs, while maintaining a primary focus on improving the team’s own execution. The speaker highlighted the roster’s depth, power play, experienced deadline acquisitions and close locker-room culture. Despite concerns about the quality of play, the immediate priority was securing four Final wins. Once the puck drops, the speaker said success depends on execution and effort.

Washington Prime Group shares fell 0.27%, closing at $7.51. Three analysts set an average 12-month price target of $6.77, ranging from $6 to $7.50. Recommendations included two Holds and one Underperform, with no Buy, Outperform, or Sell ratings; its average brokerage recommendation was 4, and its industry ranked 173 of 265. The stock’s 14-period Average True Range was 0.25, with weekly volatility of 2.76% and monthly volatility of 3.38%. Its Relative Strength Index was 65.19. Washington Prime had a $1.41 billion market capitalization and 187.31 million outstanding shares. Previous trading volume was 3.62 million shares, compared with an average of 3.47 million.

The disputed play appeared inconclusive, but the speaker trusts Toronto and the referees. Despite one poor statistical game, he strongly supports Pekks and expects him to rebound. He also credits Milwaukee’s coaches and organization with developing players and helping him mature on and off the ice.

The speaker says the team gained confidence by giving itself a chance to win through disciplined, five-man play, strong back pressure, defensive support and reliable goaltending. Against Detroit’s speed and scoring ability, keeping the game close and avoiding changes to their straightforward four-line system are essential. The team expects Detroit’s best effort and plans to maintain the same approach, possibly with shorter shifts.

Playing in his hometown created nerves and distractions, so he emphasized staying focused with teammates. He praised captain Ron Francis’s class and leadership, said younger players benefit from not fully feeling the pressure, and stressed that the team plays for one another rather than worrying about respect or attention. He also noted Detroit’s size, puck control and net-front play, saying perfection is unrealistic against such a potent opponent. Early nerves eased as the game progressed.
A premature newborn from a faith-healing family died without medical care in Oregon City, while her twin survived after treatment. Authorities are investigating; no charges have been filed.

Martin Brodeur said he is enjoying the playoff run despite wanting more Finals success. With the team still alive, he emphasized creating offensive space by driving players to the net and building on their latest win. He said the team must keep playing hard, take things day by day, and make life difficult for its opponent. Brodeur feels less pressure than earlier in his career and values time away with family to help him focus on game days.

The study examines four higher education projects created or relocated abroad by Russian academics after Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine and subsequent academic repression. It treats these initiatives as forms of “education in emergencies” operating outside the conflict zone and explores how they define their relationship to Russia, their purposes in exile, and their anticipated futures.

The projects range from informal online education to accredited degree programs. Using semi-structured interviews with project leaders and discourse analysis of public materials, the study identifies three main forms of self-conceptualisation. First, the projects function as “safe havens,” offering intellectual freedom, teaching opportunities, scholarships, visa assistance, and educational pathways for scholars and students leaving Russia. They also provide communities that preserve academic and professional identities during displacement.

Second, the projects seek to preserve academic traditions, Russian-language scholarship, research practices, and institutional networks damaged by censorship and repression. Some collaborate with international universities to reconsider this heritage, but the study finds that such reconceptualisation remains limited. Existing models, including liberal arts education and hierarchical teaching methods, are often reproduced despite their possible limitations within authoritarian or postwar contexts.

Third, the projects embody “hope-making praxis.” Although participants retain hopes of returning, they emphasize feasible action in the present rather than passively awaiting political change. Through education and international collaboration, they aim to support social transformation and contribute to a democratic future. However, their visions require further scrutiny regarding inherited biases, colonial assumptions, accessibility, and excluded groups.

The study concludes that relocated higher education projects extend beyond knowledge production by providing sanctuary, preserving academic legacies, and sustaining hope through practical action. It recommends further research on institutional and geographical differences, international influences, gaps between declared goals and teaching practices, changing relationships with the homeland, and barriers preventing displaced academics from integrating into existing international institutions.

Faviola Dadis said Steven Seagal sexually assaulted her during a 2002 hotel-room audition when she was a 17-year-old aspiring actress. She alleged Seagal touched her breasts and genitals after asking her to wear a bikini. Dadis said she suffered lasting psychological effects and delayed reporting because she feared entertainment-industry blacklisting. Los Angeles prosecutors are reviewing her recent police report. Dadis came forward amid broader misconduct reports and appeared with attorney Lisa Bloom and another accuser, Regina Simons. Seagal’s attorney did not comment; Seagal has denied other women’s allegations. Bloom said no lawsuits are immediately planned.

Meizu cut China pricing for its Pro 7 series by 600 Yuan, with prices starting at 1,999 Yuan from December 12. The Pro 7 and Pro 7 Plus feature secondary AMOLED displays, Helio processors, dual 12-megapixel rear cameras, 16-megapixel front cameras, Flyme OS 6, and 3,000mAh and 3,500mAh batteries, respectively.

Since August, Dale Capstick and her husband in Coxheath, Nova Scotia, have encountered about three dozen palm-sized giant house spiders, killing roughly 30. Neighbor Charles Andrews also captured one. Nova Scotia Museum biologist Calum Ewing identified the species as Eratigena atrica, a harmless European house spider found across parts of Canada and the northwestern U.S. Native to western Europe, it appeared in Nova Scotia in the mid-1990s. Often trapped in sinks and bathtubs, the spiders may enter homes accidentally or follow sizeable insect populations. They build non-sticky, funnel-shaped webs and use their speed to catch prey. Ewing said they will leave or starve when prey disappears, while persistent infestations can be handled by exterminators. Capstick hopes the spiders have now departed after several frightening weeks.

Undernutrition is a major risk factor for tuberculosis (TB) incidence and poor treatment outcomes. The RATIONS trial in eastern India found that six months of macronutrient and micronutrient supplementation reduced TB incidence among household contacts by 40%, while nutritional support for persons with TB was associated with approximately 35% lower mortality.

This study used a Markov cohort model to assess the lifetime cost-effectiveness of a RATIONS-style intervention for 100,000 HIV-negative household contacts in India. The intervention provided household contacts with rice, lentils, and micronutrients for six months; those developing TB received additional nutritional support during treatment. Outcomes included TB cases, deaths, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), and costs from government and societal perspectives.

Compared with usual care, the intervention was projected to reduce lifetime TB cases from 7,718 to 6,749 and TB deaths from 1,529 to 906 per 100,000 contacts. It averted an estimated 13,775 DALYs, mainly by reducing mortality. Discounted government costs increased from $0.76 million to $3.93 million, while societal costs increased from $5.24 million to $7.76 million. The incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was $229 per DALY averted from the government perspective and $184 from the societal perspective, both below India’s stated willingness-to-pay threshold of $550.

Results were most sensitive to supplementation cost and its effect on TB incidence. The intervention remained cost-effective across broad parameter ranges and was favored in more than 99.9% of probabilistic simulations at the $550 threshold. Limitations included excluding effects on transmission, relapse, disengagement from care, drug-resistant TB, pre-diagnosis costs, and broader nutritional and economic benefits. The analysis concludes that RATIONS-style nutritional support could cost-effectively reduce TB incidence and mortality in Indian populations with high burdens of TB and undernutrition.

The Bemidji Blue Ox won the Region 10C championship, defeating Crookston 7-3 after building an early 5-0 lead. Ben Thoma earned the win with seven innings, seven strikeouts and one run allowed, while Cody Benson went 3-for-5. Both teams qualified for the 48-team state tournament, but Bemidji receives a first-round bye as region champion. The Blue Ox will play the Fort Ripley–Blue Earth winner on Aug. 27 in Hamburg.

Rushin Shah, Apple’s former head of Natural Language Understanding for Siri, has joined Facebook after five years developing Siri’s voice recognition, conversational classification, and intent interpretation capabilities. He will work on natural language and dialogue understanding at Facebook but has not detailed his role. Shah cited a desire for a new challenge. His departure comes as Apple expands Siri through iOS, Macs, and the HomePod smart speaker while facing strong competition from Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant. Apple has not announced Shah’s replacement.

The lecture introduces dynamic optimality: whether an online binary search tree can process every access sequence within a constant factor of the best offline BST algorithm. In the BST computation model, searches start at the root and use parent or child pointers and rotations; insertions and deletions are excluded. Although balanced trees require \(O(\log n)\) time per access in the worst case, particular access sequences may permit faster amortized performance.

Several performance properties characterize such sequences. Sequential access should take constant amortized time. The dynamic finger property charges logarithmically according to the rank distance from the previous access. The entropy bound reflects access frequencies, while the stronger working-set property depends on the number of distinct keys accessed since a key’s previous access. The unified property combines spatial proximity and temporal recency. Pointer-machine structures can achieve it, but no BST is known to do so without an additive \(O(\log\log n)\) cost.

Dynamic optimality remains open. The best known competitive ratio is \(O(\log\log n)\), improving on the \(O(\log n)\) ratio of balanced BSTs. Splay trees are conjectured to be dynamically optimal. They move each accessed node to the root through structured rotations and satisfy sequential access, working-set, entropy, and dynamic finger properties, but neither the unified property nor dynamic optimality has been proved for them.

A geometric representation maps accesses and touched BST nodes to space-time points. A point set represents a valid BST execution exactly when every nondegenerate rectangle spanned by two points contains another point, a condition called arboral satisfaction. Thus, offline optimal BST execution corresponds to finding a minimum arborally satisfied superset of the access points. No efficient exact or constant-factor approximation algorithm is known; the best approximation factor is \(O(\log\log n)\).

The equivalence is proved by using lowest common ancestors in one direction and treaps ordered by next-touch time in the other. A natural greedy geometric algorithm processes accesses chronologically and adds points on the current row to satisfy all new rectangles. It corresponds offline to optimally rearranging the search path for future accesses. Although its optimality is unproved, its geometric decisions depend only on past accesses. Using split trees and lazy restructuring, it can therefore be implemented as an online BST.

HPE introduced the Edgeline Services Platform and two Software Defined OT apps at Discover 2017 to simplify management of expanding IoT environments and integrate IT with operational technology. The platform runs IoT applications near equipment in locations such as factories, refineries, vehicles and cities. The Data Aggregation App combines data from devices including PLCs and SCADA systems, while the Address Translation App distributes network address translations to subset networks and supports remote management. Analyst Mike Krell said HPE’s single-vendor approach could help customers navigate complex IoT technologies despite strong market competition.

For a finite-temperature CFT on flat space, temperature is the only scale, so all temperatures are related by rescaling and the gravity dual is a black hole with a planar horizon. On a sphere of radius \(R\), physics instead depends on the dimensionless quantity \(RT\), allowing distinct low- and high-temperature behavior.

The spherical theory admits three gravitational solutions: thermal AdS, a small black hole, and a large black hole. Black holes exist only above a minimum temperature, with two black-hole solutions at each allowed temperature. The small black hole has negative specific heat and never dominates, while the large black hole has positive specific heat. Comparing Euclidean actions, or equivalently free energies, shows that thermal AdS dominates below a critical temperature and the large black hole dominates above it. At the critical point the horizon radius equals the AdS radius, and the transition is first order in the large-\(N\) limit. This is the Hawking–Page transition.

The same result follows from saddle-point approximation: among gravitational saddles, the exponentially largest contribution corresponds to the lowest free energy. A toy model of matrix-valued harmonic oscillators with an \(SU(N)\) singlet condition illustrates the field-theory mechanism. Low-energy states have order-one degeneracy and dominate at low temperature, whereas states with energy and entropy of order \(N^2\) dominate at sufficiently high temperature when their large density overcomes thermal suppression.

The podcast examines balancing investment costs with simplicity. Guest John Robertson discusses indexing options, robo-advisors, the AutoInvest.ca cost-comparison tool, and his Practical Index Investing for Canadians course.

Vanguard’s one-fund asset allocation ETFs charge 0.22% and can reduce fees, but investors should consider trade-offs before leaving index mutual funds or robo-advisors. Savings may be modest for smaller portfolios: compared with Vanguard ETFs, TD e-Series costs less than $2 more monthly per $10,000 invested, while Tangerine costs about $7 more. Mutual funds and robo-advisors also support automated contributions, unlike ETFs, and ETF trading requires brokerage knowledge.

Vanguard ETFs may suit investors with simple TFSA or RRSP portfolios, but offer less flexibility for multiple or taxable accounts. VBAL and VGRO target 60% and 80% equities, respectively, leaving investors seeking other allocations without an exact option. VCNS holds 60% bonds, including substantial foreign fixed income; conservative investors are advised to consider GICs instead.

ESA inaugurated New Norcia 3, a 35-meter deep-space antenna in Western Australia scheduled to enter service in 2026. The fourth antenna in ESA’s Estrack deep-space network and second at New Norcia, it will support missions including Juice, Solar Orbiter, BepiColombo, Mars Express, Hera and several upcoming missions.

Cryogenically cooled components operating near −263°C will detect extremely weak spacecraft signals, while a 20-kW amplifier will transmit commands across billions of kilometers. The antenna can also support NASA, JAXA, ISRO and commercial missions through cross-support agreements.

Construction began in 2021 and cost an estimated €62.3 million, including €3 million from the Australian Space Agency. European and Australian companies participated, and CSIRO will operate the station locally. New Norcia complements ESA stations in Argentina and Spain, enabling continuous deep-space coverage and strengthening European-Australian cooperation.

Researchers from UCL and Imperial College London found that the last-resort antibiotic Polymyxin B kills active Gram-negative bacteria by triggering rapid production and shedding of their protective outer membrane. This creates gaps that allow the antibiotic to enter and kill the cell. High-resolution atomic force microscopy showed surface bulges forming within minutes. Dormant bacteria, whose membrane production is inactive, remained largely unharmed even when the antibiotic bound to them. Providing sugar awakened dormant cells, enabling the drug to kill them after a 15-minute delay. The findings may explain recurrent infections and suggest combining polymyxins with treatments that stimulate membrane production or awaken dormant bacteria.

The series is now a best-of-three for the Stanley Cup. Both goaltenders played well, but Tampa Bay had the advantage. The team must create better scoring chances, capitalize with a stronger killer instinct, and work hard to earn breaks next game.

Austin Police Chief Brian Manley urged those responsible for three package bombings to contact authorities. The 11-day campaign killed Draylen Mason, 17, and Anthony Stephan House, 39, and injured two women. Authorities are investigating a possible hate crime because all victims were Black or Hispanic. Rewards total $115,000. About 500 federal agents are assisting, while police have reviewed hundreds of reports, interviews and leads. Manley requested public tips and said laboratory analysis improved understanding of the bombs’ construction.

Bishop Hassan Kukah urged Nigerian politicians to improve governance and avoid taking the military’s patience with democracy for granted. He criticized leaders’ failure to meet basic needs despite abundant resources and condemned using religion to excuse misgovernance. Kukah also blamed citizens’ insufficient scrutiny of political promises, called for greater civic courage, and warned that Nigeria had become more divided since the 2015 elections. He urged government tolerance of opposing views and announced a Kukah Centre leadership forum promoting democracy, including a forthcoming lecture by Ghanaian President Nana Akufo-Addo.

Microsoft filed a Form 8-K on January 29, 2020, announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2019. The related press release was furnished as Exhibit 99.1, along with an Inline XBRL cover page data file. Chief Accounting Officer Frank H. Brod signed the report.

The West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals considered whether a private employer violated public policy by firing three at-will hotel employees who refused required polygraph examinations. The Court held that determining public policy is a question of law. It further held that at-will employees may recover when dismissal contravenes substantial public policy.

Relying on prior decisions protecting individual privacy and viewing a subsequently enacted statute restricting employer polygraph testing as embodying recognized public policy, the Court concluded that requiring or requesting a polygraph or similar test as a condition of employment generally violates West Virginia public policy. It acknowledged limited exceptions, including those contemplated by statute. The Court affirmed the circuit court’s ruling that the terminations violated public policy and remanded for further proceedings.

Justice Miller, joined by Justice Neely, dissented, arguing that no established prohibition against employer polygraph requirements existed when the employees were discharged in 1982 because the relevant statute did not become effective until 1983. Miller maintained that public policy must preexist the discharge and arise from constitutional, statutory, regulatory, or prior judicial authority, and that earlier privacy cases did not establish such a policy.

Justice Neely separately argued that applying the newly articulated rule retroactively was unfair and unnecessary. He asserted that the legislature had prospectively addressed polygraph testing and that the decision improperly altered settled at-will employment law after the employer’s conduct occurred.

After their 1946 divorce, the mother had custody of Lynda while the father maintained actual custody of Edward from age 2, except for a 14-month period when the mother retained him following a visit. In 1951, the trial court denied the mother’s custody application and confirmed custody in the father. The mother appealed, arguing that because both parents were equally fit, Civil Code section 138 favored awarding a young child to the mother. The appellate court held that the child’s best interests were controlling and that the trial court could consider Edward’s established home life with his father and the disruption another custody change would cause. It also stated that the trial judge’s hearing remarks could not impeach the final findings and judgment. The judgment was affirmed.

UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves has not ruled out tax increases ahead of November’s budget, citing geopolitical instability, U.S. tariffs and rising borrowing costs. With a projected fiscal shortfall of up to £30 billion, she is prioritising fiscal discipline and market credibility while retaining policy flexibility, creating uncertainty for businesses, households and voters.

May 9, 2001 reports covered Enron-related developments and broader business news. Questia Media, backed by Enron Chairman Ken Lay and others, cut 139 jobs after slowing book digitization and struggling to attract subscribers, though recent subscriptions had increased.

U.S. markets closed mixed: the Dow fell 51.66 points, while Nasdaq gained 25.20. Worker productivity declined for the first time in five years, raising inflation concerns. Enron shares dropped $1.93 to $56.11.

Enron Japan said deregulation had failed to create meaningful competition because of regulations, transmission costs and incumbent utility influence. It called for an independent power regulator.

In India, Enron’s Dabhol project remained embroiled in disputes with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board over costly power, unpaid bills and contractual obligations. Reports said expatriate executives’ families were relocated to Singapore and security increased, although Enron declined to comment. MSEB denied underusing its generation capacity or facing federal pressure to continue the Enron agreement. It appointed a former Bombay High Court judge as arbitrator, while lenders indicated they might support terminating the power purchase agreement if governments failed to resolve the crisis. The Swadeshi Jagran Manch demanded a judicial investigation into the deal.

Prize Petroleum sought to acquire Enron’s 30 percent stake in the Panna, Mukta and Tapti oil and gas fields, valuing it at about Rs 600 crore. Separately, U.S. energy company Williams announced plans to enter European energy trading and risk-management markets.

The lecture introduces ordinary differential equation initial value problems (ODE-IVPs), in which derivatives involve one independent variable and all initial conditions are specified at one point. Higher-order equations can be converted into first-order vector systems matching MATLAB’s standard form. Numerical solvers typically return solution vectors at multiple time points, with accuracy relative to the true solution as a central concern.

Forward Euler follows from truncating a Taylor expansion, using \(y_{\text{new}}=y_{\text{old}}+\Delta t\,f(y_{\text{old}})\). Its global error is first order in \(\Delta t\), making higher accuracy computationally expensive. Methods based on midpoint, trapezoidal, and higher-order Runge–Kutta formulas estimate the average derivative more accurately. MATLAB’s ODE45 combines fourth- and fifth-order Runge–Kutta estimates to assess error and select step sizes.

Because numerical integration repeatedly extrapolates from previously approximated values, errors can propagate and amplify. Stability depends on the norm of an error-propagation matrix involving the update formula’s Jacobian. Even physically stable equations can become numerically unstable under an unsuitable method or excessive step size. For example, applying Forward Euler to \(dy/dt=-2y\) with \(\Delta t=1\) produces nonphysical oscillation rather than smooth decay; larger steps cause divergence, while sufficiently smaller steps improve behavior. The homework requires implementing and comparing ODE update formulas, with implicit solvers to be discussed later.

The chapter presents a Model Driven Architecture approach to representing and validating extended-enterprise business processes through three connected components: a static domain model, a workflow model, and a value model. Controlled natural languages and logic-based formalisms translate business rules into structures suitable for automated reasoning.

Static domain modeling must distinguish complete, internally controlled data from incomplete external data. Closed-world reasoning supports the former, while open-world Semantic Web formalisms support the latter. Neither OWL description logics nor Horn-rule systems alone preserve all required semantics, particularly for complex relations, mixed open and closed entities, and modal business rules. Hybrid reasoning is therefore required. Business rules may also express alethic necessities or deontic obligations, creating further expressiveness and tractability challenges.

Workflow models describe activities, decisions, events, and interactions among actors. Standards include BPMN and UML Activity Diagrams, while Petri nets, process algebra, situation calculus, and temporal logic provide formal foundations. Declarative representations can support consistency checking, data exchange, annotation, and validation against static domain constraints, although dynamic behavior and large state spaces complicate model checking.

Value models describe actors, exchanged objects of value, dependencies, and estimated quantities to assess collaboration profitability. Graphical methods such as e3-value and logical representations can both support profitability calculations and decision-making.

Because all three models describe the same system from different perspectives, their consistency can be evaluated. Static consistency compares actors, value exchanges, message exchanges, and dependencies. Semi-dynamic consistency tests whether workflow behavior can meet value-model forecasts. Dynamic consistency compares expected behavior with execution logs, while process mining can reconstruct workflows from those logs.

The approach supports both prior feasibility analysis and adaptation based on runtime evidence. Remaining issues include locating areas requiring model changes, representing stakeholders’ reasons for actions, integrating customer perspectives, and improving hybrid reasoning across the different formalizations.

Casino mogul Steve Wynn settled in 2006 with a former employee who accused him of sexual misconduct, according to court filings. Wynn and an attorney recently told the FBI that the woman attempted extortion by threatening to disclose the settlement. Her attorney denied the claim, noting her emails requested no money and that she has not been questioned or charged. Wynn’s attorney said the FBI had concluded its investigation, while the FBI declined to comment. The disclosure follows reports of other misconduct allegations, including a $7.5 million settlement with a former Wynn Resorts manicurist. Wynn, who denies the accusations, resigned as chairman and CEO of Wynn Resorts. The settlement emerged in ongoing litigation involving Wynn, his ex-wife Elaine Wynn, and a former business partner.

The passage specifies SD card initialization, identification, transfer, protection, and function-switching behavior. After bus activation, the host issues CMD8 and repeatedly sends ACMD41 for at least one second or until the card reports ready. HCS indicates host support for SDHC/SDXC, while the valid CCS response identifies SDSC versus SDHC/SDXC. ACMD41 arguments must remain unchanged after initialization begins. The host obtains each card’s CID with CMD2 and assigns an RCA with CMD3, placing the card in Stand-by State. SDXC initialization matches SDHC initialization.

UHS-I initialization uses ACMD41 with S18R to request 1.8 V signaling. If the ready response reports S18A=1, CMD11 starts voltage switching; failure to respond requires a power cycle. CMD19 provides tuning blocks in 1.8 V transfer mode, with up to 40 consecutive executions completed within 150 ms, excluding host processing time.

During identification, the host remains at the identification clock frequency. It may obtain CSD with CMD9, optionally configure drivers with CMD4, and select one card for Transfer State using CMD7. Data transfers are point-to-point with the selected card. CMD12 can stop read or write operations. Programming cards may signal busy by holding DAT0 low; cards can be deselected without terminating programming or erase operations and later reselected. Resetting a card terminates pending programming and may destroy data.

The default bus width is one bit; ACMD6 selects four-bit operation but is rejected by locked cards. Block reads use CMD17 or CMD18 and include CRC protection. The maximum transfer block is 512 bytes, although smaller blocks may be supported under specified alignment conditions. Writes also use CRC; invalid lengths, addresses, misalignment, or write protection cause errors. CMD25 is preferred for faster multiple-block writes, and ACMD23 can pre-erase an expected number of blocks. ACMD22 reports successfully written blocks after an interrupted multiple-block write.

Erase operations use CMD32, CMD33, and CMD38. Protected sectors remain intact. DISCARD, supported only by SDHC/SDXC outside SPI mode, permits discarded contents to become indeterminate and has a 250 ms busy timeout. FULE logically erases the entire user area, is likewise limited to SDHC/SDXC outside SPI mode, and has a one-second busy timeout.

Write protection may be mechanical, internal, or password-based. CMD42 manages passwords, locking, unlocking, and force erase. Passwords are nonvolatile, and cards with a password set lock automatically after power-up. Card Ownership Protection adds a Force Erase Password, COP Unlock, protected force erase, and restrictions on clearing passwords. Force Erase removes user data and the normal password; FEP Force Erase requires the correct FEP and leaves the FEP stored. Locked cards accept only specified command classes and reject ACMD6.

CMD55 marks the next command as application-specific. Defined ACMDs are interpreted accordingly; undefined or illegal commands follow specified regular-command and error handling. ACMD41 is an exception because its response lacks APP_CMD status.

CMD6 checks or changes functions in six groups. Defined groups include bus speed, command systems, UHS-I driver strength, and power limit. Mode 0 queries supported functions, busy status, and maximum current or power; Mode 1 switches functions. Invalid selections cancel switching, and busy functions cannot be changed. The card returns a 512-bit status block. High-Speed mode, optional for Version 1.10 or later cards, raises interface speed to 25 MB/s and requires a one-to-one host-card connection.

CMD8 checks voltage compatibility and enables expanded initialization behavior. SDSC uses byte addressing and CMD16-selected block lengths, while SDHC/SDXC use 512-byte block addressing, disable partial and misaligned memory access, and do not support write-protected groups.

The ADS8681W/ADS8685W/ADS8689W devices support 16-bit single-ended and differential ADC inputs with bipolar or unipolar ranges and straight-binary output. LSB size equals the full-scale range divided by 2^16.

Configurable alarm functions monitor the ADC input and AVDD supply. Input high and low thresholds and hysteresis are programmable; AVDD uses fixed typical thresholds of 4.7 V and 5.3 V. Active flags clear after conversion unless the condition persists, while tripped flags clear when ALARM_REG is read. Alarm status can be reported through the multifunction ALARM pin, internal registers, or appended output flags.

The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI, dual-SDO, source-synchronous transfer, and multi-device daisy chains. Each device behaves as a 32-bit input-output shift register. Daisy-chain systems share CONVST/CS and SCLK and require optimal frames of 32 × N clocks for N devices, with throughput decreasing as device count increases.

The device operates in RESET, acquisition (ACQ), and conversion (CONV) states. RST can initiate either an application reset of configuration registers or a full power-on reset. The device acquires signals in ACQ and begins conversion on a rising CONVST/CS edge, ignoring further transitions until conversion completes.

Data frames begin when CONVST/CS falls and end when it rises. A 32-clock frame accepts a valid 32-bit command; shorter frames cannot perform writes but can read selected output MSBs. In longer frames, the final 32 input bits form the command. Supported operations include byte and half-word reads and writes, bit setting and clearing, and NOP. Output can contain conversion or register data, fixed patterns, device address, range, alarm, and parity flags.

Nine configuration registers control device identification, reset and power, input and output protocols, output data, input range and reference, alarm status, and alarm thresholds. Four standard SPI modes are supported. Read operations can use one or two SDO lines or source-synchronous operation with RVS as the output clock.

An example industrial acquisition design combines the ADS8681W with an eight-channel MUX36D08 differential multiplexer for programmable voltage, current, or temperature inputs. The ADC integrates a programmable gain amplifier, driver, and reference, supports signals up to ±12.288 V, and settles to 1% within 5 µs. A thermistor example demonstrates programmable alarm thresholds and hysteresis.

Separate AVDD and DVDD supplies require local decoupling. The device provides NAP and deep power-down modes for reduced power consumption. Recommended PCB practices include separating analog and digital routing, using short low-impedance ground connections, and placing specified AVDD, DVDD, REFCAP, and REFIO capacitors close to their pins.

The article examines digital storytelling in African higher education and teacher training, focusing on the skills it promotes and the contexts in which it is used. Digital storytelling combines narrative with text, images, audio, video, and animation, supporting digital literacy, creativity, communication, critical thinking, problem-solving, reflection, collaboration, motivation, and engagement.

Using qualitative document analysis, the study selected 15 African-context research articles published since 2000 through databases including Google Scholar, ERIC, JSTOR, and ResearchGate. The studies covered South Africa, Nigeria, Egypt, Tanzania, Uganda, and Kenya, with most using qualitative methods.

Findings indicate that digital storytelling can support identity expression, cultural understanding, community building, oral and writing performance, map-reading, higher-order thinking, reflective learning, and social activism. It can preserve oral traditions, indigenous knowledge, and languages while connecting traditional storytelling with modern technology. Applications included pre-service teacher education, geography, language learning, postgraduate research, multicultural education, and work with marginalized groups.

Challenges included limited equipment, unreliable electricity, inadequate technological skills, low confidence, rigid curricula, time constraints, and educators’ tendency to use technology mainly for administrative purposes. Some narratives also reinforced racial stereotypes. The article concludes that digital storytelling is adaptable across educational settings and can promote empowerment, cultural enrichment, and transformative learning, while emphasizing narrative content over technology.

Jeremy Corbyn used a chauffeur-driven 2.2-litre diesel Ford Galaxy for a six-mile journey from Islington to Westminster. The vehicle, emitting 189g of CO2 per kilometre and averaging 36mpg, would qualify for London’s Ultra Low Emission Zone charge. Before collecting Corbyn, it reportedly waited 40 minutes on double yellow lines without receiving a ticket.

Conservative MPs Andrew Bridgen and Andrew Percy accused Corbyn of hypocrisy for using a taxpayer-funded car despite his environmental advocacy and access to public transport. Corbyn, a cyclist who does not own a car, reportedly accepted the official vehicle following security advice. He has called for action on air pollution, supported phasing out diesel without unfairly punishing people, and pledged that Labour would introduce a Clean Air Act and clean-air zones.

Brazilian utility CPFL Energia launched Envo to provide solar equipment, installation, grid connections and support for selling excess power. The venture targets growing residential solar demand following 2015 regulations. Grid-connected solar projects rose from 7,500 in late 2016 to 10,000 by April. Santander Brasil will offer customer financing, while CPFL will source panels based on cost.
Hong Kong’s indie toy culture inspired Labubu, a globally produced toy that became a major Gen-Z trend in 2025.

Eighteen scientists, including 13 based in the U.S., received French President Emmanuel Macron’s “Make Our Planet Great Again” climate grants. Camille Parmesan and Benjamin Sanderson welcomed France’s support amid declining U.S. funding and Trump administration policies they said undermined climate science. Parmesan will study climate impacts on wildlife at a Pyrenees ecology station, while Sanderson will conduct climate-risk research in Toulouse. Macron honored the recipients ahead of a Paris summit attended by more than 50 world leaders.

The First Circuit affirmed denial of Ronald Johnson’s habeas corpus petition challenging his 1964 murder conviction. Johnson argued that the trial court failed to assess the totality of circumstances, improperly placed the burden of proving involuntariness on him, and admitted an involuntary confession. The court independently reviewed the undisputed facts and found the confession voluntary. Although Johnson was injured, minimally educated, of low intelligence, without sleep, unwarned of his rights, and surrounded by police before the interrogation, he remained alert, resistant, and aware of police procedures based on prior experience. Police neither caused his injuries nor credibly threatened or abused him, and the interrogation lasted about forty minutes. Considering all circumstances, the court concluded that Johnson’s will was not overborne and declined to decide his other claims.

University of Utah scientists mapped the shallow geology around Yellowstone’s Old Faithful using 133 portable seismometers and new techniques that extract signals from ambient vibrations and hydrothermal activity. The 2015 survey identified hour-long seismic tremors before eruptions, followed by about 30 minutes of quiet. Researchers attribute the tremors to pressurized bubbles that cool and implode as the geyser’s reservoir refills; eruptions occur at the end of the shaking.

Analysis of slowed, scattered, or blocked seismic waves revealed a probable hydrothermal reservoir west of Old Faithful. Estimated at roughly 200 meters in diameter, the network of water-filled cracks and fractures may hold about 300,000 cubic meters, or over 79 million gallons, compared with approximately 30 cubic meters released during each eruption. The survey also supports National Park Service management of an area where some buildings sit above thermal features. Researchers plan further studies on temperature effects, earthquake-wave behavior, and other geothermal areas in Yellowstone.

Secretary Stettinius urged governments to approach a general conference flexibly, avoiding formal commitments because the Dumbarton Oaks proposals might require revision. Discussions addressed objections to the name “United Nations” and whether organizational principles should specifically include treaty obligations, juridical equality, and territorial integrity. In January 1945, Stettinius sought to warn six Latin American associated nations that they could be excluded from the forthcoming conference unless they declared war and qualified as United Nations. He accelerated policy memoranda for Roosevelt’s Big Three meeting and prepared conference arrangements and the American delegation in advance. The principal unresolved issue was Security Council voting. Britain accepted a proposed compromise, while Roosevelt anticipated possibly accepting the Soviet demand for unanimity in exchange for Soviet concessions on proposed additional votes.

Worcester paid more than $11 million in overtime in 2017, including over $7 million to Police, Fire and Public Works employees. Police employees received $4.4 million in overtime and $9.3 million in detail pay. Officials said overtime reflected training, special projects, protests, grants, investigations and emergencies rather than understaffing. Some officers earned more from details than their base salaries, including George Kelly, who received $100,384 in detail pay versus $75,508 in regular pay. The city employed 7,287 people; 223 earned more than $100,000 in regular pay. City Manager Edward Augustus Jr. was the highest-paid employee, while only two of the top 50 earners were women.

AMO physics uses atoms, molecules, photons, and electromagnetic fields to study low-energy quantum phenomena. Historically focused on individual particles and collisions in gases, it now encompasses few- and many-body physics, entanglement, quantum information, quantum gases, and areas overlapping condensed matter physics. Its development progressed from observing nature to controlling internal states, motion, individual quantum systems, and increasingly complex correlated states.

Technological advances drove this evolution. Optical pumping enabled internal-state control; lasers enabled high-resolution spectroscopy, laser cooling, and Bose-Einstein condensation. Solid-state lasers became simpler and more numerous, ultrashort high-intensity pulses opened new regimes, frequency combs transformed precision metrology, and high-finesse cavities enabled single-photon studies. Current and emerging directions include quantum computation, topological states, and micromechanical oscillators.

Course 8.422 presents concepts underlying modern AMO research and may be taken before 8.421. It assumes quantum mechanics, especially perturbation theory. Topics include quantum electrodynamics, atom-light interactions, spontaneous emission and open systems, density matrices and master equations, mechanical forces of light, trapping and cooling, single photons, quantum information, trapped ions, and many-body quantum gases. It excludes advanced atomic structure, high-energy collisions, and high-intensity short-pulse physics. Assessment consists of ten problem sets and a term paper, with no midterm or final.

Atoms in optical lattices illustrate the course’s themes. Interfering lasers create periodic potentials whose behavior can be understood through classical potentials, photons, or microscopic forces. With spontaneous emission, optical lattices can produce Sisyphus cooling. Deep lattices isolate atoms for highly accurate optical clocks, especially at magic wavelengths that equalize ground- and excited-state potentials. Shallow lattices permit tunneling, band structure, and interaction-driven phenomena such as bosonic and fermionic Mott insulators. Pulsed lattices diffract matter waves, enabling atom interferometry, precision measurements, and spectroscopy of strongly interacting many-body systems. This combination of precision control and many-body physics exemplifies the field’s breadth.

This HBO Max viewing guide recommends a broad selection of current series, completed shows, classics, documentaries, and international productions. Featured genres include crime dramas, superhero stories, period pieces, medical dramas, comedies, romances, science fiction, true crime, and social documentaries.

Highlights include Mark Ruffalo as a priest-turned-FBI agent; John Cena’s violent vigilante Peacemaker; postapocalyptic, investment-banking, Targaryen, and Gotham crime dramas; and acclaimed series about televangelists, luxury-resort guests, comedians, pirates, hitmen, media dynasties, teachers, and struggling artists. Documentary subjects include Ruby Franke and Jodi Hildebrandt, the Austin yogurt-shop murders, funeral-home abuses, exotic chimp ownership, Robert Durst, queer murder victims in 1990s New York, and succession at the Texas Renaissance Festival.

The guide also notes awards, renewals, cancellations, final seasons, upcoming production schedules, and returning cast members. Several series have ended after one or more seasons, while others—including shows involving Peacemaker, the Bene Gesserit, pilots, hospital staff, and luxury resorts—have additional seasons planned or confirmed.

Indiana reported 278 flu deaths this season, and IU Health officials warn flu can persist until mid-April. Flu viruses may survive on surfaces for about a day, while norovirus can remain viable for days or weeks, allowing infection when contaminated surfaces are touched before the face.

An IU Health experiment found 15 types of normal skin bacteria on a reporter’s hands, with little difference after washing, indicating she needed to scrub longer and harder. Her cellphone carried 10 types of bacteria consistent with normal mouth, throat and skin flora. Officials recommend washing hands with regular soap for 20–30 seconds, scrubbing fronts, backs, wrists and beneath fingernails, then rinsing thoroughly. Handwashing is especially important after bathroom use, diaper changes or caring for sick people, and before eating.

Healthy Davis Together, later expanded as Healthy Yolo Together, provided free COVID-19 testing and other interventions in Davis and Yolo County, California. This study examined participant characteristics and testing patterns from November 18, 2020, through June 30, 2022, across Pre-Delta, Delta, Omicron, and Post-Omicron periods.

The program conducted 770,165 tests among 89,924 Yolo County residents, reaching approximately 41.1% of the county population and 78.4% of Davis residents. Most tests were saliva-based PCR tests. Testing peaked during Omicron, averaging 1,959 tests daily and accounting for 50.8% of infected individuals identified by the program. Participation declined considerably after Omicron. Overall, 12,626 tests were positive among 11,545 individuals.

Testing participation across most racial, ethnic, and age groups was at least 25%, except among those older than 85. The highest positivity rates occurred among American Indian/Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander, Latino, and 20–44-year-old participants. Women participated and tested frequently more often than men.

Among 67,083 adult participants, 12,591 tested regularly throughout the program. Frequent testers were most commonly women, people aged 19–34, and White participants. The proportion of frequent testers was highest during Omicron at 39.7%, with an average interval of six to seven days between tests.

The program retained participants and enrolled new testers over time, although new enrollment declined from 39,819 during Pre-Delta to 2,788 Post-Omicron. The data identify demographic and temporal patterns but cannot establish reasons for participation differences. The study recommends collecting behavioral data alongside testing information to improve future population-based public health interventions and infectious-disease models.

Extreme Networks shares fell 0.46% to $10.87. Five analysts set an average 12-month price target of $16.70, ranging from $15.50 to $18. The stock’s average brokerage recommendation is 1.2, with one Buy and four Outperform ratings. Its 14-period Average True Range is 0.48, with weekly volatility of 3.70% and monthly volatility of 4.85%. The Relative Strength Index is 45.3. Extreme Networks has a $1.25 billion market capitalization and 115.06 million outstanding shares. Previous trading volume was 1.11 million shares, below the average of approximately 2.6 million.

Abraaj’s $1 billion health care fund, promoted as a way to generate private-equity returns while improving hospitals in developing countries, drew $545 million for investments in Nigeria, Pakistan and India. Investors became concerned after learning that more than $200 million remained in cash and requested bank statements and independent forensic proof that the money had not funded Abraaj’s operations. Abraaj cited regulatory delays and the need for available cash, returned over $100 million, and hired KPMG to audit the fund. A World Bank corruption review closed without finding wrongdoing. Major investors included the World Bank’s International Finance Corporation and the Gates Foundation, each with $100 million in the fund. The fund had invested about half its capital, while its largest investment, India’s CARE hospital network, experienced declining earnings. Despite the dispute, World Bank president Jim Kim had publicly praised Abraaj founder Arif Naqvi as a model for private investment in developing economies.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 1, 2023 reported quarterly net sales of $81.8 billion, down 1% year over year, and net income of $19.9 billion, up from $19.4 billion. Diluted earnings per share rose to $1.26 from $1.20. Services revenue increased 8% to $21.2 billion, while iPhone, Mac and iPad revenue declined 2%, 7% and 20%, respectively. Total gross margin increased to 44.5%.

For the first nine months, net sales fell 3% to $293.8 billion and net income declined to $74.0 billion from $79.1 billion. Operating cash flow was $88.9 billion. As of July 1, Apple had $335.0 billion in assets, $274.8 billion in liabilities and $60.3 billion in shareholders’ equity.

Apple repurchased $18.0 billion of stock and paid $3.8 billion in dividends during the quarter. Nine-month repurchases totaled 365 million shares for $56.1 billion. The company had $4.0 billion of commercial paper and $105.3 billion of term debt outstanding.

Apple announced new MacBook Air, Mac Studio and Mac Pro models, along with Apple Vision Pro, expected in early 2024. Foreign-currency weakness adversely affected sales. Apple stated that its disclosure controls were effective and that there were no material changes to internal controls, market risks or risk factors. In the Epic Games litigation, enforcement of the App Store injunction was stayed pending appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court.

India’s Supreme Court barred parties from seeking votes based on religion, caste, creed, community or language. The author argues that the order overlooks how identity-based political mobilisation has enabled historically marginalised communities, including Dalits and OBCs, to challenge social hierarchies and gain representation. While acknowledging the harms of communal appeals, riots and polarisation, the author contends that existing laws, stronger rule-of-law enforcement and democratic political contestation are better remedies than judicial prohibition. The order is also described as impractical because identity influences elections at every level and cannot easily be monitored or eliminated. The author concludes that electoral democracy should evolve naturally, noting that voters increasingly consider development, public services and leadership alongside identity concerns.

Amazon’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2018 reported Q3 net sales of $56.6 billion, operating income of $3.7 billion, and net income of $2.9 billion, up from $43.7 billion, $347 million, and $256 million, respectively, in Q3 2017. Nine-month net sales reached $160.5 billion and net income $7.0 billion. North America, International, and AWS Q3 sales were $34.3 billion, $15.5 billion, and $6.7 billion; segment operating results were $2.0 billion, a $385 million loss, and $2.1 billion, respectively.

Operating cash flow for the trailing twelve months was $26.6 billion. At September 30, Amazon had $143.7 billion in assets, $29.8 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, $24.7 billion in long-term debt, and $39.1 billion in stockholders’ equity. The company acquired Ring and PillPack for approximately $839 million and $753 million, net of acquired cash. Amazon also adopted new revenue-recognition guidance, increasing retained earnings by about $650 million, and planned to adopt new lease-accounting guidance in January 2019.

The #MeToo movement rapidly reshaped Canadian politics, prompting resignations by Jamie Baillie, Patrick Brown and Kent Hehr amid unproven misconduct allegations. The resulting backlash raised concerns about due process and unfair consequences. The passage argues that allegations can legitimately end political careers when they undermine public trust or become too distracting, and that parties should hold leaders to high standards. Believing and supporting accusers does not negate the presumption of innocence; fairness should also presume alleged victims are truthful until evidence establishes otherwise. Although skepticism about delayed accusations may be valid, women may be coming forward now because they are more likely to be believed. For #MeToo to mature, it must remain fair while challenging the longstanding disbelief that has silenced women and perpetuated abuse.

The study examines how walking can transform an everyday activity into an aesthetic experience and foster environmental awareness and engagement among prospective teachers. Grounded in place-based critical art education and Dewey’s concept of aesthetic experience, it treats walking as a multisensory practice connecting body, mind, place, identity, community, and artistic expression.

Conducted online over 10 weeks in 2023 after the Türkiye earthquake, the study involved seven prospective fine arts teachers at a university in western Türkiye. Participants incorporated walking into their routines, created visual and textual diaries, photographed their surroundings, examined walking-related artworks—particularly Francis Alÿs’ “The Collector”—and produced their own artworks or designs. Data included class recordings, participant texts, visual diaries, artworks, and interviews. The researchers used thematic analysis, triangulation, participant validation, and multiple coders.

Three themes emerged: movement from conceptual perceptions to sensory experience, artistic inquiry into walking, and the role of place in art-based practices. Participants initially defined walking mainly as physical movement but gradually associated it with freedom, self-discovery, work, social issues, urbanization, nature, sound, belonging, and identity. Their walks increased attention to people, animals, buildings, environmental problems, city rhythms, and sounds. Artistic inquiry encouraged them to replace dominant or conventional images with subjective interpretations drawn from personal experience.

Participants produced performances, videos, collages, digital art, and other designs addressing themes such as pollution, loneliness, obstacles, urban life, peace, and street sounds. They reported stronger connections among art, everyday life, education, and place, and recognized walking itself as a possible artwork and tool for critical reflection and social awareness. Visual diaries and inquiry activities supported multiple perspectives and lesson planning, although participants experienced difficulties choosing subjects, visualizing emotions, working creatively with materials, and performing publicly.

The study concludes that walking-based, art-oriented learning can deepen sensory and critical awareness, expand relationships with place, and help prospective teachers incorporate subjective daily experiences into artistic production and teaching. It recommends further attention to participatory and community-based art in research on everyday life and aesthetic experience.

Indiana is considering outcomes-based contracts with private tutoring providers to improve reading among struggling sixth and seventh graders, tying much of the payment to student gains. Education Secretary Katie Jenner said contract details, funding, and the provider-selection process remain undecided, while the state also seeks grants and donations.

The approach has expanded since the pandemic, with 60 districts and education agencies testing it. The Center for Outcomes-Based Contracting recommends linking at least 40 percent of payments to defined outcomes. In 2025, providers achieved about half of contracted learning goals and earned 68 percent of potential bonuses.

Evidence remains limited and mixed. Programs in Texas, Florida, and Denver produced strong gains for some students but not others. Duval County continues using contracts with equal guaranteed and incentive-based payments, while Ector County is evaluating whether to resume them. Stanford researchers found that the model can improve collaboration, service alignment, and data tracking but creates financial risks and implementation challenges, particularly when attendance, participation, scheduling, and measurement affect results.
